541741.about: Fratelli Vineyard is engaged in the business of manufacturing, importing, exporting, processing and selling of wines and alcoholic beverages[1]

quarters.summary: Q1 FY27 marked a resumption of material revenue scale-up (+22% YoY, +25% QoQ) with an EBITDA turnaround (positive ~₹1.1 crore vs loss of ₹2.3 crore in Q1 FY26), driven by broad-based growth across Wine (premiumization, luxury leadership) and RTD (Shotgun), which more than doubled and is now the primary growth engine. Gross margin was largely maintained at ~80% despite RTD scaling; management reiterated FY27 EBITDA margin guidance of ~5-6% and expects net-net breakeven this financial year, with margin expansion to come from operating leverage rather than gross margin improvement as the business scales toward the FY30 revenue vision.

subsections.label: Profitability inflection
points: Net revenue from operations rose to ~₹46 crore in Q1 FY27 from ₹37 crore in Q1 FY26 (22% YoY growth) and ₹36.3 crore in Q4 FY26 (25% QoQ growth).
Reported positive EBITDA of ~₹1.1 crore versus EBITDA loss of ₹2.3 crore in Q1 FY26, marking an inflection at the EBITDA level.
Gross margin was 80% in Q1 FY27, within the 79-80% range.

subsections.label: Cost items
points: Finance cost rose to ₹3.8 crore from ₹3.1 crore LY, attributed to working capital borrowings as scale increases.
Depreciation rose to ₹2.5 crore from ₹2.3 crore LY.

subsections.label: Balance sheet and liquidity
points: Total loans/borrowings stood at ~₹130 crore, of which long-term borrowings were ~₹35 crore.
Finance costs rose due to working capital scaling; management said: 'We don't expect our debt levels to go up in any meaningful way from the current level.'
They are evaluating 'various options to bring in some liquidity… for more efficiency,' but said it is premature to disclose.

key_figures.label: Sette 15th Anniversary Limited Edition state presence

subsections.label: Wine business: premium mix resilient
points: Wine revenue grew ~8% YoY in Q1 FY27.
Premium-and-above portfolios contributed 71% of bottle revenue in Q1 FY27.
Super-premium grew ~7% YoY, with flagship J'noon up over 36% YoY, cited as evidence of strength in the luxury franchise.
Value segment delivered high growth (up 26%), positioned as a Tier 2/3 entry funnel enabling later trade-up.

Newer premium SKUs gaining distribution: Sette 15th Anniversary Limited Edition (Manish Malhotra collaboration) now in 7 states since Jan launch; Shiraz Cabernet (launched Apr FY26) registered across 11 states and 'seeing very good response.'

subsections.label: RTD (Shotgun) business: primary growth engine
points: RTD revenue more than doubled YoY in Q1 FY27; Q1 volumes ~50,000 cases sold, also more than double YoY.
FY27 ambition: management reiterated they are 'well on our way' to >200,000 cases in FY27 vs ~80,000 last year—implying RTD is the principal volume/velocity lever.
RTD product roadmap: currently 4 flavours; 'Shotgun J'noon… to be launched in Q2 FY27.'
Distribution unlock: RTD added 'more than 6,000 touch points' that were previously not meaningful for wine; total distribution now 'north of 30,000' touch points.
Repeat/offtake health: repeat ratio ~55-60% over the last 2-3 quarters; management emphasized repeats are rising and are healthy even in Tier 2/3.

subsections.label: Unit economics / mix contribution
points: RTD gross margin guided at ~70%.
RTD expected to be ~10% of total topline by end of FY27 (explicit answer to analyst).

key_figures.label: New RTD flavour to be launched (Shotgun J'noon)

subsections.label: RTD flavour roadmap
points: New RTD flavour 'Shotgun J'noon' to be launched in Q2 FY27, expanding the current 4-flavour lineup.

subsections.label: Grape sourcing mix
points: Grape sourcing mix is approximately 1/3 captive vineyards, 1/3 contract farming, and 1/3 spot purchases.

subsections.label: Temporary state-level headwinds (procedural, not demand)
points: Q1 was impacted by Delhi: 'delays in label registrations'; Uttar Pradesh: 'changes in the excise policy'.
Management stressed these are 'procedural matters… not a reflection of any weakness in demand.'
Offsets cited: Chandigarh, Haryana, Telangana, Odisha, Pondicherry performed strongly.

subsections.label: Channel mix (domestic go-to-market)
points: HoReCa ~35%, Retail ~65% of net sales.
Online alcohol remains negligible: 'very, very limited states… contribution extremely minimal.'

subsections.label: Regional revenue split
points: South 30%, West 25%, North 23%, East 11%, Defence/CSD 8%, Exports 2% of Q1 FY27 revenue.

subsections.label: RTD geographic expansion
points: Added Chhattisgarh and Karnataka, taking RTD footprint to 22 states in Q1; target 'more than 23 states' by FY-end.
Expansion pipeline mentioned: Jammu & Kashmir and Tamil Nadu (and depending on excise policy, Telangana referenced).
RTD exports have begun, reaching 2 export destinations.

subsections.label: Exports: breadth expanding, RTD export begun
points: Footprint present in 17 countries, added 2 new geographies in Q1, and expects more in Q2.
Export revenue contribution ~1.5-2% of net sales in Q1 FY27.
Notable development: exports have commenced for RTD (management referenced exports for 'both… and the shotgun'; phrasing indicates RTD export has started alongside bottled wine exports).
Profitability: 'Export business is profitable… more of a factor of scale now.'
Major markets: Asia and Europe cited as core contributing regions (5-6 core markets).

subsections.label: Vineyard sourcing economics
points: Grape sourcing mix (approximate): 1/3 captive vineyards, 1/3 contract farming, 1/3 spot purchases.
Management argued captive/contract structure helps manage volatility and supports quality.
Grape price inflation addressed: they said they have managed gross margin well partly due to this 'hedge,' but emphasized primary motivation for farming is quality.

subsections.label: RTD distribution build-out
points: RTD added more than 6,000 new touch points in Q1 FY27, expanding distribution beyond wine's existing base.

subsections.label: CSD (Army canteen) scaling
points: CSD contributed ~8% of topline in Q1.
New listings (Q4 FY26) debuted strongly: Dilt Red, Dilt Brut Rosé, Shiraz Rosé.
Upcoming listings: 'Mio and Noe sparkling wine will begin from Q2'; 'Shotgun Strong is expected in H2'.
Management expects CSD to become a more meaningful contributor through the year.

subsections.label: Competitive intensity in economy segment (state-specific)
points: Management explicitly localized discount pressure: 'mostly prevalent in the state of Maharashtra… especially in the economy segment.'
Company posture: 'quite conscious of our discounts… calibrated efforts' and willing 'to let go of that sale' where competitors offer very high schemes (especially for port/economy wines).

subsections.label: FTA (import duty changes) viewed as category-positive
points: Management expects FTAs to potentially expand the wine category, while noting remaining protections: Australia wines above US$5 keep 150% duty; Europe threshold US$2.5, above that duty drops to 75%.

Stated belief this may bring 'better quality wines at a slightly better price' and 'help grow the category,' positioning Fratelli to compete on quality/price: 'an opportunity to showcase' their wines.

subsections.label: Hospitality rollout and asset detail
points: Hospitality rollout delayed: While ₹500 crore revenue aspiration includes hospitality, management said the rollout may be 'slightly delayed' due to capex intensity and prioritization of core wine + RTD where returns are better.
Small existing hospitality: wine experience center + 4-bedroom stay (bookable), but 'very small scale.'
Material revenue impact from hospitality not expected for 'the next two years.'

Land/asset detail: most vineyards are not on Fratelli's balance sheet (long-term dry leases / farming arrangements). For hospitality, 10 acres have been acquired and sit on the balance sheet, earmarked for the project.

subsections.label: Procedural state-level headwinds
points: Delhi impacted by 'delays in label registrations'.
Uttar Pradesh impacted by 'changes in the excise policy'.
Management stressed these are 'procedural matters… not a reflection of any weakness in demand.'

subsections.label: Competitive discounting risk
points: Discount pressure localized to Maharashtra, especially in the economy segment; company is willing to let go of sales rather than match aggressive schemes on port/economy wines.

subsections.label: FTA / import duty risk-opportunity
points: FTA-driven import duty changes viewed as category-positive but protections remain (Australia 150% duty above US$5; Europe 75% duty above US$2.5 threshold).

subsections.label: FY27 outlook (near-term)
points: EBITDA margin guidance for FY27: 'around 5 to 6% for the year.'
Growth intent: maintain '20% plus' growth trajectory; Q1 seen as seasonally weaker but still delivered +22% YoY.
Profit objective: management stated they expect to be 'net net break even in this financial year.'
Brand spend discipline: brand investment historically 5-7%; FY27 guidance ~5% of net sales, with weighting toward RTD to build 'Shotgun.'

subsections.label: FY30 / Vision 2030: margin expansion lever is operating leverage, not gross margin
points: Investor concern highlighted: gap between ~80% gross margin and low EBITDA.

Management's repeated answer: EBITDA expansion comes from scale and operating leverage because the cost base is 'already geared up for a much larger business' and the company has 'industry leading gross margins.'
They positioned FY27 as the first step, implying incremental revenue drops through at higher contribution margin once fixed/semifixed costs are absorbed.

Management stated they expect to be 'net net break even in this financial year.'

Hospitality rollout may be 'slightly delayed' due to capex intensity; material revenue impact not expected for 'the next two years.'
Management expects CSD to become a more meaningful contributor through the year, with Mio and Noe sparkling wine beginning Q2 and Shotgun Strong expected in H2.
'Shotgun J'noon… to be launched in Q2 FY27.'
We see this number [Shotgun outlets, currently ~9,000] ideally going above 15,000 by close to H2.
Going forward, we will target expansion into 7 more states in FY27, including Delhi, Haryana, Uttar Pradesh, West Bengal, Tamil Nadu, Karnataka and Maharashtra.
Since launch in November '25, brand established presence across 4 states; during FY27, it will be made available in 14 more states.
We are targeting to launch Shotgun in Chhattisgarh, Karnataka, Telangana during H1 FY27.

guidance_ledger.metric: CSD sales - Merlot Wine and Noi Sparkling
guidance_ledger.statement: Merlot Wine and Noi Sparkling received CSD approvals with sales expected to commence from H1 FY27 onwards.
Shotgun is also expected to commence sales through the CSD from H2 FY27 onwards.
We have earmarked approximately INR9 crores towards routine and strategic capex requirements for FY27.
Our expectation is our capex in FY27 will be between INR6 crores to INR10 crores. I don't see us spending any more than that in capex.
Hospitality project remains in planning stage with an estimated investment of INR70-80 crores; deferred by about a year, review in H2 this year, possible action in calendar year 2027-28.
With increase of RTD business (gross margins close to 70%), overall gross margins will be between 76% to 80%.

We expect this year as well for Shotgun to be a little more than 10% of its overall top line because the base is big and we see a lot of potential in it; spends in the first 3 years are going to be on the higher side.
On the RTD, we are also launching 3 new variants, which we will see in the market in quarter 1.

risk_register.note: Last year's excessive rainfall was dealt with effectively, though it had some impact on higher cost and disease management; canals are now full as a result.

quarters.summary: Fratelli Vineyards closed FY26 with Q4 revenue growth of 13% YoY and operating EBITDA breakeven (positive EBITDA of INR1.06 crores in Q4), while full-year revenue remained largely flat due to regulatory disruptions in Maharashtra, Telangana and Uttarakhand in H1 FY26, with momentum normalizing in H2. Management guided to ~30% revenue growth in FY27, targeting net-net (PAT) breakeven at approximately INR240 crores revenue, driven by scaling of the RTD (Shotgun) business, continued premiumization/luxury growth, wider distribution, exports and CSD channel expansion, with a major capex cycle largely behind the company and the hospitality project deferred by about a year.

subsections.label: Q4 FY26 performance drivers
points: Q4 growth of 13% YoY benefited from strong traction in bottles and RTD segments alongside improved market conditions across several key states.
Telangana, which had a slow H1, delivered approximately 30% growth during the quarter as sales normalized following the renewal of retail licenses.
Haryana, Uttar Pradesh and Kerala also reported strong growth, while export business more than doubled compared to the same period last year.
EBITDA loss reduced significantly, driven by tighter cost controls, better operating efficiencies and benefits of scale as revenues recovered during the quarter.

subsections.label: FY26 full-year performance drivers
points: Full-year revenue growth remained modest due to regulatory disruptions in Telangana and Maharashtra during H1 and excise policy changes in Uttarakhand.
As headwinds eased, there was a clear improvement in momentum during H2, culminating in a stronger Q4.
Gross margins remained healthy at 79% despite changes in product mix, supported by focus on maintaining quality standards particularly within premium offerings.
EBITDA improved marginally to INR1 crore, reflecting benefits of improved operational efficiencies.
Continued investment in brands during the year through RTD launches, rebranding initiatives and strategic collaborations aimed at strengthening long-term brand equity.
Depreciation and finance costs were higher during FY26 due to commissioning of new assets and borrowings undertaken for capacity expansion and working capital requirements.

subsections.label: Capex and capital allocation
points: Completed approximately INR10 crores of capex across vineyard infrastructure, plant and machinery and other operational infrastructure during FY26.
With completion of these investments, the major capex cycle is largely behind the company; infrastructure created is expected to support growth requirements over the next 3 years.
For FY27, earmarked approximately INR9 crores towards routine and strategic capex requirements (later stated in Q&A as a range of INR6-10 crores).

Hospitality project remains in planning stage with estimated investment of INR70-80 crores; project deferred by about a year, prioritizing RTD and other wine-related projects; review expected in H2 with possible action in calendar year 2027-28.
Other than the hospitality project, no major capex need seen; company has tools available (as a listed entity) to raise capital if a compelling opportunity arises.

subsections.label: Breakeven trajectory
points: Net-net (PAT) breakeven expected at approximately INR240 crores of revenue, targeted for FY27 based on 30% growth over FY26's ~INR185 crores base.
Cost structure is now more or less geared up to support even a doubling of the business from current levels without major changes, enabling operating leverage to kick in as revenue scales.
Cost efficiency is expected to come from increasing sales of core wine and RTD business, not from the hospitality business.

subsections.label: Cost structure detail (sensitive, limited disclosure)
points: Management declined to provide detailed breakdown of employee benefit expenses (~INR35-36 crores) and other expenses (~INR85-86 crores) citing sensitivity, but confirmed cost structure is geared for scale.

subsections.label: Luxury and premium performance
points: Luxury portfolio (wines >INR2,000 MRP) continued to perform well, reinforcing leadership position in this segment.
J'NOON, the flagship luxury brand, grew at an enviable 44% during FY26.
Sette continued to strengthen its position as one of India's most loved luxury wine brands.

Landmark collaboration between Fratelli Vineyards and fashion designer Manish Malhotra commemorated 15 years of Sette through a limited edition Collector's bottle, launched January 2026, now available across 5 states; targeting expansion into 7 more states in FY27 (Delhi, Haryana, Uttar Pradesh, West Bengal, Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, Maharashtra).

Premium portfolio revenue declined 16% YoY primarily due to regulatory disruptions across Maharashtra, Telangana, Uttarakhand and Delhi, partially offset by strong growth in Haryana, UP, Kerala and Sikkim.

Margin trajectory viewed as positive because growth in super premium/luxury segments has outpaced premium segment growth, and these segments carry better gross margins; this momentum has continued into Q1 of the new year.

subsections.label: RTD (Shotgun) business
points: RTD brand Shotgun launched in H1 FY26; response extremely encouraging, selling approximately 100,000 cases in its first year and establishing presence across 18 states.
Company targeting to double RTD sales in FY27, aiming to cross 200,000 cases (RTD wine market estimated at over 1 million cases).
Distribution footprint for RTD expanded to approximately 9,000 outlets, including 2,000 new outlets added during the year; continued focus on Tier 2/Tier 3 cities.
Targeting to launch Shotgun in Chhattisgarh, Karnataka, Telangana during H1 FY27.
3 new RTD variants to be launched in Q1 FY27.
Necessary investments to double the RTD business were already made in Q4 FY26.

Shotgun's distribution reach (9,000 outlets) expected to grow above 15,000 outlets by H2, versus overall distribution universe of 30,000 outlets (bottles business, built over 15+ years, essentially available in every state).

subsections.label: Fratelli Brut (Sparkling) launch
points: Launched Fratelli Brut during FY26 as part of long-term premiumization strategy, strengthening position in the super premium sparkling wine category.
Consumer acceptance has been very encouraging since its November 2025 launch; brand established presence across 4 states, to be made available in 14 more states during FY27.
Fratelli Brut positioned at INR1,500 in the sparkling segment, described as a very good offering.

subsections.label: CSD channel performance
points: CSD channel has been one of the strongest growth engines for the company post-COVID; contributes about 8% of overall revenue currently, expected to keep growing.
Merlot Wine and NOI Sparkling received CSD approvals during FY26, with sales expected to commence from H1 FY27 onwards.
Shotgun expected to commence CSD sales from H2 FY27 (management later referenced Q4 in Q&A).
TiLT Red, TiLT Bubbly Rose, and Shiraz Rose already commenced sales through CSD channel in Q4 FY26, expected to continue delivering sales in FY27.
NOI is one of India's most preferred choices in the Sparkling segment, priced around INR1,000.
Fratelli is market leader in the Wine-in-a-Can segment in civil markets too, with more than 90% market share in India.

subsections.label: Volume/pricing color for FY26
points: Large part of FY26's modest growth was due to regulatory disruptions in H1; Premium segment (>40% of revenue) declined roughly 15% due to H1 disruptions, resolved in H2, with momentum continuing into Q1 of the new fiscal year.

key_figures.label: Expected export contribution to total revenue

subsections.label: Regional market performance
points: Telangana delivered approximately 30% growth during Q4 FY26 as sales normalized following renewal of retail licenses, after a slow H1.
Haryana, Uttar Pradesh and Kerala also reported strong growth in Q4 FY26.
Within premium portfolio, decline driven by disruptions in Maharashtra, Telangana, Uttarakhand and Delhi, partially offset by growth in Haryana, UP, Kerala and Sikkim.
Regulatory disruptions in Telangana and Maharashtra during H1 FY26, plus excise policy changes in Uttarakhand, impacted full-year growth; these headwinds eased in H2.

subsections.label: International expansion
points: Expanded footprint to 15 countries across bottled wine, canned wine and RTD portfolios during FY26.
Export revenue doubled during FY26 as a result of growing international presence.
Expect exports to contribute 5% of total revenue from FY27 onwards, positioned as a driver of revenue growth despite being small.

subsections.label: Competitive positioning and FTA impact
points: RTD segment has no impact from the ongoing FTA as it operates in a different price range (INR150-200) with a very different target group.
On the wine segment, more than 90% of revenue comes from products below INR2,000 MRP; impact from FTA would be limited to the portfolio above INR2,000 MRP.
Despite FTA-related concerns, premiumization momentum continues to grow, with luxury and super-premium brands growing fastest (e.g., J'NOON grew 40%+ last year).
Management does not anticipate much impact on the business from ongoing FTAs given current growth trends.
India-EU FTA implementation to be observed over the next year; no major impact seen currently in pricing or volume in the foreseeable future, but updates expected in coming quarters.

subsections.label: Discounting and pricing discipline
points: Schemes and discounts have remained fairly consistent year-on-year over the last 2-3 years, showing strength in brand love and distribution ability; company is now making a strong initiative to see how discounts can be brought down.
Strong focus on data analytics to identify distribution gaps and opportunities, with quarterly targets and monthly reviews to ensure availability with no gaps.

subsections.label: Sales and marketing organization
points: Close to 200 people directly involved in sales and marketing, one of the larger teams for the company's size, possibly the largest in its category.
Using Salesforce (a leading platform) to bring efficiencies in market penetration and cost control.

subsections.label: Long-term revenue aspiration
points: Company has outlined a long-term aspiration of reaching around INR500 crores of revenue by 2030, growing at a 20% CAGR.

Growth drivers cited: focus on premiumization, new product innovation and launches, the RTD segment (a whole new category where a substantial mark has already been made in year 1), and increasing width of distribution.

subsections.label: Hospitality project
points: Hospitality project remains in planning stage with an estimated investment of INR70-80 crores.
Company will continue to evaluate the project in line with market opportunities and long-term growth strategy.

Project has been deferred by about a year, with priority given to the RTD project and other wine-related projects, since Fratelli considers itself at its core a wine business, not a hospitality company.
Plan is to review the hospitality project in H2 of this year and possibly take definitive steps to action and initiate it in calendar year 2027-28.
Uncertain whether marketing spend will increase further once the hospitality business is initiated; too early to comment.

subsections.label: Vertical integration
points: Company has integrated the business backwards and forwards, including owning its own vineyards with drip irrigation, providing comfort against weather-related risks.

subsections.label: Second growth driver strategy
points: Fratelli is transitioning from being a company with a single sales segment (wine) to having two growth drivers: the wine business and the RTD business.
RTD is considered a good strategic fit given wine-based expertise, existing infrastructure and distribution, and strong category tailwinds.
Every business reaches an inflection point, and management believes Fratelli is nearing this point, after which new opportunities are expected to open for the company.

subsections.label: Regulatory disruptions
points: Full-year FY26 revenue growth impacted by regulatory disruptions in key markets such as Maharashtra and Telangana, and excise policy changes introduced during H1 FY26.
Uttarakhand excise policy changes also cited as a headwind during H1 FY26.
Delhi also cited among states with regulatory disruptions affecting the premium portfolio.
Conditions began normalizing in H2 FY26 with meaningful pickup in sales, continuing into Q4 FY26 and Q1 of the new fiscal year.

subsections.label: Weather / El Nino risk
points: Possible deficit in rainfall due to El Nino effect raised as a question; company currently comfortable due to backward/forward integration, own vineyards with drip irrigation.

Management notes weather is unpredictable — extreme conditions either way (excess rain or deficit) could have impact; last year's excessive rainfall was dealt with effectively though it had some impact on higher cost and disease management.
Canals are currently full because of excessive rainfall last year, reducing near-term concern; company continues to watch the situation closely.

subsections.label: FTA-related competitive risk
points: Potential competition from foreign winemakers once FTA comes into effect could impact the portion of wine portfolio priced above INR2,000 MRP (less than 10% of wine revenue).
RTD segment considered insulated from FTA impact due to different price band and target group.
India-EU FTA implementation impact to be monitored over the next year; no major impact seen so far in pricing or volume.

subsections.label: Cost structure sensitivity
points: Management declined to disclose granular breakdown of employee benefit and other expenses citing sensitivity of the information.

key_figures.label: Time horizon to assess FTA implementation impact

subsections.label: Overall FY27 outlook
points: Building blocks for growth are firmly in place: rapid expansion of RTD business, continued strength in luxury portfolio, wider distribution in domestic and international markets, increased CSD presence and upcoming product launches.

Regulatory conditions stabilizing and margins remaining resilient, with newer growth drivers such as RTD segment continuing to scale up; company believes it is well-positioned to capitalize on industry tailwinds.
30% growth guidance for FY27 expected to be visible from Q1 onwards.
PAT breakeven expected in FY27 as operating efficiencies come into play alongside targeted revenue growth.

subsections.label: Gross margin outlook
points: Gross margin expected to be in a range of 76-80% in coming years, with RTD business (gross margins close to 70%) becoming a larger share of the mix.

subsections.label: Capex outlook
points: Major capex cycle is largely behind the company; infrastructure created over the past few years expected to support growth requirements over the next 3 years without significant near-term capex commitments (aside from routine FY27 capex and the deferred hospitality project).

guidance_ledger.statement: Our plan and our guidance for this financial year of FY27 is to deliver a growth of approximately 30%.
With operating efficiencies coming into play, we believe PAT breakeven will be achieved in FY27; at approximately INR240 crores of revenue, we get to a net-net breakeven.
We intend and are targeting to double sales of our RTD business in FY27, expecting to cross 200,000 cases (from ~100,000 cases in year 1).
We see this number [Shotgun outlets, currently ~9,000] ideally going above 15,000 by close to H2.
We expect 5% of total revenue to come from exports from FY27 onwards.
Going forward, we will target expansion into 7 more states in FY27, including Delhi, Haryana, Uttar Pradesh, West Bengal, Tamil Nadu, Karnataka and Maharashtra.
Since launch in November '25, brand established presence across 4 states; during FY27, it will be made available in 14 more states.
We are targeting to launch Shotgun in Chhattisgarh, Karnataka, Telangana during H1 FY27.

guidance_ledger.metric: CSD sales - Merlot Wine and Noi Sparkling
guidance_ledger.statement: Merlot Wine and Noi Sparkling received CSD approvals with sales expected to commence from H1 FY27 onwards.
Shotgun is also expected to commence sales through the CSD from H2 FY27 onwards.
We have earmarked approximately INR9 crores towards routine and strategic capex requirements for FY27.
Our expectation is our capex in FY27 will be between INR6 crores to INR10 crores. I don't see us spending any more than that in capex.
Hospitality project remains in planning stage with an estimated investment of INR70-80 crores; deferred by about a year, review in H2 this year, possible action in calendar year 2027-28.
Long-term aspiration of reaching around INR500 crores of revenue by 2030 and growth at 20% CAGR.
With increase of RTD business (gross margins close to 70%), overall gross margins will be between 76% to 80%.

We expect this year as well for Shotgun to be a little more than 10% of its overall top line because the base is big and we see a lot of potential in it; spends in the first 3 years are going to be on the higher side.
On the RTD, we are also launching 3 new variants, which we will see in the market in quarter 1.
Our target of around 20% EBITDA margin (referenced by analyst, acknowledged by management) will be achieved as a function of scale, with operating leverage kicking in as business grows.

risk_register.risk: Regulatory disruptions in key markets (Maharashtra, Telangana)
risk_register.note: Impacted H1 FY26 revenue; conditions began normalizing in H2 FY26, with momentum continuing into Q4 and Q1 of new fiscal year.

risk_register.risk: Excise policy changes (Uttarakhand)
risk_register.note: Contributed to modest full-year revenue growth in FY26; described as a headwind that is easing.

risk_register.risk: Regulatory disruptions in Delhi (premium portfolio)
risk_register.note: Cited among factors causing 16% YoY decline in premium portfolio revenue.

risk_register.risk: El Nino / weather risk (rainfall deficit)
risk_register.note: Company comfortable due to backward/forward integration and drip irrigation in own vineyards; would only be impacted by extreme weather conditions.

risk_register.risk: FTA-related competition from foreign winemakers
risk_register.note: Could impact wine portfolio priced above INR2,000 MRP (less than 10% of wine revenue); no major impact anticipated given premiumization momentum; RTD segment considered unaffected.

risk_register.risk: India-EU FTA implementation uncertainty
risk_register.note: Implementation impact to be observed over next year; no major impact seen so far in pricing or volume, updates expected in coming quarters.

risk_register.risk: Excessive rainfall (prior year)
risk_register.note: Last year's excessive rainfall was dealt with effectively, though it had some impact on higher cost and disease management; canals are now full as a result.

themes.label: Premiumization / Luxury growth
themes.note: Luxury portfolio grew 15% YoY with J'NOON up 44%, and luxury/super-premium market share exceeds 50% domestically, outpacing premium segment growth.

themes.label: RTD (Shotgun) scale-up
themes.note: Shotgun sold ~100,000 cases in year 1 across 18 states and ~9,000 outlets, targeted to double to 200,000+ cases in FY27 as a new growth driver.

themes.label: Regulatory disruption headwind
themes.note: Regulatory changes in Maharashtra, Telangana and Uttarakhand caused H1 FY26 disruption and kept full-year revenue growth largely flat, though conditions normalized in H2.

themes.label: Margin resilience and operating leverage
themes.note: Gross margins held at 79% and EBITDA turned positive in Q4, with management citing cost structure geared for scale to drive operating leverage as revenue grows.

themes.label: CSD channel expansion
themes.note: CSD contributes ~8% of revenue with ~45% market share; new brand approvals (Merlot, Noi, Shotgun) expected to expand CSD contribution in FY27.

themes.label: FTA / import competition risk
themes.note: FTA could affect the <10% of wine revenue priced above INR2,000 MRP, but RTD is unaffected and premiumization momentum is expected to offset impact; India-EU FTA impact still being assessed.

themes.label: Path to PAT breakeven
themes.note: Management guides 30% FY27 revenue growth to reach ~INR240 crores revenue, the level at which net-net (PAT) breakeven is targeted.

key_takeaways: We closed FY '26 on a strong note with a growth of 13% year-on-year in quarter 4.
We achieved breakeven at the operating profit level, reporting a positive EBITDA of INR1.06 crores.

For the full year FY '26, revenue remained largely flat owing to regulatory disruptions in key markets such as Maharashtra and Telangana, as well as excise policy changes introduced during the first half of FY '26.
Our Premium & Above portfolio continued to contribute more than 70% of our overall revenue during FY '26.
Our sales in luxury category grew 15% year-on-year in FY '26, led by strong performance of our flagship brand, J'NOON, which grew at an enviable 44% during the year.
In the very first year, the [Shotgun RTD] brand has sold approximately 100,000 cases and established its presence across 18 states.
We intend and are targeting to double sales of our RTD business in FY '27.
We expect 5% of total revenue to come from exports from FY '27 onwards.

Our plan and our guidance for this financial year of FY27 is to deliver a growth of approximately 30%. With that in line, and as I mentioned, with the operating efficiencies coming into play, we believe PAT breakeven will be achieved.
We achieve a net-net breakeven at around INR240 crores.
pressing_questions: Could you outline the road map for a PAT profitability and the key milestones which you'll require to achieve it?
How large is your addressable market opportunity for the ready-to-drink beverages and wine-in-a-can product in India is? And how do you see consumer adoption evolving over these years?
How do you see competition coming in from the foreign winemakers especially when the FTA comes into place?
What is the company's current market share in the premium and the luxury wine segment? And how do you plan to strengthen your positioning in this category?

Our gross margin has been healthy at around 78%, 79%. While on EBITDA, it is still lower than our target of around 20%. So I wanted to understand on which specific cost lines are you expecting any kind of savings, operating leverage to kick in to achieve that 20% or is it that the margin will be majorly driven by the scaling up of the hospitality business only?

You have outlined a long-term aspiration of reaching around INR500 crores of revenue by 2030 and growth at 20% CAGR. But could you elaborate on the key growth drivers that will support this target because considering the current growth rate, I mean, is it achievable?

To support the company's revenue aspirations in these 3 to 4 years, what level of capex and expansion investment should we expect? And how do you plan to finance these investments? And any plans to raise external capital or increase leverage? Or will this growth will be largely funded through internal cash generation?

544304.about: Incorporated in 2002, Jungle Camps India Ltd operates wildlife camps and hotels, restaurants, and related activities in India.[1]

quarters.summary: Q1 FY27 revenue grew 12% YoY to ₹5.97 cr with EBITDA margin at 27% (vs 32% prior year, impacted by a one-off exceptional expense). Management guided to better ADR and occupancy in H2 (Oct-Mar) versus H1 due to seasonality, expects FY27 topline and bottomline improvement from new properties (Devprayag, Palash Kothi/Bandhavgarh) becoming operational in Q2, and flagged Mathura (IHG Holiday Inn Express, 105 rooms) and Sheopur Fort (heritage hotel) as FY28 growth drivers funded via a mix of IPO proceeds, internal accruals and ~₹50 crore of HDFC Bank debt by FY28-end, with debt-servicing comfortably covered by projected property-level revenues.

subsections.label: Q1 FY27 highlights vs Q1 FY26
points: Revenue from operations increased 12% YoY.
EBITDA margin declined to 27% from 32% YoY.

PAT and PAT margin declined YoY, partly due to a one-off exceptional expense of ₹0.52 cr related to write-off of project-related expenditure pertaining to the Parsili project following cancellation due to regulatory environment constraints; the item is non-recurring in nature.

subsections.label: Margin trend and drivers
points: Management attributed margin decline partly to Peepal Restaurant, a new property added last year, whose first six months were spent in setup/stabilisation, limiting EBITDA contribution despite topline growth; improvement expected in current year as Peepal stabilises.
New properties typically lower blended EBITDA margin when first added, but margins normalize toward the target ~30% once stable.
Management expects consolidated EBITDA margins in H2 (Oct-Mar) to be better than the same period last year.

subsections.label: Standalone balance sheet - tangible assets
points: ₹7 crore YoY increase in tangible assets primarily relates to capital work-in-progress (CWIP) for ongoing construction/renovation, including IPO-funded renovation (₹50 lakh capitalised) and Sheopur Fort/Pench renovation expenditure (₹3.5 crore combined, under CWIP).

subsections.label: Debt and financing
points: Debt being raised primarily for Mathura and Sheopur projects; both loans carry a two-year moratorium followed by a seven-year repayment period.
Combined monthly EMI for both properties post-moratorium estimated at ~₹53 lakh/month (~₹6.5 crore annually).
Management does not anticipate any requirement for additional working capital debt.
Company expects debt servicing to be comfortably managed from property-level EBITDA generation.

subsections.label: Other income nature
points: Other income is interest income earned on IPO funds parked in DC projects.

subsections.label: Parsili/land dispute recoveries
points: Following cancellation of the Parsili project (Sanjay Gandhi National Park) due to regulatory constraints, the ₹1.22 crore upfront premium is refundable and the ₹0.50 crore performance security (bank guarantee) will be returned; GST component will not be refunded; two years of annual lease rental paid will also be refunded.
All required formalities/documentation have been completed; amount expected to be received shortly.

₹1.35 crore received so far from this dispute; balance amount outstanding — company has filed suit to recover it since the property remains registered in its name and registration has not been cancelled.

subsections.label: Second land dispute/fraud incident
points: A separate incident involved land registered in the company's name with possession handed over, only later revealing an underlying dispute.

Total investment of ₹70-75 lakh; approximately ₹50 lakh being written off, with ₹20-25 lakh (relating to salaries/other expenses and land-related components/assets) transferable and usable at another property.

Company has strengthened due-diligence: engaging Forest Department upfront on properties with possible forest-related issues, and conducting more comprehensive checks with revenue authorities, local police and courts before proceeding with land transactions, since some disputes may not appear in initial land records.

key_figures.label: Maximum achievable occupancy in wildlife segment

subsections.label: Seasonality of demand
points: Safari season starts in October; October-December is a strong quarter with decent ADR and revenue.
January-March is also a strong period.
April, May, June are relatively slower due to rising temperatures and overall hospitality slowdown in the wildlife segment, leading to moderation in occupancy and ADR.
June, July, August: parks are generally closed but properties remain open; guests can still stay during the holiday period with discounted rates offered during off-season.
Management expects better ADR and stronger revenue Oct-Mar (H2) compared to April-Jun (H1); therefore H2 is expected to be better than H1.

subsections.label: Occupancy ceiling explanation
points: Full-year occupancy of 40% viewed by an analyst as low; management explained properties are closed for 3 months (Jul-Sep), so effective utilisation during the 9 operating months is closer to ~54% (40%/0.75).

In wildlife tourism, occupancy normally ranges 50-60% due to periods when safaris are unavailable (forest closed for 3 months); Tadoba's 57% occupancy is cited as near the practical ceiling, and ~60% is viewed as the realistic maximum for wildlife-focused properties.

subsections.label: ADR calculation methodology
points: ADR is calculated by dividing total room revenue by the total number of actual occupied room nights (based only on occupied rooms), whereas RevPAR calculation assumes rooms available across the full period (e.g., 360 days).

subsections.label: Property-level contribution and challenges
points: The three owned properties (Pench, Kanha, Tadoba) contribute the significant majority of revenue and profitability.

Rukhad Jungle Camp (leased, in the buffer forest of Pench Tiger Reserve) has only hard accommodation; despite high tariffs, being a newer/less-known destination limits business, though some improvement noted.
Bison Highway Retreat is a small (8-room) highway property with low achievable tariff, hence minimal contribution to overall numbers.
Kanha's room revenue mix contribution fell from 30% (Q1FY26) to 17% (Q1FY27).

subsections.label: Mathura Hotel (IHG Holiday Inn Express) rationale
points: Partnership with IHG under the Holiday Inn Express brand chosen because volume at the Mathura (a restricted, high-footfall pilgrimage) destination is very high and visitors tend to spend less, making a budget-focused brand a good fit.
Property scaled up from 60 to 105 rooms, plus banqueting and dining space; targeted opening in FY28.

Despite brand fee of ~7-8% of revenue, the 30% EBITDA margin target is considered achievable because the format needs a smaller team (~2 employees per room in luxury properties vs ~50 people for 105 rooms here) keeping costs lower, and ancillary revenue (F&B, banqueting) supplements room revenue.

subsections.label: Sheopur Fort
points: 90-year heritage asset being converted into a 60-key luxury boutique heritage hotel; first phase to bring 35-40 rooms online, with existing structures needing reconfiguration/fit-out.

Sheopur is a wildlife-adjacent destination (Ranthambore ~45km, cheetah relocation site ~40km, Chambal Sanctuary ~15km) but management does not intend to depend purely on wildlife tourism; plans to draw revenue from other segments including weddings.

Property design has physically separated buildings/courtyards, allowing the operational first phase to proceed without meaningful guest disturbance from ongoing construction on the remaining 25 rooms (expected to extend into FY29).

subsections.label: Palash Kothi (Bandhavgarh) and Devprayag
points: Palash Kothi: 20-room property under a 5-year management contract, located next to Tala Gate in Bandhavgarh; revenue share to owner is 13%; seasonal operations October-June; revenue to start from Q2FY27.

Devprayag: 22-room leased property from Uttarakhand Tourism Board, a spiritual (non-wildlife) destination with a three-segment opportunity; minimal capex required (max ₹1 crore) as furniture shifted from another property; primarily needs kitchen equipment and outdoor furniture; expected to commence operations shortly; revenue to start from Q2FY27.

subsections.label: Competitive positioning
points: Management does not see significant impact on ADR, margins or business from competition in Pench/Tadoba due to differentiated naturalist-led/experience-focused positioning versus purely five-star room offerings.
In competitive markets (e.g., Mathura/Prayagraj-type destinations), the company will need to adjust pricing based on demand-supply dynamics.

subsections.label: Company overview / history
points: 20-year history of building India's wildlife hospitality portfolio, starting with a single flagship camp in Pench.

Journey: Pench Jungle Camp (start) → Tadoba (2019) → Maharashtra expansion (2020) → Bison Highway Retreat (2022) → Rukhad Jungle Camp, Madhya Pradesh (2023) → BSE SME listing (Dec 2024) → first restaurant Peepal in Jaipur (2025) → Bandhavgarh management contract (Palash Kothi) and Devprayag operations commencement (2026).

subsections.label: Individual property details
points: Pench (Company's first flagship camp): 30 rooms, fully owned, located at the edge of Pench Tiger Reserve.
Kanha Jungle Camp: 20 rooms, owned.
Tadoba Jungle Camp (Muhari Gate, Maharashtra): 25 keys, owned, highest portfolio occupancy of 57%.
Rukhad Jungle Camp: situated inside the buffer forest of Pench Tiger Reserve, on a 10-year lease from MP Ecotourism Board, has the highest ADR in the portfolio.
Palash Kothi: 20 rooms, next to Tala Gate in Bandhavgarh, under a management contract.
Bison Retreat: located in Rukhad, also leased from MP Ecotourism Board.
Peepal Restaurant: located inside Central Park, Jaipur, next to the High Court and Rajya Sabha (assumed local reference), leased from RTDC; positioned as the only restaurant in that location.

subsections.label: Pipeline properties
points: Mathura Hotel, Kukru (Melghat Tiger Reserve), Ratapani Tiger Reserve (near Bhopal), and Sheopur Fort (border of MP/Rajasthan, 40-50km from Ranthambore National Park) are the four pipeline properties.
Also exploring/advanced-stage discussions at Panna, Satpura, Sariska, and Jawai Dam destinations, consistent with an asset-light, capital-efficient growth playbook.
Land held at Ratapani Tiger Reserve with permissions progressing; construction expected to start shortly.

subsections.label: Q1 FY27 business highlights
points: Expanded planned capacity of Mathura Hotel from 60 to 105 rooms.
Commenced development of Sheopur Fort as a heritage hotel.
Added Palash Kothi, Bandhavgarh under a 5-year management agreement; operations already commenced from 2026 with a soft opening.
Parsili project discontinued following regulatory constraints, with upfront premium and performance security refundable.
Secured Devprayag Tourist Rest House project in Uttarakhand.
Redeployed IPO proceeds from the discontinued Parsili project to Sheopur.

subsections.label: Kukru Jungle Camp development status
points: Located in Maharashtra, near an old tiger reserve area with few decent accommodation options; land parcel awarded by Madhya Pradesh Tourism Board (as referenced) for a tented luxury camp of 15-20 tents.
Funded entirely through internal accruals (not bank debt).
Currently working on basic infrastructure: fencing, and water supply infrastructure (pipeline, storage tanks) given the hilly terrain challenges.
Permissions/documentation for water and bio-reserve are in process; construction/contracting to follow once permissions are received.
Expected to be operational by end of FY28 (management stated 'late FY28, in March').

subsections.label: Sheopur Fort phased execution
points: Not all 60 rooms will be built at once; Phase 1 targets 35-40 rooms using existing but reconfigured structures (large rooms, washrooms) via modification/fit-out.
Property design (5 separate buildings around courtyards, fort structure with river on one side) allows Phase 1 operations without disturbance from Phase 2 construction.
Remaining 25 rooms (Phase 2) expected to take another year, extending into FY29.

subsections.label: Devprayag readiness
points: Structure already built by the lessor (Uttarakhand Tourism Board); company undertaking interior and furnishing work; expected to commence operations imminently ('next week' per management).

subsections.label: Capital efficiency and funding discipline
points: Both Mathura and Sheopur projects are substantially funded through IPO proceeds plus bank financing, keeping capital-side execution risk well managed.

Company deliberately restraining from pursuing multiple new destinations simultaneously; priority is to execute Mathura and Sheopur first before evaluating other identified target destinations (Panna, Satpura, Sariska, Jawai) after about two years.

Devprayag lease rental is ₹28,000 per year.
Kukru lease rental is ₹61,000 per year.

subsections.label: Madhura (Mathura) property investment
points: ₹2 crore invested in the Madhura property to date, with ₹1.21 crore due from government.

subsections.label: IPO objects of issue
points: IPO proceeds originally earmarked across four objects: Sanjay Dubri National Park Wildlife Resort (₹7 cr), Mathura hotel development via wholly-owned subsidiary Madhuvan Hospitality Private Limited (₹11.50 cr), Pench Jungle Camp Resort (₹3.50 cr), and general corporate purpose plus issue expenses (₹7.42 cr).
Following cancellation of the Sanjay Dubri (Parsili) project due to regulatory constraints, IPO proceeds originally earmarked for it have been redeployed to the Sheopur project.
Mathura investment via Madhuvan Hospitality Private Limited already stands at ₹8.79 cr as part of overall project funding.
₹3.50 cr applied to date for Pench Jungle Camp Resort and ₹5.92 cr applied to date for general corporate purpose.

subsections.label: Management contract structure - Palash Kothi
points: Palash Kothi is under a 5-year management agreement, with the company charging 13% of revenue from the property owner.

subsections.label: Land dispute resolution and legal recourse
points: Company has filed a suit to recover balance amount owed on a disputed land parcel since registration remains in the company's name and has not been cancelled.

subsections.label: Regulatory/lease cancellation risk
points: An analyst raised the concern that government-granted leases (e.g., with State Tourism Development Corporations) could theoretically face retrospective cancellation, citing precedents such as cancelled telecom licenses and mining leases in India.

Management responded that in tourism specifically, properties allotted by Madhya Pradesh Tourism have rarely been cancelled; cancellation clauses typically apply only if the licensee fails to develop the property within the stipulated timeline (e.g., 5 years); once developed and operated as a hotel, no cancellation clause typically applies.
Properties were obtained via competitive bidding processes (one-time premium bid plus annual rental) for Mathura, Devprayag, and Sheopur Fort.

subsections.label: Land dispute and fraud risk
points: Two incidents flagged: (1) a forest-related issue emerged after acquiring land from Madhya Pradesh Tourism Department, ultimately unresolved despite Forest Department efforts, leading to project cancellation (Parsili) and write-off; (2) a case where land was registered in the company's name and possession handed over, only later revealing an undisclosed dispute (described as fraud by the analyst).

Company has strengthened due diligence going forward: proactive engagement with Forest Department on properties with potential forest-related issues, and comprehensive checks with revenue authorities, local police and courts before land transactions, as some disputes may not appear in standard land records.

subsections.label: Execution risk on Mathura and Sheopur
points: An analyst flagged that Mathura and Sheopur are 'make-or-break' projects funded significantly via bank debt, and any execution delay of even one to two quarters could be consequential, urging close and full-time execution focus.

Management stated no significant challenges are foreseen on lease/agreement terms currently, and the company is prioritising completion of these two projects (deliberately restraining from pursuing additional new destinations simultaneously) before pursuing other pipeline properties.

subsections.label: Balance sheet / debt pressure
points: Management acknowledged current pressure on the balance sheet, particularly around the debt position, and is looking at alternative opportunities (e.g., Mathura branded hotel) to support and strengthen the balance sheet over the medium term.

subsections.label: Competitive market pressure
points: Destinations like Mathura/Prayagraj are competitive markets where pricing must be adjusted based on demand-supply dynamics; company will need to respond to market rate dynamics in such locations.

subsections.label: IR responsiveness
points: An institutional investor (running a PMS with shareholding in the company) expressed disappointment that requested details from the IR team had not been received after two to three months.

subsections.label: FY27 ADR/occupancy expectation
points: Management is hopeful of achieving around 5% YoY ADR growth for FY27, consistent with the seasonality-driven pattern (H2 stronger than H1).

subsections.label: FY27 revenue/EBITDA trajectory
points: This year's topline and bottomline are both expected to improve with the addition of Devprayag and Bandhavgarh (Palash Kothi) properties, plus stabilisation of teams at these new properties.
New properties can be expected to break even within roughly 6 months of commissioning based on company's historical experience (referencing team stabilisation cycles of 4-6 months).

subsections.label: FY28 outlook
points: Mathura and Sheopur targeted for FY28 opening, with revenue-relevant contribution expected mainly in H2 of FY28 (numbers to 'matter' in the second half).
Both Mathura and Sheopur are 12-month (non-seasonal) properties.
Kukru Jungle Camp targeted to become operational by late FY28 (around March).
Mathura lease rental once operational set at 5% of gross revenue or ₹54 lakh, whichever is higher; implying ~₹1 crore lease rental at ₹20 cr revenue level.

subsections.label: Debt outlook
points: Debt expected to reach around ₹50 crore by FY28-end as Mathura and Sheopur financing is drawn down (₹32 cr for Mathura, ₹17.5 cr for Sheopur from HDFC Bank).
₹32 crore Mathura funding to be deployed partly in the current year and partly in the next year.
Company does not anticipate any additional working capital debt requirement.

guidance_ledger.statement: Management is 'quite hopeful' of achieving around 5% YoY growth in ADR for FY27, similar to Q1 growth.
Management confirmed H2 (Oct-Mar) is expected to be better than H1 due to seasonality of wildlife tourism demand.
With Devprayag and Bandhavgarh (Palash Kothi) properties added and team stabilisation complete, both top line and bottom line are expected to improve this year.
New properties are generally expected to break even within about 6 months of commissioning.

Wildlife-segment occupancy is expected to remain in the 50-60% range at best (max ~60%), given 3 months of forest closure annually; overall company occupancy (~40%) is expected to remain broadly similar going forward, though supported somewhat by new properties in off-season.
Mathura Hotel (IHG Holiday Inn Express, 105 rooms) targeted for opening in FY28, with revenue impact mattering mainly in H2 of FY28.
Sheopur Fort (Phase 1, 35-40 rooms) targeted for opening in FY28, in the first half, with revenue impact mattering in the second half.
Kukru Jungle Camp targeted to become operational by late FY28, around March.
Remaining 25 rooms of Sheopur Fort expected to be developed over the following year, into FY29.
Peak debt expected to reach around ₹50 crore by the end of FY28 as both properties become operational, up from ₹5 crore in March 2026.
Mathura's broad revenue estimate is around ₹18-20 crore annually, with a downside scenario of ₹12 crore still considered comfortable for debt servicing.
Sheopur (35 rooms) first-year revenue estimate is at least ₹12 crore.
Company tries to maintain a 30% EBITDA margin; new properties lower margins temporarily but recover once stabilised, including for the Mathura Holiday Inn Express property.
Consolidated EBITDA margins in the second half (Oct-Mar) are expected to be better than the same period last year.
Combined EMI for Mathura and Sheopur post-moratorium is expected at ~₹53 lakh/month (~₹6.5 crore/year), which management believes will be comfortably serviced from property-level EBITDA.
Improvement in EBITDA contribution expected from Peepal Restaurant in the current year as it stabilises after last year's setup phase.
Discussions ongoing for new wildlife destinations (Panna, Satpura, Sariska, Jawai Dam); additions will happen 'if any of them materializes', with commercial viability as a gating factor.

risk_register.risk: Lease/regulatory cancellation risk on government-allotted properties
risk_register.note: Analyst flagged precedent of retrospective cancellations (telecom licenses, mining leases) as a risk to state tourism board leases; management said MP Tourism properties are rarely cancelled and cancellation clauses apply only if development timelines are missed.

risk_register.risk: Land dispute / fraud on acquired land parcels
risk_register.note: Two incidents: a forest-related issue leading to Parsili project cancellation and write-off (~₹50 lakh), and a second case where registered/possessed land later revealed an undisclosed dispute; company has strengthened due diligence (Forest Dept engagement, checks with revenue/police/court records).

risk_register.risk: Execution risk on Mathura and Sheopur (large, debt-funded projects)
risk_register.note: Analyst described these as 'make-or-break' projects funded via bank debt where even a one-two quarter delay could be significant; management said no major challenges currently foreseen and is prioritising focused execution of these two before other pipeline projects.

risk_register.risk: Balance sheet / debt pressure
risk_register.note: Management acknowledged current pressure on balance sheet/debt position and is pursuing alternative opportunities (e.g., branded Mathura hotel) to strengthen it over the medium term; peak debt expected to reach ~₹50 crore by FY28-end.

risk_register.risk: Seasonality of wildlife tourism
risk_register.note: Parks close for 3 months (Jul-Sep) annually and occupancy is structurally capped around 50-60% in the wildlife segment; April-June also sees slower demand due to heat.

risk_register.risk: Competitive market pressure in certain destinations
risk_register.note: In competitive markets like Prayagraj/Mathura-adjacent areas, pricing must be adjusted based on demand-supply dynamics; no material impact seen so far in core destinations (Pench, Tadoba) due to differentiated positioning.

risk_register.risk: New property team stabilisation drag on margins
risk_register.note: New properties typically see elevated salary and marketing spend in the first 4-6 months before reaching operational stability, temporarily lowering consolidated margins.

risk_register.risk: Construction disturbance risk during phased Sheopur development
risk_register.note: Analyst raised concern that ongoing construction of the remaining 25 rooms could disturb guests at the operational 35-40 room Phase 1; management said the property's separated building/courtyard design should prevent meaningful disturbance.

risk_register.risk: IR responsiveness to institutional investors
risk_register.note: An institutional investor reported not receiving requested details from the IR team for two to three months, expressing disappointment.

themes.label: Seasonality of demand
themes.note: Oct-Mar is the strong season with better ADR/occupancy; Apr-Jun is slower due to heat, and Jul-Sep sees park closures, structurally capping annual occupancy at 50-60%.

themes.label: Capacity expansion / new property pipeline
themes.note: Mathura (105 rooms, IHG Holiday Inn Express), Sheopur Fort (60 keys, phased), Kukru Jungle Camp, Devprayag and Palash Kothi additions expand the portfolio from 137 keys with more destinations (Panna, Satpura, Sariska, Jawai) under exploration.

themes.label: Debt-funded growth / balance sheet pressure
themes.note: Peak debt expected to rise to ~₹50 crore by FY28-end to fund Mathura and Sheopur, with management confident of comfortable debt servicing from property-level EBITDA despite acknowledged current balance sheet pressure.

themes.label: Margin normalization for new properties
themes.note: Margins dip when new properties are added (team build-up, marketing spend) but are expected to normalize toward the ~30% target within about 6 months of stabilisation.

themes.label: Land/lease due diligence and legal risk
themes.note: Two land dispute/fraud incidents (~₹70-75 lakh exposure) prompted strengthened due diligence processes covering forest, revenue, police and court checks before future land transactions.

themes.label: Branded hotel diversification (IHG partnership)
themes.note: First internationally affiliated branded hotel (Holiday Inn Express, Mathura) opens access to a larger addressable market beyond the core wildlife-safari positioning.

themes.label: Competitive positioning via experience differentiation
themes.note: Naturalist-led, experience-focused positioning has insulated ADR and margins from competitive pressure in core destinations like Pench and Tadoba.

key_takeaways: Revenue from operations for Q1FY27 grew 12% YoY to ₹5.97 cr, but EBITDA margin declined to 27% from 32% YoY and PAT margin fell to 8% from 20%, partly due to a non-recurring ₹0.52 cr exceptional expense related to the cancelled Parsili project.
ADR grew 5% YoY to ₹10,539, occupancy rose 2 percentage points to 45%, and RevPAR grew 9% YoY to ₹4,763 in Q1FY27.

Mathura Hotel (IHG Holiday Inn Express) capacity expanded from 60 to 105 rooms, targeted for FY28 opening; Sheopur Fort heritage hotel development (Phase 1: 35-40 of planned 60 rooms) also targeted for FY28.

Parsili project (Sanjay Gandhi National Park) discontinued due to regulatory constraints, with ₹1.22 cr upfront premium and ₹0.50 cr performance security refundable; IPO proceeds redeployed to Sheopur.

Palash Kothi (Bandhavgarh, 20 rooms) added under a 5-year management contract with soft opening in 2026; Devprayag (22 rooms, Uttarakhand) secured on lease, expected to commence operations imminently.

Peak debt expected to reach around ₹50 crore by FY28-end (from ₹5 crore in March 2026) to fund Mathura (₹32 cr HDFC loan) and Sheopur (₹17.5 cr HDFC loan), both with 2-year moratorium and 7-year repayment; combined EMI estimated at ~₹53 lakh/month.

Management flagged land dispute/fraud incidents (two cases, ~₹70-75 lakh exposure) and has strengthened due diligence processes; also acknowledged current balance sheet/debt pressure being addressed via the Mathura branded-hotel strategy.
Management expects both topline and bottomline improvement in FY27 from new properties, with H2 (Oct-Mar) expected to be stronger than H1 due to wildlife tourism seasonality.
pressing_questions: Sir, so this new property that you have started, doesn't it take some time or a quarter to break even in the beginning? I mean, is profitability expected from the beginning?

Sir, otherwise, if our model is seen, then it seems that we have got properties at a very attractive price... But now, if the court doesn't cancel it tomorrow, our lease agreement, which is specially with State Tourism Development Corporation.
So, broadly speaking, should we assume that we will have around ₹50 crore of debt by the end of FY28, by the time these two properties are operational?

These two projects are, in a way, make-or-break projects for the company. So, from an execution standpoint, someone needs to be very closely and fully involved. Even a small execution issue could potentially lead to a one- or two-quarter delay. Since the funding is through bank debt and not entirely our own capital, I think we need to be particularly sensitive and cautious about the execution and timelines.

There have been two incidents recently. In one case, there was a fraud related to a piece of land that we had purchased. In the second case, we recently did not receive the required permission, despite having already spent around ₹75 lakh... what steps have we taken? And how are we managing similar risks?

Sir, we run a PMS, and our PMS has some shareholding in your company. We had requested certain details from your IR team, but we have still not received them. It has been two to three months now. So, this is something we would like to express as a disappointment from our side.

544425.about: Incorporated in 2018, AJC Jewel Manufacturers Ltd is engaged in the manufacturing of gold and diamond jewellery.[1]

quarters.summary: Q1 FY27 revenue grew 124.69% YoY on strong operating leverage; management is building an integrated jewelry platform (manufacturing, design, technology, international access via Sharjah, and a new D2C silver brand Estara). FY27 India standalone revenue guidance of ₹450 Cr with a 50% YoY growth aspiration for the next three years, but no consolidated FY27 guidance yet pending Sharjah acquisition consolidation (expected update post-H1). Capacity remains materially underutilized across India and Sharjah, with working-capital intensity flagged as the binding constraint on ramp-up rather than plant bottlenecks; negative CFO trend over six years and rising receivables were acknowledged without quantified remediation targets or timelines.

subsections.label: Working capital, cash flow concerns, and management response
points: Investor highlighted receivables growing faster than sales historically.
Management attributed the increase to adding corporate clients with longer credit terms: "they have some more credit period…we will try to decrease that."
Investor noted negative CFO for six years; management responded "In the coming years we will try…to generate more cash," but gave no timeframe.
These comments tie back to management acknowledging working-capital intensity as the gating factor to fully utilize capacity.

Actionable takeaway: the call contains repeated signals that growth is being pursued ahead of cash conversion optimization; management acknowledges the issue but provides no quantified working-capital reduction targets or CFO breakeven timeline.

subsections.label: Capacity, utilization, and scaling constraints
points: Installed capacity: India (gold casting) 5 kg/day, Sharjah UAE (gold) 3 kg/day, India (silver) up to 8 kg/day.
Current run-rate utilization (approximate): India gold ~25% utilization ("1.2 [kg] per day"); Sharjah "800 grams" per day (vs 3 kg/day); Silver currently "one kilo…per day" (vs 8 kg/day).

What limits faster ramp: Working capital.
Management explicitly said achieving peak utilization needs "intensive working capital," funded "through internal accrual, debt and…maybe…equity fundraising."

544626.about: Incorporated in 2016, Exato Technologies Limited is a customer transformation partner providing technology-driven solutions that enhance customer engagement and operational efficiency[1]

quarters.summary: Exato posted a strong start to FY27 with 50% YoY revenue growth, 82% YoY EBITDA growth and 104% YoY PAT growth, driven by international business execution and order-book conversion; order book grew from Rs 600 crore to Rs 660 crore on new international logos (led by iQor BPO). Management guided FY27 revenue growth of 60-70%+ and profitability growth of 70-80%+, with ARR expected to rise from ~Rs 140 crore currently to Rs 180-200 crore by FY27-end, and IP/platform revenue expected to start contributing earlier than the previously guided March 2027/Q3FY27 timeline. The company is diversifying into a new AI infrastructure vertical and evaluating an inorganic acquisition to add geography/product capability, while continuing to target 300-500 (later referenced as 400-500) customers over 2-3 years.

key_figures.label: Order book executed cumulative up to Q4 FY26

subsections.label: Margin drivers
points: Healthy margins contributed by decent international growth, with strong contribution from international business and strong order execution happening in Q1, some part of the order book.
New logos as well as existing account expansion helped in better profitability during Q1 FY27.
AI infrastructure vertical is yet to contribute to revenue but expected to start clicking probably within a quarter, with strong contribution on revenue and profitability once it does.

subsections.label: Revenue bifurcation
points: Exports contributed close to 27.2% of revenue; BPO and IT/ITES collectively contributed more than 70% of revenue.
UK and US contributed significantly; two UK customers (one undisclosed, second is Diligenta) contributed significantly; US and Singapore are other largest global geography contributors.
Licences remain the biggest revenue contributor given the business model; services (maintenance, implementation, consulting) contributed close to 30%, helping improve profitability.

subsections.label: Employee cost / headcount
points: Headcount has been optimised and employee cost has come down versus previous quarters; this is expected to be optimised further.
CAO (Murali) is implementing AI internally across finance, HR, operations and sales to automate manual work, with similar plans for the delivery department.
Headcount will increase cautiously, with additions expected from any acquisition, on a quarter-by-quarter and project basis.
Model will remain heavily services-led but licence/product revenue will continue given reliance on riding along with global OEMs to acquire customers over the next two to three years.

subsections.label: Order book growth drivers
points: 60 crore of new orders added since Q4 presentation came from new customers onboarded, primarily international customers.

Order book expansion from 600 crore to 660 crore driven by addition of iQor BPO as a new logo (adding close to 60-65 crore of new business), plus significant expansion from current customers such as TaskUs and Diligenta.
Non-cancellable, renewable contract nature of order book: business is with data/compliance-heavy customers, giving stickiness and reducing customer-concentration risk.
More than 20 customers are on three-to-five-year contracts, which management cites as a differentiator and risk-mitigant against dependence on top 5 clients (60% of revenue).

subsections.label: Pending deals
points: Company working on a marquee deal with a couple of large BPOs, name to be disclosed once closed.
Two IP-platform-related deals with BPOs (new customers) expected to close soon, ahead of the previously stated March 2027 platform-readiness/Q3 FY27 revenue-start timeline.
One UK customer deal undisclosed pending end-of-month exchange notification.

subsections.label: Core business offering: CX and Analytics
points: CX and analytics is the growth engine, contributing significantly to success and serving as the market-entry offering.

'Customer experience as a service' is a term coined by Exato; offering is a managed-services ecosystem covering front-end activation, workforce management and interaction analytics platform combined as a service (not project-led).
Cross-sell/upsell opportunities include unified communications, AI infrastructure and ERP integration/transformation projects, all evolving under the CX and analytics umbrella.
ExatoIQ is proprietary IP used to identify solution gaps of OEMs and deploy integrated solutions where two systems must communicate, used for cross-sell/upsell across the customer ecosystem.

subsections.label: Four/five verticals structure
points: Currently operating in four verticals: CX and AI as a service; unified communication and infrastructure; ExatoIQ; and ERP.

Plan to create a fifth vertical structure: AI infrastructure, application as a service (integrating Cloud ERP/other applications, possibly via acquisition), AI as a service and CX as a service, managed services, and product.
AI is considered a subset of each vertical (CX, AI infrastructure, ERP) rather than a standalone vertical, to avoid confusing what each vertical's AI use case is.

subsections.label: Unified communications and AI infrastructure
points: Unified communication has been a steady vertical; new logos added include Kotak Life Insurance and Kotak Mutual Fund.

AI infrastructure is a newly formed line of business built over the last two months, led by Murali, Kailash Sethuraman and Paresh Sheth; expected to contribute meaningfully to revenue within a quarter once it starts clicking.
AI infrastructure will have relatively lower margin versus AI as a service/CX as a service, but is expected to open other avenues and contribute strongly to top line.

subsections.label: Revenue split outlook
points: Biggest revenue contributor expected to remain CX and AI as a service; second/parallel contributor expected to be AI infrastructure; a targeted acquisition, if it happens, would be the third largest contributor.
Services, consulting and licences expected to drive international presence and better profitability, while AI infrastructure is expected to drive top line.

subsections.label: Licence vs services mix
points: Licences remain the biggest revenue contributor given the business model; the model will be heavily services-led going forward to improve profitability, while licence/product revenue continues due to reliance on OEM partnerships to acquire customers.

subsections.label: AI-ready infrastructure practice
points: Invested significantly over the last two months in building an AI-ready infrastructure practice comprising: private AI solutions with LLMs bundled into a single-envelope infrastructure ('LLM in a Box'); adjacent networking with high-speed, secure networks and macro/micro segmentation for security ('future network as a service'); full-stack observability of production AI systems; and secure AI-ready infrastructure.
This investment forms part of the key go-to-market strategy for the next three to four quarters.
Company positions itself as a 'digital-native' partner offering 'private AI, LLM in a Box, CCaaS in a box and secure communication in a box' as single-envelope, business-in-a-box solutions.

Differentiator versus traditional infrastructure resellers: bringing predictable, sustainable inferencing cost via quantized models (vs high-token-cost frontier models) and providing GPUs that customers can virtualize/slice per requirement, addressing affordability and sovereignty/security concerns.

New model framed as 'platform plus outcome' rather than individual technology stacks — full-stack model spanning compute/infrastructure, cloud/security/observability/data, AI models, orchestration, application, and business outcome.

subsections.label: Own IP / platform journey
points: Clear strategic inclination toward developing proprietary product/platform; platform readiness was expected by March 2027, but company is on verge of signing agreements with BPOs for deals on its own platform, to be announced in coming months, with some deals expected to close this month.
IP revenue guided to start earlier than the previously committed Q3 FY27 timeline; expected to begin this month or next month; revenue notification to exchange expected by month end.
IP revenue will come from new clients (both target customers are new), and is expected to bring additional customer additions as well.
IP revenue margins expected in the range of 40-50%.

subsections.label: TOSS - Total Outsourcing Solution
points: Company has coined 'TOSS, a total outsourcing deal' where customers hand over the entire technology stack (software and/or hardware) for Exato to manage with a mixed team (customer + larger Exato team) to deliver desired outcomes.

subsections.label: AI workload / infrastructure technical distinction
points: Traditional enterprise workloads (ERPs, applications, web servers, accounting systems) run on sequential processing via CPUs; AI workloads require parallel processing via GPUs, which do not integrate seamlessly with CPUs.
GPUs are mainly used for learning/training, CPUs mainly for inferencing; customers need advice on where to use which, prompting demand for full-stack consulting and solutioning.
Geopolitical situation is driving demand for AI sovereignty — organizations wanting AI/CX/P&L data handled securely and not on public/global systems.

subsections.label: US expansion
points: Company is expanding into the US in a big way with a local presence to drive CX and analytics offerings along with AI infrastructure, Cloud ERP and ExatoIQ; previously US business was done sitting out of India.
CRO Naveen is based in the US for a couple of months for important opportunities and closures; company plans to keep adding manpower there.
Company has built a 24x7 delivery team supporting a hybrid model (sales engine in US, delivery from India), which large BPOs are seeking.

subsections.label: UK / Europe
points: UK grew more than expected in the quarter, with closed Agentic AI and services deals contributing significantly to revenue and profitability; more expected to come and expected to continue for the rest of the year.
Company is consolidating presence across Europe, not just the UK, as part of overall international market focus.
Diligenta (UK) has contributed significantly; there is more in the pipeline from this customer.

subsections.label: APAC / other regions
points: Mitel partnership upgraded to Platinum Partner status (highest APAC category); opportunities being explored in Malaysia and Singapore for Mitel.
Existing bank customers giving opportunities in Singapore, Bahrain and Dubai, adding dollar-value revenue and profitability.
Company continues to scale in the APAC market while primarily eyeing the US market.

New director Dr. Milind Raman Godbole appointed primarily to help target international markets, given his experience scaling GeBBS Healthcare Solutions from about $12 million to $230 million in revenue over ten years.

subsections.label: Acquisition geography rationale
points: Acquisition target being evaluated for geographical presence the company lacks — potentially APAC, UK, Middle East, or US — and in a business line company wants to grow (application, ERP, or product company).
