subsections.label: IntelliSmart acquisition
points: Acquisition of IntelliSmart is pending CCI approval; formal takeover to follow once approvals are in place.
Combined AESL + IntelliSmart smart meter portfolio expected to reach 4.7 crore (47 million) meters, with contract provisions for further natural volume growth.

subsections.label: Group inter-company solutioning
points: AESL positioned as the group's neutral solutioning entity for energy solutions across group companies (e.g., Adani Green, Adani Power) and third parties.

subsections.label: Right-of-way (ROW) challenges
points: ROW challenges remain present on the ground and are an industry-wide issue.
Company manages this by taking ROW decisions at ground level rather than fully depending on state machinery/administration support, working in parallel to clear ROW.
Most projects are concentrated in regions where AESL already has strong presence, allowing better anticipation of ground-level challenges and advance preparation.

subsections.label: Parallel distribution license regulatory delay
points: Parallel licenses applied for remain pending with the commission; no movement currently.
Maharashtra government has reportedly advised the commission to wait until the central government's tariff policy amendment is finalized before proceeding.

subsections.label: Revenue/margin variability in Energy Solutions
points: Quarter-to-quarter and year-to-year variability expected in Energy Solutions revenue/margins due to open positions being exposed to seasonal market price swings (summer vs monsoon/winter, irrigation demand spikes), and this quarter benefited from a delayed monsoon driving higher demand and prices versus last year.
Company's strategy is to minimize this variability by closing long-term positions on both purchase and sales sides without much time lag.

subsections.label: Transmission and HVDC pipeline outlook
points: Every year an opportunity of about INR1 lakh crore of bidding (combining central and state projects) is expected.
Lot of opportunity expected to arise from various STU projects going forward given Maharashtra, Rajasthan, UP activity.
Company has maintained ~25% market share historically and will continue at that level, translating to roughly INR20,000-25,000 crores of capex addition every year.

Two HVDC projects currently — one under bidding, one going to bidding shortly; HVDC volumes expected to continue given renewables need to be delivered over long distances, and now also due to load-center (city) demand for HVDC given overhead line constraints in dense urban areas.
KPS-1 HVDC project expected to commission by December 2029; Rajasthan (Bhadla-Fatehpur) HVDC project expected to commission at the beginning of 2029.

subsections.label: Energy Solutions platform outlook
points: Company aims to convert most Energy Solutions revenue into annuity-type long-term revenue with a small open position retained for optimization based on market conditions.
Most of the current 3,300-odd MU volume is expected to get absorbed into long-term sale contracts soon, following the long-term purchase-side tie-up already done.
Long-term contracts covering most of the capacity signed on the purchase side are at a very advanced stage, reducing the current timing gap between purchase tie-ups and sales.
Significant volume growth expected from the data center segment over time, though currently negligible.
Company plans a detailed C&I business presentation after completing next financial year, at the call around May next year (per context carried from prior quarter).

guidance_ledger.statement: We expect that every year, we would have an opportunity of about INR1 lakh crores bidding combining minimum central as well as various state projects.
We have been doing a market share of about 25%, and we will at least continue that part from our side.
Roughly about INR20,000 crores, INR25,000 crores of capex addition every year.
STU, I think annually, the volume would be about to start with about INR20,000 crores, INR25,000 crores projects. That is the least that I expect from STU side.
This KPS HVDC would be somewhere in FY29, around December '29.
Rajasthan would be at the beginning of '29.
We believe that HVDC volumes will continue... we see demand of HVDC project coming from load center side as well.
The market opportunity we believe we'll be able to encash is 7.5 gigawatt plus by 2031.
The C&I space... is a burgeoning space with close to 50 gigawatt plus market by 2030, '31.

Balanced portfolio is about 10 crores to 11 crores or 100 million to 120 million. The remaining states are Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, Telangana, a part of Andhra, and there are a few states where part quantum is also left out.

Most of the tied-up capacity on a purchase side has also tied up on our sales side... we will endeavour to do that, then most of the capacity is back to back locked-up and we don't create much of the volatility in our numbers.
As far as return profile of IntelliSmart is concerned, more or less, it will be on a similar line that we have... profitability of those numbers would be very similar to what we have for AESL.
We will have a detailed presentation on C&I once we complete next financial year and have this call again somewhere in May next year.
We will have about INR22,000 crores of capex next year (transmission ~15,500, distribution ~2,350, smart metering ~3,900), so between 21,000 to 22,000.
FY28 capex will be around 23,000, of which transmission ~20,000, distribution ~2,000, smart metering ~1,500 (order book only, excludes additional orders); overall between 22,000 to 25,000.
Capitalization number in FY27 would be about 21,000-22,000 crores.
In FY28, capitalization could be about 13,000 crores; thereafter capitalization will improve in transmission as HVDC projects start getting commissioned from FY29.
We plan to do transmission capex of about INR15,000-16,000 crores with INR8,000 crores of WIP, and plan to capitalize about INR14,500-15,000 crores out of this block.
We will continue to maintain that leverage in the ratio of around 4.5x to 4.7x.
Next year probably we'll be doing about minimum about 1 crore meters.

guidance_ledger.metric: New transmission opportunity value from market share
guidance_ledger.statement: Maintaining 25-30% market share converts to INR40,000-50,000-odd crores of new opportunity in transmission itself.
12-month pipeline would be about INR80,000 crores to INR1 lakh crores, depending on how bidding process proceeds; we expect bids of that magnitude will get finalized.

guidance_ledger.metric: EBITDA (revenue run-rate add from FY26 commissioning)
guidance_ledger.statement: This year's capitalization for transmission will add another INR1,600 crores of EBITDA (revenue) on a fully run-rate basis from projects commissioned this financial year.
Given the capitalization plan, we expect consolidated EBITDA (operating profit) could be around INR11,500 crores next year.
Once all existing under-construction transmission projects get completed with locked-in tariffs, transmission EBITDA will be 3x from existing transmission EBITDA trajectory.
Distribution business currently has INR2,500 crores EBITDA, which will translate to close to INR3,000-3,200 crores.
Smart meter business will start generating INR2,400 crores to INR3,000-odd crores of EBITDA trajectory once the entire smart meter portfolio is realized.
Currently the number is INR1,300-odd crores which is the full year tariff from the Mumbai HVDC project, which we will start accruing from next financial year.
Evaluation at MERC and STU level is ongoing; management cannot commit currently whether it will start working from this fiscal.

Management stated it will separately walk through the entire borrowing program for next 4-5 years; two things certain: leverage will not reach 4.5x-4.6x ceiling, and INR77,000 crores of capex is locked in over 4 years.

risk_register.note: Industry-specific issue that remains on the ground; managed via ground-level decisions and parallel working rather than full dependence on state machinery, plus concentration of projects in regions of existing presence aids preparedness.

risk_register.note: Matter pending with the commission with no movement; Maharashtra government reportedly advised commission to wait for central government's tariff policy amendment before proceeding.

risk_register.risk: Seasonal/quarterly variability in Energy Solutions margins

risk_register.risk: HVDC Pole 2 (Mumbai) commissioning timing uncertainty
risk_register.note: Not discussed this quarter (was raised in prior quarter regarding MERC/STU evaluation).

risk_register.risk: ROW (Right of Way) challenges from landowners/general public despite compensation orders
risk_register.note: Despite collector compensation orders as per government policy, some individuals/groups still create obstruction; police protection increasingly used; governments are systematically working to resolve this.

risk_register.risk: Regulatory/policy debate on transmission cost vs. battery storage (BESS)
risk_register.note: Ongoing policy-level debate on whether to push co-located BESS to optimize transmission cost; could affect quantum of future transmission capacity needed, though not expected to eliminate the need.

risk_register.risk: Compensation policy revision (change in law) risk
risk_register.note: Any government revision to compensation could be treated as change in law pass-through; company neutral to it but doesn't expect significant near-term revision.

risk_register.risk: China equipment sourcing restriction under TBCB
risk_register.note: Per TBCB bid conditions cannot use Chinese-manufactured equipment; no import from China envisaged, so not seen as a constraint.

risk_register.note: New domestic capacity being added by OEMs (e.g., GE, Hitachi) investing in India; supply-related issues easing out; no AESL project delayed due to equipment delivery delay owing to strategic procurement.

risk_register.risk: Uncertainty on HVDC Pole 2 (Mumbai) timeline
risk_register.note: Evaluation still ongoing at MERC and STU level; management cannot commit on commissioning timing.

risk_register.note: Olpad land possession from Power Grid expected in about a month; construction cannot start at Olpad until possession secured.

themes.note: Energy Solutions platform transitioned from incubation to full-scale business with 5 GW supply tie-up, 350 MW C&I customers, and INR590 crores EBIT in Q1.

themes.label: Smart metering scale-up
themes.note: 1.34 crore meters installed cumulatively against 2.46 crore order book; IntelliSmart acquisition to expand combined portfolio to 4.7 crore meters.

themes.label: HVDC project execution
themes.note: KPS-1 HVDC targeted for December 2029 and Rajasthan (Bhadla-Fatehpur) HVDC for early 2029; HVDC volumes expected to continue driven by renewable delivery and city-center load demand.

themes.label: Capex ramp-up
themes.note: Quarterly capex of ~INR3,500 crores delivered; annual capex addition of INR20,000-25,000 crores expected from market share-linked transmission opportunity plus similar STU volume.

themes.label: ROW & land acquisition challenges
themes.note: ROW challenges remain an industry-wide issue but are managed via ground-level parallel execution and project concentration in familiar regions.

themes.label: Leverage & capital discipline
themes.note: Management reiterated focus on execution and capital discipline even during high-growth period to reduce cost of capital and improve credit quality.

themes.label: Market opportunity sizing
themes.note: Energy Solutions targeting 7.5 GW+ RTC market opportunity by 2031, within a broader ~50 GW+ C&I market by 2030-31.

key_takeaways: AESL has transitioned into a full-scale utility platform in Q1 FY27, with all 4 business verticals (transmission, distribution, smart metering, energy solutions) now operating at full scale.
Delivered quarterly capex of close to INR3,500 crores.

Completed smart meter installation of 1.34 crore (13.4 million) meters cumulatively against an order book of 2.46 crore (24.6 million); combined with IntelliSmart acquisition, portfolio will reach ~4.7 crore (47 million) meters.
Energy Solutions platform has tied up about 5,000 MW of green energy supply capacity and about 350 MW of C&I customers, with long-term contracts expected shortly.
Energy Solutions EBIT of INR590 crores in Q1, with ~INR570 crores from long-term contracted positions and the balance from power trading/services.
Significant growth seen in transmission and energy solutions in Q1; distribution and smart metering growing at a stable pace.
Market opportunity for the Energy Solutions RTC business targeted at 7.5 GW+ by 2031, with the C&I space seen as a ~50 GW+ market by 2030-31.
Right-of-way challenges remain an industry issue but are being managed through ground-level, parallel execution approaches.
pressing_questions: Nikhil Nigania (Bernstein) asked whether AESL is competing with Adani Green to sell to the same customers (e.g., data centers), and sought clarification on AESL's role versus Adani Power in the Maharashtra ~2.5 GW round-the-clock power contract with MSEDCL — management said the PPA/LOI was issued to Adani Power but AESL will be a major participant; Nigania indicated he would take further color offline.

Mahesh Patil (ICICI Securities) sought status update on the parallel distribution licenses applied for; management indicated the matter remains pending with the commission with no movement, awaiting central government tariff policy amendment.

quarters.summary: Management guided to a sharp capex and EBITDA ramp-up over FY27-FY28, driven by transmission (HVDC projects, RAB growth), continued smart metering scale-up, and an emerging C&I business, while maintaining leverage discipline (4.5x-4.7x net leverage) and improving credit ratings. Consolidated transmission EBITDA is expected to roughly 3x over the next 36-40 months as the INR72,000 crore under-construction pipeline gets commissioned, with distribution EBITDA rising to ~INR3,000-3,200 crores and smart meter EBITDA to ~INR2,400-3,000 crores.

subsections.label: Credit rating & interest cost
points: Most assets are now rated AAA+ or AAA, a significant improvement even while capex is being scaled up significantly.
Interest cost is going down as a consequence of improved credit ratings, translating into incremental returns for shareholders.
Refinanced a $500 million bond via Apollo, a U.S. insurance investor, demonstrating financial and operational strength even amid challenging geopolitical conditions.

subsections.label: Cash flow and leverage
points: Assets are generally financed in a 70:30 debt:equity ratio; only the equity portion is funded via internal accruals, balance through debt.
Management stated full comfort in meeting all existing capex requirements across transmission, smart meter and distribution despite negative free cash flow.

Net leverage guidance maintained at 4.5x to 4.7x; management stated that leverage is not expected to reach that ceiling despite capex ramp-up, and locked-in capex of INR77,000 crores over 4 years is already committed.
CFO to walk through the entire borrowing program for next 4-5 years separately with an analyst offline.

subsections.label: Growth trajectory in operating profit
points: Operating profit was range-bound between INR4,000-4,500 crores annually for FY19-20 through FY22-23.
A step-up occurred in subsequent years: ~INR6,000 crores, then INR7,000 crores in FY25, and about INR8,000 crores in FY26.
Growth attributed to capex-based businesses (transmission, distribution, smart metering) where profitability is added upon capitalization; C&I is the exception as a non-capex-based growth driver.
Management indicated at least 3x the current transmission EBITDA trajectory once all locked-in transmission projects (with locked-in tariffs) are commissioned over the next 36-40 months.
No FY26 revenue was yet added from Mumbai HVDC in the current financial year’s numbers; full-year impact will begin flowing through in FY27.

subsections.label: CWIP/SCA accounting clarification
points: Accounting treatment has changed: SCA (service concession assets) and CWIP are tracked separately from normal conventional assets.
Once an asset is commissioned it becomes part of contracted assets; while under construction it remains part of SCA assets; both fall under non-financial assets.

Reconciliation between FY26 CWIP (~INR8,000 crores) and next year's capitalization guidance (~INR15,000 crores in transmission) explained by heavy equipment (transformers, substations) typically procured toward the fag end of a project and capitalized immediately without passing through CWIP — as occurred with the HVDC project.

subsections.label: Transmission
points: Improved market share to almost 29% of projects that went into bidding this year, up from historical 20-25%.
Will maintain market share discipline between 25% and 30%, translating to INR40,000-50,000-odd crores of new opportunity in transmission itself.
Fatehpur-Bhadla HVDC: construction has begun at both substation and line level; no significant ROW challenges faced; significant capex expected to start from the current year (FY27/28).

Khavda-Olpad HVDC: all contracts finalized; construction not yet started; Khavda land already under possession with preparative work started, environment/forest clearance proposals submitted, and ROW permission applications begun; Olpad land possession expected from Power Grid in about a month; construction to start at both sites once possession is secured.

HVDC Pole 2 (Mumbai): evaluation ongoing at MERC and STU level; management believes Mumbai will require additional transmission capacity but cannot commit on timing given the project is still under evaluation.
Mumbai HVDC commissioned fully (100%) in FY26, on a single commissioning date of 15th March; project cost was INR7,000 crores, with no additional cost or tariff being claimed.

subsections.label: Distribution (AEML)
points: AEML continues to harden assets, adding INR1,500-2,000 crores of capex every year while keeping tariffs largely constant.
Efficiency gains are transferred to investors for incremental returns while customer tariffs remain the same and service levels improve — described as a win-win.
AEML rated the number one distribution company in the country for the last 4 years.
Distribution EBIT was down about 14% in FY26 even though volumes were up and losses improved (context provided by analyst, unconfirmed by management with a specific driver).

subsections.label: Smart Metering
points: Deployment surpassed the FY26 target of 70 lakh meters, installing about 83 lakh meters on the ground — described as potentially the highest by any operator, not only in India but globally.
Smart metering is viewed as a perpetual opportunity beyond the current contractual concession period, given industry structure, with future extension or new bidding opportunities expected.
Two ways to gain additional concessions: existing contract swelling (already grown from 2.3 crore to 2.46 crore) and the balance market opportunity of 9-10 crore meters.

Pending state opportunities include Karnataka, Tamil Nadu (already approved), Telangana (whole state), Andhra Pradesh (part), Gujarat (part), and MP (part), awaiting RDSS approval from the central government; states likely to bid once respective elections are over.

subsections.label: C&I (Commercial & Industrial)
points: C&I identified as a major growth driver for the next year alongside transmission and smart metering.

About 5,000 MW of renewable capacity contracted, with dozens of third-party consumers aggregating about 1,400 MW (1.54 GW) already tied to customers; remaining capacity to be matched to customers going forward.

Even if hyperscalers/data centers become deemed distribution licensees, they will still need to source power with peculiar requirements — positioning AESL (with solar, wind and BESS capacity) to offer power infra and supply-side solutions; the end customer relationship remains unchanged.

Margins on the 1.5 GW tied-up capacity are in excess of INR0.50 per unit; remaining capacity currently operates on the merchant market, subject to day-to-day market conditions; margin certainty will increase once contracts (medium/long term) are finalized.
Detailed C&I presentation planned for the next earnings call in May next year, once FY27 is complete.

subsections.label: District cooling (emerging business)
points: District cooling business being incubated, expected to start picking up in 4-5 years' time.
A concession secured for a cluster development project in Chennai.

Management is actively engaging with various state governments to tie up opportunities at an early stage as large new development clusters emerge across the country; currently not sizable but expected to be significant going forward.

subsections.label: Capex scale-up and RAB growth
points: AEML consolidated capex across transmission, distribution and smart metering has increased significantly, nearing INR15,000 crores.

Management guided to continue improving capex and reach about INR20 (thousand) crores of capex this year (as stated verbatim), while also improving credit ratings — usually a challenging combination during rapid capex scale-up.

RAB continues to grow: AEML RAB has roughly doubled from INR5,400 crores to over INR10,500 crores; transmission RAB-based assets have grown by INR7,000 crores from the HVDC addition to a prior base of INR10,000 crores.
Management will continue to ensure the proportion of regulatory asset base (RAB) versus competitive asset base remains healthy, driving growth and cash generation.

subsections.label: HVDC project commissioning cadence and timeline
points: HVDC projects (part of the transmission capex pipeline) are expected to start getting commissioned from FY29, after which capitalization in transmission will improve further.
Mumbai HVDC was commissioned completely (100%) in the last month of FY26, on a single date, 15th March, at a project cost of INR7,000 crores.

subsections.label: Equipment sourcing / China exposure
points: Per TBCB bid conditions, the company cannot use any equipment manufactured in China; no import from China is envisaged for TBCB projects, including via EPC suppliers/equipment contractors.

Sector-wide supply-side challenges (GIS, transformers, reactors) are easing out, with new domestic capacity being added; OEMs (e.g., GE, Hitachi) have invested in India in manufacturing capacities, including for HVDC components.

Company avoided equipment delivery delays even in the difficult period due to strategic procurement practices and ordering equipment well in advance; no AESL project has been delayed due to equipment delivery delay.

subsections.label: ROW (Right of Way) challenges
points: Two types of ROW issues: (1) permissions such as forest clearance or wildlife sanctuary clearance, for which the company has structured a clear process and knows expected timelines; (2) ROW from general public/landowners (farmers, individuals), where despite compensation orders as per government policy, some individuals or groups still create obstruction.
State and central governments are increasingly serious about resolving ROW issues, including use of police protection for ROW access.

DLVC (District Level Valuation Committee) mechanism assesses prevailing market rate in an area and decides compensation accordingly, providing flexibility where the official ready reckoner/Jantri rate is lower than actual market price — this mechanism already existed (not new) and helps resolve ROW issues.
Fatehpur-Bhadla project has not faced any significant ROW challenge to date.

Any government-driven revision to compensation policy would be treated as a 'change in law' pass-through, so the company is neutral to such revisions, though management does not expect significant revision anytime soon.

subsections.label: Policy debate on transmission cost vs. batteries (BESS)
points: A policy-level debate is ongoing regarding how much transmission capacity the country should add, given cost implications, especially for renewable projects, and whether more co-located BESS should be pushed to optimize transmission costs.

Management believes interstate transmission lines will continue to be built and bid out, but expects greater future activity from states, since power still needs to be distributed to the last-mile consumer via state-level transmission corridors connecting renewable evacuation to load centers.
States such as Maharashtra, Rajasthan, Uttar Pradesh and Karnataka have already started bidding multiple intrastate projects.

Management clarified that interstate transmission build-out is not fully complete; if the country scales up battery storage massively, the required transmission quantum might reduce to some extent, but not entirely.

subsections.label: Transmission pipeline outlook
points: 12-month pipeline of INR80,000 crores to INR1 lakh crores is expected to get finalized via bidding, depending on how the bidding process proceeds.
This 12-month pipeline number has remained almost the same versus the same time last year.
Total identified projects for bidding stand at about INR150,000 crores.

Intrastate opportunity estimated at INR30,000-40,000 crores annually across all states combined, driven by states needing to build corridors connecting renewable evacuation points to load centers and then to end consumers.

subsections.label: Long-term EBITDA trajectory (verbal guidance, not formal EBITDA guidance)
points: Management does not formally guide on EBITDA but indicated that with INR72,000 crores of under-construction pipeline getting completed, this would translate to additional tariff of about INR10,000-odd crores.
Distribution business EBITDA (currently INR2,500 crores) expected to translate to close to INR3,000-3,200 crores.
Smart meter business EBITDA expected to reach an INR2,400-3,000-odd crores trajectory once the entire smart meter portfolio is fully realized.

Transmission EBITDA is expected to be roughly 2-3x the current numbers once all existing under-construction transmission projects (with locked-in tariffs) are completed and commissioned over the next 36-40 months.

Growth beyond the current 3-4 year corridor is expected to continue via C&I, potential distribution business expansion, and district cooling (an incubating business), while maintaining financial and execution discipline.

guidance_ledger.statement: We will have about INR22,000 crores of capex next year (transmission ~15,500, distribution ~2,350, smart metering ~3,900), so between 21,000 to 22,000.
FY28 capex will be around 23,000, of which transmission ~20,000, distribution ~2,000, smart metering ~1,500 (order book only, excludes additional orders); overall between 22,000 to 25,000.
Capitalization number in FY27 would be about 21,000-22,000 crores.
In FY28, capitalization could be about 13,000 crores; thereafter capitalization will improve in transmission as HVDC projects start getting commissioned from FY29.
We plan to do transmission capex of about INR15,000-16,000 crores with INR8,000 crores of WIP, and plan to capitalize about INR14,500-15,000 crores out of this block.
We will continue to maintain that leverage in the ratio of around 4.5x to 4.7x.
Next year probably we'll be doing about minimum about 1 crore meters.
We will continue to maintain that market share between 25 percentage to 30 percentage.

guidance_ledger.statement: Maintaining 25-30% market share converts to INR40,000-50,000-odd crores of new opportunity in transmission itself.
12-month pipeline would be about INR80,000 crores to INR1 lakh crores, depending on how bidding process proceeds; we expect bids of that magnitude will get finalized.

guidance_ledger.metric: EBITDA (revenue run-rate add from FY26 commissioning)
guidance_ledger.statement: This year's capitalization for transmission will add another INR1,600 crores of EBITDA (revenue) on a fully run-rate basis from projects commissioned this financial year.
Given the capitalization plan, we expect consolidated EBITDA (operating profit) could be around INR11,500 crores next year.
Once all existing under-construction transmission projects get completed with locked-in tariffs, transmission EBITDA will be 3x from existing transmission EBITDA trajectory.
Distribution business currently has INR2,500 crores EBITDA, which will translate to close to INR3,000-3,200 crores.
Smart meter business will start generating INR2,400 crores to INR3,000-odd crores of EBITDA trajectory once the entire smart meter portfolio is realized.
Currently the number is INR1,300-odd crores which is the full year tariff from the Mumbai HVDC project, which we will start accruing from next financial year.
Evaluation at MERC and STU level is ongoing; management cannot commit currently whether it will start working from this fiscal.

Management stated it will separately walk through the entire borrowing program for next 4-5 years; two things certain: leverage will not reach 4.5x-4.6x ceiling, and INR77,000 crores of capex is locked in over 4 years.
We will have a detailed presentation on C&I once we complete next financial year and have this call again somewhere in May next year.

themes.note: Consolidated capex nearing INR15,000 crores in FY26, guided to rise to ~INR20,000-22,000 crores in FY27 and ~22,000-25,000 crores in FY28.

themes.note: Mumbai HVDC fully commissioned in FY26; Fatehpur-Bhadla and Khavda-Olpad HVDC projects progressing with land possession and construction ramping up.

key_takeaways: Commissioned the Mumbai HVDC project, a RAB-based project important for Mumbai transmission capacity augmentation and integrating more renewable power for AEML.
Surpassed the FY26 smart meter deployment target of 70 lakh meters, installing about 83 lakh meters on the ground — the highest by any operator, not only in India but globally.

AEML consolidated capex (transmission, distribution, smart metering) has reached close to INR15,000 crores, with plans to reach about INR20,000 crores capex this year, alongside significant improvement in credit ratings (most assets now AAA+ or AAA) and reduced interest cost.
AEML RAB has grown from INR5,400 crores to over INR10,500-plus crores; transmission RAB-based asset grew by INR7,000 crores from HVDC addition to a prior base of INR10,000 crores.
Refinanced a $500 million bond via Apollo, a U.S. insurance investor, demonstrating financial and operational strength amid challenging geopolitical conditions.
Improved transmission market share to almost 29% of projects that went into bidding this year, with about INR150,000 crores of projects already identified for bidding.
O&M availability at 99.7%, and distribution losses reduced to 4.2% (from a starting point of 8.5%).

C&I identified as a major growth driver for next year, with close to 5,000 MW of renewable capacity contracted and about 1,400 MW already tied to third-party consumers; detailed C&I presentation planned for next year's call.
pressing_questions: Is it possible to share the percentage completion for Fatehpur-Bhadla? How much percentage completed till date? (Management: 'I don't have that number ready, Mohit, but we will send you that.')

Bharat Shah's question on whether operating profit of about INR8,000 crores and EBITDA of INR8,700-odd crores should be in the corridor of INR25,000-27,000 crores in 3-4 years' time was not directly confirmed by management, who declined to provide a specific EBITDA number.

Shirom Kapur's query on the discrepancy between smart meter operational EBITDA (non-Ind AS) reported in the 9-month FY26 presentation (INR466 crores) versus full-year FY26 (INR452 crores) despite a positive Q4 was not resolved on the call; CFO said he would have to check where the 9-month number came from.

quarters.summary: Management stated margins, yield and cost of borrowing have all "bottomed out," with gradual improvement expected from H2 FY27 onwards as the mix shifts toward higher-yielding Affordable, Emerging Markets and Corporate/CF segments. Full-year book growth guidance of 18%-20% and Affordable growth guidance of 50%-60% were reiterated, with management indicating actual delivery could exceed these guided ranges given strong July momentum. FY27 ROA is guided at ~2.4%, moderating to ~2.3%-2.35% in FY28 as negative credit cost normalizes.

subsections.label: Margin/Yield/Cost of Borrowing walk
points: Spread remained stable sequentially at 2.12%, demonstrating resilience in business model and disciplined pricing approach.
NIM moderated 19 bps Q-on-Q to 3.50%, of which 12 bps attributable to increase in leverage and 7 bps to true-up impact of Q4 FY26.

The 7 bps true-up gap was due to Q4 being a shorter quarter (90 days) with monthly annualization giving an artificial lift to NIM in Q4, which normalized in Q1; adjusted for that, the gap is only 12 bps on account of increasing leverage and lower yield on total assets.
Portfolio yield improved marginally to 9.48% for Q1 FY27 versus 9.47% in previous quarter; improvement seen across all business verticals.

Cost of borrowing increased marginally to 7.36% from 7.35% in previous quarter, with incremental cost of borrowing up 18 bps primarily due to tighter liquidity conditions and financial market volatility.

Average leverage moved from 3.6x to 3.75x during the quarter (ending debt-to-equity moved only marginally from 3.7 to 3.72); Q4 being high-disbursement quarter led to flow-through impact realized in Q1, translating into higher borrowings.
Overall yield slightly moderated due to lower investment yields even though loan book yield improved.
Disbursement yield in Q1 is higher than the book yield of 9.48%.

Prime yield grew ~8 bps in Q1 versus Q4 (8.92% base) and further improved in July; management estimates 10-15 bps of this benefit came from mix shift toward self-employed and non-home-loan products; absent mix shift, Prime yields would likely have been stable rather than declining like industry peers.
Affordable yield grew by almost 50 bps from Q4 to Q1.

Rating upgrade from CARE already received; ICRA and CRISIL upgrades underway/expected soon; benefit of ~10 bps expected on cost of borrowing from rating upgrades, with some benefit already visible on fresh borrowings at better rates.

subsections.label: Asset quality
points: Gross NPA remains below 1% at 0.95%; minor increase in 30+ and 90+ buckets is cyclical in nature and expected to come down in Q2.

A legacy account was classified as fraud during the quarter; exposure had already been fully provided for in FY22-23, hence no incremental financial impact; recovery process (legal) is separate from fraud declaration and has now begun, with discussions started with the borrower who has also approached the company; no recovery has been factored in for this account for FY27 as legal process may take time.

Recoveries remained healthy at INR67 crores (reported also as INR77 crores in Q&A) from written-off pool, resulting in negative credit cost of 12 bps; remaining written-off pool in retail is around INR340 crores.
Gap between recovery and ECL movement partly explained by OTS settlements taking a hit of INR10-12 crores, booked as write-off, occurring across Prime and Emerging on the legacy pool.

Delinquency in Prime and Emerging has sequentially improved despite the shift toward self-employed segment, attributed to a seasoned underwriting team, strong monitoring systems, and effective collection strategy.

subsections.label: Capital position
points: Balance sheet remains well capitalized with strong capital adequacy and Tier 1 ratios as of June 2026.
Net worth increased to INR19,800 crores with book value rising to around INR760.

subsections.label: Disbursement recognition change impact
points: Starting this quarter, disbursements are recognized on cheque realization basis rather than cheque handover basis, creating a one-time impact.
Disbursement growth should normalize from Q2 FY27 onwards.

Gap between reported (net) and gross (cheque handover) disbursement numbers is a combination of Prime, Emerging and Affordable, as retail and wholesale businesses have fully migrated from cheque handover to money-debited-from-account recognition.
The realization gap generally spreads over two months forward — majority in the first month, remainder in the second; minuscule flow in third month due to resale case delays.

Only interest income for the quarter is impacted by the recognition change (cannot charge interest until money is deducted from account); this impacts absolute income but not yield, since income booked corresponds to loan booked.
Fee income is unaffected by the recognition change as it continues to be based on committed disbursements; fee income growth expected to track disbursement growth going forward.

subsections.label: Affordable business strategy
points: Affordable disbursement currently below target level; company actively focusing on increasing productivity of Affordable branches.
Select Prime and Emerging Market branches have started contributing to Affordable business under a co-located branch model, with early results encouraging.
New CBO has taken charge of the Affordable business; July performance is much better than June, described as a clear indication of drastic improvement under new leadership.
July Affordable business contribution from Prime plus Emerging vertical is almost double what was delivered in Q1.

Company has strengthened the Affordable team across geographies, including two national-level resources with 20-25 years of mortgage industry vintage; major investment this year has been in Affordable business.
Company remains strict on Affordable growth guidance of ~50-60% for the year; net-to-net Q2 vs Q1 Affordable growth expected to be 2.5x-2.6x higher.
BT-in share in Affordable dropped sharply from 10.5% (Q1 FY26) to 3.4% (Q1 FY27), indicating that recent growth is primarily driven by new customer acquisition rather than balance transfers.

subsections.label: Prime and Emerging mix shift
points: Prime growth reflects a mix change from salaried to rationalized self-employed segment amid tough competition in the salaried segment.
Composition also shifted from home loan to non-home-loan products, supported by comfortable PVC (loan-to-value/prudential) norms cushion, remaining regulatorily compliant.
This mix change contributed to sequential yield improvement in Prime from Q4 to Q1.

subsections.label: Corporate/Construction Finance segment
points: Company plans to restrict construction finance portfolio to 3% of overall book in FY27, aiding overall margin improvement.

subsections.label: Micro Housing/Micro LAP business
points: Micro housing business will be run out of existing Affordable branches rather than opening new branches, to contain opex, a key metric being watched.
Policy formulated and rolled out in Q2; sourcing has started, but real financial contribution expected only from H2 FY27 onward.

subsections.label: Digital transformation and AI initiatives
points: Company continues accelerating digital transformation agenda, reimagining customer journey and core operations with a digital-first mindset.
Focus on conversational AI and document intelligence is helping simplify processes, enhance service quality, improve responsiveness and strengthen operational efficiency.
Company completed a Voice AI proof-of-concept during the quarter for the sanctioned but undisbursed pool and pre-due collections, with encouraging results.
AI-powered policy and knowledge assistance tools are currently under evaluation.
Company remains focused on building proprietary AI capabilities reflected in an in-house computing intelligence platform.
Initiatives support paperless operations and sustainability objectives while delivering a more seamless customer experience.

subsections.label: Distribution expansion
points: Company has begun leveraging selective Prime and Emerging Markets branch network to expand Affordable business; early results from co-located branch models have been encouraging.

subsections.label: Macro and geopolitical environment
points: India entered FY27 from a position of relative macroeconomic strength, although external risk increased materially during Q1 FY27.
Domestic demand remained resilient, supported by government infrastructure spending, healthy banking system liquidity and steady service activity.
Geopolitical tension in West Asia, volatile crude oil prices and uncertainty around the monsoon led to a slightly more cautious growth outlook.
RBI revised its FY27 GDP growth forecast down from 6.9% to 6.66% in June 2026 policy review, reflecting concerns around higher energy costs, supply chain disruptions and weaker external demand.
Quarter characterized by heightened global uncertainty from the U.S.-Iran conflict, leading to higher crude oil prices, increased market volatility and tighter liquidity conditions.
Despite external challenges, India's macroeconomic fundamentals remain resilient and housing demand continued to hold up well.

subsections.label: Fraud account
points: A legacy account was classified as fraud during the quarter; exposure of INR420 crores had already been fully provided for in FY22-23, so there is no incremental financial impact.
As per RBI norms, fraud declaration and recovery are two separate/parallel processes; recovery process has now begun with discussions started with the borrower, who has also approached the company.
Resolution options being explored include a partner joining hands to solve the builder challenge, or the borrower finding a buyer to sell the project.
No recovery has been factored into FY27 numbers for this account as the legal process may take time; management could not quantify expected recoveries pending buyer-seller evaluation of the project.
Historically, fraud classification tends to expedite recovery via legal recourse, as customers prefer to settle quickly to avoid the fraud classification.

subsections.label: Cost of borrowing pressure
points: Incremental cost of borrowing increased 18 bps primarily due to tighter liquidity conditions and volatility in financial markets amid geopolitical uncertainty.
Cost of borrowing remains elevated versus earlier levels, though some improvement noted versus the beginning of the previous quarter.

subsections.label: Forward outlook commentary
points: Margin, yield and cost of borrowing are all believed to have bottomed out; gradual improvement expected from H2 FY27 onwards.
Q1 growth was driven by improved productivity via technology and enhanced distribution, strengthening of Affordable and Emerging Market teams, and a focused approach on low-performing branches.
Q2 is expected to be much better than Q1, particularly in the Affordable business; July already showed very good momentum in both gross and net disbursements.
Management indicated the team is focused on delivering better growth than the 18%-20% guidance, suggesting the guidance is conservative.
Q2 gross and net disbursement numbers are both expected to beat Q1, with the recognition-related shortfall from Q1 expected to flow through in Q2.
Affordable and Emerging Market combined book contribution expected to reach 45% by end of FY27 and nearly 50% over a 2-year horizon.
Credit cost expected to remain negative for the remainder of this year given continued visibility on recoveries quarter-on-quarter.
ROA expected to settle around 2.3%-2.35% on a long-term basis, with this year targeted at ~2.4%.

ICRA and CRISIL rating upgrades are underway and expected soon, following the already-received CARE upgrade; this should further support cost of borrowing given upgrades occurred previously in a higher-rate regime.

guidance_ledger.statement: Maintaining full year guidance of 18% to 20% overall book growth.
Also maintaining growth guidance of 50% to 60% in Affordable loan book.

Cost of fund also, we strongly believe that it has also bottomed out.

This year we should continue to remain negative. We still have line of sight on good recoveries quarter-on-quarter this year at least.

On a long-term basis we are expected to settle around 2.3% kind of a ROA, 2.3% to 2.35%. Next year, this credit cost normalizing, we expect it to be around 2.3%.
In Affordable I think it should be 2.5 to 2.6x higher than what we did in Q1.
Overall should be also if I talk about net, it should be near 60%-70% higher.

subsections.label: Margin dynamics
points: Spread reduced by 10 bps QoQ from 2.22% to 2.12% due to lower incremental yield and BT (balance transfer) pressure in prime business.
Management view: yields have bottomed out and should start improving from Q1 FY27.

NIM improved by 6 bps QoQ despite spread compression; this one-off inverse relationship between spread and NIM is due to difference in methodology — spread is measured on a daily interest convention whereas NIM benefits from monthly averaging; this should smooth out from the next quarter onwards.
Yields moderated due to lower incremental yield versus book yield and higher run-offs; expected to improve from Q1 with higher mix of Emerging and Affordable business.
Cost of borrowing improved sequentially and for the full year, supported by gradual repricing with banks and transmission of policy rate cuts.
Incremental cost of borrowing edged up slightly in line with current prevailing liquidity and market conditions.

subsections.label: Opex
points: Opex growth largely driven by branch additions done in the later part of FY25 and one-time impact of implementation of new Labor Code.
35 branches added in Q4 FY26; full cost impact will be visible from next financial year onwards.
Operating leverage and scale benefits from existing business expected to partially offset these costs.
Opex to ATA expected to remain range bound between 1% to 1.1%.

subsections.label: Asset quality & recoveries
points: GNPA improvement is a direct result of strengthened collection infrastructure and continued emphasis on portfolio quality across both retail and corporate segments.
Recoveries remained strong driven by focused collection and resolution efforts.
Sale of retail properties increased YoY, underscoring improved execution across recoveries.
Marked improvement across all segments in 30+ and 90+ delinquency metrics; Affordable business showing signs of stabilization across all delinquency metrics.

30+ DPD figures presented in Investor Presentation reflect Stage-2 numbers including SICR-flagged accounts; on like-for-like basis excluding SICR, Q4 FY26 30+ DPD ratios are 2.72% for Prime, 2.11% for Emerging, and 1.32% for Affordable.
Prime segment 30+ DPD stable YoY (3.4% last year vs 3.3% now); Q3 numbers were an aberration.
SR (security receipt) recovery on corporate side: one account fully realized — this is a cash receipt (not a fair value gain), and the SR is now closed fully.

subsections.label: Capital & dividend
points: Board of Directors recommended a dividend of INR 8 per equity share (face value INR 10), subject to shareholder approval at next AGM.

subsections.label: Affordable segment
points: Affordable rebounded and grew 59% sequentially to INR 1,249 crore, largely flat vs Q4 FY25; company is 'back on growth path for affordable segment' and expects similar performance going forward.
Affordable segment growth guided at ~50% for FY27, up from INR 3,800 crore disbursed in FY26.

Affordable growth was weak in FY26/Q4 in absolute terms but management clarified this was due to deliberate checking of markets after facing challenges mid-year, which have since been resolved (temporary issues, now overcome), not a quality issue.
Affordable GNPA is below 0.6%, bouncing and 30+ under control — quality parameters in Affordable are under control.

Affordable yield decline (~75 bps QoQ) attributed to overall repo rate drop (1.25% last year) plus intense pricing competition in the market during the last quarter; NIM in Affordable was maintained via lower cost of funds offsetting yield decline.

subsections.label: Emerging Market segment
points: Emerging Market segment continued to outperform, delivering 34% YoY disbursement growth.
Composition of Affordable + Emerging expected to move from current 40% to 50%/50% (Prime vs Affordable+Emerging) over the next two years.
Growth sequence expectation: Prime growth lowest, Emerging growth higher, Affordable growth highest — applicable to both AUM and disbursement.

subsections.label: Prime segment
points: Prime segment delivered 43% YoY disbursement growth despite broader pressure on yield following rate cuts.

Management clarified Prime disbursement growth is largely 'replenishment' of book lost during the year (BT-out), while actual book growth in Prime is only 9% — hence disbursement growth appears high but book growth is not.
Prime 30+ DPD (like-for-like, excl. SICR) at 2.72% in Q4 FY26, versus 3.4% a year ago (stable YoY); Q3 was an aberration.

subsections.label: Corporate segment
points: Company restarted corporate segment with INR 335 crore disbursement in Q4 FY26 — primarily one case of ~INR 360-370 crore in Mumbai.

Focus is on reputed, good builders in top 7-8 category cities where market is strong, sell-ability is high and developer quality is good — cities include Pune, Bombay, Bangalore, Chennai, Hyderabad, Delhi.
Corporate finance business will not exceed 3% of overall book in FY27; company aims to grow this segment in a calibrated and sustainable manner.
Corporate loan yield target maintained at ~11.5%-12% (not going beyond this band to avoid focusing on lower-quality Tier B/C builders).

subsections.label: PMAY / government scheme
points: Facilitated 5,000 subsidies under PMAY, marking a significant milestone in enabling affordable housing and supporting Government of India's housing-for-all mission, supported by National Housing Bank.

subsections.label: Loan mix (housing vs non-housing)
points: Sharp increase in non-individual home loans in Q4 (non-housing loans grew from 30.6% to 32.4% QoQ, a ~2% increase) while housing loan growth was relatively soft.
Non-housing vs housing loan mix expected to remain in the range of 38%-40% at overall vertical level.
Company has scope to do more non-housing loans but is watchful of not breaching regulatory norms, which will help improve margin longer term.
Retail home loan share per PBC criteria stands at 65%, indicating room to reduce further.

subsections.label: Digital transformation
points: Launched 'Infinity' application, an in-house developed, fully digitized paperless onboarding workflow, now fully adopted by in-house sales team; helping materially reduce turnaround times and operating costs while significantly improving customer experience.
In process of onboarding all direct selling agents (DSAs) onto the platform.

Combined with Loan Origination System (LOS), the company has introduced an end-to-end digital solution from sourcing to processing to disbursement, eliminating paperwork and increasing field force efficiency (no office visits needed for file deposits).

Deployed AI-enabled calling solution for sanctioned but not disbursed cases, engaging 70% of identified pool and securing disbursement confirmation from 50% through intelligent outreach and targeted WhatsApp follow-ups.

Continuing to embed AI-led initiatives across the end-to-end loan processing lifecycle; during the quarter multiple use cases completed pilot runs including AI-driven calling for Re-KYC, pre-delinquency management, top-up offering, and fresh sales lead conversion.

New product introductions planned: Micro LAP and micro-housing loans in the ticket size range of 8-16 lakh (specifically 14%-16% mentioned segment range), to launch in Q1 FY27 in branches where Affordable business is already present.

subsections.label: Branch network & distribution
points: Extensive pan-India footprint enabled the company to effectively capitalize on growing opportunities in Affordable and Emerging market segments, particularly across high potential Tier 2 and Tier 3 locations.
Future focus will continue on increasing distribution, but priority is to make existing distribution/branches more productive.
Company is third largest player in the housing finance industry; overall industry growing at 12%-13% pace.

Distribution engagement events conducted in top 4-5 cities inviting surrounding cities' distribution partners, aimed at increasing commitment and volume from partners, to continue from April onward for the full year.

subsections.label: Corporate business geography

key_takeaways: The retail loan book grew by 16% Y-o-Y to INR 86,946 crores as on 31st March 2026. The total loan book of the company stood at INR 87,347 crores as on 31 March 2026.
The affordable and emerging market segments continue to increase their share in retail loan asset and is at 40% as on 31st March '26 compared to 37% as on 31st March '25.
The disbursement during Q4 grew by 36% Y-o-Y and 50% Q-o-Q to INR 9,355 crores.
Our GNPA continues to improve and is now below 1% mark, standing at 0.93% as of 31 March 2026.
In FY'26, Profit after tax increased by 18% Y-o-Y to INR 2,291 crores leading to an ROA of 2.66% and ROE of 12.73%.
The Board of Directors recommended a dividend of INR 8 per equity share having face value of INR 10/- for FY'26, subject to the shareholder's approval during next AGM.

Guidance for FY 2026-27: loan book to cross more than INR 1 lakh crores mark; Retail loan book projected to grow between 18% to 20%; NIM would be in the range of 3.55% to 3.65%; Credit cost continue to be benign due to recoveries from written-off pool; ROA would be in the range of 2.4% to 2.5%.
The company restarted corporate segment with disbursement of INR 335 crores in Q4 FY26. The corporate loan book stood at INR 401 crores as on 31 March 2026.
pressing_questions: How do you plan to expand lending reach, improve customer service and use digital platforms to make housing finance more accessible and transparent to all?

How are you approaching risks such as rising funding cost, regulatory compliances that keeps on changing over the time and credit defaults, while ensuring profitability remains steady and growth remains constant for the company?

Can you give more details of your growth guidance at a segment level, specifically Affordable and Emerging segment disbursement growth outlook, and more color on the corporate disbursements of INR 335 crores this quarter (single account or multiple, yields, geography)?

When guiding 2.4% to 2.5% ROA for next year, what kind of credit cost is being built into that, given last year's ROA had a 35 bps negative credit cost benefit — how will the 2.4%-2.5% ROA be delivered when recoveries eventually taper off?

Why did Affordable disbursements come down -3% in Q4 despite being the stated focus area, versus higher Prime disbursements — is this rate-related or asset-quality related, and is the low incremental yield (-75 bps QoQ) a key reason for slower Affordable disbursement pace?
What gives confidence that yields have bottomed out and will rise from here, given incremental yields are still declining?
There is a sharp increase in non-individual home loans (12% QoQ) versus soft housing loan growth (3% QoQ) this quarter — what is happening here and what is the strategy on loan mix going forward?

INDGN.about: Incorporated in 1998, Indegene Ltd provides solutions consisting of analytics, technology and commercial, medical, regulatory and safety services to life science and health care organizations[1]

quarters.summary: Indegene started FY27 strongly with Q1 revenue growth of 39.7% YoY/6% QoQ (INR terms), the best Q1 sequential growth in 4 years, driven by broad-based growth including accounts beyond top 20. Management expects FY27 organic growth to be better than FY26 with acceleration in H2, and margin recovery to the historical 19%-20% EBITDA band by Q4 FY27 (compressed from the earlier 6-8 quarter guidance to 6 quarters), aided by the outcome-based omnichannel deal starting revenue recognition from Q3 FY27 and workforce transformation productivity benefits.

subsections.label: Margin trajectory / normalization
points: Referring to August 2025 (Q2 FY26) call, investments in GTM and technology impacted margins by 150 bps starting Q3 FY26, with a 6-8 quarter normalization period originally guided.
With current and anticipated FY27 momentum, company is on track for margin normalization in 6 quarters (i.e., by Q4 FY27) rather than the wider 6-8 quarter range.

Ramp-up of signed deals through the year, notably the outcome-based omnichannel engagement won in Q3 FY26 with a top customer, has been carrying cost since going live in Q4 FY26; revenue recognition expected to start Q3 FY27, adding to H2 revenues with costs already incurred in the P&L, so most of that revenue flows straight to the bottom line.
Productivity benefits from workforce transformation and other Gen AI-led initiatives across operations and support functions will keep widening progressively.

Company reiterates trajectory set out in October last year: recovery to the historical margin band; through the inflection point in Q3 FY27, EBITDA in H2 FY27 will be back in the 19%-20% range operated in the past.
Management stated nothing in this quarter changes that expectation, and conviction has increased.

Other margin drivers besides costs already incurred: growth trajectory, investments in GTM/business leadership in the front, and revenue uptick from contracted Tectonic business — these are costs not expected to increase in line with increased revenue.

subsections.label: Margin drivers this quarter
points: Two factors caused sequential margin movement: (1) investment in workforce transformation had a one-time impact on margins this quarter but will reduce employee cost long-term and temper impact of future wage hikes; (2) company carried the cost of contracted Tectonic in certain Gen AI engagements where revenue contribution is still building slowly.

As these factors reverse (revenue from these engagements coming through, workforce transformation benefits realized), they will largely offset the impact of the annual wage hike cycle in Q2, keeping margins stable, unlike the historically declining Q2 EBITDA margin trend.

subsections.label: Currency/hedge accounting
points: Company moved to designated hedge accounting last quarter per accounting standards; mark-to-market volatility from sudden dollar-rupee or other currency movements will no longer impact results going forward.
Current undesignated hedges remain material until December 2026; company continues to hedge as in the past and believes currency volatility will not impact operating margin going forward.
Revenue from U.S. dollar is 84%-85% of total revenue.

subsections.label: Receivables and credit risk management
points: More than 90% of business comes from top 20 pharma (Fortune 500/1000) as well as multibillion-dollar mid-tier pharma companies with strong balance sheets.
Credit risk has not been significant historically; minimal provisions or bad debt write-offs even going back 27 years.
Strong governance processes and innovative deal structures used in commercial terms with biotech/emerging pharma where risk profile differs from traditional clients.
Company monitors performance on outcome-based model contracts, including getting customer sign-offs and interim markers ticked off as engagements progress in the evolving Gen AI environment.
DSO (net of unearned/unbilled revenue) was 67 days, 4 days higher QoQ.

subsections.label: Outcome-based contracts financial mechanics
points: Outcome-based contracts represent ~60-ish% of business, consistent with the 60% figure highlighted during the IPO process.
FTE component of a typical $1M-$3M outcome-based deal ramps up over 3 to 4 quarters.
Large omnichannel engagement deal has a revenue recognition delay of 3 quarters.
Client has been sharing revenue uptick data under the outcome-based model for 5 months, with encouraging results.

subsections.label: Capitalization policy
points: Company continues to invest heavily in proprietary tech stack (data layer, Cortex context layer, workflows) and has ratcheted up investment in the data layer.

As a practice, these investments are expensed rather than capitalized; management notes there is technically a case for capitalization but they continue to expense to keep P&L and balance sheet clean.

subsections.label: Growth since listing
points: Cash position has grown over 30% since listing (2 years, since Q1 FY25), with cash & cash equivalents plus investments at INR 14,602 million.
Total revenue grew 57% since listing (2 years).
Revenue per employee grew 25% over the last 2 years.

subsections.label: Deal wins - Enterprise Commercial
points: Signed 1 deal in $3M-$5M range where a top 5 customer selected Indegene to migrate their content platform.
Signed 4 deals with annual contracts in $1M-$3M range: three in commercial and one in medical.
Deal 1: extension of the Tectonic engagement with the largest customer — Germany engagement expanded to Spain.
Deal 2: a top 20 pharma company chose Indegene to support its brands across the U.S. for creative and digital production using omnichannel assets.
Deal 3: a biotech company engaged Indegene to enable its content platform end-to-end from assessment and maturity through build and migration.
Deal 4 (medical): a biotech company brought in Indegene for medical writing for submissions.

Additionally won a couple of sub-million-dollar deals viewed as first phase of larger engagements with potential to grow into multimillion-dollar relationships: one with a midsized European company supporting launch readiness with scope to extend into data analytics; another where a top 20 pharma company selected Indegene for a change management consulting assignment with potential to set up a global content factory for their international business unit.
Active client base reached 105, up 14 QoQ; $10M-$25M revenue cohort grew to 9 clients with 2 new customers added.
Portfolio value under management for the pharma brand-management deal exceeds $1 billion.

subsections.label: Demand environment
points: Customers are genuinely excited about AI potential; when ready to move, excitement translates to real expanding work, but enterprise adoption remains measured and pace of change on the ground is slower — viewed by Indegene as an opportunity rather than a concern.

Large Tectonic engagement in Germany (announced Q4) illustrates this dynamic: offtake on existing scope has been measured, but customer confidence was strong enough to expand into a further region (Spain) during the quarter.
This pattern is viewed as typical in new technology adoption cycles, favoring a partner that can understand the domain, engineer trust, and operationalize AI at scale.

subsections.label: Offerings gaining traction
points: Agentic AOR: building on proof of concept completed with a multinational pharmaceutical company (mentioned in Q4 earnings call); now in advanced discussions to close the next phase of that engagement.
Regulatory One-Click Submission: engagement with a midsized pharma company continues to expand in scope, taking on new reports, becoming a blueprint for the industry.
Continuing to scale homegrown platforms Medico-Legal Review and Medical Writing, where domain expertise is embedded in technology, central to delivering an output rather than headcount.

subsections.label: Growth since listing
points: Total revenue up 57% from Q1 FY25 (time of listing, ~2 years ago).
Active client base grew from 65 to 105; million-dollar-plus clients from 36 to 54; revenue from beyond-top-20 accounts became more than 2.5x.
Revenue per employee grew 25% in last 2 years to over $77,000; share of delivery talent with healthcare expertise rose to 29% from 22%; cash position strengthened by over 30% in same period.

subsections.label: Segment mix
points: Segment and geography mix was stable in the quarter: Enterprise Commercial (largest segment) contributed 70.6% of revenue; North America (largest geography) contributed 75.1% of revenue.

Share from largest customer cohorts declined even as those cohorts continue to grow in absolute terms, indicating healthy diversification, as accounts beyond top 20 nearly doubled YoY in rupee terms and now represent 33.4% (more than a third) of total revenue.

subsections.label: Client base widening vs deepening
points: Since listing (2 years), active client base grew from 65 to 105; million dollar-plus clients grew from 36 to 54; revenue from accounts beyond top 20 became more than 2.5x.

Deepening of top accounts is still ahead — largest clients have not yet fully shown up in these numbers; intent, opportunity and momentum are there, with evidence sitting in pipelines expected to convert to revenue soon.
Priority is to move the whole customer pyramid: get into first $50 million accounts and move more accounts to $25 million bucket.

subsections.label: Outcome/output-based contract mix
points: Company already operates at ~60% output-plus-outcome-based contracts, a level other service companies aspire to; this is not new — was highlighted during IPO process.

A significant portion of dedicated FTEs outside the 60% are standing in FTE contracts supporting these output/outcome-based engagements — specialized roles like omnichannel orchestrators, digital specialists, brand liaisons, regulatory experts across US, multiple European countries, Japan, China.
Trend of outcome-based contracts (incentives linked to client's true revenue uptick) is expanding due to breadth of capabilities and trust built with clients.

Most engagements are hybrid contracts with an FTE component that kicks in early (within a month of signing), with output-based revenues flowing as volume builds, typically taking 3-4 quarters to ramp to full potential for a typical $1M-$4M deal.

The large omnichannel engagement (>$10M ACV, announced Q3 FY26) is a pure outcome-based contract with no FTE component; revenue recognition deferred ~3 quarters based on client acceptance of outcomes measured quarterly and trued up annually; recognition expected from Q3 FY27.
Client has been sharing revenue uptick data for 5 months, with encouraging numbers reported by management.
Net revenue retention is more than 100%.

subsections.label: Renewals
points: Deal wins discussed on calls are net new business; renewals are not called out separately.

Renewal cycles typically run January to December, with cycles of 3-4 and even 5 years for some customers; volume fluctuations and periodic rate renegotiations occur but no major enterprise deal has been lost in renewals.
Annual renewal volume fluctuates 2-3% in absolute terms, plus or minus net retention.

subsections.label: Industry backdrop
points: Global pharma industry showing resilient growth in 2026, with top 20 pharma (core customer base) outpacing broader industry — top 20 global pharma cumulative revenue growth of 10-12% YoY in Q1 CY2026 vs. mid to high single-digit growth for the global pharma industry in H1 2026.

Anti-obesity remains primary growth driver, but breadth of momentum stands out — immunology, oncology, mental health all growing in double digits; 8 of the top 25 biopharma companies posted double-digit Q1 revenue growth.

Only a handful of companies with heavy loss-of-exclusivity (LoE) exposure or waning COVID-19 sales saw declines; smaller biotechs had a mixed first half with selective funding/IPO conditions, though an uptick in partnerships and M&A provided relief.
Big pharma biopharma acquisition spend exceeded $100 billion in H1, on pace for largest deal value since 2019, as companies buy pipeline to address patent cliffs.
Outlook for H2 and beyond remains constructive with analysts projecting sustained mid-single-digit global pharma growth through 2027.

No major regulatory items of note this quarter; industry navigating pricing pressure and loss of exclusivity via two-pronged response: (1) mega brands facing LoE risk reimagining marketing spend to maximize portfolio economics — benefits Indegene directly (e.g., the $10M+ omnichannel deal won in Q3); (2) drug pipeline remains near historic highs as industry shifts to advancing multiple candidates rather than betting on single blockbusters, requiring more efficient commercial operations across wider portfolios — AI seen as key enabler.

subsections.label: Indegene EDGE differentiation
points: Company describes itself as a new category, not comparable to IT services, agency, or CRO models; differentiated via 'Indegene EDGE': E-Embedded revenue partner, D-Deep domain expertise, G-Gen AI disruptor, E-Engagement model.

Embedded revenue partner: works inside clients' revenue engine (commercial/medical functions); sits on the revenue/growth side of budget (unlike IT vendors on cost side); savings from productivity/AI are redeployed by clients into more volume/content/channels returning as more work.

Deep domain expertise: built over 27 years in life sciences, more than 29% of people from healthcare background (up from 22% two years ago); work is judgment-intensive, heavily regulated, less susceptible to automation; every new technology (including Gen AI) compounds on domain knowledge.

Gen AI disruptor: Gen AI reshapes economics on demand side (rising complexity/content volumes/compliance push centralization, met at enterprise level by reengineering end-to-end processes and taking wallet share from incumbent agencies/CROs) and economics side (Gen AI drives price deflation; incumbents lack growth headroom to offset falling prices, while Indegene is large enough to serve globally and nimble enough to convert deflation into new volumes/share gains).

Engagement model: built around outputs/outcomes, not headcount; most revenue outcome-aligned; efficiency gains flow to bottom line, incentivizing faster tech adoption; reinforced by single integrated global delivery model versus scattered/local agency model.

subsections.label: Gen AI technology strategy
points: Strategy is nuanced — focused on solving customer problems (reducing cost of asset development, building IP for automated physician outreach, automating clinical study reports/protocols across ~200 reports) rather than broad employee AI training.

Technology stack: bottom infra layer is data assets (own data assets like Invisage, physician profiling; BioPharm acquisition added a data asset now integrated; buying/partnering for additional data; public data sources; own data mining) — called 'Indegene data universe'.

Second layer: Cortex platform for knowledge engineering, separating SME layer from technical layer so SMEs build workflows/knowledge engineering independent of which model (open weight or frontier) is used; architecture designed to not be wedded to one model, iterating based on accuracy/cost per use case.
Third layer: agent layer (Content Super App, Medical Writing platform) containing multiple agents delivering different outcomes (e.g., within Agentic AOR).
Top layer: Transform AI — workflows and skill sets required to deliver differentiated outcomes.

On data protection: larger pharma clients protect their own data via contracts; Indegene's systems can learn from data but it remains client's data — negotiated in every contract; broader market trend is larger pharma companies wanting their own open-weight models deployed on their own infrastructure rather than relying on frontier models that could access their data and compete with them.

AI is embedded in everything Indegene does rather than broken out as a separate revenue line; company has been on the AI journey (NLP, machine learning, computer vision) for more than a decade, predating Gen AI/GPT-3; content volumes increased 5-7x while cost per unit continued to decline via these methods.

subsections.label: Execution priorities (per CEO)
points: Continue to execute GTM engine, deepening client relationships; move the customer pyramid — get into first $50 million accounts, move more accounts to the $25 million bucket.
Continue expanding customer base — on track.
Long-term: continue investing in capabilities and tech stack, building end-to-end solutions for clients to adopt AI meaningfully and drive outcomes rather than provide point solutions.

Current-quarter priorities: convert existing pipeline (including with largest customers) into revenue, and get margin profile back with tight control — confidence is based on contracts already in hand, not future wins.

subsections.label: Investment priorities
points: Organic and inorganic capability investments over the past 4 years, combined with technology investments in Content Super App/agents and proven ability to run global commercial operations at scale, create a differentiated proposition.

Company moving upstream, capturing larger share of value chain — from running content operations and omnichannel campaigns at scale to bringing upstream capabilities like brand strategies and creatives as the same accountable partner.

subsections.label: BioPharm integration
points: BioPharm is now reasonably well integrated into the business; company no longer breaks out organic vs inorganic growth or BioPharm contribution separately (previously disclosed for two quarters) as it has become difficult to peel out BioPharm from other business.
Both organic and BioPharm are now in the base from a sequential comparison perspective.

subsections.label: Regulatory/policy risk
points: Company monitors the regulatory environment and policy decisions, especially in the U.S., which impacts the industry the most.
Currently, policy outlook is stable; drug pricing and MFN-related decisions are largely behind the industry; new launch pipeline is healthy and robust, but this remains a risk area to watch.

subsections.label: Currency/forex risk
points: Company moved to designated hedge accounting last quarter; this removes future mark-to-market volatility impact from sudden dollar-rupee or other currency movements.

Current undesignated hedges remain material until December 2026 and are the residual accounting exposure to watch; company continues to hedge as in the past and believes currency volatility will not impact operating margin going forward.
Prior quarter (Q4 FY26) carried an adverse ~240 bps impact from mark-to-market of undesignated forward contracts ahead of adopting hedge accounting, due to forex volatility.

subsections.label: Credit/receivables risk
points: More than 90% of business comes from top 20 pharma (Fortune 500/1000) and mid-tier multibillion-dollar pharma companies with strong balance sheets; credit risk has not been significant historically, with minimal provisions/bad debt write-offs even going back 27 years.
Innovative deal structures and strong governance used for biotech/emerging pharma clients where risk profile could differ.
Monitoring performance on outcome-based model contracts requires customer sign-offs and interim markers, which is an area of ongoing focus given evolving Gen AI needs.

subsections.label: FY27 outlook
points: Company expects organic growth in FY27 to be better than FY26, with acceleration anticipated in the second half.

Priority is twofold: deepen existing relationships and convert pipeline (including largest clients) into signed deals and revenue; and bring margins back to historically operated levels — both expected to start coming together in H2 FY27.

Outcome-based omnichannel engagement begins contributing from Q3, aiding both growth and profitability, alongside other deal wins scaling more meaningfully; combined with productivity initiatives, margin recovery expected to become clearly visible.

Management states confidence rests not on a single quarter but on durability of the business model over a long horizon; industry growing, large enterprises within it growing faster, AI a structural tailwind.

subsections.label: Margin guidance detail
points: Original guidance (Aug 2025/Q2 FY26 call): 150 bps margin impact starting Q3 FY26 from GTM/tech investments, with 6-8 quarter normalization period.
Updated guidance: normalization now expected in 6 quarters (narrower than the original range), i.e., by Q4 FY27 — confirmed as 3 quarters from the current call (Q1 FY27).
This is despite additional investment in large deals not originally factored into the guidance, per management confirmation.
EBITDA in H2 FY27 expected back in the 19%-20% historical range, with the inflection point at Q3 FY27; management states nothing this quarter changes that expectation and conviction has increased.
By Q4 FY27, margin expected to be in the 19%-20% range (confirmed in Q&A).

guidance_ledger.statement: We expect our organic growth in FY27 to be better than FY26, and we anticipate an acceleration in the second half.
Through the inflection point in Q3 FY27, the EBITDA in H2 FY27 will be back in the range that we have operated in the past, that is 19% to 20%.

With the current and anticipated momentum in FY27, we are on track. And the margin normalization is expected in 6 quarters, that is by Q4 of FY27 (revised down from the earlier 6-8 quarter guidance given in Aug 2025).

With revenue expected to be recognized starting Q3 FY27, it adds to our H2 revenues with costs already being incurred in the P&L, and hence, most of that revenue will flow straight to the bottom line.
Analysts projecting sustained mid-single-digit global pharma growth through 2027.
Our net retention has been more than 100% for our customers.

key_takeaways: Q1 revenues came in at INR10,631 million, growing 39.7% year-on-year and 6% quarter-on-quarter. This is the strongest quarter-on-quarter growth we have delivered in a first quarter in four years.
Growth was led by accounts beyond our top 20, which now contribute more than a third of our total revenues.
Our active client base crossed the milestone of 100, reaching 105, and we have added 2 customers to the $10 million to $25 million bucket, taking that cohort to 9.
Our revenue per employee is approximately $77,000 on a trailing 12-month basis, which remains industry-leading.
EBITDA for the quarter was INR1,795 million at a margin of 16.9%, 50 basis points higher quarter-on-quarter on a reported basis.
PBT came in at INR1,527 million, up 45.3% sequentially; PAT grew 45.9% sequentially to INR1,162 million at 10.9% of revenue, up approximately 300 basis points sequentially.

Margin normalization is now expected in 6 quarters (from October 2025), that is by Q4 of FY27, narrower than the earlier 6-8 quarter guidance, despite additional investment in large deals not originally factored in.
Through the inflection point in Q3 FY27, EBITDA in H2 FY27 will be back in the range the company has operated in the past, that is 19% to 20%.
We expect our organic growth in FY27 to be better than FY26, and we anticipate an acceleration in the second half.
