But this is despite the fact that you have invested in some of the large deals which maybe you did not factor it in when you gave this guidance. Is that fair?
What was the organic growth this quarter? And how much was from BioPharm?
What was the constant currency growth for this quarter? I don't find that number in the presentation.

As we plan to data mine our customers and scale the business, what is the percentage we are looking at these outcome-based deals? Is that going to be the norm for the industry and us as we plan to scale?

You have recently highlighted your Gen AI platform as the next phase of growth. Could you quantify what percentage of revenue is currently generated through AI-led platform engagements and how you expect that mix to evolve over the next 2 to 3 years?

SHILCTECH.about: Shilchar Technologies is engaged in the business of manufacturing Electronics & Telecom and Power & Distribution transformers. The company has recently ventured into the manufacturing of Ferrite transformers. [1]

quarters.summary: Q1 FY27 was a softer quarter for Shilchar Technologies, impacted by the ongoing West Asia crisis which affected Middle East exports through steeply elevated shipping costs and caused a sudden domestic raw material price escalation. Management expects overall business momentum to be notably better in Q2 vs Q1, with exports possibly continuing to see impact from elevated shipping costs if the West Asia situation persists, while domestic visibility is better. The FY27 annual revenue outlook remains unchanged (target of Rs. 800 crores), with the company expecting to operate its existing 7,500 MVA capacity at almost full utilization; the Phase-3 expansion (adding ~6,500 MVA, taking total to 14,000 MVA) remains on track for commissioning in April 2027, with a possibility of completing slightly earlier.

key_figures.label: Estimated revenue loss due to shipment delays
Raw material price rise passed on to customers (orders executed in Q4/Q1)
EBITDA margin difference between domestic and export clientele

subsections.label: Margin pressure drivers
points: Profitability margins for the quarter reflect both a lower export mix and partial pass-through of higher raw material prices.

Passing on the sudden escalation in commodity prices for existing orders arising from the West Asia crisis took longer than anticipated; negotiations with customers extended through much of the quarter, resulting in slower dispatches in Q1.
The situation was more severe in April and May and has eased off in recent months.

Whatever orders were on hand to be executed in Q4/Q1 saw only about 50-60% of the price rise passed on to customers; whatever is being executed now is at current market prices, so no problem is expected in achieving EBITDA on those orders.
Consolidated EBITDA margin difference between domestic and international clientele is about 10%.

subsections.label: Investor data requests
points: Revenue breakup between exports and domestic for Q1 FY27 vs Q1 FY26, and inventory days/receivable days for Q1 FY27, were not disclosed on the call; management said this information would be provided via email upon request.

subsections.label: Order book composition and execution
points: Order book of almost close to Rs 500 crores as of today, over and above whatever has already been shipped out till yesterday; described as a very strong order book.
Lot of new inquiries are on hand for which the company is negotiating; more orders are expected in coming days.
Order book split is almost 30% export and 70% domestic as of now.
These orders are mostly for Q2, Q3, and some for Q4 also; company is fully booked for Q2.
Expecting more orders which will again be for Q3 and Q4.

No orders are getting cancelled; since products are custom-based, cancellation does not exist — orders are just getting pushed out with delayed delivery dates (e.g., instead of June delivery, July or August).
Current order book orders are at current raw material prices, described as good orders with reasonable/quite good margins.
Q1 margins are expected to be exceeded in Q2/Q3 — management said margins will be higher, hoping to achieve more EBITDA.

subsections.label: Underlying demand
points: This is a cost and logistics issue and not a demand issue; underlying customer demand in both export regions (Middle East, North America) remains firm, but customers are currently lifting the bare minimum volume they need and are not stocking.

Customers prefer the company because of quality, service, and shorter lead time; once the situation normalizes, the company is confident of getting that export business back, as customers are not buying from alternate cheaper sources — they are simply being cautious given uncertainty.
Demand across key domestic and export markets remains strong, and overall business outlook continues to be robust.

key_figures.label: Time to prototype larger transformers post production start

subsections.label: Phase-3 expansion progress
points: Expansion Phase-3, adding about 6,500 MVA capacity, remains on track for commissioning in April 2027.
Civil foundation work has been completed; PEB erection and utility infrastructure work are progressing well; all equipment have been ordered.
Construction is going on in full swing; company does not anticipate any delay and may complete the project slightly earlier than projected.

Once the facility is ready for production, the company will start producing existing-range transformers first; the larger-size (higher KV class, e.g., 220 KV) product marketing will start aggressively thereafter, but customer audit, approval process and type testing take time, so larger capacity transformer orders will come a little later.
Once production starts, prototyping for bigger transformers will take around three to four months.
Company is already discussing with a few customers on the bigger transformers.

subsections.label: Capacity utilization outlook
points: Annual outlook for FY27 remains unchanged; company expects to operate its existing 7,500 MVA capacity at almost full utilization for FY27.
Q1 FY27 capacity utilization was only around 60-65%.
New facility will drive the next leg of growth for FY28 onwards.

subsections.label: Further expansion plans
points: Company has purchased an additional about four and a half acres of land adjacent to its existing land at Gavasad (common wall), and is planning further expansion in that area.

Management did not disclose the type of product, KV class, or capacity for this further expansion; plans will be firmed up once the current expansion is completed or near completion, with additional plans to follow.

subsections.label: Export cost impact
points: Container/shipping costs have risen between three to five times for certain geographies compared to pre-crisis levels, materially increasing the landed cost for customers and leading to slower pickup in export dispatches.
Increase in shipping costs is not limited to the Middle East; costs to North America have also risen significantly due to ongoing geopolitical uncertainty.
Most export terms are ex-works, so there is a significant increase in cost of procurement for customers, leading to deferment of orders.

Approximately 90% of export orders are structured such that shipping cost is not on the company's account — an increase in shipping cost does not reduce the company's margin directly, but raises landed cost for the customer.
Overall shipping cost has gone up for all export geographies the company serves — North America, Africa, and Middle East.
Company exports everywhere: North America, Middle East, and somewhat Africa.

subsections.label: Geographic mix shift
points: Geographic mix may change depending on the present situation; if the Middle East situation improves and shipping costs come down, exports are expected to return to normal levels.
To compensate for the export slowdown, the company is concentrating on the domestic market and getting more orders from local customers.
Based on current situation, domestic sales will be higher than exports for FY27 revenue mix; if the situation changes, focus will shift back from domestic to export.

Company took proactive action to shift focus from export to domestic once shipping costs disrupted exports, but since transformers are custom-made products, it takes minimum lead time of about 10 to 12 weeks or even 16 weeks to get and execute new domestic orders.

subsections.label: Domestic pricing environment
points: No pressure of lower margins in the domestic transformer market; domestic market conditions are normal, similar to about two years back and last year, with no change.

subsections.label: Competitive positioning
points: Company is competitive on quality, service, and shorter lead time versus alternate sources; customers are not buying from cheaper alternate sources, they are simply being cautious.

subsections.label: Long-term market strategy
points: For new higher-KV-class projects (e.g. 220 KV), initial margins will be lower mainly to create references and penetrate the market.

Going forward, company will continue its policy of not doing business with any state utility companies and will concentrate more on the export market once it has enough references within the domestic market.
Initially there will be low profitability in the new higher-KV segment but better margins are anticipated going forward.

key_figures.label: Shipping costs to North America increase

subsections.label: West Asia crisis and shipping cost escalation
points: Financial Year 2027 commenced on a softer note, shaped largely by the continuing effects of the crisis in West Asia, which affected Middle East exports directly and, through a sudden increase in raw material prices, affected domestic businesses.
Export recovery has taken longer than originally expected at the time of the Q4 call, primarily due to a persistent increase in shipping costs through Q1.
This is characterized as a cost and logistics issue, not a demand issue.

Annual report for FY26 (released mid-July) had indicated recovery from April onwards and was positive for Q1, based on information available when it was prepared in early June, when there were announcements that the war was ending and MOUs were being signed — this did not materialize, causing the mismatch between the annual report commentary and actual Q1 outcomes.

Domestic raw material price escalation arising from the West Asia crisis required prolonged negotiation with customers to pass through, extending through much of the quarter and resulting in slower dispatches.

subsections.label: Order push-out risk (not cancellation)
points: Orders affected by shipping cost issues are not cancelled, only pushed out with delayed delivery dates; since products are custom-based, cancellation does not exist as an option for customers.

subsections.label: Revenue and margin outlook
points: Company is on track with whatever it has targeted for top line for FY27 and does not anticipate any problem in achieving that target (Rs. 800 crores).
Overall business momentum is expected to be notably better in Q2 compared to Q1.
Exports may continue to see some impact from elevated shipping costs if the West Asia situation remains unchanged; better visibility exists on the domestic side, which should support the top line.
Company remains on track with its revenue ambitions for the year, although geographic mix may change if the West Asia situation persists.

On margins: if the situation becomes normal and exports come back online as in previous years, company is confident it can maintain the same profitability as in previous years; if the company remains more reliant on the local market, there will be a slight dip in profitability — outcome depends on how the geopolitical situation develops.
Management expects to achieve more EBITDA in Q2/Q3 versus Q1, as current order book orders are booked at current raw material prices with reasonable margins.

subsections.label: Capacity outlook
points: Annual outlook for FY27 remains unchanged; company plans to operate its existing 7,500 MVA capacity at almost full utilization.
New Phase-3 facility (adding 6,500 MVA, total 14,000 MVA) remains on track for commissioning in April 2027 and may be completed slightly earlier than projected.
New facility will drive the next leg of growth from FY28 onwards.

guidance_ledger.statement: We are on track with whatever we have targeted in terms of the top line for FY27 and we don't anticipate any problem in achieving that (target of Rs. 800 crores).

If the situation becomes normal and exports come back online as in previous years, we are confident we will be able to maintain the same profitability as previous years. But in case that does not happen and we are more reliant on the local market, there will be a slight dip.
We are planning to utilize very close to 100% of our existing 7,500 MVA capacity for year 2026-2027.

Expansion Phase-3, adding about 6,500 MVA capacity, remains on track for commissioning in April 2027; civil foundation completed, PEB erection and utility infrastructure progressing well, all equipment ordered; may complete slightly earlier than projected.

We expect overall business momentum to be notably better in Q2 compared to Q1, while exports may continue to see some impact from elevated shipping costs if the situation in West Asia remains unchanged.
Order book orders are at current raw material prices with reasonable margins; Q2/Q3 margins and EBITDA expected to be higher than Q1.

Initially margins will be lower mainly to create references and penetrate the new higher-KV market; going forward better margins are anticipated once enough domestic references exist and focus shifts more to export.

We have purchased additional land adjacent to existing land at Gavasad and are planning for further expansion; will not disclose product type, KV class or capacity yet, plans to follow once current expansion nears completion.

Once production starts at new facility, prototyping for bigger transformers will take about three to four months; larger capacity transformer orders will come a little later due to customer audit/approval/type testing; already discussing with a few customers on bigger transformers.
Around 7,000 MVA targeted for FY27, up from ~6,000 MVA in FY26.

key_takeaways: For Q1 FY27, Shilchar Technologies reported revenue for operation of Rs. 134.60 crores and EBITDA for the quarter stood at Rs. 29.23 crores. The profit after tax stood at Rs. 20.86 crores.

The Financial Year 2027 has commenced on a softer note. The quarter was shaped largely by the continuing effects of the crisis in West Asia, which affected our Middle East exports directly and through a sudden increase of price for certain raw materials, which affected our domestic businesses.

Container costs have risen between three to five times for certain geographies as compared to levels before the crisis. This has materially increased the landed cost of our customers and has led to a slower pickup in export dispatches.

I would like to emphasize that this is a cost and logistic issue and not a demand issue... Underlying customer demand in both regions remains firm, but customers are currently lifting the bare minimum volume they need.

Looking ahead, we expect overall business momentum to be notably better in Q2 compared to Q1, while exports may continue to see some impact from elevated shipping costs if the situation in West Asia remains unchanged.

Our CAPEX project, our expansion Phase-3, which will add about 6,500 MVA capacity, remains on track for commissioning in April 2027... Our annual outlook remains unchanged for FY27, and we expect to operate our existing 7,500 MVA capacity at almost full utilization.
We have an order book of almost very close to 500 crores as of today... I would say it's almost like 30% export and 70% domestic as of now.
No, in Q1 I think we did only around 60-65% of the capacity utilization.
Like I said that, you know, out of 500, almost 70% is local and 30% is exported. And no orders are getting cancelled. I mean, they are just getting pushed out.
pressing_questions: Is there a manner to quantify the revenue loss for Q1 FY27 due to the shipment delays? And also, what is our revenue run rate for this year — would management like to revisit their guidance of Rs. 800 crores of revenue?

Our annual report FY26 (released mid-July) highlighted recovery from April onwards and was positive in tone for Q1, while the recent quarter presentation indicates recovery in exports has taken longer than expected due to persistently higher shipping costs. Could management quantify the impact of the West Asia crisis and elevated trade costs on export revenue in FY27, and explain why it was pictured differently in the annual report?

Why did management not proactively ship the demand/order base from Middle East markets to domestic markets in April, given the war situation was already known, resulting in both underutilized capacity and a margin hit in Q1?
What gives management the confidence that the company won't lose export revenue permanently, considering it is not able to service client requirements in this demand-led scenario?

What is the margin visibility specifically on the Rs. 500 crore order book, given it is now more domestic-inclined versus the previous 50-50 domestic-export mix that historically supported higher margins?

quarters.summary: Shilchar expects to resume its growth trajectory from Q1 FY27 after a weak Q4 FY26 caused by temporary US tariff-related order softness and Middle East logistics disruption; management guided FY27 revenue of ~INR800 crores (with room up to INR850-900 crores), maintaining EBITDA margins around 29%-31%, backed by an order book of ~INR452 crores and order visibility of ~INR800 crores for FY27, while the Gavasad expansion (adding 6,500 MVA, taking capacity to 14,000 MVA) remains on track for commissioning in April 2027, with full ramp-up impact expected in FY29-FY30.

subsections.label: Q4 margin compression drivers
points: Gross margin compression in Q4 was driven by lower export mix (export could not be shipped in March due to Middle East crisis) which changed the raw-material consumption ratio versus domestic sales.
Raw material prices rose generally, and specifically oil prices spiked sharply in March, adding to cost pressure.
Export business carries higher margin than domestic business; the shortfall in March export dispatches directly reduced EBITDA.
Management stated that absent the Middle East disruption and RM price rises, margins would have been similar to Q1, Q2 and Q3 levels.

subsections.label: Balance sheet and capital allocation
points: Company remains debt free.
Part of the INR246 crore cash balance will be used to finance ongoing capex.
The Gavasad expansion capex of ~INR120 crores is being funded entirely through internal accruals.

subsections.label: Price revision negotiations
points: Management has approached almost all customers for price increases/revisions; active dialogues are ongoing.
Some customers have already agreed to price increases and supply has resumed to them; others remain under discussion.
For existing orders on fixed price terms, company is negotiating price rises citing force majeure conditions given the sudden, drastic RM price increase.
Some orders are based on a PV (price variation) clause, under which pricing is charged per applicable index at time of dispatch, removing margin risk on those orders.

Suppliers of copper/aluminium were also unable to honor previously booked lower prices and are demanding price rises from Shilchar, creating a unique/force-majeure situation despite the company's normal hedging practice of booking copper/aluminium immediately upon order receipt.

subsections.label: Demand recovery and drivers
points: Order inflows from US customers, which had moderated due to tariff policy uncertainty (specifically in Q3), recovered through Q4.
With subsequent US tariff policy amendments and firm demand outlook, both order intake and deliveries have picked up notably in Q1 FY27.

Domestic demand has remained firm, underpinned by India's record 55 GW of renewable energy capacity commissioned in FY26, sustaining strong order inflows in the domestic renewable transformer business.
Order visibility of ~INR800 crores for FY27 supported by robust inquiries from both domestic and export customers.
Global transformer demand remains favourable; domestic investments in grid infrastructure, T&D capacity, and renewables build-out provide strong visibility.
Management believes there is enough demand/orders in the market for all players despite industry-wide capacity expansion, and is confident of securing orders to utilize new capacity fully.
Demand in distribution transformer segment is good with limited competitive intensity and no current overcapacity situation, per management.

subsections.label: Capacity utilization clarification
points: Capacity utilization figures in the presentation are based on dispatches, not production; actual production was higher and excess was carried as closing stock as of 31 March 2026, to be dispatched in the coming year.
79% utilization / ~6,000 MVA reflects dispatches done in FY26; production-based utilization is higher than 79% (exact figure not disclosed).
Had Middle East shipments in March not been disrupted, utilization would have been ~82-83%.

Management considers 90-95% utilization to be a good/optimal level for a facility and plans to target that range in the coming year; 100% utilization was never targeted as it is impractical given maintenance/downtime needs.

subsections.label: Higher voltage class capability and approvals
points: Current manufacturing capability is up to 132 kV class transformers.
The new facility being built will have capacity to manufacture transformers up to 160 MVA, 220 kV class.
Once the new facility is ready, the company will pursue various approvals, including PGCIL approval, for the higher voltage class transformers.

Approval process involves registration and customer facility audits before actual higher-voltage production can start; meanwhile the facility will not be left idle and will take up more solar and wind transformer orders until power transformer approvals/orders come through, after which solar/wind transformer output will be reduced in favor of power transformers.

points: Civil foundation work for the site is completed.

All major production equipment has been ordered.
Capex of approximately INR120 crores is being funded entirely through internal accruals.
For FY27, the company expects to run its existing 7,500 MVA capacity at almost full utilization; the new facility will drive the next leg of growth from FY27-28 onwards.
Production at the new facility is expected to start from April 2027 onwards; full ramp-up impact of the new facility is expected in FY29-FY30.
Company has plans for further expansion beyond the 6,500 MVA addition and will announce details in the future; will not wait for the new facility to be fully utilized before planning next expansion.

subsections.label: Bushings supply for 220 kV transformers
points: There is an industry-wide shortage/long lead time concern for bushings needed for 220 kV transformers.
Current supplier is Yash Highvoltage, based in Baroda, with whom the company has a good business relationship.
Company also plans to import bushings from China.
Management characterizes the situation as a long lead time issue rather than an outright shortage, manageable by maintaining some inventory.

subsections.label: US tariff impact and recovery
points: Uncertainty around US tariff policy in preceding quarters moderated order intake from US customers, specifically in Q3 FY26.
US announced a 50% tariff on Indian goods in August (prior year), causing loss of some orders; tariff has since come down to 10%.
With tariffs no longer differentially applied (applicable to each country equally), Shilchar is competing easily again and has resumed getting orders from US customers.
Opportunities in the US market over the next three years are expected to be great, with quite good growth expected in US exports.

subsections.label: Middle East disruption and recovery
points: A significant volume of shipments scheduled for delivery to Middle East customers in March 2026 could not be dispatched due to the crisis in West Asia and resulting logistics disruptions.
These shipments were deferred, not cancelled; dispatches to the region resumed in April and the situation has improved considerably since then.
Lower export mix in Q4 due to Middle East disruption is cited as the reason for the order book's export share (30-32%) being lower than historical levels.

subsections.label: TAM / market size for inverter duty transformers (IDT)
points: The IDT (inverter duty transformer) market opportunity for the company currently exists mainly in India and some Middle East countries.
India's IDT market opportunity is linked to the government's target of ~50-55 GW of renewable energy capacity.

subsections.label: Commodity inflation
points: Transformer oil prices have roughly doubled since February 2026 to the call date and have not subsided.
Other raw material commodity prices have increased in the range of 10% to 25%.
Management stated it is difficult to predict future commodity price trends; if the Middle East crisis eases, prices may revert toward original levels, but this is uncertain.
Transformer oil cost is estimated at 8% to 12% of total transformer cost, varying by transformer rating and application.

subsections.label: Inventory management
points: Total inventory (including work-in-progress) stood at close to INR100 crores as of 31 March 2026.
During the Middle East shipping disruption in early March, the company stopped converting production into finished goods to avoid storage issues, instead holding it as work-in-progress.
Dispatches resumed in April 2026 once the shipping situation normalized.

subsections.label: Raw material hedging policy
points: Standard company policy is to immediately book copper or aluminium upon receiving an order, taking no price risk under normal conditions.

The current situation is described as unique/force majeure: even suppliers who had booked raw material at lower prices for placed orders are unable to honor those prices and are demanding price rises from Shilchar.
Some orders carry a PV (price variation) clause, under which the applicable index price at time of dispatch is charged to the customer, removing this margin risk for those specific orders.

Despite industry-wide capacity expansion by major transformer players, management is confident that market demand is strong enough to absorb new supply without difficulty in securing orders.

subsections.label: Future growth vision
points: Once the new 6,500 MVA facility is fully utilized, company can achieve turnover of around INR1,500 crores.

Company has plans for further expansion beyond the current expansion and will announce details in future; growth driver is expected to be a combination of domestic and export markets (not solely US or Middle East).

subsections.label: External disruptions in FY26
points: US tariff policy uncertainty (including a prior 50% tariff on Indian goods, since reduced to 10%) moderated order intake from US customers in Q3 FY26, weighing on Q4 dispatches.

Crisis in West Asia (Middle East) caused logistics disruptions that prevented dispatch of a significant volume of March 2026 shipments to Middle East customers; these were deferred, not cancelled, and dispatches resumed in April 2026.

Sharp, sudden commodity inflation, especially transformer oil (doubling since February) and other commodities (10-25% increase), created a force-majeure-like situation where even suppliers who had booked material could not honor prior pricing, requiring price revision negotiations with customers.
Rupee depreciation was also flagged (by an analyst) as a factor increasing input costs, particularly on imports.

Industry-wide capacity expansion by multiple transformer players raises the question of whether demand growth will keep pace with new supply, though management expressed confidence that demand remains strong enough to absorb expansion.

Growth in FY27 is not expected to be very substantial since the company is running at almost full existing capacity; a multiple/step-up in growth is expected once new capacity is added in FY27-28, with full ramp-up effect by FY29-FY30.
Management will do its best to maintain or even increase EBITDA margin from FY26 levels (29%) into FY27, targeting 29-31%.
Volume growth guided at ~7,000 MVA for FY27, up from ~6,000 MVA in FY26.

Management is confident about Q1 FY27 performance, citing resumed shipping to Middle East, a strong order book, and recovering US order intake, though declined to provide specific numbers for April 2026 or first-half FY27 split.

key_takeaways: For the full year '26, Shilchar Technologies delivered revenue from operations of INR652 crores, reflecting around 5% growth year-on-year with EBITDA of INR190 crores and an EBITDA margin of 29%.
Profit after tax for the year stood at INR158 crores, up 8% on year-on-year basis with an EPS of INR138.
On a five year basis, Shilchar's compounding story remains strong with revenue, EBITDA and PAT growing at CAGRs of 38%, 77%, and 83% respectively.

Two developments weighted on Q4 dispatches: uncertainty around US tariff policy moderated order intake from US customers in Q3, and a significant volume of shipments scheduled for delivery to Middle East customers in March '26 could not be dispatched due to the crisis in West Asia and the resulting logistics disruptions.
Both of these factors were temporary in nature and we expect Shilchar to resume its growth trajectory from the coming quarter.

India commissioned 55 gigawatts of renewable energy capacity in year '26, a record high and this sustained momentum continues to underpin strong order inflows in our domestic renewable transformer business.
Shilchar remains debt free with cash and cash equivalents of INR246 crores at the end of financial year '26.
Our Gavasad expansion number three, which will add 6,500 MVA and take our total installed capacity to 14,000 MVA, remains on track for commissioning in April '27.
Our business outlook remains strong with order visibility for financial year '27 of approximately INR800 crores, supported by robust inquiries from both domestic and export customers.

FLUOROCHEM.about: Incorporated in 2018, Gujarat Fluorochemicals Limited, earlier known as Inox Fluorochemicals Limited, is a part of the INOX Group of Companies and has been demerged from GFL Ltd, into a separate legal entity. It is one of the leading producers of Fluoro-polymers, Fluoro-specialities, Chemicals and Refrigerants in India. It is one of the top five global players in the fluoropolymers market with exports to Europe, Americas, Japan and Asia.

quarters.summary: GFL delivered strong broad-based growth in Q1 FY27 across chemical businesses driven by fluoropolymers and fluorochemicals, with sequential margin expansion and improved return ratios/working capital efficiency. Management guided to continued fluoropolymer growth of 17-20% annually, R32 capacity expansion commissioning in Q2 FY27, R134A commissioning within the financial year, AHF capacity additions matching refrigerant expansion, and battery materials scaling with a 3-digit revenue run rate expected by Q4 FY27 and significant ramp-up in FY28, with full earnings potential by FY29; the Oman battery materials project has been put on hold and relocated to India.

subsections.label: Drivers of performance
points: Growth was primarily driven by strong growth in fluoropolymer and fluorochemical businesses.
Sequential EBITDA margin improvement reflects benefits of higher volumes, improved product mix and operating leverage.
Improvements in ROCE, ROE and working capital days reflect operating performance strength and continued focus on capital efficiency, cash generation and disciplined execution.

subsections.label: Standalone vs consolidated gap
points: Standalone and consolidated numbers differ because GFL EV, GFL USA LLC and GFL GmbH (through which polymer business is routed) do not reflect in standalone but do in consolidated.
The gap widened this quarter because some CIF consignments and GIC that were earlier booked in Germany/LLC entities were instead booked/reversed in standalone itself.

subsections.label: Capitalization and capex triggers
points: Capitalization has two triggers: starting the plant, and the plant achieving intended product quality; while mechanical completion is controllable, quality stabilization timing varies by plant.

Total announced capex plan is INR6,000 crores, to be spent in phases over the next 2 years; FY27 capex spending plan is INR2,300 crores for EV and approximately INR800 crores for the chemical business.
Capitalization for these two capex tranches will come later due to a lag between capex spending and capitalization, and includes CWIP carried over from earlier years.

subsections.label: Fluoropolymers
points: Encouraging demand trends across the portfolio supported by improving volumes; new-age applications (semiconductors, data centers, electronics, automotive, green hydrogen, advanced industrial applications) creating growth opportunities.
Gradual improvement in product mix supported by increasing contributions from higher-value grades.
Growth achieved despite a challenging global environment.

Growth driven by combination of price realization and debottlenecking to enhance capacities to match market requirement; debottlenecking is a continuous process happening every second quarter as capacity utilization is reached.
Marginal price increase taken to offset input cost increases (methanol, sulfur); value-added product mix (higher grades, new applications) will reflect in subsequent quarters.

Growth is primarily driven by higher grades/new fluoropolymer volumes and moving existing products to higher grades for better value, rather than price increases; management characterizes this as value/mix shift, more mix than volume than price.

Fluoropolymer contracts often have formula-based pricing or customer understandings to mitigate raw material cost increase risk (e.g., sulfur and fluorspar price increases in Q1), protecting margins despite no explicit price hikes taken.

High-end grade approvals take longer due to niche application approval processes; company is in a cycle of continuously adding customer approvals and commercial volumes each quarter, balancing capacity and margins as it grows.

Most approvals for new fluoropolymer capacity expected to be in place by end of this financial year, enabling quicker ramp-up when new capacity comes online; commercial volumes will be taken further up in H2 FY27.
3M's exit (over past 2 years) impact has largely been absorbed; company has moved into the high-end market vacated by 3M, contributing to higher value-added growth.

AGC's announced intention to shut its UK facility has generated queries/inquiries from AGC's customers; GFL has matching grades available and qualification process has started with these customers, with traction expected in a quarter or two.

subsections.label: Fluorochemicals / Refrigerants
points: Exceptionally strong quarter, driven primarily by R32 refrigerant sales along with healthy growth across the refrigerant portfolio.

R32 capacity expansion is being commissioned; with existing capacity utilization already at peak levels, expansion will enhance ability to participate in growing global R32 market and support future demand growth.

R134A project remains on track for commissioning this financial year; combined with integrated manufacturing capabilities, established global marketing network and long-standing customer relationships, will strengthen ability to serve growing refrigerant demand domestically and internationally.
A more complete refrigerant product bouquet will enable leveraging strong global brands built over three decades.
R32 capacity has not been formally announced yet; multiple refrigerant products form a bouquet and go-to-market approach depends on product mix; capacity details to be shared over next few quarters.
Entitlement quota approach: by end of this financial year, company aims to utilize entire entitlement quota across R32, 134A, R22 and R125, offering a large refrigerant product bouquet.

134A entry rationale: strong market opportunity as refrigerants near end of cycle become valuable; supply expected to be restricted going forward with limited new supply entrants; demand remains robust; alternative (HFOs) has a much higher price point.
R32 sold in both domestic and global markets (long legacy/experience in global refrigerant marketing); sales mix is roughly 40-50% long-term contract with remainder spot or contract-to-contract.
R32 pricing between domestic and export markets stated to be very close.
R32 also marketed in combination with R125 as an R410 blend, given GFL is one of few players with both R125 and R32 available, providing a unique market position.
Full utilization of total 20,000 tons R32 capacity expected during calendar year 2027 once additional capacity is commissioned.

subsections.label: Bulk chemicals
points: Steady performance during the quarter, primarily driven by improved realizations.

subsections.label: Battery materials
points: Building a differentiated and integrated platform; in LiPF6 salt, advancing capacity expansion and customer commercialization efforts with leading global electrolyte manufacturers.
In electrolytes, qualification activities and sample development with Indian cell manufacturers progressing well, supported by customer audits and plant visits.
Across LFP cathode active materials and PVDF binders, focus remains on product consistency, customer qualification and commercial scale-up.

Businesses at different stages of qualification and commercialization; encouraged by long-term opportunity from EV adoption, battery energy storage system (BESS) deployment growth, and battery supply chain localization.

Initial capacity build is for qualification, with subsequent capacity addition for growth; significant growth in battery chemicals expected toward end of this financial year and in FY28, as capitalized gross block is still not very large relative to investment.
Some dispatches this quarter did not reflect in revenue because of CIF terms; will reflect in next quarter.

LiPF6 growth is furthest along, having nearly finished qualification and now in growth phase; PVDF is very close to finalizing qualification with revenue to follow; cathode active material revenue expected toward end of this financial year.
Full potential of battery materials investment expected to start reflecting from FY28 onward due to ~1.5 year stabilization/qualification period inherent to the industry.
Ramp-up for the incremental INR2,300 crores of EV capex expected to be faster than the initial phase, since qualification, stabilization and customer credibility have already been established.
3-digit battery chemicals revenue by Q4 FY27 and significant ramp-up in FY28 reaffirmed as on track.

subsections.label: R32/AHF capacity expansion
points: AHF capacity being added to support growing R32 and 134A refrigerant capacity, as well as other products; AHF capacity is also required for other GFL products.

AHF capacity additions will happen in phases, with the first set of capacities available by end of this year or Q3, and subsequent capacity added every quarter matched to refrigerant capacity additions.
Aim for AHF/HF is currently captive use only; not planning to sell HF or AHF externally at this time.

subsections.label: 134A plant structure
points: 134A plant is a brownfield expansion at one of GFL's existing refrigerant-producing sites.
Trichloroethylene (TCE), a restricted global product, will be imported from outside India rather than backward integrated; suppliers have been identified and this is not seen as a constraint.

subsections.label: Battery materials capacity/land
points: Oman battery materials project (~USD216 million capex) put on hold; capex being relocated to India due to geopolitical reasons causing delays, to move faster and meet customer commitments.
For India relocation, land for first phase of the project is available at the existing Dahej B (Jolva) plant, with all necessary approvals, clearances and site infrastructure support in place.
One additional site is being added in the Dahej area to support expansion, expected to be utilized for expansion toward end of FY27 and in FY28; land is not seen as a constraint for expansion.

Debottlenecking in fluoropolymers is a continuous process occurring every second quarter to balance capacity utilization with market requirement, focused on specific grades/products with growth opportunity.

subsections.label: Battery materials market opportunity
points: Global battery market was earlier projected to reach almost 1,800 gigawatt hour by 2030.

Domestic market, driven primarily by BESS, is now looking at 220-250 gigawatt hour by 2030, indicating a huge market potential expected to be captured primarily in FY28-FY29, at a much faster rate than seen so far.

subsections.label: Competitive positioning in fluoropolymers
points: GFL has moved up the value-added chain into fluoropolymer products and does not have much competition with Chinese players, who operate at a different price scale in less value-added segments.
3M's exit vacated high-end market space that GFL has moved into; AGC's planned UK facility shutdown is generating new customer inquiries and qualification opportunities for GFL.

key_figures.label: Oman project funding held via sovereign fund (OIA)

subsections.label: Oman project relocation
points: Oman battery materials project put on hold; capex being moved to India for faster execution and to meet customer commitments, driven partly by geopolitical reasons causing project delays.

The ~INR1,200 crores funding previously approved by sovereign fund OIA specific to the Oman project will not be available for the relocated India project; separate funding arrangements are being put in place for the India project.

Multiple reasons cited for the shift, including an improved overall environment for the battery industry in India versus a year ago, growth projections for the domestic market driven by BESS, and supportive policy push (e.g., battery components PLI) making the market opportunity attractive.
Ongoing fundraising process is underway to support capex requirements as the company progresses; funding is not currently seen as a constraint to project execution or capacity addition.

subsections.label: Anode active material
points: No product-specific capex has been disclosed for the anode active material product, as this information is considered confidential.

subsections.label: Macro and supply chain risk
points: Global business environment remains challenging with ongoing supply chain disruptions, commodity price volatility and an increasingly complex operating landscape.

Input cost volatility observed from March 2026 onwards, including for methanol and sulfur (used in fluoropolymer production) and fluorspar; managed through formula-based pricing arrangements or customer understandings to protect margins.

subsections.label: Regulatory/quota uncertainty
points: Refrigerant production quota allocation to new entrants is a decision resting outside GFL's control; GFL bases its expansion plans on its own entitlement per past precedent formulas (based on baseline and GWP).

Management expressed some uncertainty/lack of clarity in distinguishing between production quota and a raised concept of 'consumption quota' tied to domestic sales; committed to follow up and clarify.

points: Oman battery materials project delayed due to geopolitical reasons, prompting relocation of capex to India.

key_takeaways: On a year-on-year basis, revenue from our Chemical segment increased 23% to INR 1,574 crores, compared to INR 1,281 crores in Q1 FY26. Chemical segment EBITDA grew 29% to INR 458 crores from INR 354 crores, while segment PAT increased 33% to INR 261 crores.

At the consolidated level, revenue from operations grew 24% year-on-year to INR 1,588 crores. EBITDA increased 24% to INR 428 crores, while consolidated PAT stood at INR 219 crores, representing 19% growth over the same period last year.
Within the Chemical segment, revenue grew 16% quarter-on-quarter to INR 1,574 crores, while EBITDA increased 30% to INR 458 crores. EBITDA margin improved from 26% in Q4 FY26 to 29% in Q1 FY27.

ROCE improved by 258 basis points to 16.6% in Q1 FY27 compared to 14% in FY26, while ROE improved by 301 basis points to 15.18% from 12.17% in FY26. Working capital days reducing by 43 days to 149 days as of Q1 FY27 compared to 192 days as of Q4 FY26.
Fluoropolymer revenue grew 15% year-on-year and 8% sequentially during the quarter.
Fluorochemicals revenue increased 52% year-on-year and 44% quarter-on-quarter, driven primarily by R32 refrigerant sales.
We are expanding our R32 capacity, which is expected to be commissioned in Q2 FY27. Our R134A project remains on track and is expected to be commissioned during this financial year.
The Oman project right now, we have put on hold... those capex is now -- we are bringing it to India and planning to add those capacities in India.
We are on track and meeting our targets... 3 digit in quarter 4 and significant ramp-up in the following financial year [for battery chemicals].

Management guided FY27 capex of INR3,150 crores (INR2,300 crores for GFCL EV, INR850 crores for GFL), with battery materials business at an inflection point (LiPF6 salt approvals scaling, LFP CAM qualification expected Q3FY27, natural graphite anode addition), while fluoropolymers, refrigerants and battery materials are expected to be key growth drivers over the short-to-long term, with full earnings potential of battery materials investments expected by FY29.

subsections.label: Q4 performance drivers
points: Performance led by growth in Fluoropolymers segment and commencement of R-32 production in March 2026, marking an important milestone in the fluorochemicals growth journey.

Despite headwinds from tariff uncertainty, geopolitical tensions and elevated energy/logistics costs, the company maintained EBITDA margins and continued growth through disciplined execution, operational excellence, supply chain optimization and cost management.

subsections.label: Gross margin commentary
points: Management clarified the gross margin decline this quarter was minor (~0.5 percentage points), calling it 'pretty much flat overall' and not a significant change.

subsections.label: EV segment cost/loss jump explanation
points: Sharp increase in EBITDA loss in EV segment attributed to capitalization timing: LiPF6 plant capitalized on 5th January this quarter, after which accounting standards no longer allow capitalizing preoperative expenses/trial production losses — all expenses now flow through P&L regardless of sales ramp-up or capitalization status.
Related expense that used to be ~INR20 crores rose to ~INR45 crores.

Part of the increase was a one-time forex (buyer's credit) mark-to-market loss due to extreme dollar-INR movement linked to the Iran-U.S. conflict; this is now fully hedged (100% covered) and is not expected to recur. GFL (parent) has a natural hedge and does not need to cover this exposure.

subsections.label: Working capital / inventory days
points: Current elevated inventory days versus FY22-23 benchmark are partly a base effect: FY22-23 was an outlier year with turnover of INR6,300 crores due to an exceptional increase in chemical prices, causing abnormally low working capital cycle of 120-150 days then.

Distribution model requires stocking at Germany and US warehouses; company must keep 30-90 days inventory at plant and 30-90 days at warehouses, plus 30-60 days sea transit time depending on destination (Germany or USA).
Average credit period is 60-90 days; being fully integrated, the company has fewer creditors in its system and hence doesn't get typical credit benefit, keeping average working capital cycle high.
As EV business ramps up, procurement of raw material inventory for EV business (including LiPF6 commercial production) has added to working capital needs.
As capacities and turnover reach full levels, the denominator effect is expected to reduce working capital days automatically.
Insurance stock is kept for marquee customers in Europe and US markets who operate on Just-In-Time basis, requiring 2-3 months of stock as insurance.
Geopolitical scenario has increased voyage time from 3-4 weeks to 7-8 weeks; maintaining stock has helped convert sales despite ~8 weeks transit time to reach destinations.

key_figures.label: EV capex already invested to date

subsections.label: Fluoropolymers
points: Growth primarily driven by value-added products and higher volumes across key product categories.
Focus on high-value specialty grades, deeper customer engagement and expanding global reach supported growth momentum during the quarter.
Earlier capex in this segment should achieve its optimum utilization level in the current financial year (FY27); further capex will be incurred starting this year to continue the growth journey.
Growth for FY27 expected at 15-20% versus last year, driven by demand from semiconductor and other growth sectors, and continued focus on value-added applications and customers.

Growth figure of 15-20% includes both volume growth and price increases; price increase has been taken by the company in line with an industry price increase by a large competitor, balanced against cost push from backend raw materials.
Margins vary by grade — high-end new polymers carry disproportionately higher margins; capex additions are described as a 'mix' across grades, not proportionate across all fluoropolymers.
EBITDA performance for fluoropolymers has been in line with management's original indicated EBITDA margins when plants were set up ~2 years ago — no disconnect versus original thinking.
EBITDA expected to keep growing along with volume growth, further amplified as higher-margin new fluoropolymers are added to the mix.

No breakup of growth given between PTFE and new fluoropolymers; new capex investment is directed toward new fluoropolymers, not PTFE, as PTFE-related capacities set up a few years ago are nearing optimum utilization.

subsections.label: Fluorochemicals / Refrigerants (R-32)
points: Production and sales of R-32 commenced from March 2026, strengthening the refrigerant portfolio, despite weakness in the Middle East market in March and an overall challenging global environment; segment delivered a stable performance.
Increased production of R-32 will provide major growth in this segment in subsequent quarters.
R-32 capacity target is 20,000 tons; company has already achieved over 10,000 tons capacity and it is operating at optimal levels from April onward, to be ramped up further toward 20,000 tons.

R-32 sales are both domestic and export-oriented, leveraging legacy experience in refrigerant/export markets; some volumes are under contracts, and management is confident capacity ramp-up to 20,000 tons will face no challenge in being sold — contracted as of now.
No decision yet on further capacity additions beyond 20,000 tons; will be assessed based on market dynamics, product mix considerations and quota utilization timing.

subsections.label: Bulk chemicals (Caustic Soda) and Fluoromethane
points: Demand outlook for caustic soda expected to remain stable in FY27, but pricing likely to remain range-bound due to domestic capacity additions and balanced supply/demand dynamics.
Fluoromethane business performance expected to remain range-bound in near term amid moderate demand conditions and competitive market dynamics.

subsections.label: Battery Materials (GFCL EV)
points: Business considered at an important inflection point; battery energy storage system (BESS) opportunity has strengthened significantly over recent quarters.
All initial Phase 1 planned capacities have been commissioned and contracted for; marquee anchor customers secured across all battery material products.

LiPF6 salt has received approvals from most major global electrolyte players; commercial sales are scaling up in line with plans; orders in place for FY27 and beyond; production to be ramped up quarter-on-quarter.

LiPF6 plant capitalized on 5th January this quarter — operations have started; commercial sales for LiPF6 salt now started and revenue expected for all of FY27, with consistent growth in supply and revenue.

Cathode active material (LFP CAM): samples received initial approval; final qualification expected by end of Q3FY27; commercial supply to commence thereafter; off-take agreements already in place for entire capacity.

Natural graphite anode active material facility being set up as next phase of growth; this addition will allow the company to address nearly 70% of the value of an LFP battery cell, positioning it as one of the most integrated battery materials platforms globally; certain unspecified synergies exist with existing capabilities in natural graphite.
Binders have been fully qualified at major customers; revenue for binders expected to start in the next couple of quarters.
All contracted capacities in place (for LiPF6 and LFP) — anchor customers with agreed specs and pricing in writing, though contract details (e.g., take-or-pay terms) not disclosed.

Revenue potential framed via ~2x asset turnover approach post-gestation period (9 months to a year qualification cycle after plant commissioning); management declined to give exact revenue numbers but affirmed eventual realization of implied revenue potential once capacity utilization is complete.
FY27 expected to be a year of material quantity supply for salt (LiPF6), while LFP CAM revenue ramp is expected to start after Q3FY27 qualification.
Expect quarter-on-quarter revenue growth in battery chemicals to be significant, with a 3-digit (INR crores) revenue number expected as an exit rate by Q4FY27.
Full earnings potential of battery materials investments expected to be realized by FY29 as facilities progressively ramp up and achieve optimum utilization.

subsections.label: FY27 capex breakdown
points: Total FY27 capex of INR3,150 crores split between GFCL EV (INR2,300 crores) and GFL chemicals (INR850 crores).

Of the INR850 crores GFL capex: ~INR150 crores for expanding refrigerant gas and related infrastructure capacities; INR222 crores for new high-purity electronic specialty chemicals for the semiconductor sector; INR250 crores for adding new fluoropolymer capacities; remaining INR230 crores for increasing capacities for backward integration including regular annual maintenance capex.

EV capex of INR2,300 crores will be spent on increasing capacities across existing products plus capex for natural graphite anode active material; this is part of the overall INR6,000 crores earmarked cumulative capex for GFCL EV by FY28.
GFL capex figures are separate from the EV vertical capex since EV business is being separated out from the chemical part of the mother company investments.

subsections.label: R-32 capacity ramp-up
points: Production of R-32 already started and operating at optimal capacity levels from April onward for the 10,000-ton capacity achieved so far.
Capacity will be ramped up over time toward the 20,000-ton target; INR150 crores capex earmarked for this expansion in the current financial year, expected to happen 'very soon'.
Decision on capacity beyond 20,000 tons will depend on market dynamics, opportunities, product mix considerations, and available HCFC baseline quota, which the company has time to utilize.

subsections.label: Oman capex
points: Oman capex project remains on track; no impact from Middle East developments as Oman has been one of the safest countries in the region so far; no change to capex plan.

subsections.label: EV capex progress
points: Approximately INR1,900-2,000 crores already invested in EV/battery materials so far; plan is to invest INR2,300 crores in the coming year (FY27).
Not the entire invested capex has been capitalized yet — capitalization occurs progressively as plants are commissioned and intended purpose of the capex is achieved.
Subsequent financial year(s) expected to see similar order of capex to reach the cumulative INR6,000 crores target.

subsections.label: Fluoropolymers demand drivers
points: Long-term outlook for fluoropolymers remains constructive, supported by increasing penetration across structurally growing sectors such as semiconductors, EVs, battery energy storage systems and clean energy applications.
Global energy transition themes including hydrogen, fuel cells, electrolyzers and solar are emerging as important long-term demand drivers for fluoropolymers.
Given increasing complexity and purity requirements in these applications, specialty fluoropolymers expected to witness strong demand over the medium to long term.
Focus on high-value specialty grades, deeper customer engagement and expanding global reach supporting growth momentum.
Approval/qualification cycles for high-end fluoropolymer applications (e.g., semiconductor) are longer, but most approvals have now come in and commercial businesses have started performing well.

subsections.label: Battery materials demand drivers
points: Global energy transition continuing to accelerate; demand environment for advanced battery materials remains highly encouraging.
Battery energy storage system (BESS) opportunity has strengthened significantly over recent quarters.

Increasing investment in AI and machine learning infrastructure coupled with thriving data center capacities driving power requirements and creating structural demand for energy storage solutions globally.
Marquee anchor customers secured across battery material products, providing confidence on utilization ramp-up and commercial scale-up.

subsections.label: Macro/geopolitical headwinds
points: FY26 marked by highly volatile global operating environment: first half impacted by uncertainty around US tariff policies and evolving global trade dynamics.

Latter part of the year saw heightened geopolitical tensions amid the war in the Middle East, dampening macro and business environment, disrupting global trade flows, impacting logistics and supply chains, and contributing to elevated volatility across commodities and currency markets.
Sharp movements in energy prices resulted in higher input and logistic costs across businesses.
Conditions continue to be volatile, though some signs of stabilization are being seen.
Weakness in the Middle East market in March 2026 affected refrigerant segment performance, though the segment still delivered stable results.
Voyage/transit times have increased sharply from 3-4 weeks to 7-8 weeks due to geopolitical scenario, requiring higher inventory buffers.
Extreme dollar-INR currency movement due to Iran-US conflict caused a one-time mark-to-market forex loss on buyer's credit in the EV segment; now fully hedged (100% covered) going forward.

subsections.label: Competitive/pricing pressure
points: Caustic soda pricing likely to remain range-bound due to domestic capacity additions and balanced supply/demand dynamics.
Fluoromethane performance expected to remain range-bound amid moderate demand conditions and competitive market dynamics.

subsections.label: Overall outlook
points: Short to medium-term growth to be driven by the refrigerant and fluoropolymer segments.
Medium to long-term growth journey equally encouraging as advanced battery materials business scales up and reaches full potential in coming years.
Full earnings potential of battery materials investments expected to be realized by FY29 as facilities progressively ramp up and achieve optimum utilization level.

key_takeaways: Chemicals business Q4 revenue grew 11% YoY to INR1,358 crores, EBITDA up 13% YoY to INR353 crores, PAT up 5% YoY to INR169 crores, led by Fluoropolymers growth and commencement of R-32 production in March 2026.

AEGISLOG.about: Aegis Logistics (Formely known as Aegis Chemical Industries Ltd.), incorporated in 1956 provide logistic solutions for oil, gas, chemicals, and petrochemical industries.[1]

quarters.summary: Management expressed strong confidence in continued growth momentum into FY'27, guided by capacity expansions across ports (Mumbai, JNPA, Kandla, Pipavav, Kochi, Mangalore), a $1.2 billion cumulative capex target this fiscal year and a ~$5 billion capex pipeline through FY 2030-31, a targeted gearing ratio of ~0.6x, sustained distribution margins of INR7,000+ per ton, a push toward 2 million tons distribution volume, and the ramp-up of the newly commissioned ammonia terminal at Pipavav, even as the Gas business benefited from (and could see normalization away from) geopolitical disruption in the Middle East.

key_figures.label: EPS as % of full year FY26 EPS

subsections.label: Capital allocation & funding
points: Aegis Vopak (AVTL) is self-funded via equity dilution to enable capex and subsequent borrowing capacity, supporting the $5 billion capex journey.
Company maintains a 'fortress balance sheet' with healthy cash balance for financial flexibility to move quickly on opportunities, whether organic or inorganic.
Growth mix will use a balanced mix of equity, internal accruals and debt, targeting gearing ratio of ~0.6x.
Cash is not deployed in a rush; company prioritizes growth resulting in profits given its bottom-line driven approach.
Distribution business is franchise-driven, financed by the franchisee, so it requires hardly any capex and very low working capital.
Aegis Gas's INR870 crore other income in FY26 was due to capital gains from sale of its holding in Hindustan Aegis, which gets eliminated on a consolidated basis.

subsections.label: Gas division drivers
points: Gas division reported its highest ever EBITDA with 296% YoY growth, achieved despite a challenging global backdrop marked by geopolitical tensions and disruptions from the war in the Middle East, demonstrating logistics business resilience.
LPG sourcing volumes remained stable with marginal 1% YoY growth, highlighting strength and reliability of sourcing capabilities.

Gas distribution business growth was driven by robust demand across customer segments and continued expansion of customer base; multiple private sector customers added over the last year, momentum continuing into current fiscal year.

Sharp increase in gas EBITDA driven by two factors: resilience of logistics/sourcing business maintaining stable volumes despite challenging global environment, and outstanding distribution business performance with record volumes plus healthy margin expansion.
Vertically integrated business model (sourcing, logistics, storage, distribution) is a key competitive advantage enabling volume growth that would have been difficult to achieve otherwise.

subsections.label: Liquids division
points: Liquids division delivered its highest ever Q1 EBITDA and has recorded 5 consecutive quarters of EBITDA growth.

Remains a well-diversified and stable cash-generating business; company continues to invest in capacity expansion within this segment to capitalize on growth opportunities and strengthen contribution to overall portfolio.

subsections.label: Distribution margin per ton commentary
points: Margin of INR4,000/ton was standard till FY24-25; blended margin has risen to INR7,000+ over the past 24 months on account of geopolitical uncertainty/difficulty margin.

Management does not expect the INR7,000 margin to revert to INR4,000 when things normalize in FY27-28 onward; instead the uncertainty-driven premium is expected to be substituted by procurement efficiency gains from volume ramp-up (e.g., shipping on VLGC at ~$15 freight vs MGC at ~$50 freight, adding ~INR3,000 top-up over the base INR4,000).
Margins should be viewed as a full-year blended figure rather than quarter-to-quarter; Q1 and Q4 FY26/27 delivered well above INR5,000 (3x higher), supporting a blended full-year rate of INR7,000+.
Distribution volume growth (more geography, more customers, more terminals) is expected to bring procurement efficiencies supporting margin sustainability.

subsections.label: Volume growth outlook by segment
points: Distribution volume target: aim to reach 2 million tons in distribution over time, driven by infrastructure layout in the LPG business (new cryogenic terminals at Pipavav and Mangalore providing ullage/flexibility), not solely due to the war.

Increase in demand, ability to deliver product when it mattered most during geopolitical disruption, and ullage/infrastructure expansion across India are cited as the three drivers expected to sustain healthy YoY volume growth in distribution.
Ammonia terminal commissioning adds one more product to the gas business distribution portfolio.

Logistics volume growth benchmark is a worst-case 25% YoY; enablers (pipeline hookups, multimodal evacuation, VLGC-compliant jetties) could deliver step-up growth beyond 25% if customers utilize them and geopolitical normalization occurs.
Distribution segment growth rate is expected to exceed the 25% logistics benchmark, potentially closer to 50%, driven by increasing presence in industrial distribution.
Distribution volume trajectory rose from 500,000 to 750,000 metric tons last year; expected to cross 1 million metric tons this year (FY27) and cross 1.5 million metric tons next year (FY28).

subsections.label: Sourcing/Distribution/Logistics volume disclosure practice
points: Company does not disclose split of distribution volumes between industrial and HoReCa customers; reports logistics, sourcing and distribution volumes in aggregate.
Company does not disclose port-wise revenue/tariff splits (e.g., Mumbai terminal); tariff structure stated to be uniform across locations.

subsections.label: Mumbai Port
points: Continues to operate at high utilization level (~95%); historically a high-demand port benefiting from its location and strong customer franchise, with historical throughput of 90+ tons.

New 64,000 cubic meter liquid storage capacity being developed at ~INR125 crores investment, progressing per schedule with commissioning targeted H1 FY27; company confident new capacity will ramp up utilization quickly given customer interest and existing demand trends.
Mumbai already has a cryogenic LPG terminal, the first cryogenic terminal built in India in 1997; further expansion of cryogenic storage possible if land is secured.

subsections.label: JNPA Port
points: JNPA in Maharashtra has emerged as India's highest revenue-generating major port in FY26.
Major expansion underway comprising additional liquid storage, LPG capacity, and an LPG bottling plant, at a total capital outlay of ~INR1,675 crores.
First phase of liquid storage expansion (~100,000 cubic meters) expected to be commissioned in Q3 FY27 and will start contributing as soon as operational.

Board approved development of a 52,000 metric ton refrigerated double-walled steel LPG tank at JNPA, representing a significant strategic investment to enhance gas handling capabilities on the West Coast and consolidate Aegis's position as leading logistics player in India.

subsections.label: Haldia
points: LPG terminal backed by exclusive terminaling agreement with HPCL extending through 2038, providing long-term revenue visibility.
Acquired further 3 acres of land, providing opportunity to expand liquid business at this location; company continues to see growth opportunities here.

subsections.label: Kandla
points: Remains the largest and strategically most important port terminal for Aegis, serving a vast hinterland across Northern and Western India.
Became VLGC compliant during last year, an important step.
CRL 4 liquid terminal construction progressing well, with commissioning targeted for next year.
Nonbinding MOU signed with Larsen & Toubro for potential joint development of ammonia terminals, positioning Aegis in the energy transition opportunity at Kandla.

subsections.label: Pipeline developments (Kandla & Pipavav)
points: Jamnagar-Loni LPG pipeline is now complete and operational.
Kandla-Gorakhpur LPG pipeline progressing well, expected to be connected during H1 FY27.
These pipeline connections will enhance evacuation infrastructure, enable faster turnaround, better capacity utilization, and support handling of higher volumes at both Kandla and Pipavav.

subsections.label: Pipavav — transformational year
points: 48,000 metric ton LPG terminal commissioned June 2025, taking total LPG capacity to 70,800 metric tons; ramp-up progressing well.

Three key developments: (1) APM Terminals developing a VLGC-compliant liquids jetty expected to be completed during the year, enhancing vessel handling and larger cargo movements; (2) additional liquid rail gantry being developed, with a 15-year take-or-pay agreement secured with a leading conglomerate for petroleum products, committed volumes exceeding 0.5 million metric tons per annum, operations expected to commence by year end; (3) Kandla-Gorakhpur pipeline connectivity expected this year, enabling more efficient LPG evacuation/distribution and enhancing throughput.

Pipavav evolving into a highly integrated logistics platform comprising VLGC handling, liquid and LPG storage, bottling plant, LPG rail loading facilities, 16 truck-loading bays, and pipeline connectivity into Central India — materially improving operational efficiency and competitive positioning.

subsections.label: Ammonia terminal at Pipavav
points: Specialized ammonia storage and terminaling facility commissioned with static storage capacity of 36,000 metric tons — a significant milestone in infrastructure expansion.

State-of-the-art terminal strengthens position in specialized chemicals/gas logistics, enhances India's ammonia handling capabilities, and supports demand from fertilizer, industrial and emerging clean energy value chains.
15-year take-or-pay agreement signed with Hindustan Zinc to service its upcoming DAP (Di-Ammonium Phosphate) plant for part of capacity, providing long-term revenue visibility.

Ammonia terminal is not just a storage asset — like the LPG business, it creates opportunity to participate in distribution to industrial customers, capturing margins significantly higher than traditional storage revenues; seen as a potential new growth platform leveraging sourcing, logistics and distribution expertise into an adjacent product segment.

ITOCHU Corporation (Japanese trading house) acquired a 10% stake in Aegis Terminal Pipavav Limited, joined the Board, and has expressed intention to increase stake to 25% over next 3 years, validating long-term potential of the Pipavav asset.

subsections.label: Kochi Port
points: Board approved construction of additional 49,577 cubic meter storage capacity on newly allotted land, expected to be commissioned early in the next financial year, taking total Kochi capacity to 132,122 cubic meters.

subsections.label: Mangalore Port
points: 82,000 metric ton LPG terminal commissioned June 2025; developing LPG rail loading gantry and bottling plant infrastructure with INR52.5 crores investment.
75,000 cubic meters of liquid capacity added last year is now fully operational with full utilization, bringing total liquid storage to 193,000 cubic meters.
Additional land secured; evaluating further addition of 60,000 cubic meters of liquid capacity.

subsections.label: New ports — Vadhavan
points: Nonbinding MOU signed to participate in development of Vadhavan Port with potential investment of ~INR20,000 crores, subject to necessary approvals, land allocation and other regulatory clearances.

Opportunity aligns with long-term vision of building large-scale world-class infrastructure assets across India's energy and logistics value chain; if taken forward, would enable development of modern liquid and gas handling facilities, significantly expanding infrastructure platform and presence on the West Coast.

subsections.label: US import mix / VLGC compliance
points: India imports from the U.S. have nearly reached 1 million metric tons, reflecting a mix shift toward long-haul VLGCs; large ships come from the U.S., while both large and small ships come from the Middle East.

Some Indian terminals can only handle small ships due to lower static capacity, whereas Aegis has very large capacity terminals (especially Mangalore, Pipavav, and Kandla) that can unload an entire ship in one shot, reducing ship waiting time, demurrage, and freight cost — helping gain market share in terminaling volumes.

subsections.label: Geopolitical / Middle East disruption
points: Gas division delivered record EBITDA amidst a very challenging global backdrop marked by ongoing geopolitical tensions and disruptions arising from the war in the Middle East, demonstrating resilience of the logistics business.
Logistics throughput volumes remained resilient despite geopolitical challenges and disruptions arising from global war-led uncertainties.

Distribution margin premium (INR7,000 vs historical INR4,000) partly attributed to uncertainty and difficulty arising from geopolitics; management does not expect this premium to fully revert once conditions normalize, expecting it to be substituted by procurement efficiency gains instead.

subsections.label: Business risk discipline
points: Management stated they do not want to be driven by greed or take speculative inventory/price positions like global traders (e.g., Trafigura, Glencore, Vitol); they operate as distributors sourcing to meet demand rather than taking speculative positions, to avoid volatility risk in a volatile industry.

subsections.label: Competitive dynamics with alternative fuels
points: Morbi market (large LPG demand center) will continue to source from whichever supplier — LPG or natural gas — offers the cheapest/best value; competition exists between LPG suppliers and natural gas, and customers will switch based on value delivered.

subsections.label: Overall outlook
points: Strong start to FY27 and Q1 performance reinforce confidence in the growth trajectory of the business over coming years; multiple growth drivers taking shape from past investments and ongoing capacity expansions, positioning the company to capitalize on increasing demand and deliver sustainable growth.
Over last 5 years, EPS has compounded at over 30% annually with a healthy and consistent dividend track record, reflecting quality of asset base and disciplined capital allocation and execution.
Company remains confident in growth trajectory and committed to creating long-term value for stakeholders.
Cumulative capex target of $1.2 billion for FY27, part of a broader $5 billion capex pipeline through FY2030-31, targeting a gearing ratio of ~0.6x.

subsections.label: Distribution margin outlook
points: Management guided that INR7,000+ margin should be viewed as a full-year blended figure, not quarter-to-quarter; expects the number to end the year around INR7,000 plus given Q1 performance exceeding Q4 FY26.

The INR7,000 margin is expected to sustain into FY27-28 and beyond, substituting the uncertainty-driven premium with procurement efficiency gains from volume ramp-up (e.g., cheaper freight via VLGCs).

subsections.label: Volume growth outlook
points: Logistics volume growth benchmark is 25% YoY as a worst-case scenario; step-up growth beyond this is possible if enablers (pipeline hookups, multimodal evacuation, VLGC jetties) are utilized by customers.
Distribution volume growth is expected to exceed 25%, potentially closer to 50%, driven by expansion into industrial distribution with greater geographic presence.
EPS has grown from INR6 to INR26 over the last 10 years; company expects to continue a 25%+ CAGR even off this larger base.
Medium-term distribution volume target of 2 million metric tons.

subsections.label: Ammonia business ramp-up
points: Distribution of ammonia expected to begin imminently — within weeks to a month.
Ammonia distribution will be exclusively industrial distribution to begin with; no cylinder packing or gas stations planned.
Management declined to specify margins for ammonia distribution at this early stage, stating updates will follow after a quarter of operations.
Ammonia terminal expected to achieve 25% utilization in Year 1, with utilization growth of 30-40% YoY thereafter.

risk_register.risk: Uncertainty margin normalization / potential margin reversion

risk_register.risk: Industry volatility / speculative trading risk
