risk_register.risk: Competition from alternative fuels (natural gas) at price-sensitive customers (e.g., Morbi)
risk_register.note: Customers like those in Morbi will switch to whichever energy source (LPG vs natural gas) offers best value, reflecting ongoing competitive dynamics.

risk_register.risk: Regulatory/approval risk for new port development (Vadhavan)
risk_register.note: Vadhavan Port investment of ~INR20,000 crores is subject to necessary approvals, land allocation and other regulatory clearances.

risk_register.risk: Middle East (West Asia) supply disruption / Hormuz situation affecting LPG sourcing and volumes
risk_register.note: Shortfall improved from 50% in April to 30% in May; normalcy expected to return around Q2 FY27; multiple alternative global supply sources being developed to reduce Middle East dependency.

risk_register.risk: Energy price volatility
risk_register.note: Prices swung from INR54,000-60,000/ton up to INR150,000/ton and back to INR80,000-90,000/ton during the crisis, increasing sourcing uncertainty though management says margins remain sustainable.

risk_register.risk: Government policy shift reducing subsidized LPG cylinders (9 to 4) and promoting PNG
risk_register.note: Management downplayed the risk citing India's very low per-capita energy consumption and large scope for growth across all energy sources including LPG, PNG, natural gas and ammonia.

risk_register.risk: Phasing of capacity additions impacting Liquid segment margins
risk_register.note: Liquid business EBITDA down 5% YoY reflecting phasing of capacity additions; FY26 liquid operations were normalized with no major take-or-pay unlike prior year.

risk_register.risk: Execution risk on Vadhavan port investment
risk_register.note: Potential ~INR20,000 crore investment in Vadhavan is subject to approvals and land allocation; inclusion in capex pipeline depends on how quickly the port project and permits progress.

risk_register.risk: Ammonia business being a new, unproven product
risk_register.note: Management said it is difficult to project ammonia volumes by FY29-30 as this is a new product dependent on number of terminals constructed and locations secured.

themes.label: Record profitability / breakout growth
themes.note: Q1 FY27 PAT crossed INR500 crores milestone, up 212% YoY; EBITDA up 184% YoY, reflecting record performance across all key metrics.

themes.label: Capacity expansion across ports
themes.note: Major expansions underway/approved at Mumbai, JNPA, Kandla, Pipavav, Kochi and Mangalore, alongside a potential new Vadhavan Port investment of ~INR20,000 crores.

themes.label: Distribution margin sustainability
themes.note: Management guides INR7,000+/ton blended margin sustaining into FY27-28, with the uncertainty-driven premium expected to be substituted by procurement efficiency gains from volume ramp-up rather than reverting to historical INR4,000 level.

themes.label: Middle East supply disruption / geopolitical risk
themes.note: Gas division delivered record EBITDA despite geopolitical tensions and war-related disruptions; margin premium partly tied to this uncertainty, with eventual normalization expected around Q2 per prior guidance.

themes.label: Ammonia business entry
themes.note: Ammonia terminal at Pipavav commissioned with 36,000 MT capacity; 15-year take-or-pay agreement signed with Hindustan Zinc; distribution to begin within weeks, seen as a new growth platform with higher margins than storage.

themes.label: Strategic JV partnerships (Itochu, Vopak, L&T)
themes.note: ITOCHU holds 10% stake in Aegis Terminal Pipavav Limited with intent to raise to 25% over 3 years; nonbinding MOU signed with L&T for potential joint ammonia terminal development at Kandla.

themes.label: Conservative guidance philosophy
themes.note: Management declined to give specific ammonia distribution margins pending a quarter of actual operations, and reiterated 25% logistics volume growth as a conservative benchmark with upside from enablers.

key_takeaways: We delivered a record quarter, crossing the significant milestone of INR500 crores of profit after tax in the first quarter of this fiscal year compared to INR175 crores in Q1 of FY '26, reflecting an exceptional 212% year-on-year growth.
We reported a normalized EBITDA of INR727 crores in Q1 compared to INR256 crores in Q1 of FY '26, delivering a robust growth of 184% year-on-year.
Our Liquids division delivered its highest ever Q1 EBITDA performance and has now recorded 5 consecutive quarters of EBITDA growth.

The division [Gas] reported its highest ever EBITDA, registering a remarkable 296% year-on-year growth... amidst a very challenging global backdrop marked by ongoing geopolitical tensions and disruptions arising from the war in the Middle East.

Our gas distribution business continued its strong growth trajectory during the quarter, delivering a 91% year-on-year increase in volumes compared to Q1 of FY '26 and a 19% sequential growth over Q4 FY '26.
I'm really pleased to announce the commissioning of our specialized ammonia storage and terminaling facility at Pipavav Port with a static storage capacity of 36,000 metric tons.
ITOCHU Corporation, which has acquired a 10% stake in Aegis Terminal Pipavav Limited... has expressed their intention to increase their stake over to 25% over the next 3 years.
Cumulative capex is to reach approximately $1.2 billion in this fiscal year... we have identified a capex pipeline of approximately $5 billion through the financial year 2030-'31.
pressing_questions: Is the volume growth surpassing your own expectations? And obviously, there is some disruption due to the war. But do you think that these volumes are sticky, these customer contracts are sticky? And how do you see growth now from the 280 kt levels that we saw in this quarter?
Is it fair to say that profitability in terms of EBITDA per ton kind of peaked in this quarter? ... how do you think about profitability, say, from a near-term basis and medium term structurally?

How should we think about throughput enhancement in basic terms... how much faster can the evacuation happen in terms of turns or, say, volume guidance, I mean, which give a better sense on your utilization potential?

India at the national level still has a deficit of 15% to 20% to pre-war levels in terms of LPG. So what stops us from -- because our throughput is much higher than what we are doing. So what stops us from filling up more or the tanks more because you have ITOCHU as a partner who can do wonders. So what stops you from doing more?
When do you start the distribution for ammonia? And what will be your EBITDA per ton on that? And also, what are the means of delivering ammonia, sir?

quarters.summary: Aegis Logistics delivered a breakout FY26 with revenue up 23% YoY to INR8,333 crores, normalized EBITDA up 36% to INR1,599 crores, and PAT up 41% to INR1,107 crores crossing the INR1,000 crores PAT milestone for the first time; Q4 FY26 was the strongest ever quarter. Management guided for continued strong momentum in FY27, reiterated a 25% CAGR guidance framework, outlined a capex pipeline of $1.2 billion by March 2027 and $5 billion through December 2030, and expects LPG supply disruptions from the Middle East situation to normalize by Q2 FY27.

key_figures.label: Cash and investments on balance sheet
EPS at first guidance vs now

subsections.label: FY26 Performance Drivers
points: FY26 was described as an outstanding, breakout year for the company reflecting compounding power of diversified operations and execution discipline.
Q4 FY26 was the strongest quarter ever for the company.
Board recommended a final dividend of INR6.70 per share for FY26, bringing aggregate dividend for the year to INR8.7 per share, in line with commitment to shareholder returns.

subsections.label: Balance Sheet & Capital Allocation
points: Cash and investments grew from INR150 crores in FY22 to INR5,939 crores in FY26, a transformation positioning the company to fund growth at pace without compromising financial discipline.
Cash figure includes cash held in 100% subsidiaries, not just standalone ALL; consolidation includes AVTL cash, though AVTL cash is not significant.
Growth will be pursued through disciplined funding via a balanced mix of equity, internal accruals and debt, targeting a gearing ratio of approximately 0.6x.
Low leverage, strong cash generation and a resilient balance sheet provide financial flexibility to move quickly on opportunities.

Capex is executed by Aegis Logistics standalone (ALL) or its 100% subsidiaries via EPC, and assets are later transferred to Aegis Vopak Terminals Limited (AVTL); consolidation capitalizes at the value at which ALL bills.

Capex trajectory: $1.2 billion cumulative by March 2027; a further INR5,000 crores by FY28 (adding to the $1.2bn); heavier capex expected in FY29, FY30 and FY31 to reach the $5 billion pipeline target by December 2030/FY31.
Management reiterated it is a conservative company, citing 32% CAGR growth achieved over the last 5 years against an unchanged 25% CAGR guidance even as EPS base grew from INR6 to INR26.

subsections.label: Gas (LPG) Segment Drivers
points: LPG business recorded its highest ever revenue and EBITDA, driven by record logistics and distribution volumes.

Q4 was the highest ever revenue and EBITDA quarter for the Gas division across any quarter, with distribution volumes at a record level even as throughput held steady despite disruptions from the West Asia situation.

Distribution margin surge to ~INR7,000/ton (from ~INR4,000) attributed partly to volume growth (procurement efficiencies) and partly to margin improvement from energy price rises and uncertainty; management expects INR7,000 to sustain into FY27 as Q1 has already performed well, with continued sustainability into FY28 supported by procurement efficiencies as volumes scale further.

Distribution now sourced from multiple terminals (Mumbai, Kandla, Mangalore cryo, Haldia, Pipavav) versus earlier reliance on just Mumbai and Kandla, driving pan-India volume increase across South, East and West.
Target of 2 million tons distribution (including LPG and ammonia) expected to be reached by FY28; ammonia distribution will form part of this combined target.

Full-year effect of terminals commissioned mid-FY26 (Pipavav cryogenic, Mangalore cryogenic) expected to boost throughput in FY27, along with multimodal evacuation infrastructure (Jamnagar-Loni pipeline, Kandla-Gorakhpur pipeline, rail gantries) coming online.

subsections.label: Liquid Segment
points: Liquid business revenue broadly stable YoY; EBITDA down 5% reflecting phasing of capacity additions.
Unlike the prior year, FY26 liquid operations were all normalized with no major take-or-pay contribution.

subsections.label: Ammonia Business Economics
points: Ammonia throughput expected to run at ~25% utilization in year one, growing 30-40% YoY thereafter, similar to the LPG ramp-up pattern.
Ammonia distribution volumes expected to begin around 200,000 tons, growing 20-30% YoY.
Throughput margins expected in the INR2,500-3,000/ton range; distribution margins could go up to INR5,000/ton depending on market conditions.
One third of Pipavav ammonia terminal capacity is committed under take-or-pay to Hindustan Zinc; two-thirds remains available as open-source capacity for distribution.

Management cited CRISIL/DRHP data projecting a ~3 million ton India ammonia supply-demand gap by FY29, underpinning bullishness on the new ammonia business, though exact volume targets by FY30 are difficult to project given the business is nascent.

subsections.label: Inventory & Pricing Dynamics
points: Management clarified the company does not book inventory gains in P&L; inventory is held at cost and kept low (not more than a month), so margin improvement is not attributable to inventory revaluation gains.

Higher percentage and rupee-term margins in times of uncertainty are attributed to elevated energy prices making product harder to source, not to inventory gains; energy prices fluctuated significantly (INR54,000-60,000 to INR150,000, back down to INR80,000-90,000 per metric ton) during the Middle East crisis period.

subsections.label: Mumbai
points: Facility continues to operate at very high utilization rate.
Developing additional 64,000 kilolitres of liquid storage at a project cost of INR125 crores, progressing on schedule with commissioning targeted for H1 FY27.

subsections.label: JNPT
points: Executing a major expansion comprising additional liquid storage, LPG capacity and a new LPG bottling plant at a total capital outlay of approximately INR1,675 crores.
First phase of the liquid capacity expected to be commissioned in H1 FY27.
Evaluating a further cryogenic gas tank (36,000-50,000 metric ton static capacity) to strengthen West Coast gas handling capabilities.

subsections.label: Haldia
points: Completed acquisition of 75% stake in Hindustan Aegis LPG Limited during the year, marking entry into the East Coast market, acquired through subsidiary Aegis Vopak Terminals Limited.
Asset anchored by an exclusive terminaling agreement with Hindustan Petroleum through 2038, providing strong long-term revenue visibility.
Additional 3 acres of land acquired to support future expansion.

subsections.label: Kandla
points: One of the largest and strategically most important hubs.
In December, the group successfully handled a VLGC vessel, making Kandla a VLGC-compliant terminal.
Jamnagar-Loni LPG pipeline is complete; Kandla-Gorakhpur LPG pipeline expected to connect in H1 FY27, further improving evacuation efficiency.
Construction of CRL 4 liquid terminal progressing well with commissioning targeted for next year.
Signed nonbinding MoU with Larsen & Toubro for potential joint development of ammonia terminals, positioning the company for the energy transition opportunity at Kandla.

subsections.label: Pipavav
points: One of the most active locations this year; ramp-up of the newly commissioned cryogenic LPG terminal progressing well.
New VLGC-compliant jetty expected to be completed within the calendar year, with KGPL pipeline connection following in Q2 FY27.

When complete, Pipavav will offer a fully integrated LPG logistics ecosystem: VLGC handling, cryogenic storage, bottling plant, LPG rail gantry, truck loading bays and pipeline connectivity to Central India.
Building an additional rail gantry on the liquid side; secured a 15-year take-or-pay agreement with a leading conglomerate for petroleum products, with operations expected to commence by year-end.
Advancing India's first independent ammonia terminal, backed by a 15-year take-or-pay agreement with Hindustan Zinc for their upcoming DAP plant, with commissioning targeted for H1 FY27.
Itochu Corporation acquired a 10% stake in Aegis Terminal Pipavav Limited as a strategic partner, with intention to raise the stake to 25% over the next 3 years.

subsections.label: Kochi
points: Continuing to evaluate addition of further liquid storage on newly allotted land; further updates to be provided once finalized.

subsections.label: Mangalore
points: Commissioned cryogenic LPG terminal in June 2025; progressing construction of an LPG rail gantry, described as a very important step.
Liquid capacity added last year is now fully operational.
Additional land secured; evaluating further liquid storage expansion at this site.

subsections.label: Vadhavan Port
points: Signed a nonbinding MoU to participate in development of this port, subject to approvals and land allocation.
Will enable development of further world-class liquid and gas handling infrastructure, significantly expanding scale and geographic reach of the network.

subsections.label: Haldia Acquisition & JV Structuring
points: Completed acquisition of 75% stake in Hindustan Aegis LPG Limited via subsidiary Aegis Vopak Terminals Limited, marking entry into the East Coast market.

subsections.label: Strategic Partnerships
points: Signed nonbinding MoU with Larsen & Toubro for potential joint development of ammonia terminals at Kandla.

Itochu Corporation acquired a 10% stake in Aegis Terminal Pipavav Limited as a strategic partner, with intention to raise stake to 25% over the next 3 years; Itochu is also participating in hard assets.
Management highlighted that high-quality joint venture partners such as Itochu and Vopak have given the company a tremendous edge in sourcing alternative sources of gas.
Signed nonbinding MoU to participate in development of Vadhavan port with a potential investment of approximately INR20,000 crores, subject to approvals and land allocation.

subsections.label: Corporate Structure
points: Capex is executed by Aegis Logistics standalone or its 100% subsidiaries, with assets subsequently transferred to Aegis Vopak Terminals Limited (AVTL); consolidation capitalizes assets at the value at which ALL bills.

subsections.label: Middle East / Hormuz Supply Disruption
points: LPG supply disruptions linked to the West Asia/Middle East situation caused a shortfall versus normal volumes; shortfall improved from 50% in April to 30% in May, with further improvement expected and normalcy potentially returning sometime in Q2 FY27.

Middle East is a source of convenience, not the only source; multiple alternative supply sources exist (Canada, America, Argentina, Nigeria, etc.) with somewhat longer journey times; the crisis is seen as offering lessons on diversifying supply sources going forward, which management expects to reduce dependency on the Middle East.
Management stated it cannot make prophecies on exact normalization timing but expects continued month-on-month improvement.

In a hypothetical scenario where Hormuz does not open for three months, management believes supply sources can shift and volumes can still be recovered and grown, aided by high-quality JV partners like Itochu and Vopak.

subsections.label: Energy Price Volatility
points: Energy prices were highly volatile during the crisis period, ranging from INR54,000-60,000 per metric ton up to INR150,000 per metric ton and back down to INR80,000-90,000 per metric ton.

Elevated and uncertain energy prices increased sourcing difficulty, which management said drove higher percentage and rupee-term distribution margins, though this is not booked as an inventory gain since inventory is held at cost and for short duration (under a month).

subsections.label: Government Policy on LPG Subsidy / PNG Push
points: An analyst raised the government's move to reduce subsidized LPG cylinders from 9 to 4 and push for increased PNG adoption as a potential risk to the logistics business.

Management responded that India's per-capita energy consumption remains among the lowest in the world (comparable to Philippines), and as a developing country there is large dependency on dirty fuels (coal ~2,000 million tons, versus natural gas ~50-60 million tons and LPG ~30-35 million tons), implying ample room for growth in clean fuels including PNG, natural gas, LPG and ammonia despite the subsidy policy shift.

subsections.label: FY27 and Beyond Outlook
points: Management confident of maintaining the same momentum for FY27 as achieved in FY26.

Company philosophy is to under-promise and over-deliver (conservative management approach), rather than raise the long-standing 25% CAGR guidance despite beating it with 41% PAT growth in FY26 and 32% EPS CAGR over 5 years.
Base for growth is now much larger (EPS moved from INR6 at first guidance to INR26 currently) yet CAGR guidance target has not changed.

Longer-term perspective from FY28 onwards expected to benefit from strong foundations laid and additional opportunities arising from war-related uncertainty; management to update as these come to fruition.
Gas EBITDA expected to continue growing well due to full-year effect of terminals commissioned mid-year, multimodal evacuation infrastructure ramp-up, and continued volume growth.
Distribution margin of ~INR7,000/ton expected to be assured for FY27 (Q1 already performing well), with growth beyond FY27 driven more by volumes as procurement efficiencies scale.
Revenue expected to grow year-on-year as a product of both volume growth and price, even if prices stabilize.

subsections.label: Ammonia Business Outlook
points: Management very bullish on ammonia opportunity citing a projected ~3 million ton India supply-demand gap by FY29 per CRISIL/DRHP data.
Difficult to project exact FY30 ammonia (and combined LPG) volume targets at this early stage; ultimate volumes will depend on how many terminals are constructed/commissioned and locations secured.
Strategic partner Itochu is expanding involvement, including hard-asset participation (10% stake in Pipavav terminal, intent to raise to 25%).

guidance_ledger.statement: We definitely, again, reiterate...25% CAGR growth is not small. We have achieved 32% last five years.
We will see a $1.2 billion aggregate capex by March '27 that we have already shared.

We have identified a capex pipeline of approximately 5 billion through 2030...March '28, we would again see a capex up to INR5,000 crores coming in...you will have up to '28, we have already said, we will be $1.2 billion and then again INR5,000 crores...thereafter, you can spread it out in the next 3 years to reach $5 billion.
We'll pursue this growth with disciplined funding through balanced mix of equity, internal accruals and debt targeting a gearing ratio of approximately 0.6x.
We always had a target of 2 million tons. So, we expect that to reach by '28...that means that ammonia distribution would form part of this 2 million gas distribution that we intend to do.

We think, going ahead, we feel confident that these are sustainable margins...we expect INR7,000 to sustain from here on...for '26, '27, you are already assured of a INR7,000 average margin realization.
Overall, gas EBITDA of course will continue to grow really well going forward.
We should see normalcy return back...maybe beginning sometime in Q2 onwards.
In the current year, we expect around -- as we do in LPG, we expect around 25% utilization in the first year and thereafter growing at the rate of 30%, 40% year-on-year.
Distribution similarly, we expect somewhere around 200,000 tons to begin with and then growing 20%, 30% year-on-year.
The margins are for throughput in the ranges from around 2,500 to 3,000. In distribution, it could go up to INR5,000 depending on how the market behaves.

Our volumes are expected to grow really significantly over this year and the next. And prices, even though they stabilize going forward, volumes will take care. So, we expect the revenue also to grow year-on-year.

We will try our best to see what best volume achievement we can do by '29-'30...difficult to today project. This is a new product...but looking at the macros and looking at what lies ahead, we are very bullish.
We are confident to maintain for FY27 the same momentum...I'm confident that FY27 will continue the strong momentum that we have.

risk_register.note: Management downplayed the risk citing India's very low per-capita energy consumption and large scope for growth across all energy sources including LPG, PNG, natural gas and ammonia.

risk_register.risk: Phasing of capacity additions impacting Liquid segment margins

themes.label: Record profitability / breakout growth
themes.note: FY26 revenue up 23%, EBITDA up 36%, PAT up 41% crossing INR1,000 crore PAT milestone; Q4 was the strongest quarter ever.

themes.label: Capacity expansion across ports
themes.note: Major multi-port expansion underway at Mumbai, JNPT, Kandla, Pipavav, Kochi and Mangalore covering liquid, LPG and ammonia storage.

themes.label: Distribution margin sustainability
themes.note: Distribution margins rose to ~INR7,000/ton from ~INR4,000, driven by volume growth and energy price uncertainty; management expects this to sustain into FY27 and beyond.

themes.label: Middle East supply disruption / geopolitical risk
themes.note: West Asia conflict caused LPG shortfalls (50% in April, 30% in May) but is easing, with normalcy expected around Q2 FY27 as alternative global sources develop.

themes.label: Ammonia business entry
themes.note: New ammonia terminal and distribution business being built at Pipavav (Hindustan Zinc take-or-pay) and via L&T MoU at Kandla, targeting a projected 3 million ton India supply-demand gap by FY29.

themes.label: Strategic JV partnerships (Itochu, Vopak, L&T)
themes.note: High-quality JV partners like Itochu (raising Pipavav stake to 25%) and Vopak give an edge in sourcing alternative gas supplies and executing expansion.

themes.label: Conservative guidance philosophy
themes.note: Management reiterated unchanged 25% CAGR guidance despite outperforming it, citing a philosophy to under-promise and over-deliver.

key_takeaways: Revenues grew 23% year-on-year to INR8,333 crores.
Normalized EBITDA rose 36% to INR1,599 crores.
Profit after tax grew 41% to INR1,107 crores crossing the symbolic INR1,000 crores profit after tax milestone for the first time.
Cash and investments on the balance sheet reached approximately INR6,000 crores.
Over the last 5 years, we have delivered an earnings per share cumulative average growth rate of 32% with a consistent dividend track record.
Our fourth quarter was particularly strong with revenue up 52%, EBITDA up by 54% and profit after tax up 43% year-on-year.
The Board has recommended a final dividend of INR6.70 per share for FY '26 bringing the aggregate dividend for the year to INR8.7 per share.
LPG business recorded its highest ever revenue of INR7,689 crores, up 26% year-on-year, with EBITDA growing 68% to INR1,131 crores, driven by record logistics and distribution volumes.
pressing_questions: Nandan (Investor): asked why the company doesn't increase its 25% CAGR guidance given FY26 PAT growth of 43% and a $5 billion capex plan, to which management reiterated its conservative philosophy and unchanged guidance.

Nandan (Investor): asked for the company's goal for ammonia distribution by 2030 and LPG target by FY30, to which management said it is difficult to project today given ammonia is a new product, though they are 'very bullish'.
Anil Sareen (K16 Advisors): asked whether the Vadhavan port MoU investment is included in the $5 billion capex figure; management said only part of it will likely be included, not all.

Rajesh Agarwal (Moneyore): asked hypothetically whether the company could recover all old volumes and grow if Hormuz doesn't open for the next three months; management said yes, as supply sources would shift to alternatives worldwide.

SCHAEFFLER.about: Schaeffler India Ltd is engaged in the development, manufacturing and distribution of high-precision roller and ball bearings, engine systems and transmission components, chassis applications, clutch systems and related machine building manufacturing activities.[1]

quarters.summary: Management expects to recover lost earnings ground in H2CY26 as price/FX/steel indexation traction is expected in the second half; capex for CY26 remains guided at INR 400-500 crores with the remaining ~INR 300-325 crores to be spent in H2; exports growth momentum (28% YoY H1) is expected to be sustained cautiously (management prefers to cap exports at ~20% of revenue as a natural hedge rather than issue a growth guidance); industrial/BIS segment aspires to reach double-digit growth though non-mobility industrial already grew double-digit; KRSV/Koovers EBITDA/cash breakeven is expected only by 2029.

subsections.label: EBITDA drivers
points: Gross margin improvement contributed about INR 147 crores to EBITDA
Offset partly by increased employee cost due to new Labor Codes/wage cost implementation and some other income expenses
Net effect was a strong EBITDA performance despite cost headwinds

subsections.label: Free cash flow / working capital
points: Free cash flow was lower, attributable to input costs going up and inventories rising
Inventory build-up is a strategic/planned step to shore up stock in some business sectors ahead of evolving geopolitical situation and market demand
LPG and oil price increases raised input costs, which are yet to be compensated by customers (in discussion)
Freight cost increases and some IT costs also impacted the bottom line in the quarter
Working capital rise to INR 2,029 crores is a planned activity tied to inventory build-up for specific sectors/customer accounts, expected to be managed and recovered going forward
Management expects to recover lost ground on free cash flow in H2 of the year

subsections.label: Cost pass-through / customer recovery
points: Automotive OEM pricing works on an indexation mechanism; not all commodities (e.g., Labor Wage Code increases) are on the indexation list, making customer compensation difficult
Dialogue ongoing with OEMs on input cost increases from LPG/propane price rises due to the West Asia situation (not in indexation list)
Positive traction on price corrections expected in H2 of the year, along with steel price indexation
Customers generally expect the company to implement productivity measures (VA/VE) to absorb non-indexed cost increases rather than reimburse directly
Other expenses increase of 0.3 percentage points (from 15.1% to 15.4%) mainly due to fuel price increases; Q1 impact was only for the month of March, Q2 reflects full-quarter impact
Capacity constraint at the Hosur plant led to air freight costs for both incoming and outgoing material due to prioritizing OEM demand over VLS

subsections.label: Intercompany/export pricing methodology
points: Intercompany export pricing is done at arm's length pricing principles as per OECD guidelines
Transfer prices are determined with a true-up done at end of year in December

subsections.label: Automotive Technologies
points: Growth driven by both conventional ICE business (~20% growth) and e-mobility (timing difference contributing remaining growth)
Despite industry passenger vehicle production declining ~8% QoQ, company grew business by 3.6%, reflecting market share gains rather than higher content per vehicle or underlying volume growth
New business wins: double clutch adoption increasing in tractor segment; overrunning alternator pulley win bringing compactness to system package

subsections.label: Vehicle Lifetime Solutions (VLS/aftermarket)
points: Growth momentum (historically >20%, minimum 20% over last 3 years) slowed to 9.9-10% in Q2
Slowdown attributed to capacity constraints (notably at Hosur plant) which force prioritization of OEM demand over VLS/aftermarket during high-growth periods
Capacity gap being addressed currently; issue is not only Schaeffler's own capacity but also local supplier/supply chain capacities still under development
REPXPERT vans revived after a two-year gap, covering ~8,000 km across the country for mechanic training/upskilling and focused campaigns/workshop engagements
Portfolio expansion focus particularly on INA product range for the aftermarket

subsections.label: Bearings and Industrial Solutions (BIS)/Industrial
points: Strong new business acquisitions in the quarter across cylindrical roller bearings, DGBBs, spherical rollers, TRBs, and tri-plain bearings for raw material sector — one of the largest/highest-value industrial business acquisitions in the quarter
Core metal/raw material sector (steel, aluminium, cement) showed strong traction due to infrastructure growth, with localization of parts to serve this sector
Power transmission sector strong, ~8% growth in Q2
Wind energy saw a dip in revenue due to timing and ongoing contract negotiation/renegotiation processes with global customers; expected to recover over time
Railways sector lagged due to tender-based nature of business, with little growth QoQ
Industrial automation doing okay but room to improve via new product portfolio additions
Distribution/aftermarket side of industrial business seen as an area of opportunity, showing recovery over preceding quarter

Automotive Bearings business (within BIS) under pressure — more commoditized; company prioritizing competitiveness/margin over top-line growth, focusing on cost competitiveness and further localization
Non-mobility side of BIS (ex-automotive bearings) grew double-digit overall

subsections.label: KRSV Innovative Auto Solutions (Koovers)
points: Wholly owned subsidiary; revenue growth of INR 79 crores delivered exactly as per committed plan
EBITDA still negative as focus remains on scaling up operations

EBITDA margin change from 13.4% to 17.3% (negative movement) driven by two one-off items: introduction of sales cutoff accounting policy adjusting revenue by INR 5.6 crores, and provision for founders' bonus (payable next year in May, over 3 years) with ~INR 3 crore impact
EBITDA and cash flow breakeven expected only by 2029

subsections.label: Export drivers
points: Growth mainly due to intercompany allocations, as localization builds capacities in India (mainly at Savli), which the group leverages to serve intercompany locations worldwide when capacity is available
Demand from all regions - Europe, Asia Pacific, China - has been in double-digit range, contributing to growth
FX has been favorable, though not significantly for Europe (rupee billing there); other regions like Americas, Asia Pacific, Greater China have US dollar billing benefiting from FX
Management will be careful with future guidance due to ongoing geopolitical disruptions; recalls a similar surge reversal experienced in 2023
Order book for exports for the year is described as solid

No formal growth guidance was given historically — company's stated wish/target is to cap exports at ~20% of revenue for a good balance between domestic and exports, and for natural hedging against imports

subsections.label: Customer awards and recognitions
points: Industrial side: awards from Voith Turbo and Sandvik Mining, recognizing focused development and cost reduction activities
Automotive side: awards from John Deere and Toyota Kirloskar; appreciation award from Denso India; special category award from Escorts Kubota for long association
Zero PPM quality award received from Toyota Kirloskar, one of the most stringent quality-demanding customers, underlining commitment to zero-defect products
CSR recognition: award from CSR Convention for community development projects, including work in developing tribal areas

subsections.label: Capacity constraint resolution
points: Company addressing capacity gap that constrains VLS demand fulfillment, including both Schaeffler's own capacity and local supplier development
Working to align entire supply chain (own and supplier) with increased demand on both OEM and VLS sides

subsections.label: Macro/geopolitical
points: GDP growth showing a marked slowdown amid geopolitical situations redefining business rules even in India
Inflation (CPI) has started creeping up after a good trend in the preceding four quarters, driven by rising input costs in manufacturing and rising food prices reflected in commodity prices

Coal production declining consistently over last two months in line with carbon neutrality/renewable energy directives, while electricity generation remains positive, indicating shift toward renewables

subsections.label: Automotive sector risk
points: Passenger vehicle segment saw a production drop of ~8% in June over May, though still up 15.7% YoY

Tractor sector growth positive but requires close monitoring due to not-so-good monsoon performance so far; delayed monsoon could impact tractor business, on which the company has significant exposure

subsections.label: Input cost / FX / freight risk
points: LPG and oil price increases (due to West Asia situation) have raised input costs, yet to be compensated by customers (in discussion)
Freight cost increases and IT costs impacted bottom line in the quarter

key_takeaways: Revenue generation in the quarter was INR 2,681 crores, which is a clear 17.5% higher performance compared to last year and 7% higher than the preceding quarter Q1'26.

We were able to deliver INR 513 crores at an EBITDA level in the quarter, a clear 19% better performance than last year, resulting in a profit after tax of INR 336-337 crores, or about 12.6% profit after tax.

We also did register reasonably good free cash flow, though a little lower, attributable to input costs going up, inventories going up (a strategic step to shore up inventories), LPG and oil prices going up (yet to be compensated by customers), freight cost increases, and some IT costs.

Automotive Technologies brought in 33% growth compared to year-on-year, Vehicle Lifetime Solutions at 9.9%, Bearings and Industrial grew by about 5% on average over the year, and our export business grew 24%.
35% of our revenue comes from Automotive Technologies, Bearings and Industrial Solutions brings in about 35%, Vehicle Lifetime Solutions 12%, and exports about 17%.
KRSV/Koovers registered a revenue growth of INR 79 crores in the quarter, exactly delivering as per the committed plan, though EBITDA remains negative as focus is on scaling up operations.
At consolidated Schaeffler India Limited level (both entities put together), revenue generation has been INR 2,760 crores at an EBITDA of 18.5% and an EBIT of 15.2%.
Working capital has gone up to INR 2,029 crores, which is a planned activity to build up inventories in some specific sectors for specific customer accounts.
Capex for CY26 remains guided at INR 400-500 crores, with the remaining amount expected to be consumed in the second half of the year.
pressing_questions: Is the portfolio recalibration now complete in the industrial segment? Roughly, how much revenue did you consciously let go? And when does BIS return to double-digit growth?

On exports: in H1 we have grown about 28% YoY, well above the FY26 guidance of about 10%-12% growth. What is sustaining this momentum? Is this more of intercompany allocation, China Plus One, new geographical mandates, or rupee depreciation gains? How much H2 visibility do we have, and would you revise the CY26 export guidance further? Has there been any change in the geography mix between Europe, U.S., Southeast Asia and China?

On aftermarket: growth has come down to 9.9%-10% in Q2 versus historical >20% growth. Considering revenue has reached a large size, would growth be stable going forward, or can it reach higher levels given portfolio expansion efforts?

On cost: how are you managing commodity cost pass-through given the lag typically seen across auto component suppliers? On the minimum wage hike, are OEMs responding positively, and do you expect compensation in the coming quarter? Is the elevated level of other expenses (freight, IT costs) a one-off or should this level continue?
On pricing: how does pricing work across different segments — intercompany/exports vs OEMs vs aftermarket — with respect to commodity costs and forex?

On the non-mobility Bearings and Industrial segment, which has remained at ~INR 400 crores for the last six to eight quarters, have market shares remained stable, and could the large order wins mentioned change the trajectory of this number?
On KRSV/Koovers: revenue was flat quarter-on-quarter at INR 79-80 crores, but EBITDA margin worsened from 13.4% to 17.3% — why, and when is breakeven on EBITDA and cash flow expected?
On Automotive Technologies: what is driving the very strong 31%-33.3% run rate in the first two quarters — is it e-Axle related, and is it sustainable in H2?

On capex: with CY26 capex pegged at INR 400-500 crores and INR 175 crores spent so far, will the remaining INR 250-300 crores be deployed in H2? Can you provide the capex breakup between maintenance, automotive, industrial bearing localization and the Shoolagiri plant?

quarters.summary: Schaeffler India posted 18.8% YoY revenue growth in Q1 CY26 to INR 2,507 crores with EBITDA at 19.3% margin, though revenue declined 5.1% QoQ due to planned cost/portfolio calibration in Bearings & Industrial Solutions and a liquidity crunch impacting aftermarket demand. Management does not issue formal guidance but expressed confidence in sustaining committed numbers for CY26, expects full-year export growth of 10-12%, and continues capex in the INR 400-500 crore range with ongoing e-axle and bearing localization (reaching ~80% overall).

subsections.label: Automotive Technologies
points: Encompasses both ICE engines and electric mobility; strong performance across almost all product portfolios in ICE applications, hybrid technology also did well.

Outperformance versus underlying automotive production growth (~15%) attributed to presence across all technology platforms (ICE, hybrid, e-mobility); management sees this driven by ICE product portfolio strength this quarter, not yet from Vitesco integration benefits.

Vitesco integration benefits are yet to come for Schaeffler India stand-alone; globally seen as one entity but in India still two separate legal entities; potential synergies expected in coming quarters on e-mobility side, no legal integration currently on the cards.

subsections.label: Bearings and Industrial Solutions
points: Significant QoQ drop (-14.3%) attributed to planned recalibration/cost correction exercises carried out at the beginning of the year to balance top-line and bottom-line delivery.

Multiple contributing causes cited: continued localization efforts, product/market/application mix adjustments, intensifying local competition (including localized industrial bearing capacity), and demand softness particularly in industrial aftermarket due to liquidity crunch among distributors.

Aftermarket softness described as seasonal — Q1 industrial distribution/aftermarket is typically lower due to inventory correction around March 31st liquidity crunch; historically corrects in subsequent quarters.

Despite market-level softness, capacity utilization not impacted because idle capacity compensated through exports of industrial bearings; no cost pressure as lines remain effectively utilized; capacity utilization at plant above 80% given ~80% localization.

No major slowdown seen in power transmission or railways; some slowdown in aftermarket segment; mining sector shows little traction while infrastructure-linked sectors (cement, steel) doing well; renewable energy remains strong; overall mixed picture across end sectors (energy sector saw ups and downs).
Large wins secured in quarter in spherical roller bearings, housing area, large TRBs (tapered roller bearings) and CRBs (cylindrical roller bearings), and raw material sector.

subsections.label: Vehicle Lifetime Solutions (aftermarket)
points: Posted robust double-digit growth of 18.1% YoY; continued portfolio expansion with new products conforming to BS-VI requirements as market demand increased.

subsections.label: Battery Management Systems (BMS)
points: BMS currently sold as a stand-alone unit to customers, not integrated with e-axle; going forward, as e-axle business evolves, BMS may get integrated within complete scope of offerings.

Content per vehicle cannot be measured for BMS alone; must be totaled across full product offering (bearings, engine/transmission parts, motor, reducer, power electronics, sensors) and must be split between ICE and battery electric vehicle technology.

System-level e-axle offering (motor + reducer gearbox + power electronics) commands much higher value versus component-level offering — system level value potentially running into five digits versus component level ranging from two to four digits.

subsections.label: Localization
points: Localization percentage has reached up to 80% overall (total revenue basis, not just industrial); company continues focus on capital efficiency.
Within industrial space specifically for bearings, localization is around 60%, with still enough room to further localize.

100% localization considered unlikely as technologies evolve — e.g., e-axle initial volumes are lower, and a complete dedicated line cannot be built for a handful of bearings; in a growing, double-digit-growth economy like India, full localization is seen as impractical.

subsections.label: UK Catch Line Relocation / Shoolagiri Plant
points: UK catch line relocation process ongoing; machines have started arriving.
Company is contemplating building a second hall at the Shoolagiri plant (new greenfield project).
Line transfer is on track; focus now needed on expediting business acquisition side to fill the new capacity.

subsections.label: E-axle Localization Phase 2
points: E-axle localization is in Phase 2, focused on developing a local supplier base to source child parts (e.g., magnets currently still imported from outside India) locally and reduce imports.
Manufacturing line is being set up simultaneously with supplier base development; both are happening in parallel.
E-mobility/e-axle supply chain routes primarily through China rather than Europe, making the company competitive in the Indian market versus cheaper EU-FTA imports.
Long-term potential to move into assembly of modules from suppliers depending on competency/capability of Indian supplier base evolving; business model could be modified as suppliers mature.

subsections.label: Export Markets
points: Key export geographies served: Europe, China, Southeast Asia countries, and Americas.
No current dip in export demand seen across these geographies despite crude price spikes affecting APAC/Southeast Asia broadly.
Order book for the year is solid, current run rate showing minimum 10% growth expected, likely landing at 10-12% for full year (revised up from prior guidance of 5-10%).
Last two years focus on Southeast Asia business development in exports is now bearing fruit.
Exports are conducted entirely through intercompany/related-party group entities that book orders and resell to end customers; Schaeffler India does not export directly to end customers.

Export growth is a function of intercompany partners' order books and the group's decision on where to manufacture — group first evaluates local demand, and if local demand is strong, lines are shifted to India, after which global market is served from India as a 'best cost country'; there is no standalone strategy focused purely on maximizing exports.

subsections.label: Middle East / West Asia Supply Chain Crisis
points: Strong headwinds faced on supply chain due to Middle East/West Asia geopolitical crisis; daily crisis management team meetings instituted to keep supply chain intact.
Fuel-related input categories such as LPG and propane, which India relies heavily on imports for, have seen price increases due to choking of supply chains from the West Asia situation.

Mitigation actions include looking at alternate sourcing routes, stocking up on certain items, and exploring possibility of cost compensation from customers; too early to assess success as it has been only ~1.5 months since inflationary increases began.
Inventory buildup occurred during the quarter linked to these supply chain issues; outlook for coming quarters expected to be better.

subsections.label: Customer Awards (Q1 CY26)
points: John Deere Partner Level Excellence Award — for strong engagement from product development through business securing and serial supplies, predominantly in clutches for transmission applications.
TVS Mobility award under Vehicle Lifetime Solutions vertical, recognizing strategic partner engagement — marks the beginning of a new journey with TVS Mobility.

Rail Analysis award — first-time recognition as a valued supplier to Indian Railways and Metros, specifically for Innovation in Underframe Components and Engineering (insulation coated bearings) enabling superior performance and higher reliability.

Adani Power (largest customer in India) award — for extensive engagement, strong on-ground presence, robust distributor network, and technical engagement on their Mundra thermal power plant; recognized for innovative product offering.

ELIN (erstwhile Voith company, wind turbine generator manufacturer) valued supplier award — for outstanding contribution to quality and partnership, reflecting reliability of products supplied to wind sector.
John Deere aftermarket space award — for outstanding performance and on-time deliveries in the Vehicle Lifetime Solutions/aftermarket space.

subsections.label: Competitive Dynamics
points: Competition intensifying within India, including local players building localized industrial bearing capacity, contributing to portfolio recalibration decisions.

On e-axle, competition includes Tata AutoComp-Bosch JV; management states it is aware of competitive landscape and has a strategy to manage it while continuing focus on innovation and differentiation, without direct concern expressed.
Management declined to specify which competitors (MNC, local, or unorganized players) are gaining share in segments where recalibration occurred, stating this is for analysts to check independently.

Aftermarket portfolio expanded with new products conforming to BS-VI requirements.
Bearings and Industrial Solutions secured large wins in spherical roller bearings, housing area, large TRBs, CRBs, and raw material sector.

subsections.label: Vitesco Integration
points: Globally Schaeffler and Vitesco are seen as one entity; in India, Schaeffler India Limited and the Vitesco-related entity remain two separate legal entities.

Benefits of Vitesco integration (e.g., leveraging electronics competencies) have not yet materialized for Schaeffler India stand-alone; potential synergies expected in coming quarters especially on the e-mobility side; no legal integration currently planned.

subsections.label: Portfolio Recalibration
points: Company undertook a deliberate, more concerted recalibration/cost-correction exercise at the start of the year (compared to smaller, account-level corrections done throughout the year in the past) in the Bearings and Industrial Solutions segment to balance top-line and bottom-line delivery.

Recalibration exercise began in Q4 of last year and has now culminated; strategic intent is to focus capacity where the company is most competitive and generates the most value, even if it means giving up business that would otherwise erode profitability.

subsections.label: Geopolitical / Supply Chain Risk
points: Middle East/West Asia geopolitical conflict has created strong headwinds on the supply chain, particularly around fuel-related input costs (LPG, propane) that India relies on imports for.
Currency sensitivity — Indian rupee depreciation reduces overall GDP size in dollar terms and affects global ranking, though domestic growth stability is seen as more important.

subsections.label: Liquidity Crunch
points: Liquidity crunch observed in the market, particularly impacting cash flows to the distributor community in the industrial aftermarket segment, viewed as seasonal (linked to March 31st inventory correction) and expected to correct in subsequent quarters based on past experience.

subsections.label: Competitive Intensity
points: Intensifying competition within India, including localized industrial bearing capacity build-out by competitors, contributing to pricing pressure and portfolio recalibration.

subsections.label: Sectoral Demand Mix
points: Mining sector showing little traction; energy sector has seen mixed ups and downs, though renewable energy remains strong; overall sectoral picture uneven ('not all sectors firing on all cylinders').

subsections.label: Import Dependency
points: Certain child parts for e-mobility/e-axle products (e.g., magnets) still need to be imported as domestic supply chain does not yet exist for these special parts.

subsections.label: No Formal Guidance Policy
points: Management confirmed the company does not issue formal revenue or margin guidance (e.g., for CY27/CY28).
Only color provided is a general commitment to deliver the numbers the company says it wants to deliver, to maintain investor trust.

points: Management does not see major concerns in delivering committed numbers for the year, though continued monitoring and agility required given geopolitical supply chain headwinds; crisis management team meets daily to manage the situation.

points: Automotive sector demand trend expected to remain robust going forward given management's optimism across all technology platforms (ICE, hybrid, e-mobility).

subsections.label: Sequential margin drivers
points: Against Q4 FY'26, revenue rose Rs.350 crore to Rs.380 crore (+Rs.29 crore) but EBITDA fell from Rs.143 crore to Rs.139 crore and margin fell from 40% to 35%; PAT fell from Rs.69 crore to Rs.65 crore — top line grew while margin was given back.

Core crane rental EBITDA margin moved from 53% in FY26 to 47% in Q1 FY27, a 6-point drop, attributed to four components: (1) higher ECL provisions (~Rs.6.2 crore) driven by aging of receivables, expected to rationalize as collections improve; (2) mark-to-market reinstatement of foreign currency loan (Rs.1.4 crore), a non-cash accounting entry; (3) one-time incentive paid to frontline employees and senior management for surpassing Rs.1,000 crore top line in FY26 and extraordinary performance; (4) change in revenue mix — incremental demand served through higher ancillary equipment and cross rental of cranes rather than fresh capex.

Management characterized the higher-ancillary/cross-rental mix shift as a deliberate capital allocation choice, not margin leakage — these carry lower percentage margin but consume no capital, making them accretive to ROCE and cash generation despite being optically margin-dilutive.
Excluding forex and incentive items, underlying core margin for the quarter was approximately 49%; if credit provisions normalize during the year, core margin could cross 51%.
Core margins are regarded as structurally intact; FY27 guidance of Rs.525-575 crore EBITDA remains unchanged.

subsections.label: Working capital / DSO
points: Group DSO stood at 116 days, comprising crane rental 124 days, renewable E&C 98 days and GCC business 201 days.
This year's collection focus is heightened, and GCC collection improved in July after quarter-end June'26.
GCC DSO of 201 days reflects disruption from the USA/Israel-Iran conflict in West Asia; significant recovery occurred in July and improvement is expected to be visible in Q2 results.
Despite higher DSO in KSA versus India, the company maintains zero working capital draw in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, indicating no cash being pumped into operations there.

subsections.label: ECL provisioning
points: ECL provision is mostly related to India, with none attributable to KSA or other countries.

ECL is expected to normalize over the course of the financial year as aged debtors are recovered; a statistical model dictates the provisioning, and a positive swing of Rs.3-4 crore was added back to Q4 FY26.

subsections.label: Balance sheet / capital allocation
points: Gross debt-to-equity of 0.54x is against a guided FY ceiling of 0.72x (on a consolidated basis); this is a gross-level, not net-level, figure.
Net of a treasury surplus of over Rs.300 crore, effective net debt-to-equity is in the range of 0.3 to 0.7.
Debt-to-equity of 0.72 for FY27 is deemed comfortable; capex is planned conservatively to keep debt levels under control.

Debt in India is taken in INR at ~8% +/-0.25%; overseas debt is in USD at SOFR + 5.5-6% spread; blended weighted average cost of borrowing is a balance sheet item not disclosed quarterly (to be disclosed at half-year results).

subsections.label: Business mix commentary
points: Renewable business ran ahead of full-year mix expectation in Q1 due to execution phasing; for the full year, crane rental is expected to remain roughly two-thirds of revenue and renewable E&C roughly one-third, with renewable revenue scaling up in H2 following capex deployment later in the year.
Saudi operation has now delivered cumulative EBITDA-positive performance, an important milestone in the first year of operation.

subsections.label: Renewables (Sangreen) as complementary business
points: Sangreen Future Renewable Ltd is described as an asset-light, high-ROCE complement to the core crane rental business, generating incremental EBITDA without consuming capital and securing crane fleet demand through integrated execution.

The renewables business (with lower EBITDA margin) can grow beyond the balance sheet since it doesn't require deployment of capital in Sangreen; the entire capex remains dedicated to the crane rental business.
Blended EBITDA margin will be lower as renewables scale, but absolute EBITDA has grown significantly (FY26 EBITDA was Rs.429 crore vs FY27 guided Rs.525-575 crore, implying 20-30% growth).

subsections.label: Wind E&C margin trajectory
points: Wind E&C EBITDA margin rose from 11% to 18% YoY (before unallocated expenses); after distributing unallocated expenses across segments, margin is 10-12%.

Management expects the E&C business to settle around 12-15% margin going forward, as it is not classified as an EPC business (no procurement; turbine is free-issue from OEM/IPP) but rather engineering and construction, competing against unorganized players; Sangreen's scale, legacy (18-20 GW of wind turbine erection since the wind industry's inception in India) and governance help secure preferential rates from large PE-fund clients.

As the business scales, margin can face deprecation due to execution slowdown from client-side delays (site readiness, OEM supply, local ROW issues) or internal delays, causing lumpiness in revenue recognition under percentage-of-completion accounting.

The E&C business has doubled revenue every year for three years (from ~Rs.250 crore in year one, doubling to ~Rs.500 crore combining SFRPL and SLPL last year), with an expectation to double again this year, subject to execution capability.

Sangreen order book stood at Rs.680 crore at quarter-end, with E&C order book of Rs.686 crore currently and an inquiry pipeline of Rs.4,656 crore; approximately 15% of the current E&C order book may get postponed to next FY.

subsections.label: GCC / KSA yield and margin
points: India and Botswana business reported utilization of ~86% at a yield of 2.29%; GCC business utilization was also 86% at a yield of 4.10% — the yield differential (4.1% vs 2.29%) is described as the core of the Middle East investment thesis.
GCC total income was Rs.19 crore with EBITDA margin of 23% in Q1 FY27.

KSA EBITDA margin (~47%) is lower than India due to higher cost of operations in Saudi Arabia; management expects to pull up the EBITDA profile over time by leveraging 37 years of Indian operational history and legacy.
Yield in KSA is expected to be maintained at ~4%, notwithstanding current West Asia disruption; yield is clarified as a return on asset, not a margin figure.

subsections.label: Capex deployment plan
points: Fleet size stands at 492 cranes with a gross block of ~Rs.3,300 crore.

FY27 capex pool of Rs.652 crore approved by the board; Rs.92 crore already capitalized in Q1, with the balance Rs.560 crore to be deployed in H2, contingent on continuous monitoring of OEM delivery and project commissioning dates.
Substantially all of the capex pool is revenue generating, with an expected ~15% increase in revenue within FY27 attributable to this investment.

Entirety of FY27 capex remains dedicated to the crane rental business (Rs.652 crore), deployed at minimum 80% utilization and 2% yield hurdle; crane business is described as capex-heavy, high-EBITDA business.
India CAPEX for FY27 is ~Rs.190 crore; KSA CAPEX referenced by an analyst at ~Rs.200 crore.

subsections.label: Utilization metrics
points: India/Botswana utilization ~86% at 2.29% yield; GCC utilization ~86% at 4.10% yield in Q1 FY27.

Utilization is calculated as rental revenue divided by number of days (not to be confused with yield); prior year annualized utilization was ~80%, which management characterizes as near-100% effective utilization once mobilization/demobilization and maintenance downtime are accounted for; Q1's 86% utilization is characterized as near-100% on the same adjusted basis.

subsections.label: GCC/Middle East capex deployment amid disruption
points: Given West Asia disruption, no structural changes to the Middle East investment hypothesis; management sees only a temporary supply-chain disruption expected to normalize within the financial year (a few months to quarters).

Middle East capex allotment of ~300+ crore (324 crore), of which 316 crore is revenue-generating; orders already placed with equipment manufacturers who are responsible for delivering equipment to Saudi Arabia (via Jeddah or Dammam); no delay is anticipated, and this capex is expected to come online for revenue generation between Q3 and Q4 of the financial year.

subsections.label: Capital allocation framework
points: As international markets open, the company's role transforms from crane rental operator to capital allocator; capex decisions weigh inquiry pipeline, order visibility, order duration, look-ahead visibility for a crane, need to secure market share, and internal hurdle rate (IRR), all while maintaining group ROCE.

Group now operates across India, Saudi Arabia, Botswana and Qatar with a professional leadership team, broader product portfolio and higher-return business models (referred to as 'Elevate 2030' progressing in line with commitments).
Depot addition strategy is planned across KSA and other operating countries (currently KSA and Qatar); location and timelines not disclosed as of now.
Middle East 0-24 month pipeline stands at $38 million.

subsections.label: Macro backdrop
points: India continues to be the fastest-growing major economy; growth is described as investment-led with record government capex (Rs.12.2 lakh crore), expanding manufacturing and construction, easing financing costs (100 bps repo rate cut) and controlled inflation; India GDP grew 7.7% in FY26, tracking ~6.6% in Q1 FY27.
This environment directly translates into demand across sectors served by the company, including refining, steel, cement, power, renewables, infrastructure and heavy engineering.

subsections.label: Sector capacity build-out
points: India is adding capacity across every sector served: wind added a record 6 GW last year with ~29 GW under construction; thermal has 62 GW under bid or award; steel targets 300 million tons by 2030; cement is adding over 160 million tons; nuclear sector is opening to privatization under the SHANTI Act — each requiring heavy lift services, offering long-term opportunities for heavy lift and specialized crane services.
Saudi Aramco plans to spend approximately $0.5 trillion over the next 5 years, a key driver of Middle East demand.

subsections.label: Competitive positioning
points: Yields in India have improved over the last quarter; management does not see yields being capped by competition, and states there remains tremendous demand for cranes in the country.
No material shift observed in customer behavior on contract tenure or rate resets in India as of now.

In the E&C/wind segment, competition exists but is not organized; Sanghvi/Sangreen is positioned as the only organized, well-structured, well-governed player, which matters to large PE-fund clients requiring financially solvent, proven-execution partners.

Ranked third largest crane rental company globally by International Cranes magazine (industry gold standard), based on cumulative lifting capacity; largest is Mammoet (PE-family owned), second is Sarens.
Company describes itself as pivoting from single-country crane rental business to a capital allocator across markets, chasing the right return while maintaining ROCE for stakeholders.

subsections.label: Safety and brand strength
points: Management acknowledged there have been accidents historically, though the safety record is described as 'almost impeccable'; checklists, SOPs and safety councils are in place, with safety treated as a key value differentiator with clients.

Company has 36+ years of developed operating, technical and safety capabilities since importing its first crane when no local operator existed for the imported German technology; institutional knowledge and seasoned personnel are transferred to new markets (e.g., KSA) to maintain brand reputation.
Company is one of the fastest crane rental companies approved to work with Saudi Aramco (the gold lifting standard globally) and has already executed a shutdown job for Aramco.

subsections.label: Elevate 2030 / organizational strengthening
points: Elevate 2030 initiative progressing in line with commitments — transformation from single-country crane rental business to a group operating across India, Saudi Arabia, Botswana and Qatar with professional leadership, broader product portfolio and higher-return business models.

Focus areas include enhancing customer centricity through digital initiatives (improving responsiveness, transparency, service delivery), pursuing international expansion into new markets to diversify revenue base and strengthen global presence, and advancing digital transformation with a scheduled go-live for new HRMS and CRM software.

Renewables business (Sangreen) scope of work varies contract-to-contract across five service offerings: mechanical (crane, manpower, inter-carting, turbine commissioning), electrical, civil, ROW land/permits, and surface logistics, depending on client, contract and location.

subsections.label: Receivables / ECL risk
points: Higher ECL provisions (Rs.6.2 crore) driven by aging of receivables impacted Q1 core margin; expected to rationalize as collections improve during the year; provisioning is mostly related to India, not KSA or other countries.

subsections.label: West Asia geopolitical disruption
points: Conflict between USA/Israel and Iran has caused disruption in West Asia, reflected in the elevated GCC DSO of 201 days as of June; significant collections occurred in July, expected to show improvement in Q2 results.

Given the situation, management sees no structural change to its Middle East investment thesis, characterizing the impact as a temporary supply-chain disruption expected to normalize within the financial year (a few months to quarters), with no anticipated delay in bringing capex/equipment online in Saudi Arabia.

subsections.label: Execution / revenue recognition risk in E&C
points: E&C margins can face deprecation as the business scales due to execution slowdowns from both internal and external factors — client-side delays (site readiness, OEM supply, local ROW issues) and internal execution delays — causing lumpiness in revenue recognition under percentage-of-completion accounting.
Approximately 15% of the current E&C order book may get postponed into the next financial year due to delays in project execution caused by clients or internal factors.

subsections.label: Non-cash / accounting items
points: Mark-to-market reinstatement of foreign currency loan (Rs.1.4 crore) is a non-cash accounting entry that impacted reported margin in Q1.

subsections.label: Guidance reaffirmation
points: Guidance stands as published: FY27 consolidated revenue of roughly Rs.1,400-1,500 crore, EBITDA of Rs.525-575 crore, and blended ROCE of 16.25-16.5%; management reiterated this is unchanged despite the Q1 margin dip.
Detailed KPI and guidance disclosures are available in the investor presentation on page 25 (Q1 KPIs) and page 19 (guidance).

For FY28, group revenue is projected to scale 30-40% with EBITDA scaling 20-30% (to Rs.650-700 crore), building off the FY27 EBITDA guidance base of Rs.525-575 crore, itself 20-30% above FY26 EBITDA of Rs.429 crore.

subsections.label: Summary outlook
points: Core business is healthy, renewables are scaling, international operations are gaining traction, and the order book of Rs.1,250 crore provides revenue visibility for the year, supported by a broader project pipeline/inquiry pipeline of Rs.5,600 crore; continued focus on disciplined capital allocation, safety, and sustainable value creation for stakeholders.

key_takeaways: Revenue from operation for Q1 FY'27 was Rs. 380 crores against Rs. 273 crores in Q1 FY'26. That is growth of 39% and total income was Rs. 393 crores against Rs. 281 crores, growth of 40%. EBITDA was Rs. 139 crores against Rs. 107 crores, growth of 30% at a margin of 35%. Profit after tax was Rs. 65 crores against Rs. 50 crores, also 30% growth.
The core crane rental EBITDA margin moved from 53% in FY'26 to 47% in Q1 FY'27. That is a 6% point drop.

Excluding this FOREX and incentive item, the underlying core margin for the quarter was approximately 49% and if the credit provision rationalized as we are expecting in during the course of the year, the return crossed 51%.
Taking all together, we regard this core margin are structurally intact and our guidance for FY'27 is still between Rs. 525 crores to Rs. 575 crores which is unchanged.
Group Days Sales Outstanding (DSO) stood at 116 days which includes crane rental 124 days, renewable E&C 98 days and GCC business 201 days.
The crane rental contributes approximately 60% of revenue from operations and 37% renewable E&C and balance 3% from project EPC.
GCC total income was Rs. 19 crores at an EBITDA margin of 23% and the Saudi operation has now delivered cumulative EBITDA positive performance.

We have a secured order book as I mentioned of almost Rs. 1,250 crores, which is fully executable within this financial year, providing strong revenue visibility. In addition, we have a healthy project pipeline or inquiry pipeline of almost Rs. 5,600 crores across multiple sectors.
Our guideline stands as published. So, FY '27 consolidated revenue of roughly Rs. 1,400 crores to Rs. 1,500 crores, EBITDA of 525 to 575 and a blended return on capital of 16.25 to 16.5.
pressing_questions: FY'27 CAPEX is roughly Rs. 190 crores in India versus Rs. 200 crores in KSA. If you had one incremental crane and you could place it on either side, where does it go today and what is the deciding factor for it? Is it yield, utilization, tenure, payback or anything else?

Is this shift towards KSA a positive view on Saudi or is it partly a view that India's crane rental yields are structurally capped by competition? How do you see competition in India shaping up say over the next one to two years and overall demand and supply scenario for crane rental equipment industry?

Are you seeing any changes in terms of client behavior on contract tenure or say rate resets in India? For example, is a tier one client pushing for a shorter tenure or rate negotiation as and when more fleet becomes available?

quarters.summary: FY26 was a strong year for Sanghvi Movers with consolidated revenue growth of 36.9%, EBITDA growth of 15.6% and PAT growth of 17.7%, driven by 35% growth in India crane rental revenue, partially offset by higher costs from KSA and renewables expansion and Labour Code implementation impact. Management targets continuing similar growth (~30% in core crane rental business) in FY27, expects KSA business to achieve cumulative EBITDA and cash flow positivity within H1 FY27, and guided capex of ~INR 1,030 crores across India and KSA for FY27, with order book of INR 1,053 crores fully executable in the current year and an inquiry pipeline of ~INR 4,000 crores (India) plus $50 million (KSA, 24 months).

subsections.label: Revenue and profit drivers
points: Growth in FY26 top-line and profitability was primarily driven by 35% growth in crane rental revenue in India.
Growth was partially offset by higher costs incurred in expansion of KSA and renewable business along with the impact of Labour Code implementation.
KSA business has started generating positive monthly EBITDA recently and is expected to achieve positive cumulative (ITD) EBITDA by end of H1 FY27.

subsections.label: Balance sheet / net debt clarification
points: An analyst noted gross debt of INR 673 crores less treasury of INR 353 crores would suggest net debt near INR 300-320 crores versus reported INR 612 crores; management clarified the reported net debt figure is a consolidated number shown on a gross block basis under Ind AS, and liabilities cannot be netted off directly — only FDs linked to those liabilities are netted, giving a 'proper gross liability' view rather than netting off the entire treasury.

Management indicated the company has managed net debt-to-equity below 0.5x over the last 5 years, but with increased capex in recent years this ratio is expected to rise somewhat, though it will be maintained at certain levels.

subsections.label: Cost structure - employee costs
points: Employee cost rose ~103% YoY in FY26 due to the E&C business (Sangreen Future Renewables) growing almost twice its prior size, adding manpower-heavy fixed costs.

Additional employee cost increase attributable to aggressive investment in leadership talent in India and Saudi Arabia, aligned with the company's 5-year strategic plan 'ELEVATE 2030', and a stated intent to be an 'employer of choice'.

subsections.label: Margin profile by business unit
points: Blended EBITDA margin appears to be falling, but this reflects revenue mix shift: the core crane rental business is capital-intensive, asset-heavy and high-EBITDA-margin, while the newer engineering & construction business (Sangreen Future Renewables, carved out as a wholly owned subsidiary in 2024) is asset-light, working-capital heavy and high-ROCE but lower EBITDA margin.

Core crane rental business has grown 30% and contributed significantly to EBITDA/PAT; incremental growth beyond 30% (crossing historical revenue of INR 1,100 crores) came from the E&C business, which has doubled in revenue and is not capex heavy.
Company does not target a blended EBITDA margin; it drives business-unit level P&L given the fundamentally different economics of the two engines.
KSA business EBITDA profile benchmarked at 40-45%, which management believes can be pushed to 45-48% due to technical/operating efficiency and leaner cost structure.

subsections.label: Diesel/fuel cost pass-through
points: Diesel prices are increasing; company is in discussion with clients for a price increase.

50% of clients supply fuel themselves (HSD issue by client) so this cost is not borne by the company for those contracts; for the balance 50% of clients, company is in advanced-stage discussions for a price increase to pass on the cost.

Is an asset-light, working-capital-heavy, high-ROCE (closed FY26 ROCE ~70%), lower-EBITDA-margin business, carved out as a wholly owned subsidiary in 2024.
Opportunity size in this segment is far ahead of the company's current scale to deliver, so management is being selective/choosy about contracts to maintain healthy margin profile.

Wind EPC/E&C quarterly revenue growth (INR 106 crores to INR 116 crores YoY) appears low relative to industry wind capacity growth because: (1) demand size is far greater than the company's ability to scale and deliver at acceptable EBITDA margin, (2) there is a timing mismatch in revenue recognition under percentage-of-completion (POCM) accounting methodology versus physical capacity addition, and (3) company is selectively choosing which contracts to execute rather than expanding aggressively into EPC/E&C, as past experience of large players attempting this has shown execution struggles.
Company delivered 2 gigawatts of the country's 6 gigawatts of wind capacity addition in FY26, out of a historical track record of 17+ gigawatts of WTG installations.

Management targets 30% growth in overall consolidated revenue for FY27; when asked if wind segment growth would match this, management reiterated the 30% target applies to consolidated revenue rather than segment-specific guidance.

points: Contributed remaining 4% of FY26 operating revenue.
