subsections.label: Capacity utilization and yield drivers
points: Asset utilization improved to 79% in FY26 from 74% in FY25, reflecting stronger fleet deployment, better planning and greater execution discipline on the ground.
Q4 FY26 utilization was higher at 87% versus the full-year average of 79%.

Yield outlook: management foresees maintaining ~2.1% yield in India with a plus/minus 5% deviation going forward; drivers of yield are not fully linear/singular but tied to construction demand, crane supply, and fleet age/mix factors (discussed qualitatively without a single definitive driver).

subsections.label: Capex deployment and deferrals - Middle East
points: Two India cranes remaining as of March-end FY26 were supplied in the first fortnight of April, completing India capex for that batch.
In KSA, certain cranes faced OEM delivery delays; the related capex of INR 123 crores for 57 cranes will now be completed in the current financial year (FY27).
Board approved additional new capex of INR 190 crores in India and ~INR 200 crores in KSA, totaling ~61 new cranes to be purchased per business requirement.
Capex deployment is staggered through the year, with some supplies deferred around the monsoon period to align with orders.

Deferred/spillover capex of INR 120 crores from last year plus incremental Board-approved capex of ~INR 200-201 crores is planned for brand-new crane purchases in the Middle East (Saudi Arabia and Qatar) in FY27, totaling ~INR 320 crores for the year.

Of the deferred INR 120 crores KSA capex, some inventory is already available in-country and some is pending shipment; the balance capex has been ordered to OEMs and is in various stages of production, with none currently 'on route' (in transit) — some surplus OEM inventory in-country may be used as a fallback if fresh shipments from origin countries are unavailable.
All capex being brought online for the Middle East business is moving directly from board (approval) to site (deployment).

subsections.label: Capex reconciliation queries (unresolved on call)
points: An analyst raised a discrepancy between calculated revenue (using stated utilization and yield applied to estimated gross block) and reported crane rental revenue of INR 693 crores; management asked the analyst to send the query via email for offline response, as the live explanation was unclear.

subsections.label: India sector-wise demand backdrop
points: Wind energy is the most active and growing segment for the company; every turbine erected and wind park commissioned is likely to require the company's heavy-lift services.
Thermal continues to be a strong contributor; plants are being retrofitted/upgraded to work alongside renewables and flex up/down per grid demand.

Nuclear is an emerging high-growth opportunity, with private sector participation being discussed (Reliance, Tata, Adani; Vedanta has expressed interest); fastest-growing energy subsector at 26% CAGR.
Refinery sector: India is already Asia's largest refiner and expanding further, with government targeting top-3 global refining hub status by 2047.
Cement demand is running ahead of expectations, and 2030 target has been revised upward.

Steel: India is world's second-largest steel producer, with new demand streams opening from nuclear plants, renewable energy, infrastructure, data centers/structures, and smart cities driving appetite for specialty steel and large facilities.

subsections.label: Middle East (KSA/Qatar) expansion
points: KSA infrastructure sector witnessing strong momentum; company has built strong revenue visibility via pipeline aligned to Vision 2030, leveraging expertise in wind sector, certified operators, and robust safety standards.
Company opened up a new market in Qatar during the current regional disruption, demonstrating regional crane demand and confidence in Sanghvi Movers as supplier.
No Indian clients in Saudi currently — customers are regional/country-specific contractors, shutdown and EPC contractors.
Company believes it sits at the upper pricing spectrum in KSA versus competitors, driven by track record, brand recognition, and supply of brand-new equipment.

subsections.label: Shipping and port congestion
points: Supply chain disruption is affecting the movement of cranes from country of origin to Saudi Arabia and Qatar; if shipping line disruptions continue, there may be a postponement of capex deployment.

Rerouting cranes to Jeddah port is possible but Jeddah is also facing severe congestion, and there has been a significant hike in shipping costs due to congestion, making rerouting costly and uncertain.

Some delayed KSA capex/cranes are pending shipment; balance capex already ordered to OEMs is in various stages of production, with none currently in transit; surplus OEM in-country inventory may be used as a fallback.

subsections.label: ELEVATE 2030 strategic plan
points: Company has a stated 5-year strategic plan called 'ELEVATE 2030' focused on building organizational capabilities, including aggressive investment in leadership talent in both India and Saudi Arabia.

subsections.label: Business structuring - Sangreen Future Renewables
points: The engineering & construction (renewables) business was carved out as a wholly owned subsidiary, Sangreen Future Renewables Private Limited, in 2024, to run a distinct asset-light, high-ROCE business model separate from the core crane rental business.

Each business unit (crane rental, KSA/Middle East entity - Sanghvi Movers Middle East Limited, and E&C/Sangreen) runs its own in-house P&L to reflect fundamentally different operating and capital structures and to maximize profitability, revenue, and shareholder returns independently.

subsections.label: Right to win in Middle East
points: Company is the fifth largest crane rental company in the world, and the largest in India and Asia, with 36 years of experience and 3.5 decades of operational, safety and technical know-how.
Reputation preceded entry into the Middle East, enabling penetration into oil & gas, infrastructure, energy and other sectors in a short span.
Company has transferred significant capabilities and best practices from India to the Middle East, while also benefiting from India's lean cost structure.

There remains a structural shortage of cranes in the Middle East region — even if the crane population doubled overnight, a shortage would persist — positioning the company well from both supply and demand sides.

subsections.label: West Asia geopolitical situation
points: Current situation in West Asia was raised as a concern by an analyst regarding potential project stoppages or slowdown; management stated they are still deriving utilization of 85-90% and yield upwards of 4.5%, and remain committed to Middle East expansion capex despite the situation.

subsections.label: Shipping/logistics disruption
points: Shipping line disruption and port congestion (including at Jeddah, which is also congested) are affecting crane delivery timelines to Saudi Arabia and Qatar and could lead to postponement of capex if disruptions continue; shipping costs have also risen due to congestion.

subsections.label: OEM delivery delays
points: Certain cranes for KSA faced delivery delays from OEMs, pushing INR 123 crores of capex for 57 cranes into the current financial year (FY27).

subsections.label: Diesel/input cost inflation
points: Rising diesel prices are a cost pressure; company is in discussion with clients to pass on cost increases for the 50% of contracts where fuel is not supplied by the client.

subsections.label: Labour Code implementation
points: Impact of Labour Code implementation was cited as one of the factors partially offsetting growth in FY26 profitability.

subsections.label: Execution capacity constraints in E&C/wind segment
points: Demand in the wind E&C segment is far ahead of the company's current scale/ability to deliver at acceptable margins, leading management to be selective about which contracts to take on rather than scale aggressively, given past struggles faced by large EPC/E&C players attempting rapid scale-up.

subsections.label: Overall growth guidance
points: Management aims to maintain the same growth level achieved in FY26 into the current year (FY27), without quoting an exact number, targeting similar growth for both crane rental (30%) and consolidated revenue (~30%).
Management could not commit to how much of the ~INR 4,000 crores inquiry pipeline would convert into orders in the next 3-6 months, citing dependency on external environment.

subsections.label: KSA/Middle East outlook
points: Company is on track to achieve cumulative EBITDA and cash flow positivity in KSA/Qatar business in the coming few months (already achieved on a month-to-month basis).

Despite regional disruption, company remains committed to deploying spillover capex of INR 120 crores plus newly approved capex of ~INR 200-201 crores in the Middle East during FY27, totaling ~INR 320 crores.
Company continues to view the Middle East as a long-term opportunity spanning decades, notwithstanding current regional disruption.

subsections.label: Margin approach going forward
points: Company does not target a blended EBITDA margin given the fundamentally different economics of its business units (capital-intensive high-margin crane rental vs asset-light high-ROCE E&C); instead drives business-unit level P&L.

guidance_ledger.statement: We would like to maintain the growth we have done in the current year... our target is to achieve the same type of growth in the current year and next year.
We are positive that going forward, we will see another 30% growth in our crane rental business.
The group will deliver or expect to deliver and is internally targeting a 30% growth on its overall consolidated revenue.
KSA business has started generating positive monthly EBITDA recently, and we are expected to achieve positive ITD (cumulative) EBITDA by end of first half of current financial year.

guidance_ledger.metric: KSA cumulative EBITDA & cash flow positivity
guidance_ledger.statement: Our cumulative EBITDA and cumulative cash flow positivity will be achieved in the coming few months and we are on track to achieve it.
Our yield in the last financial year has been around 2.1%. And we foresee maintaining the same with a plus/minus 5% deviation.

We are committed to deploy the spillover capex of INR 120 crores from last year and an incremental capex of almost INR 200 crores for the purchase of brand new cranes... this year, we are forecasting to spend approximately INR 320 crores in the Middle East, specifically for Saudi Arabia and Qatar.
It will go up, but we'll maintain it at certain levels... this is definitely going to be a little up considering the capex we have done.
We do not target a blended EBITDA margin. We drive BU level P&L.
We believe... we can push that EBITDA profile to 45% to 48%.

In the core business, we have invested in FY25-26 approved capex of INR 630 crores. This year, we are doing INR 390 crores, on a total of almost INR 1,030 crores. The entirety of this capex is going towards our crane rental business.

themes.label: Revenue growth momentum
themes.note: FY26 consolidated revenue grew 36.9% YoY, driven by 35% growth in India crane rental revenue.

themes.label: KSA/Middle East expansion
themes.note: KSA/Qatar showing high utilization (85-90%) and yield (>4.5%) with cumulative EBITDA/cash-flow breakeven targeted for H1 FY27, but facing shipping/port congestion risk and geopolitical disruption in West Asia.

themes.label: Margin mix shift (core vs E&C)
themes.note: Blended EBITDA margin appears to decline due to growing contribution from asset-light, high-ROCE but lower-margin E&C (Sangreen) business alongside high-margin core crane rental business.

themes.label: Capacity expansion / capex plans
themes.note: ~INR 1,030 crores total capex planned across FY26-FY27 for core crane rental business plus ~INR 320 crores for Middle East fleet expansion (61 new cranes).

key_takeaways: For Q4 FY26, the company reported income from operation of INR 351 crores as compared to INR 236 crores in Q3 FY26 and INR 267 crores in Q4 FY25, reflecting a year-on-year growth of 31.4%.
For the full year FY26, revenue from operation stood at INR 1,070 crores, representing a growth of 36.9% over INR 782 crores reported in FY25.
In terms of segment contribution for FY26, the crane rental business contributed 65% of operating revenue and the renewables segment accounted for 31% and the project EPC contributed remaining 4%.

EBITDA for Q4 FY26 stood at INR 143 crores compared to INR 113 crores in Q4 FY25, representing a growth of 25.7% year-on-year with an EBITDA margin of 40.6%. For FY26, EBITDA was INR 429 crores as against INR 371 crores in FY25, reflecting a growth of 15.6% and a margin of 40.1%.

For the full year FY26, PAT stood at INR 184 crores versus INR 157 crores in FY25, marking a growth of 17.7%, primarily driven by 35% growth in credit rental revenue in India and partially offset by higher incurred costs from expansion in KSA and renewable business along with the impact of Labour Code implementation.
KSA business has started generating positive monthly EBITDA recently, and we are expected to achieve positive ITD EBITDA by end of this first half current financial year.
Average capacity utilization during the quarter was 87% and overall 79% for FY26, while average blended yields were at 2.24% per month for quarter 4 and average for the year is 2.12%.
As of 31 March 2026, net debt stood at INR 612 crores with a net debt-to-equity ratio of 0.47x, reflecting a comfortable leverage position.
Our order book pipeline remains robust with INR 1,053 crores in hand as on 14th May FY27, giving us a greater visibility.
As of May, our consolidated order book stands at INR 1,053 crores... our inquiry pipeline... has expanded to almost INR 4,000 crores.
pressing_questions: In the presentation, you have mentioned that we have INR 612 crores of net debt versus if I see the gross debt is INR 673 crores, and we have a treasury of INR 353 crores. So shouldn't the net debt be like around INR 300 crores, INR 320-odd crores? Is that number correct?

So I'm just asking the capacity utilization number, 79% and the yield of 2.12% per month, which is given in the presentation. If I apply those two metrics to the revenue number of INR 693 crores, which is the crane rental revenue, my gross block is not coming as per the cash flow capex and the last year gross block which you have given? (Taken offline via email)

TMPV.about: Tata Motors Group is a global automobile manufacturer. Part of the multi-national conglomerate, the Tata group, it offers a wide and diverse portfolio of cars, sports utility vehicles, etc. It has operations in India, the UK, South Korea, South Africa, China, Brazil, Austria and Slovakia through a strong global network of subsidiaries, associate companies and Joint Ventures (JVs), including Jaguar Land Rover in the UK and Tata Daewoo in South Korea.[1]

quarters.summary: TMPV Q1 FY27: Consolidated revenue Rs.95,800 Cr, EBIT margin 2.4%, PBT Rs.1,600 Cr (down YoY) as JLR wholesales fell on temporary supply constraints/Middle East conflict and elevated VME, partly offset by structural cost gains and one-offs; India business posted strong revenue growth (+65% YoY) but commodity inflation offset gains, keeping EBITDA margin flattish at ~4%. JLR maintains full-year guidance despite a weak Q1 cash performance, banking on H2 ramp-up of four BEV launches and $1.7bn cost-savings program; India targets higher double-digit volume growth in FY27 with margin step-up in H2 via pricing, cost cuts and PLI accruals.

subsections.label: JLR PBT Walk
points: PBT declined from GBP 351 million last year to GBP 109 million this year.
Volume and mix wasn't too bad given the wholesale drop, as sales balanced more into Range Rover, Range Rover Sport and Defender (now 81% of sales).
Tariffs/U.S. duties showed favorable versus last year's comparable quarter when 27.5% tariffs were paid before trade deals came into force.
Emissions showed negative this quarter versus a big accrual release in Q1 last year.

VME significantly higher at 7.1%, driven by China (economic/retailer stress, new luxury taxes post-Q1 last year) and U.S. (last year kept sales allowances deliberately low in response to tariff implementation).
Industrial operations hit by higher commodity prices.

FX/commodities item largely reflects non-repeat of a GBP 83 million favorable revaluation gain in Q1 last year, plus unrealized commodity hedge losses as aluminum and palladium reduced from quarter-start peaks.

subsections.label: JLR Cash Flow
points: Generated over GBP 0.5 billion cash profit after tax.
Nearing peak of investment cycle resulted in free cash flow pre-working capital of negative GBP 352 million.
Working capital reflects naturally high production/low sales seasonal quarter, built up but expected to largely reverse through the year (Q4 last year working capital was GBP 814 million favorable).
Post-working capital free cash flow was just under GBP 1 billion negative.

Q1 is typically JLR's weakest cash quarter due to seasonal working capital swing; results, while weaker than desired, are not inconsistent with full-year guidance but require strong performance for remainder of year.

subsections.label: India EBITDA Margin Walk
points: Margins remained flat at ~4% YoY.
Significant gains from fixed cost leverage plus 2% material cost reductions were entirely offset by 6% commodity impact YoY.
Q1 commodity impact was 4.5%, with another 3%+ residual impact expected to flow into Q2.

A 1% cumulative price increase taken across April and July; calibrated increases planned through the rest of year, with a large part of commodity offset expected via accelerated commercial/cost reductions.
PLI accruals of Rs.313 Cr came largely from Nexon.ev and Harrier.ev.
Refreshed portfolio and new launches under various stages of certification, expected to materialize from Q3.
Combination of price increases, cost reductions and PLI expected to step up margins in H2.

subsections.label: India Q2 Margin Offset Levers (Q&A detail)
points: Q2 commodity hit expected at 3%.
Price increase lever: 0.5% taken in July, not reflected in Q1 financials; further calibrated increases planned through the year.
Cost reduction lever: 2% YoY benefit for the year, with 1.5% already realized in Q1; incrementally more expected this quarter.
Seasonal IPL impact of 1% in Q1 will not repeat in Q2, providing a 1% benefit.
Net-net, despite the 3% commodity hit in Q2, margins expected to be flattish versus Q1.

subsections.label: India Capex & FCF
points: Capex of Rs.1,300 Cr for the quarter still tracking last year's trends, expected to step up as the company executes its next phase of growth per Investor Day guidance.
FCF of Rs.1,100 Cr for the quarter; operating cash profits were subdued due to commodity impact, but favorable working capital releases helped maintain strong liquidity.

subsections.label: Demand & Order Pipeline (India)
points: Demand environment in India has remained robust; strong traction from new launches/refreshes over the last two quarters continued to play out.
Monthly volume run rate scaled from an earlier average of 45,000-50,000 to consistently greater than 60,000, potentially more but for supply-side constraints.

EV order book is strong as production scales up; EV bookings up nearly 3.5x versus pre-Middle East crisis (Jan-Feb) levels due to new launches (Tiago.ev, Sierra.ev) though supply cannot yet match demand.

Sierra is doing well with a 2-3 month waiting period; production affected by casting constraints for petrol/diesel engines and sheet metal capacity stress shared across products, compounded by industry demand rising from 350,000 to 450,000 units causing press capacity issues at sheet metal suppliers; improvement expected over next two months, with bigger capacity boost from October.
Punch.ev has 8-10 months waiting period despite supplying 4,000-4,500/month; capacity being further enhanced from this month.
Dealer inventory levels are around 30 days; company aims to significantly build stock ahead of the festive period for high retail in October.

subsections.label: JLR Volume/Retail Detail
points: Wholesales down about 8,000 units and about 3,000 lower than internally planned as legacy Jaguar models were run out.
Defender remains amazingly strong, up again in wholesales.
Range Rover and Range Rover Sport were impacted by a fire at a chassis component supplier early in the quarter that knocked out several days of production not recovered.
Discovery and Jaguar are the two brands currently being reimagined.
Retails down 14.5K YoY; over 5,000 of this attributable to Jaguar run-out or Middle East conflict.
Temporary quality holds occurred right at the end of the quarter.
Deliberately balanced out of lower-margin products to improve mix.

subsections.label: JLR Regional Performance
points: U.S. and MENA wholesales flat YoY.
China down 25% YoY — the market with the biggest correction; all competitors finding China extremely difficult.
JLR focus in China: discipline on retailer stock days, innovative demand generation, running out last legacy cars to relieve retailer financial burden.

China revenue share currently 13%; likely to get a little worse before stabilizing given weak economy and industry-wide overcapacity among domestic manufacturers; recent retrospective luxury tax moves add pressure on the targeted customer segment (additional headwind versus Investor Day expectation of leveling off at a lower end).

subsections.label: JLR Product/Brand Metrics
points: Average sale price continually rising, set to be well north of GBP 80,000 (north of $100,000) per car in ~18 months as new products launch.
J.D. Power APEAL Study: Defender wins its segment; JLR ranked third out of 18 manufacturers.
Value retention: Range Rover and Defender number one in their segments in the U.S.; Range Rover and Range Rover Sport number one in UK.

subsections.label: India Wholesale/Nameplate Performance
points: Q1 wholesale volumes of about 182,000 units, up 46% YoY — nearly twice broader industry growth.
Strengthened position as #2 ranked player, market share up 200 bps YoY to 14.3%.
Performance broad-based; Punch and Nexon among top three highest-selling models in India during Q1.

New launches: Tiago ICE Facelift (May) enhanced styling/tech for hatch segment; Tiago.ev facelift strengthened EV entry segment value proposition; all-new Sierra.ev expanded portfolio in high-growth space.
Launches received positively, contributing to a healthy increase in bookings.

subsections.label: India EV Performance
points: Highest-ever EV volumes of over 34,000 units in the quarter, sustaining market leadership.
EV mix ~20% of sales in Q1, rising to 24% in July.
Strong EV order book as production scales up; exceeded 15,000 EV units in July with EV market share increasing to 43% (from 37% a year ago).

EV market share growth driven by: (1) existing products significantly enhanced in value proposition (e.g., Punch.ev demand multi-fold increase despite 4,000-4,500/month supply and 8-10 month waiting period, with further capacity enhancement this month), and (2) new products added — Sierra.ev, one more new product planned this financial year, plus two big refreshes.
Portfolio spans Rs.7 lakh to Rs.30 lakh, with 'every model punching above its weight.'
Confident of protecting and potentially increasing EV market share despite intensifying competition.
EV volumes roughly doubled over the last 1 year; EV monthly run rate exited June at 15,000 units; EV market share trending upwards of 40% in the trailing period.
EV production ramped from about 9,000 units/month roughly 4 months back to over 15,000 units/month last month.

subsections.label: JLR EV Mix/Margin Outlook
points: EV powertrains (Range Rover Electric, Range Rover Sport Electric) expected to be at least margin neutral, potentially accretive, since they are premium Range Rover products (quiet, powerful) not mass-market EVs, priced without discount.
EMA cars (smaller cars including Range Rover GT) replace end-of-life, relatively low-margin vehicles — new EVs expected at least neutral versus those replaced vehicles.

Key management watch-item is cannibalization level (overlap in expressions of interest) rather than variable margins — minimal cannibalization would flow through to significant operating leverage benefit given the business's high fixed-cost leverage.
Range Rover Electric launch starts September FY27; tentative FY27 EV volume target ~12,000 cars from JLR, more launches over next six months and beyond, further guidance to follow.

subsections.label: JLR New Product Launches
points: Four imminent launches, two more in pipeline (six total vehicle launches approaching).
Range Rover Electric and Range Rover Sport Electric come later this year.
Radical Range Rover GT and Jaguar Type 01 due early next year.
Jaguar Type 01 to start production early next year; not expected to have material impact on FY27 wholesales — impact comes through in FY28 along with the biggest impact of Range Rover GT.

Roadshow/marketing response to Type 01 described as very positive — customers who see or drive the car respond with big smiles; engineers turned an exceptional design into a sports car of exceptional quality.

subsections.label: India Avinya Product Positioning
points: Avinya democratizes the luxury vehicle experience and sits significantly premium to Safari in aspirational value.

Original launch timeline was end of 2026, but platform strategy was shifted to the Freelander platform of CJLR (following news articles and company response), delaying the project; now expected to launch in 2027.

subsections.label: JLR Europe EV Mix / Euro 7
points: Launch volumes of Range Rover Electric, Range Rover Sport Electric and Range Rover GT will be primarily sold in UK/Europe initially, where BEV leverage is strongest.
Production systems will have enough capacity to remain legislatively compliant with upcoming Euro 7 norms (from 2027).
BEV rollout will not match ICE mix — more ICE sold in North America, progressively more BEV in UK/Europe.

subsections.label: JLR Investment/Capacity
points: Investment levels and capitalization levels (74% in the quarter) remain high given six approaching vehicle launches.
Over the balance of the year, spend likely to remain similar but shift from engineering to capital as new facilities come online and series production of the four new cars begins.

subsections.label: JLR Supplier Fire Impact
points: Fire at a chassis component supplier early in the quarter knocked out the Solihull production facility (which produces Range Rover and Range Rover Sport) for several days, not recoverable within the quarter.
Issue is now fully resolved.

subsections.label: India Production Ramp-up & Constraints
points: Inventory levels around 30 days; increase last month as production rose slightly, but need to significantly build inventory ahead of festive period.
Production affected in April-May-June by labor issues and geopolitical issues.
Last month's production was 63,000 units, which would have been higher but for a rainfall issue in Sanand that caused 5 lost production days.
Targeting 65,000+ production this month, moving closer to ~70,000 units/month in coming months.
Major additional capacity enhancement work for Sierra underway for past 4-5 months, expected to show improvement over next two months with bigger boost from October as major capacity work kicks in.
Several debottlenecking actions and capacity expansion initiatives undertaken across critical suppliers, showing positive momentum in recent months.
Defender sells about 30,000 units per year in the U.S.; at JLR's scale, potential Defender sales via U.S. localization estimated at up to 50,000 units annually.

subsections.label: Middle East Situation
points: Middle East wholesales relatively flat but retail down about 1,400 units during the quarter as retailer network traffic reduced and some vehicles had trouble reaching retailers.
World is slowly adjusting to the new Middle East situation; JLR and other manufacturers finding new routes avoiding the Strait of Hormuz.
Expectation the world will progressively adjust; hope situation normalizes to allow previous routes to be used again.

subsections.label: North America Strategy
points: Focus on US market for significant part of the 10% p.a. revenue growth goal, given US has 40% of world's millionaires, propensity to SUVs (JLR strength), and strong brand affinity to Range Rover, Defender, Jaguar.
At JLR's scale, localizing existing production of existing vehicles (e.g., c.30,000 Defenders sold annually in US) in North America doesn't make sense even at 30,000-50,000 unit scale.

Approach: MoU signed with Stellantis to produce vehicles specific to the US market in North America, targeting new vehicles/new segments under the Defender brand, US-produced; aiming for formal/definitive agreement by end of year, discussions live and underway.

subsections.label: India Exports
points: Early stages of export growth; opened South Africa market last year, which significantly helped export growth.
Grew exports 4x last year off a low base; targeting closer to 2x growth of last year's level for FY27.

subsections.label: Sierra Supply Constraints
points: Sierra affected by casting constraints for petrol engines (also diesel) and sheet metal item stress due to shared capacity with other products.
Industry demand increase from 350,000 to 450,000 units created press capacity issues across many sheet metal suppliers.
Working on the issue for past 4-5 months; improvement expected this month and next two months, with major capacity enhancement kicking in from October for a bigger boost.

subsections.label: India Production Disruptions
points: April-May-June production affected by labor issues and geopolitical issues.
Rainfall issue in Sanand caused loss of 5 production days last month.

subsections.label: Industry Outlook (India PV)
points: PV industry volumes crossed 1.3 million units in Q1, supported by healthy demand following GST 2.0.
24% YoY industry growth partly reflects a relatively low base in the corresponding period last year.
Volumes expected to continue at strong levels through the year, but growth rates likely to moderate in H2 due to higher base.
Industry continues to see higher growth in greener powertrains (CNG and EV); structural shift in industry mix gaining momentum with EV+CNG at 31% of industry sales in Q1.
EV remains the fastest-growing segment, registering 77% YoY growth; EV penetration increasing every month, reaching 8% in June.
Mainstream EV adoption supported by greater OEM participation, expanding product choices, improving customer sentiment, and enabling policy environment.
Mid-Asia crisis has clearly altered consumer preferences towards greener fuels, contributing to the EV mix shift.

subsections.label: Competitive Dynamics (JLR)
points: Value-retention and APEAL rankings cited as embodiment of brand strategy versus competitors.
China: all competitors finding the market extremely difficult amid economic and retailer stress.

subsections.label: India Price Sensitivity Commentary
points: Company would ideally like to have transferred all cost increases via price, but must benchmark against competitors' price increases to avoid losing competitiveness on each product — this is why the increase has been limited to 1% so far.
Strategy: accelerate cost reduction efforts, and pass on whatever residual remains via more frequent but progressive (not steep) price increases, to avoid competitiveness/volume loss.

subsections.label: JLR Strategic Response to Industry Challenges
points: Industry challenges are intensifying globally but well known; company response focuses on cost intensification and growth/scale leverage — 'you cannot shrink or save yourself to success.'
Setting a goal of 10% revenue growth per annum, focusing on the US market for a significant part of that growth.
Cost focus areas: ex-works cost of cars, warranty, and fixed cost base; intent to save $1.7 billion in this space; more detailed update to be given as part of Q2 results.
Aim is to build greater resilience into the business model to navigate whatever lies ahead.
Break-even target of 300,000 units (from Investor Day) requires taking out cost including pound-denominated fixed costs — actions already underway.

subsections.label: North America Manufacturing Partnership
points: MoU signed with Stellantis to explore producing US-market-specific vehicles in North America under the Defender brand, aiming for a formal/definitive agreement by end of year.
Partnership would also provide a more natural hedge on JLR's currently large long-dollar position, complementing existing cash flow hedges on dollar-denominated borrowings.

subsections.label: PLI Scheme Extension
points: No discussions yet with government on extension of PLI scheme beyond FY28; company will assess to what extent it consumes its target/quota before pursuing this.

subsections.label: JLR Risk Factors
points: Middle East conflict impacting retail traffic and vehicle delivery routes (Strait of Hormuz avoidance).
Supplier fire at chassis component supplier disrupted Solihull production (now resolved).

China market: economic slowdown, retailer stress, domestic manufacturer overcapacity, and new/retrospective luxury taxes pressuring the targeted customer segment — additional headwind versus Investor Day expectations; management does not believe all bad news from China is done yet.

Commodity price volatility (aluminum, palladium, copper) — aluminum fell from ~$3,500/ton (end March) to ~$3,150/ton (end June) during the quarter but remains high; some contracts react on a quarterly lag, so an extra RM hit is expected in Q2.
Credit rating: JLR remains on the borders of investment grade but on negative watch; management in constant contact with rating agencies.
FX exposure: large long-dollar position; hedge book around 1.28 GBP/USD; company prefers a weaker sterling environment as UK's biggest goods exporter.

subsections.label: India Risk Factors
points: Commodity inflation continues to be a stress point across several key inputs, with 4.5% impact in Q1 and 3%+ expected in Q2.
Supply chain constraints persist in select areas, affecting the ability to service full customer demand (e.g., Sierra, Punch.ev).
Industry growth rates likely to moderate in H2 due to higher base effect from GST 2.0-driven Q1 growth.
Elevated commodity levels represent a near-term headwind to profitability that management intends to mitigate through controllable levers (cost reduction, pricing, PLI).

key_figures.label: JLR FY27 EV volume tentative target
India Q2 margin expectation vs Q1

subsections.label: JLR Full-Year Guidance
points: Q1 results, while weaker than desired, are not inconsistent with full-year guidance; guidance has not been dropped.
Will require strong performance for the remainder of the year to meet guidance.
Detailed update on the $1.7bn cost savings program to be given as part of Q2 results.

subsections.label: India Outlook
points: Demand environment positive; clear opportunity to continue industry-beating volume growth while enhancing profitability through disciplined execution.
Festive season expected to further strengthen demand momentum; immediate focus is sustaining growth on the back of a healthy order pipeline.
Continued new product interventions (refreshes) planned to sustain customer traction, along with capitalizing on the shift to greener powertrains.
Priority to alleviate supply-side constraints via debottlenecking and capacity expansion at critical suppliers.
Profitability enhancement via accelerated cost reduction, expedited PLI for new products, and calibrated pricing actions balancing competitiveness with sustainable margins.
Overall positive outlook entering coming quarters, with focus on disciplined execution and profitability enhancement to sustain above-market growth and value creation over the medium term.
Targeting higher double-digit volume growth in FY27, aiming to keep pace roughly twice the industry growth rate as achieved in FY26 and Q1 FY27.
Margin outlook: aim to neutralize commodity headwinds through combination of price increases and cost reduction.
By Q4, almost the entire portfolio expected to be PLI-accredited, with certifications for Tiago.ev, Punch.ev, Sierra.ev and Curvv expected to materialize starting Q3.

guidance_ledger.statement: Q1 results are not inconsistent with our full year guidance; guidance has not been dropped, though will require strong performance for the remainder of the year.
Setting a goal of 10% revenue growth per annum, focusing on the US market for a significant part of that.
Intent to save $1.7 billion across ex-works cost, warranty and fixed cost base; more detailed update to be given at Q2 results.
Average sale price set to rise, expected to be well north of GBP 80,000 (north of $100,000) per car in about 18 months.
Tentatively penciling about 12,000 cars in FY27 in the EV space; will keep updated as it goes along.
Expect new EV powertrains (Range Rover Electric etc.) to be at least margin neutral, potentially accretive, versus cars they replace.
Jaguar Type 01 production starts early next year; will not have material impact on wholesales in FY27, impact comes through in FY28 along with Range Rover GT.
Aiming to get the Stellantis MoU to a formal and definitive agreement by the end of the year.
Targeting higher double-digit growth in FY27, similar to the twice-industry-growth pace achieved in FY26 and Q1.
Will try to neutralize commodity headwinds through combination of price increase and cost reduction.
Combination of price increases, cost reductions and PLI should see margins step up in H2.
Expecting another 3% plus residual commodity impact to flow into Q2.
Net-net, despite the 3% commodity hit in Q2, margins expected to be flattish with respect to Q1.
Targeting more closer to 2x growth of what was achieved last year (which was 4x on a low base).
Targeting 65,000+ production this month, moving closer to ~70,000 units/month in coming months.
Certifications for Tiago.ev, Punch.ev, Sierra.ev, Curvv expected to materialize from Q3; by Q4, almost the entire portfolio should be PLI accredited.
Avinya launch delayed due to platform strategy shift to Freelander platform of CJLR; now expected to launch in 2027 (previously targeted end of 2026).
Confident of not only protecting but hopefully increasing EV market share despite significantly intensifying competition.

risk_register.note: Persisting in select areas (e.g., Sierra casting/sheet metal capacity, Punch.ev capacity); debottlenecking and capacity expansion underway, showing positive momentum.

risk_register.note: Jaguar wholesales down ~1,500 units versus prior quarter as last legacy stock is sold off over the next three to six months.

themes.label: JLR Volume/Wholesale Softness
themes.note: JLR wholesales down ~10% YoY on Jaguar legacy run-out, supplier fire, and Middle East conflict impacts.

themes.label: Commodity Cost Inflation
themes.note: Both India (4.5% Q1 impact, 3%+ expected Q2) and JLR faced elevated commodity/VME pressure, offsetting revenue gains.

themes.label: EV Portfolio Momentum (India)
themes.note: India EV volumes hit record highs (34,000+ units), EV market share rose to 43% in July from 37% a year ago.

themes.label: JLR BEV Launch Cycle
themes.note: Four imminent BEV launches (Range Rover Electric, RR Sport Electric, Range Rover GT, Jaguar Type 01) expected to drive top-line and margins in coming years.

themes.label: China Market Weakness
themes.note: JLR China wholesales down 25% YoY; new retrospective luxury taxes add pressure, worse than Investor Day expectations.

themes.label: US Market Expansion & Localization
themes.note: JLR targeting 10% p.a. revenue growth centered on US market; Stellantis MoU for US-specific vehicle production targeted for formal agreement by year-end.

themes.label: India Supply-Side Constraints
themes.note: Sierra and Punch.ev face long waiting periods due to casting/sheet metal capacity constraints; debottlenecking actions showing positive momentum with bigger relief expected from October.

key_takeaways: TMPV delivered revenues of Rs. 95,800 Cr for the quarter, EBIT margins at 2.4%, and PBT for the quarter stood at Rs. 1,600 Cr, down on a year-on-year basis.

JLR wholesales were down in part due to the temporary supply constraints and Middle East conflict. In addition, profitability was impacted as market conditions pushed VME up year-on-year, partially offset by favorable structural cost and other one-offs.
The domestic business delivered strong revenue growth, however, elevated commodities moderated improvement in margins.
Consolidated net debt stood at Rs.42,000 Cr at the end of the quarter. India business continues to remain net cash positive, while net debt at JLR was GBP 3.6 billion.
Wholesales were down about 10% year-over-year. This is partly caused by the run-out of legacy cars as we move to the launch of the new Jaguars, but also a fire at a supplier.
This drove revenue to GBP 6 billion with EBIT of 2.8%, a positive PBT of GBP 109 million, but a significant cash outflow.
We saw a 46% jump in volumes year-on-year... nearly 2% improvement in market share on a year-on-year basis, establishing us as a firm #2 player on registrations.

India business revenues at Rs.18,000 crores, grew 65% year-on-year, but the gains were nearly entirely offset by the steep commodity increases we saw on a quarter-on-quarter basis. EBITDA margins were flattish at 4% year-on-year.
We delivered overall wholesale volumes of about 182,000 units, which was a year-on-year growth of 46%, nearly twice the pace of the broader industry growth.
pressing_questions: Has the JLR FY27 guidance been dropped or does it still stand? And with the focus on North America, do you intend to localize some production or do we assume lower margins on any incremental volumes that you sell through?

Despite such strong raw material headwinds, we've only taken a 1% price increase. Do you believe that customers are... what do you see the price sensitivity that customers had despite demand being so strong?
What are the inventory levels at the dealers? And what is your outlook on production amongst the supply challenges?
What is the kind of volume growth and margin outlook that you can provide for FY 27?
Is the EV booking on a rising trend, even on a month-on-month basis from April? And what kind of inflows are you seeing now?
What is going to be the impact of rising EV mix on JLR margins? And if you could throw some color, whether they are going to be expected to be accretive or dilutive.
Given that our current revenue from China is 13%, how do we see that share kind of evolve? Are we expecting it to go up or down?
What sort of EV mix do you need in Europe once the Euro 7 norms possibly kick in from 2027?
If you could please share some color on the exploratory partnership discussions on potentially manufacturing our vehicles in the U.S.
What is the volume we can expect from JLR EV in FY 27 and more so in FY 28? And what's the peak volumes we can assume from the four new models we're planning to launch?

HOMEFIRST.company: Home First Finance Company India Ltd
HOMEFIRST.about: Home First Finance Company India (HFFC) is a Housing Finance Company which offers home loan with 48 hours sanctions and hassle-free process. [1]

quarters.company: Home First Finance Company India Ltd
quarters.summary: Home First began FY27 with healthy AUM and disbursement growth, robust earnings growth and stable asset quality; management reiterated confidence in delivering 25% AUM growth for FY27 while maintaining spread guidance of 5%-5.25%, opex-to-assets guidance of 2.6%-2.7%, and stable credit costs, even as it navigates a CFO transition and monitors macro/geopolitical uncertainty.

key_figures.label: Number of quarters since process improvements initiated

subsections.label: Income, yields and margin
points: Total income for the quarter was INR540 crore, up 18.6% YoY and 7% sequentially.
Portfolio yield ex co-lending stood at 13.1%, disbursement yield at 13.0%, reflecting continued pricing discipline and quality of new customer acquisition.
On the liability side, proactive management of borrowing mix led to a further 10bps sequential reduction, bringing cost of borrowing down to 7.8%.
Incremental borrowing cost during the quarter remained favourable at 7.6%.
Spread, excluding co-lending, remained healthy at 5.3%.
NIM was 6.0%, up from 5.9% in the previous quarter.

subsections.label: Operating efficiency and profitability
points: Cost to income was 32.7%, up 70bps sequentially; marginal increase in opex owing to increments and fresh hiring, partly offset by lower administrative expenses.
Reported operating cost to assets was 2.8%; company expects this to broadly remain range-bound within 2.6%-2.7% as it continues to invest for growth.
Pre-provision operating profit was INR224 crore, up 32.9% YoY, demonstrating operating leverage as the balance sheet scales.
PAT increased to INR160 crore, up 34.5% YoY and 7% sequentially, supported by 38.2% growth in NII.

subsections.label: Provisions and asset quality
points: Credit cost for Q1 was 40bps.
Provision coverage on Stage 3 assets was 23.4% as of Jun'26 compared to 23.9% in Q4FY26.
Company continued to maintain management overlays over and above ECL requirements; including these, total provision coverage was 45.3% as of June 2026, providing prudent balance sheet protection.

subsections.label: Borrowings and funding profile
points: Funding profile continues to be diversified and cost effective: 57% from private/public banks, 14% from NHB, 21% from assignment and co-lending, balance from NCDs, ECB and NBFC.
Executed a direct assignment transaction of INR285 crore during the quarter.
NHB outstanding was flat at INR354 crore between Mar'26 and Jun'26 as company had not taken any NHB drawdown; plans to take drawdown in Q2.
Except for a particular NHB scheme where the loan is fixed for 7 years, the rest of the borrowing portfolio is floating rate, allowing pass-through of borrowing cost changes to customers.

subsections.label: Capital adequacy and liquidity
points: Capital adequacy ratio was 42.6% with Tier 1 at 42.2% as of Jun'26, compared with total capital adequacy of 44.1% and Tier 1 of 43.8% as of Mar'26.
Net worth stood at INR4,483 crore and BVPS was INR429 as of Jun'26.

subsections.label: Repayment/rundown behavior
points: Calculated repayment rate was 14.3%, lower than last year's average of around 16%, driven by an exceptionally good quarter of lower BT out.
Company generally assumes 16%-17% repayment rate in its calculations; no behavioural change observed in customer prepayment patterns.

key_figures.label: Individual housing loans share of portfolio
Ticket size >INR25 lakh share (1 year prior)
Ticket size >INR25 lakh share (2-3 years prior)
Ticket size mix shift over last 2 quarters
Volume vs value contribution to disbursement growth

subsections.label: Home loan vs LAP mix
points: Growth primarily led by home loans, which grew ~7% QoQ vs LAP at ~5% QoQ; slight shift towards home loans in disbursals as well as origination this quarter.
LAP has not been a strong focus area; LAP ticket sizes remain the same while housing loan ticket sizes have moved up marginally.
NPA for home loans and LAP are broadly in the same range; LAP portfolio is fairly small at about 13%-14% of the portfolio.

subsections.label: Ticket size trends
points: Share of >INR25 lakh ticket size increased from 14% to 18% over the last year, and from about 12% 2-3 years back.
Ticket size proportion has risen by more than 320bps over the last 2 quarters, largely attributable to home loans.

Management does not expect material spread compression from ticket size increase because it continues to address the same customer segment; ticket size-wise spread distribution shows little difference between >25 lakh and <25 lakh segments.
Over time, marginal yield compression is expected as customers buying larger properties are more interest-rate sensitive, which can be offset via opex efficiencies.

subsections.label: Volume vs value drivers of disbursement growth
points: Of the 31% YoY disbursement growth, about 50% came from increase in units (origination growth of 10%-15%) and 50% from ticket size/value growth.
Productivity per relationship officer, per branch is improving marginally on the ground.
Login-to-sanction ratio is around 40% (60% decline rate), a trend that has remained secular/similar across quarters and channels.

subsections.label: Credit bureau profile of customers
points: Average bureau score of customers increased from 738 to about 750 over the last 3 years.
Customers with credit history increased to 88% now versus 74% three years prior.

New-to-credit customers reduced to nearly 12% now versus 26% three years prior, a market-wide phenomenon as more customers gain bureau access through smaller loans (consumer, two-wheeler) before seeking a housing loan.
Philosophy is to gradually move up the credit-quality curve without sacrificing yields/spreads; company has maintained committed spreads of 5%-5.25% (slightly higher) even as bureau scores improve.
CIBIL score disclosed in the deck is measured at the time of loan origination.

subsections.label: LTV trends
points: Loans with LTV above 80% are increasing as a percentage of the total gross loan portfolio, generally originated in the apartment segment.
Increasing traction in Mumbai, Pune and larger cities across Gujarat and Maharashtra is driving this rise in LTV at origination.

subsections.label: Employee productivity / RM KRAs
points: RM KRAs include both number of transactions/loans originated and total value of disbursals; productivity has been fairly stable, not improved significantly over the last 3 years.
Overall employee-level disbursal value is about INR3.5 crore per year; sales employee-level is about INR5-5.5 crore per year.

Productivity per RM (AUM per employee, AUM per branch, disbursal per branch, disbursal per employee) is expected to gradually increase with ticket size increases, though mix of new versus old RMs and attrition affect visibility of this at an overall level.

Approval rate/origination process for higher ticket sizes remains largely the same as for the rest of the portfolio; the higher-ticket segment has only gradually grown as a proportion (from ~12% to ~18% over 2-3 years).

subsections.label: Customer experience / tech differentiation metrics
points: Three key metrics tracked for tech differentiation are opex, delinquencies and customer experience (NPS).

NPS for the quarter was 79, described as one of the more quantifiable customer experience metrics; overall customer experience assessment beyond NPS is more anecdotal (branch/customer visits, market understanding of turnaround times).
Other tech-attributable metrics include disbursal per branch/employee and AUM managed per branch/employee, reflecting the company's efficient, low-cost operation compared to peers/industry.

subsections.label: AI and technology strategy
points: Technology remains a key differentiator, central to sourcing, underwriting, servicing and scaling the business.
Digital DNA built since inception has created clean, structured data going back to day one, providing a high-quality training ground for modern AI systems.
AI strategy is anchored on three outcomes: elevating customer experience, enhancing employee productivity, and driving structural cost efficiencies.
Operationalized 'Cue', an in-house AI-orchestrated omnichannel customer communications platform.
Deployed in production a bureau analyzer and a contextual bank statement analysis model, which have improved underwriting efficiency and reduced turnaround.

AI-led interventions in lead qualification, legal and technical valuation, and income analysis are currently in pilot and will progressively move to production as the intelligent underwriting stack scales.

AI interventions such as automated calling are being used in collections for softer buckets, easing the workload on relationship managers who carry both sales and collection responsibilities; this has been a contributing factor to a good collections quarter, alongside more data-driven collections given a wealth of customer data.

It would be too early to attribute cost/delinquency/customer-experience improvements specifically to AI or tech; improvement is expected to be gradual, though current low-cost operating metrics already reflect the company's tech approach.

subsections.label: Green Homes initiative
points: Certified a further 100 homes during the quarter under the Green Homes initiative, taking the cumulative number of certified homes to 550 as of June 2026.

subsections.label: Branch and headcount expansion
points: During the quarter, added four branches, one each in Gujarat, Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu and Madhya Pradesh, taking the network to 175 branches and 373 touch points.
Net addition of 133 employees, largely in customer-facing roles, taking total headcount to 1,988.

Over the last 2 quarters, added 10 branches and 282 employees; analysis shows employees-per-branch rose from 10 to 11 (adding ~1 employee/branch on average across the network, plus new branch staffing), i.e., largely a per-branch headcount increase (RM and collections roles) rather than pure front-loading for future branch additions.
In HFFC's branch structure, branch managers and relationship managers carry both sales and collection responsibilities; there is no separate functional split.

subsections.label: Regional performance
points: Maharashtra, Gujarat and Madhya Pradesh remained the largest markets, leading overall business contribution while maintaining healthy growth and portfolio quality.

In Tamil Nadu, a strengthened team is building growth momentum while maintaining stable asset quality; earlier challenges from tariff impact (Tirupur) and team-related issues are now behind, and good growth momentum is expected going forward.
Rajasthan, Uttar Pradesh and southern states gained further traction, reflecting encouraging business momentum.
Remaining markets continued to deliver consistent AUM expansion with stable asset quality.
Madhya Pradesh has grown very fast, with book almost 4x in 2 years, attributed to building a strong local team.

Tamil Nadu number of districts served reduced from 25 to 24; this reflects operational servicing decisions (a branch closer to a different district may service accounts there) rather than portfolio exit; company monitors new district portfolios from an early stage and may pause origination if early loan performance doesn't show correct trends, until the situation is better understood.

subsections.label: Future geographic growth targets
points: Medium-term (next 1-3 years) growth targets include Uttar Pradesh, viewed as a large state with significant untapped potential.
Southern states — Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh and Telangana — are also targeted for better growth in coming years.
Rajasthan is already well-penetrated and hence not highlighted as a fresh target area.
Currently, Telangana contributes about 8% and Rajasthan about 10% of AUM, both below Madhya Pradesh's contribution.

key_figures.label: Funding from private and public banks

subsections.label: Co-lending and assignment activity
points: Executed a direct assignment transaction of INR285 crore during the quarter.
Co-lending disbursements were INR46 crore during the quarter, with the co-lending book at INR617 crore, representing 3.6% of AUM.
Funding profile continues to be diversified: 57% from private and public banks, 14% from NHB, and 21% from assignment and co-lending as of Jun'26.

key_figures.label: NHB scheme fixed rate loan tenure

subsections.label: NHB scheme structure
points: A particular NHB scheme carries a fixed rate loan tenure of 7 years, distinct from the floating rate structure applied to the rest of the borrowing portfolio.

key_figures.label: Credit bureau score of customers (3 years prior)
Customers with credit history (3 years prior)

subsections.label: Geopolitical / macro risk
points: West Asia crisis situation cited as a reason PLR cut is considered unlikely at this point.
War situation has not shown any impact on collections to date; management noted no stress buildup has been observed post the start of the war.
Tariff-related stress in pockets like Surat and Tirupur has largely been addressed; those pockets are now on an improvement trajectory.

subsections.label: Competitive intensity
points: Competitive intensity for BT out remains the same in terms of customer interest in taking BT outs; no read-through of reduced BT out rate to a change in industry landscape — attributed to internal processes.

subsections.label: CFO transition
points: CFO Nutan Gaba Patwari will step down from executive responsibilities effective August 31, 2026, after 8 years contributing to the company's financial architecture, governance standards, capital position and organizational capabilities.
The Board is evaluating candidates and will conclude the CFO appointment soon.

subsections.label: Delinquency trend structure
points: 1+ DPD, 30+ DPD and Gross Stage 3 ratios follow a certain trend based on customer segment, underwriting and collection processes; management stated it would not be possible to dramatically reduce these ratios without changing customer segment or underwriting methodology, which would in turn reduce interest margins.

subsections.label: AUM growth
points: Management remains confident of delivering 25% AUM growth for FY27 while maintaining focus on profitability, portfolio quality and operating efficiency.

subsections.label: Spread guidance
points: Committed to maintaining spread of 5%-5.25% on an overall blended basis; incremental spread was 5.40% and book spread 5.30% this quarter, but long-term guidance remains 5%-5.25%; questioning of 'sustainability' at current elevated levels was pushed back on since guidance has always been 5%-5.25%.
Running a fully floating rate book; if borrowing costs rise, pricing to customers will be increased accordingly to maintain the guided spread band.

subsections.label: Operating cost to assets
points: Full-year guidance for opex to assets is in the region of 2.6%-2.7%; expect a 5-10bps YoY reduction despite a slight uptick this quarter due to increments and fresh hiring.

subsections.label: PLR outlook
points: PLR cut considered unlikely at this point given ongoing West Asia crisis and related uncertainty; not the company's expectation at present.

subsections.label: BT out rate outlook
points: BT out rate of 4.5% in Q1 is the lowest in many quarters, attributed to internal processes (branch manager engagement with BT-out customers, top-up pitching, protocol waterfall) started 5-6 quarters ago.

Uncertain whether 4.5% level will sustain; guided expectation is to control BT out in the 5% ballpark/5%-6% range; could potentially move into 4% range if the trend continues for 2-3 more quarters, but management would not commit to that yet.

subsections.label: Co-lending outlook
points: Co-lending momentum was weak this quarter due to change in process and policies causing hiccups; these are being addressed gradually as more partner banks align to the process, and numbers are expected to stabilize going forward.

subsections.label: Asset quality outlook
points: First quarter is typically an important barometer with a usual uptick in delinquencies that takes a couple of quarters to normalize back to March levels; this quarter's collections were excellent, and management hopes this trend continues, aiming to keep DPD/GNPA numbers stable across quarters.

guidance_ledger.statement: We remain confident of delivering 25% AUM growth while maintaining our focus on profitability, portfolio quality and operating efficiency.
We are committed to maintaining that 5% to 5.25% basis points spread.
I think full year guidance would be in the region of 2.6% to 2.7%; we should expect year-on-year 5 to 10 basis point reduction.
We should be able to control it in that 5% to 6% kind of a range… we should be able to kind of control it in 5% ballpark range.
PLR cut is unlikely, I think, at this point because the whole West Asia crisis, etc, is still uncertain. I don't think there will be a cut.
Those numbers should stabilize going forward as more partner banks align to the process.
We generally assume 16% to 17% in our calculations.
We should be able to keep these numbers stable across quarters.
The Board is evaluating candidates and will conclude the CFO appointment soon.

The states that we are targeting for more aggressive growth would be eventually UP... Similarly, the southern states, which are Tamil Nadu, Andhra, Telangana, these 3 states we would be targeting for better growth in the coming years.
Guidance on the credit cost is the same, 30bps to 40bps.
We should be able to maintain our cost of borrowing in Q1'27 at around the levels of last quarter.
Our strategy is to add about 30 to 40 branches every year.
Ratio of housing to LAP will broadly remain in the same ballpark, about 80%-20%.
If everything goes well, we should be able to continue that trend over the next couple of years as well.
At this point, difficult to say whether 30% CAGR (achieved Mar'23-Mar'26) can be sustained; company has guided to 25% growth.

risk_register.risk: Geopolitical/macro uncertainty (West Asia crisis)
risk_register.note: Cited as reason PLR cut is unlikely; no impact of the war observed on collections to date.

risk_register.risk: Tariff-related stress in select pockets (Surat, Tirupur)
risk_register.note: Stress has largely been addressed; affected pockets are on an improvement trajectory.

key_takeaways: AUM stood at INR16,938 crore as of Jun'26, growing 25.7% year-on-year and 6.7% sequentially.
Disbursement at INR1,628 crore is up 31.0% year-on-year and 3.6% sequentially.
Profit after tax increased by 7.0% sequentially and 34.5% year-on-year to INR160 crore, supported by 38.2% growth in Net Interest Income.
Return on Assets improved by 10 basis points sequentially to 4.2%, while Return on Equity improved by 50 basis points to 14.5%.
During the quarter, we added four branches, one each in Gujarat, Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu and Madhya Pradesh, taking our network to 175 branches and 373 touch points.
Asset quality remained stable during the quarter. Our 1+ DPD remained flat at 4.7%, 30+ DPD remained flat at 3.2% and Gross Stage 3 remained flat at 1.8%.
We remain confident of delivering 25% AUM growth while maintaining our focus on profitability, portfolio quality and operating efficiency.
As disclosed to the stock exchanges, Nutan will step down from her executive responsibilities effective from August 31, 2026.

quarters.company: Home First Finance Company India Ltd
quarters.summary: Home First enters FY27 from a position of strength with healthy AUM growth guidance of ~25% YoY, improving asset quality, robust margins, and a well-capitalized balance sheet; management expects credit cost to remain at 30-40bps, spread to be maintained at 5%-5.25%, and cost of borrowing to stay range-bound in Q1FY27, with co-lending disruption expected to normalize by June 2026.

key_figures.label: Interest on term loans growth QoQ
Impact of 2 lesser days in quarter on interest income

subsections.label: Income statement drivers
points: Interest income on term loans growth of only 1.6% QoQ versus average principal outstanding growth of 5.5% QoQ was due to: 2 lesser days in Q4 vs Q3 impacting 2.2%, a 10bps PLR cut impacting 80bps, and origination yield impact of another 80bps.
Portfolio yields (ex co-lending) at 13.2% and disbursal yields at 13% reflect continued pricing discipline and healthy customer acquisition quality.

subsections.label: Liability management
points: Cost of borrowing (ex co-lending) contracted 10bps to 7.9% through proactive borrowing mix management.
Incremental borrowing costs remained favourable at ~7.6%, giving confidence in resilience of spread profile.
Company runs a 100% floating asset book, allowing repricing as cost of borrowing moves, to avoid carrying interest rate risk on the balance sheet.
Aim is to deliver portfolio-level spread in guided range of 5% to 5.25%.

subsections.label: Operating efficiency
points: Cost-to-income improvement is encouraging as it comes alongside continued investment in distribution, headcount and technology.
Full year opex includes one-time gratuity provision of INR3.3 crores from Q3FY26 due to implementation of new labour Code.
Operating cost to assets expected to remain broadly range-bound within 2.6% to 2.7% as company continues to invest for growth.

subsections.label: Capital adequacy and liquidity
points: Balance sheet remains very well capitalized following the INR1,250 crores QIP completed in Apr'25.
This positions the company well to continue investing in growth while maintaining a disciplined risk framework.

subsections.label: Write-offs and auctions
points: Total write-off scale is more or less in line with the growth in the business, not seen as extraordinarily high.
Company auctions anywhere between 50 and 100 units a month.

key_figures.label: Home loan vs LAP yield differential
Home loan vs LAP fee income (APR) differential
Cost of funding difference: co-lending vs balance sheet
Cost of funding gap vs AAA-rated HFCs

subsections.label: Product mix strategy
points: Consistency of individual housing loan mix (83%) reflects both strength of core franchise and granularity of portfolio.
Company offers wide bouquet of products from INR5 lakh to INR40 lakh ticket size, plus loan against property (LAP).
Ratio of housing to LAP mix expected to broadly remain ~80%-20%.

Customer segment migrating to higher ticket sizes is the same customer (informal income) as before; challenges in accessing loans from larger lenders remain the same, so no impact on yields despite ticket size increase — price of houses has gone up, not customer premium-ness.
Adjusted for borrowing cost, there is no decline in yields at all; the customer is willing to pay the premium.
5 years down the line, average ticket size could be ~INR40 lakh but customer segment and challenges will remain the same, hence yields will remain the same.

subsections.label: Co-lending strategy
points: Co-lending scaling doubled in disbursement FY26 vs FY25, driven by regulatory-related disruption resolution expected by June 2026.

Co-lending used as productivity enhancement tool: when distribution identifies a more formal customer who could get a bank loan, it is pushed through co-lending channel; informal segment customers booked as regular Homefirst loans.
Co-lending expands target market, offers better proposition to channels, and increases team productivity.

Company is NOT targeting a prime book — customer segment for co-lending still pays a premium (8-10%) versus true prime rate of 7.25-8%; inflation and lack of documentation drive higher ticket sizes, not a shift to prime.
Large part of INR20 lakh-plus ticket cohort is co-lending, but a good part is also regular customers who are informal-segment customers with larger ticket sizes.

In FY27, company will continue to scale co-lending business by further strengthening enabling infrastructure, providing opportunity to serve wider customer base while driving enhanced productivity and returns.

subsections.label: Yield and spread management
points: Yields must be looked at portfolio level; 100% floating asset book allows repricing as borrowing cost moves — essential to not carry interest rate risk on balance sheet.
Company anchors to maintaining spread (not yield) at 5% to 5.25%, passing on borrowing cost changes (up or down) to customers.

In FY24 vs FY25, company had led with price increase ahead of anticipated cost of borrowing hike, leading to temporarily higher spread for a shorter period; guidance has always remained 5% to 5.25% spread range.
Increase in LAP ratio is not substantial (~1% increase), so it does not move the yield needle much.

Credit cost overall doesn't fluctuate much by product; range is 20bps to 60bps across products including LAP — company is not pursuing a strategy of higher yield with substantially higher credit cost.

subsections.label: AI strategy
points: Technology is central to how the company sources, underwrites, services and scales the business.
Digital-first approach since inception has created clean, structured data assets providing a high-quality training ground for AI systems.
AI strategy anchored on 3 outcomes: elevating customer experience, enhancing employee productivity, and driving structural cost efficiencies.
Proprietary AI agents for income assessment and contextual bank statement analysis have already been operationalized.

AI-led interventions in lead qualification, legal and technical evaluation, and bureau analysis are currently in pilot and will progressively move to production as the intelligent underwriting stack scales.

Management can more confidently predict cost-side outcomes from AI (via higher productivity) than origination-side outcomes, which are expected to be more gradual; goal on origination side is to proactively capture loans that might otherwise get declined on the ground.

subsections.label: Green homes / sustainability
points: Green homes initiative continues to make progress with certification of additional homes during the quarter.

subsections.label: State-wise trends
points: All senior leadership positions in the branch network have been filled across all states, fully focused on delivering results in FY27.
Gujarat, MP, and Rajasthan showing healthy growth and stable asset quality.
Maharashtra has regained strong momentum particularly in Mumbai and Pune, reflected in robust AUM trajectory.
All southern states, including Tamil Nadu and Karnataka, are on track for strong growth in FY27.
The e-Khata issue in Karnataka is mostly behind the company now; it had caused a minor blip in market share for one or two quarters.
In UP, team is being built, preparing a strong base for FY28.
Tamil Nadu market share was not strong to start with and dropped further last year due to muted growth; company expects to catch up in coming years now that base and teams are ready.
Tamil Nadu and Telangana challenges were largely internal team-building issues (staffing), not external/demand issues; these are now resolved and company expects a good year ahead.
No new significant competitors identified in southern states; existing set of players remain, with some more active depending on season/year.

subsections.label: Branch expansion strategy
points: Company only puts up a branch if it has potential to reach average branch disbursal potential of INR2-3 crores/month; otherwise operates as touch point/satellite location.

Branch strategy: two-pronged — some additions in new locations/cities identified across states, and greater addition in existing cities to increase branch density in larger cities to improve distribution and access.
Not targeting a specific state for the 30-40 new branches; broad-based approach.
Productivity metrics (AUM per branch, disbursal per branch, AUM per employee) expected to keep inching up as company scales.
Employees per branch may fluctuate short-term with new branch additions but broadly remains range-bound at 9-12; will only gradually move up as company scales over 2-3 years.

subsections.label: Mumbai-Pune sourcing strategy
points: Mumbai-Pune are formal apartment markets where sourcing largely comes from developers building housing projects — traditionally strongholds of banks.
Company replicated a developer-led sourcing structure (already used in Ahmedabad, Surat etc.) into Mumbai and Pune, allowing penetration into markets where banks used to be much stronger.
This transformation began ~24 months ago and has become much larger/is really taking off now.

Within RERA-approved bank-dominated projects, ~90% of customers have formal income/documentation (served by banks); the remaining ~10% with informal income who struggle to get bank loans (often from deep suburbs like Kalyan, Ambernath, Badlapur, Palghar) are Home First's target segment.
Some part of Mumbai-Pune strategy will be replicated in other larger cities (Bangalore, Delhi, Hyderabad), though those are more individual-housing markets versus developer-led.

subsections.label: Connector network
points: Wider bouquet of products (including co-lending) allows connectors to address a larger target market of customers, which is well recognized by channels.
Big jump in number of connectors in the last quarter.
Connector fee negotiations are ongoing; company addresses fee demands via timely payouts, wider product bouquet, and faster turnaround times rather than purely raising fees.
Tactical fee increases may occur for specific connectors/locations but overall movement is 10-15bps; fee planning also depends on connector throughput, file quality, and other tracked metrics.

subsections.label: Geopolitical/macro risk
points: Company has not yet observed any significant impact from the ongoing war in the Middle East on collections or bounce rates; only sporadic anecdotal discussions, nothing visible at central level.
Fresh slippage % in April 2026 is lower than April 2025 and April 2024, indicating no visible demand or credit impact so far from West Asia crisis.
No drop in demand observed due to West Asia crisis; April has been fairly good.

subsections.label: US tariff impact (H1FY26)
points: First half of FY26 saw elevated delinquencies and difficult collections partly impacted by tariffs; this issue has since been put to rest.

subsections.label: Internal execution risk (resolved)
points: H1FY26 weakness was driven by a combination of: overhang from prior credit issue causing elevated delinquencies, sluggish demand, and internal staffing issues/attrition in some locations.
These internal issues have since been resolved — positions filled, teams rebuilt, giving confidence entering FY27.

subsections.label: Co-lending regulatory disruption
points: Co-lending volumes were low this quarter due to regulatory changes; issue expected to be addressed by end of May 2026, with June 2026 expected to be a normal month.

subsections.label: Competitive intensity
points: Competition from larger HFCs and banks in ticket sizes/segments is an ongoing, cyclical dynamic (up and down by month/season) but nothing new or significant reported.
Larger HFCs losing prime loans to big banks are reportedly targeting some of the same customer 'zip codes' Home First excels in, but no significant new activity observed yet.

subsections.label: Growth outlook
points: Strong exit run rate in Q4 gives confidence entering FY27.
Company positioned to deliver around 25% YoY AUM growth based on current position.
Focus remains: grow with discipline, protect portfolio quality, improve productivity, deepen customer franchise, and continue delivering strong and sustainable profitability.

Organizational distribution strength (connector network, branches, RMs) rebuilt over last year, and delivery of last two quarters gives confidence to sustain 25% growth; FY27 confidence driven by exit momentum and continued April disbursal.

If everything goes well, growth trend could continue over the next couple of years beyond FY27, though management stated it is difficult to say at this point whether growth could return to the historical 30% CAGR (Mar'23-Mar'26) achieved previously.

subsections.label: Margin/spread outlook
points: Management confident of maintaining spread above 5%, within 5%-5.25% guidance range, regardless of borrowing cost movements — passing on cost benefit or increase to customers as needed.

Q1FY27 cost of borrowing expected to be maintained around levels of last quarter; beyond Q1, decision on repricing customers depends on actual market pricing movements including potential repo hikes and bank MCLR repricing.
Not planning to cut PLR further at the moment; company will stay put after the 10bps cut made in January.

subsections.label: Cost outlook
points: Operating cost to assets ratio expected to remain broadly range-bound within 2.6% to 2.7% as company continues to invest for growth.

subsections.label: Co-lending outlook
points: Co-lending run rate expected to be similar to or better than last year's run rate once regulatory issues are addressed by June 2026.
Company to continue scaling co-lending business in FY27 by further strengthening enabling infrastructure.

guidance_ledger.statement: Positioned to deliver around 25% year-on-year AUM growth.
Aim remains to deliver a spread at a portfolio level in guided range of 5% to 5.25%.
Expect this ratio to remain broadly range-bound within 2.6% to 2.7%.
Guidance on the credit cost is the same, 30bps to 40bps.
We should be able to maintain our cost of borrowing in Q1'27 at around the levels of last quarter.
Our strategy is to add about 30 to 40 branches every year.
Thereafter, the run rate of co-lending would be similar or maybe better than what we saw last year.
Ratio of housing to LAP will broadly remain in the same ballpark, about 80%-20%.
If everything goes well, we should be able to continue that trend over the next couple of years as well.
Not at the moment. We have already done with the 10 basis points in January. So we will want to stay put for now.
At this point, difficult to say whether 30% CAGR (achieved Mar'23-Mar'26) can be sustained; company has guided to 25% growth.

themes.note: 1+ DPD, 30+ DPD, Stage 2 and Gross Stage 3 all improved sequentially in Q4FY26; April 2026 collection trends better than April 2025 and 2024.

themes.label: AUM growth guidance
themes.note: Company guided to ~25% YoY AUM growth for FY27, down from historical ~30% CAGR (Mar'23-Mar'26), driven by rebuilt distribution and exit momentum.
