subsections.label: India business performance
points: India business growth and profitability are positively correlated per management framing; India EBITDA pre-Ind AS 116 margin expanded 6 pp YoY.

Remote optometry stores expanded 3.7x in a single year, enabling Tier+ expansion — described as the outcome of a 36-month journey that began when optometry shortage was identified as a core constraint.

subsections.label: International business performance
points: International growth was broad-based across Japan, Southeast Asia, and Middle East, with Japan delivering the strongest performance.
Middle East (about 6% of international store count) had a temporary dip in store traffic but recovered to near normal; business proved resilient.

Japan delivered record revenue growth and same-store growth this year, cited as evidence that mature-seeming international markets are actually growing rapidly once fully integrated into Lenskart's ecosystem (centralized supply chain, omnichannel, Gold subscription, product/lens portfolio depth).

KSA (Saudi Arabia) is about two years into its journey and is reported to be ahead of where Dubai/UAE was at the same stage; company remains bullish and continues opening stores there, though EBITDA breakeven timing not disclosed for competitive reasons.

subsections.label: Tier 2 and deeper market expansion
points: Opportunity in Tier 2 and beyond is now seen as larger than initially assumed because value proposition (choice, quality, speed, customer experience of an organized centralized platform) is exponentially stronger for underserved consumers there.
Opened a Lenskart store inside an army cantonment in Srinagar — the first branded retail store of any category inside that premise.
Small towns like Saharsa (Bihar), Shahdol (Madhya Pradesh), Golaghat (Assam), and Jhargram (West Bengal) each delivered about ₹16-17 lakhs per month revenue in their first year.
More than 200 Tier 2 stores added, feeding data into the GeoIQ model, which continually improves identification of new micro-markets for expansion.

Long-term store target of 4,500 is now seen as understated; management believes the addressable opportunity is larger, referencing India having 60,000-70,000 existing eyewear stores versus ~20x more jewellery stores and global optical-density benchmarks suggesting room for another 70,000-80,000 eyewear stores.

subsections.label: Meller brand traction
points: Meller is scaling beyond plan; online-first model performing well in its original markets.
Brand launched across 1,000+ stores in India, launched in Middle East, launched across all Lenskart stores in Southeast Asia, and about to launch in Japan.
Running out of stock in all markets, including Southeast Asia where a Korean pop star wearing it organically went viral.
Growth also emerging from Europe; inbound interest from top malls wanting to open dedicated Meller stores.

Ambition described as creating 'the next Gentle Monster' for a Gen Z-oriented cohort; two unconventional recent product launches (Meller Lab and another series) cited as evidence of demand-led product design working well.
Current challenge is scaling supply/delivery to meet sudden volume demand increases.

subsections.label: Premiumization alongside mass adoption
points: Company continues launching lower-priced products (e.g., New Lens Replacement program) to enable mass adoption while simultaneously seeing premiumization via Owndays lenses, progressives, Meller sunglasses, and Owndays frames.
Premium offerings are positioned to deliver roughly 10x value versus competitive brands at same/higher price points.
Reinforces brand resonance across full customer spectrum from value seekers to affluent customers.

subsections.label: AI-first operating model (FY27 priority)
points: Single biggest FY27 priority is growth, driven by transforming Lenskart from a consumer tech company into a consumer AI company, embedding AI at every level and function.
Company is working to attract AI talent, similar to earlier efforts to attract engineering talent for an eyewear company.

subsections.label: Scaling eye tests via technology
points: Ambition is 100 million eye tests at minimum, eventually a billion; given global optometrist shortage, technology is viewed as the only path to that scale.
Company will step up R&D investment for automating eye testing and for new customer acquisition innovation across products, formats, access points, pricing and offers.

subsections.label: Integrated AI-driven value chain
points: Vertical integration allows wiring intelligence across every layer of the value chain — eye test data informs product design, social trends reach manufacturing within days.
Factory floor automation is moving toward near-full automation from a current base of 75%.
Ambition to own a greater share of the value chain — equipment, raw material, manufacturing, distribution, and final mile — closing the AI feedback loop across every layer.

subsections.label: Smart glasses / B by Lenskart
points: B by Lenskart, described as a premium-priced smart eyewear product, launched in Q4 with 30,000+ customers on the waitlist and growing daily.
Smart glasses viewed as a multi-year journey; company believes it has a structural advantage via its stores, optometry network, and prescription capability.
Increased R&D investment planned to develop various forms of eyewear, with multiple product launches expected in FY27.
Management views smart glasses as eventually becoming prescription glasses, sold through optical networks, giving Lenskart a large role regardless of which company wins the hardware form factor.

On competitive intensity (e.g., Google's announced entry using Gemini Live, which Lenskart also uses), management stated nobody yet has a clear 'home run' form factor; the company will stay agile, focus on learning use cases, conversational styles, and price-point comfort rather than immediate sales.

subsections.label: Customer experience reinvention (AI-led)
points: Plans include reinventing customer experience end-to-end: app-led discovery, AI-powered planogramming, myopia management of kids.
Company is initiating 'thousands of experiments' to deliver new customer delight moments.
Investing in improving predictability of the 'last 2-3%' of every customer experience.

subsections.label: Delivery network technology
points: Next-day delivery network expanded to 78 cities (from an initial 7, then ~30), still served out of the centralized Bhiwadi facility.
Company offers a money-back promise if the delivery promise is not met.
Same-day delivery still in experimental phase — piloted in Singapore and some Indian markets; no specific target set yet; company will share data as experiments mature.

Stores are increasingly viewed as a multi-modal network (described metaphorically as a 'chemist', not a warehouse) to potentially support faster delivery experiments, alongside existing at-home frame trial services.

key_figures.label: Value delivered by premium products vs competitive brands

subsections.label: Manufacturing investment and localization
points: New Hyderabad manufacturing facility investment funded via FY26 operating cash flow alongside store capex.
Hyderabad plant and Thailand JV described as structural answers to reduce import dependence over time and mitigate currency headwinds.
Product margin resilience (64% in India) attributed to starting frame manufacturing seven years ago and localizing it to India two years ago.
Foundation for high NPS credited to automation set up at the Bhiwadi factory, including logistics and sortation, enabling next-day delivery across 78 cities.

key_figures.label: Share of business that is international
Revenue per month for select smaller-town stores (first year)
India margin at same store-count stage in FY23

subsections.label: International markets as real, growing businesses
points: International markets are not mature/slow-growing as conventionally assumed; consumer need is real and not yet served by an organized solution at scale.

Full Lenskart proposition rollout into a market is gradual: integrating centralized supply chain, omnichannel model, Gold subscription, and full product/lens portfolio depth builds a compelling value proposition, after which consumers shift via word of mouth.
Japan cited as a strong example of record revenue and same-store growth in a market assumed to be mature; the same playbook is now working across Southeast Asia and Middle East.

subsections.label: Currency and raw material exposure
points: No meaningful impact yet from freight and raw material costs, as these represent only a fraction of total cost.
Currency (rupee depreciation on imports) is the biggest cost variable/headwind, offset so far by international mix (42% of business) and continued vertical integration.
RMB appreciation from 11 to 14 and dollar-rupee depreciation offset structural margin improvements from vertical integration/process changes this year, keeping product margin flat.
Moving more production to India via the Hyderabad plant is expected to accelerate margin visibility as currency exposure reduces.

subsections.label: Market opportunity framing
points: Company currently serves only 50 million people in a world where billions need better vision; myopia problem described as big and growing.
Smart glasses described as opening an entirely new dimension of opportunity, with AI providing additional capability.

Recommended KPI for investors: trailing 12-month volume growth, described as the cleanest measure of underlying market expansion since it strips out ASP mix, currency translation, and campaign timing effects.

subsections.label: Global consumer brand building
points: Company building borderless eyewear brands serving distinct cohorts and occasions.
Plans to step up cultural collaborations (e.g., Stranger Things, Devil Wears Prada 2, Pop Mart) combined with disciplined M&A, with Meller cited as a stepping stone for future brand building.

subsections.label: Stores as community hubs
points: 3,300+ store network envisioned evolving beyond showrooms into neighbourhood hubs — part warehouse, part clinic, part service center, part last-mile node — akin to a local chemist.
Increasing store density seen as a natural logistics advantage as quick commerce reshapes customer expectations.

subsections.label: Demand resilience commentary
points: No material impact observed so far on Indian or international demand from geopolitical/macro factors; domestic consumption-driven eye health viewed as largely non-discretionary.
Middle East disturbance caused only a smaller, temporary dip in business that bounced back quickly, though management acknowledged a discretionary/fashion element exists in the category.
If consumption pressure pushes consumers toward cheaper alternatives, Lenskart's value-conscious offerings are seen as a potential strong alternative in weak macro periods.

subsections.label: Acquisitions and pro forma reporting
points: Reported financials reflect acquisitions of Dealskart, Meller, and GeoIQ from their respective transaction closing dates, while pro forma financials present these as if always part of the company for clearer trend analysis.
For Q4 FY26 there is no difference between pro forma and reported financials; differences exist only in the prior-year comparative period and will diminish over time.
Disciplined M&A cited as part of the global brand-building strategy, with Meller as a stepping stone for future brand acquisitions.

subsections.label: Currency and geopolitical risk
points: Currency (rupee depreciation on imports) flagged as the biggest cost-side variable/headwind, though offset so far by international revenue mix and vertical integration.
Geopolitical uncertainty, currency, and demand cycles could create short-term bumps in the external environment.
Middle East store traffic saw a temporary dip due to disturbance, though the business proved resilient and recovered to near normal.

subsections.label: Competitive risk in smart glasses
points: Smart glasses space is becoming very competitive, with Google announcing ambitions in this space using Gemini Live (a technology Lenskart also uses); no company yet has a clear winning form factor.

key_figures.label: Net new store additions FY27 expected

subsections.label: FY27 operating outlook
points: Net new store additions for FY27 are expected to be around FY26 levels.
Long-term steady-state EBITDA pre-Ind AS margin expectation remains unchanged at approximately 25%.
Quarterly margin will vary based on store opening phasing, market seasonality, and long-term bets made ahead of the curve.
Company will stay the course through external uncertainty (geopolitics, currency, demand cycles) and lean in further where these create opportunities.
Compounding effect of revenue and margin expected to continue, with priority on long-term value creation over short-term linearity.

Seven strategic priorities outlined for FY27: AI-first operating model; scaling to 100 million customers (eye tests); building an integrated system (greater value-chain ownership, AI feedback loop); evolving stores into multi-role community hubs; building a global consumer brand; reinventing customer experience end-to-end; and increasing R&D investment to make eyewear 'do more' (smart glasses, multiple product launches).

guidance_ledger.statement: Net new store additions for FY27 are expected to be around FY26 levels.

guidance_ledger.metric: Long-term steady-state EBITDA pre-Ind AS margin
guidance_ledger.statement: Our long-term steady-state EBITDA pre-Ind AS margin expectation remains unchanged to approximately 25%.
India eyewear units reached 29 million in FY26, up from 18 million two years ago, with the next key milestone we are working towards is 100 million.
Our ambition is not 30 million eye tests. It is 100 million at the least and eventually a billion.
Our long-term runway of 4,500 stores; management indicated this number is expected to expand materially given Tier 2 demand surprise, though no new formal number was given.
We haven't taken a specific target for same-day delivery; still running experiments and piloting in some markets.
KSA is ahead of where Dubai/UAE was at the same stage; company remains bullish but did not disclose specific breakeven timing for competitive reasons.
Margin in international has grown by another percent this year and this will continue to grow in the future; difficult to time on a quarter basis.
The compounding effect of revenue and margin will continue, but we will always prioritize action for long-term value creation over short-term linearity.

risk_register.risk: Currency / rupee depreciation on imports
risk_register.note: Biggest cost variable; offset so far by 42% international mix and vertical integration; RMB move from 11 to 14 plus dollar-rupee depreciation offset structural margin gains this year, keeping India product margin flat at 64%.

risk_register.risk: Geopolitical uncertainty and demand cycles
risk_register.note: Flagged as a source of potential short-term bumps for FY27; no material impact seen so far on Indian or international demand.

risk_register.risk: Middle East regional disturbance / store traffic dip
risk_register.note: Temporary, smaller dip in traffic that bounced back quickly; eyewear category proved resilient though some discretionary/fashion element exists.

risk_register.risk: Discretionary consumption pressure
risk_register.note: If consumers move toward cheaper alternatives amid consumption pressure, management believes Lenskart's value-conscious offerings could be a strong alternative.

risk_register.risk: Competitive intensity in smart glasses
risk_register.note: Space getting more competitive with entrants like Google (using Gemini Live); no player yet has a clear winning form factor, requiring Lenskart to stay agile.

risk_register.risk: Freight and raw material cost impact
risk_register.note: No meaningful impact seen so far as these costs are a fraction of total cost base.

themes.label: Operating leverage / margin compounding
themes.note: Q4 confirms the compounding phase thesis where incremental revenue adds more to EBITDA; India and international both saw broad-based margin expansion.

themes.label: Tier 2+ demand opportunity
themes.note: Opportunity in Tier 2 and beyond found to be larger than initially assumed, driving above-plan store additions and long-term store count target expansion beyond 4,500.

themes.label: International expansion maturity
themes.note: International markets (Japan, Southeast Asia, Middle East, KSA) are proving to be real, fast-growing businesses rather than mature/slow markets, following India's integration playbook.

themes.label: Currency headwind
themes.note: Rupee depreciation and RMB appreciation offset structural margin gains from vertical integration, though international mix and localization (Hyderabad plant, Thailand JV) provide mitigation.

themes.label: AI-led transformation
themes.note: FY27's top priority is transforming into a consumer AI company, embedding AI across eye testing, manufacturing, customer experience and value-chain integration.

themes.label: Smart glasses / B by Lenskart
themes.note: B by Lenskart launched with strong waitlist demand, but competitive intensity is rising (e.g., Google) and no player yet has a winning form factor; viewed as a multi-year journey.

themes.label: Premiumization alongside mass adoption
themes.note: Company simultaneously opens low-cost offerings (OPP, New Lens Replacement) and drives premium upgrades (Owndays, Meller, progressives), with Meller brand traction exceeding plan.

key_takeaways: First, the deeper we go, the wider the problem we are solving.
Second, international is not an experiment, it is a business.
Third, premiumization on customer's terms.
Revenue grew 41% year-on-year to ₹2,516 crores, our strongest quarter as a public company.
EBITDA grew 61% year-on-year in Q4 with EBITDA margins expanding 2.7 percentage points to 21.3%.
We crossed three key milestones for the first time: ₹1,700 crores of EBITDA, ₹1,000 crores of pre-Ind AS EBITDA, and ₹500 crores of PAT.
NPS in India reached an all-time high of 81.4.
On operating outlook, net new store additions for FY27 are expected to be around FY26 levels. Our long-term steady-state EBITDA pre-Ind AS margin expectation remains unchanged to approximately 25%.
pressing_questions: Percy Panthaki asked: For international to get to India's ~15% pre-Ind AS margin, would it get there at the same rupees million sale, the same number of stores, or some other metric — Peyush responded it's difficult to comment on which quarter it will land at 15%, recommending a longer-term view instead of quarter-by-quarter modelling.

Percy Panthaki asked whether KSA has reached EBITDA breakeven or is expected to in FY27 — Peyush said he could only share, for competitive reasons, that KSA is ahead of where Dubai/UAE was at the same stage, without disclosing a specific breakeven timeline.

CPPLUS.about: Aditya Infotech Limited (AIL) manufactures and provides video security and surveillance products, solutions, and services under the brand name 'CP Plus'.[1]

quarters.summary: Q1 FY27 marked a strong start to the year with revenue up 89.5% YoY and EBITDA margin at 14.8%, in line with the FY27 guidance of 14-15% EBITDA margin reiterated by management. The company continues to invest in backward integration (housing/enclosures, cables JV, lens localization), capacity expansion (Kadapa, Greater Noida, R&D centers), and new product categories (Pro series, Home IoT, industrial robots, drone cameras), with export opportunities expected to materialize in 18-24 months; management guided price increases of ~15-20% taken by end of H1 against a full-year target of ~25%, and reiterated FY27 EBITDA margin guidance while deferring further margin commentary to after H1 results.

key_figures.label: Marketing expense share of full-year total
Marketing expense proportion vs revenue in Q1

subsections.label: Revenue and margin drivers
points: Revenue growth driven by strong traction by CP PLUS brand in the overall AIL revenue.
IP products made up 79% of CP PLUS portfolio, reflecting increasing adoption of higher-value and intelligent AI surveillance solutions.
CP PLUS contribution rose to 87% of overall revenue.
Gross margin moderated slightly from Q4 due to exhaustion of lower-cost inventory.
EBITDA margin improvement supported by favorable product and brand mix, as well as better operational efficiencies.
Adjusted PAT growth attributed to lowering of finance costs by 59% YoY and better cost efficiencies.

subsections.label: Balance sheet and working capital
points: Working capital metrics showed meaningful progress, with reduction in inventory and debtor days resulting in improvement of cash conversion cycle to 64 days.
Balance sheet remains robust, with debt to equity reducing sharply to 0.07 level.
These metrics highlight not only growth but sustainable and profitable growth.

subsections.label: IPO / valuation milestone
points: On August 5, 2025, Aditya Infotech Limited officially debuted on the stock market under its flagship security brand CP PLUS, with an oversubscribed IPO that listed at a significant premium.
On the back of an exceptional year of business and margin growth, valuation has grown over 5x to touch nearly INR45,000 crores.

subsections.label: Other expenses commentary
points: Increase in other expenses from INR950 crores to INR1,170 crores flagged by an analyst; management stated nothing material, citing seasonality.
Marketing expense has seasonality — not linear with 20% quarterly revenue run-rate; expected to be around 30-32% of the whole year's marketing spend in H1 due to events like IPL.
Other expenses broadly in line with inflationary factors such as appraisals and other multiple items; nothing odd flagged.

subsections.label: CP PLUS brand momentum
points: CP PLUS brand continued to maintain strong momentum and contributed approximately 87% of overall Q1 revenue.
IP products accounted for nearly 79% of CP PLUS portfolio, reflecting increasing adoption of higher-value and intelligent AI surveillance solutions.

subsections.label: Cable JV business classification
points: Corelink Cable Technology JV (with Orient Cables) will manufacture CCTV cables and networking cables sold under CP PLUS brand as an attached accessories business (not part of BOM) — estimated at not less than 5% of CP PLUS's overall revenue.

Second stage of the JV involves helping localize CCTV cable cameras and harness cables (backward integration into BOM), where optimization/backward integration impact is expected to be minimal, in single-digit percentage points.

subsections.label: New corporate office & R&D center
points: Inaugurated new corporate office and R&D center on 2nd August 2026, combining a modern workplace, an experience center, and highly advanced innovation and testing laboratories.
Strengthens product development capabilities, improves team collaboration, and reinforces commitment to innovation-led growth.
Currently three operational R&D centers: Noida, Ahmedabad, and Taiwan; a new one will shortly open in Bengaluru.

subsections.label: New product category exploration
points: Actively exploring expansion into new categories: machine vision cameras, drone camera modules, industrial autonomous mobile robots (AMRs), and home IoT products such as video door phones, door locks, and smart doorbells.
Broadening professional portfolio through CP PLUS Pro series of high-end AI-powered solutions, global shutter cameras, and explosion-proof products.
Several offerings under final stage of development, targeted to launch by Q4 of this year.

CP PLUS Pro series developed by Taiwan R&D center, on highest-end categories of SOC components; intended to compete with highest category of global brands and address high-end government/enterprise demand vacuum, offering better value proposition given lower cost vs global brand pricing.
Home IoT expansion covers door phones, doorbells, and possibly door locks.
Industrial automation exploration includes industrial robots, AMRs, and high-speed high-precision machine vision cameras for manufacturing lines.

Drone gimbal cameras under study; company believes it is best-positioned to manufacture these in India as they are not currently manufactured much domestically; hopes to bring to market in coming years.
All new categories at different stages of go-to-market strategy.

Timelines: CP PLUS Pro and Home IoT categories targeted to be live by end of Q3/beginning of Q4; AGVs, home/industrial robots, and drone cameras remain at exploratory/study stage with no firm commercialization timeline yet.

subsections.label: Nexivue second brand
points: Accelerating rollout of Nexivue brand and expanding product portfolio further under this second brand in the coming months.
Enables company to serve a wider range of customers and increase channel partner coverage.

subsections.label: AI strategy
points: Artificial Intelligence represents one of the most significant growth opportunities ahead.

Progressing through multiple stages across government, enterprise, small and medium-size business, and strategic market segments — ranging from proof of concept and commercialization to development and evaluation.
Objective is to build scalable AI-powered solutions leveraging existing market presence while opening new growth avenues.

subsections.label: R&D cost disclosure
points: R&D cost is not budgeted or tracked as a percentage of revenue; treated as a strategic moat and investment area, with spend scaling as needed rather than being capped to a revenue ratio.

subsections.label: Housing & enclosure expansion
points: Housing and enclosure expansion progressing as planned and expected to become operational by Q3 of this financial year.

subsections.label: Kadapa greenfield expansion
points: Advancing on Kadapa greenfield expansion; land acquisition in final stages.
Kadapa facility currently supports a capacity of approximately 2.5 million units per month, providing foundation for future growth.

subsections.label: Greater Noida second cluster
points: Developing a second manufacturing cluster in Greater Noida; land bank identified and applied to authorities for allocation.

points: Incorporated Corelink Cable Technology Private Limited, a joint venture with Orient Cables for manufacturing of network LAN and CCTV coaxial cables.

subsections.label: Manufacturing line additions
points: This month adding three more FA lines and one MI line.
With this addition, total of 42 FA lines, 4 MI lines and 12 SMT lines by end of August.

subsections.label: Capacity expansion plan / utilization
points: Company has broadly spoken about almost doubling capacity in the next three years.
Intermediary land expansion acquired in Kadapa will be site of first expansion.
Greater Noida land bank will be the second manufacturing cluster; gradual capacity build-up expected quarter-on-quarter.
Capacity utilization currently 85-90%, varying month-on-month based on supply chain.
AIL ranked as third largest factory in the world, cited as part of manufacturing moat.

subsections.label: Backward integration / localization
points: Backward integration activities span housing enclosures, cable connectors, lenses, and (in future) bare PCBs locally with third-party supply chains.
Each localization category expected to add basis points to margins, though exact quantification premature; scale manufacturing in-house for these initiatives to kick off in Q3/Q4 of this year.

Company is building a completely backward-integrated lens plant; currently setting up a trial automatic line to produce a few lakh units while working in parallel on a fully automated plant — future localization contingent on this working out.
Localization limited to what's feasible in India and not core dependency areas like semiconductors/passive electronic components (dependent on KGD, fab, etc.), which remain non-localized for now.
Bare PCB and lens localization highlighted as next potential backward integration areas; trials already ongoing via third parties.

subsections.label: Export opportunity
points: Export is on the company's plans but is a longer-term initiative, with significant numbers expected in the next 18 to 24 months.
Current focus is on supply chain constraints and capacity expansion in the domestic market; export focus will follow after the new enterprise/Pro portfolio is released and field-tested in India.
CP PLUS Pro series (enterprise range built to global standards) is the portfolio expected to address the export opportunity.

subsections.label: Component sourcing mix
points: Critical semiconductor-based solutions are largely sourced from Taiwan, as most fabs are Taiwan-based (companies Japanese, Korean, American, or Taiwanese); Indian law disallows use of Chinese semiconductors.
Passive electronics (15-20% of BOM) sourced from both Taiwan and China.
Housing, enclosures, cable connectors being localized; trials underway for lenses and a few other categories.
Expect a shift toward 55-60% import / 40% domestic BOM split once localization initiatives kick off over the next two quarters.

Future localization possibilities tied to potential domestic fab development and India-designed chip collaboration; bare PCB scale-up and lens backward integration plant are parallel initiatives dependent on scale-up success.

subsections.label: Forex hedging policy
points: Company follows a hedging practice on forex exposure for more than five-seven years, hedged on a weekly basis and built into costs.

Detailed hedging policy reviewed and adjusted by the board; coverage of receivables and creditors has not gone below 85% at any point, adjusted between 85%-100% depending on trends; current quarter coverage at 90%+ levels.
Weekly shipment hedges are blocked in coming weeks to maintain the 85%-90% hedge range.

subsections.label: Component supply chain resilience
points: Diversified base of SOC, memory, flash, and sensor suppliers has helped reduce concentration risks and enhance ability to navigate periodic disruptions across the global component ecosystem.
Multi-sourcing strategy followed to manage risks and ensure greater supply chain resilience.
On SOC and memory sourcing, company continues rolling forecast/coverage strategy of three to four quarters with vendors; no material disruptions currently seen.
No impact from Middle East crisis on supply chain at this time, barring some impact on forex which is co-hedged; some impact flagged on freight and logistics.

subsections.label: Market share and moat
points: Market share stood at 43.3% in the Indian video surveillance industry in FY2026, per Frost & Sullivan report, with position effectively doubling over the period shown.
Reflects growing acceptance of products, wider channel penetration, and ability to address evolving customer requirements across all major vertical segments.

Moat levers cited: brand strength (almost synonymous with the category), distribution reach (increased quarter on quarter, including direct connect with SIs and end customers), unparalleled manufacturing scale (third largest factory in the world), R&D as an evolving strength enabling broad-based sourcing, and manpower/management depth.
Despite moat, competition exists — almost 40+ brands have become STQC empanelled; company maps market shares across categories and is comfortable with its positioning.
CCTV is a priority sector for the government; no deviation from policy expected at this time despite recent allowance of Chinese firms into other sectors like transformers.

subsections.label: Enterprise/government/AI-driven demand strategy
points: Enhanced focus on enterprise, government, and AI-driven opportunities; moving towards a top-down demand generation model.
Model involves identifying target accounts, engaging customers directly, securing empanelment at design stage, and fulfilling projects through system integrator and channel ecosystem.
Approach enables influencing demand and specification at an earlier stage, improving specification wins, and advancing position within the value chain.
Dedicated teams in demand generation, pre-sales, business development, and vertical solutions helping deepen customer engagement and strengthen position in larger, higher-value projects.

subsections.label: New category TAM potential
points: CP PLUS Pro series targets a decent TAM currently catered by global brands, aiming to capture share from that segment.
Home IoT (doorbells, door locks) is a new market to be developed, with potential to be part of every home and represent a great TAM over several years.
Industrial automation and drone gimbal camera markets are being explored and strategy/reports developed; work has begun with good progress but too early to size precisely.

Management responded to analyst suggestion of an additional INR5,000-10,000 crore opportunity from new categories with cautious optimism, calling these 'good adjacencies' where the company has technology expertise, without committing to the figure.

subsections.label: Leadership build-out
points: Strengthened leadership team over the last year through key appointments including Head of Credit and General Counsel.
CHRO will join shortly; recruitment for Head of Mergers and Acquisition is progressing.

Building a stronger second line of leadership across marketing, finance, product management, and sales functions to ensure leadership continuity, accelerate execution, and support sustainable long-term growth.

subsections.label: Cable JV strategic rationale
points: Corelink Cable Technology JV with Orient Cables serves dual purpose: (1) attached accessories business for CCTV/networking cables sold under CP PLUS brand, and (2) future backward integration into harness cables/BOM.

subsections.label: Input cost inflation
points: Cost hikes in DDR and SOC have been phenomenal across all product categories, not only CCTV.

Company is not passing on the full cost hike via price increase at one go, managing it on a monthly or quarterly scale depending on the product, to avoid an inflationary shock to consumers that could temporarily affect consumption.
So far no major consumption effect has been seen from price increases; company hopes to mitigate inflationary pressures going forward.
Global commentary suggests supply-side price hikes on SOC/memory are expected to continue for some more time.

subsections.label: Regulatory / STQC transition
points: STQC norm (barring Chinese semiconductors/memory in CCTV products, requiring cyber-secured, government-tested products) came into effect 9th April 2025; in March 2026 government allowed clearance of old inventory, after which (post April 1, 2026) sale of old Chinese-component-based inventory is banned.
Transition period of about one and a half years; market had pumped in old inventory in early 2025/2026, now exhausted.
40+ brands are now STQC certified and selling compliant products — increasing competitive intensity.
Supply chain and cost escalation challenges are more manageable for large organizations like AIL with ability to secure semiconductors, while smaller players are grappling with these challenges.

subsections.label: Geopolitical / external shocks
points: No impact currently from Middle East crisis on raw material procurement or supply chain, barring some impact on forex (which is co-hedged) and some impact on freight and logistics.

subsections.label: Policy risk (competitive entry)
points: Analyst raised concern about government potentially allowing Chinese firms back into protected sectors (citing transformer/electrical equipment precedent); management does not see any deviation from government policy for CCTV, which remains a priority sector.

subsections.label: Margin guidance reiteration
points: Management reiterated FY27 EBITDA margin guidance of 14-15%; Q1 stood at 14.8%, in line with guidance.
Company stands by the guidance at this stage and will comment further after half-year results; internally always tries to beat guidance.

On sustainability of margins amid low-cost inventory exhaustion, management reiterated they stick to full-year guidance, noting price rises from supply side are a pass-through with a possible time delay as increases are passed gradually to the market; internally targeting to overachieve.

subsections.label: Price increase trajectory
points: Price hikes taken vary product to product, in the 10-20% range so far, done monthly, bi-monthly, or quarterly depending on the product.
Watching cost escalations carefully into Q3 and Q4, passing to customers in a gradual manner to avoid inflationary shock affecting consumption.
By end of H1, average price increase taken is expected to be approximately 15-20%; full-year guidance is for a price increase of around 25%, monitored quarter-on-quarter.

subsections.label: Backward integration margin impact
points: Backward integration initiatives (housing enclosures, cable connectors, lenses, and future bare PCBs) expected to add 'a couple of basis points' to margins as they scale, though management declined to quantify precisely at this stage; commentary on margin improvement trajectory (e.g., FY2028) deemed premature.

subsections.label: Export timeline
points: Significant export numbers expected in 18-24 months, contingent on domestic capacity expansion and field-testing of new portfolio (e.g., CP PLUS Pro series).

subsections.label: Revenue guidance
points: FY2027 revenue guidance set at INR60-65 billion.

key_takeaways: Q1 FY2027 revenue stood at INR1,402 crores, which is up 89.5% year-on-year, driven by strong traction by CP PLUS brand in the overall AIL revenue.

Gross margin stood at 30.8%, up 810 basis points year-on-year, with CP PLUS contribution rising to 87% of our revenue. Margins moderated slightly from Q4 due to the exhaustion of lower-cost inventory.
EBITDA stood at INR208 crores, up 20% year-on-year, with margins improving by 604 basis points to 14.8%, supported by a favorable product and brand mix, as well as better operational efficiencies.
Adjusted PAT stood at INR142.2 crores, up 332.5% year-on-year, attributed to lowering of finance costs by 59% year-on-year and better cost efficiencies.

Our working capital metrics also showed meaningful progress, with reduction in inventory and debtor days resulting in the improvement of cash conversion cycle to 64 days. At the same time, our balance sheet remains robust, with debt to equity reducing sharply to just 0.07 level.

Our market share stood at 43.3% in the Indian video surveillance industry in FY2026, as per the Frost & Sullivan report. We are pleased to see strong gains in our market share, with our position effectively doubling over the period shown.
Manufacturing remains a key strategic pillar. Our housing and enclosure expansion is progressing as planned and is expected to become operational by Q3 of this financial year.
We have given our guidance for the year, which is 14% to 15% EBITDA. We in quarter one stand by that only, I think we are at 14.8%.
pressing_questions: So would it be fair to assume it could add additional at least INR5,000 crores to INR10,000 crores of opportunity? - I hope so. Let's see. With early stage, I can't comment today but these are good adjacencies is all I can say.
What is the ideal margin improvement that one should expect in possibly FY2028 from backward integration projects? - It will be early to make a comment on how much it would be.

So we are covered till next June maybe, I can assume that? - We are not talking about March or June. We are talking about a sourcing strategy where we give projections to those vendors and we cover... So that forecast is for anything for between three to four quarters.

quarters.summary: Aditya Infotech closed FY26 with market leadership (~45.4% market share in India's organized surveillance industry as of Q3 FY26) and upped FY27 guidance to revenue of INR6,000-6,500 crores (~50% growth), EBITDA margin of 14%-15%, and PAT margin of 8.5%-9.5%, even as management flagged continued global semiconductor/memory supply pressure, elevated forex costs, and inevitable input-cost-driven price hikes through 2027.

subsections.label: Q4 Margin Drivers
points: EBITDA margin improvement primarily due to favourable product mix, product and brand mix, higher localization, and better operational efficiencies.
Adjusted PAT growth attributed to lowering of finance cost by 38% and better cost efficiencies.

Gross margin surge in Q4 (900bps+ to 31.8%) driven by a combination of factors: price rise taken in Q4, low-cost inventory that was lying with the company, and higher-end project SKUs getting STQC certified in H2 and starting to come in from Q3/Q4.

subsections.label: Full Year Drivers
points: Full year revenue growth driven by market share gains across geographies.
Full year PAT growth aided by disciplined cost management and reduction in finance cost following debt repayment from IPO proceeds.

subsections.label: Margin Sustainability
points: Company has almost exhausted low-cost inventory; raw material prices are rising, with tapered/gradual price rise happening across months starting Q1 to avoid market shock.
Guidance for the whole year (14-15% EBITDA margin) is higher than last year's guidance but slightly lower than Q4 levels, factoring in this dynamic.

Management believes 14%-15% EBITDA margin should be the 'new normal' for the business going into FY27, FY28, driven by localization, cost optimization, shift towards medium-to-higher-end products, enterprise business, and premiumization; Q4 was considered a one-off high.

subsections.label: Profitability Outlook / Cost Pass-through
points: Given uncertain geopolitical environment and persistent inflationary pressures, elevated raw material costs have emerged as the benefit of earlier low-cost inventory is exhausted; replacement inventory now procured at higher cost.
While costs are being passed to customers, there is an inherent time lag in transmission of price revisions, so profitability growth may not mirror pace of revenue growth.

Company announced a price hike of 6%-8% in January 2026, with further price rises expected to continue through FY27, done on a monthly/gradual scale rather than abrupt hikes to avoid shocking the market.

subsections.label: Capital Allocation
points: Company follows a prudent, value-oriented capital allocation approach; key priority is to deploy funds through capex and selective inorganic growth opportunities aligned with long-term strategic objectives and potential to be EPS accretive.
Focus on investments that bolster R&D capabilities to sustain long-term growth, differentiation, and competitive advantage.

Capex of INR200-300 crores planned for FY27 (management indicated original plan was ~INR200 crores but may need more given upped guidance), to be largely funded via internal accruals or some debt for plant and machinery.
Company has minimal debt-equity ratio; would look at temporary debt if further capex/growth funding required.

subsections.label: Working Capital / Cash Conversion
points: Cash conversion cycle has slightly increased due to advance procurement of chips/memory (blocking funds, possible advance payments) and creditors coming down as company secures supplies.
Inventory levels and debtors have improved gradually due to operational efficiency focus.
Working capital needs factored into FY27 planning; funding expected primarily via internal accruals and some debt.

subsections.label: Government Business
points: Government-backed project demand is unpredictable ('suddenly things happen, suddenly things go slow'); overall market is 15-20% government, and company's business mix plans similarly, with no expectation of major upside from this segment this year.
Revenue from government or large government projects/tenders comes via System Integrators or PSUs.

subsections.label: Consumer vs B2B Mix
points: Consumer purchases are still less than 10% of overall business; category remains essentially B2B-led with pent-up demand from projects.

subsections.label: Volume vs Value Growth Split
points: FY26 total growth (33%) comprised roughly 18-20% volume growth and the rest ASP growth, driven by mix shift (CP PLUS internal mix change and IP-to-HD mix change); price rise was essentially only in Q4, while other three quarters saw post-STQC materials at higher prices.

subsections.label: Qualcomm Partnership
points: Strategic partnership with Qualcomm Technologies to develop AI-enabled insight-driven video security solutions for industrial, enterprise, and public safety applications.
Represents transition from traditional hardware-led surveillance towards AI-powered analytics and intelligent edge computing ecosystems.
Platform currently in advanced trial and testing phases; commercial rollout expected in a phased manner going forward; hopeful of going to market this year via SaaS/AI-as-a-security-service model.

subsections.label: L&T Semiconductor Technologies Partnership
points: Partnership focused on supply of 9 million next-generation CCTV IP cameras over the next three years, powered by LTSCT's indigenously designed vision system-on-chip technology.
Represents a major step towards building India's indigenous semiconductor and intelligent surveillance ecosystem.

subsections.label: SoC Partnerships
points: Built strong partnerships with six leading non-Chinese SoC companies: Ambarella, Qualcomm, Augentix, Innofusion, Novatek, and Realtek.
Diversified strategy has strengthened supply chain, reduced dependency risks, and improved ability to deliver products consistently despite global semiconductor challenges.
Strong alignment with top three sensor players — SmartSens, Sony, and SOI — ensuring technology and supply continuity.

subsections.label: R&D Capabilities
points: DSIR-certified in-house labs and rapidly expanding innovation ecosystem.
Strong progress in AI-powered video analytics, unified platforms, mobile applications, and multi-brand product development under the CP PLUS portfolio.
Expanding presence in Noida and Ahmedabad, plus upcoming Bangalore centre; successfully kick-started Taiwan office and R&D operations.
Rapidly scaling R&D teams and bringing in experienced global talent with over 20 years of expertise.
Vision for FY28: establish a fully functional global R&D presence, including Taiwan operations.

subsections.label: AI/Camera Evolution Vision
points: Management describes industry evolution from viewing to recording to intelligence/video analytics; increasing AI and video analytics integration expected going forward.
Cameras described as becoming 'eyes, ears, and tongue' of the AI ecosystem (with audio in/out capability), with AI (edge boxes, recorders) as the 'brain' triggering actions.
Company already announced cloud offering for home market for redundancy backup of surveillance data, optimizing platform to be cost-effective/affordable for mass-market before scale-up.
Working on AI-as-a-security-service (SaaS) model leveraging edge AI on-premise plus cloud AI; too early to quantify margin accretion but expected to pay off over a 5-year horizon.

subsections.label: Retail & Brand Presence
points: Brand Galaxy stores: 141 exclusive CP PLUS stores across Pan-India, dedicated to selling and promoting cameras and security equipment portfolio, operating under a co-funded business model to strengthen market reach and customer engagement.

subsections.label: Export Opportunity
points: Previously, hands were full/tight with domestic demand; export opportunity was expected to be considered after two-three years.

Management indicated hope to start some export action this year, though at present energies remain focused on feeding domestic demand given capacity, R&D, localization, inorganic options, and supply chain disruptions; timing and materialization uncertain.

subsections.label: Global Semiconductor/Memory Disruption
points: Global semiconductor and memory industry continues to face significant disruption due to ongoing supply-demand imbalances, geopolitical uncertainties, and manufacturing constraints.
Critical components such as SoC, DDR, flash, and sensors remain under severe supply pressure, resulting in extended lead times and rising procurement challenges.
US dollar remains at historically high levels, increasing landed cost of imported electronic components and raw materials.
Geopolitical tensions/conflict in the Middle East have led to a sharp rise in global insurance premiums and freight costs, adding further pressure to supply chain and operating environment.

subsections.label: Mitigation Strategy
points: Proactively adopted a multi-SoC product strategy along with a diversified multi-supply chain procurement strategy to strengthen flexibility, reduce dependency risk, and ensure business continuity.
Focusing on forward procurement and long-term planning to secure component availability well in advance and minimize future disruptions.
Company is securing semiconductors and memory much ahead of competition at better cost optimization, sourcing from different chipset makers as far as possible.
Sourcing from multiple channels: direct from fab makers, chipset guys, their distributors, and open market.

Half of the 6-7 large global DDR manufacturers (outside China) have stopped making DDR3 due to AI demand shifting capacities to DDR5 and above, creating memory gaps; in demand-supply imbalance situations, 'the big get bigger' and smaller players are more affected — seen as a competitive advantage for the company given its purchasing power, volume, and relationships.

subsections.label: Contracts and Agreements
points: Supply agreements with chipset suppliers are typically in place, but across the industry many agreements are becoming unstable given supply-demand volatility, cost rising on fortnightly/weekly basis, and force majeure-type situations even when advances are paid.
Company mitigating this via multi-supply chain, multi-sourcing, and multi-product R&D strategy.

subsections.label: Working Capital Impact
points: Cash conversion cycle slightly increased due to procurement of chips and memory requiring blocking of funds and possible advance payments, alongside creditors coming down as supplies are secured.
This dynamic expected to continue in the shorter term as first priority is ensuring supply consistency and security.

subsections.label: Market Share Trajectory
points: At outset, company held approximately 30% market share in Indian video surveillance market, with almost 25% in own brand CP PLUS.
At IPO time, projected own brand market share could expand to nearly 36% post-STQC implementation, assuming meaningful consolidation of Chinese players' share among Indian manufacturers.

Industry transition unfolded more favourably than anticipated; preparedness, robust localization strategy, manufacturing scale, and largest STQC-certified product portfolio enabled significantly exceeding expectations.
As of Q3 FY26, market share reached approximately 45.4%, establishing clear market leadership in India's organized surveillance industry.

subsections.label: Competitive Landscape
points: About 30 brands across current certified list; a dozen global brands certified but overall share ~10% of market; about one and a half dozen domestic brands.
No competitor plays across all vertical market segments (home, consumer, small-medium businesses, enterprise, government); most competitors are roughly one-tenth of company's size or lower.
Company not targeting a specific market share number; plans to outgrow industry growth rate naturally leading to market share gains, with focus on building capacities and ensuring supply.

Certification process was slow around October-November but has picked up for some peers; management preparing for eventual competition though believes it has a strong head start on localization, capacity, R&D, product range, and supply chain; supply chain itself remains a big deterrent for competitors this year and expected to continue into next year.

subsections.label: Industry Growth & Demand Drivers
points: Industry expected to grow at 15%-16% CAGR in unit terms; company has historically grown at ~21-22% CAGR pre-2025, consistently beating industry growth rate.

Last year's growth was muted due to transition from pre-STQC to post-STQC era; market research agencies had factored this year and next few years to be higher than 20% in quantity growth, but supply-side constraints continue.
Growth rates have not fully factored in upgrade markets from HD to IP and continued penetration runway.
Company factored 25%-30% quantity growth for FY27, expecting to continue beating industry growth rate.

High pent-up demand anticipated this year post last year's muted transition-driven consumption, but ASP cost rises are expected to have mixed effects — entry-level network cameras/recorders face higher cost rises than medium-to-high-end enterprise/project products, causing some potential shift towards analog cameras where cost rise is lower; overall unit growth guidance moderated to 15% from an earlier expectation of >20%.

Consumer/B2C spend impact from ASP hikes (as seen in mobiles/laptops) considered less relevant since company's B2C purchases are less than 10% of business; category remains B2B-led with pent-up project demand.

subsections.label: ASP and Value Growth
points: ASP growth for FY27 expected to be roughly 25%, not driven 100% by price rises — also driven by brand mix (as more projects come in) and SKU mix (increasing IP percentage) within CP PLUS portfolio.
Migration from IP-level cameras to premium-end cameras contributes to ASP growth alongside price rises since premium-end ASP hikes are proportionately lower.

subsections.label: Differentiators
points: Brand recall and presence (advertising campaigns at airports, IPL, film stars) considered the primary differentiator, along with brand's presence among consultants, large customers, and SIs via B2B shows.
Large-scale integrated manufacturing setup considered unmatched among competitors.
Broad product range across all market segments (SMB, large enterprises, government, consumer) — no competitor is relevant across all these segments.
Nearly two decades in business with long-tenured, ground-connected, experienced teams; deep R&D investment (India and offshore) considered unmatched.
Distribution reach and partner relationships also cited as differentiators.

subsections.label: Brand Building Initiatives
points: Strengthened presence across India through celebrity partnerships, sports sponsorships, and high-visibility campaigns.
New brand campaigns featuring South superstars Vijay Sethupathi and Prithviraj Sukumaran deepening audience across South India.

Title sponsorship of Punjab Kings in IPL, major airport campaigns, largest ever presence at IFSEC India 2025, and title sponsorship of PACC 2025 further strengthened market presence and brand leadership.

subsections.label: Capital Allocation for Inorganic Growth
points: Company intends to deploy funds through capex and selective inorganic growth opportunities aligned with long-term strategic objectives and potential to be EPS accretive.
Exploring opportunities that strengthen technological expertise, broaden product offerings, and enhance positioning in fast-growing markets.

subsections.label: Multi-brand Strategy
points: Multi-brand strategy (including Nexivue and Eyra) further augmenting market share growth and positioning at different price points to address possible competitive threats at any level.

subsections.label: Supply Chain & Component Risk
points: Global semiconductor/memory supply-demand imbalances, geopolitical uncertainties, and manufacturing constraints continue; SoC, DDR, flash, sensors remain under severe supply pressure with extended lead times.
US dollar at historically high levels increasing landed cost of imported electronic components and raw materials.
Middle East geopolitical tensions/conflict have led to sharp rise in global insurance premiums and freight costs.
Industry trends indicate costs likely to continue rising until 2027; price escalation deemed inevitable.

Agreements with chipset suppliers across the industry going unstable due to volatile supply-demand and cost rising on fortnightly/weekly basis; contracts can get invalidated due to force majeure-type situations even with advance payments.

subsections.label: Margin/Cost Risk
points: Low-cost inventory benefit has been exhausted; replacement inventory being procured at higher cost, with inherent time lag between cost increases and price pass-through to customers, meaning profitability growth may not mirror revenue growth pace.

subsections.label: Working Capital Risk
points: Cash conversion cycle has slightly increased due to advance procurement needs for chips/memory and reduced creditor days as supplies are secured.

subsections.label: Competitive Risk
points: Certification process picking up pace for some peers after being slow around October-November; management preparing for eventual competition though believes it retains a head start on localization, capacity, R&D, product range, and supply chain.

subsections.label: FY27 Guidance Details
points: Upping initial guidance for FY27: revenue to INR6,000-6,500 crores (almost 50% growth over last year); EBITDA margin to 14%-15%; PAT margin around 8.5%-9.5%.
Guidance reflects looking at current market and stability of CCTV industry post-STQC mandate.
CCTV market expected to show robust growth in units in the range of 15%-16%; company intends to surpass industry growth rate and aim to grow 25%-30% in the coming year.
With continued price rise in market ASP and shift in product mix, average per unit camera recovery expected to rise by 20%-25%.

subsections.label: Margin Guidance Rationale
points: Full year guidance for FY27 EBITDA margin (14-15%) is higher than last year's guidance but slightly lower than the elevated Q4 FY26 level, factoring in exhaustion of low-cost inventory and rising raw material costs.
Management believes 14%-15% EBITDA margin should be the 'new normal' for the business in FY27 and FY28, driven by localization, cost optimization, premiumization and enterprise business shift.

subsections.label: FY28 Vision
points: Expand overall production capacity to 2x of existing capacity.
Achieve complete backward integration across key components.
Establish a fully functional global R&D presence, including Taiwan operations, to drive innovation and long-term growth.

subsections.label: Capex Outlook
points: Original capex plan was around INR200 crores plus/minus, but given upped guidance, company feels it might require a little more, likely falling in INR200-300 crores range; plans being worked upon relative to new expansions.
To be largely funded from internal accruals or some debt for plant and machinery.

subsections.label: Export Timing Outlook
points: Hope to start some export action this year, though timing and materialization remain uncertain given current focus on domestic capacity, R&D, localization, and supply chain.

themes.label: Market Share Gains
themes.note: Market share rose from ~25-30% at IPO to ~45.4% as of Q3 FY26, well ahead of the ~36% post-STQC projection made at IPO.

themes.label: Guidance Raise
themes.note: FY27 guidance upped to INR6,000-6,500 crores revenue (~50% growth), EBITDA margin 14-15%, PAT 8.5-9.5%.

themes.label: Input cost inflation / Semiconductor-memory supply pressure
themes.note: Global SoC/DDR/flash/sensor supply pressure, high USD, and Middle East-driven freight/insurance cost rises are pushing input costs up, with escalation seen as inevitable through 2027.

themes.label: Backward Integration / Capacity Expansion
themes.note: JV with Orient Cables for cables, in-house housing plant, lens assembly line, Kadapa and Noida facility expansions, and a FY28 vision to double capacity and achieve complete backward integration.

themes.label: Margin Expansion & Sustainability
themes.note: Q4 EBITDA margin hit 18% (aided partly by low-cost inventory now exhausted); management believes 14-15% EBITDA margin is the sustainable 'new normal' for FY27/FY28.

themes.label: AI-led Product & Service Transition
themes.note: Qualcomm partnership and cloud/SaaS initiatives mark a shift from hardware-led surveillance to AI-powered analytics and services, though monetization timeline and margin impact remain early-stage.

themes.label: Pricing Power / Gradual Price Hikes
themes.note: 6-8% price hike taken in January 2026 with further monthly gradual hikes planned through FY27 to pass on rising input costs without shocking the market; time lag may mean profitability doesn't fully mirror revenue growth.

key_takeaways: We held approximately 30% market share in the Indian video surveillance market, with almost 25% in our own brand CP PLUS at the outset of this journey; at IPO we projected own brand share could expand to nearly 36% post-STQC implementation, but as of Q3 FY 2026, our market share reached approximately 45.4%, establishing us as the clear market leader.

Revenue grew 45.5% year-on-year to INR1,422 crores in Q4 FY26; EBITDA increased 162% year-on-year to INR258.3 crores with margins improving by 800 basis points to 18%; Adjusted PAT stood at INR169.1 crores, up 207.7% year-on-year.

Full year revenue grew 35.6% year-on-year to INR4,220.8 crores; EBITDA increased 124.1% to INR579 crores with margins expanding by 540 basis points to 13.7%; Adjusted PAT rose to INR368 crores, reflecting 166.1% year-on-year growth.

We are upping our initial guidance for FY 2027 on the revenue side to INR6,000 crores to INR6,500 crores, which is almost 50% growth over the last year; EBITDA margin to 14% to 15%; and PAT around 8.5% to 9.5%.

Manufacturing capacity has now reached 2.5 million units; targeting 90% to 100% capacity utilization; vision for FY28 is to expand overall production capacity to 2x of existing capacity and achieve complete backward integration across key components.

Strategic partnerships with Qualcomm Technologies (AI-enabled video security), L&T Semiconductor Technologies (supply of 9 million next-gen CCTV IP cameras over 3 years), and a JV with Orient Cables for LAN and CCTV cable manufacturing, along with six non-Chinese SoC partners, to strengthen supply chain and technology capabilities.
Announced a price hike of 6% to 8% in January 2026, and further price rise is expected to keep continuing in this financial year, done on a monthly gradual basis to avoid market shock.

The CCTV market is expected to show robust growth in units in the range of 15% to 16%; we intend to surpass the industry growth rate and aim to grow in the range of 25% to 30% in the coming year; average per unit camera recovery is expected to rise by 20% to 25%.
pressing_questions: On the utilization of cash / breakup of B2C or government business revenue - the moderator noted 'I think maybe later on the IR team can pass you some information on that, they will share you' when asked for revenue breakup by customer type (B2C/government).
Margin accretion from AI-as-a-service/SaaS model - management stated 'Too early, it's a new market creation, so it's too early to' quantify margin accretive numbers.

INDIAGLYCO.about: Established in 1988, India Glycols Ltd. is engaged in the manufacturing of green technology-based bulk, specialty & performance chemicals, and natural gums, spirits, industrial gases, sugar, and nutraceuticals. [1][2]

quarters.summary: IGL delivered a strong Q1 FY27 with double-digit growth in gross revenue, EBITDA and PAT, supported by a balanced portfolio and improved profitability. Business restructuring (NCLT-approved demerger into three entities) is progressing on plan. Management shared multi-year aspirations (not projections) for Spirits, Chemicals and Ennature Bio Pharma businesses, while flagging geopolitical/war-related headwinds and tailwinds affecting raw material costs and freight.

subsections.label: Margin recovery story
points: Margin recovery based on a strategic plan discussed over the last few years: managing costs better, managing feedstocks better, improving the quality of business and entering new areas driving both growth and profitability.
Consistent and stable improvement in EBITDA margin from FY22 through FY26 reflects sustained improvement in quality of business.

subsections.label: Finance cost decline
points: Finance costs declined due to debt reduction, which has also supported profitable growth.
Debt levels reduced during the quarter and debt-to-equity ratio has improved.

subsections.label: Q4 vs Q1 EBITDA comparison (analyst query)
points: Q4 FY26 EBITDA of INR203 crores included INR39 crores of dividend income from Clariant, which does not recur every quarter (dividend income comes only in the last quarter).
Q1 FY27 EBITDA of INR170 crores does not include such dividend income, explaining the sequential decline in growth percentage terms.
Management asked the analyst to send a follow-up email for a more detailed reply on quarter-by-quarter EBITDA growth percentages.

subsections.label: IGL Spirits business drivers
points: Spirits business (bifurcated from Bio-Fuel) improved EBITDA margin by 207 bps.
IMFL business drove the growth story with 26% net revenue growth and 55% volume growth (1.4 million cases).
Non-IMFL business revenues remained largely stagnant at INR279 crores despite 6% volume growth to 7.5 million cases.
Company retained dominant share in UP and Uttarakhand, benefiting from premium product offerings.

Despite a declining non-IMFL market where most big players declined, IGL maintained a dominant position in UP and Uttarakhand, led by strong brand building (e.g., Bunty Bubli, recognized by Limca Book of Records and Asia Book of Records) despite increased competition.

subsections.label: Bio-Fuel business
points: Bio-Fuel net revenue grew 7% to INR323 crores with EBITDA margin of 10.8%, an improvement of 250 bps.

subsections.label: Chemicals business (India Glycols) performance drivers
points: Chemicals business had a good quarter both in volume and value.
Green solvents (glycols and glycol ethers) volumes up 6%, value up 13%, gross margins close to 50%.
Glycols business value up 83% with strong growth in gross margins.

Performance chemicals grew 40%, lower than targeted, due to export suffering to Middle East and other countries, prohibitively expensive raw materials, and supply chain disruption resulting in flattish contribution.
Some growth seen in EO sales to the joint venture.

subsections.label: Ennature Bio Pharma performance drivers
points: Best-ever quarterly performance driven by new customer acquisitions, several nutraceutical launches, expansion of the nicotine business, and improved efficiency.

Thiocolchicoside sales grew 26% QoQ supported by strong order pipeline and improved price realization; raw material availability and pricing remain volatile and a challenge expected to continue into Q2.
Nicotine sales grew 2x QoQ driven by customer conversions in Europe.
Nicotine crude processing operations started at Kashipur plant, adding significant capacity.

Continued focus on strengthening branded nutraceuticals portfolio through strategic initiatives, new certificates/approvals for global market penetration, and disciplined capital allocation for long-term value creation.

subsections.label: JV (with Clariant) performance
points: JV growth driven by reduced disadvantage on ethylene oxide pricing due to the current geopolitical/crude scenario.
JV net revenue up 21% versus Q4; EBITDA also up significantly in high double digits versus Q4.
JV performing well both from Kashipur operations and from Clariant products sold in India, with greater thrust on exporting India-made products to other Clariant customers worldwide.

Despite tough years for IGL over the last 3-4 years (ethanol price increases, reduced EO cost competitiveness), JV performance has by and large been on track due to improved product mix, closer customer engagement, importing where required, trading in some areas, and some good luck.
Q1 FY27 JV PAT of INR21 crores compares to INR19 crores in the same quarter last year — management characterizes this as not out of the blue, though a good quarter with some tailwinds.

subsections.label: Analyst query on volume vs revenue growth mismatch (Spirits)
points: Case volume grew faster than revenue due to two factors: brand mix and state mix.
Higher growth from Uttarakhand augurs well; higher growth from Delhi does not augur as well.
Within IMFL, the mass premium segment grew faster because of new offerings in those segments.

Management expects revenue growth to exceed volume growth going forward due to premiumization (new offerings in Deluxe Whiskey, Semi-Premium Vodka, renewed focus on White Spirits, all high-margin segments).

subsections.label: Amrut brand partnership details
points: Strategic partnership with Amrut involves acquiring brands and handling distribution and marketing in select North Indian states (not building own new brands in premium/semi-premium segment).
Five Amrut products involved: MaQintosh Whisky, MaQintosh White, Prestige Green, Fusion Single Malt and Amalgam.

Partnership currently limited to select North Indian markets, with intent to extend to other markets (e.g., East) as IGL Spirits ventures there; Amrut is predominantly concentrated in West and South with insignificant direct presence in North and East.
Royalty payable to Amrut was not disclosed.

subsections.label: IMFL revenue mix outlook
points: Percentage of Potable Spirits revenue from IMFL for FY27 expected to be in excess of 30%.
Gross margins for Deluxe/Semi-Premium whiskey within Prestige & Above (P&A) segment are almost the same, contrary to how most investors perceive it.

subsections.label: Chemicals innovation and new product firsts
points: Strategy driven by strength in process chemistry, product development, applications, and partnerships, moving from product to good product to differentiated product to understanding applications to solving problems to collaborative/strategic projects.
Became the first-ever company to manufacture bio-based amines, currently supplying small quantities with expectation of growth opportunity over time.
Became the first company in the world to supply carbon-smart ethoxylates and glycols; currently small volumes but viewed as technology for the future.
Building green solvents business supply into end applications like crop protection, food, pharma, personal care, etc.
Working on new technologies utilizing carbon and producing low-carbon-footprint products, described as potentially transformational; not yet mature enough to disclose details or numbers.

subsections.label: Ennature Bio Pharma product/technology actions
points: Taking actions such as new certificates/approvals for global market penetration to drive customer and product expansion.

subsections.label: Nicotine capacity expansion
points: Nicotine crude processing operations started at the Kashipur plant, adding significant capacity.

subsections.label: Spirits manufacturing strength
points: Captive high-quality ENA production and ample available capacity provide cost advantage in operating states and protect margin.
Company is one of the largest manufacturers of ENA, giving consistent quality and sustainable cost leadership.

subsections.label: Spirits geographic footprint and expansion plans
points: Bulk of Spirits business currently concentrated in three states: UP, Uttarakhand, and Delhi; management describes this as having 'just touched the tip of the iceberg' given the size of these states.
Growth plan includes deepening penetration in existing states via both existing portfolio and new offerings.

Inorganic growth planned via introduction of new brands and entry into new states, including targeting an all-India footprint via defense channel with introduction of three to four new brands (three brands already approved, one more on the anvil).
Amrut partnership initially limited to select North Indian markets, with plans to extend to other regions such as the East as IGL Spirits enters those markets.

subsections.label: Chemicals export impact from geopolitical conflict
points: Exports of specialty/oil & gas chemicals to the Middle East collapsed due to the conflict, with shipments to the US also becoming very difficult.
Greater thrust on exporting JV/Clariant-related products made in India to other Clariant customers worldwide.

subsections.label: Business restructuring / demerger
points: NCLT sanctioned the scheme of arrangement on 17th July 2026; effective date yet to be communicated; actions progressing as per plan.
Upon effectiveness, the Spirits, Bio-Fuel, and Bio Pharma undertakings transfer to dedicated resulting companies, segregating the current India Glycols Limited into three entities.
Entity 1: India Glycols Limited (retains name) — bio-based chemicals, specialty glycols, new performance chemicals, gases, and any new chemical space areas.

Entity 2: IGL Spirits Limited — potable spirits business (IMFL and Indian-made Indian liquor) plus the Bio-Fuel (ethanol) business, combined due to synergy since a significant amount of ethanol produced is required by the potable spirits business.
Entity 3: Ennature Bio Pharma — retains nutraceuticals and APIs, plus the biopolymers business moved in from the chemicals business.
Arrangements are being made to manage costs and retain expertise across entities without hiring too many new people, managing overlaps efficiently.

Rationale for demerger: Potable Spirits has gathered scale in volume and profitability and is a consumer business with different dynamics from the B2B chemicals business; separating the businesses is expected to bring more focus; investors and partners want clarity on what they are investing in (consumer vs B2B/technology appetite differs).

subsections.label: New Business/NSU (New Speciality Unit / performance chemicals) capex plans
points: No huge capex expected this year for the NSU/performance chemicals area; incremental capex expected around INR5-10 crores, possibly INR15-20 crores based on current plans.

Not a very capex-intensive model currently; modular expansion expected as business grows rather than a large new plant (no INR400-500 crore plant expected, unless investing in new technologies, not anticipated for next 2 years).
Cumulative investment in new plant addition for this business to date is approximately INR50-60 crores (core plant expansion largely used existing assets).

subsections.label: Bacardi partnership
points: Long-standing ~15-year relationship with Bacardi; IGL is the only company in the country with an exclusive facility for Bacardi in terms of spirit maturation, reinforcing trusted-partner positioning and compliance with world-class manufacturing practices.

subsections.label: Chemicals partnerships/collaborations
points: Strategic growth hinged on innovation with good partners; strong collaborative (not merely supply) partnerships with BASF, L'Oreal, Unilever, Mibelle, and others named with permission.

subsections.label: Geopolitical conflict (war) impact - mixed
points: War has impacted the company in multiple ways - a combination of headwinds and tailwinds.
Crude spiked to a four-year high, raising crude prices and affecting supply and pricing of chemicals like glycols and other petrochemical derivatives imported from the Middle East.
Rupee hit a record low.
Freight costs became even more determining than product prices themselves; westbound cargo freights were very volatile, rising anywhere between 5 to 20 times, impacting some businesses.

Positive impact on ethylene oxide (EO) business: bio-based EO, previously more expensive than Reliance's EO for the last three-four years, became similar or slightly lower priced during the period discussed, driving greater off-take for specialty chemicals and greater penetration for glycols sold in India.

Negative impact: raw materials such as propylene oxide were either completely unavailable or prohibitively expensive, adversely impacting businesses supplying specialty chemicals within India and oil & gas materials to the Middle East (which essentially collapsed); shipments to the US also became very difficult.

subsections.label: Raw material volatility - Ennature Bio Pharma
points: Raw material availability and pricing for Thiocolchicoside continue to be volatile and expected to remain a challenge in Q2 as well.

subsections.label: Performance chemicals growth shortfall
points: Performance chemicals business grew 40%, lower than targeted, due to export disruption to Middle East/other countries, expensive raw materials, and supply chain disruption causing flattish contribution.

subsections.label: IGL Spirits outlook pivots
points: Six or seven main pivots driving encouraging outlook: continued IMFL growth momentum, new launches in deluxe whiskey and semi-premium vodka segments, increased focus on the fast-growing white spirits business, geographical and channel expansion beyond core states (UP, Uttarakhand, Delhi), inorganic gains from new brand introductions and new state entries (including defense channel for all-India footprint), premiumization, and the Amrut partnership for premium/single malt segment.
Company targeting to become debt-free from FY28 onwards.
Targeting EBITDA in excess of INR1,000 crores in the next four to five years, potentially placing IGL among the top five alco-bev companies in the country.
Guidance stated as EBITDA in excess of INR500 crores for FY27, with INR120 crores already delivered in Q1.
Volume guidance: doubling volume versus last year, driven by deeper penetration in core states with larger brand offering, particularly Deluxe Whiskey, Rum, and Semi-Premium Vodka.
Next year outlook: continued growth in healthy double digits, against an industry backdrop of only 4-5% CAGR over the last two years.

subsections.label: Chemicals business outlook
points: Leveraging position as largest supplier (combined with JV) of bio-based specialty chemicals in the world and pioneer in bio-based EO, glycols, glycol ethers manufacture; considers itself one of only two-scale suppliers of these products globally.

Growth drivers: strength in process chemistry, product development, applications and partnerships; new value-added chemicals driven by innovation and moving up the value chain from product to collaborative/strategic projects.

Aspiration (explicitly not a projection) to deliver EBITDA of about INR400 crores and revenue of approximately INR2,500 crores in the next four to five years, built on a product-by-product, customer-by-customer plan.
Renewable materials positioned as a strategic advantage, not just a credential; structural shift toward specialty-led portfolio expected to show increasingly in numbers.
Performance chemicals/value-added chemicals expected to become an important, growing part of the chemicals business on the back of a strong pipeline.

subsections.label: Ennature Bio Pharma outlook
points: Sustained growth momentum expected; nicotine expanded in both sales and capacity; continued focus on strengthening branded nutraceuticals portfolio.

Aspiration (explicitly stated as aspiration, not a plan or projection, and shared ahead of the trifurcation of businesses) of INR130-150 crores EBITDA over the next four to five years, based on an internal exercise but subject to change given industry dynamism.

subsections.label: NSU (New Speciality Unit) outlook
