key_takeaways: IGL delivered a very strong start for FY'27 with a double-digit growth in gross revenue, EBITDA and PAT, which was supported by a balanced portfolio and improved profitability.
Net revenue of INR1,130 crores, up 9% and a record EBITDA of INR170 crores. Gross revenue is up 19%, net revenue up 9%, EBITDA up 13% and PAT up 32%.
On the business restructuring front, we've got the NCLT approval. Effective date is to be communicated, and we are progressing the actions as per the plan.

The Spirits business recorded a revenue of INR361 crores, up 5.3%, EBITDA growth of 14.2%, and the company retained a dominant share in UP and Uttarakhand while benefiting from premium product offerings in these areas.
In chemicals, our revenues increased by 20.6% to INR362 crores, driven by growth in multiple areas which include bio-glycols, green solvents, as well as performance chemicals.
Ennature Bio Pharma reported its best-ever quarter with revenue rising 65% year-on-year and EBITDA increasing 188%.
The finance costs for the company declined to INR25 crores in Q1 FY27 from INR45 crores in Q1 FY26, and this is on account of debt reduction which has been supporting the profitable growth as well.
We expect to deliver an EBITDA in excess of INR500 crores [for Spirits in FY27] ... we are targeting an EBITDA in excess of INR1,000 crores in the next four to five years.

quarters.summary: Management reported a strong FY26 (gross revenue up 8.7% to INR9,827cr, net revenue up 11.8% to INR4,211cr, EBITDA up 24.5% to INR654cr at 15.5% margin, PAT up 26.8% to INR293cr) led by Potable Spirits and Bio-Fuels, with Chemicals margin improving despite a top-line dip. Outlook is cautiously optimistic across segments: Bio-Fuels growth to continue with possible blending increase beyond 20% and flexi-vehicle adoption; Potable Spirits to sustain double-digit premiumization-led growth with EBIT margins expected to be maintained/improved from ~22%; Chemicals expected to show improved profitability and top-line growth this year with performance chemicals possibly more than doubling; Ennature Biopharma expected to recover via nutraceutical/customer diversification though FY26 EBITDA improvement may be limited; the Chemical business (via JV stake sale in FY28-29) is targeted to become debt-free; a scheme of demerger is pending NCLT order expected around 21st May/early June 2026.

subsections.label: Debt reduction & capital allocation
points: Company prepaid ~INR804 crores of debt in Q4FY26, funded by INR467 crores through equity issue done in November 2025 and the rest through cash flow.
The INR804 crores prepayment includes long-term debt, working capital, and short-term loans, resulting in INR20 crores interest cost saving already reflected in results.

Net debt reduction is not fully visible in headline numbers because cash credit limits were also reduced; repayments against long-term loans are visible but amounts paid out of cash credit limits are not.
For FY27, normal debt liability of INR268 crores is due (INR168 crores in liquor, INR100 crores in Chemicals); company will also target further prepayments from cash flow beyond scheduled repayment.
CFO expects quarterly interest cost to remain in the ~INR25 crore range and continue reducing in the years to come.
Capex of ~INR830 crores in FY26, with ~INR400 crores attributable to capitalization of two grain distilleries (Gorakhpur and Kashipur); remaining capex was smaller and has been completed.

subsections.label: Accounting treatment of JV dividend
points: Accounting Standard 28 does not allow showing dividend as income; INR38.38 crores received from JV Clariant has been adjusted against the investment rather than shown as income.

subsections.label: Plant shutdown impact
points: There was a plant shutdown for catalyst change from 17th March to 2nd April, resulting in reduction in production as well as some sales.

Shutdown directly impacted ethylene oxide (EO) supply to the JV since for 15-20 days there was no EO supply to the JV; most JV-related sales are booked as EO sales, which were completely stopped during the shutdown.
As a continuous plant, shutdown also affects businesses like glycol ethers and specialty surfactants, which cannot be stocked up much in advance; MEG business was not impacted.

During the shutdown, catalyst (silver) sale realized INR98 crores against a purchase price of INR51 crores; since catalyst consumption is not provided for monthly, no profit on silver sale has been shown in the books.

subsections.label: JV (Clariant) profitability
points: JV performance is not solely reflected by monthly EO offtake from IGL; it also reflects improvement in product mix and imported/traded materials sourced from Clariant.
JV share of net profit was INR46.42 crores in FY26 versus INR46.40 crores in FY25 (flat annually), though Q4 JV contribution rose to INR12-13 crores versus prior quarters.
Management expects this JV profit-share number to improve drastically going forward if ethoxylates-based volumes pick up and there is no shutdown.

As per the JV agreement, IGL plans to sell out 24% more equity in the JV in FY28-29, which is expected to generate a handsome amount to be used to pay off term loans, making the Chemical business debt-free by FY28-29.

subsections.label: Chemicals
points: Net revenue declined 10.4% in FY26 due to loss of markets in glycol ethers (cheaper Chinese/propylene/butylene-based variants captured share) and in gases (prior year had unusually high argon prices due to shortage from steel plants/electronics demand).

Degrowth also came from lower EO offtake by the JV, partly due to a large price delta between Reliance and IGL's EO price, which has largely been adjusted now; better competitiveness expected going forward.
Despite top-line dip, EBIT and EBIT margin improved due to readjustments, letting go of low-margin businesses, and focus on higher-value-added chemicals.
Performance chemicals portfolio value and contribution both up 40%+ in FY26; company is hoping to more than double this business in the coming year (not a projection, an expectation).
Company continues to build carbon-smart materials and oilfield chemicals businesses working with global majors like BASF, New Park, Dow, L'Oreal.
IGL became the first manufacturer of a green bio-based amine for certain applications, with L'Oreal as first customer after 3-4 years of co-development; commercial supplies have started.
New products under development include dibasic esters for foundries, wire enamels, personal care, and flavors & fragrances space products.
Glycols saw growth and market maintained in Southeast Asia; niche customers continued to buy despite competitive pressure from Reliance MEG (not viewed as a direct competitor).

subsections.label: Potable Spirits
points: Strong entry into CSD (Canteen Stores Department) business; Bunty Bubbly remains the largest selling brand in India; maintained IMIL market leadership in UP and Uttarakhand.
Expanded coverage in Western UP with new brands; added ~10 new distribution stations and 7 new brands; introduced 100ml SKU per government policy; opened 42 company-operated warehouses in UP.

Introduced Amrut's Prestige Whisky in Deluxe segment in UP; introduced Bunty Vodka Jeera and Cranberry flavors; launched Amazing Vodka Jamun flavor in Q1; launched Dhurandhar Whisky in regular category.
In Uttarakhand: introduced Amrut Prestige Whisky; maintained leadership in regular whisky category with Soulmate Black; introduced Amazing Jamun, Bunty Jamun, and Cranberry variants.

Two key brands (Soulmate Whisky - a Millionaire Case Brand, and Zumba Lemoni) introduced into CSD with supplies started nationwide; third brand Zumba Black cleared preliminary screening committee (PSC), final board approval awaited.
~25% of Potable Spirits pie is IMFL, ~75% is IMIL; company focused on growing IMFL/premium segment without losing IMIL focus.

Growth strategy: (1) geographic expansion into corporation-led markets with secure credit (started in Kerala with a new French-blend brandy, expanding to Andhra Pradesh, Rajasthan); (2) new brand launches (Jamun, Cranberry flavors) with two more brands in pipeline (undisclosed).

Inherent advantage: company uses zero external ENA for its own brands (self-sufficient via captive ENA production), unlike competition; also supplies ENA to Radico, Tilaknagar, Diageo, and Bacardi (15-year partner).
Distribution rights obtained for Amrut luxury single malts in a few northern states, addressing previously unmet demand.

Bacardi bottling business primarily involves filling cost charges for low-proof (e.g., Breezer) and high-proof brands; this revenue flows into miscellaneous income, not sales revenue, and contributes only ~2-3% of total Potable revenue.
EBIT margin was strong at 22.1% for Q4 despite full-year EBIT growth (11.1%) being softer than top-line growth, attributed to an unusual prior-year quarter.

subsections.label: Bio-Fuels
points: India reached 20% ethanol blending, achieved ahead of the original 2030 schedule, driving growth in both profits and sales; excess ethanol capacity now exists relative to consumption.

Government discussions ongoing about increasing blending beyond 20% (to 21-22%) and selectively promoting flexi-fuel vehicles (operating at 85%+ ethanol); a no-operating range exists roughly between 30-85% blending.

ENA (Extra-Neutral Alcohol) business saw good sales growth; dual flexibility (grain and molasses-based production) helps optimize cost and offer different feedstock-based ENA; demand stable from IMFL, pharma, perfumery, and Bacardi packaging.

Margins supported by stable-to-lower grain prices and increasing acceptability of DDGS (protein by-product), improving profitability; government policy viewed as long-term with mechanisms to sustain industry margins even through periods of adjustment.

Feedstock mix has shifted structurally: from FY19-20 (grain 9%, C-heavy molasses 43%, B-heavy molasses 39%, sugarcane juice 9%, maize 0%) to FY25-26 (grain ~73% combining various sources, maize 46%), reflecting policy push toward grain/maize diversification.

Maize increasingly used because it is a hardier crop grown across more of the country including drier climatic zones, with scope to improve productivity potentially via genetically modified maize varieties (speculative, not a projection).

subsections.label: Ennature Biopharma
points: Top-line broadly stable (nominal degrowth) for FY26 despite challenging global macro environment and cost pressures; margins under pressure.
Q4 revenue saw a strong comeback driven by increase in Thiocolchicoside prices, recovery of the nicotine business, and strong nutraceutical numbers.
Strengthened branded nutraceuticals portfolio through global certifications and clinically backed ingredient launches; new customer acquisitions ongoing.

Business has diversified over the last three years away from dependence on a single volatile product toward the fast-growing branded nutraceutical segment, with significant investment in clinical studies for women's health and other indications (some completed, more ongoing through this financial year).
Focus on multi-geography expansion: strong presence already in Asia Pacific; new push into the US market including a recently opened US office.

Nicotine business strategically shifting from commodity/volume-driven customers to more value-added, long-term customers to sustain profitability, partly in response to a competitor's new capacity pressuring realizations; EBITDA improvement from this shift may not be significant in the current financial year but is expected to contribute to profitability over time.

subsections.label: Plant shutdown for catalyst change
points: Catalyst changeover shutdown occurred from 17th March to 2nd April, typically required roughly every 1.5 years.

Being a continuous plant, the shutdown affects ethylene oxide (EO) supply to the Clariant JV and businesses like glycol ethers/specialty surfactants that cannot be stocked in advance; MEG business unaffected.

subsections.label: Ethanol capacity strategy
points: Company maintains a '3x3 strategy' with flexibility across grain, molasses-based, and imported ethanol feedstocks, allowing use of in-house ethanol for Chemicals as an intermediate.
India now has somewhat excess ethanol capacity relative to Bio-Fuels blending consumption at the 20% blending level achieved.

subsections.label: Distillery capex
points: Major capex in FY26 was toward two grain distilleries — one in Gorakhpur and one in Kashipur — accounting for ~INR400 crores of the ~INR830 crores total capex.

subsections.label: Export impact from geopolitical conflict
points: War has adversely impacted exports, particularly for large customers like New Park, to whom oilfield chemicals are sent largely for Middle East markets; that business is largely on hold.
Company continues to work on new products and new application areas for oilfield chemicals despite export headwinds.

subsections.label: Regional performance (Potable Spirits)
points: UP is one of the largest liquor markets; IMFL top-line growth in UP was 25% for the year.
Premium IMFL brands grew in higher double-digit percentages in UP versus medium/economy brands growing 4-7%.
Focus markets for premiumization include Delhi, UP, Uttarakhand, and Kerala; expansion planned into Andhra Pradesh and Rajasthan.
Kerala market entry included launch of a new brandy using a French blend developed through extensive internal and external research.

subsections.label: Demerger scheme (NCLT)
points: Scheme of arrangement (demerger) submitted to NCLT; hearing expected on 21st May 2026.
Management is hopeful of receiving the demerger order around 21st May or within the first 10 days of June 2026; once received, company will proceed with filing at ROC and related matters.

subsections.label: JV equity monetization plan (Clariant)
points: Per the JV agreement, IGL plans to sell an additional 24% equity stake in the Clariant JV in FY28-29.
Proceeds from this equity sale are expected to be substantial and will be used to pay off term loans, with management hopeful the Chemical business will be totally debt-free by FY28-29.
Current JV shareholding ratio is 51%-49% (Clariant-IGL, per context).

subsections.label: Geopolitical / war impact
points: War has had a mixed impact overall, slightly positive: sharp increase in crude prices and availability constraints for MEG/ethanol have improved relative competitiveness of ethanol-based products, aiding margins and market share.
Negative impact on exports, particularly oilfield chemicals to Middle East via customers like New Park, largely on hold.
Raw material feedstocks like propylene oxide have seen price increases and availability challenges due to the war.
Demand has softened in some areas as a result of sustained war conditions.

subsections.label: Crude price outlook
points: Management expects crude prices to stay firm despite potential softening, citing the prolonged war, damage to oil-controlling nations aligned with the US, likely desire of these nations to keep prices higher to recover, and US interest (per Trump's 'drill baby drill' stance) in higher oil prices to support its own production.
US influence over Venezuela and Iran oil supply, and customer interest in source diversification, are cited as factors potentially benefiting IGL even with a smaller market share shift.
Historically (pre-2021, for ~15 years) IGL's EO price was equal to or lower than Reliance's EO price, suggesting recent lower-crude periods may not be the norm.

subsections.label: EO price competitiveness vs Reliance
points: For the last couple of months, IGL has been competitive versus Reliance's EO price due to rising crude prices and ample domestic ethanol availability.
A large price delta between Reliance and IGL's EO price persisted for about 1.5-2 years, contributing to Chemicals degrowth in areas like EO sales to JV; this delta has largely been adjusted now.

subsections.label: Imported ethanol price rise
points: Imported ethanol prices in India rose significantly due to freight and other factors, while domestic ethanol prices remained stable or dipped slightly.

IGL's in-house ethanol capacity (via its 3x3 strategy — grain, molasses-based, and import option) allowed it to reduce imports significantly and support Chemicals business with in-house ethanol without concern over excess capacity.

subsections.label: Competitive pressure in nicotine/nutraceutical business
points: A competitor's new manufacturing unit for a key product (nicotine-related) has put pressure on realizations, prompting IGL's strategic shift toward value-added, long-term customers.

subsections.label: Argon price volatility
points: Prior year saw extremely high and volatile argon prices due to shortages in India from increased steel plant and electronics plant consumption, which contributed to a high base and subsequent top-line decline in gases in FY26.

subsections.label: Segment outlook
points: Bio-Fuels: potential for blending beyond 20% (to 21-22%) and selective flexi-vehicle adoption could further boost demand, subject to government policy decisions.

Potable Spirits: management expects no reason margins (Q4 EBIT margin of 22%) cannot be maintained or improved through continued mix/premiumization efforts; expects to consolidate positions in Delhi, UP, Uttarakhand, Kerala and other markets, targeting high double-digit IMFL growth.

Chemicals: expects improved profitability and top-line growth in the current year; performance chemicals business hoped to more than double this year and sustain that momentum for years to come (explicitly stated as a hope, not a projection).

Ennature Biopharma: expects the business to recover in terms of volume and profitability going forward via nutraceutical diversification, clinical studies, and geographic expansion (including US market entry); EBITDA improvement in nicotine sub-segment may not be significant this financial year.
Chemical business targeted to be totally debt-free by FY28-29, contingent on JV equity monetization proceeds.
Interest cost expected to remain around INR25-26 crores per quarter and continue to reduce over the years as prepayments continue.

risk_register.note: Large price delta between Reliance and IGL EO price persisted 1.5-2 years, contributing to Chemicals degrowth; now largely adjusted, with IGL competitive versus Reliance for the last couple of months.

risk_register.risk: Imported ethanol price increase
risk_register.note: Imported ethanol prices rose significantly due to freight and other factors; domestic prices remained stable/dipped, prompting IGL to reduce imports and rely more on in-house ethanol.

risk_register.risk: Competitive capacity addition in nicotine business
risk_register.note: A competitor's new manufacturing unit has put pressure on realizations of a key nicotine-related product, prompting shift to value-added customers.

risk_register.risk: Argon price volatility/shortage
risk_register.note: Prior year had extremely high argon prices due to shortage from steel/electronics plant demand, creating a high base that led to top-line decline in gases in FY26.

risk_register.risk: Chemicals top-line decline drivers (glycol ethers, gases, EO offtake)
risk_register.note: Cheaper Chinese/alternative feedstock-based glycol ethers captured market share; lower EO offtake by JV also contributed to degrowth.

themes.label: Margin expansion trajectory
themes.note: EBITDA margin improved steadily from 9.6% in FY22 to 15.5% in FY26, driven by strategic actions across Potable Spirits, Bio-Fuels and Chemicals.

themes.label: Debt reduction / deleveraging
themes.note: Prepaid INR804 crores in Q4FY26 funded by equity issue and cash flow; debt-to-equity improved from 0.7x to 0.5x; Chemical business targeted debt-free by FY28-29 via JV stake monetization.

themes.label: Ethanol blending policy tailwind
themes.note: 20% blending achieved ahead of 2030 schedule; discussions ongoing for blending beyond 20% and flexi-vehicle adoption to further boost Bio-Fuels demand.

themes.label: Potable Spirits premiumization
themes.note: IMFL revenue share and premium brand growth rising (UP IMFL growth 25%, high double-digit premium brand growth) via new brands, CSD entry, and geographic expansion.

themes.label: Geopolitical conflict impact
themes.note: War has slightly positive impact via improved ethanol-based product competitiveness against firmer crude, but negative impact on oilfield chemical exports and raw material (propylene oxide) costs/availability.

themes.label: Chemicals portfolio upgrade
themes.note: Top-line declined due to loss of low-margin glycol ethers/gases business and lower EO offtake, but margin and performance chemicals (up 40%+) improved as company shifts to higher value-added products.

themes.label: Ennature Biopharma diversification
themes.note: Stable top-line amid margin pressure; diversifying into branded nutraceuticals, clinical studies, and US market entry to reduce dependence on volatile nicotine/Thiocolchicoside products.

key_takeaways: Gross revenues of INR9,827 crores, which is up 8.7%. Net revenues of INR4,211 crores, which is up 11.8%.
EBITDA has been INR654 crores, which is up 24.5% over last year. And the EBITDA margin itself is up to 15.5%, up 162 basis points.
At a PAT level, we are posting INR293 crores, which is up 26.8%, and the PAT margin at 6.9% is also 84 basis points up.
India reached 20% blending as far as Bio-Fuels is concerned, which drove quite a lot of growth, both in terms of profits as well as sales.
In the Potable Spirit space, we have maintained our market leadership in the markets that we are present.
In Chemicals, we've seen a bit of a dip in sales, but having said that, I think we saw significant uptick in terms of the margin percentages as well as growth in overall margin.
In Ennature Biopharma, the top-line by and large has been stable despite a relatively challenging global and macroeconomic environment, as well as cost pressures.

The company has prepaid almost about INR804 crores in this quarter, which has been funded by INR467 crores through equity issue, which we did in November '25 and rest of the funds has been put in through the cash flow, resulting in INR20 crores saving in the interest cost.
pressing_questions: On the debt profile side, is there any plan for further reduction in the coming year? Right now it's around INR25-INR26 crores kind of per quarter on the interest cost side. Whether this rate will continue in the coming quarter, and what is the average borrowing cost right now, sir? If you could possibly share that debt break-up in all three segments.
On the scheme of arrangement submitted by NCLT, hearing expected 21st of May. Is there any expected timeline for the completion of demerger?
Currently are all our plants running at optimum level, because generally we also see that a revenue decline is attributable to maintenance or a shutdown, so are things at optimum level?

Regarding the profitability of INR12 to INR13 crores that we have achieved [from JV], and the specific factors that led to these figures, can this level of performance be sustained? Furthermore, what is our current thought process regarding the JV monetization exercise? Specifically, when do we intend to exit?

ELGIEQUIP.about: Incorporated in 1960, Elgi Equipments Limited along with its subsidiaries, is in the business of manufacturing and supplying Air Compressors ** & Automotive Equipments**. It is also providing related after sales services [1]

quarters.summary: Q1 FY27 saw 23% revenue growth (7% exchange-related) and 28% EBITDA growth, with margins expected to improve further as price corrections (taken to offset a 9% raw material cost increase vs an anticipated 3-4%) flow through by end-Q2/Q3 FY27; management reiterated its 20% EBITDA margin target (earlier guided 18% by 2031), continued cost reduction/reorganization in Australia, Europe and US, the Tier-4 low-cost compressor launch in September 2026, and Demand=Match technology rollout to the rest of the world within this year.

key_figures.label: Anticipated raw material cost increase (initial estimate)
Revised/possible raw material cost increase taken
Competitor warranty cost as % of revenue
Actual raw material cost increase (India, alternate range)

subsections.label: EBITDA reconciliation
points: Good volume impact on EBITDA.
Contribution was negative primarily due to raw material cost increases, tariffs, and product mix.
Company responded via cost reduction and price correction in the market; price correction impact expected towards end of Q2 and more fully in Q3.
Confident that raw material cost impact has been mitigated; EBITDA percentage maintained same as last year, in fact slightly better, expected to continue improving.
Employee cost increase primarily due to increments given across the world; overall cost well within control.
Other expenses rose 12% primarily due to rental premises taken for the motor plant and rental facilities occupied in the US after selling existing facilities there.

subsections.label: PAT and exceptional items
points: PAT at 9.7%, roughly similar to Q1 of last year.
This includes some exceptional reorganization costs related to restructuring in Australia, Europe, and a little in the US.
Some of these reorganization costs are expected to continue into the year, but management is not too concerned as the benefit accrues quickly.

subsections.label: Balance sheet and capital allocation
points: Net cash position continues to be very strong.
CAPEX: roughly half towards MK2 program (shifting campus from city factory to new campus).
Remaining CAPEX towards land purchased in Italy (contracted six years ago, commitment had to be honored) and normal factory equipment.

subsections.label: Tariff refunds
points: Company disclosed to the market that approval of close to $4 million refund has been received; actual refund received so far is about $1.6-1.8 million.
Balance refund is pending; company awaiting further disbursement.

subsections.label: Warranty cost benchmarking
points: Warranty cost is less than 1% of revenue, reflecting quality focus and lowest defect rates in the market.
Casual references from competitors suggest their warranty costs are higher than 1%.

key_figures.label: Aftermarket (parts only, excluding service) contribution - Rest of world
India dealer aftermarket revenue - service component
US dealer aftermarket revenue - service component

subsections.label: Sales mix
points: Sales mix between compressors and automotive equipment remained by and large the same as before.
Split between India and rest of world by and large maintained despite strong India growth, due to growth in other geographies as well.
Mix between screw and piston compressors has been by and large the same; management declined to disclose the specific split citing competitive sensitivity.
Company does not break up sales by industrial/infra/retail (e.g., automotive garages) categories separately.

subsections.label: India segment performance
points: India did well across all verticals - industrial, portables, aftermarket, vacuum - all grew in the quarter.
Expected to continue growing, though growth rates may be less attractive than Q1 because last year's Q1 was muted while Q2-Q4 were strong.
Strong inroads made into growth sectors like EV, renewable energy, and semiconductor ecosystem.

subsections.label: Growth drivers - India volume growth
points: Growth was primarily volume driven, not price driven.
Growth was seen across all industry verticals, not concentrated in one segment.
Demand=Match technology (launched September last year) has driven growth by gaining entry into customers who were never ELGI customers before; traction and receptivity described as outstanding.
No major new product launches, but continuous upgrade of the entire product range (energy efficiency, competitiveness via in-house motor manufacturing) has strengthened the value proposition.

subsections.label: Aftermarket business model
points: ELGI predominantly plays in the parts business, leaving the service part to dealers as a philosophy of not intruding into the dealer's profitable segment.

In India, low labor cost means service revenue for dealers is very small (2-3% of a typical 20-25% aftermarket revenue share); ELGI does a little direct service only for large corporate customers who don't want to deal with dealers.
In the US, service is a much larger share of aftermarket revenue due to higher labor costs and lumpy per-hour service charges.
Headroom exists to grow aftermarket share both in India and rest of world relative to global benchmark of ~38%.

subsections.label: Vacuum business (Italy JV product)
points: Vacuum product already indigenized with local production started in India; selling has begun.
Q1 has been very good with a phenomenal percentage growth, expected to continue, though management declined to give specific numbers.
ELGI is a small, late entrant in this segment, so high percentage growth numbers are expected for any new entrant.
High quality of customers acquired reflects the quality of the product and marketing program.

subsections.label: New sectors - EV, renewables, semiconductor
points: EV ecosystem growth relates to compressors supplied into factories of EV vehicle manufacturers and their suppliers (not into the vehicles themselves); number of new EV players is much higher in two-wheelers than four-wheelers.

Renewable energy (solar and wind) ecosystem growth: ELGI supplies compressed air across the full production chain for solar (cell manufacturing to panel manufacturing to installation) and wind turbine manufacturing, not directly into panels/turbines.

Semiconductor ecosystem: oil-free machines used in manufacturing; ELGI supplies to suppliers of the semiconductor industry across the wide application ecosystem, including the cleanest fab environment.

These new-age sectors (EV, renewables, semiconductors) are developing sectors with high growth rates in India but not yet significant revenue contributors compared to established sectors like textiles, cement, or steel.

key_figures.label: Warranty period offered on select segments

subsections.label: Demand=Match technology
points: Launched in India in September last year; absorption has been outstanding and a contributing factor to Q1 growth.
Technology sits embedded in multiple models, introduced in phased manner starting with most popular products; wherever introduced, market acceptance has been 100%.
Being launched in the rest of the world this year; validation machines already installed in all major geographies with outstanding feedback.
Made standard on ELGI compressors for tier 1, tier 2 and tier 3; the upcoming tier 4 compressors will not include Demand=Match.
Expectation that within another year, all ELGI products worldwide will have Demand=Match embedded.

subsections.label: R&D strategy
points: Two vectors of technology/product development: (1) improving existing architecture/design philosophy to highest efficiency and lowest life-cycle cost, delivering new higher-efficiency, lower-life-cycle-cost products; (2) fundamental technology development delivering breakthroughs like Demand=Match.
Overall philosophy is to reduce total life-cycle cost for the customer by eliminating less-obvious cost elements.
Management indicated exciting developments underway but declined to disclose specifics.

subsections.label: Competitive technology positioning
points: Management states there is no technology gap versus Atlas Copco or Ingersoll Rand; in some areas ELGI considers itself superior.
Development of Demand=Match seen as evidence of mastery of the 'know-why' (not just 'know-how') of technology, built over roughly 30 years of work.

Customers buy compressors based on three parameters: energy efficiency (biggest), maintenance cost, and price; ~80% of the market focuses on efficiency and maintenance while ~20% buys purely on price.
ELGI focuses on the 80% efficiency/maintenance-focused segment; close to 70% of its industrial-side models are independently rated best-in-world on energy efficiency.
Low defect rates support ability to offer lifetime and 10-year warranties in different market segments while maintaining industry-lowest warranty cost on revenue.

subsections.label: Australia
points: Growth was a bit muted relative to other geographies (initially cited as 17% YoY, later corrected to 7% YoY).
Challenges in service business and distribution operations.
Working to reset and reorganize processes; confident of being back to expected levels by Q3/Q4.

subsections.label: Southeast Asia
points: Continues to be a bit of a challenge; part of restructuring cost is also directed towards this region.
Market is big but there remain challenges for an Indian brand in that market.
Company is working on different strategies; it is a longer-term play and not currently a significant contributor.

subsections.label: Europe
points: Currently more of a P&L play focused on ensuring the business breaks even and stays there.
Some initiatives underway to grow the top line, including plans to enter Germany and increase emphasis on Eastern Europe.
Tighter cost control will continue even while growing certain geographies and products.
Expected to show improvement in the medium term and return to where it's supposed to be.

subsections.label: North America
points: Good growth story overall, with revenue up 37% YoY in Q1 FY27.
Distribution business not performing as well as it should, primarily on the service side; a few initiatives underway to address this.
All other businesses in North America have done well, and this momentum is expected to continue.

subsections.label: Distribution network strategy
points: In India, growth strategy is not about increasing number of distributors but reorganizing the network in various geographies to make it more effective (splitting large territories for deeper penetration) - an ongoing activity.
For Tier 4 launch, a completely new set of distributors has been set up separately from existing distributors, given the different business and mindset required.
In the US, growth has primarily come from accessing new distributors in new territories.
Getting new distributors on board is a long process, unlike quickly converting a customer; this remains an ongoing, not-easily-accelerated effort.
Business is primarily distribution-led; the real challenge is providing a unique value proposition to distributors, not just end users, since distributors own the customer relationships.

key_figures.label: Share of market buying on efficiency and maintenance (vs price)
Share of market buying purely on price
Rest of world aftermarket (parts only) contribution to revenue - alternate range

subsections.label: India demand environment
points: Inquiry levels remain very strong; gestation time for finalizations is longer than normal, but demand remains robust.
Water well segment saw an uptick in the quarter, though not a dramatic difference; overall positive contribution.
Overall buoyancy noted in the economy.
Steel industry: inquiries exist, but after a period of large capacity build-up, the industry appears focused on utilizing existing capacity before making further investments.
Compressor demand from large plants can be centrifugal or screw depending on plant size.

subsections.label: Market share
points: Management believes India market share gains likely occurred given strong growth, but deferred to competitors to confirm this.

subsections.label: Right to win / competitive positioning
points: Combination of energy efficiency leadership, low maintenance cost (via low defect rates), and unique technology like Demand=Match (not available from competitors) forms the basis of disproportionate win rates with end customers.
Getting in front of the customer is a long process due to the distribution-led business model; the key challenge is winning over distributors rather than end users.

subsections.label: Tier 4 (bottom-of-pyramid) segment entry
points: Project to enter the Tier 4 segment (bottom of the industrial pyramid) aimed at responding to low-cost compressors from China.
Products validated; first orders already received.
Formal launch scheduled this month (September) at an exhibition in Hyderabad.
Distributors lined up, training programs ongoing, internal sales and service organization in place.
This year is the start year; contribution to top line will be marginal initially but expected to be a strong player in the next few years.
A completely new, separate set of distributors has been established for this segment.

subsections.label: Organizational process transformation
points: Company recognizes need to build strong processes for efficiency and operational control as it scales internationally, since there is no established playbook for an Indian company building a global business.
Plan to build a strong process layer over the next few years to eliminate inefficiencies and enable the next round of scale.

Job-location optimization exercise underway to identify where particular functions can be performed most efficiently across geographical entities (not necessarily centralizing everything in India); this consolidation is expected to reduce overall costs over the next three to four years.

EBITDA margin improvement expected to come from three levers: operating leverage (linked to new products/market share/new market growth), gross margin improvement via constant cost reduction/re-engineering, and fixed cost rationalization via the process exercise - not reliance on leverage alone.

subsections.label: Reorganization/restructuring
points: Ongoing reorganization in Australia, Europe, and to a lesser extent the US, generating some exceptional costs that may continue into the year.
Benefit of reorganization expected to materialize quickly and be positive for the company.

subsections.label: Commodity cost volatility
points: Raw material/metal commodity cost increase initially expected at 3-4%, actually came in at 5% (5-6% in India), and a possibility existed that it could go to 9%; company has taken 9% as the working assumption and implemented corrective measures.
Contribution was negative in the EBITDA reconciliation primarily due to raw material cost increases, tariffs, and product mix.

subsections.label: US tariffs
points: Current tariff stands at 25%; company has been able to absorb this effectively.
Future improvement in margins assumes tariff situation remains stable; unforeseen shocks (e.g., further tariff changes) could affect outlook.
Tariff refund process: approval received for close to $4 million, but only $1.6-1.8 million actually refunded so far; balance is pending.

subsections.label: Regional operational challenges
points: Australia has faced challenges in its service business and distribution operations, requiring process reset and reorganization.
Southeast Asia remains a persistent challenge for an Indian brand despite market size.
North America distribution business (service side) is underperforming relative to other businesses in the region.

subsections.label: Low-cost competition from China
points: Company has faced low-cost compressor competition from China at the bottom of the industrial pyramid, motivating the Tier 4 segment entry.

subsections.label: Margin outlook
points: Management expects margins to continue improving barring unforeseen tariff shocks, given effective absorption of current 25% tariff.
Target remains to grow EBITDA margin to 20%; prior guidance had indicated 18% by 2031.

Improvement expected to come from continued volume growth, price corrections flowing through by end of Q2/fully in Q3, ongoing cost reduction/re-engineering, and fixed cost rationalization through process transformation over the next 3-4 years.

subsections.label: Regional outlook
points: Australia expected to return to normal levels by Q3/Q4 FY27.
Europe expected to show improvement in the medium term and return to where it's supposed to be.
North America momentum in non-distribution businesses expected to continue.

subsections.label: Tier 4 launch outlook
points: Formal Tier 4 launch this month (September) in Hyderabad; marginal top-line contribution this year, with expectation of becoming a strong player in the next few years.

subsections.label: Demand=Match global rollout
points: Expected to be launched across the rest of the world this year, with all products worldwide expected to have it embedded within another year.

risk_register.note: Causing market caution and elongated conversion timing on orders in India; also a factor in Europe's growth outlook; affects energy security and metal commodity prices.

risk_register.risk: Product mix impact on contribution
risk_register.note: Contribution was impacted by product mix during FY25-26 alongside tariff effects.

risk_register.risk: Low-cost Chinese competition in bottom segment
risk_register.note: Chinese players making low-cost machines and selling broadly, causing churn in the bottom segment across India, Europe, US and other markets; company has developed a response product for launch in September.

risk_register.risk: Elongated conversion timing on inquiries
risk_register.note: Inquiry levels remain strong in India but conversion timing is getting elongated due to broader uncertainty, seen as a caution signal.

risk_register.risk: Muted Europe market growth
risk_register.note: Europe growth muted due to Ukraine war, energy crisis, inflation and unemployment across different countries.

themes.label: Commodity cost volatility
themes.note: Raw material cost increase came in higher than expected (5% actual vs 3-4% anticipated, with a working assumption of 9% taken), pressuring EBITDA contribution before price corrections flow through.

themes.label: US tariff impact
themes.note: Current 25% tariff has been effectively absorbed; refund approvals of ~$4 million received but only $1.6-1.8 million actually paid out so far, with balance pending.

themes.label: Regional turnaround - Europe
themes.note: Europe remains a P&L play focused on maintaining break-even/marginal profitability, with initiatives to grow top line via Germany entry and Eastern Europe emphasis.

themes.label: Low-cost competition from China
themes.note: Tier 4 segment entry (validated products, first orders received, September Hyderabad launch) is company's response to low-cost Chinese compressors at the bottom of the pyramid.

themes.label: Technology & new product investment
themes.note: Demand=Match technology rollout across India has driven strong volume growth and new customer wins; global rollout underway this year with validation machines installed in major geographies.

themes.label: Inventory & forecasting optimization
themes.note: Company continuing a broader process-layer and job-location optimization exercise over the next 3-4 years to improve efficiency and reduce fixed costs.

themes.label: New-age sector demand (EV/Renewables/Semiconductor)
themes.note: Strong growth reported in EV ecosystem, renewable energy, and semiconductor ecosystem in India, though these remain small relative to established industrial verticals.

key_takeaways: Q1 revenue grew by about 23% compared to Q1 of last year, and after that 7% was exchange related. Across the board, we had growth.
EBITDA, we grew by 28%.
India standalone has grown by about 28%. North America, we have grown by 37%. Europe, we grew by 21% and Australia, 17%.

We started off the year thinking that there will be a 3% to 4% increase in material cost, but in reality it was 5%. Then there was a possibility that it could go to 9%. We have taken 9% and we have taken some corrective measures. So, we are confident that there will not be any impact.
Our PAT is at 9.7%, roughly similar as the Q1 of last year. And this is with some exceptional reorganization cost.
Net cash position in the company continues to be very strong.

Our project to enter into what we call the tier 4 segment in the bottom of the pyramid... We are all lined up. Our products have been validated. In fact, we have got our first orders already. The formal launch is this month in Hyderabad.

Demand=Match was launched in September of last year, and the traction and receptivity has been really outstanding right. And we've been able to gain entry into customers who have never been our customers.

quarters.summary: Elgi Equipments delivered 12% revenue growth and 17% PBT growth in FY25-26, with EBITDA impacted by product mix, tariffs and higher employee/other costs from reorganization investments. Management expects Q1 FY27 topline growth similar to or slightly better than last year with similar bottom-line percentages, while closely monitoring volatile metal commodity prices (reminiscent of the post-COVID scenario) and planning price corrections in June; India demand remains strong, US business is improving across verticals, and Europe is expected to turn from consolidation to marginal profitability.

key_figures.label: Gross margins maintenance price hikes required
Other expenses increase at standalone level

subsections.label: EBITDA Reconciliation
points: EBITDA increased YoY but the story is not complete; sales grew ~12% while contribution was impacted by product mix and tariffs.
Tariff impact was marginal during the year due to variation in tariffs (10% to 50%) affecting inventory at various levels; tariff situation is now completely normal/neutralized for the company.
EBITDA should have been about 2,100 million; main difference driver was employee cost.

Employee cost increased 16%, primarily due to reorganization in US and Europe to bring processes back to India, including creation of a shared service organization; part of the cost was one-time settlement cost and increase in India headcount to compensate.
Other expenses grew ~8% due to investments in various IT initiatives.
All regions except Australia and Southeast Asia grew in revenue.

subsections.label: Sales Mix
points: Sales mix stable between compressors and automotive equipment.
Within compressor business, roughly 50-50 split between India and rest of world (90-10 rough distribution mentioned).

subsections.label: Consolidated Financials
points: Wage code impact affected all companies; provision made in Q3 now reflected in results.
Large depreciation increase primarily due to leases — company sold property in the US and took property on lease, and leases are now accounted differently.

subsections.label: Cash Position
points: Net cash position continues to be solid; company continues to generate 100% of EBITDA as cash, even normalizing for extraordinary cash inflow like sale of property.

subsections.label: CapEx Plan
points: Larger project of progressively shifting factory from city to new plant to absorb ~120-130 crores this year.
Normal balancing CapEx of ~70 crores expected, totaling ~200 crores.
Desire to spend is often much higher than capability to spend.

subsections.label: Other Expenses One-off (Standalone)
points: Standalone other expenses increase attributed to investment in India go-to-market sharpening and IT investments, primarily PLM investment.

subsections.label: Realization & Pricing Growth
points: Volume growth across multiple verticals averaged around 3-4% in FY25-26.

Pricing contribution was minimal; Demand=Match product (launched September) gained good traction in market share and better price realization but contributes only a small percentage to overall sales currently.
Foreign exchange was a significant positive contributor as the company is a significant net earner of foreign exchange.

subsections.label: Price Correction Outlook
points: In Feb-March exercise, management projected cost increases requiring 2.5-3% price correction (excluding positive forex movement), which has already been introduced in the market.
Material cost increases that would normally occur progressively through the year have instead front-loaded — about 80% of the projected annual increase already occurred in Q1.
Management will take stock of the future and correct prices further in the month of June.

subsections.label: Demand Scenario - India
points: Inquiry levels continue to be strong; conversion timing is getting elongated, which is a caution signal.
Markets are not too concerned about price/cost increases; bigger concern is uncertainty over West Asia situation resolution.
Despite war-related disruption, once transport solutions were found for Middle East, sales continued to grow there — desire to continue business as normal despite conflict.
Uncertainty is causing hesitancy in finalizing orders ('hitting the enter button').

subsections.label: Demand Drivers
points: Compressor demand is primarily driven by industrial growth converting into capacity increases; compressed air is a utility like electricity, so capacity increase in a factory raises compressed air demand.
In the US, reshoring of manufacturing as a national strategy plus general economic growth is driving capacity and compressor demand.
Same demand dynamic applies in India.

subsections.label: Sectoral Demand - India
points: Demand is broad-based across industrial sectors, not concentrated in one sector.
Some verticals (e.g., steel mills) have large but infrequent compressor requirements (e.g., once every ~10 years).
Stable, steady-demand verticals include food processing, general engineering, foundry, forging.
Large project-driven sectors come and go over time.

subsections.label: Data Centers / Emerging Sectors
points: No direct business in data centers; minor plant-level compressed air requirements exist.
Company is fully engaged with ancillary businesses that feed into data centers requiring compressed air in production areas.
Company is solidly entrenched in other emerging sectors like solar.

subsections.label: North America - Segment Detail
points: Pattons Medical has done well and grown.

Portable segment: despite market conditions and cyclicality (infrastructure development drives rental company investment peaks, followed by troughs when rental companies utilize existing assets), portable has performed well.
Industrial segment has done exceedingly well.
Distribution business opportunity is larger compared to last year, especially strong in the last two quarters.
GTM intervention planned in the US to bring process orientation for additional growth in these business models.

subsections.label: Government-Focused Businesses - Railways
points: Railways is an India-centric business; company present in inter-city railway business but not in metros.

Metros are primarily served via global tenders by global electrical multiple unit manufacturers homologated with their own vendors (Korea, Japan, Europe); company trying to enter but it's a long process.
Intercity railway has been a forte, though not described as a large business; company has been present in this space for a while.

subsections.label: Government-Focused Businesses - Defence
points: Company does not directly make defence-related products; defence is viewed as a cyclical business with large lumped orders.

Global defence companies maintain a steady pipeline across multiple countries (India, Korea, Middle East, Brazil, Israel); building a defence business only for India is not viable for Elgi's strategy, as the company wants to stay focused on compressors.
Limited presence via joint venture business supplying high pressure compressors for the Navy, including the aircraft carrier Vikrant and certain frigates and destroyers.

key_figures.label: Vacuum segment share of global opportunity

subsections.label: Demand=Match Product
points: Launched in September; gained good traction in market share and better price realization, but contribution to overall sales remains small at present.

subsections.label: Low-cost Compressor Response to Chinese Players
points: Company recognized bottom-segment churn from low-cost Chinese machines a few years ago and began building a strategy in response.
Products are now ready and validated; design and validation of the range completed.
Marketing strategy is in final stages of being designed and executed.
Plan to launch first in India in September, then rest of world next year.

subsections.label: Vacuum Technology Entry
points: Vacuum business is not larger than compressors; company is a late entrant into vacuum.
As part of the aspired $25 billion global opportunity, vacuum represents about 12-15% of that size, making it a segment worth playing in.
Entered via license agreement with DVP as a low-cost learning platform entry strategy to understand the business and technology.
Parallelly incubating technology vectors expected to provide future competitive advantage.
This is a long-term 10-12 year program, not expected to deliver huge near-term growth.

subsections.label: In-house Motor Design Advantage
points: More than 95% of motors are in-house, with lead time of ~3 days compared to 3-6 months importing from China.
Motor cost advantage stems from fundamental design principles, not from any labor cost advantage (not reliant on 'Indians being cheap').

Capability built in motor design and manufacturing gives freedom to innovate; a completely new range of motors adding significant value to compressors will be launched in the next year to year and a half.

Technical choices such as oil-cooled vs air-cooled are design decisions the company can execute; competitors may already be doing or could do similar things, but it is the fundamental design that provides the edge.

subsections.label: Factory Relocation Project
points: Larger project of progressively shifting factory from the city to a new plant, absorbing about 120-130 crores this year.

subsections.label: Regional Performance
points: All regions except Australia and Southeast Asia grew in revenue during FY25-26.
India continues to be strong across all business verticals.

America is doing very well; after reorganization/reorientation, almost all verticals are beginning to fire; further changes planned in organization, focus and go-to-market to sustain and elevate performance.
Europe has been a consolidation and cost realignment story that has been completed; organization size and cost are now in line with business size; Europe expected to be profitable.
Europe remains a strategic, large but complex market; company is well entrenched and positioned to grow, contingent on stabilization of West Asia war and global geopolitical situations.

subsections.label: US Tariff Situation
points: Tariff story is not complete/resolved; tariffs apply to exports from both the Italy factory and the India factory to the US.
Tariff moved to another section of US regulations after the earlier section was withdrawn; there was confusion over exact levels, now settled at around 25% (down from 50%).
There is talk about refund of past tariffs; company is engaged with relevant agencies but it's too early to discuss details.

subsections.label: Europe Market Detail
points: Growth in Europe muted due to multiple problems: Ukraine war, energy crisis, inflation, and unemployment across different countries.
Market remains large despite muted growth.
Growth vector for company is to gain market share organically; no inorganic play planned in Germany or Europe currently.
Germany is a country where company has never done business; exploring how to enter and gain a reasonable position — seen as a growth opportunity.
Company not interested in investing more capital in Europe at this point in time.

subsections.label: Middle East / West Asia
points: Once transport solutions were found to get products into the Middle East despite the war, sales continued to grow in those markets.
Desire among customers to continue business as normal despite conflict, though uncertainty causes hesitancy in finalizing orders.

subsections.label: Inventory Optimization Drive
points: Significant progress made on organization-wide inventory optimization; part of current cash position contributed by inventory rationalization.
Low-hanging fruit addressed so far primarily in regions selling Elgi products (units and spare parts), enabling quick significant reduction.
Reduction also achieved in Rotair in response to muted growth.
Remaining opportunity in distribution businesses in Australia and the US, which service other brands of compressors as well; building processes and tools to manage that inventory.
Opportunity for further inventory improvement also exists in India plant.
Continued improvement in inventory levels expected into FY27.

subsections.label: Demand Forecasting Project
points: Project on better forecasting has been completed with good results, but accuracy is currently at 60-70% and needs to move to around 90% for comfortable sustainability in the future.

subsections.label: Industry Structure & Competition
points: Overall industry structure is stable in India and rest of the world.

Only segment seeing churn is the bottom/low-cost segment, where Chinese players sell low-cost machines to anyone entering the compressed air business; seen in India, Europe, US and virtually every market.

subsections.label: GTM Investment - India
points: GTM strategy investment was primarily in India, running for almost a 2.5-year period; no further investment requirement seen in India now.
Focus shifting to execution rigor on India GTM.

subsections.label: GTM Investment - US
points: Certain GTM opportunities being considered in the US as the region begins to perform well, with opportunity to move to the next level of orbit.
Measured intervention planned in very specific areas; early to quantify timing or value.

subsections.label: IT / Digital Transformation
points: IT transformation is a three-to-four-year journey as company globalizes, aimed at strengthening processes for risk management, compliance and control systems.
Plan to build out processes aligned to aspirations and convert them onto a digital platform; ongoing for at least next three to four years.

subsections.label: Vacuum Business Entry via DVP License
points: Entry into vacuum business via license agreement with DVP as a low-cost learning platform strategy, rather than large capital commitment upfront.
Long-term (10-12 year) program aimed at incubating technology vectors for future competitive advantage.

subsections.label: Reorganization - US and Europe
points: Reorganizing processes in the US and Europe to bring some processes back to India, including creating a shared service organization.
Involved one-time settlement costs and increased India headcount to compensate.

subsections.label: Property Sale and Leaseback (US)
points: Company sold property in the US and took on property on lease; leases are now accounted differently, contributing to higher depreciation.

subsections.label: Commodity Price Volatility
points: Metal commodity prices are rising and uncertain in terms of how long the trend will continue; company is watching this carefully.
Comfortable until June; taking stock of scenarios going forward.
Situation currently feels similar to the post-COVID year, where commodity prices marched up weekly/monthly.
Company was previously blindsided by not watching this carefully, resulting in a hit to profitability; determined not to repeat that mistake.
Will correct prices when there is demand to do so; impact of price increases on sustained market demand at new prices is difficult to predict.
Not worried about competitive disadvantage since commodity price increases affect virtually all players.

subsections.label: Geopolitical / West Asia War
points: West Asia war and attendant fossil fuel and downstream petrochemical price increases are a key uncertainty.
Uncertainty over resolution of the West Asia situation is causing market caution and elongating conversion timing on inquiries in India, more so than concerns over price/cost increases themselves.
Europe's growth outlook also tied to stabilization of West Asia war and global geopolitical situations.

subsections.label: Q1 FY27 Outlook
points: Q1 to continue to be strong; topline growth expected similar to or maybe a little better than last year's growth.
Bottom line expected to be roughly the same in percentage terms as last year.
Comfortable with commodity cost situation until June; will take stock of future scenarios thereafter and correct prices in June if needed.

subsections.label: Regional Outlook
points: India expected to continue being strong across all verticals.
America expected to continue doing well, with further organizational and go-to-market changes planned to sustain and elevate performance.
Europe expected to be profitable this year, with a marginal profitability scenario deemed more realistic than the worst-case breakeven scenario.
Continued growth in Europe contingent on stabilization of West Asia war and geopolitical situations.

Bottom line will roughly be the same in terms of percentages

We will see continued improvement in our inventory levels into the next year in FY27

key_takeaways: Revenue grew by 12% and PBT grew by 17% for FY25-26.
EBITDA increase impacted by product mix, tariffs, and higher employee cost (up 16%) and other expenses (up 8%) due to reorganization and IT investments.

EPACKPEB.about: Incorporated in February 1999, Epack Prefab Technologies Limited is one of India’s leading players in the pre-engineered building (PEB) and prefabricated construction industry.[1]

quarters.summary: Management reiterated FY27 revenue guidance of INR1,900-1,950 crores (~30% growth), with EBITDA margins expected to normalize to 10.5%-11.5% from Q2 FY27 onwards after a ~100 bps Q1 contraction caused by steel price inflation linked to the Middle East war; the order book of INR1,380 crores as of 30 June 2026, record Q1 order booking of INR580 crores, ongoing capacity expansions (Ghiloth, Andhra Pradesh, Vithalapur/Gujarat), and the new EPACK Data Center Solutions subsidiary (INR75 crore proposed investment) underpin confidence in sustaining strong growth, with peak revenue potential pegged at INR2,700-2,900 crores post full capacity ramp-up.

subsections.label: Margin commentary
points: EBITDA margin contraction of 100 bps YoY attributed to abrupt steel price increase from the Middle East war-driven commodity cycle; company had earlier guided towards a possible 200 bps hit but managed to contain it to 100 bps via smart purchase/sourcing policy and ability to secure price increases from fixed contracts with customers.
Steel price rose 12-14/15% over the last 4-5 months post-war, but balance sheet impact was limited to just 1%.
Cost increases in the P&L (employee benefit expenses, other expenses) have mostly been on account of scale, not structural margin erosion.

Guidance reiterated: EBITDA margins to normalize to 10.5%-11.5% band from Q2 FY27 onwards as new orders are booked at post-war (higher) commodity prices and older low-priced orders get executed or repriced.
PAT margin declined to 5% from 5.4% YoY, tracking the EBITDA margin contraction.
Absolute EBITDA, EBIT and PAT all grew YoY despite margin compression, reflecting revenue scale.
Gross margin declined ~200 bps QoQ in Q1 FY27; management expects gross margin improvement to play out over 7 to 8 quarters.
Revenue historically skews toward H2 (average ~53% H2 vs ~47% H1).

subsections.label: Cash / balance sheet
points: Company noted to have a good net cash balance as of March FY26 (per an analyst's observation, confirmed by management).

subsections.label: Order book drivers
points: Order book growth of 150% YoY (INR580 crores booked in Q1 FY27 vs INR240 crores in Q1 FY26) driven by strong capex cycle in the country and ability to take up and execute bigger projects on time.
Total pending order book stood at ~INR1,376-1,380 crores as on 30 June 2026, up from an opening order book of INR1,110 crores on 1 April 2026.

Prominent orders in Q1: INR165 crores from a renewable energy company for a solar cell and solar module plant (biggest order ever, largest single order, with an 4.5-month completion cycle); first order from an automobile company for a manufacturing plant; orders from existing customers Waaree Energies and Horizon for warehousing; export orders of INR2.5 crores secured.

Sectors contributing to order book: energy sector (renewable energy, transformers, wires & cable, fiber optic) is the most promising and fast-growing; logistics and warehousing traditionally contributes 22-25%; automobile contributes ~10%; data centers contribute 4-5%; automobile and FMCG are regular 'bread and butter' contributors; future opportunities from new plants by companies like CGSW or AMNS; existing clients contribute 40-45% of order book.

FY27 new order booking target of INR2,000 crores, with balance of ~INR1,400 crores to be booked over the remaining three quarters and roughly 50% or more of the target expected to be secured in H1 FY27.

Order book coverage clarification: FY27 new order target of INR2,000 crores is on top of opening order book of INR1,110 crores; adding INR2,000 crores to INR1,110 crores gives INR3,110 crores, and after executing ~INR1,900-1,950 crores of revenue (of which EPS contributes INR180-200 crores), closing pending order book should be around INR1,250-1,300 crores at start of next fiscal.
Margin profile of order book stays broadly similar across end-user segments because margin is calculated on a tonnage basis, irrespective of sector.
PEB constitutes 100% of the total pending order book currently; typical data center building order size ranges INR60-110 crores per building.

Sandwich panel order book: 3.2 lakh sq meters at Mambattu continuous line alone in current quarter, versus a corrected combined figure of 4 lakh sq meters in the previous quarter; combined Mambattu + Greater Noida sandwich panel order book currently stands at 4.7 lakh sq meters.
Order completion cycle averaged 8 months in Q2 FY26, with order book to revenue ratio of 1.5x in that quarter.

subsections.label: Pipeline / win rate dynamics
points: Company earmarks only ~30-40% of quotations for active focus, given the customized/technical nature of buildings and the effort required for design and consultation; not all customers are equally serious about their projects.
Win rate/pipeline conversion ratio of ~15-20% (cited ~20%) is considered strong versus typical industry benchmark of 10-12%.

Loss of certain projects tied to capacity/regional availability constraints (e.g., available capacity in the north but demand concentrated in south where facility is already full) to avoid over-committing and damaging execution reputation.
Win rate from existing customers not formally tabulated but believed to be at least double the overall ~20% rate (30-40%).

subsections.label: Order size / customer concentration
points: Average order size has increased tremendously following the record INR165 crore order, moving from ~INR6.5 crores (FY26) to ~INR12-13 crores currently; median order size (less than INR12 crores) likely somewhat lower, and expected to decline further as smaller sandwich panel/modular building orders increase in mix.
On the INR165 crore renewable energy order, EPACK is sole supplier for both buildings; for larger future projects, customers may split supply between two vendors.
Company's overall market share (organized+unorganized) was 5-6% in FY26 and is expected to rise to 7-7.5% by end of FY27, versus market leader's ~12% share.

subsections.label: Fixed-price vs pass-through mechanism
points: Most orders are fixed-price contracts; pass-through mechanism doesn't work well because raw material procurement, production, logistics and site installation occur at different points in time, creating confusion with customers.
Risk from abrupt commodity price increases is mitigated by booking new orders on a near-weekly basis at current prices.

subsections.label: Business segment mix
points: EPS (packaging) business has come back to normalcy with a bit of price increase and a bit of volume growth contributing; EPS business FY27 expected revenue of INR180-200 crores and does not carry a pending order book, operating instead on a monthly rolling plan basis.
Prefab business continues to hover around 25% growth, in line with expectation for the year.

Three product lines: pre-engineered building (PEB), modular housing, and sandwich panels; sandwich panels line can be combined with either modular housing or PEB, making revenue segregation difficult, though order book and utilization for sandwich panels are disclosed separately for transparency.

subsections.label: Data center product capability development
points: Company already has design capability for hot/cold air containment zone management (similar to sandwich panel design work) and shop drawing preparation/detailing capability.
Aluminum sections and polycarbonate materials handling capability already exists from modular prefabricated housing business.
Fabrication and welding capability for pipe spooling already available at the manufacturing level; only additional equipment needed.

P&M (power & mechanical) module: about 30-35% involves racking structure and fabrication already done in-house, with additional mechanical/electrical parts integration required via tie-ups; a separate product development team has been working on this for the last 3-4 months, with capability expected to be ready in the next 3-4 months.
Company is in the process of acquiring additional capabilities via technical tie-ups or hiring people experienced in data center-related work.

subsections.label: Capacity expansion projects and timelines
points: Ghiloth (second insulated/continuous sandwich panel line, capacity 8 lakh square meters per line) to be commissioned by end of this quarter (Q2 FY27), with commercial production likely starting from the next quarter (Q3 FY27).
Andhra Pradesh second structural steel fabrication line should come up starting next quarter (Q3 FY27).

Vithalapur (Gujarat) 50,000-metric-ton-per-annum structural steel plant: commissioning expected in the last quarter of FY27 (Q4), with production starting from April 2027 (FY28) onwards; this adds to current PEB capacity of 1,47,000 metric tons, with an additional 23,600-metric-ton PEB capacity addition planned in Q2 FY27 (operational Q3), bringing total FY27 PEB capacity estimate to ~1,70,000 tons.

All these expansions (Ghiloth second line, Mambattu additional line, Vithalapur 50,000-ton line) collectively underpin the peak revenue potential of INR2,700-2,900 crores; sandwich panel realization assumption of INR1,700-2,000 per square meter implies revenue potential of INR125-140 crores per line from product sales alone, or up to INR250 crores per line including associated project revenue.

subsections.label: Utilization commentary
points: All four manufacturing plants running at almost full capacity in Q1 FY27; prefab division average utilization above 75%.

Sandwich panel line at Mambattu (LSF capacity 21 lakh square meters) ramped utilization to ~44-45% in Q1 FY27 from 25% in FY26; even without booking further orders, delivering the existing 3.2 lakh sq meter order book alone would result in 70%+ (also cited 75%) annualized utilization for this line in FY27.

Management does not consider the 90%+ utilization seen in Q4 FY26 as a sustainable benchmark; more realistic typical range is 75-80%, and even at 80-85% utilization FY28 revenue could reach ~INR2,300-2,400 crores.

subsections.label: Export strategy
points: Q1 FY27 marked the start of exports (INR2.5 crores secured), with insulated sandwich panels exported to an African nation, considered a good early start point.
Company is developing go-to-market strategy for exports and has ramped up its export sales team; also in discussion with players for exporting structural steel PEB buildings.

Difficult to quantify what percentage of total business will come from exports over the next 2-3 years, but management is hopeful it will become a sizable portion; these are described as 'early days'.

For PEB products specifically, exports have so far been limited to SAARC nations (Bhutan, Nepal, Sri Lanka); the recent African sandwich panel export is a new opening but the company has not yet received significant PEB/steel structure export orders from Africa.

Despite export opportunity, company notes that expanding domestic capacities are being fully utilized in the domestic market, so a more focused approach is needed to grow international business meaningfully.

subsections.label: Procurement / pricing management
points: Company manages commodity price risk through sourcing policy and by pricing new orders based on current raw material costs almost every week, rather than relying on pass-through mechanisms.

subsections.label: Market opportunity and positioning
points: Total addressable fabricated steel market is large and growing: India produced 164 million tons of steel last year, with ~80% of raw material being flat/long steel products; fabrication requirement is typically 12-19% of total steel produced per industry norm; India's steel capacity is projected to reach 300 million tons by 2030, implying a ~36 million ton fabricated steel market (pessimistic case) by then.
Even sustaining 30% growth through FY30, EPACK would capture only a small fraction (0.3-0.35 million tons) of that ~36 million ton fabricated steel opportunity.

Pre-engineered buildings currently contribute only 3-5% of total construction (including industrial and logistics buildings); growing acceptance of PEB for high-rise, commercial, institutional, school, hospital, data center, and parking lot applications presents a large future opportunity.
Company's overall market share (organized + unorganized) expected to rise to 7-7.5% by end of FY27 from 5-6% in FY26, versus market leader's ~12% share.

subsections.label: Data center market strategy and competition
points: Data centers already use EPACK's existing insulated Rockwool sandwich panel product line for wall and building facade systems; company has done 4-5 such projects and gets repeat orders, including a new order from Adani for their upcoming data center.

Company also bid for two complete data center structures but lost both bids on design optimization and pricing grounds, being relatively new to designing and pricing this segment; hopeful of booking a complete turnkey PEB data center order by this quarter end.

Rationale for the separate EPACK Data Center Solutions subsidiary: most hyperscale data centers in India will adopt DFMA (Design for Manufacturing and Assembly), creating opportunities in structural steel fabrication, insulated sandwich panels, and newer building/construction products (hot/cold air containment zones, pipe spooling, P&M modules) with electrical items integration; subsidiary will focus on developing suitable products for both domestic and international data center markets.

Competition in data center structures space is not limited to PEB players; also includes EPC players who take up entire projects (structures included), and integrated steel/structure companies like JSW Severfield Limited (JSSL) and JSPL's high-rise/data center wing, which do their own structure fabrication rather than outsourcing.

If an EPC player (e.g., NCC, L&T, Sam India) takes up a data center project, the structure is typically outsourced to companies like EPACK; if a steel/structure company like JSSL or JSPL takes the project, they execute the structure fabrication themselves.

key_figures.label: Proposed investment in EPACK Data Center Solutions subsidiary

subsections.label: EPACK Data Center Solutions subsidiary formation
points: Separate subsidiary floated to focus on developing products suitable for the data center market, targeting both domestic and international opportunities.
INR75 crores equity investment earmarked primarily to acquire land and set up a manufacturing facility, ahead of firming up product development plans.

Concrete utilization/funding plan for the INR75 crores is not yet finalized; management expects to have real numbers on total investment, facility location, and revenue visibility by end of this quarter (Q2 FY27).

Funding approach for the subsidiary undecided at this stage; could include some debt if needed, but management indicated any debt raised would be reasonable relative to company size, not high/substantial; company also has a healthy net cash balance as of March FY26.
Management deferred detailed disclosure on revenue potential, working capital needs, and ROCE/ROE comparison versus the base PEB business (18-20% ROCE) to the next quarter's call.

subsections.label: Commodity price risk
points: Middle East war led to an abrupt steel price increase of 12-15% over the last 4-5 months, initially expected to hit EBITDA margin by ~200 bps but actual impact contained to ~100 bps through fixed-contract price increases and sourcing management; balance sheet impact limited to just 1%.

Fixed-price contract structure creates inherent risk when commodity prices move abruptly between order booking and execution, since raw material procurement, production, and site installation occur at different times.

subsections.label: Execution risk
points: Monsoon season can delay civil works that are the customer's responsibility, which in turn can delay overall project timelines (e.g., delays faced by the customer on the INR165 crore renewable energy order despite committing to 1-month civil works completion); management does not see major challenge to EPACK's own execution capability.

subsections.label: Competitive / capability risk
points: Company's win rate of ~15-20% reflects selective bidding and capacity constraints rather than lack of competitiveness; regional capacity mismatches can cause lost orders.
In the emerging data center segment, company lost two bids due to design and pricing inexperience, being relatively new to this specific product/pricing model.
Company currently lacks capability for very heavy structures such as railway over bridges (ROBs) requiring wider span/web width; no current business in the railways segment.

subsections.label: Margin trajectory guidance
points: Improvement in EBITDA margin expected starting from Q2 FY27 onwards, driven by execution of orders booked at revised (post-war) pricing from the last two quarters, and continued full-year guidance of 10.5-11.5% EBITDA margin reaffirmed with high confidence.
Company had earlier guided for a possible 200 bps margin dip due to commodity price increase but managed to contain it to 100 bps in Q1 FY27.
FY27 revenue target of INR1,900-1,950 crores, representing ~30% growth, alongside a new order booking target of INR2,000 crores for the year.

subsections.label: Growth sustainability beyond FY27
points: Management expressed confidence in sustaining 30%-plus growth beyond FY27 through the next 3-4 years (through FY30), based on India's growing steel production capacity (to ~300 million tons by 2030) and the fabrication industry's 12-19% share of total steel produced, implying a large (~36 million ton) addressable fabricated steel market versus EPACK's projected 0.3-0.35 million ton scale even at sustained 30% growth.
Growing PEB acceptance for high-rise, commercial, institutional and data center buildings (from current 3-5% share of total construction) seen as a further long-term growth driver.
Peak revenue potential post full capacity expansion estimated at INR2,700-2,900 crores, with FY28 revenue potential of ~INR2,300-2,400 crores at 80-85% utilization.

guidance_ledger.statement: Targeted revenue of close to INR1,900-1,950 crores, a growth of ~30% over last financial year
EBITDA margins normalized at 10.5% to 11.5% from this quarter onwards; full year guidance of about 10.5%-11%
