Target was ~50+ cities and 45-50% of online volumes by mid-year FY27; company expects to comfortably cross that ahead of schedule, by next quarter end.

Model is asset-light: technology stack built in-house; first-mile and mid-mile managed via dedicated regional/local partners (Capex-light); last-mile delivered by dedicated partners exclusively for FirstCry shipments (not mixed with third-party or other brands).
Takes time to build a 'mature' city network — real impact accrues as repeat cohorts and frequency build with lag.
Key operating metrics improving: delivery TAT reduction, on-time delivery >92% (best in industry, per management).

subsections.label: Qwik (Quick-commerce) Initiative
points: Started as pilot from December 1, 2025; now considered beyond pilot phase — full strategic commitment.
Expanded to 5 cities within a few months; select catchments already exceeding 20% of online orders under Qwik with sub-3-hour delivery.
Expected to reach ~10% of overall online B2C shipments in FY27.
Leverages COCO stores, warehouses, stockist network, and some dark stores.
Aimed at defending categories impacted by competitors, especially Diapering.

subsections.label: Offline Store Expansion (India MC)
points: Company paused opening company-owned stores in FY26 to maintain capital efficiency given macro conditions.
Given Q4 offline growth improvement (best in last seven quarters), management will double down on store openings in FY27 with a mix of COCO and FOFO formats, targeting ~100 stores.

subsections.label: GlobalBees Brand Rationalization
points: Rationalization of non-core brands (lower growth, loss-making) nearing completion, targeted for Q1 FY27, enabling shift to sustainable organic top-line and bottom-line growth from Q2 FY27.

subsections.label: AI Adoption
points: AI being used across multiple facets: revenue optimization, gross margin optimization, productivity/efficiency improvements — beyond typical call-center savings/chatbots.
Examples cited: supply chain cost savings (faster product go-live improving working capital), SEO/AEO/GEO URL optimization for better conversions.
Management describes benefits as still evolving; too early to quantify bps impact, but expects a 'meaningful' outcome; may share quantified impact in subsequent quarters.
Initiative described as having started only a couple of months prior to the call.

subsections.label: Capital Allocation / M&A Stance
points: Management has not discussed or planned any buybacks internally or at board level, despite sufficient cash on the balance sheet.
No discussion regarding acquisition risk given low valuation relative to revenue; focus remains on executing FY27 growth and EBITDA expansion.

key_figures.label: Gross margin loss due to crude-linked raw material prices and rupee depreciation

subsections.label: Competitive Intensity
points: Elevated promotional/discounting intensity in diapering category from Quick-commerce and horizontal commerce players, both listed and unlisted, described as irrational; expected to persist for 4-6 quarters before subsiding, based on historical precedent (2016-2017).

subsections.label: Input Cost & Currency Volatility
points: Manufacturing segment gross margin hit by rupee depreciation and crude-linked raw material price increases due to geopolitical situation; described as more severe than past occurrences; expected to be passed on to customers and recovered from Q2 FY27, with a typical 1-2 quarter lag in customer pass-through.

subsections.label: International Market — Geopolitical/Macro Situation
points: Evolving Middle East situation causing moderation in consumer sentiment and some import complexities.

Management views this as beyond its control but also as an opportunity to optimize discounting strategy, marketing costs, and targeting for higher-LTV consumers, while continuing home brand mix improvement.

subsections.label: Logistics Cost Front-Loading
points: RocketBees and Qwik network expansion involves front-loaded costs before city/catchment networks mature; expected 40-60 bps cost impact for a few quarters before normalizing as networks mature.

key_figures.label: Qwik share of B2C shipments target
RocketBees city/volume target
key_figures.period: mid FY27 (ahead of schedule, achieved by next quarter end)

subsections.label: India Multi-channel Outlook
points: FY27 growth trajectory expected to be much superior to FY26 across both online and offline channels, driven by RocketBees, Qwik, and offline product-mix initiatives maturing.

Gross margin recovery expected starting Q2 FY27 as manufacturing-related crude/currency impact is passed to customers; diapering-related margin pressure may persist through FY27 but overall EBITDA (in Crores) expected to see double-digit growth FY27 vs FY26 for India multi-channel, driven by margin recovery, operating leverage, and non-diapering category (85% of business) margin expansion.
Offline/online GMV mix has not materially changed between FY25 and FY26; management expects a 'lag effect' to translate into online growth improvement as RocketBees/Qwik scale.

subsections.label: International Outlook
points: Continued focus on sustainable growth with goal to reduce adjusted EBITDA losses to zero as early as possible via gross margin improvement, home brand expansion, and sales mix expansion.
Management expects to continue the FY26 pace of loss reduction into FY27.

subsections.label: GlobalBees Outlook
points: Post rationalization completion (targeted Q1 FY27), expect a complete return to organic core-business growth from Q2 FY27, continuing FY26's EBITDA trajectory (4.9% core EBITDA margin).

subsections.label: AI Benefits Outlook
points: Benefits considered meaningful but not yet quantifiable; management may share specific quantified impact (e.g., bps) in subsequent quarterly updates.

guidance_ledger.statement: With current initiatives (RocketBees, Qwik, offline mix fix), trajectory of sequential quarterly better growth will continue in FY27; FY27 growth will be much superior than the entire FY26.

guidance_ledger.statement: Incremental gross margin loss (apart from Q3 impact) from rupee depreciation and crude-linked raw material prices will be regained back in Q2 as costs are passed to customers in regular BAU.

Goalpost is to reach close to 45-50% of online volumes and 50+ cities by middle of the year; company believes it is ahead of curve and will cross this before next quarter end.
Qwik deliveries over entire B2C shipments should cross roughly around 10% of overall online business over the full year of FY27.
There will be some impact of 40 to 60 bps from front-loading costs for a few quarters, normalizing as network matures.
Double down on approach to open company-owned stores in FY27 with a mix of COCO and FOFO, targeting roughly 100 stores.

Goalpost is to build international business sustainably and reduce losses to zero as early as possible via gross margin improvement, home brand expansion, and sales mix expansion; will continue to reduce losses in FY27 as done in FY26.
Growth for the offline channel should continue to be as strong as mid-teens seen in Q4 FY26.
Online business growth should improve to be much superior compared to FY26 online growth as RocketBees/Qwik networks mature, though cost is front-loaded and results have a lag.
Endeavor is to complete rationalization of underperforming brands by end of Q1 FY27, enabling sustainable organic top-line and bottom-line growth from Q2 FY27.
Too early to comment on bps impact of AI; benefit expected to be meaningful; management may share a specific number in the next quarterly update.
Company has not discussed buybacks or acquisition-related matters internally or at board level despite having sufficient cash.

themes.label: Competitive intensity in diapering
themes.note: Heightened promotional/discounting intensity from Quick-commerce and horizontal players pressured growth and margins in diapering; expected to persist 4-6 quarters.

themes.label: Quick-commerce/RocketBees expansion
themes.note: RocketBees scaled from 13 to 62 cities and Qwik to 5 cities, delivering 40%+ and 20%+ of online volumes respectively, driving improved delivery TAT and customer experience.

themes.label: International path to sustainable growth
themes.note: International EBITDA losses reduced 33-35% YoY via gross margin expansion (250-470 bps), home brand growth, and sales mix improvement, despite continued promotional pressure.

themes.label: Input cost/currency-driven margin pressure
themes.note: Rupee depreciation and crude-linked raw material costs hit India MC manufacturing gross margin in Q4, but described as transitory and expected to recover by Q2 FY27.

themes.label: GlobalBees brand rationalization
themes.note: Portfolio rationalization of underperforming brands nearing completion (targeted Q1 FY27), weighing on consolidated growth (20% vs 28% core) but improving profitability trajectory.

themes.label: Offline channel revival
themes.note: Product mix fix (width-to-depth strategy) launched in SH26 drove mid-teens offline GMV growth in Q4, expected to continue into FY27.

themes.label: FY27 growth outlook
themes.note: Management expressed confidence that FY27 growth across India multi-channel, international, and GlobalBees will be superior to FY26, driven by maturing initiatives.

key_takeaways: On the consolidated business, we are free cash flow positive for the full year. Revenue for FY26 has grown by 12% year-on-year and adjusted EBITDA has increased by 24% year-on-year for the full year.
Net losses for Q4 has reduced by 57% and for full year FY26, it has reduced by 23%.
India multi-channel business revenue at 11.4% in Q4 growth; offline channel initiative went live in Q4 SH26 and yielded mid-teens growth in GMV for offline channel.

We continue to believe that with the current initiatives that we have taken across in the India multi-channel, this trajectory of sequential quarterly better growth will continue in FY27... FY27 will have a better growth overall than compared to the entire FY26.
India multi-channel business continue to remain PAT and cash flow positive for the entire FY26.
In the international business, elevated promotional pressures from horizontal commerce players continue; adjusted EBITDA losses reduced by 33% for Q4 year-on-year and 35% for the entire FY26.

On the GlobalBees front, we had a very strong quarter on both organic side as well as profitable growth. We delivered 28% of core category year-on-year growth in FY26 with roughly around 92 Crores of adjusted EBITDA post corporate expenses.
RocketBees moved from 13 cities in Q2 and 22 cities by end of Q3 to 62 cities by end of Q4, delivering 40% plus of online delivery volumes.

Qwik crossed 5 cities by end of March, already crossing 20% of overall online orders in select catchments with sub-3-hour delivery, expected to reach roughly around 10% of overall online business over FY27.
pressing_questions: What percentage of orders are delivered through these networks (RocketBees), and what is the logistic cost increase in Q4 and expected increase in FY27?
How is the store business in ME doing, and what is the plan for store opening in FY27 given only 10 COCO stores were added in FY26?
What are the key operational and financial parameters seen in PIN codes/cities where interventions (RocketBees/Qwik) are fully deployed that give confidence of a return to growth momentum?
What exactly is the source of gross margin pressure — competitive pressure, inflation, or a mix?
Is the pressure on diapers from Quick Commerce coming largely from unlisted players, or is there behavioral change once players get listed and chase profitability?
How is AI benefiting the business, and what percentage/bps benefit can be expected in the long run?
Given trading at a low valuation compared to revenue, is there risk of acquisition, or any chance of buybacks?
What has changed to revive offline channel growth, and why is online channel growth comparatively low given the increasing organized shift?
Given continuing margin pressures, can India multi-channel EBITDA (in Crores) have double-digit growth FY27 vs FY26?
On a benchmark basis, how does RocketBees' own-delivery model compare to how competitors like Amazon, Nykaa, Flipkart handle delivery — do they do their own delivery or fully outsource?
Has the international business been impacted by the Middle East situation leading to low single-digit revenue growth, and has this affected progress toward breakeven?
How is the 6-12 years age category extension performing in terms of customer retention?

PREMEXPLN.about: Premier Explosives Limited is engaged in the manufacturing of industrial explosives and detonators. It also undertakes operation and maintenance (O&M) services of solid propellant plants at the Sriharikota Centre of ISRO and Solid Fuel Complex at Jagdalpur under the umbrella of DRDO.[1]

quarters.summary: Q1 FY27 revenue declined 28% YoY to INR102.6 crores due to dispatch/execution delays from global headwinds, supply chain disruptions and export license delays; margins were pressured by elevated raw material costs. Management expects headwinds to ease, stronger execution and revenue conversion in coming quarters, retains FY27 revenue guidance of ~INR600 crores and EBITDA margin target of 15%-20%, backed by an order book of INR1,393 crores (94% Defense) and the recently announced Apollo Micro Systems acquisition expected to open new defense electronics synergies.

subsections.label: Cost drivers
points: Decline in other expenses from INR20 crores to INR11 crores in Q1 attributed to earlier quarters having expected credit loss provisions and higher forex losses, which are not comparable apple-to-apple; underlying sustainable run rate seen at INR9-10 crores.
Operating performance impacted by elevated raw material costs amid prevailing global market conditions, creating temporary margin pressure during the quarter.
Company continues to focus on operational efficiency, cost optimization and disciplined execution to mitigate cost headwinds.

subsections.label: Margin outlook
points: Margins expected to improve because of a bouquet of products; depending on dispatch mix of products, margin percentage varies quarter to quarter.
Healthy order book and improved execution pattern (movement of materials this quarter) gives confidence that margins will improve in coming quarters.
Management reiterated EBITDA target of 15%-20% for the financial year, same as stated in earlier conference calls.

EBITDA margin decline from 15% to 6% in Q1 FY27 attributed to product dispatch mix varying by quarter; raw material cost increase and under-absorption of fixed costs contributed to the difference, expected to be made up in coming quarters.
Raw material prices have not yet normalized; company has existing contracts it must execute at current pricing, and will increase prices once these contracts are completed.

subsections.label: Order book composition & visibility
points: Order book stands at INR1,393 crores with approximately 94% from Defense segment (INR1,309 crores), Explosives segment at INR42 crores (3%), and Service (O&M) segment at INR42 crores (3%), providing strong revenue visibility and reinforcing confidence in growth trajectory.
Breakup available only between industrial explosives and defense; company has 94% defense orders and 6% regular/industrial explosives orders.
All orders are for execution over next 2 years; company expects a run rate of INR1,000 crores plus in execution, after which order book replenishes.
Management confident that sustained execution momentum, continued development of new products, and ongoing expansion initiatives will maintain a strong growth trajectory in forthcoming quarters.

subsections.label: Specific order updates
points: July 2023 flares/chaff order: LD (liquidated damages) reversal of INR30 crores still in process; expected clarity by this quarter end or by October/November due to multiple processes involved.

Remaining backlog of about INR75 crores on the July 2023 order expected to be completed in the next 4-5 months; production for flares has started in company's own plant, expected to contribute well in coming quarters.

October 2025 order of INR430 crores: previously guided ~2/3 (INR285 crores) to be completed in FY27; Q1 FY27 execution was only INR21 crores; management now states the entire INR430 crores order will be completed within FY27, as the order must be completed before the financial year ends.
Chaff material payload component is import-dependent (already executed/completed); flares are manufactured in-house, giving company capability to complete full order.

April 2026 INR350 crores international defense order: export license process is underway; import license must first be issued by the importing country before export license can be processed (minimum 3-4 months for export licensing); production not expected to start in this calendar year; some dispatches expected in the last quarter.

Export revenue expectation previously stated at INR200-300 crores for FY27; export target for current quarter set at INR150-200 crores; earlier revenue guidance referenced an INR400 crores export license backlog.

subsections.label: QRSAM inquiry
points: On being asked about expected order value from QRSAM (in context of BEL's INR30,000-40,000 crores program), management stated no tenders have been called yet, so no order size can be quantified.

key_figures.label: Bulk explosives - balance Singareni Collieries contract execution

subsections.label: Defense & Space segment
points: Revenue declined 35% YoY despite a strong defense demand environment; management clarified this was largely timing-related due to delays in receiving export licenses on export orders, not delays in customer procurement or acceptance process.
Most export licenses have since been received and company expects to complete pending executions in Q2 and Q3.

subsections.label: Bulk explosives business
points: Difficult to predict FY28 guidance for bulk explosives as prices are highly dependent on raw material input cost and there are more than 40 players/manufacturing capacities in the field.

Company has an executed contract with Singareni Collieries; balance portion of about INR25-30 crores to be executed this financial year, implying bulk explosives revenue expectation of roughly INR80 crores for FY27.
Beyond Singareni, company also has debt increase orders and export orders that will continue.

Company withdrew from Coal India business in the last year and the year before due to very low prices; margins in bulk explosives are very thin and negative in many places; Singareni is serviced because of proximity/logistics giving slightly better net cost versus Coal India; overall margin profile described as low single-digit.

subsections.label: RDX/HMX international market
points: International demand for RDX/HMX is good, but obtaining export licenses remains difficult.
Pricing varies by destination country; war scenario globally has pushed demand and prices up for the present; uncertain how pricing evolves after 2-3 years.
Management declined to quantify specific RDX/HMX price bands citing competitive sensitivity, but noted industry price bands (not company-specific selling price) are publicly available online.

subsections.label: Drones/UAV payloads
points: Company is not developing its own drone/UAV technologies; instead partnering with several drone manufacturing companies to supply payloads, participating as a partner rather than an independent standalone supplier.

subsections.label: Alternate raw material for mines/loitering munitions
points: New alternate raw material sent to DRDO for approval, intended for use in land mines and loitering munitions for drones, is undergoing testing by DRDO, ARDE and HEMRL.
Hardware components have been assembled; chemical and other component testing is ongoing; process may take another 6 months to complete.
Once cleared, this material will open doors to fully enter Adrushy mines and Ulka mines segments, which are in high demand from the Indian Army.

subsections.label: Katepally capex - RDX/HMX
points: Integration of pipelines and plant & machinery erection/installation for RDX and HMX production is almost complete.
Water trials expected to commence in September, lasting about a month, after which production of intended RDX/HMX products will begin.

subsections.label: Katepally capex - mixing plant
points: 2.5-tonne planetary mixer installed; some imported components from the mixer supplier were delayed due to maritime shipping movement issues.
Company has pressured the supplier to air-ship the delayed components; plant expected to be ready by end of September, after which dummy trials will be taken up.

subsections.label: Andhra Pradesh expansion
points: Land parcel not yet finalized; pricing has been an issue, as the explosives industry requires large landed areas where price makes a significant difference.
Company has requested the government to rework/offer a more reasonable price to enable gainful benefit from the expansion.
Expansion plans expected to continue post-Apollo transaction; management will take a call on next steps after presenting requirements to Apollo.

subsections.label: Export delays
points: Export order deliveries were delayed due to maritime shipping problems.
Delays also occurred in delivery of imported components used in finished countermeasure products, further impacting export deliveries.

subsections.label: Supply chain disruptions
points: Global headwinds and supply chain disruptions across certain programs caused delays in dispatches and project execution during Q1 FY27.
Maritime movement delays affected shipment of imported components for the Katepally mixing plant as well as export order deliveries.
Chaff material payload production remains dependent on imports, exposing the company to prevailing conditions in source countries.

subsections.label: Apollo Micro Systems acquisition
points: Recent acquisition by Apollo Micro Systems viewed as a significant milestone in Premier Explosives' growth journey, opening exciting new opportunities.

Partnership combines Apollo's strengths in defense electronics and mission-critical systems with Premier's capability in energetic materials, rocket motors, ammunition and propulsion systems, creating a broader, more integrated defense platform.

Strategic benefits for Premier include enhanced access to larger and more complex defense programs, stronger technology and R&D capabilities, wider customer reach, and improved operational efficiencies through scale and collaboration.
Combined strengths expected to strengthen Premier's position in India's growing defense indigenization and export opportunities.
Management expects the partnership to accelerate Premier's next phase of growth, strengthen competitive positioning, and create long-term value for stakeholders.

On potential naval-side order traction (given Apollo's relations with Navy, including sea mines and submarine orders), management is hopeful the association will strategically strengthen the company, but the total potential will only be known by December.

Apollo's expertise lies in defense electronics, an area where Premier currently has no expertise; company expects to gain benefits from integrating electronics with high-energy materials systems; more details expected to be shared next quarter.

subsections.label: Headwinds impacting Q1 FY27
points: Revenue impacted by delays in dispatches and project execution, primarily due to ongoing global headwinds and supply chain disruptions across certain programs.
Profitability impacted by elevated raw material costs amid prevailing global market conditions, creating temporary margin pressure.

Management believes many external headwinds are gradually easing as supply chains stabilize and execution improves, expecting stronger operational performance and better revenue conversion in coming quarters.
Export license delays contributed to Defense & Space segment revenue decline; most licenses have since been received.
Land parcel pricing for Andhra Pradesh facility remains an unresolved issue pending government response.

Bulk explosives business faces intense competition (40+ players) and thin-to-negative margins driven by raw material input cost volatility, making the segment difficult to guide beyond the current year.
Export licensing process for new international orders requires the importing country to first issue an import license, adding a structural time lag (minimum 3-4 months) to order execution.

subsections.label: Revenue and margin guidance
points: Management reiterated a target of around INR600 crores turnover for FY27, described as a considerable increase over the previous 1-2 years.
EBITDA target retained at 15%-20% for the financial year, same guidance as prior quarters, expected to be achieved via improving dispatch mix as raw material costs normalize.
Capacity for flares and other in-house-manufactured products is available to support the INR600 crores target; only chaff items remain import-dependent and thus subject to external supply conditions.
Given order book of INR1,393 crores (about 3.5-3.6x FY26 revenue), company expects an execution run rate of INR500-600 crores (targeting INR600 crores) over the next 12-18 months.

key_takeaways: During Q1 FY '27, we reported revenue of INR102.6 crores, reflecting a decline of 28% year-on-year.
The quarter was impacted by delays in dispatches and project execution, primarily due to ongoing global headwinds and supply chain disruptions across certain programs.
On the profitability front, operating performance was impacted by elevated raw material costs amid prevailing global market conditions.

Encouragingly, we believe that many of these external headwinds are gradually easing as supply chain stabilize and execution improves, we expect a stronger operational performance and better revenue conversion in the coming quarters.
As of today, our order book stands at INR1,393 crores with approximately 94% of the order book coming from Defense segment.
Regarding the recent acquisition by Apollo Micro Systems, we believe this marks a significant milestone in Premier Explosive's growth journey and opens up exciting opportunities for the company.

Our EBIT for Q1 FY '27 de-grew by 80% year-on-year to INR4.8 crores. The EBIT margin for the quarter stands at 4.7%. Our net profit decreased by 80% year-on-year to INR3 crores. The PAT margin for the quarter stands at 3%.

We remain confident that supported by sustained execution momentum, continued development of new products and our ongoing expansion initiatives, the company will continue to maintain a strong growth trajectory in the forthcoming quarters.

quarters.summary: Q4 FY26 revenue grew 20% YoY to INR89.2 crores with Defense & Space contributing 76% of revenue (up 43% YoY); FY26 revenue degrew 7% to INR388.3 crores due to lower chaffs & flares execution vs FY25 and elevated raw material prices. Order book stands at a record INR1,569 crores (4.04x FY26 revenue), providing strong medium-term visibility, with FY27 revenue guidance of INR600-700 crores at 15-20% margins, contingent on resolving raw-material and execution constraints.

subsections.label: Other income drivers
points: Other income increase (INR13 crores Q4 FY26, INR42 crores FY26) is one-off in nature, not recurring, and was the last such instance per CFO.

Driven by deferred payments/deliveries being cleared and discounts negotiated with vendors/suppliers for delays caused by non-delivery of items; expenses passed off due to these delays resulted in price discounts.

subsections.label: LD (Liquidated Damages) reversal
points: Company is still pursuing LD reversal with the Ministry of Defence (MOD) on the July '23 chaffs and flares order.
Chaffs order execution completed; a small portion of flares order execution remains, expected to be completed in Q1 of current financial year.
Pending LD reversal claim amount is around INR30 crores; company always claims for the largest amount and final approval will determine actual receipt.

subsections.label: Capex plan
points: FY26 capex incurred was close to INR28 crores.

Total capex requirement for Katepally expansion and PDK combined earlier indicated at INR45 crores + INR15 crores; PDK flare production plant already completed and productionized in FY25; balance PDK capex relates to new mixers, storage facilities, and magazines under construction.

Katepally RDX and HMX plant expansion project ongoing; large planetary mixer and supporting equipment/magazines construction ongoing; some capitalization expected by end of Q1; full qualification of plant and product may extend completion to Q3 FY27 due to explosives qualification requirements.
Remaining FY27 capex reconfirmed as same number given previously (~INR32 crores, i.e., INR60 crores total minus INR28 crores already spent).

subsections.label: Order book composition & visibility
points: Highest ever order book at INR1,569 crores, representing 4.04x FY26 revenue, providing strong medium-term visibility.

Consistent execution during the quarter strengthened positioning, enabling securing of larger and strategically significant contracts from Ministry of Defense, domestic defense players, and international customers.
Healthy order momentum continues across key product categories including chaffs and flares, rocket motors, and other defense systems, further strengthening the order pipeline.

Order book expected to continue at similar levels going forward as new facilities at Katepally and other locations come online and additional negotiated orders materialize (~INR1,000 crores plus in negotiation).

subsections.label: Export order dynamics and license risk
points: An INR18.9 crores order received in February was canceled in April because export license was not granted.

Export license approval is government-policy dependent and can be rejected depending on government policy and the destination country; this risk exists for large orders including the recently won INR350.23 crores order.
Typical time from order receipt to export license clearance ranges from 3 to 6 months, though management acknowledged some orders pending over a year.

Of ~INR800 crores in export orders, more than INR400 crores are in development stage (subject to milestone-based invoicing) and about INR400 crores are awaiting export licenses; all licenses for these orders are already secured according to management, with the pending portion being in development/execution stage rather than lacking licenses.
Export license clarity for the new INR350 crores order expected in approximately 3 months.

subsections.label: October 2025 order (INR430 crores) execution status
points: Execution on the INR430 crores order won in October 2025 has just started, following completion of a prior emergency procurement order.
Approximately two-thirds of the INR430 crores order value expected to be completed before end of FY27, with the remaining one-third flowing into the following year.

subsections.label: Pending dispatch / inspection status
points: No fixed deadline for running orders beyond internal balance accounting systems; deliveries depend on defense pre-dispatch inspection (PDI) completion.
Recently completed a PDI covering three different lines worth around INR30 crores, offered for inspection and dispatched in April.
Further quantities offered for inspection in June, with completion expected in Q1 of the current financial year.

subsections.label: Chaffs & Flares order execution
points: July '23 chaffs and flares order: chaffs execution fully completed; flares execution has a small portion remaining, expected to complete in Q1 of current financial year.
New chaffs and flares orders being negotiated; some RFPs already participated in and awaiting outcome, indicating continued order momentum in this category.

subsections.label: QRSAM order potential
points: Company is ready to take an order under the QRSAM program (expected to finalize soon) but timing is uncertain; QRSAM order inflow is not included in current estimates/guidance.

subsections.label: Defense & Space performance drivers
points: Q4 FY26 revenue performance driven primarily by strong momentum in Defense & Space segment.
FY26 overall revenue impacted due to execution of a larger volume of high-value chaffs and flares orders occurring in FY25, with execution timing affecting FY26 performance.
Operating profitability for both quarter and full year impacted by elevated raw material prices amid prevailing global tensions, a challenge experienced across the industry.

subsections.label: Domestic missile motor programs (LRSAM, MRSAM, Astra)
points: Company supplies solid propellants for LRSAM, MRSAM and Astra missile programs but not the entire rocket motor (excludes electronics guidance systems and seekers).
Execution of domestic orders from BDL and DRDO depends on free-issue materials (FIMs) supplied by these agencies; company cannot execute independently without FIM availability.
As FIMs arrive, company completes and delivers products; current run-rate is around 50 units/month across different motor types (LRSAM, MRSAM, Astra, etc.).

subsections.label: ISRO service contract
points: ISRO revenue is approximately INR18 crores per annum and is expected to remain more or less constant.
Contract has about 2.5 years of remaining life, running to around H2 FY29.
Future renewal/RFP participation expected after contract completion or during the last year of execution.

subsections.label: Jagdalpur O&M contract loss
points: Company lost the current running O&M contract for Jagdalpur plant (associated with Agni Missile propellant service) in bidding due to rising costs; a new contractor quoted lower and won the order.
Company continues to supply pyrogen igniters and other products made in its own plant for the Agni Missile program and remains the single source to DRDO for those items.

subsections.label: Andhra Pradesh land acquisition for defense manufacturing facility
points: Company is in discussions with the Andhra Pradesh government for acquisition of a 400-acre land parcel to establish a dedicated defense manufacturing facility.

Land parcel has been identified and selected from among 5-6 different parcels shown by the government; pricing negotiation is ongoing at Secretary level, with company seeking a discounted price versus government's quoted amount.

Once land price is finalized and a demand note is received, land acquisition activity will start; commissioning expected within 1 to 1.5 years given the large order book that can be executed through this facility.

subsections.label: Katepally plant expansion and incident recovery
points: Katepally incident (accident ~1.5 years back) affected production capability of large rocket motors made for ISRO and strategic systems of DRDO.
RDX and HMX plant expansion at Katepally is ongoing but not yet completed; large planetary mixer and supporting balancing equipment, plus magazines, are still under construction.
Equipment is under fabrication and building under construction; expected to reach commissioning stage by September, with production expected to start from November onward.

Full qualification of the plant and qualification of the product produced (industry requirement in explosives business) will take an additional 1-2 months after execution/commissioning completion, potentially pushing full completion to Q3 FY27.

subsections.label: Peddakandukur flares plant recommissioning
points: Flares production plant, where an accident occurred approximately 1.5 years back, has been recommissioned and is now producing.
Licenses that were suspended have been reinstated/given, and the plant is now producing; dependence on imports for flares components has reduced as a result.

subsections.label: Odisha capex plan
points: Previously identified Orissa land parcel was found unsuitable upon personal site visit; company informed the Orissa government, which is proposing new alternative areas.
Management held a video conference with Orissa government officials on the call day to discuss alternative land parcels; still hopeful of finding suitable land for future expansion.
Expansion plan structured in 3 phases: first phase already underway in Andhra Pradesh (closer location); second and third phases planned for Odisha, expected to take around 4 to 5 years.

subsections.label: Safety and automation investments
points: Following the two plant incidents in the last financial year, company has incorporated more automation, safety control equipment, and remote operations in new facilities and plants to mitigate recurrence risk.

subsections.label: Export vs domestic mix outlook
points: Revenue mix for FY27 expected to be approximately INR200 crores export and INR500 crores domestic against total guidance of INR600-700 crores.
Distribution across quarters is expected to vary, driven by inspection/dispatch timing and import dependency for some raw materials causing delays.
Majority of current export orders are development orders which convert into larger production orders once completed.

subsections.label: Raw material availability constraints
points: Operating profitability in Q4 and FY26 was impacted by elevated raw material prices amid prevailing global tensions, a challenge experienced across the industry.

Land mines, drone/loitering munition payloads, and medium-caliber ammunition production were slowed due to non-availability of raw material; Munitions India Limited (MIL) informed inability to meet requirements for high explosives needed for land mines.
Company took the matter to DRDO (technology provider) proposing an in-house-produced alternate raw material; DRDO initially refused but has since accepted to test it, with trials ongoing.
Testing/trials for the alternate raw material expected to complete in a month or two, after which production can resume with DRDO permission.

Dependence on imports for flares components has reduced following recommissioning of the in-house flares plant, though company remains dependent on imports for some other raw materials, with delays affecting deliveries due to geopolitical conditions and ship movement disruptions.

subsections.label: Competitive positioning
points: Premier continues to occupy a unique strategic position as the only Indian company qualified to manufacture countermeasures, and as the key exporter of fully assembled rocket motors.
Diversified portfolio across warheads, mines and ammunition reinforces contribution towards India's defense indigenization objectives.

Industry consolidation is occurring alongside new entrants (including in Andhra Pradesh); management notes establishing an explosive manufacturing unit or storage facility takes at least 5 years minimum, providing a durable competitive moat.

Company is well entrenched in the rocket motor business with export orders, and is focusing further on land mines, drone/loitering munition payloads, and medium-caliber ammunition where demand has grown due to recent conflicts.
Company was among the first to manufacture chaffs and flares domestically, which were previously largely imported by Indian Armed Forces, and has backward integrated many components.

subsections.label: Rocket motor scope
points: Company currently supplies solid propellants and rocket motor casings/components (hardware) but not full rocket motors including electronics guidance systems and seekers for domestic missile programs (MRSAM, LRSAM, Astra).
For export purposes, company does produce the full rocket motor and would participate in full rocket motor opportunities domestically if available.

subsections.label: Partnerships and MoUs
points: Company has one active joint venture company (with NIBE for global ammunition).

Multiple strategic memoranda of understanding (MoUs) signed with various companies, particularly in the drones and loitering munitions space, where Premier supplies payloads to drone-producing companies.
Company is actively developing new products expected to generate healthy order inflow in coming quarters.

key_figures.label: Export license expected timeline for INR350 crores order

subsections.label: Execution and safety risk
points: Two plant accidents occurred in the last financial year — the flares manufacturing facility (Peddakandukur) and the Katepally facility — affecting production capability and delivery timelines.

Flares facility is the sole domestic source for Indian Air Force requirements and holds multiple orders, so the accident's impact on deliveries was significant; company had to import components it normally produces itself, and imports were further affected by geopolitical conditions and ship movement disruptions.

Mitigation includes recommissioning of the flares plant (now producing without import dependence) and incorporation of more automation, safety control equipment, and remote operations in new facilities.

subsections.label: Raw material dependency risk
points: Raw material unavailability (notably high explosives for land mines from Munitions India Limited) delayed execution of land mines, loitering munitions, and medium-caliber ammunition orders.
Alternate raw material proposed by company is under DRDO testing; approval pending, creating uncertainty on timing for resuming full production in these product categories.

subsections.label: Export license risk
points: Export license approval is government-policy dependent and can be rejected based on government policy and destination country, creating risk for large export orders including the recently won INR350.23 crores order.
An INR18.9 crores order was cancelled in April after failing to receive an export license, illustrating this risk materializing.

subsections.label: Free-issue material (FIM) dependency risk
points: Execution of domestic orders from BDL and DRDO depends on receipt of free-issue materials (FIMs) from these agencies; company cannot execute independently without FIM availability, creating delivery pendency.

subsections.label: Contract loss risk
points: Company lost the Jagdalpur O&M service contract in competitive bidding as its costs had risen and could not match the new lower-cost contractor's quote.

subsections.label: FY27 growth drivers
points: FY27 growth expected to be driven by execution of products delayed in the previous financial year due to geopolitical conditions, and by new areas — land mines, payloads for drones/loitering munitions, and medium-caliber ammunition — which were previously constrained by raw material non-availability.
Alternate raw material is now found and accepted by company designers; DRDO testing of the alternate material ongoing, with production expected once approved.

Guidance not viewed as aggressive relative to the order book of over INR1,500 crores; company will 'try our best' to achieve it, factoring in overcoming last year's war/conflict-related raw material problems.
Run-rate based view: FY27 target considered achievable per management despite acknowledged execution risk from past plant incidents.

subsections.label: Prior guidance context
points: In the February 2026 call, management had guided toward reaching INR500 crores in revenue, but FY26 actual revenue came in at close to INR390 crores, below that prior guidance, due to multiple factors including raw material availability issues (MIL inability to supply, DRDO alternate material acceptance delay) for mines, loitering munitions and flares.

key_takeaways: During Q4 FY26, we delivered a healthy revenue performance, driven primarily by strong momentum in our Defense & Space segment. The segment contributed 76% of the overall revenue at INR67.7 crores and registered an impressive growth of 43% year-on-year.

For FY26, revenue performance was impacted due to the execution of a larger volume of high-value chaffs and flares orders in financial year '25, with execution timing affecting the overall performance during the year.
Operating profitability for both the quarter and the full year was impacted by elevated raw material prices amid prevailing global tensions, a challenge that was experienced across the industry.
Highest ever order book stands at INR1,569 crores, representing 4.04x of FY26 revenue and providing strong medium-term visibility.
In April, we secured a major export order worth INR350.23 crores from international clients for the supply of defense products.
We are currently in discussions with Andhra Pradesh government for acquisition of a 400-acre land parcel to establish a dedicated defense manufacturing facility.

Premier continues to occupy a unique strategic position as the only Indian company qualified to manufacture countermeasures. And as the key exporter of fully assembled rocket motors, our diversified portfolio across warheads, mines and ammunition further reinforces our contribution towards India's defense indigenization objectives.

The revenue from operations for Q4 FY26 grew by 20% year-on-year to INR89.2 crores. Our EBIT for Q4 FY26 grew by 35% year-on-year to INR9.6 crores. Our net profit increased by 78% year-on-year to INR6.6 crores.
The revenue from operations for FY26 degrew by 7% to INR388.3 crores. Our EBIT per FY26 grew by 42% year-on-year to INR69.3 crores. Our net profit increased by 61% year-on-year to INR45.8 crores.

BBOX.about: AGC Networks Ltd. (AGC), incorporated in 1986 by Tata Telecom Pvt. Ltd. to manufacture telecommunication equipment. It is currently held by Essar Telecom Ltd. Over the years, AGC evolved into an information and communication (ICT) solutions provider and integrator with a differentiated vertical approach in business communication systems, applications and services mainly within India.The company is present at multiple geographies such as Middle East, Africa, North America, Australia, New Zealand, Singapore, Philippines and UK servicing over 8000+ customers. quarters.summary: Black Box delivered its highest-ever quarterly revenue in Q1 FY27, up 24% YoY, with EBITDA up 38% YoY and margin expansion of 90bps to 9.3%, on the back of a record order backlog of ~US$950 million (up 83% YoY) and new hyperscaler wins including a US$131 million order. Management guided for FY27 revenue of INR7,800-8,000 crores, EBITDA of INR725-750 crores, EBITDA margin of 9.3%-9.4%, PAT of INR300-325 crores, order bookings of US$1.3-1.4 billion and order backlog of US$1.3-1.4 billion by March 2027, reiterating the FY30 aspiration of an INR18,000 crores/US$2 billion revenue company, with management indicating that a large part of the current order backlog will convert into revenue growth spilling into FY28.

subsections.label: Transformation priorities
points: Over the last three years, transformation centered around five priorities: strengthening the balance sheet, improving profitability, disciplined capital allocation, simplifying operations and building a scalable operating model.
Quality of business is now fundamentally stronger, providing a solid platform to capitalize on opportunities ahead.

subsections.label: Margin drivers
points: EBITDA margin expansion of 90bps reflects operating leverage, better business mix, disciplined execution and benefits of structural initiatives implemented over the last few years.

Operational efficiencies through global capability center in Bengaluru, AI-led productivity initiatives, centralized delivery, procurement discipline and stronger project controls continue to support margin improvement.
Company continues to invest in sales organization, engineering capabilities and delivery teams even while margins expand.

subsections.label: Organic vs inorganic revenue
points: Of the INR1,719 crores total revenue, 2S (Brazil) contributed around INR60 crores; all balance revenue is organic.
2S Q1 (June quarter) is normally weak for them as they are a networking/Cisco partner business.

subsections.label: Cash flow
points: Cash flow continues to be a key management priority; operating cash flow to EBITDA conversion expected to improve meaningfully over FY26, supported by disciplined working capital management.
Large investments in talent/people to secure the order book and convert pipeline into orders are largely done; company will continue to hire but at a more measured pace.
Operating cash flow expected to turn positive with the cash flow cycle picking up automatically as growth continues.

subsections.label: Capital allocation
points: Capital allocation philosophy remains unchanged, focused on long-term value creation across three priorities: strengthening people and technology capabilities, supporting working capital requirements of the growing business, and pursuing selective acquisitions that enhance capabilities and geographic reach.
2S acquisition reflects this disciplined approach.

subsections.label: Tax rate
points: Currently low tax rate primarily due to past operating losses carried forward in various geographies.
Tax rate depends on revenue mix across geographies and consumption of past operating losses.

subsections.label: Backlog composition and conversion
points: Backlog reflects a growing share of large multi-year and mission-critical infrastructure programs.

Growth in backlog is spilling into FY28 because execution of these large gigawatt-plus projects requires preplanning; e.g., a recently announced hyperscaler order will only start ground work (hiring etc.) from November onwards, then scale up.

Order backlog guidance of US$1.3-1.4 billion for FY27 end may be conservative since more orders will likely be added between October/November and March as current backlog of $950 million gets burned into revenue; clarity expected after Q2 results.

subsections.label: Demand drivers
points: Demand remains healthy across AI-led digital infrastructure, data centers, enterprise networking, managed services and cybersecurity.

subsections.label: Data center vs. non-data center business
points: Hyperscale cycle is currently larger; non-hyperscale enterprise expected to grow at modest double-digit ~10%, combined blend ~25%.

subsections.label: TPS / product business (Technology Product Solutions)
points: Product business revenue up but EBIT losses have also increased; management attributes this to a matter of scale.
Company has narrowed focus to mission-critical infrastructure products, particularly visualization products (KVM, Emerald product), seeing strong momentum expected to show through in coming quarters.
Investing in next-generation AI-led products in this space.
Expect ~20% growth this year, still lagging overall company growth plans but highly accretive; expect the product business to become accretive overall as it scales into next year and beyond.

subsections.label: Customer portfolio quality
points: Transitioned from a fragmented customer base to ~300 strategic accounts including hyperscalers, enabling greater wallet share, stronger revenue visibility and healthier margins.

Company has rationalized several low-value long-tail customer accounts while increasing focus on larger strategic enterprises to improve quality, visibility and profitability of revenue base over the long term.

subsections.label: Industry landscape
points: Company describes the current period as one of the largest digital infrastructure investment cycles in history, a structural transformation powered by AI, cloud computing, networking, cybersecurity and next-gen digital infrastructure expected to reshape industries and economies over the coming decade.

Convergence of multiple long-term technology trends: AI workloads driving unprecedented compute demand; enterprise networks being modernized through high-speed connectivity, edge computing, private 5G, Wi-Fi 7; cybersecurity becoming increasingly mission-critical.
Majority of hyperscaler spending occurs in markets where Black Box already has strong positions, particularly the United States.

subsections.label: Competitive moat / right to win
points: Success in the market increasingly depends on execution capability, scale experience and ability to mobilize skilled resources quickly across multiple locations rather than lowest price.
Black Box is the only India-origin digital infrastructure solutions company currently executing gigawatt-scale data center programs.
Number of players who can operate at scale globally is limited; moat is scale, capability, relationship and execution track record already demonstrated (executed close to a gigawatt cumulatively).
Company believes its 'push rate' (having to pitch) is reducing while its 'pull rate' (being invited to bid) is increasing due to demonstrated execution.
Growth can come via participating in market growth, taking share from competitors, or acquisitions; company is focused on participating in growth given the scale of the opportunity.

subsections.label: Customer relationships
points: Works with leading hyperscalers, Fortune 500 enterprises, financial institutions, healthcare organizations, manufacturers, global technology companies across more than 35 countries.
Deep embedding within customers' mission-critical environments seen as creating opportunity to expand wallet share as customers increase AI-led infrastructure investment.
Customers increasingly consolidating spending with trusted partners capable of delivering at scale.

subsections.label: Semiconductor / adjacency exploration
points: Management evaluating adjacencies such as compute/storage partnerships (not manufacturing) as a natural extension of connectivity/network stack for enterprise customers; hyperscalers are different.
Viewed as a potential opportunity to expand addressable spend/TAM; currently focused on areas of hyper growth already engaged in, but continuing to evaluate.

subsections.label: India / Asia market
points: India going through a hyper investment cycle; company is in conversation and evaluating opportunities in Europe and looking at India's potential.
Company has not yet started to harness the Indian market, which it is planning to do.

subsections.label: Four growth pillars (FY30 roadmap)
points: Growth aspiration supported by four pillars: hyperscale digital infrastructure, GSI Americas, growth across India and Rest of World markets, and evolution of technology product solutions business towards recurring and platform-led revenues.
These pillars reinforced by strong execution excellence.

subsections.label: 2S Brazil acquisition
points: Recently completed Brazil acquisition (2S) adds approximately US$50 million in annual revenue.

In addition to strengthening presence in Brazil, expands capabilities across networking, cybersecurity and managed services while providing a strategic platform to participate in the broader Latin American opportunity.
As with every acquisition, focus remains on disciplined integration and realizing long-term synergies.
2S Q1 contribution of INR60 crores reflects two months of consolidation; June quarter is typically weak for 2S given its networking/Cisco partner business.

subsections.label: M&A engine
points: Inorganic growth to be achieved by leveraging proven M&A engine, successful integration track record and a healthy acquisition pipeline.

subsections.label: Workforce scaling
points: Company continues to hire and train talent at scale, with plans to onboard nearly 2,000 professionals to ensure resources required to support customers' long-term growth plans.
These investments create significant barriers to entry and position the company favorably as customers consolidate spending with trusted scaled partners.

subsections.label: Execution and timing risk
points: Large orders require preplanning before ground work/hiring can start (e.g., new hyperscaler order work will start only from November onward), meaning growth from current backlog is expected to spill into FY28.
Guidance assumes normal execution timelines and no significant customer-led delays.

subsections.label: Hyperscaler capex moderation risk
points: Question raised on whether moderation in hyperscaler data center capex could put the company at risk of order cancellations; management believes the overall scale of AI infrastructure spend (~US$1.6 trillion over next four years, ~US$400 billion average annual) is gigantic and the company has captured only a fairly small slice of the addressable market.

Management does not see growth being hampered even if there is a shift or delay/revamp at a specific hyperscaler site, given diversification across multiple hyperscale/colocation customers, multiple sites and multiple geographies.

subsections.label: Competitive intensity risk
points: Question raised on potential risk from IT companies also providing such services; management noted the number of players who can operate at this scale and globally is limited, and bidding is not primarily price-based for hyperscalers.

subsections.label: Guidance context
points: Historically Q1 has been a relatively softer quarter for Black Box; stronger revenue conversion and operating leverage expected in H2 FY27, supporting delivery of the FY27 guidance.
Guidance assumes normal execution timelines and no significant customer-led delays.

Company remains focused on profitable growth, disciplined capital allocation, operational excellence and balance sheet strength, supported by healthy order backlog, improving customer quality and favorable industry tailwinds.

Q4 FY27 EBITDA margin expected to be in the 10%+ range or more, even as full-year guidance is 9.3%-9.4%, due to planned investments in talent/training for large-scale project execution during the year.
Company reiterated FY30 aspiration of building Black Box into an INR18,000 crores / US$2 billion revenue company.

Management indicated FY27 revenue guidance may look conservative but noted that a large part of current order backlog execution is expected to spill into FY28, implying FY28 growth will be over and above FY27 numbers.
Order backlog guidance for FY27 end (US$1.3-1.4 billion) may itself be conservative as more orders are expected to be added between October/November and March; more clarity expected after Q2 results.

key_takeaways: We have delivered our highest ever quarterly revenue, supported by improved execution of the rising order backlog and the contribution from our recently acquired Brazilian entity, 2S.

The quarter also saw our order bookings of US$339 million, taking our order backlog to a record ever of approximately US$950 million, up 83% year-on-year and providing strong visibility for future growth.

We made significant operational progress during the quarter, adding a new global hyperscaler in the United States through a US$131 million, about INR1,240 crores order while continuing to deepen our relationship with our existing hyperscalers.
Black Box is the only India origin digital infrastructure solutions company currently executing gigawatt scale data center programs.

Quarter one of FY27 was one of our strongest quarters as we reported highest ever revenue of INR1,719 crores, representing a 24% year-on-year growth. EBITDA increased to INR160 crores, up 38% year-on-year, while profit after-tax grew to INR56 crores, an increase of 18% over the corresponding quarter last year.

EBITDA margin expanded by 90 basis points to 9.3%, reflecting operating leverage, a better business mix, disciplined execution and the benefits of the structural initiatives implemented over the last few years.
Our aspiration is to build Black Box into an INR18,000 crores or US$2 billion revenue company by FY30.
Based on the visibility we have today, we remain confident in our outlook for FY27.
pressing_questions: If I look at our order backlog and say, for a moment, I exclude projects, which would be longer term in nature, I still see a 38% kind of increase in our order backlog, if I look at managed services, maintenance contracts and products, which is of course very small. So my question here really is that do you think you are being slightly conservative when you guide on '27 numbers? Or is it that you're expecting a lot of growth to maybe start in 3Q and 4Q and which is why the numbers will flow in '28?

I just wanted to touch on the non-data center part of the business because most of the growth that we are talking is coming from that piece. Is the non-data center piece sort of just treading along? Or are you expecting growth? Or is it a case that we are classifying some orders as a data center?

Since a lot of our growth plans hinge on the hyperscaler and data center segment, by any chance that there is some moderation at the hyperscalers' end in terms of data center capex, does that put us at a risk of order cancellations? Or do our growth plans change in that scenario?

What would be potentially a distinctive moat between us and our competitors when it comes to bidding for new orders? And what is our right to win against the others? And is there a potential risk from IT companies to also provide such a service?

subsections.label: Transformation phases
points: Phase 1: Fixing the basics — reduced SG&A costs, consolidated facilities, transitioned subcontractor labour to own workforce, exited thousands of low-value accounts.

Phase 2: Architecting for scale — consolidated 22 ERP systems into a unified technology stack built around SAP, Salesforce and ServiceNow; built GCC in India; centralized key functions and established global governance processes.

Phase 3: Unlocking growth — invested in strategic growth units, expanding partner ecosystem, won hyperscale data center customers, strengthened AI capabilities, and inorganic growth via acquisitions such as 2S in Brazil.
EBITDA margin expansion of 470 bps since FY23 attributed to reduced leverage, GCC in Bengaluru, improved customer mix and strengthened operational efficiency.
Balance sheet strengthened, supported by investment-grade credit ratings; capital raised of ~INR600 crores including substantial promoter participation demonstrating confidence in strategy.
Promoters (Essar, largest shareholder) invested close to INR425 crores through two rounds of capital infusion, reflecting alignment, long-term commitment and confidence in growth trajectory.

subsections.label: Growth focus areas post-transformation

Passion — described as underpinning the belief that Black Box can build the only company operating digital infrastructure at global scale across 35 markets.

subsections.label: Cybersecurity risk landscape
points: Cybersecurity risk is consistently flagged at the top of board risk profiles across organizations; driven by regulatory push (e.g., DPDP, telecom consent regulations) and survival necessity.
AI availability to attackers (spammers/scammers) mirrors its availability to defenders, escalating the cyber threat landscape.
Most organizations want real-time monitoring and want to cover cybersecurity risk but do not necessarily know how to do so — cited as an opportunity as well as a risk.

subsections.label: Execution and safety risk
points: Data center fit-out execution risk emphasized: if projects are not carefully estimated/designed, cost and margin exposure can be significant, particularly in the data center world.

Safety risk managed via 'Road to Zero' initiative with GC partner Turner; zero recordable incidents achieved since the program began just over a year ago (ongoing risk area requiring continued discipline).

subsections.label: World conflicts and tariffs
points: TPS business must navigate an 'ever-changing world of tariffs and other issues that are happening, world conflicts' to maintain a robust and efficient supply of products to customers.

subsections.label: Talent/workforce scaling risk
points: Legacy cabling-contractor workforce (thousands of small companies from the RBOC/AT&T divestiture era) generally not equipped to handle AI-scale, millions-of-connections campuses, creating both a competitive advantage for Black Box and a broader industry talent constraint.
Rapid hiring plan (2,100 additional data center employees in 12 months, workforce growth from ~4,000 to ~7,000) presents scaling and talent-management risk that requires recruitment infrastructure.

subsections.label: $2 billion journey (FY30)
points: Company targets INR12,000 crores (~$1.3 billion organically) in revenue by FY30 with 10%+ EBITDA margin — roughly 2x current overall revenue.

Four growth pillars underpinning the target: hyperscale digital infrastructure, GSI (enterprise) business, technology product (TPS) business scaling from ~$90 million to ~$200 million, and Rest of World/India expansion.
Management frames this as 'a dream with named pillars,' not merely an aspiration, built on the completed transformation foundation.
Remarks explicitly flagged as aspirational and forward-looking per safe harbour statement, and may differ from actual outcomes.

guidance_ledger.statement: FY30, we target INR12,000 crores, about $1.3 billion organically, 10% plus of EBITDA. That's roughly 2x from where we stand today from an overall revenue standpoint.
10% plus of EBITDA margin target for FY30 organic revenue target.
Within our product business, we expect to scale from where we are about $90 million to about $200 million.
Our expectation is that we're going to get to 2x growth over the next between now and FY30 with returning a 10% EBITDA margin target that we've got there.

In the next 12 months, based on what we can foresee and our bookings, allocations, and what's coming down the pipe, we will hire 2,100 additional data center team members to support all of the work that's coming our way.
From 4,000 workforce, we're going to be 7,000 people in the next few years.
The first pillar is the data center opportunity which is out here, which is growing from 1.3 megawatts to 8 megawatts, 42% CAGR.
We are growing today on the data centers about 87 gigawatts to 233 gigawatts by 2030.
We have 40% margins. We're going to grow those over time as I'll talk about here in just a second.

themes.note: Management laid out a FY30 target of ~INR12,000 crores (~$1.3B) revenue with 10%+ EBITDA margin, built on four growth pillars.

themes.label: India market entry and TAM
themes.note: India data center and IT infrastructure opportunity pegged at $7-8 billion combined, with a dedicated three-dimensional GTM strategy under new Rest-of-World leadership.

key_takeaways: At Black Box, the transformation is behind us and growth and scale is ahead of us.

The agenda for today is structured around four things: who we are, the transformation we have done, the market that lies ahead of us, and more importantly, how do we get to $2 billion in revenues by Fiscal '30.
Over INR6,000 crores of revenue in FY26, expanded by 470 basis points, PAT over 9x growth over the last three years' time, return on capital over 34%.
Today, the company carries an order backlog of over $800 million.

EBITDA has more than doubled from INR269 crores in FY23 to INR570 crores in FY26, with margin expansion from 4.3% to 9%. Our order backlog has grown from approximately $500 million to nearly $800 million, providing strong visibility into future revenue streams.

In the next 12 months, based on what we can foresee and our bookings, allocations, and what's coming down the pipe, we will hire 2,100 additional data center team members to support all of the work that's coming our way.

KRBL.about: KRBL is worlds leading basmati rice producer and has fully integrated operations in every aspect of basmati value chain, right from seed development, contract farming, procurement of paddy, storage, processing, packaging, branding and marketing.(Source : 202003 Annual Report Page No:181)

quarters.summary: KRBL delivered record quarterly profitability (highest ever) in Q1 FY27 despite a ~50% decline in export revenue due to Middle East disruption from the Iran-Israel-US conflict, offset by 37% growth in exports to other regions and 14% domestic revenue growth. Management expects export volumes to recover progressively from Q2, maintains guidance of meaningful export growth and ~10% domestic volume growth for FY27, and expects EBITDA margin for the full year at ~17-18% (vs 15% last year) and gross margin at ~30%, cautioning that Q1's exceptionally high margins (36.3% gross, 23.8% EBITDA) are not sustainable.

subsections.label: Margin drivers
points: Gross margin improvement driven by price increases, lower private label exports in the current quarter, and higher other income, partially offset by higher COGS.
EBITDA margin broadly followed gross margin trend but was partially offset by higher proportionate employee costs in the quarter.
QoQ gross profit was higher primarily due to higher other income, higher power revenue and better basmati realization, slightly impacted by higher basmati COGS.
QoQ EBITDA followed the trend in gross profit and further improved as there was an MTM loss on investments and forex revaluation loss shown under other expenses in the preceding quarter.
Management flagged that Q1 margins, while at a high level, are not sustainable — driven by very high prices during the quarter and MTM gains on the investment portfolio.
Rest-of-year margin will depend on how quickly exports scale up (order book exists but supply is constrained in many parts of the world) and on the upcoming paddy season.

subsections.label: Balance sheet
points: Increase in cash plus investments driven by lower net working capital requirement and higher internal accruals in the period.
Inventory levels (rice 389,000 tons) considered a comfortable stock position by management at end of the season.

subsections.label: Domestic business composition
points: Consumer pack and regional rice businesses performed well, while branded rice volumes saw a modest decline due to lower bulk pack sales.

Rice commodity prices moved upwards during the quarter, allowing price increases and higher realizations; the short-term price rise led intermediaries to defer bulk purchases while waiting for greater price stability.

Management views the bulk pack decline as a postponement of volumes rather than structural weakness in demand; demand remains stable and purchases are expected to progressively materialize over coming quarters.

Bulk pack business did not conclude in Q1 but is expected to be factored into Q2; over Q2 and Q3 resumption in bulk pack volumes expected, bringing full-year volume growth back to the ~10% commitment.

subsections.label: Export composition
points: Export revenue decline entirely attributable to the Middle East story; exports to every other region combined grew 37% in the quarter.
India's Basmati export volumes in Q1 were approximately 1.5 million metric tons against 1.7 million in Q1 FY26, with Middle East volumes down about 11% year-on-year.
Basmati realizations for the quarter were approximately 20% higher year-on-year and 13% higher sequentially — a volume shock caused by logistics, not a demand shock caused by buyers.

subsections.label: Modern Trade / traditional trade
points: Competitive intensity remains elevated; market share performance in parts of modern trade needs improvement — gaps identified and being addressed through sharper assortment, pricing, availability and account-level execution.

Overall market share in traditional trade declined by about 2 percentage points over Q1 last year; management stated India Gate enjoys market leadership across ~75% of Indian states but did not have quarter-specific state-level detail on hand.

subsections.label: E-commerce
points: E-commerce operating model has evolved: the team now owns the complete channel P&L including sales, gross margins, contribution margins and investments.

Pricing, performance marketing, availability and city-level execution monitored through an integrated dashboard, enabling faster decisions, stronger accountability and more productive deployment of investments.

subsections.label: Masala portfolio
points: Masala category plays a distinct role — rice is a monthly basket purchase, whereas masalas are consumed across different meals/recipes, helping expand household reach, frequency of consumer interaction, and brand engagement.

Proposition anchored in authenticity of taste and flavor, focusing on popular regional recipes that are complicated to prepare at home; building on success of biryani masala, newly launched ready-to-cook masala range received strong initial response.

subsections.label: Regional rice
points: Demand established and product quality streamlined; focus now on ensuring regular supply and operating stability.

Quick commerce particularly promising for regional rice as the category remains fragmented among regional brands while platforms increasingly require trusted brands offering consistent quality and professional servicing of a fast-moving channel.

Quick commerce platforms (Blinkit, Zepto) have approached KRBL requesting entry into more regional rice varieties since local brands lack the teams/capability to operate on quick commerce diligence, supply chain, pricing and performance marketing requirements; company plans to enter more regional rice categories on quick commerce later this year.

subsections.label: Non-basmati / Poha launch
points: Launched India Gate's Light and Fluffy Poha across 22 cities in North India during Q1; poha seen as a natural adjacency — large, stable category with low branded penetration but strongly growing branded segment.
Right to win in poha comes from sourcing capabilities, supply chain strength, distribution reach and consumer trust in India Gate brand.
Initial response from retailers and consumers encouraging; scaling to be disciplined based on consumer adoption, repeat purchases and quality of economics.

subsections.label: Gangavathi facility
points: New facility at Gangavathi expected to become operational by end of Q3 FY27, supporting the next phase of growth in the regional rice portfolio.

subsections.label: Global & India rice balance
points: Tighter world rice balance sheet than the market was pricing at the start of the calendar year expected to keep rice market firm rather than soft.
India continues to command close to 40% of global rice trade and remains the world's largest rice producer despite lower forecast domestic production.
Monsoon deficiency: Northwest (basmati belt) among deficient regions, with Punjab, Haryana and Western UP running well below normal through June-July.

Basmati belt is largely canal and tube-well irrigated, so rainfall deficit shows up first as higher pumping/input costs rather than lost acreage; however nationally paddy area has fallen more than kharif average, and deficit magnitude carries real yield risk for longer-duration varieties harvested in October-November.
Deficient monsoon on top of an already depleted pipeline expected to firm (not soften) credit prices into the new crop.

subsections.label: 2025 Basmati crop / India vs Pakistan
points: Acreage going into the season was healthy across Punjab, Haryana, Western UP, Rajasthan and parts of MP, with continued adoption of newer pest-resistant Pusa varieties.
Flood in Punjab (late August/early September 2025) destroyed crop outright on ~2 lakh hectares of cultivable land, of which ~60,000 acres was basmati.

Quality was a second issue: mildly/partially affected areas carried higher moisture, greater discolouration and lower milling recovery, while unaffected belts (Rajasthan, Western UP, parts of MP) delivered good grain length and aroma — resulting in a crop that was smaller and sharply segmented, with a wide spread between export-grade material and everything else.
Quality segregation mattered more this season than in many years — an area where KRBL's sourcing network and ageing discipline earns its position.

Basmati paddy prices climbed steadily through the year as the true size of the crop became apparent; by May, old crop paddy availability at major northern trading centres had effectively run out with no replacement until the new crop arrives in October.
Pakistan's crop outcome diverged from early flush reports of major crop loss — final damage assessment was only 5-6%, and Pakistan's economic survey reported production actually up.

Pakistan's supply came through intact but competitiveness eroded — Pakistani basmati traded at a premium versus Indian material with flat currency giving no relief, and government responded with duty drawback rather than price cut, resulting in a fall in Pakistan's export volume and value despite higher prices; India's competitiveness has been reinforced, not eroded.

subsections.label: Middle East disruption (Strait of Hormuz)
points: Conflict involving Iran, US and Israel escalated sharply on 28 February 2026; the Strait of Hormuz has been practically partially open since.
Middle East takes close to three-quarters of Indian basmati exports, making this disruption especially significant for the industry.

Cargo continued moving through Khor-Fakhan (UAE-bound), Jeddah/Saudi Arabia, and Salalah (onward to Qatar, Kuwait, Bahrain), but transshipment added 7-14 days of transit and several hundred dollars per container in handling costs.
Commercial transit through the Strait has begun to resume — described as the most promising reopening since February.
Through the disruption, importers across the region bought hand-to-mouth and deferred forward commitments; as confidence in transit returns, inquiry levels and order books are beginning to rebuild.
Gulf markets have absorbed two quarters of constrained supply; inventories have been drawn down materially and that shock will have to be replaced.
KRBL's customer relationships remain intact, brands hold shelf positions, and company has both inventory and balance sheet strength to serve demand once the route is reliable.

subsections.label: Saudi Arabia distribution strategy
points: Company continues to ship through wholesalers under an interim arrangement while searching for a long-term distribution partner; process ongoing and deliberately selective given cost of appointing a wrong partner far exceeds cost of taking more time.
Selection of a wrong partner in the past set the Saudi entity/VAT transition program back by about 1.5 years.

Own-entity/incorporation program in Saudi has been deferred in favor of finding a distributor; direct wholesale distribution continues in parallel until a new distributor is finalized — management has identified 3-4 candidate distributors and is waiting for regional peace before finalizing one.

subsections.label: U.S. market
points: U.S. market is stable for KRBL, with good business done over the last 3-4 quarters and this quarter; management to assess impact of the 18% U.S. import duty on buying patterns with distributors and channels.

subsections.label: India distribution network
points: India Gate present across ~3.3 lakh retail outlets, reaching ~1.2 crore urban Indian households; focus is on improving distribution quality (deeper direct coverage, stronger outlet execution, greater availability in underpenetrated towns) rather than pure outlet addition.

Distributor management system rolled out across top 190 distributors, which contribute ~65% of consumer pack business in general trade; active adoption improving visibility, governance and execution discipline.
