subsections.label: Supply chain remodeling
points: Second strategic priority is remodeling the supply chain, with fill rates improving to ~90% averaged with ~5-day servicing from PO receipt, working toward a benchmark of at least 95% fill rate with 72-hour servicing.

Broader organizational transformation underway including stronger processes/accountability, end-to-end supply chain excellence, order-to-cash transformation, better dashboards/analytics, faster decision-making with robust governance, and a culture of ownership and performance.

subsections.label: Inventory strategy
points: Company plans to buy more inventory this season versus recent years, given expectations of tighter market conditions, but management stressed inventory purchase decisions depend on market conditions, not merely available cash.
Current stock levels (389,000 tons rice) considered comfortable at end of season.

key_figures.label: India Gate market leadership across states

subsections.label: Brand investment / marketing campaigns
points: Third strategic priority is investing in the India Gate brand: evolving communication and media channels; April Fools' campaign used contemporary humor and popular culture to communicate ageing credentials of India Gate Classic, generating more than 45 million engagements.
Mother's Day and Father's Day campaigns moved beyond conventional greetings to build conversations around Indian values of beauty and sacrifice, together generating more than 90 million views.

Campaigns represent an evolution toward more contemporary, relevant tonality suited to new-age media platforms; these are long-term brand-building investments not evaluated on immediate sales conversion, aimed at strengthening relevance, salience and enduring equity of the India Gate brand.

subsections.label: Competitive positioning
points: India Gate enjoys market leadership position across ~75% of Indian states.

Competitive intensity in modern trade remains elevated; company responding via sharper assortment, pricing, availability and account-level execution while protecting long-term portfolio profitability.
In e-commerce, India Gate exited June with ~41% market share, maintaining a lead of ~10 percentage points over the next largest competitor.

subsections.label: Four strategic priorities (export/overall business)
points: First: disciplined procurement, prioritizing low moisture, high recovery paddy to protect both margins and brand quality — especially important given deficient monsoon this season.
Second: continued premiumization and expansion of the branded portfolio in India and internationally.
Third: deepening position with large global buyers, leveraging India's pricing competitiveness relative to Pakistan.
Fourth: operational efficiency and disciplined capital allocation.

subsections.label: Four strategic priorities (India domestic business)
points: First: democratizing distribution — focus on quality of distribution (deeper direct coverage, stronger outlet execution, greater availability) rather than pure outlet count growth.
Second: remodeling the supply chain (fill rates, servicing times).
Third: investing in the India Gate brand (contemporary campaigns).
Fourth: building the portfolio beyond rice (Poha launch, Masala portfolio expansion).

subsections.label: ED matter
points: Management stated that due to a subdued/ongoing ED (Enforcement Directorate) matter, they will not be able to respond to queries on this matter.

subsections.label: Geopolitical / logistics risk
points: Middle East conflict (Iran-US-Israel) escalated on 28 February 2026, partially closing the Strait of Hormuz — Middle East accounts for close to three-quarters of Indian basmati exports.
Freight rates rose more than tenfold from ~US$500 to as much as US$5,000 per container at peak disruption; transshipment routes added 7-14 days of transit and added handling costs.
Container space and equipment availability issues continue to slow movement even as the route partially reopens.

subsections.label: Monsoon / crop risk
points: IMD revised seasonal forecast down to ~90% of normal, with below-normal rainfall expected in August and September; cumulative rainfall running ~11% below long period average as of 5 August 2026.

Northwest basmati belt (Punjab, Haryana, Western UP) running well below normal rainfall through June-July; reservoir shortage nationally ~27% below last year in early August; all-India paddy acreage ~4% lower than last year as on 7 August.

Deficit magnitude carries real yield risk for longer-duration varieties harvested in October-November, even though basmati belt's canal/tube-well irrigation means the deficit shows up more as higher input/pumping costs than lost acreage.
New crop size still a question mark because rains came quite late; management expects clarity within 10 days (by 25 August) on crop size.

subsections.label: Margin sustainability risk
points: Management explicitly flagged that Q1 gross/EBITDA margins are not sustainable at current levels, driven by high prices and one-off MTM gains.

subsections.label: Legal / regulatory matter
points: ED (Enforcement Directorate) matter — management declined to respond to queries on this matter, citing it as subdued/ongoing.

subsections.label: Market share risk
points: Market share performance in parts of modern trade needs improvement amid elevated competitive intensity; traditional trade market share declined ~2 percentage points YoY in Q1.

subsections.label: U.S. import duty
points: 18% U.S. import duty now settled; company assessing impact on buyer purchasing patterns with distributors and channels.

EBITDA margin improvement expected vs last year

subsections.label: Export outlook
points: Export shortfall of Q1 characterized as a timing issue, not a structural one — customers and order pipeline remain intact; destination inventories drawn down and non-Middle East export business grew 37% amid disruption.
Export volumes expected to recover progressively from Q2, provided shipping conditions in West Asia continue to stabilize; company maintaining guidance of meaningful export growth for the full year.

Q2 export outlook: route is now partially open with shipments moving, though container space/equipment availability issues persist; demand is picking up and bulk business is expected to resume to some extent in Q2, with export numbers expected to be better sequentially.

Pakistani premium and freight cost pass-through: benchmark shelf prices in the Middle East have increased, allowing pass-through of extra freight costs and rice price increases if freight rates persist for another couple of months.

subsections.label: Margin outlook
points: Full-year margin will depend on how quickly exports scale up (order book exists but supply constrained in many regions) and on the upcoming paddy season.

Management's general view: margin should be slightly better than last year, quantified as about 1-2% better at EBITDA level, i.e., between 17% and 18% EBITDA margin, and about 30% gross margin for the year.

subsections.label: Domestic business outlook
points: Domestic outlook for FY27 remains positive; confident of ~10% growth in domestic volumes, supported by continued growth in consumer packs, expansion of regional rice, normalization in bulk packs, and stronger execution across channels.
This 10% domestic volume growth is the multi-year (2-3 year) commitment as well, not just FY27-specific.

subsections.label: Pricing outlook
points: Basmati prices already at the higher end of the possible bandwidth; no further price hikes planned within Q2; company to wait and watch the paddy crop season unfold before calibrating further price hikes by segment in Q3.

If peace process completes and Middle East markets fully reopen, prices are expected to increase further, though tempered by demand elasticity (staple food) and freight cost increases; new crop size (arriving from first week of September) remains uncertain and will influence pricing, with clarity expected around 25 August.

guidance_ledger.statement: We expect export volumes to recover progressively from the second quarter and we are maintaining our guidance and meaningful export growth for the full year.
For financial year '27, our outlook remains positive, and we are confident of delivering approximately 10% growth in domestic volumes.
Our outlook on the India market remains positive with a 10% domestic volume growth year-on-year, and that's the number we kind of commit to for the upcoming 2 to 3 years as well.
In general, the margin should be slightly better than last year; we would say between 17% to 18% is what we are looking at right now.
For the current year, we look at about 30% gross margin and about 17% to 18% EBITDA margin.

Regional rice, we've grown at 25% in Quarter 1, and that is the kind of target we had projected for the start of the financial year; our objective is to maintain that throughout the subsequent quarters for the rest of the financial year.

guidance_ledger.metric: Masala portfolio annualized revenue run rate
guidance_ledger.statement: We are targeting an annualized revenue run rate of approximately INR25 crores by the end of the financial year '27 (from ~INR9 crores at end of Q1).
Our new facility at Gangavathi is expected to become operational by the end of quarter 3, supporting the next phase of growth in this portfolio.

We are not going to be taking any more price hikes within quarter 2; we are going to be waiting and watching for the paddy crop season to unfold, and then we will see calibrated which segments can continue price hikes in quarter 3.

If the peace process completes and markets open up, definitely there will be an impact on price — prices are definitely going to shoot further, but limited by demand elasticity and freight costs; new crop size still a question mark, with clarity expected by 25th August.
We'll see better numbers because bulk business will also resume in the second quarter to some extent; export numbers will be much better.
This year, we'll be buying inventory, definitely we'll be buying inventory... this season, naturally, we'll be buying more.
We have identified 3 and 4 distributors and we have to finalize one of them, but we are waiting for the peace to arrive in that region.
USDA forecast India's rice exports to approximately 25 million metric tons in '26-'27, about 1 million tons higher than the previous year.
Domestic realizations of ~80,000/MT are going to remain upwards positive; another 2% to 3% improvement in average realization will be seen in quarter one on the domestic front.
Once the war is settled, exports will double up in next six months because of a big gap in food reserves and expected buffer stock/strategic reserve buying by governments and private trade.
We'll see a healthy double-digit growth in the edible oil category this financial year.
April export numbers seem to be in the same trajectory as Q4, but May and June is something that we need to see.
It is too premature to comment anything on the price; once crop size is known via the All India Rice Export Association mapping exercise, then only we can discuss more on FY27.

We are not caring to monetize that piece of parcel [60 acres], but to develop our own warehousing; any major development decision will be undertaken only after detailed evaluation and necessary approvals.

themes.note: Poha launched across 22 cities, Masala portfolio grew 74% YoY with a run-rate target of INR25 crores by FY27-end, and regional rice grew 25% with quick-commerce push planned.

themes.label: Market share leadership
themes.note: India Gate leads ~75% of Indian states and holds ~41% e-commerce share, but traditional trade share fell ~2pp YoY and modern trade share needs improvement amid competitive intensity.

themes.label: Margin sustainability
themes.note: Record Q1 gross (36.3%) and EBITDA (23.8%) margins flagged by management as not sustainable; full-year guidance of ~30% gross and 17-18% EBITDA margin.

themes.label: Basmati crop & pricing dynamics
themes.note: 2025 Punjab floods cut basmati output 20-25%, segmenting crop quality; deficient monsoon for 2026 crop raises yield risk even as India's pricing advantage over Pakistan strengthens.

key_takeaways: Exports revenue for Q1 FY 2027 stood at INR244 crores against INR485 crores in Q1 FY26, a decline of approximately 50%. That decline is entirely a Middle East story. Exports to every other region taken together grew 37% in the quarter.

Overall revenue for the quarter was INR1,496 crores lower by about 6%. The Company reported EBITDA of INR372 crores on a profit after tax of INR261 crores, the stronger quarterly profitability in the company's history.
We expect export volumes to recover progressively from the second quarter and we are maintaining our guidance and meaningful export growth for the full year.
Domestic revenue, excluding power stood at INR1,221 crores, growing 14% year-on-year.
For financial year '27, our outlook remains positive, and we are confident of delivering approximately 10% growth in domestic volumes.
Gross margin for the quarter stood at 36.3% compared to 25.7% in quarter 1 FY26.
EBITDA margin for the quarter was at 23.8% versus 13.9% in the same period last year.
As the ED matter subdued us, we will not be in a position to respond to queries on this matter.
pressing_questions: Can you please give us first on the update on Saudi Arabia entity as the incorporation and VAT transition process has completed?
With the 18% U.S. import duty now settled, are you seeing any pickup in U.S. basmati volumes or is still not focused market for KRBL?

If you could give us some color on the export market in the sense that if there were to be a scenario where the inventory depletion happens, but the freight cost doesn't come down as much as what we anticipate, do you see a situation where restocking by importers at such high price levels is possible?
Directionally, how is the export number looking for us in the September quarter?
Could you mention 2, 3 states where you have had a significant win in terms of market share and 2, 3 states where you would have probably seen a drop in market share overall?
Could you quantify the margin gains? And also on the MTM investment gains, that is part of other income, right?
In the quarter, volume growth was only 3% while NSR growth was 11%. What's the volume-led growth outlook for the full year, and can you give guidance for next 1-2 years?
Why not go more aggressive and build a broader non-basmati basket instead of evaluating products one by one, given the brand strength and cash flows?

As we understand Hormuz is opening up and exports/domestic sales will pick up, but inventory volumes for the corresponding period over the last 2 years have gone down — can you throw some color on that? Why not spend more cash on buying inventory?
Just give us some regional rice revenue targets and overall revenue targets for this financial year?
In light of the West Asia crisis and rice not moving to these areas, don't you see basmati prices going up overall once the supply gap opens?
How have realizations behaved in this quarter vis-a-vis Q4? And what was the price hike taken in Q1?
Given paddy prices continue to be strong, did we take any more price hike in this quarter, or can we expect more price hikes in the near future?
Is the best gross margin performance in 10-12 quarters just due to lower-cost inventory and price hikes, or is it structurally going to improve?

quarters.summary: KRBL expects export demand and shipment flow to improve meaningfully once Middle East geopolitical conditions stabilize, with management believing exports could double in the next six months post-settlement due to depleted regional food reserves; domestic business targets ~10% volume growth in FY27 with realizations expected to improve further, while export guidance remains unquantifiable given geopolitical uncertainty.

subsections.label: Q4 FY26 P&L drivers
points: Overall revenue for Q4 FY26 was supported by strong domestic branded sales, which partially offset the temporary decline in exports.
Gross margin decline was due to higher COGS and lower other income.
EBITDA margin decline was due to lower gross margin, partially impacted by MTM movements on investments, partially offset by lower other expenses.
PAT for the quarter was roughly flat year-on-year in absolute terms despite margin compression.

subsections.label: FY26 full year drivers
points: Domestic revenue growth of 10% was mainly driven by branded rice volume growth of 8%.
Margin improvement for the full year was mainly due to lower input costs and higher other income.

subsections.label: Balance sheet / inventory
points: Lower inventory is due to both lower per unit cost and lower quantity.
Lower inventory, coupled with higher cash profit generated in FY26, will result in lower net bank debt.
Company carries inventory of aged rice (15 months to 2 years) as well as steam rice sold from the new crop; the crop comes in September-October and selling is a mixture of old and new stock.
Company is sitting on close to INR1,000 crores in cash; no specific update on extraordinary dividend or buyback beyond the approved dividend.

subsections.label: Capital allocation
points: A dividend of 450% of face value (INR103 crores) has been approved by the Board, subject to shareholder approval at the upcoming AGM.

On real estate, primary objective remains treasury optimization and long-term value creation; core rice business remains primary focus; real estate opportunities will be evaluated selectively only where value accretive.
Regarding the Samalkha District Panipat land parcel, various monetization and development options continue to be assessed; approach remains flexible, prudent, return-focused.

subsections.label: Forex / hedging policy
points: Company has a policy to book forward hedges for 80% of what it sells, normally generating a profit of even 0.5% on the foreign exchange side via forward hedging of dollars, to avoid currency risk.
Currently the company still has to cover around $5-6 million, on which it expects to make a profit of 1.5-2% from foreign exchange.
Future sales will be booked at the day's dollar price.

subsections.label: Real estate - Samalkha land parcel
points: Total land area is approximately 130 acres, divided into two portions by the main GT road — one side ~60 acres and other side ~70 acres.
The 60-acre parcel is strategically located and currently intended for KRBL's own warehousing, given a severe space problem at the Barota plant near Sonipat.
Management noted that selling the land today would yield a much bigger profit than developing a warehouse, but business need is prioritized over monetization.
Company has received many real estate opportunities in the last three months but remains unclear whether to invest unless there is a very big opportunity where investment could be doubled.

subsections.label: Domestic business performance
points: Quarter 4 FY26 was the best ever quarter for domestic revenue, driven by 16% rice volume growth and 5% rice realization growth — a healthy combination of volume expansion and value improvement.
Branded non-basmati portfolio continues to grow at a meaningfully faster rate than the overall business, validating the strategic thrust to widen the rice portfolio beyond basmati.
Full year branded basmati growth was driven by consistent volume growth and improving realizations.

Non-basmati business is now a INR271 crores category in just a few years, growing at nearly 4x the rate of the overall domestic business, validating the consumer opportunity in branded quality non-basmati rice.

Despite competitive intensity in some channels, the company has defended and extended market leadership across general trade, modern trade and e-commerce channels — described as market leader across every channel of operation.

Q3 FY26 domestic revenue was broadly flat YoY reflecting competitive intensity and pricing headwinds at that time; Q4 showed a sharp sequential acceleration due to recovery in branded volume growth (flat in Q3 to 16% in Q4), price stabilization improving realizations, and distribution/brand investments translating into top-line outperformance.
Non-basmati maintained its strong growth trajectory regardless of the broader category cycle; management noted the market leader rebounds faster when category conditions improve.

subsections.label: Edible Oil segment
points: Edible oil business is at an early stage; distribution architecture is being put in place and is expected to scale in FY27 as distribution deepens and consumer trials build.
The blended edible oil category (~INR1,600-1,700 crores) is dominated (85-90% share) by a single brand that created the category; building brand equity is seen as a long-term journey.

Company is re-evaluating GTM in general trade specifically; MT/e-commerce continues to show positive signs, but general trade distribution needs ramping up; expecting healthy double-digit growth in the category this financial year.
Supply chain for edible oil is stable, though price volatility has been significant this financial year due to geopolitical volatility; not seen as a major risk given minimal current volumes.

subsections.label: Uplife Health rice range
points: Uplife Health rice range spans brown rice, basmati brown rice, and low GI rice segments, targeting proactive health consumers.
Brand investment and digital campaigns are driving both awareness and trial in this emerging segment.

subsections.label: India Gate Classic Masala meal mixes
points: Launched four new variants in Q4: Kashmiri Dum Aloo Masala, Patiala Paneer Tikka Masala, Purani Dilli Butter Chicken Masala, and Chettinad Chicken Masala, extending the India Gate Classic premium promise into the ready-to-cook segment with regional culinary authenticity.

subsections.label: Market share clarification (Q&A)
points: Management clarified that full financial year market share levels were shared, not Q4-specific; based on experience, the trend improved in the latter half of the year, with Q4 market share estimated 100-200 basis points higher across each channel versus last year Q4 (sequential improvement, not a full-year decline).

subsections.label: Export geography impact
points: KRBL, like the broader industry, was impacted by Middle East logistics disruption during Q4, affecting shipments to markets across the region.

Shipping routes have become concentrated through limited operational ports: Khor Fakkan emerged as a major transshipment hub for UAE-bound cargo, Jeddah for Saudi Arabia, Salalah for onward movement into Qatar/Kuwait/Bahrain, while Jordanian routes are increasingly used for Iraq-related trade flows.
Saudi Arabia business continues to progress well with consistent demand and regular shipment movement via Jeddah/Red Sea route, less affected than Kuwait, Bahrain and UAE.
Dubai exports continue via Salalah but quantums are affected and small.

Company is being extremely selective on appointing a Saudi distributor, prioritizing long-term alignment and operational stability over speed, given the financial implications of a wrong partner; current model works directly with wholesalers and Saudi orders are coming in.

subsections.label: Distribution pillar - democratizing distribution
points: Retail footprint has grown to 3.4 lakh outlets across channels, the strongest outlet presence in the packaged basmati category.
Reaching 1.2 crore urban Indian households, a key metric for long-term brand penetration goals.

Focus has sharpened on deepening presence in better quality stores and increasing penetration in under-penetrated towns, with distribution expansion becoming more granular and targeted, particularly through direct coverage investment in towns previously served indirectly.

subsections.label: Supply chain remodeling (distribution-related)
points: Established 16 C&Fs and 8 super stockists to ensure wider and deeper supply across geographies.
Move towards a stronger FOR model (structured go-to-market framework) is driving better serviceability and cost discipline.
Key focus areas include safeguarding against channel infiltration, tighter governance on GTM practices, and driving servicing/cost efficiency in modern trade and e-commerce.
These structural changes are designed to progressively improve service quality and operating margins over the medium term.

subsections.label: Brand investment campaigns (Q4)
points: Quitter Day campaign for Uplife (New Year's), built on the Uplife health philosophy, featuring Smriti Mandhana, Lakshya Lalwani and Ashneer Grover — delivered 139 million views, 113 million reach, 2.1 million engagement, and a contest that garnered 300,000-plus participation.

#NotYourBiryani campaign on Women's Day turned everyday food language into a cultural conversation challenging casual sexism — generated 36 million views, 410,000 shares, 600 stories and wide editorial coverage.

Eid campaign — strategic partnership with Zepto and Blinkit placing India Gate Classic Biryani Masala and India Gate Classic Rice at the heart of Eid celebrations — delivered 28 million reach and 59 million impressions.
Brand investments are building narratives that make India Gate culturally resonant, supporting long-term premiumization and household penetration.

subsections.label: Competitive positioning
points: Company is undisputed market leader across every channel it operates in (general trade, modern trade, e-commerce) and is investing deliberately to protect and expand this position.

Management does not see competitive pressure as a major concern even amid the war-related disruption, citing strong margin cushion on unsold export stock and buyer support for continuity of food supply despite elevated costs.

subsections.label: Strategic priorities for FY27
points: Maintaining leadership in premium branded basmati rice.
Strengthening procurement quality and supply chain efficiency.
Expanding global market reach.

On real estate, primary objective remains treasury optimization and long-term value creation; core rice business remains primary focus; real estate opportunities evaluated only where value accretive and strategically beneficial.

subsections.label: Four domestic strategic pillars
points: Pillar 1: Democratizing distribution — expanding retail footprint and household reach.
Pillar 2: Remodeling supply chain — C&Fs, super stockists, FOR model, GTM governance.
Pillar 3: Investing in the brand — high-impact campaigns reinforcing brand equity and cultural relevance.
Pillar 4: Foraying into new products and categories — meal mixes, edible oil, Uplife health rice range.

subsections.label: Geopolitical disruption - Middle East
points: Escalation of tension involving Iran, the United States and Israel significantly disturbed shipping and logistics across the Middle East during March 2026; considerable cargo remained stuck at Indian and Middle Eastern destination ports during this period, though a large part of shipment issues were gradually resolved during April and May.
KRBL was impacted by this disruption across multiple Middle Eastern markets but managed operational challenges through close coordination with buyers and support from authorities.

Sharp increase in logistics and freight costs across the Middle East; war premiums charged by insurance companies have increased materially and are being applied shipment by shipment depending on destination and route exposure.
Marine insurance coverage remains available, which has been critical for trade continuity.
Buyers across the Middle East have broadly accepted the higher freight environment due to limited alternatives for maintaining food supply continuity in the region.
Inventory levels in several Middle Eastern markets have reduced over the last few months due to shipment disruptions, expected to drive demand replenishment as logistical stability improves.

subsections.label: Basmati crop quality variation
points: Localized flooding and heavy rains in parts of Punjab and Haryana affected moisture levels and milling recovery in some pockets, while other producing regions delivered good grain characteristics, aroma and length, leading to greater segmentation between premium export grade and lower grade supply.

Pakistan basmati crop also experienced similar weather-related disruptions; while early reports pointed to severe flood-related damage, subsequent assessments indicated the overall impact was more localized, with several regions delivering satisfactory grain quality and aroma.

subsections.label: Monsoon risk for 2026 crop season
points: Recent discussions have raised concerns of a potentially deficient monsoon in India for the upcoming 2026 crop season; it is still early to make definitive conclusions, and reservoir levels and monsoon disruptions over the next few months will be critical indicators.
Any meaningful weather disruption could tighten paddy availability and support stronger price realization in the coming season.

subsections.label: ED matter
points: Management stated that as the ED matter is sub judice, they will not be in a position to respond to queries on this matter.

subsections.label: Currency / FX risk
points: Company hedges 80% of what it sells via forward contracts to avoid currency risk, though devaluation could otherwise affect margins; still has to cover $5-6 million currently.

subsections.label: Global and India rice market outlook
points: Global rice stocks are expected to decline in the coming marketing year due to lower production and higher consumption, which may keep the overall rice market relatively firm.
India continues to remain highly competitive internationally despite the tighter global balance sheet.
India expected to comfortably retain its position as the world's largest rice producer despite slightly moderating production due to weather-related concerns and early monsoon uncertainty.
Continued rise in domestic demand coupled with lower global production expectations could support stronger rice pricing trends in the coming year.

subsections.label: Export outlook
points: Exports mainly depend on the geopolitical situation; difficult to comment on near-term trajectory, but a huge gap in food storage/food surplus is foreseen once the Iran issue is resolved, which should create huge pressure on shipments and orders.

Management believes the current Middle East situation is temporary in nature and expects greater clarity in coming weeks; in the interim, shipments continue via alternate ports/routes with higher freight costs, elevated insurance premiums and longer transit times.

Management is confident the geopolitical tension will not persist for months and could reach settlement within days; once war settles, exports could double within the next six months given depleted regional food reserves and expected government/private trade buying to rebuild strategic/buffer food stocks.
April export run-rate appears to be tracking the same trajectory as Q4, but May and June trends remain uncertain; company will not share month-wise numbers.

It is too premature to comment on FY27 basmati pricing; the All India Rice Export Association has commissioned a mapping of total crop size from Punjab to MP/Rajasthan, and pricing commentary will follow once crop size is known.

subsections.label: Domestic outlook
points: Domestic business targeting average 10% volume growth in FY27 across general trade, modern trade and e-commerce, though growth will vary by channel.
Domestic realizations (~INR80,000/MT) expected to remain upward positive, with another 2-3% improvement in average realization expected in Q1 FY27.
No specific volume or margin guidance provided for the export business given prevailing uncertain conditions.
Company is comfortably placed on inventory for FY27 volume build-up in rice-equivalent terms; will build inventory in the coming season based on season pricing and expectation of heavy export demand.

subsections.label: Edible oil outlook
points: Edible oil business expected to see healthy double-digit growth in FY27 as general trade distribution ramps up, alongside continued positive momentum in MT/e-commerce.

guidance_ledger.statement: Domestic business, we are working towards the 10% volume growth year-over-year across general trade, modern trade, e-commerce.
Domestic realizations of ~80,000/MT are going to remain upwards positive; another 2% to 3% improvement in average realization will be seen in quarter one on the domestic front.
Export conditions really putting down a number is not possible; guidance not provided due to prevailing geopolitical uncertainty.
Once the war is settled, exports will double up in next six months because of a big gap in food reserves and expected buffer stock/strategic reserve buying by governments and private trade.
We'll see a healthy double-digit growth in the edible oil category this financial year.
April export numbers seem to be in the same trajectory as Q4, but May and June is something that we need to see.
It is too premature to comment anything on the price; once crop size is known via the All India Rice Export Association mapping exercise, then only we can discuss more on FY27.
We'll build up our inventory in the coming season, and looking at heavy expected export demand, we'll build up our inventory quite good.

We are not caring to monetize that piece of parcel [60 acres], but to develop our own warehousing; any major development decision will be undertaken only after detailed evaluation and necessary approvals.
USDA forecast India's total rice export in the '26-'27 marketing year at approximately 25 million metric tons, higher than the previous year despite lower domestic production.

themes.label: Middle East geopolitical disruption
themes.note: Iran-US-Israel tensions disrupted shipping/logistics across the Middle East in March 2026, driving up freight and insurance costs and denting Q4 export revenue, though buyers broadly absorbed higher costs and situation is seen as temporary.

themes.label: Export recovery potential
themes.note: Management expects exports to double within six months of any Iran conflict settlement due to depleted regional food reserves and anticipated government/private buffer stock buying.

themes.label: Domestic business momentum
themes.note: Q4 FY26 was the best-ever quarter for domestic revenue at INR1,230 crores (+22% YoY), driven by 16% volume growth and 5% realization growth, with FY27 volume growth guidance of 10%.

themes.label: Non-basmati diversification
themes.note: Branded non-basmati revenue grew 38% for the full year to INR271 crores, growing at nearly 4x the rate of the overall domestic business, validating the category adjacency strategy.

themes.label: Market share leadership
themes.note: KRBL holds leading packaged basmati market share across general trade (36.9%), modern trade (38.7%) and e-commerce (40.1%) channels for FY26.

themes.label: Category adjacencies (edible oil, meal mixes, Uplife)
themes.note: New categories like edible oil (INR12 crores revenue, early stage) and India Gate Classic meal mixes are being scaled, expected to grow meaningfully in FY27, though edible oil remains a long-term brand-building journey against an 85-90% share incumbent.

themes.label: Real estate monetization
themes.note: Management continues to prioritize treasury optimization and business use (own warehousing) over monetizing the Samalkha land parcel despite attractive real estate opportunities and profit potential.

key_takeaways: Basmati exports grew by approximately 8% year-on-year to 6.5 million metric tons, the highest ever basmati export volume achieved in the financial year. Non-basmati exports also remained strong at approximately 15 million metric tons, reflecting a growth of around 6% over the previous year.
FY2026 has been a record year for Indian rice exports.

Export revenues for Q4 FY2026 stood at INR279 crores compared to INR450 crores in Q4 FY2025. The decline was primarily due to lower export to the Middle Eastern region during the peak of geopolitical disruptions and logistic bottlenecks.
For the full financial year, FY2026, export revenue stood at INR1,555 crores, representing a growth of approximately 6% on a year-on-year.
Overall revenue for Q4 FY2026 was INR1,526 crores, supported by strong domestic branded sales, which partially offset the temporary decline in exports.
The company reported an EBITDA of INR237 crores and a PAT of INR155 crores during Q4 2026.

Quarter 4 financial year 2026 was our best ever quarter for domestic revenue. Revenues of INR1,230 crores in quarter 4 financial year 2026 is a 22% growth year-on-year, the highest ever quarterly domestic revenue for KRBL. Growth was driven by 16% rice volume growth and 5% rice realization growth, a healthy combination of volume expansion and value improvement.
Branded non-basmati revenues of INR78 crores in quarter 4, up from INR54 crores in quarter 4 financial year '25 is a growth of 44% year-on-year.
Full year domestic revenue, excluding power, stood at INR4,444 crores, a 10% growth over financial year 2025.

For financial year 2026, our channel-wise market share in packaged basmati rice stands as follows, general trade, we have a market share of 36.9%; modern trade, our market share is 38.7%; e-commerce, we have a market share of 40.1%.
A dividend of 450% of face value translating into INR103 crores has been approved by the Board and is subject to shareholder approval in the upcoming AGM.
pressing_questions: What market share gains did we see in Q4 across all the channels? (Company could only provide full-year market share, not Q4-specific figures, and later clarified sequential estimate versus prior year Q4.)
On the exports front, if you take Q4 as the base, how much further drop do you expect in Q1? (Management said it is difficult to comment as it depends on the geopolitical situation.)
Any clarity on timeline for appointing the [Saudi distributor]... (question was cut off by moderator before being fully answered.)
What is our current export run rate, e.g., how much would we have done in April? (Management declined to share month-wise numbers.)
Can we maintain the Q4 export numbers in this quarter, or would it be even lower? (Management said April seems to be on the same trajectory but May and June remain uncertain.)
Since we are sitting on close to INR1,000 crores in cash, are we looking at an extraordinary dividend or a buyback or something? (Management said no specific update beyond the approved dividend.)
Can you quantify the channel inventory that we have in the export market? (Management said it is difficult to comment on channel inventory specifically.)

BRITANNIA.about: Britannia Industries is one of Indias leading food companies with a 100 year legacy and annual revenues in excess of Rs. 16000 Cr. Britannia is among the most trusted food brands, and manufactures Indias favorite brands like Good Day, Tiger, NutriChoice, Milk Bikis and Marie Gold which are household names in India. Britannias product portfolio includes Biscuits, Bread, Cakes, Rusk, and Dairy products including Cheese, Beverages, Milk and Yoghurt.

quarters.summary: Britannia reported Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue growth of 9.5% YoY (standalone 10%), with operating profit/PBT/PAT growth outpacing sales (12.7%/13.7%/13.6%). Management indicated the company exited the quarter with mid-teens revenue growth and volume growth of ~9% (tonnage), with demand momentum expected to continue into FY27 though no explicit full-year guidance was given; input cost inflation (LPG/PNG, palm oil, sugar, milk) remains a watch-item and margins will be managed via the "virtuous triangle" of volume, value and profitability.

key_figures.label: Phantom stock accounting impact (prior year comparator)

subsections.label: Key financial lines
points: Net sales grew 9.5%, with operating profit, PBT and PAT all growing ahead of sales at 12.7%, 13.7% and 13.6% respectively.

On a 5-year trend, profit from operations at 15.3% is at an acceptable level; PBT is at a level considered reasonable given the inflationary situation from extraordinary circumstances, and PAT follows from the PBT delivered.
Exited the quarter with mid-teens revenue growth, indicating an uptrend developing through the quarter.
Volume growth (tonnage) was 9% in Q1 FY27, with pricing contributing about 1% to growth.

subsections.label: Margin / cost management (virtuous triangle)
points: Management stated they must manage between value, volume and margin as input costs remain elevated versus February levels; internally confident of keeping levers in check but did not commit to specific FY27 margin outcome.
A 'good year' is defined as a healthy balance across the virtuous triangle of volume, value and profitability, with none overtaking the other.
Ad spend on brand building is running ahead of sales growth; management attributed this partly to a lower base in the prior two years where spending had been reduced.

Price increases taken in the quarter were largely via shrinkflation (reduced grammage at same consumer price points of INR 5/INR 10), which takes time to execute due to machinery and packaging changes; management estimated only about half of input cost inflation was mitigated through price increases this quarter, with the other half unmitigated.
Expected additional pricing contribution of 1.5-2% in coming quarters.

subsections.label: PLI and other bookkeeping items
points: No PLI incentive has been booked in FY26 or Q1 FY27 as the company has not achieved the threshold growth prescribed under the scheme.
Phantom stock accounting impact for the current quarter is minimal (~INR 1 crore), much lower than the INR 52 crore figure cited by an analyst for the prior year.

subsections.label: General Trade (GT) channel
points: GT (green channel) in the last 3 quarters, and notably in the quarter gone by, is indexed at about 1.5x the growth rate of the whole of last year, indicating demand buildup in GT, the largest channel for the company.
GT business, which was under pressure in the last 2 quarters for certain reasons (dual pricing), has recovered with good momentum.

Key states (largest, most profitable states, overweighted in revenue/profitability contribution) are showing good growth with an inflection upswing; other, smaller/more nimble states are growing about 1.3x key states.

Two years back, 'focus states' referred to Hindi-belt states where Britannia was not market leader; the current 'key states' terminology refers instead to the largest and most profitable states by net sales and profitable portfolio mix — a different context from before.
In the Q1'25 chart, the orange (other) states line was equal to the green (key states) line; both have since moved ahead, with key states also advancing.

GT structural changes: added headcount in certain markets; converting some sub-distributors into direct distributors; empowering regional teams with focused portfolio, media/influencer spend, and product innovation tailored to specific market clusters (skeleton of GT structure unchanged, but execution/behavior changing).
GT sales at INR 5/INR 10 price points represent 60+% of the portfolio.

subsections.label: Other channels (e-commerce/Q-commerce/Modern Trade)
points: Other/newer channels (orange line) are growing faster, nearly 2.5x GT at an overall level.
E-commerce continues to grow with strong double-digit growth and is expected to contribute even more going forward.
Quick commerce (Q-com) is now ~80-85% of overall e-commerce, growing in healthy double digits.

E-commerce/Q-commerce sales mix differs from GT: negligible contribution from INR 5/INR 10 packs; sales skew to larger packs, impulse/adjacency categories and best sellers (e.g., Rusk, Croissant, Jim Jam, Little Hearts) which see higher traction on these channels partly because e-commerce is a larger channel contributor for them.
Modern trade is expensive; company wants to grow there without diluting margins, balancing spend against profitability.

subsections.label: Brand and product highlights
points: Croissant ARR has roughly doubled to ~INR 200 crores, growing at 30+%; recent launches Treat Triple Choco Croissant and Dubai Kunafa Croissant are also growing 30+%.
Marie Gold activated via a front-page TOI ad tying diverse regional teas to one national binding element (Marie Gold).
NutriChoice being built into a platform for healthy snacking and healthy biscuits.
Little Hearts (Gen Z-focused) growing fast; Mother's Day campaign included employee-personalized bags; Britannia cake also back on strong growth momentum via the same campaign.

Milk Bikis (largest biscuit brand in Tamil Nadu, the company's biggest state) ran a Thirukkural-themed activation printing Tamil Kurals on biscuits, resonating strongly with consumers and driving double-digit growth in TN via localized activation.
Bihar: launched Doodh Marie variant focused on that market with a healthy response; Bihar cited as a very strong market.
Eastern India (including Bengal, a large market) is growing in double digits.

Adjacency businesses: Brownie Fudge!t Cake doing brilliantly; new launches include Bourbon Roll, Butter Toastea rusk, and Sattvam Ghee (launched last year); dairy slice business via Bel JV Laughing Cow.

Dairy portfolio grew in double digits; adjacency businesses of cake, rusk and wafers delivered strong double-digit growth led by portfolio innovation; ghee business along with cheese slices doing well.
Non-biscuit portfolio, while a smaller proportion of overall sales, grew in double digits at an overall level despite the segment mix remaining range-bound around 25% of revenue.
Composition of sales from new launches versus total biscuit portfolio described as 'more or less the same' as before.

subsections.label: Market share
points: During dual pricing, sale value capture was sometimes recorded at full price (INR 5) even though the printed price was INR 4.50, creating a challenge versus competitors selling at INR 4.5.

With dual pricing over, plus focused interventions (media presence, sales team sharpness), sequential sales market share gains are being seen across a large number of biscuit categories; company plans to keep investing to sustain this.

subsections.label: International business
points: International business had a mixed quarter: pressures in the Middle East, challenges in markets like Saudi Arabia being addressed, and headwinds in North America (a large market).
Africa business, led by Kenya, is doing very well.
Rest of International and Middle East business described as a mixed bag but improving sequentially.
Outcome depends on geopolitical developments, on which management has no forward view, but the company is prepared to navigate based on experience managing the situation over the last 4 months.

A new head of International business joined 2 months back; execution and cohesion are improving, and management expects the international business to be back on a growth track from this quarter after 4 months of turbulence.

subsections.label: Distribution strategy
points: Company operates across e-commerce, modern trade, alternate channels, GT, and institutional channels (e.g., CSD), and considers itself strong in all channels relative to the market, though internally under-indexed in some.
Focus is on becoming more effective within existing channels rather than just numerical distribution — e.g., growing share of handlers and visibility/relative dominance in GT.
Opportunities identified in General Trade; modern trade growth will be pursued carefully to avoid margin dilution.
Eastern India is growing in double digits.

subsections.label: Demand environment and drivers of growth
points: Demand environment in the last few months has held up; management notes it 'seems to be there at least for the moment' without giving forward commitment.

Mid-teens exit growth in the quarter attributed to two factors: (1) elimination of dual pricing bringing back some buyers/smaller retailers who had temporarily switched to other brands, and (2) organic demand from the ground holding up independent of the dual-pricing effect.

Management stated retailers who had shied away came back in strong numbers, and reiterated the acceleration is not due to channel destocking or inventory buildup — stock does not last long on retail/wholesale shelves; growth is demand-driven, both sell-in and sell-out being strong.

GST rate cut impact expected to be gradual rather than instantaneous for Britannia because a significant portion (60%+) of sales is at fixed INR 5/INR 10 price points, where the GST benefit shows up as extra grammage rather than a visible price drop, unlike packaged goods sold at higher price points (e.g., INR 100-130) where price cuts are more visible and elasticity-driving.
Some price drops taken on larger packs, but their contribution is minimal, partly because they sit in modern trade/e-commerce with promotions that obscure price comparison.
During dual pricing, Britannia sold at INR 5 while competition sold at INR 4.50, a differential of INR 0.50.
E-commerce sales are currently about 6% of total sales.

subsections.label: Healthy snacking / regulatory positioning
points: Management believes demand for regular, indulgent, tasty products will keep growing given low per-capita consumption in India — no near-term risk of these going out of fashion.

Consumer awareness of healthy consumption is growing via multiple channels; company is committed to developing a health-focused portfolio addressing this in a smart, agile, and specific manner, in parallel with (not at the expense of) the core indulgent/premiumization portfolio.
Both portfolios (health-based and indulgent) are expected to grow in parallel.

subsections.label: Sustainability / CSR metrics
points: Nutrition foundation program reached 3.97 lakh contact points in Q1 FY27, representing 78% of the previous year's FY25-26 level.
Electricity from renewable means increased by 16%.

key_figures.label: Time since first analyst call comment on health and wellness platform

subsections.label: Strategic pillars
points: Five strategic pillars reiterated: driving efficiencies in sales, distribution and supply chain; elevating brand experience investment across channels; innovation and adjacencies development including future platforms (health); creating enterprising teams to win in 'Many Indias'; sustainability as an ongoing part of strategy.
Many 'Many Indias' projects are already underway, with outputs expected to be visible in a short period as they continue.

subsections.label: Management team
points: Management team changes are largely complete; a new head of Strategy and Corporate Development joined earlier in the week of the call.
Future changes will occur through normal business processes (e.g., retirements and replacements) rather than further structural overhaul.

subsections.label: New categories / M&A
points: Company remains committed and serious about expanding its portfolio beyond current bakery products, with internal teams working on future platforms including health and wellness, leveraging adjacencies; specifics to be shared in future, echoing commentary first made 6 months ago on an earlier analyst call.
Protein positioned as an important platform within the health platform; will be addressed at a platform level rather than single-product level.

Inorganic growth (M&A) is on the table and being actively evaluated, though management noted fewer readily available assets in food versus personal care/skincare; will pursue M&A selectively for reasons such as acquiring a strong existing brand, speed, capability, or segment technology — not simply to buy a well-performing cookie company that could be built organically.

subsections.label: Input cost inflation
points: Laminate prices (dependent on hydrocarbon prices) have risen for all companies, Britannia included.

Industrial fuel inflation is steep, particularly impacting Britannia given heavy use of LPG and PNG in baking; LPG/PNG cost index peaked at 2.5x normal in April-May 2026, has since normalized somewhat but remains ~1.5x February levels; biomass is used for a certain percentage of fuel needs; company plans to strategically mitigate LPG/PNG risk going forward.
Flour prices have held up so far, but the uncertain El Nino/rainfall situation could impact flour and wheat prices in the coming season, requiring careful monitoring.
Palm oil price is high (~INR 140, up 20+% recently) and linked to hydrocarbon prices, a watch-out item.
Sugar price rose in Q1 FY27 and has risen sharply (upwards of INR 7/kg) in the last 2-3 weeks; sugar is a watch-out given the approaching festive season and its use in many products.
Milk prices are currently high; typically ease after August as season progresses, but behavior needs to be monitored.

Overall input cost environment requires being watchful and careful, consistent with press-release commentary; however, management does not see this as a permanent phenomenon and expects eventual correction as these are cyclical, accelerated by uncontrollable events.

subsections.label: West Asia / International disruption
points: Pressures in the Middle East, challenges in Saudi Arabia being managed, headwinds in North America.
Outcome depends on geopolitical developments outside management's control; company has learned to navigate this over the past 4 months.

subsections.label: Regulatory/health trend risk
points: Regulatory direction is increasingly focused on healthy snacking; management is monitoring this as part of long-term portfolio relevance and risk assessment, and is developing a health/wellness platform in response.

subsections.label: FY27 outlook
points: Management expressed confidence in a good year ahead based on internal plans, focus and momentum, but cautioned this depends on external/uncontrollable events; explicitly declined to give firm forward guidance on demand sustainability.
A 'good year' is defined qualitatively as balanced delivery across the virtuous triangle of volume, value and profitability, without one metric being sacrificed for another.

On margins, if input costs remain at current elevated levels, management stated internally they are confident of managing the levers (value, volume, margin) but would not commit to maintaining FY26 EBITDA margin levels explicitly; how the year is exited remains to be seen.
Pricing: overall 1% price/shrinkflation impact taken in Q1; expect additional pricing impact of about 1.5-2% coming through later in the year.
International business expected to return to a growth track from this quarter (Q2 FY27) after 4 months of turbulence.
New product/category platforms (health/wellness, protein) to be revealed in the near future; no specific timeline given.

September quarter (Q2 FY27) will have a base impact related to last year's GST price-transition-driven market caution in September, which is expected to affect Britannia and other companies alike; July and August of last year were normal months.

guidance_ledger.statement: As a business, we are confident of looking at a good year... our triangle of volume, value and profitability should all fall in a healthy range as we have been doing in the past. One should not overtake the other.

If input cost remains where it is, whether we will be able to deliver [FY26 margin levels] is something we will have to see; internally we are quite confident that we are able to keep the levers in check.
If the overall impact was 1%, you will probably see maybe another 1.5% to 2% coming in.
We are expecting that our international business from this quarter will be back on a growth track.

guidance_ledger.metric: New category / health & wellness platform launches
guidance_ledger.statement: You should also be seeing output of those projects in a short period of time as they keep continuing... you will have to wait and watch, the company is committed and internal teams are already working on that.
Inorganic agenda is there on the table, but we will be careful to evaluate.
There is traction in these categories... we are also quickly working on doing something which is focused on this channel. You will see it in the near future.

guidance_ledger.metric: Q2 FY27 base effect from GST transition
guidance_ledger.statement: There is going to be a base impact in September, which I think will apply to a lot of other companies also, which will apply to us also.

We see that there is sales market share gain across a large number of biscuit categories on a sequential basis, which we are seeing, and we are positive, and we will keep investing to see that keeps happening.
Our spends on brand building are ahead of sales growth, definitely is what I can tell you.
With pricing getting normalized, we can see that during this quarter, they will get normalized, and hence, volumes in those channels will come back.

guidance_ledger.metric: West Asia supply chain de-risking / sourcing optimization
guidance_ledger.statement: We are also optimizing our sourcing between India and international manufacturing facilities for key geographies to mitigate supply-related challenges, expected to be fully operational by mid-May.
We are quite confident that by the end of the quarter, the market would quite likely stabilize on the domestic front... we are quite confident that we will do better this quarter.
We are quite confident that our portfolio, the strategy... we are quite confident that we will be able to generate demand and have a good year.
I don't think that pricing either a bit upwards or either a bit downwards is going to have any major impact from an elasticity point of view... the demand situation will remain fairly strong.
There will be calibrated price increases starting from this quarter... this includes both grammage adjustment and some of the packs which are above INR 10, some kind of a price increase.
We also know that the biscuit industry starts to have a sequential growth from June onwards when monsoon starts to hit and when children start going back to school.

guidance_ledger.metric: Value/realization growth from GST pack economics
guidance_ledger.statement: We are also positive that we will have a good realization... if it happens like that, we are happy that you brought it to the fore.
We will be adding more platforms, and you will hear about that... you would hear about them in the future.

There is active scanning and there is a very serious intent... we also have created a new platform on health. So that also would be an active consideration as we will expand this in the coming months.
We have to keep going stronger on market share, but... we are also adept at managing margins. So it is a careful orchestra which we will play very nicely.

risk_register.risk: Industrial fuel (LPG/PNG) cost inflation
risk_register.note: Prices spiked ~2.5x in April-May, currently still elevated at ~1.5x February levels; heavy usage in baking makes Britannia particularly exposed.

risk_register.risk: Palm oil price inflation
risk_register.note: Price near INR 140, up 20%+, linked to hydrocarbon prices.

risk_register.risk: Sugar price inflation
risk_register.note: Rose in Q1 FY27 and has jumped by over INR 7/kg in the last 2-3 weeks; sensitive given upcoming festive season.

risk_register.risk: Milk price levels
risk_register.note: Currently high; usually eases after August, needs monitoring.

risk_register.risk: Flour/wheat price uncertainty
risk_register.note: Held up so far but El Nino/rainfall uncertainty could affect prices in coming season.

risk_register.risk: West Asia / Middle East geopolitical disruption
risk_register.note: Pressures in Middle East and Saudi Arabia challenges being managed; outcome depends on geopolitical developments outside management's control, but stability seen after 4 months and sequential improvement noted.

risk_register.risk: North America headwinds
risk_register.note: Certain headwinds noted in this large international market.

risk_register.risk: GST dual pricing disruption in wholesale/rural channels
risk_register.note: Dual pricing impact was present in April and partly early May but ended in June; throughput now clean with no inventory buildup.

risk_register.risk: Regulatory direction on healthy snacking
risk_register.note: Regulatory direction increasingly favors healthy snacking; company assessing portfolio relevance and developing health/wellness platform in response.

risk_register.risk: PLI incentive non-realization
risk_register.note: No PLI incentive booked in FY26 or Q1 FY27 as threshold growth prescribed under the scheme was not achieved.

risk_register.risk: West Asia conflict (Strait of Hormuz lockup) disrupting vessel dispatch and manufacturing logistics for international business (Oman/Dubai)
risk_register.note: Impacted international revenue and profitability last quarter; also drove up fuel costs and ocean freight rates.

risk_register.risk: LPG/fuel supply constraints in India due to West Asia conflict
risk_register.note: No material disruption to Indian manufacturing operations; managed well despite initial concerns.

risk_register.risk: Laminate price inflation
risk_register.note: Prices fell toward end of Q4 but rose again from March and remained elevated in April due to war impact in Middle East raising granule prices.

risk_register.risk: Dual pricing / GST transition impact on wholesale and rural channels
risk_register.note: Caused transaction slowdown in B2B/wholesale (25% of business) through Jan-Mar; expected to normalize this quarter.

risk_register.risk: Milk price inflation with El Nino uncertainty
risk_register.note: Prices on an upswing; usually decline in winter, but El Nino/higher warming expected and could impact this dynamic.

risk_register.risk: Wheat/flour price uptick
risk_register.note: After a receding/positive trend, last 1 month saw prices rise due to unseasonal rains, high heat and quality issues in arrivals.

risk_register.risk: Palm oil price rise correlated with fuel costs
risk_register.note: Company forward-buys and is covered for next 5 months at a favorable rate.

risk_register.risk: General fuel (LPG/CNG) inflation
risk_register.note: Inflationary for all players; company pays market rate inflation.

risk_register.risk: Competitive volume advantage from wholesale/rural mix during dual-pricing disruption

themes.label: GST dual-pricing transition
themes.note: Dual pricing impact in wholesale/rural channels ended in June, with retailers returning and throughput clean with no inventory buildup.

themes.label: Input cost inflation
themes.note: LPG/PNG, palm oil, sugar and milk costs all elevated, requiring careful management; only about half of inflation mitigated via price increases this quarter.

themes.label: E-commerce / quick-commerce acceleration
themes.note: Q-com now 80-85% of e-commerce, growing in healthy double digits; company developing channel-specific/exclusive product focus.

themes.label: Premiumization and brand investment
themes.note: Ad spend running ahead of sales growth, driving improved brand health tracking metrics like recall and usage.

themes.label: West Asia geopolitical disruption
themes.note: Middle East/Saudi challenges being managed, North America headwinds, but Africa (Kenya) strong; international business expected back on growth track from Q2 FY27 after new international head joined.

themes.label: Growth vs margin balance / market share strategy
themes.note: Management reiterated commitment to balance volume, value and margin (virtuous triangle) while gaining sequential market share across biscuit categories.

themes.label: Cost efficiency program (CEP)
themes.note: Ongoing focus on packaging cost optimization, buying efficiency, alternate fuels, and renewable energy expansion to offset input cost pressure.

key_takeaways: Revenue from operations at console level in Q1 were about INR 4,964 crores, giving annual growth of 9.5%; on standalone basis grew at 10%.
PAT was at about 11.9% of revenue and the 12-month growth on PAT was 13.6%.
General Trade channel is now indexed at a rate about 1.5x of what was grown in the whole of last year; other channels are growing at nearly 2.5x of GT.
Volume growth for the quarter was close to 9%.
The company exited the quarter in double digits, kind of mid-teens number.
Dual pricing impact was there to a certain extent in April and marginally in first half of May, but came to an end in June.
International business had a mixed quarter: pressures in Middle East, challenges in Saudi being dealt with, headwinds in North America, but Africa led by Kenya doing very well.
On key financial lines, net sales grew 9.5% and operating profit, PBT and PAT have all been ahead of sales at 12.7%, 13.7%, 13.6%.
Input cost inflation (LPG/PNG, palm oil, sugar, milk) is a key watch-out area for the coming quarters.
pressing_questions: Firstly, just wanted to understand the comment on the quarter ending with mid-teens growth. I wanted to understand what is driving this shift? Was it the dual pricing issue that is getting addressed or is it completely addressed that is aiding this? Or was there a weak base in June or any kind of a quarter-end filling that is driving this? Or it's just genuine volume growth that you are seeing coming back as you had indicated? And can this volume growth sustain?

As we focus on driving portfolio diversification and demand environment is remaining healthy, do you see for the full year FY '27, an ability to grow operating profit or EBITDA ahead of sales growth similar to what we saw in 1Q?

Like was there any benefit of older inventory which you had this quarter? And therefore, you expect sort of Q2 margins to be a little weaker? And a subset of this question is, if input costs remain where they are today, are you confident of maintaining full year FY '27 EBITDA margins at, at least the same level as FY '26?

What is the amount of PLI that you will book in FY '27? And since that will go away in FY '28, will it hit the bottom line to that extent? Or would you fully be able to mitigate the impact of that through some other measures?

quarters.summary: Britannia closed FY26 with Q4 consolidated revenue of INR 4,686 crore (up 7.1% YoY) and full-year revenue of INR 18,858 crore (up 7.5%), with PAT growth aided by income-tax case closures. Near-term outlook is clouded by West Asia conflict-led logistics/fuel disruption and GST-transition dual-pricing issues in wholesale/rural channels, both of which management expects to normalize during Q1 FY27, with confidence in a stronger demand environment aided by monsoon-led seasonal pickup from June, continued premiumization, e-commerce/quick-commerce growth, and calibrated price increases, while cost-efficiency programs continue to be a core lever to protect margins amid fuel and laminate inflation.

points: Q4 PAT growth of 21.1% and FY26 PAT growth of 16.3% partly reflect income tax case closures leading to release of tax provisions, which is a one-off benefiting PAT margin comparability.

subsections.label: Other expenses increase
points: Other expenses grew 18% against 7% revenue growth in the quarter, driven by higher advertising and brand investment spend versus the previous quarter, as the company ramps up brand investment.

key_figures.value: high single digit to close to double digit

subsections.label: Dual pricing / GST transition impact
points: Close to 60-65% of biscuits sold at INR 5 and INR 10 price points; the price transition caused dual pricing in the market (some competitors selling at INR 4.5/INR 9 vs Britannia at INR 5/INR 10), causing transaction slowdown in rural and wholesale channels.

The gatekeeper effect in B2B/wholesale (25% of business) was impacted by GST transition and dual pricing; retail/B2C (75% of business, urban, e-commerce, modern trade, out-of-home) performed fairly well.
Dual pricing impact existed through January, February and March, not just March; West Asia-specific challenge added on top in March.
Management expects pricing to normalize during the current quarter (Q1 FY27) and volumes in wholesale/rural channels to recover as competitors also move toward full/higher price points.
Management could not precisely quantify the bps impact of dual pricing (analyst suggested 200-700 bps range) but confirmed there was an impact on transactions.
From a value-share perspective, management does not see material market share loss since price realization differential (INR 4.5/9 vs INR 5/10) is proportionally similar.

subsections.label: West Asia conflict impact on domestic vs international growth
points: West Asia impact hit domestic business specifically in March, not Jan-Feb; removing this impact, Jan-Feb-March domestic growth would have been a smoother ~9% curve.

International business revenue and profitability impacted last quarter due to vessel unavailability and demand slowdown, caused by Strait of Hormuz lock-up disrupting dispatches from Oman/Dubai manufacturing.

subsections.label: Demand outlook and seasonality
points: Biscuit industry typically sees sequential growth pickup from June onward with monsoon and school reopening season, expected to support recovery.
Management confident that with GST-led dual pricing fading, both B2C (already growing well) and B2B (25% of business) will normalize and move up.

On FY27 growth outlook, management stated confidence in generating demand via portfolio strategy, higher ad spend, marketing investment, premiumization and Many Indias strategy, but flagged uncontrollable factors like monsoon.

subsections.label: Elasticity and GST realization dynamics
points: Management does not expect major elasticity impact from calibrated price increases given category vibrancy and since the pricing move is only bringing conditions back to levels similar to ~6-7 months ago when demand was good.

On GST pack economics, management noted biscuit is impulsive/planned purchase and doesn't respond as elastically to grammage changes as other categories (chocolates, noodles), where 30% growth benefited from more visible price cuts driven by GST reduction.

Management acknowledged possibility of better realization/value growth going forward from GST-led per-pack realization increase, but says market disruption over last 4-5 months has obscured visibility on this trend so far.

subsections.label: New product launches / brand activity on air
points: 50-50 Cheeze Dipped variant launched; Doodh Marie Gold (variant of Marie Gold) launched across select markets; Good Day Butter launched.
Consumer engagement and brand activations across Tiger Krunch, Treat (wafer brand), Croissant and Jim Jam; Croissant category noted as doing very well.
Fudge It, a Gen-Z-focused cake brand, promoted significantly during Valentine's, showing significant growth and functioning as an impulse confectionery purchase.

subsections.label: Adjacency / category performance
points: Wafers continue growing healthy double digit.
Cake & Rusk has high prevalence in e-commerce, driving growth at about 1.4x of biscuits.
Brownie successfully scaled up and well accepted by consumers.
Dairy business posted double-digit growth, fueled by Ghee performing excellently over the last year.

50-50 Cheeze Dipped and its Caramel Dipped variant heavily advertised on TV during IPL, became second-biggest player in sandwich cracker segment within 3 months of launch and continues to grow month-on-month.
Signature brands Treat, Little Hearts, and Jim Jam outpacing overall company growth by about 3x, with innovation and variants planned to leverage the portfolio.

subsections.label: E-commerce / Q-com dynamics
points: E-commerce salience understated at 6% headline because ~60-65% of biscuits sell at INR 5/INR 10 price points, which have minimal e-commerce presence; adjusting for this, e-commerce contribution is upwards of 12%, described as best in class.

Newer adjacency categories growing in e-commerce at 2.7x rate, making it the fastest-growing channel; strategy includes exclusive launches, premiumized offerings and customized D2C offerings, with growing investment planned.

Quick commerce (within e-commerce) is a bright spot with sustained momentum/acceleration over recent quarters; currently ~70% of e-commerce business from quick commerce, expected to rise to ~85% as Amazon and Flipkart scale their quick-commerce models.

Shift to quick commerce changes assortment mix, allowing premiumization and higher sales of indulgent/adjacency categories versus staples-heavy marketplace model; adjacency growing almost 3x in this channel.
Company collaborating closely with platforms, adapting to their playbooks to activate brands; expects e-commerce salience (6%) to keep rising along with premium/impulse assortment mix.

Company deliberately does not proactively push INR 5/INR 10 packs on e-commerce as natural consumer disposition on e-commerce favors premium/impulse purchases; algorithmic visibility for low price point packs is limited to search/repeat-purchase, not active promotion, to avoid channel conflict and to focus spend on premium packs; however INR5/INR10 packs remain available if searched for.

subsections.label: Many Indias / regional strategy
points: Company has created regional teams supported by marketing, innovation, and R&D to address internal regional market classifications at a more local level, described as 'Many Indias'; output expected to be visible in coming quarters.

subsections.label: International manufacturing footprint and disruption
points: Significant portion of manufacturing for international markets happens in Oman and Dubai; the West Asia conflict (Strait of Hormuz lock-up) prevented vessel dispatches, impacting international business revenue and profitability, alongside sharply higher fuel costs and ocean freight rates.

No material disruption occurred to production operations at Indian manufacturing facilities despite fuel supply constraints (e.g., LPG shortage concerns) during the conflict; management credits team agility for steady manufacturing performance in India.

subsections.label: Manufacturing relocation / flexibility
points: Company has an export-oriented unit at Mundra; had previously moved North America-bound manufacturing to Oman due to tariffs, but has now moved that manufacturing back to Mundra to enable dispatch toward North America, since Oman-based manufacturing could not service that route amid the crisis.
Company is optimizing sourcing between India and international manufacturing facilities for key geographies to mitigate supply-related challenges, expected to be fully operational by mid-May.

subsections.label: ESG / sustainability KPIs (FY26 vs prior year)
points: 7% reduction in specific water consumption.
1% increase in women factory workforce; many factories are majority managed by women.
67% increase in number of beneficiaries under the Britannia Nutrition Foundation, a major CSR cornerstone.
14% increase in renewable electricity share in own plants.

subsections.label: Cost Efficiency Program (CEP) scale
points: CEP discipline has increased 10x compared to 2013-14 (over ~12 years) and has doubled compared to 2021.
Focus areas include alternate fuels, buying efficiencies, renewable energy, wastage reduction, logistics optimization, and packaging re-engineering.
Company is evaluating alternate energy sources as long-term solutions to mitigate fuel supply-led disruptions, aiming for greater self-sufficiency against future shocks.

key_figures.label: Standalone growth impacted by West Asia issue

subsections.label: Domestic vs International impact
points: Domestic (standalone) India business growth for Q4 was around 9-9.5% ex-West Asia impact, with the West Asia-related pressure concentrated in March.
International business (West Asia markets) was pulled down for the whole quarter due to inability to dispatch vessels amid the Strait of Hormuz lockup.

subsections.label: Channel-level performance
points: Rest of general trade and key accounts growing in healthy double digits.
Modern trade growing even stronger, upwards of 15-16%.
E-commerce channel growing upwards of 50%.

Wholesale/rural (B2B, 25% of business) impacted by dual pricing/GST transition; competitor with reportedly higher wholesale/rural mix (as high as ~40% vs Britannia's 25%) may have gained relative volume advantage in those channels.

subsections.label: Commodity price trends
points: Flour/wheat: receding trend through Q4 given good wheat output; in the last 1 month prices have risen due to unseasonal rains, high heat and quality issues in arrivals; still viewed as an overall positive trend for the company.
Refined palm oil: prices rose last quarter, correlated with fuel costs; company buys forward and is well covered for the next 5 months.
Sugar: behaving more or less normally.
Cocoa: prices down.
Laminate: prices fell toward end of Q4 but rose from March onward and remain elevated in April, attributed to the Middle East war impact raising granule prices.
Milk: prices trending up as seasonally typical (usually decline in winter); El Nino/higher warming expected to be a factor to watch for milk price movement.
Fuel (LPG/CNG): inflationary for everybody; openly available market price inflation being paid by the company.

subsections.label: Inventory and procurement positioning
points: Palm oil inventory/forward cover gives a favorable rate versus the market for the next 5 months.
Wheat: company is one of the most proactive/aggressive buyers with good market reading; current inventory cover of ~5.5-6 months is at an attractive price even accounting for carrying cost.
