subsections.label: Delhi T3 JV restructuring
points: Delhi T3 was previously operated in a JV structured as an SPV where TFS had a majority shareholding and hence consolidated the entity.

Plan is to bid through a different, long-term joint venture with GMR (not in SPV form) where TFS's shareholding would be 30%, meaning it would not be consolidated going forward but contribute through profit pick-up.
This new-structure tender is for a larger set of outlets than what was operated directly under the previous T3 arrangement.

subsections.label: International entity setup
points: Set up new entities in Dubai (Middle East focus) and Indonesia (Asia focus) to enable local bidding for opportunities in those markets.

subsections.label: Middle East conflict impact
points: Passenger traffic impacted by the Middle East conflict, particularly on international routes; despite disruptions, company delivered double-digit growth in sales and profitability.
Overall passenger traffic broadly flat YoY for the quarter due to significant decline in international traffic offsetting modest domestic growth.

Quarter began with a decline in overall traffic in April; May saw gradual stabilization with domestic traffic returning to growth while international traffic continued to face headwinds; June saw traffic soften again due to renewed conflict-related disruptions.

subsections.label: Softer markets
points: Mumbai and Guwahati saw softer LFL owing to traffic migration to new airport infrastructure.
Certain South India markets saw softer LFL given relatively higher exposure to Middle East traffic.

subsections.label: Cost pressures
points: Higher cost and inflation pressures were seen against the softer traffic backdrop during the quarter.

Ramp-up costs (employee and other expenses) from new outlet openings at Noida, Cochin and Delhi drove EBITDA margin moderation, though these are viewed as strategic investments to support future growth.

subsections.label: Contract renewal uncertainty
points: Delhi T3 (a material subsidiary) contract runs until 30th September 2026; JV GHL has bid for the renewal contract but results are not yet known, so management could not comment on H2 impact.
Chennai and Kolkata airports are coming up for renewal at end of March 2027 and early Q1 FY28 respectively.

key_figures.value: end of March 2027 and early Q1 2027-28

subsections.label: Near-term outlook
points: Current environment reflects temporary disruption; long-term drivers of Indian aviation remain firmly intact, supported by rising air travel penetration, expanding airport infrastructure, increasing connectivity, and growing propensity to travel.
Q2 FY27 to-date trend similar to Q1, with international traffic remaining the key delta due to route suspensions.

H2 FY27 expected to see a good bounce back in passenger traffic as major airlines restore many long-haul international routes from September/October, aligned with independent research calling for a strong H2 for India passenger traffic.

subsections.label: Growth catalysts
points: Bhogapuram Airport opening on 17th August under JV GHL marks a significant milestone.
Passenger services platform to be progressively expanded to additional airports, building on early success at Noida.
Over 50 outlets under development are expected to mature over 12-18 months and provide meaningful uplift to revenue and earnings.
The ~90 units mobilized over the last 12 months are expected to hit normalization over the next ~12 months, combined with expected traffic recovery, providing a double impact in H2.

subsections.label: Cost normalization outlook
points: Other expenses currently elevated due to ramp-up pre-operating costs at Cochin, Delhi and Noida; expected to normalize to traditional levels within another ~12 months as units perform.
Cost escalation at contract renewal (e.g., brand changes/asset refresh) expected to normalize on the lower end of the 12-month scenario.

guidance_ledger.statement: Expectation is H2 of this year should be a good bounce back on passenger traffic, with international long-haul routes suspended by major airlines expected to be restored from September & October, and independent research also calling out a strong H2 for India passenger traffic this year.
Currently till about August, traffic trend is similar to Q1, with international traffic continuing to be the delta.

Over 50 outlets currently under development across the network; as these locations open and mature over the coming 12 to 18 months, they are expected to provide a meaningful uplift to both revenue and earnings.

A large part of the ~90 units mobilized/activated over the last 12 months (many in the last 2 quarters) will hit normalization over the next ~12 months, with benefit expected to play out especially in H2 with traffic recovery.
Existing/running airport units take 12-18 months to hit normalized profit levels; greenfield airports take 18-24 months.
Higher pre-operating costs from ramp-up of Cochin, Delhi, Noida units are expected to normalize within another ~12 months, bringing other expenses back to traditional levels.
Adjusted gross profit margin of around 81% remains well within guided range.
Bangalore T1 undergoing massive upgradation; company expects further opportunities to bid for, coming up in phases over the next 12 months.
Focus is now more on Asia (given Middle East situation) with entities set up in Dubai and Indonesia to bid for opportunities; company is quite focused to participate in opportunities this year.

Highways compared to where airports were in 2008-09; company targeting WSA opportunities as ~1,000 wayside amenity plan comes online from government, approached in a calibrated manner with financial return benchmarks maintained.
When contracts go for renewal, there will logically be some cost escalation from brand changes/asset refresh, but this would normalize probably on the lower end of the 12-month scenario.
Delhi T3 contract runs till 30th September 2026; JV GHL has bid for the contract but results are not out; management could not comment on H2 impact.
Chennai and Kolkata airports would be coming up for renewal at the end of March 2027 and early Q1 of FY2027-28.
Approach is to target returns at maturity that mimic the rest of the portfolio; company will not chase growth unless it gives sustainable long-term profits.
Gross margin will be in the range of 80% to 83% on an overall basis for next year, factoring in anticipated inflationary impact due to Middle East conflict LPG price increases and other factors.

Capex on an average to be in the range of INR50 crores to INR60 crores every year, which would also be the case for FY27, predominantly for mobilization of units to fund recent concessions of Delhi, Cochin and upcoming Noida projects.
Debtor levels (which shot up to ~INR264 crores due to EATS ramp-up) expected to normalize by first half of current year back to average of around 40 to 45 days of outstandings.

Combination of pax growth (historically 7-10%) plus price/initiatives delta (7-10%) would give a normal perspective of around 18-20% LFL in a normalized environment; management would not call out an exact number.
More than 50 outlets currently in the pipeline; two more airports currently in the works in the coming months, in addition to Bhogapuram and Noida.
Roughly anticipation is about seven outlets happening originally at Bhogapuram; more mobilization details to be shared as date approaches.
Actively working towards expanding international footprint through new lounge opportunities based on initial success in Malaysia and Hong Kong; confident to deliver on this over the next few years.
Exploring wayside amenity opportunities at access-controlled expressways, a segment backed by strong government intent and investment plans in the medium-term.
May showing improving trends in passenger traffic versus March/April and versus last year's base; recovery expected once war-like situation resolves.

risk_register.risk: Middle East conflict disrupting international passenger traffic
risk_register.note: Particularly impacted international routes; significant decline in international traffic while domestic grew modestly, leading to broadly flat overall passenger traffic YoY for the quarter; renewed conflict-related disruptions in June softened traffic again.

risk_register.risk: Softer like-for-like performance in specific markets
risk_register.note: Mumbai and Guwahati saw softer LFL due to traffic migration to new airport infrastructure; certain South India markets softer given higher exposure to Middle East traffic.

risk_register.risk: Higher cost and inflation pressures
risk_register.note: Company faced higher cost and inflation pressures during the quarter against a softer traffic backdrop.

risk_register.risk: Ramp-up cost drag from new outlets (Noida, Cochin, Delhi)
risk_register.note: Employee cost and other expenses increased due to annual compensation revisions, onboarding of additional manpower for recently opened outlets at Noida and Cochin, and staffing for new passenger services business at Noida, causing EBITDA margin moderation to 35.8%.

risk_register.risk: International route suspensions by major airlines
risk_register.note: Two of the largest airlines suspended a lot of international long-haul routes towards end of May, logically due to fuel prices and geopolitical disruption; restoration expected from September & October.

risk_register.risk: JV/associate business growth mismatch vs consol
risk_register.note: JV business growth (~15%) was muted vs consol growth partly because some units in JV structures move to the company over a scheduled period, and because airports on the western side with strong Middle East exposure were impacted in passenger traffic and sales.

risk_register.risk: Delhi T3 contract uncertainty
risk_register.note: Delhi T3 contract runs till 30 Sept 2026; JV GHL has bid for the renewal but result not yet known; management could not comment on H2 impact.

risk_register.risk: Labour code impact
risk_register.note: Impact of the new labour code on ~5,000+ employees (majority on company roll) is minimal, below INR8-10 crores.

risk_register.risk: Renewal-related cost escalation
risk_register.note: When contracts are renewed there will logically be some cost escalation from brand changes/asset refresh, though more limited than fresh construction.

risk_register.risk: Middle East conflict / geopolitical disruption impacting international travel and Gulf-bound/NRI traffic
risk_register.note: Escalated in early March, weighed on international sentiment, caused near-double-digit dip in international traffic through April; continued into Q1 FY27 but showing signs of improvement in May.

risk_register.risk: India-Pakistan geopolitical conflict (May 2025)
risk_register.note: Caused temporary air traffic disruptions at the outset of FY26; a similar risk noted as impacting Q1 FY27 comparisons.

risk_register.risk: Aircraft crash-related maintenance/safety flight schedule reductions
risk_register.note: Impacted Q2 FY26 due to reduced flight schedules following the aircraft crash in June of last year.

risk_register.risk: FDTL Crew Rest Regulations implementation
risk_register.note: Temporarily curtailed capacity at India's largest carrier in December 2025.

risk_register.risk: Input cost / food inflation, including LPG price increases from Middle East conflict
risk_register.note: Food inflation around 3-5% in April; natural hedge from electric equipment usage at airports; annual supplier contracts provide robustness; anticipate some inflationary impact going forward but gross margin guided to remain in 80-83% range.

risk_register.risk: Litigation-related matters
risk_register.note: One-time provision of INR212 million created on a prudent/conservative basis; management believes its position on these matters remains strong.

risk_register.risk: EATS-driven receivables build-up
risk_register.note: Trade receivables/debtors rose to ~INR264 crores from average INR100-110 crores due to new banking relationship ramp-up (billing procedures, system integrations); expected to normalize to 40-45 days by H1 FY27.

risk_register.risk: Bank/credit card tightening on mass-market lounge access
risk_register.note: Ongoing for 18 months; mass market card access being restricted while premium card access is expanding, resulting in a net neutral-to-positive effect on lounge business given premium cardholders are frequent flyers.

risk_register.risk: Competitive threat from quick-commerce/retail entrants (e.g., Blinkit at Mumbai airport)
risk_register.note: Viewed as a retail-focused pilot with limited overlap with TFS's F&B business, which requires kitchen-prepared food versus dark-store retail delivery.

risk_register.risk: Airport privatization / regional political changes (e.g., West Bengal, Kolkata Airport)
risk_register.note: Management does not believe state-level political changes will alter the government's existing privatization pipeline of 11 airports.

themes.label: Passenger traffic disruptions
themes.note: Middle East conflict caused a significant decline in international traffic, leaving overall passenger traffic broadly flat YoY for the quarter, with April decline, May rebound, and June softening again.

themes.label: Network and outlet expansion
themes.note: Added 87 travel QSR outlets and two lounges over the last 12 months, commenced Noida operations (21 airports, 580 outlets/lounges, 153 brands), with over 50 outlets under development.

themes.label: Premiumization and brand portfolio growth
themes.note: LFL growth driven by menu innovations, promotional initiatives, calibrated pricing, premiumization, brand edits, and bundling rather than significant price escalation.

themes.label: International expansion
themes.note: Malaysia and Hong Kong lounges performing well and maturing; new entities set up in Dubai and Indonesia to pursue Asia-focused opportunities amid Middle East disruption.

themes.label: EATS technology platform monetization
themes.note: Elite Assist passenger services (meet-and-greet, porter) launched at Noida will integrate into the EATS technology platform, enabling a connected passenger ecosystem.

themes.label: Input cost / margin management
themes.note: EBITDA margin moderated to 35.8% due to ramp-up costs at Noida/Cochin/Delhi and new passenger services staffing, though adjusted gross margin of ~81% remained within guided range.

themes.label: Capital allocation discipline
themes.note: Debt-free balance sheet with ~INR9.7 billion cash; capital deployment prioritizes returns that mimic mature portfolio economics, funding airport, lounge, highway and passenger services growth.

key_takeaways: System-wide sales grew by 18% year-on-year to INR8.4 billion, while consolidated profit after tax increased by 35.6% year-on-year to INR1.3 billion.

Net contract gains of 15.9% year-on-year at the system-wide level; system-wide LFL sales growth was 0.8% for the quarter, but excluding softer markets (Mumbai, Guwahati, certain South India markets), like-for-like sales grew around 7% year-on-year across the wider network.

Commenced operations at Noida International Airport, taking system-wide presence to 21 airports; over the last 12 months added 87 travel QSR outlets and two lounges, with system-wide footprint at 580 travel QSR outlets and lounges and brand portfolio expanded to 153 brands.
Successful launch of passenger services at Noida International Airport under Elite Assist brand, including meet-and-greet and porter services, integrating into the EATS technology platform.
Over 50 outlets currently under development across the network, expected to provide meaningful uplift to revenue and earnings over the coming 12-18 months.
Consolidated revenue from operations grew by 20.6% year-on-year to INR4.5 billion; consolidated LFL sales growth stood at 4.2%; net contract gains remained strong at 20.2%.

Reported gross profit stood at INR3.9 billion (85.7% margin); adjusted for lounge aggregation cost reclassification of INR223 million, adjusted gross profit was INR3.65 billion at ~81% margin, within guided range.
EBITDA stood at INR1.6 billion, up 11% year-on-year; EBITDA margin moderated to 35.8% due to higher employee and operating costs from recently commissioned airports and new business initiatives.
Consolidated PAT increased by 35.6% YoY to INR1.3 billion; PAT margin expanded to 28.5% from 25.3%, aided by sales growth and higher other income including INR131 million GST provision write-back.
Debt-free balance sheet with consolidated cash balance of approximately INR9.7 billion as of June 30.
pressing_questions: How much of the 4.2% consolidated LFL growth came from higher spend per passenger versus other initiatives, and what is the sustainable level of LFL growth as passenger traffic normalizes?
Over the next 3-5 years, what will improve TFS economics beyond passenger traffic growth — premiumization, higher spend per passenger, or better contract terms?
What return threshold does the company target when bidding for a new airport or adding outlets, and is competitive bidding pressuring these return expectations?
Why did the JV/associate business grow only ~15% while Adani F&B and lounge revenue grew 55% YoY and GHL/GMR reported ~22% YoY growth?
Are there any new upcoming airports the company is planning to bid for, and how many outlets are planned at the recently won Bangalore T1 contract?
What is the sustainable LFL and net contract gain growth the company is targeting year-on-year?
What led to the 540 bps increase in other expenses this quarter, and what is the target going forward?
Is Delhi T3 moving to a JV in H2, and which other airports are coming up for renewal?
Will the EBITDA margin profile be similar for airports beyond Mumbai, Delhi and Bangalore if Delhi T3 moves fully to JV structure?
Do concession agreements have baked-in step-ups to minimum guaranteed rents and revenue share percentages, or do these only get revised upon contract renewal?

quarters.summary: FY26 was framed as a defining year — first full year as a listed company — marked by multiple disruptions (India-Pakistan conflict, aircraft crash-related schedule cuts, FDTL Crew Rest Regulation disruptions, Middle East conflict) that held full-year passenger traffic growth to just 1.2% YoY, yet TFS delivered system-wide sales growth of 25.4% and adjusted consolidated PAT growth of 21.4-21.5% for FY26, and management expects the near-term environment to remain dynamic while remaining confident in long-term structural aviation growth, guiding gross margins to stay in the 80-83% range in FY27 and capex of INR50-60 crores per year to fund the committed pipeline (Bhogapuram, Noida, Delhi, Cochin).

subsections.label: Full year profitability drivers
points: Margin expansion supported by operating leverage, scale efficiencies, and disciplined cost management.
Employee costs remained well controlled, reflecting productivity gains and operating leverage from scale-up across locations.
PAT growth driven by revenue growth, margin expansion, disciplined cost management, and higher contribution from joint ventures due to faster mobilization of units in the JV.

subsections.label: Balance sheet and receivables
points: Trade receivables higher due to initial ramp-up of the EATS business; expected to normalize by end of H1 of current year.
Company remains zero-debt with a healthy cash and investment position, providing significant financial flexibility to invest in growth opportunities.

subsections.label: Capital allocation
points: Company has been disciplined about cash generation and investment for the last 17 years, built on principles that are part of its DNA.
Cash reserves support new opportunities such as international lounges, and expressway wayside amenities.
ROCE at north of 40%, about 45%, described as very compelling investments.
Approach is a combination of prudent and aggressive use of funds.

subsections.label: Revenue mix and balance
points: Business continues to remain well balanced across both travel QSR and lounges, showing the strength of the integrated platform.
Travel QSR benefits from throughput and menu-led initiatives; lounges benefit from premiumization and higher dwell times at airports.

subsections.label: Brand portfolio expansion
points: Brand portfolio now spans over 145 brands with a mix of global, regional, and in-house brands.
New international brand partnerships added during the year: Gordon Ramsay, Nando's, and Wagamama, strengthening premium positioning at key airports.
In-house brands (idli.com, Cafeccino, Delhi Street) and regional brand partners (Sri Krishna Sweets, Bikanervala) continue to play an important role in driving localization and relevance.

subsections.label: Menu curation and customer engagement
points: Introduced regionally inspired menus, premium dining formats, and experiential offerings across travel QSR and lounges.
Travel QSR introduced specialized breakfast, regional menus, innovative beverages (Signature Filter Coffee, Boba Tea), and value-led combo offers.
Lounges enhanced customer engagement through seasonal activations, festival-led menus, and experiential formats, driving higher dwell times and visit frequency.
Initiatives such as culinary masterclasses with Master Chefs and food festivals like 'Swad-e-Watan' saw strong customer engagement and participation.

subsections.label: Lounge business demand dynamics (credit card access)
points: Bank/credit card access restrictions on lounges have been playing out for the last 18 months, but the market is diverging: mass market card growth is slower (high single digits) while premium card growth is much faster (more than 50%).

Premium cardholders tend to be frequent flyers (flying 3-5 times a month) versus mass market cardholders who may fly only a few times a year, so many premium cards are now offering unlimited or guest lounge access.
Despite 18 months of this dynamic playing out, lounge numbers have remained quite strong through the period.

subsections.label: EATS platform launch
points: FY26 was a landmark year with the launch of the EATS platform, enabling direct bank-to-lounge access as an integrated service (a Lounge Access Management / LAM system for banks and card networks).
Platform has been stabilizing well and management is encouraged by the response.
EATS remains a key enabler for enhancing customer access, improving convenience, and supporting higher engagement and monetization.
Plans to add ancillary services on the platform (e.g., meet and greet, porter services already offered separately) to further deepen customer engagement and unlock incremental revenue opportunities.
Platform enables differentiated experiences by consumer segment (e.g., VIP zone access, complimentary offers during events like IPL matches) via direct connection with banking/card network partners.

EATS business kick-started around Q3 FY26 / early December, tying up contracts with various banks and card networks; large part of EATS billing and revenue unlock has happened over the last 4-5 months.

subsections.label: Committed pipeline
points: Noida Airport on track for commencement of operations in coming months, strengthening committed pipeline and visibility for further growth.
Bhogapuram (new Greenfield airport in Vizag) is a long-term contract under GHL; anticipated around 7 outlets originally, with exact phasing/mobilization details to be shared closer to the date.
More than 50 outlets currently in the pipeline across committed projects.
Two more airports currently in the works (bids in progress) in the coming months, in addition to Bhogapuram and Noida.
Capex predominantly for mobilization of units to fund recent concessions of Delhi, Cochin, and the upcoming Noida project.

subsections.label: Operational resilience during disruptions
points: During periods of disruption, reduced reliance on gas wherever applicable; menus re-engineered to prioritize centrally supplied items, reducing on-site cooking load.
Raw material stocking was monitored closely to avoid stock-out situations.
Centralized operating model, strong supply chain capabilities, and scalable platform enabled effective response to disruptions at airports.

subsections.label: Domestic network expansion
points: Opened outlets at newly entered airports Cochin and Navi Mumbai, and strengthened position at existing key airport hubs.
Operationalized new outlets across Terminal 1 and 2 of Delhi Airport, enhancing presence across all terminals at one of India's most strategic aviation hubs.
Mobilization of 76 travel QSR units in FY26 across Delhi, Mumbai, Ahmedabad, Cochin, and Navi Mumbai.

subsections.label: International expansion
points: Opened a lounge in Cochin and a new Kyra Lounge at Hong Kong International Airport in partnership with SSP and Airport Dimensions — an important milestone in the international lounge journey.
Expanded footprint in Malaysia to three airports after initial success there.
Opened a subsidiary in Dubai to look at Middle East opportunities.
Opened a subsidiary in Indonesia (a very large market) in the second half of last year.

International lounge strategy leverages decade-long relationships with airlines and card networks that transcend borders, plus SSP's existing presence, contractor/supplier relationships in these markets, giving TFS a 'clear right to win.'
International expansion typically starts on a stand-alone entity basis, but partners (e.g., SSP) may be brought in case-by-case based on rationale/benefits of each opportunity.

subsections.label: Airport privatization pipeline / regional risk
points: Government privatization pipeline for 11 airports was announced earlier and reinforced by government; management does not believe political changes at state level (e.g., West Bengal/Kolkata Airport potentially going to Adani) will change this privatization schedule based on public information.

subsections.label: International vs domestic traffic divergence
points: International traffic saw nearly a double-digit dip during March-April period due to Middle East conflict, more pronounced at airports with higher Middle East/international exposure (e.g., southern airports, Goa Dabolim).
Domestic traffic remained largely flat/robust despite the disruption.

Company is agnostic to whether consumer traffic is international or domestic since food spend is similar regardless of route; a domestic bounce-back (as travelers switch from international to domestic trips) could have a positive effect.

key_figures.label: Industry passenger traffic volume expected long-term growth

subsections.label: Concession fee / airport operator dynamics
points: Airport F&B and lounge sophistication is increasing as per capita income rises and consumers seek premium experiences, mirroring high-street trends toward experiential F&B spend.
Concession fee negotiations with airport operators are a normal, constant, portfolio-level exercise; some rentals go up, some down, but nothing dramatically different is occurring currently.
Company's commercial model and scale allow it to deliver profitability irrespective of these rental dynamics, as evidenced by delivering strong performance despite near-flat traffic this year.

subsections.label: Long-term aviation growth thesis
points: India's population flying penetration (~0.3x) is far below the US (5.5x) and China (~1x); China was at a similar statistic to India's current level about 10 years ago (~400 million passengers) and has since grown faster.
Rising per capita income, government initiatives fueling the aviation industry, and propensity to spend support continued strong long-term growth expectations for Indian aviation.

subsections.label: Steady-state LFL growth framework
points: LFL growth is historically composed of three components: passenger traffic (historically 7-10% per year in India, though FY26 was disrupted), plus price inflation (5-6%) and company-led initiatives (5-6%) such as brand changes, combo offers, new products, and premiumization.

Combining pax growth (9-10% historically) with the price+initiatives delta (7-10%) would imply an LFL in the range of 18-20% in a normalized environment, though management declined to give an exact forward number.
Analyst's suggestion of ~22-25% revenue growth (ex new airports) over a 3-5 year timeframe was not confirmed with an exact number by management, who instead reiterated the historical framework.

subsections.label: Competitive dynamics — retail/delivery entrants (Blinkit at Mumbai airport)
points: Mumbai airport allowing Blinkit to set up shop for delivery to gates is viewed as a retail-focused pilot, not a threat to TFS's F&B business.
Retail presence (chocolates, books, apparel) has always existed at airports with smaller footprints/limited products; Blinkit's dark-store-style model may address items that don't fit in such shops.

Food requires actual kitchen preparation (e.g., dosa, burger) unlike retail dark-store delivery; TFS already offers 'food at gate' and grab-and-go services, so no real overlap in consumer need state is expected.

Delhi T3 tender short-term extension period

subsections.label: International lounge expansion strategy
points: Based on initial success in Malaysia and Hong Kong, actively working towards expanding international footprint through new lounge opportunities.

Exploring wayside amenity opportunities at access-controlled expressways, a segment backed by strong government intent and investment plans in the medium-term; investments in this area have just started and it is viewed as a longer-term opportunity.

subsections.label: Delhi Terminal 3 concession renewal
points: Delhi T3 tender was expiring in February and was operating through a special purpose vehicle tied to that concession; a short-term six-month extension was granted.
When the concession comes up for renewal, TFS looks to bid through its existing JV, GHL.

subsections.label: People and culture recognition
points: Recognized as The Most Admired Retailer of The Year 2025 for Employee Practices at the MAPIC Awards.
Certified as a Great Place to Work for the second consecutive year.

subsections.label: Sectoral disruptions in FY26
points: India-Pakistan geopolitical conflict in May 2025 caused temporary air traffic disruptions at the outset of the financial year.
Second quarter impacted by reduced flight schedules due to maintenance and safety reasons following an aircraft crash in June of last year.
December 2025: airline-related operational disruptions arising from implementation of FDTL Crew Rest Regulations temporarily curtailed capacity at India's largest carrier.
Q4: traffic growth impacted by the ongoing Middle East conflict escalating in early March, weighing on international travel sentiment and impacting Gulf-bound routes and NRI travel.
Passenger traffic across network airports was broadly flat YoY in Q4; full year passenger traffic growth was muted at 1.2% YoY versus historical levels of 8-9%.
Passenger volumes recovered quickly following each disruption, reinforcing view that underlying demand remains strong.

subsections.label: Near-term macro outlook risks
points: Near-term macro environment likely to remain dynamic, driven by geopolitical developments, airline capacity changes, and input cost pressures, which can impact passenger traffic.
Company is closely monitoring these developments and has action plans and experience to execute efficiently to navigate the evolving landscape.

subsections.label: Input cost / inflation risk
points: Large part of real estate is on electric equipment by nature of being in airports, providing a natural hedge against input cost pressures relative to other F&B players.
Food inflation has not played out as significantly as in other parts of the economy; food inflation was around 3-5% in April.
Price hikes are taken in line with inflation; no dramatic food inflation currently observed.
Supply relationships are anchored in annual contracts with large suppliers, making the business model robust to inflation swings.
Anticipate a bit of inflationary impact going forward due to the Middle East conflict in terms of LPG price increases and other factors, but gross margin guided to remain in 80-83% range.

subsections.label: Litigation matters
points: One-time provision for litigation-related matters created on a prudent/conservative basis (INR212 million), even though management believes its position on these matters remains strong.

subsections.label: Q1 FY27 trading trends
points: January was strong; February started strong but showed muted growth in the last few days; March saw a dip largely fueled by a drop in international traffic due to the war; April was similar to or slightly worse than March, with depressed YoY growth given a strong April last year.
Early May signs show improving trends in passenger traffic, both versus last year's base and versus the March/April trend.

subsections.label: Outlook commentary
points: Management remains very confident in the long-term growth trajectory of the Indian aviation industry and will focus on capturing the opportunity while navigating short-term disruptions.
Will continue mobilization of committed pipeline across new airports and terminals.
FY27 passenger traffic expected at around 5% per public reports/expectations, recovering from FY26's disrupted 1.2%.
Gross margin expected to remain in the 80-83% range for FY27, factoring anticipated inflationary impact from Middle East conflict-related LPG price increases and other factors.
Capex expected to average INR50-60 crores per year, including FY27, predominantly for mobilization of units for Delhi, Cochin, and Noida concessions.
Trade receivables/debtor days expected to normalize to average of 40-45 days by H1 of current year (FY27) as EATS billing relationships mature.

Steady-state LFL framework: passenger traffic (7-10% historically) plus price/initiatives (7-10% combined) suggests a normalized LFL in the 18-20% range, though management declined to commit to an exact forward number.

guidance_ledger.statement: Gross margin will be in the range of 80% to 83% on an overall basis for next year, factoring in anticipated inflationary impact due to Middle East conflict LPG price increases and other factors.

Capex on an average to be in the range of INR50 crores to INR60 crores every year, which would also be the case for FY27, predominantly for mobilization of units to fund recent concessions of Delhi, Cochin and upcoming Noida projects.
Expectation of recent public reports is that FY27 may see about a 5% passenger traffic level, recovering from FY26's disrupted ~1.2%.
Debtor levels (which shot up to ~INR264 crores due to EATS ramp-up) expected to normalize by first half of current year back to average of around 40 to 45 days of outstandings.

Combination of pax growth (historically 7-10%) plus price/initiatives delta (7-10%) would give a normal perspective of around 18-20% LFL in a normalized environment; management would not call out an exact number.
More than 50 outlets currently in the pipeline; two more airports currently in the works in the coming months, in addition to Bhogapuram and Noida.
Roughly anticipation is about seven outlets happening originally at Bhogapuram; more mobilization details to be shared as date approaches.
Actively working towards expanding international footprint through new lounge opportunities based on initial success in Malaysia and Hong Kong; confident to deliver on this over the next few years.
Exploring wayside amenity opportunities at access-controlled expressways, a segment backed by strong government intent and investment plans in the medium-term.
May showing improving trends in passenger traffic versus March/April and versus last year's base; recovery expected once war-like situation resolves.

risk_register.risk: Middle East conflict / geopolitical disruption impacting international travel and Gulf-bound/NRI traffic
risk_register.note: Escalated in early March, weighed on international sentiment, caused near-double-digit dip in international traffic through April; continued into Q1 FY27 but showing signs of improvement in May.

risk_register.risk: India-Pakistan geopolitical conflict (May 2025)
risk_register.note: Caused temporary air traffic disruptions at the outset of FY26; a similar risk noted as impacting Q1 FY27 comparisons.

risk_register.risk: Aircraft crash-related maintenance/safety flight schedule reductions
risk_register.note: Impacted Q2 FY26 due to reduced flight schedules following the aircraft crash in June of last year.

risk_register.risk: FDTL Crew Rest Regulations implementation
risk_register.note: Temporarily curtailed capacity at India's largest carrier in December 2025.

risk_register.risk: Input cost / food inflation, including LPG price increases from Middle East conflict
risk_register.note: Food inflation around 3-5% in April; natural hedge from electric equipment usage at airports; annual supplier contracts provide robustness; anticipate some inflationary impact going forward but gross margin guided to remain in 80-83% range.

risk_register.risk: Litigation-related matters
risk_register.note: One-time provision of INR212 million created on a prudent/conservative basis; management believes its position on these matters remains strong.

risk_register.risk: EATS-driven receivables build-up
risk_register.note: Trade receivables/debtors rose to ~INR264 crores from average INR100-110 crores due to new banking relationship ramp-up (billing procedures, system integrations); expected to normalize to 40-45 days by H1 FY27.

risk_register.risk: Bank/credit card tightening on mass-market lounge access
risk_register.note: Ongoing for 18 months; mass market card access being restricted while premium card access is expanding, resulting in a net neutral-to-positive effect on lounge business given premium cardholders are frequent flyers.

risk_register.risk: Competitive threat from quick-commerce/retail entrants (e.g., Blinkit at Mumbai airport)
risk_register.note: Viewed as a retail-focused pilot with limited overlap with TFS's F&B business, which requires kitchen-prepared food versus dark-store retail delivery.

risk_register.risk: Airport privatization / regional political changes (e.g., West Bengal, Kolkata Airport)
risk_register.note: Management does not believe state-level political changes will alter the government's existing privatization pipeline of 11 airports.

themes.label: Passenger traffic disruptions
themes.note: FY26 full year passenger traffic growth was muted at just 1.2% YoY due to multiple disruptions (India-Pakistan conflict, aircraft crash, FDTL regulations, Middle East conflict), though volumes recovered quickly after each disruption.

themes.label: Network and outlet expansion
themes.note: System-wide presence now exceeds 550 travel QSR outlets and lounges across 20 airports, with 76 units mobilized in FY26 and 50+ outlets in the pipeline.

themes.label: Premiumization and brand portfolio growth
themes.note: Brand portfolio expanded to over 145 brands with new international partnerships (Gordon Ramsay, Nando's, Wagamama) strengthening premium positioning.

themes.label: International expansion
themes.note: Expanding footprint in Malaysia (3 airports), Hong Kong (2nd lounge), and new subsidiaries in Dubai and Indonesia, leveraging SSP relationships and a decade of airline/card network ties.

themes.label: EATS technology platform monetization
themes.note: EATS platform launched in FY26 enabling direct bank-to-lounge access, stabilizing well, with plans to add ancillary services, though it drove a temporary receivables build-up.

themes.label: Input cost / margin management
themes.note: Food inflation modest at 3-5% in April, natural electricity hedge from airport real estate, annual supplier contracts; gross margin guided to remain 80-83% for FY27 despite anticipated LPG-related inflation.

themes.label: Capital allocation discipline
themes.note: Zero-debt company with INR8.4 billion cash/investments, ROCE of ~40-45%, disciplined investment approach into international lounges, expressway amenities, with capex guided at INR50-60 crore/year.

key_takeaways: FY26 has been a defining year for us. Not only as our first full year as a listed company, but at the same time, being one that has been marked by multiple disruptions, ranging from war-like events to airline-related challenges, which tested the resilience and adaptability of our business in a dynamic operating environment.
Passenger traffic at TFS managed airports saw a muted growth of 1.2% year-on-year for the full year FY26.

Structural drivers which include low penetration of air travel, rising disposable incomes, expansion of airport infrastructure, and increasing propensity for travel, continue to support long-term growth in the sector.
In terms of network, our system-wide presence now exceeds 550 travel QSR outlets and lounges.

For the fourth quarter, our system-wide sales grew by 27.7% year-on-year, and consolidated PAT grew by 15.1% year-on-year. Similarly, for the full year, system-wide sales grew strongly by 25.4% year-on-year to INR32 billion, and adjusted consolidated PAT grew by 21.5% year-on-year to INR4.5 billion.
Gross profit margin increased to 87.3% compared to 83.0% in the same period last year.
As of March '26, trade receivables are higher by around INR1 billion, due to the initial ramp-up of our EATS business, which we are seeing to normalize by end of H1 of current year.
Our balance sheet continues to remain strong. We remain a zero-debt company with a healthy cash and investment position of approximately INR8.4 billion, as of March 31, 2026.
Company is happy to announce an annual dividend of 10.25 per share for FY26, subject to shareholder approval.

APTUS.company: Aptus Value Housing Finance India Ltd
APTUS.about: Aptus Value Housing Finance India Ltd is a Home Loan Company. Aptus has been formed to primarily address the housing finance needs of self-employed, low and middle income families primarily from semi-urban and rural areas. Company targets first-time home buyers where collateral is self- occupied residential property.

quarters.company: Aptus Value Housing Finance India Ltd
quarters.summary: Aptus reiterated FY27 guidance of 22-24% AUM growth with disbursements up 36% YoY in Q1 and July disbursements up 25% YoY, supported by branch expansion, connector channel traction and calibrated ticket-size/pricing strategy; management remains confident on spreads (~9%), opex/AUM (2.7%, within 2.6-2.8% guided range), credit cost (~0.6%, within 0.5%±10bps range) and ROE (20%+) for FY27, while flagging a temporary NBFC collection hitch at end-June that had improved by July and is expected to normalize over the next 2-3 quarters.

subsections.label: Profitability drivers
points: Net total income increased, supported by business growth and improving operating leverage.
Return on assets remained healthy, ROE stood at little over 20%.
Spreads remained largely stable despite rationalization of pricing on certain lending segments and prudent liability management, including reduction in cost of funds.
Margins remained resilient during the quarter.
Spread maintained sequentially at 9%, driven by decline in cost of funds to 8%.
Opex as percentage of AUM remained at 2.7%, within guided range.

subsections.label: Funding profile
points: Q1 funds raised primarily through a mix of term loans, securitization and direct assignment.
Liability profile well diversified across banks (60%), NCDs (14%), securitization (18%) and balance through NHB funding.
NHB proportion in funding at its lowest in many quarters; company has applied for INR500 crores NHB refinance facility, effective cost ~7.9% after concessions.
Strong liquidity position maintained providing ample headroom to support growth.

subsections.label: Tax rate
points: Lower effective tax rate (20% vs prior 23%) is due to benefit from aggressive write-off policies, which are tax-allowable; this rate is expected to continue.
Credit cost is largely on account of write-offs rather than provisions, and write-offs are eligible for tax allowance.

subsections.label: Provisioning approach
points: Stage 1 provision coverage reduced from ~40bps to 24bps due to good repayment behaviour of customers in Stage 1 category as per the ECL model.
Provision coverage was increased in Stage 2 assets where some deterioration/increase was seen.
Write-off policy: anything beyond 500-530 days DPD gets written off; policy will continue.

subsections.label: Assignment income normalization
points: Assignment income as % of off-book AUM has been declining from as high as 40% to current 23%, expected to settle around 12-15% given a potentially higher yield book versus other high-yield products.

subsections.label: AUM vs advances gap
points: Difference between AUM (INR13,648 crores) and advances (INR12,691 crores) of about INR957 crores is due to assignment done; direct assignment adds to AUM but moves assets off balance sheet, with balance sheet assets also reduced by ECL provision and unrecognized processing fees.

subsections.label: Interest rate sensitivity
points: 66% of borrowings are variable rate and 34% fixed; of the variable portion, 35% is linked to repo rate and 31% to MCLR.
An increase in repo rate could have some impact, but estimated impact on NIM/spread is only around 0.06%, not expected to be a major impact.

key_figures.label: Non-housing loan mix in HFC (Quasi HL/top-up/insurance)
Bounce rate differential (sub-INR7 lakh vs above)
Existing customer base availing external financial products

subsections.label: Two businesses, two benchmarks
points: Aptus is one company with two businesses (HFC and NBFC) and two benchmarks; HFC should be compared with HFC peers and NBFC should be compared with NBFC peers, given each has a distinct operating model and risk profile.
Consolidated asset quality should always be assessed in the context of the portfolio mix.
HFC quality of portfolio, overdues, NPA data and credit cost compare favourably with other comparable housing companies; NBFC data also compares well with other NBFCs of similar size.
On a combined/consolidated basis, asset quality metrics increased by 20 basis points primarily on account of collection issues, higher than peers even though each individual business compares well.

subsections.label: NBFC collection issue - explanation
points: Collection efficiency drop and 30+ DPD increase primarily driven by seasonality and some moderation in collections within the NBFC portfolio, not by deterioration in customer quality.
A temporary hit occurred at the fag end of June 2026 where some commitments were not honoured by NBFC customers; this got corrected and honoured in July 2026.
This is viewed as a days/timing mismatch or seasonal/month-end trend rather than a structural asset quality issue.
Increase in NPA is broadly on account of the NBFC NPA increasing; not seen as lumpy, not specific to any particular region or customer cohort.
Corrective steps already taken in NBFC collections; Stage 2 reduced by 15-20 basis points in July 2026; improvement expected to continue in August and September.
No calibration/reduction of NBFC disbursement business planned as a result of this issue.

subsections.label: Ticket size and asset quality
points: No differential credit behaviour observed across ticket sizes except bounce rates, which were 2-3% higher for sub-INR7 lakh loans compared to above INR7 lakh loans.
Impact of business below INR7 lakh (exited last year) is progressively coming down.

subsections.label: Product mix strategy (HFC vs NBFC)
points: HFC product mix (67% housing loan / 33% non-housing) is expected to continue as this level comfortably meets the principal business criteria (NHB norms).
Any new product expansion will be done in the NBFC, not the HFC, so as to not disturb the HFC's principal business criteria mix.
New product expansion in NBFC is not expected to negatively impact ROE/ROA unless leverage/borrowings increase; management indicated profitability impact could in fact be positive.
Quasi-home loans/LAP within the parent (HFC) growing faster than home loans attributed to a lower base effect, not to differential rate optimization strategy beyond incremental HL rate calibration.

subsections.label: Disclosure change
points: Management has decided that from September 2026 onwards, separate data for both HFC and NBFC companies will be provided in the investor presentation.

key_figures.label: Maharashtra & Odisha loan book as % of total

subsections.label: Branch expansion progress
points: 33 branches opened during Q1 FY27, taking total network to 372, against full-year target of 60-70 branches.
Of the 33 branches, 10-12 were opened before May 31 and the balance in June; rent and related costs will reflect fully in Q2.
Plan to add ~20-23 branches in Q2 and the rest in Q3.
New branches being opened in newer states like Maharashtra and Odisha; contiguous branch expansion strategy of going deep into a particular state is being followed.
Despite branch and IT investment, company remains conscious of maintaining operating cost as % of AUM and as % of income, seen as a competitive advantage.

subsections.label: Connector channel
points: Connector channel contributed 8% of disbursement during the quarter and continues to show encouraging traction; expected to be augmented across Q2, Q3, Q4.
Currently ~1,000 connectors across 333 branches, averaging 3-4 connectors per branch.

subsections.label: Competitive intensity by geography
points: Competition exists in states where Aptus already operates (peers opening branches and poaching field staff), but company is also expanding into states like Odisha and Maharashtra where competition is less intense.
Market opportunity is seen in both new and existing geographies despite competition.

key_figures.label: Branches to be added in Q2

subsections.label: Branch rollout timing
points: Of the Q1 branches, 10-12 were opened before May 31 and 21-23 in June, meaning full rent/operating costs of the June-opened branches will only reflect in Q2.
25 branches planned to be added in Q2 FY27.

subsections.label: Workforce attrition by level
points: Middle management attrition running at 5-6%.
Branch manager level attrition running at 10-15%.
Field level attrition running at 40-45%, down from a prior 50-60%.

subsections.label: Customer acquisition strategy
points: Diversifying sourcing channels through expansion of connector network and increased focus on digital marketing initiatives.

Continued focus on increasing average ticket size, supported partly by inflation and calibrated customer selection strategy, helping on-board higher quality customers while maintaining healthy business momentum.

Calibrated reduction in lending rates on select loan ticket sizes, together with strategy of increasing average ticket size, continues to support customer acquisition while helping on-board higher quality customers.

Rationale for new lending products beyond home loans and SME/LAP: company is targeting next stage of growth (from ~15,000-25,000 crore level to upwards of 50,000 crore over time) and sees need to diversify product range beyond distribution strengthening.

Opportunity identified via existing customer base of over 200,000 customers who are availing unsecured/secured financial products from other vendors; company sees opportunity to introduce appropriate products in NBFC to capture this demand and augment income stream.
Customer base itself growing at about 20% per year, providing base to leverage new products.

subsections.label: Attrition trends
points: Senior level attrition: negligible.
Middle management attrition: around 5-6%.
Branch manager level attrition: around 10-15%.
Field level attrition: around 40-45%, down from earlier 50-60%, still considered high.
Company has introduced retention incentives and insurance schemes to retain field employees.
Challenge: competitors entering states poach Aptus field officers first; company is launching alternate channels to reduce dependence on people.

subsections.label: Product expansion evaluation
points: Company evaluating opportunities to broaden lending portfolio beyond home loans and SME loans through introduction of new lending products, particularly in the NBFC business.
Product segment is in a formative stage; internal discussions ongoing on which products to enter; more colour expected in the next quarter's con-call.
In HL (housing loan) business, the company will continue to remain largely focused on HL, as the gap available for non-HL products within the HL company is limited.
New product expansion is intended to leverage existing large customer base and support growth alongside distribution expansion, not as a substitute for geographic expansion.
Distribution expansion (branches, online, business associates, field staff) will continue in parallel with product expansion.

subsections.label: Strategic pillars for growth
points: Growth anchored on: diversified mix, geographic expansion, productivity, digital excellence, and product expansion.

subsections.label: Interest rate risk
points: If repo rate increases, there could be some impact given 66% of borrowings are variable (35% linked to repo, 31% to MCLR), but estimated impact on spread/NIM is limited to around 0.06%, considered manageable.

subsections.label: Competitive intensity
points: Competition cannot be ruled out; competitors are opening branches in states where Aptus operates and poaching field staff.
Company mitigating by expanding into less competitive states (Odisha, Maharashtra) and following contiguous branch expansion strategy.

subsections.label: Attrition risk
points: Field-level attrition remains high (40-45%), posing a retention challenge, especially as new entrants poach trained field staff; mitigated via retention incentives, insurance schemes, and alternate (less people-dependent) channels.

subsections.label: NBFC collection/asset quality risk (temporary)
points: Temporary hit in NBFC collections at fag end of June 2026 due to unmet commitments, leading to higher 30+DPD, GNPA and Net NPA on a consolidated basis; management describes this as a timing/seasonal issue rather than a structural credit quality problem, with correction already visible in July.

subsections.label: Overall guidance confidence
points: Based on Q1 FY27 progress, management remains confident of delivering FY27 guidance across growth, spreads, operating cost, credit cost and profitability.
Last year's guided targets were achieved, providing confidence for FY27 targets.
Q1 disbursement growth of 36% YoY and July disbursement growth of 25% YoY provide confidence in achieving FY27 AUM growth guidance of 22-24%.
Yield moderation remained in line with expectations and was fully offset by lower cost of borrowing, resulting in stable spreads.
Credit cost guidance range of 0.5% plus/minus 10bps expected to be maintained for the next 3 quarters.
Liquidity, low leverage and negotiating power with lenders support execution of guidance without pressure to accept unfavourable borrowing terms.

guidance_ledger.statement: Confident of delivering 22% to 24% AUM growth as guidance, while maintaining focus on operating efficiency.
ROE remained above 20%, consistent with our profitability guidance.
Operating expenses to AUM remained at 2.7% within the guided range of 2.6% to 2.8%.
Credit cost stood at around 0.6%, in line with the guided range of 0.5% plus or minus 10 basis points for FY27; this range will be maintained for the next 3 quarters.
Full year target of 60 to 70 branches; 33 opened in Q1, ~20-23 planned in Q2, rest in Q3.
This quarter, minimum 25% to 30% increase over the last quarter, year-on-year basis will be happening this quarter.
We expect the NIM to be around 13%.
We expect the gross spread to remain at 9%.
There might be a 2.7% to 2.8% range, but we are strongly managing operating costs.
We expect credit cost to also range in between 0.5%-0.6%.
Assignment income margin should come down to around 12% to 15%.
Impact of a repo rate increase is likely to be around 0.06%, not a major impact on NIMs/spread.
Applied to NHB for INR500 crores refinance facility; effective cost of funds from NHB after concessions would be around 7.9%.
Evaluating opportunities to broaden lending portfolio beyond home loans and SME loans through introduction of new lending products; more colour to be given in next quarter's con-call.
Growth in number of customers will broadly be around the same [as value growth]; specific numbers to be discussed offline.
Continued focus on increasing average ticket size by at least INR1 lakh as compared to last year.
From September 2026 onwards, data for both HFC and NBFC companies will be given separately in the investor presentation.
We are very confident of maintaining a consistent growth of 20-plus percent.
As a strategy, we might not want to go beyond 10% of the total AUM at any point in time. Now currently, it is at around 5%.
The impact on the AUM on terms of yield will be around 0.1%... net impact on the yield will be around 0.18%.
The range of upfront income will be in between 25% to 28%... around 25% to 27%, 28%.
Even if that plays out... ROEs will be much above 20%. So, this is, we have actually planned it this way for the next 2 years as well.

risk_register.risk: NBFC collection weakness / temporary commitment miss at end of June 2026
risk_register.note: Led to 30+DPD rising to 6.87% from 6.21%, GNPA to 1.7% from 1.52%, and collection efficiency dropping to 98.52%; management calls this a temporary/seasonal issue, already improving in July with Stage 2 down 15-20bps and 30+DPD down ~20bps.

risk_register.risk: Interest rate increase (repo-linked borrowings)
risk_register.note: 66% of borrowings variable (35% repo-linked, 31% MCLR-linked); estimated NIM/spread impact from a repo hike limited to ~0.06%, considered manageable.

risk_register.risk: Competitive intensity from new entrants
risk_register.note: Peers opening branches in Aptus's existing states and poaching field staff; company mitigating via expansion into less competitive geographies (Odisha, Maharashtra) and contiguous expansion strategy.

risk_register.risk: High field-level employee attrition
risk_register.note: Field attrition down to 40-45% from earlier 50-60%, still considered high; retention incentives, insurance schemes, and alternate less-people-dependent channels introduced to mitigate.

risk_register.risk: NHB funding pipeline / reduced NHB proportion

key_takeaways: Aptus delivered a good start for the year with assets under management growing by 21% Y-o-Y.
Disbursements reached a good level during the quarter, and the growth was broad-based across geographies and distribution channels with continued demand from our targeted customer segment.
Return on assets remained healthy, while return on equity stood at little over 20%, ROE. Spreads remain largely stable.

Asset quality remained broadly in line despite continued business growth. Credit cost broadly contained at 60 basis points during the quarter, reflecting resilience of our underwriting framework and disciplined portfolio monitoring.
We remain confident of delivering 22% to 24% AUM growth as guidance, while maintaining our focus on operating efficiency.
Q1 disbursements grew 36% year-on-year, providing confidence in achieving the FY27 AUM growth guidance of 22% to 24%.

The collection efficiency stood at 98.52%, primarily impacted to an extent by seasonality and some moderation in collections within the NBFC portfolio. Consequently, our 30 plus DPD stood at 6.87% as against 6.21% in Q4 FY26.
Encouragingly, collection performance has improved in July with the 30 plus DPD declining by nearly 20 basis points.
We have already decided. We have already discussed, from September 2026 onwards, you will get data for both the companies in the investor presentation.

subsections.label: Profitability & Spreads
points: Spread improved to 9%, driven by decline in cost of funds to 8.1%.
Cost of funds benefit is what drove the 10 bps QoQ spread increase, not AUM mix shift toward self-employed/LAP segments (explicitly clarified: 'Not because of AUM mix').

Incremental cost of funds in housing finance is around 7.8-7.9% and in NBFC between 8.2-8.3%; management does not see reduction from these rates in coming quarters, and there is a likelihood of a slight increase.
Calibrated incremental lending rates on some housing loan ticket sizes are expected to reduce yields; impact on AUM yield estimated at around 0.1%.

Plan is to maintain borrowing cost around 8.1% next year; even if incremental cost of borrowing rises 0.2%, total borrowing cost would rise 0.08%, netting to ~0.18% yield impact, already factored into business plan.

On disbursement yields: from Jan 2026 rate cuts (for housing loan customers only) dropped Q4 disbursement yield by ~0.1%; further April calibration on certain housing loan ticket sizes expected to impact disbursement yields by 0.1-0.15% and loan book yield by ~0.06%.
No yield impact was seen from exiting sub-INR7 lakh ticket size since rates for below/above INR7 lakh were never different.

subsections.label: Asset Quality Detail
points: Improvement in collection efficiency (100.5% vs 99.1%) led to dip in 30+ dpd to 6.21% vs 6.48%.
FY26 GNPA increase to 1.52% (from 1.19% in FY25) is primarily due to marginal increase in NPA of the NBFC book.
Product-wise: ~two-thirds of portfolio is HL, one-third is NBFC business; NBFC business collections are slightly lower, and NBFC NPAs are ~20-30 bps higher than HL.

Geography-wise: Karnataka shows slightly lower collection efficiency vs other geographies; company is strengthening collection systems and recruiting more collection/monitoring staff there, and also growing branch presence and collection strength in that state.
Credit cost for FY26 remained at 50 bps, within guided range.

subsections.label: Direct Assignment / Off-Balance Sheet Strategy
points: DA is done for the non-housing loan book (yields ~17-17.5%), managed as a liquidity management tool and to improve principal business criteria for the HFC.
Company plans to maintain DA absolute value of INR160-180 crores per quarter and cap it at not more than 10% of total AUM at any point (currently ~5%).

Assignment gain/upfront income percentages (28% quarter, 42% full year per analyst calc) were clarified by CFO to be in the range of 25-28% for incremental DA going forward, driven by high spread between the ~17% non-housing book yield and the ~8% DA rate; management maintains margins will not decline as the back book builds and that the same momentum will continue into FY27, though this point was contested/unresolved with an analyst (Raghav) and management offered to follow up individually.

subsections.label: Funding & Liquidity
points: Q4 funds raised (~INR980 crores consolidated) via mix of NCDs, term loans and securitization.

NHB borrowing share declined to ~9% (from 15-18% previously) because other funding sources offered better cost than NHB during the year; company has filed for a INR500 crore NHB refinance facility expected in 2-3 months, and will draw on NHB again now that NHB has cut its prime lending rate, which would also help manage interest rate risk given book is ~82% fixed rate.

Securitization mix stated to be ~11% (not increased) - prior presentation had included DA within securitization/DA pie chart causing confusion; securitization offers slightly longer tenor debt versus other sources.
NCD/securitization cost in NBFC business quoted at ~8%-8.2%, with longer duration.

subsections.label: Operating Leverage/Opex
points: Cost-to-AUM ratio increased slightly to ~2.7% in FY26 from 2.6% previously; guidance range remains 2.6-2.8%.

Increase driven by: all-time high disbursement in the quarter (more employee payouts), 39 new branches opened, and higher IT spend (security, and initiatives around Ziva (launched April '24), account aggregator, unified lending interface (ULI) introduced by RBI, digitization of land records) - viewed as investment for future process improvements.

subsections.label: Repayment / Balance Transfer Trends
points: Pre-closures are around 7-8% of total AUM; of that, 65-70% of customers close loans out of their own funds when they have surplus, rather than balance transfer, reflecting customer behavior (own-fund-driven pre-closures) rather than interest-rate competitiveness.

Only ~2-2.5% of AUM is balance-transferred to other financial institutions - stable for 8-10 years; management does not view this as a threat and stated analysis across products (including HL) shows no significant difference in BT-out rates.

subsections.label: Demand Outlook
points: Affordable housing segment is viewed as structurally robust with strong potential for growth, reinforced by FY26 performance.

PMAY 2 scheme is for urban customers and has minimal impact for Aptus's rural/semi-urban customer base; PMAY rural coverage/subsidy (if launched) would need separate assessment as PMAY 1 rural subsidy was very minimal; as of now PMAY has no impact on Aptus.

key_figures.label: Tamil Nadu YoY loan book growth

subsections.label: Customer Mix
points: Self-employed is ~78% and salaried ~22% of disbursements; overall philosophy/mix is expected to continue unchanged (noted discrepancy vs presentation figure of 80% self-employed).

subsections.label: Tamil Nadu Performance
points: Tamil Nadu YoY loan book growth is around 14%, driven by structural changes in hiring and retention of correct people, despite still-elevated attrition.

Competition in Tamil Nadu is higher because Aptus has operated there 15-16 years and is often targeted by new entrants for talent poaching; incentive schemes and productivity-based monitoring systems have helped retain staff contributing to business.
Growth in Tamil Nadu is coming largely from existing branches, as new branch additions are focused on Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, Maharashtra and Odisha rather than Tamil Nadu.

Management does not see demand/penetration saturation as the cause of relatively lower TN growth versus AP/Telangana; market still has growth headroom, and the competitive staff-poaching dynamic is being addressed via retention schemes and insurance coverage schemes for staff.
Management aims to further increase the 14% TN growth rate going forward.

subsections.label: Ticket Size / Underwriting Strategy
points: Strategy is to increase average ticket size (housing loan, quasi home loan, small business loan) by about INR1 lakh every year, partly driven by inflation and partly to help onboard higher quality customers; field executives and branch managers are aligned to this.
Higher ticket size customers show higher collection efficiencies and lower bounce rates, reducing collection team effort.

Customer profile between current and higher-ticket customers is largely the same, but the higher-ticket segment shows relatively better credit bureau and account aggregator data, and management wants loan sizes to stay at least ~2x away from typical microfinance ticket sizes (INR3-3.5 lakhs) to avoid microfinance-type customer risk.

Improved data availability (credit bureau, account aggregator, ULI) is being used to strengthen underwriting standards for better-profile customers without materially increasing risk from ticket size growth (e.g., INR9 lakh to INR10 lakh average is ~10% increase but doesn't change inherent customer risk).

key_figures.label: Planned branches in Maharashtra & Odisha (of the 60)

subsections.label: Branch Expansion Plan
points: Branch network grew to 339 as of March 31, 2026, adding 39 branches in FY26.
Plan to open around 60 branches in FY27: 30 in Maharashtra and Odisha (new geographies), balance in Andhra Pradesh and Telangana.

A senior person with experience building business in MP and Chhattisgarh has been recruited for Maharashtra; if expansion progresses well, one or two branches may open in other new states, but timing depends on how the expansion plan progresses.

key_figures.label: Branches in Andhra Pradesh and Telangana

subsections.label: Geographic Expansion
points: Company entered newer states Maharashtra and Odisha in FY26 as part of geographic expansion strategy, alongside deepening penetration in existing markets.

Concentration is currently skewed to six states; management acknowledged concentration risk and cited new-state entry as a mitigant, with cautious, staged expansion based on how initial results in Maharashtra/Odisha play out.

Karnataka flagged separately as an area with weaker collection efficiency versus other geographies, being addressed via strengthened collection staff and monitoring, alongside continued branch/business growth there.

subsections.label: Four Strategic Pillars
points: Diversified mix: focus on self-employed customers across housing and business loans with strong presence in Tier 3/Tier 4 towns.
Geographical expansion: scaling beyond South India into Maharashtra and Odisha while deepening core markets.
Productivity: driving higher output through data-led, system-driven processes.
Digital excellence: leveraging technology across sourcing, credit and collections to improve speed, control and efficiency.

subsections.label: Growth Initiatives
points: Four targeted high-impact initiatives to accelerate growth: geographical expansion, increasing average ticket size, optimizing lending rates on certain loan ticket sizes for incremental customers, and expanding the connector channel.

Connector channel launched in January 2026 as an additional lead source over and above organic leads from sales offices and digital/referral channels; every branch manager is tasked with recruiting connectors, whose leads are passed to credit for processing; traction has been good, expected to evolve into a meaningful growth driver over time though still at a nascent stage.

subsections.label: Flagged Risks
points: Geographic concentration risk acknowledged given skew toward six states, being mitigated via expansion into Maharashtra and Odisha.

Tamil Nadu competitive intensity: new entrants target Aptus's staff for talent poaching due to Aptus's long-standing reputation/leadership in the region, creating short-term attrition/growth pressure, being addressed via retention and insurance coverage schemes.
Karnataka-specific collection weakness flagged as an operational risk being actively managed with additional collection staff and monitoring.

NBFC (non-housing) segment shows slightly higher NPAs (~20-30 bps higher) and slightly lower collections versus HL portfolio, acknowledged and being addressed via strengthened collection staff given the segment's growth potential and margins.
Elections and higher temperatures in Tamil Nadu were raised as a potential risk to collections/credit cost, but management stated no impact observed; collection data in Tamil Nadu remains better.

Interest rate/spread risk: incremental cost of borrowing not expected to decline further and could rise slightly (~0.2%), which combined with calibrated lending rate cuts could compress spread/yield by ~0.15-0.2%, already factored into business plan.
PMAY 2 (urban-focused) scheme not seen as a near-term risk/opportunity for Aptus given its rural/semi-urban customer base; PMAY rural subsidy impact (if any) would need future assessment.

key_figures.label: Implied disbursement target FY27 (per analyst calc)

subsections.label: Forward Growth & Profitability Confidence
points: Management expects further improvement in growth trajectory driven by expansion into newer states (Maharashtra, Odisha), deeper penetration in existing markets, channel augmentation, higher average ticket size, calibrated lending rates on incremental loans, and improved productivity.
Confident of maintaining consistent growth of 20%+ and best-in-class ROE of 20%+.

Even with a hypothetical spread compression of 0.15-0.2% and credit cost rising from 0.5% to 0.6%, management expects to compensate via productivity gains and possible opex reduction (opex could be ~2.7%), concluding ROA may decline slightly due to leverage but ROE will remain 'much above 20%' for the next 2 years.

ROE has progressively improved over the last 4-5 years from ~14% to over 20% in Q4 FY26 (21%), reflecting conscious focus on economic value add alongside growth; management believes enough strength has been built to sustain or improve this rate.

Management expressed high confidence in delivering the 22-24% AUM growth guidance, having worked out various strategies (new states, new branches in existing states, channel additions including connector channel, and rate optimization) to reach the implied ~INR5,000 crore disbursement target for FY27; strong MIS is used to track growth by segment.

guidance_ledger.statement: We expect to deliver sustainable AUM growth of 22% to 24% driven by these initiatives.
We are very confident of maintaining a consistent growth of 20-plus percent.
Best-in-class ROE of 20% plus.
Currently it is around 0.5%. We want to have a 0.5% plus or minus 0.1%.
Our guidance has always been to maintain between 2.6% to 2.8%.
As a strategy, we might not want to go beyond 10% of the total AUM at any point in time. Now currently, it is at around 5%.
We are planning to open around 60 branches in FY27; 30 branches will come in Maharashtra and Odisha, the additional. The balance will come in Andhra Pradesh and Telangana.
The impact on the AUM on terms of yield will be around 0.1%... net impact on the yield will be around 0.18%.
The likely impact on the disbursement yields is likely to be around 0.1%-0.15%. And on the loan book, it is going to be around 0.06%.
The range of upfront income will be in between 25% to 28%... around 25% to 27%, 28%.
We have already filed an application for a INR500 crore refinance facility from NHB. And hopefully, that will come in another 2 months, 3 months.
Every year, we want to increase this by INR1 lakh.
Even if that plays out... ROEs will be much above 20%. So, this is, we have actually planned it this way for the next 2 years as well.

key_takeaways: We delivered highest quarterly disbursements of INR1,242 crores.
This has come despite not sourcing any loans of less than INR7 lakhs.
Going further we are very confident of maintaining a consistent growth of 20-plus percent and best-in-class ROE of 20% plus.
We have delivered on our guidance across key levers, be it growth, spreads, costs and credit quality and will sustain this trajectory in the coming years.
AUM grew by 21% year-on-year to INR13,107 crores.
Collection efficiency stood at 100.5% versus 99.1% in the previous quarter.
We finished FY '26 with the GNPA 1.52% as against 1.19% in FY '25.

pressing_questions: Raghav (AMBIT Capital): questioned whether assignment income margins (28% for the quarter, 42% for the full year vs peers' 8-10%) should normalize downward as the back book builds up, since future income from newly assigned loans would not offset the existing back book in the denominator — management maintained margins on incremental DA would remain in the 25-28% range and offered to follow up individually as the exchange remained unresolved on the call.

Sonal (Asian Market Securities): asked about the discrepancy between consolidated (~INR15 crores) and standalone (~INR17 crores) credit cost for the quarter versus management's comment that the credit cost issue was more on the NBFC side — the question could not be resolved on the call due to audio issues and management asked her to follow up personally.

TEXRAIL.about: Texmaco Rail & Engineering Ltd is an engineering infrastructure co. & part of the Adventz Group, The co. is involved in the business of manufacturing Rolling stock, hydro-mechanical equipment, steel castings & construction of Rail EPC, bridges, and other steel structures. [1] [2]

quarters.summary: Q1 FY27 saw stand-alone revenue of INR753 crores (impacted by lower Freight Car and Infra execution) but improved EBITDA margin (10.8%), sharp PAT growth (+85.9% YoY) and a turnaround in Rail Infra profitability, alongside an order book of INR9,923 crores with 96.4% now private/export. Management guided to core-business EBITDA improvement of 1.2%-3% over the next 1-3 years, 15-20% topline growth in FY27/FY28, mid-teen EBITDA margin ambition by 2030, and continued diversification via JVs (Touax-Trinity leasing, Wabtec air-brakes, Nymwag, Saira Asia) and export expansion (South Africa, Cameroon).

subsections.label: Revenue drivers
points: Revenue impacted by lower execution of the Freight Car division and the Infra (Rail & Green, formerly Kalindee) business.
Electrical Infra business (Bright Power) continued to perform well, reflecting sustained execution across the Electrical Infrastructure business.

subsections.label: Margin drivers
points: EBITDA remained in line with the corresponding quarter of the previous year despite lower revenues, reflecting focus on cost optimization and margin improvement.
Rail Infra and Green business reported a positive EBIT margin compared to an EBIT loss in the corresponding quarter last year, marking a significant turnaround in profitability.
Continued focus on strengthening the balance sheet through improved cash management, disciplined debt payment and optimization of borrowing costs resulted in lower finance costs.
Reduction in finance costs supported PBT growth and margin improvement.

subsections.label: Other expenses
points: Rise in other expenses is due to freight charges paid on export wagon shipments; export income is included under total revenue while the associated freight charges sit under other expenses, explaining the increase.
