subsections.label: Order book strengthening
points: Order book provides multiyear execution visibility across Freight Cars, Infrastructure, Rail Infrastructure, Electrical and other businesses.

During the quarter secured a diversified set of Indian and international orders across freight rolling stock, railway signaling, electrification and transmission infrastructure, further strengthening execution pipeline.

subsections.label: Structural shift in Freight Car order book
points: Share of private sector and export orders has increased sharply from FY25 to FY26 to Q1 FY27, reflecting increasing participation of private customers in the freight rolling market.
This diversifies order book, revenue visibility, and supports margin improvement.

subsections.label: EBITDA improvement drivers
points: EBITDA improvement achieved through better product mix, moving to higher margin products, expanding into new geographical areas, and AI-enabled efficiency improvement actions.

subsections.label: South Africa order execution timeline
points: Order is executable in the next financial year; preparation work and prototypes to start this financial year.
Maintenance element covers 15 years and amounts to around 30-35% of the whole order value.
Value has probability to significantly improve as more scope is expected to be added.
Around 50-60% of the order received so far is expected to be executed by next financial year, with balance spread over subsequent years.

The value clarified (INR4,100 crores) includes only wagon pricing and long-term maintenance; locomotive component value is separate and to be finalized once a suitable tie-up partner is confirmed - this will be additional to the amount already notified.
Outstanding 6,000-wagon order book includes the South African order.

subsections.label: Other export orders
points: Other than South Africa, company is executing an order from Cameroon.
There are a few more export opportunities in progress that will be disclosed as they materialize.

subsections.label: Wagon tender expectations from Indian Railways
points: Management and analysts note expectation of Indian Railway wagon tenders given need to induct wagons and shift modal share from road to rail (targeted 40-45% per National Rail Plan).

DFCC becoming fully operational has shown tremendous traffic growth, along with further investment in railway tracks to decongest and support container trains, suggesting progressive demand from railways.
Company currently more insulated on the private/export side; expects private OEM investment momentum to continue regardless of railway tender timing.

subsections.label: Growth/order inflow guidance commentary
points: Company expects continuous strong order flow expectations 'every day'.
Near-term order inflow expected to be driven by private and export segments, with railway tenders as a potential additional driver if they materialize.

subsections.label: Bright Power (Electrical Infra)
points: Continued to deliver strong performance with revenue growth of 76.8% YoY, reflecting sustained execution across the Electrical Infrastructure business.
EBIT margin improved to 10.8%, representing an expansion of 150 basis points YoY.
Management aims to build Bright Power into a market leader as one of its short-term initiatives.

subsections.label: Rail Infra (Rail & Green, formerly Kalindee)
points: Revenue execution was lower during the quarter.
Reported a positive EBIT margin of 1.4% compared to an EBIT loss in the corresponding quarter last year - a significant turnaround in profitability.
Turnaround of the Rail Infra business was one of the company's short-term initiatives, now yielding results.

subsections.label: Freight Car Division (FCD)
points: Core business; management states no execution challenges other than supply chain-related stress this quarter.
Product mix shifting from commodity wagons to more specialized wagons; overall focus now on top line/bottom line/profitability rather than pure volume.
Every business vertical (including foundry) is undergoing a product-mix and customer-mix derisking as part of a transitional/inflection point for the company.

subsections.label: Wheelset supply
points: No wheelset supply challenges faced as of now; company depends on supply from Rail Wheel Factory (government mandate) but has sufficient stock for export and private orders.

subsections.label: Capacity positioning
points: Management notes capacity is 'elastic' and could theoretically make 15,000-16,000 wagons if focused on commodity wagons, but company is shifting toward more specialized, higher-value wagons where volume is less relevant than top-line/bottom-line/profitability outcomes.

subsections.label: South Africa facility plans
points: Reported news of a potential locomotive plant and wagon manufacturing plant in South Africa entailing investment of about INR200-300 crores; management declined to confirm the specific investment number, stating numbers change, but confirmed openness to establishing local facilities to meet localization requirements and support export/maintenance business.

Management emphasized that establishing a footprint in South Africa is more important than the investment amount itself, as investment will scale up as the business grows; this is seen as pathbreaking for an Indian company entering a developed export market with a sustained presence.

subsections.label: Export expansion
points: South Africa order (~INR4,100 crores) is a major lumpy export win including wagons and long-term maintenance, with locomotives under a separate mandate.
Cameroon order under execution.
Additional export opportunities are in progress and will be disclosed as they materialize.
Management sees export/maintenance business expansion as a strategic priority to improve export business in wagons and locomotives.

subsections.label: Supply chain stress in Q1
points: First quarter faced supply chain challenges due to high oil and gas prices, a general industry phenomenon (not specific to Texmaco), affecting critical component suppliers.
Company and its partners had to control consumption considering potential crisis, causing some stress around supply chain.
Despite this, profitability improved due to favorable order mix, cost reduction initiatives, and strong operational control.
Company has made alternative arrangements and expects output to improve from coming quarters, with improvement already starting.

subsections.label: Other expenses - freight charges
points: Increase in other expenses driven by freight charges paid for export wagon shipments; export income is booked under total revenue while freight cost sits under other expenses.

subsections.label: Leasing market strategy

Combination brings together Texmaco's manufacturing base (largest rolling stock manufacturer with over 200 years of combined design/engineering heritage), Touax's leasing expertise, and Trinity's status as one of the largest US manufacturer/leasing company with IP of more than 200 rolling stock designs.
Texmaco's stake in the JV reduces from 50% to 34% following Trinity's entry; the JV is a joint venture company, not consolidated within Texmaco standalone.

subsections.label: Vision 2030 / Texmaco 2.0 roadmap
points: Company reiterated Texmaco 2.0/Vision 2030 roadmap, focused on disciplined execution of order book, strengthening core railway business, and building complementary capabilities.
Aim is to support sustainable growth, enhance margin resilience, and reduce/protect against historical business cyclicality.
Company remains committed to executing the Vision 2030 roadmap with discipline and vigor, potentially achieving it earlier than planned.
Capability development over the last couple of years has positioned Texmaco to capitalize on the 8-point railway reform program announced by the Railway Minister as soon as policies come to market.

subsections.label: Defence strategy detail
points: Defence is described as a very broad area encompassing multiple products (software and hardware), ranging from aircraft to bullets; company has chosen specific synergistic areas with strong national security demand, not disclosed at this stage but to be revealed when appropriate.

subsections.label: Supply chain disruption
points: High oil and gas prices in Q1 caused a general industry-wide phenomenon of controlled consumption due to crisis concerns, creating stress in the supply chain for critical components including bogies and other parts sourced from partners.
This affected freight car production levels during the quarter, though not due to lack of orders.
Company has made alternative arrangements and expects output improvement from coming quarters (already starting to improve).

subsections.label: Provision for contingencies
points: The company has created a provision for contingencies of INR700 crores adjusted against free reserves, not through the P&L account.

This is a risk mitigation measure taken by the Risk Management Committee, Audit Committee and Board in context of ongoing geopolitical tension, trade uncertainties (energy supply, shipping, transportation, supply chain), and instances of large contracts not meeting expected outcomes due to uncontrollable external factors.
The company wanted to start the next phase of Texmaco (Texmaco 2.0) with an adequate safety net.
This provision has NO cash impact; it strengthens the balance sheet and improves risk-taking capability as the company bids for large contracts.
The provision enhances financial resilience, transparency and long-term sustainability while preserving visibility of underlying operational performance.

There are huge claims pending on projects, which take time to resolve; as visibility improves on ongoing/future contract implementation and claim realizations, there is scope for potential savings out of this contingency provision.
The provision represents a maximum potential risk under a worst-case scenario.

Statutory auditors qualified their report solely because the provision was adjusted against free reserves instead of being taken through the P&L account; management believes this is the right approach as the contingency is not related to any specific risk or time frame.

subsections.label: Balance sheet & leverage

Consistent reduction in debt levels underscores commitment to enhancing financial stability, ensuring long-term growth and improving shareholder value, positioning the company to satisfy growth aspirations for coming years.
Management expects the debt-to-equity ratio to remain within range even as capex for new growth areas is undertaken; the trajectory of debt is expected to not be disproportionate.

subsections.label: Indian Railways wagon order visibility
points: Management believes Indian Railway/Indian rail story will remain robust; a significant large order was first awarded in history in 2022-23.

Despite recent silence on new large orders, government has been working to decongest railway tracks via double lines/corridors, and WDFC and EDFC (dedicated freight corridors) are coming into/already in operation, setting up for a new order cycle.

Government is also encouraging private companies to invest and participate in the wagon system; sectors like cement, steel and automobile want efficient, sustainable, lower-logistics-cost transportation, driving private wagon order momentum.
Railway is working on policies for introduction of new design wagons.
No formal bid/tender has yet been carved out for the large expected order; management views the delay/silence as strategic rather than negative, expecting flow of orders to resume.

The National Rail Plan's published target was for railway's modal freight share to reach ~47%, versus the current ~27-28%, implying a large pending wagon requirement (previously estimated 3-4 lakh wagons could not be procured at once, hence phased tranches).

Large upcoming tender (if any) could come at once or divided into tranches, but underlying requirement of ~25,000-30,000 wagons/year over 5-7 years persists; timing of the tender is uncertain (analyst floated Q3 as a possible latest timeframe, but management would not confirm).

Order pricing is inclusive of rolling stock/wagons and 15-year maintenance.
Delivery timeline is as per the letter of award, targeted for completion by FY28 end, though modifications (more or less scope) are possible depending on customer situation.

Company declined to disclose exact revenue booking split across FY27/FY28, citing order value as the guide; a significant portion of revenues is expected to accrue largely in FY28, as delivery target aligns with FY28 order completion.
Locomotive production partner/strategy not disclosed at this time due to disclosure constraints; company confirmed it has capability/eligibility to execute, without naming partners.
On raw material cost pass-through: management indicated commodity/cost aspects are covered within the overall contract envelope, including localization considerations, without giving specifics.

A few more export orders are expected, with delivery also included in this year.

Private sector wagon volumes have varied (around 7,000 to 10,000 per year recently) but are expected to consistently remain in the range of 12,000 to 15,000 wagons per year going forward.

Wheel set dependency: historically dependent on Indian Railway supply since it was mandated for Indian Railway-ordered wagons; as private orders increase, government policy on import allowance vs. mandated domestic purchase is still evolving. As of now, government states Indian Railway has enough wheel capacity to supply, and there has been a ramp-up in wheel capacity by Indian Railway. subsections.label: Texmaco 2.0 / Vision 2030 strategy
points: Vision 2030 / Texmaco 2.0 is structured into three parts: (1) Strengthening the core, (2) Synergistic diversification, and (3) Breakout diversification.

Strengthening the core: involves inclusion of certain new product lines, enhancing design and engineering capability, and reaching newer regions, while derisking the core wagon/rolling-stock business, which is inherently cyclical though structurally relevant given rail's role in efficient/sustainable transport.

Synergistic diversification: leveraging government fund allocation toward railway safety, network and passenger mobility segments; company aims to build in-house technology products (propulsion, power electronics, signaling including Kavach, electronic interlocking, MSDAC, DPWIS) to gain more control over the ecosystem and deliver total solutions rather than remain a pure supplier.

Breakout diversification: entry into defense (leveraging technical/engineering maturity as a 'sunshine sector'), digital business via Global Capability Center (GCC) and the Invariz.ai platform (powered by ServiceNow, in collaboration with a company that also partners with NVIDIA), aiming to eventually provide services company-wide and to external clients across the globe.
Target: at least 2x topline growth and EBITDA margin improvement into mid-teens-and-above range, achieved over the next 12 to 36 months.
Strategy was crafted after thorough study considering various risks and volatility, with input from top global management advisory firms based in the US and Europe.

subsections.label: Defense foray
points: Company is at an advanced stage of technology tie-ups in strategic segments potentially including autonomous vehicles and other areas; specifics not disclosed on the call.

subsections.label: Wheel segment entry

Entry into wheels is expected to help internal consumption and is linked with some assured-offtake business opportunities being worked on.
Company considered supply-demand situation before pursuing wheel segment entry; it is described as a designed move into a railway adjacency, not a sudden decision.
Management remains open to meaningful collaboration and acquisition in the wheel sector and other business segments; certain prospects are being worked on currently.

subsections.label: Real estate / land bank unlocking
points: Company has identified unutilized prime land as a result of reorganizing and restructuring operations; this is not a distressed sale but land that has come up at good value.
A separate business division/development company has been created for real estate, as land development competency differs from wagon manufacturing.

Management does not expect this to be a long-continuing division given limited land availability; development will proceed via the company's own development entity, factoring in potential regulatory changes to the Land Ceiling Act.
Intent is not to sell land for quick money but to develop it given restructuring has freed up premium-located land.

subsections.label: Invariz.ai / GCC digital initiative
points: Invariz.ai platform launched in collaboration with an international American company (partner of NVIDIA), powered by ServiceNow, providing AI integration support.
Company will have access to AWS and Microsoft cloud in addition to existing cloud access.

GCC will work on specific portfolios rather than broad wall-to-wall services, including rail solutions/rail design, CRM (customer relationship management), cost reduction in production/operations, and even areas like reducing water consumption in fertilizer use cases.

Initially anchored by Texmaco for internal use, but the ultimate vision is to build a standalone commercial AI services business that goes to market and serves clients beyond Texmaco/Adventz Group, across the globe.
Company has started bringing in a deliberately optimized (not large) number of seats/team members, leveraging AI to keep headcount efficient; a strong core team is already in place.
A soft launch reportedly occurred toward the end of 2025 in Faridabad.

Global supply chain disruptions affected production schedules, shipping, transportation and exports during both the quarter and the full year.

points: Ongoing geopolitical tension and trade uncertainties (energy supply, shipping, transportation, supply chain) have led to instances of large contracts not meeting expected outcomes due to uncontrollable external factors, prompting the INR700 crore contingency provision.
Volatile and uncertain macroeconomic situation was cited as the reason for building an 'adequate safety net' as part of the Texmaco 2.0 transformation journey.

As of now, situation is going smoothly with intermittent tightness, and Indian Railway has been ramping up wheel capacity; outlook described as a 'mixed answer' with no full clarity yet.
Company believes it has sufficient backup via private orders and export business, reducing dependence on this potential wheel-supply crisis.

risk_register.risk: Wheel set availability / supply chain disruption
risk_register.note: Hampered performance especially in Q1 FY26; global supply chain disruptions affected production schedules, shipping, transportation and exports through the year.

risk_register.risk: U.S. tariffs impacting exports/business relationships
risk_register.note: Imposition of U.S. tariffs destabilized some strong business with the U.S., adversely affecting volumes, beyond company's control.

risk_register.risk: Geopolitical tension and trade uncertainty affecting large contracts
risk_register.note: Instances of large contracts not meeting expected outcomes due to uncontrollable external factors (energy supply, shipping, transportation, supply chain); led to INR700 crore contingency provision as a safety net for Texmaco 2.0 journey.

risk_register.risk: Auditor qualification on contingency provision accounting treatment
risk_register.note: Statutory auditors qualified the report because the INR700 crore provision was adjusted against free reserves rather than through the P&L; management defends the treatment as the provision isn't tied to any specific risk or timeframe.

risk_register.risk: Wheel supply policy uncertainty for private wagon orders
risk_register.note: Unclear whether government will allow private players to import wheels or mandate domestic purchase from Indian Railway as private wagon volumes rise; currently going smoothly with periodic tightness, and Indian Railway has ramped up capacity.

risk_register.risk: Cyclicality of core wagon/rolling stock business
risk_register.note: Freight rolling stock industry is inherently cyclical, prompting the company's strategy to derisk via diversification into adjacencies, EPC, signaling, defense, digital and other nonlinear growth drivers.

risk_register.risk: Pending claims settlement timing
risk_register.note: Huge claims for projects are pending realization, which takes time; management asks for patience as these could offer scope for savings against the contingency provision.

themes.label: Wagon order cycle visibility
themes.note: Management expects a large new Indian Railways wagon order cycle (1.5-2 lakh wagons near term) but no formal tender has yet been carved out; timing remains uncertain.

themes.label: Export/Africa expansion
themes.note: Large South African order (~INR4,000 crore) plus Cameroon and other African wins signal strong export traction and a track record across 16 countries.

themes.label: Supply chain disruption (wheel sets, tariffs)
themes.note: Wheel set shortages and U.S. tariffs hurt FY26 volumes and destabilized some U.S. business, impacting both quarterly and full-year performance.

themes.label: Diversification / Vision 2030 (Texmaco 2.0)
themes.note: Company outlined a three-pronged strategy (strengthen core, synergistic diversification, breakout diversification into defense/digital/real estate) targeting 2x revenue and mid-teens+ EBITDA margin over 12-36 months.

themes.label: Balance sheet deleveraging
themes.note: Net debt-to-equity ratio improved steadily from 0.22 (FY25) to 0.18 (FY26 end), supporting funding capacity for new growth capex.

themes.label: Contingency provision & risk management
themes.note: INR700 crore non-cash contingency provision against free reserves taken as a safety net amid geopolitical/trade uncertainty, leading to an auditor qualification.

themes.label: Bright Power (electrification) growth
themes.note: Infra/electrification Bright Power division grew 66% YoY to INR610 crore revenue with 10.8% EBIT margin, a bright spot amid overall revenue decline.

key_takeaways: Q4 FY26 revenue from operations was INR1,167 crores, down 13.3% YoY, due to challenging market conditions; EBITDA was INR116 crores (~10% margin, up 1.2% YoY); PAT was INR58 crores at a 5% margin, up 206 bps YoY; direct expenses decreased 0.8% QoQ.
FY26 full-year revenue from operations was INR4,377 crores, down 14% YoY; EBITDA was INR450 crores at 10.2% margin; PAT was INR194 crores at 4.4% margin.

Performance was impacted by supply chain issues (notably wheel set availability in Q1 FY26) and weaker Rail & Green Energy (Kalindee division) performance; however, the Infra/electrification (Bright Power) division grew 66% to INR610 crores revenue with a 10.8% EBIT margin.
Net debt decreased to INR444 crores; net debt-to-equity ratio improved from 0.22 in FY25 to 0.21 in H1 FY26 to 0.18 at FY26 end.

Company created a INR700 crore contingency provision against free reserves (no cash impact) as a risk mitigation measure amid geopolitical tension and trade uncertainty, ahead of the Texmaco 2.0 transformation journey; statutory auditors qualified their report solely due to this accounting treatment.

Delivered 2,196 freight cars in Q4 FY26 (Foundry division: 8,964 metric tons); full year delivery was 8,372 freight cars (Foundry division: 34,000 metric tons), lower than last year's record but still among top freight car manufacturers by market share.

Announced Vision 2030/Texmaco 2.0 strategy targeting 2x topline growth and mid-teen-and-above EBITDA margins over 12-36 months, structured around strengthening the core, synergistic diversification (signaling, propulsion, metro/urban mobility) and breakout diversification (defense, digital/GCC via Invariz.ai, real estate).

Won a large South African order worth ~INR4,000 crores for 2,200 wagons and 30 diesel locomotives with 15-year maintenance, to be delivered by FY28; company also progressing in Cameroon and expects a few more African orders.

subsections.label: PAT decline drivers
points: PAT decline of 14% YoY attributed to impact of higher finance costs to propel expansion during the period, as well as a deferred tax provision of Rs.2.2 crores as the company shifts to the new favorable income tax regime.
Finance charge increase of about Rs.2.5 crore over same time last year mainly on account of acquisition financing of Zillion which will get charged off.
Management noted the current quarter's higher 40% tax rate is a one-off from the regime transition; requested comparisons of PAT be made against Q4 rather than Q1 due to tax rate distortions.
Tax rate expected to reduce from 35% to 25%/around 30-35% from Q2 onward under the new tax regime, which will substantially improve PAT going forward.

subsections.label: Other income sustainability
points: Other income of Rs.4.79 crores includes about Rs.2.7 crores from mutual funds which is expected to be sustainable in other quarters; overall run-rate expected around Rs.3.5-4 crores per quarter.

Rs.21 crores already received from EM Bypass sale; additional Rs.50 crores expected by year-end, adding to the existing ~Rs.97 crore mutual fund corpus and increasing other income further alongside good EBITDA performance.

subsections.label: Mutual fund portfolio
points: Portfolio consists of regular (not direct) mutual funds including ICICI All-season bond fund growth, ICICI 3-6 months Debt Index Fund growth, 360 One Bond growth fund, and Nippon fund (~Rs.23 crores at 5.91% yield); ICICI 3-6 fund yields about 7%.

Regular (not direct) mutual funds are used to keep money readily available for inorganic growth/acquisition opportunities; management stated net return from mutual funds is competitive versus market and disputed claim of paying higher fees.

subsections.label: Occupancy and ADR dynamics
points: Company retained India's leading occupancy position of 92% and maintained leadership in RevPAR in the upper upscale segment despite headwinds from West Asia crisis, near-flat air traffic growth, high energy cost and supply chain disruptions.
Since near-peak occupancy is achieved, growth is expected to be driven by ADR going forward.
Domestic passenger traffic has been flat and international air traffic into India declined by almost 10% during the quarter, contributing to ADR pressure; supply-side disruptions also cited.
Excluding Delhi, there has been deep contraction in air passenger traffic across other major cities (Mumbai -3.5%, Hyderabad -12%+, Chennai -13%).

Q2-Q4 expected to benefit from BRICS Summit in Delhi (tourism section already started), Aero Show in Bangalore, Bharat Mobility Expo (at Pragati Nagar and Yash Bhoomi near Dwarka), and around 40 wedding dates between November and March, driving occupancy and ADR upward.

Management expects ADR growth to be in the high single digits going forward, aided also by stabilization of palace properties (Ran Baas Patiala at ARR of 33,000; Lotus Palace Chettinad at ARR of 13,000).

subsections.label: Flurys expansion detail
points: Flurys, a 100-year-old brand, expanded beyond heritage Kolkata presence with a new cafe opening in Gurugram, marking start of Delhi NCR expansion.
During the quarter, a new outlet was added at Inorbit Mall Visakhapatnam.

Subsequent to the quarter, further expansion into North India with the opening of the first stand-alone Flurys Cafe in Gurugram in August; Flurys to enter New Delhi with openings at Green Park in September '26 and Greater Kailash 2 in October '26.
Growth plan for FY27: 3 more outlets in Pune (total 5), 3 in Mumbai, 5 in Hyderabad, 7 in NCR/Delhi (already signed), 4 in Bangalore (new market entry).

Exploring tie-ups: with Adani Group for airports across India; close to signing all-India deals with Phoenix Mills and DLF; close to finalizing deal with PVR that could open 10 outlets simultaneously.
Growth strategy considered steady since 2019 (17 outlets) to current 111 outlets at a CAGR of 21.5%; expansion continues via an asset-light model.
As Flurys celebrates 100 years next year, plan is to have 100 outlets of Flurys in West Bengal alone by the centenary.

subsections.label: F&B and lifestyle ecosystem
points: F&B remains an important part of overall hospitality ecosystem, contributing approximately 43% of total revenue during the quarter.
Restaurants, nightlife and experiential dining formats continue to complement the hotel business, providing additional revenue and customer engagement.
Ran Baas - The Palace - Patiala remains featured in the Pre-Versailles Global List of Architecture and Design Hotels; hosted the Rayleigh and Chateau Annual Regional Conference in July.
Several Zone by The Park and Zone Connect properties received TripAdvisor Traveler Choice Awards and recognitions during the quarter.

subsections.label: EM Bypass Calcutta development
points: Integrated hospitality-led mixed-use development comprising 218 hotel rooms and 69 service apartments; witnessed record-breaking sales of service apartments with 33 apartments already sold and healthy realization of approximately Rs.20,633 per square foot.
Project slated to be completed by early 2030.

Strong sales momentum significantly improving cash flows and providing additional support for ongoing growth initiatives; expected cash flows of Rs.70 crores this year, almost Rs.120 crores next year, followed by another Rs.100 crores in the third year and remaining Rs.30-40 crores in the fourth year, totalling Rs.300-325 crores company share.

Return on capital employed for the company currently roughly 9-10% could potentially double to past 20% as this project goes live, given hotel development being largely funded via apartment sale proceeds.
Calcutta has the lowest inventory among metro cities (only 5,111 keys) with limited new supply, expected to drive very high performance at the second hotel in EM Bypass upon opening.

subsections.label: Park Mumbai at Juhu
points: 78-room project has completed design phase and is targeted to launch in October 2027, strengthening presence in an important hospitality market.
Acquisition cost was roughly below Rs.40,000 per square foot versus market rates of plus Rs.1 lakh per square foot, considered a great acquisition; valuations expected to rise as Juhu rules change.

Property originally had 60 service apartments, now being converted into 70-80 room hotel; F&B strength (43% revenue share) and nightlife leadership (rooftop bar planned) expected to drive strong performance.

Juhu/Mumbai considered high potential market with ARRs currently in range 18,000-20,000, expected to rise further; limited hotel supply coming up in Juhu; Bombay market ARRs rising in double digits (10-15%).

subsections.label: Vizag development
points: 100-room hotel project has made good progress, with project teams on site; expected to launch during the course of this month (August) and be completed by early 2030.
Very limited/short inventory in Visakhapatnam expected to support high performance and high ARRs upon opening, aided also by location.

subsections.label: Malabar House Fort Kochi acquisition
points: Acquisition of Malabar House in Fort Kochi currently in progress; property comprises 17 keys on approximately half an acre of land; expected to be completed by October-November 2026.

subsections.label: Pune land/FSI
points: FSI available on Pune land has changed from 2.5 lakh sq ft to 6.7 lakh sq ft, expected to add immense value.
Plan is to utilize 2.5 lakh sq ft of FSI towards hotel development and 4 lakh plus sq ft towards residential development, enhancing value for the company.
Similar mixed-use development model as EM Bypass planned in Pune given land/FSI advantage.

subsections.label: Long-term portfolio ambition
points: Longer-term ambition to build a larger, more scalable hospitality platform with more than 6,000 keys by FY2030 (as stated in opening remarks) further detailed as 6,719 keys / 87 hotels over next four years, comprising 2x growth in owned assets and 3x plus growth in the asset-light model.

Growth strategy remains focused on expanding selectively across attractive markets while maintaining capital discipline; increasing opportunities to scale through managed properties and other asset-light formats particularly in emerging leisure, pilgrimage, and urban destinations.

subsections.label: Property maturity/stabilization
points: All current properties are in mature stage or entering maturity; Ran Baas Palace Patiala and Lotus Palace Chettinad (opened last year) are entering maturity phase, with occupancy expected to stabilize fully during the course of the year.
15-room Vembanad Lake property acquired this year is also likely to stabilize during the year; season starts in Q3 and peaks in Q4.

Calcutta and Vishakhapatnam properties under development expected to open in 2030; normally hotels take 2-3 years to stabilize, but due to demand-supply imbalance (Calcutta lowest inventory among metro cities, Vizag very limited inventory), both expected to open with high performance and high ARRs.

Stabilization period depends primarily on market selection; in high potential markets (e.g., Mumbai, Pune, second Calcutta hotel) stabilization can occur within 1-1.5 years or even outperform the market from year one, whereas resort/new markets (e.g., Chettinad, Patiala) take about 2-3 years.

subsections.label: SAP S4 HANA implementation
points: During the quarter, the company completed the implementation of SAP S4 HANA for Finance.
This will strengthen financial controls, improve the quality and timeliness of reporting, and enhance operational efficiency across the organization.
Investments in internal systems and processes viewed as increasingly important as the company scales its portfolio.

key_figures.value: 1.5 crores to 2 lakh per sq ft

subsections.label: Broader hospitality environment
points: Domestic travel remained largely resilient, supported by leisure travel, domestic corporate movement, weddings, and social occasions, providing a strong foundation for industry and company growth.
Demand-supply environment remained favorable with limited additions of quality hotel rooms across several key markets.

Improving connectivity and rising travel aspirations are broadening opportunity for branded hospitality beyond traditional metropolitan markets, with select Tier-2 and Tier-3 cities emerging as increasingly attractive destinations.

Structural opportunity for Indian hospitality remains strong; combination of rising domestic travel, increasing preference for branded accommodation, improving connectivity, and measured supply addition expected to support the sector over the medium to long term.

subsections.label: Portfolio positioning
points: Focus remains on building a differentiated hospitality platform across hotels, food, beverage, and lifestyle experiences.
Portfolio across luxury, upscale, and upper mid-scale segments allows addressing diverse customer requirements while maintaining distinctive brand positioning.
F&B and entertainment ecosystem (restaurants, nightclubs, bars) remains an important differentiator, allowing participation in the broader lifestyle opportunity alongside core hotel business.
Company is a market leader in nightlife and F&B (43% revenue share).

subsections.label: New market entry evaluation (Juhu case)
points: Juhu is described as a high-fashion, high-Bollywood, strong market for good hotels/boutique hotels, with ARRs in range of 18,000-20,000, expected to rise; Bombay real estate is best-performing market with properties selling at Rs.1.5 crores to Rs.2 lakh per sq ft in some cases.
Company evaluates new markets based on location quality and market potential; in high potential markets, stabilization occurs faster (1-1.5 years) and can outperform market from year one.

subsections.label: 3G / 3P organizational principles
points: Journey continues to be guided by the 3G principles of growth, governance and green, providing strategic foundation for the business.

Focus on purpose, people and performance (3Ps) defines how strategy is translated into action; together the 3Gs and 3Ps shape an organization ambitious in growth, responsible in operations, committed to people, and focused on delivering sustained shareholder value.

subsections.label: Capex funding plan detail
points: CAPEX guided for Pune (200 rooms), Navi Mumbai (250 rooms), Vizag (100 rooms), EM Bypass (220 rooms) and Jaipur (150 rooms) projects at approx. Rs.1.2 crore per room, totaling Rs.1,140 crores.

Additional acquisition costs: Zillion acquisition (~Rs.210 crores), Juhu renovation (~Rs.80 crores), Kochi acquisition (~Rs.64 crores), combining to about Rs.350 crores, which will be funded from EM Bypass proceeds.
Additional operational CAPEX of Rs.40 crores per year for 4-5 years for hotels, plus Rs.40 crores per annum for Flurys to help achieve target of 400 outlets by FY30-31.
Net CAPEX requirement after EM Bypass contribution is about Rs.1,500 crores; with current average EBITDA of Rs.240-250 crores, company should be able to finance about Rs.1,300 crores over 4-5 years.

Any incremental Rs.100-200 crores requirement can be financed given very low net debt-to-EBITDA; within this year, about Rs.200-250 crores of CAPEX requirement is expected; long-term financing line already tied up for Zillion Juhu property.

subsections.label: Mixed-use development model / ROCE strategy
points: Experience from EM Bypass service apartment sales suggests mixed-use development could be the right way forward, as hotel-only development typically yields lower/longer return on capital employed unless in high-potential markets.

Cost of land in India is significantly higher than the ideal (should not exceed 20% of project cost), reducing ROCE proportionately in a hotel-only model; mixed-use model helps offset this via monetization.
Similar mixed-use model being planned in Pune given the land/FSI advantage; overall company return on capital employed (currently ~9-10%) could roughly double by 2030 as such projects go live.

key_takeaways: 33 of the 69 apartments available for sale have been sold in our EM Bypass Hotel and Residential project at Kolkata. This will lead to improved cash flow of Rs.70 to Rs.80 crores during the course of the year, of which Rs.21 crores is already received.

Despite headwinds on account of West Asia crisis, near-flat air traffic growth during this quarter, high energy cost and supply chain disruptions, we have retained India's leading occupancy position of 92% and have maintained our leadership in RevPAR in the upper upscale segment.

In Q1 FY27, we have delivered operating revenue of Rs.167 crores reflecting a growth of 8% year-on-year. EBITDA stood at Rs.47 crores up 3% year-on-year with EBITDA margin at 28.12%. At the consolidated level, revenue achieved was Rs.172 crores up 10% and EBITDA at Rs.52 crores up 8% over last year.

PAT for the quarter stood close to Rs.12 crores, a decline of 14% year-on-year with PAT margin close to 7%. This decline is due to the impact of higher finance costs to propel expansion during this period as well as deferred tax provision of Rs.2.2 crores as the company shifts to the new favorable income tax regime.
The debt-to-equity ratio remains extremely favorable at 0.12 and net debt-to-EBITDA at 0.70.
The brand now has 111 outlets across cafes, kiosks, and tea rooms. By the end of this year, we are working to deliver 29 additional outlets to take the overall Flurys store count to 140 stores.

Looking ahead to FY27, we now have a pipeline of 12 hotels comprising of 472 keys for this year. These additions are expected to take our portfolio from the current 42 hotels with 2,677 keys to 3,149 keys by the end of FY27.

Overall, over the next four years, we plan to double the number of hotels from 42 hotels with 2,667 keys to 87 hotels totaling to 6,719 keys. 2x growth in our own assets and 3x plus growth in the asset-light model.
At Pune, the FSI available to us on our land has changed from 2.5 lakh square feet to 6.7 lakh square feet. This will add immense value to our business.
pressing_questions: ADR growth of 2%, if you can just guide us some more on this, what would have been our ADR growth in absence of the disruptions we had? Some of you are talking about lifting kind of growth on top line. So, if I want to achieve that, 2% I think will be behind the schedule. So, can we read that?

As mentioned in the opening remarks, we are now at 111 outlets. A few quarters before, we had aggressive plans on expansion of Flurys, but number-wise, we are yet to get there. So, what is really missing here, sir, if you can elaborate?

I just wanted to ask what proportion of your existing hotel portfolio is currently mature and how much of your performance improvement over the next 2 years would simply come from the newer properties turning mature.
How long does it typically take for a newly opened property to reach its targeted operating metrics and what is the trend for this stabilization period? So, is this decreasing in the coming years?

Could the service apartment component at EM Bypass ultimately generate a higher return on the underlying land than a conventional hotel development? And is this influencing how you evaluate future land parcels?
I want your capital guidance updated for FY27. If you can provide the split between old project, maintenance capital and refurbishment.
You know year on year revenue increased by 8% but PAT is contracted to 14% provided a 60% spike in interest cost. So, I just wanted to ask can you elaborate on this?
How do you assess a new market before committing an expansion to it? What are the thresholds or the return expectations you set that determine whether you enter or don't enter a particular market?

While looking at your balance sheet I could see that the mutual funds you have are regular mutual funds and not direct mutual funds. So, one of the questions was why is that? ... why aren't we buying direct mutual funds? And why are we paying higher fees by buying regular mutual funds.

quarters.summary: FY26 revenue crossed ₹700 crore for the first time (up 12% YoY) with steady occupancy/RevPAR leadership; management expects demand to improve as Middle East war/geopolitical disruptions ease, with continued expansion pipeline (EM Bypass, Vizag, Juhu, Malabar House) and a target of surpassing 6,000 keys by FY30 (from 2,677 currently, doubling hotels from 42 to 85 over four years). Outlook for FY27 includes adding 12 hotels (472 keys) taking total past 3,000 keys, Flurys expansion to 140+ outlets, and continued asset-light, capital-efficient growth funded largely via internal accruals.

subsections.label: Q4 & FY performance drivers
points: Q4 continued to reflect resilient operating performance across the portfolio, with the company maintaining its leadership position in occupancy and RevPAR.
The sale of service apartments at EM Bypass Kolkata has exceeded expectations, resulting in substantial improvement in this year's cash flow.
The 75% dividend payout approved by the board reflects the strength of the balance sheet and growth momentum.

Although profitability during the year was impacted by war and tension in the Middle East, higher depreciation and finance costs linked to ongoing expansion initiatives, the overall operating environment remained healthy, and demand trends across most key markets continued to be encouraging.

subsections.label: Capital structure and funding
points: Interest cost at present is 8.35%, the MCLR of the bank, and is expected to remain under that level.

Total capital requirement across development pipeline (Pune, Mumbai, Vizag, EM Bypass, Jaipur - 950 rooms) plus Zillion/THALI acquisition and normal/Flurys capex totals approx. ₹1500 crores, being funded mostly through internal accruals even assuming ₹250 crores EBITDA projection for five years.
Company keeps a line of credit in addition to ₹80 crores cash and cash equivalents in the books.

This year's increase in interest cost of ₹7 crores came mainly from acquisition financing of Zillion; because it was acquisition finance it is charged off to P&L, whereas project financing interest will be treated as IDC and not charged to P&L, keeping P&L under control.

subsections.label: Demand-supply dynamics
points: There is a significant demand-supply gap and it continues to be there; India has only 2,16,000 rooms in the branded category and not much supply is coming in, with supply lower by at least 200 to 300 basis points, supporting ARR growth.
Kolkata has very limited supply at the moment (5,101 keys) with only about 1,702 keys expected over the next five years, keeping the outlook for the market very positive.
Government change in West Bengal expected to drive stability, more investment, and more projects across the state including North Bengal, propelling growth.

subsections.label: Cancellations and recovery
points: Cancellations occurred because of the geopolitical situation and war in the Middle East, with significant cancellations in Delhi and Hyderabad; conditions have stabilized and improvement is expected going forward.
Two disruptions impacted the year: Operation Sindoor in Q1 and the Middle East war starting late February continuing into April; a 60-day ceasefire extension is expected to normalize the situation.
Occupancy in Delhi and Hyderabad has recovered to over 90% after the pressure from the war; ministries and corporate contracts have been re-established and RFPs are being pursued aggressively.

subsections.label: Hotel portfolio performance
points: Brands continue to demonstrate strong market positioning across several key cities, with year-round occupancy at 91% and RevPAR leadership across the upper upscale segment.

Performance outperformed the industry across several major markets including Kolkata, New Delhi, Bangalore, Goa, Navi Mumbai, and Vizag, reinforcing the differentiated design-led hospitality model and lifestyle-led guest engagement strategy.
Park Calcutta achieved 100% occupancy for the quarter and year, maintaining its record of world-leading occupancy for 10 years except the two COVID years.

Park Calcutta's high occupancy is attributed to an effective revenue management system, a dedicated team, being an entertainment destination, and exceptional location; it has a 30% repeat customer base, among the highest in the country/world.

Park Calcutta's T-RevPAR (total revenue per available room) of ~₹24,000 is the highest in the central business district, exceeding major luxury brands; beverage revenue is higher than room revenue in most months.

Ran Baas Palace and Lotus Palace, Chettinad are stabilizing; Patiala occupancy expected to reach close to 50% particularly during October-December season, considered very successful for high-ARR leisure properties.
Purity, the 17-room property in Cochin on Vembanad Lake, operated only 3 months in FY26 and will add to growth this year.

subsections.label: F&B ecosystem
points: F&B continues to be a significant contributor to the overall hospitality ecosystem and a key differentiator, supported by healthy traction across restaurants, nightlife, and experiential dining formats.
Several signature outlets — Dusk at the Park Navi Mumbai, Aqua at the Park Bangalore, Aqua at the Park Navi Mumbai, and Someplace Else — received industry recognitions during the quarter.

subsections.label: Flurys brand performance
points: Flurys grew to 110 outlets, reflecting steady and disciplined scale-up supported by improving consumer traction and brand affinity.
Flurys delivered 29% YoY revenue growth in FY26 while deepening customer engagement across markets.
Mr. Rohit Kakra appointed as new COO of Flurys effective April 2026, bringing 23 years of experience, previously COO at Costa Coffee and Pizza Hut.
Flurys is a profitable business; segment-level EBITDA not disclosed separately, but brand expected to further expand and maintain growth momentum.

subsections.label: Awards & recognitions
points: Ran Baas The Palace, Patiala featured in the Prix Versailles global list of architecture and design awards and was awarded One MICHELIN Key.
The Lotus Palace, Chettinad featured in Travel + Leisure's list of 100 Best New Hotels in the World.

subsections.label: Development pipeline progress
points: Kolkata residential and hotel project (EM Bypass) has had a successful start with apartments sold at market-leading rates; second block of apartments expected to launch September-October this year, with rates expected to further increase, closer to the festive season.

Vishakhapatnam (Vizag) 100-room development to commence construction very shortly; environment clearances now in place, project launch expected on ground August 2026; project delayed from earlier guided early 2029 to early 2030 due to delay in environmental clearance, though rest of permissions are on the way; project does not have a basement and construction starts straight at ground level which could allow faster completion.
Boutique property in Juhu (Park Mumbai) finalized design with 78 rooms; project commencement planned June 2026, completion targeted by March 2027.

Malabar House (Purity, Cochin) acquisition agreement signed in December 2025/January, delayed due to bank permission required for external payment to a foreign seller; permission now granted, final documentation ongoing, acquisition expected to conclude within June 2026 (kept in Q2 to be safe); Malabar House is a Relais & Chateaux hotel popular with foreign travellers, expected to help drive ARRs.
Signed agreement with Luxmi Tea for an asset-light Park brand hotel in Siliguri, within one of their best tea gardens.

subsections.label: Expansion strategy and key targets
points: During FY26, 7 hospitality properties were launched adding 283 keys, including three hotel launches during the quarter: Zone by the Park Darjeeling, Zone Connect by the Park Gangtok, and Zone Connect by the Park Katra.
FY27 plan to add 12 hotels totalling 472 keys, of which 8 would be asset-light, taking total key count past 3,000 by FY27.

Over the next four years, plan to double the number of hotels from 42 to 85, taking key count from 2,677 to 6,635; a 2x growth in owned hotels and 3x growth in asset-light model under Zone by the Park and Zone Connect by the Park.
FY30 vision targets surpassing 6,000 keys, expanding presence in the fast-growing mid-market segment and accelerating asset-light growth strategy.
West Bengal's combined 400 rooms are expected to double over the next four years via both ownership (EM Bypass 218 keys) and asset-light models (e.g., Siliguri with Luxmi Tea).

New hotels being planned are larger formats (200+ rooms) with premiumization: Kolkata EM Bypass 218 rooms, Pune 250+ rooms, Navi Mumbai 250 rooms (using additional FSI of 3,80,000 sq ft), moving towards super-luxury positioning to drive higher ARR.

subsections.label: Room renovation and product improvement
points: Room renovations planned across Chennai, Bangalore, Kolkata, Vishakhapatnam during the year to improve product and drive ARR.

At Park Calcutta, plan to refurbish and redo 20 rooms to raise product quality and take ARRs up; one bar already refurbished, engaging specialist companies to improve cocktail and food offerings at bars.

subsections.label: Sustainability
points: Under the Park Planet Plus program, the company has reached 100% or near 100% green mobility in guest services in owned hotels.

key_figures.label: Flurys West Bengal target for centenary year
Flurys total outlets planned over 4 years

subsections.label: Flurys geographic expansion
points: Flurys plans to add more than 30 outlets over the next 10 months, entering new markets: NCR (8 outlets), Pune (5 outlets), and Bangalore (4 outlets), plus plans for West Bengal and Hyderabad.
In preparation for its centenary year in 2027, Flurys plans to reach 100 outlets in West Bengal alone.
Expansion largely cafe format, with at least two flagship stores expected in Delhi NCR market; cafe format considered the most promising going forward.
Plan to take Flurys from current 110 outlets to 140+ outlets over next 10 months, and add 40-50 outlets over the next four years to 2030.

subsections.label: SAP S/4HANA implementation
points: Successfully completed implementation of SAP S/4HANA during the year, which will strengthen financial controls, improve reporting quality, and enhance overall operational efficiency across the organization.

subsections.label: Flurys manufacturing model change
points: Company has reimagined the Flurys business, dropping the idea of a central kitchen in New Delhi; instead outsourcing manufacturing to a vendor under a signed agreement, with processes in place for standardization of recipes and quality control.
The new outsourced model avoids a long factory development period, enabling faster growth and market reach not only in Delhi but in all metro markets including Bangalore and Pune.

Rationale: the outsourced model is more cost-effective and asset-light at both store and production level, avoiding a ₹20-30 crore investment and wait for returns, enabling faster rollout and better returns.
Recipes and craftsmanship at Flurys are fully preserved; quality inspectors/chefs will be stationed at production facilities to ensure output meets Flurys standard and customer expectations.

subsections.label: Sales & marketing / retention
points: Strengthened sales and marketing, pushing revenues through constant communication with 250,000 loyalty members.

Re-established contracts with ministries and corporates; aggressively following more RFPs for both Delhi and Hyderabad where a little impact was felt because of the Middle East war, but the situation has fully stabilized.

subsections.label: Kolkata market positioning
points: Park Calcutta's uniqueness at only 149 rooms yields the highest T-RevPAR in the central business district, exceeding all major luxury brands.

Growth in ARR expected as demand-supply mismatch continues, alongside stronger banqueting, restaurant, and bar performance; hotel has the best control over social media channels (Facebook, Instagram, YouTube) supporting market leadership retention.

subsections.label: Portfolio expansion strategy
points: Continue to expand and diversify hospitality platform through a balanced mix of owned, managed and leased assets, maintaining focus on disciplined and capital-efficient growth.
Additional growth planned via asset-light model expansion and addition of three lease properties planned to be acquired during the year.
Malabar House acquisition (Cochin) expected to complete over the next month or so, adding to performance and revenue.
Completed acquisition of Purity, a 17-room property in Cochin on Vembanad Lake (operated only 3 months in FY26).

subsections.label: Leadership strengthening
points: Appointment of Mr. Rohit Kakra as COO of Flurys (effective April 2026) to strengthen leadership capability for the brand's next growth phase.

subsections.label: Vision FY30
points: Vision centered on building a stronger, more scalable, future-ready hospitality platform, strategically expanding presence in the fast-growing mid-market segment while accelerating asset-light growth strategy for efficient, sustainable expansion.
Continue to unlock embedded real estate value while leveraging technology-led initiatives such as Nor1, the AI-driven upselling platform, to elevate guest experience and revenue optimization.

subsections.label: Geopolitical and operating headwinds
points: FY26 marked by a dynamic operating environment with volatility driven by geopolitical developments, disruptions in international travel flows, intermittent supply-side constraints including LPG shortages in select markets, inflationary pressures across operating costs, and fluctuations in travel sentiment across certain regions.
Profitability during the year was impacted by war and tension in the Middle East, along with higher depreciation and finance costs linked to ongoing expansion initiatives.

Two disruptions affected the year: Operation Sindoor in Q1 and the Middle East war starting late February continuing into April, with settlement not yet finalized though signs are positive with a 60-day ceasefire extension expected.
Significant cancellations took place in Delhi and Hyderabad due to the war; occupancy has recovered to over 90% in both hotels.

Vizag project timeline delayed from early 2029 to early 2030, primarily due to delay in obtaining environmental clearance (most difficult permission), though clearance is now in place and rest of the permissions are on the way.

key_figures.label: Expected EM Bypass cash flow improvement

subsections.label: Demand outlook
points: Demand environment for the Indian hospitality sector remains favourable; structural growth drivers including domestic travel, weddings and MICE businesses, experiential consumption, and limited supply growth across several markets continue to support strong medium to long-term industry fundamentals.
Company remains well positioned to capture this growth.

subsections.label: Growth targets
points: Clear target of surpassing 6,000 keys by FY30, focused on maintaining industry-leading occupancy levels and enhancing profitability across the portfolio.
FY27 plan to add 12 hotels totalling 472 keys, taking total key count past 3,000 keys.
Over the next four years, plan to double hotels from 42 to 85 and keys from 2,677 to 6,635, with 2x growth in owned hotels and 3x growth in asset-light model.
Flurys plans to reach 140+ outlets in the next 10 months and add 40-50 outlets over the next four years to 2030.

subsections.label: Growth on prior-year top-line miss
points: Management noted FY26 revenue growth of 12% (vs earlier mid-teens guidance) was impacted by two disruptions (Operation Sindoor and Middle East war), and characterized 12% growth as "very good" under the circumstances, with expectation of continued strong growth going forward as India's domestic travel remains strong.

key_takeaways: FY26 revenue crossed the 700-crore milestone for the first time.

Consolidated operating revenue for FY26 stood at 707 crores, registering growth of 12% year-on-year; EBITDA stood at 218 crores with EBITDA margin of 30.82%; PAT stood at 66 crores with PAT margin of 9.21%.
Occupancy for the year remained strong at 91%, ARR increased 9% year-on-year to 8,304, and RevPAR grew 7% year-on-year to 7,584.

The sale of service apartments at EM Bypass Kolkata has exceeded expectations, resulting in substantial improvement in this year's cash flow, with 29 of 34 apartments sold at Rs. 20,857 per square foot average realization.
The 75% dividend payout approved by the board reflects the strength of the balance sheet and growth momentum.
During FY26, the company launched 7 hospitality properties adding 283 keys; plans to add 12 hotels totalling 472 keys in FY27, taking total key count past 3,000 keys.
Over the next four years, plan to double the number of hotels from 42 to 85 and take key count from 2,677 to 6,635, with a clear target of surpassing 6,000 keys by FY30.
F&B revenues crossed INR 300 crores in FY26, contributing approximately 43% of total revenues.
Flurys grew to 110 outlets with 29% YoY revenue growth in FY26; plans to add more than 30 outlets over the next 10 months and 40-50 outlets over the next four years to 2030.
Profitability during the year was impacted by war and tension in the Middle East, higher depreciation and finance costs linked to ongoing expansion initiatives.

CONFIPET.about: Confidence Petroleum India Ltd is engaged in manufacturing of LPG cylinders and is also a supplier of auto LPG in India with its network of bottling plants and Auto LPG dispensing stations across India. It also supplies packed LPG cylinders and is also engaged in LPG bottling catering to industrial and commercial customers.[1]

quarters.summary: Q1 FY27 saw revenue up 117% YoY/98% QoQ largely volume-led on structural LPG customer wins from West Asia supply disruption; management does not view Q1 as a one-off and expects momentum, along with margins, to continue, guiding 10-15% QoQ growth in revenue/PAT/EBITDA with no absolute targets, while backward integration via coastal storage terminals and Type-4 cylinder commissioning remain the key near-term optionality items (order-book/timing dependent, commercial metrics undisclosed).

subsections.label: Margin framing
points: Management attributed the quarter primarily to 'strong volume growth across our LPG businesses', while also acknowledging that reported revenue was inflated by higher LPG prices.

Management repeatedly emphasized that the apparent margin compression is largely a denominator effect: higher LPG prices raised revenue, making PAT%/EBITDA% look lower even if unit economics are stable.
Quote: 'if you compare in percentage terms, you will see… not the correct picture… the margins are intact.'

subsections.label: West Asia supply disruption created a structural customer opening
points: Management described recent geopolitical disruptions in West Asia as materially tightening LPG sourcing, especially for India due to high import dependence.
Confidence leveraged diversified sourcing beyond the Middle East into 'North America, Africa, and other sourcing regions'.
Confidence leveraged its integrated import + logistics + bottling backbone.
Seven customers who initially engaged with Confidence during this challenging period have subsequently entered into longer-term procurement arrangements.
Management explicitly rejects the idea that Q1 is a one-off: 'we do not view Q1 as a one off performance… we expect this momentum to continue.'

subsections.label: Volume-led, not just price-led (management assertion)
points: Management stated YoY volumes were 'almost… doubled' and highlighted that Q1 performance was 'volume-led rather than purely price-led.'
New bulk and institutional customers were added under short to medium-term supply arrangements, improving near-term visibility.

subsections.label: Bulk LPG / Industrial
points: Added industrial accounts across FMCG, food processing, glass, ceramics.
Crisis response included prioritization: 'strategically prioritized bulk LPG supplies to industrial customers and PCD supplies' to protect continuity for key users (HoReCa/industrial).

subsections.label: Packed LPG (GoGas)
points: Customer proposition focus shifted toward retention/trust, not just acquisition.
Introduced 'Ginker Low Ginker Glow initiative' (pay-for-actual-consumption): returned cylinders weighed and credit given for unused LPG.
Management: 'customer attention and long-term relationships are becoming increasingly important alongside customer acquisition.'

subsections.label: Auto LPG (ALDS network)
points: Temporary demand softness acknowledged: 'temporary slowdown due to higher LPG prices'.
Recovery noted as prices stabilized: 'Auto-LPG volumes across our ALDS network are recovered… supported by focused marketing initiatives… and continued expansion.'
Economics highlighted: payback <18 months for a new ALDS, reinforcing their 'asset-light dispensing' scale thesis.

subsections.label: CNG retail (Bengaluru core + expansion intent)
points: Current network: 50+ stations in Bengaluru.

Throughput claims evolved materially: initially '500 to 800 kg' per day (early stage); now stated as '3 lakh kg per day' total; later cited per-station average '6000 to 6200' (kg/day implied) across live stations.
Expansion: additional 50 stations 'on track to commission' as they become operational.
New geographies under discussion (not finalized): Mumbai, Hyderabad, Indore.

subsections.label: Operating Model & Asset Footprint (Integrated LPG Value Chain)
points: Management positioned Confidence as an end-to-end LPG platform spanning procurement to last-mile delivery and adjacent fuels.
Fleet/logistics includes ships on time charter, 478+ LPG road tankers, 225+ HCBs/LCVs.
Processing/filling: 68+ LPG bottling & blending plants.
Distribution: 3,150+ LPG dealers; 3,400+ HoReCa customers; 300+ industrial customers.
Retail fuels: 315+ Auto LPG dispensing stations; 50+ CNG stations.
CNG transport assets: 82 CNG road vehicles (cascades).
Manufacturing: 15 cylinder plants + 3 high-pressure cylinder plants (plus new Type-4 line).
Strategic framing: 'integrated model allows us to participate in multiple stages of the energy value chain rather than depending on a single business segment.'

subsections.label: Network expansion targets (explicit numbers)
points: Auto LPG stations: from 315 to 500/575 in FY26–27 (management statement was inconsistent: '500 stations 75 by 2627'), then +100 in FY27–28, then evaluate to scale further.
CNG stations: from 50+ to 100 (adding ~50 more), then expand to other cities via discussions with CGD players.

subsections.label: Type-4 high-pressure cylinder plant (Bootibori/Nagpur)
points: Capex complete: 'All the machineries are installed'; commissioning depends on order flow.
Timeline language: order-linked but near-term: 'deliver in one to two months' once order book starts.
Customer targets disclosed: CGD players, fleet owners, OEMs, and cascade applications—'replacing the older kind of type 1 or type 2 cylinders.'
Margin guidance: explicitly not committed yet—management will evaluate after first deliveries.

subsections.label: CNG geographic expansion
points: New geographies under discussion (not finalized): Mumbai, Hyderabad, Indore, in addition to the Bengaluru core network.

key_figures.label: Customers who converted from crisis-sourcing to longer-term procurement arrangements

subsections.label: Backward integration / coastal storage terminals
points: Management stated they are 'actively evaluating opportunities for backward integration' and later clarified a concrete direction.
'looking forward to establish… storage terminals… at different coastal areas… under talk but yet not finalized.'
Rationale stated: reduce dependency, improve supply-chain control and margin resilience.

subsections.label: BW (strategic investor) exit
points: BW invested in FY23–24 and exited via secondary market; company says no impact to operations/capital plan.
'They are more focused into their own shipping business, and they want to exit.'
Exit was not a company buyback/redemption, so balance sheet not impacted per management.

subsections.label: Income tax search (Oct 7, 2025)
points: Search concluded in 7 days; assessment not closed.
Management stance: 'we don't see any… big amount… payable' and 'don't see any challenges' to closure.

subsections.label: FX hedging policy (import exposure)
points: Management indicated they typically pay 'time to time' under spot-type arrangements and do not hedge currently.
'we don't need to hedge… in future, whenever it is required, we will definitely do.'

subsections.label: Regulatory constraint: co-locating CNG + Auto LPG
points: PESO currently does not allow combination at same station: 'PESO don't allow the combination of CNG and Auto LPG station.'

subsections.label: Growth cadence (only directional)
points: No absolute revenue target given; they guided in percentages: 'quarter on quarter 10 to 15 percent' revenue/PAT/EBITDA growth expectation.
They stressed revenue can fluctuate with LPG prices, but profit/EBITDA should grow with volumes and operating leverage: 'revenue might be fluctuating, but the growth will be there.'

subsections.label: Margin outlook (qualitative)
points: No explicit EBITDA% or PAT% target; repeated emphasis: margins 'intact', expected to improve with higher volumes, fixed-cost absorption, and procurement scale.

revenue might be fluctuating, but the growth will be there

key_takeaways: Competitive advantage during supply shocks appears to be real and monetized: diversified sourcing + integrated infrastructure converted at least some crisis demand into longer-term procurement arrangements.
Auto LPG is treated as a high-ROCE expansion lever (payback <18 months), but volumes remain price-sensitive.
CNG scaling is underway but execution is gated by station commissioning; management's commentary suggests strong throughput ramp in Bengaluru and active geographic expansion talks.
Type-4 cylinder manufacturing is a near-term optionality with capex done and commissioning order-book dependent; end markets include CGDs/OEMs/fleets, but commercial metrics are not yet disclosed.
Backward integration via coastal storage terminals is the clearest next step management disclosed to improve supply-chain control and potentially smooth volatility.

AVG.about: Incorporated in 2010, AVG Logistics Ltd is in the business of transportation of goods, warehousing and other incidental activities, along with trading business[1]

quarters.summary: Management remains confident of delivering 15-20% revenue growth in FY27, supported by existing customers, new customer pipeline (incl. Haldiram expansion), and new business segments (liquid logistics, green transportation via Carbonlite JV). Margins are expected to improve further as capex from FY26 gets fully utilized through FY27, aided by asset sweating, better fleet utilization, and cost discipline; Q3/Q4 are expected to see higher volumes than Q1/Q2 due to seasonality.

subsections.label: Profitability growth outpacing revenue
points: Revenue grew 6% YoY in Q1 while PAT grew by nearly 30%, indicating profitability grew much faster than revenue.
This reflects execution, asset utilization and operational efficiency work beginning to show results.
Stronger growth in profitability reflects the benefit of better operational efficiency, asset utilization, and cost discipline.

subsections.label: Cost management focus
points: Continuously working on fleet productivity, reducing empty run, improving freight planning, optimizing turnaround time, improving warehouse productivity.
These may look like small operational improvements individually, but together they can have a meaningful impact on profitability.
Cost management will remain a key priority through the year: fuel efficiency, maintenance, fleet utilization, empty run reduction, freight planning, warehouse productivity.
Remain disciplined on working capital and capital expenditure.

subsections.label: Customer depth strategy
points: Growth is being pursued not only through new customers but also by working closely with existing customers to identify additional requirements across geographies and business segments.
This allows the company to increase wallet share while leveraging existing network and infrastructure.

subsections.label: Rights issue
points: INR52.93 crores raised through rights issue during Q1.
Provides additional resource for working capital and general corporate purposes.
Gives greater flexibility to support expansion plan and customers' requirements.
Further strengthened financial position as the company enters the next phase of growth.

Difficult to give a specific revenue or PAT number solely against rights issue proceeds; at overall business level, incremental revenue and better PAT expected from new contracts, higher fleet utilization, and capex.

subsections.label: Capex approach
points: Disciplined approach to capex; investment linked to business opportunity including additional vehicles for new/long-term customer contracts, specialized logistics, and technology requirements.
Haldiram contract cited as example of capex directly linked to customer requirement and long-term business relationship.
Additional fleet requirements being fulfilled through operational lease of vehicles, particularly in EV segment due to heavy capex requirement.
Investment in EV, CNG, LNG vehicles being evaluated alongside longer-term customer contracts for better visibility on utilization and returns.
Evaluating leasing of assets to balance the financial balance sheet instead of buying, talking to companies and financial institutions for leasing.
Approach aims to maintain balance between asset ownership and leasing to support business growth while keeping financial and capital requirements under control.
New assets added will contribute for a longer period in FY27, supporting revenue growth and improving PAT margins, though depreciation will increase due to new asset additions.

subsections.label: Fuel cost management
points: Fuel is an important cost for the industry; however, a significant portion of customer contracts have fuel escalation clauses which help manage the impact of changes in fuel prices.

subsections.label: Capital allocation and dividend
points: Balanced approach to capital allocation: investing in the next phase of growth while remaining committed to shareholder return.
Board declared dividend of INR1.20 per equity share for FY26, subject to shareholders' approval at the 17th AGM.
Reflects a balanced approach of investing in the business while also returning value to shareholders.

key_figures.label: Number of liquid logistics train sets purchased

subsections.label: High-margin segments
points: Better margins currently seen in dedicated vehicles, cold chain business, reefer trucks, and warehousing and factory management.
Company is doing customer warehouse operations business.

These are specialized segments where competition is less and, since vehicles are dedicated to specific customer requirements, better utilization and margin is achieved compared to traditional transportation activities.
Company will continue to focus on specialized business where more profit can be earned instead of normal transport business.

subsections.label: Liquid logistics and green vehicle margins
points: Liquid logistics, EV and LNG businesses are both higher margin because these are specialized businesses requiring government policies and route management.
Customers give better rate in terms of kilometer or destination-wise; freight of liquid/liquor goods is higher than normal goods, so margins are better there.
EV business profit is a little better as cost of operations is less in EV and LNG compared to diesel.

subsections.label: In-house real-time vehicle tracking software
points: Company developed in-house software for tracking real-time vehicle running and controlling through GPS and dashcams.
Cameras installed in vehicles for safety purposes.
Software enables customers to track and locate dedicated vehicles for their logistics operations.

Software informs customers when a vehicle will reach its destination based on standard running rate (e.g., 350 km/day), enabling better utilization/sweating of asset and better customer planning of loading/unloading.
Company has started giving customers access to this software so they can plan better, resulting in increased overall vehicle running.
Targeting minimum 15% to 20% growth in monthly vehicle running (from 1 lakh km to 1,20,000 km) by utilizing the latest software.
Incremental growth in vehicle running was achieved in August using this software.

subsections.label: Technology strategy
points: Using real-time vehicle tracking and in-house technology solutions to give customers better visibility, better control, and more flexibility.
Technology is viewed not just as adding a feature to service but as improving the way the company operates and making the business more scalable.
AI is coming up as an advancement in technology being adopted.

subsections.label: Pan-India network
points: Built a pan-India network with a diversified customer base.
More than 3,000 owned and hired vehicles, over 70 branches, and more than 7.4 lakh square feet of warehousing capacity.
Now adding technology, specialized logistics, and alternative fuel capability to this platform, giving multiple levers for growth.

subsections.label: FY27 fleet addition plan
points: Two types of models being used for fleet addition: lease model and purchase model.
Around 50-60 CNG vehicles, 100 LNG vehicle contract, and as of now 30 electric vehicle order placed with discussion ongoing for another 70 electric vehicles.
Total target is to add around 200 vehicles by March '27.

subsections.label: Liquid logistics tanker/train capacity
points: Two sets of tankers/trains already purchased.
Further purchases will not be taken onto company books; instead, future tankers/trains will be taken on lease basis, at least for the next year or so.
After that period, company may consider buying two more trains onto its books.
