subsections.label: Haldiram contract geographic coverage
points: Haldiram Nagpur dedicated vehicle deployment strengthens presence across western, southern and key eastern markets including Odisha, Bihar and Jharkhand.
Vehicles are logging from Nagpur and going to South, East and some part of the West.
Backload being taken from return journeys from areas like Bhopal, Indore, Nagpur, Jabalpur.

subsections.label: Operational efficiency initiatives
points: Focus on fleet productivity, reducing empty run, improving freight planning, optimizing turnaround time, improving warehouse productivity.
Loading vehicles both ways (e.g., Delhi to Bombay and Bombay to Delhi) to improve profitability through sweating of assets.
Backload strategy being used on Haldiram routes from Bhopal, Indore, Nagpur, Jabalpur to improve utilization.

subsections.label: Customer relationship strategy
points: Customers increasingly looking for a logistics partner who can manage multiple parts of their supply chain rather than simply provide transportation, which plays to AVG's strength.
Significant opportunity to grow business with existing customers alongside new customer acquisition.
Haldiram is a reputed customer, good paymaster, helping build opportunity for additional vehicle requirement in dedicated model in future.
Festive season (Ganesh Chaturthi, Dussehra, Diwali, Durga Puja) driving huge demand for vehicles from FMCG customers like Haldiram.

subsections.label: Green logistics customer demand
points: Customers increasingly seeking cleaner transportation solutions; company responding through CNG, LNG and electric vehicles.
Lot of steel, cement, FMCG companies wish to transition their business to electric vehicles, seen as a good opportunity for Carbonlite.

key_figures.label: Deployed Haldiram vehicles as of Aug 21

subsections.label: Haldiram FMCG contract
points: Secured a long-term contract from Haldiram, Nagpur for deployment of 100 dedicated vehicles, an important addition to the FMCG business.
Demonstrates confidence large customers are placing in AVG to manage their logistics requirements at scale.

Contract received in July; 40 of 100 vehicles deployed as of August 21, 2026; remaining 60 vehicles under deployment process, expected to be deployed in the next one to two months (currently under fabrication).
Contract will add to revenue and provide better revenue visibility as vehicles become fully operational.
Being dedicated vehicles, it helps maintain better fleet utilization and planning.
Following deployment, Haldiram management asked AVG to add another 100 vehicles by December 2026, driven partly by festive season demand.

subsections.label: Liquid logistics expansion
points: Entered liquid logistics due to strong demand and relatively limited organized competition.
Already started building capabilities to scale this business meaningfully over coming years.

subsections.label: Baidyanath Group JV / Carbonlite Logistics
points: During Q1, entered into a joint venture with Baidyanath Group to accelerate LNG powered transportation across sectors such as steel, metal and cement.
Seen as a long-term opportunity, not just a sustainability initiative, as customers move towards cleaner supply chains.
All formalities for the Baidyanath Group JV have been completed; incorporated a company called Carbonlite Logistics Private Limited with initial capital deployed.
Carbonlite is specifically focused on the sustainable/green business only — CNG, LNG and electric transportation.
Company is talking to customers for long-term contracts providing LNG and electric vehicles, and arranging finance and leasing of new vehicles for deployment.
Operations of Carbonlite expected to start from 1st October; expected to be a good opportunity given steel, cement, FMCG companies' interest in shifting to electric vehicles.

subsections.label: Vision and growth strategy
points: Objective for FY27 is to grow the business by sweating assets, deepening customer relationships, and building new growth engines.
Focus on deploying capital against real customer opportunities, improving productivity of existing assets, and maintaining operational discipline.
Growth must be responsible; new investment should strengthen ability to serve customers and create long-term value.

subsections.label: Seasonality
points: Logistics business has some seasonality; Q1 and Q3 are normal operating quarters, while Q4 usually has better volume due to higher demand for some industries served.
Quarterly numbers should be viewed in the context of the full financial year.
Higher volume expected in Q3 and Q4; historically (FY24, FY25, FY26) Q3 and Q4 have been much better than Q1 or Q2.

subsections.label: Fuel price risk
points: Fuel is an important cost for the industry; however, a significant portion of customer contracts have fuel escalation clauses which help manage the impact of fuel price changes.

subsections.label: Depreciation impact
points: Depreciation may increase during FY27 due to addition of new assets, even as overall profit and incremental growth are expected to come through.

subsections.label: FY27 growth outlook
points: Management remains confident of approximately 15% to 20% revenue growth objective for FY27, supported by existing customer base, new customer pipeline, and expansion into new business segments.
New fleet and assets added in the last year gave less revenue contribution last year but will fully utilize and support higher revenue in FY27.

Around 7% to 8% growth expected to come from new business, and around 8% to 10% growth from existing customers through new contracts and business expansion; actual contribution may depend on timing of new contracts and vehicle development.
Sincere focus on sustainable logistics (LNG, EV, CNG), with vehicles added and further plans to add new vehicles.

subsections.label: Margin outlook
points: Margins expected to improve as benefit of capex done during FY26 starts flowing through in FY27, since a major part of capex was done in the second half of FY26.
New assets/vehicles will have higher contribution and higher utilization in FY27 as they will be operational for the entire financial year.
Sweating of assets and better operational efficiency expected to drive more improvement in profit margins, particularly through both-way loaded vehicle runs.
Business margin will increase if operational costs are controlled; focus on sustainability (LNG has lower operational cost than diesel; EV has higher investment but much lower operational cost).

guidance_ledger.statement: We are expecting revenue growth of around 15% to 20% for '27 and this growth will come from our existing customers and new customers and new contracts.
Around 7% to 8% growth will come with the new business... around 8%-10% growth will come through existing customers through new contract, expansion of our business.
We are planning to do a further capex of around INR60 crores... this year capex will be INR50 crores, INR60 crores and other assets we are trying to take on lease.

Total target is to add around 200 vehicle in this March '27... around CNG, around 50-60 vehicle, LNG, we got the contract of 100 vehicles and electric, as of now we got the order of 30 vehicles, but our 70 vehicle order is discussion is going on.
They are asking us to add another 100 vehicles by December '26, 2026.
I hope the operation will start from 1st of October in this group and it will be a very good opportunity.
If our vehicles are running 1 lakh km in a month, so now we are targeting to make it minimum 15% to 20% growth, 1,20,000, by utilizing the latest software.
We expect our margins to improve as the benefit of the capex done during 25-26 start coming from this current year of '27... hopefully this year our margin will be much better.

Now further purchase, we are don't want to take our books. We want to take the future few tankers or two trains from leasing basis only... After that, we can think again to buy two more train from in our books.
We have uploaded our vision of 2030 with the INR1250 crores turnover by 2030.
We will grow in a fast manner with the 8-10 trains by 2030.
As of now we are only have 180 container tankers, but gradually we have to increase up to 1,800 tankers.
One more the rake we are targeting in FY27.

themes.label: FY27 growth guidance
themes.note: Management reiterated 15%-20% revenue growth target for FY27, split roughly 7-8% from new business and 8-10% from existing customers.

themes.label: Margin expansion
themes.note: PAT grew ~30% vs 6% revenue growth in Q1; margins expected to improve further as FY26 capex assets get fully utilized in FY27.

themes.label: Green/alternative-fuel transition
themes.note: Company adding CNG, LNG and electric vehicles, and launched Carbonlite Logistics (Baidyanath JV) dedicated to sustainable green transportation, operations expected from 1st October.

themes.label: Liquid logistics expansion
themes.note: Two tanker trains already purchased; further capacity to be added via leasing rather than balance sheet purchase for now.

themes.label: Fuel cost pass-through
themes.note: A significant portion of customer contracts carry fuel escalation clauses that help manage fuel price impact.

themes.label: Multi-modal diversification
themes.note: Growth levers being added include technology, specialized logistics (dedicated vehicles, cold chain, warehousing), and alternative fuel capability atop the core pan-India network.

themes.label: Customer concentration / large contract wins
themes.note: Haldiram Nagpur dedicated 100-vehicle FMCG contract deployed in phases, with a further 100-vehicle expansion request by December 2026 driven by festive season demand.

key_takeaways: Revenue grow 6% on year in Q1 while PAT grow by nearly 30% for us. Important point is that profitability has grown much faster than revenue.
During the quarter, we have secured a long-term contract from Haldiram, Nagpur for the deployment of 100 dedicated vehicles.
During Q1, we also entered into a joint venture with Baidyanath Group to accelerate LNG powered transportation across sectors such as steel, metal and cement.
We have built a pan-India network, a diversified customer base, more than 3,000 owned and hired vehicles, over 70 branches, and more than 7.4 lakh square feet of warehousing capacity.
As we said in our previous earning call, our objective for '27 is to deliver approximately 15% to 20% growth.
We have also continued to balance growth investment with shareholder return with the Board declaring a dividend of Rupee 1.20 per equity share for '26.
During Q1, we raised INR52.93 crores through the rights issue.
PBT increased 24.42% year-on-year to INR8.71 crores, while PAT increased 29.98% to INR6.46 crores. PBT margin improved by 98 basis points to 6.58% and PAT margin improved by 89 basis points to 4.87%.

quarters.summary: AVG Logistics closed FY26 with double-digit revenue and profit growth and management expects healthy double-digit (15-20%) revenue growth in FY27, supported by current order book, customer pipeline and new business segments including rail-based liquid logistics. The company has laid out a Vision 2030 target of INR1,250 crores turnover, and plans continued capex (~INR50 crore+ in FY27) toward fleet addition, alternative-fuel vehicles, liquid logistics rakes and warehousing infrastructure.

subsections.label: Overall financial performance
points: CFO reported a strong financial year '26, reflecting healthy growth across both revenue and profitability, driven by continued focus on operational excellence, prudent cost management, and the strength of the integrated multi-modal logistics model.

subsections.label: Lease reversal gain clarification (Ind AS 116)
points: An analyst queried whether the INR21.19 crore one-time lease reversal gain recognized in Q4 FY26 was recurring in nature, given it arose from a pre-closure of a long-term lease contract with Indian Railways.

CFO clarified this is treated as normal operational income, not a windfall gain, arising from Ind AS 116 provisioning requirements when long-term lease contracts are entered or cancelled — creating adjustments on asset, liability and expense sides.

In the current financial year, similar Ind AS lease liability and right-to-use asset provisions were also created for new warehouses taken on lease, indicating this is a regular recurring accounting process whenever long-term lease agreements are entered into or terminated.

Opinion was taken from professional firms including PwC confirming it is operational other income, though auditors required it be shown separately as a line item rather than net-off against related expenses.

On tax treatment: since the corresponding expenses were already debited to P&L and taxed in previous years, this year's reversal/gain is not considered taxable income; no tax is leviable on this reversal.

Management characterized this type of adjustment as recurring in nature at a portfolio level (since multiple long-term lease agreements are entered/terminated on a regular basis across years), even though the individual gain itself pertains to a specific contract closure.

subsections.label: Capex plan
points: FY26 capex was over INR60 crores; FY27 capex is targeted at over INR50 crores to support the growth engine, including placement of additional vehicles and long-term contracts with new customers.

Capex covers the liquid logistics train (rake) added this year with one more rake targeted in FY27, addition of CNG, EV and LNG vehicles for sustainability/zero-emission goals, plus regular vehicles as per customer requirements.
Around 100+ vehicles were added last year, with a similar target for the next financial year.

subsections.label: Result delay explanation
points: The delay in Q4 financial results was due to procedural and audit-related requirements; as the business has grown, the audit process has become more detailed requiring additional reviews and consolidation from branches.
Management remains committed to high standards of corporate governance and timely disclosure, and will try to keep within statutory timelines going forward.

subsections.label: Haldiram contract
points: Recently secured contract from Haldiram Nagpur, a leading FMCG brand, for dedicated supply of 100 vehicles for three years extendable to five years.
Haldiram supplies across Maharashtra, Gujarat, Odisha, Chhattisgarh, Telangana, Andhra Pradesh and Karnataka; demand is high ahead of the upcoming festival season.

Overall requirement from Haldiram is very high; initial deployment is 100 vehicles, with potential for the contract to expand further by another two to three months after deployment of these vehicles.
Large customer with significant movement from Nagpur to Pan-India across multiple states.

subsections.label: Revenue growth outlook basis
points: Management's growth expectation for FY27 is based on current order book, customer pipeline, and expansion into new business segments.
Existing customer base along with new customers already identified in the pipeline, plus new business opportunities, are expected to support growth during the year.

subsections.label: Business segments
points: Company operates across six segments: road transportation, rail transportation, cold chain, warehousing and supply chain management, alternative fuel vehicles, and liquid logistics.

Warehousing/supply chain management: company is increasingly getting business from customers to maintain supply chain within their factories; total company remains a multi-modal logistics provider rather than shifting primary focus solely to warehousing.

Supply chain management service involves managing warehouse and business movement, inventory movement etc.; described as a good margin segment but a highly responsible work area, as companies increasingly outsource this to 3PL companies rather than maintaining in-house teams.

subsections.label: Liquid logistics segment
points: Liquid logistics involves transportation of liquid material (chemicals) via tankers, by both road and rail; has huge demand in India.
Currently only 180 container tankers versus a target to increase to around 1,800 tankers — roughly ten times (stated as 'five times capacity' in the call) current capacity.
Two expansion options being pursued: importing tankers from China or taking tankers on lease in India; two tank trains already purchased, with a third being pursued on lease.
Segment considered attractive because very few companies operate in this space; company entered this business last year and plans to grow with 8-10 trains by 2030.

subsections.label: Technology-driven positioning
points: Company positions itself as a technology-driven integrated multi-modal logistics solution provider.
Continues investing in modified and improved technology as a regular feature of running the business.

key_figures.label: Loan financing percentage from bank/NBFCs for vehicle purchase

subsections.label: Infrastructure expansion
points: Strategic acquisition of a land parcel in Tahliwal, Himachal, for warehousing purposes to support future warehousing and logistics capacity, enhance regional presence in North India, improve operational efficiencies, and strengthen key customer relationships.

subsections.label: Asset utilization / 'asset to sweat' focus
points: Current year focus is on 'asset to sweat' — improving the running condition of vehicles to maximize revenue extraction from existing assets.
Vehicles are typically run on long routes (2,000-2,500 km) initially and later shifted to shorter routes (500-1,000 km) over their operating life, contributing to asset productivity.

subsections.label: EV/alternative-fuel vehicle capability and infrastructure
points: EV vehicle range is currently around 150-200 km per charge; company is investing in charging infrastructure at midpoints on long routes (e.g., Delhi-Amritsar, Chennai-Bangalore ~400-500 km) so EV vehicles can run on longer routes similar to diesel refueling.
Chargers already available on routes like Pune-Mumbai, Nashik-Mumbai, Ahmedabad-Mumbai; infrastructure build-out expected to remove long-route constraints for EVs over time.

EV vehicle types include rigid vehicles and trailers with trailers carrying up to 40 tons, and smaller vehicles carrying 1-9 tons; company has secured contracts on ~400 km routes (e.g., Chennai-Bangalore) and is building infra to extend range to 400-500 km.
EV vehicle economics: asset cost is high compared to diesel vehicles, but operating cost is much lower with minimal maintenance, making profitability better than diesel over the vehicle's life.

Vehicles are financed via 80-90% bank/NBFC loans; vehicles are described as earning revenue from day one, with EMI self-funded by vehicle earnings; EMI tenure of about 5-6 years against a vehicle life of 10 years (NCR/major cities) or 15 years (small cities).

subsections.label: Pan-India network
points: Strong pan-India network since inception in 2010, spanning over 70 branches and diversified customer base across FMCG, food and beverage, cement, retail, telecom, steel, automotive, pharma and industrial sectors.
Haldiram contract entails movement from Nagpur to Maharashtra, Gujarat, Odisha, Chhattisgarh, Telangana, Andhra Pradesh and Karnataka.

subsections.label: Operational discipline initiatives
points: Continuous evaluation of opportunities to improve fleet productivity, reduce empty runs, optimize freight planning, enhance warehouse productivity, and improve asset utilization.
Focus on improving turnaround times, optimizing network utilization, and strengthening execution capability across all business verticals.

Investing in building robust operational processes, compliance frameworks, and quality standards to maintain long-term relationships with leading domestic and multinational customers, as customers increasingly prioritize compliance, safety standards, service reliability and technology-enabled operations.

subsections.label: Fuel cost pass-through mechanism
points: Fuel price increases (e.g., recent significant rise in diesel prices) are largely passed through via fuel escalation clauses embedded in most customer contracts, with diesel consumption percentage specified in contracts.
Company may need to absorb cost for a short period (about a week to 15 days) before rate increases are passed on by customers, limiting the overall impact of diesel price increases on the business.

subsections.label: Customer diversification and wallet share
points: Diversified business model across transportation, multi-modal logistics, cold chain, warehousing, liquid logistics, and value-added supply chain solutions reduces dependence on any single service line or customer segment.

Increasing demand from customers for customized and integrated supply chain solutions rather than standalone transportation services; large enterprises seek partners who can optimize end-to-end supply chains, improve inventory management, ensure timely delivery, and provide greater visibility.

Focus on customer retention and wallet share expansion by identifying new logistics requirements across geographies and business verticals from the existing client base, viewed as a key driver of profitable and sustainable growth.

subsections.label: Target industry expansion
points: Historically strong in FMCG; now expanding into beverage, liquor industry, steel, cement, pharma, chemical, industrial plant and solar power industries, viewed as having significant transportation opportunity for raw material and finished goods movement.
Going forward, focus on expanding presence in high-growth sectors such as FMCG, food processing, pharmaceuticals, chemicals, retail, and industrial logistics.

key_figures.label: Haldiram contract further vehicle addition timeline

subsections.label: Carbonlite Logistics JV with Baidyanath Group
points: New 50:50 joint venture company named Carbonlite Logistics Private Limited formed with Baidyanath Group; AVG is not directly providing logistics service to Baidyanath but has created a separate logistics company jointly.
Baidyanath already holds a license for LNG gas under its own company (BLNG - Baidyanath LNG); the JV will procure LNG trucks from manufacturers such as Tata and Ashok Leyland.

Rationale driven by rising customer demand for green logistics from large customers like Tata Steel and other cement companies, who are offering long-term contracts for such green logistics solutions.
Baidyanath Group described as a very large group with turnover of INR18,000 crores, presenting a high growth opportunity for AVG.
All formalities for the JV have been completed; operations of Carbonlite Logistics are expected to start within the next one month or so.

subsections.label: Nestle India / Ashok Leyland CNG collaboration
points: Collaboration with Nestle India and Ashok Leyland for deployment of CNG-powered vehicles establishing a dedicated green logistics corridor.

This reduces carbon emissions, improves operational efficiency, and comes with a long-term contract with the customer, reflecting focus on building environmentally responsible and future-ready logistics solutions.

subsections.label: Entry into rail-based liquid logistics
points: Strengthened multi-modal capability through entry into rail-based liquid logistics segment, expanding into a high-growth market and reinforcing ability to offer safe, efficient and sustainable transport solutions for chemical and allied industries.

subsections.label: Fuel price volatility
points: Fuel prices are a very important and main cost in the industry; recent significant increase in diesel prices was flagged by an analyst as a potential risk.

Management noted contracts generally include fuel escalation clauses that pass through diesel cost increases, mitigating impact, though there can be a short lag (about a week to 15 days) before rate increases take effect.

subsections.label: EV range/infrastructure limitation
points: Current EV vehicle range is limited to around 150-200 km per charge, raising questions about suitability for long-distance routes (1,000-2,000+ km); company addressing this via investment in charging infrastructure at route midpoints.

subsections.label: Global economic uncertainty
points: Global economic uncertainties and evolving market conditions may continue to create short-term challenges, even as long-term fundamentals of the Indian logistics sector remain highly encouraging.

subsections.label: Result delay / governance perception
points: Delay in Q4 financial results reporting was noted by an analyst as not indicating a good sign; attributed by management to procedural and audit-related requirements amid business growth.

subsections.label: FY27 growth outlook
points: Management expects to deliver healthy double-digit revenue growth in FY27 (targeted at 15% to 20%), broadly in line with industry growth rate of approximately 15%-20%.

Growth to be supported by current order book, customer pipeline, expansion into new business segments (including rail-based liquid logistics), existing customer base and new customers already identified in the pipeline.

subsections.label: Vision 2030
points: Company has published a 'Vision 2030' document (uploaded a day prior to the call) targeting INR1,250 crores turnover by 2030.

subsections.label: Capex and fleet guidance
points: FY27 capex targeted at over INR50 crores, covering additional vehicle placement, long-term customer contracts, one additional liquid logistics rake, and continued CNG/EV/LNG vehicle additions.
Around 100+ vehicles targeted to be added in FY27, similar to FY26's addition.

guidance_ledger.statement: We expect to deliver healthy double-digit revenue growth in FY27... our target is to achieve 15% to 20% growth in the next year.
We have uploaded our vision of 2030 with the INR1250 crores turnover by 2030.
The financial year '27 we are also targeting INR50 crores plus to have our growth engine.
Around 100 plus vehicles we have added last year and same we are targeting in the next financial year.
We will grow in a fast manner with the 8-10 trains by 2030.
As of now we are only have 180 container tankers, but gradually we have to increase up to 1,800 tankers.
One more the rake we are targeting in FY27.
100 vehicles contract may further come by another two to three month after deployment of these vehicles.
We will start the operation of this company which is a subsidiary of the AVG in the maximum next one month or so.

risk_register.risk: Diesel/fuel price increase
risk_register.note: Significant increase in diesel prices flagged; largely mitigated by fuel escalation clauses in customer contracts, though a short lag (1-2 weeks) exists before pass-through.

risk_register.risk: Global economic uncertainty / evolving market conditions
risk_register.note: Management flagged these as continuing to create short-term challenges despite encouraging long-term sector fundamentals.

risk_register.risk: EV range and infrastructure limitations for long-distance routes
risk_register.note: Current EV range ~150-200 km per charge; company investing in charging infrastructure at route midpoints to enable longer routes (400-500 km).

risk_register.risk: Delay in financial results filing
risk_register.note: Q4 results were delayed due to procedural and audit-related requirements amid business growth; management committed to staying within statutory timelines going forward.

themes.label: Margin expansion
themes.note: EBITDA and PAT margins expanded meaningfully in Q4 and FY26 on operational excellence and cost management.

themes.label: Multi-modal diversification
themes.note: Growth strategy centered on road, rail, cold chain, warehousing, liquid logistics and alternative fuel segments reducing single-segment dependence.

themes.label: Green/alternative-fuel transition
themes.note: Expansion into CNG, LNG and EV vehicles via collaborations (Nestle-Ashok Leyland, Carbonlite JV with Baidyanath) driven by customer demand for sustainable logistics.

themes.label: Liquid logistics expansion
themes.note: New rail-based liquid logistics segment targeted to scale from 180 to 1,800 tankers and 8-10 trains by 2030.

themes.label: Fuel cost pass-through
themes.note: Diesel price increases largely absorbed via fuel escalation clauses in customer contracts with minor short-term lag.

themes.label: FY27 growth guidance
themes.note: Management guided to 15-20% revenue growth in FY27 backed by order book, pipeline and new segments, alongside Vision 2030 target of INR1,250 crore turnover.

themes.label: Corporate governance / disclosure timeliness
themes.note: Q4 results were delayed due to audit-related procedural requirements, flagged by an analyst as a governance concern.

key_takeaways: During Q4 FY26, we recorded total revenue of INR176.61 crores, registering a growth of 19.4% year-on-year.
EBITDA stood at INR34.72 crores, increasing 45.21% year-on-year, while EBITDA margin expanded by 349 basis point to 19.66%.
Profit after tax stood at INR10.71 crores, reflecting a moderate growth of 104.78% year-on-year, with PAT margin improving by 252 basis points to 6.06%.
For the full year financial year '26, we achieved total income of INR582.48 crores, representing a growth of 5.07% year-on-year.
EBITDA increased to INR112.45 crores, up 14.27% year-on-year, with EBITDA margin improving to 19.31%.
Profit after tax stood at INR26.17 crores, registering a healthy growth of 22.71%, while PAT margin expanded to 4.49%.

Based on our current order book, customer pipeline, and expansion into new business segment, we expect to deliver healthy double-digit revenue growth in FY27... our target is to achieve 15% to 20% growth in the next year.
We have yesterday we have uploaded our vision of 2030 with the INR1250 crores turnover in the by 2030 we have made the vision like for next 4 years.
Capex in the financial year '26 is INR60 crores plus and the financial year '27 we are also targeting INR50 crores plus.
pressing_questions: So there is a significant increase in the diesel fuel flow in previous months. So how that has impacted the business in future?

The one-time lease reversal gain of INR21.19 crores which is recognized in the last quarter of the financial year 26. Is it a recurring income or a one-time income by virtue of adjustment of Accounting Standard 116? If it is not recurring, like the normalized financial performance are you going to publish?
So like we have delayed our financial result for the Q4. So what was the reason for the delay? You know, it does not really indicate a good sign.

SBILIFE.about: SBI Life Insurance Company Ltd is engaged in the business of life insurance and annuity. It was started as a Joint-venture between State Bank of India and BNP Paribas Cardif S.A.[1]

quarters.summary: SBI Life delivered 14% growth in Individual Rated Premium (IRP) in Q1 FY27, within its 14-15% guided range, and VoNB margin of 26.2% (lower end of the 26-28% guided band) due to a one-off higher contribution from Group Term Insurance (GTI) business, which management expects to normalize going forward, moving margin toward the upper end of the guided band as individual business mix normalizes. Management reiterated FY27 IRP growth guidance of 14-15% and margin guidance of 26-28%, expects GST drag to continue for another ~2.5 months into Q2 before running off, and plans to launch the regular pay deferred annuity product within the next quarter.

key_figures.label: VNB margin impact from assumption change (walk)
VNB margin impact from product mix change (walk)
Operating assumption change impact (March 2026 annual review)

subsections.label: Margin walk drivers
points: The overall APE mix during Q1 had a higher share of group business, described as lumpy, which brought down margin compared to last year.
Group business margin is lower than individual business margin, so higher group contribution drags overall VoNB margin.

The -60 bps product mix impact in the VNB walk is entirely on account of the one-off GTI (Group Term Insurance) business, which is invariably lower margin than company average, despite non-par and par growing and ULIP share coming down.

No assumption change was made in Q1 FY27 itself; the -40 bps shown in the walk arises because the walk compares June last year to this year, and the actual assumption change was made as part of the annual review in March 2026.

The March 2026 operating assumption change was negative by 20 bps; this becomes 40 bps in the YoY walk due to a base effect; the change was a normal refinement in persistency, mortality and expense assumptions; the financial assumption change was also negative, not positive.
Company does not disclose product-wise margin breakdowns (e.g., quantified GTI-specific drag was not shared).

subsections.label: Cost / expense drivers
points: GST drag has been running at similar levels (~1.1-1.5 percentage points) for the last few quarters; management does not plan to reduce expenses or commissions as they are already on the lower side, but expects product mix to offset the GST drag (as seen in FY26 where the net impact was reduced to 20-30 bps).
GST impact is expected to continue for another roughly 2.5 months into Q2 (GST was waived from 22nd September last year) before running off on a like-for-like basis thereafter.

Pickup in other expenses (even adjusting for GST) is attributed to two one-off/period items: (1) higher stamp duty corresponding to significantly increased sum assured (protection and rider attachments driving up sum assured), and (2) labour code impact due to number of employees, first seen in this quarter versus June 2025.
Other expenses will continue in tandem with sum assured growth; management indicated this trend will streamline over the next three quarters as per plan.

subsections.label: Product mix evolution
points: All product segments recorded growth on an Individual Rated Premium basis and all key distribution channels achieved double-digit expansion.
The increasing contribution from protection solutions and guaranteed non-par saving products reflects evolving customer preferences and strategic focus.

Company has been strengthening its product portfolio on non-par, par and protection sides over the last 2 years, resulting in higher sales of these products while ULIP continues to sell normally; this has driven ULIP contribution down to 62% and non-ULIP up to 38% on IRP basis with majority of the increase from non-par; company's target for the full year is to maintain this kind of product mix.

Company does not have high sum-assured ULIP products; instead rider attachment on ULIP has increased, with 45-50% of policies now sold with rider attachment, up from an initial low base 1-1.5 years ago when riders were first attached to traditional products before extending to unit-linked products; attachment improved from 35% to 45% to now ~50%, and is expected to improve or maintain from this level; riders are also being offered to existing customers.
Rider APE (protection part of riders) is counted as part of protection business; exact rider APE quantification not available but to be shared separately.
Participating (Par) Individual APE grew 35% YoY to INR 2.4 billion with par segment sum assured growth of 81% YoY.
Guaranteed non-par savings business grew 27% YoY to INR 9.7 billion.
ULIP business stood at INR 24.5 billion, contributing 61% to APE versus 65% in the prior year.

subsections.label: Protection segment dynamics
points: Individual protection growth of 22% is higher than the overall IRP growth of ~14.5-15% for the quarter.

Company has been shifting focus from ROP (return of premium) to non-ROP and pure protection since last year; pure protection growth of 52% (on IRP basis, later reconfirmed as 41%) is running at a much stronger clip than ROP, though pure protection has lower ticket size than ROP, which makes overall protection growth appear more subdued versus industry peers reporting on an APE basis (~15%).
ROP to non-ROP mix has improved to 68%/32% versus 73%/27% last year, reflecting the shift towards non-ROP and pure protection.
Credit protect business is flat YoY but going as per planned numbers, with good uptick expected in coming quarters.

GTI (Group Term Insurance) business is treated as a 1-year renewable contract; new premium is counted as APE, and renewal premium goes to renewal premium — the high group contribution (~25% of APE this quarter vs typical 10-12%) is a one-off lumpy item that inflates APE and depresses margin, given GTI's inherently lower margin versus individual business; management declined to comment on details of individual contracts (e.g., whether related to a certain PSU company).

Group protection APE grew 313% YoY to INR 12.3 billion, and group new business sum assured grew 265% YoY, while individual new business sum assured grew 46% YoY; individual protection APE grew 18% YoY to INR 1.9 billion; individual sum assured growth in the protection segment was 40%; overall combined (individual+group) protection growth was ~300%; total annuity and pension new business was INR 18.9 billion; rider sum assured represented 39% of individual sum assured.

subsections.label: Channel performance drivers
points: Company has focused for last 3 years on strengthening agency channel; opened more than 100 branches in last 2-3 years; agent addition and productivity have been increasing due to sustained efforts under the earlier 'Agency 2.0' program and subsequent 'Agency Next' program, resulting in strong growth in agency.

Agency growth was strong in 2024 and 2025 too, and continued to grow last year despite a very high FY25 base; current quarter agency growth was 19%+; remaining 3 quarters expected to see even stronger contribution.

SBI remains the company's strong point, delivering strong banca growth (~10% this quarter); company continues to explore potential on the agency side; going forward, a healthy mix of banca and agency contribution will drive overall growth.
Other banks/partners mix is strongly tilted towards non-ULIP (20% ULIP / 80% non-ULIP in Q1).
New corporate agency tie-up entered with J&K Bank during the quarter; business to start sometime in this quarter.

Bancassurance (SBI + RRBs) contributed 47% of total APE, with Individual APE of INR 24.5 billion; SBI branch productivity (Individual APE per branch) rose 7% to INR 4.1 million, with non-ULIP product mix in the SBI channel improving by 200 bps YoY.

Agency channel Individual APE grew 20% YoY to INR 13.1 billion, with agent productivity of INR 2 lakh; agency channel non-ULIP share improved from 43% to 46%; agency individual sum assured grew 63%; gross agents added exceeded 34,000 and 11 new branches were added in the quarter.

Other channels (direct, corporate agents, other banks, brokers, online, web aggregators) grew 160% YoY, contributing 28% of total APE; banks other than the SBI Group grew 31% on total APE basis and 19% on Individual NBP basis.
Company has more than 60,000 Certified Insurance Facilitators (CIFs).

subsections.label: Digital / operational efficiency in distribution
points: 99.9% of individual proposals submitted digitally.
67% of individual proposals processed through automated underwriting.

subsections.label: Competitive positioning
points: Company retains leadership position with 22.2% private market share and 15.2% total market share on Individual Rated Premium basis; on total new business premium basis, private market share was 20.5% and total market share was 8.2%.
Company's 3-year CAGR of Individual Rated New Business Premium (14%) outpaces the industry CAGR (13%).

Individual protection growth (~15% on APE basis per one analyst's calculation, industry comparison basis 19%) appears weaker versus peers reporting on an APE basis; management attributes this to a deliberate mix shift toward pure term/non-ROP products with lower ticket sizes versus ROP, rather than a competitive weakness — pure protection growth itself was 41-52%.
Company sees favorable regulatory positioning versus industry: lowest surrender ratio, lowest grievance ratio, and lowest commissions in the private industry.

Non-par product demand: company sees strong demand for assured-benefit non-par products in India; keeps a close eye on yield movement and repriced products (improved IRR for customers in June per yield curve movement), resulting in good market traction.

key_figures.label: Total individual protection APE growth (industry comparison basis)

subsections.label: Flagged headwinds
points: GST impact continues to drag margins (1.1% in Q1 FY27, following 1.1% in Q3 and 1.5% in Q4 of prior periods); expected to persist for ~2.5 months into Q2 before running off on a comparable basis.

One-off spike in other expenses due to higher stamp duty (tied to rising sum assured) and labour code impact (linked to employee headcount), first seen in Q1 FY27 versus June 2025; expected to streamline over the next 3 quarters.

61st month persistency has declined YoY due to the 'COVID cohort' moving through the persistency curve (from 13th to 25th to 37th to 49th and now to 61st month); this cohort is expected to move away from the 61st month bucket by end of Q3, after which 61st month persistency should normalize by year-end.
Higher, one-off GTI (Group Term Insurance) contribution to APE created a lumpy drag on overall VoNB margin this quarter; management does not expect this lumpiness to recur frequently.

Regulatory landscape evolution is a watch item, though management views it as broadly positive and expects future regulations to benefit the industry including SBI Life, given the company's already-favorable positioning (lowest surrender ratio, lowest grievance ratio, lowest commissions versus industry).

subsections.label: Reiterated guidance
points: IRP growth guidance reiterated at around 14-15% for the year; company delivered on this front in Q1.

VoNB margin guidance reiterated at 26-28% range; Q1 came in at the lower end (26.2%), with management confident margin has bottomed in Q1 and will move towards the upper end of the guided range as product mix normalizes (higher focus on individual policies) through the rest of the year.
GST drag expected to continue for ~2.5 months into Q2 (since GST was waived from 22nd September last year), and thereafter comparisons will be like-for-like/'par-to-par'.
Deferred annuity (regular pay) product launch expected within the next quarter; company is working on the product and will launch at an opportune time.
Full-year target product mix: continuation of the current quarter-end mix trend (ULIP ~62%, non-ULIP ~38% on IRP basis, majority increase from non-par).

guidance_ledger.statement: Our growth projections for the year on IRP basis remains at 14%, 15%.
We continue to be in the range that we guided in 26% to 28%... Going forward, as the product mix normalizes, our margin will be moving towards the upper end of our band.
There will be some impact for 2.5 months in the current quarter also. And then it will be on par-to-par basis.
Other expenses will continue in tandem with the sum assured... it will streamline as per the plan over the next 3 quarters.

guidance_ledger.metric: Regular pay deferred annuity product launch
guidance_ledger.statement: Hopefully within next quarter, you will be able to see that... We are working on the product, and we'll launch the product at opportune time.
As at the end of quarter on IRP basis, ULIP contribution has come down to 62% and non-ULIP are contributing 38%... For the year also, in fact, our target is to have this kind of product mix only.
This cohort will move away from the 61st month by end of third quarter. So by end of the year, the 61st month persistency, we are expecting will be back to normal.
It is flat as compared to last year. But it is going as per the planned number. So we will see some good uptick in the coming quarters.
Rider APE, we don't have right now. So we will share with you separately.
We intend to maintain the growth rate at around 14%, which has been our CAGR for the last 3 to 5 years, and we will continue to maintain this kind of growth rate in coming year also.

Next year opex will reflect the full-year GST impact (versus half-year in FY26), but it will not have much further impact as far as opex ratio is concerned for the company due to other cost-rationalization measures.

The company has adopted a phased and well-governed approach to Ind AS transition and proposes to seek regulatory forbearance for an adoption from April 1, 2027, with comprehensive preparatory measures already initiated.
In last 2 years, we have seen approximately 3% to 4% shift from banca to agency and emerging businesses, and we expect the similar trend in coming years.
We are not targeting any reduction from SBI; what we are targeting is tapping additional opportunity on the agency and emerging business channel.

risk_register.risk: GST impact on margins
risk_register.note: GST drag of ~1.1% in Q1 FY27, in line with recent quarters (1.1% in Q3, 1.5% in Q4); expected to continue for ~2.5 months into Q2 before running off on a par-to-par basis.

risk_register.risk: One-off spike in other expenses (stamp duty, labour code)
risk_register.note: Higher stamp duty tied to rising sum assured and labour code impact (headcount-linked) drove up other expenses this quarter; expected to streamline over next 3 quarters.

risk_register.risk: 61st month persistency decline (COVID cohort)
risk_register.note: COVID-era cohort has moved into the 61st month bucket causing a dip; expected to move out by end of Q3 and normalize by year-end.

risk_register.risk: Lumpy/one-off GTI business dragging VoNB margin
risk_register.note: Higher-than-usual GTI contribution to APE (~25% vs typical 10-12%) is lower margin than individual business and dragged overall VoNB margin by ~60 bps in the mix walk; management does not expect this lumpiness to recur frequently.

risk_register.risk: Regulatory landscape evolution
risk_register.note: Company awaits shape of upcoming regulations; views current positioning (lowest surrender/grievance ratios, lowest commissions) as favorable and expects future regulatory changes to be broadly positive for the industry.

risk_register.risk: Geopolitical volatility impacting equity/fixed income markets and customer behavior
risk_register.note: Last two months of geopolitical events caused market volatility, but MF inflows remained robust and company sales in Feb-March were decent.

risk_register.risk: Sluggish industry-wide Q4 growth
risk_register.note: Entire insurance sector had a sluggish Q4, linked to global geopolitical events; company still met ~13% annual guidance.

risk_register.risk: GST cost impact on commissions and margins
risk_register.note: GST impact (from business written after Sept 22) increased opex/cost ratios and pressured VNB margin; full-year impact expected in FY27; company has offset it via product mix and interest rate benefits.

risk_register.risk: Revised Labour Law / Labour Code cost impact
risk_register.note: New one-off cost item impacting FY26 operating expense ratio alongside GST.

risk_register.risk: Interest rate / yield curve volatility affecting non-par pricing
risk_register.note: Current yield levels seen as not sustainable; company monitors and re-prices non-par products dynamically when it sees sustainable yield levels, balancing customer benefit.

risk_register.risk: Potential mandate for open-architecture bancassurance
risk_register.note: Raised via media interview by Department of Financial Services Secretary; RBI draft guidelines in public domain (effective ~July 1) do not mention open architecture; company has no additional information but is confident in navigating any regulatory change given 25-year track record.

risk_register.risk: Regulatory shift to Ind AS / IFRS 17 and Risk-Based Capital (RBC)
risk_register.note: Company preparing via phased approach and forbearance request for April 1, 2027 adoption; also monitoring RBC discussions for capital implications.

risk_register.risk: Persistency drop in 61st month cohort
risk_register.note: Likely linked to ULIP policies sold during the COVID period.

themes.label: Margin resilience via mix optimization
themes.note: VoNB margin at 26.2% (lower end of 26-28% guided band) due to one-off high GTI mix; management expects margin to move toward upper end as individual mix normalizes.

themes.label: GST/regulatory cost impact
themes.note: GST drag of ~1.1% continued in Q1 FY27, in line with prior quarters; expected to persist ~2.5 months into Q2 before running off.

themes.label: Product mix shift (non-ULIP push)
themes.note: ULIP contribution down to 61-62% from 65% a year ago, with non-par and par products gaining share; rider attachment on ULIP up to 45-50%.

themes.label: Agency channel expansion
themes.note: Agency Individual APE grew 20% YoY with 34,000+ gross agents added and 11 new branches; management expects even stronger contribution in remaining quarters.

themes.label: Protection segment momentum
themes.note: Individual protection APE grew 18-22%, with pure protection growing 41-52% as company shifts mix from ROP to non-ROP/pure term products.

themes.label: Open architecture / bancassurance regulatory risk
themes.note: Management views regulatory landscape as broadly positive given company's favorable positioning (lowest surrender, grievance ratios, and commissions); awaiting shape of future regulations.

themes.label: GTI-driven lumpy margin drag
themes.note: One-off high Group Term Insurance contribution (~25% of APE vs typical 10-12%) drove a 60 bps negative product-mix impact on VoNB margin; management does not expect frequent recurrence.

key_takeaways: New business premium stands at INR89.1 billion with a growth of 23% and private market share of 20.5%.
Individual rated new business premium stands at INR39.7 billion with a growth of 14% and private market share of 22.2%.
Gross written premium stands at INR212.9 billion with a growth of 20%.
The company's profit after tax for the quarter stood at INR7.2 billion, registering a strong growth of 22% over the corresponding quarter of previous year.
Value of new business stands at INR14.1 billion with a growth of 29%. VoNB margin stands at 26.2% for the period ended June 30, 2026.
Indian embedded value for the company as on June 30, 2026, stands at INR852.9 billion.
Our assets under management stands at INR5.2 trillion with a growth of 10% over the corresponding quarter last year.
Solvency ratio of 1.96 is as against the regulatory requirement of 1.5.
pressing_questions: Can you help provide some color on what kind of margins the GTI will contribute and where has been the overall direction of margins, given that despite GST hit, individual/ex-GTI margins appear to have improved strongly?

Can you quantify the negative 0.6% margin impact on overall VNB from GTI, and what was the positive impact in the individual business, to give color on normalized margins? (Management declined: 'We don't generally discuss product-wise margins. We don't disclose those numbers.')
Is the GTI business related to a certain PSU company, or what is the nature of this contract? (Management declined to comment on individual contracts/policies.)
Possible to quantify the rider APE? (Management: 'Rider APE, we don't have right now. So we will share with you separately.')

quarters.summary: SBI Life delivered strong FY26 growth (NBP +20%, GWP +19%, VNB +12%, VoNB margin 27.5%) despite GST and Labour Law cost impacts; management guided to continued ~14% APE/growth CAGR, VoNB margin range of 26-28% (reporting above 27%), plans to launch a deferred annuity product by Q1FY27 (June, else next quarter), and a phased Ind AS transition with regulatory forbearance sought for adoption from April 1, 2027.

key_figures.label: Opex ratio excluding GST/Labour Code impact
Annualized full-year GST impact on margin if implemented from start of year

subsections.label: PAT and cost drivers
points: Financial performance reflects the impact of GST and the revised Labour Law.
Excluding these one-time impacts, PAT would have grown 29% to INR31.2 billion.

Opex ratio and total cost ratio increases YoY (5.3%→6.1% and 9.7%→10.6%) are attributed to GST impact, opening more branches, higher IT spend for customer ease and processes, and spends on training agency force and CIFs.

GST impact on commission and renewal is reflected fully for business written after 22nd September 2025; for business written prior to that date, only renewal commission GST impact is reflected — full-year impact will show up in FY27.
Excluding GST/Labour Code impact, opex ratio would have been around 5.5% versus reported 5.3% in the prior year comparison mentioned by management.

Management does not expect opex ratio to rise materially further; other cost-rationalization measures will offset full-year GST impact in FY27; investment in branches and IT infrastructure will continue.

subsections.label: VNB Walk and margin drivers
points: VNB growth of 12% was driven by both volume growth and favorable shift in product mix.
Better product mix and benefits from interest rate movement offset the GST impact on margin, keeping margin at 27.5% despite GST impact.
Management maintained VoNB margin guidance range of 26%-28% for the year and delivered at the higher end.
Guidance for margin trajectory ahead is to stay within 26%-28% range with an endeavor to report above 27%.
Management reiterated the FY27-FY28 margin guidance range when asked whether to shift it to FY27-FY29.

subsections.label: Embedded Value walk and operating variance
points: Strong positive operating variance was seen in the EV walk, primarily coming from mortality profit and persistency and to a lesser extent expenses.
This positive variance is not from conservative/prudent assumptions but reflects the better quality of business being written and underwritten.
Last year, some persistency assumptions were already capitalized, so persistency variance is slightly lower this year versus last year.

0.2% difference between VNB assumption changes and EV operating variance is not considered significant; products currently being sold differ from the existing back book, so correlating VNB assumptions with EV operating variance directly may not be fair.

Minor refinement was made across all assumptions including demographic, expense, and other parameters due to a marginal (50 bps) persistency assumption change, attributed partly to COVID-era ULIP business persistency drop and partly to long-term protection improvement in persistency.

subsections.label: Solvency and capital
points: Solvency ratio of 1.90 achieved through efficient use of capital and internal accruals; no fresh capital raised.

Company is assessing the impact of Ind AS and Risk-Based Capital (RBC), which are being discussed at the regulatory level for introduction in the near future, and will take an appropriate call at the appropriate time.

subsections.label: Persistency
points: 13th month persistency stands at 87.9%, an improvement of 53 basis points YoY.
49th month persistency stands at 69.1%, an improvement of 107 basis points YoY.
61st month persistency saw a drop, likely related to ULIP business sold during the COVID period.

subsections.label: Claims and mis-selling
points: Death claim settlement ratio stands at 99.4% for FY26.
Mis-selling ratio stands at 0.02%, one of the lowest in the private industry, achieved through consistent right-selling approach.

subsections.label: Product mix strategy
points: Company continues to advance product diversification strategy through focused, well-sequenced initiatives; launches aligned to key customer needs across child plans, protection solutions and non-par guaranteed segment.

Strategy has been to improve product mix in favor of non-ULIP products over the last couple of years, with good product launches across non-par, par and protection segments to improve profitability via healthy product mix.
Par product growth came off a lower base last year (only a couple of products); this year new products were launched in the par category with very good customer response, driving robust growth.

Par contribution is still small (~7% of individual APE) but management expects new non-par launch to see traction and improve non-par growth, especially if interest rates stabilize allowing re-pricing with better returns for customers.
No higher sum assured ULIPs (e.g., 20x/30x cover) currently offered; company will look at the opportunity and decide in due course.

New non-par product launched (in January) replaces existing non-par product and reflects current yield; company monitors interest rate volatility and re-prices dynamically when yield curve is deemed sustainable, balancing benefit passed to customers.

On protection side, pure protection sum assured growth is significantly higher than premium share growth because pure protection carries significantly higher sum assured per policy; SBI's own protection share (4%) has remained broadly flat but mix shifted from TROP toward higher proportion of pure protection, with higher growth in number of policies and sum assured.

subsections.label: Group Credit Life / GTI
points: Q4 group business growth increase attributed to reduction in GTI (Group Term Insurance) business relative to Credit Life, not a genuine step-up.
Quarterly split of Credit Life vs group business not disclosed on call; to be shared separately.
Banca Credit Life growth of 14% viewed as reasonable, faster than bank's loan growth; attachment in home loans has increased substantially.
Attachment ratio for Credit Life on home loans is around 50%, similar to previous years.

subsections.label: Channel-wise margin disclosure declined
points: Management does not disclose VNB margin by channel; commission structures are similar across channels and margin is looked at on a company-level, longer-term basis rather than by channel.

subsections.label: Digitalization
points: Digitalization is transforming the life insurance industry, enabling enhanced services and more seamless customer experience.
Company continues efficient usage of technology for process simplification.
Deferred annuity product under development — company aims to launch by June (this quarter); if not, will launch in the next quarter.

Deferred regular-pay annuity will complete the company's full suite of annuity products (single premium deferred annuity, immediate annuity, NPS annuity); expected to lower average ticket size for annuity products and increase the number of annuitants, aiding growth in number of policies (NOP) alongside protection products.

subsections.label: Distribution strategy
points: Company leverages well-diversified multichannel distribution strategy spanning bancassurance, agency and digital platforms enabling consistent, broad-based growth across segments.

Focus for the last 2 years has been strengthening the agency channel — opening more branches, adding more agents, improving agent productivity; contribution of agency channel in distribution mix has improved over last couple of years.
Emerging business channel is small but growing fast with good investment and results; direct/website channel investment will continue and is expected to become a formidable force.

Q4 industry-wide sluggishness attributed to geopolitical events; banca channel met internal budget for the year despite Q4 dip; company focuses on annual rather than quarterly/monthly numbers and met its ~13% annual growth guidance, with 3-year CAGR slightly higher.

No confirmation of RBI communication on open-architecture bancassurance; RBI draft guidelines (public domain for a couple of months, expected effective July 1) do not mention open architecture; company confident in ability to adapt to any regulatory change given 25-year track record.

No target to reduce SBI's contribution to distribution mix; rather, tapping additional opportunity in agency and emerging business channels, whose higher growth will organically increase their share — approximately 3-4% shift from banca to agency/emerging channels over the last 2 years, expected to continue in a similar trend.

New agents hired are trained via a robust in-house system (not open architecture in agency); growth in agency contribution comes from both increased agent count and improved productivity; newly opened branches take time to breakeven but are on track and satisfactory; specific branch/vintage contribution numbers not disclosed.
Own website online channel growth for the full year is in the range of 48%-50%; company will continue to focus more on this channel.

subsections.label: Ind AS transition
points: The year marked a significant regulatory shift for the life insurance industry including GST exemptions and the regulators' announcement on transitioning to Indian Accounting Standards (Ind AS) framework, aimed at enhancing transparency and quality of financial information.

Company has adopted a phased and well-governed approach to Ind AS transition and proposes to seek regulatory forbearance for adoption from April 1, 2027, with comprehensive preparatory measures already initiated.
Company has submitted pro forma Ind AS financials to the regulator for the last two financial years and will be prepared to launch into the IFRS/Ind AS regime from next fiscal year onward.

No new KPI changes anticipated to be disclosed at this point; management will observe how the framework evolves over the next 2-3 years before introducing new KPIs, given implications for business strategy.
Company is also assessing regulatory discussions around Risk-Based Capital (RBC) for future introduction and will respond at the appropriate time.

subsections.label: External risk factors
points: Geopolitical events over the last two months have caused volatility in equity and fixed income markets, impacting customer behavior, though mutual fund inflows remain robust and company sales growth in February and March remained decent.
Entire insurance sector saw sluggish Q4 growth, linked to geopolitical events globally.

GST impact (effective from business written after 22nd September) increased cost ratios and required product-mix/margin management to offset; a permanent embedded cost going forward, with full-year impact to be seen in FY27.
Revised Labour Law/Labour Code is a new cost item impacting FY26 operating expenses.
Volatility in yield curve makes current interest rate levels not seen as sustainable, affecting non-par product pricing decisions.

Potential regulatory push toward open-architecture bancassurance (raised in media interview by Department of Financial Services Secretary) is being monitored; no confirmed information beyond public domain RBI draft guidelines.
Potential future regulatory changes from Ind AS/IFRS 17 and Risk-Based Capital (RBC) framework being monitored for capital and reporting implications.

Growth for FY26 was 13.2%, roughly in line with ~13% annual guidance despite a sluggish Q4 and market volatility.

subsections.label: Margin guidance
points: VoNB margin guidance range of 26%-28% reiterated for coming years, with an endeavor to report above 27%.
Management declined to shift the margin guidance period from FY27-FY28 to FY27-FY29 when asked; reiterated FY27-FY28 guidance stands.
Margin guidance factors in continued product-mix improvement to offset GST-related cost pressure while maintaining ~14% growth.

subsections.label: Cost ratio outlook
points: Opex ratio impact from GST will be a full-year effect in FY27 versus half-year in FY26, but management expects no material further increase in opex ratio beyond current levels due to other cost-rationalization measures, even as branch and IT infrastructure investment continues.

subsections.label: Product launch guidance
points: Deferred annuity product targeted for launch by June (Q1 FY27), or by the next quarter if delayed.

guidance_ledger.statement: We intend to maintain the growth rate at around 14%, which has been our CAGR for the last 3 to 5 years, and we will continue to maintain this kind of growth rate in coming year also.
We expect our margin will continue to be in a similar range that we maintain, about 26% to 28% range, and our endeavor is to report the margin above 27%.

Next year opex will reflect the full-year GST impact (versus half-year in FY26), but it will not have much further impact as far as opex ratio is concerned for the company due to other cost-rationalization measures.
Our endeavor is to launch this deferred annuity product in this quarter itself. So we are aiming to go live by June, we should launch the deferred annuity. Otherwise, we'll go to the next quarter.

The company has adopted a phased and well-governed approach to Ind AS transition and proposes to seek regulatory forbearance for an adoption from April 1, 2027, with comprehensive preparatory measures already initiated.
In last 2 years, we have seen approximately 3% to 4% shift from banca to agency and emerging businesses, and we expect the similar trend in coming years.
We are not targeting any reduction from SBI; what we are targeting is tapping additional opportunity on the agency and emerging business channel.

GLAND.about: Established in Hyderabad, India in 1978, Gland Pharma has grown over the years from a contract manufacturer of small volume liquid parenteral products, to become one of the largest and fastest growing injectable-focused companies, with a global footprint across 60 countries, including the United States, Europe, Canada, Australia, India and other markets. We operate primarily under a business to business (B2B) model and have an excellent track record in the development, manufacturing and marketing of complex injectables. This presence across the value chain has helped us witness exponential growth. We are promoted by Shanghai Fosun Pharma, a global pharmaceutical major.

quarters.summary: Gland Pharma delivered a strong start to FY27 with 20% YoY revenue growth, 47% YoY PAT growth and margin expansion, driven by CDMO/B2B momentum, recent launches and improved utilization; management flagged a new large strategic manufacturing agreement (USD90-100mn peak revenue potential from CY2029), an in-licensing liposomal deal (meaningful revenue from FY30), continued Cenexi integration/turnaround, and reiterated a near-term consolidated EBITDA margin target of ~30% and a re-evaluated ~20% CDMO-led growth CAGR over the next 4 years, alongside ongoing brownfield/greenfield capacity expansion.

subsections.label: Margin drivers
points: Adjusted EBITDA margin improvement YoY driven by higher CDMO revenue, favorable contribution margin mix, operating leverage, productivity improvements and cost optimization initiatives.

Gross margin benefited from favorable product mix, increasing CDMO contribution, improved operational efficiencies, procurement initiatives, yield improvement, alternate sourcing and manufacturing optimization.
Continued utilization improvement across manufacturing operations and growing contribution from value-added products supported margin expansion.

subsections.label: PAT and other income/forex
points: PAT decline vs Q4 FY26 largely attributable to forex loss in Q1 FY27 vis-à-vis forex gain in the previous quarter.
Other income comprises primarily interest income.

Forex loss of INR36 million was included in other expense in Q1 FY27, compared to forex gain of INR508 million in Q4 FY26 (included in other income) and forex gain of INR39 million in Q1 FY26 (included in other income).

subsections.label: Balance sheet and cash
points: External debt remained at a minimal level; company remains net cash surplus and well capitalized.
Cash flow from operations reflects strong operating performance and disciplined working capital management.
Focus on inventory optimization, receivables management and supply chain efficiency continues to support cash generation while ensuring uninterrupted customer service levels.

subsections.label: Capital expenditure / capital allocation
points: Capex during the quarter primarily towards capacity expansion projects, capability enhancement initiatives, infrastructure additions and investments supporting future growth opportunities across CDMO and fill/finish platforms.
Company has commenced execution of the recently announced INR2,000 crores capex program; ongoing projects for vial, ophthalmic, BFS lines and liposome products at India sites remain on track.
Capacity expansion projects for anticipated CDMO collaboration demand have been approved and are being prioritized for execution.
At Cenexi, growth capex for addition of new block with vial and lyos at BLA and high-speed ampoule line at Fontenay on track to finish by end of next year.
Immediate capex of INR165 crores earmarked for an isolator line in the oncology plant (installation expected January of this year) tied to the new strategic manufacturing agreement.
Additional capex planned for the Neuland collaboration (building a block for sterile API manufacturing), project already started.
This year (FY27) total planned capex is about INR550 crores, scaling up as brownfield projects (e.g., Suite 10 in Pashamylaram - new vial line BFS and ophthalmic line) are built out.

subsections.label: CDMO business
points: Growth driven by recent product launches and progression of existing commercial programs.
Customer engagement remains strong; company continues to attract robust global pharmaceutical companies seeking reliable sterile manufacturing partners.
Pipeline of development and commercial opportunities remains healthy, providing good visibility for future growth.
Continued expansion of CDMO partner and product portfolio validates investments in capabilities, infrastructure and customer relationships over the last several years.
During the quarter, secured multiple new CDMO contracts, including a new GLP-1 collaboration; expanded pipeline across complex injectables, peptides and drug delivery platforms.
Strong customer interest and growing funnel of opportunities provide confidence in long-term growth prospects of CDMO business.

Target is to reach ~30% CDMO contribution on a consol basis in the near term; for the next 2 years business mix expected to remain around 50-50 between CDMO and B2B; post CY29 there could be a skew where CDMO business becomes larger than B2B.

subsections.label: B2B business
points: Growth supported by increased demand from existing customers, new contract wins and higher volumes across several key products.
Recent product launches, together with strong execution and supply reliability, enabled deepening of customer relationships and expansion of market share across select products and markets.

subsections.label: Cenexi (European operations)
points: Cenexi is now fully integrated into the broader CDMO business as integration benefits between Gland Pharma and Cenexi continue to increase; its contribution is increasingly reflected in consolidated performance.
Fontenay facility delivered good performance despite disruption from the summer heat wave in Europe, benefiting from production ramp-up of new ampoule line and higher operational efficiency.

During the summer shutdown, as part of ongoing modernization, one of the older ampoule lines will be discontinued and replaced with a new high-capacity line, expected to enter production in early 2027, adding ~30 million ampoules of annual capacity for enhanced efficiency, competitiveness and growth potential.

At Hérouville facility, activity levels continue to increase steadily; revenue growth supported by higher volumes from 2 products successfully launched during 2025, which continue to gain momentum; encouraging customer demand trends and improving utilization levels noted.

In Braine-l'Alleud, secured a prefilled syringe manufacturing program for an injectable orphan drug for a European customer, strengthening the site's order book and reflecting continued momentum in business development and customer acquisition.

Cenexi will play a role in the newly announced strategic manufacturing agreement by warehousing certain products, packaging a few, and doing final QP release for the European market — an end-to-end solution requirement from the partner.

subsections.label: Growth CAGR re-evaluation
points: Previously guided ~15% CAGR over next 4-5 years; with the new strategic contract (covering ~12% of current revenue, ~9-10% three years out), company is re-evaluating CAGR upward to around 20% growth over the next 4 years, with further clarity expected next quarter/by Sept-Oct as other initiatives and discussions with additional partners progress.

Current year FY27 growth on constant currency basis still seen as 15% achievable, with potential to exceed 15% if the bag line receives FDA approval in Q3 (expected around August/September) given tight capacity constraints on bag line and ophthalmic products.

subsections.label: R&D focus
points: R&D efforts remain focused on building a differentiated pipeline, aligned with strategy of building a differentiated portfolio of complex injectable products and advanced drug delivery platforms.
Investments continue to focus on complex injectable peptides, depot products, drug delivery technologies and liposomal products.
Pipeline increasingly focused on complex injectables and differentiated platforms expected to drive long-term value.
Remain committed to strengthening development pipeline and expanding technology capabilities to support long-term growth.

subsections.label: New collaborations
points: Entered a strategic collaboration with Neuland Laboratories for the manufacture of sterile APIs for microparticle depot products; long-acting depot formulations represent an attractive, growing global pharmaceutical segment; partnership strengthens capabilities in complex injectable technologies and complements strategy of building differentiated, high-value product platforms.

Entered an in-licensing agreement with a China-based development company for development, manufacturing and commercialization of a niche liposomal product for U.S. and European markets; strengthens entry into differentiated drug delivery systems and expands product portfolio; collaboration has potential to extend beyond a single product given partner's extensive pipeline for complex injectable products; given development timelines, meaningful revenue contribution expected to start from FY30.

subsections.label: Strategic manufacturing and supply agreement (announced day before call)
points: Executed with one of the leading global pharmaceutical companies for technology transfer, manufacturing and supply of a portfolio of sterile injectables to global markets.
Portfolio comprises a diversified basket of oncology and non-oncology products in vials, lyos, ampoules and prefilled syringe presentations, covering complex and conventional injectable formulations.
Agreement expected to provide strong long-term business visibility, with revenue generation anticipated from calendar year 2029.
Manufacturing to happen entirely at Gland's Indian sites; partner is a specialty pharma global company with revenue mix of generics and complex/specialty pharma (~30-40% from specialty business).

Estimate given is a preliminary view of products being transferred over next 2 years; potential exists to add more products in future, including from partner's development pipeline of specialty products.
Technology transfer activities to start from September of this year; first set of products to be transferred within 24 months; filings to occur every quarter.
Revenue ramp-up expected from 2029 to 2030, with the entire portfolio hopefully launched by CY30 (U.S. products via CB-30 format seen as easier/faster to launch).

Cenexi's global supply/warehousing/packaging/QP release capability was cited as an enabler — without Cenexi, this end-to-end solution for the partner would not have been possible, reinforcing the strategic rationale behind the Cenexi acquisition.

Management views this as reflective of a broader opportunity: large pharma companies procuring from 80-100 different sites are looking for end-to-end solution providers; European manufacturing sites are 5-6x more expensive than India, and shifting branded manufacturing to the U.S. can cause loss of operational leverage for companies' own or other CDMO sites — creating opportunities for Gland given its quality track record and breadth of platforms.

points: Fontenay: discontinuing an older ampoule line during summer shutdown, replacing with a new high-capacity line entering production in early 2027, adding ~30 million ampoules of annual capacity.
Cenexi growth capex covers addition of new block with vial and lyos capability at BLA (Braine-l'Alleud) and a high-speed ampoule line at Fontenay, on track to finish by end of next year.

subsections.label: Positioning versus big pharma sourcing model
points: Company is targeting big pharma clients that currently procure products from over 80-100 different sites due to in-licensing and contract manufacturing over time; Gland is positioning to offer end-to-end solutions across different markets.
This approach helps partners economically (European manufacturing sites are 5-6x more expensive than India) and helps Gland gain market share in ROW markets and increase margins.

key_takeaways: We have started FY27 with a strong momentum, delivering healthy year-on-year growth in revenues, EBITDA and profit after tax.

For the first quarter of FY27, we reported revenues of INR18,003 million, representing a growth of 20% year-on-year. Adjusted EBITDA for this quarter stood at INR5,102 million with margins of 28%, while profit after tax was INR3,170 million, reflecting a healthy growth of 47% year-on-year with PAT margin of 18%.
Revenue from the CDMO segment stood at INR8,915 million, which grew by 20% year-on-year and contributed 50% of total revenues during the quarter.
Our B2B business revenue stood at INR9,088 million, contributing 50% of total revenues and recorded healthy growth of 19% year-on-year.

Yesterday, we announced the execution of a strategic manufacturing and supply agreement with one of the leading global pharmaceutical companies for the technology transfer, manufacturing and supply of a portfolio of sterilized injectables to the global markets... revenue potential is expected to be approximately USD90 million to USD100 million.
We have also entered a strategic collaboration with Neuland Laboratories for the manufacture of sterile APIs for microparticle depot products.

Another important strategic development during the quarter is our in-licensing agreement with a China-based development company for the development, manufacturing, commercialization of a niche liposomal product for the U.S. and European markets.
As of June 30, 2026, total cash and cash equivalents at the group level stood at INR35,466 million... we are a net cash surplus company with a net cash position of INR32,939 million.

quarters.summary: Gland Pharma delivered its highest-ever quarterly revenue and EBITDA in Q4 FY'26, with strong full-year growth led by CDMO ramp-up (28% growth, 46% of total revenue), new product launches (Dalbavancin, multivitamin), improving capacity utilization and a turning-around Cenexi (EBITDA positive, targeting mid-teen EBITDA in the medium term). Management guided FY'27 consolidated revenue growth of 12-13% (constant currency, excluding GLP-1 upside), a four-year consol CAGR target of 15%, base-business EBITDA margin of 33-35%, consol EBITDA margin of ~25-26%, and Cenexi revenue of ~EUR200 million with mid-to-high single-digit EBITDA by year-end FY'27.
