key_takeaways: It has been a very strong quarter and a year for us in terms of revenues and profitability. This has been driven by robust growth in the CDMO segment, alongside new product launches, improved Cenexi performance and healthy profitability across various business segments supported by ongoing cost efficiency initiatives.

For the fourth quarter FY '26, we reported revenues of INR17,428 million, reflecting a growth of 22% year-on-year. Adjusted EBITDA for the quarter stood at INR5,244 million with margins of 30% and adjusted profit after tax was INR3,667 million with margins of 21%.

For the full year FY '26, our revenue stood at INR64,307 million, registering a growth of 14.5%. Adjusted EBITDA came in at INR16,826 million, with margins of 26%, while adjusted PAT stood at INR10,455 million, with margins of 16%. The CDMO business represented 46% of total revenues supported by healthy growth of 28%, driven by our continued strategic focus on investments.
One of the major CDMO projects announced earlier is progressing well and is expected to be commercialized in H2 of FY28 with an estimated annual revenue potential of USD25 million to USD30 million.

In the GLP-1 space, we have made significant progress with 8 contracts already signed and the additional 6 to 7 are expected to be signed soon. Our current cartridge capacity now stands at 140 million units.

Cenexi recorded EUR45 million in revenue this quarter, a 4% increase over the same period last year... After a profitable Q3 FY '26 quarter, we are pleased to inform you that we delivered an EBITDA of EUR1 million in Q4 FY '26, in line with our guidance.
So for FY '27, our target is to reach at least mid-single digit, high single-digit EBITDA. By the end of this year, we should get there.
The next four years, we're looking at a CAGR of 15% at a consol basis.

ERIS.about: ERIS Lifesciences Ltd is engaged in the business of manufacture and marketing of pharmaceutical products.[1]

quarters.summary: Eris Lifesciences reported Q1 FY27 DBF revenue growth of 14% YoY and consolidated revenue growth of 13% YoY, with PAT growth of 14-15%. Management expects Cardiac to approach market growth in the next two quarters, OAD to recover to 5-6% growth once the Glimisave-MV base effect rolls off, gross margins to stay pressured for another quarter before improving from Q3 and normalizing by Q4 as Bhopal ramps up, Swiss Parenterals growth to stay neutral to low-single-digit with a possible ~200bps EBITDA margin hit (clarity by end of Q2), full-year DBF revenue growth guided at ~14% (300bps ahead of an assumed 11% market growth), and exports expected to be flattish with 200-300bps margin loss, with Bhopal facility commercializing in August.

subsections.label: Gross margin dynamics
points: Domestic formulations gross margin has been in a 76-77% band for all quarters of last year; Q1 of this year is a departure from that band.
The departure has largely happened because of product mix change, driven by Insulins and Biologics catching up in growth.

Management expects the organization to largely remain in this range for at least one more quarter (Q2), with gross margins starting to improve by Q3, and a fair chance of coming back to prior levels by Q4.

Gross margins will not essentially decide EBITDA margins going forward because the business is moving into therapies (Biologics/Insulin) where the gap between gross margin and EBITDA margin is much smaller than the company average of 39 percentage points.

In Biologics, the middle cost portion is not as large as in other domestic branded products because YPMs (value per patient/month, potential 15-16 INR lakhs) are very high, unlike the lower company-average YPM of 6.5 INR lakhs in Q1.
Gross margin recovery is expected to come from Bhopal facility ramp-up, improving the company's ability to maneuver production and costs.

Ashish Thavkar asked whether gross margin contraction also includes higher solvent prices; management confirmed there have been certain issues but said dependence is slightly lower due to a concentrated therapy mix; the impact has been more pronounced in the International business (delays in sending/receiving goods) than in DBF.

Insulin EBITDA margin is 30-31% and Biologics EBITDA margin is illustratively around 20% in Q1 FY27, reflecting the smaller gap between gross margin and EBITDA margin in these therapies versus the company average.

subsections.label: Cash flow and capital metrics
points: OCF/EBITDA of 77% is expected to be the trend for the rest of the financial year, as confirmed by the CFO.
CapEx for Q1 FY27 was INR 88 crores, reflecting continued investment behind facilities and manufacturing technology.
Effective book tax rate improved to 20% in Q1 FY27 from 22.5% in Q1 FY26.
EPS for Q1 FY27 was INR 10.3.

subsections.label: Swiss Parenterals financial impact
points: Swiss Parenterals EBITDA margin impact expected to be a couple hundred basis points due to ongoing remediation work at the facility.
Swiss Parenterals revenue growth for FY27 guided to be neutral to a low single-digit growth, with EBITDA margin compression of a couple hundred basis points.

subsections.label: Therapy-wise performance
points: DBF revenue grew 14% YoY in Q1 FY27, with 7 out of 10 therapies delivering double-digit growth.

Key franchises including Insulin and Semaglutide brand SUNDAE posted strong performances in Q1; SUNDAE achieved 20% market share by sale volume and 14% by sale value in its first quarter after launch.
Semaglutide monthly run-rate reached INR 4 crore per month as of June/July, with Endocrinologists/Diabetologists contributing 70% of prescriptions.

Cardiac segment underperformance driven largely by trailing performance in Hypertension, a large part of the Cardiology portfolio; efforts already started to get across the line, with improvement visible from data expected this month; two products are being tracked to get on track.

OAD reported growth of 2% (versus IPM/market growth of 11%) is distorted by a product (Glimisave-MV) banned last year that continues to reflect in the base; excluding this anomaly, internal growth is ~6%; anomaly expected to clear next month, after which growth should reach 5-6%.

Bridging the OAD gap to market (6-12%) is being addressed via business-as-usual approach: refocusing sales launch effort and launching a couple of new products; management expressed confidence based on past experience turning around diabetes therapy performance.

Cardiac gap bridging strategy centers on the launch of Esaxerenone, a nonsteroidal MRA third-party product; launch was delayed due to approval delays, now visible for first fortnight of August; considered a good opportunity.

VMN section saw good double-digit growth; management does not attribute this to a GLP-1 'rub-off' effect since GLP-1 has reached too few patients to have a robust adjacent-therapy effect; hunch is that stocking has gone up and become a little liberalized, but no structural explanation identified.
Women's Health already market-beating; Derma performance is strong ('right up there'); CNS also expected to be market-beating, aided by a good new product launch giving good returns.
Insulin franchise continues to be a market-share-gain story with significant headroom for growth from existing products RHI, Glargine, and a comprehensive pipeline of Insulin Analogues.
Company has approximately 4,000 MRs in India supporting these therapy franchises.

subsections.label: Swiss Parenterals
points: Growth is softer in Q1 versus anticipation; some remediation work is happening at the facility.
Management does not expect a large revenue impact, but EBITDA could see a hit of a couple hundred basis points due to remediation work.

Growth for the segment could remain in the same vicinity as current levels or even lower, ranging from neutral to low-single-digit growth (either degrowth or growth), with margins potentially compressing a couple hundred basis points.
If remediation plans succeed, margin/growth situation might improve in Q4.
Management asked for one more quarter (by end of Q2) to give a clear-cut answer on Swiss Parenterals trajectory; no full-year guidance provided yet, no promise of growth over last year.

subsections.label: Insulin Analogs pipeline
points: Two engineering batches and one PV batch of Analogs already taken at Bhopal unit; DS made by Levim, DP already sold.
Three engineering batches taken: recombinant Semaglutide, Degludec, and a Degludec combination product; plus one PV batch overall for Insulin Analogs.
These products will go through the filing process for the next phase this current quarter and then through the regulatory process.
Aspart product timeline is earlier than the others; expected to launch this calendar year, much earlier than other Analogs; the rest of the Analogs pipeline would be pushed to next year.
Management estimates the Analogs could be 'up there' in Q3, but expressed skepticism about calling out a firm date given past hits and misses in timelines.

subsections.label: Semaglutide (SUNDAE) product launches
points: Wegovy Gx (obesity SKU) version being launched this month; billing to begin by end of month and launch by next month, expected to add incrementally to Semaglutide revenue.

No price correction on Semaglutide has occurred since launch; prescriber base has not spread as fast as anticipated, so management does not see this as the right time to reduce price further; price correction could occur once the market escalates and spreads out.

subsections.label: Future product launches
points: Product launches are now viewed as a regular business activity; major launches will be specifically called out (as was done for Esaxerenone).
A big product launch is being planned for Q3 that management considers significant.
Growth is described as a function of volume, new products, and price rise.

subsections.label: Bhopal facility
points: Bhopal facility will be commercialized next month (August); licenses are in place.
Ramp-up in Bhopal will take a gradual process, with products taken one by one; by end of Q3, the facility is expected to be more or less fully ramped up.
Once Bhopal production starts, the company's ability to maneuver production/costs increases, supporting gross margin improvement, particularly for Biologics and Insulin.
Mixtard cartridge stock is believed to already be out of stock; management to verify and confirm sales figures for Q1 FY27.

subsections.label: Manufacturing investment priority
points: Over the last two years and into Q1, the company has been investing money behind facilities and manufacturing technology; this remains the priority for this year and into the start of next year, with the company largely staying away from acquisitions.

subsections.label: International business
points: Base international business remains largely uninterrupted as it has no contribution from EU markets.
CAPA actions are on track; sites are expected to be audit-ready by December.
Long-term thesis and growth strategy for the international business remains unchanged.
Export visibility for the year: flattish, or a low single-digit growth/degrowth either way; margin loss expected of around 200-300 basis points; more detail to be shared in Q2.
Global raw material/logistics issues have affected International business more than DBF, with delays in sending and receiving goods.

subsections.label: Competitive dynamics
points: A larger player vacating part of the market is viewed as a routine part of good manufacturing practice issues, not a strategic opportunity to be pursued; company was already number 1 in Units and Prescriptions before this event and intends to retain that position without relying on such events as strategy.
In-licensing is described as a continuous process, but nothing exciting to share at this point in time; acquisitions remain off the table given manufacturing investment priorities.

subsections.label: Semaglutide market adoption dynamics
points: Semaglutide market uptick has been slower than expected; management attributes this mainly to the drug's positioning being diabetes-focused (with a weight-loss effect) rather than purely obesity-driven demand that was initially anticipated.
Prescriptions are increasingly coming from KOLs; specialty mix shows Endocrinologists and Diabetologists contributing 70% of prescriptions.

For the first time, patient-level resistance is being observed at the clinic ('let me think about this'), spreading across specialties due to social media chatter; this has taken a toll on adoption pace.

Simultaneously, patients achieving successful outcomes (HbA1c of 5.2-5.3, reduced liver fat, LDL correction) are emerging on the positive side; adoption lag is attributed to the treatment escalation taking 2-3 months to show results, with the drug currently in its 4th month of use for many patients.
Management referenced a prior conference remark that peak adoption for chronic disease products typically happens in the 3rd year.

Supply-side issues in the initial launch period were driven by high Value Per Pen leading to oversized initial billing (a rush into stocking), which was a primary rather than secondary issue; this has since balanced out.
Patient resistance affects prescribing doctors as well, who become more cautious when patients ask for more time to think, creating a temporary learning curve.

Right now, affordability/pricing is not seen as the primary issue for adoption; the larger population addressable at this price point has not yet been reached, so adoption (not price) is the current constraint.
Conventional wisdom suggests pricing action will be considered once there are 4-5 thousand prescribers at a P/D of 15/18; that milestone would signal expansion to a broader population.

subsections.label: IPM growth rate commentary
points: Management believes nothing fundamental has changed on the ground for the broader IPM growth acceleration (assumed at 11% for FY27) except the GST reduction.
Hypothesis is that GST reduction may be encouraging retail-level participants to keep slightly more inventory to service patients, particularly in the more predictable chronic segment.

Prescription growth data and OPD data show no material change over the last 6-9 months, reinforcing the view that the change is inventory-related rather than demand-related; management stated this is their take without supporting data.

subsections.label: M&A stance
points: No adjacent therapeutic area acquisitions planned post Biocon Insulin business integration; capital continues to be directed toward facilities and manufacturing technology, the stated priority for this year and start of next year.
Company is largely staying away from acquisitions as a strategy for now.

subsections.label: Long-term structural shift
points: Management believes the organization has turned a corner after several years of building out new-age Biologics, Insulins, and Oncology backend capabilities.

If this structural shift plays out, it could enable the company to move to a top-tier growth trajectory, combining a fast-growing significant portfolio with a routine portfolio growing near double digits.
Management stated this transition has not yet been fully achieved but believes the company should reach it, describing this as their belief/expectation to play out over time.

subsections.label: Flagged headwinds
points: Swiss Parenterals facility remediation work is ongoing, creating softer growth and a potential EBITDA hit of a couple hundred basis points.

Global raw material/solvent price and supply chain issues have created a 'blip' in cost, more pronounced in International business (delays in sending/receiving goods) than in DBF, where therapy mix concentration lowers dependence.
Gross margin contraction (300 bps) due to product mix shift toward Biologics/Insulin is expected to persist for at least one more quarter before improving.
Semaglutide adoption facing patient-level resistance driven by social media chatter, creating a temporary adoption lag across specialties.
OAD segment growth distorted by a banned product (Glimisave-MV) impacting YoY comparison; anomaly expected to clear next month.
Cardiac segment trailing the market primarily due to underperformance in Hypertension.

subsections.label: Growth and margin trajectory outlook
points: DBF FY27 revenue growth targeted at 14%, versus assumed market/IPM growth of 11%, implying a roughly 300 basis point premium over the market.
Gross margins expected to remain in a similar range for at least one more quarter (Q2), start improving by Q3, and have a fair chance of returning to prior levels by Q4.

Domestic EBITDA margin currently at 35% (down from a potential uptick target of 37%) is a function of gross margin contraction of 300 basis points, not OAD underperformance; recovery expected in second half of the year as new facility yields improve.
Export growth outlook for FY27 is flattish (low single-digit either direction), with expected margin loss of 200-300 basis points; more detail to be shared in Q2.
OAD growth expected to recover to 5-6% in coming quarters once the banned-product base anomaly clears.
Cardiac segment growth expected to catch up to close to market growth within the next 2 quarters.
OCF/EBITDA trend of 77% expected to hold for the full FY27 year.
CAPA sites expected to be audit-ready by December (calendar year end).

guidance_ledger.statement: We expect in the next two quarters, Cardiac will be close to the market growth.

guidance_ledger.metric: Insulin Analogs (recombinant Semaglutide, Degludec, Degludec combo) filing
guidance_ledger.statement: This will now go through the process very likely to file it for the next phase in this current quarter and then it will go through the regulatory process.
Aspart should be there in this year, probably in the calendar year itself, much earlier than that.
The rest would all be pushed off to the next year.

Consider Q2 also be the same vicinity of the gross margins. By Q3, we will see that the gross margins starts improving. Q4, there is a fair chance of us coming back to where we started with more or less.

The growth could be in the same vicinity as we are today, and it could be even lower, but it will be in that zone from a neutral to a low single-digit growth, with the margins might compress a couple of 100 points. By end of Q2, we'll be able to give a clear-cut answer.

guidance_ledger.horizon: this year and start of next year
guidance_ledger.statement: Not as of now. Largely, we are staying away from acquisition. That's the plan as of now.
We see movement. We see upward movement while we talk... from a Q1 average, Q2 is looking better.

This, from our point of view, is not a good time to reduce the price further... once the market kind of escalates, it spreads out, at that point of time, there might be a good reason to correct further out.
In DBF we are looking at a 300 basis point up ahead of the market...If it is 11%, we should be at 14%.

Export by visibility today is that we will either be flattish, or there will be a growth of low single-digit either side, degrowth or growth. You consider it flattish, and we will lose certain percentage points in the margin, around 200-300 as of now.
We do have plans, but that is for the second half of this year.
I think this anomaly will get over in the next month itself. Once that anomaly gets over, we will get to 5%-6%.
As of now, the visibility is of launching in the first fortnight of August.
We are planning something for the third quarter, which to our mind would be a big product. Every time a big opportunity comes, we'll call it out.
This would be the trend to expect for the financial year.
I think that we should be up there in Q3. That's where we are pinning it up now. But there have been so many hits and misses that I'm a little skeptical of calling out a date.

The gross margin coming back is more of a function of letting in the production in our newer facility...That's why we feel that the second half of this year should see us home as of the visibility which we have today.

guidance_ledger.metric: 3-5 year organic revenue doubling / top-tier growth
guidance_ledger.statement: Structurally, there is a shift in the portfolio... This change should enable us to get to that top-tier of growth. This is what my expectation is, but look, it has to play out.
We will be commercializing it next month. Our licenses are in place. So, the commercialization will happen in August.
We feel that by the end of Q3, we should be more or less home.

guidance_ledger.metric: Derma, Women's Health, CNS market-beating growth
guidance_ledger.statement: Women's Health we are already market beating, Derma we are right up there. And CNS, yes, for sure.
37% going to 35% is... the function of gross margins being contracted by 300 basis points... second half of this year should see us home.
We guide to a growth of 1.3x of covered market growth for the current financial year.

guidance_ledger.metric: DBF H1 vs H2 margin split
guidance_ledger.statement: We expect the H2 margin to be higher than H1.
On the existing business, we are guiding a revenue growth of 18-20% this year with EBITDA margin at similar levels as FY26.
EBITDA margin at similar levels as FY26 (32%).
The EU CDMO products will get commercialized post the re-inspection and re-approval of the facilities; not counting any revenue from CDMO in FY27, anything that comes is upside.

guidance_ledger.metric: Combined CDMO + base business revenue potential
guidance_ledger.statement: Between the CDMO and the base business, we can look at a revenue of INR 550-600 crores in FY27.
37% DBF and 36% consolidated are right for the same FY27; even if there is no equity attached to that, still we maintain 36-37% margin.
We expect the return on capital employed to go from 15% to somewhere in the 23-25% range.
We expect this to be 21% zone for FY27.
Ex-Insulin double digit growth is something which could be easily achieved.
At a consol level, we should expect around mid-teens plus kind of top line growth because export we are expecting a high teens growth.
It has always been double digit; I don't think anything changing there.
A good target number for debtor days is more like 60 days, and that is what we are aiming for; within two quarters, we should be there.
We expect tailwinds for Sundae Pens starting Q2 of this year because we would have insourced the manufacturing of Sundae Pens with a phase 1 installed capacity of 5 million units per annum.
We expect the Obesity SKU to be launched in July.
INR 800 to 1000 crores EU CDMO opportunity; no impact on that book of business.
We expect 1 to 1.5 million patient by the end of the year, stable patient.

guidance_ledger.metric: Vials share of Injectable market (steady state)
guidance_ledger.statement: We expect this number (Vials as % of Injectable market) to settle down at 25-30% on a steady state basis.
Bhopal facility Cartridge line expected to come online by the second half; Vial SKUs already started, Pen fill should start sooner.

risk_register.note: Growth softer in Q1; EBITDA could see a hit of a couple hundred basis points; clarity expected by end of Q2.

risk_register.risk: Cardiac segment underperformance driven by Hypertension trailing
risk_register.note: Large part of Cardiology portfolio trailing; efforts underway, improvement expected in two quarters.

risk_register.risk: OAD growth distortion from banned product (Glimisave-MV)
risk_register.note: Continues to reflect in last year's base; anomaly expected to clear next month, after which growth should improve to 5-6%.

risk_register.risk: Gross margin contraction from product mix shift toward Biologics/Insulin
risk_register.note: 300 bps contraction expected to persist for at least one more quarter before improving from Q3.

risk_register.risk: Global raw material/solvent price and logistics disruption
risk_register.note: Blip in cost, more pronounced impact on International business (delays sending/receiving goods) than DBF due to concentrated therapy mix.

risk_register.risk: EU CDMO/EU market non-contribution to International base business
risk_register.note: Base business has no contribution from EU markets; CAPA actions on track, sites expected audit-ready by December.

risk_register.risk: Semaglutide patient-level adoption resistance
risk_register.note: Social media chatter driving patient hesitancy at clinic level across specialties for the first time, tempering adoption pace despite positive clinical outcomes emerging.

risk_register.risk: Semaglutide supply chain gush/imbalance at launch
risk_register.note: High Value Per Pen caused oversized initial billing (rush into stocking); primary supply issue has since balanced out as secondary demand caught up.

risk_register.risk: EU GMP inspection noncompliance observations (Swiss Parenterals injectable units)
risk_register.note: Procedural observations around operator behavior/movement flow in sterile areas and classified-area requirements; remediation underway with training, CAPA plan being prepared; no CapEx or line shutdowns required; timing of re-inspection depends on agency scheduling.

risk_register.risk: EU CDMO revenue postponement
risk_register.note: INR 120-140 crores of FY27 revenue postponed (not lost) pending re-approval; product is in short supply in target markets; no impact to overall INR 800-1000 crore long-term CDMO book of business.

risk_register.risk: International supply chain disruption
risk_register.note: Caused ~INR 30 crore Q4 shipment shortfall; magnitude was worse in Q4 than currently; April better than March; company hopes to recoup some losses in Q1.

risk_register.risk: Regulatory delays on new product launches
risk_register.note: gSaxenda abandoned; Aspart and Esaxerenone deferred to FY27 due to regulatory delays.

risk_register.risk: Bhopal in-sourcing delay
risk_register.note: In-sourcing/manufacturing delayed by nearly a year, causing ~INR 50 crore insulin sale loss for second year running due to continued dependence on third-party supply not matching demand.

risk_register.risk: Critical care business underperformance
risk_register.note: Critical care business did not take off as expected during FY26.

risk_register.risk: Receivables/debtor days increase
risk_register.note: Receivables rose from INR 450 crores to INR 680 crores, driven mainly by international debtor days and inventory build-up; international debtors already down 25% from March 31 level as of call date; no bad debt risk seen.

risk_register.risk: OAD segment growth drag
risk_register.note: OAD growth only 2-4% in FY26 due to Glimisave MV ban; some rebound seen in April-May; base correction expected; ex-Insulin double-digit growth still seen as achievable.

risk_register.risk: GLP-1/SEMA cannibalization of OAD/DPP-4
risk_register.note: Management does not expect near-term OAD slowdown given small relative size of GLP-1 patient base vs overall diabetes denominator; some slowdown possible only if GLP-1 penetration reaches 20-30% of diabetes population over time.

risk_register.risk: SEMA pricing pressure / competitive intensity
risk_register.note: Eris priced ~30% lower than competitors for sustainability; management expects price correction (not increase) over the next year before market stabilizes; competition expected to remain concentrated among top 5-6 players.

themes.label: International supply chain disruption

themes.label: EU GMP regulatory/compliance risk
themes.note: CAPA actions on track; sites expected to be audit-ready by December; base international business has no EU market contribution currently.

themes.label: Product mix shift margin pressure
themes.note: Gross margin contracted ~300bps due to rising share of Biologics/Insulin; expected to persist through Q2 before improving from Q3 as Bhopal ramps up.

key_takeaways: DBF (Domestic Formulations Business) clocked a revenue growth of 14% in the quarter, with 7 out of 10 therapies delivering double-digit growth rates.
Key franchises, including Insulin and Semaglutide brand SUNDAE, have all posted strong performances in Q1.
Consolidated Revenue has grown by 13% YoY in Q1. Profit After Tax has grown by 14-15%.

DBF segment delivered a 14% Revenue growth in Q1. EBITDA grew 7% YoY. EBITDA margin came in at 35%, largely led by the gross margin movement, which in turn is a reflection of the increasing importance of biologics in our product mix.
Insulin franchise continues to be an exciting story of market share gain with significant headroom for growth from existing products RHI, Glargine and a comprehensive pipeline of Insulin Analogues.
Semaglutide brand, SUNDAE, has taken off to a strong start in Q1, with a 20% market share by sale volume and 14% by sale value in its very first quarter after launch.

On the International front, the base business remains largely uninterrupted since it has no contribution from the EU markets. CAPA actions are on track, and sites are expected to be audit-ready by December.

Consolidated Revenue grew by 13% in Q1, with a Profit After Tax growth of 14.5%. Operating Cash Flow came in at 77% of EBITDA and CapEx for Q1 stood at INR 88 crores. Effective Book Tax Rate for the quarter was 20%, down from 22.5% in Q1 of last year. EPS for the quarter came in at INR 10.3.
pressing_questions: When I look at the DBF performance, we're seeing underperformance in the OAD and Cardiac segments. Especially in Cardiac, what exactly is driving this underperformance? In both these segments, by when can we expect growth to catch up with IPM levels?

Swiss Parenterals is growing quite lower than what was anticipated. Can you give us some sort of clarity on this bottom for this growth? How are we going to ramp it up from here and if you can provide some sort of full year guidance for this?
What would be the full-year revenue guidance for FY27 considering Swiss Parenterals impact and then subsequently certain therapy impact in the DBF side?
In 2-3 years' time, is there a quantum that we can mention on the top-line growth, aspirational top-line growth or EBITDA margin? Can we see doubling revenue, anywhere 3-5 years line organically?

quarters.summary: Eris guides DBF FY27 revenue growth of 1.3x covered market growth (covered market historically double digit) with DBF EBITDA margin steady at ~37% (H2 higher than H1); International existing business guided at 18-20% revenue growth with EBITDA margin similar to FY26 (32%), excluding any EU CDMO contribution (INR 120-140 crores upside pending re-inspection/re-approval); consolidated FY27 EBITDA margin expected at ~36%; ROCE expected to rise from 15% (FY26) to 23-25% over FY26-FY28 as Bhopal and Swiss Parenterals capacity investments come online.

subsections.label: Key hits and misses FY26
points: Revenue loss of INR 55-60 crores due to abandoned/delayed launches: gSaxenda (Liraglutide weight-loss SKU) abandoned due to regulatory approval delay; Aspart and Esaxerenone deferred to FY27 due to regulatory delays.

Insulin sale loss of ~INR 50 crores in FY26, similar to FY25, due to in-sourcing/commercial manufacturing from Bhopal being delayed by nearly a year on account of regulatory delays; company remained dependent on third-party supplies not commensurate with demand for the second year running.
Critical care business did not take off as expected.

subsections.label: Receivables and inventory build-up
points: Inventory increase largely driven by international business: company piled up inventory ahead of anticipated disruption but could not ship it out in Q4.

Similar inventory build-up exercise done for domestic business because key API prices moved 70-80% higher; company created large inventory as a strategic/conscious call — almost nine months of RM and PM inventory buildup.
Debtor days increase driven mainly by international business collections; company targets debtor days of ~60 days, expected within two quarters.
As of May 20 call date, international debtors already lower by 25% from the March 31 number; collections have started this quarter.

subsections.label: Capital efficiency and capital allocation
points: CapEx primarily deployed on Biologics and Sterile Injectables.
INR 150-180 crores invested in own Drug Substance (DS) capacity (own DS setup makes Liraglutide, Romiplostim in Phase 3, Teriparatide entering Phase 3).
INR 250 crores invested in Bhopal fill-and-finish site, delayed by ~1 to 1.5 years, expected to give scale advantage, margin pickup and open new markets/products once approved.

Additional plant investment in Swiss Parenterals expected to be commissioned in April, doubling current parenteral capacities; biotech capacity to reach 80 million cartridges plus similar vial capacity.

ROCE was impacted by highest-ever amortization taken in FY25 following a 6x increase in asset base in a short span; gains from expansion beginning to show from FY26 (EPS acceleration - 10% EBITDA growth led to 34-35% EPS/PAT growth).

subsections.label: Therapy-wise DBF performance drivers
points: Biggest drag on DBF growth is OAD segment, growing only 2-4%, largely due to Glimisave MV ban (INR 30 crore revenue, ~4.5% internal impact) that occurred in April last year; base correction expected by May.
Management sees rebound in OAD in April-May and expects double-digit ex-Insulin growth aided by upcoming launches like Esaxerenone.
Cardiovascular (CVD) segment has caught up on QoQ basis and is now almost on par with covered market by Q4; expected to benefit from Esaxerenone launch.
Derma segment consistently outperformed covered market in all four quarters, with EBITDA margin well above DBF average of 37%.
Insulin and Derma already outperforming and expected to continue; OAD needs more time to catch up in FY27.

subsections.label: Insulin segment growth outlook
points: Growth outpaced covered market growth by nearly five-fold in FY26.
Company confident of continued ramp-up across Cartridges, Vials, and Glargine.
First engineering batch of Bio SEMA taken at Bhopal plant ~2 weeks before call; PV batch also taken; two more batches (Degludec Plain and Degludec Lira) to be taken by month end.
Entire Degludec family and Recombinant SEMA are being developed from Eris' own Drug Substance (DS) platform, not from Biocon.

Eris Biocon platform has four commercialized products and four products with cleared PCT (either in Phase 1 or Phase 3): Romiplostim in Phase 3 (50% of Phase 3 patients already enrolled), Teriparatide entering Phase 3.

subsections.label: Semaglutide (Sundae) launch and market dynamics
points: Launched in two presentations: Vial and Pen.
For first full month (April '26), IQVIA ranks Eris #1 in Injectable Semaglutide by sale volume, #2 by sale value.
Eris market share in Injectable SEMA by units: 13% (March) to 22% (April).
Eris market share by sale value: 5% (March) to 13% (April).
Eris market share in Injectable SEMA by prescription: 8% (March), 18% (April), 22% (May).
Vials launched in March; Pen 2mg launched mid-April with just one SKU; despite that, clocked 11% market share by volume and 6% by value in pen segment for April.

Market size estimate in first month: 1.5-2 lakh active users of generic Semaglutide (later management expressed skepticism about this number, citing real Healthplix cohort data of 25,000-27,000 monthly patients).
Over 75% of prescriptions driven by diabetes rather than obesity.
Vials as % of overall Injectable market stood at 21% in April by volume; expected to settle at 25-30% on steady-state basis.
Phased launch post loss of exclusivity: Sundae Vials (March), Sundae Pen 2mg (mid-April), Sundae Pen 4mg (early May), Obesity SKU expected July.
Products priced lower than competition, viewed as more sustainable long-term price points; management expects price correction (not increase) over next year before stabilizing.

First month performance validates thesis of taking leading SEMA position based on strength of Insulins franchise: Patient Care platform, credibility with Diabetes-Endo KOLs, and cold chain handling experience.
Tailwinds expected for Sundae Pens starting Q2 once manufacturing insourced with phase 1 installed capacity of 5 million units per annum, easing supply issues and improving margins.
April industry reflection for SEMA: ~INR 4 crores, expected to build month-on-month through the year; ~20% growth expected between April and May.
Competitive intensity assessed as less fragmented than expected; top 5-6 players expected to hold 65-75% market share, expected to remain a five-six player game with #1 player holding 13-15% share.
Gross margin unlikely to reach 80% level typical of other products, but EBITDA-level profitability comparable to core business is seen as achievable once scaled.
First-month SEMA sales reflected ~INR 40-45 crores at market level with estimated 50,000-100,000 patients added.
Usage pattern: BMI <30 accounts for only 10% of prescriptions even in diabetes; 90% of prescriptions are for BMI >30, with fatty liver as another common comorbidity in early adopters.
Patient dose titration starts at 0.25mg (a 'warm up' dose); patients expected to return for dose escalation in following month.
May prescription market share (Pen+Vial combined) has increased further versus 22% reported in May; split roughly 60% Vials/40% Pens by prescription, expected 50-50 or 60-40 by units.

subsections.label: Bhopal facility ramp-up
points: Bhopal in-sourcing/commercial manufacturing delayed by nearly a year due to regulatory delays, causing insulin sale losses in FY26 and FY25.
Vial SKUs at Bhopal already started; Pen fill expected to start sooner, expected to aid H2 gross margins.

Bhopal will be one of its kind from a scale perspective once approved, expected to give good pickup in margins and open new markets and products, including a MAP facility considered a future capability.
Delayed by almost a year to a year and a half overall.

subsections.label: Swiss Parenterals expansion
points: New plant for Swiss Parenterals expected to be commissioned in April, doubling current parenteral capacities.
Combined with biotech capacity of ~80 million cartridges and similar vial capacity, expected to support Insulin shipments outside India once regulatory approvals are in place.

subsections.label: International geography outlook
points: Geographic mix has been stable over last two years: ~30% Africa, ~30% Asia, ~25% LatAm, rest diversified.
LatAm component expected to grow faster this year due to more new product approvals.
These three geographies expected to continue as key markets.

subsections.label: International supply chain disruption
points: Q4 international revenue shortfall of ~INR 30 crores due to inability to ship finished goods, resulting from supply chain disruptions related to an external situation referenced by management.
Company piled up inventory in international business early on in anticipation of disruption but could not ship it out in Q4.
Q4 disruption magnitude was worse than current levels; company expects to recoup at least some of the lost shipments in Q1; April was better than March.
Company does not expect similar magnitude of disruption to continue impacting H1.

subsections.label: Diabetes/OAD vs GLP-1 competitive dynamics
points: GLP-1 (Semaglutide) delivers effect roughly 100x that of DPP-4, but DPP-4 remains first-line everyday diabetes treatment.
Denominator of overall diabetes patients is very large, so expected 1-1.5 million GLP-1 patients by year-end is too small to move the needle on OAD/DPP-4 sales in the near term.

Management does not expect a downturn in OADs this year due to the small relative size of the GLP-1 patient base versus the overall diabetes population; some slowdown possible if GLP-1 penetration reaches 20-30% of diabetes population over time.

70% of diabetes patients should require GLP-1 per treatment guidelines but real-world uptake is far behind that guideline given early stage of market and doctor caution/patient resistance from outside voices.

subsections.label: EU GMP inspection outcome and remediation
points: EU GMP inspection outcome received last month with a list of noncompliance observations requiring remediation; largely procedural in nature with minimal impact on existing business.

Observations relate to operator behavior/movement flow in sterile/antimicrobial areas (e.g., people standing too close, not behaving properly in sterile areas), and instances where non-classified areas must be converted into classified areas; also basic hardware needs like pass boxes for RM dispensing.
No QA, QC, or data integrity issues identified.
No major CapEx required for remediation; no line shutdowns planned since existing customers are being serviced from these plants.
Agency hiring/training for remediation already completed; CAPA (Corrective Action Preventive Action) plan to be submitted to the agency soon.
Timing of re-inspection depends on agency's own calendaring/scheduling, cannot be predicted by company.
Important customer audit conducted last week and customer was satisfied with remediation progress.
Inspected facilities are the two injectable units under Swiss Parenterals (EU-approved since 2020); Eris unit for Oral Solids and Dermatology was not inspected in March.
Inspection was part of normal two-year inspection cycle for injectable facilities (OSD facilities get 3-year approval cycle), not triggered by any specific product issue.
EU CDMO products will only get commercialized post re-inspection and re-approval of the facilities.

No revenue impact to overall long-term EU CDMO book of business (INR 800-1000 crore opportunity referenced); all key contracts remain part of the book; only one product due for commercialization in Q1 is impacted, causing the revenue postponement (not loss) as the product is in short supply in target markets and customer is working alongside Eris on remediation/reapproval.

FY27 guidance of 18-20% growth for international existing business excludes any EU CDMO contribution; any CDMO revenue in FY27 to be treated as upside; management not counting CDMO revenue in FY27 base case, more likely FY28.

subsections.label: Regulatory delays impacting launches
points: gSaxenda (Liraglutide weight-loss SKU) abandoned due to delay in regulatory approval.
Aspart and Esaxerenone launches deferred from FY26 to FY27 due to regulatory delays.
Aspart product to be sourced from outside (not part of Eris' own DS platform); delay attributed to some non-quality/non-regulatory concerns; launch expected in FY27.

Insulin in-sourcing/commercial manufacturing from Bhopal delayed by nearly a year due to regulatory delays, causing continued dependence on third-party supply not matching demand for second year running.

subsections.label: Receivables/collections risk
points: Receivables increased significantly (INR 450 to 680 crores) driven by international business debtor days lengthening amid supply chain disruption and delayed collections in Q4.
Currency/FX timing factors ('dollar moving here and there') contributed to receivables timing issues.
Management does not see risk of bad debt; international debtors already down 25% from March 31 level as of call date, with collections underway this quarter.

subsections.label: FY27 outlook commentary
points: H1 expected to be a drag on gross margins due to relatively high prices and SEMA initial low profitability; H2 expected to benefit from Bhopal manufacturing ramp-up and Sundae contribution, resulting in H2 margins higher than H1.
Consol topline growth expected in mid-teens-plus range given double-digit covered market growth for DBF and high-teens growth for exports.
Management confirms even without equity/M&A contribution, 36-37% margin will be maintained.
Insulins expected to keep ramping up on the back of last year's low base, Bhopal capacity coming online, and new Degludec/Recombinant SEMA products entering the market by next year.
CVD expected to benefit from Esaxerenone launch to help catch up further with covered market.
OAD segment will need more time to catch up with covered market in FY27.

guidance_ledger.statement: We guide to a growth of 1.3x of covered market growth for the current financial year.
We expect DBF EBITDA for the current year to come in at 37%, which is a similar level as FY26.

guidance_ledger.metric: DBF H1 vs H2 margin split
guidance_ledger.statement: We expect the H2 margin to be higher than H1.
On the existing business, we are guiding a revenue growth of 18-20% this year with EBITDA margin at similar levels as FY26.
EBITDA margin at similar levels as FY26 (32%).
The EU CDMO products will get commercialized post the re-inspection and re-approval of the facilities; not counting any revenue from CDMO in FY27, anything that comes is upside.

guidance_ledger.metric: Combined CDMO + base business revenue potential
guidance_ledger.statement: Between the CDMO and the base business, we can look at a revenue of INR 550-600 crores in FY27.
37% DBF and 36% consolidated are right for the same FY27; even if there is no equity attached to that, still we maintain 36-37% margin.
We expect the return on capital employed to go from 15% to somewhere in the 23-25% range.
We expect this to be 21% zone for FY27.
Ex-Insulin double digit growth is something which could be easily achieved.
At a consol level, we should expect around mid-teens plus kind of top line growth because export we are expecting a high teens growth.
It has always been double digit; I don't think anything changing there.
A good target number for debtor days is more like 60 days, and that is what we are aiming for; within two quarters, we should be there.
We expect tailwinds for Sundae Pens starting Q2 of this year because we would have insourced the manufacturing of Sundae Pens with a phase 1 installed capacity of 5 million units per annum.
We expect the Obesity SKU to be launched in July.
INR 800 to 1000 crores EU CDMO opportunity; no impact on that book of business.
We expect 1 to 1.5 million patient by the end of the year, stable patient.

guidance_ledger.metric: Vials share of Injectable market (steady state)
guidance_ledger.statement: We expect this number (Vials as % of Injectable market) to settle down at 25-30% on a steady state basis.
Bhopal facility Cartridge line expected to come online by the second half; Vial SKUs already started, Pen fill should start sooner.

risk_register.risk: EU GMP inspection noncompliance observations (Swiss Parenterals injectable units)
risk_register.note: Procedural observations around operator behavior/movement flow in sterile areas and classified-area requirements; remediation underway with training, CAPA plan being prepared; no CapEx or line shutdowns required; timing of re-inspection depends on agency scheduling.

risk_register.risk: EU CDMO revenue postponement
risk_register.note: INR 120-140 crores of FY27 revenue postponed (not lost) pending re-approval; product is in short supply in target markets; no impact to overall INR 800-1000 crore long-term CDMO book of business.

risk_register.risk: International supply chain disruption
risk_register.note: Caused ~INR 30 crore Q4 shipment shortfall; magnitude was worse in Q4 than currently; April better than March; company hopes to recoup some losses in Q1.

risk_register.risk: Regulatory delays on new product launches
risk_register.note: gSaxenda abandoned; Aspart and Esaxerenone deferred to FY27 due to regulatory delays.

risk_register.risk: Bhopal in-sourcing delay
risk_register.note: In-sourcing/manufacturing delayed by nearly a year, causing ~INR 50 crore insulin sale loss for second year running due to continued dependence on third-party supply not matching demand.

risk_register.risk: Critical care business underperformance
risk_register.note: Critical care business did not take off as expected during FY26.

risk_register.risk: Receivables/debtor days increase
risk_register.note: Receivables rose from INR 450 crores to INR 680 crores, driven mainly by international debtor days and inventory build-up; international debtors already down 25% from March 31 level as of call date; no bad debt risk seen.

risk_register.risk: OAD segment growth drag
risk_register.note: OAD growth only 2-4% in FY26 due to Glimisave MV ban; some rebound seen in April-May; base correction expected; ex-Insulin double-digit growth still seen as achievable.

risk_register.risk: GLP-1/SEMA cannibalization of OAD/DPP-4
risk_register.note: Management does not expect near-term OAD slowdown given small relative size of GLP-1 patient base vs overall diabetes denominator; some slowdown possible only if GLP-1 penetration reaches 20-30% of diabetes population over time.

risk_register.risk: SEMA pricing pressure / competitive intensity
risk_register.note: Eris priced ~30% lower than competitors for sustainability; management expects price correction (not increase) over the next year before market stabilizes; competition expected to remain concentrated among top 5-6 players.

themes.label: Semaglutide/GLP-1 launch ramp-up
themes.note: Sundae launched in Vial and Pen presentations, achieved #1 rank by volume and #2 by value in Injectable Semaglutide for April, with market share climbing steadily across units, value and prescriptions.

themes.label: Insulin franchise strength
themes.note: RHI cartridge share rose from 13% to 24% and overall Insulin share from 12% to 16%, with growth outpacing covered market by ~5x, underpinning the SEMA launch thesis.

themes.label: EU GMP regulatory/compliance risk
themes.note: EU GMP inspection flagged procedural noncompliance observations at Swiss Parenterals units, postponing INR 120-140 crores of CDMO revenue pending remediation and re-approval.

themes.label: Bhopal capacity delay and ramp-up
themes.note: Bhopal in-sourcing delayed by nearly a year causing insulin sale losses for two years running, but Vial SKUs have started and Pen fill/Cartridge line ramp-up expected to aid H2 margins and new product launches.

themes.label: OAD segment drag vs recovery
themes.note: OAD growth of only 2-4% in FY26 due to Glimisave MV ban was the biggest drag on DBF growth, though management sees rebound in April-May and expects ex-Insulin double-digit growth in FY27.

themes.label: Capital efficiency / ROCE improvement path
themes.note: ROCE of 15% in FY26 (impacted by high FY25 amortization from 6x asset base increase) expected to climb to 23-25% by FY28 as EPS acceleration and capacity investments in Bhopal/Swiss Parenterals/DS pay off.

themes.label: International supply chain disruption
themes.note: Q4 international shipments were hit by ~INR 30 crore shortfall from supply chain disruption, inflating receivables and inventory, though April showed improvement over March.

key_takeaways: Q4 domestic business grew by 12% and EBITDA grew by 10% with a margin of 37%. For the full year, DBF revenue growth was 11% and EBITDA growth of 12% with a 37% margin.

Key misses: revenue loss of INR 55-60 crores from abandoned/delayed launches (gSaxenda, Aspart, Esaxerenone); Insulin sale loss of ~INR 50 crores due to delayed Bhopal in-sourcing; critical care business did not take off as expected.
Insulin market share in RHI cartridges increased from 13% to 24% during the year; overall Insulin market share increased from 12% to 16%; Eris Insulin growth of 32% versus CVM growth of 6.7%.
Semaglutide brand Sundae has taken off to a robust start - Eris ranked number one in Injectable Semaglutide by sale volume and number two by sale value for April '26.
EU GMP inspection outcome received with noncompliance observations that are largely procedural in nature with minimal impact on existing business; remediation is a priority.
International business guided at 18-20% revenue growth for FY27 with EBITDA margin at similar levels as FY26, excluding any EU CDMO contribution (INR 120-140 crores upside).
Consolidated PAT from continuing operations came in at INR 498 crores for FY26, a 34% YoY growth, driven by EPS acceleration where 10% EBITDA growth led to 34% PAT growth.
Closing net debt for the year was INR 2,255 crores, at 2x EBITDA, down two turns over the last two years.
ROCE for FY26 was 15% (adjusted 20% excluding M&A amortization impact), expected to rise to 23-25% range by FY28.
pressing_questions: What is the exact quantifiable impact of the EU GMP inspection issue on the EU CDMO product segment in FY27, and what is the detailed remediation timeline and strategy?
Why did receivables increase so substantially from INR 458 crores to INR 680 crores in one year, and is there any risk of bad debt?
On capital efficiency: given capital employed running at nearly two times turnover, is the business permanently stuck in a 14-15% ROCE bracket, or will it improve?
What specific EU GMP observations were found given that EU agencies are typically open to dialogue, and does remediation require infrastructure changes or line shutdowns?

AARTIIND.about: Aarti Industries Ltd, the flagship company of the Aarti group, manufacturing organic and inorganic chemicals at its major facilities in Vapi, Jhagadia, Dahej and Kutch, in Gujarat and in Tarapur in Maharashtra. The company has a strong market position in the NCB-based specialty chemicals segment.[1]

quarters.summary: Aarti Industries reported strong Q1 FY27 revenue and EBITDA growth aided by inventory/FX gains and product-mix optimization, despite Middle East conflict disrupting the Energy business exports and elevated crude-linked raw material prices impacting Non-Energy volumes. Management reiterated FY27 capex guidance of Rs 700-800 crore, expects Zone IV commissioning through FY27 (with some chemistry blocks delayed 3-6 months), Augene JV commissioning in Q2FY27, Aarti Circularity JV in H2FY27, and continues to target the previously communicated ~Rs 1,800 crore EBITDA run-rate (inclusive of Augene contribution), while flagging near-term volatility in inventory/FX gains and volumes recovery expected in Q2 FY27.

subsections.label: Revenue and margin drivers
points: Revenue growth of 41% YoY primarily driven by higher input prices passed on to customers.

EBITDA growth of 79% YoY driven by product mix optimisation, monetisation of low-cost inventories, stable demand, improved realisations for select products, and resilient execution despite temporary disruptions.
Robust supply chain and efficient inventory management resulted in market share gains and inventory gains, contributing to overall EBITDA growth.
PAT growth of 260% YoY.

subsections.label: Working capital and debt
points: Working capital requirements expanded during the quarter, driven by higher feedstock prices and increased export volumes.
Debt levels and finance costs rose to support the increased working capital requirement.

subsections.label: Gross margin dynamics
points: Sequential decline in gross margins despite inventory markup and INR depreciation benefits; management attributed this to timing of raw material purchase vs product placement, forex movement within the quarter, freight expenses, and lower volume leading to higher operating costs offset partly by lower freight cost at overall level.
Management stated quarterly gross margin numbers should not be seen as reflective of steady-state performance given plus/minus 15% monthly price volatility.
Chemical business runs on absolute deltas, not percentage margins — this behavior expected to continue.

subsections.label: Inventory and FX gain quantification
points: FX and inventory gains difficult to estimate precisely due to significant intra-quarter volatility — April-May had elevated RM prices, prices corrected in late May/June, then rose again with renewed conflict in June-July.

CFO explained forex gain arose from rupee appreciating/correcting significantly in April, allowing squaring of import positions at lower rates; also exports initially priced at lower rates versus later; rupee ranged INR92-97 during the quarter.
Inventory benefit is blended into forex gain related to import transactions; accounting mark-to-market element also plays a role.
Management view: forex/inventory-linked gains should be considered part of operating profit, not one-off.

Estimated combined FX + inventory gain impact of INR50-60 crore in the quarter, versus a forex gain of INR47 crore per the press release; analysts estimate base-business EBITDA (ex inventory/FX) at roughly INR300-310 crore.

subsections.label: Capital allocation
points: FY27 capex remains on track within Rs 700-800 crore range, with ~Rs 180 crore deployed in Q1 FY27.
With major expansion programs nearing completion, capex intensity expected to reduce significantly starting next year.
Capital deployment going forward will pivot toward high-growth, high-return niche projects.

key_figures.label: West Asia share of revenue (current quarter)

subsections.label: Energy business (Fuel Additives)
points: Energy business volumes declined 17% QoQ, versus a 7% QoQ decline in Non-Energy and 12% overall organization-level decline.
Demand visibility remains robust in Fuel Additives (Energy) business.

West Asia's contribution to revenues declined from ~15% to 2% of revenue primarily due to ongoing regional conflict, impacting sequential volumes; other international markets continue to perform well.
Efforts to develop other potential markets have strengthened ability to diversify volumes across geographies.
Business remains in market development phase; not yet at true potential.
Portfolio has become well balanced across US, Africa, Europe, Middle East and India; Southeast Asia remains uncracked.
Continued strong demand visible into Q2, supported by strong gasoline-naphtha cracks (USD15-18, also cited USD15-20 per barrel), giving confidence in ramp-up irrespective of Middle East situation.

Competition already exists — more than 2-3 players in India and 2-3 players in China in this product; company aims to maintain market leadership via new products, differentiated products for specific markets/customers, global supply chain planning, footprint optimization, and unique distribution strategy; cost positioning aims to be top decile.

Company broadening basket of fuel additive products beyond MMA; pipeline has 3-5 products at any time, not necessarily octane boosters, but broadly falling in fuel additives category; product names not disclosed.
Voyage time (2-3 months for US-bound material) does not impact margin profile but causes delayed revenue recognition under DAP terms; does not affect underlying margin.
Winter season (Oct-Dec) typically shows some demand/crack weakness for fuel additives; company preparing mitigation strategies for lean season volume placement.
Geographic distribution of Energy business well balanced across US, Europe, Middle East, Africa, India on a yearly average basis, though quarter-on-quarter one geography may pick up share.

subsections.label: Non-Energy business
points: Demand trends remained mixed within Non-Energy segment.

Polymers demand soft in Q1 due to weak demand for downstream products in US & China; recovery expected in Q2; Q1 softness partly due to bulk shipments to US customers pulled forward into Q4 of prior year, leaving lower shipment volumes in Q1; limited Middle East exposure in this segment.

Dyes and Pigments segment continues to face demand headwinds driven by subdued demand amid high raw material pricing environment and seasonal factors; global softening of demand trend reflected in growth over last 3-4 years.
Pharma demand continues to be stable with pretty robust growth.
Agrochemical volumes marginally lower due to customer resistance to source at elevated RM prices; volume recovery expected in Q2 supported by underlying stable demand.
China's suspension of export tax rebates has created favourable opportunities for NCB value chain products.

Non-energy volume drop in Q1 was combination of supply chain factors and delayed purchasing behavior by customers holding inventory in high-price environment; segment not significantly impacted by Middle East given low exposure.
Agro demand growth relatively stable; polymer demand strong particularly in EV and automotive end markets; pharma demand growth robust; dyes and pigments demand softening globally.

subsections.label: Value chain margin dynamics
points: NCB value chain had suppressed margins for a long time but recovered in the last quarter.
DCB hydrogenation chain has always had decent margins.

NT (nitrotoluene) chain remains suppressed, linked to isomer imbalance faced over last 2-3 years; company implementing innovative strategies to rebalance portfolio and hopes for better margin profile going forward.
Fuel additives segment expected to gain on margin profile with broadening of market, customer and product footprint.
PDA chain structurally remains weak due to technological disadvantage; company working on cost efficiencies to improve margin profile.

Price hikes in Pharma and Dyes & Pigments segments were higher than in Energy/polymer additives due to two factors: raw material inflation pass-through, and NCB chain pricing regime change following China's VAT/export rebate removal; some pricing gains may sustain even as raw material prices soften.

subsections.label: NCB chain capacity
points: Assets in NCB chain capable of delivering slightly more volume; company evaluating minor debottlenecking projects.
Dominant end market for NCB chain is pharmaceuticals (paracetamol is largest end user); company watching Indian market consumption potential before committing to capacity expansion.
Company will pursue debottlenecking as soon as it sees potential to sell more in India; feels demand is some time away from warranting full asset expansion.

subsections.label: Dyes, pigments, printing revenue share
points: Dyes, pigments and printing continue to be guided at 10-11% of revenue share on an ongoing basis.

subsections.label: Augene JV steady-state revenue
points: Steady-state revenue projection for Augene JV maintained at Rs 300-400 crore.

key_figures.label: Zone IV products expected by end of FY27
Zone IV products expected by FY28

subsections.label: Fuel additives capacity
points: Key fuel additives capacity expansion completed to 360 KTPA from 290 KTPA, providing additional flexibility to serve newer markets with newer products as demand evolves.
Company ramping up capacity utilization; expects to reach high levels of utilization for the expanded capacity within this quarter (Q2 FY27) itself.
Capacity for overall fuel additives block not necessarily linked to one particular product; stabilization expected over next 12 months.
No restriction or limit on further capacity increase, but focus is to demonstrate good utilization of recent expansion before deciding on further expansion.

subsections.label: DCB debottlenecking
points: Company looking to debottleneck DCB capacity to 140 KTPA backed by volume increase supported by PDCB and downstream demand.

subsections.label: Zone IV project
points: Zone IV expansion facing 3-6 month delay due to labour constraints and war-related issues, primarily in March-April timeframe driven by LPG-related labour shortage and consequent elections & monsoon.
Project being commissioned in phased manner in FY27, with ramp-up expected over FY28 and FY29.

5 different chemistry blocks in Zone IV are source of delay; multipurpose plant (MPP) and calcium chloride unit expected to commission; MPP product expected out within August, commissioning to be announced post first product.

Strategy for Zone IV changed ~1.5 years back to make the entire chain capable of producing different chemistries rather than solely chlorotoluene chain; assets retain capability to manufacture chlorotoluene chain if needed, and can produce multiple other chemistries.

97% of equipment erected and 85% of piping complete for the delayed blocks; challenge was manpower availability for piping and insulation work; company back to full manpower and expects no further delays, targeting commissioning within this financial year.

Zone IV ramp-up delay is a pure product execution challenge, not linked to any particular Agri/end-market segment; product mix diversified across agro, pharma, coating and polymers, not heavily skewed to one end market.

For most Zone IV target products, technology demonstration and product qualification via pilot facility already achieved with target customers; commercial batch qualification will occur once assets are commissioned.

Delay may lead to slower ramp-up than original anticipation given in FY27/FY28 target aspirations; company to share ramp-up phase details once better understanding of speed of ramp-up across 5 chemistry blocks is available.
Zone IV expected to yield 5-10 products by end of FY27 and 25-30 products by FY28.

subsections.label: PEDA project
points: PEDA project progressing through market seeding activities and expected to be commercialised soon.

subsections.label: Sustainability rating
points: Company achieved EcoVadis Platinum Rating 2026 with a score of 87/100, placing Aarti Industries among the top 1% of companies globally for sustainability performance.

subsections.label: Regional exposure
points: West Asia crisis had direct impact on Energy business, temporarily halting exports to the region; region's revenue share fell from ~15% to 2% in the quarter; a significant portion of volumes successfully redirected to other markets, limiting overall business impact.
Company working on opportunities to open new fronts for supply in West Asia region, expecting to regain volumes in upcoming quarters.
Geographic distribution in Energy business well balanced across US, Europe, Middle East, Africa and India on year-average basis; quarter-on-quarter volatility can shift share to one geography.
Southeast Asia remains an uncracked region for the Energy business.

Exports for the quarter were robust at 59% of revenue; good traction expected with volumes to rise in Q2; export footprint/supply chain shifting toward longer destinations like US, with revenue recognition timing tied to Incoterms (many US sales on DAP basis) causing quarter-on-quarter volatility between production/export timing and revenue recognition.

key_figures.label: China market share of global chemicals market (context for new subsidiary)

subsections.label: Augene / Superform JV
points: JV with Superform for downstream amine derivatives leverages complementary commercial and manufacturing strengths to unlock significant market potential; reflects strategic model company intends to build upon.

Partnership through Augene Chemicals combines Aarti's deep chemistry expertise and RM backward integration with Superform's market application insights to build a differentiated specialty chemicals platform.
JV remains on track for commissioning in Q2 FY27; demand tailwinds seen in a primary end-use application providing opportunities for faster ramp-up.
Commissioning activities ongoing; first sale of raw material to JV has already happened; traction seen in order book for the product planned to be produced.
Operations and ramp-up expected to start within this quarter; decent utilization level expected within first 1-2 years.
Being a 50-50 JV, it will consolidate at PAT level; PAT-level numbers to become visible from this quarter, with meaningful difference expected 2-4 quarters down the line.
Steady-state revenue projection maintained at Rs 300-400 crore; firmer estimate to follow once ramp-up and plant stabilization complete.
Two dominant end markets for Augene chemistry: coatings (larger, mostly India-focused market) and dyes; profitability expectation is higher margin profile compared to existing product portfolio.

subsections.label: Aarti Circularity / Re Sustainability JV
points: Plastic recycling initiative with Re Sustainability through Aarti Circularity slated for commissioning in H2 FY27, utilizing advanced recycling technologies for hard-to-recycle waste streams.

subsections.label: Global subsidiary expansion
points: Business expansions through subsidiaries in UAE, UK and USA progressing well and supporting better growth trajectories in various markets.
Company has planned to set up a subsidiary in China to expand base in one of the large global chemicals markets, accounting for more than 45% of global market.
China presence will enhance sourcing capabilities for key raw materials and support cost- and time-efficient supply chain arrangement.

subsections.label: Backward integration / long-term contracts
points: Execution across all long-term contracts remains stable, continuing to underpin baseline volume growth and safeguard revenue visibility.

SABIC-linked backward integration project (long-term contract announced last quarter, prior guidance of INR200-250 crore capex over a 15-year residual contract) is in project execution phase; civil and building work currently ongoing; commissioning expected around September-October 2027.

Ethylated intermediate products (OEA, MEA, etc.) and related long-term contracts (e.g., $150 million agrochemical innovator contract) are strategic focus areas; in most cases contracts pass through ethylene pricing, securing margin profile; near-term quarterly/monthly volatility possible depending on pass-through timing, but long-term volume and margin visibility is more robust.

Ethylated intermediate products (OEA, MEA) are produced only in India, China or Europe — not in Korea, Japan or Thailand — limiting direct opportunity from Northeast Asian steam cracker capacity rationalization.

subsections.label: Geopolitical and macro risk
points: Challenging macro environment with persistent geopolitical tensions in the Middle East disrupting global supply chains, increasing freight costs and driving inflation in crude-linked raw material prices.
West Asia crisis directly impacted Energy business, temporarily halting exports to the region; region's revenue share fell from ~15% to 2% in the quarter.
Short-term export headwinds may persist due to West Asia conflict, though sustained volume growth expected supported by capacity expansion and deeper market penetration.

subsections.label: Raw material price volatility
points: Elevated prices of key raw materials — Benzene, Sulphur, Methanol and Aniline among others — impacted purchasing power in specific end applications such as dyes, selected agrochemicals and polymer compounds, impacting volumes during the quarter.
Significant intra-quarter raw material price volatility: elevated in April-May, corrected in late May/June, then rose again with renewed conflict in June-July.

Risk of customer destocking / purchasing delay in a falling raw-material-price scenario always remains for crude-linked raw material/product businesses; company manages via quick pass-through for domestic RM procurement (7-15 days inventory) versus longer exposure for imported RM (1-1.5 months inventory), plus forward booking of customer orders and hedging strategies to minimize potential inventory loss.

subsections.label: Currency volatility
points: Significant currency volatility during the quarter — rupee ranged from INR92 to INR97 — creating both opportunity for FX gains and future unpredictability; management unable to commit to future FX gain/loss numbers.

subsections.label: Seasonal demand risk
points: Fuel additives basket/segment typically sees some weakness in winter season (Oct-Dec) as cracks step down and demand gets impacted; company preparing mitigation strategies for volume placement during the lean season.

subsections.label: Execution risk
points: Zone IV delay attributed to labour shortage driven by LPG issue and consequent elections & monsoon disruptions, a pure product execution challenge unrelated to end-market/demand.

subsections.label: Structural/technological risk
points: PDA chain structurally remains weak due to technological disadvantage relative to competitors.

subsections.label: Zone IV / FY28 guidance confidence
points: In response to analyst question on whether FY28 guidance remains achievable given ~6-month Zone IV delay, management stated Augene and RESL JVs, plus the MPP and calcium chloride unit in Zone IV, are expected to commission and ramp up on track; the other 5 chemistry blocks in Zone IV are where delay is seen, which might lead to slower ramp-up versus original target aspirations for FY27/FY28.
Management will remain watchful and transparent, sharing ramp-up phase details of the 5 chemistry blocks once commissioned and better understood.

subsections.label: EBITDA trajectory / run-rate outlook
points: Management declined to precisely commit to next-quarter EBITDA run-rate given plus/minus 15-20% monthly raw material price volatility; some inventory-linked gains may not repeat but could be compensated by volume growth.

Rs 1,800 crore EBITDA guidance included expected contribution from Augene JV (expected to start contributing within the guided timeframe); the Circularity/Re Sustainability JV was not anticipated to contribute meaningfully before FY27/28 timeframe.

As volume recovery happens and if pricing regime stabilizes through a quarter without significant change, underlying true potential of existing assets and EBITDA trajectory should become more visible.
Volume growth is viewed with confidence, while inventory/margin gains remain dependent on how the West Asia situation settles and the pace of raw material pricing changes (gradual vs sharp).

subsections.label: Non-energy and export volume recovery
points: Non-energy volumes expected to pick up during Q2, given end consumption demand remains stable.
Polymer segment expected to see growth on a full-year basis despite a low Q1.
Agrochemical volume recovery expected in Q2 supported by underlying stable demand.

subsections.label: Energy business outlook
points: Continued strong gasoline-naphtha crack spreads (averaging $15-18 to $15-20 per barrel) support robust demand for fuel additives; company expects to ramp up capacity utilization, potentially reaching high utilization levels within Q2 FY27.
Fuel additives portfolio to broaden from single-product dependency to multi-product portfolio over next 12 months, with 3-5 products in pipeline at any time.

subsections.label: Capex guidance
points: FY27 capex guidance maintained at INR700-800 crore, with intensity expected to reduce significantly starting FY28 as major expansion programs near completion.

key_takeaways: The quarter was characterised by a challenging macro environment, with persistent geopolitical tensions in the Middle East disrupting global supply chains, increasing freight costs and driving inflation in crude-linked raw material prices.
The West Asia crisis had a direct impact on our Energy business, temporarily halting exports to the region. The region's share in our revenues declined from about 15% to 2% in this quarter.
Revenue of Rs. 2,627 crore, representing a growth of 41% Y-o-Y, which was primarily driven by higher input prices passed on to the customers.
EBITDA of Rs. 385 crore, growing 79% Y-o-Y, driven by a combination of product mix optimisation, monetisation of low-cost inventories.
Profit After Tax of Rs. 155 crore, registering a growth of 260% YoY.
We have completed our key fuel additives capacity expansion to 360 KTPA, from 290 KTPA, providing additional flexibility to serve newer markets with newer products as demand evolves.

Barring the 3-6 months delay due to labour constraints and war related issues, our Zone 4 project expansion continues to progress. The project is being commissioned in a phased manner this year, FY27, with ramp-up expected over FY28 and FY29.
In line with our earlier guidance, FY27 CAPEX remains on track within the Rs. 700 to 800 crore range, with about Rs 180 crores already deployed in Q1FY27.

We were pleased to achieve the EcoVadis Platinum Rating 2026 during the quarter with a score of 87 out of 100, placing Aarti Industries among the top 1% of companies globally for sustainability performance.
pressing_questions: Just one question in terms of the Zone IV capex; given that it has got delayed, however, our FY28 guidance remains intact. So how confident are we to reach the lower end of guidance given that there is at least 6 months of delay in this project, and we were probably considering a decent amount of scale up happening in FY28, which will give additional EBITDA?
Sir, during the quarter, like a INR380 crore EBITDA and stripping off the INR47 crore forex benefit and some inventory gains... How do you see reaching INR1,800 crore EBITDA by FY28?
Just to clarify that the JVs, Augene & Re Aarti will not be part of the EBITDA number, right? So your guidance of INR1,800 crore is excluding these JVs. Is that correct?

quarters.summary: Q4 FY26 revenue grew 9% YoY to INR2,422 crore with EBITDA up 29% YoY and PAT up 43% YoY; FY26 revenue grew 12% to INR9,018 crore, EBITDA grew 15% to INR1,172 crore and PAT grew 27% to INR419 crore. FY26 begins FY27 with cautious optimism amid Middle East geopolitical disruptions, elevated raw material and freight costs, and a 3-4 month delay in Zone IV commissioning due to labour shortages, but management expects net debt to decline in FY27 on lower capex intensity (guided at INR700-800 crore) and improving EBITDA/cash flow, targeting net debt/EBITDA of 2.5x over the next 2 years from current 3.6x.
