subsections.label: Cost drivers
points: Freight cost significantly increased in Q4 driven by higher export shipments and increased fuel rates, accounting for bulk of the rise in other expenses.

Freight increase driven by three adverse factors simultaneously: unit freight rate (up due to West Asia war), volume (57% of revenue was exports), and destination mix (more material pushed to U.S. which has longer transit and higher freight versus Middle East).
Interest costs include INR39 crore revaluation loss on long-term foreign currency loan.
Working capital expanded during the quarter driven primarily by significant elevation in raw material prices, causing an uptick in net debt and interest expenses.

Rupee depreciated ~INR5 against USD between 31 Dec and 31 Mar, causing revaluation loss on unhedged $87 million FX loan; company has larger export portfolio acting as natural hedge but accounting requires loss recognition at balance sheet date while gains are recognized only when realized.

Increase in inventory (INR409 crore stock adjustment) reflects material exported and in transit to customers, not yet delivered, hence revenue for that portion is not recognized; also some raw material price impact from late in the month.

subsections.label: Capital allocation
points: FY26 capex was as guided at INR1,125 crore, representing a decline versus the past 2-3 years, in line with plans to optimize capital allocation.
FY27 capex guided at INR700-800 crore (later clarified as INR750-800 crore), continuing the journey to optimize capex and maximize returns, with investment focus on niche, high-return projects.

Of FY27 capex, a significant part will go toward completion of Zone IV and part toward the new backward-integration long-term contract (INR200-250 crore total, part spent this year); remainder ~INR150 crore/year is asset maintenance capex.
Bulk of CWIP of INR2,000 crore in FY26 pertains to Zone IV, which had cumulative capex of around INR1,800-odd crore.

subsections.label: Debt and net debt trajectory
points: INR4,900 crore gross debt figure was optically high due to a term loan disbursed in the last days of March combined with holidays, leaving cash temporarily unutilized; on a net debt basis the company is at around INR4,300 crore.
Bulk of the one-off cash (~INR600 crore) was already used to liquidate debt in the first week of April.
Management expects net debt to decline in FY27 given lower capex intensity and improving EBITDA/cash flow, targeting net debt/EBITDA of 2.5x over the next 2 years from the current 3.6x.

A crude price escalation scenario (e.g., to $140-150/barrel) could increase working capital requirement further and strain the balance sheet, though this is not the base case; base case anticipates pricing stabilizing or correcting, aiding working capital reduction.

subsections.label: Tax rate
points: Tax rate volatility this year was due to favorable resolution of earlier tax litigations leading to prior period and deferred tax adjustments.
Going forward, tax rate expected in the range of 9-15%, given Zone IV commercialization brings significant IT depreciation deduction.

subsections.label: Energy applications
points: Energy applications continue to hold a market-leading global position with strong presence.

Q4 volumes down 4% QoQ, primarily driven by lower exports to the Middle East due to geopolitical disruptions; impact was cushioned by successfully rerouting part of these volumes to other geographies.
Capacity utilization remained high despite disruptions, preserving wallet share with global customers.
Full impact of Middle East disruptions expected to be felt in the ongoing (current) quarter.
Ongoing volatility in refining product margins creates uncertainty on gasoline-naphtha cracks; supply chain risk on key raw materials adds near-term risk to this business.
Management balances volume growth with spread management to optimize profitability.

subsections.label: Non-energy applications - Agrochemicals
points: Agrochemicals as a basket demonstrated steady volume growth, though margin pressure continues to prevail.
The new contract win supports growth of select products/intermediates, in line with plans to ramp up already-created capacities.
Biggest driver to recover margins would be how Chinese industry behavior evolves; Chinese conduct has been a major driver of margin compression in this segment over recent years.

On agro side, company is currently able to hold on to spread (not fully pass on raw material cost increase), which is viewed as a good outcome given agrochemical customers have longer gestation periods for absorbing price rises.

Full pass-through of price rises expected over next 3-6 months provided raw material stability, given multiple inventory layers across intermediate, technical, formulation and end-consumer levels in the agrochemical chain that need to adjust first.

subsections.label: Non-energy applications - Dyes, pigments, paints
points: Relatively stable for the quarter.
Near-term impact expected on exports due to West Asia war, expected to be compensated by increase in domestic market volumes.
3:3DCBH, a core product in this segment, faces demand pressure from global markets, partially compensated by increasing local demand as global consolidation in the pigment industry occurred.
Share of dyes/pigments/printing mix in overall business remains ~10-11% and expected to remain broadly around that.
Potential demand destruction risk in low-margin segments unable to afford high raw material pricing pass-through, over a 3-6 month time frame.

subsections.label: Non-energy applications - Polymers
points: Polymers continued to perform well, in a strong growth phase driven especially by demand from EV market applications.
MPDA specifically continues to underperform due to heavy competition from China; rest of the polymer portfolio performing extremely well.
DCB chain continues to remain robust, driven by tighter capacity utilization as well as demand growth from EV market.

subsections.label: Non-energy applications - Pharma
points: Pharma application continued to remain stable during the quarter.
China's anti-involution stance and its impact on PNCB/NCB chain products should start showing benefits from Q1 FY27 onwards.
Overall non-energy/base business performed better, driven by volume growth and cost efficiencies.

subsections.label: Historical long-term contracts (4 contracts, excluding the 2 new ones)
points: One contract for advanced polymer intermediate continues to operate as per contractual terms, with secure and predictable earnings.
MMA-linked contract had target volume aspirations; on a full calendar year basis, targeted volumes were achieved, though monthly/quarterly volumes may not always be met.
Nitric acid raw material purchase contract continues to operate per contractual terms with no deviation.
Agrochemical intermediate contract has volume conditions being met, but margin has been under pressure compared to original anticipation at contract closure.
One of the 5 historical contracts was cancelled (referenced by analyst, confirmed by management).

subsections.label: Bayer contract / Dicamba intermediate
points: ~50% of that asset is used to manufacture one particular intermediate that goes into Dicamba; steady volumes currently seen, which will lead to better utilization of the asset in the coming financial year, aided by positive developments related to the final technical molecule in the U.S. and lower duties.

subsections.label: Zone IV project delay
points: Zone IV projects (multipurpose plant, calcium chloride plant, and 5 chemistry blocks) delayed by 3-4 months due to labour constraints, driven by LPG-related commercial issues and migration of labour due to elections.
35% reduction in contract labour availability in the project execution region during the quarter; project is at last-mile connectivity stage (pipeline work) which is highly labour intensive.
Company taking multiple steps to support and sustain contract labour to minimize delay.

subsections.label: Energy application capacity expansion
points: Expansion to 360 KTPA is on track and expected to be commissioned soon in line with market requirements.

subsections.label: Zone IV commissioning status
points: Zone IV comprises multipurpose plant (MPP), calcium chloride plant, and 5 chemistry blocks (also including PEDA capacity, considered an extension of MPP).
Calcium chloride plant has already had commercial runs and is under operation; expected to ramp up to full capacity over next 3-4 weeks.
Multipurpose plant and associated PEDA extension are under commissioning trials; expected to be declared commissioned and commercialized within the current quarter.
Remaining 5 chemistry blocks will commission throughout the current financial year (FY27), staggered.
Initial revenue from these assets expected to start as early as Q2 FY27, with staggered ramp-up to full capacity utilization over time due to qualification cycles.

3-4 month delay compared to original expectation, mainly due to contract labour issues; company anticipates all commissioning within FY27 despite the delay and is figuring out strategies to mitigate the EBITDA realization impact.

subsections.label: Utilization strategy
points: Improving utilization levels of existing assets has been a deliberate strategy, sometimes pushing volumes at the expense of slight margin compromise.
Some value chains like PDA are being structurally addressed for a long-term solution.
Upside potential seen in select chains like DCB (via capacity debottlenecking) and ethylation chain (via new contract plus downstream PEDA integration).

subsections.label: JV / partnership commissioning
points: Augene (Superform JV) is on track for commissioning in H1 FY27 (expected June/July timeframe), with initial focus on agrochemicals and coating end markets; expected to ramp up to full utilization within the current financial year.

Circularity/recycling JV initiative commissioning on track for CY26; unlikely to contribute meaningfully to numbers initially given it is a first-of-its-kind plant requiring time to establish the technology, but proof of technology expected to be established within the current financial year.

subsections.label: Geographic redirection amid Middle East disruption
points: Disruptions in shipments to the Middle East occurred, but company proactively redirected volumes to other geographies to ensure continuity and minimize impact on overall volumes.
Middle East region has been running dry of product for about 6-8 weeks; physically impossible to ship material there currently.
Shipments to U.S. remain relatively consistent; shipments to Europe are starting and expected to expand.
Domestic market volumes remain relatively consistent.

If Middle East situation stabilizes, there is a possibility of a sharp increase in demand in that region given the extended supply drought; conversely if situation persists beyond ~2 months, volumes to Middle East for certain molecules would see impact.

Working capital/receivable exposure varies by destination: longer voyage times (e.g., U.S. at 2-3 months) create larger working capital requirement versus shorter voyage regions (Middle East at 7-10 days).

subsections.label: Raw material availability and sourcing
points: Physical availability of methanol and sulfur is well covered currently, though at increasingly higher cost to ensure 100% plant feed.
Methanol coverage typically a couple of months; sulfur (domestic supply) coverage a few weeks via contract; coverage duration varies by commodity.
Company actively working with suppliers and customers to explore alternate sourcing and placement avenues to ensure continuity of operations amid West Asia disruptions.

subsections.label: Freight and logistics
points: Elevated freight rates increasing cost of global trade, driven by West Asia war-related issues, higher export volumes (57% of revenue), and destination mix shift toward U.S. (longer transit, higher freight) versus Middle East.

subsections.label: Utilization and pricing dynamics
points: High utilization levels (upside of 80-85%, annualized Q4 volumes near 100%) reflect deliberate strategy to push volumes, sometimes at expense of margin.
Utilization is measured at bulk product level (NCB, DCB, ethylation); downstream product-level story differs significantly across the portfolio.
NCB level pricing/margin has improved as Chinese anti-involution plays out; DCB remains robust driven by tight capacity utilization and EV-linked demand growth.
Margin recovery/pricing correction is currently occurring in select pockets, not broad-based across the portfolio; could become more broad-based if China's stated actions persist.

On absolute agro pricing, there has been a positive trajectory since January, but spread/margin (not absolute pricing) is the more relevant metric given raw materials have also risen (in some cases more than doubled).

subsections.label: China regulatory/safety scrutiny
points: Increased regulatory scrutiny on nitration chemistry-related assets in China following fire incidents, pushing industry toward continuous operation and additional safety measures.

This could lead to smaller, volume-inefficient players exiting the market over time, potentially resulting in industry consolidation and better conduct/margins going forward, though this will play out gradually, not as a knee-jerk shift.
AIL's product portfolio is significantly different from products involved in the China incidents; no direct linkage to AIL.
AIL has largely moved to continuous nitration (inherently safer than batch nitration) and enhanced safety practices over the last couple of decades, reflected in safety/sustainability recognitions.

subsections.label: Mid-to-long term confidence drivers
points: Confidence stems from ability to deliver volume growth over the last 18 months by operating with agility, gaining market share and pushing up asset utilization, reaffirming cost competitiveness for share of wallet.
As cycle turns, margin recovery on a higher volume base provides an outsized incremental benefit compared to the old baseline.

subsections.label: Two long-term contracts concluded
points: Backward integration initiative with a leading global chemical company, transitioning the relationship into a more integrated end-to-end manufacturing model with capex of about INR200-250 crore, to cater to requirements over the residual 15-year contract period; this is an additional fixed margin contract for the remaining 15-year period.

$150 million multiyear supply agreement with a global agrochemical innovator for a critical agrochemical intermediate used in crop protection formulations, extending through March 31, 2030 (4 years); this contract will be met without any incremental capex.
These developments mark a strategic shift towards deeper integration, enhanced earnings visibility and improved capital efficiency.

subsections.label: Award recognition
points: During the year, Aarti Industries was honored with the 2026 Gallup Exceptional Workplace Award by Gallup, becoming one of the first manufacturing companies in India to receive this recognition, reinforcing its position as a global manufacturing organization combining operational scale with high performance and people-centric culture.

subsections.label: Partnership / JV momentum
points: Management does not see momentum in partnership/JV conversations falling despite West Asia crisis; in fact sees momentum increasing as counterparties look for more robust and secure supply chains.
Expect many such conversations to proceed and conclude in the coming financial year.

Value proposition: ability to deliver extremely reliable and safe operations in complicated chemistries in a competitive manner; repeat long-term contract from a global major (the backward integration deal) validates this value proposition.
Nature of contracts varies: some are fixed margin, some are pure buy-and-sell linked to index prices; each partnership improves portfolio quality and earnings visibility.
Intention is for such incremental partnerships/JVs to contribute more meaningfully to business and earnings quality over the next couple of years.

subsections.label: Augene JV structure
points: Augene is a 50-50 JV and will not consolidate into AIL financials; numbers will likely be reported separately.
Philosophy is that JV should operate at a slightly better margin profile compared to where AIL currently operates.
Company will start presenting EBITDA from the JV as and when the number becomes relevant.

subsections.label: Middle East geopolitical disruption
points: Escalation of geopolitical tensions in the Middle East disrupted global supply chains, trade flows, logistics timelines and input cost structures.
Key raw material prices (benzene, sulfur, aniline, toluene, methanol) rose over 60%.
Elevated freight rates increased cost of global trade.
Curtailment of volumes from Middle East created significant supply chain issues, presenting near-term headwinds for the chemicals industry.
Middle East market has been effectively closed for shipments for 6-8 weeks; situation is considered a serious, present-day challenge, not merely a future risk.
Management describes the situation as challenging today given the speed and scale of the raw material price spike and the sudden loss of a market representing ~10% of revenue.

subsections.label: MMA / refining margin volatility
points: Ongoing volatility in refining product margins creates uncertainty on gasoline-naphtha cracks; cracks have swung from negative to +$20/barrel over the last 6 weeks given Middle East volatility.

Multiple offsetting factors affect MMA economics: naphtha-gasoline spread, absolute pricing levels, and rising raw material costs (aniline, methanol) that must be passed through; no conclusive trend expected until Middle East situation stabilizes.
Potential headwinds flagged by an analyst: rising ethanol blending (as octane booster) and gas shortages could work against MMA demand, partially offset by higher crude prices.

subsections.label: Agrochemical margin pressure
points: Persistent margin pressure in agrochemicals over the past 2 years, largely driven by Chinese industry conduct/oversupply; recovery contingent on how Chinese industry behavior evolves.

subsections.label: Zone IV execution delay
points: 3-4 month delay in Zone IV commissioning due to 35% reduction in contract labour availability, driven by LPG-related commercial issues and election-related labour migration; project currently at labour-intensive last-mile pipeline work stage.

subsections.label: Demand destruction risk
points: High raw material pricing pass-through could cause demand destruction in low-margin segments of dyes/pigments/paints business over a 3-6 month time frame.

subsections.label: Macro / discretionary demand risk
points: If West Asia war leads to a reversal of global interest rate cycle and a global inflationary scenario linked to a downward trend in global GDP, it could impact discretionary spend in both global and Indian markets; this is a potential risk being monitored, not yet materialized.

subsections.label: MPDA competition
points: MPDA (within polymer application) continues to underperform due to heavy competition from China.

subsections.label: China nitration chemistry regulatory tightening
points: Regulatory scrutiny in China following fire incidents could raise governance standards across nitration chemistries broadly, though AIL's portfolio is not directly linked to the specific incidents.

subsections.label: Working capital / balance sheet strain risk
points: A scenario where crude rises to $140-150/barrel could further increase working capital requirement and strain the balance sheet; likelihood of this scenario is unknown.

key_figures.label: EBITDA potential from capex-led initiatives (referenced by analyst, not disputed)
key_figures.value: 1,800 total run-rate incl. 150-200 from cost initiatives; 300-450 from delayed capex-led growth

subsections.label: FY27 outlook
points: FY26-27 begins with cautious optimism supported by improved capacity utilization, strong order visibility through long-term contracts, and continued progress on key growth and integration initiatives.

West Asia situation continues to pose near-term risk to availability of certain critical feedstock and placement of key products in the Middle East; company is actively working with suppliers and customers to explore alternate sourcing and placement avenues.

Company has delivered strong growth in quarterly EBITDA run rate and is on track to implement profitability improvement initiatives, including higher operating leverage, cost optimization, and incremental contributions from recently commissioned and upcoming assets.
With strategic investments, improving capacity utilization, and long-term partnerships, company positions itself to navigate near-term volatility while building a foundation for sustainable growth.

Cost and operating efficiency/operating leverage initiatives are on track with no delay; most cost initiatives will start accruing fully in the current year. Capex-led growth is behind schedule by 3-4 months, impacting the timing (not the quantum) of targeted EBITDA realization over the next 2 years; management is exploring mitigation strategies.

Net debt expected to decline in FY27 despite working capital pressure, supported by lower capex intensity and improving EBITDA/cash flow; internal target is net debt/EBITDA of 2.5x over the next 2 years from current 3.6x.

Targeted working capital days of 55-60 days is the ideal objective, though actual levels vary with market conditions/regional mix; Zone IV commercialization is not expected to materially change this trajectory.

themes.label: Middle East geopolitical disruption
themes.note: West Asia war disrupted supply chains, spiked raw material prices over 60%, and closed the Middle East export market for 6-8 weeks, impacting energy and other applications.

themes.label: Input-cost inflation
themes.note: Key raw materials (benzene, sulfur, aniline, toluene, methanol) rose over 60%, pressuring spreads across segments, particularly agrochemicals and MMA.

themes.label: Capacity expansion / Zone IV ramp-up
themes.note: Zone IV (MPP, calcium chloride, 5 chemistry blocks) delayed 3-4 months by labour shortages but expected to commission through FY27 with revenue starting Q2 FY27.

themes.label: Long-term contract wins / earnings visibility
themes.note: New backward integration contract (INR200-250 crore capex, fixed margin, 15-year) and $150mn agrochemical supply agreement mark a strategic shift toward deeper integration and improved capital efficiency.

themes.label: Deleveraging / capex moderation
themes.note: FY27 capex guided down to INR700-800 crore from INR1,125 crore in FY26; net debt expected to decline, targeting net debt/EBITDA of 2.5x from current 3.6x over 2 years.

themes.label: China supply-side dynamics
themes.note: China's anti-involution stance and safety-driven regulatory tightening on nitration chemistry could support margin recovery and industry consolidation over time, though not yet broad-based.

themes.label: Utilization-led margin recovery
themes.note: High capacity utilization (80-100% annualized in Q4) is starting to support pricing/margin recovery in select chains like NCB and DCB, though not yet portfolio-wide.

key_takeaways: For Q4 FY26, the company reported revenue of INR2,422 crore, representing a growth of 9% Y-o-Y, driven by stable domestic demand and increase in export volumes. EBITDA stood at INR342 crore, growing 29% Y-o-Y and profit after tax was INR137 crore, registering a growth of 43% Y-o-Y.

For the full year FY26, revenue stood at INR9,018 crore, up 12% on a Y-o-Y basis. EBITDA grew by over 15% to close at INR1,172 crore, while PAT recorded a growth of about 27% to close the year at INR419 crore.
In line with the guidance given, the capex for the year was at about INR1,125 crore.

The escalation of geopolitical tensions in the Middle East has led to disruptions across global supply chains, impacting trade flows, logistics timelines and input cost structures. In particular, the prices of key raw materials such as benzene, sulfur, aniline, toluene, methanol went up by over 60%.

Two long-term contracts were concluded in the last quarter: a backward integration initiative with a leading global chemical company with capex of about INR200-250 crore over a residual 15-year contract period, and a $150 million multiyear supply agreement with a global agrochemical innovator through March 31, 2030, without incremental capex.
Zone IV projects were delayed by 3 to 4 months on account of labour constraints, primarily driven by LPG-related issues and migration of labour due to election.
Capex for FY27 is expected to be in the range of INR700 crore to INR800 crore, continuing the journey to optimize capex and maximize returns.

Working capital requirements expanded during the quarter, driven primarily by significant elevation in raw material prices, causing an uptick in net debt as well as interest expenses; net debt is still anticipated to decline in the current year given lower capex intensity.
pressing_questions: On MMA economics amid gasoline-naphtha spread volatility, potential ethanol blending rise, and gas shortages — how should the split between sustainable and volatile demand drivers be understood for the next 2-3 quarters? Management acknowledged this is complex and could not provide a conclusive breakup.

On the steady-state revenue potential from the MPP and calcium chloride projects at current prices — management declined to comment on revenue, citing that today's pricing is not representative of a regular level.
On the exact capex split (asset block by asset block) for calcium chloride vs. MPP within Zone IV — management declined to share this breakup.

On what percentage of Chinese supply has gone offline due to fire incidents and regulatory scrutiny — management said it does not have this answer and noted the incidents are not linked to AIL's own product portfolio.

PRAJIND.about: Praj Industries Ltd., founded in 1983 is a leading biotechnology and engineering company globally. It offers sustainable solutions in bioenergy, water purification, process equipment, breweries, and wastewater treatment. Company is focused on the environment , energy and farm-to-fuel technology solution. Company has global offices in Thailand, Philippines, and the USA.[1]

quarters.summary: Praj expects FY27 performance to improve as strategic initiatives (Bio-IBA/blending technology, Praj GenX modularization partnerships including data centers, and internationalization) start showing results; management flagged that funding-related issues and supply-demand imbalance continue to extend project execution cycles for domestic 1G ethanol, while Brownfield, ENA, CBG (post-GOBARdhan), SAF and new Praj GenX/HiPurity/ZLD verticals are seen as emerging growth drivers over the medium term. Praj GenX is targeted to reach EBITDA breakeven by end of FY27, aided by the new hyperscale data-center order.

subsections.label: Margin drivers
points: Margins were subdued mainly because of volumes and sales mix in Q1 FY27.
International mix improvement and higher Praj GenX order volumes are expected to help margins going forward.
March-to-June quarter margin change explained by 3% material cost improvement offset by 4% rise in other expenses, driven by mix of sales and mix of execution within projects.

June 2025 vs June 2026 quarter: material cost up ~10% while other expenses down ~7%, mainly due to higher export sales in June 2025 versus June 2026; even where export orders were executed in June 2026, a majority were from the African market where margins are lower than Europe or Americas.
Material cost and other (site) expenses generally compensate for each other depending on which revenue component (equipment-related vs site-related activities) is being executed during the period.
Management is taking advance procurement/contractual measures to mitigate steel-related material cost impact going forward.

Standalone margins are lower than implied subsidiary margins; consolidated numbers now include Praj GenX (via Praj HiPurity Systems structure) whose execution mix (e.g., engineering services share) can vary quarter to quarter, making consolidated vs standalone comparisons different from before.

Historically (past decade) margins have largely been in single digits except FY24 and FY25; management declined to give specific forward margin guidance, citing ongoing portfolio expansion and mix change (domestic vs international, projects vs services, 1G ethanol vs new biofuels like isobutanol/CBG) as the basis for expected margin improvement.
Services margins are better than project margins; increasing share of services (leveraging installed base, digital and physical services) is expected to positively impact overall net margins.

Ongoing R&D and developmental investments (e.g., Praj GenX) are currently taking a chunk of margin; business is still in a developmental stage with multiple new avenues (SAF, alternative ethanol products) requiring capital or revenue investment before delivering consistent quarter-on-quarter margins.
Results from these initiatives are expected to be visible in the latter part of FY27.

subsections.label: Revenue mix (quarter)
points: Of total revenue, 66% is from bioenergy, 22% from engineering, and 12% from Praj HiPurity Systems business.

subsections.label: Domestic vs export revenue movement
points: Export revenue declined and domestic revenue increased appreciably YoY; export revenue timing depends on entry point of export orders and their execution cycle — engineering for large export orders booked this quarter will begin translating to execution from Q3 onward.

International orders share is about 40-43% this quarter (up), while international revenue share in the quarter ended June was lower at ~25-30%; this is expected to move higher in coming quarters as these orders convert to revenue.

subsections.label: New order wins
points: Received order for country's first commercial-scale demo plant for Bio-IBA (bio-isobutanol); construction expected to complete by December 2026.
Received order for a greenfield grain-to-ethanol (corn-to-ethanol) plant in Brazil, of approximately 800 KLPD capacity — a marquee reference project for Praj in the region.
Received order to deliver detailed engineering for an ethanol-to-SAF plant from an international customer, following completion of basic engineering order in the prior quarter.
Received first combined contract for supply of ultrapure water and ZLD solutions for a semiconductor company in India.

subsections.label: Domestic first-generation ethanol demand
points: Greenfield project inquiries continue only from customers in ethanol-deficit states like Tamil Nadu and Assam; slowdown expected to continue until higher blending mandate policies emerge.
Increasing demand for Brownfield solutions as customers prioritize operational efficiency improvements and value-added co-products such as Distillers Corn Oil (DCO).
Strong demand for greenfield ENA plants, where Praj has a clear technology edge.

subsections.label: Backlog execution and conversion
points: Funding-related issues persist for end customers, resulting in extended project execution cycles.
Supply-demand imbalance in the ethanol market has impacted backlog conversion to revenue.
Collections have been affected due to slow conversion of backlog; company is working to improve both execution and collections in coming quarters.

key_figures.label: Export revenue share of total revenue

subsections.label: Praj GenX
points: Secured a significant global supply agreement as engineering and manufacturing partner for critical modular infrastructure for hyperscale data centers, guaranteeing a minimum business volume of about US$50 million over the next two-and-a-half years, with potential upside depending on customer project schedules.
Marks strategic diversification into a high-growth global engineering market outside Praj's core bioenergy business, leveraging established mega manufacturing capacity at Mangaluru.
First project delivery expected over Q2-Q4 of FY27.

The INR 500 crore (~US$50m) order is not fully booked yet; only a portion has been booked so far, with the rest to be booked as firm confirmation of phases/data centers is received over the 2.5-year period.
Company expects Praj GenX to reach breakeven (considered EBITDA breakeven to start) by end of FY27, supported by improving order book volume.

Praj GenX also serves ETCA (energy transition and climate action - green ammonia, green hydrogen) segment, which has been subdued in recent years, and conventional oil & gas refining, petrochemicals, fertilizers segment; data centers is now a third segment, providing diversification to hedge against headwinds in any one segment.

No large order backlog carryforward for Praj GenX currently, but order buildup is described as impressive; new data-center orders have shorter delivery cycles, with the Q1 order for data centers potentially delivered before end of FY27.
Engineering order book share of Praj GenX not disclosed separately; management stated engineering is still shown as one basket and will disclose Praj GenX separately at an opportune time.

subsections.label: Segment mix
points: Bioenergy contributes 66% of revenue, engineering 22%, and Praj HiPurity Systems 12% (Q1 FY27).
Order intake split: 62% bioenergy, 28% engineering, 10% Praj HiPurity Systems.

subsections.label: Lifecycle services business
points: Growing steadily quarter-over-quarter; serves large customer installed base with physical and digital services ensuring optimal plant performance and efficiency.
Offers performance enhancer solutions and biogenic CO2 capture solutions.
Conducted several trials for performance enhancers in the Latin American region during the quarter to expand offerings there.

subsections.label: ZLD and Praj HiPurity Systems
points: Batteries, semiconductors, and solar panel (BSS) segment in India is opening new opportunities.
Received first combined contract for supply of ultrapure water and ZLD solutions for a semiconductor company in India, expanding solutions offerings into new emerging industry segments.

subsections.label: SAF (Sustainable Aviation Fuel)
points: ICAO has officially approved the entire supply chain, production, and handling of sugarcane and sugarcane derivatives, as well as production of SAF using sugarcane-to-jet pathways, helping validate alcohol-to-jet technology as an accepted SAF pathway.
Engagement with international customer on ethanol-to-SAF detailed engineering is progressing well, positioning Praj as a technology partner for alcohol-to-jet SAF projects.

subsections.label: Bio-IBA (Bio-isobutanol)
points: Received order for country's first commercial-scale demo Bio-IBA plant; construction to be completed by December 2026.
Government agencies are testing bio-isobutanol blended into diesel and checking engine efficiency in parallel with construction.

Science and technology viability for bio-isobutanol is established; Praj believes it has the right technology and expertise if blending mandates are introduced, though timing of any mandate is unknown.

subsections.label: Other biomaterials (Bio-bitumen, PLA)
points: Praj has technology for lactic acid, which is a feedstock for PLA.
Engaged in discussions with prospective customers for bio-bitumen and PLA-related co-products; hopeful of progress by end of FY27.

subsections.label: CBG feedstock technology
points: Praj has technologies for all kinds of feedstocks (waste to energy); successfully delivered projects on press mud (sugar mill waste), rice straw (agricultural waste), and Napier grass.

Viability for these technologies/feedstocks has been achieved, though continuous supply of quality feedstock is needed to avoid interruption to generation; challenges can arise depending on plant location and customer's feedstock supply capability.

Municipal solid waste (MSW) for CBG: feedstock segregation challenges remain a key hurdle; company is exploring solutions but not pursuing this segment aggressively yet, though not ignoring it completely.

subsections.label: Praj GenX data center technology
points: Offering involves creating infrastructure for server halls (large halls housing server racks for compute power), covering both server rack infrastructure and cooling systems to manage temperatures.
More solutions expected to be added to the portfolio as engagement in hyperscale data center infrastructure progresses.

subsections.label: Dr. Pramod Chaudhari Centre of Excellence
points: Inaugurated at Savitribai Phule Pune University (SPPU) on World Biofuel Day (August 10) as a pioneering initiative and hub for interdisciplinary research, innovation, education, and industry collaboration in the bioeconomy.

subsections.label: Manufacturing leverage
points: Praj GenX leverages established mega manufacturing capacity at Mangaluru for modular infrastructure and precision fabrication used in the hyperscale data center supply agreement.
Average greenfield ethanol plant capacity has increased over the last couple of years — earlier plants were typically 60, 80, 100 KLPD; now customers are discussing 200, 400 KLPD capacities.

subsections.label: International market developments
points: Received order for a greenfield grain-to-ethanol (corn-to-ethanol) plant in Brazil, expected to serve as a marquee reference for Praj in the region.
Closely following developments in the U.S.A. market, which has announced usage of E15 (15% ethanol blending in gasoline/petrol).

Engaging with potential customers in Indonesia, Vietnam, Kenya, Panama, Argentina, Guatemala, Costa Rica, and Bolivia, where governments are increasing the share of biofuels in their energy mix, driven by energy security and energy cost considerations.
Conducted performance enhancer trials in the Latin American region during the quarter to expand lifecycle services offerings there.
Received order to deliver detailed engineering for an ethanol-to-SAF plant from an international customer.

subsections.label: State-level CBG policy support
points: State governments such as Maharashtra, Odisha, Chhattisgarh, and Assam have announced policies to support capacity creation for CBG projects.

subsections.label: Strategic portfolio diversification
points: Efforts over the last two years — Bio-IBA/blending technology, Praj GenX partnerships (data centers and other modularization applications), and internationalization — have started showing results and creating new business opportunities.

Company is building a balanced portfolio across ZLD, Praj HiPurity Systems (battery/semiconductor/solar), and bioenergy, driven partly by stricter emission regulations and government initiatives in new manufacturing areas (batteries, solar panels, semiconductors).

subsections.label: CBG joint venture (BPCL)
points: Company continues to pursue and discuss the previously mentioned CBG joint venture with oil marketing companies; with GOBARdhan scheme coming into play, discussions may speed up.
Management declined to elaborate further on JV specifics while discussions are ongoing.

Joint ventures, especially with oil marketing companies, are seen as one way (not the only way) to grab market opportunity, offering advantages such as assured consumption of the final product; company has also executed many standalone projects and partnered with customers to bring in investments.

subsections.label: Funding and execution risk
points: Funding-related issues at end customers persist, resulting in extended project execution cycles.
Supply-demand imbalance in the ethanol market has impacted conversion of backlog to revenue.
Slow conversion of backlog has had a knock-on effect on collections.

subsections.label: Policy dependency
points: 1G ethanol domestic greenfield business slowdown expected to continue until higher blending mandate policies are implemented.
Timing of any bio-isobutanol blending mandate for diesel is unknown; management cannot predict when it will come.

subsections.label: Commodity/input cost risk
points: Upward trend in material costs due to current geopolitical scenario is expected to continue creating some pressure; company is managing this through contractual arrangements and advance procurement.
Steel-side material cost movement flagged as an area of concern; company taking advance measures to mitigate impact going forward.

subsections.label: MSW feedstock segregation challenge
points: Segregation of municipal solid waste feedstock suitable for digesters remains a technical challenge; company is not pursuing this aggressively until solutions are developed.

subsections.label: CBG market maturity
points: CBG market is still nascent/maturing, making it too early to estimate market share; multiple feedstocks and business models mean there isn't a single applicable number.

subsections.label: GOBARdhan / CBG opportunity
points: Union cabinet approved GOBARdhan, the National Circular Bioenergy Scheme, with a total outlay of over INR 23,000 crore, to be implemented from FY27 to FY36, aiming to scale domestic CBG production nearly tenfold and mobilize large-scale private investment.

Scheme is expected to be an inflection point that expedites investments via assured demand, remunerative and stable pricing, capital assistance, pipeline infrastructure, credit support, and continuous technology development.
Management expects both the CBG opportunity size and overall margins to improve once GOBARdhan-driven market opens up.

subsections.label: Margin outlook
points: Management declined to give specific margin guidance, citing ongoing portfolio and mix expansion (domestic/international, project/services, 1G ethanol/new biofuels) as levers expected to improve margins over time versus historical single-digit levels (excluding FY24/FY25).
Results from strategic initiatives (Praj GenX, internationalization, new ethanol alternatives) are expected to start showing in the latter part of FY27.

subsections.label: Praj GenX breakeven
points: Management expects Praj GenX to reach breakeven (EBITDA level, to start) by end of FY27, supported by improving order book volumes and the data center order.

subsections.label: Bio-IBA mandate potential
points: A 2% Bio-IBA blending mandate in diesel is estimated to create a project opportunity of over INR 3,000 crore.

guidance_ledger.statement: Overall, we believe efforts put in by the company over the period of last two years have started creating new opportunities as we move further into this financial year. We shall build on this momentum and deliver improved performance.

Hopefully by end of this year, we should be able to see that break-even because our volume for the order book for Praj GenX is looking better now. ... To start with, you can consider EBITDA breakeven.

We would not like to give you any particular guidance on the margins because we are still working on expanding our portfolio and also changing the mix... we obviously hope to improve the margins that you have seen historically (single digit) and get it to a better position.
The construction will get done and completed by end of this year, by December of 2026.
We are hopeful to get the success for these co-products, and therefore, by end of this fiscal, we hope to get some of this progressed.
We believe that this situation will continue till the time we see policies around higher blending mandates.
We hope that when the market opens up with the GOBARdhan opportunity... we believe that both the opportunity size as well as the overall margin will be better.

International orders are about 40%-43% this quarter. These orders will be converting over the next few months and quarters into revenue... you will start to see that percentage [rise] in the coming quarters.

We should be in that range typically [Rs.800-900 crores], but as we don't want to give any forward-looking statements, that is the right ballpark that one can assume.

key_takeaways: Consolidated income from operations for Q1 FY27 stood at INR 7.16 billion versus INR 6.4 billion in Q1 FY26; PBT before exceptional items at INR 210.5 million versus INR 96.09 million; PAT at INR 116.1 million versus INR 53.4 million.
Order intake during the quarter was INR 10 billion, with 57% from domestic market; order backlog as of June 30, 2026 stood at INR 45.9 billion, comprising 63% domestic orders.
Received order for country's first commercial-scale demo Bio-IBA plant; a 2% Bio-IBA blending mandate in diesel could create over INR 3,000 crore project opportunity.
Received order for a greenfield grain-to-ethanol plant in Brazil (~800 KLPD, corn-to-ethanol) — a marquee reference project for the region.

Praj GenX secured a global supply agreement for hyperscale data center modular infrastructure guaranteeing minimum business volume of about US$50 million over 2.5 years; management expects Praj GenX to reach EBITDA breakeven by end of FY27.
Union cabinet approved GOBARdhan, the National Circular Bioenergy Scheme, with outlay of over INR 23,000 crore (FY27-FY36), aiming to scale domestic CBG production nearly tenfold.
Received first combined contract for ultrapure water and ZLD solutions for a semiconductor company in India, opening new opportunities in batteries, semiconductors, and solar (BSS) segment.

ICAO approved sugarcane-to-jet SAF pathway, validating alcohol-to-jet technology as an accepted SAF pathway; Praj is progressing detailed engineering for an ethanol-to-SAF plant for an international customer.
Shareholders approved final dividend of 180% per share at the AGM.

quarters.summary: FY'26 performance was impacted by external headwinds including raw material price volatility, execution delays and deferred order finalizations; management expects improved performance in FY'27 driven by expected higher ethanol blending mandates (E22-E30, E85, E100), ramp-up of Praj GenX (data centers, LNG, oil & gas), CBG and SAF opportunities, and easing of execution-related cost escalations. Order intake guidance is expected to return to a steady-state band of Rs.800-900 crore, and GenX is targeted to move towards break-even in FY'27.

subsections.label: Margin pressure drivers
points: Investments in Praj GenX (long gestation period) continued through FY'26, impacting profitability.
Cost escalation in execution due to extended project execution cycles (funding and other challenges) impacted profitability while revenues remained flat.
Some one-time, non-business related items impacted bottom line in FY'26.
More than raw material prices, cost escalation in site execution (delays keeping sites open longer than time-bound schedule) put pressure on cost to execute projects.
On a YTD basis, raw material prices have remained more or less in the same range; the quarterly aberration is not primarily a raw-material-price effect.
Company has moved from 100% fixed-price contracts to contracts with some flexibility/sensitivity to raw material price changes, to protect margins going forward.
Management believes execution challenges are largely over as project cycle times are shorter (moving from Greenfield to Brownfield, smaller project sizes), with FY'27 focus on operational excellence.

subsections.label: Shareholder returns
points: Board proposed final dividend of Rs.3.6 per equity share (180% of Rs.2 face value) for FY26, subject to shareholder approval at the AGM.
An investor suggested a buyback instead of dividend/bonus/split to return value to shareholders; management stated this is a Board matter and will take the feedback to the Board.

subsections.label: Order intake trends
points: Order intake print for the quarter was the lowest in four years, partly attributed to deferred order inquiries owing to raw material cost/supply chain uncertainty.
Engineering business opportunities were pursued in Q4 FY26 but final negotiations deferred due to raw-material cost and supply-chain uncertainties; some of these orders expected to reflect in FY27.
Praj deferred ~Rs.300+ crore worth of inquiries in the quarter rather than finalizing orders, due to raw material price uncertainty under fixed-price contracting norms.
Management believes order intake should return to a typical range of Rs.800-900 crore on a steady-state basis, based on current pipeline, though this is not a formal forward-looking commitment.

subsections.label: 1G ethanol order trends
points: Greenfield fuel ethanol project ordering has declined in FY26 due to existing blending capacity already achieved under EBP-20.

Smaller-ticket opportunities are emerging: operational efficiency enhancement jobs for existing plants and orders for co-products like Distiller's Corn Oil (DCO) for corn-based plants; inquiries and order books for these have increased.
Fuel ethanol project execution cycle continues to be extended due to funding and other challenges, slowing backlog execution.

subsections.label: Bioenergy - 1G ethanol
points: 1G domestic business continued to experience slowdown in Greenfield fuel ethanol projects; expected to improve after announcement of higher blending mandates.
Increased demand seen for greenfield ENA (extra-neutral alcohol) plants; Praj has a clear technology edge in ENA.

Growing demand for Brownfield solutions as customers prioritize operational efficiency improvements and value-added co-products such as Distiller's Corn Oil (DCO); good number of DCO orders secured during the quarter with a robust inquiry pipeline.

Bio-isobutanol (Bio-IBA) technology is ready for commercialization and scale-up; first order expected in Q1 FY27; diesel blending volume requirement is much bigger than petrol, making Bio-IBA significant for India's biofuels journey.

subsections.label: CBG (Compressed Biogas)
points: Capacity ramp-up underway at a few plants using Napier grass and rice straw as mixed feedstock.
Good inquiry pipeline for projects based on press mud and Napier grass, but delays in order finalization persist.
Praj is exploring international CBG opportunities based on domestic market success.

CBG co-products FOM (Fermented Organic Manure) and LFOM (Liquid Fermented Organic Manure) can reduce reliance on imported chemical fertilizer; CBG can also be integrated into urban piped natural gas networks.

subsections.label: Lifecycle Services
points: Growing steadily, with growing traction for performance enhancer solutions and biogenic CO2 capture solutions.
More than 1,000 plants globally using Praj technology provide a source of steady growth for this business.

subsections.label: SAF (Sustainable Aviation Fuel)
points: Completing basic engineering order for one ethanol-to-SAF plant for an international customer; in discussions for the detailed engineering order for the same plant.
Draft SAF policy is ready; blending mandates expected in 2027.

Investments in SAF nationally have been subdued because strong ATF blending mandates have been delayed; Praj is tracking international SAF opportunities and is ready to participate once mandates arrive.

subsections.label: 2G ethanol
points: Three 2G ethanol projects exist in the country, and all three are being executed by Praj alone; technology available only with Praj.
As with any new technology, there is a gestation period with associated challenges, but management is confident 2G-produced ethanol can be used especially for SAF.

subsections.label: Engineering Businesses / Praj GenX
points: In Q4 FY26, several engineering opportunities were pursued but final negotiations deferred due to raw material cost/supply chain uncertainty; some orders expected to reflect in FY27.
Praj GenX: data center segment emerging as promising; in final discussions with a key customer for modularized cooling system solutions for international data centers.

Investment in GenX ongoing for 2.5-3 years to build capacity for equipment/modular plants; customer base being built through facility approvals (audits), expected to positively impact FY27 order books.

GenX facility utilization targeted via data centers, LNG, and conventional oil & gas segments; company pivoted away from the subdued ETCA (Energy Transition and Climate Action - green hydrogen, green ammonia, electrolyzers) segment toward these three.
Data center orders not one-off — once facility is certified, repeat orders expected every few months, improving capacity utilization.
GenX fixed overhead run rate continuing at ~Rs.10 crores per month.
International data center customers undergo a long certification process before placing orders; certification enables multiple future projects.
Company declined to disclose the data center customer or whether the order is from the client directly or an OEM, citing confidentiality obligations.
No GenX order booked in Q4 FY26 for data centers; good news on this expected in Q1 FY27.

subsections.label: ZLD and PHS businesses
points: Battery, semiconductor, and solar panel manufacturing segments are opening up as new opportunities for ZLD and PHS businesses.
Praj is pursuing opportunities where ZLD and PHS will offer joint solutions to these customers.
One such order was closed with a semiconductor company in the current quarter.

subsections.label: Ethanol production capacity for higher blending
points: If blending increase is between 2%-5%, current ethanol production capacities may be sufficient, but efficiency and ethanol quality improvements will be needed.
If blending mandate goes beyond 5%, additional capacity will need to be added; Praj is monitoring and preparing for this scenario.
Praj offers both capacity/throughput enhancement of existing plants via technical modifications, and new production lines, depending on customer needs and funding ability.

subsections.label: International market developments
points: U.S. House has passed legislation allowing nationwide sales of gasoline/petrol with 15% ethanol blend; Praj is monitoring developments and engaging with customers for opportunities in the Americas.

Positive biofuel-related announcements in Indonesia, Vietnam, Kenya, Panama, Argentina, Guatemala, Costa Rica, and Bolivia for increasing biofuels share in energy mix; Praj has successfully implemented projects in these countries previously and is engaged in business development there.
Praj is looking at international opportunities for its CBG business based on success in the Indian market.
Reference to Brazil and Thailand as countries that have successfully and effectively used ethanol in managing their energy mix.

subsections.label: Domestic policy/regional rollout
points: E85/E100 retail outlet rollout begins with 150 outlets across Delhi, Mumbai, Pune, and Nagpur within the next month.
Scaling to 500 outlets across major metro regions including Delhi-NCR, Maharashtra, Bangalore, Chennai, Kolkata, and Hyderabad within 6-12 months.
Target of 5,000 E100 dispensing stations nationwide within 24 months.

Maharashtra approved its State CBG Policy 2026 with an outlay of Rs.500 crores aimed at accelerating waste-to-energy infrastructure, promoting circular economy models, and expanding clean fuel production in the state.

subsections.label: Praj GenX data center strategy
points: Short-term focus: providing infrastructure for cooling systems (specially designed skids/modules with special material of construction) for server rooms/cabinets in data centers, driven by AI-related growth in energy and heat management needs.
Long-term vision: expand into other data center technology areas, including potential use of renewable/bioenergy for medium/large data centers' large energy requirements.
International data center customers require multi-angle facility certification before placing repeat orders across multiple projects.

subsections.label: Management structure
points: Ashish Gaikwad appointed MD in June (prior year); Sachin Raole elevated to Joint Managing Director and CFO to manage expanded scope of work across multiple areas as the company prepares for its next five-year plan.

subsections.label: Strategic vision
points: Company continues to progress on strategic vision aligned to global megatrends of energy security, energy transition, and sustainability despite external headwinds.

Investments in Praj GenX over the last 2.5-3 years intended to build large capacity to serve global equipment and modular plant requirements; gestation period expected to yield positive order book impact from FY27 onwards.

subsections.label: Execution and cost risks
points: Extended fuel ethanol project execution cycles due to funding and other challenges have caused cost escalation at project sites, as sites remain open longer than the time-bound schedule.
Raw material price uncertainty led to deferral of ~Rs.300+ crore worth of engineering inquiries rather than finalizing fixed-price contracts.
Company is monitoring ongoing supply chain disruption risk closely; RM price situation described as dynamic, with potential for further impact ahead.
One-time, non-business related items impacted bottom line in FY26.
Order finalization delays persist in CBG press mud/Napier grass-based projects.
ETCA segment (green hydrogen, green ammonia, electrolyzers) has become subdued over the last two years, requiring pivot to other GenX segments (data centers, LNG, oil & gas).
SAF investments nationally have been subdued due to delayed ATF blending mandates.

subsections.label: External macro/geopolitical factors
points: West Asia geopolitical situation has highlighted the need for energy security for every nation, giving impetus to biofuels production/usage globally.
Rising crude prices, geopolitical tensions and supply disruptions in the Middle East are making India's focus on CBG strategically important.
Finance Minister highlighted concerns around three Fs - fuel, fertilizer, and foreign exchange - reinforcing need to reduce import dependence, for which CBG offers a domestic solution.

key_takeaways: Our performance in Quarter 4 and full year of FY '26 was impacted by several external headwinds.
Despite these headwinds, we continue to progress on our strategic vision, which is aligned to the global megatrends of energy security, energy transition, and sustainability.
The Bureau of Indian Standards has now notified fuel specifications for E22, E25, E27, and E30 petrol blends in addition to the E85 and E100, building upon India's successful E20 program.
Our 1G domestic business continued to experience a slowdown in Greenfield fuel ethanol products. We believe this situation will improve after announcement of higher blending mandates.
We had mentioned in our previous call that our technology for bio-isobutanol or Bio-IBA is ready for commercialization and scale-up. We are expecting our first order in the current quarter of FY '27.

On CBG front, the capacity ramp-up of a few of our plants using Napier grass and rice straw as mixed feedstock is underway. While there is a good inquiry pipeline for projects based on press mud and Napier grass, there are some delays in order finalization.

On the Praj GenX front, data center segment is coming up as a promising segment. We are in final discussions with one of our key customers for modularized solutions for the cooling systems for their international data centers.

Overall, we believe the external business environment is going to remain uncertain. However, our strong technology edge in bioenergy and advanced manufacturing capabilities in modularization will help us deliver improved performance in FY '27.
Export revenues accounted for 36% for FY '26. Of the total revenue, 67% is from bioenergy, 22% from engineering and 11% from PHS business.
The order intake during the quarter was Rs. 6,580 million with 79% from domestic market and of the total order intake 86% came from bioenergy, 2% from engineering and balance 12% from PHS business.
The order backlog as of March 26 stood at Rs. 43,050 million comprising 66% of domestic order with 78% from bioenergy, 16% from engineering and balance 5% from PHS.
pressing_questions: So, I am being invested from some past three years and from past three years I am seeing a little bit underperformance in our margins and profits and other things. And even we are being an R&D company with all the innovations we are doing, why we are not able to maintain the margin and we are reducing the margin profits? Can you give some light on that?

I have been tracking Praj for many years... Now when we see CBG and SAF, we already see a lot of investment happening in India. And Praj seems to have a very minimal share in that. So, how are we supposed to track this company? Because you keep on making so many announcements to the stock exchanges on your technical excellence. But when it comes to orders, execution, margins, there were talks of margins of high teens and where the margins are right now. So, how are investors supposed to invest in your company when you are not delivering on things which you are also talking of? And secondly, Mr. Gaikwad was appointed as MD just last June. And now there is a joint MD also appointed. So, what was the requirement for that?

We are just hoping that... [engineering companies in general in India are doing very well at this stage, and Praj has invested in a lot of technologies, and right now it seems that the company is working more for the employees because of the kind of investment done in the GenX plant and the results for the shareholders are not coming]

Sir, another point like other investor also mentioned, we are like lagging in terms of performance in revenues, top lines, margins since last three years. So, would it be fair to tell that management can do a buyback to just give some value to the shareholders rather than giving a dividend and then give some bonus or a split to the existing share value?

subsections.label: Drivers of profit growth
points: ADR up 7%, occupancy up 2%, RevPAR and EBITDA both up 9%, PAT up 140% from INR7 crores to INR17 crores.
RevPAR growth was rate-led rather than occupancy-led, reflecting quality/positioning of assets rather than a favourable demand cycle.
Finance cost fell over 50% YoY (INR18.9 crores to INR8.7 crores) and was the single biggest driver of PAT more than doubling this quarter.
For FY26 as a whole, interest savings were of the order of INR24 crores at a blended cost of debt of ~8.25%.

subsections.label: Balance sheet/deleveraging
points: Deployed INR468.1 crores of IPO proceeds towards debt repayment, leaving effectively no institutional debt on the books.
Net cash position of ~INR108 crores as at 30 June 2026, reflecting continued strengthening of balance sheet.

subsections.label: Cancellation impact
points: INR14 crores impact from cancellations, ~10% of overall revenue, driven mainly by MICE event cancellation/postponement.
Of the INR14 crores cancellation impact, roughly 60% was related to F&B and the balance to rooms; rooms were quickly replaced with domestic corporate business but F&B business could not be replaced.

subsections.label: Revenue mix
points: F&B contributes about 32% of overall top line.
MICE contribution to room bookings is roughly 15% to 18% of business on a portfolio level, varying hotel to hotel.

subsections.label: Bangalore market strategy
points: Focus over here is to maintain occupancy now and focus on positioning only; ADR increase expected over coming three quarters.

Strategy included contacting domestic businesses via locally negotiated rates, focusing on staycations since MICE business over weekends was reduced, and focusing on social events and weddings to displace lost foreign travel business.

subsections.label: Portfolio occupancy dynamics
points: Five of nine hotels have occupancy above 80%, indicating scope to grow occupancy from the remaining four hotels.
ibis Styles (launched about a year ago) showing occupancy ramp from 40% in its first half-year to 70s in its second year, described as a normal ramp curve for a new hotel.

Future growth is a play of both ARR and occupancy; when market mix dips (e.g., international business decreasing), management plays between occupancy and ADR to show overall RevPAR increase; booking window has significantly reduced making quarter-ahead forecasting harder, requiring more agile decisions.

subsections.label: Kochi rebrand impact
points: Kochi (Four Points by Sheraton rebranded to Courtyard by Marriott) saw rate increase to INR4,650 but a big dip in occupancy due to reduction in crew business (partly due to West Asia crisis) and due to rebranding requiring name changes in GDS systems.
Since dip occurred in the rebranding quarter, Q2 is showing positive signs with occupancy already back to high 60s, expected to trend into 70s; minimum 10% ADR growth expected this year.
Apart from Courtyard Kochi, every other property showed an increase in occupancy; Courtyard's dip pulled down the average portfolio occupancy number.

subsections.label: F&B/MICE impact by property
points: Largest F&B impact was at Sheraton Grand given its large banqueting capacity and 50-50 rooms:F&B revenue split; other hotels averaging ~30% F&B contribution saw a lesser impact.
Across the country, the larger the MICE/catering capacity, the larger the impact from event cancellations/postponements.

subsections.label: FTA mix and travel behavior
points: FTA contribution to room arrivals dropped from a previous 60-40 domestic-foreign mix to now about 30% FTA (10% reduction).
FTAs typically pay a better/higher ADR than domestic companies, which put some pressure on overall ADR as FTA mix declined.

subsections.label: Sustainability
points: Company now uses renewable energy for 61% of total energy needs across the portfolio, with several hotels already operating above 90% renewable energy usage, a metric tracked and improved as part of broader operating discipline.

Capex on new restaurant Project Grain
Expected commissioning year for JW Marriott and Thiruvananthapuram hotels

subsections.label: Portfolio expansion plan
points: Clear growth runway with additional 1,700 keys under development, set to expand portfolio to 3,300 keys by FY31.
Expansion anchored by brands like Grand Hyatt, InterContinental, JW Marriott, and Ritz-Carlton across Bangalore, Chennai, Hyderabad, and Kochi.
This will lift luxury and upper upscale mix from 14% today to 31% by FY29 and 38% by FY31, positioning BHVL in the segment with strongest pricing power and demand-supply mismatch.

subsections.label: New hotel launch - WTC Chennai Courtyard
points: Launch of Courtyard by Marriott Chennai in the World Trade Center, a 45-key hotel, planned in Q3 (October) of FY27, strengthening footprint in a high-demand business district.

Expected minimum starting ADR of INR9,000, growing in coming months; expected to stabilize quickly with stabilized occupancy of about 80% due to captive demand from walking-distance corporate tenants in World Trade Centre.
Management is speaking to tenants in World Trade Centre to secure captive demand for the hotel all year round.

subsections.label: Live project status updates
points: Both Fairfield properties are under construction and well underway.
Grand Hyatt (originally slated for FY28) will see a slight delay pending a few approvals.
InterContinental hotel at Brigade Gateway is part of a mixed-use township, with dependency underway.
Ritz-Carlton Vaikom is well underway; designs have been finalized.
JW Marriott Chennai — excavation should start soon; the hotel is under approval.
Trivandrum (Thiruvananthapuram) hotel is under design development, pending some information before finalizing design; still in planning phase.
Tumkur Road property in Bangalore has made good progress; management is awaiting approvals to get started.
Both JW Marriott and Thiruvananthapuram hotels expected to be commissioned by 2030.

subsections.label: Capex phasing
points: Of INR3,600 crores planned capex for expansion, INR400 crores already invested in FY26, with another INR500 crores expected in FY27.

In Q1 FY27, ~INR53 crores was spent (INR45 crores CWIP, INR3.5 crores renovation, INR4 crores for new restaurant Project Grain); balance of FY27 capex (~INR350 crores) to be spent over the next three quarters, mainly in H2.

subsections.label: Funding strategy
points: Funding mix deliberately balanced: broadly 60% through borrowing and 40% through internal accruals.
Internal accruals expected to contribute over INR1,000 crores across coming years as ARR grows, new assets ramp up, and operating leverage plays its role.

subsections.label: M&A/acquisition
points: Part of IPO proceeds is earmarked for a hotel acquisition; company is under discussion and hoping to conclude a transaction in FY27, subject to due diligence.

subsections.label: Leadership changes and corporate milestones
points: Manoj Agarwal, former COO, has resigned; replaced by Mr. Vinay Gupta, who joins as CEO of Brigade Hotel Ventures Limited. Vinay Gupta was previously GM of the company's first property, Grand Mercure Bangalore, and has since worked with Accor, SAMHI and InterGlobe, along with his own entrepreneurial venture.
On 5th August, hosted 10th Annual General Meeting, the first as a listed company; Chairman Mr. M.R. Jaishankar and MD Ms. Nirupa Shankar shared insights on performance and strategic priorities.
Strengthened engagement with investor/analyst community via an in-person interaction at a Bangalore property followed by site visits to select properties.

Recognitions: MD Nirupa Shankar named to Fortune India's 100 Most Powerful Women list for second consecutive year and recognized by Business Today among India's most powerful women in 2025; Vineet Verma recognized among India's top 50 great people managers by Great Manager Institute in 2026.

Property-level recognitions: Shine Spa at Sheraton Grand Bangalore Brigade Gateway awarded best hotel spa for South by Global Spa Magazine; Cafe G at Holiday Inn Chennai OMR IT Expressway and Grand Mercure Ahmedabad GIFT City honoured on IHC London and IIHM Hospitality Honours List for 2026.

subsections.label: Geopolitical/macro headwinds
points: The conflict in West Asia remained the dominant factor through April and June; airspace disruptions and rerouting pushed up fares and journey times on several international/connecting routes.
Energy and fuel costs stayed elevated and inflationary pressures persisted through the quarter.
For an industry running on discretionary travel and event planning, a geopolitical shock of this nature is bound to have an impact.
Booking window has significantly reduced, making it hard to forecast for the entire quarter, requiring more agile revenue management decisions.

subsections.label: MICE/F&B softness
points: F&B side saw performance impacted due to cancellation and postponement of large MICE events, not just for the company's hotels but across the entire city.
MICE activity was soft on account of a comparatively dry event calendar during the quarter, worsened by geopolitical tensions.

Management views this as temporary event-driven softness rather than a structural change in demand; large-scale MICE events come every alternate year, and Q4 FY27 is expected to be an aero show year benefiting MICE.

subsections.label: FTA mix decline
points: FTA contribution to room arrivals declined from a previous 60-40 domestic-foreign mix to about 30% FTA; FTAs typically pay higher ADR, so the mix shift put some pressure on ADR.

subsections.label: Near-term outlook
points: Better pickup seen in July and a very healthy pickup expected in September; buoyancy in the market with MICE events coming back, supporting the view that events were postponed rather than fully cancelled.
Upcoming quarter (Q2 FY27) should be a lot more buoyant than Q1 FY27.
Hopeful of making up lost revenue from Q1 in the second half of the year; Q4 FY27 looking extremely healthy as it is an aero show year with more MICE events.
WTC Courtyard by Marriott Chennai launch, while a small hotel, should add to overall growth guidelines.

subsections.label: Mid-teens growth reiteration
points: Company has tried to maintain like-to-like growth in the mid-teens range; top line grew 5% in Q1 but this was impacted by the INR14 crores cancellation hit (~10% of top line) — absent that impact, mid-teens growth would have been achieved.
Remaining part of the year looking good with buoyant bookings and larger MICE inquiries, especially in September; management putting in every effort to achieve mid-teens growth for FY27.

key_takeaways: Consolidated EBITDA increased by 9% year-on-year to INR46 crores with EBITDA margin at 34.8%. GST 2.0 had an impact of 1.6% on the EBITDA margin during the quarter.
Profit after tax stood at INR17 crores as against INR7 crores in Q1 FY26, registering a 140% year-on-year growth.
ARR for the quarter was INR7,241 up 7% year-on-year, while occupancy stood at 75.7%. This resulted in RevPAR of INR5,479 representing a 9% year-on-year increase.
As of 30th June 2026, we had a net cash position of INR108 crores reflecting the continued strengthening of our balance sheet.
Finance cost for Q1 FY27 fell to INR8.7 crores from INR18.9 crores in Q1 FY26, a reduction of over 50%, the single biggest driver of PAT more than doubling this quarter.
Development pipeline entails a total Capex of approximately INR3,600 crores to build out ~1,700 upcoming keys by FY30 taking portfolio from 1,600 keys to 3,300 keys.
We had an impact of almost INR14 crores which was about 10% of our overall revenue due to West Asia crisis; better pickup seen in July and a very healthy pickup expected in September.
Leadership movement: Manoj Agarwal, former COO, has resigned and will be replaced by Mr. Vinay Gupta as CEO of Brigade Hotel Ventures Limited.

quarters.summary: Management described FY'26 as a steady and encouraging year for India's hospitality sector on strong domestic demand, with Q4 total income up 8% YoY and EBITDA up 13% YoY to INR58 crores (39.7% margin). Near-term outlook flags war/geopolitical disruption and GST 2.0 impacting margins, but domestic demand resilience, ADR growth, upcoming rebranding (Kochi to Courtyard by Marriott) and new Chennai OMR property launch in FY'27, plus a large planned capex of ~INR3,600 crores, underpin a positive demand and ARR growth outlook through FY29-FY31.

subsections.label: Cost efficiency drivers
points: Performance driven by continued focus on cost efficiency and productivity-led initiatives across the portfolio.
Interest costs have reduced due to loan repayments, positively impacting net profitability.
Other income increase driven by interest on fixed deposits kept with the bank and INR4.7 crores towards creditors reversal which is no longer payable.

subsections.label: GST 2.0 and one-off impacts on margin
points: GST 2.0 resulted in a 1.4% impact on EBITDA margin for Q4 FY26 and 0.8% impact for FY26.
FY26 EBITDA was impacted by additional property tax expenses of around INR6 crores; excluding this, operational EBITDA would have grown 19% YoY.
Excluding one-off cases (input tax credit not utilized, one-time property tax hit) and GST impact, EBITDA margin for the quarter would have been about 37.5% to 38%, in line with plan.
Payroll costs are sub-20% at 19%, utilities only 5.5% for the year, and admin & general costs are under control — all healthy operating metrics.

subsections.label: Capital allocation
points: Planned capex of approximately INR3,600 crores, of which INR400 crores already invested by FY26, to be funded through a balanced mix of debt and internal accruals.
Around 60% of capex will be financed through borrowings with the remainder supported by internal cash generation.
Internal accruals expected to contribute over INR1,000 crores in coming years, driven by steady ARR growth and operating leverage as new assets ramp up.

subsections.label: Demand mix and resilience
points: Domestic demand has remained resilient and continues to anchor growth amid global uncertainties and geopolitical developments affecting international travel.
Domestic business quickly replaced international travel demand even during the war conflict; occupancy did not drop and ADR climbed up.
Once the war conflict ends, gradual increase in international business expected, but domestic demand is confident to continue regardless.
It will always be good to maintain a healthy ~75:25 domestic:FTA mix because FTA business helps maximize ADR yield.

subsections.label: War impact on F&B and cancellations
points: F&B revenue saw slight QoQ decline of about 3% due to cancellations worth INR7-8 crores (about 5% of quarter business), linked to larger events dependent on foreign travellers and international travel.
Company was able to make up some of the loss with domestic business, but not enough to increase F&B revenue.
Greatest impact was seen in March; similar cancellations of INR7-8 crores expected in April-June, being offset with more domestic business.
Uncertain whether MICE/large events cancelled will return later in the year or be permanently lost; management hopeful they will come back once things stabilize.

subsections.label: Revenue vs RevPAR growth bridge
points: RevPAR growth of 6% (Q4) driven by ADR growth of 7% while occupancy was maintained; overall revenue growth was lower (2%) due to F&B revenue decline of ~3% YoY from large cancellations.
Room revenue increased 7% for the quarter; full-year revenue growth was 12%.

subsections.label: Bangalore market dynamics
points: Last year's Aero show created very high demand days and a compressed market in Bangalore; this year that big event was absent, though other events supported January-February performance.

March faced occupancy pressure in Bangalore because of war-related cancellations, requiring lower-paying groups to fill demand, resulting in a lesser ADR increase compared to other markets for the quarter.
This was described as a one-off; April onwards Bangalore market is again seeing good increase.

subsections.label: Occupancy vs ADR strategy
points: Occupancy held at 78% for the quarter with room to move average portfolio occupancy from 78% to mid-to-low 80s (5 of 9 hotels already had occupancies in mid-80s in Q4).
Three of nine hotels are already above INR7,500 ADR; others are borderline (some days above, some below); one or two hotels will take longer to breach that threshold.
Strategy is to increase ADR via revenue management (room rate inclusions, value-adds like laundry, complimentary breakfast, complimentary pickup) without compromising occupancy.
Portfolio's strategic locations in key business districts with minimal/low new supply allow maximizing ADR during high-demand periods while maintaining occupancy during compression periods.

subsections.label: Segment mix
points: Business mix breakdown: 50% transient (retail), 25% negotiated/contracted, 15% group, 10% miscellaneous/crew and other business.
Of the 50% retail, 60% (i.e., 30% of overall occupancy) comes from OTAs.

subsections.label: Rebranding and new development
points: Kochi hotel to be upgraded from Four Points by Sheraton brand to Courtyard by Marriott brand in coming quarter, expected to improve ADRs and profitability further; upgrade already in process.

In FY27, will launch Courtyard by Marriott in Chennai, World Trade Center, a 45-key hotel complementing existing presence in the high-demand business district of OMR in Chennai; opening targeted for Q3, expected to take a couple of quarters to stabilize.

subsections.label: Renewable energy adoption
points: Company is actively advancing adoption of renewable energy, currently at 61% with some hotels exceeding 90% usage.
