subsections.label: Gift City positioning
points: Brigade is one of the only few hotels currently in Gift City with a liquor license (only two or three such hotels).
One competing hotel announcement exists with movement on the ground, but it's just starting; no other supply expected in Gift City for at least the next three to four years.
Company plans to invest capex to add two or three more F&B/restaurant options in Gift City to capitalize on being one of the few hotels there (currently only one F&B option).

subsections.label: Portfolio market mix
points: Bangalore hotels average around INR9,000-9,500 per room, while other hotels in tier-2 markets like Mysore, Kochi, and Gift City bring down overall portfolio ADR to about INR7,500.
Goal is to bring all sub-INR7,500 hotels above that threshold to avoid GST impact in coming years.

subsections.label: Gas supply disruption management
points: 4 of the hotels run on PNG and the rest are LPG dependent; during disruptions in March and continuing to some extent, alternative fuel sources and electric induction cooking were used.
Menus were restructured/redefined to take in alternative items; no restaurant was closed and all restaurants performed as per normal schedule.
Gas supply situation has since been restored; alternative arrangements (inductions) now in place across many hotels, so no regular F&B servicing issue exists going forward.
There was no lapse in kitchen operations; no hotel ran out of gas supply despite reduced CNG line supply.

subsections.label: Build vs. acquire strategy
points: Company's strategy has always been to acquire land (buy outright or lease) and then develop, since there are very few players in the hotel construction space — a niche segment where only half a dozen to a dozen players in the country can build hotels at scale.
Company believes its USP is the ability to build efficient hotels on time and within costs, with a positive cost impact compared to the rest of the market.
As a listed entity, more acquisition opportunities are coming; company is open to acquiring assets, though acquiring comes at a much higher cost per key for a builder.

Company weighs pros and cons of getting a hotel to market via acquisition (e.g., refurbish/rebrand to bring to market quicker) versus building from scratch; acquisition opportunities are being explored but no asset has been finalized yet — this remains a key focus for the year.

subsections.label: Recognitions
points: 'By the Blue' restaurant at Grand Mercure Bangalore hotel awarded 'Best Newcomer Hotel Restaurant' at the Food Connoisseurs India Award 2025 (February 2026).
Sheraton Grand Bangalore at Brigade Gateway honored with 'Business Hotel of the Year' at the Satte Awards 2026.
Persian Terrace at Sheraton Grand Bangalore at Brigade Gateway won restaurant serving best 'Middle Eastern cuisine' at the Food Connoisseur India Award 2025 (February 2026).

subsections.label: Acquisition exploration
points: Company is in the market looking at various acquisition options but yet to narrow down on an asset; this is one of the key focus areas for the year.
CSR contribution towards skill development from the corporate office continues as part of community engagement and social responsibility initiatives.

subsections.label: Geopolitical/war impact
points: War/geopolitical disruption led to cancellations worth INR7-8 crores in Q4 FY26 (about 5% of quarter business), concentrated in larger events dependent on foreign travellers and international travel.
Greatest impact seen in March; similar cancellations of INR7-8 crores expected in April-June being offset with domestic business.
Impact reduced international mix from historical 70:30 domestic:international ratio to current 73:27 (domestic:international).

subsections.label: GST 2.0 impact
points: GST 2.0 impacted EBITDA margin by 1.4% in Q4 FY26 and 0.8% for FY26.
GST impact arises on the basis of daily room nights sold below INR7,500 requiring reversal of GST input credit, applicable even in hotels averaging above INR7,500 threshold on some room nights.
Currently around 30% of total revenue comes from room nights selling below INR7,500; this is gradually reducing as ADR increases across hotels.

subsections.label: Gas supply disruption
points: Gas supply issues occurred during last month of March with some continuation, but did not cause major disruption due to use of alternative fuel sources (electric induction) and menu adjustments.
Situation has since been restored.

subsections.label: One-off cost impacts
points: Additional one-time property tax hit and input tax credit that could not be utilized impacted EBITDA margin for the year.

subsections.label: Forward outlook
points: Demand visibility remains robust and management is positive about the year ahead.
As more luxury properties are commissioned through FY29 and beyond, portfolio average ADR is projected to exceed INR10,000 by FY29 and surpass INR14,000 by FY31, nearly double current levels.
EBITDA margin expected to increase once ARR increases, as sub-INR7,500 hotels are brought above that threshold, negating GST impact in coming years.
Once ARRs increase further (occupancy already stable, growth coming from ADR), higher EBITDA margins are expected.

risk_register.note: Led to cancellations worth INR7-8 crores in Q4 FY26 (about 5% of quarter business), concentrated in events dependent on foreign travellers; similar cancellations of INR7-8 crores expected in Apr-Jun; greatest impact seen in March; international mix reduced from historical 70:30 to current 73:27 domestic:international.

risk_register.risk: GST 2.0 impact on margins
risk_register.note: Impacted EBITDA margin by 1.4% in Q4 FY26 and 0.8% for FY26; arises from room nights sold below INR7,500 requiring GST input credit reversal; ~30% of revenue currently from such room nights, gradually reducing as ADR increases.

risk_register.risk: Gas supply disruption (CNG/PNG)
risk_register.note: Disruption during March and partially continuing; managed via alternative fuel sources and electric induction cooking with no restaurant closures; situation has since been restored.

risk_register.risk: One-off cost impacts (input tax credit, property tax)

risk_register.risk: Bangalore market demand compression due to absence of major event (Aero show)
risk_register.note: Absence of last year's Aero show plus March cancellations led to lower-paying groups filling demand and a lesser ADR increase for Bangalore hotels in Q4; described as one-off, with improvement seen from April onwards.

themes.label: Domestic demand resilience
themes.note: Domestic demand remained resilient and anchored growth despite global uncertainties, geopolitical developments, and reduced international travel.

themes.label: Geopolitical/war disruption
themes.note: War conflict led to INR7-8 crore cancellations in Q4 and similar expected in Q1 FY27, mainly impacting F&B and large events dependent on foreign travellers.

themes.label: GST 2.0 margin impact
themes.note: GST 2.0 impacted EBITDA margin by 1.4% in Q4 and 0.8% for FY26, tied to room nights sold below INR7,500 ARR threshold.

themes.label: ADR-led growth and premiumization
themes.note: RevPAR growth driven primarily by ADR growth (7% in Q4) while occupancy held steady; portfolio ADR projected to exceed INR10,000 by FY29 and INR14,000 by FY31.

themes.note: Kochi hotel rebrand to Courtyard by Marriott and new 45-key Courtyard by Marriott in Chennai OMR planned for FY27 to strengthen portfolio.

themes.label: Disciplined capital allocation
themes.note: Planned capex of ~INR3,600 crores funded ~60% via borrowings and remainder via internal accruals expected to exceed INR1,000 crores in coming years.

themes.label: Build vs acquire strategy
themes.note: Company's core strength is building hotels efficiently on time and cost, but is exploring acquisition opportunities as a listed entity, weighing higher per-key cost of acquisitions against speed to market.

key_takeaways: For the quarter, total income grew by 8% year-on-year, led by 7% increase in ARR, and occupancy remained relatively stable resulting in a 6% growth in RevPAR.
EBITDA increased by 13% year-on-year to INR58 crores, translating into an EBITDA margin of 39.7%.
Utilities as a percentage of operating revenues stood at 5% for the quarter and 5.4% for the whole year of FY '26.
Interest costs have reduced due to loan repayments, positively impacting the net profitability.
We are actively advancing adoption of renewable energy, which is currently at 61% with some hotels exceeding 90% usage.
In the coming quarter, we plan to upgrade our hotel at Kochi from a 'Four Points by Sheraton' brand to a 'Courtyard by Marriott' brand.

In FY '27, we will further strengthen the base with the launch of the Courtyard by Marriott in Chennai, World Trade Center, a 45-key hotel that complements our existing presence in high-demand business district of OMR in Chennai.
Our planned capex of approximately INR3,600 crores, of which INR400 crores has already been invested by FY '26, will be funded through a balanced mix of debt and internal accruals.
We project this to exceed INR10,000 for an average ADR by FY '29 and surpass INR14,000 by FY31, nearly double of what it is today.
Looking ahead, demand visibility remains robust and we are positive about the year ahead.

ACE.about: Action Construction Equipment Ltd is engaged in the business of manufacturing and marketing of hydraulic mobile cranes, mobile tower cranes, material handling equipment like forklifts, road construction equipment like backhoe loaders, compactors, motor graders and agriculture equipment like tractors, harvesters, rotavators, etc. It was incorporated in 1995 and concluded its IPO in 2006.[1]

quarters.summary: Q1 FY27 was ACE's best-ever Q1 in terms of revenue and profit, with 19% total income growth and 12bps EBITDA margin expansion, driven by product mix, calibrated pricing actions and operational efficiencies, even as commodity cost inflation (steel, rubber, oil, freight) pressured gross margins. Management continues to withhold full-year FY27 growth/revenue guidance, deferring a formal number to mid-to-end September 2026, citing unpredictability from geopolitical tensions, three rounds of price hikes (~10% cumulative) still working through the system, and monsoon-related seasonal softness, while reiterating confidence in growth from Hydra crane recovery, defense execution, exports, KATO JV and the structural infrastructure growth story.

subsections.label: Margin drivers
points: Continued emphasis on product quality, manufacturing efficiencies, cost optimization and calibrated pricing actions enabled best-ever Q1 performance in revenue and profit.

Gross margin contraction of ~140 bps YoY attributed by CFO Rajan Luthra to commodity price impact — steel prices up nearly 20%, and other inputs like tire, belt, rubber, plastics all rising due to geopolitical tensions.
Company taking necessary actions (price increases) to mitigate commodity cost increase and maintain margins for the full year — not aiming for margin expansion, only recovery of costs.

Some 2-3 months of inventory rolls in the system at vendor end, so price increases have a lag of 1-3 months depending on supplier; full effect of both price hikes and cost inflation expected to largely offset each other by July/August.
Aim for Q2 and possibly Q3 is to maintain and sustain profitability at last year's operating EBITDA level of a little over 15%.

subsections.label: Capital allocation
points: FY27 capex of INR200-250 crores includes INR130-140 crores for land takeover (contracted ~1.5-2 years back), INR40-50 crores for new Plant 9 (defense/new products facility), and INR50-60 crores for upgradation, robotics/automation and routine maintenance capex.

key_figures.label: Small defense orders received in quarter

subsections.label: Demand trends
points: Demand had been very strong till May-June, followed by traditional seasonal slowdown during monsoon, consistent with past years' patterns.

No major supply chain problem experienced so far apart from inflation and cost pressures; faced issues with engine supplier and casting suppliers (castings for engines) in the last ~1 month, but suppliers found ways to overcome, expected to ease further in July.

Growth expected from multiple avenues: recovery in Hydra crane market (previously subdued due to price increase/technological change), growth in construction equipment (road machinery, backhoe, forklift, tower cranes), extra revenue from inflation-led price increases, and execution ramp-up of large defense order starting August.

Company deferring a formal whole-year growth/revenue number until mid-to-end September, partly because it has pushed price increases three times in the first six months of the calendar year (January, May, June) amid weak monsoon-season buying sentiment, creating resistance and unpredictability.

Applying the historical H1 (40-45%)/H2 (55-60%) revenue split ratio, Q2 will be similar to Q1 and better than last year's Q2, allowing analysts to derive an approximate range even without explicit guidance.
Predictability of demand planning has suffered over the last 1-1.5 years due to a sequence of shocks: last year's war, Trump tariffs, and now the Iran war — all disrupting sentiment.

Demand planning process: production planned 3-6 months ahead with monthly fine-tuning; company carries 10-20% extra semi-finished/finished goods inventory per plant per month to cater to upward demand fluctuations, adjusting downward fluctuations in subsequent months.

Monsoon deficiency can cause a swing of 5-7-10% up or down in demand, particularly affecting Tier 2/rural construction and crane demand; effect typically becomes evident in the second half of the same year, specifically Quarter 3.

subsections.label: Cranes, CE & Metal Handling
points: Company sustained growth momentum across all operating segments in the quarter.

Hydra type cranes were subdued last year due to price increase from BS III to BS V emission norm change and technological skepticism among the retail rental segment; this skepticism has now settled over the last 7-8 months and Hydra volumes have started increasing in the last 3-4 months.

Hydra:NG mix expected to revert to ~60:40 (Hydra:NG) this year from last year's ~60:40 in favour of a bit more NG, and over next 1-3 years is expected to stabilize at ~50:50 as new generation cranes are perceived as more stable/safer and industrial users shift toward them.

Realizations expected to rise due to a mix shift toward higher tonnage within both Hydra (18, 20, 25 ton models launched in recent years) and new generation segments, plus price increases from emission norm changes.
Company has been leader in new generation segment for the last 2 years and expects to expand market share in NG segment this year if conditions permit.

Backhoe loader segment seen as a potential fastest-growing segment; a proof-of-concept around financing tie-up with a finance company has been implemented in 3-4 specific pockets, with full clarity expected by July-August; strong export and domestic potential seen for backhoe loaders over the next 3 years.

subsections.label: Realization drivers
points: Realization increase in Q4 FY26 was primarily driven by product mix; price hike in January was only 1-1.5%.

In Q1 FY27, realization increase driven more by price increase effective from May (impact only in June) than by mix; substantial further improvement in average pricing expected in Q2 as May and June price hikes fully reflect.

subsections.label: Tower crane capacity expansion
points: Plan for new tower crane capacity was ready and work was to begin from April, but war unfolding in March delayed the decision; company will wait till September to decide on timing — could start in October or be deferred by another 6 months.

In the interim, company made minor rearrangements and rented a small factory premises close to the existing facility, raising tower crane capacity to about 1,000 cranes, sufficient for current demand scenario.
New tower crane plant location, if pursued, will be about 4-5 km from the existing facility.

subsections.label: Plant 9 (defense facility)
points: New facility under construction, expected to be functional by end of Q3/early Q4 FY27 (around December), dedicated to defense manufacturing of special machines plus a couple of other products currently under design and validation.

This facility is the last meaningful chunk of land within the existing 100-acre complex; after this, the complex will be more or less full, though some further capacity increase possible via modifications.

subsections.label: General capacity investment
points: Company has consistently invested in expanding manufacturing capacity, modernizing facilities and strengthening automation across plants over the past few years, enhancing manufacturing flexibility, product quality and operational efficiency.
Existing capacities and improved manufacturing capabilities position the company to cater to future demand across its product portfolio while maintaining disciplined capital allocation.

subsections.label: Export dynamics
points: Export sales subdued in the quarter due to shipping issues and rising prices; Middle East orders (especially Saudi Arabia) could not be shipped in the last quarter, with some pending since March.
All pending export orders are live and expected to catch up going forward.

subsections.label: Competitive landscape
points: Competitive intensity in the domestic market remains largely unchanged over the last 3-4 months; company has had the same set of players in its segments for a long time.

Biggest current and forward-looking challenge is inflation — making products more expensive and making it difficult and time-consuming to get customers to accept price increases, with some percentage of cost increase not fully recoverable.
Inflation can also depress overall economic growth, as evidenced by leading banks/financial institutions trimming India's GDP forecast.

subsections.label: Government payment risk
points: No major issue observed with contractors receiving payments from government departments/projects; occasional state-government-level delays occur but generally get resolved, viewed as a normal part of being an EPC company/contractor.

subsections.label: Growth driver prioritization
points: Management's ranked growth drivers going forward: (1) inorganic growth and exports, (2) domestic economic growth (India GDP ~6.5-7%) feeding infrastructure/construction demand, and (3) the ACE-KATO JV contributing 2-3 years out.

Additional prospective demand drivers cited: first high-speed rail already under construction with 7 more DPRs under planning; data centers (already contributing 1.5-2% of revenue); energy storage/oil storage facilities for reserve levels; nuclear energy; solar already providing a boost.

subsections.label: KATO Works JV
points: Strategic JV with KATO Works Limited, announced previous quarter, to commence by end of July 2026 — combines ACE's manufacturing strength and domestic market leadership with KATO's globally recognized technology and footprint in heavy crane segment.

JV provides platform to expand domestic presence in truck cranes, crawler cranes and rough terrain cranes, while supporting technology upgradation, localization and export opportunities over medium to long term; strengthens positioning in higher value-added heavy crane segment, complementing existing leadership in pick and carry and tower cranes.
JV to start having some revenue from Q3 FY27; Q3/Q4 will focus on upgrading products (already in process, to be sped up); meaningful revenue from the JV expected only from FY28 onwards.

Existing Indian crane models will remain in production; upgraded models per KATO/Japanese technology standards expected to roll out from Q4 FY27, a continuous process over 1-1.5 years; dedicated KATO models for India and export markets expected to start about 1 year from now.

No royalty on machines made for the Indian market; a 3% royalty on net selling price applies only to KATO-specific design models made in India for export markets (priced nearly double of Indian pricing).
Localization of KATO-based export models targeted at 50-60% within ~2 years of rollout, given expected volume improvements in hydraulic components and other high-value parts.

KATO Japan (a broader construction equipment manufacturer) will also source components/materials from India via ACE, creating an additional revenue stream for ACE tied to localization and local manufacturing.

subsections.label: Inorganic growth
points: Management views inorganic growth and export growth as the two biggest growth drivers going forward, given cash available on the books that needs meaningful deployment.

Company will not acquire a business lacking a competitive moat or the future prospect of 3-4x to 6x possible growth; has identified some opportunities and is working on them, hopeful they will get through.

subsections.label: Defense business development
points: Defense business continuing to progress steadily; company started manufacturing rough terrain forklifts in the current quarter.
Company remains committed to developing specialized products for defense applications and expanding participation in this strategically important sector.

subsections.label: Macro and geopolitical risk
points: Escalating geopolitical tensions in West Asia, volatility in energy markets, firm steel prices, elevated freight costs and inflationary pressures across most industrial commodities have added to cost volatility and supply chain uncertainty for manufacturing businesses worldwide.
India's macroeconomic fundamentals continue to remain strong even amid an unpredictable domestic economy and increasingly uncertain global operating environment.

Company operating in turbulent, geopolitically uncertain times (Iran war escalation, potential further choke points) creating uncertainty in demand forecasting and predictability of business planning.

subsections.label: Commodity/input cost inflation
points: Commodity prices — steel, rubber, oil and derivatives — along with freight costs and currency movements remain elevated, driven by geopolitical developments and energy market fluctuations.

Overall inflation impact on costing estimated in the range of 11-12%, expected to fully settle by July or latest August; company has already pushed ~9-10% price increase and may need another ~2% depending on further volatility.

This is described as the first or second time practically every input material/component across the supply chain has seen price increases simultaneously — a 'massive commodity increase' straining procurement and vendor development teams.

subsections.label: Anti-dumping duty overhang
points: No leads so far on anti-dumping duty notification despite DGTR investigation recommending duty following Ministry of Heavy Industry's push against Chinese/imported crane flooding; Finance Ministry (implementation agency) has not implemented it.

Management's best guess is that non-implementation relates to geopolitical posturing (avoiding appearing close to China) amid last year's American tariff tensions, especially since the DGTR recommendation came just after a prime ministerial visit to China.

Company still sees 'a ray of hope' and continues pursuing the matter, viewing implementation as a win-win for the country's manufacturing capability, import substitution and government revenue via customs duty.

subsections.label: Monsoon/seasonal risk
points: Deficient monsoons can hit Tier 2/rural construction and crane demand by roughly 5-7-10%, though this effect and its evidence typically show up in the second half, particularly Quarter 3.

subsections.label: Supply chain
points: Faced supply issues with engine and casting suppliers (castings for engines) in the last ~1 month, though suppliers found workarounds; expected to ease further in July.

subsections.label: Annual growth guidance timing
points: Company will provide a full-year revenue growth target around mid-to-end September 2026, as previously indicated on the last call; still maintains this timeline.

Reluctant to give a specific growth percentage now due to unpredictable geopolitical environment and because three price increases (Jan, May, June, cumulating to ~10%) are still working through the system amid weak monsoon-season demand.
Historical seasonality (40-45% revenue in H1, 55-60% in H2) can be used to approximate a range even without an explicit number.

subsections.label: Margin outlook
points: Aim is to maintain and sustain FY26's operating EBITDA margin of a little over 15% into Q2 and possibly Q3, not to expand margins.
Price increase and cost inflation effects (both ~11-12%) expected to largely offset each other by July/August, with further price action in August/September contingent on additional cost pain.

subsections.label: Price-hike stickiness
points: If a commodity cycle rolls back within 6-8 months, a portion of the price increase is typically passed back to customers as prudent practice; if the increase persists beyond 6-8 months, industry tendency (including vendors) is not to reverse the price increase.

risk_register.risk: Extended monsoon / seasonal slowdown

key_takeaways: Company registered its best-ever Q1 performance with continued focus on disciplined execution, operational excellence and maintaining a healthy balance between growth and profitability.
On a yearly stand-alone basis, total income grew by around 19% to INR836 crores, with EBITDA margin expansion of 12 basis points to 20.40%; EBITDA increased by 19.66% to INR170.58 crores.
PBT grew by 23.81% to approximately INR156.79 crores and PAT grew by 22.47% to INR118.59 crores.
Cranes, Construction Equipment and Metal Handling segment registered consolidated revenue of INR738.37 crores, an increase of around 22% YoY, with volumes growing 17.25% YoY.

The strategic joint venture with KATO Works Limited will commence by end of July, marking an important milestone combining ACE's manufacturing strength and domestic leadership with KATO's globally recognized heavy crane technology.
Defense business continues to progress steadily, with rough terrain forklift manufacturing started in the current quarter.

Commodity prices remain volatile due to geopolitical developments; company is protecting profitability through operational efficiencies and calibrated pricing actions rather than relying solely on price increases.
Company continues to defer giving a whole-year revenue growth guidance, planning to provide a number by mid-to-end September 2026.

quarters.summary: FY26 saw best-ever Q4 revenue with sustained margins despite West Asia geopolitical crisis, crude price escalation and rupee depreciation; management expects a steady start to FY27 with continued price hikes to offset steel-led input cost inflation, while withholding formal annual guidance until mid-Q2 FY27 given macro uncertainty; medium-term FY29/FY30 revenue target of INR6,000-6,200 crores reiterated with contribution from KATO JV, defense and exports.

subsections.label: Margin drivers
points: Sustained operating margins amid geopolitical headwinds delivered best-ever Q4 revenue performance.
Company will continue to dynamically manage EBITDA margins broadly in the existing range via savings, judicious and calibrated pricing actions.
Company hopeful of sustaining EBITDA margin (excluding other income) in the range of 15% to 16%, keeping a keen eye on costs and taking calibrated price actions.
Competition margins at segment level are estimated at 8-9% vs ACE's 18-19%, giving room for price increases without going into loss.

subsections.label: Other income / mark-to-market
points: Negative other income in the quarter was due to mark-to-market losses on surplus cash investments; not an actuarial loss.
Market was negative in March (last quarter), partly recovered in April as markets moved upward.
Management hopeful other income recovers to INR20-35 crores range within the current quarter if market remains static or improves.

subsections.label: Other expenses
points: Despite volumes declining 18-20%, other expenses remained flattish/declined only 2-3% because most other expenses are of fixed nature with no direct correlation to revenue.

subsections.label: Impairment / credit losses
points: Impairment losses on financial assets represent prudent expected-credit-loss provisioning for slightly delayed receivables, not an actual realized loss.

subsections.label: Noncurrent investments
points: Noncurrent investment classification (INR700-750 crores) is an accounting definition (maturity >1 year), though most investments have 1-3 year tenure and are secured, listed and liquid, convertible to cash on short notice.
Surplus cash is being deployed into unlisted shares/debentures and bonds rather than remaining redundant.

subsections.label: Capital efficiency
points: ROCE declined from ~40% to 32% over the last two years due to idle surplus cash; company intends to deploy this productively to lift ROCE back up, and does not intend for ROCE to fall below 30-33%.
Capex will be timed to ensure investment-to-turnover ratio of ~8-10x is maintained, protecting ROCE/ROE before any capital expenditure decision.

subsections.label: Demand trends
points: Demand conditions remained stable across the market during the quarter except in March, supported by conducive macro environment and fiscal/monetary measures through the year.
Lower headline inflation for a significant part of the period supported demand in Q4.
Tower crane demand as of the call (nearly end of May) is 'full throttle'; other products also showing reasonable growth expected in Q1.
Q1 growth expected to look strong partly due to low base effect from last year (15-20% or slightly more growth possible in crane volumes in Q1).
Things started improving end of Q3 last year and continued into Q4.

subsections.label: Financing mix of customer base
points: Approximately 85-90% of cranes and construction equipment sold are financed through NBFCs and banks.
Revenue split is roughly 50-50 between rental players and direct end users (EPC, manufacturing, logistics, engineering industries).

key_figures.label: Cranes, metal handling & construction equipment income

subsections.label: Cranes/Construction Equipment segment dynamics
points: FY26 was a year of normalization for the industry following exceptionally strong FY25, which benefited from significant prebuying ahead of emission norm transition.
H1 FY26 demand impacted by emission norm transition, geopolitical situations, extended monsoon and slower project mobilization.
Industry conditions improved progressively during the year with demand momentum returning in Q4 FY26.
Market moving toward higher tonnage machines (hydra type and new generation), raising realization per piece.

Old-generation (hydra type) cranes, ~60% of the crane market, faced skepticism/fear due to transition from Tier 3 to Tier 5 electronic standards and 12-15% price increase; this segment shrank last year but has come back on track since January-February.
Q4 revenue could have been INR40-50 crores higher but export shipments meant for Middle East got stuck due to the war; also some tactical delivery moderation domestically in March.
Expect handsome growth in backhoe loaders/construction equipment, reasonable growth in material handling (forklifts), and increase in crane numbers (hydra + new generation) going forward.
New generation cranes gaining share due to special safety features, IoT- and AI-enabled features along with the ACE Live app.

subsections.label: Agri division
points: Agri division registered 9% revenue growth with margins around 1%.

subsections.label: Tower cranes
points: Tower crane volumes were slightly lower than 700, at ~680-690 units in FY26, versus capacity of 950-1,000 units.
Order books for tower cranes are full; real estate market has been good recently.
Slows slightly during monsoon season (typically mid-to-end June) but that hadn't happened yet as of the call.
Company confident of doing more tower crane numbers than last year, though precise guidance withheld until mid Q2.

subsections.label: Other/miscellaneous export revenue
points: New 'Others' segment line item (INR76.55 crores) represents revenue from miscellaneous exports sold outside India, now significant enough to be reported separately per auditors.
Volume for this miscellaneous export revenue cannot be segregated as it comprises mixed items including some construction equipment; it is a value-based figure, not a volume-based one.

subsections.label: Defense business
points: Received required approvals (NOC) for a large rough terrain forklift/telehandler order; execution expected to start next quarter.

Working on QRSAM (Quick Response Surface to Air Missile) program, building protos for two integration companies; company involved only in material handling (loading/unloading of ammunition), not firing systems; expects huge requirement over next 2-3 years.

subsections.label: JCB backhoe segment initiative
points: Work in progress on something related to the JCB backhoe segment; proof of concept expected in June or July, which should help increase numbers reasonably within this year and improve further going forward.

subsections.label: Capacity expansion completed
points: Company successfully completed planned FY26 capex, expanding capacities and enhancing operational capabilities through modernization and automation, aimed at strengthening quality/capabilities and improving market competitiveness.
Blended capacity utilization at ~60% provides headroom to capitalize on any immediate demand uptick.

subsections.label: FY27 capex plan
points: INR130-135 crores to complete land parcel contracted ~1-1.5 years back, for future expansion.
New plant within existing complex specifically for defense equipment and new products (envisaged over next 1-2 years): INR40-50 crores.
Maintenance capex of INR20-25 crores.
Total FY27 capex (ex new tower crane factory) expected to be close to INR200 crores.

subsections.label: New tower crane factory
points: Envisaged capex upwards of INR400 crores; currently have capacity so will wait and watch for demand momentum before committing.
May start working on it within this year but is need-based; if it starts this year, ~INR150 crores may be spent this year with balance next year.
Would require at least 12-18 months (more towards 18) to set up, as it will be highly autonomous.

subsections.label: Competitive landscape - pick & carry vs slew cranes
points: Chinese manufacturers do not make pick and carry cranes (generally below 30-35 ton capacity); they focus on slew/heavy cranes (40-50 tons and bigger, 360-degree slew with outriggers).

This is due to historical country-specific usage patterns: Chinese market traditionally used truck-mounted slew cranes even for smaller tonnages, while pick and carry cranes are the mainstay in India, Australia and Italy.
Fuel efficiency is not a key purchase parameter for cranes/construction equipment; the main parameters are capacity/tonnage for cranes and aggregate volume handling capability for other machines.

subsections.label: Customer segments
points: Customer base is highly diversified across infrastructure, construction, industrial units, engineering units and shipbuilding yards.
Company supplies to shipbuilding yards across the country (e.g., Goa) including recent supply of three special tower cranes to a shipbuilding yard for use in ship-building and material placement.

Shipbuilding-related revenue contribution is estimated at around 1% or less of tower crane sales (roughly 10-20 of ~700 units annually go to bigger shipbuilding-related units), with similar estimate for pick-and-carry cranes.

subsections.label: Competitive positioning vs Chinese players
points: Chinese players in heavy crane segment underselling ACE/competition by at least 25-30%, aided by lower costs even after 7.5% customs duty, freight from China, and >10% rupee depreciation.
Chinese sellers also offer 1-2 year (sometimes up to 3 year) credit terms, providing a further 7-8% annual benefit to customers.
ACE's own margin (18-19%) is much higher than estimated segment-level competitor margins (8-9%), giving room to raise prices without going into losses.

subsections.label: KATO Works JV
points: Finalized a 50-50 joint venture between ACE and KATO Works Company, Japan, combining ACE's manufacturing/distribution capabilities with KATO's globally recognized heavy crane technology leadership.
JV will serve as a dedicated platform for truck cranes, crawler cranes and rough terrain cranes, strengthening presence in the heavy crane segment.
Partnership positions ACE to accelerate technology upgradation, deepen localization, expand export opportunities, and participate in India's infrastructure/industrial capex cycle.
Existing ACE machines (currently limited tonnage) will be upgraded with Japanese technology to become world class; higher tonnage/bigger crane models will be developed and evolved within the JV.
Specific export models identical to KATO Japan production will be made in India for KATO to distribute globally; main profitability expected to lie here 2-3 years down the line.
As a side agreement, ACE will export components/materials/commodities to KATO Japan (which also makes excavators and other construction equipment), adding an additional revenue stream.
Customers willing to pay 15-20% premium for the KATO-branded/Japanese product, aiding pricing power against Chinese competition.

Global market for these cranes is much bigger than India; Chinese pricing in other countries competing with European/Japanese/American manufacturers is 50-150% higher than Indian prices, suggesting fair competition potential for KATO-ACE exports.
Current heavy crane competition remains the same 3-4 Chinese companies that built a strong Indian foothold over 10-15 years via pricing/credit term advantages.

subsections.label: FY29/FY30 revenue guidance rationale
points: To achieve the INR6,000-6,200 crore target, company needs to add roughly INR800-1,000 crores in revenue over next 3 years (or INR700-800 crores/year over 4 years).
KATO JV revenue (targeted ~INR300 crores, possibly a 'bonus' above that) is included within this overall guidance.

Drivers for the target include: recovery in cranes/CE volumes (after last year's drop), improved product/price mix toward higher models, inflation-led revenue uplift, and increasing defense and export business (target 10-15%, more towards 15%, combined defense+export contribution).
Company believes it is on track to attain INR6,000 crores+ by FY29 or latest FY30, with maybe a year of variance.

subsections.label: Geopolitical & macro headwinds
points: Escalation of West Asia crisis led to sharp rise in crude and crude-linked commodity prices, supply side disruptions and continued rupee depreciation.
Company remains mindful of evolving geopolitical environment, which could lead to temporary supply chain disruptions, demand-side hyperinflation and input cost volatility.
Machines made by ACE are capital goods, so the business is typically 'first hit, last out' in economic downturns.

Management does not believe 'the worst is behind us' — this year began with one of the most turbulent factors, crude oil prices, following last year's turbulence from emission norms, India-Pakistan geopolitical operations (Sindoor), American tariffs, and extended monsoon.
India imports more than 80% of its crude oil, making the country more exposed than others to this turbulence.
Rupee depreciation, while a headwind, is also seen as eventually helping export competitiveness.

subsections.label: Input cost inflation
points: Steel, the biggest input material, remains volatile and at elevated levels; steel is ~65% of cost and has risen 20-22% since Jan 1, implying at least ~12% price increase needed to compensate.
Overall cost increase could be in the range of 11-14%.
There is generally a 2-3 month lag between inflation occurring and its full pass-through due to inventories and orders already in process.

subsections.label: Antidumping duty uncertainty
points: DGTR ordered antidumping duties (25-52%) on Chinese crane manufacturers in September last year, but the order has not been notified/implemented by the Ministry of Finance as of the call.

There is normally a 90-day time bar for notification (would have been due by December), so the order may have become time-barred, though government has implemented such orders late in the past too; future fate unknown.

One or two of the three main Chinese importers have started assembling/localizing some models in India due to fear of antidumping duties, raising their costs by an estimated 8-10%, which should make ACE more competitive.
Newspaper headlines suggest government intent to curb nonessential imports, which could support future antidumping implementation.

subsections.label: Other income volatility
points: Mark-to-market provisioning on surplus cash investments caused a subdued/negative other income in Q4 due to market weakness in March, partially recovered in April.

subsections.label: Annual guidance timing
points: Company has refrained from giving formal annual guidance for FY27 so far and plans to provide it middle-to-end of Q2 FY27, once demand/pricing/economic trajectory becomes clearer.
Q1 FY27 is looking like a good quarter based on early trends (nearly 2 months into the quarter as of the call).
Uncertain how Q2/Q3 will pan out given geopolitical uncertainty, trade deficit imbalance and rupee depreciation.

subsections.label: Pricing action plan
points: Company has already raised prices: 1-1.5% in January 2026, ~4% (or slightly more) on May 1 2026, and plans another 5% from June 1 2026, bringing cumulative increase to 9-10%.
Additional 3-4% price increase possible later in Q2 depending on how costs settle, given overall cost increase estimated at 11-14%.
Company's competitors have also raised prices in response to the same input cost pressures across steel, rubber, plastic, copper, oils, and paints.

subsections.label: Margin outlook
points: Company aims to keep EBITDA margin (ex other income) in 15-16% range and will take calibrated price actions to protect this.

Management believes expanding margins further beyond current healthy levels (15-16% ex other income, 17-18% including other income) would be detrimental to market share, so satisfied with current profile.

subsections.label: Segment-level growth outlook
points: Expect handsome growth in backhoe loaders/construction equipment and reasonable growth in material handling (forklifts).
Expect increase in crane numbers (hydra + new generation) as skepticism around new emission-norm hydra cranes eases.
Additional revenue expected from defense (INR575 crore order book) and exports; inflation-led price increases will also add to revenue.

subsections.label: Market share outlook
points: Difficult to project market share gains precisely in current hyperinflation scenario; primary focus is retaining customers at improved pricing to offset inflation, but recent product feature additions (safety, IoT/AI features, ACE Live app) may support some market share gains.
All competitors are smaller than ACE, and all players are believed to be struggling similarly in the current environment.

themes.label: Demand recovery in cranes/CE
themes.note: Demand momentum returned in Q4 FY26 after H1 disruption from emission norm transition; hydra crane skepticism easing since Jan-Feb, tower crane order books full.

key_takeaways: On a standalone basis, we have achieved a total income of INR3,395 crores in this fiscal, which is more or less flattish. Our EBITDA margin for the year expanded by 81 basis points to 18.33% from 17.52% last year.
In absolute terms, EBITDA grew by around 4% to INR622.36 crores as against INR599 crores in the preceding year.
The total income stood at INR1,021 crores for the quarter, which is up 15% sequentially and grew by about 5.58% on a year-on-year basis.

We continue to be debt-free with sufficient availability of liquidity for the future. The Board of Directors has recommended a final dividend of 100%, that is INR2 per share for the year ended 31st March 2026.

We are pleased to announce the finalization of a 50-50 joint venture between Action Construction Equipment Limited and KATO Works Company, Japan, bringing together ACE's strong manufacturing and distribution capabilities with KATO'S globally recognized leadership in heavy crane technology.

Our blended capacity utilization for cranes, metal handling and construction equipment stands at around 60%, which provides us with enough headroom to capitalize on any immediate demand uptick in the future.

Steel, which is our biggest input material, remains volatile and at elevated levels. We will continue to look for all levers like savings, judicious and calibrated pricing actions whilst maintaining right growth equation to protect and sustain our business model.
We will continue to dynamically manage our EBITDA margins broadly in the existing range.

UFBL.about: Incorporated in 2006, Barbeque Nation Hospitality Ltd is in the business of operating a casual dining restaurant chain. [1]

quarters.summary: Q1 FY27 was described as the strongest operating quarter in recent years, with consolidated revenue growing 43.4% YoY to INR426 crores, SSSG of 28.7% and pre-Ind AS adjusted operating EBITDA margin at 8.1% (up 152% YoY). Management expects SSSG to moderate through FY27 due to a higher base (mathematical, not demand-related), continues to target 300 restaurants by FY27 (funded largely via internal accruals), and expects margin levers (gross margin recovery, mature ROM improvement, new-store cohort maturity, back-end cost leverage) to keep improving profitability, while flagging Middle East geopolitical/inflation pressure on the International segment.

subsections.label: Margin drivers
points: Pre-Ind AS adjusted operating EBITDA margin improvement reflects operating leverage from investments made in the previous year.
Barbeque Nation India gross margin improvement reflects beginning of recovery from value-led investments observed in Q4 FY26, combined with procurement and scale benefits.
International segment gross margin was softer due to Middle East crisis-related inflation impact.
Premium CDR gross margins have been steady and at healthy levels.

Mature portfolio ROM margin expansion is despite lower gross margin YoY, higher marketing spend, inflationary pressures from energy and manpower cost, and a ~2 percentage point increase in delivery mix share versus last year.

New restaurant portfolio ROM improvement (6%) is the highest in recent quarters, driven largely by Barbeque Nation expansion (faster payback) in both India and internationally; drag from new portfolio expected to reduce over time.
Back-end cost operating leverage improved as revenue scaled, reversing the prior quarter's step-up from investments in culinary, marketing, digital and central capabilities.

Four factors explain the gap between the ideal (~20%) and actual (16.2%) mature ROM: (1) ~2pp YoY gross margin decline, (2) ~1pp higher marketing spend versus last year (combined ~3pp), (3) ~2pp shift in dine-in/delivery mix causing ~60bps impact due to delivery's ~30% incremental cost of commissions and packaging, and (4) energy/fuel and minimum-wage-driven manpower inflation causing ~140-150bps impact; combined drag of ~5 percentage points.

Management does not view 18% as a hard cap on mature portfolio margin; believes businesses go through cycles and favorable cycle gains (e.g., sequential Q4-Q1 gross margin improvement) can further help.

Corporate overhead growth of 32% YoY driven by continued back-end investments: new Chief Culinary Officer joining, ~4 senior culinary hires from 5-star hotels (avg. ~20 years experience), regional culinary spocs created (previously only had ops spocs), beefed-up marketing/brand/digital teams, and strengthened core tech/digital team for app and website.
Right benchmark for back-end cost trend is Q4 FY26 vs Q1 FY27; only variance is April increments; otherwise considered a normalized level.

subsections.label: Balance sheet & capital allocation
points: Net debt increased marginally due to capex investment and ongoing expansion pipeline.
Capital allocation discipline unchanged; expansion to continue funded largely via internal accruals, with borrowings kept at prudent levels relative to business profile.

subsections.label: Revenue growth composition
points: Growth continues to be entirely volume led; no price increase taken during Q1.
Average per-cover spend changes reflect business segment mix, daypart/session mix, and value-led initiatives started from Q2 FY26.
Entire revenue growth driven by more walk-ins; dine-in volume grew ~63% while revenue grew ~43%, implying a decline in average price points which has since stabilized (similar to Q4 FY26 levels).

subsections.label: Barbeque Nation India performance drivers
points: Every metric was higher than the strong Q4 FY26 levels.

Strategic interventions scaling meaningfully: value-led campaigns during weaker dayparts, food-led occasions created, Big Buffet format in Tier 1/Tier 2 markets, and sustained investment in captive digital engagement.
Captive digital ecosystem is a structural feature deepening further in Q1 FY27.

subsections.label: International performance drivers
points: Strong performance delivered despite ongoing Middle East geopolitical situation, reflecting operational discipline and execution quality on the ground.
International continues to operate with the strongest unit economics in the portfolio.

Q1 restaurant operating margin came in slightly softer than typical levels mainly due to higher food inflation for a large part of input categories, linked to the ongoing geopolitical crisis; management taking efforts to reduce this impact and believes short-term margin impact will correct over time as situation normalizes.
Continued focus on building volume-led growth in international business also.

subsections.label: Premium CDR performance drivers
points: Ended quarter with same total network size after 1 addition and 1 closure.
Q4 FY26 cohort of new restaurants progressively maturing through FY27, expected to lift segment restaurant operating margin further in the year.

Historically takes ~18-24 months for premium CDR restaurants to mature; South-region restaurants (e.g., Chennai, Bangalore) mature faster than newer territories like Mumbai and Delhi, entered 4-5 quarters back.

subsections.label: Cross-segment observation
points: Third consecutive quarter of every segment and every channel growing at healthy double-digit rate simultaneously.
Barbeque Nation remains anchor growth engine; international operations continue to scale profitably; premium casual dining brands deliver healthy growth while maintaining robust margins.

subsections.label: Delivery business strategy
points: Three delivery brands operated: Barbeque Nation (starters/tikkas), BBQ (meals/bowls), Dum Safar (biryani).
Value SKUs launched across all platforms have performed extremely well in most restaurants.
Daypart-specific campaigns run for underperforming sessions, e.g., 'Bachelor Biryani' in Dum Safar performs well during weekday lunch, priced from INR129 (veg) up to ~INR250 (non-veg).
Increased marketing spend on platforms to drive delivery; dine-in-focused marketing also has a 'double impact' driving delivery via brand recall, given 7-8 years of delivery track record.

Delivery margins are better on an absolute and contribution margin basis, though flow-through to growth is lower due to higher marketing spend, slightly higher food cost, packaging cost and commissions.
Dine-in remains the core, captive growth model; delivery is non-captive (dependent on aggregators) but pursued as long as it is incremental and margin accretive.

subsections.label: Customer repeat/new mix
points: Repeat rates historically strong; number of days for repeat customer return is shrinking.
Ratio of new vs repeat customers is shifting slightly in favor of new customers during this intervention period, adding to overall pipeline for future repeat business.
Repeat business metric tracked via mobile number captured per bill (avg 4.3 pax per bill, one mobile number per bill).

Minimum population served by Big Buffet model
Number of restaurants in newer smaller format

subsections.label: Big Buffet market expansion
points: Model has been taken to markets with population as low as 3 lakh people, using a mix of exclusively Big Buffet or a combination of Big Buffet and regular buffet depending on market.
Based on ~6 quarters of data, current brand scale supports an estimated ~600-restaurant potential for Barbeque Nation India, up from a prior perceived cap of 400-450.

Increasing penetration within existing cities without deteriorating first-restaurant economics; example cited is Visakhapatnam, which grew from 1 restaurant 3 years ago to 4 currently operating restaurants (with a fifth under discussion), after opening 2 more, closing 1, then opening 2 more.
Not concerned about availability of trade areas to open new stores given Barbeque India's current base of only 210 restaurants relative to the larger opportunity.

subsections.label: Format efficiency
points: Restaurant format size reduced from 4,500 sq ft to 3,500 sq ft for last ~40 restaurants, achieving improved slotting and demand management while maintaining among the highest revenue per restaurant.

subsections.label: Network pipeline
points: 15 restaurants under construction as of the call date, expected to operationalize through Q2 and Q3 FY27.
New store pipeline described as healthy; FY27 expansion trajectory considered well on track.

Investments continuing in business development, projects, and legal teams to support expansion; pace could accelerate if a good site at preferred rental terms becomes available, without holding back investment.

subsections.label: Geographic contribution
points: Every business segment, every channel and every geography contributed to growth in the quarter, reflecting broad-based, structural improvement rather than isolated factors.

subsections.label: Middle East geopolitical and inflation risk
points: Ongoing Middle East geopolitical situation has caused higher food inflation for a large part of International segment's input categories, with commodity prices in some cases up ~30-40%.
International gross margin was lower by around 3 percentage points due to this inflation.
Management believes short-term margin impact will correct over time as the situation normalizes; efforts underway to reduce impact.

subsections.label: Manpower/service risk
points: A blip in service metrics occurred in April due to a manpower crisis when workers from various industries moved back to East India for election reasons; guest scores have improved over the last 3 months since then.

subsections.label: Reputational/quality risk
points: A food blogger video raised quality concerns about a product; management stated it cannot comment on the blogger's own lab testing methodology.

Company follows FSSAI guidelines with a ~30-person internal audit team auditing all restaurants monthly on FSSAI points (exceeding the annual regulatory requirement), and conducts NABL-accredited lab testing twice yearly as per FSSAI norms; products found within appropriate limits.

subsections.label: Base effect risk to SSSG
points: Management flagged that the exceptionally strong SSSG this quarter creates a higher base, and reported growth rates will moderate/neutralize as the year progresses — described as a mathematical consequence of stronger comparatives rather than a change in underlying consumer demand.
Comparable base tightens meaningfully further into FY27 as Q3 and Q4 lap the strongest quarters of FY26.

subsections.label: Inflation risk (general)
points: Higher inflationary pressures noted from energy/fuel costs and manpower costs (minimum wage changes), contributing to margin drag alongside gross margin and mix factors.

subsections.label: SSSG outlook
points: SSSG expected to moderate through FY27 due to a tightening comparable base, especially as Q3/Q4 lap the strongest FY26 quarters; this is characterized as mathematics, not a change in demand.
Management prefers not to give a specific full-year SSSG number, focusing instead on volume growth, captive customer engagement, and operating leverage as the drivers, with SSSG as an outcome.

subsections.label: Margin outlook
points: FY27 approach is to continue building on unit economics improvement via: gross margin recovery in India, mature portfolio ROM improvement, new store cohort margin improvement, and back-end cost operating leverage — each considered a directional lever expected to continue delivering through the year.

Management declined to commit to a specific double-digit EBITDA margin target, preferring to track the underlying margin levers (gross margin recovery, mature ROM expansion, new store maturity, back-end cost leverage) and treat margin as an outcome of these levers moving in the right direction.

subsections.label: Network expansion outlook
points: Company remains committed to reaching 300 restaurants by FY27 and building the portfolio from there.
Pace of expansion will remain disciplined and calibrated; will not chase a store-count target at the cost of underwriting discipline.
Could accelerate expansion if favorable sites at right rentals are available given expanded TAM view and strong unit economics.

subsections.label: Capital allocation outlook
points: Priorities remain unchanged: continue funding expansion largely via internal accruals and continue investing in the multi-engine (Barbeque Nation, International, Premium CDR) portfolio.

subsections.label: Gross margin outlook
points: Current gross margin band of ~66-67% considered a good operating band; expected to move directionally better over time, driven by India gross margin recovery, though some reversal (e.g., International, segment mix shift toward faster-growing lower-margin Barbeque India) may not fully reverse.
Management not concerned about mix-driven gross margin dilution as long as flow-through to restaurant operating margin and absolute EBITDA remains strong.

subsections.label: AOV/pricing outlook
points: No price hike taken in Q1 despite inflation; a selective, unit-level price hike could be considered once volumes stabilize on a larger base, but not at the cost of volume growth momentum.

guidance_ledger.statement: SSSG will moderate/neutralize moderately as the year progresses due to a tightening comparable base (Q3/Q4 FY27 lapping strongest FY26 quarters); framed as mathematics rather than demand change; no specific full-year number given, focus remains on volume growth.
Committed to reaching 300 restaurants by FY27, building portfolio from there with disciplined, calibrated pace.
At current scale, Barbeque Nation India brand can support around 600-odd restaurants, up from prior view of ~400-450.
Targeting 40 new restaurant additions in FY27 (vs ~35 in FY26) to reach 300 target.
Full-year capex guided at around INR140 crores, of which INR120 crores towards new outlet openings and INR20 crores towards maintenance and ancillary capex.

guidance_ledger.metric: Pre-Ind AS adjusted operating EBITDA margin
guidance_ledger.statement: Continue building on unit economics improvement via gross margin recovery, mature ROM improvement, new store cohort maturity and back-end cost leverage; margin viewed as an outcome of these levers rather than a specific target number (management declined to commit to a specific double-digit margin target).

Current gross margin band of ~66-67% is a good operating band expected to move directionally better over time; some reversal in India but mix shift towards faster-growing Barbeque India may structurally keep consolidated gross margin lower — management not concerned as long as flow-through to ROM/EBITDA remains strong.
Net debt moved marginally up from INR102 crores (FY26 end) to INR106 crores (Q1 FY27 end) due to capex investment and ongoing pipeline.
Expansion to continue funded largely through internal accruals; borrowings kept at prudent levels relative to business profile; unchanged priorities.
No price hikes taken despite inflation; selective, unit-level price hikes possible once volumes stabilize on larger base, but not at expense of volume growth momentum.
Q4 FY26 cohort of new premium CDR restaurants progressively maturing through FY27, expected to lift segment ROM further as the year progresses.
Short-term margin impact from Middle East inflation expected to correct over time as the geopolitical situation normalizes.
Mature portfolio ROM, approximately 16% on H2 FY26 basis, will move to 17% to 18%.
New store drag will stabilize at 1.5% to 1.8% as FY26 cohort matures.
Consolidated ROM expected at approximately 15.5% to 16.5%.
Back-end costs will compress to 6.5% of revenue as scale benefits compound; further down to 6% over the longer term.
Assuming ~12-13% store expansion and double-digit SSSG, reasonable to assume 22% to 25% revenue growth this year on a full year basis.
Internal aim is to maintain international SSSG at around mid-single-digit numbers.
Internal aim to maintain premium CDR SSSG at a similar range of mid-single digits as done in the past.
On a blended basis, internal aim is to be at early double-digit numbers.

guidance_ledger.metric: Salt and Toscano (Premium CDR) store additions
guidance_ledger.statement: Internal aim is around 5 restaurant additions for Salt and Toscano in FY27.

guidance_ledger.metric: Salt and Toscano (Premium CDR) store additions
guidance_ledger.statement: FY28 additions can be anywhere between 5 to 12 (later refined to current range of around 5 to 10).
Planning to add 100 to 125 restaurants cumulatively over the next 3 years (approximately 40-45 stores per year).
Not making new acquisitions; not entering new brand categories that could dilute portfolio focus; sticking to existing portfolio.

guidance_ledger.metric: AOV / average per cover realization trend
guidance_ledger.statement: AOV mix-driven decline trend may continue for 2 more quarters and after that will automatically settle down; new levels expected to be similar to previous two quarters, not materially lower.

risk_register.risk: Middle East geopolitical crisis / input cost inflation impacting International segment
risk_register.note: Higher food inflation for large part of input categories, commodity prices up ~30-40% in some cases, ~3 percentage point drag on International gross margin; International ROM came in slightly softer than typical levels.

risk_register.risk: Manpower crisis / labor shortage
risk_register.note: April blip in service due to manpower crisis (workers moving back to East India for elections); guest scores have improved over last 3 months since resolution.

risk_register.risk: Reputational risk from food quality/service criticism (blogger video, customer reviews)
risk_register.note: Recent food blogger video raised quality concerns; management cannot verify blogger's lab methodology but cites internal FSSAI-compliant audits (30-person team, monthly reviews) and biannual NABL-accredited lab testing showing products within limits.

risk_register.risk: Higher base effect moderating reported SSSG growth
risk_register.note: Strong Q1 FY27 SSSG creates a higher base; comparable base tightens further into FY27 as Q3/Q4 lap strongest FY26 quarters, expected to mathematically lower reported growth rates.

risk_register.risk: General inflation (energy, fuel, manpower/minimum wage)
risk_register.note: Contributed ~140-150 bps drag to mature ROM in Q1 FY27 alongside gross margin and mix factors.

risk_register.risk: Delivery mix shift raising costs
risk_register.note: ~2 percentage point increase in delivery mix versus last year added ~60 bps drag to mature ROM due to higher commissions/packaging costs.

risk_register.risk: Input cost inflation, particularly in Middle East business linked to West Asia crisis
risk_register.note: Contributed to ~300 bps gross margin compression in Q4 FY26; broader inflationary cycle expected on raw material and utilities/petroleum, though FY27 margin guidance is stated to be net of these pressures.

risk_register.risk: Middle East geopolitical/macro uncertainty
risk_register.note: 2 of ~8 international restaurants (Bahrain, Dubai) impacted; difficult to predict outcome, though month-on-month improvement seen in April/May vs March; company pausing new store signings there for last 3 months.

risk_register.risk: New store margin drag from heavy expansion pace
risk_register.note: Q4 FY26 was heaviest new-store opening quarter in company history, increasing drag on mature ROM from 120 bps to 180 bps YoY; expected to narrow as FY26 cohort matures over FY27 (12-24 month ramp-up).

risk_register.risk: Past execution risk in Tier 2/Tier 3 market expansion
risk_register.note: FY23 saw some restaurant closures in Tier 2/3 markets; management believes recent operating model improvements would have helped avoid some of those closures and are now incorporated into planning.

risk_register.risk: Premium CDR new-store margin compression in non-home markets
risk_register.note: New Premium CDR stores in Mumbai and Delhi (non-home markets) show compressed margins versus mature portfolio; expected to take time to ramp up, with focus this year on bringing them to mature margin levels.

themes.label: Demand recovery / SSSG inflection
themes.note: Consolidated SSSG accelerated to 28.7% in Q1 FY27 from 14.4% in Q4 FY26, continuing an inflection trajectory (Q3 FY26 ~8%, Q4 ~14.5%, Q1 FY27 ~28%).

themes.label: Multi-engine portfolio validation
themes.note: Every business segment, channel and geography contributed to growth for the third consecutive quarter, with Barbeque Nation, International and Premium CDR all delivering healthy double-digit growth.

themes.label: Captive demand moat
themes.note: ~90% of dining volumes continue to come from captive channels (app, website, call center, walk-ins); captive digital ecosystem contribution rose to 65% of Barbeque India dine-in transactions from ~61% in Q4 FY26, with MAUs up ~60% YoY to ~1.4 million.

themes.label: Gross margin / value-led volume trade-off
themes.note: Consolidated gross margin lower YoY due to value-led investments and inflation, but restaurant operating margin and EBITDA margin still expanded, reflecting management's stated preference for absolute profitability flow-through over headline gross margin.

themes.label: Network expansion pace
themes.note: 266 restaurants at quarter end with 5 additions and 15 under construction; FY27 target of 300 restaurants reiterated, with a newly expanded Barbeque India TAM view of ~600 restaurants (up from 400-450 previously).

themes.label: Margin expansion pathway to double digits
themes.note: Pre-Ind AS adjusted operating EBITDA margin rose to 8.1% (+350bps YoY, +260bps sequentially), driven by gross margin recovery, mature ROM improvement, new-store cohort maturity and back-end cost leverage, though management declined to commit to a specific double-digit target.

themes.label: Middle East macro uncertainty
themes.note: Middle East geopolitical situation continues to drive input cost inflation (commodity prices up 30-40% in some cases) causing a ~3pp International gross margin drag, though management expects normalization over time.

key_takeaways: Consolidated same-store sales growth for the quarter was 28.7%.
Consolidated revenue grew 43.4% year-on-year to INR426 crores.
Dine-in transaction volumes increased by 63.5%, accelerating further from strong momentum we witnessed in the previous quarters.
Our delivery business also continued its excellent trajectory growing 62% year-on-year.
Pre-Ind AS adjusted operating EBITDA margin improved to 8.1%, reflecting a year-on-year growth of 152%.
Barbeque Nation India delivered same-store sales growth of 33.5% supported by dine-in transaction growth of 68.6%.
Our international business continued its strong performance with revenue growth of 46.6% and same-store sales growth of 8.5%.
Our premium casual dining restaurant business delivered revenue growth of 36% with same-store sales growth of 13.6%, while continuing to maintain healthy restaurant operating margins.
Our mature restaurant operating margin reached 16.2% during the quarter, demonstrating that we are not pursuing growth at expense of return.

We closed Q1 with 266 restaurants with 5 new additions during the quarter. As of today, we have 15 restaurants that are under construction, and these will operationalize through Q2 and Q3 of this financial year.

Looking 1 year out from the current INR7 crores per outlet mature store average, what are the levers to move to INR8 crores?

Are there any specific initiatives being taken for delivery given the overall strong growth?

On the gross margin front, on a normalized basis 1-2 years down the line with inflation moderating, how should we look at normalized gross margins?
Could you give a sense of the repeat rate on value-driven customers driving the 30% SSSG growth?
What drove the improvement in ROMs of new stores, and is this sustainable for stores opening in the future?
How much of the revenue was driven by higher footfall/guest traffic versus higher average order value, and what would be sustainable over the medium term?
What is the profitability for the delivery business — will it become meaningfully margin accretive or will dine-in remain the primary earning driver?
Once the low base of the previous year is behind us for India BBQ, what SSSG range is practically possible in this business model assuming a steady consumption environment?
Are the back-end investments mainly to support restaurant growth, or will they also contribute to gross margin improvement in the longer run? What is the total capex expected for FY27?
Are you seeing inflation pressure on the UAE business, and is Q1 FY27's SSSG a one-off given the stated focus on volume growth?
How do we tackle inflation if volume goes up?

quarters.summary: United Foodbrands enters FY'27 on the back of two consecutive quarters of strong broad-based SSSG (8.2% Q3, 14.4% Q4 FY'26), targeting double-digit SSSG, 40 new restaurant additions (network to 300+), ~INR140 crore capex funded mainly via internal accruals, gross margin recovery of 100-200 bps, back-end cost compression to ~6.5%, and a pre-Ind AS adjusted operating EBITDA margin of 9-10% for FY'27, with a longer-term ambition of double-digit margins and 400-425 restaurants by FY'30.

subsections.label: Gross margin and value-led volume strategy
points: Consolidated gross margin compression of ~300 bps in Q4 FY26 is a result of deliberate choices, not deterioration.

Factor 1: change in business segment mix — Barbeque Nation India, which has lower per cover spend than international or premium CDR, grew faster than other segments, weighing down average realization.
Factor 2: targeted value campaigns to drive higher throughput in weaker dayparts (lunch occasions, weekday slots, other low throughput sessions) contributed to lower effective realization.
Factor 3: inflation in a few input items, specifically in the Middle East business related to the West Asia crisis.

Medium-term gross margin band of 67-68% remains the directional target; expect 100-200 bps recovery in FY27 over Q4 numbers, driven by procurement initiatives, scale benefits and selective realization improvements.
Internal monthly MIS shows gross margins bottomed out in February 2026 and inched up 100 bps in March and April.

Minor tweaks such as marginal pullback on some campaign offers and moving to full-price offering (not at cost of volumes) helped gross margin improve Feb-Mar-Apr; net realization improvement targeted at INR15-20 per cover through base pricing, group offering pricing, and beverage contribution levers.

subsections.label: Mature Portfolio ROM Bridge (Slide 11)
points: Q4 FY26 mature portfolio ROM improvement of 60 bps YoY is net of two deliberate investments: ~290 bps into gross margin and ~110 bps into additional marketing (marketing spend rose from 1.9% to 3% of revenue).

14.4% SSSG generated ~460 bps of operating leverage, more than offsetting these investments — indicating operating leverage equation is intact, with ~50% of every incremental SSSG rupee flowing through to restaurant operating profit.
Consolidated pre-Ind AS ROM in Q4 was identical YoY at 12.6%, but composition is materially healthier.

New store cohort drag increased from 120 bps (Q4 FY25) to 180 bps (Q4 FY26) entirely because Q4 was the heaviest new store opening quarter in company history; drag will narrow as these mature over FY27.

subsections.label: Back-end cost investment
points: Back-end cost step-up of ~100 bps (6.1% to 7.1% of revenue) is deliberate structural investment in central capabilities — culinary teams, guest experience teams, marketing capabilities, digital infrastructure.
Lever from here is operating leverage via revenue scale, not cost reduction; expect compression to ~6.5% in FY27 and further to 6% longer term.

subsections.label: Balance sheet & capital allocation
points: Net debt of ~INR102 crores funded via a combination of operating cash flows and a measured increase in borrowings to fund 35 new restaurants in FY26.

Operating within prudent leverage limits; for FY27, intent is to fund network expansion primarily from internal accruals, keeping net debt broadly stable as operating cash flow scales with H2 run rate.
FY27 capex plan of ~INR140 crores: ~INR120 crores for new store expansion (India, International, Premium CDR) and ~INR20 crores for maintenance/renovation/upgrades.
Capital allocation priority order unchanged: fund expansion primarily from internal accruals, manage leverage within prudent limits.

subsections.label: Two halves of FY26 framing
points: H1 FY26 was described as the trough of the demand cycle; H2 FY26 is where strategic interventions visibly delivered.
Right operating base to consider going forward is the H2 run rate, not the full-year average.
H1 pre-Ind AS margin ~3%, H2 ~8%; FY27 aim is to continue H2 momentum to reach 9-10%.

subsections.label: Multi-engine portfolio validation
points: Every reporting segment and every channel delivered strong double-digit growth in Q4 for the first time in recent history.
Barbeque Nation India remains anchor with 47% dine-in volume growth; International grew 27% with restaurant operating margins 23-24%; Premium CDR revenue grew 23% with mature store margins above 18%.
Each engine independently working; together creating a diversified growth platform.
Rebranding to United Foodbrands in September 2025 reflected shift from single-brand operator to multi-brand eating-out platform; FY26 results validate this thesis.

subsections.label: Captive demand architecture
points: ~90% of dine-in transaction volumes driven from own captive channels — app/website, in-house reservation center, and direct walk-ins — meaning customer relationship remains direct.
This enables closer guest engagement, deeper consumer insights, stronger brand affinity, and is viewed as a compounding structural moat.
47% dine-in volume growth is delivered through the strength of this captive demand engine.

subsections.label: Barbeque Nation India
points: Engine of quarter's recovery; strong growth in both new customer acquisitions and repeat customer transactions.
Time gap between repeat visits continued to compress; guest satisfaction scores on an upward trend.
Digital channel penetration of dine-in transactions rose from 53% (Q3) to 60%+ (Q4); MAU crossed 1.2 million, up 51% YoY.

subsections.label: International business
points: Added 4 new restaurants in FY26 — most in any year — including entry into new geographies; 3 additional restaurants under construction across Middle East and Southeast Asia.
Foundational presence-establishing work is done; focus shifts to scaling each market in FY27.
International SSSG in mid-single digits described as commendable given tough macro environment; average revenue per store ~INR12-13 crores; SSSG has been compounding over the last 5 years.

2 out of ~8 restaurants (Bahrain and Dubai) impacted by regional issues, but showing month-on-month improvement in April/May vs March; company cautious on signing new stores in that market (none in last 3 months).

subsections.label: Premium CDR
points: Added 12 new restaurants during FY26, network grew from 30 to 42 — a 40% expansion in a single year.
Heavy expansion affected near-term consolidated margins but mature restaurant unit economics working well; new store cohort in expected ramp-up phase.

Margin dip vs Q3 explained by seasonality (Q3/December is a strong quarter with disproportionate operating leverage benefit), new stores opened around Nov (Q3) vs Q4 timing effects, and one-time initial setup/liquor costs baked into Q4 new-store financials.
New stores are in newer, non-home markets (Mumbai, Delhi) requiring time to build up; all 42 restaurants are in premium areas with higher rents versus Barbeque restaurants.
FY27 store addition plan for Salt and Toscano: ~5 restaurants; FY28 range 5-12 (later narrowed to 5-10), pending stabilization of existing new-store portfolio.

subsections.label: AOV / realization mix
points: Company does not disclose specific AOV/APC numbers, but overall dine-in growth vs transaction growth difference led to Company-level AOV decline of ~14-15%.
Driven by business mix shift towards higher covers in Barbeque India (lower APC than International/Premium CDR) and by design lower-APC weaker daypart building.
Trend may continue for ~2 more quarters before settling; new levels expected to be similar to previous two quarters, not materially lower.

subsections.label: Capacity/table-turn economics
points: Restaurants can theoretically run 4 sessions/day (2 lunch, 2 dinner); a 100-seat restaurant could do up to 12,000 covers/month (~INR9 crores at INR750 price point) — company already does 4 table turns on peak days like Dec 31/Jan 1.
No supply-constraint concern seen; if volumes in a trade area exceed capacity, company adds another restaurant nearby (5-7 km away).
Salt and Toscano peak restaurant revenue ~INR11-12 crores; Barbeque India peak ~INR12-13 crores; no capacity ceiling perceived — many restaurants can do 3 table turns/9,000 covers per month.
