subsections.label: Network expansion pace and rationale
points: Company added 35 new restaurants in FY26 on a base of ~230, roughly 15% expansion — target for FY27 (40 on base of 262) is similarly ~15%, not materially different or aggressive.
11 restaurants under construction expected to become operational in Q1 and Q2 of FY27.

Cumulative target of 100-125 stores over 3 years equates to roughly 40-45 stores/year, consistent with recent pace; management targets opening 8-12 restaurants per quarter, having added 14 in the most recent quarter and ~8 in the prior quarter.

Learnings from FY23 store closures (in Tier 2/3 markets) have been incorporated into current operating model; management believes recent initiatives, if applied earlier, may have prevented some past closures.
400+ restaurant figure is a cumulative long-term (FY30) target, not an annual addition number.

subsections.label: International geographic focus
points: Entry into new geographies during FY26 (4 new international restaurants, most added in any year).
3 additional restaurants under construction across Middle East and Southeast Asia.
Focus for FY27 is scaling Southeast Asia and adopting a cautious approach in the Middle East given regional uncertainty.

Of ~8 international restaurants, 2 (Bahrain, Dubai) are specifically impacted by regional issues; no new store signings in that market for the last 3 months; company is watching and waiting to maximize potential of existing stores there.

subsections.label: Premium CDR geographic expansion
points: New Premium CDR stores are being opened in non-home markets such as Mumbai and Delhi, which will take time to build up compared to established home markets.

subsections.label: FY27 strategic priorities
points: Priority 1: Continue to drive volume-led SSSG, targeting mid-single-digit to double-digit SSSG on a normalized base for FY27; growth to remain volume-led, not pricing-led.
Priority 2: Continue planned network expansion — pipeline of 11 restaurants under construction plus advanced commercial discussions gives visibility into 40 new restaurants in FY27.

Priority 3: Continue to build on margin trajectory towards 9-10% pre-Ind AS adjusted operating EBITDA margin in FY27, with a path to double-digit margins longer term; framed as a multi-quarter build, not a single-quarter step-up, with company committing to report against each lever as the year progresses.

Priority 4: Continue to scale portfolio of brands — Premium CDR to make calibrated investments in newer markets while stabilizing new-store margins; International to focus on scaling Southeast Asia and remain cautious in Middle East.
Priority 5: Maintain capital allocation discipline — fund expansion primarily from internal accruals, manage leverage within prudent limits.

Explicit statement of what company is NOT doing in FY27: not chasing discount-led growth that compromises unit economics; not entering new brand categories that could dilute portfolio focus; not making new acquisitions — sticking to existing portfolio and compounding from current base.

subsections.label: Input cost / inflation
points: Inflation in a few input items, specifically in Middle East business related to the West Asia crisis, contributed to gross margin compression in Q4 FY26.

Entering an inflationary cycle broadly on raw material as well as utilities/petroleum side; company states its 100-150 bps gross margin improvement guidance is baked in after adjusting for these inflationary pressures.
Recent LPG price increases and Middle East inflationary pressures noted, though consolidated margins have still inched up in recent months.

subsections.label: Middle East macro uncertainty
points: 2 of ~8 international restaurants (Bahrain, Dubai) impacted by regional (West Asia) crisis; difficult to predict how the situation will evolve.
2 restaurants under construction in that market are also seeing inflation impact; company has paused signing new stores there for the last 3 months, adopting a wait-and-watch approach.

subsections.label: New store margin drag
points: Heaviest-ever new store opening quarter in Q4 FY26 increased new-store cohort drag on mature ROM from 120 bps to 180 bps YoY; new restaurants require 12-24 months to ramp up to mature economics.

subsections.label: Historical execution risk (Tier 2/3 market closures)
points: In FY23, some restaurants in Tier 2/Tier 3 markets did not work out and were shut; management flags this as a past learning being incorporated into current expansion planning.

subsections.label: FY27 guidance build/arithmetic
points: Mature portfolio ROM (~16% on H2 FY26 basis) to move to 17-18%, driven by ~100-150 bps gross margin recovery plus continued operating leverage on sustained SSSG.
New store drag to stabilize at 1.5-1.8% as FY26 cohort matures, taking consolidated ROM to ~15.5-16.5%.
Back-end costs to compress to 6.5% of revenue as scale benefits compound.

Net impact of these three levers expected to support a pre-Ind AS adjusted operating EBITDA margin of 9-10% in FY27 — framed as a full-year number, not an exit-quarter number, and factoring in seasonal lean/peak season phenomena.
This is described as a measured multi-quarter build with clear arithmetic anchors, not a single-quarter step-up; management to report progress against each lever through the year.
Guidance assumes continuation of current momentum into H1 FY27 (Q1, Q2), with expectation that some benefits carry into H2 FY27 despite lapping a stronger Q3/Q4 FY26 base.
Revenue growth guidance function of two factors: SSSG and new restaurant expansion — with 10-13% store expansion and double-digit SSSG implying 22-25% full-year revenue growth (per Q&A).

guidance_ledger.statement: Internal aim is to deliver mid-single-digit to double-digit SSSG on a normalized base for FY27; internally aim to comfortably cross double-digit SSSG on a full financial year basis.
Plan of 40 new restaurants in FY27, taking total restaurant network to 300-plus by end of FY27.
Internal target is to reach 400 to 425 restaurants by FY30.

guidance_ledger.metric: Pre-Ind AS adjusted operating EBITDA margin
guidance_ledger.statement: Internal aim is to take pre-Ind AS adjusted operating EBITDA margin to 9% to 10% in FY27 with a path towards double-digit margins going forward.

Expect approximately 100 basis points to 200 basis points of gross margin recovery in FY27 over and above Q4 numbers, driven by procurement initiatives, scale benefits and selective realization improvements; medium-term gross margin band of 67% to 68%.
Mature portfolio ROM, approximately 16% on H2 FY26 basis, will move to 17% to 18%.
New store drag will stabilize at 1.5% to 1.8% as FY26 cohort matures.
Consolidated ROM expected at approximately 15.5% to 16.5%.
Back-end costs will compress to 6.5% of revenue as scale benefits compound; further down to 6% over the longer term.
As operating cash flow scales with H2 run rate, expect net debt position to remain the same.

Planning a capex of approximately INR140 crores for next year, split across India (~INR75 crores for 30 stores), International (~INR30 crores for 5 stores), Premium CDR (~INR15 crores for 5 stores), and maintenance/renovation (~INR20 crores).
Assuming ~12-13% store expansion and double-digit SSSG, reasonable to assume 22% to 25% revenue growth this year on a full year basis.
Internal aim is to maintain international SSSG at around mid-single-digit numbers.
Internal aim to maintain premium CDR SSSG at a similar range of mid-single digits as done in the past.
On a blended basis, internal aim is to be at early double-digit numbers.

guidance_ledger.metric: Salt and Toscano (Premium CDR) store additions
guidance_ledger.statement: FY28 additions can be anywhere between 5 to 12 (later refined to current range of around 5 to 10).
Planning to add 100 to 125 restaurants cumulatively over the next 3 years (approximately 40-45 stores per year).
Not making new acquisitions; not entering new brand categories that could dilute portfolio focus; sticking to existing portfolio.

guidance_ledger.statement: AOV mix-driven decline trend may continue for 2 more quarters and after that will automatically settle down; new levels expected to be similar to previous two quarters, not materially lower.

risk_register.risk: Input cost inflation, particularly in Middle East business linked to West Asia crisis
risk_register.note: Contributed to ~300 bps gross margin compression in Q4 FY26; broader inflationary cycle expected on raw material and utilities/petroleum, though FY27 margin guidance is stated to be net of these pressures.

risk_register.risk: Middle East geopolitical/macro uncertainty
risk_register.note: 2 of ~8 international restaurants (Bahrain, Dubai) impacted; difficult to predict outcome, though month-on-month improvement seen in April/May vs March; company pausing new store signings there for last 3 months.

risk_register.risk: New store margin drag from heavy expansion pace
risk_register.note: Q4 FY26 was heaviest new-store opening quarter in company history, increasing drag on mature ROM from 120 bps to 180 bps YoY; expected to narrow as FY26 cohort matures over FY27 (12-24 month ramp-up).

risk_register.risk: Past execution risk in Tier 2/Tier 3 market expansion
risk_register.note: FY23 saw some restaurant closures in Tier 2/3 markets; management believes recent operating model improvements would have helped avoid some of those closures and are now incorporated into planning.

risk_register.risk: Premium CDR new-store margin compression in non-home markets
risk_register.note: New Premium CDR stores in Mumbai and Delhi (non-home markets) show compressed margins versus mature portfolio; expected to take time to ramp up, with focus this year on bringing them to mature margin levels.

themes.label: Demand recovery / SSSG inflection
themes.note: Two consecutive quarters of strong broad-based SSSG (8.2% Q3, 14.4% Q4 FY26), described as structural inflection not narrow recovery.

themes.label: Multi-engine portfolio validation
themes.note: Every reporting segment/channel delivered double-digit growth in Q4 for the first time, validating the multi-brand platform thesis post rebranding.

themes.label: Captive demand moat
themes.note: ~90% of dine-in volumes driven from own app/website/call center/walk-ins, seen as a compounding structural moat.

themes.label: Gross margin / value-led volume trade-off
themes.note: Deliberate value campaigns and mix-shift compressed gross margin by ~300 bps in Q4, but management targets 100-200 bps recovery in FY27 back toward 67-68% band.

themes.label: Network expansion pace
themes.note: 35 restaurants added in FY26 (most in years); 40 planned for FY27 targeting 300+ by FY27-end and 400-425 by FY30, funded mainly via internal accruals.

themes.label: Margin expansion pathway to double digits
themes.note: Pre-Ind AS adjusted operating EBITDA margin targeted at 9-10% in FY27 via mature ROM improvement, new-store drag stabilization, and back-end cost compression.

themes.label: Middle East macro uncertainty
themes.note: Bahrain and Dubai restaurants impacted by West Asia crisis and inflation; company pausing new signings there and adopting a cautious wait-and-watch approach.

key_takeaways: We delivered consolidated same-store sales growth of 14.4% in Q4 FY'26 on top of 8.2% we delivered in Q3.

Consolidated dine-in volume grew approximately 43% year-on-year with Barbeque Nation India dine-in volume growing 47%, international dine-in volume growing 27% and premium CDR dine-in volume grew 28%.
Our delivery revenue also grew by 32% year-on-year, led entirely by transaction growth.

Approximately 90% of our dine-in transaction volumes are driven from our own captive channels, that are our own app and website, our own in-house reservation center and direct walk-ins to our restaurants.
Consolidated revenue stood at INR360 crores, growing 23.1% year-on-year.
For the full year FY'26, consolidated revenue grew by 8.6% to INR1,339 crores.
H2 revenue grew 18.5% year-on-year restaurant operating profits grew year-on-year by 14.6% and the volume-led inflection is continuing into Q1 FY'27.
Our internal aim is to take pre-Ind AS adjusted operating EBITDA margin to 9% to 10% in FY'27 with a path towards double-digit margins going forward.
Our internal target is to reach 400 to 425 restaurants by FY'30.
We are not chasing discount-led growth that comprises unit economics. We are not into entering new brand categories that could dilute our portfolio focus. We are not making new acquisitions.
pressing_questions: In the opening statement, you mentioned that the momentum of high growth continues even in this quarter... Assuming that we continue such strong SSSG in the first half and then in the second statement, you mentioned we'll do like high single-digit SSSG. That means you don't expect very high growth in the second half. Like those two statements are slightly not in the same light for me. Can you please elaborate on that?

On the premium CDR segment. In Q4, we added 4 stores in the CDR segment, but our margins have literally collapsed versus Q3, especially considering the fact that more than 1 year old stores have delivered 7% SSSG. What explains this margin collapse?

The gap we are looking to accelerate store additions in a meaningful way... The last time that we did that, it really hasn't worked out well and we had to shut many stores. What learnings from them give you the confidence that we will not face a similar situation again?
On the Salt and Toscano side, what is the store addition we are planning for FY'27 and FY'28?

On SSSG in the other 2 platforms (International and Premium CDR), they are comparatively low to our Barbeque chain. Can you give some steps which we are taking to increase it? And what this number can be during FY'27?

quarters.summary: Q1 FY27 was described as a strong start to the financial year for XtraNet, with revenue up 11% YoY, EBITDA up 89% YoY and PAT up 77% YoY, driven by a favorable mix shift toward higher-margin services (65-68% of Q1 FY27 revenue vs ~46% in Q1 FY26). Order book stood at ~INR 373 crore with an active bid pipeline of ~INR 1200 crore. Management guided FY27 revenue of Rs. 500+ crore (~35-40% growth over FY26's Rs. 365 crore), targeted 35-40% CAGR growth over the next three years, and reiterated a medium-term segment mix goal with data center at 50-55%, enterprise applications at 20-25%, and proprietary platforms plus digital services together at 30%+.

subsections.label: Drivers of profitability expansion
points: Significant expansion in profitability during the quarter was supported by a favorable business mix with a sustainably higher contribution from services, together with better operating leverage across the business.
Growth was only 11% on the top line in Q1, but bottom line (EBITDA and PAT) improved drastically because services revenue was almost 66-67% in the first quarter itself.
Product deployment gives EBITDA margin of around 6-8%, while services gives end-to-end margins of around 20-22%.
Company aims to do at least 60%+ in services and less than 40% in product to deliver margins similar to last year plus 50-75 bps improvement in FY27.

subsections.label: Capital efficiency and discipline
points: Performance achieved while continuing to maintain a strong focus on financial discipline, capital efficiency and sustainable growth.
FY26 return ratios remain healthy, with both ROE and ROC in excess of 30%.
Priorities for FY27 include maintaining strict discipline around working capital, collections and return on capital as the company scales.

subsections.label: Tax rate
points: Steady tax rate for the next two years expected to be close to 25%.

subsections.label: Project evaluation / IRR benchmark
points: Company normally does IRR for all projects and maintains an internal benchmark for what fits its required IRR.
Even in annuity-based models with recurring revenue over 6-7 years, the company maintains a benchmark of at least 17-18% IRR before entering a project.

subsections.label: Order quality focus
points: Focus is not simply on increasing the size of the order book but increasingly on quality of orders pursued, including margins, payment terms, working capital requirements, execution visibility and potential for long-term managed services and recurring engagement.
This diversification across customer sectors, execution models and geographies reduces concentration risks and provides a broader platform for growth.

subsections.label: Pipeline conversion timelines
points: Order book orders are already received and under execution; standard government/large PSU conversion cycle from proposal to order is approximately 60-90 days (also cited as 120 to 150 days), while large enterprise/aviation/BFSI conversion is 30-60 days.
Approximately 40-45% of the Rs. 1200 crore pipeline is at an advanced stage, with ~30% of this expected to close in the next quarter.
Services revenue invoicing cycle is 45 to 60 days.

subsections.label: Revenue recognition model for order book
points: Revenue is recognized on a billing model — once billed to the client, only then is it taken as revenue; order book value itself is higher than what gets recognized in a given period.

For annuity/recurring contracts (e.g., an O&M contract worth Rs. 60 crore spread over 5 years), billing is done on a sustained straight-line basis (e.g., Rs. 12 crore per year) rather than a step-up model.
CAPEX-OPEX model: 50-60% of project value goes to CAPEX billing with 6-18 month execution, balance ~40% is managed services/O&M spread over 4-7 years or longer.
Annual subscription model: entire revenue split over a project duration of 5-10 years, charged on a quarterly basis, treated as recurring annuity-nature revenue.

Order book comprises 55 projects worth Rs. 373 crore as of June 30, 2026; approximately 50% of the order book is on a recurring/annuity model, and around 40% of submitted proposals are of recurring nature.
Order book split: 55% from non-government customers vs 45% government; 45% direct orders vs 55% indirect orders.

subsections.label: Blended order execution period
points: Current order book is a mix of CAPEX and OPEX; 60-65% will be executed within this financial year and the rest is spread into O&M for the next 3-5 years.
CAPEX cycle takes a bare minimum of 9 months to at least 15 months depending on scale and size of execution; services model revenue can be monthly or quarterly.
Fresh orders of Rs. 60 crore were secured in Q1 FY27, with an active bid pipeline of Rs. 1200 crore; 55% of the order book is expected to be executable in FY27.

subsections.label: Business mix shift
points: Diversified revenue mix is strategically important: while data center and enterprise applications provide scale and strong execution opportunities, increasing contributions from digital services, managed services and proprietary platforms strengthen recurring engagement, customer stickiness and overall quality of revenue base.

Increase in services contribution (65-68% of Q1 FY27 revenue vs ~46% in Q1 FY26) makes services strategically important for building greater customer stickiness and deepening engagement through managed and value-added services.
Q1 FY27 revenue split: data center infrastructure & IT operations 48%, enterprise applications 26%, proprietary platforms 14%, digital services 12%.
Government/PSU customers contributed 47% of FY26 revenue.

subsections.label: Data center growth outlook
points: Company wants to keep data center at 50% of overall revenue and is targeting 35-40% annual growth in this segment.

Growth would come majorly from data center infrastructure modernization and new disaster recovery setup creation, including network operation center and cyber security operation center under data center and IT operations.

Already have an active pipeline of more than Rs. 600 crore where participation has been done for creation of new setups in this area (out of the Rs. 1200 crore total pipeline, 50-60% is from data center and IT operations, including NOC and cyber security operation center).

subsections.label: Medium-term vertical mix goal
points: Overall goal is to grow around 35-40% CAGR over the next three years.
Data center will remain the biggest vertical at around 50-55%, enterprise applications around 20-25%, and proprietary platform plus digital services together almost 30%+.
Direction reflects focus on sustainable margins and stakeholder value creation, not just chasing order books and work.

subsections.label: Proprietary platform customer focus
points: Focus is on both B2B and B2C segments for proprietary platforms.

B2B focus includes BFSI and aviation sectors where solution delivery has already started; large enterprises, large banks, BFSI, major government/central government, PSUs, railways already added to the digital trust/PKI platform.
B2C: large portal created for XtraTrust platform, continuing to add more subscribers.

Other proprietary platform solutions include smart machines, electronic document management, visa management, decision support systems, and automation/workflow solutions built on the Synergy platform; increasing focus on automation and AI-related solutions using the homegrown Synergy platform, purely for B2B.

subsections.label: Contract structure and stickiness
points: Solutions are contracted for 3, 5, or 7-year terms and CAPEX-OPEX model; annual subscription continues year-on-year or via two/three-year contracts.
For end-to-end solution delivery, 50-60% goes into CAPEX model and 35-40% into a 3-5 year operational (OPEX) model.
Both CAPEX-OPEX and annual subscription models are offered to both B2B and B2C customers.

subsections.label: Client acquisition channel
points: For B2B, most projects come through RFQ or direct inquiry to sales and pre-sales team; company is already empaneled with multiple clients including central PSUs and large corporates, generating direct inquiries.

subsections.label: Proprietary platforms
points: Synergy: low-code AI-native digital transformation platform.

XtraTrust: digital trust and PKI-based authentication platform; among MeitY, Government of India approved Certifying Authorities (CA), authorized to issue digital signature certificates and provide e-sign services.
Platform benefits from high-regulatory entry barriers and mission-critical applications, supporting long-term adoption and strong customer stickiness.
Company has executed more than 50 data center/command center projects cumulatively to date, and delivered a total of 175 projects across FY2024-FY2026.

subsections.label: XtraTrust competitive positioning
points: Approximately 11 private players hold licenses to operate as certifying authority in India; company mainly competes with eMudhra as most other licensed players do not have a similar end-to-end solution.
Advanced portal and mechanism with 10,000+ partners across the country already using the platform for digital signature and e-sign issuance.
850,000+ subscribers onboarded on recurring (annual/biannual subscription) model.
24x7 support facility and operation center; services delivered within 30 minutes of application receipt from end subscriber.
Complete B2B model with own-built PKI solution and PKI engine, deployed with large enterprise, government and enterprise customers.
Enhancing data center capacity and capability for XtraTrust to handle more load and onboard more users/subscribers, targeted over the next one quarter.

subsections.label: Data center capacity enhancement
points: Company is enhancing capacity and capability of its own data center infrastructure (deployed for XtraTrust) to handle more load, targeted within the next one quarter, so more users/subscribers can be onboarded.

subsections.label: International expansion
points: Company continues to actively pursue opportunities in the international market, which remain an important avenue for diversifying the revenue base and increasing the contribution from international business over the medium term.
Company currently has a presence across 15+ states and 10+ industries.

subsections.label: Inventory strategy amid hardware inflation
points: Cost of hardware has moved almost 3x-4x over the last year; this was a strategic call of the company, different from many other players, to keep good inventory on hand for past projects where there is no price escalation clause with government.
This inventory strategy takes care of costs, avoiding buying at today's heavy prices; whatever is procured going forward will come at newer, higher prices.

Getting product itself is becoming a challenge in addition to higher prices, but the company has not faced any order cancellation so far; strategically working to fulfil customer requirements end-to-end.
Future supply/price trends need to be monitored closely.

subsections.label: Pricing pass-through mechanics
points: Business model is not a pass-through; company buys products for its own projects, handles deployment/implementation/configuration and managed services in-house, then adds services and delivers to customer.

From bidding to order conversion takes approximately 60-90 days; company obtains a firm rate confirmation in writing from the manufacturer, locking the price for a project so there is no price escalation on that specific order.
Inventory is built immediately after receiving an order for execution of that project, avoiding escalation risk on that order.
Price escalation risk only affects repeat orders or new orders; for new bids the company now factors in price escalation mechanisms and is submitting proposals accordingly.

Company has started applying a price escalation mechanism on a year-on-year basis depending on USD variation and OEM policy/price escalation due to global supply chain disruption, and pursues such escalation clauses when repeat order provisions exist in RFPs.
Products, third-party goods and software are generally procured at the time of order issuance; most services during execution are provided by the internal team.

subsections.label: Industry landscape
points: Indian technology landscape continues to evolve rapidly, driven by increasing digitization across enterprise and government sectors, and rising adoption of cloud, AI, and data-intensive applications.
Overall IT spending in India expected to continue growing at a healthy double-digit rate, with increasing investment across infrastructure, software, and IT services.

Data center market growth driven by cloud adoption, AI workload, data localization, and increasing enterprise digitization, creating significant opportunity for data center infrastructure, managed IT services, and ongoing technology support.
Indian data center market estimated at USD 5.5 billion in 2025, projected to grow to over USD 13 billion by 2034 at a CAGR of 10%+.

subsections.label: Company positioning
points: XtraNet is an integrated technology solution provider with over 24 years of experience delivering digital infrastructure and technology solutions to governments, PSUs, and private enterprises.
Combination of project-based execution capabilities with recurring managed services and platform-led revenue is a key strength.

Strong focus on e-governance, digital trust, and data security, smart cities and enterprise solutions, data center infrastructure, smart machines positions the company across mission-critical technology applications and BFSI banking solutions, providing resilience against potential disruption from AI-led technological shift.

Continues to expand engagement with existing customers through cross-selling across data centers, enterprise applications, digital services, and proprietary platforms, addressing a broader set of customer requirements while increasing wallet share.

subsections.label: Workforce
points: Team comprises 500+ permanent employees and 370+ contractual employees, giving strong workforce-based support for expanding business opportunities.

subsections.label: Hardware price inflation and supply
points: Cost of hardware has moved almost 3x-4x over the last year, a widely known industry-wide trend.
Beyond higher prices, getting the product itself is becoming a challenge.
Company has not faced any order cancellation so far but must keep monitoring how the future plays out closely.
USD variation and OEM policy/global supply chain disruption can trigger price escalation on repeat or new orders.

subsections.label: FY27 priorities
points: Execute the existing order book efficiently and convert it into revenue and cash flows.
Maintain the improvement in profitability through an improved business mix and operating discipline.
Continue expanding higher value services, managed services and proprietary platform business.
Maintain strict discipline around working capital, collections and return on capital as the company scales.
Targeting FY27 revenue of Rs. 500+ crore, representing 35-40% growth, with a sustainable growth target of 35% and a 3-year revenue CAGR target of 35-40%.

subsections.label: Confidence factors
points: Combination of a strong order book, improving revenue quality, significantly stronger profitability and healthy return ratios gives confidence in the underlying direction of the business.
Objective is to translate opportunities into consistent revenue growth, healthy profitability, stronger cash generation and sustainable long-term value creation for shareholders.
Already participated in new projects of around Rs. 1200 crore and expects to participate in similar-sized projects in the next quarter (3-6 months).

guidance_ledger.statement: Targeting 500+ crores for FY27, approximately 35-40% growth over FY26's Rs. 365 crore, with existing order book of Rs. 375 crore (55-60% executable this year) supporting sustainable growth of 35%.
Looking forward to 35% to 40% annual growth in the data center segment.

guidance_ledger.statement: Want to keep data center at 50% of overall revenue; medium-term target 50-55%.
Enterprise applications will be around 20-25% of revenue in the medium term.

guidance_ledger.metric: Proprietary platforms + digital services revenue share
guidance_ledger.statement: Biggest share in service margin (proprietary platform + digital services) will be almost 30%+.
Overall goal is basically to grow around 35% to 40% CAGR in the next three years' time.
Aiming for 50-75 bps margin improvement in this financial year versus last year's margins, driven by services mix >60%.
Steady tax rate close to 25% considered for the next two years.
Approximately 40-45% of the Rs.1200 crore pipeline is at an advanced stage, and hopefully in next one quarter, will be able to close approximately 30% of this.
Already participated in new projects of around Rs. 1200 crore; in the next one quarter (3-6 months) will be participating in similar-sized projects.
Company wants to do at least 60%+ in services and less than 40% in product going forward.
Maintains an internal benchmark of at least 17-18% IRR before entering any project, especially annuity-based models.

risk_register.risk: Hardware/product price inflation (3x-4x increase over past year)
risk_register.note: Cost of hardware has moved almost 3x-4x over the last year; company had strategically built inventory to mitigate, but new/repeat orders will face higher input costs.

risk_register.risk: Product availability/supply challenge
risk_register.note: Beyond higher prices, getting the product itself is becoming a challenge; no cancellations faced so far but future needs close monitoring.

risk_register.risk: Currency (USD) variation impacting OEM pricing
risk_register.note: USD variation from submission to repeat order, along with OEM policy or price escalation due to global supply chain disruption, can affect costs; company now builds escalation clauses into new bids/RFPs.

risk_register.risk: Margin compression during large project CAPEX/go-live phase
risk_register.note: During 12-14 month CAPEX deployment phases of large projects, margins are lower (product-driven ~6-8%) before service-led margins (20-22%) kick in as O&M revenue ramps.

risk_register.risk: Working capital / collection cycle in government business
risk_register.note: Government payment cycle runs approximately 120-150 days versus 45-60 days for O&M/services revenue, requiring strict working capital discipline as company scales.

themes.label: Recurring/annuity revenue model

AFFLE.about: Incorporated in 1994, Affle is a global technology company with a proprietary consumer intelligence platform that transforms ads into recommendations helping marketers to effectively identify, engage, acquire and drive transactions with their potential and existing users[1]

quarters.summary: Affle 3i delivered its 14th consecutive quarter of sequential top-line growth in Q1 FY2027 with highest-ever quarterly revenue, EBITDA, PAT and consumer conversions; management reaffirmed medium-term 20%+ CAGR guidance and the 10x decadal growth vision (targeting completion in ~5 years), flagged progress on a larger inorganic M&A (due diligence phase, targeted close by early 2027), and expects margin expansion within FY2027 especially in Developed Markets, even as RMG/FinTech regulatory-macro headwinds and the Bobble investment situation remain open risk items.

subsections.label: Revenue and profitability drivers
points: Q1 FY2027 revenues of INR 7.47 billion grew 20.4% y-o-y, considered robust given the negative impact of regulatory and macroeconomic headwinds on some customer segments like RMG.
Over 95% of revenues witnessed over 25% growth y-o-y after adjusting for the RMG/FinTech-related impact, reaffirming execution against medium-term guidance.
Sequential revenue growth of 3.1% was driven by broad-based momentum across industry verticals in both India and international markets.
EBITDA margins improved from 22.3% to 22.4% q-o-q; no major forex volatility this quarter versus Q4.
PAT margin improved 60 bps sequentially to 16.6% from 16.0%, with PAT growing 21.7% y-o-y and 7.5% q-o-q to INR 1.28 billion.
PBT of INR 1.58 billion grew 22.1% y-o-y and 6.6% q-o-q (4.7% q-o-q from operations).
Effective tax rate for FY2026 full year was 18.6%.

subsections.label: Cost structure
points: Inventory and Data costs at 63.2% of revenue, broadly in line with previous quarter.
Employee costs increased 3.4% sequentially primarily due to annual appraisal/bonus release in a few geographies; y-o-y increase of 7.8% despite higher currency-related outflows.
Other expenses at 5.6% of revenue from operations, increased marginally (INR 2.3 million q-o-q) due to ongoing business promotion spend supporting Developed Markets expansion.

subsections.label: Cash flow / working capital
points: No material changes in collection risk; company on track for a robust OCF to PAT ratio for the full year.

FY2026 OCF to PAT ratio of 110% reflects up-fronting of cash collections (~INR 40-45 crore collected in March ahead of year-end), which is now reflected as weaker OCF in Q1 FY2027 (41% OCF to EBITDA conversion).
Management expects OCF to PAT ratios to normalize as the year progresses, reaching about 80-85% by Q3.

subsections.label: Currency impact
points: Stable USD movement versus various currencies this quarter, unlike Q4/Q3 when there was a spike in USD versus other currencies.
72% of business comes from Emerging Markets and India where cross-currency ROIs are guaranteed/promised to clients, requiring CPCU rate adjustments; only 20% of US business is dollar-to-dollar.
A steep increase in US currency rates in the prior quarter had affected take rate/inventory cost; this quarter was largely flattish sequentially due to muted dollar movement.
Average CPCU rate is above INR 60, but on a currency-adjusted basis some benefit is passed to advertisers, impacting margins in the short term.

subsections.label: Capital allocation
points: Backed by strong performance, balance sheet and disciplined capital allocation, company remains positioned to pursue both organic and inorganic growth opportunities in line with 10x vision.
Continued investment in scalable technologies and strengthening global revenue mix to be executed with financial discipline.
Bobble investment carrying value disclosed at INR 136 crore in the press release.

key_figures.label: Consecutive quarters of sequential top-line growth
Track record of consistent execution as a listed entity

subsections.label: Execution track record
points: Delivered 14 consecutive quarters of sequential top-line growth as of Q1 FY2027.
Track record of consistent execution spans 7 years as a listed entity.

subsections.label: Direct vs agency channel mix
points: Direct customer contribution stepped up to ~79% of revenue in Q1 FY2027 versus ~74% for full FY2026.

Management does not strategically distinguish between billing directly with advertisers versus through agencies; 100% of business has direct advertiser technology integration regardless of billing channel.

Certain Emerging Markets verticals see advertisers preferring to work directly with the platform given strong presence there; mix could shift differently as the company expands in Developed Markets or completes acquisitions; no forward guidance given on this ratio.

subsections.label: Vertical mix qualitative color
points: In India and Emerging Markets, categories E and F are robust and doing well across the board; category G (RMG) recovery phase still ongoing; category H (healthcare, hospitality) also doing well with strong conviction.
Qualitative ranking in India/EM: category E, F, H and G in that order.
In Developed Markets, categories E and G are doing better at the moment versus F and H, though F and H show strong momentum and possibilities ahead.

key_figures.label: Awards won at Connected TV Asia Symposium 2026

subsections.label: AI-powered Consumer Platform Stack
points: Deepening verticalization strategy, strengthening direct advertiser integrations and expanding audience intelligence capabilities to enhance scale and competitiveness of the AI-powered Consumer Platform Stack across connected devices (mobile, CTV and other agentic/autonomous intelligent connected devices).

Built on the launch of Niko and OpticksAI, enhanced capabilities with new AI-led innovations for mobile app marketers, growth managers and advertisers, giving deeper consumer intelligence and full-funnel campaign visibility.
Combining AI-driven campaign intelligence with real-time performance analytics enables faster data-driven decision making, smarter campaign optimization and stronger marketing outcomes.

subsections.label: Autonomous / agentic intelligent connected devices (AICDs)
points: Vision extends beyond mobile/CTV to autonomous agentic intelligent connected devices — mobile with AI agents assisting human input, smart TVs becoming more context-aware and autonomous, vehicles becoming more autonomous with agentic intelligence, and public/retail screens potentially using cameras/context to tailor content.

Company is ring-fencing IP around human-versus-non-human content/data distillation technology (whether an ad is shown to a human or AI, and whether content is human-created or AI-created) as a key future differentiation.

subsections.label: IP portfolio
points: Robust IP portfolio of 300+ unique enforceable patent claims spans fraud intelligence, human vs non-human data distillation, precision targeting, contextual and gesture-based advertising, and next-generation AI-native ads and engagements across key industry verticals.
Reinforces differentiated and defensible position as the digital advertising ecosystem evolves.

subsections.label: Industry recognition
points: Won 18 awards at Connected TV Asia Symposium 2026, including Best CTV AdTech for Addressable TV and Best CTV Technology Company of the Year.
Recognized at e4m India Digital Marketing Awards 2026, including Best Campaign - Use of Mobile and Mobile Monetization.
Received Gold Award for Best Cross-Channel Programmatic Campaign at Agency Reporter Programmatic Asia Awards 2026.
Platforms continue to be recognized across multiple categories in Singular's latest quarterly trend reports.

subsections.label: CTV strategy
points: CTV showing very positive engagement with consumers at the moment; company's approach is conversion-first CTV and cross-screen capabilities (e.g., CTV working with smart QR codes or other engagement models with mobile) driving conversions rather than selling channel-specific inventory.

Company differentiates itself as a consumer-centric platform engaging consumers across the entirety of connected devices in their journey (mobile, CTV, in-car devices, in-store screens), driving one efficient conversion per consumer rather than selling commoditized inventory at a single touchpoint.

Advertising budget/impression allocation across mobile, CTV and other AICDs is directed proportional to consumer attention and where maximum attention-to-conversion ratios are achieved; algorithm-dependent channel selection.

subsections.label: Case studies featured
points: Five customer-approved case studies featured in the earnings presentation this quarter.
First case study: conversion-first CTV and cross-screen capabilities maximizing new converted diners and first orders for a leading QSR app in India (Domino's referenced in Q&A).

Next three case studies: leading travel brands across Emerging Markets leveraging AI-powered campaign optimization, proprietary audience intelligence and bid optimization to target high-intent travelers, driving stronger booking performance and consumer engagement.

Last case study: a leading German quick commerce player leveraging Affle's Consumer Platform to scale presence in a new European market (Netherlands), combining AI-powered keyword intelligence, agentic AI and app growth intelligence to target high-intent grocery shoppers with sustained efficiency.

subsections.label: Device / smartphone trend commentary
points: Management sees no impact from slowing smartphone adoption or rising device costs (memory prices) on business; instead observes increasing time spent by consumers on digital content consumption across markets.
Number of connected devices following a consistent pattern without deviation; possible secondhand device usage or delayed upgrades not seen as impacting company metrics.

key_figures.label: Developed Markets ex-currency growth YoY (analyst estimate)

subsections.label: India and Emerging Markets
points: Continue to anchor business growth, growing 20.2% y-o-y and 4% q-o-q, contributing 72.2% of revenues in Q1 FY2027.
Management sees continued meaningful, sustained growth in India and Emerging Markets with no challenge foreseen; strong competitive advantage versus competitors who are finding it hard to keep up.

subsections.label: Developed Markets
points: Grew 20.7% y-o-y (~1% q-o-q; estimated 11-12% ex-currency y-o-y), contributing 27.8% of revenues, supported by disciplined sales execution, deeper customer engagements and continued new logo additions.

Developed Markets account for a disproportionately high share (more than 50%) of steadily growing global advertising budgets; company aims to progressively increase participation and align revenue mix with global ad budget mix.

Management disagrees that a mature/large Developed Markets addressable market will slow overall growth; expects at least 20%+ growth in Developed Markets consistently given a smaller base and differentiated business model.
Growth pegs identified in Gaming, E-commerce, Entertainment, and positive growth even in Healthcare across top 10 verticals company is deeply verticalized for.

U.S. is the largest Developed Market and the strategic focus, both organically and inorganically; meaningful growth seen in the U.S. across categories E, F, G, H; U.S. vs non-U.S. split not disclosed.
Target of activating over 100,000 mobile apps to reach over 500 million connected devices in Developed Markets this year.

subsections.label: CPCU unit economics: Emerging vs Developed Markets
points: Volume of business/traffic in Emerging Markets is about 5x higher than in Developed Markets for a similar level of revenue, because there are far more users/devices in Emerging Markets.
Company runs an almost 22%-23% EBITDA business anchored on Emerging Markets despite harsher unit economics from high volume of activity.

In Developed Markets, unit economics are more favorable given existing efficient technology stack; described as an easier journey versus Emerging Markets, though exact margin/CPCU numbers not disclosed.

key_figures.label: Revenues with over 25% YoY growth (adjusted for RMG/regulatory impact)
Developed Markets share of global ad spend

subsections.label: Growth quality and market positioning
points: 95% of revenues grew over 25% y-o-y on an adjusted basis (excluding RMG/regulatory impact), underscoring underlying growth quality across the customer base.
Developed Markets represent more than 50% of global advertising spend, framing the company's strategic push to expand its footprint and align revenue mix with this larger addressable opportunity.

key_figures.label: Historical AdColony full-company acquisition price quoted (2020-21)
Target connected devices reach (alternate figure mentioned)

subsections.label: AdColony asset acquisition
points: Strategic acquisition of AdColony assets enhances publisher ecosystem and audience intelligence capability, reinforcing ability to deliver premium consumer conversions with measurable ROI for advertisers globally.
Aim to activate over 100,000 mobile apps to reach over 500 million connected devices in Developed Markets this year (alternate figure cited in discussion as 400 million-500 million devices).

In 2020-21, the company had an opportunity to acquire the entire AdColony business/entity, but the asking price was around $400 million; in 2026, only the strategic assets (technology and brand) were acquired at a more efficient valuation — described as a 'windfall strategic gain'.

Activation of already-dealt-with apps via SDK integration will happen in the normal course of business through this year without incurring dramatically new costs, unlocking deeper reach and audience/consumer intelligence across 500 million connected devices in Developed Markets alone.

AdColony brand carries goodwill/reputation built over a decade or two among publishers in Developed Markets, expected to accelerate SDK integration and credibility with brands/advertisers versus a purely organic Affle-only approach.

subsections.label: Larger inorganic M&A
points: Company is making strong progress on the larger inorganic acquisition, entering the phase of due diligence by third-party advisors appointed by the company.
Aim to close the larger M&A by early 2027; identified targets are expected to accelerate expansion across Developed Markets by providing deeper and differentiated access to customers and verticals.

Any acquisition must be accretive on the bottom line, support a sensible margin profile, and not slow the growth trajectory; management would only proceed if convinced the combined entity (existing business plus acquisition) can deliver at least 20% combined growth and meaningful bottom-line performance (EPS and cash flow growth).
Company has raised appropriate funding to be ready for the M&A and has appointed third-party due diligence partners; will report progress as legally permissible.

10x growth vision is expected to be achieved via a combination of over 20% organic growth plus meaningful strategic acquisitions that, combined, continue to grow at 20%+; next milestone should be $1 billion of revenue, expected within the next few years via organic growth and acquisition.

subsections.label: Bobble investment situation
points: INR 136 crore investment for sale in Bobble disclosed in the press release; Bobble has reportedly filed for bankruptcy due to non-payment of debt and interest.
Management believes Bobble, as a keyboard technology platform with 15-18 million active users in India, is a valuable asset, but believes it is not being managed well by the company's management.
Court orders (Singapore arbitration/SIAC and Indian High Court) have granted Affle inspection rights into Bobble's management, which have been denied by Bobble's management despite the orders.

Management believes the insolvency proceeding was allowed to happen (for a reportedly paltry sum of INR 5 crore) to avoid clear court orders against Bobble's management; the matter has been appealed/challenged in courts with legal advice being sought.
Auditors, audit committee and Board have approved the appropriate level of disclosures.
From an accounting perspective, no reliable basis exists yet for a permanent impairment given the early stage of proceedings; impairment will be tested once the appeal is decided in NCLT.

subsections.label: Regulatory and macroeconomic headwinds
points: Regulatory and macroeconomic headwinds impacted certain customer segments such as RMG (Real Money Gaming), which was a contributor last year but not this year, and certain areas of FinTech and other categories.

After adjusting for this impact, 95%+ of revenues grew over 25% y-o-y, which management considers defensible; unclear how long it will take for market forces to normalize such that 100% of the business shows 25%+ growth.

subsections.label: Gross margin pressure from currency adjustment
points: Average CPCU rate is above INR 60, but on a currency-adjusted basis the company passes some benefit to advertisers due to currency adjustments, which has impacted margins in the short term.
A steep increase in US currency rates in the previous quarter had affected the take rate/inventory cost; this quarter's dollar movement was largely flattish.

subsections.label: Bobble insolvency risk
points: Bobble's bankruptcy filing due to non-payment of debt and interest, involving 15 million to 18 million active users in India, creates uncertainty over the INR 136 crore investment carrying value.
No permanent impairment taken yet as there is no reliable basis at this early stage; impairment testing pending NCLT appeal outcome.

subsections.label: Growth guidance reaffirmation
points: Internal execution plans are pegged at 25% growth, giving management conviction that external analyst modeling at around 20% growth is conservative, since 95% of business is actually growing at 25%+ on an adjusted basis.
At least 20%+ growth expected in Developed Markets consistently, with a differentiated business model and smaller base supporting this despite market maturity.

10x growth vision expected to be achieved in about five years (half the decade), via combination of 20%+ organic growth plus strategic acquisitions that combined also grow at 20%+; next milestone of $1 billion revenue expected in the next few years.
Management aims for two to three 10x growth cycles over the next two decades under current leadership.

subsections.label: Margin outlook
points: Margin expansion should occur within this financial year, especially in Developed Markets, aided by AdColony-driven scale (100,000+ app activations, 500 million connected devices reach) and broader strategic initiatives to enhance competitive moat.
PBT growth of 22% versus revenue growth of 20.4% already shows margin expansion at the bottom line despite regulatory/macro and currency headwinds.

subsections.label: Cash flow outlook
points: OCF to PAT ratio expected to normalize as the year progresses, with an expected 80-85% ratio by Q3 FY2027, versus 41% OCF to EBITDA conversion in Q1 FY2027.

subsections.label: M&A timeline outlook
points: Larger inorganic M&A due diligence in progress with third-party advisors; targeted to close by early 2027.
Company committed to transparency on M&A progress and will report back within legal limits.

subsections.label: Festive quarter demand outlook
points: Management remains encouraged by the demand environment across key markets as it looks ahead to the upcoming festive quarter.

key_takeaways: Q1 FY2027 marks our 14th consecutive quarter of sequential top-line growth and we recorded our highest ever quarterly revenue, EBITDA, PAT and consumer conversions.
During the quarter, we delivered revenues of INR 7.47 billion, a growth of 20.4% y-o-y.
Over 95% of our revenues witnessed over 25% growth y-o-y, adjusting for that impact, reaffirming our consistent execution on the medium-term guidance that we have committed to our stakeholders.
EBITDA stood at INR 1.68 billion for the quarter and recorded a robust 20% y-o-y growth, with stable EBITDA margins at 22.4%.
Profit After Tax for the quarter stood at INR 1.28 billion, growing by 21.7% y-o-y.

India and global Emerging Markets continue to anchor our business growth, growing by 20.2% y-o-y and contributing 72.2% of our revenues in Q1 FY2027... Developed Markets... grew by 20.7% y-o-y and contributed 27.8% of our revenues.

The strategic acquisition of AdColony assets enhances our publisher ecosystem and audience intelligence capability... We aim to unlock significant competitive advantage by activating over 100,000 mobile apps to reach over 500 million connected devices in Developed Markets this year.
We are making strong progress on the larger inorganic acquisition, as we enter the phase of due diligence by third-party advisors appointed by us. We aim to close the larger M&A by early 2027.

Our robust IP portfolio, representing 300+ unique enforceable patent claims, spans across fraud intelligence, human versus non-human data distillation, precision targeting, contextual and gesture-based advertising and next generation AI native ads and engagements across key industry verticals.

How have costs of data assets moved in response to [AI/agentic AI build-out]? ... In general, for you as a player in this ecosystem, in Developed Markets specially, how have these costs moved? Is there any advantage and opportunity specifically from that?
Trying to understand the unit economics for CTV and our broader strategy for CTV, because the base would be relatively smaller on the CTV channel and how are we seeing CTV as a space growing?

On the Developed market side, if you can help us understand the CPCU unit economics... margin will stay more or less same, but the absolute flow through would be relatively higher. Is it the right way to think about it?

Are you seeing any early signs of an impact from slowing smartphone adoption globally as high memory prices take device costs higher? Are you witnessing any sort of moderation in the incremental device additions... or any impact on replacement cycles?

OCF to EBITDA conversion was relatively weak this quarter at about 41%... Can you just dive a bit deeper into what drove this weak conversion in Q1 FY2027? Is this an active call to deepen penetration across certain geographies or verticals?

On the strong growth and margin performance, could you help us understand the impact of currency movements on this quarter and maybe the last few quarters? What part of our cost base is dollar-denominated?

If we look at in terms of increasing penetration in Developed Markets, which are the key areas, industry we want to target through organic or inorganic route? ... do you think that it can have an overall impact on our growth rates going forward?

In terms of the SDK integrations for us in Developed Markets, are you seeing greater willingness among premium app publishers to integrate Affle's SDKs? How should we think about potential SDK penetration there?
Can you give a ballpark how [the new large acquisition] can look like for Affle and how big it can be, how the margin profile will look like?

As a prudent company, do we have to write off this amount or make a provision?

quarters.summary: Affle 3i delivered its 13th consecutive quarter of sequential topline growth in Q4 FY2026 despite geopolitical macro headwinds, and management reiterated its medium-term guidance of 20%+ organic CAGR and 10x decadal growth vision, targeting EBITDA margins of 23-25% over time. The company is preparing for inorganic growth via a ~INR 11 billion preferential warrant issue to promoter Affle Holdings, with a shortlist of ~4 acquisition targets and a realistic chance of concluding a meaningfully sized transaction within calendar year 2026.
