subsections.label: Q4 FY2026 P&L drivers
points: Revenue growth sustained the 13th consecutive quarter of sequential topline growth despite challenging macro/geopolitical environment.
PAT growth (16% YoY) was relatively subdued versus EBITDA growth due to a lower effective tax rate in the base quarter (Q4 FY2025).
Profit before tax from operations (excluding other income) grew in line with EBITDA at 20.8% YoY.
Employee benefit expenses remained largely flat, aided by ongoing AI and innovation investment driving productivity.
Other expenses declined sequentially reflecting natural moderation in business promotion activity following a sequentially active Q3.
No material changes in collection risk during the quarter; working capital management remains disciplined.

subsections.label: Full-year FY2026 drivers
points: EBITDA growth of 26.3% outpaced revenue growth, reflecting operational efficiency focus.
PAT margin expanded slightly despite lower other income during the year.
Profit Before Tax from operations (excluding other income) grew 28.5% YoY, outpacing EBITDA growth and reflecting underlying strength of core operations.
Operating cash flow growth at ~25% CAGR over 5 years underscores earnings quality and disciplined working capital management.

subsections.label: Gross margin trend and rationale
points: Gross margin has been declining for the last 7-8 quarters even as absolute gross margin and EBITDA grow.
Management stated the decline is a conscious, calibrated investment decision, not a response to competition, tied to verticalization, premium positioning and going deeper into developed markets.

Investments are targeted at premium device models/touch points, CTV, and premium placements to find high lifetime value users, and to build verticalized audience/advertiser intelligence integrated with first-party data.

Management expects about a year more of this investment phase, followed by a second year of margin recovery toward better levels (implying moderation back toward 37-38% range over time), with a long-term expectation of improved margins and stronger bottom-line performance eventually.

subsections.label: Other expenses and other income bookkeeping
points: Decline in other expenses largely attributed to moderation in business promotion expenses; Q2 and Q3 are typically the highest spend quarters, with some spend in Q1; Q4 moderation is mainly on account of marketing spend timing; some additional efficiencies exist but are not significant standalone drivers.

Other income is part of treasury operations; decline mainly due to exchange gains normalization; company has been repaying borrowings (reducing cash to that extent) while also accumulating cash; large part of expenses (data/inventory costs, employees outside India) are booked as exchange-related items.

subsections.label: Capital raise for M&A
points: Board approved a preferential issue of equity shares/warrants to strengthen the balance sheet for acquisition readiness.
Corporate promoter Affle Holdings will invest to acquire ~7.4 million warrants at INR 1,487 each, totaling approximately INR 11 billion, with 25% payable upfront, post shareholder approval.

Rationale for warrant route over QIP: company already has substantial cash; warrant structure is meant to demonstrate capital strength during negotiations with target companies and to shore up certainty of cash availability given the plan to close acquisitions within the calendar year.

key_figures.label: Revenue via large ad agency group partners

subsections.label: CPCU business model scaling
points: CPCU business continued to scale in Q4 FY2026, with conversions, CPCU rate and CPCU revenue disclosed.
For the full year, the unique ROI-linked CPCU business model continued to be in a high growth momentum, driving full-year revenue growth.
CPCU model works across mobile in-app, CTV, and digital out-of-home; over 90% of focus is on in-app mobile and CTV, with a smaller percentage on digital out-of-home.
Fundamental insight is that conversion must happen inside the advertiser's environment (app or storefront), requiring deep first-party data integration.

subsections.label: Direct-to-advertiser model and agency relationships
points: Around 75% of revenue pathway is direct with the advertiser, with no other company involved in between.
Around 25%+ of revenue is through large ad agency group partners, but even there the tech stack integrates directly with the end advertiser's app because the CPCU model requires it.
Management believes the role of ad agencies will continue to be relevant but will evolve, potentially becoming more efficient or higher value.

subsections.label: Verticalized approach across industries
points: Growth has been broad-based across key industry verticals and geographies.
Competitive advantages seen across e-commerce, entertainment, fintech, food tech, and increasingly healthcare, attributed to verticalized approach and direct-to-advertiser integration.
AI algorithms and experiences are deeply verticalized for specific industry verticals, providing differentiation versus horizontal competitor solutions.

subsections.label: Customer engagement and repeat business
points: Growth anchored in existing customers spending more in existing markets and extracting new budgets in new markets where the customer already operates.
Sales and marketing teams constantly pursue new logos across industry verticals in both existing and new (under-calibrated) markets such as developed markets.
Several customers have worked with Affle for over a decade, reflecting a healthy mix of long-term retained customers and new logo additions.
Customer engagement is cyclical/budget-based (e.g., Diwali-to-Diwali budget planning in India) rather than one-time.

subsections.label: New case studies featured
points: Case study 1: driving high-value iOS shoppers' conversions for a quick commerce player in Europe, targeting high lifetime value users at key intent moments for first-time purchases.
Case study 2: driving existing gamers' conversions for a global gaming advertiser via AI-driven audience modeling and interactive creatives to boost repeat conversions and ROI.

Case study 3: scaling new user conversions and maximizing ROI for an Indian fintech customer via on-device, in-app premium placements, AI-powered intent/recommendation engine, and dynamic creative optimization.

subsections.label: AI platform integration
points: During the year, the company integrated OpticksAI and Niko into its consumer platform stack, driving improvements in creative optimization and automated campaign management.
Deepening AI-native capabilities across the organization with focused efforts on upskilling teams and embedding AI into day-to-day workflows for higher productivity and effective execution.
Adoption of OpticksAI and Niko AI seen across customers, delivering value on iOS and Android, and expanding beyond mobile to CTV.

subsections.label: IP/patent moat
points: IP portfolio spans fraud intelligence, human-versus-nonhuman distillation, precision targeting, contextual and gesture-based advertising, and next-generation AI-native ads/engagements across key verticals.

Human-vs-non-human filtration IP, filed since pre-IPO 2017, is highlighted as an increasingly important differentiator with the advent of agentic AI and AI-generated content/apps; competitors are seen as not responding to this aspect as strongly.

As agentic AI evolves, ad budgets are expected to bifurcate over the next 5 years: a large part targeting humans directly, a smaller but meaningful part targeting authenticated AI agents, with a critical need to filter out non-authenticated/noisy agents (digital fraud) — an area where Affle's IP provides advantage.

subsections.label: Industry recognition
points: Platforms ranked among top ROI-driving ad partners and growth leaders globally in the Singular ROI Index 2026, with placements across various categories.

Received Best MarTech Platform of the Year plus 5 other accolades at DIGIXX Summit and Awards 2026, Most Effective Tech Platform at the Maddies, and wins across categories at the 16th India Digital Awards.

subsections.label: GenAI/LLM ecosystem strategy
points: Company is conducting its own integrations and experimentation with LLM platforms similar to a competitor's OpenAI/ChatGPT advertising pilot (live since March 2026 in US, Australia, Canada).

Views LLM platforms as ecosystem-level plays that will spawn app stores and millions of AI-generated/human-generated apps needing consumer acquisition (CPCU spend) and ad monetization — framed as a potential new advertiser vertical/category ('GenAI apps') within its existing category structure.
Emphasizes that the greater value is in preparing the whole ecosystem (not just integrating with one underlying LLM) for the advent of GenAI apps and sites wanting advertising.

subsections.label: SDK and footprint
points: Works with SDK partners as well as its own SDK; footprint spans mobile, CTV, connected household devices, digital out-of-home, and walled garden integrations.
Footprint (across all channels reaching the consumer) exceeds 4 billion connected devices.
Footprint expansion strategy involves going deeper with publishers given the unique advertiser demand commanded via verticalized integrations.

key_figures.label: India + global emerging markets revenue share
India + global emerging markets growth YoY

subsections.label: Geographic growth balance
points: Balanced growth sustained across India and international markets in Q4 FY2026.

Growth achieved despite temporary softness in select markets and verticals during the quarter due to geopolitical events, driven by disciplined sales efforts, deeper customer engagements and new logo additions.

Developed markets delivered resilient performance and are viewed as an area where the company is currently 'under-calibrated' with long runway for growth via verticalization, premium positioning, and first-party data integration investment.
M&A strategy explicitly targets strengthening presence in developed markets (North America and Europe) via acquired customer bases and sales teams.

subsections.label: Competitive positioning vs walled gardens and GenAI natives
points: No significant change in competitive ecosystem; competitors are responding to AI in their own ways, doing what is 'appropriate and obvious'.

Affle's edge: working directly with advertisers with deeper conversion-level first-party data integrations under the CPCU model, plus deep verticalization across top industry verticals (not a horizontal solution).

Walled gardens' AI automation tools are helping them; AI is viewed as a clear tailwind across the board (walled gardens, Affle, other competitors) — the key question is who captures more of the expanded AI-oriented digital ecosystem.
Competitors largely not on CPCU model and not deeply integrated with advertisers' first-party data, making it hard to replicate Affle's positioning.

subsections.label: Barriers to entry / consolidation dynamics
points: Affle is a strong B2B platform deeply integrated with advertisers; data/app integrations across verticals and geographies are non-trivial and time-consuming to replicate.

New entrants would face high difficulty; incumbents (example cited: The Trade Desk, a DSP focused on ad agencies) would need a massive transition to shift to a CPCU, direct-to-advertiser, first-party-integrated model.
Management does not characterize the intelligence being built as 'low-cost AI' — it is deep, verticalized, premium advertiser/audience intel not readily replicable via generic cloud/AI tools.

subsections.label: SSP (supply-side platform) stance
points: Management's view on pure supply-side-focused (SSP) platforms is not favorable; believes such point solutions will be commoditized and will find it extremely hard to compete.
Affle's strategy is always to be an end-to-end platform, never gravitating to a point solution distant from the paying advertiser.

subsections.label: Resilience in macro downturn / recession
points: Management (with 21 years leading Affle) views the CPCU/ROI-linked business model as resilient and likely to become the 'go-to' model for advertisers when budgets tighten during tough economic times.

Q4 FY2026 (Jan-Mar 2026) was called out as a tough quarter geopolitically and without the benefit of festive seasonality (unlike the Oct-Dec quarter, typically the highest due to Diwali/Christmas/holidays), yet the company still grew topline and EBITDA sequentially, demonstrating resilience.

subsections.label: LTV and CPCU pricing dynamics
points: Affle differentiates conversions by lifetime value (LTV) — e.g., a premium device user's conversion is valued higher for advertisers than a lower LTV user's conversion for the same transaction type.
Over the last 10 years, CPCU volumes and CPCU pricing have both grown, attributed to rising consumer purchasing power/economic growth rather than being explicitly linked one-to-one with inflation.
Company models a long-term average inflation assumption of about 2% CAGR in its business planning, acknowledging inflation varies year to year.

subsections.label: Digital out-of-home (DOOH) outlook
points: Affle positions itself as a consumer-centric platform (not device-specific like mobile, CTV, or DOOH-only competitors), focusing on 4 billion consumer-connected devices.

DOOH is viewed as a small but interesting extension to capture the consumer's journey outside home/office, converting an 'ignored' screen into an engagement screen for tracked conversions/footfall, particularly valuable for high-LTV users who buy online and also walk into stores.
DOOH is not the emphasis point of the platform; management stated 90%+ focus is on in-app mobile and CTV.

subsections.label: M&A pipeline and process
points: Company continues to actively pursue growth opportunities strategically aligned with its 3i vision.
More than 10 companies evaluated; shortlisted to about 4 for deeper due diligence, deeper assessment, and negotiations.

Deal sizes span small, mid-sized, and larger transactions; management declined to give specific ticket-size guidance (including declining to confirm a ~$200 million ballpark) to avoid skewing analysis.
Company may execute more than one transaction during the rest of the financial year.

Realistic chance of concluding a meaningfully sized transaction within calendar year 2026 (not necessarily the full financial year), pending completion of due diligence, negotiation and governance processes.
Management will provide clearer timeline once closer to definitive agreements.

subsections.label: Acquisition target profile
points: Target capability profile: direct access to a larger base of advertisers and sales force, ideally with existing initial integrations with customers in developed markets or globally.
Strategy is to assess whether these integrations/relationships can be leveraged and transformed into Affle's verticalized, first-party-data-integrated, direct-to-advertiser CPCU platform model.
Valuation approach will be extremely conservative and prudent given it is company capital ('hard-earned money') being deployed, and given the buy-vs-build decision.

Historical precedent: acquisitions made 2020-2023 were not initially on a CPCU model and were barely breaking even on a unit economic basis; all have since been transformed into the CPCU business model, though transformation takes time (potentially by year three).
Any acquired business's sales teams would be trained to upsell/cross-sell Affle's CPCU conversion use cases to their existing customer base over time.

subsections.label: Rationale for capital raise (warrant route)
points: Purpose is to strengthen the balance sheet and demonstrate capital strength/seriousness to target companies' boards during negotiations.
Ensures the company is well capitalized and ready to move swiftly on the right acquisition opportunities this year.
Framed as a proactive, disciplined step in executing inorganic growth strategy, consistent with the calibrated discipline shown in organic growth.

subsections.label: Macro and geopolitical headwinds
points: Temporary softness in select markets and verticals during Q4 FY2026 due to geopolitical events required recalibrations.
Q4 FY2026 (Jan-Mar 2026) was a tough quarter geopolitically and lacked the tailwind of festive seasonality (unlike Oct-Dec quarter), yet the company still delivered sequential growth.
Management flagged current geopolitical situation and signs of recession as a factor being monitored, though framed CPCU as resilient in such environments.

subsections.label: Tax rate base effect
points: Q4 FY2026 PAT growth (16% YoY) was subdued in percentage terms due to a lower effective tax rate in the base quarter (Q4 FY2025).

subsections.label: Working capital / collections
points: No material changes in collection risk during the quarter; management continues to prioritize efficient working capital management.

subsections.label: Growth guidance rationale
points: Company reiterated it is firmly on course to deliver on medium-term guidance of 20% CAGR as it progresses toward its 10x decadal growth vision.
Organic growth calibration is set at around 20%; even if inorganic transactions are executed, the combined entity's goal is to average toward 20% growth in the near-to-medium term.

Management stated growth could be pushed faster but would come at the cost of profitability, since not every advertiser segment is as profitable as the ones the company focuses on; some sales orders are declined if they don't lead to profitable/sensible outcomes — priority is high-quality, predictable revenue.
Gross margin investment phase expected to last about a year more, followed by a second year of margin recovery toward better levels.
EBITDA margin trend has moved from mid-20s (implied historical range reference) to around 22-23% currently, with an explicit goal to constantly move the notch up toward the 23-25% target band.

guidance_ledger.statement: Firmly on course to deliver on medium-term guidance of 20% CAGR as we progress towards our 10x decadal growth vision; delivering about 20%+ growth over the next 5 years is our goal.
10x decadal growth vision; getting to 10x growth is a committed plan and we are on track to getting there.

Combined entity (including any inorganic transactions) should average towards 20% growth with clear emphasis on bottom-line efficiencies, delivering close to about 23% to 25% EBITDA over a period of time.

In about a year, we should be able to achieve the level of verticalization and intel needed; hopefully around that time onwards, we should see another year of bringing it back to better levels, where we don't need to invest as much.

There's a realistic chance that we may conclude a meaningfully sized transaction within this year itself (calendar year 2026); we may do more than one in terms of how we execute through the rest of this financial year.

We remain confident in the resilience of our business model and the strength of our AI-powered Consumer Platform Stack to sustain this momentum through FY2027 and beyond; we look forward to a very strong performance going forward into FY2027.

risk_register.risk: Geopolitical events causing temporary softness in select markets/verticals
risk_register.note: Required recalibrations during Q4 FY2026; growth still achieved via disciplined sales efforts, deeper customer engagements and new logo additions.

risk_register.risk: Lack of festive seasonality tailwind in Q4 (Jan-Mar) versus typical Oct-Dec peak quarter
risk_register.note: Cited as a recurring structural feature of the advertising business, compounding geopolitical headwinds in the quarter.

risk_register.risk: Signs of recession / tightening global marketing budgets
risk_register.note: Management believes CPCU/ROI-linked model becomes more attractive, not less, when advertiser budgets tighten in tough times.

risk_register.risk: Competitive response from walled gardens and GenAI-native ad platforms
risk_register.note: Viewed as a broad tailwind for AI in ad tech overall; Affle believes its direct-to-advertiser, verticalized, CPCU, first-party data model differentiates it, and competitors face high barriers to replicate this quickly.

risk_register.risk: Agentic AI / non-human traffic filtration risk (ad fraud)
risk_register.note: Emerging challenge as agentic AI grows; risk of ad budget loss to noisy, non-authenticated AI agents; Affle's human-vs-non-human IP is positioned as a mitigant/differentiator.

risk_register.risk: Lower base-quarter tax rate distorting YoY PAT growth comparison
risk_register.note: Q4 FY2026 PAT growth appears subdued (16% YoY) due to lower effective tax rate in Q4 FY2025 base quarter; full-year ETR was in line YoY (18.6% vs 18.3%).

risk_register.risk: Inflation impact on consumer disposable income / LTV / CPCU pricing
risk_register.note: Inflation can reduce consumer disposable income even as CPCU pricing has historically risen with GDP/purchasing power growth; company models ~2% long-term inflation in planning.

themes.label: CPCU business model resilience
themes.note: Management views the ROI-linked CPCU model as resilient and a likely 'go-to' model for advertisers during macro/geopolitical/recessionary tightening, evidenced by sequential growth in a tough, non-festive Q4.

themes.label: Gross margin investment for verticalization
themes.note: Gross margin has declined ~250bps over several quarters due to conscious investment in premium, verticalized audience/advertiser intelligence in developed markets; expected to normalize over roughly two years.

themes.label: Inorganic growth / M&A readiness
themes.note: ~INR 11 billion warrant issue to promoter Affle Holdings to fund M&A; pipeline narrowed from 10+ to ~4 shortlisted targets with a realistic chance of a meaningful deal closing within calendar 2026.

themes.label: AI/GenAI competitive positioning
themes.note: Direct-to-advertiser, first-party data integration, deep verticalization and human-vs-non-human filtration IP are positioned as durable moats versus walled gardens, GenAI-native platforms and DSPs like The Trade Desk.

themes.label: Developed markets expansion
themes.note: Developed markets grew 18% YoY and are described as 'under-calibrated' with a long runway for growth; M&A strategy explicitly targets bolstering developed-market presence.

themes.label: Patent/IP moat build-out
themes.note: 5 new patents granted in FY2026 taking cumulative grants to 18 (21 filed & pending, ~300 enforceable claims), reinforcing technology differentiation ahead of agentic AI proliferation.

themes.label: Medium-term growth and margin guidance
themes.note: Reiterated 20% organic CAGR and 10x decadal vision, with a new explicit EBITDA margin target band of 23-25% over time.

key_takeaways: In Q4 FY2026, we delivered revenue of INR 7.24 billion, an increase of 20.3% y-o-y, sustaining the growth momentum that has defined Affle's trajectory over the past years.

Our continued focus on improving operational efficiency and productivity translated into EBITDA of INR 1.61 billion, growing over 20.3% y-o-y. PAT stood at INR 1.20 billion, increasing by 16% y-o-y, with the growth remaining relatively subdued given our lower effective tax rate in the base quarter last year.
Our CPCU business continued to scale, delivering 120.3 million conversions at a CPCU rate of INR 60.0, translating into CPCU revenues of INR 7.21 billion.

India and global emerging markets together contributed 71.6% of our revenues, while growing by 21.2% year-on-year. Our developed markets delivered a resilient performance, growing 18.0% year-on-year, and contributed 28.4% of our revenues in Q4 FY2026.

For the full year, we delivered revenues of INR 27.1 billion, a growth of 19.5% y-o-y, with EBITDA of INR 6.1 billion at a robust growth of 26.3% y-o-y and PAT of INR 4.55 billion, growing 19.1% y-o-y.

We received 5 new patent grants during the year, taking our comprehensive IP portfolio to 18 unique patents granted and 21 filed & pending. With around 300 unique enforceable patent claims, our patents span across fraud intelligence, human versus nonhuman distillation, precision targeting, contextual and gesture-based advertising and next-generation AI native ads and engagements across key industry verticals.

Our Board has approved a preferential issue of equity shares to strengthen our balance sheet. Post our shareholders' approval, our corporate promoter, Affle Holdings, will invest to acquire ~7.4 million warrants at INR 1,487, totaling approximately INR 11 billion, with 25% upfront payment.
We are firmly on course to deliver on our medium-term guidance of 20% CAGR as we progress towards our 10x decadal growth vision.

ESCORTS.about: Escorts Ltd. is one of India’s leading engineering conglomerates engaged in the manufacturing of Agri-machinery, Construction & Material Handling Equipment and Railway Equipment. [1]

quarters.summary: Escorts Kubota posted record Q1 FY27 domestic tractor volumes and revenue growth aided by favorable rabi harvest, government procurement and positive farmer sentiment, but margins were compressed by commodity cost inflation linked to West Asia geopolitical disruption, rupee depreciation and higher logistics/import costs; management expects continued cost pressure in Q2 with partial price pass-through, cautious optimism on tractor industry (mid-single-digit growth guided for FY27), flattish export volumes in FY27 with growth expected in FY28 (esp. North America), and total capex guidance of INR850-900 crores for FY27 including greenfield land investment.

subsections.label: Margin Commentary
points: Margin during the quarter were adversely impacted by commodity cost inflation driven by geopolitical tension and related supply chain disruption.

Q1 FY27 net profit is not directly comparable YoY because Q1 FY26 reported PAT includes the RED business divestment impact; excluding the prior-year exceptional gain from sale of land and building, standalone net profit growth would be about 26% YoY.

Tractor business faced close to 5% cost impact from commodity inflation in Q1; about 1% of that is due to minimum wages for contractor labor increase in Haryana (unique to the company); excluding that, all-India industry-level commodity cost increase was about 400 basis points.
Part of the cost impact was offset by operating leverage from 23% revenue growth on the tractor business, and a ~1%-1.5% price increase taken in April.

subsections.label: Capital Allocation / Buyback
points: Promoters collectively hold about 68% plus, with non-promoter non-public shareholding (IEPF etc.) taking total to about 70%, limiting further buyback scope since buyback cannot exceed 5% while remaining listed.

Buyback possibility exists as part of capital allocation strategy but requires alignment between promoters; new buyback rules help public shareholders but not necessarily promoters whose priority is to increase promoter holding.
Company holds a cash surplus of about INR10,000 crores.

subsections.label: Capex Guidance
points: Capex divided into two categories: greenfield project (land acquisition) expected at INR450-500 crores, land already allotted and paid for; groundbreaking expected this month.
Normal capex expected at INR350-400 crores.
Total capex for the year (including greenfield investment) expected at about INR850-900 crores.

FY28 capex will depend on the greenfield construction plan; overall capex for greenfield project is INR2,000 crores; if demand continues to be good, capex on greenfield may be preponed; normal capex expected to remain in the range of INR350-400 crores.

subsections.label: Tractor Business Drivers
points: Domestic tractor industry maintained growth momentum in Q1 FY27, achieving record high first quarter volume, supported by healthy farmer cash flow, favorable crop economics, adequate reservoir levels and continued government support towards agriculture and rural development.

Company's domestic tractor sales were highest ever Q1 volume, driven by combined impact of ongoing initiatives across product portfolio enhancement, channel effectiveness and retail execution, gaining 36 basis points of market share.
Regional demand dynamics favorable with key markets North and Central outperforming other markets (North/Central ~22% growth vs other markets 15.4% growth).
Non-tractor revenue share of Agri Machinery segment revenue rose to 19% in Q1 FY27 from 18% in Q1 FY26.
Dealer inventory level currently at 30 days.

subsections.label: Product Portfolio Update
points: Shaurya series under Powertrac, launched for southern market in late Q4 FY26, is gaining traction and supporting market share gains across key southern geographies.

During the quarter, portfolio further strengthened with expansion of Digitrac range under Powertrac and new Star series under Kubota brand, enhancing presence across customer segments and applications.
Multiple product launches planned over coming months to strengthen competitiveness across core, premium and application-specific markets.
Promaxx (introduced last year) contributes over 20-22% of overall Farmtrac sales, having helped cater to the 4-wheel segment substantially and grow Farmtrac brand across the country.
Digitrac expanded with a 4x4 model, massively impacting volumes and market share across PT (Powertrac) states; contributes 23-25% of total Powertrac portfolio.

Small gap remains in Powertrac portfolio in 4-wheel drive segment (35 HP-50 HP), which company intends to cover over next few months; this segment is growing across the country and certain states are highly driven by 4-wheel segment where company has underperformed.
Farmtrac portfolio covers over 80% (close to 85%) of applications used in the country, so there is not much concern on white space there.

Kubota brand focused on 20-30 HP niche orchard/compact segment and 41-50 HP segment, which together contribute almost 70-80% of industry; company intends to continue focusing on these segments; segments over 50 HP are marginal.

Kubota brand introduced a fresh series last year to expand footprint beyond its stronghold in Western, Southern and Eastern India, helping improve situation in North and Southern markets; more products lined up this year.
4x4 segment growth is higher than normal industry growth due to Promaxx-driven volumes, though no clear-cut industry data exists for this segment.

subsections.label: Construction Equipment Business
points: CE industry growth (~23% for Crane, Backhoe loader, Mini Excavator, Compactor combined) primarily driven by the Crane industry, which grew 46% YoY; company CE volume grew 27.4% to 1,344 machines and CE segment revenue grew 39.2% to INR419.6 crores (vs 5.8% growth in the prior year).
CE segment revenue growth adversely impacted by commodity cost inflation.
Short-term challenges related to inflation due to West Asia crisis, but sustained demand expected to help normalize business health.

Q1 growth of ~45% for the Crane business is versus a subdued Q1 FY26 base impacted by BS V introduction; against a normal (non-subdued) quarter, growth would be around 20%, which is considered sustainable except for current quarter impact from good rains benefiting Agri but hurting Construction Equipment activity.

Growth driven by government push on infrastructure project completion (road construction rate was nearly half in FY26 compared to 2024-25, prompting renewed government focus); state-level developments in Andhra Pradesh (new capital city), West Bengal (new development), and traction in solar power and metro rail projects across cities.
Backhoe loaders expected to grow ~5-7% and Compactors ~5-6% for the year, while Mini Excavators and Cranes expected to see high growth.
Customers showing pushback via longer decision time and deeper negotiation due to multiple price hikes, but demand expected to be a leveler; prices expected to stabilize by Q2.
Company gained 2.7% market share in Construction Equipment last year (FY26).

subsections.label: Export Performance
points: Tractor industry export growth concentrated in >40 HP segment (~30% growth) where company presence is limited, whereas company's key export segment (<40 HP compact tractors) declined about 8%, and vessel availability challenges due to geopolitical situation impacted shipments.

Sales to Kubota global network account for approximately 61% of export volume; company continues working closely with Kubota to strengthen export portfolio and expand presence across target international markets.
Component/spare parts export was a flat quarter with expected pickup in growth going forward; growth expected to more than double over the next 2 years from the last year's base of INR160-170 crores.

subsections.label: Captive Finance / Channel Strategy
points: Captive finance company introduced in limited states with 250 dealers onboarded so far; penetration level hit 10-12% in Q1, improving to 15%+ in July.
Plan to expand to southern states this year to support new product launches and grow business there.

Idea is that captive finance helps in weak/opportunity markets where financing was a difficulty, while in stronger markets financing is not an issue; if 20-25% of volume comes through captive finance, this can lead to delta increase in overall numbers helping market share gain.
By FY27, expect almost 40-50% dealership coverage; full pan-India coverage expected by FY28.

subsections.label: Regional Demand
points: South, traditionally a weak geography, saw the highest industry growth at close to 33% versus overall industry growth of 19% in Q1; company's South market share (3-brand) stands at ~6%, gaining 0.5-0.6 percentage points in Q1 FY27.
Major company growth was in South and then in Northern and Central parts of the country.
Gujarat market growth partly aided by annual government subsidy (timing and quantum vary year to year); UP growth is organic and not related to subsidy.

subsections.label: Export Outlook
points: Industry tractor exports grew 17.7% YoY to 29,778 tractors in Q1 FY27 (from 25,307 in Q1 FY26), while company export volumes declined to 1,405 tractors from 1,733, reflecting the mix shift toward >40 HP segment where company presence is limited.
FY27 export volumes for the company expected to be more or less flattish, despite Q1 decline, as the balance three quarters are expected to make up for it.
FY28 export growth expected to be good; North American market may start opening up, and if the company begins exporting there, volumes are expected to do very well.

subsections.label: Commodity & Geopolitical Risk
points: Geopolitical uncertainties in West Asia continue to disrupt supply chains and freight markets.
Shipping disruption and depreciation of Indian Rupee against the US Dollar increased commodity, logistics and imported component costs.

Tractor business faced ~5% cost impact from commodity inflation in Q1, with further 1.5-2% pressure expected in Q2; company expects this to be a temporary phenomenon with possible reversal starting from Q4, though geopolitical situation remains difficult to predict.

Price increases taken will not fully compensate for cost increases; any price hikes taken will be permanent in nature (no rollback) since companies won't disturb the market for a short-term 3-4 month cost spike.
Construction equipment sector faces short-term inflation challenges related to West Asia crisis.

subsections.label: Seasonal / Monsoon Risk
points: Monsoon distribution and festive seasonal demand, especially against the high base of last year, flagged as key monitorables for coming months.
Good rains this quarter, while beneficial for Agri sector, are expected to negatively impact Construction Equipment activity this quarter.

subsections.label: Customer Pushback Risk
points: Customers in construction equipment segment showing pushback to price hikes via longer decision-making time and deeper price negotiations.

subsections.label: Tractor Industry Outlook
points: Underlying demand environment for tractor industry remains supportive; company remains cautiously optimistic on industry outlook while tracking geopolitical developments and commodity cost trends.

Previous guidance of plus/minus 2-3% variation revised upward; management now expects mid-single-digit growth for the industry for the financial year, based on strong Q1 and last 45-50 days of positive trends.
Company expects to grow above industry mid-single-digit growth due to continued market share gains.

subsections.label: Margin/Pricing Outlook
points: Further cost pressure of 1.5-2% expected in Q2 on top of the already continuing 5% cost impact; discussions on price pass-through ongoing but quantum not finalized; expected to happen sometime this quarter.
Price increase will not cover the entire material cost increase; expectation is for the situation to stabilize and possibly reverse from Q4.

subsections.label: Construction Equipment Outlook
points: CE industry overall growth for the year expected in the range of 12-15%; Mini Excavators and Cranes expected to see high growth; Backhoe loaders expected to grow 5-7%; Compactors 5-6%.
Company to continue being aggressive in Crane segment, supported by new models launching from October onwards, targeting both specific applications and entry-level products.

Cumulative price hike in Crane segment since last year stands at 15-16%; cumulative price increase so far in H1 FY27 (including January hike) is 5%, with effective price increase passed on (after channel discount adjustment) at 6%.

subsections.label: Export Outlook
points: FY27 tractor export volumes expected to be flattish; FY28 expected to see good growth, especially if North American market opens up.
Component exports: flat this quarter, but growth expected in second half; over the next 2 years, company expects component export revenue (from ~INR160-170 crores last year) to more than double.

subsections.label: Capex Outlook
points: Total capex for FY27 guided at approximately INR850-900 crores, including greenfield land investment (INR450-500 crores) and normal capex (INR350-400 crores).
FY28 capex could be higher if greenfield construction is expedited, given overall greenfield capex plan is INR2,000 crores; normal capex expected to remain INR350-400 crores range.

subsections.label: Captive Finance Outlook
points: By FY27, almost 40-50% of dealerships expected to be covered by captive finance; full pan-India coverage targeted by FY28.

guidance_ledger.statement: Currently, we are looking at a middle or mid-single-digit growth for the financial year (revised from earlier plus/minus 2-3% variation guidance).
Growth for Escorts should be higher than the mid-single digit anticipated for the industry, due to continued market share gains.
On top of the continuing 5% cost impact, another 1.5% to 2% sort of pressure will be there in Q2.
We are hoping it will start getting reversal in Q4 [regarding commodity cost pressure].
There would be a price hike going forward, but the quantum and date we've yet to finalize.
Overall for the whole year, we are looking at anywhere between 12% to 15% overall industry growth.
Backhoe loaders will grow at about 5% to 7%.
Compactors also will grow at about 5% to 6%.
This year, FY '27, we expect the export to be more or less flattish in nature; overall volumes will be flat in FY27.
FY28, we are looking at a good growth coming in; North American market may start opening up, and if we start exporting there, numbers will do very well.
In another 2 years, we're looking at almost more than doubling the numbers [component export revenue, from ~INR160-170 crores last year].
Overall, about INR850 crores to INR900 crores of capex for this year, including greenfield investment (INR450-500 crores for land) and normal capex (INR350-400 crores).
FY28 capex will depend on the greenfield plan; overall greenfield capex is INR2,000 crores; if demand continues good, some capex may be preponed; normal capex will remain INR350-400 crores.
By FY27, we expect almost 40%, 50% dealership will get covered; by FY28, pan-India coverage.
From a normal quarter (non-subdued base), the growth would have been somewhere around 20%, which we feel is sustainable.

risk_register.risk: Geopolitical uncertainty in West Asia disrupting supply chains and freight markets
risk_register.note: Continues to disrupt supply chain and freight market, driving commodity/logistics/import cost inflation.

risk_register.risk: Rupee depreciation against US Dollar increasing costs
risk_register.note: Increased commodity, logistics and imported component costs during the quarter.

risk_register.risk: Commodity cost inflation (metal and rubber)
risk_register.note: Tractor business faced ~5% cost impact in Q1 with further 1.5-2% pressure expected in Q2; expected temporary with possible reversal from Q4.

risk_register.risk: Minimum wage increase for contractor labor in Haryana
risk_register.note: Contributed about 1% of the cost impact, unique to the company.

risk_register.risk: Vessel/shipping availability challenges
risk_register.note: Impacted export shipments during the quarter due to geopolitical situation.

risk_register.risk: High base effect / seasonal demand uncertainty
risk_register.note: Monsoon distribution and festive seasonal demand against high base of last year flagged as key monitorable.

risk_register.risk: Rain impact on construction activity
risk_register.note: Good rains beneficial for Agri sector but expected to impact construction activities this quarter.

risk_register.risk: Customer pushback on price hikes (Construction Equipment)
risk_register.note: Customers taking longer to decide and deeper negotiation to fetch prices due to multiple price hikes.

risk_register.risk: Limited market presence in >40 HP export segment
risk_register.note: Industry export growth concentrated in >40 HP segment where company presence remains limited.

themes.label: Commodity cost inflation
themes.note: Metal, rubber and imported component costs rose due to West Asia geopolitical disruption and rupee depreciation, compressing EBITDA margin to 11.2% from 13.1%.

themes.label: Tractor market share gains
themes.note: Company grew domestic tractor sales 22.9% YoY vs industry 18.6%, gaining 36 bps market share aided by new product launches (Shaurya, Promaxx, Digitrac, Star series).

themes.label: New product launches driving growth
themes.note: Promaxx, Digitrac, Shaurya and Kubota's new series are driving volume and share gains across regions, with more launches planned including a 4x4 series to close portfolio gaps.

themes.label: Construction Equipment demand recovery
themes.note: CE volumes grew 27.4% aided by government infrastructure push, though partly against a low BS-V transition base; FY27 industry growth guided at 12-15%.

themes.label: Pricing action / pass-through
themes.note: Price hikes taken (tractors ~1.5% in April; CE ~6% cumulative) are only partially offsetting cost inflation, with further hikes under consideration but not finalized amid competitive/demand sensitivities.

themes.label: Export headwinds
themes.note: Company's key <40HP export segment declined 8% amid vessel availability challenges; FY27 export volumes expected flattish, with growth anticipated in FY28 via North American market opening.

themes.label: Captive finance expansion
themes.note: Captive finance penetration rising (10-12% in Q1, 15%+ in July) across 250 onboarded dealers, expected to reach 40-50% dealership coverage by FY27 and pan-India by FY28, aiding share gains in weaker markets.

key_takeaways: Operating revenue from the continuing operation at INR3,178.9 crores, up by 28% year-on-year.
EBITDA at INR355.4 crores, up by 9.4% Y-o-Y. EBITDA margin in Q1 at 11.2% as compared to 13.1% in the corresponding quarter.
PBT from continuing operations before exceptional item at INR493.8 crores, up by 18.2% Y-o-Y, highest ever in Q1.
Net profit from continuing operations stood at INR387.3 crores, up by 4% Y-o-Y; excluding prior year exceptional gain of INR76 crores, net profit grew by 26% Y-o-Y.

Our domestic tractor sales stood at 35,457 tractors, highest ever in Q1 volume for the company, registering a growth of 22.9% year-on-year and as compared to industry growth of 18.6% Y-o-Y. This translates into 36 basis point gain in share of market during the quarter.
Construction Equipment segment revenue came at INR419.6 crores, up by 39.2% as against 5.8% in the corresponding quarter, adversely impacted due to commodity cost inflation.
Margin during the quarter were adversely impacted by commodity cost inflation driven by geopolitical tension and related supply chain disruption.
On the export front, the tractor industry exported 29,778 tractors in Q1 FY '27, up by 17.7%... our export volumes stood at 1,405 tractors as compared to 1,733 tractors in Q1 FY '26.
Currently, we are looking at a middle or mid-single-digit growth for the financial year [tractor industry FY27 outlook].
pressing_questions: Aniket: So you mentioned the fact that costs will further increase in Q2. Just wanted to understand how much of a price hike would be needed further to sort of offset this cost increase?

Preet: Are we seeing any pushback from the customer due to multiple price hike, like you mentioned 6%, 7% last year and 6%, 7% this year, total cranes, you would have taken 15%, 16% price hike. Are we seeing any postponement of purchase for this year? Or is there -- because a lot of price hike would have happened in the month of May and June. So is this 12% to 15% number shall we consider as a conservative or somewhat aggressive kind of number?

Vikram Damani: We have cash surplus of almost INR10,000 crores. Our capex requirements are nowhere sort of close to that, plus we are getting -- generating cash every year. Given the change in the buyback rules, can we expect something along those lines?

GLOBUSSPR.about: Globus Spirits Limited, established in 1992 is primarily engaged in the business of manufacture and sale of Indian Made Indian Liquor (IMIL), Indian Made Foreign Liquor (IMFL), Bulk Alcohol hand sanitizer, and Franchise Bottling. It has a unique 360⁰ model straddling across the entire alcohol value chain. It is the 1st to set up a grain distillery and launch branded DDGS in India. [1] [2] [3]

quarters.summary: Q1 FY27 revenue grew 13% YoY to INR789 crores (corrected to INR788.8 mn/INR7,888 million), EBITDA grew 33% YoY to INR79.5 crores at 10% margin, and PAT grew 49% YoY (corrected) to INR27.6 crores at 4% margin, driven by better capacity utilization, improved manufacturing profitability, and continued resilience in R&O with stronger traction in P&A. Management maintained manufacturing EBITDA/litre guidance of INR5-7, R&O EBITDA margin guidance of 15-17%, capacity utilization guidance around 85% (Q1 came in at a record 89%), and reiterated no major capex plans besides INR50-60 crore maintenance capex, with debt reduced to INR650 crores net debt from INR660 crores in March.

subsections.label: Corrections issued during call
points: Company clarified via footnote that Revenue, PAT and PAT growth were inadvertently misstated during the call as INR7,887 million, INR278 million and 50%; corrected figures are Revenue INR7,888 million, PAT INR276 million and PAT growth 49%, as per financial results, investor presentation and other filings.
EBITDA per litre for the manufacturing segment was inadvertently said as INR6.6 during the call; the correct figure as per financial results, investor presentation and other filings is INR6.5.

subsections.label: Capital allocation and debt
points: Refinancing and debt optimization actions already undertaken have contributed to improvement in current ratio to 1.01x and interest coverage to 3.14x.
Net debt is at the same level of INR650 crores versus INR660 crores in March 2026.
Capital discipline is a key part of growth strategy; entire P&A business has been self-funded from cash flow generated by manufacturing and R&O businesses.
Once capex plans finished after commissioning the UP facility, no further capacity expansion is planned; all cash generation is being fed into growing P&A.

P&A investments show up as other expenses (manpower, marketing etc.); P&A margin has improved from approximately 60% negative a couple of years ago to nearly breakeven now, with profitability expected sooner rather than later.

Strategy going forward is quarterly cash generation feeding P&A growth while maintaining healthy debt pay-down; management sees some growth opportunities being missed and is looking for solutions while maintaining balance sheet health.

key_figures.label: UP captive consumption share of capacity

subsections.label: Overall performance drivers
points: Performance reflects structural improvements across the business: better capacity utilization, improved manufacturing profitability, and continued resilience in R&O with stronger traction in P&A.

Manufacturing gives supply security, cost control, quality consistency, and free cash flow; consumer business gives the opportunity to build brands, deepen distribution, and improve quality of growth over time.

subsections.label: Manufacturing (Bulk/ENA-Ethanol)
points: Business supported by strong ENA demand across states.
Manufacturing is described as an active operating platform, not a passive capacity business; company continues to optimize between products, raw materials, geographies, and customer opportunities.
Objective is not to maximize volume in a quarter but to optimize margin, cash flow, and strategic supply for the consumer business.

UP facility is becoming increasingly important as UP is a key consumer market; manufacturing capability in the state gives a structural advantage, improving ability to service demand, manage costs, and support both R&O and P&A.

subsections.label: P&A (Prestige & Above)
points: Growth was broad-based across states, supported by stronger traction in brands such as Terai, Snoski, and Brothers & Co.
Growth is not dependent on a single brand or single market; coming from geographical expansion, deeper distribution, and better market execution across portfolio.

Negative EBITDA is comfortable at this stage as investments go into distribution, brand visibility, and market development; focus is not just volume growth but building profitable, sustainable markets.

P&A viewed through core markets (building depth/profitability) vs emerging markets (foundational investments for future growth engines) framework, keeping expansion disciplined; company enters markets where portfolio has 'right to win'.

Growth drivers vary by brand and geography because the category sits differently in different markets (e.g., UP differs from Delhi, West Bengal, Assam, Jharkhand) based on which segment - vodka, semi-premium, deluxe whiskey - has high salience; fluctuations in brand performance across states are expected to continue for the next couple of years as more markets are added.
Company sees itself as having a portfolio of three-four solid P&A brands and a similar number of powerful luxury brands, not dependent on a single brand or state.
Snoski gaining traction in UP with new variants (chili mango and jamun flavours) launched.

Emerging markets keep moving into core markets over time as they perform; benchmark used is that in the third complete year after launch, a state should become a profitable growth state; first-phase states have already crossed that threshold.

Total presence now 11 states including luxury; 6 states being driven toward core status, of which 4 (including Delhi, UP) are already core and 2 are on the verge; intention is to reach 10 core states in a couple of years.
Assam and Jharkhand P&A entries are giving positive energy; consumer and trade partners have welcomed with open arms, high level of acceptance, good tidings expected ahead.

subsections.label: R&O (Regular & Others)
points: R&O not only continues to provide resilience and cash generation but has also started growing volumes.
Rajasthan continued to deliver stable and consistent performance, remaining an important mature market demonstrating strength of execution in R&O.

UP R&O is now scaling well; milestone significant because UP is a large market where manufacturing presence, distribution capability, and portfolio strategy work together to sustain growth, given the size of business available there.

Strategy is to build value in layers: R&O gives foundation for scale, distribution and cash generation; P&A is the future core expanding reach and improving mix; luxury portfolio intended to strengthen aspiration, innovation and long-term brand equity.
R&O inventory is very low (under a week), quick in/quick out, largely cash or short 1-2 day credit business, hence a good cash flow business.

Haryana R&O: company has stayed slow on investment due to a 'yo-yo' regulatory environment; is doing away with some legacy portfolio, renovating/upgrading and launching new products as consumer taste/packaging profiles evolve; expects modest growth in Haryana over next two-three quarters.
Delhi R&O: company has secured a tender and is re-entering Delhi after a lull; this is a tender-driven market dependent on tender volumes.

West Bengal R&O: currently going through steps of getting regulatory approvals; management confident approvals are 'round the corner', expects to secure them this quarter and re-enter the market within about 60 days after approval; market environment applies equally to all players, and management does not see the market becoming unfavorable — at worst status quo, possibly slightly better.

subsections.label: Capacity outlook
points: Aside from maintenance capex of about INR50-60 crores per year, no plans for capex to increase ENA/ethanol capacity.
Aside from incremental changes of maybe 1% or so due to new technologies over time, no significant change in capacity expected as part of FY29 strategy.

Despite significant industry-wide oversupply/overcapacity of ethanol at E20 levels over the last few quarters, company has been able to utilize facilities well over 85%, and this quarter achieved a record 89% at a higher installed capacity base, due to flexible product nature of facilities between ENA and ethanol.

subsections.label: UP plant
points: UP plant capacity utilization is more than 90% (per CFO), running well with no red flags.

About 25% of UP capacity is utilized captively, with the rest currently bulk sale; this ratio changes month-on-month because the facility is both a molasses and grain facility, requiring capacity optimization between producing and storing different materials.

UP has become a very important international sales source given positive UP government policy encouraging international sales; the unit has been pivoted to be a flagship international sales source, and the optimization of internal versus external volumes is still underway.

subsections.label: State-level market notes
points: West Bengal IMIL market is about 26-27 lakh cases a month (just above 2.5 million cases), a sizable market, slightly smaller than Rajasthan and Haryana individually.
Distributor network in UP is a private network mandated by excise policy (no corporation model as in some other markets); company follows excise processes and rules to distribute brands.
UP is described as a huge market (almost 95-odd lakh cases a month) for R&O.

subsections.label: Raw material sourcing and inventory
points: Company has secured raw material supply from FCI at a fixed price through the year across different regions based on capacity locations.
Company can take a limited (not entire) position on maize purchase mix to lock in price for the period that has seen most inflation.
Broken rice is subject to inflationary pressures without a hedging mechanism available.
Company has managed to secure inventories giving good cover going into Q3 and Q4 despite monsoon-related concerns; no dramatic impact seen on the maize crop scheduled for this time.
Q2 is historically a more inflationary quarter for agri commodities (fuel and raw material) every year; this is already budgeted for.
Company does not carry significant PET bottle or raw material inventories in Rajasthan operation due to its scale, so cannot take meaningful positions on PET prices.

In UP, inventory is managed via a combination of company-managed warehouses (inventory on books) and third-party managed warehouses (ex-factory sale, no meaningful inventory number, only a few days' worth).
R&O inventory is very low in number of days due to quick in/quick out nature and mostly cash/short-credit sales model.

subsections.label: Ethanol/E20 controversy
points: Recent social media/press controversy on E20 ethanol blend allegedly damaging passenger car engines; automobile associations, automobile manufacturers and petrol companies have clarified there is no such damage being reported.
Management does not see this controversy impacting overall ethanol demand; ethanol offtake for the industry is very sticky and has been fairly consistent over recent months, growing about 7.5% YoY.

subsections.label: Input cost inflation - glass/PET/energy
points: Recent inflation seen across the board in glass and PET; cost-push of glass, depending on brand and pack, is in double digits, in mid-teens, moving between 10% and 16-17%.
This cost-push 'yo-yo' is expected to persist for a while in both glass and PET; energy prices also flow through various parts of the business in various forms.

Management does not currently see significant impact from raw material price inflation on R&O margins; whatever had to happen has happened in Q1, with no further impact expected, though it remains a 'wait and watch' situation; aggressive growth is seen as positioning the company better than peers to withstand this challenge.

subsections.label: UK FTA / Scotch price impact
points: UK FTA becoming reality is expected to be a tailwind, but situation is still vague as it depends on whether overseas partners change base prices; no indications yet of any tinkering on pricing from the other side.

Rupee has depreciated 20% against the pound over the last year, so overall business impact from the FTA is not expected to be very significant; company is not a market maker for scotch prices and will get whatever benefit comes as will other players.
Focus remains on execution in markets rather than banking on FTA-driven price benefits.

subsections.label: Regulatory/state policy risk
points: Bihar prohibition: difficult to give timelines on policy change, but management believes prohibition in Bihar will eventually be reversed; expectation is 1-2 years for the new Chief Minister's tenure to see a change start happening, with a full reversal potentially over a 2-year period.

West Bengal R&O re-entry pending regulatory/manufacturing license approvals, expected this quarter with market re-entry ~60 days after approval; regulatory delays of a month or two either way are normal for final hurdles.

subsections.label: Monsoon/agri commodity risk
points: Rainfall deficit in eastern north India this year; company has created a hedge for raw materials in the east and does not see any significant change this year over last year.
No material impact seen on the all-India manufacturing margin guidance of INR5-7 per litre from this rainfall deficit.

subsections.label: Priorities for balance of FY27
points: Keep manufacturing business operating efficiently and within a disciplined margin framework.
Continue to build R&O as a resilient and growing consumer business.
Scale P&A with focus on market depth, brand strength, and profitable growth.
Maintain balance sheet discipline while investing behind the long-term opportunity.
Objective is to create a stronger, broader, and higher quality alcobev company with manufacturing depth, consumer reach, and financial discipline, built quarter by quarter.

subsections.label: Manufacturing margin guidance
points: Guidance on margin per litre is INR5 to INR7; Q1 performance (INR6.5/litre) is firmly within that range.
Going forward, similar range-bound performance is expected in this business; not concerned about margin changes within the INR5-7 range for the rest of the year.
All-India manufacturing margin guidance of INR5-7 maintained for all quarters of this year despite eastern rainfall deficit concerns.

subsections.label: R&O margin guidance
points: R&O EBITDA margin guidance is around 15% to 17%, down from the 17-18% levels achieved in the last couple of years, primarily due to UP's slightly lower price point/margin profile compared to Rajasthan as UP grows exceedingly fast within the mix — this is described as a mix/state-mix change, not a structural impact from raw material inflation.

subsections.label: Capacity utilization guidance
points: Guidance around 85% capacity utilization; Q1 came in significantly higher at 89%.

subsections.label: Ethanol demand outlook
points: Ethanol demand at current scale expected to grow at about 7% to 7.5%, in line with petrol growth; E20 remains the main demand driver.

Talk of additional blending grades (E85, E50) exists but requires vehicle compatibility; some launches from Maruti seen, but not enough compatible cars yet; focus remains on E20 growing at the same rate as petrol consumption.

subsections.label: P&A profitability trajectory
points: P&A margin has improved from approximately 60% negative EBITDA margin a couple of years ago to nearly breakeven now, with profitability expected 'sooner rather than later'.

subsections.label: UP R&O growth outlook
points: Management declines to quantify UP R&O growth per quarter (e.g., whether 0.1 million cases added per month), citing an FY29 guideline for UP already given and reluctance to project quarter-by-quarter growth in a market being actively fought for; UP will continue to resonate strongly as the next big bankable opportunity in R&O.

subsections.label: P&A core/emerging market growth outlook
points: Declined to give specific split of growth between mature vs newer P&A states, citing that emerging markets keep moving into core over time, distorting any fixed benchmark; intention is to reach 10 core states in a couple of years from the current 5 core (6th approaching).

guidance_ledger.statement: Guidance on margin per litre is about INR5 to INR7. We are firmly within that in Q1. Going forward, I'm expecting similar range-bound performance in this business.
Our guidance for R&O has been around 15% to 17% EBITDA margins... rather than 17%, 18% levels, that's going to come down to maybe 15%, 16% levels.
Our guidance is around 85%, so this quarter has been significantly higher than our guidance.
Aside from maintenance capex which we have a guidance of about INR50 crores, INR60 crores a year, we don't have any plans for capex in increasing ENA/ethanol capacity.
I do not see any significant change in capacity as part of our FY29 strategy at least, aside from incremental changes of maybe 1% or so due to new technologies.
The intention is to, in a couple of years, actually reach 10 core states.
We are expecting ethanol demand at this scale to grow at about 7%, 7.5%, which is in line with petrol growth.
As of now there is a reasonable view that this quarter we should be able to secure them [regulatory approvals]. We will after that within 60 days or so we should be able to get back into the market.
My expectation is 1 to 2 years of the new Chief Minister for it to -- for a change to start happening over a 2-year period would be a complete reversal.
We are also dreaming to stay very aggressive in UP. We will see high growth coming out of our UP R&O... it is our next big bankable opportunity in R&O.

guidance_ledger.metric: P&A growth split by market maturity
guidance_ledger.statement: It gets very difficult to start giving these breakdowns... your base will keep on getting so distorted every 2, 3 quarters that any number that you start putting it as a benchmark will raise more queries than answers.
From approximately 60% or so negative margin a couple of years ago, we are now at nearly at breakeven. In fact, we should be getting to profitability sooner rather than later.
Haryana at this point of time, I still see modest growths in the next two-three quarters from where I look at it.

guidance_ledger.metric: UP captive vs external capacity optimization
guidance_ledger.statement: It's about 25% internal, but we need to optimize that in the quarters to come.
Maintaining a reasonably healthy debt pay down as the years go by... maintaining a healthy balance sheet.
INR5 to INR7 is our guidance for the EBITDA per liter... FY26 was that range and FY27, we expect the same range.
INR500 crores is what we have called out (not INR1,000 crores).
We are totally committed to delivering the FY29 objective... managing a 50% total growth on our P&A portfolio.
20 crores is what the other units will give us aside from UP, and UP should give us about somewhere around 2 crores liters... well over 20 crores will be the target for this year.
I believe in the coming year, Rajasthan plus UP will give us higher than 7% growth. At this point, we are not in a position to give a more specific guidance.
Interest will go back to around INR14 crores, INR15 crores per quarter.
This year, we do not see a need to achieve the business plan given some of the operational improvements and leverage we've been able to get... this year, we don't see a need at all.
We have systematically reduced our annual debt outflow from INR67 crores per annum to just INR14 crores projected for FY27.
When we said the 8 states, that is a minimum number where we definitely are ensuring the expansion will happen.
It becomes an additional volume driver... this number can keep on increasing.

risk_register.risk: E20 ethanol blend controversy over alleged engine damage
risk_register.note: Social media/press controversy; automobile associations, manufacturers and petrol companies clarified no damage reported; no impact on overall ethanol demand seen.

risk_register.risk: Ethanol/ENA industry oversupply and overcapacity
risk_register.note: Significant oversupply at E20 has persisted for several quarters, but company still utilizing facilities well over 85% (89% this quarter) due to flexible ENA/ethanol product mix.

risk_register.risk: Glass and PET cost-push inflation
risk_register.note: Cost-push in glass is in double digits (10-16/17%), expected to persist for a while in both glass and PET; energy prices also flow through various parts of business.

risk_register.risk: Agri commodity (maize, broken rice) seasonal inflation
risk_register.note: Q2 is historically inflationary for agri commodities every year; already budgeted for; broken rice has no hedge available, limited maize hedging possible.

risk_register.risk: Rainfall deficit in eastern north India
risk_register.note: Company has created a hedge for raw materials in the east; no significant change seen this year vs last year; no material impact expected on manufacturing margin guidance.

risk_register.risk: Bihar prohibition
risk_register.note: No timeline visibility on policy change; management believes reversal is likely over 1-2 years under new Chief Minister.

risk_register.risk: West Bengal R&O regulatory/license delay
risk_register.note: Still going through regulatory approval steps; expected this quarter with re-entry ~60 days after; delays of a month or two on final hurdles are normal.

risk_register.risk: Haryana R&O environment uncertainty ('yo-yo')
risk_register.note: Company has stayed slow on R&O investment in Haryana due to environment volatility; expects modest growth only.

risk_register.risk: UK FTA / Scotch pricing uncertainty
risk_register.note: Situation still vague depending on whether overseas partners change base prices; rupee depreciated 20% vs pound over past year limiting significant impact; company not a market maker for scotch prices.

risk_register.risk: Rising operating expenses / capital needs vs shareholder returns
risk_register.note: Analyst flagged rising opex and expansion capital needs; management says P&A self-funded from manufacturing/R&O cash flow, no further capacity capex planned, focus on capital discipline while growing P&A.

risk_register.risk: Geopolitical (Iran crisis) driven input cost inflation - glass bottles/PET, logistics, freight
risk_register.note: Caught company by surprise; efficiency/mitigation measures rolled out across packaging, raw material, freight; expected impact to be modest, not severe.

risk_register.risk: Delhi (R&O) excise policy volatility
risk_register.note: Policy in complete flux with some periods at zero volumes; company halted R&O operations in Delhi until policy stabilizes.

risk_register.risk: West Bengal license transition / regulatory delay
risk_register.note: Manufacturing license shift in process with no committed timeline for relaunch; impact now largely negligible going into FY27.

risk_register.risk: Haryana market instability
risk_register.note: Described as still a 'yoyo' market.

risk_register.risk: Seasonal agri-commodity cost inflation
risk_register.note: Annual feature - costs rise end of Q1 into Q2 (monsoon-related) and ease end of Q3/Q4.

risk_register.risk: ENA supply/permission lead-time friction
risk_register.note: Longer state-permission process for ENA vs ethanol caused one-time inventory buildup in Q4, expected to normalize in Q1.

risk_register.risk: UP margin dilution risk
risk_register.note: UP growth is less profitable than Rajasthan volumes, expected to pull down blended R&O margin from Q4's 18% toward 16-18% target range.

themes.label: Bulk manufacturing margin stability (ENA/ethanol mix)
themes.note: Manufacturing EBITDA/litre guidance of INR5-7 maintained; Q1 delivered INR6.5/litre at record 89% capacity utilization despite industry-wide ethanol oversupply, aided by flexible ENA/ethanol product mix.

themes.label: P&A core-to-emerging market transition (FY29 vision)
themes.note: P&A revenue up 35% YoY/38% QoQ with broad-based growth across brands (Terai, Snoski, Brothers & Co.); core states now at 5 (6th approaching) with intention to reach 10 core states in a couple of years; P&A margin improving from ~60% negative to near breakeven.

themes.label: Regulatory/state policy tailwinds (Bihar, WB, UP, Karnataka)
themes.note: West Bengal R&O re-entry pending regulatory approvals expected this quarter with re-entry ~60 days later; Bihar prohibition reversal expected over 1-2 years; UP continues to scale strongly as manufacturing/distribution advantage plays out.

themes.label: Geopolitical cost inflation (glass/logistics)
themes.note: Glass cost-push inflation in double digits (10-16/17%) expected to persist for a while in both glass and PET, with energy prices also flowing through various parts of the business.

themes.label: Debt optimization / deleveraging
themes.note: Net debt flat to slightly down at INR650 crores (vs INR660 crores in March); current ratio improved to 1.01x and interest coverage to 3.14x via refinancing and debt optimization actions.

themes.label: Ethanol blending / ENA export tailwind
themes.note: Ethanol demand expected to grow ~7-7.5% in line with petrol growth; company leveraging international ENA sales, especially via UP plant now pivoted as a flagship international sales source, to utilize capacity amid domestic ethanol oversupply.

themes.label: UK FTA scotch price tailwind
themes.note: UK FTA expected to be a tailwind for whisky brands (Mountain Oak, Brothers & Co.) but situation remains vague pending whether overseas partners adjust base prices; rupee depreciation of 20% vs pound over the past year limits the expected magnitude of benefit.

key_takeaways: Revenue from operations grew 13% year-on-year to INR7,887 million (corrected to INR7,888 million). EBITDA grew 33% to INR795 million (INR79.5 crores) and PAT grew 50% year-on-year to INR278 million (corrected to 49% growth and INR276 million).
EBITDA margins improved to 10% at an overall basis and PAT margins improved to 4%.

Manufacturing Segment grew 11% year-on-year to INR4,720 million. Sales volume stood at 56.11 million litres with capacity utilization at 89%. Overall, the EBITDA margin for this business was INR6.6 per litre (corrected to INR6.5 per litre).
P&A revenue grew 35% year-on-year and 38% sequentially to INR550 million. Volumes grew 45% year-on-year and 45% sequentially to 0.42 million cases. EBITDA for the quarter was negative INR13 million.

In regular and others, revenue grew 10% year-on-year to INR2,564 million. Volumes grew 13% year-on-year to 4.48 million cases and EBITDA grew 13% year-on-year to INR440 million. UP R&O volumes grew 2.4 times year-on-year and crossed 0.2 million cases per month during the quarter.

The company reported a revenue of INR789 crores, representing a year-on-year growth of 13%. EBITDA for the quarter stood at INR79.5 crores, registering a growth of 33% over the corresponding period last year, while EBITDA margin stood at 10%. Profit after tax for the quarter was INR28 crores, reflecting a strong year-on-year growth of 49%. PAT margin for the quarter stood at 4%.
Improvement in current ratio to 1.01x and the interest coverage to 3.14x.
Net debt is at the same level of INR650 crores as of June 2026, versus INR660 crores in March 2026.
pressing_questions: How much additional volume growth can be achieved without any major capacity expansion, and at what utilization level would the next capex cycle become necessary?

Given UP volumes grew on a lower base at 0.2 million cases exit run rate, what sort of incremental monthly growth (e.g., 0.1 million cases/month) should be expected going forward, and will R&O margins normalize as absolute EBITDA grows?
Can a breakdown of P&A growth between mature/core states and newer/emerging states be provided to understand repeats and depth of brands?

One of the key competitors in UP's IMFL segment holds ~40% market share but delivers only single-digit EBITDA margin — what gives confidence that Globus can achieve double-digit EBITDA margins in R&O?
What is the current capacity utilization of the UP plant specifically?

quarters.summary: Management reiterated commitment to its FY29 Vision (consumer/P&A revenue target of INR500 crores, ~50% total P&A portfolio growth), guided bulk manufacturing EBITDA to remain in the INR5-7/liter range for FY27, expects debt outflow to drop sharply (from INR67cr to INR14cr p.a.) post refinancing freeing up ~INR53cr liquidity, and paused its planned equity fundraise as internal accruals and debt optimization are seen as sufficient to fund the FY27 consumer expansion plan; company flagged near-term cost headwinds from geopolitical/logistics/glass-bottle price pressures which it expects to largely mitigate.

subsections.label: Debt optimization
points: Most critical intervention this quarter was optimization of long-term debt profile via comprehensive strategic refinancing of existing term loans.
Refinancing leveraged strengthened credit profile to secure superior interest rates and optimize repayment schedule.
Reduced annual debt outflow from INR67 crores to INR14 crores projected for FY27, unlocking INR53 crores of direct liquidity for consumer business expansion, bypassing need for external equity.
Blended interest rate across all borrowings reduced by 50 basis points through refinancing and treasury management.

subsections.label: Deleveraging and capital efficiency
points: Reduced absolute borrowings by INR57 crores in FY26 vs FY25 while expanding consumer footprint, funding growth through internal accruals not balance sheet.
Current ratio crossed 1x threshold (0.96x to 1.01x), indicating elimination of short-term liquidity deficits and shift to operational surplus.
Interest coverage ratio nearly doubled (1.76x to 3.14x), derisking enterprise against macro/interest rate shocks.
ROE increased 3x in FY26 vs FY25 through debt reduction, lower interest burden and optimized asset utilization.

subsections.label: Interest cost dynamics (Q&A)
points: Q4 interest cost jump of INR3 crores was due to UP term loan interest previously being capitalized; post-commissioning, interest must be expensed.
Refinancing should plateau interest cost to a reasonable level of INR14-15 crores per quarter going forward.

Debt repayment obligations decrease this year due to renegotiated principal repayment schedule; interest rate renegotiation separately reduces interest cost by INR2.5-3 crores and borrowing levels by INR30-35 crores.

subsections.label: Capex and debt paydown plan
points: Maintenance capex of INR40-50 crores plus additional INR20-30 crores for growing malt whiskey aging inventory capacity and bottling infrastructure.
Residual cash after providing for IMFL working capital will go towards paying down debt; management declined to commit to a zero-debt timeline.

subsections.label: Net debt and working capital
points: Net debt for the company stands at INR627 crores.
Working capital days for R&O is 5-6 days at Q4 exit; expected to rise slightly in Q1 onwards.
