P&A share of revenue within consumer
Delhi share of total P&A volumes
Delhi share of overall P&A business
P&A EBITDA loss (prior quarters, cited by analyst)
Additional label registration cost impacting Q4 P&A loss
New to-category brands injected in Rajasthan

subsections.label: Consumer portfolio architecture
points: Regular and others is the core category, delivering high volume and deep distribution across core markets of Rajasthan, UP, Delhi and West Bengal, offering superior value.
Prestige & Above is the future core category operating at substantially higher per-unit contribution, the vehicle for geographic expansion and driving up average realizations per case.
Within P&A, a luxury segment has been isolated - brands designed as market makers to define categories and lead consumer trends.

subsections.label: P&A core vs emerging markets
points: Distribution strategy built on core markets (3+ years of operations, engines of near-term volume/profitability) and emerging markets (0-3 year gestation phase requiring foundational investment).
5 core markets currently exist, 4 of which are profitable; emerging markets are being systematically groomed into core markets.
As emerging markets scale into core markets, reliance on any single state like Delhi is systematically diluting, providing a structural hedge against state-specific volatility.

subsections.label: Delhi impact on P&A
points: Delhi historically an outsized contributor at 33% of total P&A volumes in FY25; a specific isolated disruption in Delhi severely impacted aggregate growth in FY26.
Delhi volumes dropped to 60% of Q3 FY25 levels in Q3 FY26; sharp recovery brought Q4 FY26 Delhi volumes back to 90% of Q4 FY25 levels.
Removing the Delhi anomaly, P&A business grew 58% YoY, outpacing industry benchmarks.

Delhi is 'almost there' - came in with only a 10% shortfall vs prior year by Q4, down from a 40% shortfall; management expects to be over the hump soon and will continue sharing Delhi performance for a couple of quarters.

subsections.label: P&A regional updates
points: North continues as primary springboard followed by East; execution doubled in UP, penetrating deeper into Tier 3/4 cities and expanding availability in Haryana and Rajasthan.
Simultaneously expanding luxury footprint into smaller affluent markets.
In the East, following stabilization of West Bengal, advanced into Assam in Q3 and initiated operations in Jharkhand last month; early data validating strategy.
Phase 2 of geographical spread in Assam already initiated this quarter, establishing East as a definitive second growth engine.

subsections.label: P&A quarterly loss driver (Q4)
points: Loss increase in Q4 (INR5cr vs INR1.2-2cr in prior quarters) driven by business decisions to invest in emerging markets at specific junctures (e.g., opening Jharkhand) rather than smoothing quarterly performance.

Additional INR3-3.5 crores of label registration costs paid for new brand launches timed for Jan/Feb (ahead of excise year change) rather than after, contributing to higher expensed losses without reflecting underlying business health, where 4 of 5 core states are profitable.

subsections.label: R&O structural overhaul
points: During FY26, executed strategic wind-down of legacy portfolios in West Bengal and Haryana - a calculated near-term absorption of volume pressure to clear channels ahead of deploying a new optimized portfolio.
That transitional phase and rebasing of the segment is now complete.
UP being positioned as a massive growth engine with introduction of full brand range and 5 new SKUs; Rajasthan being attacked with 4 new to-category brands to reignite category growth.
R&O Delhi volumes were in complete flux (some periods zero, some periods growth); as of end of Q4, decided not to operate in Delhi for R&O brands until policy stabilizes.
7% degrowth in volumes from 'other markets' (ex Rajasthan+UP) is combination of Delhi, West Bengal and Haryana; only UP and Rajasthan grew 7% collectively; UP was zero last year.

West Bengal: whole manufacturing license shifted to a different location to reset; license process in progress, difficult to commit exact quarter; will relaunch with full-fledged new portfolio when ready. West Bengal impact now negligible going into FY27 (initiated wind-down end of July); some marginal Bengal volume expected in Q1.

R&O margin closed Q4 at 18% (above target range); target margin range is 16-18%; UP growth is less profitable than Rajasthan, so blended margin expected to be a bit lower going forward though absolute rupee profit will be larger as business scales.

subsections.label: P&A brand portfolio strategy
points: Luxury bucket comprises Doaab and Terai families, currently receiving strengthening focus.

Mainstream P&A drivers are Mountain Oak (including Lemoned Rum variant), Brothers & Company (including B15), and Snoski (including several flavors) families - core top/bottom-line drivers for short-medium term.
Strategy evolved from a one-brand show (Mountain Oak) to a multi-brand portfolio to reduce dependence on any single brand or market's short-term vagaries.

subsections.label: P&A realization/margin trajectory
points: Net realization per case not disclosed separately by category/brand (e.g., Doaab/Terai); management to internally review whether to disclose in future.
As luxury portfolio scales across markets on top of core P&A segments, NSVs expected to rise, though quarter-to-quarter blips don't reflect strategic trend.
Company will continue updating on core market count as emerging markets transition (numerical count to update as markets migrate).

subsections.label: UP disclosure policy
points: Company not currently disclosing separate UP volume numbers to protect competitive information; may reconsider disclosure if it does not weaken competitive position.

subsections.label: FY29 vision on P&A growth math
points: P&A FY29 target is INR500 crores (not INR1,000 crores as one analyst mis-cited).
Volumes grew 40% YoY (ex-Delhi) with ~3% price/mix change explaining why revenue growth (58% ex-Delhi) differs from volume growth.
As base increases, even modest growth rates on a larger base compound to reach targets - management confident despite deceleration concerns.

key_figures.label: Capacity derating when shifting Eastern plants to maize
Q4 bulk exit run rate (cited by analyst)
Internal transfer price margin for ENA between divisions
P&A brand entry timeline in Bihar (historical)

subsections.label: Capacity base and utilization
points: Following commissioning of UP distillery last quarter, installed capacity base stands at 334 million liters per annum, marking culmination of the multi-year capacity enhancement journey.
6 highly flexible distilleries strategically located across raw material and consumption hubs of North and East India.
Multi-raw material multi-product strategy has successfully stabilized margins, delivering INR6.2/liter EBITDA for FY26 and INR8.3/liter for Q4 FY26.
80% capacity utilization for the year (adjusted for UP start-up) is well within the annual guidance of 80-85%.

subsections.label: Bihar/Jharkhand strategic shift and Q4 volume dynamics
points: Executed a strategic shift in Bihar and Jharkhand facilities from predominantly ethanol to a mix of ENA and ethanol due to lower ethanol offtake by oil marketing companies.
Because ENA commands a lower market price than ethanol, this shift contributed to a slight top-line revenue drop - viewed as a timing issue, not a demand issue.

Supply/dispatch cycle for ENA is inherently longer due to the web of state permissions required (importing, receiving and supplying states), resulting in a one-time inventory buildup at facilities during Q4, expected to liquidate in Q1.
ENA's longer supply lead time versus ethanol is because ENA can be converted to alcohol, so states require more accountability/paperwork on its movement to protect revenue.

Increasing exports also added to material in the pipeline, contributing to lower Q4 volumes; combination of 3 factors (maize derating, ENA inventory buildup, export pipeline) led to slightly lower Q4 volume.

subsections.label: Maize vs rice optimization
points: Optimizing raw material feed between maize and rice requires technical changes; running Eastern plants entirely on maize derates total capacity by 75 KL/day for those units.

This derating is a known operational variable factored into profitability models when deciding between maize and rice procurement; company optimizes for margins and cash flow, not just absolute volume; decision is made per-plant, not for all 3 Eastern plants simultaneously.

subsections.label: Bulk volume outlook and exports
points: ~20 crores liters bulk sale guidance excludes captive consumption, which sits on top.
UP expected to add ~2 crores liters, with some capacity potentially consumed internally as UP portfolio grows; overall bulk volume target 'well over 20 crores liters' for the year.

Exports (ENA) began in Q4 with 3.7 million liters; described as an additional volume driver, not strategically more or less profitable than domestic bulk sales - overall basket still targeted at INR5-7/liter EBITDA.

subsections.label: Transfer pricing / cross-subsidization
points: Company maintains a policy of transfer pricing ENA between divisions after factoring in an INR5 margin for the manufacturing business, to avoid cross-subsidization of margins across divisions.
Reported bulk sale volume excludes captive/manufacturing volume used internally.

subsections.label: Regulatory/policy tailwinds by state
points: Karnataka policy change to alcohol-content-based taxation cited by analyst as a favorable structural shift, though company currently has no presence in South/Karnataka; intends to enter once reach is strengthened in existing regions.
UP cited as a big opportunity given same-party government policy seen as favorable; company has full presence with captive distillery.
West Bengal: currently a cooperative market plus private retail; medium-term outlook is for excise policy to become more liberal, propelling growth, though timing uncertain.
Bihar: management believes the state prohibition will eventually be lifted given neighboring states are capturing category revenue; timing uncertain (could be phased or full reopening).

When Bihar opens, Globus will enter with its full brand portfolio immediately (unlike the brand-by-brand approach taken when P&A launched ~4.5-5 years ago) given its structural manufacturing base advantage in the state.

subsections.label: Expansion strategy for new states (FY29 plan)
points: FY29 plan envisages minimum 8 new states for expansion; strategy is not exclusively captive manufacturing - decisions made on a case-by-case efficiency basis between own units and third-party manufacturing partners (e.g., Assam currently uses third-party manufacturing).
8-state figure is a minimum baked into FY29 guidance; actual expansion could exceed this.

key_figures.label: P&A business gestation period for emerging markets
Core market classification threshold (years of operations)

subsections.label: Geopolitical / input cost pressures
points: Iran crisis-related geopolitical developments have created cost pressure across industries, including on glass bottles/PET, logistics and other cost lines; caught the company by surprise but efficiency measures have been rolled out (packaging material, raw material, freight costs) and a full-fledged tracking project is underway.
Management expects impact to be 'modest' given mitigation measures, and believes governments will eventually concede to price increases as many operators struggle under the cost pressure.
Lower tariff on scotch is a mitigating factor for higher raw material costs this year, though it doesn't offset the entire cost impact; benefit expected to start this year, exact timing uncertain.

subsections.label: Delhi policy volatility
points: R&O Delhi policy has been in complete flux, with some periods showing zero volumes and others showing growth versus prior year; company decided to stop operating R&O brands in Delhi until policy stabilizes (as of end of Q4).

subsections.label: West Bengal / Haryana disruption
points: Strategic wind-down of legacy R&O portfolios in West Bengal and Haryana caused near-term volume pressure; West Bengal license shift process ongoing with uncertain timeline; Haryana continues to be a 'yoyo' market.

subsections.label: Seasonal agri-commodity cost variability
points: End of Q1 into Q2 typically sees inflation in agri commodities/raw material/fuel prices due to monsoons; raw material prices tend to come down toward end of Q3/Q4 - an annual seasonal feature affecting bulk EBITDA per liter.

subsections.label: Ethanol vs sugar competitive dynamic (addressed, not seen as risk)
points: Analyst raised hypothesis that oil marketing companies might prefer sugar-based ethanol over grain-based in rising crude scenario; management clarified OMCs have zero preference between sugar and grain ethanol, and sugar-based ethanol has capacity constraints given the need to also produce sugar.

subsections.label: Fundraise status
points: Enabling resolutions for a fundraise remain in place; investor conversations validated strategic roadmap and confirmed strong institutional appetite, but immediate necessity for external capital has been abated for FY27 execution.

Two factors shifted stance: (1) internal accruals - revised business plan shows stronger cash flow trajectory than initially projected around Q2/Q3 of last year, enabling self-funding of growth; (2) debt optimization - renegotiated debt terms improved liquidity profile and reduced cost of capital.

Company will continue evaluating opportunities and maintaining dialogue with investors within the resolution's validity period but is under no immediate pressure to dilute equity; priority is to leverage internal engine toward FY29 goals.
For subsequent periods beyond this year, management will wait and watch performance over first 2-3 quarters and broader macro/political events before commenting further on fundraise need.

subsections.label: Manufacturing/bulk guidance detail
points: EBITDA per liter guidance remains INR5-7 regardless of ethanol/ENA mix; FY26 achieved INR6.2 (INR6.3 cited later) full-year and closed within range; Q4 overshot at INR8.3 due to seasonal effects, but full-year FY27 guidance remains INR5-7.
Strategic margin profile of bulk business is structurally INR5-7/liter; no anticipated event in FY27 where margins would be strategically higher; guidance applies for FY27 as it did for FY26.

subsections.label: P&A and R&O growth outlook
points: Company declined to give piecemeal quarterly/annual growth guidance for P&A beyond the FY29 50% total growth target, citing quarter-to-quarter volatility.
For R&O, Rajasthan+UP combined grew 7% in FY26; management expects Rajasthan+UP to grow at a higher rate in FY27, though specific numerical guidance was not given.

UP April monthly run-rate not disclosed due to new excise year, route-to-market changes, inventory buildup and new brand launches distorting the number; management expects to exceed FY26 Rajasthan+UP growth starting Q1 onward.

subsections.label: Manufacturing margin/liquidity mechanics reiterated in Q&A
points: Debt optimization delivered via two levers: reduced debt repayment burden (freeing liquidity) and reduced interest rates, together saving a total of INR50 crores for FY27.
Interest cost, after returning to expensed (non-capitalized) treatment post UP commissioning, will settle at INR14-15 crores per quarter.

guidance_ledger.statement: INR5 to INR7 is our guidance for the EBITDA per liter... FY26 was that range and FY27, we expect the same range.
INR500 crores is what we have called out (not INR1,000 crores).
We are totally committed to delivering the FY29 objective... managing a 50% total growth on our P&A portfolio.
Overall, our capacity utilization was 80%, and that's well within the annual guidance that we have of 80% to 85%.
20 crores is what the other units will give us aside from UP, and UP should give us about somewhere around 2 crores liters... well over 20 crores will be the target for this year.
Our target in this space is 16% to 18% [previously noted 16-17%]... it will be a little bit lower than that for sure [vs Q4's 18%].
I believe in the coming year, Rajasthan plus UP will give us higher than 7% growth. At this point, we are not in a position to give a more specific guidance.
Maintenance capex is around INR40 crores to INR50 crores... overall I foresee somewhere between INR60 crores to INR80 crores of capex sustaining for a few years.
Interest will go back to around INR14 crores, INR15 crores per quarter.
This year, we do not see a need to achieve the business plan given some of the operational improvements and leverage we've been able to get... this year, we don't see a need at all.
We have systematically reduced our annual debt outflow from INR67 crores per annum to just INR14 crores projected for FY27.
When we said the 8 states, that is a minimum number where we definitely are ensuring the expansion will happen.
It becomes an additional volume driver... this number can keep on increasing.

risk_register.risk: Geopolitical (Iran crisis) driven input cost inflation - glass bottles/PET, logistics, freight
risk_register.note: Caught company by surprise; efficiency/mitigation measures rolled out across packaging, raw material, freight; expected impact to be modest, not severe.

risk_register.risk: Delhi (R&O) excise policy volatility
risk_register.note: Policy in complete flux with some periods at zero volumes; company halted R&O operations in Delhi until policy stabilizes.

risk_register.risk: West Bengal license transition / regulatory delay
risk_register.note: Manufacturing license shift in process with no committed timeline for relaunch; impact now largely negligible going into FY27.

risk_register.risk: Haryana market instability
risk_register.note: Described as still a 'yoyo' market.

risk_register.risk: Seasonal agri-commodity cost inflation
risk_register.note: Annual feature - costs rise end of Q1 into Q2 (monsoon-related) and ease end of Q3/Q4.

risk_register.risk: ENA supply/permission lead-time friction
risk_register.note: Longer state-permission process for ENA vs ethanol caused one-time inventory buildup in Q4, expected to normalize in Q1.

risk_register.risk: Bihar prohibition (opportunity foregone)
risk_register.note: Market remains closed; management monitoring legislative landscape; sees eventual reopening as likely given lost tax revenue vs neighboring states.

risk_register.risk: UP margin dilution risk
risk_register.note: UP growth is less profitable than Rajasthan volumes, expected to pull down blended R&O margin from Q4's 18% toward 16-18% target range.

themes.label: Fundraise deferral / internal accruals
themes.note: Enabling resolutions for equity fundraise remain but immediate need abated as stronger cash flow trajectory and debt optimization allow self-funding of FY27 growth plans.

themes.label: Debt optimization / deleveraging
themes.note: Refinancing cut annual debt outflow from INR67cr to INR14cr, reduced borrowings by INR57cr, improved current ratio (0.96x→1.01x) and interest coverage (1.76x→3.14x), tripled ROE.

themes.label: Delhi disruption and recovery
themes.note: Delhi volumes dropped sharply in Q3 (both P&A and R&O) but P&A recovered to 90% of prior-year Q4 levels; R&O Delhi operations halted pending policy stability.

themes.label: Bulk manufacturing margin stability (ENA/ethanol mix)
themes.note: EBITDA per liter guided at INR5-7 regardless of ethanol/ENA/export mix; multi-raw-material multi-product strategy stabilizes margins amid strategic shift toward ENA in the East.

themes.label: Ethanol blending / ENA export tailwind
themes.note: National ethanol blending mandates rising and global ENA arbitrage opportunity (elevated global energy costs constraining international ENA supply) opened export volume driver, starting with 3.7 million liters in Q4.

themes.label: P&A core-to-emerging market transition (FY29 vision)
themes.note: Company reiterated FY29 target of INR500cr P&A revenue and 50% total growth, driven by emerging markets (East expansion into Assam/Jharkhand) transitioning into core, profitable markets.

themes.label: Geopolitical cost inflation (glass/logistics)
themes.note: Iran crisis-related cost pressures on glass bottles and logistics flagged as a new headwind, expected to be modestly mitigated via efficiency measures and lower scotch tariffs.

themes.label: Regulatory/state policy tailwinds (Bihar, WB, UP, Karnataka)
themes.note: Bihar prohibition potential reopening seen as a first-mover opportunity; West Bengal policy expected to liberalize medium-term; UP and Karnataka-style favorable policy environments cited as growth enablers.

key_takeaways: In FY26, nearly 40% of our total revenues came from the consumer portfolio. And within this, P&A contributed 16% of the revenue... in FY24, the P&A business contributed just 6% of our total consumer revenues.

Following the commissioning of our UP distillery last quarter, our installed capacity base stands at 334 million liters per annum... We now operate 6 highly flexible distilleries... For the year, we achieved a strong 80% capacity utilization... delivering INR6.2 per liter EBITDA for FY26 and INR8.3 per liter for Q4 FY26.

We executed a strategic shift in our Bihar and Jharkhand facilities, transitioning from predominantly ethanol production to a mix of ENA and ethanol... This is obviously a timing issue, and we do not see this as a demand issue. This inventory buildup will get liquidated in Q1.

As we move into the execution phase of our FY27 business plan, the immediate necessity for external capital has been abated... We will leverage our robust internal engine to drive towards our FY29 goals.

FY26 delivered a robust aggregate performance with revenue increasing 27% year-on-year to INR164 crores and volumes rising 31% to 1.19 million cases [P&A]... When we isolate and remove the Delhi anomaly from the data, our P&A business grew at an exceptional 58% year-on-year.
Transitioning to the Regulars and Other segment... For the full year FY26, revenue was INR900 crores, up 4% with volumes at 15.7 million cases and EBITDA delivering a 12% expansion to INR158 crores.

We have systematically reduced our annual debt outflow from INR67 crores per annum to just INR14 crores projected for FY27. This action alone unlocks INR53 crores of direct liquidity in the coming year.
Current ratio... from 0.96x in FY25 to 1.01x in FY26... Interest coverage ratio... improved from 1.76x in FY25 to 3.14x in FY26... our return on equity has increased 3x in FY26 compared to FY25.
pressing_questions: Could we get a numerical clarity on the Delhi numbers? ...if you could just quantify FY25, what was the sales -- million cases sales in the regular segment in Delhi and FY26, what it is? (Management declined to give the numbers on the call: 'We are not prepared to give you the numbers immediately on this call.')

What is our maintenance capex now that we won't be growing any further beyond UP? (Followed by: given that plan, will the company start paying down debt aggressively to reach zero debt in 1-2 years? Management declined to comment on zero debt.)

What is the realization per case for the premium products (Doaab and Terai family)? (Management: 'We do not release that... we don't release realization per case on an ongoing basis' - took the question under consideration for internal review.)

Is it possible to quantify what is the funding requirement now to expand the IMFL portfolio to reach the ~INR500 crore FY29 vision, and is internal cash flow post debt restructuring good enough to fund that plan? (Management: 'many of these things are wait and watch'.)

SYMPHONY.about: Symphony was established in 1988, in Ahmedabad, India. The company is engaged in the manufacturing and trading of residential, commercial, and industrial air coolers in the domestic and international markets. It is the largest air cooler manufacturer in the world. [1] 97% of the revenue comes from the sale of Air coolers.[2]

quarters.summary: Q1 FY27 (June 2026 quarter) saw domestic momentum and margin discipline, with US and China subsidiaries offsetting reduced exports and IMPCO/CTPL headwinds. Near-term outlook flags margin pressure from elevated commodity/plastic costs (dependent on how long the "war" lasts), partial price pass-through already taken outside household coolers, expected significant sales growth in Mexico/USA next summer (FY28) assuming normal weather, muted secondary sales expected in the near term with primary/off-season buying continuing, and no further capital allocation to Australia.

key_figures.label: Price hike in non-household cooler segment

subsections.label: Adjusted numbers rationale
points: EBITDA and PAT should be viewed adjusting for a onetime non-cash expenditure of ₹5 crore in June '26 versus an exceptional ₹9 crore of higher income in June '25.
On apple-to-apple basis EBITDA is ₹53 crore vs ₹38 crore and Consol PAT is ₹43 crore vs ₹35 crore, up 23%.

subsections.label: Margin performance
points: Gross margin percentage marginally increased to 49.8% despite headwinds, geopolitical situation, pressure on commodity prices, and inventory overhang due to bad summer of '25.
EBITDA margin percentage improved to 12.6%.

subsections.label: Historical revenue context
points: June '26 for consolidated as well as standalone has witnessed second highest revenue vis-a-vis any historical June quarter, led by domestic performance supported by gross profit margin and EBITDA margin expansion.

subsections.label: Capital allocation / dividend
points: Board of Directors announced interim dividend of ₹1 per share (face value ₹2), total payout of about ₹7 crore.

subsections.label: Financial ratios and balance sheet
points: Core capital employed and net worth (standalone) have further reduced/rationalized on account of impairment done in FY '26.
Treasury at ₹345 crore is after remitting ₹225 crore to Australia for repaying their acquisition loan and working capital loan until 30 June '26; treasury almost in line with 30 June '25.
Consolidated capital employed is now almost half versus prior year as CTPL Australia was taking away substantial capital.

key_figures.label: Modern trade share of India topline
General trade share of India topline
One-time write-back/gain on sale of Bonaire USA shareholding & IPRs (CTPL Australia)

subsections.label: BISP (Beyond India Summer Products)
points: BISP i.e. sales not dependent upon Indian summer constituted about 48% of consolidated TTM revenue (₹560 crore), reinforcing strategic derisking and diversification from Indian summer.
On standalone basis, BISP accounts for topline of ₹179 crore in TTM i.e. 23%, and is profitable almost close to double digit EBITDA percentage.
BISP consists of large space ventilated air cooling and exports, plus tabletop fans (sell around the year) and water heaters.
On consol level, BISP also includes sales by subsidiaries reflecting geographical diversification (Bonaire USA, GSK China etc.), hence higher share (48%) vs standalone (23%).
Tabletop fans and water heaters have already been launched in modern retail and GT channels, present in top cities across the country; not everywhere yet but expanding over time.

subsections.label: Bonaire USA
points: Bonaire USA is back on track with 35% revenue growth and robust profitability mainly on account of successful scale-up of new models of air-cooler.
Revenue grew to ₹36 crore from ₹27 crore, EBITDA to ₹18 crore from ₹7 crore, and PAT of ₹17 crore.
Products are essentially rebranded Indian SKUs sold via Home Depot and Lowe's, two of the largest US retailers in home care category.
Model 'Air Force' (same name in India, under Bonaire brand in USA) registered the greatest sales growth.
Sales aided by a very good summer in the USA, especially Southwest (core market).

subsections.label: GSK China
points: GSK China revenue grew by 43% to ₹34 crore from ₹24 crore, EBITDA to ₹6 crore from ₹2 crore, and PAT of ₹5 crore, with operating leverage lifting profitability.
GSK China on standalone basis is now completely debt-free, having repaid all debt along with interest to Symphony India, similar to what happened with IMPCO Mexico years before.

subsections.label: IMPCO Mexico
points: IMPCO Mexico weak due to two consecutive mild summers (2025 and 2026), first time in memory this has happened; even employees with 30+ years tenure have never witnessed two consecutively mild summers.
Revenue declined to ₹54 crore from ₹66 crore, EBITDA to ₹3 crore from ₹7 crore, and PAT of just ₹1 crore.

subsections.label: CTPL Australia
points: CTPL Australia revenue continues to soften (₹27 crore vs ₹31 crore), but company reinforcing commitment that there won't be any further capital allocation.
EBITDA loss widened to -₹4 crore from -₹2 crore.
Impairment and write-off is completely behind, having been recorded in FY '26.

PAT of ₹36 crore includes one-time gain of ₹42 crore from write-back/gain on sale of shareholding in Bonaire USA and IPRs; this has been netted off at consol level (operating level PAT excludes this).

subsections.label: Domestic / Modern Trade
points: Domestic India revenue grew 15% despite huge inventory overhang before the summer.
All different segments of modern trade grew in excess of 100%.
Digital channels including D2C are highly profitable, in excess of normal domestic business, with huge potential to scale up.
Modern trade (including e-commerce, D2C, large format and large regional stores) constitutes in excess of 1/3rd of India topline; general trade constitutes 60-65%.
MT vs GT profitability is almost comparable.

Modern trade/e-commerce/D2C growth surge attributed to these channels not carrying elevated channel inventory (unlike general trade which carried over inventory from previous year); growth is a function of inventory levels, not sustainable at this rate going forward.

subsections.label: Export performance
points: Standalone exports from India declined mainly on account of geopolitical and shipping disruptions.
Middle East, which was primarily impacted, continues to remain affected.

From other regions, costs have shot up significantly, impacting overall demand and buyer sentiment; landed costs have gone up and buyers are unable to pass on the entire increase, making purchases more muted; not yet back to normal.

subsections.label: Regional demand patchiness
points: Q1 demand for air coolers was patchy particularly in North India and even East India due to uneven weather patterns.
No secondary sales expected in coming quarter, but primary sales (off-season buying by channel partners) will happen in current and subsequent quarters.

subsections.label: Inventory normalization
points: As of 30th June '26 (season-end), there is no inventory overhang either at trade level or company level; it is completely normalized.

subsections.label: US market rationale for air coolers
points: Coolers are not viewed as a poor man's air conditioner outside India; sold not only in USA but across Europe and even Middle East (where energy is abundant and price is not a consideration).

In US Southwest, houses are centrally air conditioned but coolers are bought for outdoor usage (near pool, backyard, garages); some models sold as whole-house coolers mounted on ceiling cooling through ducts, or window-mounted coolers.
Coolers provide humidity beneficial in dry conditions, making them a good alternative to air conditioning in dry Southwest climate.
Product is portable, plug-and-play — most compelling advantage.

subsections.label: Australia vs US distribution strategy
points: US strategy vastly differs from Australia: US has a warehouse and sells to large retailers (Home Depot, Lowe's); in Australia, retailer-driven business is still small, bulk goes to installation companies (closest resemblance to India's GT channel).
The two markets are very different in structure; lessons/models from one market could not be directly implemented in the other.

subsections.label: Commodity cost / geopolitical war impact
points: Costs (including plastic) are elevated due to ongoing war; timeline of normalization unknown.
Margin pressure likely in short term; company will pass on some but not all cost increases to market since duration of the situation is unknown.
Despite value engineering and cost reduction efforts, some impact on margins is expected, difficult to quantify as yet.

subsections.label: Export/geopolitical disruption
points: Middle East export markets remain affected by geopolitical disruptions.
Elevated shipping/landed costs in other export regions are muting buyer demand as buyers cannot pass on full cost increases.

subsections.label: Weather dependency
points: IMPCO Mexico impacted by two consecutive mild summers (2025, 2026), unprecedented in memory of 30+ year employees.
Q1 domestic demand was patchy in North and East India due to uneven weather patterns.

subsections.label: Australia (CTPL) weakness
points: CTPL Australia revenue continues to soften; company has committed to no further capital allocation to this business.

subsections.label: Margin outlook
points: In short term, margins are likely to be impacted due to elevated costs from geopolitical war; company will pass on some but not all cost increases.
Difficult to quantify magnitude of impact despite value engineering and cost reduction efforts.

subsections.label: Price hikes
points: No price hike taken yet in household cooler segment.
7% to 10% price hike taken in other segments; more hikes to come in the days ahead, extent uncertain and dependent on war/cost normalization.

subsections.label: Mexico and USA summer outlook
points: Mexico: after two consecutive mild summers, statistically almost impossible for summer of '27 to be mild again; expect fairly robust summer and significant sales growth, though no specific number given yet.
USA: if next summer is as good as this year (robust), sales should further increase next year.

subsections.label: Bonaire USA / GSK China trajectory
points: US summer extends into current quarter, so revenue will be seen in current quarter, but next two quarters likely to see much less revenue in US market as coolers are a summer-seasonal product.

GSK China has more even sales cycle due to industrial coolers and exports; expected to continue momentum, coming quarters based on export orders received; believe should do fairly good in coming quarter.
Bonaire USA current quarter should be good, but after that expected to be more muted.

subsections.label: Secondary/primary sales trend
points: No secondary sales expected in coming quarter, but primary sales (off-season buying by channel partners) expected in current and subsequent quarters.

subsections.label: Modern trade growth sustainability
points: 100%+ modern trade growth attributed to lack of channel inventory (unlike general trade); this rate of growth is unlikely to continue and should not be expected going forward.
As inventory normalizes across all channels, general trade and other channels are expected to register growth per business plan.

subsections.label: Australia strategy
points: No additional capital will be deployed in Australia business; whatever can be done without deploying additional capital will be done, and updates will be shared as it unfolds.
No new product introduction, distribution or manufacturing changes planned for Australia — 'just more of the same, nothing new'.

subsections.label: Water heater / tabletop fan expansion
points: Already launched in modern retail and GT channels, present in top cities; expansion to be extended over time to more channels/geographies.

key_takeaways: Domestic momentum, absolute margin discipline, and as far as overseas subsidiaries are concerned, the robust performance of US and China cushioned the reduced export, and IMPCO and CTPL headwinds.
Consolidated revenue stands at ₹378 crore, up by 8% YoY, EBITDA stands at ₹48 crore, up from ₹38 crore, up by 26%, while Consol PAT stands at ₹40 crore, down from ₹42 crore.
Apple to apple, EBITDA for June '26 is ₹53 crore versus ₹38 crore, while Consol PAT ₹43 crore versus ₹35 crore i.e. up by 23%.
BISP segment constituted about ₹560 crore on a consol basis in trailing 12 months i.e. almost 48%, reinforcing strategic derisking and diversification from Indian summer.
Bonaire USA is now back to track and revenue grew by 35% with a robust profitability mainly on account of successful scale-up of new models of air-cooler.
GSK China revenue grew by 43% and operating leverage lifted the profitability, as well as now, GSK China on a standalone basis is completely debt free.
CTPL Australia revenue continues to soften, but we are reinforcing our commitment, there won't be any further capital allocation.

Domestic sales i.e. India revenue grew by 15%, despite huge inventory overhang before the summer and importantly all different segments of modern trade grew in excess of 100%, while digital channels including D2C are highly profitable, in excess of our normal domestic business and has a huge potential to scale up.
As of 30th June '26 i.e. our season-end, there is no inventory overhang either at a trade level or at a company level, it is completely normalized.
Standalone exports from India declined mainly on account of geopolitical and shipping disruptions.
pressing_questions: Could you provide your outlook for the ROW business over the next two to three quarters, particularly for the USA and Mexico, with expectations of strong summer conditions in these markets, do you expect demand to improve meaningfully?

Have export shipments now fully resumed or are you still facing logistic or shipping-related disruptions? Are geopolitical uncertainties continuing to affect order inflows or execution in key export markets?

Bonaire USA and GSK China delivered healthy growth during the quarter, while IMPCO Mexico and CTPL Australia remained relatively weak, how should we think about the growth trajectory of each of these businesses over the next few quarters?

During Q1, demand for air coolers was somewhat patchy, particularly in North India due to uneven weather patterns. Could you help us understand the impact this had on your sales and demand trends across regions?
How have secondary sales trended in July and early August? Have you seen any improvement in offtake after the normalization of weather conditions?

quarters.summary: FY26 consolidated revenue declined 28% YoY with PAT turning negative due to Australia impairment; management has executed a balance-sheet reset - impairing entire Australia equity investment, ring-fencing US business as a direct Symphony India subsidiary, and committing to no further capital allocation to Australia. Near-term outlook hinges on an expected pickup in Indian summer demand from mid-May 2026, with subsidiaries (Mexico, China, US, Brazil) expected to become incrementally profitability accretive going forward, and cost increases (PVC) expected to be passed on from July onward.

subsections.label: BISP portfolio
points: BISP (Beyond India Summer Products) includes large space ventilated air cooling, tower fan, kitchen fan, water heater, exports from India and overseas subsidiary sales — the product portfolio not specifically dependent on Indian summer.
BISP represents partly product diversification and geographical diversification, derisking the business.
In India, BISP segment is already profitability-accretive at both EBITDA and PBT level.

Household residential cooler EBITDA is significantly better than BISP; BISP is being built with substantial advertisement and sales promotion expenses over last 3-4 years but still delivers decent high-single-digit EBITDA margin.

BISP EBITDA margin has potential to be in line with air cooler business through operating leverage; in some categories (e.g., large space ventilated cooling) EBITDA margin already stands even higher than residential air cooler category.

subsections.label: Subsidiary performance
points: IMPCO Mexico registered flattish revenue during the year with overhang of channel inventory.
GSK China is doing well, registering decent top line as well as profitability growth.
USA business registered strong momentum despite geopolitical and tariff issues; profitability on quarterly and annual basis intact as it was pre-tariff, pre-geopolitical turmoil.
Subsidiaries (Mexico, China, US) at EBITDA level, if normalized, are almost in line with Symphony India business.
Equity investment in Mexico and China put together is less than ₹5 crores; company doesn't have equity capital deployment in Mexico, China or Brazil.

With Australia balance sheet reset, subsidiaries expected to incrementally contribute to profitability going forward; Australia was described as a huge and consistent drag that had distorted the picture.

subsections.label: Water heater category
points: Water heater category launched in FY26 was a launch year, so revenue wasn't material.
Products were well received by customers and channel partners wherever sold; unique product proposition includes hair fall control geyser, a technology no competitor has.
Company has launched a value range of products as well, giving a full suite from the flagship Spa product to value price points.
Geographical spread of water heater category will be wider this year versus last year's very limited markets, expected to drive revenue growth over time.

subsections.label: Domestic regional performance
points: South, Western and part of Central India saw decent performance starting third week of March into April.
North and East India channel inventories to a major extent have already been rationalized, but weather disturbances persisted in April and until now.
Regional demand contribution varies year after year depending upon season; it is not the case that any one region (North/East) always contributes the most.
Starting current week (mid-May), decent summer sales expected, with a runway of 4 to 6 weeks of decent summer sales if summer sets in as it has historically in past years.

subsections.label: Export performance
points: Export revenue was impacted mainly on account of ongoing Middle East geopolitical headwinds.

subsections.label: Australia distribution model change
points: Plan is to change Australia business model to distributors across the country who will invest, buy products from India or China, warehouse and sell to local dealers, instead of the subsidiary itself holding warehouses and distributing to dealers.
This mirrors a similar arrangement already in place in Brazil, which the Australia model will replicate.

subsections.label: Australia acquisition history and rationale
points: Symphony acquired Australia business in 2018 with strategic rationale to build broader international business, providing entry into developed markets such as Australia and USA and adding an established brand portfolio.
Post-acquisition, Australia business encountered a materially different operating environment with a series of external factors.
Within 15-16 months post-acquisition, company witnessed COVID-related world's longest lockdown for almost 21 months, preventing time to integrate and symphonize the business.

Due to changes in local regulation, company had to exit certain key products, especially gas-based products; replaced with new set of products more suited to local market, coupled with overheads reduced to less than half.
Integrated manufacturing facility was converted into an outsourced business model; marketing network was also enhanced and expanded.
Despite all turnaround efforts, original acquisition thesis for Australia has not translated into financial outcome due to external situation.

subsections.label: Australia reset structure
points: Board decided on a balance sheet reset including impairment in relation to Australia business.
US business ring-fenced as a direct subsidiary of Symphony India; Bonaire USA equity and Bonaire brand IPRs (valuable for US and other markets) bought over by Symphony India.
Company fully recognizes investors' concern about performance of Australia, its capital efficiency, and year-after-year losses; investors always like disciplined capital allocation.
Board and company have categorically decided no further capital investment or allocation will be made to Australia business.

Post-reset, CT Australia will essentially just have a management team and some office space to manage affairs, with commercial transactions entirely between distributors and Symphony's China/India entities.
Winding up/closing CT Australia is not currently being considered; focus is on making distribution more effective and efficient without draining resources further.
Monthly CODB of ~500K-600K includes significant warehousing and rental costs, expected to further reduce once warehousing costs are eliminated.

subsections.label: Capital return
points: No share buyback planned as of now; management characterizes the Australia/US/loan buyback restructuring as a form of buyback.
Board will consider buyback at the right time as done in the past; decent payout has continued irrespective.

subsections.label: Geopolitical and tariff risk
points: USA business faced geopolitical and tariff issues but maintained profitability momentum; tariff on India-origin products had come down to about 12% and became a non-material, non-issue; no tariff applies to Mexico-origin products.
Export revenue was impacted mainly due to ongoing Middle East geopolitical headwinds.

subsections.label: Demand/channel risk
points: Channel caution existed until 31 March 2026 because of inventory overhang and a bad summer in 2025.
Weather disturbances continued in North and East India in April and until now, delaying expected summer uptick.

subsections.label: Cost inflation risk
points: Other expenses significantly higher versus historical levels; PVC price increase recently witnessed.
Cost increases are expected to be passed on from July onward once fully new production takes place; June quarter benefits from lower-cost old inventory.

key_takeaways: On a consol basis, for the year FY26, top line stood at ₹1,131 crores, down by 28% Y-o-Y, leading to PBT (before exceptional items) of ₹149 crores, down from ₹326 crores. After providing for exceptional onetime impairment provision and net of some of the write-back, the PAT stands at negative ₹141 crores.

Coming to stand-alone performance of Symphony India, Revenue is ₹765 crores, down from ₹1,182 crores. PBT (before exceptional items) stands at ₹164 crores, down from ₹329 crores and profit after tax after exceptional items stands at negative ₹166 crores.

For Q4 FY26 i.e. March quarter, on a consolidated basis, revenue is ₹338 crores, down from ₹488 crores. Gross margin percentage, the noteworthy barometer of the profitability is intact. It is 46.4%, in line with previous year. Of course, EBITDA has taken a toll mainly on account of economies of scale and operating leverage and hence, EBITDA margin stands at 15.5% down from 21.2%.
The Board of Directors and company has very importantly and categorically decided that no further capital investment or allocation will be made to Australia business.

We have ring-fenced U.S. business by making it a direct subsidiary of Symphony India and Bonaire USA equity has been bought over by Symphony India at a valuation of ~₹30 crores. In addition to that, some of the IPRs, especially Bonaire brand of Australia is valuable, particularly for U.S. business and other markets. And hence, those IPRs have been also bought over by Symphony India for about ₹23 crores.

So entire equity investment made in Australia worth of ₹348 crores cumulatively, including about ₹298 crores in the current year has been impaired. In other words, now there is nothing more to impair in terms of the equity investment from Symphony India.
USA business has registered strong momentum despite geopolitical and tariff issues and the profitability on a quarterly and annual basis is intact as it was in pre-tariff, pre-geopolitical turmoil.
The Board of Directors has declared final dividend of ₹5 on a face value of ₹2, amounting to total annual payout of ₹62 crores. This payout is despite taking an impairment.

TCS.about: Tata Consultancy Services is the flagship company and a part of Tata group. It is an IT services, consulting and business solutions organization that has been partnering with many of the world's largest businesses in their transformation journeys for over 50 years. TCS offers a consulting-led, cognitive powered, integrated portfolio of business, technology and engineering services and solutions. [1]

quarters.summary: TCS reported Q1 FY27 revenue growth of 2.2% QoQ / 13.9% YoY in INR (flat QoQ / 2.7% YoY in USD; 40 bps QoQ / 3.2% YoY in constant currency), with operating margin at 24% (down 130 bps QoQ mainly due to wage hikes) and net margin at 19.2%. Management remains optimistic that demand will improve in Q2 FY27 as pent-up technology backlog gets released and clients across most sectors (except Consumer) show turnaround signs, while continuing to invest in AI capabilities and partnerships; margin aspiration is to exit towards 25%+ and progressively move closer to FY26 levels over the medium term.

subsections.label: Margin drivers
points: Operating margin declined 130 bps sequentially to 24%, primarily due to wage hikes.
Q1 rollout of annual increments for global workforce impacted margins by 170 bps.
Company strengthened partnership ecosystem and made targeted investments, partly offset by 40 bps of currency benefit and operational efficiencies.

Strong profitability allows significant investment aligned with company aspirations, including AI capabilities, talent transformation, partner ecosystems, platforms, domain solutions and go-to-market capacity.
Company continues to drive operational rigor through pyramid optimization, productivity improvement, better resource fulfillment, automation and disciplined cost management.
Approach is not to optimize margins in isolation but to invest in capabilities strengthening long-term competitiveness while delivering industry-leading profitability and return ratios.

Segmental margin decline of 250-300 bps across Manufacturing, Communications, Life Sciences and Others primarily reflects the 170 bps wage impact, with some additional segment-level investment prioritization.
Company usually takes a big margin headwind upfront in Q1 and inches up through the year; aims to exit at 25%+ margin and achieve it sooner rather than later.
Aspiration is to progressively inch up closer to at least FY26 margin levels, balancing growth investments with operating discipline.

subsections.label: Cost category refinement
points: This quarter TCS undertook a refinement of cost categories to address the previously elevated 'other expenses' line, providing a clearer view of underlying cost drivers.

This change has no impact on overall expenses or operating margins; prior periods have been aligned for comparability, with prior four-quarter comparative details available on the quarterly fact sheet.
TCS has done away with the split-up of COR and SG&A cost categories.

subsections.label: SG&A/investment color
points: SG&A investments (per IFRS published financials) have been increasing, driven by investments in talent, strengthening partnerships and targeted investments.
This also includes some charges related to M&A.

subsections.label: Capital allocation
points: Capital allocation policy remains unchanged; company remains committed to returning substantial free cash flows to shareholders while judiciously investing to support long-term growth aspirations.

key_figures.label: Mega deals won in last 5 quarters

subsections.label: Deal momentum
points: Strong order book closure and large deal momentum continued, with net new AI-led business transformation deals.
US$800 million mega deal with SKF marks the 6th mega deal win in the last 5 quarters.
Multi-million $ strategic partnership agreement signed with ServiceNow.
Multi-million $ deal signed with a Europe-based Fortune Global 50 firm.
Healthy client additions maintained across $10 million+, $5 million+, and $1 million+ revenue bands on a sequential basis.

Mega deals cut across industries but share a common scope: optimizing the run with AI combined with partnering on business transformation; AI acceleration mainly comes through discretionary transformation projects bundled in, with AI brought in earlier in execution (Ops or transformation) versus in the past.
Only a marginal shift in order book mix toward more AI-transformative deals versus renewals; not a significant shift.

subsections.label: Demand environment and near-term outlook
points: Geopolitical uncertainties that began around March continued through the quarter; ongoing conflicts continue without a clear timeline for resolution.
Clients deferred some projects during the quarter.
Management remains optimistic that demand will resume sometime in Q2, primarily because customers have a significant amount of pent-up technology backlog to be completed.
Rate of change of the geopolitical/demand dynamic cannot be precisely quantified; confidence stems from customer conversations and stronger visible uptick in select verticals (e.g., life sciences).

subsections.label: Retail/consumer deal conversion
points: Strong prior-year deal-win growth in retail and consumer has not yet fully translated to revenue because a few large projects ended this quarter, and new project net additions are still ramping up and not yet adequate to offset the decline.
Growth is expected as large signed projects start yielding revenue in subsequent quarters.

subsections.label: Client engagement/pricing models
points: Client engagement models span multiple archetypes: output/outcome-based commitment models (fixed duration business outcome commitments), fixed price/fixed capacity models (AI lab offering, building capacity once customer sees value), and continuing T&M arrangements (with accountability for outcomes).
Transaction-based and outcome-based commitments are increasing particularly in autonomous GBS deals (F&A, HR, customer experience), which historically had very little T&M.

subsections.label: BFSI
points: BFSI delivered good growth across geographies.
Banks in the US are doing very well; management is optimistic about sustained growth in the BFSI segment.

subsections.label: Tech, Software and Services
points: Continued growth momentum; won several large and mid-sized deals including a multi-million-dollar deal with ServiceNow.
Management expects tech services to continue to grow.

subsections.label: Consumer Business Group
points: Quarter driven by a combination of inflationary pressures and ongoing geopolitical uncertainties impacting discretionary spend.
Client priorities focused on managing increasing costs; growth initiatives remain selective, centered on targeted areas delivering scalable impact without increasing risk exposure.
Airlines in North America and non-essential retail are specific sub-segments under stress due to global geopolitics.
Consumer business expected to turn around once there is better market sentiment on geopolitics.

subsections.label: Life Sciences and Healthcare
points: Declined this quarter; however core demand for AI transformation, automation and compliance initiatives is intact.
Recovery expected soon; management expects life sciences could turn around in Q2.

subsections.label: Manufacturing
points: Continued softness in certain segments like auto; decision-making influenced by tariff pressure, macro uncertainty, EV recalibration, supply chain resilience and cost discipline.

Outlook remains positive based on multiple net new deal wins this quarter, including the US$800 million SKF deal, a new multi-million-dollar Network Model engagement with ABB, and a multi-million-dollar deal with a Global Fortune 50 European firm — all net new AI-led opportunities.
Auto segment impact due to multiple reasons; management expects manufacturing to turn around in Q2.

subsections.label: CMI (Communications, Media, Information)
points: Industry headwinds continue to play out; modest growth delivered in this sector.

subsections.label: ERU (Energy, Resources & Utilities)
points: Slight decline this quarter, but positive growth prospects seen on the back of AI infrastructure build-out, electrification, renewables, energy security and mining critical materials.

subsections.label: Regional Markets
points: Growth driven by India, Public services, and products and platforms.

subsections.label: Deal examples across segments
points: North American utility major: renewal transformed into a future-ready operating model modernizing operations across grid management, customer experience, asset management and workflow enablement, with AI governance and lifecycle management; TCS won renewal with an AI-first proposition and was chosen as partner for transformation into an AI company.
Multiple deal wins in autonomous GBS this quarter across HR, finance, and customer experience, with agentic operating model at the core of customer value commitment in BPS.

Large retailer: 70 agents orchestrating IT-Ops across more than 60 infrastructure and application workflows integrated with customer's ITSM tools; shift from largely human monitoring to AI-led 24/7 monitoring resulted in 30% faster remediation and 80% fewer incidents.

Global specialist insurer: seven AI agents (including specialized medical and fraud review agents) operating alongside human examiners for worker compensation workflow; human plus AI operating model cut claim settlement time by 40%, replacing a legacy sequential human-handoff process.

subsections.label: AI services revenue trend
points: AI services revenue continues to accelerate, reaching $2.6 billion annualized revenue at end of Q1 FY27, up 13.6% QoQ.

Incremental AI revenue added was $75 million this quarter versus $125 million in the March quarter; AI revenue is not like traditional ADM annuity revenue — many projects are one- to two-quarter engagements requiring new wins to sustain revenue accrual, making quarterly growth lumpy.
Management is satisfied with continuous quarter-on-quarter growth trajectory and increasing client conversations yielding more opportunities despite non-recurring nature of the work.

subsections.label: Infrastructure to Intelligence strategy and partnerships
points: Announced a global premier partnership with Anthropic, giving early access to the Claude family of models, 50,000 licenses, a joint GTM campaign, co-creation of industry solutions, and TCS iON as a training and certification partner.

TCS became the first GSI partner for Mistral AI; will build sovereign and custom AI models for enterprises and establish a dedicated COE for developing industry solutions across BFSI, healthcare, manufacturing, and public sector.

Launched TCS SovereignSecure Cloud for Europe, addressing rising demand from governments and regulated enterprises for compliance, sovereign, and AI-ready cloud infrastructure; strengthens TCS's leadership presence in Europe as clients prioritize data residency, operational control, and geopolitical risk mitigation.
Launched a dedicated Global Value and Innovation Center business unit to help enterprises build, operate, transform, or divest global capability centers.

HyperVault is strengthening TCS's market positioning and deepening 360-degree partnership with clients and ecosystem partners; in Q1 FY27 these partnerships enabled two very large IT services deals that were net new for TCS.
AI Acceleration Playbook ('Innovate with AI, Build with AI, Scale with AI') introduced last year uses the concept of rapid build engineers, similar to forward deployment engineers (FDEs).

subsections.label: Forward Deployed Engineers (FDE)
points: TCS's definition of FDE is evolving; FDEs work in pods/squads and the entire operating model around FDE is being defined.

An FDE differs from a product manager: FDEs are multi-skilled specialist engineers deep in one particular skill (technical or domain), working with a toolkit to solve a specific problem, similar to TCS's long-standing 'T-factor' capability model.

Management would not put a specific number on current FDE headcount given the transition period, but targets at least 1% of the employee base to work in the new operating model over time — described as a gradual transition, not a one-time jump.
TCS is already working in the FDE model via its rapid build methodology, though the definition and operating model are expected to keep evolving.

subsections.label: AI monetization and productivity pass-through
points: Difficult to quantify what portion of business has already gone through productivity pass-through; opportunities to unearth productivity benefits are found as projects come up for renewal.
In many cases, when TCS proactively identifies opportunities to reduce client spend, clients allocate additional work instead, limiting top-line impact.

Rule-of-thumb productivity gain passed on to clients from leveraging AI is in the 10% to 15% range, viewed over the tenure of a project; this varies by project type (new software development, monitoring, production support each behave differently) and is often front-loaded then smoothened over the project term.

Management does not see the kind of massive $1 trillion IT spend contraction referenced in other industry forums; overall headcount increased this quarter, indicating no such contraction in TCS's book of work.

subsections.label: Model strategy / AI architecture
points: Enterprises are expected to use multiple models — one LLM plus many SLMs or multiple LLMs within the same family — using older models for certain queries and newer models for certain workloads, driven by model FinOps considerations around on-prem versus cloud token-based usage.
System integrators are expected to play a greater role ensuring client AI spend is well spent and value is delivered as model architecture complexity increases.

Making technology choices and integrating them into an existing diverse, complex landscape across the Infrastructure to Intelligence stack is increasingly challenging given fast-changing technology; TCS's long-standing client relationships and product/technology partnerships position it to convert product capability into enterprise value.

subsections.label: Regional demand
points: Europe leadership presence strengthened via SovereignSecure Cloud launch as clients prioritize data residency, operational control, and geopolitical risk mitigation.

US corporate revenue growth is described as decent, with consensus expectations of broad-based industry growth for the year; however, this has not fully translated into a correspondingly strong pickup in technology spend historically correlated with such growth.
India, Public services, and products & platforms drove growth within Regional Markets.

subsections.label: Client priorities
points: Client priorities increasingly aligned with TCS's focus areas: AI-led transformation, modernization, cybersecurity, sovereign cloud, platform rationalization, and vendor consolidation.
Enterprises are investing in transformation that improves resilience, productivity, security and readiness for AI, and TCS is favored as a partner of choice.
Management encouraged by quality of wins, strong client mining, steady AI monetization, offering relevance, and strength of long-term competitiveness.

subsections.label: SKF deal strategic rationale
points: SKF deal driver is TCS's ability to partner with the customer to transform their business and technology landscape and help them become an AI-first company.

Deal is holistic: optimizing run across infrastructure and applications with AI-led efficiencies, S/4HANA transformation (not a simple upgrade but full process mining, AI-driven process redesign, and AI-based execution), plus industry value chain transformation spanning SKF's global operations.

subsections.label: System integrator role
points: As multi-model architectures and complex tech stacks proliferate, the system integrator role is expected to increase in importance for helping clients make technology choices, integrate technologies into existing landscapes, and derive enterprise value.

subsections.label: Partnerships and new business units
points: Global premier partnership with Anthropic (Claude models, 50,000 licenses, joint GTM, co-creation of industry solutions, TCS iON training/certification partner).
First GSI partner for Mistral AI, building sovereign/custom AI models and establishing a dedicated COE across BFSI, healthcare, manufacturing, and public sector.
Launch of TCS SovereignSecure Cloud for Europe.
Launch of dedicated Global Value and Innovation Center business unit for global capability center services (build, operate, transform, divest).
SG&A investment increases include some charges related to M&A activity.

subsections.label: Aspiration
points: TCS continues to advance towards its aspiration to become the world's leading AI-led technology services company, pursued with discipline, responsibility, and continued focus on creating sustainable value for clients, employees and shareholders.

subsections.label: Geopolitical and macro headwinds
points: Geopolitical uncertainties that increased around March continued through the quarter, with ongoing conflicts and no clear timeline for resolution.
Clients deferred some projects during the quarter as a result.
Consumer Business Group impacted by inflationary pressures and geopolitical uncertainty affecting discretionary spend, particularly airlines in North America and non-essential retail.
Manufacturing (notably auto) affected by tariff pressure, macro uncertainty, EV recalibration, supply chain resilience needs and cost discipline.
CMI industry headwinds continue to play out, limiting growth to modest levels.

subsections.label: Wage/cost headwind
points: Annual wage increments rolled out globally in Q1 impacted operating margins by 170 bps, the primary driver of the 130 bps sequential margin decline.

subsections.label: Demand outlook
points: No specific revenue or earnings guidance is provided by the company.
Management expects demand to improve sometime in Q2 FY27, driven by customers' pent-up technology backlog.

Sector-level Q2 expectations: BFSI continues to look good; Manufacturing expected to turn around in Q2; Life sciences could turn around in Q2; Tech services expected to continue growing; Consumer business expected to turn around once geopolitical sentiment improves; a good turnaround is seen emerging in almost every other sector except consumer.

subsections.label: Margin outlook
points: Company aims to exit at 25%+ operating margin and strive to achieve it sooner rather than later, typically taking a big margin headwind upfront in Q1 and inching up through subsequent quarters.
Aspiration is to progressively move closer to at least FY26 margin levels over the medium term, balancing growth investments with operating discipline.

subsections.label: FDE operating model target
points: Target of at least 1% of employee base to work in the new FDE/rapid-build operating model over time, characterized as a gradual transition rather than a one-time jump.

guidance_ledger.statement: We don't provide any specific revenue or earnings guidance, and anything said on this call which reflects our outlook must be reviewed in conjunction with the risks the company faces.

We are still optimistic that the demand will resume at some time in Q2, primarily because our customers have a significant amount of pent-up technology backlog to be completed. I expect the demand to improve sometime in Q2. We're generally optimistic on Q2 going in at this time.
Manufacturing, we believe will turn around in Q2.
Life sciences could turn around in Q2.
Tech services will continue to grow.
Consumer business will turn around once we have a better market sentiment on geopolitics.

We want to exit at 25% plus and strive to achieve it sooner rather than later... our aspiration would be to make the right investments and to progressively inch up closer, at least to the FY26 levels.

guidance_ledger.metric: FDE / new operating model employee share
guidance_ledger.statement: We would definitely target to have at least 1% of our employee base to work in the new operating model. But this is not a one-time jump, it is a transition.

In most places, the productivity gain passed on is around 10% to 15% range... it is an ongoing process and it will be very difficult to say whether we are done with all productivity gains being passed on.
Last quarter, we onboarded 14,000 campus graduates and as we speak, we are visiting the top universities across the country and hiring for top talent, specifically looking for AI-native skills.

guidance_ledger.metric: AI mega deal replicability across sectors
guidance_ledger.statement: Mega deals cut across industries; in terms of scope they have something in common... acceleration comes where AI is brought earlier into execution.
We do not believe that there would be a drastic reduction in white-collar [employment]... we don't fully agree that AI is going to reduce the overall white-collar jobs.
We are quite positive about FY27, quite positive about the international growth
We are looking at a regular Q1, regular Q2 that we are used to seeing... we are also expecting a stronger 1H. Our planning assumption is along those lines only
On the wage increments, you should expect a similar impact on what we have seen in the past annual increment cycle, which had been in the range of 150 to 200 basis points
Our expectation is AI will be net accretive, like to see the initial year, our attempt would be to ensure that we arrest the degrowth while the AI revenue increase
By and large, most of the headwinds we know probably are behind us, excepting few that may come up or that we have already accounted for
HyperVault Business has made significant progress this quarter on its journey to build out 1 GW of capacity

key_takeaways: First, Q1 FY27 reflects continued growth momentum and the strength of our strategic positioning despite the geopolitical and macroeconomic headwinds.

Our Q1 revenue stood at ₹72,275 crore, growing 2.2% sequentially and 13.9% year-on-year. This is the fourth consecutive quarter of growth. Growth was led by BFSI, Technology, software and services, regional markets, and products and platforms.

Second, strong order book closure and large deal momentum continued. We delivered a TCV of $9.5 billion, including net new AI-led business transformation deals such as, US$ 800 million mega deal with SKF; 6th mega deal win in the last 5 quarters, Multi-million $ strategic partnership agreement with ServiceNow, Multi-million $ deal with Europe-based Fortune Global 50 firm
The third key takeaway is our AI services revenue continues to accelerate. At the end of Q1 FY27, it stands at $2.6 billion in annualized revenue, which is up 13.6% QoQ.

Fourth, client priorities are increasingly aligned with our focus areas of AI-led transformation, modernization, cybersecurity, sovereign cloud, platform rationalization, and vendor consolidation. We maintained healthy client additions across $10 million+, $5 million+, and $1 million+ revenue bands on a sequential basis.
Fifth, our operating margins stood at 24%, down 130 bps sequentially, primarily due to wage hikes.
Finally, we continue to advance our Infrastructure to Intelligence strategy through unique partnerships with frontier AI companies and new launches.

quarters.summary: TCS delivered its third consecutive quarter of sequential CC growth (1.2% QoQ) in Q4FY26 with broad-based momentum across markets and a record $12 billion TCV including three mega deals, while full-year FY26 revenue declined 2.4% in CC even as operating margin hit a 4-year high of 25%. Management enters FY27 with confidence and positivity on growth, aided by a strong order book, broad-based client-band additions, accelerating AI services revenue ($2.3 billion annualized) and progress on the HyperVault AI infrastructure business, though margins are expected to see near-term headwinds from annual increments while the medium-term aspiration is to move margins towards 26%.

subsections.label: Margin drivers (Build-Partner-Acquire reinvestment)
points: Improvement in realizations driven by continued focus on value-led delivery contributed a 40 bps benefit.
Currency was supportive during the quarter, providing a translation tailwind of 110 bps.

Consistent with the 'Build–Partner-Acquire' strategy shared at Analyst Day, these tailwinds were consciously reinvested back into strengthening capabilities and growth engines rather than flowing through to margin.

Under 'Build': higher external consultants' cost (40 bps) incurred to capture demand and protect delivery timelines/quality while scaling internal capabilities; targeted interventions in critical talent, certifications, upskilling and niche delivery pods; ongoing impact of the India wage code included; together these accounted for 40 bps impact.

Under 'Partner': stepped-up investments in ecosystem partnerships (OpenAI, AMD, ServiceNow announcements) focused on industrializing AI solutions, increasing cross-sell, and improving speed-to-value via deeper hyperscaler/platform collaboration; increased go-to-market activity (client events, showcases, industry forums) linked to expanding demand pipeline and improving conversion; together a 50 bps margin impact.

Under 'Acquire': integration-related investments of ~10 bps as acquired capabilities were embedded into the operating model, including talent alignment, platform integration, GTM enablement and delivery readiness, aimed at accelerating synergy realization and scaling new offerings.
FY26 operating margin excludes a few one-off items relating to severance-related expenses, legal provisions, and impact of changes in India wage code.

subsections.label: Capital allocation and cash
points: Cash conversion this quarter continued to be strong, exceeding 100% of net profits.

Company remains firmly committed to returning substantial free cash flow to shareholders through a consistent and shareholder-friendly dividend policy, while prudently expanding investments under the 'Build-Partner-Acquire' framework.

subsections.label: Restructuring / one-offs (Q&A)
points: No one-offs called out for Q4; the combined one-off for the year is ₹1,300 crores.
The restructuring program that was started has been completed.

subsections.label: FY27 margin outlook (Q&A)
points: Exiting FY26 at a four-year high on annual margins at 25%, with continued positive momentum expected; focus will be to ensure growth with profitability, not shying away from making the right investments for strategic growth.
Immediate headwind stepping into FY27 will be annual increments; continued focus on Build-Partner-Acquire framework investments will also weigh on margins.
Mitigation planned via better operational rigor using usual levers and optimization on non-employee expenses; rupee depreciation helps but is not guaranteed.
Overall intent to balance and keep margins within a tighter reach, with an aspiration to move towards 26% on a longer-term basis.
Wage increment margin impact expected to be similar to past annual increment cycles, in the range of 150 to 200 bps.

subsections.label: SG&A trend (Q&A)
points: SG&A has been elevated in H2 due to investments under the Build-Partner-Acquire strategy — incremental investments on partnerships, recruitment and training, and new businesses are reflected in SG&A; some part of the increase (both absolute amount and as % of revenue) will remain elevated.

subsections.label: Margin vs growth strategy (Q&A)
points: Management believes focus on margin does not affect revenue growth; good margins provide greater flexibility to approach new deals and be more competitive in gaining market share.
Company states it does not lose deals on pricing and works with customers to give the best solution while winning deals.
Margin generated enables investment for growth, citing the last two acquisitions and investment in HyperVault as examples enabled by margin strength.

subsections.label: Order book strength
points: Q4 order book performance was very strong, with $12 billion TCV including three mega deal wins from Marks and Spencer, a leading telecom operator in the UK, and a leading American healthcare & pharmacy retailer.
This underscores the strength of the five-pillar strategy and AI-led positioning across services.
Momentum broad based across major markets, with North America, UK and Europe all growing sequentially in CC, and most industry segments also growing.

Strong order book closures in FY26 were led by vendor consolidation, AI-led modernization, scaling AI across the enterprise, digital core and data platform modernization, operating model transformation, and regulatory compliance.

subsections.label: Renewal vs new business characteristics (Q&A)
points: Deal characteristics this quarter were about 50-55% renewals and 40-45% new programs; this typically varies in a 40-60% band one way or another.

Renewals are, by and large, happening on time; TCS proactively offers early renewal when there's an opportunity to infuse greater AI, deliver greater productivity, and expand scope, whenever mutually beneficial.

subsections.label: FY27 growth outlook (Q&A)
points: Management declined to put a specific number on FY27 growth but expressed strong positivity and confidence about FY27 and about international growth given a good order book, three strong mega deals booked in the quarter, positive momentum across most industry verticals, and traction in new-age services.
Regular Q1 and Q2 seasonality is expected going forward, consistent with historically stronger first half.
