subsections.label: Client metrics
points: Every revenue band saw healthy additions this quarter after a gap of about 2 years, which speaks to early signs of stability and growth returning to mid-sized and large accounts.

subsections.label: BFSI
points: BFSI vertical continued to grow this quarter.

Client demand remained technology-led and outcome focused through Q4, shaped by heightened macro and geopolitical volatility; increased uncertainty around interest rates, inflation, and central bank actions influenced client sentiment, resulting in cautious investment decision-making.

Despite this backdrop, clients continued to prioritize core and legacy modernization, data estate transformation, cloud migration, scaled AI/GenAI deployments, productivity-led operating model transformation and vendor consolidation.
Spending patterns increasingly shifted from experimentation to industrialized business-driven transformation, with strong emphasis on cost discipline, regulatory resilience, and measurable outcomes.
Caution flagged for BFSI is specific to the current geopolitical/macro backdrop and not a broad-based caution (clarified in Q&A).

subsections.label: Consumer Business Group (CBG)
points: CBG saw another quarter of good growth, supported by market share gains and emerging pockets of technology conviction, resilience and guarded optimism.
Retail globally and TTH in UK/EMEA led growth, while CPG and TTH North America segments declined.

Enterprises continued to tightly align spending to initiatives delivering near-term efficiency, cost control, and operational resilience, with growing emphasis on vendor consolidation, technology simplification, legacy modernization, and selective AI/GenAI adoption.

CBG had 2 mega deal wins this quarter, helping propel its TCV to an all-time high — the Marks & Spencer renewal/expansion (a customer for well over a decade) and a mega deal with a leading American healthcare and pharmacy retailer, a longstanding trusted strategic partnership retained by TCS.

Example: for the American healthcare and pharmacy retailer, TCS modernized a mission-critical claims processing platform (processing over 5 million prescriptions daily) via cloud-native re-architecture, event-driven processing, complex multisystem integrations and enterprise-grade security, compressing claims cycles from 48 hours to 12 hours, enabling AI-driven decisioning and autoscaling to support growing prescription volumes.

subsections.label: Life Sciences and Healthcare
points: Saw marginal growth this quarter.

Healthcare payers managing rising costs and growing friction with providers due to preauthorization and claims issues; key priorities include affordability, transparency, simplicity, and better patient experiences.

Organizations focusing on data marketplaces, cyber resilience, and AI to boost productivity, while regulatory changes add to compliance costs and administrative burdens, prompting selective modernization focused on efficiency.

Pharmaceutical industry streamlining pipelines and adopting AI to tackle growth and pricing pressures; companies in Americas and UK/EU focusing on efficiency through vendor consolidation, tech modernization, and enterprise-wide transformation.

subsections.label: Manufacturing
points: Manufacturing vertical saw good growth this quarter despite macro uncertainties and impact to global supply chains.

Client demand remained cautious in Q4, shaped by macroeconomic uncertainty, tariff volatility, recalibration of EV demand, and continued restraint in capex across Automotive, Industrial, and Chemicals.

Customers prioritized near-term cost optimization and operational resilience, with sustained focus on AI-led productivity including predictive maintenance and quality automation, alongside ERP and cloud modernization to streamline operations and improve reliability.

subsections.label: Technology and software
points: Saw reasonable growth this quarter given the environment.

Client demand remained disciplined amid a challenging macro environment, shaped by heightened geopolitical tensions, tariff-related uncertainty, and increasingly stringent manufacturing and data-sovereignty requirements.

Customers continued to prioritize cost rationalization to fund a strategic pivot towards AI-led transformation, with spend focused on vendor consolidation, GCC expansion, and structural efficiency, and resulting savings reinvested into scaling AI across core operations and product portfolios.
Incremental investments also directed towards digital sovereignty and supply-chain resilience.

subsections.label: CMI (Communications, Media & Information)
points: Saw a modest decline this quarter, but promising signs of a rebound in IT spending in CMI.
Telecommunications companies advancing journeys to expand into adjacent businesses while enhancing efficiency of core operations, paving the way for growth and innovation.

Momentum remains strong in securing large deals within telecom sector; TCS signed its first mega deal in CMI this quarter — a significant expansion of a long-standing partnership with a leading UK-based telecom operator.
The five-year contract will see TCS lead the operator's comprehensive IT transformation journey for its consumer business, leveraging advanced AI, Cloud, and Digital Engineering capabilities.

TCS to take end-to-end responsibility for running the entire IT systems of the operator's consumer base and become its strategic technology partner, consolidating the entire landscape previously spread across multiple service providers.

subsections.label: ERU (Energy, Resources & Utilities)
points: ERU demonstrated robust growth this quarter.
Within ERU, the Energy & Resources segment performed well, led by supply chain modernization initiatives gathering momentum in the near term.
The Utilities segment is experiencing stress, and significant cost optimization opportunities are opening up.

subsections.label: AI momentum and adoption
points: FY26 was a pivotal year for enterprise AI adoption across industries; for the first time since GenAI's advent in late 2022, the shift from experimentation to scaled AI deployment showed marked improvement.
AI became a core part of every customer conversation and solutioning, creating a tailwind for enterprise adoption.
Strong deal momentum seen across new services in Enterprise Transformation, Digital Engineering, and Cloud Modernization.

AI revenue growth expected to be structurally similar to the digital transformation cycle: initial cannibalization of traditional revenue offset increasingly by AI revenue growth, though management could not predict exact timelines of the crossover.

AI-related revenue productivity is 'much better' than TCS average/traditional business at both onsite and offshore, though margin comparability is not being called out yet since AI investments are temporary/in initial phase.

subsections.label: Get AI Ready
points: Working with customers to upgrade infrastructure to be scalable and secure, modernize core applications, and set up modern data foundations; significant part of technology spend being invested in these areas.

Example: modernized mission-critical crew management systems using Generative AI for a European Airline, reverse-engineering complex legacy systems to reconstruct core business logic, powered by the Google Gemini platform, giving the airline a scalable foundation for new-age crew operations.

Example: for a US car rental company, executed a complex legacy data warehouse migration of over 20 terabytes of mission-critical data to a modern data platform, decommissioning legacy systems for an estimated $2.5 million in savings and establishing a scalable data foundation.

subsections.label: Lead with AI
points: Created an AI acceleration playbook — Innovate with AI, Build with AI and Scale with AI — deployed across a significant number of customers to solve high-value business problems in rapid deployment cycles of 12-16 weeks.
Example: for a leading US utility company, conducted CxO-level AI immersion programs and built an Enterprise AI Platform providing a secure, scalable foundation to industrialize AI adoption.
Physical AI deployment gaining traction in industrial sector via digital twins, computer vision, and quadruped-based solutions driving efficiencies, throughput and safety.

Example: for an electronics manufacturer, integrating NVIDIA Omniverse-driven digital twins with autonomous quadruped-based inspection systems in fabrication facilities, driving better construction accuracy and proactively identifying safety hazards.

subsections.label: Services transformation ('Human + AI' Service autonomy model)
points: Created a services re-design framework called the 'Human + AI' Service autonomy model, integrating service-line-specific industry-leading tools central to the Five-pillar strategy.
Resonating well with customers by providing a well-defined framework for consistent deployment across the enterprise; being taken proactively to existing customers and new prospects.
Challenge: enterprises have invested in AI tools but not yet reaped expected productivity benefits — the model aims to systematically help customers address these gaps.

Example: for a UK retailer, deployed the AI-Engineering framework with agents through the software lifecycle — translating unstructured requirements into structured specifications, executing spec-driven coding, testing, and deployment — reducing deployment cycle time by about 40%.
Business process services becoming a fast adopter of Agentic AI; working with multiple customers on AI-led GBS transformation.
Example: for a steel major, proactively deployed AI agents in procurement bid management process, reducing order-to-invoice cycle from 28 days to under 10 days.

Agentic BPS gaining traction; adoption cycles for implementing AI in business process services are faster this year versus FY25, as customers are more confident putting AI into production, with focus on guardrails, security and governance.
In FY26, all next-gen services delivered strong growth across industries and markets, backed by continued investment in AI, talent, and innovative solutions.

subsections.label: AI deal composition (Q&A)
points: AI deals are of two kinds: many mega deals have significant AI embedded in delivery and business transformation; separately, the $2.3 billion annualized figure specifically calls out AI for business transformation revenue across industries and markets, largely rapid-build 12-16 week solutions delivered with forward-deployed engineers, including AI modernization work.

subsections.label: HyperVault Business
points: HyperVault has made significant progress this quarter on its journey to build out 1 GW of capacity, including winning customer commitments, land parcel finalizations and partnering agreements.

TCS actively engaging across the full ecosystem of hyperscalers, semiconductor companies, and model providers, with TCS as the integration partner across infrastructure, engineering, and AI-led services.

Demand signals remain strong and are translating into structured engagements and commitments, positioning TCS at the forefront of this build-out; this infrastructure layer is forming the foundation of TCS's full-spectrum Infrastructure-to-Intelligence play.
Engagements with hyperscalers and frontier AI model companies have moved beyond early exploration into design alignment, security frameworks, site due diligence, and commercial structuring.
Demand converging around large, anchor AI workloads in the 100-200 MW range per customer.

HyperVault has aligned a deep partner ecosystem including Tata Power, Tata Projects, Tata Communications, GE, Honeywell, ABB, Siemens, and many customers, covering EPC, power, cooling, controls, network and security.
Partnered with OpenAI to build 100 MW capacity, with an option to scale to 1 GW.
In collaboration with AMD, combining their 'Helios' rack-scale AI architecture with Tata group synergies to create high-density AI capacity in India.
Signed an MOU with ABB to strengthen collaboration across IT infrastructure and applications, digital and industrial AI initiatives, data centres, and other emerging technologies.

subsections.label: AI Partnerships
points: In FY26, invested significantly in strengthening AI partnerships spanning Enterprise partners, Hyperscalers, Deep Tech AI-native partners, and domain-specific partners.
In Q4, forged several strategic partnerships expanding joint collaboration including with ServiceNow, Google Cloud and ABB.

With OpenAI, announced a partnership spanning multiple high-impact areas — empowering Tata group employees with ChatGPT Enterprise, building industry-specific agents, joint go-to-market initiatives, and creating state-of-the-art AI infrastructure.
Working significantly with Anthropic already, with strategic partnership announcements to come in the near future; working closely with Mistral.

Trying to shape partnerships differently/more strategically than traditional GTM partnerships, as '360-degree partnerships' across four pillars: (1) becoming customers of each other via HyperVault capacity commitments (e.g., OpenAI 100 MW/1 GW), (2) using their products (e.g., ChatGPT Enterprise, Anthropic Claude), (3) industry-specific solutions, and (4) specific GTM motions similar to past strategic partnerships.

subsections.label: Company strategic aspiration
points: TCS aspires to be the World's largest AI-led Tech Services company, powered by: capitalizing on AI-led renewals, vendor consolidation and cost optimization deals resulting in market share gains; using new-age services & adjacencies enabling enterprises to 'Get ready for AI'; becoming a full-stack AI services player (Infrastructure to Intelligence) delivering maximum ROI via end-to-end industry value chain reimagination; and building new revenue streams such as AI infrastructure.
Made good progress across all these opportunity areas in FY26.

subsections.label: Geopolitical and macro headwinds
points: Q4 growth occurred against a backdrop of intensifying geopolitical conflicts and macro-economic uncertainty.

Direct impact from the current geopolitical situation has so far been restricted to the Middle East and, to some extent, the travel and transportation industry; no major impact seen in other industries so far.
If the situation continues and results in further supply chain disruption or other secondary issues, it may have a broader impact; caution flagged in BFSI is geo-specific, not broad-based.
Employees and families stationed in West Asia are safe; TCS is in constant touch with them providing necessary support amid tough times.

subsections.label: Sector-specific caution
points: BFSI: heightened macro and geopolitical volatility, increased uncertainty around interest rates, inflation and central bank actions influencing cautious client investment decision-making.

Manufacturing: client demand remained cautious due to macroeconomic uncertainty, tariff volatility, recalibration of EV demand, and continued capex restraint across Automotive, Industrial and Chemicals.
Technology and software: disciplined demand amid challenging macro, heightened geopolitical tensions, tariff-related uncertainty, and stringent manufacturing and data-sovereignty requirements.
Utilities segment (within ERU) experiencing stress.

subsections.label: Headwinds outlook (Q&A)
points: By and large, most known client-specific headwinds are believed to be behind the company, excepting a few that may come up or have already been accounted for; management cannot predict what happens down the line but believes most issues are behind.

subsections.label: Margin headwinds
points: Annual salary increments effective April 1 will be an immediate margin headwind entering FY27, with impact expected similar to past cycles (150-200 bps).

Continued investment under the Build-Partner-Acquire framework will also weigh on margins, partially mitigated by operational rigor and non-employee expense optimization; currency tailwind from rupee depreciation is not guaranteed.

subsections.label: No formal revenue/earnings guidance
points: As is customary, the company does not provide any specific revenue or earnings guidance; any forward-looking statements on the call must be reviewed in conjunction with risks outlined in the quarterly fact sheet.

subsections.label: FY27 outlook commentary
points: Management is quite positive about FY27 and about international growth, though declined to put a specific growth number, citing a good order book, three strong mega deals booked in the quarter, positive momentum across most industry verticals, and traction in new-age services.
Regular/stronger first-half (H1) seasonality expected to continue, consistent with the planning assumption used historically.

Margins: focus will be on growth with profitability; aspiration to move margins towards 26% on a longer-term basis, while absorbing near-term headwinds from annual increments and Build-Partner-Acquire investments.

AI revenue expected to be net accretive in the initial year, with the aim to arrest degrowth in traditional revenue while AI revenue increases; over time AI-related revenue is expected to grow much faster than any deflation in the rest of the business, following a similar dynamic to the digital transformation cycle.

guidance_ledger.statement: As you are aware, we don't provide any specific revenue or earnings guidance
We are quite positive about FY27, quite positive about the international growth
We are looking at a regular Q1, regular Q2 that we are used to seeing... we are also expecting a stronger 1H. Our planning assumption is along those lines only
We'd like to move towards 26%, but on a longer-term basis
On the wage increments, you should expect a similar impact on what we have seen in the past annual increment cycle, which had been in the range of 150 to 200 basis points
Our expectation is AI will be net accretive, like to see the initial year, our attempt would be to ensure that we arrest the degrowth while the AI revenue increase
By and large, most of the headwinds we know probably are behind us, excepting few that may come up or that we have already accounted for
HyperVault Business has made significant progress this quarter on its journey to build out 1 GW of capacity

themes.label: Sequential growth recovery
themes.note: Third consecutive quarter of sequential CC growth (1.2% QoQ) broad-based across North America, UK and Europe, though FY26 overall declined 2.4% CC YoY.

themes.label: AI-led demand and monetization
themes.note: Annualized AI services revenue crossed $2.3 billion, with AI embedded across mega deals and expected to be net accretive to growth in FY27.

themes.label: Margin resilience amid reinvestment
themes.note: FY26 operating margin hit a 4-year high of 25% (Q4 at 25.3%), even as tailwinds from realization and currency were reinvested into Build-Partner-Acquire initiatives; FY27 faces wage increment headwinds with aspiration to move towards 26% long-term.

themes.label: HyperVault AI infrastructure build-out
themes.note: Significant progress on 1 GW capacity target, including OpenAI (100 MW, option to scale to 1 GW), AMD collaboration, and ABB MOU, with demand converging around 100-200 MW anchor workloads per customer.

themes.label: Client base broadening and mega deal momentum
themes.note: Healthy client additions across all revenue bands after ~2 years, plus $12 billion Q4 TCV including three mega deals (M&S, UK telecom, US healthcare/pharmacy retailer).

themes.label: Geopolitical and macro uncertainty
themes.note: Impact currently limited to Middle East and travel & transportation, but BFSI, Manufacturing and Technology verticals show cautious client spending amid tariff, rate and geopolitical volatility.

themes.label: Talent and wage cost normalization
themes.note: Annual increments reinstated effective April 1 after two deferrals since COVID, expected to create a 150-200 bps margin headwind entering FY27.

key_takeaways: We are very pleased to announce third consecutive quarter of sequential growth. We delivered a strong 1.2% sequentially on a constant currency (CC) basis, in the backdrop of intensifying geopolitical conflicts and macro-economic uncertainty.

Our order book performance was also very strong in Q4, with $12 billion in TCV including three mega deal wins from Marks and Spencer, a leading telecom operator in the UK, and a leading American healthcare & pharmacy retailer.
Every revenue band saw healthy additions this quarter after a gap of about 2 years, which speaks to the early signs of stability and growth returning to our mid-sized and large accounts.
We have announced annual salary increments for our eligible associates across all grades, effective April 1.
The momentum we see in our AI Services, which continued to accelerate impressively, standing at US$2.3 billion on an annualized basis.
The promise we see in our HyperVault Business – which has made significant progress this quarter on its journey to build out 1 GW of capacity.

Even though our FY 2026 revenue declined by 2.4% in constant currency, we delivered a strong $40.7B in TCV including 5 mega deals. We maintained a strong focus on execution to deliver an operating margin of 25%. This is the highest operating margin achieved in the last 4 years.

We are very pleased with the continuous revenue growth momentum we have seen in the last 3 quarters. In Q4, our Revenue grew by 1.2% QoQ in constant currency, with an operating margin of 25.3% and a net margin of 19.4%.
pressing_questions: Is there any foreseeable change in quantity or quality of client inquiries or even bookings around agentic AI implementation post first week of Feb when Anthropic announced a string of agentic AI launches?

Many frontier model companies are just announcing a new project or agent which may be in their development pipeline but not yet launched (e.g., Claude Mythos) — is this leading clients to defer existing IT spends to wait and watch for the product to hit the shelf?
How do we think of FY27 growth, given the exit run rate and where our order booking is and also high expectations around some AI-led deflation?
Should we start getting back to 3-4% growth in the international business where TCS used to be, or better, or is the recovery going to be far more gradual this year?
SG&A in the second half has been elevated — is this the new normal or will it normalize back to below 15%?
Is our restructuring done or is there more cost associated with it still to come through?

If you keep the macro aside, would you expect the new AI services to be accretive to revenue growth in fiscal '27, net of all the deflation seen in renewals/existing business, or is it too early to confirm any such trend?
AI for business — when you look at revenue productivity and margins in that portion of the business, how does it compare to company average?

AXISBANK.about: Incorporated in December 1993, Axis Bank Limited is a private sector bank.It has the third-largest network of branches among private sector banks and an international presence through branches in DIFC (Dubai) and Singapore along with representative offices in Abu Dhabi, Sharjah, Dhaka and Dubai and an offshore banking unit in GIFT City.[1]

quarters.summary: Axis Bank's Q1FY27 NIM at 3.46% is flagged as the cycle bottom, with management reiterating the structural NIM guidance of 3.8% over the previously communicated time period, aided by retail disbursement-led mix recalibration and deployment of incremental FCNR(B) liquidity; growth is guided to continue at industry-plus-300bps in the medium term, cost-to-assets is expected to keep trending down (no terminal number given) over the next 18-24 months, and asset quality/provisioning remain stable with a ₹2,001 cr precautionary buffer untouched during the quarter.

subsections.label: NIM bridge - YoY
points: 34 bps YoY NIM decline attributed to: 19 bps due to full impact of 125 bps repo rate cut in current quarter vs only 25 bps rate cut in same quarter last year, net of benefit in cost of funds due to liability repricing; 16 bps due to change in balance sheet mix over last 12 months.

subsections.label: NII vs advances growth gap - YoY
points: Gap between 8% YoY NII growth and 19% YoY advances growth attributed to: 6% due to full impact of 125 bps repo rate cut vs 25 bps cut in same quarter last year, net of cost of funds benefit from liability repricing; 5% due to change in balance sheet mix.

subsections.label: NIM bridge - QoQ
points: 16 bps QoQ NIM decline attributed to: 3 bps due to interest reversal from seasonality of Agri slippages in Q1 vs Q4; 4 bps due to change in balance sheet mix through the quarter (comprising both asset and liability mix, including proportionality between earning assets and total balance sheet); remaining 9 bps due to change in pricing of loans (full impact of prior quarter's pricing visible on yields, repricing of contracted loans, and incremental loans priced lower amid competitive intensity).

subsections.label: Opex movement drivers
points: YoY opex increase of ₹420 cr attributed to: 38% linked to volume, 44% technology and growth related, remainder BAU.
QoQ opex decline of ₹744 cr included ₹271 cr from one-time staff cost items; other-than-staff opex down 9% QoQ largely driven by lower statutory costs and lower volume-linked expenses.

One-off items driving the reversal: (i) ₹129 cr Q4FY26 provident fund charge (tied to adverse G-Sec rates from RBI administrative action at quarter end) reversed substantially in Q1 as G-Sec rates eased; (ii) gratuity item; (iii) true-up of excess variable pay provision.

subsections.label: Precautionary/West Asia stress provisioning
points: Q4FY26 additional one-time provision of ₹2,001 crores was created proactively based on assessment of evolving macroeconomic and geopolitical uncertainties; no drawdown occurred in Q1FY27, so balance remains ₹2,001 crores at June 30, 2026.
This provision continues to be prudent/precautionary and does not reflect any deterioration in asset quality or adverse credit trends in the loan or investment portfolio as of the reporting date.

subsections.label: Capital raises
points: US$600 million Additional Tier 1 and US$300 million senior debt raised, strengthening capital position and funding profile; AT-1 saw interest from high quality long-only investors.
AT-1 raised till quarter end (US$500 mn) plus post quarter-end (US$100 mn) places the bank comfortably to call back existing AT-1 on its contracted call date, subject to regulatory approvals.
Bank reiterates it does not need equity capital for either growth or protection pillar.

subsections.label: Investment yield clarification
points: Management noted a 6 bps QoQ increase in average earning investments per average balance sheet data, contrasting with an analyst's period-end figure observation; discrepancy attributed to period-end flows from AT-1 and senior bond raised on 30th June getting placed.

subsections.label: ECL transition outlook
points: Assessment as of 31st March 2026 balance sheet indicates marginal impact on net worth from ECL transition, as ECL is an exposure standard vs IRAC being an outstanding standard, requiring provisions for unfunded exposures plus RBI-prescribed floors.

On a go-forward basis, industry (including Axis) expected to see higher provisions to assets in the first year of ECL transition given how Stage 1 and Stage 2 provisioning will run against the 40 bps of standard asset provisioning applicable today.

subsections.label: Wholesale growth drivers
points: Wholesale Banking growth remains broad-based driven by sectors benefiting from strong transaction flows.

Relationship-led strategy with continued scaling of Mid-Corporates and Conglomerates, and deeper One Axis engagement enabling wallet share gains while steadily improving yields and relationship economics.

Corporate loans span project finance, term loans and working capital across sectors such as energy, commercial real estate, infra and metals; management does not expect rapid transition to bond markets even as bond markets normalize, expecting transition only as assets mature in the natural course.
91% of corporate lending is to A- and above rated corporates; over the last 5 quarters the bank has not slipped down the credit spectrum.
Wholesale RAROC stands head-to-head with retail; return assessment includes not just NIM but ancillary business such as higher balances, trade fees, FX, etc.

subsections.label: SME growth drivers
points: SME franchise delivering strong and diversified growth, with digital and analytics as key enablers of scale, enhancing sourcing, speeding up credit decisions and improving customer experience while supporting disciplined and scalable growth.

subsections.label: Retail growth drivers
points: Retail disbursement trends continue to sustain and remain encouraging, supported by focus on sourcing quality customers, maintaining underwriting rigor and scaling distribution through effective execution across multiple distribution channels.

subsections.label: Deposit franchise
points: FCNR(B) deposit is attracting strong interest from NRI customers, seen as a meaningful opportunity to augment deposit base through NRI franchise and proactive outreach to banks across overseas markets.
Efforts remain focused on further strengthening the deposit franchise through increased granularization and a more stable liability mix, supporting a resilient and well-diversified funding base.
New-to-Bank franchise scaling with improving quality and premiumization, evidenced by 18% YoY increase in NTB average balances.
Corporate Salary segment continues to be a strong growth driver; Existing-to-Bank salary book also grew, reflecting continued strengthening of corporate salary franchise and customer deepening.

subsections.label: Burgundy / Wealth
points: Burgundy continues to be key driver of premiumisation; strength and consistency of proposition recognised with Burgundy Private honoured at PWM Wealth Tech Awards 2026.

subsections.label: Overseas / foreign currency loans
points: Foreign currency loans grew sharply but this growth is purely opportunistic - based on selective participation in sectors and clients meeting internal RAROC thresholds and offering reciprocal flows/fee opportunities; no specific directional change in portfolio mix intended, and bunching can occur in a particular quarter.
Overseas book is high-quality: 98% rated A- and above, 64% of outstanding to top 10 conglomerates.
Overseas book does not include FCNR or leveraging component (per management clarification, without directly confirming or denying).

subsections.label: Wholesale funding vs corporate loan stickiness
points: Corporate loans span project finance, term loans and working capital; loans given for shorter working-capital cycles vs longer-term project finance/term loans are expected to remain with the bank rather than transition quickly to bond markets.
No specific bunch-up of temporary-period loans created this quarter that would run off quickly; normal ratios of a typical wholesale franchise are being maintained.

subsections.label: Repricing terms on corporate loans
points: Repricing of corporate loans (e.g., linked to T-bill/repo) generally cannot occur absent a credit event; repo-linked loans can be repriced typically at quarter end when there is a repo change.

subsections.label: AXIOM enterprise AI operating model
points: AXIOM is designed to systematically embed AI in the functioning of the Bank by adopting a capability platform-led approach.

Core idea: build capabilities once, govern them centrally, and deploy them many times across the enterprise, creating reusable AI assets leveraged across businesses, functions, products, and customer journeys, driving consistency, speed, and scale.
Regular updates on AI transformation journey introduced last quarter; details on Slides 13 and 14 of investor presentation.

subsections.label: Industry recognition for digital/AI/innovation
points: Named 'Best Digital Bank' at the Financial Express India's Best Banks Awards.
Won 'Best AI-Driven Customer Experience Initiative' at the 14th Digital Customer Experience Awards 2026.
Received Platinum Award at the Infosys Finacle Innovation Awards 2026 for leveraging next-generation technologies to drive innovation in corporate banking.

quarters.summary: Axis Bank closed FY26 with strong all-round growth (advances +19% YoY, deposits +14% YoY) and improving profitability (consolidated ROA 1.64%, ROE 15.15% in Q4), while voluntarily creating a ₹2,001 crore one-time standard asset provision against West Asia-conflict stress scenarios. Management reiterated its through-cycle NIM target of 3.80% (15-18 months from last rate cut transmission), a 70:30 retail/SME-to-wholesale mix aspiration, an 18% aspirational bank-level ROE, and expects continued disciplined, calibrated growth faster than the industry into FY27, while flagging heightened geopolitical/macro uncertainty (West Asia conflict, oil, inflation, currency) as a key watch item.

subsections.label: Two clarifying accounting items
points: Citi India Consumer Business acquisition (FY2022-23): intangibles of ₹8,714.24 crores recognized per independent valuer report; Bank fully amortised these through P&L in FY2022-23 as a prudent measure to protect dividend-paying capacity; no deferred tax asset was created at the time nor was deductibility considered in current tax provisioning pending regular tax assessment.

During Q4FY26/FY26, following conclusion of regular tax assessment proceedings, tax depreciation on these intangibles was allowed, reducing tax expense by ₹2,193.20 crores (comprising reversal of excess prior-year tax provisions of ₹1,129.80 crores, reduction of current year tax expense by ₹265.85 crores, and recognition of deferred tax asset of ₹797.55 crores). Effective tax rate for FY26 stands at 17.25%.

Voluntary enhancement of standard asset provisioning: In Q4FY26, the Bank proactively created an additional one-time provision of ₹2,001 crores based on assessment of evolving macro/geopolitical uncertainty, in line with its conservative risk-management philosophy.
This provision is prudent/precautionary and does not reflect deterioration in asset quality or adverse credit trends; core asset quality metrics remain stable and within risk guardrails.

Provision creation/utilization/reversal is governed by a Board-approved framework, calibrated via internal stress testing under 'severe but plausible' downside scenarios; adverse stress scenario assumes average oil above US$150 for 12 months, inflation at 7.4%, and currency depreciation of ~20% from current levels.
Management stated this provision is considered sufficient to absorb potential incremental provisioning charge to P&L even under the most adverse FY27 stress scenario modelled.
Net impact of the two one-time items plus a trading loss (due to year-end rate movements from extraneous factors) is net-neutral on P&L for the quarter.

subsections.label: NIM and margin drivers
points: NIM decline for FY26 (-29 bps YoY) reflects absorption of 125 bps repo rate cut pass-through.
Bank maintains through-cycle NIM stance of 3.80%, measured from date of last rate cut transmission.

Structural NIM drivers: improving balance sheet mix (loans+investments 89% of total assets); Retail+CBG share of advances declined 471 bps YoY to 67% as a conscious strategy to optimize NII in the near term, with plan to rebalance over a 3-year planning horizon given 24% YoY/19% QoQ growth in retail disbursements; RIDF low-yielding bonds declined ₹5,761 crores YoY; liability quality (outflow rate) at 28.8% moved adversely and remains a focus area; QAB CASA at 37% with 39 bps CASA pricing improvement FY26 vs FY23, offsetting marginal YoY decline in QAB CASA via rate benefit across the liability stack.

Repo-linked book (61% of loan book per slide 14) received full repricing effect in the current quarter from the December rate cut, since repo rate pricing transfer occurs at end of quarter of rate cut announcement.
No artificial day-count convention management in NIM computation; number of days in quarter is simply annualized for days in the year; G-sec book follows market-standard 30/360 methodology.
Residual TD repricing: management did not disclose percentage but confirmed 'some legs left on that lever' going forward.
Cost of deposits declined 46 bps YoY / 4 bps QoQ on disciplined funding strategy execution.

subsections.label: Opex detail
points: YoY opex increase of ₹629 crores: 36% attributable to technology spends, 33% volume-linked expense growth, balance BAU expense partly offset by reduction in statutory costs.

QoQ opex increase of ₹830 crores, of which ₹408 crores due to one-time staff cost items (₹126/₹129 crore employee benefit provisioning this quarter vs ₹282 crore one-time reversal of no-longer-payable staff expenses in the prior quarter, causing opposite-direction swings).
QoQ period-end headcount declined by 552; opex other than staff up 7% QoQ, largely BAU volume-linked growth offset by PSLC cost reduction.

subsections.label: Wholesale Banking strategy
points: Wholesale Banking has evolved from a balance-sheet-centric model to an ecosystem-led approach, driving diversified, high-quality growth in relatively strong-cycle segments, deepening relationships to enhance share of wallet, improve risk visibility, and deliver planned RAROC.

Incremental wholesale growth seen in power (largely renewables), commercial real estate, data centers, NBFCs (largely PSL driven), and manufacturing; growth remains selective and quality-led, maintaining pricing filters and RAROC discipline, and leveraging balance sheet for reciprocal transaction flows leading to fee/float expansion and 'One-Axis' outcomes (corporate salary, Axis Capital, trusteeship, etc.).
Wholesale RAROCs held up in FY26 versus FY25; no dilution in risk standards; 91% of the wholesale book rated A- and above on both stock and flow basis.

subsections.label: SME franchise

subsections.label: Retail franchise
points: Retail disbursement growth remains strong and risk-calibrated, centred on credit-tested customers, strengthened underwriting discipline, and balanced scaling across proprietary and partner-led distribution channels.

Growth in retail disbursements is not a Q4 phenomenon; acceleration was visible in the prior quarter as well; investments in technology/digital and deepening branch relationships with existing customers are helping accelerate momentum, which is expected to eventually feed into overall book growth.

subsections.label: Premiumisation / Burgundy

subsections.label: Loan book composition
points: Loan book is granular and well-balanced with retail advances at 55%, corporate loans at 33%, CBG at 12% of overall advances.

~73% of loans are floating rate; ~48% of fixed rate book matures within 12 months; breakup of floating rate book by benchmark type and MCLR re-pricing frequency detailed on Slide 14 of investor presentation.

subsections.label: RAROC/ROE mix debate
points: Management confirmed wholesale RAROCs have held up through FY26 versus FY25 without dilution of risk standards; theoretical question raised on why mix (wholesale vs retail) matters if RAROC holds up — answer: RAROCs are leverage-agnostic but ROEs are leverage-dependent, and there's a finite leverage a financial institution can carry to retain its AAA rating, necessitating a balanced book.

In the near term, Bank is optimizing for NII with wholesale growth but plans to recalibrate the book back toward the 70:30 retail/SME-to-wholesale target mix; recalibration is described as continuing/ongoing, driven by strong retail asset disbursement activity levels on the ground.
Aspirational ROE at bank level is 18%; retail/SME ROEs assumed marginally higher than wholesale ROEs, though management declined to disclose segment-level ROE figures.

subsections.label: Geopolitical and macro uncertainty

The Bank remains watchful entering FY27 given ongoing uncertainties, though confident in its ability to grow in a disciplined, calibrated manner faster than the industry.

The additional standard asset provision of ₹2,001 crores is tied to an identified pool of loans (across customer segments/products) per a risk-team stress-testing framework; provision will be drawn down if slippages occur from this pool in FY27, though not all such loans require oil at $150 to slip (some may slip at $110).

risk_register.note: PSL compliance achieved at headline and sub-segment levels only inclusive of PSLC purchases, not organically compliant.

themes.label: NII/NIM optimization vs through-cycle target
themes.note: Near-term wholesale-led growth is NIM-dilutive; Bank reiterates 3.80% through-cycle NIM target achievable 15-18 months from last rate cut transmission.

themes.label: Wholesale-led growth acceleration
themes.note: Wholesale advances grew 38% YoY driven by ecosystem-led approach in power/renewables, CRE, data centers, NBFCs and manufacturing, with RAROC discipline maintained and 91% of book rated A- and above.

themes.label: Retail disbursement momentum & mix recalibration
themes.note: Retail disbursements grew 24% YoY/19% QoQ across home loans, vehicle, agri and personal loans; management signals ongoing recalibration back toward 70:30 retail/SME-to-wholesale mix.

themes.label: Asset quality improvement / technical slippage runoff
themes.note: GNPA, net credit cost and slippage ratios improved YoY/QoQ; technical impact slippages fell sharply (net slippages now 0.07%) and disclosure to be discontinued from Q1FY27.

themes.label: Precautionary provisioning for geopolitical/macro risk
themes.note: ₹2,001 crore one-time standard asset provision created against an identified loan pool for West Asia conflict-related stress scenarios (oil >$150, inflation 7.4%, currency -20%); core asset quality otherwise stable.

themes.label: AI-led transformation (AXIOM)
themes.note: Bank is only ISO 42001-certified BFSI globally; expects AI to drive meaningful bottom-line impact over next 18-24 months via AXIOM operating model.

themes.label: Cost efficiency / operating leverage
themes.note: Cost-to-assets declined 18 bps YoY to 2.28% despite adding 400 branches, aided by technology-led efficiency gains and a 3% YoY workforce reduction.

key_takeaways: Our total advances grew 6% QOQ and 19% YOY, within which Wholesale grew 38%, SME 24% and Retail 8% on YOY basis.
Our consolidated Q4FY26 ROA was 1.64% and ROE was 15.15%
Our GNPA was at 1.23%, declining 17 bps QOQ and 5 bps YOY; while the Net credit cost was at 0.37%, down 13 bps YOY and 39 bps QoQ

During the quarter and year ended 31st March 2026, following the conclusion of regular assessment proceedings by the income tax authorities, tax depreciation on these intangibles was allowed... the tax expense for Q4FY26 and FY26 is lower by ₹2,193.20 crores

During Q4 of FY26, the Bank proactively strengthened its balance sheet by voluntarily enhancing its prudent provisioning framework for standard assets... the Bank created an additional one-time provision of ₹2,001 crores during the quarter.

Between the two one-time items above and trading loss in the quarter due to year-end rate movements driven by extraneous factors, the net impact on the P&L of these three items combined is net neutral on P&L.
We have not shifted away from our stance that we expect to deliver 3.8% NIM through cycle... we will get to through-cycle 3.80%, 15 to 18 months from transmission of last rate cut.
As we step into FY27, we are watchful of the ongoing uncertainties, however we stay confident in our ability to grow in a disciplined and calibrated manner, faster than the industry.
pressing_questions: Could you remind us if there is any day-count convention benefit in your NIMs? Secondly, if the full 25 bps rate cut from December has been passed on your EBLR book? And thirdly, if there's any residual TD repricing left on your book?

At 34% year-on-year, you are growing your corporate book meaningfully faster than your peers. What opportunity do you see that others may not be seeing? Could you show us how this has benefited your ROA or is that still left in the future?
When do we reach to this 3.8 through the cycle NIM guidance that we have earlier provided? Any comment on when do we think we can achieve this 3.8%?

Wanted to get a sense on what could be the loan yield uplift from the absence of interest reversals due to technical slippages next year? Is there a possibility of any recoveries that can be achieved in these technical slippages in the next fiscal?

You talked about your buffer provision you created this quarter quoting $150 oil price. Does that mean that if the situation gets worse from here on, you would actually be drawing down on these provisions this year itself?
Given deposit growth for the sector has moved up but loan growth has moved up even faster, is there a potential for deposit rates to rise from here?
Since we can't observe segmental RAROCs for the company, if you were to triangulate the ROEs, is it meaningfully lower than a number like 15% or are you targeting for a different number here?
Have we reverted back to where we were earlier on credit filters, or are you still comfortable to hold the stance that you're more open to take a bit more risk than before?

WELSPUNLIV.about: Welspun Living Limited, part of the US$ 2.7 billion Welspun Group, is one of the largest home textile manufacturers in the world. The Company offers a wide spectrum of Home & Technical textile products and Flooring solutions. The Company has established itself as a thought leader within the home textile industry over the years and continue to focus on the enablers viz. Innovation, Branding and Sustainability to consolidate its leadership position. [1] It manufactures a wide range of home textile products ranging from towels, bath robes to sheets, tob and basic& fashion bedding. It also entered into the business of carpets flooring solutions recently. [2]

quarters.summary: Welspun Living posted its strongest quarter in seven quarters with 23.5% YoY consolidated revenue growth and 140bps YoY EBITDA margin expansion; management reiterated FY27 guidance of double-digit revenue growth and low-teens EBITDA margins, targeting a gradual move toward 15% margin over the next year and ROCE improvement to low teens during FY27, while flagging raw material inflation and the Vapi flood as near-term headwinds (Q2 impact) with recovery expected by Q3/Q4.

key_figures.label: Green power share of total consumption
EBITDA margin gap to normalized target
FY27 capex guidance (repeated by Manish Bansal)

subsections.label: Margin drivers
points: Margin expansion driven by healthy volume recovery, operating leverage, and an improving business mix.

Three key drivers cited: (1) volume recovery and tariff share unwinding converting into operational leverage on a largely fixed cost base, (2) improving business mix, (3) cost discipline via structural cost actions taken over the last years including reducing energy cost, automation, and improved throughput.
Margin expansion is structural, not circumstantial, driven by process simplification, automation acceleration, and deployment of AI tools and Industry 4.0 technologies on shop floors.

Gross margin declined in the quarter primarily due to raw material inflation; management expects raw material costs to remain a factor to watch given crude and cotton price trends; guided that margin numbers projected will be maintained even if RM stays at similar levels.

subsections.label: Capital allocation
points: Capital allocation philosophy remains unchanged — investing selectively behind projects that enhance productivity, improve operational efficiency, and strengthen long-term competitiveness.
Board approved INR121 crores debottlenecking and modernization project at Anjar facility in July, replacing older technology with more advanced technology and improving plant utilization.
This forms part of overall FY27 capex, guided at INR400-500 crores range.
Next year's capex guidance too early to project; company to provide guidelines closer to end of this financial year.

subsections.label: Sustainability / Green power
points: Significant progress in transitioning Anjar manufacturing complex toward a greener power ecosystem.
With commissioning of the CTU line, Anjar facility commenced receiving 100% green power supply from mid-July 2026.
With Anjar now fully powered by green energy, 79% of Welspun Living's total power consumption is now green.

subsections.label: Working capital & balance sheet
points: Continued to strengthen the quality of the balance sheet through disciplined working capital management, healthy cash generation, and prudent capital allocation.

Priorities remain focused on improving quality of growth by strengthening cash generation, enhancing asset productivity, maintaining disciplined capital allocation, and delivering sustainable improvements in return ratios.

subsections.label: Tariff refunds
points: Tariff refund process is progressing in line with the applicable regulatory framework; necessary procedures for eligible claims initiated and refunds have started being received where applicable.
Timings and quantums remain subject to completion of the administrative process.

subsections.label: Home textiles / branded businesses
points: Continue to be the world's largest exporter of terry towels; position built on technology, innovation, and customer trust accumulated over three decades.
IP portfolio stands at 50 patents, described as a deepening moat.
Christy delivered 16% growth this quarter, supported by strong U.K. performance, expanding presence in the Middle-East, and growing traction in the United States.
Welhome is increasing acceptance across North America, Japan, and newer markets.

Christy towels featured throughout the Wimbledon Championships, continuing a partnership spanning nearly four decades; Christy monogram woven into HygroCotton towels featured in court-side moments and player interviews.

Global B2B business grew more than global branded business this quarter; B2B remains the anchor of all businesses and will continue to grow strongly; branded business is around 18% of revenue but B2B is the stronger anchor.
Home textiles volume growth was a mix of volume and value; GIT (goods-in-transit) factor and 50-60 day dispatch stagger effect also play into realized numbers this quarter.

subsections.label: Domestic business (India)
points: Domestic businesses grew 21.3% YoY, sustaining trajectory from Q4; Welspun and Spaces continuing to strengthen presence across key channels.
B2B and B2C both grew in strong double digits.
Ongoing shift from unorganized to organized home textiles market continues to be a structural tailwind; widely distributed brand position to capture increasing share.
Domestic retail is near breakeven on EBITDA this time, with growth of around 20%; on target to achieve INR1,000 crores revenue.
Both Welspun and Spaces businesses continue to show great growth across the country.

subsections.label: Flooring
points: Turnaround efforts beginning to deliver visible results; EBITDA margins materially improved to 10.4%, highest in over two years, reflecting operational discipline and structural actions taken over the past year.
Strategic shift towards soft flooring (area rugs and other qualitative products) driving margin upside.
Diversifying beyond the U.S. into markets such as Australia and Canada through strategic partnerships; strengthening presence in commercial flooring.
Margins considered sustainable, not a one-off; driven by qualitative product mix shift, geographic diversification, and cost controls.

FY27 outlook: continued focus on soft flooring across categories; India commercial flooring space (wall-to-wall, carpet tiles) growing with investment; global opportunity in UK/Europe (soft flooring, area rugs) via FTA; continued geographic diversification into Australia, New Zealand, Canada, and GCC; qualitative product focus expected to protect margins from dilution.
No top-line spillover from last quarter into this quarter's flooring or overall numbers.

key_figures.label: Anjar debottlenecking capex (alternative figure cited by Manish Bansal)

subsections.label: U.S. onshore pillow facilities
points: Ohio pillow facility has ramped up to around 81% utilization.
Nevada facility has commenced operations and is building momentum in the sleep category.
Together, these facilities strengthen customer proximity, improve speed to market, and enhance supply chain agility.
On track to double revenue to reach USD60 million this year in the pillow business.
Mattresses are not part of the sleep ecosystem product expansion plan; focus remains on pillows.

subsections.label: Utilization across categories
points: Utilizations will be over 80% across all verticals (towels, sheets, rugs) for the full year, with quarter-to-quarter staggering; bed linen at 60% in Q1 is expected to average toward 80-85% for the full year, implying higher utilization in later quarters.
Debottlenecking of ~INR120 crores at Anjar is in processing, expected to add build-up of around 10-20 tons per month volume, addressing choke points in dyed/processing categories.

Additional bath category capacity expansion being explored given 80% utilization and large market opening in Europe; investment decisions will be guided by ROIC prudence, but company will not hesitate to invest to capture opportunities.

subsections.label: Vapi facility flood
points: Unprecedented flooding at the Vapi facility; immediate priority was safety of people — every person on site evacuated safely within a few hours.
Operations partially resumed within a week and are expected to be restored in a phased manner.
Teams responded by activating contingency plans and rerouting production.
Company is fully insured and working closely with insurance providers to facilitate claims process.
Q2 FY27 will be impacted largely due to the flood; Q3 and Q4 expected to see restoration, with annual double-digit growth target maintained.

key_figures.label: Pakistan share of U.K. home textile imports

subsections.label: UK/Europe FTA opportunity
points: India-U.K. free trade agreement, effective 15th July, puts India on an equal tariff footing with Pakistan, which today holds over 50% of U.K. home textile imports.
Welspun is not starting from scratch — Christy, Disney brand relationships, and established retailer network mean the company is already embedded and ready to scale.
U.K. and Europe businesses delivered 20%+ growth this quarter; expect double-digit growth in U.K. businesses over the coming years.
Europe FTA conversations are 'right around the corner'; conversations with retailers have already begun and working relationships exist.
Order inflows for UK have begun conceptually with FTA conversations; product approval/development cycle means confirmations will gradually flow into the system.

India overall in a good position as FTAs open up for UK, with Europe and other countries following; U.K. market ~USD5-7 billion with Pakistan at ~50% share seen as a market-share opportunity to capture.
Medium-term aspiration: America share around 50-51% or up to 55%, with rest of world (UK, Europe, Japan, India, others) contributing the balance, moving non-EU/non-US mix from 41% toward 50%.

subsections.label: US market dynamics
points: Consumer spending across all segments described as very healthy; U.S. retail sales grew 5.2% YoY in May; recent consumer data across Father's Day, Mother's Day, back-to-school season very healthy; footfalls increased across key retailers.
Fed held rates steady; overall America described as resilient with healthy growth momentum in consumption.
India in a strong position given America needs huge capacities and no neighboring country has comparable capacity; incremental business continuing to flow given robust demand.

No market share lost during the tariff disruption period due to long-term strategic partnerships with retailers in largely replenishment-driven U.S. business; company and retailers collaborated through tough tariff times.

subsections.label: Flooring geographic diversification
points: Diversifying beyond the U.S. into markets such as Australia and Canada through strategic partnerships.
Also targeting New Zealand and GCC for geographic diversification in flooring.

key_figures.label: Anjar facility green power supply commencement

subsections.label: Freight & logistics
points: Long-term partnerships with all freight carriers have yielded results in managing container availability issues that some competitors have flagged.
Market freight rates have increased, but impact to customer dispatches will not be affected.

subsections.label: Pricing strategy / positioning
points: Welspun operates in mid-to-better-to-best categories and does not work in opening price points, which helps protect margins even as non-U.S. geography mix (relatively lower margin) grows.
Raw material cost increases are being passed on to customers this time, in clear conversations and negotiations on new order pricing; company states it will not be able to bear those costs itself.

Tariff cost historically borne through a mix of company, retailer, and consumer absorption depending on case, customer, and program; tariff impact already passed on to U.S. consumers and not retracted; this cost is now baked into current margins (down from 50% exposure to current ~10%).

subsections.label: Awards & recognition
points: Welspun Living received the platinum trophy for highest global exports and gold trophies for innovation and excellence in ESG at the TEXPROCIL Export Awards 2026, reinforcing differentiated global market position.

subsections.label: Raw material inflation
points: Gross margin decline in the quarter primarily attributed to raw material inflation; crude and cotton price trends flagged as macro factors to watch going forward.
Cotton price increase has been sharp in recent months; crude oil derivatives have also moved up significantly.
Company states raw material cost increases will be passed on to customers going forward, and does not expect a major reversal of costs already borne.

subsections.label: Vapi flood impact
points: Unprecedented flooding at Vapi facility will impact Q2 FY27 largely; company fully insured and working with insurers on claims; recovery expected by Q3/Q4 with annual double-digit growth target maintained.

subsections.label: Tariff / trade policy uncertainty
points: U.S. tariff framework has currently preserved India's competitive position; India-U.S. BTA talks progressing with optimism for positive outcome.
Tariff cost absorption is a case-by-case mix of company, retailer, and consumer; already baked into margins currently at ~10% versus prior 50% exposure.
One competitor cited managing performance/margins comfortably up to 18-20% tariff; management response framed around collaborative approach with retail partners as tariff levels evolve with BTA.

subsections.label: RoSCTL export incentive risk
points: RoSCTL scheme is up for termination by September; uncertainty on whether government will extend it.
If RoSCTL is eliminated, export incentive as a percentage of EBITDA is described as quite decent/material; company is awaiting outcome and hoping for a positive resolution.

On incentive base case, if there is any negative outcome/lapse, the impact/brunt would be borne across all industry players (pass-through), not solely by Welspun; base case assumption is for likely continuation or positive outcome.

subsections.label: West Asia conflict / geopolitical cost risk
points: Analyst raised question on whether FY27 margin guidance factors in potential cost spikes due to ongoing West Asia conflict; management's response focused on volume recovery, mix improvement, and cost discipline as levers toward 15% margin, without specifying a distinct West Asia cost provision.

subsections.label: Overall outlook
points: Company remains confident of delivering double-digit revenue growth and EBITDA margins in the low teens for FY27, and remains well-positioned to capitalize on opportunities ahead.
EBITDA margin of 12.5% expected to move gradually toward 15% over the next one year, driven by volume recovery, tariff share unwinding, mix improvement, and cost discipline.
Company will maintain the double-digit growth trajectory demonstrated this quarter for the next couple of years, per management response to a growth-cadence question.
Next year's capex too early to project; guidance to be provided closer to end of this financial year.
Flooring business margins of ~10% considered sustainable and expected to be maintained for the full year and going forward.
Bed linen utilization, currently 60% in Q1, expected to average toward 80-85% across the full year as quarters progress.

guidance_ledger.statement: We remain confident of delivering double-digit revenue growth ... for FY27.
EBITDA margins in the low teens for FY27; our full year guidance for EBITDA margins will be targeting around low-teens.
Right now it's 12.5%, and as we grow forward in the next one year, we will see that moving towards 15%.
We continue to target an improvement in ROCE to the low teens during FY27.
We continue to expect FY27 capital expenditure in the range of INR400 crores to INR500 crores.
Next year, it is too early to project now; closer to end of this financial year we will come back for next year guidelines.
We are on track to double revenue to reach USD60 million this year.
Our utilizations will be over 80% across [all categories]... the average we are talking about an 80%, 85%.
We are on the target to achieve INR1,000 crores [domestic business].
We already are looking at USD100 million in terms of our global brands as well.
Medium-term aspiration to move your non-EU revenue mix from 41% to 50%... America will be around 50%, 51%, mostly, or 55%, and the rest of the world... will contribute to this portion.
We can assume 10% or present margin for the entire year and going forward, is it doable? Yes.
I mean, you have seen the growth this time and we will maintain.
Quarter two will be impacted largely... however quarter three, quarter four, we are going to restore it. So annually... it will continue to give the double-digit growth and we will be on the track.
RoSCTL is up for termination by September... we will wait till this happens, and we hope for the best.
India again is a very good commercial space that is growing... we will see India in the terms of wall to wall, carpet tiles will grow.
We will continue to maintain these numbers... we will maintain our numbers that we have committed on the low teens.
Owing to current optimization, we look at next three years that we will achieve the INR15,000 crores target; in current optimized capacity we can move up to around INR11,500 to INR12,000 crores.
Indian market will again grow at a rate of around 26% to 30%.
In an ideal world, next year we will be a net debt zero company unless we plan any additional capex or special requirement.
This year we did around $27 million. Next year we intend to double that - we are talking about $60 million.
The utilization will be above more than 86% across all the three categories as we go forward.
Flooring, INR1,000 crores kind of a number we are talking about right now.
We are going to look at kind of EBITDA steady state of around more than 20% here.
Welhome is well positioned for a double-digit growth.

risk_register.risk: Raw material cost inflation (cotton, crude/crude derivatives)
risk_register.note: Gross margin decline in the quarter attributed to raw material inflation; cotton and crude prices flagged as ongoing watch items; costs being passed to customers going forward.

risk_register.risk: Vapi facility flooding
risk_register.note: Unprecedented flooding caused evacuation and partial operations halt; Q2 FY27 to be impacted; fully insured, claims process underway; recovery expected Q3/Q4.

risk_register.risk: U.S. tariff policy uncertainty
risk_register.note: Current U.S. tariff framework has preserved India's competitive position; India-U.S. BTA talks progressing with optimism; tariff cost now ~10% vs prior 50% exposure and baked into margins.

risk_register.risk: RoSCTL export incentive scheme termination
risk_register.note: Scheme up for termination by September; uncertain whether government will extend; elimination would be material to EBITDA via export incentives; any negative outcome expected to be borne industry-wide.

risk_register.risk: West Asia geopolitical conflict cost impact
risk_register.note: Analyst flagged potential site/input cost spikes due to ongoing West Asia conflict as a risk to the 15% margin target; management did not explicitly quantify a provision.

risk_register.risk: Lower margin profile of non-U.S. geography mix
risk_register.note: As non-U.S. geography share grows, these markets are structurally lower margin; company plans to protect margins by focusing on mid-to-better-to-best categories rather than opening price points.

risk_register.risk: Container/freight availability
risk_register.note: Some competitors flagged container availability issues; Welspun states no impact due to long-term freight carrier partnerships, though market freight rates have increased.

risk_register.risk: U.S. tariff volatility (Section 122, Section 301, BTA uncertainty)
risk_register.note: Tariff moved from 10% to 25% to 50% and back to 10%; conversations ongoing on refunds and BTA rate of 15%-18%; Section 301 investigation initiated on multiple countries including India.

risk_register.risk: West Asia / geopolitical conflict disrupting freight, energy and commodity costs
risk_register.note: Pressured freight, energy and commodity costs across global supply chain in FY26; Global Flooring business saw sharpest impact; situation remains uncertain requiring close monitoring.

risk_register.risk: Strait of Hormuz / Red Sea logistics disruption
risk_register.note: Exports rerouted via Cape of Good Hope adding 15-20 days transit; company adapted to this routing over time; GCC exposure minimal at 2% of revenue.

risk_register.risk: Input cost inflation (cotton, man-made fiber, crude, yarn, dyes, polymers)
risk_register.note: Cotton up 10%, man-made fiber up 20%+, crude up 40%, yarn (terry towel/bedsheet) up 20-30%, dyes/chemicals up 20%, polymers up 20%; conversations ongoing with customers on 50-50 cost sharing.

risk_register.risk: Rupee depreciation / currency
risk_register.note: Rupee at INR96/USD but no net delta gain once full commodity cost basket increase considered; hedging policy and 65/35 ratio maintained across group.

risk_register.risk: Cautious retail buying and softer discretionary demand
risk_register.note: FY26 impacted by cautious retail buying, tariff uncertainty and softer discretionary demand especially in H1; Q4 showed green shoots and sequential improvement.

risk_register.risk: U.S. inflation impact on consumer demand
risk_register.note: Inflation could be up in America; however retail demand still seen as robust with expected growth versus last year.

risk_register.risk: Global Flooring / Advanced Textiles softer demand
risk_register.note: Global Flooring saw 25.1% YoY decline; Advanced Textiles saw 20% YoY decline due to volume pressure and slower export uptake; medium-term outlook constructive on FTAs.

themes.label: Margin recovery
themes.note: EBITDA margin expanded to 12.5% in Q1 FY27, third consecutive quarter of improvement, on volume recovery, operating leverage, mix, and cost discipline; guided toward low teens for FY27 and 15% over the next year.

themes.label: FTA-driven market access
themes.note: India-U.K. FTA effective 15th July puts India on equal tariff footing with Pakistan (50%+ of UK imports); UK and Europe businesses grew 20%+ this quarter with Europe seen as the next opportunity.

themes.label: Tariff volatility
themes.note: U.S. tariff framework has currently preserved India's competitive position and BTA talks are progressing, but tariff cost absorption remains a case-by-case mix between company, retailer and consumer.

themes.label: U.S. pillow capacity expansion
themes.note: U.S. onshore pillow business grew 2.3x; Ohio at ~81% utilization and Nevada facility commenced operations, on track to double revenue to USD60 million this year.

themes.label: Input cost inflation
themes.note: Gross margin declined this quarter due to raw material inflation (cotton, crude derivatives); costs being passed on to customers going forward.

themes.label: India domestic growth engine
themes.note: Domestic business grew 21.3% YoY with both B2B and B2C in strong double digits, driven by the structural shift from unorganized to organized home textiles market; targeting INR1,000 crores.

themes.label: Branded business scale-up
themes.note: Christy grew 16% with Wimbledon partnership visibility; Welhome gaining acceptance in North America and Japan; global brands targeting USD100 million with 27% YoY growth.

key_takeaways: We had the strongest quarter in seven quarters, with consolidated revenues growing 23.5% year-on-year and 15.4% sequentially to INR2,828 crores, while EBITDA margins expanded to 12.5%, improving by 140 basis points year-on-year and 170 basis points sequentially, driven by healthy volume recovery, operating leverage, and an improving business mix.
Profit after tax nearly doubled, with PAT margins improving from 3.8% to 5.7%. More importantly, Q1 revenue is 9% above the same quarter of FY25, the pre-tariff baseline.
Margin expansion is now in its third consecutive quarter, from 6.8% at the trough to 12.5% today, and it is structural, not circumstantial.

The India-U.K. free trade agreement, effective 15th July, puts India on an equal tariff footing with Pakistan, which today holds over 50% of U.K. home textile imports. Our U.K. and Europe businesses delivered 20% plus growth this quarter.
Home textiles exports grew 28.1% year-on-year, our strongest quarter in recent years.

Our U.S. onshore pillow businesses grew 2.3x this quarter. The Ohio pillow facility has ramped up to around 81% utilization. Our Nevada facility has commenced operations and is building momentum in the sleep category. We are on track to double revenue to reach USD60 million this year.
In India, our domestic businesses grew 21.3% year-on-year, sustaining the trajectory from Q4 with Welspun and Spaces continuing to strengthen their presence across key channels.

In flooring, our turnaround efforts are also beginning to deliver visible results. EBITDA margins materially improved to 10.4%, highest in over two years, reflecting operational discipline and structural actions taken over the past year.

We would like to briefly address the unprecedented flooding at our Vapi facility... Operations partially resumed within a week and are expected to be restored in a phased manner. We are fully insured and are working closely with our insurance providers to facilitate the claims process.
We remain confident of delivering double-digit revenue growth and EBITDA margins in the low teens for FY27 and remain well-positioned to capitalize on the opportunities ahead.

What are the sustainable levers behind flooring's 10.4% EBITDA margin, the best in the segment's history?

Can management quantify the Q2 impact from the Vapi flood?
What is the outlook for capacity utilization by segment for the full year, particularly for bed linen which was only 60% in Q1?
Is domestic retail now EBITDA positive, and how are Advanced Textiles and domestic retail performing?
Given the 15% EBITDA margin aspiration versus current 12.5%, what specific levers bridge the 250bps gap, and does guidance factor in West Asia conflict-related cost spikes?

Is the growth in global B2B (versus branded) business a sign of prioritizing private label over the branded portfolio?

Does the sleep ecosystem leadership ambition include category expansion beyond sheets/pillows, e.g., smart bedding or mattresses?
How is US retail demand/order book visibility shaping up in the near-to-mid term?
At what tariff level is the company confident of maintaining balanced performance, given a competitor cited comfort up to 18-20% tariff?
As non-US geography share increases (structurally lower margin), what levers will sustain overall profitability?
Has India seen any tangible change in sourcing allocation or incremental order wins now that tariff position has normalized, or is growth from existing customers only?
Has Welspun lost any market share with customers during the past year of tariff issues?
What are management's thoughts on the potential termination of RoSCTL by September, and its impact on EBITDA given the size of export incentives?

With the Anjar debottlenecking, what capacity increase can be expected and when will it commission? Are there plans for bath category capacity expansion given 80% utilization and European market opening?
Regarding input cost inflation (cotton, crude derivatives), are customers compensating with price increases, and is there any risk of reversal of previously absorbed tariff costs?

quarters.summary: FY26 was a year of external shock absorption (tariff volatility, geopolitical tensions, demand softness) with Q4 marking a decisive sequential inflection - revenue grew 7.7% QoQ and EBITDA margin improved 313 bps to 10.8%. Management guides FY27 to be a year of measured volume recovery and margin progression, targeting double-digit revenue growth and EBITDA margins advancing into the teens, supported by tariff easing, FTAs (UK by June-end, Europe by January-end), Nevada/Ohio pillow ramp-up, and continued cost discipline; net debt targeted at zero next year barring major capex.

points: Tighter controls led to reduction in debtors and inventory.

key_takeaways: Revenues improved quarter-on-quarter. Margins stepped up meaningfully. Cash flows remained strong and execution momentum is clearly visible entering FY27.

PARADEEP.about: Incorporated in 1981, Paradeep Phosphates Limited is a manufacturer of non-urea fertilizers and India’s second largest private sector phosphatic company. The company is engaged in manufacturing, trading, distribution, and sales of a variety of complex fertilizers such as DAP, three grades of Nitrogen-Phosphorus-Potassium (namely NPK-10, NPK-12, and NP-20), Zypmite, Phospho-gypsum, and Hydroflorosilicic Acid.[1]

quarters.summary: Q1FY27 saw strong financial and operational performance with revenue up 36% YoY and EBITDA per ton at best-in-class levels, despite Middle East/Hormuz-led raw material volatility. Management guided sustainable EBITDA of ~Rs.5,000/ton for FY27 with the current Rs.7,000/ton quarter benefiting from low-cost opening inventory; phosphoric acid expansion (5 to 7 lakh tons) remains on track for Dec'26/Aug-Sep'27, the larger 3 lakh ton phosphoric+sulphuric acid expansion is planned for FY29-30, and the Board approved a Rs.250 crore aluminium fluoride plant to diversify into non-subsidy industrial chemicals, targeted to be commissioned in 22-24 months with expected topline of Rs.180-200 crore and EBITDA of ~Rs.50 crore.

subsections.label: Q1FY27 result drivers
points: Strong performance attributed to existing supply chain efficiency, sourcing diversification strategy for key raw materials, and Pan-India marketplace selling and distribution capabilities despite Middle East crisis-led raw material price/availability volatility.
EBITDA per ton increase to Rs.7,000/MT mainly on account of low-cost stock held at the beginning of the year (opening inventory benefit), not expected to sustain.
Backward integration of sulphuric acid at both Mangalore and Paradeep running full stream, combined with harnessed raw material inventory, contributed to EBITDA improvement.

subsections.label: Working capital and cash flow
points: Additional inventory built up in prior quarter was liquidated in Q1FY27.
Inventory increase this quarter mainly on account of higher trading volumes; otherwise raw material and finished goods inventory reduced.
Debt reduced by Rs.700 crores on an overall basis; cash flow from operations was positive.
Robust cash flow driven by 43% YoY growth in cash flow from the market and 22% YoY higher subsidy collections for the same period.

subsections.label: EBITDA per ton outlook
points: Company reiterates sustainable EBITDA guidance of Rs.5,000 per ton for the year as the number being targeted at year-end, hoping to cross it with government/industry coordination.
Once expansion projects (backward integration) are completed, sustainable EBITDA of Rs.7,000+ per ton is expected, achievable in phases over roughly two to two-and-a-half years.
Overall EBITDA per ton at company level is not expected to face pressure despite higher trading volumes, due to supply chain efficiencies built into the system.

subsections.label: DAP vs NPK mix shift
points: Significant growth in DAP is a technical/tactical shift driven by policy - DAP profitability appears significantly better compared to NPK currently.

As a market strategy, focus on NPK continues; NPK farmer sales grew 6% even as overall NPK volume degrowth was seen, driven by significant price increase taken in NPK portfolio to maintain profitability, partially passed to the customer.

Stark price gap between DAP (Rs.1,350/bag) and NPK complexes (Rs.2,100-2,500/bag) is driving farmer shift toward DAP; this is viewed as a short-term/tactical situation, not a structural or fundamental shift.
Company's long-term view on NPK remains strong, with capacity augmentation plans having a huge thrust toward NPK.
Farmer shift back to NPK expected to happen quickly if price differential normalizes to within Rs.200/bag; currently the gap is about Rs.1,000/bag.
South India shows higher awareness levels and continues using NPK portfolio predominantly despite price gap elsewhere.

NPK adoption drivers beyond price: farmer awareness of balanced fertilization (phosphate, potash, micro-nutrients, organic carbon), soil health awareness, sulphur deficiency in soil, and productivity results; overuse of nitrogen/urea remains an issue in the country.
Removal of MRP cap on DAP by government (if it happens) expected to help rebalance the portfolio; not seen as likely in the short term.

subsections.label: Trading/import strategy
points: Traded volumes for rabi season expected to be significantly higher than last year (~2,70,000 tons), aided by ~0.5 million tons of imports secured, helping Q2 and Q3 through December.

Portfolio of traded products includes NPK, DAP, TSP (long-term perspective, high phosphate/low nitrogen strategy) and ammonium sulphate (encouraged by government as alternate nitrogen/sulphur source).
DAP traded volume was low in Q1 (~1,000 tons) as company relied on manufactured DAP; TSP and ammonium sulphate trading were more significant.

Any shortfall in production will be made good through trading so there is no overall decrease in sales; strategy is to optimize between manufactured and imported volume to maintain market share and stakeholder value, not pure volume growth.

subsections.label: Market share and brand strength
points: Balanced regional focus across North, East, West and South markets (particularly strong in West and South) provides demand-side advantage.
Strong brands Jai Kisaan Navratna and Jai Kisaan Mangala enjoy farmer trust, aiding offtake and cost advantage.
Full portfolio flexibility across Urea, DAP, and NPKs gives the company an edge in offering complete solutions to farmers.
Company maintains leadership position in both market share and product pricing.
