subsections.label: Backward integration benefits
points: Full benefit of expanded sulphuric acid capabilities available during the quarter, reflecting strength of backward integration in phosphoric acid and sulphuric acid, and helped improve quality of earnings.

Sulphuric acid capacity fully utilized; not sold outside currently — entire output consumed by fertilizer facilities. Sulphuric acid used both for phosphoric acid production and for N20 (sulphur-dominated) product.

Co-generated power from sulphur-to-sulphuric acid process was sold to grid at the beginning of last quarter, but stopped due to fluctuations in sulphur/sulphuric acid availability; facility remains available.

subsections.label: Phosphoric acid & granulation expansion progress
points: None of the expansion plans have changed due to short-term turbulence from the Middle East situation.
Phosphoric acid expansion from 5 to 6 lakh tons expected by this December; 6 to 7 lakh tons expected mostly by August-September next year — same timeline as previously communicated.
Execution for the incremental phosphoric acid capacity already underway; equipment already ordered.

Larger expansion of 3 lakh tons phosphoric acid plus sulphuric acid capacity is progressing as planned, with final commercial discussions ongoing; expected to come in one shot around FY29-30 (mid, second quarter of FY29-30), with capex quantum of Rs.3,500-3,600 crores.
Granulation capacity debottlenecking (3.7 to 4 lakh tons) at Odisha plant is underway with contract already awarded, expected by December.

subsections.label: Aluminium fluoride project (non-subsidy diversification)
points: Board approved Rs.250 crore investment for aluminium fluoride plant at Paradeep facility to diversify into related industrial chemical space and strengthen non-subsidy portfolio.
Investment reinforces manufacturing excellence by converting a by-product (hydrofluorosilicic acid) into value-added products.
Basic engineering work currently in progress; sourcing strategy for aluminium fluoride raw material being finalized.

Currently producing 9,000-10,000 tons per annum of hydrofluorosilicic acid (FSA), which is fully sold to outside parties as raw material; new plant intends to convert this into higher-value aluminium fluoride instead.
Plant designed at 15,000 MT capacity to enable utilization of entire hydrofluorosilicic acid output through aluminium fluoride conversion; commissioning expected in 22-24 months from Q1FY27.

No major challenge seen in terms of B2B saleability/marketability of the product; extensive background work completed before board approval; product does not require a gestation period with smelting customers despite import specification differences.
Target market mainly the Odisha region where aluminium industry is present; company sees itself as a strategic player able to sell and market without much difficulty.
Product aims to reduce reliance on imports of aluminium fluoride into India.

subsections.label: Urea plant policy impact (Goa & MCFL)
points: New urea policy notified; company evaluating full implications versus current energy benchmark.
Energy efficiency investment at Goa (reducing 0.2 G-Cal per ton on urea production) has been completed and capitalized, delivering benefit starting this quarter.

On a normalized basis, Goa's EBITDA per ton improvement from this energy investment is assumed at Rs.700-800/MT for Q1FY27; under the new urea policy, Goa sees a positive EBITDA impact of about Rs.1,500/MT, while Mangalore (MCFL) sees a negative impact of Rs.700-800/MT.

subsections.label: Raw material sourcing amid volatility
points: Sulphur and phosphoric acid prices going up create strain on overall working philosophy; company scouting various sourcing opportunities and getting some support from ammonia price reduction.
Current sulphur price is $1,000+/ton (post-Q1) versus Q1FY27 average of $850/ton; current sulphuric acid price is $350-370/ton.
Company operating around 70% of phosphoric acid capacity currently; expects added government support going forward.
Company also augmenting via imported DAP and NPKs, with a robust pipeline for the rabi season through imported product lines.
Currently no specific long-term sulphur sourcing arrangement exists due to fluctuations; procurement happening entirely on spot basis on both sides.
Company declined to disclose exact sourcing cost of sulphur, citing commercial sensitivity, but stated it has been competitive versus global benchmarks.

Rock and acid availability (via OCP relationship) is a key strength versus peers — no serious issue in rock availability, superior quality rock and acid sourcing; only smaller supply chain issues may arise.
Good raw material planning has enabled the company to convert market uncertainty into a relative strength.

subsections.label: Inventory and stock dynamics
points: Low-cost opening inventory held at start of the year played a significant role in boosting Q1FY27 EBITDA per ton.
Inventory increase this quarter mainly attributable to higher trading volumes; raw material and finished goods inventory otherwise reduced versus prior quarter.

subsections.label: Non-subsidy business diversification
points: Company continues to focus on fertilizer business as core, with backward integration as current thrust; entering specialty/industrial chemicals space represents next area of focus.
Aluminium fluoride project is described as 'only the beginning' — management is seriously considering further initiatives in this space.
Long-term vision is for at least 20% of EBITDA to be supported through non-subsidy business over time, though this is described as a long-term target with no specific timeline.
Capital allocation shift toward other industrial chemicals expected after FY29, once current backward integration and capacity expansion priorities are completed.

subsections.label: Execution priorities (next few quarters)
points: Tactical shift towards more profitable product (DAP) in Q1FY27 given raw material volatility, while maintaining a strong long-term view on NPK backed by upcoming capacity augmentation.
Company continues to explore leveraging its wide product portfolio manufacturing capability across facilities.
Focus on optimizing supply chain wherever price advantage arises, given strong sourcing/logistics capabilities.
Key priority areas for coming two-to-three quarters: phosphoric acid capacity expansion, the larger capacity expansion planned for FY29-30, and continued supply chain optimization.

Commercial priorities include market development (building high-nutrient-use nano category portfolio), balancing NPK and DAP portfolio amid supply and monsoon-related demand risks, and driving profitable growth while maintaining leadership in market share and pricing.

subsections.label: Middle East / Hormuz disruption
points: Middle East crisis has led to sharp escalation in volatility of raw material prices and availability.
70% to 75% of global trade of sulphur and ammonia moves across the Strait of Hormuz; supply disruptions for these commodities expected to continue in the short term.
Industry making concerted efforts via empowered committees (government and senior industrial officials) working in close coordination to ensure fertiliser security for the nation and farmers.
Company remains committed to driving growth through focused operational discipline amid the challenging environment.

subsections.label: Monsoon-related demand risk
points: Apart from the current supply chain risk, monsoon posed a challenge; however, July has been a good month for rainfall, easing this concern somewhat.

subsections.label: Policy/price cap risk (DAP-NPK gap)
points: Stark price gap between government-capped DAP MRP and market-priced NPK complexes is creating demand distortion favoring DAP; seen as a short-term issue rather than fundamental change.
Removal of MRP cap on DAP is not viewed as likely in the short term, though management expects it could be addressed going forward.

key_figures.label: EBITDA improvement from backward integration completion

subsections.label: EBITDA per ton guidance
points: Management reiterates sustainable EBITDA guidance of Rs.5,000/ton as the number targeted by year-end, hoping to cross it with government/industry coordination.
Q1FY27's higher Rs.7,000/ton is not expected to sustain given it benefited from low-cost opening inventory.
Post completion of expansion projects, sustainable EBITDA of Rs.7,000+ per ton is expected in phases, over roughly two to two-and-a-half years.
Company does not expect pressure on overall EBITDA per ton despite higher trading volumes anticipated for the rest of the year, due to supply chain efficiencies.

subsections.label: Non-subsidy business ambition
points: Long-term target of at least 20% of EBITDA from non-subsidy businesses (such as industrial chemicals), though timeline is described as long-term and evolving.
Capital allocation shift toward other industrial chemicals expected post-FY29, after backward integration and current capacity expansions are completed.
Aluminium fluoride plant expected to contribute Rs.180-200 crores in topline and Rs.50 crores in EBITDA post-commissioning.
EBITDA improvement of 30-35% expected post completion of backward integration.

subsections.label: Trading volume outlook
points: Company declined to give exact forward guidance on rabi trading volume numbers but indicated it would be significantly higher than last year's ~2,70,000 tons, aided by ~0.5 million tons of imports secured for Q2/Q3 through December.

guidance_ledger.statement: We continue to say that we should have a sustainable EBITDA of Rs.5,000 per ton. I think that is the number we are looking at the end of this year. And hopefully, with all the coordination that we are having, we should be able to cross that number.

We feel actually realistic EBITDA for a year would be around Rs.5,000 per MT. Once we complete our expansion projects, what we have explained earlier, we should be in a position to have a sustainable Rs.7,000 plus per MT... It could come in phases actually. You can take it as two to two and a half years.

guidance_ledger.metric: Phosphoric acid capacity expansion (5 to 6 lakh tons)
guidance_ledger.statement: The phosphoric acid expansion, what earlier we said is about Rs.5 lakh to 6 lakh will become a reality by this December.

guidance_ledger.metric: Phosphoric acid capacity expansion (6 to 7 lakh tons)
guidance_ledger.statement: The Rs.6 to 7 lakh is also going to happen mostly by August, September next year.

guidance_ledger.metric: Larger phosphoric acid & sulphuric acid expansion (3 lakh tons)
guidance_ledger.statement: The bigger expansion... is also going on as per what we have planned... It will come in one shot, actually. We have set a FY29-30... mid of the FY29-30... around second quarter of FY29.

guidance_ledger.metric: Granulation capacity debottlenecking (3.7 to 4 lakh tons)
guidance_ledger.statement: Debottlenecking is actually expected by again December. The contract is already awarded. It is going in full swing.
We are currently looking quite optimistic about getting this plant commissioned within 22 to 24 months.
We expect at least a top line of Rs.180 crores to Rs.200 crores coming out of this facility.
Expecting at least Rs.50 crores of EBITDA which is coming out of this.
Over a period of time, the long-term vision is that at least 20% of the EBITDA should be supported through non-subsidy, but that is a long term target that we have kept for ourselves.
The sustainable EBITDA guidance that we give is Rs.5,000 at the moment, which when we complete our backward integration, everything should be improved by 30% to 35%.

We are not giving a forward guidance on the exact numbers as of now, Prashant, but it will be significantly higher [than last year's ~2,70,000 tons]... we almost secured half a million tons of imports as far as the traded products are concerned, which will help us from both Q2 and Q3, right up to December.

guidance_ledger.metric: Overall EBITDA per ton amid higher trading volumes
guidance_ledger.statement: Overall, I think we continue to maintain that EBITDA per ton at a company level, because there are a lot of supply chain efficiencies that have been brought into the system. So, overall, we do not think that there is a pressure on EBITDA per ton below the guidance that we have talked about.
That I think you should ask maybe the political people, but currently it does not seem in the short term, but I think somewhere going forward, it should get at least removed.

guidance_ledger.metric: Capital allocation shift toward industrial chemicals
guidance_ledger.statement: With long-term view of non-subsidy business contributing 20%, so after FY29, we can see capital allocation shift towards other industrial chemicals... Yes, of course.

Currently the spread was 5,300 (INR/ton). As we deepen backward integration across Phos Acid and Sulfuric Acid, the spread is going to increase. But given the global situation, hard to give a specific number for FY27; backward integration benefit should flow in FY27.
We will still hold ourselves because let things settle and we will come back actually.
EBITDA percentage is not the right metric for the industry; EBITDA per ton is preferred, but given the Middle East situation, a specific number cannot be given at this moment.
Normal CAPEX will be around INR 600 crores, which is completely financially closed.
Expansion of Phos Acid from half a million tons to 0.7 million tons expected to close this year, giving an incremental 200,000 tons of Phos Acid in FY27.
We should be able to take a call in terms of our proposed 3,000 tons per day Sulfuric Acid within this quarter.
Debottlenecking of granulation capacity at Odisha plant, roughly around 2 lakh ton, expected to come this current year (FY27), with incremental volumes coming in second half.
Of the total ~0.3 million tons debottlenecking target, 0.2 million tons targeted this year and remaining 0.1 million ton targeted for FY28.
Backward integration will be around 80% to 90% once Phos Acid expansion and other initiatives complete.
We have covered most of Q1; Q2 situation is unfolding, difficult to give a direct answer beyond Q1.
Production volume remains almost steady to a large extent, at least 70% to 80% for us in Q1.

guidance_ledger.metric: MCFL urea Sulfuric Acid synergy benefit
guidance_ledger.statement: Using team from Sulfuric Acid plant to the other one, at least almost INR 1,000 per ton could be the impact, which is on a favorable side.
With the 6.4 to 6.1 Gcal energy efficiency, in current gas price scenario, it will be around INR 1,000 to INR 1,200 per ton of urea at EBITDA level.
The delta between imported Sulfur/Sulfuric acid input and indigenous Sulfuric acid is normally around INR 3,000, but at current level it will be reduced to around INR 1,500-2,000 delta.
All other major CAPEXs, as said earlier, is likely to be done by FY28 and FY29.

guidance_ledger.metric: Goa urea production capacity (with supportive policy)
guidance_ledger.statement: With the new change in policy, Goa can do up to 4.5 lakh tons of urea (vs 4 lakh tons currently).
If there is a supportive policy, MCFL can still produce more than 4 lakh tons; overall RAC is around 4 lakhs, with supportive policy can go up to 4.4-4.5 lakh tons.
We don't see any reason for subsidy delay given no custom duty on ammonia/Sulfur, Kharif stock build-up and consumption happening, and subsidy is adequately budgeted with government budget support.

risk_register.risk: Middle East/Hormuz raw material disruption (sulphur, ammonia availability and price volatility)
risk_register.note: 70-75% of global sulphur and ammonia trade moves via Strait of Hormuz; sulphur price rose from Q1 average of $850/ton to $1,000+/ton currently; disruptions expected to continue in the short term.

risk_register.risk: Strain on operating philosophy from rising phosphoric acid and sulphur prices
risk_register.note: Company operating at ~70% of phosphoric acid capacity; hopeful for added government support.

risk_register.risk: Monsoon impact on demand
risk_register.note: July has been a good month for rainfall, easing earlier monsoon-related demand concern.

risk_register.risk: DAP-NPK price gap distorting product mix
risk_register.note: Stark ~Rs.1,000/bag gap between capped DAP MRP and NPK complex prices driving farmer shift to DAP; viewed as short-term, not fundamental; NPK shift expected to reverse quickly if gap narrows to within Rs.200/bag.

risk_register.risk: No long-term sulphur sourcing contracts, fully spot-based procurement
risk_register.note: Currently no specific long-term arrangement for sulphur due to fluctuations; procurement happening on spot basis on both sides.

risk_register.risk: Subsidy receivable buildup
risk_register.note: Outstanding subsidy of Rs.4,600 crores as of 30 June 2026, though Rs.2,650 crores received in Q1FY27 and subsidy collections grew 22% YoY.

risk_register.risk: Middle East geopolitical situation / Strait of Hormuz disruption impacting ammonia and sulfur availability and pricing
risk_register.note: Middle East contributes 70-75% of ammonia and sulfur raw materials, most shipments via Strait of Hormuz; industry stock remains balanced but under close government-industry coordination.

risk_register.risk: Elevated Sulfur prices/international stress
risk_register.note: Sulfur prices remain under stress for last few months internationally; domestic sourcing (MRPL, IOC) provides comfort but international sulfur remains stressed.

risk_register.risk: Elevated Ammonia prices
risk_register.note: Ammonia sourcing diversified from Strait of Hormuz to East Coast/Southeast Asia, but prices remain elevated globally.

risk_register.risk: INR depreciation
risk_register.note: Cited as a headwind alongside raw material volatility despite which company delivered consistent performance.

risk_register.risk: Raw material availability constraint on production
risk_register.note: All three plants currently running at around 80% (not above 90%) primarily due to raw material constraints (ammonia and sulfur/Sulfuric Acid intensive products).

risk_register.risk: Uncertainty on Q2FY27 raw material coverage/visibility
risk_register.note: Q1FY27 largely covered but Q2 situation still unfolding; industry engaging in near-daily discussions with government (Secretary of Fertilizers, MDs of major companies) for clarity.

risk_register.risk: Subsidy timing/delay risk
risk_register.note: Analyst raised concern of potential subsidy delay at elevated raw material prices; management does not foresee delay given no custom duty, adequate budget support and government engagement.

risk_register.risk: Volatile global raw material price/margin environment affecting FY27 guidance
risk_register.note: Management declined to give specific EBITDA per ton or revenue guidance for FY27 given ongoing Middle East volatility.

themes.label: Middle East/Hormuz raw material disruption
themes.note: 70-75% of global sulphur/ammonia trade moves via Strait of Hormuz; sulphur price surged from $850 average in Q1 to $1,000+ currently, disruptions expected to continue short term.

themes.label: Backward integration expansion
themes.note: Full sulphuric acid capacity benefit drove 32% YoY production growth and 7% phosphoric acid growth; phosphoric acid expansion (5-7 lakh tons) on track, larger 3 lakh ton expansion planned for FY29-30.

themes.label: NPK/value-added mix shift
themes.note: Tactical shift to DAP (55% volume growth) over NPK (9% degrowth) due to Rs.1,000/bag price gap, though NPK farmer sales grew 6% and long-term NPK strategy remains intact.

themes.label: FY27 guidance withheld amid volatility
themes.note: Company reiterates Rs.5,000/ton sustainable EBITDA guidance for FY27 while declining to give exact rabi trading volume or RM cost pass-through numbers given evolving situation.

themes.label: Working capital / subsidy receivable buildup
themes.note: Outstanding subsidy of Rs.4,600 crores but Rs.2,650 crores received in Q1, debt reduced by Rs.700 crores, and operating cash flow turned positive with 43% growth in market cash flow.

themes.label: Government policy support & subsidy adequacy
themes.note: New urea policy notified with +Rs.1,500/MT benefit for Goa but -Rs.700-800/MT impact for Mangalore (MCFL); government coordination expected to help address raw material cost increases.

themes.label: Capacity utilization amid raw material constraints
themes.note: Phosphoric acid capacity utilization at ~70% amid sulphur/RM volatility even as existing capacity runs near 100%; sulphuric acid capacity fully utilized internally with no meaningful external sales.

key_takeaways: In Q1 FY27, revenue from operations increased 36% YoY to Rs.6,124 crores, EBITDA rose 21% to Rs.742 crores, PBT increased by 24% to Rs.526 crores, and PAT stood at Rs.393 crores. Sales volume grew by 4% to 9.85 lakh tons, just close to a million ton sale.

During the quarter, full benefit of expanded capabilities of sulphuric acid was available to us, due to which the sulphuric acid production was higher by 32% on a YoY basis. Phosphoric acid production was higher by 7% on a YoY basis, reflecting the strength of our backward integration benefits.
Our key expansion project of phosphoric acid expansion, that is phase-I from 5 lakh ton to 7 lakh ton is on track.

The board of PPL in its Q1 FY27 meeting approved an investment proposal of Rs.250 crores for setting up aluminium fluoride plant at our Paradeep facility, to enter and diversify into related industrial chemical space and build a non-subsidy portfolio.
70% to 75% of global trade of sulphur and ammonia moves across the Strait of Hormuz. The supply disruptions for these commodities are expected to continue in short term.

This quarter EBITDA is around Rs.7,000 per MT, and last year in the same quarter it was around Rs.6,500 per MT. This increase is mainly on account of the stock, what we have got at the beginning of this year.

We feel actually realistic EBITDA for a year would be around Rs.5,000 per MT. Once we complete our expansion projects... we should be in a position to have a sustainable Rs.7,000 plus per MT... two to two and a half years.
Despite industry phosphatic fertilizer volume being flat this quarter, company is able to grow 13% volume YoY.
pressing_questions: For Q2 FY27, how are we placed on sourcing of raw materials and whether at these prices of sulphur, are we willing to continue to buy and manufacture acid or is it worthwhile now to buy acid and use it for manufacturing of fertiliser?

Considering current RM cost in terms of all the raw materials and currency rates, what could be the EBITDA per ton we are able to make or there is shortfall of Rs.5,000, how do you mitigate or any thinking towards the government additional subsidy we expect?
Is there any possibility to remove the pricing cap on DAP?

quarters.summary: PPL delivered robust FY26 financial and operational performance with strong revenue, EBITDA and PAT growth, and continues to invest in backward integration (Sulfuric Acid and Phos Acid capacity expansion). However, management flagged significant near-term uncertainty from the Middle East/Strait of Hormuz situation impacting ammonia and sulfur availability and pricing, and declined to give specific FY27 revenue/EBITDA-per-ton guidance until the situation stabilizes, though Q1 FY27 raw material requirements are largely covered and backward-integration benefits are expected to flow through FY27.

subsections.label: Operating Cash Flow Drivers
points: Negative operating cash flow of ~INR 1,000 crores mainly on account of increase in inventory and increase in trade receivables and subsidy.
Increase in inventory is to accommodate the increase in raw material prices, and this will unfold in Q1 FY27.
Strategic call taken to hold additional inventory of around 30 odd days.
Subsidy receivable increase is mainly on account of increase in DAP prices/DAP subsidy and other items that came toward the end of the period.
Management expects all these items to unwind in Q1 FY27 and to reap the benefit of stock holding and subsidy receivable in Q1.

subsections.label: Debt & Working Capital
points: Gross debt increased to INR 6,800 crores, largely reflecting subsidy receivable buildup.
Company has adequate working capital limits; money stuck in subsidy and inventory will wind up in Q1FY27.

Management does not see the debt level going up beyond current level — in all probability it should come down once subsidy parcel flows and inventory is consumed (main consumption in June and July), reducing working capital borrowing.

subsections.label: Subsidy Receipt Timing
points: Subsidy received of INR 2,600-odd crores in Q4; outstanding subsidy of INR 3,800 crores (both brought coal and channel stock).

Company has received subsidy up to April end; management does not see subsidy being delayed as ammonia and Sulfur have no custom duty, Kharif stock build-up/consumption is happening, and subsidy is adequately budgeted with government budget support.

subsections.label: CAPEX Plan
points: Normal CAPEX for FY27 will be around INR 600 crores, for which financial closure has been done.
Total new project cost is INR 3,600 crores; in FY26 most spend was at engineering stage, actual cash flow to start in FY27.
All other major CAPEX, as said earlier, is likely to be completed by FY28 and FY29.

subsections.label: Demand Drivers
points: Sales volume growth led by strong performance in value-added NPK grades.
Company grew NPK volumes despite industry degrowth, reflecting a long-term strategy to provide balanced nutrition.
In the current year mix could shift because of Sulfur constraints, tilting strategy more toward securing phosphate and nitrogen (urea/DAP) to maintain food security.
Government is expected to put emphasis on urea and DAP; complexes (NPK) continue but are priced higher for farmers relative to DAP and TSP.

Farmer's natural first preference is typically urea and DAP; in current situation with too much variance between NPK price and DAP price, a balanced growth in both segments is expected, but overall phosphatic segment remains strong.
Kharif season supply well covered; company confident and optimistic about Kharif; making efforts for faster future raw-material tie-ups.
Opening stocks and good visibility on Kharif; clarity on Rabi supply chain expected in another two to three months.

subsections.label: Pricing
points: Company retains price leadership in the NPK market and has taken a price increase in NPK.
Not entire price increase can be passed on to customer given extremely high sulfur and ammonia prices; company expects government support on this.
Strategy includes focusing on products like DAP for margin clarity to maintain overall profitability.
Government's advantage-disadvantage policy for DAP/TSP factors in import price changes, adjusting bottom line positively with price changes.

subsections.label: NPK Category Growth
points: Growth led by strong performance in value-added NPK grades; NPK as a category, including TSP, grew 22% to 24.64 lakh tons.
Company among top two-three companies in NPK volumes with N20 grade growing 9% YoY to 14.5 lakh metric tons.

subsections.label: Traded/Import Products
points: TSP traded volume ~2.8 lakh metric tons and DAP traded ~2.2 lakh metric tons for FY26; overall import portfolio ~0.6 million tons.
For Q4, DAP imported was 0.3 lakh metric tons and TSP was 0.4 lakh metric tons.
Traded products carry a lower EBITDA per ton than the blended company-level figure.

subsections.label: MCFL Urea Plant Economics
points: Reduction in benchmark energy norm from 7.3 to 6.5 impacted EBITDA by around INR 3,000 per ton — this was due to expiry of an investment benefit given for switching from naphtha to gas, not a policy change per se.
Current MCFL urea EBITDA per ton is around INR 6,000-6,500, and margins in urea are a function of global gas prices.
Sulfuric Acid capacity expansion at MCFL is expected to help via power generation, with an estimated favorable impact of at least INR 1,000 per ton.

subsections.label: Goa & MCFL Plant Utilization
points: Goa plant produced ~4 lakh tons of urea and ~7 lakh tons of NPK in FY26; MCFL produced ~4 lakh tons of urea and ~3.5 lakh tons of NPK.
Both plants completed RAC (Reassessed Capacity) quantity; Goa energy saving project undertaken after RAC completion.
Goa NPK utilization is roughly 0.7 to 0.8 (of capacity); Mangalore NPK is at almost full capacity of 0.4.
With supportive policy, Goa could produce up to 4.5 lakh tons of urea and MCFL could produce more than 4 lakh tons.
Company declined to give specific Q3/Q4 split for MCFL urea production, will share separately.

subsections.label: Blended EBITDA per ton
points: Company reports EBITDA per ton on a blended, company-level basis (including all products/segments) rather than segment-specific; blended EBITDA per ton was 5,700 in Q4 and 5,300 for the full year, up from spread cited as 5,300 in one instance.

subsections.label: Sulfuric Acid & Phos Acid Expansion
points: During FY26, commissioned Sulfuric Acid plant at Paradeep (0.5 million ton capacity) and at Mangalore (0.1 million ton capacity), increasing company-level Sulfuric Acid capacity by 0.6 million tons annually, a 45% increase of total capacity.
Benefit of incremental Sulfuric Acid capacity commissioned this year will be available in FY27 and will aid in improving quality of earnings further.
Plan to double Phos Acid capacity from 0.5 million tons to 1 million tons is on track; endeavor is to make all sites 100% backward integrated in phosphoric acid.
Phase-I of Phos Acid expansion (0.5 to 0.7 million tons) at Paradeep is underway, expected to be commissioned by FY27.

Next Sulfuric Acid project (proposed 3,000 tons per day) is at the stage where commercial offers are coming in; company expects to take a decision within the current quarter; company is in the vendor finalization stage, quotes received, separate team working on it.
Phos Acid expansion will be coupled together with the new Sulfuric Acid project.
Paradeep is almost fully backward integrated; the 0.5 to 0.7 expansion should cover most of the other two units' Phos Acid requirement.
For Phos Acid, Mangalore is 100% backward integrated in Sulfuric Acid; for N20 product, ~10% import requirement remains.
Company commitment to CAPEX remains unchanged despite global challenges.

subsections.label: Goa Energy Efficiency Project
points: Goa plant energy efficiency project completed in Q4FY26; shutdown taken from February, completed in last week of April.
Improved energy benefits (moving from 6.4 to 6.1 Gcal) have started accruing.
At current gas price scenario, this will translate to around INR 1,000 to INR 1,200 per ton of urea at EBITDA level.

subsections.label: Debottlenecking & Other Capacity
points: Debottlenecking of granulation capacity at Odisha (Paradeep) plant of roughly 2 lakh tons expected to come in FY27, with incremental volumes expected in H2.

Total debottlenecking across sites expected to contribute about 0.3 million tons, with 0.2 million tons targeted this year and the remaining 0.1 million tons targeted for FY28; partly from Mangalore, with both units contributing some growth.
All other major CAPEX projects are likely to be completed by FY28 and FY29.

subsections.label: Capacity Utilization
points: Production volumes achieved almost 100% capacity utilization of existing capacities in FY26, reflecting continued manufacturing excellence.
Currently all three plants running at around 80% (not above 90%), primarily due to raw material constraints (ammonia and Sulfuric Acid/Sulfur related).

subsections.label: Distribution & Digital Outreach
points: Through expanded distribution and digital outreach, company now engages with over 15 million farmers across 18 states, supported by more than a lakh retailers and 6,800 dealers, and a strong on-the-ground advisory network.

subsections.label: Raw Material Sourcing & Middle East Disruption
points: Middle East contributes significantly to raw materials, particularly ammonia and sulfur — almost 70-75%, with most shipments across the Strait of Hormuz.

Industry stock remains balanced at this point; industry is making concentrated efforts, and an empowered committee comprising government and industry officials is working in close coordination to ensure fertilizer production and raw material sourcing planning.
Sulfur prices remain under stress for last few months; expectation that de-escalation of Hormuz situation would remove major impact, but internationally remains under stress currently.

Company sources 100% of Sulfur from MRPL Mangalore via the recently commissioned plant (300 tons planned, now running at ~400 tons); ~20-30% of Paradeep's Sulfur requirement comes from IOC Paradeep; domestically company is poised toward a comfort position, though internationally remains under stress.

Ammonia sourcing has largely diversified away from the Strait of Hormuz to the East Coast/Southeast Asian countries; Sulfur remains a critical resource that continues to be sourced partly through the Strait of Hormuz.
One of the vessels secured for Sulfur came via the Strait of Hormuz.
Company is also earnestly sourcing Sulfur domestically to partially supplement supply; an industry consortium is working on securing Sulfur and ammonia in a transparent way.
Company is now focusing on low-Sulfur-grade products (e.g., increasing DAP) to minimize Sulfur requirement.
Q1FY27 raw material requirement is largely covered; Q2 situation is still unfolding and difficult to give a direct answer beyond Q1.
Industry actively engaging with government almost daily (discussions with Secretary of Fertilizers and MDs of major companies) particularly for Q2 visibility.

subsections.label: Gas Cost Pass-Through
points: Gas cost for the quarter was around $14/MMBTU, currently moved up to around $18-19/MMBTU due to supply disturbance.
Entire urea energy cost is a pass-through; increase in gas cost will be passed through and will not impact urea bottom line.

subsections.label: Procurement Consortium
points: Government has structured industry-consortium buying (via India Potash Ltd, IPL) on behalf of five-six large phosphate companies, including PPL, to discover transparent L1 prices instead of individual spot positions.
Company has only picked up quantity at L1 prices from the two recent IPL tenders.

Rationale: important that farmers get phosphates and nitrogen for the cropping season, and maintaining a certain strategic inventory as a country strengthens bargaining position for subsequent season.

subsections.label: Market Leadership
points: Company retains price leadership in NPK market; NPK price increase taken.
Company is among top two-three companies in NPK volumes.
Management confident of maintaining market leadership; good visibility on Kharif; expects clarity on Rabi supply chain within two to three months.
No concern on market leadership except for very unacceptable situations where the value chain is impacted.

subsections.label: Geopolitical / Supply Risk
points: Middle East situation and disruption across the Strait of Hormuz has caused a spurt in key raw materials (ammonia and sulfur) prices and availability concerns, given Middle East's 70-75% contribution to these raw materials.

INR depreciation and global uncertainty/volatility in key raw material availability and pricing cited as headwinds despite which company delivered consistent performance through operational agility, integrated operations, and supply chain sourcing efficiencies.
Sulfur remains a critical resource of concern; ammonia sourcing has been diversified away from Hormuz but Sulfur continues to be partly routed via Hormuz.
Two 'anxieties' flagged for production: ammonia side and Sulfur/Sulfuric Acid side.
Elevated global raw material prices (exceptionally high urea and DAP prices) flagged as an unusual/exceptional situation.

Potential risk of subsidy timing/delay was raised by an analyst, but management does not see subsidy being delayed given no custom duty on ammonia/Sulfur, adequate budget support, and ongoing government engagement.

subsections.label: Outlook Commentary
points: Management remains optimistic about fertilizer demand, continued government trust on soil health, and rising shift towards balanced and specialized nutrient applications.

Company remains in a challenging time amidst the Middle East situation with spurt in key raw material (ammonia, sulfur) prices; industry stock remains balanced and an empowered committee of government and industry officials is coordinating on production/sourcing planning.

Management unwilling to give a specific EBITDA per ton number for FY27 given global situation uncertainty, but expects backward integration benefits (Phos Acid, Sulfuric Acid) to flow into FY27 and to increase the spread over time.
Management declined to give FY27 revenue guidance, preferring to 'let things settle' before committing.
Company's endeavor is to secure raw materials to produce; if achieved, growth is expected.

Management stated EBITDA percentage margin is not the right metric for the industry — EBITDA per ton is the preferred metric, but a specific FY27 number could not be given at this time given Middle East situation.

No specific production guidance given beyond Q1 due to uncertainty; production volume expected to remain steady to a large extent (70-80% in Q1); slight shift away from ammonia-intensive and sulfur-intensive products depending on policy clarity.
Achieved S&P Global ESG score of 76, ranked in top 2% of global chemical sector during FY26.

The delta between imported Sulfur/Sulfuric acid input and indigenous Sulfuric acid is normally around INR 3,000, but at current level it will be reduced to around INR 1,500-2,000 delta.
All other major CAPEXs, as said earlier, is likely to be done by FY28 and FY29.

guidance_ledger.metric: Goa urea production capacity (with supportive policy)
guidance_ledger.statement: With the new change in policy, Goa can do up to 4.5 lakh tons of urea (vs 4 lakh tons currently).
If there is a supportive policy, MCFL can still produce more than 4 lakh tons; overall RAC is around 4 lakhs, with supportive policy can go up to 4.4-4.5 lakh tons.
We don't see any reason for subsidy delay given no custom duty on ammonia/Sulfur, Kharif stock build-up and consumption happening, and subsidy is adequately budgeted with government budget support.

risk_register.note: Middle East contributes 70-75% of ammonia and sulfur raw materials, most shipments via Strait of Hormuz; industry stock remains balanced but under close government-industry coordination.

risk_register.risk: Elevated Ammonia prices
risk_register.note: Ammonia sourcing diversified from Strait of Hormuz to East Coast/Southeast Asia, but prices remain elevated globally.

risk_register.note: Cited as a headwind alongside raw material volatility despite which company delivered consistent performance.

risk_register.note: All three plants currently running at around 80% (not above 90%) primarily due to raw material constraints (ammonia and sulfur/Sulfuric Acid intensive products).

risk_register.risk: Uncertainty on Q2FY27 raw material coverage/visibility
risk_register.note: Q1FY27 largely covered but Q2 situation still unfolding; industry engaging in near-daily discussions with government (Secretary of Fertilizers, MDs of major companies) for clarity.

risk_register.risk: Subsidy timing/delay risk
risk_register.note: Analyst raised concern of potential subsidy delay at elevated raw material prices; management does not foresee delay given no custom duty, adequate budget support and government engagement.

themes.note: Ammonia and sulfur (70-75% from Middle East) sourcing and pricing under stress due to Strait of Hormuz situation; industry-government coordination ongoing.

themes.note: NPK (incl. TSP) volumes grew 22% to 24.64 lakh tons, outpacing industry which degrew, driven by balanced nutrition strategy and market leadership.

themes.label: Working capital / subsidy receivable buildup
themes.note: Negative operating cash flow (~INR -1,000 crores) and elevated gross debt (INR 6,800 crores) driven by inventory build-up and subsidy receivables, expected to unwind in Q1FY27.

themes.label: Government policy support & subsidy adequacy
themes.note: Government engaging closely with industry on raw material sourcing; no custom duty on ammonia/sulfur and adequately budgeted subsidy reduce delay risk.

themes.label: Capacity utilization amid raw material constraints
themes.note: Plants running at ~80% currently due to ammonia and sulfur constraints versus near-100% utilization achieved in FY26.

key_takeaways: In the Financial Year 2026, revenue from operation increased by 29% Y-o-Y to INR 21,826 crores. EBITDA rose up by 33% to INR 2,259 crores. Profit before tax increased by 46% year-over-year to INR 1,328 crores. And the profit after tax stood at INR 1,000 crores, up by 52%.
For the quarter-ended March, the company reported total revenue of INR 4,702 crores with an EBITDA of INR 484 crores with the PBT stood at INR 202 crores and the profit after tax at INR 161 crores.

Production volumes grew by 8% year-over-year and it stood at 36.66 lakh metric tons, achieving almost 100% capacity utilization of our existing capacities, reflecting our continued endeavor for manufacturing excellence.
Sales volume rose up to 42.1 lakh metric tons with a 10% Y-o-Y. Growth was led by strong performance in value-added NPK grades. NPK as a category, including TSP, grew by 22% to 24.64 lakh tons.

During the year, we commissioned our Sulfuric Acid plant at Paradeep, half a million ton capacity, and at Mangalore, 0.1-million-ton capacity, thereby increasing our Sulfuric Acid capacity at company level by 0.6 million tons annually, an increase of 45% of the total capacity.
Our plan to double the Phos Acid capacity from 0.5 million ton to 1 million tons is on track, and directionally, we endeavor to make all our sites 100% backward integrated in phosphoric acid.
Sustainability remains core to our operations and during the year, we achieved S&P Global ESG score of 76 and ranked top 2% in the global chemical sector.

However, we remain in the challenging time amidst the Middle East situation, and we have seen spurt in key raw materials, particularly ammonia and sulfur... which is almost like 70%-75%, and most of the shipments across the Strait of Hormuz.
pressing_questions: What could be the medium-term EBITDA per ton trajectory as the company deepens backward integration and shifts toward higher-margin NPK, given FY26 EBITDA per ton was around INR 5,100-5,300?
How is raw material availability placed for Q1 and Q2 FY27, and how much of requirement has been bought pre-war vs. at current higher prices?
Could operating cash flow / subsidy receivable timing be a recurring issue leading to increased short-term working capital borrowing?
Is there a possibility that fertilizer subsidies could get delayed given elevated raw material prices and import duty related steps?
What is the Q3 vs Q4 production volume split for the MCFL urea plant (management declined to share on the call and said they would follow up separately)?

MANYAVAR.about: Vedant Fashions Limited caters to the Indian celebration wear market with a diverse portfolio of brands. The company offers its customers a one-stop destination for every celebratory occasion and the largest men's Indian wedding and celebration wear by revenue.VFL commands a dominant position in conventionally unorganized market segment.[1]

quarters.summary: Management remains focused and confident in the core strengths of the business — brand equity, operational efficiency, customer experience, marketing, replenishment systems, store network and back-end infrastructure — positioning the company for sustained long-term growth; H2 FY27 (especially Nov-March) is expected to be strong, with confidence in the Q3 product lineup and marketing investments, while Sept-Oct is expected to be relatively weaker due to a postponed Navratri.

subsections.label: Gross margin trend
points: Q1 FY27 gross margin of 65.7% is an improvement over Q4 FY26's 65%.

Compared to Q1 FY26, GST rate revision (implemented end of Q3 FY26/September) played a role in the year-on-year gross margin decline, as Q1 FY27 is not yet part of the GST base — GST base effect starts from Q3 onward.
On a peer-on-peer (sequential quarter) basis, gross margin has improved.

subsections.label: Primary vs secondary sales differential
points: Primary sales growth is around 3%-7% while secondary sales growth is around 3%-3.5%, despite Q1 being affected by Adhik mass for around 30 days.
The company has a complete auto-replenishment mechanism where replenishment happens based on front-end requirement, causing quarterly primary/secondary growth to vary.
Management recommends reviewing both parameters at a full financial year level, as over a full year primary and secondary revenue growth generally trend in a similar direction.

subsections.label: Premiumization and ASP
points: Premium brand Twamev outperformed the company average in overall growth.
Q1 SSG was a mix of volume and price, broadly half and half.

Ambition for ASP growth in the year is slightly higher than current levels, but planning for that typically plays out later in Q2, Q3 and Q4; management expects to start achieving higher ASP growth from mid-Q2 onward.

subsections.label: Wedding calendar outlook
points: This financial year, Navratri is slightly postponed due to Adhik mass versus an early Navratri last year — the key year-on-year change.
January this year has wedding dates versus none last year, providing a slight benefit.
November to March is expected to be a fantastic period; October this year may be slightly weaker than last year; September-October period may be more difficult.
Broadly, the wedding calendar is in line year-on-year and might be slightly stronger overall.

subsections.label: MBO + SIS vertical
points: Internally, MBO plus SIS is now defined and tracked as a separate vertical with different benchmarks and growth alignment than EBO.
A new leadership team has been built to boost this vertical.
EBO stores average around 3,000 sq ft while SIS stores are a few hundred sq ft, justifying the split.
Q2 is the biggest season for the MBO/SIS vertical; management is confident of the numbers to be achieved.
Majority of MBO/SIS bookings for Q2 are already completed with very good response seen in dealer meets.

subsections.label: Mohey brand
points: Mohey has been performing much better than the last couple of years compared to the company average.
The company has doubled down on non-bridal categories such as stitched suits, sarees, and crop-top lehengas, seeing a large part of growth in Mohey coming from these categories.
Plans include continuing to double down on these categories and being more aggressive with digital marketing for these newer categories to accelerate the brand.

subsections.label: Diwas brand
points: Good trends seen from the market even though this does not yet reflect in Q1 numbers.
Majority of MBO/SIS bookings for Q2 for Diwas are completed with very good response in dealer meets, driven by price points and target audience.
E-commerce contracts and deals cracked with Myntra, Amazon, Blinkit, Zepto for Diwas.
Management describes being more prepared than ever from an online channel perspective this year in terms of inventory planning at channel warehouses.
High excitement for Diwas numbers this year given the preplanning of supply chain for Q3.

subsections.label: International business
points: Company is strong primarily in two international markets: UAE and North America.
Both markets faced tremendous pressure in the last couple of months — UAE due to war-related issues and challenges, North America due to tariffs.
Management hopes these challenges will be overcome and the company can return to growth in this vertical.

subsections.label: VFL Brahma launch
points: Company launched VFL Brahma, a direct connector of the entire company's data to its AI brain, aimed at fostering a further culture of speed and efficiency.

subsections.label: Store closures - reasons
points: Three primary types of closures: (1) market has shifted to a newer part of town where the company has already opened a new store, making the older store's continued operation or renovation unviable given no expected growth in that older market; (2) a larger store opened in a bigger neighboring town within a Tier 3 cluster draws customers away from smaller stores in that cluster; (3) the smallest category — stores that never performed well from day one due to a new-store-opening mistake.

Closures were more strategic and front-loaded into Q1 this year because Q2 is the off-season for the company; management aimed to close larger stores within Q1 to avoid bearing rentals into Q2, while being more aggressive on openings towards H2 when majority of business occurs.
Management explicitly stated it has never faced a closure reason attributable to competition.

subsections.label: Store opening and rationalization strategy
points: Core goal for the financial year is to deliver a very good SSG; company also has a good pipeline for gross openings.
Plan is for good SSG delivery in H2 to be followed by good growth in store count.
Typical tail (openings) in a financial year is 3%-4%, expected to hold this year too.
As rental pressure eases over time, the company plans to be more aggressive with gross openings.
Majority of this year's gross openings will only start at the end of Q2 and early Q3.

subsections.label: New store productivity
points: Situation on new-store productivity versus closed stores remains largely similar to what was mentioned in the last earnings call, with not much change since majority of last year's gross openings were already commented on then.
Management will comment on newer store trends once majority of this year's gross openings begin (end of Q2/early Q3).

subsections.label: Franchisee economics
points: Required revenue per sq ft for healthy franchisee ROI depends on the tier of city: close to INR 7,000/sq ft in Tier 3, INR 8,500/sq ft in Tier 2, and INR 10,000-10,500/sq ft in Tier 1, against franchisee capex of INR 2,100-2,150/sq ft in Tier 2/3 and closer to INR 2,500/sq ft in Tier 1.

Franchisees have made great ROI over recent years and continue to make good ROI currently; there is no pressure of the sort suggested, and franchisee economics has never been a concern even with new store openings.

subsections.label: Competitive landscape / industry store count
points: Players who entered the industry 3-4 years ago are starting to close stores, while newer players are adding stores; net-net, the industry's total store count was not increasing.
Internal research across 8 top states shows the number of stores has started to come down in these states.
Stores closing down among other players are also often very large stores.

Dead stock is described as extremely painful in the celebration-wear industry, and once that pain hits after 2-3 years of operating, it's difficult to recover — a dynamic increasingly understood by newer entrants, driving their closures.
Review shows hardly any competing players achieving decent revenue per square foot, making it difficult for regional/local players to sustain.
Too early to conclude whether the overall market is shrinking, since store closures among competitors are a recent development and those stores were not doing very high revenues in the first place.

It is too early to confirm whether the company is seeing a growth benefit in regions where competition has exited; stores where competition opened nearby had previously shown a better delta than other stores; management wants another 2-3 quarters before drawing conclusions.

subsections.label: Auto replenishment and inventory
points: Company operates a complete auto-replenishment mechanism based on front-end requirement, which can cause primary and secondary sales growth to diverge at a quarterly level.
Inventory days stood at 34 days on a TTM basis (June 2026).
Preplanning of supply chain has been done for Q3, particularly supporting the Diwas brand's online and e-commerce channel inventory readiness.

subsections.label: Marketing campaigns
points: Mega campaign 'Made for Each Other' featuring Rashmika Mandanna and Vijay Deverakonda became one of India's most liked campaigns and a blockbuster hit with over 1 billion views, amplifying brand visibility and engagement for Manyavar and Mohey.
Twamev advanced its 'Truly You' proposition through influencer-led narratives with celebrities such as Nupur Sanon and Salim Merchant visiting Twamev stores to explore the new luxury collection.
Diwas executed targeted digital and social media initiatives through summer and monsoon season, broadening reach and engagement across marketplaces.

The Rashmika/Vijay campaign's monetization strategy was to maximize eyeballs on social media to establish the brand as the trendiest Indian fashion brand and drive top-of-mind relevance, converting into store footfall.
Campaigns of this scale are expected to deliver brand recall benefits over 5-6 years, not just in the immediate next quarter; benefit is expected to play out over the next 3-5 years.

Strategy shift going forward: from top-of-mind awareness campaigns to more consideration and conversion-led, highly relevant social-media-driven campaigns focused on product and 'why Manyavar', capitalizing on the recall already built.

subsections.label: Customer retention
points: Year-on-year growth seen in overall retention numbers.
A separate internal task force has been set up to drive repeat business, which is an increasingly large part of the business.
Management has further plans to announce (likely materializing within the month) to improve retention/repeat-purchase metrics, to be detailed in the next earnings call.
Customer database size stands at nearly 90 lakh customers, as referenced from last quarter.

subsections.label: Management confidence / outlook drivers
points: Confidence for H2 driven by product lineup ready for Q3, marketing investment plans for Q3, and initiatives across marketing, product, supply chain and technology fronts undertaken in Q1/Q2 that are expected to reflect in growth during Q3.

A recent tour across multiple Indian cities and stores reaffirmed management's view of the company's competitive advantage over industry peers in product, store experience, location and pricing combined.

subsections.label: International market pressures
points: UAE market has faced tremendous pressure due to war-related issues and challenges in recent months.
North America market has faced challenges due to tariffs in recent months.

subsections.label: Seasonal calendar risk
points: Navratri is postponed this year due to Adhik mass, making September-October comparatively weaker/more difficult versus last year.

subsections.label: Industry structural risk (competition)
points: Dead stock is extremely painful in the celebration-wear industry and difficult to liquidate at a discount, a risk factor that has driven newer entrants who underestimated this to eventually close stores after 2-3 years.

subsections.label: Revenue growth composition
points: Majority of growth for the year is expected to come from SSSG, with additional positive impact from productivity delta between new stores and closed stores, plus net store openings.
Aggressive targets set for MBO, SIS and e-commerce channels are expected to provide a decent bump to total revenue.
Overall, management remains optimistic about achieving decent growth in these other channels given new senior leadership for those teams.

subsections.label: SSG expectation
points: A high single-digit SSG for the balance 9 months of FY27 was characterized by management as a fair understanding of how the business is being viewed, with new store openings to follow once SSG improves.
Management confirmed expectation of a net positive financial year despite challenges.

guidance_ledger.statement: A high single-digit SSG for the balance of 9 months of FY27 is described as a fair understanding of how management views the business, prior to new store openings resuming.
Despite closures and challenges, the company will still be looking at a net positive financial year.

Typical opening tail of 3%-4% in a financial year, which will hold this year; majority of gross openings will start at end of Q2/early Q3; as rental pressure eases, company will be more aggressive on gross openings; good SSG delivery in H2 to be followed by growth in stores.
November to March is expected to be a fantastic period; broadly the wedding calendar is in line year-on-year and might be slightly stronger.
October this year might be slightly weaker than last year, and the September-October period might be slightly more difficult due to postponed Navratri.

Ambition for ASP growth in the year is slightly higher than current run-rate; company will start achieving these gains from somewhere between mid of Q2 as merchandising planning plays out in later parts of Q2, Q3 and Q4.

quarters.summary: Vedant Fashions closed FY26 with retail sales crossing INR 2,008 crores (up 6.1%) and Q4 retail sales up 7.8% with SSG of 4.6%; management remains focused on driving SSG via ASP improvement, retention initiatives and AI-led efficiency, while store network expansion stays disciplined with net additions expected to normalize only from FY27 as the company prioritizes retail quality over aggressive footprint growth. Cost inflation (fabric, ~50-150 bps impact) and GST-related base effects are expected to normalize going into FY27, and management expects to firm up capital allocation policy by the next earnings call.

subsections.label: Margin drivers
points: Gross margin contraction of ~150 bps during FY26 attributed majorly to the GST aspect (revised GST rates rolled out September 2025), which impacted revenue, gross margin, and PAT.
Blended GST pre-change was approximately 10%, which has now increased slightly, creating a lasting gap between consumer sales and reported revenue.
Margin also depends on mix of store types (18% vs 29.5% plus GST models), though this factor plays a smaller role than the GST change itself.

Fabric cost inflation (linked to the war) expected to add 50-150 bps to overall cost on a INR100 product basis (fabric is INR8-10 of COGS on a INR100 MRP product), but management expects to manage this well over time; majority of orders for current SKUs already placed at existing prices, so new fabric price impact should be limited to 10-15 bps.

subsections.label: Other expenses
points: Other expenses declined ~7% in Q4 FY26 versus Q4 FY25 due to efficiency gains in inventory management leading to lower job expenses, and marketing costs being lower specifically in Q4 (though higher for the full year versus last year).

subsections.label: Capital allocation
points: Historically the company has paid out about 50% of profits as dividends since IPO.
Capital allocation policy is being actively discussed internally; management expects to have a concrete answer by the next earnings call.
Company has cash on books to explore acquisitions but nothing currently in the pipeline; acquisition cost for existing small regional players seen as higher than cost of organic store openings.

subsections.label: Demand drivers
points: Footfalls improved by low single digits in Q4 FY26 - first such increase after many quarters.
Conversions remained stable at already high levels, helped by quick merchandising cycles (~2.5x designs versus last financial year) amid escalating competitive intensity.
Average basket size improved ~1.5% in Q4, aiding volumes.
ASPs had not moved as quickly as historically due to pressure over the last 2 years; company plans to focus on improving ASPs going forward to aid SSG.

ASP improvement will come from category mix upgradation (cross-selling Manyavar consumers into Twamev/Mohey, which have higher ASP than Manyavar) and merchandising collection upgrades (e.g., moving core kurtas from INR4,000 to INR4,500 bracket) rather than price hikes on existing products.

Wedding date calendar dynamics: May FY27 impacted by Adhik Maas; June/July expected better as July has wedding dates versus none last year; H2 comparison affected by early Navratri in September last year versus normalized October Navratri this year - no major structural wedding-date challenge overall.

March FY26 was a standout month driving majority of quarter's growth; April continued decently; consumer sentiment turned neutral again after geopolitical conflict (war) started in late Feb/early March 2026.

subsections.label: Brand mix & revenue per sq ft
points: From a revenue per square feet perspective, Twamev EBOs perform slightly better than Manyavar EBOs, and Mohey slightly lower than Manyavar, though broadly all are on similar lines.

Any Manyavar store where Mohey could be added has already been converted; going forward, opportunity lies in identifying high revenue-per-sq-ft Manyavar stores where a bigger store format could add Mohey - assessed on a quarterly basis.

Twamev strategy remains to sign the best stores in top Indian markets (target originally 30 stores) before expanding further; company is actively signing the next set of 5-6 Twamev stores, though management would not confirm the number 30 as a firm target.
Twamev store openings are staggered due to build-to-suit property structures with 18-20 month lag between signing and opening; some Twamev openings could extend into first two quarters of FY28/FY29.

Diwas (online-focused brand) plans to pilot small-format (~1,000 sq ft) Manyavar-branded kurta stores focused on kurtas and jackets in high-throughput neighborhoods (e.g., Bangalore) - not planned for full-scale rollout this financial year, only a pilot/concept.

subsections.label: Retail sales vs net sales gap
points: Gap between retail (customer) sales and net sales (reported revenue) increased to 29% in FY26 versus FY25, mainly due to the GST rate revision from September 2025; reported revenue equals consumer sales minus GST component and franchisee margin.

Growth rates in primary sales and secondary sales generally move in the same direction each year, but this year showed a 2%-3% gap mainly due to GST; this is expected to normalize from the upcoming financial year (FY27).
The GST-driven gap between retail and net sales is expected to persist structurally at current elevated levels even as growth trends re-align.

subsections.label: Consumer retention initiative
points: Company has ~90 lakh consumers in its database; a major FY27 initiative is to increase engagement/repeat purchase ('call back') from this existing consumer base - described as a largely untapped, greenfield revenue opportunity since the company has not historically focused on retention.

subsections.label: Network expansion & rationalization
points: Company adopted a focused, disciplined approach to network expansion during FY26, prioritizing strategic, sustainable store openings while rationalizing underperforming locations, resulting in a small net addition of ~4,200 sq ft to retail area for the year despite gross addition of ~1 lakh sq ft.
Company successfully expanded Twamev brand through a new EBO during the year.
Average revenue per sq ft of new stores opened is ~85% better than the average revenue per sq ft of stores closed in FY26.

About 5%-6% of current retail area falls in an underperforming category management is not satisfied with, versus a normal industry closure rate of 2%-3% per year; management expects to again close 5%-6% of retail area in FY27 while still targeting net positive sq ft growth.

Company plans for gross store openings to remain stable in the coming financial years while some consolidation continues; the quality of new stores opened will be much better than the quality of stores closed, so overall retail quality should improve.
Management expects net additions/openings to start normalizing by next financial year (FY27) as SSG-focused strategy matures.
New stores tend to be larger, allowing many of them to carry the Mohey brand alongside Manyavar, contributing to better average ASP in new stores.

subsections.label: Regional performance
points: In Q4 FY26, all regions performed decently well overall, with some pockets performing slightly better than others; no major region-wise divergence highlighted beyond this.

subsections.label: New market expansion challenges
points: Company sees opportunity in 'new India' cities/towns (e.g., a city like Bhopal) for large-format stores, but rental levels in these markets are running 1.3x-1.4x above what the company expects to be sustainable.

Company continues to invest resources in identifying stores at rental levels sustainable for the next 12-15 years, even in metros - example cited: no Manyavar store in South Bombay beyond Lower Parel, with potential for 2 more stores there once high-visibility properties become available (dependent on existing tenants vacating).

No challenges related to wedding dates or franchisee investment willingness were identified; nearly all stores are signed directly by the company itself, so franchisee-related store commitment issues have not occurred.

subsections.label: Multi-brand & online channels
points: Plans to further improve business through other channels such as multi-brand outlets (SIS format) and online segments, especially with Diwas starting to scale up.

No quick-commerce partners (e.g., Zilo, Blinkit) are currently willing to use Manyavar store inventory for fulfillment - they require their own warehoused inventory; company would need to launch its own quick-commerce service/app and use stores as dark hubs if it wants to pursue this model.

subsections.label: Inventory efficiency
points: Company has been bringing efficiency into inventory management, which contributed to lower job expenses and a decline in other expenses in Q4 FY26.

subsections.label: Marketing initiatives
points: Executed wide-ranging marketing across multiple brands and channels integrating digital and traditional platforms to elevate brand visibility and consumer engagement.

Launched landmark 'Made for Each Other' campaign featuring Rashmika Mandanna and Vijay Deverakonda, conceptualized as a musical rom-com by composer Amit Trivedi; became the most-liked organic branded collaboration on Instagram in India; one of the fastest campaign turnarounds ever, from celebrity confirmation to production in 6 days.

Launched 'Manyavar Shaadi Show', a 6-episode YouTube podcast hosted by Karan Johar featuring Kriti Kharbanda, Pulkit Samrat, the Mohan Sisters, Vishal Punjabi and industry experts, exploring modern Indian wedding planning; garnered strong viewership and positive audience response.
Manyavar social media campaign featuring cricketer Rinku Singh amplified brand visibility, complemented by successful launch of the Aranya Collection.

Mohey ran the 'Mohey Rang Do' campaign; Twamev advanced its 'Truly You' proposition via fresh collection launches, influencer narratives and experiential activations; Mebaz ran the 'Celebrations Begin with Mebaz' campaign; Diwas executed targeted digital/social initiatives during festive windows to broaden reach on marketplaces.

Management notes marketing mix modelling has historically given inconclusive results for attributing SSG to specific campaign types; large milestone campaigns (like Vijay-Rashmika, or Virat-Anushka in 2017) are viewed as having multi-year (5-6 year) top-of-mind impact, while the wedding podcast targets consumers researching weddings online, and significant investment is made in search keywords (e.g., sherwani, Indo-Western searches) to drive store traffic.

subsections.label: Competitive intensity
points: Competitive intensity in the industry has escalated over the past couple of years but company tracks competition closely across markets.

In the last 7-8 months, players that entered in 2022 have started closing down, while players that entered in the last 1-2 years have continued opening stores pan-India; net-net, industry saw net store closures with no material net new openings.

Regional competitors (excluding larger national groups, whose dynamics differ) typically follow a 4-year cycle: exciting first year post new-store investment, heavier marketing/merchandising investment in year 2 when sales disappoint, heavy discounting/liquidation in year 3, and store closure in year 4 - a natural cycle for regional players lacking strong equity backing.

subsections.label: Overseas wedding/travel dynamics
points: Management does not expect government discouragement of foreign travel to materially affect business either way, since families doing destination/overseas weddings are typically premium and not the company's core target audience; conversely, weddings held in India that invite foreign guests represent a strong opportunity given Manyavar's quick turnaround capability.

subsections.label: M&A stance
points: Company tracks every company in the wedding/celebration wear space but has nothing currently in the acquisition pipeline or actively being explored.

Company has cash on its books to pursue acquisitions and cited its track record of turning around acquired businesses (e.g., Mebaz) as a strength, but notes no acquisition targets currently exist at meaningful scale in the sector - cost of acquiring small regional players would exceed the cost of organically opening new stores in the same areas.

subsections.label: AI / technology-led initiatives
points: Company is making significant investment in AI to enable agentic AI across departments (product, marketing, supply chain) so that different functions' AI agents can communicate and improve overall efficiency.

Example given: for Google Search ad campaigns with ~20,000 line items, historically only the top 20 line items were reviewed by senior management and the next 200 by middle management, with only the top 600-700 items ever analysed by humans; the company has now built an AI system that analyses and optimizes all 20,000 keywords autonomously.

Easy AI use cases have already been deployed; more complex use cases requiring integration with larger systems are still in progress; company is training every team member to understand and deploy AI agents.

subsections.label: Macro & geopolitical
points: A geopolitical conflict ('war') that started in late February/early March 2026 caused consumer sentiment to turn from positive back to more neutral, though not to a large extent.
Government discouragement of foreign travel was raised as a potential factor but management does not see it materially impacting the target customer segment.

subsections.label: Cost inflation
points: Fabric and other input cost inflation linked to the war is expected to add roughly 50-150 basis points to overall product cost (e.g., INR1-1.5 impact on a INR100 MRP product where fabric is typically INR8-10 of cost), though management believes this will be manageable over time and current-season orders are largely already booked at existing prices, limiting near-term margin impact to about 10-15 bps.

GST rate revision (effective September 2025) has been the majority driver of the gap between retail/customer sales and reported net sales/revenue, and of gross margin contraction (~150 bps) during FY26; this GST-related impact is expected to normalize from FY27.

subsections.label: Real estate/rental costs
points: High real estate rental costs, especially in newer 'new India' markets, are cited as the primary constraint on store expansion (rather than franchisee willingness), as company seeks properties sustainable for 12-15 years at signed rental levels.

subsections.label: Competitive intensity
points: Escalated competitive intensity from both national and regional players over the past couple of years, though early signs suggest players that entered in 2022 are beginning to close down.

subsections.label: Outlook
points: No specific SSG guidance given for FY27; management states it is targeting everything within its control (footfalls via campaigns, conversion via tech initiatives, ASP improvement, basket size via training) to drive better SSG numbers.

Gross store openings to remain stable in coming financial years with continued but disciplined additions; some consolidation/closure will continue, but the quality of new stores will be much better than stores closed, improving overall retail quality; net additions expected to normalize/improve from FY27.
GST-driven gap between retail sales growth and net sales growth expected to normalize from the upcoming financial year (FY27), though the absolute gap level is expected to persist structurally.
Gross margin should not be materially impacted by fabric cost inflation beyond roughly 10-15 bps near-term, given most current-season orders are already booked at existing prices.
Capital allocation/dividend policy currently under internal review; management expects to communicate a concrete policy by the next earnings call.

Twamev EBO expansion to continue via signing the next 5-6 stores in top markets, but actual openings will be staggered over the next financial year and possibly into FY28/FY29 given 18-20 month build-to-suit lead times; management would not commit to the previously discussed 30-store target within the next 2.5 years.

Diwas to pilot a small-format Manyavar-branded kurta store (~1,000 sq ft) in high-throughput neighborhoods (e.g., Bangalore) this financial year, focused on kurtas and jackets; no full-scale physical rollout planned yet.

Key excitement areas for the year: (1) consumer retention/reactivation initiative targeting the ~90 lakh consumer database, (2) ASP improvement after being subdued for 2-3 years, and (3) AI/agentic AI investments across departments expected to materially improve efficiency.
