key_takeaways: Retail sales, that is, the sale of our customers, stood at approximately INR 561 crores, reflecting a growth of 7.8% over Q4 FY25 with SSG of approximately 4.6%.
FY26 marked an important milestone for the Company as retail sales of our customers crossed the INR 2,000 crores mark, reaching INR 2,008 crores and reflecting a growth of 6.1% over FY25.
As of March 2026, Vedant Fashions’ EBO network stands at about 1.79 million square feet, spanning across 669 stores in 252 cities and towns globally.

Revenue from operation during the quarter was around INR399 crores with a growth of 8.7% over Q4 of FY25. The Company continued to report industry-leading gross margin of 65% and healthy EBITDA margin of 45.6%.
The Company also reported strong PAT margin of around 28.6% and the profit after tax stood at around INR 114 crores with a growth of around 13% over Q4 of FY25.

The Company reported revenue from operation of around INR 1,436 crores with a growth of around 3.5%. The Company continued to report industry-leading gross margin of around 65.7%, along with healthy EBITDA margin of around 44.3%. The EBITDA during the period stood at around INR 636 crores.
The Company also reported healthy PAT margin of 26.2% and the profit after tax stood at around INR 376 crores.
During FY26, the Company reported strong cash conversion ratio of approx. 98%, which has been computed based upon operating cash flow to PAT, excluding finance income.
pressing_questions: Rahul Agarwal (Ikigai Asset Managers) asked on SSG momentum outlook for FY27 and new store opening plans, on input inflation/gross margin guidance, and on why the gap between retail sales and net sales has widened to 29% - management gave only directional, non-specific responses on SSG and margin guidance.

Harsh Shah (Bandhan Mutual Fund) asked what marker management would use to decide when to resume store expansion (e.g., 3-4 quarters of consistent mid-single-digit SSG) - management did not commit to a specific SSG threshold or timeline.
Rishi Mody (RDM Advisory) asked whether the Twamev store count would move from 8 to 30 within the next 2.5 years - management declined to confirm the number 30 as a target.
Harsh Shah asked about capital allocation/dividend policy for the cash balance - management said a concrete answer is not yet available but expected by the next earnings call.

METROPOLIS.about: Metropolis Healthcare Limited is one of the leading Indian diagnostics companies. The Company owns a chain of diagnostic centres across India, South Asia, Africa and the Middle East.

quarters.summary: Metropolis delivered a strong Q1 FY27 start, exceeding guidance with ~17% YoY revenue growth and 210bps EBITDA margin expansion, driven predominantly by volume growth (no price increase in 18 months). Management reiterated FY27 guidance of 14%-15% revenue growth (volume-led) and 100-150bps EBITDA margin improvement this year, targeting a 27%-28% EBITDA margin over this year and next, while continuing network expansion, Specialty/TruHealth mix improvement, tech/AI investment, and disciplined inorganic growth (Metropolis 3.0 strategy).

key_figures.label: Average margin for regular test portfolio (company level)

subsections.label: Margin drivers
points: EBITDA margin expansion driven by healthy volume-led operating leverage, disciplined cost management, and continued progress on productivity agenda.

Laboratory transformation program (standardizing testing platforms, consolidating vendors, increasing automation, improving procurement efficiencies) is a key contributor; benefits are at different stages of roll-out, with further gains expected as remaining platform transitions and automation initiatives go live in coming quarters.

Organic business delivered healthy margin expansion YoY and sequentially despite the relatively lower margin profile of Core Diagnostics and the impact of advancing annual employee increments from July to April this year.

subsections.label: Revenue growth composition
points: 17% revenue growth supported by 10% patient volume growth and 11% test volume growth, with the balance from richer mix and improved realizations.
No price increase over the last 18 months; last price increase was January 2025.
Only industry-wide price increase during the period was for CGHS tests, which benefited other players more than Metropolis since CGHS is a very small (~1%) part of Metropolis's business.

subsections.label: B2C performance
points: B2C delivered 18% revenue growth with balanced contribution from enhanced revenue across mature centers and ramp-up of centers added over the last year.
Growth was strong across own centers and Tier-2/Tier-3 markets, with rural centers delivering 36% revenue growth.
CLM-led customer engagement, local micro-marketing, strong brand pull, and increasing digital adoption contributed to patient acquisition.
Specialty revenue within B2C grew 21%, while TruHealth and value-added offerings (body vital checks, consults, ECG) supported higher revenue per patient.
B2C patient volume growth was 13.5% in Q1 FY27.

subsections.label: B2B performance
points: B2B grew 15%, led by deliberate focus on hospitals, clinicians, and high-quality organized institutions, prioritizing relationships where scientific capabilities, Specialty portfolio, service quality and nationwide network create a higher right to win.
Partner portal and digital enablement initiatives are improving visibility, service responsiveness and access to wider test menu for partners.
With presence in 750+ towns, targeting additional business from smaller laboratories and hospitals in these markets.
Q1 FY27 B2B growth figure of 15% now includes Core Diagnostics revenue in the denominator (unlike Q4 FY26's 15% which was organic-only, excluding Core).
Most B2B business is Specialty-driven, since B2B customers (smaller labs, hospitals, institutions) outsource specialized/Semi-Specialty tests they cannot perform in-house.
B2B patient volume growth was 6% in Q1 FY27.

subsections.label: North India / Core Diagnostics integration review
points: North India revenue grew 19% YoY, now 18% of overall revenue (up from single-digit before Core acquisition), supported by successful integration of Core Diagnostics, Scientific Pathology Agra, and DAPIC Dehradun; emerged as fastest-growing region.
First objective of Core acquisition (building genomics platform) has succeeded: genomics portfolio has doubled over the past year and is one of the fastest-growing segments within Specialty.
Second objective (strengthening North India brand via clinician/hospital relationships) achieved: North India revenue contribution rose to 18% from single-digit pre-acquisition.

Third objective (shareholder value via disciplined acquisitions): Core acquired at <2x revenue with plan to reach ~25% EBITDA margin in 3-4 years; based on FY27 expected EBITDA, effective acquisition multiple is ~10x EBITDA.

Core is in final leg of integration; focus shifting from integration to growth, leveraging Metropolis pan-India network to expand Core Super Specialty capabilities, drive higher test volumes, improve network utilization, and create operating leverage.
Agra and Dehradun acquisitions performing well, tracking ahead of revenue growth and EBITDA expectations.

Genomics and Core Super Specialty menu are complementary: genomics brings advanced testing/interpretation, Core adds deeper Super Specialty oncology portfolio and clinician relationships; Core test menu is being taken to existing clients, prescribing clinicians and service networks across India.
Core Diagnostics margins: high single-digit currently (~8%), with a 3-4 year target of ~25% EBITDA margin post-acquisition.
Core Diagnostics revenue is part of B2B segment; revenue per patient metric for B2B also applies to Core.

subsections.label: TruHealth / Specialty growth engines
points: TruHealth grew 22%, supported by integrated preventive healthcare offerings and targeted digital customer acquisition initiatives, and now contributes 18% of Q1 FY27 revenue.
Radiology integrated wellness packages grew >40%; premium TruHealth packages grew >50%, led by doctor consultations, body vital checkups and ECG-led extensions.

Specialty Diagnostics grew 17%, supported by increasing adoption of advanced testing, deeper clinician engagement, and cross-selling of Core Diagnostics, oncology and Super Specialty capabilities; Specialty now contributes 40% of revenue across a portfolio of 2,200+ tests.

TruHealth has two parts: consumers checking overall wellness proactively, and consumers up-selling from an illness test to a bigger wellness bundle; goal is to be a 'health partner' covering blood, vitals, basic radiology, cognitive/mental health assessment.

TruHealth 'Mind and Body' initiative includes basic radiology (X-ray, ECG, sonography); genomics not yet part of TruHealth as predictive genomics for wellness (vs illness) is not yet scientifically validated in India.
No specific individual package targets for TruHealth, but continued innovation and growth expected across multiple markets.

Currently majority of TruHealth/wellness activity is in Tier-1 and early Tier-2 towns; Tier-2 second half and Tier-3+ markets are starting to gain traction, providing headroom for further TruHealth build-out; sequence in new towns is Routine/Semi-Specialty first, then Specialty, then TruHealth.
TruHealth margins are largely in line with company-level margins; TruHealth ticket size is currently around INR 2,500.
36 new tests added in Q1 FY27, following 347 new tests added in FY26.

subsections.label: International business
points: International business continued to perform well, delivering healthy growth in both revenue and EBITDA.
Market leaders in two of the five countries of operation; ranks among top three players in all markets.

Business model similar to India, with specialized testing offshored to India reference laboratories, though African market operating environment differs; company has built deep market understanding and capabilities over the years.

subsections.label: Technology & digital transformation
points: Technology remains a strategic pillar of long-term growth; executing a company-wide automation and digital transformation program spanning labs, customer engagement, vendor consolidation, commercial operations, finance, procurement and support functions.
Strengthening data governance and ensuring DPDP-compliant handling of patient data with focus on privacy, security, and responsible use of information.
Within labs, automation and in-platform standardization are improving quality, throughput and turnaround times, particularly in oncology and Specialty Diagnostics.

Beyond laboratories, AI and automation are improving workflow efficiency, strengthening decision-making, enhancing customer engagement, improving inventory management, and simplifying back-office operations.

These initiatives are creating productivity gains and building a more scalable, data-led, efficient operating model across the organization, anchored in quality (EQAS score of 99%, report accuracy of 99.99%, accredited/benchmarked lab network).

subsections.label: Scientific differentiation
points: Every lab in the network is either accredited or benchmarked to recognized quality standards.

~30,000 specialist doctors across the country prescribe tests through Metropolis, and every leading hospital (individual and chain) in the country engages with Metropolis, reflecting depth of clinician trust built through scientific programs, educational initiatives and sustained engagement.

key_figures.label: New centers added per quarter (recent run-rate)
Ratio improvement per net center additions

subsections.label: Network expansion strategy
points: Network expansion is a key growth enabler; over the last two years, presence strengthened while deepening footprint within existing markets.
Expanding network is improving accessibility, driving patient acquisition, and increasing sample throughput across laboratory infrastructure.

Expansion strategy is data-driven rather than opportunistic: every new center is selected based on detailed market mapping including population density, healthcare infrastructure, competitive intensity, and ability to establish a strong market position.

Company is not further expanding beyond the current 750 towns; instead deepening presence in these towns, leveraging existing networks, logistics systems and collection centers, to avoid additional cost stress on margins.
Lab expansion agenda has been halted for the last five quarters, contributing to margin protection since new towns/labs are not adding further cost at this point.

Center rationalization occurs once every 12-18 months to remove low-productivity or quality-issue centers, or where partners exit; latest rationalization (300 centers) occurred after nearly two years and was executed without materially impacting revenue since those centers had very low productivity.
500-center expansion target for FY27 is a net number (i.e., after accounting for rationalization); >500 centers added in the trailing 12 months, including 300 centers added in Q1 FY27 alone.
Center-to-laboratory ratio improved from 1:21 a year ago to 1:24 currently.

Lab count has been coming down in the last two quarters, partly due to consolidation of overlapping labs post-Core acquisition; management sees little further opportunity to rationalize labs, so the center-to-lab ratio will rise mainly via center additions (targeting ~1:30 by year-end via ~500 net center additions, i.e. roughly 5 additional centers per lab).

subsections.label: Productivity initiatives
points: Improved productivity of existing network through focused operating initiatives: increasing throughput at high-potential centers, rationalizing underperforming locations, redeploying resources to more productive markets.
Volume growth reflected balanced contribution from healthy growth across mature centers and ramp-up of centers added over the last 12 months.
Continued investments in micro-marketing, deeper clinician engagement, expanded test menus, and targeted activation of newly launched centers are accelerating growth across existing and new markets.
New center maturation cycle (2-3 quarters to deliver numbers) has been running for 5-6 quarters and continues to give benefits; recent run-rate of new center additions has been 200-250 per quarter.

subsections.label: Lab-on-lease model
points: Metropolis runs a lab-on-lease model where it takes over a pathologist-run lab and brings in Metropolis systems, processes and people; this model has been running for many years (~10 years).
Over time, some lab-on-lease sites are acquired outright, while others continue under the lease model for a longer duration, depending on opportunity.
Management could not provide the exact number of labs currently under this model on the call and said it would follow up.

subsections.label: Industry structural growth drivers
points: Indian diagnostics industry entering a phase of sustained structural growth supported by three reinforcing shifts: (1) shift from unorganized to organized quality-led diagnostic providers as expectations on accuracy, consistency, testing capability and service standards rise; (2) healthcare ecosystem expanding beyond metros with new hospital capacity, rising OPD/IPD volumes, more specialists, and improving Tier-2/Tier-3 access, plus hospitals outsourcing more specialized/high-end testing to providers with strong quality systems and nationwide reach; (3) treatment pathways becoming more advanced (targeted therapies, biologics, biosimilars in oncology, neurology, autoimmune disorders) increasing need for precise diagnosis, patient stratification, biomarker-led treatment selection and monitoring, expanding molecular/genomic/immunological testing.

These shifts are broadening the addressable market for diagnostics and creating a structural opportunity in Specialty Testing, though this opportunity will not accrue evenly across the industry — Specialty Diagnostics requires years of investment in scientific expertise, quality systems, clinical credibility, specialist relationships and broad high-end test portfolio, creating meaningful entry barriers.

No third-party industry-level data exists on unorganized-to-organized share shift; anecdotal evidence from vendors and B2B customers suggests volume growth is slower at smaller/unorganized labs (buying less materials) versus faster growth at organized players, and some very small labs are shutting down; this is described as a slow, steady, non-catalytic consolidation trend, not a sudden shift from ~10-15% organized to 30%.

subsections.label: Competitive dynamics
points: No irrational competitive behavior observed; normal competitive intensity of the diagnostics industry (seen for 10-15 years) continues, with everyone jostling for market share.

Of ~3 lakh labs across the country, only ~10% are run by MD pathologists (90% run by technicians); technician labs typically serve GP referrals for common illnesses and outsource Semi-Specialized tests, while MD pathologist labs/hospitals/nursing homes treat more complex diseases and outsource more Specialty tests — Metropolis targets B2B customers with ability to outsource specialized tests.

Many new entrants pursue volume at high servicing cost and fail to achieve profitability, often plateauing around INR 50-75 crores/year revenue before realizing scaling profitably is harder than expected; differentiation comes from unit economics and quality of business, not just distribution/sample pickup.
Scaling profitably requires the right domain expertise, scale opportunities, and ability to build doctor trust that generates full-price patients and Specialty tests.

subsections.label: GLP-1 / diabetic industry trend
points: Tests required for pre-screening/pre-prescription GLP-1 are fairly common tests; while packages have been created for pre-GLP testing, doctors often write their own prescriptions rather than only the packages, making it difficult to isolate GLP-specific contribution to organic growth.
Considered still early days as GLP-1 adoption (injections/drugs) is expected to play out over a longer period.

key_figures.label: Core Diagnostics margin target post-acquisition integration

subsections.label: Metropolis 3.0 strategy — FY27 execution priorities
points: 1. Accelerating network expansion: continue expanding network to improve accessibility, especially Tier-2/Tier-3 towns, and drive higher sample volumes through recently commissioned labs, resulting in better capacity utilization, operating leverage and profitable growth; targeting ~400-500 new centers in Tier-2/Tier-3 towns this year.

2. Strengthening Specialty Diagnostics: expand advanced testing portfolio while deepening clinician engagement; growth in Specialty also drives higher Routine/allied test volumes, improving wallet share and customer retention; aim to increase Specialty contribution to 45% from current 40%.

3. Strengthening TruHealth portfolio through targeted wellness offerings and higher customer engagement, driving adoption, customer lifetime value and market share in preventive diagnostics; expanded beyond pathology to include basic radiology, vital checks and consultations; while not expected to become a huge revenue contributor, it helps increase average revenue per patient and build consumer engagement.

4. Leveraging technology and AI: continued investment in digital platforms, automation and AI to improve customer experience, lab efficiency, doctor/patient engagement, and support long-term profitable growth.

5. Pursuing disciplined inorganic growth: with recent integrations progressing well, building acquisition funnel and continuing to evaluate high-quality, strategically aligned assets that can create long-term value through the proven integration playbook.

subsections.label: M&A pipeline / future acquisition criteria
points: Continue to be open to bolt-on acquisitions following the same path as before: acquiring a strong consumer brand based on ethical practices, strong science and positive unit economics; reputation of people behind the business matters since they continue working post-acquisition; disciplined valuation is essential.
Also open to doing larger deals if there is accrual of value for shareholders (EPS accretive) at the right price with potential for turnaround.
Recent acquisitions (beyond Core) are now fully integrated and performing in line with expectations, benefiting from the wider Metropolis network, operating processes and commercial capabilities.

Core Diagnostics currently in the final leg of integration; one year since acquisition, used to reflect on progress against original objectives (genomics platform build, North India brand strengthening, shareholder value creation) — all three objectives assessed as being met or on track.

subsections.label: Flagged headwinds
points: Weather unpredictability due to climate change heavily influences the business (diagnostics demand tied to weather-driven disease patterns), making growth difficult to predict precisely.

Geopolitical situation and raw material (RM) cost pressures were raised by an analyst as potential margin drags alongside expansion into lower-margin Tier-2/Tier-3 markets; management responded that Tier-2/Tier-3 expansion is not adding cost stress since further town expansion beyond 750 towns and lab expansion have been halted.
GLP-1/diabetes testing trend contribution is difficult to isolate and its full impact on diagnostics demand will 'play out a little longer over time' — still early days.
Core Diagnostics currently operates at a lower margin (high single-digit ~8%) than company average, which is a drag on consolidated margin until the 3-4 year target of ~25% is reached.
Advancing annual employee increments from July to April this year created a cost impact on margins in the quarter.
CGHS one-time pricing benefit accrued more to other industry peers than to Metropolis, and this one-time benefit will not recur next year.

key_figures.label: Patient volume growth contribution to CAGR

subsections.label: Outlook commentary
points: Q1 FY27 exceeded stated guidance on revenue growth; management believes FY27 revenue growth outlook of 14-15% is sustainable, primarily volume-driven, with patient volume growth expected to contribute 9-10% and realization/mix contributing 5-6% to the medium-term CAGR.

Expect EBITDA margin improvement of 100-150 bps in FY27, supported by ongoing operational efficiencies and cost optimization initiatives; over this year and next, focused on reaching 27-28% EBITDA margin.

Management reiterated 14-15% medium-term CAGR guidance despite an analyst question on whether the strong Q1 print (and other players' rising base-rate growth) suggests conservatism; management prefers not to focus on quarter-by-quarter seasonality given unpredictability (e.g., weather/climate impact) and feels comfortable with 14-15% for the full year.
No price increase planned in the near term; will pass on part of inflation to consumers at the appropriate time when market is conducive.
CAPEX for FY27 (Group basis, including all acquired entities) expected to be similar to last year's INR 65 crores.
Confident of enhancing Core Diagnostics revenue and EBITDA growth going forward per previously given estimates (path to ~25% EBITDA margin in 3-4 years from acquisition).
Confident of continuing to grow the international business across markets where Metropolis is a leader (top 2) or top-3 player in all five countries of operation.
Targeting 400-500 net center additions and a center-to-lab ratio of 1:30 by year-end FY27, alongside raising Specialty's revenue contribution to 45% from the current 40%.

themes.label: Margin expansion / operating leverage
themes.note: EBITDA margin expanded 210bps YoY to 25.2% in Q1, driven by volume-led operating leverage, cost management and lab transformation, with 100-150bps improvement guided for FY27 and a 27-28% medium-term target.

themes.label: M&A integration playbook
themes.note: One year post Core Diagnostics acquisition, all three original objectives (genomics build, North India brand, shareholder value) assessed as on track/achieved; Agra and Dehradun acquisitions tracking ahead of expectations.

themes.label: Network productivity shift (capex to throughput)
themes.note: Town expansion halted beyond 750 towns and lab expansion paused for five quarters; focus is deepening existing network, center-to-lab ratio improving toward 1:30, with rationalization of underperforming centers.

themes.label: Specialty & genomics mix improvement
themes.note: Specialty grew 17% and now 40% of revenue (targeted to rise to 45%); genomics portfolio doubled over the past year, aided by Core Diagnostics integration.

themes.label: Digital/D2C scale-up
themes.note: Company-wide automation/AI transformation spanning labs, customer engagement, procurement and back-office; partner portal enabling B2B digital enablement; TruHealth digital acquisition driving 22% growth.

themes.label: Tier 2/3 outpacing Tier 1 growth
themes.note: Rural centers delivered 36% revenue growth; Tier-2/Tier-3 network expansion (400-500 new centers targeted) remains a key growth and volume driver.

themes.label: Pricing discipline amid GST constraints
themes.note: No price increase taken in 18 months (last hike January 2025) as GST benefits were passed to consumers instead; management not contemplating a near-term price increase but will pass on inflation when the market is conducive.

key_takeaways: Revenue grew by about 17% year-on-year to INR 450 crores, ahead of stated guidance, while EBITDA margin expanded by 210 basis points to 25.2%.

Despite no price increase over the last 18 months, delivered 17% revenue growth, supported by 10% growth in patient volumes and 11% growth in test volumes, with the balance coming from a richer mix and improved realizations.

During the last 12 months, added more than 500 service centers, including 300 centers in Quarter 1 2027, and remain on track to add more than 500 centers during the current financial year; now operating across 750 towns.
Center-to-laboratory ratio improved from 1:21 a year ago to 1:24 in Quarter 1, and remain on track to improve this to around 1:30 by year-end.
North India now contributes 18% of the company's revenue, up from a single-digit contribution before the Core Diagnostics acquisition, and has emerged as the fastest-growing region in our network.
Genomics portfolio has doubled over the past year and is now one of the fastest-growing segments within our Specialty business.

Believe that we can sustain revenue growth outlook of 14%-15% for the year, and expect an improvement of 100-150 basis points on EBITDA during the current financial year, remaining focused on achieving an EBITDA margin of 27%-28% over this year and next year.
Q1 PAT stood at INR 57 crores, growing at 26% year-on-year; PAT margin expanded by 90 basis points to 12.6%.
pressing_questions: Can you specify the exact number of labs currently operating under the lab-on-lease model? (Management could not provide the number on the call and said they would come back with it.)

Could you split the 27%-28% medium-term margin guidance between the drag from cost pressures/geopolitical dynamics and the benefit from productivity improvements? (Management gave a qualitative rather than quantified split.)

quarters.summary: Metropolis delivered FY26 organic revenue growth of 13.7% (ahead of guided 12-13%) with organic EBITDA margin at 25.9% (+140bps normalized), and guides to a 14-15% revenue CAGR with 27-28% EBITDA margin over the next 3 years, driven by patient volume growth, RPP/price increases, network productivity (lab-to-center ratio moving to 35:1), mini-hub expansion, genomics scale-up, and disciplined M&A integration (Core Diagnostics reaching high-single-digit EBITDA in Q4, targeting 20%+ in 3 years).

subsections.label: Capital Allocation
points: Bonus share issue done in March '26 to enhance liquidity of shares for shareholders.
Board recommended another interim dividend of INR1 per share, reflecting strength of financial position and continued commitment to creating long-term value for shareholders.
Capex for FY26 stood at INR65 crores; capital allocation strategy will become increasingly selective and productivity-driven going forward.
Investments now focused on targeted network addition, specialty test expansion, technology upgrades, and digital capabilities.
With most of the lab network already in place, future growth expected to benefit from improved operating leverage and enhanced productivity as volume scales.

subsections.label: Depreciation Increase (Q4)
points: Depreciation increased sharply QoQ due to a mix of factors: genomic machinery coming online, capex investment concentrated in the later part of the year (hence Q4 sees full depreciation impact), and more aggressive network expansion in H2.

subsections.label: Intersegment Eliminations
points: When business generated from MHL is processed by the Specialty/Core (genomics/oncology) business, there is elimination of revenue and margin at the consolidation level, explaining the gap between organic margin and group-level margin bridge.

This intercompany transfer/elimination will continue as MHL drives more high-end oncology/core-product revenue through its distribution network — as revenue grows, more intercompany adjustments will occur, but the group-level number nets this out.

From Q1 FY27 onwards, the company will report only one number in its presentation — an organic/company-level number — since the acquisitions are now a year old and everything becomes organic from April 1; last year separate figures were shown because acquisitions/integrations were still in progress.

key_figures.label: MHL Group TruHealth Revenue Growth YoY
MHL Group Specialty Revenue Growth YoY
Expected TruHealth mix increase next year

subsections.label: Channel Performance (B2C/B2B)
points: B2C organic revenue growth supported by healthy demand across wellness, specialty, and routine testing, along with better customer engagement through both physical and digital channels.

B2B organic revenue growth driven by improving ease of doing business, enhancing service consistency, deepening institutional and corporate relationships, and building a more sustainable portfolio with better unit economics.

subsections.label: TruHealth and Specialty Segment Detail
points: TruHealth and Specialty continue to perform very strongly, improving both customer engagement and overall mix quality of the business.

Specialty mix expected to be taken higher via two levers beyond existing specialty testing capabilities: the genomics journey being accelerated, and Core Diagnostics' product capability being deployed across the MHL network.
Management expects Specialty contribution to reach around 40% this year.

TruHealth mix can go beyond 25% over the next 2-3 years; every year the mix is moving up by a couple of percentage points, with plans to include vital checkups, consults, basic radiology, and other adjacent services in TruHealth packages, improving overall RPP.
Digital revenue in Metropolis has higher customer lifetime value than brick-and-mortar business; enhancing digital contribution would enhance RPP growth.

subsections.label: Intersegment Elimination Impact on Margin
points: Core Diagnostics improved to high-single-digit EBITDA margin in Q4 FY26, while when subtracting MHL Group revenue/EBITDA from MHL organic numbers, the M&A portion margin computes to around 4-5% due to intersegment elimination of revenue and margin at consolidation — this benefit sits within the organic margin reported.

subsections.label: 3-Year Achievements Recap
points: Organic CAGR revenue growth of 13% over last 3 years on like-to-like basis, largely driven by test volume and patient volume growth.
Restored organic revenue margins to pre-COVID levels of around 26%.
Expanded lab capacity by more than 50% and increased presence to more than 750 towns and cities across India.
Built strong retail D2C mindset resulting in self-referrals contributing 40% and B2C business accounting for 60% of revenue, creating a more sticky, higher-margin business model.
Expanded into basic radiology and vital checks in some centers on a pilot basis, encouraged by response.
Established robust technology architecture enabling digital channels to grow from 0% to 25% of revenue while making the organization significantly more automated.
Strengthened scientific capabilities, enhanced reputation amongst doctors and hospitals, added entire genomics segment.
Expanded North India business, increasing contribution from mid-single-digit to 17% of revenues.
Added, enhanced, and rebuilt a stable and better-quality management team.

subsections.label: Digital and AI Strategy
points: Approach to digital and AI continues to be practical, measured, and focused on high-impact use cases; AI seen as an enabler of productivity, service quality, customer engagement, and workflow efficiency, not a near-term disruptor in pathology.

Over the past few quarters, digital and AI tools strengthened across customer and partner platforms, lead management, workflow automation, contact center quality, and selective diagnostic applications.

Three distinct digital channels drive customer acquisition: the Metropolis app, the company website (customer places test requests), and the customer data platform (CLM engine) which reaches existing customers with next-best-action recommendations based on past testing trends.
Digital revenue is largely D2C; cost of servicing digital channels is relatively lower than non-digital channels, so margins improve as digital revenue scales; digital drives volume first.

subsections.label: Genomics Platform
points: Genomics journey continues to advance steadily and remains a key strategic pillar for the future.
Integration of Core Diagnostics and ongoing strengthening of central genomics platform deepens capabilities across oncology, reproductive health, inherited disorders, and precision diagnostics.

Platform anchored by 2 CAP-accredited genomic labs (Gurgaon and Bombay) plus a growing team of genetic counsellors across the country, strengthening ability to deliver high-end genomic testing with quality interpretation and scale.
Integration has enabled expanded access to high-end genomic testing across India through both B2C and B2B channels.
Personalized interpretation for every patient rests on institutional expertise and knowledge, not equipment — positioning Metropolis as a trusted, credible leader in specialty genomics testing.
Genomics and scientific symposiums held in Mumbai and Chennai received strong participation and response, indicating big gaps in the market for good clinical reports that Metropolis can fill.

subsections.label: Platform Modernization
points: Steady progress on productivity and platform modernization: lab platform upgrades, infrastructure consolidation, vendor consolidation, and more optimal use of technology across the network.
These efforts are helping simplify the operating backbone, improve efficiency, and support structural cost discipline over time.

key_figures.label: Mini hubs from existing collection centers upgraded
New mini hub centers to be set up

subsections.label: Network Build-out Shift to Productivity
points: Over last 2 years, significant investment in expanding/strengthening lab and service center backbone; that heavy build-out phase is now largely behind, focus shifted from expansion capex to throughput-led productivity.

Priority is not just adding more infrastructure, but getting more output, better efficiency, and stronger leverage from infrastructure already created — a key shift in operating model and driver of margin improvement.
Center-to-lab ratio strengthened from 20:1 to 24:1, testament to focused execution to improve network density and drive higher throughput.
Over next 18 months expect to strengthen feeder center network further, moving ratio closer to 30:1 in many markets depending on cluster maturity; over 3-year horizon target 35:1.

Last year no significant new labs added (lab addition phase over about a year back); in coming year also not planning to add a high number of labs — this, combined with center additions feeding existing labs, drives lab utilization up.

Labs are of different categories (big regional reference labs, global labs, satellite labs, greenfield labs) making a single lab utilization metric difficult; utilization growth can be related to overall volume growth of 14-15% per year.

subsections.label: Mini Hub Strategy
points: Mini hubs differ from standard collection centers (which only collect blood samples for transport to lab) by adding services like ECG, X-ray, and in limited locations sonography — piloted over past 2 years and found to increase RPP per patient.
Mini hubs will include more basic radiology modalities beyond X-ray/ECG — potentially bone density machines, mammography machines, or bigger X-ray machines (not CT/MRI).
Idea is to create enough services at local level — blood plus radiology plus possibly consultation — making bigger, more service-infrastructure centers usable for both retail and corporate customers.
Mini hub capex will be higher than a standard collection center, roughly similar to a satellite lab, estimated at INR30-40 lakh.

subsections.label: Gross Margin / Productivity Drivers
points: Lab platform consolidation and upgrades — consolidating vendors and moving to better, higher-efficiency, more productive, technology-enabled, scalable platforms — provides a scale advantage and improves material consumption.
Barcoding introduced across all 220 labs during the year further improved material consumption percentages.
No significant new lab additions in the current or coming year contributes to gross margin improvement as existing labs get better utilized.

subsections.label: Tier-wise Growth Dynamics
points: Tier 1 growth boosted by Core Diagnostics, which is largely on a Tier 1 setup, showing much higher growth in Tier 1 in the last year.
Tier 2 growth boosted by cities like Dehradun and Agra that have been added via acquisitions, showing higher Tier 2 growth.
Tier 3 and above is growing at about 26% to 30% in the last few quarters, showing much higher growth than Tier 1/Tier 2 on a like-to-like basis, and this trend is expected to continue.
Tier 1 growth clarified as closer to 11%, not single digit as earlier implied in the discussion.

subsections.label: Mumbai Market Detail
points: Mumbai is the company's biggest market with about 500 service centers spread across the metropolitan area and outskirts (Kalyan, Borivali, Virar, Vasai, etc.), with continuous network footprint expansion.
Most parts of Mumbai are growing at 13-14% revenue growth YoY; micro-market segmentation (e.g., Kalyan vs Thane growth) was not disclosed.

Company continues to see much higher patient volume growth in the northern part of the market due to new acquisitions there, but otherwise stable and good patient volume growth is seen broadly across geographies (Mumbai in line with overall company volume growth, give or take ~1%).

key_figures.label: Core Diagnostics EBITDA improvement
key_figures.period: within 4 quarters of acquisition, achieved Q4 FY26

key_figures.label: Number of acquisitions completed in FY26

subsections.label: M&A Integration Progress
points: Integration progressing broadly in line with expectations; Core Diagnostics moved from -2% EBITDA to high-single-digit EBITDA in Q4, completing the committed 4-quarter mission.
On path for the 3-year commitment of 20%-plus EBITDA at Core Diagnostics.

Priority over past few quarters has been stabilization at the core, driving process alignment, integrating platforms, and realizing synergies across acquired businesses so they are seamlessly embedded within Metropolis operating DNA.

Beginning to see tangible value emerge not just from increased scale but from enhanced capabilities, lab consolidation, better network utilization, procurement efficiencies, and a stronger foundation to support future growth.
Going forward, focus will shift more towards driving volumes and scaling the platform, unlocking efficiencies and leverage for a clear pathway to margin expansion.
Dehradun, Agra, and Kolhapur acquisitions continue to operate at margins above the company average.
Company believes it is building a repeatable M&A integration playbook across processes, people, systems, quality standards, and commercial synergies — an important capability going forward.
FY26 included four acquisitions, all seamlessly integrated, contributing to a fast overall growth rate of about 23.6% for the year.

subsections.label: Inorganic Growth Outlook
points: There are about 3 lakh labs in India, with 90-odd-percent being single labs; some regional chain labs exist; many assets are available for acquisition but quality often does not meet Metropolis's standards.
Company will remain selective but continues to see and explore opportunities; will pursue acquisitions only when the deal is strategic and at the right price, not merely to add growth.
Broadly expects to continue seeing inorganic action for the next few years.
Additional growth over the next 3 years will come partly from adding strategic and value-additive acquisitions, alongside organic growth via patient volumes, RPP growth, and price increases.

subsections.label: Reporting Structure Change
points: Since acquisitions are now a year old, everything will be organic from April 1; from Q1 FY27 onward, only one number (organic/company-level) will be shown in the presentation, versus split reporting shown last year during active integration.

subsections.label: Pricing/Tax Constraint
points: No price increase was taken in Q4 FY26 due to GST reasons, unlike last year; this left the price lever as an opportunity for growth later in the year.
At this point in time, company is not looking at a price increase in the current fiscal, but would not hesitate to do so if there is a need as the year progresses.

subsections.label: Insurance Channel Limited
points: Test volume from insurance companies is very insignificant at this point in time; company does not have high volumes from the insurance segment and is just building its portfolio.

subsections.label: M&A Target Quality Constraint
points: Many diagnostic assets available for acquisition may not meet Metropolis's quality standards for what it would like to buy, limiting inorganic opportunities to selective, strategic deals.

subsections.label: Competitive Landscape
points: Competition will always be there in the diagnostics industry, but management believes the structural runway remains strong without any unreasonable or disruptive competitive environment.
No third-party data is available to confirm the shift from unorganized to organized players; assessment is based on management's on-ground sense.

subsections.label: 3-Year Vision
points: Vision to grow at a CAGR of 14% to 15% in revenue over the next 3 years; organic revenue would come primarily via patient volumes, RPP growth, and price increases, with an additional part from adding strategic and value-additive acquisitions (only at the right deal at the right price).

Goal to reimagine processes through automation and technology enablement to drive center productivity and margin expansion, targeting a sustainable group EBITDA margin of 27% to 28% over the next 3 years, supported by profitability across every regional market and bringing Core Diagnostics to a 20%+ margin profile.
Aim to continue being the most respected scientific brand not just in the West and South but also in the North and East of India by building relationships and trust amongst doctors.
Plans to build a network of 100 mini hubs over 3 years (50 upgraded existing collection centers, 50 new centers), encompassing pathology and basic radiology to service retail and corporate clientele.

Plans to expand asset-light collection center network by adding 1,500 more centers, taking lab-to-center ratio to 1:35 from current 1:24, and enhancing center productivity of existing centers by 20% over 3 years.

Aim to build capability for a tech-enabled D2C vertical focusing on enhanced chronic business acquired and serviced via digital and physical channels; digital revenue has higher customer lifetime value than brick-and-mortar business.

subsections.label: Near-term FY27 Guidance Detail
points: Management expects about 125-150 bps EBITDA margin improvement in the coming fiscal year.
About 8-9% patient volume growth is estimated for the coming fiscal, with the remaining ~5% of growth coming from realization.

Patient volume growth remained healthy in the 7-8% range as company exits FY26, supported by lab additions made over recent years, continuous center expansion, and acceleration of the digital agenda; company is optimistic of sustaining this going forward.
RPP growth being driven by improving mix, led by enhanced TruHealth offerings, higher specialty mix, and increasing contribution from genomics.

subsections.label: Long-term Margin Philosophy
points: Margins can keep expanding as long as the business keeps growing with cost growth lower than revenue growth (operating leverage), but maximizing EBITDA is not viewed as the smartest strategy.

Management believes a sustainable EBITDA of 27-28% over the next 3 years makes sense; any further operating leverage generated would preferably be reinvested in the business — adding services, building the brand, or building further distribution — rather than purely maximizing margin.

themes.note: Heavy lab/center build-out phase is largely behind; focus shifts to throughput, lab-to-center ratio improving from 20:1 to 24:1, targeting 35:1 in 3 years.

themes.label: Specialty & genomics mix improvement
themes.note: TruHealth and Specialty segments growing strongly (20-21% and 16-17%), with genomics and Core Diagnostics products expected to push Specialty mix to ~40%.

themes.label: Digital/D2C scale-up
themes.note: Digital channels grew from 0% to 25% of revenue over 3 years, driven by app, website, and CLM engine, with lower servicing cost and higher customer lifetime value.

themes.label: Tier 2/3 outpacing Tier 1 growth
themes.note: Tier 3 and above growing 26-30% versus Tier 1 closer to 11%, aided by acquisitions in Tier 1/Tier 2 markets like Core Diagnostics, Dehradun, and Agra.

themes.label: Pricing discipline amid GST constraints
themes.note: No price hike taken in Q4 due to GST reasons and none currently planned for FY27, leaving price as a lever for later in the year if needed.

key_takeaways: We delivered organic revenue growth of 13.7%, better than our stated guidance of 12% to 13%.
On a normalized basis, organic margins expanded by around 140 basis points to 25.9%, supported by sustained productivity improvements, ongoing lab platform upgrades, and consolidation initiatives.
We have committed that within 4 quarters of doing the acquisition, we would move from a negative 2% EBITDA to a high-single-digit EBITDA in Q4. We have completed this mission.
We are on our path for our 3-year commitment for a 20%-plus EBITDA at core.
Over the next 3 years, the vision is to grow at a CAGR of 14% to 15% in revenue.
Goal of achieving a sustainable group EBITDA margin of 27% to 28% over the next 3 years, supported by profitability across every regional market and bringing core to a 20% plus margin profile.

We would expand our asset-light collection center network by adding 1,500 more centers, taking the lab-to-center ratio to 1:35 from the current 1:24, and enhancing center productivity of existing centers by 20% over 3 years.

MHL Group revenue stood at INR 425 crores, reflecting a year-on-year growth of 23% with EBITDA margin of 25.4%. For the full year, revenue stood at INR 1,646 crores, growing 23.6% year-on-year with an EBITDA margin of 24.4%.

EMUDHRA.about: Emudhra is a licensed certifying authority involved in issuing digital signature certificates in India under its eMudhra brand. The company is licensed by the Controller of Certifying Authorities (CCA), Ministry of Information Technology, and operates under the guidelines set by the Information technology Act.[1]

quarters.summary: Management reported a strong start to FY27 with total income up 28% YoY and EBITDA/PAT growth outpacing revenue, driven by Enterprise Solutions and the Cryptas acquisition, even as Trust Services saw a temporary decline due to a token-standard transition. Guidance for FY27 remains unchanged at 18% organic growth and 25% PAT growth, with a 3-year ambition to double PAT (not necessarily revenue), continued international expansion (UAE Trust Service launch), and Cryptas expected to turn profitable this year.

subsections.label: Margin drivers
points: This quarter, the margin slightly improved because token sales (lower margin business) were lower in the overall composition.
Enterprise sales share was higher compared to Trust Service (a lower percentage), and Enterprise sales carry a higher margin — these two factors led to higher blended margin.

Going forward, margins may not further increase suddenly because the company is adding more salespeople across geographies; some senior people have joined recently and their extra salaries will weigh on margin.
Overall, management expects to maintain EBITDA margin around 25% and PAT margin around 16-16.5%.

subsections.label: International segment profitability drag
points: International business profitability is lower than domestic because it comprises three elements: the services business (18-20% gross margin, ~INR 150 crore business per last year), the Cryptas business (~INR 100 crore business, not profitable at all last year but gradually improving, with profit expected this year), and the own product segment (profitability even better than the Indian business).

Combined together, overall segment-wise profitability is lower than the Indian segment profitability, but is expected to improve over time as Cryptas becomes profitable and the product/services segments grow.
A second drag is the cost of new senior executive hires in several new markets (USD 200,000-300,000 per person); this cost will be offset as volumes improve.

subsections.label: B.V. (European subsidiary) loss
points: The INR 4 crore consolidated net loss from subsidiaries is predominantly from the European subsidiary B.V., driven by legal expenses incurred.
Cryptas sits under B.V.; when Cryptas becomes profitable, B.V. will also become profitable.
Apart from Cryptas, B.V. independently appointed a senior salesperson in Rome chasing several leads; if even one or two materialize, B.V. will turn profitable.
Management does not expect the loss to continue in the current year.

subsections.label: Returns profile (ROE/ROCE)
points: As profit increases every year, reserves increase, which adds to the equity base, so ROE has not risen proportionally with profitability improvements even as Enterprise Solutions mix has grown.
Management views ~14.5-15% (last year's level) as a reasonable ROE to maintain.
Management believes their EBITDA margin (>25%) and PAT margin (>16%) profile compares favorably to peer cybersecurity companies, many of which run near-zero margins.
As a strategy, the company has not borrowed much; higher leverage could improve ROE but would not improve ROCE, and the company prefers not to create a borrowing burden.

subsections.label: Enterprise Solutions
points: Remained primary growth engine, growing approximately 50% YoY and contributing 65% of total income.
Of the 28% total income growth, approximately 13% came from Cryptas acquisition, with the balance from organic growth led by Enterprise Solutions.
Within the product segment, organic growth was 25% and Cryptas (inorganic) contributed the other 25% of growth (base moved from about INR 80 crore).

subsections.label: Services Business
points: Delivered growth of around 5% YoY, supported by new customer additions in the United States.
Services revenue is 19-20% of overall quarterly revenue; service margins were not specifically called out this quarter but broadly follow the historical margin profile (18-20% gross margin).

subsections.label: Trust Service Business
points: Saw a temporary decline during the quarter following transition to a new global security standard for digital signature tokens effective September.

Channel partners reduced stocking of legacy tokens ahead of the expiry, resulting in reduced demand; typical quarterly token volume of INR 8-9 crore fell by INR 5-7 crore due to lower partner stocking.
Token business carries low margin (~10% gross margin on average), so top-line may remain lower next quarter too but bottom-line impact is limited.
ePass token (major token) recertification to FIPS 140-3 is largely done and pending final approval from CCA; expected certified by around September, after which token volumes should recover.
ProxKey token is reportedly not being recertified.
A new token called 'innate' is already certified but has low production capacity/volumes currently.

subsections.label: PrivaTrust (Data Privacy/Consent Management)
points: Already live with consent management capabilities; multiple pilots/proof-of-concepts underway with a few wins expected soon.
India's DPDP Act compliance deadline gives large organizations time till end of year or into next year; other organizations also need to implement.

Additional modules planned: data discovery and classification of personally identifiable information (across storage, files, folders, databases) and handling of personal data shared with third-party vendors (e.g., CRM vendors).
This is a new addition to the product stack; initial focus is India given DPDP Act, particularly for B2C-focused entities that must comply quickly.

International expansion (Europe, China, other markets with nascent/forming privacy regulations) planned once foothold established in India; better sense of opportunity direction expected in a quarter or two.

subsections.label: SecurePass (India and beyond)
points: Growth drivers: (1) compliance mandates from Central Bank and capital markets regulator on stronger authentication forcing banks/capital markets entities to improve cybersecurity posture; (2) larger deal values than even CertiNext — typical large bank/government deal INR 4-6 crore to start, possibly higher; full PIM+PAM suite could be north of INR 10 crore per large bank; (3) privileged identity/privileged access management becoming compliance mandates (regulatory and voluntary) following recent data breaches, which typically occur when critical administrator privilege/credentials are compromised.
Company looking to expand SecurePass to adjoining markets: Philippines, Indonesia, Africa, and recently some conversations in the Middle East.
Many more deals in pipeline in Indian context, under RFP evaluation at various stages.

Defense is also a market: already has a defense agency customer with identity access management implemented across 200 internal applications; conversations ongoing with other defense and ancillary agencies.

subsections.label: US Products business
points: Reasonably good growth seen in lead pipeline and initiatives.

University federation (InCommon), won last year, continues to onboard more universities, increasing brand visibility for CertiNext in North America; already issuing 1,000-1,500 certificates per day via the university network, with momentum expected to further improve.
Active lead initiatives in IoT-related PKI use cases (healthcare and other industries), bringing device-level trust.

General pipeline building/lead generation in upper mid-market and lower enterprise segments in the US, with positive conversations around SSL/Trust, driven by the shift to 47-day SSL certificate expiry and post-quantum transition trends.
Local brand and data center presence were baseline requirements enabling these conversations and pipeline building.
US Enterprise segment growth rate maintained at about 25%; outlook positive, though North American pipelines take time to convert; company has a captive client base to expand upon.

subsections.label: Cryptas turnaround
points: Cryptas contributed approximately INR 200 million (INR 20 crore) of revenue in what is typically a seasonally weak quarter in Europe.
First sale of eMudhra's CertiNext certificate lifecycle management platform (via Cryptas) to a large German data center customer.
First mSigner deployment integrated with PrimeSign Trust Services (a Cryptas subsidiary) for an Austrian city municipality — a qualified signing service across the EU.
These wins validate product-market fit and demonstrate ability to cross-sell the broader eMudhra platform into the Cryptas customer base.

Integration effort over the last six-seven months focused on substituting third-party competitor products (e.g., Keyfactor) used by Cryptas with eMudhra's own IP (CertiNext CA, CLM), enabling cost savings via transfer pricing to India when substitution occurs.

Cryptas has marquee customers particularly in German-speaking Europe across banking, insurance, oil & gas — all now prospects for cross-selling eMudhra products; pipeline being chased with results hoped in the next few quarters.
Management is very confident of Cryptas turning profitable in FY27, citing the two wins as foundation.

subsections.label: R&D and innovation
points: R&D investment remained tightly aligned with the evolving cybersecurity landscape.

Introduced Cryptographic Bill of Materials (CBOM) analysis within CertiNext, enabling enterprises to discover where cryptography is deployed across their IT environment and helping them prepare for the transition to post-quantum cryptography.
Continued strengthening of broader product portfolio with AI-powered capabilities in emSigner and commercial launch of PrivaTrust Consent Management Modules.

Existing product suite (CertiNext and SecurePass) being significantly strengthened to capture Agentic AI security opportunity; company monitoring bolt-on capabilities from US startups working in Agentic AI security space, which may be pursued in the future though nothing is immediate.

subsections.label: Post-quantum readiness opportunity
points: Increasing regulatory and industry focus on post-quantum readiness, together with the need for organizations to inventory and modernize their cryptographic assets, creates a significant long-term opportunity for the certificate lifecycle management and PKI platform.

subsections.label: Cybersecurity and AI convergence / Agentic AI
points: Cybersecurity and AI are becoming increasingly interconnected; as enterprises deploy AI at scale, trust, identity, and cryptography become foundational infrastructure.
Company's five-platform strategy positions it to capitalize on these structural trends while expanding internationally.

Agentic AI problem statement: agents communicating with one another or with systems need identity (a digital signature certificate) since they cannot enter username/password/OTP; also need traceability/verifiability/legal validity when agents take decisions on behalf of humans (e.g., approving a loan).
As Agentic AI and GenAI adoption ramps up in enterprises (still early stage), company expects to be a beneficiary; views AI as a structural tailwind to the business.

Adoption is at a very early stage — early conversations on understanding Agentic AI risk, to be followed by pilots to secure the Agentic AI landscape, and then adoption over time; too early to quantify opportunity, possibly clearer in about a year once pilots begin.
No specific revenue currently generated from Agentic AI use cases; company doing active R&D.

subsections.label: International momentum
points: International markets now contribute 66% of revenue; encouraging momentum across Europe, North America, the Middle East and Africa.
Europe was particularly encouraging this quarter, driven by Cryptas cross-sell wins (German data center, Austrian municipality).

subsections.label: UAE Trust Service launch
points: Company is at the final step of the QTSP license application process in UAE, expected to complete towards the end of this quarter to beginning of next quarter, after which the service can launch.
The offering is similar to the Aadhaar eSign type in India but built on a local UAE identity ecosystem, aimed predominantly at the local market for banking and other segments.

It is meant to complement the existing emSigner offering in UAE; embedding banks and regulated entities is a timed process that will happen over a duration; company is in early stages of setting up the go-to-market process.
The product is enterprise-oriented, not a retail product; final signer is a retail customer but the sale is predominantly to banks and NBFCs, similar to how Aadhaar eSign functions in India.

subsections.label: SecurePass geographic expansion
points: Looking to expand SecurePass reach to Philippines, Indonesia, Africa, and recently some conversations have started in the Middle East.

subsections.label: Acquisition philosophy
points: Company does not venture into high-risk acquisitions; will only pursue if valuation is reasonable and it fits the company's philosophy.
Past acquisitions have been highly value-driven, focused on ability to grow the acquired business further.
Several potential acquisitions are seen but rejected due to high pricing or lack of management/cultural fit.
Company remains extremely cautious on profitability, having maintained profitability and growth since listing.

subsections.label: TI Infotech / 3i Infotech dispute
points: No update on the case; police have taken management's statement (Monday) and extensively noted the company's side of the story along with evidence provided.
Timeline for resolution is in the hands of the police; company does not know when they will close the matter or take further action.

Regarding Capital MXT's reported acquisition of a 5% stake in the company (referenced in context of the dispute), management clarified this stake acquisition is related to the Executive Chairman's personal investment and not related to eMudhra.

subsections.label: Token standard transition impact
points: Transition to a new global security standard for digital signature tokens (effective September) caused a temporary decline in Trust Service revenue as customers/channel partners reduced demand for legacy tokens ahead of expiry.
Q2 top-line for Trust Services likely to remain impacted as well, though bottom-line impact is limited given low token margins (~10%).

ePass token recertification (FIPS 140-3) mostly complete, pending final approval from CCA (Controller of Certifying Authorities); expected certified around September, after which volumes should recover.
New 'innate' token already certified but with low production capacity, limiting near-term volume contribution.

subsections.label: International segment cost pressure
points: Higher cost of senior executive hires (USD 200,000-300,000 per person) in new international markets is weighing on international segment profitability, to be offset as volumes improve.

subsections.label: European subsidiary (B.V.) losses
points: B.V. incurred legal expenses contributing to a consolidated net loss of about INR 4 crore; loss expected to reduce once Cryptas and B.V.'s own sales initiatives (senior salesperson in Rome) turn profitable.

subsections.label: 3i Infotech / TI Infotech legal matter
points: Ongoing police investigation with no update; timeline for resolution uncertain and outside company's control.

subsections.label: Unchanged FY27 guidance
points: Guidance remains unchanged from previous quarter: organic growth of 18% and PAT growth of 25%.

Focus areas: driving profitable product-led growth, expanding international footprint, executing UAE Trust Service launch, and maintaining disciplined EBITDA and PAT margin while continuing to invest in innovation.

subsections.label: 3-year vision (FY27-FY29)
points: FY30 vision not defined, but a 3-year vision has been set: to achieve 2x profitability (PAT) in three years (FY27, FY28, FY29); 2x revenue growth may not happen.
Expecting organic growth of 18-20% per year; any acquisitive growth would be additive.

To achieve the 2x PAT target, Enterprise Solution has to gradually grow more (growth in Services business is almost negligible); Trust Service may grow 15-20%; Enterprise Solution business will grow more, maybe 20-25% per year.

Order book metric (published annually, since IPO in 2022) is the key operating metric investors should track each year to assess progress toward doubling PAT; historically there has been a multiple on the order book that translates to following year's business performance.

Using current revenue projected at 1.18x for three years and current profitability (INR 110 crore) projected at 1.25x for three years, investors can derive the implied PAT margin, which could be 17-18% versus current 16%.

subsections.label: Segment growth outlook
points: International Enterprise Solutions margin not separately guided going forward; overall expecting 25% PAT growth and 18% top-line growth for FY27, adjusting for variances across segments.
US Products/Enterprise segment growth rate of about 25% being maintained; outlook positive.

key_takeaways: During the quarter, our total income grew by 28% YoY to INR 1,925 million, while EBITDA increased by over 40% to INR 504 million, taking our EBITDA margin to 26.2%. Profit after tax grew 28% YoY to INR 320 million, with PAT margin remaining healthy at 16.6%.

Of the 28% growth in total income, approximately 13% was contributed by the Cryptas acquisition, while the balance reflects healthy organic growth across our core businesses led by continued strength in our Enterprise Solution portfolio.

Enterprise Solutions remained our primary growth engine, growing approximately 50% YoY, and contributing 65% of total income, while our Services Business also delivered growth of around 5% YoY, supported by new customer additions in the United States.
International markets now contribute 66% of our revenue, and we continue to see encouraging momentum across Europe, North America, the Middle East and Africa.

Through Cryptas, we achieved our first sale of eMudhra's CertiNext certificate lifecycle management platform to a large German data center customer, while also securing the first mSigner deployment integrated with PrimeSign Trust Services for an Austrian city municipality.
Our Trust Service business saw a temporary decline during the quarter following the transition to a new global security standard for digital signature tokens, which comes into effect in September.

Finally, from an outlook perspective, our guidance remains unchanged from what we shared in the previous quarter, that is to achieve an organic growth of 18% and work towards achieving a PAT growth of 25%.
Our three-year vision is to achieve 2x profitability in three years, but 2x revenue growth may not happen.
pressing_questions: What is the outlook for margins over 2027 and beyond, especially given the current lower profitability of the international business relative to domestic?

How should investors think about relative contribution from revenue growth versus profitability improvement while achieving the goal of doubling the bottom line over three years, what margins are achievable, and what is the most critical execution risk?

Could management help investors understand the FY30 vision for the company, and how the revenue mix across Trust Service, Enterprise, and Transformation Services is expected to evolve, and where the major growth drivers are emerging?

As Enterprise Solution's share of revenue has grown, why has this not yet translated into a corresponding improvement in ROE and ROCE, and what would management consider a sustainable ROE/ROCE over the medium term?

quarters.summary: FY2026 saw total income of INR7,132 million (up 35% YoY), EBITDA of INR1,654 million (up 33%) and PAT of INR1,100 million (up 26%), driven by strong Enterprise Solutions growth (product-led, 55% YoY) and international expansion. For FY2027, management guides ~18% organic revenue growth and 25-30% (likely 27-28%) PAT growth, with an ambition to double PAT over the next 3 years, supported by AI, data sovereignty, PQC transition and tightening compliance tailwinds; US product order book is expected to be ~2.2-2.3X next year vs prior guidance of 2X due to Middle East order delays from the regional conflict.
