subsections.label: Drivers of PAT growth
points: PAT growth of ~27-28% projected is driven by higher composition of product business, since product gross margin is much higher compared to services and trust services.
As product composition increases in revenue mix (since services is not growing), gross margin, EBITDA and PAT will grow higher accordingly.

subsections.label: Cryptas profitability trajectory
points: Cryptas moved from a Q1 integration loss of ~1.6-2 crores to a Q2 integration profit of ~2 crores, netting to roughly 1-2 crores profit for the year.
Profitability improvement is a continuous effort; company is in 8-9 conversations to replace competing American CLM solution with eMudhra's own CLM solution at Cryptas customers.
FY27 estimate of over $1 million profit from Cryptas depends on success in converting these customers to eMudhra's CLM solution; European bank sales cycles tend to be long.

key_figures.label: Enterprise Solution and Service segment revenue

subsections.label: Three-segment business structure
points: eMudhra operates as a three-segment business: Enterprise Solution, Trust Services, and Pure Services.
Enterprise Solution growth has been the defining feature of FY2026, driven by both organic growth and acquisitions (Cryptas).

Pure Services remained flat, largely in line with industry trends; in North America the services business continues to create enterprise relationships and the company will pursue cross-sell opportunities into its product portfolio from this base.

subsections.label: Product platforms driving Enterprise Solutions
points: Certificate lifecycle management platform CertiNext and identity and access management platform SecurePass added enterprise accounts across financial services, government, energy and education globally.
Proportion of product-led revenue in the mix has grown.
CertiNext added accounts in gaming, ERP, energy and financial services across the US and Europe, and in critical infrastructure in Africa.
SecurePass mandates won with defense agencies, large banks and government departments in India requiring converged identity management.

subsections.label: India Enterprise quarterly volatility
points: India enterprise business saw a decline in the quarter, but this reflects a high base in Q3 (a larger defense deal booked then), optically making Q4 appear as a drop; full-year India enterprise growth was 27.6%.

subsections.label: Trust services growth drivers
points: Trust services grew ~30% despite the new income tax circular reducing digital signature certificate requirements.

Growth driven by enhanced partner-model services, increased sales of combo certificates (instead of simple digital signatures), increasing direct retail sales, separate token sales now available directly via portal, and increased e-sign volumes.
Pure eSign (used only for signature) is classified under trust services, while eSign combined with emSigner goes under enterprise.

subsections.label: Primesign/Cryptas revenue classification
points: Primesign (Cryptas subsidiary) revenue is currently classified under Enterprise Solution because it is sold along with other enterprise offerings.

subsections.label: Order book classification
points: The INR238 crore order book disclosed is largely on the product business side only and does not include any services element.

key_figures.label: PQC transition mandate deadline for critical infrastructure

subsections.label: R&D focus areas
points: R&D investments in post-quantum cryptography (PQC), CertiNext and SecurePass have translated into customer wins across target markets.

Ongoing R&D focused on two areas: Agentic AI being embedded as a capability layer across all four platforms, since AI agents acting on behalf of enterprises require digital identities, signed authorizations, and audit trails which the products are built to support.
Data privacy stack addresses need to manage, protect and demonstrate compliance around personal data, aligned with India's DPDP Act and GDPR in Europe.

subsections.label: Quality and governance certifications
points: In FY2026, renewed or maintained CMMI Level 5, WebTrust, ISO 27001 and SOC 2 Type 2 certifications.
eMudhra remains the only Indian certifying authority listed in all major browser trust stores.

subsections.label: Google root certificate policy change
points: Google effected a policy change on multipurpose certificates for new root certificates; the 15th June date was not a strict deadline but part of an annual recurring policy change process.
Company's new roots have been submitted and are in queue for distribution across Google environments (Chrome, Android, etc.).
No business impact expected as existing roots remain trusted on Google during a transition period until new roots are accepted; company continues to issue from existing roots in the meantime.

subsections.label: PQC deployment/POC status
points: Quite a few PQC-related POCs are ongoing, driven by clear mandates from domestic regulators and global bodies on transition requirements.
Some POCs expected to reach fruition in closed user group scenarios within this financial year.
Clear directives require critical infrastructure companies to move out of conventional algorithms to PQC by 2029-2030.
PQC deployment opportunities are mostly in BFSI (particularly critical large banks), defence, and some critical government agencies.

subsections.label: AI/cybersecurity market dynamics
points: Management clarified that AI models like Anthropic Claude and Mythos are foundational models providing capabilities to identify infrastructure vulnerabilities, not standalone cybersecurity products competing with certificate/identity management vendors.
These models significantly expand the attack surface as previously undetected vulnerabilities come to the forefront, requiring enterprises to significantly better their cybersecurity posture.
A large public sector bank recently announced it will ramp up cybersecurity spend by 50%, reflecting this dynamic; product companies like eMudhra help enterprises improve their cybersecurity posture.

subsections.label: Product stickiness / switching costs
points: Core products (identity/authentication/access and certificate lifecycle management) sit at the heart of client core workflows, e.g., authentication systems power customer login for internet banking at large banks.
Products are considered more core than peripheral to client infrastructure, making switching/replacement a cumbersome affair once implemented.

subsections.label: Revenue recognition model
points: No change in product revenue model; company continues recurring billing as well as license model.

Even if order intake is larger, revenue can only be recognized upon execution, which for large bank/government clients depends on their infrastructure and team readiness apart from eMudhra's software, so not everything gets recognized as revenue immediately.

key_figures.label: Middle East and Africa revenue share

subsections.label: North America
points: Notable win: large TLS certificate order for a university federation in the United States (InCommon consortium, ~700 universities enrolled), a meaningful step in establishing credibility across US markets.
This order came via a US trust service vendor and gives visibility across the entire consortium and several other segments; competitors like DigiCert have also publicized this deal.
Company expects 25-30% growth (or more) in the US product segment next year on the back of this momentum.
Company has invested in senior management resource in the US and in a data center, which is starting to yield results, alongside cross-selling from the US acquisition.

subsections.label: Europe
points: Acquisition of Cryptas brought Primesign and eIDAS-aligned service provider capabilities; Cryptas integration ongoing.
Actively cross-selling CLM platform into Cryptas customer base; deals expected to close in the next few quarters.
NIS2 and DORA regulations continue to drive demand for compliant PKI and identity controls across European banks and critical infrastructure.
Through Cryptas, company is trying to sell products with demos and discussions happening; European bank sales cycles tend to be long.

subsections.label: India
points: Trust services franchise continues to perform steadily; e-sign business processes well over 3 lakh daily transactions in banking and financial services.

subsections.label: Middle East
points: Completed e-signature workload rollouts for banking customers in Oman; seeing continued upgrades across existing base.
Some Middle East orders expected in March got delayed due to the war that started from February end, but management expects these orders will still come.

subsections.label: Africa
points: Growing area of focus with active DPI (Digital Public Infrastructure) deployments underway, including certificate lifecycle management for critical IT infrastructure and e-signature rollouts across government and banking.
Represents a significant long-term opportunity for the end-to-end DPI stack covering digital ID, PKI, e-passports and e-sign; company is investing in building presence there.
In discussion with a number of potential deals in the Africa market.

subsections.label: Infrastructure / data sovereignty
points: Data centers now operating in the United States, Europe, UAE and India, positioned to meet data sovereignty requirements across key markets.
Enterprises and governments increasingly require cryptographic operations and identity workflows be processed within their jurisdiction; multi-region footprint addresses this directly.

subsections.label: Identity access management geographic expansion plan
points: Identity access management product has not yet been taken to the US as it's not part of the full plan; focus has been on certificate lifecycle management in the US where good traction is building.

Immediate focus this year is to take identity access management to adjoining markets outside India, leveraging strong references and credibility built in India; first attempts likely in Asia Pacific, Middle East, and Africa.

subsections.label: FY2027 growth themes
points: FY2027 is positioned as a year of product-led growth organized around three themes: (1) cyber security — convergence of agentic AI, zero-trust mandates and post-quantum risk driving enterprise demand for data security products; (2) DPI deployments in emerging and frontier markets, with several pipeline opportunities in Africa, Middle East and Asia-Pacific at advanced stages; (3) SME and banking adoption of emSigner, addressing a large untapped opportunity in India's MSME segment and across banking, via product simplification and partner-led distribution.

subsections.label: M&A strategy / bolt-on acquisitions
points: Company remains open to selective bolt-on acquisitions where they bring differentiated AI-based cybersecurity capabilities or accelerate market access.

As of now, no acquisition is in the pipeline, unlike prior two years when acquisitions happened around July-August; company will evaluate opportunities but feels current CLM/SecurePass feature sets are competitive globally.
Main area of interest for acquisition is AI integration into identity, authentication and cybersecurity suite.
If a suitable small product company is available, acquisition could occur in Q3 or Q4 of FY27; most likely such a company would be based in the US, not other geographies.
Ambition to double PAT over the next 3 years.

subsections.label: 3i Infotech dispute
points: Company clarified matters regarding the 3i Infotech dispute, but nothing has moved since; no complaint received from police or any police inquiry.
3i Infotech had stated it would file a complaint with SEBI, but company has not received anything from SEBI either.

Because 3i Infotech took actions without giving eMudhra opportunity to explain, eMudhra has sent a legal notice to 3i Infotech and its directors stating their actions were wrong; awaiting their reply.
As of the call, nothing has really progressed on either side compared to the situation 2 months prior.

subsections.label: Geopolitical disruption
points: War in the Middle East starting from February end has delayed some orders expected in March; company expects these delayed orders will still materialize, and has factored this into a slightly lower order book growth projection (2.2-2.3X vs. earlier expectation of 2X).

subsections.label: 3i Infotech dispute
points: Ongoing unresolved dispute with 3i Infotech; legal notice sent by eMudhra; no regulatory or police action has materialized either way, and situation remains stagnant.

subsections.label: Revenue recognition timing risk
points: Order intake does not automatically translate to revenue recognition; execution depends on client infrastructure and team readiness for large banks and government clients, creating timing lags between order booking and revenue recognition.

key_figures.label: Order book growth projection for next year

subsections.label: Segment-level FY27 growth breakdown
points: Services segment expected to see mostly no growth, in line with general global services trend.
Trust services expected to grow around 20% (vs 30% last year), predominantly from India.
Balance of growth predominantly expected from the enterprise product segment, estimated at 25-30% growth.

subsections.label: Guidance philosophy
points: Management stated they always want to estimate in a reasonable way rather than overestimate, noting that over the last 4-5 years, whatever guidance given has been achieved 100%.
Given the potential for unforeseen changes in the world, management gives estimates with 100% conviction rather than aggressive targets.

guidance_ledger.statement: Organic growth of around 15% to 18%, most likely 18%
Bottom line may be around between 25% to 30%, could be around 27%-28%
Ambition to double PAT over the next 3 years
Next year also, we can see 25%-30% growth definitely in the US product segment, if not more
We have projected little over 2X maybe 2.2X-2.3X the order book as the next year projection (revised down from earlier 2X due to Middle East order delays)
This year we estimate 20% will come [in trust services], vs 30% last year
The balance growth predominantly will come in the enterprise product... there the growth we estimate is almost 25% to 30%
Services, mostly no growth will come because that is in line with the general services trend across the world
This year we are estimating almost over a million dollar of profit from the Cryptas

risk_register.note: War starting from February end delayed some Middle East orders expected in March; management expects these will still materialize but has factored delay into a slightly reduced order book multiple guidance (2.2-2.3X vs prior 2X expectation).

risk_register.risk: 3i Infotech legal/regulatory dispute
risk_register.note: Dispute remains unresolved; no police or SEBI action has materialized on either side; eMudhra has sent a legal notice to 3i Infotech and directors and awaits reply; situation unchanged from 2 months prior.

risk_register.risk: Revenue recognition timing lag vs order intake
risk_register.note: Order value does not immediately convert to revenue; execution depends on large bank/government client infrastructure and team readiness, delaying revenue recognition.

risk_register.risk: India income tax circular reducing DSC requirements
risk_register.note: New income tax circular reduced requirement for digital signature certificates, but trust services still grew ~30% due to other growth drivers (combo certificates, tokens, retail, partner model).

risk_register.risk: Expanding AI-driven attack surface
risk_register.note: New AI models (e.g., Mythos) expand the attack surface by exposing previously undetected vulnerabilities, requiring enterprises to significantly improve cybersecurity posture — framed as both a risk and a demand driver for eMudhra's products.

risk_register.risk: Long European bank sales cycles
risk_register.note: Sales cycles in Europe for large banks tend to be long, affecting pace of Cryptas CLM cross-sell conversion and associated profitability uplift.

themes.label: Product-led growth / mix shift
themes.note: Increasing share of product-led revenue (CertiNext, SecurePass) drives higher gross margin, EBITDA and PAT growth versus services and trust services.

themes.label: International/US expansion
themes.note: International revenue at 64% of total, up 39% YoY; US product business grew from ~$7M to $9.5M+ with a major InCommon university consortium win.

themes.label: PQC transition
themes.note: Multiple PQC POCs underway in BFSI, defence and government segments ahead of 2029-2030 regulatory mandates to migrate off conventional algorithms.

themes.label: Agentic AI as demand driver
themes.note: AI models expand the attack surface, creating both cybersecurity risk and increased enterprise demand for eMudhra's identity/authentication and audit products.

themes.label: Middle East/Africa expansion
themes.note: Active DPI deployments and pipeline in Africa and Middle East, though war since February delayed some orders that are still expected to materialize.

themes.label: M&A / bolt-on acquisitions
themes.note: No acquisition currently in pipeline (unlike prior two years); open to selective AI-focused bolt-on acquisitions, likely US-based, possibly in Q3/Q4 FY27.

themes.label: 3i Infotech dispute
themes.note: Legal dispute with 3i Infotech remains stagnant with no regulatory or police action on either side since clarification was issued two months prior.

key_takeaways: FY2026 was a year of compounding momentum: total income of INR7,132 million, up 35% year-on-year, EBITDA of INR1,654 million, up 33%, and PAT of INR1,100 million, up 26%. Over a 5-year horizon, PAT compounded at 30.5% per annum.

Enterprise Solution accounts for 59% of revenue and grew 55% year-on-year, with organic growth of 23% and acquisitive growth of 32%. Trust services business represents 20% of revenue, up 32%. Pure Services business is 21% of revenue and remained flat.
International revenue is now 64% of total and grew nearly 39% year-on-year; operations span 15 offices across five regions serving customers in more than 35 countries.

A notable win was a large TLS certificate order for a university federation (InCommon consortium, ~700 universities) in the United States, a meaningful step in establishing credibility across US markets.
FY2027 is a year of product-led growth organized around three themes: cyber security, DPI deployments in emerging/frontier markets, and SME/banking adoption of emSigner.
Ambition is to double PAT over the next 3 years, with tailwinds from AI, data sovereignty, PQC transition and tightening compliance requirements.
FY27 guidance: organic revenue growth of ~18%, PAT growth of 25-30% (likely 27-28%), order book growth projection of 2.2X-2.3X (revised down from 2X due to Middle East order delays).
pressing_questions: Will it be possible to quantify this deal, ballpark? (regarding the InCommon consortium order) — Management declined to quantify individual deal sizes.

Isn't the guidance that you have claimed... slightly underwhelming given the kind of growth in cybersecurity that is anticipated should be far higher? — Management defended conservative guidance philosophy, citing 100% guidance achievement track record over last 4-5 years.

MANIPALHOS.about: Incorporated in 2010, Manipal Health Enterprises Limited is a healthcare service providers, operating a large network of multi-specialty hospitals, clinics, and diagnostic centres across the country.[1]

quarters.summary: Q1 FY27 was Manipal Health Enterprises' inaugural earnings call post-IPO, reporting volume-led revenue growth of over 38% YoY to INR3,091 crores and network EBITDA growth of over 26% (30%+ excluding a one-off gain in the prior year). Management guided to continued growth via bed capacity additions (~1,000 beds planned for FY27 including Electronic City, Nashik, Raipur and Kinder), ramp-up of Bengaluru greenfields, Sahyadri integration over an 18-month playbook, deleveraged balance sheet (net debt/EBITDA to fall to 0.9x post IPO debt repayment in Q2), and INR4,000 crores capex over the next 3-4 years to add 3,000 beds, while keeping an eye on inorganic opportunities in Kerala, NCR and Hyderabad.

subsections.label: Margin dip drivers (ex-Sahyadri)
points: The ex-Sahyadri margin dip from 26.5% (Q1 FY26) to 25% (Q1 FY27) is explained by two one-off factors: a one-off material cost benefit/reversal of INR15 crores relating to a pre-acquisition contract in Medica in Q1 FY26 (0.6% impact), and greenfield doctor costs in Kanakapura and Yelahanka (Bengaluru greenfields), which are fully staffed with doctors early in their life cycle (0.5% impact for the network).

Some slowness in scheme patients' collections across the sector also contributed marginally to the margin dip; management does not view these as operational issues or a sustainable trend, but as one-offs that will resolve as greenfields ramp up and collections normalize through the year.

subsections.label: Capital allocation & leverage
points: Net debt to EBITDA is currently 2.8x; post repayment of debt in Q2 FY27 (trigger already initiated post IPO funds receipt), net debt/EBITDA will fall to 0.9x at Q1 level.
Company is comfortable operating at industry-average leverage of 1.5x-2x and would only go higher for an opportunity that cannot be missed.
Company plans to spend ~INR4,000 crores of capex over the next 3-4 years to add 3,000 beds (including Mumbai/Juhu greenfield).
Current-year capex guidance is ~INR2,000 crores due to greenfields and brownfields coming up; INR900 crores already spent in Q1, front-ending capex to capture the benefit/leverage for the full year.

subsections.label: Volume-led growth philosophy
points: Growth was driven by volumes — more patients accessing care — which management considers a sustainable model for growth in care delivery, rather than a price-led (ARPOB/ALOS-led) growth strategy pursued by some peers.

subsections.label: Centres of Excellence (CoE) / CONGO-R mix
points: Six CoE specialties — Cardiac Sciences, Oncology, Neurology, Gastroenterology, Orthopaedics, Renal Sciences — continue to be a key growth driver with rising revenue contribution.

Oncology is among the fastest-growing components of the CONGO-R mix, growing nationally and not only in Delhi NCR; three greenfields commissioned in Bengaluru in the last 12 months all have comprehensive oncology facilities, supporting national oncology capacity.

CONGO mix complexity difference (not contribution) is the advantage Manipal has over Sahyadri — moving up complexity of CONGO cases in Sahyadri is the exact playbook being deployed, expected to positively impact ARPOB and other financial parameters.

subsections.label: Sahyadri integration progress
points: Integration playbook follows a fixed process taking about 16-18 months.
Regional HR structure has been put in place, mirroring the structure used for other clusters/regions.

In three key metros (Bengaluru, Kolkata, Pune) interoperability of clinicians has increased — 58 clinicians now move across both Sahyadri and Manipal brands across the nine Pune hospitals (7 ex-Sahyadri, 2 ex-Manipal).
Full brand rechristening into Manipal typically takes 14-16 months from integration date; the Manipal element has already been introduced into the Sahyadri logo/brand.
Digital penetration in Sahyadri is at an early stage (22-23% of revenue) and management is bullish on digital channels.

Other initiatives include business development in upcountry markets, internal conversion efficiency processes, infrastructure upgrades to bring hospitals up to Manipal systems, and a service strategy being put together for Sahyadri.

Volume-led growth, clinical enhancement, and operating efficiencies drove Sahyadri's EBITDA margin improvement to ~17.5% in Q1; turnaround to network-level margin will take time but priorities are in place.
Length of stay improvement (8% reduction to 2.8 days) in Sahyadri came through operating efficiencies despite increasing case complexity.

subsections.label: East region (AMRI/Medica/Columbia Asia)
points: AMRI grew 17% and Medica grew 15% YoY; management runs East as one state and Calcutta as one city combining AMRI, Medica, and Columbia Asia.
Cash and TPA business in East grew 22% despite overall East growth of 17%, as government scheme business has been flat.

A transition is underway where the current government scheme may get rechristened to a national scheme, causing a slowdown in government mix; hospitals are in discussion with authorities and expect to hear on the way forward shortly.
In the interim, brand equity is being used to attract cash and TPA patients.
Investments in East include added doctors/clinical talent; Dhakuria facility to add extra beds with a fully integrated oncology program coming on stream next quarter.

subsections.label: Out-of-hospital / digital initiatives
points: E-pharmacy, telehealth, and Manipal AI (MAI) chatbot initiatives were highlighted as part of out-of-hospital earnings, contributing to overall digital revenue of INR710 crores (23% of overall revenue) in Q1 FY27.

subsections.label: Clinical technology investments
points: Installed a linear accelerator and a PET-CT at the Nashik hospital.
Introduced optical coherence tomography at the flagship MHB Old Airport Road facility in Bangalore and two other Bangalore locations.
Commissioned an AI-assisted neuro biplane cath lab at the Mukundapur facility in Kolkata, supporting a newly launched interventional radiology program for the region.

subsections.label: Clinical milestones
points: Whitefield hospital (Bangalore) performed the world's first robotic pancreatic surgery on a 1-month-old infant.
Vijayawada hospital (Andhra Pradesh) performed the state's first emergency living-donor liver transplant.
Kanakapura (South Bangalore) and Yelahanka (North Bangalore) greenfield facilities, both in their first year of operations, completed their first robotic renal transplants.

subsections.label: Greenfield & brownfield pipeline
points: Nashik hospital commissioned a brownfield capacity addition of 103 beds along with a newly installed linear accelerator and PET-CT, increasing its overall licensed bed capacity to 307 beds.

50th hospital launched in July 2026 in Electronic City, Bangalore, along promised timelines, adding ~300 beds and marking the 13th Manipal facility in Bangalore, taking city-wide licensed capacity to nearly 3,000 beds.

Kinder Hospital acquisition in Whitefield, Bangalore adds 100 beds; deal is pending completion of a couple of conditions precedent (CPs), expected to close in the next 60 days; asset comes with land and building included, meaning no rental leakage during remodeling.

Kinder Hospital will be temporarily closed for a few months for renovation/remodeling from a women-and-children facility into a multispecialty facility (minus transplants, which will remain at the Whitefield hub); remodeling expected to take about 6-7 months / 8-9 month project timeline.
Raipur is the next large greenfield expected to come on stream towards the end of FY27 (Q4 FY27); Juhu (Mumbai) and Wakad (Pune) are subsequent greenfields in the pipeline.

Sahyadri network capacity expansion: Deccan Gymkhana undergoing expansion with an entire new tower being added; Hadapsar adding beds; Wakad (North Pune) greenfield started; Nashik added oncology capacity (100+ beds, LINAC, PET-CT); Ahilya Nagar introducing oncology capabilities, expected to add ~80 beds in FY28.

Two Bengaluru greenfields (Kanakapura in South Bangalore, Yelahanka in North Bangalore) are in their first year of operations; Kanakapura broke even at EBITDA level in its fifth month, Yelahanka broke even in its second month — both ahead of internal expectations, delivering 13% EBITDA margin in Q1, ahead of plan.

subsections.label: Sub-100-bed hospital model rationale
points: Management noted that while an ideal minimum size for an independent multispecialty hospital would be 250-300 beds, Manipal has successfully run multiple sub-100/150-bed hospitals historically (the original Columbia Asia model was largely sub-100-bedded, moved from secondary to tertiary care).

Kinder's 100-bed addition is viewed as capacity addition within an already well-served Whitefield micro-market (two existing large multispecialty hospitals), providing a 'running start'; the facility will offer full multispecialty services (cath lab, CT, MRI, theatres) barring transplants, which remain centralized at the Whitefield hub.

subsections.label: Kinder Hospital acquisition
points: Company announced a transaction to acquire the entire business operations and assets of Kinder Hospital in the Whitefield area of Bangalore, adding 100 beds; deal is not being pursued for Kinder's existing women-and-children/infertility business, which management called 'frankly irrelevant' to the rationale — the acquisition is purely about capacity addition in the high-growth Whitefield micro-market where Manipal already runs two large, high-performing multispecialty hospitals (Whitefield and Varthur).

Manipal already has infertility capability in its existing Whitefield hospital, so Kinder's infertility/obs-gynae specialty will not be retained; the hospital will be temporarily closed for renovation and reopened as a multispecialty extension of the existing Whitefield/Varthur quaternary care capability.
Transaction includes land and building, eliminating rental costs during and after remodeling; expected to close within next 60 days pending CPs.

subsections.label: Sahyadri acquisition integration philosophy
points: Management follows a set 'playbook' for acquisitions/integration that has worked in past acquisitions (AMRI, Medica, Columbia Asia), involving capital investment, advanced technology, doctor interoperability, conversion efficiencies, CONGO mix improvement and service standards — being applied to Sahyadri.
Sahyadri came in as an under-managed asset with low EBITDA margin (17% now vs 25% for ex-Sahyadri network); management has confidence in replicating the past turnaround playbook.

subsections.label: Corporate structure / focus
points: Despite a regulatory change permitting for-profit entities to run medical colleges (and a peer entering that business), management has no plans to bring medical college operations into the listed entity; intends to remain focused on providing tertiary/quaternary brick-and-mortar hospital care and remain a specialty provider with high-acuity Centres of Excellence focus.

subsections.label: Inorganic growth aspirations
points: Company has keen interest to expand into Kerala as and when an opportunity arises, further expand presence in NCR, and look at Hyderabad — inorganic opportunities viewed as an additional growth lever beyond existing committed capacity expansion.

subsections.label: Collections / payer mix
points: Scheme patients' collections have been a little slow across the whole sector in Q1, contributing marginally to the margin dip; expected to improve as the year progresses.
Government/institutional payer mix (~14%) tends to be associated with a higher ALOS.

In the East region, a transition is underway where the current government scheme may be rechristened into a national scheme, causing a slowdown in government-mix growth; timeline for resolution is uncertain but hospitals are in discussion with authorities and expect an update shortly.

subsections.label: Greenfield ramp-up costs
points: Greenfield doctor costs at Kanakapura and Yelahanka (Bengaluru) are elevated in the early part of their operational life as they are fully staffed with doctors, temporarily dragging down composite network margin by about 0.5 percentage points.

subsections.label: Growth levers outlined by management
points: Largest bed capacity in the country (13,000+ beds), with 1,000+/2,000+ beds coming on stream in a short period, providing headroom for capacity-led growth.
Low ALOS combined with 65% occupancy provides headroom to grow occupancy further within the current network before needing new capacity.
CONGO-R / Centres of Excellence high-acuity mix continuing to grow as a key margin and growth lever.
Sahyadri margin improvement lever — from 17% currently towards ex-Sahyadri network margin of 25%.
Ramp-up of greenfields — three already commissioned in Bengaluru in the last 10 months, plus Raipur (end of FY27), followed by Juhu (Mumbai) and Wakad (Pune).
Continued operating efficiency improvements in material cost, length of stay, conversion efficiencies, and digital revenue.

Deleveraged balance sheet post-IPO (0.9x net debt/EBITDA) provides ability to raise funds for expansion into new geographies (Kerala, NCR, Hyderabad) as an inorganic lever, separate from the other organic levers.

Management declined to guide to a specific core network growth number or specific margin target/timeline, characterizing current trends (volume-led growth, CONGO-R mix, ARPOB improvement) as secular tailwinds rather than one-offs.
Several hospitals in the portfolio already operate at >30-32% margin, indicating room for the broader network to converge upward, though no specific number or timeline was given.

For FY27, three major bed-capacity initiatives are expected: Electronic City (~300 beds, Q2 FY27), Nashik (103 beds, already added), and Raipur (Q4 FY27); Kinder (100 beds) might also come into FY27 if accelerated. Ahilya Nagar (~80 beds) is expected in FY28.

guidance_ledger.statement: Company laid out a plan to add about 1,000 beds in fiscal '27, in a staggered/phased manner via Electronic City (~300 beds), Nashik (103 beds already added), Raipur (Q4 FY27), and potentially Kinder (100 beds) if accelerated.
Ahilya Nagar could add about close to 80 beds in FY28.
As the company adds 3,000 beds over the next 3-4 years (including Mumbai greenfield), it will spend around INR4,000 crores of capex.
Current year, company will end up spending almost INR2,000 crores of capex because of greenfields and brownfields coming up; INR900 crores already spent in Q1.
Once debt is repaid in Quarter 2 (trigger already initiated post IPO funds), net debt to EBITDA will go down to 0.9x at quarter 1 level.
Company is fairly comfortable operating at industry-average leverage of 1.5x to 2x; would only go higher due to an opportunity that cannot be missed.
Not guiding to a specific core network growth number, but Q1 trends (volume-led growth, CONGO-R mix, ARPOB improvement) are secular tailwinds expected to sustain, not one-offs.

Management does not want to indicate a specific number or timeline for margin expansion, but greenfields ramping up and Sahyadri improvement are expected to pull up composite portfolio margin toward levels seen in mature hospitals (>30-32% margin in several hospitals).

guidance_ledger.metric: Sahyadri EBITDA margin convergence to network average
guidance_ledger.statement: Integration process takes about 16 to 18 months; reaching network-level EBITDA margin is 'sometime away' but expected to progress via operational efficiencies, clinical talent, out-of-hospital initiatives, and business development.
Full-fledged rechristening into Manipal brand usually takes about 14 to 16 months from the day of integration; dates are being decided.
Transition of scheme mix (current scheme to national scheme) is 'on the anvil'; hospitals are in discussion with authorities and should hear from them very shortly on the way forward.
Company has keen interest to expand to Kerala as and when an opportunity arises, further expand presence in NCR, and look at Hyderabad — as inorganic growth opportunities.
Kinder Hospital will be temporarily closed for a few months for renovations (an 8-9 month project) before reopening as a multispecialty facility; transfer expected within next 60 days pending CPs.

risk_register.risk: Scheme/institutional patient collections slow across the sector
risk_register.note: Scheme patients' collections have been a little slow in Q1 as the whole sector has been talking about; expected to improve as the year progresses.

risk_register.risk: Greenfield ramp-up costs (doctor cost) dragging composite margin
risk_register.note: Greenfield doctor costs at Kanakapura and Yelahanka added about 0.5 percentage points drag on network margin as facilities are fully staffed with doctors early in life; expected to normalize as greenfields ramp up.

risk_register.risk: Government scheme mix transition in East region
risk_register.note: East region government scheme may get rechristened from the current scheme to a national scheme, causing a slowdown in the government payer mix; matter is on the anvil with authorities and should get closed shortly.

risk_register.risk: Government/institutional payer mix associated with higher ALOS
risk_register.note: Institutional/government payer mix (~14%) tends to be associated with a higher average length of stay compared to cash/insurance patients.

themes.label: Volume-led growth
themes.note: Growth was driven by volumes — more patients accessing care — considered by management a sustainable model versus price-led (ARPOB/ALOS) growth.

themes.label: Sahyadri integration
themes.note: Sahyadri EBITDA margin improved to ~17.5% in Q1 through doctor interoperability, conversion efficiencies, CONGO mix and service standards, on an 16-18 month integration playbook.

themes.label: Greenfield ramp-up
themes.note: Bengaluru greenfields (Kanakapura, Yelahanka) broke even ahead of plan and delivered 13% EBITDA margin in Q1, though early doctor costs dented composite margin by 0.5pp.

themes.label: Capacity expansion / bed additions
themes.note: ~1,000 beds targeted for FY27 via Electronic City, Nashik, Raipur and Kinder; INR4,000 crores capex planned over next 3-4 years for 3,000 beds.

themes.label: CONGO-R / high-acuity mix
themes.note: Centres of Excellence revenue contribution rose to 65% with 45% IP revenue growth; oncology mix rising from 10.8% to 12.2% at network level.

themes.label: Deleveraging post-IPO
themes.note: Net debt/EBITDA to fall from 2.8x to 0.9x post Q2 FY27 debt repayment, providing headroom for further expansion including inorganic opportunities.

themes.label: Payer mix / scheme collections
themes.note: Slow scheme patient collections sector-wide and a pending government scheme transition in the East region are near-term headwinds being monitored.

key_takeaways: Our Q1 revenue of INR3,091 crores represents a growth of over 38% year-on-year. Our network EBITDA was INR749 crores, a growth of over 26% over last year. Excluding a one-off gain that we had in the first quarter of last year, the growth is over 30%.
Our operating margin excluding Sahyadri was 25%, and at a network level that includes Sahyadri Hospitals, is at 24.2% for the quarter.

Our inpatient volumes grew by about 39%, and OP volumes by 26% over Q1 of last year. Average occupancy across our network was 65%, a 290 bps increase over Q1 of last year, while we maintained an industry-leading ALOS of just 2.7 days.
Our digital revenue grew significantly and contributed about INR710 crores during the quarter, representing about 23% of our overall revenue.
Our Centres of Excellence... continue to be a key growth driver, their revenue contribution rising to about 65% in Q1 of FY27. During this quarter, IP revenues across these specialties grew by 45%.
Sahyadri reported revenue of INR332 crores in Quarter 1, a growth of over 13% compared to last year. EBITDA for the quarter was INR58 crores, a growth of about 19% year-on-year.
We launched our 50th hospital along the promised timelines in the last month, in the month of July, and it added about 300 beds more to our licensed capacity.
The company announced a transaction to acquire the entire business operations and assets of Kinder Hospital in the Whitefield area of Bangalore.

HEG.about: HEG Ltd is a leading manufacturer and exporter of graphite electrodes in India. It operates the largest single-site integrated graphite electrodes plant in the world.[1] It is a part of LNJ Bhilwara Group which also has presence across IT Enabled services, power generation & textiles.[2]

quarters.summary: HEG delivered a strong Q1 FY27 with double-digit revenue growth and sharp EBITDA/PAT expansion YoY and sequentially, despite a marginal decline in volumes and continued geopolitical/cost headwinds. Management expects >90% capacity utilization to continue in coming quarters, gradual price increases from October onwards to cover rising needle coke and other input costs, continued progress on the HEG Advanced Materials demerger (awaiting NCLT pronouncement), and long-term positive demand outlook driven by EAF capacity additions and decarbonization trends. Greentech (TACC anode project and Bhilwara Energy hydro/solar) is expected to scale to a 4-digit EBITDA by 2030.

subsections.label: Drivers of profitability improvement
points: Revenue growth and margin expansion driven by improved realization from product and geographical mix, disciplined cost management, and continued focus on operational excellence, despite a marginal decline in volumes.
Sequential recovery from Q4 FY26 losses (driven by MTM loss in foreign equity investments) to strong Q1 FY27 profitability.
Segmental profit jump attributed to improvement in realization while needle coke costs remained on old stock levels.

subsections.label: Balance sheet & capital allocation
points: Company remains debt-free with no long-term loan borrowings.
Strong liquidity position (treasury ~INR858 crores) provides financial flexibility to pursue future growth opportunities while maintaining resilience across business cycles.
Other income of INR43 crores includes fair valuation gain on investments (shown in segmental reporting) in addition to interest income of INR7-8 crores.

subsections.label: Booking cycle and pricing lag
points: Electrode companies are typically booked 3-4 months ahead; new price hikes will only start showing up from October onward as company is committed up to September.
New business being booked in existing markets (India and elsewhere) is at higher prices even though bulk of near-term volume is already committed at older prices.
Company is booked more or less fully for the next 1-2 quarters, limiting near-term ability to pass on rising input costs.

subsections.label: TACC (anode) contracting
points: TACC is negotiating 3-5 year contracts with customers; about 70% of the contracts (in terms of capacity) are expected to be closed within the next 1-1.5 months.
These will be long-term contracts with top Tier-1 players across the world.

subsections.label: Middle East / diversification impact
points: Middle East represented around 20% of revenue over the year; despite war-related disruption, no volume was lost in Q1 as the company operated in excess of 91% utilization.
Diversification across ~30+ countries allowed temporary shipping delays to be absorbed without material volume loss.
Management declined to disclose specific market-by-market volume shifts, citing competitive sensitivity, but noted such shifts happen quarter-to-quarter and are not unusual.

subsections.label: U.S. exposure and regulatory risk
points: U.S. represents less than about 10% of HEG's business; company has not engaged in dumping.
CVD preliminary results expected by end July, anti-dumping determination by end September.

Management intends to retain presence in U.S. given higher prices there, even if some market share is lost; diversified market presence makes it possible to absorb volumes elsewhere if punitive duties are imposed.

subsections.label: Global graphite electrode market structure
points: Management disputes analyst estimate that the Chinese share of the ~600 Kt UHP electrode market is around 1/3 (200,000 tons), suggesting the actual figure is much less, maybe half of that estimate.

Steel industry utilization globally is currently less than 75%; pricing improvement is linked to return of steel demand and to new electric arc furnace capacity coming online, since no new blast furnace capacity is being added in Europe or the U.S.

subsections.label: Capacity utilization performance
points: Plant operated at average capacity utilization of more than 90% during the quarter, reflecting strong operating efficiency; expected to continue operating above 90% in forthcoming quarters.

Capacity utilization during the quarter stood at 90%+, marginally lower than the corresponding period of last year, but impact of lower volumes was offset by better realization, improved operating efficiencies and effective cost management.
Management does not see headroom beyond 94-95% utilization as reaching 100% requires ideal conditions which are never fully achieved; expects to close the year between 90% and 95%.

subsections.label: Capacity expansion rationale
points: 100,000 tons per annum plant remains the world's largest single-location plant; its scale and cost-efficient operations place HEG among the most competitive producers globally.
Further expansion to 115,000 tons is on track for commissioning by early 2028, widening the capacity gap versus the next two largest global plants (~70,000 tons each).
Expansion validated by OECD steel outlook showing ~71 million tons of new EAF steelmaking capacity planned globally for completion by end 2028.

subsections.label: EAF capacity tracking
points: Management is tracking each new EAF facility globally; delays of a few weeks/months or early implementation in some cases are practical given these are $1-2 billion greenfield projects.
Estimates of new EAF capacity additions over the next 2-3 years and into 2029-2030 are considered broadly correct, with a possible variance of plus/minus 10-20%.

EAF capacity commissioned combined in 2024-2025 stood at 20-21 million metric tons, with 8-10 million metric tons commissioned in H1 CY26 alone; ~60 million metric tons expected over CY2026-2028, and 25-30 million tons already commissioned over the trailing 3-5 quarters.

subsections.label: TACC (anode/Greentech) capex phasing
points: Of the total INR2,200-2,300 crores anode project capex, 40% has already been spent; the larger amount will be spent over the next 3 quarters.
Company expects 90-95% of payment to be completed by FY27 with the balance 10% in Q1 FY28.

Land currently held is capable of supporting around 30,000 tons of capacity; upon completing the current 20,000-ton project, company will consider expanding by another 10,000 tons at an incremental capex of ~INR800 crores, targeted for 2029 (not before).

Anode project targeted payback of 4-5 years on capex; TACC debt secured to date stands at INR1,240 crores from SBI, with gross debt expected to reach ~INR1,500 crores by 31 March 2027; future 30,000-ton phase carries a total capex of INR3,100 crores to be financed on a 70-30 debt-equity structure.

subsections.label: Bhilwara Energy / Greentech capacity build-out
points: Two existing hydro plants (300 MW combined) are debt-free and generate free cash flow of INR320-350 crores per year.
New 75 MW hydro project acquired from previous partner Statkraft; ~30% of work already completed, enabling commissioning in 2.5 years versus normal 4-5 year hydro build timeline.
New 300 MW DC solar C&I project expected to commence operations within the next 18 months.

Hydro projects are run-of-the-river IPPs with 30-40% peak power sold at higher rates (up to INR7-10/unit) versus regular power around INR4/unit, yielding a weighted average realization of around INR5.5+/unit.

subsections.label: Global steel market backdrop
points: Global steel production showed signs of gradual stabilization in H1 CY26, indicating contraction is bottoming out and demand beginning to find its floor.
Steel production outside China remained highly resilient, expanding after many years, representing a supportive demand environment for HEG's products.
HEG does not sell electrodes directly to China, but Chinese domestic steel market dynamics continue to influence global pricing.

Weak Chinese real estate sector has forced domestic mills to export surplus steel production; despite an easing versus the 2025 peak, exports remain at historically elevated levels, prompting a broad wave of defensive trade measures (anti-dumping, safeguard duties) across the U.S., EU and India.
India remained one of the strongest performing steel markets, supported by robust domestic demand for infrastructure, construction and manufacturing.
Matured economies (U.S., Germany) saw a solid broad-based recovery; Vietnam posted exceptional growth, cementing its position as a major Southeast Asian steel powerhouse.

subsections.label: Export mix and market diversification
points: HEG exports continue to be in the region of 70-75% of sales, a pattern consistent over the last 25-30 years, spanning the smallest African/Latin American markets to the largest consuming markets (U.S. and Europe).
Diversification across ~30 countries enabled the company to offset any temporary Middle East-related shipping delays without losing volume.

subsections.label: Needle coke and input cost pass-through timing
points: Rising raw material costs (needle coke, energy, shipping/freight) are gradually getting reflected in input costs; company managing these developments through operational efficiencies.

Needle coke and other input cost increases will not have an immediate P&L effect, as companies typically carry 3-4 months of stock and conversion of needle coke to electrode is itself a 3-4 month process; impact expected toward the end of the year (around November-January).
As the company is currently unbooked for the affected future quarter, it will raise prices for that period to cover the cost rise.
Middle East war has materially impacted energy prices globally, disrupted world trade, and pushed shipping costs and transit times disproportionately higher in some cases.
Needle coke prices have risen by a ballpark $200-300/ton since the Middle East disruption began, equating to roughly 10-15% of total electrode production cost.

subsections.label: Competitive pricing landscape
points: Two competitors (an American company and a Japanese company) have announced steep price increases in the last 6-7 weeks (respectively $600-1,200/ton and $930/ton), reflecting industry-wide cost pressure (raw materials, oil, shipping).

Only 3-4 major global graphite electrode producers exist; HEG expects to follow suit with price increases given rising own costs, but nothing substantial expected in the next 1-2 quarters as the industry is largely booked.
Management declined to comment on whether GrafTech's and Tokai Carbon's announced price hikes are being absorbed by steelmakers, stating this will only be known in the next 1-2 quarters.
As an industry, all producers need a price increase given rising energy costs, ocean freight and needle coke costs.
Media commentary indicated realized price improvement of 7-8% in Q1 FY27.

subsections.label: Pricing strategy and margin protection
points: Company aims to maintain current margins (approximately 28-29% including other income, consistent between the last quarter and this quarter) and expects to have a higher margin than peers.

New business booked in various markets is at higher prices; company is testing various markets/customers/price points and expects to know within 1-2 months what average price increase can be achieved.
Management declined to specify exact dollar-per-ton price increase targets on the call, citing competitive sensitivity.

subsections.label: Market structure debate
points: An analyst's estimate that the global UHP electrode market is ~600 Kt with ~1/3 supplied by China was disputed by management, who suggested the Chinese supply share is much lower (maybe half of the estimate).
Pricing improvement is expected to be tied to the return of steel demand and to new EAF capacity additions, since no new blast furnace capacity is being built in Europe or the U.S.

subsections.label: Composite scheme of arrangement / demerger
points: The composite scheme of arrangement (HEG Advanced Materials demerger) is progressing well; NCLT has reserved its order and the company is awaiting pronouncement.

Company will provide an update shortly on the timeline for effecting the scheme and the record date, and will hold a dedicated investor call to explain the HEG Advanced Materials business once the order is pronounced and received.

Post-consolidation, the Greentech entity will have around 32.9 crore outstanding shares (up from current HEG's ~19.7-19.8 crore), with ~13 crore additional shares to be issued to Singularity and to promoter/RSWM shareholders in BEL; no fresh issuance of shares is expected after this routing. Both tranches of Singularity investment are already covered within the 32.9 crore share count.

subsections.label: Bhilwara Energy (BEL) structure and funding
points: BEL owns 51% of Malana Power entity; the balance 49% (previously held by Statkraft) was acquired for ~INR1,200 crores, funded 50% via commercial bank borrowing and 50% partly from the family office and partly from BEL.
BEL itself is a debt-free company and has been so for a number of years.

Of the total debt, INR600 crores already sits in BEL's subsidiary books; company expects to retire these debts by the time of merger with the Greentech entity, so no additional debt is expected to be added to the merged books from this transaction.

TACC's own debt (separate from BEL) currently stands at INR1,240 crores secured from SBI, with balance funded by own capital/internal accruals; by 31 March 2027, gross TACC debt is expected to reach ~INR1,500 crores; further debt for FY29 capacity expansion (targeting a 70-30 debt-equity structure) will be decided based on need.

subsections.label: Greentech business potential (TACC anode + Bhilwara Energy)
points: TACC anode project to start commercial production in Q1 of next fiscal year, ramping from 40-50% utilization in year 1 (generating INR600-700 crores revenue) to over INR1,200 crores in year 2 and INR1,500-1,600 crores in year 3, at an EBITDA margin of around 35% across all three years.

Bhilwara Energy's 2 existing hydro plants (300 MW) generate INR320-350 crores of free cash flow annually as they are debt-free; additional planned hydro (75 MW, by 2030) and solar (300 MW DC, within 18 months) projects are expected to add a combined ~INR200 crores of EBITDA.
Combining anode and energy businesses, HEG Greentech is targeting a 4-digit (i.e., over INR1,000 crores) EBITDA by the year 2030.

subsections.label: Geopolitical and trade risk
points: War in the Middle East has materially impacted energy prices, disrupted world trade, and pushed shipping costs and transit times disproportionately higher in some cases.
Changes in U.S. trade policy (tariffs, country/product-specific measures) are disrupting established global trade channels.
Various changes in trade policy across countries and ongoing geopolitical tensions remain key sources of near-term uncertainty.
U.S. regulatory action: CVD preliminary results expected by end July, anti-dumping determination by end September; outcome remains uncertain, though management states HEG has not engaged in dumping.

Sustained elevated Chinese steel exports have prompted defensive trade measures (anti-dumping, safeguard duties) in the U.S., EU and India, which could affect global steel and electrode market dynamics.

subsections.label: Input cost risk
points: Rising raw material costs — needle coke, energy, ocean freight — are gradually getting reflected in input costs, pressuring margins until prices can be repriced (with a 3-5 month lag).

Needle coke prices have risen by a ballpark $200-300/ton since the Middle East disruption began, equating to roughly 10-15% of total electrode production cost; further increases are being watched quarter by quarter.

subsections.label: Market structure / demand risk
points: Global steel industry utilization is less than 75%, and Western (non-HEG) graphite electrode players are operating at lower utilization (60-65% per an analyst's estimate), raising questions about whether pricing can improve amid a perceived supply surplus.
Pricing improvement is contingent on return of steel demand growth and on new electric arc furnace capacity additions.

subsections.label: Capacity and utilization outlook
points: Management expects to continue operating above 90% capacity utilization in forthcoming quarters, closing FY27 in the 90-95% range; management stated they will produce at 90-95% utilization 'come what may.'
115,000-ton capacity expansion remains on track and should be operational by early 2028, widening HEG's scale advantage over the next two largest global plants.

subsections.label: Pricing outlook
points: Price hikes from HEG are expected to start showing effect from October onward as current bookings run through September; magnitude not specified but management intends to at least cover cost increases and improve margins if possible.
Company declined to give specific dollar-per-ton guidance, noting it will take 1-2 months to know the average price increase achievable across various markets.
Needle coke cost increases (10-15% of production cost) will start affecting P&L toward the end of the year (roughly November-January) given the long stock/processing cycle.

subsections.label: Margin outlook
points: Management intends to maintain margins at levels seen in Q1 FY27 (~28-29% including other income), stating there is 'not much difference' expected quarter to quarter, and expects to sustain a higher margin than competitors.

subsections.label: Demerger timeline outlook
points: Company awaiting NCLT pronouncement on the composite scheme of arrangement; will provide timeline update on record date and hold an investor call on HEG Advanced Materials once the order is received.

subsections.label: Greentech outlook
points: TACC anode project targeted to reach FY29 at 100% capacity utilization following ramp from ~40% utilization in FY28.
HEG Greentech (TACC + Bhilwara Energy) targeting a combined 4-digit EBITDA by 2030.

guidance_ledger.statement: Operated the plant at average capacity utilization of more than 90% during the quarter, reflecting strong operating efficiency and expect to continue operating at more than 90% in the forthcoming quarters as well.
We think we'll close the year between 90% to 95%; no more headroom beyond 94% or 95% because conditions are never ideal.
Further expansion that we are currently undertaking to reach 115,000 tons is on track and should be in operation by early 2028.

Whatever price hikes will come in later will actually start showing up later in the year (October onwards); new business booked at higher prices; we will follow peers who have announced steep price increases, but nothing substantial in the next 1-2 quarters as mostly booked.
We will be able to maintain the margins that we are now talking about (28-29% including other income) and we will have a higher margin than anybody else.
The rise in needle coke costs will start taking effect towards the end of the year; as we are unbooked for that quarter, we will be raising prices for the end of the year to cover the rise in cost.
NCLT has reserved its order and the company is awaiting pronouncement; will provide an update shortly on the timeline of effecting the scheme and the record date.

Expect revenue of around INR600-700 crores in the first year at 40-50% utilization, ramping up to more than INR1,200 crores in year 2 and crossing around INR1,500-1,600 crores in year 3, with EBITDA margin of roughly 35% across all three years.
FY28 would be kind of 40% capacity utilization; FY29 will be 100% there.
For the anode project, it will start commercial production Q1 of next year.
Out of the entire INR2,200 crores, 40% is already spent; larger amount to be spent in next 3 quarters; hoping entire 90-95% payment done by FY27 and balance 10% in Q1 FY28.
As soon as current 20,000 ton project is complete, will quickly decide on expanding by 10,000 tons more at a capex of around INR800 crores; facility would come up by 2029, not before.
Plan to put up one more hydro project totaling 75 MW, which will start operations by 2030 (2.5 years from today).
One solar project of 300-megawatt DC capacity C&I project, which will start operation in the next 18 months.
By the year 2030, HEG Greentech should be aiming at a 4-digit EBITDA between all the businesses combined.

In these 3 years '26, '27, '28, we are talking about almost 60 million metric tons to come; between 25-30 million tons has already come in the last 3-4-5 quarters; 8-10 million metric tons already come up in H1.

risk_register.risk: Rising input costs (needle coke, energy, freight)

risk_register.risk: Middle East geopolitical conflict / Strait of Hormuz disruption
risk_register.note: Caused order postponements (~20% of annual sales region), freight cost spikes from $20-30 to $200-300 per ton, and force majeure letters to affected customers.

risk_register.risk: Needle coke price/availability risk tied to crude oil
risk_register.note: Crude oil rally could push needle coke prices up; no clarity yet, expected around mid-June 2026 when next quarter's contracts are negotiated; current coverage only till September via existing shipments.

risk_register.risk: Energy and freight cost inflation
risk_register.note: Energy and freight costs have risen, prompting need for price increases; absorbed with a lag due to long production/shipping cycles.

risk_register.risk: US anti-dumping/countervailing duty investigation

risk_register.risk: Regional order/pricing mix volatility
risk_register.note: Quarter-to-quarter margin/price movement driven by which regional orders ship in a given quarter, not underlying price weakness; expected to normalize by April-June.

risk_register.note: Only three-four needle coke suppliers globally (Japan, US); no new greenfield capacity built in ~70-80 years, raising future supply risk if demand surges.

themes.label: Capacity expansion & cost leadership
themes.note: HEG's 100,000 ton plant remains the world's largest single-location facility, running at >90% utilization; expansion to 115,000 tons on track for early 2028, widening the gap versus next-largest ~70,000 ton plants.

key_takeaways: We have begun the financial year on a strong note, delivering a meaningful improvement in profitability despite a marginal decline in volumes.
On a stand-alone basis, revenue from operations increased by 11% on a year-on-year basis to INR681 crores compared with INR613 crores in Q1 of the previous year.
Stand-alone EBITDA increased by 38% on a year-on-year basis to INR211 crores from INR154 crores, with EBITDA margins also improved to 29% compared with 23% in the corresponding quarter of last year.
Stand-alone profit after tax increased by 53% on a year-on-year basis to INR110 crores from INR72 crores, while consolidated profit after tax increased by 23% to INR122 crores from INR100 crores.
Capacity utilization during the quarter stood at 90% plus, which is marginally lower than the corresponding period of last year.
The company remains debt-free with no long-term loan borrowings, and our treasury stood at approximately INR858 crores as of 30th June 2026.
The composite scheme of the arrangement is progressing very well. The NCLT has reserved its order and the company is awaiting pronouncement of the order.

The medium- to long-term outlook for graphite electrodes demand remains highly positive, supported by decarbonization policies including EU's carbon border adjustment mechanism (CBAM), and approximately 71 million tons of new electric arc furnace steelmaking capacity planned globally for completion between now and end of 2028.
pressing_questions: How much was the share of Middle East in Q1 and which region did we divert lost volumes?

If we have had 20% roughly volumes from Middle East market over the years, then can you elaborate a little bit which markets we have diverted those volumes to where you see the better demand and has absorbed your balance volumes? And also, you can quantify, if possible, how much the Middle East volumes have de-grown by?

In terms of both CVD and ADD regulatory action being planned in the U.S. market, what rate in your internal assumptions would you have considered so that the U.S. volumes for us continue to hold or grow?
What have you contracted on the new bookings in dollar-per-ton basis? And what percentage of your second half volumes is now booked at this level?

The way the market is structured with Western capacity utilization still in the range of 60-65%, what gives us the confidence that the pricing can improve when the market is still sort of in a supply surplus?

If U.S. market sort of levies the ADD or something, that market could become relatively less lucrative for us. So then would we be more dependent on the demand coming up in Europe, which will decide where the prices would move and whether we can benefit from it?

quarters.summary: Management flagged mixed near-term conditions (Middle East disruption, rupee depreciation, cost inflation) but reiterated a structurally positive long-term outlook for electric arc furnace steelmaking and graphite electrode demand, driven by decarbonization and trade regionalization (CBAM, Section 232). Q1-Q2 FY27 EBITDA margin guided at ~20%, with full-year FY27 also expected at (+20%). Price hikes are being pursued for unbooked orders from H2 FY27 onward, with orders booked till September 2026 already. The composite scheme of arrangement (demerger) is progressing, with NCLT approval expected in Q2 FY27.

subsections.label: Full Year Performance Drivers
points: Improvement in PBT and net profit came from higher volumes, better control on input costs and focused monitoring on all fixed costs.
Operating margins remained stable in the range of 15% to 20% during the year, with more than 90% capacity utilization during the year.
Company remains financially strong with no long-term debt as of 31st March 2026, and a treasury of around INR 792 crores.

subsections.label: Quarterly Loss Explanation
points: Q4 loss of INR 189 crores is mainly attributable to fair value impact on foreign investment (GrafTech stake) and rapid depreciation of rupee (5% within the quarter).
These are entirely unrealized losses, taken as per applicable Indian Accounting Standards.
Excluding the unrealized losses, operating margins for the quarter are intact and reasonably comparable with previous quarters.
Other expenses appear higher versus previous quarter due to fair valuation losses and FX exchange loss from rapid rupee depreciation being classified there.
Other income was lower in the quarter due to the fair valuation loss being classified under other expenses; going forward expected to be in line with previous quarters.
Unrealized FX loss is expected to reverse if rupee appreciates; some reversal could be seen in the next quarter.

subsections.label: Rupee depreciation impact on business
points: Company gains from rupee depreciation as a net exporter; foreign exchange outgo is mainly on account of needle coke, which is a smaller part compared to total realization.
Management declined to share specific numbers on dollar-denominated cost proportion versus rupee-denominated costs when asked to quantify net benefit retained from rupee depreciation.

subsections.label: Margin/mix commentary
points: Gross margin contraction per ton Q-on-Q attributed to order mix shuffling due to Middle East war disruption — some Middle East orders postponed and other orders substituted in that quarter.
Logistic costs are much lower for Middle East shipments versus other regions, contributing to mix-driven margin movement.
Management clarified pricing itself did not change; it was about which regional orders shipped in the quarter.

subsections.label: Booking cycle and pricing process
points: Company books orders for three to six months in advance; as of the call, booked almost up until September.
For unbooked orders, company is looking at price increases, with quantum depending on region and what steel companies can absorb, and on competitor pricing.
Aim towards H2 FY27 is to have a price increase not only to protect margins but to help improve them further.
All new inquiries are being priced taking into account increased costs; company offering increased prices in the market for uncommitted volumes.
Quantum of price increase is difficult to specify (could be $300-$500 range mentioned qualitatively) and depends on regional absorption and peer group pricing actions.

subsections.label: Middle East disruption impact on order flow
points: Orders from Kuwait, Saudi and other Middle East customers had to be postponed due to disruption; other customer orders given precedence instead.
As soon as the Strait of Hormuz opens and business normalizes, pending Middle East orders will be shipped quickly.

Middle East steel companies are desperate to keep plants running and are willing to pay $200-$300 extra per ton for electrodes trucked to their plants (via ocean to a port then trucked), versus normal $20-$30 freight cost, since closing a steel plant is far costlier.

Force majeure letters were sent to Middle East customers where impacted by freight cost increases from $20-30 to over $300; those customers are taking material FOB Mumbai and paying extra freight themselves.
Freight costs have also increased for US and Europe but not yet at a level requiring contract renegotiation — still absorbable.

subsections.label: Volume/pricing quarter dynamics
points: Q4 saw slightly lower volume (~1000 tons) and some price depression purely due to regional sales mix / order mix, not underlying price weakness; expected to recover quickly by April-June.
Between Q3 and Q4, sales volume impacted by about 1000 tons due to postponed orders; most postponements were diverted rather than lost.

subsections.label: TACC (Greentech/battery materials) customer qualification
points: Pilot plant for sampling was set up more than 18 months back; good progress made with leading OEMs across the world.
Indian cell capacity appears delayed, but company is actively working with Indian OEMs as well as global companies like LG, Panasonic, CATL, at different stages of sampling.
Sampling work is going extremely well, as is plant commissioning; no change in plant commissioning date from April.
Expect a decent 40% to 60% capacity utilization in the first year itself due to ongoing customer acquisitions; no technology bottlenecks currently being faced.

subsections.label: Needle coke vs battery-grade coke technical distinction
points: Needle coke is technology-based product; no new greenfield needle coke plant or new entrant globally in ~70-80 years.
Graphite electrode production requires only this specific needle coke from the three-four existing suppliers, with no substitute available.

Battery/anode applications use needle coke as one of several (six-nine) raw material inputs and can substitute it with other materials if price rises sharply, unlike graphite electrode manufacturing which has no substitute.

There is a separate anode-grade coke that these same companies also produce, distinct from needle coke used for electrodes; abundant needle coke supply during recent low electrode industry utilization periods indicates battery demand was not absorbing needle coke supply as some feared.

subsections.label: Bhopal Plant
points: Plant near Bhopal remains the largest single-site location of electrode plants anywhere in the world, with capacity of 100,000 tons.
This makes HEG one of the most cost-competitive companies due to its size and location in India.

Company operates at healthy utilization levels, probably the highest globally, averaging more than 90% for the whole year as well as the past three-four immediate quarters, based on expanded 100,000-ton capacity, reflecting strong operational efficiency, low cost and disciplined planning.

subsections.label: Expansion progress
points: Construction of the additional 15,000-ton expansion (taking capacity to 115,000 tons) is progressing as planned, targeted for completion by early 2028.
This expansion will further strengthen ability to serve incremental global demand at a competitive cost.
Except HEG's expansion, nobody else globally has announced any new capacity as yet; it takes two to three years to even make a small brownfield expansion.

subsections.label: Global capacity backdrop
points: Over the last 40-50 years of the graphite electrode industry globally, except HEG, there has not been any new expansion anywhere else in the world (India, Europe, America or Japan); capacities have on the contrary shrunk in the last four-five years.

Needle coke: no new greenfield needle coke plant has been built anywhere in the world in the last ~78 years and no new entrant in 70-80 years; only three-four suppliers exist globally, from Japan and US.

subsections.label: Regional trade dynamics
points: Regionalization of steel trade accelerating, driven by rising protectionist measures globally in response to structural overcapacity, particularly in China.
Measures include Section 232 in US, anti-dumping and safeguard actions in Canada, Mexico, India, Brazil and similar steps across other regions, reshaping trade flows.
In Europe, Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM) imposes a carbon tax on steel imports, incentivizing lower-emission steel production/export, achievable only via electric arc furnace route.

EU's upcoming tariff rate quota regime, effective as early as 1 July 2026, expected to further restrict steel imports into EU and increase EU's own steel production, which has been declining quarter after quarter.
Europe already 50-55% EAF-based and adding at least 25-30 million tons of new EAF capacity, some already commissioned, some under construction.

subsections.label: Steel industry macro backdrop
points: Global crude steel production decline is mainly China-driven; China typically produces more in Q4/Q1 then tapers in Q3/Q4 to align with environmental and policy targets (close to about a billion tons annual production).
US saw modest growth driven by steady industrial demand; Europe remained relatively muted; Japan, Brazil and several other large steel producing countries were broadly flat to slightly negative.
India continues to be a standout performer, supported by strong infrastructure and construction activities.
China continues to face domestic demand pressure resulting in elevated export levels, impacting global pricing and driving trade protection measures worldwide.
Geopolitical tensions from Middle East conflicts are contributing to volatility in energy markets and supply chains.

subsections.label: China UHP export competition debate
points: Analyst cited GrafTech commentary that Chinese players supply about one-third of the existing 650 KT UHP graphite electrode market demand, bringing down industry capacity utilization to 60-65%.

HEG management response: cannot speak to GrafTech's specific reasons/logic; China is predominantly exporting high-power grade electrodes but does also export UHP electrodes, estimated at ~100,000 tons out of 400,000 tons total Chinese electrode exports, mostly in low-powered furnaces/sizes up to 24 inches.

GrafTech's low utilization (~60-65%) is a matter for GrafTech to explain to its own stakeholders; HEG is running at 90%+ due to its cost-competitive plant scale and India location, and does not attribute its own performance to Chinese UHP export pressure.

subsections.label: US/EU trade actions
points: US countervailing and anti-dumping duty investigations against Indian and Chinese electrode imports are ongoing; outcome expected around September 2026.
HEG has engaged strong law firms in both India and US, submitted data; expects clarity in next four-five months.

Management believes HEG's US pricing is amongst the highest and does not believe it is doing anything seriously wrong; as lowest cost producer, believes it can absorb reasonable duties/taxes if imposed.

subsections.label: GrafTech investment rationale
points: Investment in GrafTech shares was undertaken as a deliberate long-term strategic investment; conviction anchored in structural fundamentals of the business rather than near-term market movements.
Rationale: GrafTech is the only graphite company in the world that is 75-80% backward integrated into needle coke (via its own needle coke plant covering about 75% of its own capacity).

Historical precedent: 5-6 years ago when electrode prices rose 3-5x, needle coke prices also rose from about $1,000 to about $4,000 over 5-7 quarters; GrafTech, uniquely having ~80% captive needle coke supply, made additional $2,000-$3,000 per ton on needle coke on top of electrode price gains, while others (including HEG, Japanese players, Graphite India) had to buy needle coke at $3,000-$4,000 higher cost.
Thesis: if/when a similar shortage cycle recurs as EAF capacity ramps (100 million tons of new EAF capacity), GrafTech stands to benefit doubly — from electrode prices and needle coke margins.

Stock had gone up 30-40% after initial purchase, then down 30-40%, and has recovered significantly in the last 2-3 months; management maintains full commitment to the investment and confidence in long-term value creation.

subsections.label: Composite scheme of arrangement (demerger)
points: Composite scheme of arrangement is progressing well.
NCLT convened meetings of equity shareholders, secured creditors, and unsecured creditors of HEG scheduled for Tuesday, 5th May, to seek approval.
Subject to shareholder, creditor and other regulatory approvals, scheme could be approved by NCLT sometime in Q2 of the current financial year (FY27).
