subsections.label: Geopolitical/Middle East disruption
points: Middle East conflict (Strait of Hormuz-related disruption) has caused order postponements from Kuwait, Saudi and other Middle East customers (~20% of annual sales region).
Freight costs to Middle East spiked from $20-30 to over $300 per ton; force majeure letters sent to affected customers.
Energy and freight cost increases flagged as a factor pressuring near-term margins and prompting need for price hikes.

subsections.label: Input cost / commodity risk
points: Rise in crude oil prices could push up needle coke prices (needle coke is a derivative of decant oil); no indication yet on quantum, expected clarity around mid-June 2026 when next quarter's contracts are discussed.

Needle coke supply is covered from origin till end-June shipments, covering costs until September via the ~45+45 day shipment/processing cycle; not protected for other India-sourced materials or energy.
Cost increases in energy and freight are being absorbed with a lag due to long production/shipment cycles (2-5 months to produce electrode, up to 40-45 days shipping to US).

subsections.label: Trade protectionism / regulatory risk
points: US countervailing and anti-dumping duty investigation against Indian and Chinese electrode imports; outcome expected in ~4-5 months (around September 2026).

Global trend of increasing protectionism (Section 232, anti-dumping/safeguard actions in Canada, Mexico, India, Brazil) could affect export volumes, though management believes HEG's cost leadership allows absorption of reasonable duties.

subsections.label: FX/translation risk
points: Unrealized fair value losses on GrafTech investment and rapid rupee depreciation (5% within Q4) drove a net loss of INR 189 crores for the quarter; loss will reverse if rupee appreciates.
FX loss quantified at INR 35-40 crores within the quarter, entirely unrealized.

subsections.label: Energy cost impact on EAF economics
points: Rising gas/energy prices in Europe/US are a major cost component for EAF steelmaking; management believes this does not materially change EAF economics as impact depends on each country's power generation mix, with only marginal impact given gas-based power plants more prevalent in Middle East than US/Europe.

subsections.label: Margin outlook
points: In Q3 FY26, company had guided for sustenance of EBITDA margin around 22% for the next couple of quarters; in Q4 this could not be sustained due to Middle East crisis.
For Q1 and Q2 FY27, EBITDA margin expected to be around 20% given committed volumes, though management noted uncertainty ('should be around that number').
For the full FY27 year, EBITDA margin expected to be (+20%).

subsections.label: Price hike trajectory
points: Aim towards H2 FY27 is to achieve price increases, both to protect and improve margins.
Quantum of price increase difficult to specify at this stage — depends on regional absorption capacity and competitor actions.

Full price hike benefit unlikely to be seen immediately given 3-6 month order booking cycles and multi-month production/shipping lead times; time lag exists between announcing a price increase and realizing it.

subsections.label: Long-term structural demand outlook
points: Structural shift toward EAF steelmaking, supported by decarbonization policies and trade realignments, continues to strengthen the long-term demand outlook for electrodes despite mixed near-term conditions.

About 20 million tons of new greenfield EAFs already commissioned globally (ex-China) in the last 12-18 months; additional 60 million tons at different stages of implementation expected in production by 2028, and another ~30 million tons by 2030 — totaling a little over 100 million tons of new EAF installations ex-China.
This EAF growth is expected to translate into incremental electrode demand of around 200,000 tons by 2030, excluding China.
Company's recent expansion from 80,000 to 100,000 tons and planned next expansion to 115,000 tons (targeted operational early 2028) positions it to meet a portion of this new demand.

key_takeaways: Global crude steel production in Q1 (Jan-Mar) 2026 stood at around 459 million tons, marking a decline of roughly 2% year-on-year, while registering a sequential recovery of about 8% versus Q4 of last year, mainly China-driven.

Structural shift toward electric arc furnace steelmaking, supported by decarbonization policies (CBAM) and trade realignments, continues to strengthen the long-term demand outlook for electrodes despite mixed near-term conditions.

About 20 million tons of new Greenfield electric arc furnaces have already been commissioned in the last 12 to 18 months all over the world, and an additional 60 million tons are at different stages of implementation, expected in production by 2028, and another about 30 million tons by 2030 — expected to translate into incremental electrode demand of around 200,000 tons by 2030, excluding China.

Sales volume increased by 20%, revenue grew from INR 2,153 crores to INR 2,569 crores; EBITDA increased from INR 388 crores to INR 497 crores, with margins increasing from 17% to 19%; net profit increased from INR 101 crores to INR 181 crores for FY26.

Q4 FY26 reported a loss of INR 189 crores, mainly attributable to fair value impact on foreign investment (GrafTech) and rapid rupee depreciation (5% within the quarter) — entirely unrealized losses; excluding these, operating margins for the quarter are intact and comparable with previous quarters.

Middle East disruption impacted about 20% of annual sales region; orders postponed, freight costs to the region spiked from $20-30 to $200-300 per ton, with force majeure letters sent to affected customers.
The composite scheme of arrangement (demerger) is progressing well; NCLT convened meetings scheduled for 5th May 2026, with approval anticipated in Q2 FY27 subject to regulatory approvals.

Company reaffirmed its GrafTech investment stance as a deliberate long-term investment anchored in structural fundamentals (GrafTech's unique 75-80% backward integration into needle coke), unaffected by near-term market volatility.

EBITDA margin guided at around 20% for Q1 and Q2 FY27, and (+20%) for the full FY27 year, versus a prior guidance (given in Q3) of sustaining ~22% margin, which was not met in Q4 due to the Middle East crisis.

quarters.summary: Q1 FY27 saw strong balance sheet growth (global business +15.4% YoY, advances +17.4% YoY, deposits +13.8% YoY) with margins within guided band, but net profit was sharply impacted by a USD 600mn NMC settlement paid on 1 July 2026. Management retained FY27 guidance across credit growth (12-14%), deposit growth (10-12%), NIM (2.75-2.95%), credit cost (<0.6%) and slippage (1-1.25%), while ROA guidance is under watch pending Q2 review, and flagged an upcoming ECL transition impact of ~110 bps on CRAR / 15-20 bps on credit cost from April 2027.

subsections.label: Profitability drivers
points: Operating profit almost flat YoY at INR 8,127 crore due to sharp fall in treasury income offsetting NII growth.

Fall in treasury income (from ~2,000-2,200 crore to 800-893 crore) attributed to G-sec yield rising from ~6.10-6.13% (June'25) to 6.78% (June'26), impacting revaluation gains rather than trading profit.
Fall compensated partly by first-time PSLC sale income of ~270 crore and higher TWO recoveries (>1,000 crore vs 650-700 crore in prior quarters).
NII growth of 9.5% aided by interest income growth (6.8%) outpacing interest expense growth (5.2%); NII stood at ~12,500 crore for the quarter.
Operating profit has consistently run in the 7,000-8,000 crore range over the last 15 quarters, reflecting stable underlying earnings power.

Net profit excluding the exceptional NMC item was INR 5,528 crore, with ROA of 1.10% and ROE of 16.57% on an underlying basis, versus reported net profit of INR 1,278 crore, reported ROA of 25 bps and reported ROE of 3.89% after the settlement.

subsections.label: NMC settlement impact
points: Bank entered out-of-court settlement with joint administrator of NMC Health PLC, NMC Healthcare Limited and NMC Holding Limited; liability capped at USD 600 million, paid 1 July 2026, notified to exchanges 2 July 2026.
Settlement resolves all claims without admission of liability or wrongdoing; terms remain confidential due to sub-judice status vis-à-vis other defendants.
Claims against the Bank in Abu Dhabi Global Market and High Court of Justice in England and Wales have been discontinued.
Financial impact fully absorbed and recognized in P&L for quarter ended 30 June 2026; reviewed by Central Statutory Auditor and captured in audit report.

Decision was commercially prudent based on legal advice, considering time, cost and litigation uncertainty, and the stage of trial/negotiation — described as low relative to overall claim quantum (reference figure ~5,000 crore) against all parties.
Bank's floating provision of INR 2,500 crore was NOT used for this settlement; it continues to be held for the upcoming ECL migration.
Recovery action against principal individual defendants will continue in India and outside.
No specific provision for the litigation was made per legal advice, since specific provisioning is not permitted for an ongoing litigation/settlement case.

subsections.label: Business growth and balance sheet metrics
points: Global business reached INR 30.5 lakh crore, up 15.4% YoY; total asset book size now over INR 21 lakh crore.
Global advances grew 17.4% YoY (domestic advances +16.1%, international advances +23.3%); March 2026 advance book growth was also >16% YoY.

Total deposits grew 13.8% YoY, with domestic deposits +14.7% and international deposits +8.9%; domestic CASA deposits grew 10% and term deposits grew 17.8%; domestic current deposit growth was 14.5% YoY.
Domestic credit-deposit ratio stood at 83.31% and CASA ratio at 37.72% as of 30 June 2026.
Yield on advances was 7.37%; cost of deposits eased 12 bps QoQ to 4.66%; global NIM was 2.77% and domestic NIM 2.93%.

subsections.label: Asset quality
points: GNPA ratio improved 29 bps YoY to 1.99%; Net NPA ratio improved 10 bps YoY to 50 bps.
Provision Coverage Ratio (incl. TWO) at 93.28%.
Slippage ratio improved 25 bps YoY to 0.91%, guidance range for FY27 is 1-1.25%.
Credit cost fell to 0.29% versus 0.55% in Q1 FY26, aided by write-off of only INR 625 crore in Q1 FY27 versus INR 2,200 crore in Q1 FY26.
CRILC SMA 1&2 (% of standard advances) improved sharply to 0.07% from 0.40% a year earlier (also cited as improvement from 0.18% to 0.07%).
Collection efficiency (excl. agri) at 99.2%, up from 98.9% in the prior quarter.

subsections.label: Capital and liquidity
points: CET1 ratio at 13.9%, Tier 1 ratio at 14.41%, CRAR at 16.30% as of 30 June 2026, up from 15.8% in Q4 FY26.
Quarterly average LCR at ~127%.
Planned equity capital raise of INR 8,500 crore in the medium term by March 2028, and Tier 2 capital raise of INR 6,000 crore in FY27.
ECL transition (effective 1 April 2027) expected to impact CRAR by ~110 bps (~INR 12,000-12,500 crore) and credit cost by 15-20 bps.

subsections.label: Sequential decline explanation (Ajmera Q&A)
points: Deposits/advances decline from March levels attributed to normal seasonality — March is typically the most productive quarter for all banks, followed by a natural post-March decline; this year's YTD decline was smaller than usual despite strong YoY growth.
GNPA/NNPA sequential uptick attributed to lower denominator (RWA lower in June vs March) and the conservative write-off approach taken to protect Provision Coverage Ratio.

subsections.label: Investment book duration and revaluation
points: Duration on investment book increased QoQ and YoY to take advantage of the higher yield environment (peak yield ~7.13-7.14%) across AFS, HTM and FVTPL books; treasury book size ranged 3.40-3.70 lakh crore.
As yields subsequently declined (to ~6.75-6.80%), the Bank saw upside/write-back on those investments — revaluation gain of 365 crore this quarter reflects lower yields at June-close versus March.
Bank stated it is positioned across all three books to be adequately protected against any future rate hike.

subsections.label: Fee income optimization
points: Commission/exchange/brokerage fee income down ~47% YoY; management attributed this partly to strategic trade-off — pricing/processing yields let go in favor of higher advances book growth (an 'all-in yield' approach); flagged as an area needing focus going forward.

key_figures.label: Overseas book as % of global book

subsections.label: Retail, agri and MSME growth
points: Organic retail book grew 18.4% YoY.
Agriculture advances grew 18.7% YoY.
Organic MSME growth was 20.3% YoY (~20% rounded).
Within retail: home loans +14.7%, mortgage loans +27.4%, auto loans +25.3%, education loans +10.8% YoY.

subsections.label: Corporate book strategy
points: Corporate loan growth was strong YoY (15.3%, >15% rounded) but the book de-grew 7% YTD — the only segment with YTD de-growth.

Strategy involves letting go of very finely priced, non-MCLR-linked assets in favor of shifting corporate borrowers to MCLR or near-MCLR benchmarks, given elevated deposit cost structure; described as 'strategy bang on' by management.

subsections.label: International/overseas business
points: International book size has grown from INR 1,05,000 crore in March 2021 to INR 3,00,000 crore currently, growing 15-20% for many quarters.
Overseas book is currently 16-17% of the global book, with a target share of 19-20% within a couple of years.
Bank has repositioned overseas presence over the last 5 years in terms of branch network and business, and is now a big player in the global syndication market.
Multiple new geographies under consideration for expansion — driven by strategic sense for the Bank and India's FTA signings; already present in some FTA-signed countries.

Governance, underwriting model, risk management, compliance framework and AML framework in international operations have been significantly strengthened since 2021; Group CRO and Group CCO now have oversight on all overseas operations.

Bank is in process of underwriting/facilitating ECB (~1.5 billion) for public sector undertakings via swap window, using overseas branches to fund and route money into India — additive to the 4-5 billion FCNR/MTN/OFCB target.

Rupee deposit rate offered on FCNR(B)

subsections.label: Acquisition financing
points: Bank is tying up with one foreign bank for merger and acquisition finance; currently evaluating 3-4 deals jointly with them.

subsections.label: Peer comparison
points: Management stated CASA ratio of 37.72% is a top-quartile number among large peer banks.
Domestic NIM of 2.93% and global NIM described as top-quartile despite the Bank carrying a larger global book.

Bank's deposit growth (both CASA and overall) has consistently outperformed system median due to long-standing focus on deposit mobilization; bulk deposit share as % of total deposits was reduced significantly over the last several years from a higher level 3-4 years back.

key_figures.label: Expected minimum FCNR(B) contribution to fundraising
Positive effect on bulk deposit dependency from FCNR
ECB underwriting for PSU via swap window

subsections.label: FCNR(B) / NRI resource mobilization
points: Bank anticipates raising ~4-5 billion USD across FCNR(B), MTN and OFCB/ECB instruments; roughly 700 million (media meet figure) / 600 million+ (analyst meet figure) raised via FCNR as of 24 July 2026, expecting to cross 1 billion by month-end.
Expected minimum FCNR(B) contribution to the overall fundraising target is 2 billion USD.
Loan against FCNR(B) deposits offered to eligible NRI customers; some customers place funds directly without borrowing, others take loan against FCNR(B) deposits.
Framework for NRI deposit mobilization also includes NRE deposits, though no separate specific target/data was available on the call (offered to furnish later).
FCNR(B) inflows via swap window expected to reduce dependency on bulk deposits by an estimated 17,000-18,000 crore.

Rupee deposit cost for FCNR(B)-linked resources is competitive at ~6.4-6.5%, described as landed cost for rupee resources; overseas branches lend against FCNR(B) deposits at their own cost of funds, generating margins at both ends of the transaction.

subsections.label: Dollar bond / capital markets issuance
points: Bank has taken ratings for a dollar bond but has not yet tapped the market, waiting for the right pricing window; initial market conditions were seen as overrated/less favorable.
Board-approved mandate allows raising beyond 1 billion via bond route if pricing and market conditions are favorable; initial plan is up to 1 billion out of the 4-5 billion overall target.
Swap window for the bond route is available until 31 December 2026.

subsections.label: Capital raise plan
points: Two-pronged capital raise: INR 8,500 crore equity raise planned in medium term (by March 2028), with actual timing dependent on requirement — capital position is currently healthy.

INR 6,000 crore Tier 2 capital raise planned in FY27 (an earlier matured amount not raised last year) — pricing and timing to be determined; not an immediate requirement given healthy CRAR of 16.3% and CET1 of 13.90%.

subsections.label: Branch expansion, hiring and AI/workforce strategy
points: Bank added ~260 branches last year and continues to expand branch network (current count ~8,400 branches).
Hiring plan of ~6,000 headcount last year (not all joined); plan to hire ~7,000 headcount in FY27.

Bank is an early/major user of AI in process and customer interface (tools referenced: Aditi, Adi); AI expected to repurpose workforce toward relationship-focused roles rather than reduce headcount, even as hiring continues.

key_figures.label: ECL impact on CRAR (original estimate before pullback)

subsections.label: Geopolitical and macro headwinds
points: Management flagged ongoing global geopolitical issues as a headwind causing caution on upward revision of credit growth guidance despite outperformance in March FY26 full year and Q1 FY27.
Uncertainty specifically flagged around future deposit growth trajectory amid prolonged geopolitical issues; guidance would be revisited if deposit growth certainty improves.

As of now, geopolitical issues have not disrupted the domestic economy materially — some impact managed via government schemes like ECLGS for MSME segment; economic parameters currently look sound, but management remains cautious about the impact of prolonged continuation.

subsections.label: NMC litigation risk
points: NMC legacy litigation and cross-border settlement is now resolved/closed for the Bank vis-à-vis NMC Health PLC/Healthcare/Holding entities, with liability capped at USD 600 million (reference claim amount cited at ~5,000 crore), but recovery action against principal individual defendants continues in India and abroad.

subsections.label: ECL (Expected Credit Loss) transition
points: Bank flagged an upcoming impact from ECL transition effective 1 April 2027, estimated at ~110 bps on CRAR (translating to ~INR 12,000-12,500 crore) and 15-20 bps additional impact on credit cost.
Floating provision of INR 2,500 crore is earmarked to buffer this ECL transition impact.
Impact to be spread over 4-5 years; capital raise plan (equity + Tier 1/Tier 2) intended to offset the CRAR impact.
Earlier expected gross impact was 125 bps minus a ~50 bps pullback; with final guidelines issued, pullback is now ~15 bps, netting to ~110 bps CRAR impact.

subsections.label: Full-year guidance retained across metrics
points: Credit growth guidance retained at 12-14%, deposit growth at 10-12%, CD ratio at 84-86%, NIM at 2.75-2.95%, credit cost below 0.6%, and slippage at 1-1.25% for FY27, all reiterated at prior levels despite outperformance in Q1 FY27, due to caution around geopolitical headwinds and deposit growth uncertainty.
ROE guidance retained at 15-16% for FY27.

ROA guidance is under watch for FY27 given Q1 impact from NMC settlement (Q1 FY27 ROA below 1%); full-year ROA guidance to be given after Q2 review; management expects ROA to be above 1% in Q2, Q3 and Q4 FY27 individually, consistent with the Bank's historical run of >1% ROA over the last 17-18 quarters.
Management stated it may revisit/upsize growth guidance if continuing upside growth trends persist through the year.

risk_register.note: Out-of-court settlement of USD 600 million paid 1 July 2026; claims in Abu Dhabi Global Market and UK High Court discontinued; recovery action against principal individual defendants continues in India and abroad.

risk_register.note: Management sees no material disruption yet but remains cautious; keeping credit growth guidance unchanged at 12-14% due to prolonged geopolitical uncertainty and its potential impact on future deposit growth.

risk_register.note: Depositor preference shifting from normal deposits toward capital markets, with money returning to the banking system more via wholesale rather than retail deposits; Bank says it maintains good control over bulk+CD deposit percentage.

themes.label: NMC settlement / legacy litigation closure
themes.note: USD 600mn out-of-court settlement paid, closing a long-standing cross-border dispute, but sharply denting reported net profit and ROA/ROE for the quarter.

themes.label: Balance sheet growth momentum
themes.note: Global business, advances and deposits all posted strong double-digit YoY growth, better than full-year FY26 run rate.

themes.label: Asset quality improvement
themes.note: GNPA, Net NPA, slippage ratio and CRILC SMA data all improved YoY, aided by conservative write-offs to protect PCR.

themes.label: Margin management within guided band
themes.note: NIM at 2.77% global / 2.93% domestic remained within the 2.75-2.95% guided band despite deposit cost pressure.

themes.label: ECL transition preparedness
themes.note: Bank flagged ~110 bps CRAR impact and 15-20 bps credit cost impact from ECL migration effective April 2027, to be buffered by floating provision and capital raise plans.

themes.label: NRI deposit / FCNR mobilization and overseas fundraising
themes.note: Bank targeting 4-5 billion USD via FCNR(B), MTN, OFCB and ECB routes to bolster liquidity and reduce bulk deposit dependency.

themes.label: Treasury income volatility
themes.note: Treasury income fell sharply YoY due to rising G-sec yields, partly offset by PSLC sale income and higher TWO recoveries.

key_takeaways: As at the end of Q1 FY 2027, the Bank's global business stands at INR 30.5 lakh crore registering a YoY growth of 15.4%.
Our global advances have grown by 17.4% YoY with domestic advances growing at 16.1% and international at 23.3%.

The Bank entered into an out-of-court settlement to resolve a legacy litigation issue of NMC group. The liability of the Bank in these proceedings is limited to the sum of USD 600 million, which was paid on 1st July 2026.

Net profit for Q1 FY 2027, after absorbing the impact of the settlement, stands at INR 1,278 crores. Without the impact of this exceptional item, net profit for the quarter would have been INR 5,528 crores.
Return on assets stands at 25 bps, excluding the impact of the exceptional item, ROA would have been 1.10%.
Our GNPA ratio has improved by 29 bps, YoY and stands at 1.99%. Net NPA ratio is below 1% at 50 bps, an improvement of 10 bps YoY.
On the credit growth, continue to have the same guidance of 12 to 14% growth. The deposit growth, continue to have the same guidance of 10 to 12% growth.
The Bank continues to hold the floating provision of INR 2,500 crores, which I said earlier.
On the ECL front... the impact of the ECL would be almost 110 bps on the CRAR translating into something around INR 12,000 crore.
pressing_questions: Can you elaborate on how much was the settlement? I mean, how much was the claim on the bank and how much did you settle ultimately?

Sir, this NMC case is a big case... You'll have always maintained that you'll will fight this case legally... So, what has changed? Why did you all take this decision to take such a big hit on your books?

In terms of internal processes at the Bank, what action have you taken, underwriting, Anti-Money Laundering KYC requirements... what went wrong? How have you corrected it? Has the RBI asked anything on this, are they scrutinizing this case? Is there any potential for further penalty with regard to this case or this is permanently settled for good?

In terms of the disclosure, even in the annual report, we just indicated that this case is pending but in terms of the liability amount given that it was so huge at almost 600 odd million, why there was no indication in terms of the liability which can accrue to us even closer to the settlement of the case?
If you can just highlight the nature of this entire case that is leading to this kind of a liability... So would the liability have been much much higher had this not been settled out of the court?

MAHLOG.about: Mahindra Logistics Ltd is an integrated logistics & mobility solutions provider. The company offers Supply Chain expertise to diverse industry verticals such as Automotive, Engineering, Consumer Goods, Pharmaceuticals, Telecommunications, Commodities, and E-commerce. [1]

quarters.summary: Q1 FY27 marked a step-up in profitability (PAT of INR25.4cr vs loss of INR10.8cr in Q1FY26) with consolidated revenue up 23% YoY. Management guided toward continued PAT positivity, EBITDA breakeven for the Express (Rivigo) business within FY27, medium-term gross margin expansion of 150-200 bps across the overall business, and reaffirmed the white-space reduction glide path (95% reduction by September 2026). Contract Logistics margins faced temporary headwinds (manpower, start-up costs, fuel lag) expected to normalize through the year.

subsections.label: Profitability drivers
points: Significant step-up in profitability attributed to strengthened operating model, sharper execution, discipline/rigour, strong customer focus and improved quality of growth.
PAT included INR4 crores of interest on income tax refund in the other income line, not expected to recur in subsequent quarters; excluding this, operating PAT is approximately INR21.4 crores.

subsections.label: Contract Logistics margin dilution drivers
points: Gross margin diluted by 46 bps YoY in Contract Logistics due to three factors: (1) start-up costs from opening a new site almost every week during Q1 as sales targets were exceeded — sites take 3-4 months to normalize profitability; (2) manpower shortages across the country due to LPG shortage and reverse migration to villages, requiring ad hoc higher-cost manpower hiring (since stabilised); (3) fuel price increase pass-through lag — fuel is a pass-through but POs must be amended with customers, causing a lag (not same-day).
Of the YoY gross margin dilution (approx 40 bps), management estimated about half came from start-up/ramp-up costs — a temporary bunching in one quarter expected to normalize as the year progresses.
EBITDA growth of 31% YoY and margin expansion from 6.6% to 6.9% in Contract Logistics achieved via overhead efficiencies and operating leverage offsetting the gross margin dilution.

subsections.label: Depreciation clarification
points: Depreciation increase YoY is due to overall increase in warehousing space (not a YoY decline — that decline was specific to 'white space', not total warehousing space), plus the Ind AS 116 curve impact from capitalisation of new warehouses (similar effect seen in Q2 of prior year).
Sequentially, depreciation has not increased substantially and is broadly in line, both on standalone and consolidated basis.

subsections.label: Contract Logistics business
points: Growth driven by continued strong momentum in M&M auto and farm/tractor businesses as well as growth in other 3PL verticals including e-commerce.

New customer wins across business segments reflect stronger customer solutioning capability, customer focus, improved service delivery and deeper customer engagement; Q1 wins exceeded the company's own aggressive internal stretch-goal plan.
Manufacturing and telecom vertical called out as doing exceptionally well; won a couple of very large marquee clients in manufacturing space in the last quarter.

M&M wallet share is significant; company continues to win a large part of M&M's business coming on stream, and is also winning substantial non-Mahindra business (e-commerce, manufacturing, telecom); relative growth contribution between M&M and non-M&M not quantified.

New large sites (e.g., ~2 lakh sq ft site at Luhari near Gurgaon for a marquee customer) take about 3-4 months to normalize operations and profitability; small sites (e.g., last mile, <1,000 sq ft) normalize within about 10 days.

subsections.label: Express (MESPL/Rivigo) business
points: Business continues its turnaround journey with uptick in volume and yield and disciplined cost control now firmly embedded in the system.
Focus remains on EBITDA breakeven with PAT progression to follow in a calibrated manner.

Management does not disclose Express volumes (in tonnage) or the volume-vs-yield split, citing that disclosing this would allow reverse calculation of margin profile; objective is not to maximize volume at the expense of yield.
No particular sector driving Express growth — growth is broad-based across a cross-section of sectors.
Some seasonality expected: heavy rains can cause operational issues in Q2, typically offset by festive demand pickup in Q3.

Sequential EBITDA loss reduction (~INR1 crore) was smaller than the sequential gross margin improvement (4.8% to 6%) would suggest, attributed to manpower cost headwinds (ad hoc hiring) common to Contract Logistics and B2B Express, plus fuel cost pass-through lag — fuel escalation has been passed on to 80% of B2B Express customers so far, unlike large Contract Logistics contracts (e.g., M&M) which get passed within 48 hours.

subsections.label: Last Mile Delivery (LMD) business
points: Revenue decline of 16% YoY was a conscious strategic choice, previously communicated, to prioritise profitable business over low-margin business amid sustained pricing and cost pressures.

This strategy drove gross margin expansion, supported by improved business mix and disciplined cost management; network recalibration and focus on profitable sites; business continues to be EBITDA profitable.

subsections.label: Freight Forwarding business
points: Revenue decline reflects customer attrition experienced during the recent transition phase of the business and the geopolitical crisis; also macro-led disruptions leading to volume decline from some key customers.
Leadership team has been strengthened; focus on expanding commercial coverage, rebuilding customer pipeline, and driving growth while maintaining service levels and operational discipline.
Despite challenges, gross margin remained healthy and in line with historical trends, with efficiency gained in fixed costs; business remains EBITDA positive.

subsections.label: Mobility business
points: Revenue growth largely contributed by expansion of client base in the B2B vertical.
Focus on acquiring new customers on B2B side; on B2C side, focus is on stabilising and building the recently launched airport taxi business at Noida International Airport (branded Alyte).
Majority of Mobility business is B2B (large majority); specific percentage split not disclosed.
Historically ~9-10% gross margin business; as business scales, operating leverage expected with some improvement in EBITDA percentage profile, alongside commensurate investments in B2B.

Margin profile (2-3% EBITDA) attributed to being heavily weighted towards employee transport services (lower margin) rather than higher-margin on-call/chauffeur car service model, plus insufficient scale for full operating leverage versus larger peers with 10-12% margins.

subsections.label: Mahindra (M&M) customer concentration
points: M&M share of business has risen from below 50% back up to ~60% currently (was ~70% three years ago) because Mahindra's auto and tractor businesses have grown faster than overall industry growth, increasing their share of company revenue.
Management has no target to reduce this ratio; objective is to win as much business as possible from both Mahindra and non-Mahindra clients.

subsections.label: White space reduction progress
points: Company is firmly on track to achieve its glide path of reducing white space by 95% by September 2026, from the 1.6 million sq ft base identified in Q1 of last year.
Overall warehousing utilisation levels are currently very high, but the company does not disclose the specific utilisation percentage as it could be disadvantageous when pitching for new business.
Total warehousing space currently stands at ~21 million sq ft.

subsections.label: Fuel escalation pass-through mechanics
points: For M&M, fuel escalation beyond a 5% threshold is adjusted and passed through within 24-48 hours, reflecting the more streamlined process for large, established contracts.

subsections.label: New customer wins and economics
points: New customer wins are hard-fought, won against national RFQs in a highly competitive logistics industry; wins are based on a combination of pricing, quality of solutioning, execution reputation, and governance brought by the Mahindra Group — not on pricing alone.
Company does not disclose the margin profile of new customers but states it aims to be competitive while ensuring profitability, not just revenue/volume for its own sake.

subsections.label: Cross-selling / customer overlap
points: A key internal objective is to cross-pitch all MLL verticals to existing 3PL customers; significant work has been done and wins achieved, but management acknowledges there is still a lot of work to be done in fully exploiting this cross-sell opportunity.
Customer overlap between Last Mile Delivery and Express Mobility businesses is described as 'not so much' currently, though achieving such synergies remains an internal target.

subsections.label: Airport taxi business (Alyte) strategy
points: Strategy is to scale cautiously and only where the business is profitable; company is withdrawing from Mumbai Airport as the Alyte service there did not meet internal profitability threshold.

Doubling down on Delhi Airport (preferred/most prominent counter lane at gate number 2) and Noida International Airport, where MLL is the preferred taxi partner; will scale fleet in line with Noida Airport's own flight/capacity additions.
Company scales up only where it can secure preferred rights/lanes, and withdraws where it cannot.

subsections.label: Industry consolidation view
points: Management is bullish on the logistics industry overall, viewing it as historically unorganized ("anybody with 2 trucks is a logistics company"); expects consolidation and increasing organization as India's GDP grows, disposable income rises, and companies increasingly value sustainability, time, and expertise — favoring established players.

subsections.label: Manpower availability
points: Manpower shortages across the country in Q1 due to LPG shortage and reverse migration to villages required ad hoc, higher-cost manpower hiring across Contract Logistics and B2B Express; situation has since stabilised/normalized.

subsections.label: Fuel/diesel cost pass-through lag
points: Fuel is a pass-through cost but there is a lag in passing it to customers because POs need to be amended and discussed; for large contracts like M&M, escalation beyond 5% is passed within 24-48 hours, but for B2B Express's large tail of hundreds of customers, negotiation with each takes longer — currently 80% of B2B Express customers have had the fuel escalation passed on.

subsections.label: Freight Forwarding — customer attrition and geopolitical crisis
points: Freight Forwarding revenue decline attributed to customer attrition during a recent business transition phase and the ongoing geopolitical crisis, along with macro-led disruptions causing volume decline from some key customers.

subsections.label: Site start-up/ramp-up costs
points: Rapid pace of new site openings (almost one per week in Q1) in Contract Logistics created temporary start-up cost drag on margins, expected to normalize as sites mature over 3-4 months.

key_figures.label: Gross margin expansion target (overall business, medium-term)

subsections.label: Forward priorities
points: Priorities remain unchanged: continue to scale core business profitably, strengthen the Express Logistics network, improve asset utilisation, and leverage technology to drive productivity and customer experience.

Company reiterated three focus areas going forward: (1) revenue and PAT growth, (2) improved operational efficiency and excellence, (3) growing base of highly satisfied customers who see tangible value.
Vision remains to be India's number one logistics service provider, delivering superior customer experience through technology-led solutions.

subsections.label: Express EBITDA breakeven timeline
points: Management reiterated confidence in achieving EBITDA breakeven for the Express business in FY27, but declined to specify whether this would occur in Q2, Q3, or Q4.

subsections.label: ROCE outlook
points: Company does not share forward-looking guidance on ROCE, but noted the ROCE metric has been improving and is healthier than a year back; will share the number at the end of H1 (Q2) along with the balance sheet.

guidance_ledger.statement: We will work towards continuing our trajectory of PAT positivity and improvement in operating performance.
Our target is to become EBITDA positive in this year... we are very confident of achieving this.
We have said that 150 to 200 bps is kind of the expansion that we are looking at in the gross margin from a medium-term perspective, for the overall business.
We are firmly on our track to achieve our glide path on reducing our white space by 95% by September '26.

As the business expands in top line, we will continue to see some operating leverage... eventually, as the business grows in scale, we should see some improvement in the percentage EBITDA profile of the business.
We have historically been between a 9%-10% kind of gross margin business in the Mobility segment, and we will continue to work towards that kind of gross margin profile.
At the end of H1, when we share our balance sheet, we will also share that [ROCE] number with you at the end of quarter 2 half yearly, which is looking much healthier than what it was a year back.
We don't have a target to reduce that ratio at all... I would like to win 100% business from Mahindra and 100% business from all other non-customers.
Noida Airport will scale up at their own pace, and we will scale up that business along with the Noida Airport... we are doubling down on the Delhi Airport.
No new explicit growth percentage given this quarter; prior guidance of mid-to-high teens growth not restated with a number this call.

guidance_ledger.statement: Not explicitly restated this quarter.

guidance_ledger.statement: Not mentioned in this call.
Fuel escalation for M&M passed within 48 hours; for B2B Express, 80% of customers have had fuel escalation passed on so far, remainder ongoing.
Right now we are not sharing any such target [INR20,000 crores turnover]; management denied having stated this at the AGM.

guidance_ledger.metric: Company vision - #1 logistics provider in India
guidance_ledger.statement: We remain committed to becoming the number 1 logistics services provider in India, delivering superior customer experience through technology-led solutions.
Utilization level for Alyte Prive (asset-heavy B2B mobility) is an internal metric; range not shared.
We will also do a little bit of investment in our tech in FY27 because we believe that in the last 2 years, we have not invested into that.

risk_register.risk: Manpower shortages / ad hoc hiring costs
risk_register.note: Driven by LPG shortage and reverse migration to villages across the country in Q1; situation has since stabilised/normalized, impacted both Contract Logistics and B2B Express margins.

risk_register.risk: Fuel/diesel cost pass-through lag
risk_register.note: Pass-through to large contract customers (e.g., M&M) happens within 24-48 hours, but for B2B Express's large customer tail it takes longer to negotiate; 80% of B2B Express customers have had the fuel escalation passed on so far.

risk_register.risk: Freight Forwarding customer attrition and geopolitical crisis
risk_register.note: Revenue declined 39% YoY to INR45 crores due to customer attrition during business transition and geopolitical crisis; leadership strengthened to rebuild customer pipeline.

risk_register.risk: Site start-up/ramp-up costs from rapid new site openings

key_takeaways: We delivered a significant step-up in profitability this quarter, moving from a PAT loss of INR 10.8 crores in Q1FY26 to a PAT profit of INR 25.4 crores in Q1FY27.
Alongside this, our consolidated revenue grew by 23% Y-o-Y, reflecting broad-based strength of our businesses.
In Q1, [Express] revenue grew by 58% Y-o-Y and the gross margin improved from negative INR 3.6 crores in Q1FY26 to a positive of INR 9.2 crores in FY27.
In our Contract Logistics business, Q1 revenue grew by 26% Y-o-Y and our gross margins grew by 21% Y-o-Y.
We are firmly on our track to achieve our glide path on reducing our white space by 95% by September '26.

In our Last Mile Delivery business... revenue moderation, we had a degrowth of 16% Y-o-Y was a conscious strategic choice... this strategy has actually worked very well for us, and it has driven our gross margin in quarter 1 up by 62% Y-o-Y.

In our Freight Forwarding business, revenue for Q1FY27 stood at INR 45 crores, reflecting the impact of customer attrition experienced during the recent transition phase of the business and the geopolitical crisis that we are currently facing.
Our reported EBITDA for the quarter is INR 115 crores, up from INR 76 crores in Q1 FY26.

If you could clarify how much of that [Contract Logistics margin contraction] could get reversed... if we are looking at a structurally lower margin, we were like 7.7% in Q4 FY26. So is it fair to say that the new normal is 7%?

quarters.summary: FY26 marked Mahindra Logistics' return to PAT profitability after two years of losses, driven by contract logistics wins, Express business turnaround, and operational excellence. Management expects continued margin expansion and operating leverage benefits going forward, with Express business targeting EBITDA breakeven (no committed timeline) and mid-to-high teens revenue growth over the medium term; Freight Forwarding faces near-term geopolitical headwinds from the West Asia war expected to persist.

subsections.label: Adjusted EBITDA methodology
points: New slide in investor deck titled Adjusted EBITDA introduced at analyst request, showing reported EBITDA adjusted for rent expense of long-term leases.

Under Ind AS 116, cost of long-term leases is accounted under interest and depreciation lines and therefore does not reflect under reported EBITDA; actual rent paid for long-term leases is deducted from reported EBITDA to arrive at adjusted EBITDA.
Reported EBITDA for the quarter/year is higher than adjusted EBITDA due to this Ind AS 116 lease accounting treatment.

subsections.label: Gross margin drivers
points: Year-on-year expansion in consolidated gross margin attributed to operational discipline and financial rigour initiatives.
Standalone business expanded gross margin by 80 bps with expansion across most verticals.
Improving trajectory in the MESPL (Express) business substantively contributed to gross margin expansion at the consolidated level.

subsections.label: PAT and profitability turnaround
points: Reported PAT for FY26 was INR2.3 crores versus a loss of INR35.8 crores in FY25.
Operational PAT of INR8.2 crores is grossed up for the tax-adjusted impact of the exceptional item taken in Q3 FY26 towards past gratuity service cost under the new Labor Codes.
At both reported and operational levels, MLL has turned profitable after two consecutive loss-making financial years.

subsections.label: Cash flow items - ROU reversal and credit provisioning
points: ROU reversal of INR14.38 crores relates to Ind AS 116 lease accounting: leases capitalized upfront cause higher P&L hit in initial years; when a lease is terminated before contracted end or a property is pre-closed, a reversal occurs, tied to business decisions on opening/closing sites.

Expected credit loss provision (~INR28 crores) taken in line with accounting prudence and management judgment on aged receivables based on assessment of recoverability; this is part of ongoing business, with management stating nothing further warrants provisioning at this moment for the short term.

subsections.label: Contract Logistics
points: Multiple wins across segments with steadily improving customer level economics.
Focus on operational efficiencies and profitable customers driving gross margin growth.

Seamless handling of operations at scale of Mahindra & Mahindra (second largest automotive company in India, world's largest tractor company by tractors produced, moved and sold) establishes right to win in managing large, complex, high-velocity networks - a competitive advantage.

Company evaluating a couple of new segments to enter to improve mix and profitability; market study underway; decision on which segment not yet finalized but one segment will be entered this year (FY27).

Warehousing space reduced from ~20.4 million sq ft (Q3 FY26) to ~19 million sq ft (Q4 FY26); relinquishment reflects business decisions on non-profitable customers/leases relinquished or lapsed over last 4 quarters, alongside new business wins (pipe-in/pipe-out dynamic).

subsections.label: Express (MESPL) business turnaround
points: Positive gross margins for the full year with tangible improvements in service quality, network utilization and unit economics.
Meaningful uptick in both volumes and yield with disciplined cost control embedded across organization.
Focus remains on EBITDA improvement with PAT progression to follow in a calibrated manner.
Sequential GM improvement for three consecutive quarters: INR20 lakh (Q2 FY26) to INR2.7 crores (Q3 FY26) to INR6.6 crores (Q4 FY26).
Losses at EBITDA level have substantially reduced versus FY25.
Volume growth described as mid- to high-teens YoY; quarter-on-quarter volume growth much higher than YoY.

Yield improvement driven by better customer experience and consistent improvement in network service levels tracked monthly over last 12 months, enabling price corrections with specific clients (not a blanket price increase); mix also favorable, with e-commerce growing faster than other segments within Express.
Company does serve e-commerce clients within Express Logistics but declined to share revenue quantum or industry-wise yield breakup (e.g., INR/kg) citing competitive sensitivity.
Retail segment brings better yield than B2B but is less predictable; B2B offers longer-term, more predictable relationships.

Tech investment planned in FY27 as company believes tech spend was under-invested in the last 2 years; company describes itself as tech-focused with a strong tech backbone supporting the Express business, though granular details (e.g., sorting belts) not disclosed.

subsections.label: Freight Forwarding
points: Growth in Q4 and full year driven primarily by improved trade flows, operating leverage and a diversified customer base.

Segment facing headwinds due to evolving geopolitical conditions (West Asia war) expected to persist in the near term; shipping line issues, containers jammed in ports, higher freight premiums, insurance premiums, and fuel surcharges are increasing costs and causing customer caution/delay.
Full year revenue growth driven by both volume growth and rate expansion.

subsections.label: Mobility
points: Focus on improving utilization for the asset-heavy part of the business, Alyte Prive (premium B2B offering currently offered in Delhi), and on acquiring new customers for the B2B side.
Significant scale-up in large B2B accounts drove FY26 revenue growth.
Utilization level considered an internal metric; management declined to share current level or target range.

subsections.label: Last-mile delivery
points: Revenue decline due to strategic choices/consolidation at certain sites in Q4 YoY to improve profitability.
Gross margin and EBITDA improving sequentially; pruning of unprofitable sites completed in FY26 with no further pruning expected; profit-making clients expected to grow going forward.
Operational excellence recognized with accolades from leading e-commerce players.

subsections.label: E-commerce and quick commerce
points: Business has scaled meaningfully, reaching more than INR1,000 crores in annual revenue at MLL level, reinforcing position in a fast-growing, future-ready segment of the logistics ecosystem.

SASKEN.about: Established in 1989, Sasken is a specialist in Product Engineering and Digital Transformation providing concept-to-market, chip-to-cognition R&D services to global leaders in Semiconductor, Automotive, Industrials, Consumer Electronics, Enterprise Devices, SatCom, and Transportation industries, etc. Located in India, the company has presence all over the world

quarters.summary: Sasken started FY27 on a positive note with consolidated revenue up 24% YoY to ₹339 Crores, driven by continued momentum across automotive connectivity, semiconductor design and AI-native engagements; order booking was healthy at US$47 million TCV (US$34 million from new wins). Management's focus for the rest of FY2027 is on disciplined, profitable growth — converting recent bookings into revenues, improving execution consistency and quality of business mix, maintaining cost discipline, and continuing investment in talent/capability to strengthen the Chip-to-Cognition position; the company does not provide formal margin or revenue guidance but reiterated its 60x4x3 strategy (with the 3-year timeline now seen as metaphoric, possibly extending by 1-2 years) and expects to add 5-6 more sales heads during the year.

key_figures.label: Software Services EBIT margin (historical, 6 quarters ago)

subsections.label: Margin drivers
points: Gross margin growth was contributed primarily by the software services segment, which saw continued margin expansion.
Software services gross margin improved by 240 basis points to 30.6%, driven by improved utilization, disciplined cost management and benefits of scale.

Product Solutions segment margin moderated to 5.9%, declining 310 bps sequentially, reflecting expected industry-wide headwinds (memory availability, component pricing) along with changes in project mix.
Memory pricing affects margin percentage because while costs are passed on to the customer, the incremental margin carry does not come through in the same way.
Silicon business is moving towards productization, which is impacting margins; some of these products will ship through the year and margins should be viewed on a full-year basis.
Management believes actions taken in Q1 will help margins stabilize over the year.

subsections.label: PAT/EBIT sequential moderation
points: Sequential PAT moderation was due to normalization of one-off benefits recorded in other income during Q4.
Foreign exchange gains in the current quarter were lower compared to the previous quarter, which had benefited from favorable currency movements.

subsections.label: Cash flow and capital allocation
points: Operating cash flows have been negative for the last two years despite profit growth, due to continued investment in the business (working capital and fixed assets) as the company scales; not due to any collection challenges.
Cash consumption is not limited to Borqs; other engagements also need working capital for capacity expansion, receivables and inventory.
In Q1, cash flow impact came partly from building inventories to manage the memory shortage.
Management expects large cash consumption again this year but aims to move towards cash flow positive using a mix of internal accruals and external funds; this remains work in progress.

Cost increase (headcount up 9% but cost up only ~3%) reflects a mix of lateral and fresher hires; Q4 had one-off bonus catch-up costs that are not recurring; utilization improvement helped offset cost growth without impacting margins.

subsections.label: Borqs breakeven economics
points: Borqs entity break-even point is at about US$12 million quarterly revenue; beyond that, incremental revenue will add to the bottom line as scale happens.
Last year the Borqs business was at a net loss.

key_figures.label: Annual Contract Value (ACV) of orders won

subsections.label: Order book nature
points: The published $47.1 million figure is the order booked in the current quarter, not the total order backlog; it will be delivered over multiple years.
Of the total, the $40.5 million ACV reflects the portion expected to be delivered within the next 12 months.
Order backlog typically gives a carry of 9-10 months, similar to other IT services companies, which supports meeting annual numbers.

On silicon, some orders are multi-year and depend on customer offtake; growth rates seen in Silicon last year are expected to continue, but specific breakdown of production vs. other order types will not be disclosed.

subsections.label: 60x4x3 strategy and $4 million+ accounts
points: The 60x4x3 strategy stemmed from learnings on serving marquee Fortune 500/Fortune 100 customers, with a target to grow accounts to at least $4 million run-rate revenue within roughly three years (a metaphoric timeline that may extend by one or two more years).
Company has completed two years (9th quarter, entering 10th of 12 quarters) of this journey; six customers have been at $4 million+ for four consecutive quarters.
Names of specific customers being targeted for $4 million+ this financial year will not be disclosed, but the strategy and focus remain intact, supported by continued sales bandwidth addition.

Company does not provide formal revenue guidance for the 60x4x3 outcome but is confident of being directionally on track; growth is the most important imperative, and how it splits across segments will be identified later.
New logos added: 5 new customer logos in Q1 FY27; active customers rose to 93 from 79 in Q1 FY26.
Top five customer revenue concentration increased to 56% from 52% prior period.

key_figures.label: Product Solutions gross margin (prior comparative in Q&A)

subsections.label: Software Services performance
points: Software services was the key growth driver in the quarter, growing 24.3% YoY and 4.8% QoQ to ₹219 crores.
Margin improvement attributed to improved utilization, disciplined cost management, and benefits of scale.

subsections.label: Product Solutions performance
points: Product Solutions revenue of ₹120 crores grew 23.6% YoY but moderated 3.9% sequentially following a strong Q4.
Business continued to navigate industry-wide pressures relating to memory availability, component pricing, and program mix.
Margin drop from 12.8% to 5.9% was influenced by memory pricing (pass-through costs reduce incremental margin carry) and a change in product mix as the silicon business moves towards productization.
Some silicon products will ship through the year; margins should be assessed on a full-year basis, with expectation of stabilization.

subsections.label: Disclosure practice
points: Company currently discloses business performance only as Product Solutions and Software Services, not by offering/vertical (auto, satellites, cellular communications, smart devices, digital semiconductor), as management believes vertical-level disclosure could distort the picture at this stage of scale.
Both Software Services and Product Solutions grew more than 20% YoY, reflecting traction across verticals including automotive and communication devices.

subsections.label: Chip-to-Cognition strategy
points: Sasken has evolved from a pure communications and device engineering services company into a full-stack 'Chip-to-Cognition' engineering partner over more than three decades.
Capabilities now span semiconductor design, embedded software services, connected devices, and increasingly AI-native engineering.
Chip-to-Cognition positioning is about participating across the complete engineering lifecycle with full-stack engineering depth.

subsections.label: Technology and demand trends (Hareesh Ramanna)
points: Global engineering R&D landscape being reshaped by AI-enabled systems, software-defined platforms, connected devices, and intelligent automation; customers seek partners spanning silicon, embedded software, devices, cloud, and intelligence.

Automotive undergoing software-led transformation driven by software-defined vehicles, centralized computer architectures, 5G, and Vehicle-to-Everything (V2X); AI accelerating feature development, validation, and time-to-market.
Communications trend towards a 'connected world' with seamless experience across home, vehicle, and enterprise devices as the key mantra going forward.

Communication infrastructure driven by 5G advanced, secure private networks, and AI-led network operations; recent engagements across massive MIMO, Beamforming, and Open RAN reflect relevance in this market.

Within smart devices, on-device AI and memory supply pressure are reshaping product economics, encouraging customers to prioritize higher value enterprise and specialized devices; enterprises adopting generative and agentic AI to shorten product cycles.

subsections.label: Silicon business (Anup Savla)
points: Semiconductor industry continues to see sustained investment across AI, edge computing, automotive electronics, and intelligent connectivity.
Demand for custom silicon and specialized architectures is increasing the need for advanced design capabilities.

Analog and mixed signal engineering remain highly specialized domains with scarce experienced talent, pushing companies to seek partners with deep specialized design expertise rather than building in-house.

As chip architecture becomes more complex and development cycles shorten, customers are engaging partners earlier — from architecture and IP development through physical design, verification, validation, and embedded software.

Silicon business is at an early stage for Sasken but being built with a long-term perspective, focused on deepening specialized capabilities, strengthening customer relationships, and increasing participation in higher-value, longer-duration semiconductor programs.

Advanced skills such as RF and mmWave, once seen as niche, are becoming pervasive, playing an important role in defining overall quality and competitiveness of semiconductor products (chiplets, memory integration, package design).

Company sees projects across the spectrum including power, connectivity, and automotive roadmap interfaces; current revenue mix already reflects implementation/execution of such technologies, expected to grow further with AI-enabled design.

subsections.label: Product Solutions / ODM capability
points: With Borqs integrated, Sasken can support customers from concept and design through certifications, production, deployment, and after-sales service, deepening product ownership.
ODM capability enables full product design starting from silicon licenses and advanced knowledge of silicon platforms, helping drive growth.
Full product engineering capability (from silicon to cloud) has been appreciated by customers and contributed to new wins.

subsections.label: Certifications and partnerships
points: GlobalFoundries IP certification and Intel certification have been confirmed/achieved; formal TSMC relationship progress is ongoing.

All three (GlobalFoundries, Intel, TSMC) partnerships have seen substantial, significant progress resulting in additional design-work activity, but details cannot be announced due to non-public nature.

subsections.label: IP licensing vs engineering services
points: Management does not see any conflict between running an engineering services business and an IP licensing business; the two are viewed as complementary, with AI playing a role in achieving this.
Example: customers seeking customized silicon to embed their own IP engage Sasken for IP development including integration of their own IP, working alongside big chipset/SoC makers.

subsections.label: Facility expansion
points: Inaugurated Sasken Silicon Incubation Center in Hubballi to strengthen university collaboration and development of future semiconductor talent.
Opened a new Center of Excellence in Hyderabad, expanding access to engineering talent.

subsections.label: Capacity-related working capital
points: Some working capital consumption relates to capacity expansion needs across engagements, in addition to receivables and inventory.

subsections.label: Geographic mix
points: Revenue mix remained broad-based across geographies and was evenly distributed across North America (30%), EMEA (25%), India (26%), and APAC (20%) regions.

subsections.label: Make in India / China Plus One
points: Make in India trend showing up in a big way with shifts happening; European and US customers asking for products to be fully designed outside China (China Plus One), or in some cases products that cannot be made out of China at all.

Two-wheeler module market still largely sourced from China due to cost sensitivity, but a shift is being observed where customers may look for local module development beyond just instrument clusters (e.g. NAD and other modules).

subsections.label: Memory shortage impact
points: Company built up inventories in Q1 to manage the ongoing memory shortage, which contributed to the cash flow impact in the quarter.
Memory availability and component pricing pressures continue to affect the Product Solutions segment industry-wide.

key_figures.label: Headcount at end of Q1 FY26 (including inorganic Borqs addition)
Inorganic headcount addition from Borqs (at that time)

subsections.label: Customer engagement highlights
points: Multi-year capability engagement won with a global hyperscaler.
Strategic engagement won with a global technology company to deliver services on AI and automation, spanning agentic AI, LLM validation, and intelligent testing.
Two hyperscaler engagements disclosed this quarter — one for next-gen device across platforms and one for OS sustenance — confirmed to be with different hyperscalers.
These engagements reinforce that the Chip-to-Cognition positioning is resonating with customers, with demand increasingly shifting towards intelligent AI-led work.

subsections.label: Talent and sales bandwidth
points: Global headcount growth from 1,900 (end of Q4 FY2025) to about 2,600+ (end of Q1 FY2027, 2,658 people) is described as largely organic addition, since the ~300-person inorganic addition from Borqs had already been included in the 2,200 headcount reported at end of Q1 FY2026.
Headcount split: approximately 2,400 engineers and 263 corporate staff; headcount grew 9% QoQ while cost grew only 3% QoQ.
Attrition rate stood at 9.8% with utilization at 85%.
CSAT score of 4.5 out of 5 versus industry benchmark of 3.75.
Company plans to add at least 5-6 more sales heads during the rest of the year to improve account coverage.
Leadership (Mody, Ramanna, Savla) also personally engage in sales through their industry connects; delivery-led growth also contributes to account mining, alongside dedicated sales additions.

A large part of business is delivered through a combination of headcount and AI; headcount may become less of a sole growth-tracking metric going forward as AI's role increases, requiring other metrics to communicate growth.

subsections.label: Team seniority (Silicon business)
points: Strong emphasis placed on making teams independent through training on core skills and giving ownership via visibility into the work performed.

Execution across customers is handled independently at multiple seniority levels within the Silicon team, given analog/RF/mmWave design are niche, hard-to-find, and sought-after skill sets grown largely in-house.

subsections.label: Borqs acquisition integration
points: Borqs acquisition (closed end of FY2025) broadened smart devices and ODM capabilities, strengthened relevance with global hyperscalers and automotive customers, and added greater product ownership to the portfolio.
Integration over the last 12 months has worked out well for both Sasken and Borqs, with benefits seen in scaling both Services and Product Solutions businesses.
Combined forces have helped engage with larger customers in services (technical + size synergy); progress on Product Solutions wins will be reported as actual wins come through.
Hareesh Ramanna leads experience and technology for the overall Sasken Group; his industry contacts and reach are helping penetrate and grow customers Sasken could not have reached independently.

subsections.label: Silicon business build-out
points: Silicon business deepened capabilities in chip design, engineering, and innovation over the last two years, part of the strategic inflection making Sasken more diversified and product-focused across the engineering value chain.

subsections.label: Inorganic growth optionality
points: Management acknowledged there may be some capability gaps which could be addressed inorganically as opportunities arise, alongside organic growth across silicon, devices, and software services vectors.

subsections.label: Industry-wide headwinds
points: Product Solutions business continued to navigate industry-wide pressures relating to memory availability, component pricing, and program mix, which moderated segment margins to 5.9% (down 310 bps sequentially).
On-device AI and memory supply pressure are reshaping product economics in smart devices, encouraging customers to prioritize higher-value enterprise and specialized devices over regular ones.

China cost competitiveness remains a headwind — two-wheeler module customers continue to source from China market due to cost sensitivity despite availability of Sasken-designed modules, unless a shift (e.g. regulatory or supply-chain) changes this dynamic.

subsections.label: Cash flow risk
points: Operating cash flows have been negative for the last two years due to continued investment in growth (working capital, fixed assets); expected to remain a large cash consumer again this year, with efforts underway to move towards cash flow positive.

subsections.label: Forward priorities
points: Priority through the rest of FY2027 is disciplined and profitable growth: converting recent wins to sustainable revenues, improving execution consistency, and continuing to invest in talent and capability that strengthens the Chip-to-Cognition position.
Focus for the remainder of FY2027 will be on converting bookings into revenues, improving quality of business mix, maintaining cost discipline, and driving sustainable, profitable growth.

Company does not provide formal revenue or margin guidance, but reiterated confidence in achieving 60x4x3 objective directionally, potentially requiring one more year beyond the original 3-year metaphoric timeline.
Management committed to maintaining margins while sustaining growth momentum, per Rajiv Mody's assurance in response to a margin-vs-growth trade-off question.
Silicon margins expected to stabilize over the year as productization-related shipments occur through FY2027.
Plan to add 5-6 more sales heads during the rest of the year to support account mining and coverage.
Company aims to move towards cash flow positive, using a mix of internal accruals and external funds, though timeline is work in progress.

guidance_ledger.metric: Revenue growth (60x4x3 - accounts to $4M+ run rate)
guidance_ledger.statement: 60x4x3 strategy targets growing customer accounts to at least $4 million run-rate revenue within roughly three years (metaphoric timeline); company is in its 9th-10th quarter of 12 and may take one or two more years to fully achieve it.
Company expects to add at least five to six sales heads during the rest of the year to ensure coverage across accounts.
Management does not want to give specific margin guidance but will constantly drive efficiencies and value pricing to improve margins, while maintaining margins alongside growth momentum.

Company expects large cash consumption again this year but the effort of management is to try and quickly get to cash flow positive, using a mix of internal accruals and external funds; work in progress.

guidance_ledger.metric: Product Solutions / Silicon segment margin stabilization
guidance_ledger.statement: Some actions taken in Q1 are expected to help margins start to stabilize over the year; silicon margins should be viewed on a full-year basis given multi-year product shipments.
Borqs entity break-even point stands at about US$12 million quarterly revenue; beyond that it will add to the bottom line as scale happens.

In response to an analyst back-of-envelope estimate of ₹2,500-3,000 Crores in revenue ballpark tied to 60x4x3 execution, management did not confirm a specific number but reiterated confidence in directionally achieving the 60x4x3 goal.

risk_register.risk: Memory availability and component pricing pressure
risk_register.note: Continued industry-wide headwind affecting Product Solutions segment margins and requiring inventory build-up in Q1 to manage memory shortage.

risk_register.risk: Product mix shift towards productization in Silicon business
risk_register.note: Impacting Product Solutions/Silicon margins in the near term; expected to stabilize over the full year.

risk_register.risk: China cost competitiveness in modules/two-wheeler market
risk_register.note: Customers remain cost-sensitive and continue sourcing modules from China despite availability of Sasken-designed alternatives, unless supply dynamics shift.

risk_register.risk: Negative operating cash flow due to growth investment
risk_register.note: Operating cash flows negative for two consecutive years due to investment in working capital and fixed assets as the business scales; expected to continue with large consumption this year.

risk_register.risk: Foreign exchange gain normalization
risk_register.note: Lower forex gains in Q1 versus Q4, which had benefited from favorable currency movements and one-off other income benefits, contributing to sequential PAT moderation.

themes.label: Chip-to-Cognition strategy
themes.note: Full-stack positioning spanning semiconductor design, embedded software, devices and AI-native engineering is resonating with customers and driving new wins.

themes.label: 60x4x3 account mining strategy
themes.note: Six customers have sustained $4M+ run-rate for four quarters; management reiterates the 3-year metaphoric target may extend by one to two years.

themes.label: Borqs integration
themes.note: Acquisition has broadened ODM/product ownership capability and helped win larger customers; integration over 12 months described as very satisfactory.

themes.label: Product Solutions margin pressure
themes.note: Memory availability, component pricing and productization-driven mix changes moderated Product Solutions margin to 5.9%, down 310 bps sequentially.

themes.label: AI-led demand shift
themes.note: Demand increasingly shifting towards intelligent AI-led engagements including agentic AI, LLM validation and AI-enabled design across auto, communications and silicon.

themes.label: Negative operating cash flow / capital intensity
themes.note: Operating cash flow negative for two consecutive years due to investment in working capital and fixed assets as the business scales; large consumption expected again this year.

themes.label: Silicon business build-out and certifications
themes.note: Silicon business early stage but scaling with progress on GlobalFoundries, Intel and TSMC partnerships and growing RF/mmWave/analog project pipeline.

key_takeaways: Revenues up by 24% year-on-year with healthy order booking of US$47 million in total contract value, including US$34 million from new deal wins, and five new logos added.

Growth was accompanied by a broader customer base and continued momentum across automotive connectivity, semiconductor design, and AI-native engagements, including a multi-year capability engagement with a global hyperscaler and a strategic engagement with a global technology company on AI and automation.
Global headcount reached 2,658 people while maintaining attrition at 9.8% and improving utilization to 85%.
Inaugurated Sasken Silicon Incubation Center in Hubballi and opened a new center of excellence in Hyderabad.
Total consolidated revenue for the quarter was ₹339 Crores, increasing 24% year-on-year and 1.6% sequentially.

Software services revenue of ₹219 Crores up by 24.3% year-on-year and 4.8% sequentially; Product Solutions revenue of ₹120 Crores, increasing by 23.6% year-on-year and moderating by 3.9% sequentially, following a strong Q4.

Gross margin for the quarter stood at 21.9% and ₹74 Crores in absolute terms, up by 48% year-on-year, and a decline by 1% sequentially; software services gross margin improved by 240-basis points to 30.6%, while product solution segment margins moderated to 5.9%, declining by 310 basis points sequentially.
EBITDA for the quarter was ₹31 Crores, with a margin of 9.5%; EBIT of ₹21 Crores, translating to an EBIT margin of 6.3%; Consolidated profit after tax stood at ₹23 Crores with a margin of 6.9%.
We serve 93 active customers during the quarter compared to 79 in the corresponding period last year, with top five customers remaining broadly stable at approximately 56%.
CSAT score remained strong at 4.5 out of 5 compared with the stated industry benchmark of 3.75.
Closed the quarter with a healthy cash and investment position of ₹356 Crores.
pressing_questions: So as per our strategy, so the 4 million plus customer has been at six for four consecutive quarters. Like, and our customer base has gone from 79 to 93 and the top five concentration is up 52 to 56. So, what is the pipeline of accounts you expect to cross $4 million in FY2027?
I know you already mentioned about drop in Product Solutions margin from 12.8 to 5.9. So, like, what was the major reason? Was it like memory pricing or something different?

If I just sort of do a back of the envelope calculation, you are 60x4x3... are we looking at close to 2,500 to 3,000 sort of a ballpark in terms of a revenue number and if we are, then given the fact that we ended 26 at about roughly about Rs.1,150 odd Crores, what do you think will drive that growth?
So, this is getting largely consumed by Borqs, is my understanding correct?
And for the Borqs entity, I think we mentioned in the past that we should be able to break even at a 60, 70 million dollar top line. Does that still hold?

Have you won any commercial orders or are we close to winning anything because the recent auto wins I am only seeing software related auto wins... when can we expect something in the Borqs side of things from the automotive segment?

CYIENT.about: Cyient (formerly Infotech Enterprises Limited) is an Indian multinational technology company that is focused on engineering, manufacturing, data analytics, and networks and operations. Infotech Enterprises Ltd. was established in 1991 in Hyderabad.[1]

quarters.summary: Cyient's Q1 FY27 saw DET revenue decline slightly in constant currency (-0.5% QoQ, -0.9% YoY) due to market-specific weakness (energy/strategic units) and discretionary project delays from West Asia war disruptions, while EBIT margin improved to 13.2%. Management pushed out the 15% EBIT exit target from Q4 FY27 to H1 FY28, citing slower revenue ramp-up despite cost levers being on track. Order intake grew 5.3% YoY with strong momentum in new business (EN/NN) and large deal pipeline building to over $300 million. Semiconductor business continues fast growth (Kinetic consolidation) with breakeven expected only in FY28; DLM delivered highest-ever order book and sustained double-digit EBITDA margins; Cyient completed its buyback and closed a $30 million EAAA financing round, and announced the TAO Digital Solutions acquisition to expand lifecycle engineering capabilities.

key_figures.label: DET FCF conversion to normalized PAT

subsections.label: DET margin drivers
points: EBIT improvement driven by continued cost optimization and favorable foreign exchange from a stronger USD.

Gross margin definition refined this quarter to reflect full accountability of project linked costs (software, hardware, facility seat, technology incubation spend) — a presentation change only with no impact at EBIT level; prior periods restated for like-to-like comparison.
EBIT outcome achieved despite higher restructuring costs over near-term quarterly average experienced in Q1.

subsections.label: PAT and tax commentary
points: YoY PAT decline reflects lower other income as Q1 FY26 benefited from a one-off reinstatement gain.
Effective tax rate increase YoY driven by a shift in profit mix towards higher tax jurisdictions and some prior period true-ups; company working on initiatives to bring this down.

subsections.label: Cash flow commentary
points: QoQ FCF decline primarily due to certain payments for which provisions were created in Q4 but paid in Q1; Q1 FCF conversion pattern is consistent with prior years, hence broadly flat YoY.
Capex spending this quarter is a little higher, reflective of cyclical IT system refresh and a project ramp-up.

subsections.label: Capital allocation
points: Share buyback successfully completed during the quarter; promoter group, directors, and key management personnel did not participate, reinforcing confidence and commitment in long-term value.
Buyback acceptance and extinguishment occurred after the reporting period (June 30, 2026), so no impact on Q1 FY27 results as reported.

With buyback fully settled and TAO Digital Solutions on track to close by August, capital allocation priorities for the year are largely executed; team focus now turns fully to integration and converting margin trajectory into a sustainable higher base.

subsections.label: Reporting structure
points: Only change to reporting structure this quarter is the inclusion of Kinetic in the semiconductor segment.
Q1 includes $10.4 million from Kinetic Technologies within the semiconductor segment, its first quarter of consolidation.

New business (EN/NN) order intake growth QoQ
Large deals won (Q4 FY26 + Q1 FY27)
Large deals created and qualified in Q1

subsections.label: Order intake drivers
points: Underneath the headline revenue decline, momentum in the funnel and order intake tells the full story of underlying demand strength.
Focus on building up larger deals is starting to show momentum.
DLM order book momentum continues to be a strong anchor, closing at highest ever order book supported by strong order inflow.

subsections.label: Existing business renewal softness
points: Existing order book renewal was depressed due to two primary factors: project-based work coming to a planned end, and delays in restart of discretionary projects that count as renewals.
Management clarified this has nothing to do with structural or market issues, but rather timing and customer willingness to commit to new projects.

Consecutive quarters of double-digit DLM EBITDA margin
