Consecutive quarters of organic semiconductor growth

subsections.label: Transportation & Mobility
points: Real standout quarter, remains strongest engine delivering fifth consecutive quarter of growth.
Growth not driven by one project; growth achieved across all three constituent segments — aerospace, rail, automotive — quarter-over-quarter and double-digit YoY in each.

Growth is a combination of market tailwinds and company's discovery of opportunities via lifecycle engineering strategy, expanding footprint beyond ER&D dollars; volume growth in number of assets serviced is a key driver.

On existing programs and already-budgeted programs, no impact yet from geopolitical disruption, but a continued West Asia war could threaten flying hours and create revenue compression industry-wide; impact so far only in select discretionary/value-add projects, not business-as-usual.

subsections.label: Network & Infrastructure (telecom/connectivity)
points: Rebounded as anticipated post Q4 setback, which was flagged as a quarter-specific problem.
Growth could have been higher had it not been for delayed start to some already-won Q4 FY26 programs; underlying demand for higher bandwidth and smarter systems remains strong.

Large part of business focused on fiber build-out with significant capex spend announced by customers (private corporations, not government-funded, though tied to government initiatives); visibility remains strong.

Some seasonality tied to customers' fiscal year and fund allocation timing; Celfinet acquisition diversification into holistic connectivity offering is helping offset seasonality, contributing to funnel growth and deal wins.
Most of the delayed connectivity ramp-up has now been completed.

subsections.label: Strategic units (energy, mining & minerals, healthcare)
points: Degrowth of -8.2% QoQ primarily due to contraction in the energy business.
Energy weakness traced to ramp-down of one single very large project (from ~2 years ago) that is now completely over; not a market share loss but a base effect.

Two of three markets in strategic units (mining & minerals, healthcare) show strong potential and growth; energy needs one to two more quarters for growth to rebound; overall aim is to narrow the gap if not make it flat.

Turnaround steps: (1) rebuilt go-to-market team in several geographies to align with market needs, (2) reprioritized which offerings are taken to market given current conditions, (3) broadened service portfolio beyond plant engineering — reflected in a Q1 large deal win with a large energy OEM for digitalization of their service parts catalog.
Cross-selling into North America from the Citec (Europe-centric) asset has started, though meaningful results not expected until Q2; aim is geography mitigation.

Company has unique nuclear engineering capability with tailwinds in North America and recent European announcements; mid-stage conversations with new customers, anticipating wins in nuclear energy in one to two quarters.
Other market segments in strategic units continue to deliver adequate results, expected to gain further momentum as funnel translates.

subsections.label: Semiconductor business — three verticals
points: Services business continues to grow; won a deal from the Semiconductor Complex of India to upgrade their fab in Mohali, among other deals; strong and growing pipeline.
Custom ASIC turnkey business pipeline now stands at more than $100 million, building fast, powered by new design wins and a deepening roster of blue-chip marquee clients.

Custom ASSP business has low-power and high-power parts: low-power expanded via Kinetic Technologies acquisition, fully consolidated in Q1 for the first time; high-power being developed organically, consuming most cash flow and contributing to lower operating profitability, with research phase completed and development now in full swing.
Semiconductor gross margin is higher than the services business gross margin, as expected.

Breakeven for semiconductor business (PAT level) expected only in FY28; growth outlook strong for both organic business and Kinetic; about $3 million per quarter in amortization from the Kinetic acquisition must be covered.

subsections.label: Cyient DLM
points: Q1 FY27 began on a strong note, reinforcing that underlying business strength remains intact and past investments are translating into tangible results, also reflected in DLM's valuation.

Quarter played out against continued geopolitical uncertainty, evolving design/demand patterns, and global supply chain disruptions including the West Asia crisis; despite this, execution stayed strong, meeting delivery commitments and strengthening customer trust.

Strong revenue growth YoY across a diversified revenue mix; sustained double-digit EBITDA margins for four consecutive quarters reflecting operational excellence, revenue quality, and disciplined cost management.
Key leadership hires in strategy, sales, and operations substantially complete, strengthening go-to-market engine.

Structural drivers remain intact: rising electronic content, supply chain diversification, and broader outsourcing strength; differentiated design-led manufacturing model and strong customer relationships position DLM well.

subsections.label: Compound semiconductor / GaN initiative
points: Compound semiconductor initiatives continue to advance, anchored by a push into the Indian gallium nitride (GaN) power market.

Seven new GaN powered chips launched, leveraging Navitas technology, addressing rapidly growing demand for high-efficiency, high-power density solutions across AI data centers, telecom, fast-charging consumer applications, industrial power systems, and e-mobility platforms.

subsections.label: Lifecycle engineering strategy
points: Company has been focusing on lifecycle engineering capabilities, opening a far larger market than the traditional ER&D outsourcing market of $80-100 billion — full product lifecycle opportunity is close to 20 times that.

Customer products stay in service for decades and, with more sensors on board, generate more data than ever — volume of data doubling every quarter in Cyient's segments — creating value to capture across development, manufacturing, supply chain, and aftermarket/MRO.

Agentic AI-driven MRO platform is a clear example of lifecycle shift: brings engineering, supply chain, and shop floor into one AI operations platform, turning lost time back into real output for serviced assets.

Platform-based MRO offering launched at the Farnborough Airshow this week with encouraging customer engagement; opportunity framed around products designed once but maintained across a service life of 50+ years, where growing economic value now sits.

Company layers domain expertise and agentic MRO platform playbook on secure AI infrastructure to deliver intelligent outcomes; conviction that AI value is realized only when domain experts shape it — AI augments, does not replace, expert delivery.

subsections.label: TAO Digital Solutions acquisition
points: Cyient announced an agreement to acquire TAO Digital Solutions this quarter, described as the first delivered step of the M&A strategy.
TAO adds depth in data and software engineering, including cloud-native platforms, helping guide key customers through AI adoption and keep AI running reliably in production via AIOps once live.
TAO works in the same mission-critical industries and platforms as Cyient, where data is complex and there is little room for error, especially deploying AI at scale.
TAO employees are present across North America, India, Taiwan, and parts of Europe.
Closing is progressing well; all closing conditions expected to be satisfied by August 2026; anticipated closing sometime in late Q2 timeframe.
$1.4 million in transaction costs expensed in Q1, normalized/treated as non-recurring.

TAO revenue contribution expected to be closer to the $40-50 million range if closed within shared timelines; management declined to comment on TAO's margin profile (EBITDA ~20%/high teens assumption) before closing, awaiting updated financials as part of closing deliverables.
TAO debt will be a US dollar-based SOFR-plus-spread debt, fairly low compared to Cyient's cost of capital and substantially lower than debt raised in India.

subsections.label: EAAA financing / capital raise for Semiconductors
points: Financing agreement with EAAA signed at $500 million post-money valuation; round closed with $30 million of fresh capital raised through a combination of debt and equity.
Described as a strong vote of confidence in strategy and trajectory, giving balance sheet strength to invest in growth and scale.
Semiconductor total incremental debt (Kinetic + TAO estimate) is approximately $250 million; Kinetic (Singapore-based) debt carries an interest rate of 1.25% plus spread, all-in below 3%.

subsections.label: Group structure / demerger question
points: Management stated no plan currently to pursue a clean demerger of DLM given significant interdependence between DLM and Cyient — DLM benefits from Cyient's engineering capability and vice versa; many engineering deal wins are attributable to manufacturing capability, a differentiator versus competitors.

Establishing DLM's own capital structure was intended to provide an avenue for value unlock, which has been established and is available to Cyient shareholders indirectly; current structure to continue for the foreseeable future.

subsections.label: Leadership additions
points: Baskar Nagarajan joined as global head of Avionics Delivery, bringing nearly three decades of experience at Honeywell, HAL and Alstom, having led teams of thousands on complex safety-critical programs; strengthens work in the transportation segment.
Rahul Sarkar joined to lead alliances and partnerships, having built partnership and ecosystem relationships across hyperscalers, AI platforms, and OEMs over 12 years at Tech Mahindra.

subsections.label: Investor Day
points: Investor Day planned for August 25, 2026 in Mumbai, to engage with leadership team on strategy, growth priorities, and the road ahead; management to go deeper on strategy including where the DET business is headed.

subsections.label: Geopolitical / supply chain disruption
points: West Asia war and resulting geopolitical uncertainty caused customers globally to be cautious on starting new discretionary programs, contributing to revenue slowness in Q1.

Continued disruption theoretically threatens flying hours in aerospace, which has already had some impact; if disruption continues for longer it can create further disruption and revenue compression in the industry — impact so far limited to select discretionary/value-add projects, not business-as-usual work.
DLM's quarter played out against continued geopolitical uncertainties, evolving design/demand patterns, and global supply chain disruptions including the West Asia crisis.

subsections.label: Discretionary spend caution / macro overhang
points: Slowness in awarding discretionary projects as customers globally were cautious on starting new programs amid uncertainty.
Macro overhang persists in areas like energy vertical decision-making and aerospace projects that had received verbal go-ahead but have since stalled, though existing business remains unaffected.

key_figures.label: EBIT exit target
key_figures.period: pushed from Q4 FY27 to H1 FY28

subsections.label: EBIT trajectory
points: Still working towards 15% EBIT but now believe it may take longer than originally aimed Q4 FY27; expect to reach it in H1 of next year (FY28).
Plan rested on two levers: internal cost focus and revenue growth trajectory; company remains firmly on track on cost side but running behind on revenue ramp-up, which is now the focus area.
Decision taken not to cut back on investments critical for turnaround in service portfolio mix, important to sustain momentum for future growth.

Cost/optimization levers (rate increases from customers, productivity and automation-related savings, G&A optimizations) are on track; absorption from growth will come a little later since growth has been muted.

subsections.label: Revenue growth outlook
points: No formal guidance was given; company had earlier indicated an aim towards mid-single digit growth for FY27, which is now challenged given the weak start to the year, making the ask rate for the rest of the year harder.
Hopeful of growth returning in a meaningful way in H2 of FY27; still working through the numbers with no specific commentary on where growth will land.
Growth build-up expected to occur slowly over the quarters.

subsections.label: Wage hike
points: Wage hike decision is a separate conversation driven by market forces; company will take a call looking at all scenarios at the beginning of H2.

guidance_ledger.statement: We are still working towards a 15% EBIT [exit target] but we now believe that this may take a little longer than the Q4 FY27 we originally aimed for... we will see a path towards 15%. It will take us a couple of quarters into the next year by which time we hope to get there... we will reach 15% in H1 next year [FY28]
We expect the full year run rate of ETR to be between 27% and 28%

We had earlier indicated revenue growth in FY27 would be in mid to high single digit range... that will be challenged... We are hopeful of growth returning in a meaningful way in H2 of this year. We do not have the details to give a specific commentary on where that will land us
In terms of breakeven, it looks like breakeven will happen only in FY28
Growth will continue to be very strong, we see a strong pipeline, both for the signed organic business and the acquired entity... we are not overtly worried... very good growth opportunity
It definitely will be closer to about $40-50 million range if you are able to close with the timelines that we are sharing right now
We are expecting to satisfy all the closing conditions by August 2026... anticipated to be sometime in the late Q2 timeframe

guidance_ledger.metric: Strategic units / energy vertical growth rebound
guidance_ledger.statement: We are confident that this will start showing market comparable results in the next two, three quarters... for growth to rebound we probably will need one or two more quarters... our overall attempt should be to narrow the gap, if not make it flat
We anticipate to start seeing wins in nuclear energy in about a quarter to two quarters in a significant way
We probably will not have meaningful results for this Q2, but the idea is to make sure that we build up the momentum so we can do some geography mitigation for next Q2
We will take a call looking at all the scenarios in the beginning of H2 on the wage hike itself

risk_register.risk: West Asia war / geopolitical uncertainty causing supply chain disruption and customer caution on discretionary spend
risk_register.note: Resulted in slowness in awarding discretionary projects globally and contributed to Q1 revenue decline; theoretically threatens aerospace flying hours if prolonged, which could compress industry revenue.

risk_register.risk: Discretionary project delays / decision-making uncertainty
risk_register.note: Customers cautious on starting new programs; overhang persists in energy vertical and select aerospace projects that received verbal go-ahead but have since stalled; existing business unaffected so far.

risk_register.risk: Energy vertical contraction within strategic units
risk_register.note: Strategic units degrew -8.2% QoQ primarily due to energy business contraction following completion of a large legacy project; management expects 1-2 more quarters before growth rebounds.

risk_register.risk: Effective tax rate increase
risk_register.note: ETR up 350 bps YoY driven by shift in profit mix towards higher tax jurisdictions and prior period true-ups; company working on initiatives to bring it down, targeting 27-28% full year run rate.

risk_register.risk: Semiconductor high-power ASSP cash consumption / lower profitability
risk_register.note: High-power ASSP business being developed organically is consuming much of the cash flow and has led to lower operating profitability; will continue to consume cash for at least next 4-5 quarters.

risk_register.risk: Kinetic acquisition amortization drag
risk_register.note: About $3 million per quarter in amortization from Kinetic acquisition needs to be covered, pushing out semiconductor PAT breakeven to FY28.

risk_register.risk: Network & Infrastructure program start delays
risk_register.note: Growth could have been higher had it not been for delayed start to some already-won Q4 FY26 programs; most connectivity ramp-up delay is now resolved.

themes.label: Margin expansion via cost optimization
themes.note: DET EBIT margin improved to 13.2%, up 79 bps QoQ and 114 bps YoY, driven by cost optimization and favorable forex, though 15% exit target pushed out to H1 FY28 due to slower revenue growth.

themes.label: Discretionary spend caution / geopolitical overhang
themes.note: West Asia war disruptions and macro uncertainty led customers to delay discretionary project awards, contributing to a constant-currency revenue decline.

themes.label: Lifecycle engineering / AI-led expansion
themes.note: TAO Digital Solutions acquisition and agentic AI-driven MRO platform launch extend Cyient's reach across the full product lifecycle, a market ~20x the traditional ER&D outsourcing opportunity.

themes.label: Semiconductor scale-up
themes.note: Strong growth across services, custom ASIC (pipeline >$100M) and ASSP (Kinetic consolidation) verticals, but PAT breakeven pushed to FY28 due to high-power ASSP R&D cash burn and Kinetic amortization.

themes.label: Energy vertical weakness in strategic units
themes.note: Strategic units degrew -8.2% QoQ due to energy contraction after a large legacy project ended; turnaround steps (GTM rebuild, portfolio broadening, nuclear/cross-sell push) expected to show results in 2-3 quarters.

themes.label: Large deal pipeline momentum
themes.note: Order intake up 5.3% YoY with new business intake up 64% YoY; 5 large deals won over two quarters and additional large deal pipeline exceeding $300 million.

themes.label: Capital allocation execution
themes.note: Buyback of Rs.720 Crores completed and $30 million EAAA financing round closed at $500 million valuation, largely completing the year's capital allocation priorities ahead of TAO integration.

key_takeaways: DET Q1 revenue of $162.5 million, down 0.5% QoQ and 0.9% YoY in constant currency; INR revenue up 2.7% QoQ and 10.6% YoY
DET EBIT margin (normalized) at 13.2%, up 79 bps QoQ and 114 bps YoY driven by cost optimization and favorable forex
EBIT exit goal of 15% pushed out from Q4 FY27 target to H1 FY28 due to slower revenue ramp-up, while cost levers remain on track
Order intake up 5.3% YoY; new business (EN/NN) order intake up 64% YoY and 49% QoQ; large deal pipeline of over $300 million after winning 5 large deals over two quarters and qualifying 9 more in Q1
Transportation & Mobility grew 14.8% YoY in constant currency, fifth consecutive quarter of growth, across aerospace, rail, and automotive
Strategic units degrew -8.2% QoQ primarily due to energy business contraction; management expects comparable growth in 2-3 quarters
Cyient Semiconductors: combined Cyient + Kinetic revenue of $17.9 million; organic semiconductor growth of 5% QoQ for fifth consecutive quarter above 5%; breakeven expected only in FY28
Cyient DLM closed at highest-ever order book with book-to-bill ratio in excess of 1.5 and sustained double-digit EBITDA margins for four consecutive quarters

Completed share buyback of 6.4 million shares at Rs.1,125/share (Rs.720 Crores, ~5.76% of paid-up capital); closed $30 million EAAA financing round at $500 million post-money valuation for Semiconductors
Announced acquisition of TAO Digital Solutions to expand lifecycle engineering/AI capabilities, expected to close by August 2026 with revenue contribution of $40-50 million
Investor Day planned for August 25, 2026 in Mumbai

SPECIALITY.about: Incorporated in 1999, Speciality Restaurant Ltd is in the business of operating restaurant outlets / sweet shops[1]

quarters.summary: Management expects the positive momentum from Q1 FY27 (11.35% SSSG, gross margin expansion) to continue, with Q3 FY27 flagged as a particularly strong quarter ahead; the company is refraining from committing to a specific INR600 crore revenue target but is working towards good percentage growth. Cash of INR162 crores is expected to be maintained by year-end as capex will be funded from business cash generation. Brand portfolio is being restructured into three power verticals (Oriental, Italian, QSR) with older brands to be phased out, while Sweet Bengal, Walters Burgers and liquor-led renovations are cited as key growth levers.

subsections.label: Margin drivers
points: Gross margin improved by 1.2% to 71.1% from 69.9% previous year, primarily because of managing portions, inefficiencies and continued negotiations with vendors because of volumes, achieved despite inflationary trend witnessed during the quarter.
Management generally locks into rate contracts for the financial year or on a 6-month basis, which helps buffer against short-term cost pressures.

A proactive management decision to convert from oil-fired/gas-fired ranges to induction (electricity-based) processes helped avoid the gas availability crisis; the company now operates in a hybrid mode able to switch to induction when needed.
When facing the gas crisis as an opportunity, the company worked on efficiencies such as correct portion sizing, which led to raw material cost benefits and helped neutralize inflationary increases.

During the quarter, service charge (levied until 7th June) was withdrawn across restaurants; a tactical price increase was taken to neutralize this impact — this was the price action taken this quarter, not a broad-based hike.
Historically the company has maintained gross margins within plus/minus 50bps; when there is heavy pressure on raw material and margins, neutralization is done via tactical price increases.

Inflationary pressure affects not only gross margins but also other expenses such as staff cost, power, light, fuel, and licensing costs (which increase every year), requiring balance to maintain margins.

subsections.label: Delivery vs dine-in economics
points: Delivery business has grown to 29% of total portfolio revenue while dine-in continues to grow as well; dine-in revenue rose from INR71 crores last year to INR81 crores currently.

Management clarified that focus on dine-in continues; brand value (e.g., Mainland China, Asia Kitchen) plays an important role and results in increased delivery too — it is not a deliberate shift away from dine-in.
Average order value for dine-in brands/categories is considered one of the highest as per aggregator data.

Delivery growth has been powered by new formats (Walters Burgers, Sweet Bengal, Haka digital-first brand), increased consumption occasions, marketing/advertising in delivery segments, tactical discounting, and recruitment of delivery personnel.

EBITDA margin uptick is a combination effort; cloud kitchens are only 11 in the portfolio (kitchens within kitchens doing brand sales from existing dine-in restaurants); delivery growth triggers favorable operating leverage once a threshold revenue increase is crossed, despite direct variable delivery costs.

subsections.label: Cash flow and capital allocation
points: Cash flows are managed such that the company expects to maintain the INR162 crore cash level by year-end because capex will be taken care of by cash generation from the business in the coming months.

subsections.label: Other financial notes
points: Corporate cost as % of revenue currently stands at 4%.

subsections.label: Demand trends
points: July was an extremely good month compared to earlier July periods; the trend for the first 7-10 days into August has also been good, showing tailwind for both dine-in and delivery.

Weekend demand remains highest across the industry (worldwide and in the company's own restaurants), with weekday demand varying by location — some locations see weekdays performing better than weekends depending on whether the area is corporate or residential.
Weekday tactical offers, discounts, set meals, corporate lunches, and delivery combo meals are used and vary from brand to brand.
Weekend vs weekday sales proportion continues to be on the same numbers as previously mentioned (previously cited as 45-55 in proportion).

Cyclicality from events like Shravan (20-25 days) does not have a major impact given the company's large presence across the country including Southern India, though Western India (Mumbai) sees a slight impact around Ganpati days, partially offset by substantial growth in Sweet Bengal revenue during such periods.

subsections.label: Brand portfolio restructuring into three verticals
points: Company has been creating brands over the past 35 years; every store currently operating is profitable.
Going forward, the company will focus on three futuristic verticals to power growth: Oriental, Italian (led by new brand Siciliana as growth engine), and QSR (Sweet Bengal and Walters Burger).

All brands in the portfolio will be restructured under these three broad heads (Oriental, Italian, QSR); older brands not fitting these categories will progressively be dropped from the portfolio as focus shifts to power brands.

subsections.label: Sweet Bengal
points: Hero product for Sweet Bengal is the Kheer Kadam, backed by data as the most loved, most talked about, and most differentiated product versus competing sweet brands; promoted at every occasion and kept on top of the shelf and top of mind.
Second most famous product is Mishti Doi, followed by Sandesh — all pure Bengali-categorized sweets that bring repeat customers.
Sweet Bengal previously faced slower growth challenges due to shelf-life limitations for perishable sweets made from one expensive capex-loaded facility and transported to various locations.
Company has cracked a 30-day shelf life using new modern technology and packaging, enabling expansion into many new markets, which is expected to grow visibility and revenue.
Added shelf life via new technology, modified packaging, and brand evolution are cited as enablers for growth of Sweet Bengal, positioned as an independent-potential vertical within QSR.

subsections.label: Oriental cuisine multi-brand price-tiering strategy
points: Post-pandemic store closures (29 stores shut) prompted a strategic rethink: Oriental segment needed to operate across different price segments to capture a wider pie and avoid brand fatigue/cannibalization from expanding Mainland China alone (previously, near 5-km locations were eating into own sales).
New Oriental brand tiering: Gong (premium, INR2,500/person), Mainland China (INR1,250/person), Asia Kitchen (mall-focused, INR1,050-1,100/person), and Haka (delivery-first, INR600/person).

This tiering allows the company to capture the Asian segment in any city via different brand fascias without cannibalization; growth strategy also includes running Oriental delivery brands (Gong, Asia Kitchen, Haka, Mainland China delivery) from the same physical unit.

Mainland China store count grew modestly from 31 (FY22) to 35-36 (FY26) because the company underwent a renovation phase of old Mainland China stores (in operation for 9-10 years) into a higher-throughput format internally called 'Mainland China 2', which has delivered progressive post-renovation numbers.
Gong is a new brand from an Oriental cuisine perspective, started in Pune, now in Mumbai (Bandra), with upcoming openings in Vasant Kunj, Delhi and a second location in Pune.
Oriental business remains the biggest contributor to overall revenue at sub-50% share and management continues to prioritize growth from this segment.

subsections.label: Bizarre Asia format
points: Bizarre Asia was created as a buffet format for Oriental cuisine as a proof of concept; it requires a large space and huge manpower.

The format launched around October (approaching two-year incubation) and remains profitable at that location, but focus on expansion is more on Asia Kitchens and Mainland China; Bizarre Asia will be added tactically wherever a suitable buffet-format location arises.

subsections.label: Liquor strategy across brands
points: Renovated Mainland China and Asia Kitchen locations now feature a visible bar with bartender and bottle displays, driving a phenomenal jump in liquor sales; at least five renovated Mainland China locations already have this; every renovated Mainland China going forward will have a bar, as will Asia Kitchen by Mainland China mall locations.
Company has multiple contracts and liquor tie-ups with liquor companies and partners, and liquor sale is planned to be a big focus area going forward.
Liquor/wine revenue share is 8-9% at existing food-driven stores versus 40% at Episode One (wetland restaurant); liquor sale share is 38% at Gong and around 25% at Siciliana.

subsections.label: Walters Burgers (QSR)
points: Walters is now on a growth path since roughly one year has passed; between 10 to 15 Walters stores are planned to be added this financial year, distinguishing it from the main restaurant count.
Currently operates 3 principal stores and 2 cloud kitchens; stores being opened going forward are physical stores, not cloud kitchens.
Revenue contribution from Walters is currently very insignificant at 1.3% of quarter revenues but grew almost 300%-odd from the previous quarter with the addition of just one new store.

Central kitchen facility model is helping bring margins up and costs down; a specialized QSR team has been built, and 5 new stores are planned by end of this year; QSR/Walters Burgers will be a heavy focus vertical in the years to come.

subsections.label: Weekday/weekend and geography-driven performance nuance
points: Weekend vs weekday sales split varies by location depending on whether the area is corporate (weekdays slower) or residential (weekends slower).

subsections.label: Growth vertical prioritization
points: Going forward, all three power categories — Oriental, Italian, and QSR — will be given equal weightage for expansion.

Growth of Oriental brands from a single location benefits all associated delivery brands (Gong, Asia Kitchen, Haka, Mainland China delivery) operating from the same unit — growth occurs both via physical stores and delivery in parallel.

Italian cuisine (via Siciliana) has provided very good operational leverage inside malls; company now signs simultaneous deals for Asia Kitchen and Italian brands together in the same mall spot, yielding a better revenue/effort ratio and manpower cost leverage due to two units sharing a spot resulting in higher combined revenue.

The next phase of Speciality Restaurants will be as much about building scalable brands as it is about building restaurants, with focus on profitable, disciplined growth while making brands relevant to the next generation of customers.

subsections.label: Competitive/segment interest in QSR/burger space
points: There is significant private equity interest and interest from other players in the QSR/burger space, prompting focus and investment in Walters Burgers as the company's entrant in this space.

subsections.label: Speciality Hotels India Private Limited (Odisha/Durgapur land monetization)
points: A plot of land was given to Speciality Restaurants by IDCO, Government of Odisha, for creating a food and beverage complex; the entity is named Speciality Hotels India Private Limited (not 'Speciality Hospital').
The plot has been developed under joint development and will comprise restaurants, banquets, and service apartments, to be utilized later.
Company will hold around 34% of the demerged company post completion of the building.
Joint development is progressing and management expects to complete the development by this financial year end.

subsections.label: Manpower constraint
points: The biggest and, in management's opinion, the only real constraint to expansion is getting trained manpower for restaurants — maintaining service standards and consistency in the dining space is a challenge; all other factors (locations, capital allocation, etc.) can be managed, but skills/staffing is the key bottleneck to quadrupling restaurant expansion.

subsections.label: Input cost inflation and gas availability
points: Inflationary trend was witnessed during the quarter affecting raw materials, staff cost, power, light, fuel, and licensing costs (which increase every year).

Gas crisis affected availability broadly; Mumbai had pipe gas so did not suffer much from cylinder availability, but management's proactive conversion from gas-fired ranges to induction (hybrid mode) mitigated this risk going forward.

subsections.label: Weekday footfall variability
points: Weekday footfalls remain a challenge relative to weekends in general, requiring tactical discounts and offers; this varies significantly by location, brand, and whether the area is corporate or residential.

subsections.label: Revenue outlook
points: Management declined to commit to a specific INR600 crore revenue figure for the year but reiterated they are working hard to achieve good percentage growth going forward, with Q3 FY27 flagged as expected to be a good quarter.
Demand trend has been very positive in Q1 FY27 and management hopes to maintain this kind of performance going forward.

subsections.label: Cash position outlook
points: Cash flows are managed such that the company expects to maintain the INR162 crore cash level by year-end, as capex needs will be funded by business cash generation in the coming months.

subsections.label: Expansion plans
points: New restaurants planned per financial year (excluding Walters): 8 to 10 restaurants; 15 new store openings planned for FY27.
New Walters stores planned: 10 to 15 stores this financial year, with 5 coming up by end of this year and 4 opening in upcoming quarters.
Speciality Hotels India development expected to be completed by this financial year end.

risk_register.risk: LPG/PNG fuel supply disruption

risk_register.risk: Brand fatigue and cannibalization from over-concentration of single brand

key_takeaways: This has been the company's 20th profitable quarter, which means we are, for last 5 years, into profits.
The same-store sales growth has been at 11.35% precise during quarter one FY27 as compared to quarter one of FY26, with like-and-like stores operating during both the quarters.

There have been improvement in gross margins by 1.2% to 71.1% from 69.9% previous year, primarily because of managing the portions, inefficiencies and continued negotiations with our vendors because of volumes.
This has been achieved despite the inflationary trend witnessed during the quarter of the current financial year.

subsections.label: Profitability drivers
points: Improvement in profitability supported by same-store sales growth of 2.25% in Q4 vs previous year.
Gross margins improved from 69.1% to 70.4% because of efficiencies despite inflationary trends, aiding profitability improvement.
SSG improvement in April driven by increase in dine-in covers across formats and restaurants; delivery is growing in any case.

Slower SSG in prior periods attributed to restaurants not having been renovated over a period of time (some for 10-11 years); renovation/refreshment program (starting Andheri West, Pune, Bangalore) expected to drive SSG growth in coming quarters.

subsections.label: Cost structure clarifications
points: Restaurant-level EBITDA of 15-16% is calculated post-rentals; this differs from consolidated cash-flow-based EBITDA margin which is after corporate costs.
Corporate costs, which had remained elevated (6-7%) due to lack of expansion for 2 years post-COVID, are now stepping down to 4% as fixed costs get amortized over a larger, expanding restaurant base.

subsections.label: Capital allocation
points: Company is debt-free.
Buyback query raised by an investor given cheap valuations and cash pile; management stated decision would need to be taken up by the Board, and could not commit given prevailing situations.

subsections.label: Brand portfolio and positioning
points: Focus brands currently are Mainland China, Asia Kitchen, Haka, Gong, Siciliana, Walters and Sweet Bengal.

Panda Express (competitor's fast QSR entrant) is viewed as a different brand segment/category from Mainland China (fine casual) and Asia Kitchen (casual fun dining); no threat or loss of business anticipated.
Company already operates a digital QSR, delivery-first brand called Haka to address any consumption shift toward fast QSR.

Brand hierarchy by price point: Gong (premium Asian dining, launched in Bandra) > Mainland China (fine dining) > Asia Kitchen (casual fun dining, mainly in malls) > Haka (digital QSR, delivery-first).
Strategy is to have an Asian brand for every price point, leveraging 35 years of Asian cuisine expertise; plans to replicate 'cut copy paste' expansion approach for Asian brands.

Non-focus brands (~8 brands each contributing <10%) remain profitable units and will not be shut, but no further expansion planned for these as part of company strategy for upcoming years (decision taken post-pandemic to pause other brands).

subsections.label: Delivery model across brands
points: Each cuisine requires different equipment and manpower scale; from Mainland China kitchens, company delivers Asia Kitchen, Haka and Gong as well.
Physical outlet brands will continue to have up to 4 different deliveries within the same cuisine family from single kitchens.

subsections.label: Franchise model
points: Franchisee model requires no investment from company; franchisee pays 6% of top line as royalty to the company.
Currently 7 franchisees remain out of a prior count of 11.
Company seeks strategic partners with 'skin in the game' who bring skill, know-how, passion and experience to run restaurants for long-term relationships, rather than purely capital-based takers.

subsections.label: Brand-specific growth plans
points: Asia Kitchen positioned as ideal mall fit, expected to grow alongside growth of malls in India.

Gong targets premium Asian segment with average spend per cover double that of Mainland China, giving higher throughput; after Bandra launch, next outlets planned in Pune (second Gong outlet) and Delhi (Vasant Kunj).
Management believes Mainland China and Asia Kitchen could scale to near 50 restaurants over the next 5 years ('very close to that number').

Walters: 15 new stores planned this year, taking total to 20 stores for the brand; operational hours being extended (deliveries favorable until 3-4 a.m.); new product lines including focused dessert and beverage lines planned; commissary set up in Maharashtra geared for 20-25 stores.

Sweet Bengal: rebranding in process (delayed), to be launched soon; new product lines planned; FMCG packaging ranges under consideration once rebranding, store refresh and new product lines are activated.

subsections.label: Occupancy / capacity utilization
points: Occupancy is a mixed bag depending on individual restaurant; Gong (highest price point) has comparatively low overall occupancy given business distribution skewed toward weekends vs weekdays.
On average, based on installed capacity of covers, company operates at around 2x of existing capacity on average basis.

subsections.label: Store maturity
points: Except for openings during the year, rest of the stores are all mature, as company targets breakeven between 4 to 6 months of restaurant opening.

subsections.label: Renovation program
points: Renovation/refurbishment underway after 10-11 years, starting with Andheri West, then Pune, then Bangalore, with around 4 restaurants refreshed as of April onward.
Renovation expected to reverse SSG slowdown, particularly for Mainland China, with management expecting double-digit SSG going forward.

subsections.label: Capex per store economics
points: Capex for Sweet Bengal and Walters is much lower than Mainland China/Asia Kitchen as these are smaller-format stores.
Standard restaurant footprint targeted at 2,500-3,000 sq ft maximum; Gong (high-end brand) targets around 6,000-6,500 sq ft.

subsections.label: LPG/PNG supply crisis response
points: Company formed an Emergency Response Team (ERT, originally formed during pandemic) on March 4, 2026 anticipating disruption to LPG/PNG supply and shift of PNG allocation from 2 bars to 1 bar.
Began importing wok-based induction units from China (~300 units) after prior successful simulation/testing in cloud kitchens lacking fire department gas permissions.
As a debt-free company, such incremental expenditure does not strain finances; company prioritizes maintaining high standards and ensuring 'the show must go on.'
78% of the restaurant chain, including the new Siciliana (Italian) chain, is now running on non-fuel (electric) power; goal to reach 100% conversion within 20 days.

Pilot test at one restaurant showed ~6% cost saving from electric induction versus gas on an apples-to-apples basis, attributed to elimination of pilot-flame wastage (continuous low flame kept burning in gas systems) which is auto-cut in electric induction/fryer systems.
Management expects cost to be same or lower versus traditional LPG/PNG given rising northward trend in gas prices.

subsections.label: Competitive positioning
points: Panda Express entering India via a competitor viewed as different format/category (fast QSR) vs company's fine casual (Mainland China) and casual fun dining (Asia Kitchen) formats; no threat perceived.
Chinese Wok (competitor) raising funding noted by analyst as a signal of consumption possibly moving toward fast QSR; company response is its own digital QSR brand Haka.

subsections.label: Pricing strategy
points: Despite tremendous input cost headwinds (fuel, energy, freight), company took only a 4% price rise, wanting volume increase to mitigate costs without earning extra margin, as company operates in discretionary spend area and does not want to burden customers; philosophy is 'the leader holds the price line.'

subsections.label: Demand resilience / consumer spending
points: Management does not currently see pressure on consumer wallet despite general market concerns about inflation/geopolitical uncertainty (noted in staples/grocery retail sector); company preparing tactical promotions (redemption coupons) similar to pandemic-era tactics to ease customer spend without heavy discounting.

Historically, based on company's upper-middle-class, higher-discretionary-spend clientele, no significant reduction in spend has been observed during past inflationary periods or domestic shocks (apart from COVID), and no change seen in dine-in or delivery patterns.

subsections.label: Input cost inflation
points: Input costs (fuel, energy, freight due to petrol/diesel prices) have risen tremendously, described as 'a very bad patch' on the cost side.
Company took only a 4% price hike despite these headwinds to avoid burdening discretionary-spend customers.

subsections.label: LPG/PNG supply disruption
points: Anticipated disruption to LPG and PNG supply, with PNG allocation cut from 2 bars to 1 bar, described as an unprecedented event 'out of the syllabus,' worse than the pandemic in some respects, linked to a changing world order and international community dependency.
Company mitigating via emergency response team and shift to electric induction cooking equipment, targeting 100% conversion within 20 days from 78% currently.

subsections.label: Consumer discretionary spend risk
points: Potential double-edged risk from inflation: rising food inflation costs on one side and possible cut in discretionary spending on the other, given upper-middle-class clientele; management currently does not see any impact materializing.

subsections.label: Geopolitical uncertainty
points: FY28 revenue target caveated as 'subject to Mr. Trump's behavior,' indicating geopolitical/trade related uncertainty is viewed as a risk to outlook.

subsections.label: Revenue and growth targets
points: Management agreed with an analyst's suggestion of ~15% revenue growth for FY27 given new launches, and indicated it could be 'more.'
Implied targets: ~INR 600 crores topline in FY27 and ~INR 700 crores by FY28 at a slower pace, caveated 'subject to Mr. Trump's behavior' (referring to geopolitical/trade uncertainty).
EBITDA expected to improve 15-16% in line with revenue increase, tempered by front-end costs of new restaurants opening over the next 2 years.

subsections.label: SSG outlook
points: Following renovation of key restaurants (starting Andheri West, Pune, Bangalore), management expects SSG to move to double digits in coming quarters, as already signaled by April SSG of 11.57%.

subsections.label: Network expansion outlook
points: 32 new outlets planned this year (8 restaurants, 15 Walters, 10 Sweet Bengal), taking total touchpoints from 121 (as of March 31, 2026) to over 150 by end of FY27; growth is expected to continue year after year.

themes.label: Same-store sales growth recovery
themes.note: SSG improved sharply to 11.57% in April from 1.49% for FY26, driven by store renovations and higher dine-in covers; management guides to double-digit SSG going forward.

themes.label: Cash generation and capital allocation

key_takeaways: Company has been making consistent profits for the last 19 quarters, with revenue CAGR of 12.39% and PAT CAGR of 11.16% over the last 5 years.
Revenues during the quarter grew by 13.65% year-on-year, with profit after tax increasing by 44.20%.
The improvement in profitability is supported by same-store sales growth of 2.25% in the quarter compared to the previous year.
Gross margins improved from 69.1% to 70.4% because of efficiencies despite inflationary trends, aiding profitability improvement.

VOEPL.about: Incorporated in 2015, Virtuoso Optoelectronics Ltd is a manufacturer of White Goods and also offers Electronics Manufacturing Services[1]

quarters.summary: Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose to INR 376.6 crores (~85% YoY, ~18.7% QoQ over a strong Q4 FY26), with EBITDA margin steady at ~9.3% and PAT up ~103% YoY to INR ~9 crore. Management reiterated FY27 revenue CAGR guidance of 35-40% for the next 3-5 years and EBITDA margin guidance of 9-10% for FY27, with margin improvement expected to flow through mainly from next year as raw material pricing stabilizes; capacity expansion across AC, EMS, deep freezers and compressors is underway with utilization targeted above 75% on an aggregate basis, and a possible upward revision to guidance to be assessed after Q3.

key_figures.label: Commercial refrigeration revenue at full utilization

subsections.label: Margin trajectory
points: EBITDA and EBIT behaved similarly in Q1 FY27; margins stayed at levels similar to Q4 FY26 (~9.3%).

Pressure on margins in the quarter was attributed to raw material issues that have persisted; pricing is expected to stabilize over the next couple of quarters as price increases requested from customers/market average out.

Margin improvement in AC business is expected to come from next year rather than this year given raw material and dollar/RM fluctuation uncertainty tied to the 'fluid war situation' and shipment issues.
Difference between OEM and ODM model margins is not significant — about 1% to 1.5%.

Compressor EBITDA currently at about 5-6%/6-7% (6% plus/minus 1%); improvement of a percent or two expected once backward integration is complete and existing manufacturer inventory is consumed, expected next financial year.
EBITDA margins expected to move closer to 10% from current 9.3% once raw material pricing stabilizes and buying-range bandwidth is known; 9.3% is still considered a healthy number.

subsections.label: Working capital and financing
points: Net working capital days at 85 for end of Q1.
Higher interest cost (~INR1.5 crore increase) is primarily attributed at the consolidated level to the OCDs (optionally convertible debentures) taken on.
Cost of borrowing on the OCDs is in the mid-teens.

Compressor project (total value ~INR500 crore including scale-up and backward integration) — first phase funded via ongoing equity raise and INR150 crore OCD debt, covering the business up to mid of next year; funding mode (debt vs equity) for subsequent phases to be decided over the next 12 months.
Company plans to maintain a balance of debt and equity going forward to avoid overstretching; primary funding source continues to be debt with a healthy equity balance.
Debt-equity ratio expected to remain in the same region for the next 12 months.
This year's fundraising round is ongoing; further funds may be raised next year or the year after as required, but planned expansion is largely tied up.

subsections.label: Standalone vs consolidated anomaly
points: Standalone and consolidated top-line show little difference currently because Virtuoso Optoelectronics is buying for Virtuoso Compressors (an anomaly); this is expected to normalize going forward.

subsections.label: Depreciation
points: Sequential fall in depreciation from Q4 FY26 to Q1 FY27 explained by a one-time ROU (right-of-use) component accounted for the first time in Q4 FY26, which has since normalized; current Q1 level considered the steady-state number going forward unless new ROU or fixed assets are added.

subsections.label: Segment mix strategy
points: High growth verticals (AC, compressor) are being balanced against slightly better-EBITDA verticals (components, EMS, refrigeration) to achieve diversification in both top line and bottom line.

AC revenue share expected to remain around 60% next financial year because AC is one of the faster growing segments among the company's product categories, despite capacity build-out in EMS, deep freezers and compressor.

subsections.label: AC customer concentration
points: AC revenue now comes from four to five different customers versus heavy reliance previously.
Biggest AC customer (implied Voltas) contribution has come down from in excess of 60% in FY26 to 40-45% currently, with a forward expectation of 25-35% as diversification continues.
One or two customers expected at 30-40% and one or two at 10-20% for the coming season.

Historic supply chain disruption with the core AC customer has stabilized; prices have stabilized; management characterizes this as part of a historical 3-4 year bad cycle that has now passed, with steadier cycles hoped for the next 3-4 years.
Management declined to name AC customers beyond confirming Voltas, citing relationship considerations; confirmed actively working to add both small and large new AC customers.

subsections.label: Compressor customer base
points: Working with almost 8-9 customers across the compressor industry, covering the majority of refrigeration product manufacturers.
Earlier customers currently take a larger share of compressor business, but this is expected to even out by year-end, with no single customer expected to exceed 20-23%.

subsections.label: Deep freezer customer base
points: Three primary customers plus two-three smaller customers; larger customers expected to contribute 25-35% of segment revenue.

subsections.label: Component business (VPPL/Chennai/Sanand)
points: Rationale for keeping VCPL/VPPL separate from listed entity VOEPL: enables focused teams, transparency, and fair treatment of external customers versus captive requirements since components are a critical product for multiple customers including VOEPL itself.
About 15% of VPPL's business comes from VOEPL (captive), with remaining 85% going to external customers.
About 5-7% of Sanand plant output is directed to Nasik for plastic extrusion sheets required for the refrigeration business.
Compressor captive requirement is about 2-3% of overall sales, with the remainder going to external customers.
Both Chennai and Sanand component plants are 'picking up numbers' and the company hopes to keep building on this segment.

subsections.label: Commercial refrigeration
points: Onboarded another marquee customer in commercial refrigeration.

Q1 was slightly slower for commercial refrigeration due to a price increase that the market (B2B, shopkeepers/end consumers) did not immediately absorb, deferring buying decisions; Q1 projections have deferred to Q2/Q3 but overall full-year projections/indications remain unchanged.
Entered medicinal refrigerator segment in addition to hard top and glass top rail; plans to soon enter the Vizi Cooler segment.

Peak revenue potential from commercial refrigeration at full utilization (400,000 capacity) estimated at INR 600 crore; a more realistic 60-70% utilization for this seasonal product implies about INR 360 crore revenue at ~INR15,000 average cost per unit (240,000 units).

subsections.label: Washing machine business
points: This year focus remains majorly on the existing anchor customer; additional customers will be considered once the product is scaled up with more variety and larger capacity.
No new product category planned for the current financial year beyond adding sizes/models within existing categories (AC sizes, commercial refrigeration models, Vizi Cooler).

subsections.label: Backward integration
points: Deepening backward integration on EMS and CFF plastics planned for H1 FY27.
Company is moving up the value chain by becoming an ODM, with R&D focus on high potential categories like AC given a strong order book for the forthcoming season.

Compressor consolidation: acquired a 22-acre land parcel for consolidating compressor business at one location; expansion will continue and operations will be moved to the new location over the next one to three years.
Backward integration for compressor includes localization of shell manufacturing and motor assembly.

subsections.label: Capacity build-out timing
points: Compressor production began in late December of the prior year and is running about three months ahead of the original schedule.
For AC, capacity utilization of more than 60-65% is difficult to achieve immediately for this seasonal product; ramp happens over time.
Compressor capacity added will need 12-24 months to reach desired utilization due to customer validation cycles and approvals.

Commercial refrigeration current manufacturing unit will max out at 400,000 capacity; beyond that, a larger CapEx for a separate facility would be required, but this has not yet been planned; company intends to fully utilize (sweat) the current asset before further expansion.
Compressor AC-specific compressor manufacturing has not been finalized; only refrigeration compressor is confirmed to date; company will revisit AC compressor plans if a suitable opportunity arises.

subsections.label: Group structure rationale
points: Separate entity (VCPL/VPPL) structure allows focused management teams, ensures transparency in dealing with customers, and avoids giving partial treatment to captive manufacturing requirements versus external customers for critical products.

subsections.label: Compressor vertical consolidation
points: Acquired a 22-acre parcel of land for further consolidation of the compressor business at one location; capacity will continue to expand and operations will be moved to the new location over the next one to three years.

subsections.label: PLI 2.0
points: PLI 2.0 is more focused on the component ecosystem; company has plans to take advantage of it but will share details once scheme guidelines are finalized and the company's own plans are more consolidated.

subsections.label: Raw material and input cost pressure
points: Margin pressure in Q1 attributed to persistent raw material issues across the refrigeration and air conditioning industries.
Compressor supply chain has heavy dependence on imports, which is indirectly dependent on the dollar, adding to cost volatility.
Logistics became more tedious and expensive due to shipment delays.
Primary imported components facing challenges: copper, aluminium (still predominantly imported), and compressors.

Government has introduced QCO (Quality Control Order) guidelines; Indian captive capacities for these components are coming online and sampling with domestic suppliers is ongoing, expected to smoothen out over a few months.
Some cost impact on the electronic side (PCB/chips) but no significant direct impact so far from the chip segment.
Commodity prices are trending upward again currently; company manages inventory based on customer projections rather than pre-emptively stocking.

subsections.label: PLI incentive phase-out
points: PLI benefits (currently availed, covering this year) are set to go away in 2027; discussions with customers on how to pass on the impact are ongoing and expected to conclude over the next 12 months.
Effective impact of PLI is about 1% of the company's overall EBITDA (specifically in the AC business).

Management does not believe the removal of PLI will sway the OEM/brand vs ODM/OEM equation in a specific direction, though there is a wishful view that the lack of direct brand benefit might slightly favor outsourcing; actual impact will play out over time.

subsections.label: Commercial refrigeration demand deferral
points: Q1 was subdued for commercial refrigeration due to a price increase that the B2B market (shopkeepers/end consumers) did not immediately absorb, deferring buying decisions.

subsections.label: Customer concentration / management change risk (AC vertical)
points: Historical disruption at the core AC customer (implied Voltas) related to management changes; company believes this is now more stabilized with better projections and plans in place for the next year.

subsections.label: Guidance reiteration
points: Management maintains the 35-40% revenue CAGR guidance and 9-10% EBITDA margin guidance for FY27, noting Q1 growth and healthy order book support the plan.

Q1 and Q4 are the company's biggest quarters; Q1 has given a slight head start, but a decision on upward revision of guidance will be made after seeing how Q3 goes — an update is expected at the end of Q3.

Management explicitly declined to revise FY28 revenue estimates upward when prompted (staying with 35-40% CAGR guidance) despite implied peak revenue potential of INR2,000 crore being floated by an analyst.

subsections.label: AC vertical outlook
points: Strong order book visibility for the forthcoming AC season is expected to underpin achievement of full-year numbers.
AC margins are under pressure from raw-material costs and are expected to improve mainly from next year rather than this year.
AC revenue share expected to remain around 60% next financial year, as AC continues to be one of the faster growing segments.

subsections.label: Compressor vertical outlook
points: Government restricts compressor imports to 40% currently; company hopes this cap will reduce over the next year or two, increasing available addressable market.
Compressor EBITDA margin expected to improve by a percent or two mainly from next financial year, once backward integration and inventory consumption at other manufacturers progress.

subsections.label: Segment revenue guidance for FY27
points: AC to remain 55-60% of overall revenue; EMS ~10%; commercial refrigeration ~10%; components/washing machine/other ~5%; compressor to move up to ~15% of overall revenue (from 8% prior year).
