risk_register.risk: Raw material price pressure (copper, aluminium, compressors - imported)
risk_register.note: Persistent RM issues pressured Q1 margins; pricing now expected to stabilize over the next couple of quarters as price increases are passed through.

risk_register.risk: Dollar/currency and import dependence in compressor supply chain
risk_register.note: Compressor supply chain heavily dependent on imports, indirectly dependent on the dollar; uncertainty continues from 'fluid war situation' and shipment issues.

risk_register.risk: Logistics disruption
risk_register.note: Logistics became more tedious and expensive due to shipment delays; management indicates most of the disruption is now past.

risk_register.risk: PLI incentive phase-out (2027)
risk_register.note: PLI benefits going away in 2027; ~1% EBITDA impact in AC business; discussions with customers ongoing, to conclude over next 12 months.

risk_register.risk: Commercial refrigeration demand deferral (pricing pass-through)
risk_register.note: Q1 slower due to price increase not immediately absorbed by B2B market; overall year projections unchanged, growth expected by year-end.

risk_register.risk: AC customer concentration / historical management-change disruption
risk_register.note: Historical disruption at core AC customer has stabilized; diversification has reduced top customer share from >60% (FY26) to 40-45% currently.

risk_register.risk: Government import restriction changes on compressors
risk_register.note: Government currently restricts compressor imports to 40%; expected to reduce in next year or two, which would expand addressable market for the company.

risk_register.risk: Seasonal capacity utilization constraints (AC, refrigeration)
risk_register.note: Being seasonal products, immediate utilization above 60-65% is difficult; ramp happens over time and requires 12-24 months validation cycles for new capacity.

risk_register.risk: Commodity price uptrend
risk_register.note: Current trend in commodity prices is again moving upward; company manages inventory based on customer projections rather than pre-stocking.

risk_register.risk: Raw material price volatility/inflation
risk_register.note: Margin pressure from RM cost increases has been compensated via price hikes; RM rates remain uncertain in the market, pricing not fully immune to fluctuation until rates settle.

risk_register.risk: Ind AS transition impact on PBT/PAT
risk_register.note: First year of Ind AS adoption; right-of-use assets impacted the EBITDA-to-margin waterfall, and I-GAAP to Ind AS adjustments took a toll on PAT margin this year.

risk_register.risk: Import policy dependency for compressor margins
risk_register.note: Compressor margins are dictated by the quantum of Chinese imports the government allows; current 40% relaxation keeps margins at 6-7% this year.

risk_register.risk: PLI scheme expiry/uncertainty
risk_register.note: This year is expected to be the last year for the PLI scheme; no concrete roadmap yet on renewal, though government reportedly working on options to support the industry.

risk_register.risk: AC capacity constraint limiting customer additions
risk_register.note: Capacity was fully utilized in the last 1-2 months, preventing the company from adding new AC customers this year despite ongoing customer talks.

risk_register.risk: Competitive entry in compressor segment
risk_register.note: Two competitors are planning entry into the compressor OEM/ODM market over the next year or so, which could affect market share, though demand gap is expected to remain large enough.

risk_register.risk: Energy crisis, commodity inflation, BEE norm change
risk_register.note: Cited by an analyst as an industry headwind; company says margins were protected via components mix, ODM shift, customer support, and product diversification despite these factors.

risk_register.risk: Execution risk on capex/expansion plans
risk_register.note: Last year's market slowdown led to conserving cash and not pushing non-essential projects; 100% execution of plans is not always in the company's control, e.g. prior target of 150K-400K freezer capacity did not materialize as originally planned.

themes.label: Segment diversification away from AC
themes.note: Non-AC revenue share now ~40%; compressor mix rising to ~15% from 8%; AC customer concentration reduced from >60% to 40-45%.

themes.label: Compressor capacity ramp-up
themes.note: Compressor capacity moving from 2.8 million to 6 million units, running 3 months ahead of schedule at >50% utilization; 22-acre land parcel acquired for consolidation.

themes.label: Import policy / localization tailwind
themes.note: Government restricts compressor imports to 40%, expected to ease in 1-2 years, expanding addressable market; QCO guidelines driving domestic sourcing for copper/aluminium.

themes.label: Raw material cost pass-through
themes.note: RM cost pressure hit Q1 margins; price pass-through to customers ongoing with margin improvement expected mainly from next year.

themes.label: OEM to ODM transition in AC
themes.note: ODM vs OEM margin difference is not significant, about 1-1.5%; AC margin improvement pushed to next year.

themes.label: Capacity expansion funding via debt
themes.note: Compressor project (~INR500 crore) funded via equity raise and INR150 crore OCD debt for phase one; remaining funding mode to be decided within 12 months; debt-equity ratio to stay in same region.

themes.label: Revenue growth guidance reiteration
themes.note: 35-40% revenue CAGR and 9-10% EBITDA margin guidance for FY27 reiterated; possible upward revision to be assessed after Q3.

key_takeaways: On a consolidated level, the company achieved INR 376.6 crores worth of revenue, an ~85% jump versus Q1 FY26 and an 18.7% jump over Q4 FY26.
EBITDA margins stayed at similar levels compared with Q4 FY26, at 9.3%-odd.
At a PAT level, there was a very significant jump when compared with Q1 FY26, almost 103%, moving from INR6.4 crores to INR9 crore.
Going forward in FY27, the company aims for utilization levels in excess of 75% on an aggregate level and is deepening backward integration on EMS and CFF plastics in H1 FY27.
Compressor production has already begun (from end of December) and is running at more than 50% utilization, about three months ahead of schedule.

EMS capacity moving from 4 lakh cph to 12 lakh cph in two phases; AC capacity moving from 1 million to 1.8 million over 12-15 months; deep freezer capacity moving from 1.5 lakh to 4 lakh units in two phases; compressor capacity moving from 2.8 million to 6 million by December/January.
The company continues to maintain its FY27 guidance of 35-40% revenue CAGR for the next 3-5 years and 9-10% EBITDA margin, with a possible upward revision to be evaluated after Q3.
Compressor consolidation: acquired a 22-acre parcel of land for further consolidation of the compressor business at one location.
AC top customer (Voltas) concentration has reduced from in excess of 60% in FY26 to 40-45% currently within the AC vertical, with a forward expectation of 25-35%.
pressing_questions: Are we some sort of revising the guidance for the entire year? I think the guidance was 35%, 40%, but we have grown much better than that.
Sir, one more last question - like once the plant reach the minimum utilization, how much additional revenue and ROCE do you expect?

Given the government push for localization and QCO link compressor imports exemptions extended till March 27, how is VOEPL planning to scale this beyond 50% utilization to beat this target of 50% revenue share and what are the margin profile expected once full work order integration is achieved?

quarters.summary: Virtuoso Optoelectronics closed FY26 with 18% revenue growth and improved EBITDA margins after a challenging H1 that was fully recovered in H2, led by a strong Q4. Management guided to a 35-40% revenue CAGR over the next 3-5 years, capacity expansion across all four segments (EMS, AC, refrigeration, compressor), and expects EBITDA margins around 9-10% in FY27 with PAT margin improvement of 50-100 bps over the next two years, while reiterating (not revising) the growth guidance despite a lower absolute FY27 revenue expectation than earlier flagged.

subsections.label: Full year performance drivers
points: Year defined the resilience of Virtuoso despite a very challenging H1 with multiple factors at play; the company recovered the entire year through the last six months.
PBT levels remained more or less stagnant because this is the first year the company moved to Ind AS, and right-of-use assets played a role in the waterfall from EBITDA to margins.
Q4 FY26 was the mainstay of the company's comeback for the year, beating an already excellent Q4 FY25.

subsections.label: Employee expense increase
points: Employee expenses increased in Q4 because the company started small and, as it diversified, is creating a structure with new hires across multiple locations (two plants in Chennai, one in Sanand, multiple locations in Nasik).
Company is establishing a business-unit-head methodology with each business headed by a unit head, adding to hierarchy and cost, but nothing extraordinary beyond that.

subsections.label: Trade receivables
points: Trade receivables increase this year is a normal thing; numbers are at par with what one would expect, no trouble in cash collection.

subsections.label: Capital allocation
points: INR250 crore is a blanket equity approval taken by the company; it does not mean the company will actually raise that amount or on a specific timeline.
INR150 crore approval is for the subsidiary and is the exact amount needed for the first phase of compressor expansion from 2.8 million to 6 million units.
AC segment capex will primarily be funded via debt; company aims to maintain a debt-equity ratio of about 1:1.

PAT margin fell owing to adjustments from I-GAAP to Ind AS transition this year; going forward PAT margin should improve by 50-100 bps over the next two years, though exact numbers cannot be predicted.

subsections.label: Diversification away from AC dependence
points: Till last year the company was more of a single-product company with heavy dependence on AC, contributing ~70-75% of revenues; this has now come down to ~60% with the balance ~40% coming from other segments (EMS, refrigeration, components, compressor), an encouraging trend expected to help in the long run.
AC is expected to stabilize around 50-60% of revenue going forward as a target for healthy diversification, though this is not a hard line and could vary by seasonality and product mix.
Compressor contributed a good revenue share despite only three months of actual production being available last year; this year's contribution is expected to be even higher.

subsections.label: AC / RAC business
points: Moved from OEM to ODM model in AC segment last year, which helped acquire additional customers and is expected to continue helping going forward.

AC margins have not necessarily improved from ODM shift yet but this helped protect margins under RM cost pressure; realizations have remained largely stagnant despite the ODM shift, though there is hope of getting a little more given ODM status.
Currently catering to 4 AC customers; in talks to finalize new ones but capacity constraints in the last 1-2 months limited additions this year; hopeful of 1-2 new names next season.
RAC demand: numbers for March were strong and April-May-June also look on course for an excellent quarter; growth of ~30-40% is targeted for FY27 RAC volumes.

RAC utilization target of 60-65% is considered very healthy based on company's understanding and experience, targeted on increased capacity of 1.3 million (conservatively can consider 60-65% base on current 1 million capacity as new capacity comes online blended across the year).

subsections.label: Commercial refrigeration
points: In addition to hardtop deep freezers already being manufactured, the company has added a glass-top range.

subsections.label: Compressor business
points: Started commercial production of compressors in January; running at ~60% capacity utilization in the fifth/sixth month of production, with confidence of reaching ~80% utilization in the next two to three months.

Current value addition on compressors is 5-10%, expected to remain at these levels until capacity targets are hit; post that, backward integration phase aims to take value addition to ~60% odd in the next five years.

Compressor margins are a two-factor story: dictated by the quantum of Chinese imports allowed (currently 40% relaxation vs earlier 100%) and margins are expected to stay between 6-7% this year, with potential to move closer to double digits in the next 2 years with complete stoppage of imports; over next 4-5 years hope to hit 11-12%.
Enough customer interest exists that gives confidence the additional compressor capacity will be booked fast; company is confident it will secure enough clients/pipeline for expanded capacity.

subsections.label: Product mix presentation correction
points: There was a correction noted in the presentation: the revenue share figures presented were actually a 12-month (full year) revenue share, not a 9-month figure as initially labeled; this will be rectified.

key_figures.label: AC current capacity base for utilization target

subsections.label: Capacity expansion across four segments
points: Capacities have been set up in all four segments (EMS/lighting, AC, refrigeration incl. commercial refrigeration, and compressor); going forward the focus is to increase utilization of existing assets while also increasing capacity further.
New EMS facility being added altogether, an advanced facility compared to the current one; phase 1 to complete in the next three months (by end of August), phase 2 by end of this FY.
AC capacity move from 1 million to 1.8 million is incremental, targeting 1.3 million before the AC season and 1.8 million by end of this FY.
Deep freezer capacity expansion happens in two phases; first phase targeted to complete before the start of the forthcoming season.
Compressor capacity expansion from 2.8 million to 6 million is a 9-10 month journey, expected to complete by March; work has already started.

Last year's overall market slowdown led the company to conserve cash and not push non-essential projects; expansion continues to be part of strategy based on demand and resource availability, but 100% execution of plans is not always in the company's control.

subsections.label: Compressor capacity trajectory clarification
points: Prior guidance was to take compressor capacity to 7.5 million by this year end; current target is 6 million — the initial plan was always two phases (2.8mn to 5mn, then to 7.5mn), so there is no change in plans, it's just that the current phase targets 6 million to optimize line productivity and minimize operational costs, not because of the government QCO order.
If demand and long-term contracts allow, the company will look at increasing capacity further to 7.5 million, 9 million, or even 9.5-10 million in the next financial year.
Backward integration for compressors is planned as phase 2 of the strategy, targeting ~60% value addition in the next five years, once capacity targets are hit.

subsections.label: Backward integration and new facilities
points: Company continues deepening backward integration philosophy (EPS, plastics, CFF, EMS capabilities) as it has over the last six-seven years.
New tool room in Nasik has become operational and is being scaled, improving turnaround times for product development.
Compressor subsidiary (Virtuoso Compressors Private Limited) is looking to set up a separate manufacturing facility of its own in Nasik; development work expected to start shortly.

Virtuoso Polymers subsidiary has two units — one in Sanand and one in Chennai; Chennai being the first year of operation is not expected to contribute a massive number, maybe 5-6% contribution if achievable.

subsections.label: Revenue potential of expansion
points: The current set of expansion (annualized, accounting for seasonality) is good enough to take the company beyond INR2,500 crores, though management noted a jump from INR800 crores to INR2,500 crores in two years is a big ask that will probably come but take a little more time.

key_figures.label: Raw material price pass-through to customers

subsections.label: Demand environment
points: AC segment is seeing enough and good demand, helped by the ODM shift and a small existing base giving a long growth runway; March numbers were strong and April-May-June also look on course for an excellent quarter.
EMS and refrigeration segments also have enough demand, evidenced by the company's expansion plans in both.
Company believes there will be two or three active players in the compressor segment within a year or two, creating healthy competition, but still believes it can fill 6 million units of capacity.

subsections.label: Competitive landscape - compressors
points: Two competitors are known to be planning entry into the compressor OEM/ODM market, with local manufacturing expected to start by end of Q3/Q4 or early Q4 for one, and mid next year for another.
Currently, the company understands nobody else is doing reciprocating compressors in the OEM/ODM segment domestically.
Market share, pricing, and product/service quality of each manufacturer will determine how the competitive landscape evolves.

subsections.label: Raw material pass-through
points: Raw material price pass-through to customers has been about 10-15% as a ballpark figure across the industry (from manufacturers to brands to end consumers) over the last five-six volatile months; the exact pass-through varies by customer and product and is not a fixed number.
Pricing increases are an industry-wide phenomenon, not specific to Virtuoso, and customers are acknowledging this and trying to help manufacturers.

key_figures.label: Number of expected new compressor competitors

subsections.label: Corporate structure
points: VOEPL is the flagship listed company with two subsidiaries: Virtuoso Compressors Private Limited and Virtuoso Polymers.
Virtuoso Polymers has two units — one at Sanand and one in Chennai; Compressor subsidiary is looking to set up its own separate manufacturing facility in Nasik.

subsections.label: Mainboard migration
points: Company has received in-principle approval from BSE for mainboard migration; expecting in-principle approval from NSE in the next week or so.
Beyond NSE approval, another four to six weeks are required for the actual migration/listing to happen; safe to assume completion by end of August, though management hopes it does not take that long.

subsections.label: OEM to ODM transition
points: Shift from OEM to ODM model in the AC segment last year was a significant strategic move that helped acquire additional customers and is expected to continue benefiting the company going forward.
No finalized plans yet to manufacture rotary compressors (used for AC) — only reciprocating compressors for refrigerators are currently being made.

subsections.label: Raw material cost volatility
points: Whatever margin pressure came from increased raw material prices has been compensated by price hikes, but no real gain — margins were just protected, not enhanced.
Uncertainty remains in RM rates in the market; until final RM/market price settles, pricing cannot be completely immune to fluctuation.
Impact was mitigated through a combination of factors: addition of customers, use of old inventory, government support via subsidies, and product diversification.

subsections.label: Ind AS transition impact
points: This is the first year of moving to Ind AS; right-of-use assets played a role in the waterfall from EBITDA to margins, keeping PBT levels largely stagnant despite EBITDA improvement.
Adjustments from I-GAAP to Ind AS took a toll on PAT margin this year.

subsections.label: Import policy dependency (compressors)
points: Compressor margins depend heavily on the quantum of Chinese imports allowed by government policy; currently a 40% relaxation vs the earlier 100% import scenario dictates near-term margins staying at 6-7%.

If import restrictions had been imposed at 100% immediately, there would have been chaos in the market since Virtuoso is currently the only OEM/ODM reciprocating compressor manufacturer; hence a calibrated step-by-step approach was taken by the government.

subsections.label: PLI scheme uncertainty
points: This year would be the last year for the PLI scheme; there is no concrete roadmap yet from government on renewal, though the government is reportedly working on some options to support the industry.

subsections.label: Capacity constraints limiting customer additions
points: During the last 1-2 months, AC capacity was fully utilized, creating a capacity constraint that prevented adding new AC customers this year.

subsections.label: Competitive entry risk (compressors)
points: Two competitors are planning to enter the compressor OEM/ODM market over the next year or so, which could affect the demand-supply balance, though management still expects enough demand gap to absorb its own expanded capacity.

key_figures.label: Compressor margin trajectory
key_figures.value: 6-7% this year, moving toward 11-12% in 4-5 years

subsections.label: Growth guidance reiteration
points: Management clarified that FY27 revenue is not being revised down; the guidance of 35-40% CAGR on an INR825 crore base remains the same, and exact numbers will be shared over the course of the year.
Company is not hardlining the AC-to-non-AC mix target; 50-60% AC share is a ballpark guidance for healthy diversification, subject to change with seasonality and product mix.

subsections.label: Margin outlook
points: AC margins expected to remain where they are this year barring macroeconomic jolts.

Compressor margins expected to move from 6-7% this year toward double digits over the next 2 years (with complete stoppage of Chinese imports) or over 4-5 years to 11-12% (combining import restrictions and backward integration).
Overall EBITDA margin for FY27 is expected to be closer to double digits, specifically between 9% and 10% (management called the earlier suggestion of 12% 'a very wishful number').

Q4 FY26 was the mainstay of the comeback, with revenue of INR317 crores vs INR240 crores in Q4 FY25

TIPSMUSIC.about: Tips Industries Limited, incorporated in 1996, is engaged in the business of Production and Distribution of motion Pictures and acquisition and exploitation of Music of Rights. The co is also a leading producer of Punjabi films in the country. [1][2]

quarters.summary: Management maintained guidance of 20% revenue growth and 20% PAT growth for FY'27, with content acquisition budget guided at INR90-100 crores for the year (20-25% of revenue over the long term). Q2 onward is expected to see full revenue impact of Q1 releases; YouTube Shorts renewal deal update expected by end of Q2 FY'27; Board to evaluate open market vs tender-offer buyback on August 5, 2026, with a commitment to distribute last year's PAT of INR217 crores via dividend and buyback this year.

key_figures.label: Last year's PAT to be distributed as dividend/buyback
Cost per song increase multiple (FY26 vs Q1 FY27)

subsections.label: Content cost accounting policy
points: As per conservative accounting policy, the entire content cost of new releases is expensed in the quarter of release, while corresponding revenue only started coming from mid-May, causing a mismatch between cost and revenue recognition timing in Q1.
Content cost increased 90% YoY driven by new releases, primarily film music which is inherently more expensive than non-film/regional music released in the comparative period last year.

subsections.label: PAT degrowth explanation
points: PAT declined 4% YoY in Q1 FY27 despite 21% revenue growth, attributable to the front-loaded expensing of content costs for new releases against only partial revenue recognition in the quarter.

subsections.label: EBITDA margin dynamics
points: EBITDA margin should be evaluated on an annual basis rather than quarterly, since quarterly numbers see aberrations due to timing of content releases and cost recognition.
On an annual basis, margin is expected to remain in the 65-70% range as previously maintained historically.

subsections.label: Employee cost trend
points: In the December quarter, due to a change in the labor code, several full-time consultants were moved onto payroll, which reduced other expenses and increased employee costs, but the net impact on profit was nil.
Employee cost is expected to remain at a similar quarterly run rate as Q1 for the full year.

subsections.label: Cash distribution / capital allocation policy
points: Cash distribution policy is primarily linked to PAT earned in the prior year, distributed via dividend and buyback in the current year, rather than being linked to any accumulated war chest.
Company remains committed to distributing last year's PAT of INR217 crores this year via dividend and buyback.
Buyback quantum will depend on maximum limits allowed by exchanges/SEBI once policy specifics are finalized.

subsections.label: Content cost per song not a reliable metric
points: Comparing content cost per song YoY is not the right metric because this quarter's releases were primarily film music (more expensive) versus last year's releases which were primarily non-film and regional music (less expensive).

Company maintains a conservative approach in acquisitions, avoids bidding wars, and divides content sourcing roughly 1/3 from Tips Films, 1/3 from outside production houses, and 1/3 internally produced (non-film), limiting cost pressure.

key_figures.label: "Hai Jawani Toh Ishq Hona Hai" YouTube views
Revenue from content released in last 3 years (new songs)
Revenue from catalog spanning past 3 decades (old songs)
Music library addition (Gujarati catalog)
key_figures.period: added by end of Q4 FY26

subsections.label: New release performance
points: Key releases 'Hai Jawani Toh Ishq Hona Hai' and 'Main Vaapas Aaunga' received an encouraging response from audiences.
'Tere Liye' from the movie 'Prince' secured a position among the top 10 songs on Spotify's daily charts, highlighting the enduring appeal of the music library and catalog.
Female versions of 'Tere Paas Mein' witnessed strong traction on Spotify.

subsections.label: Growth softness explanation (Q1 FY27 vs prior quarters)
points: The two movie releases this quarter got released mid-May and during June, so the full revenue impact is not reflected in this quarter's numbers; full impact will be seen from Q2 onwards.

Management would not comment on digital vs non-digital breakdown separately, but noted digital segment contributed around 75% of revenue in the quarter, which is considered healthy, with both digital and non-digital expected to grow as the year progresses.

subsections.label: Subscription vs advertising revenue mix
points: Subscription-based revenue currently averages 10-15% of platform revenue in India versus more than 50% globally, where subscription is the main revenue driver.
Most platforms (Spotify, YouTube, others) are pushing more towards subscription, and management expects that percentage to rise in India over the next 3-5 years.
Paid subscribers in India are growing in the range of 40-50% CAGR.

subsections.label: Global vs India per-stream royalty gap
points: The gap between global (INR0.50-0.90 per stream) and India (INR0.04-0.10 per stream) royalty rates is primarily explained by the subscription gap — globally, subscription price is higher and subscription penetration is around 50-60%, whereas in India subscription price is lower and subscription is around 15% of revenue.

subsections.label: Catalog composition / new vs old song revenue
points: Approximately 15% of revenue comes from content released over the last 3 years (new songs), while the balance 85% is spread across the past 3 decades (old catalog).

subsections.label: Music library addition
points: The additional 4,000 songs added to the library (library size moved from ~34,000-38,000 range) resulted from a Gujarati catalog acquired last year; by end of Q4 FY26 the catalog was fully digitized and added to the library.

subsections.label: Industry growth vs company growth
points: Overall music industry growth this year is expected to be in single digits, while the company continues to see strong traction and maintains guidance of 20% growth for itself, driven by content performance and catalog strength.

Management could not comment on why the overall industry pie is growing slower than the subscription sub-segment (growing at 40-50%) despite subscription representing 10-15% of overall revenue; management attributed the company's own higher growth to strong content performance rather than commenting on the broader industry dynamics.

subsections.label: Spotify/platform pricing
points: Spotify revised subscription prices in mid-May; management expects this to increase revenue for the company, with no material impact expected.
As of now, apart from Spotify and YouTube's price hikes at the end of last calendar year, no other player has taken a price hike, though management believes there could be something in the pipeline.
Amazon Music has started its 3-tier structure for non-Prime members, which is viewed as quite positive news for the industry.

subsections.label: Competitive intensity from international players
points: Management does not expect entry of large international players with deeper pockets for content acquisition to create significant impact on the company, citing existing relationships in place and the company's own strong music creation capability (providing music to film companies) as a differentiator.
Company does not compete in the upper bandwidth of content acquisition and focuses on the mid-level segment, aiming to survive competitive intensity better than peers.

subsections.label: Platform revenue dependency
points: Company does not disclose platform-wise revenue share bifurcation (e.g., Spotify) as these are competitive data points.
Management does not see risk from potential platform concentration/dependency, noting platforms also require content from music labels, creating a win-win relationship.

subsections.label: Artist exclusivity practice
points: Company does not have exclusivity arrangements with any major artists and is not in the artist management business; it is focused primarily on the music content business.
Company signs major artists on a song-wise deal basis (1, 2, or 3 songs at a time) rather than long-term exclusivity.

subsections.label: Buyback plan
points: Board has announced a separate Board meeting on August 5, 2026 to consider a buyback of shares.

Board wants to evaluate the open-market-linked buyback option (effective from August 1) in addition to the tender-offer route, before deciding; this caused the buyback agenda to be rescheduled/deferred by a few days from the originally planned date.
Buyback quantum will depend on maximum limits allowed by stock exchanges and SEBI, to be finalized once the policy specifics are clear.

subsections.label: Stake sale/partnership speculation
points: Management clarified there is no stake sale or purchase from the promoters' end; various market rumors circulate quarterly regarding stake sale, but nothing is in the pipeline.
Company is not looking to bring in strategic investments into the company.
Company already has partnerships as the sole distributor for Warner Music and Sony Music Publishing among larger labels, differentiating it in the market.

subsections.label: Leadership position update
points: Following the exit of Mr. Hari Nair, the company is actively searching for a suitable replacement; in the interim, Sushant Dalmia and Girish Taurani are handling responsibilities as business as usual.
Management noted there are very few qualified candidates for this position in the industry, but expects to fill it soon given the position's importance.

subsections.label: Content sourcing mix
points: Company's content sourcing is roughly divided 1/3 from Tips Films (its own production house), 1/3 from outside production houses, and 1/3 produced internally (non-film music), limiting dependency on external production houses.

subsections.label: Content cost recognition mismatch
points: Conservative accounting policy of expensing entire content cost of new releases in the release quarter, while corresponding revenue accrues over subsequent months, creates a quarterly cost-revenue mismatch that can depress reported quarterly PAT and margins even amid revenue growth.

subsections.label: Content cost recovery timeline
points: Content cost recovery (e.g., for a film) does not happen in 1-2 months; it typically takes 4-5 years for full recovery.

For 'Hai Jawani Toh Ishq Hona Hai' (released June 5), money from satellite and OTT rights is yet to fully come in; the accounting cycle is expected to complete in the next 15-20 days (approx. 1.5-2 months from release), after which the film's cost recovery/profitability should become clearer; the film benefited from a subsidy from being shot in London.

subsections.label: Competitive intensity from international entrants
points: Large international players entering the market with significant capital to spend on content acquisition could increase industry-wide content acquisition costs versus levels seen 5 years back.

Management indicated that focusing on the mid-level content segment (rather than competing in the upper bandwidth) may still expose the company to some competitive intensity leading to slightly higher costs than currently, though management does not expect a significant negative impact.

subsections.label: Leadership gap
points: Vacancy following exit of Mr. Hari Nair in a key business development/deals-related role; industry has very few qualified candidates, creating a search challenge.

Company's A&R team ensures good quality music is sourced, and its limited dependency on outside production houses (1/3 of content) reduces cost pressure risk.

subsections.label: EBITDA margin outlook

subsections.label: Quarterly performance drivers
points: Employee cost increased 78% YoY in Q4 FY26 on account of provisions made for annual increments.
Employee count reduced from 105 to 98, and the company would return to earlier Q3/Q2 run rates in terms of employee cost going forward; Q4 provision is on the higher side basis performance.
No one-off revenues contributed to the 32% YoY growth in Q4; growth attributed to repertoire performance.

subsections.label: Content cost accounting policy
points: Content cost fall YoY (15.8% vs 23%) was due to the movie 'Hai Jawani Toh Ishq Hona Hai', originally slated for theatrical release Feb/March and music release in January, being postponed to June, shifting the cost to Q1 FY27.

Company follows a clear policy: once a song of any movie/album is released, the entire album cost is expensed in the P&L on that day; no advances or provisions are carried on the balance sheet for content costs ahead of release, including arrangements with related party Tips Films.
Related-party dealings with Tips Films would be driven by contractual terms, at arm's length and per industry practices.

subsections.label: Capital allocation
points: Company distributed total dividend of INR166 crores to shareholders in FY26.

Management prefers dividends/buybacks over overpaying for content that lacks quality-price match, citing risk of overpaying (e.g., paying INR40 crores for songs generating only INR2-3 crores business, with INR37-38 crores going to drain).

points: The dip in digital revenue mix for FY26 (70% vs 71-75% range in prior three quarters) was due to a couple of platforms closing down during the year, a headwind to digital growth.

Q4 quarterly digital/non-digital split follows the same ~70-30 pattern as full year; quarter-to-quarter mix can fluctuate 2-3% either way and is not considered a concern.

Non-digital revenue increase in Q4 attributed to strong performance across publishing, public performance and brand segments; management believes seasonality causes Q3/Q4 to typically outperform Q1/Q2.

points: The 75% international / 25% domestic split noted in annual report notes to accounts reflects currency of receipt (foreign currency denominated, primarily via YouTube and Warner billing overseas), not actual consumption geography.

Company has recreated many songs, largely drawing from its own catalogue.
Management believes its catalogue is currently the best performing versus other labels.

subsections.label: Bundled services stance

points: Management believes competitors acquiring film companies for content are not necessarily growing from doing so, calling it 'a myth', and considers Tips Music's own selective acquisition policy the best in the industry.

key_takeaways: Company recorded quarterly revenue of INR103.9 crores, delivering a YoY growth of 32%. Operating EBITDA for the quarter stood at INR76.9 crores, reflecting a YoY growth of 106%. Additionally, PAT for Q4 FY26 came in at INR59 crores, making a 93% YoY increase.
For FY26, the revenue came in at INR375.5 crores, marking a 21% growth, while PAT amounted to INR216.6 crores, showing a YoY increase of 30%.
In FY26, the company distributed a total dividend of INR166 crores to shareholders.
Management's target for FY27 is 20% top-line growth and 20% bottom-line growth, kept conservative for now with clarity expected in 1-2 quarters.

points: Head-wise comparison of profitability for Q1 FY26-27 vs Q1 FY25-26 and Q4 FY25-26 was presented, covering raw material, employee cost, finance cost, depreciation, manufacturing expenses and admin/selling/other expenses.
Finance cost has come down significantly due to payoff of loans last year.

Management clarified apparent raw material % change was explained via the detailed profitability comparison sheet, addressing an analyst query on reclassification; management noted stock-in-transit increase affected consumption calculation.

subsections.label: Tax rate explanation
points: Higher current tax liability this quarter arose from differences in depreciation and gratuity treatment as per Income Tax Act versus book accounting.
Higher deferred tax liability arose because of a change in the surcharge rate of income tax, creating a difference on the entire block for deferred tax liability calculation.
Full-year blended tax rate guided at 25.62%.

subsections.label: CAPEX allocation
points: Of the disclosed 77.4 crores CAPEX for the year, about 40 crores is for heat treatment plant replacement (characterized by management as not true capex but a replacement program for old equipment) and the remaining ~30-35% is for additional capacity expansion.

subsections.label: Royal Enfield ramp-up
points: Commercial supplies to Royal Enfield started from January onwards; company has done around 8 months of turnover on this project so far.
Nominated for roughly 10,000 sets per month (motorcycles); company was ramping up and reached a level of 7,500-8,000 sets, sustaining that level currently.
Engine is a 350cc model; multiple additional projects under development for new variants/engine changes are under confidentiality with the customer.

Customer (Royal Enfield) follows a multi-supplier strategy rather than single-source, unlike RACL's export business model; company does not disclose percentage split between itself and other suppliers as this is commercially sensitive.

Management deliberately cautious on scaling up volumes for multi-supplier customers — will only invest in additional capacity once demand sustainability is confirmed, given the capital-intensive nature of the business and risk that volatility hits smaller suppliers first.
Confirmed as a fair assumption that scale-up to full potential (e.g., toward 20,000 units) is deliberate and paced as the customer relationship develops.

subsections.label: Growth composition
points: Revenue growth of ~20-22% last year came from a mixture of existing project growth and new projects across multiple platforms, customers, vehicle models and engine models — described as too comprehensive to break down platform by platform.

No major product is currently at true end-of-life; where a project nears end of life, a successor project with higher value addition typically follows, meaning revenue is not lost but tends to increase.

Historically, over the last 10-15 years, a new customer has been added roughly every two-three years, alongside continuous addition of new models by existing customers — both incremental (new customer) and sustaining (existing base) growth expected going forward.

subsections.label: Sole-supplier vs multi-supplier dynamics
points: In export business, RACL remains the sole supplier for a given component until end-of-life of that product — a formal agreement structure typical of global OEMs (Europe, Japan, US) due to traceability/quality-risk concerns.
Domestic/Indian companies (e.g., Royal Enfield) typically follow a multi-supplier strategy, unlike export customers.

ZF works across many platforms/OEMs (passenger cars, virtual clutch market) via a portal-based RFQ system with no human interface — RACL, as a registered supplier, receives notifications for new RFQs and can choose to participate.

subsections.label: KTM update
points: KTM had faced financial insolvency issues previously but has bounced back and is delivering good numbers, reaching near pre-COVID volumes.

KTM's business ownership context involves Bajaj; RACL's direct relationship remains with KTM Austria (established over 15 years), and there is no direct communication yet with Bajaj for India production, though management is open to opportunities.
KTM has launched a new 'Duke Series 790' model with positive market reception reported in the US market; the entire kinematic (gear train) for that bike is supplied by RACL.
From September, KTM vehicles will start being classified/produced as 'model year 2027'; forecast for coming months is very good.
RACL already has strong presence in Indian two-wheeler industry via Royal Enfield and TVS, independent of any Bajaj-KTM India development.

subsections.label: ZF business
points: ZF business saw sluggishness in recent years due to weak performance of the end product (a high-end premium car under platform sharing) — now shifted to a more mainstream SUV platform (X5), bringing volume traction back.
Currently operating at 50-60% utilization of installed capacity for this project.
Peak year of ZF revenue for this specific project was originally planned for 2028 but has now shifted to 2030 due to volume delays.
Customer has shifted assembly for this program from within Europe to a lower-cost East European location, improving competitiveness and potentially increasing RACL's share.
Early-stage discussions ongoing between ZF's end customer and another OEM for a similar project targeting the Chinese market — still very preliminary.
Separate ZF electric power steering (EPS) project for an American OEM is being invested in; commercial supplies expected to start end of 2027 or mid-2028; described as a big project for RACL.

subsections.label: Royal Enfield / premiumization trend
points: Industry-wide shift of OEMs moving from in-house gear production to outsourcing, driven by OEMs wanting to focus on assembly (described as 'king of the supply chain') and by growing trust in established precision supply chains.
TVS is now launching motorcycles above 350cc more than before; RACL is single source for the entire gear train for all TVS motorcycles, including platforms under Norton and Apache models.
One or two other big OEMs are approaching RACL to expand presence in the premium motorcycle segment.
Royal Enfield investing roughly 6,000-7,000 crores in a new plant near Andhra Pradesh, with focus on motorcycle assembly rather than loose parts production — a driver of the outsourcing shift.

subsections.label: Precision manufacturing capability
points: Difficulty in supplying high-performance vehicle gears is not in making individual samples but in consistently producing at large scale without 100% inspection feasibility (checking one part for practical characteristics takes roughly 30-40 minutes, making full inspection impractical/cost-ineffective at volumes of 100,000-200,000 parts/month).

Success depends on three factors: process capability, traceability (to trace issues back to root cause/batch/date), and technology (e.g., grinding processes) suited to high-RPM applications including EVs and high-performance motorcycles.
Evolution of supply chain trust in India has enabled OEMs to shift from in-house to outsourced high-precision production.

subsections.label: Arc Technologies tie-up
points: Tie-up with Arc Technologies aimed at moving up the value chain from 'build to print' to 'concept to print.'
Currently working with two potential customers on this platform; details to be disclosed once finalized due to confidentiality.

key_figures.label: Heat treatment plant building/construction completion target
Scope 1 emission share from LPG (HT fuel)
Scope 1 emission share from DG sets
Scope 1 emission share from fugitive emissions & company vehicles

subsections.label: Heat treatment plant replacement
points: Entire heat treatment plant being constructed afresh, replacing outdated LPG-based equipment (much of it over 30 years old and past end-of-life) with electric-based furnaces described as state-of-the-art, aligned with the company's machining processes.
Construction progress documented via photos dated January 24, August 16, and August 24.
Management anticipated the energy crisis roughly a year back and took proactive action, though equipment procurement lead times are long.
If all goes to plan, trial production targeted by January 2027 with full commissioning expected by end of financial year, after which entire production will switch to the new facility.

subsections.label: ESG / carbon footprint
points: Gajraula plant runs entirely on 100% green energy and generates no Scope 2 carbon emissions from that site.
Scope 2 emissions (321 tons) are predominantly from the Noida unit and corporate office; company plans to set up rooftop solar at Noida to reduce this.
Scope 1 emissions are dominated by LPG use in heat treatment (73%); this is expected to decline significantly once the heat treatment plant shifts entirely to electric furnaces.
DG set emissions (23% of Scope 1) are described as difficult to control.
Company will begin sharing this ESG dashboard with investors on an ongoing basis going forward.

subsections.label: Geography reclassification
points: Company has changed its geographic reporting pie from prior classification to now report regions as Europe, India & Asia Pacific, and North America.

subsections.label: RFQ portal process
points: Global OEM customers (e.g., ZF group) operate large digital RFQ portals; registered suppliers like RACL receive automatic notifications when a new RFQ is uploaded and can choose to bid, with no human interface required in the initial stage.
Marketing department reviews the portal on a set day each week to identify and act on relevant RFQs.

subsections.label: Export tools/RFQ trend
points: An analyst-cited data point from bearing companies suggests an unprecedented pace of RFQ/RFI inflow from Europe; management confirmed witnessing a similar 'spurt' in RFQs/RFIs but cautioned it is too early to gauge how much converts into serious business, framing it as part of a broader geopolitical realignment of supply chains and logistics routes toward India.

subsections.label: Customer risk-sharing on failed models
points: When a customer's vehicle model fails or underperforms, causing supplier losses, customers typically find ways to support suppliers (cash compensation, alternative business, or cost increases on existing business) depending on relationship strength and supplier quality rating — 'A-rated' suppliers receive more support than lower-rated ones; both global and domestic customers follow this practice.

subsections.label: Pricing/realization disclosure policy
points: Management declined to disclose per-kit realization or value-per-kit metrics for domestic business, citing competitive sensitivity — knowledge of pricing could let competitors underbid using the same volume-times-price calculation, particularly given the domestic market's high price sensitivity.

subsections.label: Non-auto diversification
points: Company has identified potential focus areas outside core automotive: (1) aerospace for civil aviation, seen as a fast-growing area particularly tied to Airbus (Boeing forecast less strong), leveraging RACL's existing precision, machining and ESG-aligned skills; (2) actuators/micromotors as a diversification area; (3) robotics, where gear demand is seen as significant despite differing designs — few Indian manufacturers are present in this space (mostly at infancy stage), Chinese competition is difficult to crack, so Europe is the targeted region for exploration.
Company already does industrial manufacturing on a pilot basis for Bharat Heavy Electricals and other companies, seen as having scale-up potential.

Investment so far in these new areas is in the form of human resources and strategic thought/effort rather than committed capital; company follows an 'incubation' philosophy — testing before committing significant capital ('will never splurge'), scaling up only once a track is proven stable.
Timeline of 'a few months to one or two years' before zeroing in and executing concrete action on these new areas.

subsections.label: Investor engagement
points: Company held its first investor call from its factory location.
Annual plant visit for investors scheduled for the first week of December 2026, with registration on a first-come-first-served basis due to limited slots.

subsections.label: Employee recognition / culture
points: Recognized as Best Organization to Work 2026 by ET Edge (an initiative of Times Group), reflecting focus on inclusive growth, leadership development, workplace excellence and employee engagement.

Annual award ceremony (previously skipped due to unavoidable circumstances) held this year at Jim Corbett for senior employees, including Best Department of the Year, Chairman's Award for Exemplary Leadership, Emerging Leader of the Year, and Employee of the Year recognitions — held outside the Gajraula plant for the second time.

subsections.label: CSR initiatives
points: Sponsoring education for more than 400 kids at a school in Nithari village, Noida, and women empowerment sessions in Noida.

Expanded CSR focus to higher education sponsorship: 13 students supported in FY25-26 (courses at Federal Institute of Hotel Management, Jet King Information, AC Academy in hotel management, cloud computing, and radiology); 14 students selected for FY26-27 sponsorship (courses in cloud computing, AI, and radiology).

subsections.label: Macro/geopolitical and energy risk
points: Geopolitical conflicts and severe energy crises (starting March 2026 and ongoing) cited as challenges faced during the year; India is still not free of the energy crisis.
European economy growing slower by Indian standards but automotive/two-wheeler industry there is described as doing well, having seen a plateau in 2025-26.

subsections.label: Customer concentration mitigant
points: No single customer accounts for more than approximately 20% of revenue, which management cites as limiting the impact of any one customer's growth or decline on overall top line.

subsections.label: Multi-supplier customer risk
points: For customers following a multi-supplier strategy (e.g., Royal Enfield), smaller suppliers are at greater risk of being hit first during demand volatility; management therefore takes a cautious approach to capacity investment for such customers.

subsections.label: Confidentiality-driven business risk
points: Disclosing customer-specific volume/pricing splits (e.g., Royal Enfield sourcing share) could create business risk by revealing competitive information to rivals and violate customer confidentiality preferences.

key_figures.label: Prior FY27 revenue growth guidance reference

subsections.label: Revenue guidance stance
points: Management declined to revise FY27 revenue guidance upward mid-year despite KTM's rebound and Royal Enfield traction, stating revenue guidance is given once a year and treated as a benchmark with a typical plus/minus 5% variance.

Reasoned that even if one customer grows significantly, since no customer exceeds ~20% of revenue share, the overall top-line impact from a single customer's swing is limited, making a guidance revision inappropriate at this point.
Management stated confidence in performing well within the previously forecast limits.

subsections.label: Margin outlook
points: Management indicated current EBITDA margins have been sustained for a long period and should be aspired to as a target, but cautioned that margins are not stationary and a variance of about 2 percentage points can occur quarter to quarter or year over year given current market volatility; the core aspiration is to maintain basic profitability.

subsections.label: Tax rate outlook
points: Full-year blended tax rate guided at 25.62%, despite this quarter's higher effective tax rate of 47% (driven by depreciation/gratuity differences and a deferred tax liability change from a revised income tax surcharge rate).

subsections.label: Long-term growth ambition
points: Company reiterated an ambitious annual growth target of 15-20% per year; management noted that in absolute terms this ambition translates to needing to roughly double current revenue over the next three to four years given current scale.
Management stressed growth will always be pursued with caution and sustainability rather than chasing pure numbers ('rat race').

subsections.label: CAPEX outlook beyond FY27
points: Next year's (2027-28 onward) CAPEX figure not yet disclosed; management stated CAPEX guidance is typically announced around January and asked for a couple of months' patience; policy of announcing CAPEX yearly will continue.

Confirmed gear manufacturing is a capital-intensive business requiring regular ongoing investment to support growth; investments made this year (77 crores, including heat treatment replacement and capacity expansion) will partly come into force in FY26-27 and partly in FY27-28.

subsections.label: M&A / new business openness
points: Management confirmed openness to inorganic growth / acquisitions to accelerate expansion into new areas (aerospace, actuators, robotics, industrial, defence) as and when suitable opportunities arise.

subsections.label: BMW SOP timeline
points: Level one approval already completed; conditional/pilot shipments have started; final approval and customer sign-off visit scheduled for October 24, 2026; BMW supply confirmed to start from October 2026.

subsections.label: Project Venus (BMW electric sports car)
points: Progressing on track; level one approval granted; final approval visit scheduled October 24, 2026; pilot supplies already shipping by sea to be ported to customer plants; production ramp contingent on end-consumer acceptance of the vehicle once launched.

key_takeaways: We clocked that consolidated turnover of 512 crores in FY 25-26.
In Q1 of FY26-27, we clocked a consolidated turnover of 132.60 crores.
On a quarter on quarter basis, we clocked a turnover of 132.6 crores as against 108.7 crores last year, same quarter, which is a growth of close to 22%.
EBITDA has grown from 27.29%, which was 25.11%, to 32.19 crores, which is a growth of close to 18% on an absolute basis.
And PBT has grown from 11.26 crores, which was 10.36%, to 16.82 crores, which is 12.68%, which is a growth of close to 50%.
Your company has been recognized as the best organization to work 2026 by ET Edge, which is an initiative of Times Group.

The heat treatment plant, its foundation was done on 21st of January 2026... we are expecting the building and construction to be completed by October 2026... if all goes well, we are planning to start the trial production by January 2027.
KTM has already bounced back and it is really doing very good numbers.

We are working at 50% to 60% utilization of the installed capacity [ZF project]. The peak year of ZF revenue for this specific project initially was 2028, but since that couple of years went away, they shifted to 2030 now.
pressing_questions: Do you plan to revise your guidance for this year in terms of top line growth given KTM's bounce back and Royal Enfield traction? And do you see that growth accelerating next fiscal year as well?

There isn't, you know, very healthy uptake in the EBITDA margin profile for you this quarter, closer to 180-190 basis points gains. Do you see that this amount of margin profile being sustaining going forward as well?
What should be the blended tax rate for the full year? Since you're taking a high charge, can we expect low taxation for next three quarters?

Have we done any reclassification of any line items, because our raw material cost was usually 30-33% as a percentage of sales, whereas for this quarter it has become quite low at 22-23%, whereas other expenses have taken a higher share?
What is the CAPEX for next three years?
Are we also open for acquisition to accelerate our growth?

quarters.summary: RACL Geartech closed FY26 with consolidated revenue crossing the ₹500 crore milestone (₹512 crore) and record profitability, driven by ramp-ups in commercial vehicle, PAS car and premium motorcycle (Royal Enfield, Kawasaki) programs, and new EV/steering projects (Titan, Venus, Crystal) approaching SOP in FY27. Management guided FY27 revenue of ₹565 crore ± 5%, reiterated without revision, and flagged a ₹77.45 crore FY27 CAPEX plan, with a longer-term ambition (not formal guidance) of ₹1000 crore in 3-5 years.

subsections.label: Milestone achievement
points: Closed the year with consolidated revenue of 512 crores, an all-time historical revenue figure with all-time historically high profit margins.
This is a common saying when the going gets tough, tough gets going — growth maintained despite global turmoil, geopolitical situations, and business challenges.
Growth attributed to a decade of strengthening operations, technology base, and customer base.

subsections.label: Debt & capital allocation
points: Debt-equity improved from 1.3x to 0.63x; current ratio improved from 1.05 to 1.38; DSCR and debt-to-EBITDA also improved significantly.
Total debt decline from ₹297 crore to ₹221 crore attributed to equity infusion done last year, not to reduced investment.
Budgeted CAPEX plan for FY27 is ₹77.45 crore, with corresponding bank debt to be availed accordingly.

Company philosophy: debt is not a bad word, becomes bad only if borrowed and spent injudiciously; strict fiscal discipline in borrowing — borrow only when there is assured business and invest only where there is sustained and justified profitability.
RACL will never borrow money until there is an assured business; never invests on anticipation of business.

subsections.label: Quarterly margin variance
points: Q4 gross margin sequential softness explained as expenses booked across Q3/Q4 causing spillover rather than a structural change — business viewed on annual, not quarter-to-quarter, basis.

key_figures.label: RE motorcycles running on RACL parts (current)
Recreational vehicle segment share (historical, 3-4 years back)

subsections.label: Segment mix evolution
points: PAS Car business started in FY2022-23 from 0% and is now 13% of total revenue — a new entrant and 'next league of growth' expected to change further over next 2-3 years.
Commercial vehicle share grew from 7-8% (2022-23) to 20% of total revenue currently.
Two-wheeler share declined from 40-45% historically to ~30% currently, not due to reduced business but because other segments are growing at a higher rate.
Tractor/agriculture grew from ~10% (3-4 years back) to current 10% level (mix cited as roughly stable/mentioned twice).

No business has reduced in absolute terms; dependence on two-wheeler/agriculture (lower value addition, higher competitiveness) is decreasing relatively as higher-value segments (PAS car, CV) grow faster, aiding overall value addition.
Cost to component/customer is higher in challenging segments (CV, PAS car) due to stronger quality aspects and customer requirements.

subsections.label: Royal Enfield program
points: Name of new customer bagged in January 2026 revealed as Royal Enfield — a high-volume project from a domestic premium motorcycle customer.
Project involves gears with application in transmission and engine gearbox assembly, to be produced at Gajraula main plant.
Samples submitted last week for validation; production expected to start in August-September for the 350cc motorcycle engine, 5-speed gearbox.
Per-kit value not disclosed (not a public number); TAM in terms of number of bikes also confidential due to platform sharing considerations.
No customer intent currently to move from gears to full assemblies for RE, though RACL is equipped and does full gearboxes for TVS and KTM.
RE supply chain needed ramp-up investments, lined up in the last quarter; RE currently at 10,000 motorcycles running on RACL parts, targeting 20,000 but managed gradually due to capacity constraints.
One more RE project under discussion which could make RE a substantial customer in coming years.
RE business, being high-volume, carries different (lower) profitability initially since it started only a few months back; EBITDA margin expected to improve over time.

subsections.label: Kawasaki program
points: Kawasaki India customer for 2-3 years with minuscule business on high engine CC parts; being a Japanese company, they start small before opening up platforms.
Received high-volume project from Kawasaki Japan for 15 parts, of which one part has already started; 9 pilot lots to be submitted, with start of production anticipated early next year.
Export-oriented project; SOP targeted October 27th with validation/resourcing approvals from January onward for mass production.
Engine is a general-purpose engine used across SUVs, up to 200cc motorcycles, and lawn mowers — broad application potential.

subsections.label: TVS Norton / RTX 400
points: Norton just relaunched after ~10 years of closure; first model is a 1.2 litre bike targeting a niche, premium market.
TVS is investing heavily in branding; volumes currently humble but expected to grow; exact numbers confidential due to customer confidentiality.
Management views Norton as 'a brand of the future'.

subsections.label: Commercial vehicle demand drivers
points: CV growth from existing customers, not new wins; linked to European Union infrastructure and defence spending amid Russia-Ukraine and current geopolitical turmoil.
Reconstruction/rehabilitation material demand in conflict-affected regions increasing truck demand.
When ocean traffic is disrupted, traffic shifts to road transport, increasing road transport demand.
Domestic commercial truck business also growing.

MAN Trucks resourcing: a 4-year roadmap (2021-2025) for shifting production of gears historically made in-house by MAN to RACL; 2025 was the final year of full relocation, so this segment's growth going forward will be organic rather than driven by resourcing completion.
CV component margins not disclosed individually — company works on consolidated basis; management implies margins are broadly comparable/good given 20% revenue share.

subsections.label: BHEL / industrial gears
points: Empanelment/approved vendor list status with BHEL achieved; supplies have started for industrial gears.

Sensitive/industrial nature of product limits public disclosure of specific parts; mass production has started; hinted some components used in critical equipment ('keeps the nation and the sea safe').

subsections.label: ZF business
points: Previous year saw some challenges with ZF; this year things are looking good, business appears to have plateaued last year and is now growing; good orders being received.

key_figures.label: Shift drum additional part numbers planned

subsections.label: Project Titan (BMW electric car)
points: Final sign-off expected in August with customer visiting; mass production start targeted October 2026, possibly October-November.
Goes into BMW electric car application.

subsections.label: Project Venus (BMW electric sports car)
points: Same platform as Titan; both projects have been in sample development for the last 1.5 years, now in final VS2PS (validation) stage.
Final approval expected in August; production start targeted October-November 2026.
Represents part of the EV reduction gearbox (no automatic transmission concept exists in EVs — always a reduction gearbox); reduction gear set reduces the number of gears to three or four.
BMW is a major EV player; success here is expected to open growth opportunities with BMW and other customers.

Both Titan and Venus will feature zero-paper documentation — fully digital, end-to-end traceability from steel mill to finished product, covering every process/product/operator/dimensional data — described as a 'digital smart factory Industry 4.0' concept with virtual real-time plant visibility; further details to be shared in a future call.

subsections.label: Project Crystal (electric power steering, US market)
points: Developed in India with ZF Rane for electric power steering system for the US market.
Sampling of 600 sets already under validation in Mexico and at the US OEM end.

Will remain the company's main focus for prototyping once Titan/Venus enter SOP; requires huge capacity build and investment, with CAPEX planned for next year; expected to be the next big revenue driver for RACL in coming years.

subsections.label: Commercial truck electric power steering (ZF)
points: Electric power steering for truck segment for ZF; samples to be submitted within a week; SOP expected September-October this year, pending validation.
Small initial volume but seen as entry into the power steering systems market for trucks in the US, where RACL currently has zero presence.

Rationale: electric steering enables ADAS functionality (hydraulic steering systems do not support ADAS); light-weighting and quick sensor response needed; mass ADAS adoption and electrification of trucks expected to be a growth driver.

subsections.label: Shift drum project
points: Outside RACL's traditional gear product portfolio — a shift drum mounted on the transmission assembly that enables gear shifting.
Start of production next month despite US-Mexico trade issue; volume of ~150,000 units per annum for the first part number.
Six to seven additional part numbers to be added over the next year for this customer.

subsections.label: PAS car technology diversification
points: Beyond gears, RACL is growing in electrical power steering systems (usable in both electric and fuel-steering vehicles), roll control parts for chassis (e.g., BMW 7 series), and reverse steering systems (rear tires rotating with front tire turn).
Differentiation in EV cars now focused on chassis technology, suspension comfort, turning radius, safety/comfort features rather than just power output/ratio, which is no longer a differentiator.

subsections.label: R&D & long-term innovation
points: Company created a five-year vision document in 2019 (aiming for a '5 billion' scale by year 25) that guided entry into PAS car, reduction of three-wheeler application dependency, technology investment planning, five-year CAPEX planning, and R&D tie-ups.
R&D tie-up executed with ARRK, a Munich-based R&D house.

Future R&D/product initiatives beyond the ₹1000 crore vision are being worked on but management declined to disclose specifics, citing competitive sensitivity ('RACL as a company always has a first foot where there is no crowd').

subsections.label: Facilities overview
points: Company founded in 1983; registered office in New Delhi.
Two manufacturing locations: mother plant at Gajraula and second plant at Noida.
One Austrian subsidiary; corporate office based at Noida; multiple warehouses in Europe.
Core competencies include gear cutting, precision machining, and all auto-ancillary competencies, with required company/plant certifications in place.

subsections.label: Sustainability initiatives
points: Won an outstanding social responsibility award; recognized as a green manufacturer with sustainable, green, ethical manufacturing practices and corporate governance disclosures.
Awarded by Grindex 2026 for excellence in technology, manufacturing, and responsible business practices.
Company will begin reporting carbon emission numbers every quarter starting next quarter, to differentiate from conventional Indian ecosystem where carbon footprint is rarely calculated or reported.
Planning to plant roughly 2,500 trees around company premises to reduce carbon footprint; company states it is at zero in Scope 2 but has footprint in Scope 1 and 3.

subsections.label: Export/geography exposure
points: Exports are 70-72% of revenue with heavy exposure to Europe and Japan (per analyst framing); management confirms hardly 2-3% of dollar exports go directly to the US.
Regular exports flow through European Union, Mexico, and Canada; so far no such tariff-related challenges observed.

Feedback from various agencies indicates US tariffs are being borne by the end consumer, not the supplier, so tariffs are not hurting supplier segment sentiment despite some customer pressure for reductions.

subsections.label: Manufacturing base shift — Eastern Europe
points: Observed trend: Central/Western European manufacturing kings (Germany, DACH region) focusing on design, R&D, and innovation while shifting hardcore manufacturing to Eastern Europe (Hungary, Romania, Slovakia) due to lower labor costs while retaining European systems/law standards.

Eastern Europe manufacturing is becoming more efficient, faster, higher output, operating six-to-seven days a week, helping offshoring demand to India, Indonesia, Thailand as China is seen as a risk nobody wants to take.

Central Europe still not shifting mechanical component manufacturing fully to Eastern Europe; instead increasingly looking to China or other Asian countries, with India positioned as having the biggest competitive advantage given China-plus-one strategy.

Electronics/semiconductor manufacturing (highly automated) may still favor Eastern Europe due to lower manpower dependency, but mechanical components (gears) always require manpower content, giving India a persistent edge versus both Central and Eastern Europe.

India's competitive edges cited: ESG/sustainability compliance and trust factor built over 15 years in Europe, energy cost advantage supported by growing solar dependence, and being the world's second-largest steel producer versus European steel constraints.

EU-India FTA also cited as a positive, with norms applicable from January 1 (year not specified), expected to support sustainable trade interest between Europe and India; parallel reference to a prospective US agreement ('American FBI' — as stated) still to be seen.

subsections.label: Raw material sourcing
points: Raw material consumption is essentially domestic; company does not import any major raw materials.
Some child parts/BOP components (e.g., bearings, oil seals) are imported, but these constitute hardly 2-3%, with an upper limit of 5%, of total imports/raw materials.
India's position as the world's second-largest steel producer cited as a competitive advantage supporting domestic sourcing strategy.

subsections.label: Cost/inflation management
points: Input cost inflations are serious and high; company is speaking to customers for interim support/price increases.
Rupee depreciation is helping offset some of the inflationary pressure on exports.

No major supply-chain driven concerns tied to Middle East tensions for RACL's own OEM customers, though broader Indian supply chains have been affected by unavailability issues; company states it is working to resolve related cost pressures.

subsections.label: Customer portfolio breadth
points: Management states barring one or two brands in the world, most premium motorcycle brands buy gears/gearboxes/transmission assemblies from RACL.
Existing customers include TVS, KTM, Royal Enfield, Kawasaki, ZF, ZF Rane, BMW, MAN Trucks, BHEL.

subsections.label: Growth philosophy / target framing
points: Management pushed back on accelerating growth beyond 20% given the absolute base is now larger (20% of ₹500 crore = ₹100 crore vs 20% of ₹400 crore = ₹80 crore), and gear business is highly capital-intensive, premium/niche/super-premium segment requiring high technology and investment.

Growth strategy emphasizes sustainability: avoiding haste that could compromise quality, matching investment lead times/costs to growth, and building teams capable of managing growth — rather than chasing higher percentage growth.
Competitive comparison: in the broader gear/precision shaft business, growing at 20% is already difficult to match versus competitors making sensors/electronic parts.

₹1000 crore target framed as a directional vision (3-5 years) rather than firm guidance; management stresses 1000 is 'just a number' and sustainable growth (jobs, people, bankers' money) matters more than hitting a specific figure/year; if achieved early, next target would be ₹2000 crore.
Company previously grew only 1% in a year when KTM (a major customer) had its shop shut for six months, illustrating resilience.

subsections.label: Market cap perspective
points: Management and an investor (Piyush Jain) agreed not to focus on market cap targets; management stated market cap reflects investor confidence/trust rather than being a management-controlled metric, and that market cap will follow if the business keeps delivering.

subsections.label: Vision documentation
points: In 2019, management (Prabh and Chairman) created a five-year vision document targeting a '5 billion' scale company by year 25 (calendar, not fiscal), including plans to enter PAS car, reduce three-wheeler dependency, invest in EV-related technology, prepare a five-year CAPEX plan, and pursue R&D tie-ups (executed with ARRK, Munich-based R&D house).
A similar vision document is being prepared for the ₹1000 crore target but will not be publicly disclosed to preserve competitive positioning.
This time, the new vision document will not include a market cap number, per Chairman's comment.

subsections.label: RACL 3.0 diversification
points: Referenced 'RACL 3.0' strategy (discussed in an earlier call) around growth in electrical power steering systems, roll control parts, and reverse steering systems as part of broader PAS car / EV mobility diversification.

subsections.label: Geopolitical and macro risks
points: Management describes 'challenging and tough times' with global turmoil, geopolitical situations, business challenges, and rapidly changing daily scenarios affecting businesses in a big way.
Global inflation ('input cards going over the roof') affecting industries worldwide, though RACL's business/company continues to grow despite this.

US tariff policy: feedback suggests tariffs are borne by the end consumer, not passed onto suppliers; so far no slowdown or major hurt to supplier segment observed, though customers occasionally ask for cost reductions.

Middle East tensions have led to issues at some OEM levels in the EU per an analyst question, though management states RACL's own OEM customers are not really impacted by demand; broader Indian supply chains have faced unavailability issues.
Input cost inflation is serious and high; management is engaging customers for interim support and pricing relief.
Currency: rupee depreciation is providing some offset to inflationary cost pressure on exports.

subsections.label: Business/customer risk
points: Prior year (FY25) growth was impacted by external factors including issues at a customer end (e.g., KTM bankruptcy-related slowdown, when KTM's shop was shut for six months, RACL still grew 1%), plus Europe market slowdown.
RE (Royal Enfield) ramp-up requires supply chain investment and capacity management; cannot scale to 20,000 units immediately.

subsections.label: FY27 guidance reaffirmation
points: Guidance of ₹565 crore ± 5% for FY27 (originally given in Q3) is not being revised at this time; management retains this flexibility band but expresses confidence in meeting the guidance.

CAPEX plan for FY27 disclosed as ₹77.45 crore, with corresponding bank debt to be availed accordingly; details of CAPEX beyond FY27 (for reaching ₹1000 crore) will be disclosed once documents are finalized/mature.

subsections.label: ₹1000 crore vision
points: Management targets reaching ₹1000 crore in the next 3 to 5 years, though this is not treated as firm guidance ('1000 is just a number'); focus remains on sustainable growth over speed.
If achieved earlier than planned, next milestone would be renegotiated to ₹2000 crore.

key_takeaways: We have closed the year with a very, very magnificent note of crossing 500 crores of milestone revenue by having a consolidated revenue of 512 crores.
Our profit margins are also all time historically high and it has shown a very, very magnificent growth.
We are proud to share that FY26, we achieved a consolidated revenue of 512 crores. We have almost 29 active customers and more than 1600 SKUs.
Royal Enfield is now part of our product customer portfolio.
We have received a very high volume, huge project from Kawasaki Japan wherein there are 15 parts which will come to us and one part has already started.
Project Titan, which goes to BMW electric car, the final sign off is in August. The customer is visiting and then October '26, we can start the mass production.
We have this awarded by Grindex 2026. They recognized as organizations demonstrating excellence in technology, manufacturing and responsible business practices.

We have a guidance of 565 plus minus 5% for FY27 in Q3... At the moment, we are not [revising] because this plus minus 5 is a flexibility which we will keep. But yeah, we are very confident we should be able to meet whatever we are giving as a guidance.
