MARICO.about: Marico Limited is one of India's leading consumer goods companies, operating across beauty, personal care, wellness and foods in India and select international markets. Portfolio includes Parachute, Saffola, Hair & Care, Nihar, Livon, Set Wet, Beardo, Just Herbs, True Elements, Plix, Cosmix and 4700BC; products reach 1 out of 3 Indians.[1]

quarters.summary: Marico started FY27 with consolidated revenue growth of 23% and EBITDA/PAT growth of 25% (highest profit growth in 28 quarters). Management reaffirmed full-year aspirations of double-digit consolidated revenue growth to comfortably cross INR15,000 crores, high-teens EBITDA growth with an aspiration to touch 20%, India high single-digit volume growth (with a possible double-digit volume growth quarter in the next 3 quarters), international mid-teens constant currency growth, and continued progress toward Vision 2030 (INR20,000 crores revenue, mid-teens EBITDA CAGR). Near-term, Q2 input costs are expected to be relatively higher due to crude/vegetable oil inflation even as copra remains range-bound ~30-35% below peak.

subsections.label: Margin drivers
points: Gross margin expanded 30 bps YoY led by softer copra prices, favourable channel and portfolio mix from strong growth in premium portfolio, GT growth, and profitable scale-up of food and digital-first portfolio.
A&P expenses grew 25% as company continued to invest significantly behind brands to strengthen long-term equity, support innovation and drive consumer salience.
EBITDA margin improved 40 bps YoY to 20.7%, a strong quarter built on a high base from the corresponding period last year.

Gross margin outlook mixed: benefits from lower copra consumption offset by significant cost push in LP, polymers and edible oil (60-70% cost increase), with the entire hit not passed on to consumers; company will try to hold gross margin percentage rather than guide a specific number.

EBITDA margin guidance framed via reverse math: crossing INR15,000 crores revenue implies EBITDA margin expansion of ~140-150 bps versus last year on a full-year basis; management pushed back on the 20% EBITDA growth target being termed conservative.

subsections.label: Non-standalone India business profitability
points: Non-standalone India EBIT grew ~40% in the quarter, reflecting profitability improvement in food and digital brands driven partly by mix and partly by raw material benefit.

subsections.label: India core business execution
points: Both general trade and modern trade recorded double-digit growth; Project SETU continued to strengthen general trade execution, driving wider reach, superior assortment quality, improved service levels and improved ROI for distribution partners.
Quick commerce continued accelerated scale-up, contributing around 5% of India business revenues (ex digital brands); all digital channels combined account for over 20% of India business revenues.

subsections.label: Parachute Rigids
points: Delivered strongest volume performance in the last 20 quarters and gained over 400 bps volume share, marking a new high.

Revenue growth reflects anniversarization of prior-year price increases and pricing actions during the quarter as company proactively passed on value to consumers in non-price-point large packs amid softening copra prices.
Performance underscores enduring franchise strength and competitive advantage in supply chain versus smaller players, built over decades of managing commodity cycles.

10% volume growth deconstructed: no grammage changes made; deep/relatively deeper price cuts taken selectively on higher-MRP loyalty packs addressed prior downgradation/titration in use; supply chain resilience helped versus smaller players hit harder by packaging/fuel challenges; execution of price drop (pipeline/scheme management, single drop, no month-end spend smoothening) was much better than in the past; some organized competition has become more rational, avoiding negative gross margin selling.

Only one price drop (~10%) taken on loyalty/non-grammage packs in Q4; no grammage increase made even as copra deflated; company does not expect further pricing action given move into off-season and no cost-side correction expected.

AI-led demand sensing/forecasting and supply chain investment have kept distributor pipeline very thin (one of the lowest in FMCG), enabling much faster (vs historical 8-10 week lag) transmission of price drops to market.

subsections.label: Value-Added Hair Oils (VAHO)
points: Continued strong momentum led by mid- and premium segment; mid/premium hair oils portfolio delivered close to high-teens volume growth, the profitable part of the mix; market share gains continue.

Encouraging progress in almond oil franchise; aim to build to INR100 crores+ ARR franchise by FY28; category disruption rationale drawn from prior Amla playbook (once at 9% share vs leader's 78%, later achieved market leadership) and supported by SETU-driven distribution access and stronger execution.

VAHO growth breakup: mid/premium segment delivered high-teens volume growth with even higher value growth; growth benefited immensely from Project SETU and continued investment in innovation, premiumization and distribution expansion.

subsections.label: Saffola Edible Oil
points: Revenue growth reflects calibrated pricing actions in response to further input cost increases; volume decline reflects rationalized supply of select variants in certain channels to maintain threshold profitability, trading off volume growth.

Entry-point Saffola is more commoditized and is being selectively reduced (share of contribution of packs) to avoid consumers below threshold profitability; Saffola Gold/loyal users not impacted by cold-pressed oil competition.

Cold-pressed oil viewed as category of the future; company's own cold-pressed foray progressing, with gross margin structure far superior to core Saffola Edible Oil; expected to become sizable portion of Saffola business by next year.

Saffola brand has for 20 years encouraged use of right oil in lesser quantity (LOSORB technology invented for less oil absorption); mid-single-digit volume growth considered acceptable as portfolio pivots toward Foods, which may become the bigger part of Saffola architecture within a couple of years.

subsections.label: Diversification: Foods & Premium Personal Care
points: Combined Foods and Premium Personal Care portfolio (incl. digital-first brands) has achieved significant scale, growing ahead of core portfolio, improving profitability, consumer relevance and addressable market.

Foods growth driven by addition of 4700BC and Cosmix expanding addressable market into attractive demand spaces, while core Saffola Foods franchise continues strong double-digit growth; ex-Cosmix/4700BC growth was in double digits; 4700BC and Cosmix volumes not yet included in India volume growth number until they enter the base.

Premium Personal Care scaling well; encouraging traction in shampoos with aspiration of near INR100 crores revenue this year; launch of Parachute Advanced Protein hair conditioner expands addressable market and complements premiumization agenda.

4700BC and Cosmix tracking well on integration; expected to end year ahead of initial assumptions while remaining mindful of profitability; Marico now has two digital platforms (foods, premium personal care) enabling synergies, shared expertise and best practices.

subsections.label: Digital-first portfolio (Beardo, Plix, Cosmix)
points: Digital-first portfolio led by Beardo and Plix delivered strong growth alongside structural improvement in profitability, exemplifying digital playbook combining entrepreneurial brand building with disciplined capital allocation and operating leverage.

Plix has pivoted toward premium personal care (plant-based hair and skin food) beyond plant protein/ACV; hero SKUs exist with strong innovation engine and digital marketing (influencer/content) capability; strong AOV D2C component seen as a competitive edge; Plix (~INR800 crores) not expected to sustain 30-40% growth but has legs via modern trade/beauty outlets given wide category spectrum.

Cosmix has journey ahead in VMS space and was already mid-to-high-teens profitable margin at acquisition; both Plix and Cosmix described as having significantly loyal consumers with good repeat rate and equity via D2C ownership of consumer relationship (tracked via LTV/CAC and repeat rates).

Priority is profitable growth (20-25% growth with profitability preferred over 40-50% growth with cash burn); Beardo at double-digit profitability, Plix at high single-digit trending toward double-digit; path to profitability seen for other brands over next 12-18 months with burn now low.

Company aims for a structured tuck-in playbook into platforms rather than fragmented acquisitions; confident of a ~INR4,000 crores digital business with early-teens EBITDA margin by 2030; digital structure largely finalized with one or two things still to do.

subsections.label: International business
points: Bangladesh experienced transient moderation due to pricing anniversarization and demand softness amid persistent high inflation, accentuated by sharp rise in fuel/energy prices; focused category initiatives continue to sustain market share gains.

Vietnam growth driven by strong performance across male and female personal care categories, supported by structural transformation via investments in innovation, distribution and digital commerce capabilities; SETU-like GTM transformation enhanced execution quality and competitiveness.
MENA (Gulf and Egypt) delivered resilient performance despite inflationary pressures and operating challenges in Gulf, driven by strong execution, focused innovation and continued market share gains.
South Africa growth led by hair care with key brands Black Chic, Just for Kids and Isoplus performing well.

subsections.label: Channel strategy
points: Management follows an 'and' theory rather than 'or' theory on channels; entry barriers to organized trade have significantly reduced allowing new INR100 crores brands to emerge quickly, but entry barriers to solid GT distribution (especially rural/middle India) remain high, making GT a source of sustainable competitive advantage for the next 5-7 years.

Alternate channels viewed as drivers of premiumization and as test markets for innovation while avoiding cannibalistic growth; multiple growth levers maintained rather than dependence on one channel (shift began 2-3 years ago with Project SETU).
Quick commerce has established itself in India and is bound to grow due to certain structural factors; company investing behind it, aided by its six-seven digital brands.

Relative slowdown (not absolute decline) observed in modern trade and marketplace e-commerce growth in recent quarters versus quick commerce's acceleration; channel shift into quick commerce is coming from multiple channels (difficult to isolate GT vs MT), attracting a less price-sensitive, convenience-seeking shopper; channel-specific pack architecture used to minimize cannibalization and to test-market new products.

subsections.label: Competitive landscape - plant protein/ACV/D2C wellness
points: High competition from HUL's Oziva, Tata 1mg-type players and e-commerce/online medicine private labels in plant protein, collagen and ACV space; company sees value in 2-3 players developing the category to convert fad into habit.

Company focuses on D2C to own the consumer relationship and partner the wellness journey, tracking LTV/CAC and repeat/loyalty rates as healthy; performance-marketing-led growth in a single channel viewed as unsustainable.

subsections.label: Shampoo market entry
points: Aspiration is to be a mainstream shampoo player nationally (national launch, not phased by market); leveraging Parachute Advanced equity and strong distribution built via Project SETU for direct market execution rather than wholesale-led entry.

Company has a proven shampoo model overseas: sustained growth versus multinationals in Bangladesh (~year 4-5) and Middle East (~year 2-3), giving confidence for India despite dominance of multinationals and strong local players; will take one year at a time rather than commit to a 3-5 year vision.

Contrasted with prior body lotion/moisturizer business: category penetration is low, has not grown significantly amid winter shrinking from global warming, and has pivoted to low-margin OT-driven brands, which did not fit the fewer-bigger-bolder strategy despite possible 10-15% market share.

subsections.label: Vision 2030 and EDGE framework
points: Advancing toward Vision 2030 target of INR20,000 crores revenue with mid-teens EBITDA CAGR; focus areas: strengthen core franchises, expand into adjacencies with right to win, scale digital businesses profitably, and further diversify international growth engine.
EDGE framework anchors next phase of growth: Expanding total addressable market and portfolio, enhancing Distribution and digitization, Growing profitably, and creating an Empowered organization.

Building larger growth engines by strengthening core categories via sustained investment and wider portfolio participation across cohorts, formats and channels, while driving a structural shift toward premium, more profitable categories via bigger, bolder bets.
Reducing share of commodity-linked businesses, shifting portfolio toward more profitable categories for stronger unit economics, lower cyclicity and better operating leverage over time.
GTM transformation via Project SETU (India, now Vietnam) already yielding benefits; next leg of journey focuses on sharpening execution via smart analytics, AI and integrated digital ecosystems.

Organization focus on high-quality talent with founders' mentality/owner's mindset and value-driven frugal culture; leveraging AI, analytics and automation to improve visibility, speed and decision support while empowering teams for accountability, collaboration, execution excellence and discipline.

subsections.label: M&A integration (4700BC, Cosmix, digital brands)
points: 4700BC and Cosmix acquired earlier this year; minimum 3-year learning/integration period; viewed via platform lens (foods platform, BPC platform) enabling shared expertise, resource/cost sharing across brands.

Organizational structure includes CEO India business and CEO international business; management spends significant time on digital; playbook now structured for platform tuck-ins rather than fragmented acquisitions.
Digital structure largely finalized (one or two items remaining) following prior special call discussion; confident in reaching ~INR4,000 crores early-teens EBITDA margin digital business by 2030.

subsections.label: Macro and cost headwinds
points: Global macro environment remained volatile with supply chain disruptions and increasing energy costs impacting economic activity.

Domestic consumer inflation rose led by food and a marginal fuel price hike, though it remained within RBI's threshold; company will continue to monitor evolving inflationary conditions and monsoon progress.

Some international economies experienced transient headwinds from geopolitical developments manifesting as inflation and other costs; Bangladesh saw demand softness from persistent high inflation and a sharp rise in fuel/energy prices; Gulf region faced inflationary pressures and operating challenges.

Crude and vegetable oils continue to exhibit upward price bias, expected to make input costs relatively higher in Q2, even as copra prices remain range-bound ~30-35% below last year's peak (with some recent upward bias).
Cost increase on crude-led derivatives such as LP and polymers has been in the range of 60-70%, creating gross margin pressure only partly passed on to consumers.
Despite global supply chain disruptions, company maintained strong supply chain assurance via strategic positioning of raw materials, packaging materials and finished goods, aided by extreme agility.

subsections.label: Full-year aspirations
points: Strong start to the year sets the base for full-year aspirations of double-digit revenue growth to cross INR15,000 crores easily, high-teens EBITDA growth with aspiration to touch 20%.
Expect India high single-digit volume growth and international mid-teens constant currency growth; expect to hit another double-digit India volume growth quarter sometime in the next three quarters.

Management used a cricketing analogy (getting off to a strong start in the powerplay to stay ahead of the Duckworth-Lewis curve) to frame building early momentum to navigate potential later volatility.

Parachute expected to deliver decent volume growth in the next one or two quarters but guidance maintained at mid-single-digit for the year, with the 10% Q1 growth described as an aberration not expected to be sustained.

subsections.label: Cost outlook

key_takeaways: We have started the year on a very strong note with a consolidated revenue growth of 23% and EBITDA and PAT growth of 25%, making our highest profit growth in the last 28 quarters.

The India business delivered one of the strongest quarters in recent years with 11% volume growth and revenue growth of 21%, led by robust momentum in core business and continued scale-up of new growth engines.
Over 96% of the business continued to gain or sustain market share and over 99% of the business continued to gain or sustain penetration on a MAT basis.
International business reported 15% constant currency growth, led by outperformance in Vietnam and MENA.
Gross margin expanded 30 basis points year-on-year, led by softer copra prices, a favourable channel and portfolio mix... EBITDA margin improved 40 basis points year-on-year to 20.7%.
Parachute Rigids delivered 10% volume growth with strongest performance in the last 20 quarters and gained over 400 basis points in volume share, marking a new high.

The strong start to this year has set us well to achieve our full year aspirations of delivering double-digit revenue growth to cross INR15,000 crores easily. We are confident of achieving high-teens EBITDA growth and aspire to touch 20% EBITDA growth during this year.

As we advance towards the Vision 2030 to achieve INR20,000 crores in revenues with mid-teens EBITDA CAGR, our focus remains clear: strengthen our core franchises, expand into adjacencies where we have a right to win, scale up our digital businesses profitably and further diversify our international growth engine.

quarters.summary: Marico closed FY'26 with multi-year highs in India volume growth, international constant-currency growth and consolidated revenue. Management guides for FY'27 high single-digit India volume growth, mid-teen international constant-currency growth, double-digit consolidated revenue growth to cross INR15,000 crores, and high-teen EBITDA growth (raised from mid-teens), subject to stable macros; medium-term (FY'30) aspiration is to comfortably cross INR20,000 crores in revenue with mid-teen EBITDA growth.

subsections.label: Margin guidance drivers
points: Peak margin years were also years of low commodity inflation; this year copra tailwind is offset by potential crude-derivative cost hit.
Gross margin expected to expand 350-400 bps for FY27 over FY26 exit.
A&P investment to be increased by 200-250 bps.
Net operating margin expansion base case of ~150 bps (range 150-200 bps) after accounting for A&P step-up.
Current year ~17% EBITDA growth partly reflects a denominator effect from significant revenue growth.

High-teens EBITDA growth guidance is considered ambitious given crude at ~110 and crude-linked derivative inflation; management stated they would be 'the only company' giving such guidance in this environment.

Guidance raised from mid-teens (stated in Q3 call) to high-teens EBITDA growth due to firmer view on copra being range-bound, profitable acquisitions (Skinetiq, Cosmix), improving digital business margins, and proactive pricing actions.

subsections.label: Cost environment
points: Divergence in input trends: copra corrected ~35% from peak and expected range-bound; vegetable oils and other crude-linked inputs show upward bias due to Middle East geopolitical tensions.
Weighted average input cost increase for next year is extremely marginal; price hikes already implemented will neutralize the impact.
Price elasticity model was challenged last year — Parachute carried flat volume growth despite 60% price increase, prompting possible recalibration of pricing model over next couple of years.

subsections.label: Parachute
points: Delivered low single-digit volume growth after adjusting for mlage adjustments, showing resilience.

Strengthened distribution and back-end/supply chain capabilities position Marico advantageously versus smaller players.
Brand continued to strengthen leadership position during the year.
RPI: last year copra prices rose 120-130% but Marico took only ~60% price increase; current 10% price cut on non-price-point packs does not materially change RPI versus loose coconut oil.
Price elasticity model challenged — flat volume growth maintained despite 60% price increase last year due to strong brand equity; possible recalibration of pricing model over next couple of years.

subsections.label: Value Added Hair Oils (VAHO)
points: Robust growth in Q4 with volume growth in low 20s and meaningful market share gains.
Full-year portfolio grew 20%, led by mid and Premium segments (non-Shanti Amla portfolio) which delivered close to double-digit volume growth on 2-year CAGR basis.
Entered almond oil category under Hair & Care franchise with considerable inroads in modern trade already.
Expected to sustain double-digit volume-led growth, supported by focused innovation pipeline, improved availability post-GST rationalization, and distribution expansion under Project SETU.
6-7% price increase already taken in response to crude derivative cost increases; anniversarising of this pricing expected in H1 FY27.

Industry-wide VAHO growth acceleration seen across players, partly attributed to shift from ATL to BTL competitive spend and GST-driven shift from unbranded to branded portfolios; Marico repivoted strategy toward investing in mid/premium segments from Q2, driving VAHO acceleration since then.

subsections.label: Saffola Edible Oils
points: Steady performance in elevated pricing environment; stable growth expected in FY27 while maintaining threshold-level profitability.
Will remain disciplined in passing on input cost movements via calibrated pricing, while driving premiumization and higher growth in cold pressed oils, Saffola Gold and total variants.
Okay with low to mid-single-digit volume growth subject to threshold-level margin; volume/value growth could fluctuate quarter to quarter given volatility.
Some pantry stocking noted in early March due to West Asia crisis.

subsections.label: Foods
points: Transitioned to mid-teen growth on back of double-digit growth in core Saffola Foods in Q4; portfolio exited FY26 at INR1,000+ crores revenue.
Wholesome play spanning Saffola (mainstream health/wellness), True Elements (clean label, modern breakfast/snacking), 4700BC (premium gourmet snacking), Cosmix and Plix (functional nutrition).
Growth delivered alongside significant improvement in profitability; focus on fewer, bigger, more profitable plays and category development via innovation and execution.

Q4 overall Foods growth (16-17%, including M&A) understated organic momentum because True Elements is lapping a high base quarter and underwent SKU rationalization of low-GC products to accelerate profitability path; teens growth expected in True Elements for FY27.
Plix pivoting more toward Personal Care, reducing its Foods growth contribution.
Cosmix included for only ~50 days in the quarter (not a full quarter).
FY27 base case growth expectation of 20% (range 20-25% or more), with results expected to show from Q1 FY27.

subsections.label: Premium Personal Care
points: Comprises Serums, Male Grooming, Skin Care; scaling with focus on profitable growth.
Digital-first portfolio scale-up accompanied by structural profitability improvement; aim to exit FY27 at double-digit EBITDA margins and teens EBITDA margins by FY30.
Beardo and Plix on accelerated growth trajectory with improving profitability.

subsections.label: Digital business / portfolio mix
points: 55% of core advertising spend now digital; 100% for digital brands.
Combined Foods+PPC (incl. digital-first brands) revenue share rose to 23% of India business in FY26 despite sharp pricing-led growth in core portfolio.
Expect share to expand to ~27% in FY27 (revised up from earlier 25% target); aspire to about one-third of business by FY30.

subsections.label: Plix brand detail
points: Currently hitting mid to high single-digit EBITDA margin, expected to reach double digits soon.
Started with ACV (apple cider vinegar) as hero product; pivoted toward hair and skin food/Personal Care as it expanded TAM and carried higher profitability.
D2C is ~45% of Plix business, enabling cross-sell/upsell (e.g., ACV consumer buying hair growth serum).
New launches planned in nutraceuticals space, including an ACV canned drink already available on 1-2 quick commerce platforms, reflecting global shift from carbonated soft drinks to healthy drinks.

Cosmix positioned as more serious nutraceutical/protein play (vitamins, supplements) vs. Plix as a more 'fun' brand; going forward, center of gravity of Plix expected to shift more toward Personal Care given higher long-term profitability.

Management philosophy: prefers 20-25% growth with steady profitability increase over 60% growth without profitability improvement; digital business (incl. Beardo) targeting 20-25-30% growth en route to teens profitability by 2030.

subsections.label: International business — Bangladesh
points: Maintained strong momentum; recent quarterly growth accelerated (22%, 29%, 35% over last two quarters) attributed to pricing actions taken into account plus decent volume growth from core and newer portfolio (shampoo, baby, etc.).
On steady-state basis, expect double-digit growth to continue; quarterly swings should not be over-read.
FY27 outlook aided by a democratically elected government for the full year versus a fragile government for most of FY26.
Business foundation, moats, and favorable cost structure seen as enabling healthy growth despite consumption/inflation uncertainties.

subsections.label: International business — MENA/Gulf/Egypt
points: Gulf region performance in the quarter impacted by near-term supply-side constraints in March (shipment issues); primary sale impacted more than offtake due to alternative routing options (e.g., via Egypt).
Egypt continued to deliver strong growth.
MENA contributes only 4% of total turnover; no immediate major concern seen despite ongoing monitoring.

subsections.label: International business — other markets
points: Vietnam, South Africa and export markets continued scaling up as key growth engines, strengthening portfolio resilience.

Steady progress in premiumizing international portfolio via expansion into beauty and personal care categories and innovation, expected to drive differential growth and margin expansion over medium term.

subsections.label: Offtake and share trends
points: Offtakes remained robust with over 95% of portfolio gaining/sustaining market share and over 90% maintaining/improving penetration on MAT basis.
Investments under Project SETU yielding visible results, particularly in rural reach and execution quality, supporting revival/sustained growth of general trade this year.
Alternate channels (organized retail, e-commerce, quick commerce) continue to scale strongly, driving differential growth in urban and premium portfolios.

subsections.label: Competitive dynamics vs. smaller players
points: Supply chain constraints (polymers, packaging material, fuel) affecting smaller players more; Marico ensured supply chain assurance and foresaw the situation, buying ahead where possible.
Smaller players face working capital constraints during high inflation, limiting their ability to stock/position build, unlike in prior deflationary cycles when they became more active.

Management believes advantage (inflation plus constrained availability for smaller players) will continue for some time, supporting Marico's competitive positioning and expected volume/market-share gains from smaller players over next few quarters.
Government has contained shock from current crisis better than other emerging markets, aiding sector consumption; organized players seen as having better coping ability.

subsections.label: Portfolio transformation strategy
points: By FY30, expect substantially transformed portfolio, lowering share of commodity-linked businesses from more than 70% to 50% over a decade.
Medium-term strategy anchored in expanding TAM, sharper portfolio choices, accelerated premiumization, and continued investment in digital media analytics, automation and AI capabilities.

subsections.label: VAHO industry dynamics
points: Analyst noted VAHO growth acceleration is an industry-wide phenomenon across listed players, not just Marico; possibly linked to coconut oil becoming less affordable during copra inflation, causing some market share shift toward VAHO.
Management attributes VAHO acceleration to repivoted investment strategy toward mid/premium segments and GST-driven shift from unbranded to branded VAHO.

subsections.label: Recent acquisitions integration
points: Positive start for recent acquisitions (4700BC, Cosmix, Skinetiq, Vietnam deals, etc.) with no major hiccups reported.
Company has developed a playbook for integration and valuation, partnering with strong founders in each case.
House-of-brands structure enabling back-end synergies benefiting long-term profitability (e.g., price-point pack for 4700BC popcorn taken over by GT; immediate modern trade synergies).
Acquisitions avoided where business is fundamentally weak or unit economics are not viable; success rate described as fairly okay so far.
Two of three recent acquisitions (Skinetiq, Cosmix) are already profitable (Skinetiq mid-20s margin, Cosmix high-teens margin).

subsections.label: Macro/geopolitical risks
points: Onset and progression of monsoon and inflationary impact of the West Asia crisis flagged as key monitorables.
Vegetable oils and other crude-linked inputs show upward bias driven by ongoing Middle East geopolitical tensions.
Gulf region supply-side constraints in March impacted shipments/primary sales (MENA contributes only 4% of turnover; no major concern currently).
FMCG inflation identified historically as the biggest enemy of consumption, especially at bottom of pyramid/rural; risk of down-trading if inflation increases.
Potential strong El Niño effect could impact consumption in back half of year, stretching into Q1 of following year.
Management notes these are external/macro factors rather than internal (Marico-specific) execution factors, which are currently viewed as on track.

subsections.label: Supply chain risk mitigation
points: Despite ongoing geopolitical tension, maintained strong supply chain assurance via strategic positioning across raw materials, packaging materials and finished goods; no material disruption foreseen in near term.

We expect the share of these new businesses to expand to about 27%, which was earlier targeted to reach 25% in FY '27 and aspire to move about one-third of our business by FY '30.
By FY '30, we expect to have substantially transformed the portfolio, resulting in lowering the share of commodity-linked businesses from more than 70% to 50% over a decade.

We expect to sustain high single-digit volume growth in the India business in FY '27. The international business is expected to maintain strong momentum and mid-teen constant currency growth driven by broad-based performance across markets. At a consolidated level, we aim to deliver double-digit revenue growth to cross INR15,000 crores in revenues and high-teen EBITDA growth, subject to stable macros.
At a consolidated level, we will aim to sustain double-digit revenue growth to comfortably cross INR20,000 crores in revenues and aspire for mid-teen EBITDA growth by FY '30.
pressing_questions: Is the upward revision on EBITDA guidance (mid-teen to high-teen) despite new acquisition drag and sharp crude derivative inflation justified — what is driving the change in assumptions?
Given FY27 guided margins are lower than 3 of the past 5 years' margin highs despite copra correction and improving mix, is the guidance conservative or is something being missed?

Is Bangladesh's sharp acceleration (22%, 29%, 35% over recent quarters) a one-off due to delayed pricing/soft base, and will it decelerate given the new democratically elected government context for FY27?
On PCNO/Parachute, what is the relative price index (RPI) after price cuts, and what incremental pricing action is planned given the firm view on copra?
Is the industry-wide VAHO growth acceleration linked to coconut oil price unaffordability, and could this reverse as copra prices fall, potentially acting as a buffer for copra volumes?
Can Plix sustain 20-25% growth given it is approaching INR1,000 crores ARR, or will it need to unlock new channels beyond online to sustain that pace?

FORTIS.about: FHL was incorporated in February 1996. The company’s first healthcare facility became operational in Mohali, Punjab in 2001. It is a leading integrated healthcare service provider in India. The healthcare verticals of the company primarily comprise hospitals, diagnostics and day care specialty facilities. Currently, the company operates its healthcare delivery services in India, Nepal, Dubai and Sri Lanka with 36 healthcare facilities with approximately 4,000 operational beds. [1] Company controls its diagnostics business through its 57% owned subsidiary SRL Limited. It is amongst the largest private diagnostics chains. It has a presence in over 600 cities and towns, with an established strength of 415 laboratories, 8,200 direct clients and 1,400 Collection Centers. [2]

subsections.label: ESOP charge and margin impact
points: ESOP scheme rolled out from 23rd April; charge will initially be higher depending on vesting, then gradually come down over next 3 years.
ESOP charge for this quarter reflects fewer days as scheme was rolled out mid-quarter.
Company still maintains 25% EBITDA margin guidance, expecting some cost reduction and efficiency improvement, plus revenue growth, to offset ESOP cost.

Roughly 55%-60% of ESOP recipients are doctors and administrative/operator staff; proportion may vary depending on needs.
ESOP philosophy was deliberated over about 1.5 years before implementation; not a reactionary move to poaching.

subsections.label: Margin drivers/levers for FY27-28 (150-200bps ex-ESOP, 25% by FY28)
points: New units (ramp-up stage) contributed negatively by 0.4% to overall EBITDA margin currently; expected to contribute positively by about 1% going forward.
Legal costs from ongoing Delhi High Court hearings burdened profitability in current and prior quarter.

Existing hospitals with lower occupancy (e.g., BG Road, Mulund) showing signs of improvement, seen as a lever for margin improvement.

subsections.label: Hospital business drivers
points: Several key hospitals such as Jaipur, Noida, Faridabad, and Mulund witnessed margin expansion compared to corresponding quarter of previous year and trailing quarter.
Key facilities such as Mulund and Faridabad registered revenue growth in excess of 20% compared to corresponding previous period.
Hospital occupancy impacted to some extent by new units undergoing renovation (e.g., Bangalore) but still at around 70% on enhanced base.

14 facilities contributing 70% of hospital revenues already have occupancy of close to 74%; balance 6 hospitals in 10-20% margin range have occupancy room but occupancy previously slided down in FY26.

Levers to ramp up occupancy include new units (Manesar, Yeshwanthpur, Greater Noida) strengthening clinical talent and marketing, and improvement at low-occupancy units like BG Road; expected to ramp up occupancy by another 2-3 percentage points.

subsections.label: Manesar and Greater Noida performance

subsections.label: Oncology / chemo business dynamics
points: 200 bps decline in onco share within specialty mix attributed to chemo business impact, not other specialties.
Hospitals in Punjab and Jaipur have large ECHS beneficiary base; NCR hospitals have large CGHS beneficiary base; chemo drug pricing mechanism with 30% discount on MRP causing dip.
Oncology growth was previously ~23-24%, now down to about 5%; expected to stabilize in 10-12% range going forward, driven by radiation and surgical oncology expertise and comprehensive care focus.

Within the specialty mix there are pluses and minuses: diagnostic tests/investigation/procedure prices have gone up while chemotherapy prices have gone down; net effect not significant but oncology division growth has become muted partly due to high base after several years of high growth.

subsections.label: Diagnostics (Agilus) business performance
points: Preventive and specialized portfolio revenues grew 27% and 13% respectively versus prior year period.
Continued improvement in products and customer mix supported by higher B2C contribution.
High realization per test and per patient reflects increasing adoption of specialized diagnostics and favorable portfolio mix shift.
Growth this quarter came significantly from volume growth as well, seen as sign of revival after a stagnant period caused by factors including the brand change.
Rationalization of lab network along with customer touch points undertaken as part of transformation project; journey to be accelerated under new leadership.
NCR region growth has been strong after focused efforts; plan to replicate in other regions.
B2C ratio expected to move from 53% to at least 55% and eventually 58% in coming quarters, given B2C is more sticky and profitable and helps build infrastructure.

Company adhering to 3% O&M fee agreement on Gleneagles revenue; in discussions with IHH regarding potential stake increase/participation, no call option currently in any of the 2-3 hospitals operated.

key_takeaways: We reported consolidated revenue of INR 2,545 crores, a growth of 17.5% over Q1 of financial year '26.

Our hospital business revenues have grown by 19% to INR 2,187 crores while Q1 financial year '27 diagnostic business gross revenue has grown up by 10.2% to INR 407 crores versus the previous corresponding quarter.
Our consolidated operating EBITDA pre-ESOP expenses increased by 15.8% to INR 568 crores, delivering a margin of 22.3% versus 22.6% in Q1 of financial year '26.
The hospital business reported an operating EBITDA of INR 471 crores, which translates into a margin of 21.5% compared to 22.1% in Q1 of financial year '26.
Excluding the impact of these facilities on a like-to-like basis, operating EBITDA margin in the quarter was similar to Q1 of financial year '26 at 22%.
The operating EBITDA margin of the Diagnostic business for the quarter improved to 23.9% from 23% in quarter 1 of financial year '26.
Our consolidated reported profit after tax before exceptional items for the quarter increased by approximately 4% to INR 263 crores.
On the balance sheet front, the company's net debt stands at INR 2,233 crores with a net debt-to-EBITDA ratio of 1.01x as of June 30, 2026, as against 0.92x on June 30, 2025.

We also recently entered into an O&M agreement for a 300-bedded greenfield multi-specialty hospital to be developed in Cuttack. This marks Fortis Healthcare's entry into Odisha, further expanding our presence in growth markets.
Our Board has also approved installation of a proton facility at our flagship hospital in Gurgaon as well.

And secondly, how do we kind of achieve that 25% EBITDA margin? Can you explain in a bit more detail like what are the cost levers? Or is it pure operating leverage? What are the some of the building blocks for that?

We are reporting only 9%, 10% top line growth whereas industry is growing at 15% and especially our growth was largely on the account of realization improvement, whereas industry has witnessed strong demand growth. So can you provide some color on what are the challenges we are facing? Is this related to still re-branding or all?
Sir, what is your Capex guidance for this year? Also last year we are seeing some acquisitions, inorganic moves. Is that something which we can expect this year as well?

quarters.summary: Fortis reported steady FY26 and Q4 FY26 growth across Hospitals and Diagnostics, with margin expansion in both segments. Management reiterated FY28 hospital EBITDA margin guidance of 25% with 1.5-2% YoY improvement, guided FY27 hospital revenue growth of 15%+ with 150bps EBITDA margin improvement, and Agilus guided FY27 EBITDA margin of 23-24% with double-digit revenue growth. Key headwinds flagged include international patient business softness, CGHS/ECHS onco drug price capping impact, and intense competition/lower occupancy in specific clusters like BG Road; brownfield expansion (FMRI, Mohali, Shalimar Bagh, Amritsar) and IHH's potential stake increase/equity infusion remain key strategic swing factors.

subsections.label: Occupancy dynamics - larger hospitals
points: Occupancy drop in larger hospitals like FMRI, BG Road, Faridabad attributed to drop in international business (international grew ~11% in Q4 vs ~18-20% for the full year) and to medical onco drug price capping impacting hospitals with larger ECHS/CGHS business share, mostly in Punjab region.

subsections.label: FEHI and Jaipur performance

subsections.label: BG Road underperformance
points: BG Road occupancy at 55% versus regional benchmark of 63-64%, attributed to lower government business mix (more TPA/cash business) and intense competition in the region (hospital shares boundary wall with another large competitor).
Immediate endeavor is to bring occupancy above 60% and operationalize enhanced capacity before increasing further; unit is on management's radar for improvement.
Brownfield capacity expansion in Bangalore (about 100 more beds) is being held back until occupancy improves.

subsections.label: Manesar
points: Manesar revenue of INR140 crores for FY26, exceeding expectations.
Manesar occupancy at 48%, described as deceptive since new beds were opened during the year and ramp-up is ongoing.

Unit had an EBITDA loss last year as a new unit but has since broken even and started contributing to EBITDA.

subsections.label: ARPOB growth drivers
points: FMRI ARPOB growth driven by international business (grew 20% over the year on gross basis, and international revenue includes markup that lifts ARPOB), plus new technology additions like MR Linac and Gamma Knife and strong onco/daycare business.
Last quarter saw dip in international business but the year-on-year ARPOB number still shows growth.

subsections.label: Revenue contribution of new units
points: Reported hospital revenue for Q4 FY26 was INR2,000 crores; excluding new units (TMI, People Tree, Adayu, Jalandhar) revenue was INR1,928 crores, indicating very little revenue contribution from these new units so far.

subsections.label: Gleneagles
points: Gleneagles revenue and EBITDA for the full year not available as it is not consolidated with Fortis; trending around INR70 crores per month.

subsections.label: Diagnostics business - Agilus
points: Gross additions of 125 customer touchpoints in Q4 supported 5% volume growth; B2C to B2B ratio fixed at 53:47 for the quarter.
For FY26, B2C to B2B revenue ratio remained stable at 52:48, reflecting balanced traction across channels.

Network expansion via gross addition of over 675 customer touchpoints and 20+ laboratories (including 10 hospital lab management laboratories), strengthening footprint in focus cities and emerging micro markets.

Preventive health and wellness portfolio saw healthy growth, supported by increasing awareness and adoption of preventive panels and corporate wellness programs; contributed 13% to overall mix in FY26 vs 11% last year, reinforcing position as key long-term growth driver.
Portfolio expanded with 50+ new tests across oncology, molecular diagnostics, prenatal care, immunology, infectious diseases, gastroenterology and neuro-oncology.
Volume-to-value split for FY26 was roughly 5% growth in volume; expectation for FY27 is about 70% from volume and 30% from value.

subsections.label: Bed capacity expansion
points: Added approximately 800 beds to the network in FY26 through combination of brownfield expansion and inorganic acquisitions.
In January 2026, acquired 125-bed People Tree Hospital in Yeshwanthpur, Bengaluru, along with adjacent land parcel enabling future expansion to over 300 beds.
In September 2025, entered long-term lease for 200-bed multi-specialty hospital in Greater Noida, strengthening NCR presence.
In July 2025, consummated acquisition of 228-bed Shrimann Superspecialty Hospital in Jalandhar, along with adjacent land parcel enabling future expansion to over 450 beds.
All acquisitions/arrangements focused on key growth clusters to leverage existing strength and position in these geographies.
Launched Adayu, a 36-bed specialized mental health care facility in Gurugram in November 2025, addressing distinct demand for mental health infrastructure separate from multi-specialty hospitals.
Expanded capacity across existing network by adding approximately 250 beds through brownfield expansion, primarily in Manesar, Noida and Faridabad.

subsections.label: Brownfield expansion plan (next 4 years)
points: Plan to add around 1,800 beds through brownfield expansion over next 4 years.

In FY27, expect to add capacity of more than 400 beds, with new tower at FMRI expected to be operationalized within weeks, and balance bed additions at Noida, Manesar, Amritsar, and FHKI Kolkata during the year.
FMRI new tower originally planned for last quarter of last financial year has moved to FY27; company moving well on brownfield expansion program overall.
Next year targeting around 500+ bed commissioning on brownfield side.

Capacity move: dedicated bed guidance in January PPT was 465 beds for FY28, revised to 173 beds in latest PPT — approximately 300-bed deviation now pushed to FY29, mainly attributed to Shalimar Bagh due to expected approval-related issues; once resolved, expansion will move fast.

subsections.label: Equipment/medical infrastructure
points: In FY26, company augmented medical infrastructure by commissioning several high-end equipment including soft tissue surgical robot, MRI machines, cath labs and PET CT, reaffirming commitment to advanced treatment options and physician-based care.

subsections.label: FMRI capacity
points: FMRI occupancy is close to 90% on some days and up to 95%, described as almost unmanageable; new beds getting commissioned over the next week, so no expected lag in absorption of new capacity.
FMRI capacity utilization is healthy at around 85-90% occupancy; facing bed shortage.

Initial plan is to operationalize new tower in phased manner (not all beds immediately) due to cost impact; company plans to open around 100 beds in current financial year but could open all beds if occupancy ramps up fast.

Brownfield expansion experience has been good — able to ramp up capacity quickly with economies of scale improving margins, as seen in Faridabad (50 beds added last year) and Noida (~100 beds added last year); similar or better outcome expected at FMRI.

subsections.label: Other brownfield/greenfield projects
points: New towers coming up in Mohali and Shalimar Bagh, expected to take about 2.5-3 years; also a large expansion planned in Amritsar.
Brownfield capacity in Bangalore (BG Road) not yet commissioned (about 100 more beds) pending occupancy improvement; expansion is in the same existing building.
Mulund currently at about 65% occupancy; possibility of adding another tower being planned since prior new capacity there is well absorbed.

Maturation cycle: for greenfield hospitals, cash breakeven typically happens at 18-24 months, followed by about a year to reach 18-20% EBITDA margin; for brownfield, capacity absorption is generally immediate since it is an existing hospital becoming larger, driving economies of scale and quicker profitability improvement.

subsections.label: M&A activity
points: Acquisition of People Tree Hospital (125 beds) in Bengaluru in January 2026 along with adjacent land parcel for future expansion to 300+ beds.
Acquisition of Shrimann Superspecialty Hospital (228 beds) in Jalandhar in July 2025 along with adjacent land parcel for future expansion to 450+ beds.
Long-term lease arrangement for 200-bed multi-specialty hospital in Greater Noida signed in September 2025.
Launch of Adayu, a specialized mental health care facility, as a foray into an emerging care segment distinct from multi-specialty hospitals.

subsections.label: Diagnostics demerger
points: Management stated current focus is on improving profitability/margin of the Diagnostics business rather than any demerger; business has started showing good results and focus is on extracting full potential.
Management stated this is not the right time for any value-locking action; once the business matures and performs as per market/competition, alternatives (including demerger) could be considered.

subsections.label: Gleneagles transaction
points: Gleneagles transaction is under deliberation and evaluation; no timeline can be given.
If the transaction proceeds, it will require majority of minority shareholder approval; management will come back to investors once ready with a proposal.

subsections.label: IHH stake increase
points: IHH group CEO indicated plan to increase stake in Fortis to 50% with a fresh equity infusion of around INR10,000 crores planned to meet growth aspirations; India described as a focused market for IHH via Fortis.
No specific timeline given; investment expected to occur as and when Fortis needs growth capital.

subsections.label: Competitive positioning strategy
points: Main differentiator versus PE-backed competition and asset-light platforms is clinical quality outcome and patient satisfaction.

PE-backed platforms viewed as a future opportunity for legacy/strategic players like Fortis; concerns exist about valuations being driven by these transactions, but market expected to address this over time.

subsections.label: Digital/preventive health strategy
points: Management acknowledged importance of primary care/online consultation platforms space but noted these consultations don't always lead to hospitalization and channels are not well formed; Fortis's core operation remains focused on tertiary, quaternary and critical care.

Company will gradually develop digital presence via its app and enhance offerings in the primary care space, but this is not a current focus area due to high cash burn associated with such businesses.

Management explicitly stated collaborating with third-party consultation platforms is not being considered, citing past experience that such collaboration would be dilutive to Fortis's presence; company will continue to develop its own platform, which requires further improvement.

subsections.label: International patient business softness
points: International patient business growth slowed to ~11% YoY in Q4 FY26 versus 18-20% for the full year, contributing to occupancy drops in larger hospitals like FMRI, BG Road, Faridabad.
Company is broadening its market base for international patients, concentrating more on Africa and other countries to mitigate the international business dip witnessed in the last quarter.
Domestic business growth has more or less offset the loss in international business revenue.

subsections.label: CGHS/ECHS onco drug price capping
points: Medical onco drug price capping under CGHS/ECHS (capped at 30% of MRP) has led to drop in revenue and occupancy, particularly in hospitals in Punjab region with larger ECHS/CGHS business share.
Company has stopped taking certain patients for drugs where adequate margin isn't earned, asking patients to procure drugs from CGHS stores or the market instead.
No immediate number available for revenue drop; no clarity yet on whether the price cap will be resolved — industry has submitted representation to government but outcome/timeline uncertain.

CGHS/ECHS have since increased prices for almost all specialties, though full impact has not materialized yet as registration for the new super-specialty category and billing clarity are still in progress.
Impact assessed as negative on revenue but not significantly on margin, since margins on capped-price patients were not being earned in the first place.

subsections.label: Intense competition / BG Road
points: BG Road faces intense competition, sharing a boundary wall with another large hospital in the city, contributing to occupancy of 55% versus a regional benchmark of 63-64%.
Lower share of government business (more TPA/cash mix) at BG Road also contributes to occupancy pressure.

subsections.label: Doctor cost/attrition
points: Slight increase noted in doctor costs; management does not expect further significant increases, having already taken necessary steps; minimal expected movement among senior clinicians.

subsections.label: Approval delays
points: Shalimar Bagh brownfield expansion delayed due to expected approval-related issues; expansion will move fast once resolved.

key_figures.label: Hospital EBITDA margin YoY improvement pace

subsections.label: Hospital business guidance
points: Hospital business guidance for FY27 revenue growth is 15%+.
EBITDA margin expected to improve by another 150 basis points in FY27.
FY28 hospital EBITDA margin target of 25% remains absolutely intact; management is more confident of delivering progress every year, at least 1.5-2% YoY improvement.
FY27 guidance is on an organic/ongoing basis, not including any pending acquisitions; acquisitions would be over and above the stated guidance.

Margin improvement levers include: increasing occupancy at large under-optimized hospitals (BG Road, Mulund); newer units (Manesar, Greater Noida, Ludhiana) that were loss-making last year now turning EBITDA positive and expected to contribute more strongly; brownfield expansion driving margin improvement via economies of scale; and completion of integration of recent acquisitions contributing to revenue and EBITDA.

subsections.label: Diagnostics business guidance
points: Agilus achieved its previously guided FY26 EBITDA margin range of 22-23%.
For FY27, Agilus guided EBITDA margin of 23-24%, with further investments planned into new centers.
Revenue growth improved to about 8.5% in FY26 from lower levels previously; company hopes to touch double-digit revenue growth in FY27.
Volume-to-value relationship expected at roughly 70% from volume and 30% from value for FY27, similar to the ~5% volume growth pattern seen this year.

guidance_ledger.statement: Revenue-wise, we are well poised to see on hospital side, 15% plus revenue growth.
EBITDA side, we expect another 150 basis point margin improvement for the current financial year.
That guidance remains absolutely intact... we can continue to deliver this progress every year, at least to 1.5% to 2% year-on-year — target of 25% by FY28.
As we had guided earlier, this year, we said that we'll be around 22% to 23% in terms of EBITDA. So we are there.
For the coming year as well, we'll be around 23% to 24% kind of EBITDA margins.
We'll definitely improve and touch about double digits this year is what we are hoping.
We expect that next year, it would be similar about 70% coming from volume and 30% coming from value.
We expect the Jaipur to grow around 15% plus next financial year with EBITDA margin in the range of 13%, 14%.
In the current financial year, our target -- our plan is to open around 100 beds. But if the occupancy ramps up fast, we can open all the beds also.
Over the next 4 years, we plan to ramp up bed capacity further through brownfield expansion by adding around 1,800 beds.

We expect to add capacity of more than 400 beds with a new tower at FMRI expected to be operationalized within weeks and balanced bed addition at Noida, Manesar and Amritsar as well as FHKI Kolkata coming during the year.
Next year, we are targeting around 500-plus bed expansion, commissioning of 500-plus beds on the brownfield side.
As regard the capex guidance, we expect to incur around INR900 crores annually on the capex, which may include 60% towards maintenance capex and balance is the growth capex.

guidance_ledger.metric: IHH stake increase and equity infusion
guidance_ledger.statement: There is a plan to increase their stake to 50%, and they have also mentioned some amount around INR10,000 crores fresh equity infusion in the company for meeting the growth aspirations... no specific time line I can give you, but it will happen over a period of time as and when the companies need the capital.
In the January PPT, we have dedicated 465 beds for FY28. Now in the latest PPT, we are guiding 173 beds... that 300 bed deviation is largely now in FY29 (mainly Shalimar Bagh due to approval issues).

risk_register.risk: International patient business slowdown
risk_register.note: International business growth slowed to ~11% YoY in Q4 FY26 from 18-20% for the full year, contributing to occupancy drops at FMRI, BG Road, Faridabad; company is diversifying to Africa and other markets to mitigate.

risk_register.risk: CGHS/ECHS onco drug price capping
risk_register.note: Drug price cap at 30% of MRP under CGHS/ECHS led to revenue/occupancy drop mainly in Punjab region hospitals; no clarity on resolution timeline; impact on margin limited since capped-price business wasn't profitable anyway.

risk_register.risk: Intense regional competition (BG Road)
risk_register.note: BG Road occupancy at 55% versus 63-64% regional benchmark due to competitive intensity and lower government-business mix; on management's radar for improvement.

risk_register.risk: Doctor cost/attrition
risk_register.note: Slight increase in doctor costs noted; management does not expect further major increases and is comfortable with the clinician pool.

risk_register.risk: Regulatory/approval delays
risk_register.note: Shalimar Bagh brownfield expansion delayed pending resolution of approval-related issues, pushing ~300 beds of capacity from FY28 to FY29.

risk_register.risk: PE-backed competitive intensity and valuations
risk_register.note: Management flagged rising PE-backed platform competition and asset-light models in Indian hospital sector, with concerns about valuations being driven by such transactions.

themes.label: Margin expansion
themes.note: Consolidated EBITDA margin rose to 22.8% in FY26 from 20.4% in FY25, with hospital margins improving from 20.5% to 22.2% and Diagnostics margin guided up to 23-24% in FY27.

themes.label: Capacity expansion / brownfield
themes.note: Company added ~800 beds in FY26 via brownfield and acquisitions and plans ~1,800 more beds over the next 4 years, though FY28 bed target revised down (465 to 173 beds) with ~300 beds pushed to FY29 due to Shalimar Bagh approval delays.

themes.label: International patient business softness
themes.note: International patient revenue growth slowed sharply to ~11% in Q4 from 18-20% for the full year, pressuring occupancy at flagship hospitals like FMRI, BG Road and Faridabad.

themes.label: CGHS/ECHS pricing headwind
themes.note: Government drug price capping on oncology treatments under CGHS/ECHS hurt revenue and occupancy mainly in Punjab-region hospitals, with no clarity yet on resolution.

themes.label: Diagnostics turnaround (Agilus)
themes.note: Agilus delivered improved revenue growth (8.5% FY26) and margin expansion (23.6% FY26 EBITDA margin vs 17.7% FY25), with guidance for double-digit revenue growth and 23-24% margin in FY27.

themes.label: IHH parent support / capital infusion
themes.note: IHH indicated plans to raise its stake to 50% with a potential ~INR10,000 crore fresh equity infusion to support growth, though no firm timeline given.

themes.label: Competitive intensity (PE-backed platforms)
themes.note: Management acknowledged rising PE-backed competition and asset-light models in the sector, viewing it as both a valuation risk and a future consolidation opportunity for legacy strategic players like Fortis.

key_takeaways: Consolidated revenues for FY26 stood at INR9,128 crores, a growth of 17.3% over FY25.
Hospital business revenue grew 19.1% to INR7,773 crores in FY26, while diagnostic business net revenues were at INR1,355 crores, a growth of 8%.
Consolidated operating EBITDA increased 31.3% to INR2,085 crores, translating into a margin of 22.8% in FY26 versus 20.4% in FY25.
Consolidated profit after tax for the year increased 31.5% to INR1,064 crores in FY26 compared to INR809 crores in FY25.
The company's net debt stands at INR2,334 crores with a net debt-to-EBITDA of 1.09x as on March 31, 2026, as against 0.93 on March 31, 2025.
Hospital occupancy in FY26 was 68% compared to 69% in FY25; occupied beds increased by 15% from 2,838 beds in FY25 to 3,270 beds in FY26.
Revenue from international patients grew 18.5% to INR639 crores, contributing 7.8% to overall hospital business revenue.
Board recommended a dividend of INR1 per share (10% of face value) for the fourth consecutive year.
Company added approximately 800 beds to its network in FY26 through brownfield expansion and inorganic acquisitions.
Occupancy drop in some hospitals attributed to slowdown in international business and CGHS/ECHS onco drug price capping in the Punjab region.
IHH group CEO indicated a plan to increase stake in Fortis to 50% with around INR10,000 crores fresh equity infusion for growth aspirations, though no specific timeline was given.

FY27 guidance: hospital revenue growth of 15%+ with 150bps EBITDA margin improvement; FY28 hospital EBITDA margin target of 25% reiterated with confidence of 1.5-2% YoY improvement; Diagnostics FY27 EBITDA margin guided at 23-24% with double-digit revenue growth.
pressing_questions: How much impact would the discontinuation of onco treatment (due to CGHS/ECHS drug price capping) have on revenue, and is there a possibility this gets resolved?
What is management's view on margins for next year in the hospital business given new capacity coming in and doctor cost dynamics?
Why were CGHS patients being counted in occupancy in the first place if they could be daycare/chemo business rather than occupancy?
When do you think the CGHS onco price cap issue gets resolved, and how does this pan out?
Is there any thought on demerging the Diagnostics business and keeping Hospitals as a standalone business?
Can you provide the revenue contribution from the 800 new beds added this year, broken down between acquired assets and brownfield expansion?
What is the revenue and EBITDA of Gleneagles for the full year, and what is the timeline for the Gleneagles transaction?
Any update or timeline on IHH increasing its stake in the company and the reported equity infusion?
What is the current revenue run rate and KPIs for Manesar, and is there any cannibalization effect on FMRI from Manesar?
What is driving the significant ARPOB growth at FMRI and FEHI despite occupancy dips?
Given the January PPT indicated 465 beds for FY28 versus 173 beds in the latest PPT, which facilities account for the ~300-bed deviation now pushed to FY29?
How does management view increasing PE-backed competition and asset-light models in the Indian hospital sector, and how does Fortis differentiate itself?
What is the normal maturation cycle for a hospital to move from loss-making to a mature 20%+ EBITDA business, for both greenfield and brownfield expansions?

QUESS.about: Quess Corp Limited (Quess) is India’s leading business services provider, leveraging its extensive domain knowledge and future-ready digital platforms to drive client productivity through outsourced solutions.[1]

quarters.summary: Q1 FY27 saw broad-based double-digit revenue growth across all three core segments (General Staffing, Professional Staffing, Overseas) with sharp PAT/EPS growth, a zero-debt balance sheet, and management guiding for continued margin expansion, GS headcount net addition of 30,000+ for FY27, Professional Staffing margins held at 11-12%, overseas margins targeted at 6.5-7%, and the Quess 2.0 partner-led capital-light strategy aiming for 20-25% of revenue from higher-margin, dollar-linked businesses over the next 3-4 years.

subsections.label: Margin drivers
points: Sequential EBITDA margin moderation of 20 bps was largely a function of the annual merit cycle and variable pay reset typically flowing through in Q1.
An additional 11 bps contraction in margin in Q1 over Q4 FY26 was due to the one-time pass-through revenue of Rs. 176 crore for the Labor Code.
PBT and PAT grew considerably faster than revenue, reflecting genuine operating leverage layered on top of a couple of one-off items.

Other income was higher largely attributable to the income tax refund of Rs. 261 crore (including Rs. 22 crore interest) received during the quarter, pertaining to prior years and representing a one-time cash and balance sheet positive impact.
Remains a zero-debt company as of June 2026 with a healthy net cash position, reflecting continued balance sheet strength and discipline.
Final dividend of Rs. 3 per share for the last financial year subject to approval at the AGM on 25 August 2026, in line with commitment to reward shareholders.

subsections.label: General Staffing
points: Continued scale leadership and execution discipline; described as the scale engine of the business providing stability, cash generation and a broad operating base.
Growth led by CRT (Consumer, Retail, Telecommunications), Manufacturing and Allied verticals, while BFSI saw a marginal decline.

BFSI split into core banking (facing strong regulatory headwinds on what can/cannot be outsourced) versus NBFC/fintech/housing finance (large opportunity but smaller scale per account); recovery in BFSI will take time as relationships build.

Manufacturing PAPM is higher (800-1100) than the broad GS PAPM (600-700), but requires intensity in sourcing, infrastructure (65 offices), and technology investment built over 18-19 years — not easy to scale.
Focus continues on higher-value segments: construction, Manufacturing and VAS, supported by technology and AI-led sourcing/productivity initiatives.
DSO remains tightly controlled at 15 days AR (28 days including UBR), reflecting continued collections discipline.
GS has over 37,000 open mandates at quarter-end plus a strong sales pipeline heading into Q2.
Fixed-variable mix in GS contracts is roughly 70-30; 38% of Q1's new contracts came with variable markup, but these need time to mature and scale to benefit from variabilization.
Gross margins differ by vertical: Consumer at 2-3% versus Manufacturing at 5-6%.

subsections.label: Professional Staffing
points: Delivered another quarter of profitable GCC-led growth; GCC engagements account for 71-72% of headcount and 68% of revenue.
Sequential dip in EBITDA reflects annual merit cycle and variable pay reserve typically landing in Q1, which has historically normalized as the year progresses.
Gross margin to EBITDA conversion remained above 50%, sustaining double-digit EBITDA margins even after absorbing merit cycle payouts, underscoring structural strength.
Internal priority remains to scale Professional Staffing to a Rs. 30 crore quarterly EBITDA run rate.
India has 2,407 GCCs; Quess has captured only ~10% of them, representing a large addressable opportunity; India attracts 250-300 new GCCs annually, of which ~5% are from the Japanese ecosystem.

Some individual GCCs may mature and see hiring slowdowns, but new GCCs, international corridors (e.g., Japan corridor live), and geographic/practice-based intensity support continued bullishness on GCC growth.

GCC talent deployed is mostly in the 5-13 year experience category (niche talent), commanding revenue per associate of Rs. 1.5-2.5 lakh/month with a decent margin profile, roughly matching technology talent deployed in Southeast Asia in revenue/PAPM terms.

subsections.label: Overseas business
points: Delivered consistent double-digit growth across geographies with diversification across Singapore, Middle East and rest of the world; EBITDA margins remained stable despite currency fluctuations, with 37 new logos added and overall overseas EBITDA margin at 6.2%.
Singapore: General Staffing added 17 new contracts and 37 local nationals to headcount.
Malaysia: scaled to 873 headcount with 55% YoY revenue growth and 4.1% EBITDA margin.
Middle East: 27% revenue growth, 18% EBITDA growth YoY, 12% EBITDA margin.
Philippines: 17% YoY revenue growth with 10% net margin.
Two overseas markets already operate at double-digit EBITDA margins; the rest are sub-5%, blending to the overall 6.2-6.5% margin.
GS profit pool currently represents 50% of total company profit, with Professional and International combined making up the other 50%.

subsections.label: Sourcing strength & client differentiation
points: Sourcing infrastructure built over 18-19 years is a key differentiator: 65 offices, presence at 6,464 pin codes, 41% of associates in Tier-3 and below.
Every second core employee is a recruiter; 1,400 total recruiters with 750 dedicated to General Staffing.
Sourcing gross adds reached 46,000 in Q1 FY27 versus 29,000-30,000 in the comparable prior-year quarter, with 18,000 hires sourced in June alone, reflecting scaled-up sourcing momentum.
Scale sourcing capability differentiates Quess with clients, especially for tougher mandates like Manufacturing and Construction.

Structural policy shifts (GST, COVID transition) have historically benefited the largest operator disproportionately within 6-18 months; headcount roughly doubled from ~240,000 (March 2021) to 482,000 today over five-plus years.

Management declined to quantify how much near-term benefit will accrue from potential client consolidation toward large operators due to labor law/compliance complexity, but stated continued focus on capturing such opportunities with people, scale and technology.

subsections.label: Quess 2.0 strategy
points: Digital platform businesses remain in investment phase, building blue-collar jobs marketplace and AI-driven recruitment/workforce solutions.

Repositioning current volume engine towards higher margin, value-accretive growth via partner-led, capital-light talent corridors across five focus segments: Healthcare, Technology, MEP and Civil, Hospitality and Allied, Finance and Professional.
Japan corridor is signed and in execution; Europe (particularly Nordics) in advanced discussion stages; Israel in discussion; North America at early exploration stage.

Model is CAPEX-light and partner-led across territories: Far-East (Japan), Israel, UK, Germany, Nordics, Canada, US — not about setting up operating staffing companies in these countries since they have turned demographic negative 15-25 years ago.

Intent is to leverage disproportionate business flowing from these mature/demographically-negative markets to India on both talent and technology (feeding GCC strength), and to build reverse skilled talent mobility for international markets.
One announced partner is a listed Japanese company, reputed in HR technology space (not staffing); other four partners not yet disclosed pending MOU/MSA finalization.

Margin trajectory for Quess 2.0 corridors expected to be closer to international/professional corridor margins, and much lower than General Staffing platform margin; management declined to give exact margin guidance before MSAs are signed and delivery begins.

No M&A currently planned; global scale ambition to be pursued via capital-light partnership corridors rather than acquisitions; management will inform investors if a value-accretive M&A opportunity arises at the right valuation.

Target for higher-margin businesses to reach 20-25% of revenue over the next 3-4 years, with GS profit pool mix targeted to fall from 50% currently (down from 65-68% about 18 months ago) to 35%, while higher-margin business profit pool mix rises from 50% (up from 30-35% 18 months ago) to 65%.
Overseas revenue currently represents 7% of total (dollar-denominated), versus 93% INR-denominated; total international headcount stands at 7,000.

Worldwide HR services market is ~$700 billion, of which India is $19-20 billion (Quess holds 9-10% share by value) and the rest-of-world ex-India is $680 billion (Quess holds <1% share); 60-65% of that $680 billion market is concentrated in US/Canada/Nordics/UK/Japan combined.

subsections.label: Global ambition / market context
points: Stated goal from demerger ~1 year ago was for Quess to become world's #1 staffing organization (from rank 4th/5th then to currently 3rd/4th by volume), requiring 125,000 additional associates to reach a target workforce of 6-6.3 lakh associates.
North Star ambition is 1 million associates by 2030.
India's demographic dividend expected to remain positive for at least the next 18 years, underpinning the 1 million headcount North Star.
Indian government pursuing FTAs with multiple nations (Europe FTA announced, expected to fructify in calendar 2027; US FTA hoped to happen soon), each including chapters on embedded skilled mobility.

Indian nationals have historically performed well in Middle East (blue/grey collar) and North America (technology talent); management expects these corridors to open further as mature economies seek to solve internal healthcare, technology, and skilled-trade shortages.
Rest-of-world staffing markets are more consolidated among mature players versus the more fragmented/organized-vs-unorganized dynamic seen in Asia/India.

subsections.label: Regulatory / Labor Code transition
points: New Labor Code implementation resulted in a one-time revenue impact of Rs. 176 crore in Q1 FY27, booked as liability once customers confirm choice between FTE and permanent model; this is a pass-through with no profitability impact.
As of Q1, ~68% of customers have confirmed their model choice; company expects to cover the entire customer base by end of Q2 / early Q3 FY27.

Remaining liability to be booked in Q2 is estimated to be lesser than the Rs. 170 crore booked in Q1 (roughly one-third of Q1's figure), with normal recurring numbers being small thereafter and not expected to meaningfully bump up revenue.

subsections.label: BFSI regulatory headwind
points: Core banking sector faces strong regulatory headwinds around what can and cannot be outsourced, which has led to marginal decline in BFSI within General Staffing.
NBFC, housing finance and fintech opportunity remains large but individual account scale is smaller (a few hundred each), and recovery will take time as relationships are built.

subsections.label: Forward outlook (management closing remarks)
points: Festive season demand visible across client base, giving confidence heading into the seasonally strongest quarter for both sourcing and sales.
Strong foundation laid across headcount and contracts positions the company well to convert demand into revenue as it comes through.
H1 performance, along with Professional Staffing and international business, expected to aid margin growth for the rest of FY27.

FY27 focus areas: driving GS volume with net addition of 30,000+ associates, sustaining growth momentum in Professional Staffing and overseas business, driving margin expansion across segments, scaling dollar-linked talent corridors under Quess 2.0, and continued disciplined capital allocation and balance sheet strength.
Professional Staffing EBITDA margin guided at 11-12% ongoing; overseas EBITDA margin guided to improve to 6.5-7% forward from current 6.2-6.5%.

key_takeaways: We are pleased to start Q1 FY27 on a strong note with broad-based growth and improvements in the quality of our earnings.
For Quarter 1 FY27, we delivered a consolidated revenue of Rs. 4,182 crores, reflecting a 15% year-on-year growth while a 7% quarter-on-quarter growth.
The EBITDA during this quarter came in at Rs. 85 crores. This is a 21% year-on-year growth with a margin at 2.02%.
PAT stood at Rs. 82 crores, growing at 61% year-on-year and 28% quarter-on-quarter with an EPS of Rs. 5.5, also up 61% year-on-year.
During the quarter, due to the implementation of the new Labor Code, resulted in a one-time revenue impact of Rs. 176 crores as well.
During this quarter, we received income tax refunds for the past financial years, including interest of Rs. 261 crores, which contributed to higher other income for the period.
Importantly, we remain a zero-debt company as of June 2026 with a healthy net cash position, reflecting the continued strength and discipline of our balance sheet.

Q1 FY27 reflects continued momentum across our portfolio. With all three core segments delivering double-digit revenue growth on a year-on-year basis, we ended the quarter with a headcount of approximately 4,82,214 associates, which is up 4.5% year-on-year, reinforcing our position as India's largest domestic staffing platform.

In terms of the IT staffing, Professional Staffing segment... are we seeing some signs of normalization in terms of GCC hiring? And can there be a shift between some slowdown in GCC versus some pickup in the IT services traditional hiring there in the IT staffing?

So, on the Quess 2.0 pivot that you highlighted in your presentation, I just wanted to understand the economics better. So, would the reverse migration have similar margins to the current overseas staffing business that we do and the inbound GCC business be similar to the Professional Staffing business that we have?

So, given that this Quess 2.0 pivot that we are doing is through a partnership model, so just want to understand the economics and the margins. Would they be similar to the business that we do currently?
It has been four quarters since we have seen the ELI scheme coming. Can you throw some light on the benefits you have accrued from that? How is the penetration?

quarters.summary: Quess Corp closed FY26 with steady execution, strong margin expansion and improved earnings quality despite modest revenue growth; management guided FY27 focus on scaling Professional Staffing and Overseas business, sustaining margin expansion (2%+ heading to 2.4% medium-term), driving higher return on capital, and continued disciplined capital allocation, with General Staffing expected to return to 10-11% headcount growth and 12-13% revenue growth.
