subsections.label: Q4 FY26 Highlights
points: Q4 FY26 was a quarter of strong margin expansion and improved profitability, reflecting continued benefits from mix improvement, operating discipline and cost optimization.
Consolidated revenues showed broadly stable sequential performance.

This margin expansion indicates improved operating leverage, a more favorable business mix, and sustained cost discipline across the organization, reflecting in operating margins for all businesses combined and crossing INR 100 crore for the quarter.

Reported PAT increase supported by operating leverage and lower exceptional impacts; on an adjusted basis, PAT remained stable sequentially, reflecting underlying business strength and consistency in earnings quality.

subsections.label: FY26 Full Year Highlights
points: While revenue growth remained calibrated during the year, the financial performance reflects a deliberate focus on profitability and earnings quality rather than volume-led expansion.
This reflects disciplined execution in a year of external transitions, particularly around Labor Code implementation.
EBITDA-to-operating cash flow conversion remains strong, highlighting disciplined working capital management and high-quality earnings.

subsections.label: Capital Allocation & Balance Sheet
points: Balance sheet remains strong and well-capitalized with zero gross debt.
Free cash flow generation remains healthy, supported by strong EBITDA growth and tight working capital management.

Board proposed final dividend of INR 3 along with a special dividend of INR 3 marking 10 years of IPO, reflecting confidence in cash generation and commitment to shareholder returns while maintaining adequate liquidity for growth objectives.
Total payout aligned with free cash flow.

subsections.label: Tax & Contingent Liability (Q&A)
points: ETR guidance of 7-10% for next 3 years given business mix and new sectors being targeted.

Contingent liability comprises two elements: 80JJAA litigation (industry-wide, sub-judice, company continues to avail 80JJAA exemption, no ETR impact expected) and GST litigation (early-stage, involves ~10 insurance companies as co-litigants, slow progression expected, no concrete conclusion expected this year, current stand maintained until final conclusion).

subsections.label: Portfolio Mix Shift
points: FY26 reflects a clear shift in business towards higher margin, more sustainable segments even as leadership position in co-staffing was maintained.
At a portfolio level, high margin businesses (Professional Staffing and Overseas) now contribute 50% of total profitability, a structural shift beginning to reflect in margin trajectory.

This structural shift in mix combined with cost discipline, pricing optimization and improved execution has been the primary driver of margin expansion during the year; complemented by cost management and delivery efficiencies.

subsections.label: General Staffing — Scale Leadership with Execution Discipline
points: Continued resilience and strong execution at scale despite structural transitions including Labor Code implementation, geopolitical instability and portfolio recalibration.

Discontinued milestone-based project (7,000 resources) which did not meet financial metrics/cash realization thresholds was completely closed and dialed down in FY26; no other such known discontinuation event currently anticipated.
Revenue growth modest YoY; significant investments made in verticalization, technology and hiring of recruiters to make the business future-proof and future-ready.
Headcount growth remained measured owing to global factors and supply-side talent shrinkage, especially in latter part of the financial year.
DSO tightly managed showing strong collection discipline.
BFSI and CRT verticals saw near-term softness, offset by stability in newer lines of business including manufacturing and infrastructure-led construction demand.
Focus continues on improving profit per associate, enhancing client mix, and driving operational efficiency at scale.

Margin at 1.5% supported by pricing discipline and cost control even amid BFSI/CRT softness; GS has modeled next 4-year trajectory on both volume and value strategy, with customers in construction and value-added manufacturing yielding slightly higher margin than traditional GS margins.

Sales team capable of delivering 275-300 new logos per year; in the last 12 quarters added more than 100,000 new headcounts; recruitment team can consistently deliver headcount growth in a stable environment.
Sequential decline in quarterly GS revenue attributed to one-time incentive pass-through and gratuity billing in Q3 due to Labor Code implementation.
Expect to return to 10-11% headcount growth and 12-13% revenue growth for General Staffing.
Collect & Pay expected to be maintained between 70-76% even as business diversifies into construction and manufacturing verticals with 30-60 day DSO trends.

subsections.label: Professional Staffing — High-Quality Growth Engine
points: Delivered a record strong quarter and a year of profitable growth, driven by focus on high-margin digital and technology roles, rationalization of low-yield engagements, and strong demand from GCCs.
Double-digit margins believed sustainable, supported by structural demand and disciplined execution; management guidance is to remain in the 11-12% margin category for the medium term.
GCC-led engagements account for 71% headcount, reflecting strategic positioning in high-value niche roles.

Margin structural story built over ~5 years since 2020-2021 (from 4.7% to ~12%), involving moving away from low-margin 0-3 year experience category, pivoting to GCCs, building niche/high-experience execution capability.

Q4 seasonality: lowest working days in the year plus furlough spillover into Q4 (and January) depress reported quarterly revenue/margin under T&M model, masking underlying net additions/margin improvement which should show in H1.
61 new logos acquired in FY26; over 50% already active with 200+ resources deployed; real impact expected to show in H1 FY27.

GCC demand differs structurally from IT services — GCCs need experienced (7-8+ years) niche talent (data centre, AI, cybersecurity, product) vs IT services' entry-level volume hiring; this yields higher revenue per person and higher margin.

AI/GCC penetration shifted skill mix: two years back only 30% of demand was in AI/data/cloud/cybersecurity space, now ~60% of total demand, commanding better bill rates and margin; skill bracket shifted from 0-4 years experience to 4-10+ years.
Large demand-supply gap in emerging technology skills where staffing companies play a big role since large organizations lack ready deployable talent internally.
Seeing wider GCC demand emerging from Asia-Pacific in addition to India, and company is looking at new corridors to tap GCC demand.
Net billable associate additions of ~400+ in FY26, with 50% from new signups (61 logos) and 50% from existing logos.
Confident net addition for next couple of years will be in double digit 10-12% range, with roughly 50:50 split between new signups and existing accounts.

subsections.label: Overseas Business — Diversified Growth with Margin Expansion
points: Consistent growth and improving margin driven by diversification across geographies.

Middle East, Singapore, Malaysia and Philippines all posted growth; Middle East closed FY26 with strong revenue and EBITDA growth and highest margin among segments; Malaysia showed strongest revenue growth; Philippines crossed 700 headcount milestone; Singapore stabilized during the year with improved revenue mix and cost efficiency after prior challenges over last six quarters.

Q4 revenue jump explained by three factors: core organic growth plus one-time pass-through, new customer additions, and INR currency devaluation gains against operating geographies' currencies; moderating for ~INR 10 crore one-time pass-through, ~INR 32 crore was organic growth, new customer growth and FX gain.

Middle East: essential-services portfolio diversification (technology, insurance, telecom, e-commerce/logistics, banking, retail) built over 7-8 years reduces exposure to any one segment/customer/market; record revenue and collection in Q4 despite regional geopolitical concerns; crossed AOP targets on revenue, EBITDA and margin during the quarter; management continues to monitor situation closely and stay in touch with customers.
Overall international portfolio is now better balanced and structurally more profitable.
Blended margin target maintained at (+6%) for the international mix and book going forward.

subsections.label: Digital & AI Strategy
points: Digital platforms continue to remain investment-focused with a layer of AI; sharpened focus towards AI-led solutions with a plan for the coming three years.
Building a blue-collar marketplace, AI-driven recruitment and workforce solutions to strengthen long-term position in technology-led workforce management platforms.
Recognized with LinkedIn Talent Award 2025 for 'AI Pioneer', reflecting focus on innovation in talent acquisition.

subsections.label: International Footprint
points: Overseas operations span Middle East, Singapore, Malaysia and Philippines with differentiated growth and margin profiles across geographies.

Middle East operations diversified across essential-services sectors including technology, insurance, telecommunications, e-commerce and logistics, banking and retail over the last 7-8 years, reducing concentration risk to any single segment, customer or market.

key_figures.label: Talent as share of GCC problem to solve

subsections.label: Customer & Talent Recognition
points: Certified as a 'Great Place to Work' for the 7th consecutive year, with recognition across India, Singapore and Middle East.

GCC engagement model includes direct engagement with clients as well as indirect partnerships — with consulting firms that bring businesses to India needing an execution partner, and with real estate developers holding space mandates — with Quess positioned to serve talent needs (80% of the GCC problem) across all these channels.

subsections.label: Portfolio Recalibration
points: Post-demerger philosophy: any business not meeting the company's financial metrics or cash realization thresholds will be exited/discontinued — as executed with the 7,000-headcount milestone-based project that was closed during FY26.
Company is one year post its demerger and describes itself as foundationally strong in its 19th year, with balance between business/execution focus and treasury/finance strength.

subsections.label: Regulatory / Macro Risks
points: Labor Code implementation caused structural transitions during the year including one-time incentive pass-through and gratuity billing impacts in Q3; rules are yet to be notified and law is still evolving; more client confirmations on approach expected in Q1 and Q2 FY27, with full confirmation expected by end of Q2, after which the impact will be taken.

GST 2.0 implementation, Labor Code, and global factors including geopolitical instability and state elections all occurred within a seven-month span, creating structural headwinds for General Staffing headcount growth.

Geopolitical instability in the Middle East is being watched closely; company maintains treasury/balance-sheet robustness to handle eventualities and pay employees/associates on time; diversified essential-services portfolio mitigates concentration risk.
BFSI and CRT verticals within General Staffing saw near-term softness.
Prior-year (Q4 FY25) BFSI regulatory-based impact caused a 37,000 headcount decline, creating a high base effect and ~7% revenue shrinkage impact that is now largely normalized.

Potential indirect risk to GCC demand story from large US companies talking about reducing headcounts, which could trickle down to their GCC operations — though management notes GCC roles are structurally different (skilled, 7-8+ years experience) from volume-driven IT services roles, and sees emerging demand from Asia-Pacific GCCs.
80JJAA litigation is an industry-wide matter, currently sub-judice; company continues to avail the exemption; concrete progress expected this year but outcome uncertain.

GST litigation is in early stage, involving ~10 insurance companies as co-litigants; slow progression expected with no concrete conclusion likely this year; company must maintain current stance on contingent liability until final conclusion.

subsections.label: FY27 Outlook
points: As the company moves into FY27, focus will be on scaling Professional Staffing and Overseas business, driving margin expansion across segments, leveraging technology and AI platforms, and continuing disciplined capital allocation.
Management remains confident in ability to deliver sustainable, profitable growth with improving return ratios.

Financial priorities for FY27: sustaining margin expansion trajectory while maintaining strong cash conversion, driving higher return on capital, and supporting growth investments while ensuring capital discipline.

Overall blended EBITDA margin guided at 2.2% if current portfolio mix persists, but given anticipated higher clip-rate growth in General Staffing (a 1.5% margin business) in FY27, near-term guidance is (+2%) moving to 2.4% in the medium term (3-year horizon).
Professional Staffing margin guided to remain in the 11-12% category for the medium term.
Overseas business margin guided to continue working towards (+6%) blended margin.

General Staffing expected to return to 10-11% headcount growth and 12-13% revenue growth in FY27, aided by sales team capacity of 275-300 new logos/year and installed sourcing capacity of 50,000 people/quarter (vs. recent delivery of only 37,000-38,000).
Professional Staffing net headcount additions expected in double digits (10-12%) over the next couple of years, split roughly 50:50 between new signups and existing logos.
No further known discontinuation events currently anticipated after closing the 7,000-headcount milestone project.
Labor Code client confirmations expected to build through Q1 and Q2 FY27, with full confirmation expected by end of Q2 FY27, after which impact will be taken into financials.
ETR guidance of 7-10% for the next three years, with no expected impact from 80JJAA or GST contingent liabilities on ETR at this stage.

key_takeaways: For Q4 FY26, we delivered a revenue of INR 3,892 crores, reflecting a 6% year-on-year growth, while the EBITDA came in at INR 86 crores up 28% year-on-year, with the margins expanding to 2.2%. PAT stood at INR 64 crores, with an EPS of INR 4.3.

For the full-year FY26, revenues stand at INR 15,305 crores, with an EBITDA at INR 312 crores, reflecting 19% growth in EBITDA and a PAT excluding one-time exceptional item at INR 230 crores, up 10% year-on-year. This marks a healthy ROE of 20%.
Importantly, our EBITDA-to-operating cash flow conversion remains strong at 80%, highlighting the disciplined working capital management and high-quality earnings.
The Board has thus approved a special dividend of INR 3 per share on account of the 10th Anniversary of our IPO and a final dividend of INR 3 per share.
At a portfolio level, high margin businesses now contribute 50% of the total profitability, a structural shift that is beginning to reflect in our margin trajectory as well.

Professional Staffing has delivered another record strong quarter for us and a year of profitable growth... The revenue for the year has come out at INR 930 crores, which is up 13% year-on-year. EBITDA increased sharply to INR 111 crores, up 43% year-on-year. Margins have expanded to (+12%).
Overseas business: For the year FY26, the revenue stands at INR 1,197 crores, up 5% year-on-year. EBITDA increased to INR 77 crores, up 21% year-on-year.

As we move into FY27, our focus will be on scaling Professional Staffing and Overseas business, drive margin expansion across segments, leveraging technology and AI platforms, and continuing our disciplined capital allocation.
pressing_questions: On Overseas business, we saw a sharp uptick in Q4. Could you help us understand what were the drivers behind this growth and to what extent is this sustainable versus being one-off in nature? Additionally, any color on how the Middle East business could be impacted by the ongoing geopolitical situation?
On General Staffing margins, margins expanded by 20 basis points year-on-year. What are the key drivers behind this improvement, and should we view this level of margins as sustainable going forward?

Professional Staffing margins are now 12.7%... Do we think there is more room to improve these margins further? Overseas at 6.2% as well while General Staffing remains at 1.5%. As the higher margin segment scale, what is the expected blended margins we expect over next 2-3 years?

Can you provide more details on the revenue and margin impact of this discontinuation [7,000 headcount project]? Also, are we largely done with this restructuring or do we think that in FY27 there could be some revenue hit because of further discontinuation of the project?

GCC within Professional Staffing now contributes 71% of the headcount. How does GCC margin profile compare to the broader Professional Staffing? And is there further GCC-led margin upside we foresee? Also, do we see any risk to this GCC story we have seen in the last couple of years, as many of the large US companies are talking about reducing headcounts this year.

What percentage of our revenue or client would have accepted, let us say, revised terms or revised rate based on the new Labor Code-related revision and where discussions are still, let us say, happening?

If we just compare the Professional Staffing margins to the competition, we are just almost like double of that irrespective of the GCC contribution being in the 70% range for the competition also. So, what exactly we are doing differently here and what gives us the confidence that these kinds of margins in the Professional Staffing is sustainable over a medium-to-long term.

IVALUE.about: Incorporated in 2008, iValue Infosolutions Limited is a Strategic Technology Advisor, secures and manages enterprises’ digital assets in hybrid-cloud environments. With 500+ experts, the company offers custom solutions and services, partnering with top OEMs across India, SAARC and SEA.[1]

quarters.summary: iValue delivered gross sales of INR 641.2 crore (up 5.7% YoY) and PAT of INR 15.7 crore (up 51.7% YoY) in Q1 FY27, broadly in line with expectations given its H2-skewed business rhythm. Management reiterated its FY27 guidance of 20% growth in both gross sales and PAT, citing a pipeline of INR 6,150 crore (up 6% QoQ) with steady win rates of 30-35%, continued annuity growth (14% YoY, 46.4% of gross sales), and strong momentum in Cybersecurity and DCI (AI-led infrastructure demand), even as ILM budgets are temporarily reallocated toward GPU/Data Center spend.

subsections.label: Gross margin recovery
points: Gross margin declined in Q1 FY26 due to INR depreciation against USD and low-margin deals; company recovered on both aspects in Q1 FY27 despite similar rupee depreciation this quarter as well.
Q1 FY27 margin of 8.1% matches the Q1 FY25 level, indicating normalization from the one-off dip in Q1 FY26.

subsections.label: PAT growth drivers
points: Sustained cash flows during current and last quarters helped reduce finance costs, supporting PAT growth.

Historically, bottom-line growth has outpaced top-line growth; management expects this trend to continue in FY27, with margins helped in Q1 by favorable base but partly offset from Q2 onward by annual appraisal cycles starting July 1.

subsections.label: Revenue lumpiness / large deals
points: Business depends on a few large deals (2-3 per year) which typically occur in Q3/Q4, making H2 cyclically stronger; FY26 was an exception with large deals (e.g., GSTN ~INR150 crore billing in Q2 FY26) occurring in Q1/Q2, causing a higher base and muted YoY growth optics in FY27 Q1.

Management emphasizes evaluating performance on a full-year basis rather than quarterly, citing a 10-year track record of 23% CAGR in gross sales and 28% CAGR in PAT (per investor presentation Slide 6).

FY26 full year gross sales grew ~20% and PAT grew ~19.5%; gross profit rose to INR266 crore in FY26 from INR240 crore in FY25 (10% growth); quarterly gross sales growth was 3% in Q3 FY26 and 12% in Q4 FY26, with gross profit growth of 9-10% in prior quarters, illustrating typical annual margin range of 9-10%.

subsections.label: Working capital and balance sheet
points: Net working capital days improved by 1 day YoY to 52 days as of 30 June 2026 (vs 53 days a year earlier).
Meaningful reduction seen in inventory, historically a small component of the working capital cycle.

subsections.label: Corporate actions
points: First AGM post-listing scheduled for 19 August 2026.

subsections.label: Pipeline dynamics
points: Pipeline stood at INR 6,150 crore, up 6% over the last quarter (an addition of ~INR300 crore last quarter), reflecting strong demand across segments.
Win rates holding steady at 30-35% annualized, supporting confidence in meeting the year's growth commitment.

Pipeline (funnel) composition by segment (DCI, Cybersecurity, ILM) is not precisely known upfront since pricing negotiations and win/loss mix across order pieces determine final composition; however, DCI is expected to be 18-20% of total revenue for the full year.

Once a deal reaches quote stage, conversion to order typically takes less than a month, but reaching quote stage requires demos, curated solutioning through COE, and customer approvals — a longer overall process before entering the 'sanitized' pipeline figure.

Customers have prioritized budgets toward GPU and data center spend, causing surge in some business pillars while others (e.g., ILM) see a temporary dip; on a normalized annual basis, overall growth of ~20% in top line and PAT is expected across the five business pillars, with some quarter-to-quarter variation between pillars.

subsections.label: Supply chain / delivery timelines
points: Supply chain has been impacted for almost a year and has become cyclical; iValue's represented OEMs have comparatively shorter delivery delays (~1.5 months) versus other OEMs in the market reportedly taking 7-8 months, viewed as a relatively fortunate position, possibly due to earlier-cycle order fulfillment becoming a new normal.

subsections.label: Growth drivers by segment
points: Growth during the quarter was driven by Cybersecurity, DCI, ALM, and Cloud.

Cybersecurity remains the core engine and largest business vertical, contributing 44% of top line in Q1 FY27; growth of 8% YoY attributed to continued demand though slower than some competitors cited by an analyst (25-30% industry growth claims); management maintains cybersecurity will sustain 45-50% share of top line annualized.

DCI (Data Center Infrastructure) grew 180% YoY (alternately cited as 186%) and reached 22% of gross sales in Q1 FY27; it is a key growth accelerator supported by rising AI-led infrastructure demand, GPU-based infrastructure investments, hybrid public cloud and storage modernization; OEM Arista cited as taking leading position in GPU infrastructure stack.
Cloud and ALM segments each grew ~47% YoY.

ILM/ALM segment (budget-reallocated segment) saw a decline of 60% YoY attributed to temporary reallocation of enterprise budgets toward GPU/Data Center spend due to AI adoption, not a structural weakness; management expects ILM to normalize and pick up from Q3 onward, viewed on an annuity basis.
Hitachi-linked ILM business specifically slowed as budgets shifted to Data Center (private/public); management asks to view this on an annuity, not quarterly, basis.

Top 15 OEMs contributed 74% of gross sales in Q1 FY27 (vs traditional benchmark of top 15-20 OEMs contributing 75-80%, i.e. roughly an 80/20 ratio), with 12 of the top 15 OEMs showing growth in the quarter.

subsections.label: Annuity business dynamics
points: Annuity-led business grew 14% YoY (alternately cited as 13.7%) and constitutes 46.4% of gross sales (INR297 crore absolute), up from 43.1% in Q1 FY26; the ~3 percentage point increase attributed to upsell within existing customers and price uptick, not a hit to net-new revenue.
Annuity/renewal duration varies by customer type: 3 years for enterprise customers, 5-7 years for Government and BFSI, 9 years for Defense and similar.
First year of a contract is considered net-new; subsequent years considered renewal/annuity; a tech refresh after contract expiry is again counted as net-new.
On a TCV basis, ~60% of a 5-year deal's value is typically realized as ACV in year one, with ~10% per annum in each of the remaining four years (illustrative, varies by solution and order).
Overall annuity/renewal rate sustained around 45%, though this can move up/down depending on strength of net-new business growth.

subsections.label: Hardware vs software mix
points: Hardware/software split is a derived outcome of customer solution requirements, not a planned or tracked metric; hardware share can rise or fall quarter to quarter depending on deal mix, and the 28% hardware gross sales decline in Q1 FY27 reflects this dynamic rather than a standalone trend.
Hardware prices have risen over 40% in certain portions of the portfolio, while hardware remains about 30% of overall business.

subsections.label: OEM ecosystem and platform consolidation
points: Company has 100+ (alternately cited as 67) OEM relationships and delivers ~32-33 solution stacks through its Centre of Excellence (COE).

OEM platform consolidation (OEMs acquiring or being acquired, bundling services into platforms) viewed as an opportunity rather than a threat, as iValue's multi-stack, multi-OEM curation capability remains relevant even as OEMs integrate acquired companies into unified platforms.
Company has not seen revenue loss from OEM M&A activity to date; in some cases gains access to newly acquired OEM products to sell.

subsections.label: New geography entries
points: Company began generating revenues in Vietnam, Philippines, and Middle East in Q1 FY27; while amounts are still small, being able to attract customers in the first quarter of operations in these geographies is viewed as a noteworthy achievement.
Geographic expansion remains an area of focus for the year.
Domestic (India) contributed 87% of gross sales in Q1 FY27, with international at 13%.

subsections.label: Distribution/channel model
points: Business model works exclusively with system integrators; direct business is an exception rather than the norm.

System integrators take purchase orders and quotes from end customers; iValue is not contractually bound to be their exclusive annuity provider but positions itself as 'first among equals' via first-sale support work, aiding annuity renewal wins.

subsections.label: Data center capex opportunity
points: Multiple large players (Airtel NEYSA, Sify, Reliance-Meta 168MW data center) are building out data center capacity in India; management sees this as widening the addressable market (TAM), but notes many variables remain before infrastructure is ready to translate into concrete revenue numbers.
India data center power demand estimated at 9-11 megawatts over the next 2 years; current India data center capacity is about 1.5 gigawatts, with potential future capacity of 7-9 gigawatts.

Public data centers: majority of large public/hyperscaler data center contracts go directly to OEMs, limiting iValue's direct opportunity share in that segment; iValue does get some opportunities but this is a relatively smaller play.

Private (captive) data centers — for institutions, government, or private groups — represent the larger and greater opportunity for iValue, as these deals are less likely to be captured entirely by OEMs directly.
Company sees benefit accruing more once data center infrastructure is actually built and operational, rather than during the build-out phase itself.

subsections.label: Competitive positioning amid OEM platform consolidation
points: When an OEM partners with only one or two other OEMs for a joint go-to-market motion, they address only a smaller portion of the ecosystem; iValue differentiates by bringing the full multi-OEM stack (currently ~67-100+ OEMs) to the customer, which management argues supports rather than erodes its margins.

Value-added differentiation, not the underlying technology segment, determines pricing power/margins — DCI is not inherently more profitable than other segments; margins depend on the degree of solutioning value iValue delivers in a given deal.

subsections.label: Sales/GTM organization
points: Organization structured around three external stakeholder groups — end customer, system integrator, and OEM — each with dedicated leadership: a Chief Business Officer for OEM relationships, and a Chief Revenue Officer overseeing customer/partner relationships (including separate teams for tier-1 vs tier-2/3 customers).

A horizontal pre-sales function and the Centre of Excellence (COE) support solutioning and demonstration needs across all verticals; this operating model has been in place and refined over roughly 18 years.

subsections.label: Leadership transition
points: CEO (referred to as Shrikant) has stepped down for personal reasons after successfully delivering on his responsibilities; management thanked him for his contributions.

Going forward, Sunil Pillai (Chairman & MD) will continue to lead India operations, while Krishna Raj Sharma (KRS, Executive Director, seven years as CEO tenure previously) will oversee international operations; both will jointly oversee overall responsibility previously held by the CEO.

Sunil Pillai stated he is personally spending more time in the business than in past years; both he and KRS have prior hands-on experience managing these functions before the tenure of a professional CEO.
New leadership appointments: Umashankar Krishnamoorthy as Chief Business Officer, Sameer Kanse as Chief Revenue Officer, and Mitish Chitnavis as Chief Technology Officer.

Management clarified there is no broader restructuring; the senior team (Sunil, KRS, Sriram) has been together for ~18 years, and the outgoing CEO Shrikant was a long-time industry friend (more than 10 years relationship) who stepped in on a personal basis to run the India business while KRS focused on IPO execution and overseas expansion; Shrikant is now exiting the country to join family overseas.

subsections.label: Shareholder base evolution
points: Following the exit of anchor investor Creador (which fully monetized its investment), several new marquee institutional investors and long-term funds have joined the shareholder base.
Kabir Thakur (associated with Creador) continues on the board as a Non-Executive Director, ensuring continuity of strategic guidance and governance.

subsections.label: Inorganic growth
points: Management confirmed inorganic growth opportunities are being actively evaluated; any opportunity offering good business synergy will be explored, with updates to be shared with investors if there is material progress.

KRS's increased focus on international operations was in the context of overseeing overseas expansion and having previously led the IPO process, not explicitly confirmed as a precursor to a specific inorganic deal.

subsections.label: Contract structure illustration
points: TCV contract terms range from 3 to 9 years depending on customer type; illustrative example of a 5-year TCV deal valued at $500, with $300 realized in year one and the remaining $200 spread across years 2-5 at roughly $50 per year in annuity value.

subsections.label: Supply chain / delivery delays
points: Supply chain impact has persisted for almost a year and has become cyclical; some OEMs in the market face delivery delays of 7-8 months, though iValue's represented OEMs face a comparatively shorter ~1.5 month delay.

subsections.label: Budget reallocation risk
points: Customer budgets are being reallocated quarter-to-quarter toward GPU/Data Center/AI infrastructure, temporarily softening segments like ILM/ALM; management frames this as a timing/reallocation issue rather than genuine demand loss.

subsections.label: Currency/FX
points: INR depreciation against USD affected margins in Q1 FY26 and continued in Q1 FY27, though the company was able to take better cover/pricing action this year to protect margins despite similar depreciation.

subsections.label: Hardware pricing pressure
points: Hardware prices have risen in certain portions of the portfolio; large enterprise customers with frozen budgets push back on OEMs and software vendors for discounts to stay within budget, which management says has not resulted in volume degrowth in Q1.

subsections.label: OEM/vendor consolidation risk
points: Ongoing OEM consolidation (existing OEMs acquiring or being acquired) creates a risk of account/revenue share shifts, though management states no negative revenue impact has been observed from this trend to date.

subsections.label: Leadership transition
points: Departure of CEO and other senior personnel (framed by an analyst as three top executives leaving citing personal reasons) raised as a potential restructuring risk; management maintains there is no broader restructuring underway.

subsections.label: Full-year growth commitment
points: Management remains confident of achieving FY27 growth guidance of 20% growth in both gross sales and PAT, consistent with prior guidance.
Bottom-line growth is expected to continue outpacing top-line growth, as has been the historical pattern.

H2 is expected to contribute meaningfully higher than H1 in both revenue and profitability, driven by enterprise budget cycles and deal closures towards year-end, consistent with the company's 'natural rhythm.'

Company reiterated confidence based on pipeline (INR 6,150 crore) and steady 30-35% win rates to support the 20% growth commitment despite quarter-to-quarter segment variability across the five business pillars.
Annuity business expected to sustain a 45-46% share of gross sales going forward.

subsections.label: Segment-level outlook
points: ILM/ALM demand expected to normalize and pick up again from Q3 onward as budget reallocation toward AI/data center normalizes.

DCI (Arista-led) expected to remain a bullish growth area given continued AI/GPU infrastructure investment, with DCI expected to contribute 18-20% of full-year revenue and Cybersecurity to sustain 45-50% of top line on an annualized basis.
Company expects similar large marquee deals to recur this year as in prior years, though timing/quarter of occurrence can vary.

key_takeaways: We are pleased to begin FY27 with a decent performance, which reflects the strength of our business model, diversified technology portfolio and disciplined execution.
During the quarter, we delivered gross sales of INR 641 crores, a growth of approx 6% on year-on-year basis, and a PAT of INR approx 16 crores, a growth of 52% on year-on-year basis.

Growth during the quarter was driven by cybersecurity, DCI, ALM, and cloud. Cybersecurity continues to remain our core engine, contributing 44% to our top line, while DCI continues to be a key growth accelerator, supported by rising AI-led infrastructure demand.

Our annuity-led business continues to scale steadily, growing at 14% year-on-year during the quarter. Our pipeline currently stands at INR 6,150 crores, up 6% over the last quarter, reflecting strong demand across segments.
With win rates holding steady at 30% to 35%, we remain confident of meeting our growth commitment for the year.
We would also like to inform you that our CEO has decided to step down due to personal reasons after having successfully delivered on the responsibilities and strategic priorities entrusted to him.
As mentioned on the last earnings call, we remain confident of achieving our growth guidance of 20% growth both in our gross sales and PAT.

Following the exit of Creador, our long-term anchor investor, several marquee institutional investors and long-term funds have joined our shareholding, reflecting confidence in iValue's business model, market positioning, and long-term growth prospects.
pressing_questions: Bhavin Shah: We've had our gross sale growth of 5.7% for the quarter. Hardware prices have actually gone up by over 40%, and which I think, is 30% of our overall business. So effectively, are we seeing negative growth on a like-to-like basis? On top of that if we have a 46% coming from annuity business, does it mean that the net new sales are a serious challenge for us? And I'm finding it difficult to contrast against the 20% normal growth guidance that we've been talking about.

Hitesh Goel: Can you just explain cybersecurity and ILM sales growth this quarter? Because in cybersecurity, whatever we are hearing from your competitors and our channel checks, the growth is quite superior for other players. And also, in ILM management, why is there a 60% decline on a Y-o-Y basis? Is there some deferment of demand or something?

Vibhav Khandelwal: If we notice in the last couple of months, some of our OEMs have been acquired by larger companies like Palo Alto, Cisco, and IBM. So, going forward, do we expect to retain these accounts, or is there some risk that would lead to some account share loss because of this?
Shlok Akolia: Over the past few months, nearly three of our topmost executives have left the company, citing personal reasons. So, is there any major restructuring going on?

Bhavin Shah: In one of the quarter calls, you had mentioned about excess revenue booking in the first quarter of FY26. Could you quantify that number? Because otherwise, the negative number looks fairly high, which may not be the case.

quarters.summary: iValue delivered strong FY26 growth (gross sales up 19.5%, PAT up ~20%) broad-based across all four technology segments, with strong FY27 outlook driven by a qualified opportunity book of INR 5,800 crore, cybersecurity/AI tailwinds, DCI/AI data center demand, and a Google Cloud order book exceeding INR 300 crore; management expects FY27 to outperform FY26 in both revenue growth and profitability, while maintaining an 18-20% top-line and 20-22% PAT growth trajectory and evaluating capital allocation options including inorganic growth or shareholder returns (dividend/buyback).

subsections.label: Operating Leverage
points: Over the last one-two years, the organization made necessary investments in manpower, office space and other relevant aspects for the next two to three years.
Because of these prior investments, more than 85% of incremental gross margin (vs last year) flowed down into EBITDA this year.
Management believes this operating leverage will sustain, with at least more than 70% of incremental gross margin expected to flow to incremental EBITDA over the next two to three years.

subsections.label: New Labour Code Impact
points: A one-time cost of around INR 5.7 crore was reported as of Q3'26 due to incremental cost pertaining to gratuity and leave encashment on account of the new Labour Code.
Salaries were restructured, resulting in a saving of INR 50 lakh, bringing the total one-time cost down to around INR 5.2 crore.
PAT of INR 102.3 crore is stated before this exceptional hit.

subsections.label: Working Capital Improvement
points: Receivables grew slower (17.5%) than top line (20%), while payables grew faster (33%) than top line — attributed to favorable payment terms negotiated in certain large deals and good collections.
Inventory declined significantly from INR 12 crore to INR 6 crore, reflecting robustness of the operating model.
Net working capital days improved to 30 days; management does not expect this to be achievable every year but targets sub-40 days going forward.

subsections.label: Cash Position & Return Ratios
points: Cash flow from operations of INR 108 crore — first time in iValue's history that operating cash flow exceeded PAT.
Best-in-class return ratios recorded: adjusted ROCE (adjusted for net cash) of ~40.5% and ROE of ~18%.
Adjusted ROCE calculation: net worth reduced by net cash of INR 212 crore, then used for ROCE computation.

subsections.label: Contingent Liabilities
points: Contingent liabilities related to pending disputes with customs and GST authorities declined from INR 10.7 crore (FY25) to INR 6.3 crore, as some cases received favorable judgments with none having an adverse impact.

subsections.label: Gross Margin Drivers
points: Gross margins are negotiated on a deal-to-deal basis (both with customers and vendors/OEMs) rather than being determined by sheer price increases or volumes, given the multi-OEM solutioning model.

Q1 FY26 saw a margin dip (6.8% vs overall average 9.1%) due to a spillover of deals structured in Q4FY25 into Q1FY26, where the company had to absorb dollar forex changes and component cost changes to support the system integrator and customer.

Q4 margins are historically higher than other quarters due to back-end/volume rebates from OEMs achieved on hitting certain numbers, and because Q4 is when most customer budgets close, giving better negotiating leverage (including with Indian OEMs wanting to close their year strong).
Business is cyclical with H2 stronger than H1, and margins stronger in H2 than H1.
YoY gross margin declined 90 bps in FY26 primarily due to the Q1 hiccup.

subsections.label: Long-term Receivables
points: A specific deal from two years ago had receivables spread across multiple years; company received payment for first two years, third year not yet received but now within 12 months so it will move from long-term to short-term receivables.

subsections.label: Gross Debt
points: Gross debt is cyclical — Q1 typically sees higher debt because Q4 large deals' vendor payments and obligations come due in Q1.
On a full-year basis, gross debt is expected to remain around the INR 40-60 crore benchmark.

subsections.label: Opportunity Book Clarification
points: The INR 5,800 crore figure represents qualified leads/opportunities captured in CRM, not an order book; these could span deal durations of three, five or more years.
The company does not know upfront whether a customer will commit to 2, 3 or 5 years until deal closure.

Conversion rate uplifted to 30-35% (from ~25% previously) due to two trends: customers making decisions faster (potentially due to certain market events), and the company's COE being able to showcase integrated solutions more effectively, improving turnaround time versus 4-5 years ago.

subsections.label: Q4 Large Deals
points: A little more than a couple of large deals were cracked in Q4, similar to the previously disclosed GSTN deal; execution and billing are ongoing but account names are being withheld as other listed companies may wish to disclose these names themselves.

subsections.label: Large Enterprise Deal Visibility
points: BFSI vertical is seen enhancing requirements with growth/spike expected.
Cybersecurity will continue to dominate, followed by DCI and then cloud business, sequentially dominating FY27 growth.
Average deal size for marquee deals varies from account to account; management declined to give a ballpark figure.

key_figures.label: ALM, cloud and others YoY growth
ALM, cloud and others QoQ growth
Other verticals (healthcare, automobile, pharma, etc.) combined share

subsections.label: Segment Growth Overview
points: All four technology segments (Cybersecurity, DCI, ILM, ALM/Cloud/others) recorded growth during FY26; cybersecurity grew fastest and is the largest/core engine at 50% of gross sales.
DCI is described as a key growth accelerator with strong Q4 growth.
ILM degrew both sequentially (-70% QoQ) and YoY (-20%) in Q4.

subsections.label: Cloud (Google Cloud) Business
points: Google Cloud (GCP) business built an order book exceeding INR 300 crore in FY26, providing multi-year revenue visibility expected to translate into sustained revenue over the next three to five years.

Billing is based on customer workload usage/metering — GCP meters usage, bills the customer, and iValue subsequently bills the customer; actual revenue could exceed the INR 300 crore commitment based on workload growth.
This model is unique to Google among OEMs; other OEM businesses largely follow a capex model, with the annuity/renewal (subscription/renewal) business comprising about 40-45% of total turnover.

Cloud engagement creates deeper customer interaction, integration, high stickiness, recurring consumption-led billing, and long-term managed services opportunity, making it a highly annuity-driven, high margin-visibility business viewed as a stable, scalable revenue engine over coming years.

subsections.label: OEM Portfolio
points: Six new OEMs added over the last one year (details in investor presentation).
Total OEM portfolio of 115 OEMs, with more than 50 from cybersecurity.

Company has the largest wallet share among typical distributors with top 15-20 OEMs it works with, due to value-added solutioning; does not get 100% wallet share as every large OEM in India works with 3-4 distributors.

subsections.label: Vertical Mix
points: BFSI is the largest vertical at ~40% of gross sales.
Government contributes sub-20%.
ITES and Telecom together contribute ~20%.
Other verticals (healthcare, automobile, pharma, etc.) together contribute ~20%.

subsections.label: Hardware/ASP Impact
points: Hardware is customized per customer order and placed with the OEM only after customer order, so no spike from hardware price inflation was seen in Q4 despite ~30-35% hardware mix; management notes the trend may not continue and expects a possible spike going forward.

subsections.label: AI Strategy
points: Cybersecurity growth is increasingly centered around AI, with AI security seen as paramount for enterprises.
Company is working on use cases around LLM security, AI governance, AI risk management, and integration of AI into SIEM, SOAR, observability, and threat intelligence platforms.
AI and next-generation digital infrastructure is viewed as one of the most transformative technology shifts globally; despite some hype, management sees it as a significant long-term opportunity.

Over recent quarters, the company has strengthened capability across AI-led infrastructure, GPU computing, cybersecurity, cloud, data management, and high-performance digital platforms to align with evolving enterprise and government requirements.
An AI strategy slide has been added to the investor presentation.

subsections.label: Geographic Expansion
points: Over the last three-four years, the company has steadily expanded presence across the SAARC region.
Building on this momentum, the company is now evaluating opportunities to enter select ASEAN markets.

Strategy will be measured and paced, initiating operations on a controlled scale to assess market viability, customer adoption, and long-term sustainability before committing significant investment for accelerated growth and expansion.

Middle East is seen as an opportunity area (driven by cybersecurity/AI demand amid geopolitical situations), but the company has 'hibernated' plans there for now due to the current situation, with intent to explore once conditions improve.

subsections.label: Component/Supply Availability
points: Cybersecurity (50% of turnover) is viewed as more of a necessity for customers, so the company continues to foresee ability to supply customers on a timely basis despite reported memory/chip shortages.

In the DCI space, there could potentially be a slowdown from component availability, but OEMs, the market, and customers have adapted/planned well for such delays, and management currently foresees no gaps unless something catastrophic occurs outside its control.

subsections.label: Forex Hedging
points: Company hedges dollar-to-rupee exposure as an 18-year ongoing practice with high discipline.
Quotes sent to market are short-duration (one week, two-three days), which helps control/mitigate potential forex changes during the quote validity period.

subsections.label: Value-Added Solutioning Model
points: Company does not just trade in products but sells solutions via multi-OEM integration; negotiates prices with both customers and vendors on every deal.

Example: cybersecurity enterprise customers need best-in-class products from multiple OEMs; iValue identifies right OEM combinations, understands underlying IT architecture, showcases solutions via COE (touch-and-feel), and after customer approval, the system integrator places the order with iValue, which procures from multiple OEMs and provides pre-sales, post-sale, and implementation support.
Ideal end customers are at the high end of the pyramid — large enterprise customers plus high end of mid-market; mid-enterprise defined roughly as ~5,000 users.

subsections.label: Competitive Positioning
points: Key differentiators: ability to operate beyond traditional technology partner boundaries with multi-OEM integrated solution capabilities, deep engagement across system integrators and enterprise customers, robust COE-led pre-sales/solutioning framework, and domain-led expertise across BFSI, healthcare, manufacturing and other verticals — positioning as a strategic technology transformation partner.

Global peers/comparators cited: Exclusive Networks (was listed at DRHP filing but went private before iValue's IPO, so no longer comparable) and Infinigate (large player in European/Middle East markets).

TD SYNNEX and Arrow offer more value additions in mature markets like the US/Europe than in India, given different business models and smaller proportion of business in India relative to their scale (e.g., $100 billion overall business with a much smaller India proportion).
No listed Indian competitor named; among private players, business models differ enough that straightforward comparison isn't possible.

Win rate/leverage is higher where iValue adds significant value addition (solutioning, BOQ/BOM development, negotiation); in scenarios with little value addition, it competes on a level playing field with typical distributors.

Better distribution economics than peers like Redington attributed to 18 years of BFSI/government/defense/enterprise vertical practice engagement, solutioning approach (not off-the-shelf), and network/solution architecting work with OEMs and system integrators.

subsections.label: Risk Underwriting
points: Financial risks taken on: must pay OEMs regardless of collection from customers; currency risk since OEMs are paid in dollars; inventory risk if end customer/system integrator cancels or modifies an order after it is placed with the OEM; and other contract-related risks.

Business risks: company does not sign SLAs (these are generally done by system integrators); job is limited to delivery and successful post-sale implementation once the solution is agreed among all parties.

subsections.label: Capital Allocation & Shareholder Returns
points: Board continues to evaluate avenues for long-term value creation, including strategic inorganic opportunities as well as shareholder returns initiatives such as dividends or share buybacks.

If the company does not pursue a suitable inorganic growth opportunity, the board may consider enhancing shareholder returns, subject to sustained business performance, cash flow visibility, capital allocation priorities, and requisite approvals.
If no successful inorganic deal materializes this year, the company will come out with a dividend/buyback policy and determine execution timing during this year or early next year.

subsections.label: M&A Criteria
points: Business synergy is of paramount importance; focus areas for potential targets include cybersecurity, cloud business, DCI business, and geography expansion (ASEAN).
Unlikely to find a target fitting all criteria, but targets fitting most aspects with clear management and business synergy will be considered.

subsections.label: Supply Chain / Component Risk
points: Reported shortages for memory and chips could pose supply chain disruption risk, particularly in the DCI space; cybersecurity is seen as more resilient given it's viewed as a necessity.
OEMs, market and customers have adapted planning to these delays, reducing perceived risk, barring catastrophic events outside company control.

subsections.label: Currency/Forex Risk
points: Rupee depreciation could influence top line and EBITDA; managed via 18-year hedging practice and short-duration quotes (1 week to 2-3 days) to limit forex exposure window.

subsections.label: Q1 FY26 Margin Pressure
points: Deals structured in Q4 of the prior year spilled into Q1 FY26; forex changes and component cost changes required the company to support the system integrator and customer, causing a margin dip in Q1 (though no loss was incurred).

subsections.label: Geopolitical Risk (Middle East)
points: Middle East expansion plans have been paused ('hibernated') due to current war-related situations in the region, despite seeing traction/opportunity there.

subsections.label: FY27 Outlook
points: Management remains highly optimistic about FY27 and expects it to outperform FY26 in both revenue growth and profitability.
Confidence stems from a strong executable pipeline, growing annuity-led revenues, accelerating AI and digital infrastructure opportunities, and operating leverage benefits.
Continued focus on profitable growth, healthy cash flow generation, disciplined execution, and building a scalable technology-led business with long-term shareholder value creation.
Overall FY27 focus: profitable growth, better balance sheet discipline, and ensuring sustained operating leverage; FY27 growth expected to be faster than FY26 in both top line and profitability.
Acceleration in FY27 growth is stated to be on both an underlying basis and not merely FX-related.

key_takeaways: Financial year 2026 has been a year of strong and consistent execution for iValue, where we delivered gross sales of INR 2,913.9 crore, a growth of 19.5% on year-on-year basis, and a PAT of INR 102.2 crore, a growth of 20% on year-on-year basis.
The growth during the year has been broad-based across all four technology segments. In fact, all our four segments have recorded growth during the year.

Cybersecurity continues to remain our core engine with 50% contribution to our gross sales, which has also grown the fastest in this year. While DCI continues to be a key growth accelerator and happy to report 29% growth for Q4FY26.
Our qualified opportunity book has reached up to INR 5,800 crores with conversion rates in the range of 30% to 35%.

During financial year 2026, we successfully built an order book exceeding INR 300 crore [Google Cloud], which provides strong multi-year revenue visibility and is expected to translate into sustained revenues over the next three to five years.
Looking ahead, we remain highly optimistic about FY 2027 and expect it to outperform FY 2026 both in terms of revenue growth and profitability.
This is the first time in iValue's history where we are able to showcase a cash flow from operations higher than our PAT.
We were able to record best-in-class return ratios of adjusted ROCE, adjusted for net cash, of around 40.5% for the full year and ROE of around 18%.

JNPR.about: Incorporated in 2011, Juniper Green Energy Limited is one of India's leading renewable energy independent power producers (IPPs), engaged in developing, building, operating, and maintaining utility-scale renewable energy projects.[1]

quarters.summary: Juniper Green Energy delivered its first quarterly results as a listed company with record revenue, EBITDA and quarterly commissioning; management remains on track to commission 2 GW for FY27, targeting 4.5 GWh of BESS by June 2027 and 10 GWh by March 2028, with run-rate EBITDA guidance of ~INR 2,700-2,750 crore for the ~4 GW FY27 exit portfolio and ~INR 4,500 crore for the ~6 GW FY28 exit portfolio.

subsections.label: Record Quarter Highlights
points: First set of results presented as a listed company
Delivered highest ever quarterly revenue and EBITDA and highest ever renewable capacity commissioned in a single quarter
IPO raised INR 1,800 crore primary, strengthening balance sheet post-IPO (net worth increased from INR 3,463 crore to INR 5,200 crore)

subsections.label: Refinancing & Debt

Weighted average cost of debt for operational portfolio now around 8.5%
One-time refinancing cost of INR 18 crore impacted PAT in the quarter; PAT would have been higher (adjusted for tax) without this one-off

subsections.label: Depreciation Policy Change
points: Depreciation policy has been aligned to market practice as followed by other companies, based on an assessment/estimate done by the company

subsections.label: Capex Plan

This is expected to increase to around INR 22,000 crore by March '27, including capacity of around 3,900 MW being commissioned by March '27 and CWIP for capacity coming in subsequent quarters

subsections.label: Peak Power / FDRE Traction
points: Strong traction for peak power because many states are struggling with peak demand gaps
Many FDRE PPAs and bid-out BESS capacity have not materialized industry-wide, giving Juniper an edge given it has delivered on FDRE commitments
Won SECI thermal mimic tender (870 MW/2,200 MWh, 230 MW contracted, tariff INR 5.26) – LOA already received
Won 50 MW GUVNL wind project at INR 3.51/unit

subsections.label: LOA to PPA Conversion Outlook
points: 550 MW of FDRE capacity remaining for LOA-to-PPA conversion
350 MW in advanced discussions with confirmed buyer interest from procurers
150 MW hybrid project also in advanced discussion
Thermal mimic (1 GW peak + 2.2 GWh) expected to convert fast given attractive tariff relative to thermal tariffs
Combined expected conversion: >2 GW peak plus ~4 GWh BESS in the next few months

subsections.label: SECI Demand Aggregation Policy Change
points: Government has asked SECI to conduct bids only after aggregating demand from DISCOMs, which management believes could improve LOA-to-PPA conversion by reducing 'DISCOM shopping' behavior seen in earlier tenders where different tariffs were discovered due to multiple entities bidding
May reduce total number of tenders happening versus multiple entities tendering independently, but should improve conversion quality

subsections.label: Thermal Mimic Tender Design
points: Tender designed to replicate a thermal plant's round-the-clock output profile through solar, wind and storage combined
Tariff meaningfully below thermal power cost
Tender covers a wider geographic scope than earlier state-specific load-following tenders and requires 12-hour peak power provision

Expected overall CUF of ~75% for the project, comparable to typical thermal plant CUF of 70-80%, which removes prior transmission-charge waiver ambiguity issues that arose from lower renewable CUF (~30%)
CUF requirement was reduced to below 60% during daytime per last-minute tender changes, aligning with thermal plant expectations

Earlier load-following tenders (state-specific, tariff ~INR 5.50) did not gain traction due to narrower scope and lack of all-night peak power provision; battery prices at that time were not favorable for managing 24-hour profiles

subsections.label: Operational Performance
points: Highest ever quarterly renewable capacity commissioned in a single quarter
Commissioned India's first FDRE project under the SJVN FDRE tender during the quarter — a first for the country and proof point for the company's growth model
BESS assets performing well with round-trip efficiency of approximately 91% and state of health of around 99.6%, reflecting quality of BESS operations capability

subsections.label: Portfolio Quality
points: 98% of contracted capacity is with off-takers rated A and above
98% of portfolio secured through long-term PPAs typically running for 25 years
Days receivable outstanding at 19 days as on June 30, among the lowest in the sector, reflecting strength of off-takers

subsections.label: Run-rate EBITDA Trend
points: Run-rate EBITDA for the 2,575 MW commissioned as on date stands at INR 1,620 crore, up from INR 1,050 crore for the capacity commissioned as of March '26, reflecting improving unit economics as more capacity comes online

subsections.label: Curtailment Management
points: Curtailment largely restricted to TGNA (temporary grid connectivity) capacity — a 50 MW merchant plant in Bikaner with an existing 100 MWh battery that mitigated curtailment
This battery will double to 200 MWh within a month to fully eliminate curtailment on this capacity
Some FDRE capacity on TGNA also experiences curtailment, currently offset by an existing 400 MWh battery with further addition expected by October
Overall curtailment impact estimated at 2% to 2.5%, unrelated to CUF performance which came in at 30.2% for the fleet

subsections.label: BESS Economics
points: BESS revenue is not tracked as a standalone line item as batteries are bundled into FDRE/hybrid/thermal-mimic contracts under a common tariff, making it difficult to isolate BESS-specific revenue
Returns on newer FDRE/hybrid tenders are in the higher teens on an overall basis; early FDRE tenders had significantly higher returns as an early mover
Standalone BESS (pure merchant/transmission-element) not being pursued meaningfully currently due to lower returns; opportunistic merchant BESS will be pursued
Of the 4.5 GWh being installed by June '27, 1.5 GW/GWh is not linked to any specific project and will run as merchant for the next 1-2 years
An additional ~700 MWh is expected to be added by December 2026 (in stages) on top of the current ~500 MWh, and this will also run merchant, with some later moving into a PPA by June

Margins on merchant BESS this year improved: daytime charging tariffs have fallen from ~INR 2.50 (previously) to INR 1-1.30; sale side average was ~INR 8 for full year '25 but this year includes sales on HPDAM market (cap up to INR 20), expected to push full-year sale numbers higher, though weather will play a role

subsections.label: BESS Sourcing Strategy
points: Company has adopted a fully integrated BESS solution approach (container + PCS + EMS from a single entity), differing from the more fragmented Indian industry approach where container, PCS and EMS integration are sourced separately
This mirrors how BESS procurement happens globally (e.g., in the West)

Limited players offer this fully integrated solution in India: Envision (which owns AESC, a leading cell manufacturer), Sungrow (world's largest integrator); Fluence has exited the market; company is also in talks with CATL and others

Full 4.5 GWh contracted to date is entirely from Envision (AESC cells, Envision containers, PCS, and EMS integration done via Envision-owned company 'Universe', a large renewable data analytics company)
LTSA with supplier covers both warranties and O&M for 15-20 years depending on battery life/cycle type
Flexible throughput warranty: double-cycle (C/2) batteries get 15-year life; single-cycle (C/4) batteries get 20-year life

subsections.label: Battery Pricing Trend & Technology Evolution
points: Container prices for ~2-2.5 GWh of batteries closed around January 2026 were $59-60/kWh; prices later rose to $68-70/kWh (lithium carbonate driven) before cooling to $65-68/kWh currently
All-in price (BOS + tax + duty) around $100/kWh for the lower-priced batch and ~$110/kWh for a batch closed a couple months back at ~$68 container price

Technology evolution: initial FDRE model (2023) used wind+solar overbuild due to battery prices >$300/kWh; as prices fell to $150-160/kWh, wind capacity was halved, solar kept steady, and battery capacity increased to 1.5x contracted capacity with C/2 (double-charge) batteries; as prices fell further to ~$100/kWh, wind was reduced to a small capacity, solar increased, and battery capacity doubled with a C/4 (single-charge, discharging 4 hours at night plus 2+2 peak hours) design offering buyer flexibility on discharge timing

At current battery prices (~$100-108/kWh), solar+battery matches or beats solar+wind+battery returns, making solar+battery preferable operationally since it's easier to execute without losing returns; wind is added in current tenders (like thermal mimic) primarily to accentuate returns rather than as a technical necessity

subsections.label: Module Pricing
points: Non-DCR module prices closed at INR 12.1-12.2 per watt peak, driven down by a supply glut in both China and India
Company's current capacity (apart from the thermal mimic tender) does not require DCR modules and it is not currently buying DCR
DCR module price assumed for thermal mimic tender is around INR 17 per watt peak

subsections.label: Grid & Connectivity Risk Assessment

Balance ~1 GW is largely on CTU but substations are mostly already operational
One substation with ~300 MW of capacity is operational but the overall system under completion should be done by December — no major risk to 2 GW target seen from grid slippage
Connectivity, land and financing for the pipeline are largely tied up and execution is progressing well across sites

subsections.label: TGNA Strategy

Evacuation infrastructure for FDRE projects largely built by company itself; civil work, boundary work and piling proceed ahead of structure and module installation which is deferred until GNA is ready
Under TGNA, batteries or a limited renewable-to-battery-absorption capacity will be commissioned first

subsections.label: Execution Capability

Over 14,000 acres of land banked for under-construction and awarded pipeline
More than 200 identified wind turbine installation locations

subsections.label: IPO Milestone

IPO strengthened balance sheet, taking net worth from INR 3,463 crore (pre-IPO, as on 30 June) to INR 5,200 crore post-IPO

subsections.label: Corporate Structure
points: Company maintains a simple, straightforward holding-company structure with individual projects executed through separate SPVs, a typical structure for infrastructure businesses
Each SPV is used to sign PPAs and secure project financing in a ring-fenced environment; whenever the company wins a tender for connectivity and PPA, it is done through a separate SPV structure
No explicit plan discussed to consolidate or rationalize subsidiaries beyond this standard SPV-based approach

subsections.label: Grid/Transmission Risk
points: Risk of delays in transmission (CTU-level) potentially affecting the 2 GW FY27 capacity addition plan; management believes this risk is manageable since most substations are already operational or near completion by December
TGNA (temporary connectivity) capacity is exposed to curtailment; mitigated via battery deployment

subsections.label: Curtailment
points: Curtailment of 2-2.5% currently experienced, restricted to TGNA capacity (50 MW Bikaner plant and some FDRE capacity on TGNA); expected to be fully eliminated with additional battery installations

subsections.label: Battery/Commodity Price Volatility
points: Lithium carbonate price movements have driven battery container prices up (from $59-60 to $68-70/kWh) before cooling to $65-68/kWh, indicating exposure to raw material price volatility

subsections.label: Tender/Policy Uncertainty
points: Earlier load-following tenders faced tariff and structural issues (state-specific scope, no all-night peak power) which limited execution; new demand-aggregation policy by government for SECI tenders could reduce number of tenders even as it improves conversion
