key_takeaways: On behalf of the team, I would want to start by thanking our shareholders and new investors for the trust you have placed in us. Our IPO, through which we raised, INR 1,800 crores, was a significant milestone

This has been a milestone quarter for us. The first set of results we are presenting to you as a listed company. We have delivered our highest ever quarterly revenue and EBITDA and the highest ever renewable capacity that we have commissioned in a single quarter
Fleet-wide CUF for Q1 FY27 came in at 30.2%, up from 28.2% in the same quarter last year. Generation has grown by 72% to 944 million units
We commissioned 601 megawatt peak in the quarter alone. 458 megawatt peak of solar and 143 megawatts of wind, our highest ever quarterly commissioning
During this quarter, we commissioned India's first FDRE project under the SJVN FDRE tender, a genuine first for the country and a proof point for the model we have built our growth around

Total income for Q1 FY27 grew to INR 324 crores, which is 79% year-on-year increase from the last year number of INR 181 crores. Our EBITDA also grew 86% year-on-year to INR 294 crores versus INR 159 crores last year, and this takes to our EBITDA margin to 91%, an improvement of roughly 300 basis points year-on-year
Our total, our total PPA portfolio is roughly 6 gigawatts peak, right? And our LOA portfolio is roughly around 5 gigawatts peak now

Put together, as on date, our total portfolio now stands at close to 11,200 megawatts of capacity plus nearly 9 gigawatt-hours of BESS. With FDRE and wind-solar hybrid projects making up 84% of our portfolio and a blended weighted average tariff of INR 3.7
pressing_questions: Do you see any risk on account of delays in transmission coming in which can hurt your plan for 2,000 megawatts?
As a strategy, while substation may be ready, the whole grid may not be ready. Would you be open to setting it up under the TGNA route or would you like to wait for full GNA?
Can you also talk about your experience of any curtailment during the quarter and how much it would have impacted your revenue?

Following the IPO, does management intend to rationalize or say consolidate the current 56 subsidiaries? And then what is the roadmap for simplifying the corporate structure as more SPVs become operational?

With BESS becoming a much larger part of the portfolio, could you help us understand the economics of these BESS projects, particularly the expected returns or margins, the revenue model, and whether you see BESS becoming a meaningful contributor to your EBITDA over the next 2-3 years?
What is the kind of capacity that we expect to operate on a merchant basis for FY27 and FY28?

Regarding the Thermal Mimic project, how should one think about operational challenges there, and would there be some surplus power generation which you'll need to sell to grid or something that you'll need to buy from the grid?

EVEREADY.about: Incorporated in 1934, Eveready Industries India Limited is one of the leading manufacturers of dry cell batteries in India and offers products such as batteries, flashlights, lighting solutions, and home appliances. [1]

quarters.summary: Eveready expects to sustain profitable growth momentum despite commodity and forex headwinds, with alkaline market share targeted at 25-30% exit share in 2 years, Jammu plant expected to stabilize with a 10% gross margin uplift on alkaline SKUs after a year, potential further pricing actions on zinc inflation, near-term debt-free status expected in 4-5 quarters, and long-term strategic/M&A plans to be firmed up in 2-3 quarters.

key_figures.label: Consecutive quarters of YoY revenue growth
Balance amount expected from Noida Plot B2 sale (prior quarter reference)

subsections.label: Margin protection
points: Calibrated pricing actions and continued focus on operational efficiencies enabled the company to protect margins and maintain profitability despite commodity/forex inflation.
No one-offs in Q1 results — margins were purely a function of operational efficiencies and calibrated price actions taken in response to zinc price increases.
Employee cost was almost flat (2-3% increase) YoY because last year Q1 had a full-fledged Noida plant, which has since been disposed of, offsetting normal HR optimization costs.

subsections.label: Balance sheet / debt
points: Debt proceedings currently hover around INR165 crores; against this, INR200+ crores has been invested in the Jammu plant which is yet to yield results, effectively making net borrowing negative from that lens.
Company expects to become like-to-like debt free in the next 4-5 quarters.
Company is paying down debt ahead of schedule; no need for additional fund infusion at present, though this could be reconsidered as part of long-term strategy.

subsections.label: Jammu incentive / GST subsidy
points: No formal GST approval yet for the Jammu NCSS incentive scheme; discussions with the state industries department are at an advanced stage.

Under the NCSS scheme (introduced by government in 2021), the company is eligible for a 3x refund of eligible plant & machinery investment in the form of GST paid in the state over a period of 10 years.

subsections.label: Noida asset sale
points: Noida sale is not yet fully completed — of 2 plots, one has been executed and the second is expected to close shortly.
The Noida plant rationalization was undertaken to reduce fixed costs, without delay, as part of manufacturing footprint rationalization.

subsections.label: Capitalization of Jammu pre-operative expenses
points: All pre-operative expenses for the Jammu plant till the date of capitalization (29th May) have been capitalized as per accounting standards and added to assets.
Post-29th May, expenses are being charged to the P&L.

subsections.label: Tax / one-time items
points: Whole-time director consulting/remuneration of INR2 crores approved by NRC and Board in recognition of strategic contribution and decision-making guidance; management confirmed this arrangement is ongoing.

subsections.label: CCI matter
points: Next CCI hearing scheduled for the last week of September; management stated it cannot currently estimate the potential financial impact.

key_figures.label: Overall Indian dry-cell market share (combined zinc+alkaline)
Alkaline share of company's total portfolio

subsections.label: Battery business
points: Segment delivered strong quarter, recording 11.9% revenue growth, supported by healthy performance across both alkaline and carbon zinc batteries.
Alkaline portfolio continued to be the key growth driver, delivering close to 48% volume growth.
Market share expanded to 18% within alkaline sector, reflecting results of premiumization strategy.

Carbon zinc battery business delivered stable performance, with volume growth commensurate to industry; calibrated pricing actions and scale efficiencies protected profitability while reducing manufacturing costs across legacy portfolio.
Strong growth witnessed across digital channels — Q-commerce, quick commerce and e-commerce — reflecting changing consumer buying preferences and strength of omnichannel distribution strategy.
Alkaline market share has grown from about 3% to about 18% over the last 30 months, driven by brand and consumer acceptance even while the product was imported.

subsections.label: Flashlight business
points: Overall demand remained soft due to delayed onset of monsoon, which deferred seasonal demand and resulted in lower volumes of conventional battery-operated flashlights.

Rechargeable flashlight portfolio remained a key growth driver, supported by continued product innovation, premium product offerings and increasing consumer adoption of rechargeable solutions, offsetting structural slowdown in traditional battery-operated segment.

Company is actively working to expand flashlight usage beyond traditional rural/seasonal applications by developing products for urban consumers and newer everyday use cases, broadening addressable market.

subsections.label: Lighting business
points: Business benefited from strong demand across key product categories; pricing environment showed signs of stabilization after a prolonged period of price erosion (value erosion softened after about 18-20 months), improving revenue visibility and supporting margin resilience.
Healthy volume growth witnessed in higher-margin categories — particularly emergency LED bulbs and electrical accessories.
Electrical accessories portfolio gaining momentum, led by encouraging performance of insulation tapes and introduction of wires and MCBs.
Lighting segment broke even in Q1 FY27; management expects this to broadly hold through the year.
Cost push was extremely high in Q1 despite value-erosion softening; growth trajectory expected in Q2/Q3, though extent of growth and cost softening needs to be watched.
Emergency bulbs and lighting accessories expected to grow; wires expected to grow; regular GLS bulb growth uncertain.

Lighting strategy focuses on hero products (e.g., emergency bulbs with batteries, synergistic with battery heritage), regional focus (5-6 states account for >3/4 of business), and leveraging dual distribution channels (general trade/FMCG-style plus growing electrical channel) that many competing lighting companies lack.

subsections.label: Wires and MCBs / adjacent electrical categories
points: Initial start made about 6 months back; company aims to double the business in current financial year and target 1-2% market share, though this remains preliminary.
Wires are sourced, not manufactured in-house; sourcing capacity currently supports 2x-3x growth headroom.

subsections.label: Market share dynamics / mix shift
points: A few years back zinc accounted for >95% of the dry-cell mix and alkaline ~5%; today alkaline accounts for slightly above 15% of the mix and zinc continues to dominate at 85%.
Company's zinc portfolio share (58%) has remained mostly flattish; growth has come from alkaline where the company had single-digit shares 3 years ago versus 18% today.

Panasonic and Nippo are close followers in the zinc segment (Nippo slightly ahead of Panasonic); Duracell is a key competitor holding the larger pie within alkaline; Nippo and Panasonic have single-digit shares within alkaline.

subsections.label: New product launches
points: Introduced hybrid flashlight — Eveready's first patent-applied flashlight product — combining convenience of rechargeable technology with reliability of conventional batteries.

Launched India's first portable liquid mosquito vaporizer, an innovative mosquito repellent with rechargeable battery-powered portable design enabling consumers to carry the vaporizer while traveling or indoors; this is Eveready's first patent-applied innovation in the anti-mosquito liquid vaporizer category, launched across select markets.

Launched a rechargeable flashlight (SHOR) with an animal alarm feature for farm protection, designed to help farmers protect crops from animal intrusion through a 100-decibel alarm combined with a red UV strobe light.
Launched Xtrabright emergency LED bulb within the emergency portfolio, offering double the illumination of a standard emergency bulb during power cuts.
Company continues to reinforce leadership as market leader in the organized mosquito racket category.
Innovation remains central to Eveready's long-term growth strategy.

subsections.label: Jammu facility commercialization
points: Commercial production commenced at Jammu facility on 29th May 2026 — an important milestone during the quarter.

Plant strengthens manufacturing capacity, improves operating leverage, and supports expansion of the alkaline battery business, providing scale, flexibility and supply chain resilience for the next phase of growth.
Jammu is currently the only alkaline manufacturing facility in India, giving it particular significance for both domestic demand and export/white-label opportunities.

Plant renewable energy: since only 2 months into production, a grid connection has been taken along with solar panels installed; company committed to maximizing solar/renewable power at its plants and prefers an asset-light leasing/rental model given rapidly changing capital costs of assets.

Jammu facility costs (raw material, manufacturing cost, overheads) are now an integral part of battery cost of goods sold rather than a separately trackable finished-goods import cost, and will flow through cost of goods sold as units are sold.

subsections.label: Noida plant disposal
points: Noida plant closed last year as part of manufacturing footprint rationalization; sale of 2 plots — one executed, second expected to close shortly — undertaken to reduce fixed costs without delay.

subsections.label: Channel strategy
points: Strong growth witnessed across digital channels — Q-commerce, quick commerce and e-commerce — during the quarter, reflecting changing consumer buying preferences and strength of omnichannel distribution.
Lighting business is regionally concentrated: 5-6 states account for more than 3/4 of the lighting business, pushed through electrical and general trade channels; modern trade is an emerging channel.
Jammu plant opens new opportunities in white labelling and export markets, positioning the company to scout for battery white-label opportunities across other countries seeking to source from Asia.

subsections.label: Renewable energy / sourcing
points: All large plants, including Jammu, are equipped with maximum possible solar power; company prefers asset-light leasing/rental models given rapidly changing capital costs.
Wires business is fully sourced rather than manufactured in-house, unlike some competitors who manufacture their own wires.

subsections.label: Competitive dynamics
points: News report of a Japanese competitor potentially closing plants in India was noted as speculative by management; management indicated any vacated market space would typically be occupied by other brands automatically.
Amazon Basic launching battery SKUs was raised by an analyst as a competitive question; management did not provide a specific quantified response beyond general market share commentary.
Panasonic and Nippo are close followers in zinc (Nippo slightly ahead); Duracell holds a larger pie within alkaline; Nippo and Panasonic hold single-digit shares in alkaline.

subsections.label: Cannibalization view
points: Management does not believe alkaline growth is cannibalizing carbon zinc sales in the near term; growth is being driven by consumers trading up to higher-power devices (smart remotes, toys, blood pressure machines, optical mice, etc.) that consume more power than earlier simple devices, rather than by like-for-like substitution.

Cannibalistic dynamics are more likely to emerge only once high-drain device demand saturates and alkaline crosses roughly 20% saliency of the overall battery market; this has occurred in other markets like Europe and the US but management expects limited impact over the next 1-1.5 years.

subsections.label: Market share growth outlook and market sizing
points: Alkaline market share of 18% is expected to continue on similar momentum, with exit share targeted between 25% and 30% over the next 2 years as the Jammu plant stabilizes and operational efficiencies improve.
The battery market by value is expected to keep growing as premium batteries make further inroads into consumer households, driven by increasing device penetration and multiple devices per household.

subsections.label: Long-term strategic plan / M&A
points: Management requested another 1-2 quarters before providing a long-term (3-year) EBITDA/turnover CAGR forecast, citing the need for a calculated, planned approach with parallel execution given recent strong quarters.

Company is internally deliberating whether to pursue M&A or focus on building/investing in its existing core business as part of long-term horizon vision; decision to be incorporated into long-term firm plan to be shared in 2-3 quarters.
No current need for extra fund infusion given strong performance and ahead-of-schedule debt repayment, though fund infusion could be considered in due course as part of long-term strategy.

subsections.label: Asset rationalization
points: Noida plant sale (2 plots) undertaken as part of manufacturing footprint rationalization to reduce fixed costs; one plot executed, second expected to close shortly; no immediate plans for further asset rationalization beyond current initiatives, but company will update if opportunities arise.

key_figures.label: Employee cost increase excl. Noida effect

subsections.label: Macro / commodity headwinds
points: Global businesses continue to navigate persistent geopolitical uncertainty, supply chain disruptions and inflationary pressures; commodity markets remain volatile with currency fluctuations adding further uncertainty to input costs.

Zinc prices continued to remain elevated versus prior-year levels; several other key raw materials — electrolytic manganese dioxide, electrodes, acetylene black, and lighting products/components — also witnessed inflationary trends.

Company monitors zinc prices on a weekly basis; if margins come under significant pressure, another round of price/margin corrections may be necessary, though frequent short-interval price hikes are not ideal.
Commodity prices and currency movements remain key watch areas going forward.

subsections.label: Flashlight seasonal demand risk
points: Delayed onset of monsoon deferred seasonal demand and resulted in lower volumes of conventional battery-operated flashlights, contributing to a 6.7% revenue decline in the flashlight segment.

subsections.label: Regulatory / compliance risks
points: BIS norms for flashlights were fully implemented on paper as of last year; adoption/absorption among non-branded organizations in India is yet to be seen and will need continued compliance drive; company's flashlights are fully BIS compliant and all production facilities produce only BIS-compliant flashlights. Rigorous implementation may take another 2-3 quarters.

Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) compliance has operational and pricing-mechanism challenges; company is working with the Ministry of Environment and Climate Change and the Pollution Control Board to resolve these; no absolute cost figure available yet pending regulatory/pricing clarity, expected to be clarified in the next quarter update.

CCI matter has a hearing scheduled for the last week of September; management cannot currently estimate the potential financial impact (analyst referenced a possible INR150 crore cash outgo scenario, not confirmed by management).

subsections.label: Competitive risk
points: Speculative news of a Japanese competitor potentially closing India plants; Amazon Basic entering battery SKUs — management notes these as general competitive dynamics without specific quantified impact.

subsections.label: Outlook themes
points: Management remains optimistic about sustaining growth momentum through the remainder of the year; premiumization strategy continues to gain traction, investments in manufacturing and innovation are beginning to yield results, and distribution network continues to expand across traditional and emerging channels.
Commodity prices and currency movements remain key watch areas; company remains committed to timely actions to protect profitability while delivering sustainable long-term value creation.
Long-term (3-year) EBITDA/turnover CAGR guidance and M&A strategy to be shared in 2-3 quarters once plans are finalized.

guidance_ledger.statement: In a very sustainable capacity utilization, we are looking for at least 10% gross margin increment from our Jammu plant once fully stabilized after a year.
We should be looking at an exit share of 25% to 30% at the end of 2 years from now.
We see shortly in the next maybe 4 to 5 quarters, the company should be having a positive and should be a like-to-like debt free.
Requested about 2 to 3 quarters' time before giving long-term (3-year) EBITDA or turnover CAGR forecast, given the need for a very calculated, planned way with parallel execution.

Whether to go on any acquisition or focus on building/investment on existing core is being internally deliberated; long-term firm plan will be incorporated when management comes up in the next 2-3 quarters.
Trying to double from where we were at the close of last financial year in wires/MCBs, potentially clocking 1% to 2% market share.
In quarter 1 we broke even in lighting; let's watch for it throughout the year, my sense is mostly it should hold.
There is seemingly a move towards growth in quarter 2 and quarter 3; emergency bulbs, lighting accessories and wires should grow, though regular GLS bulb may not.
Should zinc prices remain overwhelming and margins come under inflection, another round of price or margin corrections will not be surprising.
No current need for extra fund infusion given strong performance; may be considered in due course as part of long-term strategy.
Awaiting pricing and regulatory clarity on EPR; will be able to give better clarity on the next quarter update.
Second Noida plot sale is expected to close shortly.
Next CCI hearing is around the last week of September; management will provide an update after the hearing.
Given 11.5% margin delivered in FY26 despite headwinds, sense is we should be able to hold around the same region in FY27, though times are turbulent.
Anticipating at least 30% utilization level to end the year.
We expect production of more than 100 million units in the first year of operations.
From a breakeven point of view, between 5 to 6 years should be an ideal breakeven point for this plant going forward (payback perspective).
At full annualization basis, year 1 onwards at the operating level, we will be at breakeven.
We continue the journey of further debt reduction in FY27; our aspiration is to keep reducing debt.
Anywhere between 20% to 25% towards alkaline and 75% carbon zinc will be how the category repositions itself.

guidance_ledger.statement: Alkaline segment would easily become 1/3 of the overall battery segment in India over the next 5 to 10 years.
We've been holding on to about 10% A&P and that will go through even in the new financial year.
If the geopolitical situation carries on beyond quarter 1, could see challenges; else sense is it should continue the way it did in last 1-2 quarters.
If cost ambiguity continues over this quarter as well, we may then need to look at pricing again somewhere in quarter 2.
For FY27, we'll be transitioning to the new 22% tax regime under Section 115BAA, subject to utilization of carryforward business loss.

themes.label: Commodity & forex cost pressure

themes.note: Debt at ~INR165 crores; company expects to become like-to-like debt free in 4-5 quarters, paying down debt ahead of schedule.

themes.label: Lighting price stabilization

key_takeaways: Revenue for the quarter stood at INR407.7 crores, registering a growth of 9% year-on-year — marking the seventh consecutive quarter of year-on-year revenue growth.
EBITDA came in at INR61.5 crores while maintaining an EBITDA margin of 15.1%.
Profit after tax stood at INR37 crores, representing a growth of 22.3% over the corresponding quarter last year.

The battery segment delivered another strong quarter, recording 11.9% revenue growth, with the alkaline battery portfolio delivering close to 48% volume growth and market share expanding to 18% within the alkaline sector.

An important milestone during the quarter was the commencement of commercial production at the Jammu facility on the 29th of May, strengthening manufacturing capacity and supporting expansion of the alkaline battery business.
The flashlight segment revenue declined by 6.7% due to delayed onset of monsoon deferring seasonal demand, though the rechargeable flashlight portfolio delivered over 20% revenue growth.
The lighting business delivered an encouraging quarter, registering healthy 13.7% growth, with the pricing environment showing signs of stabilization after a prolonged period of price erosion.

Zinc prices continued to remain elevated at around $3,500 per ton compared to levels of below $3,000 per ton during a major part of last year, alongside inflationary trends in several other key raw materials.
pressing_questions: Can you give us the guidance on what kind of OPM we will be earning from the alkaline sales earlier versus what we can expect to earn at INR100 crores level in first year and at peak capacity level at INR400 crores level?
Are we now in a position to give a 3-year EBITDA or a turnover CAGR forecast?

One of our directors were paid a consulting fee — is a concerned person now a whole-time director in another Burman company and are we still paying him that INR2 crores of consultancy fees, or has that stopped?
As Eveready brand, is there any plan for any M&A now that we have spent so much time on the brand and it's such a strong brand, why are we not exploiting it in a much larger manner?
Any update on the CCI matter and potential INR150 crores cash outgo that can possibly come if it isn't in our favour?
What is our monthly fixed expenses that we are incurring for the Jammu facility that will flow now through the quarterly results?

quarters.summary: Eveready closed FY26 with 8.2% revenue growth and 8.9% EBITDA growth (EBITDA margin 11.5%), led by the battery segment; management expects to hold margins around similar levels in FY27 amid rupee depreciation and elevated zinc/crude costs, with the newly commissioned Jammu alkaline plant, continued premiumization, pricing actions and debt reduction seen as key levers for FY27 and beyond.

Profit booked on Noida land sale
Balance amount expected from Plot B2 transition
Rupee/USD exchange rate range during FY26

subsections.label: Margin & Cost Management
points: EBITDA margin of 11.5% reflected disciplined cost management, improved product mix and pricing interventions despite elevated commodity cost pressures.
Calibrated pricing actions in carbon zinc and alkaline batteries were undertaken to navigate cost headwinds while maintaining margins without disrupting market competitiveness.
Strong cost governance was supported by effective forex hedging and manufacturing footprint efficiencies to mitigate cost headwinds.

Management indicated headwinds for FY27 are stronger than those faced in FY26, but given 11.5% margin delivered last year despite headwinds, sense is margins should be held around the same region going into FY27.
H1 is generally a few percentage points better than H2 in terms of revenue, with festival-related plus/minus variations.

subsections.label: Balance Sheet & Capital Allocation
points: Strengthening the balance sheet remained a key priority through FY26, supported by disciplined working capital management, calibrated procurement, inventory optimization and tight cash flow control.
Debt reduction remains a clear priority; company aspires to continue the debt reduction journey further in FY27.

Company entered into two separate agreements for sale/transfer of leasehold rights for Plot B1 and Plot B2 at its Noida plant; transfer of Plot B1 (including built-up structures and fittings) was formally completed on 30th March.
No additional capex beyond routine capex is anticipated at this point; first preference for proceeds from Plot B2 sale will be debt reduction.
Net debt should come down significantly with proceeds from Plot B2 sale expected in the current year.

subsections.label: Tax Position
points: Group has evaluated the option under Section 115BAA and intends to transition to it once benefits under Section 80-IE are fully utilized; company will transition to the new 22% tax regime for FY27.

Current year write-off of around INR500 crores of old ICD provisions created a business loss, allowing capital gains from the Noida land sale to be set off against business losses, resulting in no tax payable; MAT balances have not yet started being utilized.
After business losses are fully utilized, only 25% of MAT adjustment will be allowed going forward in subsequent years.
FY27 tax provisioning should be modeled at 22%, subject to utilization of carryforward business losses.

key_figures.label: Carbon zinc saliency within battery category (current)
Projected carbon zinc saliency (3 years out)

subsections.label: Battery Business
points: Battery segment growth supported by strong demand across both alkaline and carbon zinc categories.

Alkaline portfolio continued to perform exceptionally well, delivering healthy volume growth; consumer preference for high-performance products, rising usage of power-intensive devices and premiumization trends continue to support the shift.
Lithium batteries were launched earlier in the year, reinforcing alignment with structural demand trends.

Carbon zinc battery prices were increased during the year to partially offset the steep rise in zinc costs; distribution strength and brand trust helped maintain category stability and market position.
Mosquito racquets continued to scale up and now command a leadership position within the segment in urban markets.
Alkaline growth in India is clocking over 20% CAGR in volume terms; over the next 5-10 years, alkaline segment could easily become 1/3 of the overall battery segment in India.

Alkaline is more premium to zinc batteries; some cannibalization of zinc battery volumes expected as alkaline saliency rises, but overall battery category value should improve, fueled by rising penetration of power-intensive devices (blood pressure machines, toys, smart remotes, optical mice, electric toothbrushes).

In India there is currently not a very significant price difference between carbon zinc and alkaline (unlike other countries where the gap is larger), positioning India at a 'sweet spot' to move towards alkaline quickly; premium side of zinc will compete with alkaline while price-sensitive economy/popular segment continues to favor zinc.
Volume drivers will remain to be alkaline, whereas premiumization will potentially happen in both zinc and alkaline segments over the next couple of years.

Flashlight and lighting volume growth may not reflect a clean picture due to varied price points (products ranging from INR50 to INR300), so value premiumization sometimes occurs with lower volume turn.

subsections.label: Flashlight Segment
points: Traditional battery-operated flashlight category remains relatively mature; rechargeable formats continue to gain traction and remain a strategic focus area.
New product launches such as power banks and chargers seeing encouraging initial traction, strengthening the portable energy solutions portfolio.
Recent BIS standard mark mandate for flashlights (implemented by end of January 2026) augurs well for the company as it expects higher traction towards quality-compliant branded offerings.
Pushing hard on flashlights priced INR500 and above, the more premium segment in the flashlight category.

subsections.label: Lighting Business
points: Growth supported by good volume growth across consumer lighting categories.
Pricing remained competitive in the LED segment; focus on higher-value SKUs, portfolio upgradation and disciplined channel execution supported both growth and profitability.
Electrical accessories momentum remains encouraging as company expands presence and increases penetration via general trade channel reach.
Lighting reported good double-digit quarter-on-quarter growth; management believes this is sustainable and ideally should be able to do better.

key_figures.label: BIS standard implementation deadline for flashlights

subsections.label: Jammu Plant Commissioning
points: Jammu manufacturing facility is India's only operating alkaline battery facility; inaugurated by Shri Manoj Sinha, Lieutenant Governor of J&K, on 22nd April 2026.
Represents an important step forward in strengthening manufacturing self-reliance and expanding the premium portfolio; strategic decision taken almost 1.5 years back.
Phased ramp-up planned over the coming years; plant significantly enhances supply resilience as company transitions from fully imported alkaline batteries to domestic production.
Over time, expected to improve cost efficiencies, support margin expansion and strengthen competitiveness in the fast-growing alkaline segment.

In addition to alkaline batteries, the facility will support manufacturing lines for batteries (carbon zinc), flashlights and lighting products, creating stronger backward and forward integration across the portfolio.
Commercial production expected to commence shortly (within a few weeks, in the current quarter, not Q2).
Movement from importing to local alkaline production allows some margin decompression initially; margins expected to continue improving as plant absorbs overheads with rising production.
From breakeven perspective, plant payback estimated at 5-6 years, but operational breakeven (at full annualization, including the carbon zinc plant also set up) expected from year 1 onwards.

Jammu facility capable of producing alkaline batteries, zinc batteries, flashlights and lighting products, all initially for domestic production and sales; futuristically positioned to explore white-labelling of alkaline batteries for international markets given global trade realignment.

Company continuously optimizing its manufacturing facilities; smoothly exited Noida plant while setting up the future-ready Jammu alkaline plant — manufacturing realignment initiated from the November (Q2) Board meeting.

subsections.label: Tax Incentives on Jammu Plant
points: There are GST-linked incentives available in the J&K state, but the Jammu plant has not yet received approval under the incentive scheme.

Government wants to promote J&K as an industrial belt; company chose Jammu for the incentive opportunity as well as favorable cost of operations; company is working closely with Jammu government authorities and industrial department and will update investors on any developments.

key_figures.label: Projected alkaline share of overall battery segment in India

subsections.label: Competitive Positioning
points: Company as category leader is setting the path for the battery category to take price increases and remain sustainable given cost pushes and recent cost ambiguity; if ambiguity continues, further pricing may be considered in Q2.

BIS compliance mandate for flashlights expected to raise the cost of compliance for unorganized/unbranded players who currently simply import products; this could also raise quality question marks for such players.

About 70% of the flashlight market is unbranded and heavily dependent on China; rupee depreciation of ~15% against yuan over last 15 months uniformly impacts all players dependent on Chinese imports, but BIS compliance is the game-changer expected to benefit branded players like Eveready.
Even if only half the unbranded flashlight market becomes BIS compliant, branded players should make much better gains from the unbranded segment.

key_figures.label: Time since decision to set up Jammu plant

subsections.label: Non-core Asset Sale / Manufacturing Realignment
points: Company continuing manufacturing realignment initiated at the November (Q2) Board meeting, including the Noida plant closure/exit.
All company plants remain operational currently; company will update on further realignment plans once finalized.
No further noncore asset sales beyond the Noida land transactions have currently been shortlisted/announced.

subsections.label: Bain Capital route-to-market efficiency program
points: Bain capital-led route-to-market efficiency work concluded roughly 2 years ago.

Company growth trajectory has moved from mid-single digit (flat for a decade) to high single digit, with last 2 quarters showing 9%-10% growth, reflecting the next step of acceleration despite commodity volatility and market turbulence.

subsections.label: Commodity & Currency Risks
points: Commodity volatility, particularly zinc prices, may continue in the near term into FY27.

Rupee has weakened to INR94-95 levels against USD; crude prices above $100+; difficult to predict whether this rupee/crude trend is short-term or long-term; company is closely monitoring developments on both forex and zinc price fronts and will take calibrated pricing action if needed.
Headwinds for FY27 are viewed as stronger than those faced in FY26.

subsections.label: Demand Risk
points: Urban demand revival could be impacted if recent geopolitical sentiment persists beyond Q1, potentially posing challenges to sustained recovery.

key_figures.label: Proposed corporate tax rate under Section 115BAA

subsections.label: FY27 Outlook
points: Company sees FY27 as an important year of optimization with the Jammu plant ramp-up, stronger alkaline penetration, premiumization across batteries and lighting, and continued expansion in adjacencies such as mosquito racquets and power banks.
Broader focus remains sustainable growth, double-digit operating margins, stronger manufacturing integration and disciplined capital allocation.
Company believes FY26 foundations position it strongly for FY27 and the next phase of value creation.
Urban demand revival trend from the last couple of months expected to continue unless recent geopolitical sentiment causes challenges extending beyond Q1.

guidance_ledger.statement: Given 11.5% margin delivered in FY26 despite headwinds, sense is we should be able to hold around the same region in FY27, though times are turbulent.
Anticipating at least 30% utilization level to end the year.
We expect production of more than 100 million units in the first year of operations.
From a breakeven point of view, between 5 to 6 years should be an ideal breakeven point for this plant going forward (payback perspective).
At full annualization basis, year 1 onwards at the operating level, we will be at breakeven.
We continue the journey of further debt reduction in FY27; our aspiration is to keep reducing debt.
We should be looking at exiting with 20% market share (up from current 16%, from less than 10% a year back).
Anywhere between 20% to 25% towards alkaline and 75% carbon zinc will be how the category repositions itself.

guidance_ledger.metric: Alkaline category share of overall battery segment
guidance_ledger.statement: Alkaline segment would easily become 1/3 of the overall battery segment in India over the next 5 to 10 years.
We've been holding on to about 10% A&P and that will go through even in the new financial year.
Lighting's recent double-digit QoQ growth looks to be sustainable; ideally should be able to do better.
If the geopolitical situation carries on beyond quarter 1, could see challenges; else sense is it should continue the way it did in last 1-2 quarters.
If cost ambiguity continues over this quarter as well, we may then need to look at pricing again somewhere in quarter 2.
For FY27, we'll be transitioning to the new 22% tax regime under Section 115BAA, subject to utilization of carryforward business loss.

guidance_ledger.metric: Balance amount from Plot B2 sale
guidance_ledger.statement: Balance around INR90-odd crores money we will definitely get in the current year when the transition gets executed.
We don't anticipate, at this point of time, any additional capex beyond the routine capex.

risk_register.risk: Zinc commodity price volatility
risk_register.note: Zinc prices moved 20% plus/minus during FY26; headwinds seen as stronger heading into FY27.

risk_register.risk: Rupee depreciation / forex volatility
risk_register.note: Rupee has moved from INR83-91+ range in FY26 to INR94-95 currently; difficult to predict if this is short-term or long-term.

risk_register.risk: Crude oil price increase
risk_register.note: Crude prices hovering above $100+, impacting cost as crude is a widely-used input across products.

risk_register.risk: Urban demand uncertainty / geopolitical sentiment
risk_register.note: Recent geopolitical sentiment could impact urban demand revival if it persists beyond Q1 FY27.

risk_register.risk: Cannibalization of carbon zinc by alkaline
risk_register.note: As alkaline saliency rises, some cannibalistic impact on carbon zinc volumes is expected, though overall category value should improve.

risk_register.risk: Unbranded/unorganized competition in flashlights
risk_register.note: About 70% of flashlight market is unbranded and China-dependent; BIS compliance mandate expected to raise compliance costs for unorganized players, benefiting branded players like Eveready.

risk_register.note: GST-linked incentive scheme exists in J&K but Jammu plant has not yet received approval under the incentive scheme.

themes.label: Alkaline premiumization
themes.note: Alkaline share of battery business rising (16% share, targeting 20% exit, ~10% of battery business), driven by premiumization and power-intensive device penetration.

themes.label: Jammu plant ramp-up
themes.note: India's only alkaline plant commissioned, INR200cr investment, 360mn unit peak capacity, expected to enhance margins and self-reliance over FY27 and beyond.

themes.label: Commodity & forex cost pressure
themes.note: Elevated zinc costs, rupee depreciation to INR94-95, and crude above $100 create margin headwinds into FY27.

themes.label: Debt reduction / balance sheet strengthening
themes.note: Debt reduced by more than INR100 crores in FY26 with further reduction targeted in FY27, aided by Noida land sale proceeds.

themes.label: BIS compliance tailwind in flashlights
themes.note: Mandatory BIS standard for flashlights expected to raise costs for unbranded/unorganized players, favoring branded players like Eveready.

themes.label: Urban demand recovery
themes.note: Urban consumption showed momentum in value-led/everyday categories but discretionary spending remained selective and could be impacted by geopolitical sentiment.

themes.label: Manufacturing realignment / non-core asset monetization
themes.note: Noida plant exit and Plot B1/B2 leasehold sales (INR251 crores total) fund growth while realigning manufacturing footprint around Jammu.

key_takeaways: FY '26 closed with a gradually improving demand environment supported by steady rural consumption and signs of recovery in urban demand.

For FY '26, we delivered a revenue growth of 8.2%, along with EBITDA growth of 8.9%. On a full-year basis, EBITDA margin stood at 11.5% reflecting disciplined cost management, improved product mix and pricing interventions despite elevated commodity cost pressures.
The battery segment delivered growth of 9.3% in FY '26, supported by strong demand across both alkaline and carbon zinc categories.
A major highlight during the quarter was the commissioning of our Jammu manufacturing facility, India's only operating alkaline battery facility.

With an investment of approximately INR200 crores, the facility has a peak capacity of up to 360 million alkaline batteries annually with a phased ramp-up planned over the coming years. We expect production of more than 100 million units in the first year of operations.
Debt reduction remains a clear priority, having reduced debt by more than INR100 crores in the current fiscal year.
During the quarter, the company entered into 2 separate agreements for the sale and transfer of its leasehold rights in respect of Plot B1 and Plot B2 located at its Noida plant.

As we move into FY '27, we remain optimistic. While commodity volatility, particularly zinc prices, may continue in the near term, the pricing actions already undertaken combined with improving internal efficiencies, provide confidence in our operating outlook.
Our broader focus remains clear: sustainable growth, double-digit operating margins, stronger manufacturing integration and disciplined capital allocation.

So is the understanding correct that going forward, this amount payable to that director will now stop?
Do we have any tax incentive on this J&K plant? And if yes, what are the -- can you give a little colour?

TRITURBINE.about: Triveni Turbine Ltd is primarily engaged in business of manufacture and supply of power generating equipment and solutions. [1] It was a division of Triveni Engineering & Industries Ltd[2] since 1970s and was demerged w.e.f from Oct 2010 into a separate entity.[3]

quarters.summary: Q1 FY27 was a challenging quarter with revenue up 19.2% YoY but EBITDA margin down sharply to 18% from 25.8% and PBT margin down to 15.7% from 23.5%, driven by a softer order mix from H1 FY26 flowing through execution, delivery phasing of strategic (near-zero margin) orders like NTPC CO2 storage, and export dispatch deferrals due to 3-4x higher freight rates. Management remains confident of top-line and bottom-line growth for full-year FY27, though it will be back-ended into H2, with order booking, export share, and aftermarket momentum all improving even as the domestic enquiry book showed weakness during the quarter.

key_figures.label: Historical EBITDA margin range referenced by analyst
NTPC CO2 energy storage order balance to be executed (as of Q4 FY26)

subsections.label: Margin drivers
points: Execution in this quarter reflects the business environment and order intake of roughly a year ago; softer order mix of H1 FY26 has carried through to Q1 FY27 profitability.
Delivery phasing of certain strategic orders has also added to the softening of margins.
A strategic NTPC CO2-based energy storage project was taken at negligible/near-zero margin to validate technology and prove a use case; it does not contribute to profitability.
Higher percentage of domestic execution as part of the revenue mix is depressing on margins; the main pull-down on margin is the increased share of domestic (non-export) orders in the revenue mix.

Export orders were deferred by clients because freight rates rose 3x-4x and vessel availability declined, pushing execution/revenue recognition from Q1 to Q2/Q3; this is borne by clients as contracts are FOB.

Orders were taken at a point in time of commodity price volatility, and margins (especially domestic) were already low at that time; execution is in line with expected margins, so this is not a surprise.
Fixed-price/rate contracts mean price escalations must generally be absorbed at the time of contract; company builds in contingency to de-risk commodity cost volatility.
Bought-out item percentage varies order-to-order (30% to 70%) and scope customer-to-customer; no standard/fixed percentage; mix also changes quarter-on-quarter based on delivery readiness.
Company reiterated long-term belief that PBT margin over 20% is maintainable in medium and long term.
Rupee movement noted as beneficial to margins going forward; comprehensive income vs net income comparison cited as an indicator of future margin direction.

Geopolitical uncertainty has increased volatility in both dispatch and order booking, turning what was previously half-yearly lumpiness into quarterly/monthly lumpiness; management expects this lumpiness to continue for a couple more quarters, cutting both ways (positive and negative).

subsections.label: Balance sheet
points: Balance sheet improved in the quarter versus Q4 FY26: reduction in receivables, reversion to negative working capital, and an increase in cash balance.

subsections.label: Order booking mix shift
points: Growth in order booking was led entirely by exports and aftermarket.

Export order booking growth reflects continued traction and momentum across Southeast Asia, Africa, and Europe, and across segments such as biomass, waste-to-energy, in addition to conventional segments.
Domestic and product order booking witnessed a slowdown during the quarter.

Higher share of exports and aftermarket orders reflects continued strengthening of business mix, improving order book quality and shifting portfolio towards better margin offerings, expected to support profitability as those orders are executed.

subsections.label: Closing order book quality
points: Overall order book improvement attributed to international expansion strategy coupled with continued innovation and entry into new product segments.
Aftermarket closing order growth driven by contract wins in geothermal and utility segments, and continued traction in refurbishment and performance optimisation solutions.

Positions company to capitalise on opportunities across geothermal, process industries, utility-scale refurbishment, and renewable thermal solutions amid growing global emphasis on energy efficiency, decarbonisation, renewable energy adoption and decentralised power generation.

subsections.label: Enquiry trends
points: Enquiry generation in the international market has improved while domestic market has seen weakness; company reports enquiries on a fixed six-month/full-year basis rather than quarterly, since market does not move quickly.
International markets showing strength: United States and Southeast Asia; some green shoots in Europe.
North Africa and Middle East markets are quite depressed; SAARC region remains depressed.
Indian market enquiry has seen a broad-based decline across all industries, though direct customer conversations suggest the market is flat rather than declining.

Enquiry finalisation gestation period is typically 6-12 months; orders finalised this quarter stem from enquiries received 6-12 months earlier; softening seen in current-quarter enquiry generation will affect order finalisation a few quarters later, but enquiry finalisation numbers are well compared to last year.
Domestic order finalisations have experienced longer gestation periods, with customers not concluding orders as quickly as earlier quarters; management expects a bounce back.
Decline in enquiry book does not necessarily reflect lost demand at a level of concern, since the enquiry book is several times larger than annual domestic demand.

subsections.label: Volatility management
points: Only way to overcome volatility from geopolitical disruptions is via a large enough order book to smooth out customer delays and other disruptions.
Expanding product range to cater to varied demand structures is intended to help build the order book for greater resilience.

subsections.label: Aftermarket business
points: Aftermarket business reliant on two streams: own installed base (spares and service growth) and refurbishment (larger market based on installed base of rotating equipment).

Strong growth seen on refurbishment side and exports; local capabilities investment (e.g., gas turbine utility businesses) takes time to build but offers long-term, good margin visibility for coming years.
Aftermarket order translation seen across sectors and regions (Southeast Asia, Africa - notable jump in African market; some traction in India on refurb side).
Sector-wise aftermarket wins seen in gas turbine, geothermal, biomass, and old utility turbines; company moving into utility segment (higher value addition) from industrial segment.
Customers increasingly asking for gas turbine maintenance, repair and overhauling support, adding to refurb business; refurb business also covers small compressors in addition to steam turbines.

subsections.label: API turbine business
points: Traction seen in API business from thermal power plants coming up in India and oil & gas opportunities, though decision-making in oil & gas is getting deferred due to geopolitical tensions.
Company now looking at oil & gas opportunities beyond Middle East into Americas and European countries; secured API business orders from Europe this quarter.

subsections.label: US aftermarket (SAPC-driven)
points: US aftermarket order contribution has been less than 10% of the ₹6 billion figure referenced by an analyst for last two quarters' aftermarket wins, given limited US installed base presence historically.

Growth anticipated from aftermarket and new product demand in US market, though it will take time due to US federal/state-level certification and licensing requirements for repair and maintenance work.

key_figures.label: Enquiry conversion timeline in U.S. market

subsections.label: R&D and new product lines
points: Continued heavy investment in R&D to develop newer product ranges/lines to expand offering for customers to utilise heat or waste heat requirements, for either process requirements or power generation.

Development of Organic Rankine Cycle (ORC) technology continuing, with intent to expand in the coming year; ORC enquiry pipeline increasing, targeting a largely under-addressed market globally including Americas, for power generation from low heat.
Company working on combining ORC with geothermal as an integrated, more efficient and cost-effective solution rather than a single product; on track with positive results expected in near future.

Heat pump not viewed as a standalone product; being combined with Mechanical Vapor Recompression (MVR) to offer a total solution for customers with low-pressure, low-quantity steam requirements, which can replace small packaged boiler opportunities.

A demo unit for heat pump has been created; some MVR orders are under execution as initial orders; adoption is taking time as it is new technology and customers want experience of efficiency/ROI before wider adoption.
Company describes itself as a single-product company adding multiple products to build a solution orientation for customers, without taking on EPC responsibilities/liabilities.

CO2-based energy storage (NTPC project, technology partner Energy Dome) is a first-of-its-kind technology validation project; pilot plant in Europe running and giving positive results; site execution at faster pace, expected to reach commissioning phase by end of Q2/early Q3.

Round-trip efficiency and life-cycle cost of the CO2 BESS technology were competitive enough for the company to commit; European plant performance is appreciated by the customer, but Indian replication still needs to be proven.

Company has a strong relationship with its technical partner (implied Energy Dome) on CO2 BESS; nature of relationship/exclusivity not disclosed publicly, but company is committed to jointly approaching the market.
Validation timeline and post-validation demand generation for CO2 BESS considered premature to determine; described as a first-of-its-kind project.

Company has manufacturing capability to build up to ~250 MW sub-critical packages if a policy such as one referenced for NTPC's smaller packages arises; qualified under relevant guidelines up to that range, though participation decision pending.
COO's role repositioned this quarter to 'business transformation' focused on AI-specific initiatives, reinforcing focus on agility, productivity, customer delight, and product relevance.

subsections.label: US market — data centres and SMR
points: Huge demand seen for data centres in the US, historically powered by gas turbines; gas turbine delivery lead times have extended to 3-5 years, prompting customers to look at combined cycle, conventional route, and small modular reactors (SMR) as alternatives.
50% of utility gas turbines come up in combined cycle format; other 50% in simple cycle due to water availability or other constraints.

US enquiry conversion timeline is typically more than 12 months; traction seen this quarter and next; product order booking expected to precede refurbishment order booking in the US, as refurb requires ongoing qualification/registration.
Company is qualified by consultants, OEs and EPCs in the combined-cycle space in the US; competition exists but few manufacturers; local workshop presence builds customer confidence.

Small modular reactor (SMR) opportunities are at enquiry stage with EPCs/developers; described as first-of-its-kind, longer gestation than combined-cycle data centre applications, as configuration (movable module concept in the US) is still being finalised.

subsections.label: US facility utilisation
points: Utilisation of the US facility depends on order booking; company optimistic on growth in order booking on both aftermarket and product sides.
Product-side execution from the US facility expected only in FY 2028.
For the current year, US facility utilisation will be adequate but not at a high utilisation level; entity is expected to break even.

US subsidiary incurred a substantial loss in Q1 operations, anticipated given the order book did not yet exist; company is targeting breakeven for the US operations this year given increasing market reach and enquiries.

key_figures.label: US aftermarket order contribution vs ₹6 billion reference

subsections.label: Regional demand
points: US subsidiary continued to receive healthy enquiries; market continues to grow in both enquiry book and management optimism for future demand for products and aftermarket services.
Focus in Americas remains on strengthening local service and product capabilities and deepening market presence to build a strong term footprint.
International expansion strategy cited as contributing to overall order book improvement, alongside innovation and entry into new product segments.

subsections.label: Freight and logistics impact
points: Freight rates for exports have risen 3x to 4x, and vessel availability has become less easily available for customers, causing clients to defer/push out dispatches needed from the company.
This delay is largely confined to export orders since domestic market doesn't suffer from the same freight/vessel availability issues.
Contracts are FOB, so freight and logistics costs are borne by clients, not the company.

subsections.label: Competitive positioning
points: Combined-cycle/data-centre space in the US is competitive but has few manufacturers; company only includes enquiries in its enquiry book where it is pre-qualified by customers.
Company competes with the same global players in the US as in rest of world; local presence with workshop gives customers confidence.

Pricing/margin varies by market share position: lower market-share markets are priced differently versus markets with higher market share and greater customer acceptability; margins vary across domestic and export markets and across individual orders.

subsections.label: Volatility and demand structure diversification
points: Company aims to build a large enough, diversified order book (via product range expansion) to smooth out volatility from customer delays and geopolitical disruptions.
Company continues to push global market share as a key driver of achievement over coming years, aided by diversified reach and local presence enabling export exposure relative to its size.

key_figures.label: Export orders deferred due to logistics cost and freight rates
key_figures.value: deferred by one to two quarters

subsections.label: Geopolitical and logistics risk
points: Geopolitical uncertainties have brought volatility in both dispatch and order booking this quarter.
Freight rates up 3-4x and reduced vessel availability have delayed export execution/dispatch by clients, pushing revenue recognition to later quarters.
Volatility that used to be smoothed on a half-yearly basis is now appearing on a quarterly/monthly basis; expected to continue for a couple more quarters, cutting both ways.
Oil & gas API decision-making being deferred due to ongoing geopolitical tensions despite underlying opportunity.

subsections.label: Domestic demand softness
points: Domestic enquiry generation showed a dip this quarter; broad-based decline across industries in the Indian market.
Domestic order finalisation gestation periods have lengthened, with customers waiting and watching rather than concluding orders.

subsections.label: Regional market weakness
points: North Africa, Middle East, and SAARC regions remain depressed markets for enquiries.

subsections.label: US market structural constraints
points: US market's federal structure requires individual state-level certification and licensing for repair/maintenance work, a time-consuming process limiting near-term aftermarket order booking contribution.
US subsidiary incurred a substantial loss in Q1 as anticipated due to lack of an existing order book.

subsections.label: Margin risk from strategic/technology-validation orders
points: NTPC CO2 energy storage project taken at negligible/near-zero margin for technology validation purposes, not contributing to bottom line in initial years.

subsections.label: Full-year outlook
points: Company remains optimistic on growth of both profit and revenue for full-year FY 2027, which will be back-ended.
Majority of NTPC-related revenue delivery expected to be taken care of within the first half of the year; project due for commissioning in Q2, with certain revenue recognized in Q2 as well.
Company confident of top-line and bottom-line growth for FY27; extent of growth expected to be on the higher end versus a double-digit range suggested by an analyst, though no specific number given.
Company optimistic on growth in margins, both in absolute and percentage terms, in the second half of the year.
On PBT margin, company reiterated belief that over 20% is maintainable in the medium and long term (no new specific number given for near-term quarters).
US operations targeted to be breakeven this year, with product-side execution and higher utilisation expected only from FY 2028.
Growth in order booking is expected in both aftermarket and product segments, contingent on book-and-build of spares in the coming months.
Domestic market expected to show signs of recovery in coming months, per management's optimism despite internally observed weakness.
Data centre/combined-cycle enquiry-to-order conversion in the US is hoped to materialise this year (per CMO commentary).

guidance_ledger.statement: We remain optimistic on growths of both profit as well as revenue for the full-year FY 2027, which will of course be backended... as we look at the full-year FY 2027, we are confident to exhibit top line and bottom line growth.
The company is optimistic on the growth, both in margins and absolute and on a percentage basis in the second half of this year.
As a company, we believe that a PBT margin of over 20% is something that we can maintain in the medium and long-term.
We had alluded at the end of Q4 that we still had about ₹175 crores of the order to get executed. It could be split, maybe 40% in Q1, Q2, and then the rest in Q3.
We are quite confident of growth in this year... the extent of growth should be on the higher end of what you are suggesting [double-digit].
We look at the entity breaking even for sure... We are also targeting to make this year as a break-even for U.S.
The product will only get executed possibly in FY 2028... utilisation of the facility will be adequate [this year] but will obviously not be at a high utilisation level.
We are optimistic that the domestic market will show some signs of recovery in the coming months as well.

guidance_ledger.metric: US data centre/combined cycle order conversion
guidance_ledger.statement: We are hoping it could translate in this year. We are hopeful.
We continue to invest heavily into research and development... this includes the development of our Organic Rankine Cycle developments, and we are keen to expand this in the coming year.

guidance_ledger.metric: CO2 BESS technology validation and commercialisation timeline
guidance_ledger.statement: When we can actually establish validation of technology is something that is a little premature for us to determine, both on timelines... But we are optimistic that this presents a market.

guidance_ledger.metric: API share of order booking/revenue (prior guidance)
guidance_ledger.statement: Prior guidance: revert to having a meaningful 10% plus number in order booking and revenue (not reiterated with new specifics this quarter, but API traction discussed).

guidance_ledger.metric: Closing order book growth (indicative minimum for FY27)
guidance_ledger.statement: Prior guidance of ~9% enquiry/order book growth as minimum anticipated; this quarter closing order book grew 5.1% YoY.
Prior guidance that exports would be more than domestic this year; this quarter domestic share rose (export share 48.8% vs 49.3% prior year), reflecting stronger domestic contribution this quarter.
Prior guidance of comfort with 25%+ EBITDA margins; this quarter margin fell to 18%, with recovery expected in H2.
Prior guidance that Geothermal, ORC and CO2 markets will be large markets for the company in the next 2-4 years; reiterated through continued R&D and enquiry pipeline growth commentary this quarter.
Prior guidance that MVR/heat pump market will remain small as a contribution but increasingly allow penetration into the customer; reiterated this quarter with commentary on slow initial adoption.

guidance_ledger.metric: Order intake sustainable level per quarter (₹500-700 crore)
guidance_ledger.statement: Prior guidance on aspiring to higher order intake levels (₹500-700 crores per quarter); this quarter order booking was ₹568 crores.
Prior guidance to invest significantly more into AI; this quarter COO role repositioned to business transformation focused on AI-specific initiatives, with updates to be provided in coming quarters.
FY27 will also be somewhat of a back-ended year; receivable at end of March 31, 2027 may be in a similar level just because of the execution profile of our order book.
We believe that this current year should be positive, if not at worst breakeven. ... when we get into FY '28 onwards that we'll be able to deliver profitability from the U.S. operations.

guidance_ledger.metric: API share of order booking and revenue
guidance_ledger.statement: We believe in the coming quarters and years, it will revert to having a meaningful 10% plus number in our order booking as well as in revenue.

risk_register.risk: Freight rate increases (3-4x) and reduced vessel availability delaying export dispatches/revenue recognition
risk_register.note: Customers have pushed out dispatches, shifting execution from Q1 to Q2/Q3; impacts largely confined to export orders since domestic doesn't face same issue.

risk_register.risk: Geopolitical uncertainty causing volatility in dispatch and order booking
risk_register.note: Volatility that used to smooth out over half-year periods now appears quarterly/monthly; expected to continue for a couple more quarters.

risk_register.risk: Domestic enquiry/order slowdown
risk_register.note: Domestic order booking down 35.4% YoY and product order booking down 11.6% YoY; broad-based decline in enquiry generation across industries, though enquiry book remains several times annual demand.

risk_register.risk: Near-zero margin on NTPC CO2 storage technology-validation order
risk_register.note: Order taken knowingly at negligible margin to validate first-of-its-kind CO2 energy storage technology; will not contribute to bottom line in initial years.

risk_register.risk: Depressed regional markets (North Africa, Middle East, SAARC)
risk_register.note: Markets in North Africa, Middle East are quite depressed; SAARC region remains depressed.

risk_register.risk: US market regulatory/certification complexity
risk_register.note: US federal structure requires individual state-level certification/licensing for repair and maintenance work, a time-consuming process limiting near-term aftermarket contribution.

risk_register.risk: US subsidiary losses due to lack of order book
risk_register.note: Substantial loss incurred in Q1 in US subsidiary operations, as anticipated, because the order book did not yet exist; targeting breakeven this year.

risk_register.risk: Deferred decision-making in oil & gas / API opportunities
risk_register.note: Ongoing geopolitical tensions are delaying decision-making despite underlying opportunity potential in oil & gas and thermal power plant segments.

risk_register.risk: Commodity price volatility embedded in fixed-price contracts
risk_register.note: Orders taken at fixed BOP cost; if commodity prices increase materially during execution, that risk is carried by the company, though de-risked with contingency in costing.

risk_register.risk: India-Pakistan conflict impact on API order booking and Q1 revenue
risk_register.note: Impacted large anticipated API segment orders and Q1 revenue at start of FY26.

risk_register.risk: US tariff-related uncertainty
risk_register.note: Led to more muted order booking during the year.

risk_register.risk: Middle East / West Asia conflict
risk_register.note: Year-end conflict impacted revenue and order booking; API outlook from Middle East not factored into FY27 projections due to ongoing uncertainty; management anticipates certain conflicts to continue.

risk_register.risk: Export order finalisation delays
risk_register.note: Delays during FY26 due to geopolitical issues caused flattish export order inflow; management sees improving traction/discussions going into FY27.

risk_register.risk: Currency volatility / MTM losses
risk_register.note: ₹8.5 crore MTM loss in Q4 due to rupee volatility; expected to be adjusted in subsequent quarters; such losses/gains may recur annually due to hedging policy.

risk_register.risk: Commodity price inflation (copper, aluminium, steel)
risk_register.note: Prices have increased but rate contracts, diversified suppliers and pass-through to customers expected to protect margins.

risk_register.risk: US permitting delays (water permits for combined cycle)
risk_register.note: Water permitting for combined cycle/steam turbine addition takes longer than air permitting for gas turbines, creating uncertainty on enquiry-to-order conversion timing.

risk_register.risk: Weaker brand recognition in US vs global competitors
risk_register.note: Company has to compensate with on-ground service capability, technical breadth, execution speed and reliability guarantees.

risk_register.risk: Elevated receivables / back-ended execution
risk_register.note: Receivable days rose to 84 from 49 YoY due to execution profile and March-end billing skew; similar elevated levels expected in FY27 due to order book execution profile.

risk_register.risk: CO2/long-duration energy storage technology and cost uncertainty
risk_register.note: NTPC project has seen cost increases (absorbed, still marginally profitable); full cost-to-conversion, technical performance and round-trip efficiency under Indian conditions still to be assessed; Indian cost appetite for such storage is extremely low.

themes.label: Margin mix volatility
themes.note: EBITDA margin fell to 18% from 25.8% YoY due to softer order mix, NTPC near-zero-margin strategic order, and higher domestic revenue share; recovery expected in H2.

themes.label: Export growth momentum
themes.note: Export order booking grew 53.4% YoY to 68% of total order booking, and export share of closing order book stood at 57%, though export dispatch was deferred by freight rate spikes.

themes.label: Geopolitical disruption
themes.note: Freight rates up 3-4x and vessel availability constraints deferred export dispatches; management notes volatility now surfaces quarterly/monthly instead of half-yearly.

themes.label: US market expansion
themes.note: US enquiries and traction growing (data centres, SMR, combined cycle), but aftermarket contribution remains under 10% of referenced figure and US subsidiary posted a Q1 loss; targeting breakeven this year.

themes.label: New product / technology diversification
themes.note: Continued investment in ORC, heat pump/MVR combinations, and first-of-its-kind CO2-based energy storage (NTPC/Energy Dome) technology validation with positive European pilot results.

themes.label: Enquiry pipeline build-up
themes.note: International enquiry generation (US, Southeast Asia, Europe green shoots) improved, while domestic enquiry generation showed a broad-based dip this quarter, though enquiry book remains far larger than annual demand.

themes.label: API segment recovery
themes.note: API traction seen from Indian thermal power plants and new orders secured from Europe this quarter, alongside expansion into Americas oil & gas opportunities, despite deferred decision-making from geopolitical tensions.

key_takeaways: As we had anticipated, the quarter remained challenging. Revenue from operations came in at ₹4.43 billion, up by 19.2% year-on-year.

Profitability, however, was softer in the quarter. EBITDA stood at ₹797 million at a margin of 18% against 25.8%, and a profit before tax of ₹697 million was down 20.1% at a margin of 15.7%, as opposed to 23.5% at the same quarter of the previous year.
The execution in this quarter reflects the business environment and order intake of roughly a year ago. So the softer order mix of H1 FY 2026 has carried through to Q1 FY 2027 profitability.

On the order booking front, the order booking for the quarter stood at ₹5.68 billion as compared to ₹5.36 billion in Q1 FY 2026, a growth of 6.1% year-over-year, an increase led entirely by exports and aftermarket.
Export order booking grew 53.4% year-over-year, accounting for 68% of the total order booking as against 47% in Q1 FY 2026.
The closing order book stood at ₹21.8 billion as of the 30th of June as compared to ₹20.74 billion a year ago, reflecting a 5.1% year-on-year increase.

The aftermarket business also continued to gain strong momentum, with closing orders increasing 115% year-over-year to ₹6.24 billion on the back of contract wins in the geothermal and utility segments.
Having said that, as we look forward, the enquiry generation in the international market has improved while the domestic market has seen weakness.

The company is optimistic on the growth, both in margins and absolute and on a percentage basis in the second half of this year. And as we look at the full-year FY 2027, we are confident to exhibit top line and bottom line growth.
pressing_questions: What was the impact of the NTPC order? ... what was the quantum? ... What was the kind of contribution of impacts from the commodity inflation also in this quarter?

Last time you highlighted, roughly about 18 GW for the global enquiries and domestic enquiry was about 7 GW. How that has grown and what is the primary reason for the domestic slowdown? Any particular industry or are you seeing delays from the customers in terms of conversions of orders?

With respect to the NTPC CO2 storage, how much of revenue contribution would have happened during 1Q? And given the fact that this is going to get commissioned in 2Q, how much amount of execution is likely to happen during that quarter?

With respect to the bought-out components. Out of the total COGS, can you give us an indication of how much would be the bought-out component, and was there any price inflation in that which we were not able to pass-through?

With respect to the consolidated EBITDA margin, we were somewhere around 20%-22%. That has fallen significantly this quarter... for H2, what kind of sustainable EBITDA margins going forward, we can expect?

In Q1, either for us or for other global steam turbine makers, has this [global data centre] opportunity started getting converted to actual order placement, or is this still in advanced evaluation phase?
Broadly, how much is that [aftermarket ₹6 billion orders] from North American region? ... what kind of size can we attain in next 2 to 3 years?
In FY 2027-2028, how much of investment rate loss will be there in U.S.? ... Is 2028 the year where we can be very well utilised in the American facility?
So, is this solely because of the bought-out mix being higher, or are there other elements that are affecting margins domestically?
What are we doing, just to ensure that this volatility in the business... comes down [given recurring geopolitical disruptions]?
Do we have any exclusivity with Energy Dome in terms of technology or is it open for all? What leverage do we have by taking this pilot in India?
This validation [CO2 BESS] when will happen... how much time the validation takes, and when do we see more orders and more tenders coming in for this in the future?

quarters.summary: FY26 saw record annual revenue (₹21.81bn, +9% YoY) with H2 growth of 125% YoY offsetting a soft H1 impacted by geopolitical disruptions; management expects FY27 to remain back-ended, guides on continued long-term growth and margin rates (~25%+ EBITDA), expects export orders to exceed domestic in FY27, expects US subsidiary to turn profitable/breakeven in FY27 and meaningfully profitable from FY28, and flags a nearly-doubled enquiry pipeline (steam turbine based) as a source of confidence for order booking growth going forward, even as API, Middle East and currency-related uncertainties persist into FY27.

subsections.label: FY26 performance narrative
points: Against backdrop of multiple challenges including geopolitical disruptions, tariff-related uncertainties and volatile global environment, company delivered satisfactory performance for FY26.
Q4 FY26 contributed meaningfully to full-year performance, helping offset relatively softer first half of the year.
India-Pakistan conflict at start of year impacted order booking (large anticipated API segment orders that did not materialise) and revenue in Q1.
Subsequent quarters saw tariff-related challenges with United States leading to more muted order booking.
Year ended with conflict in West Asia which impacted both revenue and order booking.
Demand conditions across certain markets remained uneven in H1; H2 saw significantly improved execution momentum across businesses.
Performance supported by healthy order backlog, robust enquiry pipeline and resilient business model despite uncertainties.
Diversified presence across sectors and geographies and strong execution capabilities helped navigate market uncertainties.

subsections.label: Margin drivers Q4
points: Margin compression in Q4 principally due to change in segmental mix — greater share of strategic project (NTPC BESS), MTM loss, and lower percentage of Aftermarket as % of sales.
For full year, margins are largely in line with expectations; management anticipates continuing long-term growth and margin rates seen in previous quarters/years.
Aftermarket has much higher profitability than export; low-margin strategic order (NTPC) combined with lower Aftermarket % of sales impacted Q4 profitability.
Management encourages viewing performance on trailing 12-month basis rather than quarterly, given lumpiness.

subsections.label: Balance sheet & receivables
points: Receivables reflect execution profile of certain large projects and billing skewed towards end of March, expected to be liquidated in subsequent quarters (significant amount already liquidated as of call date).
Elevated receivable days seen as likely to persist into FY27 given execution profile of order book being back-ended; receivable levels at end of March 2027 may be similar due to execution profile.
Company continues to maintain negative working capital on non-balance-sheet ending days (March 31 and September 30).

subsections.label: Commodity cost / margin protection
points: Movement in material prices observed (copper, aluminium, steel all increased), but not expected to impact supply chain procurement or margins.
Diversified supplier base and long-term rate contracts help insulate from cost escalations.
For large orders, company negotiates cautious/favorable supplier rates.
Where necessary, some cost escalation can be passed to customers who are equally sensitive to commodity price movements, with a small time lag.
Extended global supply chain network plus customer pass-through ability expected to help maintain bottom line.
