subsections.label: Order booking drivers
points: Q4 FY26 order booking underpinned by traction across both domestic and international markets and a favourable segment mix.
Export orders driven by demand across key markets including Europe, Turkey and Southeast Asia.
Aftermarket order booking witnessed strong momentum in the quarter.
Healthy order inflows across key and high-value segments during Q4 FY26 resulted in improvement in closing order book.
International expansion strategy, continued innovation and entry into new product segments contributed to export orders share of closing order book.
Order book mix witnessed meaningful improvement supported by strong scale-up of Aftermarket business during the year.

subsections.label: Enquiry pipeline detail
points: CO2-based products are newer and not reflected in enquiry book yet, pending performance validation of current installation and determination of business model.
Growth in enquiry book is for steam turbine-based applications only (product and Aftermarket), including to the extent API requires a steam turbine.
North America enquiry generation of ~3GW driven by data centre investments (initially gas turbine based, now including combined cycle and renewable/geothermal based demand).
Turkey is the only market showing a slight decline in enquiry book visibility; all other markets show growth.
India enquiry growth driven by thermal power generation and fixed capital formation demand from user industries including paper, pulp, cement, steel and process cogeneration applications.
Southeast Asia and Europe continue to show enquiry book growth in both renewable energy-based applications and industrial CapEx.
Within India, steel and cement contribute maximum in terms of size/proportion of enquiry base, but growth is broad-based across sectors including process cogeneration, sugar, IPPs.
US enquiry growth of ~1000% is from a low base (low prior visibility); disproportionate compared to rest-of-world growth.
Data centre end market contributes well in excess of half of the US enquiry book.
US demand areas: combined cycle applications for data centres, biomass plants, pulp and paper, and Geothermal; also small modular reactors.
Enquiry conversion delayed during the year due to geopolitical issues causing finalisation delays, particularly affecting export order inflow which was flattish for the first time in several years.
Going into FY27, discussions and traction are increasing, and management expects export orders to exceed domestic orders this year.
Growth in closing order book of ~8-9% gives an indication of minimum anticipated growth; management expects order booking growth to accelerate going forward, aided by US contribution.

Order intake expected to remain lumpy depending on external situations and size of turbines/projects delivered; aspiration is towards higher intake levels (₹500-700 crore range mentioned as aspirational, not guidance).

subsections.label: API segment
points: API is a key growth and profit driver for the business; large anticipated orders at start of FY26 did not materialise, making API a lower % of order book and revenue than anticipated.
API has a larger revenue share than order book share currently; expected to revert to a meaningful 10%+ share of order booking and revenue in coming quarters/years.
Middle East conflict outlook not factored into any FY27 projections for API; if conflict ends, expect repair, maintenance, refurbishment and new order demand from that market.
Globally, higher oil prices have driven resurgence in enquiries and order finalisations in API segment for both upstream and downstream; company largely participates in downstream.
Middle East had larger share of enquiry book/order booking in last two years; requirement now seen as more global including Africa, US and India.

subsections.label: Aftermarket detail
points: Aftermarket comprises three segments: spares, service, and refurbishment.
Spares and service driven by Triveni's own installed base, growing based on installed base from 2-3 years prior.

Real growth in Aftermarket comes from refurbishment based on on-ground capability in certain geographies (e.g., Africa) to convince customers; includes lower value-add and higher value-add projects including overhaul and repair parts manufacturing.
More clarity on African operations expected in subsequent quarters.
US Aftermarket orders can be turned around and executed rapidly (within next year), while product-side orders may execute in FY28.

subsections.label: New product introductions
points: Entry into geothermal products segment is a key milestone, a technically demanding segment constituting a growing part of enquiry book; foretells good market opportunity and entry for the company.
R&D continues to innovate and deliver new products for existing steam turbine customers as well as newer rotating equipment solutions.

Carbon dioxide-based platform under development; introduction of organic Rankine cycle (ORC) turbine to capture waste heat at lower temperatures, targeting geothermal and low waste heat recovery/industrial process applications (not for data centres).

MVR compressors form a much smaller market segment, not significant to enquiry book or order booking currently; expected to remain small contribution but useful for penetrating customers and displaying technical prowess, especially when coupled with heat pump innovations.
Drive turbine market is cyclical, tracking thermal power expansion; currently thermal power and oil & gas (upstream/downstream) are expanding, with good demand seen in API segment in Q1.
Geothermal, ORC and CO2 (subcritical energy storage) markets expected to be large contributors over next 2-4 years; MVR/heat pump market expected to remain small but high-profit and constant.
None of the newer initiatives (geothermal, MVR, drive turbine, CO2) are currently very meaningful contributors to enquiry book at this point in time.

subsections.label: CO2 subcritical energy storage (NTPC project)
points: Company wants to finish current project and let the plant stabilise before articulating business plan for CO2-based long-term energy storage.

Significant billing occurred on the NTPC project this quarter with some cost increases already absorbed; project remains marginally profitable (~3% PBT level) with over two-thirds already recognised as revenue.

Full cost-to-conversion and technical performance/round-trip efficiency assessment (including under Indian conditions, since temperature affects cycle calculations) still pending before finalizing business approach.

Company aims to be a value-added player rather than integrator of others' technologies in long-duration energy storage; evaluating flow battery and kinetic thermal-based energy storage systems among other research areas.

CO2-based long-duration storage evaluated similarly to pumped hydro in terms of application but currently significantly higher cost; challenge is to scale down costing to match Indian cost appetite, which is extremely low.
No active RFP-stage marketing discussions currently on CO2 storage technology; some technical parameter discussions ongoing.

subsections.label: R&D and innovation strategy
points: No fixed Board-mandated target for share of revenue from new products; R&D priority driven partly by opportunistic commercialisation requirements.
Strong technical bench strength: R&D (7.5%+), engineering (8%+) and servicing (35%+) workforce shares underpin customer satisfaction focus.

Newer technology introductions provide longer-term growth path; company remains predominantly a steam turbine company in near term, expected to evolve into multi-product, solution-oriented company in medium/long term.
Company to invest significantly more into AI adoption to remain technologically ready for disruption within industries, companies, and the market generally; updates to be provided in coming quarters.

subsections.label: Export performance
points: Export revenue remained a key growth driver for FY26, increasing 30% YoY and rising to 58% of overall revenue from 48% in FY25.
Export orders contributed 51% to closing order book, aided by international expansion strategy, innovation and new product segment entry.
Strong export performance in Q4 supported overall revenue growth, but was impacted by segment mix of lower Aftermarket spares execution and NTPC order execution.

subsections.label: US market entry
points: Newer entry into US market has led to disproportionate increase in enquiry book from US relative to rest of world due to previously lower visibility.
US enquiry book grew to represent 15%+ of total enquiry book, up from 1-2% previously.
US demand driven by combined cycle applications for data centres, biomass plants, pulp and paper, and geothermal.

Sales approach in US is consistent with global messaging (reliability, robustness, value, uptime, service backup); differentiator is on-ground US servicing capability though brand recognition is weaker than global competitors.

Permits for water (needed for combined cycle) take longer than for air (needed for simple cycle/gas turbine), so combined cycle addition may lag initial gas turbine installation, affecting conversion timing of enquiries into orders.

Q4 was a profitable quarter for the US subsidiary, but full-year FY26 saw a loss of about ₹8 crore in that subsidiary; management expects this year to be positive or at worst breakeven, with meaningful profitability expected from FY28 onward due to scale, overhead absorption and order profitability.

subsections.label: Other geography detail
points: Africa - growing on-ground refurbishment capability driving Aftermarket orders, including overhaul and repair parts manufacturing contracts; more clarity to be provided in subsequent quarters.
API order geography shifting from being largely Middle East-centric in the last two years to more global, including Africa, US and India.

subsections.label: Sourcing & cost management
points: Diversified supplier base used to mitigate cost escalation risks.
Long-term rate contracts for large components help insulate from commodity price escalations (e.g., copper, aluminium, steel prices rising).
For large-magnitude orders, extra caution taken in negotiating supplier rates.
Some cost escalations may be passed to customers, who are equally sensitive to commodity price movements, with a small time lag.
Extended global supply chain network aids in maintaining bottom line despite commodity volatility.

subsections.label: Competitive positioning
points: Company does not lose orders based on price in international markets; margin/price is generally not the deciding factor in competitive bidding.

Market is largely oligopolistic globally; competitiveness is based on providing right value proposition (reliability, robustness, technical service, timely delivery and performance) rather than being cheapest.

Currency depreciation seen as a margin expansion opportunity rather than a tool for price discounting; other countries (e.g., Japan) have also faced currency declines, so competitive intensity not seen as materially changing.

In US market, company differentiates via on-ground servicing capability, breadth of technical offering, execution speed, and reliability guarantees to offset weaker brand recognition versus established global competitors.
Sells to integrators, EPCs or developers; permitting is the developer's responsibility, not Triveni's.

High win percentage once in front of a customer for order finalization; the challenge is enquiry visibility and being in front of the customer, hence enquiry book growth is seen as a strong indicator of potential demand.

subsections.label: Data centre market opportunity
points: Combined cycle solutions for data centres arise as some data centres convert from pure gas turbine to combined cycle configurations to improve efficiency (gas turbine ~30-35% efficiency alone vs ~50% in combined cycle).
Approximate ratio cited: for every 3 MW of gas turbine capacity, about 1 MW of steam turbine capacity may be added on the waste heat side (rough approximation).

Combined cycle addition can be installed at initial setup or retrofitted later, as water permitting (needed for steam turbine/combined cycle) is separate from and slower than air permitting (needed for gas turbine/simple cycle).
Decision on combined cycle vs simple cycle rests fully with the developer/customer based on permitting, funds availability, and speed requirements — not influenced by Triveni.
Contract structuring varies by developer: some club gas and steam turbine contracts under one lead (e.g., gas turbine OEM), some split via EPCs, some order everything themselves; no set format.

Company does not expect margin expansion or pricing gains from data centre-linked demand disproportionate to what's generally available; priority is sustainable entry into the space given supply constraints in energy solutions/rotating equipment globally.
When long-term service contracts are offered as part of data centre-related orders, only near-term (one-year executable) portion is taken into the order book, not the full contract duration.

subsections.label: Geopolitical and macro risks
points: India-Pakistan conflict at start of FY26 impacted order booking (large anticipated API orders) and Q1 revenue.
Tariff-related challenges with the United States led to more muted order booking during the year.
Middle East/West Asia conflict at year-end impacted both revenue and order booking; management anticipates certain conflicts to continue into projections.
Delays in enquiry-to-order finalisation across export markets during the year attributed to geopolitical issues, contributing to flattish export order inflow for the first time in several years.

Rupee volatility caused a mark-to-market loss of ₹8.5 crore in Q4, expected to be adjusted in subsequent quarters; such MTM losses/gains may recur annually due to currency volatility and hedging policy.
Commodity price increases across copper, aluminium and steel noted, though not expected to significantly impact margins given rate contracts and pass-through ability.
US permitting timelines (particularly for water, needed for combined cycle) are long and uncertain, creating uncertainty over conversion timing of enquiries into orders.
Weaker brand recognition versus established global competitors in the US market is a competitive risk being addressed through on-ground service capability and technical differentiation.
API segment outlook from Middle East not factored into FY27 projections due to ongoing conflict uncertainty.

subsections.label: Outlook commentary
points: Management shies away from giving direct numerical guidance but points to ~9% growth in closing order book as an indication of minimum anticipated growth for FY27.
FY27 expected to remain a back-ended year similar to FY26 due to order book execution profile; receivables at end of March 2027 may remain at similar elevated levels.
Expect exports to exceed domestic revenue in FY27.

Expect long-term growth and margin rates similar to previous quarters/years to continue, with margins generally stable around mean ~25% EBITDA level (with quarterly fluctuation such as 27-28% in some quarters).
US subsidiary expected to turn profitable or at worst breakeven in FY27, with meaningful profitability expected from FY28 onward.
API expected to revert to a meaningful 10%+ share of order booking and revenue in coming quarters/years.
Geothermal, ORC and CO2 markets expected to become large contributors over the next 2-4 years; MVR/heat pump expected to remain small but high-profit and constant contributors.
Company anticipates disruptions to continue in FY27 (geopolitical), but believes streamlined processes will help navigate uncertainties.
Company to invest significantly more in AI to remain technologically prepared for disruption; updates to be provided in coming quarters.

guidance_ledger.metric: Closing order book growth (indicative minimum for FY27 order booking)
guidance_ledger.statement: We shy away from giving direct guidance, but what we do have is a growth in the enquiry closing order book by about 9%. And so that gives you an indication of the minimum growth that we would like to anticipate.
FY27 will also be somewhat of a back-ended year; receivable at end of March 31, 2027 may be in a similar level just because of the execution profile of our order book.
We believe exports would be more than the domestic (this year).

Going forward, we anticipate that we will continue our long-term growth and long-term margin rates that you have seen in the previous quarters and years... comfortable with our margins of what is 25% plus EBITDA.
We believe that this current year should be positive, if not at worst breakeven. ... when we get into FY '28 onwards that we'll be able to deliver profitability from the U.S. operations.

guidance_ledger.metric: API share of order booking and revenue
guidance_ledger.statement: We believe in the coming quarters and years, it will revert to having a meaningful 10% plus number in our order booking as well as in revenue.

When I look forward in terms of in the next couple of years or next three, four years, the Geothermal market will be a large market for us. I think the ORC market will also be large for us. We think that the CO2 market... may be quite a large market for us.
The MVR and heat pump market will remain small as a contribution to Triveni Turbine, but it will increasingly allow us to penetrate into the customer.

guidance_ledger.metric: Order intake sustainable level per quarter
guidance_ledger.statement: Should it be higher than ₹500 crores or ₹700 crores. Obviously, we believe that it should be, the higher number is what we aspire towards. But we'll have to see that.
We have seen a good growth in the market in this current year, and we anticipate next year as well for it to have a good growth.
We will be investing significantly more into the movement into AI. We think that we need to be technologically ready for any disruption... We will provide these updates in the coming quarters.

risk_register.risk: India-Pakistan conflict impact on API order booking and Q1 revenue
risk_register.note: Impacted large anticipated API segment orders and Q1 revenue at start of FY26.

risk_register.risk: US tariff-related uncertainty
risk_register.note: Led to more muted order booking during the year.

risk_register.risk: Middle East / West Asia conflict
risk_register.note: Year-end conflict impacted revenue and order booking; API outlook from Middle East not factored into FY27 projections due to ongoing uncertainty; management anticipates certain conflicts to continue.

risk_register.risk: Export order finalisation delays
risk_register.note: Delays during FY26 due to geopolitical issues caused flattish export order inflow; management sees improving traction/discussions going into FY27.

risk_register.risk: Currency volatility / MTM losses
risk_register.note: ₹8.5 crore MTM loss in Q4 due to rupee volatility; expected to be adjusted in subsequent quarters; such losses/gains may recur annually due to hedging policy.

risk_register.risk: Commodity price inflation (copper, aluminium, steel)
risk_register.note: Prices have increased but rate contracts, diversified suppliers and pass-through to customers expected to protect margins.

risk_register.risk: US permitting delays (water permits for combined cycle)
risk_register.note: Water permitting for combined cycle/steam turbine addition takes longer than air permitting for gas turbines, creating uncertainty on enquiry-to-order conversion timing.

risk_register.risk: Weaker brand recognition in US vs global competitors
risk_register.note: Company has to compensate with on-ground service capability, technical breadth, execution speed and reliability guarantees.

risk_register.risk: Elevated receivables / back-ended execution
risk_register.note: Receivable days rose to 84 from 49 YoY due to execution profile and March-end billing skew; similar elevated levels expected in FY27 due to order book execution profile.

risk_register.risk: CO2/long-duration energy storage technology and cost uncertainty
risk_register.note: NTPC project has seen cost increases (absorbed, still marginally profitable); full cost-to-conversion, technical performance and round-trip efficiency under Indian conditions still to be assessed; Indian cost appetite for such storage is extremely low.

themes.label: Export growth momentum
themes.note: Export revenue +30% YoY to 58% of FY26 revenue; export orders hit record ₹5.16bn in Q4 (+174% YoY), contributing 51% of closing order book.

themes.label: US market expansion
themes.note: US enquiry book grew ~1000% (low base) to 15%+ of total enquiry book; Q4 was profitable for US subsidiary though FY26 full year posted a ~₹8 crore loss; breakeven/profitability targeted FY27-28.

themes.label: Enquiry pipeline build-up
themes.note: Overall enquiry book nearly doubled YoY; product segment enquiry book at 18GW (nearly double FY25); India enquiry book up ~100% to ~7GW.

themes.label: Margin mix volatility
themes.note: Q4 margin compression driven by lower Aftermarket % of sales, low-margin NTPC strategic order and MTM loss; management maintains full-year margins stable around 25% EBITDA mean.

themes.label: Geopolitical disruption
themes.note: India-Pakistan conflict, US tariff issues and Middle East/West Asia conflict all impacted order booking and revenue timing during FY26, with some risks expected to persist into FY27.

themes.label: New product / technology diversification
themes.note: Entry into geothermal, ORC and CO2-based subcritical energy storage (NTPC strategic project) seen as long-term growth avenues, though contribution to date remains not meaningful.

themes.label: API segment recovery
themes.note: API orders underperformed anticipation in FY26 due to conflict-related delays, but expected to revert to 10%+ share of order booking/revenue as global oil price-driven enquiries resurge.

key_takeaways: During FY '26, we achieved our highest ever annual turnover of ₹21.81 billion, registering a growth of 9% over FY '25.
Export revenue remained a key growth driver, increasing 30% year-on-year and contributing 58% of our overall revenue compared to 48% in the previous year.
Aftermarket as a percentage of sales did decline on a year-on-year basis.
EBITDA stood at ₹5.27 billion with margins of 24.2%, while profit before tax before exceptional items stood at ₹4.9 billion, which remained broadly stable year-on-year with margins of 22.5%.
Profit after tax registered a decline of 3%, primarily on account of an exceptional charge of ₹157 million, which is recognised towards employee benefit obligations under the new wage code.

We delivered our highest ever quarterly revenue of ₹6.8 billion, reflecting a growth of 26% year-on-year; during the quarter, the share of exports in the overall revenue increased to 60%, registering a 46% growth year-on-year.

Q4 FY '26 recorded a 19% year-on-year growth with total order booking of ₹7.54 billion; Export orders booking touched a record high of ₹5.16 billion during the quarter, registering a growth of 174% year-over-year and contributed 69% to total order booking.
Our closing outstanding order book increasing by 8% year-on-year to ₹20.54 billion, with export orders contributing 51% to our closing order book.
Our entry into the geothermal products segment is a key milestone for the company in a technically demanding segment and a segment which constitutes a growing part of our enquiry book.
The enquiry pipeline has grown and nearly doubled over the past year, allowing greater confidence in order booking going forward.
pressing_questions: Can you give a bifurcation or possible broad bifurcation as to how much of the enquiry book has been contributed by existing products, new products, and incrementally by foray into newer geographies like U.S.?

What would have been the contribution in FY '26 of new initiatives (Geothermal, drive turbine for boiler feed pumps, MVR compressors, CO2-based applications), and what is the near-term target market size for each over a two-three year period?

Regarding long-duration energy storage, your technology partner globally seems to have signed partnerships with Google, ENGIE and Alliant Energy suggesting technology validated at scale, but your messaging is more cautious — what is the caution about, adoption in India or the technology itself?
Could you give an idea on the size of FY '26 addressable market in megawatt terms for the less than 100 MW market in India, and how this market is expected to grow?
What is the size of API turbines in revenues, orders and order backlog, and is this business expected to grow faster than the overall business?

What are the expectations in terms of conversions for FY '27 in the U.S. business — more confidence on product or Aftermarket side — and how competitive is Triveni vis-à-vis global MNCs in that market?
Is there any notable conversion on the data centre piece in current U.S. order backlog and enquiry?
What should be the expectation for growth this year given lumpiness, and how much of the current order book has lumpy orders?
Regarding overall export order inflows (~₹1,200 crore, flattish for the first time), is there a challenge in enquiry conversions in markets other than the U.S.?
Any bulky order booked this quarter in Aftermarket exports, and what is the sustainable run rate given increased Aftermarket offering?
At the Board level, is there a target share of revenue from new products, or is it on a best-effort basis?
How much of the NTPC battery energy storage order has been executed and what is the margin profile?
In light of currency depreciation, what is the competitive position vis-à-vis global competitors bidding from different economies?
Considering the Middle East conflict, what is the outlook on the API Turbine Business specifically from Middle Eastern customers for FY '27?
Understanding the trajectory of EBITDA margin — have margins bottomed out, or is more stress expected due to the Middle East crisis?
Is there a sustainable level of order intake to expect every quarter?
On the U.S. market, what is the competitive landscape and positioning, and what pushbacks are received from end customers during conversion?
For combined cycle products for data centres, is order visibility accompanied by servicing/AMC contracts, and are there pricing tailwinds similar to other hyperscaler-linked products?
Despite the data centre opportunity, why has there been slow uptake globally of steam turbine/organic Rankine cycle solutions in this industry?
Given large CCGT players like Siemens have their own steam turbine solutions, what space is open for Triveni to participate?
With margin mix shifting on three fronts (domestic to export, OEM to Aftermarket, standalone turbines to solutions), how should one think about margin trajectory going forward?
Where does CO2 battery technology fit versus BESS and pump storage in the Indian long-duration storage landscape, and are there ongoing discussions for this technology in India?
How do customers typically validate the viability of a relatively new technology like CO2 storage before placing an order, as with NTPC?

BAJAJCON.about: Bajaj Consumer Care is engaged in the business of cosmetics, toiletries and other personal care products. The Company has presence in both domestic and international markets.(Source : 201903 Annual Report Page No: 98)

quarters.summary: Bajaj Consumer Care delivered a strong Q1 FY27 with revenue growth of over 28% and consolidated EBITDA nearly doubling to INR84.4 crores (24.7% margin), despite gross margin pressure from West Asia war-led input cost volatility. Management expects Q2 FY27 gross margins to remain under stress with sequential easing expected in Q3/Q4, reiterated its EBITDA margin aspiration of low-to-mid 20s, reiterated long-term double-digit-to-low-teens growth aspiration for core brands, and gave no formal quarterly/yearly guidance, while continuing to invest in Aarohan distribution expansion and the non-ADHO growth portfolio.

key_figures.label: Savings on employee cost and other fixed costs
EBITDA margin (as referenced by analyst, alternate)

subsections.label: Margin drivers
points: Gross margin dropped from 63% in Q4 FY26 sequentially to 61.8% in Q1 FY27 due to unprecedented volatility in raw material prices caused by the West Asia war and its cascading impact.
Despite the sequential drop, gross margin showed a 510 basis point improvement over Q1 FY26.
Company took selective and calibrated price increases and MLH (mL/weight) reduction across the portfolio to protect margins.
Advertising spend was maintained at 14.6% of revenue even amid cost pressure, reflecting continued brand investment.
Company optimized on other fixed costs including employee costs, taking advantage of operating leverage to deliver savings of over 600 basis points versus Q1 FY26 and versus the sequential quarter.
As a result, EBITDA doubled YoY to INR84.4 crores at 24.7% margin, with PAT of INR70.7 crores at 20.7% margin.
Management clarified there were no significant one-offs in the quarter; some expenses naturally skew between quarters but there was no deliberate deferral or acceleration of costs.

key_figures.label: General trade and organized trade channel growth
ADHO (Almond Drop Hair Oil) volume growth (MLH adjusted)
Non-ADHO growth portfolio contribution to revenue
Non-ADHO growth portfolio long-term aspiration growth

subsections.label: ADHO (Almond Drop Hair Oil)
points: ADHO delivered low-teens volume growth on an MLH-adjusted basis, up from mid-single-digit growth in previous quarters.
ADHO ASP growth was 29% YoY on a consolidated basis.
Growth came across all pack groups and channels, with small packs and sachet business standing out as leading the growth.
The improvement in volume growth was driven by good traction across smaller unit price points.
Positive movements were registered across most consumer metrics for the brand.
Company maintained a robust SOV-SOM ratio in traditional media while increasingly shifting toward digital channels of communication.
Significant investment was made behind influencer-led marketing campaigns across major digital platforms, receiving positive consumer feedback.
ADHO portfolio contributes approximately 80% of revenue.

subsections.label: Non-ADHO / Growth portfolio
points: The growth portfolio (cluster of smaller, non-ADHO brands) grew high single-digit sequentially against the previous quarter, improving its run rate, and contributes approximately 15% of revenue.
Growth occurred despite value deflation in the coconut portfolio, which forms a large part of this mix.

Coconut portfolio saw sequential volume growth despite a volume-value correction taken on per-ml realized prices against Q4, as company rationalized its discount to the market leader to a level enabling profitable operation.
Coconut volume scale-up is being driven by distribution and wider availability of the product, not by higher grammage or free volumes/MLH change.
Management declined to disclose extensive data on the coconut portfolio, citing it as a small but extremely competitive segment.

Banjara's contributes approximately 5% of revenue and is being revamped with pilots underway to identify a disruptive growth approach; management will disclose more once ready with ideas. Banjara's is expected to be the second-biggest, if not the biggest, leg of the growth portfolio strategy.
Further diversification of the growth portfolio beyond coconut is described as more immediate on the agenda, not far away.
Management intends to give detailed disclosure on growth portfolio progress on an annual basis given it comprises several small businesses competing against large competitors in sub-segments.
Institutional business mix is less than 1% of revenue and was weak in the quarter.
Non-ADHO growth portfolio's long-term aspiration is to grow in the high 20s.

subsections.label: Domestic trade channels
points: General trade channel continued momentum, growing in line with organized trade, with both channels delivering growth in strong 20s.
Performance was broad-based across urban retail, wholesale, and rural.
Rural business, which recovered in H2 of last year, saw strong growth this quarter and grew in line with urban.
Within organized trade, both modern trade and e-commerce performed well, with growth across sub-channels and customers, with the exception of institutional business which was weak.

subsections.label: International business
points: International business had a challenging year last year but delivered a very strong rebound this quarter, albeit on a weak base.
Performance was strong across countries, giving management confidence in sustainable future growth for this channel.
Key markets Nepal and Bangladesh demonstrated continued double-digit growth and margin improvement.
MENA, which was challenged last year, delivered very strong growth.
Rest of World, which witnessed tariff and other related disruptions last year, also rebounded strongly.

subsections.label: Project Aarohan (distribution expansion)
points: Aarohan is being executed for the first time in four big states called out by management, for FY27.
Even in states where Aarohan has already been implemented, the endeavor to expand direct distribution continues.
Aarohan delivers roughly a 200-300 basis point delta as a one-time benefit when first executed due to change of mix from indirect/low-supervision to high-impact direct distribution.
Benefits from added outlets to the network are expected to be milked for efficiency over a long period, making it a multi-year sales and distribution exercise rather than a purely one-time benefit.
The one-time impact is also on a relatively small mix of the overall business, making it difficult to precisely segregate growth attribution.

subsections.label: M&A
points: Management stated there is nothing to disclose currently on M&A strategy or targets, including for the growth portfolio.
Management will update the market as and when there is something to disclose.

subsections.label: Growth portfolio roadmap (INR500 crores target)
points: Management intends to come back once a year with more details on progress toward the INR500 crores growth portfolio roadmap.
Requested patience given the portfolio comprises several small businesses competing against large competitors in sub-segments.

subsections.label: Input cost volatility
points: War in the Gulf created extreme volatility in petroleum-related products like LLP (linear alkylbenzene/LLP) and packaging material.
Inflationary trend also seen in edible oils like mustard and almond, which have not fallen from historical prices even in the harvest season as they used to previously.

Company has high-cost inventory in the system currently; spot prices are expected to cool sequentially over the next few months, but the situation remains dynamic and difficult to predict (e.g., uncertainty over whether the war is truly over).
Q2 FY27 gross margins expected to remain more under stress compared to Q1, though behavior will vary by commodity - some may see higher-priced inventory carried into Q2, others may be flat.
Management stated it's very difficult to generalize, as it depends on inventory holding/cover at end of Q1 and how quickly certain items cool off.

subsections.label: Execution risk
points: Management identified execution risk as the single largest risk to sustaining growth performance over the next two years.
Sustaining low-teens to double-digit long-term growth aspiration will require consistent execution to gain market share, gain more consumers, and widen distribution/outlet reach.

subsections.label: Competitive intensity
points: Coconut portfolio operates in an extremely competitive segment, limiting frequency of detailed disclosure.
Management declined to comment on unorganized segment competitive dynamics in copra-based markets like Kerala, stating these are not structurally big markets for the company.

key_figures.label: EBITDA margin aspiration range (low to mid)

subsections.label: Margin outlook
points: Gross margins expected to remain in a tough zone in Q2 FY27, with sequential easing expected over Q3 and Q4.
EBITDA margin currently running on the higher side of the company's aspiration; further trajectory will depend on how revenue performs flowing into the bottom line.
No pricing actions are planned; pricing will not drive any further margin expansion going forward.
Company does not give formal quarterly or yearly guidance on specific numbers.
Aspiration remains to operate EBITDA margin in the low-to-mid 20s (20 plus); business is dynamic and will sometimes be on the lower end and sometimes higher end of that spectrum.

subsections.label: Growth outlook
points: Long-term aspiration is to deliver consistent double-digit to low-teens year-on-year growth.
Current exponential growth (28%+ YoY revenue) is expected to settle down to a lower number as the company begins lapping the exponential growth bases of the past few quarters.
Management would be disappointed if the company does not deliver double-digit growth in any quarter, though it cannot predict exact quarterly landing.
Non-ADHO growth portfolio long-term aspiration is to grow in the high 20s and add meaningfully to overall mix; no short/medium-term guidance provided.
Advertising spend expected to continue operating in the historical 15-16% range, with continued investment behind brands; not an area targeted for cost squeezing.

guidance_ledger.statement: We are happy to operate in the low to mid 20s in terms of what we would be happy with our business.
Margins at a gross margin level will continue to remain in a tough zone in quarter two and then they will expect to sequentially ease over quarter three and four.
From a pricing perspective, pricing is not going to drive any further margin expansion. We don't have any pricing actions planned in.
Our aspiration on a long-term basis is to deliver a consistent double-digit performance, double-digit to a low teens performance.
This exponential growth as we will start lapping up those growth exponential growth bases of the past, will soon settle down to a slightly lower number.
Long term, we want to grow in the high 20s on that portfolio and for it to add meaningfully to our overall mix.

We've been operating on number if you look at our historical averages have been around 15% to 16%. We will try and operate in that zone... we will continue to double down and invest and stay consistent over our advertising spends over the medium term.

Aarohan delivers anywhere around a 200 to 300 basis point delta as a one-time when we are executing because of the change of the mix... after that it will be there. And that too also will be on a small mix.
We intend to come back once a year and give you more details in terms of the progress.
As of now, we can just say we have nothing to disclose... as and when we have some update to disclose, obviously we will come back and update the market.
As you know, we don't give guidances... beyond that we don't give quarterly or yearly guidance for specific numbers, so I don't want to comment more on it.
Our core brands would basically, we've anyways said that if we do around a double-digit revenue CAGR over a period, we'll be happy.

We are getting into the third phase of Aarohan which involves us going to five new states where we had not gone so far... we will work and extract the benefits of the project in those five states through this year.
I think 4% is sustainable. There would be a lap up which will start happening state-by-state there, so that might lead to some tapering.

guidance_ledger.metric: Margin outlook amid input cost inflation
guidance_ledger.statement: Despite the current situation, we feel confident about our ability to maintain margins in the current approximate range. However, as the situation unfolds over the next month or so, we will freeze our strategy and continue to fine-tune our actions over the subsequent quarters.
We don't give guidances... Where and which is our happy zone, I've already indicated, there's no point doing that again, but guidances we don't give.
I have already given, we will not give margins on basically -- we will give guidance on margins. But what we've repeatedly said, we aspire to maintain margins between the low to the mid 20s.
With the new leadership, we have renewed our efforts behind getting and fixing the markets of Rest of World and MENA, and I'm confident that we will soon be seeing a turnaround in this business.
We will continue to grow the businesses in Nepal and Bangladesh in a profitable and a sustainable manner.

risk_register.risk: Input cost/raw material volatility due to West Asia war (petroleum-related products, edible oils like mustard and almond)
risk_register.note: Extreme volatility in LLP and packaging material; edible oils have not fallen from historical prices even in harvest season as they used to previously; situation remains dynamic and unpredictable.

risk_register.risk: High-cost inventory in system
risk_register.note: Company carrying high-cost inventory; spot prices expected to cool sequentially over next few months, but supply chain worst believed to be behind.

risk_register.risk: Gross margin pressure in Q2 FY27
risk_register.note: Margins expected to remain more under stress in Q2 vs Q1, with sequential easing expected in Q3/Q4.

risk_register.risk: Execution risk on sustaining growth/market share gains
risk_register.note: Identified as the single largest risk to sustaining double-digit to low-teens growth over next two years; depends on consistent execution of market share and distribution gains.

risk_register.risk: Weak institutional business
risk_register.note: Institutional business was weak this quarter versus other organized trade sub-channels, though it forms less than 1% of company mix.

risk_register.risk: Intense competition in coconut/growth portfolio
risk_register.note: Coconut and non-ADHO segment described as extremely competitive, limiting disclosure frequency; company competes against large unorganized and organized players.

risk_register.risk: Volatility/unpredictability of geopolitical situation (Gulf war status)
risk_register.note: Couple of weeks back thought war was over, now less sure; evolving situation makes near-term outlook difficult to predict.

risk_register.risk: Input cost inflation (LLP, packaging material, mustard, copra) driven by the Gulf war
risk_register.note: War in the Gulf created extreme volatility in LLP and packaging prices and delayed expected cooling in mustard and copra, which held at pre-war levels; nearly 100% of the cost base is under inflation.

risk_register.risk: Dynamic/volatile macro situation limiting forward visibility
risk_register.note: Management repeatedly declined to give margin/revenue guidance citing an extremely volatile environment; strategy to be frozen/fine-tuned over coming quarters.

risk_register.risk: International business weakness (Rest of World, MENA)
risk_register.note: Overall IB declined in the quarter and had a challenging year; leadership change made to fix Rest of World and MENA markets.

risk_register.risk: Muted performance in CSD/CPC sub-channels
risk_register.note: Within organized trade, CSD and CPC performance was muted even as modern trade and e-commerce performed well.

risk_register.risk: Category maturity perception (hair oil as 'sunset sector')
risk_register.note: Management pushed back strongly, calling hair oil a mature but not sunset category with $2bn+ size, 20%+ margin and 92% penetration, and highlighting the company's own headroom given <10% share.

themes.label: Input-cost inflation
themes.note: West Asia war caused extreme volatility in petroleum-related products and packaging material, plus edible oil (mustard, almond) inflation that hasn't eased in harvest season as historically.

themes.label: Margin expansion / turnaround
themes.note: EBITDA margin doubled YoY to 24.7% via cost savings and operating leverage even as gross margin dipped sequentially to 61.8% from 63%.

themes.label: Portfolio diversification (non-ADHO growth portfolio)
themes.note: Growth portfolio grew high single-digit sequentially despite coconut value deflation; Banjara's being revamped as a potential second major leg alongside coconut.

themes.label: Distribution expansion (Project Aarohan)
themes.note: Aarohan being executed for first time in four big states, delivering ~200-300 bps one-time delta with multi-year continuous distribution benefits expected.

themes.label: Channel mix shift to organized trade
themes.note: General trade grew in line with organized trade in strong 20s; modern trade and e-commerce performed well, though institutional business was weak.

themes.label: International business turnaround
themes.note: Strong rebound across countries on a weak base; Nepal/Bangladesh continued double-digit growth, MENA and Rest of World rebounded strongly after last year's challenges.

themes.label: No formal guidance stance
themes.note: Management reiterated it does not give quarterly/yearly numerical guidance, holding only to broad aspirations on margin (low-to-mid 20s) and growth (double-digit to low-teens).

key_takeaways: In this quarter, the company was able to deliver a revenue of INR341 crores with a growth of over 28%.
Despite these measures, we saw our gross margins drop from 63% in the sequentially last quarter to 61.8% in this quarter.

Overall, as a result of all of these, our EBITDA on a consolidated basis for quarter one has doubled to deliver an absolute EBITDA of INR84.4 crores, which translates into a margin of 24.7% and the corresponding PAT for quarter one stands at INR70.7 crores with a margin of 20.7.
The current quarter saw a continued momentum in our general trade channel, which grew in line with organized trade with both channels delivering growth in strong 20s.
In international business, we had a challenging year last year and I am happy to report that we have had a very, very strong rebound.
Almond Drop Hair Oil continues with its strong performance in this quarter as well. We have delivered a low teen volume growth on an MLH adjusted basis.

On the growth portfolio, which is a cluster of smaller brands, non-ADHO brands... performed well in the quarter, with the overall portfolio growing high single-digit sequentially against the previous quarter and improving its run rate.

The war in Gulf has created extreme volatility in terms of petroleum-related products like LLP and packaging material. It has also led inflationary trend in case of edible oils like mustard and almond, which have not fallen from their historical prices even in the harvest season like they used to do so previously.
pressing_questions: Just wanted to get a sense on margins for this quarter as well as going ahead... is there kind of any one-off in this quarter on the margins because I see that like other expenses Y-o-Y is very muted despite a fairly good top line and volume growth?

So just wanted to know your overall thoughts on, one is, why this quarter the non-ADHO has been a little bit subdued and secondly, how do you see this panning out and what are your sort of priorities in this portfolio?
But just to some clarity that, Q2 also gross margins obviously will remain under pressure... certain companies have blocked their Q2 at a higher rate as compared to Q1. So just your view on that?
Sir, any update on the M&A strategy? Should we expect, you know, in this year any progress on the M&A side looking at any targets on from a diversification point of view?

So when we see this performance, what is the single biggest risk of sustaining, let's say, 20%... just let's say if we have to sustain this performance, what is the single biggest risk that you are seeing for next two years?
Is it a one-off, and you've also mentioned that this is a stressful situation. So, are we being conservative when we say that we aspire to grow in low teens?

quarters.summary: Bajaj Consumer Care closed FY26 with net revenue crossing INR1,000 crores for the first time (INR1,153 crores, +21%), gross margin of 60%, EBITDA margin 19.5% and PAT margin 16.5%, a year management called a "turnaround" setting the base to march ahead. Management expects to operate gross margins in the same zone (low to mid 20s EBITDA margin) over the medium term, faces rising input cost inflation (LLP, packaging, mustard, copra) due to the Gulf war, plans frontal pricing actions in the near term, and is targeting the non-ADHO "growth portfolio" to reach ~INR500 crores over the next 3 years (from INR225 crores in FY26). Company does not give formal guidance but reiterated directional aspirations on margins, portfolio growth and distribution expansion (Project Aarohan phase 3 into 5 new states in FY27).

key_figures.label: Advertising & sales promotion as % of revenue
Top line growth referenced in COGS discussion

subsections.label: Margin drivers
points: Gross margin improvement of ~650 bps on a full year basis came from a mix of strategic pricing, revenue management and mix improvement.
In the previous quarter, the company optimized the mileage (MLH) of some key packs based on consumer insights and revenue management principles, delivering a realization improvement.
Management feels confident about the gross margin level reached and intends to operate in the same zone over the medium term.

EBITDA margin expansion of ~500 bps sequentially (Q3 to Q4) attributed to MLH reductions supported by high transaction growth without hurting revenue, plus favorable mix movement between Q3 and Q4, and a higher absolute revenue delivery in Q4 versus Q3 which flows through given the gross-margin-driven cost structure.
No one-off items in the quarter other than the first full-year consolidation of Vishal Personal Care (acquired in Q1 FY26), which has no prior-year base.

subsections.label: Cost inflation and pricing response
points: War in the Gulf created extreme volatility in prices of LLP and packaging material; also delayed price cooling in mustard and copra, which have held at pre-war levels rather than falling further as expected.
Nearly 100% of the cost base is under inflation — some inputs at 50-60% inflation, others at 20-30% inflation.
Company has taken MLH (mileage) adjustments in Q4 that also helped margin, and expects to take some frontal pricing in the current quarter (Q1 FY27) to manage margins.
If hyperinflation eases in Q2/Q3, situation could normalize; if it persists, further fine-tuning of pricing/cost actions will be needed quarter to quarter.
Existing inventory positions cover a good portion of the quarter, buying time to tide over the input cost cycle; impact to consumers expected to remain limited if situation eases in the near term.
Management is monitoring input costs on a nearly daily basis and taking calls as needed; is being cautious about raw material purchases and managing pricing in a narrow band.

subsections.label: Sustainability of margins
points: Management does not give formal guidance but reiterated an aspiration to operate EBITDA margin in the low-20s to mid-20s band over the medium term.

Q4's ~23-25% EBITDA margin came partly from MLH-driven price actions taken before cost inflation (which management noted began hitting only from March) and from revenue outperformance flowing through given the gross-margin-heavy cost structure.

key_figures.label: Vishal Personal Care + Banjara's contribution to total revenue
Value-added hair oil category share held by ADHO
Non-ADHO growth portfolio implied CAGR to reach INR500 crores

subsections.label: ADHO brand performance
points: ADHO delivered a full year revenue growth in the 20s, with growth coming across pack groups and channels.
Company continues to register volume market share gains on ADHO on a quarterly as well as MAT basis.

ADHO is a larger beneficiary of the Aarohan distribution exercise compared to other portfolio brands, seeing benefit across GTM types — urban, wholesale and rural — whereas the rest of the portfolio primarily benefits in retail.

subsections.label: Growth (non-ADHO) portfolio strategy
points: Non-ADHO 'growth portfolio' is already a positive contribution and profitable portfolio.

Company will focus on growing this portfolio to ~INR500 crores over the next three years via a combination of scaling existing brands (Bajaj Coconut, Bajaj Banjara's as the two key brands) and introducing new brands.
The INR500 crores target is for the overall growth portfolio (including coconut), not for coconut alone; South India is a strategic focus for coconut but not the sole strategy.
New product launches are planned this year as part of the growth portfolio push.
The INR500 crores aspiration is based on the current business; any future acquisitions would be a top-up, not included in the target.
Within non-ADHO growth portfolio (~INR225 crores, ex Banjara's INR50-60 crores), the balance is split between coconut and amla, with a large part being coconut.

subsections.label: Banjara's profitability outlook
points: Banjara's still not at full profitability; biggest lever for margin improvement is expected to be scale, as it is still a sub-INR100 crores business — moving to INR100-200 crores size should unlock scale benefits since the categories it operates in are inherently high gross margin.
Banjara's is being run as a separate business unit by conscious choice to drive execution and revenue growth, meaning it is not fully optimized/integrated for cost minimization at this stage.

subsections.label: Channel performance
points: General trade channel saw continued recovery in Q4, growing ahead of other channels, delivering strong teens growth on a full year basis, driven by ADHO momentum and Project Aarohan distribution efforts.
Both urban and rural GT performed well; within urban, retail and wholesale sub-channels did well.
Rural business was muted in H1, revived in Q3, and continued strong performance in Q4; however on a full year basis urban outperformed rural.
Organized trade grew strongly (20s YoY in Q4); within OT, modern trade and e-commerce performed ahead of the channel, while CSD and CPC were muted.
OT crossing 30% of overall sales is viewed as a milestone giving ability and scale to premiumize and innovate faster.
No channel filling / trade inventory buildup observed post GST changes; trade and distributor inventory levels are lean and management is happy with inventory status.

subsections.label: Rural growth drivers
points: Management attributes urban and rural turnaround to direct company actions — fixing advertising on ADHO, strong brand investment, and go-to-market fixes via Project Aarohan — rather than to macro environment shifts or category shift from coconut to perfumed hair oil (being a more premium brand, less exposed to such shifts).

subsections.label: Project Aarohan distribution expansion
points: Aarohan phase 1 covered Delhi, Haryana, Rajasthan, Chhattisgarh.
Entering third phase of Aarohan, expanding into five new states (including Bihar, Gujarat, Jharkhand, Odisha) not covered so far; work started towards end of Q4 FY26, to be executed through FY27.

Aarohan delivers a consistent ~4% growth delta versus non-Aarohan areas across multiple state mixes, models and interventions; some tapering expected as lapping occurs state by state, but management remains confident the delta is sustainable.

subsections.label: International Business (IB)
points: IB had a challenging year overall and declined in Q4.
Key markets Nepal and Bangladesh grew; highlight was Bangladesh reaching breakeven and further margin improvement in Nepal.
Company will continue to grow Nepal and Bangladesh in a profitable and sustainable manner.
Leadership change in IB; renewed efforts to fix Rest of World and MENA markets, with management confident of a turnaround soon.
India remains the company's primary focus market ('bull's eye focus') while some work continues on international business.

subsections.label: Regional market opportunity
points: South India is viewed as an attractive market given very low current penetration and share, offering higher delta opportunity, though other regions (Hindi belt, Maharashtra, Bengal, etc.) also offer growth headroom.
Company aspires to gain market share across all states and channels, with the degree of aspiration varying by state/cluster.

key_figures.label: Quarterly revenue considered as new base estimate

subsections.label: Category outlook
points: Management does not believe hair oil is a sunset sector; it is a mature category with a $2 billion+ market, 20%+ margins, 92% penetration, and continues to grow at high single digits YoY — very few categories in the country combine such high penetration, scale and profitable growth.
Company has high headroom to grow within the category given its current sub-10% market share; priority is to execute and gain more category share, with India as focus market.

key_figures.label: Non-ADHO portfolio remainder after excluding Banjara's estimated contribution

subsections.label: Acquisition integration
points: Vishal Personal Care, acquired in Q1 FY26, is seeing its first year of consolidated revenue contribution; there is no prior year base for comparison.
Bajaj Banjara's is in its first year under Bajaj ownership.

subsections.label: Diversification strategy
points: Company began a journey of diversification to reduce dependence on ADHO, and within GT channel, diversification across channels; management believes both channel and portfolio diversification are in a good place, providing a springboard for future growth.

subsections.label: Input cost volatility
points: War in the Gulf has created extreme volatility in LLP and packaging material prices, and delayed expected price cooling in mustard and copra, which have held at pre-war levels.
Nearly 100% of the cost base is under inflation, with varying degrees (20-30% to 50-60%) across items.
Situation is dynamic and being monitored nearly daily; strategy to be frozen and fine-tuned over subsequent quarters as the situation unfolds over the next month or so.

subsections.label: International business weakness
points: Overall international business had a challenging year and declined in Q4; Rest of World and MENA markets remain weak, requiring renewed leadership focus.

subsections.label: Explicit no-guidance stance
points: Management reiterated multiple times during Q&A that the company does not give formal guidance (on margins, revenue base, or advertising spend as % of revenue going forward), citing volatility in input costs and pricing actions.
Commentary should be interpreted directionally rather than as guidance.

subsections.label: Directional aspirations
points: Company aspires to operate EBITDA margin in the low-20s to mid-20s zone over the medium term, prioritizing revenue enhancement while remaining within this range.

Non-ADHO growth portfolio targeted to reach ~INR500 crores in 3 years (implying ~30s% CAGR), via scaling Coconut and Banjara's plus new brand launches; core ADHO brand aspiration is double-digit revenue CAGR.
Aarohan project to expand into five new states in FY27, targeting to extract the ~4% growth delta benefit already seen in existing Aarohan states.

Advertising investment level (current ~15% of revenue) is viewed as the right level for the brand over a multi-year perspective, and management would want to maintain it, though near-term (quarterly/yearly) trajectory cannot be forecast given cost volatility.
Management expects to take frontal pricing action in the current quarter (Q1 FY27) to manage cost inflation impact.

guidance_ledger.statement: We aspire to maintain margins between the low to the mid 20s.
We will further focus on growing this portfolio to around INR500 crores in size over the next three years.
Our core brands would basically, we've anyways said that if we do around a double-digit revenue CAGR over a period, we'll be happy.

We are getting into the third phase of Aarohan which involves us going to five new states where we had not gone so far... we will work and extract the benefits of the project in those five states through this year.
I think 4% is sustainable. There would be a lap up which will start happening state-by-state there, so that might lead to some tapering.

We believe this level of advertising is the right level of advertising for a brand like ours, and we would want to maintain it. But what will happen next quarter, what will happen next year, I am not in a position to tell you.

guidance_ledger.metric: Margin outlook amid input cost inflation
guidance_ledger.statement: Despite the current situation, we feel confident about our ability to maintain margins in the current approximate range. However, as the situation unfolds over the next month or so, we will freeze our strategy and continue to fine-tune our actions over the subsequent quarters.
We don't give guidances... Where and which is our happy zone, I've already indicated, there's no point doing that again, but guidances we don't give.
I have already given, we will not give margins on basically -- we will give guidance on margins. But what we've repeatedly said, we aspire to maintain margins between the low to the mid 20s.
With the new leadership, we have renewed our efforts behind getting and fixing the markets of Rest of World and MENA, and I'm confident that we will soon be seeing a turnaround in this business.
We will continue to grow the businesses in Nepal and Bangladesh in a profitable and a sustainable manner.
I think in this quarter, I think we will have to take some amount of frontal pricing as well to manage the quarter.

risk_register.risk: Input cost inflation (LLP, packaging material, mustard, copra) driven by the Gulf war
risk_register.note: War in the Gulf created extreme volatility in LLP and packaging prices and delayed expected cooling in mustard and copra, which held at pre-war levels; nearly 100% of the cost base is under inflation.

risk_register.risk: Dynamic/volatile macro situation limiting forward visibility
risk_register.note: Management repeatedly declined to give margin/revenue guidance citing an extremely volatile environment; strategy to be frozen/fine-tuned over coming quarters.

risk_register.risk: International business weakness (Rest of World, MENA)
risk_register.note: Overall IB declined in the quarter and had a challenging year; leadership change made to fix Rest of World and MENA markets.

risk_register.risk: Muted performance in CSD/CPC sub-channels
risk_register.note: Within organized trade, CSD and CPC performance was muted even as modern trade and e-commerce performed well.

risk_register.risk: Category maturity perception (hair oil as 'sunset sector')
risk_register.note: Management pushed back strongly, calling hair oil a mature but not sunset category with $2bn+ size, 20%+ margin and 92% penetration, and highlighting the company's own headroom given <10% share.

themes.label: Margin expansion / turnaround
themes.note: Gross margin up ~650 bps for FY26 to 60%; EBITDA margin recovered to 19.5% full year and 25% in Q4 on mix improvement, MLH-driven pricing actions and revenue outperformance.

themes.label: Input-cost inflation
themes.note: Gulf war-driven volatility in LLP, packaging, mustard and copra prices is pushing nearly 100% of the cost base into inflation, prompting planned frontal pricing action.

themes.label: Portfolio diversification (non-ADHO growth portfolio)
themes.note: Non-ADHO portfolio (Coconut, Banjara's, new brands) delivered INR225 crores in FY26 with an aspiration to reach ~INR500 crores in 3 years.

themes.label: Distribution expansion (Project Aarohan)
themes.note: Aarohan delivers a consistent ~4% growth delta and is entering phase 3, expanding into five new states in FY27.

themes.label: Channel mix shift to organized trade
themes.note: Organized trade now contributes 30% of sales and grew 20s YoY in Q4, driven by modern trade and e-commerce, giving scope to premiumize.

themes.label: International business turnaround
themes.note: Overall IB declined in the quarter, but Nepal and Bangladesh grew with Bangladesh reaching breakeven; leadership change made to fix Rest of World and MENA.

themes.label: No formal guidance stance
themes.note: Management repeatedly declined to provide specific margin/revenue guidance, citing volatility, while reiterating directional aspirations (low-20s to mid-20s EBITDA margin).

key_takeaways: Net revenue of INR1,153 crores at a growth of 21%, first time crossing the INR1,000 crores mark.
Gross margin of 60% and full year EBITDA of INR224 crores at a margin of 19.5%, and full year PAT of INR190 crores at a PAT margin of 16.5%.
Q4 standalone revenue stood at INR308 crores, a growth of 28% year-on-year; consolidated revenue stood at INR327 crores with a growth of 32%.
Gross margin stood at 63% for the quarter and 60% for the full year, registering a significant improvement of around 650 basis points against last year on a full year basis.

EBITDA on a standalone basis for quarter 4 grew by 131% to INR78 crores, translating into an EBITDA margin of 25%; consolidated EBITDA was INR77 crores, a growth of 135%, translating into an EBITDA margin of 23.7%.
Standalone PAT for quarter 4 stood at INR64.1 crores with a margin of 20.8%; consolidated PAT was INR63.6 crores with a margin of 19.5%.
General trade channel grew ahead of other channels and delivered a strong teens growth on a full year basis, driven by ADHO momentum and Project Aarohan.
Organized trade registered a strong 20s growth Y-o-Y in quarter 4, now contributing 30% to overall sales.
International business declined in the quarter overall, but Nepal and Bangladesh grew, with Bangladesh reaching breakeven and Nepal seeing margin improvement.
Non-ADHO 'growth portfolio' delivered revenue of INR225 crores in FY26, with an ambition to grow it to around INR500 crores over the next three years.

Company does not give formal guidance; management reiterated an aspiration to operate EBITDA margin in the low-20s to mid-20s band, with cost inflation and pricing actions expected to be managed quarter to quarter.
pressing_questions: So I wanted to understand if you could give some color, how much is volume? Is volume the main driver behind the 6.7% quarter-on-quarter growth? ... So if you could explain this math?

In the last quarter's conference call, you had mentioned that for now the margins will take a pause at the current levels, which were at around about 18.5%. And then after a few quarters, we will see the journey towards higher margins. Whereas now we have seen in one quarter only the EBITDA margin going up 500 basis points sequentially. So what has changed for the outcome to be so much different versus what your commentary was?

Just wanted to understand, in light of that, what is the sustainable margin that we should take over the next two to three quarters because this 23.2% or 23.4% whatever you have done this quarter is on the back of effective price increases through MLH reductions before the cost inflation has come through?
What percentage of growth improvement should we see from your Project Aarohan initiative in FY27?
Is the hair oil sector is a sort of a sunset sector in the especially in the young generation and urban generation today?
How does one think about the outlook for say next one -- FY27? Should we think somewhere in the band of 19% to 20% or should it could be higher also?

Is it fair to consider this around INR315 crores to INR320 crores to be the new base quarterly? And considering that we have reached this outperformance revenue, as you mentioned, should we expect the sweet spot of margins that you mentioned to continue?

MPHASIS.about: Mphasis a global Information Technology (IT) solutions provider specializing in providing cloud and cognitive services, applies next-generation technology to help enterprises transform businesses globally.(Source : 202003 Annual Report Page No:36)

quarters.summary: Mphasis maintains FY27 guidance of high single-digit to low double-digit constant-currency revenue growth and EBIT margin band of 14.75%-15.75%, with Q2 FY27 positioned to deliver the best sequential constant-currency growth in three years, backed by record pipeline (2.8x since Mphasis.ai launch), AI-led deals at 70% of pipeline, and net new TCV of $461 million (fifth consecutive quarter above $400 million). Operating cash flow conversion is expected to remain at ~80% of net income through FY27, normalizing further from FY28 as large-deal capital investments mature.

subsections.label: Margin drivers
points: Q1 FY27 EBIT margin was down 60 bps, impacted by ramp-up costs of new deal wins and the TAP acquisition costs.

TAP acquisition had a margin impact of about 0.35%; a large portion (two-thirds) of the potential consideration was structured as earn-out flowing through the P&L (not purchase accounting), so this impact will play out over the next couple of years.
The other big margin driver was a steep drop in utilization, taken in anticipation of the growth trajectory being guided to; this drop is expected to reverse as growth materializes.
Company expects normalization over the course of the year as investments start to pay off.
No meaningful one-time transaction costs were incurred for the TAP acquisition since it is not a large ($1 billion) acquisition.

subsections.label: Cash flow and DSO
points: OCF for the quarter was tepid partly due to delayed collection of Q4 debtors; heavy lifting for OCF is expected in Q2-Q4.
Other current liabilities came down because $14 million was paid for contract acquisition costs on large contracts that had been accrued but not yet paid to clients.
Annual FY26 variable pay component typically gets paid out in Q1, contributing to seasonality (as seen in the prior year too).
Company reiterates 80% operating cash flow to net income conversion commentary for FY27.
DSO trend is expected to progressively improve through the remainder of the year.

OCF to PAT conversion (translating to ~50% OCF to EBITDA) is expected to normalize in FY28; FY27 is softer because large deals won required capital investment spread over a 12-18 month period; once these deals stabilize, they generate incremental cash via recovery of the upfront investment, which funds the model going forward — this baseline impact does not incrementally worsen with new similar deals, since unwinding of past deals offsets new ones.

subsections.label: Hedge losses
points: Hedge losses are expected to trend down if currency remains near 95, though it is currently a little higher; cumulative hedge losses (OCI) fell about INR 50 crores between March and June.
It will take a couple of quarters for improvement to substantially reflect in operating margin; hedge losses will improve but not go away fully.

subsections.label: Vendor-consolidation deal accounting and economics
points: Vendor consolidation-led customer contract acquisitions are structured as discrete transactions (not a single multi-part deal); a larger client vendor-consolidation strategy precedes but each transaction is separate.

Disclosure of such deals in notes to accounts is mandatory, driven by acquisition accounting construct even though no entity is taken over; the disclosed PPA is almost entirely customer relationship and customer intangibles, which get amortized.
Typical payout/consideration for such deals is between 1x and 1.2x revenue.

Deal margin profile: typically almost all of the upfront amount is expensed immediately (since it is a deal, not M&A); post-expensing, the deal's profitability is assessed to remain in line with company average (sometimes a little lower, sometimes higher) on a case-by-case basis, and this is not seasonal or back-ended — contracted margin plays out after the initial ~3-month period.

subsections.label: Pipeline traction from Tria launch
points: Within seven weeks of platform launch, multiple opportunities moved from conversation to closure and are now moving to execution — described as 'demand compression'.

ARR and managed services opportunities are being bundled together in Tria deals — a revenue quality signal shifting from point-in-time project revenue toward recurring, platform-attached revenue that leverages 'reuse-ability' within client relationships.
Large deal activity is being influenced by Tria at the evaluation stage, acting as a proof point converting large-deal conversations via governed, measurable outcomes rather than capability alone.

New addressable penetration is being seen at existing clients, opening use cases and budget pools not accessible under the previous service-led model — the attach-rate dynamic central to the platform revenue thesis is beginning to show up.

subsections.label: TCV-to-revenue correlation dynamics
points: The correlation between TTM TCV and revenue fell from >0.9 to 0.74, reflecting a healthy mix of short-burst, early-deployment-led deal wins that get consumed within a quarter or within the next 2 quarters (rather than a longer/steady conversion pattern), which reduces the correlation.
Foundation-building deals typically get done within 12-16 weeks, followed by scale deployment across 6-7 waves — every short-consumption-period deal, regardless of size, pulls the correlation down.

TCV-to-revenue conversion pace has remained steady overall, and backlog strength from prior quarters continues to support in-quarter revenue; deployment-ready nature of the stack is also enabling shorter-cycle deals to close and ramp faster than traditional bespoke delivery.

subsections.label: Solution mix driving pipeline
points: Modernization and Everything-as-a-Platform are driving the strongest pipeline growth, mapping directly to recently launched product lines and platform.
Breadth of growth across verticals, deal sizes, and solution archetypes is revalidating the platform thesis — not a vertical-specific tailwind or a single large deal inflating the picture.

subsections.label: Client pyramid / wallet share expansion
points: On a trailing-twelve-month basis, five clients were added in the $20 million-plus band, reflecting wallet-share expansion and successful ramp of large deals won over recent quarters.
Two new clients added in the $5 million-plus band YoY; one new client added in the $10 million-plus band QoQ; client graduation trend has been consistent over past quarters.
Top 1-10 accounts grew 11.1% YoY; Top 11-30 accounts grew 21.0% YoY — a deliberate outcome of strategy to build the next tier of $100M+ and $50M+ accounts.
On sequential TTM basis, Top 11-30 grew 6.2% while Top 10 grew 1.6%.
Reduction of one client in the $150 million+ band reflects normal TTM ranking dynamics (account moved marginally below threshold on trailing-twelve-month basis while remaining healthy).

subsections.label: Deal wins and TCV
points: Net new TCV was $461 million in Q1 FY27, marking five consecutive quarters of net new TCV above $400 million.
Three large deals closed in Q1, the largest exceeding $100 million.
AI-led deals accounted for 63% of Q1 TCV wins, with AI-led deals now representing 70% of pipeline versus 12% previously — pipeline has grown 2.8x since the Mphasis.ai launch.
Total pipeline grew 8% QoQ and 28% YoY; Non-BFS pipeline grew 18% QoQ; large deals (>$20 million) pipeline grew 10% QoQ; BFS pipeline grew 100% YoY.
Trailing-twelve-month TCV stood at $1.8 billion.
