subsections.label: Service line drivers
points: Enterprise Applications growth (11.9% YoY Direct) was driven predominantly by AI-led modernization deals.
BPO was the standout service line this quarter (up 12.7% QoQ and 14% YoY Direct), driven by healthy pipeline conversion and new deal wins closing in-quarter, led by AI-led propositions.
TMT returned to strong growth (16.4% QoQ, 13.6% YoY constant currency) as recent deal wins ramped up.
Others segment growth (5.2% QoQ) was driven by new deal wins in Retail; Logistics and Transportation reflect some first-order impact from geopolitical challenges.

subsections.label: Vertical commentary
points: BFS growth (9.4% YoY, 0.8% QoQ Direct) reflects a compound quarterly growth rate of over 3.5% across the past eight quarters, the strongest among peers, reflecting depth of domain context and right to win in financial services; BFS is described as stable on the back of eight quarters of structural growth.
Insurance grew a strong 17.8% YoY but declined 3.1% sequentially, following four consecutive quarters of strong growth; expected to be a key growth driver through FY27.

Insurance growth of 35% in FY26 set a strong base; the recent sequential softness reflects certain project milestone completions, not a client impact or a reflection on pipeline/growth potential — no client impact to call out.

Insurance segment cost inched up 18% QoQ due to ramp-up of teams for a transformation program being delivered; normalization expected over the next 2 quarters, with a return to usual margins in that business; this is a conscious investment choice expected to yield further growth.

Logistics is more headwinded given macro and geopolitical environment; it has become a smaller unit, so small number changes drive high percentage variations; more work to be done in Logistics as well as Airlines and Railroads.
Insurance and TMT continue to be expected drivers of growth through the remainder of the year, alongside stable BFS.

subsections.label: Mphasis Tria platform and Enterprise Agency thesis
points: The 'Agency Gap' is defined as the space between what enterprises can do with AI and what they can actually deploy, govern, and hold accountable at scale; every large enterprise now has AI tools but very few have enterprise agency (the ability to make better, faster, governed decisions and convert them into measurable outcomes embedded in the operating model).

Mphasis Modernize™ and Mphasis Optimize™ are connected product motions on the same Mphasis Tria™ platform, not separate offerings: Modernize builds enterprise memory (extracting structured context from systems, rules, workflows, process history); Optimize uses that memory to continuously improve decision loops driving commercial and operational performance — revenue, pricing, demand, supply chain, risk.

The platform converts a one-time transformation engagement into a repeatable, expanding motion — starting with modernization, creating structured enterprise knowledge, then extending into optimization use cases improving revenue, customer experience, and operating performance, compounding value with each deployment.

Agentic AI as shipped by major platform vendors is characterized as a capability, not an outcome; Enterprise Agency is described as governed, explainable, measurable decisioning built into the operating model, not layered on as another tool.

Opportunity Maximization approach is elevating conversations from CIO/CTO level to the business agenda — CFO on revenue cycle performance, Chief Distribution Officer on advisor productivity, COO on operational efficiency.

subsections.label: Model strategy and SLM/token economics
points: No large enterprise will go native/first-party with any single frontier model; enterprises want the ability to plug in and plug out different models due to cost concerns and risk of obsolescence.

Many large clients are experimenting with open source and open weight models (including new models from China referenced from the prior week), which will pressure token costs since cost of tokens varies dramatically by model choice.

Model choice itself is expected to commoditize fairly quickly; the real opportunity lies in helping clients build a stack that can ingest new developments over the next 2-3 years — including SLMs, governance layers, and other capabilities — which map to what Tria fulfills.

subsections.label: Forward Deployed Engineers (FDE) model
points: FDEs are elite engineers engaged to do forward deployment of the platform; in some cases they become experts in Mphasis Tria, in other cases in a client-specific platform variant ('Tria++').
Engagements are not necessarily all onshore, though early engagements require onsite presence in small pods of 3-5 people (sometimes smaller), depending on engagement size.
FDE role: deliver proof of value, then hand over to scale delivery via the onsite-offshore model.

FDE function will not involve large team numbers but commands high billing rates given the elite skill level; however, the real revolution/opportunity is in platform deployment (which drives stickiness and scale capability for managed services), not the FDE profitability itself — described as a 'starter pack that scales'.

subsections.label: Regional performance
points: Americas continued to be the primary growth engine, growing 3.9% QoQ and 11.4% YoY Direct.
ROW delivered a strong sequential recovery (6.1% QoQ constant currency) led by the GCC ecosystem.
EMEA numbers this quarter were impacted by revenue moving to other geographies for a globally structured deal; the underlying health of the EMEA business remains intact.

subsections.label: Competitive positioning
points: Competitive intensity in traditional/renewal deals has gotten more fierce as everyone tries to protect their turf during renewal cycles; management states they are not competing on price.

The competitive model being pursued is bringing an AI deployment that fundamentally reshapes and transforms how clients run operations (IT or business), rather than playing a pricing/productivity-passback game.

Some competitors are forward-forecasting 60-70% productivity gains in outer years from AI without having figured out how to deliver it; management says it is being careful to play to its own strengths rather than get pulled into a pure pricing game.
Price discounting only works with effort-based pricing; outcome-based pricing changes the equation, making discounting less relevant for clients.

subsections.label: Client conversation dynamics / demand environment
points: Enterprise clients are moving from 'inning one' (model/tool adoption, experimentation, efficiency/savings) to harder ROI and governance questions, with a debate on strategy for the 'second innings' of enterprise AI.
Clients are questioning whether current AI deployments can withstand the pace of new frontier-model developments emerging every 3-6 months.

Old-school thinking about discretionary tech spend is expected to change; additional pockets of spend outside traditional tech budgets can be unlocked with a strong business case (e.g., revenue conversion improvement, better underwriting decisions, improved inventory/demand forecasting).

Opportunity Maximization approach aims to go beyond CIO budget conversations to address what an enterprise needs to transform, helping shape the path to becoming an AI-first enterprise — a role traditional consulting environments are seen as falling a bit short in filling.

Traditional long-term annuity run deals are seen as highly susceptible to disruption/passback narratives around productivity; the focus instead is on embedding AI into strategic initiatives and programs.
Most CIOs are transitioning from having a distinct 'AI strategy' to embedding AI at the heart of a broader business strategy.

Company view: macro environment (interest rates, geopolitics, AI disruption fears) is not materially different for Mphasis than for peers; visibility is being driven client-by-client, deal-by-deal, account-by-account rather than by macro prediction.
U.S. is described as the frontier market for adoption of new tech, and the company believes it has found a good sweet spot with early adopters there.

subsections.label: Pricing model evolution
points: Clients' purchasing models are evolving away from purely input/capacity-based pricing toward some form of outcome-based pricing in areas amenable to it; outcome-based pricing is distinct from output-based pricing.
Some deals already priced/constructed under this evolving model showed up in Q1, with more evolution expected going forward.
Company is selling deals combining ARR with managed services components, providing more operating leverage than a traditional pricing model alone.

Gross margin expansion opportunity is expected over the next 2-3 quarters as platform adoption expands and attach rate increases; the extent of reinvestment versus flow-through to P&L remains a call management will continue to make.

key_figures.label: Red Oak deal expected consummation timing

subsections.label: TAP acquisition
points: TAP acquisition (announced third week of April) is now converting, contributing to pipeline transacting; the investments made in FY26 in Tria, the platform operating model, and TAP are converting into FY27 growth.
TAP acquisition costs impacted Q1 FY27 EBIT margin by about 0.35%, with two-thirds of consideration structured as earn-out flowing through the P&L over the next couple of years.

subsections.label: Red Oak / vendor consolidation deal
points: Red Oak consolidation is baked into the FY27 outlook, but consummation has not yet happened; work has not started yet, expected to start around end of August/early September, with assignment of contracts and takeover of employees in progress.

Given the timing, Red Oak will not have a full-quarter impact on Q2; management does not consider the incremental Red Oak contribution large enough to materially change the high single-digit to low double-digit growth guidance range.
Customer consolidation initiative payouts typically range between 1x and 1.2x revenue as consideration.

subsections.label: OKIN transaction
points: OKIN transaction contributed $4 million in Q1 revenue, with total contract value including contingent consideration of $5.5 million.

subsections.label: Category creation - Enterprise Agency
points: Management describes 'Enterprise Agency' as a newly created category, driven by client need for partners who can help solve problems using AI and drive measurable economic outcomes.

subsections.label: Macro and geopolitical risk
points: Macro environment is complex, creating uncertainty and a degree of client caution in committing to programs; interest rate cycle appears to be reversing, with the upcoming Fed meeting seen as highly uncertain.
Company faces the same macro challenges as peers: interest rates, geopolitics, and AI disruption fears.
A potential interest rate shock combined with an oil shock could create broader economic disruption, though this is not predictable and is not embedded in current guidance.

subsections.label: Vertical-specific headwinds
points: Logistics and Transportation reflect first-order impact from geopolitical challenges; the vertical has become a smaller unit, so small changes drive large percentage swings; more work needed in Logistics, Airlines, and Railroads.
Insurance sequential decline follows project milestone completions after a strong FY26 (35% growth) and four consecutive quarters of strong growth; no client-specific impact identified.

subsections.label: AI disruption / obsolescence risk
points: Density of frontier model launches is increasing, raising client concerns about whether current AI deployments will withstand the 'next new' development in 3-6 months.
Explosion in coding assistants gave customers pause about long-term technology choices, illustrating the obsolescence risk of committing to a single model/tool strategy.

subsections.label: Currency / hedge risk
points: Hedge losses are expected to continue but trend down if currency (INR) remains near 95; rupee is currently a little higher than that level.

subsections.label: Outlook narrative
points: Q1 establishes the foundation; investments made in FY26 (Tria, platform operating model, TAP acquisition) are now converting, with pipeline transacting and prior deal wins ramping to revenue.

Q2 is positioned to deliver the best sequential constant-currency growth in three years, supported by the highest pipeline ever carried and the strongest short-cycle deal activity in several quarters.
FY27 guidance of high single-digit to low double-digit constant-currency growth is maintained despite the uncertain macro environment.
EBIT margin band of 14.75%-15.75% is maintained; management frames this as a deliberate platform investment posture rather than defending a floor.

Operating cash flow conversion of ~80% of net income is expected to continue through FY27, with normalization expected from FY28 as large deals won mature and begin generating incremental cash recovery of upfront investment.
Red Oak consolidation deal is baked into the FY27 outlook, though not expected to have a full-quarter impact in Q2 given the expected end-August/early-September start.
Insurance expected to be a key growth driver through FY27; Insurance segment cost/margin normalization expected over the next 2 quarters.
TMT and Insurance expected to continue as growth drivers through the remainder of the year, with BFS remaining stable.

guidance_ledger.statement: We are also maintaining our FY27 guidance: high single-digit to low double-digit growth in constant currency, despite the uncertain macro environment.
Margins remain targeted within the band of 14.75% to 15.75% EBIT; not because we are defending a floor, but because we are making deliberate platform investments while holding financial discipline.

guidance_ledger.metric: OCF to PAT / OCF to EBITDA conversion
guidance_ledger.statement: You should see a normalization of that in FY28. The reason FY27 is softer... is that some of these large deals that we won necessitated certain amount of capital investment... Once that stabilizes, those deals start generating incremental cash.

We have a transformation program that is being delivered for which we had to ramp up the teams, and we expect that normalization to happen over the next 2 quarters. Structurally, I think we'll get back to the margins that we operate in usually in that business.
We expect Insurance to be a key growth driver for us through FY27.
Insurance and TMT continue to be drivers of growth through the remainder of the year as well.
I still expect the hedge losses to trend down... it will take a couple of quarters for it to substantially start reflecting from an operating margin standpoint. It will improve but not go away fully.

guidance_ledger.metric: Gross margin expansion from platform adoption/attach rate
guidance_ledger.statement: We do expect that as the platform adoption expands and the attach rate starts to show up over the next 2 to 3 quarters, we definitely have an opportunity to expand the gross margin.

The Red Oak is baked into our outlook... it will not have possibly the full quarter impact for Q2... if you kind of normalize it for half the year, it may not be as meaningful to kind of look at and it is well within the range that is already kind of baked in.
More work to be done, both in Logistics as well as in Airlines and Railroads, and we'll continue to report on that as we go forward.
We also expect to maintain an operating cash flow to net income conversion ratio of approximately 80%.
We exceeded our initial guidance of 'better-than-industry' growth, delivering more than 2x industry growth while maintaining margins within our target band of 14.75% to 15.75%.
We expect this segment to return to sequential growth in the coming quarters.

You will see continued impact of hedge losses in at least the first half of FY27 and then it will kind of taper down a bit; you will see some of it reflect into lesser hedge losses only in H2 and not in H1.
The Board has recommended a dividend of INR 62 per share for FY26.

risk_register.note: Complex macro environment creates client caution in committing to programs; interest rate cycle reversing with uncertain upcoming Fed meeting; same macro challenges faced by peers.

risk_register.risk: Potential interest rate/oil shock
risk_register.note: An interest rate shock combined with an oil shock could create broader economic disruption, though not predictable and not embedded in guidance.

risk_register.risk: AI disruption / model obsolescence risk
risk_register.note: Increasing density of frontier model launches raises client concerns about whether AI deployments will withstand the 'next new' development in 3-6 months; coding assistant explosion caused customer pause on technology choices.

risk_register.risk: Logistics/Transportation vertical softness
risk_register.note: Reflects first-order impact from geopolitical challenges; vertical has become a smaller unit so small changes drive large percentage swings; more work needed in Logistics, Airlines, Railroads.

risk_register.risk: Insurance sequential decline
risk_register.note: Sequential decline follows project milestone completions after strong FY26 growth (35%) and four consecutive quarters of strong growth; no client-specific impact identified; normalization expected over next 2 quarters.

risk_register.note: Hedge losses expected to trend down if currency stays near 95 (currently a bit higher); cumulative OCI hedge losses fell ~INR50 crores March-June; improvement will take a couple of quarters to reflect in margin and won't fully disappear.

risk_register.risk: Utilization drop from ramp-up ahead of growth
risk_register.note: Steep drop in utilization in Q1 was taken in anticipation of Q2 growth trajectory; expected to reverse as growth materializes.

risk_register.risk: Competitive intensity / pricing pressure in renewal cycles
risk_register.note: Competitive intensity in traditional deals has gotten more fierce as vendors protect turf during renewal cycles; some peers forward-forecasting 60-70% productivity gains without having figured out delivery, risking a pricing race.

risk_register.note: Impacted YoY growth (0.8%) despite healthy QoQ momentum (6.9%).

themes.label: AI-led pipeline & deal conversion

themes.label: BFS/Insurance growth strength
themes.note: BFS delivered >3.5% CQGR over 8 quarters (stable, strongest among peers); Insurance grew 17.8% YoY but declined 3.1% QoQ off a high FY26 base (35% growth) due to milestone completions, not client impact.

themes.label: Margin discipline within target band
themes.note: EBIT margin down 60 bps QoQ on ramp-up costs and TAP acquisition impact (0.35%), but company reiterates 14.75%-15.75% FY27 band and expects gross margin expansion opportunity over next 2-3 quarters as attach rate rises.

themes.label: Working capital / cash conversion reset
themes.note: OCF was tepid this quarter due to delayed Q4 debtor collections and $14M contract acquisition cost payment; OCF-to-PAT (~50% of EBITDA) expected to normalize only in FY28 as large-deal upfront capital investments mature.

themes.label: Decision Intelligence / M&A stack build-out
themes.note: Mphasis Tria platform (Modernize + Optimize) and TAP/Red Oak/OKIN vendor-consolidation acquisitions are converting pipeline into ARR+managed-services deals and expanding the 'Enterprise Agency' platform thesis.

themes.label: Logistics/TMT vertical softness
themes.note: Logistics remains headwinded by geopolitical challenges and has become a smaller unit prone to high percentage swings, while TMT returned to strong growth (16.4% QoQ, 13.6% YoY) on recent deal wins ramping.

themes.label: AI productivity passback vs reinvestment
themes.note: Management is resisting price-based/productivity-passback competition in renewal cycles, instead pursuing outcome-based pricing and platform deployment (Tria/FDE model) to protect margins and differentiate from peers forecasting 60-70% AI productivity gains.

key_takeaways: Q2 is positioned to deliver the best sequential constant currency growth we have delivered in three years.
We are also maintaining our FY27 guidance: high single-digit to low double-digit growth in constant currency, despite the uncertain macro environment.
Margins remain targeted within the band of 14.75% to 15.75% EBIT; not because we are defending a floor, but because we are making deliberate platform investments while holding financial discipline.
Operating cash flow conversion is expected to remain at 80% of net income through FY27 as well.
Since the launch of Mphasis.ai, our pipeline has grown to 2.8 times its original size and reached an all-time high at the end of Q1.
AI-led deals have grown from 12% of pipeline to 70%, where they are now stabilizing.
Net new TCV for Q1 was $461 million - the fifth consecutive quarter above $400 million.
Q1 FY27 revenue came in at $471 million, growing 2.1% sequentially and 8.3% YoY in constant currency terms.
Q1 FY27 EBIT margin was down by 60 bps impacted by ramp up costs of new deal wins and the TAP acquisition costs.
pressing_questions: Just trying to understand how much of those [Insurance and Logistics drag] were something that you didn't really anticipate? And in terms of client conversations, are you sort of sensing incremental caution in any form because we have also sort of late in terms of commentaries picked up some caution even from banks' spending and discretionary and so on?

In terms of the outlook that you have shared for next quarter... there is this consolidation of Red Oak also, which is probably coming up in the next quarter. So how much would that be contributing to the kind of growth in that? And if I remove that also, do you expect the organic... core business... to be as strong as you'd expected?

Can you just give us the margin walk, how much was probably the impact of the earn-out for the acquisition, the currency impact? And given that we are almost at the bottom of our guidance, how can we build the margin trajectory for the remaining part of the year?
The correlation which we give between TTM TCV and revenue... it came down this quarter, which is a bit surprising. Can you help us understand how to read that metric?
The targeted conversion of OCF to PAT... translates to about 50% OCF to EBITDA. And that's roughly like half the industry norm. How long do you expect this to continue?

points: Margins maintained within stated band while investing for growth.

points: OCF was temporarily impacted by ~$17 Mn due to system-related delays in customer remittances; collections realized in early April.
DSO improved by a day; current receivables up but contract assets down as fixed-price milestones got accepted by customers, moving unbilled to receivables.
Contract assets are always included as part of DSO; movement is an internal shift within DSO components, not a new category.
Steep reduction in non-current receivables, partly offset by currency and growth impacts.
Company operated historically at OCF/net income >100%, but pivot to annuity, large deals with year-one savings passed to clients necessitated working-capital investment.
Company has chosen to invest via working capital to drive growth; targeting a discipline floor of 80% OCF/net income conversion going forward.
Other liabilities (linked to contract acquisition cost for large deals) declined in FY26 as payments were made to clients, reflected in OCF.

subsections.label: Pipeline composition and drivers
points: Pipeline growth is broad-based and well-balanced across verticals, deal sizes and solution archetypes.
BFS segment led pipeline growth at 89% increase, complemented by continued expansion across non-BFS sectors.
Healthy distribution across deal sizes: large deals >$20 Mn TCV grew 40%, mid/smaller deals below $20 Mn grew 34%, underscoring pervasive AI-driven demand across enterprise scales.
Modernization and Everything-as-a-Platform (XaaP) archetypes drove the strongest pipeline growth, reflecting early-stage AI-led opportunities as clients re-architect technology and operating models.
Growth driven by NeoIP-led solutions embedded across offerings and the differentiated full-stack AI approach.
Sustained pipeline momentum and deal conversion expected to build on FY26's record TCV performance into FY27.

subsections.label: Service line performance

ITO service line declined YoY reflecting a strategic decision to scale down the non-core ATM business and reallocate toward higher-value, AI-led opportunities.

subsections.label: Vertical performance
points: BFS and Insurance verticals continue to lead growth, driven by strong execution and increasing adoption of AI-led transformation programs.
BFS growth at overall company level was partially moderated by ramp-down of non-strategic ATM business.
Direct BFS full-year growth supported by wallet share expansion in large existing accounts and strong conversion of new wins and new logos.
Insurance momentum reflects increasing traction of AI-driven decisioning use cases across underwriting, claims, and risk operations.

Growth remains broad-based and aligned with expectations, with AI-led transformation increasingly acting as the primary driver across verticals.
BFS momentum: bulk of BFS/Insurance growth driven through in-account action, deal-making and ramping up deals sold heavily in Q1, accelerating growth into H2.
Pipeline shows rapid buildup in BFS even after a strong year, giving confidence to sustain momentum, though rate of growth vs FY26 remains to be seen based on conversion speed.

Logistics vertical stabilized in H2 due to internal churn — adding new customers and winning deals outside of rampdowns; given the vertical's size, one or two large wins could swing growth; gradual recovery expected through FY27.

TMT vertical grew healthy double-digits YoY for FY26, having been a very small business three-four years ago; diversification driven by leadership investments (e.g., new global Insurance business leader appointed, CPG/Retail added via recent acquisition).

subsections.label: Client pyramid
points: Client pyramid continues to strengthen, particularly across middle tiers, reflecting deeper relationships and successful scaling of new wins.
Broad-based expansion driven by consistent wallet share gains in existing accounts combined with disciplined ramp-up of large deal wins.
Top client has outperformed company-average growth for the third consecutive quarter in Q4.

Proactively engaging top clients with AI-led propositions to expand engagements and participate in emerging spend areas such as SDLC transformation, AI infrastructure buildouts, and modernization of foundational technology stacks.

subsections.label: NeoIP platform
points: NeoIP platform accelerates orchestration of modernization, automation, and AI-driven transformation, helping organizations move from experimentation to production.
NeoIP provides foundational layer of context, traceability, and intelligence across data, processes and decisions, ensuring AI outcomes are explainable, trusted and actionable at scale.
Strategy evolving beyond IT-centric transformation toward a stack enabling true business and operational transformation.

McKinsey research cited: nearly 80% of AI-driven transformation will occur outside the IT function, changing the paradigm from IT-led technology transformation to business-function-owned value creation, with IT as enabler providing secure architecture, data foundations, integration frameworks and governance.

AI-driven value being seen in supply chain optimization, revenue growth management, pricing and promotions, demand and inventory planning, underwriting modernization and payments transformation—improving underwriting throughput, reducing fraud, lowering loss ratios, often without replacing core systems.

subsections.label: Continuum AI / Theory and Practice integration
points: Build-out of AI stack significantly accelerated through acquisition of Theory and Practice and its Decision Intelligence platform, Continuum AI.
Continuum AI is a modular, scalable decision intelligence platform for real-time, high-stakes enterprise decision-making across demand forecasting, pricing, marketing and supply chain.

Differentiator: spans descriptive insights to predictive modeling to prescriptive optimization, harmonizing intelligence across functions while preserving complexity of customer behavior and business context.

Leverages causal modeling, optimization and behavioral economics to translate business objectives into actionable intervention strategies; accelerates time to value through prebuilt ML models and reusable model ontologies in revenue optimization, marketing and promotions.
Combines enterprise memory and data foundations with decisioning and execution layers to enable measurable business outcomes.
Onboarded tier-one enterprise clients in CPG and Retail sectors who have validated the platform in production environments.
Onboarded a specialized team of AI practitioners and domain experts to accelerate product roadmap.

NeoSaBa and other assets built out of the XaaP tribe formed part of the foundation for the Neo stack; XaaP pipeline growth linked to platform build-out, not to ERP cannibalization since Mphasis lacks a large ERP practice (more a custom application business).

subsections.label: Delivery model / metrics evolution

Management expects to add new metrics over the next one-two years as legacy metrics (like on-site vs offshore revenue) become less significant amid shift to outcome/milestone-based propositions.

key_takeaways: Q4 reflected a clear acceleration in growth momentum, supported by disciplined execution. We delivered 2.5% sequential and 7.1% YoY growth in constant currency, alongside a strong operating margin of 15.4%.

Our Direct business, now comprising 98.6% of total revenue, grew 9.2% YoY in constant currency. We also delivered strong TCV wins of $407 Mn in the quarter, with a majority driven by AI-led propositions.

Across FY26, our AI-first strategy drove significant pipeline expansion; 38% YoY, with 69% of the pipeline now AI-led. Consistent conversion of this pipeline has resulted in a record net new TCV of $2.12 Bn, representing 68% growth over the prior year.
We also strengthened our client pyramid, adding 4 clients in the $20M+ category; 2 clients in the $50M+ category; 1 client each in the $75M+ and $100M+ categories.
We exceeded our initial guidance of 'better-than-industry' growth, delivering more than 2x industry growth while maintaining margins within our target band of 14.75% to 15.75%.
I am also pleased to share that the Board has recommended a dividend of INR 62 per share for FY26.
Despite ongoing macro uncertainty, we expect to deliver high single-digit to low double-digit growth, supported by disciplined execution and increasing demand for AI-led transformation in FY27.

We remain committed to operating within our target band of 14.75% to 15.75%, while continuing to invest in platforms and capabilities. We also expect to maintain an operating cash flow to net income conversion ratio of approximately 80%.
pressing_questions: So obviously, conversion can be lower. But in that context, when we look forward, you mentioned 80% sort of conversion, if that includes the $16 million, which passed out from last year to this year, which is FY '27. How are you thinking about free cash flow conversion in the near term? And how should we think about that sort of normalizing longer term? In that context also, this contract assets moving to DSO. What should be your ideal DSO?

OCF to profit. We indicated 80%, but if I look your last 10-year average, it's always above 100% kind of number. Now, it is obviously a step different than what we used to operate it. So, if you can provide broad thought process around it, whether the new way of working require relatively weaker cash conversion.

Most of the companies that reported earnings had highlighted deferrals to project starts. And what you are highlighting and what the data is suggesting is contrary to this thesis. So, just trying to understand, was there anything that, you saw differently versus what the peers that saw?

If I look at your margins in this quarter, and if I strip out the hedging losses, which are, of course, temporary, we are probably at multi-year high in terms of EBIT margins, ex-FX... are we looking at increase in investments in FY27 that could have some impact on this given that your growth is also accelerating?

LANDMARK.about: Incorporated in 1998, Landmark Cars Limited is the leading premium automotive retail business in India with dealerships for Mercedes-Benz, Honda, Jeep, Volkswagen, and Renault. The company also caters to the commercial vehicle retail business of Ashok Leyland in India.[1]

quarters.summary: Landmark Cars delivered its best-ever Q1 with pro forma revenue up over 22% YoY and PAT nearly doubling, driven by operating leverage and cost discipline. Management expects a more normalized and consistent demand trajectory through the later part of FY27 after last year's GST-related lumpiness, with Q2-Q4 expected to be normalized quarters (no repeat of last year's traumatic Q2). EV aftersales, new ChargeZone partnership, workshop capacity expansion (Mumbai/Jogeshwari), and OEM-specific momentum (Mercedes, MG, Mahindra, BYD, Kia, Honda) are seen as key growth drivers going forward, alongside continued cost focus and debt reduction from robust cash generation.

subsections.label: Margin drivers
points: Price hikes by OEMs (due to global raw material cost increases) are passed through as a percentage share to dealers, so margin percentage doesn't increase but absolute margin number increases.

New vehicle sales margin improvement driven by market operating price dynamics, one-time benefit of price hikes, demand exceeding supply reducing need for customer freebies, and improving target achievements with OEM brands.

Aftersales margin uptick partly attributable to annual bonus accounting timing (booked in Dec/March quarters, not Q1/Q2), and new ChargeZone charging revenue stream expected to be high-margin/pure profit from commissions.

subsections.label: Why gross profit is not the best lens
points: Newer brands have different margin/cost structures than legacy brands — some may earn 16% aftersales revenue contribution while newly onboarded brands may only have 5-7%, giving lower gross profit but potentially lower prescribed OEM operating costs.
Management believes EBITDA, PAT and cash profit are better metrics than gross profit given the mix complexity across brands and sales/aftersales proportions.
Offered to walk analysts through a spreadsheet explanation in a one-to-one meeting.

subsections.label: Capital allocation & cash generation
points: Company continues to look at OEM-related capital deployment opportunities (new OEM entries, expansions, or takeover opportunities) but will act on its own terms without rushing.
Dividend payout was increased meaningfully last year.
Excess cash flow, with capex on the lower side for now, is expected to keep reducing debt and consequently decrease finance cost — management confirmed this understanding as correct.
Q1 capex spend was less than the proportionate share of the full-year INR50 crore guidance; management could not commit for the rest of the year.

subsections.label: Cost discipline
points: Management reiterated unequivocal commitment to continued cost focus on employee cost and other expenses, expecting these to further decline as a percentage of revenue as revenue grows with newer launches and rising ASP.

Management noted a track record of walking the talk on cost targets (e.g., previously targeted 4% cost reduction and achieved it) and declined to give a specific 2-year efficiency number, promising more granular guidance later.

subsections.label: Mercedes-Benz
points: Continues to be the leading luxury brand in India.
Working on its biggest-ever product offensive with over 40 new models expected to launch globally starting 2027.
Focus on top-end vehicles paying off with strong demand, reflected in rising ASP.

Q1 revenue decline QoQ attributed to seasonality — first 2 quarters of the financial year account for 40% of business, last 2 quarters account for 60%; June quarter is the slowest in the Indian auto industry; last year's base was lower and industry growth accelerated post GST 2.0 from Sept/Oct.

subsections.label: MG Motors
points: Increased EV penetration has positively impacted MG; MG is the second largest EV OEM.
New MG Majestor commenced deliveries last quarter, strengthening premium portfolio.
More models expected across EV and hybrid powertrains; new SUV launching later in August expected to significantly boost volumes.
Received LOI for an additional MG showroom in Ahmedabad.

subsections.label: Mahindra
points: Continues strong momentum; new launches well received with more launches to follow later this year.
New Mahindra workshop starting operations soon in Hyderabad to cater to strong aftersales momentum; capacity in Hyderabad already exhausted.

subsections.label: BYD
points: Continues to perform well; supply expected to significantly improve throughout the rest of the year.
Hybrid models to launch later this financial year.
New outlets in Pune became operational in July, expected to further increase market share.
BYD's luxury brand Denza to launch in India shortly.
Company selling hundreds of BYD vehicles a month, more than anticipated, prompting plans to add more BYD workshop capacity.

subsections.label: Kia
points: Healthy momentum post launch of new Seltos, which received a great response.
Recently launched Syros EV received healthy order bookings across India.
New Sorento expected to launch in September; brand expected to continue good performance throughout the year.

subsections.label: Honda
points: Encouraging improvements supported by City, Amaze and Elevate.
Launch of City Facelift and ZRV strengthens presence across sedan and premium SUV segments.
Alpha 0 electric SUV to launch later this year, timed with broader EV switch.

subsections.label: Ashok Leyland / Commercial Vehicles
points: Commercial vehicle market continues to remain strong, reflected in performance of Ashok Leyland dealerships.

subsections.label: Aftersales mix dynamics
points: New high-growth brands contribute 38% of new car sales but only 19% of aftersales, indicating significant upside potential in aftersales as these brands mature.
Aftersales sales growth outstripping service growth is a mix effect, not a sign of weak service growth — service is growing at its historic 14-15% rate.

EV aftersales revenue per vehicle currently appears higher than ICE (excluding warranty, since battery replacement under warranty would skew numbers), but margins are expected to be similar, not necessarily higher, going forward; management does not expect it to be lower in near term.

subsections.label: Competitive dynamics
points: Audi India getting aggressive via new model launches, targeting market share increase from 8% to 16%.
Management views new competitive entrants as generally expanding the addressable luxury market rather than purely cannibalizing Mercedes share.
Luxury market penetration has reduced over the last year even as overall market grew, contrary to general belief; premium and mass segments have grown faster than luxury segment recently.

subsections.label: Workshop consolidation strategy
points: Workshops vary greatly in size, from 5,000 sq ft to 1 lakh sq ft, so number of workshops alone is not a meaningful comparison metric.
New 50,000 sq ft Jogeshwari (Mumbai) workshop inaugurated to house Mercedes-Benz, BYD and Jeep; company will consolidate smaller workshops into this larger facility, giving up smaller ones.
On paper, total workshop count may appear to reduce or stay flat, but significant capacity is being added at the consolidated location with better margins, better control and lower operating costs.
Management is considering disclosing workshop capacity via number of bays rather than number of workshops, in response to investor feedback.

subsections.label: Capacity utilization approach
points: Company treats asset allocation as fungible across brands and geographies — capacity is shifted between brands at showroom or workshop level based on demand, rather than adding new capacity immediately.
Utilization level varies by location and brand; management declined to give a single utilization percentage figure.
Company has resized/reshaped workshops and showrooms as part of this capacity optimization activity.

subsections.label: Brand-specific capacity needs
points: Mahindra & Mahindra workshop capacity in Hyderabad already exhausted, prompting new workshop opening.
Additional workshop capacity being added for Kia, MG, and especially BYD given rapidly rising BYD volumes.
New BYD outlets in Pune became operational in July 2026.

subsections.label: Outlet classification
points: Company has stopped classifying outlets as "new" — a couple of quarters back it moved all outlets into one bucket rather than carving out newer, less-ramped outlets.
Business nature involves continuously having 2-5 new outlets at any given time; some recently opened outlets (e.g., 2 new BYD outlets in Pune opened ~10 days prior) are not yet at optimal capacity.

subsections.label: ChargeZone partnership
points: MoU signed with ChargeZone, one of India's leading EV charging networks, to build a comprehensive EV ecosystem for customers.
EV customers will receive wallet credit redeemable at ChargeZone charging locations; Landmark will earn a share of charging revenue from onboarded customers.

Described as an industry-first partnership between retailers and a charging service provider, creating an additional recurring revenue stream and deepening engagement with EV customers beyond point of sale.
ChargeZone already works with most major OEMs across mass market, premium and luxury brands, so partnership is not expected to conflict with OEM charging initiatives.
Landmark is onboarding EV customers onto ChargeZone's existing operational network rather than building additional charging capacity itself.
Revenue share is on a recurring, multi-year basis; company declined to disclose specific commercial/unit economics publicly, citing first-of-its-kind exclusivity and desire to avoid being copied.

subsections.label: EV aftersales revenue potential
points: Initial study indicates no negative impact on aftersales revenue from EVs compared to ICE vehicles.
EVs run more on the road due to lower cost of running, increasing frequency of workshop visits for periodic maintenance and accident repairs.
EV accident repairs cost more than ICE vehicles, as seen globally, ensuring higher revenue per vehicle for the full year for EVs currently.

Sophisticated EV technology means EVs come to authorized workshops more often than ICE counterparts, a trend also noted in commentary by Penske, a leading American automotive retailer, in the US market.

subsections.label: OEM expansion / M&A pipeline
points: Company is in talks with some OEMs who may be entering India, some who may want to expand, and some potential takeover opportunities, but will act on its own terms without rushing.

Business platform described as stabilized after a period of rapid expansion ("blood transfusion" into the system) that changed the fiber of the company; metrics are now returning to where they belong.
Awaiting details on recent media reports of a potential deal between JSW Group and Volkswagen India.

subsections.label: Macro and seasonal risks
points: Prior year saw quarterly lumpiness driven by GST-related changes, deferred purchases and subsequent pent-up demand; while largely behind the company, effects were visible.

Management cautions against extrapolating current performance given a "VUCA world" (volatility, uncertainty, complexity, ambiguity), and hopes for absence of macro shocks affecting the FY28 profitability outlook.

Increased competitive intensity from Audi's aggressive market share targeting could theoretically pressure Mercedes-Benz, though management believes new entrants generally expand rather than cannibalize the addressable market.
JSW-Volkswagen potential deal remains an unresolved/unclear external development the company is monitoring.

subsections.label: Profitability outlook
points: Q2 FY27 and subsequent quarters expected to be normalized, without repeat of last year's "traumatic" second quarter disruption.
Cost focus to continue; employee cost and other expenses expected to further decline as a percentage of revenue as revenue grows via newer launches and rising ASP.
Management hopeful (not committed) that FY28 profitability could handsomely cross the peak cycle profits of FY23, subject to no major macro shocks.

subsections.label: Demand outlook
points: Management expects the demand environment to be positive with a more normalized and consistent demand trajectory through the later part of FY27, as last year's GST-related lumpiness dynamics are largely behind the company.

subsections.label: Capital allocation outlook
points: Excess cash flow, combined with lower capex for now, expected to continue reducing debt and consequently decrease finance cost.
Borrowing costs described as stable, with no lenders seeking higher rates.

guidance_ledger.metric: Pro forma EBITDA margin (new car sales)
guidance_ledger.statement: Should we assume that this year, quarter 2 and going forward, quarter 3 and 4 will be a more normalized quarter with like an EBITDA margin of 1.5% on pro forma on new car sales? - Yes, it would be a normalized quarter.
We expect a more normalized and consistent demand trajectory through the later part of the year.
I do not expect any disruption like what we have seen in this second quarter [last year]. Last year second quarter was a traumatic period, and I don't expect that to repeat.

Our capex, which we had guided in the last year closing at around INR50 crores, we are as of now in line. The first quarter, we have spent less than the proportionate share. I can't say for the rest of the year so far.
Excess cash flow will keep on reducing the debt and subsequent decrease in the finance cost. It is right.

guidance_ledger.metric: Employee cost & other expenses (as % of revenue)
guidance_ledger.statement: We believe that this still as a percentage has way to go down... can the cost still go down? Yes, they can.
Is it fair to assume that somewhere in FY28 we should be handsomely crossing the profits which we did in our peak cycle of FY23? - We are on a trajectory which is going to take us there.
Going forward for the entire year, our rental cost or like including the adjustment will be around INR100 crores, INR110 crores - Yes, INR100 crores around.
Cash flow last year, it was 0.95%. We will be around that only.
EBITDA percentage is 5.8%, which is roughly similar to the last 2 years, we are maintaining that percentage. We see further improvement in that percentage.
Let me see if we, over a period of time... whether we can actually give you the number of bays that we have rather than the number of workshops.

guidance_ledger.metric: Aftersales gross profit disclosure by quarter
guidance_ledger.statement: Is it possible to share the breakup of the gross profit quarter-wise in your PPT for aftersales and new car sales - I'll, Abhisar bhai, take this back with me. We will see what we can do.
The number of cars and the critical mass and the capacity being reached, this will reach [match new car sales mix], sooner rather than later.
The supply for BYD will significantly improve throughout the rest of the year.

guidance_ledger.metric: MG new SUV launch volume boost
guidance_ledger.statement: A new SUV, which is to be launched later this month in August, and we expect that to significantly boost volumes.
We expect the brand to continue its good performance throughout the year.
The expansion that we see for the current year, two, three years is a very long time... the extra rapid growth that we saw 18 months back in one shot, I don't think that we are looking at this year.

This is the year where we want to get the profits back and we have been continuously working on all the metrics very diligently... we will have profitable growth continue to happen and you will see it this year.
We have a 10-year track record... I believe that what we have done on a consistent basis is what one should look at and not overtly look at this margin continuing. We will strive to do that.

Over a period of time, it will keep on increasing. I cannot comment on the pace or the timing of this increase... because of where our currency is and the inflation is, things will keep on increasing.
That's the endeavor. That's what I said at the beginning of the call, that this year is where we are trying to strive to get all of our metrices to where they belong.

So far, we have had no discussion with any OEM about renegotiating our margins as such. So, if the prices go up, we tend to make more money per unit... but one will have to wait and watch how that kind of pans out.
India will also...the product onslaught for them in India will begin possibly from next year... we do expect that the large number of them will make their way to India.
We expect BYD to continue its strong performance this year and substantially grow its volumes... this should be a much better year for BYD.
Unless something happens on a macro basis, which is beyond our control, we are well poised for better results... we are keeping our fingers crossed for a much better year.

risk_register.note: Corresponding period last year saw lumpiness from GST-related changes, deferred purchases and pent-up demand; largely behind the company now.

risk_register.risk: Seasonality of automotive demand
risk_register.note: First 2 quarters of financial year are 40% of business, last 2 quarters are 60%; April-June is the slowest quarter industry-wide.

risk_register.risk: Macro/VUCA uncertainty affecting FY28 profitability trajectory
risk_register.note: Management flagged living in a 'VUCA world' and hopes no macro shocks occur to derail the trajectory toward FY28 targets.

risk_register.risk: Increased competitive intensity in luxury segment (Audi)
risk_register.note: Audi India targeting market share increase from 8% to 16% via aggressive new model launches; management believes this expands rather than cannibalizes the market.

risk_register.risk: Uncertainty around potential JSW-Volkswagen India deal
risk_register.note: Awaiting details of recent media reports of a potential deal between JSW Group and Volkswagen India.

risk_register.risk: EV component/battery warranty cost uncertainty
risk_register.note: Warranty-related costs (e.g., battery replacement) excluded from aftersales revenue/margin analysis due to high value and evolving nature; management taking a cautious stance as EV aftersales economics are 'just unfolding'.

risk_register.risk: Brand-specific margin/cost structure complexity
risk_register.note: Newer brands have different margin, cost, manpower and infrastructure requirements versus legacy brands, complicating gross margin comparability quarter-on-quarter.

risk_register.risk: Foreign exchange fluctuations and global supply challenges leading to OEM price increases
risk_register.note: Most OEMs increased prices in April with another increase expected in June, partly due to FOREX and global supply challenges.

risk_register.risk: Geopolitical tensions ('war') and associated macro uncertainty
risk_register.note: Management noted resilience of demand so far despite ongoing geopolitical tensions, but flagged hesitancy in commercial vehicles in the last 8-10 days and supply challenges at one or two OEMs.

risk_register.risk: EV transition reducing after-sales revenue
risk_register.note: Global studies (Goldman Sachs) suggest a 12-14% potential after-sales revenue impact from EV penetration versus ICE, though management believes impact in after-sales will be marginal, not material.

risk_register.risk: OEM margin renegotiation risk
risk_register.note: No OEM has approached Landmark to renegotiate dealer margins yet despite OEM-side raw material/margin pressure; outcome uncertain going forward.

risk_register.risk: BYD supply/quota constraints
risk_register.note: BYD ran out of quota for non-homologated car imports in the prior quarter, impacting sales; resolved with new year's quota allocation, and most cars sold now fall outside the quota system.

risk_register.risk: Seasonality in auto industry
risk_register.note: The auto industry sees generally better sales in the last two quarters of the year, a factor to be kept in mind when assessing full-year performance.

risk_register.risk: Store-level profitability / written-down investment risk
risk_register.note: Company continuously evaluates portfolio and store-level profitability, closing unprofitable locations (e.g., a Volkswagen outlet) while being mindful of investments made and written-down asset value.

themes.label: EV portfolio strength
themes.note: 30% of vehicles sold by value are EVs; EV aftersales revenue per vehicle currently higher than ICE due to higher usage and repair costs, with no negative impact on aftersales business.

themes.label: After-sales scale-up
themes.note: New high-growth brands contribute 38% of new car sales but only 19% of aftersales, indicating significant untapped upside as capacity and critical mass build up; ChargeZone partnership adds a new recurring revenue stream.

themes.label: Margin & cost discipline
themes.note: New vehicle sales margins improved from 1.7% (FY25) to 2.3% currently; management reiterated commitment to further reducing employee cost and other expenses as % of revenue.

themes.label: OEM price hikes & FOREX
themes.note: OEMs including Mercedes-Benz have taken price hikes due to global raw material costs; dealer margin percentage doesn't rise but absolute margin does; ~3% of Q1 revenue growth attributed to price increases.

themes.label: BYD supply/homologation dynamics
themes.note: BYD supply expected to significantly improve through the rest of the year; new Pune outlets operational; hybrid models and Denza luxury brand to launch, driving need for added workshop capacity.

themes.label: Debt reduction & cash generation
themes.note: Robust operating cash flow (INR60 crore in Q1) combined with lower capex is expected to continue reducing debt and finance costs; borrowing costs remain stable.

themes.label: Consolidation over expansion
themes.note: Company stopped classifying outlets as 'new'; focus is shifting to consolidating smaller workshops into larger, more capacity-efficient facilities (e.g., Jogeshwari) rather than rapid outlet expansion.

key_takeaways: Our financial year '27 started on a strong note with pro forma revenue from operations growing at over 22% year-on-year to deliver our best ever Q1 performance in a seasonally soft quarter.
Profit after tax nearly doubled ahead of the revenue growth.
30% of the vehicles sold by value have been EVs at Landmark, much, much higher than the industry.
The initial study indicates that there is absolutely no negative impact on aftersales revenue from EVs as compared to ICE vehicles.
We have signed an MoU with ChargeZone, one of India's leading EV charging networks... This is an industry-first partnership between retailers and the charging service provider.
We believe that the way to look at our business may be better at EBITDA and PAT level along with cash profit from business rather than the gross profit level.
Looking ahead, we expect the demand environment to be positive... we expect a more normalized and consistent demand trajectory through the later part of the year.
Today, we are inaugurating a large 50,000 square foot workshop in Mumbai to cater to Mercedes-Benz, BYD and Jeep.
pressing_questions: So from 2 to 3-year perspective, how should one look at it given that we are generating now strong cash flows... are there any white spaces which we may tap into maybe probably the OEM additions or further outlet or workshop additions?
From an overall profitability perspective, is it fair to assume that somewhere in FY28 we should be handsomely crossing the profits which we did in our peak cycle of FY23?
Now that we have enough showroom penetration, the focus incrementally will be on workshops... is it fair to assume that over the next 2, 3 years, the mix of showroom and workshop can be 50-50?

Is it fair to assume that given the higher contribution of EV, this aftersales contribution will also grow much, much faster and possibly it will match your new car sales mix maybe sooner rather than later?

Can you like explain like kind of in unit economics how this new [ChargeZone] partnership is going to help us? ... How much units does a car usually consume and what kind of revenue share are we looking at from this segment?
Is it possible to share the breakup of the gross profit quarter-wise in your PPT for aftersales and new car sales so that we at least get the trend?
Internally, what's your target of converting EBITDA to CFO? Is there any particular target?

quarters.summary: FY26 closed with 20% YoY topline growth (ahead of 13% industry growth), highest-ever turnover, gross profit and EBITDA, and a 758% YoY jump in Q4 PAT; management is entering a "consolidation" phase in FY27, prioritizing profitability and cash generation over rapid store expansion, with CAPEX guided at a historical ballpark of ~INR 50 crore and continued debt reduction expected, while flagging seasonality and macro/FOREX-driven OEM price hikes as key swing factors.

subsections.label: Margin drivers
points: EBITDA growth (30% YoY) outpaced revenue growth, reflecting continuous cost optimization and efficiency measures undertaken.
Employee costs and other operating expenses were within the set internal benchmark at 4% of proforma revenue.
The exceptional item for Q4 includes expenses written-off in relation to outlet closures and relocations.
The exceptional item for the year includes a gratuity provision due to the new Labor Code and expenses written-off in relation to outlet closure and relocation.
Standalone business profitability (largely Mercedes-driven) should be viewed on an annual rather than quarterly basis, as OEM target bonuses sometimes get pushed to one or another quarter.

subsections.label: Cash flow & capital allocation
points: Company generated net operating cash flow of INR 267 crore (approx., actual INR 267.5 crore) in FY26 and continues to prioritize cash generation in operations.
Board approved a dividend of INR 1.5 per share for FY26 (subject to shareholder approval), up from INR 0.50 paid last year.

Interest-bearing debt reduced by INR 27 crore in FY26; company expects to generate good cash flow in the coming year, which should further reduce debt, though expansion could require additional long-term capital/debt.
No large CAPEX planned for FY27; historic average CAPEX (pre rapid-expansion phase) was around INR 50 crore, which could serve as a ballpark, though management did not commit to a firm number.

subsections.label: Pricing/inventory-linked margin benefit
points: When OEMs raise prices, Landmark can sell existing held inventory at the new higher MRP, generating a one-time gain only on stock held at the time of the price hike, not on future purchases.
This also results in a marginal (not material) increase in absolute margin per unit since the margin percentage applies on a slightly higher base price.
No OEM has approached Landmark about renegotiating dealer margins despite raw-material/margin pressure; higher OEM prices generally translate to more absolute margin per unit for Landmark.

subsections.label: After-sales business performance
points: After-sales business crossed the milestone of INR 1,000 crores in annual revenue, placing Landmark among a select group of Indian companies across industries achieving such scale in after-sales.

After-sales margin had fallen below 18% (the 10-year average) in a prior quarter but has now recovered; management cautions not to overtly extrapolate the current strong margin quarter-on-quarter but to look at the consistent multi-year trajectory.
Focus is on sweating assets more and raising ASP (both for car sales and car service) as that is where the maximum profit can come.
Sharp Q4 rise in after-sales realization (to INR 30,072 per service) driven by OEM bonuses for meeting quarterly/annual targets plus rising spare part prices (due to metal prices and FOREX).

subsections.label: EV vs ICE servicing economics
points: Currently ~47% of service income comes from accident repairs, largely covered by insurance companies.

Global studies show EV accident repair costs are higher than ICE (battery replacement is costlier and parts more expensive), so after-sales revenue impact from EV penetration is not materially negative, though there is some marginal impact.

Goldman Sachs report (published a few years back) estimated a 12-14% revenue drop in after-sales from EVs vs ICE, as accident repair remains constant while other value-added services (polishing, interior cleaning, tires, seats, brakes) also remain constant; management notes India outcomes remain to be seen.

subsections.label: OEM-wise business updates
points: Mercedes-Benz launched the all-new V-Class (~INR 1.4 crore) and new electric CLA (~INR 55 lakh), both opening to strong demand with waiting periods stretching a few months; deliveries started this quarter. New S-Class launching in June will be Mercedes' first plug-in hybrid product in India.

Mercedes has retained/maintained #1 position for 11 years and has been consistently increasing top-end vehicle penetration, growing value-wise even as it focuses on per-car realization over pure volume numbers.

Mercedes is at the beginning of a new global product life cycle, driving the announced 40 new global product launches over the next few years; India onslaught for these expected to begin possibly from next year, though not all 40 models are expected to reach India as some are market-specific.

BYD models Sealion 7, Atto 3 and eMAX have been homologated for India; supplies started arriving from April; hybrid vehicles from BYD expected later this year. BYD's Q4 sales challenges were due to running out of quota for non-homologated cars, resolved with a new year's quota; most BYD cars sold are outside the quota system, positioning FY27 as a much better year for BYD.
Kia's New Generation Seltos has strengthened demand with an approximate two-month wait time; more product launches planned this year.
Renault Duster deliveries commenced mid-April with positive response; hybrid variant expected during the festive period; first of multiple new Renault launches expected in India.

Honda announced a comeback strategy backed by 10 upcoming product launches; recently launched new City, and announced ZR-V Hybrid SUV and Alpha Electric SUV launches; Landmark continues to be Honda's largest partner in India.
Stellantis/Jeep announced a new Jeep SUV developed in India in collaboration with Tata Motors, to be developed domestically and exported.

JSW MG Motors had a strong year with MG Windsor as the highest-selling EV model in India; plans to introduce three new models (EV, hybrid, ICE) this year, starting with the Majestor delivering this month. MG Select (premium brand) had a positive first year and plans one more model launch this year.
Mahindra & Mahindra continues strong momentum with stabilized sales/service outlets.

Volkswagen: one unprofitable Gujarat location was closed after continuous evaluation of store-level profitability and no near-term outlook for profitability; Landmark remains Volkswagen's only dealer in Gujarat at profitable locations, with future outlet decisions based on demand/supply and mindful of investment written-down value.

subsections.label: Facility openings/ramp-ups
points: Pune Sales and Service outlets for BYD will be operational in July, expected to further increase market share for BYD in the country.
Hyderabad workshop (operationalized in March) has stabilized and is ramping up as expected.
New after-sales facility in Hyderabad for Mahindra is likely to start operations in July, driven by strong after-sales momentum.

Company has built significant capacity over the last 18 months across brands and geographies and is now entering a consolidation phase to optimize operations and sweat existing assets rather than pursue rapid expansion.

key_figures.label: Mercedes-Benz consecutive years as number one luxury OEM in India

subsections.label: Store footprint changes
points: A specific unprofitable Volkswagen location was closed after continuous store-level profitability evaluation; no rumor confirmed beyond this specific closure.
Landmark remains Volkswagen's only dealer in the state of Gujarat, at profitable locations.
Future outlet numbers will be decided based on demand and supply dynamics.

subsections.label: Inventory management
points: Landmark had consciously reduced inventory days down to around 30 days (from 36 days two quarters back), but in March, anticipating price hikes and possible supply chain disruption due to macro events (tariff war), consciously chose not to go below the ~30-day mark and built inventory up slightly.
Management does not intend to build further inventory; expects to remain in and around current levels, and to return to the earlier ~30 days or lower once the current price-hike-driven stock is sold.
Higher inventory allows Landmark to leverage pricing advantage (selling at new higher MRP), ensure better availability for customers, and continue benefiting from healthy retail demand.

subsections.label: BYD import route
points: BYD models are currently imported via the CBU route; Landmark is hoping/waiting for a shift to the CKD route over time.
Currently there is a cap of 2,500 units under CBU import without homologation; this cap does not apply once a vehicle model is homologated (after paying duty).

subsections.label: AI/technology adoption in operations
points: Company has started utilizing AI-based calling in its call centres and plans to expand to more AI use cases over time to improve efficiency, optimize costs, and enhance customer experience.
