subsections.label: Demand drivers
points: GST 2.0 rationalization played a critical role in stimulating demand by reducing ownership cost and attracting previously undecided customers.
SUVs continue to dominate customer preferences and remain a standout category during the year.

India is the third-largest passenger car market globally (behind China and US), offering a long growth runway; most partner OEMs and global automotive players are increasingly positioning India at the center of their growth strategy (citing Honda, Renault, Jeep announcements).
India's auto retail is entering FY27 on strong momentum; with current fuel prices, management believes EV penetration will significantly rise.

Landmark's EV sales contribution (21%+) is well ahead of overall India EV penetration (~5%), reflecting its bet on OEMs focusing on EVs paying off; BYD, Mahindra & Mahindra and MG Motors are leaders in their EV segments.

Despite macro 'war' events and OEM price hikes, demand has remained resilient so far — a positive surprise for management — except some hesitancy in commercial vehicles in the last 8-10 days and some supply challenges at one or two OEMs.
Nearly all OEMs (Mahindra, Honda, MG, MG Select, Mercedes) have taken or announced price increases; hard to quantify but essentially all have raised prices, driven partly by FOREX.

subsections.label: Dealership market opportunity/TAM
points: Largest auto dealership groups in China and the US contribute only about 2-2.5% of entire auto sales in those markets; Landmark is not even halfway to that share, indicating a large runway for growth via dealership setup/acquisition regardless of overall industry growth.
Company aims to demonstrate that it can now combine growth with profitability, having already demonstrated it can achieve growth in the last two years.

subsections.label: Corporate structure clarification
points: In response to a query about a promoter reclassifying to non-promoter category, management clarified there was a family separation that had happened previously, and the individual in question was not holding any shares as a promoter.

key_figures.label: Time period referenced for outlet ramp-up demonstration
Duration of hard work reiterated by management for consolidation year

subsections.label: Consolidation strategy
points: After significant investments in expansion across brands and geographies over the last two years, Landmark is entering a consolidation phase emphasizing optimizing operations and sweating existing assets rather than rapid new expansion.

Company aims to templatize its rapid growth approach and demonstrate that it can achieve profit recovery in the way it historically has, with the current year being one where teams are highly focused on cost.

Growth will continue but not at the extra-rapid pace seen 18 months back; growth this year will come from already-committed initiatives (Pune BYD outlet, Mahindra workshop) plus one or two other items in the pipeline, rather than large new rapid expansion.
Long-term (two-three-year) goal is to grow the company to a significantly larger scale profitably.

subsections.label: Macro and geopolitical factors
points: Foreign exchange fluctuations and global supply challenges have led most OEMs to increase prices in April, with another price increase expected in June.
Ongoing geopolitical tensions ('war') have driven price hikes and raised fears of supply chain disruption, prompting Landmark's inventory build-up decision.
Commercial vehicle segment has seen some hesitancy in demand in the last 8-10 days, alongside supply challenges at one or two OEMs.

subsections.label: EV transition impact on after-sales
points: EV penetration could marginally reduce after-sales revenue per global studies (Goldman Sachs report cited 12-14% potential revenue impact), though management believes the impact is not material given constant accident-repair and value-added service revenue streams.

subsections.label: OEM/dealer margin risk
points: No OEM has yet approached Landmark to renegotiate dealer margins despite OEM-side raw material and margin pressure; management flags uncertainty on how this may evolve ('one will have to wait and watch').

subsections.label: BYD supply/quota risk
points: BYD faced inventory/supply issues in the prior quarter due to running out of quota for non-homologated car imports, impacting sales; resolved with new year's quota allocation.

key_figures.label: Return on capital employed target for after-sales business

subsections.label: Outlook commentary
points: Management expects continued profitable growth this year, focused on getting profit metrics back to historic levels as newly opened outlets stabilize.

Expansion pace for FY27 (and next two-three years) will be far more measured than the rapid growth of the last 18 months; growth will continue via already-committed projects (Pune, BYD, Mahindra workshop) and one or two pipeline items.
No large CAPEX planned for FY27; historic average CAPEX pre-rapid-expansion was around INR 50 crore, offered as a ballpark without being a firm commitment.
Debt is expected to reduce further given anticipated good operating cash flow generation in the coming year, though expansion could necessitate additional long-term debt/capital.

Management is confident in near-term profitability across almost all of its portfolio, citing FY26 as a positive base, while flagging that industry seasonality (last two quarters generally stronger) and macro factors beyond its control remain key swing variables.
Mercedes' 40 new global model launch program is expected to bring a large (but unspecified) number of models to India, with India-specific onslaught likely starting next year.

guidance_ledger.statement: We do not have a very large CAPEX in mind for this year. Historically... our historic average is around INR 50 crores. That could be taken as a ballpark, but I am not trying to stick my neck out with numbers.
The expansion that we see for the current year, two, three years is a very long time... the extra rapid growth that we saw 18 months back in one shot, I don't think that we are looking at this year.

This is the year where we want to get the profits back and we have been continuously working on all the metrics very diligently... we will have profitable growth continue to happen and you will see it this year.
We have a 10-year track record... I believe that what we have done on a consistent basis is what one should look at and not overtly look at this margin continuing. We will strive to do that.

We generated INR 267 crore operating cash flow... we are likely to generate good cash flow in the coming year as well. So, our debt is going to reduce. Only thing is if we expand, then there might be some uses of the debt.

Over a period of time, it will keep on increasing. I cannot comment on the pace or the timing of this increase... because of where our currency is and the inflation is, things will keep on increasing.
That's the endeavor. That's what I said at the beginning of the call, that this year is where we are trying to strive to get all of our metrices to where they belong.

So far, we have had no discussion with any OEM about renegotiating our margins as such. So, if the prices go up, we tend to make more money per unit... but one will have to wait and watch how that kind of pans out.
India will also...the product onslaught for them in India will begin possibly from next year... we do expect that the large number of them will make their way to India.
We expect BYD to continue its strong performance this year and substantially grow its volumes... this should be a much better year for BYD.
Unless something happens on a macro basis, which is beyond our control, we are well poised for better results... we are keeping our fingers crossed for a much better year.

risk_register.risk: Foreign exchange fluctuations and global supply challenges leading to OEM price increases
risk_register.note: Most OEMs increased prices in April with another increase expected in June, partly due to FOREX and global supply challenges.

risk_register.risk: Geopolitical tensions ('war') and associated macro uncertainty
risk_register.note: Management noted resilience of demand so far despite ongoing geopolitical tensions, but flagged hesitancy in commercial vehicles in the last 8-10 days and supply challenges at one or two OEMs.

risk_register.risk: EV transition reducing after-sales revenue
risk_register.note: Global studies (Goldman Sachs) suggest a 12-14% potential after-sales revenue impact from EV penetration versus ICE, though management believes impact in after-sales will be marginal, not material.

risk_register.risk: OEM margin renegotiation risk
risk_register.note: No OEM has approached Landmark to renegotiate dealer margins yet despite OEM-side raw material/margin pressure; outcome uncertain going forward.

risk_register.risk: BYD supply/quota constraints
risk_register.note: BYD ran out of quota for non-homologated car imports in the prior quarter, impacting sales; resolved with new year's quota allocation, and most cars sold now fall outside the quota system.

risk_register.risk: Seasonality in auto industry
risk_register.note: The auto industry sees generally better sales in the last two quarters of the year, a factor to be kept in mind when assessing full-year performance.

risk_register.risk: Store-level profitability / written-down investment risk
risk_register.note: Company continuously evaluates portfolio and store-level profitability, closing unprofitable locations (e.g., a Volkswagen outlet) while being mindful of investments made and written-down asset value.

themes.label: Consolidation over expansion
themes.note: After 18 months of rapid capacity build-up across brands and geographies, FY27 is framed as a year of consolidation focused on sweating existing assets and restoring profitability rather than rapid new store growth.

themes.label: EV portfolio strength
themes.note: Landmark's EV sales contribution (21%+) far exceeds India's overall EV penetration (~5%), driven by strong positioning with BYD, Mahindra and MG.

themes.label: OEM price hikes & FOREX
themes.note: FOREX and global supply challenges are driving OEM price increases (April, with more expected in June), which raises ASP and gives Landmark a one-time inventory margin gain but also creates demand uncertainty.

themes.label: After-sales scale-up
themes.note: After-sales business crossed INR 1,000 crore annual revenue milestone, with realizations rising on OEM bonuses and spare-part price increases.

themes.label: Margin & cost discipline
themes.note: Highest-ever annual EBITDA (INR 283 crore, 5.8% margin) and 758% YoY Q4 PAT growth reflect continuous cost optimization outpacing revenue growth.

themes.label: BYD supply/homologation dynamics
themes.note: BYD supply resumed from April after prior-quarter quota exhaustion; new models homologated and Pune outlet opening in July should support volume growth.

themes.label: Debt reduction & cash generation
themes.note: Interest-bearing debt reduced by INR 27 crore in FY26 on strong operating cash flow (INR 267 crore); further reduction expected in FY27 absent major expansion-led borrowing.

key_takeaways: Financial year 2026 has been a good year for us, marked by multiple milestones and encouraging performance across key segments. On an annual basis, we delivered 20% year-on-year top-line growth, ahead of the industry growth of 13%.
One of the achievements we were particularly proud of is the performance of our after-sales business that crossed the milestone of INR 1,000 crores in annual revenue.
After a slow first half, Financial Year 2026 closed with 47 lakh passenger vehicles that were sold. This marks a 13% year-on-year growth.
For Landmark, EVs contribute to over 21% of its sales... India's EV penetration in passenger cars is more or less 5%.
We are now entering a more consolidation phase where the emphasis is on optimizing operations and sweating our existing assets.
For Financial Year 2026, we have made the highest ever turnover, gross profit and EBITDA.
The company reported its highest-ever annual EBITDA of INR 283 crore, with an EBITDA margin of 5.8% and continues to maintain cost discipline.
Profit after tax stood at INR 38 crore, marking 120% year-on-year growth.
Additionally, the Board of Directors approved a dividend of INR 1.5 per share for FY26 subject to shareholder approval as against INR 0.50 paid out last year.
pressing_questions: How do we see profitability going forward — gross margins and EBITDA margins — and do we see the pace of store expansion coming off drastically over the next two, three years?
How do we see the after-sales business margin sustainability given the record 20%+ margin this quarter with only ~5% volume growth?
What would be the CAPEX guidance for FY27?
How is the car servicing frequency and cost for EV versus ICE, and how do you see servicing revenues scaling with rising EV penetration in the portfolio?
Do you expect demand to weaken as OEMs take price hikes — can you give color on premium, mid-end and EV segments?
Among OEM partners, who has taken the most price increase, and who hasn't?
On inventory buildup — is this purely supply chain management, or can the company capture a benefit from price hikes?
On BYD homologated models — will these come via the CKD route?
Any particular reason for the sharp increase in after-sales revenue per vehicle service (Q-on-Q and Y-on-Y)?
What is the capital employed in the after-sales business, and can ROC return to a double-digit trajectory given recent garage expansion?
Is it true that Mercedes is planning a record number of new launches in India over the next year or two?
Is it true that Volkswagen has stopped some stores from Landmark?
Given macro/raw material pressure at OEMs, is there any renegotiation of dealer margins underway?
Do you expect ASP per vehicle to keep increasing, and how does that flow through to EBITDA per vehicle?
Regarding BYD inventory issues seen on VAHAN in Q4 — will there be no further inventory issues going forward?
How do you really benefit from an ASP increase — is it cost, margin, or something else — and did the GST reduction impact margins?
VAHAN data shows BYD sales growing but Mercedes sales flat/declining — how is Landmark's performance tied to these OEMs, and is market share being maintained?
One of the promoters has indicated he wants to be reclassified as non-promoter — who is that, and how many shares does he hold?
How do you plan to reduce debt going forward, given debt was already lowered this year?

HINDUNILVR.about: Hindustan Unilever is in the FMCG business comprising primarily of Home Care, Beauty & Personal Care and Foods & Refreshment segments. The Company has manufacturing facilities across the country and sells primarily in India.[1]

quarters.summary: Capital Markets Day 2026: Management reset strategy around "Winning in New India," targeting competitive, volume-led growth after two years of muted growth. Guidance: no numerical earnings growth target given, but reiterated FY27 will be better than FY26, with focus on competitive volume-led revenue and profit growth. EBITDA margin range revised to 22-24% (upper end raised from 23.5% to 24%) to allow investment ahead of growth, targeting ~500bps margin expansion ("Fuel for growth") over 5 years via premium mix, operating leverage, Future Savings Lab, and AI-led media effectiveness. Capex guidance raised from ~2% to ~3% of turnover to power growth and savings, with 85-90% directed to growth/savings programs.

subsections.label: Material announcements / quantification

Fuel for growth target: ~500 bps over 5 years, from four levers: premium mix (margin accretive portfolio planned to grow 1.5x the rest); operating leverage (fixed costs to grow at 0.7-0.8x topline growth); Future Savings Lab (multi-year savings program to add ~100 bps savings over 5 years); AI-led media effectiveness (at least ~10% improvement).

'Desirable brands' enable pricing power ('stretch the brand premium pricing power').

Deployment: higher productive capex (growth + savings); portfolio shaping (brand extensions, bringing global brands, bolt-on M&A); continue top-quartile dividend payout ratio (claimed).

12m+ positively impacted via Prabhat program.
Board-level sustainability oversight; ESG embedded in KPI framework.

CFO: GDP print 7.8%; demand 'stable'; CPI ~5% not 'destroying consumption.'
Margin range widening not attributed to inflation, but flexibility for investment ahead of growth.

subsections.label: What changed vs prior CMD / why confidence now

CFO pointed to sequential growth step-up in last four quarters: 'three, five, seven, and ten' (implied acceleration trend).

subsections.label: Executive incentives / ESOPs
points: Priya clarified ESOP split is aligned to ownership: 62% Unilever / 38% HUL, and annual bonus is 100% linked to India performance (top line, bottom line, cash): 'zero bonus if HUL does not perform.'

subsections.label: Vector 1: Consumption-led growth
points: Management tied consumption expansion to rising affluence and infrastructure (tap water/LPG) with category-specific evidence of consumption differences between affluent and value seekers: laundry 1.2x, soaps 1.3x, tea 1.5x, shampoo 1.7x.
Dishwash example: Thailand per-capita dishwash is 3.5x India, driven by more utensils/variety as affluence rises.
HUL argues it is best placed to capture consumption given brand strength + distribution (e.g., Vim: "number one brand power… 90% value-weighted distribution").

subsections.label: Vector 2: Premiumization inflection
points: India's premiumizers (60-65% of population per management) are now near the income band where premiumization "starts to inflect."
HUL claims portfolio is structurally advantaged in premium, with 1.3x relative market share in premium vs mass.
Premium focus is supported by disproportionate investments: two times more investment vs the average, with 60% on digital.
Dove moved from #9 to #5 in HUL brand rank; management stated "Dove will become the number two brand rank for HUL." Extension includes body wash, hair treatments, and entry into body lotions.

subsections.label: Vector 3: Market making (category penetration extremely low)
points: HUL highlighted penetration gaps vs Indonesia: hair masks (India <1% vs 64x), sun care (India 2% vs 17x), body wash (India 2% vs 16x), dishwash liquids (India 7% vs 7x), laundry liquids (India 13% vs 3x), face cleansing (India 17% vs 2x).

Market-making playbook: superior product + clear trial trigger; education + "mammoth scale" sampling (homes, stores, quick commerce); partnerships (e.g., washing machine OEMs for liquids); trial packs.
Actionable takeaway: Management's confidence on the 40% market making delta is rooted in a codified multi-year playbook and large penetration headroom, not near-term share gains.

subsections.label: Vector 4: New spaces (selective expansion)
points: Management explicitly stated it will not enter all adjacencies, but will decisively and selectively enter a few based on right to win, profit pool, and sustainable long-term growth.
Minimalist (mastige skincare): acquired; 2x growth since acquisition (~₹900cr ARR); positioned as next brand to join the 1000 crore club.
Oziva (wellbeing/VMS): scaled 4x since acquisition.

Horlicks Protein: launched in powders + RTD; positioned to democratize protein (not gym protein); differentiated via yeast-based protein (citing 60% adult lactose intolerance), plus fiber (6x increase) to improve absorption; single-serve sachets for convenience; priced as low as ₹82 per drink.

subsections.label: Home Care (Vandana Suri) — revenue ₹23,672cr, 37% of HUL, 19% segment margin
points: Growth levers: consumption (affluence expands wardrobes; India home care spend per capita 2.5x lower than Vietnam; washing machine adoption at 28% HH penetration, urban 'one out of two' households); grams per usage explicitly called out as a new consumption lever.
Premiumization: 57% of laundry market still tier-3 (~3m tons) waiting to be premiumized.
Format upgradation: bars → powders → liquids; liquids penetration ~13% (quarterly) vs Vietnam 5x.
New spaces: entered floor cleaners with Vim floor cleaner (last year).
Wheel (tier-3) reinvigorated; now largest brand in tier three, digital-first rural deployment; Gen Z relevance (two-thirds of Gen Z in rural/tier-4).
Surf Excel: last decade 3x volume growth, 4x turnover growth; premiumization via EasyWash + format shifts.
Vim Liquids: trigger-led conversion — odor removal positioned as a key adoption driver in non-veg households; bars still 75% of the Vim liquids/bars category market.

subsections.label: Beauty & Wellbeing (Harman Dhillo) — turnover ~₹15,000cr, 7 brands >₹1,000cr
points: Key strategic construct: next wave of beauty in two parts — democratizers (low consumption, low format penetration, GT-heavy, TV still meaningful) vs power spenders/premiumizers (omni-channel; discovery/education online).
Competitive moat claimed: portfolio + RTM + customized reach models 'no other organization can copy.'
HUL is #1 in share of new triers in multiple beauty segments (skincare, hair treatment, light moisturizers).
Premium/masstige brands gaining penetration with affluent cohorts as they upgrade.
Dove hair positioned as premiumization + regime expansion platform (treatments, masks, bond repair); access packs ensure democratizer participation.

Sun care as market making: structural tailwinds (heat + women stepping out); multi-brand sun portfolio grew from 1 to 4 brands since 2024; 100% in-vivo tested tech; sensorial barriers addressed; 600x step-up in advocacy models; entry-level sunscreen priced at ₹10.
Glow & Lovely positioned to drive 'responsible skincare.'
White spaces: Minimalist (focus on ethos/transparency + synergies + Unilever R&D infusion); Wellbeing/VMS: global Liquid IV launched; pipeline brands referenced (Ollie, Gruns).

subsections.label: Personal Care (Vipul Martur) — revenue ₹9,500cr, 19% segment margin, 5 brands >₹1,000cr
points: Consumption: rural consumption growing 1.8x urban, with infrastructure/lifestyle shifts; India vs Brazil cited as 2x consumption gap.
Lux positioned as consumption engine; brand transformation using science/aesthetics/sensorials/social-first/Gen Z framework.
Premiumization: ~7 lakh tons mass skin cleansing headroom; premium bars (Dove serum bar, Pears glycerine) growing faster; HUL outpacing premium bar growth.

Body wash described as reaching adoption inflection; category growth ~4x rest of skin cleansing; HUL body wash business grew 4x over 4 years; market-development model includes education on usage + heavy sampling because benefit realization takes 4-5 occasions.
Oral care: Closeup leadership in freshness; whitening as rapid growth segment (India only 1/20th of whitening contribution vs comparators; cited China/Turkey comparison).
Deodorants as new space: aimed at functional sweat/odor protection for rising working women; leverages Unilever patented tech.

subsections.label: Foods & Beverages (Raj Rasneek Kohli) — revenue ₹14,000cr, ~20% segment margin, 7 brands >₹1,000cr
points: Strong leadership in tea, nutrition, ketchup/sauces, coffee, soups, jams.

Demand drivers: premiumization (more flavors/formats/functionality); climate warming driving expansion from hot to cold beverages; health/wellness driving protein/fortification; working women driving convenience/cooking aids/condiments.

Horlicks reposition from 'health food drink' to 'lifestyle nutrition'; brings back science and nutrition to the core with superfoods (oats/almonds/millets), Nutrimax tech, 6x fiber, no added sugar, BCAA; reported double-digit growth in last two quarters.
Horlicks Protein addressed 4 barriers (need, digestibility, taste, trust); yeast-based + probiotic fiber; single-serve; affordability; trusted brand moat.
Kissan repositioned from kids condiment to 'flavor hacking'/'great Indian food brand'; chutneys opportunity cited as consumed 4x of ketchup.
Beverages evolution: mass→premium, kettle→cup (nuclear families; instant formats), hot→cold (RTD expansion); China tea evolution cited as an analog (premium/RTD/functionality increasing sharply).

subsections.label: Core strategic message
points: Management framed the next leg of growth around a structurally shifting Indian consumer and a more segmented opportunity set ("India isn't a single landscape… it's a kaleidoscope").
Stated objective is to deliver "competitive, volume-led growth" with sharper resource allocation and execution upgrades after "growth has been muted in the last two years."

Allocating resources more sharply to fewer, bigger bets

Executional step-up in marketing and in-store
Rewired organization, more simple, more agile

subsections.label: The New India demand model (structural changes)
points: Priya Naya attributes the opportunity to income distribution shifts and five structural changes: 377m Gen Z ("These consumers are absolutely changing India"); rising women workforce participation to 43% (from ~23-25%); data + digital payments ("50% of the world's global payments go through India"); roads/infrastructure where improved access drives ~30% incremental growth when connectivity improves; rural modernization (tap water, LPG) changing product usage patterns.

subsections.label: Segmentation framework
points: HUL's segmentation framework is a 24-cell grid across income cohorts (democratizers/premiumizers/affluent), where they live (70% tier 4/rural; 20% small towns; 10% large cities), and where they shop (GT, modern trade, e-com, quick commerce, specialist GT etc.).

Actionable investor takeaway: Management is explicitly moving from "India as one market" to hyper-segmented investment theses by cohort x geography x channel; brand roles are being assigned by pocket (example: Clinic Plus → rural democratizers; Dove → premiumizers; Nexxus → online).

quarters.summary: HUL delivered its highest USG in 13 quarters (10%) in Q1 FY27, with management guiding that FY27 will be better than FY26 and EBITDA margin expected to remain around the current guided range (~23%), even as commodity and currency volatility persists and monsoon/geopolitical uncertainty is monitored.

subsections.label: Earnings quality
points: Strong growth in EBITDA and PAT(bei) reflects the quality of earnings and the resilience of the business.
Reported PAT declined 2% YoY due to a one-off tax credit of ~INR330 crores in the base period of June quarter'25; adjusted for this, PAT grew 11% YoY.
EBITDA Margin of 23% was delivered within the guided range despite external volatility, via financial discipline across all lines of the P&L.

subsections.label: Capital/cost management
points: Rigorous savings program coupled with disciplined P&L management helped manage cost inflation and generate fuel for growth.
Backed by a strong balance sheet and healthy cash generation, the company continues to invest behind brands, innovation and market-making capabilities.
Management noted cost inflation running near ~10% versus pricing actions of ~5%, but said EBITDA (not gross margin) is the metric being managed via leverage across all P&L lines.

Management indicated that even passing on half of the inflation via pricing has historically allowed margins to be maintained within the guided range; feasible EBITDA margin maintenance seen for crude oil in the $75-$100/barrel range (not feasible at $140-$160/barrel).

subsections.label: Home Care
points: Home Care delivered 14% USG driven by high-single digit UVG — its strongest performance in 3 years.
Fabric Wash delivered broad-based double-digit, volume-led growth; bars and powders sustained their step-up, while liquids grew competitively and accelerated their double-digit growth trajectory.

Household Care accelerated performance, delivering double-digit USG and UVG; Vim Liquid reported another quarter of double-digit growth with market development actions continuing to increase penetration.
Given external volatility, continued inflation in crude-linked derivatives is being managed via calibrated price increases across the segment.

Home Care EBIT reportedly fell even as top line grew strongly; management said it will calibrate between price, savings and procurement benefits given continued volatility in crude, to navigate competitively.

subsections.label: Beauty & Wellbeing
points: Hair Care delivered another quarter of double-digit, volume-led growth; premium hair care (hair masks, serums) continues to outperform, reinforcing market leadership.

Skin Care and Colour Cosmetics grew high-single digit, led by double-digit growth in Premium Skin Care; Minimalist strengthened its double-digit growth trajectory and has been expanded aggressively in off-line channels since acquisition.
Vaseline Gluta-Hya franchise broadened its portfolio with the launch of a smoothening body lotion, enabling category premiumization and de-seasonalization.

Health & Wellbeing saw a soft quarter as OZiva business transitions towards emerging consumer demand spaces; management remains committed to investing behind the portfolio, citing non-linear growth typical in nascent wellness categories (after ~80% growth in FY26).

Both mass business (sequential improvement) and premium business (acceleration) contributed to the strong double-digit Beauty growth; brands Simple, Vaseline, Pond's are all growing at extremely strong double-digits; Minimalist and Simple are accelerating both online and off-line; e-commerce and modern trade (Channels of the Future) growing double-digit.

subsections.label: Personal Care
points: Segment delivered 4% USG driven by price increases taken in response to continued palm oil inflation for the second consecutive year.

Skin Cleansing grew mid-single digit, driven by Premium Bars (Dove, Pears) delivering double-digit, volume-led growth; sustained market development in Bodywash accelerated its double-digit growth trajectory while strengthening category leadership.
Oral Care delivered mid-single digit growth; premium innovations (Closeup White Now, Pepsodent Gum Care, Sensitive Care) continued to gain traction in higher-benefit demand spaces.

Soaps category volume decline attributed to two years of sequential palm-oil-led cost inflation impacting the category overall; countered via premiumization (Dove, Pears growing strong double-digits) and conversion to Bodywash (low penetration, HUL leads and is growing double-digits); mass portfolio (Lux, Lifebuoy) also being driven for growth.
Management noted GST rate cuts (18% to 5%) partly offset consumer-level pricing, but the palm-oil inflation effect over two years, not just the GST period, is impacting category volumes.

Different demand trends exist across pop-strata segments (rural vs metros vs large towns) within soaps; company does not disclose brand/segment-level market share but says it continues to win turnover-weighted market share overall.

subsections.label: Foods
points: Premium Tea reported low-single digit UVG, while Coffee delivered double-digit, volume-led growth; RTD formats and Bru Gold continued to scale up.
Lifestyle Nutrition continued momentum with double-digit growth in both Horlicks and Boost; category recorded its fifth consecutive quarter of positive UVG.
Boost crossed the INR1,000 crore annual turnover milestone, becoming HUL's 21st brand in the INR1,000 crore+ club.
Relaunched Horlicks Superfoods and RTD offerings continue to see positive traction; Horlicks Biscuits continued double-digit growth momentum.

Packaged Foods delivered high-single digit growth, led by robust performance in Unilever Food Solutions, Mayonnaise and International Sauces; Kissan Chutney maintained encouraging momentum with two new variants launched in the quarter.
Early read of the new tea season shows an inflationary trend; pricing calls will be made as the buying season progresses and commodity trends become clearer.

subsections.label: Growth breadth
points: Q1 volume growth of 5% (vs 6% in Q4) mainly reflects moderation in tea and soaps volumes; other subsegments saw a pickup in volume growth trajectory.

Management characterized growth as broad-based: across categories (Laundry to Dishwash, Coffee, Horlicks and Boost, Beauty & Wellbeing, Hair Care, Skin Care), across channels (GT, quick commerce, MT, e-com), and across rural/urban and mass/premium — providing confidence for going forward.
Rural and urban growth both robust; rural growth has stepped up over recent quarters as a key driver, while overall demand remains stable in both.

key_figures.label: Formulation development timeline acceleration (Liquids Lab of the Future)

subsections.label: Innovation infrastructure
points: Launch of Unilever Fragrance House in India, part of a global program to advance fragrance creation capabilities in-house and with key fragrance houses, combining science, consumer insight and artificial intelligence.

Liquids Lab of the Future in Mumbai uses advanced AI and digitally enabled facilities to accelerate innovation in future-facing high-growth formats, cutting formulation development timelines by up to 6 times.

Company investing ahead of the curve in innovation, technology, manufacturing and digital transformation to remain future-fit and create desire at scale; more strategy details to be shared at the Capital Markets Day in September.
AI is being embedded across the value chain as a core enabler of operations, not a standalone initiative.

subsections.label: Manufacturing excellence
points: Haridwar factory recognized by the World Economic Forum's Global Lighthouse Network in the Supply Chain Resilience category.
Sonepat factory recognized by the WEF Global Lighthouse Network in the Sustainability category.
With these recognitions, HUL now holds 8 WEF Lighthouse designations across 6 sites, the highest for any company in India.
Digitally powered agile R&D and flexible manufacturing capabilities helped maintain service levels through the quarter's volatility.

subsections.label: Channel and rural/urban trends
points: Quick commerce continued to grow strong double digits (40-50%).
In General Trade (GT), distribution growth was led out of small towns and rural areas; GT has come back to growth with a step-up.
Off-line expansion continued for digital-first brands like Minimalist and Simple.
Rural and urban growth both robust and continue to be strong; rural growth has stepped up over the last few quarters, becoming a bigger driver.

Digital-first distribution centre in Vijayawada uses AI-enabled real-time visibility to create a digitally orchestrated fulfilment ecosystem, improving accuracy and transparency through faster demand sensing, warehouse operations, truck tracking and digital proof of delivery.

subsections.label: Supply chain resilience
points: Global procurement network scale ensured continuity of supplies without disruption during the quarter's volatility.

Digital-first distribution centre in Vijayawada uses AI-enabled real-time visibility for demand sensing, warehouse operations, truck tracking and digital proof of delivery, improving accuracy and transparency.

subsections.label: Competitive positioning
points: Turnover-weighted market share gains continued in the quarter, reinforcing the view that growth is competitive.

50 brands across 15 categories straddle the price-benefit pyramid, positioning the company to serve diverse evolving consumer needs and implement calibrated pricing while preserving consumer franchise.

Management rejects the notion that growth is skewed only to premium (K-shaped); says growth is competitive at both mass and premium ends, with premium subsegments growing faster in line with overall market shape, consistent even within rural markets.

In quick commerce, competitors are entering the space and it is evolving rapidly; HUL's growth in Q-com is strong double-digit (40-50%); strategy is to win via improved availability, curated tech solutions, tailored assortments, price-pack architecture built for Q-com, sharper execution/partnership with platforms, and leveraging data/insights to improve conversion, visibility and repeat usage.

On liquid detergents and other liquids (low penetration segments), strategy is to develop/grow the market; competition is expected but HUL leads market development and will use the right portfolio/price architecture as the market develops.

Bodywash: category described as very low penetration; HUL leads the category and continues to grow it in double-digits, converting soap-bar bathing consumers to liquid via sampling and consumer education.

Portfolio expansion strategy has three buckets: (1) extending existing brands into new demand spaces (e.g., Horlicks into protein, Vaseline into light moisturization); (2) bringing more Unilever global brands into India demand spaces; (3) bolt-on acquisitions (e.g., Minimalist, OZiva) leveraging scale, R&D and category leadership synergies.

On D2C brand saturation trend (Bain report, ~INR500cr ceiling cited by an analyst question), management sees this as an opportunity given HUL's wide distribution and ability to scale acquired brands (e.g., Minimalist scaling post-acquisition).

subsections.label: Marketing spend strategy
points: A&P spend increases (highest in 11 quarters) should be viewed alongside improving return on marketing investment (AI-enabled ROI programs) and procurement leverage on media costs, rather than purely on a like-for-like growth-rate basis.
Competitive spend on GRP levels has been increasing, and SOV/SOM have been rising, with HUL number one in most categories, contributing to a sizable absolute A&P spend.

Marketing spend is maintained as a healthy balance between long-term brand-building spend and short-term acquisition/performance spend, guided by proprietary long-term and short-term ROI modelling to prioritize by brand.

subsections.label: Portfolio/M&A moves
points: Bolt-on acquisitions such as Minimalist and OZiva provide better exposure to growth and are being scaled with leverage of HUL's scale, R&D capability and category leadership synergy benefits.
Minimalist has been expanded aggressively in off-line channels since its acquisition last year and has 'taken off in a big way' post-acquisition.
Management noted that barriers to entry for new brands may have reduced but barriers to scale have gone up, favoring an incumbent with distribution scale like HUL.
'Power moves' strategy: sharply allocating financial and human resources within a few key low-penetration, high-growth segment bets across businesses.
Market development strategy: doubling down as category leaders on sampling activities, penetration-building resources, and assortment expansion in low-penetrated categories.
Execution strategy: doubling down on distribution and assortment growth in both general trade and organized trade, built on specialist routes to market including quick commerce.

Portfolio strategy: continuing to drive portfolio towards higher velocity areas via extending existing brands into new demand spaces, introducing more global Unilever brands, and bolt-on acquisitions.

Priya Nair reflecting on completing 1 year as CEO: happy with progress but not satisfied; cites work on portfolio, investment allocation, go-to-market progress (assortment, distribution, channel architecture) and multi-year brand/innovation plan as key fundamentals.

subsections.label: Macro and commodity risks
points: Increasingly uncertain global environment characterized by geopolitical tensions, volatile commodity markets and currency fluctuations.
Commodities and currencies remain elevated; company continues to monitor progress of monsoon.
Crude-linked derivative cost inflation impacting Home Care segment; calibrated price increases being taken to manage this.
Continued palm oil inflation for a second consecutive year impacting Personal Care/Skin Cleansing category volumes and requiring price increases.
Tea season showing early inflationary trend; pricing decisions to be made as season progresses.

Monsoon: rainfall progression started with a huge deficit which has since reduced to 15% of the overall; management does not see meaningful impact on the Indian economy as long as the deficit remains between 15%-20%.

El Nino/agri impact: agriculture is ~15% of India's GDP; in a difficult year vs a good year the impact is estimated at 50-60 basis points to overall GDP growth, but portfolio spread across categories provides confidence to navigate without change in guidance; MSP increases of ~5-6% provide some insulation to rural incomes.
Guidance for FY27 is described as risk-adjusted, factoring in both macroeconomic environment and portfolio risk.
Q-com competitive intensity: new players entering the quick commerce segment, making it a rapidly evolving competitive space.
Competitive intensity from value players flagged in liquid detergents, hand wash and beauty as a factor being navigated via market development and portfolio/price architecture.

subsections.label: Outlook commentary
points: FY27 is guided to be better than FY26, based on continued action on market development, channel expansion and portfolio transformation.

EBITDA Margin expected to remain around the current guided range, achieved via structural savings, calibrated pricing actions and judicious media investments despite elevated commodities and currencies.

Management reiterated no change in confidence versus prior quarter despite outlook wording shift to 'continue to monitor monsoon and geopolitics'; described as continuing caution on economic scenario, not a change in underlying confidence.
Demand environment guided as stable; management does not guide on a quarterly basis and does not see inflation-led demand impact materializing.
Guidance is risk-adjusted, i.e., known macro and portfolio risks are already factored into the FY27 > FY26 outlook.
Focus remains on delivering competitive volume-led growth anchored to key priorities.

key_takeaways: Turnover for the quarter stood at INR17,184 crores, with an Underlying Sales Growth of 10%, driven equally by volume and price. This represents our highest growth in 13 quarters.
Our growth trajectory has strengthened from 3% in the first half of FY'26 to 10% in this quarter.
We stepped our A&P spends up sequentially to INR1,657 crores, the highest in 11 quarters.

EBITDA Margin of 23%, which was within the guided range. Absolute EBITDA grew 8% year-on-year to INR3,947 crores, while Profit After Tax before exceptional items grew 9% year-on-year to INR2,731 crores.

The reported Profit After Tax after exceptional items stood at INR2,680 crores, declining 2% year-on-year due to one-off tax credit of ~INR330 crores in the base period of June quarter'25. Adjusted for this, the Profit After Tax stands at 11% growth year-on-year basis.
Home Care delivered 14% USG, driven by high-single digit UVG. This is its strongest performance in 3 years.
Beauty & Wellbeing delivering 12% USG, driven by high-single digit UVG.
Personal Care segment delivered 4% USG for the quarter, driven by price increases taken in response to continued palm oil inflation for the second consecutive year.

Foods segment delivered a USG of 7%, driven by mid-single digit UVG; Boost crossed the INR1,000 crore annual turnover milestone, making it our 21st brand in our portfolio to be in the INR1,000 crore plus club.
Backed by the continued action on market development, channel expansion and portfolio transformation, we remain confident that FY'27 will be better than FY'26.
We, therefore, expect EBITDA Margin to remain around the current guided range.

subsections.label: PBT margin drivers
points: Excluding bullion, PBT margins were around 5.1% in Q1 FY27, down from 5.5%-5.6% previously.

The decline was attributed to three factors: a one-time customs duty gain of INR30-40 crores that had to be given back to consumers via offers to promote old gold exchange; margin dilution of 0.2%-0.3% inherent to old gold exchange versus cash purchase of bullion; and the absence of a one-time platinum/silver gain (~0.2%) seen in the prior period.

Management expects that for the full year, PBT margins should be maintained at least at the previous year's level on a conservative basis, as cash-for-gold volumes are expected to negate the margin dilution from old gold exchange, and promotional offers for exchange have been tapered down.

Employee cost increase (a periodic 'better increment' beyond usual annual increment, given once in a few years to retain talent) contributed roughly 0.2%-0.3% to margin pressure in Q1, and is expected to continue but be offset by operating leverage.
Customs duty benefit was approximately INR41 crores in Q1 FY27 and is expected to be around INR60 crores in Q2 FY27; this benefit largely flows through Q2 and does not extend into Q3.
Management noted the customs duty buffer may conservatively continue to be shared with consumers rather than retained as margin benefit.

subsections.label: Margin dilution vs cash-for-gold mechanics
points: Exchange is done at the store's board rate; when buying bullion for cash, the company gets a 0.5%-0.75% markup on the spot rate versus the sale rate, a markup not available in an exchange transaction — this is the source of margin dilution.
Cash-for-gold purchases are made at a discount to the spot price, making the practice margin accretive, and is expected to negate the dilution caused by old gold exchange.
Capital employed for exchange versus cash-for-gold purchase is broadly unchanged, since the company would have bought bullion the next day regardless; only the timing differs.

subsections.label: Capital allocation / debt reduction
points: Regarding non-GML debt reduction, company is on track to complete repayment by end of September; post that, steps will be initiated for release of the second tranche of real estate collaterals.

Agreements signed with potential buyers for two separate parcels of non-core real estate land for aggregate consideration of ~INR102 crores; sale process expected to conclude and consideration received before end of the ongoing quarter.
Company reiterated plan to become non-GML debt-free within 'a couple of months', i.e., by September.

subsections.label: Non-South market growth
points: Kalyan has been growing in non-South markets over the last two-three years; revenue share from non-South markets is now more than 50%-60%.

Kalyan positions itself as a hyperlocal brand keeping 30%-40% local inventory and 50%-60% national inventory, competing with local players via local inventory and national players via national inventory.

subsections.label: Old gold exchange / recirculation program
points: The 'Shine with India' gold recirculation campaign was launched in response to sharp rise in international oil prices and resultant forex pressure, aiming to increase share of recycled gold and reduce dependence on imported gold, making the business more resilient.

The campaign was well received by customers, raising recycled gold share of revenue to over 46% in Q1 FY27 and over 55% in June; management aims to maintain this share in the range of 55%-60% going forward.

Cash-for-gold (buying old gold from customers for cash rather than exchange for jewelry) is a newer product gaining momentum; for the June quarter, gold-for-cash was in single digits and is moving to double digits.

Cash-for-gold applies not only to existing Kalyan customers but also to those who previously sold gold to unorganized players, since organized players historically only bought back their own sold gold; now this segment is becoming organized industry-wide, with peers also adopting cash-for-gold.

subsections.label: Store expansion targets
points: No change in target of 84 Kalyan showroom openings in India for FY27; H2 is usually heavier than H1 in terms of store expansion, consistent with last year's pattern.
No change in Candere target of ~50 showrooms for the financial year.
ATM regional brand: first showroom in Chennai on August 21, followed by four more in subsequent months, expanding beyond Chennai into other cities.

subsections.label: Competitive positioning
points: Kalyan positions itself between regional/local unorganized players and national players, with brand acceptance strong across the country, driving expansion and strong same-store sales growth (SSSG) over the last two-three years.
Management stated there is 'no new strategy' required; focus remains on execution, given 70-80 showroom additions per year under the FOCO model.
Movement from unorganized to organized market continues strongly across India; management sees the company as a clear beneficiary along with other major sector players.

On franchise partners: most FOCO franchisees are financial partners already in franchise business, automobile industry, etc., acting purely as financiers without an active management role; no existing independent jewelers have converted to become Kalyan franchisees.

subsections.label: Cash-for-gold market dynamics
points: Management noted that almost all organized players have now started offering cash-for-gold schemes, and it is growing as an industry segment; it does not dilute the Kalyan brand in any way.

subsections.label: New regional brand launch – Akshaya Thanga Maligai (ATM)
points: Company unveiled its first regional brand exclusively tailored for Tamil Nadu markets, named Akshaya Thanga Maligai (short name ATM).
Inventory at ATM will be curated specifically for Tamil Nadu preferences with designs, rates and price points aligned to regional locations and buying patterns.
The brand is positioned to compete directly with established regional jewelry chains and unorganized players rather than Kalyan's existing showroom network.
First showroom to launch on 21st August in Chennai, followed by four more showrooms in the coming months; expansion will predominantly be FOCO / asset-light.
Two of the initial showrooms will be in Chennai; additional showrooms planned in other cities as well.

Management described the Tamil Nadu market opportunity as huge given the scale of regional and local competitors; will provide more details on future scale-up plans for ATM after the first four showrooms are established.

subsections.label: No bonus share issuance
points: Management confirmed no plans for a bonus share issue as of now.

subsections.label: Gold price volatility
points: Sharp rise in international oil prices and resultant pressure on forex was a driver behind launching the gold recirculation campaign to reduce dependence on imported gold.
Gold prices dipped about 15%-20% over the last 2-3 months; management does not overreact to such price corrections, viewing them as part of usual cyclicality.

Demand pauses are typical during periods of price volatility as consumers take a wait-and-watch stance to gauge price direction, but wedding demand cannot pause more than 2-3 weeks since weddings must proceed on schedule; discretionary demand can pause for up to 1-1.5 months.

Volatile gold prices historically required grammage/design adjustments (lightweighting) in products; procurement team manages this by keeping products at a 'sweet spot' of consumer affordability, an ongoing/usual process rather than a new development.
No committed policy exists regarding customs duty changes passing through to consumers; treatment depends on market dynamics at the time.

subsections.label: Employee cost increase
points: Standalone employee cost rose ~54% YoY; this reflects a periodic better-than-usual increment (beyond the standard annual increment) given once in a few years to motivate and retain talent, not a one-time bonus payout; management expects this elevated cost trend to continue in future quarters but expects operating leverage to offset the impact.

subsections.label: Corporate governance query
points: An analyst raised a question about past corporate governance issues related to related-party transactions (RPT) highlighted by Moneylife magazine and flagged by Motilal Oswal and other mutual funds; management declined to comment on this line of questioning.

subsections.label: Full-year margin outlook
points: For the full year, management does not expect an impact on PBT margins from old gold exchange dilution; even on a conservative basis, they expect to maintain PBT margins at least at the previous financial year's level.
This expectation is underpinned by growing traction in cash-for-gold (margin accretive) negating exchange-related dilution, and by tapering of promotional offers for exchange.

subsections.label: Debt reduction timeline
points: Non-GML debt repayment on track to complete by end of September 2026; company expects to become non-GML debt-free within 'a couple of months'.
Post debt repayment, company will initiate steps for release of the second tranche of real estate collaterals.

subsections.label: Store expansion guidance reiterated
points: 84 Kalyan showroom target for India in FY27 unchanged.
~50 Candere showroom target for FY27 unchanged.
ATM: 5 showrooms planned in the near term (1 in Chennai by Aug 21, plus 4 more), with further scale-up plans to be shared later.

subsections.label: Non-core asset sale timeline
points: Sale of two parcels of non-core real estate land (aggregate consideration ~INR102 crores) expected to conclude and receive consideration before end of the ongoing quarter.

subsections.label: Customs duty benefit outlook
points: Customs duty benefit for Q2 FY27 expected to be in the range of INR60 crores; this benefit largely flows through in Q2 and does not extend into Q3.

subsections.label: Candere profitability outlook
points: Candere expected to remain PAT positive for the current financial year, continuing the trend since H2 of the last financial year.

guidance_ledger.statement: For the full year, we are even on a conservative basis, we hold to the PBT margin of the last financial year.

Regarding the non-GML debt reduction, we are well on track to complete the repayment by end of September. Post that, we will initiate steps for the release of the second tranche of real estate collaterals.
No change in target of number of showrooms in Kalyan and Candere; usually H2 is heavier than H1 in terms of store expansion.
For Candere also you had guided for 50 stores - Yes, no change in target.
The first showroom will be launched on 21st August in Chennai and shall be followed by another four showrooms in the next coming months.

We have signed the agreement with potential buyers for 2 separate parcels of land with an aggregate consideration amount to around INR102 crores. We expect to conclude the sale process and receive consideration before the end of the ongoing quarter.
Our efforts will be to maintain the share in the range of 55% to 60% going forward.
It's in the range of INR60 crores for Q2.
Candere has been PAT positive for the first quarter and should continue for this financial year.
Way forward ROCEs will further improve because we focus on capital-light expansion.
For the future scale-up and things, let us finish these four showrooms and then we'll come back to you with the plan for ATM.
We want to make it a non-GML debt-free in the running financial year. And if things go really well, we might do it by H1 itself, but we don't want to guide you in that direction.
GML will be maintained the same levels unless we get something more; going forward we will also focus on increasing the GML, but this will depend on the sanctions available from banks.
PBT India has been in the range of 5.5%-5.6%. I think that is here to stay, and some operating leverage can come in.

There has been some advantage because of the platinum and silver margin, which cannot be sustained for the next financial year; the changed inventory procurement pattern is also not going to come for the next financial year.
INR300 crores of non-GML reduction at approx 9-10% interest implies about INR30 crores reduction; combined with the INR20 crore one-off in FY26, total reduction is INR50 crores.
If you are trying to put a number for the next 3-5 years, we usually don't guide more than 10% SSSG, even though I don't have a reason for it given recent 20-30% actuals.
Close to 50% of the cash generated will be used for dividends and debt reduction, capex etc. Balance 50% will be parked for Candere and the regional brand; further allocation details to come later.
The time line set for the set no 1 asset disposal was before September of this year, which I think is going in the right direction.
We have also started process to release the second set of assets from the banks, which I don't want to give you a time line, but I will give you more details when it reaches more closely.
South may we will restrict in 13 to 15 showrooms, majority in metros like Bangalore, Chennai, Hyderabad.

guidance_ledger.metric: Middle East FOCO conversion cash flow
guidance_ledger.statement: Hypothetically, if the conversion happens big time, cash flows should come, but we will come back when it is very close to happening; no budgeting is being given now.

risk_register.risk: Gold price volatility and its impact on consumer demand pauses
risk_register.note: Consumers pause during volatile price movements; wedding demand can only pause 2-3 weeks while discretionary demand can pause up to 1.5 months; July demand was reported good.

risk_register.risk: Rising international oil prices and forex pressure driving gold import dependence
risk_register.note: Triggered launch of 'Shine with India' gold recirculation campaign to reduce dependence on imported gold.

risk_register.risk: Margin dilution from old gold exchange
risk_register.note: Exchange is margin dilutive by 0.2%-0.3%, expected to be offset by growing cash-for-gold adoption which is margin accretive.

risk_register.risk: Employee cost inflation
risk_register.note: One-time-in-a-few-years higher increment to retain talent drove 54% YoY standalone employee cost increase and ~0.2%-0.3% margin impact in Q1; expected to persist but offset by operating leverage.

risk_register.risk: Corporate governance / related-party transaction concerns
risk_register.note: Analyst raised historical RPT/governance concerns flagged by Moneylife and mutual funds; management declined to comment.

risk_register.risk: Gold price correction requiring grammage/design adjustments
risk_register.note: 15%-20% gold price correction over last 2-3 months is a usual challenge managed via procurement's 'sweet spot' product strategy; management does not overreact.

risk_register.risk: Absence of one-time gains (customs duty, platinum/silver) in future periods
risk_register.note: Customs duty benefit expected to taper (flows mostly in Q2, not into Q3); platinum/silver one-time gain (~0.2%) from Q1 last year not expected to repeat.

risk_register.risk: Gold supply disruption from Middle East tensions / GST import license delays
risk_register.note: Management stated there is abundant gold supply, no issue with availability via alternate channels like IIBX GIFT City and domestic bank sourcing.

risk_register.risk: Adhik-Maas (extra inauspicious month) impacting Q1 FY27 wedding sales timing
risk_register.note: Possibility that Adhik-Maas days are slower than usual wedding days, though revenue may be preponed/postponed rather than lost overall.

risk_register.risk: GML sanction limits in India constraining loan growth
risk_register.note: Unlike Middle East where GML has no cap tied to gold price, Indian banks maintain fixed GML sanction limits; not all banks provide GML.

risk_register.risk: High base effect in FY27 vs exceptional FY26 growth
risk_register.note: H2 FY27 will face a higher base than H2 FY26; management could not guarantee continuation of historical growth rates but noted growth has continued despite high bases previously.

risk_register.risk: Non-sustainability of one-off margin tailwinds (platinum/silver gains, procurement pattern change)
risk_register.note: Platinum/silver margin benefit (~INR20 crores) and the changed inventory procurement pattern from FY26 are not expected to recur in FY27.

risk_register.risk: Advance tax interest one-off inflating FY26 interest cost
risk_register.note: INR20 crore one-off interest paid due to under-budgeted advance tax estimate; expected not to recur, factored into FY27 outlook.

themes.label: Demand recovery
themes.note: Demand remained robust in Q1 barring one month of Adhik-Maas slowdown; July demand trends reported strong on the ground.

themes.label: Margin sustainability
themes.note: PBT margin ex-bullion dipped to 5.1% from 5.5%-5.6% due to customs duty giveback, exchange dilution and employee cost, but management expects full-year margins to hold at last year's level via cash-for-gold traction.

themes.label: Debt reduction
themes.note: Non-GML debt repayment on track for completion by end of September, followed by release of second tranche of real estate collaterals.

themes.label: Candere turnaround
themes.note: Candere revenue more than doubled YoY to INR141 crores and posted a profit of INR2.1 crores versus a loss last year; expected to stay PAT positive for FY27.

themes.label: Franchise (FOCO) expansion strategy
themes.note: Kalyan continues capital-light FOCO expansion of 70-80 showrooms a year with franchisee ROCE around 14%; new regional brand ATM also to expand via FOCO.

themes.label: SSSG divergence South vs non-South
themes.note: Non-South markets now contribute more than 50%-60% of revenue, reflecting continued growth outside the core South market.

themes.label: Gold price volume trade-off
themes.note: 15%-20% gold price correction over 2-3 months typically boosts volumes since customers buy to a budget, though volatility can cause temporary demand pauses.

key_takeaways: Q1 performance has been very satisfactory given the overall context. Demand remained robust during most part of the recently concluded quarter, except for 1 month of Adhik-Maas, during which wedding-related demand slowed down in certain parts of the country.
Consolidated revenue growth ex-bullion and PAT growth have been 38% and 32%, respectively; on a standalone basis, the revenue growth ex-bullion and PAT growth have been 38% and 25%, respectively.

Sharp rise in international oil prices and the resultant pressure on forex led us to launch our 'Shine with India' gold recirculation campaign... helping us to increase the share of recycled gold as a percentage of revenue to over 46% during Q1 FY 2027. For the month of June, the share of recycled gold was in excess of 55%, and our efforts will be to maintain the share in the range of 55% to 60% going forward.

We have unveiled our first regional brand exclusively tailored for Tamil Nadu markets. We have named it Akshaya Thanga Maligai and will also be known by its short name ATM... The first showroom will be launched on 21st August in Chennai and shall be followed by another four showrooms in the next coming months.

We have made considerable progress with respect to the sale of non-core real estate assets. We have signed the agreement with potential buyers for 2 separate parcels of land with an aggregate consideration amount to around INR102 crores.

Regarding the non-GML debt reduction, we are well on track to complete the repayment by end of September. Post that, we will initiate steps for the release of the second tranche of real estate collaterals.

The company reported consolidated revenue of INR10,008 crores, a growth of 38% over the corresponding quarter of the previous year. Consolidated EBITDA came in at INR633 crores versus INR508 crores. Consolidated profit after tax came in at INR349 crores versus INR264 crores.
For the full year, we are even on a conservative basis, we hold to the PBT margin of the last financial year.
pressing_questions: Just wanted to know about any bonus issued from the company? / How can we compete with Tanishq, whose share price is very high compared to ours?

There were some issues in the past regarding corporate governance with RPT etc. Moneylife magazine highlighted it and Motilal Oswal and some other mutual funds raised issues. If you would like to say something on that front, because that overhang might be there on our company.

When you look at margins excluding the impact of the inventory gain, PBT growth on standalone basis comes to only 14% - one of the lowest seen where profit growth has been lower than revenue growth. On the PBT margin side, how should we look at that going forward, and was there anything else that led to lower margins this quarter?

quarters.summary: Kalyan Jewellers reported a strong Q4 and FY26 with consolidated revenue growth of 66% (Q4) and 43% (FY26) and PAT growth of 118% (Q4) and 89% (FY26). Momentum continued into Q1 FY27 with strong Akshaya Tritiya sales and encouraging wedding-related consumer demand. Management plans to open 150 showrooms in FY27 across Kalyan, Candere and a new regional brand, complete non-GML debt reduction in India during FY27 (possibly by H1), and expects India PBT margin to stay in the 5.5%-5.6% range with some potential operating-leverage improvement; SSSG is recommended to be modeled conservatively at ~10% over a 3-5 year horizon despite recent 20-30%+ actuals.

subsections.label: Debt reduction plan
points: Reduction of non-GML debt in India by INR360-odd crores during FY26, part of an already announced plan to pay down non-GML debt in India completely.
Over the last 3 years, non-GML debt in India has been reduced from INR1,300 crores to INR300 crores.
Management aims to make India non-GML debt-free during the current financial year (FY27); if things go well, it could happen by H1 FY27, but management does not want to guide firmly on timing.

Debt level remained high in H1 FY26 because debt repayment for the year had not yet happened; gold metal loan (GML) pricing also tapered down around Q1, contributing to higher sequential interest cost.

subsections.label: Interest cost movement
points: Interest cost increase attributed mainly to higher processing charges and interest paid on advance tax due to an under-budgeted estimate for the full year.
Adjusting for the INR20 crore one-off related to advance tax interest and the anticipated INR30 crore reduction from non-GML paydown in FY27, total expected interest cost reduction is INR50 crores.

subsections.label: Capital allocation
points: Close to 50% of cash generated will be used for dividends, debt reduction, capex etc.
Balance ~50% will be parked for funds needed for Candere and the new regional brand; further allocation details to be shared later in the year.
Expansion is predominantly franchise-based (FOCO), so expansion itself does not require heavy incremental capital.
Some portion of cash will be budgeted for additional inventory in stores needing it, largely funded by inflows from the gold savings scheme given high SSSGs.

7-8 'hybrid' stores over the last 4 years involved relocating owned stores to bigger premises, where Kalyan's investment was the existing inventory from the old store and the franchisee partner brought additional/incremental capital and shared capex.

subsections.label: Margin drivers
points: Gross margins have improved but the improvement level has been maintained rather than continuously rising; showroom-level mix (South vs non-South), product mix sold, and FOCO mix all affect margin quarter to quarter.

Pilot project of shifting sourcing to a new set of vendors, which had provided a margin benefit, was already partially started in Q4 of the prior year and thus embedded in that quarter's gross margin base, explaining the apparent reversal versus Q3 FY26.

Some gross margin gain came from platinum and silver price/margin, but this benefit (~INR20 crores) is not expected to be sustained in FY27; inventory procurement pattern change from last year also not expected to repeat.
Going forward, gains are expected from operating leverage and interest savings, though the extent will depend on how the year unfolds.
India PBT margin has been in the 5.5%-5.6% range and is expected to stay in this range with potential for additional margin improvement from operating leverage.
ROCE management approach: when gold price rises by INR100, inventory per store is increased only by INR30-40, with volume reduced at the store level to manage ROCE.

subsections.label: Candere business
points: Candere grew revenue by 160% in FY26 on the back of very strong same-store sales growth and aggressive network expansion.
Candere turned PAT positive from the second half of FY26.
Going forward, Candere will focus more on driving SSSG along with expanding its showroom footprint.
Candere gross margins are higher (mid-30s) because the studded ratio in Candere is more than 70%.
Out of the 150-showroom FY27 opening guidance, Candere is expected to account for a similar number as last financial year, 50-55 stores.

subsections.label: SSSG divergence — South vs non-South
points: There is a significant divergence in SSSG between South and non-South this quarter, more pronounced than in prior quarters; South SSSG was lower than non-South.
South SSSG moved from about 25% to 29%, while non-South saw much higher acceleration; the shift toward non-South has been visible since Q3 and continued to be more pronounced in Q4.
Possible explanation offered: South may have a higher base.

SSSG trends between FOCO and COCO stores in non-South are looking more or less the same; first-year revenue growth for any new store (franchise or non-franchise) tends to have better SSSG than showrooms older than 5-7 years because gold savings scheme revenue also comes in.
Non-South is not uniform across all its markets — there are regional variations within non-South.

subsections.label: Volume vs value dynamics
points: Customers come with an INR budget rather than a volume budget; as gold prices rose ~60-70% over the last year, customers cannot proportionally increase spend, so volumes decline when prices rise and increase when prices are lower.
Company pushes customers toward studded jewellery and more precious/uncut stones, and reduces gold purity (22K to 18K, 18K to 14K) to help customers manage the pain of higher jewellery prices.

Revenue per store is better for COCO than FOCO because owned showrooms are typically bigger in initial times; FOCO stores have a smaller inventory basket and smaller revenue basket — for franchisees the focus is more on stock turn and profitability rather than only revenue per store.
Franchisee revenue per store is currently about INR50-52 crores, expected to keep rising as SSSG applies to franchisee stores as well.

subsections.label: Coin/investment demand
points: Coin sales during this year's Akshaya Tritiya were lower than estimated, unlike Dhanteras where coin sales were higher than estimated.

Q3 FY26 saw unusually high customer inquiry for gold coins (especially around Diwali), requiring higher-than-usual inventory; that quarter was considered abnormal, and otherwise coin revenue has remained normal.
Company does not proactively push coin sales and does not sell bullion.

subsections.label: Domestic expansion
points: First Kalyan showroom launched in the U.K. during FY26.
FY27 plan is to open 150 showrooms across Kalyan, Candere and the new regional brand.

South India expansion in FY26 focused on metros like Bangalore and Chennai, with intent to add Hyderabad and more metro stores; going forward South expansion will remain restricted to about 13-15 showrooms, majority in metros, since South already has deep Tier 2/Tier 3 penetration.
Outside South India, expansion has been more aggressive at over 60-65 showrooms, and this pattern is expected to continue.
No additional FOCO showrooms added in South this quarter beyond the prior quarter's count of 30 out of 99.

This quarter's apparent net reduction in store count (28 gross additions, net change of -4/-5) is mostly due to relocating existing stores to bigger premises (a 'hybrid' model) rather than actual closures; only one showroom (a small showroom in Madurai, in a location accessible only to 2-wheelers) was actually closed.

subsections.label: New regional brand
points: The third/new regional brand launch was planned for Q4 but has been delayed because post-election dust has not settled in the state where the company wants to open the new brand; the company is waiting for the situation to settle before starting its campaign.
Preparation is otherwise complete; only the timing needs to be managed according to on-ground conditions.

subsections.label: Middle East franchise conversion
points: Company temporarily converted 4 FOCO showrooms to COCO to facilitate discussions with a few Arab investors keen to open FOCO showrooms of Kalyan, in a range of about INR200-250 crores.

This franchisee model being discussed with Arab investors would cover not only new store openings but also conversion of old stores, with a bigger ticket size; nothing has materialized yet, no guidance is being given on it, but discussions are progressing in the right direction.
2 new showrooms were opened in the Middle East (inventory increase, not yet generating a full year of revenue) and 5-6 showrooms were renovated into bigger square footage with additional inventory.

Hypothetically, if a large-scale FOCO conversion in the Middle East occurs, cash flows would be generated, but management declined to provide any budget/guidance on this until the plan is closer to fruition.

subsections.label: Consumer demand momentum
points: Q4 momentum that began in Q3 continued and the company ended the financial year on an excellent note.
Strong growth witnessed in Akshaya Tritiya sales in the current quarter (Q1 FY27), with continued encouraging momentum in consumer demand, especially around wedding purchases.
April (start of FY27) has started off very well, and even against a high base, the company has been able to grow.

subsections.label: Employee/staffing model
points: All store employees are managed and provided by Kalyan, not the franchisee, even in FOCO stores; only rarely does a franchisee employ an accountant outside or inside the store.

subsections.label: Gold supply
points: Despite Middle East tensions and news of delays in renewal of GST-related import licenses, there is abundant supply of gold in the country and the company continues to receive regular inventory from banks.
IGST notification permits qualified jewellers, banks and importers to import gold through the India International Bullion Exchange at GIFT City, Gujarat.
Banks also procure gold from domestic sources such as scheme deposits and the gold deposit scheme; company sees no issue with gold supply.

subsections.label: Calendar/seasonality risk (Adhik-Maas)
points: Adhik-Maas (extra inauspicious month) in Q1 FY27 could shift wedding-related purchase timing; business can move between quarters but revenue is not lost at a full-year level, though there is a possibility that Adhik-Maas days could be slower than usual wedding days, partially offset by preponed purchases.

subsections.label: GML availability constraint
points: Unlike the Middle East where there is no cap on gold metal loans as gold prices rise, in India banks maintain a limit on GML availability; not all banks in India provide GML, which is a limitation on increasing GML in India.
GML in India is expected to be maintained at existing levels rather than increased significantly, given sanction constraints from banks.

subsections.label: High base risk for FY27 growth
points: FY26 was an exceptional year for Kalyan and the entire jewellery sector; H2 FY26 had a high base, and H2 FY27 will face an even higher base, raising the question of whether historical growth rates can be sustained, though management notes the company has grown even against high bases previously.

subsections.label: Non-GML debt elimination
points: Company aims to become non-GML debt-free in India during the current financial year (FY27); if things go well, this could be achieved by H1 FY27, though management does not want to firmly commit to that timeline.

GML (gold metal loan) is expected to be maintained at roughly current levels rather than expanded significantly, subject to bank sanction limits; focus going forward will also include efforts to increase GML where possible.

subsections.label: Margin outlook
points: India PBT margin of 5.5%-5.6% (FY26 level) is expected to be sustained ('here to stay'), with potential for some additional margin improvement from operating leverage.

Gains previously seen from silver/platinum price movements and changed inventory procurement patterns are not expected to repeat in FY27; operating leverage and interest cost savings are expected to be the main margin levers going forward, dependent on how the year unfolds.

subsections.label: SSSG outlook
points: SSSG has been unusually high (20-30%+) over the last 2-3 years; for any 3-5 year projection, management recommends modeling only about 10% SSSG, despite lacking a specific justification for why it should be lower than recent actuals.

subsections.label: Asset monetization
points: Timeline for disposal of the first set of collateral-released assets (~INR180 crores) is targeted before September 2026, and this is tracking on plan.
Process has also started to release the second set of assets (~INR200 crores) from banks; no timeline given yet, with more details to be shared closer to execution.
