risk_register.note: Possibility that Adhik-Maas days are slower than usual wedding days, though revenue may be preponed/postponed rather than lost overall.

risk_register.risk: GML sanction limits in India constraining loan growth
risk_register.note: Unlike Middle East where GML has no cap tied to gold price, Indian banks maintain fixed GML sanction limits; not all banks provide GML.

risk_register.risk: High base effect in FY27 vs exceptional FY26 growth
risk_register.note: H2 FY27 will face a higher base than H2 FY26; management could not guarantee continuation of historical growth rates but noted growth has continued despite high bases previously.

risk_register.risk: Non-sustainability of one-off margin tailwinds (platinum/silver gains, procurement pattern change)
risk_register.note: Platinum/silver margin benefit (~INR20 crores) and the changed inventory procurement pattern from FY26 are not expected to recur in FY27.

risk_register.risk: Advance tax interest one-off inflating FY26 interest cost
risk_register.note: INR20 crore one-off interest paid due to under-budgeted advance tax estimate; expected not to recur, factored into FY27 outlook.

themes.label: Demand recovery
themes.note: Strong Akshaya Tritiya sales and encouraging wedding-related consumer demand momentum continuing into Q1 FY27.

themes.label: Debt reduction
themes.note: Non-GML debt reduced from INR1,300 crores to INR300 crores over 3 years; target to be fully non-GML debt-free in India in FY27, possibly by H1.

themes.label: Candere turnaround
themes.note: Candere revenue grew 160% in FY26 and turned PAT positive from H2 FY26, with 50-55 new stores planned for FY27.

themes.label: SSSG divergence South vs non-South
themes.note: Non-South SSSG accelerated much more than South this quarter, a bigger gap than seen in prior quarters.

themes.label: Franchise (FOCO) expansion strategy
themes.note: Expansion remains predominantly franchise-based, requiring limited incremental capital from the company; Middle East franchise conversion discussions with Arab investors ongoing but unconfirmed.

themes.label: Margin sustainability
themes.note: India PBT margin expected to hold at 5.5-5.6%, but one-off gains from silver/platinum and procurement pattern changes are not expected to recur in FY27.

themes.label: Gold price volume trade-off
themes.note: Rising gold prices reduce purchase volumes as customers work within a fixed INR budget; company mitigates via studded jewellery push and lower-purity gold options.

key_takeaways: Q4 has been fantastic. The pickup in momentum we witnessed during the third quarter continued during the last quarter, and we ended up the financial year on an excellent note.
While consolidated revenue and PAT growth for the quarter have been 66% and 118%, respectively, stand-alone business recorded revenue growth of 68% and PAT growth of 97%, respectively.
For the full financial year, we recorded a consolidated revenue in excess of INR35,700 crores and a PAT of INR1,350 crores.
During the last financial year, we launched 129 showrooms across Kalyan and Candere formats, including the first Kalyan showroom in the U.K.
The year also saw a reduction of debt in India by INR360-odd crores, in line with the already announced plan to pay down the non-GML debt in India completely.

FY 2026 also saw Candere growing its revenue by 160% on the back of very strong same-store sales growth and aggressive network expansion. More importantly, Candere turned PAT positive from the second half of FY 2026.
In line with our announced dividend policy, Board of Directors has recommended a dividend of approximately INR257 crores, payout of around 20% of the net profit generated during FY 2026.
During the ongoing financial year, we plan to open 150 showrooms across Kalyan, Candere and the new regional brand.
We witnessed strong growth in our Akshaya Tritiya sales this year, and we continue to see encouraging momentum in consumer demand, especially around the wedding purchases during the current quarter.
pressing_questions: So just if you can give clarity on what led to such a big divergence [in South vs non-South SSSG]?
Given the strong profitability that you have witnessed in FY '26, is there a possibility that you might be able to pay that off entirely by, say, by H1 FY '27 end? [non-GML debt]
So, hypothetically, if that conversion happens [Middle East FOCO to franchisee conversion], broadly maybe INR800 crores to INR1,000 crores worth of cash flow gets generated?

And your growth strategy of FOCO-based growth and you have given an outlook of 70 stores. Based on that, if I have to look at a 2-year out or a 1-year out absolute debt number, is it fair -- is it possible to share that?

ALIVUS.about: Glenmark Life Sciences, a subsidiary of Nirma Limited, a diversified conglomerate with interest in consumer products, cement, chemicals and pharmaceuticals. It is a leading developer and manufacturer of select, high-value, non-commoditized, active pharmaceutical ingredients (APIs) in chronic therapeutic areas. The company further operates in Contract Development and manufacturing operations to offer services to specialty Pharmaceutical companies.

quarters.summary: Alivus reported Q1 FY'27 revenue growth of 6.4% YoY to INR640 crores, with strong non-GPL growth (26.5% YoY) offsetting a steep GPL decline (-52.6% YoY) due to inventory rationalization. Management guided FY27 revenue growth of 10-12% skewed to H2, EBITDA margins sustained at 30-32% (with potential upside to ~34% in steady state), while flagging geopolitical/war-related raw material cost pressure (solvents and KSM) as the key reason for conservative guidance despite current 36.6% EBITDA margin. GPL is expected to be flattish for FY27 with H2-weighted recovery; non-GPL and CDMO momentum expected to continue, supported by new launches and a robust HP API pipeline.

subsections.label: Profitability drivers
points: Favourable product mix and newer launches helped improve gross margins to 60.2%, an increase of 510 basis points YoY.
Enhanced operational efficiencies and forex gains supported a 650 basis points YoY improvement in EBITDA margins to 36.6%.
Margins reflect the quality of growth and disciplined execution.
Rupee depreciation is currently favoring the company as a net exporter, aiding exchange gains.

subsections.label: Gross margin sustainability discussion
points: Management attributed gross margin improvement to two main reasons: new launches and operational efficiency.
Margins from launches are not expected to fully drop off because the company is always ready with second-generation processes and markets are still opening up for recently launched molecules.
Operational efficiency gains are described as incremental and expected to continue delivering benefit.
Management indicated the ~60% gross margin level should broadly hold in the near term, with normal quarter-to-quarter variability.

subsections.label: EBITDA margin guidance rationale
points: Management stated it could guide to a better margin, even up to 34%, but is being cautious due to the war situation and its impact on raw material prices.
As a company, management stated it has always been conservative — communicating what it can deliver, with any upside being additional.
CFO noted that if GPL revenue recovers in H2 FY27, blended EBITDA margin could moderate from the current 36.6% towards around 34% in a steady-state scenario, which is factored into the 32% guidance.

subsections.label: R&D spend outlook
points: R&D spend as % of sales has been rising and is expected to settle at a steady state of around 4%.
R&D investment is largely API-focused, including new API development and second-generation/next-generation process development to keep margins comfortable.
A smaller CDMO-related R&D element supports customers with analytical and regulatory work for specialty CDMO projects, including 505(b)(2) filings.
Management does not expect rising R&D spend to negatively affect PAT margins; PAT is expected to remain healthy as pipeline strength drives both growth and margins.

subsections.label: Cash flow and balance sheet
points: Free cash flow generation was strong during the quarter.
Company continues to remain debt-free.
Receivables are coming in a timely manner, with no defaults seen.
A slight increase in inventory is expected going forward as the company builds inventory to support customers in a timely manner and lock in more predictable prices amid rising raw material costs.
Balance sheet cash position viewed as a good position to face uncertainty and challenges effectively.

key_figures.label: CVS + CNS contribution to top line
Chronic therapies contribution to top line

subsections.label: GPL business
points: GPL business decline was a result of inventory rationalization at the customer.
Q4 was pretty strong, followed by a dip in Q1.
Strong execution across the non-GPL portfolio helped offset the GPL impact.
GPL growth is expected to remain flattish in FY27; the business has historically been weighted towards H2, and a similar trend is expected this year resulting in stronger H2 performance.
GPL customer is an old, very big customer with more than 50 commercial products supplied; Q1 is not seen as an indicator of how the full year will go.
Management is confident that in a worst-case scenario, GPL growth for the full year will be flattish (consistent with the INR700-750 crore range delivered over the last 3 years).

subsections.label: Non-GPL business
points: Non-GPL growth driven by successful new product launches and strong demand across all geographies.
Recently launched products continue to gain scale across markets, providing greater diversification to the revenue base and a platform for sustainable growth.
Non-GPL business confirmed to be more margin accretive than the GPL business.
Healthy growth momentum in non-GPL business expected to continue, supported by a robust product pipeline, recent launches and sustained demand across all markets.

subsections.label: CDMO business
points: CDMO business performance varies quarter-to-quarter given its inherently lumpy nature.
Segment expected to gain momentum in H2 FY27, supported by contributions from newly added projects.
Two new CDMO contracts previously flagged for early H2 FY27 closure remain on track.
Current CDMO revenue comes from 5 projects; company is in active discussions on about 7 new projects, though these take time to fructify.
Focus remains on life cycle management and specialty CDMO (including 505(b)(2) filings); projects typically take about 1 to 1.5 years to get going, with regulatory approvals also not taking long.

CDMO growth is expected to grow faster than the overall business over the next 2-3 years, driven by 2 new projects kicking in and older projects returning, though management could not quantify a specific number.
CDMO margin (currently ~33%) is expected to see improvement as a mix between CDMO growth and new API launches, rather than from CDMO alone given its still relatively small overall volume.

subsections.label: Therapeutic mix
points: CVS and CNS continued to anchor growth during the quarter.
Chronic therapies remained the dominant contributor to top line.

subsections.label: High potent API pipeline
points: Pipeline remains robust with 617 DMF and CEP filings globally as on June 30.
HP API portfolio continues to advance, targeting an $82 billion TAM across 29 products in the active grid.
Of the 29 products: 13 validated, 7 in advanced stages of development, and remaining 9 progressing through lab development stages.
HP API commercialization pipeline starts off end of calendar '27 (aligning to FY28) with patent expiries, followed by a good run for the next 4 to 5 years.
Customers need to buy launch quantities and prepare for launch, so activity starts a bit earlier than the actual launch date, but projections for meaningful contribution are more FY28.

subsections.label: R&D focus areas
points: R&D investment is largely API-driven, targeting new API development and second/next-generation process development to protect margins.
Some CDMO-related R&D supports customers with analytical and regulatory work for specialty projects, including 505(b)(2) filings.

subsections.label: Solvent recovery technology
points: Company has introduced a membrane-based solvent recovery technology in addition to regular distillation, which is proving effective and could be scaled up.
This technology could improve solvent recovery by about 5% to 10%, though not all solvent can be recovered.

Net consumption of solvents is favorable for the company's processes, but a wide product basket means a much broader range of solvents is used than a company with a narrower portfolio, which has cost impact given rising oil prices.

key_figures.label: Reg market business share of total business

subsections.label: Solapur project
points: Solapur continues to progress as planned, with a little bit of delay; expected to be operational in early Q3 FY27 (pushed from prior Q2 FY27 guidance).
Part of the delay attributed to a slowdown related to labor and a few other factors.
Priority is to get Solapur Phase 1 and 1.1 on track; once built and audited by FDA or a European agency, ability to use Solapur for regulated markets improves significantly.
Management intends to trigger a regulatory inspection within a year of Solapur becoming operational, targeting a good run rate for the next 3 to 4 years servicing business with Solapur.
Company does not want to hurry Phase 3, as executing it quickly risks significant under-absorption; approach is calibrated, with Phase 3 execution delayed by about a year to Q4 FY27.
Once operational, Solapur will initially be loaded with large-volume intermediates for captive consumption and a backward integration block, keeping the facility busy.

Solapur can only service ROW (rest of world) business initially — for about a year — since it lacks regulatory market approval; over 80% of the business is reg market business which cannot come out of Solapur yet.

subsections.label: Ankleshwar and Dahej brownfield expansion
points: Ankleshwar and Dahej capacity expansions are on track and have not been pushed out (only Solapur has been delayed).
Dahej getting 160KL and Ankleshwar getting 110KL of additional capacity, with brownfield manufacturing infrastructure completion expected in 8-9 months.
Priority on capex has continued to be completion of the Dahej and Ankleshwar expansions since over 80% of business is regulated market business which these reg sites service.
These brownfield expansions, combined with Mohol, give comfort in managing business for this year and going into next year.

subsections.label: Taloja R&D center
points: Construction at the Taloja R&D center has begun in earnest and is on schedule.

subsections.label: Capacity sufficiency for growth
points: Capacity is not seen as a challenge for growth at Alivus; facilities are described as top of the line.

Current capacity, at 80-90% utilization, considered sufficient to support double-digit growth guidance for FY27 and expected double-digit growth in FY28, even before Solapur gets regulatory inspection.

key_figures.label: Solapur ROW business parking period before wider markets

subsections.label: Geographic demand
points: Broad-based growth was seen across all markets during the quarter, highlighting the strength of the diversified business.
Non-GPL growth driven by strong demand across all geographies.

subsections.label: Pricing and customer engagement on raw material costs
points: Raw material prices have increased, though not very steeply, and the company has managed to pass on part of the increase to customers.
Customers have given positive feedback acknowledging the situation and are willing to support price pass-through, but this cannot be done across the board.
This customer engagement exercise for cost pass-through, previously done occasionally, is now being conducted more regularly to avoid margin erosion.

subsections.label: CDMO market positioning
points: Indian CDMO companies are seen to be in a sweet spot gaining more traction, especially demand from the U.S.
Alivus's CDMO focus remains on life cycle management and specialty projects rather than broad-based CDMO expansion.

subsections.label: Acquisition strategy
points: Company has around INR800 crores on its balance sheet and has been considering acquisition opportunities.
Capacity/facilities acquisition is not a priority since Alivus already has sufficient top-of-the-line capacity; would not spend money on facilities.
Interest lies in pipeline acquisitions only if from a very different platform/pipeline than what the company already has.
Company is actively looking at synergistic opportunities that add greater value beyond a simple '1 plus 1 equals 2' combination — aiming for '1 plus 1 equals 3 or 4'.
Strategy described as 'API plus' — expanding laterally to get more out of existing and new portfolio, and leveraging platform technology for both API and CDMO.

subsections.label: Execution priorities
points: Top execution priority is getting new product launches right, building on strong contribution from launches over the last 3 quarters.

Launch momentum is strong because patents do not expire simultaneously across all markets, giving newer products significant volume growth opportunities as patents expire in different markets at different times.
Key priority is to service across markets effectively as this launch pipeline develops.

subsections.label: Compliance track record
points: Company has had a decent compliance track record; received VAI status in Ankleshwar and NAI status in Dahej from FDA.

As a result, fewer major regulatory agencies are currently coming for audits this year, making the audit scenario relatively light from major agencies, although customer audits continue to happen normally.
No major compliance pressure issues currently foreseen.

subsections.label: Geopolitical/war-related cost pressure
points: The ongoing war situation is impacting raw material prices, prompting management to remain cautious in guidance despite confidence in a potentially higher margin.
Raw material price increases started with solvents and are now moving towards KSM (key starting materials).
Company is actively monitoring raw material cost impact almost on a daily basis and engaging with customers more regularly (versus occasionally before) to pass on costs and protect margins.
Rising oil prices are impacting solvent costs given the company's wide product basket and correspondingly wide solvent usage range.

subsections.label: GPL business volatility
points: GPL business saw a steep 52.6% YoY decline in Q1 due to customer inventory rationalization, creating investor hesitance about whether it could offset non-GPL efforts if it were to degrow materially for the full year.
Management maintains confidence GPL will be flattish for the full year based on historical H2-weighted patterns and the scale/diversity of the customer relationship.

subsections.label: Capacity execution risk
points: Solapur has experienced delay, partly due to a slowdown related to labor and other factors.

Analyst raised concern that with utilization at Ankleshwar/Dahej already high (80-90%+), capacity constraints could challenge growth in H2 FY27 or FY28 if further delays occur; management clarified Ankleshwar and Dahej expansions remain on track and only Solapur has slipped.

subsections.label: Overall outlook
points: Company guiding for revenue growth of 10% to 12% in FY27 with growth skewed towards H2 FY27.

Company remains confident of sustaining EBITDA margins in the 30% to 32% range, though management indicated it could guide higher (up to 34%) if not for caution around the war situation's impact on raw material prices.
GPL growth expected to remain flattish in FY27 with H2-weighted performance; non-GPL growth momentum expected to continue.
CDMO segment expected to gain momentum in H2 FY27 and grow faster than the overall business over the next 2-3 years.
FY27 capex guidance of approximately INR540 crores.

guidance_ledger.statement: We are guiding for revenue growth of 10% to 12% in FY '27 with growth skewed towards H2 FY '27.
We also remain confident of sustaining EBITDA margins in the 30% to 32% range.
We can guide to a better margin, frankly. I mean, even up to 34%. The issue is this war situation... so we need to be a little bit cautious.
We expect to incur a capex of approximately INR540 crores in FY '27.

While growth in the GPL business is expected to remain flattish in FY '27... we expect a similar trend to play out this year, resulting in a stronger H2 performance... we are pretty confident that in the sort of worst case, it will be a flattish growth.
We expect the healthy growth momentum in the non-GPL business to continue, supported by a robust product pipeline, recent launches and sustained demand across all markets.
We can expect the segment to gain momentum in the second half of the year, supported by contributions from newly added projects.
On the capex front, Solapur continues to progress as planned. There's a little bit of a delay, but it's going to be operational in early Q3 of FY '27.
Construction at Taloja, the R&D center has begun in earnest, and it will happen on schedule.
It starts off in the end of calendar '27 with the patent expiries, but then we have a good run for the next 4 to 5 years with the pipeline on HP API... our projections are more FY '28.
You previously highlighted that you're expecting to close 2 brand new CDMO contracts in early H2 FY '27. So is that still on track? -- It's on track.
We should sort of end up at a steady state of around 4%.

guidance_ledger.horizon: within a year of Solapur operational
guidance_ledger.statement: We are going to trigger an inspection within a year from some major regulatory agencies... then that's a big milestone... we get a good run rate for the next 3 to 4 years for servicing the business with Solapur.
Solapur is not going to run empty... capacity is not a challenge for the growth at Alivus... this capacity enough to grow at double digits for FY'27, FY'28 before Solapur gets inspection.
We expect that margin improvement will come as a mix between CDMO as well as the new launches.
The capacity we are adding today will take us from 1,198 KL in FY24 to a planned 2,690 KL by FY28, positioning the company to drive sustained growth well beyond FY28.
Solapur Phase 1 is progressing as planned and is expected to be operational in Q2 of this year.
We hope to close 2 new deals in the second half early second half of this year.
We expect that when Solapur starts off, we should start off with a robust 40% to 50% utilization and then probably take it up to 60%, 70% in the following year.
Capacity utilization in the brownfield will be pretty rapid in terms of bringing it at the 80%, 90% level in a matter of 2 to 3 quarters.
It would go down a little bit more because Solapur will be coming online soon and some of the brownfield capacity will also be coming in... it would come back up once the utilization picks up.
We would comfortably be able to add another 700 to 800 kiloliters of capacity of API capacity in Solapur... that should give us a runway for at least 3 to 4 years in Solapur.

risk_register.risk: Geopolitical/war situation impacting raw material prices (solvents and KSM)
risk_register.note: Management flagged the war situation as the key reason for conservative EBITDA margin guidance, with raw material price increases moving from solvents to KSM; company monitoring costs daily and engaging customers more regularly on pass-through.

risk_register.risk: GPL business volatility/inventory rationalization
risk_register.note: GPL declined 52.6% YoY in Q1 due to customer inventory rationalization, but management expects flattish full-year growth based on historical H2 weighting and long-standing customer relationship.

risk_register.risk: Solapur project delay
risk_register.note: Solapur commissioning pushed to early Q3 FY27, partly due to a slowdown related to labor and other factors; Phase 3 further out to avoid under-absorption.

risk_register.risk: Capacity constraints amid high utilization
risk_register.note: Analyst raised concern about high utilization (80-90%+) at Ankleshwar/Dahej limiting growth, but management clarified these expansions remain on track and capacity is not viewed as a constraint on double-digit growth.

risk_register.risk: Rising oil prices impacting solvent costs
risk_register.note: Wide solvent usage range due to broad product basket makes the company sensitive to oil price increases, partly mitigated by new membrane-based recovery technology.

risk_register.risk: Regulatory/compliance pressure
risk_register.note: Company received VAI in Ankleshwar and NAI in Dahej from FDA, leading to fewer major agency audits this year; customer audits continue normally with no major compliance issues foreseen.

risk_register.risk: Tariff and regulatory uncertainty disrupting global supply chains, elevated logistics and energy costs
risk_register.note: Factors have been disrupting supply chain and creating uncertainty across global markets during the last 2 years; resilience and agility deemed critical.

risk_register.risk: Geopolitical conflicts / war impacting global demand and supply chains
risk_register.note: FY27 expected to be a bit challenging because of the war; supply chains have a little bit of constraint, though demand visibility remains good.

risk_register.risk: Raw material cost inflation (solvents, other materials)
risk_register.note: Solvent costs increased significantly (12-13% of overall cost); certain raw materials have gone up and likely to increase further, though customers are agreeable to absorb reasonable price increases.

risk_register.risk: Freight/logistics cost increase
risk_register.note: Freight was impacted starting February 28, 2026; largely passed on to customers.

risk_register.risk: Fire incident at Dahej plant
risk_register.note: Impacted intermediate side of facility; INR20 crores loss booked in other expenses in Q4 FY26; some spillover into Q1 FY27 expected but not very significant.

risk_register.risk: Loss of PLI (Production Linked Incentive) benefit
risk_register.note: Margin improvement over FY24-FY26 was achieved despite the loss of PLI benefit.

risk_register.risk: Price erosion in base business
risk_register.note: Non-GPL, non-CDMO base business saw price erosion of about 5.5%; overall portfolio erosion of around 4.5% due to price reductions on some products.

risk_register.risk: GPL business volatility/wavy growth
risk_register.note: GPL business growth described as 'wavy' and not expected to stay in line with the faster-growing non-GPL business.

risk_register.risk: Regulatory inspection pending for capacity ramp-up (Solapur/Ankleshwar/Dahej)
risk_register.note: Company hopes to get Solapur inspected soon to enable further expansion ramp-up; separate query on Ankleshwar/Dahej inspection status.

themes.label: Non-GPL diversification
themes.note: Non-GPL grew 26.5% YoY, offsetting a 52.6% YoY GPL decline and providing greater revenue diversification and sustainable growth platform.

themes.label: CDMO recovery
themes.note: CDMO grew 3.8% YoY with 2 new contracts on track and 7 active project discussions; segment expected to gain momentum and grow faster than overall business in H2 FY27 and beyond.

themes.label: Margin expansion
themes.note: Gross margin rose 510bps YoY to 60.2% and EBITDA margin rose 650bps YoY to 36.6%, driven by launches, mix, operational efficiency and forex gains.

themes.label: Capacity expansion (Solapur)
themes.note: Solapur pushed to early Q3 FY27 due to labor-related delays, while Ankleshwar and Dahej brownfield expansions (160KL and 110KL) remain on track.

themes.label: Geopolitical/war-related cost pressure
themes.note: War situation driving raw material (solvent and KSM) price increases, prompting conservative EBITDA margin guidance despite potential for up to 34%.

themes.label: High potent API pipeline buildup
themes.note: 29 products in active HP API grid targeting an $82 billion TAM, with 13 validated; commercialization expected to start end of calendar 2027 (FY28).

themes.label: Capital allocation shift post-Nirma
themes.note: Company holds ~INR800 crores cash and is evaluating synergistic acquisitions focused on differentiated pipelines rather than facilities, given existing capacity sufficiency.

key_takeaways: We reported revenues of INR640 crores, which is a 6.4% year-on-year growth during the quarter.
Our non-GPL business delivered strong growth of 26.5% year-on-year, driven by successful new product launches and strong demand across all geographies.
GPL has been muted as a result of inventory rationalization... a decline of 52.6% year-on-year.
While growth in the GPL business is expected to remain flattish in FY '27... we expect a similar trend to play out this year, resulting in a stronger H2 performance.
A favourable product mix and newer launches helped improve gross margins to 60.2%, an increase in 510 basis points year-on-year.
Enhanced operational efficiencies and forex gains also supported 650 basis points Y-o-Y improvement in EBITDA margins to 36.6%.
Our CDMO business recorded 3.8% Y-o-Y growth during the first quarter.
The pipeline remains robust, with 617 DMF and CEP filings globally as on June 30.
We are guiding for revenue growth of 10% to 12% in FY '27 with growth skewed towards H2 FY '27. We also remain confident of sustaining EBITDA margins in the 30% to 32% range.
pressing_questions: Is 60% gross margin sustainable given last 3 quarters of material improvement, or will it normalize as new launches mature? (Ahmed, Unifi Capital)
Given the 30-32% EBITDA margin guidance appears conservative relative to sustainable gross margins, why not guide higher? (Ahmed, Unifi Capital)
What gives confidence that full-year GPL will be flattish (INR700-750 crores range) despite the steep Q1 decline, and investor hesitance about this offsetting non-GPL gains? (Ahmed, Unifi Capital)

Solapur Phase 3 appears pushed out by another year and even FY27 capacities delayed by a quarter or two — why the delay, and how is capacity being planned given high utilization at existing sites? (Pratik Kothari, Unique PMS / Ahmed, Unifi Capital)
With INR800 crores on the balance sheet, what is the acquisition strategy — facility-focused or pipeline-focused? (Yog Rajani, Omega Portfolio Advisors)
How many new CDMO customers/products have been added in the last 2-3 quarters, and how are inquiries trending? (Bhawana Israni, Ambit Asset Management)

quarters.summary: Alivus Life Sciences reported FY26 revenue of INR2,552 crores (up 6.9% YoY) with EBITDA margin of 33.6% (highest in company history) and reaffirmed confidence in sustaining EBITDA margins in the range of 30%-32% going forward; capex of ~INR540 crores planned for FY27, fully funded through internal accruals, focused on Solapur greenfield and R&D platform, with capacity expansion from 1,198 KL (FY24) to a planned 2,690 KL by FY28.

key_figures.label: Loss due to fire booked in other expenses

subsections.label: Cash Flow Utilization Shift
points: Prior to FY24, while the operating engine was strong and consistently generated cash, a large part of that cash was upstreamed (to parent).
FY24 marked a clear inflection point in how the company utilizes its cash, moving towards capex investment, dividend payouts and building a cash reserve.

Over the last 2 years, cash from operations of about INR984 crores was generated, of which INR472 crores was invested in capex, INR61 crores paid as dividend, resulting in a war chest of INR451 crores.
Entire FY27 capex of INR540 crores (including carryover commitments from FY26 and fresh capital investments) will be funded through internal accruals.

subsections.label: Margin Drivers
points: Gross margin improvement driven by new launches, product mix and operational efficiency.

EBITDA margin improvement despite loss of PLI benefit, driven by favorable product mix, disciplined cost management, operational efficiencies and increasing focus on high-value differentiated products.

Margin improvement has 3-4 factors: operational efficiency, better cost processes implemented, CDMO mix improvement (from 6% of revenue in FY25 to 7% in FY26), and good launches of generic API in multiple markets.
Margins improved from 28% in FY24 to 34% in FY26 reflecting that new business being added is more profitable and value accretive.
Backward integration (Ankleshwar, Dahej to Solapur) has not yet contributed significantly to margins as Solapur is not yet online; expected to contribute once Solapur commissions in Q2.

subsections.label: Fire Incident at Dahej
points: Fire impacted only the intermediate side of the Dahej facility; the API/finished area was intact, so no significant production/sales delays experienced.
Some spillover into Q1 expected but not very significant; company hopes to tide over by Q1.
Loss due to fire of INR20 crores booked in other expenses in Q4, causing a jump in that line item.

subsections.label: Employee Cost
points: Employee cost jump in the quarter is organic, driven by accrued performance bonuses payable to employees given the company's good performance.

subsections.label: Forex Impact
points: As a net exporter, rupee depreciation benefits the company; forex gains booked in other income for the year and quarter.

subsections.label: Raw Material / Cost Inflation
points: Freight costs impacted starting February 28, 2026, largely passed on to customers.
Solvent costs increased significantly but contribute only about 12-13% of overall cost, so overall impact is not expected to be significant.
Company is in touch with customers regarding added freight/material costs; most customers are agreeable to absorb the added cost.
Operational costs expected to remain stable even in a war situation because the company moved away from gas to operating briquette boilers, avoiding impact from gas shortages or price hikes.
Certain raw materials have gone up and are likely to go up further; customers have given a green light to absorb reasonable price increases.

subsections.label: Asset Turnover Outlook
points: Asset turnover could temporarily go down below 2 as Solapur and brownfield capacity come online, but expected to come back up once utilization picks up.
Company's asset turnover remains comparatively strong versus industry.

subsections.label: Non-GPL vs GPL Mix
points: Non-GPL segment's contribution to overall business steadily increased from 59% in FY22 to 71% in FY26, reducing dependence on the GPL business.
This growth reflects increasing diversification of portfolio and geographies, supported by robust demand across regulated markets and sustained momentum from new product launches.
Non-GPL business contribution expected to continue increasing going forward.
GPL revenues have remained relatively stable over the past 2 years while non-GPL revenues have grown at a CAGR of 7.5% during the same period.
In the non-GPL business, the company is already growing at double digit; GPL business is described as 'wavy' and not expected to stay in line with non-GPL growth.
As non-GPL business grows faster, contribution of GPL business will be much less going forward.

subsections.label: CDMO Business Recovery
points: Meaningful recovery in the CDMO business witnessed from Q3 FY26, as existing projects gained traction and newer projects scaled up.
CDMO business has grown 18%; CDMO share of revenue increased from 6% in FY25 to 7% in FY26.
CDMO fourth and fifth projects have kicked in nicely; some revival even on earlier projects; momentum expected to continue.
Company hopes to close 2 new CDMO deals in the early second half of FY27 (previously expected within next 6 months per last call, now moderated to early H2, could also come in H1).

subsections.label: Therapeutic Mix
points: CVS and CNS continued to lead growth during the quarter, together contributing 50% to top line.
Gaining traction in newer therapies like respiratory and anti-allergy, collectively contributing more than 10% of revenues.
Chronic therapies continue to outgrow acute segment.

subsections.label: New Product Launches
points: New launches are not a very significant contributor to top line revenue growth; ramp-up will continue to happen on those products.
Growth aided by new product launches and recovery in CDMO business.

subsections.label: High Potent API (HP API) Portfolio
points: HP API portfolio remains on development path with 28 products in the pipeline: 12 validated, 7 in advanced stages of development, remaining 9 progressing through land development stages.
Validation means the innovator/client has started taking small validation/exhibit batch quantities from the company for engaged molecules.
Only revenue contribution currently from HP API segment is sale of exhibit batch quantities, not very significant, since patent expiries for most HP APIs will start from 2028.
HP APIs typically attract better margins, but this remains to be seen as it plays out.
HP API contribution will start coming in from FY28 as customers order material 6-9 months before launches; will come from Ankleshwar and Dahej sites.

subsections.label: Pricing and Volume
points: Significant volume growth seen across all segments of the business.
Pricing environment has been reasonably stable for the company's markets and portfolio; war situation should not affect this pricing environment.
Overall portfolio price erosion of around 4.5% due to some price reductions given on certain products.
Price erosion in non-GPL, non-CDMO base business is about 5.5%, yet base business grew ~13%.

subsections.label: Contracting Structure
points: In CDMO, the company has longer-term contracts.
On the generic API side, fewer contracts exist and even where present, they are not very long term — typically 1-2 years at most.

Company prefers shorter/flexible contracts given the dynamic environment, avoiding being locked into cumbersome clauses; this flexibility helps in situations like the current war-driven price increase requests.

key_figures.label: Expected R&D spend as % of sales (ceiling)

subsections.label: R&D Focus Areas
points: Pipeline remains robust with over 611 DMF and CEP filings globally as on March 31, 2026.
R&D focus areas include flow chemistry, high potent API, iron complexes, and an evolving CDMO pipeline.
Company has commercialized one flow chemistry product which is doing exceedingly well, boosting confidence multifold in employing flow chemistry for more complex molecules.
Company is looking seriously into pellets and granules as a lateral expansion of the API business, referred to internally as 'API plus'.
Pipeline buildup is geared more towards more complex molecules.
R&D spend as % of sales is not expected to cross 4%; likely to be at 4% in the next year or two before settling down.
R&D investment historically (pre-Nirma) was focused on picking the right molecules for portfolio; post-ownership change, investment now extends laterally into new technology areas.

subsections.label: Strategic Differentiation
points: Company's DNA/path chosen 7 years ago (as Glenmark Life Sciences) was to have some element of uniqueness or higher entry barrier in offerings, aiming for differentiation to sustain the business profitably long-term.
Portfolio is more niche and chronic-oriented and less commoditized versus some peers, which affects the extent of benefit from broad price hikes but also limits downside from pricing pressure.

key_figures.label: Additional API capacity addable at Solapur
Ankleshwar and Dahej contribution to revenue

subsections.label: Solapur Expansion
points: Solapur Phase 1 is progressing as planned and expected to be operational in Q2 FY27.
Construction of new R&D center in Taloja, Navi Mumbai is underway.
Capacity being added will take company from 1,198 KL in FY24 to a planned 2,690 KL by FY28, positioning the company for sustained growth well beyond FY28.
Solapur Phase 1 comprises 370 KL for the backward integration (BI) block and 120 KL for the API block.
The 370 KL BI capacity at Solapur is for backward integration and will not contribute directly to front-end sales; should not be factored into revenue models.
Solapur is currently for the RoW market only; plan is very much to implement Solapur for regulated markets as well in future.
Solapur should give a good runway of at least 3-4 years once expansion beyond current capacity is ramped up, pending regulatory inspection.
Company can comfortably add another 700-800 KL of API capacity in Solapur beyond the current 120 KL on the 40-acre land bank.

subsections.label: Capacity Utilization Ramp-up Plan
points: Capacity utilization in brownfield facilities (approved, FDA-inspected sites) will ramp up rapidly to 80-90% in 2-3 quarters.
Solapur, being greenfield, is expected to start with a robust 40-50% utilization based on product mapping done, then increase to 60-70% in the following year.
Company has historically been calibrated in capacity buildout, not overly adventurous, building out in phases.

subsections.label: Ankleshwar and Dahej Capacity
points: Ankleshwar has further capacity to ramp up, but company intends to go slow there since it already contributes 65-70% of revenue.
Dahej is full in terms of capacity.

subsections.label: Backward Integration
points: Backward integration from Ankleshwar and Dahej to Solapur has not yet played out significantly because Solapur is not yet online and lacks capacity for backward integration in regulated plants.

Once Solapur is up and running (expected Q2), the company hopes to implement backward integration projects on a few key projects, with momentum building over time, offering scope for margin improvement.

subsections.label: Regulatory Inspection
points: Solapur is not yet commissioned/inspected; separate query about regulatory inspection status pertains to Ankleshwar/Dahej rather than Solapur.
Company hopes to get Solapur inspected soon to enable ramp-up of expansion there.

subsections.label: Geographic Performance
points: FY26 growth supported by strong execution across markets including Europe, Japan, Latam, RoW and India.
Mature geographies (India, Europe, Latin America, U.S.) are contributing quite evenly and significantly.
Japan is the newest geography, added in the last 4-5 years; relatively small compared to other geographies but growing well.
Overall growth across all geographies has been significant, aided by portfolio molecule selection tailored across geographies.

subsections.label: Nirma Ownership Milestone
points: FY26 marks completion of 2 full years with Nirma as promoter.
Partnership with Nirma brought enhanced financial strength, long-term stability and greater flexibility to invest in future growth opportunities.
Focus on building a more diversified and resilient business model, strengthening product portfolio, expanding capabilities and improving overall quality of business.

Pre-Nirma ownership focus was purely on portfolio selection (cherry-picking right molecules) with limited scope to go laterally; capex was geared to volume expansion and new product introduction as patents expired.

Post-ownership change, company invests more freely into lateral growth areas (flow chemistry, complex molecules, CDMO, API plus) since it isn't just limited by capacity buildup constraints for a fixed future portfolio.

subsections.label: Inorganic Growth Strategy
points: Company is actively looking at inorganic opportunities with the direction to enhance the existing platform.
Goal is to extract more value from the large and diverse API pipeline through lateral buildup of allied platforms.
No specific deal confirmed as imminent.

subsections.label: Geopolitical and Macro Headwinds
points: Uncertainties around tariffs and regulatory shifts have disrupted supply chains, elevated logistics and energy costs, and created uncertainty across global markets.
Ongoing geopolitical conflicts and uncertainties around global demand require continued watchfulness of the external environment.
Current year (FY27) expected to be a bit challenging because of the war; supply chains have a little bit of constraint, though demand visibility is pretty good.
War situation is prompting the company to seek price increases from customers on raw materials to offset cost inflation.

subsections.label: Cost Inflation
points: Freight costs impacted from February 28, 2026, largely passed on to customers.
Solvent costs increased significantly (solvents are 12-13% of overall cost), contributing to raw material cost increases, though overall impact not expected to be significant.
Certain raw materials have gone up and likely to increase further; customers have agreed to absorb reasonable price increases.
Yuan appreciation could affect import costs (raised by analyst, not directly quantified by management).

subsections.label: Fire Incident
points: Fire at Dahej plant impacted the intermediate side of the facility; some spillover expected into Q1 FY27, though not very significant.
INR20 crores loss booked due to fire in other expenses for Q4 FY26.

subsections.label: Margin Guidance
points: Company remains confident in the strength of business fundamentals and ability to sustain EBITDA margins in the range of 30% to 32% going forward.
Management notes it is a bit early to give whole-year margin guidance for FY27 given war-related supply chain constraints, though demand visibility is good.
With ongoing capex and continued investment in new technologies and products, company remains confident in ability to sustain the margin trajectory.

subsections.label: Capex and Capacity Guidance
points: FY27 capex of about INR540 crores planned, including carryover commitments from FY26 and fresh capital investments, entirely funded through internal accruals.
Investments focused on building new capabilities at Solapur (greenfield project) and strengthening the R&D platform.
Capacity to increase from 1,198 KL (FY24) to a planned 2,690 KL by FY28, positioning the company for sustained growth well beyond FY28.

subsections.label: CDMO Deal Pipeline
points: Company hopes to close 2 new CDMO deals in the early second half of FY27 (timeline moderated from a prior expectation of within 6 months, i.e., by June/July); could also come in the first half, a little later.

subsections.label: Growth Trajectory
points: Non-GPL business already growing at double digit; GPL business growth remains uncertain/wavy.
Priority remains a good margin profile and strong cash generation rather than pursuing growth at the cost of margins.

guidance_ledger.statement: We remain confident in the strength of our business fundamentals and our ability to sustain EBITDA margins in the range of 30% to 32% going forward.
We plan to incur a capex of about INR540 crores, which includes carryover commitments from FY26 as well as fresh capital investments; entire capex will be funded through internal accruals.
The capacity we are adding today will take us from 1,198 KL in FY24 to a planned 2,690 KL by FY28, positioning the company to drive sustained growth well beyond FY28.
I don't think we'll cross 4%; we'll probably be at 4% in the next year or 2, and then it should settle down.
Solapur Phase 1 is progressing as planned and is expected to be operational in Q2 of this year.
We hope to close 2 new deals in the second half early second half of this year.
We expect that when Solapur starts off, we should start off with a robust 40% to 50% utilization and then probably take it up to 60%, 70% in the following year.
Capacity utilization in the brownfield will be pretty rapid in terms of bringing it at the 80%, 90% level in a matter of 2 to 3 quarters.
It will start in FY28 because customers order material at least 6 to 9 months before the launches happen.
It would go down a little bit more because Solapur will be coming online soon and some of the brownfield capacity will also be coming in... it would come back up once the utilization picks up.
We expect the contribution from the non-GPL business to continue to increase going forward.
We would comfortably be able to add another 700 to 800 kiloliters of capacity of API capacity in Solapur... that should give us a runway for at least 3 to 4 years in Solapur.

themes.label: Non-GPL diversification
themes.note: Non-GPL contribution rose from 59% in FY22 to 71% in FY26, growing at double digit and reducing dependence on GPL business.

themes.label: CDMO recovery
themes.note: CDMO business recovered from Q3 FY26 with 18% growth and share rising from 6% to 7% of revenue; 2 new deals expected in early H2 FY27.

themes.label: Margin expansion
themes.note: EBITDA margin reached 33.6% in FY26 (highest in company history), up 360 bps YoY, despite loss of PLI benefit, driven by mix, cost discipline and efficiency.

themes.label: Capacity expansion (Solapur)
themes.note: Solapur Phase 1 (370 KL BI + 120 KL API) to be operational in Q2 FY27; total capacity to rise from 1,198 KL (FY24) to 2,690 KL by FY28.

themes.label: Geopolitical/war-related cost pressure
themes.note: War-related tariff, freight and raw material (solvent) cost inflation is being passed on to customers with their agreement; overall impact seen as manageable.

themes.label: High potent API pipeline buildup
themes.note: 28 HP API products in pipeline (12 validated) but meaningful revenue contribution not expected until FY28 due to patent expiries starting 2028.

themes.label: Capital allocation shift post-Nirma
themes.note: Post-Nirma ownership, cash generation is being redirected into capex, dividends and a cash war chest rather than upstreaming, with FY27 capex fully funded by internal accruals.

key_takeaways: Revenue for FY26 stood at INR2,552 crores, registering 6.9% year-on-year growth, with the non-GPL business leading momentum with 13% growth.
EBITDA margins of 33.6% were delivered for FY26, expanding by 360 basis points, highlighting inherent strength and operating efficiency of the business.
Non-GPL segment's contribution to overall business increased from 59% in FY22 to 71% in FY26, reducing dependence on the GPL business.
11 new products were added during the year, taking the current portfolio to 176 unique molecules; 49 new customers were added, taking total customer base to about 900.
Solapur Phase 1 is progressing as planned and is expected to be operational in Q2 of FY27; construction of new R&D center in Taloja, Navi Mumbai is underway.

Pipeline remains robust with over 611 DMF and CEP filings globally as on March 31, 2026; high potent API portfolio has 28 products in the pipeline (12 validated, 7 advanced, 9 in land development stages).
Company remains confident in sustaining EBITDA margins in the range of 30% to 32% going forward, despite geopolitical conflicts and global demand uncertainties.
FY27 capex of about INR540 crores is planned, entirely funded through internal accruals, focused on Solapur and R&D platform; capacity to increase from 1,198 KL in FY24 to a planned 2,690 KL by FY28.

HAPPSTMNDS.about: Incorporated in 2011, Happiest Minds Technologies Ltd is a next generation IT solutions & services Company[1]

quarters.summary: Happiest Minds announced a proposed combination with ITC Infotech that accelerates its USD1 billion revenue target from FY31 to FY28, with the combined entity expected to post ~18.1% EBITDA margin (FY26 basis) and a targeted 100 bps margin expansion from scale efficiencies; the merger is expected to complete over the next 15 months via CCI, shareholder and NCLT approvals, with detailed integration, leadership and cross-sell plans to be worked out post CCI approval and more clarity expected around the January investor call.

subsections.label: Margin outlook and drivers
points: No margin dilution expected for Happiest Minds shareholders; 18%/18.3% seen as the stable margin base which should improve given efficiencies of scale and synergy overlap.
Valuation modelling treated both companies on an 'A plus B' basis — individual growth trajectories combined without remodeling synergy uplift into the base projections.

Margin expansion (100 bps) to be driven through scale-based SG&A cost defrayal over a larger revenue base, consolidation of overlapping office space/facilities in common geographies, and improved operational efficiencies including better bench management and faster deployment turnaround.
Combined entity ranks 11th among Indian IT services companies by FY26 revenue, with combined FY26 pro-forma revenue of INR7,033 crores.

sections.title: Segment & Product Performance — Combined Entity Profile

subsections.label: Combined industry exposure
points: Industry exposure will span BFSI, CPG and retail, manufacturing, travel and hospitality, healthcare, high-tech and education, providing greater diversification across sectors and economic cycles.
Vertical mix: CPG and retail 28%, BFSI 20%, manufacturing and industrial 17%, travel and hospitality 12%, healthcare and Ed-tech ~6-7% each.
ITC Infotech brings 50+ Fortune Global 500 clients and 16+ FTSE 100 clients to the combined customer base of 800+ customers across 30+ countries.

subsections.label: ITC contribution within ITC Infotech revenue
points: ITC is not a very significant portion of ITC Infotech's revenues; there is some related-party transaction contribution (hotels-related), properly disclosed in ITC Infotech's filed financials.

sections.title: Product & Technology — AI Strategy and Platforms

subsections.label: AI capability complementarity
points: Happiest Minds' strength is on the digital/software side of AI and data, more generative AI oriented; ITC Infotech brings deeper capabilities in physical and plant/manufacturing/industrial AI given its strength in Industry 4.0, PTC and PLM.
Happiest Minds has its own AI platform, Rel(AI)Build; ITC Infotech has IQStudio and K-Fabrik — plan is to harmonize these platforms to add value to customers.

AI is central to strategy; market moving from experimentation toward enterprise-wide deployment of generative AI and agentic AI, requiring partners combining AI talent with data, cloud, cybersecurity and engineering capability backed by industry context.
Expanded partner ecosystem includes Microsoft, SAP, ServiceNow, PTC, Google, Amazon, various AI companies and leading cybersecurity providers, strengthening ability to deliver integrated solutions.

As a ~INR7,000-crore company, the combined entity will become a more important partner to ecosystem players (Microsoft, ServiceNow, PTC, Amazon, Google) in terms of both revenue delivered to partners and implementation support.

subsections.label: Geographic balance rationale
points: The combined business will be more geographically balanced across Americas (38%), Europe (31%) and rest of world (31%), giving greater talent depth, geographic reach and delivery capacity.

sections.title: Market & Customer Strategy — Cross-sell and Client Base

key_figures.label: ITC Infotech number of customers in portfolio

subsections.label: Cross-sell opportunity
points: The two client portfolios and service offerings are highly complementary, creating meaningful opportunities for cross-selling and deeper account penetration; ITC Infotech brings 500+ customers to the portfolio.

Happiest Minds' AI, data, digital engineering and cybersecurity capabilities can be taken into ITC Infotech's enterprise relationships; ITC Infotech's SAP, PLM, infrastructure, enterprise applications and transformation capabilities can be offered to Happiest Minds' customers, especially in retail, CPG, manufacturing and healthcare.
Larger, more strategic transformation/turnkey deals have a better chance of being won by a larger, combined entity able to string together all required capabilities.

No overlap seen so far among large customers of both companies; there could be one or two overlapping customers, viewed as positive since it enhances upside from cross-selling with limited channel conflict.
Detailed analysis of all 800+ customers (including tail accounts) has not yet been done and will take place a couple of months later.

subsections.label: Growth visibility parameters (post USD1bn target)
points: Management flagged three parameters investors should focus on beyond the headline USD1 billion target: a cross-sell index to be developed to track cross-selling extent; the number/value of large deal proposals generated and their conversion rate; and order booking/TCV movement to see if there is a significant jump in value.
More detailed articulation of these growth drivers expected in the coming months, potentially at the January investor call, depending on CCI approval timing.

subsections.label: Transaction rationale
points: Promoter Mr. Soota had expressed intention to pare down his stake to fund legacy not-for-profit organizations (SKAN) and capitalize his healthcare venture Happiest Health; had carried out bulk deals earlier but funding needs of these entities have since grown substantially.

Transaction combines complementary capabilities: Happiest Minds' AI, digital, product engineering, cloud, data and cybersecurity strengths with ITC Infotech's enterprise transformation, SAP, PLM, Industry 4.0 and industry-specific solutions.
Together will create a broader end-to-end proposition from strategy/design through engineering/implementation to modernization, operations, infrastructure management and security.
Industry consolidation and vendor consolidation trends, plus need for broader capabilities and greater execution scale for larger transformation programs, motivated the combination.
Cultural alignment between both customer- and people-centric organizations expected to help preserve Happiest Minds' entrepreneurial energy and agility while benefiting from scale.
Promoter divesting 22.1% of a total 44.2% holding for an aggregate cash consideration of INR1,330 crores; share swap ratio set at 25 ITC Infotech shares for every 81 Happiest Minds shares.

Post-merger, ITC Limited will hold 73.4% of the combined entity (alternate figure cited as 73.6%), with public shareholders (including Mr. Soota's 7.55%) holding 26.6%, above the 25% minimum public shareholding requirement.

Valuation multiples: Happiest Minds at 15.1x FY26 EV/EBITDA versus ITC Infotech at 13.6x; implied market caps of INR6,167 crores for Happiest Minds and ~INR11,920-12,000 crores for ITC Infotech, for an implied combined entity market cap of INR18,087 crores.

ITC Infotech is about 2.17x the size of Happiest Minds by revenue; ITC Infotech has made 2 acquisitions historically and grew revenue from INR2,246 crores in FY20 to INR4,718 crores in FY26, a ~14% 5-year CAGR.

Tranche 1 priced at INR390/share and Tranche 2 at INR400/share for the 22% of Ashok's 44% shareholding acquired, with an average transacted price of INR395/share against an implied/assessed valuation of INR405/share.
ITC Infotech synergy benefit target set at 10%.

subsections.label: Deal structure and governance
points: Board approved scheme of merger for amalgamation of Happiest Minds into ITC Infotech (not the reverse) partly due to Minimum Public Shareholding (MPS) requirements as a listed company.
Relative valuation and swap ratios based on reports from independent valuers PwC and Grant Thornton, reviewed for fairness and opined on by ICICI Securities.
ITC Infotech is currently a privately held company (100% owned by ITC); post NCLT approvals, Happiest Minds will be delisted and merged into ITC Infotech, then the combined entity relisted.

A rights issue by ITC into ITC Infotech will occur to fund the cash purchase of Mr. Soota's shares; ITC (100% shareholder of ITC Infotech) will subscribe, with no valuation implication as this was already factored into the ratios.
Open offer not triggered because the stake acquisition (11% + 11% tranches = 22%) does not cross the 24% control threshold.

subsections.label: Path to completion / near-term priorities
points: Steps to completion: CCI approval, shareholder agreement/approval, NCLT approval, then merger consummation — full process expected over ~15 months, with Tranche 1 approval expected Q3 FY27 (this year), Tranche 2 approval in Q1 FY28, and listing of the combined entity expected in Q2/Q3 FY28.
Until all regulatory approvals are received, both companies will continue to operate as separate entities in full compliance with law.

Integration plan to be developed to ensure smooth transition, incorporated into the scheme and discussions between parties, but discussions on leadership structure, roles and incentives will only begin once CCI approval is received.
Immediate priorities: maintain business momentum at Happiest Minds, ensure continuity for stakeholders, progress through merger process in disciplined manner, and ensure uninterrupted client service.

subsections.label: Integration and synergy realization
points: Cross-selling and leveraging complementary capabilities to be prioritized once CCI approval is received; operational leverage/synergies can only be meaningfully realized once entities are legally merged.

Synergy opportunities identified: cross-selling into each other's client bases (e.g., Happiest Minds' AI/data/digital/cybersecurity into ITC Infotech's enterprise relationships in retail, CPG, manufacturing, healthcare; ITC Infotech's SAP/PLM/infrastructure/enterprise apps into Happiest Minds' customers), participation in larger transformation programs, and optimization of the combined operating model.

19,000-employee combined base expected to yield synergies via better utilization, deployment leveraging and reduced bench across both organizations, though detailed workforce planning deferred to post-CCI-approval phase.
No specific employment retention contracts for top management exist; commitment made to retain people from both organizations to preserve complementary strengths on business and delivery sides.

Client overlap assessment: no overlap seen among large/top customers from either side so far; possible limited overlap in smaller/tail customers not yet analyzed in depth (detailed review of all 800+ customers expected a couple of months later).

subsections.label: Regulatory and process risk
points: Proposed transaction remains subject to applicable regulatory, shareholder and statutory approvals as well as other customary closing conditions.
Path to completion requires sequential approvals: CCI, shareholder agreement, NCLT, and then merger — a 15-month process seen by some analysts as long.

subsections.label: Currency risk on billion-dollar target
points: Growth targets and CAGR figures (14-15%) are computed in INR terms based on ITC Infotech's historical rupee reporting; conversion to the USD1 billion figure is done by dividing the rupee number by an assumed ~95-96 INR/USD rate, meaning currency movement could affect whether the dollar target is met.

subsections.label: Integration and retention risk
points: Analyst flagged risk of attrition on the sales team side during integration; no specific incentive plan yet finalized, though management committed to retaining people from both organizations.
No firm contractual commitment exists for top management continuity post-merger; discussions on structure and responsibilities to occur after CCI approval.

key_figures.label: Implied revenue CAGR to reach USD1bn

subsections.label: Outlook commentary
points: Management reiterated that reaching USD1 billion looked difficult earlier but is now well within sight given the combination; the target year has been moved up from FY31 to FY28, implying a revenue CAGR of ~14-15% over the next 2 years.
Combined entity operating margin target of 18.3%+ set for FY28.
Next detailed update on growth drivers, cross-sell metrics and AI revenue contribution expected in a few months, potentially at the January investor call, contingent on CCI approval timing.

guidance_ledger.statement: This transaction between Happiest Minds and ITC Infotech significantly accelerates our vision of becoming USD1 billion revenue Company, moving our target which was for FY31 to FY28.
which is hurtling towards a revenue top line of a billion dollars by FY28 and operating margins of a similar number expected to be around 18.3% plus.

ITC Infotech's margin percentage is about 18.3% EBITDA and we are talking about 18.1% for the combined entity. This is based on FY26 numbers. We did about 17.3% for the year, and they come in at 18.3% and that's what we have projected as an average of 18.1% for FY26.

planning to have a combined entity of a margin expansion of 100 bps points... That margin expansion will happen through scale... defray SG&A cost over a much larger base... operating efficiencies... improved turnaround time on deployment.

guidance_ledger.statement: the post-merger targets... reaching USD1 billion, which assumes 15% kind of a CAGR over the next two years... it is in INR terms.
We expect the merger to be consummated and completed over the next 15 months.

key_takeaways: Happiest Minds and ITC Infotech announced a proposed combination, significantly accelerating the vision of becoming a USD1 billion revenue Company, moving the target from FY31 to FY28.

Mr. Soota will divest 22.1% of his total 44.2% holding in two tranches for an aggregate cash consideration of approximately INR1,330 crores; Tranche 1 follows CCI approval (expected Q3 this year), Tranche 2 follows shareholder approval for the merger (expected Q1 FY28).

Under the scheme of merger, Happiest Minds shareholders will receive 25 shares of ITC Infotech for every 81 shares of Happiest Minds; listing of the combined entity on BSE/NSE is expected in Q2/Q3 of FY28.

On consummation of the merger, ITC Limited will hold 73.4% of the combined entity, public shareholders (including Mr. Soota) will hold 26.6%; Mr. Soota, with 7.55% holding, will be the largest individual shareholder but not a promoter.

Happiest Minds was valued at 15.1x FY26 EBITDA and ITC Infotech at 13.6x FY26 EBITDA; implied market cap of INR6,167 crores for Happiest Minds and about INR11,920-12,000 crores for ITC Infotech, with combined entity valued at about INR18,087 crores.

On a FY26 pro-forma basis, the combined businesses generated approximately INR7,033 crores in revenue, which would rank as the 11th largest IT services Company in India by FY26 revenue, with more than 19,000 professionals serving over 800 customers across more than 30 countries.

The combined entity's margin is expected to be around 18.1% (FY26 basis: Happiest Minds at 17.3%, ITC Infotech at 18.3%), with a targeted 100 bps margin expansion driven by scale efficiencies, SG&A defrayal, office consolidation and improved bench/deployment efficiencies.

Until all regulatory approvals are received, Happiest Minds and ITC Infotech will continue to operate as separate, independent entities; integration planning and cross-sell/GTM discussions will begin in earnest only after CCI approval.

quarters.summary: Happiest Minds started FY27 on a strong note with Q1 operating revenue of INR629 crores (+14.3% YoY in rupee terms, +2.6% QoQ and +6.7% YoY in constant currency) and EBITDA margin of 21.7%/operating margin of 17.5%, while continuing to invest in AI capabilities, platforms, talent and GTM. Management reiterated its FY27 revenue growth guidance of 12.5% YoY, citing strong pipeline, large deal conversions expected in Q3/Q4, and reaffirmed the FY28 aspiration of 15% growth as unchanged, while flagging geopolitical/war-related macro disruption and AI-capex sentiment as key risks to guidance.

subsections.label: Margin performance drivers
points: Operating margin at 17.5% of revenue was almost the same as last quarter and the same quarter last year.

Margin performance was despite a currency loss on forward contracts of about INR11 crores and a spike in provision for delayed collection/receivables of about INR5 crores, both compared to the previous quarter.
Adjusting for these two one-off instances, operating margin stands at about 19.75%, higher than the expectation of 17.5% to 18.5% (not a formal guided range).
PAT adjustments relate only to acquisition costs (accounting noise), consistently adjusted for over previous quarters; they do not account for forex losses or receivable provisions.

Annual wage increment traditionally occurs in Q2; structures up to C7 get increments in Q2 and C7/C8 in October, split across the year; this will pressure margins in Q2, to be clawed back through volume and value growth.

subsections.label: Capital efficiency
points: ROCE improved to 23.9% and ROE to 15.5%, both up significantly from 21.8% and 12.8% last quarter respectively — a focus area for the company.

subsections.label: Working capital
points: DSO improved to 92 days from 94 days in the previous quarter despite one-time provisions taken; management describes this as conservative accounting and states they are working to collect most of those provisions.

subsections.label: Demand environment
points: Demand environment remains mixed with discretionary spending continuing to be selective.
Enterprise technology investments increasingly shifting towards AI-led transformation, data modernization, cloud, cybersecurity, and productivity initiatives.
Pipeline remains strong and has grown both sequentially and significantly year-on-year, providing confidence in growth outlook.
Discretionary spend is being pushed toward specific areas: customers are optimizing support/maintenance/infra (the 'run' part of operations) using AI, and redeploying savings into AI and innovation.

subsections.label: Deal conversion / pipeline detail
points: A few mid-to-large size deals in the pipeline; a couple need to be converted to start contributing to revenue in Q3 and Q4.
Two large deals closed — one in Q1 and another earlier this month — beginning to ramp up and expected to reach three-digit (crore) size.
A few other deals closed where the first project is being implemented/executed, expected to lead to more such projects and engagements.
Strong program/initiative in place to expand presence within existing customers, expected to contribute to growth.
Two Arttha banking deals: one is being extended (not very hopeful), the other is taking time to close but expected to close in Q2.
Pipeline for non-linear growth platforms like EduWeave and Insurance-in-a-Box is reassuring.

Growth is coming increasingly from Middle East, India, Southeast Asia and APAC; constant-currency reporting is impacted because volume growth in these regions is divided by dollar terms — an accounting nuance management intends to address.

TCV is not disclosed since IPO; company internally tracking it now but growth philosophy is anchored on land-and-expand strategy rather than TCV; repeat business, customer additions, and customer cohort revenue split (50% from customers with the company >5 years and <5 years) are used instead to show revenue health and repeatability.

Deal sizes in pipeline are increasing; business commitments/new sign-ups are going up; new business pipeline changing for the better due to restructuring under two BUs (PDES and Infra/Security) and new business leadership.
Several much larger deals spanning multiple years are in the pipeline; hoping a couple close during the quarter to help growth in subsequent quarters.
Focus on six to ten key accounts with disproportionate attention, aiming to grow them into $20 million accounts (Hypo strategy).

subsections.label: Pricing
points: No systemic trend of customers negotiating rate decreases; some customers had rate increase discussions/negotiations as is typical annually; company has been able to effect rate increases with quite a few customers despite the environment.
Customers are asking for demonstrated impact of AI tools in SDLC; company working out metrics to show value delivered by these tools.

Contracting model (Fixed Price vs T&M) is a pricing/billing bucket, not indicative of whether work is outcome-based; most work within both FP and T&M buckets is outcome/output-based per SOWs even when billed T&M.

subsections.label: Industry vertical performance
points: Growth led by Healthcare & Life Sciences, up 22% YoY and 4% sequentially.
BFSI remained the largest vertical at 27% of revenues.
EdTech contributed 16% of revenue and delivered modest growth.

High-Tech recorded a strong sequential recovery, driven by a large engagement signed with a customer the company had been working with at smaller scale for a few months; large TCV engagement started in April; possibility of a second large engagement with the same customer; another customer recently signed expected to ramp up.

EdTech vertical risk has manifested and stabilized; recovery supported by EduWeave (digital EdTech platform for universities) built on experience from US and Philippines customers, with around 4 conversations in advanced stage and a couple close to signing; also targeting universities as a previously-unpursued segment.
Hi-Tech vertical grew 10% QoQ this quarter but this pace is not expected to repeat every quarter; growth still expected to continue.

subsections.label: Business unit (BU) performance
points: GBS (Generative AI Business Services) has grown handsomely albeit on a smaller revenue base; expected to continue growing well through the year given investments, market opportunities, and capabilities.
There is a pull-through from GBS into PDES revenues.

IMSS business unit saw a sequential drop driven by a one-time license revenue booked in Q4 that did not repeat in Q1; IMSS pipeline is strong and good growth is expected to be demonstrated by next quarter.

GBS deals are shifting from use-case-based/POC engagements toward two models: a 'pod' model where the company acts as an external engineering team, and bundled larger deals combining AI with digital transformation.
GBS margin improvement driven by improved utilization and cross-selling from other BUs into generative AI; original target was for GBS to become at least 10% of overall company revenue.
AI is not confined to the GBS bucket — it is embedded across the company, e.g., SecAIGenie platform used in security delivery is part of security offerings but not counted within GBS.

Plan to calculate total AI-led revenues (not just GBS AI-led revenue) across the whole company by carving out AI impact/relevance per project rather than by technology; exercise to be completed by end of September, to be shared at Q2 results.
Sales team being transformed: segregating hybrid BDMs into dedicated new-name (NN) BDMs and account managers, with associated changes and churn.

subsections.label: Operational metrics
points: Active customers flat at 306 versus last quarter.
Billion-dollar corporation customers increased by one to 92, contributing approximately 60% of revenue.

Repeat business remains strong, cited as 94.4% by Venkat and later stated by Joseph as having risen from 92.4% to 94.5%, reflecting customer relationships and confidence, and helped by investments in client engagement.
Utilization moderated marginally to 81% (down about 0.4 percentage points) — described as not a cause for concern but remains an area of focus.
Net hiring up by about 32 people.
Voluntary attrition improved from 17% to 15.4%.
