subsections.label: AI strategy — three priorities
points: Building a secure and reusable enterprise AI platform customizable for various domains, on top of which vertical solutions can be created.
Embedding AI across the entire software development lifecycle and across all services provided to customers.
Delivering measurable productivity and quality improvements for customers given how young/new many AI technologies are in the marketplace.

subsections.label: Enterprise AI platform
points: Provides a modular, secure, and model-agnostic foundation for enterprise AI adoption.

Key design principle is reuse — customers leverage reusable AI agents, flows, and accelerators rather than building every AI application from scratch, reducing implementation time and improving consistency and scalability with appropriate governance, security and human oversight.

subsections.label: Proprietary platforms
points: Enterprise AI platform together with Arttha, Insurance in a Box, Multi-Omics, and EduWeave platforms help customers accelerate AI adoption while combining proprietary IP with engineering capabilities.
These platforms create differentiated entry points into customer relationships, lead to non-linear growth, and support larger, long-term transformation engagements.

subsections.label: AI in software engineering and delivery operations
points: AI is helping shorten development cycles, improve code quality, strengthen documentation, and increase test coverage while accelerating application development/modernization; all outputs continue to undergo established engineering security and quality review rigor.
Reliable platform enables agentic software engineering within secure, governed enterprise environments where human engineers and AI agents collaborate throughout the development lifecycle.
AI automation embedded across quality engineering, infrastructure operations, cybersecurity, and data engineering.
Security, privacy, model governance, and human oversight built into both the enterprise AI platform and the delivery process/methodology.

subsections.label: AI monetization / productivity translation
points: Most customers use some form of productivity tool except in areas like hardware or high-risk industries; monetization from productivity gains remains a mixed bag.
For fixed price projects, AI productivity tools are included in estimation, with upside shared between company and customer while some is held back.

For T&M projects, a dedicated ~40-person Center of Excellence (COE) for AI in SDLC, with AI champions embedded in customer engagements to drive adoption/use of tools, acts as an additional revenue source.

subsections.label: AI hiring approach
points: Difficult to find candidates with more than six months to one year of AI experience given pace of technology change; company built in-house training to make new hires AI-native engineers (SDLC and AI solutions).
Hiring split across three buckets: replacement hiring, hiring for future capability (junior AI-skilled talent), and hiring for current project needs (accented toward AI skills where relevant).

subsections.label: Competitive positioning in AI
points: Creation of a dedicated Generative AI Business Unit (GBS) allowed the company to build depth in AI faster than peers relative to its size.
Company was an early adopter of classical AI/ML (2013-2014) helping retail, travel and other customers with personalization/recommendation engines and adaptive learning.
Relative to larger peers like TCS/Infosys, company believes it has more depth and differentiated offerings despite having fewer AI engineers in absolute numbers.
Pre-existing digital foundation and specialization positioned the company as a niche digital transformation player even before generative AI became mainstream.
Organizational agility ('agile always' tagline) allows the company to quickly adjust investment direction as AI technology evolves.

subsections.label: Geographic mix
points: Americas continued to be the largest market, contributing 57% of revenues.

Growth was increasingly diversified across other markets, with India and APAC growing approximately 9% and 10% sequentially respectively, providing greater balance and supporting long-term growth ambitions.

Growth increasingly coming from Middle East, India, Southeast Asia and APAC; constant-currency reporting is impacted since volume growth in these regions gets divided by dollar terms — a nuance management intends to address in how growth targets are accounted for.

subsections.label: Notable wins during the quarter
points: Selected as strategic data and AI partner for a leading North American energy infrastructure company.
AI-powered test automation engagement for a leading Australian insurance provider.
Digital commerce modernization program for a leading Indian multinational CPG company.
Salesforce-based product engineering engagement for a global consulting company.
Multi-year managed security services engagement with a major Middle Eastern retailer.

subsections.label: Client engagement investments
points: Investments in sales engine, account mining, and better client engagement contributing to larger deal sizes and improved pipeline.
Existing customers showing opportunities much larger in size than typical.
Sales team being segregated into new-name (NN) BDMs and account managers as part of transformation.
Hypo strategy: focusing disproportionate attention on six to ten key accounts with a goal of growing them into $20 million accounts.

subsections.label: Restructuring
points: Business restructured into two BUs — PDES (Product & Digital Engineering Services, inclusive of GBS pull-through) and IMSS (Infra, Security and related) — under new leadership (Maninder heading business), contributing to improving new business pipeline.
FY27 revenue growth guidance of 12.5% does not include contribution from potential acquisitions, though it includes acquisitions already completed/onboarded as of now.

subsections.label: Macro and geopolitical risk
points: Ongoing war and its impact on inflation and other factors, if it drags out for too long, viewed as the key risk ('elephant in the room') to sustaining Q1-level performance and to FY27 guidance.
Broader geopolitical disturbances contribute to overall macro uncertainty.
Possible 'reality check' emerging in the AI world itself regarding capex and spend levels, which could have a trickle-down effect on sentiment beyond the macro picture.

subsections.label: Demand-side caution
points: Discretionary spending remains selective/cautious, though redirected toward specific AI and innovation areas rather than eliminated.

subsections.label: Receivables/collections

subsections.label: Wage cost pressure
points: Annual wage increment cycle in Q2 (and partly October for senior structures) expected to pressure margins, to be offset via volume and value growth.

subsections.label: FY27 outlook
points: Company continues to focus on achieving FY27 revenue guidance of 12.5% growth, supported by strong pipeline visibility, accelerating AI adoption, and business model resilience.
Guidance implies a strong growth CAGR of around 5% for the remaining three quarters of the year.
Growth visibility is a combination of already-won deals ramping up, pipeline conversion (a few mid-to-large deals expected to convert in Q3/Q4), and expansion within existing customers.
FY27 guidance does not include contribution from potential future acquisitions.

key_takeaways: Operating revenue for the quarter stood at INR629 crores, representing 14.3% year-on-year growth in rupee terms. In constant currency, revenue grew 2.6% sequentially and 6.7% year-on-year.

We also maintained a healthy EBITDA margin of 21.7% while continuing to invest meaningfully in AI capabilities, enterprise platforms, talent, and go-to-market initiatives that will support our long-term growth.

Our AI portfolio continues to expand with over 100 AI agents, around 60 repeatable use cases, and a growing suite of AI-powered solutions and accelerators enabling faster deployment, greater reuse, and stronger customer outcomes.

From an industry perspective, growth was led by Healthcare & Life Sciences, which grew 22% year-on-year and 4% sequentially. BFSI remained our largest vertical at 27% of revenues, while EdTech contributed 16% and delivered modest growth. High-Tech too recorded a strong sequential recovery.

Geographically, the Americas continued to be our largest market, contributing 57% of revenues. Growth was increasingly diversified across our other markets with India and APAC growing approximately 9% and 10% sequentially respectively.

Coming straight to our adjusted profit after tax for the quarter, it stands at about INR80.5 crores, which is 12.3% of our total income, showing a growth sequentially of 12.9% and a year-over-year growth of 14.3%.
From a capital efficiency standpoint, ROCE improved to 23.9% while ROE stood at 15.5%, both up from 21.8% and 12.8% last quarter, so a significant improvement and this has been a focus for us.
On the strong start to FY27 and the visibility we have today, we continue to focus on achieving our FY27 revenue guidance of 12.5%.

Generative AI improves developer productivity, so how are we ensuring that the productivity gains translate into higher revenue rather than lower billing?
Where does Happiest Minds believe that it has a sustainable competitive advantage against companies like TCS, Infosys, or Persistent who are also heavily investing in AI?

MEDANTA.about: Global Health Limited is one of the largest private multi-specialty tertiary care providers operating in the North and East regions of India. The company has key specialties in cardiology and cardiac science, neurosciences, oncology, digestive and hepatobiliary sciences, orthopedics, liver transplant, and kidney and urology.[1]

quarters.summary: Medanta delivered strong Q1 FY27 growth with consolidated income up 26% YoY and improving EBITDA margins; Noida losses narrowed sharply and management now expects Noida to reach EBITDA breakeven earlier than previously guided. The company scaled up its Guwahati project to 650 beds with higher capex, continues to add beds and procedural capacity across the network, and remains confident in its long-term growth strategy and demand tailwinds, while not providing explicit margin guidance.

key_figures.label: Nonrecurring exceptional income (EPCG interest liability reversal)
Future capex requirement for expansion plan

subsections.label: P&L drivers
points: Growth was broad-based, driven by robust patient volumes, improved realization, continued scaling of Medanta Noida and sustained momentum across established hospitals.
Below EBITDA, YoY comparison reflects higher depreciation and finance costs associated with expanded asset base, particularly following commissioning and ramp-up of Noida.

PAT YoY comparison impacted by non-recurring exceptional income of INR196 million in Q1 FY26 relating to reversal of potential interest liability on EPCG, subsequent to merger of 100% subsidiary MHPL with GHL; excluding this onetime item, underlying earnings trajectory continues to remain very healthy.

subsections.label: Cost and cash flow management
points: CFO noted a continuous focus on cost line items including material cost, manpower cost and other cost items, with constant effort ongoing around this.
Overall cash flow has been strong over the previous year and continues in that direction with no decline seen in cash flow generation.
Cash flow, along with debt, is expected to fund future growth; the company has a strong balance sheet with very low leverage as of today and does not see any challenge on that front.

subsections.label: Capex clarification
points: The INR4,850 crores capex figure represents future capex required to complete announced projects; capex already spent is part of the balance sheet today.
In Q1 FY27, INR1,610 million of capex was incurred.

key_figures.label: Cluster 2 IPD volume growth excluding Noida

subsections.label: Demand drivers
points: Network continued to witness healthy growth in patient volumes, driven by increasing demand across key specialties, higher case complexity and sustained trust from patients and referring physicians.
ARPOB growth supported by favorable case mix, increasing contribution from high acuity specialties and improvement in operational efficiency.

ARPP introduced this quarter as an additional operating metric to provide perspective on revenue generation relative to inpatient volumes (as distinct from ARPOB, which measures revenue per occupied bed day); Q1 FY27 ARPP broadly similar to corresponding period last year, reflecting stable realization despite continued ramp-up of newer and existing facilities.

subsections.label: Structural demand tailwinds
points: Significant continued tailwind on demand across regions (especially central and northern India) with respect to flight to quality care.
Greater awareness of health across the board, with rising income levels and affordability increasing access opportunities.

Establishing presence in new territories (e.g., Lucknow, Patna) elevates quality of care awareness in those areas; similar dynamic anticipated for Guwahati, where increased demand and flow-through to Gurgaon from the Northeast has already been observed following the Guwahati announcement.
Company believes demand will continue to increase as access to healthcare and affordability improve; the real challenge will be delivering high-quality, ethical supply to meet demand.
No significant reduction expected in volume growth in the short term; still significant unfulfilled potential in Bihar and Eastern UP regions.

subsections.label: Attrition
points: Very negligible to no attrition seen at senior clinical levels across any hospitals in the last 6-18 months.
High attrition rates persist in nursing and among junior doctors, consistent with industry trends, but no significant shift among senior doctors.

key_figures.label: Cluster 2 total income growth YoY (including Noida)

subsections.label: Cluster reporting change
points: Beginning this quarter, previously referred-to 'mature hospitals' are now reported as Cluster 1 (Gurugram, Indore, Ranchi) and 'developing hospitals' are now Cluster 2 (Lucknow, Patna, Noida); composition of hospitals remains the same.

subsections.label: Cluster 1 performance drivers
points: Performance supported by 14% increase in inpatient volumes reflecting continuous demand.
ARPOB growth of 7% driven by favorable specialty mix and improved realizations.
Average length of stay improved to 2.8 days while occupancy remained stable at 63%, reflecting continued focus on operational efficiency without compromising patient care.
ARPP of Cluster 1 almost similar to previous corresponding quarter.

subsections.label: Cluster 2 performance drivers
points: Cluster 2 continues to be the growth engine of the company.
Excluding Noida, robust underlying performance highlighted by Lucknow and Patna delivering strong revenue and EBITDA growth with strong margin.
Increase in inpatient volumes and occupied bed days reflects continued capacity expansion across the hospitals.
ARPOB growth supported by favorable case mix and improved realization across the network.
Occupancy for Cluster 2 marginally lower YoY due to phased commissioning and capacity addition at Noida.

subsections.label: Specialty mix (oncology) clarification
points: Management clarified that cancer specialty share as reported in investor presentation actually increased from 13.7% to 14.4% YoY, contrary to an analyst's read of a decline.

Kidney and urology specialty share grew from 7.6% to 8.2%; urology and kidney cancer work is reflected in this department, not within the cancer specialty (surgical cancers, GI cancers, orthopedic cancers are captured in their respective specialties).
There is no significant impact on pricing related to cancer growth; change reflects sales mix shifts as other specialties grow faster than cancer ('pie of a hundred').
Quarterly seasonality affects specialty mix (e.g., more cardiac or gastro work in certain months); better to assess specialty mix on an annualized basis.
Cancer as a specialty, as reported, is growing, with no dip in growth.

subsections.label: Gurgaon vs Lucknow growth comparison
points: Gurgaon is a 15-year-old, 1,500-bed hospital running quite full, versus Lucknow, a 5-6-year-old hospital at about 750 beds — structurally different and not directly comparable.
Eastern UP population base is over 100 million versus a much smaller NCR/Gurgaon-Delhi-Haryana geographic base.
Lucknow has performed at exceptional growth rates not typically seen in Indian hospitals over its 5-6 years of operations; this level of growth is not considered 'normal'.
Gurgaon still shows double-digit volume growth despite its high scale (1,400-1,500 beds), a feat management considers notable.
Company believes it is the only major listed hospital chain to have grown consistently in double digits on volume (rather than tariff/revenue/realization) over the last several years.

subsections.label: Retail pharmacy segment
points: Company currently operates about 13 retail pharmacies outside the hospital network, some also running within clinics.
Retail pharmacy and lab businesses viewed as an extension of care offered to patients touching the Medanta ecosystem; will remain connected as one ecosystem including home care and clinics.
Expansion planned in markets with high patient demand such as UP and Bihar, where there is a significant shortage of high-quality, credible medicines.

Growth pace expected to increase modestly (e.g., from adding ~10 pharmacies a quarter to 15-20), but no rapid exponential growth (not going from ~20 to 100-200) expected in next 4-6 quarters; steady growth expected.
No current plans to extend retail pharmacy/lab footprint beyond existing hospital catchment areas.

key_figures.label: Joint replacements using robotic technology at Medanta Lucknow

subsections.label: Technology investments
points: Medanta Lucknow has done over 1,000 joint replacements using the latest robotic technology, on top of thousands of robotic surgeries executed across the system in every specialty, including complex cardiac and other specialties.
Continued investment in advanced technologies, multidisciplinary programs, and world-class clinical talent to strengthen position as a destination for complex care.

Adding complex LINAC procedures for cancer treatment, newer-generation radiation diagnostic capabilities in CT/MR, and significant scale-up in robotic procedures and equipment across the network (soft tissue and orthopedic robots).
Noida already has high-end equipment installed, including 14 OTs, latest radiation oncology machine, robot, and O-arm.

key_figures.label: Guwahati incremental capex for additional 250 beds

subsections.label: Guwahati expansion rationale
points: Scale-up of Guwahati project driven by revised building bylaws and National Building Code 2026, allowing additional FSI at no cost, additional ground coverage, and increased height restriction (to 60 meters), enabling more building on the same plot of land without additional land purchase.
Higher capex is linked not just to bed count but to expanded procedural capacity: operating rooms, cath labs, and LINAC/radiation oncology bunkers have all roughly doubled versus the prior plan.
Objective is to improve access to advanced tertiary and quaternary healthcare for patients across the Northeast, where significant demand currently travels outside the region for complex treatment.
Construction activity is already underway in Guwahati and most approvals are in place; management does not see any specific government Tier 2/3 city policy as necessary to expedite this project.

subsections.label: Project pipeline status
points: Construction underway at South Delhi; design, statutory approval and planning activities progressing at other announced locations.
Combination of bed and procedural capacity additions expected across Ranchi, Indore, Gurgaon, Lucknow and Patna.
Ranchi 100-bed facility already functional but still scaling up; Indore 80-bed acquired facility expected to help address missing cancer services in both Indore and Ranchi.

Noida bed additions reflect additional floors opening up in a single-tower hospital structure (unlike other facilities with multiple towers); operating rooms were fully commissioned on day 1, so no near-term incremental OT capacity increase is expected in Noida, though non-OT procedure areas (cath labs, radiation oncology) may expand as demand grows — no capex planned for this in the next couple of quarters.

subsections.label: International business
points: International patient revenue reflected strong growth despite current geopolitical tensions.

subsections.label: Domestic expansion into new geographies
points: Guwahati expansion aims to serve the Northeast region where patients currently travel outside the region for complex care.
Increased flow-through to Gurgaon hospital observed from the Northeast following the Guwahati hospital announcement.
As Medanta enters new geographies, it expects continued impact on existing facilities as brand awareness builds in those areas.

subsections.label: Talent strategy
points: Talent remains core to the delivery model; onboarding of 70+ doctors including 50+ senior clinicians across specialties strengthens medical depth and multidisciplinary care ability.
Continued addition of clinical capabilities across the network, including new departments/facilities and beefing up existing specialties with more doctors.

subsections.label: Retail/ancillary services strategy
points: Retail lab and pharmacy scaling continues opportunistically across already-identified markets and areas, viewed as part of a continuity-of-care ecosystem alongside home care and clinics.

subsections.label: Execution priorities
points: Broad strategic priorities do not change quarter to quarter; commitment to delivering exceptional clinical and operating performance across all 6 hospitals, which most consider fairly mature except for the newer Noida facility.
Continued focus on scaling Noida across clinical talent, beds, and operational/financial parameters, with performance currently ahead of internal expectations.
For the 5 existing hospitals (Gurgaon, Lucknow, Patna, Ranchi, Indore), continued focus on clinical quality, adding departments/facilities, and heavier investment in technology.

subsections.label: Geopolitical / international demand risk
points: International patient revenue grew despite current geopolitical tensions.

subsections.label: Manpower attrition risk
points: High attrition rates continue in nursing and among junior doctors, an industry-wide trend, though no significant senior clinician attrition observed.

subsections.label: Specialty mix seasonality
points: Quarterly seasonality can shift specialty mix (e.g., more cardiac or gastro work in certain months), making quarter-on-quarter specialty share comparisons less reliable than annualized views.

subsections.label: Financial risk management
points: CFO stated no challenge is seen on balance sheet leverage, cash flow generation, receivables or regulatory compliance fronts; continuous cost management effort ongoing on material and manpower costs.

subsections.label: Government policy uncertainty
points: Analyst raised the possibility of a revised government policy to expedite hospital setup in Tier 2/Tier 3 cities; management stated it does not see a need for such policy for its Guwahati project as approvals are already largely in place, though welcomed any such supportive policy for the industry generally.

subsections.label: Noida outlook
points: Based on current operating trajectory, company expects Noida to achieve EBITDA breakeven earlier than previous expectations.

Current occupancy at Noida hovering in the 30%-40% range, but management considers this number not particularly significant given continued rapid bed additions (occupancy will fluctuate as 30-50 beds are added every few months).
Volume growth in Noida has been robust, with bed growth increasing almost 30%-40% quarter-on-quarter.
No significant additional investment expected in most specialties at Noida (already has high-end equipment); liver transplant not yet offered there, though kidney and bone marrow transplant are.

subsections.label: Margin outlook
points: Company does not give explicit margin guidance.
Including Noida's reported losses (~INR5 crores for the quarter), consolidated EBITDA margin is already around 24%; excluding Noida, margin profile is already about 26%.

No significant structural reason foreseen for a significant negative impact on margins going forward; expect to benefit from operating leverage as Noida matures, with no very significant additional cost expected to come into Noida.

No significant structural difference in cost base is anticipated across units going forward, so margin should at least remain stable or continue to grow, though normal business cost growth (increments etc.) will apply.

subsections.label: Volume growth outlook
points: No significant reduction in inpatient volume growth expected in the short term across the network.
Lucknow and Patna continue to see growth in the 'upwards of 20%' range; Gurgaon still shows about 7%-10% volume growth despite its scale.
Growth in Lucknow/Patna units has been largely volume-linked as no tariff increase has been taken for long periods.

subsections.label: Capacity/expansion outlook
points: Announced expansion pipeline represents nearly 3,350 additional beds, providing a runway for sustainable long-term growth.
Company plans to continue adding both bed and procedural capacity (OTs, cath labs) across Cluster 1 (Gurgaon, Indore, Ranchi) and Cluster 2 (Lucknow, Patna) units going forward.
Retail pharmacy count expected to grow steadily (e.g., pace of new pharmacy additions per quarter may increase modestly) but not at an exponential/multiplier rate over the next 4-6 quarters.

subsections.label: CGHS rate hike impact
points: CGHS rate hike announced in October is fully factored into Q1 FY27 (April-June) results; benefit is not separately quantified/reported.
CGHS business represents only about 10%-12% of Medanta's overall business, so the hike is not expected to move the needle significantly on total company revenue, though it is beneficial.
Company's growth is mainly led by volume rather than tariff.

guidance_ledger.statement: Based on the current operating trajectory, we expect Noida to achieve EBITDA breakeven earlier than our previous expectations.
We don't give margin guidance as such... we should be benefiting from the operating leverage as Noida matures. There is no very significant additional cost that needs to come in Noida.
We still see about 7% to 10% volume growth in our Gurgaon facility... we don't, at least in the short term, see any significant reduction in this kind of growth volumes.
We continue to see growth in Lucknow and Patna in the upwards of 20% range.

80-bed facility, which we had acquired, which should come on board towards the end of Q2, maybe early Q3 in Indore... both of these facilities will help us to provide the missing services around cancer.
We will probably in the coming quarter, activate 2 more operating rooms. That should take our total operating room capacity to almost 44, 45 operating rooms.
We will also be commissioning hopefully in this coming quarter, which is Q2, additional cath labs. So we may add 2 to 3 cath labs.

It is unlikely you will see in the short term any incremental operating room capacity increase in Noida Hospital... you may see increases as the demand improves on increasing procedure areas which are non-OT like cath labs, radiation oncology, etc. But that will take some time... no capex planned in the next couple of quarters.
We have scaled up our plans for Guwahati, which will now have 650-bed super specialty hospital... estimated project cost of approximately INR9,700 million.
Together, our announced expansion pipeline now represents nearly 3,350 additional beds, providing a strong runway for sustainable long-term growth.

I don't think you will see our pharmacies go from a number of 20 to like 100 or 200 or anything like that in the next year... maybe adding 10 pharmacies a quarter, maybe it will become 15 or 20... you will see steady growth across the network.
On the larger overall P&L of the company or overall revenue of the company, I don't think that this is moving it by several hundred basis points or anything like that. But of course, it's beneficial.
We do expect this unit to break-even during the course of this year... during the course of the second half of this financial year, we do expect the unit to break-even.
On a cumulative basis... it really depends how quickly we are able to get the occupancy to somewhere in the 40% to 45% range... I don't want to give you a definitive commitment.
We will likely see some amount of bed addition in both the units in the first half of the year as itself.
2 operation theaters will be activated in Q1 itself and another 2 operation theaters, we hope to get activated either towards the later part of Q1 or at least by Q2.
Maybe if you are sitting in May of 2026, you could say May of 2029 hospitals could be up and running. But that may not be FY29 numbers, that may be more FY30 numbers.
The company expects to add approximately 500 beds across its existing hospitals with a minimum capex investment.
Medanta will add approximately 2,700 beds through 5 greenfield projects over the next 3 to 4 years.
Across the entire expansion pipeline, total project capex over the next 5 years is approximately INR 45,000 million.
The overall capex for the year will be somewhere around INR 800 crores to INR 900 crores.
Next year, it will be in the range of INR 600 crores to INR 700 crores.
We do expect to see this growth hit upwards of 20% as this unit scales, 20% to 30% like we've seen in some of the other units.
We do believe that as the complexity scales up, you will continue to see ARPOB growth... you may see some ARPOB benefits.
We do believe at some point in time you will see the challenges in the Middle East taper off... we do believe Bangladesh also as an international market will eventually come back.

risk_register.risk: Geopolitical tensions affecting international patient inflows
risk_register.note: International patient revenue grew 23% YoY despite current geopolitical tensions.

risk_register.risk: High attrition among nursing staff and junior doctors
risk_register.note: Continues to be at high attrition rate for the industry, though no significant senior clinician attrition seen.

risk_register.risk: Specialty mix seasonality distorting quarterly comparisons
risk_register.note: Certain quarters see more cardiac, gastro or medicine/respiratory work; better viewed on annualized basis.

risk_register.risk: Regulatory/policy uncertainty around Tier 2/3 city hospital setup
risk_register.note: Analyst referenced possible government policy changes; management said no specific need for it given Guwahati approvals already in place.

risk_register.risk: Higher depreciation and finance costs from expanded asset base
risk_register.note: YoY comparison below EBITDA reflects higher depreciation and finance costs particularly following commissioning/ramp-up of Noida.

risk_register.risk: Noida ramp-up losses / gestation period
risk_register.note: EBITDA loss at Noida declined sharply from INR236 million in Q4 FY26 to INR49 million in Q1 FY27; breakeven expected earlier than previously anticipated.

risk_register.risk: Middle East geopolitical situation impacting international patient inflows
risk_register.note: Despite some short-term challenges given the situation in the Middle East, management sees continued runway as Noida's international funnel activates and new countries scale up.

risk_register.risk: Bangladesh international market softness
risk_register.note: Management believes Bangladesh as an international market will eventually come back, implying it remains subdued currently.

risk_register.risk: Noida ramp-up / breakeven uncertainty
risk_register.note: Breakeven depends on reaching 40-45% occupancy range; cumulative annual loss level not committed to given uncertainty on accumulated losses.

risk_register.risk: War for clinical talent / manpower cost inflation
risk_register.note: Management flagged shortage of high-quality clinical talent and expects some war for talent on the clinical side, particularly as new competing hospitals open in Gurgaon.

risk_register.risk: New competitor hospitals opening in Gurgaon
risk_register.note: Two new competitor hospitals expected in Gurgaon around September-October; no senior clinician attrition observed so far, and management does not see this as a major demand risk.

risk_register.risk: Clinician/doctor capacity constraints in Lucknow and Patna
risk_register.note: Doctor capacity becoming an issue in Patna and Lucknow as units scale, requiring lateral hiring.

risk_register.risk: ICU/critical care bed constraints in Patna
risk_register.note: Patna significantly constrained in terms of need to add ICU and critical care beds; orders already placed for addition.

themes.label: Noida ramp-up
themes.note: Noida EBITDA loss declined sharply from INR236 million (Q4 FY26) to INR49 million (Q1 FY27), with breakeven now expected earlier than previously guided.

themes.label: Capacity expansion / bed & greenfield pipeline
themes.note: Guwahati scaled up to a 650-bed hospital (~INR9,700 million cost); overall announced pipeline now nearly 3,350 additional beds, plus brownfield bed/OT/cath lab additions across Ranchi, Indore, Gurgaon, Lucknow, Patna.

themes.label: Mature hospital margin trajectory
themes.note: Cluster 1 EBITDA margin improved to 24.1% from 23.4% YoY; management does not give explicit margin guidance but sees no structural reason for margin deterioration.

themes.label: Developing hospital scale-up (Lucknow, Patna, Ranchi)
themes.note: Cluster 2 (excl. Noida) delivered 28% revenue growth and 40% EBITDA growth with 32% EBITDA margin; Lucknow/Patna IPD volume growth around 27%.

themes.label: International business growth
themes.note: International patient revenue grew 23% YoY to INR782 million despite current geopolitical tensions.

themes.label: Clinical talent / manpower cost pressure
themes.note: 70+ doctors onboarded including 50+ senior clinicians; negligible senior attrition but continued high attrition in nursing and junior doctor ranks.

themes.label: Inorganic growth / M&A optionality
themes.note: Indore 80-bed acquired facility expected to come online end of Q2/early Q3, adding cancer services capability.

key_takeaways: Consolidated income for the quarter was INR13,262 million, representing a healthy growth of 26% year-on-year.
EBITDA, excluding Noida, witnessed a growth of 24% year-on-year to INR3,201 million, with margins improving to 25.8%.
Reported EBITDA, including Noida stood at INR3,153 million, registering a healthy 23% year-on-year growth with EBITDA margins of 23.8%.
Profit after tax was INR1,573 million compared to INR1,590 million in Q1 FY26, impacted by a nonrecurring exceptional income of INR196 million recognized in Q1 FY26.
Inpatient volumes increased by 28% year-on-year, while outpatient volumes grew by 34%.
Noida generated total income of INR855 million compared to INR525 million in Q4 FY26; EBITDA loss declined sharply from INR236 million in Q4 FY26 to only INR49 million in Q1 FY27.
Based on the current operating trajectory, we expect Noida to achieve EBITDA breakeven earlier than our previous expectations.
We have also revised the scale of our proposed Guwahati hospital... expanded to a 650-bed super specialty hospital with an estimated project cost of approximately INR9,700 million.
Together, our announced expansion pipeline now represents nearly 3,350 additional beds, providing a strong runway for sustainable long-term growth.
pressing_questions: Beyond the regular outlook, what are the top 2 to 3 execution priorities you are focusing on in the coming quarters? And alongside that, what do you see as the biggest risk in patient demand shifts or competitive pressure?
As Noida matures, do you believe the consolidated EBITDA margin can move back towards the 25%, 26% range or will the expansion-related investments keep margins around current levels?
For the 2,950 beds that you plan to add, how much of that capex is already incurred?
If I look at your specialty contribution mix, so oncology, the share has come down from, say, 14.2% last year to 13.5%. Would it be fair to assume that this would be because of the CGHS provision?
Have you seen the impact of CGHS rate hikes that were announced in October come into full flow from this quarter? And if you could quantify the benefit as well to the revenue and the margins.

Margin from Cluster 2 hospitals except Noida is far greater than margin from Cluster 1 hospital. Can we assume this Cluster 2 hospitals to have 30% margins for the near future? And also once the utilization ramps up with respect to Noida facility, will that also be a 30% margin business?

quarters.summary: FY26 was a strong year for Medanta with 20% total income growth, EBITDA margin improvement (excl. Noida) and 15.1% PAT growth; Q4FY26 was the highest ever quarterly revenue and EBITDA quarter. Going forward, Noida is expected to break even during H2 FY27, mature hospital margins are expected to remain stable in the 24-25% range, capex guidance is given for FY27 (~INR800-900 crore) and FY28 (~INR600-700 crore), and the company plans ~500 bed additions across existing hospitals plus ~2,700 beds via 5 greenfield projects over the next 3-4 years with total project capex of ~INR45,000 million over 5 years.

key_figures.label: Total income growth YoY excl. Noida

subsections.label: FY26 highlights
points: Total income grew 20% YoY to INR 45,089 million; excluding Noida, growth was 17%.
EBITDA excl. Noida grew 19% YoY to INR 11,343 million with margin improving to 25.7% from 25.4%.
EBITDA incl. Noida stood at INR 10,560 million with margins of 24.2%, reflecting expected early-stage operating losses from Noida.
Consolidated PAT increased 15.1% YoY to INR 5,541 million.
Board recommended a final dividend of INR 0.50 per share, representing 25% of the face value of INR 2 per share.

subsections.label: Q4 FY26 highlights
points: Highest ever quarterly revenue and EBITDA reported; EBITDA figures exclude non-cash ESOP expenses.
Total income grew 25% YoY to INR 11,958 million, driven by strong patient volume, healthy occupancy and improving realization across the network.
EBITDA excl. Noida grew 27% YoY to INR 3,142 million with margin of 27.5%.
EBITDA incl. Noida grew 17% YoY to INR 2,906 million with margin of 24.3%.
PAT grew 40% YoY to INR 1,417 million with PAT margin improving to 11.8% from 10.6% in Q4 FY25.

subsections.label: Balance sheet & capital allocation
points: Exited FY26 with net cash position of INR 5,906 million.
Generated operating cash flow of INR 7,144 million during the year, growing at a 4-year CAGR of 21%.
Capital plan for expansion pipeline (~INR 45,000 million over next 5 years) fully supported by internal accruals and project-specific debt that may be taken.
Balance sheet strength provides flexibility to execute growth pipeline with appropriate discipline.
Capex for FY27 guided at ~INR 800-900 crore; capex for FY28 guided at ~INR 600-700 crore.

Management clarified capex commitments differ from cash flow timing — cash flows for greenfield hospital builds are back-ended rather than front-ended, with differences between CWIP and capitalized amounts.

subsections.label: Demand drivers
points: Volume growth driven by sustained growth in patient volumes, improving realizations and consistent execution across hospitals.
ARPOB growth driven by improvements in ALOS and change in case mix.
Management noted occupancy is a function of how many patients sleep in the hospital at midnight, not the only metric reflecting volume/throughput — a lot of work moving towards day care globally.

Growth levers cited: adding services/specialties where gaps exist (e.g., cancer in Indore, specialties in Noida), bed additions across existing facilities, procedural capacity additions (OTs, cath labs), growth in minimally invasive/robotic/complex care (e.g., TAVI volumes reportedly highest in the country), international growth in new markets.
OPD Pharmacy business continued strong traction with 46.2% YoY revenue growth in Q4.

subsections.label: New hospital competition (Gurgaon)
points: Two new competitor hospitals expected to come online in Gurgaon around September-October period; management has been discussing this for 2-3 quarters.
No senior clinician lost to competing hospitals as of the call date; no major attrition seen.

Management does not view rising local hospital supply as a major demand risk — historically Gurgaon has seen hospitals open, close, and get acquired without denting Medanta's growth; more doctors/hospitals in a territory tend to attract more patients disproportionately.
Precedent cited: demand did not fall when Max Dwarka opened up nearby.

subsections.label: Mature hospitals
points: Mature hospital portfolio comprises Medanta Gurugram, Indore and Ranchi.
Matured margins were nominally down 40 basis points during the year largely due to increase in employee costs, offset partly by improvement in material costs.
All corporate manpower costs are loaded onto the Gurgaon unit, requiring moderation when evaluating Gurgaon unit stand-alone performance.
Q4 margin improvement (26.7% vs 25.7% YoY) reflects actions to optimize material cost; further cost optimization actions being taken in Gurgaon.

Management believes margin profile of mature units will remain largely stable in the 24-25% range, with some upward tick possible from full-year impact of tariff increases and CGHS benefits (partial year impact in FY26, full year impact expected in FY27).

subsections.label: Developing hospitals (excl. Noida)
points: Continue to outperform with strong revenue and EBITDA growth and margin improvement.

Lucknow (6.5 years old) and Patna (4.5 years old) continuing to show ~30% YoY growth on volume and revenue basis despite being large-scale (600-1000 bed) assets, not the plateauing typically expected.

subsections.label: Ranchi
points: Newly built 110-bed hospital in Ranchi commissioned during the year, complementing existing 200-bed facility.
Growth constrained historically by bed availability and quality of infrastructure of the older asset; recent growth of ~15-16% seen post-expansion.
Company expects growth to scale to 20-30% as impanelments (CGHS, railways, NABH) complete and additional specialties like oncology are added.
Runs as a single campus — some specialties will move to newer site, some remain on older site; older hospital beds being shut for renovation.

subsections.label: Indore
points: 80-bed hospital acquisition (post year-end, May 2026) under business transfer agreement, expected to be operationalized in Q2 FY27.
Located under 500 meters from existing Indore facility; will add oncology capabilities and complement existing multi-specialty facilities, enabling comprehensive integrated cancer care program.

subsections.label: Lucknow & Patna bed/OT additions
points: Patna occupancy running close to 70%, significantly constrained on ICU/critical care beds; orders already given for bed addition expected within H1.
Lucknow adding super-specialty capacity including Neonatology, ICUs; bed additions expected in H1 as well.
Beyond beds, both units adding 4-5 operating theaters each — procedural capacity seen as bigger growth constraint than beds given high procedural orientation of group.
Gurgaon adding operation theaters: 2 activated in Q1, another 2 expected by later Q1 or Q2; additional cath lab capabilities also being added.

ARPOB growth levers for Lucknow/Patna: tariff adjustments possible (Patna has had zero tariff increase in ~4.5 years of operation), scaling robotic work (second robot planned for Lucknow), new services (liver transplant, chest/thoracic surgery, lung transplant in Patna), Mother & Child services recently started in Patna (shorter LOS, ARPOB accretive).

subsections.label: Noida facility ramp-up
points: 550-bed Noida facility commenced operations during the year; formally inaugurated in November 2025.
Operationalized 382 beds, 98 ICU beds, 14 operating theaters; onboarded over 200 doctors and 75+ senior clinicians.

Clinical programs scaled rapidly: over 1,600 surgeries including robotic procedures, over 5,000 Cath lab procedures, initiation of advanced therapies including CAR T-cells, bone marrow transplant, and kidney transplants.
Achieved NABH accreditation within first 6 months of operations.
Progress made on empanelments including insurance, corporate, PSU; received CGHS empanelment in May 2026.

Some specialties not yet started in Noida: pediatric services (started towards end of FY27), obstetrics practice, and liver transplant practice — these will have their own margin/realization profile impact as they scale.
Occupancy currently running around 30%, changing dramatically month-on-month as impanelments come online.
Current ARPOB running in the INR 70,000-80,000 range, cautioned as not a stable baseline since largely cash-based tariff on small base; expected to normalize closer to Gurgaon ARPOB levels.
All major empanelments were done or in process of completion within a week of the call (not all done by March 31, 2026); a few pending.

subsections.label: Projects update
points: Board approved 400-bed Varanasi hospital project in March 2026 under build-to-suit lease arrangement with a partner; company's capex directed towards MEP, interior fit-out and medical equipment.
Varanasi project builds on 1,000-bed Lucknow hospital and 550-bed Noida hospital to strengthen Uttar Pradesh presence, addressing significant unmet need in Eastern UP.
Completed land acquisitions for proposed 400+ bed Guwahati hospital; various regulatory approvals secured.
South Delhi project: Diaphragm wall on site 1 completed; civil tender expected to be awarded by end of next month.
Mumbai and Pitampura (Delhi) projects at various stages of regulatory approvals.

Greenfield hospitals expected to take ~3 years from construction start to construction end (based on Noida timeline); hospitals announced now (May 2026) could be operational by ~May 2029, translating to FY30 numbers rather than FY29.

key_figures.label: International revenue mix of consolidated revenue
Lucknow/Patna volume and revenue growth YoY

subsections.label: International business drivers
points: Despite short-term challenges from the Middle East situation, management sees continued runway as Noida's international funnel activates.
New countries in Africa, Southeast Asia and CIS region are scaling up as growth drivers.
Management expects challenges in Middle East to taper off eventually and hopes Bangladesh market to eventually come back as well.
Strong traction seen from newer markets like Africa, Southeast Asia and CIS contributing to over 30% growth in international business this financial year.

key_figures.label: Company revenue growth level (quarters back to)
Quarters since last at 25% growth level

subsections.label: M&A/inorganic growth
points: Acquired land to set up 400+ bedded multi-specialty hospital in Guwahati (Northeast region).
Partnered to build a 400+ bed hospital in Varanasi.
Subsequent to year-end (May 2026), expanded presence in Indore through acquisition of an 80-bed hospital under a business transfer agreement, to add oncology capabilities.
Management stated it cannot reveal M&A/O&M transactions until fully complete and announced to exchanges; a couple of other transactions being explored, both O&M and M&A.
Company philosophy: will not pursue M&A for its own sake — evaluates quality of asset, values/ethics of partner, deal structure, financial rationale and territorial need before proceeding.
Actively exploring pure acquisition as well as partnership/O&M models beyond greenfield expansion.
Hub-and-spoke strategy referenced: Varanasi cited as execution of previously stated goal to expand in Eastern UP after Lucknow (1,000 beds) stabilized.
Management confirmed continued evaluation of brownfield, greenfield and bolt-on strategies, and potential sister markets to NCR such as Jaipur or Chandigarh, without committing to specifics.

subsections.label: Key risks flagged
points: Short-term challenges in the international business given the situation in the Middle East.
Bangladesh international market has not yet recovered.

Noida cumulative losses depend on pace of occupancy ramp-up (targeted 40-45% range for breakeven); management declined to give a definitive commitment on cumulative loss levels for the year given uncertainty on accumulated losses carried into profitable quarters.
War for clinical talent / shortage of high-quality clinical talent flagged as an industry-wide issue, with associated manpower cost implications as new competing hospitals open in Gurgaon.
Clinician capacity constraints emerging in Patna and Lucknow as those units scale, requiring lateral hiring.
ICU/critical care bed constraints in Patna requiring urgent bed addition.

subsections.label: Forward outlook statements
points: Management expects Noida hospital to break even during the course of H2 FY27 (second half of this financial year), rather than a specific Q2 target.
Cumulative Noida losses for the year depend on how quickly occupancy reaches the 40-45% range typically associated with breakeven; no definitive commitment given.

Mature hospital margin profile expected to remain stable in the 24-25% range going forward, with potential slight upward movement from full-year impact of tariff increases/CGHS benefits recognized only partially in FY26.
Ranchi growth expected to scale up to 20-30% as impanelments complete and additional specialties (e.g., oncology) are added.
Greenfield hospitals (2 in Delhi, 1 in Mumbai) not expected to be operational before FY30, based on ~3-year construction timeline from announcement.
~500 beds to be added across existing hospitals in the short term with minimal capex; ~2,700 beds to be added via 5 greenfield projects over next 3-4 years.
Total project capex across entire expansion pipeline estimated at ~INR 45,000 million over next 5 years.
Capex guided at ~INR 800-900 crore for FY27 and ~INR 600-700 crore for FY28.
Management does not provide explicit margin guidance but expressed confidence margins will not dip materially.

guidance_ledger.statement: We do expect this unit to break-even during the course of this year... during the course of the second half of this financial year, we do expect the unit to break-even.
On a cumulative basis... it really depends how quickly we are able to get the occupancy to somewhere in the 40% to 45% range... I don't want to give you a definitive commitment.
We are feeling fairly confident about the margin profile remaining in this kind of 24% - 25% range. We don't see any real reason for any kind of dips.
We will likely see some amount of bed addition in both the units in the first half of the year as itself.
2 operation theaters will be activated in Q1 itself and another 2 operation theaters, we hope to get activated either towards the later part of Q1 or at least by Q2.
Maybe if you are sitting in May of 2026, you could say May of 2029 hospitals could be up and running. But that may not be FY29 numbers, that may be more FY30 numbers.
The company expects to add approximately 500 beds across its existing hospitals with a minimum capex investment.
Medanta will add approximately 2,700 beds through 5 greenfield projects over the next 3 to 4 years.
Across the entire expansion pipeline, total project capex over the next 5 years is approximately INR 45,000 million.
The overall capex for the year will be somewhere around INR 800 crores to INR 900 crores.
Next year, it will be in the range of INR 600 crores to INR 700 crores.
We do expect to see this growth hit upwards of 20% as this unit scales, 20% to 30% like we've seen in some of the other units.
We do believe that as the complexity scales up, you will continue to see ARPOB growth... you may see some ARPOB benefits.
We do believe at some point in time you will see the challenges in the Middle East taper off... we do believe Bangladesh also as an international market will eventually come back.

risk_register.risk: Middle East geopolitical situation impacting international patient inflows
risk_register.note: Despite some short-term challenges given the situation in the Middle East, management sees continued runway as Noida's international funnel activates and new countries scale up.

risk_register.risk: Bangladesh international market softness
risk_register.note: Management believes Bangladesh as an international market will eventually come back, implying it remains subdued currently.

risk_register.risk: Noida ramp-up / breakeven uncertainty
risk_register.note: Breakeven depends on reaching 40-45% occupancy range; cumulative annual loss level not committed to given uncertainty on accumulated losses.

risk_register.risk: War for clinical talent / manpower cost inflation
risk_register.note: Management flagged shortage of high-quality clinical talent and expects some war for talent on the clinical side, particularly as new competing hospitals open in Gurgaon.

risk_register.risk: New competitor hospitals opening in Gurgaon
risk_register.note: Two new competitor hospitals expected in Gurgaon around September-October; no senior clinician attrition observed so far, and management does not see this as a major demand risk.

risk_register.risk: Clinician/doctor capacity constraints in Lucknow and Patna
risk_register.note: Doctor capacity becoming an issue in Patna and Lucknow as units scale, requiring lateral hiring.

risk_register.risk: ICU/critical care bed constraints in Patna
risk_register.note: Patna significantly constrained in terms of need to add ICU and critical care beds; orders already placed for addition.

themes.label: Noida ramp-up
themes.note: Noida scaling rapidly with NABH accreditation, CGHS empanelment, and reduced quarterly EBITDA loss (INR320mn to INR236mn); breakeven targeted for H2 FY27.

themes.label: Capacity expansion / bed & greenfield pipeline
themes.note: ~500 beds planned near-term plus ~2,700 beds via 5 greenfield projects over 3-4 years, backed by ~INR45,000 million capex over 5 years.

themes.label: Mature hospital margin trajectory
themes.note: FY26 margins nominally down 40bps YoY on higher employee costs, but management expects stability in 24-25% range with possible upside from tariff/CGHS full-year impact.

themes.label: International business growth
themes.note: International revenue grew 33% YoY to INR2,780 million, mix rising to 7% of consolidated revenue, despite Middle East headwinds and soft Bangladesh market.

themes.label: Clinical talent / manpower cost pressure
themes.note: Management flagged a 'war for talent' amid new competing hospitals in Gurgaon and clinician capacity constraints in Lucknow/Patna, with associated cost implications.

themes.label: Developing hospital scale-up (Lucknow, Patna, Ranchi)
themes.note: Developing hospitals (excl. Noida) grew revenue 29% and EBITDA 35% YoY; Lucknow and Patna continuing ~30% growth even 4.5-6.5 years post-launch, defying typical plateauing.

themes.label: Inorganic growth / M&A optionality
themes.note: Company exploring both O&M and M&A transactions selectively (e.g., Indore 80-bed acquisition), guided by asset quality, partner values and financial rationale rather than pursuing M&A for its own sake.

key_takeaways: Total income grew by 20% year-on-year to INR 45,089 million. Total income, excluding Noida, grew by 17%.
EBITDA excluding Noida, grew by 19% year-on-year to INR 11,343 million. EBITDA margins improved to 25.7% compared to 25.4% in the same period last year.
EBITDA including Noida, stood at INR 10,560 million with margins of 24.2%, reflecting the expected impact of early stage operating losses from our newest hospital.
Consolidated profit after tax increased by 15.1% year-on-year to INR 5,541 million.
Q4 FY26 was a strong quarter for Medanta with the company reporting its highest ever quarterly revenue and EBITDA.

Noida remains a key strategic asset for us... From a financial standpoint, Noida has delivered revenue of INR 906 million and an EBITDA loss of INR 783 million during FY2026. Importantly, Q3 FY2026 was the peak quarterly loss for Noida at INR 320 million. Q4 loss reduced to INR 236 million even as bed capacity expanded from 328 to 382.
On the international business side, revenue grew by 33% year-on-year to INR 2,780 million. International mix has expanded from 6% to 7% of consolidated revenue.

Medanta will add approximately 2,700 beds through 5 greenfield projects over the next 3 to 4 years. Across the entire expansion pipeline, total project capex over the next 5 years is approximately INR 45,000 million.
We exited FY2026 with a net cash position of INR 5,906 million and generated operating cash flow of INR 7,144 million during the year growing at a 4-year CAGR of 21%.
pressing_questions: Is it possible assuming that 300 beds were operational from the day 1 of the quarter, is it possible to give what was the occupancy for the quarter for this unit [Noida]? And do you expect this unit to break even by quarter 2 of next year?
So if the breakeven is in second half, so should we expect some losses even on small amount next year for the Noida?
Looking at the progress on these projects [2 in Delhi and 1 in Mumbai], do you think that any of these units can come up in first half of FY29 or these would be beyond FY29?

Now that we are inching closer towards break-even in this fiscal... should we think about Noida's ramp-up differently more so because this is also a region of our core strength... So should we think any differently post the break-even?

With the strong net cash position, which you have and cash generation is pretty strong on an annual basis, any plans for over and above this bed expansion, any plans for any inorganic expansion which you have on your cards?

BHARTIARTL.about: Bharti Airtel Ltd is one of the world’s leading providers of telecommunication services with presence in 18 countries representing India, Sri Lanka, 14 countries in Africa. [1]

quarters.summary: Bharti Airtel delivered another quarter of strong consolidated performance (revenue up 5.7% QoQ, EBITDAaL up 4.2%, margin 51%) led by continued Africa momentum and resilient India growth, with management reiterating discipline on capex, continued build-out of new growth bets (financial services, data centers, cloud, Airtel Money) and a pivot to fiber-first in homes amid FWA cost/quality issues. Bharti Hexacom also posted steady growth in revenue, EBITDAaL and net adds, with management flagging home-broadband acquisition-quality correction as transient and reiterating capex discipline and progressive dividend policy.

subsections.label: Balance sheet & capital allocation
points: Consolidated net debt to EBITDAaL improved to 0.7x and India without passive infra is now lower than 1x, underpinned by prudent capital allocation, disciplined capex and continued operational excellence.
Strength of balance sheet recognized by leading global agencies which sustained rating upgrades during the quarter.
Operational discipline continues to remain an enabler of strong performance with focused execution and efficiency improvements through the War on Waste initiative.

Raised $1 billion at Nxtra (data center arm) to accelerate investments; management indicated future funding decisions (own balance sheet vs entity-level fundraise) will be taken opportunistically as they arise, but Nxtra will need to lever up (equity infusion plus debt) to build out required capacity.

Management does not set explicit ROCE targets; focus is on growing the business, extracting operating leverage, and operating fiscally prudently on cost and capex; will not make short-term capex cuts to boost ROCE.

subsections.label: Capex allocation commentary
points: Radio/core capex has moderated across the portfolio over the last couple of years; may see step-ups depending on competitive dynamics.
Large part of capex directed to transport layer including fiber (including homes business) rather than radio.
5G standalone capex is very modest as it is largely a software/switch-on capability.
Rapid capex scale-up expected for data center portfolio as Nxtra grows from 120-130 MW to 1 gigawatt over the next few years.
Company will not hold back on capex wherever there is a legitimate need to step up growth, remain competitive, or fund newer bets.

subsections.label: Mobile ARPU drivers
points: ARPU benefited from an extra day during the quarter.
Improvement driven by upgrade within current customer base via consumption of data, movement to unlimited plans, and postpaid acceleration via Fast Lane technology (network slicing on 5G).
Substantial headroom seen in mid-term from handset upgrades (feature phone to smartphone), rising data usage, 5G adoption and international roaming.
Postpaid is a key ARPU growth lever with significant opportunity ahead; postpaid penetration still low.

subsections.label: Homes segment
points: Net adds of 473,000 represents a moderation versus previous quarters' trajectory, attributed to tightened acquisition quality after learnings from FWA expansion (higher churn, weaker continuity in certain cohorts under low entry-level pricing) and rising global memory/chipset pricing challenging FWA economics.
Traction already showing momentum in improvement over last few weeks/months as acquisition quality is repaired.
One Airtel plan (fixed-mobile convergence) central to strategy, seeing promising adoption; convergence seen as lever to deepen customer relationship and reduce churn.
Digital TV adds driven by strong adoption of IPTV; IPTV take rates continuing to improve, supporting convergence agenda.

subsections.label: Airtel Business (B2B)
points: Large deal wins across core connectivity and digital portfolio; visibility on sustained growth in coming quarters.
Digital businesses (cloud, cybersecurity, IoT, digital platforms, CPaaS) delivering solid performance with notable deal wins.

B2B portfolio comprises three types of businesses: connectivity (healthy margins), wholesale (low margins, subject to price pressure and messaging shift from SMS to WhatsApp), and digital businesses (data center, cloud, CPaaS, IoT, cybersecurity - heavier investment).
Quarter saw step-up in digital businesses plus step-up in connectivity, particularly global side with larger deal wins, positively impacting underlying margin.

As portfolio retools toward digital (cybersecurity, CPaaS = lower margin due to lower investment; connectivity, IoT = healthy margins; cloud/data centers = significant investment), margins expected to trend slightly downward longer term, but real focus metric is faster revenue growth given large, fast-growing addressable markets.

B2B capex volatile, still mid-teens as % of revenue; material step-up expected from data center rapid build-out (lumpy, land-dependent) vs modular Cloud investment (first-round investment across three regions already completed).

subsections.label: Financial services (Airtel Finance)
points: Recently went live with lending services (NBFC), about nine months from license application date, achieved by reusing existing digital platforms (data platforms, CLM platform, channel platform) from the Telco inside the NBFC.

Airtel Payments Bank continues strong performance; integrated with NBFC lending and payments under 'Airtel Finance' storefront; early moves on savings via fixed deposits and more engagement options planned.
Digital capabilities expected to deliver lower delinquencies, lower cost of acquisition, lower collection costs, helping scale NBFC and payments bank.
Management does not see conflict between Airtel Finance/NBFC and other partners in the storefront; comparable structure exists among large NBFCs; RBI regulations dictate operation within LSP segment.

subsections.label: Data centers (Nxtra)
points: Ambition to build one gigawatt over next few years; market share currently viewed as low relative to Company's scale.
Many contracts already stitched up; additional land being acquired in right locations, with landmark deals to be finalized in coming quarters.
Data center market comprises hyperscalers and domestic enterprises; large part of hyperscaler workloads run out of Mumbai, hence key consideration for reaching 1GW is securing land parcels in Mumbai.

Existing contracts (including Google, confirmed as included in 120MW-to-1GW plan) plus upcoming build of a couple hundred MW over next couple of years, with remaining gap to be filled via Mumbai land parcels.
Management states clear line of sight to reaching the 1 gigawatt ambition.

subsections.label: Airtel Cloud
points: Almost all critical services now live on the platform; strength/readiness reflected in certifications received from MeitY among others, strengthening go-to-market proposition.

Business needs four things to succeed: right talent, capital already invested, go-to-market capability, and right solutions for continuing to build customer needs; stepping up significant investment to scale.
Cloud business incubated separately within B2B; building top-notch talent group while depending on B2B go-to-market teams to open doors for technical sales/solution architecting.

Longer decision gestation cycles due to workload sensitivity, integration effort and egress costs when moving from hyperscaler/private cloud; commercialization (usage-based billing) is a muscle being built.
Traction seen around simple, easily-bought propositions: disaster recovery/backup-as-a-service, storage-as-a-service, video surveillance-as-a-service.
Larger deals seen in sovereign cloud space for sensitive workloads (regulated/PSU spheres), where certification work is underway.

subsections.label: Bharti Hexacom segment detail
points: Capex directed towards 5G densification, network modernization, and growing homes and IPTV business.
Home broadband bundles content and non-content offerings; no separate digital TV segment—everything bundled into home broadband, customer not counted twice.
Postpaid penetration low but steadily growing quarter-on-quarter, indicating quality customer focus.
Depreciation jump of 4.9% QoQ was raised by an analyst; response pending in transcript excerpt.
EBIT margin for home segment tends to be negative/immaterial; timing of profit translation raised by analyst, response pending in transcript excerpt.

subsections.label: AI and digital platforms
points: Real-time and context-based decisioning expanded to 7.7 billion next best actions, live across all channels led by Airtel Thanks App.
AI-led anti-spam solution identified over 93 billion spam calls and 4 billion spam messages, blocked over 1.4 million fraudulent links.
Call center Voicebot interactions increased to 309 million this quarter.

AI applied across 30,000 field engineers via patented technology allowing inferencing on the endpoint device rather than the cloud, using real-time image processing to standardize workmanship, leading to step change in quality of installs/fault repair and enforcing safety measures.

A small language model runs on the field engineer's regular handset (endpoint device) for local inferencing — described as an in-house engineering breakthrough; potential to extend into stores and other areas.
Cost of these AI workloads dropped from Rs.30-35 Crores (when run on cloud) to near zero when run on-device via small language model.
All transformation led by a homegrown agentic platform focused on cost-efficient automation and compute with guardrails for customer safety, privacy and sovereignty.

Converged data engine (digital experience layer) enables faster execution and customer engagement with greater precision by bringing together customer context, data intelligence and digital tools for personalized interventions.

subsections.label: Fast Lane / 5G network slicing
points: Fast Lane technology leverages network slicing on 5G to deliver differentiation on postpaid, driving business acceleration.

Slicing technology makes the network more efficient and generates more capacity; at empty-network level the tangible difference is limited, but shows up as differentiated experience when networks are congested/crowded.
Customers on Fast Lane demonstrate differential experience technically; overall network efficiency improvements have also improved speeds for all customers, not just sliced customers.
Interest in upgrading to Fast Lane as reassurance of superior experience is working well, showing positive signs and some acceleration in interest.

subsections.label: War on Waste
points: Core pillar for cost discipline; sharpened focus on identifying/eliminating waste, redesigning ways of working, redesigning tower operations to eliminate diesel consumption, and making sharp choices in homes business capex deployment.
These efforts helped navigate the phase of global cost headwinds; considerable further work acknowledged as needed to build a more efficient, resilient, sustainable operating model.

subsections.label: Network/infrastructure investment
points: Building world-class infrastructure: expanding fiber availability, strengthening quality for flapless networks, augmenting subsea capacity, deepening data centers and data-center-to-data-center connectivity via OPGW infrastructure.
Continued investment in transport layer and advanced 5G capabilities, including network slicing for 5G efficiency and effective capacity expansion.
Working with Indus to deploy high energy-efficiency power equipment and advanced energy storage solutions to reduce diesel dependence across sites.

subsections.label: Hexacom energy cost trend
points: Energy costs lower YoY for Hexacom partly due to seasonal benefit from solar-based towers and some one-offs in the quarter; underlying trend broadly stable.

Full impact of higher diesel prices not yet seen in the quarter as DG set diesel stocks are not emptied completely (timing lag); seasonality allowing more solar generation has also helped, with ramped-up solar sites.

subsections.label: Africa opportunity framing
points: Africa likened to India nearly 10 years ago - large, young and increasingly digital population with meaningful headroom for penetration-led growth.
Enterprise and data center opportunities in Africa remain largely untapped.
Africa contributed almost half of consolidated revenue growth of ~16% for the last year.

Africa's market structure is typically 2-3 players (mostly 2), with cheap and abundant spectrum, so investment is directed mainly at network/transport (fiber, including landlocked-market needs) and homes business.

subsections.label: Bharti Hexacom circle dynamics (Rajasthan & Northeast)
points: Northeast is a large circle with difficult terrain; Rajasthan more developed than parts of Northeast but also difficult terrain; combination of wireless and wired-line strategy suited to these circles versus more developed circles like Maharashtra or Tamil Nadu.
Shillong (within portfolio) is extremely developed with aspirational demographic profile.

Competitive intensity in Rajasthan is extremely high (national players operate across all 22 telecom circles, no relenting unless an operator strategically deprioritizes a circle); Northeast is comparatively more comfortable competitively for Hexacom, though ground-level intensity on acquisition/network experience is similar; terrain differences require unique solutions especially in Northeast.

subsections.label: Africa stake / EPS-accretive transaction
points: Completed an EPS-accretive share swap transaction during the quarter, increasing Airtel's stake in the Africa business to over 79%.
Strengthens participation in Africa's growing profit pool and underscores belief in scale/durability of the opportunity.

subsections.label: Group cohesion / synergies across India, Indus, Payments Bank, Africa
points: Significant heft brought to Airtel operations over last 18 months; benefits now accrue across technology, network, supply chain and talent, enabling more cohesive operation and execution.

Three additional areas called out for group cohesion: B2B (solutions and go-to-market capability replicated across the continent), Homes (India lessons extended to Africa), and Energy efficiency (working with Indus on high-efficiency power equipment/energy storage to cut diesel dependence).
Belief that large synergy opportunity exists across India Business, Indus Towers, Airtel Payments Bank and Africa operations going forward.

Indus experience in India affirmed decision to introduce Indus into Africa; Indus's low-cost architecture (construction, digitization, energy management, tower performance observability) replicated to Africa from day one, expected to improve Airtel Africa's opex on rentals, IP fees and energy.

Indus starting with three markets in Africa; further expansion to other African markets not committed but described as an 'exciting opportunity' contingent on how the initial three markets perform, given Indus's lean, remote-monitoring-based operating structure.

subsections.label: Airtel Money London listing
points: Given growth trajectory and large addressable opportunity, Airtel Money is preparing for a London listing in the second half of 2026.

subsections.label: Indus Towers expansion rationale
points: Africa tower company industry currently has very high costs/rentals; Indus presents a viable low-cost alternative benefiting Airtel Africa's opex performance (rentals, IP fees, energy) and improved observability of tower performance.

subsections.label: FWA cost and quality headwinds
points: Low entry-level pricing in FWA attracted customers but led to inconsistent outcomes: higher churn and weaker continuity in certain cohorts.
Rising global memory and chipset pricing has also challenged FWA economics.
Company tightened acquisition quality, is doubling down on improving churn, and pivoting toward fiber with FWA deployed only with sharper precision where economics/customer quality are compelling.

Management clarified that customer acquisition slowdown is linked to quality-of-acquisition correction, coinciding with (but not solely caused by) the period of rising memory prices; the two should not be simplistically correlated.
On fiber side, memory price impact (via copper/router components) is modest and being absorbed.

FWA has two challenges: installing in the wrong place leads to poor experience, and installing with poor quality of acquisition creates a double whammy requiring box retrieval; company is pivoting FWA deployment only to locations where fiber is not accessible.

subsections.label: International roaming impact (West Asia crisis)
points: Previous quarter's West Asia crisis had led to a decline in international roaming; this quarter shows improvement/repair versus previous quarter.

subsections.label: Pricing architecture disrepair
points: Industry pricing architecture needs repair; current structure offers unlimited data at very low pricing levels, capping ARPU — viewed as unhealthy operating model.

Management believes industry needs an architecture progressing from small to medium to large to extra-large plans (as in other markets), and does not believe entry-level pricing itself needs to change.
Correcting this architecture cannot be done unilaterally by Airtel; timeline for correction remains uncertain.

subsections.label: Diesel/energy cost timing
points: Full impact of higher diesel prices not yet reflected in the quarter for Hexacom due to timing lag from existing DG set diesel stocks.

subsections.label: Smartphone/refurbished phone inflation
points: Refurbished phone circulation has increased amid inflation; strong sub-additions currently seen with no impact yet, but long-term impact on customer wallet from smartphone price inflation is yet to be seen.

subsections.label: Africa growth outlook
points: Business on sustained momentum of 20%+ CAGR growth; headroom for growth continues to be high.
Expect contribution of Africa to overall portfolio growth to be substantially higher than its base contribution to the business, meaning Africa's share of the overall portfolio will keep growing.
Investments into Africa will continue to step up.

subsections.label: Mobile ARPU longer-term outlook
points: With a more sensible price architecture, management view is that in the next five to seven years sustained ARPU growth of 4-5%, maybe slightly higher, is achievable, driven by rising affluence in India.
No need to touch entry-level pricing, which is viewed as good enough.

subsections.label: Data center ambition
points: Ambition to build 1 gigawatt of data center capacity over the next few years, with existing contracts, upcoming builds (couple hundred MW over next couple years) and Mumbai land acquisition providing line of sight to the target.

subsections.label: Return on capital
points: Management declines to set explicit ROCE targets; sees ROCE improvement as an outcome of growth and operating leverage rather than a standalone target.

guidance_ledger.statement: Wherever there is a legitimate need for the business to step up growth, be competitive, or plan newer bets, the Company will not hold back on capex; rapid capex spend expected for data center scale-up from 120-130MW to 1 gigawatt

Ambition to build one gigawatt, with existing contracts (including Google), a couple hundred MW of upcoming build over the next couple of years, and Mumbai land acquisition providing clear line of sight to the target
