key_takeaways: Consolidated revenue was Rs.58,500 Crores, growing at about 5.7% sequentially; Africa maintained strong growth with constant currency revenue growth of 5.7%; India excluding passive infra grew 3.6% sequentially.
Consolidated EBITDAaL was at Rs.29,800 Crores, growth of 4.2%, margin at 51%; operating free cash flow (EBITDAaL minus capex) was over Rs.16,450 Crores; capex was about Rs.13,390 Crores.
Consolidated net debt to EBITDAaL improved to 0.7% and India without passive infra is now lower than 1%.
Completed an EPS accretive share swap transaction that increased Airtel's stake in the Africa business to over 79%; Airtel's Africa operations generate an annualized EBITDA of over Rs.35,000 Crores.

Africa Airtel Money has achieved meaningful scale with Q1 revenue of over $400 million growing at 26% year-on-year in constant currency terms; Airtel Money is now preparing for a London listing in the second half of 2026.
In mobile India, added 3.3 million revenue earning customers, 5 million smartphone data customers, and 1 million postpaid customers (highest ever addition in any quarter); ARPU came in at Rs.264.

Homes delivered net adds of 473,000, a moderation over previous quarters' trajectory, attributed to tightened acquisition quality after learnings from FWA expansion (higher churn) and rising memory/chipset pricing challenging FWA economics.
Airtel business revenue came in at about Rs.5,670 Crores, growing 3.2% sequentially and nearly 12% over last year, with digital businesses revenue growth of nearly 6% sequentially.

Bharti Hexacom delivered revenue of Rs.2,510 Crores (up 4% sequentially), EBITDAaL of about Rs.1,210 Crores at 48.2% margin, mobile customer base of 29 million with net adds of about 210,000, and ARPU of Rs.259.
pressing_questions: On the mobile ARPU, what led to strong improvement quarter-on-quarter? Was there any product revamp or some specific plan adoption rows like Fast Lane? Should we expect this trend to be sustainable in absence of tariff hike?
On Airtel business, can you break down the levers of such growth into various sub segments like connectivity, cloud, data center and discuss the outlook - is this kind of number sustainable?

On capex, how much reallocation is happening towards projects like AI infrastructure (data centers, subsea cables, sovereign compute) and how does 5G standalone play a role in the overall capex number?

On B2B revenue mix, with increased share from asset-light/low-margin digital services (CPaaS, digital), how do you expect overall Airtel business EBITDA margins to trend over the next two to three years, and what are the conversion cycles for recent Airtel Cloud deals into revenue?

Since you raised $1 billion at Nxtra to accelerate data center investments, is it fair to say that hereon, wherever there's a meaningful step-up in capex, you will look for external sponsorship, or will you lean on your own balance sheet?
On the data center business, does scaling from 120-130 MW to 1 gigawatt include the Google contract or is this purely the Co-lo Nxtra is looking to do?
On FWA, what was the churn rate, and does this materially change the growth rate - will you be able to maintain the run rate despite the churn rate?
On finance cost in Africa, does Airtel Money's interest on leverage also get captured in the interest cost line?
What gives confidence of scaling data centers to one gigawatt power - is there a strong pipeline given multiple operators are targeting similar scale and India is currently at roughly 1.6 gigawatt?

On homes, margins are under pressure and lowest in recent past, with sub-additions also lowest in seven-to-eight quarters - is this a conscious slowdown given cost inflation, high base catching up, or increased competitive landscape?
Given Africa's thrust, what contribution do you see Africa scaling to over the next three to five years (EBITDA, invested capital, or other frame of reference)?
Return on average capital employed is now above 20% - is there any reason ROCE would not expand at least 500 basis points over the next three years?

On India ARPU, are you suggesting that in the near term you don't see pricing architecture corrected and all ARPU growth will be organic, with a less frequent tariff hike cycle going forward? And with decent growth and improving organic ROCE already, why is a price hike needed at all?

On Indus expanding to three African markets, what advantages does Airtel Africa get from having Indus versus using other towers, and is it safe to say Indus should logically expand to remaining African markets over time?
On the depreciation jump of 4.9% QoQ at Hexacom, is there a particular reason for the sharp increase?
On the EBIT margin for the home segment at Hexacom, which tends to be negative/immaterial, when should we see revenue translating into profit growth in the home segment?

quarters.summary: Bharti Airtel closed FY2026 with lifetime-high consolidated revenue and margin improvement, strong deleveraging, and a sharply higher dividend. Management flagged ARPU growth as weaker than desired in Q4 due to geopolitical/roaming impacts and intends to accelerate ARPU via postpaid upgradation and pricing architecture reform (no near-term tariff hike commitment). Capex is expected to stay in the ballpark of FY2026 levels, with continued investment directed to core network, transport/fiber, data centers, financial services and cloud. The Board approved a share-swap to raise Airtel Africa stake by 16.3% (no-cash, value-accretive), and management reiterated ambitions of 1GW data center capacity, an 800 million customer base (500m India + 300m Africa) over time, and a long-term goal of Bharti Telecom regaining 51%+ controlling stake.

subsections.label: Capital allocation priorities
points: First priority: invest in core business (India, Africa, Indus Towers) — Africa stake increase was predicated on this.
Second priority: continue deleveraging to the extent required.
Third priority: invest in adjacencies (data centers, financial services, cloud).
Financial services investment will be done carefully and prudently, with focus on collection efficiency and compliance.

Once core, deleveraging and adjacency capital needs are met, additional capital would go to dividends/buybacks; no plans for further capital deployment outside India in near term other than bolt-on acquisitions in towers, cloud, cybersecurity, B2B.

Chairman noted Company will not become like IT firms that only do dividends/buybacks without reinvesting; will consider buying good value telecom assets globally over medium-to-long term, but nothing currently on the table.

subsections.label: Finance cost / deleveraging dynamics
points: Consolidated finance cost impacted by a one-off in Africa which will unwind.

In India, a large part of debt reduction happened towards the end of the quarter; rights issue money came in around mid-March and AGR dues payment happened on the last day of the quarter, so finance cost has not yet reflected full benefit of deleveraging; reduction expected going forward.

subsections.label: ROCE outlook
points: Management declined to give specific 2-3 year ROCE targets; expects continued operating leverage from scale and cost discipline (war on waste) to drive additional returns as growth continues.

subsections.label: Mobility
points: Mobility sustained revenue market share gains to reach a lifetime high share.
ARPU increase of Rs.3 in Q4 considered unsatisfactory; part attributed to West Asia crisis and international roaming revenue impact.
Growth levers going forward: postpaid upgradation, data consumption growth in 5G, handset upgrades from feature phones, international roaming, rural network expansion program.

subsections.label: Homes
points: Homes accelerated strongly in FY2026, adding 4.2 million customers.
FWA continued to expand addressable market while FTTH footprint deepened via accelerated home pass expansion.
IPTV launch well received with encouraging adoption; Digital TV saw turnaround with strong IPTV-led net adds in Q4.
Market potential of nearly 100 million connected homes in India over medium term, driven by smart TV penetration, evolving content consumption, need for reliable/secure connectivity.
Memory/chipset supply and price challenges have led company to double down on fiber-first strategy over FWA given fiber's superior/reliable experience.
One Airtel converged plans recently launched offering bundling convenience, flexibility, value; convergence (Wi-Fi+mobile) reduces churn ~50%.

New customer acquisitions occur at slightly lower ARPU vs traditional base but this is plateauing; acquisition ARPU has not been declining over many quarters — mix effect from existing high-plan customers drives blended ARPU down.
Homes business framed as a long-term moat given low churn, high customer lifetime value, further enhanced by convergence (content+mobility).

subsections.label: B2B / Airtel Business
points: B2B revenue growth driven by multiple deal wins in IoT, security, cloud, core connectivity, and Nxtra; strong order book/funnel across domestic and global business.

B2B portfolio comprises: (1) commoditized messaging business — flattish/declining due to price pressure and OTT migration, low margin, no capex; (2) core connectivity — growing faster than industry low-single-digit growth due to share gains, leading position in distributed businesses (manufacturing, distribution, BFSI); (3) data centers; (4) digital businesses (CPaaS, security, cloud) — lower margins due to different capex/cost structures.
Management view: stepping up growth will bring some margin pressure due to business mix shift, but focus remains on growing topline and absolute EBITDA/profit faster.
Need to improve position in IT and IT services space within core connectivity.

subsections.label: New growth bets / adjacencies
points: Three adjacencies sharpened via disciplined experimentation: data centers, financial services, Airtel Cloud — filtered by 'proven right to win' and 'differentiated value proposition'.

Data centers: progressing toward 1GW capacity ambition over next few years; Nxtra announced $1bn fund raise from marquee investors plus Airtel participation, seen as validation of opportunity/execution.
Financial services: Airtel Money Limited received RBI approval to operate as non-deposit taking NBFC, progressing to commercial launch; LSP business continues strong growth.
Airtel Payments Bank delivered strong quarter with MTUs, revenue run rate, and deposit growth as noted in key figures.
Airtel Cloud: telco-grade sovereign cloud gaining traction with deal wins in Q4 and April, ongoing conversations with multiple customers; building credentials/attributes required by customers.
Company early in these bets but encouraged by progress; committed to same discipline/customer centricity as core business.

subsections.label: Group synergies
points: Working across technology, network, supply chain, talent across the group; tech stack already extended to Africa, Payments Bank, Indus Towers at arm's-length pricing.
B2B and homes identified as two areas for massive synergy; working to reduce diesel dependence via high-powered batteries and renewable power.

subsections.label: Pricing architecture / ARPU strategy
points: Management view: India pricing architecture is 'broken' — unlimited data plans capped around Rs.340-350 vs much higher unlimited price points globally (US $60-70, Europe €35/£30-35).
Fix requires moving from small/medium/large/extra-large allowance tiers enabling natural upgradation pathway; given income stratification in India, ARPU should rise if architecture changes.
Caution flagged on raising entry-level (Rs.199) prices given current environment.
As of now, market remains competitive; company will not do anything that hurts its business; no immediate move to metered 5G data despite aspiration for usage-based pricing.

Organic ARPU growth of 5% YoY relies on postpaid upgradation, upgrades within consumption tiers, and driving customers to best-fit plans; potential incremental headwind from softening handset shipments/rising prices affecting 2G/4G-to-smartphone upgrades, though not yet materially impacting.

subsections.label: Home broadband competitive positioning
points: Management declined to comment directly on competitor (Jio) FWA vs fiber performance comparison.

Uses third-party data (e.g., Meta) on session/connection counts across wireless, fixed, and FWA mediums to gauge competitive performance; notes performance has been 'very, very delightful' over last couple of quarters versus two quarters ago.
Strategy remains 'fiber first' — wireless (FWA) used to augment reach only where fiber is unavailable.

subsections.label: Africa market opportunity
points: Confidence in long-term Africa growth given low tele-density (~45% unique SIMs), low smartphone penetration (~52%), low data consumption per customer, young demographic profile.
Two large growth opportunities: (1) homes, enterprise and data centers; (2) Airtel Money with potential further value unlock via listing.

Chairman likened Africa's current stage to India 10-12 years ago given young, growing population and technology/AI adoption tailwinds; most African markets have only 2-3 operators vs India's 3 with 2 dominant players.

subsections.label: Africa stake acquisition (share swap)
points: Board approved (day before call) a share swap transaction between Airtel and ICIL to acquire additional 16.3% stake in Airtel Africa, raising Airtel's stake to 78%.
Transaction is no-cash and described as value-accretive to Airtel shareholders; equivalent to acquiring another large company (~$3 billion transaction).
UK regulations allow ownership up to 90%; ambition is to reach that ceiling over time, aided by Airtel Africa's own ongoing buyback program and potential opportunistic blocks from other investors.
Rationale: valuable, deeply understood asset with high underlying growth (data/tele-density/smartphone penetration headroom) and Airtel Money value-unlock potential.

subsections.label: Promoter shareholding structure
points: Chairman's stated vision: Bharti Telecom (BTL) should be the sole controlling promoter shareholder, historically holding ~51% or just over 50%; current gap is about 10% to get back to that level.
Singtel's direct stake gap to equalization reduces from ~6% to 3.6% post this transaction; at less than 1%/year over 3-4 years, this puts Singtel on its stated equalization path.

Chairman's cherished desire: use twin levers of enhanced dividends and potential buybacks (over next couple of years) to give BTL capacity to buy more shares and move above 50% stake, over the next decade as leadership transitions to next generation.

subsections.label: Capital deployment scope
points: For now, no plans for further capital deployment in non-India assets beyond the Africa transaction; will continue bolt-on acquisitions in towers, cloud, cybersecurity within B2B.

Financial services capital allocation guided at Rs.20,000 Crores over next five years (Rs.14,000 Crores from Airtel), though actual deployment could be 'significantly less' depending on demonstrated success; business will be scaled back if not proving out within 1-1.5 years.

Longer-term aspiration to acquire good value telecom assets globally, but nothing currently under consideration; philosophy is to avoid becoming a pure dividend/buyback-only company like some IT firms.

subsections.label: Nxtra / data center business model
points: Nxtra business model is primarily tenancy/colocation-based; not currently offering GPU-as-a-service.
Partnership with Google involves building a large AI data center in Visakhapatnam on a colocation basis for Google.

Company using a few hundred GPUs for its own AI workloads; GPU efficiency has improved ~10x over 2.5 years and costs have fallen, though company remains cautious on GPU-as-a-service given rapid technology change.
Data centers being built with latest cooling technology, power efficiency, and standardized build-out toolkit to remain fungible across customers.
~50-60% of India data center demand originates from Mumbai; land acquisition and construction will be needed to scale toward 1GW ambition.

subsections.label: Geopolitical crisis impacts
points: Ongoing geopolitical crisis (West Asia) impacting: international roaming revenue; capex due to INR depreciation; restriction on gas supply affecting galvanizing industry, in turn leading to lower tower build-outs; energy price increases (already impacting Africa).
Company mitigating impact through amplified war on waste initiatives.

subsections.label: Component cost/supply pressures
points: Cost pressures currently confined to specific areas: servers and memory prices as well as component availability.

Memory/chipset supply and price challenges specifically affecting homes/FWA connectivity costs — cost to connect a home via FWA was roughly on par with fiber a year ago but has become 'very much more expensive' in the last 3-4 months, prompting pivot back to fiber-first strategy and digital tools to minimize FWA installs where fiber is available (installed in April, ramping over coming months).
Handset prices have risen sharply in recent weeks, creating potential headwind to smartphone upgrade-driven ARPU growth, though impact not yet seen; being watched closely.
Significant re-engineering/redesign steps underway to mitigate server/memory cost pressures; also reducing diesel dependency across sites via renewables/high-powered batteries.

subsections.label: Finance cost / one-offs
points: Consolidated finance cost affected by a one-off item in Africa expected to unwind; India finance cost stickiness explained by timing — large debt reduction, rights issue proceeds, and AGR dues payment all occurred near quarter-end, so full benefit not yet reflected.

subsections.label: Regulatory/provisioning (Hexacom)
points: A regulatory charge was taken this quarter as part of prudent, regular-cadence review of the basket of charges/ecosystem developments, guided by auditors/Board/audit committee; not a new demand — reflects a change in interpretation of an existing/known matter (previously possibly disclosed as contingent liability) rather than a new exceptional item.

subsections.label: Capex outlook
points: Company does not typically give capex guidance but expects FY2027 capex to be in the ballpark of FY2026 levels, give or take.

Radio/core capex moderating in India (growing in Africa); transport capex to be stepped up including fiber points of presence and edge data center build-out (56 edge data centers planned over next 18-24 months); home business and cloud/data center/financial services investments to continue as focus areas.
Wireless capex at ~16% of sales (decade low); management is not chasing a specific target level and will deploy more if higher 5G densification is required.

subsections.label: ARPU trajectory
points: Management determined to accelerate ARPU growth via postpaid penetration, best-fit plan upgrades, and consumption-driven upgrades; expects continued headroom for 'many quarters to come' even absent tariff hikes.
No near-term tariff hike explicitly signaled; fundamental fix seen as pricing architecture reform, timing uncertain ('let us see how this plays out over time').

subsections.label: Long-term customer ambition
points: Chairman reiterated an ambition of 800 million customers across mobile, home broadband, digital services and financial services combined between India (500 million) and Africa (300 million), described as a visible, not-too-distant goal.

subsections.label: Data center capacity ambition
points: Continued progress toward building 1 gigawatt of data center capacity over the next few years, with ambition to keep building beyond that given Mumbai's outsized share of India data center demand.

subsections.label: Africa ownership ambition
points: Ambition to raise Airtel's stake in Airtel Africa up to 90% (the regulatory ceiling in UK), aided by Airtel Africa's buyback program and potential further share acquisitions over the coming years.

subsections.label: Promoter shareholding ambition
points: Chairman's ambition for Bharti Telecom to return to controlling shareholding of 51%+ within roughly the next decade, aided by dividends and potential buybacks.

subsections.label: Financial services investment plan
points: Rs.20,000 Crores planned allocation over next five years (Rs.14,000 Crores from Airtel) for financial services, though actual spend could be significantly lower depending on demonstrated success within 1-1.5 years.

key_takeaways: We delivered another year of strong performance. Our consolidated revenue crossed another milestone and came in at a lifetime high of about Rs.2,11,000 Crores backed by strong performance in both India and Africa.
EBITDAaL came in at about Rs.1,08,000 Crores with a margin of 51.2%.
India EBITDAaL excluding passive, came in at about Rs.72,500 Crores, growing around 18% and delivered a 3.1% improvement and stood at 51.7%.
Net debt to EBITDAaL now stands at 1.1. The Board recommended a dividend of Rs.24 per share, a significant increase over last year's Rs.16 per share.
We have sharpened our focus basis the result of the experimentation in three specific adjacencies: these are data centers, financial services and Airtel cloud.
The Board yesterday approved a share swap transaction between Airtel and ICIL to acquire additional 16.3% in Airtel Africa.

Mobile, we added 4.7 million customers in Q4 and 5.8 million out of those were smartphone customers. Our ARPU for the quarter came in at Rs.257, which on an EDB basis was an increase of Rs.3 for the quarter. We are not happy with the ARPU increase of Rs.3.

We ended the year on a strong note with a healthy order book and a funnel across domestic and global business with multiple wins from large enterprises... we ended the year with a strong order book growth of 17% in FY2026.
We rolled out upwards of 8 million home passes to cross 45 million home passes and we continue to expand rapidly.
pressing_questions: Given the large free cash flow generation, how are you thinking about progressively, what payout may look like in a steady state, and what are the other priorities in terms of assets outside of India that you may potentially look to explore in the future given the strong free cash flow generation and the criteria you may look to assess any asset that you may want to acquire outside India?

Is it even realistic to assume any meaningful tariff hikes in the foreseeable future, given the business is doing generally okay from a free cash flow returns perspective without one, and what will really change the ARPU trajectory given postpaid and data adds are already strong on a large base?

What will it really take for the industry to move to usage based pricing, given unlimited offers are still going on since 5G rollout and the two leading telcos have not yet decided to move even 5G to metered data - is there a path in mind or is it just an aspiration still?

On Hexacom mobile growth lagging Airtel on both revenue and EBITDA growth despite under-penetration levers, what changed this quarter and what corrective measures have been taken - should this accelerate for the coming year?

What does the regulatory charge this quarter pertain to - is there any new demand from the government which has affected you this quarter, or was this earlier part of contingent liabilities and has now been provided for?

BHARTIHEXA.about: IIncorporated in 1995, Bharti Hexacom Ltd provides consumer mobile services, fixed- line telephone and broadband services in Rajasthan and Northeast telecom circles[1]

quarters.summary: Bharti Hexacom (and parent Bharti Airtel) delivered another quarter of strong consolidated performance; for Hexacom specifically, revenue grew 4% sequentially to Rs.2,510 Crores with EBITDAaL margin of 48.2%, mobile net adds of ~210,000, and homes/office business growing 8% sequentially on 75k net adds, though home broadband acquisition quality tightening (mirroring the wider Airtel group's FWA recalibration) and chipset/memory price inflation are near-term headwinds. Management gave no formal financial guidance for Hexacom ("we do not give guidance"), reiterating capex will continue to be directed to 5G densification, network modernization and homes/IPTV growth, with capital deployed as needed to sustain competitive, profitable growth while maintaining a comfortable net debt position.

subsections.label: Depreciation increase
points: Sanjesh Jain (ICICI Securities) flagged a sharp sequential jump in depreciation of 4.9% quarter-on-quarter and asked for the particular reason; the transcript excerpt cuts off before Soumen Ray's response is captured.

subsections.label: Home segment profitability
points: Sanjesh Jain asked about EBIT margin for the home segment, noting it tends to be negative or immaterial, and asked when revenue growth would translate into profit growth in the home segment for Hexacom; response not captured in the provided excerpt.

subsections.label: Energy cost trends
points: Aditya Bansal (Motilal Oswal) noted energy costs were lower YoY despite higher diesel prices and asked whether this reflected timing differences or efficiencies.

Karthikeyan Velu attributed this primarily to seasonal impact, with solar-based towers providing benefit, and some one-offs in the quarter; on a trend basis it is more or less trending in the same direction.

Soumen Ray clarified diesel price increases had not been felt for the full quarter (only part of the quarter), and that DG sets run on existing diesel stock rather than empty tanks immediately, so full diesel impact has not yet been seen; seasonality allowed for more solar generation as sites were ramped up, helping a bit, but underlying sequential trend is more or less as planned.

subsections.label: ARPU tailwind
points: ARPU of Rs.259 benefited from one extra day in the quarter.

subsections.label: Mobile net-add seasonality
points: Rishabh Dhancholia (HSBC) noted mobile subscriber net-add trends were relatively weaker this quarter versus historical trends and versus the sequential growth seen in pan-India Airtel numbers, and asked what drove this and whether anything was circle-specific.

Soumen Ray responded that looking sequentially over the last ~16-20 quarters, there is a certain seasonality in customer depletions both in the industry as well as in each operating company, with a higher trend of customer additions typically seen towards the second half of the year, a pattern demonstrated over the years.

subsections.label: Home broadband acquisition quality correction
points: Home broadband continues to be seen as a very large opportunity with no relenting on effort to seize it.
Two technologies are used to give a whole broadband Wi-Fi experience to the customer (fiber and FWA).
Management found reasons to become tighter on quality of acquisition, and what is seen in this quarter is the effect of that correction in the way customers are acquired.

No fundamental change in the assumption of market size, share-gain approach, or pricing/converged solutions (home broadband with content, fixed-mobile convergence) — the change is a quarter-specific effect of the acquisition-quality correction that management expects to unwind going forward.
Postpaid penetration has been low this quarter but is showing steady quarter-on-quarter growth in postpaid customer additions, viewed positively from a quality-customer perspective.

subsections.label: Home broadband product mix / IPTV
points: The home broadband number reported includes two kinds of offerings: one including content and one excluding content; everything is bundled into home broadband since there is no separate digital TV segment reported for Hexacom, but customers are not counted twice.

Hexacom's share of overall Airtel home broadband has increased; the FWA acquisition-quality calibration applied across the country has had a somewhat lesser impact in Hexacom's markets, though the underlying approach (improving quality of acquisition) is consistent across the country, and growth is expected to return to prior rates in the next couple of quarters.

subsections.label: Circle demographics and strategy
points: Vivekanand Subbaraman (Ambit Capital) asked how many of Airtel's relevant 400 cities (for FWA/FTTH homes market) fall within Bharti Hexacom's circles (Rajasthan and Northeast) and the absolute homes opportunity in Hexacom.

Soumen Ray estimated close to about 15-17 of the 400 cities fall in these two circles, but emphasized understanding circle demographics matters more: Northeast is large with difficult terrain; Rajasthan is more developed than parts of Northeast but still difficult terrain.

A combination of wireless and wired-line reach is described as a good strategy for these two circles compared to more developed circles like Maharashtra or Tamil Nadu; approach will be nuanced by location, e.g., Shillong is described as extremely developed with strong aspirational demographic profile.

subsections.label: Competitive intensity by circle
points: Vivekanand Subbaraman followed up asking whether the competitive landscape is as fierce in Rajasthan and Northeast, especially for homes-business customer acquisition, as in the rest of Airtel's footprint.

Soumen Ray: Rajasthan is extremely competitive; national players operate across all 22 telecom circles so there is generally no difference in competitive intensity unless an operator strategically deems a circle less relevant, which is not the case here.
Northeast: Hexacom is in a very comfortable competitive position.

Rajasthan is described as a far more competitively heated market; ground-level intensity on customer acquisition and network experience delivery is no different from any other circle, though terrains differ, requiring unique solutions especially in Northeast.

subsections.label: Capital allocation vs parent's new bets
points: Vivekanand Subbaraman asked whether, since Airtel (parent) is stepping up capex in areas like data centers—an opportunity unavailable to Bharti Hexacom (BHL)—there are areas where Hexacom can reinvest capital to achieve improved revenue growth versus the industry from a strategic three-to-four-year standpoint.
Soumen Ray responded that 5G densification is a big objective and fiberization continues to be a big job to be done.
Data center is a separate entity that gets consolidated in the overall India numbers but does not apply to the telco organization (Hexacom) itself.
Whatever is the ask of the business to maintain healthy, competitive and profitable growth will be attended to.
As of now the company is in a very comfortable position on net debt to EBITDA and would like to remain there, but will spend adequately if there is a call to drive competitive and profitable growth.

points: Broader Airtel group commentary (applicable context for Hexacom's homes business) notes rising global memory/chipset pricing has challenged FWA economics, alongside quality-of-acquisition issues from aggressive low entry-level pricing that led to higher churn and weaker continuity in certain cohorts.
Home broadband acquisition-quality tightening in this quarter is described by Hexacom management as the cause of the moderation seen, expected to unwind in subsequent quarters.

subsections.label: Diesel/energy cost variability
points: Diesel price increases had only been in effect for part of the quarter, and DG sets run on existing stock rather than reflecting price changes immediately, so full diesel cost impact has not yet flowed through; seasonality (higher solar generation) provided some offsetting benefit this quarter.

subsections.label: Competitive intensity
points: Rajasthan circle described as a far more competitively heated market than Northeast, requiring continued focus on customer acquisition quality and network experience.

points: Strong results with continued operating leverage, led by razor sharp execution and operational excellence.
Strong operating leverage attributable to continued efforts on portfolio premiumization and the war on waste agenda.
Company further strengthened its position in both markets with sustained revenue and market share improvement.
Capex spends during the year were directed towards 5G densification, network modernization and growing the homes and IPTV business rapidly.

subsections.label: Mobile growth comparison vs Airtel India
points: Hexacom's revenue and EBITDA growth in FY2026 lagged Airtel India's growth rates on both metrics.
Management stated Hexacom's underpenetration thesis in its two circles has borne out well and the ARPU gap versus Airtel has closed.

Postpaid penetration and international roaming (IR) dynamics will create some differential versus Airtel; smartphone upgrade stress could cause Hexacom to lag slightly since it is a strong growth indicator.
Management said the business is competitive and not lagging the market, and will look at new ways of driving convergence to accelerate growth.

points: Hexacom largely restricts capital deployment to mobile and FTTH, which are fully funded, unlike Airtel's broader growth engines (data centers, financial services, cloud) which are not available to Hexacom.
Lower investment requirement is a positive, but it also restricts future growth avenues compared to the parent.

MEESHO.about: The Company is an app-based marketplace that is operated under the brand of Meesho that connects sellers and end consumers. Its offerings span categories including fashion, accessories, electronics, home and kitchen items, health, and fitness equipment, and office supplies.[1]

quarters.summary: Management expects logistics costs to keep declining despite fuel-price and minimum-wage headwinds, with efficiencies continuing to be passed to sellers/customers via lower AOV over time; growth trajectory remains on the long-term 25% CAGR (5-year) guidance with Q2/Q3 combined expected to look similar to trend despite a Diwali-timing shift into October; contribution margin is expected to keep improving via fulfilment-margin restoration and ad-revenue growth, with new initiatives (Kirana Club, low-cost local logistics) still pre-product-market-fit and capped at an annual EBITDA budget of ~INR200 crores.

subsections.label: Logistics cost trajectory
points: Company anticipates continuing to reduce logistics cost at a very good pace, consistent with commentary since IPO.
Changes in fuel prices and minimum wages are viewed as small blips in the overall cost-reduction picture, and this was reflected in the current quarter's numbers.
All channels (not just Meesho) are impacted by fuel and wage hikes; as Meesho becomes more efficient, online as a channel is expected to gain share from other channels.

During Q1, fuel price hikes came through on both Valmo network and 3PLs, along with minimum wage changes across the ecosystem — these were absorbed in the quarter, with some timing effect since the fuel price hike was announced around May.
Cost per delivered order came down by about INR1 QoQ due to efficiency measures, largely offsetting the fuel/wage headwinds.
Logistics operations are now running on a fully stabilized basis, beyond the Q2/Q3 disruption seen in the previous year, and continuing efficiency gains are expected to show up in upcoming quarters.

Cost increases and pricing increases to the ecosystem happened simultaneously in the last quarter — no timing lag between cost coming in and being passed to revenue; company generally takes pricing steps only when there is an actual effective price cut for sellers.

subsections.label: AOV dynamics
points: Baseline AOV decline guidance is about 5% YoY as efficiencies are passed on; last quarter's AOV declined by about 2% YoY, i.e., a lesser decline than the general guidance.

Early in the quarter, raw material costs (e.g., polyester pricing) moved up, leading to some product pricing increases; fuel hike impact was also partly passed on into pricing, pushing AOV up versus baseline expectation.
As efficiencies are regained and passed to customers, AOV is expected to resume its trajectory of becoming lower than before.

subsections.label: New initiatives / Horizon 2 budget philosophy
points: New initiatives operating loss was INR39 crores in Q1 FY27.
No fundamental change to philosophy: company operates with a budget hard cap on new-initiative burn (~INR200 crores annually in EBITDA terms), to remain frugal on experiments.
Quarter-on-quarter variances happen, but the budget cap approach continues until initiatives graduate to Horizon 1 and move to the marketplace, after which IRR math applies.
Company will communicate proactively if the budget cap changes.

subsections.label: Contribution margin trade-off vs growth
points: Two dynamics drive contribution margin: (1) logistics margin (charge vs cost) had come down during last year and is now being restored, then held broadly constant with efficiencies passed to sellers/customers as pricing; (2) improving ad revenues have a downstream positive impact on contribution margin, intended to be kept in the P&L.
Company takes calls every week/month/quarter on efficiency of spends in terms of CAC, LTV and IRRs, investing more to grow faster as long as investment guardrails (S&M spend) are met.

subsections.label: Sequential growth seasonality
points: Sequential NMV growth of 2% this quarter reflects seasonality dynamics rather than a change in underlying business; year-on-year comparison is the more appropriate lens.

Last year had a higher share of S&M spend as % of NMV, causing some prior quarters' growth (even 50%+) to look elevated — those were exceptions, not the norm; apart from that S&M spend effect, nothing else in the core business changed.
Some prior seasonality (e.g., Eid) shifted between quarters year-over-year, affecting comparability.
Company reiterated long-term NMV growth guidance of 25% CAGR over the next five years, higher in initial years and lower in later years, as the baseline it works with.

subsections.label: Q2/Q3 outlook and Diwali timing
points: Q2 this year will differ from Q2 last year because last year's annual festive sale (Meesho Blockbuster Sale) started within Q2 (September) since Diwali fell earlier; this year Diwali is pushed to November, so the annual sale will start in October (Q3).

This is a significant GMV-generating event, so YoY growth rate variations are expected in Q2 vs the recent trajectory, but Q2 and Q3 combined will look similar to the ongoing trajectory — a timing difference only, flagged proactively.

subsections.label: Merchant base and monetization
points: NMV per seller down ~25% YoY, driven by strong growth in the merchant base rather than a change in monetization ability.

Merchant base growth driven by product improvements: easier onboarding, easier selling/listing, better discovery, and improved logistics efficiency even for very small merchants (where per-pickup costs are typically higher).

As competition among merchants on the platform increases, propensity to spend on monetization (ads) over the long term is higher; platforms with large seller bases globally tend to monetize more on ads because sellers compete for discovery.
Company will continue investing in growing merchant base of all sizes as it is viewed as important for long-run monetization levels.
ADU growth was 29% for the year, with frequency growth of 9% YoY.

key_figures.label: Sellers advertising on platform (share of GMV-contributing sellers)
Sellers for whom Meesho is primary income source

subsections.label: Meesho Mall
points: Company does not disclose the share of NMV contributed by Meesho Mall or the share of ad revenue coming from Meesho Mall brands versus smaller merchants.
Ad revenue from brands on Meesho Mall, as a percentage of NMV, is higher than the overall platform because brands tend to spend more on ads than a typical seller in the economy.
Meesho Mall continues to grow at a much faster pace than the overall platform and is described as a substantial, not insignificant, part of the business.

Management anticipates Meesho Mall will be a large part of the growth story over the next three, five, or more years, and will keep contributing to the long-term ad revenue goal since more ad revenue is generated when brands sell on the platform.

Meesho Mall brands can advertise similarly to any other seller; the added advantage is a 'Meesho Mall authentic' tag that improves conversion, but the ad product itself (performance marketing ads shown in the feed, tagged as ads) is no different from what other sellers use.

subsections.label: Ad monetization / seller advertising adoption
points: Close to two-thirds of GMV-contributing sellers currently advertise on the platform, with scope to increase this further.
Steps taken over the last two to three quarters to simplify the ad product and better align it with sellers' ROAS objectives have helped increase adoption quarter-on-quarter.

Not only are new sellers becoming active on ads, but existing advertisers are using ads across more of their catalog, which increases the pool of ad-eligible products and improves the ad experience for consumers.
This ad adoption expansion toward the largest GMV-contributing seller base is a key area of focus for upcoming quarters.
ROAS levels are similar to the prior quarter.

subsections.label: Seller economics
points: Difficult to precisely gauge Meesho's salience to an average seller's overall top line since much offline-business data isn't directly available to the company (and may not share the same GST ID).

Internal surveys/checks indicate that for a majority of the GMV-contributing seller base, Meesho is one of their primary sources of income; specifically, for more than 50% of sellers, Meesho is a primary income source.

subsections.label: Frequency trends by cohort
points: Annual frequency (with 29% ADU growth) still grew by about 9% year-on-year.
Growth in frequency comes from older cohorts continuing to increase frequency, as well as newer cohorts entering at higher frequency than a year before.
Company does not disclose specific frequency figures by cohort (older vs newer), but both are trending positively.

subsections.label: AI in seller operations
points: Seller onboarding on Meesho has been one of the fastest relative to any other horizontal or vertical e-commerce player, even before the AI wave, and the process continues to be made simpler and more efficient.
AI has enabled automated taxonomy, trust and safety checks on every catalog/product uploaded to test genuineness and prevent counterfeits, using vision models for identification.
Product attributes are now automatically populated via AI rather than requiring manual seller input, which was previously time-consuming and caused drop-offs.
AI is described as all-pervasive across the business — not just seller operations but also consumer-facing features and the Software Development Life Cycle (SDLC), improving developer productivity.

subsections.label: AI and competitive moat
points: Productivity gains in software development allow the company to move faster and solve roughly 2x as many problems as before, strengthening the flywheel.

New products like Vaani are now possible because of GenAI, creating experiences not previously possible, bridging the gap with offline shopping and making it easier for new users to experience e-commerce.
AI-driven improvements are viewed as strengthening the existing moat in multiple ways.

subsections.label: Valmo vs 3PL insourcing strategy
points: Fundamental objective: the lowest-cost provider in a particular lane (source-destination combination) is given a significant proportion of volume in that lane, whether Valmo or a third party.

Efficiencies are being gained not just from Valmo but also from other third-party logistics partners as their volumes grow, density increases, and they pass back some savings via volume-linked rate cards.
No specific guidance on what Valmo's ultimate share will be; the objective function is to continue reducing overall cost per delivered order.
Valmo's share of volumes was about 50% last quarter, similar to the quarter before that.

subsections.label: Corporate/legal restructuring of Valmo (GTA)
points: Valmo is an aggregator of various small businesses across mid-mile, last-mile, and first-mile operations.
During the quarter, the business was reorganized (as noted in the previous quarter) so the organizational and corporate structure resembles this aggregator model.
Valmo Transportation Private Limited (VTPL) now houses the middle-mile and last-mile operations under a Goods and Transport Agency (GTA) license classification under GST law.

A large part of the Valmo business has moved under VTPL; on a consolidated basis nothing changes significantly, but on a standalone basis there will be movements between Meesho Limited, Meesho Technologies Private Limited, and VTPL.

VTPL will only house middle-mile and last-mile operations available under the aggregator/GTA model; first-mile operations and sort-center operations for Valmo will remain part of Meesho Limited, so VTPL financials may not offer a fully direct comparison of overall Valmo business.
Company will consider what more to disclose about VTPL financials going forward for better understanding.

subsections.label: New local/low-cost logistics network
points: Differs from Valmo (a national logistics network) — certain categories, especially perishables and fast-moving consumer goods, require a fundamentally different, more local logistics network with faster transport and higher product-integrity/safety requirements.
This new supply chain is being built to support new grocery-related initiatives and is still very early — in the experimentation stage, not yet proven at scale.
If successful, it should extend Meesho's value proposition to more price points and categories, including grocery and staples, and sub-INR20/INR30 products that are hard to ship nationally.
A lot of the capability being built in Valmo for the core business is also required to make this new network work, so it may take a longer time to reach product-market fit.

subsections.label: Competitive intensity
points: Competition and intensity of competition in the sector have always been present; management does not believe intensity has changed in either direction, including regarding recent tweaks by other large horizontal e-commerce platforms for goods priced under INR1,000.
Sub-platforms have been launched by competitors to compete with Meesho over the years; this is viewed as expected given the size of the opportunity.

Company continues to move forward on its own mission/vision, scaling aggressively, with improving pricing, selection (due to large seller base), and overall proposition, alongside good growth and cohort retention.
Competitive intensity is expected to remain high, consistent with going after a large opportunity.

key_figures.label: Annual budget cap for new initiatives (EBITDA)

subsections.label: Kirana Club acquisition rationale
points: Contribution to P&L will only happen over the long term; the business is very small and at an early product-market-fit stage, with a lot of work needed before it contributes to company P&L.

Rationale: similar to Meesho, Kirana Club has created a disruptive value proposition for Kiranas across the country, including small towns, remote and rural areas previously underserved by online platforms — before Kirana Club, only limited Kiranas in big cities could be served online.
Belief that Kirana Club can create similar value for retailers broadly, not just Kiranas, aligned with Meesho's overall mission.
Strong capability overlap exists — particularly low-cost logistics (where Valmo can play a big role) and broader commerce/technology capabilities built by Meesho.

Kirana Club will remain in the 'new initiatives' disclosure bucket; management plans to be patient given the large long-run opportunity, and it could eventually help expand Meesho's addressable market into grocery and other B2B use cases, not just grocery.

subsections.label: Articles of Association amendment
points: Standard amendments relate to nominee investor and director/founder positions, typical of post-IPO changes sought at the first Annual General Meeting.
The AGM is upcoming and will seek appointments for director positions for founders and certain investor nominees — essentially regularizing arrangements that existed until the IPO.

subsections.label: GST/GTA regulatory scrutiny
points: News flow relates to the GTA model reorganization mentioned earlier; management notes precedence of other horizontal e-commerce players using a similar model — not a new model.

Company reviewed both the letter and spirit of the law and believes the restructuring is in the right direction; reasonable legal and accounting opinions were taken from leading law firms and accounting firms.

No question has been asked by any regulatory or tax authority on this matter to date; the proxy advisory's question was also directed at SEBI, but no communication has been received from SEBI on this topic.
Management has good reason to believe there is no risk exposure arising from this matter but will continue to monitor how it progresses.

subsections.label: Karnataka Gig Workers Act / welfare fee
points: The Karnataka Gig Worker law is currently under clarification-seeking by the company, in conjunction with other consumer internet players.
The court has put a stay on any actions related to this law currently.

From a conservative standpoint, the company continues to make provisions for any related costs in its P&L, so there should be no adverse impact if required to pay; amounts involved are not material in nature.

subsections.label: Fuel price and minimum wage inflation
points: Fuel price hikes came through on both the Valmo network and third-party logistics providers during Q1, alongside minimum wage changes across the ecosystem.
These cost increases have largely been absorbed/offset through efficiency gains, with continued efficiency expected in coming quarters.
Raw material cost inflation (e.g., polyester pricing) also affected product pricing early in the quarter.

key_figures.label: Annual budget cap for new initiatives (EBITDA)

subsections.label: Growth guidance
points: Long-term growth guidance is 25% CAGR over the next five years, expected to be higher in initial years and lower in later years — this remains the baseline the company works with.
Q2 and Q3 combined this year are expected to look similar to the ongoing growth trajectory, despite a timing shift in the festive sale (Diwali) from Q2 to Q3 (October) versus last year (September).

subsections.label: Logistics cost and contribution margin outlook
points: Logistics cost reduction is expected to continue at a good pace going forward, with fuel/wage changes viewed as minor blips rather than trend-changers.

Contribution margin is expected to keep improving via restoration of fulfilment margin and growth in ad revenue, though the pace of contribution-margin delta improvement was not quantified as accelerating beyond current dynamics.
Efficiency gains in logistics are expected to largely be passed on to customers as lower pricing, supporting growth.

subsections.label: New initiatives budget
points: No change to the philosophy of capping new-initiative (Horizon 2) burn at roughly INR200 crores annually (EBITDA basis); company will communicate proactively if this changes.

guidance_ledger.statement: Anticipate continuing to reduce logistics cost at a very good pace, consistent with commentary since IPO; fuel price and minimum wage changes are small blips that don't change the path.

Baseline AOV decline should be about 5% year-on-year as efficiencies are passed on to customers; last quarter's actual decline was about 2% YoY due to cost pass-through, expected to resume trajectory of lower AOV.
Long-term growth guidance of 25% CAGR over the next five years, higher in initial years and lower in later years.
Q2 this year will look different YoY due to Diwali sale timing shift into October (Q3), but Q2 and Q3 combined will look similar to the ongoing growth trajectory.
No fundamental change to philosophy; annual budget cap of roughly INR200 crores (EBITDA) for new initiatives; will communicate proactively if this changes.
Contribution margin expected to keep improving driven by restoration of fulfilment margin and continued growth in ad revenue.

Contribution to P&L will happen over the long term; business is very small and at early product-market-fit stage.

Provisions continue to be made conservatively in the P&L for potential gig-worker welfare costs; amounts not material even if required to pay.

Long-term NMV growth guidance remains 25% CAGR over the next five years, higher in initial years and lower later; Q2 FY27 growth will differ YoY due to the Diwali festive sale shifting from September (Q2 last year) to October (Q3 this year), but Q2+Q3 combined are expected to track the ongoing trajectory.
Company reiterated it has good reason to believe there is no risk exposure from proxy-advisory-flagged GST/GTA questions, having received no regulatory or SEBI communication on the matter.

quarters.summary: Meesho's Q4 FY'26 call centered on margin recovery after transient Q2/Q3 FY26 logistics disruptions, with contribution margin improving 170 bps sequentially to a 4% exit rate, continued ad-revenue monetization gains, growth in Meesho Mall for value-focused brand distribution, and a philosophy of investment-return-based (not budget-based) spend on marketing and logistics in-sourcing (Valmo). No specific EBITDA break-even guidance was given, but management expects LTM FCF and contribution margin to keep improving, with some residual carry-over impact from FY26 one-offs expected to persist for a few quarters.

key_figures.label: Sequential contribution margin improvement

subsections.label: Contribution margin recovery drivers
points: One-time logistics headwind of 145 bps during Q2 and Q3 of FY26 is now behind the company; baseline going forward is the 4% Q4 exit contribution margin rate.

The Q2/Q3 FY26 disruption was transient, caused by capacity disruption from a 3PL consolidation event around May last year; short-term higher-rate capacity was built to protect customer experience and has since been unwound with more optimum cost structures put in place in Valmo and other 3PL partners.
Contribution margin is split into two components: ads-related margin and fulfilment-side margin; ad revenue improvements flow largely into contribution margin since cost of serving ads is low.

Fulfilment cost improvements are driven by reducing failed delivery percentage (via better address geo-accuracy and improved partner-assignment logic) and by rising prepaid share reducing cash-handling costs.

Delta improvement in contribution margin going forward expected to be slower than the Q3-to-Q4 jump, driven by continued ad revenue growth and further restoration of fulfilment margins over the next two quarters.

subsections.label: Revenue per order vs contribution margin framing
points: Revenue per order declined from ~INR57 in FY24 to ~INR47 in FY26, partly explained by declining logistics cost and accounting changes (revenue now reported net of first-order discounts, netted against sales & marketing expense) and by rising prepaid mix (lower revenue but also lower cost per order, net neutral at contribution margin level).

Management considers contribution margin, not revenue per order, the right trajectory metric since ads is a high-gross-margin business while logistics is lower-gross-margin, so revenue-line optics can diverge from underlying margin trends.
Reported ad revenue as % of NMV increased quarter-on-quarter despite optical softness in per-order revenue.

subsections.label: Cash flow
points: LTM (last-twelve-months) FCF is management's preferred guiding line item over quarterly cash flow due to volatility from timing of sale events near quarter-end.

Impact of items stemming from Q2/Q3 FY26 will continue to be carried over for the next few quarters, but overall FCF trajectory on a quarterly basis should keep improving given margin and growth improvement.

Cash flow from operations (CFO) negative trend over past three quarters includes some one-offs from past periods; overall EBITDA trend and negative working capital cycle improvement indicate improving CFO trajectory; management to consider sharing a reconciliation separately.
Cash balance reduction of ~INR300 crores driven by timing of NMV/sale events near quarter-end (more NMV in last 15-20 days of a quarter creates volatility versus if the sale event occurs earlier).
Some cash taxes paid out have been adjusted off from net cash balance as they are expected to be returned based on trajectory of overall profit/PPT.

subsections.label: Below-contribution-margin cost levers
points: Three large below-contribution-margin cost line items: new user acquisition (return-threshold based, not %-of-NMV based), people cost, and technology/infrastructure cost.
People cost expected to grow slower than NMV growth rate over the next few years as cost-to-serve reduces, generating operating leverage.

Technology infrastructure cost includes cloud provider contracts with 2-3 year renegotiation cycles; as scale increases, larger discounts are obtained, so trajectory of this line item moves in step-cycles rather than linearly.
Above contribution margin, most significant transient impacts have been resolved; some further scope to increase fulfilment margins remains over the next two quarters.

Online transaction penetration of smartphone users (other emerging markets)
First-year frequency increase over last 3 years

subsections.label: User growth runway
points: India's online transaction penetration among smartphone users is close to 30%, versus north of 80% in other emerging markets, indicating large headroom for user growth.
Annual transacting user base grew 33% YoY even off a large base.

264 million user base discussed; management does not view household-level translation as meaningful since e-commerce shopping of Meesho's browse-based kind is done more on an individual basis than household basis, similar to how e-commerce transactor counts mimic messaging-app user counts in China/Southeast Asia.

subsections.label: Order frequency trends
points: Users maturing on the platform over ~3 years see frequency rise to 15 times or more; FY24-and-before cohorts are expected to have a similar frequency.

Counterintuitively, first-year frequency of new users has been increasing for the last three years due to pricing, assortment, and technology innovation improvements — new users now start from a higher baseline than three years ago (frequency roughly doubled from baseline).
This increasing first-year frequency trend is more than offsetting any potential socioeconomic drag from expanding into deeper/rural parts of India.
Comparable value-focused e-commerce companies in China have frequencies closer to 100 times, indicating large remaining headroom.
Propositions like Meesho Mall and content commerce are also expected to contribute to higher first-year frequency.

subsections.label: Inflation sensitivity
points: Historically (since the 1970s), value-focused companies tend to gain share during high-inflation periods as consumer budgets tighten — viewed as a potential tailwind.
Possible offsetting headwind from lower absolute spending amounts during high inflation; net effect to be observed as it progresses.

subsections.label: SKUs per order strategy
points: Platform is built to make ordering as frictionless as possible, keeping SKUs per order near 1 rather than pursuing basket consolidation.

Unlike warehouse-origin models used by some competitors, Meesho orders ship directly from sellers'/factories to consumers, limiting consolidation opportunities; hence SKU-per-order is not a focus metric despite competitor moves like free shipping on second unit from the same seller.

key_figures.label: Growth in catalogs/products live on ads

subsections.label: Ad monetization / seller adoption
points: Return on ad spend (ROAS) continues to be one of the industry best, multiples higher than other e-commerce players in India or globally.
More than two-thirds of sellers by GMV weighting are active on ads; the key metric tracked is number of catalogs/products advertised, which grew more than 40% YoY and continues to improve QoQ.
Seller ad budgets have grown more than double over the last one year, signaling rising willingness to spend as sellers see good ROAS.

Management is deliberately operating at high ROAS currently to activate more sellers as first-time advertisers before considering raising ad pricing; plans to raise pricing at the 'right time' once steady-state ad revenue is much higher.
Cannot charge differential pricing to different sellers since it's a bidding product; the signal watched is growth in advertiser budgets rather than segmented pricing experiments.
Minimum ROAS threshold for sellers varies by category and is market-dynamics driven (margin structure of categories); no single specific threshold is targeted.

subsections.label: Meesho Mall
points: Meesho Mall is scaling for affordable/value brands and value packs across national, regional, and D2C challenger brands; positioned for 'mass India', not just premium customers.
National brands are scaling selection on Meesho, reaching customers for the first time via a channel that overcomes limitations of typical Kirana/GT distribution networks.

As Mall moves beyond unbranded goods into categories like FMCG and beauty, its contribution margin is currently lower than core marketplace because the business is in an investment phase focused on onboarding brands/selection rather than maximizing margin; this investment phase is expected to continue for the next few years before margin focus increases.

subsections.label: Seller cohort/concentration trends
points: Seller concentration (Pareto) continues to reduce as more sellers become active and larger on the platform; DRHP disclosed earlier data on this trend, and the number of sellers forming the platform's Pareto continues to increase at a fairly rapid pace.

Quality of non-GST sellers acquired is described as pretty good; platform systems (built over 10 years) restrict visibility for low-quality new sellers, so return rates remain stable and are not being negatively impacted by non-GST seller growth.

Non-GST seller growth is expected to continue at a fast pace since total addressable sellers in India (tens of millions of product businesses) was previously restricted to a sub-million base when non-GST sellers were not allowed to sell online; this restriction has changed.

subsections.label: Rural user focus
points: Plan to invest a lot more in acquiring rural customers over the next one year.
Vaani (voice AI shopping agent) has helped convert more rural customers onto the platform, reducing CAC for this segment.

As you go deeper into India, CAC would typically rise on a like-for-like basis (higher convincing threshold), but AI/product/pricing improvements have lowered this friction, keeping CAC in a fairly limited zone despite rural expansion.

subsections.label: Valmo (in-house logistics) strategy
points: No specific fixed target for Valmo's in-sourcing share; volumes are allocated to whichever logistics partner (Valmo or third-party) is most cost-efficient for each lane, with third-party logistics partners competing across the board.

As Valmo continues to innovate and improve cost structure, its share is expected to keep increasing organically, similar to trends seen at global operators like Mercado Libre or Shopee that focus on in-sourcing/batching for cost benefits.
Consolidation/batching efficiencies are already happening within Valmo, alongside other supply-chain cost efficiencies gained through scale.

At the current ~50% in-sourcing mix, the company believes it is at/near the most cost-optimized structure; the mix will keep adjusting based on evolving cost realities rather than a fixed target (e.g., not deliberately pushing in-sourcing down to 30% for further contribution margin/FCF gains).

subsections.label: Cost-of-delivery (COD) reduction and prepaid mix
points: BNPL (buy-now-pay-later) initiatives are still early in their life cycle; not yet a major driver of COD reduction.
Key driver of rising prepaid share / falling COD share has been reduction in cost of prepaid orders, which is passed back to consumers via better prepaid discounts.
Going forward, continued investment in BNPL is showing good early signs and is expected to become an additional driver over time.

Cash-on-delivery orders carry higher costs due to cash handling charges, and prepaid orders have better delivery rates, leading to better total cost optimization; this shift improves the overall logistics cost structure.

subsections.label: Logistics cost drivers
points: No specific quantitative near-term logistics cost reduction figure provided, but key qualitative drivers include: (1) shift from COD to prepaid transactions improving cost structure, (2) rising ecosystem volumes increasing network density across last-mile and middle-mile legs (benefiting both Valmo and 3PL partners), and (3) multiple ongoing innovations within Valmo expected to yield cost benefits over time, though not yet quantifiable; may be quantified in coming quarters.

Automation in sort centres is a big focus area; already being experimented with in several places, with a multi-year goal of bringing state-of-the-art automation to all sort centres, expected to drive future efficiency gains.

No specific capex model has been finalized for mid-mile/sorting automation; some partners are willing to invest and set up facilities on Meesho's behalf, and the company will decide on direct capex investment based on payback period economics as things develop.

subsections.label: Failed delivery reduction
points: Improvements made over the last couple of quarters in reducing misrouted orders by improving geographical address accuracy and moving away from more aggregated partner-assignment approaches, reducing the rate of failed deliveries and consequently the blended cost of serving an order.

subsections.label: Value proposition and CAC
points: CAC reduction is attributed to historical investments in technology and price-value proposition improvements for rural users, not solely to a rural customer mix shift.
Vaani (voice agent) and other AI/algorithm investments have reduced the friction between app installation and first order placement, keeping CAC in a limited range even amid rural expansion.

Marketing/advertising spend is not budgeted as a fixed percentage of NMV; investment continues as long as it meets an internal return-on-investment hurdle threshold; this philosophy is not expected to change.
As NMV base grows, user acquisition spend may not scale at the same rate longer term, though this is a longer-term trend rather than a fixed quarterly pattern.

subsections.label: Competitive/global benchmarking
points: Comparisons drawn to global value-focused e-commerce operators (Mercado Libre, Shopee) on in-sourcing/batching strategies.
Comparable value-focused e-commerce frequency benchmarks in China are cited as much higher (~100x) than Meesho's current levels, indicating headroom.
Value-focused companies historically gain market share during high-inflation periods as consumer budgets tighten.

subsections.label: Meesho Mall expansion strategy
points: Big focus area for the company; goal to make Meesho Mall a critical part of distribution for every brand, growing fast even at the cost of near-term contribution margin during the current investment phase.

Aim is to serve brands for a billion people eventually, not just big cities, reaching mass India by overcoming Kirana/GT distribution network access limitations that have historically constrained brands.

subsections.label: Logistics disruption headwind
points: Q2 and Q3 FY26 experienced a transient 145 bps one-time logistics headwind, caused by capacity disruption following 3PL consolidation around May last year; short-term higher-cost capacity was built to protect customer experience and has since been unwound.
This issue is considered structural/resolved and a one-time occurrence, not expected to recur, with the 4% Q4 FY26 contribution margin exit rate as the new baseline.

subsections.label: Macro/inflation risk
points: Uncertain macro environment is prompting consumers to focus more on value, which management views as broadly favorable for a value-focused platform like Meesho, though there could be a headwind if absolute consumer spending amounts decline in a high-inflation scenario.

subsections.label: 3PL industry consolidation dynamics
points: Industry consolidation among logistics partners has led some to focus more on margins rather than chasing volume/offering better rates, which is a factor management is monitoring in the context of Valmo's scaling and potential need for further mid-mile/sorting investments.

subsections.label: No specific short-term guidance provided
points: Management stated there is no specific short-term guidance to share at this point on EBITDA break-even timing.
LTM FCF continues to be the guiding line item rather than quarterly FCF, given quarter-to-quarter volatility from sale-event timing near quarter-end.
Both margin improvement and growth trajectory are expected to keep improving FCF on a quarterly basis over time, despite continued carry-over impact from FY26 one-offs for a few more quarters.

Contribution margin improvement pace going forward is expected to be slower than the Q3-to-Q4 jump, driven by continued ad revenue growth and further fulfilment margin restoration over the next two quarters.

Below-contribution-margin cost lines (people cost, technology/infra cost) are expected to grow slower than NMV over time, generating operating leverage, though not necessarily in a linear fashion (tech infra costs move via 2-3 year cloud contract renegotiation cycles).

guidance_ledger.statement: No specific guidances to share at this point on EBITDA break-even timing
LTM FCF should keep on improving on a quarterly basis given margin improvement and growth, though carry-over impact from FY26 one-offs will continue for some time
Delta improvement in contribution margin would be slower than Q3-to-Q4 jump, driven by ad revenue improvement and some restoration on fulfilment margin
No specific goal for Valmo's OC share; will keep giving volumes to the most cost-efficient player per lane, share expected to increase as Valmo innovates and improves cost structure
Will continue to invest in marketing/new-user acquisition as long as return-on-investment threshold is met; plan to invest a lot more in acquiring rural customers over next one year
Goal is to bring state-of-the-art automation within all sort centres over the next few years

guidance_ledger.metric: Below-contribution cost operating leverage (people cost, tech/infra cost)
guidance_ledger.statement: People cost and technology/infrastructure cost expected to grow slower than NMV growth rate, generating operating leverage, though not strictly linear due to 2-3 year cloud contract cycles
Contribution margin for Mall will remain lower than core marketplace during the current multi-year investment phase focused on brand/selection onboarding; margin focus will come once business matures
Plan to eventually raise ad pricing once steady-state ad revenue is much higher than today, timing to be determined

risk_register.risk: Transient logistics disruption (145 bps one-time headwind) from Q2/Q3 FY26 3PL consolidation-driven capacity shortage
risk_register.note: Capacity has been unwound and more optimum cost structures put in place; 4% Q4 FY26 contribution margin is the new baseline

risk_register.risk: Macro/inflation uncertainty affecting consumer spending behavior
risk_register.note: Viewed as a potential tailwind for value-focused platforms historically, though absolute spending could act as a counter-headwind

risk_register.risk: 3PL industry consolidation leading partners to focus on margins over volume/pricing
risk_register.note: Being monitored in context of Valmo's scaling and potential mid-mile/sorting investment needs

risk_register.risk: Cash flow from operations negative trend expanding over past three quarters
risk_register.note: Management attributes this partly to one-offs from past periods; overall EBITDA and working capital trend seen as improving on LTM basis

risk_register.risk: Cash balance volatility due to timing of sale events near quarter-end
risk_register.note: Smoothed out when viewed on LTM FCF basis rather than quarterly cash flow

themes.label: Contribution margin recovery
themes.note: 170 bps sequential improvement to 4% exit rate as one-time Q2/Q3 FY26 logistics headwind (145 bps) is resolved

themes.label: Ad monetization ramp-up
themes.note: Ad revenue as % of NMV rising, catalogs on ads up 40%+ YoY, seller ad budgets more than doubled in a year, ROAS kept high to drive seller adoption before pricing changes

themes.label: In-sourcing (Valmo) vs 3PL logistics mix
themes.note: No fixed target for Valmo share; allocation driven purely by per-lane cost efficiency, expected to rise organically as Valmo innovates

themes.label: User acquisition and CAC efficiency
themes.note: AI tools like Vaani reducing CAC even while expanding into rural/deeper India; spend governed by ROI threshold, not fixed budget

themes.label: Meesho Mall / value brand distribution
themes.note: Fast NMV growth for Mall but lower contribution margin during multi-year investment phase focused on brand/selection onboarding

themes.label: Free cash flow trajectory
themes.note: LTM FCF is guiding metric; expected to keep improving with margin and growth gains despite carry-over of FY26 one-offs

themes.label: Growth runway / demand headroom
themes.note: India's online transaction penetration (~30%) far below other emerging markets (>80%), supporting 33% YoY annual transacting user growth

key_takeaways: Contribution margin improved 170 bps sequentially in Q4 FY26, with about 110 bps from logistics cost improvement, as the one-time Q2/Q3 FY26 logistics headwind (145 bps) is now behind the company; 4% is the new Q4 exit contribution margin baseline.
No specific EBITDA break-even guidance provided; LTM FCF remains the preferred guiding metric given quarterly cash-flow volatility from sale-event timing.
Valmo in-sourcing share (~50-55%) has no fixed target; volumes go to whichever partner (Valmo or 3PL) is most cost-efficient per lane, and share is expected to rise organically as Valmo innovates.

Ad revenue as % of NMV increased QoQ; more than two-thirds of sellers (GMV weighted) are active on ads, with products/catalogs on ads up more than 40% YoY and seller ad budgets more than doubling over the last year; ROAS remains among the industry best.
Annual transacting user base grew 33% YoY; India's online transaction penetration of smartphone users is only ~30% versus >80% in other emerging markets, indicating large growth runway.

Meesho Mall is scaling fast for value brands across mass India (not just premium customers), currently in an investment phase with lower contribution margin than core marketplace as the company prioritizes brand/selection onboarding over margin.

Revenue per order declined from ~INR57 (FY24) to ~INR47 (FY26), largely due to declining logistics cost, an accounting change (revenue netting of first-order discounts against S&M costs), and rising prepaid mix; management considers contribution margin the more instructive trajectory metric than revenue per order.
Cash balance declined ~INR300 crores QoQ due to timing of NMV/sale events near quarter-end and some tax-related reclassification; this volatility is smoothed out when viewed on an LTM FCF basis.
pressing_questions: Given free cash flow is the North Star, why not push in-sourcing (Valmo) down further (e.g., from 50% towards 30%) to further expand contribution margin and free cash flow?
Cash flow from operations on an absolute basis has expanded negatively for the past three quarters, even as CM and adjusted EBITDA margins improved — how does this reconcile?
Why has monetization (revenue per order) not moved QoQ despite NMV growth and rising ad contribution?
Should the 145 bps one-time logistics impact be assumed fully absent next year, flowing straight through to EBITDA?
What initiatives are underway to ensure logistics issues seen in FY26 do not recur and the business becomes more resilient?

TORNTPHARM.about: Torrent Pharmaceuticals Ltd is one of the leading Indian Pharmaceutical Company engaged in research, development, manufacturing and marketing of generic pharmaceutical formulations.[1] It is the flagship company of Torrent Group which also has presence in power and city gas distribution businesses.[2]

quarters.summary: Torrent Pharma reported strong Q1 FY27 consolidated growth (revenue +55%, EBITDA +61%) post the JB Pharma merger (effective 8th July 2026, appointed date 21st Jan 2026). Management guided to double-digit FY27 revenue growth for JB India Rx and high single-digit to low double-digit CC growth for JB CDMO/international, with cost synergies tracking ahead of the earlier ~INR450 crore/3-year plan (now expected well above INR100 crores in Year 1) and no EBITDA impact expected from transient integration-led revenue softness over the next 2-3 quarters. Semaglutide faces a near-term supply disruption (alternate source secured, SKUs expected back by end-August) that will delay the INR250 crore India target; Brazil semaglutide filing remains pending with ANVISA amid competitor approvals. Germany remains challenged by a key supplier's exit and tender losses, while US has turned profitable this year on cost savings and new launches.

subsections.label: Margin drivers
points: JB margin improvement is largely due to cost synergies being implemented sooner than expected; a minor part could be from operating leverage (CDMO growth) but primarily cost synergies.

Cost synergy realization steps started in Q4 FY26 and continued in Q1 FY27; every quarter should see some incremental margin improvement, though the exact quantum cannot be committed as some savings are being reinvested into the business per territory.

Base business gross margin improvement driven by: (1) annual price increases typically effective from April, (2) higher India branded business contribution to mix (76% vs historical 74%), and (3) some positive forex impact.
Opex increase of 22% partly reflects forex inflating expenses and partly reflects Q1 seasonally higher branded-business spend compared to rest of the year.

subsections.label: Cost synergy target update
points: First-year synergy target of INR90 crores is being tracked well ahead; management confirmed synergy realization will be above INR100 crores but declined to give an exact number due to uncertain top-line impact from ongoing portfolio changes.
Manufacturing synergies are being taken up in a second phase and are not included in the current synergy number.

Three-year synergy realization timeline could be much faster than originally planned given the merger completed roughly six months ahead of schedule; management wants one-two more quarters before firming up whether the year-3 margin target could be achieved in year 2.
