subsections.label: Demand trends
points: India organic growth (including semaglutide) reached 19% in Q1 FY27, a step-up from the prior quarters' IPM growth trajectory of 12.5-13%.
3-4 mature brands above INR100 crores are growing at single digits, indicating some maturation within the larger brand base even as overall growth accelerates.
JB India Rx integration focus period is targeted at 6 months, during which brand/division transfers from JB to Torrent are expected to be completed.

subsections.label: JB merger timeline
points: JB merger appointed date was 21st January 2026, with effective completion on 8th July 2026.

subsections.label: JB integration impact on segments
points: Following operational reset executed in Q4 FY26, JB business showed healthy recovery in Q1 FY27: India Rx +13%, international (incl. CDMO) +12%.
Business integration progressing well with policies/practices now largely aligned with base business across all territories.

Minor and transient revenue impact expected in some territories over next 2-3 quarters as certain brands/divisions are merged from JB to Torrent; sales trajectory typically returns to normal a few months after brand transfer if executed well.

International JB business evaluating portfolio rationalization of lower-margin, lower-priority products in certain territories (similar to earlier India trade generics rationalization) to enable network optimization.
JB CDMO business continues to perform well with no further integration required.

subsections.label: India base business drivers
points: 19% India growth driven by overall IPM growth pickup, new launch performance, and volume growth acceleration from field-force expansion.
India base growth breakdown: volume +5.1%, price +7.7%, new products +6%, versus IPM breakdown of volume +2%, price +5.8%, new products +3.3%.
Curatio growing 34% driven by OTC ad spends and field-force expansion; further field-force expansion planned in Curatio given positive outcome, expected to sustain high growth for rest of year.
Torrent (combined with JB) now ranks #1 in cardiac market, the largest and among the fastest-growing IPM segments — market outperformance continues.

Ex-semaglutide organic growth ~16%; ex-Curatio and ex-sema growth ~15-16%, indicating base brands (28 brands above INR100 crores, several growing 20%+ among top 10) also contributing meaningfully, likely aided by expansion done over last 2-3 years.
JB's own cardiac/gastro brands grew at a similar average trajectory to historical trends this quarter (some slightly slower, some slightly faster).

subsections.label: Semaglutide franchise
points: Strong Q1 start with 36% combined oral+injectable market share; held 94% oral share in June even after a new competitor entered.
Unforeseen supply issue with manufacturing partner for injectable product is a temporary setback; alternate supply source secured; all Semalix SKUs expected back in market by end of August.

Loss of sales expected in July and most of August from affected SKUs (20% of monthly contribution); management hopeful of quick market share recovery given established brand equity; no impact on oral brands or reusable SKU.

On track for INR250 crore FY target absent the supply issue (INR50 crore booked in Q1, up from previously indicated INR200-250 crore range); management wants one more quarter before revising annual objective post-recovery observation.

Market plateauing observed after initial ramp — attributed to intensity of early promotion/trials leading to drop-offs, side-effect-driven discontinuation among wrong-fit patients, and possible channel overstocking; not viewed as a concern, expected to improve gradually; July already showing traction, oral drop-offs lower than expected.
Estimated total India semaglutide (oral+injectable) market size ~INR700-800 crores or slightly bigger in year one.

subsections.label: Brazil segment detail
points: IQVIA data shows Torrent Brazil growing 19% vs 4% market growth, aided by strong top-brand performance and recent launches (primarily rosuvastatin ezetimibe).
Generics division contributes ~22% of Brazil sales and is a strong growth contributor.

One-time channel inventory reduction undertaken in response to channel requests for extended credit periods amid rising interest rate costs, causing primary sales growth (constant-currency revenue of BRL147 million, +3% YoY) to lag secondary sales; secondary sales continue to reflect underlying demand momentum per IQVIA data.
Excluding the channel inventory correction, constant-currency sales would have grown 15%-18%; normalized mid-teens growth expected to return in Q2.

subsections.label: US and Germany segment detail
points: US constant-currency revenue reached $44 million, +23% growth, driven by new launches achieving target market share plus certain one-time opportunities; US business turning profitable this year (unlike the last five years) via cost savings and new launches; 17 products launched in last 30 months contributing $20-25 million, largely compensating price erosion; trajectory expected to keep improving on both top-line and bottom-line.

Germany constant-currency revenue was EUR29 million, down 9% YoY, driven by supply disruption at a third-party supplier (contributing 10-15% of Germany revenue, now out of business) and lower tender off-take; despite cost-reduction efforts, company still sometimes outbid by peers in tenders; management states 'not out of the woods' in Germany, more cost optimization needed to win tenders.

subsections.label: Geographic approach
points: Management stated they battle by country rather than as a consolidated 'base business ex-JB' constant currency figure; India, Brazil, US and Germany together represent about 85% of the business.

Branded markets (Russia, Philippines, Mexico, Brazil) performing well and ahead of underlying market growth; generic markets (US, Germany) show divergent trends — US stabilizing/improving, Germany still challenged.
Torrent (with JB) ranks first in the cardiac market.
US business revenue is now approximately flat in USD terms compared to FY14, underscoring the scale of the recent turnaround.

subsections.label: Supply disruption
points: A key third-party supplier accounting for 10-15% of Germany revenue has gone out of business, disrupting supply in that market.

subsections.label: Field force and productivity
points: Combined field-force strength stood at 9,400 reps (base business 7,200 + JB 2,200) at end of Q1 FY27, with combined PCPM (per capita per month productivity) just over 10 lakhs and further scope for improvement.
JB field-force attrition down sharply to 16% in June vs nearly 30% pre-acquisition, reflecting integration progress.

Base business rep additions will come largely via restructuring from JB divisions rather than fresh expansion; overall total MR count is expected to reduce despite base business additions, with Q2 strength expected near 9,000; end-of-year headcount not yet charted but likely similar or slightly lower.

subsections.label: IPM growth acceleration
points: IPM growth has picked up this quarter across chronic and acute therapies; management cannot yet attribute the driver definitively (possible factors include shift from trade generics to Rx, though management personally does not think this is the primary driver) and will assess over the next 2-3 quarters.
Higher-than-expected volume uptick seen in the market generally, not just for Torrent; too early after one quarter to pinpoint the exact cause.

subsections.label: Germany competitive position
points: Germany market share has declined from about 7% to 5% over the last four to five years amid various challenges.

subsections.label: Brazil semaglutide competitive dynamics
points: Five recent semaglutide regulatory approvals in Brazil, four of which went to a single competing company, giving that competitor a first-mover advantage ahead of Torrent's own approval.
Management expects double-digit market share in Brazil semaglutide once Torrent's own product is approved and launched.

subsections.label: JB Pharma merger
points: Merger of JB with Torrent Pharma completed effective 8th July 2026; appointed date 21st January 2026; process ran roughly six months ahead of schedule.
Next set of integration activities already initiated post merger completion, including merging certain brands and divisions in India business from JB to Torrent.

subsections.label: Capital allocation and future M&A
points: Management prefers to wait at least another 12-18 months post JB acquisition (currently ~6 months in) to gain comfort that integration has gone smoothly before evaluating new opportunities.
Company would not want to exceed roughly 3x-3.5x net debt to EBITDA (current leverage 2.07x) for any future opportunity considered.

India acquisition opportunities would always be preferred first over international, size being equal; absent a major India opportunity currently on the horizon, mid-size international acquisitions may be considered.

Revenue synergies from JB integration are viewed as achievable only from next year onward given integration-related changes happening this year; potential seen in cross-sell, knowledge transfer and combined field force, particularly in cardiac and gastro brands/segments, but management wants full integration completed before quantifying.

subsections.label: Key flagged risks
points: Transient revenue impact in some JB territories over next 2-3 quarters as brands/divisions are merged from JB to Torrent, with the process typically taking a few months before sales trajectory normalizes.
Semaglutide injectable supply disruption at manufacturing partner (unforeseen and temporary); alternate source secured, but sales loss expected in July and most of August.
Semaglutide market plateauing/drop-offs due to over-promotion driven early trials, product side effects among ill-fit patients, and potential channel overstocking.

Brazil semaglutide first-mover advantage lost as competitors received ANVISA approvals first (four of five recent approvals to a single company); regulator timeline for Torrent's own approval remains uncertain ('months, not years' per management's own perception, not a regulator commitment).

Germany: key third-party supplier (10-15% of Germany revenue) has gone out of business, hurting supply; company continues to be outbid by peers in the tender process despite cost efforts — management states 'not out of the woods' in Germany.
Brazil one-time channel inventory reduction (in response to channel requests for extended credit amid rising interest costs) depressed primary sales versus secondary sales this quarter.

subsections.label: Outlook statements
points: For full year FY27, double-digit revenue growth for JB's India Rx business should still be possible given robust Q1 underlying trend (an uninterrupted quarter); international business expected to recover post changes implemented.
JB CDMO business expected to deliver high single-digit to low double-digit constant currency growth for the full year, given continued strong performance and no further integration required.

Cost synergy realization tracking ahead of plan and expected to increase quarter-on-quarter, which should offset any potential revenue weakness such that there should be no EBITDA-level impact for JB this year; management emphasizes no essential costs cut that could hinder growth.

Overall India base business expected to continue outperforming market growth; FY27 focus areas: improving market share in focus therapies, improving field-force productivity in expanded divisions, and continued scaling of the Curatio business.
Management wants to wait one more quarter (post semaglutide supply recovery observation) before providing a revised annual objective for the semaglutide franchise.
Management declined to give full-year margin guidance for the combined entity, wanting to wait one more quarter for the merged business to settle post July 8th system/business integration trigger.

Three-year JB synergy realization timeline could accelerate given the merger closed ~6 months ahead of schedule; management wants 1-2 more quarters before confirming whether year-3 margin targets could be pulled into year 2.

Base business EBITDA margin guidance reiterated at least 0.5% improvement per year, in line with the trend of the last two years; Q1 registered a 0.5 percentage point improvement to 33.3% from 32.8% last year, with sustainable gross margin seen rising up to about 77%.

guidance_ledger.metric: JB India Rx business revenue growth
guidance_ledger.statement: For the full year FY27, double-digit revenue growth for JB's India Rx business should still be possible given the robust underlying trend seen in Q1 of an uninterrupted quarter.
The international business should also recover post the changes implemented; high single-digit to low double-digit constant currency growth for the full year should be possible for JB CDMO.
Cost synergy realization should further increase quarter-on-quarter, offsetting any potential revenue weakness; there should not be any impact at the EBITDA level for the JB business this year.
First-year synergy target of INR90 crores is being tracked well ahead; certainly going to be above 90, definitely above 100 crores.
The three-year synergy realization could be much faster than originally planned given the merger completed about six months ahead of schedule.

guidance_ledger.metric: JB margin trajectory (year-3 target achieved in year-2)
guidance_ledger.statement: Whether the year-3 margin target for JB could be achieved in year 2 itself - management said 'you'll have to wait for one or two quarters more... but the way things are moving on, it's looking positive.'

Revenue synergies are only comfortable starting from next year because of changes happening this year; good potential exists via cross-sell, knowledge transfer and combined field force, particularly in cardiac and gastro segments.

guidance_ledger.metric: India base business growth vs market
guidance_ledger.statement: Going forward, we expect our overall India base business to continue outperforming the market growth.
We are hopeful that the Curatio business should continue with a similar high growth trajectory for the rest of the year.

We were well on track to achieve our INR250 crores target for the year in absence of the supply issue; but given the supply issue, that's definitely not going to be possible; we would rather wait for another quarter to see recovery and then give the annual number.
We have already secured an alternate supply source for the product and are hopeful that all Semalix SKUs should be back in the market by the end of August.

We remain hopeful that we should be able to recover our market share quickly due to the early established brand equity; this setback should not materially derail the overall leadership trajectory of the brand for the rest of the year.
We expect the normalized growth rate to come back to again mid-teens level growth as reflected in the IQVIA data.
I would guess that it'll take months and not years, but that's my perception rather than any definite comment from the regulator.

guidance_ledger.metric: Brazil semaglutide expected market share upon launch
guidance_ledger.statement: As long as we are not very far behind, we are confident that we'll be able to capture a double-digit market share, as we have done and demonstrated many times in the past.
This year we would be a profitable entity in the US, unlike the last five years; US is on a stable trajectory and will only get better from here in top line and bottom line.
I can't say we are out of the woods in Germany; I would say right now we are still in the middle of the woods.
I would like to wait for one more quarter till the combined entity settles before I can try and give you some guidance for the full year.
Base business guidance since the last two years has been at least a 0.5% improvement; Q1 registered 0.5% improvement to 33.3% vs 32.8% last year.
Anything up to 77% is looking definitely sustainable; beyond that other factors have played out contributing to incremental gross margin.
We expect that Q2 the MR strength should be closer to 9,000; end of year, we haven't charted out yet, but it probably will be around the same, maybe slightly less.

guidance_ledger.metric: JB integration focus for next 6 months
guidance_ledger.statement: For the next six months, the focus will be largely on ensuring that the merging of divisions and transfer of brands from JB to Torrent goes smoothly; growth initiatives will be looked at after that, by end of year.
We would not want to be above, say, 3x or 3.5x net debt to EBITDA for whatever opportunity we consider.

In absence of any demand shocks in the financial year due to geopolitical factors, we expect that our base business may potentially deliver very strong year-on-year organic growth, higher than the previous year.
So can we expect, let's say, a mid-teens kind of a growth on your organic India business for FY27? - Yes...that would be realistic.
I would guide you towards a double-digit growth for Torrent in the coming years...over the course of 26-27, we should be between 10% to 15% of top-line growth.
Low single-digit growth for next year. Below 5%. In constant currency.
I would say that single-digit growth is a good way to look at US going forward for the next couple of years before we get our own major product launch.
We would be having a single-digit number of launches in the coming 9 months, 10 months.
We're at about 5% this year in FY26. Maybe incremental 0.5% is what could be expected in the upcoming year.
We had guided for up to INR450 crores synergies by year 3, and about 20% of that in year 1... 60% to 80% cumulative in the next year and then the last 20% in the third year.
The confidence on the revenue synergy getting delivered is certainly getting higher, but again the timeline remains the same...this year we will not see any material synergies.
We anyway had a plan to go up to 7,500 in FY27. That plan continues, that will be executed as per plan.
Margin, EBITDA margin of the Semaglutide franchise would obviously be much, much lower...hopefully by next year I think it should start reversing.
We can share an update on that maybe by next quarter.
We would launch in three teams, and ideally we'll launch about maybe two products per team per year.
Our objective is that any new such launch should add incrementally minimum 1% to 2% to the total India growth over the first year or two years of launch.
Our launch timeline we cannot share at this moment, but would be in the next 12 to 18 months. Certainly not before the patent expiration.

risk_register.note: Minor and transient impact expected in some territories over next 2-3 quarters as brands/divisions are merged from JB to Torrent.

risk_register.risk: Semaglutide injectable supply disruption
risk_register.note: Unforeseen supply issue with manufacturing partner; alternate source secured, SKUs expected back by end of August, sales loss expected in July-August.

risk_register.risk: Semaglutide market plateauing
risk_register.note: Market showing signs of plateauing after initial ramp-up due to over-promotion driven trials, side-effect-driven discontinuation, and possible channel overstocking; management not concerned, expects gradual improvement.

risk_register.risk: Brazil semaglutide competitive/regulatory delay

key_takeaways: Consolidated revenues were INR4,921 crores, up by 55%, while operating EBITDA at INR1,664 crores was up by 61%. Operating EBITDA margin for the quarter stood at 33.8%.
The merger of JB with Torrent Pharma has been completed with effect from 8th of July, appointed date being 21st January 2026.

During the quarter, the underlying JB business reported revenues of INR1,201 crores, up by 10% Y-o-Y, with operating EBITDA of INR424 crores and EBITDA margin of 35.3%, registering an improvement of more than 6%. JB India branded business grew at 13% for the quarter. International business grew by 12%.

Torrent base business revenues grew by 17% for the quarter. Operating EBITDA for the quarter was INR1,240 crores, up 20%, with margins now at 33.3%. India business reported strong growth of 19%, while Brazil revenues grew up by 27%. On the generic business side, US business grew by 36%, which includes certain one-time opportunities, while Germany revenues were up by 3%.
Leverage, that is net debt to EBITDA, stands at 2.07x considering underlying EBITDA of the combined company.

With the completion of the merger process in July, we have now already initiated the next set of integration activities... there could be a minor and transient impact in revenues in some territories until the integration is completed over the next 2 to 3 quarters.

The recent unforeseen supply-related issue with our manufacturing partner for the injectable product is an unfortunate temporary setback. However, we have already secured an alternate supply source for the product and are hopeful that all Semalix SKUs should be back in the market by the end of August.
With INR50 crores of combined sales registered in Q1, we were well on track to achieve our INR250 crores target for the year in absence of the supply issue.

On semaglutide, following the strong start, our semaglutide franchise in India recorded Q1 market share of 36% for the oral and injectable combined as per the Pharmatrac Dataset. Even with one more competitor entering the oral market, we were able to hold on to 94% market share in the month of June.

During the quarter, we undertook a one-time channel inventory reduction in response to channel requests for extended credit periods amid rising interest rate costs, which led to a primary sale which is inferior to our growth of our secondary sales.

In Germany, our business registered a constant currency revenue of EUR29 million, down by 9%. The growth continued to be impacted by supply disruption at third-party supplier and lower tender off-take during the quarter.
pressing_questions: Is it fair to assume that the margin we were expecting for JB in year three is now possible in year two itself?
So, for the base business, would it be possible to share what would be your constant currency growth this quarter (Torrent Pharma on a consol. level, excluding JB)?
Anything on the margins you would like to call out in terms of your guidance for the full year? Are we reiterating or any color on margins for the full year?
For example, in the US piece, the absolute revenue levels are virtually the same as it was in FY14 in USD terms. How should we see the trajectory going forward for US as we move ahead?
How do you see Germany picking up this year and next year given market share decline from about 7% to 5% over the last four, five years?
Is it because of Dr. Reddy's issue where the approval for us is stuck (Brazil semaglutide)?

quarters.summary: Consolidated Q4 FY26 revenue grew 42% YoY to INR4,197 crores with operating EBITDA up 41% at 32.3% margin, driven by JB Pharma consolidation from 21st January 2026; base business (ex-JB) grew 16% with margins at 32.7%. Management expects India base business to potentially deliver very strong YoY organic growth in FY27 (higher than FY26), led by Semaglutide, Curatio, chronic outperformance and new first-to-market launches, absent demand shocks; Brazil is guided to 10-15% top-line growth in FY26-27; Germany is guided to low single-digit (below 5%) CC growth; US is expected to see single-digit growth for the next couple of years; JB Pharma merger synergies of up to INR450 crores by year 3 remain on track with phasing possibly accelerating.

subsections.label: Merger and accounting update
points: Pursuant to the acquisition of controlling stake in JB Pharma, consolidated financial statements include JB Pharma, its subsidiaries, and acquisition effects from 21st January 2026.
Shareholder approval for merger of JB Pharma with Torrent has been received; process is in the last stage; final NCLT hearing expected next month.

Amortization charge of INR257 crores pertains to fair valuation of intangibles that came onto the balance sheet as part of business combination accounting (Ind AS 103), under the fair value method for non-controlling interest.

Minority interest of minus INR25 crores reflects allocation of net adjusted profit (JB stub-period PAT of INR143 crores less net amortization/DTL impact of INR195 crores = INR52 crores balance), split 51.2% NCI / 48.8% owners' equity — not the raw JB reported profit.
Amortization/DTL impact is expected to sustain going forward as the run-rate to model for full year, effective from 21st January.

subsections.label: Margin trajectory and ESOP treatment
points: EBITDA margin trajectory for the merged entity is tracking ahead of expectations for the first year post-acquisition; some cost synergies were realized sooner than planned.
Reported/press-release EBITDA margin figures are stated excluding ESOP charges.
As JB will not carry ESOP cost going forward (post-acquisition), margin improvement is expected from Q1 onwards on a like-for-like basis.

subsections.label: India business drivers
points: Torrent's base business ex of JB grew at 15% during the quarter versus IPM growth of 10% as per PharmaTrac; base business continues to be amongst the fastest growing out of top 10 companies in IPM on full-year basis.
Curatio business growth of 27% in FY26 driven by strong demand generation on account of OTC ad spends and field force expansion; hopeful of continued strong traction in coming year.
Field force expansion over past two years has been executed well and will continue to be pursued in the upcoming financial year.

Key levers for India outperformance: Semaglutide launch adding significantly to base business growth, continued strong traction in Curatio, chronic business outperformance, and upcoming first-to-market new launches.

subsections.label: Semaglutide launch dynamics
points: Launch off to a very strong start, ranked first out of all generic launches; two brands launched - Semalix and Sembolic.
Product availability in both injectable and oral formats has benefited the brand significantly; early advantage expected to help sustain high market share over coming quarters.

As of 21st May, one more competitor has entered the oral market, which will impact oral market share; however two-month head start and early mover advantage provide comfort on maintaining majority share.

Semaglutide franchise EBITDA margin is currently much lower than corporate average due to lower gross margin at launch (higher API cost) and higher launch spends; approach has been to prioritize market share first, profitability later; margin trajectory expected to start reversing next year.
Injectable manufactured by partner; oral is manufactured and developed in-house, with API outsourced.
Injectable gross margins expected to follow normal trajectory towards base business level over time (partner product may have slightly lower margins, not materially lower).
Oral gross margins currently lower than injectable but expected to improve over next 6-12 months as Semaglutide API prices drop significantly.
Vial format being explored but not a big priority currently; bigger opportunity seen in pens and oral; in-house manufacturing considered if product scales to sizeable opportunity.

Pricing: injectable price is being held steady with no plans to reduce; oral price was reduced from INR149 to INR109 per tablet after initial launch at higher price due to higher API procurement cost at the time; no further oral price reduction expected from here.

Comparison to Sitagliptin (2023 launch, best launch in past decade in diabetes space) which did INR70-75 crores in first year with 20-22% generic market share; Semaglutide currently trending toward INR200-250 crores at this stage, reflecting a much larger opportunity.

Supply from partner (for injectable) not seen as a major constraint on most SKUs; some lower-dosage SKUs could see temporary supply challenges but contribution to overall sales from those SKUs is low.

subsections.label: New product pipeline (India)
points: First to launch generic Brexpiprazole in April in India after conducting clinical trials; classified as a moderate-sized CNS/psychiatry opportunity expected to help improve market share in CNS.

Phase 3 clinical trial ongoing for Resmetirom (USFDA-approved for NASH); no innovator currently present in India; if trial completes successfully within projected timelines, company may be first to launch in India post patent expiry; classified as a large-sized opportunity.
Patent for Resmetirom expected to expire within the next year; launch timeline expected 12-18 months out, strictly after patent expiration.
Objective for any new first-to-market launch is to add incrementally a minimum 1-2% to total India growth over first year or two of launch.
Several other such first-to-market products being worked on in India with goal of early mover advantage.
No material increase in R&D spend expected from this pipeline strategy; largely a reallocation of spend to India from other markets.
In talks with multiple companies in China for in-licensing, particularly interesting opportunities in oncology; deal terms still being worked out.

subsections.label: Brazil business performance
points: Q4 constant currency revenue of BRL259 million, 11% YoY growth (internal sales basis); IQVIA data shows Q4 market growth at 6% with Torrent growing at 17%.
Healthy volume growth coupled with mid-single-digit price increases.
New launches in large markets like Rosuvastatin and Ezetimibe getting good traction; first oncology product launched in Brazil.

Rosuvastatin/Ezetimibe market is roughly trending towards BRL850 million per year, among the largest single markets Torrent operates in Brazil, with ~8.5% market share currently, working towards building further share.
Q4 growth breakup: volume growth flat to slightly negative, price increase ~5%, new introductions (NI) contributing ~7%; NI is the main driving force in the business.
Guidance suggests annual trend (rather than quarterly variation) is a better indicator; both internal sales and IQVIA annual trends match over time.
Rich pipeline of 58 molecules awaiting ANVISA approval; launch capacity constrained by team structure — historically three teams, launching about two products per team per year.

subsections.label: Germany business performance
points: Constant currency revenue of EUR31 million, down 1%; growth impacted due to disruption at a third-party supplier.
Regulatory development: automatic substitution of biosimilars and inclusion of biosimilars in the tender system in Germany.
Torrent has launched its first biosimilar in Germany (with a European partner) and will start participating in tenders in coming months; tenders expected first in June-July timeframe.

Landscape for biosimilars changing rapidly - moving from non-substitutable, promotion-driven model to substitutable, tender-driven model similar to generics, which fits Torrent's core tender-based business model.

Early days for biosimilar business; sales not yet material; company has not yet quoted in any tender; open to partnerships with Asian manufacturing partners in addition to current European partner to build out portfolio over time.

subsections.label: US business performance
points: Constant currency revenues of USD38 million, up 9%; growth from new launches where target market share achieved, and increased purchase volume on existing products.
Business is profitable before R&D expenses (stated objective); working towards full profitability including all costs.

Expect single-digit number of new launches in coming 9-10 months; potential of each product depends on number of competitors; single-digit revenue growth expected as a reasonable outlook for next couple of years pending a major product launch.
No 180-day exclusivity products where company is sole Day-1 filer currently.

subsections.label: JB Pharma CDMO / international business
points: JB Pharma's international CDMO business was impacted due to change of control and realignment of business practices.
Negative impact also from ongoing geopolitical situation in the Middle East.
Discontinuation of certain JB businesses done in Q4 will remain in effect for rest of the financial year; no plans for further discontinuation at this stage.

subsections.label: Semaglutide market dynamics (India)
points: Oral market expected to end up being maybe 20-30% of injectable market size; company currently has higher oral share due to lack of other players, but this should normalize as competitors enter.
General reception from prescribers favors products closer in convenience/usage to the innovator, as it requires less patient education.
Company's own Semaglutide sales are faring higher than internally projected.
Market size uncertain 3-5 years out given dynamic competitive landscape, more innovator pipeline expected in next 1-2 years, and more oral innovation potentially entering market.
Overall considered the biggest launch and biggest opportunity for the industry by multiple factors, despite uncertainty on ultimate market size.

subsections.label: Semaglutide market dynamics (Brazil and int'l)
points: In Brazil, Ozempic is declining rapidly while Wegovy is growing fast, driven by ANVISA's strict stance disallowing off-label Ozempic use for weight loss since Wegovy launch about a year ago; historically Ozempic was used for weight loss due to Wegovy's absence.

No Semaglutide launches yet in Brazil as of the call date, market off-patent for a couple of months; ANVISA has rejected some files but approved none yet; all filers so far have filed Ozempic, none for Wegovy.

Company's Ozempic file is under ANVISA review with no clear approval timeline; expects to be among first five players on Ozempic side despite declining market; Wegovy filing in Brazil still in progress, no update to share yet.

Local Brazilian manufacturers face duty on APIs but not finished products; Torrent imports finished products and pays duty on those; customs duty (8%) is absorbable given high gross margins of branded generic market and not seen as a hurdle.

In other international markets (Canada, Turkey, Saudi Arabia, etc.), company disclosure has been limited; company believes it is ahead of the curve versus peers in some smaller markets; already filed Ozempic in about four-five markets and is in 'Wave 1' of launches (sometimes first-to-market) in about five markets; in other markets, positioned in Wave 2 or Wave 3.
No volume guidance provided for pens/injectors/devices across markets for FY27-29, as volumes depend on competitive dynamics.

subsections.label: Pricing strategy
points: Management expects Semaglutide pricing in India to broadly follow normal IPM price trajectory of about 4-5% annual increases, rather than aggressive price erosion, despite differing go-to-market approaches by competing companies at varying price points.

subsections.label: JB Pharma acquisition and merger process
points: Shareholder approval received for merger of JB Pharma with Torrent; process in last stage; only NCLT approval remaining, with final hearing expected next month.
Consolidated financials include JB Pharma, its subsidiaries and acquisition effects from 21st January 2026 pursuant to acquisition of controlling stake.

subsections.label: Cost synergies
points: Guided synergy target of up to INR450 crores by year 3, phased 20% in year 1, 60-80% cumulative in year 2, and remaining ~20% in year 3.
Synergy execution remains on track with no material update from the last call; difficult to quantify quarter by quarter as action implementation and actual savings reflection may lag.

Margin trajectory for this year is tracking ahead of expectations, with some costs taken out sooner than planned; phasing of synergies appears to be accelerating, i.e., what was expected next year may be delivered this year — actual quantum for next year to be confirmed in a couple more quarters.

subsections.label: Revenue synergies
points: Confidence on revenue synergies being delivered is increasing as management spends more time managing the business directly, though timeline for material revenue synergy realization remains unchanged (not expected this year due to implementation lead time).

subsections.label: China in-licensing opportunity
points: In talks with multiple companies in China, particularly interesting opportunities in oncology products; deal terms still being worked out, timing uncertain.

subsections.label: Flagged headwinds
points: Potential demand shocks in the domestic Indian market due to geopolitical factors are unknown and could impact India business growth expectations for FY27; too early to comment on GDP growth impact.
Germany business growth impacted by disruption at a third-party supplier.
JB Pharma's international CDMO business impacted by change of control/realignment of business practices and by the ongoing geopolitical situation in the Middle East.
Semaglutide oral market share to be impacted by entry of an additional competitor in the oral market as of 21st May.
Potential supply constraints from partner on some lower-dosage Semaglutide injectable SKUs, though contribution of those SKUs to overall sales is low.
Uncertainty around ultimate Semaglutide market size given unknown competitive dynamics, more innovator pipeline entrants over next 1-2 years, and potential new oral innovator products.

subsections.label: India outlook
points: Expect India base business to continue outperforming market growth, driven by Semaglutide, Curatio traction, chronic business outperformance, and first-to-market launches.

In absence of demand shocks due to geopolitical factors, base business may potentially deliver very strong YoY organic growth, higher than the previous year; a mid-teens kind of growth characterized as 'realistic' by management if no external demand shocks occur.
Field force plan to reach 7,500 in FY27, after which, combined with full JB MR strength post-merger, no further expansion plans.

subsections.label: Brazil outlook
points: Double-digit growth guided for coming years; expect 10-15% top-line growth over FY26-27; guidance given on annual basis rather than quarterly due to volatility in quarterly IQVIA/internal sales data.

subsections.label: Germany outlook
points: Low single-digit growth (below 5%) expected in constant currency terms for next year.

subsections.label: US outlook
points: Single-digit number of launches expected in coming 9-10 months; single-digit revenue growth expected for next couple of years before a major product launch occurs.

subsections.label: Semaglutide outlook
points: Update on supply constraints for certain SKUs and market share to be shared in coming quarters; margin trajectory expected to start reversing next year as gross margins improve with declining API costs.

guidance_ledger.statement: In absence of any demand shocks in the financial year due to geopolitical factors, we expect that our base business may potentially deliver very strong year-on-year organic growth, higher than the previous year.
So can we expect, let's say, a mid-teens kind of a growth on your organic India business for FY27? - Yes...that would be realistic.
I would guide you towards a double-digit growth for Torrent in the coming years...over the course of 26-27, we should be between 10% to 15% of top-line growth.
Low single-digit growth for next year. Below 5%. In constant currency.
I would say that single-digit growth is a good way to look at US going forward for the next couple of years before we get our own major product launch.
We would be having a single-digit number of launches in the coming 9 months, 10 months.
We're at about 5% this year in FY26. Maybe incremental 0.5% is what could be expected in the upcoming year.
We had guided for up to INR450 crores synergies by year 3, and about 20% of that in year 1... 60% to 80% cumulative in the next year and then the last 20% in the third year.
The confidence on the revenue synergy getting delivered is certainly getting higher, but again the timeline remains the same...this year we will not see any material synergies.
We anyway had a plan to go up to 7,500 in FY27. That plan continues, that will be executed as per plan.
Margin, EBITDA margin of the Semaglutide franchise would obviously be much, much lower...hopefully by next year I think it should start reversing.
We can share an update on that maybe by next quarter.
We would launch in three teams, and ideally we'll launch about maybe two products per team per year.
Our objective is that any new such launch should add incrementally minimum 1% to 2% to the total India growth over the first year or two years of launch.
Our launch timeline we cannot share at this moment, but would be in the next 12 to 18 months. Certainly not before the patent expiration.

key_takeaways: Consolidated revenue for Q4 was INR4,197 crores, up by 42%, while operating EBITDA at INR1,356 crores was up 41%. The combined operating EBITDA margin stood at 32.3%.
Excluding JB Pharma, Torrent Pharma's base business revenues grew by 16% for Q4, operating EBITDA grew by 16%, and the margins were 32.7%.
For the full year, the overall revenue grew by 15%, EBITDA margins were maintained at 32.7%, and operating EBITDA grew by 16%.

Our two largest branded markets, India and Brazil, continue to deliver healthy double-digit growth. India business grew at 15% and Brazil grew at INR growth rate of 30%. On the generic side, US business grew at 31% INR growth and Germany grew at an INR growth of 16%.
We have received the requisite shareholder approval for the merger of JB Pharma with Torrent, and we are in the last stage of the process now.
The overall leverage, that is net debt to EBITDA considering JB's full year EBITDA for FY'25-'26, stands at 2.3x.
Today, the board has recommended a final dividend of INR9 per equity share.

Our launch is off to a very strong start and is ranked first out of all the generic launches. Torrent held 38% share among generic players as per the PharmaTrac April data set, with 28% share in the injectable format and 100% share in the oral format.

We had guided for up to INR450 crores synergies by year 3, and about 20% of that in year 1... our early sense is that the margin trajectory that we had expected for this year, we are tracking above that so far.

Management reiterated guidance of consolidated adjusted EBITDA breakeven by Q3 FY28 and ₹1,000 crores adjusted EBITDA by FY31, while continuing aggressive investment in InstaHelp, which it views as strategically critical despite structurally lower margins.

subsections.label: Quarterly performance drivers
points: Consolidated NTV grew 42% YoY to ₹1,465 crore, and consolidated revenue grew 44% YoY to ₹528 crore in Q1 FY27; total orders grew 79% YoY to 13.2 million.
1.2 million new customers were added, taking annual transacting user base to 9.3 million.
Growth was broad-based across the business, and the core became even more profitable.
Consolidated Adjusted EBITDA loss of ₹(65) crores was almost entirely driven by InstaHelp's loss of ₹(132) crores.
Excluding InstaHelp, the rest of operations delivered an adjusted EBITDA profit of ₹67 crores, up more than 100% (specifically about 116%) YoY.
Balance sheet remains very strong with cash and treasury investments of ₹2,019 crores, only about ₹2 crores lower than the previous quarter end, even while investing in InstaHelp.
InstaHelp loss per order improved by 101 (rupees) QoQ.
India Consumer Services Adjusted EBITDA margin improved 170 basis points YoY to 6.9% of NTV from 5.2% in the prior year.
Native Adjusted EBITDA loss improved 410 basis points YoY.
InstaHelp's required service professional payout currently stands at ₹130 to ₹160 per hour.

subsections.label: India core services acceleration
points: India Consumer Services excluding InstaHelp grew 29% NTV YoY to ₹1,056 crores, first time crossing ₹1,000 crores NTV in a quarter.
This marks the fourth straight quarter of acceleration (10% → 19% → 21% → 26% → 29% YoY).
Core business continues to compound based on consistent quality, customer trust, increasing partner earnings, and densification of micro-markets.
Management noted the 29% growth partly benefits from a muted base last year due to unseasonal rains and monsoons, but the acceleration is broad-based, secular and strong.

Margins in this business have spikiness in AMJ and OND quarters, so margins are best visualized yearly; YoY margin improvement was a healthy 170 basis points, taking margin to 6.9% of NTV from 5.2% a year ago.
Long-term guidance for this business is 9-10% adjusted EBITDA margin as % of NTV; currently at 6.9%, giving confidence of reaching that target.

Beauty segment called out as an important growth contributor: improved supply-side quality via retraining/retooling, a mobility program giving service professionals (mostly women) access to two-wheelers (majority now have access, up from a minority a year back), expanded assortment (Japanese facials, Ayurvedic facials/solutions with Forest Essentials in Luxe category).
Tier 2 markets are performing even better than Tier 1, and management feels only beginning to realize potential there.
Even in oldest, most penetrated cities like Delhi NCR and oldest categories, fair headroom remains, keeping those micro-markets performing well.

Annual transacting user growth of over half a million (~5 lakh) QoQ attributed partly to seasonality but also to secularly solid funnel metrics (MAUs, DAUs, MTUs) and improving conversion and fulfillment rates.
Growth not driven by more aggressive marketing — marketing spend nearly flat YoY (₹24 crore to ₹25 crore) with better ROI.

subsections.label: International scale-up
points: International business scaling fast and profitably; expected to become the second core profit engine of Urban Company going forward.
International NTV grew 76% YoY (58% ex-currency impact) to ₹237 crore.
Both UAE and Singapore delivered profitable growth.
JV in Kingdom of Saudi Arabia grew well with margin; management now has line of sight of profitability in the JV in coming quarters.

subsections.label: Native growth and margin improvement
points: Native NTV grew 51% YoY to ₹119 crore, and net revenue grew 60% YoY to ₹95 crore, with Adjusted EBITDA loss narrowing to (7.3)% of NTV from (11.4)% a year ago, a 410 basis-point improvement.
Native continues to demonstrate strong growth with improving margins.
As early water-purifier cohorts complete their first replacement cycle, about 75% are renewing filters through Urban Company, adding a recurring, higher-margin revenue stream.
Management has line of sight of profitability in Native over the next few quarters; incremental capital needed until cash generation begins is expected to be not very substantial.

New premium product launches: M3 water purifier (3-year no-service-needed, stainless steel tank, adaptive mineralizer, pH balancer) succeeding M1/M2 (2023, 2-year no-service model); Native Lock Ultra smart lock with inbuilt camera, auto-unlock, lurker alert, tamper-proof design, highly rated online.

Native strategy: not building a consumer durables company; focused on premium, tech-first, adjacency categories to core services, capturing disproportionate share of profit pool (even if not revenue share); may add at most one more category over next 5 years, deliberately limited to avoid proliferation.
Native aims to serve the platform's 9.3 million annual transacting users more deeply as an extension of core services, building a 'home platform of services and solutions.'

subsections.label: InstaHelp scale-up
points: InstaHelp is the company's largest investment today and continues to scale; delivered 3.82 million orders, up 43% QoQ.
Loss per order improved from ₹(447) in Q4 to ₹(346) in Q1 FY27 as micro-market density built up.
Company investing aggressively in InstaHelp to cement leadership in a category viewed as strategically important.
Addressable market (TAM) in top 15 cities estimated between ₹7,000 crore and ₹12,000 crore NTV annually.
Management declined to go beyond the shareholder's letter disclosures on InstaHelp given competitive dynamics.

subsections.label: Training capacity - Core services
points: Management mindful of the need for adequate training infrastructure and trainer capacity, alongside leveraging AI to make training more efficient.
Describes training engine as 'running smoothly and well-oiled' currently, catering to growth, with a clear plan for the next few quarters.

subsections.label: Training capacity - InstaHelp
points: Pace of supply addition in InstaHelp has been very high; keeping pace with training infrastructure and trainer capacity is 'all hands on deck.'
Focus is not just on adding more training rooms/trainers, but improving training efficacy and ROI on training.
Category training/supply build-out expected to take longer to settle down (referenced anecdotally via a market where InstaHelp was 'sold out').

subsections.label: Strategic rationale for InstaHelp investment
points: InstaHelp seen as strategically relevant: a high-frequency category enabling entry into the home weekly (vs. monthly/quarterly for core services), creating a volume moat around the core business and driving multi-visit app usage.
Investment in InstaHelp viewed beyond category-level ROI, factored into the larger platform strategy.

Given the large TAM view (base case ₹7,000-8,000 crore, bull case ₹10,000-12,000 crore NTV annually across top 15 cities), management believes it is important to be aggressive and capture a disproportionate share of both the TAM and its profit pool.
Base case assumes 7-8 million monthly transacting households (bull case 10-12 million) at 3 transactions/month per household, implying ~20 million annual transacting households in the base case.

Actions of all 3 market players over past 6 months show household coverage limited to 3.5-4 million households, with investment going into subsidizing repeat-user orders rather than TAM expansion — Urban Company acknowledges being 'as guilty' of this given competitive dynamics.

subsections.label: InstaHelp AOV and pricing dynamics
points: Management believes AOV must reach ~₹300/hour (TAM assumption of ₹200-300/hour full price) for InstaHelp to break even, driven by required service professional payout of ~₹150/hour (rule of thumb, range ₹130-160/hour, gross margin breakeven) plus ~₹50/hour to cover customer support, marketing, team, and training costs.

Service professionals can utilize a maximum of 140-150 hours/month currently; target net earnings for supply attractiveness are ₹20,000-22,000/month, compared to offline gig worker earnings of ₹15,000-17,000/month.
Required pricing for full cost coverage is ~₹200/hour, against offline competing subscription pricing of ₹80-100/hour (up to ₹120/hour).
Competitors reportedly believe steady-state AOV will remain low; management notes evidence of pricing reaching target levels in less competitive micro-markets, though growth/penetration is impacted.
Unclear how long pricing correction will take — modeled as worst case up to 5 years given sustained competitive intensity.

Frequency assumption of 3 transactions/month per household used in TAM base case; a bull-case scenario assumes 30-40 uses/month is unlikely to scale broadly since that requires the category to shift from 'back-up' to 'main' service, which has not been evidenced at scale; only a non-large sub-segment (bachelors/young users) show 8-10 uses/month.
Future cohorts typically behave no better than early cohorts in Urban Company's marketplace-building experience, tempering frequency assumptions.

subsections.label: Competitive and consolidation dynamics
points: Category evolution and competitive intensity still early for consolidation to play out.
Management expects capital markets (especially private) to eventually focus beyond narrative to actual business health, size of prize.
Company intends to sustain pressure on private competitors, retain leadership, and increase market share to be the eventual winner.
Management views this market, like most home services, as winner-take-all, where trust compounds to the number one player; does not believe the market can support multiple large winners.
Reiterated stance from prior call: 'playing to win… not playing to look elegant… don't want to give an inch away.'

subsections.label: Competition in Beauty
points: Competition in the Beauty vertical is fairly high; management views competition as healthy, keeping the company focused on winning via its cheaper/faster/better proposition.

subsections.label: AI adoption
points: Company pushing to become an AI-native company; still early in fully leveraging AI benefits across the business.
AI-led supply-side and customer-side support; AI used in supply-side onboarding, training, quality control/audits across millions of jobs via proof-of-work audits, and fraud detection/control.
More than 90-95% of code is now written by AI, generating leverage in engineering costs and headcount.
Marketing team leveraging AI end-to-end (creative creation, campaign deployment, optimization, learning/redeployment); Finance and HR teams also using AI end-to-end.
AI benefits have started showing up in margins but there is a long way to go; AI also viewed as a lever to improve marketplace health and quality of service, not just cost/efficiency.

subsections.label: Capital allocation framework
points: India Consumer Services expected to remain profitable and cash generating; company will remain disciplined, maximizing growth with sustainable, steady margin improvement rather than squeezing margins overnight.

International (UAE, Singapore - wholly owned subsidiaries) expected to remain profitable; company wants to maximize growth given tremendous market runway rather than maximize profits in the short term.
Saudi JV growing exceptionally well; company now has line of sight of profitability in coming quarters.
Native has line of sight of profitability over next few quarters; incremental capital needed until cash generation begins expected to be not very substantial.
InstaHelp is the primary area of ongoing investment; company evaluating quarter-on-quarter the right level of investment as views on market size and competitive intensity evolve.

When consolidated adjusted EBITDA breakeven is reached (expected latest in next ~18 months), management plans to step back and optimize capital allocation framework to decide where to deploy balance sheet capital to grow faster.
No plans to enter new international markets; focus remains on India and deepening penetration domestically.

subsections.label: International market focus rationale
points: Management bandwidth cited as primary reason for not entering new geographies — full focus needed on India plus UAE, Singapore, and Saudi JV given healthy growth (76% YoY NTV, 58% ex-currency) and large opportunity size.

Entering and winning in a new market requires more than execution — customized playbooks, timing and luck; cited mixed past experience internationally (success in UAE/Singapore vs. earlier launches in Australia and US pre-COVID/around COVID that did not have the same favorable conditions).
Company concluded existing markets (India, UAE, Singapore, Saudi JV) are large enough to warrant full management focus for the next few years; may reconsider new market entry in future years.

subsections.label: Native category strategy
points: Native to remain focused on 2 categories (water purifiers, smart door locks) for now; may add at most 1 more category over next 5 years but does not intend to proliferate.

Native not intended to become a broad consumer durables company; focused on serving Urban Company's existing user base (9.3 million annual transacting users) with premium, synergistic products extending the platform from services to a 'home platform of services and solutions.'

subsections.label: Base effects on growth
points: 29% YoY India Consumer Services growth partly aided by a muted base in the same quarter last year due to unseasonal rains and monsoons.

subsections.label: Competitive intensity in InstaHelp
points: Competitors reportedly believe AOV will remain structurally low, contrary to Urban Company's ₹300/hour breakeven assumption.

All 3 market players' current investment is going largely into subsidizing repeat-user orders rather than expanding household coverage/TAM, a dynamic Urban Company admits participating in given competitive pressure.
Uncertain timeline for pricing correction — modeled conservatively as up to 5 years given sustained competitive intensity.

InstaHelp margin profile expected to remain structurally lower than core India Consumer Services — likely low single-digit at best, with no intention of making money from the business over the next 5 years.

subsections.label: InstaHelp category evolution risk
points: Uncertain whether frequency (currently observed at 30-40 uses/month in compressed-AOV cohorts) will sustain once pricing corrects; historical marketplace-building experience suggests future cohorts often behave no better than (and often worse than) early cohorts.

subsections.label: Reiterated targets
points: Company continues to retain guidance of consolidated adjusted EBITDA breakeven by Q3 FY28, and ₹1,000 crores in adjusted EBITDA by FY31.
India Consumer Services long-term guidance of 9-10% adjusted EBITDA margin as % of NTV reiterated; management not in a rush to hit it, prioritizing growth first, margin discipline second.
Once the 9-10% margin stage is reached, company will have optionality to decide whether to push margins further or reinvest for faster growth.

InstaHelp assumed to break even by FY31 at a low single-digit margin at best; management states no intention of making money from InstaHelp over the next 5 years, and would be 'happy' if it simply breaks even.
Management believes consolidated adjusted EBITDA breakeven could occur 'latest in the next 18 months or so,' at which point capital allocation framework will be revisited.
No plans to enter new international geographies for the foreseeable future; focus remains on India, UAE, Singapore, and the Saudi JV.
Native expected to reach profitability ('line of sight') over the next few quarters, with limited incremental capital required until then.

key_takeaways: On a consolidated basis, Q1 NTV grew 42% year-on-year to reach ₹1,465 crore, and revenue grew 44% year-on-year to reach ₹528 crore. Total orders reached 13.2 million, which is up 79% year-on-year.

India Consumer Services, excluding InstaHelp, grew 29% in NTV year-on-year to reach ₹1,056 crores - the first time it crossed 1,000 crores of NTV in a quarter... Adjusted EBITDA margin was 6.9% of NTV, up from 5.2% the same period last year.

Our International business is now scaling fast and profitably and will become the second core profit engine of Urban Company in the coming time. NTV grew 76% to reach ₹237 crore. Both UAE and Singapore delivered profitable growth.

Native continues to demonstrate strong growth with improving margins. NTV grew 51% year-on-year to reach ₹119 crores, and net revenue grew 60% year-on-year to reach ₹95 crores. Adjusted EBITDA loss narrowed to (7.3)% of NTV from (11.4)% a year back.

InstaHelp is our largest investment today... We delivered 3.82 million orders, up 43% quarter-on-quarter. The Adjusted EBITDA loss was ₹(132) crores. Loss per order improved from ₹(447) in Q4 to ₹(346) in this quarter... the addressable market in the top 15 cities ranges anywhere from ₹7,000 to ₹12,000 crores NTV annually.

Consolidated P&L Adjusted EBITDA loss stood at ₹(65) crores. But this was almost entirely driven by InstaHelp's loss of ₹(132) crores. Excluding InstaHelp, the rest of our operations delivered an adjusted EBITDA profit of ₹67 crores, which is more than 100% growth from the same period last year; specifically about 116%.
We ended the quarter with ₹2,019 crores in cash and treasury investments on our balance sheet which is only about ₹2 crores lower than where we ended the last quarter.
We continue to retain our guidance of consolidated and Adjusted EBITDA breakeven by Q3 FY28, and ₹1,000 crores in adjusted EBITDA by FY31.
pressing_questions: At what point in time, we can make a bold statement that the growth trajectory has shifted north side, from India Consumer Services NTV growth perspective because this flywheel is suddenly now giving you results that we have been waiting for some time.

Just trying to understand why the segment [InstaHelp] should deserve this much of time and attention and bandwidth of the management... Do they [competitors] get any right to win in the core categories just because they are present in this segment?

By 3QFY28, you would get too close to break-even at the consol Adjusted EBITDA level... would that be a time when you would start thinking about allocating more capital to new segments... or new geographies in International business?
Given just your track record in the three markets where you operate in... why should you not be able to export that same model to a few other markets and expand it?

Given that you have revisited your TAM assumptions this time around, and are also calling out explicitly that margins here [InstaHelp] would be structurally lower than the core businesses at least now, do we have enough comfort and confidence that this segment can be profitable at all?

Both your competitors in this space are actually of the view that AOV of the segment is not going to increase, and it might remain low. What gives you comfort that the steady-state AOV could eventually be at ₹300?

We do see that often existence of multiple players offering similar services and also incurring cash burn, it results in some eventual consolidation. Are you seeing any signs of this happening in the InstaHelp type vertical anytime soon?

quarters.summary: Q4 FY26 was described as a strong close to Urban Company's first year as a listed company: consolidated NTV grew 42% YoY to ₹1,148 Cr and revenue grew 43% to ₹426 Cr, with over 10 million orders in a single quarter for the first time. Management reiterated guardrail targets of consolidated adjusted EBITDA breakeven by Q3 FY28 and ₹1,000 Cr adjusted EBITDA by FY31, while investing aggressively in InstaHelp to build market leadership; core India Consumer Services, International and Native businesses are all on improving profitability trajectories.
