subsections.label: Core is accelerating with structurally improving margins
points: India Consumer Services excluding InstaHelp grew 26% in Q4 — the fastest pace in 11 quarters.
Margin expansion attributed to structural improvement, not one-off factors, with the business having been loss-making as recently as FY24.

Management explained that acceleration is driven by hitting inflection points in densification across categories and micro-markets, producing a 'faster, cheaper, better' flywheel: higher service-professional utilization → higher earnings → lower cost to serve → better value for customers → higher retention and quality.
UC Instant rollout (30–60 minute service) is in early innings and is expected to be a further growth driver as it scales across the marketplace.

Growth acceleration has been broad-based across cities in the last few months; management believes the real constraint was building high-quality supply, not demand — 'we've left demand on the table' across cities and categories.

Margin should be assessed year-on-year, not quarter-on-quarter, due to seasonality: Q1 and Q3 are structurally stronger than Q2 and Q4 because marketing/supply ramp-up occurs in preceding quarters and Q4 includes annual appraisals.
Long-term aspiration is for India Consumer Services to reach ~10% adjusted EBITDA as % of NTV over a longer period, with margin expansion occurring every year (pace varying).

subsections.label: International — scaling and profitable
points: UAE and Singapore NTV growth strong despite some demand headwind in UAE in March from Middle East conflict escalation.
International business turned adjusted EBITDA positive for FY26 as a whole and is now 4x its scale of four years ago.

Middle East demand is now 'more or less back to square one' — recovery essentially complete; the earlier dip in UC's business was more resilient than most competitors, evident in year-on-year growth staying healthy through the disruption.
UAE competitor JustLife has been in the market roughly as long as UC; competition described as healthy, with both players growing well and mutual learning between them.
Singapore has many smaller, non-major competitors; market described as very exciting and growing profitably.
Saudi Arabia JV (revenue not recognized) is shaping up well with growth in the right direction and improving margins; management now sees a clear line of sight to profitability there.

Subscription models (e.g., recurring deep cleaning) in UAE and Singapore are locking in households into higher-frequency use and accelerating growth; some learnings being applied to India via cleaning subscriptions and bundling programs, and potentially to InstaHelp over time.

subsections.label: Native — path to profitability
points: Growth driven by existing two product lines (water purifiers and smart electronic door locks); no timeline given for reaching a revenue quadrupling target, but these two categories are expected to be meaningful contributors.
Installed base growth also drives recurring service revenue in addition to product sales; early retention signals are healthy and above industry averages.
Some incremental new products may contribute revenue but the large part of growth is expected from existing categories.
Elevated losses partly reflect R&D spend on new products; core Native business is described as already approaching near-breakeven.
Management is confident of reaching breakeven in 'the next few quarters' despite continued new product launches, though no precise timeline given.

subsections.label: InstaHelp — investment phase
points: A business that didn't exist at start of FY26 delivered strong order volumes and NTV in Q4; loss reflects cost of building the market — consumer acquisition, network density subsidies, supply onboarding.
Management declined to share further detail beyond the shareholder letter, citing competitive dynamics.
Losses expected to remain elevated for the foreseeable future; management wouldn't commit to a specific number of quarters, citing the need for 'manoeuvrability' within the guardrail targets.
AOV in InstaHelp will move up and down quarter to quarter as a mix of tactics and strategy; management is focused on loss per order trending down over time.

Elevated marketing spend this quarter (including around the Cricket World Cup) to acquire users and build the brand was the primary driver of the swing in loss per order; contribution loss per order (CM-level) actually improved / moved positively — the loss per order swing was driven by fixed marketing cost, not contribution margin deterioration.
Both existing Urban Company consumer cohorts and entirely new, first-time customers are adopting InstaHelp — it is helping expand the total addressable customer base.

InstaHelp density requirements are far more granular/hyperlocal than the core business or other consumer internet businesses, which may constrain achievable market size, though the exact TAM implication is uncertain.
Company strategically believes market structure could tend toward a winner-take-all outcome given this is a 'business of trust,' similar to the core; intends to replicate its core market leadership.
Payment structure to professionals is per-hour based but dynamic, varying by professional quality, micro-market, time of day/week; company continually experiments with variable/fixed structural mix.
No current disclosure on the cross-utilization ratio/proportion between core and InstaHelp customer cohorts.

subsections.label: Densification vs expansion strategy
points: Priority remains on densification and deeper penetration of existing micro-markets over proliferation into new ones; expansion will continue but in a 'calibrated' fashion.
Full coverage of top cities may not happen even over a long period because some parts of cities lack adequate density to achieve effective cost-to-serve.
Prioritized micro-markets are those where densification can eventually drive them to breakeven and profitability, even if loss-making in the interim.
InstaHelp requires far more granular/hyperlocal density than even quick commerce, making the prioritization playbook even more critical.

International expansion strategy is deliberately limited: company has fully owned subsidiaries in UAE and Singapore, and a JV in Saudi Arabia (KSA); no plans to launch additional international markets for the foreseeable future, prioritizing India and these existing markets until medium-term guidance targets are achieved.

key_figures.label: Company's share of total addressable market
Partner support queries handled via AI

subsections.label: Competitive positioning — Core
points: Management does not spend significant time tracking competition in India Core, viewing competition as highly distributed across categories and micro-markets.

Growth attributed mainly to internal factors (faster/cheaper/better flywheel) rather than competitive dynamics; company felt supply-constrained for most of the quarter, implying demand was left unmet.
AOV sensitivity in the core business is described as low and manageable, versus very high sensitivity in InstaHelp.

subsections.label: Competitive positioning — InstaHelp
points: Management characterizes current competitive intensity and irrationality in InstaHelp as 'pretty manageable' and 'nothing new,' drawing on ~12 years of experience through multiple competitive cycles.
Company explicitly states it is 'optimizing to win' and market share over 'on-paper elegance,' and is willing to be irrational if required to defend market position.

Company is not planning to expand into adjacent services (e.g., cooks, drivers, elderly care) despite competitors experimenting there; strategic focus remains on densifying and winning core InstaHelp segments given limited resources.

Belief that any player executing well on quality, safety and trust can gain acceptance; competition seen as healthy for keeping company focused and could help grow the overall market pie rather than just splitting a smaller one.

Historically, competition has been limited to one or two verticals rather than the full horizontal category skew that UC operates across (60+ categories); management sees UC's ability to execute across many categories/micro-markets as a differentiator.

subsections.label: AI-enabled strategy
points: AI layer embedded in everyday operations across the core platform.
Quality: AI used extensively in proof-of-work, auditing 100% of images shared during jobs, and running diagnostics in repair/appliance/handyman categories.
Customer & partner support: AI-driven support handling helps deliver lower cost to serve; AI also used to generate top-of-funnel partner referrals from past job completions.
Demand forecasting has become simpler and more accurate with AI.
Early revenue-generation use cases: AI-driven reminders for Native filter replacement; AI-based visualization of interior spaces for the Revamp offering to simplify decision-making.
Engineering: majority of code now shipped via GenAI, a major shift from prior periods; AI also used for fraud detection.

subsections.label: Flagged headwinds
points: UAE saw a demand headwind in March 2026 from escalation of the Middle East conflict, though the business has since returned to near-full recovery.
Elevated and prolonged InstaHelp losses are expected as the company builds market leadership; no fixed timeline for improvement given.
Competitive intensity/irrationality in InstaHelp flagged by an analyst as a risk given recent competitor fundraising, though management characterizes current intensity as manageable.

Temporary workforce/supply displacement risk was raised around elections; management noted some demand loss was seen in the recent month but described it as a routine, anticipated BAU issue for which the company had prepped by onboarding more professionals in advance.
AOV in InstaHelp continues to trend lower, raising analyst concern about difficulty of future AOV recovery and its impact on steady-state margin economics.
Granular/hyperlocal density requirement in InstaHelp could structurally constrain the addressable market size relative to other consumer internet models.

key_figures.label: India Consumer Services long-term adjusted EBITDA margin target

subsections.label: Guardrails and management commitments
points: Company retains its target of consolidated adjusted EBITDA breakeven by Q3 FY28 and ₹1,000 Cr adjusted EBITDA by FY31, framed as guardrails for management flexibility on InstaHelp investment.
Native business breakeven expected 'in the next few quarters,' though no precise timeline was given.
India Consumer Services margin trajectory expected to continue expanding annually, at varying pace, toward an eventual ~10% adjusted EBITDA margin (% of NTV) over the longer term.
No incremental international market launches planned until medium-term guidance targets are achieved.
Management believes execution in the core business provides enough buffer/cushion to sustain the breakeven target even if the external environment deteriorates or InstaHelp investment needs increase.

guidance_ledger.statement: We retain our target of consolidated adjusted EBITDA breakeven by Q3 FY28
₹1,000 crores by FY31

guidance_ledger.metric: India Consumer Services adjusted EBITDA margin (% of NTV)
guidance_ledger.statement: eventually this business should get to about 10% adjusted EBITDA as a percentage of NTV, over a longer period of time
We are fairly confident on the trajectory from here on to achieve break-even... it should happen in the next few quarters
Target of quadrupling net revenue of this business, largely from water purifiers and smart electronic door locks; no timeline given deliberately
Losses remaining elevated for the foreseeable future; loss per order should keep coming down and over time losses come down, but timeline to be calibrated
We are clear we're not launching any other international markets... focused in India and these two markets for now, and for the foreseeable future

risk_register.risk: Middle East conflict escalation impacting UAE demand
risk_register.note: Demand headwind seen in UAE in March 2026 from Middle East conflict escalation; business now 'more or less back to square one,' near-full recovery.

risk_register.risk: Elevated and prolonged InstaHelp losses
risk_register.note: ₹119 Cr adjusted EBITDA loss in Q4FY26 reflects cost of building the market (acquisition, subsidies, supply onboarding); no fixed timeline to reduce given, management wants 'manoeuvrability.'

risk_register.risk: Competitive irrationality in InstaHelp
risk_register.note: Analyst flagged competitor fundraising and irrational competitive intensity; management calls current intensity 'pretty manageable' and says it will match irrationality if needed to defend share.

risk_register.risk: Election-related temporary supply/workforce displacement
risk_register.note: Some demand loss seen in the recent month, but management had prepped by onboarding more professionals in advance; described as a routine BAU issue, nothing unusual.

risk_register.risk: Declining InstaHelp AOV
risk_register.note: Analyst raised concern that continually lower AOV could make recovery harder and push out steady-state margin targets; management says AOV will move up and down quarter to quarter.

risk_register.risk: Hyperlocal density constraint on InstaHelp TAM
risk_register.note: InstaHelp requires far more granular/hyperlocal density than core or other consumer internet businesses, which may constrain the addressable market; exact impact unknown.

themes.label: Core margin expansion
themes.note: India Consumer Services (ex-InstaHelp) adjusted EBITDA margin expanded from 1.6% to 3.3% of NTV in Q4, and from 3.3% to 4.1% for FY26, on a densification-driven 'faster, cheaper, better' flywheel.

themes.label: InstaHelp investment phase
themes.note: InstaHelp posted ₹119 Cr adjusted EBITDA loss in Q4 driven by elevated marketing spend and market-building costs, with management prioritizing market leadership over near-term profitability.

themes.label: International profitability and scale-up
themes.note: UAE and Singapore NTV grew 84% in Q4 and the international business turned adjusted EBITDA positive for FY26, now 4x its scale of four years ago, with UAE demand largely recovered from a March dip.

themes.label: Native path to breakeven
themes.note: Native losses narrowed from -14.7% to -9.9% of NTV YoY in Q4, with management expressing confidence in breakeven within the next few quarters despite continued R&D-driven new product investment.

themes.label: Competitive intensity in InstaHelp
themes.note: Management describes current InstaHelp competitive irrationality as manageable and states it will match irrational competitive behavior to defend market share and leadership.

themes.label: Densification over geographic expansion
themes.note: Strategic priority remains deepening supply/demand density in existing micro-markets rather than proliferating into new cities or international markets.

themes.label: AI adoption across operations
themes.note: AI is embedded in quality checks (100% image audits), partner support (55% of queries), demand forecasting, early revenue use-cases, and code generation (>90% of code shipped via GenAI).

key_takeaways: Q4 was a strong close to what I believe was a defining year for Urban Company — our first as a listed company.
We delivered our highest consolidated NTV growth in 15 quarters, crossed 10 million orders in a single quarter for the first time, and meaningfully improved the profitability of our core businesses.
One — the core is accelerating, with structurally improving margins.
Two — International is scaling rapidly, and now profitable.
Three — Native is on a clear path to profitability.
Four — InstaHelp is our most significant investment today, and we're leaning in.
We retain our target of consolidated adjusted EBITDA breakeven by Q3 FY28, and ₹1,000 crores by FY31.
Given the competitive dynamics in this space, we've shared everything we're able to on InstaHelp in the shareholder letter. We won't be going beyond that on this call.
pressing_questions: When you say losses remaining elevated for the foreseeable future, are you expecting potential losses to also increase from these levels? And when you say elevated for a prolonged period of time, are we talking about four quarters, eight quarters, longer than that?
Average order value continues to get lower — would it be more difficult to recover AOV if they keep getting lower, taking you further away from steady-state margin expectations in InstaHelp?
Any guardrails you want to indicate on loss-per-order given irrational competition — a threshold beyond which it would be okay to let go of market share?
What would be a reasonable range for steady-state unit economics or EBITDA margin in the medium term for InstaHelp, given it's a relatively new business not seen in most other countries?
Considering InstaHelp requires hyper-densification which could constrain TAM, and competitors are attacking irrationally, what criteria would trigger paring back investment versus doubling down?
Is winning in InstaHelp in India more important than pursuing international opportunities beyond UAE and Singapore, where competition may be more limited?

ROSSARI.about: Rossari Biotech was started in 2003. They are among the largest manufacturers of textile specialty chemicals in India.[1]

quarters.summary: Rossari delivered its highest ever quarterly revenue (Rs. 697.2 crore, +28% YoY) and EBITDA (Rs. 80.6 crore, +18.7% YoY) in Q1 FY27, driven by HPPC, TSC and AHN growth of ~28% YoY each and export growth of 21% YoY, though EBITDA margin at 11.6% remained below normalized potential due to institutional/consumer business drag, product mix and raw material/freight volatility. Management continues to target ~15% consolidated FY27 revenue growth, a steady-state EBITDA margin of ~15% over 2 years, gradual EO availability improvement by December, continued Thailand and Saudi Arabia expansion, and portfolio rationalization (B2C exit, non-core asset monetization) to strengthen margins and returns.

key_figures.label: Base business margin range (shorn of B2C)
EBITDA margin release from exiting B2C
Expected finance cost run-rate going forward
One-off phenol raw material cost hit
Historical annual revenue base (6 years ago)

subsections.label: Margin drivers
points: EBITDA margin of 11.6% (vs 12.5% YoY) reflects impact of institutional and consumer business, product mix, and cost environment.
Core B2B business (excluding institutional & consumer) delivered ~14% EBITDA margin on ~13% EBITDA growth YoY (Core B2B EBITDA of Rs. 85 crore), reflecting underlying strength of core portfolio.
Losses in institutional/B2C verticals moderated due to focus on improving product mix, operational efficiency, and cost discipline, even as growth in these verticals remained flat YoY.
Raw material price volatility and freight cost spikes (linked to insurance costs, vessel unavailability, and geopolitical disruption) caused margin loss despite ability to pass on RM price hikes.

One raw material (phenol) caused a ~Rs. 5 crore hit in the quarter due to delayed China shipments forcing high-price market purchases; management believes this was a one-off and pricing has normalized.
A large anticipatory RM purchase block (in anticipation of further price rises) also impacted the quarter negatively when the market moved the other way.
Institutional margin (EBITDA per kg metric preferred) impacted by RM/freight volatility and non-operative/seeding costs from expansion into new geographies like Saudi Arabia.
Company reiterated 11.6% margin level as the expected base level going forward, not expected to decline further.
Target of steady-state ~15% EBITDA margin (consolidated level) over next 2 years, contingent on portfolio recalibration, product mix improvement, and utilization stabilization.
Base business (shorn of B2C) already runs at 14-15% margin range.

subsections.label: Capital allocation & balance sheet
points: Net debt reduced to Rs. 248 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs. 280 crore in March (FY26), aided by office monetizations; balance sheet remains healthy with strong liquidity and comfortable leverage.
Focus on improving working-capital efficiency, strengthening cash generation, and maintaining capital allocation discipline.

Completed sale of Andheri office during the quarter for Rs. 10.5 crore proceeds, following Kanjurmarg office sale of Rs. 24 crore in Q4 FY26, as part of ongoing monetization of non-core/underutilized assets; will continue evaluating further such monetization opportunities in a calibrated manner.

Only profit element from office sales is recognized in other income (Rs. 3.2 crore in Q1 FY27); Andheri office was held in Unitop's name and was revalued 5 years back during consolidation, resulting in lower recognized profit.

Interest expense of Rs. 11 crore in Q1 FY27 increased YoY because term loans related to CAPEX were previously capitalized (including part of last year and the year before); as CAPEX projects have come on stream and started delivering, interest costs are now flowing through the P&L; expected finance cost run-rate going forward is Rs. 9-10 crore.
Debt attributable to B2C/institutional business is ~Rs. 50 crore.

India CAPEX has been slowed down to calibrated spending, focused only on new products/molecules in R&D (including pharma molecules and aroma chemicals); no large new spends planned this year or next, with focus instead on utilizing existing capacity investments.
KSA (Saudi Arabia) spending so far limited to very initial operational and exploratory/pre-operational expenses.
Company has grown from an annual revenue base of ~Rs. 600 crore about 6 years ago to a current quarterly revenue scale of ~Rs. 700 crore.

key_figures.label: HPPC, TSC, AHN segment growth YoY

subsections.label: HPPC segment
points: HPPC, TSC, AHN segment grew ~28% YoY in Q1 FY27.
Continued broadening presence across higher value applications: personal care, pharmaceutical applications, agrochemicals, and performance chemicals.
Improving utilization of ethoxylation capacities plus growing new product pipeline provides foundation to scale the business further.
HPPC crossed Rs. 550 crore quarterly revenue milestone, reflecting increasing scale and depth across key applications and end-user industries.
Pharma business revenue was over Rs. 50 crore in FY26; company targets Rs. 70-75 crore this year (alternate management estimate cited a lower Rs. 30-50 crore potential for FY27).

subsections.label: Textile Specialty Chemicals (TSC)
points: Launched a dedicated Fibre Chemicals Division during the quarter, expanding capabilities across the fibre-to-fibre value chain.

Supported by application-driven R&D platform, formulation expertise, and manufacturing capabilities, enhancing ability to offer integrated value-added solutions and expand addressable market within textile industry.
Non-EO esters, NMMO, NMM, and NFM products have gained traction and driven volume growth within textile applications.

subsections.label: Animal Health & Nutrition (AHN)
points: New products such as trace minerals, vitamin premixes, and enzyme premixes have been implemented, driving growth despite EO constraints.
Vitamin premix plant has become operational and started contributing to top line.

subsections.label: Institutional & B2C business
points: Domestic institutional and consumer business continued to operate in a relatively subdued environment, weighing on overall profitability.

Company plans to exit the B2C (consumer) portion of the business but will retain the institutional cleaning products business, which is described as the more profitable core cleaning chemicals business.
Institutional business alone carries higher debt due to the tagged-along consumer business.
Growth in institutional/B2C verticals remained flat YoY, but losses have moderated due to product mix improvement, operational efficiency, and cost discipline.
Institutional business margin was 16% in FY26, moderating to a range of 13.6-15.8% in Q1 FY27.

subsections.label: New product contribution
points: Products innovated in the last 2-3 years — NMMO, MDEA, spray-cooled powders, biosurfactants, fibre finishes, and the vitamin premix plant — have started contributing meaningfully to the top line, with some having already shown sales in Q4 of the prior year.
Investments in new capacities/products are expected to take about 2-3 years for full utilization and revenue ramp-up.

subsections.label: Pricing vs volume growth
points: Of the overall YoY growth, volume grew about 10%, with the rest of the growth driven by higher pricing (mostly RM pass-through).

subsections.label: Capacity utilization & ramp-up
points: Improving utilization of ethoxylation capacities is supporting HPPC business scale-up.
Utilization levels across manufacturing capacities improved during the quarter, contributing to revenue and EBITDA growth.
Priority is to drive assets toward optimal utilization, improve product mix, and generate stronger operating leverage from investments made over the past few years.

EO capacity is now practically 100% utilized except for a small addition in batch reactors; further growth expected from non-batch continuous ethoxylation (MDEA plant, a major investment) ramping up over the next 12 months, which should yield higher margins.
Company is finding formulations with lower EO and higher non-EO components (e.g., 2-mole lauryl alcohol ethoxylate) to work around EO supply constraints and utilize capacity.

subsections.label: R&D centre
points: New R&D centre commissioned in the previous quarter is progressively ramping up, integrating research, product development, and application capabilities on a single platform.

Facility is strengthening cross-team collaboration, accelerating new product development, and supporting faster scale-up and commercialization of differentiated technologies across end-user industries.

subsections.label: Thailand blending plant
points: Greenfield blending plant established in Thailand during the quarter to strengthen presence in Southeast Asia; contributed Rs. 2-3 crore to revenue in Q1 FY27.

Facility enhances ability to offer customized formulations, respond faster to local market requirements, and improve supply chain efficiency, and provides platform to progressively expand product offerings across the region.
It is a small formulation unit aimed at getting closer to Southeast Asian customers; currently working only on textile products, with plans to add AHN and HPPC molecules longer-term.
Investment in the plant is only Rs. 10-15 crore; management cautions not to expect too much from this small facility.

subsections.label: Saudi Arabia (KSA) greenfield initiative
points: Progress being made on proposed initiative in Saudi Arabia, supported by access to globally competitive raw materials and a well-developed petrochemical ecosystem.
Considered an important strategic step to strengthen long-term footprint, enhance supply-side competitiveness, and create a scalable platform for regional and global markets.
Still at survey stage, formalizing raw material/feedstock allocations and land allocations; nothing finalized yet — will announce once concluded.
Project will involve a mix of both EO and non-EO products, chosen based on higher margin/realization potential.
Gestation period expected to be about 1.5 years from announcement to first kilo of production.
Discussions ongoing with partners, suppliers, project consultants, and the KSA ministry, which is keen on partnership for setting up downstream products.
Conviction in long-term potential remains intact despite prevailing geopolitical uncertainty.

key_figures.label: Export growth vs Q1 last year (alternate figure)

subsections.label: International business momentum
points: Exports grew 21% YoY (also cited as 20-21%) to ~Rs. 160 crore, representing 23-24% of total revenue in Q1 FY27, supported by increasing wallet share with strategic partners, addition of new customers, and wider acceptance of specialty solutions across key overseas markets.
Company remains focused on deepening presence in existing geographies while selectively expanding into markets with attractive long-term potential.
No specific export percentage target is set, but management aims to keep growing export business alongside domestic growth, generally maintaining the export share between 23-25% of total revenue.

subsections.label: Portfolio rationalization
points: Several measures already initiated to address margins below normalized potential: monetization of non-core assets, rationalization of lower margin businesses, improvement in product mix, and tighter cost discipline.

Company evaluating rationalization of select non-core businesses and assets to simplify the portfolio, redeploy capital and management bandwidth toward higher-return opportunities, and improve overall quality of earnings.
Plan to exit the B2C (consumer) business specifically, while retaining the institutional cleaning products business (core cleaning chemicals), which is more profitable.

Investment in B2C/institutional business shares core assets (e.g., Silvassa plant) with other businesses; no separate investment identified for this vertical, but debt attributable to it is ~Rs. 50 crore.
Exiting B2C is expected to release at least 2-3% EBITDA margin improvement, since base business (shorn of B2C) already runs at 14-15%.

subsections.label: Long-term growth ambition
points: Company continues to invest in market presence (exhibitions, customer visits, customer interactions) as it targets to more than double Rossari's scale over the next four years; management stated it will not stop seeding these initiatives merely to show a slightly higher EBITDA margin in the near term.

key_figures.label: Gestation period for Saudi Arabia project post-announcement

subsections.label: Geopolitical and freight volatility
points: Freight prices have risen sharply due to renewed war/geopolitical tensions after appearing to stabilize; contracts signed earlier had to absorb the price increase, and new orders taken in the last month were priced considering the higher freight.
Insurance costs and unavailability of vessels linked to geopolitical tension are causing margin loss despite ability to pass on raw material price increases.
Uncertainty from war and geopolitics is making it difficult to predict growth and financial outcomes even on a quarterly basis.

subsections.label: Raw material volatility
points: Significant RM price volatility, e.g., phenol delayed shipments from China forced market purchases at high prices, costing ~Rs. 5 crore in the quarter.
A large anticipatory purchase block of an RM (expecting price rises) backfired when the market moved the other way, further impacting margins in the quarter.

Company differentiates itself from single-molecule commodity chemical makers (e.g., soda ash, acetic acid) who benefited from inventory gains/PPP spreads in Q1; as a diversified specialty chemicals player, Rossari's broader RM basket bore the brunt of volatility instead.

subsections.label: EO availability constraint
points: EO (ethylene oxide) availability remains a challenge; sole domestic supplier controls pricing based on global EO pricing, limiting negotiation ability, though supplier is described as reputed and fair.
New EO capacity expected to become available only by end of this calendar year (hopefully before December).

subsections.label: Revenue growth outlook
points: Despite Q1 FY27 growth of 28% (well above prior 15% FY27 guidance), management reiterated it would stick to the ~15% annualized top-line growth estimate shared in the last call, citing global uncertainty making quarterly prediction difficult.
Company remains confident and bullish on prospects overall despite inability to precisely quantify growth.

subsections.label: Margin outlook
points: 11.6% margin level in Q1 FY27 expected to be the base level going forward (not expected to decline further).
As capacity utilization improves over next few quarters/years and low-margin businesses are exited, relative margin improvement is expected.
New areas like pharma and aroma chemicals expected to aid EBITDA margin improvement.
Target of steady-state ~15% consolidated EBITDA margin achievable in 2 years once recalibration steps materialize.
For at least the next couple of quarters, margins will remain under pressure from pricing and raw material volatility.

subsections.label: EO availability and FY28 outlook
points: Expecting more EO availability by end of this calendar year (hopefully before December), which should support growth from capacities installed even in non-EO-requiring areas ramping up this financial year.
FY28 expected to be a better year than FY27 given a full year of additional EO availability.

subsections.label: CAPEX outlook
points: India CAPEX has been slowed to calibrated spending, limited to new products/molecules under R&D (pharma, aroma chemicals); no large new spends planned this year or next.
Focus instead is on ensuring existing capacity investments are well utilized.
KSA spending remains at initial operational/exploratory pre-operational stage; broader investment intent unchanged.

guidance_ledger.statement: This year I would still stick to our 15% kind of growth, something we had spoken about even in our last call, even though this quarter has been a stronger quarter for us. On an annualized basis, I think we would stick to our earlier estimates that we had shared of around 15% kind of top-line growth.
Our aim is that once we recalibrate the whole business mix, the product mix, we should have a steady state, the EBITDA margins at around 15% at least once these steps that we are taking materialize.
These level of margins (11.6%) you can expect to be the base level.
This year we should do Rs. 70 - Rs. 75 crore in pharma this year (last year more than Rs. 50 crore).
It could be a revenue potential of close to Rs. 30 crore - Rs. 50 crore for this year.

guidance_ledger.horizon: by end of calendar year 2026 / before December
guidance_ledger.statement: We are expecting more EO by the end of this year, hopefully will come before December.
FY28 should be better, hoping that the availability of EO will come on stream by the end of this calendar year and then we will have a full year next year in FY28 with additional EO.

In India currently we have slowed down on all the CAPEX spends because we are now doing very calibrated spending on new CAPEX. Only certain new products or new molecules that are in R&D... otherwise no large spend are intent this year and the next year.

We are still doing a survey and trying to formalize some raw material, feedstock allocations, and some land allocations. This is still work in progress and nothing has been finalized. As soon as we finalize something we will announce.
It should take about 1.5 years for us to start the first kilo of production once we make the announcement.
The MDEA plant... ramping up should happen in the next 12 months. We should definitely see higher margins there.
Going forward the finance cost should be at close to this Rs. 9 crore to Rs. 10 crore kind of a run rate.
We are looking at scaling up Rossari to more than double from here over the next four years.

guidance_ledger.metric: EBITDA margin improvement from B2C exit
guidance_ledger.statement: In terms of EBITDA margins if you see it will release at least 2%-3% EBITDA. Shorn of this business we are close to about 14%, in some years we are even 15% of the EBITDA margins.
We do not target any specific number... generally the percentage remains around between 23%-24%-25%.
We should do an asset turn of at least between 3-4x at peak utilization.
The target is to actually get debt free in the next 18 months, but the time will tell. Currently, the plan is to keep bringing down our debt over the next 18 months.
The CAPEX plan for this year would be I think anything between Rs. 50 crore to Rs. 75 crore; even at very peak levels, we would reach Rs. 70 crore - Rs. 75 crore number.
We should do about between Rs. 50 crore - Rs. 75 crore at its peak, but we will not reach Rs. 50 crore in this year itself.

In FY27, we should look at breakeven or even profitability, along with the divestment of some lower-margin businesses or those that contributed to EBITDA losses. We feel FY27 should be a very good year for the institutional business.
The plan is we would like it to happen in 2027, but it could take more than a year, 2 years.

We are expecting the new EO capacities at Reliance to also come in the later part of this year probably by Q3; Reliance will release more EO from December when their partial expansion is done, with more coming up next December.
Thailand is going to now start contributing meaningfully from this year, probably from quarter 2 onwards we should see meaningful ramp-up in the Thailand facility.
We see revenues coming from the premix starting this quarter, and a full-scale premix facility capacity enhancement in the next year.

guidance_ledger.metric: Growth ramp-up in high-value segments (pharma, oil & gas etc.)
guidance_ledger.statement: The expectation is that ramp-up will happen over the next 2-3 years while current segments of core agro, textile and AHN keep seeing latent growth happening parallelly.
We believe these efforts are putting the right building blocks in place to significantly accelerate growth over the next 2 to 3 years.

risk_register.risk: Geopolitical uncertainty and war-related disruption impacting freight and business predictability
risk_register.note: Freight prices shot up again due to renewed war/geopolitical tensions after earlier stabilization; new orders priced considering higher freight; management says it is very difficult to predict outcomes given war/geopolitical developments.

risk_register.risk: Freight cost volatility (insurance costs, vessel unavailability)
risk_register.note: Freight became a major component of margin loss due to insurance costs and unavailability of vessels.

risk_register.risk: Raw material price volatility
risk_register.note: Company can pass on RM price increases but up-and-down volatility creates buyer uncertainty; phenol shipment delays from China caused a ~Rs. 5 crore hit in the quarter from having to buy at high market prices; believed to be a one-off, now normalized.

risk_register.risk: EO (ethylene oxide) supply constraint
risk_register.note: Sole domestic EO supplier controls pricing based on global EO pricing with no room to negotiate; new EO capacity not expected until end of calendar year.

risk_register.risk: Institutional/consumer (B2C) business drag on profitability
risk_register.note: Domestic institutional and consumer business continued in a subdued environment, weighing on overall profitability; growth flat YoY though losses moderating.

risk_register.risk: Anticipatory raw material purchase mismatch
risk_register.note: A large anticipatory RM purchase block made in expectation of further price rises backfired when market moved the other way, impacting the quarter.

risk_register.risk: KSA project uncertainty amid West Asia crisis
risk_register.note: Despite prevailing geographical/geopolitical uncertainty, company's conviction in long-term potential of Saudi Arabia initiative remains intact; project still in survey/formalization stage.

risk_register.risk: Non-operative/seeding costs from new geography expansion
risk_register.note: Pre-operative expenses from Saudi Arabian venture and other new geography seeding put pressure on margins.

risk_register.risk: Middle East geopolitical conflict / uncertainty
risk_register.note: Ongoing conflict in the Middle East created uncertainty across raw material markets, supply chains and logistics during FY26 and may have impact over coming quarters; Iran war referenced by an analyst as an FY27 concern.

risk_register.risk: Domestic demand softness
risk_register.note: Domestic demand conditions remained relatively soft during certain periods of the year; institutional and B2C business performance remained subdued.

risk_register.risk: Institutional/B2C business losses
risk_register.note: Losses in institutional and B2C business continued to moderate through H2 FY26 due to focus on product mix, operational efficiency and cost discipline, though the segment continued to be a challenge overall.

risk_register.risk: Agro season weather risk (El Nino)
risk_register.note: Agro season is dependent on El Nino, which can affect the season; too early to comment, though similar worries last year did not materialize.

risk_register.risk: Textile industry pass-through resistance
risk_register.note: Some resistance encountered in passing through cost increases specifically in the textile industry, though supplies are being controlled to maintain profitable margins.

risk_register.risk: Elevated operating expenses from capacity/talent investment
risk_register.note: Expenses remained elevated during the year due to ongoing investments in capacity expansion, new business development and capability building, including significant employee cost growth.

themes.label: Margin pressure from RM inflation
themes.note: EBITDA margin fell to 11.6% from 12.5% YoY due to RM/freight volatility, phenol shipment delays costing ~Rs. 5 crore, and a mistimed anticipatory purchase block.

themes.label: Geopolitical/Middle East disruption
themes.note: Renewed war/geopolitical tensions drove sharp freight price increases and continue to create pricing/predictability uncertainty; KSA project proceeds despite West Asia crisis.

themes.label: Capacity expansion & ramp-up
themes.note: EO capacity ~100% utilized; MDEA continuous ethoxylation plant ramping up over next 12 months; new R&D centre and vitamin premix plant contributing to growth.

themes.label: CAPEX rephasing / capital discipline
themes.note: India CAPEX slowed to calibrated spending on select new molecules (pharma, aroma); no large new spends planned this year or next; KSA spend still exploratory.

themes.label: Portfolio shift to value-added/high-margin segments
themes.note: Growth from new products—NMMO, MDEA, spray-cooled powders, biosurfactants, vitamin premixes, pharma—alongside launch of dedicated Fibre Chemicals Division targeting higher-value applications.

themes.label: Non-core asset & business divestment
themes.note: Sold Andheri office (Rs. 10.5 crore) following Kanjurmarg office sale; plans to exit B2C consumer business while retaining more profitable institutional cleaning business, expected to release 2-3% EBITDA margin.

themes.label: Export & international diversification
themes.note: Exports grew 21% YoY to ~Rs. 160 crore (23-24% of revenue); Thailand blending plant operational; Saudi Arabia greenfield initiative in formalization stage.

key_takeaways: We commenced FY27 on a strong note, delivering our highest ever quarterly revenue and EBITDA, with consolidated revenue growing 28% YoY.

The quarter witnessed strong growth across each of our core business segments, with the HPPC, TSC, and AHN business all growing by around 28% YoY. Notably, the HPPC business crossed Rs. 550 crore quarterly revenue milestone.
Our international business maintained its positive momentum, with exports growing 21% YoY during the quarter.

While the business has achieved significant scale, margins remain below their normalized potential. We have already initiated several measures to address this, including the monetization of our non-core assets, rationalization of lower margin businesses, improvement in product mix, and tighter cost discipline.

EBITDA for the quarter stood at Rs. 80.6 crore, representing a growth of 18.7% YoY and making our highest ever quarterly EBITDA. The EBITDA margins stood at 11.6% compared to 12.5% in the corresponding quarter last year.
Excluding the institutional and consumer businesses, our core B2B operations delivered EBITDA of Rs. 85 crore, registering a growth of 13% YoY, with an EBITDA margin of approximately 14%.
We further strengthened our presence in Southeast Asia through a greenfield blending plant in Thailand.
We are also making progress on our proposed initiative in Saudi Arabia... Despite the prevailing geographical uncertainty, our conviction in the long-term potential of this initiative remains intact.

Now that your availability is getting struggled, we have added lot of capacity. What are we trying to do, to see that we keep growing consistently in a scenario where assuming that the EO availability will remain challenge for some time, what are the growth lever do we have for it?

quarters.summary: FY26 closed with Q4 marking the highest-ever quarterly revenue and EBITDA; full-year revenue grew 15% YoY (volume driven) with all three segments (HPPC, Textiles, AHN) delivering double-digit growth in Q4. Management guides FY27 revenue growth of at least ~15% (similar to FY26) with consolidated EBITDA margin maintained at 12%-13%, supported by new ethoxylation/premix/Thailand capacities, pharma/agro/oil & gas segment expansion, cost optimization, non-core asset divestment, and portfolio rationalization in the loss-making institutional/B2C business, which is targeted to reach breakeven/profitability in FY27. Company is also rephasing its previously announced Rs. 192 crore capex plan and reviewing broader investment plans amid Middle East geopolitical volatility and raw material cost inflation.

subsections.label: Margin drivers
points: Gross margins were relatively lower with the quarter's sales mix impacting overall margin profile.
March saw raw material price increases of 25%-30%, impacting costs; some older orders for the quarter were honored at these higher costs in March.
Some cost increases have since been passed on to customers and some are in process of being passed through over April and May.
Higher revenues along with disciplined cost management and operating efficiencies helped contain impact at the EBITDA level.

Institutional and B2C businesses continued to operate in a challenging environment during the year, impacting overall profitability; losses have continued to moderate through H2 FY26 driven by focus on improving product mix, enhancing operational efficiency and maintaining cost discipline.
Excluding institutional and B2C businesses, core B2B operations delivered 14% EBITDA margin for the year, reflecting underlying strength and stability of the core business.

Expenses remained elevated during the year primarily due to ongoing investments in capacity expansion, new business development and capability building; as investments scale up and utilization improves, operating leverage is expected to support margin improvement over coming years.

subsections.label: Other income / asset monetization
points: Other income during the quarter includes sale of office space in Mumbai with net income of Rs. 19 crore; this is the first step toward liquidating non-core assets, with more planned during the current year.

subsections.label: Balance sheet & capital allocation
points: Balance sheet remains strong with healthy liquidity and comfortable leverage levels, providing flexibility to pursue growth initiatives.
Company internally decided to rephase the earlier CAPEX plan of Rs. 192 crore across Rossari, Unitop and Tristar announced in April, in light of evolving business requirements and market conditions.

Earlier capex (particularly ethoxylation capacities) was delayed as Reliance revised its own capacity expansion plans; Rossari moderated capex spend accordingly, partly capitalizing capacity in Q3 and balance in Q4 (March).

The other CAPEX plan (amine range products, pilot plants, R&D expansion at sites) was not immediately commenced given the earlier delays and current business/global environment; R&D site spend was redirected into the new Navi Mumbai R&D facility.

Rephased spend (~Rs. 190 crore across 3 sites) is being planned over this year and partly into next year; decision reflects optimization of cash flow management and ROCE considerations - want current capacity to generate earmarked returns before further CAPEX.
FY27 CAPEX plan of Rs. 50-75 crore includes a pharma facility and a couple of small capexes, one likely in aroma chemicals space, both within the Rs. 50 crore range.

Plans this year: use cash flows to bring down overall debt levels; shed non-core assets (Mumbai office space already sold, more office spaces and underutilized assets across India to be sold); trim product profile and business segments.
Target is to become debt-free in the next 18 months, though timing may vary; plan is to keep bringing down debt over the next 18 months.
No share buyback plans despite trading at less than 10x EBITDA (historical low).

Standalone vs consolidated profit divergence explained by inter-company product mix - similar products sold from subsidiaries and Rossari to different customers, with blending happening interchangeably; best to view performance at consolidated level as the standalone-consolidated revenue mix can change quarter-on-quarter.

subsections.label: Demand conditions
points: Ethoxylate demand: no demand-side challenge, orders remain robust; agro season dependent on El Nino, which is too early to comment on (similar worries last year did not materialize).
Good pipeline of projects worked on by sales and business development teams over the last 12 months, with results expected to show.
Ethoxylation utilization is practically 90%-100% of maximum capacity, running 24/7, 365 days a year, with no downtime except for planned expansion stoppages.
Domestic demand conditions remained relatively soft during certain periods of the year; institutional and B2C businesses performance also remained subdued.

key_figures.label: Segment-level EBITDA margin variance vs company average

subsections.label: Segment performance drivers
points: Performance during the quarter was broad-based with all three business segments delivering healthy double-digit growth, supported by a diversified portfolio and balanced exposure across end markets despite a dynamic operating environment.

Growth supported by continued customer engagement, product development efforts and steady execution; focus remains on strengthening customer relationships, expanding the product basket, improving market penetration and building scale in relevant chemistries and applications.

subsections.label: Segment margin profile
points: Company does not disclose segment-wise EBITDA margins in detail, but at EBITDA level all three businesses are roughly at company-level margins, with some segments 1-2% higher or lower.

At gross margin level, textiles has a decent gross margin, AHN (the smallest segment) has a higher/the highest gross margin, and HPPC is a mixed bag (agro, non-agro, other products) with agro and oil & gas sub-segments having better gross margins within HPPC.
Pharma, an area HPPC is expanding into this year, is expected to fetch the highest gross margins across all segments once it reaches a reasonable size.
Textile segment has a split of specialty and some commodity chemicals; specialty textile margins are very healthy.
Fixed cost profiles vary across the three business segments though EBITDA margins converge near company level.

subsections.label: Competitive landscape
points: AHN competitors: global majors Kemin, Cargill, Novus, Vetnex (Pfizer/Zoetis); Indian players Natural Remedies and Jubilant.
Textile competitors: Archroma (also has constant portfolio and BASF portfolio, a leader), Croda, CHT, Pulcra.

HPPC competitors: global surfactant majors BASF, Dow, Lubrizol, Syensqo, Evonik rule the market globally; other players include SABIC (Saudi Arabia), Petronas (integrated), Chinese companies, and domestic player India Glycols; imports come from all sources into the Indian market.
Listed company Fineotex Chemical also operates in textile chemicals and other specialty chemicals; management could not comment on like-to-like portfolio comparison.

subsections.label: B2B vs B2C/Institutional
points: Most growth discussed is expected to happen in the core B2B business; on the consumer side, the entire business and product profile is being relooked to focus only on products with stronger margins.
Subtracting Rs. 250-260 crore of B2C business revenue from total revenue gives the B2B revenue contribution.

Institutional business FY26 performance was relatively muted with expanding losses; FY27 targeted to reach breakeven or profitability, aided by divestment of some lower-margin/EBITDA-loss-contributing businesses.

subsections.label: R&D and innovation strategy
points: Company is gradually evolving from a formulation-led approach towards developing broader platform technologies with multi-vertical applicability, enabling more scalable and differentiated solutions across end-user segments.

Meaningful progress in product development and application-led innovation during the year, with newer products contributing increasingly to the business and sustainable chemistries, including biosurfactants, gaining traction.

New R&D facility set up in Navi Mumbai brings together existing R&D operations, including the IIT Mumbai center, under one roof, expected to provide a stronger platform for innovation, product development, application-led research, and improve collaboration and support faster scale-up of new technologies.
R&D site spend originally planned under the rephased CAPEX plan has been redirected to meet R&D needs from the new Navi Mumbai facility.

subsections.label: Pharma product development
points: Among Rossari's chemistries (surfactant, acrylic, enzymes, silicones), all can potentially go into pharma; current focus is on surfactant chemistry and polyethylene glycols (PEG) across a range of molecular weights (400, 600, 1,000, 2,000, 3,350, 4,000, 6,000, 10,000, 20,000 and above).
Other esters manufactured by the company can also go into pharma.
Focus areas within pharma also include coating products and products used to make gels for pharma and personal care.
Ongoing work on one pharma product expected to come up sometime this year (FY27).

key_figures.label: Total installed ethoxylation capacity (post Dahej expansion)

subsections.label: Ethoxylation expansion
points: Unitop commissioned additional ethoxylation capacity at Dahej, taking total installed ethoxylation capacity to 66,000 metric tons per annum, enhancing supply reliability and improving ability to serve customer requirements more effectively.

New EO capacities at Reliance expected to come on stream in the later part of FY27, probably by Q3; Reliance's partial expansion is expected to release more EO supply from December, with more capacity coming up next December.
Company is confident market demand exists to absorb the new EO capacity.

subsections.label: Unitop capacity ramp-up
points: The 15,000-ton Unitop capacity commissioned in Q2 FY26 was at 10%-15% utilization in Q3; utilization improved (though exact Q4 figure not available) and is ramping up.
Growth from the subsidiary in Q4 was largely attributed to higher utilization of this capacity.

subsections.label: Thailand facility
points: Thailand plant came on stream in the last quarter (towards end of March) - a small blending unit, not a full-scale textile chemical plant, set up to do blending to meet Southeast Asia customer requirements.
Plan is to bring raw materials for blending activities directly from China at more competitive rates.
Thailand facility expected to start contributing meaningfully from this year, with meaningful ramp-up expected from Q2 FY27 onwards.
Will start with textile products, some AHN, and then evaluate expansion into other products within the home and personal care basket depending on customer response.
Thailand revenues are inclusive of, not incremental to, the targeted 15% overall growth for FY27; will not reach the Rs. 50 crore peak figure in the current year.

subsections.label: Premix plant (AHN)
points: Premix plant previously expected in Q1 FY27 has already been commissioned; revenues from the premix expected to start from this quarter.
Full-scale premix facility capacity enhancement expected next year (beyond this initial ramp-up).

subsections.label: CAPEX rephasing
points: As Reliance revised its capacity expansion plans, Rossari also moderated its capex spend; earlier capex (particularly ethoxylation) was delayed from planned commissioning the year before last, with capacity partly capitalized in Q3 and balance in Q4 (March).

Other CAPEX plan (amine range products, pilot plants, R&D expansion) not immediately commenced; being rephased over this year and partly next year given current business environment and global situation.
FY27 capex includes a pharma facility and a couple of small capexes, likely including one in the aroma chemical space.

subsections.label: Export momentum
points: Continued export momentum during the year with exports growing 11% YoY in FY26, supported by deeper engagement with existing customers and expansion into geographies across Latin America, Europe, Southeast Asia and Africa.
Focus on increasing wallet share with key partners and expanding into newer markets continues to strengthen the international binder business and diversify the growth profile.

subsections.label: New/expanding geographies
points: North American market being targeted for both personal care and agro business.
In Latin America, company is already strong in agro and is trying to build the business further there.
In textiles, ramping up exports through Bangladesh, Southeast Asia/Asian countries, Thailand, Turkey and Brazil; export growth in textiles expected to outperform domestic growth.
In Personal Care, phenoxy business is one of the largest globally, and with new capacities the company is entering newer markets across the globe.

subsections.label: International expansion - Saudi Arabia
points: Progress continues on the proposed initiative in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, seen as an important strategic step towards strengthening long-term manufacturing footprint and enhancing supply-side competitiveness.
Despite recent geopolitical developments, management remains confident of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia expansion plans.

subsections.label: Raw material sourcing
points: Current raw material position is stable; supply chain teams have maintained availability across all raw materials with no stock shortages.
Ethylene Oxide (EO) supply is very stable and made domestically, so no imports required for EO.

Phenol is sourced from various sources including Thailand, Malaysia, India and China; company is not buying anything from the Middle East currently; significant material also comes from the U.S., which does not pass through the Strait of Hormuz.
Acetic acid has plenty of alternative sources; silicones are sourced from China; acrylic acid is manufactured in India and sourced from various domestic sources.
Unlike other industries, dependence on Middle East raw materials is not as significant, though global prices have risen overall.

Last month (March), some raw materials had to be purchased at higher prices due to existing customer orders, impacting gross margins; from April onwards, high raw material purchase costs are being passed through with added margins into final prices, with customer acceptance given visible global geopolitical situation.
No foreseen issues on RM sourcing and availability going forward for the range of raw materials purchased.

subsections.label: Pass-through
points: No major challenge in passing through raw material cost increases; pass-through has been implemented from 1st of April across most products.
Some resistance encountered in the textile industry specifically, but supplies are being controlled to ensure profitable margins are maintained everywhere.

subsections.label: Systems / ERP
points: SAP S/4HANA implementation is helping create a stronger digital foundation across the business, improving visibility, coordination and decision-making across functions.
Continued advancement of responsible manufacturing agenda through structured waste management and sustainability-led operational practices.

subsections.label: Customer diversification
points: Products are very well diversified with low customer concentration; no single customer accounts for more than 2% of sales, reflecting good diversification.

Growth (25% sales CAGR, 18% profit CAGR over last 6 years) has majorly come from repeat sales, but also from acquiring new customers and cross-selling new products into existing customers to increase wallet share.

subsections.label: Value-added product focus
points: Strategy is to focus on value-added, higher-margin products (food, personal care, pharma, cosmetics, animal health and nutrition) while consciously cutting down on low-margin products, expected to help increase gross and EBITDA margins.
Company does not currently disclose a specific value-added sales metric but is considering improving disclosure/data in future presentations.

Growth strategy spread across multiple segments - pharma, oil and gas, aroma, personal care, food processing, institutional/cleaning chemicals for health & hygiene, and animal health & nutrition - not concentrated in just one or two verticals.
Focus is on getting into a 'higher orbit' for EBITDA, with teams being tuned/trained to focus on improving return on capital employed and EBITDA margins in each business.

key_figures.label: Big CAPEX projects (pharma facility and aroma chemical) upper limit

subsections.label: Non-core asset divestment / portfolio restructuring
points: Company is undertaking cost optimization and portfolio rationalization initiatives in the institutional and B2C domestic segments.

Plan to sell non-core assets and businesses that are not core to operations and require significant investment to grow, especially consumer businesses pulling down gross and EBITDA margins; once these are no longer part of Rossari, margins should improve.
First divestment step already executed - sale of Mumbai office space (net income Rs. 19 crore); more office spaces and underutilized assets across India planned for disposal this year.

Company is evaluating how to restructure business segments, particularly consumer-focused businesses that do not receive adequate management time, energy and money for growth; cashing out could help streamline the core business and allow those businesses to grow under new ownership.

Nothing concrete finalized yet on divestment plans/value; management would not hazard a specific rupee value or timeline, though the aspiration is for divestment to happen in 2027, potentially taking 1-2 years; management wants to exit at good value to a buyer who can grow the business given its inherent strength.

Consumer-focused business asset block does not account for a large proportion of total assets - most of the asset base pertains to B2B businesses; consumer product assets were carved out as add-on blocks from B2B segment assets.
No promoter stake sale or exit plans, contrary to market rumours in January/February; promoters remain focused on growth.

subsections.label: Growth priorities
points: Strategic steps across capacity expansion, portfolio development, customer relationships, exports and international initiatives are steadily strengthening the foundation of the business, expected to significantly accelerate growth over the next 2-3 years.

Ramp-up in value-added segments (pharma, oil & gas, etc.) expected to take 2-3 years to reach optimum utilization; core segments (agro, textile, AHN) expected to see latent growth continue in parallel.

subsections.label: Geopolitical and raw material risk
points: The year saw external challenges including volatility in certain raw materials markets and disruptions arising from geopolitical developments in the Middle East.
Ongoing conflict in the Middle East has created uncertainty across raw material markets, supply chains and logistics, which may have an impact over the coming quarters.
Immediate focus is on navigating the current environment through closer customer engagement, calibrated pricing actions and disciplined execution.
March saw raw material price increases of 25%-30%, impacting costs for orders honored during that month.

subsections.label: Agro/weather risk
points: Agro season is dependent on El Nino, which can affect the season; too early to comment, though similar worries last year did not materialize.

subsections.label: Institutional/B2C business risk
points: Institutional and B2C businesses continued to operate in a challenging environment during the year, impacting overall profitability, with domestic demand conditions relatively soft during certain periods and subdued performance in institutional/B2C.

subsections.label: FY27 growth and margin outlook
points: Internally, the company plans to deliver at least similar growth in FY27 as achieved in FY26; if the global situation improves, growth trajectory could be much better.
New capacities will be on stream for the full year in FY27, and new EO capacities at Reliance are expected to come in the later part of FY27, probably by Q3.

EBITDA margins expected to remain at current levels of 12%-13% in FY27; certain initiatives (moving into better-margin segments like pharma) are expected to help improve margins from H2 FY27 onwards, though current guidance is to maintain existing margin levels next year.

Growth drivers for FY27 include capacities put up in FY26 (available for more than half of FY27), pharma and agro segment focus, and oil & gas segment growth - these 3-4 initiatives are expected to help drive the 15%+ growth target.

Employee cost, which rose significantly in FY26 due to talent investment ahead of expansion plans, is not expected to grow at similarly elevated levels in FY27, though some new talent will still be added.
Ramp-up in high-value segments is expected to take 2-3 years to reach optimum capacity utilization, with core segments (agro, textile, AHN) providing parallel latent growth.

Management is bullish on at least a minimum 15% growth in FY27 based on capacity ramp-ups (premix, Thailand, ethoxylation), new geography expansion (North America, Latin America, Southeast Asia, Turkey, Brazil) and new segment entries (pharma).

subsections.label: Institutional business outlook
points: FY27 targeted as the year for the institutional business to reach breakeven or even profitability, aided by divestment of some lower-margin or EBITDA-loss-contributing businesses.

subsections.label: Debt reduction outlook
points: Plan to bring down debt significantly over this year and over the next roughly 18 months, with an aspirational target of becoming debt-free in that period, though management cautioned timing could vary.

guidance_ledger.statement: We will continue to do at least minimum similar kind of growth that we have done in this year; if things improve globally, growth trajectory will be much better.

Currently the EBITDA margins will remain at these current levels between 12% to 13%; some initiatives (getting into better margin segments like pharma) will come into play probably by H2 and should help improve margins, but current margins will be maintained next year.
We should do an asset turn of at least between 3-4x at peak utilization.
The target is to actually get debt free in the next 18 months, but the time will tell. Currently, the plan is to keep bringing down our debt over the next 18 months.
The CAPEX plan for this year would be I think anything between Rs. 50 crore to Rs. 75 crore; even at very peak levels, we would reach Rs. 70 crore - Rs. 75 crore number.
We should do about between Rs. 50 crore - Rs. 75 crore at its peak, but we will not reach Rs. 50 crore in this year itself.

In FY27, we should look at breakeven or even profitability, along with the divestment of some lower-margin businesses or those that contributed to EBITDA losses. We feel FY27 should be a very good year for the institutional business.
The plan is we would like it to happen in 2027, but it could take more than a year, 2 years.

We are expecting the new EO capacities at Reliance to also come in the later part of this year probably by Q3; Reliance will release more EO from December when their partial expansion is done, with more coming up next December.
Thailand is going to now start contributing meaningfully from this year, probably from quarter 2 onwards we should see meaningful ramp-up in the Thailand facility.
We see revenues coming from the premix starting this quarter, and a full-scale premix facility capacity enhancement in the next year.

guidance_ledger.metric: Growth ramp-up in high-value segments (pharma, oil & gas etc.)
guidance_ledger.statement: The expectation is that ramp-up will happen over the next 2-3 years while current segments of core agro, textile and AHN keep seeing latent growth happening parallelly.
We believe these efforts are putting the right building blocks in place to significantly accelerate growth over the next 2 to 3 years.

risk_register.risk: Raw material price volatility
risk_register.note: March saw raw material price increases of 25%-30%, impacting costs; some have since been passed through to customers, others in process over April-May.

risk_register.risk: Domestic demand softness
risk_register.note: Domestic demand conditions remained relatively soft during certain periods of the year; institutional and B2C business performance remained subdued.

risk_register.risk: Institutional/B2C business losses
risk_register.note: Losses in institutional and B2C business continued to moderate through H2 FY26 due to focus on product mix, operational efficiency and cost discipline, though the segment continued to be a challenge overall.

risk_register.risk: Agro season weather risk (El Nino)
risk_register.note: Agro season is dependent on El Nino, which can affect the season; too early to comment, though similar worries last year did not materialize.

risk_register.risk: Textile industry pass-through resistance
risk_register.note: Some resistance encountered in passing through cost increases specifically in the textile industry, though supplies are being controlled to maintain profitable margins.

risk_register.risk: Elevated operating expenses from capacity/talent investment

themes.label: Margin pressure from RM inflation
themes.note: March raw material price hikes of 25%-30% and unfavorable sales mix pressured EBITDA margin to 11.3% in Q4 and 11.9% for FY26, down from 12.7% in FY25.

themes.label: Geopolitical/Middle East disruption
themes.note: Middle East conflict created uncertainty across raw material markets, supply chains and logistics, with possible impact over coming quarters.

themes.label: Capacity expansion & ramp-up
themes.note: Ethoxylation capacity expanded to 66,000 MTPA at Dahej; Unitop, Thailand blending unit and AHN premix facility ramping up to drive FY27 growth.

themes.label: CAPEX rephasing / capital discipline
themes.note: Previously announced Rs. 192 crore capex across Rossari, Unitop and Tristar rephased amid evolving business conditions; FY27 capex trimmed to Rs. 50-75 crore.

themes.label: Portfolio shift to value-added/high-margin segments
themes.note: Strategic push into pharma, oil & gas, aroma and other high-margin verticals expected to improve gross and EBITDA margins over 2-3 years.

themes.label: Non-core asset & business divestment
themes.note: Company selling non-core assets (Mumbai office sale realized Rs.19 crore net income) and evaluating exit from consumer-focused/B2C and institutional businesses to streamline core B2B operations and cut debt.

themes.label: Export & international diversification
themes.note: Exports grew 11% YoY in FY26 with expansion into Latin America, Europe, Southeast Asia, Africa, North America; Saudi Arabia manufacturing initiative progressing despite geopolitical headwinds.

key_takeaways: We concluded FY26 on a very strong note, with Q4 marking our highest-ever quarterly revenue and EBITDA performance. For the full year, we delivered revenue growth of 15%, which was primarily volume driven.
From a segment perspective, HPPC delivered growth of 18% during the quarter, Textiles grew by 20% and AHN recorded a growth of 14%.
On the export front, we witnessed continued momentum during the year with exports growing by 11% YoY in FY26.
Excluding the institutional and the B2C businesses, our core B2B operations delivered an EBITDA margin of 14% for the year, reflecting the underlying strength and stability of our core business.
We internally have decided to rephase our earlier CAPEX spend, which was announced in April of Rs. 192 crore across Rossari, Unitop and Tristar.
Currently, the EBITDA margins will remain at these current levels between 12% to 13% [for FY27].
The target is to actually get debt free in the next 18 months, but the time will tell.
In FY27, we should look at breakeven or even profitability [for institutional business], along with the divestment of some lower-margin businesses.

Post this CAPEX that is expected to get completed, what will be the peak revenue potential of the company if you operate at full utilization across manufacturing facilities?

How are we looking at the institutional business in terms of scaling up and when do we now expect breakeven happening?

ETERNAL.about: Incorporated in 2010, Zomato Limited is one of the leading online Food Service platforms in terms of the value of food sold. Its offerings include food delivery, dining-out services, Loyalty programs, and others. As of December 31, 2020, Zomato has established a strong footprint across 23 countries with 131,233 active food delivery restaurants, 161,637 active delivery partners, and an average monthly food order of 10.7 million customers.[1]

quarters.summary: Management raised the long-term quick commerce margin guidance to 6% (from a 5-6% range) citing efficiency gains from higher capex per store and larger store sizes; competitive intensity in quick commerce is described as high but "more predictable" with Q1 seen as the peak so far; NAOV in Blinkit is expected to remain range-bound going forward while growth is driven by order/frequency growth; food delivery MTU growth is driven by both new customer additions and higher frequency; Bistro and Nugget remain early-stage, cautiously scaled businesses; District (going-out) continues to expand across five categories with dine-out and movies as largest contributors.

key_figures.label: EBIT margin (long-term, GAAP incl. ESOP & depreciation)
Capex per store (earlier guidance, incl. warehousing)
Free delivery eligibility threshold before change (Gold member)

subsections.label: Margin composition
points: EBIT margin of 4% is GAAP and includes both ESOP expenses and depreciation.
Adjusted EBITDA margin is close to 6%.

subsections.label: Inventory losses
points: Inventory losses of 1.8% of NOV are largely driven by perishables and have been fairly asymptotic; not expected to materially improve aside from mix changes.
All such losses are netted out at the gross profit level, forming part of COGS; gross profit is net of these losses.

subsections.label: Working capital
points: Net working capital reduced from 18 days to the current 14 days, and is expected to reduce further to a steady-state estimate of 12 days.
Reduction driven largely by lower-than-expected inventory carrying days, enabled by improved replenishment and throughput across stores and supply chain, not by terms-of-trade optimization.

subsections.label: Capex per store vs cash flow
points: Capex per store guidance of ~INR 2.5 crore should be viewed over a longer term (6-9 months or more) since a large part of capex (warehousing) is lumpy; over a longer period, capex per store is lower than INR 2.5 crore and expected to remain so.
The prior INR 1 crore capex-per-store figure also included warehousing fees, so is comparable to the new INR 2.5 crore figure.

Capex expansion (150% increase vs prior assumption) relates significantly to overall supply chain efficiency (ability to store more products per warehouse, ship more efficiently), not solely store-level throughput.
Quarter's quick commerce capex was INR 700 crore, with 200 stores added in the quarter.

subsections.label: Payables
points: Payables increase of ~INR 1,650 crore includes both trade payables and expense payables.
Trade payables increase driven by scale of business growth, not by seeking better payment terms with brands; expense payables fluctuate.
Management does not see anything unusual to highlight on payables trend.

subsections.label: Tax / OCF
points: Higher OCF this quarter partly reflects a tax refund related to certain expenses that were ambiguous regarding allowability; company had deposited higher advance tax and received a refund.
This is normal course of business and such items may recur occasionally, but nothing structural.
