subsections.label: Blinkit AOV/NAOV dynamics
points: Blinkit volume growth was 21% QoQ this quarter, versus a historical Q1-Q2 range of 18-20% and 26% growth in the prior year's Q1-Q2.
NAOV drop is in the same range as last year; largely related to small pattern changes during the quarter, not material shifts in throughput or category share.
Some NAOV softness may also stem from lower product prices due to competitive price-matching.

Management does not expect NAOV to grow from here; year-on-year it is flat (accounting for Q1 seasonality); NAOV may climb in Q3 due to seasonality but is not expected to move up meaningfully overall.

NAOV is treated as an outcome, not a driver — a function of category mix and product assortment; what matters is NOV and margins, not NAOV per se, since smaller high-margin categories/products can offset lower NAOV.

Assortment expansion into low-NAOV categories, plus rising frequency (leading to smaller basket sizes as ordering becomes a daily use case), both create a drag on NAOV even as general merchandise assortment (higher margin) expands; net effect: NAOV expansion is not currently anticipated, even as wallet share per customer increases.
MTUs (quick commerce) are comfortably over 30 million currently, with implied MTU spend on the platform of less than INR 2,000/month.

subsections.label: Growth drivers - existing cities vs geographic expansion
points: Most of Blinkit's aggregate growth is coming from existing cities rather than new geographic expansion.

subsections.label: Cohort spend & retention
points: Older cohorts spend 3x versus three years back; directionally most of this growth is from order frequency growth rather than AOV growth, as NAOV stabilizes with only slight growth over time for a customer cohort.

The 3x cohort growth figure is calculated on the full original cohort (including customers who churned and never returned), not just retained customers; e.g., if 40 of 100 acquired customers never return, retention is only 60%, yet the reported growth reflects the full cohort base.

subsections.label: City-tier growth differential
points: Non-metro cities are growing faster off a smaller base, so percentage growth rates appear higher.
Competitive intensity is concentrated mostly in groceries in top-tier cities, causing some share shift and dampening tier-1 city growth numbers, though tier-1 growth remains robust overall.

subsections.label: Store throughput/size
points: New economics point to 2,100-2,200 orders per day per store for bigger stores.
Store upgrades to larger, more optimal properties are ongoing but not treated as a regular exercise; larger stores drive higher throughput.

subsections.label: Take rate vs contribution margin
points: Improvement in take rate has not fully flowed to contribution margin due to increased cost of doing business from minimum wage hikes in several states, and because larger, newly opened stores have lower initial contribution than smaller, more mature stores.

Business is seasonal — Q1 last-mile costs are typically higher due to summer heat; year-on-year comparison shows a large part of gross profit/take-rate increase has translated into contribution increase; the right comparison period is Q1 versus Q1 of the previous year, and margin can also be affected by category mix changes.

subsections.label: Pareto/customer concentration
points: In food delivery, roughly the top 15-18% of customers drive about 80% of revenue; in quick commerce, this ratio is described as much flatter (less concentrated).

subsections.label: Food delivery MTU growth
points: Increase in MTUs is a combination of acceleration in new users added over the last 3-4 quarters and a function of category growth plus more frequent transacting by existing customers.
Food delivery MTU/NOV disclosures do not include Bistro; Bistro is in a separate entity with clear segregation of accounts and no overlap in NOV or bottom line.

subsections.label: Bistro business
points: Adding about 10 kitchens per quarter as pace of expansion.
Older kitchens showing progress in throughput; company is refining assortment mix, menus, menu pricing and operational infrastructure/efficiency.
Mindset mirrors early Blinkit build-out: fix basic processes first, then expand more aggressively once profitability and confidence improve; currently expanding cautiously.

subsections.label: Response to competitor formats (Toing/Ownly)
points: Trying to be price competitive in specific markets where these platforms spend aggressively; approach has been sufficient so far to defend share.
Example: last year, Gold member free-delivery eligibility threshold was lowered from INR 199 to INR 99, reducing cost for customers seeking low-value orders.

subsections.label: Restaurant count
points: Monthly active restaurant count dipped slightly this quarter due to LPG situation in the country causing some restaurants to go offline; described as a temporary impact, not a structural rationalization.

subsections.label: District (going-out business)
points: District operates across five categories; dine-out and movies are the largest revenue contributors currently.
Among newer categories, retail stores and events appear most promising, though still early; focus is on how much value is added to the supply ecosystem and improving customer experience.
Difficult to predict growth trajectory for newer categories at this stage, though trends are described as promising.
District's customer base is considered different from food delivery — a higher-spending base, reflected in higher NAOVs; still room to grow even at this NAOV level.
District will have a smaller customer base and will operate in fewer cities compared to food delivery and quick commerce.

subsections.label: Nugget (enterprise AI business)
points: Company remains largely in stealth mode on Nugget and will share more in coming quarters.
Described as an enterprise AI product business seeing good traction in an evolving AI market; management wants a couple more quarters to build its thesis before sharing more.
Costs in this business are largely manpower-related, not GPU/infrastructure spend.

subsections.label: Store format strategy
points: Plans to add gourmet-format stores in tier-1 cities as part of assortment focus; whether this results in more split orders depends on real estate and infrastructure availability, with some larger stores able to house broader assortment within the same store.

Company aims to avoid tilting too much toward split orders since that could hurt customer experience, though in practice this has not materially occurred; customers value product availability more than avoiding split orders.

subsections.label: Competitive intensity — quick commerce
points: Q1 was the peak of competitive intensity seen to date, due to a higher number of players and aggressive behavior, but competition has become more 'predictable' since most competitors are subsidizing via product discounts and delivery fees, particularly in grocery.
Management does not see much room for competitors to go materially deeper on subsidies without significantly ballooning losses.

Discounting is viewed as less effective in quick commerce than e-commerce because quick commerce operates with smaller store sizes and limited shelf space — discounting low-margin categories dominates sales from that limited space with less ability to expand assortment reliably, unlike e-commerce which uses large warehouses to fulfill broader discounted assortment.

subsections.label: Value vs discounting philosophy
points: Company frames itself as a supply-creation business: channeling supply toward discounts risks trapping the business, since customers acquired via subsidy have no reason to stay once discounts are withdrawn — they migrate to other platforms or exit the category; management sees no clear recovery path for platforms relying on subsidy-led acquisition.

Historical experience: a few years ago the company was the number 3-4 player in several markets (especially in the south) and initial e-commerce-style discounting did not work; success instead came from building infrastructure, and the company is now the leading player by NOV in most of these markets.

Strategy is not zero customer value — as platform profitability improves, a portion is reinvested into more competitive product prices to tap into more price-sensitive customer cohorts gradually, as part of platform growth into a larger addressable market (source of incremental MTUs).

Current elevated discounting levels are viewed as unsustainable and expected to recede in the near future, reducing pressure on the company to discount to stay competitive; even so, any future price reductions would be a deliberate choice to pass on scale benefits to customers, not a reaction to competitor pricing.

Company does not track competitor discounting closely beyond a point; its baseline for pricing decisions is its own view of sustainable long-run product prices, and price cuts are made only when they can be sustained long-term, not as short-term customer acquisition tactics.

subsections.label: Market share / growth attribution
points: Management does not attribute the quarter's quick commerce growth recovery to a specific factor (market share regain vs. industry-wide growth) — this is described as speculative; company instead focuses on data it can rely on, notably improved customer retention.
No specific change was made to drive the MTU surge despite lower marketing spend and fewer store additions this quarter, per management.

subsections.label: Productivity gains
points: Productivity gains have been ongoing since the business started, spanning dark store level, warehouse level, supply chain, marketing efficiency, and assortment — not limited to recent quarters or cohort maturation alone.

subsections.label: Competitive intensity
points: High number of aggressive players in Q1, viewed as peak competitive intensity to date; competitors mainly subsidizing via product discounts/delivery fees, concentrated in grocery.

subsections.label: Cost pressures
points: Minimum wage increases implemented across several states raised cost of doing business, partially offsetting take-rate gains in contribution margin.
Seasonal cost pressure: Q1 last-mile delivery costs typically higher due to summer heat.

subsections.label: External/regulatory disruption
points: LPG situation in the country caused some restaurants to go offline temporarily, contributing to a slight dip in monthly active restaurant count in food delivery.

subsections.label: Inventory loss risk
points: Inventory losses (1.8% of NOV, largely perishables) have plateaued (asymptotic) and are not expected to materially improve going forward, aside from potential mix shifts.

subsections.label: Margin guidance revision
points: Long-term quick commerce margin guidance raised toward the higher end of the previously guided 5-6% range to 6%, based on increased capex per store driving efficiency, and increased average store sizes.
Company declined to provide specific Q2 volume growth guidance for Blinkit, citing no comment on quarter-specific numbers at this stage.

Management indicated that absent unexpected changes, as long as growth continues per expectations, there are no near-term margin pressures anticipated and margins should continue to improve directionally — though this was offered as a qualified 'at this point' statement, not a firm commitment.

subsections.label: ROCE framework
points: Currently EBIT margin is negative for the overall business, so there is no calculable ROCE today; the ROCE framework previously given is meant as a guide for how much to invest in the business going forward, not a current realized metric.

Higher capex with lower per-store NOV growth is being rationalized as market expansion (e.g., opening stores in smaller cities with lower NOV per day per store but still profitable at ~6% margin), aimed at growing absolute profit dollars while keeping ROCE healthy; management stated it is comfortable with capex per store, working capital, NOV per store, and margin figures moving around as long as ROCE math holds.

key_takeaways: Long-term quick commerce margin guidance raised to 6% (from 5-6% range) driven by higher capex per store efficiency and larger average store sizes.
Competitive intensity in quick commerce peaked in Q1 but has become 'more predictable' as competitors mainly subsidize via product discounts/delivery fees in grocery, with limited room to go deeper.
Older customer cohorts spend 3x versus three years back, driven mostly by order frequency growth rather than AOV growth; this is measured across the full original cohort including churned customers.
Blinkit NAOV is expected to remain range-bound going forward; NAOV treated as an outcome of category mix, not a driver, with NOV and margins being the key focus.
Take-rate improvement has not fully flowed to contribution margin due to minimum wage hikes and lower initial contribution from newly opened larger stores; seasonal Q1 last-mile costs also a factor.
Capex per store guidance of ~INR 2.5 crore should be viewed over a longer period given lumpiness from warehousing investment; longer-term trailing capex per store is actually lower.
Net working capital reduced from 18 days to 14 days currently, with a steady-state target of 12 days, driven by lower-than-expected inventory carrying days and improved replenishment/throughput.

Discounting is viewed as structurally less effective in quick commerce than e-commerce due to smaller store sizes/limited shelf space; company frames itself as a supply-creation business avoiding a subsidy-led growth trap.
Bistro and Nugget (enterprise AI) remain early-stage businesses being cautiously scaled, with more disclosure on Nugget promised in coming quarters.

District operates across five categories with dine-out and movies as largest contributors; newer categories (retail, events) show promise but trajectory is uncertain; District has a smaller, higher-spending customer base than food delivery/quick commerce.
pressing_questions: Aditya Suresh (Macquarie) asked management to calculate current ROCE for the business; Akshant Goyal responded there is no ROCE currently since EBIT margin is negative, and the ROCE framework is meant to guide future investment rather than reflect a present figure.
Abhisek Banerjee (ICICI) asked for color on the Nugget business (what exactly it does); management said they are still largely in 'stealth mode' and will share more details in coming quarters.

Swapnil Potdukhe (JM Financial) asked whether Q2 quick commerce volume growth would be in line with historical 18-26% QoQ growth range; management declined to comment or guide on the specific quarter.

quarters.summary: Management reiterated a longer-term three-year guidance of 60% NOV CAGR in quick commerce (Blinkit) and steady-state margin of ~3-3.5% (implied via ~3% EBITDA margin commentary), alongside a $1 billion EBITDA target by FY29 and District EBITDA guidance by FY30, while declining to give specific near-term (FY27) growth or dark-store count guidance beyond the March target of 3,000 stores, citing the need for flexibility amid continued high competitive intensity across markets.

subsections.label: Food delivery
points: Contribution per order saw a slight dip in the quarter; management attributes this to multiple sequential factors including AOV seasonality, last-mile delivery seasonality (delivery partner supply changes by month), and supply chain cost efficiencies — no single dominant driver, and no change to long-term trajectory.

Platform fees have been increasing while a lower MOV of ~INR 99 has been offered to improve affordability — management clarifies platform fee applies to all customers, while discounts/offers are targeted to price-sensitive cohorts in specific geographies where subsidies drive growth; the strategy is to raise overall revenue per order via platform fees and channel that revenue to select price-sensitive cohorts.
A mid-quarter platform fee hike was taken; full flow-through to bottom line expected next quarter.

Management is reinvesting incremental margin/monetization gains into growth given good ROI seen in the last two to three quarters, rather than banking it straight to margin — this could result in either margin expansion or growth uptick, both optimizing for absolute EBITDA dollars.

No plans to replicate Swiggy's 'Toing' affordability model; management not clear on what problem it solves for consumers or restaurants and will stay focused on core Zomato business unless a clearer thesis emerges.
Bistro remains a small, early-stage experiment showing early signs of a business model evolving, but not yet positioned as a major bet.

Rise in active delivery partners (30% YoY) versus lower order growth (15% YoY) explained by more part-time riders working on the platform, increasing partner counts but reducing orders per shift per day.

Fuel price sensitivity: past experience (e.g., GST hike) shows cost increases can be passed to consumers without much demand impact; unless a drastic fuel price increase occurs, no meaningful margin impact expected.

subsections.label: Quick commerce (Blinkit)
points: MTU additions remain strong because marketing spend for new customer acquisition has not been reduced, even as fixed costs stayed flattish quarter-on-quarter — competitors have reportedly pulled back on marketing, resulting in extremely low customer acquisition cost (CAC) for the company; same marketing dollars are yielding more new customer additions (lower CAC).

Decline in orders-per-customer (from ~3.6 to ~3.35) attributed largely to acceleration in new customer additions (with typically lower initial ordering frequency) rather than deterioration in customer retention; retention has not been materially impacted despite higher pricing in certain geographies versus competitors.

Even in top-8 cities with 80-90% pin code coverage, customer penetration is not maxed out; assortment expansion will drive higher wallet share for existing customers, but customer addition will continue to be an equal or larger contributor to growth given low penetration within covered pin codes.
Dark store size (bigger vs smaller) is a hyperlocal decision based on available square footage, specific neighborhood, and urban infrastructure — no single standard applies across cities/localities.

Ad monetization: 'Non-paid' ads (brands/platforms not selling on Blinkit) are insignificant; most ad revenue is from brands stocked/sold on the platform. No breakdown given between SKU-linked ads, checkout ads, and brand-page ads.
Quick commerce is doing more ad revenue as % of NOV than food delivery already, despite being a younger business; final steady-state level not yet known.

subsections.label: District
points: Media reports of event cancellations (e.g., due to artists unable to travel to India because of war) not expected to impact the broader growth path of District, as events are only part of the business, which now spans multiple categories.
No plans to add new categories to District beyond current offerings; travel is not a current focus area.

Hyperpure, despite being the smallest business and reporting a small margin in the quarter, is included within the company's overall billion-dollar profit target and is described as meaningful and relevant, contrary to suggestion it is being excluded.

subsections.label: Capacity disclosure limits
points: Management declined to disclose prior-quarter or prior-year warehousing capacity figures for comparison, stating this is intentionally not disclosed.

Automation in warehouses is increasing across all facilities and expected to continue over the next few years, governed by an ROCE-based framework rather than automation for its own sake — capex decisions depend on cost/efficiency uplift from automation.
No specific capex guidance was given for automation beyond store additions over the next three years.

subsections.label: Inventory / 1P transition
points: Inventory days rose during the Q2-to-Q3 transition period when share of 1P (first-party) inventory model increased, but there has been no meaningful further increase from Q3 to Q4 apart from growth expected from overall business scale.
Management states inventory days are fairly steady currently and are not related to the tier 1/2/3 city split of the business.

subsections.label: Competitive positioning
points: Management does not consider it possible to reliably estimate overall market growth rate in quick commerce given multiple private/unlisted competitors and lack of visibility into their numbers; the company's own focus is on maintaining 'quality of growth' rather than matching an external market growth benchmark.

Non-negotiable priority for reaching quick commerce profitability is maintaining quality growth that meaningfully moves the business toward profitability and sustainability — not any single KPI such as orders per store or NAOV.
Company states it is not seeing user/MTU penetration approaching saturation in the foreseeable future despite competitive intensity from well-capitalized players.

Management confident in maintaining pricing discipline in quick commerce despite prevalent discounting in the market; hard to assess how much of market activity is 'froth' versus artificially discount-inflated demand.

Orders per day per store metric has stayed broadly flat for a long period; management does not guide on this metric specifically since business building blocks may evolve, and it's possible for margin targets (5-6%) to be achieved even without this metric rising.

Competitive intensity is described as fairly high broadly wherever the company operates, including tier 2/3 cities, with different aggressive players in different markets — competition is described as 'everywhere.'

Company states it is not opting for 'unhealthy' growth to grow faster right now, believing healthy growth in both the short and long term is the right approach, even though faster growth is technically achievable via less disciplined tactics.

Monitoring metric for reacting to competition: customer retention and customer frequency on own platform — as long as these are not meaningfully impacted, current strategic stance/principles will be maintained.

subsections.label: External/macro risks
points: Competitive intensity in quick commerce has not meaningfully changed versus prior quarter and remains high across geographies, including tier 2/3 cities, with different aggressive competitors in different markets.

Event cancellations in District's events category (e.g., due to artists unable to travel because of war-related disruptions) flagged as a media-reported risk but not expected to materially affect District's overall growth trajectory given business diversification across categories.

Fuel price increases could raise last-mile delivery costs; impact on demand/margins depends on the quantum of increase and how much is passed on to consumers — historically (e.g., GST hike) cost increases have been passed on without much demand impact, but a drastic increase could have more impact.
Market froth/discount-driven demand in quick commerce is difficult to assess, creating uncertainty about the true health and sustainability of competitor growth rates.

subsections.label: Margin path / capital allocation framework
points: As food delivery/QC contribution moves to 5-6% margin, contribution margin is expected to trend up year-on-year.

No specific guidance given on how much of ad revenue as % of NOV/GMV is embedded in the 5-6% quick commerce margin assumption; management says this is still being discovered as quick commerce is a younger business than food delivery.
No cap in mind on ad revenue as % of GMV; will respond to market realities and reinvest any incremental ad income into growth if favorable.

subsections.label: Blinkit profitability unlocks
points: No further specific unlocks (cost or monetization) are being assumed beyond current execution trajectory to reach ~3% margin over three years; management believes continuing to execute as-is should get them there.

No cap in mind for ad revenue as % of GMV; will respond to market realities, potentially allowing margins/investment in growth to rise if ad income increases.

risk_register.risk: Sustained high competitive intensity in quick commerce
risk_register.note: Competitive activity hasn't meaningfully changed from the prior quarter; management maintains its stance while monitoring the situation.

risk_register.risk: Competitive intensity in tier 2/3 cities
risk_register.note: Competitive intensity is fairly high broadly wherever everybody operates, with different aggressive players in different markets — described as competitive everywhere.

risk_register.risk: Event cancellations affecting District's events category
risk_register.note: Media reports of artist travel disruptions (due to war) causing event cancellations not expected to impact overall District growth trajectory given business diversification.

risk_register.risk: Fuel price increases raising last-mile delivery costs
risk_register.note: Impact depends on quantum of increase and pass-through to consumers; historically passed through (e.g. GST hike) without major demand impact; a drastic increase could have more impact.

risk_register.risk: Market froth/discount-driven demand distorting true competitor growth
risk_register.note: Difficult to assess how much of market growth is genuine versus artificially inflated by discounts.

themes.label: Quick commerce growth guidance
themes.note: 60% NOV CAGR guidance reiterated for quick commerce over the next three years, built on assortment expansion, geographic expansion and demand densification.

themes.label: Competitive intensity
themes.note: Competitive activity remains high and largely unchanged across geographies including tier 2/3 cities, prompting flexible near-term guidance rather than fixed FY27 numbers.

themes.label: Quick commerce path to profitability
themes.note: Blinkit targeting ~3% steady-state margin over three years with no further unlocks assumed beyond current execution.

themes.label: Customer acquisition cost efficiency
themes.note: Lower CAC in quick commerce as competitors pull back on marketing spend, enabling strong MTU growth on flat fixed costs.

themes.label: Monetization strategy (platform fees & ads)
themes.note: Platform fees rising even as targeted discounts improve affordability for price-sensitive cohorts; ad revenue as % of GMV has no set ceiling and could expand margins or fund growth reinvestment.

themes.label: Growth vs margin trade-off philosophy
themes.note: Management optimizes for absolute dollar EBITDA growth rather than margin percentage, reinvesting incremental monetization gains into growth where ROI is favorable.

themes.label: Disclosure limitations
themes.note: Management repeatedly declined to disclose granular metrics (warehousing capacity trends, metro vs non-metro splits, top-20-city contribution, ad revenue composition) citing strategic reasons.

key_takeaways: Quick commerce guidance of 60% NOV CAGR over three years is based on assortment expansion, geographical expansion, and demand densification in existing cities, with potential entry into newer cities.

FY27 growth will not be 100% as previously indicated, expected closer to 70-80% per analyst calculation, though management declined to confirm a specific number, preferring flexibility to respond to market dynamics.
Company remains firmly on track for its 3,000 dark store guidance by March, with no further specific store guidance given beyond that.
MTU additions remain strong on flattish fixed costs because competitors have pulled back on marketing spend, giving the company extremely low customer acquisition costs.
Decline in orders-per-customer (from ~3.6 to ~3.35) is largely due to acceleration in new customer additions rather than a decline in customer retention.
Food delivery contribution per order saw a slight dip due to multiple sequential factors (AOV, last-mile seasonality, supply chain costs) with no change to long-term trajectory.
Management confident of maintaining pricing discipline in quick commerce despite prevalent market discounting, and does not see user/MTU penetration nearing saturation.
Hyperpure remains included within the company's overall billion-dollar profitability target despite being the smallest business.
pressing_questions: What margin of safety or room for error is built into the 60% CAGR guidance if competition remains as is or worsens, and what is the pecking order of user growth, frequency and AOV as growth drivers? (Management declined to provide detailed building blocks or projections with that accuracy.)
What proportion of consolidated advertising & promotion cost goes to Blinkit specifically? (Management stated this cannot be stripped apart across businesses.)
What is the breakup of business size (revenue/orders per day) between metro and tier 1/tier 2 towns? (Management declined to disclose this breakup intentionally.)
What was the warehousing capacity a quarter or a year back, to assess capacity build-out uplift? (Management declined to disclose historical warehousing capacity figures.)
Would the top 20 cities still represent about 40% of the 60%+ CAGR quick commerce guidance? (Management declined to give this breakup.)
What is the composition of ad revenue between SKU-stocking brands, checkout ads, and brand-page ads? (Management gave only a partial answer, noting non-paid ads are insignificant.)

SYNGENE.about: Syngene (established in 1993) as a Biocon subsidiary is India's first Contract Research Organization (CRO) which expanded later to be an integrated service provider offering end-to-end drug discovery, development, and manufacturing services on a single platform (CRAMS). Total research & manufacturing infrastructure for the company is spread across 1.9 million square feet across locations. [1]

quarters.summary: FY27 is framed as a year of transition, course correction and disciplined execution under new leadership. Management guides for a single-digit revenue decline in rupee terms for FY27 with EBITDA margins in the mid-20s, with H1 significantly weaker than H2 (H2 expected meaningfully stronger on CDMO and discovery ramp-up), and a return to profitable, sustainable double-digit growth expected from FY28 onwards as Mangalore utilization ramps, Bayview and Stelis are operationalized, and commercial execution is sharpened.

subsections.label: Revenue decline drivers
points: 16% YoY revenue decline in Q1 FY27 primarily reflecting absence of offtake from Zoetis in this quarter
Additionally experienced attrition of a few clients in the research services business
Attrition attributed to competitors offering commoditized services at lower cost; company chose not to compete on price and opted out of such low-margin opportunities

subsections.label: Margin performance drivers
points: Margin performance reflected impact of lower revenues together with foreign exchange hedge loss of INR 50 crores during the quarter
Impact partially offset by ongoing cost optimization program, including employee-related costs and other expenses
Cost optimization program started sometime in last fiscal (FY26) and continues this year

subsections.label: Exceptional items
points: Exceptional charge of INR 10 crores net of taxes related to termination benefits extended to employees in accordance with company-approved policy
Consequently reported PAT was negative INR 9 crores versus INR 1 crore PAT before exceptional items

subsections.label: Capex and investment
points: Capex of ~INR 70 crores during the quarter, primarily in Bayview facility and other investments across technology platforms, including automation and AI-capabilities
Company will continue investments through the year primarily in operationalizing Bayview facility, expanding capabilities and advancing new modalities

subsections.label: Cash balance dynamics
points: Net cash balance declined from ~INR 1,800 crores (prior year) to INR 1,541 crores; cash balance has a seasonal structure where Q1 (calendar year) sees advances received from customers which are utilized through the year, leading to a declining trajectory that picks up towards year-end
Nothing unique occurred this quarter versus the usual seasonal cash cycle
Company will continue to invest cash into the business per ongoing strategy

subsections.label: Margin outlook for second half
points: Margin improvement expected from cost-saving activities undertaken in FY26 and continued cost-saving initiatives this year
A couple of years back, steady-state margins were higher than mid-20s
Q4 has historically always been the highest-margin quarter for the company due to seasonality, aiding H2 margin appreciation
Bayview facility will not be capitalized during this fiscal year (capitalization per accounting policy), so there will be very minimal Bayview-related expenses in the P&L this year
Cost optimization on operating expenses and people costs is independent of Bayview capitalization

subsections.label: Next year margin view
points: Too early to comment on margins for next year (FY28); management does not expect a flattish margin to continue into next year given expected good growth improving margins

subsections.label: Zoetis/Librela demand trajectory
points: Zoetis revenues not completely zero but a very small percentage; Zoetis has inventory for the next couple of years as it has also seen a decline in its own sales
Company has certain delivery obligations to Zoetis this fiscal year, more weighted to the second half
Molecule not expected to be zero even in FY28; Zoetis expected to provide forecast for FY28 by end of this year

subsections.label: Pipeline conversion
points: New commercial organization requires gestation time between receiving RFPs and translating that into revenue
Company sees good green shoots on filling the Zoetis gap but expects to provide better visibility/color starting next quarter
Bayview facility: expressions of interest received, one or two converted into project-based CMO requirements in the U.S., but actual revenues will only start showing from next year

subsections.label: Discovery/Research services business
points: Management declined to give a specific Q1 growth number for discovery business beyond the 78%/22% split, noting discovery services need to differentiate further via new science and technologies to avoid commoditization and race-to-the-bottom pricing
Heavy focus on AI-led differentiation expected to drive turnaround by end of fiscal

Discovery services do not differentiate strongly between small molecule and large molecule opportunities internally; company believes it is well-distributed between both, though Syngene has a differentiated large-molecule discovery capability and takes a higher share of large-molecule discovery work versus other Indian companies
New areas like oligos, ADCs and bispecifics are increasingly coming to Syngene, offering high-value services with better revenue and margin mix; company is doubling down on these opportunities

subsections.label: CDMO business
points: CDMO reaffirmed as the primary long-term growth engine

Small-molecule CDMO (Mangalore) has had very low utilization in past years; good discussions and a few lock-ins secured for both commercial and clinical molecules; significant ramp-up in utilization expected this fiscal, continuing into FY28, driving small-molecule CDMO revenue growth

Mangalore opportunities are more direct manufacturing opportunities; focus also on integrated drug discovery and development so molecules move from discovery labs to development/manufacturing facilities to capture more value
Large-molecule CDMO: operationalizing Bayview facility by end of this year; discussions ongoing with prospective customers wanting to utilize the facility, expected to drive FY28 revenue growth

Stelis facility: customers already signed up; batches taken for a few customers; ramp-up happening this year and continuing into next year; most molecules at clinical or development stage, not yet a large-volume commercial molecule from Unit 3
Non-Librela CDMO demand for Bayview/Unit 3: discussions ongoing on both human health and animal health side; robust pipeline exists, with the key task being to convert pipeline into business

CDMO differentiation versus competition: very few companies other than Chinese and Korean players can offer what Syngene offers in large-molecule CDMO; in Indian context, Syngene is differentiated at scale, quality and capabilities
CDMO now ~20-22% of revenue mix per this quarter (per discussion in Q&A), though small vs large molecule split within CDMO was not disclosed

subsections.label: Clinical research / clinical trials business
points: Clinical trial activities are a small base currently but have grown significantly over the last year; difficult to discuss in detail due to low base
New leadership and new capabilities being added in translational research; strong growth expected starting this fiscal, becoming a significant part of business going forward
Differentiates Syngene from other Indian clinical research companies, many of which focus on BA/BE studies, while Syngene targets global Phase II/Phase III studies

Management declined to quantify future revenue share (e.g., ~20% of total revenue in 3 years) as other businesses will also grow; clinical business will grow in both absolute and percentage terms but exact proportion not quantified

Syngene has partnerships in countries like Australia and Europe to take trials into the clinic faster than possible in India, given long approval timelines in India for first-in-human, Phase I and Phase II trials

Analyst requested a dedicated presentation/webinar on the clinical trials landscape (enrollment geographies, regulatory pathways, data harmonization across countries); management agreed it is a good suggestion and noted a webinar was previously done with Dr. Mrinal in December (last year) and another may be done later this year

subsections.label: AI-enabled discovery platform (Syn.AI)
points: Continued strengthening of Syn.AI, the AI-enabled scientific platform for accelerating drug discovery services
Developed giga-scale virtual screening capabilities enabling larger molecule libraries to be screened and prioritized, accelerating identification of promising drug candidates
Advanced AI-driven de novo design capabilities, helping accelerate design and optimization of novel drug candidates
These investments aimed at enhancing productivity and improving speed to science, creating greater value for customers
AI integration across discovery workflow combines computational biology, machine learning and advanced data science with deep experimental expertise
AI and digital technologies expected to deliver greater customer value and strengthen competitive position going forward

subsections.label: Sustainability recognition
points: Recognized for the second consecutive year in Time Magazine and Statista's World's Most Sustainable Companies 2026 ranking, selected from more than 5,800 companies across 43 countries

subsections.label: Bayview facility
points: Bayview facility in the U.S. being made into a state of readiness; expected to be operationalized later this year
Prospective customers already visiting the facility, but customer lock-ins will happen only after operationalization, which gives customers confidence
Bayview will not be capitalized this fiscal year per accounting policy, minimizing P&L impact this year
Expanding global manufacturing footprint via Bayview positions Syngene as trusted end-to-end partner for biologics innovators

subsections.label: Mangalore facility
points: Had very low utilization in past years
Significant ramp-up in utilization expected this fiscal year, continuing into FY28

subsections.label: Stelis facility (Unit 3)
points: Customers signed up and batches taken for a few customers
Ramp-up happening this year and continuing into next year
Molecules mostly at clinical/development stage; no large-volume commercial molecule yet from Unit 3

subsections.label: Global footprint
points: Bayview facility in the U.S. expanding global manufacturing footprint and offering diversified geographic exposure
Partnerships in Australia and Europe to support faster clinical trial execution outside India
India-specific regulatory environment for clinical trials cited as slower than other parts of the world for first-in-human, Phase I and Phase II approvals

subsections.label: Commercial execution focus
points: Sharper market segmentation, greater customer engagement and more focused business development approach under new commercial leadership (Abhijit Zutshi)
Deliberate move away from low-margin, commoditized service opportunities where competitors undercut on price; company opts out rather than compete on cost
Focus on high-value, differentiated services rather than competing in a 'race to the bottom'

subsections.label: CDMO competitive positioning
points: In large-molecule CDMO, few companies globally other than Chinese and Korean players can match Syngene's offering
Having a U.S. facility (Bayview) provides advantage given tariffs and 'Make in U.S.' considerations, supporting discussions with customers on both human health and animal health sides

key_figures.label: World's Most Sustainable Companies ranking - companies evaluated
World's Most Sustainable Companies ranking - countries covered

subsections.label: Leadership transition
points: Kiran Mazumdar-Shaw has stepped in as Executive Chairperson to drive the strategic reset
Siddharth Mittal appointed Managing Director and CEO, bringing 13 years of experience at Biocon shaping strategic direction and transforming commercial/operational capabilities

Abhijit Zutshi, former Chief Commercial Officer of Biocon's Generics business, brought in to strengthen the commercial organization with sharper market segmentation, greater customer engagement and more focused business development

subsections.label: Strategic repositioning
points: Company had drifted towards a larger share of commoditized research services with limited differentiation and inevitable pricing pressure
Biologics manufacturing business became disproportionately dependent on a single large customer (Zoetis); loss of that business significantly impacted near-term financial performance
First priority: build a much stronger commercial engine, winning business, deepening customer relationships, expanding strategic partnerships across global biotech/pharma
Second priority: reaffirm CDMO as the primary long-term growth engine
Third priority: move up the value chain by expanding differentiated discovery capabilities, integrating AI across the discovery workflow

Fourth priority: invest in emerging scientific modalities and strengthen capabilities in translational science and clinical research to partner with customers from target identification through early clinical development
Large-molecule CDMO remains one of Syngene's strongest strategic differentiators, combining integrated biologics capabilities from cell line development to commercial-scale manufacturing
Current year characterized as one of rebuilding rather than maximizing growth

subsections.label: Partnership: Translational Health Science and Technology Institute (THSTI)
points: Signed MoU with THSTI, a premier institution under Department of Biotechnology, Government of India
Collaboration establishes operational partnership for early and late-phase clinical development, translational research and bioanalytical sciences
Will enable evaluation and execution of first-in-human and Phase I clinical programs, along with bioanalytical, biomarker and patient-based clinical research programs

subsections.label: International clinical trial partnerships
points: Syngene has partnerships in Australia and Europe to take molecules into the clinic faster than possible in India, given lengthy Indian regulatory approval timelines

subsections.label: Geographic diversification (Biosecure Act)
points: Biosecure Act and inclusion of certain Chinese companies on related lists seen as a great advantage, offering opportunity to shift molecules from China to India

subsections.label: Customer concentration / loss of Zoetis
points: Loss of business from a single large customer (Zoetis/Librela) has had significant impact on near-term financial performance
Reinforced importance of building a more diversified and resilient commercial portfolio
Zoetis has inventory for next couple of years amid its own sales decline; delivery obligations continue this fiscal, more in H2; molecule not expected to reach zero even in FY28

subsections.label: Commoditization / pricing pressure in research services
points: Drift towards commoditized research services where differentiation is limited and pricing pressure inevitable
Attrition of a few clients in research services business attributed to competitors offering services at lower cost; company chose not to compete on such terms

subsections.label: Foreign exchange
points: Foreign exchange hedge loss of INR 50 crores impacted Q1 FY27 margin

subsections.label: Regulatory environment for clinical trials in India
points: Indian regulatory landscape needs to change to hasten clinical trial opportunity in India; approvals for first-in-human, Phase I and Phase II take much longer than other parts of the world
Industry-wide effort underway to resolve these regulatory pathway issues; some government support and regulatory changes still required

subsections.label: Execution/gestation risk
points: New commercial organization needs time between securing RFPs and converting them into revenue, contributing to a slower near-term ramp

key_figures.label: Implied H2 EBITDA margin needed to meet guidance

subsections.label: Revision from prior guidance
points: Guidance revised down from previously broadly flat revenue expectation to single-digit revenue decline for FY27, driven by the impact of the absence of Zoetis contribution
Company is working to fill the Zoetis gap with other customers, but expects this to happen only by the end of the fiscal year

subsections.label: H1 vs H2 phasing
points: H1 to see significant impact; better visibility on both CDMO and discovery businesses expected in H2
Second half expected to be much stronger than first half

subsections.label: Return to growth
points: Actions this year (rebuilding, restoring commercial momentum, improving asset utilization, driving operational efficiency) expected to position Syngene for a return to profitable and sustainable growth from FY28 onwards
Aim is to get back to double-digit sustainable growth starting next fiscal (FY28)
Mangalore utilization ramp-up to continue into FY28, driving small-molecule CDMO revenue growth
Bayview and Stelis revenue contributions expected to show from FY28

subsections.label: Medium/long-term growth outlook
points: Management declined to quantify or give qualitative medium/long-term revenue growth guidance incorporating new facilities (Stelis, Bayview) and Mangalore utilization, citing it is too early given the new leadership team is still conducting a deep diagnosis
Requested patience of at least one quarter before providing more accurate guidance on these questions

subsections.label: Next-year margin commentary
points: Too early to comment on FY28 margins; management does not expect margin to remain flattish next year given expected growth improving margins

guidance_ledger.statement: For the full financial year, we do expect a single-digit decline in revenue in rupee terms
EBITDA margins in the mid-20s
H1 is where we will see a significant impact. In H2, we have better visibility on both CDMO as well as our discovery businesses
By the end of this fiscal, we expect these actions to position Syngene for a return to profitable and sustainable growth, which will be delivered from FY28 onwards
Our aim is to really get back to a double-digit sustainable growth, which we think we will be able to do starting next fiscal
This fiscal year itself, you will see a significant ramp-up in utilization. And the increase in utilization will continue in FY28, which will drive revenue growth in our small molecule CDMO business
We are looking at operationalizing Bayview... which will drive revenue growth in FY28
We see a ramp-up happening during this year and continuing into next year [at Stelis]
We do not expect the molecule to be zero even in FY28... Zoetis will come back by end of the year with their forecast for FY28
At this stage, I don't think we'll be able to quantify or give a qualitative guidance as well [on medium to long-term revenue growth with Stelis, Bayview, Mangalore]
It's too early to comment on the margins for next year... we do not expect a flattish margin to continue next year
It will become a larger part of our business, both in absolute terms as well as in percentage terms [but cannot quantify percentage]
Research services accounted for 78% of the sales, while CDMO accounted for the remaining 22% for the quarter
we do expect Q1 to have a more pronounced adverse impact of Librela destocking

quarter 1 and quarter 2 will have almost no Librela. There is some minor Librela volumes towards the end of the year... we have no incremental revenue plans for Librela beyond one small amount in the last quarter

Aspirationally, for sure, we definitely want to improve the margins... do we still have the aspiration to go towards the high 20s, maybe 30% margins? ... But as of now, we're guiding only for the year, and we're guiding it towards the mid-20s
we would expect to end '27 on a growth trajectory and the Librela effect will then have washed out... look beyond '27 for a more sustained and higher growth trajectory
I think it will grow around U.S. inflation at some level. But its expansion going forward will be determined by the nature of the strategic outlook and the new areas of expansion and opportunity

risk_register.note: Loss of anchor customer had significant near-term financial impact; biologics manufacturing business became disproportionately dependent on this single customer; delivery obligations and inventory dynamics continue to weigh into FY28

risk_register.risk: Commoditization and pricing pressure in research services

risk_register.risk: Foreign exchange volatility

risk_register.risk: Indian regulatory environment for clinical trials

risk_register.risk: Leadership transition execution risk

risk_register.risk: Librela destocking / single large molecule biologics client impact
risk_register.note: Continuing headwind expected to persist through Q1/Q2 FY27 with more pronounced adverse impact in Q1, washing out by end of FY27.

risk_register.risk: Geopolitical uncertainties

risk_register.risk: Middle East conflict - cost/logistics impact

risk_register.note: Management assesses tariff impact on Syngene as negligible; no material effect anticipated on business; RFPs continue to be received from prospective customers.

risk_register.note: Analyst raised macro headwinds in biotech funding; company did not quantify impact by vertical but expects growth across chemistry, biology/biotherapeutics, and translation/clinical legs going forward.

risk_register.note: Ability to pass on cost increases to customers is not one-size-fits-all; depends on customer-by-customer and contract-by-contract negotiation and nature of molecule/services.

themes.label: Librela headwind
themes.note: Absence of Zoetis/Librela offtake was the primary driver of the 16% YoY revenue decline in Q1 FY27, with continued impact expected through FY27 and into FY28.

themes.label: Leadership transition
themes.note: Siddharth Mittal takes over as MD & CEO with Kiran Mazumdar-Shaw as Executive Chairperson and Abhijit Zutshi leading a strengthened commercial organization; new team requests time to complete a deep diagnosis before giving fuller guidance.

themes.label: CDMO pipeline acceleration
themes.note: CDMO reaffirmed as primary growth engine, with Mangalore utilization ramp-up, Stelis customer lock-ins, and Bayview operationalization all expected to drive FY28 revenue growth.

themes.label: Margin guidance discipline
themes.note: Mid-20s EBITDA margin guidance reiterated despite a weak 12% Q1 margin, relying on H2 cost optimization, seasonality and revenue uptick to average out to mid-20s for the year.

themes.label: New modality capability build (ADC/peptides/biologics)
themes.note: Company doubling down on new-area molecules like oligos, ADCs and bispecifics coming into discovery pipeline, seen as offering better revenue and margin mix.

themes.label: Geopolitical/tariff risk
themes.note: U.S. tariffs, 'Make in U.S.' considerations and the Biosecure Act's inclusion of Chinese companies seen as advantageous for Syngene, supporting Bayview demand and potential shift of molecules from China to India.

themes.label: Commoditization/pricing pressure in discovery services
themes.note: Drift into commoditized research services led to client attrition as competitors undercut on price; company is deliberately repositioning toward differentiated, AI-led discovery services.

key_takeaways: FY27 is a year of transition for Syngene — a year of course correction, strategic renewal, and disciplined execution under a new leadership team.
For the full financial year, we do expect a single-digit decline in revenue in rupee terms and EBITDA margins in the mid-20s.
By the end of this fiscal, we expect these actions to position Syngene for a return to profitable and sustainable growth, which will be delivered from FY28 onwards.
Revenue from operations for the quarter was at INR 736 crores, a decline of 16% year-on-year, primarily reflecting the absence of offtake from Zoetis in this quarter.
Operating EBITDA for the quarter stood at INR 91 crores with an EBITDA margin of 12%.
Profit after tax, before exceptional items was INR 1 crore... reported profit after tax was a negative INR 9 crores.
We ended the quarter with a net cash balance of INR 1,541 crores.
Second, and this is very important, we are reaffirming CDMO as the primary growth engine of long-term growth.
Large-molecule CDMO remains one of Syngene's strongest strategic differentiators.
pressing_questions: On a base of FY27, could you give a medium to long-term outlook? What's the kind of revenue growth that we're looking at with these new facilities – Stelis, Bayview – coming in, and with Mangalore also currently underutilized? (Management response: 'At this stage, I don't think we'll be able to quantify or give a qualitative guidance as well.')

Is it fair to believe that, over a period of three-year time, this clinical trial revenue stream will be about 20% of the total company's revenue? (Management response: 'We cannot quantify in terms of percentage because other businesses will also grow.')

Since Bayview would be commercialized/capitalized next year, would we most likely see a flattish margin next year itself as well? (Management response: 'It's too early to comment on the margins for next year... we do not expect a flattish margin to continue next year.')

quarters.summary: FY26 closed with muted top-line growth of 3% YoY, though Q4 delivered strong 13% sequential growth. Management guided FY27 to broadly flat performance with EBITDA margins in mid-20s, a muted H1 (Librela destocking impact concentrated in Q1/Q2) followed by a meaningfully stronger H2, with FY27 positioned as a year of strategic reset and execution ahead of stronger growth from FY28 onwards.

subsections.label: Q4 Cost Drivers
points: Raw material costs decreased YoY due to business mix changes.
Staff costs increased due to earlier-year investments in people.
Other direct costs (power & utilities) increased due to new facilities at Bayview (US) and the biologics facility in Bangalore becoming operational.
Other expenses decreased due to cost optimization initiatives.
Hedge loss increased due to the difference between average and spot hedge rates.
Depreciation increased in line with plans due to addition of capacities at biologics manufacturing sites in Bangalore that became operational this year.
Interest expense declined as borrowing reduced in Q4 FY26 versus the same quarter last year.
Other income increased primarily due to higher cash and equivalent balances.

subsections.label: Exceptional Items & Tax
points: Government of India notified 4 labour codes consolidating 29 existing labour laws; company reassessed impact resulting in a gratuity remeasurement credit of INR20 crores net of tax.
Expenses of about INR25 crores net of tax recognized under exceptional items related to termination benefits extended to employees under an approved policy, part of organizational rebalancing.
Normalized effective tax rate changed due to change in profit mix across units.

subsections.label: Capex Allocation
points: Capex during the quarter was around $10 million; ~50% in research services (capability build and contractual obligations/dedicated centres) plus regular maintenance capex.
Nearly 40% of capex was in the CDMO business.
Remaining capex was towards digitization, automation and common infrastructure.

subsections.label: Margin Guidance vs Actuals Reconciliation
points: Company had cut FY26 EBITDA margin guidance to 22-23% in January but delivered 25%, driven by continued cost efficiency/frugality plus product/services revenue mix change versus anticipation, and some costs going into exceptional items.
Full year revenue came broadly in line with constant currency forecast/guidance given earlier.

Management reiterated mid-20s EBITDA margin guidance for FY27, factoring in expected utilization curve improvement on recently acquired/built sites; aspirationally wants to move margins toward high-20s/30% but is guiding only for the coming year at mid-20s.

subsections.label: CDMO Pipeline Build
points: Encouraged by acceleration in pipeline buildup in CDMO business.
At Unit 3 biologics facility in Bengaluru, increased client interactions from large pharma and emerging biotechnology companies during the quarter.

Commercial manufacturing in biologics is a long-cycle business: client engagement typically begins with process R&D, followed by development work, clinical batch production and ultimately commercial supply.
Seeing encouraging interest in integrated capabilities, supporting a healthy pipeline across different stages of the value chain.
Healthy pipeline of deal flows expected to translate into stronger growth from FY28 onwards, per Kiran's opening remarks.

subsections.label: Bayview Facility Pipeline
points: At Bayview biologics facility in the US, preparations progressing well and company actively engaging with prospective customers as it moves toward operationalization of the site this year.

subsections.label: CRO/CDMO Mix and Outlook
points: For FY26, mix was broadly two-third CRO business, one-third CDMO business, consistent through Q3 and Q4.
Mix expected to be directionally similar for FY27, with minor changes as the year evolves.
Company is focusing more on CDMO business, which management believes will provide more aggressive and sustainable growth (Kiran Mazumdar-Shaw).

subsections.label: Research Services Sub-Mix
points: Chemistry, the legacy foundation of Syngene, remains the biggest part of the research services business.
Biology and biotherapeutics form a growing part where Syngene believes it is well placed as a lead player in India.
Translation and clinical services are at a lower starting point currently but showing encouraging opportunities for growth.
Company expects growth across all three legs (chemistry, biology/biotherapeutics, translation/clinical) going forward.
Biotherapeutics seen as a differentiated capability playing into a high-growth part of the contract research market.

Translation and clinical research business expected to see significant expansion over coming years as clinical trials pick up in India and translational capability integrates more broadly with discovery capabilities.

subsections.label: Clinical Trials Vertical
points: Clinical trial revenue flow is an ongoing business tied to a global trial win communicated in Q2; the trial will pan out over a few years, contributing to revenue in this quarter and coming years.
Company is focusing more on the clinical trials business as a newly added vertical for FY27, though no separate quantitative outlook was broken out.

subsections.label: New Modality Capabilities
points: Global pharma/biotech pipelines increasingly shifting towards novel modalities such as peptides, antibody drug conjugates (ADCs) and oligonucleotides.

Industry estimates indicate these advanced modalities account for over 40% of clinical pipelines and are growing materially faster than traditional small molecules due to their ability to address complex disease targets.
This shift is driving demand for partners offering integrated end-to-end capabilities across these platforms.
Company invested ahead of the curve in strengthening capabilities in these modalities, building on existing biology and biotherapeutics discovery capabilities.
During the quarter, commenced operations at a state-of-the-art antibody drug conjugate (ADC) discovery laboratory designed to support early-stage research.
This ADC discovery facility complements and integrates with existing ADC development and manufacturing capabilities, enabling a seamless pathway from discovery through scale-up and production.

subsections.label: AI in Drug Discovery, Development & Manufacturing
points: AI implications on discovery, development, and manufacturing expected to be profound, though exact timeline and landing point uncertain; rapid changes already evident.

AI applications aim to improve timelines, improve predictability through modelling, reduce risk through enhanced predictability, and enhance innovation by finding new targets and improving target validation.
In clinical development, AI applications are being seen in patient recruitment, data management, and translational sciences to enhance predictability of drug discovery.
In manufacturing, company is already working with digital twins to enhance ability to manage and optimize manufacturing.

Syngene has invested in new capabilities including a team of AI scientists applying algorithms to enhance service offerings and create customer value; working in this arena with many companies in its customer base.

subsections.label: Gestation Period for New Capabilities
points: Building CDMO capacities requires qualification stages, trial batch runs and regulatory approval structures, typically taking 12, 18, or 24 months depending on the nature/state of readiness of the site.
Unit 3 took about 18 months to become operational and be capitalized.
Bayview is expected to go through initial trial runs; engineering batches and capitalization expected once regulatory approvals are obtained, though timeline cannot be commented on right now.

New capability enhancements in hard gel capsules, ADCs and peptides expected to contribute towards the pipeline build referenced by Kiran, contributing towards an exit into FY27/28 on a growth trajectory as Librela impact clears by end of FY27.

key_figures.label: Time taken for Unit 3 to become operational and capitalized
Typical timeline for capacity qualification/regulatory approval

subsections.label: Small Molecule Platform
points: Commissioned a new commercial-scale facility for liquid-filled hard gelatin capsules, strengthening oral solid dosage capability and enabling support for increasingly complex formulations with greater precision and reliability.

subsections.label: Large Molecule Biologics Platform
points: Expanded Bengaluru facility with the addition of a GMP bioconjugation suite, enabling fully integrated end-to-end manufacturing of antibody drug conjugates.

This capability brings monoclonal antibody production and GMP bioconjugation into a single site, helping accelerate development timelines while complementing existing strengths in payload and linker manufacturing.
Biologics manufacturing sites in Bangalore became operational this year, driving depreciation increase.

subsections.label: Unit 3 Capitalization
points: Unit 3 was capitalized at the beginning of Q1 FY26; costs of people etc. are now fully coming into the P&L.

subsections.label: Bayview Facility Status
points: Bayview facility impact is only partially in the P&L; facility not yet fully capitalized.
Company will update on Bayview's capitalization and forward plans as they progress.
Preparations progressing well and company moving toward operationalization of the Bayview site this year.

key_figures.label: Length of Bristol-Myers Squibb collaboration legacy
Future horizon of Bristol-Myers Squibb collaboration

subsections.label: Middle East Conflict Cost Impact
points: No disruptions to continuity of service and supplies on Syngene's ongoing business despite Middle East conflict-related developments; navigated successfully by the team in conjunction with partners.
Some cost increases seen in some areas, including price spikes in some inputs.
Uncertainty on how long the situation will continue and to what extent it may persist.
Company is reengineering distribution and logistics and reviewing costs, and engaging with customers and collaborators.

Contracts are not one-size-fits-all with regard to pass-through of cost increases; ability to pass on costs depends on customer-by-customer and contract-by-contract negotiation, and on the nature of the molecule and support/services required.
No material impact currently anticipated at this point in time; situation to be monitored as it resolves.

key_figures.label: S&P Global Sustainability Yearbook ranking in life sciences sector
TIME Magazine/Statista ranking - India pharma and biotech sector

subsections.label: Zoetis Follow-on Molecule (Lenivia)
points: Company does not currently have any participation in Zoetis's follow-on molecule to Librela (Lenivia) going forward.
Company did some clinical work for Zoetis previously, but in terms of ongoing commercial production discussions are underway with nothing confirmed beyond that at this time.

key_figures.label: Advanced modalities share of clinical pipelines

subsections.label: Bristol-Myers Squibb Partnership Extension
points: Extended long-standing partnership with Bristol-Myers Squibb through to 2035, broadening the scope of collaboration across the drug development life cycle spanning discovery, translational sciences, pharmaceutical development, manufacturing and clinical research.
Relationship legacy spans 28 years, with a new 10-year forward horizon enabling strategic thinking given evolving new modalities and AI's implications for discovery and development.
Extension provides a strategic framework for mid- and long-term planning to support Bristol-Myers Squibb's pipeline/portfolio evolution.

Management declined to comment on short-term revenue implications; historically the relationship has grown over the years but is already substantial in scale, and growth is expected to not be linear, potentially growing around US inflation level, with expansion determined by strategic outlook and new areas of opportunity.

subsections.label: Leadership Transition
points: Kiran Mazumdar-Shaw returns as Executive Chairperson at a pivotal point in Syngene's journey.
New team includes Siddharth and Abhijit coming in from Biocon Generics.

Decision plan has been in place for some time, with Peter Bains involved in the decision; belief that a full-time CEO presence in India was needed given the importance of close oversight for CDMO operational excellence.
Siddharth has played an important role at Biocon and understands the CDMO business given Biocon's manufacturing operations experience.
Abhijit brings strong commercial and business development experience, having built partnerships including with Viatris, Pfizer and Cuban partnerships, among others.
No external candidate evaluation was mentioned as considered; Kiran has worked closely with the new team for many years and expressed confidence in resetting and rebuilding the Syngene model.
Peter Bains served effectively as interim CEO during the transition.

subsections.label: ESG & Sustainability Recognition
points: Included in the S&P Global Sustainability Yearbook 2026, placing Syngene among a select group of leading companies globally and among the top 10 in the life sciences sector.
Recognized by TIME Magazine and Statista as one of the world's most sustainable companies, ranking number 1 in India's pharma and biotechnology sector and amongst the top 20 globally.

subsections.label: Cost Rationalization / Organizational Rebalancing
points: Termination benefits reflect rebalancing of the organization following earlier-year investments in people; staff costs rose due to those earlier investments, followed by rebalancing in some parts of the organization.
Management declined to comment further on how this rationalization will play out in the future beyond the margin guidance already provided.

subsections.label: Librela Destocking Headwind
points: Continuing impact from a single large molecule biologics client (Librela) is a key structural headwind weighed against steady growth of the underlying business.
Q1 and Q2 of FY27 expected to have almost no Librela revenue, with minor volumes towards the end of the year; no incremental revenue plans for Librela beyond one small amount in the last quarter.
Q1 FY27 expected to see a more pronounced adverse impact from Librela destocking versus other quarters.
Underlying business (excluding Librela) grew in high-single digits in FY26, per management; overall reported growth with Librela was 3%.
Librela headwind will continue to have effects through FY27, with the effect expected to wash out by the end of FY27, enabling an exit into FY27 on a growth trajectory.

subsections.label: Geopolitical Uncertainty / Middle East Conflict
points: Current geopolitical uncertainties cited as a factor behind the broadly flat FY27 guidance.
Middle East conflict-related developments have led to some cost increases and price spikes in certain input areas, with uncertainty about duration and extent.
No material impact currently anticipated at this point in time; company reengineering logistics/distribution and monitoring situation.

subsections.label: Biotech Funding Macro Headwinds
points: Analyst raised macro headwinds in biotech funding as a factor potentially affecting discovery services verticals (discovery, translation, clinical trials); company did not quantitatively break down the mix or impact by vertical but expects growth across all three legs going forward.

subsections.label: FY27 Outlook
points: Given current geopolitical uncertainties and near-term impact of Librela, company expects broadly flat performance for FY27.
EBITDA margins to be maintained in the mid-20s through disciplined cost management and sharper operational execution.
FY27 expected to start on a muted note with H2 FY27 meaningfully stronger than H1, as growth is weighted towards the second half as new contracts ramp up and business momentum improves.
Q1 FY27 expected to have a more pronounced adverse impact of Librela destocking.
FY27 characterized as a year of strategic reset and execution, with a healthy pipeline of deal flows expected to translate into stronger growth from FY28 onwards.
Bayview facility cost impact expected to be baked into the mid-20s FY27 EBITDA margin guidance.
Management continues to hold mid-20s margin guidance and does not comment on longer-term aspiration to reach high-20s/30% margins beyond stating it as an aspiration.
Company expects to end FY27 on a growth trajectory as Librela effect washes out, positioning FY28 for more sustained higher growth.

themes.label: Librela headwind
themes.note: Single large molecule biologics client destocking impact continues to weigh on growth through FY27, expected to wash out by year-end.

themes.label: New modality capability build (ADC/peptides/biologics)
themes.note: Investment ahead of the curve in ADC discovery lab, GMP bioconjugation suite, and hard gelatin capsule facility to capture shift towards peptides, ADCs and oligonucleotides.

themes.label: Margin guidance discipline
themes.note: FY26 margin beat prior cut guidance (25% vs 22-23% guided) on cost efficiency and mix, while FY27 guided flat at mid-20s despite aspiration for higher margins.

themes.label: CDMO pipeline acceleration
themes.note: Increased client interactions at Unit 3 Bengaluru and Bayview US facility as company pursues sustainable growth via CDMO focus.

themes.label: Strategic partnership deepening (Bristol-Myers Squibb)
themes.note: BMS partnership extended through 2035, broadening scope across the drug development lifecycle, providing decade-long strategic planning horizon.

themes.label: Leadership transition
themes.note: Kiran Mazumdar-Shaw returns as Executive Chairperson with new team (Siddharth, Abhijit from Biocon Generics) to strengthen CDMO operational oversight and business development.

themes.label: Geopolitical/tariff risk
themes.note: Management assesses Section 232 tariff impact as negligible while flagging Middle East conflict-related cost pressures with no material impact anticipated yet.

key_takeaways: FY26 closed with a muted top line growth of 3% year-on-year. However, it is important to note that Q4 delivered a strong 13% sequential growth, which reinforces our confidence that the underlying momentum of the business remains intact.

Given the current geopolitical uncertainties and the near-term impact of Librela, we expect a broadly flat performance for FY27 while maintaining EBITDA margins in the mid-20s through disciplined cost management and sharper operational execution.
We also expect to start FY27 on a muted note with H2 of FY27 to be meaningfully stronger than H1, with growth weighted towards the second half as new contracts ramp up and business momentum improves.
We believe that FY27 will be a year of strategic reset and execution with a healthy pipeline of deal flows that will translate into stronger growth from FY28 onwards.

Syngene generated a healthy INR521 crores in free cash during the year with a closing net cash balance of INR1,800 crores, reflecting the ongoing robustness of our operating model and disciplined execution.
A key highlight was the extension of our long-standing partnership with Bristol-Myers Squibb now extending through to 2035.
During the quarter, we commenced operations at our state-of-the-art antibody drug conjugate discovery laboratory, which is designed to support early-stage research.
We were included in the S&P Global Sustainability Yearbook 2026, placing us among the select group of leading companies globally and among the top 10 in the life sciences sector.

Now we are $419 million in '26, and we are guiding for flat growth. But I'm just saying when does it get higher, right? Is there -- what needs to kind of get us back on a growth path on revenue?

So is the wallet size bigger? ... So that obviously should translate into higher revenues than what you have received from Bristol in the past, yes?

TATATECH.about: Incorporated in 1994, Tata Technologies Limited is a global engineering services company offering Product Development and Digital Solutions.[1]

quarters.summary: Tata Technologies expects FY27 to be a "breakout year," guiding to strong double-digit organic revenue growth with services as the primary growth engine and margin expansion supported by scale, utilization, delivery productivity, AI-led efficiency and disciplined cost management. Management expects growth to accelerate in H2 FY27 versus H1, with quarter-over-quarter EBITDA margin expansion continuing despite Q2 wage hikes and temporary Germany headwinds.
