subsections.label: Margin drivers
points: Margin performance during the quarter reflected a combination of business mix and the deliberate upfront investments required to support the ramp-up of several large strategic wins.
Services business delivered a healthy 120 bps improvement in gross margins, partly offset by a 250 bps decline in Technology Solutions margins, resulting in an unfavourable mix impact.

Several large strategic engagements and full vehicle programs entered the mobilization phase during Q1, requiring upfront investments in talent, ramp-up, capability development, transition activities and delivery readiness ahead of revenues reaching steady state levels — creating near-term margin dilution but seen as critical to scaling multiyear programs.
Temporary headwinds within parts of the Germany business as certain customers work through restructuring and cost optimization initiatives.
Annual wage increase to be implemented in Q2; company expects to absorb the associated cost impact while still delivering sequential margin improvement through operational discipline and execution.
Management stated these factors may moderate the pace of margin expansion in the near term but do not alter confidence in the long-term opportunity.

subsections.label: Profitability quality
points: Q4 FY26 PBT included a one-time reversal of the provision related to the new Labour Code; excluding this nonrecurring benefit, underlying profitability improved meaningfully in Q1.

subsections.label: Balance sheet
points: Maintaining a strong balance sheet with robust liquidity is a key focus.
DSO remained stable at 97 days reflecting healthy collection efficiency; billed DSO increased sequentially while unbilled DSO declined.

subsections.label: Deal momentum
points: Continued strong traction in large strategic deal pursuits, reflecting customers' increasing willingness to entrust Tata Technologies with business-critical transformation initiatives.

The most significant win was the $100 million strategic engagement with Tenneco, expanding the relationship beyond traditional engineering services into a multiyear transformation program spanning engineering, digital technologies, AI-enabled processes and operational modernization.

Secured a strategic engagement with a leading North American industrial equipment manufacturer, expanding role across systems engineering, software engineering and embedded software development, leveraging AI-enabled engineering methodologies to improve development productivity, accelerate product realization and reduce time to market.
Deepened relationship with a leading global OEM through a Range Extender Vehicle program drawing on vehicle engineering, powertrain integration, validation and systems development capabilities.
Selected as preferred engineering partner by a leading off-highway manufacturer to support new product development and total cost of ownership optimization initiatives.

Continued strong progress on the strategically significant full vehicle development program with a leading Japanese automotive OEM discussed in the previous earnings call — notable because Japanese OEMs have historically been highly selective in choice of engineering partners, and this customer had no prior relationship with the company in this space.

Management indicated the list of deals cited is not exclusive — additional business has been closed and momentum carried into Q2, though specific customer names/sizes were not disclosed; more detail expected at end of Q2.
Customers are increasingly engaging Tata Technologies on larger multiyear programs combining engineering, software, AI and digital transformation capabilities.

subsections.label: Tenneco deal detail
points: Relationship with Tenneco in engineering has existed for about 6 years, established during the pandemic; Tenneco was a listed US company before Apollo bought them out roughly 3 years ago and has been accelerating significant restructuring and transformation.
Engagement spans engineering, program management, supply chain development, process optimization and digital transformation.
Deal was won last quarter; execution begins in Q2 FY27 and will ramp through the fiscal year, scaling toward the end of the calendar year and into next fiscal year.
It is a 5-year deal; majority of the deal is new business, with a small element of renewal of existing business wrapped in.
Company expects to discharge some existing capacity into the deal but will also bring in additional headcount during ramp-up, representing additional cost.

Management views the deal as a blueprint for what is likely to occur within the manufacturing extended supply chain, similar to how the BMW JV is viewed as a best-practice demonstration for standing up a GCC.

subsections.label: Demand drivers / propulsion mix
points: Over the last couple of years, investment in EVs has been tapering toward a more balanced propulsion mix; the company is propulsion-agnostic, currently delivering work packages and full vehicles across ICE, hybrid, plug-in hybrid and full BEV.

Demand had been compromised over the last ~18 months by tariff announcements and tapering EV demand in geographies like the United States; these headwinds are now starting to come to an end with greater clarity for customers, prompting renewed investment.

subsections.label: Full vehicle program pipeline
points: Management declined to give specific numbers on how many full vehicle programs remain in the pipeline beyond what has been closed, citing confidentiality, but reiterated that deal momentum continues to build.

key_figures.label: Technology Solutions segment sequential revenue growth
Anchor accounts contribution to services revenue
Embedded and software business growth QoQ (USD)

subsections.label: Automotive diversification
points: Automotive remains the largest vertical, but the business is becoming healthier and more diversified.
Automotive non-anchor revenue growth reflects continued progress in reducing customer concentration and expanding presence across global OEMs.
Contribution from anchor accounts to services revenue reduced to 48.9% in Q1, an improvement of 150 bps sequentially, enhancing resilience and creating a broader base for future growth.

subsections.label: Diversification beyond automotive
points: Aerospace and IHM together are becoming increasingly meaningful contributors to growth, providing further evidence that the diversification strategy is delivering results.

subsections.label: Embedded & software momentum
points: Growth in embedded and software business reflects increasing software content in vehicles and positions the company to capitalize on the long-term industry shift towards connected, autonomous and software-defined mobility solutions.

subsections.label: Technology Solutions mix
points: Sequential growth in Technology Solutions was led by education business (+9.1%), while product business degrew 2.6% primarily due to seasonality, as the product business typically experiences strong demand in the final quarter of the calendar year.
Disproportionate growth of education vs. product piece within Technology Solutions led to the decline in Technology Solutions margins (education business grew faster than product piece).

subsections.label: Aerospace outlook
points: Management has consistently messaged confidence in scaling Aerospace at a faster rate than automotive, driven by involvement in Airbus' strategic supplier outsourcing list, Tata Group investments in Aerospace, rising Southeast Asia/India air-travel demand, and associated MRO/assembly infrastructure investment.
Growth over the last 4-5 years represented a CAGR of about 40%, which management believes can continue; in the next 2-3 years, management sees a trend towards a $100 million target for Aerospace.
Growth is now broad-based, not predicated upon a single customer — cemented relationships with Airbus, key components of Airbus's supply chain, and propulsion players in North America.

subsections.label: Non-anchor / anchor growth outlook
points: Growth is relatively broad-based across both anchor and non-anchor accounts and across geography.
Uptick seen in Germany despite headwinds associated with performance challenges at some German OEMs; expected to continue.
Strong momentum in Scandinavia following securing a position within Volvo's consolidated strategic supply chain, with revenues from that customer scaling.
The Japanese OEM full-vehicle win is starting to provide opportunity to address Japan as a white-space geography, described as both a sizable and strategically important win.

Revenue mix of the company today is relatively balanced between three major regions: Asia, Europe and North America; company does not break out non-anchor contribution by US vs Europe at a sector level.

subsections.label: Europe growth engine
points: Europe has become an increasingly important growth engine for the business, supported by the successful integration of Es-Tec and growing presence across the region, reinforcing belief that the region will remain a significant contributor to future expansion.
Germany continues to strengthen from a strategic white space to one of the most important growth markets.

subsections.label: BMW TechWorks strategic relationship
points: BMW TechWorks continues to scale successfully and has crossed the milestone of 2,000 engineers.

While BMW TechWorks is not consolidated into Tata Technologies revenue, it remains an important strategic relationship that strengthens software-led engineering credentials, enhances access to next-generation mobility programs and reinforces the position as a trusted partner to one of the world's leading automotive manufacturers.

subsections.label: Japan white space
points: The Japanese OEM full-vehicle development program provides opportunity to address a geography where the company has historically not done a great deal of business.

subsections.label: Workforce management
points: Net reduction in headcount primarily reflects continued optimization of delivery capacity with a balanced approach towards managing the mix between full-time employees and outsourced resources.

As demand conditions continue to improve and deal momentum strengthens, the company remains disciplined and selective in hiring, focusing investments on strategic skill areas and growth priorities to align talent deployment with client demand while maintaining operational efficiency.

subsections.label: Talent retention
points: Improvement in voluntary attrition reflects the strength of the employee value proposition, investments in learning and career development, and opportunities to work on leading-edge engineering and digital transformation programs.

Building a future-ready workforce remains central to strategy as the company scales in embedded software, software-defined vehicles, cybersecurity, digital engineering and AI-led engineering services.

subsections.label: Outsourcing thesis
points: As the clock speed of technology change accelerates, customers are expected to increasingly shrink focus onto things core to their brand's DNA and increasingly look to outsource.

Propensity to outsource is positioned predominantly toward organizations like Tata Technologies that have demonstrated ability to take on turnkey responsibility for complete work packages and complete products.

Decisions to outsource a complete product are typically made at the top of the customer hierarchy (C-suite, Head of Engineering, CTO), and long-cultivated relationships give the company influence over both product engineering and outsourcing decisions.
Growth is broad-based, predicated substantially on full vehicle outsourcing, with halo effects extending into embedded software and digital.

subsections.label: China speed/cost value proposition
points: Value proposition in the full-product space is underpinned by ability to deliver 'China speed and China cost' at global automotive quality standards, built on more than a decade of China footprint experience, amplified by AI investments.
AI acts as a force multiplier for productivity, enabling things increasingly difficult for competitors and the industry at large.
Western OEMs typically develop vehicles in 36-48 months; the company has demonstrated ability to develop full vehicles and top hats in 18-24 months, evidenced by vehicles already on the road.

subsections.label: Learnings from new energy vehicle relationships
points: Prior work with new energy vehicle companies like VinFast and NIO (early China launch) exposed the company to significant product, process and speed-to-market innovation, but that space proved relatively volatile in demand — these customers invest in a product, test the market, and invest in follow-on products only dependent on success, creating inconsistency and unpredictability of revenue.

Over the last 2 years, focus has shifted to delivering the same value proposition to traditional OEMs, where demand is much more consistent and stable, allowing movement from one program to another with the same or increased headcount — improving the quality/predictability of revenue.

subsections.label: Cross-selling via Es-Tec / BMW
points: Cross-selling additional services to customers like Volkswagen and BMW is happening; momentum at BMW and VW has been pleasing.
Es-Tec acquisition completed in November of last year, so cross-selling there is less mature than at BMW.
Building the BMW partnership and Es-Tec due diligence allowed the company to sanity-check strategy with leadership teams of both companies, providing access and influence.
Increasingly good standing of BMW TechWorks (the BMW JV) is opening doors and influence being fully harvested.

Despite VW's ongoing restructuring/challenges, the Es-Tec platform is expected to support direct business through Es-Tec and VW's strategy to balance R&D concentration across geographies; part of the pipeline being built is consistent with this.

subsections.label: AI strategy
points: AI strategy is built around 4 priorities: transforming service delivery, building differentiated offerings, strengthening AI partnerships and delivering AI-ready talent, anchored on enterprise-wide adoption with trust and responsible AI built in from the start.

Through chromosome.ai, the company is codifying decades of engineering knowledge into repeatable frameworks, accelerators and solutions that improve productivity, quality, scalability and delivery speed.
AI is viewed as both a margin lever and a strategic differentiator, helping clients engineer better products faster and more efficiently.
Volume of work should not be seen as constant/shrinking due to AI — rather product cycles are accelerating, which is the real net impact of AI (per management).

subsections.label: Talent development
points: Through TechVarsity (internal university), delivered over 9,000 learning hours across GenAI, software-defined vehicles and cybersecurity this quarter, strengthening capabilities of over 2,000 employees.

Broader learning ecosystem delivered over 20,000 training hours to 3,000-plus employees this quarter; TechVarsity conducted 90-plus programs including focused technical learning across 40-plus niche skill areas.

subsections.label: Customer recognition
points: Tata Technologies was honored with JLR's Visionary Supplier Award in June 2026, recognizing its role in supporting JLR's enterprise and manufacturing transformation journey across multiple initiatives and programs.

subsections.label: Two-year strategic repositioning
points: Over the last 2 years, the company has deliberately built a more resilient, diversified and future-ready organization — strengthening the customer portfolio, expanding global footprint, deepening capabilities in high-growth technology areas, and positioning closer to where long-term engineering and manufacturing transformation spend is moving.

subsections.label: Macro / customer budget selectivity
points: External environment remains dynamic; customers continue to be selective in how they allocate engineering budgets, particularly across the global automotive value chain.

subsections.label: Germany / customer restructuring
points: Temporary headwinds within parts of the Germany business as certain customers work through restructuring and cost optimization initiatives.
Uptick seen in Germany despite headwinds associated with performance challenges at some German OEMs.

subsections.label: Wage increase cost impact
points: Annual wage increase to be implemented in Q2 FY27 is expected to create a cost impact that the company will absorb while still delivering sequential margin improvement.

subsections.label: Tariffs & EV demand tapering (easing)
points: Demand had been compromised over roughly the last 18 months by tariff announcements and tapering of EV demand in geographies like the United States; these periods are now starting to come to an end with greater clarity being provided to customers.

subsections.label: New energy vehicle customer volatility
points: Historical experience with new energy vehicle companies (VinFast, NIO) showed that space to be relatively volatile in demand, with inconsistent and unpredictable revenue as customers invest in a product, test the market, then decide on follow-on investment.

subsections.label: FY27 growth guidance
points: Based on current visibility, the company continues to expect strong double-digit organic revenue growth for FY27, with services as the primary growth engine and margin expansion supported by scale, utilization, delivery productivity, AI-led efficiency and disciplined cost management.

Management does not see a tapering of growth in H2; it expects growth to accelerate as the year progresses, with confidence having grown since the start of the fiscal year due to deal signings, momentum and customer engagement.

Growth is expected to be much greater in the second half of the year than in the first half; how growth spreads across quarters will depend on ramp-up factors (team mobilization and customer readiness/infrastructure investment).

subsections.label: Margin guidance
points: Rather than focusing on any specific margin milestone, management emphasizes greater confidence in the growth trajectory; given strong demand and deal momentum, it will seek to accelerate growth without compromising the ambition of quarter-over-quarter margin expansion.

Q2 profitability outlook is expected to continue to see quarter-over-quarter growth, which should absorb the impact of the wage increases; quarter-over-quarter margin expansion is expected to continue.

subsections.label: Aerospace outlook
points: Management expects continued strong Aerospace growth, trending towards a $100 million target for Aerospace revenue within the next 2-3 years, driven by Airbus supplier relationships, Tata Group Aerospace investment, and Southeast Asia/India air travel demand infrastructure investment.

subsections.label: Non-anchor/anchor and geography growth outlook
points: Growth outlook is expected to be broad-based across anchor and non-anchor accounts and across geography, expected to continue medium to long-term with possible quarterly spikes as different program opportunities are secured.

guidance_ledger.statement: Based on our current visibility, we continue to expect strong double-digit organic revenue growth for FY27 with services as the primary growth engine and margin expansion supported by scale, utilization, delivery productivity, AI-led efficiency and disciplined cost management.

guidance_ledger.metric: Growth cadence across FY27 (H2 vs H1)
guidance_ledger.statement: We do not see a tapering of growth in the second half of the year. We actually see growth accelerating as we move through the quarters of this fiscal... I expect growth to be much greater in the second half of the year than in the first half of the year.
The quarter 2 profitability outlook will continue to see quarter-over-quarter growth, which should take care of the salary increases... our quarter-over-quarter expansion would continue.

guidance_ledger.metric: Operating margin exit run-rate (18% by Q4)
guidance_ledger.statement: Rather than focusing on any specific margin milestone, we would emphasize that we are materially more confident on our growth trajectory... we would seek this opportunity to accelerate growth without compromising on our ambition of quarter-over-quarter margin expansion.

We have closed additional business, and we've taken that momentum into the second quarter. I'm not at liberty to give you too many details in terms of customer names or the size of these deals... hopefully, we'll be able to share more at the end of Q2.
I certainly think in the next couple of 3 years, I think that we can trend very successfully towards the $100 million target for Aerospace.
The growth that we've seen in the last 4, 5 years, which I think has represented a CAGR of about 40%... I think that is a CAGR that we can continue.

The growth outside of our anchor accounts is scaling and expanding faster than the growth with our anchor customers... we expect that to continue certainly medium to long-term. There may be some spikes during different quarters.
No new mention in this call; prior guidance was that within the next 2 to 3 years, the company has the opportunity to get to the $1 billion revenue North Star.
Our partnership with BMW continues to scale well. BMW TechWorks has now crossed a key milestone of 2,000 engineers and continues to strengthen our credentials in software-led automotive engineering.
We had guided that we expected Q4 to deliver more than 10% sequential revenue growth.
We had guided...alongside an operating margin exceeding 16%.
We expect to close more deals in the next 4 to 6 weeks.
We expect the strong growth momentum to continue [in Aerospace].

risk_register.risk: Customer selectivity in engineering budget allocation across the global automotive value chain
risk_register.note: External environment remains dynamic; customers continue to be selective in how they allocate engineering budgets, particularly across the global automotive value chain.

risk_register.risk: Germany business headwinds from customer restructuring/cost optimization
risk_register.note: Navigating some temporary headwinds within parts of the Germany business as certain customers work through restructuring and cost optimization initiatives.

risk_register.risk: Q2 FY27 annual wage increase cost impact
risk_register.note: As the annual wage increase is implemented in Q2, the company expects to absorb the associated cost impact while still delivering sequential margin improvement.

risk_register.risk: Tariff-related and EV demand tapering headwinds
risk_register.note: Demand had been compromised over the last ~18 months by tariff announcements and tapering EV demand in geographies like the United States; these periods are now starting to come to an end with clarity being provided to customers.

risk_register.risk: Volatility of new energy vehicle (NEV) customer demand
risk_register.note: Space represented by new energy vehicle companies like VinFast and NIO is relatively volatile in demand, with inconsistent and unpredictable revenue as follow-on investment depends on market success of prior products.

risk_register.risk: VW restructuring challenges
risk_register.note: Notwithstanding the challenges and restructuring that VW is going through, the Es-Tec platform is expected to still support business as VW balances R&D concentration across geographies.

risk_register.risk: Margin dilution from upfront investment in large deal mobilization
risk_register.note: Several large strategic engagements and full vehicle programs entered mobilization phase in Q1, requiring upfront investments creating near-term margin dilution ahead of steady-state revenue.

risk_register.risk: Geopolitical uncertainty / tariffs and trade actions causing OEM product-plan pauses/deferrals
risk_register.note: Uncertainty began easing in H2 FY26 as customer decision-making restarted meaningfully.

risk_register.risk: Middle East crisis impact on commodity supply chains (aluminium, plastics)
risk_register.note: Likely to impact pricing and supply ability for customers; expected to tighten discretionary spend if crisis extends, but not expected to impact capex or new-product commitments; impact modelled into guidance.

risk_register.risk: EV project write-downs at Stellantis, Ford, GM, Renault
risk_register.note: Management views these as balance-sheet cleanup, not indicative of reduced underlying new-product investment; propulsion portfolio now more balanced than 2 years ago.

risk_register.risk: European OEM announcements potentially headwind to ES-Tec/VW business
risk_register.note: Business plan currently being delivered consistent with plan underpinning the November ES-Tec acquisition despite these announcements.

risk_register.risk: JLR cyber-attack impact
risk_register.note: JLR has returned to the normal run rate maintained before the cyber-attack in September/October.

risk_register.risk: Chinese OEM competitive intensity
risk_register.note: Innovation and speed of Chinese OEMs observed at Beijing Auto Show driving competitive concerns in Europe and North America; expected to spur catch-up investment by non-Chinese OEMs.

risk_register.risk: Voluntary attrition
risk_register.note: Increased marginally to 16.2% from 15.8%, described as within manageable range reflecting normal movement in a gradually improving, competitive talent environment.

themes.label: Demand recovery / inflection
themes.note: FY27 poised to be a 'breakout year' with strong double-digit organic growth guided; tariff and EV-demand tapering headwinds of the last ~18 months are starting to end, prompting renewed customer investment.

themes.label: Full Vehicle Program wins
themes.note: Tenneco $100M multiyear engagement and continued progress on Japanese OEM full vehicle program; management confident in continued deal momentum though would not disclose further pipeline specifics.

themes.label: Margin expansion / operating leverage
themes.note: EBITDA margin up 10 bps QoQ to 16.1%, aided by services gross margin gains, but offset by Technology Solutions margin decline, ramp-up investments in large deals, and upcoming Q2 wage hikes.

themes.label: Portfolio & customer diversification
themes.note: Automotive non-anchor revenue up 56.3% YoY, anchor contribution to services revenue down to 48.9%; Aerospace and IHM increasingly meaningful contributors alongside geographic diversification into Europe.

themes.label: AI-led delivery transformation
themes.note: chromosome.ai and AI strategy (4 priorities) positioned as both margin lever and differentiator; management argues AI accelerates product cycles rather than shrinking work volume.

themes.label: Geopolitical & tariff risk
themes.note: Tariff announcements and EV demand tapering that compromised demand over the last ~18 months are starting to come to an end, providing clarity for customer investment decisions.

themes.label: ES-Tec / BMW JV integration
themes.note: BMW TechWorks crossed 2,000-engineer milestone with rising JV profit contribution; Es-Tec/BMW relationships enabling cross-selling into VW and BMW, with Europe revenue up 10.1% QoQ.

key_takeaways: For Q1 FY27, total revenue was $175.4 million, representing growth of 4.3% quarter-on-quarter and 25.2% year-on-year in constant currency.

Services revenue was $136.6 million, up 4.3% quarter-on-quarter and 24.4% year-on-year in constant currency, while Technology Solutions revenue was $38.8 million, growing 4.2% quarter-on-quarter and 27.9% year-on-year in constant currency.
Our operating EBITDA was approximately $28 million, translating into an EBITDA margin of 16.1%, an increase of 10 basis points sequentially.

The most significant win was our $100 million strategic engagement with Tenneco, which expands our relationship beyond traditional engineering services into a multiyear transformation program spanning engineering, digital technologies, AI-enabled processes and operational modernization.

Automotive non-anchor revenue reached $43.9 million, growing 6.7% quarter-on-quarter and 56.3% year-on-year, reflecting continued progress in reducing customer concentration and expanding our presence across global OEM.
Aerospace revenue grew to approximately $10.2 million, up 6.4% quarter-on-quarter and 38.1% year-on-year, while IHM revenue reached approximately $15 million.

Q1 revenue from Europe reached approximately $67.9 million, representing growth of 10.1% quarter-on-quarter and reinforcing our belief that the region will remain a significant contributor to future expansion.

Based on our current visibility, we continue to expect strong double-digit organic revenue growth for FY27 with services as the primary growth engine and margin expansion supported by scale, utilization, delivery productivity, AI-led efficiency and disciplined cost management.
pressing_questions: So, sir, largely, I wanted to understand that you reiterated double-digit organic growth for '27 after delivering a very strong number in Q1. So, does this imply some moderation in H2 or has the visibility actually improved further since the beginning of the quarter?
Are you seeing any OEMs shifting engineering budgets away from EV platform toward hybrid or ICE refresh program over the last 3 months? And how is the demand we are getting from Europe and U.S.

I just wanted to understand, I mean, what's really underpinning this because most of your peers who are the specialists seem to be singing quite a different tune. So, is this about your client portfolio being different, the service portfolio being different or are you being a lot more diversified with clients or is this about involvement in new hybrid platforms? What's actually the reason why your outlook seems very different compared to the peers?

You spoke about how it's turnkey engagements. So, can I think about the AI impact as not being really deflationary for you? Is that something that you're seeing? Because what kind of impact that you're seeing at all on pricing?

You announced the Tenneco deal and one full vehicle program in Q1. Now last quarter, you had mentioned that you were positive on closing 2 full vehicle programs in the next 8 to 12 weeks, out of which 1 you have already closed... could you give us a sense of how many such full vehicle programs do you have in pipeline now at this point in time that you are confident of closing in?

Given the investments that we are making on the wage hikes that are coming up in 2Q, do we see the same, are we sticking to the same guidance that we said in the past of 18% EBITDA margins by 4Q of the year? Or does that also change given in the light of the investment?
Can you provide the revenue contribution of Es-Tec in Q1 FY27? I think I missed this.
Can you provide the absolute numbers for this quarter for the software solutions [8.5% QoQ growth]?

quarters.summary: Tata Technologies delivered Q4 FY26 revenue growth of ~12.4% reported (12% CC) and EBITDA margin of 16%, beating prior guidance of >10% sequential growth and >16% operating margin. Management guided for FY27 double-digit organic constant-currency top-line growth (excluding ES-Tec inorganic contribution) and an exit operating margin run-rate exceeding 18%, driven by operating leverage, portfolio mix improvement, disciplined execution, and increasing BMW JV contribution. Growth is expected to be broad-based, with H2 FY27 likely faster than H1, though quarter-to-quarter consistency is expected; guidance is based on existing order book/pipeline, not assuming demand-environment improvement.

subsections.label: Q4 Performance vs Guidance
points: Company had guided Q4 to deliver >10% sequential revenue growth and operating margin exceeding 16%; both commitments were delivered.
Reported revenue growth of 15.1% exceeded the ~10% guidance shared last quarter.
Performance reflects a full 3-month contribution from ES-Tec compared with just 1-month in the prior quarter.

subsections.label: Exceptional Item / Labor Law Provision
points: A one-time exceptional expense of INR 140 crores was recorded in Q3 FY26 related to provisions for employee benefits following changes introduced under India's new Labor Law.

Upon further assessment and greater clarity on implementation, the company determined the actual impact would be lower than initially estimated, leading to reversal of INR 56 crores in Q4, resulting in a one-time exceptional gain.

subsections.label: Balance Sheet & Cash Flow
points: Balance sheet reflects strong financial health with solid cash position, robust liquidity, and favourable DSO level.
Collection efficiency improved during the quarter, with both billed and unbilled DSO improving.

subsections.label: Capital Allocation
points: Board recommended final dividend plus a proposed special dividend, taking total FY26 dividend to INR 11.70 per share, in line with dividend paid last year.
Both final and special dividends are subject to shareholder approval at the forthcoming AGM.

subsections.label: BMW JV Profit Anomaly
points: The sequential dip in BMW JV share of profit (from ~INR 7 crores to INR 6.5-6.6 crores) was described as a one-quarter phenomenon due to a true-up of whole year expenses in Q4, not a degrowth trend.
Management expects the JV contribution to return to its prior growth run-rate after this one-time true-up impact.

subsections.label: Full Vehicle Program Pipeline
points: Large system-level awards and Full Vehicle Programs were largely absent from the market during FY25 and H1 FY26 due to geopolitical uncertainty, tariffs and related trade actions causing OEMs to pause, defer, or re-sequence product plans.
As uncertainty eased in H2 FY26, customer decision-making restarted meaningfully; today there is visibility into multiple Full Vehicle Programs across the pipeline.
These are multi-year, multi-domain programs, not point solutions.

Company does not view a full vehicle program as a stand-alone revenue stream but as a strategic wedge — an entry point to embed deeply into customer's product life cycle and expand systematically across engineering, embedded software, manufacturing, digital continuity, and ongoing transformation services.

subsections.label: Q4 Deal Wins
points: Long-term strategic engagement with a North American commercial vehicle OEM to deliver end-to-end expertise across PLM, testing and quality assurance, MES, and project management.

Collaboration with a European automotive OEM to design, develop, and integrate advanced comfort electronics features across multiple vehicle programs, spanning Systems Engineering, Software Development, and Integration, enhancing In-Vehicle User Experience and enabling scalable deployment across current and future platforms.
Partnership deal with a European automotive OEM to provide supplier quality and coordination support, focused on strengthening supplier governance and quality execution.

Multi-year engagement with a Tier 1 automotive supplier to superscale a previously secured global engineering centre, positioning the company as a strategic long-term partner and accelerator for upcoming pipeline.

subsections.label: April 2026 Deal Wins
points: Large multi-year partnership with a European luxury automotive OEM to own their enterprise PLM service transformation and operations across all product domains, including engineering, manufacturing, supply chain, purchasing, and IDT.

Full-Vehicle Program with a leading Japanese automotive OEM, marking entry into the Japanese market at meaningful scale and strengthening Asia footprint; reinforces full-vehicle engineering credentials and validates ability to partner with global OEMs on large, complex programs across geographies.

subsections.label: Demand Drivers / Cadence
points: Growth in Q4 was broad-based rather than driven by a single customer or program.

OEMs are looking for partners who can deliver China-like speed and cost efficiency while meeting global quality, governance, and reliability standards; Tata Technologies increasingly recognized as one of the few players who can do this at scale.
Guidance for FY27 growth is driven by the order book and probability-adjusted pipeline including deals in process of closing, not factoring in any improvement to the demand environment.
Management expects growth cadence to be consistent across quarters, though H2 FY27 is likely to grow faster than H1 given a strong signings period and expected deal closures in the next 4-6 weeks.

key_figures.label: Aerospace and Industrial Heavy Machinery growth QoQ

subsections.label: Automotive
points: Automotive showed renewed momentum with non-anchor customers growing meaningfully faster, driven by increased activity across multiple European and global OEMs.
JLR returned to the normal run rate maintained before the cyber-attack; new deals secured across both Anchor accounts and automotive non-Tata Group accounts.

subsections.label: Aerospace & Industrial Heavy Machinery
points: Aerospace and Industrial Heavy machinery continued to scale, reinforcing the diversification deliberately built over the last 2 years.
Growth underpinned by successful execution of key projects across service lines.

Aerospace business propelled by involvement in the EMES3 program at Airbus; also working with propulsion/engine manufacturers in North America and growing relationship with Air India as it builds its MRO footprint in Bangalore.
Airbus is a flagship account, but growth is described as relatively balanced, not solely reliant on Airbus.

subsections.label: Technology Solutions / Products / Education
points: Technology Solutions business saw 12% sequential expansion (CEO) / segment reported INR 353 crores revenue led by strong education performance (CFO).
Products business declined 10%, coming off a seasonally strong Q3 and reflecting normal phasing of customer PLM budgets.
Education business delivered a strong finish to the year on the back of improved demand traction and steady execution across programs.

subsections.label: Portfolio Mix / Embedded Software
points: Focus on Embedded Software and Services has improved portfolio mix; company now uniquely positioned to address Mechanical, Digital, and Embedded requirements of customers.
Segment mix continued to improve with strengthening presence and strong growth across Aerospace and IHM verticals; strong growth momentum expected to continue.

subsections.label: Customer Concentration
points: Top 20 customers now make up almost 88% of business, reflecting reinforced commitment to strategic customers.
Real influence at C-suite level manifesting in large outsourcing projects, particularly full vehicle programs, affording influence across entire manufacturing customer requirements.

subsections.label: AI Strategy / Chromosome AI
points: Company accelerating deployment of AI across the delivery model, including Generative and agentic AI, to improve productivity, consistency, and predictability across complex programs.
AI is described as a core execution enabler, helping compress cycle times, improve quality, and run large multi-geography programs with greater confidence.
Clear focus areas established to embed AI across the automotive NPI value-chain, spanning engineering, manufacturing, supply chain, and aftermarket.

Proprietary AI platform, Chromosome AI, acts as an orchestration layer across product development processes, integrating AI seamlessly into each stage of the life cycle to enable workflow automation, fast decision-making, and cross-functional collaboration across programs and geographies.

Chromosome AI designed to deliver tangible outcomes: improving engineering efficiency, reducing costs, compressing product-development timelines, while providing a scalable foundation for sustained multi-year growth from digital and AI-led engineering services.
AI deployed across all delivery LOBs and enabling functions with fairly aggressive targets on unit-cost of delivery in each area, factored into the margin walk over the next 12 months.

subsections.label: Talent / AI Readiness
points: Focused learning programs rolled out in areas such as Gen AI, Software-Defined Vehicles and Cybersecurity to accelerate capability building in next-generation skills critical to growth.
More than 50% of engineering workforce is now AI-ready, positioning the company to drive innovation and deliver greater value as the technology landscape evolves.

subsections.label: Capacity / Delivery Engine Investment
points: Deliberate decision earlier in the cycle to protect and strengthen the delivery engine and continue investing through the downturn rather than optimizing for short-term margins, reflected in headcount net addition.
As demand conditions continue to improve, hiring will remain selective and disciplined, focusing on strategic areas aligned with growth priorities.

subsections.label: Talent & Attrition
points: Voluntary attrition increase over the trailing 12 months is described as marginal and within a manageable range, reflecting normal movement in a gradually improving and competitive talent environment.
Continued focus on employee engagement, career progression, and targeted retention initiatives; confident in ability to manage attrition effectively into FY27.

subsections.label: Skilling Programs
points: TechVarsity, the in-house technical learning platform, reached an important milestone during FY26 delivering technical modules to unique employees covering approximately 85% of the workforce.
Focused learning programs rolled out in Gen AI, Software-Defined Vehicles and Cybersecurity to accelerate next-generation skill capability building.

subsections.label: Geographic Broad-Basing
points: Large deals were broad-based not just sectorially or by client but also geographically: one PLM deal was in the United States, another in Europe, and the Full-Vehicle deal in Japan.
Company sees developing traction across almost every country where it has a presence.
Improvement being seen in almost every geography, factored into the budget for the year; forecast for H1 of the year consistent with this trend.

subsections.label: Japan Entry
points: Full-Vehicle Program win with a leading Japanese automotive OEM marks entry into the Japanese market at meaningful scale, further strengthening Asia footprint.

Japanese OEMs have very high standards and expectations for partners; being entrusted with full vehicle program responsibility (including a top hat and adjustments to an existing platform) seen as proof the value proposition is resonating across the market.

subsections.label: China Market Awareness
points: Management notes innovation and speed of Chinese OEMs (observed at Beijing Auto Show) driving competitive concerns in Europe and North America.

Company is involved in the Chinese market, has understanding of developments there, and is working with Chinese companies; believes it is well positioned to support customers in Europe, North America, and Japan to resist competition from Chinese OEMs and their supply chains.

subsections.label: BMW Joint Venture / ES-Tec Acquisition
points: Germany was highlighted as a strategic gap in the portfolio at IPO; this has now been firmly addressed through the BMW joint venture and the ES-Tec acquisition.
Over the past 18 months, company built a structurally more resilient and diversified business, anchored by improving mix and addition of marquee global OEMs such as BMW, Volkswagen, and Airbus.
Post-merger integration plans with ES-Tec are on track; CEO and CFO visited Wolfsburg to assess cross-sell opportunity at VW and synergies within the Tata Technologies customer base.
Business plan committed to by ES-Tec is being supported by both teams; business has already been won and further growth is being pursued.

Synergies being pursued in two ways: ability to cross-sell into VW specifically, and ability to extend portfolio of services into existing customer base; tangible progress and proof points demonstrated on both.
Despite announcements from some European OEMs that could otherwise pose a headwind, the ES-Tec business plan is being delivered consistent with the plan underpinning the November acquisition.
BMW JV headcount and revenue continue to point in a positive growth direction.

subsections.label: Geographic Diversification / German Market
points: German OEMs have traditionally surrounded themselves with local engineering and IT-service providers and been reticent to embrace contribution from India-based organizations; this is changing.

The BMW announcement made 18 months ago is seen as a signal to the market; company is in advanced discussions with a number of OEMs and Tier 1s in the German market about diversifying and balancing delivery topology to include significant India presence.

subsections.label: Focus / No New Verticals
points: Board strategy discussions consistently conclude there is more than enough headroom in Automotive, Industrial Heavy Machinery, and Aerospace to satisfy growth aspirations; no plans to diversify into other industry verticals currently.
Staying laser-focused on these verticals is viewed as enabling greater relevance to customers and faster growth.

subsections.label: $1 Billion Revenue North Star
points: Company's North Star revenue target remains $1 billion.

Plan is to get back to double-digit revenue growth this year, sustain it next year, and complement with 1 or 2 inorganic transactions; management believes this could be achieved within the next 2 to 3 years.

subsections.label: Tariffs / Geopolitical Uncertainty
points: Through much of FY25 and H1 FY26, geopolitical uncertainty and impact of tariffs and related trade actions led many automotive and Industrial Heavy Machinery OEMs to pause, defer, or re-sequence product plans, causing large system-level awards and Full Vehicle Programs to be largely absent from the market.
Management expects a catch-up in investment by European and North American OEMs as they resist competition from Chinese OEMs.

subsections.label: Middle East Crisis / Commodity Supply Chains
points: Management flagged the likely impact of the Middle East crisis on commodity supply chains, particularly the supply of aluminium and plastics, which is likely to affect pricing and supply/build ability for customers.
Expects discretionary spend among customers to tighten if the Middle East crisis continues to extend, though this is not expected to impact capex or new-product commitments.
Company has modelled the impact of the Middle East situation and factored it into guidance; confident the indirect impact will not undermine double-digit growth expectations for the year.

subsections.label: EV Write-downs / OEM Balance Sheet Cleanups
points: Large EV project-specific write-downs noted at Stellantis, Ford, GM, and Renault over past 4-5 months.

Management view is that these should not distract from the more telling trend of latent demand to invest in new products building up after a period when new-product investment was paused amid tariff-related uncertainty.
Portfolio of propulsion systems now more balanced compared to 2 years ago when the industry was 'all in on EVs'.

subsections.label: European OEM Announcements
points: Announcements from some European OEMs could, in other circumstances, have a headwind effect on ES-Tec/VW-related business, but the business plan is currently being delivered consistent with the plan underpinning the November acquisition.

subsections.label: JLR Cyber-Attack Impact
points: JLR anchor customer had a cyber-attack event in September/October (prior period) impacting run-rate; JLR has now returned to the normal run rate maintained before the cyber-attack.

Growth is expected both inside and outside the Tata Group, informed by knowledge of cycle plans, priorities, and influence in customer decision-making.
Cadence expected to be consistent across quarters, with H2 FY27 likely faster than H1 given signings pipeline.

key_takeaways: Q4 revenues grew by nearly 12% quarter-on-quarter in constant currency, with Services showing a similar step-up and margins improved sequentially - reflecting operating discipline and the early benefits of operating leverage as volume scaled.

This performance marks a clear inflection point for the business after a mixed first half, and importantly, the growth we saw in Q4 was broad-based rather than being driven by a single customer or program.
Today, we have visibility into multiple Full Vehicle Programs across our pipeline. Two of these were closed during Q3 and Q4, and we expect at least another 2 to close over the next 8 to 12 weeks.

We continue to expect double-digit organic top-line growth, excluding any inorganic contribution from ES-Tec, and we expect to exit FY27 with an operating margin run rate that exceeds 18%, driven by operating leverage, portfolio mix improvement, and disciplined execution.
From a profitability standpoint, our EBITDA margin for the quarter came in at 16%, representing a roughly 200 basis points improvement from Q3.

Our Board has recommended a final dividend of INR 8.35 per share for FY26, representing a payout of 62%. In addition, the Board has proposed a special dividend of INR 3.35 per share, taking the total dividend for the year to INR 11.70 per share, in line with the dividend paid last year.
For the fiscal 2026, the business generated free cash flow of INR 742 crores, representing a healthy EBITDA-to-FCF conversion of 87%.
In the last 4 years, our Aerospace revenues have grown 8x and is now at over $40 million in terms of annual run rate.

UJJIVANSFB.about: Ujjivan Small Finance Bank Limited is a mass market focused bank in India, catering to financially unserved and underserved segments and committed to building financial inclusion in the country. It started its operations as Ujjivan Financial Services Limited, a Non-Banking Financial Company in 2005 with the mission to provide financial services to the ‘economically active poor’ who were not adequately served by financial institutions. [1]

quarters.summary: This call was called at short notice primarily to address the early retirement of MD & CEO Mr. Sanjeev Nautiyal due to health reasons and the transition to Ms. Carol Furtado as Interim MD & CEO (subject to RBI approval); management reiterated that the bank remains on track to meet its FY27 guidance and growth plans, with no change to previously communicated strategy, and asset quality trends are tracking better or in line with Q1 performance with no material El Nino/West Asia crisis impact seen so far.

subsections.label: Loan book and asset quality
points: Performance across loan book growth and asset quality has resulted in a pristine and diversified loan book.
Q1 loan book growth of approximately 29% year-on-year with GNPA at 2.2% is testament to continued execution.
Strategic priority of diversifying the loan book has resulted in the secured book share growing past 50%; diversification strategy is well on its trajectory.

subsections.label: Deposits and cost of funds
points: Even though the market has been under a lot of pressure on the deposits front, the bank has been able to grow the CASA book at a healthy 38% year-on-year with overall cost of funds at 6.9% for Q1.
Growth has been funded with due care and at minimal cost.

subsections.label: MD & CEO transition
points: Mr. Sanjeev Nautiyal tendered early retirement as MD and CEO due to continued health concerns; he had not been keeping good health since mid-July, worked from home for a few days, then was on leave till the day before the call.

The Board took up the development and, after due consideration, accepted his early retirement request; the Board places on record its appreciation for his valuable contributions and stewardship during his tenure.
The Board has requested Ms. Carol Furtado, Executive Director, to take over as Interim MD and CEO, subject to RBI approval.

Carol Furtado is described as a seasoned banker with over 3 decades of extensive experience across business, strategy, operations, people and institutional functions; a key member of the leadership team that built Ujjivan; recognized for developing leaders, empowering teams and building a culture of ownership and accountability.
The NRC (Nomination and Remuneration Committee) has been mandated to search for a successor for Mr. Nautiyal.

Board and management assured stakeholders that the bank operates with strong governance standards, robust internal controls and a highly experienced management team, and that strategic direction, business priorities and execution capabilities continue to deliver on plans.
There is no material factor apart from Mr. Nautiyal's health for his sudden exit; management confirmed there is no issue with regard to business strategies or the working of the bank.

Mr. Nautiyal had an unexpired term of nearly about a year and had not expressed any intention not to seek a second term, so the Board did not feel the urgency for succession planning at that point; management will keep more robust succession planning in mind for future eventualities, referencing past leadership instability (compared to HSBC/UMB by an analyst).

Search process for successor: originally planned to start around October/November, but due to the early retirement, the search process is being started quickly; management is hopeful to complete the process to submit names to RBI in about 3 to 4 months.

After names are submitted to RBI, assuming a cooling period, it would take additional time (analyst estimated at least ~6 months) for a new candidate to join; management will factor this while identifying candidates, and it is early to say more at this stage.
The bank will definitely consider internal candidates for the MD role; Carol Furtado is considered a serious candidate and has expressed her desire to be a candidate for the regular MD position.
Desired profile for external candidates is still being worked out and will be shared later.

No further capital raise timeline change communicated as a result of the leadership transition; strategic diversification and the SFB-to-universal-bank transition journey continue without alteration, though management did not comment on a specific timeline for approaching RBI regarding transition to universal bank.

subsections.label: New leadership hire
points: Announcement of the joining of Mr. Vikas Agarwal as Business Head, MSME; he is a Chartered Accountant and seasoned banker with over 25 years of experience across MSME, business banking, retail banking, credit, product development and distribution.

subsections.label: Capital raise
points: Board approval to raise capital already exists; even if the capital raise were to be delayed due to the management change, it will not have any impact on growth momentum over the next 2-3 quarters or on FY27 performance.
The bank remains well capitalized and committed to its growth plans for FY27.

subsections.label: El Nino / weather monitorable
points: In the Q1 earnings call, management had flagged that more than the West Asia crisis, the El Nino impact would be a key monitorable from an asset quality and growth perspective.
Asset quality trends on both secured and unsecured businesses have tracked better or in line with Q1 performance, with no deviations observed as of now.
Management confirmed there is no major impact seen from El Nino relative to earlier expected trends/implications — 'Nothing. Absolutely nothing.'

subsections.label: Leadership transition risk
points: Sudden/abrupt nature of the CEO exit raised concerns among analysts about leadership instability, referencing prior instances at the bank.
Management acknowledged the concern and committed to more robust succession planning in future, though no specific new Board-level process was announced at this stage.

subsections.label: FY27 guidance reaffirmation
points: The bank remains on track to meet its FY27 guidance; the Ujjivan team is committed to delivering strong performance in FY27 and beyond with no change to the strategy previously outlined and communicated.
Post Q1 performance retains momentum both on business as well as strategic spends planned for FY27.

Festive season looks promising, backed by capacity additions supported by robust domestic economic performance; this will be further augmented by a brand campaign poised for launch during the festive season.
On the MSME front, the bank is proceeding as per what was planned for this financial year; guidance terms will be met, with more details to be shared in the Q2 earnings call.
Even if the capital raise is delayed due to the management transition, there will be no impact on FY27 performance; the bank remains well capitalized and committed to its FY27 growth plans.

Strategic diversification (including the SFB-to-universal-bank transition journey) remains well on its trajectory and is not being altered by the leadership transition, though no specific timeline was given for approaching RBI on universal bank transition.

quarters.summary: Ujjivan SFB delivered steady Q1FY27 business growth with diversified loan book growth, stable asset quality, and raised its FY27 ROA guidance to 1.8-2% (from earlier levels) while lowering credit-cost guidance to 0.9-1% of average total assets; full year opex is now guided lower at ~6.4% of average assets, with capacity-building spend (~INR250 crores) starting from late Q1 and building through the remaining quarters. Management remains confident of achieving FY27 asset growth of 25% and maintaining secured-book mix guidance of 56% by March'27, even as it stays watchful of funding cost pressure, competitive intensity in CASA mobilization, and weather-related/macro risks.

subsections.label: Opex commentary
points: Operating expenses remained well managed quarter-on-quarter, while personnel cost increase reflects salary increments effective from April 26, hiring and towards gratuity and leave encashments.
Other expenses were lower sequentially on account of lower business generation expenses and lower CSR expenses.
Capacity building expenses (branch opening, branding, tech and analytics capabilities) started kicking in from late Q1 and effect would be seen over remaining quarters.
Deferred commencement of expenses, coupled with ongoing efficiency gains, will result in full year opex being lower than earlier planned at around 6.4% of average assets.
Not much of the INR250 crore capacity-building spend was incurred in Q1, which supported the quarter's higher profits; spending started in June and will build up in coming quarters.
Going forward (beyond FY27), investments would be slightly lesser leading to year-on-year improvement in opex ratio as efficiencies kick in, though exact figures not yet shared.

subsections.label: NIM/Cost of funds
points: Cost of funds continued its downward trajectory during the quarter.
Repricing benefit on borrowings is largely exhausted; cost of funds expected to remain at current level or slightly elevated with only a few bps movement either way.

No significant increase in cost of funds expected going forward due to availability of instruments such as IBPC, refinance, and securitization which were not used in Q1 but will be used to keep it stable.
Yield support expected from MFI doing well along with higher-yielding segments such as gold, two-wheeler, used car, and micro mortgage, sustaining NIM guidance given at the start of the year.

subsections.label: Liability strategy
points: Bank effected rate increases in June on key buckets in line with intended ALM outcome amid tight liquidity.
Bulk deposit ratio at about 30%, guiding factor is to keep it around 30% through the year using various interventions.
Retail TD currently cheaper than bulk TD this quarter, and bank is gaining momentum in retail TD, planning to continue this.

subsections.label: Affordable housing & micro mortgages
points: Affordable housing and micro mortgages recorded strong growth, underscoring resilient customer demand and effective execution across key markets.
Affordable housing distributed through 581 branches and micro mortgages through 323 branches benefit from broad geographic dispersion and a well-defined state-wise collateral framework.
Disciplined underwriting approach supported by calibrated LTV and FOIR thresholds continues to reinforce portfolio quality while enabling sustainable growth.

GNPA across affordable housing and micro mortgages remained stable at 1.2% and 0.6% respectively (as per opening remarks); in Q&A, more granular micro mortgage PAR/NPA cited as increasing marginally (PAR 1.2%→1.5%, NPA 0.47%→0.55%) as the book (3 years old) matures.
Affordable housing markets are semi-urban and urban, with minimal metro presence; ticket size of INR16-20 lakh helps maintain yields despite competitive pressure.
Affordable housing yield maintained around 12.5%, has hovered near this level for several quarters because of mix of ticket sizes and geographies; management does not see a need to revisit strategy.

Micro mortgages started ~3 years back, now about INR1,800 crores, yields much healthier at ~19.5%, ~70% of business semi-urban, average ticket size INR7-8 lakhs (vs range of INR10-15 lakhs); yield doesn't fall significantly even if ticket size rises to INR10-12 lakhs.
Micro mortgage book is not yet mature (18/24 MOB numbers not fully representative); natural increase in PAR expected as book ages, but 18/24 MOB NPA still below 2.5%, indicating quality is holding.

Incremental disbursement mix expected to tilt marginally more towards micro mortgages as capacity build-out continues (affordable housing capacity ~INR350-375 crore/month; micro mortgage exit run-rate targeted at INR140-150 crore/month by March).

subsections.label: MSME
points: MSME portfolio growth driven by maintaining prudent underwriting standards; product offerings within segment enhanced (added purchase invoice discounting).
Working capital and supply chain finance jointly contribute around 28% of the MSME book, helping customer diversification and increased deposit mobilization.

Ticket size increase (LAP from INR58-60 lakh to INR80-90 lakh; working capital from INR70-80 lakh to INR1.1-1.2 crore) is a conscious strategy started in Q1, resulting in book yield trending down to ~10.5% from 11-11.5%; disbursement yield is lower than book yield.
Yield and opex are two variables consciously monitored — as ticket size rises, opex declines (though not fully offsetting yield decline); risk plus opex reduction together help offset yield decrease.
Management currently comfortable continuing in the current ticket-size band for this year; further ticket-size increases, if any, would only be considered next year.

Higher ticket MSME lending viewed as a leveraged product — lower ROA but higher ROE — and opens up nonfund-based opportunities (bank guarantees) and overall banking/liability relationships; early success seen in these areas.

subsections.label: Gold loans
points: Gold loans continue to be a strong growth driver, a new but promising business for the bank; sourcing across 455 branches with an increase of 106 branches in the quarter.

New-to-bank customer share rose sharply to 40% in the quarter, driven by activation of 100+ branches for gold loans plus increased demand from existing microfinance customers migrating into gold loans.
Plan is to increase active branches from ~430-440 currently to ~575 by year-end, targeting monthly disbursement exit run-rate of ~INR230-250 crores by March.
Loan officer productivity in gold loan branches reaches INR25-30 lakhs within a year of operation across branches and regions; ~250 more branches to be activated this year.
Being a late entrant has allowed the bank to understand nuances of gold loan business and build a product fitting the market and already largely aligned with newer RBI policies.
Gold loan is heavily concentrated in South India industry-wide, but bank sees opportunity in East, Northeast and Northern regions where the market is less penetrated.
Bank intends to eventually offer gold loans from almost all operating branches, barring a small number with operational constraints.

subsections.label: Vehicle loans
points: New two-wheeler segment continues to do well; offered across locations catered by 337 branches with focus to enhance mix of mid-premium and EV segments.
Portfolio quality remains steady with GNPA at 1.7%.
Pre-owned cars piloted in Karnataka; pilot completed, plan is to test in 2-3 geographies this year before scaling next year once customer segment, pricing and local flavor are better understood.
Commercial vehicle categories (LCV/HCV), if pursued, would only be considered after this financial year.

subsections.label: Microfinance
points: Sustained momentum in the micro banking sector drove growth in the micro banking book.
After seven quarters of degrowth, borrower base has started to grow, supported by 1.72 lakh new customer additions in Q1, marginally above Q4FY26 numbers.
All states have completely stabilized in terms of repayment behavior; bucket X collection efficiency steady at ~99.7% (ranging 99.60%-99.75% across states).
Guardrails have led to minimal four-lender-and-above exposure, now below 1.5%, indicating no overleverage in the market and consistent repayment among deleveraged customers.
MFI credit cost expectation on unsecured book of ~2% may trend slightly lower; Q1 MFI credit cost on GLP was about 1.9%.
Slippages reduced significantly — annualized slippages at 1.72% in Q1FY27 versus 2.68% in Q4FY26 (annualized), driving improved credit cost outlook.

Demand is increasing across almost all states except Kerala, where the bank strategically limits growth; branch expansion for microfinance focused more on UP, Rajasthan, and some in Bihar, where portfolio has behaved better over the last 3-4 years.

subsections.label: New initiatives
points: Unsecured Fast Track loan has completed a successful pilot and is ready for scale-up; a pure digital product utilizing account aggregators and bureau details.
Pre-owned cars piloted in Karnataka, to create a growth engine within the vehicle loan business.
Lending to mid-corporates has commenced with disbursements in Q1.
MSME product suite expanded with purchase invoice discounting.

subsections.label: Liability franchise initiatives
points: High net worth program, Ivory, has witnessed strong momentum, becoming an important pillar of the affluent banking franchise.
Insurance cross-sell penetration has improved further, reflecting stronger customer engagement.
Mutual fund distribution offering, now accessible via mobile and Internet banking, is seeing growing customer adoption.
Co-branded credit card is currently in testing phase and expected to further strengthen customer engagement and product penetration.
Segment-focused liability strategy — bank is focused on HNI, NR, TASC customers, and corporate salary segments rather than treating customers uniformly.
Focus on top 8 and top 30 markets has yielded ~75% YoY CASA growth and ~36% overall growth in these markets; bank will continue focusing here.
FCNRB rates being used to leverage newly created forex capacities; INR60-odd crores mobilized in Q1 via FCNR, with confidence in achieving previously guided numbers.

Insurance income (fee income) dip this quarter explained by disbursal seasonality — Q4 disbursal was all-time high, making Q1 not comparable; overall insurance/fee income growth is ~15% YoY and expected to be maintained.

Liability-only customers largely also hold savings accounts; bank does not onboard standalone term deposit customers — either through micro banking or liability franchise, backed predominantly by savings accounts.

key_figures.label: New branches operationalized in FY27 (till Q1)

subsections.label: Branch expansion & geographic focus
points: As part of FY27 plan, bank has operationalized 38 new branches, taking total count to 814 as of June'26.
144 branches planned for opening this year; 38 already opened, 106 more to open, giving distribution support for liability mobilization.
Liability strategy focuses on top 8 and top 30 markets which have delivered ~75% YoY CASA growth and 36% overall growth.
Gold loan geographic opportunity seen beyond South India (which is industry-heavy) — in East, Northeast, and Northern regions where the market is less penetrated.

Microfinance branch expansion is happening across many states but with greater focus in UP, Rajasthan, and some in Bihar, where the portfolio has performed better over the last 3-4 years; Kerala is strategically limited for growth.

subsections.label: Macro & geopolitical risks
points: Geopolitical situation in West Asia, which started in February this year, continued to create uncertainty across global markets during the quarter; while ceasefire discussions emerged, the situation remains fluid.
Softening of global energy prices from their peak, coupled with easing Indian commercial gas supply restrictions, has smoothened commercial operations.

Weather-related uncertainties continue to pose risk due to strengthening of El Nino in the months ahead; rabi crop harvest has led to better outcomes currently, but any delay in kharif crop sowing might impact H2 economic activity — this remains a key monitorable.

RBI's June MPC review kept policy repo rate unchanged at 5.25% with a neutral policy stance; real GDP growth for FY27 recalibrated to 6.6%, inflation forecast projected at 5.1% for full year, within RBI's defined band.
Banking sector continues to remain resilient per RBI governor, supported by healthy credit demand, steady deposit mobilization and adequate liquidity.

subsections.label: Funding and margin risks
points: Bank remains mindful of the prevailing funding rate environment and continued competitive intensity in CASA mobilization, along with pricing pressures across key asset products and resulting impact on margins — factored into the raised ROA guidance.

Deposit pressure in the market acknowledged; management does not see a very significant increase in cost of funds, but a marginal increase is expected; no immediate requirement for further upward rate revision currently seen, will remain watchful of market movement.
Bank is watchful of macro environmental factors on credit quality and will continue to take timely corrective steps to address any developments.

subsections.label: Revised guidance rationale
points: Strong performance across asset products has more than offset the impact of macroeconomic headwinds and reinforced confidence in achieving FY27 planned asset growth of 25%.
Full year opex now expected to be lower than earlier planned at around 6.4% of average assets, due to deferred commencement of capacity-building expenses coupled with ongoing efficiency gains.

Bank continues to witness encouraging trends in asset quality with credit cost at 0.9% and absolute slippages during the quarter remaining lower than anticipated; accordingly revising FY27 credit-cost guidance to 0.9%-1% of average total assets.
Bank is moving away from guiding credit cost on average gross loan book to average balance sheet for better alignment.

Taking into account funding rate environment, competitive intensity in CASA mobilization, pricing pressures across key asset products and their impact on margins, along with strength of operating performance, improving asset quality and enhanced cost outlook — bank is raising FY27 ROA guidance to 1.8%-2%.
Revised guidance driven by a combination of both opex and credit cost improvements, not one factor alone.
Deposit pressure impacts have already been baked into the 1.8%-2% ROA guidance; management does not foresee a very significant increase in cost of funds, only a marginal one.
Bank maintains secured loan mix guidance of 56% by exit March'27.

NIM guidance given at start of year is maintained, supported by MFI segment performing well along with higher-yielding segments (gold, two-wheeler, used car, micro mortgage) and no major expected change in cost of funds due to available instruments (IBPC, refinance, securitization).
Beyond FY27, opex-to-assets ratio expected to improve year-on-year as capacity-building investments taper and efficiencies kick in, though exact figures not yet provided.
CASA ratio: bank reiterated commitment to previously projected CASA ratio target (discussed at last year's analyst meet, ~30%), and may over-deliver slightly.
