risk_register.risk: Macro environmental factors on credit quality
risk_register.note: Bank remains watchful of macro environmental factors and will take timely corrective steps to address developments.

themes.label: Deposit franchise strengthening / CASA growth
themes.note: Highest YoY deposit growth in the last couple of years at 25%, CASA up 37.8% YoY, with continued focus on top 8/30 markets, HNI/NR/TASC segmentation, and new levers like Ivory, mutual fund distribution, co-branded card.

themes.label: Secured book diversification (housing, MSME, gold, vehicle)
themes.note: Secured book crossed 50.4% of loan portfolio, with strong growth across affordable housing, micro mortgages, MSME, gold and vehicle loans; secured mix target of 56% by March'27 reiterated.

themes.label: Asset quality / credit cost improvement
themes.note: Bucket X collection efficiency steady near 99.7%, MFI slippages fell to 1.72% annualized from 2.68%, prompting a downward revision in FY27 credit-cost guidance to 0.9%-1%.

themes.label: ROA guidance raise on cost & credit-cost tailwinds
themes.note: FY27 ROA guidance raised to 1.8%-2% on combination of lower opex guidance (6.4% of average assets) and improved credit cost outlook.

themes.label: Funding cost and margin pressure
themes.note: Cost of funds declined to 6.86% in Q1 but tight liquidity led to rate hikes in June; management expects only marginal increase ahead with NIM guidance maintained.

themes.label: New business scale-up (gold loans, vehicle, digital lending)
themes.note: Gold loan book up 248.6% YoY with branch and disbursement capacity expansion plans; new pilots in pre-owned cars, unsecured Fast Track digital loans, and mid-corporate lending progressing.

themes.label: Macro and weather-related risk monitoring
themes.note: Geopolitical uncertainty in West Asia and El Nino-driven kharif sowing delay risk flagged as key monitorables for H2, even as high-frequency domestic indicators remain stable.

key_takeaways: Bank delivered another quarter of steady business growth, with strategy centered on strengthening liability franchise, building a diversified asset portfolio, and maintaining prudent risk management practices.

Bank operationalized 38 new branches taking total count to 814 as of June'26; delivered highest YoY growth in deposits at 25% in the last couple of years, taking deposit book to INR48,129 crores; CASA deposits grew to INR12,930 crores, up 37.8% YoY.

Secured book progress on track with more than half of loan book secured at 50.4% as of June'26; secured book expanded to INR21,638 crores, up 42.7% YoY; bank-level gross loan book reached INR42,903 crores, growing 28.9% YoY.
Bucket X collection efficiency for the quarter stood at 99.68%; after seven quarters of degrowth, borrower base has started to grow, supported by 1.72 lakh new customer additions in Q1.

Bank-level asset quality continued to be stable with GNPA reducing by 10 bps to 2.17%; provision coverage ratio strengthened further to 85%; profit after tax at INR317 crores, resulting in ROA of 2.2% and ROE of 18.2%.

Bank is revising FY27 credit-cost guidance to 0.9%-1% of average total assets and raising FY27 ROA guidance to 1.8%-2%, on the back of strong operating performance, improving asset quality and enhanced cost outlook.

Capacity building expenses of ~INR250 crores planned for the year have started kicking in from late Q1; this deferred commencement, coupled with ongoing efficiency gains, will result in full year opex being lower than earlier planned at around 6.4% of average assets.

New asset initiatives: Unsecured Fast Track loan (digital, pilot completed, ready for scale-up), pre-owned cars piloted in Karnataka, lending to mid-corporates commenced, MSME product suite expanded with purchase invoice discounting.
pressing_questions: Can you share the current ROA profile of the affordable housing book, excluding micro mortgages? And how do we see the ROA of that portfolio shaping up in the coming year? — Management declined to provide product-level numbers.
Among the non-MFI businesses, which of the businesses are yet to achieve PPOP level breakeven? — Management stated they don't give vertical-wise guidance at this moment.

Can you give us the MFI slippage number in rupees? — Management said they would provide it (partially answered later as provisions held of INR657 crores, but explicit rupee slippage figure not stated in the transcript).

KTKBANK.about: Karnataka Bank is engaged in providing a wide range of banking & financial services involving retail, corporate banking and para-banking activities in addition to treasury and foreign exchange business.[1]

quarters.summary: Karnataka Bank delivered improved Q1 FY27 metrics across growth, margins, asset quality and profitability, with management guiding continued 15% overall business growth (10-15% liabilities, 15-20% advances), RAM-led yield improvement, targeted ROA of 1.35%-1.40% going forward, and confidence in sustained NIM and cost-to-income improvement, while flagging global geopolitical/commodity/monsoon risks and awaiting clarity on ECL provisioning impact.

subsections.label: NIM and margin drivers
points: Improvement in net interest margin was driven by the bank's focused initiatives in the RAM segment with an emphasis on enhancing yields alongside a calibrated improvement in retail term deposits aimed at optimizing the cost of funds.
Loan yields will be strengthened by accelerating retail growth while stabilizing the corporate portfolio through high quality and better yielding assets.

Sequential Q-o-Q improvement in cost of funds is expected to be supported by continued efforts to reduce dependence on bulk deposits and replacing the same with retail deposits at a card rate and focus on CASA buildup.

subsections.label: Asset quality drivers
points: The sustained quarterly improvement in both gross and net NPA ratios reflects the bank's strengthened efforts to curb slippage and enhance monitoring efficiency supported by the functioning of regional collection centres.
Bank has continued making accelerated provisioning to increase PCR.
For calculation of CRAR for June 2026, eligible profits as required under extant RBI guidelines have been considered.

subsections.label: Cost to income drivers
points: Bank's focus on low-cost deposits to reduce the cost of funds, along with an emphasis on RAM and high-yield portfolios to enhance loan yields is further expected to improve net interest income and support sustained control over the cost-to-income ratio.

subsections.label: SMA / stress commentary (Q&A)
points: Q1 FY27 SMA has gone up to INR3,435 crores and SMA-2 has gone up from INR635 crores to INR750 crores in a quarter with the lowest provisions, per analyst observation.
Management: from around double digit CD ratio issues, stress has been brought down to single digit and efforts are continuously on; focus is on SMA-0, SMA-1 and SMA-2, not just SMA-2.
Management attributed part of the Q1 SMA increase to 2-3 holidays prior to 30th June causing single/double-day defaults, otherwise stress is very much under control.
Management does not foresee or require additional provisioning because of slippage going forward.

On ECL mandate implementable from next year: CRAR is quite comfortable; bank working on it every quarter and has created a dedicated team from 1st April; management is confident of managing any 1% regulatory impact without issue.

subsections.label: Employee cost commentary (Q&A)
points: Employee cost fluctuations are due to yield movement affecting provision for gratuity and other retirement benefits, done every quarter as per auditors' guidance.
Provision increase has not been utilized for the purpose of declaring profit.
Employee cost is expected to remain in the same range going forward and is described as very well under control despite reduced employee headcount.

key_figures.label: Retail segment growth contribution (MSME, housing, gold, vehicle loans)
RAM (retail, agri, MSME) growth this quarter
Retail plus MSME and agri growth last quarter

subsections.label: Strategy on retail/RAM vs corporate
points: Overall strategy is to continue focus on growing retail, Agri and MSME (RAM).
Trajectory focuses on accelerating retail expansion and stabilizing the corporate portfolio by prioritizing high-quality, better-yielding assets.
Bank continues to reduce low-yield corporate exposure in accordance with earlier stated strategy.
Systematically replacing the IBPC book with higher-yielding loans to drive margin expansion.

Focus on reducing bulk/large corporate exposure percentage-wise (not size-wise), duly offset by growth in retail and mid-corporate; large corporate growth this quarter driven partly by repayment/tenor and yield considerations, and conscious decisions to take up bulk portion to the extent of repayments only.

subsections.label: Retail hub initiative
points: Retail hubs started in all 15 Regional Offices/centres across India immediately after new management took over charge last year; this has started driving retail business growth, giving management confidence that retail growth will come as per expected line.

subsections.label: Mid-corporate trajectory
points: Mid-corporate book was negative in first 2 quarters of last year, moderated in Q3, showed growth in Q4, and grew further in Q1 FY27 (5th quarter), with continued actions on the ground supporting confidence in further growth.

key_figures.label: Yield on advances bottomed-out level referenced by investor

subsections.label: Digital and Technology initiatives
points: Bank is leveraging IT investments through modular and faster implementation of solutions.
Bank is exploring leveraging AI tools for improving internal efficiencies, including improving processes.
Major solutions in progress: new treasury application, new NPA solution, implementation of development opportunities, digital FD, secured credit cards, voice bots for sales and collections.

subsections.label: Product development — MSME
points: Launched 3 products under MSME: GST OD, LAP for MSME, dropline OD for MSME.
2 products in pipeline: incorporation of dropline OD features to key MSME products, end-to-end digitization of key MSME products.

subsections.label: Product development — Retail
points: Retail products in development stage: surrogate-based lending for housing and mortgage loans, digital document execution for vehicle loans, end-to-end portal for channel partners, up to 90% funding on project cost for purchase of ready-built/under-construction residential units, and digitization of the gold loan.

subsections.label: Product development — Liability & ADC
points: Flexi deposits for HNI customers launched; account automatically creates a deposit account for amount over and above a predefined threshold.
Liability product under development: virtual account facility.
In ADC channel, entered MoU with Pine Labs for PoS facility, launched on April 21, 2026.
Additional pipeline products mentioned in Q&A: secured credit cards, online trading, and advances against shares and mutual funds.

key_figures.label: Branches planned to open in FY27
Remaining branches planned before end of H1

subsections.label: South India market opportunity (Q&A)
points: Analyst noted Karnataka Bank is South-predominant, with opportunity in GCC, manufacturing, defense, aerospace and new emerging businesses/supply chain in South India that other regions (barring 1-2 states in West) may be missing.

Management response: continued effort from branch and online channels, IT enablement already done and more requirements coming based on internal study and peer group benchmarking; focus on products per customer (banking and non-banking).

subsections.label: Cross-sell and customer base strategy (Q&A)
points: Analyst raised that retail term deposits below INR3 crores implies roughly 30,000-50,000 customers, questioning how many products are being cross-sold to this base and how the bank plans to strengthen connect with new products (housing loan, student loan, gold loan, etc.).

Management: continued effort from branch, online, IT enablement already done, and further enhancement based on internal study and peer benchmarking; product-per-customer focus for both banking and non-banking products is in line; new products to be launched are tailored to public requirement.

subsections.label: Agri strategic partnerships
points: Entering strategic partnership with self-help groups to expand agricultural lending portfolio while contributing to achievement of priority sector lending targets.
Exploring opportunities under electronic negotiable warehouse receipts with agriculture clusters to strengthen post-harvest financing, enhance farmer liquidity and grow agri business portfolio.

subsections.label: Leadership update
points: Mrs. Biji S S assumed charge as Executive Director of Karnataka Bank effective July 15, 2026, bringing a distinguished banking career spanning more than 30 years, expected to significantly strengthen the Bank's leadership team.

Analyst questions on MD/CEO tenure extension: management stated it is a process guided by best practices, that the Board is capable of taking such decisions, and that updates will be made via Stock Exchange filings as has been done previously (first time, second time, permanent) — no specific new disclosure on tenure status was given.

subsections.label: Governance and investor feedback process
points: There is a system and process by which every investor concern is updated to the Board by the MD; immediate actions are taken wherever possible, and feedback is taken seriously for implementation wherever more time is needed.

subsections.label: Overall strategic positioning
points: Bank's core strength lies in solid foundation and readiness to capture emerging growth opportunities; recent progress includes expanding retail and MSME portfolios, rationalizing funding costs and enhancing asset quality, establishing a robust baseline for sustained growth.

Strategy is firmly execution-led with digital transformation and targeted product offering gaining strong momentum; management stated these initiatives will drive steady improvements in margins, profitability and key ratios over coming quarters.
Bank differentiates itself through prudence, resilience and customer-centric approach despite global headwinds; backed by strong capital adequacy, comfortable liquidity and disciplined execution.

Management reiterated commitment to building a future-ready, governance-driven institution, and highlighted continuous efforts across recovery, slippage improvement, technically written-off account recovery, and improving other income through third-party products.

subsections.label: Macro environment risks
points: Monetary Policy Committee maintained neutral stance and kept policy rate unchanged in June 2026 meeting.
Prolonged West Asia conflict escalates risk to growth and inflation.
High frequency indicators show domestic economic activity remains resilient; private consumption steady and fixed investment holds strong momentum despite cost pressures.
Supply disruptions and elevated commodity prices could impact economic activity going forward.

A potentially deficient Southwest monsoon poses risk to agricultural demand, though crop diversification and climate resilient practices, alongside strong capacity utilization, healthy credit flows and government capex, will continue to support investments.

Given heightened inflationary risks, MPC is awaiting further clarity; bank maintains a measured, cautious outlook, navigating external dynamics with strict prudence while closely tracking inflation trajectories.

subsections.label: SMA / asset quality risk (Q&A)
points: Analyst flagged SMA increase to INR3,435 crores and SMA-2 increase from INR635 crores to INR750 crores in a quarter with lowest provisions, questioning whether higher provisions are coming.

Management attributed part of the rise to holidays around 30 June causing short-duration defaults, stated stress is under control, and does not foresee requiring additional provisioning going forward due to slippage.

subsections.label: ECL transition risk (Q&A)
points: ECL mandate becomes implementable from next year; analyst asked whether additional provisions will be required.
Management: CRAR is comfortable, dedicated team working on this since 1st April, and management is confident of managing any regulatory impact (cited as up to 1%) without issue.

subsections.label: Growth guidance
points: Bank keeps by and large 15% growth in the business as guidance, with around 10% to 15% growth in liabilities and 15% to 20% growth in advances as the continued effort to arrive overall at 15% growth.
RAM continues to be reiterated as the focus area, specifically gold loan, housing loan, car loan, education loan, personal loans, 2-wheeler, retail LRD and mortgage loans as continuous focus areas.
Management described its approach as 'low promise, higher delivery' and stated that objective will continue to be pursued.

subsections.label: Growth outlook commentary (Q&A)
points: For the past around 18 years, April was always negative for the bank (April-May continuing negative in growth); this year, growth was positive from April itself, giving management confidence that FY27 growth will be good, aiming to make it 'better and best'.
Priority is to increase the CD ratio further from current ~78%; with CRAR comfortable, focus is on increased lending given well-capitalized position.

subsections.label: ROA/ROE and margin outlook (Q&A)
points: Previously guided 1%-plus ROA; achieved 1.29% as of June 2026; management now aiming for 1.35% to 1.40% ROA going forward.
Effort will continue to drive continuous improvement in ROA rather than a fixed exit-run-rate target for the year.

NIM has shown improvement over recent quarters (below 3% in earlier quarters, above 3% in Q4, further improved in Q1 FY27) and management gave assurance that NIM will continue to improve, taking into account quality of accounts being onboarded and recovery.

subsections.label: Yield on advances outlook (Q&A)
points: Yield on advances has gone down but started showing improvement; management gave assurance that improvement will continue going forward.

guidance_ledger.statement: We keep by and large 15% growth in the business... around 10% to 15% growth in liabilities and 15% to 20% growth in advances... so as to arrive overall at 15% growth.
Since it is already 1.29%, I am aiming 1.35% to 1.40%.
Further improvement has happened in this quarter and it will continue to improve. That much assurance I will give you.
Yield on advance has gone down and it started showing improvement... it will continue to improve.
Priority is to increase the CD ratio... going forward also, we continue to improve the ratio.
Bank's focus on low-cost deposits... is further expected to improve net interest income and support sustained control over the cost-to-income ratio.
We have plans for opening around 31 to 32 branches during the current financial year. One branch we have already opened. Remaining 12 to 13 branches, we have plans to open before the end of H1.

guidance_ledger.metric: Retail/RAM growth focus (gold, housing, car, education, personal, 2-wheeler, retail LRD, mortgage)
guidance_ledger.statement: RAM is the focus area... will be the continuous focus area.
We have a lot of actions happening on the ground. With that, I am quite confident that it will grow.
Employee cost... it will be in the same range next quarter onwards.
We are quite capable of managing this... we don't foresee any problem because of that.
We don't foresee or we don't require any additional provisioning because of slippage, going forward.

risk_register.note: Escalates risk to growth and inflation.

risk_register.risk: Supply disruptions and elevated commodity prices
risk_register.note: Could impact economic activity going forward.

risk_register.risk: Deficient Southwest monsoon
risk_register.note: Poses risk to agricultural demand, though mitigation measures like crop diversification and climate resilient practices are being adopted.

risk_register.risk: Inflation trajectory / MPC stance
risk_register.note: MPC maintained neutral stance and kept rate unchanged in June 2026; awaiting further clarity given heightened inflationary risks; bank maintains measured, cautious outlook.

risk_register.risk: SMA/asset quality stress (SMA-2 increase)
risk_register.note: SMA total rose to INR3,435 crores and SMA-2 to INR750 crores in Q1 FY27; management attributes part to holidays around 30 June causing short-term defaults and states stress is under control with no additional provisioning foreseen.

risk_register.risk: ECL transition (regulatory provisioning change)
risk_register.note: ECL mandate becomes implementable from next year; management states CRAR is comfortable and a dedicated team has been working on this since 1 April, expressing confidence in managing regulatory impact.

risk_register.risk: Low-yield corporate/bulk exposure
risk_register.note: Bank continues to reduce low-yield corporate exposure and bulk deposits percentage-wise, offsetting with retail and mid-corporate growth.

themes.label: NIM expansion
themes.note: NIM improved to 3.20% in Q1 FY27 from 3.07% in Q4 FY26 and 2.82% in Q1 FY26, driven by RAM-focused yield improvement and lower cost of funds.

themes.label: Asset quality improvement
themes.note: Gross NPA improved to 2.58% and Net NPA to 0.87%, with PCR rising to 84.70%, though SMA-2 rose to INR750 crores in the quarter.

themes.label: RAM-led growth strategy
themes.note: Bank continues prioritizing retail, Agri and MSME (RAM) growth over low-yield corporate/bulk book, with RAM advances up 12% YoY.

themes.label: Deposit cost optimization
themes.note: Cost of funds improved 22 bps QoQ to 5.16% via shift from bulk to retail term deposits and CASA buildup; IBPC book being replaced with higher-yielding loans.

themes.label: Branch network expansion
themes.note: Bank plans to open 31-32 branches in FY27, with most planned before end of H1, to support retail/RAM growth ambitions.

themes.label: Leadership continuity/governance
themes.note: New Executive Director Biji S S took charge; however, analyst questions on MD/CEO tenure extension were not directly answered, with management citing process and best practices.

themes.label: Macro and external risks
themes.note: Geopolitical tensions (West Asia conflict), commodity price pressures, and monsoon risk to agri demand flagged as external headwinds, alongside cautious MPC stance.

key_takeaways: Bank has achieved its highest ever aggregate business, which stood at INR1,97,007 crores as of June 30, 2026, up by 3% Q-o-Q from INR1,92,119 crores in March, 2026 and up by 11% Y-o-Y from INR1,77,509 crores in June, 2025.

Gross Advances stood at INR86,610 crores as on 30th June, 2026, reflecting a Q-o-Q growth of 4% from INR83,340 crores as on 31st March, 2026 and a Y-o-Y growth of 17% from INR74,267 crores as on 30th June, 2025.
Net interest income Q1 FY27 stood at INR938.29 crores as compared to INR842.95 crores in Q4 FY26, registering a Q-o-Q growth of 11%.
Net interest margin stood at 3.20% for Q1 FY27 vis-a-vis against 3.07% in Q4 FY26 and 2.82% in Q1 FY26.

Profit After Tax for Q1 FY27 was INR418.95 crores as against INR408.19 crores in Q4 FY26 with Q-o-Q increase of 3%. There is an increase in PAT from INR292.40 crores in Q1 FY26 with a Y-o-Y increase, which is at 43%.
Gross NPA as on 30th June, 2026 stood at 2.58% as against 2.78% in March, 2026, thereby showing an improvement of 20 basis points.
Net NPA percentage as on 30th June, 2026 stood at 0.87% as against 0.98% in March, 2026, demonstrating 11 basis points Q-o-Q improvement.
Return on Equity: Q1 FY27 return on equity stood at 12.48% as against 12.69% in Q4 FY26 v/s 9.58% in Q1 FY26.
Return on Assets: Q1 FY27 ROA stood at 1.29% as against 1.27% in Q4 FY26 and 0.97% in Q1 FY26.
CRAR was at 21.10% as on 30th June, 2026 in comparison to 20.07% as on 31st March, 2026.
pressing_questions: Sushil Choksey: Sir, we are guiding for a lot of retail growth, MSME growth, RAM, agriculture advances and others. Our current branch network, we have not expanded despite growth areas which we are focusing on. So first, what are we doing to initiate on that expansion, what strategy, whether it is co-lending, direct assignment? Second thing is, what is the outstanding book which we have sanctioned and in unsanctioned pipeline, which would enable growth?

Vinay Nadkarni: Your Q1 FY27 special mention account has gone up to INR3,435 crores... your SMA-2 also has gone up from INR635 crores to INR750 crores in a quarter when you have the lowest provisions. So, does that indicate that there would be higher provisions coming in current and in the future quarters?
Yashwanth Thippeswamy: I have been watching from past 1 year... one of our fellow investor has raised a point about your tenure extension. So please help us understand what is the status on that?

Jyoti Khatri: Sir, just continuing with the earlier question with respect to the continuity of the CEO, it wasn't very clear. So, if you can help us with that. So, the Board is yet to approve a new CEO or the existing CEO's term, right, for future?

Manoj Yeddanapuri: So given that, what's actually driving that 25% growth in the other segment, if you could elaborate on that part? And given that, so at what point do you think that RAM starts growing faster than the corporate part?

ACC.about: ACC Limited (incorporated in 1936), a member of the Adani Group, is principally engaged in the business of manufacturing and selling of Cement and Ready Mix Concrete. The Company has manufacturing facilities across India and caters mainly to the domestic market.[1][2]

quarters.summary: Ambuja Cements delivered stronger profitability with EBITDA margin improving 331bps to 16.7% and net cost reduced by INR206/ton sequentially to INR4,241/ton, despite absorbing ~INR110/ton of West Asia geopolitical cost escalation and INR50/ton of scheduled kiln maintenance costs. Management reiterated full-year FY27 cost guidance of INR4,250/ton, an 8% trade volume growth guidance (already seeing 8% Y-o-Y trade growth in July), installed capacity reaching 119 million tons by FY27-end, and FY27 capex of ~INR6,500 crores; trade sales share is targeted to stay upwards of 75% going forward, with a further INR250/ton cost reduction targeted by FY28-end (cost to reach ~INR4,000/ton or below).

subsections.label: Cost bridge for INR206/ton reduction
points: Savings came from raw material (efficient fly ash sourcing), power (RE power benefit and lower price per unit), and clinker factor improvement of ~2%
Logistics contributed marginally, ~INR10 per ton
Fixed cost optimization also contributed despite lower capacity utilization
The INR206 reduction is after absorbing INR110/ton West Asia escalation impact and INR50/ton scheduled kiln maintenance cost — gross underlying savings were INR316/ton
Breakup shared: efficiency factor ~INR30-50/ton, input material and logistics ~INR50/ton, clinker factor ~INR50/ton, fixed cost optimization ~INR80/ton

Net operating cost per ton stood at INR4,241 (also cited as INR4,240) in Q1 FY27 versus INR4,447 in Q4 FY26, and versus INR4,700-5,000/ton at the time of the Holcim acquisition in September 2022; manpower cost was INR222/ton

subsections.label: Overall financial results
points: Revenue of INR9,500 crores in Q1 FY27, Operating EBITDA of INR1,589 crores, EBITDA margin of 16.7%, up 331 basis points QoQ
Blended EBITDA/ton (gray cement + RMX) of INR931/ton; gray cement-only EBITDA/ton of INR911/ton
PAT of INR660 crores; net worth of ~INR72,000 crores as of Q1 FY27
Termination-related exceptional items of INR24 crores in the quarter; zero impairment recorded
Raw material cost (consolidated, absolute) of INR1,526 crores in Q1 FY27

subsections.label: RMC segment margin decline
points: RMC EBITDA margin fell sharply from 14-15% in FY26 quarters to 7% (INR33 crores EBITDA) in Q1 FY27
No specific reason given; management cited raw material pricing and certain financial/lease accounting factors as contributors, described segment as still small and offered to discuss separately

subsections.label: Depreciation run-rate
points: Depreciation number was lower in the quarter; CFO clarified prior quarter (Q4 FY26) depreciation was elevated due to true-up entries taken on account of merger of Sanghi and Penna
Depreciation expected to stay at similar level going forward

subsections.label: ICD and inter-company arrangements
points: ICDs from ACC and Orient to parent are within approved shareholder limits, carry 8% coupon, consistent with ongoing company merger
Ambuja operating company itself carries zero debt; cash flows managed from operating cash flows

MSA arrangement: Ambuja supplies cement to ACC/Orient given its higher capacity share — 1.6-2 million tons (also cited as 3 million tons) supplied to ACC by Ambuja in the quarter, ensuring proper payouts across group companies

subsections.label: Capex and investment plans
points: Capex spend of INR1,500-1,600 crores in Q1, representing 25% of the FY27 total capex target of INR6,500 crores
Sanghi jetty expansion investment of ~INR600 crores planned; Penna AFR/WHRS investment requirement of INR100-150 crores planned

subsections.label: Power and other operating metrics
points: Power revenue rose to INR140 crores in Q1 FY27 from INR70 crores in Q4 FY26, on power units sold rising to 45 crore units from 24 crore units, reflecting green power capacity ramp-up
Temporary closure of plants affecting ~3.5 million tons of capacity, expected to last around 6 months
Fly ash consumption at 30%; lead distance reduced Y-o-Y from 269 km to 249 km with freight per ton remaining stable
Market share growth target of 8-10% and capacity addition annual target of 10 million tons reiterated; targeted utilization on expanded base of 70-75% going forward
Cost per ton expected at ~INR4,250 for FY27 overall, broadly in line with Q1's INR4,240

key_figures.label: North cluster trade volume growth Y-o-Y
Low/negative EBITDA volume curtailed in South

subsections.label: Regional demand dynamics
points: Total volume declined 7% YoY in Q1 FY27, with trade sales volume down 2% and non-trade volume down 21% YoY
North: highest EBITDA cluster, grew 2% trade volumes YoY with sharper reduction in lower-margin non-trade volumes; contributed ~25% of regional volume mix
Central: stronger market with higher proportion of premium cement enabling higher EBITDA margins; improved share of blended cement; ~10% of regional volume mix
West: well balanced between trade and non-trade (Mumbai, Gujarat markets stronger on non-trade margins); grown positively in both trade and non-trade at 2% YoY; ~30%+ of regional volume mix
East: sustained trade volumes, maintained healthy EBITDA margins; ~25% of regional volume mix
South: consciously reduced lower-margin volumes (~1 million tons curtailed) while increasing channel network and focus on trade volumes; highest degrowth cluster; ~10% of regional volume mix
Overall capacity utilization was 65% in Q1 FY27
Q1 disruption attributed to geopolitical tensions affecting diesel availability and interim packing bag availability issues, plus channel gear-change disruptions
Confidence in recovery reflected in July trade volume growth of 8% YoY

subsections.label: NSP / pricing commentary
points: Sequential ASP growth was among lowest in industry despite improved trade sales share; management attributes this partly to accounting/Incoterms treatment where certain expenditures are netted off NSP unlike some peers

Y-o-Y NSP declined versus UltraTech's reported NSP; this quarter ~INR100 lower vs UltraTech versus historically ~INR50 higher in preceding 8 quarters, attributed to one-off Q1 disruption from factors beyond control (diesel shortage, packing bag issues, AGP green sales in Himachal) and channel investment this quarter
Price is market-driven; company intends to focus on cost control as the controllable lever for delta improvement

subsections.label: South strategy on curtailed volumes
points: ~1 million tons of low/negative EBITDA volume curtailed in South; strategy is to improve cost of specific plants (green power, AFR, WHRS, fly ash sourcing, raw material/fuel mix, clinker factor reduction) to make volumes viable and migrate them into trade segment
South channel investment expected to take one to two quarters more to ramp; other four clusters progressing well

themes.label: Cost inflation & margin pressure
themes.note: Industry profitability pressured by higher imported fuel, freight costs and West Asia geopolitical developments (INR110/ton absorbed), yet company still delivered INR206/ton sequential cost reduction and 331bps EBITDA margin improvement to 16.7%.

themes.label: Acquired asset turnaround (Sanghi/Penna)
themes.note: Orient at 87% utilization performing well; Sanghi improving with INR600cr jetty investment; Penna needs channel investment (INR100-150cr) to lift utilization and margins.

themes.label: Capacity expansion recalibration
themes.note: 119 million ton capacity target by FY27-end reaffirmed via multiple staggered project commissionings, but Maratha clinker line timeline pushed from earlier FY27 quarters to FY28.

themes.label: Premiumization & trade sales mix
themes.note: Trade sales share rose from 74% to 78%, premium products at 34% of trade sales, targeted to stay upwards of 75% going forward.

themes.label: Capital discipline / capex moderation
themes.note: FY27 capex maintained at ~INR6,500 crores with 25% (~INR1,500-1,600cr) spent in Q1; priority shifting from capacity addition to converting scale into productivity and returns.

themes.label: Management candor on execution gaps / strategic reset
themes.note: Management acknowledged prior efficiency capex delays but highlighted improvement in Q1 (INR206/ton savings); also transparent on RMC margin decline without a definitive single cause and on temporary plant suspensions being a considered optimization exercise, not mothballing.

themes.label: Demand softness & pricing power
themes.note: Q1 saw 7% total volume decline YoY (2% trade, 21% non-trade) due to geopolitical disruptions, but July already showing 8% YoY trade volume recovery; ASP/NSP underperformed versus peers this quarter, attributed largely to one-off factors and accounting treatment differences.

key_takeaways: Ambuja Cements delivered stronger profitability with EBITDA margin improving 331 basis points to 16.7%, EBITDA per ton of INR931, net operating cost reduced by INR206 per metric ton sequentially to INR4,241 per ton, PAT of INR660 crores and net worth of almost INR72,000 crores on revenue of INR9,500 crores.

Trade sales share improved from 74% to 78% of overall sales; premium products comprise 34% of trade sales; company saw 2% negative YoY growth on trade and 21% negative YoY growth on non-trade volumes, but is seeing 8% YoY trade volume growth in July.

Clinker factor improved by approximately 3% to 64%, share of blended cement increased to 85%, and net operating cost reduction puts the company firmly on track for its guidance of INR4,250 per ton for FY27.
RE power capacity is now at 973 megawatts, up almost 500 megawatts over the past year; WHRS capacity stands at 228 megawatts; unit power cost reduced from INR5.9 per kWh to almost INR4.9.

Company expects total cost savings of INR130 to INR150 per ton from ongoing initiatives (lead distance reduction, raw material logistics optimization, RE power and efficiency gains), reinforcing confidence in achieving total cost of INR4,250 PMT by end of FY27, and targeting a further INR250/ton reduction to reach ~INR4,000/ton by FY28-end.

Ambuja has evolved into a 109 million ton capacity integrated cement platform; expansion projects (Dahej, Salai Banwa, Bhatinda, Jodhpur, Kalamboli, Warisaliganj) will increase installed capacity to 119 million tons by end of FY27; Maratha clinker line pushed to commission next year (FY28).

Company absorbed additional cost of INR50 per metric ton this quarter from scheduled maintenance on ~12% of kilns and built up clinker inventory of 1 month and coal inventory of around 3 months for competitive edge in Q2, while absorbing ~INR110/ton cost impact from West Asia geopolitical escalation.

Temporary closure of very old ACC facilities and one acquired-company facility (~3.5 million tons annual capacity) for about six months for optimization purposes; company clarified no permanent mothballing and no further impairments expected beyond the INR24 crore termination-related exceptional item from a VRS scheme in South India.
pressing_questions: Given the strategy of chasing value over volume, will FY27 see very muted volume growth versus the previous quarter's guidance of ~80 million tons, and will lost market share in Q1 be recouped in the balance 9 months?
Despite improvement in trade sales, why has ASP increase on a sequential basis been one of the lowest in the industry - is it geographical mix or something else?

Given substantial coal and clinker inventory versus peers' commentary of INR80-100 cost increase sequentially in Q2, can it be assumed that on a variable cost basis there is unlikely to be any cost increase in Q2?
Why did trade volumes decline 2% YoY despite the heavy focus on trade, and what was the regional dynamic behind this?

How should the ICDs from ACC and Orient to the parent be read, especially given Ambuja group-level cash access, and should this be linked to the parent company's INR22,000-23,000 crore debt maturing in FY27?
What is the timeline and rationale behind the delay of the Maratha clinker line from earlier 2Q/3Q FY27 timelines to now FY28?
What kind of market share gain is expected given demand decline in volumes, and when will actual cost measures translate into the previously discussed EBITDA per ton trajectory of INR1,200-1,500?
In retrospect, do management view the acquisitions (Penna, Sanghi, etc.) as more of an asset or a liability?

quarters.summary: Ambuja Cements delivered its highest-ever annual sales volume in FY'26 with normalized EBITDA up 31%, but Q4 costs peaked at INR4,500/tonne due to acquired-asset issues, packaging cost shocks and higher freight/branding costs. Management guided FY'27 volume growth of ~8% to ~80 million tonnes (vs industry growth of 5-5.5%), cost reduction of INR250/tonne in FY'27 and another INR250/tonne in FY'28 (cumulative INR500/tonne over 2 years vs earlier INR3,650/tonne target), capacity expansion recalibrated to 119 million tonnes by end of FY'27 (vs earlier 140-155 million tonne ambition, timeline pushed to FY'30), and capex of INR6,000-6,500 crores for FY'27, with management candidly acknowledging execution delays and a "reset" in ambition timelines while reiterating the original capacity target is not abandoned.

points: Successful amalgamation of Sanghi Industries and Penna Cement with Ambuja Cements is now completed; ACC and Orient Cement amalgamation is under process
One Cement platform strategic initiative intended to sharpen focus on operational performance, business synergies, and overall higher degree of compliance

Balance sheet of Ambuja consol now has finalized purchase price allocation (PPA) of Orient and Penna (previously provisional till December); marginal changes in balance sheet from goodwill/intangible asset classification, and P&L changes in depreciation and deferred tax accounting treatments

FY25 and FY26 not comparable like-to-like: FY25 does not include Orient Cement; Penna was consolidated from Aug 16, 2025 (7.5 months in FY25 vs 12 months in FY26); Orient included for only 11 months in FY26, not present in FY25 at all

subsections.label: Inorganic growth stance
points: Inorganic growth opportunities continue to be evaluated but current focus is squarely on organic development and greenfield expansion as the number 1 priority
On JP assets resolution, management declined to comment as the Resolution Professional is another listed company; will respond as developments occur

subsections.label: Ambition reset
points: Management acknowledged a partial reset in ambition versus original goal at time of Adani acquisition (to double capacity/volume and become industry leader) — timeline is being pushed out, not the underlying target itself
Reset driven by recognition of underperformance in delivering on prior commitments; decision to step back, course-correct, and refocus before pursuing further capital investment
Guidance now given is considered 100% controllable internally; any miss will be attributed to internal execution, not external factors

subsections.label: SLA-based operating partnerships
points: Company has tied up SLA (service level agreement) based contracts for a few plants, believing competent partners exist in India who can run plants at the aspired efficiency level
SLA partners also expected to help clean up past union-related issues carried over from Ambuja/ACC legacy, reducing cost and improving efficiency

subsections.label: 5 key monitorables (management-defined KPIs for next year)
points: 1) Discipline on L1 plants delivering to respective markets
2) Discipline on trade versus non-trade sales mix
3) Reducing raw material consumption cost as well as electricity/energy consumption cost
4) Improving channel network to help increase sales
~80% of the focus is on cost reduction; management states it does not make sense to make further capital investment until delivering on current promises

subsections.label: Industry headwinds in FY26
points: Industry consolidation and GST 2.0 reforms occurred alongside adverse and extended weather conditions, global geopolitical factors, and various state elections affecting demand

subsections.label: Cost headwinds
points: West Asia war-related packaging cost disruption emerged in late February through full month of March, adding roughly INR250/tonne of cost escalation
Fast-moving global situations and dynamism in energy costs, fuel and diesel pricing make it difficult to provide long-term cost estimates for the next 2-3 quarters until stabilization
Delayed railway infrastructure completion has prevented company from optimizing fly ash raw material costs to desired levels; expected to complete in coming months
3 to 6 month delay on some efficiency capex projects, expected to gain momentum and deliver benefits in coming quarters

subsections.label: Demand-side risks for FY27
points: Expected inflationary pressure and weak monsoon likely to keep cement demand soft
Industry pricing power weak: despite cost increases, industry has been unable to pass on price increases due to soft demand
April and May demand observed as subdued and soft

subsections.label: FY27 outlook themes
points: Focus firmly on streamlining operations and margin expansion in FY27
Continued focus on trade sales and premium product sales given leadership in that segment
Continued focus on improving reliability at Penna and Sanghi and overall asset utilization, targeting 5-10 percentage point utilization improvement on their combined 19 million tonnes capacity
Company remains committed to end-state sales volume targets, supported by sharper focus on higher utilization of existing capacities while operationalizing and stabilizing new capacities
Capacity expansion plans recalibrated to be more gradual, prioritizing optimization of current capacities and disciplined capital allocation to maximize returns on capital employed
India's long-term infrastructure story considered fundamentally strong and secular despite near-term softness expected from inflation and weak monsoon
Ambuja to remain focused on disciplined execution, strengthening brand penetration, scaling trade sales, driving premium cement sales, and maintaining cost and capital discipline

guidance_ledger.statement: Consol volumes expected to grow by almost 8% to around 80 million-odd tonnes in FY27
Industry is believed to grow at around 5% to 5.5% given inflation and weak monsoon headwinds
Expecting to hit capacity of almost 119 million tonnes by end of FY27, with proposed ongoing additions of 10 million tonnes of GU
Target plans previously targeted for FY28 (140-155 million tonnes) could move to around FY30
Targeting cost reduction of INR250/tonne for FY27, bringing average to around INR4,250/tonne from peak of INR4,500/tonne
Additional cost reduction of INR250/tonne targeted for FY28, cumulative INR500/tonne reduction over 2 years (vs earlier longer-term target of INR3,650/tonne, not abandoned but timeline extended)
Cost expected to remain flattish at around INR4,500/tonne in Q1 FY27 before tapering down through the year

guidance_ledger.horizon: unspecified (contingent on no further global escalation)
guidance_ledger.statement: If nothing increases further in global prices, cost could decline by at least INR150-200/tonne from raw material (fly ash) and green energy cost savings
Capex estimate for FY27 kept at INR6,000-6,500 crores, may change by a couple hundred crores
Annual capex of roughly INR65-70 billion for next 2 years, of which ~INR4 billion already under execution and balance for debottlenecking plus maintenance capex
Target utilization for Sanghi pegged at 65-70% for FY27
Target utilization for Penna pegged at 55-60% for FY27
Existing assets of Ambuja and ACC pegged at closer to 75-80% utilization for FY27
Overall Ambuja consol level average utilization expected at 70-75% ballpark for FY27 given softer demand scenario
Target to increase utilization by at least 5% to 10% for Sanghi and Penna assets (combined 19 million tonnes capacity)

guidance_ledger.statement: 36% premium cement share of trade sales considered a good number to sustain going forward
Earlier guided 15 million tonnes of debottlenecking exercises across assets continues, though timing may differ based on return on investment
4 million tonnes of clinker capacity to be added at Maratha, taking clinker capacity to 73 million tonnes
New Mundra clinker line of 2 million tonnes planned, targeted over 24-28 months
New Assam clinker capacity of 2 million tonnes via new limestone block, to start end of this year
Project IRR target of 18% (all equity money, equity-like return expectation) for new capex
Management declined to give specific EBITDA/tonne guidance, citing it would be a Herculean task at this stage; will keep updating over next 2-3 quarters as things become clearer

key_takeaways: FY '26 was a year of resilience for the Indian cement sector marked by industry consolidation and the GST 2.0 reforms on one side, while the adverse and the extended weather conditions, global geopolitical factors and the various state elections also affected the industry and demand in some or the other way.

Ambuja delivered a resilient performance for the year, achieving its highest ever annual sales volume of 73.7 million tonnes, up 16% Y-on-Y, and on a normalized basis, the EBITDA of INR6,539 crores, up 31%, at INR887 per metric ton, up 12%, and the PAT of INR2,647 crores, up 17%.
Premium cement accounted for 35% of the trade sales during the year, reflecting sustained progress on premiumization.

During financial year '26, we also made meaningful progress on the portfolio integration. Successful amalgamation of Sanghi Industries and Penna Cement with Ambuja Cements is now completed, while ACC and Orient Cement is under process.
The newly acquired assets, particularly Sanghi and Penna, they witnessed lower utilization levels. Sanghi still remains at around 57% on cement capacity utilization, while Penna is 46%.

I have mentioned earlier about our journey to achieve cost of almost INR4,000 a tonne by March '26 exit... in terms of the full year of '26, we have achieved a figure of INR4,400 a tonne, which is almost 10% higher to our own target.

On our overall consol volumes, we are expecting it to grow in FY '27 by almost 8% to around 80 million-odd tonnes... At an industry level, we believe that given the headlines of inflation and weak monsoon, the industry may grow at around 5% to 5.5%.

We are expecting to hit capacity of almost 119 million tonnes by end of FY '27... Capacity expansion plans, we are recalibrating in line with our approach to take the advantage of the recent railway policies on bulk cement terminals, with additions pursued more gradual.
So we'll be honest with you. Yes, partially, there is a reset. We are not moving away from the target. Yes, we are moving away from the time line.
Let me just add that cost, we are looking at roughly INR250 a tonne reduction this year and then another reduction of INR250 next year as well. That is the minimum reduction that we are looking at.
pressing_questions: So in this quarter, as per the investor deck, volumes have grown by about 10-odd percent. But if I adjust them to the Orient cement volumes, they are more like flattish on a Y-o-Y basis... for FY '27, we have given a guidance of 80 million tonnes, which is roughly a growth of 9% to 10% against the backdrop that we are expecting a much softer industry growth of 5%. So I'm just wanting to request overall color on your volumes?

By when will we get a color on the next leg of capex because the first day when the asset was acquired, the vision was to double the capacity and take it to 140 in the interim, we even increased it to 155. And now we are taking a slightly a step back... is it that we are more open to pursue inorganic growth, which helps us catapult to that overall growth target? Or we still believe organic is the way to go?
If I look at Slide 27, the realization has hardly moved Q-o-Q versus for peers, it is up somewhere between 1.5% to 2%. So is it mainly because of mix? Or what is driving this weaker revenue?

Given Ambuja's cost delivery has been all over the place over the last few quarters, can you give us some guidance where you move away from cost to EBITDA per tonne by FY '28? Given where your EBITDA per tonne is today and over the next 2 years, where do you see the EBITDA per tonne reach?
Now that you have talked about cumulatively INR500 per tonne of cost improvement over the next couple of years, are we shying away from the earlier target of INR3,650 that you had shared earlier?

What prompted us for a reset right now? If you could highlight 5 key monitorables that probably you have set for yourself for last -- for next 1 year? And how does SLA fit in overall scheme of things after the reset?

When Adani had acquired these cement assets, you had voiced out an ambition to kind of become the industry leader and double capacity and volume. So in that context, the current guidance seems to be quite subdued. So is it fair to say that there is a reset in ambition kind of from the earlier kind of thought that was there at the time of the acquisition?

Our capex is continuously getting delayed. As Adani standard, we are known for a pro capex and the very fast execution. But at the cement side, we are continuously getting delayed, especially like Maratha plant... What is the issue behind and continuously, we are getting some breakdowns at our bigger plants. Is it the maintenance-related issue or what we are facing currently right now?

SHIPROCKET.about: Shiprocket Ltd is an API-led, merchant- first e-commerce enablement platform for Indian MSMEs and large retailers, spanning domestic/cross-border shipping, fulfilment, checkout, marketing, omnichannel commerce, hyperlocal delivery and finance facilitation.[1]

quarters.summary: Shiprocket's Q1 FY27 (first quarter as a listed company) saw revenue grow 34% YoY to INR592 crores, with adjusted EBITDA growing 9x to INR8.9 crores; management expects core EBITDA margin to remain broadly in the 12.5%-13% range with continued investment behind growth, while emerging segment continues to narrow losses driven by mix-shift toward higher-margin MarTech and operating leverage; no explicit timeline given for emerging segment reaching EBITDA breakeven.

subsections.label: PAT and EBITDA delta driver
points: Adjusted EBITDA improved by INR7.9 crore and PAT improved by INR4.3 crore. The delta is primarily increased in share-based payments, which had happened a couple of quarters back, reflecting in this quarter.
Overall loss before tax has improved from INR18 crores negative to INR13.7 crores negative.

subsections.label: Adjusted EBITDA definition
points: In our case, adjusted EBITDA is essentially cash EBITDA. It is adjusted largely for ESOP cost and for the Ind AS 116 rent treatment. This is essentially cash coming into bank.
Every order is incremental to the bottom line; adjusted EBITDA per transaction has grown from INR0.22 to INR1.45.

subsections.label: Contribution margin to EBITDA cost structure
points: Contribution margin essentially has direct cost plus opex investments around KAM, performance marketing, etc. Everything relating to getting overall revenue comes in as cost there.

Adjusted EBITDA comes after contribution margin, netting overheads which include G&A cost of head office (~1500-person organization), with a large part of that investment going into emerging, and more so in product and tech.
Two levers identified: mix shift towards MarTech (growing faster) and operating leverage.

subsections.label: Core business drivers
points: Core transactions grew 31%, revenue grew 22%; many large D2C merchants performed better this quarter compared to last quarter, giving a larger footprint in the mix and stronger retention/growth.
Rate compression on the input side from partners is also manifesting in these numbers (margin improvement).
Contribution is made up of a mix of enterprise versus long-tail customers, as well as mix of shipment modes, zones, etc.; some operating leverage from people costs.
Management expects core CM/EBITDA to maintain around current range as it has in the last trajectory; over a 3-year trajectory, core adjusted EBITDA moved from 6% to 12.8%.

subsections.label: Emerging segment composition
points: Emerging has three businesses: Omnichannel (largest, up 92%, fueled by quick commerce and PTL, works with long tail), Cross-Border (down marginally, long tail exposure, global volatility hit merchant confidence, focus now on higher margin/profitable customers amid macro stabilization), and MarTech (youngest, small base but growing rapidly, slightly better margin, high potential).

subsections.label: Realization per shipment/transaction trend
points: The declining realization per shipment/transaction (96→89→84→72) reflects overall transactions count (unique orders, could be shipment or checkout transaction) rather than core alone, and is partly due to mix shift between core (falling share) and emerging (rising share, now 30% of business) which includes rapidly growing MarTech.

Core transactions grew 31% while core revenue grew 22% due to two factors: input cost compression being passed on, and larger merchants growing faster contributing to mix shift (gradation in revenue per transaction in core based on volume-based pricing).

subsections.label: Cross-sell dynamics
points: Wider base is buying more of the stack; cross-sell on 2,24,000 merchant base has grown 150 bps from 7.3% to 8.8%.
Some of this is same merchants buying more of the stack, and some is emerging becoming an entry point in its own right — merchants who come first through emerging and then use core.
One merchant buying two products and same merchant buying four are both counted once in cross-sell mix; merchants served via emerging climbed from ~30,000 to ~48,000 same quarter YoY.

subsections.label: Power merchant / ARPU reconciliation
points: Overall merchant count on TTM basis is growing (2,24,000+); Power ARPU growth has been stronger as top merchants are growing much more strongly, a function of how the market has behaved (larger merchant base growing rapidly).
Company has simultaneously focused on overall funnel expansion; over a longer period, as base expands, results should follow, but near-term will be a function of macros.

subsections.label: Core value-added services (undisclosed breakup)
points: Core business includes domestic shipping plus value-added optionalities like Delivery Boost, early CODs, insuring goods in transit, NPS measurement on tracking pages, etc.; company does not disclose the breakup between domestic shipping and value-add contribution.

Whether to build these into the platform or monetize them is a function of how it helps the merchant and current company priorities; current focus is on continuously adding transactions rather than expanding every drop of margin, since transaction acquisition is more valuable (of the INR32,000 crores GMV last year, roughly 25%-30% goes into marketing).

subsections.label: Quikpay (checkout innovation)
points: Remembers shopper's preferred UPI app/payment mode and surfaces it in one tab, along with discount/net savings upfront, reducing cognitive load at checkout.
Outcome for merchant: higher prepaid share and higher checkout conversion; higher prepaid mix reduces cash-on-delivery handling and RTO cost, making it margin-accretive, not just top-line improving.

subsections.label: Steal Deal (cart-stage innovation)
points: Sits at cart stage just before payment; recommends a complementary product personalized to shopper, creates urgency with limited-time offer, and gamifies the basket (e.g., 'add INR99 more and shipping is free').
Outcome: higher average order value and higher attach rate per order; monetizes existing traffic without incremental acquisition cost.

subsections.label: AI Assist (chat/support innovation)
points: Answers shopper queries pre-order (product questions, recommendations, can initiate checkout in chat) and post-order (order status, returns, cancellations), cutting merchant support load.
Differentiator versus rule-based older chat bots: merchant gives a URL, system reads the site, builds its own knowledge base, goes live rapidly, and keeps learning.

subsections.label: AI Ads (ad creative innovation)
points: Produces ad creatives in minutes, addressing the small merchant's real barrier (creative production, not ad budget); provides multiple formats, static banners for every placement, editable templates, Shorts from product images, and 360 spin views.

Differentiator versus generic AI tools is context: Shiprocket can see brand's own connected ad account performance and category-level performance, personalizing creative emphasis (e.g., headphone ad vs. face cream ad) and improving via thousands of creatives generated across the network.

subsections.label: Omnichannel quick-commerce fulfillment integration
points: For a D2C brand selling on quick commerce, the hardest operational challenge is keeping stock ready-to-ship, securing a truck, and getting a delivery slot at the warehouse — work otherwise done manually via email, spreadsheets, and WhatsApp.
Shiprocket's system integrates with quick commerce platforms: warehouse order triggers automatic notification, truck assignment for pickup, delivery slot booking, and goods reaching the warehouse.

Effectively aggregates purchase orders across many D2C brands into slots, giving brands visibility into what is coming and where the truck is, enabling brands to ride the overall quick commerce growth story.
