subsections.label: Market opportunity
points: India has about 8% retail penetration, low compared to US and China; India is at the beginning of digitization in Tier 2 and 3 cities, where half of India's e-commerce is already Tier 2+ cities.
Shiprocket has a majority of its GMV coming from Tier 2 and 3 cities.
India has about 6 crore MSMEs; even excluding kirana, there remain many small businesses needing to digitize.

subsections.label: Competitive positioning vs 3PLs / point solutions
points: Business model connects with leading 3PLs (India Post to best courier companies covering hyperlocal, air, surface, forward, reverse, special logistics) without owning assets.

Overwhelming majority of the INR32,000 crores GMV last year is the D2C channel, which is the fastest-growing part of the market per reports; couriers focusing on D2C/SMB can participate too, but Shiprocket's differentiator is the platform tailored to merchant needs with several sub-segments/use cases/workflows built over years.

Data scale is a differentiator versus independent point solutions: over a decade of consumer behavior data, 15 crore consumers served, 30 crore online shoppers in market, 93% checkout address auto-fill, fraud-scoring on RTOs across consumer and address data.
Having an independent vertical software versus a connected, integrated stack sharing data across functions (checkout, ads, omnichannel/PTL) is what drives outcomes for merchants.

subsections.label: Customer acquisition (CAC) trend
points: CAC acquired through digital marketing (YouTube, Google, organic content, events); merchants land on apps/websites, sign up, complete KYC, put money in wallet, start shipping; inside sales assist onboarding.

CAC fluctuated: ~3,100 in Q1 FY26, ~2,800 last quarter (Q4 FY26), ~3,600 this quarter (Q1 FY27) — described as experimental (trying new ways to reach new/reactivate customers), not seasonal; break-even (CAC at ~3,000-odd breaks even with margin from customers in short span) is the focus rather than the absolute number; management does not expect CAC to trend into an ever-increasing number.

subsections.label: Merchant graduation / lifecycle & realization differential
points: Pricing is based on volumes because Shiprocket has contracts with partners offering discounts/pricing tied to volume; aggregator model lets Shiprocket cherry-pick right quality and SLA for each shipment using predictive model built on over 70 crore shipment data records.

Value proposition scales with brand size: for smaller brands, enablement itself is the value; for larger brands, instant routing/data intelligence becomes more valuable as spillover demand and choke points occur.
Realization/yield differs by segment as a function of volume vs pricing dynamics — larger merchants may pay slightly lower shipping rates as volume grows, consistent with market norms.

Merchants may enter through core (shipping) or through emerging (e.g., marketing solution first, shipping opportunity created later) depending on their lifecycle stage and immediate problem; company's framework is to enable merchant orders and progressively power more margin pools regardless of entry point.

subsections.label: MarTech opportunity
points: MarTech enables checkout/conversion suite plus newer capability to drive more traffic and better ROAS via platforms like Instagram, Facebook, WhatsApp using commerce/behavior data.
Delivered ROAS model links delivery data to marketing targeting to manage RTO (relevant given large COD share in India) and generate creatives grounded in purchase/catalog/consumer/inventory data.
Penetration of MarTech is described as a healthy mix across top, power, and long-tail merchants rather than concentrated in one segment — not broken out segmentally.

subsections.label: Platform/business model design
points: Platform connects with over 250 partners across payment gateways, courier companies, warehousing partners, ERP and accounting companies — everything a merchant needs to run their business.
Works with over 42 courier partners to provide varied use cases (hyperlocal, documents, cross-border, etc.).
Asset-light model allows deep ownership of data on consumer, carrier, and seller behavior; company sits in the money flow (checkout and COD), becoming a trust maker between partners and merchants.

Platform built modularly (catalog, payments, fraud, warehouse/inventory management) similar to leading marketplaces, but distributed as an operating system rather than sold as software; monetized on consumption basis.
Two economic segments: Core (shipping orchestration business) and Emerging (omnichannel, cross-border, MarTech) — the latter monetizing the same core transaction across additional margin pools.
Intelligence powered from over 700 million transactions to date.

subsections.label: Past acquisitions and integration track record
points: Acquired WMS systems.
Acquired the entire PTL and cargo business as a technology capability in fiscal '22.
Merged with number two competitor Pickrr in 2023, which brought team, talent, and the checkout business.
Company has historically been acquisitive and integrated successfully, delivering results across core and emerging.

subsections.label: Cross-border volatility
points: Cross-border revenue was down marginally; global volatility has hit merchant confidence in this segment; company is focused on higher margin and profitable customers, with stabilization of macro, focus continues to be on profitability in this piece of emerging.

subsections.label: Competitive intensity from 3PLs entering D2C/SMB
points: Third-party logistics partners have gotten focused on D2C and SMB segment; management notes this is a fast-growing market and everybody will want to participate, but positions Shiprocket's tailored, data-driven platform as its differentiator against this competitive pressure.

subsections.label: Seasonality
points: One seasonality baked into the business: in Q3 (the general e-commerce peak season), merchants working outside marketplaces pull out of marketing and redirect inventory to marketplaces (which represent a bigger opportunity for them during the season), making Q3 not the best quarter for Shiprocket unlike general e-commerce trends. No other seasonality effects noted.

subsections.label: Power merchant/macro dependency
points: Power ARPU growth being driven by larger merchants growing faster is a function of how the market has behaved; near-term (next couple of quarters) results from funnel expansion efforts will be a function of macros.

subsections.label: CAC volatility
points: CAC has fluctuated across quarters (Q1 FY26: ~3,100; Q4 FY26: ~2,800; Q1 FY27: ~3,600) due to experimentation with different acquisition channels/reactivation approaches; management does not expect CAC to trend into an ever-increasing number.

key_figures.label: Steady-state EBITDA margin range suggested by analyst

subsections.label: Core business margin outlook
points: Contribution margin (CM) has improved a little over revenue growth and is expected to maintain around that range as it has in the last trajectory.

Core adjusted EBITDA has grown from 6% (three years ago) to 12.8% currently; company continues to invest behind growth and sales as opportunities are seen ahead; over a longer period, leverage can be modeled given the design of the business where every core transaction is margin-accretive after overheads.

subsections.label: Emerging segment margin outlook
points: No specific timeframe given for guidance on when emerging could reach EBITDA breakeven.
MarTech is higher margin and growing rapidly (base still small) and is seen as a driver for continued contribution margin improvement.

Emerging CM percentage moved from about 9%-10% last year to about 15% this year while adjusted EBITDA moved from -38% to about -24%; growth is described as the real lever continuing to drive all metrics.

subsections.label: Merchant funnel expansion outlook
points: Company has focused on and doubled down on funnel expansion (adding more merchants at the base); over a longer period of time this should show in results, though near-term performance will be a function of macros.

guidance_ledger.statement: CM has improved a little bit over revenue growth this quarter and we expect it to maintain around that range as it has in the last trajectory.

Over a larger period of time, you can model how the leverage kicks in because of the design of the business, where essentially every transaction that happens in core is margin-accretive to the bottom line after overheads are removed; the rate of growth of overheads model from historical data.
Won't be able to give you a timeframe in terms of guidance [for when emerging could reach EBITDA breakeven], but the MarTech business is higher margin and growing at a very rapid clip.

guidance_ledger.metric: Merchant funnel expansion / power merchant growth
guidance_ledger.statement: We are increasing the funnel, and we've doubled down on that part of the business as well... over a longer period of time... you should see that results, but not obviously, what happens practically over next couple of quarters etc will be the function of macros.
I don't expect the CAC to trend into an ever-increasing number, that's not sort of the direction... we can assume that to be within a range.

risk_register.risk: Global macro volatility impacting cross-border merchant confidence
risk_register.note: Cross-border revenue down marginally; global volatility has hit merchant confidence; focus shifted to higher-margin, profitable customers pending macro stabilization.

risk_register.risk: Seasonal Q3 weakness due to merchants shifting to marketplaces
risk_register.note: In Q3 e-commerce season, merchants outside marketplaces pull out of marketing and redirect inventory to marketplaces, making Q3 relatively weaker for Shiprocket unlike general e-commerce trends.

risk_register.risk: Dependency on larger merchants' growth / macro-driven power merchant performance
risk_register.note: Power ARPU growth driven by larger merchants growing faster is a function of how the market has behaved; near-term results from funnel expansion will depend on macros.

risk_register.risk: CAC volatility from acquisition experimentation
risk_register.note: CAC fluctuated from ~3,100 to ~2,800 to ~3,600 across recent quarters due to experimentation with different acquisition channels; management does not see this as a rising trend.

risk_register.risk: Competitive pressure from 3PLs entering D2C/SMB segment directly
risk_register.note: Third-party logistics partners have gotten focused on D2C and SMB segment; acknowledged as a fast-growing market that others will want to participate in.

themes.label: Segment mix shift (Core vs Emerging)
themes.note: Emerging share of revenue rose from 24% to 30% YoY, driven by faster growth (70% YoY) than core (22% YoY), improving overall contribution margin and EBITDA trajectory.

themes.label: Operating leverage / margin expansion
themes.note: Core adjusted EBITDA margin improved from 6% three years ago to 12.8% this quarter; emerging adjusted EBITDA improved ~1380 bps YoY to -24%, driven by contribution margin gains and overhead leverage.

themes.label: Cross-sell / platform stickiness
themes.note: Cross-sell of core merchants buying emerging products rose from 7.3% to 8.8%; merchants served via emerging grew from ~30,000 to ~48,000 YoY.

themes.label: AI/tech-led product innovation
themes.note: New launches this quarter — Quikpay, Steal Deal, AI Assist, AI Ads — aimed at boosting conversion, AOV, and margin-accretive prepaid mix for merchants.

themes.label: Cross-border demand softness
themes.note: Cross-border revenue within emerging was down marginally due to global macro volatility denting merchant confidence; focus shifted to higher-margin profitable customers.

themes.label: Competitive positioning via data scale
themes.note: Management argues data scale (70 crore+ shipment records, 15 crore consumers, 93% checkout address auto-fill) differentiates Shiprocket from single-point competitors and 3PLs entering D2C/SMB directly, even as competitive intensity is acknowledged.

themes.label: MarTech as emerging growth driver
themes.note: MarTech, the youngest and smallest emerging sub-business, is growing rapidly at higher margin and is seen as a key lever for future contribution margin improvement, though no EBITDA breakeven timeline was given.

key_takeaways: Our transactions grew 36% and GMV 31% this quarter. Against an FY26 revenue growth of 24%, we grew revenue at nearly 34% this quarter.
Merchant up 14%, ARPU up 18%, giving us overall 34% revenue growth.

Adjusted EBITDA, although on a very small base, frankly, grew 9x to INR8.9 Crore, and the other thing I would highlight is overall trailing 12 months' matrices, which is 216 million transactions processed.
Revenue from operations was INR592 crores, up 34%. Core was INR412 crores, up 22%. Emerging was INR180 crores, up 70%.
Emerging share itself in the business with, owing to the higher growth, has moved from 24% last year to 30% in this quarter.

Core adjusted EBITDA was, for the quarter was INR52.7 crores, margin was 12.8%, and it was 50 bps better than last year's same quarter. Emerging adjusted EBITDA moved from negative 38% to negative 24%, roughly 1380 bps improvement in a 12 months' time.

Adjusted EBITDA improved by INR7.9 crore and PAT improved by INR4.3 crore. The delta is primarily increased in share-based payments, which had happened a couple of quarters back, reflecting in this quarter.
Last year, we made almost like INR0.22 of adjusted EBITDA per transaction. This quarter, we are making like INR1.45 per transaction on EBITDA.
pressing_questions: Sachin Salgaonkar (BofA Securities): asked whether core business growth trend with contribution margin/EBITDA margin outpacing revenue growth would continue, and whether 12.5%-13% could be considered steady-state EBITDA margin for the core business.

Sachin Salgaonkar (BofA Securities): asked for a timeframe on when the emerging business (MarTech, Omnichannel, Cross-Border) could reach EBITDA breakeven — management declined to give a specific timeframe.
Della Desai (Axis Capital): asked why core business CAC has moved up both YoY and QoQ (~3,100 → ~2,800 → ~3,600).
Della Desai (Axis Capital): asked how many power merchants are using MarTech / how to think about MarTech penetration into core GMV — management stated this is not segmentally broken out.
Avnish Sharma (JM Financial): asked how to reconcile Power ARPU up ~25% with power merchant count being slightly lower YoY.

Kunal Thanvi (Banyan Tree Advisors): asked whether large D2C companies that scale up have ever moved directly to logistics partners, bypassing Shiprocket, and about realization/margin differential between largest customers and long-tail customers.

Kunal Thanvi (Banyan Tree Advisors): asked about Shiprocket's right to win against existing point-solution competitors in fulfillment/cargo and MarTech/checkout, and whether it is easier to convert existing customers vs. sell to new merchants.

Kunal Thanvi (Banyan Tree Advisors) follow-up: asked about the potential market size for MarTech, whether contextual ad help extends beyond own websites to platforms like Instagram/Facebook, and whether MarTech profitability/flow-through to profit differs from core.

Shreyansh Talesra: asked about the decline in average realization per shipment (from ~96 in FY24 to ~72 currently) and whether core business shipment-level realization is disclosed separately, and requested breakup of domestic shipping platform revenue vs. value-added services within core — management stated this breakup is not disclosed.

MCX.company: Multi Commodity Exchange of India Ltd
MCX.about: The MCX) commenced operation in Nov,03 is India’s first listed, national-level, electronic exchange, and India’s leading commodity derivatives exchange which offers the benefits of fair price discovery and price risk management to the Indian commodity market ecosystem. The Exchange operates under SEBI. [1]

quarters.company: Multi Commodity Exchange of India Ltd
quarters.summary: Q1 FY27 saw a consolidation after an exceptionally strong Q4 FY26, with total income up 85% YoY to INR752 crores and revenue from operations up 88% YoY to INR702 crores, EBITDA more than doubling to INR544 crores at a 72% margin, and PAT at INR413 crores; management expects growth momentum at the fundamental level to continue into FY27 even as one-off geopolitical/macro tailwinds from Q4 FY26 normalize, with focus on expanding participation, product suite, liquidity, technology infrastructure, and new segments (coal exchange, electricity, indices) while awaiting regulatory clarity on FPI participation expansion and RBI bank guarantee norms.

key_figures.label: SGF contribution
key_figures.value: lower than the decline in revenue or transaction income

subsections.label: P&L drivers
points: EBITDA more than doubled YoY, demonstrating scalability of business model and continued focus on efficiency.

Performance reflects healthy year-on-year growth across all key financial parameters, though it is a consolidation/normalization versus an exceptionally strong Q4 FY26 driven partly by geopolitical/macro factors.

subsections.label: Other income
points: Other income saw drastic sequential and YoY growth, reflecting sharp Q4 growth and macro environmental factors; management expects this to moderate/consolidate but demonstrate a strong baseline level as exchange growth continues.
Growth expected to remain strong for FY27 on controllable factors, though very strong macro factors seen earlier may or may not recur.

subsections.label: SGF contribution
points: SGF contribution decline on a Q-o-Q basis was lower than the decline in revenue/transaction income; SGF is a function of multiple parameters per SEBI-prescribed monthly methodology.

Contribution depends on assessment of whether more needs to be infused into the fund per SEBI calculation, and how much buffer/headroom is desired above the calculated requirement, causing variation quarter to quarter.

subsections.label: Employee cost
points: Employee cost growth driven by a mix of new employee additions plus increments, and a bit of higher variable pay in a subsidiary this year.
Approximately 8% to 9% of the increase is a one-time item that will not recur in coming quarters.

key_figures.label: Bullion Options Notional ADT growth QoQ
Bullion Options Premium ADT decline QoQ
Gold options all-variant Average Open Interest (AOI)
India electricity spot market daily transaction share

subsections.label: ADT & participation growth
points: Very strong growth across ADT reflects increased market depth, deeper liquidity, and wider adoption of commodity derivatives by market participants.
Client participation encouraging with traded client base doubling YoY, highlighting increasing acceptance of commodity derivatives as an effective hedging and investment tool.

subsections.label: Volume mix shift (crude/natural gas vs gold/silver)
points: Mix of volume tilting more towards crude and natural gas contracts amid higher volatility there; gold and silver notional volume rose over 100% but premium (p/n) has fallen, compressing premiums.
Volume-wise gold and silver remain healthy (ADV up), but there is a price-related and volatility-related impact kicking in; volatility is a determining factor in premium decline.

Decline in premium ratio attributed predominantly to market factor of lowered volatility in both gold and silver, not to participation mix shift or contract mix shift (Silver 100 to Gold 10, BULLDEX); premiums of both gold and silver at similar levels; participation remained stable compared to last quarter.

Notional turnover increase alongside volume increase indicates growing usage of Options for its designed hedging purpose; open interest (AOI) also increased for both gold and silver variants, indicating more participation despite premium decline being a function of changing market/volatility conditions.

subsections.label: Traded UCC trend
points: UCC growth quarter-on-quarter over recent quarters reflects new members and expanded participant interest; this quarter is roughly flat versus a high prior quarter driven by high volatility and opportunity.

Underlying trend of new members and new participants remains positive; management expects higher UCC numbers this year versus FY26 full-year close of 20 lakh, without committing to a specific number, citing continued headroom for growth.

subsections.label: Crude oil options volume flatness
points: Despite three months of heightened crude prices and volatility this quarter versus roughly one month in Q4, crude oil options quantity was flat/marginally lower QoQ because Q4 was a heightened one-off; core trend line this quarter remains healthy.
Volatility is market-driven and can be attributed to volume changes.

subsections.label: Bullion vs energy counterbalancing
points: Between the two big product pillar segments, energy and bullion, a counterbalancing effect tends to occur — energy contributes more when bullion is tepid, and vice versa.
Bullion volatility, while lower than the previous quarter, is still at levels where the market requires to hedge and use the platform for regular business purposes.

subsections.label: Bullion volume softness in June/July
points: Bullion numbers were softer in Q1 amid price softness/lower volatility in gold and silver following destocking and geopolitical environment changes in June.

Silver 100 Grams launch was well received, reflecting more affordable hedging/investment product for industry and investors; retail interest in smaller gold contracts (10-gram futures) also aided by home-delivery models introduced by some players.

subsections.label: Competitive intensity
points: Challenger exchanges (large competitors from adjacent equity space) have become active in the commodities segment; MCX is tracking new member registrations and FPI additions as leading indicators.

Main contracts have held strong against head-on competition; some competitive actions on expiry date changes have had only a couple of days of temporary volume impact, not affecting MCX's own volume; competitive activity is being watched closely with an action plan being developed.

key_figures.label: Transactions handled per day (4 quarters ago)

subsections.label: Technology capacity and investment
points: Continued investment in technology in a smart, efficient manner, prioritized after risk and compliance.

Successfully handled large volume growth over the past year (from under 1 billion to over 3 billion transactions/day) with capacity to handle more than double current levels, positioning well for future growth.
New Executive Director for Critical Operations and Technology (Sanjay Rajpal) has joined to ensure platform readiness for scale and resilience in a cost-managed manner remains a top priority.

subsections.label: Product launches
points: Successful launch of Silver 100 Grams Futures contract in response to market demand given high silver prices; contract has already shown very good performance and become a more accessible hedging/investment product.
BULLDEX (launched last year) is undergoing a rework on both Futures and Options, expected to give a good bump up on Indices.
Indices remains a continued area of focus across bullion, metals, and overall commodity space, with a few plans currently in the pipeline expected to hit market over the next few months.

Metal contracts (e.g., copper) have seen impact from warehouse rationalization and contract simplification, with a continued strong focus area to build depth; headroom for growth seen in the options portfolio for metals.

key_figures.label: MCX global ranking - Commodity Options Exchange
MCX global ranking - Commodity Derivatives Exchange (by contracts traded)
AMCs using MCX bullion price for AUM calculation

subsections.label: Global leadership position
points: As per FY2025 statistics, MCX is the world's largest Commodity Options Exchange and fourth largest Commodity Derivatives Exchange by number of contracts traded, reflecting participant confidence and reinforcing commitment to innovation, market development, and operational excellence.

subsections.label: MCX price / AUM benchmark adoption
points: Following a regulatory directive that exchange discovered price be used by AMCs for AUM calculations, MCX worked closely with the industry; 50+ AMCs are now using MCX bullion price as a reference for AUM calculations.

Each fund had to secure board approval and policy sign-off; focus has been on service orientation to market needs rather than an immediate revenue stream; both implicit and explicit revenue streams from this are expected to follow, with plans around data services to be shared over the next couple of quarters.
Data-related income opportunity from AMC price adoption not yet quantified for the current quarter's revenue contribution.

subsections.label: Competitive moat
points: MCX's edge relies on two pillars: deep understanding of commodity market risk (Good Delivery standards, warehouse inventories, delivery-based contracts creating integrity in price discovery by merging derivative with physical contracts) and strong technology moat.

subsections.label: Good Delivery Norms expansion
points: Expanded Good Delivery Norms to include silver, empanelling the country's first domestic silver refiner, in line with policy narratives around bullion; norms aligned with best-in-class global standards.

Three more domestic gold refiners empanelled, and the Good Delivery framework extended across all contracts, supporting domestic refining and India's self-reliance in precious metals; welcomed by the industry.

subsections.label: Coal Exchange
points: At an early stage of work on a coal exchange; on regulatory approval, MCX Coal Exchange of India has been incorporated, with other procedural items in play towards next steps.

Aims to create a transparent, efficient, technology-driven national coal trading ecosystem aligned with government market reforms and MCX's long-term strategy of expanding into new commodity segments.
This is not a derivatives initiative at this point but a coal exchange; having this foundation is important going forward to cover the whole energy basket.

subsections.label: RBI bank guarantee regulation
points: RBI regulation on bank guarantees, originally meant to come into effect in April with a 90-day absorption period, is now in force; impact is expected to be more of a Q2 action than Q1.

Not expecting a very significant detrimental impact; will have implications on cost of funds for some flows associated with members, expected to be optimal as industry finds its own mechanism to deal with it; nothing significantly detrimental seen at this stage.
Unable to quantify the proportion of trades backed by bank guarantees, as this varies daily based on margin calls and members use multiple instruments.

subsections.label: Volatility normalization
points: Normalization of premium ratio in bullion is expected given trends in global volatility; lower volatility in gold and silver this quarter versus the previous quarter is a market-driven factor contributing to premium decline.

Q4 FY26 was an exceptionally strong quarter driven partly by geopolitical/macro factors that may not repeat; Q1 FY27 reflects normalization without those extreme factors, though foundational growth elements remain strong.

subsections.label: Regulatory uncertainty on FPI expansion
points: SEBI and the commodity derivative action committee reportedly examining expanding FPI participation to non-cash/beyond-energy contracts; MCX awaiting progress and staying with what's in the public domain.

SEBI has a strong focus with independent teams within MRD at senior levels working on the commodity segment; timelines on open regulatory items (e.g., position limits, colocation) cannot be commented on, though MCX is working with focus to close these out.

subsections.label: Competitive activity
points: Challenger exchanges (from adjacent equity space) stepping up activity given strong commodity market growth; some competitive actions such as expiry date changes have had limited, temporary (few days) impact without affecting MCX's own volumes; being watched closely.

subsections.label: Growth outlook
points: Growth momentum at the fundamental level expected to continue to be good into FY27; while exceptional Q4 FY26 factors won't necessarily repeat, foundational growth elements remain strong.
Other income expected to be on a strong track this year; strong macro factors may or may not kick in but all controllables show strong indicators.

subsections.label: UCC growth outlook
points: Expect higher traded UCC numbers this year versus FY26 full-year close of 20 lakh, without committing to a specific number; headroom for growth continues to be substantive.

subsections.label: Index products outlook
points: Expect a good bump up on Indices from the BULLDEX rework (Futures and Options); a few plans in the pipeline to hit the market over the next few months.

subsections.label: Electricity derivatives outlook
points: Expect continued build-out of participation from power players including DISCOMs, with positive lead indicators; expect the derivative-to-spot ratio in India's electricity market to grow to reflect global market multiples over time, in the very early phase of this journey.

subsections.label: Data services / AMC monetization outlook
points: Plans around data services beyond current offerings expected to be shared over the next couple of quarters; both implicit and explicit revenue streams from AMC price adoption expected to follow.

guidance_ledger.statement: Growth momentum at the fundamental level to continue to be good; while the exceptional Q4 driven by many other factors holds last year's numbers, we expect the numbers this year to be on a strong momentum as well.

guidance_ledger.metric: Other income / total income growth FY27
guidance_ledger.statement: We do see growth to be on a strong track this year; while very strong macro factors may or may not necessarily kick in, all the controllables have strong indicators and we do expect the numbers to be strong.
Last year, we closed at 20 lakh at a full year number. We do expect to have higher numbers this year. The headroom for growth continues to be substantive.

We are not expecting this to have a very significant detrimental impact. We'll have to wait and watch what the actual impact of this turns out to be; expect it to be optimal in nature as industry finds its own mechanism to deal with it.

There's a rework on the BULLDEX product in play on both Futures and Options; expecting that to give a good bump up on Indices; a few plans currently in pipeline will hit the market over the next few months.
Looking at more participation from power players starting to make inroads, including with the DISCOMs, good open interest buildup; all lead indicators on that look positive.

We absolutely expect this to be reflective of what we see in global markets. We are in the really early phase of this journey... this will grow to be a very strong contract for India, reflecting what you're seeing globally.
On approval from the regulator, we have incorporated the MCX Coal Exchange of India and other procedural items are in play towards the next steps on this.

We do have some plans around data services over and above what we have today, which over the next couple of quarters, I think we'll be able to share more; we do believe that both implicit and explicit streams of revenue will follow.
We are keen, no doubt about it. We are awaiting sort of progress on this count. We'll stay with what's available in public domain as the details on this get worked through.

guidance_ledger.metric: SEBI dedicated commodity derivatives department / open regulatory items (position limits, colocation)
guidance_ledger.statement: We can't comment on timelines for the open items. We are working with a lot of focus to get things over the line.
Capacity-wise, very well positioned as we speak in terms of the growth that is coming our way, with capacity to handle more than double current transaction volumes of over 3 billion/day.
This will continue to be a strong focus area to build depth in the contract, given headroom seen especially in copper portfolio.
We believe the coming year will be a strong year.
Will every quarter be a big jump over the previous quarter, perhaps not... there will be macro factors and cyclicity that will play out.
FPI contribution currently stands at about 2% to 3% of ADT, and within Energy segment they are double-digit contributors; we see this number growing.
If this were to get permitted by the regulator, we'll be able to take this to market fairly soon; we do have our plans in place and we'll be able to activate them at short notice.
We are prepared with our next lot of products, and we will look at suitable requirements in energy, metals, as well as other segments.
We will also be looking at moving further on METALDEX this year; focusing attention on futures on indices as well along with options.
Our focus will be on efficiency... but the focus is not going to be on spending less; we have to continue to spend smart.
We have strong plans for the capital on hand, including both organic and inorganic opportunities, new product segments, ancillary spaces.

risk_register.risk: RBI bank guarantee regulation impact on prop trading volumes / cost of funds
risk_register.note: Now in force after 90-day absorption period; impact expected to be more of a Q2 action than Q1; not expected to be very significant/detrimental but will have implications on cost of funds for some member flows.

risk_register.risk: Volatility normalization in bullion (gold/silver) reducing premium ratio
risk_register.note: Premium to notional ratio fell from 1.03% to 0.35%, a 68% yield compression, attributed predominantly to lowered volatility in gold and silver, a market-driven factor.

risk_register.risk: Normalization from an exceptionally strong Q4 FY26 base (geopolitical/macro one-offs)
risk_register.note: Q1 FY27 reflects consolidation/normalization versus Q4 FY26 which was boosted by significant geopolitical factors not repeating at the same extent.

risk_register.risk: Competitive intensity from equity-side challenger exchanges
risk_register.note: Big competitors from adjacent equity spaces are stepping into commodities given strong growth; some competitive actions on expiry date changes noted, with limited temporary impact; being watched closely with an action plan in development.

risk_register.risk: Regulatory uncertainty on FPI participation expansion beyond energy contracts
risk_register.note: SEBI reportedly examining expansion; MCX awaiting progress, no firm timeline available.

risk_register.risk: Open regulatory items with SEBI (position limits, colocation)
risk_register.note: No timelines can be commented on; MCX working with focus to resolve these.

risk_register.risk: Crude oil options volume flatness despite heightened volatility period
risk_register.note: Volume flat/marginally down QoQ despite three months of heightened crude price/volatility, attributed to Q4 being a heightened one-off and market-driven volatility factors.

risk_register.risk: Bullion volume softness from lower volatility in June/July
risk_register.note: Price softness/lower volatility in gold and silver in June after destocking amid changing geopolitical environment led to softer bullion numbers this quarter.

risk_register.risk: Operating risk (platform, surveillance, risk management, CCL margin/collateral operations)
risk_register.note: Considered risk number 1; each element gets challenged during high market uncertainty; company spends most of its time on this.

risk_register.risk: Competition risk from large equity Exchange competitor entering commodities
risk_register.note: Competitor has placed significant focus on commodity segment, launched multiple bullion and energy products; MCX bullion market share remains untouched over last 2 years; energy segment seeing some shallow, misaligned expiry-related activity.

risk_register.risk: Regulatory risk (MII compliance framework)
risk_register.note: Being under SEBI's MII regulatory ambit requires strong compliance team focus and investor services/relations attention.

risk_register.risk: RBI lending norms for prop traders
risk_register.note: Could have potential impact on credit lines for a certain segment of members across trading market segments; RBI has given extension for market to plan mitigating factors; management disputes analyst's BG/FD funding-mix estimate, noting FDs (fully funded) are the largest portion versus BGs.

risk_register.risk: High volatility and delivery risk in commodities during FY26
risk_register.note: Periods of high volatility and potential delivery risks across multiple commodities were rigorously and effectively managed with minimum disruption; market integrity maintained at highest level.

risk_register.risk: Uncontrollable market-structure disruption (e.g., market coupling, sudden competitor share shifts)
risk_register.note: Analyst raised concerns citing IEX market coupling and BSE options market-share gain as examples; management termed these 'uncontrollables' and declined to comment or identify any specific recognized concern.

risk_register.risk: Interoperability of clearing corporations (equity vs commodity)
risk_register.note: Interoperability only feasible with 100% similar products (e.g., same ISIN in equities); commodities may differ; ultimate decision rests with regulator; management does not see this as reducing MCX's sticky liquidity.

themes.label: Bullion & Energy volume growth
themes.note: ADT grew strongly to INR10.5 lakh crores with Futures ADT up 47% YoY and Notional Options ADT up 266%, but bullion premiums compressed 68% on lower volatility even as gold/silver ADV rose.

themes.label: FPI participation expansion
themes.note: 35 new FPIs added taking count to 220, contributing 2.5% of ADT at a higher ADT base; awaiting regulatory progress on expanding FPI participation beyond energy contracts.

themes.label: Retail/UCC participation growth
themes.note: Traded client base doubled YoY to 13.72 lakh; UCC growth roughly flat QoQ after a high-volatility Q4, but underlying new member/participant trend remains positive with expectation of higher full-year numbers than FY26's 20 lakh.

themes.label: Competitive intensity from equity Exchanges
themes.note: Challenger exchanges from adjacent equity spaces stepping up activity; main contracts have held strong against competitive actions like expiry date changes, with only temporary limited impact.

themes.label: New business lines (electricity, coal exchange)
themes.note: MCX Coal Exchange of India incorporated on regulatory approval; electricity futures Q1 ADT at INR37 crores with ~55% market share and >70% OI market share, reflecting early-stage but strong traction.

themes.label: Cost discipline vs growth investment
themes.note: Continued smart, efficient investment in technology (capacity to handle over double current 3 billion transactions/day) alongside a one-time 8-9% employee cost bump not expected to recur.

themes.label: Regulatory risk (RBI norms, FPI policy)
themes.note: RBI bank guarantee regulation now in force with impact expected to be gradual and not significantly detrimental; FPI expansion beyond energy and SEBI's dedicated commodity department remain pending with no firm timelines.

key_takeaways: We are pleased to begin FY27 with another quarter of strong operational and financial performance, reinforcing the structural growth in India's commodity derivatives market and the resilience of our business model.

During the quarter, our total income increased by 85% to INR752 crores and revenue from operations grew to INR702 crores, which is an 88% growth. EBITDA more than doubled to INR544 crores, and there is a good EBITDA margin of 72% with a PAT at INR413 crores.

The quarter witnessed very strong growth across the Average Daily Turnover, the ADT. This grew to INR10.5 lakh crores. Futures ADT grew by 47% year-on-year, and overall ADT showed growth over last quarter. The Notional Options ADT has also grown by 266%.
Our traded client base doubled from previous year to 13.72 lakh clients this quarter.
We've had a very successful launch of the Silver 100 Grams Futures contract... has already seen a very good performance.
We have worked very closely with the industry and have a number of AMCs, at least 50-plus AMCs, who are today using MCX bullion price as a reference for AUM calculations.

Expansion of Good Delivery Norms... we've included silver and also empanelled the country's first domestic silver refiner... Three more domestic gold refiners have also been empanelled, and the Good Delivery framework has also been extended across all contracts.
On approval from the regulator, we have incorporated the MCX Coal Exchange of India and other procedural items are in play towards the next steps on this.
As per FY2025 statistics, MCX is the world's largest Commodity Options Exchange and fourth largest Commodity Derivatives Exchange by number of contracts traded.
pressing_questions: So, what is creating this shift [gold/silver notional volume rising while premiums fall]? And how we see the rise in the gold and silver volumes in the mix?
If you could give us some sense around what proportion of the trades might be backed by bank guarantees currently or in last quarter, that would be helpful.
SEBI looking at expanding FPI participation to contracts beyond energy — any update regarding that or any colour regarding how you see that play out?

Can you decompose this 68% yield compression, say across four buckets: mechanical notional inflation from higher gold and silver prices, implied volatility normalization post Q4 spike, participation mix shift towards further OTM and shorter-dated strikes, and the contract mix shift from Silver 100 to Gold 10 and BULLDEX? What is the contribution of each, and which are structural rather than cyclical?

In the next three years, how much do we anticipate the ratio of traded electricity derivative volumes to deliverable supply to evolve? And which category (algo hedgers vs speculators) do we expect to offer a higher growth rate?

SEBI would revise the dedicated commodity derivatives department — could you provide updates on whether that has happened or is imminent, and any timelines for open items like position limits, colocation?
This quarter had three months of heightened crude prices and volatility versus one month in Q4 — why did we not see a significant increase in crude oil options volumes this quarter?

quarters.company: Multi Commodity Exchange of India Ltd
quarters.summary: MCX reported a strong FY26 close with growth across all key financial parameters, driven by bullion and energy volumes; management expects the coming year to be a strong year (though not every quarter will necessarily show sequential growth over the previous quarter given cyclicity), continues to invest in technology, product pipeline and risk management, and is pursuing new growth avenues like electricity derivatives and a proposed Coal Exchange, while watching competition, regulatory (RBI lending norms, FPI access), and operating risks closely.

key_figures.label: Average daily turnover growth (futures and options)
Interest income on margin money (prior year)
Interest income on margin money (full year FY26)

subsections.label: Revenue and Profitability
points: Consolidated revenue from operations more than doubled to INR2,302 crores for full year FY26, supported by nearly 2.5 times increase in average daily turnover across both futures and options.
Profit after tax crossed INR1,300 crores and EBITDA at INR1,774 crores, reflecting both scale benefits and continued cost discipline.

subsections.label: Margin / Cost Discussion
points: Management noted that product license fees and other expenses grew faster than revenue in the quarter, preventing the expected margin expansion; management confirmed there was no one-off item in these line items.
Focus going forward will be on efficiency rather than spending less — continued investment in technology and people is required to be ready to execute growth plans.
Software support charges have been stable compared to the jump seen in Q4 of the prior year; expenses will be incurred as and when business requirement arises, done efficiently.
Increase in other expenses for the quarter attributed to market development activities and business-related professional charges.

SGF (Settlement Guarantee Fund) contribution was higher this quarter to keep the reserve fund at a healthy level to aid risk mitigation decisions; SGF is a SEBI requirement computed per SEBI's formula/methodology and is maintained in line with business growth; no fixed percentage of transaction charges has been defined for SGF contribution; company stated it is in a comfortable position with a good cushion on SGF, with the requirement being a function of volatility, margin levels, volumes and open interest rather than a simple fixed number.

subsections.label: Capital Allocation
points: Despite a strong year of profit and cash accretion, payouts have declined; management stated it is important to maintain a funding chest for growth, covering both organic and inorganic opportunities, new product segments and ancillary spaces; certain strategies are at a very early stage but there are strong plans for the capital on hand.

key_figures.label: Retail participation vs equities (number of people trading)
MCX market share in bullion (vs competitor)

subsections.label: Bullion and Energy Drivers
points: Energy and bullion are the two big volume drivers; both have grown, with bullion growth much higher (more than 4 times) and energy growth also good and strong over a very high base.

Globally and in India, requirement strength shifts between bullion and energy at different points in time, creating a balancing effect between the two segments and forming part of the structural growth foundation.

subsections.label: FPI Participation
points: FPI participation is currently limited primarily to the cash-settled Energy segment; onboarding of FPIs has been strong and the pipeline is strong.

A consultation paper is under discussion regarding allowing FPIs into gold and silver contracts (beyond cash-settled segment); MCX is contributing to the consultation and will act once results are out.
FPI contribution stands at about 2%-3% of overall ADT at the MCX level, but within the Energy segment specifically they are a double-digit contributor, and this number is expected to grow.

subsections.label: Retail/UCC Participation
points: UCC increased 64% for the full year, partly aided by onboarding of discount and non-discount brokers; management wants a democratic increase in participation without being overly aggressive in any one space.
Retail participation in commodities is at 35% of equities in terms of number of people trading; not every equity investor is expected to become a commodity investor.

Growth actions include working with digital brokers/members, consolidated ledger initiatives, and improving user experience of MCX trading vis-à-vis equity markets; further user-experience streamlining opportunities remain.

AMCs, mutual funds, wealth channels and other segments are seen as future participation channels for retail; regulatory action is expected to give mutual funds more flexibility to increase commodity exposure in portfolios in coming months.

subsections.label: Electricity Derivatives
points: Electricity contracts are in early stage; rather than tracking revenue, the company tracks membership, onboarding, trading and throughput.
About 50 commercial participants onboarded along with a large number of trading members; UCC numbers going up month-on-month.

Converting DISCOMs into participants is an important part of the plan and takes time, but some progress is expected; engagement continues with SEBI, CERC and state regulators (since much policy comes from states) and with large traders operating on the spot market, producers (solar and other), large industrial consumers and distribution side participants.

subsections.label: Competitive Position
points: Bullion market share has remained untouched over the last 2 years despite a large competitor launching multiple bullion and energy products.

Competitor's recent activity on changing expiry dates in the energy segment is seen as leading to shallow, one-day-in-a-month activity, viewed as misaligned with global structuring required for contract integrity; MCX does not want to react with moves inconsistent with how commodity products should operate.
Company's core actions remain focused on driving participation in existing portfolio, creating awareness, bringing in new participants and hedgers, and developing new products based on market needs.

The biggest moat is liquidity in MCX's contracts; while equity Exchanges entering commodities may have some natural synergies and could make entry a 'tad easier,' the real benefit to participants comes from being in a liquid exchange where they can enter/exit as required.

subsections.label: Product Pipeline
points: Company had a certain number of products planned last year and launched according to what the market would appropriately take; next lot of products is prepared, with focus on suitable requirements in energy, metals and other segments.
BULLDEX options generated a lot of interest in the futures segment; company is taking market feedback to focus more on futures on indices along with options.
Further work planned on METALDEX this year as the indices portfolio is both deepened and expanded.
Company denied media reports (clarified via a response on X) about weekly contracts being considered on the index side, calling such reports misleading.

subsections.label: Colocation Readiness
points: If regulator permits colocation in commodities, MCX will be able to take this to market fairly soon per market requirements; plans are already in place and can be activated at short notice.
Competitor equity Exchanges already offer colocation services in equities, prompting the question on MCX's readiness.

subsections.label: Contract Innovation
points: Product development efforts focused on contract innovation and enhanced expiry frameworks contributed to deeper liquidity and wider market access.

subsections.label: Institutional and Retail Participation
points: Institutional and retail investors have increasingly embraced the commodity asset class, leading to broader and deeper market participation.

Growth is described as structural along with cyclical tailwinds — increasing participation from a diverse set of market participants, improving awareness and acceptance of commodity derivatives, and introducing more participants to both the hedging instrument and asset class positions the company for sustained expansion.

subsections.label: Competitive Landscape
points: A large competitor has placed significant focus on the commodity segment, including launching multiple bullion and energy products.

Equity Exchanges entering the commodity space could have natural synergies, but the liquidity moat that MCX has built is viewed as the primary differentiator; management stated it will not ignore the fact that it should overcompensate for any experiential simplicity that may be available to users on other platforms.

Discussion on BSE's rapid gain of options market share (from near-zero to ~37-38% incrementally in about 3-3.5 years) was raised by an analyst as an example of dramatic competitive shifts, but management characterized such scenarios as uncontrollables it would not comment on directly.

On interoperability between equity and commodity clearing corporations: liquidity does not simply move due to interoperability; MCX has sticky liquidity and industry-wide participation; interoperability is only feasible when products are 100% similar (e.g., same ISIN in equities), which may not be the case in commodities; ultimately an interoperability decision rests with the regulator.

subsections.label: Agri Commodities Opportunity
points: Company is in discussions and working groups with industry and regulator on various policies, including relaxation of regulations for agri commodities; management could not share specifics on potential market size but said whatever opens up in that space will be beneficial and MCX will look at playing a stronger role.

subsections.label: Coal Exchange
points: MCX recently won the license to set up a Coal Exchange; the Coal Exchange will be an independent entity operating as a subsidiary, not part of MCX as a company.
As MCX is a Market Infrastructure Institution (MII) under SEBI's regulatory ambit, SEBI approval was required to proceed with this line of business.

The business is seen as closely associated with the commodity derivatives Exchange business, with the opportunity being to establish a spot market in coal where a mechanism already exists, along with opportunity for structuring, consolidation and a common pan-India platform.
Company is in the early stage of establishing the entity; further steps remain, including rules to be formed by the suitable regulator in that space before the entity becomes operational.

subsections.label: 'Price in India: Hedge in India' Initiative
points: Company initiated a focused drive called 'Price in India: Hedge in India' to strengthen the commodity derivatives ecosystem, promoting and deepening hedging participation within India for SME and corporate hedgers.

subsections.label: Capital Deployment Strategy
points: Management indicated plans for capital on hand include both organic and inorganic opportunities, new product segments and ancillary spaces, with certain strategies at a very early stage.

key_figures.label: MCX share of clearing corporation funding via Bank Guarantees (BGs) - per analyst estimate
Industry average BG funding share - per analyst estimate

subsections.label: Operating Risk
points: Operating risk is considered risk number 1 — the ability to operate and deliver on market opportunity (platform, surveillance, risk management, CCL operations on margins and collateral) is challenged during periods of high market uncertainty; this is a risk the company spends most of its time managing.

subsections.label: Competition Risk
points: Company acknowledges it has not historically faced strong competition and has been a majority market-share player; staying agile, innovating, and challenging itself is seen as the best defense.

subsections.label: Regulatory Risk
points: Being a Market Infrastructure Institution (MII), regulatory risk and working within the compliance framework take significant management attention, supported by a strong compliance team and investor services/relations functions.

subsections.label: RBI Lending Norms for Prop Traders
points: New RBI lending norms for prop traders could have a potential impact on the market; RBI has given further extension allowing the market to plan mitigating factors, and MCX is in touch with and working with members on this.
A certain segment of members across all trading market segments will have some of their credit lines impacted.

On funding mix, an analyst noted MCX/clearing corp funding via Bank Guarantees (BGs) is 55-60% of total margin funding versus 35% for the industry; management (Rishi Nathany) disputed the analyst's numbers, stating FDs contribute the largest portion of margin money funding (which is fully funded and would not be impacted), while BGs contribute a much lower percentage than FDs, so impact from RBI norms may not be as large as suggested.

subsections.label: Delivery and Volatility Risk (FY26)
points: During FY26, the company navigated periods of high volatility and challenging market conditions across multiple commodities, including potential delivery risks, which were rigorously and effectively managed with minimum disruption to market functioning; market integrity was maintained at the highest level despite broader economic risks.

subsections.label: Uncontrollable Market Structure Risks
points: Analyst raised concerns about scenarios like IEX's market coupling issue, which derailed price discovery (a key Exchange function) and commoditized the Exchange's role, and BSE's rapid options market share gain versus a large incumbent, as examples of risks not obviously visible when things are healthy.

Management characterized these types of scenarios as 'uncontrollables' that it would not comment on or react to; when pressed on whether there was anything in the realm of recognition that concerns management, response was that there is nothing specific it is worried about.

subsections.label: Outlook for FY27
points: Management believes the coming year will be a strong year, though exactly how each quarter will play out remains to be seen; company acknowledges cyclicity in the business with some quarters historically better than others.

Growth is viewed as structural (diverse participant growth, improving awareness/acceptance of commodity derivatives, regulatory/policy opportunity still to play out over the years) combined with cyclical tailwinds.

Priorities going forward: highest standards of governance, risk management and market integrity; strengthening infrastructure; continued investment in technology; delivering seamless trading experience; innovation, liquidity enhancement and long-term value creation for stakeholders.

guidance_ledger.statement: We believe the coming year will be a strong year.
Will every quarter be a big jump over the previous quarter, perhaps not... there will be macro factors and cyclicity that will play out.
FPI contribution currently stands at about 2% to 3% of ADT, and within Energy segment they are double-digit contributors; we see this number growing.
If this were to get permitted by the regulator, we'll be able to take this to market fairly soon; we do have our plans in place and we'll be able to activate them at short notice.
We are prepared with our next lot of products, and we will look at suitable requirements in energy, metals, as well as other segments.
We will also be looking at moving further on METALDEX this year; focusing attention on futures on indices as well along with options.
We are in the early stage of establishing that entity and taking it forward; there are steps left before the actual entity starts getting operational.

From launch to date, it has been growing month-on-month in its participation and presence in the market; converting a few DISCOMs is an important part of the plan, and we are at a point where some of that is going to come in as well.
Our focus will be on efficiency... but the focus is not going to be on spending less; we have to continue to spend smart.
We have strong plans for the capital on hand, including both organic and inorganic opportunities, new product segments, ancillary spaces.

risk_register.risk: Operating risk (platform, surveillance, risk management, CCL margin/collateral operations)
risk_register.note: Considered risk number 1; each element gets challenged during high market uncertainty; company spends most of its time on this.

risk_register.risk: Competition risk from large equity Exchange competitor entering commodities
risk_register.note: Competitor has placed significant focus on commodity segment, launched multiple bullion and energy products; MCX bullion market share remains untouched over last 2 years; energy segment seeing some shallow, misaligned expiry-related activity.

risk_register.risk: Regulatory risk (MII compliance framework)
risk_register.note: Being under SEBI's MII regulatory ambit requires strong compliance team focus and investor services/relations attention.

risk_register.risk: RBI lending norms for prop traders
risk_register.note: Could have potential impact on credit lines for a certain segment of members across trading market segments; RBI has given extension for market to plan mitigating factors; management disputes analyst's BG/FD funding-mix estimate, noting FDs (fully funded) are the largest portion versus BGs.

risk_register.risk: High volatility and delivery risk in commodities during FY26
risk_register.note: Periods of high volatility and potential delivery risks across multiple commodities were rigorously and effectively managed with minimum disruption; market integrity maintained at highest level.

risk_register.risk: Uncontrollable market-structure disruption (e.g., market coupling, sudden competitor share shifts)
risk_register.note: Analyst raised concerns citing IEX market coupling and BSE options market-share gain as examples; management termed these 'uncontrollables' and declined to comment or identify any specific recognized concern.

risk_register.risk: Interoperability of clearing corporations (equity vs commodity)
risk_register.note: Interoperability only feasible with 100% similar products (e.g., same ISIN in equities); commodities may differ; ultimate decision rests with regulator; management does not see this as reducing MCX's sticky liquidity.

themes.label: Bullion & Energy volume growth
themes.note: Bullion volumes grew more than 4x and energy grew strongly off a high base, the two main structural and cyclical volume drivers for FY26.

themes.label: FPI participation expansion
themes.note: FPI contribution stands at 2-3% of overall ADT and double-digit share within Energy, with pipeline strong and a consultation paper pending on allowing FPIs into gold/silver.

themes.label: Retail/UCC participation growth
themes.note: UCC grew 64% for the full year aided by digital broker onboarding, though retail participation (35% of equities by trader count) is expected to grow steadily rather than aggressively.

themes.label: Competitive intensity from equity Exchanges
themes.note: A large competitor has intensified focus on bullion/energy products, but MCX's bullion market share has stayed untouched over 2 years, with liquidity cited as the key moat.

themes.label: New business lines (electricity, coal exchange)
themes.note: Electricity derivatives growing month-on-month with ~50 commercial participants onboarded; Coal Exchange license won, to operate as an independent subsidiary, still in early stage.

themes.label: Cost discipline vs growth investment
themes.note: Product license fees and other expenses grew faster than revenue in Q4, capping margin expansion; management says focus is on spending efficiently, not on spending less, as it invests for growth.

themes.label: Regulatory risk (RBI norms, FPI policy)
themes.note: New RBI lending norms for prop traders could impact credit lines for a segment of members; FPI access to non-cash-settled commodities awaits regulatory consultation outcome.

key_takeaways: For the full year FY '26, the consolidated revenue from operations more than doubled to INR2,302 crores, and this was supported by nearly 2.5 times increase in the average daily turnover across both futures and options. The profit after tax crossed INR1,300 crores and EBITDA at INR1,774 crores, reflected both the scale benefits and the continued cost discipline.

To strengthen the commodity derivatives ecosystem, we've initiated a focused drive 'Price in India: Hedge in India'. This promotes and deepens hedging participation within India for SME as well as corporate hedgers.
Our two big drivers of volume are energy and bullion... bullion has had a much higher growth... it has grown more than 4 times, the energy growth has also been good and strong over a very high base.
The FPI contribution currently stands at about 2% to 3% of ADT... within the Energy segment, they are a significant contributor... in the double-digit contribution of energy.
For the full year, [UCC] is up by 64%.
From whatever we see, our bullion numbers remain untouched when it comes to market share over the last 2 years.

The RBI lending norms, the way we see it could have a potential impact... there will be a certain segment of members, across all segments of the trading markets who will have some of their credit lines impacted from this.
When it comes to coal, the coal Exchange is an independent entity. It will not be part of MCX as a company. It will operate as a subsidiary.

Electricity contracts are still in early stage at this stage... We've got about 50 participants from the commercial participant side and a large number of members who contribute and trade, the UCC numbers also are going up month-on-month.
pressing_questions: What are the factors making this growth structural, given bullions clearly driving most of the volumes and bullion volatility also driving a lot of this picture?
Is there any update on the consultation paper about allowing FPIs into gold and silver contracts, and what is the contribution from FPIs in energy products (crude oil and natural gas)?
If regulator allows colocation in commodities, in what time would MCX be able to roll out these services to traders, and what is the preparedness?
Regarding the steep increase in UCC (64% for the full year), is it fair to assume this is now in the base, or is more retail participation expected, and what is driving this expansion?
On product pipeline — where are things in terms of launch of metal contracts, and on index options scaling up, is FPI restriction the only bottleneck or are there other factors?
With a competitor launching multiple bullion and energy products, what is MCX doing to protect market share?
Has MCX done any analysis on volumes that will be hit from RBI's new lending norms for prop traders, split between small and big prop traders?
Why did product license fees and other expense line items grow faster than revenue, preventing expected margin expansion — was there any one-off?

In a seemingly 'win-all' scenario with volumes rising rapidly, what could actually go wrong or unravel MCX's growth momentum (beyond routine operational/competitive/regulatory risks) — e.g., analogous to IEX's market coupling issue or BSE's dramatic options market share gain from equity markets?

What are the key factors or drivers that would change a retailer's or trader's mindset to shift from MCX to another Exchange, and what incremental offering would competing Exchanges need to gain market share?
Could regulatory relaxation for agri commodities scale up in coming years, and what could be the potential market size relative to energy or bullion?

Is interoperability of clearing corporations between equities and commodities the main reason liquidity hasn't shifted between Exchanges, and what is MCX's view on regulator allowing interoperability at a later stage?
Given MCX's clearing corporation funding mix (55-60% via BGs vs 35% industry average per analyst estimate), is MCX at higher risk from the RBI regulation impact?
Despite a very strong year of profit and cash accretion, payouts have gone down — what are the plans for this conserved cash, and what spend is expected for next year?

ROLEXRINGS.about: Rolex Rings is a leading manufacturer of forged and machined components in India and is one of the top 5 forging companies in India. The company is a Global supplier of hot rolled forged, machined bearing rings and automotive components for various segments of vehicles, Industrial Machinery, Wind Turbines and Railways

quarters.summary: Q1 FY27 revenue grew 4.3% YoY to INR304 crores, held back by a temporary labor shortage on the shop floor (April-mid June) rather than demand issues; operations normalized from June '26, with July '26 recording the highest-ever monthly revenue. Auto components (export-led) grew strongly while bearing rings (domestic/industrial-led) declined; margins expanded YoY for the third consecutive quarter aided by mix shift and cost discipline. Company completed its INR180 crore buyback, is now fully debt-free, and reiterated mid-teen revenue growth guidance for FY27 with EBITDA margin guided at 21-22%, while flagging ocean freight/geopolitical cost pressures as a near-term margin risk.

key_figures.label: EBITDA margin (as inadvertently stated on call, later corrected)

subsections.label: Margin expansion drivers
points: Gross margins for the quarter came up compared to Q1 FY26, reflecting a favorable shift in product mix, disciplined raw material management, and scientific production/cost control measures at plant level.
Margin expansion came through even in a quarter where production was constrained due to labor and other matters.
This is the third consecutive quarter of year-on-year margin expansion, reflecting a structural improvement in the business.
As volumes normalize and the order book converts fully into output, margin trajectory should hold and strengthen further as value-added process products grow as a share of revenue mix.

subsections.label: Capital allocation / buyback
points: INR180 crores buyback of 1 crore equity shares concluded during the quarter, with the promoter group choosing not to participate so full benefit flowed directly to non-promoter shareholders.
Company is now fully debt-free and clear of all legacy CDR obligations, and is carrying cash surpluses.
Management views this buyback as the first of many steps in returning value to shareholders, given a cleaner capital structure than at any point in company history.
Strategy for cash use: distribute profits to shareholders (potential dividend or another buyback round), alongside exploring inorganic growth/JV opportunities.
