subsections.label: Bearing rings softness
points: Softness concentrated in the industrial business/segment, particularly in domestic and European markets — an area of broader industry-wide stagnancy flagged previously.
It reflects the same labor-driven output constraint that affected the quarter's overall production.
Softness mainly in high-volume, bigger-size components in the industrial segment; it was the domestic-facing portion that saw softness this quarter.
Loss/reduction in industrial segment mainly due to one customer group (5-7 plants supplied) that had a huge reduction and cancellation of orders, mainly in Europe.

subsections.label: Auto components strength
points: Auto components continued to gain share within overall mix; shift towards higher value-added process products expected to continue over coming quarters.

Auto components is now a predominantly export-oriented business and delivered the strongest growth this quarter, validating the strategic shift toward a higher-value export-facing precision machine components business alongside the traditional bearing rings franchise.
New programs won in the previous fiscal have ramped up further; existing customers increased volumes significantly, driving export auto components growth.
A couple of new orders expected to start in Q3 FY27, adding further to the segment.

subsections.label: Domestic auto components decline
points: Decline mainly because of deferring of certain production plans of a couple of automotive OEMs; not due to loss of business or production constraint (barring the small labor portion).
Stellantis started with revenue recovery, though not yet at last year's level; gradually picking up and expected to be on track with FY25 levels or better.
Expect better numbers in domestic auto components from Q2 onward as Tier 1/Tier 2 customers' supply to overseas principals gains up.

subsections.label: Bearing ring domestic automotive vs industrial
points: Except for one customer, other customers in the bearing rings-for-automotive-application segment have increased their wallet share, adding incremental volumes and new components from existing programs.
Company sees no downward trend, but rather an upward trend in the bearing ring segment for automotive applications.
For the industrial bearing ring segment, customer guidance for next couple of quarters indicates only marginal growth.

subsections.label: Timken relationship
points: Bearing ring exports decline of ~10% mainly attributed to Timken's continued weakness.
No much change yet in business with this particular customer; strategy is to develop new customers and not depend on a particular group/plant, expanding base in US and Europe.
Approaching certain plants of existing customers not yet in the customer basket; response expected in a couple of quarters.

subsections.label: Allison / Dana
points: Allison customer revenue, annualized on 4 months of business, has already crossed FY25 levels.

Allison's acquisition of Dana: senior-level meeting held with Dana management along with Allison; they are eager to explore higher size/higher volume product potential with Rolex, but development/on-paper revenue will take a minimum of 12-18 months.

One US customer with the 1.75 billion order pipeline flagged a year back is on hold except a couple of orders due to tariffs (OEM has held the project); rest of projects coming back with gradual improvement, and new FY26-won programs have also started.

subsections.label: CV / off-highway opportunity
points: One customer acquired a division of a global multinational in the commercial vehicle/heavy vehicle segment, with a good rapport of 12-14 years, expected to give a good turnaround with incremental YoY volumes.
One customer nearing finalization in Europe for CV/off-highway heavy-duty vehicles, and discussions ongoing with another in the US.

subsections.label: Industrial segment exploration
points: Concentration is on maximum/incremental utilization of capacity across product range, segment, territory, volume, revenue and margin.
Dialogues ongoing with a very big auto customer in Europe for commercial vehicle and industrial segment products.
One domestic customer has diversified into industrial segment/bearing; good inquiry received and certain samples already submitted, turnaround expected.
Government registrations/approvals initiated for certain untapped industrial areas.

subsections.label: Large-size bearings trend
points: Demand shift towards large-size bearings not as pronounced as expected, but global bearing manufacturers are moving slightly towards production of bigger sizes.
This will not hamper or reduce demand for automobile/smaller size bearings where the company is present.
Good amount of inquiries and trial/run processes ongoing with existing global customer in this segment.
Applications for larger-size bearing rings are mainly industrial, mechanical, windmills and other critical equipment.
Margins on these rings are better than traditional bearing ring business due to value-added and critical processes, similar to auto components margins.

subsections.label: Labor shortage impact
points: Production ran below full potential for part of the quarter due to a shortage of labor on the shop floor, meaning the order book could not be converted into output at the desired pace.
This is a general phenomenon, particularly in April, May and until mid-June, flagged previously in the last call; situation improved from June '26 onwards, with operations back to normal by Q2 FY27.
No specific reason beyond seasonality: hot summer in the region, a significant out-of-state labor force taking vacation/wedding season/agricultural crop season leave for 15-30 days.
These are semi-skilled workers with long tenure with the company; management did not want to lose such skilled/trained labor.

Mitigation: adding temporary extra labor at reasonable cost, running 3 shifts, giving overtime for about 2-2.5 months; this comes with some additional cost, but returning trained labor gives better quality output and efficiency versus temporary labor.

No revenue was lost due to labor shortage — it was deferred by about a month, not discontinued; extra labor and shift management helped mitigate, though human output capacity was somewhat reduced in the hot months of April/May.

subsections.label: Capacity fungibility and target mix
points: No specific target for mix between bearing rings and auto components — facilities and equipment are fungible and can produce both.
Company would accept large program orders (5-7 years) with desired margin levels regardless of product type, subject to available capacity.

subsections.label: US market
points: US market is coming back, with customers reengaging after a prolonged period of caution.

Buyers who were cautious through FY26 due to tariff uncertainty and adverse market factors are now placing orders again with confidence, signaling genuine overseas demand pickup and intact customer relationships translating into order flow.
Company has not lost a single customer through the tariff disruption or the European war impact in the last year or the year before.

subsections.label: Europe
points: Europe continues to fire on the back of expanding automotive components presence there.
Ocean freight to Europe still under control, though dialogue on freight cost sharing has already been initiated with customers there too.

subsections.label: Ocean freight / container shortage
points: Ocean freight and availability of ocean freight to the US has gone up more than 2x-3x due to Hormuz/Europe/Iran/US geopolitical factors, impacting margins to some extent.

Container availability at reasonable cost remains an issue; shipping lines have indicated they are not getting vessels back to India due to geopolitical reasons; issue may persist and spill over to Q2.
Company is trying to manage container availability despite cost pressure and vessel constraints.

Discussions initiated with customers on reimbursement of high ocean freight expenditure incurred in Q1/June onward; positive indications received from majority US customer group (major chunk of ocean freight paid there); one customer has already changed import delivery terms temporarily; some pass-through to customers expected in coming quarters.

It is difficult to change current program terms from DAP/DDP to Ex Works, but customers have historically helped reimburse abnormal freight cost increases (as happened previously when freight rose more than 3x-4x).

subsections.label: Raw material sourcing
points: Raw material for bearings is majority sourced from Indian steel plants.

subsections.label: US customs duty refund
points: Company successfully registered with US customs authority for duty drawback/refund related to tariffs and HS codes.
Refund process has started but not in full swing; a marginal amount has been received and already accounted for in this quarter's numbers; major chunk yet to be received.
Refund of export duty, when received, will be added to revenue, not other income.

subsections.label: Competitive positioning
points: Competition exists in all businesses; company's USP is its facility, range of products, precision level, tooling department, product yield, and customer association.
Company does not see itself losing out despite competitors claiming higher export quality/pricing from certain steel sourcing countries.

subsections.label: New customer development
points: Strategy is to develop new customers for the bearing rings segment (auto or industrial, overseas) rather than depend on a particular group/customer, since major domestic players are already in the customer basket.
Approaching certain plants of existing customers not yet in the customer basket, expecting response in a couple of quarters.

subsections.label: Inorganic growth / JV exploration
points: Exploring inorganic growth, association, or JV with an overseas player to be based in India, to increase utilization of Rolex facilities and add more value-added processes where the third party has expertise and a ready market.
This exploration is at a primary stage; a global agency has already been appointed, and a positive turnaround is expected down the line in 6-9 months.
Intention is to remain based in India for production/value-added processes due to cost benefits.

The JV/tie-up would add more value-added processes on existing products, leveraging a partner's expertise and readily available OEM relationships that Rolex currently lacks direct contact with, since starting a new customer relationship can take 15-18 months due to validation/audit activities.
Overseas partners are also inclined to shift to low-cost production countries given their own conversion cost and inflationary pressures.
It is too premature to say whether the JV/tie-up would be in an allied area like defense/aerospace or elsewhere.

subsections.label: Defense and aerospace entry
points: Company has initiated certain steps/registrations for defense; also exploring aerospace with some initial registration/approval/certification obtained.
Revenue contribution will take good time; management is hopeful for something from defense down the line in about 12 months, working aggressively with a third party.
Working closely with a very senior consultant on defense, started about 1.5 months back; focus is on round job or hot forging products that suit existing facility, based on what agencies approve.

subsections.label: Capital allocation strategy
points: First priority is distribution of profits to shareholders/stakeholders — potentially dividends or another round of buyback, following the completed INR180 crore buyback.

subsections.label: Key risks flagged
points: Seasonal labor shortage in April-May-mid June driven by hot summer, out-of-state labor migration for vacation/wedding/agricultural season — a recurring general phenomenon in the industry.
Ocean freight cost spike (2x-3x normal) and container/vessel availability issues due to Hormuz/Europe/Iran/US geopolitical tensions, which may persist into Q2 FY27.
Industrial bearing ring segment stagnancy, particularly domestic and European markets, driven by one large customer group's order cancellations/reductions across 5-7 plants mainly in Europe.
Timken's continued weakness impacting bearing ring exports.
Domestic auto OEMs deferring production plans, impacting domestic auto components revenue in the quarter.
US tariff-related project hold: one customer's 1.75 billion order pipeline project largely on hold except a couple of orders, due to tariffs.

subsections.label: Outlook commentary
points: With the labor situation now fully normalized, Q2 FY27 expected to reflect better strength of the order book without the execution constraint that held back Q1's output.

Company remains confident in mid-teen revenue growth guidance for FY27, on the basis of healthy order book, improving product mix, expanding margins, reengaging export customers, and a clean debt-free balance sheet.
New customer programs onboarded over the past year are progressing well and expected to ramp up further as the year progresses.

Company sees FY26 as a lesson that no business is immune to external disruption, but a business built on strong fundamentals, deep customer relationships, and operational discipline can absorb disruption and come out stronger; Q1 FY27's internal labor constraint reinforced this without denting order book, margins, capabilities or customer relationships.
Ambition remains to be the most trusted precision forging partner for the world's leading bearing and automotive Tier 1, Tier 2 and OEM customers.

guidance_ledger.statement: We remain confident in the mid-teen revenue growth guidance that we have given for fiscal '27.
Maybe more than mid-teen or coming close to the 20% number for fiscal '28.
We expect EBITDA margin to be in the range of 21% to 22% in this fiscal FY27, conservatively.
50 basis points up on the FY27 number would be there in FY28.
Capex in the range of INR30 crores to INR40 crores on an annual basis, year-on-year.
We target to touch somewhere about 70%-72% utilization.
I'm a bit confident to cross between INR425 crores to INR450 crores in auto component exports for FY27.
65% to 70% of revenue would be from auto components this fiscal.

guidance_ledger.metric: Export share of auto components mix
guidance_ledger.statement: More than 75% of the auto components mix would be from exports.
Guidance from customers in the industrial segment indicates marginal growth for the next couple of quarters.
Annualizing 4 months of business, Allison revenue has already crossed FY25 levels; almost on track with fiscal '25 numbers.
Development and revenue on paper from exploring higher size/volume products with Dana (via Allison acquisition) will take a minimum of 12-18 months.
Hopeful for something from defense maybe down the line in 12 months.
Expect a positive turnaround on JV/association front down the line in 6-9 months; global agency already appointed.
Expect better numbers in domestic auto components from Q2 onward as Tier 1/Tier 2 customers' overseas supply gains up.
Container/vessel availability issue may persist to some extent, spilling over to Q2.
US order flows expected to resume meaningfully from Q1 of FY27 as tariffs normalize and customers re-engage.

key_takeaways: Revenue from operations came in at INR304 crores, up 4.3% compared to Q1 FY26; the constraint was not demand but an execution issue — a shortage of labor on the shop floor.
The situation improved from June '26 onwards, and operations were back to running normally by Q2 FY27; July '26 recorded the highest revenue since inception.

Revenue from auto components grew 13.5% YoY to INR163 crores, while revenue from bearing rings declined 6% YoY to INR118 crores, with softness concentrated in the industrial segment, domestic and European markets.

EBITDA for the quarter was INR69 crores (excluding other income), up 12% YoY, with EBITDA margin at 22.6%, up 100 bps YoY; PAT grew 22% YoY to INR60 crores with PAT margin at 19.8%, up 290 bps YoY — the third consecutive quarter of YoY margin expansion.

INR180 crores buyback of 1 crore equity shares concluded during the quarter, with the promoter group not participating; company is now fully debt-free and clear of all legacy CDR obligations, carrying cash surpluses.
Company remains confident in the mid-teen revenue growth guidance for fiscal '27, with EBITDA margin expected in the range of 21% to 22% conservatively.

US market is coming back with customers reengaging after a prolonged period of caution; Europe continues to fire on the back of expanding automotive components presence; company has not lost a single customer through tariff disruption or European war impact.
Current capacity utilization is at 63%-65%, targeted to touch 70%-72% this year, with capex guided in the range of INR30-40 crores annually.

subsections.label: CDR/RoR closure and capital allocation
points: Rolex Rings was admitted to Corporate Debt Restructuring (CDR) in 2013, fully exited CDR by clearing all dues to lenders by 2022.
On 31 March 2026, company honored its Right of Recompense (RoR) obligation in full, making total payment of INR101 crores to consortium lenders; every commitment to every lender has now been met.
With RoR fully settled, company enters next phase with no legacy obligations, no covenants, no restrictions, free to focus on building the business and rewarding shareholders.
In April 2026, Board approved buyback of 1 crore shares at INR180/share aggregating INR180 crores; promoters/promoter group chosen not to participate so full benefit flows to public shareholders.

Company is in process/thought process to offer further dividend but wants to preserve some cash given capital-intensive nature of industry and prevailing global economic uncertainties; buyback to be honored first, dividend consideration next.
RoR element is absolutely finished with no further payments coming up on that front.

subsections.label: Gross margin drivers
points: Gross margin expansion mainly due to positive shift in product mix towards higher-value machine auto components and better raw material management.
Incremental Q4 gross margin also aided by change of steel sourcing from overseas to domestic on certain product processes.
Cutting out custom duty related revenue recognized from Q2/Q3 customer receivables, major factor for incremental GP margin remains product mix and steel sourcing shift.

subsections.label: One-time other expense items (Q4 FY26)
points: Two one-time items explain substantial increase in other expenses in Q4 FY26, not indicative of structural cost increase: (1) ~INR22 crores paid as US customs duties, ~50% of which is yet to be received from customers — company conservatively recognized entire expense this quarter while related revenue will be recorded in Q1/Q2; (2) ~INR6 crores (INR60 million) in legal and professional expenses related to closure of the RoR settlement with consortium lenders — a one-time charge that will not recur.

Duty applicability timing creates lag: duty is payable by company as goods are cleared at US Customs, but customer reimbursement occurs only when they lift material from consignment warehouse per credit terms, creating timing mismatch between expense recognition and revenue/reimbursement recognition.

Company paid duty at rates up to 53% during peak tariff period while customers are expected to reimburse only at the 25% rate now applicable, with the differential recognized as expense; company also expects a refund from the US government (IEEPA-related, pre-November 2025) which will partly need to be repaid to the customer.

Refund is expected only for additional duty (10%, 25%, 50% incremental slabs) paid under IEEPA up to 31 October 2025; duty paid post-Section 232 classification (25% from November 2025) will not be refunded; refund process still involves certain litigation/complexities.

subsections.label: US tariff disruption and recovery
points: Sharp escalation of US import tariffs, peaking over 50% on auto components, created significant headwinds in export business, particularly commercial vehicle/heavy commercial vehicle segment core to US exposure.

A major customer temporarily shut down the relevant plant entirely when duties moved from 3% to 53%; supply to that program went to almost zero; this customer accounts for ~75% of the 30% US revenue loss.
Despite disruption, company has not lost a single US customer; programs remain intact; disruption viewed as tariff-driven and temporary.

With duties normalizing, US order flows expected to resume meaningfully from Q1 FY27; customers who were in wait-and-watch mode through FY26 are re-engaging; recovery pace depends on how quickly customers rebuild inventory pipelines and production schedules.

For last four-five months there has been no change in duty structure except a Supreme Court decision; that decision does not cover Section 232, under which company's product falls (25% duty), which customers and their OEMs have accepted as manageable.
From February 2026 onwards, dispatch levels to the affected customer began returning to pre-slowdown levels; recovery already partially underway.

subsections.label: Europe demand drivers
points: Europe growth (25% in FY26) driven by new plants of existing European customers (including US and Mexico-based plants) where company previously had no presence, with orders won in previous fiscal now ramping up meaningfully from Q1 FY27.

60%+ of new program awards are from European customers, reflecting structural tailwinds: China+1 sourcing strategies, qualification track record, and long-term relationships with global Tier 1 companies.

Europe growth mainly from passenger vehicle and light commercial vehicle segment (~70%), balance from industrial segment (25-30%); European stimulus/economic revival supporting end-use demand despite inflationary conversion/power/labor costs.
Growth in Europe is not from inventory restocking/clearance — these are new customers/new plants with no prior inventory pile-up; growth reflects actual production ramp-up.

New European orders are primarily on the auto components side; company previously had limited auto segment presence in Europe (bearing rings segment somewhat down due to industrial weakness) but now has a good presence in auto components.

subsections.label: Domestic market dynamics
points: Domestic revenue grew 50% YoY with contributions from both bearing rings and auto components; broader set of Indian OEMs and industrial customers recognizing product quality and competitiveness.

Addressable hot-forging bearing ring domestic market estimated at INR1,600-1,800 crores (vs. broader INR2,200 crores range cited in presentation for wider bearing rings business); company holds ~30% share of the addressable segment.

Import substitution trend ongoing — certain higher-range products still imported, but import components have significantly reduced vs two years back; customers diversifying/increasing capacity to produce bigger-size products domestically, though pace of substitution has been slower than expected due to geopolitical disruptions.
Domestic market share expected to grow by 10-15% YoY jump on domestic bearing ring business, though reaching 50-70% share is a multi-year (not 1.5-2 year) journey.
India automotive and industrial markets continue to grow; early contributions emerging from EV and industrial programs, expected to become increasingly meaningful over next 2-3 years.

Import transit periods have stretched a bit but expected to settle in next 3-4 months, with no significant impact on inventory days expected.
Sales-in-transit inventory (per Incoterms with customers) inflates reported annual inventory days to 150-160 days versus 70-85 days on an operational basis.

Some increase in EV traction in the domestic market, but overall ICE market has also grown; company does not foresee significant EV penetration for the next 5-7 years, though it is prepared to produce components (gears, transmission parts, bearings) required for EVs if/when penetration increases.

subsections.label: Growth drivers / diversification

In US, growth has been muted due to duty tariff issues; in dialogue with a couple of industrial bearing companies who are in appraisal process but deferring due to duty matters.

In domestic market, incremental business gained in bearing rings and auto segments over last three years; company now supplies indirectly to domestic OEM car manufacturers through a couple of suppliers, a segment it did not previously address.

key_takeaways: In March 2026, precisely on 31st of March 2026, Rolex Rings has honored its Right of Recompense obligation in full, making total payment of INR101 crores to our consortium lenders. Every commitment made to every lender has now been met. The slate is completely clean.

In April 2026, our Board approved a buyback of 1 crores shares at INR180 per share, aggregating to INR180 crores. The promoters/promoters group has chosen not to participate, ensuring that full benefit of this buyback flows directly to all public shareholders.

The sharp escalation of U.S. import tariffs, which peaked at over 50% on our auto components, created significant headwinds in our export business... On an annualized basis, our U.S. exports were approximately 30% lower than what we had in fiscal '25.

Full year revenue from operations came in at INR1,144 crores broadly, in line with last year revenues. We more than compensated for the U.S. shortfall through strong growth in Europe and a robust domestic performance.
Revenue from Europe grew by almost 25% during the year compared to previous fiscal. And out of that, 60% of our new business nominations came from European customers only.
India continued to perform well. Domestic revenue grew by 50% year-on-year, with both bearing rings and auto components contributing meaningfully.

Though we face challenges in the U.S., I want to be clear, we have not lost a single U.S. customer... The disruption was tariff-driven and temporary. With duties now normalizing, we expect U.S. order flows to resume meaningfully from Q1 of current fiscal, that is FY 2027.

Our gross margin expanded meaningfully from 49.4% to 51.5% in fiscal 2026, reflecting the positive shift in product mix towards higher-value machine auto components and a better raw material management.
Even as the U.S. import tariffs created revenue headwinds, we held EBITDA margins above 20%, a testament to the underlying quality of our business.
Our business generated INR190 crores in our operating cash flow and spent hardly INR36 crores on capex, leaving substantial free cash for the company to deploy.
We are expecting somewhere about 15%, 17% growth in fiscal '27 and obviously, high teen or even beyond that in for fiscal '28.
pressing_questions: Sir, going forward, what are the key growth drivers that we can expect from the company -- in order to address these demand and cyclical challenges that we have across geographies, are there any plans for new product introductions or new customers, any market share gains, anything that you can highlight, sir? (raised regarding structurally constrained growth as demand across the three key geographies rarely remains strong simultaneously)

Sir, my second question is just something bookkeeping... can you give me the segment-wise number, which you regularly give on the call, that is domestic bearings, export bearings, etcetera? (FY25 comparative breakup requested separately)
Since we have 30% market share, who would be our next serious competitor?
Any inorganic opportunities are we looking at since you have some cash on the balance sheet? Any specific segment you're looking at?

HINDALCO.about: Incorporated in 1958, Hindalco Industries Ltd. is a flagship company of the Aditya Birla Group. The Co and its subsidiaries are primarily engaged in the production of Aluminium and Copper. It is also engaged in the manufacturing of aluminium sheet, extrusion and light gauge products for use in packaging markets like beverage and food, can and foil products, etc. [1]

quarters.summary: Management struck a constructive tone: India upstream/downstream and copper posted record EBITDA per ton and margins, Novelis showed resilience despite the Oswego fire impact (viewed as a timing issue), long-term Novelis EBITDA/ton guidance of $600 was reiterated, the fourfold India downstream EBITDA target by FY30 was reiterated, and consolidated net leverage was maintained below the 2x threshold at 1.95x. Key upstream expansion projects (Aditya alumina refinery/smelter, captive coal mines) and Novelis' Bay Minette facility remain on track, while copper concentrate tightness, tariff impacts at Novelis, and West Asia-linked commodity volatility remain watch items.

subsections.label: Brand royalty
points: Ownership of the Aditya Birla brand remains with Birla Group Holdings Private Limited (BGH), which had not charged royalty historically, an exception among large Indian conglomerates.
New royalty framework marks a transition from family-driven stewardship to structured governance; investment in the brand is intended to strengthen it for the future.
Novelis disclosed the royalty in its 10-Q; Hindalco, under SEBI LODR, will disclose related-party transactions biannually via exchange filings due in October.
Royalty amount is below Hindalco's materiality threshold and does not distort capital allocation or dividend policy.
No clarity yet on review period/duration of the royalty arrangement (e.g., 3-year or 5-year review cycles common elsewhere).
Royalty capped at INR225 crores per year each for Hindalco and Novelis, at a rate of up to 0.25% of revenue.

subsections.label: Exceptional items / GAAP differences
points: The consol-level exceptional hit of INR300 crores relates to a difference between US GAAP and Ind AS treatment of the Oswego fire impact; under Ind AS it is shown as exceptional, while under US GAAP it sits in unallocated.
As Oswego restarts and insurance recoveries come in, this exceptional item is expected to go away.

subsections.label: Intercompany elimination
points: Intercompany profit elimination increased by approximately INR750 crores QoQ, due to upstream selling to downstream with a price mismatch requiring revaluation as LME rises; this correction sits within the intercompany elimination line.

subsections.label: Cash cost trends
points: Cash cost increased 4-5% (management restated to 5%) in Q1 FY27 vs Q4 FY26; Q1 benefited from low-cost inventories.
Q2 expected to see coal price increases in the northern region during the monsoon period, driving another 5-6% cost increase Q2 vs Q1.

subsections.label: Leverage and tax
points: Consolidated net debt-to-EBITDA at 1.95x as of June 2026, near the ongoing 2x net leverage threshold.
Effective tax rate under the new tax regime is 26%.
LTIFR (safety metric) at 0.21 for Q1 FY27.

subsections.label: Novelis valuation assumptions
points: Analysts suggested WACC assumptions for Novelis of 9% or 9.2%, versus a suggested baking level of 8-8.5%.

subsections.label: India upstream aluminium
points: Shipments up 3% YoY; revenue up 44% YoY; quarterly EBITDA of INR7,390 crores, up 81% YoY; EBITDA per ton of $2,331.
Record quarterly EBITDA and all-time high EBITDA per ton, backed by favorable macros and strong performance across the value chain.
EBITDA margins at a record 55%, among the best in the global industry.

subsections.label: India downstream aluminium
points: Shipments up 3% YoY to 104 Kt; quarterly EBITDA of INR298 crores, up 30% YoY from INR229 crores in Q1 FY26; EBITDA per ton a little more than $303.
Strong performance driven by higher volumes, product mix and premiumization.

$300/ton margin considered a multi-quarter high but described as not fully sustainable at that level; management guided to ~$250/ton as more sustainable for the remaining quarters given Aditya FRP is still ramping up.
Longer-term (FY29-30 perspective) aluminium downstream EBITDA per ton guided to be over $300.
High MJP (metal premium) helped push margins up on the downstream side, since downstream pricing to customer = metal + MJP + conversion premium.

subsections.label: India copper
points: Overall metal shipments of 105 Kt, down 16% YoY due to planned maintenance shutdown.
CCR volumes of 96 Kt, down 8% YoY due to tighter market conditions.
Record quarterly EBITDA of INR918 crores, up 36% YoY, driven by better realizations in byproducts and operational efficiencies.
Planned maintenance shutdown impacted anode production through the concentrate route; excluding shutdown effect, EBITDA per ton would have been around $1,000, reflecting underlying business strength.
Copper and downstream aluminium volumes expected to be higher in Q2 as electrical sector weakness and planned shutdown effects unwind.

subsections.label: Novelis
points: Shipments of 916 Kt, down 5% YoY from 963 Kt in Q1 FY26; adjusted EBITDA of $516 million, up 24% YoY; adjusted EBITDA per ton of $563, up 30% YoY.

Q1 performance demonstrated resilience despite temporary impact of the Oswego fire, which contributed a net positive $18 million to EBITDA this quarter, including $47 million of insurance proceeds received.
Oswego mill successfully restarted in June and is ramping up steadily toward normal operating levels.
Outage impact viewed largely as a timing issue rather than structural, with a significant portion of current year headwinds expected to be recovered over the course of next fiscal year.
Long-term EBITDA per ton guidance of $600 remains unchanged.

Confidence supported by accelerated execution of the $350-400 million structural cost reduction program, having achieved $225 million in run-rate savings so far, delivering sustainable productivity, efficiency and margin improvements.
Scrap prices continue moving in a positive direction, supporting margin improvement.

Section 232 tariff impact rose to $70 million in Q1 FY27 from $24 million in Q4 FY26, related to Novelis not yet producing enough in the US, requiring more imports; theoretically if all assets run optimally there would be enough onshore capacity, but post-Oswego-fire reconfiguration required more third-party/import dependence to keep customers supplied via lease service.
Management cautioned against simply adding back the $70M tariff impact to imply EBITDA/ton over $600, citing many moving parts including metal prices.
Tariff impact expected to persist at some level for the next couple of quarters as supply chains are reconfigured; not expected to go to zero immediately even after Oswego normalizes.

Own-network material sourcing (vs third-party) changes cost classification: third-party costs go into 'cost of the fire' (below the line), while own-network tariff costs are not classified there — explaining why tariff impact rose this quarter versus earlier quarters when more third-party sourcing was used.
USMCA status uncertain/long drawn out; not expected to have major impact currently, no basis to believe imminent changes.

subsections.label: Alumina
points: Missed one ship sale this quarter, resulting in lower external alumina volume of 138 Kt; next quarter expected to be ~190 Kt.
Global alumina prices slightly picking up from historic lows, currently around $330-340.
Alumina prices expected to remain in this range as long as Middle East smelters remain out of the market, since that is the largest third-party alumina market (China is largely self-sufficient).

subsections.label: India downstream 4x EBITDA ambition breakdown
points: Downstream includes aluminium downstream, aluminium specialty sales, and copper downstream combined — this combined base is targeted to go 4x by FY30, not just aluminium downstream alone.
Cumulative FY25-FY26 EBITDA base for this combined downstream is around INR36-38 billion, targeted to reach INR145-150 billion in 4 years.
Management to provide more clarity on copper downstream contribution specifically in coming quarters, as it is currently merged with other downstream figures.
Downstream margins are progressing better than expected; main challenge is getting products qualified and ramping up volumes.

subsections.label: Upstream expansion projects
points: Aditya Alumina refinery and aluminium smelter expansions progressing well and on track, integral to strategy of doubling upstream capacities while strengthening integration and cost leadership.
Aditya smelter expansion in two phases of 180 pots each; first 180 pots come exactly at the same time as the refinery, in December CY27; next 180 pots in December CY28.
Post both expansions, company expects to remain net long alumina by about 800 Kt, similar to its position today.
Meaningful/full contribution from Aditya refinery and Phase 1 smelter expected only in FY29, since commissioning is December-January of the coming fiscal year.
Aditya alumina refinery order placement is 95% complete.

subsections.label: Captive coal mines
points: Progress continues on Chakla, Bandha, and Meenakshi captive coal mine development projects.
Chakla expected to produce 1 million tons in FY28; Bandha expected to add 0.5 million tons from mid-year, together roughly 1.5-1.6 million tons combined for FY28.
As these mines become operational, they will strengthen resource security, lower production costs, support margin expansion, and enhance the earnings profile of the upstream business.
Management declined to provide a specific per-ton cost reduction estimate for FY28 from Chakla/Bandha coal volumes, saying results will show in due course.

subsections.label: Downstream growth projects
points: Aditya FRP plant ramping up well, already making a meaningful contribution to output.
Aditya battery foil and Taloja AC Fins facilities commissioned last quarter; both progressing well with customer qualification underway.
Specialty alumina/precipitated hydrate facility advancing through customer approval stages, nearing commercialization.

subsections.label: Copper capacity
points: Copper smelter expansion, e-waste recycling projects, and other sustainability-led initiatives progressing as planned.
Inner Grooved Tubes project will further strengthen downstream portfolio and value-added product capabilities.

Copper smelter expansion timed deliberately during adverse conditions since it will take ~3 years to come online; management views long-term demand and precious-metals supply chain as supportive of good returns despite near-term concentrate tightness.
Smelter will use some scrap; additionally, a scrap melting project at Pakhajan is commissioning this year, which is seen as more financially viable and will use significant copper scrap.
Recycling project economics: on a pure copper basis, current returns are more attractive than copper smelting (including sulfuric acid sale); project IRR is in the high teens.

subsections.label: Bauxite/coal auctions
points: Karlapat bauxite auction concluded at 175% premium, implying bauxite cost of about INR8,000/ton.
Company has existing bauxite mines in Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, and Odisha; will maintain a prudent, disciplined financial approach to participating in ongoing/future bauxite auctions.
Management had not heard of the Damchua and Surbena blocks specifically mentioned by an analyst; other auctions ongoing over the next month.

subsections.label: Bay Minette facility
points: Bay Minette facility has a targeted capacity of 600 Kt.

subsections.label: Renewable energy capacity
points: Renewable energy capacity (solar/wind/hydro) at 470 MW as of end Q1 FY27, plus 35 MW pump storage tie-up capacity.
Planned additional 414 MW of solar & wind capacity and 90 MW of RE RTC pump storage capacity during the year.
Expected total renewable portfolio (solar/wind/hydel) of 884 MW and RE RTC capacity of 125 MW by end FY27.
Aluminium-specific GHG footprint at 19 tons CO2/ton aluminium in Q1 FY27; aluminium recycling rate improved to 29% from 27% in Q1 FY26.

subsections.label: Working capital normalization
points: Novelis expects to release cash via reduction of inventory and reduction of payables as it normalizes working capital cycle and reduces third-party material buying.
Directionally $300-400M expected in the next couple of quarters, with potential to do better.

subsections.label: Insurance recovery timeline
points: Cumulative cash flow impact from Oswego fire of $1.4 billion so far, net of $300 million recoveries received to date.
Timing of recoveries is difficult to predict precisely; expected final net cash impact after all recoveries is approximately $600 million.
A couple hundred million may fall into FY28, but a decent recovery is expected within the current fiscal year.

subsections.label: Copper concentrate supply chain
points: Company has 85% of its concentrate requirements blocked in, indicating no security-of-supply issue for concentrate at present.

Exploring copper mines within India and neighboring countries for backward integration, but questions the economics of paying for mine equity at current elevated LME-driven mine valuations (e.g., South America, Australia).
One copper exploration block under evaluation with drilling ongoing; preliminary samples look good, though extent/volumes will take more than another year to evaluate; more blocks expected to come.

subsections.label: Flyash logistics
points: Flyash dispatches were temporarily impacted by rail rake availability, despite strong demand for flyash and bauxite residue across cement, road construction, and quarry backfilling applications.

subsections.label: Aluminum price volatility
points: Even before the Mid East conflict escalated, aluminum prices had strengthened largely due to closure of the Mozal smelter, reaching around $3,150/ton.
Heightened concerns over potential supply disruptions drove prices sharply higher to a peak of $3,850/ton before moderating to $3,200/ton following the ceasefire.
Management remains constructive on aluminum: market expected to have a wider deficit than pre-conflict expectations (1 million tons vs 0.3 million tons for CY26).

Higher prices likely to incentivize supply response including smelter restarts in Europe and West Asia and faster ramp-ups in Indonesia and Southeast Asia, helping rebalance the market over the medium term.

subsections.label: Global aluminum demand/supply dynamics
points: Q1 CY26: Chinese aluminum production up 3% YoY to ~11 million tons, while ex-China production declined 8% YoY to 7 million tons; global production of 18 million tons down 1% YoY.
China consumption growth of 2% (~12 million tons) driven by strong demand from new energy vehicles and robust exports of semi-fabricated and finished products; property sector remains weak.
Outside China, demand declined 2% as softer conditions in Europe, North America and Middle East more than offset growth in India.
Global consumption grew 1% YoY to ~19 million tons; demand continues to outpace supply, with the market in a deficit of ~1 million tons in Q1 CY26, providing continued support to fundamentals.

subsections.label: India aluminum demand drivers
points: India aluminum demand of ~1.5 million tons, up ~3% YoY, driven by automotive (supported by GST 2.0 related benefits and continued vehicle production growth), packaging, industrial machinery, and consumer durable segments.
Electrical segment saw moderation as certain contractor-led projects were deferred due to price volatility during the quarter.
India continues to outgrow global aluminum demand and remains one of the most attractive long-term growth markets for the industry.
Flat rolled products demand growth of >10% YoY driven primarily by strong demand from packaging and consumer durable.

subsections.label: India copper demand
points: India copper demand (incl. domestic supplies & scrap) of 359 Kt, down 9% YoY from 396 Kt in Q1 FY26, driven by inventory optimization by customers and a more cautious purchasing approach amid uncertainties arising from the West India conflict.

subsections.label: Global copper concentrate market
points: Global copper production up 2.6% YoY to 7.2 million tons vs consumption of 7.5 million tons in Q2 CY26, resulting in a net deficit of ~0.3 million tons.
Concentrate availability tight across the industry; TC/RCs at historically low levels (range of -26 to -30 cents/pound), at times negative.
Reflects broader trend of global smelting capacity growing faster than mine supply availability.
Stronger byproduct credits provided some support to smelter economics, but concentrate supply remains the key constraint.
Tight market conditions expected to persist, with concentrate availability and TC/RC likely to remain under pressure throughout the rest of the year.

subsections.label: Sulfuric acid / sulfur pricing
points: Sulfuric acid prices staying elevated, expected similar level in Q2 as Q1.
Sulfuric acid prices driven by the sulfur index, which is currently high due to impact of the West Asia crisis.
Company is counting on sulfur/sulfuric acid revenue given low TC/RCs; management hopes there is no tapering off in H2, though sulfur index remains elevated.

subsections.label: MJP (metal premium)
points: MJP is up because Middle East supplies to Japan and Korea have been impacted.
MJP expected to stay slightly high as long as that Middle East metal is out of the market, likely coming down next year once Middle East smelters are back.
Company trying to capture a bit more exports given elevated MJP, but not significantly changing domestic/export sales mix given downstream requirements and still-good domestic market returns.

subsections.label: India downstream 4x EBITDA ambition
points: Accelerating upstream expansion in both aluminum and copper while building a significantly strong downstream portfolio, with the ambition of a fourfold increase in downstream EBITDA by FY30.

subsections.label: Novelis 3x30 strategy
points: Novelis remains focused on executing the mid- to long-term 3x30 strategy, aimed at driving sustainable growth, higher profitability and stronger returns.

subsections.label: Brand royalty governance transition
points: New royalty framework for use of Aditya Birla Group marks transition from family-driven stewardship to structured governance across the group, applying to both Hindalco and Novelis at 0.25% of revenue capped at INR225 crores/year each.

subsections.label: Backward integration in copper
points: Evaluating copper exploration blocks within India and in neighboring countries as part of backward integration strategy, though management does not see urgency given 85% concentrate coverage and expensive mine equity valuations globally.

subsections.label: Hedging program
points: For the rest of FY27, 29% of aluminum commodity exposure hedged at $3,004/ton, and 18% of currency exposure hedged at INR91.63/USD.
For FY28, 21% of aluminum commodity exposure hedged at $3,160/ton, with a target level noted around $3,200/ton.

subsections.label: Macro risks
points: Global growth projected at 3% in CY2026 vs 3.5% in CY2025, vulnerable to renewed geopolitical tension, commodity price volatility, tighter financial conditions, trade fragmentation, and a possible correction in technology-related expectations.
Global inflation projected to rise to 4.7% in CY2026 from 4.1% in CY2025, reflecting higher energy, food and fertilizer prices, signaling a temporary pause in the global disinflation process.
Middle East & Central Asia growth expected to slow sharply to 0.7% in CY2026 from 3.7% in CY2025; US growth projected at 2.3% (from 2.1%); China growth projected at 4.6%, down from a prior 5%.
India GDP growth projected at 6.7% for FY27 (RBI projection) vs 7.7% in 2025; India inflation projected at 5% for FY27 vs 2.1% in FY26.
India downside risks include geopolitical uncertainties, volatility in global financial markets, external headwinds and weather-related disruptions.
India inflation upside risk from global commodity price shocks, monsoon uncertainty and El Nino conditions.
RBI has retained a neutral policy stance, balancing growth support and price stability.

subsections.label: West Asia conflict impact
points: War created negative supply shock through higher energy and commodity prices, partially offset by strong technology-led investment and demand.
Direct disruption to Middle East & Central Asia growth.
Aluminum price spike to $3,850/ton and moderation to $3,200/ton tied to conflict escalation and subsequent ceasefire.
Copper refined demand in India subdued due to customer caution amid uncertainties from the conflict.
MJP elevated due to Middle East supply disruptions to Japan/Korea; sulfuric acid/sulfur prices elevated due to the crisis.

subsections.label: Tariff / trade policy risk (Novelis)
points: Section 232 tariff impact of $70 million this quarter tied to import dependence while Oswego ramps back up; expected to persist at some level for the next couple of quarters.
USMCA status uncertain amid ongoing back-and-forth between US and Canadian governments; no major impact currently expected but situation is being monitored.

subsections.label: Copper concentrate market risk
points: TC/RCs at historically low, sometimes negative levels; concentrate availability tight and expected to remain under pressure through the rest of the year.
Global smelting capacity growing faster than mine supply availability, a structural constraint on the industry.

subsections.label: Operational risk (Oswego fire)
points: Oswego fire caused temporary production impact at Novelis; mill restarted in June with steady ramp-up; viewed as timing issue with headwinds expected to substantially recover next fiscal year.
Cumulative net cash flow impact from the fire has been $1.4 billion, with final net cost after all insurance recoveries expected to be approximately $600 million.

subsections.label: Electrical segment weakness (India)
points: Electrical segment demand moderated as certain contractor-led projects were deferred due to price volatility during the quarter.

subsections.label: ESG / carbon regulation risk
points: CBAM and evolving carbon pricing mechanisms (Europe at ~EUR80/ton carbon, developing India CTS platform) flagged as more significant risks than lack of consistency in low-carbon aluminium definitions across markets.

No consistency across markets today on what constitutes low-carbon aluminium; Platts index shows negligible price upside ($15-20/ton) for low-carbon aluminium currently, with the low-carbon threshold generally defined around 6 tons CO2 per ton aluminium.

subsections.label: General outlook
points: Overall, Hindalco is exceptionally well positioned for the future, backed by integrated business model, strong resource base, disciplined capital allocation and growth investments across the value chain.
Management expects a good FY27 overall, with strength across upstream, downstream, Novelis, and copper.
Novelis performance in Q1 expected to get better going forward this year.
India business is in a high capex year, so net debt-to-EBITDA is not expected to materially change across coming quarters; if Novelis leverage comes down in Q4, consol leverage should follow.
Hindalco consolidated net leverage target of ~2x on an ongoing basis.

subsections.label: Novelis outlook
points: Long-term EBITDA per ton guidance of $600 unchanged.
Structural cost reduction target of $350-400 million by FY28 exit, with $225 million in run-rate savings already achieved as of Q1 FY27.
Novelis consolidated net leverage expected to be below 4x going forward, with a peak expectation of ~4.5x moving a little higher by end of the September quarter.
Working capital release of $300-400 million guided over the next couple of quarters.
Expected final net cash impact from the Oswego fire of approximately $600 million cumulative, post all recoveries.

subsections.label: India downstream EBITDA target
points: India downstream EBITDA targeted to grow fourfold (4x) by FY30, from a cumulative FY25-FY26 base of ~INR36-38 billion to a target range of INR145,000-150,000 crores (INR145-150 billion per analyst framing) by FY30.

subsections.label: Near-term operational guidance
points: Q2 FY27 cash cost expected to increase 5-6% vs Q1 FY27, driven by monsoon-related coal price increases in northern India.
Next quarter external alumina sales expected at ~190 Kt, recovering from a missed ship sale in Q1.
Sulfuric acid EBITDA contribution expected to be similar in Q2 to Q1.
India downstream aluminium EBITDA/ton guided at ~$250 sustainable for remaining quarters of FY27, rising to over $300/ton longer-term (FY29-30).
Chakla captive coal mine expected to produce 1 million tons in FY28; Bandha expected to add 0.5 million tons from mid-year.
Meaningful contribution from Aditya refinery and Phase 1 smelter expansion expected only in FY29.

subsections.label: Hedging guidance
points: For the rest of FY27, 29% of aluminum commodity exposure hedged at $3,004/ton, and 18% of currency exposure hedged at INR91.63/USD.
For FY28, 21% of aluminum commodity exposure hedged at $3,160/ton, with a target level noted around $3,200/ton.

guidance_ledger.statement: Importantly, our long-term EBITDA per ton guidance of $600 remains unchanged.
We remain committed to our 3-year goal of permanently reducing our cost structure by $350 million to $400 million by FY28 exit.
With another quarter of solid execution behind us, run rate cost savings are now at $225 million as we accelerate all cost efficiency initiatives.

guidance_ledger.metric: Bay Minette rolling & recycling facility completion
guidance_ledger.statement: The 600 KT Bay Minette greenfield rolling and recycling facility is on track for completion this year, with initial commissioning of key assets already underway.
Accelerating upstream expansion while building a strong downstream portfolio with the ambition of delivering a fourfold increase in downstream EBITDA by FY30.
At Novelis, we remain focused on executing the mid- to long-term 3X30 strategy, aimed at driving sustainable growth, higher profitability and stronger returns.
We remain disciplined in our capital allocation approach and committed to maintain net leverage at around 2x on a consol basis.
Based on all the visibility that I can see right now, we will be below 4x; leverage will move up a little at end of September before coming down through both lower net debt and higher EBITDA.
On the India side, this is a high capex year for us, so I don't expect our net debt-to-EBITDA to materially change across the coming quarters.
We will try to give more clarity on the total downstream probably in the next quarter.
We have been sort of targeting more around the USD250 for the remaining quarters of this year because Aditya FRP is just ramping up.
The longer-term aluminum downstream EBITDA per ton, we have always said it's going to be over $300.
Chakla is expected to produce about 1 million tons.
Bandha will only start from the middle of the year, expecting about 0.5 million tons for Bandha.
FY29 as the full, meaningful numbers coming in, because it commissions December to January of the coming fiscal year.
Next quarter, we will be selling about 190 kt of external alumina.
Sulfuric acid prices staying elevated, so it would be fair to say a similar number like Q1 for Q2.
We are expecting maybe another 5% to 6% increase Q2 to Q1 due to higher coal prices in the northern region during monsoon.
Our hedging positions in aluminum for the rest of FY27 stands at around 29% on the commodity at USD3,004 per ton and 18% in the currency at INR91.63 per USD.
For FY28 currently we are at 21% at 3,160 and we are trying to catch levels at 3,200; our view on FY28 is that once the Middle East smelters come back, 3,200 is a good level for FY28.
Directionally I can see 300 to 400 million coming in the system in the next couple of quarters.

guidance_ledger.metric: Net cash impact from Oswego fire
guidance_ledger.statement: At the end, when all insurance recoveries come, our net loss cash impact from the fire will be about 600 million; a couple hundred million may go into FY28 but a decent recovery will happen within this fiscal year.
For the next couple of quarters, there will be some level of tariffs; it will not go to zero until supply chains are set back in order.

guidance_ledger.metric: India aluminium downstream and copper volumes
guidance_ledger.statement: The volumes in Q2, both for copper and downstream aluminum will be higher.
As long as the Middle East smelters are out, alumina prices will remain in the $330-340 range, since that is the largest third-party alumina market.
MJP will stay slightly high as long as Middle East metal is out of the market, and probably next year it will come down once Middle East smelters are back.

Back in April 2025, we set an FY26 exit savings run rate target of $75 million, which we raised last quarter to $125 million. With another quarter of solid execution behind us, that run rate is now $200 million.

guidance_ledger.metric: Bay Minette EBITDA per ton (post ramp-up)
guidance_ledger.statement: The overall EBITDA per ton that we've been talking about off that facility would be north of $1,000 per ton.
Novelis continues to execute its mid- to long-term 3 by 30 strategy, focusing on delivering sustainable growth and enhance profitability by 2030.
We remain committed to maintain our net leverage around 2 times at the consol level.
Consolidated net debt peak should be between INR80,000 crores and INR90,000 crores over the next 2 years.
In FY27, the India capex will be about INR12,000 crores.

risk_register.risk: West Asia conflict-driven commodity market disruption

risk_register.risk: Copper TC/RC and concentrate tightness
risk_register.note: TC/RCs at historically low, at times negative levels (-26 to -30 cents/lb); concentrate availability tight and expected to remain under pressure through rest of the year as global smelting capacity outpaces mine supply.

risk_register.risk: Novelis Section 232 tariff exposure
risk_register.note: Tariff impact rose to $70 million this quarter from $24 million in the prior quarter due to increased import dependence while Oswego ramps back; expected to persist at some level for the next couple of quarters.

risk_register.risk: USMCA policy uncertainty

risk_register.risk: Novelis Oswego fire operational impact

risk_register.risk: India Electrical segment demand deferral

risk_register.risk: Macro growth slowdown / geopolitical & inflation risk

risk_register.risk: CBAM / carbon pricing regulation

risk_register.risk: Flyash dispatch logistics constraint

risk_register.risk: Geopolitical conflict in West Asia impacting global growth, supply chains and commodity markets

risk_register.risk: Novelis Oswego plant fire outage

risk_register.risk: Cost inflation (furnace oil, CP coke, pitch)

themes.label: Bay Minette expansion

themes.label: Copper TC/RC and sulfuric acid tightness

themes.label: India upstream capacity doubling
themes.note: Aditya Alumina refinery and aluminium smelter expansions progressing well and on track, integral to strategy of doubling upstream capacities and strengthening integration and cost leadership.

themes.label: Captive coal mine ramp-up

key_takeaways: Consolidated business segment EBITDA was up 58% year-on-year at INR13,481 crores this quarter; consolidated profit after tax was up 75% year-on-year at INR7,013 crores.
At Hindalco India business, business segment EBITDA was up 73% year-on-year at INR8,606 crores; quarterly profit after tax was INR5,301 crores, up 86% year-on-year.
India upstream aluminium delivered a record quarterly EBITDA of INR7,390 crores, up 81% year-on-year, an all-time high EBITDA of USD2,331 per ton, and record EBITDA margins of 55%.
India copper business posted a record quarterly EBITDA of INR918 crores, up 36% year-on-year, on better byproduct realizations and operational efficiencies.

Novelis recorded adjusted EBITDA of $516 million or $563 per ton, up 24% and 30% respectively year-on-year, including an $18 million net positive impact from the Oswego fires and $47 million insurance proceeds; run rate cost savings now at $225 million.
Long-term Novelis EBITDA per ton guidance of $600 remains unchanged, supported by the $350-400 million structural cost reduction program.
Consolidated net debt-to-EBITDA stood at 1.95x as of June 2026, below the stated threshold of 2x, despite the temporary impact of the Oswego fire incident.
Ambition of a fourfold increase in India downstream EBITDA by FY30 reiterated, with all key upstream expansion projects (Aditya alumina refinery and aluminium smelter) progressing well and on track.

New brand royalty framework: Hindalco and Novelis will each pay up to 0.25% of revenue to Birla Group Holdings Private Limited, capped at INR225 crores per year, described as below materiality threshold with no impact on capital allocation or dividend policy.
pressing_questions: In the Novelis 10-Q, it is mentioned that Novelis will pay up to 0.25% of revenue as royalty to an entity — clarification sought on what that is and why it is being paid from Novelis.

There have been many investor questions on the USD70 million of tariff at Novelis; if excluded, EBITDA per ton would have been more than USD600 per ton — why did the tariff impact increase significantly from USD24 million last quarter to USD70 million, and why is that not excluded from adjusted EBITDA?

Given the target net leverage of 4x for Novelis is essentially a function of either net debt coming down or EBITDA going up, and given EBITDA run-rate implies leverage is already near 4x, can we not expect a level well below 4x?
Would it be possible to quantify the extent of working capital release over the next 3 quarters at Novelis?
How should the downstream EBITDA target of INR145-150 billion by FY30 be reconciled with a current cumulative FY25-26 base of only INR36-38 billion?
Can you give a per-ton cost reduction figure for FY28 from the captive coal volumes (Chakla and Bandha)?

quarters.summary: Consolidated EBITDA up 11% YoY at INR10,812 crores; PAT down 51% YoY due to exceptional items (Novelis Oswego fire) but adjusted PAT up 10% YoY. India business, copper and aluminium upstream/downstream all delivered strong performance; Novelis navigated Oswego fire and tariff headwinds with adjusted EBITDA/ton close to $500 and long-term guidance of $600/ton intact. Management expects Novelis to recover in FY27 (Oswego restart, Bay Minette commissioning), India upstream expansion (Aditya smelter/refinery, captive coal mines) to progress on track, and copper business to benefit from tight TC/RCs and elevated sulfuric acid prices near-term before normalizing.

Precipitate hydrate facility (specialty alumina) commissioned this quarter, undergoing customer approvals.
Copper smelter expansion, e-waste recycling and sustainability-led initiatives progressing as planned; copper smelter will take about 3 years and is just starting.
Inner grooved tubes project (35 KT copper tube for air conditioning) in trial runs/customer qualification.
Pakhajan 50 KT e-waste recycling plant to commission in August, processing copper e-waste scrap.

Battery-grade copper foil facility being planned at smaller capacity than earlier envisaged (previously guided FY28) as battery manufacturing in India has not taken off as fast as expected; smaller capacity based partly on exports to come in next 2 years.

Coal mix in Q4: 61% linkage, 30.7% e-auction, remainder from own mines.
Global aluminium cost curve for majority of Western smelters is at least $300-400 higher than India, placing the broader cost curve around $2,000-2,200 per ton.

Captive coal mines aim to standardize and flatten the cost curve over the next 15-20 years by controlling coal supply and pricing, even though today's spot auction coal prices are currently low (Chakla and Bandha expected at similar level to today's price; Meenakshi will still be substantially lower than today's prices).

subsections.label: Aluminium price/supply dynamics
points: Aluminium prices continued to strengthen during the quarter, supported by steady demand across packaging, electrical, machinery and transportation.
Conflict in West Asia has led to one of the most significant supply disruptions in the aluminium market, expected to tighten availability particularly through Q2 and Q3 of CY26.
Market deficit estimate revised from 0.3 million tons to 1.5 million tons for CY26, expected to support prices and drive visible inventory drawdowns.
Supply response expected including restarts in Europe and West Asia and faster ramp-ups in Indonesia and Southeast Asia, helping rebalance the market over the medium term.

subsections.label: China and global market balance
points: China production increase in Yunnan largely offset by closures in Shandong; consumption moderated on softness in building & construction, solar, and NEVs, resulting in a broadly balanced Chinese market.

Rest of world production increased on Indonesia and Spain capacity additions, partly offset by lower West Asia output; consumption softened on transport weakness, though packaging and electrical demand remained resilient, leading to a surplus.

subsections.label: India aluminium demand drivers
points: Growth broad-based, supported by structural drivers in automotive, continued strength in electrical demand, and stable packaging demand.
Indian market continues to outperform global markets on stronger underlying demand fundamentals.

subsections.label: India copper demand drivers
points: Strong growth driven by infrastructure investment, increased electrical applications and strong sectoral demand particularly from white goods and winding wires.

subsections.label: Global copper concentrate market
points: Remains in an unprecedented tight phase in 2026 driven by structural mismatch between smelting capacity and mine supply.
Spot TC/RCs crunched to record lows as stronger sulfuric acid realizations partially offset weaker treatment terms, sustaining smelter buying interest.

Tight environment expected to persist through the year; any restart/ramp-up of key mining operations in Africa or Central America (e.g., Grasberg, Cobre Panama) could relieve tightness and lead to some TC/RC recovery.
More than 85% of copper is contracted at the benchmark, so company will get TC/RCs close to zero or slightly negative this year.

subsections.label: Premiums and inventories
points: Global aluminium inventory around 8 million tons (40 days), dramatically down especially with the West Asia conflict.

Premiums reflect local phenomena: MJP up due to freight increases and low Japan availability; Midwest up due to Trump tariffs (50%) being baked into the premium rather than reflected in LME, as majority of primary aluminium into the US comes from Canada; ECDP driven by other local factors.
LME reflects global supply/demand while premiums reflect local availability and transportation costs.
Delta between domestic realization and export narrowed with Midwest at $380; exports may be slightly higher in Q1.

India risks tilted to the downside, conditional on further escalation and widespread conflict, heightened volatility in global financial markets, and weather-related events.

Global copper concentrate market tightness driven by supply issues at Grasberg and the Cobre mine in Panama; any restart could ease TC/RC negativity.

risk_register.note: 3 fatalities reported at Indian operations during FY26 despite LTIFR improving to 0.23; company committed to corrective actions.

risk_register.risk: Battery manufacturing demand in India slower than expected
risk_register.note: Battery-grade copper foil facility being scaled down/delayed as battery manufacturing in India has not taken off as fast as expected.

themes.label: Novelis Oswego fire recovery
themes.note: Oswego fire cut Q4 shipments by 73 KT and EBITDA by $53 million, but Hot Mill is on track to restart in the next few weeks with recovery expected in FY27.

themes.label: Bay Minette expansion
themes.note: 600 KT greenfield rolling and recycling facility scheduled for completion this year, targeting commercial coils by FY28 and EBITDA/ton north of $1,000 post full ramp-up.

themes.label: Copper TC/RC and sulfuric acid tightness
themes.note: Negative TC/RCs and elevated sulfuric acid prices (driven by West Asia conflict and China export curbs) boosted Q4 copper EBITDA to a record INR907 crores, though management sees this normalizing toward INR600-700 crores/quarter beyond Q1FY27.

themes.label: India upstream capacity doubling
themes.note: Aditya Alumina Refinery and Aluminium Smelter expansions on track as part of the strategy to double upstream capacities, with first 180 pots commissioning December CY27.

themes.label: Captive coal mine ramp-up
themes.note: Chakla, Bandha and Meenakshi progressing through clearance/box-cut stages; meaningful volumes expected only from FY28 (Chakla) and FY29 (Meenakshi), aimed at flattening the cost curve over 15-20 years.

themes.label: West Asia conflict-driven commodity market disruption
themes.note: Aluminium market deficit for CY26 revised sharply upward to 1.5 million tons from 0.3 million tons, supporting prices, while also driving cost inflation (furnace oil) and copper/sulfuric acid price volatility.

themes.label: Balance sheet and leverage discipline
themes.note: Consolidated net debt-to-EBITDA maintained below 2x at 1.83, with management guiding a peak consolidated net debt of INR80,000-90,000 crores over the next 2 years amid aggressive capex.

key_takeaways: Our consolidated business segment EBITDA was up 11% year-on-year at INR10,812 crores this quarter.
The consolidated profit after tax was down 51% on a year-on basis at INR2,597 crores this quarter due to the impact of exceptional items, including the impact of the Novelis Oswego plant fire.
If we adjust the impact of this exceptional item, our consolidated PAT stands at INR5,796 crores this quarter, up 10% year-on-year versus the prior period.

At Hindalco India business, our business segment EBITDA was up 17% year-on-year at INR6,610 crores this quarter, whereas our quarterly profit after tax was at INR3,549 crores, up 11% on a year-on-year basis.

Novelis recorded a shipment of 917 KT after adjusting for 73 KT lower shipments due to Oswego fire, reflecting a decline of 4% year-on-year over 957 KT shipments in the same period last year. Adjusted EBITDA for the quarter stood at $498 million or $543 per ton, reflecting a 5% year-on-year.
Importantly, our long-term guidance of $600 per ton remains intact, supported by accelerated execution of our $350 million to $400 million structural cost reduction program.
At the consolidated level, we continue to maintain a strong balance sheet with net debt-to-EBITDA below 2 times at 1.83 at the end of March 2026.

All our key upstream expansion projects, including Aditya Alumina Refinery and Aluminium Smelters are progressing well and remain on track as we advance with our strategy of doubling our upstream capacities.
Our strategic priorities are clearly defined in our accelerating upstream expansion in aluminium and copper, while driving a fourfold increase in downstream EBITDA in India by FY30.
pressing_questions: Sumangal Nevatia: On overall, on the cost, can we share what is our outlook on the aluminium cost of production going up or down in the coming quarters? And with respect to the coal mines, given now we are very close to commissioning, is it possible to share what sort of volumes we are expecting in FY27, FY28 from captive coal?

Pinakin: FY26 capex was INR31,619 crores, primarily given the surge in capex at Novelis. Now can you give us a sense of the consol capex across India and Novelis over the next 3 years, how it will play out between the two businesses?
Indrajit Agarwal: Do you have a peak net debt number in mind? I understand you have a net debt-to-EBITDA number in mind, but absolute net debt number, do you have something in mind on that?

Parthiv Jhonsa: Do you expect that this INR900 crores of EBITDA on a quarterly basis is a new normal till the time global headwinds are not clear? Or should we expect this to remain around say, INR900 crores to INR1,000-odd crores on a quarterly basis?

Vikash Singh: This Bay Minette cold mill, which we are going to operationalize, just wanted to understand how would be the spreads on the cold rolling only until your hot mill comes into play? And given that the overall commissioning would take a year's time, how should we look at the fixed cost associated with that startup?

Ritesh Shah: Power has been chased by several other industries, primarily data centers globally. Given we have the advantage of procuring local coal, how do you see the cost differential, say, for Hindalco versus Rest of the world? How structural you see and some outlook over there would be quite helpful.

HORIZONIND.about: Incorporated in 2009, Horizon Industrial Parks, backed by Blackstone Group, is India’s largest industrial and logistics infrastructure developer, owner, and operator by total network.[1]

quarters.summary: Horizon delivered its strongest-ever quarter (Q1 FY27) with 23% YoY revenue growth and 80% EBITDA margin, closed a landmark IPO raising INR4,250 crores that materially deleveraged the balance sheet, and guided to continued double-digit growth via contractual escalations, large-park development, in-city expansion and value-added services, with management expecting the reported P&L to turn profitable from Q2/Q3 FY27 onward.

subsections.label: Profitability drivers
points: Net loss of INR12 crores for Q1 FY27 continues to be impacted by non-cash depreciation and interest expense.
Cash depreciation in the business is negligible given new assets.
Significant interest savings expected post the INR3,900 crores (39 billion) of deleveraging.
Adjusting for non-cash depreciation and interest impact, pro forma cash PAT stands at INR116 crores.
Strong internal accruals combined with balance sheet headroom position Horizon to reinvest and maximize shareholder value.

FY26 net loss came in worse than forecast (about 3.5x), but management views the P&L loss differently from cash PAT after adjusting for non-cash book depreciation (~INR75 crores quarterly) and pro forma interest savings from debt paydown.
Management guidance: P&L expected to turn profitable (black) from Q2/Q3 FY27 onward.

subsections.label: Leverage & Capital Structure
points: IPO in August 2026 raised INR4,250 crores of fresh primary capital, deployed for deleveraging, bringing net debt down to INR2,500 crores proforma as of end-June, or 12.5% of enterprise value.
Total capital raised between December 2025 and August 2026 was INR4,250 crores, with INR3,900 crores of debt repaid/paid down post-IPO.
IPO fundamentally changes Horizon's growth profile — stronger balance sheet, access to capital markets, financial flexibility.
Growth headroom in the company is expected to fund capex going forward; capex requirement of INR1,500-2,000 crores over next 3 years to be funded roughly 1/3 internally and 2/3 via incremental debt.
Current cost of debt is about 8.2%; post-deleveraging, credit ratings expected to improve materially, bringing cost down by 40-50 basis points.
Yield on capex for the incremental 25 million sq ft pipeline guided at 13-14%.

subsections.label: Leasing & Re-leasing Dynamics
points: Leased 1.9 million sq ft across 13 transactions in Q1 FY27, onboarding 9 new customers and adding INR65 crores of incremental contracted revenue.
Contracted revenue run rate reached nearly INR970 crores (also cited as INR967 crores) as of end June 2026, growing strongly.
Three-fourths (75%) of quarter's leasing came from industrial customers.

Company demonstrated healthy re-leasing spreads (12% in Q1) well ahead of the 5% contractual escalation; historically 12-15% re-leasing spreads seen in past years; about 300,000 sq ft has expired and been re-leased this year.
WALL of about 7.1 years underpins large re-leasing growth opportunity.

About 13% of portfolio (~4 million sq ft) comes up for expiry over next 21 months (1.4 million sq ft in next 9 months of this fiscal, 2.2 million sq ft next fiscal), being tracked closely with good conversations underway.

subsections.label: Development-to-Revenue Translation
points: Of 29.3-29.5 million sq ft operational platform, 26.9 million sq ft is operational today and will see near-full realization over next 12 months; balance 2.4 million sq ft is pre-leased, currently under construction with completion in 6-9 months plus 3 months stabilization (9-12 months total).

FY27 target: 6.5 million sq ft of leasing (~30% growth vs last fiscal), with 5 more million sq ft of buildings to be delivered over the next 9 months and 4-4.5 million sq ft of incremental leases to be signed.
By fiscal year-end, operational assets expected to reach ~34-35 million sq ft, with occupancies targeted in high-90% range.
About 80-85% of contracted revenue run rate is on existing assets (near-full 12-month revenue realization within 12 months); remaining 2.4 million sq ft has ~9-month average stabilization period.

subsections.label: Rental Pricing Trends
points: High single-digit market rent growth seen in deeper micro-markets, contributing to re-leasing spread outperformance versus the 5% contractual escalation.
In-place base rent plus CAM currently INR27.20 per sq ft.
Industrial segment rents run about 20% above standard bare-bone warehousing rents (INR29+ vs INR24 per sq ft), reflecting a 15-20% average premium.
In-city multi-story asset rentals guided at INR70-75 per sq ft, versus INR65-70 per sq ft for existing mid-mile assets.

subsections.label: Development Cycle & Pre-leasing Practice
points: Build cycles typically take 9-12 months.
Pre-leased area of development stood at 2.4 million sq ft as of 30 June 2026; company typically manages about 20-30% of development cycle through pre-leases.
Of the remaining 70-75% not pre-leased, half gets leased during construction and half is kept as stock-in-trade.
Current stock-in-trade area is about 1.6 million sq ft as of 30 June 2026, out of the ~29.5 million sq ft operational platform.
