subsections.label: Deal structure & rationale
points: Arvind Advanced Materials Limited (AAML) acquired 61% stake in Dalco-GFT at a valuation of 7.75x CY2025 reported EBITDA, transaction valued at $136 million.
Entire existing top management of Dalco-GFT will continue, aligned with vision of taking the company forward.
Deal is margin accretive and EPS accretive at Arvind consolidated level.
Acquisition funded through a combination of debt at AAML and debt at Dalco-GFT to take benefit of taxation at both geographies.
Financial ratios post-acquisition are within existing covenants signed; expected to improve within 12 months.
All financing transactions closed and completed as of the call date; consolidation starts immediately from day of the call.

Structured to acquire balance stake in 2 tranches — one in 2 years, another at 4 years — with residual equity from the financial investor sponsor going away over time, while management's equity is retained longer (weighted more towards year 4).
Founder/management retains ~16-17% stake for the entire 4-year period, with alignment via newly redone performance-linked long-term incentives for the entire management team.
Rationale for seller exit: two promoters built the company from insignificant scale; want to partially realize wealth created; financial sponsor's objective was to build and exit.
Deal done through a competitive process; management believes fair value was paid given company's growth, quality of management, synergy potential, and global footprint aspiration.

subsections.label: Ownership & equity math (raised by analyst Monish Ghodke)
points: EV of acquisition is about $136 million; ~$16-17 million net debt in the company; purchasing ~70% economic interest for an outlay of $84-85 million.
Total equity value of the company pre-deal is about $120 million; sellers retain $35-36 million of that equity rolling into the new entity.
Resulting total equity value is about $86 million, of which seller holds $35-36 million, yielding AAML's resulting ~61% stake due to debt taken at the US level.
Existing shareholders (sellers) are also participating in the debt, which is why the ownership numbers work out as described.

subsections.label: Debt financing details
points: $50 million total debt at the US entity (up from $15 million pre-deal, i.e., $35 million incremental) and $60 million raised in India (AAML level).
Cost of debt: ~5.5% (US dollar terms, based on current SOFR) and ~6% for AAML (India) given Arvind's high credit rating.
Arvind Group historically avoids long-term debt on its books; this opportunity was funded via debt because it was deemed highly attractive.
5-year loan raised; management's aim is to wind down this debt over the next couple of years.

subsections.label: Management continuity & incentive alignment
points: Entire existing management team retained, including founder Joey Duncan and CEO Matt Sims, plus David, Brian, Odra — described as a stable, close-knit, high-performing 5-6 decision-maker team together for 7-8 years.
Management still owns 39% equity stake at time of deal; incentives aligned with Arvind's growth vision.
Company redone entire performance-linked long-term incentive structure for management team to be incentivized for next value-creation phase.

After 4 years, if things go well and management still wants to continue, Arvind will find ways to incentivize them further, similar to practice with Indian businesses; residual equity will be bought by Arvind with additional incentive structures on top.

subsections.label: Synergy roadmap / phased growth plan
points: First unlock: more aggressive growth trajectory than in the past — company was previously PE-owned and focused on efficiency/profitability rather than growth.
Company at 85% capacity utilization with ~$5 million capex/year planned — enables growth in mid-teens rather than historical 10%.

Manufacturing to remain close to point of consumption (products are high loft / air-heavy, making long-distance shipping costly) — no plans to relocate manufacturing outside current 2 US facilities for at least 2 years given headroom (space for 3 more lines).

Second and third order synergies: bringing Dalco-GFT's technologies to India to address growing Indian market (~2.5 years horizon after focusing on US business first); using Arvind's India knowledge/manufacturing platform to bring products to US market; leveraging existing sales channels to cross-sell products in both directions.
Filtration business in the US (currently underrepresented for Arvind) identified as another synergy opportunity using the new asset base.

Fungibility of needle-punch nonwoven platform allows diversification across end-markets (auto, geotextiles, roofing, flooring) which provides risk containment across industry cycles — tested via financial modeling across cycles.
Company's participation is largely US-domestic /protected market with limited market risk from geographies like China.

subsections.label: Internal restructuring query (Awanish Chandra)
points: Announcement of internal restructuring where Arvind subscribed 100% equity in a US company with a step-down subsidiary was purely part of the structuring of this transaction, now consolidated at 61% ownership of Dalco-GFT — not indicative of other planned acquisitions.

subsections.label: Disclosure commitments
points: Management committed to share full financials (all 3 statements) of Dalco-GFT along with Q1 FY27 results.
Headline balance sheet numbers (including goodwill, intangibles, asset value) to be shared separately/immediately with analysts and investors post-call.

subsections.label: Acquisition & integration risks
points: Management acknowledges that acquisitions and ventures generally carry difficulty, particularly for Indian companies expanding abroad.

Risk mitigation approach: same technology platform Arvind has run in India for over a decade; no change to Dalco-GFT's operating team (low-touch integration model, no intent to relocate manufacturing to India or unlock cost synergies via management changes); facility footprint is small (fewer than 150 employees, 70-80 blue collar) relative to Arvind's scale, making integration manageable.

Fungibility of the asset base across multiple end-markets (auto, geotextiles, roofing, flooring, etc.) provides risk containment — when one industry slows, others can compensate; tested financially across different cycles.
Most end-markets served (e.g., US auto) are relatively protected from external geographic risk (e.g., China), limiting market risk from outside geographies.

subsections.label: Leverage / debt-to-EBITDA
subsections.note: Analyst flagged that leverage (debt-to-EBITDA) is on the higher side post-acquisition.

guidance_ledger.statement: We should be able to grow in the mid-teens rather than 10%. That is our ambition going forward.
That's one of the key inputs to why at AMD, we have a 20-plus percent growth aspiration.

guidance_ledger.metric: Dalco-GFT historical revenue growth vs margin growth
guidance_ledger.statement: The historical track record of the company is to grow revenue in double digits as well as margin in high teens. We expect that with the combination of markets that we are in, we will continue to maintain that 10% to 12% revenue growth and mid-teens margin expansion or margin growth rather.
There is already a plan to put in approximately $5 million of capex every year.
Our expectation from India is approximately 18% to 20%... we will still want to grow in the high teens and hopefully 20% plus.
Our current thinking and medium-term plan is to quickly pay down the debt... our aim would be to almost wind this down over the next couple of years.
The financial ratios post acquisition of Dalco-GFT is within the covenants that we have already signed in for. We expect this to improve in 12 months' time.

guidance_ledger.metric: India line of business for Dalco-GFT technology
guidance_ledger.statement: The expectation is that some point in the next 2.5 years, we will fire that process till then we will be very busy accelerating the U.S. business.
The capex plan for this year should be ready in 3 to 4 months.
When we do the quarter 1 financials at that time, the whole financials of Dalco-GFT will be there.

risk_register.risk: Integration risk of overseas acquisition
risk_register.note: Management noted acquisitions/ventures abroad generally carry difficulty; mitigated via low-touch model, retaining existing management team, and small footprint (<150 employees) relative to Arvind's scale.

risk_register.risk: Raw material (polymer/petroleum-linked) cost inflation
risk_register.note: Polymer prices have risen due to petroleum linkage; impact so far manageable, some cost increases passed on to customers; situation evolving amid ongoing geopolitical/war situation.

risk_register.risk: Elevated leverage / debt-to-EBITDA post-acquisition
risk_register.note: Analyst flagged leverage on the higher side; management's medium-term plan is to pay down debt over the next couple of years since Arvind Group historically avoids long-term debt.

risk_register.risk: Customer/platform concentration risk in automotive
risk_register.note: While ~85-88% of products are sole-sourced (indicating stickiness), model platform life is 6-7 years; supplier could be displaced if something goes materially wrong with the product, though this is described as rare.

risk_register.risk: Market risk from geographic slowdown in single end-market
risk_register.note: Fungibility of the needle-punch nonwoven platform across auto, geotextiles, roofing and flooring provides containment of risk across industry cycles; most end-markets (e.g., US auto) are relatively protected from external geography risk such as China.

themes.label: Global M&A / Inorganic growth
themes.note: AAML acquired 61% of Dalco-GFT for $136 million to gain immediate scale, global footprint, and access to a $2.5 billion TAM in needle-punch nonwoven technology.

themes.label: Management continuity & incentive alignment
themes.note: Entire existing Dalco-GFT management team retained with realigned long-term incentives; founder retains 16-17% stake through the 4-year period.

themes.label: Capacity expansion
themes.note: 85% utilization with ~$5 million/year capex plan and room for 3 more lines supports mid-teens growth ambition.

themes.label: Customer stickiness / sole-sourcing
themes.note: 85-88% of automotive products are sole-sourced given deep specced-in relationships with 6 largest Tier 1 customers, reflecting strong customer trust.

themes.label: Leverage / debt financing
themes.note: Deal funded via $50 million US debt and $60 million India debt; analysts flagged elevated leverage, though management plans to pay down debt over the next couple of years.

themes.label: Input-cost inflation
themes.note: Petroleum-linked polymer raw material costs have risen, though impact assessed as manageable so far with some pass-through to customers.

themes.label: India market entry via US technology transfer
themes.note: Plans to bring Dalco-GFT's technology/knowledge to India are envisioned within the next 2.5 years, positioned as a second-horizon synergy after US business acceleration.

key_takeaways: Arvind Advanced Materials Limited (AAML) has acquired 61% stake in Dalco-GFT at a valuation of 7.75x of calendar year 2025 reported EBITDA, with the transaction valued at $136 million.

Dalco-GFT is a company established in 1988 with a 4-decade track record, 2 manufacturing units in US (South Carolina and North Carolina), capacity of 75 million pounds, historical growth rate of 10%, margin of 17%, and pre-acquisition return on capital of 40%.

The acquisition is expected to accelerate AAML's global footprint and reduce supply-chain risk associated with the current geopolitical situation, giving access to a TAM of $2.5 billion across all segments.
The entire existing top management will continue with the company, and the deal is both margin accretive and EPS accretive at Arvind consolidated level.

The acquisition is funded through a combination of debt at both AAML and debt at Dalco-GFT to benefit from taxation at both geographies; financial ratios post-acquisition are within existing covenants and expected to improve in 12 months.
Capacity utilization is currently around 85%, with a plan for approximately $5 million capex every year; company expects to grow revenue in the mid-teens rather than the historical 10%.

Raw materials are predominantly petroleum-linked polymers, with 65-70% sourced locally in the US and the balance from Korea and Vietnam; working capital of about 60 days is in line with Arvind Limited's existing metrics.

Debt raised: $50 million at the US entity (up from $15 million) and $60 million at AAML (India), at costs of 5.5% and ~6% respectively; medium-term plan is to wind down this debt over the next couple of years.

What is the goodwill number that you're guiding on Arvind Limited books?

The press release says fund this acquisition, $50 million will be raised in the U.S. entity and $60 million in the AAML, but the cost should be around $80 million given $136 million and 60% stake — but $110 million is being raised — could you throw some light on this?
If we look at the leverage side of debt-to-EBITDA, it's on the higher side. How do we plan here actually, what's our thought process?
It will be good for everyone if you can share the whole financial of Dalco, all 3 financial statements — at least headline numbers so we can make our numbers on this.

JSWCEMENT.about: JSW Cement is a leading Indian manufacturer of green cement, known for its sustainability and use in major infrastructure projects

quarters.summary: Q1 FY27 saw strong overall demand (South/West/East cement demand +~6% YoY; North +~11% YoY) driven by government capex, with management expecting continued strong infra/large-project demand for the rest of the year. Consolidated revenue grew 22% YoY but EBITDA fell 7.5% YoY on fuel/packing cost pressure and North marketing investment; North operations are expected to reach EBITDA breakeven by Q2/September FY27, GGBS growth guidance was revised down to high single digits for FY27 (from earlier mid-teens/~7mn ton reference), and overall company cement volume growth (incl. North) is guided at high teens for FY27. Capex guidance of ~INR2,300 crores for FY27 and ~INR2,000 crores for FY28 was reaffirmed, with long-term capacity expansion to 43.5 million tons continuing, Central region plant decision expected in coming quarters, and Punjab, Fujairah and Dolvi expansions on separate timelines.

subsections.label: EBITDA decline drivers
points: Despite improvement in realizations, EBITDA declined mainly due to cost pressures in fuel and packing, plus the substantial marketing investment of about INR33 crores made in North region during quarter one.
Raw material and power and fuel increased on a quarter-on-quarter basis, primarily due to higher fuel cost and impact of Nagaur operations.
Other expenses increased 4.5% QoQ largely related to heavy marketing investment in the North region and higher packing cost during the quarter.

subsections.label: Cost trends
points: Logistic cost per ton reduced by 2% QoQ with a slight reduction in lead distance of 4 km as well as from efficiency measures.
Company is working towards increasing share of domestic fuel to optimize costs in coming quarters.
Fuel cost expected to remain similar in Q2 as Q1, but expected to come down in Q3 as domestic coal purchases increase.

subsections.label: JV deconsolidation
points: Company is a JV partner in JSW One, which intends to list within this financial year.

Earlier JSW One was incurring losses, requiring write-down of the entire investment over different quarters; recent fund raise brought net worth into positive zone, and the INR55 crores reflects the company's share of that net worth per accounting standards.

subsections.label: Marketing spend outlook
points: Investment for marketing in North has already largely been done; benefit expected to be reaped in following quarters.
Full company marketing expenditure for the year expected at about INR130 crores, which includes technical spends also.
This run-rate is expected to rise further as company enters newer territories such as Punjab, Western UP, Central UP.

subsections.label: North incentive recognition
points: Capital subsidy incentive (23% on eligible capital investment) not yet booked in Q1; documents submitted, awaiting eligibility certificate expected within about two months.

Incentive recognition (~INR50 crores for first three years, then INR65 crores, then INR80 crores) is linked to how much capex is completed/capitalized; company awaiting completion of WHR, OLBC, AFR capitalization before confirming amount for the year.
Incentive will be routed through P&L; exact accounting treatment (revenue vs other line items) still being discussed with auditors given complexity of capital subsidy accounting.

key_figures.label: GGBS large infra project approvals received

subsections.label: Cement volume drivers
points: For ease of comparison, if North operations excluded, volume increase was 8% YoY.
Demand in April and early May affected by labor migration and state elections, but a strong rebound was seen in June.
Industry growth excluding North was around 6%, while company excluding North delivered 8%; East and West outperformed industry, South saw a headwind due to topical reasons now behind the company.
Company expects to deliver high teens growth at overall company level for FY27 (including North).

subsections.label: GGBS performance and outlook
points: GGBS volume growth was relatively muted at 2.6% YoY in Q1, impacted by RMC closures in the West, aggregate availability issues in the South, and unviable OPC/slag cost mix; also affected by labor migration from election-related disruption.
Guidance for Q2 FY27, despite being a monsoon season, is for improvement over Q1, with signs already visible in July.

Company has received approvals for over 29 large infra projects in Q1 and expects the pipeline to remain robust; expects GGBS to grow in high single digits for the year (revised down from earlier mid-teens guidance), with strong outlook continuing into FY28 as capex/infra approvals compound.
GGBS pricing strategy has not changed; the realization movement seen is primarily a dispersion/geographic mix effect (South vs West split), not a change in pricing stance.

subsections.label: Cement pricing/realization strategy
points: Highest realization increase was in East region followed by South and West.
Investments in brand building and ground connect with decision-making influencers/network in North are helping increase price or reduce the price gap in the A category band.
Continuous effort to reduce discount structures is also boosting realization.

subsections.label: North region ramp-up
points: North region achieved strong volume ramp-up; market reception has been very positive.

Company expects utilization closer to 60% plus by end of the year in North; capacity will rise from current 2.5 million tons to 3.5 million tons with additional 1 million ton coming in September end/early October, which affects the full-year utilization percentage despite exiting June at 68%.

subsections.label: RMC business strategy
points: RMC approach is largely symbiotic with wherever the company has a cement/GGBS footprint; setups are either commercial, dedicated, or captive (captive largely for JSW Group use).
Of the 15 current RMC plants, most are in West and South near GGBS sourcing units, but 2 units are already in the North.

Incremental RMC expansion (15 to 35) will be scattered across geographies; commercial/dedicated plants mirror cement synergies, while captive plants mirror JSW Group's own expansion across North, West, South and East.
RMC margins are difficult to project currently since captive margins differ from commercial/dedicated; in the first 12 months of new plants, RMC typically makes little money.

subsections.label: Nagaur (North) cost-reduction infrastructure
points: Substantial progress made on installation of WHRS, OLBC, and AFR co-processing system at the Nagaur integrated unit, expected to commission in the next few weeks, which is going to bring down costs significantly.
Additional 1 million ton grinding capacity in Nagaur is on track and expected to be commissioned by end of Q2 FY27.

The real cost kicker for North operations will occur once clinker costs come down with OLBC commissioning, alternate fuel and waste heat recovery kicking in, and the move from imported coal to lignite -- all planned for Q2, with benefits expected to kick in thereafter.

Current breakeven utilization is higher (55-60%) because limestone is currently transported by road and WHRS is not yet operational; once these are in operation, breakeven would be at much lower utilization levels.

subsections.label: Long-term capacity expansion sequencing
points: Company evaluating options between Central, Northeast and North expansion; all three are on the priority list, but sequencing decision expected in coming months.
Long-term plan is to finish the 43 million ton expansion first, then pursue the balance 25 million tons over the following three-four years.
Central region plant is on the priority list; company hopes to make an announcement in coming quarters.

subsections.label: Punjab expansion status
points: Company has spent only on land so far (about INR50-60 crores); most of the plant land is already secured, with only a small parcel for the approach road still to be purchased.
Company is awaiting Environmental Clearance (EC); a couple of rounds of discussion/hearing have happened with the Pollution Control Board (PCB); work at Punjab will be initiated once EC is received.
Capex guidance figures quoted include Punjab, as Punjab is integral to the company's overall North plans.

subsections.label: Green energy capacity progress
points: Prior target was to achieve 49% green energy share by 4Q FY26 and 63% by FY27; company acknowledges slight delays mostly related to land, which are now behind it.
Within September, entire previously informed green energy capacities are expected to be available, enabling the company to hit 60% plus green energy share implemented from Q3 onwards by end of FY27.

subsections.label: Regional demand drivers
points: Government capex did much of the heavy lifting in the quarter; state capex and infra construction goods output continue to grow YoY.

In MMR, pace is picking up in the bullet train project - the Maharashtra packages, and the Western Coastal Road project at Mumbai will gather pace post monsoons; road-related works expected to pick up speed.
In Pune, the Pune Ring Road project, various new elevated road packages, and a few new metro projects are planned.

In South region, Amaravati new capital development project in AP is gaining speed; NPCIL nuclear power plant expansion in North Karnataka and several large road packages in Chennai and Kerala expected to generate substantial demand.
Strong residential activity is seen in Pune, Hyderabad, and Bangalore, and substantial residential redevelopment is happening in Mumbai and suburbs.

subsections.label: GGBS regional exposure
points: GGBS sales have a roughly 60-40 split between South and West; South was impacted by aggregate availability issues while growth came primarily from the West in Q1.

key_takeaways: FY27 has started off on a strong note for the company despite the ongoing uncertainty around the West Asia crisis and the impact of state elections held early in the quarter.

Cement demand in South, West, and East regions grew approximately 6% Y-o-Y in quarter one FY27; the North region, where the company started sales in this quarter, saw substantially higher demand growth of approximately 11% Y-o-Y.
Total sales volume in quarter 1 FY27 increased by 15% Y-o-Y to 3.81 million tons; cement volumes sold was 2.34 million tons, increased 27% Y-o-Y (8% Y-o-Y excluding North operations).

Consolidated revenue was INR1,896 crores, an increase of 22% year-on-year and flat quarter-on-quarter; consolidated operating EBITDA was INR299 crores, lower by 7.5% year-on-year, mainly due to cost pressures in fuel and packing plus substantial marketing investment of about INR33 crores in North region.

GGBS volume growth was relatively muted at 2.6% Y-o-Y, impacted by RMC closures in the West, aggregate availability issues in the South, and unviable OPC/slag cost mix; guidance revised to high single-digit growth for the year.
North region average utilization was 55% in quarter one, touching almost 68% in June '26; company expects to be closer to 60% plus by end of the year and EBITDA breakeven by Q2/September.

Net debt was INR3,856 crores at the end of June with net debt to EBITDA at 2.95 times; company incurred capex of INR337 crores during the quarter against a full-year guidance of about INR2,300 crores.
Company expects to deliver high teens growth at an overall company basis for cement (including North) for FY27.

subsections.label: Middle East / West Asia crisis
points: West Asia crisis brings issues for the cement industry: packing bags, imported fuel, and rising petrol and diesel costs, creating near-term uncertainty for overall economic growth and cement demand outlook.
Company is carefully monitoring the situation, tightening belts wherever necessary, and preparing to react quickly and be nimble in the fast-changing environment.
Rupee depreciated sharply against the dollar in Q4, resulting in a net cost impact of INR13.4 crores.
UAE grinding unit commissioning delayed by a month due to the war, now expected by end of April 2027.
Despite war-related uncertainty, clinker supply for the Dolvi unit is secured till December of the current year via fixed-price contracts with a Japanese source tied up pre-war.

subsections.label: Demand softness / labor & election disruption
points: April '26 demand was relatively soft due to inflationary pressures from the Middle East war situation.
Shortage of labour and impact of elections in Tamil Nadu, Kerala and West Bengal (labour migrating back to home states for elections) impacted volumes in April.
Management expects activity to normalize from May onward.

subsections.label: GGBS supply disruption
points: Temporary slag availability issues at the Dolvi unit required rerouting supplies to certain markets from the Vijayanagar plant, impacting approximately 1.2 lakh tons of GGBS volume.
Some RMC sites in the Western region were closed early in the quarter due to pollution concerns, compounding the GGBS demand slowdown (a key GGBS customer segment).
Slowdown seen in January and February, recovery seen in March; disruptions considered behind the company as of May.

subsections.label: Regulatory delay - Punjab EC
points: Delays in obtaining Environmental Clearance (EC) at Mansa, Punjab have pushed out the Punjab grinding unit timeline beyond FY28 as originally intimated.
Elections due in Punjab around February next year are slowing government approval processes.

Company decided to add 2.5 MTPA grinding capacity at Nagaur instead, to better utilize Nagaur clinker in the interim, replacing the Punjab 2.75 MTPA in the long-term capacity plan with 2.5 MTPA at Rajasthan.

key_figures.label: Cost savings target FY27 per ton
Cost savings target FY28 per ton

guidance_ledger.statement: In FY27, performance is forecasted to be in the mid-teens to high-teens, excluding the North; we maintain our stance on that.
We maintain our guidance of 50% to 60% utilization for the full year of 2.5 million ton grinding capacity at Nagaur.

We hold on to our original guidance; targeting around 7 million tons of GGBS volume this year (versus ~6.5 million tons prior reference), no change from original guidance despite RMC/pollution disruption.
We intend to spend about INR2,300 crores in FY27.
We intend to spend about INR2,200 crores in FY28.

More than 50% of forecasted cost savings levers have been achieved; expect this to jump to close to 75% in FY27 (25% more added across power cost, logistics and premiumization), around INR100 per ton in FY27 and balance in FY28.
Green energy capacity is expected to rise from around 24% currently (FY26) all the way up to 63% and beyond.

Punjab grinding unit is not going to come up by FY28 as earlier intimated; this would definitely get shifted due to delayed EC approval, with Punjab elections due around February next year slowing the process.

guidance_ledger.metric: Additional Nagaur grinding capacity (2.5 MTPA) commissioning
guidance_ledger.statement: This unit is expected to commission by quarter 4 of FY28, with estimated investment of INR430 crores.
The broader guidance touching the 43 (43.5) million ton mark by FY30 remains intact; the only change is replacing Punjab's 2.75 MTPA with 2.5 MTPA at Rajasthan.
The remaining capacity expansion plan remains on track and will take the company to a grinding capacity of 46 MTPA with a clinker of 13.04 MTPA.
Because of the war, commissioning is delayed by a month; now hoping by end of April 2027 for commissioning.
Assume 25% tax rate for modeling purposes from FY27 onwards, consequent to adoption of the new tax regime.
Rajasthan incentive as approved by the state will be INR50 crores towards capital subsidy plus some number on electricity duty waiver, flowing through revenue.

Once the additional 6 MTPA grinding consumes the entire 3.3 million tons of clinker produced in Rajasthan, the company will probably have to think about putting up a second clinker line in Rajasthan, but that decision is not yet taken.

risk_register.note: Creates near-term uncertainty for overall economic growth and cement demand outlook; company monitoring and tightening belts.

risk_register.risk: Rupee depreciation against the dollar
risk_register.note: Sharp devaluation in Q4 amounted to a net cost impact of INR13.4 crores.

risk_register.risk: Labor shortage and election-related disruption in Tamil Nadu, Kerala, West Bengal
risk_register.note: Labour migrated back to home states for elections, impacting April volumes; expected to normalize from May.

risk_register.risk: Slag availability constraint at Dolvi unit
risk_register.note: Impacted ~1.2 lakh tons of GGBS volume in Q4, requiring rerouting from Vijayanagar; recovery seen from March, considered behind the company as of May.

risk_register.risk: RMC plant closures due to pollution concerns (Western region, incl. Mumbai and Pune)
risk_register.note: Closures affected GGBS demand in Jan-Feb; all RMC plants (commercial and dedicated) are back online across Bombay and Pune as of now.

risk_register.risk: Regulatory delay in Environmental Clearance (EC) for Punjab (Mansa) grinding unit
risk_register.note: EC delayed; Punjab plant will not commission by FY28 as earlier planned; Punjab elections due Feb next year slowing government approvals.

risk_register.risk: War-related delay to UAE grinding unit commissioning
risk_register.note: Commissioning delayed by a month due to the war; now expected by end of April 2027.

risk_register.risk: Steel price increase impact on GGBS/slag pricing
risk_register.note: Slag prices governed by a 5-year contract with price discovery every 2.5 years (started October 2024); management does not expect any windfall gain from steel price increases as GGBS pricing has no direct correlation to steel prices.

themes.label: Demand recovery
themes.note: April '26 demand soft due to Middle East war-led inflation, labour shortage and election disruption in Tamil Nadu, Kerala, West Bengal; management expects normalization from May.

themes.label: North India expansion
themes.note: Nagaur integrated plant (3.3 MT clinker, 2.5 MT grinding) commenced commercial operations in March 2026, launch pad into Rajasthan and Haryana, with strong dealer/customer response.

themes.label: Capacity expansion
themes.note: Board approved additional 2.5 MTPA grinding at Nagaur (INR430 crores) taking Nagaur to 6 MTPA; long-term target of 46 MTPA grinding / 13.04 MTPA clinker and 43.5 MTPA by FY30 reconfirmed.

themes.label: Regulatory delay - Punjab EC
themes.note: EC delays at Mansa, Punjab pushed the Punjab grinding unit beyond FY28; Nagaur expansion partly compensates for this delay.

themes.label: Margin improvement / cost savings
themes.note: Operating EBITDA margin up 460 bps YoY to 19.3% in Q4; cost savings program more than 50% achieved, targeting ~75% by FY27 driven by power, logistics and premiumization, aided by rising green energy share (24% to 63%+).

themes.label: GGBS supply disruption
themes.note: Slag availability issues at Dolvi and RMC plant closures due to pollution concerns impacted GGBS volumes in Q4, though issues considered resolved as of May.

themes.label: West Asia war impact
themes.note: War situation drives inflationary pressure on packing bags, imported fuel, and rupee depreciation, and delays UAE grinding unit commissioning by a month.

key_takeaways: The company listed in August 2025, a major milestone as one of the youngest cement companies in India.

Integrated plant at Nagaur in Rajasthan comprising 3.3 million ton of clinker and 2.5 million tons of grinding capacity started commercial operations in March 2026, serving as the launch pad into Rajasthan and Haryana.

Total sales volume in Q4 FY26 increased by 7% Y-o-Y to 3.99 million tons; cement volume sold was 2.35 million tons, up 12% Y-o-Y; GGBS volume sold was 1.57 million tons, up 5.4% Y-o-Y (FY26 full year GGBS growth 12% Y-o-Y).
Cement realizations for Q4 FY26 were INR4,673 per ton, up 4.8% QoQ across all regions; GGBS realization was INR3,682 per ton, a slight QoQ improvement.

Board approved an additional 2.5 MTPA cement grinding capacity at Nagaur (taking total Nagaur grinding capacity to 6 MTPA) due to delays in EC at Mansa, Punjab, with estimated investment of INR430 crores, expected to commission by Q4 FY28.
Q4 FY26 revenue was INR1,895 crores (+11% YoY); operating EBITDA was INR365 crores (+46% YoY), INR916 per ton; operating EBITDA margin was 19.3%, up 460 bps YoY.

FY26 revenue was INR6,512 crores (+12% YoY); operating EBITDA was INR1,240 crores (+44% YoY), INR888 per ton for the year; adjusted PAT was INR668 crores; Board recommended dividend of INR0.50 per equity share.
Net debt was INR3,635 crores as on 31 March 2026, in line with guidance.
pressing_questions: Sir, the second question, what is our capex guidance for, say, the next few years? And in particular, if you could also highlight what capex has been spent on the Rajasthan plant till date?

After the expansion that you've announced further in Rajasthan, which will take your capacity over 6. Where does the additional clinker for your Punjab plant gets sourced as and when the approvals and permissions come through in the Punjab plant?
On this pollution issue in some cities of Western India and subsequent closure of RMC unit, is that issue completely behind? Or do you still see some impact of that?

INNOVACAP.about: Incorporated in January 2005, Innova Captab Ltd is a pharmaceutical company is an integrated pharmaceutical company in India with a presence across the pharmaceutical value chain.[1]

quarters.summary: Innova Captab delivered Q1 FY27 revenue/EBITDA growth of 34%/33% YoY, broadly in line with its growth trajectory, reinforcing confidence in the FY27 guidance of 20%+ revenue growth with profitability outpacing revenue. Growth was supported by steady order flows, expanding product portfolio and deeper customer engagement across CDMO and branded generic businesses; Jammu is ramping up in line with expectations (posted its first positive EBITDA of INR1-1.5 crores this quarter) and the company reiterated its 20%+ volume growth guidance and 15-16% (+/-2%) blended EBITDA margin band, with margin expansion expected as Jammu scales and contributes at base-business margin levels.

key_figures.label: Volume growth contribution to overall revenue growth
key_figures.period: Q1 FY27 YoY, overall manufacturing capability level

subsections.label: Gross margin movement
points: Movement in gross margin is a combination of overall business mix; it is down 1-1.5% YoY, which is in the normal course of business and mainly due to the contribution of different business mix in the overall kitty.
On a full-year basis, gross margin is expected to maintain around 35.5% plus/minus 2%.

subsections.label: Other expenses
points: Other expenses as a percentage of revenue slightly reduced YoY, though overall absolute cost increased commensurate with the increase in operations.
There was a slight increase in logistics cost, which has been duly factored in over the period and was not material to overall revenue scenario.

subsections.label: Working capital
points: Initial working capital for Jammu ramp-up was already built up and factored in during previous year's ramping phase.
Company is maintaining its expected cash conversion cycle of 90 days plus/minus 10 days at the entire group level.

subsections.label: Capex plans
points: General capex will proceed in normal course of business for both maintenance and certain growth capex to augment overall capabilities in existing manufacturing plants.
Regarding the new Baddi plot bought last year, the plan is on the same line and the company is still firming it up; a more concrete plan will be brought to market once finalized.

Future expansion tranches are expected to be smaller (e.g., INR200-250 crores) versus the earlier INR500 crores Jammu expansion, so the drag on existing margin from new capex should not be as material.
Any greenfield project expansion will be informed to the street once finalized, with Board approval.

key_figures.label: Branded generic business revenue growth YoY
Sharon Bio / organic business growth expectation

subsections.label: CDMO business
points: Growth driven by expanding product portfolio, addition of new customers, and deeper engagement with existing customers, resulting in higher wallet share.

Continue to witness healthy demand across customer base; focus remains on strengthening relationships with existing customers, increasing share of business with them, and adding new customers across therapeutic categories and dosage forms.
Built a broad and diversified product portfolio supported by strong formulation development capabilities; continuing to invest in product development and complex dosage capabilities.

subsections.label: Branded generic business
points: Continued healthy momentum supported by continued traction across key markets.
Strategic focus remains on strengthening presence in existing markets and gradually expanding into newer domestic and international geographies.
Continuing to broaden product offering and deepen market penetration supported by integrated manufacturing and product development capabilities.
Over medium and long term, branded generic business seen as providing significant opportunity to further diversify revenue base and strengthen presence across key markets.

subsections.label: CDMO vs branded generic - conflict of interest
points: From a plant/manufacturing perspective, branded generic business is treated as a normal CDMO customer with no additional or special treatment.
Products transferred from manufacturing to branded generic business are transferred on an arm's length basis in an open, competitive market.
It is normal and accepted industry practice for a CDMO business to also have a branded generic business; no conflict of interest per se.

subsections.label: Sharon Bio performance
points: There has been a seasonal impact on Sharon's performance this quarter; on a full year level, expected to continue growing as per organic business expectation.
Organic business (including Sharon) is expected to grow in early teens; the additional flavour on top to reach 20%+ overall comes from Jammu ramp-up.

subsections.label: R&D and new product development
points: Overall R&D spend ranges between 0.7% to 1% of total revenue.
Continuous flow of new product developments; R&D works on new products with firm timelines for short-term, mid-term and long-term commercialization, depending on customer and market demands.
Semaglutide product development status is unchanged since last con-call; company is closely watching developments and the plant team is working on batches.

key_figures.label: Jammu optimum utilization for peak revenue

subsections.label: Jammu ramp-up
points: Jammu plant just started ramping up; annualized capacity utilization for the quarter is around 25-30%.
Ramp-up is pacing as expected; Q1 has a seasonal impact across the entire year, and healthy season picks up from Q2 onwards, so Jammu plant is expected to ramp up further in coming quarters.
This quarter Jammu posted its first positive EBITDA of INR1-1.5 crores, having crossed the breakeven line.

Once Jammu ramps up, most of the margin will flow into the company's contributing margin at the overall level; base business margin profile is normalized at 17-18% (not the current 20%), and Jammu should also move toward that band, upgrading overall company margin by 2-3% once it starts giving contributing margin.

Jammu peak/optimum revenue potential estimated at INR1,400 crores at 65-70% utilization; margin estimates for Jammu are inclusive of government incentives already factored into revenue and profitability statements.

Visibility on ramp-up timeline tied to onboarding of domestic marquee customers, presence in ROW/regulated markets, customer and country audits, and dossier/product approvals; plant started in January of previous year with significant audits already completed and plant approved; product approvals from different markets expected by end of this financial year.
Jammu has been expanded in the category of Penem, Beta and Cepha, where sufficient capacity exists for the next two to three years.
Jammu expected asset turn at optimum level is north of 3x.

subsections.label: Capacity expansion strategy
points: Existing capacity will saturate with volume growth, requiring expansion in tablet, capsule, liquid categories (categories not covered by Jammu, e.g. core Baddi portfolio) to sustain growth.

Second growth engine is opening up new dosage forms or therapeutic categories where the company is not currently present (currently present in six-seven categories out of a large formulation/dosage/therapeutic category landscape); past expansions in new areas have successfully driven revenue growth.
Both engines (expanding existing strong areas nearing saturation, and entering new dosage/therapeutic categories) are expected to help maintain 20%+ CAGR going forward.
Any strategic/concurrent move for basket extension will go through Board approval and be communicated to the street with detailed proposal.
Baddi new plot purchased last year: plan is being firmed up; company will bring a more concrete plan to market once finalized.

subsections.label: Margin bridge / structural view
points: Ex-Jammu (base business) EBITDA margin this quarter is approximately 20%, but normalized base business margin is guided at 17-18% band (not 20%) due to volatility across periods.
Overall consolidated margin guidance remains at 15-16% plus/minus 2%; assuming 20% for future overall margin is considered a very high expectation; 17-18% is seen as a fairer number as Jammu matures.
Any new capex/new factory can have a 1-2% drag on margin until it matures.

subsections.label: Export/domestic mix
points: Exports contributed 32% of revenue during the quarter, reflecting continued progress in expanding presence across international markets.
At overall consolidated level, domestic business is around 70% and export business is around 30% (branded and CDMO business area-wise breakup not tracked separately).

subsections.label: Pricing
points: Company operates a cost-plus / pass-through pricing model for API costs; API price movements are generally a pass-through rather than a gain/loss driver.

In some cases inventory in hand can positively impact margins, and in other cases having sales orders without matching inventory can negatively impact margins; company does not speculate on API prices and focuses on business performance.
This quarter, prices moved toward the increase side, and the company is able to pass through pricing to customers at a certain level.

subsections.label: Macro and geopolitical factors
points: Business mix tailwinds depend on other macro, political and geopolitical reasons which keep changing; company will evolve as and when these unfold.
Growth challenges will always be present in scaling to 20-25% growth; management states the team needs to overcome these challenges to prove ability to grow at that rate.

subsections.label: API price volatility
points: API price pass-through model means in some scenarios inventory holding can positively or negatively impact margins depending on timing versus sales orders in hand.

key_figures.label: Potential overall margin upgrade from Jammu contribution
Jammu revenue crossing mark for steady state
Volume growth guidance (alternate upper range mentioned)

subsections.label: Overall guidance
points: Company reiterates confidence in delivering 20% revenue growth guidance for FY27 with profitability outpacing revenue.
Growth guidance of 20%+ is stated on a volume growth basis, keeping price as a constant; after closing Q1 and mid-Q2, company hopes to deliver 20%+ volume growth on a year-on-year closing basis.
Company does not want to give guidance at a line-item level; overall guidance is 20% at the consolidated company level, factoring in all line items rolled up.
Margin guidance maintained at 15-16% plus/minus 2%; as Jammu matures and starts contributing margin, overall margin could see a 2-3% extension from the 16% base.

guidance_ledger.statement: Confident in ability to deliver on guidance of 20% revenue growth and profitability outpace revenue for FY27.
Maintaining that we are growing north of 20% on volume and very much confident that we should be growing on a 20% plus volume growth in coming period also.
Margin profile will remain 15-16% blended level, plus minus 2% to factor all volatilities.
Normalized margin should be taken in a band of 17% to 18%, not 20%.

guidance_ledger.metric: Overall margin expansion from Jammu contribution
guidance_ledger.statement: Once Jammu start giving a contributing margin, overall margin from base of 16% should upgrade towards 2% to 3% extension.
Gross margin posted around 35.5%; overall full year level should maintain between this range plus minus 2%.
At an optimum level, expect the asset turn from Jammu plant would be north of 3x.
Jammu plant at peak will do a revenue of around INR1,400 crores, an optimum revenue anticipated at a utilization of 65% to 70%.
General maintenance capex will be in range of INR20 crores to INR25 crores.
Growth capex for existing capability augmentation/debottlenecking should be in the range of INR20 crores to INR30 crores.
Plan for new Baddi plot bought last year is on the same line; still working to firm it up, will come to market with a more concrete plan once firmed up.
Organic business (Sharon Bio) growth should be in early teens.
Maintaining expected cash conversion cycle of 90 days plus-minus 10 days for entire group level.
Overall R&D spends range between around 0.7% to 1% of total revenue in general.
With improving scale and operating leverage, expect EBITDA growth to outperform revenue growth, as the Jammu plant utilization ramps up further.
PAT growth should outpace EBITDA growth added by the fact that depreciation and financial costs related to the Jammu facility are largely fixed and already reflected in the base.
Next year, the margin should be better than the current year; overall outlook is positive for margin expansion, though exact quantum depends on product basket, geographical presence etc.

In coming quarter, as the Jammu ramp-up is going on, we are very much positive that in coming quarter, we should be able to achieve EBITDA positive as well as start covering the fixed cost on Jammu part.
The overall potential of this block at an optimum level should be in the range of INR450 crores to INR500-odd crores revenue.

guidance_ledger.metric: New capex depreciation/interest impact on P&L
guidance_ledger.statement: This will take time -- this will kick in not in FY '27 or maybe partly kick in for FY '28. Because any new project, if we start with the greenfield, it takes 1.5 years to start the commercial production.

risk_register.risk: Macro and geopolitical factors affecting business mix and product/sales mix tailwinds
risk_register.note: Business mix tailwinds depend on macro political and geopolitical reasons which keep changing; company will evolve as these unfold.

risk_register.risk: Growth execution challenges in sustaining 20-25% growth
risk_register.note: Management stated challenges will always be there in growing 20-25%, and the team needs to overcome them.

risk_register.risk: API price volatility under pass-through model
risk_register.note: Pass-through model means inventory timing versus sales orders in hand can create positive or negative margin impact, though company does not speculate on API prices.

risk_register.risk: Slight increase in logistics costs
risk_register.note: Slight increase in logistics cost noted YoY/QoQ but factored in and not material to overall revenue scenario.

risk_register.risk: Seasonal impact on Q1 performance and Sharon Bio
risk_register.note: Q1 typically has a seasonal impact on the entire year's performance including Jammu ramp-up and Sharon Bio revenue; healthy season picks up from Q2 onwards.

risk_register.risk: API/raw material price increases due to Middle East conflict
risk_register.note: Uptick in prices of raw materials and major ingredients due to ongoing conflict; largely passed on to CDMO customers under cost-plus pricing model.

risk_register.risk: Cephalosporin API price volatility
risk_register.note: Prices reduced in Q2/Q3 FY26, stabilized in early Q4, then rose due to conflict; on YTD basis (including April) there is an increase in prices; not a meaningful sequential increase within Q4 itself.

risk_register.risk: Regulatory compliance burden (Schedule M)
risk_register.note: Schedule M now effective across the country; company facilities are compliant, giving compliant players an advantage over non-compliant facilities.

themes.label: Jammu ramp-up
themes.note: Jammu posted first positive EBITDA (INR1-1.5 crores) and grew revenue to INR107 crores from INR90 crores last quarter, with utilization at 25-30% annualized; ramp-up pacing as expected with Q2 onward seasonality favorable.

themes.label: Operating leverage / margin expansion
themes.note: Ex-Jammu margin at ~20% this quarter but normalized base business margin band guided at 17-18%; overall consolidated margin guidance maintained at 15-16% plus/minus 2%, with 2-3% upside once Jammu contributes margin.

themes.label: CDMO customer base expansion
themes.note: CDMO revenue grew 32% YoY driven by expanding product portfolio, new customer additions, and deeper engagement with existing customers resulting in higher wallet share.

themes.label: Capacity expansion (Baddi)
themes.note: Plan for new Baddi plot purchased last year is still being firmed up; company will bring a concrete plan to market once finalized, with no new capex figure disclosed this quarter.

themes.label: Regulated markets / Sharon Bio
themes.note: Sharon Bio saw seasonal impact this quarter, with organic business (including Sharon) expected to grow in early teens for the full year, with Jammu providing the additional flavour to reach 20%+ overall.

themes.label: Input cost inflation
themes.note: Pricing moved toward the increase side this quarter; company operates a cost-plus pass-through model for API prices, with no material margin impact called out.

themes.label: Regulatory certifications & compliance
themes.note: Significant audits at Jammu already completed and plant approved; product approvals from different ROW markets expected by end of this financial year, supporting ramp-up trajectory.

key_takeaways: We have started financial year '27 on a strong note, delivering strong year-on-year growth of 34% and 33% in revenue and EBITDA respectively for the quarter.

The performance is broadly in line with growth trajectory we have outlined in the year and provides further confidence in our ability to deliver on our guidance of 20% revenue growth and profitability outpace revenue for FY27.
The CDMO business reported revenue of INR328 crores during Q1 FY27, reflecting a year-on-year growth of 32%.
The branded generic business continued to maintain healthy momentum with revenue of INR142 crores, growth of 39% year-on-year basis.

Consolidated revenue for the quarter stood at INR470.9 crores, registering a strong 34% year-on-year growth supported by strong demand across both our business areas. Exports contributed 32% of our revenue during this quarter.
EBITDA for the quarter stood at INR75.1 crores, a growth of 33% year-on-year with a margin of 16%. Profit after tax for the quarter came in at INR44.1 crores, reflecting a growth of 42% year-on-year.
This quarter we have posted a positive EBITDA for Jammu to the tune of INR1 crores to INR1.5 crores.
So, my general maintenance capex will be in range of INR20 crores to INR25 crores. And growth capex... should be in the range of same range around INR20 crores to INR30 crores.
pressing_questions: So, can you -- is it possible to give the breakup for our branded business between domestic and international branded?
And sir, what are the asset turns that we expect from this particular plant [Jammu]?

I was asking about what was the networking capital cycle as of June 30, 2026? And also, are the inventory holding days and trade receivable normalizing back towards the historical levels following the Jammu ramp up?
How many new products or formulations were commercialized in the first quarter and what is the planned R&D spend percentage to sales at the remainder of the FY27?
How should we look at a possible conflict of interest between your CDMO business and your branded generic business?

So, on the utilization side, the current assets how much more volume growth is possible from the whole combined assets. Is it a two-year volume growth, three-year volume growth that you have with you?

Sir, like one more few things our Jammu plant at peak will do a revenue of around how much?
Any pricing pressure have we seen on the API side or in any of our products in this quarter?

quarters.summary: Innova Captab reported its highest ever annual performance in FY'26 with 31% revenue growth, driven by broad-based growth across CDMO and Branded Generics businesses and Jammu facility ramp-up. Management guided to 20%+ revenue growth going forward, with EBITDA growth outpacing revenue growth and PAT growth outpacing EBITDA growth as Jammu utilization ramps up further and operating leverage improves.

subsections.label: Balance sheet & capital allocation
points: Balance sheet continues to demonstrate strong resilience, reflecting effect of strategic decisions undertaken over past few years now translating into tangible execution on the ground.
Disciplined capital allocation, prudent leverage profile and sustained investment in capacity and capabilities have built a solid financial foundation to support growth ambitions.

subsections.label: Gross margin
points: Y-o-Y gross margin decline is mainly due to change in product mix; change in raw material prices on the upward side has no impact on the gross margin.

subsections.label: EBITDA/PAT growth drivers
points: With improving scale and operating leverage, EBITDA growth expected to outperform revenue growth as Jammu plant utilization ramps up further.
PAT growth should outpace EBITDA growth as depreciation and financial costs related to the Jammu facility are largely fixed and already reflected in the base.
Overall incremental growth should translate into much stronger profitability going forward.

Next chunk of revenue growth from Jammu will trigger operating leverage since maximum operating expenses (electricity, employee benefits) are already committed, expected to yield a few percentage points improvement in EBITDA.
Long-term investment/new plant costs (e.g., interest) during construction phase are capitalized and will not directly flow to P&L, supporting margin expansion.

Depreciation and interest costs are already taken care of in FY'26, so if EBITDA improves, PAT will outperform EBITDA — evidenced by H2 vs H1 and quarter-on-quarter trends where revenue increase led to EBITDA and PAT growing better than revenue.
New capex-driven depreciation/interest costs will not kick in for FY'27, and may only partly kick in FY'28, since any new greenfield project takes about 1.5 years to reach commercial production.

subsections.label: CDMO business
points: Continued to deepen presence in domestic pharma market by expanding customer base to over 350 clients, including several leading pharmaceutical companies in India.
Reflects continued emphasis on product development, customer-centric innovation and long-term partnership.
Q4 growth mainly led by increased product portfolio, adding new customers and deepening wallet share with existing customers.
Going forward, sees strong opportunities to further expand wallet share with existing customers while also adding new relationships across therapeutic categories and dosage forms.
Baddi facility growth mainly came through volumes; Jammu facility growth came from ramp-up for the full year.
CDMO revenue growth in FY26 (~INR200 crore) was fuelled by both domestic and exports; facility/geography-level breakup not tracked and not available.

subsections.label: Branded Generics business
points: Strong growth of 51% during the year, driven by geographical expansion into high potential domestic and international markets, coupled with deeper penetration in existing geographies.
Q4 growth described as a testament to distribution strategies.
Domestic Branded Generics business is entirely in the form of trade generics (not ethical marketing).
Growth strategy: hybrid model combining a ground-level distribution model (distributors, stockists, retailers) with on-field staff who work with stockists, wholesalers and retailers to push sales.
Business acumen in pharmaceutical trading — product placement, dosage form selection, and market penetration at all tiers — is helping scale revenue.
Domestic angle: largely focused where Innova has capability, but open to other product segments as well.
Geography split for Branded Generics roughly 70% domestic and 30-35% exports (not tracked at business-area level formally).

subsections.label: Sharon Bio performance
points: Sharon has integrated well over the last 2 years since acquisition.
Mainly has presence in export regulatory markets (Canada, UK, Europe, Australia).
Margin profile is better than the company's average EBITDA margin.

subsections.label: Customer concentration
points: CDMO business is well diversified amongst major pharmaceutical companies in India and globally, not over-reliant on any single customer or product.
Branded Generics business, being spread across distributor-stockist-retailer levels, also has low dependency on any single customer, geography or location.
At a group level, export business is also well diversified, not heavily reliant on a few customers.

subsections.label: Regulatory certifications
points: Cephalosporin facility in Baddi received UK-MHRA approval during the year.
Jammu blocks received PIC/S certification through SMDC Ukraine.
These certifications will support entry into regulated international markets and strengthen positioning as a quality-focused pharmaceutical manufacturing partner.
Company holds MHRA certification, EU-GMP certification and PIC/S certification, i.e., both international and local compliant plants.

subsections.label: R&D / Semaglutide opportunity
points: Company is closely monitoring the semaglutide market; initial R&D work on the product has yielded positive results.
Two aspects being tracked: market side and execution of exhibit batches and filing to local FDA.
Not racing for initial launch since the product category is already launched by others; company will be ready with a 'wave 2' approach if the product performs well in the market.

subsections.label: CDMO/CRDMO strategy and R&D vision
points: CDMO partnership is essential for front-end marketing companies — covers capacity gap, product gap and technology gap; an essential B2B partnership.

Company vision spans three domains: (1) complex/niche segment products like peptides, already being worked on; (2) traditional business as done over last 10-20 years; (3) expanding capability into new dosage forms not currently present.
Jammu facility has expanded into multiple segments like BFS, respules, and different drug categories like beta-lactam and penems.
Strong product pipeline in R&D expected to support business with well value-added margins as well as top line.

Company is a generics-focused company; R&D/development is focused on generics segment; multiple products going off-patent present opportunities via reverse engineering and early market launch as an advantageous play.
Being a CDMO company provides advantage of being a front-lining partner with multiple companies, enabling cost sharing.

subsections.label: Jammu facility ramp-up
points: A key highlight during the year was successful completion of first full year of operation at Kathua facility in Jammu; ramp-up has progressed steadily with high quality and compliance standards maintained across all functions.
Facility continued to witness encouraging progress, with several marquee customers successfully completing audits and validating stability data along with other key parameters.
Management remains confident about scale-up of the facility and its contribution to growth over coming years.
This quarter Jammu is nearing EBITDA breakeven; management expects to achieve EBITDA positive and start covering fixed costs in coming quarters.
Jammu facility caters to both CDMO and Branded Generics businesses across all geographies; facility-wise/business-area-wise revenue breakup not tracked and not available.
Jammu manufacturing capability spans injectables, general facility, cephalosporin, beta-lactam and penems.

subsections.label: Baddi facility expansion
points: Baddi general block facility is at higher utilization, prompting a land acquisition for a new general block construction (oral tablet, capsule, oral liquid facility) to relax the Baddi portfolio and support growth momentum.
This expansion covers the existing Baddi portfolio (general oral facility), not the injectables/cephalosporin/beta-lactam/penem categories already covered in Jammu.

Plan is still under deliberation; a more concrete plan will be shared once finalized. Broadly, capex should be incurred across both FY27 and FY28, with weightage/portion of spend still to be finalized.

subsections.label: Manufacturing infrastructure
points: Manufacturing infrastructure remains a core strength, built as advanced and technology-driven facilities supported by automation, stringent quality systems and globally compliant manufacturing practices.
These capabilities provide scalability, consistency, traceability and operational flexibility to support continued growth.

subsections.label: Utilization / operating leverage
points: Jammu facility utilization at around 10% versus other facilities at around 75%, indicating scope for margin expansion via operating leverage as Jammu ramps up.

Management indicated next year's margin should be better than current year but noted the extent depends on product basket, geographical presence and other factors, making a precise number difficult to forecast; overall outlook is positive for margin expansion.

subsections.label: Regulated international markets
points: Sharon operates in markets like Canada, UK, Europe and Australia.
Cephalosporin block also operates in Canada, Europe and UK markets.
Company continues to focus on these markets, filing products in the territory and getting endorsements for multiple products.
Sees healthy, better growth in this business with better margins, especially in these markets.

Company covers all engines simultaneously — regulated market, domestic trade generics, and CDMO — equally; growth in one segment does not necessarily change overall product mix as all categories are focused equally.

subsections.label: Raw material availability and pricing
points: No shortage/availability concern for raw materials despite global issues; prices are going up but availability is not a concern.

Unlike COVID situation (which had demand-side disruption), current situation has demand increasing at a normal pace with disruptions mainly on the supply side, impacting prices rather than availability.

Due to the ongoing Middle East conflict, there has been an uptick in prices of raw materials and major ingredients; since CDMO pricing with customers is on a cost-plus basis, these increases have largely been passed on to customers.

Cephalosporin API prices had reduced during Q2 and Q3 FY26 and started stabilizing in first half of Q4, before the conflict played out; this cephalosporin API dynamic was called out as a major impact affecting revenue during the year.
No meaningful sequential increase in cephalosporin prices within Q4, but on a YTD basis including April, there has been a price increase.

subsections.label: Schedule M compliance
points: Schedule M is now effective across the country.
All company facilities are compliant with local and international regulations (MHRA, EU-GMP, PIC/S certifications).
Companies that comply with Schedule M will be in an advantageous position versus non-compliant facilities.

subsections.label: Cephalosporin market positioning
points: Government has implemented MIP (Minimum Import Price) ensuring the Indian cephalosporin ecosystem does well, positioning the company favorably given its dedicated UK-MHRA approved cephalosporin unit.

subsections.label: Sharon Bio acquisition
points: Sharon Bio acquisition has helped the company expand into regulated territories (Canada, UK, Europe, Australia).
Sharon has integrated well over the last 2 years since acquisition.

subsections.label: Geopolitical / input cost risk
points: Middle East conflict has led to an uptick in raw material and API prices; while largely passed on to customers under cost-plus CDMO contracts, this represents an external cost pressure.
Cephalosporin API price volatility (reduction in Q2/Q3 FY26, stabilization in early Q4, then increase due to conflict) has impacted revenue during the year.
On a YTD basis (including April), there has been an increase in cephalosporin prices.

key_figures.label: Baddi new block optimum revenue potential

subsections.label: Growth and profitability outlook
points: With multiple growth levers in place — capacity ramp-up, expanding product portfolio, deeper market penetration and a strong R&D engine — company is confident in ability to deliver 20%+ revenue growth and create long-term value for stakeholders.
With improving scale and operating leverage, EBITDA growth is expected to outperform revenue growth as Jammu plant utilization ramps up further.
PAT growth should outpace EBITDA growth, aided by the fact that depreciation and financial costs related to the Jammu facility are largely fixed and already reflected in the base.

Next year's margin should be better than the current year, though the exact extent depends on product basket, geographical presence and other factors — overall outlook is positive for margin expansion.
At a group level, management reiterated confidence in maintaining 20%+ volume growth from FY26 to FY27, with Jammu playing a major role, though facility-wise breakup is not available.
New capex-related depreciation/interest costs will not kick in for FY27 and may only partly kick in for FY28, given any greenfield project takes about 1.5 years to reach commercial production.

guidance_ledger.statement: Confident in ability to deliver 20% plus revenue growth and create long-term value for stakeholders.
With improving scale and operating leverage, expect EBITDA growth to outperform revenue growth, as the Jammu plant utilization ramps up further.
PAT growth should outpace EBITDA growth added by the fact that depreciation and financial costs related to the Jammu facility are largely fixed and already reflected in the base.
Next year, the margin should be better than the current year; overall outlook is positive for margin expansion, though exact quantum depends on product basket, geographical presence etc.
We would like to maintain that we are very much confident of maintaining that 20% plus volume growth from FY '26 to FY '27.

In coming quarter, as the Jammu ramp-up is going on, we are very much positive that in coming quarter, we should be able to achieve EBITDA positive as well as start covering the fixed cost on Jammu part.
Overall capital outlay should be in the range of INR150 crores, INR170 crores for the new Baddi general block, to be incurred in both FY '27 and FY '28.
The overall potential of this block at an optimum level should be in the range of INR450 crores to INR500-odd crores revenue.

guidance_ledger.metric: New capex depreciation/interest impact on P&L
guidance_ledger.statement: This will take time -- this will kick in not in FY '27 or maybe partly kick in for FY '28. Because any new project, if we start with the greenfield, it takes 1.5 years to start the commercial production.

risk_register.risk: API/raw material price increases due to Middle East conflict
risk_register.note: Uptick in prices of raw materials and major ingredients due to ongoing conflict; largely passed on to CDMO customers under cost-plus pricing model.

risk_register.risk: Cephalosporin API price volatility
risk_register.note: Prices reduced in Q2/Q3 FY26, stabilized in early Q4, then rose due to conflict; on YTD basis (including April) there is an increase in prices; not a meaningful sequential increase within Q4 itself.

risk_register.risk: Regulatory compliance burden (Schedule M)
risk_register.note: Schedule M now effective across the country; company facilities are compliant, giving compliant players an advantage over non-compliant facilities.

themes.label: Jammu ramp-up
themes.note: First full year of Jammu operations completed with INR300 crore revenue in FY26; nearing EBITDA breakeven with expectations to turn EBITDA positive in coming quarters, driving future operating leverage.

themes.label: Operating leverage / margin expansion
themes.note: Management expects EBITDA growth to outpace revenue growth and PAT growth to outpace EBITDA growth as Jammu utilization ramps up and fixed costs are already absorbed in the base.

themes.label: Regulatory certifications & compliance
themes.note: UK-MHRA approval for Baddi cephalosporin facility and PIC/S certification for Jammu blocks strengthen positioning for regulated international markets; Schedule M compliance seen as an advantage.

themes.label: Input cost inflation
themes.note: Middle East conflict driving up raw material and API (especially cephalosporin) prices, though largely passed through to CDMO customers under cost-plus contracts.

themes.label: CDMO customer base expansion
themes.note: CDMO business grew 24% in FY26 with customer base expanded to over 350 clients; management sees opportunity to expand wallet share and add new relationships.

themes.label: Capacity expansion (Baddi)
themes.note: New Baddi general block planned with INR150-170 crore capex over FY27-FY28, targeting INR450-500 crore optimum revenue potential to relieve high utilization at existing Baddi facility.

themes.label: Regulated markets / Sharon Bio
themes.note: Sharon Bio (Canada/UK/Europe/Australia focus) generated ~INR240 crore revenue in FY26 with better-than-average EBITDA margins, complementing cephalosporin block's regulated market presence.

key_takeaways: FY '26 has been a defining year for Innova Captab as we achieved our highest ever annual performance, reflecting the strength of our business model, execution capabilities and customer relationship.

On a full year basis, revenue stood at INR1,630 crores, registering a healthy growth of 31% year-on-year, while Q4 revenue come at INR448 crores, delivering a strong growth of 42% compared to the corresponding quarter last year.
A key highlight during the year was the successful completion of the first full year of operation at our Kathua facility in Jammu.
The CDMO business reported revenue of INR1,133 crores, during FY '26, reflecting a year-on-year growth of 24%.
Coming to our Branded Generics business, we delivered a strong growth of 51% during the year.

We also achieved important regulatory milestones during this year. Our cephalosporin facility in Baddi received UK-MHRA approval, while our Jammu blocks received PIC/S certification through SMDC Ukraine.

With multiple growth levers in place, capacity ramp-up and expanding product portfolio, deeper market penetration and a strong R&D engine, we are confident in our ability to deliver 20% plus revenue growth and create long-term value for our stakeholders.

With improving scale and operating leverage, we expect EBITDA growth to outperform revenue growth, as the Jammu plant utilization ramp up further. PAT growth should outpace EBITDA growth added by the fact that the depreciation and financial costs related to the Jammu facility are largely fixed and already reflected in the base.
pressing_questions: Can you provide a split of the CDMO segment revenue growth into volume and realization growth both for FY '26 and current quarter? (facility-level color provided, but a precise volume/realization split was not fully quantified)
Can you provide a rough split between CDMO business and Branded Generics business in the INR300 crores Jammu top line for FY '26? (Management stated this breakup is not tracked/available)
Was the majority of the CDMO business growth (~INR200 crore YoY) driven by domestic or exports business? (Management stated this quantitative breakup is not available)
Was the bulk of the export business growth (~INR200 crore) driven by Branded Generics or CDMO business? (Management could not comment on this breakup)

EIEL.about: Established in 2009, Enviro Infra Engineers is engaged in the design, construction, operation, and maintenance of water and Waste-Water Treatment Plants (WWTPs) and water supply projects (WSSPs) for government agencies/entities.[1]

quarters.summary: Enviro Infra Engineers reported Q1 FY27 revenue of INR359.2 crores (+49% YoY), EBITDA of INR75.7 crores (EBITDA margin 21.07%), and PAT of INR45.2 crores (PAT margin 12.38%). Management reiterated FY27 guidance of ~INR2,000 crores consolidated revenue, EBITDA margin 21-22% (standalone water business) / 19-20% blended with renewables, PAT of INR260-270 crores (13-14% blended PAT margin), and order inflow guidance of ~INR2,500 crores (of which INR256.9 crores already secured via two HAM projects). Total order book stood at ~INR6,721 crores providing multi-year revenue visibility, with execution expected to ramp meaningfully from Q3 FY27 as BESS procurement (NTPC 930 MWh project) commences.

subsections.label: Margin decline drivers
points: Decline in EBITDA margin attributed to a blend of factors: increase in raw material/input cost, blend with renewables business (which carries lower margin), and higher employee cost from team building during last financial year as new projects were won.
Employee cost rose to ~7% of revenue in Q1 versus historical 3-3.5%, expected to normalize to 5-5.5% as the year progresses; team size increased from 900 to 2,300 employees since IPO to present.
Finance cost currently ~4% of revenue expected to normalize to 3-3.5% at blended annual level as topline scales toward INR2,000 crores.
Raw material price impact estimated at 1-2% of overall topline, factored into the lowered EBITDA margin guidance of 21-22% (from earlier 22-24%).

Price variation clause in tenders linked to WPI/CPI provides some cost pass-through, but company must absorb part of the increase; anticipated margin improvement as war-related conditions settle did not materialize.
Gross margin declined significantly YoY in Q1 FY27 versus Q1 FY26 due to raw material cost increase.
PAT margin currently ~12.5%, with expected improvement of 1.5-2 percentage points in FY27 as employee and finance costs normalize.
EBITDA margin was 21.07% in Q1 FY27 (standalone and consolidated with renewables both ~21%) versus 26.65% in Q1 FY26 and 18.7% in Q4 FY26; PAT margin was 12.38% in Q1 FY27 versus 12.37% in Q4 FY26.

subsections.label: Cash flow and working capital
points: Unbilled revenue/working capital position remains 'bloated' and has not improved; slow movement despite funds being allocated by government clients.
Company confirms no slippage in meeting liabilities; cash flow position stable with significant unencumbered funds available.

Operational cash flow expected to turn positive once government funds are released, though no guarantee given; historically OCF has been impacted by service concessionaire receivables (recognized as investment activity, negative impact of ~INR85 crores).
No history of bad debts in the company, and management does not foresee any going forward.
JJM total order book/receivables exposure of INR150-160 crores; JJM MP billing (trial/commissioning) currently INR15-20 crores.

subsections.label: Suyog Urja acquisition structure
points: Total acquisition value of Suyog Urja Limited is INR311 crores across three tranches; first tranche of INR111 crores already paid; second tranche of INR100 crores payable after FY27 (~July), subject to KPIs on revenue, bottom line and order book (amount may vary based on achievement); third tranche payable after FY28.
Second tranche funding to be a mix of internal accruals and acquisition debt.
FY27 consolidation reflects ~51% economic interest with full 75% impact to flow through from FY28 once second tranche completes, subject to achieving FY26 revenue/order book targets.
Investment in renewable segment referenced at INR75 crores in ROE discussion, with expected profitability from renewable segment of INR60-70 crores.

subsections.label: Revenue and order momentum
points: Revenue from operations of INR359.2 crores in Q1 FY27, up 49% YoY; EBITDA of INR75.7 crores, up 17.87% YoY; PAT of INR45.2 crores, up 6.47% YoY.
Revenue phasing for FY27 expected at ~20% each in Q1-Q3 and ~40% in Q4.
Order inflow of INR256 crores achieved so far in FY27 against expected order inflow of INR2,500 crores for the year; remaining INR2,250 crores expected for balance of year.
Water/wastewater bid pipeline of interest ~INR7,000 crores currently; additional bidding pipeline of INR6,000-7,000 crores.

Starting order book at the start of last year was INR1,200 crores, with revenue guidance historically representing 90-95% of starting order book; order book available at start of current financial year is INR2,700 crores (water segment), with similar 90-95% conversion rate assumption.
Water and wastewater segment revenue conversion rate assumption of 50% expected to yield ~INR1,300 crores topline in FY27.
Company strike rate (bid win rate) was ~20% in the last financial year.
