subsections.label: Order book composition and visibility
points: Total order book of ~INR6,721 crores provides strong revenue visibility, diversified across water/wastewater (INR3,694 crores) and renewable energy/BESS (INR3,027 crores).
Diversified order book allows participation across multiple segments of the environmental infrastructure and clean energy value chain.
Water order book split: execution orders INR2,696 crores, O&M orders INR998 crores; renewable order book split: execution orders INR1,948 crores, IPP and O&M orders INR1,079 crores.

subsections.label: New order wins in the quarter
points: Secured new EPC and O&M contract worth INR113 crores from Sardar Sarovar Narmada Nigam Limited in Gujarat, strengthening water infrastructure portfolio.

Through step-down subsidiary Suyog Urja Limited, secured a renewable energy contract worth INR207.5 crores for land aggregation and balance of plant works for a hybrid wind-solar project, strengthening renewable energy value chain capabilities.

Secured two HAM projects in Varanasi under Namami Gange totaling INR256.9 crores: a 60 MLD STP at Lohta (INR130 crores) and a 45 MLD STP at DDU Nagar (INR126.8 crores), both with an 18-month construction period followed by 15-year O&M.
With these additions, HAM portfolio has increased to five projects, strengthening long-term revenue visibility and order book quality.

subsections.label: Execution timelines by segment
points: Water/wastewater execution order book (~INR2,700 crores) has an execution timeline of 18-24 months, effectively to be executed over the next two years.
Renewable order book (~INR2,000 crores) has an execution timeline of 12-18 months.

All turnkey water/wastewater projects (EPC, HAM) come bundled with O&M spanning 5-15 years (avg ~10 years), which can yield ~INR100 crores of topline; O&M gives better EBITDA margin but its value relative to execution remains 3-5%.
Renewable O&M spans 5-12 years for EPC-linked O&M, while IPP income accrues over 25 years.

HAM project process: after award, ~5.5 months required before physical execution start (1.5 months for SPV creation, 4 months for design/drawing and financial closure with condition precedents satisfied by concessionaire (NMCG) and department (UP Jal Nigam)); execution then spans 18-24 months; post-construction, 3-month stabilization period to achieve COD (commercial operation start date) based on performance guarantees, after which 15-year O&M with annuity and interest payments commences quarterly.

JJM-linked water order book (~INR100 crores, a portion of a prior INR1,200 crores order book) expected to complete within this financial year; five projects to be commissioned one by one, with the first expected to be commissioned by October, triggering 10-year O&M.

subsections.label: Bidding pipeline and strike rate
points: Present bid pipeline under evaluation is ~INR3,000 crores; an additional INR6,000-7,000 crores of projects have been invited for bidding and bids are being submitted, keeping the water/wastewater order book pipeline 'very bullish'.

In renewables, company is not aggressively pursuing new orders currently given the already healthy order book; focus remains on executing solar, wind, and BESS before further order book growth, though INR600-800 crores of wind EPC opportunities are being pursued, including Suyog Urja's own wind EPC pipeline of INR800 crores with expected additional orders of INR500-600 crores in FY27.

Strike rate (bid win rate) has been ~20% in the last financial year, supporting an expected order inflow of ~INR2,500 crores for FY27; INR256 crores already secured, leaving ~INR2,250 crores expected for the remainder of the year.
Water/wastewater bid pipeline of interest (Amrut 2, Namami Gange, state government projects backed by World Bank/ADB/JICA loans) stands at ~INR7,000 crores, separate from renewables.

subsections.label: HAM project status detail
points: Of the five HAM projects, one is completed, a second is nearing completion at Mathura, a third at Saharanpur has completed three of eight milestones and is ahead of schedule, and the two newly won Varanasi HAM projects are expected to commence work in October/November.
Company has submitted bids for two more HAM projects currently under evaluation, with more HAM opportunities expected to come up for bidding in the next 3-4 months as DPRs are being finalized.

subsections.label: Water and wastewater segment
points: Remains the core of operations with execution spread across multiple states and project categories including WWTPs, WSSPs and ZLD projects, contributing 71% of consolidated revenue (INR255 crores in Q1 FY27).

Different margin profiles across EPC, HAM, and project types (STPs vs. common effluent treatment plants) drive product mix and blended EBITDA margin outcomes; segment EBITDA margin expected at 21-22% for FY27.

subsections.label: Renewable energy platform
points: Renewable segment revenue contribution rising to ~29% of consolidated revenue (INR104 crores in Q1 FY27), reflecting increasing scale; capabilities now span solar, wind and BESS with both EPC and IPP opportunities.

Wind segment contributed INR80 crores of the INR359 crores total revenue in Q1 FY27, driven by Suyog Urja, which itself contributed INR80 crores in the quarter against an expected FY27 revenue of INR400-450 crores; Suyog Urja carries EBITDA margin of 15-16% and PAT margin of 12%+.
Renewable segment (solar/wind/BESS) EBITDA margin expected at 15-18% for FY27, resulting in a blended EBITDA margin expectation of 19-20%.
Company sees the combination of solar/wind/BESS capabilities providing a broader platform to participate in India's transition to cleaner, more flexible energy infrastructure.
Renewable execution order book stands at INR2,000 crores with O&M and IPP revenue order book of ~INR1,000 crores; company overall present in 17 states.

subsections.label: BESS execution timing
points: NTPC BESS project (930 MWh) procurement of materials will commence in Q3 FY27, expected to drive a significant jump in topline from Q3 onwards.

subsections.label: CBG / biogas diversification
points: Two biogas-to-electricity and CBG projects have been completed and commissioned.

Entered a new CBG project from agricultural waste as part of developing a cattle feed shelter in MP on ~275 acres, which will also include agricultural residue (Napier grass) feedstock and a solar farm development.

subsections.label: Geographic expansion
points: Company now present in 17 states, reflecting continued geographical expansion within India as part of diversification strategy.

Company has already submitted bids for overseas projects and is awaiting outcomes; also looking forward to desalination project opportunities, potentially via joint ventures, expecting overseas and desalination projects to be in company's scope by end of financial year.
Potential business opportunity flagged in the Middle East once ongoing war/conflict situation ends, if company is well placed to bid.

key_figures.label: HAM projects submitted for bidding, pending evaluation

subsections.label: Diversification strategy
points: Company evolving into an integrated engineering service specialist across industry verticals, leveraging technological and project expertise across a wide range of projects.
Convergence of water infrastructure, renewable energy and energy storage seen as a meaningful long-term opportunity.
Diversification in water segment pursued via geographical expansion (domestic then overseas), entry into ZLD, water reuse from STPs, desalination, and joint ventures.

Diversification in renewables pursued by entering solar, then wind (via Suyog Urja acquisition), then BESS, integrating across the entire renewable value chain; once current order book execution completes, company may move into developer role and pursue hybrid opportunities.
CBG derived from wastewater treatment segment is another area of focus to create a good value chain.
Three-tranche Suyog Urja acquisition structure (INR311 crores total) tied to KPIs on revenue, bottom line, and order book at each tranche; second tranche due after FY27, third after FY28.

Last financial year characterized as a period of significant developmental work — team building, new order wins in water/wastewater, integration into renewables (solar asset acquisition, BESS bidding and NTPC BESS EPC win, BESS IPP acquisition, Suyog Urja wind EPC acquisition) — results of which are expected to accrue in the current financial year.

subsections.label: Input cost and margin risk
points: Increase in raw material/input costs since the start of the financial year led to a reduction in EBITDA margin guidance (from 22-24% to 21-22%).

Price variation clauses in tenders (linked to WPI/CPI) cover some cost increase, but company must absorb part of the increase itself; anticipated relief from war-related cost normalization has not materialized.

subsections.label: Working capital / government payment delays
points: Unbilled revenue and working capital position remain bloated, not improved from prior quarter; slowdown in cash flow receipt from government clients.
Management hopes for improvement by September but working capital cycle has remained slow despite fund allocation.

subsections.label: Execution and guidance credibility risk
points: Last financial year saw a large gap between guided (35% growth) and achieved topline, attributed to slower-than-expected order book accumulation rather than execution shortfalls (conversion versus starting order book was 90-95%).
Analyst flagged concern about repeat of prior year's guidance miss; management maintains confidence citing healthy current order book as the basis for FY27 guidance.

subsections.label: JJM funding risk (eased)
points: JJM and JJM 2.0 funding was a risk in the past but funds are now streamlining and releasing; company's MP-based JJM projects did not see funds stalled even in the prior financial year.

subsections.label: Guidance reaffirmation and rationale
points: Management reaffirmed FY27 revenue guidance of INR2,000 crores and PAT guidance of INR260-270 crores, citing no slippages across renewable (solar IPP, BESS IPP, BESS EPC) or water segments.

Q1 revenue of INR360 crores considered on target despite appearing below a straight-line 20-21% quarterly run-rate, because BESS project (NTPC, 930 MWh) material procurement will commence in Q3, driving a significant revenue jump from Q3 onward.
Even without any new orders, current order book alone is expected to be sufficient to achieve the INR2,000 crores topline target for FY27.
Management targets to at least meet guidance and would like to 'outdo' it, while maintaining INR2,000 crores as the official guidance figure.
Water segment guidance based on conservative 50% conversion rate of the INR2,700 crores order book, implying ~INR1,300-1,350 crores of revenue.

For the next two to three years, company expects continuous growth of at least 25-30% while maintaining healthy margin levels; explicitly stated it is not inclined to take on projects where margin profile is low.
FY27 EBITDA margin guidance of 19-20% blended (21-22% standalone water), with PAT margin guidance of 13-14% blended; order inflow guidance of INR2,500 crores for FY27.

guidance_ledger.statement: Revenue guidance is INR2,000 crores for this financial year.
We stick to our guidance of INR260 crores to INR270 crores PAT levels.
For the current financial year, we have lowered our guidance a bit in the range of 21% to 22%.
At a blended level we can expect the EBITDA margins to be somewhere in the range of 19% to 20%.
At a blended level the EBITDA margins could be in the range of 19% to 20% with profitability's in the range of somewhere around 13% to 14%.

We can expect an order inflow of somewhere around INR2,500 crores to be there in the current financial year... out of this INR2,500 crores, INR256 crores is what we have got... we expect that INR2,250 crores in the current financial year.
Our expectation is in the range of INR400 crores to INR450 crores what we will do as revenue from Suyog Urja Limited.
We do expect another INR500 crores to INR600 crores projects which will come in wind EPC segment for this financial year.
We expect some good orders in the wind EPC segment wherein we are looking for some good projects of around INR600 crores to INR800 crores further getting accumulated in the company.
We look forward to a continuous growth of somewhere around 25% - 30% which should be bare minimum at which the company should keep on growing and with maintaining the healthy margin levels.
In water and wastewater treatment segment we expect EBITDA margin somewhere in the range of 21% to 22%.
In the renewable segment which spans over solar, wind and BESS, the EBITDA margin shall be in the range of 15% to 18%.
We have maintained a conservative conversion rate of 50% and we are expecting INR1,300 crores to be our topline.
We expect a prudent level of somewhere around 5% to 5.5% of the employee cost when we will move ahead in this financial year.

At a blended level during this entire financial year when the topline is expected to be in the range of INR2,000 crores, so we can expect this financial cost to be also to be in the range of 3% to 3.5%.
We do expect that cash flow, operational cash flow should turn positive. We do hope but we cannot give any guarantees on this.
By September when we will come out with our cash flow position, I am quite sure that we will be sitting at a healthy cash flow level.
If we see by the end of this financial year, the overseas projects and the desalination project should also be there in the company's scope.

We do have two projects for which the bid evaluations are underway... we are expecting some HAM projects which will be available for bidding in next three to four months' time since the DPRs are just on the move.
We are looking forward to a top line of around INR2,000 crore for FY27.
A topline of around INR2,000 crores with PAT number somewhere around 13.5% to 14%, so INR270 crore to INR280 crore can be the PAT number.
Last year, we had given a guidance of 35% growth in topline, and that we did not meet.
In the BESS business, which is EPC, we will expect PAT margin somewhere in the range of 10%.
We look forward to achieving PAT margins in the range of 10% to 12%, a blended one from the renewables. It will vary from project to project.
A 1:1 debt level is we would not like to cross at any point of time... as a consolidated books as well.
I don't think that it will be a bigger amount in terms of capex... I think it can be to the tune of INR20 crores, INR30-odd crores, not more than that.
Last year we did somewhere around INR250 crores in Q1. The present position will be much better even despite the global crisis which is ongoing.
Execution timeline is 18 months to 24 months for these (renewable ~INR2,000 crore order book) projects.

risk_register.risk: Raw material / input cost inflation
risk_register.note: Increase in raw material cost since start of financial year led to lowering of EBITDA margin guidance from 22-24% to 21-22%; estimated 1-2% of topline impact.

risk_register.risk: Working capital / bloated receivables and slow government fund release
risk_register.note: Position not improved versus last quarter; still bloated, though company has unencumbered funds and no liability slippage; slowdown in cash flow from government clients.

risk_register.risk: Guidance credibility / execution vs order book accumulation
risk_register.note: Prior year guidance miss attributed to slower-than-expected order book accumulation, not execution; conversion versus starting order book was 90-95%.

risk_register.risk: Employee cost increase from team expansion
risk_register.note: Team size grew from ~900 to 2,300, pushing employee cost to ~7% of revenue in Q1 versus historical 3-3.5%; expected to normalize to 5-5.5%.

risk_register.risk: Higher finance/interest cost impacting profitability
risk_register.note: Finance cost currently ~4% of revenue, linked partly to renewable/IPP blend; expected to normalize to 3-3.5% at blended annual level.

risk_register.risk: JJM funding delays
risk_register.note: JJM and JJM 2.0 funds are now streamlining and releasing; MP-based JJM projects did not see funds stalled even last year; total JJM exposure small (~INR150-160 crores).

risk_register.risk: Price pass-through limitations on new orders
risk_register.note: Price variation clause (WPI/CPI-linked) covers part of cost increases, but company must absorb some portion itself in EPC pricing.

risk_register.risk: Elongated order finalization/bid evaluation timelines across the sector
risk_register.note: Led to slower-than-expected conversion of bid pipeline into orders, causing FY26 revenue guidance miss.

risk_register.risk: Re-bidding of projects due to technical glitches
risk_register.note: A project where company was L1 (Nov-Dec) went into re-bidding after department cancelled all bids; lost timeline, outcome neither favorable nor unfavorable.

risk_register.risk: Projects stuck in design/approval stage
risk_register.note: MIDC CETP ZLD project and 2 Bangalore projects remained in design stage, preventing revenue recognition despite mobilization costs being incurred.

risk_register.risk: Geopolitical global crisis raising commodity and battery cell import costs
risk_register.note: Prompted 1-2 percentage point downward revision to EBITDA margin guidance (to 21-22% from 22-24%); lithium-ion battery import prices have risen, leading to deferred procurement.

risk_register.risk: Partial cost pass-through via price variation clauses
risk_register.note: Price variation clauses cover only part of market cost increases, not the entire price increase, requiring lowered margin guidance.

risk_register.risk: Delayed government fund releases (AMRUT scheme)
risk_register.note: Funds did not get released as expected by March across Chhattisgarh, MP, Rajasthan, Haryana, Punjab, stretching UBR days to 195 and net working capital cycle to 166 days; funds from Chhattisgarh have since been released and others are expected soon.

risk_register.risk: Historical delays in central government fund releases (previously Jal Jeevan Mission, now AMRUT)
risk_register.note: Management noted challenges with timely release of centrally sponsored funds over the last two financial years versus a historically more timely release pattern.

risk_register.risk: Funding gap on partially-funded, highly-executed projects
risk_register.note: 3-4 projects that are 70% complete have received only 10-15% of contracted funds, creating a significant cash gap despite fast execution.

risk_register.risk: OCF distorted by long-term service concession receivables
risk_register.note: 15-year long-term service concession agreement receivables must be included in OCF per audit policy, making post-tax OCF appear negative (-INR63 crore) despite adjusted OCF being positive.

themes.label: Margin pressure from commodity/input costs
themes.note: Raw material cost increase, employee cost rise, and renewable business blend drove EBITDA margin down to 21.07% from 26.65% YoY, prompting lowered full-year guidance to 21-22% standalone / 19-20% blended.

themes.label: Order book strength
themes.note: Total order book of ~INR6,721 crores across water/wastewater and renewables provides strong revenue visibility, with new wins of INR113 crores, INR207.5 crores and INR256.9 crores secured in the quarter.

themes.label: Renewable energy diversification
themes.note: Renewable platform (solar, wind, BESS) now contributes ~29% of consolidated revenue, with Suyog Urja wind EPC integration and NTPC BESS project expected to drive scale from Q3 FY27.

themes.label: Working capital stress / government fund delays
themes.note: Unbilled revenue and working capital cycle remain bloated with slow government client fund releases, though management expects improvement by September and reports no bad debts.

themes.label: Guidance credibility / execution delays
themes.note: Management defended prior year's guidance miss as due to slower order book accumulation (not execution, which achieved 90-95% conversion), and reaffirmed FY27 revenue/PAT guidance despite Q1 appearing below straight-line run-rate.

themes.label: BESS/battery storage first-mover positioning
themes.note: NTPC 930 MWh BESS project procurement to commence Q3 FY27, expected to drive a significant topline jump; Suyog Urja wind EPC pipeline also expanding.

themes.label: Segment margin mix impact
themes.note: Water/wastewater EBITDA margin guided at 21-22% versus renewable segment at 15-18%, with blended margin of 19-20% reflecting the changing revenue mix as renewables scale.

key_takeaways: Total order book stands at approximately INR6,721 crores providing strong revenue visibility for the coming periods, comprising INR3,694 crores in water and wastewater treatment segment and INR3,027 crores across renewable energy and BESS.
Revenue from operations stood at INR359.2 crores, registering a growth of 49% Y-o-Y driven by continued execution across the order book.
EBITDA stood at INR75.7 crores, registering a 17.87% Y-o-Y growth; EBITDA margin stood at 21.07% compared with 26.65% in Q1 FY26 and 18.7% in Q4 FY26.
Profit after tax stood at INR45.2 crores, registering a 6.47% Y-o-Y growth, while PAT margin stood at 12.38%, broadly stable sequentially compared with 12.37% in Q4 FY26.

The core water and wastewater treatment segment contributed approximately INR255 crores representing 71% of the consolidated revenue; renewable segment revenue contributed approximately INR104 crores, around 29% of consolidated revenue.

During the quarter, secured a new EPC and O&M contract worth INR113 crores from Sardar Sarovar Narmada Nigam Limited, a renewable energy contract worth INR207.5 crores via Suyog Urja Limited, and two HAM projects in Varanasi worth a combined INR256.9 crores, taking the HAM portfolio to five projects.
Management maintains FY27 guidance of ~INR2,000 crores revenue, INR260-270 crores PAT, EBITDA margin 21-22% (standalone)/19-20% (blended), and order inflow of ~INR2,500 crores.
Management expects a significant revenue jump from Q3 FY27 onwards as procurement for the NTPC 930 MWh BESS project commences.
pressing_questions: Last year there was a massive delta between what the management committed and what was achieved. I think we gave over about 7% year-on-year target. How confident are we this year in terms of execution and achieving the topline guidance of what you have been providing? And are we chasing growth at the cost of margins?

As per our history of execution, Q1 constitutes around 21% of our total turnover. So, if we follow this, our turnover should be in the range of around INR420 or INR425 crores, but this quarter we delivered around INR360 crores. What was the reason of this lower-than-expected execution and do you still stick to your guidance of around INR2000 crores turnover in FY27?

Last year we had a problem in execution as we could not get the order in time. So, we were not able to meet our target. This year we have order in hand. Do you foresee any other headwinds which may not allow us to achieve this target?

These INR2,000 crores revenue guidance was like, is still, we already have the orders in hand. What is the best strategy we can have to execute much more or get the revenue of around let's say INR2,500 crores or INR3,000 crores?

quarters.summary: FY26 revenue grew 7.5% YoY to INR11,456mn with EBITDA margin at 24.2%, though management admitted the earlier 35% topline growth guidance was missed due to elongated order finalization/re-bidding delays and projects stuck in design stage. For FY27, management guided to ~INR2,000 crore topline (conservative, ~42% conversion of the current ~INR4,800 crore order book) with EBITDA margin lowered to 21-22% (from 22-24%) due to a geopolitical/commodity cost shock, and PAT margin of ~13.5-14% (PAT of INR270-280 crore). Order book stands at an all-time high of over INR6,814 crore (including O&M/IPP), providing revenue visibility for FY27 and FY28, with FY28 revenue expected to grow 35-40% further on the balance order book.

subsections.label: Margin compression explanation
points: Management stated margin compression is not structural but arises from a mix of factors: cost of manufacturing actually declined by ~1 percentage point (positive), while employee cost rose to ~6% of revenue (up ~1.5 percentage points) because employees were mobilized on projects that remained in the design stage without generating revenue.
Other expenses rose to 3.5% of revenue, including an ECL provision of INR10 crore booked as per Ind AS.
Depreciation increased by ~INR25 crore due to procurement of various construction equipment.
A component of ~INR100-120 crore of revenue came from renewable IPP execution with practically no margin, distorting the reported blended margin.
Full-year EBITDA margin remained above 24%, indicating no real margin compression on an annualized basis despite the Q4 optics.

subsections.label: Working capital stretch
points: Working capital cycle stretched to 166 days from a targeted 95-100 days, mainly due to non-release of funds from AMRUT projects across Chhattisgarh, MP, Rajasthan, Haryana and Punjab by March as expected.
Company did not slow down execution despite funds not being released; project momentum was maintained.
UBR (unbilled revenue) days rose sharply to 195 days while receivable days actually declined to 53 days.
Positive development: funds from Chhattisgarh have been released, and confirmation received that funds are coming for Rajasthan, Haryana and MP.

In some projects (3-4 instances), a project that is 70% complete has received only 10-15% of funds, creating a large funding gap despite fast execution (target completion of 2-year projects within 13-14 months).

subsections.label: Cash flow
points: Adjusted OCF was positive in FY26; OCF pre-tax was almost balanced at ~INR4 lakh positive.
OCF post-tax was negative INR63 crore, distorted by service concession agreement receivables which are inherently 15-year long-term receivables but must be included in OCF per audit policy.
Management expects the situation to ease in the next financial year as MP water supply projects near completion and AMRUT fund releases come through, which should reduce UBR levels and improve OCF.

subsections.label: Debt profile
points: Finance cost has dipped versus last financial year despite rising debt.
Total debt of INR422 crore comprises INR250 crore long-term debt (tied to assets/term loans/HAM projects) and INR175 crore short-term loan (part of CC utilized at certain points).
Company will not cross a 1:1 debt level on a consolidated basis; if leverage rises, it will consider offloading/monetizing assets, especially to manage development projects in the renewable segment.

subsections.label: Order book composition and visibility
points: Total order book of over INR6,814 crore provides robust revenue visibility over next 24 months.
Current execution order book of INR4,800 crore covers at least 2 financial years (FY27 and FY28) along with decent growth expected.

Recent additions include BUIDCO project, Pune/Nashik sanitation projects under Swachh Bharat Mission, 4 BESS EPC projects from NTPC across UP, Assam, Karnataka and Telangana, plus a 150 MWh BESS project acquisition in Bihar, positioning the company as a first mover in India's 90 GW battery storage pipeline.

subsections.label: Reasons for FY26 revenue guidance miss
points: Guidance of 35% topline growth was missed due to elongated order evaluation/bid finalization timelines across the sector versus anticipated faster conversion.

A project where the company was L1 in Nov-Dec went into re-bidding due to a technical glitch that forced the department to cancel and re-invite all bids, costing timeline (re-bidding outcome was neither favorable nor unfavorable to the company, just a lost timeline).
Some projects bagged around August (an MIDC CETP ZLD project and 2 Bangalore projects) remained in the design/approval stage through the year and could not generate revenue.

Despite the shortfall, conversion of the INR1,200 crore order book on hand at the start of FY26 into revenue was ~95%, indicating the issue was more about the pace of new order additions/conversion rather than execution delay on order book in hand.

subsections.label: FY27/FY28 order book to revenue conversion approach
points: FY27 revenue guidance of ~INR2,000 crore represents a conservative ~42% conversion of the current INR4,800 crore order book, intentionally conservative to avoid repeating the prior guidance miss.
FY28 revenue could come from the balance order book of ~INR2,800 crore, or conservatively INR2,500-2,600 crore, implying continued growth in the 35-40% range historically targeted.

Renewable segment execution timeline for the current ~INR2,000 crore order book is 18-24 months; management is being conservative and not projecting a higher execution/revenue number for FY27 from renewables specifically.

subsections.label: Water & wastewater segment strengthening
points: Four completed projects highlighted: 100 MLD STP at Jodhpur (upgraded to IFAS biological reactor system, with power generation from biogas and ultra-filtration for disinfection); 55 MLD STP at Varanasi (substantial electricity offset via solar cells placed atop the reactor — first such implementation in India, acknowledged by NMCG); 25 MLD CETP at Sarigam; 30 MLD STP at Bhiwadi.
Company is increasing pre-qualification capabilities for complex wastewater treatment plants, becoming eligible for higher capacities, and expanding geographical presence.

subsections.label: Renewable segment build-out
points: Renewable platform established across solar, wind and BESS within about a year, motivated originally by sustainability/waste-to-energy and solar integration experience from water projects.
Order book built to ~INR2,050 crore within a year, including the 930 MWh NTPC BESS combination project, 150 MWh BESS acquisition, and Suyog wind EPC acquisition.
Segmental revenues and profitability will be presented separately going forward for clearer visibility.

Combined blended profitability across water and renewable is expected at ~14% PAT margin on the ~INR2,000 crore FY27 topline (INR270-280 crore PAT), with a possible 1-2 percentage point pressure from the geopolitical/commodity cost crisis.

subsections.label: O&M / IPP income
points: O&M order book for wastewater treatment is INR950-odd crore; O&M/IPP income under renewable is INR1,000 crore (also cited as INR1,079 crore in order book breakdown).
O&M margins are comparatively higher than execution margins; O&M revenue (water-wastewater) forms only 3-5% of total revenue currently but is increasing in absolute terms year-on-year.
IPP income from renewable O&M expected to generate decent IRR in future, adding to absolute profitability from the O&M business.

subsections.label: BESS segment margin dynamics
points: BESS EPC PAT margin currently expected around 10%, pressured by rising lithium-ion battery cell import prices.

Company is prioritizing BOS work (civil works, transformers, HT electrical lines) first, deferring lithium-ion battery procurement until prices settle, while design and mobilization work has already started.

subsections.label: Segment revenue disclosure detail
points: Renewable segment revenue for the full year was INR120 crore (also stated as INR129 crore); Q4 alone contributed INR117 crore of renewable revenue versus only ~INR12 crore through 9M, reflecting the segment's recent start (first project came in August).

Renewable revenue guidance for FY26 was originally ~INR200 crore, against which ~INR120-130 crore was achieved — a shortfall attributed evenly (~INR100 crore each) between renewables and wastewater segments.

subsections.label: Technology component by plant type
points: STPs and CETPs have a significant technology component — the biological reactor design and choice of equipment materially affect capex; CETP design is considered one of the most complex systems, with tech/design effort being substantial.

Water treatment plants (conventional type) are comparatively less tech-heavy and more civil-work/construction-management oriented; desalination plants bring the tech component back into significant play.

CETP costs vary widely by industry inlet characteristics (textile, ZLD systems, food industry, metal processing, petrochemical), each requiring different plant design, making generalized per-MLD costing difficult.

Contract mode: water treatment plants and CETPs generally bid in EPC mode; some STPs come under HAM mode; future models may include BOT/revenue-generation structures as treated water recirculation to industry becomes a potential revenue stream (early stage).

subsections.label: New technology implementations
points: 100 MLD STP at Jodhpur uses IFAS biological reactor upgrade, biogas-based power generation, and ultra-filtration for disinfection.
55 MLD STP at Varanasi offsets a substantial portion of electricity requirement via solar cells placed on top of the reactor — a first-of-its-kind implementation in India, acknowledged by NMCG.

MIDC CETP ZLD project for a textile complex requires UF and RO components, which will help build pre-qualification for entering desalination projects; company is actively looking at desalination opportunities, potentially via joint ventures.

subsections.label: Capex approach
points: Capex for project execution is largely need-based: equipment requirement per new project generally INR4-5 crore, with company first considering repetition/reuse of existing equipment across projects before purchasing new equipment.
No major capex planned beyond last financial year's level (~INR20-30 crore); management does not expect capex to be a significant amount going forward.

subsections.label: Geographic project spread
points: AMRUT projects being executed across Chhattisgarh, MP, Rajasthan, Haryana and Punjab.
NTPC BESS EPC projects located in Uttar Pradesh, Assam, Karnataka and Telangana, plus a BESS project acquisition in Bihar.
Company is expanding geographical presence in wastewater treatment as it gains pre-qualification for higher-capacity, more complex plants.

subsections.label: Commodity/import cost pressure
points: Rising commodity/raw material prices, linked to an ongoing geopolitical global crisis, are pushing up costs; lithium-ion battery cell import prices for BESS have risen.
Company plans to defer procurement of lithium-ion batteries until prices stabilize, while proceeding with BOS work (civil, transformer, HT electrical lines) and design/mobilization in the interim.
Price variation clauses in most contracts allow partial pass-through of cost increases to customers, but do not cover the entire market price increase, necessitating a lowered margin guidance.

subsections.label: Client de-risking via B2B/private clients
points: Renewable segment order book is largely B2B: NTPC orders reduce receivable risk; Suyog's wind EPC projects are executed for A to AAA-rated private companies, helping de-risk the client base versus reliance on government payment cycles (which faced delays under Jal Jeevan and AMRUT schemes).

Government-funded/centrally sponsored water projects have faced payment delays from the center over the last two financial years versus historically timely release; funds are now understood to be earmarked for release under AMRUT.

subsections.label: Future diversification opportunities
points: Desalination: actively looking into opportunities, potential entry via joint ventures, aided by UF/RO pre-qualification being built through the MIDC CETP ZLD project.

Transmission & Distribution (T&D): current NTPC BESS projects involve EHV transformers and transmission/HT lines, building pre-qualifications; company is not actively bidding in T&D currently given a decent order book, but views it as a potential future diversification opportunity.

subsections.label: Renewable energy platform build-out
points: Acquisition of Suyog Urja Limited, a wind EPC company, described as a significant milestone strengthening execution capabilities in renewables and providing access to an experienced team with a strong project delivery track record.
Acquisition of a 150 MWh BESS project in Bihar.
Company has appointed dedicated business heads for each division and built a renewable energy team of over 250 professionals led by experienced industry veterans across the renewable value chain.

Diversification strategy described as disciplined and complementary to existing water infrastructure strengths, targeting convergence of water infrastructure, renewable energy, energy efficiency and environmental sustainability.

subsections.label: Reporting structure
points: Company will present renewable segment revenues and order book separately as a distinct segment/company going forward, giving clearer segmental profitability visibility.

subsections.label: Key risks flagged
points: Order finalization/bid evaluation timelines across the water sector remained longer than anticipated, delaying order book conversion into revenue.
Re-bidding of a project (where company was L1) due to a technical glitch forced by the department, causing lost timeline.
Projects remaining stuck in design/approval stage (MIDC CETP ZLD project, 2 Bangalore projects) prevented revenue recognition despite mobilization.
Geopolitical global crisis has led to rising commodity/raw material and lithium-ion battery cell import costs, prompting a 1-2 percentage point downward revision to EBITDA margin guidance.
Price variation clauses in contracts do not fully offset market price increases, only partially compensating for cost inflation.
Delayed release of funds from AMRUT scheme projects across Chhattisgarh, MP, Rajasthan, Haryana and Punjab led to elongated working capital cycle (166 days) despite continued execution momentum.
Government/central funding delays over the last two financial years for centrally sponsored projects (previously Jal Jeevan Mission delays, now AMRUT scheme) versus historically timely fund releases.
Instances where projects that are 70% complete have received only 10-15% of contracted funds, creating a significant funding gap in 3-4 projects.

subsections.label: FY27 outlook rationale
points: Management deliberately set a conservative FY27 revenue guidance of ~INR2,000 crore (only ~42% conversion of the INR4,800 crore order book) to avoid repeating the prior year's guidance miss.

EBITDA margin guidance lowered to 21-22% from 22-24% due to global geopolitical crisis pushing up commodity and raw material costs; management does not expect this to be a bigger hit, foreseeing only a 1-2 percentage point dip if unresolved.
FY27 PAT guidance of INR270-280 crore corresponds to ~13.5-14% PAT margin on ~INR2,000 crore topline, split as ~INR1,350 crore from water & wastewater and ~INR650 crore from renewables.

Q1 FY27 expected to be meaningfully better than Q1 FY26 (~INR250 crore), despite ongoing global cost pressures, though no specific number was given; three entities now contribute — parent EIEL, the renewable subsidiary, and Suyog (wind EPC).
FY28 growth expected to continue in the historical 35-40% range, based on execution of the balance order book (~INR2,800 crore, or conservatively INR2,500-2,600 crore).

subsections.label: Analyst pushback on guidance credibility
points: An individual investor (Sheetal Shah) directly questioned the credibility of guidance given the prior year's miss and requested realistic, achievable targets going forward; management responded that this year's INR2,000 crore guidance (42% conversion) is a deliberately conservative, doubly-sure figure based on order book already in hand, unlike last year's growth guidance which depended on orders not yet secured.

risk_register.note: A project where company was L1 (Nov-Dec) went into re-bidding after department cancelled all bids; lost timeline, outcome neither favorable nor unfavorable.

risk_register.risk: Projects stuck in design/approval stage
risk_register.note: MIDC CETP ZLD project and 2 Bangalore projects remained in design stage, preventing revenue recognition despite mobilization costs being incurred.

risk_register.risk: Geopolitical global crisis raising commodity and battery cell import costs
risk_register.note: Prompted 1-2 percentage point downward revision to EBITDA margin guidance (to 21-22% from 22-24%); lithium-ion battery import prices have risen, leading to deferred procurement.

risk_register.risk: Partial cost pass-through via price variation clauses
risk_register.note: Price variation clauses cover only part of market cost increases, not the entire price increase, requiring lowered margin guidance.

risk_register.risk: Delayed government fund releases (AMRUT scheme)
risk_register.note: Funds did not get released as expected by March across Chhattisgarh, MP, Rajasthan, Haryana, Punjab, stretching UBR days to 195 and net working capital cycle to 166 days; funds from Chhattisgarh have since been released and others are expected soon.

risk_register.risk: Historical delays in central government fund releases (previously Jal Jeevan Mission, now AMRUT)
risk_register.note: Management noted challenges with timely release of centrally sponsored funds over the last two financial years versus a historically more timely release pattern.

risk_register.risk: Funding gap on partially-funded, highly-executed projects
risk_register.note: 3-4 projects that are 70% complete have received only 10-15% of contracted funds, creating a significant cash gap despite fast execution.

risk_register.risk: OCF distorted by long-term service concession receivables
risk_register.note: 15-year long-term service concession agreement receivables must be included in OCF per audit policy, making post-tax OCF appear negative (-INR63 crore) despite adjusted OCF being positive.

themes.label: Guidance credibility / execution delays
themes.note: FY26's 35% growth guidance was missed due to elongated order evaluation timelines and projects stuck in design stage; management is now giving deliberately conservative FY27 guidance to rebuild credibility.

themes.label: Renewable energy diversification
themes.note: Company built a renewable platform (solar, wind, BESS) within a year via Suyog Urja acquisition and NTPC BESS wins, growing order book to ~INR2,050 crore.

themes.label: Order book strength
themes.note: All-time high order book of over INR6,814 crore gives revenue visibility for FY27 and FY28.

themes.label: Margin pressure from commodity/input costs
themes.note: Geopolitical crisis raising commodity and lithium-ion battery import costs led to 1-2 percentage point cut in EBITDA margin guidance (22-24% to 21-22%).

themes.label: Working capital stress / government fund delays
themes.note: Net working capital cycle stretched to 166 days due to delayed AMRUT scheme fund releases across multiple states, though release is beginning to ease.

themes.label: BESS/battery storage first-mover positioning
themes.note: NTPC BESS wins (930 MWh) and Bihar acquisition (150 MWh) position company as a first mover in India's 90 GW battery storage pipeline.

themes.label: Segment margin mix impact
themes.note: Blended margins impacted by low/no-margin IPP execution revenue mixing with core EPC business; management plans separate segmental reporting for renewables going forward.

key_takeaways: Total order book has surged to over INR6,814 crores, providing robust revenue visibility over the next 24 months.

In Q4 FY26, our revenue from operations stood at INR4,273 million, representing a growth of 8.8% year-on-year. EBITDA stood at INR799 million, while the EBITDA margin came in at 18.7%. PAT for the quarter was INR543 million with PAT margin at 12.4%.

For the full year, our revenue reached INR11,456 million, a growth of 7.5% year-on-year... EBITDA for the full year improved by 3.4% to INR2,768 million with a margin of 24.2%... PAT for FY26 was reported at INR1,884 million with a margin of 15.9%.

Last year, we had given a guidance of 35% growth in topline, and that we did not meet... the delay, a partial delay in the evaluation process, this is one of the factors... this is why we have missed the revenue guidance which we projected.

We are just projecting a topline of INR2,000-odd crores, which will replicate into a conversion of somewhere around 42%... I am reducing my EBITDA guidance to somewhere around 21% to 22%, which was earlier 22% to 24%.
The working capital has got stretched to 166 days. The main reason this time has been... the funds didn't get released from the AMRUT projects.

A significant milestone during the year was the acquisition of Suyog Urja Limited, a wind EPC company... In addition, we secured multiple BESS projects and expanded our participation in emerging opportunities within the energy storage ecosystem.

We secured 4 BESS projects from NTPC... having a combined capacity of 930 megawatt-hour, and the value is approximately INR1,070 crores... This positions us as a first mover in India's 90 gigawatt battery storage pipeline.
pressing_questions: Manish Choraghe: Last year, we had given a guidance of 35% growth in topline, and that we did not meet. And if we look at the Q4 margins, that are the weakest margins. So are we facing any execution delays in the business?

Darshil Jhaveri: I didn't get the margin that you were saying that INR100 crores was from IPP which led to a lower margin, because even in Q3, we were very confident of being able to do INR230 crores of PAT, right?... So then what changed?

Sheetal Shah: What are the factors that you are banking on, which will help us to achieve this? ...do we face -- can we face such situation this year also or we are banking only on our order book to achieve this target? And what factors which can go against, which may hamper us in not achieving this goal?

Sheetal Shah: I just wanted to give a suggestion to sir to give a realistic projection henceforth, sir. That is only our request as an investor to you, sir. Only achievable targets and realistic targets, sir.

Anboli: Sir, also my another question is, going forward, how can an investor should look at this company? Just as Mr. Manish at starting, it was like Wastewater Treatment Company, now it is into BESS. And going forward, what are the plans? Are we into desalination kind of things?
Anboli: Sir, one follow-up. Are we looking only into India, or just into abroad as well? [connection lost, unanswered]

quarters.summary: Management flagged that soda ash (Industrial essentials, ~50% of revenue) faces near-term pricing and cost challenges from Chinese oversupply, elevated Chinese inventories, and Middle East-driven freight/input cost inflation, while Living essentials (salt, bicarbonate, prebiotics, feed/food/pharma) and Farm essentials (Rallis, Morocco JV) continue steady-to-strong demand. Consolidated revenue was up 14% YoY with EBITDA down ~INR 100 crores YoY on sharply lower realizations, even as standalone India business delivered strong growth (revenue +10%, EBITDA +35%, PAT from continuing operations +12%); annualized capex is being guided to around the depreciation level (~INR 1,200 crores) and net debt reduced via asset monetization, with management watching post-October developments in Kenya HFO, India limestone/logistics and the Middle East conflict for further cost impact.

subsections.label: Consolidated vs Standalone performance
points: Consolidated revenue was up 14%, but EBITDA was down about INR 100 crores compared to previous year despite sharply lower realization.
Net debt was lower by INR 5,692 crores compared to previous quarter on account of monetization of assets.

Standalone was a very strong performance with higher volumes and stronger realizations backed by higher fixed cost control, with revenue up 10% and EBITDA up 35% YoY, and PAT from continuing operations up 12% YoY.
Some projects were capitalized leading to higher depreciation.

subsections.label: India margin expansion drivers
points: EBITDA margins in India rose to 28%, more than 10 percentage points higher QoQ, partly due to inventory optimization: plant-level optimization to deliver higher salt volumes led to throttling of soda ash production, not related to market demand.
Bicarbonate volumes were impacted by realignment of some tendered contracts foregone during the quarter due to pricing issues, expected to be recovered during the year.
Inventory gains from low-cost coal are expected to reverse next quarter as fresh coal inventory comes in at elevated pricing (due to higher freight cost, not basic price).

Price increases have not yet been transmitted to all customers (only spot price increase realized so far); management expects volumes to remain steady but margin could see marginal pressure from cost side.
Guided sustainable EBITDA margin for India business is around 18%, with ~32-33% GC margin.

subsections.label: Debt & Capital Allocation
points: Debt reduction of INR 300 crores compared to March came from sale of land and some shares held by the company; non-core land/investments monetized during the quarter totaled about INR 300 crores.
Non-core land monetization planned in second half/after Q2; other non-core monetization options to be evaluated as required, no specifics committed on this call.

Annualized capex guided to be around the depreciation number (~INR 1,200 crores consolidated FY26 depreciation), with intent to stay at or below that level through the year including all planned capex.

subsections.label: Cost items
points: Employee cost included a one-off reversal of about INR 43-45 crores; adjusted run rate would be higher (~INR 590 crores) versus INR 517 crores last year and INR 524 crores in Q4, largely due to rupee depreciation impact on overseas costs and Q1 seasonal variable pay payouts.

UK EBITDA was impacted by two one-off items totaling about GBP 2.4 million: loss on sale of EU ETS (expected to reverse by October quarter) and prior period adjustments; UK is expected to be EBITDA positive and trend toward PBT breakeven for the full year and from next quarter onwards as one-offs are not expected to repeat.

subsections.label: New segment structure
points: Company reclassified reporting from two segments (Basic Chemistry and Specialty Products) into three: Living Essentials, Industrial Essentials, and Farm Essentials.
Farm Essentials comprises Rallis and Morocco (reported as JV income).
Living Essentials comprises salt, bicarbonate, prebiotics, and products for feed, food, and pharma.
Industrial Essentials comprises soda ash, silica, and industrial chemicals including bromine, chlorine, and caustic.

Objective is to sharpen focus on non-cyclical, sustainability-led products with high customer stickiness and less pricing volatility, and to align capital allocation and reporting with how the business is actually run.
Reclassification reflects investor feedback seeking better visibility into what is driving growth for each business rather than one large combined segment.
Geography-specific reporting will continue to be provided to analysts alongside the new segment view.

By geography: in India, standalone revenue is split between Living and Industrial; US and Kenya fall fully under Industrial; UK falls fully under Living (having shut down industrial businesses 100% as unsustainable); Singapore folds into Living Essentials.

subsections.label: Rallis (Farm Essentials)
points: Rallis saw overall revenue growth due to higher volumes and higher pricing.
EBITDA growth was primarily driven by better volume in crop protection and optimization of fixed cost.

subsections.label: IMACID associate
points: IMACID did not produce during the quarter because of high sulfur prices; operations have just begun.
Income from associates turned negative this quarter due to the plant not running; margin pressure expected to continue but the business is expected to be profitable for the full year.

subsections.label: Sodium-ion battery development
points: Company has produced the first full battery pack including BMS (battery management system) and full assembly, undergoing testing by power companies and data centers for storage applications.
Business strategy for sodium-ion battery is being reviewed, focused on energy storage for renewable power and data centers rather than mobility applications, including drones.
A drone flight test was conducted purely to prove the product in an extreme application; customer specification focus remains on static/stationary applications, not mobility.
Technology uses soda ash as a cathode active material, which the company already manufactures; the process has been patented.
Piloting/testing phase is underway and expected to take the better part of the year (6-9 months) before specifics on commercialization plans, energy density, and cycle metrics are shared.
Company will focus on chemicals and cathode active material production; decision on whether to enter full prismatic or cylindrical cell manufacturing will be shared as plans unfold.
Domestic Indian demand seen as very strong given growth in data centers and renewable power focus; exports not ruled out but not yet part of formal strategy.
For lithium battery/lithium carbonate production, two parts of soda ash are needed for every part of lithium carbonate produced; equivalent sodium-ion ratio to be shared after piloting.
Full-scale plant for sodium-ion battery is expected about two years after the pilot/lab-to-customer phase, which itself is targeted to conclude by end of year.

subsections.label: LFP battery recycling
points: Company is setting up a recycling unit internally, planned for Mithapur, with no major capex needed.
Initial volume will be small because the number of vehicles older than seven-eight years is currently very small.
Business will be built on OEM tie-ups, especially with auto manufacturers.

subsections.label: Project timelines
points: 82.5 KTPA salt plant in India expected to become operational by this fiscal year-end, with market supply starting Q1 of next financial year.
210 KTPA salt plant in South India has a 24-month execution timeline.
50 KTPA silica plant has a similar 24-month execution timeline; both projects expected to become operational sometime during 2028.

subsections.label: Regional demand trends
points: China and US demand remain mostly flat.
LATAM demand has strengthened, supported by rising lithium carbonate production, with exports to Argentina up 53% and Chile up 32%.
Southeast Asian demand declined marginally and is the region with maximum pricing pressure from Chinese exports.
Arabian Gulf saw major market demand disruption; elsewhere no major disruptions despite cost pressures.
India continues to demonstrate stronger demand momentum long-term, supported by renewables and electrification focus.

subsections.label: US business
points: US had higher revenue YoY due to higher volumes, partially offset by slightly lower pricing.
EBITDA impacted by lower realization and higher fixed costs (fixed in USD but higher in INR terms due to exchange rate).
Demand remained stable; export markets, especially Southeast Asia, were well supplied.
US did well mainly on higher exports to LATAM and Northeast Asian markets; largely vacated Southeast Asian exports to Chinese suppliers, similar to other US players.
Domestic US demand is stable with no volume growth, pricing broadly stable (a USD 3-4 shift here and there); main cost pressure is on logistics/transportation, being addressed customer by customer.
US volume/export vs domestic split to be shared next quarter.

subsections.label: UK business
points: UK had higher revenue YoY due to higher volumes, with lower pricing in some product segments.
EBITDA impacted by higher variable costs from the Middle East crisis (higher gas prices).

subsections.label: Kenya business
points: Kenya had higher volumes partially offset by lower prices, especially in Southeast Asian markets; fixed costs under control.
Margin compression driven by HFO price increases tied to oil price rise (from USD 70 to USD 100), not so much market price pressure.
Kenya contracts are hedged on HFO up to October; impact beyond that depends on how long the conflict drags on.

subsections.label: Singapore business
points: Singapore's integration plan is going well.

subsections.label: India pricing/contract structure
points: India took a spot price increase of about INR 2,000 per tonne on soda ash; contracts are reviewed quarterly with customers, some contracts have received the increase, others remain on old prices.

India soda ash sales volume declined 12% QoQ and bicarbonate sales volume declined 19% QoQ, reflecting the plant-level optimization toward salt volumes and tendered contract realignment described in Financial Performance.

subsections.label: Competitive dynamics
points: China threat applies globally, not just to India, US, or Southeast Asia; company will work with regulatory authorities to keep domestic industry healthy given India manufacturing presence.

Chinese producers continue to operate at high utilization with elevated export volumes and no significant announced supply curtailments; market rebalancing will depend on supply rationalization, which management is closely watching.
Most Chinese manufacturers are said to be losing money on a cash basis at current pricing levels.

In India, competitive intensity has increased in the short term mainly due to one competitor adding capacity (not primarily a China effect); this capacity is expected to be absorbed by market growth during the year, reducing intensity.

Bicarbonate: premium markets (UK, Singapore) require customer approval and plant clearance before supply starts, insulating them from a big competitive shift; China has bicarb surplus but this mainly impacts technical grade.

subsections.label: Pricing outlook commentary
points: Global pricing expected to remain subdued given elevated inventory levels, while several domestic markets continue to see steady pricing.

Chinese soda ash pricing has moved largely in tandem with Yuan-USD rate; fall in Yuan sale price has been commensurate with dollar depreciation, keeping pricing broadly flat; no major shift expected; USD 170 seen as likely bottom, closer to USD 160-170 range.

Chinese soda ash inventory stands at 1.73 million mt, with export FOB prices in the USD 160-180/tonne range and CIF prices into Southeast Asia in the USD 170-190/tonne range; China has an additional 10 million tons of soda ash capacity adding to the oversupply threat.
Oil price increase from USD 70 to USD 100 is the key driver of higher Kenya HFO pricing.

subsections.label: Portfolio reshaping strategy
points: Strategic direction is to move away from cyclical business, with soda ash identified as the most cyclical; soda ash operational strength will continue as it remains a major profit driver when it recovers.
Within Industrial Essentials, focus will shift toward silica, which is relatively more non-cyclical than soda ash.
Capex will be directed more toward growth in food, feed, and pharma (Living/Farm essentials) and toward de-commoditizing the portfolio, consistent with the company's multi-year strategic direction.
Farm sector is run as a separate subsidiary, reinforcing the segment-focused capability-building rationale.

subsections.label: Asset monetization
points: Debt reduction driven by sale of land and shares held by the company during Q1.
Non-core land monetization planned for second half/after Q2; other non-core monetization avenues to be evaluated as needed, without further commitment on this call.

subsections.label: Geopolitical/Middle East conflict impact
points: Elevated raw material and freight costs across the industry are being caused by geopolitical tensions in the Middle East.
Kenya HFO pricing directly tied to oil price rise (USD 70 to USD 100); Kenya contracts hedged only up to October, with impact beyond that dependent on how long the conflict drags on.

India faces potential impact from limestone sourcing if the conflict continues beyond October/November — domestic production and stocks can only cope with production needs, and fresh consignments from the Middle East (Fujairah) are currently priced very high due to transportation costs.

UK impacted by higher gas prices caused by the Middle East crisis, feeding into higher variable costs; hedging planned going forward but remains an open item as gas prices are expected to revert to mean at some point.
Key watch items highlighted: Kenya HFO, India limestone, and energy cost increases in India and US driven by logistics costs, beyond October.

subsections.label: China oversupply risk
points: Chinese soda ash inventories reached an all-time high of 1.73 million mt with producers continuing to operate at high utilization and elevated export volumes; no significant supply curtailments announced.
China has an additional 10 million tons of soda ash capacity, posing a dumping threat to all global markets, not just India, US or Southeast Asia.
Company will work with regulatory authorities in India to protect domestic industry.

subsections.label: Farm sector risks
points: Monsoon variability, potential El Niño conditions, and higher input costs are being watched in the Indian farm sector, though outlook remains moderately positive as higher commodity prices are expected to push farmers to protect crops using crop protection products.

subsections.label: Logistics cost pass-through risk
points: US cost pressure is mainly on logistics and transportation (outsourced), being addressed customer by customer to pass on costs, remaining an open item.
India freight and forwarding costs increased during the quarter but were largely passed on to customers.

subsections.label: Capex outlook
points: Annualized capex is expected to be around the depreciation number (~INR 1,200 crores based on FY26 consolidated depreciation), with intent to stay at or below that level for the full year including all lined-up capex.

subsections.label: Margin outlook
points: India business margin expected to normalize toward ~18% EBITDA margin (18-20% reversion range) / ~32-33% GC margin as coal inventory benefits reverse and price increases are not yet fully transmitted to all customers.
US export margins to Southeast Asia are at breakeven/unremunerative levels, expected to remain so through the year unless China undertakes capacity rationalization.

subsections.label: UK outlook
points: UK expected to be EBITDA positive and trend toward PBT breakeven for the full year, with a specific expectation of breakeven from next quarter onward as one-off items are not expected to repeat.
EU ETS-related loss is expected to reverse by the October quarter as part of a cyclical pattern.

subsections.label: Sodium-ion battery / recycling outlook
points: Piloting expected to conclude in about 6-9 months, providing clarity on customer responsiveness; by end of year, company expects to move from lab to initial customer offers/units.
Full-scale commercial plant expected about two years after the initial pilot-to-customer phase.
Specific technical metrics (energy density, cycle life) and soda ash requirement ratios for sodium-ion battery to be shared after piloting is complete.

subsections.label: Debt / monetization outlook
points: Company plans to monetize some non-core land in the second half/after Q2, and will evaluate other non-core monetization opportunities as required, without further commitment at this stage.

guidance_ledger.statement: Annualized capex will be around the depreciation number (~INR 1,200 crores consol FY26 depreciation), trying not to exceed it, in fact below that, including all capex lined up.
In terms of sustainable margin it would be around 18%, ~32% to 33% GC margin.

guidance_ledger.horizon: FY27 full year and from next quarter
guidance_ledger.statement: UK should be EBITDA positive as well as tending towards PBT breakeven for the full year, but also from next quarter onwards because these one-offs we don't expect it to repeat.

guidance_ledger.metric: US export margins to Southeast Asia
guidance_ledger.statement: Export volumes to Southeast Asia are just at breakeven level or unremunerative, and that is likely to remain so at least through the year unless capacity rationalization happens in China.

guidance_ledger.metric: Chinese soda ash FOB pricing floor
guidance_ledger.statement: We don't see pricing in China dropping below anywhere around USD 160 to 170 at FOB level; it may be safe to say USD 170 was the bottom.

guidance_ledger.horizon: 6-9 months from Q1FY27 / end of year
guidance_ledger.statement: We expect the piloting to finish in about 6 to 9 months so that we at least get a clear understanding of customer responsiveness; by end of the year, we should have some element of lab to at least initial customer offers and units.
The full-scale plant will come two years after that [end of pilot phase].

We're looking at monetizing some part of non-core land available in the country in the second half or after Q2 onwards; we will also look at what we can do in terms of any other non-core we can look at monetizing.
IMACID did not produce this quarter due to high sulfur prices but they'll be profitable for the year.
Since they have hedged HFO which covers them up to October, we'll have to see what happens beyond October if the war drags on beyond that.

If the conflict continues beyond certain point of time, beyond October, November, we will have an impact coming in in terms of the limestone because domestic production and stock can only cope with production there.

guidance_ledger.metric: Global soda ash pricing (repeat of prior guidance)
guidance_ledger.statement: Global pricing is expected to remain subdued given elevated inventory levels; several domestic markets will continue to have steady pricing.
We do expect during the course of the year that [competitor] capacity will get absorbed and intensity will drop.
The salt plant in India 82.5 KTPA should get operational by this year-end, supplying to market by first quarter of next financial year.

guidance_ledger.metric: 210 KTPA South India salt plant / 50 KTPA silica plant timeline
guidance_ledger.statement: The 210 KTPA Salt plant in South India has a 24-month execution time, similar to the 50 KTPA silica plant; they will become operational sometime during 2028.
Split we'll give next quarter.
On sodium, we'll come back with specifics as soon as the piloting phase is over.
Next year we expect the debt to remain overall at similar levels because the pressure on the business is there for next year also.
The return is expected to be in the upwards of 20%, which is our cut off, for the debottlenecking capex of INR 100 crores coming on stream in 12-14 months.
If this capex were to stay, this will be towards anywhere between 15% at the low end or 20% at the high end.
Valinokkam by the same token again is in the range of 20%.

guidance_ledger.metric: Dense ash plant utilization from solar glass demand
guidance_ledger.statement: We do expect at least 50% utilization as it comes on stream and the balance with the growth.

guidance_ledger.metric: Incremental dense ash demand from solar glass
guidance_ledger.statement: When the solar glass units are running, we would be anywhere between approximately 7,500-10,000 tons of demand every month for the dense ash incrementally during the initial period.
Global demand is expected to be broadly flat in the near term, constrained by weak macroeconomic conditions and soda ash excess capacity.
These actions taken over the next few quarters will improve further the outcomes in terms of margin and profitability.
We will talk about more about them maybe in the Q1 quarterly call / maybe end of Q1.
We are monitoring the situation, and we'll give the better update in terms of post-conflict what are the changes in the next quarter results call.

themes.label: Domestic sourcing shift in India
themes.note: India margin boosted this quarter by coal inventory optimization, though fresh coal imports are coming in at elevated freight-driven pricing, and limestone imports risk becoming costlier from the Middle East if conflict persists.

key_takeaways: Reclassified segments from Basic Chemistry/Specialty Products into Living, Industrial, and Farm Essentials to sharpen focus on non-cyclical, sustainability-led products and align capital allocation.
Consolidated revenue up 14% YoY but EBITDA down ~INR 100 crores YoY on sharply lower realizations; net debt down INR 5,692 crores QoQ on asset monetization.
Standalone India performance was strong: revenue +10%, EBITDA +35%, PAT from continuing operations +12% YoY, driven by higher volumes and stronger realizations.

India EBITDA margin jumped to 28% (10+ pts QoQ) partly from coal inventory optimization and salt/soda ash production mix shifts, but management guided sustainable margin closer to ~18% (32-33% GC margin) as these benefits reverse.
Soda ash industry faces global oversupply from China (record 1.73 million mt inventory, additional 10 million tons capacity) and Middle East-driven cost inflation, keeping global pricing subdued.
India took a spot soda ash price increase of about INR 2,000/tonne; not yet fully transmitted across all contracts.

US export volumes to Southeast Asia remain at breakeven/unremunerative levels likely through the year; Kenya margins compressed by HFO price rise linked to oil at USD 100; UK hit by one-off GBP 2.4 million items but expected to trend to PBT breakeven.

Sodium-ion battery: first full battery pack (including BMS) produced and undergoing testing for stationary/static storage applications (renewables, data centers), not mobility; piloting expected to conclude in 6-9 months, full-scale plant about two years after that.
LFP battery recycling unit being set up in Mithapur with no major capex, built on OEM tie-ups, starting with a small initial volume.
Annualized capex guided to be around depreciation level (~INR 1,200 crores), with further non-core asset monetization planned for H2FY27.

Is the sharp India margin expansion this quarter (28% EBITDA margin, +10pts QoQ) a temporary benefit from low-cost coal inventory, and is it sustainable next quarter or should margins revert to the 18%-20% range?
What assets exactly were monetized to reduce debt, and what was the value?
Any ballpark numbers on soda ash requirement per gigawatt/megawatt for sodium-ion batteries?
Could the sodium-ion battery technology also be scaled for exports, or is it purely domestic-focused?
When can more details be shared on the sodium-ion battery commercialization plan?
Can you share a breakdown of US volumes between domestic sales and exports?
Is the income from associates (IMACID) turning negative due to higher sulfur prices, and what is the outlook for the IMACID business?

quarters.summary: Global soda ash demand is expected to remain broadly flat near-term due to weak macro conditions and industry-wide excess capacity, with the Middle East conflict raising energy, raw material, shipping and transportation costs; management is focused on protecting margins, preserving cash and maintaining balance-sheet strength while continuing to grow non-soda ash revenue and pursuing disciplined, cycle-dependent capex (soda ash capex only when the cycle turns; growth capex directed to non-soda ash businesses like bicarbonate, salt, bromine, silica). FY27 capex is guided at ~INR 1,300 crores with net debt expected to stay at similar levels to FY26 year-end.
