subsections.label: Consolidated performance drivers
points: Revenue down 2% YoY as lower exports from US were offset by higher volumes in India.
EBITDA decline mainly on account of subdued prices across all geographies.
Exceptional charge of INR 1,837 crores for impairment of goodwill in US and INR 159 crores of deferred tax write-off; tax write-off expected to be reviewed once the unit starts making profits.

subsections.label: Standalone performance drivers
points: Revenue up 3% YoY; EBITDA down 6% due to lower realization.
PAT from continuing operations down 51% YoY.

subsections.label: Goodwill impairment / mining rights clarification
points: US GAAP has no concept of mining rights; only goodwill exists in US books, which is what was impaired ($208 million).
Mining rights are an India/Ind AS/IFRS concept and remain intact and are being depreciated over 100 years based on mine life.
Business is valued as a whole; shortfall in valuation first knocks off goodwill before impacting other assets.

subsections.label: Cash flow and working capital
points: Operating cash flow saw a sharp dip, partly led by an increase in working capital.
Management attributes future improvement to exiting unremunerative markets (Southeast Asia) and higher domestic sales proportion improving working capital cycle.

subsections.label: Net debt and capex outlook
points: Net debt without leases at INR 5,961 crores as of March 31, 2026.
FY27 capex guided at ~INR 1,300 crores, mostly maintenance capex in Mithapur and US, plus growth capex in South India (Valinokkam, Silica) and Singapore (Novabay).
Net debt expected to remain at similar levels in FY27 as pressure on the business is expected to continue.

subsections.label: Cost line items (analyst query)
points: Freight and forwarding charges rose from INR 148 crores to INR 166 crores despite volume increase from 2,15,000 to 2,22,000 metric tons (standalone); management to revert with details separately.
Employee benefit costs rose from INR 67 crores to INR 84 crores quarter-on-quarter, attributed to year-end adjustments; full-year employee cost was INR 313 crores vs INR 293 crores in the prior year.

subsections.label: India (Gujarat/Mithapur)
points: Gujarat facility achieved 1 million tons of soda ash production, higher than previous year; price drop was offset by higher volume.
Drop in EBITDA in India attributed to increase in fixed cost compared to previous year.

subsections.label: US operations
points: US export volumes were lower; company stopped selling into unremunerative Southeast Asia market during the quarter, aside from one pre-existing contract shipment.
Sequential EBITDA improvement in US linked to cutting exports to loss-making markets.

subsections.label: UK operations
points: UK had lower revenue due to lower volumes, partly offset by pricing; PBT higher than previous year.
EBITDA decline this quarter driven by preponing a planned April shutdown into March for operational/product capability reasons; expected to result in better operating parameters going forward.
Unhedged gas portion moves daily, making it hard to confirm on a given day whether price increases fully cover costs; on a weighted-average basis they do cover so far.

subsections.label: Kenya operations
points: Increase in volumes in Kenya partially offset lower realization.
50 kilo tons of electric calciner soda ash was operationalized in Kenya during the quarter.
Kenya depends on HFO from the Middle East; currently about 40 days (later referenced as 45 days) of supply cover; market rate for HFO has risen ~50-60% beyond the cover period.

subsections.label: Rallis (agri) business
points: Overall revenue growth of 6%, volume growth of 5%, price growth of 1%, driven by growth in both crop care and seed business.

subsections.label: Non-soda ash portfolio
points: Non-soda ash revenue grew 14% YoY, in line with company's strategic focus to grow non-cyclical, non-soda ash business.
Non-soda ash revenue includes bicarbonate, salt, silica, FOS, bromine, chlorine, cement, and Rallis.

key_figures.label: China Hubli plant capacity (permit expired, maintenance)
China spot export offer price range

subsections.label: Capacity expansion projects
points: Debottlenecking capex of INR 100 crores expected to come on stream in 12-14 months, with IRR above the company's 20% cutoff; driven by ability to produce more from current steam capacity given growing market needs.

Precipitated silica plant undergoing detailed review; if capex proceeds, IRR expected in the 15% (low end) to 20% (high end) range; project benefits from being the only South India silica unit serving the tyre industry with a large freight-cost advantage over Gujarat-based units.

Dense ash project is a repurposing of existing plant (exiting cement business) to produce dense ash for solar glass demand; minimal incremental capex since it reuses existing facilities, expected to be the least-cost dense ash plant built anywhere.

Valinokkam project targeted at ~20% IRR; capital intensity is roughly 2x that of Mithapur, but higher capital cost expected to be offset by savings in logistics/freight costs by serving Southern markets directly.

Cuddalore silica plant expansion (INR 775 crores incremental capex, 50,000 tons) benefits from no incremental fixed cost since it uses the same plant location and largely the same people, generating operating leverage and higher EBITDA per ton; more specifics to be shared in Q1 call.

subsections.label: Global capacity rationalization
points: China Hubli plant (~800,000 tons) had a production permit expiration and started maintenance work.
A US producer with 1.36 million tons capacity has mothballed its plant.
Solvay reduced production by about 180,000 tons at its Spanish plant.
Most capacity shutdowns/maintenance were initiated pre-conflict; the conflict may have accelerated decisions, with visible effects showing towards the end of March.

Older synthetic soda ash plants in China are taking maintenance closures or running at lower utilization; early signs of structural shift but not yet substantial; listed Chinese companies' financials show operating stress.

subsections.label: China inventory and pricing dynamics
points: China inventories remain elevated at ~1.8 million tons and fairly stable; until stock levels fall, no major market impact expected; company will track this metric quarterly.
Chinese prices show increase in dollar terms but remain roughly flat in Renminbi terms.

subsections.label: Regional demand patterns
points: India continues to exhibit relatively robust demand growth with higher capacity utilization across all sectors.
China and US witnessing flat demand; in US mainly due to reduced off-take in the container glass segment.
Southeast Asia prices remain unremunerative, especially for US producers; company has stopped selling into this market.
Imports into India from Iran and Turkey (via Red Sea) have slowed to roughly half of pre-conflict levels; movement from other exporters also reduced in April; trend likely to continue.
Customers increasingly favor domestic sourcing over imports, seeking greater allocation from domestic producers to reduce import dependency going forward, while maintaining some import share.
Rupee depreciation provides natural protection/positive effect for domestic Indian producers and sales.

subsections.label: Regional supply chain resilience
points: US operations largely insulated from Middle East disruption; gas is fully hedged, watching prices closely.
UK operations largely insulated as brine is sourced from own wells; some spike in unhedged portion of gas is a price issue, not availability, and has been passed to customers.
India uses imported coal mainly from Indonesia, which remains undisrupted; pricing movement has been addressed via price changes.

India's biggest supply issue is availability of imported limestone; company has adequate stock and has moved to blended domestic/imported limestone, enabling smooth operations for the next three months.
Kenya unit depends on HFO from the Middle East and is the unit management is watching most closely; currently ~40-45 days of supply; working on alternate sourcing.

Government notification restricting ammonia supply from fertilizer units to non-fertilizer users could affect the company (ammonia used in small quantities, cycled roughly once every 15 days); company has adequate current supply and has written to government about the potential industry-wide impact; non-fertilizer industrial use is ~1% of total ammonia consumption in the country.

subsections.label: Cost pass-through mechanics
points: Output-side logistics costs are mostly a pass-through to customers per contractual arrangements.

Input cost increases have been transparently communicated to and passed on to customers across most units, except UK where daily gas price fluctuation makes it harder to confirm full pass-through in real time.

India carries three to four months of stock and hedging positions that help buffer near-term cost impacts; future shipments are expected to be more expensive, and customers have already been informed with corrective pricing actions taken.

Expected dense ash plant utilization from solar glass demand

subsections.label: Customer sourcing behavior shift
points: Customers who previously imported are requesting increased domestic allocation, driven by realization of import supply risk; they intend to reduce (not eliminate) import dependency while maintaining some import share.
This shift is viewed as a positive market development for domestic producers.

subsections.label: Solar glass demand outlook
points: When solar glass units are running, incremental dense ash demand estimated at approximately 7,500-10,000 tons/month during the initial period; more specific demand trajectory to be shared as units come online.
Dense ash repurposed plant expected to see at least 50% utilization initially from this demand, with balance filled by growth over time.

subsections.label: Sodium bicarbonate demand
points: India sodium bicarbonate output increased from about 140,000 tons to 290,000 tons, fully sold out.
Growth driven by increased coal-fired power generation (flue gas desulfurization use); biggest buyer is NTPC, with close ongoing engagement.

subsections.label: Novabay Pte Limited acquisition (Singapore)
points: Acquisition of Novabay Pte Limited, Singapore, was completed on 19th March 2026.
FY27 capex includes some spend allocated to the Singapore company acquired recently.

subsections.label: Related-party arrangement (Tata Consumer)
points: Iodized salt sales to group company Tata Consumer continue under the same structure and arrangement as approved by the board since the 2019 demerger; no change to the agreement; also reviewed by Tata Consumer management.

subsections.label: Capital allocation philosophy
points: Soda ash business capex will only occur when the cycle returns; management is clear this cycle has not yet turned.
Growth investment focus is on non-soda ash businesses: bicarbonate, salt, bromine and various other chemicals.
Company continues to adopt a disciplined approach to capital allocation to ensure resilience through the current phase of the cycle.

subsections.label: Geopolitical/Middle East conflict impact
points: Middle East conflict has driven up energy and raw material prices, increasing production costs across various parts of the world (especially outside the US), and increased shipping/transportation expenses.
No clear evidence yet of demand erosion, but a prolonged conflict could begin to weigh on demand.
Geopolitical developments in West Asia since late February have disrupted supply chains and raised costs, with varied impact across geographies; overall sales performance remains steady despite this.

subsections.label: Tariff and trade policy uncertainty
points: Geopolitical risk and ongoing US-China tariff uncertainties continue to cloud global demand visibility.

subsections.label: Customer financial stress risk
points: Key monitoring point is whether customers come under financial pressure due to the crisis and resulting cost pass-throughs; not observed in the marketplace so far, but company remains watchful.

subsections.label: Kenya HFO availability risk
points: Kenya's HFO supply, sourced from the Middle East, is the single most closely watched risk; currently ~40-45 days cover, with market rates up 50-60% beyond that cover; alternate sourcing being worked through the system.

subsections.label: Ammonia supply policy risk
points: Government notification advising fertilizer units not to supply ammonia to non-fertilizer users could disrupt small but critical non-fertilizer ammonia use (~1% of total consumption); company has written to government flagging industry-wide impact; currently unaffected but monitoring closely.

subsections.label: Trade defense / regulatory risk
points: Government is investigating both anti-dumping duty (ADD) re-initiation and a safeguard duty (which would include quantity restrictions) rather than duty alone.

subsections.label: Soda ash oversupply / demand risk
points: Global demand expected to be broadly flat near-term, constrained by weak macro conditions and, specifically for soda ash, industry-wide excess capacity.
China and US witnessing flat demand; US flatness mainly due to reduced off-take in container glass segment.

subsections.label: Forward outlook
points: Global soda ash demand expected to remain broadly flat, with pricing expected to stay range-bound, reacting mainly to energy cost increases that producers may pass on.
Solar glass and lithium carbonate are expected to continue driving demand as the world pivots toward renewable/natural energy sources, benefiting soda ash globally.
Company will provide better clarity on post-conflict capacity changes and impacts in the next quarter's (Q1 FY27) results call.

Management expects disciplined execution, supply chain responsiveness, cost and cash discipline, and portfolio shift toward non-soda ash business to improve margin and profitability outcomes over the next few quarters.
Net debt expected to remain at similar levels to FY26 year-end through FY27 given continued business pressure.

guidance_ledger.statement: Around INR 1,300 crores capex for next year, mostly maintenance capex in Mithapur and US, plus growth capex in South India (Valinokkam, Silica) and Singapore.
Next year we expect the debt to remain overall at similar levels because the pressure on the business is there for next year also.
The return is expected to be in the upwards of 20%, which is our cut off, for the debottlenecking capex of INR 100 crores coming on stream in 12-14 months.
If this capex were to stay, this will be towards anywhere between 15% at the low end or 20% at the high end.
Valinokkam by the same token again is in the range of 20%.

guidance_ledger.statement: We do expect at least 50% utilization as it comes on stream and the balance with the growth.

guidance_ledger.metric: Incremental dense ash demand from solar glass
guidance_ledger.statement: When the solar glass units are running, we would be anywhere between approximately 7,500-10,000 tons of demand every month for the dense ash incrementally during the initial period.
Overall, pricing is expected to remain range-bound and react mainly to the energy cost increases, which some of the producers may pass on.
Global demand is expected to be broadly flat in the near term, constrained by weak macroeconomic conditions and soda ash excess capacity.
These actions taken over the next few quarters will improve further the outcomes in terms of margin and profitability.
We will talk about more about them maybe in the Q1 quarterly call / maybe end of Q1.
We are monitoring the situation, and we'll give the better update in terms of post-conflict what are the changes in the next quarter results call.

themes.label: Soda ash cycle downturn / oversupply
themes.note: Global demand flat with industry-wide excess capacity weighing on prices and margins across geographies.

themes.label: Geopolitical/Middle East disruption
themes.note: Conflict has raised energy, raw material and shipping costs and disrupted supply chains, but is also slowing competitor imports into India, boosting domestic sourcing.

themes.label: Non-soda ash diversification
themes.note: Non-soda ash revenue grew 14% YoY to INR 6,946 crores, in line with strategy to reduce cyclicality.

themes.label: Cost pass-through discipline
themes.note: Company has largely passed on input cost and shipping cost increases to customers across most geographies, protecting margins.

themes.label: Capital allocation discipline / cycle-linked capex
themes.note: Soda ash capex deferred until cycle turns; growth capex directed to non-soda ash projects (silica, Valinokkam, dense ash, Singapore) with 15-20%+ IRR targets.

themes.label: Kenya HFO availability risk
themes.note: Kenya's HFO supply from the Middle East remains the most closely watched operational risk with limited days of cover and sharply higher market rates.

themes.label: Domestic sourcing shift in India
themes.note: Indian customers are increasingly requesting higher domestic allocation to reduce import dependency amid geopolitical disruption, aided by rupee depreciation.

key_takeaways: Global demand is expected to be broadly flat in the near term, constrained by weak macroeconomic conditions and more specifically amongst all our products, the soda ash excess capacity.
The recent Middle East conflict has driven up the energy and raw material prices, increasing production costs across various parts of the world, especially other than US.
India continues to exhibit relatively robust demand growth with higher capacity utilization across all sectors.

Revenue was down by 2% at INR 3,438 crores compared to previous year; EBITDA was at INR 274 crores compared to INR 327 crores Q4 of last year, mainly on account of subdued prices across all geographies.
An exceptional charge of INR 1,837 crores is provided on account of impairment of goodwill in US and INR 159 crores of deferred tax write-off.

During the quarter, we acquired Novabay Pte Limited, Singapore; this acquisition was completed on 19th March 2026. In addition to this, 50 kilo tons of electric calciner soda ash was operationalized in Kenya.
Non-soda ash revenue grew 14% from INR 6,118 crores in FY25 to INR 6,946 crores in FY26, in line with company's focus to grow non-cyclical and non-soda ash business.

Management is focused on reinforcing supply chain planning, maintaining cost discipline, improving operational agility to address near-term disruptions; priorities remain firmly aligned to protecting margin, preserving cash flows, and maintaining balance sheet strength.
pressing_questions: Okay, but I mean 20% ROCE would mean something like say INR 150 crores odd of earnings EBIT from that project. Would that be a fair assessment? (on Cuddalore silica plant returns — management deferred detailed revenue/EBITDA disclosure to the Q1 FY27 call)

How much capacity has been shut post-conflict versus pre-existing shutdowns? (management stated most closures were pre-conflict and promised a better post-conflict update in the next quarter's results call)

INDIQUBE.about: Incorporated in 2015, IndiQube Spaces Ltd provides workplace solutions to its clients.[1]

quarters.summary: Q1 FY27 marked the highest ever quarterly revenue for Indiqube at INR428 crores (up 37% YoY) with improving profitability metrics across EBITDA, EBIT and PAT. Management reiterated the annual guidance of ~2 million sq ft area addition per year, occupancy ranges (80-85% corporate, 85-90%/86-90% mature centers), EBITDA margin range of 19-21%, EBIT margin 11-13%, PAT margin 8-10%, and continued solar capacity expansion (additional 25-30 MW planned this year at INR100-120 crores capex). VAS contribution is expected to keep rising by 2-4 percentage points from the current ~17% over the coming years, with margin on VAS revenue around 15% as the company prioritizes growth/scale over margin expansion in DesignQube, IndiCare and Eco for the next 1-2 years.

subsections.label: Profitability quality
points: Profitability strengthened as the company scaled, with EBIT margin improving to 13% in Q1 FY27 from 11% in Q1 FY26, and PAT margin expanding to 8% from 6% during the same period last year.
EBITDA margin remained healthy at 20%, demonstrating operating leverage inherent in the platform and ability to translate growth in scale with stronger profitability.

subsections.label: Debt & interest expense
points: Interest expense on outstanding debt increased because debt was taken specifically for the solar plant expansion, not for the normal leasing business.

subsections.label: Capex and cash flow disclosure
points: Capex deployment is defined as a combination of interiors capex, Design and Build project capex, solar investment, and vendor payment cycles — all recurring in nature, so capex cannot be viewed as directly proportional to area addition every period.

Management declined to give provisional capex/cash flow numbers for the quarter since these are subject to H1 audit and review; full detail will be provided with H1 numbers to avoid giving an estimate that later changes.

subsections.label: Margin stability across occupancy fluctuations
points: Even with 1% fluctuation in occupancy up or down, margins are expected to remain in the same guided range across coming quarters and years.
Sensitivity of overall EBITDA margin to occupancy dropping slightly (e.g., 90% to 88-89%) is stated to be low.

key_figures.label: GCC contribution to revenue (alt figure cited)
Estimated Indian IT services companies within enterprises share

subsections.label: Value Added Services (VAS) evolution
points: Offerings include Grow (core managed workspace proposition), DesignQube (rebranded from Bespoke, enabling participation in design and creation of workspaces), IndiCare (rebranded from IndiQube One, addressing operations, employee experience, facility requirements, and being extended into retail for end-to-end store/branch management), and Eco (helping customers build sustainable, energy efficient commercial spaces).
VAS is tracked on a consolidated basis; the INR39 crores one-time VAS revenue this quarter arose from all three 'other services' — DesignQube, IndiCare and Eco.
Although categorized as one-time, this kind of growth is expected to keep recurring, so it should structurally be considered ongoing even though quarterly percentages may fluctuate.

Priority for the next couple of years is on scale and growth for DesignQube/IndiCare/Eco rather than margin expansion, given significant demand opportunity; VAS margin will remain around 15% for the next one to two years, with the company unwilling to compromise growth for margin at this stage.
VAS contribution to revenue rose to 17% in Q1 FY27 from an intermediate level of 15% and a prior level of 12%, with expected further increase of 2-4 percentage points in coming years.

subsections.label: Customer base composition
points: Client base spans Global Capability Centers, Indian conglomerates, unicorns and high-growth startups, with GCC contributing 53% of revenue, startups/unicorns 23%, and Indian enterprises 28% (of which an estimated 10-12% are Indian IT services companies).

Client base described as very diverse; most properties (barring a single-digit exception) are multi-tenanted, so one tenant leaving does not typically vacate a building since other clients are willing to take up space.
Attrition has been negative — net seat expansion among staying clients exceeds seats vacated by leaving clients.

GCC growth has been broad and reflects a broader India real estate growth story, not just company-specific; GCC share of area mix is expected to rise moderately over time but not drastically, from ~49-50% currently toward a potential future 54-55%, up from 42% in 2020-21.

855 total clients as of June 2026, with top 5 customers contributing only 12% of revenue and multi-center clients contributing 41% of revenue; ~90% of occupants come from clients with more than 100 seats.
Client renewal rate stands at 90%; notice periods are 60 days for smaller clients and 90 days for larger clients.

subsections.label: Institutional vs non-institutional supply mix
points: About 20% of supply is institutional (listed REITs or large funds), up from ~12% a couple of years back; remainder is from ultra-HNI landlords, including the large Noida center owned by an ultra-large HNI family group despite its size.

Institutional-grade supply commands higher pricing and higher common area maintenance costs, but also attracts a higher proportion of GCC tenants who pay a higher price, resulting in fairly consistent margins across institutional and HNI-driven supply.

key_figures.label: Annual seats addition equivalent to 2 million sq ft
Time to reach ~90% occupancy for new centers

subsections.label: RPA vs AUM timing dynamics
points: Rent-paying area expansion is tracked on an annual rather than quarterly basis because timing of new center additions varies significantly quarter to quarter; hence flat sequential RPA movement this quarter does not indicate slowdown.
Company has ~3.9 million sq ft (~97,000 seats) already signed and in the pipeline, providing full coverage toward the ~2 million sq ft annual addition target.

Most delivery of buildings/RPA addition is timed for the Jan-Feb period to allow sufficient marketing time before the slower leasing season (festive/Christmas/New Year holidays), which is why RPA has remained flat even as AUM increased.
Signed supply typically gets delivered between 12 to 18 months from signing.

Area under management grew by 1.91 million sq ft with 17 new centers launched during the year, bringing current AUM to 10.61 million sq ft, rent-paying area to 7.8 million sq ft, and rent-yielding area to 6.74 million sq ft; H2 FY26 rent-paying area addition was 1.14 million sq ft.

subsections.label: New center ramp-up economics
points: New centers typically take five to six months to reach operating break-even (approximately 52-57% occupancy), then continue ramping to around 90% occupancy within 9-12 months.
Full capex recovery takes about 36 months, distinct from the much shorter operational break-even period; growth is therefore not expected to pressure margins.
Overall occupancy stood at 86% in Q1 FY27, within the corporate-level occupancy guidance range of 80-85% and mature center range of 85-90%, compared to an 81-85% range over the last 3 years.

subsections.label: Micro-market focus
points: Supply is concentrated in key, well-performing micro-markets (e.g., Bangalore's Outer Ring Road corridor between Silk Board and Marathahalli, and Whitefield) where occupancy levels are typically 85% and above.

Company has deliberately limited exposure to oversupplied micro-markets like North Bangalore, where vacancy levels are high despite large new additions, keeping exposure below 0.5 million sq ft even with over 6.5 million sq ft total in Bangalore across 76 centers.
Tech park presence has grown to almost 20% of the portfolio as the company has picked up more tech park supply.

subsections.label: Large-format center strategy (Noida)
points: New large Noida center — among the largest in NCR and across the entire portfolio — will go live by mid next year (targeted Q2 FY28 or Q3).
Company already has two centers in Noida and a few in Gurgaon, giving confidence from prior market reconnaissance to pick up a larger, high-quality, tech-park-grade product.

Decision driven by positive market tides in Noida — better administration, law and order, and the upcoming Jewar airport — rather than being demand/customer backed; most large supply pickups are proactive (land, expand, build scale) rather than back-to-back with a specific customer requirement.

Strategy remains micro-market centric: dense micro-markets (e.g., Nariman Point in Mumbai) will see smaller or renovated buildings, while tech-park-centric large-occupier locations (e.g., Navi Mumbai, Noida Expressway) favor larger-format products.

subsections.label: Geographic diversification and expansion plans
points: Bangalore share of portfolio (currently 60-64%, with Chennai at 10%) is expected to gradually decrease as NCR, West (Mumbai) and Hyderabad markets grow faster, in addition to continued strength in Chennai and Bangalore.
Company plans to add larger supply in Hyderabad and Mumbai in the current financial year, continuing the post-COVID aggressive expansion strategy in both cities.

Bangalore's dominance is expected to continue given it is India's largest and fastest-growing real estate market, with GCC/unicorn/startup growth rates there exceeding the national average; Bangalore accounted for 12.7 million sq ft (~28%) of India's 45 million sq ft total commercial real estate absorption in H1 CY26, against a cumulative national stock of 1.1 billion sq ft and a historical secular growth rate of 6-7%.
Hyderabad is highlighted as a city with very robust GCC activity alongside Bangalore.

subsections.label: Tier-2 city performance
points: Occupancy, profitability and unit economics in Tier-2 cities are similar to Tier-1 cities, with no significant deterioration seen, despite much smaller scale.
Cheaper real estate acquisition cost in Tier-2 cities (INR50-70 per sq ft) is passed through via more aggressive/lower seat pricing (INR6,500-7,500 per seat), resulting in no margin hit.

key_figures.label: Bangalore absorption share of India total

subsections.label: Sustainability strategy
points: Nearly 30 MW of solar capacity is operational, comprising solar farms in Karnataka and Maharashtra plus rooftop installations across the country, as a step toward the long-term ambition of transitioning the Indiqube portfolio to 100% green power.

Company will continue to double down on solar as clients increasingly expect a full-blown sustainability solution amid green transition trends; will add capacity for itself and a small part for clients as required.
Solar-related debt has increased specifically to fund solar plant expansion, distinct from debt for the normal leasing business.
Planning to add 25-30 MW of solar capacity this year (FY27), requiring solar capex of INR100-120 crores, with the solar investment delivering an IRR of 18-22%.

subsections.label: Company evolution / platform strategy
points: The last decade was about building and evolving Indiqube — expanding from Bangalore to multiple cities, progressing from managed workspaces to an integrated managed spaces platform, broadening services, and transitioning from a private limited company to a listed institution.

The next phase is about compounding what has been built, combining geographical expansion, deeper customer relationships, growing VAS contribution, strong operating leverage, and sustainability initiatives.

Ambition is to become the 'total outsourcing solution' for commercial spaces via the integrated Indiqube platform, combining managed workspace footprint expansion with an increasing range of per-customer services.

subsections.label: Area addition guidance reiterated
points: Management reiterated the ~2 million sq ft annual area addition guidance despite flat quarter-on-quarter rent-paying area, attributing this to timing of building delivery rather than demand slowdown or increased competition.
3.9 million sq ft (97,000 seats) already signed provides full coverage for the annual target.
Corporate-level occupancy is guided at 80-85% and mature center occupancy at 85-90% (also cited 86-90/88-91%), with EBITDA margin guided at 19-21%, EBIT margin at 11-13%, and PAT margin at 8-10%.
VAS contribution is guided to increase by 2-4 percentage points from the current 17% level over coming years.
Solar capacity addition of 25-30 MW is guided for FY27, requiring INR100-120 crores of solar capex.

subsections.label: Quarterly disclosure enhancement
points: In response to an analyst request for quarter-wise breakup of rent-paying area additions, management stated they currently only provide yearly figures but will take note of the request for future disclosure.

guidance_ledger.statement: We definitely intend to continue operating within the same range... close to 2 million square feet annually which translates to approximately 44,000 seats per year.
We would maintain that 80% to 85% occupancy at the corporate level.
85% to 90% on the mature centers.
EBITDA margin would range from 19% to 21%.
My EBIT margins would be in the range of 11% to 13%.
My PAT margin would be in the range of 8% to 10%.
We expect the contribution of VAS revenue in fact to increase further from 17% by 2% to 4% approximately... structurally the contribution of the VAS you would see is increasing.
Our margin in my VAS revenue would be around about 15% and this is going to be like this for the next one or two years at least... at the expense of the scale, we would not compromise on our growth.
This year we intend to add another 25 to 30 megawatts worth of capacity.
Translating into a requirement of about INR100 crores to INR120 crores capital expenditure.
Our solar IRR has been very healthy, typically it has been between 18% going up to 22% kind of an IRR wherever we have invested in solar.
We are very hopeful that in this financial year we should be able to sign up larger spaces in both the cities [Hyderabad and Mumbai].
This will go live by middle of next year... Q2 FY28 or maybe Q3, that's the timeline in which the building should go operational.

Steady state centers... occupancy ranges between say 86% going up to 90%-91%... overall occupancy is about 81% going up to 84%-85% and currently it stands at 86%. Better to pick up a range which is 86% going up to 90% for a steady state center and 82% going up to 85%-86% for the overall occupancy.
We see that certainly the GCCs from 49% today may grow to 54%-55%, typically but we don't see that changing very, very drastically.
We will take a note of it [request for quarterly breakup of RPA addition], in future, but as of now we would have just this [yearly] number.

guidance_ledger.metric: Capex and cash flow disclosure for H1
guidance_ledger.statement: Our H1 numbers we will completely detail out both capex and cash flow... since it was not audited as of now, I would refrain from talking about the numbers.
We plan to add approximately 1.5 million square feet to 2 million square feet every year, which means 33,000 seats to 44,000 seats every year.
Top-line growth of approximately 25% to 30%.
Per square feet of the CAPEX is about 1650 [INR]; depending on area addition, multiply by 1650.
It is in line with the revenue growth... the cost would be in line with the growth itself.
Maybe 5% to 10% per inflation, you can see in this INR 192 over a year, on an overall basis may happen.
Next year, we plan to give you some kind of bifurcation of the solar so that it is much clearer on how much CAPEX or what kind of investment we are doing on the solar and sustainability initiative.

That kind of guidance we could look at... whatever we are expecting to be a rent-paying area in the next quarter, like that, those could be basically disclosed in advance... we will consider and try to implement.

risk_register.risk: Seasonality in leasing uptake
risk_register.note: Leasing uptake is typically higher from Feb-March through October; slows during festive/Christmas/New Year holiday periods, affecting the timing of rent-paying area additions relative to AUM growth.

risk_register.risk: Oversupply/vacancy in weaker micro-markets (e.g., North Bangalore)
risk_register.note: Company has deliberately limited exposure (<0.5 million sq ft) to micro-markets like North Bangalore where vacancy levels are high due to oversupply.

risk_register.risk: Geographic concentration in Bangalore
risk_register.note: About 60-64% of seats are in Bangalore; company expects this share to gradually reduce as NCR, West and Hyderabad grow faster, though Bangalore will remain dominant given it is the largest, fastest-growing market.

risk_register.risk: Client attrition / lease renewal risk
risk_register.note: Attrition has been negative (net positive), renewal rate at 90%, top 5 customers only 12% of revenue, and most properties are multi-tenanted so a single tenant leaving does not significantly impact the building.

risk_register.risk: Capex/cash flow disclosure uncertainty (unaudited)
risk_register.note: Management declined to give provisional capex and cash flow figures since H1 numbers are subject to audit and review, to avoid giving estimates that could later change.

risk_register.risk: New center ramp-up / capex recovery period
risk_register.note: Full capex recovery for new centers takes about 36 months, though operating break-even is achieved much sooner (5-6 months); management indicated no expected margin pressure from growth given this ramp profile.

risk_register.risk: Geopolitical volatility / war-related material cost inflation
risk_register.note: 5-7% bump-up in materials cost pushing CAPEX per sq ft from INR 15.50 to INR 16.50; company currently absorbing the increase rather than passing to clients.

risk_register.risk: AI impact on businesses and workspaces
risk_register.note: Broader uncertainty flagged but no negative impact observed so far; low-end jobs seen as more at risk than high-end/quality roles.

risk_register.risk: Single-tenant/single-building concentration
risk_register.note: Only ~10% of portfolio is single-tenant/single-location; mitigated via preference for multi-tenancy buildings to avoid zero occupancy risk.

risk_register.risk: Tier-2 city supply/landlord maturity gaps
risk_register.note: Quality real estate supply may be lacking in some Tier-2 cities and landlords may lack maturity to handle GCC-quality clients, creating chicken-and-egg problem.

risk_register.risk: Overexpansion / growth-at-any-cost risk
risk_register.note: Management deliberately avoids overshooting given geopolitical situation and AI uncertainty to avoid a position it may later regret.

risk_register.risk: Rising energy costs
risk_register.note: Green power/solar investment intended to structurally reduce operating costs and insulate from rising energy costs.

risk_register.risk: Micro-market oversupply/vacancy risk
risk_register.note: Avoiding locations like Manesar, North Bangalore, Navi Mumbai where vacancy levels are 15-25%, to prevent value erosion analogous to hotel industry oversupply dynamics.

themes.label: Margin expansion
themes.note: EBIT margin improved to 13% from 11% and PAT margin to 8% from 6% YoY, reflecting operating leverage as the company scales.

themes.label: Occupancy trend & seasonality
themes.note: Overall occupancy at 86%, within the guided 80-85%/86-90% ranges; RPA additions are timed for Jan-Feb to avoid slower festive-season leasing periods.

themes.label: VAS scale-up
themes.note: VAS contribution rose from 12% to 15% to ~17% of revenue, with a one-time INR39 crore recognition this quarter and expected further increase of 2-4 percentage points; margin held at ~15% as growth is prioritized over margin expansion.

themes.label: GCC-led demand / Flex adoption
themes.note: GCCs contributed 53% of revenue this quarter, up from ~42% in 2020-21 and expected to reach 54-55% over time, driven by broader India commercial real estate growth.

themes.label: Green power / solar expansion
themes.note: 30 MW of solar capacity operational with plans to add 25-30 MW more in FY27 at INR100-120 crores capex, generating 18-22% IRR, supporting the ambition of 100% green power.

themes.label: Disciplined/sustainable growth strategy
themes.note: Company reiterated ~2 million sq ft annual area addition guidance backed by 3.9 million sq ft of signed headroom, with a micro-market focused 'Follow the Talent' strategy and geographic diversification into Noida, Hyderabad and Mumbai.

themes.label: Geographic diversification
themes.note: Bangalore remains ~60-64% of the portfolio but its share is expected to gradually decline as NCR, Hyderabad and Mumbai see faster growth alongside continued Bangalore dominance.

key_takeaways: Q1 27 marks a very strong start for the year with Indiqube delivering its highest ever quarterly revenue of INR428 crores representing growth of 37% year-on-year.
Our EBITDA increased by 34% to INR87 crores, EBIT grew from 59% to INR55 crores, while PAT increased by 91% to INR35 crores.
EBIT margin improved to 13% in Q1 FY27 from 11% in Q1 FY26, while PAT margin expanded to 8% from 6% during the same period last year. EBITDA margin remained healthy at 20%.
During the year, we added 1.91 million square feet to our area under management, and we launched 17 new centers.

As of June 2026, we catered to 855 clients... GCCs contributed 53% of our revenue during the quarter and multi-center clients (clients who have taken more than one center) accounted for about 41% of our revenue. Nearly 90% of our occupants come from clients who have taken more than 100 seats.
Nearly 30 megawatt of solar capacity is already operational, comprising capacity from our solar farms in Karnataka and Maharashtra, as well as rooftop installations across the country.
Our VAS contribution has grown from 12% to approximately 15% and is currently around 17% of our total revenue. We expect this contribution to increase further over time.
We have consistently said that we intend to add close to 2 million square feet every year and we remain committed to that growth trajectory.
pressing_questions: So, you've reiterated your guidance of 2 million square feet of area addition annually, but if we look at quarter one of FY27, there is no change in your operational area addition. So how do you think the remaining supply additions will be distributed across Q2 to Q4 to meet this guidance? Are you seeing some sort of a slowdown in supply or increased competition?

My first question is on the recent new center addition that we have done in Noida... just wanted to get a sense in terms of timeline of operational for this center and what's giving you confidence to add such large centers... how much of this is demand backed?

I just wanted to get some sense of the cash flows for the quarter, so what's the kind of OCF that we have generated for the quarter and what has been the capex? And if you could also provide some sort of capex guidance for the balance of the year?

So, our overall revenue to rent ratio is 2.2. Could you please give us a bit more detail on it, on a city basis. Are there cities that are materially higher and cities that are materially lower and what would the range be?

quarters.summary: FY26 was a record year for IndiQube with revenue growth of 37%, EBITDA growth of 60% and PAT growth of 145%, alongside occupancy improvement, VAS mix expansion, and solar/green power scale-up. Management guided FY27 rent-paying area addition of 1.5-2 million sq ft (33,000-44,000 seats), revenue growth of 25-30%, EBITDA margin of 18-21%, PAT margin of 8-10%, CAPEX per sq ft of ~INR 1650, and 30-35 MW of incremental solar capacity across Karnataka, Tamil Nadu and Maharashtra with INR 125-150 crores of capex.

subsections.label: Margin & Profitability Drivers
points: Growth accompanied by consistent margin improvement: EBITDA margin expanded from 18% in FY25 to 21% in FY26, PAT margin improved from 5% to 9% over the same period.
Cash flow from operations strengthened significantly, increasing 147% YoY to INR 304 crores.
Performance demonstrates resilience of business model amid geopolitical volatility and AI-related uncertainty around workspaces.

subsections.label: CAPEX Bifurcation & Variance vs Guidance
points: Previous guidance was CAPEX for the whole year similar to range of 1H (~INR 180 crores), implying ~INR 360 crores guided; actual came in at INR 413-414 crores.
Delta versus guidance driven by solar investment of INR 73 crores which was not fully anticipated, generating savings of INR 22-23 crores per year.
CAPEX deployment total is sum of interior CAPEX, design-and-build, solar investments and vendor payment cycles.

CAPEX per sq ft increased from INR 15.50 to INR 16.50 due to ~5-7% bump-up in cost of materials from geopolitical/war-related factors; company is currently absorbing this increase rather than passing to clients; premiumization of interiors also factored into this cost.

subsections.label: Solar Depreciation & Tax Benefit
points: Depreciation on solar assets will reflect mainly in FY27 since large part of deployment happened from October onward, going live through Feb-March.
Company eligible for accelerated depreciation (40%) on solar, expected to help improve PAT.

subsections.label: IPO Proceeds Reallocation
points: Reallocation of CAPEX use-of-proceeds since DRHP filing to address needs that have become important: design-and-build capital assets, interior CAPEX, solar CAPEX, refundable security deposits to landlords for new supply (LOIs), and investment headroom for real estate/adjacent ventures IndiQube may pursue.
General corporate purpose allocation and debt repayment plan kept unchanged.

subsections.label: Lease Liability Outlook
points: Lease payment/cost growth expected to be in line with revenue growth (guided at 25-30%), with EBITDA maintained in 18-21% range.

subsections.label: Growth Pace vs Cash Reserves
points: Despite having more cash than some peers, management is not pursuing more aggressive growth because the business is not viewed as winner-takes-all; sustainable, quality-focused growth is prioritized over growth at any cost.
Company maintains AUM (area under management) more than 50% ahead of occupied/rent-yielding area at any point as growth headroom (9.6 million sq ft AUM vs 6.3 million rent-yielding).
Landlord relationship credibility (e.g., 70% of Bangalore landlords from one community) and zero litigation/default history with landlords cited as reasons for cautious growth approach.

subsections.label: Demand Drivers & AI Impact
points: No impact of AI on demand seen so far; management believes low-end jobs may be impacted but quality/high-end jobs (product management, domain knowledge) are being added in substantial numbers.
Depreciating rupee seen as positive for export-led GCC industry, making India more attractive as $1 buys more locally, expected to drive more work to India.
Premiumization trend: companies looking for plug-and-play managed offices with more flexibility as they seek distributed offices closer to talent.
US has 6,000 banks but fewer than 60 have set up India GCCs so far — indicates long tail of future GCC growth over next 4-5 years.
GCC diversity increasing beyond North American/BFSI-retail mix to include European, East Asian, global players in logistics, healthcare, manufacturing, shipping, mining sectors.
GCCs tend to hire in 3-digit numbers per center (not 4-digit), but volume of GCCs entering India is very high, so absorption over next couple of years is expected to be GCC-led with high-quality mix.

subsections.label: Hub-and-Spoke Leasing Trend (MNC direct leasing)
points: Large MNCs (e.g., Uber, NVIDIA) directly lease hub locations (2 lakh sq ft to 1 million sq ft) for long-term, high-control, strategic infrastructure investment (IT infra, labs, data centers).
Spoke locations (secondary R&D centers) are typically where Flex/IndiQube-type operators are engaged.

Within hub locations, some MNCs still engage IndiQube-type players for design-and-build plug-and-play services (5-year deals cited with an automotive major in Hyderabad and a mining major in Chennai).

For a large company with a 5 million sq ft India portfolio, only 20-25% expected to move to Flex — Flex share for large occupiers seen rising from <100,000 sq ft five years ago to 1-1.5 million sq ft now, becoming an increasing percentage of overall portfolios rather than binary decision.

subsections.label: Micro-market Strategy & Pricing Power
points: Focus on micro markets with >90% occupancy (e.g., Guindy in Chennai, OMR/Mahabalipuram Road, Outer Ring Road, Golf Course Road) where demand-supply equilibrium supports sustained rental inflation of 4-5%.
Avoiding markets with high vacancy (15-25%) such as Manesar, North Bangalore, Navi Mumbai.
Renovation focus: ~25% of portfolio is renovated buildings; ongoing pickup of renovation opportunities (e.g., transformation in Nariman Point area).
Preference for picking up full/bigger buildings where availability and appetite allow.

Commercial economics: wholesale-retail rental theory applies when Flex operator picks up large blocks vs smaller floors; differential more pronounced (20-25%) in non-institutional/independent buildings vs modest (5-10%) in institutional supply with long tenures.

Realization uplift driven by (1) 5-6% contractual rental inflation, (2) shift toward premium/institutional supply which commands higher pricing (e.g., properties earlier picked at INR 70-80 now being done at INR 21-30 differential noted as premium range), and (3) pricing elasticity from churn allowing re-leasing at higher rates in demand-supply mismatch micro markets.

subsections.label: Space Sourcing Strategy
points: ~90% of space uptake is speculative/proactive based on internal research and anticipated growth of existing customer base in a micro market, rather than reactive to a specific client RFP.
Back-to-back (client-driven RFP) business is limited.
Single-tenant, single-building/location exposure is only ~10% of portfolio; company prefers multi-tenancy buildings to mitigate risk of full vacancy if one client exits.

subsections.label: Tenant Mix
points: IT/ITES tenants ~49% of rents (down from ~51% in FY25); Indian Enterprises ~58% of rents (down from ~60% last quarter).

Management does not expect abrupt shift in tenant vertical mix — expects gradual movement as GCC diversity increases (manufacturing, logistics, healthcare); IT/ITES will continue to be the largest vertical.

subsections.label: Occupancy Clarification
points: End-of-month occupancy for March 2026 was 81%, but the more relevant metric — average occupancy during the year — was 84%; actual annual dip is only ~1%, not the apparent ~4% quarter-on-quarter dip.
EBITDA margin expansion from 18% to 21% would not have been possible if there had been a meaningful 4% occupancy decline, supporting the view that underlying occupancy trend is stable.

Quarterly fluctuations in occupancy/area addition are natural due to timing of new area addition and ramp-up phase of newly operational buildings; annual view (area addition, revenue, EBITDA) is the correct lens, not quarterly.
AUM (9.66 million sq ft) is at various stages and expected to convert to operational/rent-paying stage over the next 18-24 months.

subsections.label: Value-Added Services (VAS)
points: VAS services bifurcated into recurring (amortized over 3-5 years, e.g., subscription-like offerings) and one-time (e.g., IT products, custom workstations/chairs paid upfront) — one-time VASP contribution is difficult to predict quarter to quarter.
Total VAS contribution expected to rise from 15% to 17-18% of revenue next year.

Growing multiplier trend: clients with offices within IndiQube and additional offices elsewhere in India are increasingly asking IndiQube to manage those external offices too, expanding VAS scope beyond IndiQube buildings.

VAS margins (10-15%) are less accretive than core space business EBITDA (18-20%), but VAS provides significant client stickiness ('glue') via B2B and B2C service offerings and drives scale even if not margin-accretive to the same degree.

subsections.label: MiQube Technology Platform
points: MiQube recorded 1.4 million transactions in FY26, reflecting growing adoption across client base.
New space management module and vehicle pooling feature within transport module have seen strong traction.

subsections.label: Green Power Strategy
points: Goal of transforming portfolio to 100% green power via open access and rooftop solar.
Continued focus on green power expected to structurally reduce operating costs and insulate from rising energy costs, especially relevant amid current elevated energy cost environment.
New area being added is being made green from day one as a requirement.

Demand driver: GCCs setting up micro/mini data centers within IndiQube facilities are heavy power consumers ('power guzzlers') — two such clients cited; IndiQube's 100% green power capability in many buildings gives a double advantage of high-quality infrastructure plus green power supply.
Predominant focus states for solar addition: Karnataka (largest), followed by Maharashtra and Tamil Nadu.
Company plans to provide clearer bifurcation of solar CAPEX/investment disclosure next year for greater transparency on sustainability initiative spend.

subsections.label: Key Micro Markets
points: Key micro markets of focus include Delhi/Outer Ring Road (Ecoworld — premier tech park in Bangalore), Chennai (Guindy, OMR/Mahabalipuram Road), Golf Course Road, and other high-occupancy locations.
Signed up significant space in Ecoworld, described as the most premier tech park in Bangalore.
Institutional supply availability varies by city — e.g., Hyderabad's HITEC City lacks grade B space, so uptake there is largely institutional.

subsections.label: Tier-2 City Expansion
points: India has 50 cities with population over 1 million; jobs increasingly moving to where people are, a 'democratization of jobs' driving distributed office demand.
Coimbatore highlighted as a standout Tier-2 city — only South Indian non-capital city with population over 3 million, compared to how Pune was 20-25 years ago; seeing very good traction.
Company describes itself as the largest player in the down South 3 states.
Nature of jobs in Tier-2 differs: significant healthcare back-office work, mostly graduate hires (not engineering), with ~70% women employees.

Tier-2 story described as promising but a 10-year story; scale is not yet there, and there are 'chicken and egg' problems — quality supply may be lacking and landlords may lack maturity to handle GCC-quality clients.
Tier-2 city pickup strategy is a mix of proactive (based on market research, e.g., Coimbatore) and reactive (based on existing client request for a location) approaches.
Company does not plan to aggressively add many new cities — maybe a couple more per year — with focus remaining on deepening presence and micro-market selection within existing 17 cities.

subsections.label: CRISIL Rating & Financial Discipline
points: CRISIL A+ Stable rating supports confidence in ability to grow with scale, discipline and profitability.

subsections.label: Investment Headroom
points: INR 64 crores of IPO proceeds allocated toward investment into any real estate or adjacent ventures that IndiQube may find interesting going forward.

subsections.label: Growth Philosophy
points: Business viewed as not winner-takes-all, more comparable to IT services industry structure with multiple large players ('Big 5') each pursuing different growth strategies.
Preference for sustainable growth over growth at any cost, drawing an analogy to hotel industry value erosion risk in oversupplied micro markets (e.g., Navi Mumbai).
Maintains AUM headroom of >50% versus occupied/rent-yielding area at any point in time to support future leasing without overextending.

subsections.label: Geopolitical & Cost Pressures
points: War/geopolitical volatility cited as a factor causing ~5-7% bump-up in cost of materials used, pushing CAPEX per sq ft from INR 15.50 towards INR 16.50; company currently absorbing this rather than passing to clients.

No major supply disruptions (e.g., unlike LPG supply disruption) have been faced, though tiles were in short supply at one point; large part of procurement is from vendors manufacturing in India, limiting dollar/forex impact on CAPEX.

subsections.label: AI Disruption Uncertainty
points: Broader uncertainty around impact of AI on businesses and workspaces flagged as a backdrop risk for FY26, though no negative impact observed so far; low-end job categories seen as more at risk than high-end/quality roles.

subsections.label: Tier-2 Expansion Risks
points: Chicken-and-egg problem in Tier-2 cities: lack of quality real estate supply and landlords lacking maturity to handle GCC-quality clients.

subsections.label: Single-Tenant Concentration Risk
points: Single-tenant, single-building exposure (only ~10% of portfolio) viewed as a risk because full client exit could leave a building at zero occupancy; company mitigates via multi-tenancy building preference.

subsections.label: Overexpansion Risk
points: Management deliberately avoiding overshooting growth given geopolitical situation and AI uncertainty ('big elephant in the room'), to avoid a position it may later regret.

subsections.label: FY26 Guidance vs Actual
points: Prior guidance was ~30% revenue growth; actual achieved was 37%, an outperformance of 7 percentage points.
EBITDA guidance range of 18-21% and PAT guidance range of 8-10% were both met as per FY26 actuals.

subsections.label: Forward Metrics Disclosure Consideration
points: Management is considering providing advance disclosure of expected quarterly rent-paying area additions to help investors anticipate results, in response to analyst suggestion; indicated visibility exists but this granular metric has not been shared historically.

Indicative monthly run-rate shared: 1-1.5 lakh sq ft/month RPA addition and 1-1.25 lakh sq ft/month RYA addition (at ~80% conversion), though management stopped short of committing to a formal quarterly disclosure metric.

subsections.label: Lease Payment / Cost Guidance
points: Lease payment (cost) growth expected to track in line with revenue growth guidance of 25-30%.

themes.label: Margin expansion
themes.note: EBITDA margin expanded from 18% to 21% and PAT margin from 5% to 9% in FY26 alongside strong revenue growth.

themes.label: Occupancy trend & seasonality
themes.note: End-of-month occupancy dipped to 81% in March 2026 vs 85% prior quarter, but average annual occupancy of 84% (vs steady-state 87-88%) shows only a mild dip; management stresses annual over quarterly view.

themes.label: VAS scale-up
themes.note: Value-added services grew from 12% to 15% of revenue in FY26, guided to reach 17-18% next year, driven by expanding B2B/B2C service scope beyond IndiQube buildings.

themes.label: GCC-led demand / Flex adoption
themes.note: GCC absorption at 44% of overall office absorption, with hub-and-spoke leasing model driving Flex uptake for large MNCs, and a long tail of future GCC growth expected over 4-5 years.

themes.label: Green power / solar expansion
themes.note: Operational solar capacity growing (Latur 4MW, Yadgir 20MW, Virudhunagar 2.7MW) with 30-35 MW planned addition next year to reduce energy costs and meet GCC data-center power demand.

themes.label: Input cost inflation (CAPEX materials)
themes.note: Geopolitical/war-related factors pushed CAPEX per sq ft from INR 15.50 to INR 16.50 due to 5-7% material cost bump-up, currently being absorbed rather than passed to clients.

themes.label: Disciplined/sustainable growth strategy
themes.note: Management prioritizes sustainable, defensible micro-market growth over aggressive expansion despite available cash, viewing the business as not winner-takes-all.

key_takeaways: FY26 has been a landmark year for IndiQube. We delivered record performance across key financial metrics supported by strong revenue growth, continued margin expansion, and a significant strengthening of profitability.
We achieved our highest-ever revenue of INR 1,469 crores, representing a growth of 37% year-on-year. EBITDA crossed the INR 300 crore milestone and is growing at 60% year-on-year.
Profit after tax improved sharply by 145% to INR 125 crores.
EBITDA margin expanded from 18% in FY25 to 21% in FY26. PAT margin improved from 5% to 9% over the same period.
Our cash flow from operations also strengthened significantly, increasing 147% year-on-year to INR 304 crores.
During the year, we have added close to 1.6 million square feet in rent-paying area and launched 15 new centers.
Our steady state occupancy improved from 87% to 88%, reflecting strong utilization and sustained demand across our mature centers.
The contribution to overall revenue increased to 15% compared to 12% last year [VAS].
Our technology platform MiQube continues to play an important role in this journey. Over the last year, MiQube recorded 1.4 million transactions.

Just wanted to get your sense on the trajectory for the occupied area... how this operational area of 6.3 million square feet should pan out over the next two quarters.

While I believe we have more cash available than, say, some other peers, why aren't we being more aggressive with our growth strategy in terms of either larger sizes or more properties in our portfolio?

SBIN.about: State Bank of India is a Fortune 500 company. It is an Indian Multinational, Public Sector banking and financial services statutory body headquartered in Mumbai. It is the largest and oldest bank in India with over 200 years of history.[1]

quarters.summary: SBI reported record Q1FY27 net profit of ₹21,121 crore with operating profit up 9.77% YoY and domestic NIM resilient at 3%, reinforcing full-year NIM guidance. Management reiterated broad-based credit growth guidance of 14-15% (revised corporate credit growth to 14-15%), maintained confidence on asset quality (gross/net NPA at two-decade lows) despite a sequential uptick in slippages, and flagged that ECL provisioning impact numbers will be shared only after Q2FY27 once IT systems are updated, with no major capital adequacy impact expected. FCNR(B) mobilization of ~$6 billion so far (target ~$10 billion / ₹1 trillion) is expected to reduce bulk deposit reliance without materially impacting NIM, while forex fee income is expected to recover after bottoming in Q1 due to RBI's NOP guideline impact.

subsections.label: Deposit growth dynamics
points: Deposit growth to be seen from lens of liquidity available; wholesale/bulk deposit rates have risen to levels the bank is unwilling to match.
Retail franchise performing well with term deposit growth at 14% and savings bank growth of 10% on a ₹17.5 lakh crore base, an exception versus industry struggling with CASA.
Significant liquidity in balance sheet with excess SLR of ₹3.06 lakh crore as on 30 June, rising to ₹4 lakh crore currently, aided by FCNR(B) flows.

Bulk deposit treated as a treasury activity — treasury decides whether to access bulk deposits or borrow more cheaply elsewhere; this balance was achieved well in Q1, reflected in cost of resources and NIM stability.
~7 bps NIM uptick mainly due to cost of deposits going down.

subsections.label: Miscellaneous expenses and income — comparability
points: Miscellaneous expenses this quarter clubbed insurance expenses; excluding insurance, expenses were broadly flat YoY (₹2,385 crore vs ₹2,266 crore); insurance expenses were ₹1,723 crore vs ₹2,074 crore prior year.

Q4 numbers include carried-over bulk expenses (₹7,774 crore in Q4FY26, reduced to ₹4,108 crore in Q1FY27, a decline of ₹5,800-6,000 crore QoQ), so Q4-to-Q1 comparison is misleading; correct comparison is YoY (Q1 vs Q1).
Bank has decided to amortize bulk expenses over three quarters starting this quarter to avoid the Q4 expense bump distorting comparisons going forward.

Miscellaneous income also should not be compared with Q4 since bulk income (e.g., locker rents) is booked entirely in Q1, creating sequential variability (a ₹4,000 crore QoQ decline versus ₹6,600 crore in Q1FY26); ideal comparison is YoY.
Other provisions rose to ₹1,270 crore in Q1FY27 from a reversal of ₹366 crore in Q4FY26, of which ₹750-800 crore relates to PLI, with expected annual PLI provision of ₹3,000 crore for FY27.

subsections.label: Fee income outlook
points: Fee income as % of overall income still only ~15% versus potential to reach 20%; focus areas include loan processing charges, government business, and CVE activities.

₹500 crore improvement in government business fees is a combination of accounting treatment (accrual basis for cash management solutions per auditor guidance, ~50% of increase) and usual growth from retail side; ex-adjustment growth would have been ~29% YoY.

subsections.label: Pension provisioning trend
points: Pension is a combination of regular contributions (on a declining trend) and actuarial assessment/MTM gains that vary quarterly based on yields; MTM gains on pension & gratuity fund were ₹935 crore in Q1FY27 versus ₹1,125 crore in Q1FY26.
Real/significant cost impact from declining pension contributions expected only post-2035, since NPS was introduced in 2010; incremental decrease till then.
Interest on IT refund fell sharply to ₹220 crore in Q1FY27 from ₹1,002 crore in Q4FY26; dividend income from subsidiaries fell to ₹31 crore from ₹72 crore in Q1FY26.

subsections.label: Forex fee income decline
points: Forex fee income of ₹500 crore in Q1FY27, decrease primarily due to greater market volatility from the war and RBI guidelines (effective last week of March) limiting net open position to $100 million, impacting market liquidity.
Markets have started to normalize; forex fee income believed to have bottomed out in Q1 with better performance expected in forthcoming quarters, normalizing toward ₹1,500 crore.

subsections.label: Credit pipeline and asset base
points: Corporate credit pipeline (undisbursed term loans + unutilized working capital + pipeline) exceeds ₹9 lakh crore currently.
CD ratio at 82% currently; corporate credit growth at 18% in Q1FY27.
FCNR(B) leverage funding example: ₹1 lakh crore on a ₹60 lakh crore deposit base.
System-wide home loan book (~₹34 lakh crore) viewed as a large illiquid asset with potential for securitization.

subsections.label: Corporate loan book — MCLR transition
points: Flat sequential growth on corporate side versus strong SME/retail/Agri growth attributed to combination of moving part of T-bill linked portfolio to MCLR and some customers seeking alternatives unwilling to pay MCLR.
T-bill pricing itself being renegotiated in many cases, improving yield; transition still work in progress, not fully completed.

Sequential dip in corporate book is seasonal but much less severe than in prior years; large base (33% of book is corporate — largest in the system) makes percentage growth appear smaller versus peers.
Strong pipeline exceeding ₹9 lakh crore including undisbursed term loans, unutilized working capital, and pipeline; M&A financing seen as a strong new opportunity.

subsections.label: Gold loan strategy
points: Personal gold loans outstanding at ₹1.25 trillion and agri gold loans at ₹1.85 trillion as on 30 June 2026, totaling ₹3.1 trillion; yield range 8.5-8.9% with average ticket size ₹2.5-3 lakh.

Growth in retail gold loan at near 100%, entirely industry-wide driven by PSU banks with limited competition from large private banks; yields charged are lower than private peers due to larger average ticket size versus smaller-ticket competitors who pay higher rates.
Loan-to-value maintained below 55-56%; limited scope to raise rates significantly given customer price sensitivity — bank will not move to double-digit yields.

Gold loan treated as opportunistic (not core portfolio) — zero risk weight makes it ROE-accretive with small margin compromise; some Xpress Credit customers shifting to gold loans due to ~3% interest rate arbitrage, which may slow gold loan momentum and support Xpress Credit growth going forward.

subsections.label: Personal loan penetration and collections buildout
points: Xpress Credit growth ~8% sequential traction in Q1FY27; industry personal loan growth ~10-11% for banks versus 20-25% for NBFCs targeting self-employed segment; banks have shallower product penetration among self-employed/professional customers due to weaker collection mechanisms versus NBFCs.
Currently 99% of Xpress Credit borrowers are salaried; 75-76% of recoveries happen via automated SB-to-loan sweeps rather than active collection.

Bank building a full-fledged collection vertical from scratch, led by a dedicated Head of Collection Vertical, targeting ~6,000 Feet on Street to be deployed via subsidiary SBOSS, combined with analytics/AI models, branch network and contact center — a roughly 1-year buildout before entering deeper self-employed/professional personal loan and MSME segments where pricing power exists.
Deepening penetration expected to occur across home loan, personal loan and MSME products beyond current levels.

subsections.label: Current account trends
points: Government current account balances virtually drying up industry-wide, but SBI maintaining current account market share due to strong 14% YoY growth in non-governmental deposits; overall current account growth 4-5% YoY.
Overall system current account balances expected to continue declining.

subsections.label: Asset quality / slippages commentary
points: Fresh slippages of ₹7,046 crore in Q1FY27, up from ~₹5,500 crore in Q4FY26, typically higher in Q1 seasonally; comparison should be YoY (Q1 vs Q1) rather than sequential.
Slippage breakdown by segment: Agri ₹2,600 crore, SME ₹2,300 crore, Personal ₹2,100 crore.
Of the ₹7,046 crore Q1 slippages, ₹1,400-1,500 crore already pulled back as of the call date.
Management does not see building stress in gross/net NPA, SMA, or slippage trends despite the sequential uptick.

subsections.label: Emerging business verticals (CHAKRA / Centre of Excellence)
points: Bank has set up a Centre of Excellence developing deep sectoral expertise (Data Centers, GPU, hydrogen, solar, and other emerging/aspirational sectors) via the CHAKRA initiative, updating risk models through deeper engagement with industry players.

Building pipeline in these sectors; also seeing strong traction in Merger & Acquisition financing, a newly opened business line, with high customer interest including from software companies that traditionally did not borrow from banks.

Funding requirement (~₹30 lakh crore CapEx cycle over next 4 years per an analyst estimate) will require structural shift — non-bank capital pools (pension funds, mutual funds, insurance) need to participate; bank exploring securitization of illiquid assets (e.g., ~₹34 lakh crore system-wide home loan book) to expand funding capacity, contingent on non-bank participation.

subsections.label: Digital initiatives
points: Launched digital re-KYC journey enabling eligible customers to update KYC seamlessly through a digital interface.
Strengthened YONO ecosystem with new digital customer journeys including a seamless 3-in-1 onboarding process for savings, Demat and trading accounts.
Introduced YONO Ji, an agentic AI-powered virtual round-the-clock assistant on YONO Business, and expanded WhatsApp banking for current account customers.
Integrated trade finance suite into YONO Business and adopted AI in trade finance operations to improve turnaround time and customer experience.
Launched MSME Dream, extending the business rule engine coverage for SME loans up to ₹10 crore (from ₹5 crore earlier), enabling faster credit decisions while maintaining underwriting discipline.
Expanded digital document execution nationally for Kisan Credit Card and Agri Gold loans to improve customer convenience.

PRISM predictive stress monitoring platform leverages internal and external data sources to identify early signs of borrower stress, also enhancing preparedness for the proposed ECL framework implementation.

AI models used extensively to generate analytical leads across product segments (home loan, Xpress Credit, gold loan, MSME loans) for operating staff/Feet on Street to convert into business, aggregating to ₹22,000 crore.
Digital acquisitions on the new YONO platform continuing to grow steadily, contributing to productivity, customer experience and cost optimization.

points: Trade finance constitutes about one-third of the foreign office book; this book is being reduced to fund FCNR(B) leverage.

subsections.label: FCNR(B) mobilization mechanics
points: In the last FCNR cycle (2013), SBI's leverage was 70% of deposits raised, but that time flows were heavily back-ended due to leverage/SBLC confusion; this cycle flows expected to be more spread out.
FCNR deposits are covered under DICGC insurance up to ₹5 lakh.
RBI guidelines limit net open position (NOP) to $100 million, constraining forex market liquidity and contributing to lower forex fee income.

subsections.label: Industry benchmarks
points: Mutual fund industry size at ₹82 lakh crore as of June.
Retail and industry gold loan growth both running at ~100%, industry-wide phenomenon driven by PSU banks.
Competitor (private peers/regional players) gold loan yields run at 10-11%, higher than SBI's 8.5-8.9% due to smaller average ticket sizes.
Industry personal loan growth at 10-11% for banks versus 20-25% for NBFCs, reflecting NBFCs' deeper penetration of the self-employed segment via stronger collection infrastructure.

subsections.label: Subsidiary value unlocking
points: Successful listing of SBI Funds Management Limited marks a significant milestone in unlocking value within the SBI group.
SBI General Insurance identified as next listing candidate, though no timeline given.
Bank continues to focus on supporting long-term growth of each subsidiary.

subsections.label: CHAKRA initiative / emerging sector financing
points: CHAKRA Centre of Excellence developing dedicated teams with deep sectoral expertise across emerging industries (Data Center, GPU, hydrogen, solar) to build risk models and engage with industry players, still in early days with an emerging pipeline.
Building capability to underwrite in new segments; new customer classes emerging, e.g., software companies now borrowing from SBI for acquisitions.
M&A advisory/financing is a newly opened business line with strong traction and industry consultation of SBI.

Exploring securitization structures to unlock funding capacity from illiquid asset portfolios (e.g., large home loan book), contingent on broader non-bank participation in the financial system, estimated at ~₹30 lakh crore capex requirement over next 4 years.

subsections.label: Collection vertical buildout
points: New full-fledged collection vertical being built from scratch, led by a dedicated Head of Collection Vertical (Hemant), targeting ~6,000 Feet on Street via subsidiary SBOSS, combined with analytics/AI and branch/contact-center network — expected over ~1 year — to enable deeper penetration into self-employed/professional loan segments.

subsections.label: CFO appointment
points: New CFO (Mr. Agrawal) welcomed, noted to have experience handling large fundraising and recently led roadshows worldwide; analyst referenced a 5-year term commitment.

subsections.label: ECL transition timeline
points: IT systems expected to have all models and data pushed by 18th August; correct numbers on ECL impact to be given at Q2 results meeting rather than now.

Assurance given that ECL will not have any major impact due to expected capital augmentation from mutual fund listing and a planned major divestment, plus intent to take regulatory dispensation allowing transition impact to be spread over time (reducing annual capital adequacy impact).
Roll-forwards from SMA to NPA remain very limited for SBI (Stage 1/2 rarely becoming Stage 3), but floor rates on SMA 1 and 2 could still have some run-rate credit cost impact.
No current expectation of any major impact forcing pass-through of costs to customers in the first year, unless credit cycle moves adversely beyond a certain threshold.

subsections.label: Slippage and SMA uptick
points: Analyst flagged an uptick in absolute gross/net NPA numbers after several quarters, SMA 2 doubling QoQ, overall SMA rising a little, and fresh slippages rising to ~₹7,000 crore from ~₹5,500 crore, alongside a rise in other provisions to ₹1,270 crore from a reversal of ₹366 crore in the prior quarter.
Management does not view this as indicative of building systemic stress, citing seasonal Q1 pattern and partial pullback of slippages.

subsections.label: Deposit competition
points: Deposits described as an extremely competitive landscape with wholesale deposit rates rising to levels the bank is unwilling to match.

subsections.label: Global macro backdrop
points: Q1 unfolded against a global backdrop marked by geopolitical uncertainty, evolving trade dynamics and continued volatility across commodity and financial markets, though Indian economy remained resilient.

subsections.label: Corporate market pricing risk
points: Shift between market (CP/NCD) funding and bank funding is now very fast, unlike the historical lag; corporate pricing likely to be more determined by CP/NCD rates (a function of system liquidity) than by liquidity alone, potentially leading to some yield moderation.

subsections.label: Credit growth guidance rationale
points: 14-15% credit growth guidance anchored on nominal GDP expectation of 12-12.5%, with SBI historically growing 2-3% above nominal GDP.
18% YoY credit growth attributed to base effect from a muted Q1 last year across the banking system, not seen as sustainable/representative run-rate.
Internal industry estimate is 15-16%; if economic activity is primed more, SBI could move toward 16% level, but broader guidance remains at 14-15%.
Corporate credit growth guidance revised to 14-15% (from prior 12-13%); overall FY27 loan growth guidance range revised to 13-15% from prior 12-14%.

subsections.label: Margin outlook
points: Chairman reiterated full-year NIM guidance of 3% (domestic basis), declining to give quarterly outlook.
FCNR(B) domestically expected to have no significant NIM impact given it is not a large proportion versus ₹60 lakh crore deposit base.

Overseas, no major NIM impact expected either, since foreign offices largely reduce trade finance book (margin often lower than FCNR(B) yield) to fund the FCNR(B) leverage, keeping overall bank NIM broadly unaffected.

subsections.label: FCNR(B) program details
points: No explicit internal target for FCNR mobilization, but estimate of ~$10 billion / ~₹1 trillion appears reasonable based on inquiries, visibility and customer outreach; bank may exceed this.
As of the call date, $6 billion mobilized via FCNR(B), $1 billion via OFCB, and $300 million via ECBs, totaling $7.3 billion funded for foreign offices.
FCNR(B) contributed ₹45,000 crore in the latter part of July 2026, versus ₹7,000-8,000 crore in the June quarter (Q1FY27), showing acceleration.

Unlike 2013 episode where flows were heavily back-ended due to leverage confusion, this time ~70% of SBI's prior-cycle deposits were raised late-cycle but current flows expected to be more spread out since there is no confusion on leverage or SBLC issuance.
Leverage on FCNR(B) currently provided entirely by the bank's own foreign/overseas offices.
FCNR(B) deposits are covered under DICGC insurance up to ₹5 lakhs.

subsections.label: Bulk deposit proportion
points: Bank declines to disclose bulk deposit proportion (treated as a dynamic treasury activity) but confirms the proportion is significantly coming down, helped by FCNR(B) flows; a ₹1 lakh crore FCNR(B) flow would reduce bulk proportion correspondingly.

subsections.label: Subsidiary listing plans
points: Successful listing of SBI Funds Management Limited completed, described as a significant milestone in unlocking group value.
SBI General Insurance remains the next candidate for potential listing, though no specific timeline has been given.

risk_register.note: Fresh slippages rose to ₹7,046 crore in Q1FY27 with SMA 2 doubling QoQ, but management attributes this to seasonal Q1 pattern and states ₹1,400-1,500 crore already pulled back, seeing no building stress
