subsections.label: PB Health expansion
points: One hospital (Noida) is fully operational, generating ~₹150 Cr revenue and ₹20-30 Cr profit annually.
Next hospital (Central Gurugram) set to go live within weeks, starting next week, operational by month end.
Additional hospitals being pursued in Gurgaon and Delhi, and expansion being explored outside Delhi.

PB Care+ preferred hospital network (500 hospitals) operates as an asset-light coordination model, distinct from the owned/operated hospital business; over the next year these two models (network coordination and full hospital ownership) are expected to converge, with the company taking over O&M operations of some network hospitals under the PB Health brand.

PB Health is in late-stage conversations to raise capital but has not yet approached PB Fintech for investment; PB Fintech has the right (not obligation) to invest up to its pro-rata stake (26-28%) if/when a round comes to the board.
PB Health has no immediate cash requirement, having used less than 30% of its existing cash.

subsections.label: Other strategic considerations
points: Management stated no other new growth opportunities or adjacencies are currently being explored or discussed at either board or management level in the last 3 months.

Paisabazaar's long-term aspiration (not board-approved) is to list itself as a separate entity in 4-5 years, with strategy oriented toward becoming a broader financial engagement/wealth platform (credit, savings, bonds, mutual funds, points, tokens).

Life insurance industry deferred-commission-revenue debate: company has advocated for deferred payment structure for 10 years and is broadly supportive of such a change if it happens; health insurance EOM-reduction conversation is also welcomed without specific comment.

Management stated it does not want to speculate on take-rate/commission scenarios; if the whole savings-business industry's commission structure matched Policybazaar's own low take rate, ~98% of other industry players would likely be unable to continue, which would represent 'industry destruction, not industry expansion.'

subsections.label: Regulatory uncertainty
points: Recurring media speculation on potential commission caps/tighter commission regulation, but management states no confirmation has been received from the regulator or seen by insurance companies; management differentiates between two separate ongoing conversations — deferred revenue recognition in life insurance (company supportive) and lower EOM structure in health insurance (company neutral/welcoming) — and states remaining rumors are media-driven only.

If commission/take-rate structures were reduced, management believes profitability would be redistributed between the company and insurers given the company's already-thin health insurance cost base, but exact mechanism (reinsurance, JV, reinsurance broker, etc.) and timing (3-6 months) remain unclear.

Potential deferred-commission-revenue rules could affect cash flow (strong impact possible) though P&L impact under Ind AS accounting is expected to be minimal; exact effect depends on eventual rules, which are not yet finalized.

subsections.label: Operational disruption
points: UAE business suffered ~10 days of zero booking capability in March due to regional conflict (bombing started Feb 28) combined with an AWS outage about 5 days into the disruption, since the business runs on AWS; despite this, UAE still grew 3% YoY for the month and 10-12% for the quarter.

subsections.label: Business quality risk
points: Phygital (physical fulfilment) model carries inherent quality risk since interactions are not on recorded lines; company manages this via verification calling and culture-building, though management states it remains 'very watchful' about this risk.

subsections.label: Industry sustainability risk
points: Management flagged that rising claims costs for the small cohort of frequent claimers could become unsustainable for the industry without introducing customer 'participation' (co-pay, limited/tiered networks), describing this as a necessity rather than a preference.

subsections.label: Growth guidance
points: Management reiterated its standing guidance of approximately 30% growth, noting the company has historically always beaten this guidance.

Management declined to give forward guidance on next year's growth rate for health/term specifically, citing unpredictability, but expressed confidence ('Next year growth; no problem') based on fundamentals (segmentation, correctly priced products, trained sales team using GenAI tools, and service/claims experience).

subsections.label: Paisabazaar outlook
points: Management expects Paisabazaar to be significantly EBITDA positive next year, driven by operating leverage as the stabilized cost base is absorbed by scaling revenue.
Estimated ~30% additional operating leverage available from the current employee base without further headcount expansion.

subsections.label: POSP outlook
points: Management expects a meaningful improvement in POSP growth in the next financial year given an opportune moment for deepening penetration (smaller cities model maturing, competitor consolidation).

subsections.label: PB Corporate (PBFP) outlook
points: Management plans continued investment in the corporate broking business over the next few years, prioritizing growth and quality over near-term profitability; expects this business could ultimately be significantly more profitable than POSP once scaled.

subsections.label: Capital allocation outlook
points: No finalized capital allocation plan; buybacks and dividends have been discussed informally but not brought to the board.

guidance_ledger.statement: We always guide about 30%, we always beat that guidance.
We expect it to be significantly positive next year, so we actually expect quite a strong year from Paisabazaar.
Maybe about 30% or so is something that we can get with the current employee base.
I think you will find us being very aggressive this year on POSP... I think we should see a meaningful improvement in growth in the next financial year.
Corporate business will require investment still in the years ahead... this can be significantly more profitable than the POSP business... but that's not the immediate focus.
Next year growth; no problem.
We don't really have a plan on what to do with the capital... conversation about buybacks and dividends... not even gone to the board.
PB Health is going to be raising capital. They will be close to that... late-stage conversations to raise capital.
It'll take another 2-3 years to actually flesh that out fully... building a trail, building a recurring revenue stream.
From a renewal revenue perspective... probably not the next 2 years, from a renewal revenue of that.

themes.label: Health & Term insurance growth momentum
themes.note: Health has grown 60%+ for 13 straight quarters; term insurance had a standout Q4 driven by execution improvements and post-GST tailwinds.

themes.label: Paisabazaar turnaround
themes.note: Paisabazaar turned EBITDA-positive this quarter with management expecting significantly positive EBITDA next year on operating leverage from a stabilized cost base.

themes.label: Regulatory/commission uncertainty
themes.note: Ongoing media speculation about commission caps and deferred revenue rules, though no confirmation from the regulator; company is broadly supportive of deferred-revenue and lower-EOM structures.

themes.label: New product diversification (savings, MF, bonds, healthcare)
themes.note: Paisabazaar pursuing mutual fund (ARN) and bond licenses via stock-broking license, plus daily SIP innovation; PB Health hospital network expanding with new hospitals going live.

themes.label: AI as productivity, not margin, lever
themes.note: AI is being used to boost sales/customer service productivity and claims/risk assessment rather than as an immediate cost/margin optimization tool.

themes.label: POSP quality vs scale trade-off
themes.note: Company shifting toward smaller, more granular agents (83% of premium from small agents now vs ~50% a year ago) while planning aggressive POSP expansion this year.

themes.label: Capital allocation ambiguity
themes.note: No board-approved plan yet for large cash balance; informal discussion only on buybacks/dividends; PB Health may seek pro-rata investment from PB Fintech in a future funding round.

key_takeaways: We grew 42% year-on-year, to almost ₹30,000 Cr... led by new protection premium, which grew at 57% year-on-year. And the PAT is at ₹670 Cr, which represents 2.2% of our premium.
For the full year, our insurance premium obviously grew at 42%, but for the quarter, it grew at 46% year-on-year.
The new protection business in Q4FY26 was up for the year 57%, health at 68%... term is catching up fast.

Our renewals... has gone up for the last 12 months rolling from ₹668 Cr to ₹935 Cr, up ₹267 Cr. And for the quarter, this is at an ARR of ₹1,126 Cr, up from ₹689 Cr, so that's a growth of 63% year-on-year.
Our EBITDA is at -4%, with a 5% contribution margin. We've grown at 43% year-on-year.
PB Partners has 450,000 advisors... 99% of the PIN codes in the country are covered. Our UAE business grew 54% year-on-year.
Our revenue has grown at a CAGR of 48% over this period, over the last 4 or 5 years, and our PAT has grown from -58% to 10% in the full year of 2026.
Paisabazaar, on an operating basis, is positive on EBITDA this quarter, and honestly, internally at least, we expect it to be significantly positive next year.
We've acquired one hospital, which is an operating hospital, makes about ₹20-30 Cr of profit in a year, does about ₹150 Cr of revenue... Our next hospital is to go live in the next few weeks.
Only 5% of these lives... used a claim more than once... the remaining 85-odd customers... represents about 67% of all insurance policies, have no customer who has ever claimed for the last 10 years.
pressing_questions: Any incremental discussion on any cap on commissions or tighter commission regulation?

Just wanted to understand from the full-year point of view, around ₹6,800 Cr of revenue what we have reported, how much of the revenue, we have recognized, but yet to be received from the insurer?

REFEX.about: Refex Industries Limited specializes in trading eco-friendly refrigerant gases and providing comprehensive solutions for responsible coal procurement and ash disposal.[1]

quarters.summary: Refex Industries entered FY27 with strong momentum across businesses, led by 76% YoY standalone revenue growth in Q1 FY27, driven by ash & coal handling execution and initial wind turbine deliveries. Management guided to continued strong growth in ash & coal handling (better than FY26's ~28% CAGR), a ramp-up in wind turbine execution to ~INR1,700-1,800 crores for FY27 at 5-6% net margin (with wind turning profitable/break-even by year-end), and progress on the mobility demerger, targeted for completion around Q3 FY27.

subsections.label: Reporting basis clarification
points: Presentation and media release highlight standalone results because wind business is very new (second quarter of operations) and mobility business is being demerged, making standalone the right apple-to-apple comparison versus prior-year same quarter.

Previous financial year same quarter revenue was INR327 crores on a comparable basis; comparing to a consolidated number of INR900 crores would be a wrong comparison because wind business itself was not there in the previous year same quarter.
Going forward, as wind numbers add up quarter-on-quarter (already present from Q4), consolidated presentation will become the right way to present, e.g. from Q4 of this financial year.

subsections.label: Margin variance explanation (ash & coal handling, Q1 vs Q4 last year)
points: Margin was close to the same as Q4 of last year; the difference was due to a one-time other expense of bank processing charges (INR4 crores) arising from a loan takeover from Indian Overseas Bank, which offered better terms.

subsections.label: Balance sheet and capital discipline
points: Balance sheet continues to remain healthy; company remains committed to maintaining financial discipline while simultaneously investing in growth opportunities across businesses.
Net debt is close to zero; utilized debt is majorly towards bank guarantees and LCs; company has a good bank balance as of now.

subsections.label: Promoter pledge
points: A reduction in promoter pledge has already been disclosed last month; a further disclosure is expected in the next 15 days reflecting continued reduction.
There is continuous repayment happening, and on a milestone basis, release of pledged shares is happening; certain shares are expected to get released in the next two weeks.
Process is going as per plan with no challenges; regular release of pledged shares expected going forward.
When opportunity comes, promoters will keep acquiring shares from the market (referencing recent uptick in promoter stake).

subsections.label: Order book and pipeline dynamics
points: Robust order pipeline supports strong momentum across businesses; ash & coal handling growth benefited from a growing order book during the quarter.

Wind order book in hand is INR1,860 crores, of which INR525 crores has been executed, leaving a balance of INR1,300 crores to be executed within the current financial year (does not spill over to next year).
A few wind orders are in advanced stages of closure, expected to close in the next 30-60 days.
New wind orders won going forward will spill over to next financial year for execution.

Difficult to quantify wind order pipeline precisely because inquiry could be in gigawatts, but actual conversion in India is not easy to predict; substantial orders expected this year, at least better than last year.

Company is winning many digital tenders in ash & coal handling over the last four months; expects a better order book by Q4 of this financial year (consolidated order book, difficult to predict precisely).

subsections.label: Ash & coal handling business
points: Continued to deliver strong operational performance during the quarter and remains the largest contributor to the company's revenue and profitability.

Refex has built one of India's most comprehensive, technology-enabled ash utilization platforms, providing integrated solutions across the entire value chain including ash evacuation, transportation, utilization, logistics management, and regulatory compliance.
This integrated approach has created a robust nationwide ecosystem for sustainable ash management, making Refex the most preferred vendor for thermal power plants.

Business benefited during the quarter from healthy execution across major project locations, a growing order book, an improved operating environment versus corresponding last year, and sustained demand for integrated ash management solutions.
Volume run rate seasonality: Q2 will be little slow, Q3 and Q4 will scale up; there is no capacity constraint — it is a matter of multiplying fleet and people.
Company is working in 42 thermal power plants currently, representing 30%-35% penetration of thermal power plants in India, with a lot of potential for future opportunities.
Realization varies from INR450 to INR1200 per km per ton, purely dependent on distance and volume.

subsections.label: Wind energy business
points: Continued execution of customer project deliveries under existing order books during the quarter; business has transitioned from initial development/order book creation phase into an active delivery phase.

A key milestone: successful erection of India's first 5.3 MW wind turbine by a customer at its project site in Koppal, Karnataka — an important step towards commercial deployment of next-generation wind turbine platform.

Wind business margin in Q1 was very small (in fact an EBITDA loss of INR34 lakhs) because part of the phase is in transit and part of material billing has not yet happened; billing will occur in Q3 and Q4 leading to better margins in coming quarters.
Combined margin of Q1 and Q2 will tilt towards Q3 and Q4 in the wind turbine business.

Wind JV structure: technology is a direct transfer, JV partner does not own equity for the technology; partner owns 23% and manages complete operations of the business (industry partner); company owns 76%-77%.

Turbine installed (130m height) at customer site is completely operational and giving desired results as projected; customer is happy and there could be potential negotiation for a next order from the same customer.

Company is a pure product supplier — does not do EPC; scope is delivery of turbine, tower, and blade to site; installation, land acquisition, and regulatory compliance are handled by customer/IPP and separate installers.
Payment terms: ~95% of money comes on supply; ~5% may be held pending installation and testing completion to ensure turbine performance.
No orders received yet for blade replacement (older blades being replaced by new ones) — still under discussion in various forums but nothing concrete on ground.

5.3 MW turbine size not seen as a determinant of market size; wind industry itself is growing, government has an ambition to achieve 100 GW by 2030, and better technology/size will always get priority.

subsections.label: Mobility business
points: Execution remains on track; business continues to operate on an asset-light model and added a few new clients during the quarter, strengthening presence in the premium corporate mobility segment.
Refrigerant gas manufacturing business fully discontinued in the last quarter.
Green mobility (Refex Mobility) business is under discontinued operations and anticipated to go off completely by end of Q3 FY27, post which there will be no further loss in P&L from this business.
Mobility business is not being closed — it is being demerged into a separate listed company via a mirror shareholding structure; will operate under new listed entity.

subsections.label: Silvassa manufacturing facility
points: Silvassa is a leased facility; total capex done by the company is only for repairs and maintenance, close to INR3.5-4 crores.

It has a manufacturing capability of about 1 GW; in wind, 100% of components are not manufactured in-house at the factory — similar to an automobile company model with OEMs making different parts and assembly happening at the center.
Silvassa plant is a pure assembly plant where most components are manufactured across different parts of the country and assembled there; all designs of the parts are owned by the company.
1 GW technically could mean roughly INR5,000-6,000 crores of revenue.
Company makes the whole turbine including towers, nacelle, and blades; currently blades are imported, but localization is under progress and expected in about 6 to 12 months.

Company works with multiple OEMs across the country (56-60 vendors) for developing various products; owns the technology, license, and design; blades will be manufactured in-house, rest will be developed at third-party locations.

Localization process: 12 months from now, ~85% of components are expected to be localized, enabling similar margins to peer turbine makers (18-20% EBITDA) about 2 years down the line as localization and plant capacity increase.

subsections.label: Domestic focus
points: Both core businesses (fly ash/ash handling and wind power) are concentrated only on the domestic side at present.
Focus as of now is only to strengthen presence in the domestic market; there are no immediate plans for exports.

subsections.label: Railway-based transport (RCR)
points: Railways being used for coal and ash handling is expected to affect the business positively; company has started into Rail-cum-Road (RCR) transport.
Railway announced a discount in freight tariff, which will help take the business to newer areas like Northeast where power plants are fewer but cement company requirements exist.
Will help transport more material from West Bengal, Jharkhand, Bihar to Northeast India; expected to add new revenue avenues in addition to existing road transport operations.

subsections.label: Competitive intensity in ash handling
points: Increased competition is viewed as helpful, not a threat, because it will create more awareness among customers and vendor partners and help grow the business overall.

Company considers itself the only organized business player in this industry; more players entering would complement rather than compete, as the market itself is being discovered and there is a huge gap of opportunities for multiple players.
Industry fundamentals continue to remain strong, driven by increasing power demand, expansion of thermal generation capacity, and greater regulatory focus on achieving 100% ash utilization.

Customers increasingly seek integrated and technology-driven partners who can deliver operational excellence along with regulatory compliance; Refex remains well-positioned to capture emerging opportunities.

subsections.label: Wind sector tailwinds
points: FY26 was the highest ever wind installation year for the industry; FY27 has an industry target of 9-10 GW.
There is reportedly a shortage of turbines being discussed in the market.

Renewable energy is shifting from single source to a mixture of multiple sources (wind, solar, storage) because government now needs round-the-clock power rather than seasonal power, which causes grid stability issues.
Management sees strong tailwinds in the sector for the foreseeable future, with a mixture of all three renewable sources being installed.

Turbine makers generally achieve 18%-20% EBITDA margins; Refex aims to reach similar margins about 2 years down the line as localization and plant capacity increase, with margin improvement expected to become visible from FY28 onward as localization starts.

subsections.label: Wind turbine environmental/bird safety consideration
points: Management acknowledges concern around bird deaths caused by wind turbines; noted there is no technology in the world that can completely avoid this.
High wind velocity at blade tips is managed; noted turbines are now largely recognized by birds in a locality such that 99% avoid coming closer; a small residual risk (~1%) remains.
Company's intent is to do whatever possible to preserve nature, referencing Jain principles of not harming any living being.

subsections.label: Mobility demerger
points: Demerger process is progressing as planned; during the quarter, received approval from the honourable NCLT court to convene meetings of shareholders and creditors as part of the scheme arrangement.
Pursuant to NCLT's direction, the equity shareholders meeting has been scheduled for next month.

Upon completion of the demerger, the mobility business will operate as an independent entity focused exclusively on premium, clean, reliable, and sustainable mobility solutions, with its own growth strategy, capital allocation framework, and operational priorities.
Restructuring is expected to unlock significant long-term value by enabling sharper strategic focus and enhanced execution capabilities for both Refex Industries and Refex Mobility.
Mobility business is not being closed down — refrigerant gas business has been fully closed, but mobility will become a separate listed company via mirror shareholding structure.

No plans currently for a strategic partner in mobility business; that is still under demerger and legal process — once demerger happens and business runs as independent entity, partnership will be considered as per business requirement.

subsections.label: Capital allocation post-demerger
points: Capital allocation for both ash handling and wind businesses will happen based on requirements as profitability and revenue keep growing; company will keep updating shareholders/investors on direction.

Currently, focus is more on the ash handling business; there is not much capital requirement in the wind business currently, but as indigenization and growth/localization occur, capital requirements may arise at the entity level — company may raise working capital or term loan from banks, or capital allocation from holding company could happen.

Volume outlook: Q2 will be little slow, Q3 and Q4 will scale up, consistent with the historical seasonal pattern where Q4 and Q1 always give better results.
Company maintains historical CAGR guidance of 30%-35%, and expects to do better than last year's ~28% growth in the current financial year.
Margins for ash & coal handling business are expected to be maintained at similar levels through Q2, Q3, Q4.

subsections.label: Wind business outlook

Full-year net margin target for wind business is 5%-6% (referred to as net/PAT margin, not EBITDA); Q1 and Q2 margins will be weak/negative, tilting toward stronger margins in Q3 and Q4.
Wind business is expected to become profitable by end of this financial year (FY27).
Next year's wind growth rate expected to be very good, though direct comparison to this year's low base (FY26 revenue of INR225 crores) would not be meaningful.

Wind margins expected to reach turbine-maker peer levels (18%-20% EBITDA) about 2 years down the line as localization and plant capacity increase; margin improvement visible from FY28 as localization starts.

Equity shareholders meeting for the demerger scheme scheduled for next month, pursuant to NCLT direction.

themes.label: Margin guidance consistency

themes.label: Diesel/logistics disruption
themes.note: Geopolitical developments caused intermittent diesel supply constraints and logistics disruptions during the quarter, managed via diversified fleet and technology-enabled processes.

themes.label: Promoter pledge reduction

key_takeaways: We have entered FY27 with a strong momentum across our businesses supported by robust execution, a healthy order pipeline, and continued progress across our strategic growth platforms.
Ash and coal handling business continued to deliver a strong operational performance during the quarter and remained the largest contributor to the company's revenue and profitability.
During the quarter, we also witnessed intermittent diesel supply constraints and logistics disruptions arising from ongoing geopolitical developments.
A key milestone during the quarter was the successful erection of India's first 5.3 megawatt wind turbine by our customer at its project site in Koppal, Karnataka.

The mobility business demerger process is progressing as planned; during the quarter, we received approval from the honourable NCLT court to convene meetings of shareholders and creditors as part of the scheme arrangement.

On a standalone basis, revenue for the continuing operations for the quarter stood at INR619 crores compared to INR351 crores in the corresponding quarter in the previous financial year, representing a year-on-year growth of 76%.
EBITDA for the quarter stood at INR105 crores compared to INR39.6 crores in the corresponding quarter for the previous financial year; EBITDA margin stood at 17%.
Profit after tax for the quarter stood at INR73.6 crores compared to INR33 crores during the same period in the previous financial year, representing growth of 123%; PAT margin improved to 11.9%.

SOUTHBANK.about: Established in 1929, South Indian Bank was the first ‘scheduled bank’ amongst the private banks in Kerala. It has strong presence in south India and particularly in Kerala. South Indian Bank provides retail and corporate banking, para banking activities such as debit card, third party financial product distribution, in addition to Treasury and Foreign Exchange Business.[1]

quarters.summary: South Indian Bank's Q1 FY27 call, the last with outgoing MD & CEO P.R. Seshadri, highlighted NIM recovery (up 28bps QoQ, 20bps YoY to 3.23%), 17% net profit growth, and continued strategic focus on shifting mix away from corporate toward retail/MSME/gold loans over the medium term, even as corporate book share rose opportunistically this quarter. Management guided to positive full-year operating leverage, moderating credit costs, fee income recovery, and continued FCNR growth, while flagging geopolitical (West Asia) risk and a pending CEO transition before/around September 30, 2026.

subsections.label: NIM drivers
points: Bank clawed back the NIM dip that occurred due to repo rate cuts.
Substantial chunk of high-rate deposits rolled off and repriced downwards by 40-60 bps between January and June 2026, driving the reduction in cost of funding.
Increased CASA balances (average CASA grew 19%) helped manage cost of funding.
Bulk deposits were dropped by 50% from a year ago, reducing arbitrage losses from being overfunded (paying more on deposits than earned placing money overnight with RBI).
Asset yield increase of ~5 bps was largely driven by shift in mix and a portion of the corporate book linked to T-bills, which moved up sharply during the period.

subsections.label: Fee income weakness
points: Fee income softness attributed by management to a one-off, not a trend; bank was focused on NIM management rather than fees.

Difference between Q4 FY26 core fee income (INR191 crores) and Q1 FY27 (INR179 crores) attributed in large part to a technical/process change in account renewal fee charging, which will be fixed going forward.

Reduction in recoveries (a portion of which is attributed to interest income depending on loan nature/location) also contributed to lower noninterest income; Q1 is traditionally a softer quarter for recoveries.
Treasury and forex income was very muted this quarter versus a spectacular Q1 FY26, and Q4 FY26 was zero.
Q1 FY26 also benefited from ~INR60 crores PSLC sale income and FLDG income (from credit cards, since discontinued per RBI guidelines), neither of which recurred this quarter.

subsections.label: Cost of deposits and opex outlook
points: Management does not expect this sharp reduction in cost of deposits to continue at the same pace going forward, as a substantial portion of the repricing impact is already baked in.
Bank is restarting branch rollout in a small way after freezing almost everything for 3 years, targeting key locations chosen carefully for accretive outcomes.
CFO does not expect opex increase to materially alter P&L structure; expects opex growth in the 5-6% range for the year.
This quarter did not show positive operating leverage, but full-year aim remains positive operating leverage.

subsections.label: Security receipts
points: Recovery on security receipts was purely a recovery of principal; no additional upside was recognized in P&L this quarter since the entire SR upside was recognized when the SR itself was originally recognized.

subsections.label: DICGC insurance repricing
points: Bank benefited from non-uniform DICGC insurance repricing among banks, resulting in a QoQ reduction of about INR10 crores, roughly a 15% reduction for the full year.

subsections.label: ECL transition impact
points: Effective interest rate change under ECL is not expected to materially change NII; working is still ongoing and no concrete number is available yet.

key_figures.label: Corporate portfolio share of total loan book

subsections.label: MSME, gold loan, mortgage, home and auto loan focus
points: Bank continues to focus on MSME loans, mortgage loans, home loans and auto loans; these growth numbers exclude the impact of any IBPC/DA entered into.

Gold loan Q-o-Q net growth was muted (0.8%) due to a change in process/policy occasioned by an RBI circular on gold loans effective April 1, which caused some co-lending and portfolio purchase arrangements to run off (~INR270 crores); branch banking gold loan growth itself was solid, and management expects material growth going forward.

MSME growth has been a little muted from expectations due to uncertainties that caused caution; management expects to return to scale mode this quarter, continuing the narrative of shifting balance sheet mix from corporate to better-yielding assets like MSME.

subsections.label: Corporate book
points: Corporate portfolio grew to around 40% of total loan book versus a strategic objective of bringing it down to around 30%.

Growth was driven by opportunistic deployment of liquidity with high-quality, low-risk corporate counterparties amid uncertainty in West Asia, and because corporate pricing improved dramatically for shorter duration facilities during the quarter.

These are short duration assets that can be wound down quickly; management views this as a one-time adjustment due to environmental conditions and existing credit lines/liquidity, with intent to wind down corporate balances in the long run as opportunities allow.
Yield improvement in corporate was driven by both T-bill movement and market rate hardening due to tighter liquidity; retail pricing did not move upward in the same way.

subsections.label: FCNR(B) deposits
points: FCNR(B) deposit growth was good this quarter (6% QoQ); bank is participating actively in the scheme, pricing to match domestic INR liquidity cost.
Vast amount of flows expected in August-September as the offer window is open until September 30.
Bank is working with its Dubai representative office; scope of activities permissible has been an area of focus with the Central Bank of the UAE.

Bank does not have credit lines from external entities nor an entity in GIFT City, so offering leverage is not currently possible; customers placing FCNR deposits are placing unlevered deposits; if foreign bank credit lines materialize, volumes could materially change.

subsections.label: SMA-1 and SMA-2
points: SMA-1 and SMA-2 increase of ~INR80 crores QoQ attributed to seasonality typically seen in Q1 versus Q4 (consistent with prior year trend lines, e.g., March'24 vs June'24, March'25 vs June'25); management reviewed constituents and believes they are reversible and do not materially add to risk carried.

subsections.label: ECLGS scheme
points: Utilization of the ECLGS limit remains a struggle relative to disbursement; bank is looking at progressively increasing ECLGS contribution to the book.

key_figures.label: Trade and FX platform revenue growth YoY

subsections.label: New systems and platforms
points: Bank is working on a series of new systems to enable more effective participation in other products.

Trade and FX platform expected to go live by end of September with full capabilities, enabling customers to do FX bookings, LCs, guarantees, sending/receiving money overseas, and settling export/import bills electronically.
Currently FX revenues are limited but growing at 40-50% YoY; new systems are expected to drive higher business volumes and revenues.

subsections.label: Geopolitical risk
points: Disturbances in West Asia (Persian Gulf) cited as reason for preferring high-quality, low-risk corporate exposure over growing higher-risk retail/MSME assets in the current environment.
Uncertainty associated with the Persian Gulf continues; slippage guidance for the year factors in some deterioration on account of the West Asia problem.

subsections.label: FCNR leverage constraint
points: Bank lacks credit lines from external entities and does not have an entity in GIFT City, limiting its ability to offer leverage on FCNR deposits; engaging with foreign banks to obtain lines but these have not yet materialized.

subsections.label: CEO succession
points: This was the last conference call for MD & CEO P.R. Seshadri in his current capacity; he is nearing the end of his tenure and declined to give guidance that would bind his successor.

subsections.label: NIM outlook
points: Management believes the rate cycle has switched and is more likely to increase than reduce; if so, NIMs should harden as repo rate changes come into effect.
No specific NIM number guided, but bank believes it is reasonably well positioned with respect to NIM and expects positive outcomes for the year.
Bank gives effect to repo rate changes on a T+1 basis, meaning it was most impacted when rates fell but is also positioned to benefit first if rates rise.

subsections.label: Operating leverage
points: Bank aims to achieve positive operating leverage for the full year despite not achieving it this particular quarter, supported by NIM traction and business line growth outpacing cost increases.

subsections.label: Fee income recovery
points: Management views the fee income softness as an aberration/one-off that will be fixed going forward, not a lasting trend.

subsections.label: Credit cost outlook
points: Current 9 bps credit cost is viewed as probably generous; credit costs are expected to moderate from here, if anything.

subsections.label: Capital deployment plan
points: Plan for deploying excess capital is to grow the balance sheet at market growth rate plus about 2 percentage points, and to change asset mix toward retail and MSME (non-AAA rated) assets with higher capital charge but also higher yield, which will increase risk density and spreads over time.

subsections.label: ROE/ROA trajectory
points: Bank has historically guided ROA in the 100-110/115 bps range, expected to migrate to 120-125 bps over time; ROE would follow given leverage, though CEO declined to give a more concrete number given his impending departure.

subsections.label: FCNR growth outlook
points: Growth has been robust and management expects continued good growth, with a vast amount of flows expected in August-September before the offer window closes September 30.

subsections.label: MSME growth outlook
points: Management expects to return to 'scale mode' this quarter after a muted period, continuing the narrative of shifting balance sheet mix from corporate toward MSME.

subsections.label: Corporate book long-term direction
points: Long-run aim remains to bring corporate book down, with continued opportunistic engagement as long as remunerative in the near term.

guidance_ledger.statement: We believe the rate cycle has switched and is more likely to increase than reduce; if that belief is right, NIMs from here should harden as repo rate changes come into effect. We are reasonably well positioned with respect to NIM and expect the outcomes for us during the year will be positive.
This quarter we do not have positive operating leverage, but for the full year, our aim is to get full positive operating leverage.
We are not expecting any significant increase in opex to materially alter the P&L structure; we should be within the range of maybe 5%-6%.
This lower noninterest income line is an aberration which will get fixed as we move forward; it's a one-timer, not a trend.
Our trade and FX platform is hoping to go live by end of September with all capabilities.

We think that our slippage will be in the neighborhood of INR500 crores to INR750 crores, INR800 crores will be the maximum slippage given current trend lines, even assuming some deterioration on account of the West Asia problem.
Our recoveries will be in the neighborhood of INR800 crores to INR1,000 crores; hopefully we should be able to close to around INR1,000 crores for the year.
The 9 basis points that we currently have is probably on a generous side; hopefully our credit costs will moderate from here, if anything.

guidance_ledger.metric: Corporate book share of balance sheet
guidance_ledger.statement: Our aim in the long run is to bring corporate down; under current circumstances given West Asia disturbances, we continue to look for opportunities on the corporate side as long as they are remunerative, but long run those balances will be wound down.

The plan for deploying excess capital is to grow the balance sheet at wherever the market is growing plus a couple of percent above where the market is growing, and to change the asset mix toward retail and MSME.
We had said that we'd be in the 100 to 110, 115 range. Over time, that should sort of migrate to 120, 125.
Given our leverage, you can compute the return on equity automatically; I'm hesitant to give a more concrete answer considering I'm nearing the end of my tenure.
Underlying core growth from our branches is quite solid, and we are reasonably confident that going forward, you will see material growth on the gold loan business.
This quarter, we will go back to the scale mode; we intend to keep our narrative intact on changing the balance sheet mix from shrinking corporate and increasing contribution from MSME.
We are looking at progressively increasing that ECLGS contribution to the book.

We believe a vast amount of these flows will come in August and September because the offer is open until September 30; pace of growth is good and we are quite confident we will get reasonable numbers.
We are in a very small way restarting branch rollout in key locations, being very careful as to where we put branches to get accretive outcomes.

The advantage from repricing of bulk deposits may not be there in the same quantum in coming quarters, but we continue to ensure NII holds, with repo rate increases (if they occur) expected to work further in the bank's favor.
We don't expect that there will be any material change from effective interest rate coming in as part of ECL; working is still on, initial workings reflect no material change.
Within corporate, the ultra-short duration assets should go down from roughly 20-25% of the corporate book down to perhaps 10% of the book.
Expenses cannot be kept at this level indefinitely; you will see expense growth coming forward, but we are hopeful that will be more than compensated for by revenue growth.
I expect that all of this will happen in such a fashion that the new incumbent can be in position before or immediately after the end of my term (30th September).
We've been talking at the board level to grow branches in Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Karnataka, Maharashtra, Gujarat and New Delhi; there will be some growth, done very deliberately.

risk_register.risk: Geopolitical tension in West Asia / Persian Gulf
risk_register.note: Cited as reason for preferring low-risk corporate exposure and as a factor incorporated into slippage guidance for possible deterioration.

risk_register.risk: Lack of external credit lines / no GIFT City entity limiting FCNR leverage
risk_register.note: Prevents bank from offering leveraged FCNR deposits; working with foreign banks to obtain lines but not yet materialized.

risk_register.risk: CEO succession
risk_register.note: This was Seshadri's last earnings call as MD & CEO; declined to give guidance that would bind successor.

risk_register.risk: Fee income softness / process issue
risk_register.note: Attributed to a technical/process change in account renewal fee charging and softer Q1 recoveries; management says it is being fixed.

risk_register.risk: Regulatory change in gold loans (RBI circular effective April 1)
risk_register.note: Caused runoff of co-lending/portfolio purchase arrangements (~INR270 crores), muting Q-o-Q gold loan net growth to 0.8%.

risk_register.risk: SMA-1 and SMA-2 seasonal increase
risk_register.note: Increase of ~INR80 crores QoQ viewed as seasonal and reversible, consistent with prior year patterns; not seen as materially adding to risk.

risk_register.risk: Gold price volatility impacting LTV/margins on gold loan book
risk_register.note: Managed via VaR framework, 30-day moving average and partial standard deviation caps; tested during Jan/Feb gold price fall from $5,500 to $4,100/oz with successful margin calls.

risk_register.risk: Geopolitical stress (Middle East conflict) potentially raising slippages and credit cost
risk_register.note: Management expects both slippages and credit cost to deteriorate, not improve, though impact magnitude is 'unknown unknown'; no material change in customer behavior observed yet.

risk_register.risk: Treasury income volatility / market conditions
risk_register.note: Treasury income fell from INR77 crores in Q3 to almost nil in Q4 due to market conditions, described as a generic, industry-wide impact.

risk_register.risk: ECL transition accounting impact
risk_register.note: No material one-time or steady-state impact expected given declining SMA (0.6% of book) and PCR near 80%; no floating provisions currently held.

risk_register.risk: ECLGS guarantee claim recovery challenges
risk_register.note: Claiming the final 25% of ECLGS guarantee is a challenge as settlement with borrowers is disallowed under the scheme; full legal process required, otherwise even the first 75% collected must be returned.

risk_register.risk: NRI deposit market share / West Asia region concentration
risk_register.note: No stress seen from West Asia conflict; growth in NR deposits stepped up to 12% in FY26 from 7% in FY25, though historical market share loss cannot be ruled out due to lack of data.

risk_register.risk: Efficiency frontier limiting further cost optimization
risk_register.note: Management believes operating costs, kept largely flat for 8-10 quarters, cannot be reduced further and will need to rise with distribution and technology investment.

themes.label: NIM expansion trajectory
themes.note: NIM recovered to 3.23%, up 28bps QoQ and 20bps YoY, driven by deposit repricing, CASA growth and bulk deposit reduction; management expects hardening if rate cycle turns upward.

themes.label: Retail/MSME mix shift away from Corporate
themes.note: Corporate book rose to ~40% of loan book this quarter opportunistically despite a stated long-run goal of reducing it to ~30%; MSME growth was muted but expected to resume scale mode.

themes.label: Gold loan growth and risk management
themes.note: Gold loan book grew 43% YoY though QoQ growth was only 0.8% due to RBI-circular-driven runoff of bulk/co-lending arrangements; branch-led core growth remains solid.

themes.label: Asset quality improvement
themes.note: Gross NPA down 177bps YoY to 1.38%, Net NPA down to 26bps, PCR improved to 94.51% including write-off; SMA-1/2 rose seasonally but deemed reversible.

themes.label: Positive operating leverage / cost discipline
themes.note: Operating leverage was not positive this quarter but management still targets full-year positive operating leverage with opex growth guided at 5-6%.

themes.label: CEO succession uncertainty
themes.note: This was Seshadri's final earnings call as MD & CEO; he declined to give guidance that would bind his successor, and an investor questioned the bank's leadership stability.

themes.label: Geopolitical / external risk overhang
themes.note: Disturbances in West Asia cited as reason for favoring low-risk corporate exposure and factored into FY27 slippage guidance.

key_takeaways: The bank declared net profit of INR378 crores for quarter 1 FY '26-'27, registering a growth of 17% compared to INR322 crores in Q1 FY '25-'26.
Total deposits grew by 11% to INR125,817 crores from INR112,922 crores on a Y-o-Y basis. Retail deposits, which excludes bulk deposits, grew by 14% to INR124,306 crores from INR109,368 crores.
Gross Advances grew by 17% to INR104,368 crores from INR89,198 crores... if we were to exclude the impact of this [technical write-off], then the Y-o-Y growth is actually 18%.
Net interest margin for the quarter was 3.23%. With this, we have clawed back the dip in net interest margin that occurred as a consequence of the repo rate cuts.
Bank declared the highest ever net interest income in the quarter at INR1,025 crores, which is a growth of 23% compared to INR832 crores registered during Q1 FY '25, '26.
Capital adequacy ratio for the bank was at 19.62% and the Tier 1 ratio stands at 18.93% as on June 30, 2026.
Overall, gross NPA reduced by 177 basis points from 3.15% to 1.38% on a Y-o-Y basis. Net NPA reduced by 42 basis points from 68 basis points to 26 basis points.
The gold loan business grew by 43% and now stands at INR24,930 crores with an average LTV of 65.25% and an average ticket size of INR2.94 lakhs.
As many of you know, this is the last conference call that I will be attending in my current capacity as the Managing Director and CEO of South Indian Bank.
pressing_questions: With CRAR at 19.6% and legacy book cleaned up, what's the 3-year plan for deploying excess capital? And where do we see ROEs sustaining on a steady-state basis?
Why don't South Indian Bank is having a leadership stability? Previously, Mr. Murali also left in 3 years, and you're also leaving in 3 years?

quarters.summary: Management guided to loan growth of 15-16% in FY27 (matching or exceeding industry growth), expects NIMs to continue widening on asset-mix change and deposit repricing, believes credit cost has bottomed at 3 bps for the bank with slippages/credit costs likely to trend upwards given geopolitical stress, and reiterated commitment to positive operating leverage for a third consecutive year while planning selective branch expansion and product-mix shift toward Retail/MSME/Agri away from Corporate.

subsections.label: Other income / Treasury dip
points: Dip in other income mainly because of Treasury; market conditions in Q4 meant the bank was not able to generate much treasury income compared to INR77 crores in Q3, which fell to almost nil in Q4.
Treasury revenue softness described as a generic, industry-wide impact, not specific to the bank.

Management believes shift in business mix towards Retail and MSME (which generate significantly larger non-interest revenue than Corporate) will automatically increase non-interest income going forward.
Bank working on new solutions to increase non-interest revenue streams, including a new solution called 'TF Online' enabling corporate and MSME customers to engage on export/trade finance.
Substantial increase in FX revenue streams noted; enhancement of FX and trade platform planned to increase non-funded, fee-based engagement with customers.

subsections.label: Employee expense one-off
points: Employee expenses declined materially in the quarter due to a one-off write-back of approximately INR80 crores obtained based on year-end actuarial valuation, done in compliance with the Accounting Standard.

subsections.label: Technical write-off accounting
points: The INR1,163 crore (FY) / INR1,048 crore (Q4) technical write-off relates to accounts that have already been 100% provided for; this is not an actual bad-debt write-off.
There is no P&L impact from the technical write-off; the only impact is on the PCR (Provision Coverage Ratio) and gross NPA reduction, while net NPA is unaffected.
Of the Q4 gross NPA reduction of ~INR13 billion (vs INR3 billion in Q3), the technical write-off of INR1,048 crores was a major factor, with the balance being recovery.

subsections.label: Operating cost trajectory
points: Bank has kept operating costs largely flat for the last eight to ten quarters by 'sweating' assets to become more profitable and efficient.

Management believes an efficiency frontier is being approached, beyond which further efficiency gains become harder; expense growth is expected going forward due to planned investment in distribution and technology.
Bank aims to ensure expense growth is more than compensated for by revenue growth, sustaining positive operating leverage — achieved for two years running, targeted for a third.

subsections.label: Deposit cost dynamics
points: Around 60-65% of deposits are due for repricing during FY27 given the average tenor of the book; this is expected to benefit NIMs since these deposits were contracted at higher rates earlier.
Despite this, cost of deposits rose by 2-3 bps in Q4 because the bank slightly repriced deposit rates upward (as its rates were lower than competitors) to support deposit growth in some buckets.
Going forward, deposits contracted at higher rates in earlier years are yet to reprice and are expected to reprice at a lower current running rate, benefiting cost of deposits.

subsections.label: Distribution / cross-sell income
points: Share of distribution income (income from sale of third-party products) is still fairly low; partly attributed to the bank's own reticence to push such products aggressively, prioritizing customer trust.
Bank sells personal loans to its own customer base largely via pre-approved offers; loss rate on this book runs at approximately 3.5-4% against spreads of 11-12%.
Bank is underrepresented in salary-savings customers working at large corporations — an area of focus started about 18 months ago.

subsections.label: Other income breakup
points: Major items within the other income bucket (INR195 crores in Q4, INR760 crores for FY) include bancassurance income and recovery from technically written-off accounts; detailed breakup to be shared separately.

subsections.label: Gold loan portfolio growth and risk management
points: Gold loan book grew 46% in FY26, including portfolios purchased by the bank (portfolio buyout).
Average LTV of 57.18%; average ticket size approximately INR2.71 lakhs.
Bank uses a Value at Risk (VaR) framework to measure gold price volatility risk, stress-testing the portfolio for historical peak-to-trough gold price movements and setting caps on exposure.

During Jan/Feb, gold prices fell from a peak of $5,500/oz to about $4,100/oz, testing the bank's margin-call processes; customers whose margins eroded were identified and asked to repay or top up margin, with a large number of customers paying promptly; gold prices recovered before further action was needed for remaining customers.
Bank applies a 30-day moving average and a partial standard deviation (50% or 25% of one full standard deviation) to gold price volatility for risk mitigation rather than a flat LTV rupee cap.
Vast majority of gold loan book is organic; portfolio buyout/co-lending accounts for roughly 8-10% (previously stated as ~15%, then corrected downward in discussion).

Bank's total portfolio buyout across all products stood at roughly INR2,000 crores at end of last quarter; management now prefers pass-through certificates (PTCs) over portfolio buyouts due to credit enhancement benefits, having earlier favored buyouts to demonstrate portfolio growth.

subsections.label: Mortgage, auto and MSME loans
points: Mortgage loans and auto loans are other significant areas of focus, with significant year-on-year growth achieved in both.
MSME loan book grew approximately 15% for the year, driven by focus on better yield, better mix and better pricing discipline.

MSME growth strategy is to build depth (not width) in growth-supporting geographies and markets already entered recently, with concentrated resource allocation, investment in infrastructure and manpower.

Sequential decline of ~2% in MSME segment in Q4 was attributed to the MSME write-off of INR554 crores, not to any credit stress; on a gross basis MSME actually grew quarter-on-quarter (the net dip being roughly INR230-240 crores); no significant current stress visible in the MSME portfolio.

subsections.label: Old vs new book distinction
points: Old book now accounts for only about 12% of gross advances; management is internally debating whether the old/new distinction remains useful given losses across the board are low (Q4 slippage ratio only 15 bps).
Some old-book facilities are working-capital lines renewed annually, making run-off timing hard to predict; term facilities will amortize to term.
Bank reclassifies an old facility as new if enhanced limits are given; if lines are merely maintained, they remain classified as old.

subsections.label: Product mix target (Corporate vs Retail/MSME/Agri)
points: Management wants to bring the corporate book down from 38% to about a third (33%) of the total balance sheet over a 2-3 year period.

Within corporate, ultra-short-duration, lower-yielding assets (LC bills etc., currently 20-25% of the corporate book) are targeted to be reduced to roughly 10% of the corporate book; these ultra-short assets provide liquidity buffers but at very low yield.

The freed-up ~5% of portfolio is intended to move into Retail, MSME and Agriculture where spreads are significantly larger; specific growth numbers for each segment are tracked internally but not disclosed.

subsections.label: Non-resident (NRI) deposits
points: Non-resident deposits grew 12% in FY26 versus 7% in FY25, indicating stepped-up growth despite a representative office in the Gulf with small staff strength whose productivity has been rising.

Management is uncertain whether market share in NRI deposits has been lost historically, as SLBC market-share statistics for Kerala are not readily available, but believes recent performance has been significantly better.
As of FY23, GCC region accounted for ~80% of NRI deposits; the current (FY26) breakdown by region was not available on the call and will be shared subsequently.
No stress observed in NRI deposits due to West Asia conflict; if anything, a slightly enhanced level of activity in inward remittances and deposits has been observed.

subsections.label: Branch network strategy
points: Bank has focused on sweating existing branch assets to improve efficiency rather than aggressive branch expansion; total value addition from branches has doubled over the last eight to nine quarters, with more runway still available.
Branch count actually shrank from 955 to 948 over the last seven-eight quarters, i.e., no net branch growth recently.

Bank plans to selectively increase branches in areas of Southern India with low branch density, and has discussed at board level growing branches in Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Karnataka, Maharashtra, Gujarat and New Delhi — to be done deliberately while preserving efficiency gains.

Branch expansion will not be the only growth lever; alternate distribution mechanisms are being built out, including working with market participants like DSAs (Direct Selling Agents), which the bank had not previously used.

subsections.label: Digital distribution build-out
points: Bank launched a new digital offering called 'SIB RED', a full-fledged digital bank, towards the end of March.

Bank continues to build digital assets such as 'Fincredibles' and an active blog, which has a large number of followers, intended to attract digital-friendly customers as a hook for originating business.

subsections.label: Gold price volatility risk
points: Price volatility of gold is the key risk in the gold loan book; managed via a Value at Risk (VaR) framework with caps set on portfolio exposure based on historical peak-to-trough volatility (30-day VaR).
A real-life gold price movement could differ from historical patterns, meaning the VaR-based caps may not always hold, though management believes it is the only substantive method available.
Bank uses a 30-day moving average plus a partial (50% or 25%) standard deviation adjustment for risk mitigation, rather than a flat rupee-based LTV cap used by some peer banks.

subsections.label: Credit cost and slippage outlook
points: Management believes credit cost has bottomed at 3 bps for the quarter and does not expect it to go lower under normal organic circumstances.

Both slippages and credit cost are expected to trend upwards going forward, especially given geopolitical stresses emanating from the Middle East and elsewhere; management describes the ultimate impact as an 'unknown unknown' that is very hard to predict.

No material change in customer behavior has been observed so far, though the crisis is still young and effects take time to flow through; hypothesis is that both slippage and credit cost will deteriorate, not improve.

subsections.label: ECL transition impact
points: Bank currently holds no floating provisions in its books ahead of ECL (Expected Credit Loss) transition.
No material one-time impact expected from ECL transition, given declining SMA1+SMA2 trend (currently ~0.6% of total loan portfolio) and provision coverage ratio near 80%.
On a steady-state basis also, no material impact expected from ECL transition, assuming asset quality holds at current levels, though slight changes could occur depending on market conditions.

subsections.label: ECLGS scheme experience
points: Entire MSME portfolio is expected to qualify for the ECLGS scheme (ticket size capped at INR100 crores), though management has not fully reviewed the new scheme's terms.

Historically, ECLGS portfolio behaved similarly to the bank's core portfolio — no significant behavioral difference between ECLGS-availed and non-availed clients, other than non-availed clients being on a somewhat better footing from day one since they didn't need incremental credit.

Claiming the first 75% of ECLGS guarantee has generally been easy; claiming the remaining 25% has been more challenging because settlement with a borrower is not an allowed method under the ECLGS scheme — if a settlement is done, even the already-collected first 75% must be returned; legal process must be completed in full to claim the balance 25%.

The new scheme predominantly targets the airline segment and other MSME sectors; management does not currently see comparable stress on the portfolio as during the original COVID-era ECLGS 1 phase, and is unsure how much drawal will occur under the new scheme.

subsections.label: Loan growth outlook
points: Management aims to grow loan book at least at industry rate; current industry view is that next year's loan growth may be shallower than last year's, but the bank is still targeting 15-16% growth.
If industry growth is higher than the bank's target, the bank intends to match industry growth.

subsections.label: NIM outlook
points: NIM drivers for FY27 include change in asset mix (larger proportion of Retail and MSME vs low-margin Corporate) as the biggest driver, and potential rate hikes given the bank gives effect to RBI rate changes on a T+1 basis (making it the most impacted on the way down but the biggest beneficiary on the way up).
Bank is changing goal-setting methodology to include specific revenue goals (not just headline growth), pressuring front-end teams to price assets more appropriately.
NIM improved 6 bps in Q3 and 9 bps in Q4; management expects NIMs to continue widening with no reason foreseen for that trend to stop.
Repricing of ~60-65% of deposits during FY27 (contracted earlier at higher rates) expected to further support NIM.

subsections.label: Operating leverage / cost outlook
points: Bank aims to deliver positive operating leverage for a third consecutive year (achieved in the prior two years), even as expense growth is expected to resume due to planned investment in distribution and technology.

subsections.label: Succession planning
points: The Board is actively engaged in a CEO succession search process and is aware of the need to communicate names to RBI within the required timeframe; no material additional details on timeline were provided.
MD's term ends on 30th September; management expects the process to conclude such that a new incumbent can be in position before or immediately after the end of the current MD's term.

guidance_ledger.statement: We are still aiming to get between 15% and 16% loan growth; if the industry were to do higher than that, we will match industry.

NIMs will continue to widen; we don't see any reason why they should actually stop widening, driven by asset mix change, deposit repricing (60-65% of deposits due for repricing) and potential rate hikes.
Our aim is to ensure that we continue to have positive operating leverage; we'd like to make that a third year running.

guidance_ledger.metric: Corporate book share of balance sheet
guidance_ledger.statement: We would like to bring our corporate book down to about a third of our total balance sheet from the current 38%.
Within corporate, the ultra-short duration assets should go down from roughly 20-25% of the corporate book down to perhaps 10% of the book.
My own view is that we've seen the trough when it comes to credit cost... both slippages and credit cost should trend upwards, especially given the geopolitical stresses.
Expenses cannot be kept at this level indefinitely; you will see expense growth coming forward, but we are hopeful that will be more than compensated for by revenue growth.
I expect that all of this will happen in such a fashion that the new incumbent can be in position before or immediately after the end of my term (30th September).
We've been talking at the board level to grow branches in Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Karnataka, Maharashtra, Gujarat and New Delhi; there will be some growth, done very deliberately.
We don't estimate any material impact from ECL transition, either one-time or on a steady-state basis, given declining SMA numbers and PCR near 80%.

key_takeaways: The bank declared its highest ever net profit for the year at INR1,455 crores for the financial year 2025-2026, which implies a growth of 12% compared to INR1,303 crores in the prior year.
Total deposits grew by 15% to INR1,23,346 crores from INR1,07,526 crores.
Gross advances grew by 14.5% to INR1,00,274 crores from INR87,579 crores.
During the last financial year, we have done a technical write-off to the extent of INR1,163 crores, excluding which the year-on-year growth would be at 15.8%.
Net interest margin for the year was at 2.91%.
Provision coverage ratio, excluding write-off, improved by 810 basis points year-on-year to reach 79.87%, and PCR including write-off reached 94.10% at the end of the year.
Overall gross NPA reduced by 177 basis points from 3.2% to 1.43%. Net NPA reduced by 63 basis points from 0.92% to 0.29%.
During the last financial year, our gold loan business grew by 46% and now stands at INR24,729 crores with an average LTV of 57.18%.
This is the second year in which we've delivered positive operating leverage.
pressing_questions: Is there any search operation going for succession plan for the bank... how much time will it take or it may be internal person or from outside search is going on?
On gold prices and the portfolio impact: how do you control the LTV at the higher end when gold prices fluctuate significantly (e.g., a 20% fluctuation)?
At what rate do we intend to grow our loan book in FY27, assuming gold might not contribute so significantly the way it did in FY26?
What would be the NIM drivers going into FY27 considering we may see a rate hike at the fag end of the calendar/fiscal year?
The non-resident deposits as a percentage of total deposits have been coming down — are we losing market share in non-resident deposits?
What is the impact of the one-time transition impact of ECL and do we hold any buffer floating provisions for the same?
With respect to the MSME segment, there was a sequential decline close to 2% — any stress being witnessed on the MSME portfolio?

RATEGAIN.about: RateGain Travel Technologies Ltd is the leading distribution technology company globally and the largest Software as a Service (SaaS) provider in the travel and hospitality industry in India. The firm offers travel and hospitality services across different verticals like hotels, airlines, online travel agents, meta-search companies, package providers, car rentals, cruises, and ferries.[1]

quarters.summary: Q1 FY27 was a record quarter on scale and profitability, with operating revenue of INR 785 crore (+188% YoY, +9.7% QoQ) and Adjusted EBITDA of INR 193 crore (+289% YoY). Management raised FY27 guidance to the upper end of prior range — revenue ~INR 3,100 crore (~70% YoY growth) and Adjusted EBITDA margin of 22.5%–23.5% (raised from 21.5%–22.5%) — citing successful phase-1 integration, growth visibility, and expected further synergies as GTM accelerates. Deleveraging continues on track with a target to be net debt free by FY28, and FY27 priority shifts from integration to monetization, scaling enterprise adoption and deepening wallet share.

subsections.label: Record quarter on scale and profitability
points: Operating revenue INR 785 crore, +188% YoY (management also cited +187.6% YoY), +9.7% QoQ.
Annualized run-rate ~INR 3,140 crore.
Organic growth (combined entity) 17.5% YoY in INR terms, management confirmed.

Adjusted EBITDA management headline INR 193 crore (+289% YoY); CFO disclosed Adjusted PATDA/EBITDA INR 116.8 crore (14.9% margin) and reported PATDA INR 94.9 crore (12.1%). Transcript reflects mixed terminology; both anchored to the same quarter.
A one-time revenue uplift in Q1 of $2.5m from FIFA World Cup exposure; management expects this to normalize marginally going into Q2.

subsections.label: Earn-out / deferred consideration mechanics (Sojern)
points: Deferred consideration (contingent payout) will run at ~INR 80–90 crore/year through Q3 FY29.
Current quarter add-back INR 21.9 crore, consistent with INR 20–22 crore/quarter guidance.

subsections.label: Cash flow and deleveraging
points: Management: FCF conversion tends to improve later in the year; targeting ~75% conversion or better for FY27.
Debt repayment: additional $16m repaid 'yesterday'; total repaid $47.5m, i.e., 38% of acquisition debt raised in Nov 2025 for Sojern.
Outstanding debt: $77.5m; net debt INR 615.4 crore; cash & equivalents INR 255.6 crore.
Clear target: retire the balance and be net debt free by FY28.
CFO notes other income fell (INR 3.1 crore vs INR 20.7 crore YoY) because surplus cash was deployed into acquisition/deleveraging — 'structural relocation of capital.'

subsections.label: Martech (largest engine; now 81%+ of revenue) — Hotels/properties
points: Core proposition: direct bookings + marketing ROI, with a material portion outcome-based (management: 'we grow as our hotels grow').
Sojern Commission: new wins accelerated YoY, supported by a larger global GTM team.
Email channel newly introduced; 'strong early adoption' and expected lift to net revenue retention.

Bidding tech upgraded using ML models leveraging the expanded intent dataset; management cites 'meaningful increase' in performance — 'smarter bidding' driving more bookings and higher revenue per property.
Enterprise traction: 'healthy revenue uptick'; North America and co-op programs called out as strong.

subsections.label: Martech — Destinations / co-op programs
points: Differentiator: measurement/economic impact attribution — 'economic impact reports… in terms of visitor arrivals and economic impact, not just clicks or impressions.'
Goal: become the 'most trusted measurement partner for destinations anywhere in the world.'
Pricing power improving post-unification (see pricing section).

subsections.label: Martech — Corporate
points: Converting existing data partners into customers; one partner signed a two-year extension; others scaling spend.
Car rental momentum via collaboration with CAS team relationships — explicitly framed as a cross-sell opportunity.

subsections.label: APAC (early synergy proof point)
points: 'Strongest ever quarter' for new customer wins, +200% YoY.
Strong momentum in properties commission with record new properties in region.
Management: 'clearest early proof of the phase two go-to-market synergies.'

subsections.label: Distribution: moving from 'connectivity' to 'commerce optimization'
points: Buyer conversations shifting: 'beyond connectivity towards distribution optimization, profitability, and AI-native automation.'
Claimed customer outcomes: '30–40% optimization in ARI traffic' and better rate accuracy.

RateIQ adoption cited as resonating with enterprise chains connected to many OTAs; identifies which channels drive bookings and where revenue leaks (missing inventory, parity breaks, underperforming connections) and 'quantifies the commercial impact of each.'
Pipeline: management says they are 'on the verge of signing a very large customer in the Middle East' as a validation/catalyst.

Growth rate currently modest: CFO states distribution organic growth 3.1% YoY, but management expects newer launches (ARI identification + RateIQ) to translate to meaningful revenue in coming quarters and suggested distribution should show double-digit growth by fiscal year-end.

subsections.label: 'Direct stack' (booking engine + connectivity + payments)
points: Highlighted as proof of unified platform strategy and cross-sell growth lever, particularly in APAC with 'good traction.'
Management calls out large wins and strong pipeline in APAC due to sales infrastructure investments.

subsections.label: AirGain / Airlines; OTA; Car (dash/CAR commentary)
points: Airlines: key win Philippine Airlines partnership, strengthening SEA position — 'dominant provider with most of the region's major airlines.'
Cross-sell potential into performance marketing for airlines.
Product: AirGain's AI Digest live for all customers; extended into conversational analytics (positioning as 'AI first pricing intelligence').
OTA: renewed multi-year partnership with a leading global OTA; 'healthy volume growth.'
Car: strong engagement for Rev AI price recommendation; management claims a 'good size order book' building.

subsections.label: KPI/Reporting nuance investors should note (contract wins)
points: Management flagged a disclosure issue: reported contract wins (~INR 141 crore) are 'largely new logos' and exclude upsell/expansion with existing customers; thus, it may underrepresent commercial momentum, especially now with Sojern scale where many prospects are already customers in some form.
They intend to introduce better KPI reporting as lead indicators.

subsections.label: AI/product strategy: agentic roadmap and faster experimentation
points: Product strategy is explicitly 'agentic': 'build AI agents that do the actual work… a revenue manager agent, a distribution agent, a marketing agent.'
Start semi-autonomous, then move toward fully autonomous as customers gain comfort.
Strategic direction: from tools to 'the agent that actually does the job.'
New/expanded AI features: AI price visibility across Navigator/Parity — shows how hotel pricing appears on emerging AI-driven discovery/search platforms.
Parity Plus next-gen: AI-powered issue identification and prioritization + automates test bookings for enterprise.
Management claims AI has materially increased product velocity: 'the level of experimentation… has never been higher… one dollar of R&D… produce a lot more than it could pre-AI.'
Market thought leadership: featured in Skift coverage; management frames it as evidence they are shaping the narrative, not merely using AI.

key_figures.label: Buyer conversion outcome: optimization in ARI traffic

subsections.label: Strategic positioning: from 'travel tech platform' to an AI-led operating system
points: Management frames FY26 as a structural inflection: Sojern acquisition, unification of Adara under Sojern, and creation of the 'world's largest source of travel intent data.'
Current positioning: 'an AI-powered operating system for travel revenue growth, connecting demand generation, distribution, and revenue optimization on one platform.'
Claimed moat: 'No other player combines travel intent data at this scale, provides distribution infrastructure of this depth and an AI-powered commercial intelligence under one roof.'
FY27 priority shifts from integration to monetization: 'focus shifts decisively from integration to monetization, scaling enterprise adoption, deepening wallet share.'
Customer base: 14,000+ customers, with cross-sell highlighted as 'significant… with structure and urgency.'
Customer outcomes explicitly defined as: 'Acquire guests efficiently, engage them meaningfully, and expand wallet share over time.'

subsections.label: Pricing power, competitive dynamics, and GTM execution
points: Post Sojern–Adara unification, management reports reduced discounting pressure: 'need to discount is much lesser now… We can hold our price.'
Most evident in destinations, where competition is weaker: 'second and third… are distant… we are seeing weaknesses… one of them approached us to buy them out.'
Rather than overt price hikes, strategy is bundling: 'include some freebies… measurement products… [vs.] we're the only game in town, so you've got to pay more.'
Properties: negotiating higher outcome-based fees on a large India regional chain deal due to 'power of one platform.'
Deal velocity outlook: integration mostly complete, but property-side team unification in Europe/US still pending; management expects further acceleration as this completes.

subsections.label: Other notable disclosures
points: Airbnb not a threat: positioned as a customer, not competitor.
'Others' revenue category: monetization of travel intent audiences for non-travel brands (example: Visa/Mastercard targeting cohorts such as FIFA travelers).

subsections.label: M&A appetite
points: Management expects no deal in FY27; 'most likely… an event in 2027', emphasizing continued valuation discipline.

subsections.label: Headwinds / watch items explicitly mentioned
points: Q1 had one-offs (FIFA uplift) that will normalize in Q2.

Distribution organic growth currently low (3.1% YoY); management's thesis is that new AI-led products (ARI identification, RateIQ) and direct stack commercialization should shift it to double-digit by year-end, but this remains execution-dependent.
Management declined to break out Sojern vs legacy economics due to integration: 'very difficult to give attribution… unified teams… unified platform.'

points: Management revised FY27 guidance upward to the upper end of prior range: Revenue ~INR 3,100 crore for FY27 (stated as ~70% YoY growth, while still expecting double-digit organic growth).

Adjusted EBITDA margin: 22.5%–23.5% (raised from 21.5%–22.5%), citing successful phase-1 integration execution, growth visibility across combined entity, expectation of further synergies as GTM accelerates.
Reinvestment posture remains: will look to reinvest for growth consistent with '15–20%' near-to-mid-term aspiration.

themes.label: Distribution segment growth lag
themes.note: Distribution organic growth at 3.1% YoY remains modest, though management expects double-digit growth by fiscal year-end via ARI identification and RateIQ adoption.

key_takeaways: Record quarter on scale and profitability: Operating revenue INR 785 crore, +188% YoY, +9.7% QoQ; Adjusted EBITDA INR 193 crore (+289% YoY).
FY27 guidance raised to upper end of prior range: Revenue ~INR 3,100 crore (~70% YoY growth); Adjusted EBITDA margin 22.5%–23.5% (up from 21.5%–22.5%).
Deleveraging on track: $47.5m repaid (38% of Sojern acquisition debt), targeting net debt free by FY28; net debt INR 615.4 crore.
FY27 priority shifts decisively from integration to monetization, scaling enterprise adoption, deepening wallet share.
APAC called out as clearest early proof of phase two go-to-market synergies, with strongest ever quarter for new customer wins (+200% YoY).
Distribution organic growth currently modest at 3.1% YoY, but management expects double-digit growth by fiscal year-end driven by ARI identification and RateIQ.
Pricing power improving post Sojern-Adara unification, particularly in destinations where competition is weaker.
Management expects no M&A activity in FY27, with the next event likely in 2027.

quarters.summary: RateGain enters FY27 with strong momentum: Q1 FY27 revenue at an all-time high of INR785 crores (up 188% YoY), organic growth of 17.5% YoY, and record adjusted EBITDA margin of 24.6%. Management revised FY27 guidance upward — revenue to ~INR3,100 crores (70% YoY growth) and adjusted EBITDA margin to 22.5%-23.5% (up ~100bps from prior guidance) — citing successful Phase 1 Sojern integration, strong go-to-market synergy signs (especially in APMEA and Mya), and continued cross-sell potential across a 14,000+ customer base. Middle East disruption remains a headwind while a one-time $2.5 million FIFA World Cup revenue uplift is not expected to repeat at the same scale in Q2.
