subsections.label: Margin drivers
points: Adjusted EBITDA margin reflects the true operating margin of the business, adjusted to exclude deferred deal consideration payable to Sojern team over three years.
Deferred consideration will run at roughly INR80-90 crores a year and will be incurred up to Q3 FY29.
This quarter's add back was INR21.9 crores, consistent with the previously guided INR20-22 crores per quarter range.

subsections.label: EBITDA to PAT bridge
points: Amortization of acquisition cost increased sharply due to additional amortization related to the Sojern acquisition.
Finance costs reflect acquisition-related debt now on the books.
Other income declined as surplus cash previously earning interest was deployed towards the Sojern acquisition — described as a structural relocation of capital, not a recurring operational drag.

subsections.label: Cash flow and capital allocation
points: FCF generation typically improves as the year progresses; company on track for 75% conversion or better for the full year.
Additional $16 million debt repayment made a day before the call, taking cumulative repayment to 38% of total debt taken for the Sojern acquisition (November 2025).
Company remains on track to retire balance of acquisition-related debt and be net debt-free by FY28.

subsections.label: FIFA World Cup one-time impact on margins
points: One-time revenue uplift of $2.5 million in Q1 from FIFA World Cup positively impacted EBITDA in Q1 as well; expected to normalize marginally into Q2.
Net impact after accounting for ~$1 million Middle East headwind is roughly $1 million net uplift; at ~70% gross margins this translates to roughly $600,000-$700,000 EBITDA benefit.

subsections.label: Gross margin outlook
points: With increasing Martech mix, gross margin expected to remain around 70% in the near term.

Management would not commit to returning to previous ~75% gross margin level at this point, but indicated upside is possible depending on pricing power execution, particularly on the property side where bundling enables charging more.

DaaS segment organic growth (Q1 as referenced by Bhanu)
Distribution segment organic growth (Q1 as referenced by Bhanu)

subsections.label: Martech - Properties, Destinations, Corporate
points: Martech is the largest growth engine, now contributing over 81% of revenue; runs across properties, destinations, and corporate, with APMEA called out separately.
Proposition for hotels: drive direct bookings and improve marketing ROI; much of this business is outcome-based so revenue grows as hotels grow.
New wins on Sojern commission accelerated compared to last year with another strong quarter of new property additions, aided by a bigger global GTM team.
Email is a new channel recently introduced seeing strong early adoption, helping expand presence with customers and lift net revenue retention.

Bidding technology became significantly more sophisticated with ML models powered by expanded travel intent data driving real-time bidding decisions, translating into more bookings and higher revenue per property.
Strong traction continues with large enterprise brands and properties, with healthy revenue uptick YoY.

Destination segment had a strong quarter with healthy uptick around FIFA World Cup, healthy growth across key North American accounts and within co-op programs (jointly run marketing campaigns with destinations and travel supply partners).
Key differentiator in destinations is economic impact reports showing visitor arrivals and economic impact beyond clicks/impressions; goal to be the most trusted measurement partner for destinations.
In corporate: traction converting existing data partners into customers (a flywheel gaining momentum); one key partner signed a two-year extension; other larger brands scaling up spending.
Renewed momentum in car rental segment driven by closer collaboration with the DAAS team, opening cross-sell opportunity.

APMEA delivered its strongest ever quarter for new customer wins, up 200% YoY, and signed a record number of new properties on the properties commission product — seen as clearest early proof of phase-two go-to-market synergies.

subsections.label: Distribution
points: Strategic work of the past year translating into a stronger, more differentiated platform; enterprise conversations moving beyond connectivity toward distribution optimization, profitability, and AI-native automation.
Company increasingly positioned as a strategic, outcome-oriented infrastructure partner rather than just a connectivity provider.

Agentic ARI makes Uno the world's first channel manager built on intelligent distribution logic, prioritizing rate/inventory updates by booking urgency and commercial impact; hotels seeing 30-40% optimization in ARI traffic and better rate accuracy.
Enterprise customers increasingly adopting Agentic ARI alongside RateIQ.

RateIQ solves the problem of large chains connected to dozens of OTAs by using AI to show which channels drive bookings and where revenue is leaking (missing inventory, parity breaks, underperforming connections), quantifying commercial impact of each.

Uno Viva (Agentic AI voice platform) expanded from voice into multi-channel activation, now supports 50+ languages including WhatsApp; improved adoption/conversion with key customers; nearing signing of a very large Middle East customer.
Direct stack (booking engine + connectivity + payments) had a strong quarter with good traction in Mya, seen as proof point of unified platform strategy and a significant cross-sell/growth enabler.

Company expects distribution business to show double-digit growth by end of fiscal year, driven by RateIQ traction (uplift demonstrated to ~a dozen customers, all at different discussion stages) and the direct stack rollout, particularly strong wins in APMEA.

subsections.label: DAAS (Air, OTA, Car)
points: DAAS segment delivered steady, reliable performance in Q1 and continues to gain traction in key segments; described as a continued winner.
Philippine Airlines partnership strengthened position in Southeast Asia, where company is now the dominant provider with most of the region's major airline customers.
Strong cross-sell potential seen from airline customer base into Martech performance marketing product.
AirGain's AI Digest now live with all customers, extended into conversational analytics, positioning AirGain as an AI-first pricing intelligence platform.
Renewed partnership with one of the world's leading global OTAs for a multi-year term; continued deepening of presence across key accounts with healthy volume growth.
Car segment delivered strong performance with continued enterprise engagement and expansion discussions progressing for RevAI price recommendation product.
Anticipating some very large Airline segment deals which, if they come through, could significantly bump up DaaS revenue.
RevAI product (launched a couple years ago) finally seeing significant traction with a good-sized order book; monetization expected to further bump up DaaS revenue.
An experiment being run on the hotel side within DaaS that management will discuss further if it yields results.
OTA and Hotel segment within DaaS expected to stay steady.

subsections.label: New contract wins reporting caveat
points: Management flagged that the INR141 crores new contract win figure (combined Sojern + RateGain) largely represents new logos and does not account for upsizing of existing customers, so it understates true business wins.
Company is working on a better KPI/reporting methodology to give improved lead indicators on business wins; prior periods' reported new contract win figures share the same limitation.

Quarterly run-rate of new contract wins for Martech has hovered around INR96-98 crores despite ~25-30% YoY growth reported last year; distribution run-rate around INR50 crores, partly impacted by sunset of a sub-brand of an OTA.

subsections.label: AI strategy across products
points: Approach is to build AI agents that do the actual work of the industry: a revenue manager agent, a distribution agent, a marketing agent — beginning semi-autonomous and becoming fully autonomous as customers grow comfortable.
Today largely provide tools these teams use; direction is to provide the agent that actually does the job.
AI price visibility live across Navigator and Parity, letting hotels see how pricing shows up on emerging AI-driven search and discovery platforms.
Next generation of Parity Plus launched this quarter with AI-powered issue identification and prioritization, automating much of the test booking process for enterprise customers.
ChatGPT ads on property launched this quarter, capturing travel intent upstream as discovery shifts toward AI.
Uno Viva (CRS-integrated AI voice agent) supports 50+ languages across multiple channels including WhatsApp, recovering revenue from hotel calls that would otherwise go unanswered.
AirGain moved beyond search into conversational analytics, surfacing trends/anomalies/insights in natural language, with AI Digest now live for every customer.
Company featured in Skift's flagship coverage on AI and travel this quarter, positioning itself as a voice explaining what AI means for the industry.
AI embedded across commercial workflows spanning marketing, pricing, distribution, and guest engagement; building as an AI company from India for the world.

subsections.label: R&D velocity and pricing approach for new products
points: AI has expedited ability to bring new products to market; level of experimentation at RateGain described as never higher in the past 20 years.
AI allows $1 of R&D investment to produce much more output than pre-AI; challenge has shifted from building capability to speed of go-to-market.

Pricing for new products is a combination of outcome-based, subscription-based, and transactional-based models; company is A/B testing pricing methodology depending on product maturity to see what resonates with customers.

subsections.label: Regional demand dynamics
points: Travel demand held firm across major markets with the FIFA World Cup lifting activity in North America.

Middle East continues to face uncertainty/disruption; revenue from the region moved down from ~$970,000/month before disruption to ~$425,000/month today; remains a headwind but seen as a recovery opportunity as conditions stabilize.
FIFA World Cup and related destination campaigns provided a one-time revenue uplift of $2.5 million, not expected to repeat at the same scale in Q2.

APMEA is where FY27 go-to-market synergy thesis is playing out fastest, with strongest ever quarter for new customer wins (up 200% YoY) and record new property signings on properties commission product.
Southeast Asia: Philippine Airlines partnership strengthens position; company now dominant DAAS provider with most of the region's major airlines as customers.
India: company reported being about to sign a very large deal with a regional chain, negotiating higher outcome-based fees due to unified platform strength.
Property team unification completed in APAC; Europe and US property teams yet to be unified, with acceleration expected once that unification occurs.

subsections.label: Pricing power dynamics
points: Combination of factors driving pricing power: unification of Sojern and Adara reduced internal competition allowing the company to hold price rather than discount during negotiations.
On the destination side, second and third competitors are seen as distant and showing weakness; one competitor approached RateGain to be bought out.
Company avoiding straightforward price hikes in destinations (market perception risk) and instead bundling in measurement product freebies to position pricing power more subtly.
On the property side, unified platform enabled negotiation of higher outcome-based fees versus core fees, e.g., in a large regional chain deal in India.
Unification of Sojern and Adara data significantly enriched the platform's data, increasing marketing performance of ad dollars spent by customers.

Ability to bundle adjacent capabilities/products into one platform is appealing since most customers are not sophisticated and want a one-stop shop (unified Martech stack or full direct booking stack).

subsections.label: Cross-sell strategy
points: With more than 14,000 customers across combined business, cross-sell opportunity is significant and being pursued with structure and urgency.
Every product and commercial motion aligned to three customer outcomes: acquire guests efficiently, engage them meaningfully, expand wallet share over time.
Airline customer base within DAAS seen as strong cross-sell potential into Martech performance marketing product.
Renewed car rental momentum driven by closer collaboration with DAAS team, opening significant cross-sell opportunity.

subsections.label: Competitive positioning / market perception
points: Company positions itself as combining travel intent data scale, distribution infrastructure depth, and AI-powered commercial intelligence under one roof — no other player combines all three at this scale (described as a moat).
Media recognition: featured across Skift, CNBC, CNBC Asia on World Cup travel demand, positioning RateGain as becoming the definitive voice on travel demand, a position no competitor holds today.

Airbnb is viewed as a B2C vacation rental company and an actual customer (connectivity and DaaS solutions), not a competitor; RateGain expected to grow as Airbnb grows given the strategic partnership.

'Others' revenue contribution (6.5% of revenue) comes from travel intent data/cohort use cases sold to non-travel industries, e.g., credit card companies like Visa and MasterCard running campaigns targeting travelers (e.g., FIFA World Cup travelers).

subsections.label: Sojern integration progress
points: FY26 marked the structural inflection point with the Sojern acquisition, unification of Adara under the Sojern brand, and creation of the world's largest source of travel intent data.

Company transitioning from a travel technology platform (FY26 entry) to an AI-powered operating system for travel revenue growth (FY27), connecting demand generation, distribution, and revenue optimization on one platform.

First phase of Sojern integration — bringing companies together and delivering cost synergies — is complete and executed well; focus now shifts to second phase: revenue and go-to-market synergies, with early strong signs, most visibly at Mya.

People integration agenda across policies, processes, rewards, and systems is now substantially complete; focus has moved to scaling — a unified performance rhythm, an AI-native people ecosystem, and deeper leadership continuity across regions.

Difficult to attribute margin/revenue performance separately to Adara vs Sojern since teams and platforms have been fully unified; in some cases, Adara campaigns are being migrated onto Sojern platforms.

subsections.label: M&A outlook
points: Management confirmed M&A is being actively looked at even now given successful integration track record, but company remains judicious about valuation and targets.
No M&A expected to close this fiscal year; next M&A event most likely to occur in 2027.

subsections.label: Headwinds flagged
points: Middle East disruption continues to weigh on revenue, down from ~$970,000/month pre-disruption to ~$425,000/month currently; viewed as a headwind but also a recovery opportunity as conditions stabilize.
FIFA World Cup revenue uplift of $2.5 million in Q1 is a one-time item and not expected to repeat at the same scale in Q2, meaning growth normalizes going forward.

Attribution difficulty between Adara and Sojern contributions to margin/revenue synergy due to full team and platform unification, making it hard to isolate individual entity performance for external stakeholders.

subsections.label: Revised FY27 guidance rationale
points: Full-year revenue guidance revised to the upper end of the previously shared range, at around INR3,100 crores for FY27, signifying 70% YoY growth and capturing double-digit growth for the combined base.
Adjusted EBITDA margin guidance raised to 22.5%-23.5% for FY27, roughly 100 basis points (1 percentage point) higher than the earlier 21.5%-22.5% range.
Upward revision reflects successful execution of first phase of integration, growth visibility across combined entity, and further synergies expected as go-to-market accelerates.

Company will continue to reinvest into the business for higher growth, consistent with aspiration to grow at 15%-20% in the near to mid-medium term; nature of reinvestment differs for a B2B company vs B2C, focused on strengthening product and presence in key geographies.
Management indicated confidence that FY27 revenue guidance of INR3,100 crores is a number the company should 'definitely beat' rather than merely a target to be happy achieving.
Organic growth (INR terms) expected to trend toward the higher end of the 15%-20% range as the year progresses, particularly in Q3 and Q4, driven by acceleration of integration-related momentum.
Distribution business expected to show double-digit growth by end of fiscal year FY27.

themes.label: Sojern integration synergies

themes.label: Margin expansion

themes.label: Deleveraging / debt paydown

themes.label: Middle East demand disruption

themes.label: AI-native product velocity
themes.note: AI has expedited product development and launches (Agentic ARI, RateIQ, Parity Plus, ChatGPT ads on property, Uno Viva multi-channel) across the platform.

themes.label: Cross-sell and pricing power
themes.note: Unified Sojern/Adara data and platform enabling reduced discounting, bundled offerings, and cross-sell across 14,000+ combined customers.

themes.label: One-off event impact (FIFA World Cup)
themes.note: $2.5 million one-time revenue uplift from FIFA World Cup boosted Q1 but is not expected to repeat at the same scale in Q2.

key_takeaways: For Q1 FY27, we reported our highest ever quarterly operating revenue of INR785 crores, up 188% year-on-year.
Our annualized revenue run rate now stands at a new all-time high of INR3,140 crores.
Our organic revenue growth for the combined entity stood at 17.5% year-on-year.
Our adjusted EBITDA margin stood at 24.6%, another record margin with our adjusted EBITDA coming at INR193 crores, up 189% compared to the same period last year.
We now expect full-year revenue to come in at the upper end of the range we shared with you last quarter, around INR3,100 crores for FY27... growth of 70% year-on-year.
We now expect adjusted EBITDA margins of between 22.5% to 23.5% for FY27, roughly 100 basis points or 1 percentage point uplift from the earlier 21.5% to 22.5% range.
We have made an additional repayment of $16 million on our outstanding debt yesterday and now have repaid 38% of our total debt taken in November 2025 for the Sojern acquisition.
APMEA delivered its strongest ever quarter for new customer wins, up 200% year-on-year.
pressing_questions: Considering that a lot of the people integration is largely behind us, do you think that we should start seeing better deal velocity?

So, then in that case, even for full year FY27, your revised guidance of 3,100 crores, is it fair to say it's more like a number you would definitely beat rather than a number you'll be happy achieving?
What would be the margin benefit from this incremental USD1.5 million in that 24.6% adjusted number that you have reported?

There is one-off impact... mathematically, there is an external entity that has come and latched on to RateGain... So that external entity is right now at nearly 30% EBITDA margin. Is that a fair statement to make?
Would it be possible to call out X of Sojern? What was our Martech growth this quarter?

Is it fair to say that with increasing Martech mix, 70% is kind of the range that we will settle at or can we go back to the previous 75% number? And on the M&A side, would it be something that we will again start looking out for by the end of this year, given that we are pre-paying a lot of debt?

DATAMATICS.about: Datamatics is a Digital Technologies, Digital Operations, and Digital Experiences company that enables enterprises to go Deep in Digital to boost their productivity, customer experience and competitive advantage. Datamatics enables enterprises to combine various relevant Digital Technologies to improve productivity and customer experience to build sustainable competitive advantage[1]

quarters.summary: Datamatics started FY27 on a positive note with Q1 FY27 revenue growth of 9.9% YoY to INR 513.9 crores and EBITDA margin expansion of 343 bps to 19.7%, driven by AI-first strategy and disciplined cost management. Management reiterated high single-digit revenue growth guidance for FY27 citing continued market softness from geopolitical/war-related uncertainty, while targeting EBITDA margins of ~19-20% for the year and a 3-year revenue target of ~INR 3,000 crores (organic + inorganic) from a current base of ~INR 2,000 crores.

key_figures.label: EBITDA growth YoY (as restated by CFO)
Net cash and investments (net of debt)

subsections.label: Cost items
points: Annual salary increments were rolled out effective April 2026, and the impact has been accounted for during the quarter.

AI R&D investment is expensed at approximately INR 40-50 crores a year; management plans to sustain this level for the current year given the pace of change in AI technology and ongoing platform investments.

If the INR 40-50 crores AI R&D investment is added back, EBITDA margin on Digital Technologies practice would be materially healthier since all investments are fundamentally booked into the technology service area.

subsections.label: Cash balance clarification
points: The reported INR 710.2 crores net cash and investments (net of debt) pertains to quarter-end (30 June 2026) and is BEFORE the INR 200 crores TNQTech payout, which occurred in the subsequent (current) quarter.

subsections.label: Capital allocation
points: Company is in dialogue with some companies from an M&A standpoint; no conversation has matured to a reportable level.
No specific plan for a buyback was confirmed; cash could be used for better allocation such as acquisitions.

subsections.label: Margin trajectory
points: Across the board, company is at about 19% EBITDA margin currently, with an expected ~0.5% improvement this financial year, targeting closer to 20%.
Some practices (e.g., Digital Experiences) are showing an upswing due to good deal wins in this financial year.
Digital Technologies EBITDA margin appears lower partly because all R&D/tech investments are booked into that service area; adjusting for this shows a fairly healthy margin across the board.

key_figures.label: Lumina Datamatics global ranking in digital content outsourcing
EBITDA margin range for TNQTech/Lumina publishing businesses

subsections.label: Digital Operations
points: Revenue and margin pickup noted by an analyst; growth driven partly by TNQTech integration which is already embedded in Digital Operations segment reporting.
TNQTech is growing healthily; going forward focus should be on the Digital Content space (part of Digital Operations) as an integrated offering.

subsections.label: Digital Technologies
points: Segment has had muted growth alongside margin pressure over past few periods per an analyst observation.
Good traction seen on KAi underwriting solution and KAiSDLC/KAiBRE solutions for enterprise/legacy modernization; projects already kicked off with encouraging customer response.
AI-powered legacy modernization tools reduce risk and timeline significantly (e.g., a 3-year project can potentially be done in 6 months).
Underwriting solution is getting good response; company in dialogue with all top insurance companies in India, and some good ones in the U.S. and Europe.

Operations and Technologies are increasingly converging — operations understand business processes, technology understands tech, and combining both delivers maximum customer value; this makes segment separation more difficult over time.
Underwriting product revenue booking has started with the first customer, with a few more expected soon; product will be recognized within Digital Technologies.

subsections.label: Digital Experiences
points: Segment revenue declined YoY, but seeing an upswing due to some good deal wins signed in this financial year.

subsections.label: Industry footprint / client concentration
points: Education and Publishing is the largest segment by revenue contribution, followed by Technology & Consulting, BFSI, Manufacturing & Logistics, Retail, and Not-for-profit & Government.
Client concentration remains healthy across top 5/10/20 clients.

subsections.label: AI-led deal wins
points: Majority of new deals won this year have been on the back of AI capabilities.

Recent AI-led wins include: SBI Life Insurance selecting Datamatics TruAI underwriting for agentic AI-powered automation in underwriting operations; an American pet wellness and veterinary care provider expanding engagement to deploy an AI-powered voice agent; a leading American consumer product company selecting Datamatics KAiBRE and KAiSDLC (agentic AI-powered solutions) to extract and transform complex legacy business logic for application modernization.

subsections.label: TNQTech integration
points: Integration of TNQTech into Lumina Datamatics is now complete.
Combined organization has strengthened capabilities and continues to show healthy growth.
Company has reinforced its position as a global leader, ranking among the top three digital content outsourcing companies in the world.

subsections.label: Competitive landscape
points: Management does not see large IT services players like Persistent or Coforge as direct competitors in the customer base they target.
Competitive situations are increasingly arising from well-funded local AI/auto-tech companies bringing new technology solutions to market.
Increasing competition also comes from customers' internal tech teams and captives (GCCs), as many companies are setting up their own captives in India and experimenting with AI internally.
Start-up ecosystem is well-funded and brings interesting solutions, posing a competitive challenge.

subsections.label: Customer sector focus
points: Company remains focused on its core sectors (insurance, banking/BFSI, logistics, etc.) rather than actively diversifying into new sectors, though it may opportunistically pick up deals outside core focus areas when they arise.

subsections.label: Customer spending patterns
points: No major pattern shift observed across verticals or geographies (U.S., Europe); customers are increasingly engaging with AI and automation investment.
Some degree of market softness persists.
Projects are trending toward smaller-tenure engagements (3, 6, 9 months) versus traditional large multi-year annuity deals, driven by AI project characteristics.
Despite shorter project tenures, overall deal sizes are actually increasing; margins remain stable with no major shrinkage.

subsections.label: M&A
points: Company is in dialogue with some companies from an M&A perspective; no deal has matured to a reportable stage.
Future growth (3-year ~INR 3,000 crore target) expected to be a mixture of organic and inorganic growth, including bolt-on acquisitions.

subsections.label: TNQTech integration completion
points: Integration of TNQTech into Lumina Datamatics is now complete, strengthening capabilities and contributing to healthy growth; this consolidated Datamatics' position among the top three digital content outsourcing companies globally.

subsections.label: Market softness
points: There is still a degree of softness in the market because of the ongoing war and related geopolitical uncertainties, which fluctuate day to day.
Management believes the global economy needs to stabilize; once war-related uncertainty settles, the environment should become more stable.

subsections.label: Customer automation / insourcing
points: Key risk: customers are increasingly automating in-house and may choose not to outsource automation to third parties like Datamatics, which would shrink outsourcing budgets and pressure companies across the Indian outsourcing industry.
Second key risk: customers moving toward setting up their own captives (GCCs), reducing reliance on outsourcing vendors.

subsections.label: Revenue growth guidance
points: Company has projected and is maintaining a high single-digit revenue growth guidance for FY27, despite Q1 FY27 revenue growth of 9.9% YoY, due to continued market softness from war-related uncertainty.

Analyst noted apparent inconsistency between strong Q1 growth (43% Y-o-Y, referring to PAT growth, clarified by CFO) versus full-year high single-digit guidance; CFO clarified the 9.9% figure is revenue growth while 43% pertains to PAT growth.

subsections.label: 3-year revenue target
points: Management is targeting roughly INR 3,000 crores in revenue within a 3-year window (starting from the current year, FY27), up from a current base of roughly INR 2,000 crores.
This target is expected to be a mixture of organic growth and inorganic (M&A) growth.
Management cautions that due to the pace of AI-driven transformation across the outsourcing/BPO/tech industry, it is hard to predict exactly where the company will end up.

subsections.label: EBITDA margin guidance
points: Company expects to maintain EBITDA margins in the range of 19% to 20% by year-end FY27, with roughly 0.5 percentage point improvement expected this financial year over the current ~19% level.

subsections.label: R&D spend outlook
points: AI R&D investment will be maintained at approximately the same level (INR 40-50 crores/year) for FY27; budget for next year is yet to be determined given the fast pace of change in AI, to be decided during next year's planning cycle.

subsections.label: Revenue growth drivers
points: Key drivers to accelerate revenue growth toward the INR 3,000 crore target include how well AI-based platforms take off — agentic underwriting, claim processing, KAiBRE, KAiSDLC, and SuperCX (contact center/front office automation) — plus some degree of bolt-on acquisitions.

guidance_ledger.statement: We have projected a high single-digit growth in our guidance. We are maintaining that.

We are looking at about a 3-year window of about INR 3,000-odd crores. We are about INR 2,000 crores right now roughly. So, we are looking at roughly in that range... a mixture of organic and inorganic growth.
We are looking at about, roughly 0.5% improvement in this financial year. So, we should be hitting closer to 20% this financial year... We are roughly maintaining the same 19% to 20% EBITDA margins.
We will keep it at approximately the same level because right now, there's a lot happening in that space... So, we will sustain it at the same levels for this year.
I'm quite bullish on the Digital Technologies. Also, the underwriting solutions that we built is getting a good response... I'm very confident that, that will give us a good revenue stream.

risk_register.risk: Market softness due to war-related geopolitical uncertainty
risk_register.note: Management flagged continued softness in the market due to ongoing war and uncertainty, with unpredictable day-to-day developments; global economy needs to stabilize.

risk_register.risk: Customer in-house automation reducing outsourcing budgets
risk_register.note: If customers automate themselves and choose not to outsource automation to third parties, outsourcing budgets could shrink, pressuring companies in the Indian outsourcing industry.

risk_register.risk: Customer shift toward captives (GCCs)
risk_register.note: Organizations increasingly setting up their own captives/GCCs, which could reduce reliance on outsourcing vendors like Datamatics.

risk_register.risk: Competitive pressure from well-funded AI/auto-tech startups and internal tech teams/GCCs
risk_register.note: Management sees more competition from local well-funded auto-tech companies and customers' internal tech teams/captives than from larger IT players like Persistent or Coforge.

themes.label: AI-first strategy / AI-led deal wins
themes.note: Majority of new deals won this year, and ~60% of FY27 deal wins, have been AI-led or AI-driven, including SBI Life underwriting, voice agent, and legacy modernization (KAiBRE/KAiSDLC) wins.

themes.label: Margin expansion
themes.note: EBITDA margin expanded 343 bps YoY to 19.7% in Q1 FY27; company targets ~19-20% margins with ~0.5pp improvement for FY27.

themes.label: TNQTech/Lumina Datamatics integration
themes.note: TNQTech integration into Lumina Datamatics is complete, strengthening capabilities and healthy growth; company ranks top 3 globally in digital content outsourcing.

themes.label: Macro/geopolitical softness
themes.note: Management flagged continued market softness tied to war-related uncertainty impacting demand, cited as reason for maintaining conservative high single-digit FY27 revenue guidance despite strong Q1.

themes.label: Captive/insourcing and automation risk
themes.note: Key risks flagged: customers automating in-house and reducing outsourcing spend, and customers setting up their own captives (GCCs), both potentially shrinking outsourcing budgets.

themes.label: M&A / inorganic growth
themes.note: Company in dialogue with potential M&A targets (none matured yet); 3-year INR 3,000 crore revenue target expected to be a mix of organic and inorganic growth.

themes.label: Digital Technologies platform build-out
themes.note: Digital Technologies revenue growth was muted (6.1% YoY) with lower EBIT margin (8.9%) partly due to R&D investment being booked there, but management is bullish on underwriting/KAi platforms gaining traction with first customer revenue booked.

key_takeaways: Our revenue for Q1 FY27 grew at 9.9% on a year-on-year basis to INR 513.9 crores.
EBITDA for the quarter stood at INR 101.1 crores, representing a 31.1% year-on-year increase, while our EBITDA margins improved by 343 basis points to 19.7%.

We are seeing strong market validation of our AI-first strategy. Customers are increasingly choosing Datamatics for our ability to combine AI innovation with execution excellence, enabling us to win larger, higher-value engagements across both existing and new customers.
The majority of the new deals we have won this year have been on the back of our AI capabilities.

I am pleased to announce that the integration of TNQTech into Lumina Datamatics is now complete. The combined organization has strengthened our capabilities and continues to show healthy growth. We have firmly reinforced our position as a global leader and rank amongst the top three digital content outsourcing companies in the world.
So, we have projected a high single-digit growth in our guidance. We are maintaining that. There is still a degree of softness in the market because of the war and the uncertainties.
We are looking at about a 3-year window of about INR 3,000-odd crores. We are about INR 2,000 crores right now roughly.
We are roughly maintaining the same 19% to 20% EBITDA margins.
pressing_questions: So, we expensed approximately INR 40 crores to INR 50 crores a year as AI R&D investment. So, what would be the guidance there for this year? Are we expending more or less this year as well?

So, we have reported INR 710 crores approx cash balances. This is before the INR 200 crores TNQTech payout? ... So, is there a plan for a buyback, or will that be used for a better allocation like from acquisition?
And last question, would we report segment-wise data for AI as a service sooner or later, since we are ramping up there?

So, is this growth trajectory going to continue? What sort of growth can we see for the whole year FY27? ... you're giving a single-digit growth guidance for the whole year seems a little inconsistent, which is because of some seasonality where H1 is more dominating than H2. Is that the case?
And our TNQTech integration is fully completed, what sort of revenue did TNQTech complemented in Q1?
Do we have any like a 5-year blueprint on where does the company want to reach by the year 2032 or say, 2030 in terms of margins or in terms of net profit in any of these metrics?
What are the key factors required to accelerate this revenue growth from here on? ... What will be the key revenue drivers?
And what can go wrong in this, if you say like in FY27 or in next 1 year, what can go wrong? What are the risks here for us?
How are the customer spending patterns evolving in different verticals in different geographies like U.S. and Europe? Are we seeing any changes?

STYL.about: Incorporated in 1993, Seshaasai Technologies Limited is a technology-driven, multi-location solutions provider, specializing in payment solutions, communications, and fulfilment services.[1]

quarters.summary: Q1 FY27 revenue grew 21.1% YoY to INR 377 crores (down 6.9% QoQ, seasonally weaker H1), with EBITDA margin at 25.1% (up 135 bps YoY) despite gross margin compression to 41.7% from higher input/geopolitical costs. Management reiterated a medium-term revenue growth target of 8%-12% YoY, expects H2 FY27 to be stronger than H1 on seasonal BFSI pickup and IoT momentum, and continues to defer specific margin guidance citing macro/geopolitical uncertainty, while expecting margin improvement via operating leverage and product mix in H2.

subsections.label: Revenue and margin drivers
points: Revenue moderated sequentially versus Q4 FY26 because Q4 is historically the strongest quarter in terms of revenue; the QoQ decline should be viewed from that perspective.
Gross margin moderated as cost of materials consumed increased faster than revenue, driven by material cost mix pressure from rising geopolitical issues.

Traditionally H1 revenues are lower than H2 revenues, and hence higher costs (COMC) show in H1; due to product mix and operating leverage, COMC would be lower in H2, as played out in Q4 of last financial year.
Despite gross margin pressure, disciplined management of employee and other operating costs supported EBITDA profitability.
PBT growth was supported by operating growth and a substantial reduction in finance cost.

Input cost impact on COGS in Q1 was predominantly attributable to war-related factors: ~40-45% directly attributable to currency, and the remainder due to direct impact of the war on input costs (commodity pricing, logistics, freight cost).

subsections.label: Balance sheet and capital allocation
points: Company remains well-capitalized with healthy cash and cash equivalents.
IPO proceeds utilization remains in line with the stated objects of the issue.
Healthy margins, strong balance sheet, and diversified revenue streams provide a solid platform to support the next phase of growth.

key_figures.label: Value of two multi-year PSU bank tenders won

subsections.label: Tender wins
points: Won two multi-year tenders from leading PSU banks in the quarter, representing approximately INR 73 crores in revenue over the tender period.

subsections.label: Order book / pipeline visibility
points: Business is essentially back-to-back, with demand being put to the company by customers; current guidance for the year is based on the visibility customers have given.
Company has a steady order pipeline basis on which annual guidance was given; further order pipeline updates to be shared in coming quarters.
Healthy demand seen across key verticals, supported by deeper customer engagement, increasing adoption of technology-led solutions, and strong momentum in non-payment businesses.

subsections.label: Payment solutions
points: Continues to see healthy demand and deeper customer engagement; strong relationships and proven execution capability continue to support business momentum.

Premium metal card business continues to gain strong traction and remains an important growth driver; increasing adoption from banks and Fintech partners seeking to enhance customer engagement and differentiate premium offerings.
Metal card category offers superior margins and strengthens position in the high-value card issuance market.
Encouraging traction from global markets, particularly Europe and Africa, providing an additional avenue for growth; company has just begun nascent stages of exporting cards to Africa and Europe.
Growth build-up viewed as both volume-driven and value-driven (premiumization, sustainability offerings, Gen Z/wealth segment demand) for existing volume.
UPI impact on card issuances viewed as largely played out; UPI transaction volumes rising but UPI user base growth has reached near-saturation, undermining further erosion risk.

Company is more concerned with card issuances than transaction volumes on cards; credit cards retain value proposition via issuer benefits/discounts/schemes that UPI doesn't offer; debit card holders tend to keep a card in addition to UPI usage.
Government contemplating MDR on UPI transactions above a threshold, which could narrow the difference between UPI and card economics since MDR would then apply to both.
Customer volume forecasts underlying business plans have already factored in the UPI impact/aspect.

Not looking to expand into payment gateway/aggregator space; company's strategy is focused on logical adjacencies within its current high-end technology, compliance-moat, physical-product, scalable, decentralized business model rather than new infrastructure-heavy areas.

subsections.label: Communication and fulfilment solutions
points: Delivered steady performance backed by recurring requirements from BFSI, enterprise, and government customers.

Indian enterprises continuing to invest in digitalization, automation, cloud-led communication infrastructure, and secure customer engagement platforms, providing strong relevance for the company's solutions.
Segment continues to provide stability to overall business and supports the objective of building a more balanced revenue mix.

subsections.label: IoT solutions
points: Remained a key growth driver during the quarter; RFID continues to emerge as a significant long-term opportunity across retail, logistics, pharmaceuticals, food supply chains, and manufacturing adopting RFID-led traceability and automation.
Market seen as still in early stages of adoption, offering substantial headroom for growth.
Strategy focused on moving beyond standalone RFID tags towards integrated end-to-end traceability solutions combining hardware, software, data intelligence, and supply chain orchestration.

Particularly excited about pharmaceutical traceability opportunity, driven by regulatory requirements, product authentication needs, and supply chain visibility; progress made through customer engagements, pilot projects, and infrastructure readiness.

Continued progress in SIM and eSIM businesses; following successful commercial rollout of SIM card production, strengthening engagements with telecom operators and expanding presence in digital connectivity ecosystem.
Currently serving ~20-25% of a large (third-largest) telecom operator's requirement for pre- and post-paid SIMs, built over the last four to five months.
Unique certification stack, secure personalization capabilities, and integrated eSIM platform position the company to capitalize on growing eSIM adoption and enterprise IoT applications.

IoT growth in Q1 (145% YoY) looks exaggerated partly because Q1 and Q2 of last year were relatively weak for IoT, while Q3 and Q4 last year were strong; growth traction and plan remain intact, not signaling a slowdown; expect IoT to still contribute close to 15% to 18% of revenue by year-end.

subsections.label: Margin comparison across verticals
points: Margins are not separately disclosed per vertical due to multiple adjacencies and common costs across the three verticals; blended EBITDA margin came in at close to 25% this quarter.
Payment solutions and IoT margins are more or less similar; communication and fulfilment margin is slightly lower.

subsections.label: Insurance client base movement
points: Decline in number of insurance clients (life insurance from 13 to 10, general insurance from 9 to 7) reflects churn of customers who were doing very nominal/almost zero business with the company as they moved fully digital.
None of the specific churned customers went in for a re-tender; company has not lost any material business as churned relationships had very nominal business value historically.

subsections.label: Facility expansion
points: Nagpur and Bengaluru facilities are still under construction.
Bengaluru facility expected to be operational by end of calendar year after necessary regulatory approvals.

Bengaluru greenfield facility for metal cards is almost in the ready state; company will move into certification and compliance processing, expected to be in that process by Q4; facility should be operational before end of calendar year, adding significantly to metal card capacity.
Capacity expansion underway at Bengaluru facility to meet growing demand for metal cards; company well-positioned to support both domestic and international opportunities in this space.

subsections.label: Capacity utilization dynamics
points: Capacity utilization is cyclical; higher utilization (85-90%) occurs during customer renewal cycle demands or month-end loads, while average utilization is 65-70%.

Capex plan for FY27 to maintain the range previously stated (INR 140-160 crores per year), using IPO proceeds as per stated objects, to reinforce position across all three verticals and deepen capacities for future growth.

subsections.label: Global market traction
points: Encouraging traction from global markets in payment solutions, particularly Europe and Africa, providing an additional avenue for growth going forward.

Company has just begun the very nascent stages of exporting cards from India to Africa and Europe; plans to leverage India manufacturing advantage in premium products to further fuel growth via this channel.

subsections.label: Chip pricing and inventory strategy
points: Chip prices procured in the first calendar quarter remained largely flattish in USD terms YoY, with some marginal price improvement more than offset by the dollar/currency impact (chip pricing is always in USD).

Strategy over the last couple of quarters has been to increase inventory holding of chips for both IoT and payment solutions businesses, allowing the company to secure better pricing via inventory holding, reflected in working capital days.

No clear price impact seen yet from suppliers, but lead times from suppliers have increased; company has a forward bias that pricing could be different sometime next year but has no clear indications yet; situation being watched closely, with appropriate action to be taken (supply chain management and customer engagement) if upward price revisions occur.

subsections.label: Supply chain agility
points: Management focused on strengthening supply chain agility through diversified sourcing and strategic inventory management to respond effectively to changing market conditions and ensure business continuity.

subsections.label: Customer base and relationships
points: Top 10 customers contributed almost 56% of revenues, and more than 95% of revenues came from existing clients, showcasing stickiness of client relationships and strong renewal/repeat business characteristics of the business model.

subsections.label: UPI vs. cards competitive dynamics
points: Company views UPI as not directly impacting card issuances since it is more concerned with issuances than transaction volumes; credit and debit cards retain distinct value propositions (issuer benefits, alliance discounts, schemes) not offered by UPI.
UPI user base growth has reached near-saturation even as transaction volumes rise, supporting the view that the UPI impact on cards has largely played out.
Potential future MDR on UPI transactions above a certain threshold (under government consideration) could narrow the economic difference between UPI and cards.

subsections.label: Strategic focus / adjacencies
points: Company's approach to new businesses is to focus on high-end technology with a compliance or technology moat, involving a physical product that can scale over time on a decentralized basis.

Not pursuing entry into payment gateway/aggregator space, as that market already has established players; instead focusing R&D and energy on logical adjacencies within current product offerings that leverage existing infrastructure and resources.

subsections.label: Growth and investment focus
points: Continued investment in innovation, automation, and technology capabilities to support long-term growth across businesses.
Continued investment in future-ready technologies to drive the next phase of growth journey; company remains committed to creating long-term value for stakeholders.

subsections.label: Macro and geopolitical headwinds
points: Operating environment impacted by geopolitical uncertainties, currency fluctuations, and cost pressures, which may create near-term headwinds.
Rising geopolitical issues put pressure on gross margins via the material cost mix in the quarter.

Input cost escalation attributed predominantly to war-related impact: ~40-45% directly attributable to currency, remainder from direct impact of the war on commodity pricing, logistics, and freight costs.
Company is actively working with customers on price revisions and taking steps to protect margins and maintain healthy profitability in response to these headwinds.

Macroeconomic situation, order book, execution timelines, capacity utilization, geopolitical situation, and input cost escalation cited as moving parts not fully within company's control, cited as reason for not giving precise margin guidance.

subsections.label: Regulatory risk
points: Government contemplating applying MDR on UPI transactions above certain threshold, which is a factor being monitored regarding payment solutions economics.

subsections.label: Supply chain / input cost risk
points: Lead times from chip suppliers have increased; no clear price impact seen yet but company holds a forward bias that pricing could change next year; situation being watched closely.

key_figures.label: Expected IoT revenue contribution by year-end

subsections.label: Revenue growth guidance
points: Medium-term target of delivering revenue growth of 8% to 12% YoY, supported by diversified revenue mix, recurring business base, strong customer relationships, and focus on future-ready technologies.
H2 FY27 expected to be stronger than H1, driven by seasonal pickup in BFSI demand, steady momentum in communication and fulfilment businesses, and continued growth in the IoT segment.

subsections.label: Margin guidance approach
points: As a matter of practice, company does not put out specific EBITDA or PAT margin numbers; instead offers visibility on drivers (order book, execution timelines, capacity utilization) rather than outcomes, citing that precise numbers would be 'false precision' given macro/geopolitical uncertainty and input cost escalation not within company's control.
Company commits to transparently sharing quarter-on-quarter how factors affecting margins play out, providing input parameter building blocks rather than specific margin figures.

Expect no dramatic change in margin numbers from current levels, but operating leverage and improved H2 product mix should provide a positive bias to margins going forward, assuming the macroeconomic situation does not deteriorate further.
Q1 margin outcome should not necessarily be seen as the base for the full year, since margin depends on evolving operating leverage and product mix through the year.

subsections.label: Segment growth guidance
points: IoT business expected to grow at a similar pace to last year's ~45% YoY growth in the current year; in the following year (FY28), growth expected to moderate to a range of 35% to 40% due to a higher base.
Communication and fulfilment solutions business expected to remain in the flattish range for coming years (achieved close to 30% growth last year).

Payment solutions business growth driver factored in at about 10% to 12% growth CAGR; expect decent growth over this year and next, evolving with product mix and other opportunities; overall internal plan of close to 12% CAGR as indicated earlier in the year.
IoT expected to still contribute close to 15% to 18% of revenue by end of year despite exaggerated-looking Q1 growth due to weak year-ago base.

subsections.label: Capacity/Bengaluru facility contribution outlook
points: Bengaluru facility expected to commercialize by end of this calendar year; management expects it will contribute meaningfully to revenue from FY28 onwards, with a hope for some contribution even in the current year, though too early to quantify.

key_takeaways: We are pleased to report a strong start to FY27 with a superb revenue growth of 21.1% on Y-o-Y basis reflecting the strength of our diversified business model and continued execution of our strategic priorities.

While the quarter witnessed some pressure on gross margins from the material cost mix due to rising geopolitical issues, however, disciplined execution and operating efficiencies enabled us to deliver growth in EBITDA and maintain healthy margins.
In this quarter, we won two multi-year tenders from leading PSU banks, which represent approximately INR 73 crores in revenue over the tender period.
Our payment solutions contributed 42% to total revenue in Q1 FY27 and saw a nominal growth of 5% on Y-o-Y basis.
Communication and fulfillment solutions contributed 40% to total revenue in Q1 FY27 and witnessed a growth of 13% on Y-o-Y basis.
IoT solutions contributed 18% to total revenue in Q1 FY27 and witnessed a growth of 145% on Y-o-Y basis.
These strengths support our medium-term target of delivering revenue growth of 8% to 12%.
In Q1 FY27, our revenue from operations stood at INR 377 crores, up 21.1% Y-o-Y and down 6.9% Q-o-Q.
EBITDA for the quarter came in at INR 94 crores with an EBITDA margin of 25.1%, an increase of 135 bps Y-o-Y.
Our PAT for the quarter stood at INR 60 crores, registering a growth of 63.8% Y-o-Y with margin at 16%, up 418 bps Y-o-Y.
The top 10 customers contributed almost 56% of our revenues, and more than 95% of our revenues came from existing clients.
pressing_questions: So, we have performed really well on a year-on-year basis, so how should we look at the whole year in terms of revenue and margins?
So basically, on the gross margin part... can we pass on these cost to the customers? Also, what would be the expected gross margins for the full financial year 2027?
You have indicated in the last call, that margins will be maintained at current levels. So, do we assume that Q1 could be a base for the current year?
The Bengaluru facility that is going to commercialize by end of this year, can we expect meaningful revenues from FY '28? Would you like to quantify or give us any targets?
When you look at the payment solution business, how much is the chip prices up on a Y-o-Y basis, and at what pricing do we have the inventory currently?

quarters.summary: Q4 FY'26 revenue grew 8.1% QoQ / 9.6% YoY to ~INR 404-405 crore with EBITDA margin at 30.8% (up 330bps YoY) and PAT margin at 20.2% (up 316bps YoY), driven by stronger execution, communication & fulfilment and IoT growth. FY'26 revenue declined 1.5% YoY to INR 1,441 crore due to payment solutions moderation, offset by CFS and IoT growth, with EBITDA margin at 27.4% (up 204bps) and PAT margin at 16.7% (up 146bps). Management declined to give formal FY'27 guidance citing geopolitical/macro uncertainty, deferring to post-Q1 FY'27, but expects IoT growth to match/exceed FY'26's 47% and payment card business to bottom out and improve; capex of INR 160-200 crore planned across Payment Solutions, IoT and modernization.

subsections.label: Margin drivers
points: Gross margin improvement in Q4 driven by procurement consolidation, advanced inventory planning aligned to global trade cycles, and more efficient vendor payments, causing 7-8% savings at material consumed level for the full year.
In Q4 specifically, adverse foreign exchange movement had an impact, but materials procured in early Q4/late Q3 combined with higher sales versus Q3 delivered operating leverage benefits.
EBITDA and PAT margin improvement driven by: gross margin improvement, reduction in finance cost in H2 following debt repayment post-IPO, and interest income earned in H2 post IPO funds.
PAT margin improvement also aided by lower finance costs following debt repayment post-IPO, resulting in improved earnings conversion.

subsections.label: Working capital
points: Net working capital days have been rising over the last two years; this partly reflects inventory build-up to navigate global supply challenges in Q1 and Q4, and post-IPO cash sitting on balance sheet giving a lopsided picture.
Inventory positions and trade receivables are broadly in line with the business and are being continuously monitored and improved.

subsections.label: Capital allocation / IPO utilization
points: IPO proceeds utilization remains in line with stated objects of the issue; Q4 funds utilized towards capex, GCP, and issue expenses.
Capex plan of INR 160-200 crore for FY27 across Payment Solutions and IoT verticals plus overall modernization, part funded from IPO proceeds.

Capital allocation guiding themes remain consistent across verticals: businesses with recurring revenue, technology need, scalability, and mandatory/needed products for end customers; going forward allocation toward software/technology resources will increase as IoT deepens.

subsections.label: Payment Solutions
points: Segment impacted by broader industry factors: moderation in issuance volumes from PSU and Private banks, lower renewal card volumes due to lower base year issuance during COVID-19 period, timing differences in renewal cycles, and tighter regulatory/compliance environments for banks and fintechs.
Company has not lost a single customer and added 21 new customers across banks and fintechs.

Strong trends in premiumization, increasing opportunities in transit ecosystems, and strengthening pipeline in advanced card products such as metal cards, biometric cards, and other secure chip form factors; expect gradual improvement in volumes as banking cycles normalize.

First Indian card manufacturer to file metal card patents (Oct 2021) and first to receive global payment scheme approvals for metal cards (March 2023); patent for metal cards granted Feb 2026, reflecting continued focus on product innovation, R&D, and IP creation.
Won a multi-year tender from a leading PSU bank representing approx INR 8.7 crore in revenue over the tender period.
Domestic payment scheme RFP and global fintech RFP for metal card variants still under process and evaluation.

Payment card business driven by four revenue drivers: renewal cards (majority of volume), new cards on account opening, credit cards per bank issuance policy, and transit/fintech program cards (forex cards etc.).

Renewal cycles impacted post-COVID (March 2020 lull for 1-1.5 years) and banks rationalizing renewal processes; surge seen in FY21-22, FY22-23; management expects renewal numbers should improve versus COVID-impacted levels.
New card issuance and credit cards depend on bank strategy for onboarding, risk mitigation on unsecured lending, and regulatory risk weight changes on unsecured credit card portfolios.

Company seeking to premiumize offerings (metal cards, logistics services) and has traction in transit programs: working with partners on three state government projects for free transport to citizens/beneficiaries, and metro card projects.
Management expects payment card business to bottom out and see upward trajectory going forward.
Metal card currently ~4% of payment solutions business, expected to improve in coming year.
Non-BFSI portion of payment card business (system integrators for transit projects, forex/gift cards) is close to ~4% of total payment card business.

Payment cards market share was 31.6% (per FY25 industry data); company aims to remain relevant to evolving customer needs by 2030 via premiumization, metal cards, biometric card certification, sustainability (recycled PVC, wooden cards), and new form factors (feature phone automation for large PSU banks under NDA).

Company works with banks on Mudra cards, Kisan Credit Cards, financial inclusion cards as service provider; works as system integrator on transit programs for students, senior citizens, veterans, women beneficiaries; evaluating pilot projects for single card platforms across multiple state government benefits (conceptual stage).

subsections.label: Communication and Fulfilment Solutions
points: Evolved into a technology-driven integrated solutions platform combining secure communication, fulfilment digital workflow orchestration, traceability, and logistics integration capabilities.

Backed by proprietary platforms RUBIC, eTaTrak, and IOMS, and pan-India execution infrastructure; positioned as strategic partner for large-scale, secure, time-sensitive communication and fulfilment requirements.
Benefits from strong customer relationships, operational scalability, and recurring business opportunities; important contributor to growth, profitability, and cash flow profile.
Added close to 8 new customers in FY26; management sees possible marginal decline ahead but overall comfortable.

subsections.label: IoT Solutions
points: IoT gaining traction as long-term growth engine driven by increasing adoption of RFID, growing importance of traceability across supply chains, and rising demand for sensor-based/platform-led ecosystems.

Momentum building in project for one of the largest Indian retailers across major fashion brands using integrated RFID, Bluetooth and sensor-based analytics; traction seen across retail, renewable, healthcare, power generation, and GCC industries.

Bengaluru facility received GSMA SAS-UP certification for SIM/eSIM manufacturing, personalization, data generation, PKI certificate handling — one of few global players with these integrated capabilities.
SIM card division started contributing materially to revenue in Q4 FY26; already working with a leading telecom player to supply SIM cards.

eSIM commercial production yet to start; expected once integration processes and final compliance leg are completed (one more process to finish by July-August), with eSIM revenue expected from H2 of the year.

Growth plans: expansion into apparel-adjacent categories (cosmetics, accessories) for large retail customers; localization of inlay manufacturing to reduce import dependence, leveraging local chip bonding infrastructure; targeting Tier 2 retailers following demonstrated ROI with Tier 1; harmonized Bluetooth/GPS/RFID technologies for warehousing/logistics visibility solutions.
IoT business grew 45-48% YoY in FY26 (cited as 45% by Pragnyat in business update and ~47-48% in Q&A); management expects FY27 growth to at least match, if not exceed, this pace.

Product mix improvements driven by working toward premiumization and end-to-end value chain capture (e.g., logistics services) across payment and CFS businesses; metal card cited as a growth engine contributing to better margins.

New sectors targeted: grocery and pharma (globally growing themes, India lag of ~12-18 months expected; small POCs already underway in pharma given India's role as pharma outsourcing hub); textile traceability opportunity linked to EU/UK FTA and EU Digital Passport (EUDP) requirements — mixed opportunity between conventional traceability and RFID depending on value/criticality of goods.

Company on Walmart's approved vendor list for RFID; exploring global market via partners after establishing domestic case studies; RFID frequency ranges vary by country; competitiveness rests on antenna design/simulation, R&D labs, test benches, and in-house semiconductor chip bonding capability built over 2.5 years.

Rolled out asset-handling software (Bluetooth + RFID) for a large government power-generating company on a 10 sq km plant under construction, integrated across handheld devices and cloud; calibrated approach with specific use cases now stable, moving toward larger ecosystem rollouts.
SIM is a nascent business currently at ~30% capacity utilization of stated capacity; installed SIM capacity is about 7 million SIMs/month.
eSIM: conceptually capable of producing about 2-2.5 million units/month, but form factor variability could range 2-3 million eSIMs/month depending on product; commercial production not yet started.
RFID capacity utilization averaged ~70% for the year, with spike to ~80-85% utilization during Q4.

Inlay manufacturing equipment in place for 2.5 years; company scaled up during IPO process to now have 3 plants capable of inlay manufacturing; working on RFID inlays for solar market and innovative products in cosmetics/healthcare; better margins expected versus buying inlay from third parties once scale is reached.

key_figures.label: Global payment scheme approval for metal cards received

subsections.label: Patents and IP
points: Filed for 6 new patents in FY26 across products and solutions, taking total tally to 19 patent applications filed, of which 5 have been granted to date.

Metal card patent process: filed October 2021 (protection begins from filing date, not grant date); company has been selling patent-protected metal card products for the last 3 years regardless of grant timing; patent granted February 2026 makes it a bigger enabler now in protecting against IP transgression/violation by others, though it was not viewed as a major business enabler previously since protection already existed since filing.

Patent regime clarified: a granted patent protects the specific novelty/process used; it does not prevent others from producing similar products via their own distinct innovation/novelty, provided they comply with their own defined process.

subsections.label: eSIM technology explainer
points: eSIMs are components embedded in device/equipment/vehicle circuitry (unlike regular SIM cards) requiring personalization and embedded top-up profile layer per device usage, aligned to GSMA global interoperability standards; form factor can be changed/embedded per customer environment.
Example use case: electric smart meters where eSIM sits inside circuitry enabling direct communication with power distribution company, eliminating manual meter reading.

key_figures.label: Navi Mumbai and Kundli facilities operational
Top raw material categories consumed used for sourcing optimization

subsections.label: Facilities
points: Navi Mumbai and Kundli facilities became operational in Q4 FY26.
Nagpur and Bengaluru facilities are still under construction.
Bengaluru facility received GSMA SAS-UP certification for SIM/eSIM manufacturing and personalization during the quarter.

subsections.label: Inlay manufacturing / backward integration
points: Equipment for inlay manufacturing in place for 2.5 years, handling nano wafers onto RFID antennas — sophisticated and intricate process.
Scaled up manufacturing as part of IPO process; now has 3 plants capable of inlay manufacturing.

Backward integration into inlay manufacturing viewed as strategic tool to increase market share, profitability, and reduce import dependence amid supply chain constraints, cost/pricing volatility from currency fluctuation.
Currently working on own RFID inlays for solar market plus innovative cosmetics/healthcare products; better margins expected once meaningful scale is reached versus buying inlay from third parties.
Backward integration into semiconductor chips for payment solutions business is a question management deferred, to be shared once good progress is made.

subsections.label: International expansion
points: Company does not have significant export revenue currently; working on evolving product portfolios for international markets.

Working with partners in other countries on a back-to-back basis for local opportunities rather than opening own personalization bureau; no plans to open an overseas personalization bureau in the current year.
Deepening focus on international opportunities in FY27, especially niche IoT and Payment Solutions products.

Some large overseas fintech players have shortlisted the company in their global RFP; opportunities under evaluation for the last 4-5 months with expected positive outcomes but no revenue visibility yet.
Domestic payment scheme RFP and global fintech RFP for metal card variants still under process and evaluation.

subsections.label: Sourcing and procurement
points: Multiple management initiatives implemented for top 50% of raw material categories, including procurement consolidation, advanced inventory planning aligned to global trade cycles, and more efficient vendor payments, delivering 7-8% savings at material consumed level for full year.
Inventory build-up undertaken to better navigate global supply chain challenges expected in Q1 and Q4.

subsections.label: Customer strategy
points: Deep customer engagement across banking, BFSI, government, enterprise, retail, logistics, telecom, and technology ecosystems sustains recurring revenues, increases wallet share, enables cross-sell of integrated solutions, and expands into adjacent offerings.
Not lost any major account across verticals; added 21 new accounts in payment business, 65 new customers in IoT business, and 8 new customers in CFS business in FY26.
Approach to competitiveness: focus first on domestic market, build case studies, then explore global market via partners.

Long-term vision by 2030: continuous innovation to remain relevant to evolving customer/payment landscape needs (premiumization, biometric/sustainable cards, new form factors) to be a sizeable value contributor in the payment ecosystem.

key_figures.label: Recurring revenue as percentage of total revenue

subsections.label: Business transformation and diversification
points: FY26 was a landmark year as the company completed its listing (IPO) during the year.
FY26 marked as a year of transformation and transition — deliberate efforts to diversify business, strengthen technology-led capabilities, and build future-ready platforms across key verticals.

Continued investment in innovation, automation, premiumization, and new growth platforms, with strengthened focus on recurring and technology-driven businesses, reflecting transition toward a solutions-oriented, platform-led organization.

~97-98% of revenue is recurring in nature, driven by ongoing card issuance programs, regulatory/compliance-driven communication requirements, fulfilment engagements, and repeat ordering cycles in RFID/IoT solutions.

Capital allocation guiding themes across 25-year history: preference for businesses with recurring revenue, technology need, scalability, and mandatory/needed products for end customers; capex infrastructure/equipment/tech platforms largely common across verticals, with allocation toward software/technology resources expected to increase as IoT deepens.
Management reaffirms unchanged value proposition and business focus pre- and post-IPO; no loss of business intensity or focus.

subsections.label: Headwinds flagged
points: Global macroeconomic and geopolitical uncertainties including supply chain disruptions, currency volatility, and broader demand conditions flagged as risks for FY27.

Payment Solutions segment impacted by moderation in issuance volumes from PSU/Private banks, lower renewal card volumes due to lower base year issuance during COVID-19, timing differences in renewal cycles, and tighter regulatory/compliance environments for banks and fintechs.
Adverse foreign exchange movement impacted Q4 margins, given import-dependent cost base.
Rising input prices across materials and currency volatility cited as factors management wants more visibility on before providing margin guidance.
Bank strategies on risk mitigation for unsecured lending and regulatory increase in risk weights assigned to unsecured credit card portfolios affect new card/credit card issuance.

subsections.label: Outlook commentary
points: Management remains cautiously optimistic for FY27 while mindful of global macroeconomic and geopolitical uncertainties (supply chain disruptions, currency volatility, demand conditions); diversified business model, strong customer relationships, recurring revenue base, and continued investment in future-ready technologies seen as positioning the company well.
Formal FY27 revenue/segment guidance deferred; management prefers to wait until after Q1 FY27 for better visibility given geopolitical situation and uncertainty.
Margin guidance for FY27/FY28 also deferred pending more clarity on currency fluctuation, input cost trends, and supply chain challenges.
IoT business expected to grow at least at the same pace as FY26 (47-48% YoY), if not better, in FY27.
Communication and Fulfilment Solutions business expected to see some stability, with possible marginal decline, which management is comfortable with.
Payment card / metal card business expected to show good growth visibility for the coming year as banking cycles normalize.
eSIM revenues expected to start contributing from H2 of the year once integration and compliance processes are completed.
Capex plan of INR 160-200 crore for FY27 across Payment Solutions and IoT verticals plus overall modernization, partly funded via IPO proceeds.

guidance_ledger.statement: At this point in time, it's difficult to give guidance for FY '27, considering the macroeconomic environment; will revisit at end of Q1

Plan of investing close to about INR 160 crores to INR 200-odd crores through the year across Payment Solutions and IoT business verticals, as well as overall modernization, of which some funds would come from IPO fund
Current business outlook for IoT business in FY27 — expect numbers should be definitely better than this year; should be definitely growing upward of 47% in the IoT business
We see some stability in our communication and fulfilment business. There could be a marginal decline, but overall we are fine with that

guidance_ledger.metric: Payment card / metal card business growth
guidance_ledger.statement: We have good visibility this year in terms of growing that business as well as the base payment card business

Due to the current geopolitical situation, macroeconomic factors, currency fluctuation, and supply challenges, we probably would not want to give any guidance at this stage; will set guidance once more visibility is achieved
We expect eSIM revenues to help us from H2 of this year
Whatever is the payment landscape by 2030, Seshaasai would be a sizeable value contributor in that ecosystem

guidance_ledger.metric: Metal card mix in payment business
guidance_ledger.statement: Metal card overall in our payment solution business contributes close to about 4% in the payment [business], and we see that hopefully to improve in the coming year

themes.label: IoT scale-up
themes.note: IoT solutions grew 45-48% YoY in FY26 contributing 11-12.4% of revenue, with SIM division starting to contribute materially and eSIM commercialization expected in H2; management expects at least similar growth in FY27.

themes.label: Payment card volume moderation
themes.note: Payment Solutions (~50% of FY26 revenue) impacted by PSU/Private bank issuance moderation and lower renewal volumes post-COVID base effect; management expects bottoming out and gradual improvement.

themes.label: Margin expansion
themes.note: EBITDA margin up 330bps YoY to 30.8% and PAT margin up 316bps YoY to 20.2% in Q4, driven by procurement savings, operating leverage, lower finance costs post-IPO debt repayment, and interest income.

themes.label: Backward integration / inlay manufacturing
themes.note: Company scaled to 3 inlay manufacturing plants; viewed as strategic tool to increase market share, profitability, and reduce import dependence amid supply chain constraints.

themes.label: IPO capital deployment
themes.note: Company utilized INR 405 crore of total INR 600 crore IPO/pre-IPO funds by end FY26; balance INR 195 crore planned for subsequent periods including FY27 capex of INR 160-200 crore.

themes.label: Guidance deferral amid macro uncertainty
themes.note: Management repeatedly declined to give formal FY27 revenue/segment/margin guidance citing geopolitical and macroeconomic uncertainty, deferring to post-Q1 FY27.

themes.label: Patent and IP creation
themes.note: Metal card patent granted in Feb 2026 (filed Oct 2021), taking total patent applications to 19 with 5 granted; reinforces product innovation and IP protection strategy.

key_takeaways: During the quarter, we reported revenue from operations of INR 404 crore, reflecting a growth of 8.1% sequentially and 9.6% on a Y-o-Y basis.
Moving to the full year FY '26 performance, we reported revenue from operations of INR 1,441.1 crores, a drop of 1.5% on Y-o-Y basis.

Around 97% to 98% of our revenue is recurring in nature, driven by ongoing card issuance programs, regulatory and compliance-driven communication requirements, fulfilment engagements, and repeat ordering cycles in RFID and IoT solutions.
We have filed for six new patents in FY '26 across products and solutions, taking the total tally to 19 patent applications filed, out of which 5 have been granted to date.
EBITDA for the quarter came in at approximately INR 125 crores, with an EBITDA margin of 30.8%, an increase of 330 bps Y-o-Y.
Our PAT for the quarter stood at approximately INR 82 crores, with the PAT margin at 20.2%, up 316 bps Y-o-Y.
The top 10 customers contributed almost 62.8% of our revenue, and more than 96.6% of our revenues came from existing customers.
As of 31st March 2026, we had cash and cash equivalents of approximately INR 398 crores, including unutilized IPO funds of approximately INR 195 crores.
The Board of Directors has recommended a dividend of INR 2.5 per share.
