Any quantification on how you see the margins scaling up over the next year, 1.5 years with SIM/eSIM contribution? (Management deferred specific quantification, citing need to watch FX and input price evolution)

RKFORGE.about: Ramkrishna Forgings Ltd is primarily engaged in manufacturing and sale of forged components of automobiles, railway wagons & coaches and engineering parts. [1][2] It is the 2nd largest forging player in India.[3]

quarters.summary: Management reported strong Q1 FY27 operational/financial performance with revenue growth, EBITDA margin improvement, and continued order momentum. Forward outlook: guidance for ~20% plus export growth, ROCE build-up to 20% in FY28, net debt reduction to ~Rs.1,500 crores by FY27 end, FY29 revenue target of Rs.8,000 crores (22-25% CAGR over next 3 years), continued utilization ramp-up across forging/casting/cold forging/press capacities, and gradual margin improvement, with meaningful aerospace/non-ferrous (titanium, Inconel, aluminum) revenue contribution expected only after 2 years (8-10 quarters).

key_figures.label: Operational cash flow after working capital (last year)

subsections.label: Revenue & Margin Drivers
points: EBITDA margin improved to 17.96% from 17.11% in previous quarter reflecting better operating leverage and improved product mix.

Gross margin rose 535 bps QoQ but EBITDA margin rose only 85 bps QoQ; management attributed the gap mainly to energy cost and shipping cost that could not be passed on, not merely price revisions — better product mix also contributed to gross margin gains.

Rupee depreciation of 1-1.5% in the quarter is entirely passed on to customers via currency pass-on contract clauses, so currency movement (appreciation or depreciation) does not materially affect margins.
Domestic realization jump QoQ attributed to mix change toward higher-margin, higher-realization products driven by improved utilization, not a specific single segment.

subsections.label: Subsidiaries Performance
points: Subsidiary margins only marginally better (50-100 bps higher) than previous quarter; the apparent jump to 21% from 16% is largely due to higher elimination effects.
Depreciation in subsidiaries increased due to capitalization of completed projects in Q4, and this higher depreciation level will continue going forward.

subsections.label: Balance Sheet & Working Capital
points: Working capital showed elevation in the quarter due to West Asia crisis-related shipping cost/transit time impacts, but improvement journey to continue going forward.

Internal targets: improve debtor days by 5-10 days, inventory days by another 5 days, and increase creditor days by another 10 days — cumulative improvement of 15-20 days, expected to take about a year (roughly 10 days per year over two years) rather than one or two quarters.
Operational cash flow after working capital for last year (FY26) was about Rs.840 crores, described as highest in company history.

subsections.label: Capital Allocation
points: Company to continue prudent capital allocation — reduce leverage while deploying adequate capital toward growth investments and maintenance capex.
Majority of strategic capex now behind the company; focus shifting to sweating existing assets via higher utilization, improved asset turn and operating leverage.
Total capex guidance for the year is around Rs.350 crores, including Rs.20-30 crores further investment into the Rail JV (first phase almost complete).

key_figures.label: Passenger vehicle share of Rs.278 cr orders
Two-wheeler share of Rs.278 cr orders
New orders from Metro segment (Indian Railways)
PV segment ICE vs EV split

subsections.label: Order Wins Detail
points: Healthy order inflows during the quarter reflecting sustained customer confidence in manufacturing capabilities, engineering expertise, and execution track record.

Of the Rs.278 crores automobile orders, entire business is domestic; the 18% two-wheeler business is a domestic brand crankshaft business from the Gurugram machining facility, and the 82% passenger vehicle order is also for the domestic market.
Rs.15 crores new orders won from Metro segment of Indian Railways.
The order announced (Rs.228 crores referenced) is completely from EV, specifically domestic EV manufacturers, not export.

Passenger vehicle segment overall order book is roughly 50% ICE and 50% EV; current sales skew more to EV but bulk ICE supplies are starting, and the split is expected to stabilize near 50-50 going forward.
Non-automotive share of order book continues to improve, reflecting strategic focus on building a more balanced business portfolio.
Demand supported by healthy investment activity across infrastructure, industrial manufacturing, and commercial vehicles.
Customer discussions across North America and Europe have become increasingly constructive compared to a year ago.

Management confident of sustaining healthy order momentum next two years (FY27, FY28); current order book described as 'flooded' with new RFQ inflows; incremental demand cited as the biggest challenge currently faced.
For next two years, passenger vehicle, oil & gas, and non-auto sectors like earthmoving equipment are cited as giving extreme confidence for tangible non-CV/non-auto growth.

subsections.label: Wheel JV / Rail Business
points: 80,000 confirmed wheel order from Indian Railways for manufacturing passenger trains, locomotives and Vande Bharat (wagons not included).
JV partners have an additional obligation of close to 25,000 wheels, taking total utilization commitment to close to 1,10,000 wheels, which will keep the plant occupied till end of FY28.
Beyond FY28, company working with export customers beyond Europe and North America for additional wheel demand traction; names not disclosed yet.

JV partners can only buy wheels for private-sector wagons they manufacture; for Indian Railways-owned wagon builders, cast wheels are supplied free-of-cost (FOC) by Indian Railways' own Bangalore facility, so RKFL cannot supply more to that segment.
Management could not comment on overall Indian market annual wagon/casting wheel demand size.

Rail wheel plant (RKTR) trial production has started; company expects to submit first 300 wheel samples to Indian Railways for testing in August; bulk production and full-fledged supply to Railways expected to start by September-October.

Railway business outside the JV is entirely separate — RKFL has its own significant standalone order book for railways which is continuously growing; the JV covers only wheel manufacturing and nothing else.

subsections.label: Mexico Project
points: Production has started at the Mexico facility; ~Rs.6 crores revenue recognized in Q1 FY27.
Significant revenue contribution from Mexico expected to start from Q3 FY27 onward.

subsections.label: Casting Division
points: Casting plant was capitalized last quarter (per March stock exchange release); production has started but plant remains work-in-progress, with gradual capacity ramp-up expected over the next three quarters.

Casting division realizations came off QoQ; management called this a one-off — new capacity ramp-up led to production of some components at sub-optimal realization purely to build utilization; realization expected to recover to previous or better levels in coming quarters.

subsections.label: Cold Forging
points: Company working diligently to improve cold forging capacity utilization; expects to cross 70% utilization by Q3.

key_figures.label: Press capacity utilization target (post new press line)
Peak capacity utilization guidance (before next capex)

subsections.label: Utilization Ramp-up
points: Production ramp-up across new forging and casting facilities continues as planned; majority of strategic capex now behind, focus shifted to sweating assets via higher utilization and asset turn.
Overall forging/casting utilization expected to improve gradually every quarter, as demonstrated by strong Q1 utilization and top-line growth.

Ring rolling capacity already running at 127% utilization; no plans to add further ring rolling capacity — management expects to sustain near-peak utilization for next two to three years given current order book.
New press line being added at current 60% utilization; press line capacity build takes at least four to five quarters, by which time company expects to be at ~80% press utilization.
Capacity addition decisions are based on order book and customer confirmations, not merely current utilization levels.
Company expects to run at 75-80% overall capacity utilization before needing next major capex.

subsections.label: Non-Ferrous / New Capability Build
points: Non-ferrous capability build for aluminum, titanium, Inconel and nimonic grade forgings for aerospace, robotics and semiconductors already underway; aluminum forging has already reached bulk production.

Stainless steel and Inconel/titanium capability still work-in-progress; heating arrangements being added, no major capex required for current RFQs — incremental capex expected in range of Rs.10-15 crores, at most Rs.20 crores for near-term needs; significant additional capex only required once business scales meaningfully.
No major capex decisions will be announced until end of FY28, pending clearer order book visibility and approvals in new verticals (aerospace, semiconductors, robotics).

subsections.label: Net Block / Capacity Potential
points: On current net block of ~Rs.3,700 crores (including casting under capitalization), asset turn of 2.5x implies potential sales of ~Rs.9,000 crores at 100% capacity utilization, though 100% utilization is considered impractical; realistic sustainable utilization target is 75-80%.

key_figures.label: Export revenue share target (full year, consolidated)

subsections.label: Export Markets
points: International business recorded further improvement in the quarter, led by stronger demand from North America, alongside improving customer engagement and order execution across Europe.
Tariff-related developments remain an area of close attention, but the operating environment has become considerably more stable, providing greater visibility and confidence across export markets.
Management expects one of the best years ever for RKFL export revenue, both from North America and Europe, driven by new order wins from existing and new customers.
Cannot comment on customer names/brands but confirms broad-based growth in both Europe and North America.
Expected export revenue for FY27 will be the highest ever for RKFL.

subsections.label: Diversification Strategy
points: Commercial vehicle remains core business, but increasing opportunities seen across passenger vehicles, electric vehicles, energy, mining, off-highway and railway segments.
Non-automotive share of order book continues to improve, reflecting strategic focus on a more balanced portfolio.
Company expanding presence across passenger vehicles, electric vehicles, and advanced materials (aluminum, specialty alloy forgings), broadening addressable market and creating new growth avenues.
Zero current exposure to aerospace activity; company is quoting RFQs and building order book expected to take shape over next two years; RFQ names not disclosed.

Best period for RKFL described by management as having 'just started,' with confidence in significant traction across growth and balance-sheet improvement over the coming quarters/years and next 3-4 years of visibility.

Passenger vehicle, oil & gas, and non-automotive sectors like earthmoving equipment cited as sources of extreme confidence, expected to be a next major growth lever/transformation for RKFL over next two years.

subsections.label: New Ventures
points: Company looking at new ventures within forgings and casting boundaries in non-ferrous products — manufacturing from aluminum, titanium, Inconel and nimonic grades — for aerospace, robotics and semiconductors.
Seeking to leverage advanced manufacturing capabilities to participate as a strong engineering company in high-technology sectors traditionally dominated by global players.
Casting operations integration substantially completed; focus remains on scaling production and improving operating efficiencies.

Aerospace/titanium/Inconel foray is a multi-year journey — meaningful revenue contribution expected only after at least 8-10 quarters (2 years); significant portion of stainless-steel forging expected to start from Q4 FY27 orders already received.

subsections.label: Geopolitical & Cost Risks
points: West Asia conflict resurgence remains an overhang; tariff negotiations could arise again, though operating conditions have become more stable versus prior quarters' heightened volatility.

Primary risk to margins flagged as geopolitical issues leading to shipping delays, which increase working capital pressure, and rising energy prices — energy being one of the biggest cost components in the forging/steelmaking process; escalation of war-driven energy prices seen as a major profitability risk.
Commodity (steel) cost increases are passed on to customers with a one-quarter lag; gas and other volatile costs are not fully passed on as customers are unwilling to absorb such fluctuating costs.

Shipping costs have seen abnormal increases; expected to stabilize gradually but described as a 'roller coaster'; company still working with customers on how to absorb this cost without a definitive resolution.
No hedging mechanism exists for steel price — alloy steel is purchased on spot, quarter-on-quarter, based on prices declared by steelmakers each quarter.
No improvement seen yet in Q2 market conditions for energy/shipping costs; moderation unlikely until geopolitical issues are resolved.
Currency risk is minimal as all contracts include currency pass-on clauses — neither depreciation nor appreciation materially affects RKFL's margins.

key_figures.label: Overall capacity utilization ceiling before next capex
Working capital improvement target
key_figures.value: 15-20 days total (debtor -5 to -10 days, inventory -5 days, creditor +10 days)

subsections.label: Overall Outlook
points: FY28 target of Rs.8,000 crores revenue delayed by one year due to past tariff/internal upheavals; now targeting FY29 for Rs.8,000 crores, implying ~22-25% CAGR over next three years.

Management declined to give a specific margin range for the full year but affirmed continued quarter-on-quarter improvement, aided by rising utilization and export mix, with aspiration to return to historical (~22%) margin levels — timeline not specified.
Domestic demand expected to remain robust; next half (post rainy season, from around September) expected to be extremely exciting for domestic demand, though no specific volume growth number given.
Management confident for next seven quarters (FY27-FY28) based on current order book and RFQ inflows.
Debt reduction to continue into FY28, though company does not intend to become a zero-debt company — leverage will be kept in check while continuing to grow.
No new major capex plans until end of FY28 pending order book visibility in new verticals; current capacity considered sufficient for next two years of significant growth.

guidance_ledger.statement: Momentum from H2 FY26 has carried into Q1 FY27; continued growth trajectory expected
This year we are looking at somewhere between 12% to 15% ROCE
Next year in FY28 we will target 20% ROCE
We are looking at almost 35% revenue on a consol balance sheet coming from exports, for a full year basis; it will be highest ever revenue for RKFL in exports
We are looking at almost 20% plus growth in terms of exports

risk_register.risk: Energy price escalation

key_takeaways: Consolidated revenue for the quarter stood at Rs. 1,217 crores, which is flat quarter-on-quarter, and it has registered a growth of 19.84% year-on-year.

EBITDA excluding other income stood at Rs. 218.47 crores, that is up by 47% year-on-year and 5% quarter-on-quarter, while EBITDA margin improved to 17.96% from 17.11% in the previous quarter, reflecting better operating leverage and improved product mix.

Profit before tax for the quarter stood at Rs. 65.34 crores versus Rs. 23.9 crores year-on-year, and while profit after tax for the quarter stood at Rs. 46.88 crores versus Rs. 11.7 crores year-on-year, reflecting a growth of 172% and 297%, respectively.

During First quarter FY27, we have secured business worth Rs. 278 crores with a program life of four years from automobile segment. The company also won new orders worth Rs. 15 crores from Metro segment of Indian Railways.
This year what we are looking at somewhere between 12% to 15% ROCE this we will end, and next year in FY28 we will target 20% ROCE.

We are looking at almost 35% revenue on a consol balance sheet coming from exports, for a full year basis... It will be highest ever revenue for RKFL in this financial year for ever done in terms of exports.

We have already guided in our last call, we will reduce at least Rs. 500 crore of leverage in this financial year and we are on track of that... by the end of the year, we should be down to Rs. 1,500 crores of net debt.

With last year's performance and now continuing improving on that performance, I think we have got delayed by one-year and I think we are on track right now with FY29 target as Rs. 8,000 crores... Around 22% to 25% CAGR we will have for next three years.

quarters.summary: Management expects an improved operating trajectory from Q1 FY27 onwards on the back of a strong domestic order book, resumption of North America Class 8 truck demand, ramp-up of the rail wheel JV (commercial production from Q1 FY27, 40,000 wheels targeted this year), near-full utilization in castings (85-90%), press plant utilization of ~85% and overall forging+casting utilization of ~80% (~350,000 tons) by FY27 year-end, along with planned debt reduction of Rs. 400-500 crores and moderated capex of ~Rs. 300-400 crores for FY27.

subsections.label: Q4 FY26 Performance Drivers
points: Strong performance in domestic market supported by resilient performance in international market helped deliver solid top-line growth YoY and QoQ.

Profit in consolidated accounts impacted by elimination of profit from subsidiaries (Rs. 5.9 crores) and loss from Mexico subsidiary (Rs. 4.5 crores), total impact of ~Rs. 10.4 crores; net profit could have been much higher on a consolidated basis otherwise.

subsections.label: FY26 Full Year
points: Full-year PBT declined 24% YoY compared to FY25 (excluding exceptional item).

subsections.label: ECL Provisioning Explanation
points: Rs. 42 crores ECL provisioning made in Q4 in light of income from an electricity duty order received in the previous quarter, recognized as exceptional income; company did not want to carry this into P&L, so on a prudent basis considering current economic scenario and global volatility, provided ECL on receivables.
This amount is receivable in full but was provided for as headroom; expected to help in future.

subsections.label: Capital Allocation / Debt & Capex Outlook
points: Significant debt reduction planned this year on the back of promoter funding and good performance — targeting reduction of Rs. 400-500 crores.
Capex for FY27 expected to be Rs. 300-400 crores maximum (~Rs. 400 crores), mostly value adds and JV contribution, with a further Rs. 50 crores in JV equity contribution pending.
Most of thrust this year is on debt reduction rather than fresh capex; FY28 capex plans not yet frozen, still gathering customer feedback on capacity requirements.
Company has spent about Rs. 800 crores plus of capex over the last two years.

subsections.label: Margin Outlook / Utilization Leverage
points: Current Q4 margin level expected to sustain and improve further as utilization economics scale, provided energy price increases are passed on to customers.
Expected margin improvement of at least 100-150 basis points versus current, contingent on ability to pass on energy price increases.
Company not yet able to pass on energy price increases; discussions with customers are in advanced stage; industry-wide dynamic, timing/quantum uncertain.

subsections.label: Order Book Composition
points: During Q4, company secured new orders worth Rs. 594 crores for program life of four years; 56% from Automotive segment, 44% from Non-Automotive segment, reflecting continued progress in diversification strategy.
Of Rs. 594 crores: Rs. 334 crores from Auto sector (Rs. 323 crores from CV, Rs. 11 crores from EV); Rs. 258 crores from energy segment (Non-Auto) and Rs. 2 crores from off-highway.

Order book split across years is presented on an incremental basis year-on-year — the FY27 figure of Rs. 1,550 crores (down from Rs. 2,200 crores shown in the prior presentation) reflects residual orders after FY26 execution moved out; FY28 figure of Rs. 2,800 crores represents Rs. 1,100 crores incremental over FY27.

Energy segment order wins (~Rs. 258 crores) driven by energy storage devices trend — orders received from companies in North America market with ambitious energy storage plans requiring forgings and castings mix.
Of the Rs. 323 crores CV order win, more than 50% is export and around 50% is domestic.

subsections.label: Railway Segment
points: Railway business has been a strong pillar of growth; company has taken steps to deepen footprint and enhance capabilities in this segment in recent years, now paying dividends as railway share of revenue grew to 7.5% in FY26 vs 4.6% a year ago.

Rail wheel joint venture remains on track with commencement of production anticipated by Q1 FY27; company targeting supply of ~40,000 wheels to Indian Railways this financial year (FY27), with plant capacity set up for 230,000 wheels.

300 trial wheels to be submitted around June/July for approval; commercial production expected to start once plant begins manufacturing (end of May/June), without waiting for approval of the 300 trial wheels.

Wheels selling price cannot be disclosed exactly since contract was awarded two years back and requires real-time pricing update for inflation; wheel plant expected to generate roughly Rs. 400-450 crores in revenue once ramped, at margins in a similar trajectory to the forging business.
Cannot provide exact component-by-component revenue achievement for railway assembly undercarriage; overall railway business at 7.5% of revenue, targeting double-digit share this year.

subsections.label: Trailer Axle (B2C) Business
points: Trailer axle business — company's first B2C venture — generated roughly Rs. 120 crores revenue in FY26 with about 4-5% market share after two years of operation; management satisfied with progress.
Targeting to roughly double this business to Rs. 250 crores revenue in FY27 with market share target of about 10%.

subsections.label: Casting Business
points: Standalone casting business commenced commercial production only on 31 March, hence nil standalone contribution in FY26; entire FY26 casting revenue was from subsidiary/consol.
Sales lower than production due to machining mix; additional casting capacity (added by end of March) expected to generate Rs. 400-500 crores revenue in coming years at current commodity levels.
Casting margins expected at 15-16%.

subsections.label: Aluminium Forging / EV & PV Diversification
points: Post commissioning of aluminium forgings facility, company has already started bulk supplies to EV equipment manufacturers globally and is developing more aluminium forging products for CV manufacturers globally.

Aluminium forging margins at ~14-15% at absolute numbers on a commodity price of ~Rs. 400/kg; contribution margin considered much higher than current business due to higher commodity-linked realization.

EV segment performing extremely well both domestically and overseas; company aggressively working on improving passenger vehicle (predominantly EV) portfolio as part of diversification strategy to reduce ICE dependence; guided for 10%+ revenue from PV/EV segment in two years' time — management confirmed 10% PV target is synonymous with 10% EV at overall level.

subsections.label: Aerospace / Titanium & Alloy Foray
points: Exploring opportunities to set up capacity to manufacture titanium and other stainless-steel products for aerospace; bidding for several opportunities in domestic and global markets; in talks with several OEMs globally and in India, but no contract yet to provide realistic revenue numbers.
Expects this to start reflecting in the order book by this financial year-end, but revenue impact expected only 12-24 months out due to long lead times and approval timelines — not before FY29.

subsections.label: Utilization Trends & Ramp-up Plan
points: Q4 forging utilization of ~70% vs 83% a year ago is not directly comparable due to addition of 8,000-ton pressline and other forging capacity additions; utilization expected to happen from order book already in place, with much better utilization expected this year vs last quarter.

Cold forging utilization at 40% mainly because approvals for passenger vehicle sector cold forging are taking longer in global markets; utilization will improve as approvals come through, though no firm timeline can be given; management hopeful of reaching 75-80% cold forging utilization by year-end.
Press plant utilization expected to reach ~85% by FY27 year-end; difficult to guide quarter-on-quarter due to dependence on approvals.
No plans this financial year to increase ring-rolling capacity; ring-rolling has historically operated above 100% utilization (currently 121%) without negatively affecting equipment life.

subsections.label: Rail Wheel JV Facility
points: Rail wheel JV plant capacity set up for 230,000 wheels; commercial production to start as plant begins manufacturing (end of May/June 2026), targeting 40,000 wheels supply to Indian Railways in FY27, ahead of/without waiting for 300 trial wheel approvals.

subsections.label: Capex Plans
points: This year is a year of consolidation — capex capped at Rs. 300-400 crores maximum, mostly value adds and JV contribution (including remaining Rs. 50 crores JV equity contribution); thrust is on debt reduction rather than fresh capacity growth.
FY28 capex plans for further growth not yet frozen; company still in discussions with customers on future capacity requirements.

subsections.label: Domestic Market
points: Domestic macroeconomic environment remained relatively favourable; India continued to stand out as one of fastest-growing major economies, supported by resilient consumption, sustained government capex, infrastructure activity, and improving manufacturing momentum.
Following GST rate rationalization in September, sustained momentum in domestic auto industry with all segments — M&HCV, tractors, PVs — reporting double-digit growth in Q4.

subsections.label: Export / North America Market
points: Class 8 trucks in North America are very strong currently; since last 3 months, destocking has been happening in warehouses in North America, with fresh revenues expected from this quarter onwards in significant manner; expected to sustain for at least 2 years, till Q3 calendar year 2027.
FY27 expected to be a growth year for North America performance vs previous year, aided by new customer wins and coming online of Mexico operations expected to go live in a couple of weeks/months.

With new order wins in European market and current global market trend, export mix expected to significantly improve over next two years, moving above 40% (from historical 40-42%); export always more remunerative than domestic, so margins expected to considerably improve over next ~8 quarters (2 years) as export mix improves.
Export realization increased from Rs. 1.77 lakhs/ton to Rs. 1.85 lakhs/ton; export realizations always better than domestic — as export share grows, overall realization improves.
FY27 export volumes expected to come back strongly and be much better than in previous years in terms of overall mix/percentage to sales.

subsections.label: Supply Chain / Geopolitical Impact on Trade
points: Shipping cost up 15-20% and shipping days increased by 15-20 days due to geopolitical disruptions (Middle East conflict).
Floating inventory situation currently in line, unlike previous disruption episode.
No revenue exposure or clientele exposure to West Asia region.

subsections.label: Raw Material Sourcing
points: Aluminium raw material for forging sourced from Hindalco; buying is basically customer-directed.

subsections.label: Pricing Pass-through Mechanism
points: All pricing is based on pass-ons; steel (main commodity) price increases passed on to customers every quarter with a one-quarter lag, so margins are largely unaffected by raw material price movement.

Other consumables like gas affect bottom line and are negotiated with customers on a yearly basis; company has gone back to customers citing force majeure clauses amid geopolitical issues and expects compensation for gas/energy price increases to come soon, though timing and quantum are uncertain and industry-wide in nature.

Realization is directly linked to commodity price; raw material prices continued to decrease through FY26, which affected realization figures vs FY25; better product mix in H2 FY26 helped offset this effect.

subsections.label: Macro & Geopolitical Risks
points: Global macroeconomic environment turned incrementally more challenging in Q4 FY26, though conditions vary across regions and sectors.

Outbreak of conflict in Middle East adversely impacted operating conditions towards the latter part of the quarter, causing energy price volatility, persistent inflationary pressures, and renewed supply chain disruptions creating uncertainty for the business environment.
Current geopolitical issue is also viewed as a risk to growth outlook, even as order book supports confidence in growth.
Shipping costs and transit times have increased due to geopolitical disruptions.

subsections.label: Energy/Commodity Cost Pass-through Risk
points: Gas and other consumables costs (post raw material) are a source of margin risk; company yet to pass on energy price increases to customers; discussions in advanced stage but timing/quantum uncertain since it is an industry-wide dynamic, not isolated to the company.
Margin improvement of 100-150 bps contingent on ability to pass on these energy price increases.

subsections.label: Approval Timeline Risk
points: Cold forging utilization improvement dependent on passenger vehicle sector approvals in global markets, which are taking longer than expected, with no firm timeline achievable.
Aerospace/titanium alloy foray has long gestation due to lengthy approval timelines for long-lead items; revenue impact not expected before FY29.

subsections.label: Overall Outlook Statement
points: With rail wheel JV, order book, and capacity growth levers firmly in place, management is confident that from next quarter onwards the company will return to an improved operating trajectory and sustain momentum throughout FY27.
Management declined to give specific FY27 revenue growth number but stated confidence in continued growth trajectory and healthy growth in both top-line and bottom-line for FY27.

On prior guidance of 10-15% CAGR growth for FY27/FY28, management indicated confidence of surpassing this without committing to a specific number, citing current order book strength, though flagged geopolitical issues as a risk factor.

FY27 export volumes expected to come back strongly and be much better than in previous years in terms of overall mix/percentage to sales; North America performance expected to be a growth year vs previous year.

key_takeaways: We reported consolidated revenues of Rs. 1,216.78 crores, that is higher by 28% on year-on-year basis compared to Rs. 947.21 crores in Q4 FY25.

EBITDA excluding other income is Rs. 208.19 crores in Q4, higher by 111% year-on-year compared to EBITDA of Rs. 98.5 crores in Q4 FY25. The margin improved to 17.1%, higher by almost 220 basis points quarter-on-quarter.
Profit before tax is Rs. 64.33 crores in Q4 FY26 compared to Rs. 29.69 crores in Q3 FY26, reflecting a 117% quarter-on-quarter growth.
On the full-year numbers, we reported consolidated revenue of Rs. 4,238 crores for the full year FY26, that is higher by 5% on year-on-year basis compared to Rs. 4,034 crores in FY25.
The share of business from railways grown to 7.5% of revenue in this year against 4.6% a year ago.

During the Q4, the Company secured new orders worth Rs. 594 crores for the program life of four years. 56% of these orders were from Automotive segment and balance 44% were from the Non-Automotive segment.
Our rail wheel joint venture remains on track with commencement of production anticipated by Q1 FY27.
We are looking to reduce the debt by at least Rs. 400 to Rs. 500 crores in this year.
I think Class 8 trucks are very, very strong right now... we are looking at fresh revenues coming in from this quarter onwards from North America Class 8 trucks in significant manner.
pressing_questions: So, my first question was regarding the presentation. So, like there's a Rs. 600 crores reduction. So, have any of the orders been revoked or something?
Sir, can you give me a rough idea what will be the revenue growth in FY27?

Sir, my question was in respect of realization for our forgings... yet our realizations have been poorer than the Q4 of FY 2025. So even if we move forward with a higher capacity utilization, how do we plan to improve our realization of Rs. 1lakh per ton, sir?

Sir, there is a given in the notes of the results, there has been some loss provisions that we have made vis-à-vis tariffs that some of our customers have had to bear. So can you explain something pertaining to this ECL, what exactly is this?
So do you see possibility of going back to the previous highest utilization peak margins?

MASFIN.about: MAS Financial Services Limited is a non-deposit taking NBFC registered with the RBI. It is engaged in offering retail financing products for MSMEs, home loans, two-wheeler loans, used car loans and commercial vehicle loans. [1]

quarters.summary: Management reported a high-quality Q1 FY27 with consolidated AUM crossing INR16,000 crores (21% YoY growth), PAT growth of 27% consolidated, and reiterated its guidance of 20%-25% AUM growth, hoping to be at the higher end of the spectrum. Cost of borrowing declined to 9.25% and is expected to stabilize in the 9.2%-9.3% range; capital adequacy remains strong at 23.25%. Housing finance subsidiary is scaling up with plans to expand into South India (Tamil Nadu, Karnataka) from this quarter, with results expected in Q3/Q4. Credit cost is expected to remain range-bound between 1.25% to 1.75% depending on asset mix, with ROA targeted between 2.75% to 3.25%.

subsections.label: Profitability & Growth
points: High-quality growth this quarter (125th quarter of performance), consistent with company philosophy of steady, consistent growth.
Consolidated AUM crossed INR16,000 crores landmark; company doubles AUM every 3-3.5 years, on track from INR10,000 crores base in December 2024.
AUM growth of 21% consistent with 20% to 25% guidance range; moving towards plus-20% mark, expected to improve QoQ depending on distribution spread and macro.

subsections.label: Asset Quality
points: Portfolio quality remains stable and strong compared to March 2026.

Despite probable headwinds from West Asia conflict expected at the start of the quarter, asset quality did not deteriorate, attributed to resilience of MSME borrower sector and prudent credit extension approach.

subsections.label: Credit Cost Drivers
points: Credit cost increase from 1.2%-1.3% to 1.6% driven by higher on-book AUM growth (8.25% QoQ vs 5.5% overall AUM growth) requiring higher standard asset provisioning.
Standard asset provisioning in Stage 1 & 2 increased from 0.65% to 0.7%, entailing extra provisioning of INR5-7 crores; excluding this, credit cost would normalize.
A combination of higher on-book portfolio, marginally higher Stage 1/2 provisioning (a buffer), and prudent write-offs this year explains the credit cost level.
Write-off of INR19 crores in June (vs INR29 crores in March) was offset by higher ECL provisioning, keeping overall impairment cost roughly the same between March and June.
Write-offs are a regular feature for assets where recovery is uncertain.
Credit cost will remain range-bound between 1.25% to 1.75% depending on asset configuration/product mix pursued during the year; commercial vehicle growth would raise both yield and credit cost.
These credit cost movements have not affected ROAs or profitability.

subsections.label: Capital & ROA
points: Capital adequacy ratio at 23%+ provides strong base to raise liabilities and generate liquidity at optimum rate.
Company maintains ROA range of 2.75% to 3.25%; credit screen acts as a cushion depending on environment improvement or deterioration.

Better environment provides more business opportunities via calculated risk-taking, but the dictum of extending credit only where due is maintained, so profitability is not substantially increased beyond what's already factored in.
Branch sweating (from branches opened post March 2024) expected by 2027-2028 or earlier; will signify company at the higher end of the ROA spectrum.

subsections.label: Liquidity & Funding
points: Average liquidity balance of INR1,000 crores maintained during the quarter, with sanctioned borrowing line of INR1,900 crores.
Direct assignment transaction of INR700 crores completed, in line with sanctioned direct assignment lines of INR700 crores.
Cash credit facility of INR1,400 crores, with average utilization level of 70% to 75%.
Term loans of INR400 crores and non-convertible debentures of INR650 crores raised during the quarter.
Sanctioned borrowing lines of INR250 crores remain available for future drawdown.
Average cost of borrowing declined to 9.25%, down 55 bps YoY and 15 bps QoQ vs the March quarter; incremental borrowing cost stood at 9.2% to 9.25%.
Target borrowing cost of 9.25% to 9.3% expected over the next 1-2 quarters, with an aspiration to eventually reach pre-COVID sub-9% levels.

subsections.label: Cost Efficiencies / HR
points: Employee count reduced by 380 this quarter due to technology adoption, reflected in lower employee cost.

Tech is helping via automation reducing manpower requirement; contribution seen across origination, underwriting, operations, and soft-bucket collections (bots, auto-allocation, partnership-led origination).
Difficult to quantify future efficiency gains precisely as company sometimes maintains staff strength while testing tech before full implementation.

Cost-to-income should stabilize or reduce marginally over time; ROA (not cost-to-income or yield in isolation) is the right way to assess a diversified product company since a high-yield product may also carry high operating cost.

subsections.label: Core Business Mix
points: Company continues to predominantly focus on prime MSME segment (77% of book), bifurcated into MEL (INR6,153 crores, up 23% YoY) and SME (INR5,485 crores, up 21% YoY), both showing good growth with stable, good asset quality.

Two-wheelers (14% of book, INR1,039 crores, up 19% YoY), commercial vehicles (INR1,096 crores, up 13% YoY) and salaried personal loans (9% of book, INR1,374 crores, up 21% YoY) add diversification flair to the asset base.

subsections.label: Housing Finance Subsidiary
points: Housing finance AUM of INR976 crores, up 23% YoY, with total income of INR30 crores (up 30% YoY), PBT of INR5.70 crores (up 62% YoY) and PAT of INR4.27 crores (up 55% YoY) driven by lower operational cost as AUM grows.

Company is striking distance from INR1,000 crores AUM; internally aspires to reach growth potential of around 35% for housing finance, but continues to prioritize risk and profitability over just AUM growth.
Not growing only at 22-23%; actively strengthening distribution system, including planned expansion into South India.
Gross Stage 3 at 0.98% and net Stage 3 of 0.68% with sufficient buffer despite 100% secured book; capital adequacy of 35% with capital available as needed — very strong footing.
Average yield of ~14% and average credit cost of ~0.5%.
Company confident it will soon be value accretive for the parent.

Two priority workstreams for housing finance: (1) improving efficiencies in current distribution, (2) expanding distribution into South India — Tamil Nadu and Karnataka — starting this quarter, with recruitment underway; results expected to show in Q3 and Q4.
Priority also includes rationalizing TAT (turnaround time) and improving processes, benchmarking against peers to move faster in overall loan processing.

subsections.label: MRHMFL OCPS Redemption
points: MAS as parent regularly invests as per requirement in the subsidiary; INR10 crores of OCPS (3,33,000 shares) was to be redeemed over time or converted into equity.

Since MRHMFL capital adequacy is currently more than 37% and the company does not require additional capital, it did not proceed with OCPS conversion, and the amount was refunded to the parent (25% of total outstanding OCPS redeemed in cash).

subsections.label: Technology Strategy
points: Company operates on a build-and-operate model with an in-house team of close to 100 people consisting of business analysts and software engineers.
Recent adoption of AI is driving changes and efficiencies within the tech department.

Complete LOS (Loan Origination System) exists for all products; LMS has been in place for a long time; LOS is now being augmented with BRE (Business Rules Engine) and substantial straight-through processing, albeit with human intervention required given the borrower profile sold to.
Tech is creating efficiencies at the credit delivery level.
Tech automation across origination, underwriting, operations, and soft-bucket collections includes bots and auto-allocation; some partnerships also help with origination.
Difficult to quantify future manpower efficiency gains precisely, as staff strength is sometimes maintained while testing tech before full implementation.

subsections.label: Distribution Network
points: Assets created through strong distribution network of 16,500 centers via 209 branches, plus partnerships with more than 200 NBFCs — a model now more than 15 years old.
Partnership model contributes 33% of assets vs 67% from direct distribution currently (in the 66-67% range).

Direct distribution share is gradually expected to increase in favor of direct distribution to 70%+ within the next 8 to 12 quarters, and to around 70-72% in the next 1-1.5 years from the current 66-67%.

subsections.label: Housing Finance South Expansion
points: Housing finance company targeting expansion into South India, specifically Tamil Nadu and Karnataka, starting this quarter, with recruitment underway; results expected from Q3/Q4 onward.

subsections.label: Leadership / Succession Changes
points: CRO Nishant Jain (with company ~7-8 years, a qualified chartered accountant) elevated to Director-Operations, covering credit risk and operations, reporting to the Executive Director and CEO, effective September 1, 2026.

Darshil Thakkar (qualified chartered accountant, cost accountant and company secretary, rank holder, with company more than 10 years, previously holding a key position on credit delivery in SME and RAC space) elevated to the role of CRO.
These changes aim to strengthen middle management and create a strong succession path within the organization; such changes are expected to happen more frequently going forward.
Management characterized this as a designation change / internal change (clarified in Q&A in response to a press release query).

subsections.label: West Asia Crisis / Energy Dependence
points: Probable headwinds from the West Asia conflict were expected but did not fully play out, attributed to (a) resilience of MSME borrower sector and (b) prudent credit approach.

As soon as the crisis emerged, credit screens were tightened on likely affected areas, particularly energy-dependent businesses such as restaurants and manufacturing units dependent on gas/natural gas, and export-oriented businesses.
Even energy-dependent units that faced business problems largely managed to remain standard with other lenders too; no massive defaults observed.

Eligible demand definitely decreased due to tightened credit screens; login-to-disbursement ratio also decreased in Q1 and Q2 to a certain extent, but has since stabilized somewhat; how it plays out this quarter remains to be seen.
This impact has not been substantial enough to derail the 20%-25% AUM growth guidance, though it requires more field work/ground effort to find eligible borrowers.

subsections.label: Monsoon / Flood Impact
points: Weaker monsoon and subsequent overflooding in some regions raise questions on two-wheeler segment credit; company will design/tighten credit screens based on geography-specific, ground-level information gathered from sales, collection and credit teams.

Recent floods in Gujarat: many parts of Gujarat still in floods, making it difficult to assess impact right now; historically such events have caused only temporary (a day or two) operational disruption without lasting asset quality stress, though outcome is still evolving.

subsections.label: Used CV Segment Credit Tightening
points: Demand for used commercial vehicles has been robust overall, but eligible demand was slightly lower after tightening credit screens amid current crisis, especially concerning energy/fuel costs for used CVs.
Distribution and product processes for commercial vehicles are being calibrated; volumes along with desired quality expected to be achieved within the next 1-2 quarters.
Fluctuation in CV collection efficiency is considered normal; no undue risk seen on portfolio quality or losses from this fluctuation.
Company will wait and watch for 1-2 quarters before growing CV book more aggressively, given fluid current situation.

subsections.label: Macro / Rate Environment
points: Cost of borrowing is dependent on macro situation, RBI policies, and market liquidity from time to time; reduction beyond current levels not guaranteed.
Inflation numbers and RBI's stance on rate hikes are currently 'on the fence,' making near-term (sub-9%) borrowing cost reduction a stretch.

subsections.label: Forward Guidance Summary
points: Company remains committed to growing AUM anywhere between 20% to 25%, hopefully at the higher end of the spectrum.
Company aims to double AUM and profitability every 3 to 4 years, majority through internal accruals (non-dilutive growth).
Spread target of 7% to 7.5% translating into NIMs of 8% to 8.5% expected to be sustained.

Cost of borrowing expected to remain stable/stabilize around 9.2% to 9.3% for the next 1-2 quarters; aspiration to eventually move back towards pre-COVID sub-9% levels longer term, aided potentially by a credit rating upgrade (actively pursued, timing uncertain).
ROA guided to remain in 2.75% to 3.25% range, with an aspirational ROA target of 3%.
Credit cost guided to remain range-bound between 1.25% to 1.75%, dependent on asset/product mix.
Off-book AUM strategy target maintained at 20% to 25% of AUM via direct assignment and other off-book transactions.
Direct distribution share targeted to reach ~70-72% in the next 1-1.5 years and 70%+ within 8-12 quarters.

Housing finance business AUM growth expected to pick up with South expansion (Tamil Nadu, Karnataka), with results visible from Q3/Q4; company internally aspires to reach growth potential of ~35% for housing finance over time.
Very high possibility that full-year growth could be at the higher end of the 20%-25% range, given decent MSE and SME growth this quarter (though not a firm prediction).

guidance_ledger.statement: Consistent to our guidance of 20% to 25%; hopefully at the higher end of the spectrum, doubling AUM and profitability every 3 to 4 years, majority through internal accruals.
Very high possibility full-year growth could be closer to the higher side of 20% to 25%, given decent MSE and SME growth this quarter.
Capital adequacy ratio at 23%+ provides adequate headroom to support medium-term growth strategy; will continue to maintain strong capital adequacy.
Objective remains to maintain 20% to 25% of AUM as off-book through direct assignment and other off-book transactions.
Internally aspire to reach housing finance growth potential of around 35%; expanding distribution into South India (Tamil Nadu, Karnataka) to accelerate growth, with results expected in Q3/Q4.
Striking distance away from INR1,000 crores (currently at INR976 crores).
First target is to maintain cost of borrowing at 9.25% to 9.3%; sub-9% (pre-COVID) aspiration is longer-term and depends on macro stabilization and potential credit rating upgrade.
Spread of 7% to 7.5% translating into NIMs of 8% to 8.5% expected to be maintained/sustained.
Credit cost will remain range-bound between 1.25% to 1.75%, dependent on asset configuration/product mix pursued during the year.
ROA maintained in the 2.75% to 3.25% range; aspiration to reach 3% plus.
Direct distribution expected to increase to around 70% to 72% in next 1-1.5 years, and to 70%+ within next 8 to 12 quarters, from current 66-67%.
Company will wait and watch for 1-2 quarters before growing CV book more aggressively, given current fluid environment; volumes with desired quality expected within next 1-2 quarters.
Branches opened post March 2024 will sweat (become profitable/efficient) by 2027-2028 or even earlier.
Credit rating upgrade is being actively pursued, which could help reduce borrowing cost, though timing cannot be predicted.
Pursuing vision of 2036 to be a INR1 lakh crores AUM.
Strategic goal remains same, to maintain 20% to 25% of assets under management as off-book.
Range bound is anywhere between 16% to 17%, sustainable for FY '27 as well.
Currently at around 35%, range bound between 35% to 37%.
Should see increase in branches from anywhere from 30 to 35 branches this year across area of operations.
Currently have debt tie up almost for half the year for '26-'27; no reason we will not be in a position to tie up very soon for the whole year.
Hopefully sometime in the future, can be a leader in this category, take provisioning coverage up to 50-55% (analyst hope, not firm management commitment).

risk_register.risk: West Asia crisis / energy-dependent business stress
risk_register.note: Expected headwinds largely did not play out due to MSME borrower resilience and prudent/tightened credit screens on energy-dependent sectors (restaurants, gas-dependent manufacturing, export-oriented businesses); eligible demand decreased but no massive defaults seen; impact not substantial enough to derail 20-25% AUM growth guidance.

risk_register.risk: Used commercial vehicle segment eligible demand / fuel cost sensitivity
risk_register.note: Eligible demand slightly lower after tightening credit screens given energy/fuel cost concerns; distribution and product processes being calibrated; expect desired volume and quality within 1-2 quarters; fluctuation in collection efficiency considered normal.

risk_register.risk: Weak monsoon / flooding impact on two-wheeler and general asset quality
risk_register.note: Weaker monsoon in some regions followed by overflooding in others; credit screens will be tightened per geography based on ground-level information; outcome still evolving.

risk_register.risk: Gujarat floods
risk_register.note: Many parts of Gujarat still in floods at call time, making impact difficult to assess right now; historically such events cause only temporary (day or two) operational disruption without lasting stress on asset quality.

risk_register.risk: Macro/rate environment uncertainty (RBI policy, inflation)
risk_register.note: Inflation and RBI's stance on rate hikes are 'on the fence,' making near-term (1-2 quarter) reduction in borrowing cost below 9.25-9.3% a stretch; sub-9% pre-COVID level is a longer-term aspiration.

risk_register.risk: Higher on-book AUM leading to increased standard asset provisioning
risk_register.note: On-book AUM growth of 8.25% QoQ (vs 5.5% overall AUM growth) drove Stage 1&2 provisioning up from 0.65% to 0.7%, adding INR5-7 crores to impairment costs this quarter.

risk_register.risk: US tariff issue impact on select sectors (textile, FMCG)
risk_register.note: Company remains cautious/watchful on select segments (textile, FMCG) since the U.S. tariff issue; that cautious stance continues, though overall demand across MEL/SME, manufacturing and trading businesses is stable.

risk_register.risk: Middle East / West Asia crisis and inflationary trend from higher crude/input prices
risk_register.note: Could affect incremental lending environment and potentially reverse NPA improvement trend if it spirals out of control; company presumes borrowers remain in good financial position for now.

risk_register.risk: Sector-specific stress in textile, FMCG, agro-linked MSMEs
risk_register.note: These sectors remain on the cautious/watch list this quarter as previously highlighted.

risk_register.risk: Newly added cautious sectors: petrol pumps, gas agencies, transporters, chemical-related industries
risk_register.note: Added to caution/negative list in Feb end/mid-March due to potential Middle East-linked supply effects on gas and related inputs.

risk_register.risk: CV/logistics sector vulnerability to abnormal macro situations
risk_register.note: Logistics and transport are typically the first casualty in abnormal situations; company growing CV book at a slower, cautious pace for 1-2 quarters.

risk_register.risk: Macro/election/inflation surprise risk
risk_register.note: Good business momentum expected to continue into new financial year only if there are no massive negative inflation surprises post-election results.

risk_register.risk: Data-driven risk model misuse (generic extrapolation)
risk_register.note: Company avoids generic data extrapolation approach seen in earlier fintech losses (10-15%); relies on back-tested, experience-based risk models.

themes.label: AUM/AUM Growth Guidance
themes.note: Consolidated AUM crossed INR16,000 crores with 21% YoY growth, consistent with 20%-25% guidance; company optimistic about hitting higher end of range for full year.

themes.label: Asset Quality Improvement
themes.note: GNPA at 2.58% and NNPA at 1.70%, stable vs March 2026, despite expected West Asia conflict headwinds not materializing.

themes.label: Cost of Borrowing Decline
themes.note: Average cost of borrowing reduced 55 bps YoY to 9.25%; expected to stabilize at 9.2%-9.3% near term, with sub-9% pre-COVID levels as a longer-term aspiration aided by potential credit rating upgrade.

themes.label: Tech/AI-led Risk Management (LOS/BRE)
themes.note: In-house tech team of ~100 people; LOS now augmented with BRE and straight-through processing; AI adoption driving efficiencies; employee count reduced by 380 due to tech adoption across origination, underwriting, operations, and collections.

themes.label: West Asia Crisis / Inflation Risk
themes.note: Tightened credit screens on energy-dependent sectors pre-empted stress; eligible demand decreased somewhat but no massive defaults; impact assessed as not substantial enough to derail growth guidance.

themes.label: CV Book Cautious Growth
themes.note: Used CV eligible demand slightly lower due to tightened credit screens amid fuel/energy cost concerns; company calibrating distribution and product processes, expecting desired volume with quality in 1-2 quarters.

themes.label: Housing Finance Scale-up
themes.note: Housing finance AUM grew 23% YoY to INR976 crores with PAT growth of 55%; South India (Tamil Nadu, Karnataka) expansion launched this quarter, with results expected in Q3/Q4.

key_takeaways: This was, 125th quarter of performance... steadily and consistently is the fastest way to reach your destination.

Profitability that we could register along with a very strong asset quality also at 27% on consolidated basis and 25% on standalone basis. With a very strong AUM growth of 21%, consistent to our guidance of 20% to 25%.
We crossed once again a landmark of INR16,000 crores in AUM... we double our AUM every 3-3.5 years, we are well on track doing the same if you consider INR10,000 crores in say December 2024.
We remain very strong at GNPA of close to 2.58% and NNPA of 1.70%. Despite probable headwinds of the conflict, which we were expecting in the beginning, but fortunately did not play out.
Capital adequacy ratio stood at a very strong plus 23% this quarter also... we did good in reducing our borrowing cost by almost 55 basis points to 9.25% from the erstwhile borrowing cost.
We could also reduce the employee count by 380 this quarter, which you will see is reflected in the employee cost also and that is because of the adoption of technology.
On the housing finance side... strong growth of profitability of 56% because of the lower operational cost as we are growing our AUM. We are striking distance away from INR1,000 crores.

We remain committed to our guidance of growing anywhere between 20% to 25%, hopefully at the higher end of the spectrum, just doubling our AUM and profitability every 3 to 4 years and majority through internal accruals.
pressing_questions: Can you kindly share the demand that you are observing in the used CV business? Moreover, how has been the collection efficiency as we have witnessed a sharper uptick in the gross NPA vis-a-vis other segments?
Given the monsoon has been weaker this year, do we foresee any weakness in credit discussions for the two-wheeler segment as we witnessed a degrowth on quarter-on-quarter basis?
We have witnessed a back-to-back increase in yields and advances for the second quarter. So, how sustainable are these yields? And what was the primary driver for this increase?
Are we going to witness any further reduction in our cost of funding given we have already reached our target of 9.2%?
On this West Asia crisis... have you seen any change in terms of demand or stress in any particular pocket because of the crisis lingering on for so long?
What is the write-off number this quarter and last quarter?
On our housing subsidiary, what would be some things we are doing that could help us take the growth to the next level? I feel currently, we're still a little bit behind our guidance.

Now our off-book growth was slow this quarter, and we have fallen a bit under what our target mix is. Was there something to call out this quarter and do we expect the off-book growth to also catch up going forward this year?

quarters.summary: MAS Financial reported strong Q4/FY26 growth with AUM crossing INR15,000 crores and consolidated PBT crossing INR500 crores; management guided to continued 20-25% AUM growth, housing finance growth of 30-35%, and reaffirmed the vision of reaching INR1 lakh crores AUM by 2036, while flagging caution on CV book growth and select MSME sub-sectors due to Middle East crisis-linked inflation risk.

subsections.label: Milestones
points: Crossed around INR15,000 crores in AUM.
Consolidated basis crossed INR500 crores in profit before tax (PBT) and INR100 crores in profitability for the quarter.

subsections.label: Asset Quality Commentary
points: NNPA at parent maintained at around 1.70% despite tremendous headwinds during the year.
Housing finance company maintained excellent quality of assets at around 0.68% net NPA, while carrying additional buffers in both companies.
Credit quality improvement across zero DPD, 1-30, 31-60 DPD buckets noted by an analyst as phenomenal, aside from 91-120 DPD.
Provisioning coverage has gone up to 41.89% this quarter, with hope to reach 50-55% in future like other NBFCs.
Management attributes asset quality improvement to steps taken since '24 to extend credit where due and tighten credit screens, now showing results.
Company aggressively wrote off more than 0.10% of assets beyond the 2.57% gross stage 3 level as a forward-looking buffer, using available profit rather than showing higher profitability.

Write-off policy: loans written off post 360 days (also stated as post 365 days), applicable across all product segments; this quarter's write-offs were more in unsecured loans (combination of secured and unsecured).
Recovered amounts from written-off accounts are written back; P&L reflects net figure.

subsections.label: Dividend
points: Company to declare a final dividend of INR0.75 per share, taking total dividend to INR2 per share (20% of face value).
Company maintains a strategy of 10% dividend payout on profit.
Interim dividend of INR1.25 per share already declared and paid after December; final dividend subject to shareholders' approval.

subsections.label: NII and Yield Drivers
points: NII grew 11% sequentially versus AUM growth of 4% sequentially; growth attributed to lower incremental cost of borrowing (9.39% vs earlier 9.75%-9.8%) and an MCLR reset this quarter (MCLR reset happens every year).

Company does not upfront income from assignment transactions but amortizes it; sufficient provisioning brings it close to amortized income levels, so assignment quantum doubling did not drive NII growth via income upfronting.

Yield increase attributed mainly to growth in fintech-sourced business and two-wheeler business (two-wheeler yields 19%-23%, grew 35% this year); SME product mix changes (e.g., tie-ups like PhonePe for smaller loans vs SME loans up to INR5 crores) also affect yields.

Fees and commission income depends on how disbursement in a product is structured — as upfront fees/commission or built into interest yield; for fintech-sourced business (~10% of business), interest is booked fully in the book and interest rate differential is booked as commission expense.
Opex to be viewed with income: if fees/commission expense rises, income also rises at the top, allowing company to maintain ROAs between 2.75% and 3%.
Yields are kept range-bound between 16% and 17% by design; last quarter's lower yield offset by different low-yield product mix, this quarter offset by fintech/two-wheeler mix.

subsections.label: Cost of Borrowing
points: Average cost of borrowing for the quarter stood at 9.39%, a 42 basis point reduction from the same quarter last year; calculated on daily average balance and includes all costs, not just ROI.
Expected to decline further to around 9.20%-9.25% over the next 2-3 quarters.
Uncertain whether incremental rate benefits will be passed to borrowers or retained; depends on market situation.

subsections.label: Asset Mix
points: MSME (MEL + SME) contributes more than 70% of business; focus to continue on MSME as it has for the last 30 years.
Increase in the wheels (two-wheeler) business over time will add slightly to diversification of assets going forward.
CV portfolio has been cautiously grown at a lesser pace given energy dependency and logistics exposure amid Middle East crisis-related risks.

CV book growth has been slow for many quarters versus industry growth; internally, risk perspective suggests CV book should grow at a slower pace for coming 1-2 quarters before picking up pace in line with overall AUM growth, due to perception that logistics/transport are typically the first casualty in abnormal situations.

subsections.label: LOS and BRE Rollout
points: Company works on a build-and-operate tech model; Loan Origination System (LOS) has been successfully launched for all products.
Now in process of launching Business Rule Engine (BRE) with the help of AI.
With sufficient data at disposal, tech aimed at improving efficiency in customer service and employee efficiency, complementary to employees, and can help reduce cost in medium to long term.
Two-wheeler is a product where good progress made with faster processing, faster disbursals, and automated rule engines via LOS/BRE.
On MSME/SME side, BRE has replaced manual verification of policy parameters by credit managers with system-run algorithms generating a score, driving risk pricing and approval/rejection decisions.
Rules framing largely unchanged so far; management wants to run the scorecard for another 1-2 quarters, observe output, run statistical models, and then potentially frame newer policy parameters.

SME is described as a 'ripe product' for automization due to reliable formal data availability; MEL remains more manual due to requirement of physical assessment and visits, though exploring automization of MEL via BRE to optimize credit/sales resources and control opex.
Approval rates have been steady; company aims to see these continue into the new financial year.

subsections.label: Use of Data and AI in Risk Management
points: Data usage is unique to each company's experience with that data; a generic extrapolation approach (as seen in earlier fintech losses of 10-15%) is avoided.
Company back-tests risk models on available data before making decisions, aiming for consistency in borrower assessment via scoring models, which reduces debt/risk and brings consistency.
Use of data will progressively increase as more data points demonstrating characteristics accumulate; risk models are built from data experience over time, not purely from external data sources.
Progression: started with LOS, then business rule engines (now 6-9 months old), now shifting to AI-based risk management.

Early warning system described as 'ears very close to the ground' — assessing ground-level situation and talking to borrowers (e.g., contacted 2,000-3,000 commercial vehicle borrowers after Middle East crisis for feedback).
100% banking-based or E-NACH-based collection allows bouncing data to serve as an early warning signal; credit screens framed based on bouncing data and ground feedback.

subsections.label: Distribution Strategy
points: Strong distribution across more than 200 branches and 16,500 centers reach, continuing to expand.
Distribution consolidated via two channels: direct channel (branches/centers) and partnership with NBFCs (a nearly 15-year-old proven model).
Gujarat branch count declined by two due to dynamic recalibration process — branches merged or opened based on contribution/potentiality assessment to keep opex in check; not opened just for count.

This year, branch count did not increase much because company focused on 'sweating' existing branches (believes in building up squares rather than linear expansion) to ensure branches contribute to profitability.
Next year, branch count expected to increase by approximately 30-35 branches across areas of operations.

subsections.label: Investor Day / Long-term Vision
points: Company reiterated its long-term Vision 2036 of reaching INR1 lakh crores AUM, as shared at the Investor Day conference on 16th February.
Management believes this ambitious target is achievable in the medium to long term with support of the whole team on 'mission mode'.

subsections.label: Middle East / West Asia Crisis
points: Middle East crisis has led to caution around energy-dependent and logistics-linked borrowers.
Company contacted 2,000-3,000 commercial vehicle segment borrowers for feedback on impact of the Middle East crisis and their outlook.

Potential inflationary trend (higher crude/input prices) could affect incremental lending environment and could reverse the NPA improvement trend if it spirals out of control, though this is presumed unlikely as of now.

In February end/mid-March, company added petrol pumps, gas agencies, transporter profile, and certain chemical-related industries to a cautionary/negative list due to potential Middle East-linked supply effects on gas and related inputs.
Textile, FMCG, and agro-linked MSMEs remain cautious sectors this quarter, as previously highlighted.

subsections.label: Macro/Market Dependent Factors
points: Post-Diwali and GST cut exuberance combined with seasonally stronger Q4 supported good business momentum.
Outlook for continued momentum depends on no massive negative surprises on inflation post-election results.

subsections.label: Growth Outlook
points: Company continues to have confidence to grow AUM anywhere between 20% to 25%, given positive macro situation, prioritizing risk management and profitability over just growth.
Housing finance company grew around 23% this year; aspiration to grow it between 30% to 35% given its lower base.
Housing finance was at striking distance of INR1,000 crores AUM; ideally would have liked to touch it this year, but likely to take a quarter more.
Vision 2036 targets INR1 lakh crores AUM; management views this as ambitious but achievable in medium to long term.
Debt tie-up already secured for almost half of FY27; confident of tying up for the whole year soon; main challenge is achieving a better rate of interest, momentum for which started from Q4 onwards.
Plans in medium term to diversify resource mix via fresh fundraising through ECBs, foreign and development financial institutions, mutual funds, PMS, etc., at competitive cost.

guidance_ledger.statement: Confidence to grow AUM anywhere between 20% to 25%, given positive macro situation, prioritizing risk management and profitability over just growth.
Pursuing vision of 2036 to be a INR1 lakh crores AUM.
Will continue to maintain the capital adequacy of around 20% going forward.
Strategic goal remains same, to maintain 20% to 25% of assets under management as off-book.
Would aspire to grow housing finance business anywhere between 30% to 35% given its lower base.
At striking distance away from INR1,000 crores; ideally would have liked to touch it by this year, but it may take a quarter more now.
From 9.39%, we can see this going down to around 9.20% to 9.25% over next 2-3 quarters.
Range bound is anywhere between 16% to 17%, sustainable for FY '27 as well.
Credit cost anywhere between 1% to 1.25% on closing AUM statistically; could see 1.5%-1.6% if aggressive write-offs are opted for, without disturbing ROAs/ROEs much.
Currently at around 35%, range bound between 35% to 37%.
ROAs after opex and credit cost appropriated from NIMs will be anywhere between 2.75% to 3%.
Should see increase in branches from anywhere from 30 to 35 branches this year across area of operations.
This book should grow at a slower pace for coming 1 or 2 quarters before really picking up pace in parallel to the overall growth of the AUM of the company.
Currently have debt tie up almost for half the year for '26-'27; no reason we will not be in a position to tie up very soon for the whole year.
Hopefully sometime in the future, can be a leader in this category, take provisioning coverage up to 50-55% (analyst hope, not firm management commitment).

risk_register.risk: Middle East / West Asia crisis and inflationary trend from higher crude/input prices
risk_register.note: Could affect incremental lending environment and potentially reverse NPA improvement trend if it spirals out of control; company presumes borrowers remain in good financial position for now.

risk_register.risk: Sector-specific stress in textile, FMCG, agro-linked MSMEs
risk_register.note: These sectors remain on the cautious/watch list this quarter as previously highlighted.

risk_register.risk: Newly added cautious sectors: petrol pumps, gas agencies, transporters, chemical-related industries
risk_register.note: Added to caution/negative list in Feb end/mid-March due to potential Middle East-linked supply effects on gas and related inputs.

risk_register.risk: CV/logistics sector vulnerability to abnormal macro situations
risk_register.note: Logistics and transport are typically the first casualty in abnormal situations; company growing CV book at a slower, cautious pace for 1-2 quarters.

risk_register.risk: Macro/election/inflation surprise risk
risk_register.note: Good business momentum expected to continue into new financial year only if there are no massive negative inflation surprises post-election results.

risk_register.risk: Data-driven risk model misuse (generic extrapolation)
risk_register.note: Company avoids generic data extrapolation approach seen in earlier fintech losses (10-15%); relies on back-tested, experience-based risk models.

themes.label: Asset Quality Improvement
themes.note: NNPA maintained at 1.70% at parent despite headwinds; DPD buckets improving sharply except 91-120 DPD; provisioning coverage rose to 41.89%.

themes.label: AUM/AUM Growth Guidance
themes.note: Company reiterated 20-25% AUM growth target and Vision 2036 of INR1 lakh crores AUM.

themes.label: Cost of Borrowing Decline
themes.note: Cost of borrowing at 9.39%, down 42 bps YoY, expected to fall further to 9.20-9.25% over next 2-3 quarters, aided by MCLR reset.

themes.label: Tech/AI-led Risk Management (LOS/BRE)
themes.note: LOS launched across all products; BRE rollout with AI progressing, especially strong in two-wheeler and SME; MEL remains more manual.

themes.label: West Asia Crisis / Inflation Risk
themes.note: Middle East crisis prompting caution on CV, logistics, energy-linked and newly added sectors (petrol pumps, gas agencies, transporters, chemicals).

themes.label: CV Book Cautious Growth
themes.note: CV book growing slower than industry due to risk perception around logistics/transport in current macro environment; expected to remain slow for 1-2 quarters.

themes.label: Housing Finance Scale-up
themes.note: Housing finance AUM grew 22.41%, aspiring for 30-35% growth, strong profitability (35% annual growth in PAT) with low NNPA of 0.68%.

key_takeaways: Crossed around INR15,000 crores in AUM and, on a consolidated basis, crossed INR500 crores in PBT and INR100 crores in profitability for the quarter.
Growth on a consolidated basis is around close to 19%, increasing profitability by 21% on a year-on-year basis for the whole year; quarter profitability rise on corresponding quarter basis is 25%.
On standalone basis, around 19% growth in AUM, 20% growth in profitability for the whole year; quarter-to-quarter increase in profitability is around 23%.
NNPA at the parent maintained at around 1.70% despite tremendous headwinds during the year; housing finance company maintained excellent quality of assets at around 0.68% net NPA.
MSME (MEL + SME) contributes more than 70% of business, focus continuing since last 30 years; wheels business to slightly add to diversification going forward.
Confidence to grow AUM anywhere between 20% to 25%, prioritizing risk management and profitability over just growth.
Capital adequacy at 22.84% with Tier 1 capital around 21.5%; will continue to maintain capital adequacy of around 20% going forward.
Housing finance company grew around 23%; aspire to grow it between 30% to 35% given lower base; at striking distance of INR1,000 crores AUM, may take a quarter more to touch it.
Final dividend of INR0.75 per share declared, taking total dividend to INR2 per share (20% on face value); dividend payout strategy maintained at 10% of profit.
Pursuing vision of 2036 to be a INR1 lakh crores AUM, as shared at Investor Day conference on 16th February.
pressing_questions: Sir, my first question was generally in today's scenario of big data and AI, right, so a lot of information, a lot of data sets are available to all the lenders, to all financial institutions. I want to get some flavor and understanding from you as to how you are leveraging it for your risk-adjusted growth.

Secondly, sir, just staying on data and understanding data. I wanted to understand that do you also have an early warning system in place, which helps you with your risk management? And can you throw some flavor around that?
So just wanted to get a sense how big a role does assignment play in your higher NII growth? Because I believe there is some upfronting of income because of assignment.
So just wanted to get a better sense from you, what are you seeing in your segment which is restricting you to grow CV book?
So, my second question is regarding the higher credit cost observed during the quarter. So, was it due to the impact of West Asia conflict or some stress in certain pool accounts?

USHAMART.about: Usha Martin Ltd is primarily engaged in manufacture and sale of steel wires, strands, wire ropes, cords, related accessories, etc. It is also involved in sale of other products such as wire drawing and allied machines.[1]

quarters.summary: Usha Martin delivered a strong start to FY27 with 16.4% YoY consolidated revenue growth to INR 1,033 crore, 44% EBITDA growth to INR 208 crore (20.1% margin) and 41% PAT growth to INR 142 crore, driven by product mix improvement and full pass-through of input cost inflation. Management reiterated FY27 guidance of 10-12% volume growth, ~15% value growth, a minimum 20% EBITDA margin base, and capex of INR 250-300 crore, while flagging continued Middle East disruption, CBAM exposure from FY28, and ongoing strategic reviews of the UM Cables and Thailand businesses.

subsections.label: Profitability drivers
points: Profitability growth driven by a richer product mix, effective cost recovery and strong operating leverage, enabling significant expansion in earnings.
Company protected profitability and expanded margins despite a significant increase in key input and logistics costs by implementing pricing actions across segments to pass through increases.
Together with improvement in product mix, cost discipline and operating efficiencies, this enabled EBITDA margin expansion to 20.1%.

subsections.label: Cash flow and balance sheet
points: Profitability translated directly into cash; operating cash flow of ~INR 242 crore represented cash conversion of 116% of operating EBITDA.
Closed the quarter with a net cash position of ~INR 465 crore.
After funding capex of INR 73 crore, free cash flow stood at INR 135 crore.
Continued focus on working capital management further strengthened financial flexibility and ability to invest in growth priorities.

Long-term credit rating upgraded by India Ratings and Research to IND AA- from IND A+ with a stable outlook, reflecting continued strengthening of financial profile, healthy cash generation and prudent capital allocation over the past few years.

subsections.label: MD remuneration clarification
points: Rajeev Jhawar clarified the reported 4x jump in his remuneration in the Annual Report was an anomaly: he had voluntarily forgone his bonus (~INR 8 crore) for FY24-25 due to austerity measures taken during a major business restructuring (including European business and cost initiatives).
