subsections.label: Wire ropes
points: Value growth strong at 18% YoY even as overall volumes were marginally lower; volume decline largely due to Middle East operations.
Middle East volumes down ~28% due to continued geopolitical and market disruptions; realizations improved ~36% on better pricing and favorable mix, holding revenues broadly at last year's levels.
Across India, U.S. and Europe, healthy volume growth seen; geographic diversification helped overall rope business remain robust.
Domestic rope volumes grew ~12% YoY, value grew ~21%, supported by healthy demand across crane, elevator and fishing segments.
U.S. growth came mainly from elevator and mining segments; Europe saw good traction across oil and offshore renewables and value-added services.

subsections.label: Wires
points: Business delivered healthy growth with volumes up ~19% and revenue growing ~32% YoY.
Portfolio today is largely domestic driven; exports represent a significant growth opportunity.
Already begun supplying to select European customers in high-value applications such as automotive and rockfall protection; considerable headroom to scale as further approvals are secured.

subsections.label: Plasticated LRPC
points: Continued to gain traction, supported by healthy demand both domestic and export; recorded highest-ever volume and value for the segment this quarter.
First international order for plasticated LRPC strand for a stay cable application secured this quarter, an important step opening meaningful international opportunities.
Black LRPC has become largely commoditized, while plasticated offers genuine differentiation and better value; this will be central to competing in the LRPC segment.
Topline growth in LRPC segment (3.9% YoY) occurred despite a volume decline YoY, aided by plasticated mix.

One major approval verbally confirmed with a global customer with high domestic market share; paperwork slightly delayed but progressing, and the customer has already started quoting with Usha Martin's product.

Next year, expect to fully utilize the 6,000-ton capacity as approvals come through; company is already considering further capacity increase ahead of time so that in 18-24 months it can meet growing demand.
LRPC realizations seeing slight depression due to ongoing monsoon and project slowdown in domestic states.

subsections.label: Oceanfibre (synthetic slings)
points: Continues to build momentum; while a small part of overall business, encouraged by progress across offshore and heavy-lifting applications and pipeline of opportunities.
Complements core product portfolio and seen as an important growth lever going forward.
Last year was the first full year of commercial operations; revenue has been on an upward trend each of the last 5 quarters.
Goal to scale from current 2-3 million GBP level to 10 million GBP level over the next few years; being a high-margin business, this will add significantly to bottom-line performance.
Used in oil and offshore, wind energy applications where steel wire ropes cannot be used due to delicate/sensitive platform components; heavy lifting applications.
Specialized, critical application requiring approvals and track record to build the business, consistent with the value-added product strategy.

subsections.label: Galfan wire (GALSTAR brand)
points: Progressing well with good demand in the domestic market.

Export approvals in place; supplying to the European market for critical rockfall protection applications where approvals are based on performance and reliability, not just price, so scale-up takes time.
Priority now is to broaden customer base and secure more approvals.

subsections.label: UM Cables and Thailand
points: UM Cables is not part of core business; company is evaluating opportunities to use the strategically located West India facility to grow the value-added wire and wire rope business, but does not see long-term future in the cable business itself.
Thailand plant is strategically located with a strong customer base in the ASEAN region and is a leading player in Thailand; margins improved in Q1 and order book outlook for the year is better.

Company is developing a strategic model to make Thailand more profitable via better realizations and enhanced product mix, targeting a well-evolved plan within 6 months, addressing it over the next 2-3 quarters.
One option being considered is better integration of the Thailand plant with the India plant, similar to synergy models used in Dubai and the UK.

Elevator rope capacity expansion completion target

subsections.label: Capacity expansion projects
points: Key project underway is expansion of elevator rope capacity by approximately 6,000 metric tons per annum; additional capacity expected to be commissioned in phases beginning October, with the project scheduled for completion by Q1 FY28.
Investments focused on expanding capacity in specialized wire rope and improving manufacturing efficiency.
Also modernizing and expanding furnaces to meet increased demand.

In India, elevator market growing at ~20% with all major OEMs setting up presence; biggest constraint currently is capacity — once additional capacity comes in, company expects to grow with the market and also capture more share it currently cannot cater to.

subsections.label: U.S.
points: Market share slightly below 5%; ~9-10% of total revenue comes from U.S./Americas region.
Underpenetrated market relative to overall size; seen as an important expansion opportunity, especially in elevators, mining and oil & gas.

subsections.label: Europe
points: Second largest market after India at ~27% of quarter topline; own rigging shops, service centers and manufacturing give a big advantage.
Established presence in U.K. and Netherlands; headroom seen in Germany, Italy, Denmark, Norway and the North Sea area where share is relatively smaller.
Strategy is geography-specific rather than treating Europe as a whole, to identify where share gains are possible.

subsections.label: India
points: Market share viewed segment-wise: elevator rope ~60-65% share with room to grow, but capacity is the biggest current constraint.
Ports segment: >95% market share; focus is on retaining share while capitalizing on ongoing port expansion in India.
Strong dealer network catering to other high-value sectors (piling, ports, mining) in the domestic market.

subsections.label: Middle East
points: Volumes down ~28% due to ongoing geopolitical conflict; port, marine and offshore, and construction businesses all affected.
Projects across Saudi Arabia delayed or stalled; distributors have taken a conservative approach to stocking.
Company focus in this region was to maximize inquiry conversions, sell through value-addition route and optimize product mix to reduce top-line and bottom-line impact.
Company has its own factory and own rigging shop in Saudi Arabia, seen as an important advantage to capture opportunities once conditions improve.

If geopolitical conditions improve, opportunity would be across the portfolio: crane ropes (piling), elevator ropes, port cranes, marine applications, GP ropes, large diameter and drill line ropes for oil & offshore, and plasticated LRPC for bridge/infrastructure projects.

subsections.label: Asia Pacific
points: Some project-related delays during the quarter, but described as delays rather than lost demand; projects still under negotiation/pipeline expected to mature.
Company stepping up customer engagement and identifying areas such as crane ropes and elevators to build more regular (non-project-driven) business; a key focus area through the year.

subsections.label: 'One Usha Martin' initiative
points: Company will continue to improve mix, scale newer verticals and strengthen collaboration across global operations through the 'One Usha Martin' initiative.

subsections.label: Non-core business review
points: UM Cables not part of core business; company evaluating opportunities to repurpose its strategically located West India facility to grow value-added wire and wire rope business rather than continue in cables long term.

Thailand plant strategic review underway to improve profitability via product mix, realizations and possible integration with the India plant (synergy model similar to Dubai and UK); well-evolved plan expected within 6 months, addressed over next 2-3 quarters.

subsections.label: New customer approvals pipeline
points: Continuous pipeline of new customer approvals across elevator, oil & offshore, and crane industries; approval processes can take a few quarters to two-to-three years.
Ongoing approval process across plasticated LRPC, GALSTAR (zinc-aluminium wires) and Oceanfibre businesses, supported by global development and design centres.
Company keeps confidentiality on customer names but adds on average at least 10-12 new customers every few months across various segments.

subsections.label: Middle East geopolitical disruption
points: Continued geopolitical and market disruptions caused ~28% Middle East volume decline; port, marine/offshore and construction businesses affected; Saudi projects delayed/stalled; distributors conservative on stocking.

West Asia crisis is already impacting topline; resolution would create a big opportunity for reconstruction demand, oil & gas activity and infrastructure projects, but situation remains very uncertain and daily changing.

Currently a lot of ports in the Middle East are not functional, which could delay safety-mandated replacement cycles somewhat, though replacement demand remains fairly predictable given safety mandates.

subsections.label: Input cost inflation
points: Wire rod prices ~7% higher YoY and zinc prices ~28% higher YoY; freight costs also remain elevated.
Company implemented pricing actions across segments to fully pass through cost increases (100% pass-through on commodity inputs including steel, gas and other inputs), with no cost absorption.

Steel price increase is passed through as an absolute amount (e.g., INR 7,000/ton increase on a ~INR 50,000-55,000/ton steel price, up 13% Q-o-Q) — not as a percentage of the much higher finished product price (INR 1,80,000-3,50,000/ton for wire rope) — explaining why EBITDA/ton did not rise proportionally to the % steel price increase.
Oil & gas price volatility from the West Asia crisis has been successfully passed on to customers through transparent communication; no impact currently expected on operating profitability from this.

subsections.label: CBAM (Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism)
points: Currently negligible impact, but post-FY28 impact possible on products/regions served.

Wires (HS code 7217) already under CBAM's definitive period for EU exports; company has appointed a consultant to assess cost impact per ton and is regularly communicating with customers on joint mitigation strategy.

Wire rope (HS code 7312) not yet in the definitive period (expected around FY28) as it is a more complex steel derivative; cost impact per ton for wire rope not expected to be much higher than wires from an energy-consumption perspective, since large part of the cost/emissions impact comes from input steel material rather than the company's own processes.
Company working with suppliers to identify options to minimize overall CBAM impact ahead of FY28.

subsections.label: Asia Pacific project delays
points: Project-related delays in the region during the quarter, though described as delays rather than lost demand.

subsections.label: UM Cables and Thailand profitability
points: UM Cables division not performing well; Thailand segment noted as PAT negative previously, though Thailand margins improved in Q1 with a better order book outlook for the year.

subsections.label: Volume and value growth
points: Company reasonably confident of 10-12% volume growth for FY27, including Middle East operations, unless the situation worsens further from current levels.
Confidence based on capacities already in place and fairly strong inquiries; approach will be value-led volume growth.
Value growth of ~15% expected depending on product mix, alongside the volume growth target.
Wire Rope volumes remain a clear priority; approach will focus on both volume and value given time required for approvals with specialty customers.

subsections.label: Margin outlook
points: Minimum EBITDA margin base of 20% guided going forward, with quarter-on-quarter variation possible in the 20-21% range due to product/geographic mix.
As new capex volumes come online and product mix improves, margins expected to move upwards from this new base.
Focus will always be on absolute EBITDA growth, not just EBITDA per ton, given capacity already created.

subsections.label: Capex outlook
points: FY27 capex guided at INR 250-300 crore, including routine/maintenance capex, to support 10-12% volume growth and ~15% value growth.
Elevator rope capacity expansion (~6,000 tons/year) is the main project, along with furnace modernization/expansion.

subsections.label: Realization outlook
points: Company expects to maintain a healthy realization for wires and wire ropes going forward, slightly better than Q1 levels.
LRPC realizations may see slight depression near-term due to monsoon and project slowdown in some states.

International rope realizations (INR 3,70,000-3,80,000/ton) depend on product mix (Oceanmax, GP ropes, drill line ropes) and order maturity each quarter; not necessarily fixed at this level going forward.

subsections.label: Thailand turnaround plan
points: A well-evolved strategic plan for improving Thailand plant profitability (via product mix, realizations, possible India integration) expected within 6 months, to be addressed over the next 2-3 quarters.

guidance_ledger.statement: Consolidated revenue increased by 16% year-on-year to INR 1,033 crore.
We feel and we still maintain that we will be able to get to 10% to 12% growth of volume in this financial year, including the Middle East operations, unless situation worsens.
About INR 250 crore to INR 300 crore would be the capex for us to be able to continue with topline growth of 10% to 12% in terms of volume and around 15% on value.
For FY27, we continue to expect capex of approximately INR 250 crore to INR 300 crore.

Our base, as we have been maintaining, would be at 20%. As various new capex volumes go up as well as the product mix improves, we should be able to see it moving upwards; new base would be at around 20%, with a minimum of 20%.
There could be a quarter-on-quarter variation in terms of margin in the 20% to 21% range due to the product segment and also the geographic mix.

guidance_ledger.horizon: commissioning from October, completion Q1 FY28
guidance_ledger.statement: A key project underway is the expansion of our elevator rope capacity by approximately 6,000 metric tons per annum. The additional capacity is expected to be commissioned in phases beginning October with the project scheduled for completion by the first quarter of FY28.
This year, our target is 3,500 to 4,000 tons for plasticated LRPC (up from 2,500 tons last year).
Next year, we should be able to fully utilize the [6,000 ton] capacity as these approvals come through.
We are already thinking about how we can further ahead of time, increase our capacity so that in 18 to 24 months' time, as these projects pick up, we are still able to meet the demands of the market.
Our goal is to see how we can take this from 2 million to 3 million GBP level that it is now to, say, 10 million GBP level over the next few years.

In the next 6 months, we would be in a position to have a fairly well-evolved plan for this, which should create a long-term improved profitability coming from our Thailand plant... we would be addressing it in the coming 2 or 3 quarters.
We hope to maintain a healthy realization of our products, slightly better than what we did in quarter 1.
On the LRPC side, we are seeing a slight depression in terms of the realizations because of the ongoing monsoon and the project slowdown in the states.
We are working with our suppliers as well to see what are the options available to us so that we can minimize that overall impact when it hits us in FY28.
Earlier benchmark was 18-19% operating margin; now company feels it should be able to look at a minimum of 20% operating margin due to product mix and other factors.
Planning to increase rope capacity by close to 6,000 tons as part of the capex plan.
Black LRPC expected to be around 48,000 tons, similar to last year.

guidance_ledger.metric: Oceanfibre synthetic sling & plasticated LRPC scale-up
guidance_ledger.statement: Expect meaningful scale up in FY27 and beyond for Oceanfibre synthetic business and plasticated LRPC.
Over the next 18 months, significant improvement in operations of the Thailand plant expected as modernization and capacity expansion progress.
Focus would always be to improve overall absolute EBITDA numbers, not just EBITDA per ton, given the large capex and plant capacity created.
Fairly strong order book and visibility for rope demand for the next 6 months at least, though not quantified.
Actual real rope demand from Parvatmala project will likely come in probably 2 to 3 years as projects move to final implementation stages.
Company is evaluating selective organic and inorganic opportunities in markets where footprint is still limited, particularly value-added and rigging areas.

risk_register.note: Volumes down ~28% (≈1,000 tons); ports, marine/offshore and construction businesses affected; Saudi projects delayed/stalled; distributors conservative on stocking; situation remains uncertain and daily changing.

risk_register.risk: Input cost inflation (steel/wire rod, zinc, gas, freight)

risk_register.risk: CBAM (Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism)

risk_register.risk: Asia Pacific project delays
risk_register.note: Project-related delays during the quarter, described as delays rather than lost demand; projects still in pipeline/negotiation.

risk_register.risk: UM Cables underperformance
risk_register.note: Non-core division not performing well; company evaluating repurposing the facility rather than continuing in cables long term.

risk_register.risk: Thailand plant profitability (PAT negative previously)
risk_register.note: Margins improved in Q1 with better order book outlook; strategic plan for further improvement being developed.

risk_register.risk: Oil & gas price volatility from West Asia crisis

risk_register.risk: Middle East geopolitical conflict
risk_register.note: Led to slower customer activity, project delays in Dubai and Saudi Arabia, disrupted supply chains affecting shipment timing, and below-normal volumes; impacted rope volume by about 900 tons in Q4.

risk_register.risk: Raw material availability tightness / input cost inflation (steel, gas, LPG)
risk_register.note: Broader geopolitical situation created tightness in raw material availability and pressure on input costs; LPG/propane price rose from INR 60,000/ton to INR 120,000-130,000/ton; steel and gas prices rising since January.

risk_register.risk: US tariffs and trade uncertainty
risk_register.note: US market has share of challenges around tariffs and trade uncertainties on the ground, though company still sees good growth opportunities.

risk_register.risk: Project execution delays (Parvatmala)
risk_register.note: Real rope demand from Parvatmala expected only in 2-3 years due to project implementation timelines and some delays in customer approvals; wire rope is the last part of such projects.

risk_register.risk: Product mix volatility affecting margin/volume trade-off
risk_register.note: Margins depend on mix between wires, LRPC and within rope categories on a month-to-month/quarter-to-quarter basis; not a straight line trend.

themes.label: Margin expansion via product mix
themes.note: EBITDA margin expanded 380bps YoY to 20.1% driven by richer product mix, cost recovery and operating leverage; value-added rope share rose to 73% from 70%.

themes.label: Middle East geopolitical disruption
themes.note: Middle East volumes down ~28% (~1,000 tons) due to geopolitical conflict, though realizations improved ~36%, holding revenue broadly flat.

themes.label: Input cost inflation (steel, gas/LPG)
themes.note: Wire rod up ~7% YoY, zinc up ~28% YoY, steel up ~13% Q-o-Q; fully passed through to customers with no margin absorption.

themes.label: International expansion & market share gains
themes.note: Healthy volume/value growth in India, U.S. and Europe; first export order for plasticated LRPC and GALSTAR wires supplied to European customers.

themes.label: Capacity expansion & capex
themes.note: FY27 capex guided at INR 250-300 crore, mainly for ~6,000 ton elevator rope capacity expansion (commissioning from October, completion Q1 FY28) and furnace modernization.

themes.label: New product scale-up (plasticated LRPC & Oceanfibre slings)
themes.note: Plasticated LRPC hit record volume/value and secured first international order; Oceanfibre revenue trending up each of last 5 quarters with high 65-70% gross margins.

themes.label: 'One Usha Martin' cost efficiency program
themes.note: Company will continue to improve mix, scale newer verticals and strengthen collaboration across global operations through the 'One Usha Martin' initiative.

key_takeaways: Consolidated revenue increased by 16% year-on-year to INR 1,033 crore.
Operating EBITDA stood at INR 208 crore, a 44% increase year-on-year with an EBITDA margin of 20.1%.
Across our businesses, value grew faster than volume, reflecting improved realizations and our continued shift towards specialized products.

We generated operating cash flow of approximately INR 242 crore, representing cash conversion of 116% of operating EBITDA and closed the quarter with a net cash position of approximately INR 465 crore.
During the quarter, we incurred capital expenditure of approximately INR 73 crore. For FY27, we continue to expect capex of approximately INR 250 crore to INR 300 crore.
During the quarter; the Company's long-term credit rating was upgraded by India Ratings and Research to IND AA- from IND A+ with a stable outlook.

Middle East volumes were down approximately 28% due to continued geopolitical and market disruptions. However, realizations improved by approximately 36% on the back of better pricing and a more favorable mix, which allowed us to hold revenues broadly at last year's levels.
A key milestone this quarter was our first international order for plasticated LRPC strand for a stay cable application.
pressing_questions: So when can we start seeing an uptick in the volume? Because I understand that Q1 is normally a seasonally weak quarter as well. And we have seen historically that Q2 has been a very high volume bump up for the wire rope business. So, shall we see a similar trend this year?

So how much of the margin impact is there from LRPC this quarter? And will that be negatively impacting the next quarter? If so, will there be some positive impact coming from the cost side on the wire rope and the other businesses to negate that impact?

If we take a look at the steel prices have increased meaningfully during the quarter around 13% Q-o-Q, but the EBITDA per ton has improved by only approximately 3% Q-o-Q. Additionally, the EBITDA margins contracted sequentially despite a lower contribution from the plasticated LRPC business. So, if you could just help us understand the key factors which limited the EBITDA per ton expansion.

quarters.summary: Usha Martin closed FY26 with consolidated revenue of INR 3,691 crore and Operating EBITDA of INR 705 crore (19.1% margin), ending the year net-cash positive at INR 332 crore. Management enters FY27 targeting a minimum 20% operating margin, 10-12% volume growth over the next 2-3 years, capex of ~INR 300 crore over the next 2 years to expand rope, specialized wire and plasticated LRPC capacity, and scale-up of Oceanfibre synthetic slings and plasticated LRPC, while continuing to evaluate organic and inorganic growth opportunities, even as Middle East geopolitical conflict and elevated input costs (steel, gas/LPG) pose near-term headwinds.

Expected rope volume growth with Middle East impact

subsections.label: Cost & Margin Drivers
points: Rope volumes came in lower than expected due to Middle East crisis impacting demand by about 900 tons in the quarter; excluding this, rope volume growth would have been about 8% for the quarter.
Q4 rope volume growth was about 5%, impacted by Middle East disruption.
Wire Rope international price crossed INR 300,000 per ton for the first time, reflecting a fairly healthy product mix.
Standalone operations are now entirely debt-free, an important milestone; company debt-free across all geographies except one.
Free cash flow of INR 457 crore achieved despite consciously building inventory buffers to manage supply chain disruption from the geopolitical situation.

Cost efficiencies from 'One Usha Martin' program (fixed employee cost down 3%, admin expenses down over 7%) contributed to margin improvement alongside product mix shift and rising international revenue share (55% to 57%).

subsections.label: Order Book Visibility
points: Growing order book from new customers for H1 FY27 in value-added rope applications - oil and offshore, elevators, port cranes and mining.
Europe order book pickup looking strong, giving good visibility into H1 FY27.
Fairly healthy order book for specialized/higher value-added products with good visibility for H1; company does not quantify specific order book numbers.
85% of business comes through the replacement market, supported by strong dealer network in India and own distribution arms/subsidiaries internationally.
No pushback in demand seen from Europe/America markets; a lot of projects and inquiries in the pipeline; some good orders secured for H1.

subsections.label: Middle East Demand Impact
points: Ongoing Middle East conflict led to slower customer activity and project delays in Dubai and Saudi Arabia; volumes came in below normal levels, impacting rope volumes by about 900 tons in Q4.
If Middle East conflict resolves, management expects a huge opportunity from reconstruction as well as oil & offshore production activities; plant operations in the region remain normal and safe.

International revenue share of total topline
International revenue share of total topline (prior year)
Value-added products share (oil & offshore, crane, other)

subsections.label: International Rope Business
points: International rope business performed well, especially in Europe and the Americas; segments like cranes, elevator and mining saw good traction.
Ranchi's upgraded manufacturing capability and Brunton Shaw's brand now integrated together, enabling execution of larger, more complex projects for global OEMs and end users.
Executed a landmark Oceanmax project at Ranchi facility, including the largest single reel rope production ever undertaken at the plant, demonstrating capability from recent capital investments.

subsections.label: Europe
points: Europe is about 26% of topline; performed well in FY26 with a positive outlook for FY27.
Integrated model between Ranchi manufacturing and Brunton Shaw brand has helped increase share with premium OEM customers, especially in high-performance segments like cranes and mining.
Closer work with customers is providing value-added services instead of just standard products, increasing customer stickiness.
Company market share in Europe is about 10-12% including service centres and factory presence.

subsections.label: United States
points: US grew from 7% to 9% of topline in FY26 despite challenges around tariffs and trade uncertainties.
High-value market (elevator ropes, crane ropes, mining ropes); prior years' work helped navigate challenging conditions.
Company market share in the US remains sub-5%, indicating tremendous opportunity for growth.

subsections.label: Middle East
points: Company is the only manufacturer of Wire Ropes in the GCC region, giving it a larger relative market share despite a large unorganized/general-purpose rope market there.

subsections.label: Value-Added Product Mix
points: Value-added products (oil & offshore, crane and other) share remained roughly steady at 53% between FY25 and FY26, but mix within value-added categories shifted: fishing rope share decreased (lower value, specialized) while crane, mining and elevator share increased (higher value).
Looking at the 53% figure in isolation is not the right way to assess value addition, since realization varies significantly across sub-categories even within value-added ropes.

Most value addition in the business comes from the rope side; in normal Wire and LRPC, the company passes on steel cost increases and maintains realization ratios, while zinc-aluminium wires (GALSTAR) also command higher value.

subsections.label: Plasticated LRPC & Black LRPC
points: Traditional/black LRPC expected to continue at around 48,000 tons in FY27, similar to FY26.
Plasticated LRPC expected to reach close to 5,000-6,000 tons as approvals convert into orders; capacity is 6,000 tons per annum.
Current plasticated LRPC run-rate is around 2,500 tons/year; major customer approvals expected within a couple of weeks, which should help double volumes to 4,000-4,500 tons.
Plasticated LRPC would be gradually substituted for black LRPC over time as approvals and projects materialize; company is working with global players on approvals, close to achieving them.
Once capacity utilization nears full, company would take steps to further augment plasticated LRPC capacity to 8,000-9,000 tons in future phases.

subsections.label: Synthetic Slings (Oceanfibre)
points: In the first year of Oceanfibre synthetic sling business, good traction achieved with customer approvals and repeat orders; significant growth expected this year and in coming years.

subsections.label: Capacity Utilization by Plant
points: Total rope capacity is about 140,000 tons at ~75% utilization.
Wire capacity is about 80,000 tons at 75-78% utilization.
Normal LRPC capacity is about 60,000 tons and plasticated LRPC capacity is about 6,000 tons; both running at about 70% utilization.

subsections.label: Capex Plan (Next 2 Years)
points: Company plans to spend close to INR 300 crore over the next 2 years to expand manufacturing capacity for elevator ropes, specialized wires, and plasticated LRPC.

About 70-75% of capex is planned for rope capacity expansion (~6,000 tons addition), with the balance ~30% for augmenting specialized wire capacity and adding equipment/testing facilities for plasticated LRPC.
Plasticated LRPC capacity may be further augmented to 8,000-9,000 tons in future steps once current 6,000-ton capacity nears full utilization, with costs included in the 2-year capex plan.
Company is also evaluating selective organic and inorganic growth opportunities, particularly in value-added and rigging areas, to expand global presence and get closer to customers.

subsections.label: Gas/LPG Management
points: LPG/propane cost rose from INR 60,000/ton to INR 120,000-130,000/ton; total consumption is 250-300 tons/month across all furnaces (not attributable to a specific product), adding INR 2.5-3 crore/month in cost, with total monthly gas cost now INR 4.5-5 crore.
Company is shifting about 25% of gas requirement to natural gas via a newly completed pipeline near the plant to mitigate cost/availability risk.
Increased gas costs have been passed on to customers as part of product pricing; proactive inventory buffers built to avoid production disruption; no disruption expected on account of gas shortage.

subsections.label: Thailand Plant Modernization
points: Thailand plant is a fully integrated facility starting from wire rod (similar to Ranchi and Hoshiarpur), unlike Dubai/UK plants which start from wire and strands.

Modernization and capacity increase underway for specialized cords and specialized elevator ropes, with focus on value-added products like fine cords for gondola ropes, elevators and port crane ropes.
Significant improvement in Thailand plant operations expected over the next 18 months.

subsections.label: Regional Demand Outlook
points: India demand growing at 6-8% overall; company holds a fairly large market share in India and expects to maintain/slightly increase share, particularly in faster-growing segments like elevator and ports.
Europe and America demand for oil & offshore, crane and wind energy remains strong, driven by countries seeking energy security; no pushback in demand expected from these markets.
Middle East market share benefits from being the only manufacturer of Wire Ropes in the GCC region, despite a large general-purpose/unorganized rope market segment there.

subsections.label: Raw Material & Supply Chain Management
points: Proactively built additional raw material inventory to ensure continuity of supply amid geopolitical tightness in raw material availability, resulting in no disruptions to production.

In wire and LRPC, input cost increases were passed through, keeping margins unaffected; in rope, a better product mix (shift toward higher value-added applications) improved realizations and margins while helping manage volatility in rod and gas prices.
Faster decision-making enabled the company to stay ahead of the geopolitical situation rather than reacting to it.

subsections.label: Competitive Positioning
points: Company competes with players like Bridon, Teufelberger and WireCo in higher-end product segments (oil & offshore, elevators, mining, ports) in markets like Europe and the US.

General-purpose rope market exists in every geography, but company's growth focus and increasing market share is coming from premium segments where OEM approvals, references and field performance data built over the last 2-3 years are being leveraged.
On the GP rope side, the company sells largely through its own rigging shops which use these ropes for finishing.

subsections.label: Industry Growth Benchmark
points: Normal global industry growth for wire rope is about 6-7%; company aims to outgrow this given its low base and market share in markets like Europe and the US, aiming for 10-12% volume growth over the next 2-3 years across Wire Rope, specialized wires and plasticated LRPC.

subsections.label: 'One Usha Martin' Program
points: Program continues to drive efficiency across the group; cost base has become structurally leaner while revenue shifts toward higher-value products, geographies and applications, giving clear operating leverage.
Benefits visible on cost side: fixed employee costs down 3%, admin expenses down over 7% YoY even as topline grew 6%; strong cost discipline now embedded in India as well as subsidiaries.

On revenue side, better collaboration between India and subsidiaries across high-value segments; global references from one location help build markets in others via shared references and performance data.
Cumulative cost savings from the program over the last 18 months are approximately INR 65-70 crore.
Program has become part of company's DNA/discipline; management will continue working on shifting more back-office services to India and further optimizing costs.

subsections.label: Capital Allocation & Inorganic Growth
points: Strong operating cash flows and positive net cash position give bandwidth to invest from internal accruals.

Company will continue targeted capex where demand visibility is clear, and is evaluating selective organic and inorganic opportunities in markets where footprint is still limited, particularly in value-added and rigging areas to get closer to customers globally.

subsections.label: Geopolitical / Middle East Conflict
points: Ongoing Middle East conflict led to slower customer activity, project delays in Dubai and Saudi Arabia, disrupted regional supply chains affecting shipment timing, and below-normal volumes; this contributed to about 900 tons of lost rope volume impact in Q4.
Broader geopolitical situation created tightness in raw material availability, putting pressure on input costs.

subsections.label: Input Cost Inflation
points: Steel and gas prices have been on an increasing trend since January; LPG/propane cost rose sharply from INR 60,000/ton to INR 120,000-130,000/ton.
Company has been able to pass on cost increases in wire and LRPC segments and in wire rope through better product mix, but continued vigilance required amid rising steel, gas and logistics costs.

subsections.label: Trade/Tariff Uncertainty (US)
points: US market faces challenges around tariffs and trade uncertainties on the ground, though company sees good opportunities given its high-value product focus.

subsections.label: Project Timing Risk
points: Parvatmala project real rope demand expected only in 2-3 years as projects move to final implementation stages; wire rope is typically the last part of such projects, and there have been some delays in customer approvals.

subsections.label: FY27 Outlook
points: Three areas give confidence for the year ahead: (1) value-added rope applications (oil & offshore, elevators, port cranes, mining) with growing order book from new customers for H1; oil & offshore has added tailwind from countries prioritizing energy security; (2) newer verticals Oceanfibre synthetic slings and plasticated LRPC maturing, with meaningful scale-up expected in FY27 and beyond; (3) strong balance sheet and cash flow provide bandwidth for capex and selective organic/inorganic growth.

Company enters FY27 from a position of strength: healthy balance sheet, richer product mix, and growth engines beginning to deliver; management states 'the hard work of building the foundation is largely done, now it is about execution and scaling up.'

Margin benchmark raised from earlier 18-19% range to a minimum of 20% operating margin, driven by product mix; absolute EBITDA growth (not just per-ton) remains a key focus given large capacity/capex base.

Volume growth target of 10-12% for the next 2-3 years applies across all segments (Wire Rope, specialized wires like GALSTAR, plasticated LRPC, Parvatmala-related), barring major geopolitical disruptions.
Black LRPC expected to remain around 48,000 tons in FY27 (similar to FY26); plasticated LRPC expected to reach 5,000-6,000 tons as approvals convert to orders.
Thailand plant modernization expected to show significant operational improvement over the next 18 months.

guidance_ledger.statement: Earlier benchmark was 18-19% operating margin; now company feels it should be able to look at a minimum of 20% operating margin due to product mix and other factors.
Company hopes to achieve 10% to 12% volume growth across Wire Rope, specialized wires and plasticated LRPC for the next 2 to 3 years, barring major geopolitical issues.
Company intends to spend close to INR 300 crore over the next 2 years to increase manufacturing capacity for elevator ropes, specialized wires, and plasticated LRPC.
Planning to increase rope capacity by close to 6,000 tons as part of the capex plan.
Plasticated LRPC volume expected to reach close to 5,000 to 6,000 tons as approvals convert into orders.
Once approvals come through, company expects to double plasticated LRPC volumes from current run-rate of 2,500 tons to 4,000-4,500 tons.
Once nearing full utilization of 6,000 ton capacity, company would augment capacity further to 8,000-9,000 tons in steps.
Black LRPC expected to be around 48,000 tons, similar to last year.

guidance_ledger.statement: Expect meaningful scale up in FY27 and beyond for Oceanfibre synthetic business and plasticated LRPC.
Over the next 18 months, significant improvement in operations of the Thailand plant expected as modernization and capacity expansion progress.
Focus would always be to improve overall absolute EBITDA numbers, not just EBITDA per ton, given the large capex and plant capacity created.
Fairly strong order book and visibility for rope demand for the next 6 months at least, though not quantified.
Actual real rope demand from Parvatmala project will likely come in probably 2 to 3 years as projects move to final implementation stages.
Company is evaluating selective organic and inorganic opportunities in markets where footprint is still limited, particularly value-added and rigging areas.

risk_register.note: Broader geopolitical situation created tightness in raw material availability and pressure on input costs; LPG/propane price rose from INR 60,000/ton to INR 120,000-130,000/ton; steel and gas prices rising since January.

themes.label: Margin expansion via product mix
themes.note: Shift toward higher value-added ropes (oil & offshore, elevator, crane, mining) and 'One Usha Martin' cost savings pushed margin benchmark up to a minimum 20% from earlier 18-19%.

themes.label: International expansion & market share gains

key_takeaways: We closed FY26 with consolidated revenue of INR 3,691 crore. Operating EBITDA grew from INR 597 crore last year to INR 705 crore this year, reflecting a margin of 19.1%.
Operating cash flow conversion was healthy at 104% of the operating EBITDA. We ended the year with a net cash position of INR 332 crore compared to a net debt of INR 63 crore in the previous year.

In Q4, revenue stood at INR 979 crore, up 9.3% year-on-year. Operating EBITDA was INR 212 crore, the highest since the sale of the steel business with margins at 21.6% and EBITDA per ton at approximately INR 39,500 per metric ton.

The ongoing conflict in the Middle East led to slower customer activity and project delays in both Dubai and the Saudi Arabian markets. Supply chain in this region were also disruptive, affecting the timing of some shipments. Volumes in the Middle East came in below normal levels.
International revenues now account for 57% of total topline, up from 55% last year, reflecting good traction across global markets.
We closed the year with a consolidated net cash position of INR 332 crore and with standalone operations now entirely debt free. This is an important milestone for the Company.

In next 2 years, we intend to spend close to INR 300 crore to increase our manufacturing capacity for elevator ropes and some more opportunities where we see for some specialized wires and also increasing our capacity of plasticated LRPC.
We hope to be able to get to that 10% to 12% volume growth for the next 2 to 3 years.

SHANKESH.about: Incorporated in 2005, Shankesh Jewellers Limited is engaged in the business of manufacturing and providing customised handcrafted gold jewellery.[1]

quarters.summary: Shankesh Jewellers' maiden earnings call following its NSE/BSE listing on August 25, 2026 covered Q1 FY27 results and the company's business model. Q1 FY27 revenue grew 55% YoY to INR424 crores with strong margin expansion across gross profit, EBITDA and PAT; management attributed growth primarily to product mix (higher-margin 18-karat and festive/intricate collections) rather than volume, which remained approximately flat YoY. Management highlighted a strong 3-year financial trajectory (FY23-FY26) with revenue CAGR of ~21.5%, EBITDA CAGR of ~90.1% and PAT CAGR of ~120%, alongside improving ROCE/ROE and declining debt-to-equity. No specific forward volume/margin guidance was provided despite repeated analyst requests for quantified outlook; management deferred detailed numbers to future quarters/separate calls.

key_figures.label: ROE and ROCE approximate level cited by analyst

subsections.label: Growth drivers
points: Revenue growth of 55% YoY was attributed to better customer relationships and growth from Q1 FY26 to Q1 FY27; volume was described as kept consistent even though gold prices increased.
Management stated the sales growth is majorly because of product mix rather than volume growth, since volume remained approximately the same YoY.

Margin fluctuation quarter-on-quarter is explained by the varying product mix sold each quarter — e.g., festive/exclusive collections (like Diwali or Akshaya Tritiya) carry more intricate, handcrafted designs that command a premium, versus normal-phase periods with more standard products.
Management prefers to focus on absolute profit amount rather than percentage margins when evaluating performance.

subsections.label: Margin sustainability - analyst pushback
points: Multiple analysts (Nishita, Bijal Shah, Amar Nath) pressed management for quantified/mathematical explanation of margin expansion from ~2.5% EBITDA margin in FY23 to ~14% in Q1 FY27, noting no peer (listed B2B or B2C, e.g., Kalyan, Titan, Sky Gold) has shown similar margin expansion.
Management's response remained largely qualitative, citing product mix, gold price gains, and being 'blessed to be in the gold jewellery business,' without providing granular numeric breakdown.

Management acknowledged gold price gains have historically contributed 1-2% or 2-3% plus/minus to margin, but Bijal Shah noted no inventory gain should have occurred this quarter as gold prices moved down, yet margin still expanded.
Sunil Jain offered to arrange a separate call to provide further clarity, noting Q1 FY27 results do not yet reflect IPO proceeds since IPO money came after the Q1 close.

subsections.label: Accounting policy - gold valuation
points: Company follows an average-cost accounting method for gold book value, which explains discrepancies when comparing Q4 vs Q1 (highest gold price quarter) versus consistent margins when comparing Q1 to Q1.
Hedging policy: the company buys back gold immediately at current market price whenever it sells, so there is no hedging loss from gold price re-purchase.
Inventory valuation (weighted average) is currently below market price; management does not see a current requirement for additional inventory hedging.

subsections.label: Working capital and funding
points: Company has no long-term debt/funding; historically has funded working capital (inventory) through internal accruals/equity (profits ploughed back into the business) and short-term working capital loans from banks.

IPO objective included reducing debt; company plans to use IPO equity to repay working capital loans, effectively funding a portion of inventory (which is short-term in nature) via equity, though management maintains that ongoing/growing working capital requirement is a persistent need, not one-off.
Bank funding has supported growth 'since 2009 or 2008'; company now has two funding doors open — bank debt and equity — to use as needed depending on order size and business requirements.
Post IPO, equity base has effectively doubled from INR209 crores (FY26) to approximately INR450 crores.

Cash-flow/operating margin has not yet reflected IPO capital as listing occurred on 25th August 2026, after the Q1 FY27 close; company expects the operating cash flow to improve once IPO capital is deployed.

Trade receivables of INR126 crores equate to ~20-22 days (or 22-23 days) as of balance sheet date, partly due to gold price increases; company gives some credit to established/growing customer relationships, offset by near-cash payment terms to job workers/suppliers.

Employee cost declined sequentially from INR11.3 crores in Q4 FY26 to INR3.3 crores in Q1 FY27 due to a one-off ex-gratia payment to directors in Q4 FY26 that was not repeated; management expects employee cost to remain at or below the Q1 FY27 level going forward.

subsections.label: Corporate vs non-corporate mix
points: Steady shift towards corporate customers over the years — contribution to revenue increasing from 55% in FY24 to 64% in FY26, highlighting growing depth and strength of relationships with established jewellery players.

Corporate clients select designs from Shankesh's stock and also engage in co-creation; billing to corporate clients happens via sales bill (inventory built to the corporate client), with certain corporate clients providing development advances depending on order size — arrangement varies.
Company is purely a B2B business supplying major corporate and individual store retail partners pan-India, including top retailers across cities like Bombay, Patna, Kanpur; no B2C segment.

subsections.label: Product mix - 22K vs 18K
points: 22-karat remains the major revenue driver while 18-karat is a growing market; company had first-mover advantage starting 18-karat handcrafted jewellery three years back.
18-karat jewellery revenue grew from INR18 crores in FY24 to INR221 crores in FY26, reflecting growing acceptance of the product offering and expanding addressable market.
18-karat fetches a somewhat higher margin than 22-karat due to it taking more time to manufacture, though the difference is not described as 'extravagant.'
Wastage/making charges range from approximately 4% to 14% across the handcrafted product mix; management could not comment on machine-made wastage benchmarks as company doesn't specialize in that.

subsections.label: Bridal jewellery focus
points: Approximately 60% of sales comes from bridal jewellery, an area of specialization built over decades.

Bridal/occasion jewellery carries emotional and cultural significance, and customers look for intricate design, customization, personalization, and consistent quality — a key differentiator versus machine-made products.

Management does not view itself as capturing a dominant share of the ~INR4.5 lakh crore bridal jewellery market (part of ~INR8 lakh crore total India jewellery market) but claims a 'lead' via handcrafted specialization; no listed peer specializes purely in bridal jewellery segment per management.

key_figures.label: Wastage loss range for handcrafted jewellery
Manufacturing turnaround time for handcrafted jewellery
Gold price decrease from Q4 FY26 to Q1 FY27

subsections.label: Asset-light karigar model
points: Business is asset-light: company focuses on customer requirement, design, and sourcing while leveraging an established network of karigars for crafting; semi-finished jewellery returns for metal/purity checks, finishing, quality control, labeling, and final stages.
This model provides flexibility to work with customers on specific designs/collections, cater to large/bulk requirements, and understand customized job-work requirements.
Asset-light karigar ecosystem enables supporting higher volumes without a proportionate increase in fixed manufacturing infrastructure.

subsections.label: Job worker / karigar network dynamics
points: Number of job workers (contract manufacturers) has seen a steady decline with increased attrition in FY26, but this reflects industry consolidation/organization — company now prefers working with fewer, larger, more organized contract manufacturers who can offer better design, quality, and finish.

Despite the decline in the number of individual job workers, the overall workforce under contract manufacturers (700-800 people) has increased as capacity per contract manufacturer has grown (e.g., one manager who had 20 people now has 30-35 people).

72 contract manufacturers (job workers) as of FY26, each managing sizeable manufacturing teams; management states current karigar base can scale to accommodate 30%, 40%, or 50% growth without bottleneck.
Management stated they do not see any current bottleneck to scaling volumes with existing karigar strength, and remain open-minded to challenges as they scale.

subsections.label: Handcrafted vs mechanized production
points: Manufacturing takes approximately two to three weeks for a batch of jewellery (e.g., 10-20 pieces), reflecting delicate hand-designed process.
A very minimal portion of pieces uses 3D printing techniques to add a decorative touch ('tadka') to designs, but the major focus remains fully handcrafted.

Company uses handcrafted karigar techniques rather than automated CNC or 3D printing at scale, citing the emotional/design differentiation of handmade jewellery versus machine-made ('masala chai made by hand' analogy).

subsections.label: Pan-India presence
points: Company serves across India, with Maharashtra, Bihar, Odisha, Tamil Nadu, and Uttar Pradesh as established core markets where strong customer relationships have been developed.
Pan-India presence is well-diversified across West (32%), East (28%), South (21%), and North (18%) India in FY26, reflecting a broad-based customer footprint.
Growth opportunity identified in expanding geographic presence while continuing to deepen presence in established markets.

key_figures.label: Bridal jewellery market size
key_figures.value: more than 50% of INR8 lakh crores

subsections.label: Company history and milestones
points: Shankesh Jewellers was established in 1992 focused on high-quality, handcrafted gold jewellery and strong customer relationships.
Shankesh Jewellers Private Limited was incorporated in 2006.
First INR500 crores turnover achieved in 2021; first INR1,000 crores turnover achieved in 2024.
Converted into a public limited company in 2025.
Made public market debut with listing on NSE and BSE on 25th August, 2026 — this was described as the company's maiden earnings call.

subsections.label: Growth avenues identified by management
points: Deepen relationship with existing customers as they expand retail networks — objective to grow wallet share alongside customers.

Structural opportunity from ongoing formalization/organization of the Indian jewellery industry, where established customer relationships, craftsmanship capabilities, quality processes, and asset-light production ecosystem can become increasingly valuable.
Continue strengthening customer retention through co-creation and customized product development.
Expand geographic presence while deepening presence in established markets.
Leverage asset-light karigar ecosystem to support higher volumes without proportionate increase in fixed manufacturing infrastructure.
Expand breadth of product portfolio across bridal, festive, contemporary, and bespoke jewellery in both 22-karat and 18-karat segments.

subsections.label: Potential future product expansion
points: Company is researching feasibility of moving into 14-karat and 9-karat gold jewellery given rising popularity amid higher gold prices, though gold hardness increases at lower karats making handcrafting more difficult; no current commitment, contingent on market demand.
No current plans for studded diamond jewellery, but open to entering that segment if market demand requires.
No current plans to set up a machine-made jewellery manufacturing unit; company will remain focused on handcrafted segment for now, though open to opportunities in the future.

key_figures.label: Estimated cost of working capital loan

subsections.label: Gold price volatility
points: Highly fluctuating gold prices (up and down) create margin pressure industry-wide; rising bond yields amid current geopolitical situation are putting pressure on gold prices internationally, with expected impact in India as well.
Company mitigates hedging risk via a 'buy what we sell' policy — immediately repurchasing gold at current market price whenever sold — avoiding losses from re-hedging at different prices.
Average-cost accounting method for gold book value can create sequential (Q4 vs Q1) margin comparison distortions, though YoY (Q1 vs Q1) comparisons remain more consistent per management.

subsections.label: Customer in-house integration risk
points: Analyst raised concern that major customers (e.g., Kalyan, P.N. Gadgil) are increasingly moving towards integrated models, appointing their own karigars in-house instead of outsourcing to companies like Shankesh, potentially threatening Shankesh's outsourcing-based value proposition.

Management responded that handcrafted jewellery requires years of specialized experience, creativity, and design capability that cannot be easily replicated in-house; customers will continue to value co-creation, design structure, and design mix that Shankesh provides.

subsections.label: Competitive intensity / lack of differentiation clarity
points: Analyst (Amar Nath) challenged management to explain the company's competitive moat versus larger peers in a market where many established karigar-based players (e.g., in Bengal) have operated for hundreds of years.

Management's response centered on handcrafted specialization, emotional attachment to bridal jewellery, and being a preferred vendor to top customers (backed by industry recognitions/awards), without providing quantified differentiation versus peers.

subsections.label: Working capital gap - receivables/payables
points: Analyst flagged a potential working capital gap given the company pays suppliers largely in cash/near-instantly while extending credit to customers, raising questions on funding of this gap alongside inventory financing.
Management confirmed some credit is extended to customers as relationships deepen over time; trade receivables were ~20-22 days as of balance sheet date.

subsections.label: Lack of quantified forward guidance
points: Management declined to provide specific volume CAGR or margin guidance for the next 3 years when directly asked, stating 'as of now, I'm not ready with any figures in my hand' but indicated more clarity would be provided in Q2/Q3.
Management indicated broad expectation of growth 'at a certain pace, which is almost similar or something better' to historical performance, without quantification.

In response to repeated analyst requests (particularly from Amar Nath and Bijal Shah) for a mathematical/granular breakdown of margin drivers and sustainability, management offered to address further via a separate call and through the IR agency, deferring detailed quantification.

Sunil Jain noted that Q1 FY27 results do not yet reflect the impact of IPO proceeds, as IPO money was received after the Q1 close, implying future quarters may show different dynamics once capital is deployed.

guidance_ledger.statement: Analyst asked for volume outlook and sustainable EBITDA margins for next 3 years with CAGR figures; management stated 'Sorry, as of now, I'm not ready with any figures in my hand. But obviously, as the future comes in, quarter two, quarter three, we'll be ready with things in hand as well.'

Analyst asked if 10% PAT margin is sustainable long term; management responded 'the product mix and what we are doing right now, obviously, we see that the growth is there in the company and we try to achieve whatever best we can in the coming future as well' without confirming a specific number.
Management stated 'our future expectations also stays down the same line that we grow at a certain pace, which is almost similar or something better to what we have done earlier.'
Management is researching feasibility of moving into 14-karat and 9-karat jewellery 'as and when the market requirement comes'; currently not in these segments.
'As of now, not thought of it, sir. As the, if the market is requiring, for sure, we'll get into that sector as well.'
'For now, we will still focus on this [handcrafted] segment as well... in the coming future, whenever we get any opportunity, we are open to thoughts.'
Management indicated employee cost will remain around INR3.3 crores level or even less in upcoming quarters (versus INR11.3 crores in Q4 FY26 driven by one-off ex-gratia).
Management stated funding decisions between debt and equity 'will be taken as and when required only,' with 'two doors open' (bank debt and equity) depending on order size and growth needs.
Management offered to provide more granular numeric detail on margin drivers via a separate call and through IR agency, deferring quantification asked by multiple analysts.

risk_register.risk: Gold price volatility / fluctuation impacting margins industry-wide
risk_register.note: Company mitigates hedging risk via 'buy what we sell' policy — immediately repurchasing gold at current market price when sold; average-cost accounting can create sequential margin comparison distortions.

risk_register.risk: Customers moving to integrated/in-house karigar models (disintermediation risk)
risk_register.note: Analyst flagged that major customers like Kalyan, P.N. Gadgil are moving towards in-house karigar appointment instead of outsourcing; management maintains handcrafted specialization and co-creation relationships remain valuable and hard to replicate.

risk_register.risk: Lack of clear competitive moat / commoditized handcrafted karigar market
risk_register.note: Analyst challenged management on differentiation versus larger peers and hundreds-of-years-old karigar traditions (e.g., in Bengal); management's response was largely qualitative (handcrafted specialization, preferred-vendor recognitions) without quantified differentiation.

risk_register.risk: Working capital gap on receivables/payables alongside inventory financing

risk_register.risk: Negative/constrained operating cash flow due to growing working capital needs
risk_register.note: Management confirmed the company does not have long-term funding; growth requires ongoing working capital funded via internal accruals/equity and bank facilities, and cash flow effect of IPO proceeds not yet reflected in Q1 FY27.

risk_register.risk: Job worker/karigar attrition and consolidation trend
risk_register.note: Steady decline in job worker count and increased attrition in FY26 attributed to industry organization/consolidation toward fewer, larger, better-quality contract manufacturers; overall karigar headcount under contract manufacturers has grown despite fewer named job workers.

risk_register.risk: Lack of quantified forward guidance reducing investor confidence
risk_register.note: Multiple analysts (Nishita, Bijal Shah, Amar Nath, Lavita Lasrado) requested specific numeric guidance/breakdowns on margin drivers and volume outlook; management repeatedly deferred to future quarters, citing lack of figures on hand.

themes.label: Margin expansion vs quantification gap
themes.note: Q1 FY27 EBITDA/PAT margins expanded sharply (EBITDA margin ~14%, PAT margin ~10%) but management could not provide granular quantified breakdown of drivers despite repeated analyst requests.

themes.label: Product mix shift (18K growth)
themes.note: 18-karat jewellery revenue grew from INR18 crores (FY24) to INR221 crores (FY26), fetching somewhat higher margins than 22-karat and driving mix-led growth.

themes.label: Corporate client mix deepening
themes.note: Corporate customer contribution rose from 55% (FY24) to 66% (Q1 FY27), reflecting deepening relationships with established jewellery brands.

themes.label: Gold price volatility and hedging policy
themes.note: Company follows a 'buy what we sell' policy to avoid re-hedging losses, using average-cost accounting; gold price swings and rising bond yields remain an industry-wide margin risk.

themes.label: Asset-light karigar model / disintermediation risk
themes.note: Asset-light karigar network enables scalability without heavy capex, but customers (e.g., Kalyan, P.N. Gadgil) increasingly building in-house karigar capacity poses a long-term risk to the outsourcing model.

themes.label: IPO-led capital structure improvement
themes.note: Post-IPO equity base nearly doubled to ~INR450 crores from INR209 crores (FY26), intended to reduce debt and fund growing working capital needs; debt-to-equity improved from 2.1x (FY23) to 0.8x (FY26).

themes.label: Lack of forward guidance
themes.note: Management repeatedly declined to provide specific volume/margin CAGR guidance for coming years, deferring detailed numbers to future quarters or separate calls.

key_takeaways: Revenue from operations at INR424 crores, growing 55% year-on-year from INR273 crores in Q1 FY26.
Gross profit at INR66 crores, up by 95% year-on-year and 7% quarter-on-quarter, accompanied by gross margin expansion of 323 basis points year-on-year and quarter-on-quarter, respectively.
EBITDA stood at INR61 crores, increasing 92% year-on-year and 30% quarter-on-quarter, with EBITDA margin improving by 279 basis points year-on-year and 504 basis points quarter-on-quarter.

PAT increased to INR43 crores in Q1 FY27 from INR22 crores from Q1 FY26, showing increase of 100% year-on-year and 36% quarter-on-quarter, with PAT margin improving by 230 basis points year-on-year and 385 basis points quarter-on-quarter.

Corporate customers contributed 66% of Q1 FY27 revenue, while non-corporate customer contribute 34%. Within product portfolio, 22-karat jewellery contributes approximately 80%, and 18-karat jewellery contributes approximately 20%.

Revenue has increased from INR909 crores in financial year '23 to INR1,062 crores in financial year '24 and INR1,404 crores in financial year '25 and INR1,631 crores in financial year '26, representing a 3-year CAGR of approximately 21.5%.

EBITDA has increased from INR23 crores in financial year '23 to INR158 crores in financial year '26, representing a CAGR of approximately 90.1%. PAT has increased from INR10 crores to INR107 crores over the same period, representing a CAGR of approximately 120%.
The financial year '26 ROCE stood at 41.6% and ROE at 50.9%. At the same time, our debt-to-equity ratio has improved significantly from 2.1x in financial year '23 to 0.8x in financial year '26.
pressing_questions: Management, since you are a new IPO company and listed in the market, you know, this question has just been, you might have already seen in the last 1 hour, we, as an investor and a fund house, we need a data. And I appreciate your answers in all the questions, which is quite generic in nature, sir. We need certain figures, certain growth outlooks, and certain quantified numbers. A verbal explanation can help, but the question is since many of the participants has asked, including me as well, because your current numbers are quite extraordinary compared to what your peers are already delivering in the market... it is better to be explained by numbers to the people to understand from where it is coming, and then we can understand whether it is sustainable going forward, or it is maybe happening for one-time situation.

So, this 2.5% EBITDA margin going to 14% margin, which is probably the highest in the industry, can you give us some mathematical number that what is your product mix which has changed and what is the margin in that category and how it has changed?

Sir, this quarter there was no gold price gain, as gentleman before me explained, and your margin has expanded. And I do not see in this quarter any of the company which is there in gold have seen [margin expansion]. It is extremely surprising that this quarter, ideally, you should have an inventory loss, and in that you are seeing a margin expansion.
Sir, would you be able to give any numbers to the CAGR, your future volume outlook, and at least for next 3 years? Any visibility if you can provide?

Now, once those your customers going more towards an integrated model, how big that is a threat for you? Because if they started doing everything on their own, then the value what your company is, which is a kind of an outsourcing karigari model, how sustainable it is?

DLF.about: DLF Ltd with its subsidiaries, associates and JVs is engaged in real estate development, from the identification and acquisition of land to planning, execution, construction and marketing of projects. It is also engaged in business of leasing, generation of power, provision of maintenance services, hospitality and recreational services which are related to the overall development of real estate business.[1]

quarters.summary: DLF reported a resilient but muted Q1 FY27 in pre-sales terms (INR 657 crores of new sales bookings due to deferment of the Aureva senior living launch), while cash generation, rental annuity performance, and balance sheet strength remained strong; management reiterated its broad guidance for the year's sales target and highlighted a deep rental pipeline (11-12 million sq ft under construction plus further pipeline in Cyber City, Hyderabad, Cyber City 2), with FY28 expected to be an inflection point when large projects like the Arbour begin contributing to the P&L and unlocking embedded gross margin potential (~INR 39,000 crores).

subsections.label: Accounting practice
points: Company continues to follow a conservative completed contract method of accounting under current applicable laws and standards, which recognizes revenue and profit from projects only once completed in the relevant period.

Management believes FY28 will be an inflection point from a reporting perspective, as large products starting with the Arbour will begin to contribute to the P&L, unlocking the significant embedded gross margin potential (~INR 39,000 crores) that management has highlighted over several quarters.

subsections.label: Segment reporting change
points: From the current quarter, DLF Limited has started reporting segment financials depicting individual performance of both development and rental businesses.
A new slide has been added to the presentation showing the combined scale of the rental business across DLF, DCCDL and Atrium.

subsections.label: DCCDL profit variance
points: DCCDL PAT of INR 717 crores in Q1 FY27 is slightly lower than Q4 FY26 (~INR 780 crores) because Q4 included one-time entries such as DTA and other items that had bumped up the profit.

subsections.label: Credit ratings
points: DCCDL ratings from CRISIL and ICRA continue to be AAA, with a reasonably fine borrowing rate at the portfolio level (7.14% for the quarter).

subsections.label: Land acquisition
points: Company pursuing a couple of strategic land parcels within Gurgaon in addition to contiguous parcels; some advances made in the previous quarter under agreements expected to fructify over the next 3-4 quarters.
The INR 545 crores spent over the last 2 quarters includes an INR 80-crore deposit (10% EMD) for an NCR region auction that has not yet happened/fructified.
As land parcels fructify over the next 1-2 quarters, they are expected to translate into additional GAVs.

subsections.label: Dahlias sustenance sales
points: Sales pace for Dahlias this quarter (fewer units than the typical 12-15 per quarter historically) is attributed to a deliberate, algorithm-based price increase strategy rather than a demand slowdown; entry price is now INR 100 crores+, ranging up to ~INR 160-170 crores on higher floors, with realizations over INR 1 lakh per sq ft (up to INR 1.2-1.25 lakh on higher floors).

Cumulative Dahlias sales reached almost 65%, versus an original 3.5-year sell-out target now expected to be achieved in about 15-16 months, with the remaining sell-out horizon expected to take another 3 years, compared to a historical benchmark of ~20% sell-through per year over 5 years for typical super luxury projects.

Presentations and sales attention are being calibrated to the new higher price points, requiring more time and attention per transaction versus lower-ticket products (e.g., USD 500,000-600,000 products).
Momentum is also linked to the anticipated unveiling of the Dahlias Experience Center after Diwali.
Interest for Dahlias is coming from all over the country and NRIs (25-30% of business), with management citing ongoing meetings outside Delhi NCR (e.g., Kolkata) as evidence.
Management indicated more sales have been recorded this quarter but withheld disclosure pending completion of paperwork, hinting at upcoming benchmark-setting news.
Almost all lower and mid floors of South tower and most mid/low floors of North tower are sold; some high floors have also sold.

Management stated there is no direct 1:1 correlation between price appreciation and sales velocity — pricing follows a planned price matrix and pace of sales, and is an iterative process; the next Dahlias phase is dependent on both physical construction progress (raft level currently; construction takes 3-3.5 years) and commercial (sales) progress, implying at least a 3-year cycle before complete sell-out.

People are expected to acclimatize to new price points given demonstrated value versus Camellias, Aralias and Magnolias; DLF Golf Links is described as 'the Beverly Hills of India,' with an anecdotal neighbor resale upside example of INR 30-35 crores.

subsections.label: Land acquisition/cost trends
points: Construction costs remain stable and strong versus last year, with average cost increasing but trajectory/momentum remaining strong.
Land acquisition activity has picked up; company evaluates parcels of interest as they arise, pursuing strategic Gurgaon parcels.

subsections.label: Goa Residential Project
points: Goa Residential project (distinct from the Goa Mall) is involved in PIL-type litigation, not uncommon in that region.

All approvals for Goa residential have been secured; management is choosing caution, avoiding accepting customer payments/creating third-party interest until the litigation path is clearer — a customer-first approach.
Nothing legally stops DLF from launching, but company is deliberately holding back pending clarity.

If Goa residential doesn't launch this year, the impact on the INR 20,000 crore guidance is limited since Goa was only around 10% (~couple of thousand crores) of that guidance; management expects to comfortably swing the target via other launches.

subsections.label: Mumbai strategy
points: Following a spectacular launch last year, a follow-through launch is expected within this fiscal year, possibly within the calendar year.
The existing Mumbai development has potential to become a more than 5 million sq ft development over the next few years.

Management is exploring other Mumbai opportunities ('dipping toes in water' project done well) but will be selective, seeking projects where DLF can add true value; Mumbai remains part of medium/long-term strategy.

subsections.label: Cyber City 2 / SPR
points: DLF has consolidated 70-80 acres of land at SPR (referred to as Cyber City 2); sizing and launch timing decisions have not yet been finalized and are expected to be taken sometime next year.

subsections.label: Privana ecosystem
points: Next phase of Privana launch expected early next year (not last quarter as earlier hoped).
South, West and North phases of Privana are all sold out; secondary market demand and appreciation are strong (secondary sale prices INR 2,500-4,000/sq ft).

No plotted development scheme planned for Privana as a general product; any small plotted enclave would only be for collaborator obligations. Privana continues to be positioned as a high-rise scheme, adjoining a 10,000-hectare green lung, viewed as the next big contiguous project after DLF5.
Next Privana phase expected to be a taller/more evolved product than the North phase.

subsections.label: Hamilton 2 / Aureva launches
points: Aureva (retirement/senior living policy scheme) launch is pending final RERA approvals, expected in the coming weeks; deferment of this launch caused the muted quarterly sales bookings.
Hamilton 2 product is still on the drawing board with a good level of market interest/excitement; company will announce once the product is finalized, expected in H2 of the fiscal year.

subsections.label: Office leasing environment
points: AI-related hiring impact debate among multinationals/GCCs and the Iran-U.S. war dynamics slowed decision-making of global companies over the last 2 quarters, as uncertainty deterred commitments.
Over the last 4-5 weeks, management has observed 'green shoots' of international companies returning, making enquiries and starting to take decisions; Q2 and Q3 expected to be good quarters.
Newer projects — Cyber Park, Atrium Place, Downtown Gurgaon, Downtown Chennai — are nearly 100% leased.
Capex programs for Downtown Gurgaon Phase 2 and Downtown Chennai Phase 2 are progressing at full speed.

Improved leasing activity is driven by GCC and other multinational companies who were awaiting signs of resolution in the Iran-U.S. war before making decisions; local Indian companies and existing tenant expansions continued uninterrupted throughout the period. Large-format demand (250,000 sq ft+, 300,000 sq ft+) has now started moving.

Overall rental portfolio exceeds 50 million sq ft, with occupancy over 95% on a space basis and over 97% on a value basis; portfolio rental growth was 8.5-9% YoY in Q1 FY27; Downtown Gurgaon Phase 2 leasing at about 40% and Taramani (Chennai) pre-leasing at 17-18%.

subsections.label: Retail / malls
points: Three new malls (Midtown Plaza, Summit Plaza, Goa) are becoming operational; with the Goa OC received in July, all 3 malls will be operational in the current financial year, leading to a significant increase in DLF entity rental run-rate.
Midtown Plaza is fully operational (85% open, 96-97% leased).
Summit Plaza had its opening pooja and soft launch; expected to reach full bloom in the next 2-2.5 months; leasing about 90%.

Goa mall (705,000 sq ft super area, expected rental INR 170-175/sq ft) got its OC (as of July 31, leasing at 64%, targeting 85-90% in the next 6-8 weeks); finishing works and leasing in progress; targeting mall opening either end of this year or early next year; a number of brands unfamiliar with the Goa market are taking longer to commit, but momentum is strong; anchor fit-out to start later this month.
Retail consumption and spend in Q1 have been per budget (slightly better), with 13.5-14% growth YoY.
Company continues focus on sustainability, green initiatives, safety and compliance with 'zero tolerance.'

subsections.label: CAM charges
points: Minimum wage revisions have had a marginal impact (~2-2.5%) on CAM costs; no pushback from tenants since it is a pass-through under a national law, and the company gets CAM charges audited annually, sharing results transparently with tenant partners (refund or true-up based on audited certificate).

subsections.label: Rental ramp-up / stabilization
points: Midtown Plaza and Summit Plaza are just starting; both expected to reach steady rental state by Q4 FY27.
Goa mall expected to stabilize by around May/June of next year.
Atrium Place Tower 1 expected to receive OC in September, after which it will move to steady-state rental for that tower; Atrium Place currently has a weighted average rental of about INR 175/sq ft.
Data Center 3 in Noida will add to rental income around March/April of next year.
Otherwise, the current rental base is largely steady state.
Group-level rental income was roughly INR 1,600 crores in Q1 FY27, with FY27 exit rentals guided between INR 7,300 and 7,500 crores at the group level.

subsections.label: Commercial expansion pipeline (next 11 million sq ft)
points: Downtown Gurgaon Phase 2 expected to finish by end of FY29; includes an iconic tower 'One Downtown' with a multilevel car park to be consumed within Phase 2 basements.
Chennai Towers 4 and 5 (3.5 million sq ft) expected to complete by beginning of FY28.
About 3.5-4 million sq ft of leasing remains to be done across these two new projects.
Construction start for Hyderabad or Cyber City (part of the next 11 million sq ft pipeline) is on the radar, but detailed planning likely to begin sometime next year.

subsections.label: Rental pricing trends in Gurgaon
points: Rentals have risen materially between older Cyber City buildings and newer developments; Downtown Phase 2 new leasing now averaging INR 200/sq ft versus current Cyber City average of INR 140-150, with new buildings (post ~2 years) expected to command INR 210-220/sq ft, and Downtown 4 currently averaging INR 150-155/sq ft.
On a like-to-like (time-adjusted) basis, the rental premium of new buildings over old is about 20%, versus a 30% headline gap, since new buildings will only be delivered about 2 years later.
