subsections.label: Data center strategy
points: The data center business comprises 3 components: real estate, power, and data storage/rack technology.

DLF has decided to focus only on the real estate component — constructing data centers for companies as real estate developers — and does not intend to get into buying technology or running data centers itself.

subsections.label: Land monetization strategy
points: In response to peers rapidly expanding into data centers to monetize land parcels faster, DLF confirmed it will remain a real-estate-only developer for data center projects and not enter the technology/operations side of that business.

subsections.label: Strategic land parcels
points: Company is pursuing a couple of more strategic (versus purely contiguous) land parcels within Gurgaon, with advances made in the prior quarter under agreements expected to fructify over the next 3-4 quarters.

subsections.label: Geopolitical/macro uncertainty
points: AI's impact on hiring by multinationals/GCCs and the Iran-U.S. war dynamics (from February onward) slowed global companies' decision-making over the last two quarters, as businesses dislike uncertainty.
Management now sees green shoots in the last 4-5 weeks with international companies returning and starting to make decisions, expecting Q2 and Q3 to be good quarters.

subsections.label: Litigation risk (Goa Residential)
points: The Goa Residential project (distinct from the mall) is involved in PIL-type litigation, described as not uncommon in that part of the country.
Despite having all approvals, management is choosing a cautious, customer-first approach — not accepting customer payments or creating third-party interest until the litigation path is clearer.

subsections.label: Cost/regulatory risk
points: Minimum wage revisions increased CAM costs marginally (2-2.5%), though this is a pass-through with no tenant pushback given transparent annual audits.

subsections.label: Broad guidance reiteration
points: Management stated the current quarter was a muted pre-sales quarter due to the Aureva launch deferment, but hopes to still stick to the broad sales guidance for the year (~INR 20,000 crores for FY27).
Continued focus on cash flows, embedded margins, and fiscal prudence.
Strategic land investments will continue as opportunities arise.
Rental business continuing at an excellent clip in both leasing and rental income growth.

Deep rental pipeline: over 11-12 million sq ft under construction across Downtown Gurgaon, Downtown Chennai and Atrium; a further few million sq ft pipeline in Cyber City itself, plus Hyderabad and Cyber City 2 — described as possibly the deepest rental pipeline in the country's real estate sector.

subsections.label: FY28 inflection point
points: FY28 expected to be an inflection point from a reporting perspective as large products, starting with the Arbour, begin contributing to the P&L, unlocking the ~INR 39,000 crore gross margin potential highlighted over several quarters.

key_takeaways: Overall collection for the current quarter stood at INR 2,406 crores. Operating cash flow continues to be strong at over INR 1,300 crores in the quarter.
New sales bookings for the quarter were INR 657 crores, reflecting the timing impact of deferment of our launch of Aureva, our senior living product.

Our rental portfolio stands at over 50 million square feet and continues to operate at an industry-leading occupancy at over 95% in terms of space and over 97% in terms of value. Our revenue stood at INR 1,605 crores, yielding an EBITDA of INR 476 crores for the quarter.
Net profit for the quarter was INR 794 crores versus INR 766 crores in the same period last year.

We strongly believe that FY28 would be an inflection point from a reporting perspective, wherein all our large products, starting from the Arbour, will start to contribute to the P&L and consequently, we will start to unlock the significant gross margin potential that we have been highlighting over the last several quarters now.

In the current quarter, in the month of July, we also got the operation certificate for our mall in Goa. With this, all 3 malls in DLF Limited will be operational in the current financial year, leading to a significant increase in run rate of rental business within the DLF entities itself.

Moving to DCCDL. Our consolidated revenue stood at INR1,917 crores, reflecting a growth of 10% year-over-year, yielding an EBITDA of INR 1,474 crores. Net profit continues to be a strong performance of INR 717 crores, a growth of over 20% year-over-year.
This quarter from a pre-sales standpoint was a muted quarter and thank you for understanding the reason for that. And hopefully, we still stick to our broad guidance for sales for the year.
pressing_questions: What is the status of our Goa project? And are we still on track for the INR200 billion guidance in the event that the Goa project doesn't come through in FY27?

Since we've got a very good price appreciation, are we going to compromise on sales velocity to price appreciation and try to take the prices higher? Or it's going to be the other way around now that the project has got literally revalued...going forward, since we have 2 more phases left here, we can look at a higher sales velocity or we're going to look at holding off a higher sales velocity because of further price increases?

quarters.summary: FY26 closed with record collections, strong cash surplus, zero gross debt in the development business, and healthy sales bookings in line with guidance. Rental business delivered exceptional NOI growth with high occupancy, and management reiterated a mid-teens NOI growth / 20-25% CAGR guidance over the next 4-5 years, while for FY27 the company plans to broadly stay on the ~INR 20,000 crore sales booking trajectory and ~INR 9,000 crore new margin creation, with cash generation and dividend trajectory expected to remain strong.

subsections.label: Cash & Capital Allocation
points: Zero gross debt position achieved in the development business in FY26, as committed previously.
Board recommended dividend of INR 8 per share, a 33% YoY growth, in line with stated commitment of enhancing shareholder return combined with strong performance and growing cash flows.

Dividend is driven by two pieces: a large chunk (roughly two-thirds) is Cyber City's dividend to DLF, which operates like a normal rental company with debt-to-NOI at a comfortable sub-3.5x level generating more FCF; DLF's own cash flows are also growing.
No formal dividend guidance is given, but trajectory across the last 4-5 years has been continuing growth and management hopes this is maintained.

Three-pronged approach to deploying the RERA-escrowed cash (INR 11,200 crores) once unlocked from FY27/28 onwards: (1) increasing shareholder return, (2) capex for the annuity/rental business pipeline already committed, (3) opportunistic margin-accretive land/deal reinvestment.

subsections.label: Cost/Overhead Trends
points: Marketing brokerage payout is linked to collections and paid on a milestone basis; a robust collection in the previous quarter caused brokerage to become due and bump up in the current quarter sequentially.

Marketing costs are a normal phenomena; overheads bump could be year-end provisioning; full-year overhead number should be taken as guidance and is not expected to change further, though quarter-on-quarter view can be misleading.
Deferred tax assets recognized in 1-2 legal entities with accumulated losses in the last financial year; tax refund flows seen in the current year are expected to continue in the future.

subsections.label: Revenue Recognition Accounting Policy
points: Company follows the Completed Contract Method (CCM), which is conservative; large projects starting from Arbour will start getting delivered from FY27/28 onwards, creating a virtuous cycle of free cash flow and healthy margin booking in the P&L as projects reach final delivery.

subsections.label: Launch Pipeline Detail
points: Healthy launch pipeline of almost INR 20,000 crores for the year, comprising Gurugram products, Mumbai, Goa, some residual projects, and Dahlias.
Gurugram: 2 good projects lined up — Senior Living and Hamilton 2.
Goa: approvals all done; a PIL is pending, company wants to avoid creating third-party rights before proceeding; otherwise ready to launch.
Privana last phase: not expected this year, planned for next year.

FY26,27 should have 1 big launch in DLF City, expected in the INR 8,000-9,000 crore range or higher; Arbour Senior Living launch expected; next phase launch of Westpark; Dahlias to continue selling; Goa to come into play at some stage.
Arbour Senior Living launch expected in the next 1-3 months (within this calendar year).

The medium-term launch pipeline update (currently ~INR 60,000 crores) is a status update against the original INR 1,14,000 crore, 5-year pipeline laid out about 2 years back; every quarter the company updates cumulative launched vs to-be-launched pipeline; it is not the pipeline ceiling — next phase projects are already identified but will be unlocked at a pace matching market absorption and execution capability.

subsections.label: Presales Philosophy
points: Management considers presales one of the 'wrongest metrics' to track the company; company could do INR 50,000 crores of presales given land bank and demand but chooses to prioritize margins and cash flows over presales growth.
Comfortable generating INR 9,000-10,000 crores of margin every year and INR 7,000-8,000 crores of free cash flow every year on the DevCo side.
From next year onward, company enters a 'virtuous cycle of completions' from a bookkeeping standpoint.
Guidance can be revised upward if demand continues to be strong — there is an upside risk to the ~INR 20,000 crore guidance, but base case trajectory is maintained.
Company was highest in presales in some years historically, but that was a byproduct of chasing margins/products, not a target in itself.

subsections.label: Dahlias Demand & Pricing Trajectory
points: 60% of Dahlias already sold; last 32 units sold have transacted at almost INR 100 crores (about INR 90-odd crores), with a South/North price differential of about INR 20-30 crores depending on size and PLC.

Units originally priced around INR 60 crores are now at INR 90 crores; units originally around INR 75 crores are now about INR 110 crores — phenomenal price growth attributed to overall offering appeal (Experience Centre still pending).
Dahlias per-sale average now touching about INR 135 crores.
Camellias (ready product) currently trading between INR 80-150 crores; Dahlias has caught up to near Camellias pricing much faster than expected (achieved in ~1.5 years versus an expected 4 years).
On a per-square-foot super-area basis, Camellias trades around INR 1,20,000/sq ft while Dahlias averages about INR 1 lakh/sq ft — roughly a 20% differential.
On a carpet-area basis, Camellias/Dahlias prices exceed INR 1,50,000-1,60,000 per sq ft, which management says has caught up to or exceeded super-luxury pricing in South Mumbai/Worli.
No single developer in the country has crossed double-digit unit sales in the INR 100 crore-plus price bracket in a quarter, underscoring the scale of Dahlias demand.

subsections.label: Land Bank Monetization
points: North & metros land bank of ~40 million sq ft (outside the immediate launch pipeline) is considered marketable, though some parcels may not fetch best pricing today and are better launched in 2-3 years.
Example cited: Privana would have monetized very differently if launched 6 years earlier versus its actual launch timing, illustrating the value of timing launches to market readiness.
Total balance potential land bank of 137 million sq ft is described as fully monetizable, contingent on right price point, right demand timing, and matching execution capability.

subsections.label: Q4/FY26 Rental Highlights
points: Atrium Place (JV with Hines) is now fully leased; occupation certificate received for three towers during the year, OC for the fourth tower expected in Q2 FY27 though it is fully leased and in final stages of completion.
Midtown Plaza is 95% leased and operational.
Summit Plaza is 95-97% leased; expected to open most likely in the second half of July.
Promenade Goa has a line of sight of leasing to the extent of 50%; mall expected to be completed around August, with opening 2-3 months thereafter.

Exceptional NOI/EBITDA growth of 34-35% this year was largely because some assets got completed at the end of the previous year and their entire income came through in the current year since they became 100% leased; management cautions this is not to be taken as a basis for the future, since the construct-to-market cycle for a property takes about 4 years and results won't be uniform every quarter/year.
4-5 year guidance remains intact: mid-teens growth in NOI and 20-25% CAGR growth over the next 4-5 years.

subsections.label: Office Business
points: Newer properties with higher rental rates are 99-100% leased, occupied and generating revenue.

Recent AI-related developments and the Iran-U.S. war have not impacted the portfolio per se, but large tenants are reviewing internal processes and decision-making, which could cause some deferral in decision-making without disturbing the structural strength of the business.

SEZ concept is in structural decline as a category; company has converted ~4 million sq ft of its 16-17 million sq ft SEZ portfolio into non-processing areas, including a small de-notified portion; existing tenants who have not exhausted their 80-I tax incentives continue to take SEZ space on lease.
Lowest SEZ vacancy is in Cyber City Gurgaon; company striving to close the rental gap between Cyber City and SEZ rentals for new take-up, now down to within 10-12%.
Chennai, Silokhera and Hyderabad continue to see marginal rental increases.

Gurgaon is viewed by management as setting a standard of quality that makes it the first call for global blue-chip companies, especially GCCs; recently completed leasing of the entire Atrium Place Tower 4 to a single US-based tenant.

Chennai portfolio benchmark: crossed INR 100/sq ft rental about 2 years ago in Taramani; top floors (with 360-degree city/sea view) in Tower 4 and 5 leased at INR 145-150/sq ft; average rental realization expected between INR 125-130/sq ft.

subsections.label: Retail Business
points: Retail business continues to do well, driven by ability to create experiences for tenants and continuously improve retail offering quality.
Growth of about 10-11% expected in income from existing properties in the current year, plus incremental growth from the 3 new malls coming online.

subsections.label: Downtown Gurgaon Phase 2 & Taramani Details
points: Downtown Gurgaon Phase 2 is an integrated development of 7.5 million sq ft (2 million mall + 5.5 million offices split into 4 towers: Tower 5, 6, 7, 8).
Tower 7 (2.2 million sq ft) is nearly fully leased; Tower 5 and 6 have now been released and are in the process of being leased.
Finishing timelines for these towers are later part of FY28/early FY29.
An iconic tower construction (between Ambience and Tower 2,3,4, where the multilevel car park currently sits) will start about 2.5 years from now.

Downtown Taramani (3.5 million sq ft) construction progressing well; reasonably confident of completion in Q2 of next fiscal year (FY28); project changes made to create a central atrium between Towers 1-5; ~500,000 sq ft already leased with balance leasing underway.
FY28 will see completion of two new towers totaling 3.5 million sq ft in Downtown Taramani.

For FY27, apart from Atrium (3.2 million sq ft expected to generate about INR 700 crores of rent), the 3 malls will also get completed and leased; income accrual on Atrium/malls starts this year but full income benefit will only flow in the following year.

Combined exit rental run-rate target for FY27 across DCCDL and rest of DLF assets is about INR 8,200 crores; management noted lightheartedly it could have been $1 billion had the Iran-US war not happened.

Company is in Mumbai for good; will continue to be cautious and calibrated but open to lucrative opportunities in Mumbai; Westpark should remain a strong core.

Westpark total pipeline is in excess of 5 million sq ft super area; 900,000 sq ft launched so far; next phase of ~800,000 sq ft to be launched this fiscal; further phase of 500,000-600,000 sq ft the fiscal afterwards; company also exploring organic growth options in and around Westpark and other Mumbai development opportunities with its JV partners.

Continued strong focus on EHS (Environment, Health & Safety) and Governance leads at times to a delayed start when launching new projects because of an exhaustive internal checklist process.

Company expects to maintain strong cash generation and hopeful continuation of the dividend growth trajectory, though no formal dividend guidance is provided.

Overall FY27 outlook framed as continuing the strong momentum from FY26, building on launch pipeline (DLF City big launch, Arbour Senior Living, Westpark next phase, Dahlias, eventual Goa), while maintaining cautious, calibrated execution given governance/EHS checklist rigor.

key_takeaways: We are pleased to report a strong close to FY26, wherein we have delivered robust earnings, healthy sales booking and strong cash generation, supported by sustained demand momentum across our development business and continued strength of our annuity business.

We had a record collection of over INR13,500 crores in this fiscal, representing a growth of 15% year-over-year, which led to healthy cash surplus generation of over INR 7,700 crores, reflecting a growth of 25%.
Our net cash position at the end of FY26 stood at INR 14,155 crores, of which close to INR 11,200 crores are in the RERA escrow accounts, signifying a robust balance sheet strength.
As per our commitment, we achieved zero gross debt position in the development business in the last fiscal.

New sales bookings for the year was in line with our guidance and stood at INR 20,143 crores, led by successful sellout of Privana North in Gurugram, West Park in Mumbai and very well supported by our super luxury offering in Dahlias.
Our rental portfolio stands at 50 million square feet and continues to operate at industry-leading occupancy of 95%.

For DCCDL, I think we had another outstanding year with revenues close to INR 7,400 crores, a growth of almost 15%. EBITDA at over INR 5,700 crores a growth of 16% and net profit before exception of INR 2,726 crores, a growth of almost 38%.
The Board has recommended a dividend of INR 8 per share for shareholders' approval, which represents a growth of 33% year-over-year.

subsections.label: Margin movement drivers
points: EBITDA down QoQ but not a broad margin squeeze — realization improved and every cost line below gross margin improved; entire negative movement sits in cost of goods sold.

Realization rose to INR15.02/watt peak (up 8% QoQ) driven by mix, not price — 76 MW of DCR modules (materially higher realization) lifted the blended number; with domestic cell procurement agreements now in place, DCR mix expected to rise further.

Revenue layers: IPP/utility business is base load — large steady volumes but tighter margins; Mid-market and C&I price better and lift blended margin; Distribution is fastest-moving and richest gross-margin segment, and was the fastest-growing channel this quarter.

Cost of goods rose INR1.86/watt peak — largely input-price driven: war-related base metal inflation (aluminum, copper) feeding into frames/bus ribbon/interconnect ribbon (~35% of raw material balance); crude oil spike hitting EVA encapsulant (~12% of raw material balance); Chinese cell price spike from previous quarter flowing through inventory into this quarter.

MSAs' pass-through benefit only covers cell cost, not BORM (balance of raw materials); with transportation, EVA and metals costs rising, that impact could not be passed through; even on cell front, oversupply made it difficult to fully pass on price increases to customers.
Cost pressure is real but identified, concentrated in one line, and largely transitory — expected to ease as metals, crude, and cell prices normalize and older high-cost stock works through.

Deliberate cost program underway: value engineering across bill of materials, alternate vendor procurement strategy to broaden sourcing and lower input cost, rationalizing logistics by aligning inbound/outbound movements to production plan, moderating discretionary overheads, tightening inventory cycle to release working capital and cut carrying cost.
Scale effect: each lever is a per-watt saving; as volumes grow with new lines, savings multiply across a larger base — absolute savings expected to be substantial and build quarter-on-quarter.
Employee costs stepped up modestly and deliberately to staff new lines ahead of volume; will absorb as utilization builds.
These are early-stage reads; fuller benefit of cost program to show over coming quarters as initiatives mature and the two ramping facilities fill out.
Company's margin decline of 50% vs peers this quarter, against a previously referenced EBITDA margin range of ~16%.

Co-location of all three stages (ingot-wafer, cell, module) inside a single fence at Gangaikondan removes fixed overhead — one utilities base, one shared infrastructure, no transport/handling stages between stages.

Investing now in enabling infrastructure (land, power, water, evacuation) ahead of capacity to allow quick, lower-cost augmentation of wafer/ingot capacity once ALMM wafer content mandate and DCR demand firm up.
Major funding for FY27/FY28 capex will come from debt; financial closure in process; debt disbursement to start end of the month (of the call).

key_takeaways: This quarter, we clocked our highest ever quarterly volume of 1,006 megawatts, up 32% on the same quarter last year. Revenue grew by 38% year-on-year.
Our order book closed at 7.9 gigawatt and its composition is shifting towards a diversified customer base, which helps us improve price realizations.
We have sold 76 MW of DCR modules this quarter, which exceeds the full year number for the last fiscal. In the subsequent quarters, we expect the numbers to increase manifold.
Revenue from the quarter was about INR1,563 crores, up 8% sequentially and close to 38% year-on-year.
EBITDA for the quarter was at INR126 crores at a margin of 8.06%, and PAT was at INR19.78 crores. EBITDA is down on the quarter... This was not a broad margin squeeze.
Our per-watt peak realization rose to INR15.02 per watt peak, up 8% sequentially. The driver here is the mix, not the price.
Our unit cost of goods rose by INR1.86 per watt peak in the quarter, and that single line is effectively the whole of the gross margin movement.
We shared a formal outlook for FY27 on our 8th May call... we will revisit that outlook at our H1 results again.
Vikram Solar received the Ecovadis Platinum rating second time in a row, placing us in the top 1% of the ~200,000 companies assessed worldwide.
pressing_questions: Sir, firstly, wanted to confirm, what was the spread per watt during this quarter? And secondly, just wanted to understand, if I understand correctly from the cost inflation point of view, 88% of our order book had a cost escalation clause with the clients. So, what was the reason this was not passed on to customers?
Our current order book is somewhere close to, I think, 8 GW. How much of this is executable in this year?

I understand that the ALMM-2 extension could have caused some issue to the players who are very much strong in the DCR segment. But as we are not in the DCR segment till now... how this could have impacted us very badly as compared to other players where they have reported only 1% or 2% drop in margins and our margins are almost hit by 50%?
So, my question is that, when can we expect the normal range of EBITDA margin in the upcoming quarters? And as compared to the peers, what is our future visibility?

So, in Q1 FY27, our total saleable module stands to around 1 GW. In Q4 FY26, management has given a guidance for the production of module to reach around 7 to 8 GW in FY27 end. So, do we still follow that guidance only or if management will like to slightly change the guidance as per the current scenarios?
But if the current situation continues, so then can we expect the similar sort of margin 8% or do you expect the margin to go further down also?
Sir, if you can just give a wider margin in terms of the DCR versus non-DCR sales in terms of at EBITDA margin level?

quarters.summary: FY26 was a record year for Vikram Solar with all-time high revenue, EBITDA and PAT, driven by an accelerating domestic solar demand cycle. Management guided to ~8 GW production, EBITDA of INR1,500-1,600 crores (~74% growth over FY26) in FY27, with a phased backward-integration capex roadmap (modules → cells → wafer/ingot) and a 15 GWh BESS platform targeted by FY30, financed via a disciplined debt-equity mix while keeping ICR above 2.5x and net-debt-to-equity below 1.5x.

subsections.label: Record Year Metrics
points: Every key metric — revenue, volumes, EBITDA, PAT — reached an all-time high in FY26.
Crossing the 3-gigawatt shipment mark in a single year is a first for Vikram Solar, placing it among leading Indian solar manufacturers.
EBITDA margin expansion of 500bps reflects operating leverage as expanded capacity came on stream.
Q4 touched a 1 gigawatt quarterly production run rate for the first time, providing a useful operating baseline going into FY27.

subsections.label: Balance Sheet Strength
points: Net working capital cycle compressed from 82 days in FY25 to 44 days in FY26, reflecting tighter receivable management, disciplined inventory deployment, and timely cash generation.
The company carries no long-term debt; working capital net debt stands at just INR64 crores with net-debt-to-equity of 0.03, paving way for the next capex cycle from a position of strength.

Capex programs to be financed via disciplined mix of debt and equity, with phasing of capex, debt tranches and internal accruals calibrated to stay within guardrails (ICR above 2.5x, net-debt-to-equity below 1.5x even at peak drawdown).

subsections.label: Margin Dynamics (Q4)
points: Realizations per watt-peak rose ~INR0.60 in Q4 versus Q3, but costs rose by INR0.80 due to the war-related impact, denting per-unit EBITDA by INR0.20 and causing a slight EBITDA margin impact.
Company focuses on per-EBITDA-watt-peak basis; expects some further rationalization in coming quarters but absolute EBITDA numbers expected to rise with scale.
Non-DCR volume expected to deliver EBITDA of INR1.75-2 per watt-peak on average for FY27; DCR procurement segment (25% of execution) expected to yield INR2-2.5 per watt-peak.

subsections.label: Capex Financing Detail
points: Cell capex plan for 12 GW revised to INR5,400 crores after switching machinery sourcing from Thailand to China (10% cost increase); deployment largely in current year with 10% spillover to FY28.

BESS 5 GWh cell-to-pack assembly to cost ~INR150 crores, spent mostly in current year; BESS cell manufacturing construction to start around October 2026 with 24-month construction period, current-year spend (land/initial expenses) not exceeding INR200 crores.

Wafer-ingot first 6 GW phase construction expected to start Q2/Q3, with initial advances to suppliers within INR100 crores in current year since land is already in place at Gangaikondan; balance 6 GW to follow similar INR600 crore/GW thumb rule, with Board approval expected in subsequent financial year.

Debt guidance revised: previous INR3,500 crore FY27 debt plan (based on full 12 GW cell in one phase) now phased into 9+3 GW; FY27 closing debt expected at INR3,200 crores, with FY27 BESS and wafer-ingot outflows funded mainly via internal accruals; FY28 debt expected to rise to INR6,500-6,600 crores as wafer-ingot capex phase comes in.

Interest cost during capex period is capitalized to the project and not charged to P&L; P&L impact of debt for cell asset (commissioning ~March 27) and wafer-ingot asset (commissioning FY29) will show up post-capitalization period.

subsections.label: Raw Material Cost Movement
points: Increase in crude oil impacted EVA cost; aluminium frame cost rose with aluminium going from $3,100/ton to $3,600/ton, partly compensated by a corresponding fall in cell prices, limiting impact in the current quarter.
Cell costs moved up during the year on higher silver prices and the removal of China's export VAT rebate.

MSAs with customers allow pass-through of cell cost and dollar appreciation to the extent of 80%; going forward with cell and wafer-ingot integration, pass-through dynamics will need reassessment as company can't sit with terms in isolation.

Sequential increase in Q4 finance cost driven by lease rental debited for the Vallam facility (equipment lease finance basis) coming on track, plus increased working capital deployment on account of higher inventory; term loan debt has come down while working capital debt remains at similar level.

subsections.label: Order Book Composition Change
points: The 1.9 GW order inflow does not include distribution; distribution orders were removed from the order booking format.

Most distribution was in the Non-DCR segment running a recurring order book arrangement with distributors; as the market moves to DCR and the company operates this year on outsourced cell supplies, the format has changed to spot buying by distributors instead of a recurring order book.

Distribution remains a strong area of focus — distributor network expanded to 110-plus distributors plus 550-plus dealers/system integrators exclusive to Vikram Solar; this number is expected to multiply with the DCR procurement deal in place.

C&I order book (1.5 GW) is switching to DCR and undergoing renegotiation to optimize margins on the DCR portfolio given limited supply; will be counted as fresh bookings if they fit the margin profile.
US export order of 0.6 GW was deemed unviable by the IPP due to sunset of certain incentives in the US market, hence removed from order book.

Remaining ~1 GW US export order book is with reputed IPPs worked with in the past on long-term conversations; company still believes it can execute these, and is working on a traceable, compliant supply chain avoiding prohibitive tariffs/duties, looking at North Africa for cell sourcing that does not attract high tariffs.

subsections.label: DCR/Non-DCR Transition
points: For FY27, demand continues to be anchored in Non-DCR in the near term while gradually transitioning towards DCR; company strategy is to participate meaningfully across both segments.
Production will continue to be predominantly Non-DCR aligned in the current year while proactively positioning for emerging DCR opportunity via the 2 GW procurement agreement (Jupiter International).
Jupiter International cell procurement agreement is phased to address DCR demand post the June 2026 deadline, with the entire offtake ballooning in H2 FY27.
Non-DCR segment will operate within grandfathered ~87 GW of projects; depending on execution pace over next two years, this determines the Non-DCR order book; rest will move to DCR.
Hardly any DCR volume booked in the current quarter; main occupancy has been Non-DCR; FY27 will see DCR offtake come in.

With enforcement from June 2026, DCR demand build-up is staggered; existing cell nameplate base is in ramp-up/stabilization phase so effective output is lower than nameplate, meaning demand will likely exceed supply even after new capacities are set up this year.

subsections.label: BESS Policy & Demand
points: DCR mandates for BESS targeting 60% localization highlighted in presentation; these are indicative numbers given by CEA and Ministry of Heavy Industries.
Company anticipates a similar policy to the Approved List of Battery Manufacturers; an Advanced Chemistry PLI already exists.
Government viability gap funding outlay of about INR18,000 crores on demand side; pipeline of BESS tenders worth ~100 GWh already in RFP/bid submission stage.

subsections.label: Deployment Track Record
points: Crossed 10-gigawatt cumulative global module deployment during the year, representing over 25 million modules supplied, supporting power generation for more than 5 million homes in India.
Scaled from 5 gigawatt to 10 gigawatts in just two years, reflecting steady execution in a policy-supportive environment.

subsections.label: Technology Strategy
points: Deliberate technology-first capital allocation philosophy built on 20 years of execution through every meaningful technology pivot — multi-crystalline to Mono PERC to N-type TOPCon — having learned that the cost of choosing the wrong vintage of equipment is paid for the entire operating life of the asset.
Orders placed for cell equipment belonging to the latest TOPCon Plus generation with efficiency enablers built in from the outset, aimed at a meaningful mark-up over industry baseline.
Higher watt-peak per cell translates into more consistent module performance and better realizations over time.
Next 3 gigawatts of cell capacity planned to be of superior technology with incremental efficiency in the subsequent year.

Industry dominant technology currently is N-TopCon in both cell and module (correcting a questioner's assumption of HJT dominance); HJT is used by only one large peer with limited capacity, true for global average too.

The 9 GW first-phase cell plant uses N-TopCon, specifically 'TopCon Plus' with incremental processes giving a leg-up in efficiency over the industry baseline of 25.2%, taking it to ~25.4-25.5%, creating more wattage in modules and better per-watt realizations.
Current capex cost for the technology is in line with industry; numbers have been made public.
TopCon Plus cell setup uses a process called LECO, which reduces silver consumption via thinner silver fingers.

R&D and applied research projects underway to further replace/reduce silver consumption, though too soon to confirm commercial-scale outcomes; various technologies being researched globally in established labs with which the company has collaborations.

subsections.label: Integration Roadmap
points: Integration strategy moves through three deliberate stages: modules first, then cell, then wafer and ingot; each stage adds depth and reduces exposure, bringing more of the value chain under control.
By the end of the roadmap, Vikram Solar will be fully integrated from ingot to module.

Vallam (5 GW) was one of the fastest greenfield module manufacturing builds of this scale in India, taken from ideation to commissioning in under nine months, delivering lower manpower intensity, faster line throughput, and reduced defect rates from day one; the same playbook is being replicated at Gangaikondan.
At Gangaikondan, the 6 GW module facility is in final stretch of completion with first module output on track for June 2026; management confirmed via Q&A that the schedule remains intact.

9 GW TOPCon cell facility: civil and PEB works well advanced, on track for completion by September 2026; cleanroom and MEP completion in October; equipment installation sequenced across October-November; power infrastructure (executed by Siemens) scheduled for commissioning in November; utilities build-out follows in December; first cell expected end December/early January, followed by sequential commissioning through March 2027 and production ramp-up during Q2 FY28.
This 9 GW cell facility takes the company to roughly 70% of backward integration; a further 3 GW cell facility planned in FY28 completes the cell stack for full cell-level integration.

12 GW wafer-ingot facility: first phase of 6 GW to be added at existing Gangaikondan site, approved at the Board meeting the day prior to the call, with expected outlay of approximately INR3,700 crores and commissioning in FY29.

Gangaikondan will become a single integrated solar manufacturing campus (ingot to module) with zero transport cost between fabs, zero transit damages, and nil inventory buffers between stages, delivering significant structural cost and quality advantage.
Balance 6 GW of wafer-ingot capacity to follow similar economics; Board approval for that expected in the subsequent financial year.

BESS roadmap: 5 GWh cell-to-pack facility to commission by March 2027, followed by first phase of 7.5 GWh of battery cell manufacturing in FY29 and second phase in FY30, reaching the 15 GWh target by FY30.

Fast-forward three-year outlook: operating a 6 GW wafer-ingot facility scaling to 12 GW by FY30, a 12 GW cell facility, and 15.5 GW module capacity, fully integrated and technology-current, among a small handful of serious full-stack manufacturers in India.

subsections.label: Historical Scale-up
points: Company has grown from 12 megawatts in 2009 to 15.5 gigawatts of modules by Q1 FY27, evolving from a private company to a public listed company with an A-plus credit profile.

key_figures.label: Dealers/system integrators exclusive to Vikram Solar

subsections.label: US Market
points: Previously planned 3 GW module capacity in the US and 2 GW in India have been effectively scrapped in favor of focusing on backward integration.

US market groundwork revealed the domestic requirement for traceable supply down to the quartz level is very stringent, and skilled manpower availability in the US domestic front is a challenge, making India a far more attractive opportunity for capital and management bandwidth.

Since November, India's exports to the US (cells or modules) have almost completely zeroed out; current export order book (~1 GW) is with reputed IPPs from long-term relationships and is expected to still be executed.
Company is working on a traceable, compliant supply chain avoiding prohibitive tariffs/duties; considering North Africa for cell sourcing due to lower tariffs.

subsections.label: Other Export Markets
points: Exploring the EU as a market with some non-Chinese supply tenders for a couple of countries ongoing.
Also focusing on Australia and the Middle East, with encouraging conversations.

subsections.label: Domestic Distribution Strategy
points: Distribution channel remains a strong hold and area of focus; 20% of Non-DCR volumes last year came through distribution channel, expected to multiply with the DCR procurement deal in place.

Distribution had not previously participated in PM Surya Ghar due to lack of DCR cells; the company's now-robust and expanded distribution channel will leverage DCR cell availability for this segment, offering better margins.

subsections.label: Inventory Management
points: Company maintains inventory of 30 days at the plant level and about 60 days at vendor's/on-water level as its standard cycle.
With the Vallam facility coming in, inventory levels have increased, though the overall net working capital cycle (net of payables credit) has been brought down to 44 days.

subsections.label: Raw Material Sourcing Shift
points: Cell equipment for the 9 GW facility is now being procured directly from China rather than the previously planned Thailand sourcing, resulting in a 10% capex cost increase.

subsections.label: Industry Backdrop
points: Geopolitical disruptions over the past 2 years, most recently in West Asia, reinforce that for import-led economies like India, energy dependence is now a structural risk, not a price cycle risk.
Solar is no longer being pulled by incentives; it is being pushed by policy, supply chain realignment, and energy security — security, economics, and policy are now aligned.

Mr. Amitabh Kant (former NITI Aayog CEO and India's G20 Sherpa) described India's import dependence as a national security crisis and called for non-fossil capacity to scale from 500 GW to 1,500 GW by 2030 alongside large-scale storage and critical mineral processing at home.
India added 45 GW of solar in FY26, nearly double the 24 GW target and roughly 87% higher than FY25; cumulative installations reached 150 GW (53% of the 283 GW non-fossil base).
CEA's National Grid Action Plan projects peak demand rising from 289 GW to 459 GW by FY36, requiring the installed solar base to scale from 150 GW to 509 GW — roughly 3.5x today's pace.
BESS, currently below 1 GWh, must reach 320 GWh by FY35 per the national pathway.

Utility-scale projects led FY26 additions with a record 34 GW, the highest ever in a single year; rooftop solar crossed 8.5 GW, powered by rapid uptake of PM Surya Ghar Yojana; together with PM-KUSUM distributed segment, overall capacity built reached unprecedented levels — described as a structural reset of India's energy architecture.

subsections.label: Competitive Landscape
points: Given barriers of capital access, technology, execution capability, customer intimacy, and a regulatory framework requiring integration, only a few players will sustain; sector expected to stabilize around 80-100 GW of nameplate fully integrated sustainable capacity held by a small group of serious full-stack players, with total addressable market heading towards a similar number.

Three factors converging in the company's favor: growing domestic demand, local manufacturing depth making integration a competitive moat rather than a cost, and Vikram Solar's existing hard assets — 9.5 GW module manufacturing scaling to 15.5 GW, a technology platform transitioned to N-type, an established customer base, and a clear integration roadmap.

Differentiators versus peers cited: 20 years as one of the initial industry players, deep understanding translated into right capacities/technologies, high customer intimacy, and strong brand reliability/quality perception, combined with backward integration underway.

subsections.label: Leadership Change
points: Sameer Nagpal welcomed as new Chief Executive Officer, bringing over 35 years of leadership experience across diverse sectors with a proven record of architecting turnarounds, building high-performance teams, and driving profitability.
His mandate is to drive operational discipline across the platform, strengthen execution rigor, and align the business for the next phase of growth.

subsections.label: Energy Platform Strategy
points: Battery energy storage viewed as the next major growth frontier — policy-anchored, margin-accretive, and the piece that converts intermittent solar into dispatchable power.

This completes the company's energy platform, taking it from a product company to a complete energy solution provider delivering solar plus storage as dispatchable power, positioning Vikram Solar as partner of choice for the transition.
At this point, focus is completely on backward integration on the module side and expanding into BESS; not considering forward or horizontal integration currently.
BESS expansion begins with assembly, then backward integrates into cell manufacturing.

subsections.label: Cost & Input Risks
points: Cell costs moved up during the year on higher silver prices and the removal of China's export VAT rebate.
Crude oil increase impacted EVA cost; aluminium frame costs rose from $3,100/ton to $3,600/ton, partly offset by a fall in cell prices.

Silver consumption is an industry-wide area of concern; company is researching ways to reduce/replace silver consumption but confirms it's too soon to tell on a commercial scale beyond current LECO-based reduction.

subsections.label: Export/Trade Risks
points: India's exports to the US (cells or modules) have almost completely zeroed out since November.
A 0.6 GW US export order was deemed unviable by the IPP due to sunset of certain incentives in the US market, leading to its removal from order book.
US domestic manufacturing requires stringent traceable supply down to the quartz level and faces skilled manpower availability challenges, deterring US capacity plans.

subsections.label: Policy Transition Risk
points: Shift from Non-DCR to DCR regime (cell-level mandate effective June 2026) requires renegotiation of existing C&I and distribution order books to fit margin profiles, creating near-term order book uncertainty.
Sector-wide relative oversupply/well-balanced cell market noted until utility-scale DCR norms practically kick in (expected FY28/early FY29).

subsections.label: Forward Outlook
points: Four durable takeaways emphasized: (1) real earnings base with record revenue, record margins, double-digit PAT, and a strong no-long-term-debt balance sheet; (2) integration, technology alignment, execution and customer confidence are becoming defining factors for long-term competitiveness beyond scale alone; (3) capex financed through a well-structured diversified mix so no single source bears disproportionate burden in any year; (4) company building the platform for long-term market leadership, having grown from 12 MW in 2009 to 15.5 GW of modules by Q1 FY27 with an A-plus credit profile.

Fast forward three years: company expects to operate a 6 GW wafer-ingot facility scaling to 12 GW by FY30, a 12 GW cell facility, and 15.5 GW module capacity, fully integrated and technology-current, against an industry that will have rationalized to roughly 80-100 GW of sustaining capacity with a similar demand envelope.

key_takeaways: The earnings base is real: record revenue, record margins, double-digit PAT, and a strong balance sheet with no long-term debt.
Order book strength, repeat customer depth, demand visibility across segments, and a consistent track record of operational execution is the foundation on which cash flow projections rest.
In this environment, scale alone is no longer sufficient. Integration, technology alignment, and execution and customer confidence are becoming the defining factors for long-term competitiveness.

Capex is financed through a well-structured, diversified mix. The phasing of actual spends and the sequencing of financing tranches are designed so that no single source, including internal accruals, bears a disproportionate burden in any given year.

Vikram Solar is building the platform for long-term market leadership. From 12 megawatts in 2009 to 15.5 gigawatts of modules in Q1 FY27; from a private company to a public listed company with an A-plus credit profile, this is a company that has consistently turned ambitions into execution.
FY26 has delivered record growth, record profitability, and a healthy balance sheet, a solid platform to engage with what is unfolding in the broader market.
Highest-ever quarterly production of approximately 1 gigawatt, highest-ever order booking of approximately 1.9 gigawatts, and highest-ever quarterly revenue of over INR1,450 crores in Q4.

Our working assumption is that the sector will stabilize around an 80 to 100 gigawatt of nameplate fully integrated sustainable capacity held by a small group of serious full-stack players, and the total addressable market is heading towards a similar number.
pressing_questions: Since silicon wafers and silver are key inputs for your business, how are rising raw material costs, especially silver, impacting your overall cost structure and to what extent are you able to pass these increases on to customers?
With this level of growth, what's the growth guidance that you will give to the investors — will margins grow at the same rate or a different rate?

Since the debt level plan for FY27 was earlier INR3,500 crores, and BESS/wafer-ingot projects were postponed to FY29, will FY28 debt levels be similar, and will the bottom line be staggered around INR500 crores due to interest outflow?
Even after industry overcapacity or insufficient cell capacity factors, will the expected EBITDA per watt-peak improvement to ~INR5 by FY28 still hold, or are other factors at play?

JTLIND.about: JTL Infra Ltd is an integrated manufacturer and supplier of steel tubes, pipes and allied products with manufacturing facilities in India.[1]

subsections.label: Quarterly Performance Highlights

PAT of INR35 crores is after INR2.8 crores of additional non-cash depreciation arising from the March 2026 asset revaluation at JTL Defence Limited, erstwhile RCI Industries & Technologies Limited.
Operational revenue per ton and operational EBITDA per ton improvement supported by an improved product mix and continued focus on operational efficiencies.

Barring JTL Defence contribution, EBITDA per ton for the steel tube and pipe segment was around INR4,750, itself a growth versus prior levels.

Given normalized HRC situation, management is confident INR4,750 EBITDA per ton in JTL Steel tube and pipe segment is sustainable in coming quarters with an upward trajectory, and consolidated INR5,000 EBITDA per ton is achievable.

subsections.label: Working capital

Company is opting for dealer financing, which will further bring down the working capital cycle.

Working capital cycle was earlier stretched because of a government-focused base with long payment dues; shift toward exports and dealer network (dealer payments ~7-8 days) will improve the cycle to 35-40 days levels by FY28.

JTL Defence capex outflow this year expected to be not more than INR15 crores, with a similar amount expected next year; this capex will change product placement, not overall capacity, of JTL Defence.

subsections.label: Order book dynamics
points: Export order book quantifiable at plus-INR75 crores because it involves a longer delivery period.
Domestic order book is a moving/dealer-network market with daily rather than fixed-day ordering; local market delivery is between 7 to 10 days, so order book changes daily.
Dealer network contributes 50-60% of entire sales, with orders placed on a daily basis.

subsections.label: Government vs. dealer/export demand strategy
points: Government capex has seen a little increase versus two years back, but company has intentionally reduced reliance on government sector, which is seasonal.
Derabassi (Punjab) plant, earlier dedicated to government demand, has shifted mode toward dealer market.
Company opens up to government orders selectively when favorable size opportunities arise.
Government contribution fell from over 25% earlier to under 5% last year as focus shifted to dealer and export markets.

subsections.label: Primary vs secondary demand
points: Record-breaking demand seen in secondary products currently, aided by a wider primary-secondary price spread.
Spread has widened from a historical normal of INR4-5/kg to INR8-12/kg range in the last quarter.
Company's ~45-50% secondary market capacity allowed it to capitalize on this demand; demand pattern expected to continue as long as the spread persists.
Difference currently remains similar with continued bumper demand in the secondary market.

subsections.label: Dealer distribution network
points: Current dealer network is sufficing the products.

DFT product (a volume pusher) is going directly to departments like MMRDA and airport authorities rather than through dealers, as the company has impanelled most of these places itself, resulting in direct sales instead of earlier dealer-routed sales.

Company gaining share in the DFT segment via empanelment in multiple places in Maharashtra.
Good export demand for DFT sections; borders opened to USA, Mexico, and Canada for DFT exports.
Value-added composition close to 35%, consistent with past levels; target is minimum 50-60% value-added once CRM processes running from 1 million ton to 2 million ton capacity are complete.

subsections.label: Specialized/primary product gains
points: Company gaining market share in specialized products - low dia, high thickness, replacing seamless pipes with thicker-wall products.
Active gains via direct supply to OEMs and dealer network in these niche products, which only a few players in India produce; earlier these were largely imported.

Products being deployed into replacement of seamless pipes in hydraulic and automotive segments, where price sensitivity and need for higher-grade materials exist; company has been able to penetrate these areas.

subsections.label: Volume growth drivers
points: Growth in DFT volumes (from ~10,000 tons/quarter to 20,000-25,000 tons/quarter) driven by both new capacity coming online and market share gains via empanelment.
Export market also seeing good demand for DFT sections with new border openings to USA, Mexico, Canada.

subsections.label: JTL Defence business update
points: Volume guidance for JTL Defence is not fixed for this year, but topline target remains close to INR150 crores.
Run rate improved from ~100 metric tons/month to 120 metric tons/month in Q1 FY27, targeting 500 tons/month by exit quarter.
Q4 FY26 EBITDA margin of 20% was exceptional, led by inventory gains; Q1 FY27 margin was 12%; long-term margin target remains 10-15% given it is a new business setup being tested and refined.

JTL Defence entering coin segment and bullet shell segment; capex primarily for machine renovation/new machines needed for these segments, not to change overall capacity but to change product placement.

Future product mix envisioned as a blend: ~25-30% (200 tons) toward mint factory (coins, pigments), ~30-35% (350 tons) toward bullet shells and casings, and remaining ~350 tons toward current dealer and automobile market (copper coils/foils/sheets), including customers like Minda Corp, a major copper coil procurer.

subsections.label: Mangaon facility ramp-up
points: Utilization at Mangaon facility currently about 42%; company confident of achieving desired capacity addition of close to 1 million tons by end of H1.
Company-level utilization currently at 55%, expected to reach 65% by year-end, majorly led by utilization increase at Mangaon facility, expected to drive a better H2.
DFT production at Mangaon currently 7,000-10,000 tons, with huge room to grow, potentially doubling; once achieved, plant utilization will touch 60% with margin improvement.

subsections.label: Capacity expansion phasing
points: Capacity expansion coming in phases: ~7 lakh tons to be commissioned by H1 end (out of the 1 million ton target), and remaining 3 lakh tons (API pipes, previously announced) to be commissioned by next year around this time.
Ramp-up will take time; new capacity will contribute incrementally every quarter, but full utilization levels expected only by FY29.

Peak utilization target of ~70% could be achieved as early as FY29 or as late as FY30, subject to capex completion timing for the last leg.

subsections.label: Revenue potential at peak
points: Current realization per ton is close to INR60,000 (referenced also as INR6,000 in a different context in transcript); as company moves into value-added products, realization expected to increase to INR65,000-66,000 per ton.
At peak utilization of 70% on 1.4 million tons capacity and INR65,000/ton realization, this represents the peak revenue potential on the current capex cycle.

subsections.label: JTL Defence capacity
points: JTL Defence hot plant capacity is close to 1,000 tons per month (12,000 tons annualized).

Capex planned will not change overall capacity of JTL Defence but will change product placement — shifting existing copper foils/sheets output toward bullet shells, casings, and mint factory production.

subsections.label: Export dynamics
points: Exports dipped to 5% this quarter, majorly due to container shortages happening globally, causing lag in dispatches.
Company has a healthy/one of its biggest ever order books of exports currently on hand; going ahead, expects to cover the shortfall.
Issues in Hormuz and lack of container/transportation availability affected exports in Q1; situation expected to improve, allowing recovery of the lag in Q2.
Recently awarded certifications like ACRS and started exports to the Americas (USA, Mexico, Canada), generating good interest.
ACRS certification is majorly relevant for Australia and is helping the company gain market share there.
Earlier target of 10% of total sales to exports remains the target for coming quarters; the 5% shortfall will be accounted for in coming quarters.

subsections.label: Domestic distribution strategy
points: Company shifting focus toward dealer network and exports rather than government sector, which is seasonal.
Derabassi (Punjab) plant, earlier dedicated toward government demand, now also serving the dealer market.
DFT product now largely sold directly (not through dealers) to departments like MMRDA and airport authorities, since company has impanelled most of these places itself.

subsections.label: JTL Defence business direction
points: JTL Defence (erstwhile RCI Industries & Technologies Limited) entering coin segment and bullet shell segment, requiring machine renovations and some new machine orders.

Management stated JTL Defence will not be predominantly a shell company; the mix will span mint factory (coins/pigments), bullet shells/casings (defence), and dealer/automobile copper products (e.g., supply to Minda Corp).

subsections.label: Logistics and geopolitical disruption
points: Container shortages happening all over affected export dispatches in Q1 FY27, causing exports to dip to 5% of sales versus a 10% target.
Issues in Hormuz and lack of availability of containers and transportation affected first quarter exports.
If logistics situation improves, company expects to cover the export lag in the second quarter.

points: Government capex/demand is seasonal, prompting the company to intentionally reduce reliance on government-sector sales in favor of dealer and export markets.

points: H2 usually stronger than H1; management expects similar or higher volumes than Q1 in coming quarters plus ~20% growth to cross the 30% FY27 volume growth guidance, aiming to deliver more than that.
July was an all-time high month; run rate suggests an all-time high quarter ahead as well, aided by strong secondary demand gap between primary and secondary products.
EBITDA per ton guidance intact at INR4,500 for steel segment for the year; consolidated level target of INR5,000 expected in coming quarters.

subsections.label: Export guidance
points: Earlier mentioned target of 10% of total sales to exports remains the target for coming quarters; the 5% shortfall this quarter will be accounted for going forward.

subsections.label: JTL Defence guidance
points: Volume guidance not fixed for this year, but topline target remains close to INR150 crores for FY27.
Targeting a run rate of 500 metric tons/month of JTL Defence products by exit quarter (Q4 FY27), i.e., within a month rather than a quarterly aggregate.
Long-term EBITDA margin target of 10-15% maintained despite near-term wavering as the business is new; Q1 FY27 delivered 12% margin versus an exceptional 20% in Q4 FY26 (inventory gains).

subsections.label: Working capital guidance
points: Targeting working capital cycle of 35-40 days by FY28, down from 75 days currently and 90 days previously, aided by shift to dealer/export focus and dealer financing.

Very confident to achieve the desired capacity addition of close to 1 million tons by end of H1.
Overall company level operating at 55% utilization currently; by year-end, this level should be close to 65%.

As we are pouring into value-added products going ahead, we can expect the realization to increase from INR60,000 to INR65,000, INR66,000 going ahead.

For this year, the capex outflow is close to INR100 crores, and this will be completing our entire capex left over, taking the company to 2 million tons.
After the current capex, there will be only maintenance capex of INR30 crores, INR40 crores every year at max.
The top line is something that we're still trying to achieve, and we'll be touching close to INR150 crores of top line.
By exit quarter, we'll be touching close to 500 tons (metric tons per month) of sales in defence.
It's too soon to maintain the exact 15% margin going ahead, but the long-term margin is 15%; can be wavering, but 10% to 15% is achievable in the long-term proposition.
Our target in the coming future is minimum 50% to 60% of our products will be value added, once all CRM processes running from 1 million ton to 2 million tons capacity are complete.
By FY28, we are targeting a working capital cycle of 35 to 40 days.
The capex outflow for JTL Defence this year would be not more than INR15 crores, and a similar amount is expected in the next year as well.
July for us was again an all-time high month; going ahead with the run rate we'll be able to achieve an all-time high quarter as well.
Going ahead, we should be targeting INR5,000 EBITDA per ton.
Our total export guidance or export target for the company is to reach export contribution of 15%; right now we have reached an export sales percentage of 10%.
We are very confident that our DFT only will be scaled up in a much higher way and that will result to a total utilization levels about 60%-70% for this year itself at the Mangaon facility.
To reach a capacity of 2 million tons by FY27, yes, that's the intact target.
Total plan for capex is close to INR100 crores and INR120 crores for this full financial year (INR60-70 crores in H1 for new capacity, INR30-40 crores maintenance capex in H2).
We should be drifting close to 25% to 30% ROCE for the next years... we should be seeing ROCE coming back to traditional levels of 25%, 20% levels.
We are already at 150 metric tons of run rate of per month. And by exit quarter of this year, we should be at a run rate of 500 metric tons a month.
The total capacity over there is to deliver up to 700 to 800 metric tons a month, which we shall be achieving by FY29.

As we are inching towards the finishing stages of the capex, by probably next financial year, we should be having a positive cash flow.

key_takeaways: The company achieved its highest ever quarterly revenue from operations and EBITDA in Q1 FY27. Revenue from operations reached INR722 crores, while EBITDA was INR59 crores with a margin of 8.1%.

Profit after tax for the quarter was INR35 crores with a margin of 4.9%. PAT of INR35 crores is after INR2.8 crores of additional noncash depreciation arising from the March 2026 asset revaluation at JTL Defence Limited, erstwhile RCI Industries & Technologies Limited.

The company has reported a sales volume of 1,18,513 metric tons during Q1 FY27, reflecting 17.8% year-on-year growth. Operational revenue per ton increased to INR60,882 while operational EBITDA per ton without other income improved to INR4,954 per metric ton, supported by an improved product mix and continued focus on operational efficiencies.

During the quarter, the company continued to strengthen its presence across key end user industries through its value-added product portfolio. DFT structural steel pipes continue to gain acceptance across the dealer network and industrial applications, supported by improved production and capacity utilization at the Mangaon facility.

The quarter also marked progress in strengthening the company's presence in the water infrastructure segment with the receipt of INR27 crores order for the supply of galvanized iron pipes for water supply and distribution projects in Himachal Pradesh.
The company continues to focus on improving operational efficiencies, expanding the contribution from value-added products and strengthening its presence across domestic and export markets.

quarters.summary: FY26 saw record annual and quarterly sales volumes with revenue/EBITDA/PAT growth; management guided 30% volume growth for FY27 on current capacity (with potential upward revision once Mangaon color-coated/GT capacity ramps by end of H1), 10-15% EBITDA/ton growth, export orientation target of 15%, capacity expansion to 2 million tons by FY27, ROCE recovery to 25-30% as capex cycle completes, and JTL Defence scaling toward 500 metric tons/month by exit quarter and 700-800 MT/month capacity by FY29.

subsections.label: Margin drivers
points: Operational EBITDA per ton improved during Q4 FY26, driven by better realizations and increasing share of value-added products in the overall mix.
On a quarter-on-quarter basis, EBITDA per ton was around INR150 higher than the last quarter, in a steady state situation.
Q4 last year was an extraordinarily weak quarter because of volatility in steel, making the Y-o-Y EBITDA per ton growth appear larger than the underlying trend.
Revenue per ton is very much dependent on the HRC cost, which has been rising, pushing up revenue per ton and realizations.
No inventory carrying gain in Q4; whatever products were sold got realized, with no change in inventory as such.
Some discounts had to be given in certain places to push DFT as a new product in the market, affecting profitability despite strong volumes.

subsections.label: Capital allocation / Cash flow
points: Operating cash flow has been negative for the last 2-3 years and debt has increased this year, linked to the heavy capex cycle undertaken.
As the company approaches the finishing stages of capex, positive operating cash flow is expected by probably next financial year.

ROCE/ROE have fallen due to the heavy capex cycle over the past 1.5-2 years, with a lot of assets in CWIP and not yet sweating; as assets get capitalized and start production, ROCE/ROE should bounce back to traditional levels of 20-25%.

subsections.label: Demand environment
points: The market is on a good track at the moment; there was a lot of correction after the duty was introduced in November, prices went up and there has been a lot of stocking since then.
Due to recent elections in 2-3 states, there was a little bit of a slowdown in the first week, but as of today there is a good pickup from the market.
Management expects the market to remain good in the coming quarter with no problem in the pickup of material.
Healthy demand across infrastructure, construction and industrial applications continued during FY26.
Demand from infrastructure, industrial and construction-related segments continues to remain supportive.

subsections.label: Seasonality
points: Seasonality exists because of monsoon hitting the entirety of India; H1 is when the new financial year gears up with newer projects being announced, taking time, so H1 is generally a little slower and H2 is a little faster than H1.
Due to international and local scenario factors, these seasonalities have not played their essential core role in the last few years.
This year, there is good demand expected in Q1; Q2 would specifically be guided by the monsoons; export market keeps going on regardless, so overall it should be a good quarter.

subsections.label: Value-added product mix
points: DFT structural steel pipes continue to gain acceptance across infrastructure and structural applications, driving overall volume growth.
Increasing contribution from value-added products supported margin improvement and overall business performance during the year.

Right now the company is selling DFT pipes, galvanized pipes and black pipes — DFT does not carry a very different revenue per ton from black pipes; color-coated items carry a different (higher) revenue per ton, so the increase in revenue per ton will be seen in the future as the mix shifts toward color-coated.
Almost towards closing stage of capex at Mangaon; by end of H1 the facility should be fully running with the new capex, enabling greater color-coated contribution.

subsections.label: JTL Defence
points: JTL Defence manufactures copper, brass and phosphorus bronze alloys; the plant was acquired under the JTL umbrella in December, formerly known as RCI Industries.
Q4 FY26 was the first quarter with new management; the plant is in an overhaul stage with a lot of minor capex being done.

20% EBITDA margin in Q4 was aided by inventory gains since the capacity just started in the quarter, and is not considered a fair run-rate number going forward; going ahead 10-15% EBITDA margin is targeted for coming quarters if copper prices are stable.
Business model is a mix of job work and outright sales, so tonnage and revenue will not scale in direct proportion.

Company is in a fully backward-integrated process at JTL Defence, from procuring copper and zinc through to making the bullet shell, including making ultra-thin foils; there are limited players in this specific business model and management is not aware of any listed peer in the same business, differentiating it from generic copper-alloy converters.

subsections.label: Export business
points: Export business recorded healthy traction during the year, supported by wider market reach and improving customer additions across geographies.
Majority of export volumes are value-added products — mainly galvanized and increasingly DFT.

Export margin is not quantifiably superior to domestic margin as a thumb rule; it depends on relative pricing between Indian and export markets — currently Indian HR coil and pipe market is more expensive than export market.
Gain from exports comes from higher volumes (economies of scale from singular large-size orders) rather than higher margin per se.

subsections.label: Certifications
points: Company recently obtained ACRS certification, which is required to supply pipes to Australia; it is the only company in the Indian pipe segment to have this certification.
Company has recently explored options to supply to USA and Canada as well.
Getting DFT products impaneled/certified in various places is an ongoing process supporting scale-up of DFT.

subsections.label: Mangaon expansion
points: Majority of sales volume addition has happened from the Mangaon facility itself; company is getting empanelled in most places for DFT products.

Capacity to move from 1 million tons currently to 2 million tons with the new expansion.
