points: Company continued strengthening presence across domestic and export markets during the year.
Export sales percentage has reached 10% on higher volume growth; company aims for 15% export orientation as overall company volumes grow in coming years.
Currently Indian market for HR coil and pipe is more expensive than the export market, so the company has to work on the basis of import-linked pricing for exports.

subsections.label: Inventory
points: No inventory carrying gain in Q4 FY26; there was no inventory gain as such — whatever products were sold got realized, with no change in inventory.

subsections.label: Customer/market positioning
points: Improving customer additions across geographies supported export traction during the year.
Company remains focused on strengthening its market presence across infrastructure, industrial and construction segments.

subsections.label: JTL Defence acquisition
points: JTL Defence (formerly RCI Industries) plant was acquired under the JTL umbrella in December; it manufactures copper, brass and phosphorus bronze alloys.

Company previously went through NCLT before this acquisition; peak potential revenue previously achieved by the company (as RCI Industries) before NCLT was INR1,500 crores, representing the opportunity ahead.
By FY29, company will target getting as close as possible to that historical peak revenue level.

subsections.label: External/market factors
points: Duty introduced in November led to price correction and subsequent stocking activity in the market.
Recent elections in 2-3 states caused a little bit of a slowdown in the first week of the relevant period.
Geopolitical situations rolling out globally create difficulty in giving an exact number or exact growth target, and can cause 1-2 months/weeks of unforeseen delay in capacity execution.
Delay in color-coated complex capex occurred due to rains and multiple other factors, pushing out the volume growth outlook versus earlier targets.
Discounts had to be given in some places to push DFT as a new product in the market, impacting near-term profitability despite strong volume growth.
Copper price increases benefited JTL Defence margin in the recent quarter (inventory gains), but if copper prices are stable going forward, margins are expected to normalize to 10-15%.
Operating cash flow has remained negative for 2-3 years and debt has increased this year due to the heavy capex cycle.

subsections.label: Volume and capacity outlook
points: 30% volume growth Y-o-Y for FY27 is achievable with current capacity itself; whatever comes over and beyond once new capacity comes online per the timeline will be used to revise the target upward.

This is a downgrade in absolute terms versus a prior guidance of 6 lakh tons for FY27 and 9 lakh tons for FY28 (30% growth implies ~5,20,000 tons), attributed to delay in the color-coated complex capex due to rains and other factors.

By next quarter's end, management will have a fairer picture on how the new capacity has started and how it is playing out in the market, and might revise guidance back toward previously mentioned levels.
2 million ton exit capacity target by FY27 remains intact.

subsections.label: Profitability and returns outlook
points: EBITDA per ton for FY26 was INR3,900; guidance is for 10-15% growth this financial year, taking it to roughly INR4,500-4,800.
As new CRM capacity for color-coated and galvanized volumes unfolds, management will be in a better position to give future EBITDA per ton outlook; INR5,000 EBITDA per ton is a longer-term target.

ROCE expected to drift to 25-30% in the next years as capex completes and CWIP assets get capitalized and start production, reversing the fall in ROCE/ROE caused by the heavy capex cycle of the past 1.5-2 years.
Positive operating cash flow expected probably by next financial year as the company nears the finishing stages of its capex cycle.

guidance_ledger.statement: Given the run rate that we are on at and how we are adding capacity, it's safe to say that we'll be able to deliver about 30% volume growth Y-o-Y.
We'll be able to deliver a 10% to 15% EBITDA per ton growth as well; from INR3,900 levels, we should be touching somewhere close to INR4,500 to INR4,800 for this financial year.
Going ahead, we should be targeting INR5,000 EBITDA per ton.
Our total export guidance or export target for the company is to reach export contribution of 15%; right now we have reached an export sales percentage of 10%.
We are very confident that our DFT only will be scaled up in a much higher way and that will result to a total utilization levels about 60%-70% for this year itself at the Mangaon facility.
To reach a capacity of 2 million tons by FY27, yes, that's the intact target.
Total plan for capex is close to INR100 crores and INR120 crores for this full financial year (INR60-70 crores in H1 for new capacity, INR30-40 crores maintenance capex in H2).
We should be drifting close to 25% to 30% ROCE for the next years... we should be seeing ROCE coming back to traditional levels of 25%, 20% levels.
We are already at 150 metric tons of run rate of per month. And by exit quarter of this year, we should be at a run rate of 500 metric tons a month.
The total capacity over there is to deliver up to 700 to 800 metric tons a month, which we shall be achieving by FY29.
For this full year, we should be targeting close to INR150 crores to INR200 crores of top-line in the company.
If the copper prices are stable, we'll be able to deliver close to 10% to 15% EBITDA margins.
By FY29, we'll also target that we get as close as possible to the revenue of that company (peak potential of INR1,500 crores).
As we are inching towards the finishing stages of the capex, by probably next financial year, we should be having a positive cash flow.

Previous quarter guidance was 6 lakh tons in FY27 and 9 lakh tons in FY28; current 30% growth implies ~5,20,000 tons due to capex delay, but as soon as capacity starts, guidance will be revised and by next quarter's end there will be a fair picture, possibly delivering what was mentioned before.

It will be very tough for us to give the exact utilization levels right now. Coming ahead in next quarter, we will definitely come and give the utilization levels guidance as we'll be closer to our capex.

risk_register.risk: Delay in Mangaon color-coated complex capex due to rains and multiple other factors
risk_register.note: Caused downgrade of volume guidance from prior 6 lakh tons FY27 / 9 lakh tons FY28 target to ~5,20,000 tons implied by 30% growth guidance.

risk_register.risk: Geopolitical situations globally
risk_register.note: Creates difficulty in giving exact growth/number targets and can cause unforeseen 1-2 month delays in capacity execution.

risk_register.risk: Duty introduction and price volatility (November)
risk_register.note: Led to price correction and subsequent stocking in the market; some short-term slowdown around elections but recovering.

risk_register.risk: Discounting to push new DFT products
risk_register.note: Some places required discounts to push the new DFT product, affecting realizations/profitability despite volume growth.

risk_register.risk: Negative operating cash flow and rising debt
risk_register.note: Linked to the heavy capex cycle; expected to turn positive probably next financial year.

risk_register.risk: Copper price volatility impacting JTL Defence margins
risk_register.note: 20% margin in Q4 was aided by inventory gains from rising copper prices; not considered a fair/sustainable number; normalized margin expected at 10-15% if copper prices are stable.

risk_register.risk: CWIP / underutilized assets depressing ROCE/ROE
risk_register.note: Heavy capex cycle over past 1.5-2 years led assets to sit in CWIP, not yet sweating, pulling down ROCE/ROE versus traditional 20-25% levels.

risk_register.risk: Election-related slowdown in certain states
risk_register.note: Caused a little bit of slowdown in the first week but market has since seen good pickup.

themes.label: Capacity expansion
themes.note: Mangaon expansion to 2 million tons (incl. 7 lakh ton cold rolling complex for color-coated/GT pipes) intact for FY27, but color-coated complex capex faced delays due to rains, pushing out volume upside.

themes.label: Value-added product mix shift
themes.note: Value-added products at 27% of Q4 mix; DFT pipes gaining acceptance, with color-coated products expected to lift revenue per ton once capex completes by end of H1.

themes.label: Export growth
themes.note: Export contribution reached 10% in Q4 with a medium-term target of 15%, driven mainly by galvanized and DFT products and new certifications (ACRS for Australia; exploring USA/Canada).

themes.label: JTL Defence ramp-up
themes.note: New defence business (copper/brass/phosphorus bronze alloys) scaling from ~100-150 MT/month toward 500 MT/month by FY27 exit and 700-800 MT/month by FY29, targeting INR150-200 crore FY27 topline.

themes.label: Margin normalization
themes.note: Q4 EBITDA/ton of INR4,700 partly reflects steady-state improvement; guidance of 10-15% EBITDA/ton growth for FY27, while JTL Defence's 20% Q4 margin (aided by copper inventory gains) is expected to normalize to 10-15%.

themes.label: Capex cycle and returns
themes.note: Heavy capex cycle has depressed ROCE/ROE and kept operating cash flow negative with rising debt; recovery to 25-30% ROCE and positive operating cash flow expected as capex completes, likely next financial year.

themes.label: Guidance revision/downgrade
themes.note: Prior FY27/FY28 volume targets of 6 lakh/9 lakh tons were scaled back to ~5,20,000 tons (implied by 30% growth) due to capex delays, with management indicating potential upward revision once new capacity is confirmed.

key_takeaways: Revenue from operations for financial year '26 was INR2,136 crores, while EBITDA came in at INR166 crores. Profit after tax for the year was INR103 crores.

The company reported its highest ever annual sales volumes of 3,95,900 metric tons during financial year '26, supported by higher throughput across facilities and improving contribution from value-added products.

Revenue from operations for the quarter was INR693 crores, reflecting growth of 47.5% year-on-year and 47.2% quarter-on-quarter. EBITDA for the quarter was INR58 crores, while profit after tax came in at INR38 crores.
The company also achieved its highest ever quarterly sales volume of 1,23,262 metric tons during Q4 financial year '26.
Given the run rate that we are on at and how we are adding capacity, it's safe to say that we'll be able to deliver about 30% volume growth Y-o-Y.

Sneha, it's easier to say that our total export guidance or export target for the company is to reach export contribution of 15%. Right now, we have reached an export sales percentage of 10% on a higher volume growth.
We are about 35%-40% range at our Mangaon facility... that will result to a total utilization levels about 60%-70% for this year itself at the Mangaon facility.

So, majority capex has been done for the 2 million tons capacity, but there's only some bit of capex left for H1, which is close to INR60 crores, INR70 crores... So the total plan for capex is close to INR100 crores and INR120 crores for this full financial year.
We should be drifting close to 25% to 30% ROCE for the next years, given that a lot of our assets are not sweating and a lot of capex is happening, a lot of assets are in CWIP as well.
So, for this full year, we should be targeting close to INR150 crores to INR200 crores of top-line in the company [JTL Defence].
pressing_questions: So we were earlier targeting 22.5 lakh tons of exit capacity by FY27. So just rechecking is that guidance pretty much intact?

We have guided around 30% volume growth this year, but in the previous quarter, if I look at, we were guiding for at 6 lakhs in FY27 and 9 lakhs in FY28. But if I take the 30% volume growth, it comes to around 5,20,000. So just wanted to know what is the reason behind it? Why have we downgraded guidance from 6 lakhs to if we take 30%, it comes to around 5,20,000?

So when do we expect to turn positive operating cash flow because the last 2 to 3 years, we have been posting negative cash flow. And if I look at the debt as well, this year has increased. So just wanted to know when can we expect positive operating cash flow coming in?

AWHCL.about: Antony Waste Handling Cell Ltd is engaged in the business of mechanical power sweeping of roads, collection and transportation of waste, waste to energy project and undertake the designing, construction, operation and maintenance of the integrated waste management facility in Kanjurmarg, Mumbai.[1] It is one of the top five players in the Indian municipal waste management industry with a track record of ~20 years.[2]

quarters.summary: Management flagged Q1FY27 as a "transitional" quarter with margin pressure driven largely by non-recurring items (CIDCO bio-mining closure costs, employee cost restatement, refinancing prepayment charge) rather than structural deterioration; top-line momentum remains intact with a new Rs.243 crore Greater Noida contract win, and the WtE plant at PCMC is expected to restart by first week of October 2026 following a tragic monsoon-related incident, with margin normalization expected from H2FY27/FY28 as escalations and new higher-margin contracts (BMC, Atkoli) kick in.

subsections.label: Margin compression drivers
points: EBITDA compression driven by 3 factors: higher operating expenses (vehicle hiring and transportation costs at the CIDCO plant), employee costs (rose 18% YoY, now 34% of revenue vs 30% a year ago), and deferral of certain Q4FY26 waste disposal transformation activities into Q1FY27, adding an incremental expense of approximately ₹10 crores.
Finance costs rose 35% YoY reflecting higher debt base ahead of refinancing.
PAT decline further impacted by one-time ₹7 crore expense related to prepayment of the Antony Lara Renewable Energy term loan.
Management views this quarter's profitability as transitional rather than structural, given the one-off nature of both the transportation cost deferral and the refinancing charge.

Employee cost spike attributed to Labour Code change restating actuarial assumptions and incremental headcount for new projects; part anticipated (new project), Labour Code quantification was a surprise.
Labour cost as % of revenue historically 30-31%; spiked to 34% this quarter as an aberration, expected to normalize over next 3 quarters with margin expansion stepping in thereafter.

Bulk of labour cost increase expected to be passed through via annual escalation clauses in tender conditions, but with a timing mismatch (cost incurred now, escalation applied ~6 months later based on contract anniversary).

subsections.label: Refinancing details
points: Successfully refinanced the term loan of Antony Lara Renewable Energy Private Limited (material subsidiary operating the PCMC WtE facility), bringing interest rate down from 10.25% to 8.25% per annum, a 200 bps reduction, on a ₹140 crore refinanced loan, extending tenure by 15 years.
Net benefit of ₹14 crores after netting off the ₹6 crore prepayment charge incurred in Q1FY27.
This is a meaningful reduction expected to support cost of capital going forward and deliver recurring interest savings and stronger cash flow generation from the WtE facility.
Weighted average cost of debt (10.1% as of June 2026) expected to trend lower as the Lara Renewable refinancing benefit fully reflects going forward.

subsections.label: Force majeure / impairment
points: Force majeure event at WtE project in PCMC caused by extreme monsoon conditions resulted in damage to a portion of project assets; does not impact core operating assets.
Expected impairment charge of ₹22-24 crores to be treated as an exceptional/extraordinary item separate from core operating performance, to be reflected in Q2FY27.
Estimate does not yet factor in any recovery expected from insurance claims, which could offset part of the impact; situation still evolving, more details expected in Q2 results.
Auditors flagged the need for structural review by OEM suppliers before cost estimates can be finalized; not a compliance issue but a review pending due to structural damage from the landslide.

subsections.label: Debt composition
points: Incremental gross borrowing since Q4 (up ₹22 crores) attributed to working capital for the AP WtE project (Kadapa and Kurnool) ramp-up and the new BMC C&T contract that started in Q1.

Total debt of ₹420 crores comprises ₹220 crores long-term and ₹140 crores short-term; ₹350 crores of long-term debt due over next 3-5 years, with roughly ₹40-odd crores (₹28 crores plus ₹12 crores) due in next 12 months.
Net debt of ₹324 crores against gross debt of ₹435 crores and cash/bank balances of ₹111 crores, translating to net debt-to-equity of 0.4x.
DSO at 114 days, within the historical range of 90-115 days seen over the last 18 quarters.
Pending receivable of ₹15 crores related to a favorable court judgement.
Effective tax rate assumption of 25% going forward.

subsections.label: New contract win - Greater Noida
points: Secured new contract from Greater Noida Industrial Development Authority for procurement and comprehensive O&M of electrical mechanical road sweeping machines across Greater Noida East zone.
₹243 crores project over 5 years with a further 2-year extension option; expected to commence in Q3FY27 and contribute approximately ₹46 crores in revenue in its first year.
Project involves deploying 16 electric sweepers along with supporting infrastructure and manpower covering approximately 640 kilometers of roads daily.
Company also secured a new contract from Greater Noida Municipal Corporation, mentioned during Q&A as won 'yesterday' (relative to call date).

subsections.label: Volume growth outlook
points: BMC contract (7 wards bagged) will add around 1,500 tons per day; Atkoli processing project in Thane will add another 600-800 tons per day starting Q3/Q4FY27, but neither is reflected for the full year yet.
BMC contract started with only 1 ward with 7 days of operation in Q1; Q2 will show a slightly better number on tonnage, with Q3 and Q4 reflecting full-state operation from the BMC contract.
Atkoli project will also reach full volume by Q4; Q4FY27 will be the test of total volumes handled and will become the base for the company going forward.
Growth from existing portfolio (6-9% via escalations) plus new contract scope (10-15% additional) is expected to be lumpy given the 2-3 quarter lag between LOA signing and P&L recognition.

subsections.label: C&T business
points: C&T revenue up 10% YoY to ₹156 crores (mentioned in Q&A as approximately ₹166 crores) on tonnage of 0.55 million tons (up 6% YoY, ~5.5 lakh tons per Q&A), driven by higher volumes across project sites and contractual tariff-linked escalation.
C&T revenue mix rose to 62% of total revenue in Q1FY27 from 60% in Q1FY26.

Revenue per ton for C&T is difficult to quantify because revenue also includes 3 projects (Thane, Jhansi, Varanasi) billed on number of households/units and trips rather than tonnage; scope of each project differs, with tipping fee ranging ₹1,800 to ₹4,200 depending on scope, number of vehicles, and contract duration.
Management declined to comment on divisional EBITDA margin, citing commercial sensitivity in the B2G market.

subsections.label: Processing business / RDF / Compost
points: Processing segment revenue growth moderated to 3% YoY (₹75 crores) mainly because the CIDCO bio-mining contract (a specific 2-year project) got over in the last quarter, creating a high base effect; processing tonnage of 0.85 million tons grew 5% YoY. MSW processing revenue mix held steady at 28% versus 28% a year ago; other operating income mix fell to 7% from 9%, contracts & others flat at 3%.
Total tonnage across C&T and processing reached 1.4 million tons, up 5% YoY.
Going forward, with the Atkoli project up and running by Q4FY27, the processing segment is expected to return to growth trajectory.
RDF sales of 40,000 tons, down 28% YoY, not directly comparable to Q1FY26, which had benefited from meaningful contribution from the now-completed CIDCO bio-mining project.
RDF sales decline attributed purely to timing of dispatches, not weaker demand; company is adding more customers and selling from PCMC plant in addition to CIDCO and Kanjurmarg.
RDF net realization improved to upwards of ₹300 per ton in Q1FY27 versus ~₹250 per ton in Q1FY26.
Compost sales remained broadly stable at ~6,000 tons.

subsections.label: Waste-to-Energy (WtE) at PCMC
points: WtE plant generated over 20 million green units during the quarter, avoiding ~2,782 tons of CO2 equivalent emissions; Scope 1 emissions of 6,601 tons CO2e and Scope 2 emissions of 835 tons CO2e recorded for the quarter.
MRF and composting operations resumed from July 28, 2026, currently processing around 400 tons of waste per day; WtE plant itself expected back by first week of October 2026.
During shutdown, fixed costs of ₹2.5-3 crore per month (~₹7 crore cumulative) will sit on the books; revenue will restart on a full-stream basis from first/second week of October.
Tipping fee revenue will continue, but power generation and sale revenue will be hampered during the shutdown period.
Company expects to be at full WtE capacity by Q4FY27.

subsections.label: C&D recycling
points: C&D facility achieved industry-leading recycling rate of 96%.

C&D operations recovered after BMC's two policy decisions made it mandatory for large builders to send construction & demolition waste to processing plants, boosting tonnage which had been a problem in the initial year.
Currently processing close to 600-650 tons per day against a capacity of 600 tons/day (+/-10%); plant has started delivering better financial results.
FY27 C&D revenue guidance carried over from prior quarter at ₹18-20 crores.

subsections.label: Portfolio strategy
points: Company historically ~70% C&T and 30% processing revenue mix; targeting a move towards a 50-50 portfolio between C&T and processing/WtE.

Existing portfolio provides organic growth scope of 6-9% depending on tipping fee escalation; new contract wins/scope provide additional 10-15% growth, though recognition is lumpy as it takes 2-3 quarters from contract signing (LOA) to P&L impact.

subsections.label: Processing capacity utilization
points: C&D processing tonnage currently running at 600 to 650 tons per day.
Example cited of an integrated CBG-type project sending 1,000 tons of city waste.

subsections.label: Vehicle scrapping diversification
points: Management had previously discussed entering vehicle scrapping business (identifying land, ordering machinery) but subsequently decided not to proceed due to low ROI and multiple issues.
Company is still evaluating auto scrap business as a capital-intensive area; not rushing into it but continues to view it as a potential area of diversification.

subsections.label: Compressed Biogas (CBG) / GOBARdhan scheme evaluation
points: Management has evaluated compressed biogas (CBG) projects under the GOBARdhan scheme where municipal solid waste is an input, with long-term offtake agreements possible with city gas distributors or oil marketing companies.

Company views CBG as part of an integrated waste project rather than standalone — the WtE plant handles the dry fraction while the wet fraction would be sent to the CBG plant; a standalone CBG plant is considered too small to be viable.
Management confirmed intent to pursue such integrated contracts (WtE + CBG) in the future.
Mumbai's Kanjurmarg project may see technology shift towards CBG and WtE options as directed by High Court/Supreme Court monitoring.

subsections.label: Andhra Pradesh WtE project progress
points: Company has obtained possession of land at both Kadapa and Kurnool sites.
Technology and EPC contractor JFE India has completed civil designs; civil contractor has been appointed and mobilized equipment at Kadapa; Kurnool mobilization expected in the next couple of weeks.
Financial closure for the AP project is at its last stage; company is confident of completing these projects as per schedule.

subsections.label: Long-term growth trajectory
points: Company revenue has grown from ~₹400 crores at listing in 2021 to a current scale of ~₹1,000 crores.

subsections.label: PCMC Waste-to-Energy tragic incident
points: On July 8, 2026, the PCMC region received exceptionally heavy rainfall of approximately 650 mm, well above anything historically recorded in the area.

A mound of legacy waste at the dumping site adjacent to the company's WtE facility collapsed onto the company's administrative building; 23 individuals were present, 14 were rescued, 9 lost their lives.

Company is bearing all medical and counsel expenses for the injured, providing ₹40 lakh financial assistance to each affected family, covering all funeral-related expenses, offering employment to immediate family members of the deceased, supporting education of minor children, and providing assistance navigating medical insurance and statutory claims - support to continue as long as needed.

Management clarified the waste mound involved was legacy waste located outside the area allocated to the company by the Corporation, and its remediation was not part of the company's contractual scope of work.

As a precautionary measure, activity at the WtE plant was temporarily suspended pending full structural and safety assessment; Municipal waste Collection and Transportation were unaffected throughout.
MRF and composting operations resumed from July 28, 2026; WtE operation will restart only after thorough review and certification by OEMs and Hitachi.
Company continues to cooperate fully with all concerned authorities.

subsections.label: Force majeure / structural damage / auditor note
points: Force majeure event caused by extreme monsoon conditions resulted in damage to a portion of WtE project assets; does not impact core operating assets.

Auditors flagged that a review is needed by OEM suppliers to assess structural damage before finalizing cost estimates; not flagged as a compliance issue by management, but a landslide-related structural review pending, expected to be addressed in Q2.

subsections.label: Cost inflation pressures
points: Higher operating expenses including vehicle hiring and transportation costs at the CIDCO plant pressured margins.
Employee costs rose due to Maharashtra state government revision in DA rates (new Labour Code) creating a timing mismatch versus escalation recovery.

Management flagged inflationary pressure from high crude/crude derivative prices; cost of additives, fabrication, and gases used for cutting/repairing metals has become expensive, especially after the recent conflict in the Gulf of Hormuz.

60-70% of operating expense is labour-centric, fuel-centric, repairs-and-maintenance-centric, and tonnage-inflow-dependent — items partly beyond company's quarterly control (e.g., DA increases cannot be forecast with exactitude).
Escalations cover approximately 80% of operating cost, but there is a lag before increases are recovered.

subsections.label: Litigation / regulatory risk - Kanjurmarg
points: Joint petition filed by Antony Waste and State of Maharashtra with Supreme Court hearing scheduled August 12, 2026.

Management does not see a risk of the Kanjurmarg project being moved to another location since Supreme Court has indicated it wants to see practicality of BMC shifting the project or finding an alternate source, and there is currently no viable alternate option.
Monitoring committee appointed by the Bombay High Court has been supportive and appreciative of initiatives taken at Kanjurmarg.

Any change is more likely to be in the context of a technology shift (city of Bombay moving toward CBG and waste-to-energy technology options), which High Court and Supreme Court are also likely to favor.

subsections.label: RDF/inert disposal closure cost pattern
points: Bio-mining contracts show a cost spike in the closure phase: as a project nears completion, inert material (which cannot be sold to cement companies, unlike RDF) must be disposed of, driving up transportation/disposal costs in the last part of any bio-mining contract.
Similar closure-cost dynamic expected/observed in the Greater Noida bio-mining contract as well.
The ₹10 crore incremental cost related to CIDCO bio-mining closure is not expected to repeat since the CIDCO contract is complete.

subsections.label: Business volatility / quarterly performance variability
points: Management acknowledged recurring 'surprises' each quarter are inherent to the waste management business given cost items (labour, fuel, repairs) that are difficult to forecast precisely on a quarterly basis.

Management recommends viewing company performance on an annual or multi-year basis rather than quarter-on-quarter, citing revenue growth from ~₹400 crores at listing (2021) to ~₹1,000 crores currently, with EBITDA margin having remained largely steady upwards of 20-22% over the last 4 years despite quarterly volatility.

subsections.label: Margin trajectory outlook
points: Management expects margin profile to slightly improve going forward due to re-negotiation of terms with transport entities; will not be as bad as Q1.
Labour cost pressure expected to see respite in H2FY27 as bulk of projects have escalations linked in.
FY27 has certain upticks: BMC contract starts from Q3 with slightly better margin profile; Atkoli capex reimbursement comes in by Q4 with higher margin profile.
Internal threshold is to return to historical margin trend, but can vary plus or minus a quarter.
Margin trajectory expected to normalize to historic levels within the next 3 quarters as labour cost as % of revenue reverts to the 30-31% historical range, with margin expansion stepping in FY28.
By FY28, once escalation approvals for labour cost increases have been passed through, margin trajectory is expected to be back to historic levels.
FY27 EBITDA margin guided to be below the long-term 20-odd% (referenced long-term target of 22-24% by analyst).

subsections.label: WtE restart & full capacity outlook
points: WtE plant expected to restart operations by first week of October 2026 with revenue starting on a full-stream basis from first/second week of October.
Company expects to be at full WtE capacity by Q4FY27.

subsections.label: Volume/tonnage outlook
points: BMC contract (starting Q3FY27) to add ~1,500 tons/day incrementally; Atkoli project to add 600-800 tons/day incrementally, both ramping through Q3/Q4FY27 with full run-rate visible from Q1FY28.
No further one-off expenses anticipated for the remainder of FY27 apart from the WtE-related impact expected in Q2.

guidance_ledger.statement: Analyst referenced long-term guidance of around 22% to 24% EBITDA margin; management confirmed internal threshold is to go back to historical margin trend.

Margin pressure in Q1 not expected to persist at same level; internal threshold is to return to historical margin trend by FY27 end, though it can be plus or minus a quarter, aided by BMC contract (Q3) and Atkoli capex reimbursement (Q4) which have better margin profiles.
Margin trajectory expected to be back to historic levels in FY28 once labour cost as % of revenue normalizes to 30-31% range and escalation approvals are passed through.
WtE plant expected back by first week of October 2026; revenue to start on full-stream basis from first/second week of October.
Company expects to be at full WtE capacity by Q4FY27.
Fixed costs of approximately ₹2.5-3 crore per month during shutdown, cumulating to around ₹7 crore on the books.
Expected impairment charge in the range of ₹22-24 crores, to be treated as exceptional/extraordinary item, excluding any insurance recovery; more details in Q2 results.
Weighted average cost of debt (currently ~10.1%) expected to trend lower as Lara Renewable refinancing benefit fully reflects going forward.
Processing segment expected to return to growth trajectory once Atkoli project is up and running by Q4FY27.
Existing portfolio gives scope of 6% to 9% growth depending upon tipping fee escalation.
New business/scope of additional growth will give around 10% to 15% additional growth, though lumpy given 2-3 quarter lag from LOA signing to P&L recognition.
Company moving from ~70% C&T/30% processing towards a target 50-50 portfolio mix between C&T and processing/WtE.
Q4FY27 will represent the total test of volumes handled (with BMC and Atkoli ramped up), becoming the base for the company going forward into next financial year Q1.
No further one-off expenses anticipated for the remainder of FY27 apart from the WtE-related impact expected in Q2.
The ₹10 crore incremental transportation/disposal cost related to CIDCO bio-mining closure is not expected to repeat since the CIDCO contract is complete.
25% stated assumption of effective tax rate for group companies (carried over from prior quarter, not newly restated this call).

We remain confident of delivering 15% to 20% revenue CAGR over the next 5 years, backed by a record Rs.18,000 crores order book, 2 large-scale WTE projects in Andhra Pradesh, an expanding EPR platform and India secular tailwind in urban-based infrastructure.
EBITDA margins held at around 22% for both Q4 and full year, in line with our stated guidance.
Incremental capex would be around Rs.750-odd crores needed for the Atkoli processing, 2 WTE projects at Andhra Pradesh and BMC 2 C&T contracts.
The 2 WTE projects that we have envisaged of AP will start contributing to revenue post FY29.
We expect an uptick in the current year; a fair assumption would be Rs.18 crores to Rs.20 crores on the C&D business in the current year.
BMC C&T contracts revenue stream of Rs.1,330 crores spread over 7 years, averaging Rs.190 crores per year as the annual run rate.
Total capex of Rs.650-700-odd crores (~Rs.750 crores) will be captured into contract revenue over the next 2-2.5 years, spread 40% in FY27/28 and balance 60% in FY28/29.

risk_register.risk: Input cost inflation (fuel, additives, repairs & maintenance)
risk_register.note: Cost of additives, fabrication, and cutting/repair gases has spiked, exacerbated by the recent conflict in the Gulf of Hormuz; ~60-70% of opex is labour/fuel/R&M-centric and tonnage-dependent, partly beyond company's quarterly control.

risk_register.risk: CIDCO bio-mining contract closure cost spike
risk_register.note: Closure-phase disposal of inert material caused ₹10 crore incremental cost in Q1; contract now complete, cost not expected to recur.

risk_register.risk: Kanjurmarg litigation / Supreme Court hearing
risk_register.note: Joint petition by Antony Waste and Maharashtra State; Supreme Court hearing Aug 12, 2026; management does not see risk of project relocation given lack of practical alternative; monitoring committee supportive.

risk_register.risk: Escalation timing mismatch
risk_register.note: Cost increases (labour, other) incurred immediately but escalation recovery only occurs after ~6 months based on contract-specific annual escalation cycle, covering ~80% of operating cost.

risk_register.risk: Quarterly earnings volatility / unpredictability
risk_register.note: Management acknowledged repeated quarterly 'surprises' are inherent to the business; recommends evaluating performance annually/multi-year rather than quarter-on-quarter.

risk_register.risk: Structural damage requiring OEM review (auditor flag)
risk_register.note: Auditors noted need for OEM supplier review of structural damage before cost estimates can be finalized; expected to be resolved in Q2.

risk_register.risk: Rising fuel cost and minimum wage hikes
risk_register.note: 100% of revenue has escalation built in; minimum wage change impact was only Rs.5.2 crores on the entire books, well cushioned versus large infra peers.

risk_register.risk: Delay in realization of escalation cash flows
risk_register.note: Liability is acknowledged and accepted by clients per tender conditions and is contractual; past delays were due to absence of standing committees/elected members, now largely rectified as most municipal corporations have elected members.

risk_register.risk: Auto tire recycling / scrapping business demand shortfall
risk_register.note: Institutional demand has not captured expectations; company in wait-and-watch mode before investing incremental capital.

risk_register.risk: C&D segment volume delay
risk_register.note: Extended Mumbai monsoon (lasting until post-November) delayed C&D volume pickup and dragged EBITDA; volumes have since picked up sharply from February onward due to BMC policy mandate.

risk_register.risk: Higher vehicle deployment and hiring costs at Nagpur, Noida, PCMC
risk_register.note: Additional vehicles deployed due to higher tonnage, along with higher hiring costs, contributed to slight EBITDA softness YoY.

risk_register.risk: Bhiwandi and other arbitration matters
risk_register.note: Supreme Court dismissed BNCMC's SLP, directing disbursement of Rs.15 crores settlement with 9% interest on delay; reinforces confidence in resolution of remaining arbitration matters.

risk_register.risk: PAT growth lag versus EBITDA growth
risk_register.note: Attributed to higher interest and depreciation from WTE plants and 3 large C&T contracts capitalized over last 3 years; gap expected to persist until AP WTE projects contribute revenue post FY29.

themes.label: Margin Discipline via Escalation Contracts
themes.note: EBITDA margin fell to 16.8% in Q1FY27 from 24.4% YoY due to cost inflation, CIDCO closure costs, and refinancing charge, though escalations cover ~80% of opex and management expects normalization by FY28.

themes.label: EBITDA-to-PAT Gap (Interest & Depreciation)
themes.note: PAT fell to ₹0.7 crores from ₹23 crores YoY, hit by higher finance costs (+35% YoY) and a one-time ₹7 crore loan prepayment charge.

themes.label: Balance Sheet Strength & Leverage Capacity
themes.note: Refinanced ₹140 crore Lara Renewable loan cutting rate from 10.25% to 8.25%, extending tenure to 15 years for a net ₹14 crore benefit; gross debt at ₹435 crores, net debt-to-equity at 0.4x.

themes.label: WTE Expansion (Andhra Pradesh)
themes.note: Land possession secured at Kadapa and Kurnool, civil designs completed by JFE India, civil contractor mobilized at Kadapa, financial closure nearing completion.

themes.label: Order Book Visibility
themes.note: New ₹243 crore, 5-year Greater Noida road-sweeping contract secured, expected to commence Q3FY27 and contribute ~₹46 crores in year one; BMC and Atkoli ramp-ups to drive volume growth through FY27.

themes.label: C&D Segment Regulatory Tailwind
themes.note: BMC policy decisions mandating builders send C&D waste to processing plants helped the facility reach 600-650 tons/day against 600 tons/day capacity, delivering better financial results with 96% recycling rate.

themes.label: Non-MSW Revenue Diversification
themes.note: Management evaluating compressed biogas (CBG) under GOBARdhan scheme as part of integrated waste projects, while previously explored vehicle scrapping business was shelved due to low ROI.

key_takeaways: We delivered healthy year-on-year revenue growth of 6%, reaching ₹269 crores, driven by higher volumes across our project sites and supported by contractual tariff linked escalation.

During the quarter we successfully refinanced the term loan of Antony Lara Renewable Energy Private Limited, our material subsidiary operating the WtE facility in PCMC. This refinancing brought the interest rate down from 10.25% to 8.25% per annum.

We secured a new contract from the Greater Noida Industrial Development Authority for the procurement and comprehensive O&M of electrical mechanical road sweeping machines... This is a ₹243 crores project over 5 years with a further 2-year extension option... Expected to commence in Q3 FY27 and contribute approximately ₹46 crores in revenue in its first year.
The EBITDA came in at ₹45 crores, which is down 27% year-on-year and 33% sequentially with EBITDA margin at 16.8% compared to 24.4% in Q1 FY26 and 22.8% in Q4 FY26.

This compression was driven by 3 factors, higher operating expenses... employee costs, which rose 18% year-on-year and now represents 34% of our revenue versus 30% a year ago and the deferral of certain Q4 FY26 waste disposal transformation activities into this quarter, which added an incremental expense of approximately ₹10 crores.

PAT for the quarter stood at ₹0.7 crores, down sharply from ₹23 crores in the same period last year, further impacted by a one-time expense of ₹7 crores related to the prepayment of the Antony Lara Renewable Energy term loan.
We expect an impairment charge in the range of around ₹22 crores to ₹24 crores, which we will treat as an exceptional extraordinary item separate from our core operating performance.
We view this quarter's profitability as transitional rather than the structural thing given the one-off nature of both the transportation cost deferral and the refinancing charge.
pressing_questions: Why we always keep seeing surprises? ... this quarter we see the margins have gone for a toss and this was not called out in previous con calls, you were always saying that our margin profile will be in the range of 22%, 24%, depending upon the contracts what we have.

I also saw in the report that there is a joint petition being applied by Antony Waste and state of Maharashtra. And tomorrow, there is hearing from Supreme Court on 12th of August... suppose we get anything against the government and Antony waste, do you see any impact to us?
Can you just elaborate what concerns we have [with the auditor compliance note]? Did we comply with any of the regulations, is it?

quarters.summary: Management guided to 15-20% revenue CAGR over the next 5 years, backed by a record Rs.18,000 crores order book, 2 large-scale WTE projects in Andhra Pradesh, an expanding EPR platform and India's urban infrastructure tailwind, while EBITDA margins are aspired to be sustained at 20-22% aided by contractual escalations; the AP WTE projects will start contributing to revenue only post FY29, with incremental capex of ~Rs.750 crores mainly for Atkoli processing, the 2 AP WTE projects and the BMC 2 C&T contracts.

subsections.label: P&L Drivers
points: FY26 operating revenue growth underpinned by higher volumes, contractual tariff escalation and consistent execution across project portfolio.
Core operational revenue including project revenue crossed Rs.1,000 crores for the first time, reflecting scale built over 25 years.
EBITDA margins held at around 22% for both Q4 and full year, in line with stated guidance, reflecting disciplined cost management even while investing in scale.
Both Q4 FY25 and full-year FY25 included a onetime income of Rs.24 crores; adjusted for this, Q4 PAT is up ~67% YoY and full-year PAT up 20% YoY, demonstrating strong underlying earnings momentum.

PAT has remained relatively flat over the last 5 years despite steady revenue/EBITDA growth mainly due to higher interest and depreciation as WTE plants and 3 large C&T contracts kicked in over the last 3 years; difference will persist until AP WTE projects contribute revenue post FY29.

subsections.label: Balance Sheet & Capital Allocation
points: Net debt to equity at 0.3x gives firepower to borrow more for upcoming projects backed by assured revenue streams and long-term contracts.

Both WTE AP projects come with a firm commitment from JFE, the technology vendor, at a fixed-term cost contract, capturing cost overrun risk and time overrun risk well within the nature of the business.
Company financially in a much stronger position today than pre-COVID; A- rating at key downstream subsidiary level, BBB+ at listed entity level; cost of borrowing sub-10%.

Debt pay-down normally funded from operations; cash flow from operations before working capital was ~Rs.220 crores in FY26, part used to repay debt; aggressive policy of paying down debt to build healthy cash cushion for future projects.

subsections.label: Tax
points: Deferred tax reversal of Rs.19 crores driven by two factors: Rs.8 crores tax on undistributed profit returned due to AG Enviro merger into Antony Waste (one-time item), and a Rs.83 crores tax provision created at Section 80-IA Antony Lara SPV related to incremental capex, with Rs.3 crores of excess tax provision written back.
Stated assumption of effective tax rate for group companies going forward is 25%.

subsections.label: Cost Inflation
points: Employee expenses up 19% and other expenses up 17% in FY26 due to increased headcount, normal wage inflation and minimum wage changes under the Labour Code.
Minimum wage change impact on entire books was only Rs.5.2 crores, described as well cushioned compared to other large infra companies.
Other expenses include a major chunk of RDF transportation costs and hiring expenses, which increased over the last two quarters driven by higher RDF transportation volumes (177,000 tons sold).

subsections.label: EBITDA Margin Softness Factors
points: Slight EBITDA softness YoY attributed to three factors: (1) construction & demolition waste volumes picking up late due to extended Mumbai monsoon lasting until post-November, which dragged numbers since the cost factor differs for the C&D entity; (2) additional vehicles deployed at Nagpur, Noida and PCMC due to higher tonnage, reflected in higher cost; (3) higher hiring costs.

subsections.label: Legal/Arbitration Development
points: Supreme Court dismissed Bhiwandi Nizampur City Municipal Corporation's Special Leave Petition in the long-standing Bhiwandi arbitration matter, directing the corporation to disburse a settlement amount of Rs.15 crores within 3 months with 9% interest on any delay.
This favorable ruling reinforces track record of contractual compliance and gives added confidence in resolution of remaining arbitration matters.

subsections.label: Order Book Composition & Visibility
points: Order book as of March 2026 stands at an all-time high of Rs.18,000 crores, providing exceptional revenue visibility and underpinning confidence in sustained compounding growth ahead.
Rs.18,000 crores revenue split is broadly 60% processing and 40% C&T businesses.

Incremental capex needed is around Rs.750 crores, mainly for the new projects: Atkoli processing, the 2 WTE projects at Andhra Pradesh, and the BMC 2 C&T contracts, since bulk of existing C&T operations (excluding BMC's 2 contracts) are already funded with revenues already flowing.
Order book execution: most contracts are either 7 years or 20 years in tenor; ~40% of revenue will be executed in the next 5-7 years (C&T operations), with the balance spread over the next 15 years.

subsections.label: BMC C&T Contracts
points: BMC C&T contracts revenue stream corrected to Rs.1,330 crores spread over 7 years, averaging Rs.190 crores per year as the annual run rate (correction issued to an earlier erroneous statement of Rs.1,000 crores over 10 years).

subsections.label: Pipeline / Tenders
points: Company has bid for 3 collection and transportation contracts in the northern part of the country and one waste-to-energy project in the southern part of the country; these are at the bidding stage.

subsections.label: Volume & Revenue Growth Drivers
points: FY26 was a year of broad-based volumes growth across the platform, driven by new project additions, contract renewals and continued scaling of biomining and RDF operations.
Q4 momentum was particularly strong in processing, reflecting improved utilization at biomining and MRF facilities.

Volumes jump mainly came from the CIDCO Biomining Project, a fixed-term contract; revenue jump is not commensurate with the volume jump because of this; non-CIDCO Biomining revenue growth was ~8%, representing underlying revenue growth.

subsections.label: C&D (Construction & Demolition) Segment
points: C&D business contributed around Rs.9 crores of revenue in FY26, lower than anticipated.
Expect an uptick in the current year; from February onwards volumes jumped to averaging 480-520 tons per day compared to 280-300 tons per day in the previous 8 months.

Uptick driven by a strong BMC policy change making it mandatory for developers to route C&D waste through professional/authorized collection and processing units; this policy push, delayed by about a year due to lack of elected members and procedural delays, is now translating into higher volumes expected to persist.
Fair assumption for current year C&D revenue is Rs.18-20 crores.

subsections.label: Non-MSW / Diversification Revenue Streams
points: Non-municipal revenue streams strongly skewed towards RDF sales, compost, recyclables and EPR.

New business line Click2Clean, part of Antony Recycling, is a B2B segment into small-scale pest-control recyclables and deep housekeeping for clients including P.N. Gadgil, Asian Paints, Suntory Wines, Beams.
Going forward, revenue from sale of power to DISCOMs from the AP WTE projects will also add to this non-MSW revenue bucket.

subsections.label: EPR Credits
points: Company entered the EPR business and monetized nearly 20% of allotted EPR credits in the first year of PCMC WTE operations, described as a strong initial proof point.
Recognized close to Rs.2.2 crores of EPR credits eligible and earned in FY25.
Not yet a significant amount, but once the pattern is established and quantified, EPR could add close to 10% of PCMC WTE's revenue.

subsections.label: Contract Revenue Composition
points: Of the Rs.160 crores booked in FY26 (none of which relates to the new AP/BMC projects), not more than 25% is actual contract/project costing revenue; the balance comes from sale of RDF, compost and mechanical sweeping revenue sitting under the same bucket.
70% of that revenue composition will continue in the current financial year, though allocated to different revenue heads.

subsections.label: WTE Technology Partnership
points: Strategic partnership with Japan's JFE Engineering for WTE development in Andhra Pradesh deepens the company's technology edge.

Both AP WTE projects come with a firm commitment from JFE, the technology vendor, at a fixed-term cost contract, which captures cost-overrun risk and keeps time-overrun risk within the nature of the business.

subsections.label: PCMC WTE Performance
points: PCMC WTE facility delivered 69.3 million units of green power in FY26 and helped avoid approximately 10,000 tons of CO2e emissions during the year, validating the company's technology and execution capability as it scales into the 2 large AP WTE projects.

subsections.label: PCMC WTE Plant Utilization
points: Company had approximately 90 days of planned and reparative shutdown during the year, which reflected in a lower PLF of 56%.
Post the maintenance period, the plant has been operating at approximately 86% PLF consistently.

subsections.label: Capex Deployment for New Projects
points: Total capex of Rs.650-700-odd crores (also referenced as ~Rs.750 crores) will be captured into contract revenue/contract costing over the next 2 to 2.5 years for the AP WTE and related projects.

Capex/contract revenue booking pattern normally spread in a 40:60 ratio between Year 1 and Year 2 (24-month construction period, spanning calendar years); a part will fall in the current financial year and a larger chunk in the following financial year.
Rs.750 crores capex split as 40% in FY27/28 part and balance 60% in FY28/29.

subsections.label: New Contracts by Region
points: Secured 2 waste-to-energy projects in Andhra Pradesh, 2 new collection and transportation contracts in Mumbai, and a preprocessing solid waste facility in Thane during FY26.
Bid for 3 collection and transportation contracts in the northern part of the country and one waste-to-energy project in the southern part of the country, currently at bidding stage.

subsections.label: Mumbai WTE Update
points: On the Mumbai waste-to-energy matter, the issue is being taken seriously at the Bombay High Court, which has been seeking a long-term sustainable solution; management believes the corporation will come back with a WTE proposal in the near future.

subsections.label: FY26 Platform Expansion & Milestones
points: FY26 marks 25 years of Antony Waste's journey in transforming India's waste management landscape, evolving into a scaled, purpose-driven platform.
Board recommended a maiden dividend of Rs.0.50 per equity share (10% of face value of Rs.5), reflecting confidence in financial position while preserving capital for the next phase of growth.
Company entered the EPR business; secured 2 WTE projects in Andhra Pradesh, 2 new C&T contracts in Mumbai, and a preprocessing solid waste facility in Thane.
Strategic partnership with Japan's JFE Engineering for WTE development in Andhra Pradesh deepens technology edge.
Successful merger of AG Enviro Infra Projects into the company strengthened operational integration and long-term capability base.
Company operates with ~10,000 employees, vendors and support staff across the country.

subsections.label: Cost Inflation Risks
points: Rising fuel cost and minimum wage hikes in certain states flagged as a near-term macro pressure by an analyst; management noted 100% of revenue has escalation built into the system, so cost pressure is passed through contractually.
Minimum wage change under the Labour Code had only Rs.5.2 crores impact on the entire books, described as well cushioned compared to other large infra companies.
Delay in realization of escalation cash flows can occur, but the liability is acknowledged and accepted by clients per tender conditions and is contractual, arriving in due course.

subsections.label: Historical Delay Risk (largely resolved)
points: Past delays in recognizing escalation were due to absence of standing committees and elected members at municipal corporations; now most corporations have elected members, so this procedural risk is largely rectified and significant recognition delays are not expected going forward.

subsections.label: C&D and Recycling Demand Risk
points: Auto tire recycling and scrapping businesses have not captured expected institutional demand; management is in a wait-and-watch mode until the industry stabilizes before investing incremental capital into a revenue-generating mode.

subsections.label: Arbitration Risk
points: Bhiwandi arbitration matter with Bhiwandi Nizampur City Municipal Corporation was a long-standing dispute; Supreme Court's dismissal of the corporation's SLP is a favorable resolution, though other arbitration matters remain outstanding (management now has added confidence in their resolution).

subsections.label: Growth Outlook
points: Company remains confident of delivering 15% to 20% revenue CAGR over the next 5 years, backed by the record Rs.18,000 crores order book, 2 large-scale WTE projects in Andhra Pradesh, an expanding EPR platform, and India's secular tailwind in urban infrastructure.
Long-term aspiration is to maintain 20% to 22% EBITDA margin, supported by contractual escalations across 100% of revenue.
AP WTE projects will start contributing to revenue only post FY29, which will help close the interest/depreciation-driven gap between EBITDA growth and PAT growth.

Focused on driving sustainable growth through disciplined execution, operational excellence and continued innovation, supported by record order book, growing project portfolio and expanding opportunities across the waste management value chain.

key_takeaways: FY '26 was a year of broad-based volumes growth across our platform. The C&T volumes grew approximately 9% year-on-year to 2.12 million tons, while processing volumes expanded approximately 19% to 3.6 million tons.
FY '26 operating revenue reached Rs.920 crores, which is up 9%, while Q4 operating revenue came in at Rs.254 crores, up 14%.
Our core operational revenue, including project revenue crossed Rs.1,000 crores for the first time.
EBITDA margins held at around 22% for both Q4 and for full year, in line with our stated guidance.
Our order book as of March 2026 stands at an all-time high of Rs.18,000 crores, providing exceptional revenue visibility.

We remain confident of delivering 15% to 20% revenue CAGR over the next 5 years, backed by a record Rs.18,000 crores order book, 2 large-scale WTE projects in Andhra Pradesh, an expanding EPR platform and India secured tailwind in urban-based infrastructure.
The Board has recommended a maiden dividend of Rs.0.50 per equity share, that is 10% of the face value of Rs.5.

The Hon' Supreme Court dismissed the Bhiwandi Nizampur City Municipal Corporation's Special Leave Petition, directing the corporation to disburse the settlement amount of Rs.15 crores within 3 months with an interest of 9% on any delay.
pressing_questions: Sir, my first question is regarding the top line performance. So when we are guiding 15-odd percent top line CAGR expectation, I feel, based on the contractual term, you will see a significant bump in FY '28, '29 with the new waste-to-energy plants coming in. So from the working capital perspective and the debt component perspective, how you are seeing that aspect?

Sir, if we look at company's performance over the last 5 years, both revenue and EBITDA have grown steadily while the PAT has remained relatively flat. Could you help us understand the key reasons behind it? And how can the PAT growth be going forward?

Sir, we also have seen our employee expenses and other expenses increased by around 19% and 17%, respectively, during FY26... second was during some decline in EBITDA margins this year. So could you share some light on the factors what impacted our EBITDA margins?
In terms of the C&D, what has changed, which has led to the doubling of the volumes? And is this the volume that we should look at or that we will see incremental volume increase over this?

TECHM.about: Tech Mahindra Ltd provides comprehensive range of IT services, including IT enabled service, application development and maintenance, consulting and enterprise business solutions, etc. to a diversified base of corporate customers in a wide range of industries.[1]

quarters.summary: Tech Mahindra delivered its strongest revenue growth since the start of its transformation journey in Q1 FY27 (revenue up 6.1% YoY reported, 6.6% YoY CC), with margin expansion for the 11th consecutive quarter (EBIT margin 14.4%). Management reiterated confidence in achieving FY27 targets of above-peer-average growth and 15% operating margin, while flagging some Q2 headwinds (European auto one-off pullback, Comviva seasonality reversal) offset by ramp-up of large deals and continued healthy order book, subject to macro volatility.

key_figures.label: Estimated impact of European auto acceleration pullback on next quarter revenue

subsections.label: Margin drivers
points: Margin expansion was led by volume growth and savings from Project Fortius, partially offset by Comviva seasonality and business mix.
Seasonality on visa/travel costs from Q4 to Q1 impacts gross margin negatively.
Comviva seasonality was a negative to gross margin.
European auto segment accelerated program deliveries were dilutive to gross margin.
SG&A benefits continue from portfolio company consolidation.
Going forward, margin improvement will be a mix of gross margin actions (Project Fortius fixed price productivity, higher T&M utilization) and continued SG&A benefit from portfolio consolidation.
Management has not articulated a specific exit margin target but expects margin to move upwards of 15% by Q4, tracking towards FY27 target.
Wage increase to be effective from Q2 FY27 in a phased fashion, will be a margin headwind; also anticipate some productivity pressures from an AI perspective.

subsections.label: Cash flow and working capital
points: DSO improvement driven by higher collection efficiency, plus some accelerated payments that will normalize next quarter, and a favorable FX benefit on AR (versus negative in prior period) that will also normalize.
Working capital strategy remains a key focus area; will continue to improve on a long-term basis though quarterly seasonality will persist.

subsections.label: Capital allocation / investment
points: Continuing to invest in AI capabilities via Makers Lab, the core of the innovation engine, translating emerging technology into practical enterprise solutions.
Building differentiated capabilities in domain-specific and sovereign AI.

Investments in talent, IP, and software licenses will continue and be calibrated based on growth opportunity areas (e.g., Communications, Learning, Engineering, Retail/CPG centers of excellence in Hyderabad).

subsections.label: SG&A one-offs clarification
points: No one-off provision reversal or bad-debt related provision reversal in SG&A this quarter that would impact going forward.

key_figures.label: Clients generating >US$50 million revenue, increase YoY

subsections.label: Deal momentum
points: Deal wins were broad-based across key verticals and geographies, with largest deal wins coming from manufacturing and HLS verticals.
This is the third consecutive quarter of deal TCV above US$1 billion.
Based on ACV won over the last 12 months, ISG named Tech Mahindra among the top 15 sourcing standouts across all regions: Global, Americas, EMEA, and Asia.
Management stated large deal outcomes are quite binary (zero or one) and forecasting beyond a quarter or two is limited; pipeline currently looks strong.

subsections.label: Demand environment
points: Every vertical delivered YoY growth during the quarter; positive momentum expected to continue based on pipeline and ramp-up of recent deal wins, subject to macro environment.

Demand shift observed: application development demand skewing towards modernization; platform/enterprise application demand (ServiceNow, SAP, Salesforce) strengthening rather than facing a 'SaaS eclipse'.
Strong demand seen in data and AI family: cloud AI services, data engineering (Databricks, Snowflake), and GenAI frameworks.

key_takeaways: For the quarter, we reported revenues of US$1.66 billion, representing a 6.1% year-on-year growth on a reported basis and 6.6% growth in constant currency.
Operating margins stood at 14.4%, reflecting sustained execution discipline, operational rigor, and a continuous focus on profitable growth.
Overall, every vertical delivered year-on-year growth during the quarter.

The number of clients generating more than US$50 million in revenue increased by seven year-on-year, reflecting the trust our clients place in us and our ability to expand strategically within our key accounts.

We delivered total deal wins of US$1.078 billion... Based on the annual contract value won over the last 12 months, ISG named Tech Mahindra among the top 15 sourcing standouts across all regions: Global, Americas, EMEA, and Asia.
We delivered our strongest revenue growth since the start of our transformation journey, while continuing to expand margins for 11 consecutive quarters.

We generated US$167 million of free cash flow during the quarter, up 94% on a Y-o-Y basis. Higher collection efficiency supported the DSO improvement to 84 days, a reduction of five days on a quarter-on-quarter basis.

The momentum we've built across growth, deal wins, client engagement, and profitability gives us confidence that we are well-positioned to deliver on our FY 27 ambition of achieving above average of the peer growth and an operating margin of 15%.

So how sustainable from here on we should see -- should we expect a similar performance in the coming quarters [on DSO and free cash flow]?

If you can help us understand that on a year-on-year basis, do you expect the growth to accelerate further from here on, maybe into high single digit for the full year? High single digit or how to think about the full year growth, that would be very helpful.

Were you surprised by any segment or was this a plan and as you look at the performance, can you maybe separate out the demand environment, was it -- has it improved at all or were you just taking more successful at taking share and the same comment if you can make for the rest of the year, your confidence of sustaining this comes from your own execution or you think demand is also improving?

When you joined TechM, you mentioned that the pricing of Tech Mahindra is comparable to peers, implying potential of high teens margins. Does that assessment hold true even today, and if yes, have you thought through as to how you would use the surplus margin in case you're able to execute well over the coming quarters?

Now we are near to the aspirational margin of 15%, is it fair to assume the TCV has an upwards scope in the coming quarters because discipline approach on the margin, that challenge is reducing quarter-on-quarter?

quarters.summary: Tech Mahindra closed FY26 with highest-ever deal wins (USD 3.79bn, up 42% YoY), revenue growth of 1.9% reported / 0.6% CC for the year, and EBIT margin expansion of 290bps to 12.6%. Management reiterated FY27 targets of organic constant-currency revenue growth above peer average and 15% EBIT margin, citing 10 consecutive quarters of margin expansion (6.4% exit margin to 13.8% in Q4FY26) and rising deal-win momentum (Q4 deal wins USD 1,073mn, up 35% YoY) as evidence the three-year transformation plan (turnaround, stabilization, benefit realization) is on track heading into FY27, the "most important year" of the journey.

key_takeaways: We closed the year with the highest ever deal wins in the last many years.
Full-year revenues stand at USD 6.385 billion, up 1.9% on a reported basis and 0.6% in constant currency.
Operating profit is USD 797 million, up 31.4% year-on-year, with margins expanding by about 290 basis points to 12.6%.
We closed the year with total deal-wins of USD 3.79 billion, representing a 42% growth year-on-year.
We are reiterating our FY27 financial targets... including achieving organic constant currency revenue growth above our peer group's average and achieving an EBIT margin of 15%.
We've now had 10 quarters of margin expansion, so going from an exit margin of 6.4% to 13.8% in the most recent quarter.

In line with our stated capital allocation policy, the board has approved final dividend of Rs. 36 per share, taking the total dividend announced for the year at Rs. 51 per share, the highest ever we've done.
Our NPS score for this year is now the highest in the industry.

subsections.label: Cost drivers
points: Employee cost increased due to annual increments/wage impact and a slight increase in headcount.
Power and fuel cost rose slightly mainly due to increase in coal rate.
Depreciation increased mainly due to capitalization of the backward integration plant at Dahej, Saykha, which was not capitalized in the prior quarter.
Interest cost decreased due to repayment of loans using IPO funds.

subsections.label: Other income / land sale
points: Other income increase mainly due to sale of land.

Of the INR8 crores (approx.) other income, ~INR5.7 crores relates to the land sale gain under consideration (66,000 sq. meters sold to Indo GSP, promoter group company, for INR23 crores, board approved in April).
No further one-off other income is planned for upcoming quarters; run rate impacted by increase in manpower cost not fully flowing through to PAT.
Excluding the one-off land sale gain, PBT would be roughly flat versus last year's INR29 crores rather than up ~18%.

subsections.label: Margin drivers
points: Gross margin improvement (240 bps) is broadly due to increase in product mix moving more towards specialty and differentiated (patented) products.
Margin increase supported by higher share of patented products in B2C business and good margins in B2B business.
PAT margin expected to increase further due to reduction in interest cost during the year.

subsections.label: IPO proceeds utilization
points: IPO objective was repayment of loans; loans repaid as per the stated object during the quarter.
Remaining small amount pending settlement of brokerage expenses from banks, expected to take 2-3 months to finalize before IPO account can be closed.

subsections.label: Seasonality
points: Last year Q2 was around 60% of full year's PAT; management expects a similar proportional split this year, with the absolute number increasing due to anticipated growth.

subsections.label: Product mix and growth drivers
points: Good growth in volumes of recently launched products like PCT 410 and Fighter, gaining scale in Q1.
Good growth and momentum from B2B customers co-marketing patented products, increasing farmer-level presence through their distributor network.
Strategy: when launching combinations in B2C, also offer to B2B co-marketers to increase product availability and niche positioning.

subsections.label: Business mix evolution
points: Domestic business currently split roughly equally between B2C (45%) and B2B (45%) of quarterly revenue, with exports at 10% of quarterly revenue; annually, domestic is 80% and exports 20%.
Formulations comprise 75% of business and technicals 25%.
Patented products represent 20-22% of B2C business currently, out of a broader 200+ patented product portfolio.
Aim is to nearly double patented product share within B2C business over 3 years.
Company believes it can grow faster than industry growth rate and gain more market share in states where already strong, like Maharashtra and Gujarat.
Targets over next 3 years: branded (B2C) business to reach 45-50% of domestic revenue, B2B to reach 30-35%, and export share to remain around ~20%.

subsections.label: Market share opportunity
points: Current domestic market share is roughly 3-3.5%, seen as a good opportunity to grow given strong manufacturing base.
Company sees scaling to 7-8% market share as achievable for a company of its size.

key_figures.label: Data generation lead time for technical R&D

subsections.label: Capacity and facility notes
points: Company operates multiple manufacturing facilities across India producing both technicals and formulations — an integrated model versus peers who do only one or the other.
Technical plants are multi-product and allow swapping to high-value, low-volume products to accommodate upcoming pipeline products.

Formulation plants are not seen as a bottleneck since the process is simpler (no chemical synthesis/reactions) and could be outsourced; facilities are designed to cater to peak season, hence lower average utilization.
Depreciation increased due to capitalization of the backward integration plant at Dahej, Saykha (previously not capitalized).

subsections.label: Domestic vs export seasonality
points: Business is more Kharif-led; H1 is important, and within H1, Q2 is critical due to main monsoon and demand consumption.
Export business typically gears up in H2 of the financial year, particularly for Latin America (major market Brazil) where the season is predominantly in H2.

subsections.label: International markets - Brazil / Latin America
points: Brazil is the largest global market; there is pressure on demand due to pricing volatility causing customers to delay buying.
Delayed buying patterns made timing of material delivery critical; due to China's better logistics, some orders were transferred to China despite GSP being cost competitive.
Overall Brazil demand currently not great; destocking expected, with demand for upcoming season (starting October) expected to pick up from September for H2.
Company is cautious on Brazil due to liquidity issues and credit challenges; focusing more on B2B customers with established relationships.
For other Latin America geographies (Argentina, Uruguay), identifying small pockets and planning tie-ups with second-tier distributors for further distribution in their strength geographies.
Parallelly pursuing registrations for pipeline products to exploit manufacturing facilities year-round by selling registered molecules in other parts of the world at different times of year.

subsections.label: International focus rationale
points: Main international focus is Latin America (Brazil, USA) because their crops are similar to India's and their season is nearly opposite to India's, allowing technical plants to run 12 months by servicing the reverse season after Kharif in India.
Also planning for Africa and Asian countries, but by volume/value, Brazil, USA and Latin America are the main markets.
Presence also exists in parts of Southeast Asia.

subsections.label: Raw material dynamics
points: Volatility in raw material pricing in the last quarter due to geopolitical situations; availability was not a concern but prices were very volatile, especially for products linked to petrochemicals.
Logistical challenges were present in the earlier part of the quarter.
Rupee depreciation of ~10-11% since last quarter also impacted raw material prices.

In B2B business, cost increases can generally be passed on to customers; in B2C business, there is a time lag in passing on raw material cost increases, but inventory helped cover rising costs, keeping Q1 fairly stable.
Material supply constraint is not currently present (as of ~6 weeks into Q2); July monsoon has been supportive and covered a major part of the country.

key_figures.label: PBT growth cited by analyst (up %, later disputed)

subsections.label: Farmer behaviour and adoption
points: Positive shift in farmer behaviour: increasing awareness of specialty chemicals in areas like West Bengal (previously fragmented, small farmers with less spending capacity), aided by company groundwork.
New generation of farmers is more aware, more connected to social media, and better able to evaluate products for maximum value.
Shift from curative spraying (post-infestation) toward preventive spraying, in line with developed-market trends, minimizing crop damage.

subsections.label: Strategic focus shift
points: Objective is to move increasingly towards formulations and brand products, supported across all three verticals (B2C, B2B, export).
B2B business increasingly includes specialized formulations to fill customer portfolio gaps and make GSP's patented products more reachable to farmers.

subsections.label: Flagged headwinds
points: Global geopolitical developments and climate-related risks caused certain volatility and supply chain disruptions in the quarter.
Customer holdback of demand anticipated due to pricing volatility.
War and crude price volatility, along with IMD's El Nino declaration, led farmers, channel partners and formulators to delay buying in the early part of the quarter.
Brazil liquidity issues and credit challenges are a concern, prompting cautious approach and focus on established B2B relationships.
China's better logistics model led to some export orders being diverted away from GSP despite cost competitiveness.
South India states (Andhra, Telangana, Karnataka) remain in a wait-and-watch situation from a monsoon standpoint.

subsections.label: Growth outlook
points: Company has been growing at ~15% and expects to continue growing at around that rate.
Better growth in EBITDA and PAT margin expected due to product mix shift towards differentiated portfolio and reduction in interest cost.
EBITDA expected to grow around 13-14% over the upcoming 2-3 years; overall EBITDA level expected around 12-13%.
Q2 progress on track for anticipated growth despite early monsoon delays; South India states remain a watch item.
Q2 expected to again contribute roughly ~60% of full-year PAT (similar proportion to last year), with absolute PAT number expected to increase due to anticipated growth.

subsections.label: Segment mix outlook
points: Domestic business (80% of annual revenue) mix expected to shift with branded (B2C) business growing to 45-50% and B2B to 30-35% over next 3 years.
Export share expected to remain around 20% for the next 3 years.
No further one-off other income (like the land sale gain) expected in remaining quarters of the year.

themes.note: Geopolitical volatility and rupee depreciation (~10-11%) drove raw material price volatility, particularly for petrochemical-linked products.

themes.label: Capacity headroom
themes.note: Technical utilization at 70-75% with multi-product plant flexibility; formulation utilization at 25-30% designed for peak season, not seen as a bottleneck.

themes.label: Export/international expansion
themes.note: Brazil demand delayed by pricing volatility with some orders diverted to China, but destocking-led demand expected to pick up from September for H2; tie-ups planned in Argentina/Uruguay.

themes.label: Weather/monsoon risk
themes.note: Early-quarter buying delays due to war/crude volatility and El Nino fears eased as July monsoon turned favorable and acreage of cotton, soybean, chillies increased; South India (AP, Telangana, Karnataka) still wait-and-watch.

themes.label: B2B vs B2C pricing power
themes.note: B2B business can generally pass on raw material cost increases; B2C has a time lag but is cushioned by inventory, with margin gains from both patented B2C and B2B mix.

themes.label: R&D and innovation-led differentiation
themes.note: Pipeline of 1-2 new technical products and 2-3 new patented formulations per year planned for the next 4-5 years, including new herbicide and potato-focused products to fill portfolio gaps.

key_takeaways: Overall, the financial performance in Q1 FY27 was stable, especially considering the volatile operations environments.
Revenue remained broadly stable during the quarter with strong momentum in the domestic business. However, it was partly offset by temporary raw material constraints in the international business.

Overall, the realization in the business has been better. The gross margins have improved. This improvement is broadly due to the increase in the product mix that is there wherein we have moved more towards our specialty and differentiated products.
The overall EBITDA if we see has stood at around 11%.
Finally, the profit after tax has increased by almost 16% to INR26.4 crores in the first quarter.

As you might be aware, ICRA has upgraded our rating from A to A+ stable for our long-term as well as short-term facilities for A1. This upgrade is majorly due to the repayment of borrowing from our IPO and the continued good performance of the company.
Brazil predominantly being the largest market globally, so there is a lot of pressure in terms of the demand in Brazil.

Overall, the demand is not very great currently. We are expecting that destocking and the material that is required for the upcoming season which start from October, we see that demand should then kick in in September for the H2.
