quarters.summary: GSP Crop Science reported strong 9M FY26 growth in revenue, EBITDA and PAT despite a weak agrochemical season last year due to excess rain; management expects continued sustainable growth led by patented/innovative products, with raw material and logistics cost inflation (from the Middle East conflict) largely passed on to customers, and capacity seen as sufficient to support the next 3 years of strategy.

subsections.label: P&L Drivers
points: 9-month revenue and EBITDA growth achieved despite a bad agrochemical season last year caused by 60 days of continuous rain.
EBITDA growth of 32% attributed to support from all three business verticals (B2B, B2B export, B2C) plus innovative process, patented products and new product launches.
PAT of INR75 crores is stated after an exceptional item adjustment of INR4.5 crores related to additional provisions for the new labor wage code effect.
Company strategy across three verticals (B2B, B2B export, B2C) and patented product mix underpins expectation of good and sustainable future growth.

subsections.label: Pricing Pass-through
points: Because of crude price increases from the Middle East conflict, raw material prices increased; company has passed this on to customers via a 10%-15% price hike from 1st April.

In B2B, prices are elastic and easier to pass on cost increases; in B2C there is a lag (typically two to three months) before price increases are accepted due to channel inventory, distributor network and generic market competition.
Gross profit per kg is expected to broadly sustain since cost increases are largely transferred as price increases.

Demand for nutrition products (seaweed-based, amino acid-based, liquid fertilizer categories under the fertilizer act) is expected to increase because of fertilizer shortage/high fertilizer cost driven by higher gas and ammonia prices, pushing farmers toward alternative nutrition products; company has 3-4 such products with good potential this year.
Anticipated demand ahead of the Kharif season is leading B2B partners to seek supply assurance, which is also a factor in price/demand dynamics.

subsections.label: Business Verticals
points: Company operates three verticals: domestic B2B, domestic B2C (through distributor network reaching farmers via 24 C&F locations), and export (B2B, to 37 countries).
Domestic B2B constitutes ~40% of revenue, domestic B2C ~40%, making domestic 80% total; export is 20%.

subsections.label: Patented Product Strategy
points: Differentiation strategy: introduce off-patent technicals first-in-India, then combine with existing/newer molecules to create patentable novel combinations solving multiple farmer problems in one solution.

102 patents received, 108 in pipeline; 12 patents commercialized in last 3 years, driving increase in patented product revenue contribution from 3% (3 years ago) to 17% currently, and margin profile improvement.
Strategy includes giving patented molecules to co-marketeers in B2B business after popularizing them in own B2C brand network first.

Example: PCT-410, a three-way combination seed treatment product launched 3 years back, scaled to INR50-70 crores in revenue over 2-3 years; used for coating seeds before sowing, improving germination rate and yield; popularized via marketing demonstrations and trade demonstrations at dealer level.
One product launched in FY26: an insecticide-fungicide mixture for paddy crop; seeing good results, expected to take one season to ramp up, viewed as high potential.
Plan is one to two patented product launches per year, based on segment/crop targeting.
Registration process for a single new patented combination product takes ~5 years due to long trial and data generation requirement.

Team of ~300 sales professionals and 30-35 marketing professionals; company feels 1-2 launches/year is the right pace to give due importance and scale products given team size handling both generic and new product business.

Co-marketing partners for patented products include Rallis, Sumitomo Chemicals, Mankind Pharma (Mankind Agri division), and Chambal Fertilizers; arrangement works as white-labeling — manufactured by GSP, marketed by partner company.
Company also making intermediates in-house (started an intermediate company last year) to reduce dependency on China, part of ongoing strategy.
Margin comparison: generic products carry gross margin (on material consumed) of ~35-40%; patented products carry ~55-60%, i.e., a 20-25% premium.

CTPR product example: product patent expired in 2022, process patent expired December 2025; R&D team developed innovative process, launched product in October '22, and GSP is now one of the largest technical manufacturers of this product in India.
SLR product: a suspo-emulsion formulation, first-of-its-kind launched in India by GSP; other formulations also launched first-in-India by GSP.
Company presence across all 23 states and major crops (paddy, sugarcane, corn, wheat, vegetables, rice); particularly strong in paddy and pulses, seen as having future growth potential for India.

subsections.label: R&D Structure
points: Company runs two R&D functions: technical R&D and formulation R&D.
Technical R&D focuses on innovative process development — for molecules going off-patent in future, R&D plans up to five years in advance to make the product viable from basic raw material.
Formulation R&D develops new formulations, e.g., SLR (suspo-emulsion), first launched in India by GSP among other first-in-India formulations.

subsections.label: Facility Details
points: Two technical plants — one near Ahmedabad, and the biggest plant at Nandeshari — plus one intermediate plant.
Formulation plant utilization is lower (30-40%) due to seasonality; it is a simpler plant involving mixing and grinding, no chemical reaction.
Technical plants run at 70-75% utilization currently; peak achievable utilization for both technical and formulation facilities is ~90%.
At peak utilization, with current revenue mix (75% formulations, 25% technical), company expects to reach INR1,900-2,000 crores revenue.
Additional capacity headroom exists via de-bottlenecking within existing facilities.
Newer chemistries being introduced are low-volume, high-value products, allowing good business value with minimal additional capacity.
Current plant capacity assessed as sufficient to cover the company's ~3-year strategy.

subsections.label: Export Expansion
points: Company has opened a subsidiary in Brazil as part of export expansion strategy.
Registering patented products already established in India in other geographies, specifically Brazil, to create a differentiated product portfolio for expansion there.
Exploring whether these patented products can also be patented in these new geographies.
Not exporting any product to the Middle East.

subsections.label: Sourcing
points: Raw materials/intermediates sourced mostly from China; intermediates imported from China are used to manufacture technicals.

Company maintains ~45 days of inventory for imported raw materials as a strategy, limiting immediate impact from availability concerns; some very critical/rare raw materials remain a concern but overall impact is limited.
Company also maintains inventory at all stages — raw material, finished goods, and bulk — allowing phased absorption of cost escalation.

subsections.label: Logistics
points: Logistics costs have increased because ship availability has decreased; freight from China has almost doubled, and this cost increase has been passed on to customers.
If shipping/logistics delays are prolonged by another month or so, there is a possibility that supply could be impacted; currently company is fully covered on inventory and production.

subsections.label: Input cost impact
points: Crude price increases due to Middle East conflict have raised raw material prices across the board, with availability concerns in a few raw materials.
Price increases seen in intermediates and also in ancillary products like packing material (plastics, which are petrochemical derivatives).
Fertilizer costs are very high due to increased gas and ammonia prices, and fertilizer availability is also a concern.

subsections.label: B2B Cost Pass-through Dynamics
points: In B2B business, majority of cost increases have been passed on to customers, including global B2B export clients, since global B2B clients (including in China) are aware of the same cost scenario and competitors are also raising prices.
Certain technicals that the company also procures (rather than manufactures) have seen their price increases passed onto GSP by suppliers.
Demand-supply dynamics ahead of Kharif season mean B2B partners want assured supply, which supports price acceptance despite cost pass-through.

subsections.label: Corporate History & Strategy
points: Company started by the Chairman's father in 1985; more than 40 years old.
Core strengths: manufacturing, R&D, and patents.
Started an intermediate manufacturing company last year to reduce dependency on China; strategy to continue in future.
Co-marketing/white-labeling partnerships for patented products with Rallis, Sumitomo Chemicals, Mankind Pharma (Mankind Agri), and Chambal Fertilizers.
Brazil subsidiary opened as part of international expansion strategy, including product registration and potential patenting abroad.

subsections.label: External Headwinds
points: IMD has forecasted El Nino for the Kharif season; management does not see much challenge from this given GSP's strength is in paddy, which is largely grown in irrigated areas (40% of paddy consumption is where irrigation facility is available).
Rising fertilizer prices could impact farmer profitability/spend, though management sees this as an opportunity for nutrition products rather than a pure risk.
Middle East conflict has led to crude price increases, raising raw material, logistics, and fertilizer costs; company has passed on 10-15% price increases from 1st April to mitigate.
Shipping/logistics disruptions (reduced ship availability, near doubling of freight from China) could impact supply if prolonged beyond another month.
In B2C, cost pass-through faces a lag of two to three months due to channel inventory, distributor network, and generic market competition, creating margin pressure risk in the interim.
Previous year's season was very bad for agrochemicals due to 60 days of continuous rain.

subsections.label: Forward Outlook
points: Management expects growth to be good and sustainable in future supported by the three business verticals, innovative processes, and patented/new products.
Company targets 40-50% of revenue from patented products in the next 2-3 years, up from current ~20%, continuing the growth rate experienced over the last 3 years.
Overall revenue/business growth is targeted to continue at recent growth rate plus an additional 5-7% for the upcoming 3 years.
Plan to launch one to two new patented products annually going forward.

Existing capacity (with scope for de-bottlenecking and focus on low-volume high-value new chemistries) is seen as sufficient to support the company's ~3-year strategy, with peak utilization revenue potential of INR1,900-2,000 crores.
Detailed 3-year revenue and margin guidance was declined to be shared specifically, though broad growth rate expectations were given.

guidance_ledger.statement: the growth rate that we've been experiencing since last 3 years, we're expecting that this or at least higher growth rate by another 5%-7% is what we're targeting for the upcoming 3 years
broadly, on a very high basis, almost 40% to 50% revenue will be coming from this kind of products

our plan is that we'll be coming up with such launches, one or two launches on an yearly basis wherein we'll be adding products in our portfolio based in the segment that we're targeting for particular crops
with peak utilization, we'll be almost reaching around INR1,900 crores to INR2,000 crores
Currently, it will be difficult for us to share [a detailed 3-year vision on revenue and margins]

key_takeaways: Company is more than 40 years old with main strength in manufacturing, R&D and patents; two technical plants and one intermediate plant.
10 products in last 15 years were first launched in India by GSP among products previously imported by multinational companies.
102 patents received, 108 patents in pipeline; 12 products commercialized from these patents in last 3 years.
Patented product business revenue contribution has grown from 3% three years ago to 17-20% currently.

9-month FY26 revenue of INR1,114-1,150 crores, EBITDA of INR153 crores (up 32% YoY), and PAT of INR75 crores (vs INR59.6 crores last year), the latter after an exceptional item of INR4.5 crores related to labor wage code provisions.
Business split: domestic B2B ~40%, domestic B2C ~40% (total domestic 80%), export ~20% across 37 countries via 5,000 distributors and 24 C&F locations.
Price increase of 10%-15% implemented from 1st April to pass on higher raw material, crude, and logistics costs stemming from the Middle East conflict.
Technical plant utilization at 70-75%, formulation plant utilization at 30-40% (seasonal), with peak utilization achievable at ~90% and potential revenue of INR1,900-2,000 crores at peak.
Company targeting 40-50% of revenue from patented products in the next 2-3 years, plus 5-7% higher growth rate than recent years for the upcoming 3 years.
Opened a subsidiary in Brazil and is registering patented products for international expansion, including potential patenting in new geographies.

HYUNDAI.about: Incorporated in May 1996, Hyundai Motor India Limited is a part of the Hyundai Motor Group, which is the third largest auto original equipment manufacturer in the world based on passenger vehicle sales.[1]

quarters.summary: Domestic demand momentum was strong in April-May (+13% YoY) but a supplier fire incident in June disrupted production, cutting Q1 domestic growth to 5.4% YoY; management expects the lost production to be fully recovered within Q2 (mostly already recovered in July) and reiterated FY27 domestic and export volume growth guidance of 8-10% and EBITDA margin guidance of 11-14%. Growth is expected to be led by two new H2 launches (an ICE Mid-SUV in the festive season and the first dedicated mass-market EV), Pune third-shift ramp-up from October 2026, and export recovery from Q2 onwards despite continuing US-Iran/Middle East and Strait of Hormuz-related disruptions.

key_figures.label: Cumulative price hikes taken in calendar year
Localization level (a couple of years ago)

subsections.label: Margin drivers - YoY & sequential common headwinds
points: Production disruption impacted volumes, especially of certain high-margin models.
West Asia conflict impacted export volumes.
Commodity cost pressures were a common headwind on both YoY and sequential basis.
On YoY basis, margins were additionally impacted by cost associated with capacity stabilization.
These pressures were partly offset by favourable exchange rate and calibrated pricing strategy.

subsections.label: Sequential margin drivers
points: Margins impacted sequentially by increase in discount levels and lower government incentives due to seasonality.
Discount increase was in line with typical seasonal trend for the quarter.
Discount levels remained below industry average and below Q1 FY26 levels, reflecting disciplined pricing approach.
Sequential headwinds partially mitigated by continuous cost optimization initiatives and absence of certain one-off expenses incurred in Q4 FY26.

subsections.label: Commodity cost impact detail
points: Commodity impact was roughly 100 bps QoQ, largely from precious metals and copper.
Impact minimized via calibrated pricing strategy, cost reduction efforts, and absence of a one-off commodity cost seen in Q4 FY26.
YoY commodity impact was about 200 bps.

subsections.label: Cost items - employee cost & other expenses
points: Employee cost YoY increase mainly due to Pune plant commencement and yearly salary revisions.
Other expenses increase mainly attributed to higher freight cost, especially for export operations; freight cost increases are generally recovered from distributors and do not impact margins.
Cost optimization efforts include improving localization and value engineering activities to protect margins.

subsections.label: Pricing actions
points: Company takes a calibrated approach to price hikes; 3 price hikes cumulatively ~100 bps taken so far in calendar year.
Future price decisions will factor in commodity trend, market conditions and other factors.

key_figures.label: Rural outlets proportion of new outlets

subsections.label: Venue performance
points: All-new Hyundai Venue continues to witness strong customer traction despite intensifying competition, recording its highest-ever quarterly volumes in the domestic market.

subsections.label: Rural vs urban demand
points: No slowdown seen in rural markets despite Vahan registration data showing slower rural growth vs urban; El Nino-type impact not observed for 3-4 years.
Rural traction attributed to strategy of allocating 6 out of 10 new outlets to rural areas over past 3 years, deployment of mobile service vans, and strong SUV acceptance in rural markets.
Road infrastructure improvement in rural areas and wider internet-driven information dissemination have boosted rural awareness of new products.
SUV contribution in rural areas is now equal to urban areas.
Rural momentum continues unabated; management does not see pressure on rural growth.

subsections.label: Creta / Seltos dynamics
points: Most of the 13,900-unit production loss from June disruption was of Creta.
Management does not attribute urban-rural growth divergence to Creta disruption since SUV contribution is similar across rural and urban.
On Creta facelift/FMC timing, management declined to give specifics, saying it will be announced at the right time.

subsections.label: Market share outlook
points: FY26 exit market share was ~12.3-12.35%; company expects to do much better than that by FY27 exit once both new models are up and running.
In H2, company expects to outpace industry growth aided by two new models, fleet sales, and Venue volumes from Pune third shift.

subsections.label: CNG/green technology roadmap
points: CNG is described as cheapest way to meet CAFE compliance and helps increase volumes; particularly potent in the sub-15-20 lakh segment.
By 2030, company plans minimum 6 CNG models, 4 EVs, and 5-6 hybrids as part of a technology-agnostic strategy.
Company targets more than 50% sales through green fuels by 2030.

CNG contribution hit a highest-ever quarterly level of ~18.2% (18% per MD commentary) in Q1 FY27, with Aura CNG contribution reaching a highest-ever 95% and Exter CNG contribution reaching a highest-ever 32%.

subsections.label: AI strategy across business
points: AI is already part of how HMIL operates: in Sales & Marketing via Hyundai AI Sales Agent, HyGenie chatbot, and dealer AI platforms enhancing customer engagement and sales effectiveness.
In Service, AI supports customer interactions, service automation, VOC analytics, and conversational insights for better customer experience and operational efficiency.
In Manufacturing and Supply Chain, company is working toward AI-enabled quality inspection, predictive maintenance, and production optimization.
In products, company is advancing in-vehicle AI capabilities for more natural, personalized, and proactive customer experiences.
Vision is to evolve AI from a productivity tool into an intelligent co-worker supporting employees, augmenting decision-making, accelerating innovation, and transforming the value chain.

Management declined to quantify specific P&L impact/cost savings from AI (headcount avoidance or conversion uplift) at this stage, but says a 360-degree AI effect will be visible across sales, service, manufacturing, supply chain and products, especially with future product launches.

subsections.label: New EV positioning
points: First mass-market dedicated EV launch for HMIL in India; management declined to comment on exact profitability/cost structure versus competitors.

Company is targeting PLI (Production Linked Incentive) eligibility for this new EV model, requiring 50% domestic value addition; targeting day-1 readiness for PLI compliance, though administrative processes could take time.
Strong localization push on battery packs and other elements including power electronics.
HMC (parent Hyundai Motor Company) global EV strength expected to help; heavy use of AI planned in EV proposition.
myHyundai app gives customers access to 30,000 charging points as part of overall EV value proposition.

subsections.label: New Mid-SUV positioning
points: Positioning for the new ICE Mid-SUV will be very different from Creta - a 'technology-first' positioning targeting Gen Z and digitally native customers, moving toward software-defined vehicles and connected mobility platform.
Management sees a clear market space between the 4-meter and ~4.4-meter SUV segments opening up, evidenced by more competing models entering; company sees a clear opportunity here alongside Creta.

subsections.label: SOP / export sequencing for new launches
points: Standard operating procedure is to launch a model domestically first, then in export markets after about 3 months.
Emerging market customer preferences/economics are similar to India, so both the mid-SUV and EV are expected to have good export traction, though specific export plans/numbers not yet disclosed.

subsections.label: Pune third shift
points: Company progressing with preparations to commence third-shift operations at Pune facility from October 2026, with Phase 1 potential capacity of 170,000 units on a 3-shift basis.
This development effectively advances the capacity ramp-up plan by nearly two years.
Third shift enables meeting growing customer demand and accelerating business growth.
Entire Pune plant (with third shift/line) will be dedicated to the new Venue, catering to both domestic and export demand.
Pune plant currently operates on 2 shifts.

subsections.label: Chennai Plant 1 utilization drivers
points: Capacity utilization at Chennai Plant 1 is currently low (72% in CY2026) because Venue production got shifted (to Pune).
With new models coming in, utilization is expected to rise to 88-90%, and further to 90-92% in CY2027 - described as a major game changer for cost optimization.

subsections.label: Production recovery from June disruption
points: Recovery from the supplier fire incident-related disruption returned operations to normalcy within a short period, reflecting company's agility.
Most of the impacted production volume already recovered in July; remaining recovery expected in August-September, fully within Q2.

Verna PE planned markets by Q3

subsections.label: Export headwinds
points: US-Iran conflict, which started towards the end of last financial year, continued to impact Middle East exports during Q1 FY27.
Export volumes also affected by temporary production disruption in June.
Shipping/freight disruption near Strait of Hormuz continues; company is working with logistics partner to find ways around this.
Mexico exports faced tariff-related challenges but held steady, with some good orders still received.

subsections.label: Export recovery drivers
points: Healthy order backlog maintained across key markets; customer demand remains robust.
New Venue receiving encouraging response in export markets; currently being ordered in 29 of a planned 35 total export markets.

Shipments started for Verna PE and Exter PE, including left-hand-drive Exter, strengthening product offerings/competitiveness in export markets; Exter LHD planned to reach 13 markets and Verna PE 25+ markets by Q3 FY27.
Efforts in Central and South America (CSA) during Jan-Mar and Apr-Jun quarters helped offset Middle East weakness, driving 23% YoY CSA growth with steady demand.
Company expects export shipments to increase from July itself as Middle East orders reopen and post-fire production recovers.
Management expects to exceed the 48,000-unit quarterly export run-rate (Q1 FY26 level) in coming quarters.

subsections.label: Export ASP dynamics
points: ASP improvement partly offset by mix shift toward CSA (hatch-dominated) due to reduced Middle East shipments.
Once Middle East reopens, Verna (sedan) and automatic-transmission mix (common in Middle East) are expected to further raise ASP.
Broader strategy is to enhance SUV mix in exports from current 13-14% (versus 70% domestic SUV mix), with company actively working towards that.

subsections.label: Dealer/channel expansion
points: Rural network expansion: 6 out of 10 new outlets are being allocated to rural areas, ongoing for 3 years.
Mobile service vans deployed to strengthen rural service reach.

subsections.label: Dealer inventory
points: Dealer inventory came down in June due to production disruption; retail numbers were still met.
Company is now rebuilding inventory over July-September ahead of the festive season, taking a balanced/prudent approach rather than overloading dealers.
Retail momentum remains high, supported by lower discount levels versus last year.

subsections.label: Supplier fire incident
points: A fire incident at one of the company's supplier facilities temporarily impacted vehicle production in June, constraining ability to fully meet market demand.
This was the primary driver of lower-than-expected domestic volume growth for Q1.

subsections.label: Localization progress
points: Localization level improved from ~77-78% a couple of years ago to 83% currently, driven by aggressive localization push.
Mid-term target is to reach 90% localization by 2030.
Continuous value engineering activities being conducted with supply chain partners; plant-level employee cost reduction idea programs also in place.

subsections.label: Export logistics
points: Freight/shipping disruptions near the Strait of Hormuz continue to affect Middle East export logistics; company working with logistics partner on mitigation.

subsections.label: Industry growth / base effect risk
points: Industry growth in H1 was elevated due to a low base (pre-GST rate cut in September last year); from October, base effect is expected to make industry growth muted/lower single digits in H2 FY27.

subsections.label: Volume outlook
points: Supported by production normalization, strong demand momentum, upcoming festive season and planned product launches, company expects to bounce back strongly in coming quarters and deliver stated 8-10% domestic growth guidance for FY27.
Company must grow minimum 8-10% in H2 to offset the 5.4% growth in Q1, given the FY27 domestic guidance is reiterated.
Two new models in a high-growth segment and the Pune third shift (more Venue volumes) are cited as specific factors expected to help Hyundai outpace industry growth and regain market share in H2.

On exports, healthy backorders, continued portfolio expansion (new Venue, Exter LHD, Verna PE), and resilient operations expected to drive strong recovery in export volumes from Q2 onwards, in line with the stated 8-10% full-year export growth guidance.

subsections.label: Margin outlook
points: Company remains confident of delivering EBITDA margin within the guided range of 11-14% for FY27.

As volumes recover and plant utilization improves, operating leverage is expected to progressively strengthen, combined with cost optimization initiatives, to drive sustainable margin improvement through the rest of the year.
Management stresses all decisions are guided by the commitment to the 11-14% EBITDA range, balancing volume aspiration with margin discipline.

H2 arrival of 2 new models (typically launched with zero discount in first year) expected to help manage discount levels without resorting to aggressive price hikes, supporting margins within guided range.

subsections.label: Regulatory compliance outlook

subsections.label: Industry growth outlook
points: H2 industry growth expected to reflect the 'real' growth given a higher post-GST base; management expects lower single-digit industry growth in H2 FY27 due to high base and raw material cost headwinds.
Full-year industry growth guess is in the range of 6-9% (with some alternative estimates cited at 8-9%), acknowledging wide variance in different companies' projections (some as low as 5-7%).

subsections.label: Market share outlook
points: Company expects to exit FY27 with market share meaningfully better than the FY26 exit level of ~12.3-12.35%, aided by the two new models being fully ramped up by year-end.

key_takeaways: Fiscal '27 began on a very strong note. The first 2 months of the quarter reflected healthy momentum with cumulative sales in April and May growing by 13% year-on-year, supported by a favourable demand environment and our strategic product actions.

However, the fire incident at one of our supplier facilities temporarily impacted vehicle production in June, constraining our ability to fully meet market demand. As a result, domestic volume growth for the quarter was 5.4% year-on-year, lower than our initial expectations.
We expect to recover the impacted production volume within Q2 with most of it having already been recovered in July month itself.

Supported by production normalization, strong demand momentum, upcoming festive season and our planned product launches, we expect to bounce back strongly in the coming quarters and deliver our stated growth guidance of 8% to 10% for FY27.

The US-Iran conflict, which started towards the end of last financial year, continued to impact our Middle East exports during Q1 FY27... we expect strong recovery in export volumes from Q2 onwards and remain confident in delivering our stated full-year growth guidance of 8% to 10%.
We remain confident of delivering EBITDA margin within our guided range of 11% - 14% for FY27.

We are also progressing with preparations to commence third-shift operations at our Pune facility from October 2026. This development would effectively advance our capacity ramp-up plan by nearly two years.
The new ICE Mid-SUV is planned for launch during the festive season, which will further strengthen our SUV offering and accelerate our volumes meaningfully in high-demand segment.
pressing_questions: Chandramouli Muthiah (Goldman Sachs): asked for confirmation on export volume recovery confidence given ongoing shipping disruption near Middle East, and the key models/drivers behind the ~7% YoY / 5-6% QoQ export ASP improvement.

Jyoti Singh (Haitong Securities): asked whether export volumes can recover to the Q1 FY26 level of 48,000 units within the next two quarters and requested quantification of the actual P&L impact of AI initiatives so far (headcount avoidance or conversion uplift) - management declined to quantify the AI cost-saving impact.
Pramod Kumar (UBS): asked management's exit market share aspiration for FY27 given the market share lost due to production issues.

quarters.summary: Hyundai Motor India closed FY26 with domestic H2 recovery post GST rate rationalization, record Q4 domestic volumes, strong export growth of 16.4% (beating 7-8% guidance), and EBITDA margin of 12.2% within the 11-14% guided range. For FY27, management guided 8-10% domestic and export volume growth, highest-ever capex of ~INR 7,500 crores, two new SUV nameplate launches (one dedicated EV compact SUV, one ICE mid-SUV) from the Chennai plant, continued margin guidance of 11-14% despite near-term commodity headwinds, and further Pune capacity expansion to 320,000 units (overall group capacity >1.1 million units by 2030).

key_figures.label: Current margin level referenced in Q&A

subsections.label: Margin drivers - YoY
points: On YoY comparison, PBT for Q4 FY26 reflects elevated commodity prices, costs associated with capacity addition and unfavourable product mix.
Though volumes were better, the cost pressures outweighed the benefits, leading to a decline in margins on a year-on-year basis.

subsections.label: Margin drivers - Sequential
points: On sequential basis, better volumes, calibrated pricing actions and higher government incentives helped to partially offset the impact of commodities and unfavourable sales mix during the quarter.

subsections.label: Full year margin trend
points: While H1 was very strong, margin softened in H2 due to costs associated with capacity addition and elevated commodity prices.
FY26 EBITDA margin of 12.2% was within the guided range of 11%-14%, reflecting solid execution despite costs associated with capacity addition and commodity price pressures.
Resilient FY26 performance was supported by robust volume growth in exports, calibrated pricing strategy in the domestic market, and proactive cost reduction efforts.

subsections.label: One-off cost items
points: A large part of the sequential employee cost increase relates to the impact of Labor Code provisions and some accounting impact relating to actuarial provisions where assumptions were revisited; management believes this is largely a one-off and should not ideally repeat next quarter.
On commodity cost, the one-off impact relates to vendor compensation for the past period.
Out of the 120 bps sequential commodity margin impact, roughly 50-60 bps is considered a one-off that might not recur in upcoming quarters.

subsections.label: Pricing actions
points: Price increase done in January to the tune of 60 basis points, followed by a selective price increase for Venue in March, and one more price increase planned in May.
Price increase strategy is calibrated based on overall market conditions, balancing volumes and profitability.

subsections.label: Discounts
points: Discounts on ASP reduced substantially from 2.6% in Q3 to 1.9% in Q4.

subsections.label: Capital allocation
points: Board of Directors recommended a dividend of INR 21 per share for FY26, translating to a payout ratio of 31.4% on consolidated profit.

key_figures.label: Domestic volume growth (highest ever quarterly domestic sales)

subsections.label: Export backlog
points: Even in Middle East, the company is having a healthy back order, giving confidence that volumes should come back strongly once macro and geopolitical conditions improve.

subsections.label: Product highlights
points: Verna and Exter enhanced/refreshed during the quarter, reigniting design, technology, safety and comfort to resonate with young Indians.
All-new Venue continues to garner milestones and recognitions, recently crowned 'Compact SUV of the Year' by Autocar; secured 5-star safety rating under Bharat NCAP testing.
Aura recorded its highest ever quarterly sales in Q4 FY26, and highest ever full-year sales as well.
Creta continues its reign as segment leader, led by strategic product enhancements in line with evolving consumer needs.
Refreshed launch of Exter and Verna poised to further accelerate volume momentum in coming quarters.
All-new Venue continues to be a strong growth driver with overwhelming customer response, reinforcing strong position in the compact SUV segment.

subsections.label: Segment mix
points: SUVs continue to be the major contributor to domestic volumes.
Hatches and sedans showed growth during the quarter, aided by GST benefits and product actions.
Clear shift visible away from traditional fuel options towards more eco-friendly powertrains; multi-powertrain strategy positions the company to capture diverse market needs.

subsections.label: Rural/Urban penetration drivers
points: All-time high rural penetration underpinned by strong product offerings and on-ground efforts to strategically enhance network reach.
Urban growth turned positive from Q3 FY26 onward and accelerated in Q4, alongside continued rural growth.

subsections.label: New model plans FY27
points: Two completely new nameplates to be introduced in FY27: one a localized dedicated EV in the compact SUV space (Hyundai's first mass-market dedicated EV, designed for India, launching before CAFE 3 norms kick in, expected to be in a high-volume segment), and the other an ICE SUV expanding presence in the mid-SUV category (more than 4 meters).
Both launches positioned in high-demand segments aimed at broadening portfolio and deepening presence; volume contribution from these two models expected to be substantial in FY27, not small.

Company sticking to Investor Day commitments: in this fiscal, launched one full model change (Venue), one derivative (Venue N Line), and two facelifts (Exter and Verna); over the next 2 years guided for three full model changes and two new models, exactly per plan.
Both new nameplates not only planned for domestic market but will also be considered for export markets in due course.
MPV and off-roader launches were not confirmed for this cycle; management declined to comment on whether they shift to FY29-FY30.

subsections.label: PBT bridge - volume vs mix
points: On a QoQ (Q4 over Q3) basis, better volumes, especially in the domestic market, were a bigger driver than mix impact, even though export mix and SUV mix were relatively lower this quarter.

Two new SUVs launching in FY27 are expected to help the company grow well in the SUV segment; other segments have also started growing, helping Chennai capacity utilization even before the new models kick in.

subsections.label: CAFE compliance
points: Fully met CAFE requirements for FY26; ended CAFE 2 at 114.49 g/km vs. target of 117.585 g/km, a favorable gap of 3.095 g/km (internal calculation).
For CAFE 3, based on the recent draft, requirements have been calculated and the company remains confident of meeting compliance backed by strong powertrain strategy.
CAFE compliance is not just about one EV model; company has a robust and comprehensive plan across the portfolio.
Margin guidance of 11%-14% considers all new models across all segments - EV, petrol, hybrid, diesel, SUV, small car.

key_figures.label: CAFE 2 CO2 level disclosed in earlier quarter

subsections.label: Upcoming EV
points: New EV will mark entry into a new (compact SUV) segment for the company as Hyundai's first mass market dedicated EV, designed and made keeping India in mind.
Management declined to confirm whether the EV is linked to Hyundai Group's cell localization tie-up with a local player, stating disclosures for the day were complete.

subsections.label: Third manufacturing facility
points: FY26 marked commencement of the company's third manufacturing facility (Pune), coinciding with GST rate rationalization and product launch cycle, creating strong leverage for growth in H2.

subsections.label: Capacity expansion plans
points: Previously announced capacity expansion plans of reaching 250,000 units in Pune by calendar year 2028.

Following completion of Phase 2 expansion in CY2028, further capacity expansion of 70,000 units planned at Pune plant to support future growth aspirations, taking total Pune capacity to about 320,000 units and overall capacity to more than 1.1 million units by 2030.

Timeline: Phase 1 of 170,000 units already done; Phase 2 of 80,000 units to come in 2028 (bringing Pune to 250,000); balance addition of 70,000 units to come between 2028 and 2030 (taking Pune to 320,000).
Driving force behind the expansion beyond Phase 2 is the addition of more models - presently only one model (Venue) is produced in Pune, with more to follow.

subsections.label: Chennai plant utilization
points: Both upcoming new models will be manufactured at the Chennai plant, which will bring back utilization to healthy levels after it had dropped when Venue was shifted to Pune.

Historically, 90%-95% capacity utilization at Chennai plant was a key reason for the company's strong profitability in past years; utilization temporarily dropped after Venue moved to Pune, and the two new models from Chennai are expected to restore utilization.
Company continuously evaluating ways to increase production of Venue in Pune.

On a 2-shift basis, Pune plant capacity is capped at around 130,000-140,000 units; on 3-shift basis it can reach ~170,000 units; company will consider adding a third shift at Pune if volumes are sufficient to support it.
Pune plant production of Venue increased from initial 8,000 units/month to current 12,000 units/month, with continuous efforts to increase further, including through exports.

subsections.label: Capex breakdown FY27
points: Of the INR 7,500 crore FY27 capex (highest ever in recent years), a major part (~45%-50%) will go towards upcoming new products, and around 30% will go into plant-related investments, including Phase 2 expansion in Pune and upgradation of the Chennai plant.

subsections.label: Cost elements from Pune ramp-up
points: Elements such as overhead cost and depreciation from the new Pune plant have impacted margins as ramp-up of operations continues; the major depreciation-related impact was already reflected in Q3, with further increases expected as ramp-up continues, but increased volumes should help absorb these fixed costs and improve margins.

subsections.label: ESG / clean energy
points: Achieved RE100 across facilities during the fiscal year, reinforcing commitment to clean energy adoption.

Leveraging AI across operations with a clear AI roadmap aimed at unlocking opportunities across manufacturing efficiency, quality enhancement, supply chain optimization and enhanced customer experience.

subsections.label: Network expansion
points: Almost 90 sales outlets added this year, with approximately 7 out of 10 new outlets coming in rural areas.
Rural penetration continues to increase; company expects to continue focus at roughly a 7:3 rural-to-urban outlet ratio for at least the next couple of years.
Opportunities in rural areas seen as very strong going forward, especially post-GST, supported by network and marketing activities including 30-year celebration.

subsections.label: Export markets
points: Export growth in FY26 driven by robust demand across emerging markets and continued focus on expanding into new geographies.

Middle East export volumes impacted by geopolitical conflict (war), particularly in March; countermeasures include aggressively focusing on other markets such as Latin America and Mexico, where shipments were increased in the last quarter.
Company also evaluating alternate shipping routes to mitigate Middle East disruption.
In Q4 FY26, company commenced exports of new Venue and will continue to expand into newer geographies; HMIL will serve as a global manufacturer for the new Venue for HMC (Hyundai Motor Company).
Verna PE and Exter PE to be launched in export markets as well; Exter LHD version introduction planned to strengthen volumes in LHD markets.
Two new domestic nameplates will also be considered for export markets in due course.

Company positions itself as agile to grab further opportunities beyond 8%-10% growth given available capacity and new models.

themes.note: Two new SUV nameplates (a dedicated compact EV and an ICE mid-SUV) planned for FY27, expected to deliver substantial volume accretion and support CAFE compliance.

themes.label: Regulatory compliance (CAFE)
themes.note: Company outperformed its CAFE 2 target for FY26 and expressed confidence in meeting CAFE 3 requirements based on the draft norms and powertrain strategy.

key_takeaways: Q4 FY26 domestic volumes grew 8.5% YoY, marking the highest ever quarterly domestic sales since inception.
Export volumes grew 9.4% YoY in Q4 and 16.4% for the full year, significantly outperforming initial guidance of 7% to 8%.
FY26 EBITDA margin stood at 12.2%, within the guided range of 11% to 14%.
April FY27 domestic volumes registered growth of 17% year-on-year.
Company guided domestic and export volume growth of 8-10% each for FY27, backed by two new SUV nameplate launches (one dedicated EV compact SUV, one ICE mid-SUV).
FY27 capex guided at approximately INR 7,500 crores, the highest ever capex in recent years.
Further Pune capacity expansion of 70,000 units announced post Phase 2 (CY2028), taking Pune capacity to 320,000 units and overall capacity to more than 1.1 million units by 2030.
Board recommended a dividend of INR 21 per share for FY26, a payout ratio of 31.4% on consolidated profit.
pressing_questions: On the margin side, articulate the margin levers given the guidance range of 11% to 14% versus current ~10.5% margins amid further commodity pressure, and quantify commodity pressure faced in the current quarter versus next quarter and the pricing action taken.
On exports, given high Middle East exposure but a guided 10% growth, what is the underlying basis/color; and on domestic 8%-10% growth, will the company gain market share given new launches?
Any guidance on timing of the two new model launches during FY27, and whether volumes from these models are built into the 8%-10% guidance?
Can the capex of INR 7,500 crores be broken down by area?
Can the one-offs mentioned (Labor Code impact, commodity one-off) be quantified, and what is the sustainable employee cost run-rate?
Is the new EV linked to the Hyundai Group's cell localization tie-up with a local player?
Given Pune still has capacity ramp-up headroom, why are both new models going to Chennai instead of Pune, and how does this affect fixed cost absorption and utilization?
On the PBT bridge, was volume a bigger driver than mix given adverse export and SUV mix this quarter?
On the export growth guidance, given increased capacity is no longer a constraint, what is the underlying basis for 8%-10% growth amid adverse geopolitics?
What is the timeline for the additional 70,000-unit Pune capacity expansion beyond Phase 2, and what is the driving factor behind it given already high existing capacity?

PWL.about: Physicswallah is an edtech company offering test preparation courses for various competitive examinations like JEE, NEET, UPSC, etc., and upskilling courses like Data science and analytics, banking and finance, software development, etc[1]

quarters.summary: Q1 FY27 revenue from operations grew 24% YoY to INR1,054 crores, with online growth of 33% and offline/other growth of 16%, largely in line with management expectations. NEET exam calendar shift (5-7 weeks) dented Q1 collections/enrollments but post-result (July 16) collections grew ~50% YoY; management reiterated full-year guidance of 30% revenue growth and 100% EBITDA improvement, with offline business targeted to reach near profitability/break-even by year-end.

subsections.label: Segment-level reporting
points: As part of improving quality of reporting, company initiated segment-level reporting after discussion with auditors; reported revenues and EBITDA separately for online and offline business for the first time.
Provided reconciliation of online EBITDA and offline EBITDA along with overall EBITDA.

Given the academic/cyclical nature of the business, management believes a full-year view of segments will provide meaningful direction; this was also a key reason for reporting financials on the last permissible day.
Q1 FY26 numbers have been restated due to changes in allocation discussed with auditors, largely towards accounting of B2B revenues and some 'others' category revenue reclassified.

subsections.label: Cost leverage drivers
points: Improvement in pre-Ind AS EBITDA margin (624 bps YoY) driven by leverage across cost items.
Employee cost (excluding ESOP) lower by 2.6% YoY.
ESOP cost remained flat YoY in Q1, giving leverage of 117 bps.
Continued leverage on distribution and marketing expenses; marketing spend leverage improved 172 bps YoY.
AI-led automation contributing to leverage in people costs.

subsections.label: One-time charge
points: Company took a one-time non-cash charge related to additional stake purchase in Saarthi IAS, largely due to better-than-expected financial performance of Saarthi.

subsections.label: Cash/treasury and capital allocation
points: Treasury of INR5,600 crores as of June 30, 2026 (referenced again as of 31st July), including IPO proceeds of INR2,000 crores.
Capital allocation will largely be towards new online content and categories, both organic and inorganic.
Offline expansion approach will be opportunistic and limited to geographies fitting cohort economics; new centers planning to be decided over next 2 quarters.
Company is keenly looking at AI-first opportunities complementing offerings, including personalized AI tutor investment.
Cash position increase of ~INR600 crores QoQ attributed to negative working capital cycle business model where students pay fees upfront; this cyclicity recurs every year from Q4 to Q1.
Online business nature involves one-shot upfront annual fee payment by students (e.g., ARPU of ~INR4,000).

subsections.label: Online categories & buckets
points: Online business bucketed into 3 groups: (1) very high profitable categories - JEE, NEET, CA, MBA, Commerce, Boards; (2) path to higher profitability - GATE, UPSC, State PSCs, Foundation, government exams, some state boards; (3) slightly loss-making/growth categories - NEET PG, Skills, Curious Junior, vernacular (ventured recently).
Curious Junior online business expected to become break-even this year despite being in the loss-making bucket.
Path-to-higher-profitability categories (UPSC, GATE, Foundation, state boards) are approaching higher profitability; mature categories (JEE, NEET) also improving margins.
As NEET PG, vernacular, and Curious Junior break even and contribute to EBITDA, overall online margin expected to expand further from FY26's 27%.

Foundation category has lower ARPU than NEET and lower average teacher salary cost, but addresses a much deeper/larger market than JEE/NEET; steady-state profitability for Foundation anticipated to be higher than NEET but will take longer to reach; current margin delta between NEET and Foundation is not large.

subsections.label: NEET exam calendar shift impact
points: NEET UG examination pattern/calendar shifted by 5-7 weeks this year, impacting collections and enrollments across core PW business and subsidiary Xylem in Q1.
Post NEET results announcement on July 16, collections have grown ~50% YoY, viewed as encouraging.
This is viewed as a quarterly shift (enrollments moving from Q1 to Q2), similar to a precedent shift seen in 2024 where no change in overall annual enrollment resulted.
Government exam notification decline also impacted enrollments; subsidiary Utkarsh saw a significant ~800k enrollment delta due to this cyclicality, expected to see spikes in upcoming years.

Offline enrollment did not improve much despite ~63 new centers added, primarily attributed to NEET exam delay as offline business is majority JEE-NEET; students took ~1.5 months longer to decide to join offline centers post re-examination and re-result.
NEET PG enrollment grew ~50% YoY and collections grew ~100% YoY; CA, CS, ACCA enrollment grew 30% YoY.
Vernacular category enrollment/revenue jumped 1.7x YoY, with enrollment growth cited as 70% YoY; state board enrollment and revenue doubled (100%) YoY.

Online growth adjusted for NEET impact (like-to-like) estimated at 19%-20%; offline growth adjusted similarly estimated at 20%-25%; offline revenue growth had NEET cycle been on time estimated at 22%-25%.
Additional NEET-related online enrollments estimated lost: 1 to 1.5 lakh students.
Curious Junior enrollment improved 67% YoY and collections improved 150% YoY.

Online early learning and K-12 revenue grew 88% YoY, with K-12 online enrollment growth of 40%-41% YoY (enrollment rising from 0.55 million to 0.78 million students, revenue from INR56 crores to INR105 crores); state boards TAM estimated at 6 crores.

subsections.label: Online early learning and K-12
points: Category includes Foundation, Pre-foundation, Curious Junior, Commerce, SIP, Boards including state boards.
More students attending schools are opting for online tuition, seen as a huge market opportunity.
Category includes Grade 6-8, Grade 3-5 explorations underway, all growing tremendously.
State board initiative expanded from 7 to 14 state boards; regional teams, regional teachers, regional YT distribution being formed to cater to demand.
K-12/state board seen as a great LTV business — capturing students early creates lifelong learning partnership.

subsections.label: Vidyapeeth (offline) performance
points: Vidyapeeth (70% of offline business) demonstrated 7% ARPU improvement despite intensified competition, while competitors' ARPU is flat or shrinking.
Company has taken conscious call that offline business is not an affordable business; intends to become #1 in ARPU, results, and other metrics in offline.
Vidyapeeth delivering better profitability than the overall offline average, in terms of both ARPU growth and bottom-line growth.

Seat utilization metric (total students/total seats) historically improved from 1.77 to 1.99, with 5-7% average annual improvement; improvement pace may slow given less aggressive expansion going forward.
Non-academic to academic staff ratio being optimized; Vidyapeeth becoming more academic in nature via central-level cost optimization, automation, and hiring/training fresher faculty.
Student-teacher ratio (previously in 80s) expected to increase (become higher) this year, driving bottom-line growth.
Kota center specifically has seen decline in student inflow, but remaining centers delivering 13-15% margin profile.
Margin lever for early centers being explored: hybrid course model where students come to center only twice a week, potentially improving student-teacher ratio and capacity utilization.
ARPU seen as a good future growth lever for Vidyapeeth once majority city-level results are achieved.
Online revenue grew 33% YoY with online bottom line improving ~600 bps YoY; offline revenue grew 14% YoY with offline bottom line improving 400 bps YoY.

subsections.label: Pathshala to Vidyapeeth conversion
points: Pathshala center count declined from 84 (end of March) to 70 currently; management clarified zero Pathshalas were closed — mature/scaled Pathshalas are converted into larger Vidyapeeth centers as they grow.

subsections.label: Offline drag categories
points: Drag on offline profitability coming from newer categories entered in the past two years: UPSC, government exams, CA.

subsections.label: School Integrated Program
points: Pan-India program partnering with existing schools, sending Vidyapeeth faculty to teach students within schools.
Partnership grew from 15 schools to more than 50 schools last year.
Completely asset-light model; company takes some guarantee from schools regarding number of student admissions.

subsections.label: K-12 market and competition
points: No significant competition in K-12 market currently; company positions itself as category creator and small market leader.
Overall K-12 market size is 250 million students across all categories; addressable market is online tuitions (covered via Curious Junior) and state boards (covered via state board initiatives).

subsections.label: Results/outcomes performance
points: Online results have never been a challenge — company delivers maximum number of selections across NEET, JEE, UPSC, CA, etc. due to teaching maximum number of students.
Offline results are compared against competitors; company is investing in offline results vertical, which is one reason for slowing offline expansion and focusing on unit economics and results.
Delivered maximum number of NEET and JEE selections compared to any coaching in India this year (claimed, verified, and published results).
Company has couple of ranks in Top 100 this year; share of Top 100 increasing 5-10% YoY.
Produced All India Rank 1 in International Junior Science Olympiad this year, beating competitors.
Vision is to become the top result-producing centers in offline; offline is not about affordability but about top results.

subsections.label: New product launches
points: Launched PW Books app — a digital book learning experience with AI-native reading; showing strong initial traction (covered in shareholder letter); rated 4.7 on Play Store with 2.2 million downloads.
Created new skilling category called 'Earners' offering short-term skilling courses in digital marketing, graphic design, AI-led courses; shaping up well.
Pi (OTT learning platform, ~40,000 enrollments) and PW Talk (~130,000 enrollments) continue to grow rapidly.
Books app actual launch happened one and a half years back after development; digital books specifically launched by Alakh on internet almost two-three months back.

New initiatives typically require a pilot of one to one-and-a-half years to assess learning outcomes, engagement, and retention before being reported; company generally reports an initiative in shareholder letter once used by 100,000 paid students.

subsections.label: AI initiatives
points: AI remains a core focus area for the company.
Launched 'Ask AI' — an AI-led doubt-solving engine within batches; majority of doubts are now solved by Ask AI, viewed as a great achievement by the product team.
Creating an AI companion for kids and a one-to-one Socratic AI tutor at a very affordable price; product already in beta phase, to be rolled out to students by next quarter.
AI-led efficiency contributing to leverage in people costs via automation.
Since success seen in AI-powered digital books, similar AI initiatives (AI tutor, AI companion) planned for launch this financial year.
Company keenly looking at AI-first opportunities complementing offerings, including personalized AI tutor investment (capital allocation angle).

subsections.label: Annual guidance reiterated
points: Annual guidance of 30% revenue improvement and 100% EBITDA improvement for FY27 remains the same, reiterated despite Q1 NEET-related impact.

Management believes it is largely in line to deliver the annual operating plan (AOP) for FY27, based on Q1 revenue of INR1,054 crores versus INR847 crores in Q1 FY26 and full FY26 revenue of ~INR3,900 crores.

Enrollment vector and ACPU (average collection per user) vector should not be treated as rigid metrics individually — there will be a tradeoff between the two, but overall topline commitment (AOP) remains intact.
For YTD enrollment guidance, company is not specifically guiding a number, but revenue and EBITDA guidance remain intact.

Recommended to look at H1 consolidated numbers as a better proxy given NEET admission cycle shift and new notifications; revenue is the right proxy per management, best assessed on a year-to-date basis across PW and all subsidiaries.

subsections.label: Offline profitability outlook
points: Guidance for offline business is near breakeven/near profitability this year; management confident of achieving this.
Improvement driven by better teacher quality, delivery/experience improvements, slower center expansion, and more focused approach — no abrupt increase in average teacher cost in offline.
No plans to introduce 'star teachers' into offline business; teachers are produced internally through faculty training program, with batch size limited to 80 students.
Offline steady-state profitability target of 13-15% will largely come from ARPU improvement and improving outcomes; these are the two clear metrics being tracked in offline this year.

key_takeaways: We are making good progress across all our education categories. Our focus now is to continue build online early learning and K-12 business, which has grown by almost 88% year-over-year.

SIMPLEXCAS.about: Incorporated in 1971, Simplex Castings Ltd is a manufacturer of castings and engineering solutions.[1]

quarters.summary: Simplex Castings delivered a strong Q1 FY27 with 35% YoY revenue growth, 25% YoY EBITDA growth and 45% YoY PAT growth, backed by an order book that has expanded to Rs 150 crore+ from a historical range of Rs 80-100 crore. Management reiterated the FY27 revenue target of Rs 300 crore and the FY28 target of Rs 500 crore (the latter requiring capacity expansion beyond the existing two units, via organic or inorganic growth), while guiding for capacity utilization to reach ~80% by end of FY28 and working capital days to reduce from ~100-120 days to 60-70 days by FY28-end, driven by a shift toward faster-moving railway/power products and use of RXIL/Invoice Mart bill discounting platforms.

Q1 FY27 revenue growth YoY (as mentioned by Mr. Avinash)

subsections.label: Working capital strategy
points: Strategic shift in product mix at Unit 1 towards faster-moving products with shorter execution and realization cycles, to be progressively implemented at Unit 3 as well.

Changing product mix in an engineering/manufacturing business is a gradual process involving changes across order selection, production planning, capacity allocation and customer mix; improvement will be progressive, not immediate.
FY27 viewed as an important transition year; by FY28 company expects a much more controlled and disciplined working capital structure targeting 60-70 days.
Objective is not only to grow revenue and profitability but to make growth significantly more cash-efficient, converting a greater share of operating cash generation into free cash flow.
Railway bogies have a fast 30-45 day cycle: manufacture by 15th of month, payment received by 30th; once sold to wagon builders, builders must pay upfront before goods leave the factory.
Company registered with RXIL and Invoice Mart platforms, receiving payments roughly 30-35 days after dispatch via bill discounting at 5-5.5% annualised interest.

Next year targeting more than Rs 100 crore from railway business and another ~Rs 100 crore from power sector (BHEL orders via RXIL) — neither done last year — expected to be the major driver in reducing the working capital cycle.
No simple calculation for the exact split of improvement between new fast-cycle businesses vs faster invoicing/discounting, but overall trajectory is downward.

subsections.label: Fundraise / Capital structure
points: Current fundraise is expected to be sufficient to reach the Rs 500 crore FY28 revenue projection; no further fundraise is currently anticipated for that target.

Capital work in progress (~Rs 30 crore) has been deployed towards both working capital needs and capital expansion, currently at the Tedesra/Rajnandgaon unit, expected to complete this financial year.
Any further facility/expansion beyond existing plans is intended to be financed through own accruals rather than fresh capex or additional borrowings.

key_figures.label: Steel sector share of order book (as referenced)

subsections.label: Order book quality and management philosophy
points: Management deliberately keeps order book in the Rs 100-150 crore range rather than maximizing it, citing liquidated damages risk on delayed orders (limited to 5%, some go up to 10%), preferring sufficient execution time.
Confident of maintaining order book at the 100-150 crore level given execution capability.
Some orders in pipeline expected to convert this specific quarter.

subsections.label: Shipbuilding order pipeline (Mazgaon Dock)
points: First 3 sets of castings for Mazgaon Dock's big shipbuilding project already cast; first set offered for inspection.
Current order is for 5 sets (~Rs 4.5 crore), followed by one more order in pipeline (~Rs 8 crore).

Company expects much bigger orders going forward given government thrust on shipbuilding sector; has served Mazgaon Dock, Goa Shipyard, Hindustan Shipyard, Cochin Shipyard and private players for many years.
Company holds both American Bureau of Shipping and Indian Bureau of Shipping certifications, giving it better positioning versus competitors for large, intricate castings.

subsections.label: Wagon/bogie order timing
points: Expecting wagon orders to come to wagon makers in August-September; quoted tenders for normal wear-and-tear railway requirements expected around September.
Full/consistent 200-bogie monthly capacity utilization will only start once railway placement of wagon orders materializes.

subsections.label: Railways / Bogies
points: Company was earlier making bogies in Simplex Casting till 2019, with 20% direct from Indian Railways (via wagon repair shops) and 80% from wagon builders.
Consistent 200-bogie monthly capacity only ramps once railway places wagon orders with wagon makers; capability is slightly higher than 200 but company is understating it conservatively.

Railways was historically 40-50% of business till 2019; strategy is to bring it back to ~40% to hedge against steel sector cyclicality (steel sector expected to boom for next 4-5 years before a cycle turn).

subsections.label: Power sector fabrication
points: Company suddenly seeing a flush of offers from power sector players like BHEL, L&T; expects ~Rs 100 crore of business from this.
Capex on fabrication side is partly for fabricated locomotive bogies, expected to generate turnover of Rs 60-70 crore.
Margins in power sector and railway (both largely tender/fabrication business) will be similar to current levels — not higher — as these are tender-driven businesses.

subsections.label: Defence & Shipbuilding
points: Defence + shipbuilding combined targeted at 10-15% of business in FY27, continuing at similar levels next financial year; management does not expect aggressive 20-30-50% growth in defence given collaboration model with ordnance factories.

Strategy is to collaborate closely with ordnance factories (starting with Gun Carriage Factory Jabalpur/Khamaria) to support capacity expansion beyond their existing special-purpose machine capacity (targeting X to 1.5-2X demand), leveraging Simplex's flexible machine shop.
Plan to work with one ordnance factory first, then expand to others; components being made for Dhanush artillery gun.

Historical defence pedigree: only private-sector company making turrets for T-72 tanks; Simplex Group made Shaktiman truck chassis (1955 to production end); missile testing range/test bench work at Itarsi, Balasore, Chandipur; developed road wheel for Sarath (Sarthak) armoured personnel carrier for HVF Medak ~3 years ago.

In shipbuilding, currently makes A brackets, B brackets, turbo castings, rudder stock; next step is sub-components, sub-assemblies or complete systems (e.g., steering systems); in discussion with companies for technology for other shipbuilding items.
Not pursuing crankshaft/diesel generator castings for data centers due to highly specialised, intricate machining requirements, but pursuing smaller data-center castings.

subsections.label: Steel / Metallurgical sector
points: Traditional market is steel and railways; company will be choosy and take better orders in steel to replace/feed the current year's Rs 300 crore revenue target, given visibility in order book and pipeline.

Correcting terminology: business is better described as ferrous/non-ferrous metallurgical sector rather than just steel — traditional large customers include Balco, Vedanta, Hindustan Zinc, Nalco, Aditya Birla group, as equipment needs are similar across metallurgical industries.
20% of order book currently from non-ferrous sector (vs 20% steel referenced).

subsections.label: EPC (potential future segment)
points: EPC division historically operated only in metallurgical/power sector (sinter plants, blast furnaces, rolling wheels); not interested in railway bridges, highways or other loads outside company's own manufacturing units' interest.
Last EPC order was in 2016 (Rourkela Steel Plant); division was disbanded in 2020 due to bad steel industry conditions, to avoid overheads, but credentials remain with Simplex Castings.
Any future EPC project will be executed within Simplex Castings itself, not a separate entity; EPC target NOT included in the Rs 500 crore FY28 target as guided.

Company is choosy — will only quote for EPC packages giving at least 30-40% load to own factories and with minimum 15-20% margin; peak historical EPC revenue was ~Rs 100 crore/year over 3-4 year projects.
Currently order sizes considered are Rs 100-150 crore, executable in ~2 years, constrained by banker bank-guarantee limits rather than capital; company does not want to dilute equity for this.

Payment structure: 5% PBG upfront (no payment), 10% advance against bank guarantee, billing-based payments per design/drawing submission, ~10% retained for preliminary commissioning and final acceptance.

Example: Bhilai Steel Plant's new universal rail & structural mill (~Rs 600 crore) — main package goes to SMS/Danieli for equipment (not EPC), but smaller enabling-work packages (reheating furnace, rolling mill parts, stack etc.) designed by consultants are where Simplex would compete directly as EPC contractor, not as subcontractor to SMS/Danieli.

subsections.label: Technology collaborations
points: All past technology collaborations were technical transfers (not royalty-based); these have been completed, and no royalty is payable currently for any past technical collaboration.

subsections.label: Precision engineering capability
points: Company currently limits itself to grey iron and steel; does not work with exotic metals like nickel alloys (corrosion/thermal resistant) at present, though open to moving up the value chain.

Has precision casting and precision machining (CNC) capability, but not full range — lacks 5-axis/7-axis/9-axis/12-axis machines needed for tool & die or turbine blade machining, as these were not required for current product range.

Sees enough expansion opportunity within existing heavy casting/heavy machining value chain (where MNC tolerance/cost requirements are already very precise) without necessarily moving into exotic materials, though open to eventually doing so.

subsections.label: Capacity expansion plans
points: Capex currently underway at Tedesra/Rajnandgaon unit, targeted for completion this financial year, focused on fabrication for power sector business and fabricated locomotive bogies.

Foundry capacity addition is planned as debottlenecking (not major new capex) — adding one CNC machine plus conveyors/cranes — company deliberately avoiding heavy capex at one time, preferring to stabilize and earn first, having just come out of first year of a two-year improvement phase.
A full new machine molding plant for foundry is only at drawing-board stage, contingent on internal approvals after achieving stability.

Existing two units (Unit 1 and Unit 3) are seen as the right fit for Rs 300-350 crore of revenue; capacity for growth beyond that (towards Rs 500 crore) needs to come from a different area — via organic or inorganic (M&A) growth — not from expanding these two units alone.
Company has a land bank reserved for normal expansion of the two existing units; any new/extra capacity opportunity would be a separate, distinct investment.

subsections.label: Regional positioning
points: Bhilai location is strategically important — anything happening in the ferrous or non-ferrous equipment space in that region has to come out of Bhilai, where there are only a few large players besides Simplex, giving the company a natural advantage.
ArcelorMittal is expanding capacity in three locations — two in Odisha and one in Andhra Pradesh (Vizag) — creating capital goods opportunity for Simplex given its steel-sector credentials.
Second-round players like Shyam Metalics and Rungta are also expanding, adding to regional demand for capital goods equipment.

Company offices located in Delhi, Bombay, Calcutta and elsewhere, but manufacturing units (for both Simplex Castings and the separate Simplex Engineering and Foundry Works) are located only in and around Bhilai.

subsections.label: Payment platform usage
points: Registered with RXIL and Invoice Mart platforms to receive early payments through bill discounting at 5-5.5% annualised interest rate, roughly 30-35 days after dispatch — used to improve overall working capital cycle.

subsections.label: Competitive positioning
points: Company holds American Bureau of Shipping and Indian Bureau of Shipping certifications — one of the few players with both — giving better chances than competitors for large, intricate shipbuilding castings.

60-year-old company with full range of credentials in the steel/metallurgical sector, having done complete plants for equipment historically (sinter plants, pellet plants, blast furnaces), positioning it as an obvious partner for anyone entering the Indian market.
Management-controlled infrastructure (1,200 workers, 100+ machine tools, 30 acres of land, skill sets) is described as difficult/expensive to replicate, providing a durable competitive moat.

In defence, ordnance factories are seeking manufacturers with flexible machine shops able to perform specialised machining for expanded production beyond existing special-purpose machine capacity — a niche Simplex aims to fill.

subsections.label: Simplex 2.0 strategy
points: Company entered the year with significantly greater confidence in direction and scale versus a year ago; over six decades built deep engineering/manufacturing capabilities across heavy castings, fabrication, machining and EPC, with strong position across steel, power, railway, mining and other critical industries.

'Simplex 2.0' strategy: participate in larger projects, manufacture more complex/higher-value products, diversify revenue base, and extract greater productivity from the existing manufacturing platform.
Railways to become an important new growth vertical; also expanding into defence, oil & gas, shipbuilding sectors.
Focus is now on converting broader opportunity landscape (thermal/power, railways, defence, oil & gas, shipbuilding) into orders, and orders into profitable revenue.

Long-term ambition beyond Rs 500 crore includes machine tool castings, defence at scale, and other verticals — potentially via buying a technology company or joint-venturing with one; company has already executed complete steel plants (sinter plants, pellet plants, blast furnaces) via its EPC division historically.

Management's near-term focus (this year and next) is disciplined execution and delivery of existing commitments; larger/bigger opportunities are being tracked but kept on the 'back burner' / drawing board until the company is stronger.

subsections.label: Capacity expansion beyond 500 crore
points: Growth beyond Rs 300-350 crore (towards Rs 500 crore) requires capacity from a different area than the existing two units — via organic or inorganic growth — plans already identified and being worked on, though not disclosed in detail.

New facility/expansion investment intended to be financed via own accruals; no further capex or major fresh borrowings planned beyond the current fundraise; not looking to dilute equity further for the EPC push either.
Three fronts being worked on for growth: (1) railway business, (2) increasing power business, (3) a portion of EPC business.

subsections.label: Green hydrogen DRI project — closed
points: Company was awarded a green hydrogen-powered DRI plant pilot project (joint initiative of Ministry of New & Renewable Energy and Ministry of Steel) in consortium with IIT Bhilai, with Simplex as consortium leader; total project size ~Rs 300 crore, of which ~Rs 160-161 crore was government grant.

Project could not proceed because the tender required IP and asset ownership to be transferred to government in the same proportion as the grant, which GST Council ruled constituted a taxable supply (not a free grant), triggering ~Rs 30-35 crore of additional GST liability that neither government nor company had planned for.
After multiple discussions between the Steel Ministry, company and consultants, both sides concluded the tender needed to be scrapped and reissued; Simplex withdrew and the tender was reissued.
Reissued tender changed basic conditions (requiring bidder to already be operating a DRI plant, which Simplex was not), so company did not participate in the second round.
Confirmed: there is no commercial opportunity going forward from this project; it is closed.

subsections.label: Corporate history / group structure clarification
points: Simplex Engineering and Foundry Works (without foundry) is a separate, privately-held entity owned by promoter's cousins, unrelated corporate structure — not the same as Simplex Infrastructure (owned by Munduras, Calcutta-based), which has never been part of the Simplex group.

Original company founded 1941 in Jabalpur as Simplex Engineering and Foundry Works by the promoter's great-grandfather; moved to Bhilai ~1958-1960 with Bhilai Steel Plant's development; in 1970 foundry business was carved out into what became Simplex Castings; in 2003 Simplex Engineering and Simplex Castings were formally split into two separate entities, with Simplex Castings going public in 1992.
Any future EPC project will be executed within Simplex Castings itself using its own credentials, not through any separate/other entity.
