subsections.label: Order execution and liquidated damages risk
points: Every order carries liquidated damages exposure if delayed beyond a particular time — most limited to 5%, some up to 10% — a key reason management deliberately caps the order book at Rs 100-150 crore rather than maximizing intake, to ensure sufficient execution time.

subsections.label: Bogie/wagon order timing dependency
points: Full ramp-up to consistent 200-bogie monthly production depends on railway placing wagon orders with wagon makers, which had been expected around August-September but is contingent on external timing.

subsections.label: Green hydrogen project GST/tender risk
points: Green hydrogen DRI pilot project was closed due to an unplanned ~Rs 30-35 crore GST liability arising from tender conditions requiring IP/asset transfer to government in proportion to grant received; reissued tender's changed eligibility conditions (requiring existing DRI plant operation) further excluded the company from participating again.

subsections.label: Banking limits constraint on EPC
points: EPC order sizes are currently constrained to Rs 100-150 crore due to limitations from bankers and bank guarantee limits, rather than by capital availability; management is not seeking further fundraise but may need enhanced bank guarantee limits.

subsections.label: Steel sector cyclicality
points: Management notes the steel sector is expected to remain strong for the next 4-5 years but flags that cyclicality is a known historical pattern, which is why the company deliberately hedges with railways alongside steel to maintain consistent growth and turnover.

subsections.label: Revenue guidance
points: Rs 300 crore FY27 target reaffirmed: Rs 60 crore already achieved in Q1, remaining ~Rs 150 crore order book to be executed this financial year, plus some pipeline orders expected to be completed by March — management confirmed 'we are in line.'

Rs 500 crore FY28 target reaffirmed as achievable, though it will require capacity beyond the existing two units (Unit 1 and Unit 3), sourced via organic or inorganic growth, for which specific plans are already being worked on.
EPC business revenue target (if it materializes, ~Rs 100 crore/year) is explicitly NOT included in the Rs 500 crore FY28 target.

subsections.label: Margin outlook
points: Railway and power/fabrication business margins expected to remain similar to current levels (not higher) since these are tender-driven businesses.
Management intends to be more selective/choosy on other (non-tender) business, focusing on niche, complex, preferred-supplier products to increase PAT margin from that portion of the business.
Overall PAT margin is expected to improve (not decline) as complex/niche products are prioritized, even as new railway/power business is added.

subsections.label: Working capital / cash flow outlook
points: FY27 positioned as a transition year for working capital improvement; FY28 targeted for a much more controlled and disciplined working capital structure at 60-70 days.
Fundraise currently underway expected to be sufficient to fund the path to Rs 500 crore; no further fundraise anticipated for that target.

subsections.label: Capacity utilization outlook
points: Utilization to gradually increase from current 50-60%, targeting at least 80% by end of next financial year (FY28).

500 crores... we have got very specific plans for the 500 crores; capacity expansion has to be in a different area, either organic or inorganic growth.
By FY28, we expect an operating cycle with much more controlled and disciplined working capital structure, targeting days of 60 to 70 days.

Expecting almost a turnover of 60-70 crores from fabricated locomotive bogies.
The number is somewhere around 200 bogies we can roughly manufacture per month... we are understating it conservative, capability is slightly more, but we are aiming at 200 numbers.

quarters.summary: Simplex Castings delivered a landmark FY26 with double-digit growth across revenue, EBITDA and PAT, and is targeting continued growth via railway wagon bogies (RDSO approval received), fabricated bogies, coke oven doors, power sector orders and possible acquisitions, with revenue targeted at Rs 300 crore in FY27 and Rs 500 crore by FY28, subject to execution risk, acquisition/EPC success and railway order flow.

subsections.label: FY26 Performance
points: Company delivered a landmark performance in FY26 with robust double-digit growth across all key parameters while significantly strengthening the balance sheet.
Consolidated revenue grew around 18% to Rs 202 crores.
EBITDA increased by 20% to Rs 37.39 crores with margin expansion.
PAT rose strongly by 40.5% to Rs 21.26 crores.

subsections.label: Q4 YoY De-growth
points: Current year Q4 revenue de-grew versus the previous Q4 figure of approximately Rs 67 crores.
Reason cited: contractual manufacturing business is dependent on site activities undertaken by customers, which affected dispatches.
There was a slight increase in inventories of finished goods that could not be liquidated due to site conditions of the customer; these were realized in April/May (Q1 of next fiscal).
Part of the impact was due to unavailability of gases (LPG) which affected all fabrication plants' supplies, hitting the top line.

subsections.label: Margin Discussion
points: Margins improving due to favorable market conditions across power and steel sectors where projects are time-bound and orders are flowing in, allowing the company to be more selective.
Company's stated margin goal is to remain in the range of 8-10% at minimum, despite delivering ~11% PAT margin in the quarter.
Being in contractual manufacturing, several factors need to be managed to sustain or improve margins going forward.

subsections.label: Capital Allocation / Fundraising
points: Second preferential issue was targeted at Rs 50 crores, split between Rs 25 crores capital and Rs 25 crores working capital for fabricated bogies.
Management is evaluating debt or equity options to fund the fabricated bogies growth plan.
CAPEX for FY26 was around Rs 15 crores; FY27 CAPEX target maintained at Rs 25 crores.

Capacity for cast bogies (200-250 sets/month) has already been built via the first preferential issue; equipment is fully in place and trials have been completed, but assets remain in Capital Work in Progress (CWIP) until commercial production begins, after which they will be converted into fixed assets.

Railway, steel and power sectors all showing strong order flow expected to continue in the coming year.

Change in West Bengal government scenario being watched as a factor potentially affecting order flow.
Company expects to be consistently making 200 bogies (its built capacity) from September onward.

subsections.label: Wagon Bogies
points: Restarting wagon bogie business after RDSO approval; business previously done for 20-30 years until 2019 (plant sold to Texmaco).

Present product is cast bogies including assemblies (CP top, CP bottom, main three castings, magnet steel casting); other components like couplers, springs, side-bearers, braking system sourced externally, then assembled and supplied as a total set.
Market split: roughly 70-75% of bogie demand comes from wagon manufacturers (new wagons), 20-25% from Indian Railways directly (replacement/spares).

Historically (till 2019) wagon manufacturers like Texmaco, Titagarh outsourced roughly 20-30% of bogie requirements to third parties like Simplex because manufacturers also produce couplers, other railway castings (e.g., CMS crossings) and export orders limit their own capacity.
Company plans to expand product range from bogies to couplers and other components over time — a consistent growth plan for railway products.

subsections.label: Fabricated Bogies
points: New product line for Simplex, used in locomotives, passenger coaches, metro and Vande Bharat; company previously did cast bogies and cast locomotive bogies but not fabricated bogies.
Developmental order taken; product to go into testing phase.
About 1,400 engines requiring about 2,800 locomotive bogies represent the addressable demand, plus coach, metro and Vande Bharat bogie demand.
Roughly half of the second preferential issue proceeds are being allocated to develop fabricated bogie facilities due to seen huge demand and fewer competing players.
Growth plan: after locomotive fabricated bogies, expand into coach bogies, then Vande Bharat and metro bogies.

subsections.label: Coke Oven Doors
points: Very important, high-margin segment for Simplex, using Japanese technology described as state-of-the-art.
There are a little more than 25 coke oven battery installations across major steel plants (e.g., Bhilai Steel Plant has 11 batteries, Rourkela and Bokaro have around 11/9 batteries).
Roughly 150-180 batteries required in India currently across integrated steel plants (140 million tons capacity), each plant needing 7-12 batteries.

Industry shifting from 'Top Charging' to 'Stamp Charging' technology, which allows use of lower quality coal; SAIL has started replacing batteries accordingly - the SMS and Thyssen orders were for SAIL's first two stamp-charging plants.
Expecting orders for two more batteries from L&T for ISCO; overall order potential of two to three battery-related orders (doors) per year from the existing 140 million ton capacity.
An additional ~140 million tons of capacity is planned to be built by 2030 (management expects more realistically by 2040), requiring another 70-80 coke oven batteries.
Company does not supply doors alone but also door frames and flash plates.
Segment expected to grow from Rs 50-60 crores currently to about Rs 100 crores over the next 2-3 years, assuming India continues to source from domestic suppliers rather than China.

subsections.label: Power Sector
points: Company was a top BHEL supplier (award received 1999-2003); work volume had declined from 2004 to 2019-20 but has now picked up again.
Government power ministry ordered about 32 thermal power plants to BHEL and 16 to L&T, to be commissioned by 2032, driving demand for equipment.
Company products for power sector go into pulverizer/coal mill, pumps, and structural components for plant buildings.
All 32 and 16 planned plants are coal-based thermal power plants.

subsections.label: Other Segments (Valves, Pumps, Non-ferrous, Machine Tools)
points: Company is one of the biggest manufacturers of butterfly valve castings, pump castings, gearbox castings and machine tool castings.
Also does significant non-ferrous/aluminum work for Hindalco, Vedanta, BALCO, HZL - supplying sawmills, ladles, ports.

subsections.label: Defence & Shipbuilding
points: Currently supplying simple items to shipyards: A-brackets, B-brackets and stern boss castings, welded to hull structure where the propeller shaft passes.

Company's flexible jobbing-style foundry (handling few kilos to 50-55 tons single piece) gives an advantage in low-volume, high-precision segments like defence and shipbuilding, where global capability is largely concentrated in India and China.
Turret component (developed exclusively as a private company) for T-72 tanks is no longer relevant since replacement by T-90 with fabricated parts done in-house by customer.
Working with Gun Carriage Factory (GCF), Jabalpur on components for Dhanush (India's Bofors-equivalent artillery gun); company is one of multiple suppliers, not sole source.
Defence ministry has asked ordinance factories to scale Dhanush production (e.g., from 20 to 40 units) to test capability, prompting search for suppliers.

Management stated they will not aggressively expand defence/shipbuilding for now, focusing execution bandwidth on steel, railways and power; will revisit deeper expansion once management bandwidth allows.

subsections.label: Rejected Diversification - Centrifugal Rolls
points: Company considered entering centrifugally cast rolls (used in DRI plants as heat-resistant, stainless steel HK-40 grade air-inlet pipes; also usable for some copper bushes and shipbuilding) requiring investment of about Rs 1.5-2 crores using existing furnace/crane/shed facilities.

Market survey found sufficient competing suppliers closer to customers in Western and Eastern regions (Tata, Rourkela), plus Jindal Steel and Power's own captive plant, leaving only the Raipur region addressable - decided not viable and dropped the plan.

Company has spare land available at both plant units for future expansion/mechanization to reduce dependency on manpower.

subsections.label: Wagon Market Structure
points: Historically about 20-25% bogie outsourcing occurs from major wagon manufacturers to third-party foundries like Simplex, since manufacturers also need capacity for couplers, other railway castings and export orders.
Mega wagon tender news resurfacing; last such large order was in 2022, requiring 8,000-10,000 wagons over 3 years (~3,000 wagons/year, ~6,000 bogies/year, ~6,000 tons of castings).

subsections.label: Steel Plant Landscape & Coke Oven TAM
points: India/China are the primary regions where integrated steel plants (with coke ovens) remain preferred, given coal and iron ore availability; rest of world (mostly West) is decarbonizing and phasing out coke oven batteries.
Of total 180 million tons Indian steel capacity, ~40 million tons is DRI-route (no coke battery needed) and ~140 million tons is integrated (needs coke ovens).
About 20 integrated plants exist (e.g., JSW ~5, Tata ~3, SAIL ~7), needing an estimated 150-180 batteries in total currently.
Additional ~140 million tons of new integrated capacity planned (company target year 2030, management's own estimate more realistically by 2040), requiring another 70-80 new coke oven batteries.

subsections.label: Defence Customer Relationships
points: Working with Gun Carriage Factory (GCF) Jabalpur, which manufactures Dhanush (India's Bofors equivalent); company is one of multiple suppliers being tested by ordinance factories after defence ministry pushed for higher indigenous capability post-'Sindhu' related developments.

subsections.label: Acquisition Plans
points: Company was in discussions for acquisitions; one deal failed due to high valuation multiples sought by Indian targets in similar (railways) line of business, two other discussions are currently open.
Decided to look at acquisition targets outside India where PE multiples are more sensible/manageable.
Acquisitions will remain within similar/related fields (steel, power, railways) - no plans to enter new business lines.
Potential acquisition size discussed as being in the range of roughly Rs 20-100 crores ('somewhere in between').

subsections.label: EPC Strategy
points: Company works in EPC sector 'in a small way' and plans to continue being a very focused EPC company targeting specific projects where part of the production comes back to its own shops.

Company explicitly stated it is not a bridge or road-making company - its EPC focus remains within the metallurgical/plant-building sector (e.g., could join as a consortium member with OEMs for something like a blast furnace project).

subsections.label: FY28 Revenue Target Strategy
points: FY28 target of Rs 500 crores depends on three pillars: (1) execution discipline - achieving the FY27 Rs 300 crore target is seen as a prerequisite, (2) successful acquisition and/or EPC order wins, and (3) growth in railway orders (locomotives, fabricated bogies etc.).
Cast bogies are viewed as providing a repetitive, low-design-change revenue base that can lock in 30-40% of production without major re-qualification effort.

subsections.label: Execution Risk
points: Execution is flagged as the single biggest risk to achieving the Rs 500 crore FY28 target; failure in execution would jeopardize the order booking target as well.
Steel price volatility and gas (LPG) supply disruptions have already affected fabrication plant operations and dispatch timing.

Labor availability is a growing challenge as source states (UP, Bihar, Bengal, Orissa) see improving local economies, making it harder to recruit; company is focusing more on skilling local people and considering mechanization to offset manpower dependency.

subsections.label: Customer Site Dependency
points: As a contractual manufacturer, dispatch timing is dependent on customer site readiness/activities, which caused inventory build-up of finished goods that could not be liquidated in the reporting quarter.

subsections.label: Acquisition Valuation Risk
points: High valuation multiples sought by Indian acquisition targets led to one deal falling through; company is now looking outside India for more reasonably valued targets.

subsections.label: Funding Requirement for Growth
points: Company may need to raise additional capital (debt or equity) to fund fabricated bogie capital and working capital needs beyond the originally planned Rs 50 crore preferential issue.

subsections.label: Revenue Targets
points: FY27 revenue target of Rs 300 crores: Rs 200 crores from existing business (already closed/secured), Rs 50 crores from railways (cast business), and roughly Rs 50 crores from power sector.
FY28 revenue target of Rs 500 crores contingent on: achieving the FY27 target, execution discipline, success in EPC orders and/or acquisitions, and growth in railway orders.
Margins for FY27 expected to remain similar to current levels; a possible margin uptick from cost-reduction initiatives may become visible in Q3/Q4 of FY27.
Company maintains its previously communicated 45-50% CAGR guidance for the medium-term.

subsections.label: Railway Ramp-up Outlook
points: Expecting to receive orders for 100-200 bogies within about a month's time from discussions currently underway.
From September onward, company expects to consistently run at its built capacity of ~200 bogies/month.
Coke oven door segment revenue expected to grow from Rs 50-60 crores currently to about Rs 100 crores over the next 2-3 years.

MONOLITH.about: Incorporated in 2018, MonolithischIndia Ltd is a manufacturer of pre mixed high-quality ramming mass[1]

quarters.summary: Monolithisch India delivered its highest ever quarterly revenue, EBITDA, PAT and volume in Q1 FY27, driven by rapid adoption of the premium SGB Limited product (~50% of revenue vs ~15% prior quarter, expected to rise to 60-65% in Q2 FY27). Management guided Q2 FY27 revenue of INR55-60 crores and reiterated FY27 revenue guidance of ~INR250 crores, with the greenfield Metallurgica facility (more than doubling capacity from 2.56 lakh MTPA to 5.74 lakh MTPA) on track for dry run on 14th September 2026 and commercial production expected from ~23rd-24th September 2026.

subsections.label: Profitability drivers
points: Improvement in profitability primarily driven by higher premium products, better operational efficiency and disciplined execution across the business.
Average SGB Limited series realization is around INR800-900 better than the previous product, with additional cost of around INR200-250.
Company also saved around 10% on employee costs relative to the volume handled versus last quarter, and gained some savings from inventories held (buying price better than what was sold).

subsections.label: Freight accounting treatment
points: INR4-6 crores of freight inward has been moved to indirect/other expenses per Companies Act schedule requirements; company buys and sells products inclusive of freight but bifurcates when there is cost volatility to absorb leverage risk, moving to ex-plant basis.

This freight reclassification, when added back, brings gross margin closer to prior quarter levels (66.12% vs 64.89%), with the residual difference attributed to product mix changes (previously more boron/boric series, now mix of both) rather than freight alone.

subsections.label: Cost structure improvement
points: Gross margin improvement not attributed to product mix alone; new machinery installed from IPO proceeds (started around September last year) reduced labour costs, electricity costs and wastage significantly versus prior periods.
Labour-intensive process efficiency improved: same number of people now manufacture 15,000-16,000 tons/month versus 10,000 tons/month a year back.

subsections.label: Tax rate
points: Management could not confirm precise reason for prior quarter's lower 18.7% tax rate versus current 25%, speculating it may relate to a DTA/DTL adjustment at Mineral India; offered to respond via email query.

subsections.label: Land and capex
points: Land cost roughly INR15-20 lakhs per acre; company has bought around 4 acres with agreement for 5-6 acres more at the greenfield campus, which started at ~12.5 acres and is now ~14-15 acres with room to expand on 3 sides.

Of the total capex allocation of INR44.90 crores from IPO proceeds, INR28.79 crores have been deployed, with balance of INR15.69 crores to be utilized in a phased manner through the remainder of FY27.

subsections.label: Demand scenario
points: Company currently has around 130-135% of order book than what it can supply on a monthly basis.
Once Metallurgica comes into action, the 20-30% shortfall will be covered from that additional capacity.

Demand from integrated steel plants (with power plant, sponge plant, furnaces, TMT wire) is very stable and rarely leads to absolute shutdowns; they may slightly decrease or increase production but keep running.
Last 15 days saw a down cycle in the steel industry up till the 23rd, but the last 5 days showed strong demand improvement, illustrating day-to-day dynamics of the industry.

subsections.label: Pricing / realization economics
points: SGB Limited series commands a premium of around INR700-800 per metric ton over previous product, with additional cost of around INR250-300, driven by 15-20% better campaign life for customers, making the premium immaterial versus their downtime/profitability gains.
Average base product price is around INR7,800 per ton (FOR basis) versus SGB Limited at around INR8,700-9,100 per ton.

Generally price trend for the company's products does not decrease; it may only decrease minutely if additive costs change significantly; over a 5-6 year trend, once cost levels are reached for CP or SP, they do not fall back.
SGB Limited volume was roughly 20,500 metric tons of the 52,000 metric ton total volume handled in Q1 FY27 (excluding trading quantity).

subsections.label: SGB Limited adoption
points: One of the biggest highlights of the quarter has been the exceptional response to next-generation premium product SGB Limited, reflecting rapid customer adoption driven by superior performance (15-20% campaign life improvement) and differentiated minimum heat assurance.
Process improvement across both operating units will further accelerate adoption of the SGB Limited series.
It takes about one to one-and-a-half months for an existing customer to shift from one product to another as they evaluate benefit versus cost.

Company's long-term objective is to slowly transform entire sales to the SGB series wherever it can get better revenue, realization and acceptability, contingent on market adoption; the new Metallurgica plant will be better equipped to handle this product than current brownfield facilities.

subsections.label: Customer concentration
points: Top 10 customers on a group level basis account for around 25-35% of revenue; concentration appears higher if measured by parent company rather than by individual GST-registered plant/location, since large groups like SAIL have multiple plants (Bhilai, Bokaro, Rourkela, Vizag, Durgapur) treated as separate entities.

At certain customers wallet share reaches 70-85%; incremental wallet share growth of 5-10% expected within existing customer lines if product differentiation improves, plus new customer tapping via volume expansion and ongoing trials.

subsections.label: Mineral India performance
points: Mineral India delivered high gross margins (90-95%) in the last 2 quarters because it held inventory of additives/packing material procured at a much better rate (INR130-135) than current procurement rate (INR150-155), following prior-quarter shutdowns taken to achieve capacity.

subsections.label: Realization/volume dynamics
points: Realization increase attributed to two reasons: higher-rate product mix (SGB Limited sold at premium) and cost savings on labour/inventory versus last quarter.
No volume decline QoQ; volume increased ~7% based on company data; confusion arose because trading-basis volumes are excluded from the reported 52,000 MT figure.
Trading component (additives ~INR3-3.5 crores plus lower-grade material trading ~INR1-1.5 crores) exists in both current and prior quarters.

subsections.label: Greenfield project timeline (Metallurgica)
points: Landmark greenfield project continues to make good progress and remains on track for commissioning in Q2 FY27.
Dry run scheduled on Ganesh Chaturthi, 14th September 2026 (2 days, without loading), followed by ritual ceremony on 16th September, then technical trials/settling of products for 10-15 days.
Commercial sales expected from around 25th September or 1st October, but Pitru Paksha period (25th September to 10th) may affect timing; target for commercial production is 23rd-24th September.

Upon commissioning, the project will more than double manufacturing capacity from 2.56 lakh MTPA to 5.74 lakh MTPA, making it the largest and most advanced single-campus ramming mass manufacturing facility known to management globally.
Facility backed by advanced automation and sophisticated integration will strengthen presence in the high-demand eastern region.
Production will ramp up over the next 3-4 months as it is a greenfield project requiring time to establish; company is taking a modest view of INR40-60 crores of revenue from the project in FY27.

1-2 month delay in the greenfield project has occurred due to civil labour shortages, potentially linked to West Bengal elections, though management would not fully attribute the Q1 revenue shortfall to this.

subsections.label: Capacity strategy rationale
points: Company opted for one large capacity expansion rather than incremental annual capex increases (as done previously at the Monolithisch plant, e.g., 130 to 160), because incremental expansion capex costs were significantly higher in aggregate than a single large capacity buildout, and a single large plant allows distinct, clean crushing and mixing zones sized to capacity.
Company aims to operate at a minimum 85-90% capacity utilization level.
There is plenty of land bank available in the greenfield area for further brownfield capex and future projects, with a rural setting allowing expansion on three sides.

subsections.label: Rajasthan capacity plans
points: Company has plans to establish operations in Rajasthan; land has been finalized and given to a party on a turnkey basis to complete the industrial conversion process.

key_figures.label: Additional distance advantage to southern market from greenfield

subsections.label: Export strategy
points: Company has been exporting for the last 2-3 years on a regular basis, largely through Indian traders who further sell to markets close to Nepal and Bangladesh.

Nepal and Bangladesh payment schedules have been disturbed over the last 1-2 years; company did direct business with Nepal one-and-a-half years before the 'Gen Z' unrest there, then shifted to trading via intermediaries.

Once things stabilize and adequate capacity is available from Metallurgica, the prime target is to penetrate Bangladesh and Nepal directly and also tap the southern market (Hyderabad, Telangana region), given the new greenfield plant's 120-150 km additional proximity advantage to the south versus the current plant.
Metallurgica's prime objectives are to tap nearby export markets such as Nepal and Bangladesh, and further penetrate markets closer to the eastern and southern regions.

subsections.label: Competitive positioning / moat
points: Brand reputation built over 35-40 years; father associated with the consumable business since 1983, subsidiary started making ramming mass in 2007; six-year revenue CAGR roughly 60-65%.
Management declined to fully detail the 'moat' on the group call, offering a one-to-one meeting or factory visit for deeper explanation.

Company's maximum advantage is that its product performs equally well compared to Rajasthan-based competitors while being costed much less for the customer, enabling faster capacity consumption than competitors.

Customer stickiness is roughly 50-50: half of customers are not very price sensitive, half are very price sensitive; product quality plus established brand supports fast customer swaps when better performance is offered.

subsections.label: Industry structure
points: Industry is non-surveyed with only approximate figures available; competitors include Rajasthan-belt players (small, big, large) and local-belt players (smaller); market includes listed and good unlisted players, not dominated by only a few large players currently, though bigger/better-quality players are gaining share from unorganized players.
Once Metallurgica capacity comes online, company expects to have the largest capacity in the industry.

Steel demand outlook is promising, supported by government initiatives from January that helped the steel industry; more room from government support could further benefit domestic steel and, by extension, ramming mass demand.

Company intends to tap two lines of growth: (1) products similar to its existing range where its brand presence and manufacturing know-how already exist (three-four identified similar products), and (2) broader silica-related opportunities (a globally-discussed topic), though management declined to give detailed guidance on this until the AGM.

subsections.label: AGM roadmap
points: Company will announce an AGM date in the next one or two weeks, where detailed roadmap on high specialty silica opportunity and other new product plans for the next two years will be laid out.
Details on capex plans, silica-based product entry, and other strategic roadmap items will be disclosed partially at the AGM and partially as projects reach a closer development phase.

subsections.label: Backward integration and acquisitions
points: Management declined to comment on any backward integration initiative, stating updates will come through the right sources as and when things develop.
No update on previously discussed acquisition plans at this time.

subsections.label: Long-term positioning
points: Company does not want to position itself only as the largest ramming mass manufacturer in the world (expected to happen naturally within 6 months to 1.5 years on a sales basis, and within 2 months on a capacity basis), but rather as the biggest company handling silica and silica-related products in India, including high-value and value-added/crushing-related products, not confined to ramming mass alone.
FY28 target is to be the largest in terms of what the company manufactures and sells, potentially achieved before FY28; management intends to maintain the CAGR achieved over the last five-six years.

subsections.label: Macro and demand risks
points: Despite a challenging macroeconomic environment, the company continues to strengthen its market position through superior product quality, timely delivery, efficient inventory management and strong technical support.
Guidance is dynamic and industry demand shifts day-to-day based on customer sales; company has historically fallen short or exceeded guidance by 2-5% and expects this dynamic to continue.
Recent down cycle in the steel industry (up to the 23rd) followed by a strong pickup in the last 5 days illustrates demand volatility.

subsections.label: Execution risk
points: 1-2 month delay in the greenfield project due to civil labour shortages, potentially related to the West Bengal elections, contributed to part of the revenue shortfall versus guidance.
Q1 FY27 revenue guidance (previously INR52-55 crores) was missed by roughly INR3-4 crores, attributed to broader demand dynamics and the greenfield delay rather than a single cause.

subsections.label: Input cost / freight volatility
points: Freight cost volatility (e.g., fuel cost increases due to geopolitical factors such as war) has led the company to bifurcate ex-plant pricing from freight to manage leverage/risk exposure.
Mineral India's high margins in recent quarters were partly due to holding lower-cost inventory; current additive procurement costs have risen (INR150-155 versus INR130-135 previously).

subsections.label: Export market disruption
points: Nepal and Bangladesh payment schedules have been disturbed over the last 1-2 years, prompting a shift from direct sales to trading via intermediaries in these export markets.

points: Company commenced FY27 on a strong note, building on FY26 momentum; reflects strong customer demand, increasing acceptance of premium product portfolio and continued operational excellence.

Remains confident of achieving Q2 revenue guidance of INR55-60 crores and FY27 revenue guidance of approximately INR250 crores.

key_takeaways: We have commenced FY27 on a very strong note, building on the exceptional momentum of FY26. During the quarter, we delivered our highest ever quarterly revenue, EBITDA, PAT, and volume handled.

Our landmark greenfield project continues to make good progress and remains on track for commissioning in Q2 FY27... Upon commissioning, the project will more than double our manufacturing capacity from 2.56 lakh MTPA to 5.74 lakh MTPA.

One of the biggest highlights of the quarter has been the exceptional response to our next-generation premium product, SGB Limited. During Q1 FY27, the product contributed approximately 50% of our revenue, a significant increase from around 15% in the previous quarter.
We expect SGB Limited contribution to increase to nearly 60% to 65% of revenue in Q2 FY27, supporting improved realizations and sustainable margin expansion.
For Q2 FY27, we expect revenue in the range of INR55 crores to INR60 crores, while for FY27, we remain confident of achieving our revenue guidance of approximately INR250 crores.

Revenue stood at INR47 crores, registering a strong 64% year-on-year and 16% quarter-on-quarter growth... EBITDA for the quarter stood at INR13 crores, increasing 99% year-on-year and 15% quarter-on-quarter, while profit after tax reached INR10 crores, reflecting a robust 135% year-on-year and a 24% sequential growth. EBITDA and PAT stood strong at 28% and 21%, respectively.
At present, we have around 130%, 135% of order book than what we can supply on a monthly basis.

quarters.summary: Monolithisch India closed FY26 with record revenue, EBITDA and PAT, driven by volume growth, SGB Limited traction and operational efficiencies. For FY27, management guided Q1 revenue of INR52-55 crores and full-year revenue of INR250-300 crores with EBITDA margins of 22-25%, supported by capacity expansion (Greenfield project, Mineral India Global uplift), Metalurgica scale-up and SGB Limited mix improvement, targeting group capacity of 5,74,000 MTPA and positioning as the largest ramming mass manufacturer globally by late Q1/early Q2 FY27.

subsections.label: Profitability Drivers
points: Q4 FY26 performance driven by higher volumes, sustained customer demand, improved operational efficiency, and consolidation of group operations.
Record high margins driven by enhanced contribution from SGB Limited's product portfolio, improved operational efficiencies and effective inventory management.

FY26 record-breaking performance driven by successful completion of Brownfield expansion, acquisition of Mineral India Global Private Limited, improved operational efficiency, strong customer response, and SGB Limited contribution.

subsections.label: Realization Clarification
points: Management clarified there is no drop in realization; apparent decline in analyst calculations is due to inclusion of non-premix (without additives) product sales, where additive cost of INR1,600-1,800 is deducted, lowering the rate to around INR6,500.
Average realization of the product increased by around INR400 in Q4 YoY and around INR300 on a full-year YoY basis.
SGB Limited category includes both premix (boric acid, boron) and non-premix varieties, contributing to blended realization variance.

Non-premix share (SLM-980) was slightly higher than last year during January-February due to uncertainty in additive rate fluctuations; this is normal part of business, sometimes skewed to one quarter.

subsections.label: Cost Structure
points: Raw material cost fluctuation between Q3 and Q4 is due to procurement basis: FOR (freight-inclusive) vs Ex-plant (freight excluded, booked as indirect expense).
When transporters are expected to hike rates dynamically, company shifts to Ex-plant procurement to keep transportation cost in its own hands, moving the cost to indirect expenses instead of COGS.

Other expenses (staff, guard, etc.) do not scale with production volume/tonnage and are expected to remain stable; only transportation cost (when included in raw material) will grow in line with revenue.

Trading of additives (boric acid) contributed to stock-in-trade rise: company procures additives, analyzes market rates, and swaps/sells to unorganized players before expiry at a premium price when opportunity arises; no fixed margin, purely opportunistic trading gains aided by favorable global conditions.

subsections.label: Working Capital & Balance Sheet
points: Receivable days improved from ~72 to 50-60 days over the last year.
Inventory has increased as company maintains continuous supply commitment; historically avoided stopping plant operations even during COVID.
Company maintains inventory buffer (2-3 months, up to 100-120 days) to guard against additive/raw material supply shortages (boron oxide from Europe/US, boric acid from Middle East).
Creditor days slightly reduced due to cash payments to packaging industry amid short supply concerns (LPG-related issues).
Company is almost debt-free; management does not intend to take on debt, preferring to use surplus cash to stock inventory which has historically yielded 10-15% premium after 8-10 months of holding.
Incremental working capital may be required as revenue scales, tied to sales volume rather than fixed cost; exact quantification uncertain at present.
Greenfield capex is fully funded from funds already in hand; company is evaluating internal shift of INR5-6 crores toward working capital but will not require external debt to meet committed capex.

subsections.label: SGB Limited Product Positioning
points: SGB Limited launched last year, witnessing strong initial traction and encouraging customer response, positioned as next-generation premium offering.
Company expects over 60% customer migration from SGB 777 starting Q1, driven by superior product performance and reliability.
First-of-its-kind warranty-backed proposition in the segment garnering significant customer interest and trust.

Positioned as an upgrade within existing customer base; expected to drive better realizations and support margin expansion via stronger pricing power without hurting customer economics, while improving customer efficiency.
SGB Limited category includes premix (boric acid, boron) and non-premix grades, using a different set of stone and machinery compared to SGB 777.
Product cycle: company already supplies to a customer; when offering an upgraded product, runs a trial campaign (15-20 days); if successful, converts customer from existing/other vendor.

Quality differential vs SGB 777: warranty life increased from 45-50 hours (SGB 777) to 50-55 hours+ (SGB Limited), with peak performance up to 61-62 hours; driven by new manufacturing mechanism post-IPO and new mining locations identified in Madhya Pradesh (near Delhi) in addition to conventional Bihar mines.
Management declined to rank SGB Limited against organized/unorganized competition, stating the market should decide.

subsections.label: Customer Cannibalization / Market Expansion Dynamics
points: Most large customers require product in volumes such that they never depend on a single vendor (typically 70-95% share per client, rarely 100%), so SGB Limited is expected to expand company's own wallet share rather than only cannibalizing existing SGB 777 volume.
Of 100-120 clients, only 10-15 are expected to take 100% single-handedly from the company; remaining will be at 80-95% share.
Company cannot disclose exact order book numbers due to competitive pricing sensitivity in the industry.

subsections.label: Mineral India Global Product Mix
points: Mineral India deals with smaller furnaces (~15 MT range) versus Monolithisch's larger furnace clientele.

After new machinery installation, Mineral India will cater to bigger furnaces, bringing realization closer to par with Monolithisch, though margins expected to be marginally lower (1-2%, or per another comment 5-10% lower) due to lack of Monolithisch's advanced machinery edge and smaller scale (indirect expenses divided over smaller tonnage).

subsections.label: Greenfield Project
points: Major Greenfield project executing capacity enhancement expected by end of Q1 FY27 or early Q2 FY27, backed by automation, integration and renewable energy.
New facility located in West Bengal, strengthening presence in high-demand Eastern cluster, aimed at capturing growing demand and supporting long-term growth.

Company is expanding land at the Greenfield campus and has identified new project opportunities including high-value silica-based offerings, to be taken up after completion of ongoing Greenfield project.

Machinery suppliers are high-grade global players (Finland, Metso, Steinmüller) who do not manufacture lower-capacity machines for crushing and mixing, justifying the large capacity jump in one phase rather than gradual increases like peers.
Net block considered low relative to industry standards for the capacity being added.
Company expects a fixed definitive inauguration date for the new plant to be announced at the AGM.

subsections.label: Brownfield Project
points: Brownfield project commissioned by replacing existing production line with minimum capital outlay and limited downtime.
Ongoing efficiency improvements in the newly established line led to reduction in consumables and labor cost in Q4 FY26.

subsections.label: Mineral India Global
points: Capacity expansion at Mineral India Global (wholly-owned subsidiary) completed; plant ready to operate at enhanced capacity pending statutory approvals expected within 15 days.
Major shutdowns were taken in H1 to complete upgrades; approvals now received; plant should run at 90-95% efficiency going forward.

Mineral India caters to smaller furnaces (~15 metric tons range); post new machinery installation, will cater to bigger furnaces, bringing realization closer to par with Monolithisch, though margins expected to be 1-2% (or 5-10%) lower than Monolithisch due to smaller scale and less economies of scale / lack of advanced machinery edge of SGB Limited.

subsections.label: Automation & Labor Efficiency
points: Automation funded through IPO proceeds; company aims to reduce labor dependency due to labor availability concerns (more than cost) observed over the last five years.
Per-labor output has improved significantly from initial manufacturing levels (2,000-3,000 tons/month) to current scale.

Metalurgica expected to be even more labor-efficient as it is an entirely integrated project, unlike Monolithisch which underwent renovation; extra ramming and improvement areas already identified for Metalurgica.

subsections.label: Capex Plans
points: No new capex plans announced for FY27/FY28 beyond current commitments; company will complete existing plans.
Capex guidance for FY28 and next steps to be detailed at the AGM.

subsections.label: Market Sizing & Growth
points: Market has doubled over the last five-six years per management's industry experience; expected to keep growing every year in line with India's steel demand growth.
Management does not have a formal research report but bases estimates on industry experience.

subsections.label: Competitive Positioning
points: Competitive edge cited: proximity to maximum iron ore availability (Odisha, Jharkhand) and to steel plants concentrated in Chhattisgarh, Madhya Pradesh, Jharkhand, Odisha, West Bengal, Bihar, where most iron ore/pellet melting activity occurs; scrap-based belts are more towards the Jalna/northern region.
Company believes it is well-placed geographically relative to this demand concentration.

subsections.label: Demand & Supply Dynamics / Order Book
points: Company reports a very strong order book; cannot comment on competitors' order books.
Demand strategy: 50% from existing customers (who are also on heavy capex plans) and 50% from new customer acquisition previously untapped due to low production capacity.

Not worried about oversupply concerns; expects small/regional unorganized players to exit the industry in the next 5-6 months due to volatility in additive and bag rates and capital intensity requirements.

subsections.label: Recognition
points: Company recognized as one of Bharat's Best-to-Billion Brands 2026 by ETH, reflecting strong growth trajectory, scalable business model, and market leadership position.

subsections.label: Silica-based Segment Entry
points: Company is expanding into adjacent silica-based segments as part of long-term growth strategy; further detail to be disclosed at the AGM once specific products are finalized.
Company has identified three-four segments where its earlier expertise can be helpful; will opt for one to proceed after completing the Greenfield project.
No immediate plant setup planned; approach is to expand the campus first, complete Greenfield project, then decide on specific silica-based product line.

subsections.label: Geographic Expansion / Joint Ventures
points: Board approved exploration of strategic expansion initiatives including joint venture agreements with mine owners and establishing manufacturing/processing facilities in new regions (e.g., Rajasthan) where transportation makes current product delivery uneconomical (freight can add ~INR4/kg on top of ~INR6.5-7/kg base cost).
Approach for new regions: enter into joint ventures with mine owners guaranteeing 5-10 year supply or minimum quantity supply commitments before investing capital.

subsections.label: Long-term Vision
points: Company scaling from INR130 crores to a targeted ~INR400-500 crores over the next two years is viewed as a key board-level vision.

If surplus cash is available, company would explore additional silica-related and consumable refractory-related products leveraging existing reputation and experience, but only after completing current commitments (Greenfield, SGB scale-up) before pursuing a 'bigger vision'.
Company aims to be recognized as best-in-class for both customers and shareholders, tracking a consistent CAGR trajectory since inception in 2018/2019.

subsections.label: Seasonality
points: Q2 (rainy season) typically remains dull for the industry due to rain dynamics requiring extra liners in the product and more difficulty in manufacturing; downstream steel industry also faces dull demand in this period, impacting Q2/Q3 margins relative to Q1/Q4.

subsections.label: Supply Chain / Input Cost Volatility
points: Global uncertainty has caused ramming mass raw material rates to increase faster than average historical trend in the last 2-3 months.
Boron oxide travels largely from Europe/US and boric acid from the Middle East; supply chain dependent on these regions remaining stable.

War/geopolitical situation cited as reason for maintaining higher inventory levels (2-3 months, up to 100-120 days) as a hedge against potential shortages of additives/bags; inventory would reduce by ~50% once situation normalizes.
Short supply from packaging industry sector (attributed to LPG-related issues) affected creditor days/cash payment terms.

subsections.label: Working Capital Uncertainty
points: Incremental working capital requirement as revenue scales is difficult to quantify precisely at this stage; tied to sales volume growth.

subsections.label: Competitive/Industry Structure Risk (framed as opportunity)
points: Small/unorganized regional players face volatility in additive and bag rates and may be forced to exit the industry within the next 5-6 months due to lack of capital strength — flagged as an industry dynamic rather than a risk to the company specifically.

key_takeaways: FY26 has been a landmark year for us, with the company achieving its highest ever annual volume handled, revenue, EBITDA and PAT, driven by strong volume growth, resilient customer demand and improved operational efficiencies.
From financial year 23 to FY26, the company has delivered a strong CAGR of 48% in revenue, 68% in EBITDA and 72% in PAT.
We are also confident of becoming the largest manufacturer of ramming mass by late Q1 FY27 to early Q2 FY27.

For FY27, we remain optimistic and are targeting revenue of INR250 crores to INR300 crores with EBITDA margins in the range of 22% to 25%, supported by strong scale-up by addition of Metalurgica and an improving product mix led by SGB Limited.
Q4 FY26 was our strongest quarter to date, with revenue, EBITDA and PAT up by 35%, 75% and 81% to INR41 crores, INR11 crores and INR8 crores respectively on a year-on-year basis.

Consolidated revenue stood at INR135 crores, registering a strong 39% year-on-year growth. EBITDA up 52% year-on-year to INR32 crores and EBITDA margin stood strong and steady at 23.63%. Profitability remains robust, with PAT by 60% year-on-year to INR23 crores, ROCE for financial year 26 at 46% with almost debt-free balance sheet.
The company expects over 60% customer migration from SGB 777 starting Q1, driven by superior product performance and reliability.
Monolithisch India Limited has been recognized as one of Bharat's Best-to-Billion Brands 2026 by ETH.
pressing_questions: What is the expected realization or EBITDA margins on the silica-based products, and what is the peak revenue potential from these products? (Management deferred detail to the AGM once products are defined.)

Query on stock-in-trade jump to 25% (consolidated) / 40% (standalone) in Q4 — attributed to opportunistic additive trading rather than core operations.
Query on drop in raw material cost from INR17 crores (Q3) to INR10 crores (Q4) despite higher sales — attributed to shift between FOR and Ex-plant procurement basis.

STYLAMIND.about: Stylam Industries is engaged in the manufacturing of decorative laminates under the brand name “STYLAM” and exports its products primarily to European and South East Asian countries. It manufactures a wide range of high-quality decorative laminates, specialty surfaces, PU+ lacquer coating, solid surfaces and compact laminates. [1]

quarters.summary: Management reiterated that new plant commercial production is targeted for maximum 1st September 2026 (hopeful for 15th-20th August), with dry run/trial already underway; delay attributed to old family issues and construction-related problems (rain in Chandigarh delayed project by 1-2 months). Ramp-up guided conservatively at 25-30% capacity utilization in the first year, expected to generate INR250-300 crore revenue from the new plant in FY27, with the domestic market restructuring expected to show visible results from Q3 FY27 onwards. Overall EBITDA margins are expected to remain steady at 19-20%+ even after the new capex comes online, and export vs domestic mix may shift slightly but is not expected to hurt margins.

subsections.label: Margin drivers
points: Margin spike beyond 20% attributed to efficiency gains and higher utilization, not inventory gains from wooden/raw material price volatility.
Management stated: 'No inventory gain, nothing. It is our efficiency and more utilization and if you go for sales figures it is increased. So when sales increase, the expenses automatically reduce.'
Margins expected to remain at similar levels (19-20%+) even after the new capex plant starts end of August.

subsections.label: Employee cost & depreciation
points: 10% Q-o-Q decline in employee cost explained by CFO as due to actuarial valuation being considered in the audited balance sheet for the year-end (31 March 26) quarter on a six-monthly basis, which was not considered in Q1.

Employee cost expected to remain at similar levels going forward as major hiring cost for the new plant (supervisors, high-level people) has already been incurred; only incremental labor/supervisor costs remain.
Depreciation for the new plant will begin accruing from next month onwards (post commissioning); specific quantification was not provided due to audio issues on the call.

subsections.label: Domestic segment margin
points: CFO/management could not quantify the exact margin delta for the domestic business but confirmed that losses which were occurring in the domestic market for many quarters have been reduced, which is the primary driver of any margin improvement.
Company does not calculate EBITDA margins separately for domestic vs export since production and many expenses are common; margins are expected to be similar across both.

subsections.label: Domestic vs Export mix
points: Domestic currently contributes ~25% of overall revenue; management does not expect export market to contract, ratio may increase slowly for domestic without hurting overall EBITDA margins.
Company aims to run the domestic market efficiently so growth in domestic share does not hamper margins.

subsections.label: Existing plant capacity status
points: Laminate segment still has a slight capacity gap of about 5-10% if efficiency is improved further.
Acrylic capacity is completely empty currently; management is revamping both domestic and export teams which will include acrylic focus.

key_figures.label: New plant commercial production target date

subsections.label: Commissioning timeline & delay reasons
points: Commercial production targeted for 1st September 2026 (first week of September), with hope for 15th-20th August; dry run/trial production already ongoing.
Delay caused by multiple reasons including an 'old family problem' that slowed the project, and heavy rain in Chandigarh a few months back that delayed construction by 1-2 months.
Management stated there is no further risk to the timeline beyond a possible one-week delay; work has restarted after the family issue was resolved.
Plant described as 'world number best plant' with large machinery and boiler capacity; construction complexity contributed to timeline slippage.
Environmental clearance issues previously flagged in an earlier call have since been resolved.

subsections.label: Ramp-up plan
points: Ramp-up will be assessed month-on-month based on customer demand; there are no annual POs typical in this industry.
Management guided conservatively to 25-30% capacity utilization for the new plant in its first year (clarified after some confusion with an analyst over 50% figure).
Company is confident of achieving INR250-300 crore revenue from the new (third) plant in FY27 despite the delay, as there is sufficient order backlog for the new plant.

subsections.label: Export market performance
points: Highest quarterly exports ever recorded this quarter.
Europe is the best-performing export region currently; APAC and Middle East also showing positive momentum.
Growth expected from both existing geographies and new geography additions.
US and Middle East together contribute roughly 10-15% each of laminate revenue; exact Middle East breakdown to be shared via follow-up email.

subsections.label: US tariff situation
points: US tariff on Indian laminate exports remains at 10%; a news report on the morning of the call suggested the rate was due to drop to 0% from 24th July but was instead re-implemented at 10%, requiring further confirmation.
No change in duty as of the call date; orders continue to be processed as before.

subsections.label: Domestic market rebuild activities
points: Domestic restructuring involves adding new distributors and partners across various Indian cities/states where Stylam was previously not present (previously focused on only 4-5 cities).
Opening new warehouses wherever required and rebuilding trust/confidence with distributors.
Building a new sales/marketing team dedicated to domestic business.
Process expected to take three to six months for distributor/partner additions across new markets; overall domestic revamp expected to take two to three quarters, per earlier guidance.

subsections.label: Raw material cost trends
points: Raw material situation (kraft paper, deco paper, phenol, melamine) remains unpredictable, tied to the West Asia war situation.
Even if the war stops, raw material prices are not expected to fall drastically; any reduction would be gradual and could take six to nine months to normalize.
Price hikes taken by the company are expected to remain intact unless raw material costs decline, in which case some reversal may be needed.

subsections.label: Logistics
points: Logistics remains a significant challenge for the entire industry globally, particularly noted for the Middle East region, but is described as 'part of the business' and being managed by the company like all other players.

key_figures.label: Course correction timeline for domestic business

subsections.label: Domestic price hikes
points: Multiple, product-specific price hikes taken across different segments of the domestic market in Q1 FY27; management stated it is difficult to give one standard percentage as each product application (e.g., 1mm laminate, 0.8mm, compact laminate) has a different price hike.
No further price hike currently anticipated as raw material costs are stable; a rethink would occur if raw material costs rise further.

subsections.label: Domestic brand positioning
points: Management noted the industry norm is domestic being the core business with exports smaller, whereas for Stylam it has historically been the reverse; the company aims to build similar strength domestically as it has in exports.
No unique or new strategy — approach is opening warehouses, rebuilding distributor trust, adding partners, and getting the right team in place, along with marketing activities to rebuild the brand.

subsections.label: AICA partnership status
points: Aica has officially joined as a strategic partner this month (July 2026) after taking 40% shareholding via open offer at INR22.50; first Board meeting held on 22nd of the month (two days before the call).
No involvement from Aica in daily operations; they are a strategic partner sitting in Japan, with quarterly Board meetings to review results.

No discussions yet regarding exports to Aica or new business initiatives; potential technology transfer (for laminates or any other product) may evolve over the next 3-4 months but nothing concrete yet.

Aica has not shared their expectations or ideas for the company but is reportedly very happy with the Q1 results; management believes it will exceed the revenue estimate given to Aica even accounting for the plant delay, due to sufficient order backlog for the new plant.
Aica is expected to eventually start sourcing acrylic (they already buy acrylic/OEM from the USA), though timing remains uncertain — management expects clarity in the next 3-4 months.

Management emphasized Stylam's own laminate market is already bigger than Aica's India/Vietnam operations; Aica's HPL brand is strong mainly in Japan, with other regional plants not performing as well.
No plan to increase promoter stake from the open market currently; promoters hold 17% and no preferential allotment plan was confirmed.
As of the call date, it has been roughly 45 days (over one month) since the open offer completion.

subsections.label: Next capex plans
points: Major new capex announcement (beyond the current new plant) delayed to next quarter; company is evaluating options side-by-side but wants to focus on successfully starting the current plant first.

Directionally, new capex being considered will focus on strengthening the domestic market (rather than laminates) — likely wood panel adjacencies such as plywood, MDF, or particle boards, since laminates face eventual industry saturation.
New capex, when finalized, will be more oriented toward domestic market than exports.

subsections.label: Geopolitical/input cost risk
points: Resurgence of West Asia war situation flagged as a risk to raw material costs (kraft paper, deco paper, phenol, melamine, other chemicals).
Uncertainty over whether price hikes taken will need to be reversed if raw material costs decline due to war resolution.

subsections.label: Tariff uncertainty
points: Confusion/uncertainty around US tariff changes — a news report suggested the 10% tariff was due to drop to 0% from 24th July but was instead continued at 10%; management needs to recheck the exact situation.

subsections.label: Logistics risk
points: Global logistics challenges, particularly for Middle East shipments, are impacting the industry broadly, not just Stylam.

subsections.label: Execution/delay risk
points: Repeated delays in new plant commissioning (previously guided for June/July, now pushed to August/September) due to family issues and construction-related problems (rain delays).

subsections.label: New plant revenue & utilization outlook
points: Company guiding to 25-30% capacity utilization and INR250-300 crore revenue from the new plant in FY27, its first year, despite the delay, due to sufficient order backlog.
Previously mentioned estimates (before the delay) were 35-40% utilization and INR350-400 crore revenue for the new plant.
Expected revenue from the new plant in its second year (FY28) is INR600-700 crore.

subsections.label: Domestic turnaround timeline
points: Domestic market revamp expected to show visible results from Q3 FY27 onwards, not Q2, consistent with earlier guidance of two-three quarters for restructuring.
Q1 FY27 domestic volumes similar to Q4 FY26; Q2 FY27 expected to show slow ramp-up; significant ramp-up expected in Q3 FY27.

subsections.label: Margin outlook
points: Margins expected to remain in the 19-20%+ range even after new capex plant starts, unchanged despite lower exports Q-o-Q this quarter.
Domestic and export EBITDA margins are expected to be broadly similar going forward since costs (production, most overheads) are largely common.

We want to be conservative on the call, so 30% plus capacity utilization for the new plant... 25% to 30% on a conservative basis.
Whatever you are expecting around INR300 crores revenue from this third plant would definitely be there... based on INR250 crores to INR300 crores, it would be easily achieved from the third plant.
Margins will remain the same, that is why even when the new capex will start end of August, we can expect the similar kind of margins 19%, 20% plus.
You will definitely see the results from Quarter 3. I won't even say Quarter 2, but you will see the results from Quarter 3 onwards.
There won't be any contraction in the export market at all; the ratio might be same... if we are doing a 25% [domestic] of whole revenue right now, that might increase slowly.
As of now, whatever price hike we have taken; it would remain intact. If there is a reduction in raw material, if the war stops, we have to reverse a little bit.
We might delay it until next quarter... once plant is operated by end August, early September, definitely we will announce about our new capex.

guidance_ledger.metric: Employee cost run-rate post new plant

guidance_ledger.metric: Domestic vs export EBITDA margin parity
guidance_ledger.statement: We actually don't calculate both the things separately... but I think the margins would kind of be the same.
We will generate growth on the existing geographies as well as adding more geographies... Europe is doing good, APAC region and Middle East too.

guidance_ledger.metric: New plant revenue contribution (FY27, first 3 quarters)

subsections.label: Margin sustainability
points: 49% gross margin achieved in Q4 FY26 (management clarified this is gross/material margin, not EBITDA level margin, when asked by an analyst who cited 39% for the quarter separately).
Management stated the gross margin may see some up and down across the industry but cannot be assumed to remain exactly the same throughout the year.

Revenue top-line share is expected to increase while expenses reduce as new plant volumes (INR300-400 crore incremental) come in without proportional extra expense, reducing raw material cost impact by 1-2%.
Domestic-business-specific EBITDA is not tracked separately; company reports EBITDA on a consolidated/entire-company basis only.

subsections.label: Capital allocation on new plant
points: New plant capex of INR334 crores has been incurred with no associated debt instalments or interest payments outstanding — management stated there is no financing cost burden on this expansion.
Fixed costs for the new plant (including manpower hiring of up to ~150 workers) have already been absorbed into Q4 FY26 results, so incremental cost when the plant starts will be marginal.
Profitability from the new plant is expected from 'day 1' of commercial production since fixed costs are already accounted for.

subsections.label: Demand resilience
points: Management stated April was the best month for the company, with 3-figure (crore) sales from the older plant alone, first time in company history achieved with good margins.
Demand is expected to remain resilient despite price hikes; management does not believe price increases will mute construction/purchase demand.

Customers understand raw material cost pressures and are largely accepting price increases (3-5% passed on to almost every manufacturer's customers), though 100% pass-through is not always possible due to competition with European companies less impacted by commodity costs.

key_figures.label: Export vs Domestic revenue split outlook

subsections.label: Acrylics
points: Acrylics segment underperformed expectations with only INR15 crore turnover in FY26.
Growth driver: AICA Japan (strategic partner) sells large quantities of acrylic sourced from Europe and US (DuPont) and is planning to buy acrylics from Stylam, creating a new demand channel.
Domestic acrylic focus had been limited due to prior family issues affecting business oversight; company is now also pursuing this product in the domestic market.
Target for FY27 raised to INR50-70 crores.

subsections.label: Domestic vs Export strategy post-acquisition
points: Management stated no special or different strategy for domestic vs export; the intent is to run domestic business with the same systematic, low-cost approach as export, without hiring extra people.

Domestic business restructuring has been ongoing for only ~3 months since new management took over that vertical; brand visibility improvement is expected to take a few months (management indicated 2-3 quarters is a fair assumption), given confidence issues stemming from past policies rather than brand awareness.

Domestic and export markets are being handled by professionals in a structured way; management structure remains unchanged post open-offer completion — export led by Mr. Jagdish Gupta, domestic largely by Mr. Manit Gupta, with no split of one-person-per-market.

subsections.label: Technology transfer under SHA with AICA
points: As part of the Shareholders' Agreement (SHA) with AICA, the company will gain access to AICA's patented HPL (High Pressure Laminate) technology, to be introduced in Stylam's India operations within 2-3 months — described by management as something that 'will be a surprise' to competitors.

subsections.label: New plant commissioning delay
points: New capacity was originally guided to come live by November, then shifted to March in the previous call, and now guided to end-June/early-July.

Delay reason: a Supreme Court observation/clarification around October-November requiring the company to obtain Environment Clearance (EC), for which no Central Empowered Committee (CER) clearance mechanism was available in Haryana at the time; the company applied to the Ministry of Environment, Delhi, and the EC process took 3+ months.
As of the call, the plant is in the final stage; machine testing was expected to start within 2-3 weeks (by end of May 2026).
Management stated there is now little scope for further delay, with commercial production targeted end-June, maximum early-July.

subsections.label: Capacity expansion and utilization strategy
points: New capacity involves different laminate sizes targeting the same customer base but a different market; some sizes will be produced in India for the first time.
New plant is not dependent on any single customer (contrary to an analyst's assumption about Wilsonart-related white labeling).
Company is already in discussions with a set of customers for the new sizes, expected to help achieve 80%+ capacity utilization of the new plant within the next 2 years.

If run at full capacity, revenue could effectively double versus existing capacity (management indicated existing capacity plus new could be ~100% incremental) — though management is being conservative in projections due to the ongoing war situation.
If the new plant runs at full capacity, some machines may be moved out of/rationalized from the old plant.
Existing (old) plants will not see major new capacity additions; instead, growth from old plants will come via more value addition rather than new capex, as capacity is currently a bottleneck there.

subsections.label: US tariff and logistics
points: Current US tariff on Stylam's exports is 10%; this may go under review around 1st July under a 150-day rule tied to a Supreme Court process; tariff rates for competing countries were not disclosed by management.
No delays experienced in shipping from India to US in the last month versus normal; prices are FOB, so freight cost fluctuations are passed on and accepted by customers.
Ocean freight rates, which spiked sharply at the immediate onset of the war, have started reducing.

subsections.label: Raw material cost trends
points: Raw material commodity prices have increased across the industry (not specific to laminates) due to supply disruptions from the Middle East market amid the ongoing war.
No immediate impact from price increases as the company had ordered phenol 3-4 months in advance and is still receiving material at old prices.
Melamine stock is sufficient for 5-6 months, while the war has been ongoing for about 2 months, providing a buffer.
Gas has seen some cost effect; craft paper and paper generally have not seen much effect.
Forward booking/contracts for chemicals mean some material is still being procured at old prices even as current prices have risen for crude-oil-linked items.

Domestic price increases were implemented in 2 tranches; export price increases were made wherever possible, though 100% pass-through is not achievable due to competition with less-impacted European players.
A broader recessionary trend is noted in India as people are not able to sell as much, moderating overall price impact expectations.

subsections.label: AICA/Kogyo strategic partnership and open offer
points: Open offer by AICA (Aica Kogyo, Japan) is completed/near completion; management structure remains unchanged post-deal — export and domestic responsibilities remain with the same promoter directors as before, with professionals handling both markets.

AICA is described purely as a strategic partner with no operational role; even though AICA holds a put option per the Shareholders' Agreement (SHA) to potentially acquire further shares, this does not imply displacement of promoters.

The deal originated due to family issues, per management, rather than a strategic sale intent; management stated their aim is not to sell any stake, and they are considering announcing further expansion plans in coming quarters.

Aica Global currently does not purchase any material from India; they have their own plant in Rudrapur. The deal is expected to be finalized within about 1 month from the call date, after which discussions on potential supply arrangements (e.g., the ~INR200-250 crore business AICA currently sources from third parties) could begin.

Per the agreement, promoters have to tender the remaining 40% of shares (beyond what AICA acquires via the open offer) to AICA — described as a binding agreement, not a discretionary discussion point.
Aica Kogyo has patented HPL technology that will be introduced into Stylam's India operations within 2-3 months as part of the SHA.

Once the deal and remaining legalities (targeted around mid-June) are completed, management plans to sit down with AICA/Kogyo to explore how each can help grow export and domestic business, including possible plant-level synergies.

subsections.label: War-related and macro risks
points: An ongoing geopolitical 'war situation' is cited repeatedly as the source of raw material cost pressure (crude oil, Middle East-linked commodities) and market unpredictability, causing management to give conservative guidance.

If elevated oil prices and sea freight rate increases persist through the whole of CY2026, EBITDA margin impact is expected to be limited to plus/minus 1-2%, offset partly by 2-3% EBITDA cushion from operating leverage on new revenue and 3-5% additional profitability from favorable EUR/USD exchange rates.
Indian diesel and petrol prices are expected to increase in coming days if the war continues, which would have broader personal and business-level impact.
Customers are aware of cost pressures and are requesting patience ('just wait, maybe war will finish') rather than resisting price increases outright.
US tariff review is a live uncertainty, potentially changing around 1st July under a 150-day Supreme Court-linked rule.

Market volatility referenced qualitatively by management (e.g., unpredictability tied to global political developments) as a reason they cannot make firm long-term predictions on stake retention or deal outcomes.

subsections.label: Clarifying guidance figures
points: Management clarified that the INR250-300 crore new plant revenue figure for FY27 is a 'rough' base figure derived from utilization assumptions, and the 20-25% overall growth figure is also a rough estimate based on this year's actuals plus expected growth — not an exact number for FY27 close.

Management could not reconcile precisely why INR300 crore incremental revenue from the new plant alone would exceed a 25% overall growth guide, stating both figures were rough approximations rather than precisely modeled numbers.
Margin profile of the new plant is expected to follow the same pattern as guided previously (22-24%).
By FY28, assuming no drastic adverse events, company could deliver an ~22% EBITDA margin, per management's directional confirmation.
Next big capex/expansion plan beyond the current new plant will be communicated in the 'next quarter' call, according to management.

themes.note: Domestic operations restructured over past 3 months under new management focus; brand awareness is high but confidence needs rebuilding, with visible impact expected in 2-3 quarters.

themes.label: Acrylics ramp-up
themes.note: Acrylics underperformed in FY26 (INR15 crore) but targeted to grow to INR50-70 crore in FY27, potentially aided by AICA Japan sourcing.

key_takeaways: Third greenfield laminate plant at Manak Tabra expected to start commercial production by end-June to early-July, delayed due to Supreme Court-mandated Environment Clearance requirement.
New plant expected to contribute INR300-400 crores revenue in FY27, ramping to INR600-700 crores in FY28, and potentially INR900-1,000 crores at peak utilization.
Laminate division capacity utilization was 74% in FY26; new plant utilization guided at 30-40% from Q2 FY27, reaching 80%+ within 2 years.
Overall company revenue growth guided at 20-25% for FY27; margin profile of new plant expected at 22-24%, in line with prior guidance.
Gross margin was 49% in Q4 FY26; management indicated some quarter-to-quarter variability is possible.
Acrylics segment, which underperformed with only INR15 crores turnover in FY26, is targeted to reach INR50-70 crores in FY27, aided by potential AICA Japan sourcing.
Post open-offer completion with AICA (Aica Kogyo, Japan), management structure remains unchanged; AICA is a strategic partner with no operational role, though a put option exists under the SHA.
Export vs domestic revenue mix was 75%/25% in FY26 and is expected to remain similar in FY27, with domestic share being actively built up.
Total capex incurred on the new plant stands at INR334 crores, funded without associated debt instalments or interest.
pressing_questions: What is the exact pendency now for the new plant given repeated delays (from November to March to June/July)?

So, I think the math is not really matching because INR300 crores anyway gives much more than 25% growth in FY27. So, if you can just put more color around that, that would be good.

PNGJL.about: Established in 1832, P. N. G Jewellers Ltd is in the retail business of gold, silver, and diamond jewellery[1]

quarters.summary: Q1 FY27 was the company's highest ever first quarter, with revenue up 41% YoY to INR2,413 crore, EBITDA up 57% YoY to INR192.4 crore (8% margin) and PAT up 52% YoY to INR105.3 crore (4.4% margin), despite record gold prices. Management reiterated FY27 store expansion plans (~25 new stores taking network to ~103), reaffirmed EBITDA margin guidance (~7% for FY27, with a comment on ~7% EBITDA margin target being tracked), targeted PAT margin of 4.1%-4.25% (underlying, ex-hedging gains) for FY27 and 4.5%-4.7% by FY29, and laid out a three-year store network and deleveraging roadmap (177 stores and debt below INR1,000 crore by FY29).
