subsections.label: Gross margin drivers
points: Year-over-year gross margin appears flat, but this is because hedging gains are shown separately; adjusted gross margin (net of hedging gains) increased by ~40-50 bps YoY.

Studded jewellery has a materially different (higher) margin compared to plain gold/metal jewellery; with a studded ratio of 10-11%, the retail gross margin target is 12.5%-13.5%, and considering bars & coins mix, overall gross margin should be between 13%-14%.

Hedging gain last year was on a lower retail base while this year's similar hedging gain sits on a bigger base, which mutes the visible YoY margin improvement despite mix shift toward jewellery/retail.

New territories (UP, Central India) currently contribute only ~3% of overall retail mix; margin gains from mix shift will become more visible as these regions' share of retail grows over the next couple of years.

subsections.label: Other expenses discipline
points: Other expenses grew only 5% versus revenue growth of 41%, due to a conservative approach on incremental spend amid early-quarter demand uncertainty in the industry.
Scheme redemption discount share was lower this quarter versus last quarter, reducing other expenses.
Marketing spend was kept conservative; ~250-300 hoardings were cut versus last year, keeping marketing cost within the 1.5% target.
No new stores were opened in the quarter, so there was no associated travel or launch-related expense.

Expenses are expected to rise in Q3/Q4 in line with planned store expansion, but management remains confident of delivering the annual EBITDA guidance within a slightly higher but comparable cost base.
Full-year other expenses guided at ~3% of total sales, translating to approximately INR400 crore for the year.

Last year's elevated other expenses (~INR500 crore+) were driven by one-time items: UP launch and new celebrity endorsement spend (~INR40-50 crore), one-time marketing campaigns (e.g., anniversary/foundation day sale campaigns), and the one-time Pethwa branding campaign for Central India; these one-time expenses are expected to be largely neutralized this year.
Crossing the INR10,000 crore revenue milestone last year triggered gratitude sales that also inflated last year's other expenses base.

subsections.label: Other income
points: Other income is primarily interest income on fixed deposits; the decline from Q4 FY26 (corrected to INR12 crore, not INR31 crore) to Q1 FY27 (INR10 crore) reflects a reduction in FD balances placed on mortgage.
Funds redeemed from FDs are now sitting partly as cash on the balance sheet and partly deployed as margin money for hedging.

subsections.label: Borrowings and deleveraging
points: Total borrowings (ex-GML) at ~INR1,200 crore are broadly in line with March levels, no major movement.
GML utilization is INR300-400 crore against banking limits.
Plan to reduce total loan (INR1,500-1,550 crore) by INR500-600 crore by FY29, bringing it below INR1,000 crore, with an ambition to be debt-free within the next four to five years.

subsections.label: Capital allocation
points: Capital allocation for the year will remain focused on high-return store expansion, strengthening the franchise network, digital investments, and operational excellence.

subsections.label: Demand drivers
points: Indian jewellery industry remained resilient April-June despite record gold prices; demand supported by weddings and an outstanding Akshaya Tritiya.
Customers continued to gravitate towards lightweight jewellery, studded products, and old gold exchange trends, favoring trusted organized players with strong brand and transparent pricing.

Adhik Maas did not drive a big turnout this year, primarily due to silver prices hovering at a high level (silver being the item typically sought after during Adhik Maas); Adhik Maas saw routine sales, not a standout season.
The additional month (Adhik Maas) postponed weddings, which are expected to benefit Q2 and a large portion of Q3.

subsections.label: Retail vs franchise vs e-commerce mix
points: Broad-based revenue growth across retail, franchise, and e-commerce; retail growth driven by 46% SSSG.

E-commerce growth of 20% reflects continued traction across marketplaces, the D2C platform and digital initiatives, though the company has consciously decided to focus e-commerce more on jewellery (studded and plain gold) rather than bars and coins, which may slow overall e-com sales while improving margins.

Franchise revenue growth of 8% is muted partly due to timing/accounting effects: an initial 100% stock-turn is booked when a franchise starts (since the company stocks it up and gets paid), and subsequent replenishment happens weekly or as required, creating timing differences between when franchise partners pay and when stock is fully sold (franchise sales are booked as B2B, not B2C).

Franchise economics are becoming a growing area of focus; company is gaining access to franchise partners' systems to monitor B2C environment and customer demand more closely, expecting better economics to become visible.

subsections.label: Bars & coins / retail categorization
points: 'Bars and coins' in retail refers to what is sold at store counters, with average ticket value less than 5 grams; over 50% of these purchases convert into jewellery, making this a productive sale channel.
The separate 'Others' category in segmental reporting is primarily corporate/bulk sales to companies, a small/minuscule number.
Going forward, three reporting categories will be used: retail (of which ~78-79% jewellery, 20-21% bars & coins), franchise, and e-commerce.

subsections.label: Litestyle format merchandise mix
points: Litestyle was originally launched with ~80% gold inventory and only 15-18% studded; through experience the company realized studded mix needs to increase.
Merchandise mix is being reworked to eventually reach 80% studded inventory and 20% gold inventory at the store level, enabling a 50-60% studded ratio.
Once studded mix increases, litestyle margins are expected to converge toward industry levels of 30-35%, versus the current 18-20% gross margin.
Litestyle studded ratio was 32.9% in Q1 FY27, and per a later comment has moved to ~34% currently, doubling expectation over the next 12 months.
Litestyle plans to grow store count to 65-70 by March 2029 and to a long-term target of 100 stores over the next few years.

subsections.label: Expansion approach and geographic footprint
points: Q2 will see a few launches, while the bulk of expansion is planned across Q3 and Q4 through a franchise-led approach across both legacy and litestyle formats.
Expansion is deepening presence in Maharashtra while expanding reach in Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Central India, and NCR.
This year's plan is to expand more on the FOCO (franchise) channel because last year expansion was more weighted to COCO; the next two years will be a combination of COCO and FOCO.

New store site selection uses a catchment-area framework: expansion is planned strategically based on customer base in the catchment area, and a minimum distance/guideline framework is used so that COCO and franchise stores in similar territories serve different catchments and do not cannibalize each other's sales; some natural cannibalization is expected but is factored in as new stores also address new customers.

UP expansion is on track per prior guidance on stock turn and studded mix projections; some UP stores are only three to four months old, but older stores are also on track; UP markets have accepted the brand well.
A new store is planned soon in Ayodhya.

Store count stood at 78 at end of Q1 FY27 (57 COCO, 21 FOCO), with plans to add 25 stores in FY27 to reach 103 (63 COCO), 37 more in FY28 to reach 140 (86 COCO, 54 FOCO), and 37 more in FY29 to reach 177 stores by March 2029 (113 legacy, 64 litestyle; 75 COCO, 40 FOCO).

New franchise plans include 10 legacy-format and 5 litestyle-format franchises in FY27, with 8-10 new franchises opening in UP this financial year; UP's studded mix is running upwards of 18%, above the originally projected 15%.

subsections.label: Inventory ratio normalization
points: The higher historical stock-turn ratio (~7-8x, two years ago) was primarily due to refinery sale and heavy B2B sale activity; after ending refinery sale and B2B sales, the ratio has rationalized to the previously guided stabilized range of 3.5x to 4x (currently ~4x).

subsections.label: Competitive positioning
points: Company is gaining market share from competition in Maharashtra; the unorganized segment is moving fast towards organized players, bringing in a lot of new customers.
CRM is actively working to ensure a healthy share of new customer acquisition and deeper engagement with the existing customer base.

subsections.label: Promoter shareholding / QIP plan
points: Promoter shareholding above 75% is seen as a potential overhang on the stock; the company has an enabling board resolution in place and is monitoring the market to come up with a QIP at a suitable time to bring shareholding to the desired level.

subsections.label: Gold price and margin volatility
points: Record/elevated gold prices were a backdrop for the quarter, though demand remained resilient.
Company follows a conservative spend approach when facing periods of potential demand softness in the industry.

subsections.label: Adhik Maas / seasonal calendar impact
points: Silver prices hovering at a high level dampened the usual Adhik Maas silver-buying turnout this year.

subsections.label: Overall guidance reaffirmation
points: Despite elevated gold prices, performance remains in line with previously communicated guidance.

Company remains confident of delivering sustainable growth throughout FY2027, supported by a 194-year-old legacy, disciplined execution, growing pan-India presence, and continued formalization of the jewellery industry.
Management remains confident of delivering the guided EBITDA within a slightly higher but comparable cost base in Q3/Q4, even as expenses are expected to rise with planned store expansion.
Target PAT margin of ~4.2% (range 4.1-4.25%) for FY27, rising to 4.5-4.7% by FY29; full year EBITDA margin guidance ~7%.
Full year other expenses guidance of ~3% of total sales (~INR400 crore), representing an ~INR100 crore reduction versus last year; marketing cost guided at 1.5% of sales.
FY26 saw a 50-60 bps net profit margin benefit from inventory/hedging gains, with underlying PAT margin ex one-time gains at 3.2-3.3%.

subsections.label: Hedging progression plan
points: Intent is to be fully hedged for the next financial year; hedging ratio had come down due to margin increase but has recovered to 70%+; Q2 target is ~80%, aiming for 80% by Q3 FY27 (before Diwali), with the aim to be fully hedged (90-100%) next year (FY28).

key_takeaways: PNG delivered a revenue of INR2,413 crores, up 41% year-over-year. EBITDA grew 57% year-over-year to INR192.4 crores, with the EBITDA margin at 8%, while profit after tax grew 52% year-over-year to INR105.3 crores, with a PAT margin at 4.4%.
Festive sales growing 80.3% year-over-year to INR251.4 crores.
We ended the quarter with 78 stores. Looking ahead, we remain committed to opening around 25 stores during FY2027, taking our network to approximately 103 stores by the year-end.

Consolidated revenue from operations grew 41% year-on-year to INR2,413 crore, driven by broad-based growth across retail, franchise, and e-commerce. Retail grew 56% on the back of 46% SSSG. Franchise grew 8% and e-commerce grew 20%.

Gross profit for the quarter stood at INR319.6 crores with a gross margin of 13.2%. EBITDA stood at INR192.4 crores, up 57% year-on-year, with EBITDA margin expanding 80 bps to 8%. Profit after tax stood at INR105.3 crores, up 52% year-on-year, with PAT margin up 40 bps to 4.4%.

Retail studded ratio improved to 10.9% from 9.9% in the previous quarter, with our recently launched stores in North and Central India already running stud ratios of 15% to 18%... while Litestyle by PNG posted a stud ratio of 32.9%.
53% of gold bars and coins purchases converting into jewellery this quarter, up from 46% in the last year.
Despite elevated gold prices, our performance remains in line with our previously communicated guidance.

quarters.summary: Q4 and full year FY26 saw PNG cross INR10,000 crore revenue milestone (FY26 revenue INR10,739 crore, +40% YoY) though Q4 gross/EBITDA margins dipped YoY and QoQ due to a mix shift toward low-margin gold bars & coins, discounting on Foundation/Gratitude Day, and franchise mix; management reiterated FY26 guidance was met (12% gross margin, 6.6% EBITDA margin, 3.8% PAT margin) and raised FY27 guidance to INR13,500 crore revenue with EBITDA margin of 7-7.5% and PAT margin of 4%, expecting the bars/coins mix to normalize back to ~25% as import duty hikes and PM's appeal shift demand from gold-as-investment to gold-for-jewellery/old-for-new exchange.

subsections.label: Margin dilution drivers - Q4 YoY
points: Gross margin dilution of 230 bps (2.3%) in Q4 FY26 vs Q4 FY25 attributed to three factors.

Factor 1: higher share of gold bars and coins in sales mix (28% in Q4FY25 to 40% in Q4FY26, value from INR450 crore to INR1,400 crore) contributed ~150 bps decline, as this segment operates on a structurally thin spread; driven by consumer shift of gold from consumption to investment.
All gold bar and coin sales are purely B2C to customers; there is no refinery or B2B business.
Factor 2: 1% lowering in studded jewellery mix, a one-time impact due to Foundation Day and Gratitude Day offers involving heavy discounting on gold making charges.
Factor 3: marketing promotion and trade discounts in excess of INR50 crore for Gudi Padwa, Foundation Day and Gratitude Day offers, impacting margins.
Despite Q4 dip, full year gross margin estimate of ~12% and PAT level of 3.75-4% was maintained.

subsections.label: Margin dilution drivers - Q4 vs Q3 FY26
points: Franchise sale proportion increased by ~INR200 crore in Q4 as five new franchises were added; franchise gross margins are in the 2.5-3% range, contributing to the margin dip vs Q3.
Gold bars and coin sales increased from INR1,100 crore in Q3 to INR1,400 crore in Q4, further pressuring margins.
Studded ratio declined by 1% quarter-on-quarter, negatively impacting margins.
Gain from unhedged portion of sales was INR45 crore in Q3 FY26 versus INR20 crore in Q4 FY26 (and INR7.4 crore in Q4 FY25), a further factor behind the margin dip.

subsections.label: Hedging strategy
points: Monthly sales average ~600 kg of gold; inventory held ~2,000 kg.
Hedging stood at 67% as of Q4 FY26 versus 55-57% in Q4 FY25 - an improvement of 10-12 percentage points.
Hedged gold quantity at end of March 2026 was 1,300 kg (67% of the ~2,000 kg... consistent with monthly sales-based coverage).
Full-year FY26 average hedging was around 60%, gradually rising from 57% in Q4 FY25 to 63% in Q3 FY26 to 67% in Q4 FY26.
Plan to increase hedging further to 75-80% (potentially up to 80%) in FY27 to eliminate margin volatility.
High margin/premium costs on MCX (15-20%) previously created a cash burden that discouraged full hedging, as blocking funds there would trap capital needed for operations.
Gains from the unhedged portion of sales have declined as hedging increased (INR7.4 crore in Q4FY25, INR45 crore in Q3FY26, INR20 crore in Q4FY26).

subsections.label: Credit rating upgrade
points: Long-term credit rating upgraded to A+ stable from A during the quarter; short-term rating reaffirmed at A1.

Upgrade reflects continued strengthening of business profile, healthy financial position, and disciplined approach to capital and debt management, enhancing ability to access capital at competitive terms.

subsections.label: Comparison with industry peers
points: Big/leading industry players also reported gross margin drops of ~600 bps for Q4 FY26 vs Q4 FY25, a similar trajectory to PNG, attributed by management to the same product-mix change (gold investment demand).

subsections.label: QIP and promoter shareholding
points: Enabling board resolution for QIP is valid till end of August; company has not yet decided to proceed given a good year and self-sufficient business, but may explore it depending on market conditions.
Promoter shareholding reduction to 75% requirement has a compliance timeline until September 2027 (listed September 2024, three-year window).

subsections.label: Retail segment drivers
points: Retail growth of 51% YoY to INR8,131 crore for FY26 led by healthy same-store sales growth of 43%, driven by wedding and festival demand, improved product mix, and contribution from newly added stores.

subsections.label: E-commerce
points: E-commerce delivered 105% YoY growth reflecting increasing digital adoption and rising consumer preference for convenience-led jewellery purchases; company continues to strengthen digital capabilities to enhance customer engagement and accessibility.

subsections.label: Franchisee model
points: Franchisee segment grew 83% YoY to INR1,292 crore driven by store expansion and healthy traction across existing operational markets.
Franchise-led model supports asset-light expansion strategy while strengthening brand reach across diverse geographies.

subsections.label: Volume growth
points: Despite the sharp run in gold prices, positive traction in volume was seen: gold volume grew 27% YoY, silver volumes rose 37% YoY, diamond volumes rose 125% YoY in Q4.

subsections.label: LiteStyle business

subsections.label: Import duty and gold investment demand
points: Increase in customs duty on gold and advance authorisation scheme announced; advance authorisation applies mainly to exporters and is not applicable to PNG since its business is purely domestic.

Import duty increase is directly passed on to consumers, so it will not impact margins directly, but may reduce demand for bars and coins (lower-margin) and push interest toward gold jewellery via exchange of old jewellery for new.
Elevated gold bar and coin sales in Q4 reflected a temporary demand shift toward gold as investment rather than consumption, further elevated by the prevailing geopolitical situation.

With the Prime Minister's appeal and the import duty increase, consumer behaviour is expected to gradually shift toward exchanging old gold for new jewellery, with bars/coins demand expected to eventually flow into jewellery demand as conditions stabilise.
Management views the Q4 gross margin impact as largely one-time and mix-driven, not structural.
Industry-wide effort underway to discourage B2C gold coin sales above 5 grams, encouraging lightweight jewellery and old-for-new exchange.
Peer/industry-wide gross margin declines of ~600 bps in Q4 FY26 vs Q4 FY25 suggest a sector-wide impact from the same gold-investment demand mix shift, not company-specific competitive weakness.

It is still early to fully assess the overall impact of the evolving import duty situation; company continues to calibrate its strategy accordingly and may update FY27 guidance next quarter if required.

key_takeaways: FY26 marks the year in which we crossed INR10,000 crores of revenue, a milestone for the first time, reporting a full year consolidated revenue of INR10,739 crores, a growth of 40% year-over-year.
The total consolidated revenue grew by 123% year-over-year to INR3,544 crores [in Q4], a clear reflection of the strong festive and continued demand across each of our core business segments.

There was a gross margin dilution of almost 2.3%, 230 basis points [in Q4 FY26 vs Q4 FY25], primarily due to higher share of gold bars and coins in the overall sales mix, a 1% lowering in studded jewellery mix, and marketing promotion and trade discounts in excess of INR50 crores.
The share of gold bars and coin sales in the overall revenue mix rose 28% in Q4 FY25 to 40% in Q4 FY26.
The company remains committed to the gross margin guidance of around 12 to 13% with the EBITDA of 7 to 7.5% and a PAT of 4%.
During Q4 FY26, we added 12 new stores... taking our total store count to 78 as of March 31st, 2026. On a full year basis, we added 25 new stores.
Our hedging as we speak, as of Q4, was around 67%... we have increased the hedging by 10 to 12%.
We are currently maintaining a guidance of INR13,500 crores revenue along with an EBITDA margin of 7% to 7.5% and a PAT margin of 4% for FY27.
During the quarter, our long-term credit rating was upgraded to A+ stable from A, while the short-term rating was reaffirmed at A1.
pressing_questions: The clarification that the management has provided for the margin drop - quite a few reasons appear more structural than one-off (discounts likely to repeat, new market discounts likely to continue, franchisee share likely to inch up as more FOCO stores open) - can you elaborate on why we think of them as one-offs?

The peers in the industry have reported their gross margins and EBITDA in the normal range as compared to Q3 - what has led specifically to the decline on our side? Is it competition or low demand in the jewellery segment?

key_takeaways: We delivered a healthy 13.7% year-on-year growth in revenue to INR169.7 crores in Q1 FY27. The underlying demand environment continues to remain stable across our key markets. However, the quarter was impacted by a very sharp increase in styrene-based raw material prices.
The average styrene-based raw material price was around INR135 at the beginning of Q4 FY26, which increased at its peak to approximately INR225 in Q1 FY27. That's almost a 65% increase in prices.

As a result, we saw an effective price realization of around 5% in Q1. From Q2 onwards, we expect the full price increase of approximately 9% to be reflected as the earlier price orders progressively roll off and the revised OEM pricing starts flowing through.
We expect EBITDA margins to improve to between 14% to 15% in Q2 FY27 and reach the normal state of 18% to 20% on a run rate basis by Q4 '27, subject to raw material prices remaining broadly stable.
Our first phase of 1.5 million helmets of additional annual capacity is progressing as planned and is expected to become operational beginning October and September.
Our engagement with Decathlon is progressing well, and commercial production is expected to commence from October.

Once our Italy operations become fully functional in October 2026, we will be much closer to the customer... rather than asking a distributor to forecast demand several months in advance, we can increasingly move towards a more responsive and just-in-time supply model.

Consolidated revenue stood at INR169.7 crores. EBITDA for the quarter stood at INR19.6 crores with a margin, EBITDA margin of 11.5%. PAT for the quarter stood at INR12.3 crores with a PAT margin of 7.2%.

quarters.summary: Management guided to FY27 revenue growth of ~17-18% with EBITDA margins broadly similar to FY26, though Q1 FY27 is expected to see gross margin pressure from raw material inflation before recovering in subsequent quarters. Capacity is being expanded by 3 million units (1.5mn by Q2 FY27, another 1.5mn over subsequent 15-18 months) taking installed capacity from ~9.25mn to over 12mn units (~33% increase over FY26), and exports (currently 20% of revenue) are targeted to reach 23-24% in FY27 and ~30% in 2-3 years, supported by a new Italy-based warehousing/distribution subsidiary.

subsections.label: Margin Drivers
points: Gross margins remained relatively stable despite rising raw material prices; 8-9% price hike expected to largely offset material cost increases on a full-year basis.

Material prices are volatile; if RM prices remained at peak levels for the full year, the 8-9% hike would not be sufficient, but management has already seen drops in material prices in the last two weeks and expects further drops.
Q1 FY27 expected to see gross margin pressure; subsequent quarters expected to see margin recovery/expansion as material costs ease relative to price hikes taken.

Gross margin expansion from 48% (FY23) to ~60% (FY26) attributed primarily to two factors: product mix shift (higher share of SMK premium brand and exports) and material cost decline (FY23 had shipping crisis and higher material prices).
Over the last two years, material prices have not changed significantly, yet gross margins still improved, indicating mix-driven improvement.

EBITDA margin differential: SMK is ~10 percentage points higher than STUDDS brand (e.g., if STUDDS EBITDA is 17%, SMK would be ~27%); export margins are similar to SMK since most exports are SMK-driven, hence export margins are also ~10pp higher than domestic.

If current raw material price hike (post-drop from peak) sustains for the full year, an additional 2-2.5% price increase would be needed to fully offset it, though management does not expect this scenario.

Previously (credit rating report ~2 years ago) it was projected that crossing INR 750 crores turnover would trigger operating leverage taking EBITDA margin to 22-23% (as seen in FY19-20), but management does not expect to reach 22-23% this year due to current raw material price pressure; however, better margins than last year are expected over a 12-month horizon as SMK and exports (higher-margin businesses) continue to grow.

subsections.label: Capital Allocation
points: Board approved formulation and implementation of an Employee Stock Option Plan (ESOP) for eligible employees of Studds Accessories Limited and its subsidiary companies (India and overseas), subject to shareholder approval at the ensuing AGM.
Board recommended a dividend of INR 3 per equity share (face value INR 5) for FY26, translating to a 60% payout.

subsections.label: Other Expenses Commentary
points: Q4 other expenses included some marketing spend (not event-related) and a gratuity calculation adjustment linked to a wage change in Haryana effective 1st April; other miscellaneous expense heads and slight interest-on-taxes impact also contributed, though not substantial; detailed head-wise split to be shared later.

subsections.label: Portfolio Mix Transformation
points: STUDDS core brand continues to operate at large volumes, growing steadily at ~3% CAGR from 68.7 lakh units (FY24) to 72.6 lakh units (FY26), reflecting brand resilience, distribution network strength, and relevance across mass and mid segments.

SMK volumes have grown at an exceptional ~52% CAGR, reflecting growing acceptance of premium products globally, strengthening international brand positioning, and ability to compete in technologically advanced, design-led categories; SMK is evolving into a powerful premium global brand and becoming the company's growth engine.

Private label business has scaled at ~22% CAGR, opening new opportunities for partnerships with internationally recognized brands, deepening export market presence, and strengthening manufacturing capabilities and product quality standards.

Overall volumes grew from 71 lakh to 77.4 lakh units (~4.4% CAGR) despite a relatively mature industry environment; growth accompanied by improvements in product mix and premiumization supporting ASP growth and profitability.

STUDDS will continue to provide scale stability and domestic market leadership, while SMK and private labels will increasingly drive premiumization, exports, ASP expansion, and overall value creation.

subsections.label: ASP Trends
points: SMK ASP grew from INR 2,359 (FY24-25) to INR 2,552 (FY25-26), roughly an 8-10% increase.
Private label ASP (largest brand, O'Neal) grew from INR 1,831 (FY24-25) to INR 1,918 (FY25-26).
ASPs across SMK and white-labeling expected to grow further given a 9-10% price increase taken in export markets from 1st April.
Blended ASP (domestic + exports) rose from INR 752 (Q3 FY26) to INR 815 (Q4 FY26).

subsections.label: Innovation Pipeline
points: Innovation remains core to strategy; 5 new products launched across helmet segment in FY26, along with more than 50 new graphics designed.
Plan to launch 6 more products in FY27, with continued focus on refreshing the portfolio with modern designs, enhanced safety features, and premium styling aligned with evolving consumer preferences.

subsections.label: New Category Expansion — Riding Accessories
points: Company is in advanced stages of prototype development for riding jackets and external Bluetooth communication systems for helmets.
Commercial sales of these new products anticipated to begin from H2 FY27, aimed at strengthening the premium product portfolio and increasing consumer engagement across categories.

subsections.label: Certifications
points: Company holds certifications specific to various export markets, including Brazilian certification and Indonesian certification; has recently applied for Sri Lankan certification.

European and American homologation together cover an estimated 70-80% of the world's certification requirements, but larger markets like Brazil and Indonesia require their own country-specific certifications.

subsections.label: Capacity Expansion Plan
points: Company on track to increase manufacturing capacity by 1.5 million units by Q2 FY27; a second phase of an additional 1.5 million units is expected over the subsequent 15-18 months.
With both phases completed, total installed capacity increases from ~9.25 million units to over 12 million units, a nearly 33% increase compared to FY26 levels.
New capacities will become operational only in the second half of the year, so full benefits are expected to accrue gradually over time.

The stated 12 million capacity figure assumes a 50% painted / 50% unpainted product mix; capacity is fungible — if more unpainted or non-graphic helmets are produced, effective capacity would be higher (unpainted helmets require less processing time than complex graphic variants, allowing enhanced production efficiency).

subsections.label: Manufacturing Flexibility
points: High fungibility and flexibility of manufacturing operations allow dynamic optimization of throughput depending on product mix and manufacturing complexity.
Flexible manufacturing setup enables shifting production between STUDDS and SMK products in response to real-time market demand trends.

subsections.label: Europe Subsidiary — Italy (relocated from Spain)
points: Company is setting up a subsidiary in Italy (originally planned in Spain) to function as a warehousing and distribution hub, reducing transit times, improving supply responsiveness, and serving European customers more efficiently; also addresses markets with currently limited direct presence.
Warehouse location will be Reggio Emilia, near Parma — centrally located in Italy to minimize transportation costs for a dealer-direct model.

Reason for switching from Spain to Italy: Spain already has a strong second-largest distributor who felt cannibalization risk from a direct company warehouse/subsidiary there; distributor committed to keep more inventory and serve the market better, so company will continue via distributor model in Spain.

Italy did not have a direct importer (was fed through a Dutch distributor with small volumes) despite being one of the top 2 markets in Europe, making it a better candidate for a dealer-direct warehousing model.

Incorporation documents for the Italy subsidiary have been signed and are expected to arrive within 2-3 days; warehousing arrangement being set up with a third-party 3PL; operations expected to start mid-Q2 FY27, with sales beginning from that sector at that time.
Distributors in other regions are expected to continue buying from India (avoiding warehousing costs in Italy), though some may buy directly from the Italy warehouse.

subsections.label: Export Market Expansion
points: Key growth countries for FY27 export focus: Colombia (already strong), Mexico, USA, Italy (moving to dealer-direct model via own warehouse), Turkey, Sri Lanka, Indonesia, and Philippines.

New distributors appointed in the last six months: a chain with 1,200 retail stores in Mexico (largest in the country), a new distributor in Turkey (appointed this month), and a distributor in England (appointed a couple of quarters ago).

Domestic and international market supply for helmets globally is dominated by four manufacturing hubs: Indonesia, India, China, and Vietnam; Mexico currently has no significant internal helmet manufacturing; across Latin America (except Brazil and one company in Colombia) there is minimal local manufacturing.

Management does not expect entry into many large new countries going forward since presence already exists in most large markets; future growth will come from deeper penetration of existing markets given large untapped market size (e.g., Mexico ~2.5 million unit market, company share <1%).

subsections.label: Domestic Distribution Strategy
points: Domestically, only a couple of new distributors were added in FY26; strategy is not to add many distributors but to penetrate deeper with current distributor network to protect partner profitability and avoid price wars.
New distributors will be appointed selectively (perhaps one or two per year) only where markets are identified as underpenetrated.

subsections.label: Seasonality
points: Sales seasonality has been consistent for the last 2-3 years at approximately 45-47% in H1 and 53-55% in H2; the main driver is that people prefer wearing helmets more in winter (H2) than in hot summer months (H1), though the effect is not highly significant.

subsections.label: Organized vs Unorganized Market Shift
points: A massive structural shift from unorganized to organized helmet market is underway in India, driven by stricter safety regulation enforcement; current raw material cost pressure period is expected to accelerate this shift as smaller unorganized players may be unable to absorb cost increases and may shut down.
Current estimated unorganized market share is ballpark 20-30% (not more than 30%, not less than 20%); expected to trim down to about 10-15% over the next 2-3 years.

subsections.label: Inventory Increase Drivers
points: Inventory days increased year-on-year, attributed to an additional warehouse set up in Faridabad, India during the year.
Higher inventory levels also linked to increasing sales in the US market requiring higher stock there.
Management considers 85-90 days of inventory a comfortable, sustainable level going forward.

subsections.label: Industry Backdrop
points: Global two-wheeler industry evolving due to rising urbanization, increasing mobility needs, growing rider safety awareness, and premiumization trend across riding gear and accessories.
Premium motorcycle ecosystem, motorsports culture, and adventure touring segments expanding steadily, creating long-term opportunities for branded helmet and riding accessory companies.

India remains one of the largest and fastest growing two-wheeler markets globally, supported by rising disposable income, increasing penetration of premium motorcycles, stricter safety regulations, and greater consumer awareness towards quality and branded products.
Industry is gradually shifting from an unorganized, price-driven market to a more branded, premium and safety-focused ecosystem.

subsections.label: Competitive Response to Price Hikes
points: All brands across the industry have taken price increases in response to raw material cost pressure; some brands have taken increases even higher than the company's 8-9%.
China has implemented price increases for all OEM customers as well, reflecting a broad-based industry response depending on inventory levels carried by different players.

No demand pressure observed post price hikes as of the call date; dealers and customers reportedly expected a larger price increase given known cost pressures, and management noted it has never reduced prices historically to avoid getting caught in a 'catch-22' position if costs later fall.

subsections.label: Motorsports & Brand Building
points: Recently hired a dedicated racing manager to strengthen international racing ecosystem presence and enhance SMK's global brand visibility.

Participated in the Moto4 Latin America Cup through SMK helmets, hosted alongside the MotoGP World Championship in Goiânia, Brazil, as part of the FIM Latin America Road to MotoGP development program — positioning SMK within the global racing ecosystem.

Moto4 participation is the starting step toward eventual entry into MotoGP (progression path: Moto4 → Moto3/Moto2/SBK → MotoGP); plan is to enter MotoGP in calendar year 2028, with calendar year 2027 focused on other motorcycling events like SBK (already has four races), Moto2, and Moto3.

Currently sponsoring/working with 10-15 riders including in the Italian Championship kids' circuit, aiming to build brand loyalty with young riders (age 10-12) over a ~10-year horizon so that by the time they reach MotoGP (around age 20), they have grown up using the company's helmets.

subsections.label: Leadership Change
points: Mr. Bharat Goyal, currently VP Finance and Investor Relations, has been appointed Chief Financial Officer of the company effective 1st July 2026, recognizing his role in strengthening financial processes and strategic planning initiatives.

subsections.label: Non-Motorized Helmet / Decathlon Engagement
points: Company continues to strengthen brand-building initiatives on the non-motorized helmet front; progressing well with Decathlon engagement, with initial supplies expected to commence in July 2026.

subsections.label: Long-Term Vision
points: Ambition is to build STUDDS into a globally respected rider safety company with leadership across both scale and premium categories.

Company describes its growth as a structural transformation rather than growth driven by a single product or temporary cycle, based on early recognition of consumer shift toward premium, feature-rich, safety-certified products.

US subsidiary (acquired a couple of years ago) recorded its first profitable year in FY26, illustrating that new subsidiary ventures typically face one to two years of margin pressure before turning profitable — a pattern expected to also apply to the new Italy subsidiary, though at a scale too small to impact the consolidated balance sheet materially.

subsections.label: Raw Material Price Volatility
points: Raw material prices have been on an upward trend since March, though no challenges currently seen in sourcing or availability of key raw materials.

Price increases of 8-9% averaged across portfolio and distribution channels from 1st April 2026 to safeguard margins; management does not expect this to fully offset costs if RM prices stayed at peak levels for the full year, but expects some relief as prices have already started dropping in the last two weeks.

An example cited: a raw material priced at 100 rose to ~150 at peak and has since come back to ~120-125 — not yet back to original November-December pricing; expected to take another 2-3 months to normalize further.

If current (post-drop) RM price levels sustain for the full year, an additional 2-2.5% price increase would be needed to fully offset costs, though management does not expect this scenario to materialize.
Q1 FY27 gross margins expected to face pressure from RM costs before recovering in later quarters.

subsections.label: Unorganized Market Disruption
points: Price pressure from rising raw material costs may not be sustainable for unorganized/smaller players, some of whom may be forced to shut down operations, accelerating the shift toward organized market share.

subsections.label: FY27 Outlook
points: Company remains confident about continuing growth momentum into FY27, with expected revenue growth of ~17-18% while maintaining EBITDA margins at broadly similar levels to FY26.

Management does not expect EBITDA margins to reach the previously projected 22-23% level (as seen in FY19-20) upon crossing INR 750 crores turnover, due to current raw material price pressures, but expects better margins than last year over a 12-month horizon as SMK and export mix continues to grow.
Exports expected to grow from 20% of revenue in FY26 to 23-24% in FY27, and to ~30% within 2-3 years, driven by penetration of existing large markets rather than entry into many new countries.

SRGHFL.about: SRG Housing Finance Ltd, established in 1999, is an NHB-registered housing finance company focused on affordable housing finance for rural and semi-urban borrowers. Products cover home purchase, self-construction, renovation, extension and Loan Against Property (LAP). Company serves 25,000+ customers through 96 branches.[1]

quarters.summary: Management called this special investor/lender clarification call to deny an Economic Times article alleging Rs 400 crore of promoter-linked fund siphoning and NPA/loan-book manipulation, following NHB's Red Flag Account (RFA) classification of the company in September 2026. Management denies all allegations, cites strong capital adequacy (39.21%), 25% quarterly and 33% FY25-26 PAT growth, no history of default, no rating downgrade (Acuite kept rating under watch), stable management, and lender comfort; disbursements/fresh sanctions have been temporarily slowed as a precaution pending completion of the NHB audit (expected to close soon), with normal business expected to resume from Q3/Q4, and the board has approved converting from an HFC to an NBFC for multi-product growth.

subsections.label: Capital strength and repayment history
points: Capital adequacy ratio is 39.21%, more than double the regulatory minimum.
Company has never delayed or defaulted on any instalment of any lender, bank, financial institution, or NHB in its entire history.
Collection and repayment is comfortably more than the obligation; liquidity position is strong to cover all lender obligations.
No slowdown in collections; collections continue to be strong.
Liquidity flow statement has been submitted to the rating agency (Acuite) from March 2020, and separately submitted through next March.

subsections.label: Liquidity buffer explanation
points: Company has always kept liquidity close to it as a management decision since inception, sized to cover future obligations.
Buffer maintained is 2-3 months of repayment obligations; e.g., if monthly collection is Rs 10 crores, buffer held is roughly Rs 30 crores.
Management declined to disclose exact cash/bank/FD balance on the call, stating it would be shared when quarterly results are released.

subsections.label: Rating status
points: No downgrade in credit rating; Acuite has confirmed the rating while keeping it under watch.

subsections.label: Promoter capital commitment
points: Promoters have given personal guarantees to the majority of bank lenders.
Promoters are ready to infuse up to 100% of required capital into the company if the need arises in the future, according to need.
Promoters have increased their stake by 1% recently as a signal of commitment.

subsections.label: Loan book verification
points: More than 15,000 active loan accounts; field verification and KYC process for all these accounts has been completed.
The 25,000 figure referenced in a prior call includes both active (15,000) and previous/closed accounts; KYC has been done for all of these as well.
100% of loans/mortgages are registered in the central registry.
Not a single loan account is promoter-related or given to related parties — management states this figure is zero and has never been company practice.

subsections.label: HFC to NBFC conversion
points: Board has passed a resolution to convert the company from a registered Housing Finance Company (HFC) to a Non-Banking Finance Company (NBFC) to enable work across multiple products and multiple growth avenues in the near future.
Company will continue to do housing finance business even after becoming an NBFC; it is not exiting housing loans.
Management rejected the suggestion of keeping the HFC entity as-is and instead setting up a 100% subsidiary to hold the NBFC license, stating it is not efficient to do the same work in two companies.
This is a future plan; the board has just decided, and the process is expected to take at least 6 months, including obtaining NOCs from stakeholders and further discussions.
Segment/product focus for the new NBFC entity and lender discussions on financing cost implications not yet finalized — management stated it is too early in the process.

subsections.label: Media and regulator engagement
points: Company has emailed the Economic Times formally denying/contesting the information published, stating the reported information is incorrect.
Management is willing to discuss the communication with Economic Times separately/individually with interested stakeholders.
Company will provide written letters/communication to lenders/banks for their audit purposes upon request.

subsections.label: Lender engagement
points: Company held individual meetings with all lenders and their senior officers; each lender wanted to speak individually, and the meetings were satisfactory and comfortable.

Multiple participants (bankers on the call) requested a formal lenders' meet similar to the investor call for better communication and confidence-building; management responded it will consider this ('we will see').

subsections.label: NHB Red Flag Account (RFA) classification
points: NHB classified the company's account as a Red Flag Account (RFA) in September 2026 as part of a routine supervisory/audit process; NHB does not declare fraud via the Red Flag classification itself.
The classification stems from NHB's regular annual audit process, which started in July 2026 and typically runs for around two months.
Regulators do not publicly comment on or disclose supervisory matters of specific entities; this is an internal regulatory process.

Management has not received any formal written communication from NHB specifying the reasons for the red flag or listing specific accounts of concern; communication is ongoing and expected to conclude once the audit closes.
Management's view is that the audit should be completed promptly so the red flag can be removed.
Management denies the media report's claims regarding fictitious/unidentified loan accounts and understated NPAs, stating NHB has not communicated any such findings.

Management has slowed fresh sanctions and disbursements as a precautionary measure during this period; part-disbursement is ongoing but new business is slow, with existing sanctions from banks held pending resolution.
Management does not expect this slowdown to be long-term (5-15 days to about a month characterized in one response), and expects Q2 numbers to reflect the impact, with Q3 and Q4 expected to be good.
No RBI-mandated 90-day online sanction disbursal deadline breach is expected despite the slowdown; management confirmed compliance will be maintained within the timeframe.
No sanction covenant breach, facility recall, or repayment delay has occurred with any lender due to the RFA tagging; no lender has raised a recall.
No repayment acceleration or adjustment made on any account as a result of the situation.
No borrower delays in EMI repayment observed as a result of the news article/panic.

subsections.label: Reputational and media risk
points: An Economic Times article published on 10 September 2026 alleged that Rs 400 crore was siphoned off by promoters to related entities, which management fully denies.

The alleged Rs 400 crore figure represents about one-third of total loan amount and, per management, is practically impossible given the average ticket size (~Rs 12 lakh) and loan book size (~Rs 130 crore over ~5,000 accounts implied in that example, versus total book of Rs 1,100 crore).
Management states every loan is backed by a verified borrower, verified property, and a complete disbursement trail; not a single rupee has ever been transferred to any promoter since inception.

Analysts questioned the motivation/source of the leak, suggesting it may have been shared with the media before the NHB audit process concluded, which management denies came from NHB or any regulator.

Analysts raised industry-wide reputational risk parallels to trust crises in NBFC/HFC/MFI sector previously seen at PNB Housing Finance and DHFL, where erosion of trust caused sharp share price declines (80-90%) and further loan repayment issues due to loss of borrower/lender confidence.

An analyst suggested SRG proactively share periodic collection efficiency and ALM/liquidity data (as some MFI companies did during past sector stress) to reassure stakeholders; management said it will consider the suggestion ('we will pay attention to your suggestion').

subsections.label: Governance stability
points: No member of senior management has resigned in the last 3-4 months; leadership team is stable and committed.
Board is stated to be confident, with no internal issue flagged regarding the company.

key_figures.label: Potential business slowdown duration due to red flag

subsections.label: Near-term business outlook
points: Impact of the disbursement slowdown will be visible in Q2 numbers; Q3 and Q4 expected to be good.
Management expects the NHB audit and red flag matter to be resolved within roughly 1-2 months (some responses indicated 15-20 days to a month).
New sanctions already received from banks will be disbursed once the audit/red flag matter is closed, and business will resume/move ahead with lenders.
There is no shortage of demand in the business; the slowdown is a precautionary, temporary measure, not demand-driven.
Management will get further clarity/details on the reasons for red flag classification and any specific issues only after the NHB audit report is finalized.

guidance_ledger.metric: NHB audit / Red Flag resolution timeline
guidance_ledger.statement: Management expects the NHB audit to be completed and the red flag removed soon, within roughly 15-20 days to 1-2 months.
Impact of the slowed disbursements and fresh sanctions will be visible in Q2 numbers.
Business is expected to normalize and Q3 and Q4 will be good once the audit/red flag issue is resolved.
Profit after tax has grown by 33% in FY2025-26.
Profit after tax has grown by 25% in the quarter.
Promoters are ready to infuse up to 100% of required capital into the company if the need arises in the future.
Board has approved conversion from HFC to NBFC; process expected to take at least 6 months including NOCs from stakeholders.
Management confirmed it will comply with RBI's mandatory 90-day online disbursal requirement for existing sanctions despite the slowdown.
Liquidity position submitted to rating agency is stated to be okay through next March.

risk_register.risk: NHB Red Flag Account (RFA) classification pending audit resolution
risk_register.note: NHB classified the company as RFA in September 2026 as part of routine supervisory audit started in July 2026; audit expected to close in ~1-2 months, after which reasons and any required remediation will become clear.

risk_register.risk: Media allegations of Rs 400 crore fund siphoning to promoter-linked entities
risk_register.note: Economic Times article dated 10 September 2026; fully denied by management as practically impossible given loan book size, average ticket size, and disbursement trail; company has emailed the newspaper disputing the report.

risk_register.risk: Allegations of NPA manipulation and fictitious/unidentified loan accounts
risk_register.note: Management denies these allegations; states loans are backed by verified borrowers/properties and 100% central registry mortgage registration; clarity expected only after audit completes.

risk_register.risk: Slowdown in fresh sanctions and disbursements
risk_register.note: Company has proactively slowed new disbursements/sanctions as a precaution during the audit period, expected to impact Q2 numbers; management frames this as temporary, not demand-driven.

risk_register.risk: Reputational risk / erosion of stakeholder trust
risk_register.note: Analysts drew parallels to past NBFC/HFC/MFI trust crises (PNB Housing Finance, DHFL, MFI sector stress) where loss of trust led to sharp share price declines and repayment issues; management has held individual lender meetings to maintain confidence.

risk_register.risk: Potential regulatory/compliance findings from ongoing NHB audit
risk_register.note: Management could not specify in advance what, if anything, may be flagged in the final audit report; outcome and any corrective steps will be known only post-audit.

risk_register.risk: Operating cost pressure from disbursement slowdown
risk_register.note: Management stated no current shortfall in operations since the slowdown is expected to be short (days to about a month), and full teams will be needed once business resumes.

themes.label: Regulatory scrutiny / NHB Red Flag Account
themes.note: NHB classified SRG as a Red Flag Account in September 2026 as part of a routine annual audit process started in July 2026; resolution expected within 1-2 months.

themes.label: Media allegation / reputational risk
themes.note: Economic Times article alleged Rs 400 crore siphoning to promoter-linked entities and NPA manipulation, fully denied by management as practically impossible.

themes.label: Liquidity and repayment strength
themes.note: Management cites strong capital adequacy (39.21%), 2-3 months liquidity buffer, and a clean repayment history with no lender default ever.

themes.label: Disbursement slowdown as precaution
themes.note: Fresh sanctions/disbursements slowed as a precaution during the audit period, expected to hit Q2 numbers with recovery seen in Q3/Q4; demand itself is not a constraint.

themes.label: Lender and rating agency confidence
themes.note: Individual lender meetings held and deemed comfortable; Acuite kept rating under watch with no downgrade; no covenant breach or recall by any lender.

themes.label: HFC-to-NBFC conversion for diversification
themes.note: Board approved conversion to NBFC to enable multi-product growth while continuing housing finance; process expected to take at least 6 months.

themes.label: Promoter commitment and governance stability
themes.note: Promoters offered to infuse up to 100% capital if needed, increased stake by 1%, given personal guarantees to lenders, and no senior management resignations in recent months.

key_takeaways: We fully deny this news. First, the mentioned Rs 400 crore siphoning-off amount represents about one-third of our total loan amount. We clearly deny this and, in our books, every loan is a verified borrower, verified property and is supported by a complete disbursement trail.
We have more than 15,000 active loan accounts and the field verification and KYC process of all these accounts has been completed.
From the beginning of the company till date, not a single rupee of any promoter has been fund transferred.
The NHB does not declare a fraud in the Red Flag account. This classification has been done in September and we are in communication with the NHB.

As we have already introduced the stock equity process, our board has passed a resolution that the company wants to be converted from its registered housing finance company to its non-banking finance company.
Our capital adequacy ratio is 39.21%, which is more than double the regulatory minimum. Profit after tax has grown by 25% in the quarter and has grown by 33% in the financial 2025-2026 period.
The company has never delayed or defaulted any instalment of any lender, bank, financial institution, or NHB in its entire history from the beginning.
We have now slowed our fresh sanctions and disbursement for some time. You will see the impact of this in the Q2 numbers.
There has been no downgrade in our credit rating. Acuite has confirmed our rating by keeping it under watch.
In the last 3-4 months, no member of our senior management team has resigned. Our leadership team is completely with us, stable and committed.
Our promoters have given personal guarantee to the majority of bank lenders. If the company needs capital, promoters can infuse it in the future.
We have had a meeting with all our lenders and their senior officers. And the meeting was satisfactory and comfortable.
pressing_questions: Jinal Sheth (Awriga Capital): Why was the account red flagged in the first place, and can there be any classification issues from our side? (Management could not confirm reasons before audit completion.)

Harsh Chaurasia (Orbit Exports Family Office): Once the NHB audit is over, can a separate, neutral third-party re-inspection be conducted to validate the book and restore reputation? What are the specifics of the alleged fictitious promoter-related accounts and NPA manipulation? (Management deferred full clarification to post-audit findings.)

Prashant Talpade: Has NHB communicated any reason for the red flag classification, or given any indication on fictitious loan accounts/NPA understatement? (Management stated no such communication received.)

Vaibhav Tiwari (Lighthouse Canton): Given rising stress in Rajasthan (SRG's major segment), how should the evergreening and fictitious book allegations be viewed pending audit? Which specific NBFC product segment will the company target post-conversion, and what lender feedback exists on financing cost implications? (Management said clarity will come only post-audit; NBFC product plan not yet finalized.)

Ravi Purohit (Securities Investment Management): Suggested SRG proactively disclose monthly collection and collection efficiency data (as MFI companies did during past sector stress) to reassure investors given the black-box nature of finance companies and history of trust-driven share price collapses (PNB Housing, DHFL). (Management said it would consider the suggestion.)

Multiple participants (Shivanand - Karnataka Bank; Nihar Jena - Bandhan Bank) requested that management organize a formal lenders' meet similar to the investor call for better communication and confidence-building. (Management responded 'we will see'.)
Yash (RevX Capital): Requested regular disclosure of updated collection efficiency and ALM/liquidity numbers to counter panic-driven EMI non-payment concerns. (Management said 'Let us see'.)
Mohit Wahi (Utkarsh SFB): Asked management to share any response received from Economic Times regarding the company's rebuttal email. (Management agreed to share if/when received.)

SIS.about: Security & Intelligence Serv.(India)is directly and indirectly engaged in rendering security and related services consisting of manned guarding, training, and indirectly engaged in paramedic and emergency response services; loss prevention, asset protection and mobile patrols; facility management services consisting of cleaning, housekeeping and pest control management services in the areas of facility management; cash logistics services consisting of cash-in-transit, ATM cash replenishment activities and secure transportation of precious items and bullion; and alarm monitoring and response services consisting of trading and installation of electronic security devices and systems through its subsidiaries, joint ventures and associates.(Source : 202003-01 Annual Report Page No:101)

quarters.summary: SIS delivered a strong start to FY27 with 29.7% YoY revenue growth and 36.2% YoY EBITDA growth in Q1, and management flagged Labour Codes implementation (rules notified May 8-9, 2026) as a multi-quarter tailwind expected to become EBITDA and PAT accretive over the next 3-4 quarters as minimum wage hikes and pass-throughs take effect. The company approved its fifth buyback (first via the open market route) worth INR106 crore, and reiterated its ambition to be among India's top-100 companies with INR500 crore+ PAT and consistent 15% growth/15%+ return profile, with FY26 and FY27 seen as the first two years of this "15 and 15" run.

subsections.label: Capital allocation / Buyback
points: Board approved the fifth buyback, this time via the open market route (previously all via tender route), taking advantage of SEBI reopening the open market window after a long gap.
SIS is among the first few companies to use the open market buyback window.
Buyback maximum sanctioned price of INR478.50 implies a decent premium to the current trading price.
Buyback scheduled to open the following week from the call date.
Once concluded, cumulative capital returned to shareholders since IPO would exceed INR700 crore.
This is designed for minority shareholders; promoters are not participating.
This marks the ninth occasion of capital return (5 buybacks, 4 dividends) since IPO.

subsections.label: Margin resilience
points: EBITDA above the INR200 crore milestone for another quarter; flat QoQ but up 36.2% YoY, reflecting strength, resilience and scalability of the operating model.
Constant endeavour to improve margin profiles across all segments via focus on customer contract margins and rationalizing SG&A costs.

subsections.label: Return ratios
points: ROCE improved to 16.7% from 14% a year ago; consistently pursuing incrementally higher ROCE as guided.
ROCE bottomed at 11.8% in Q1 FY25 and return on equity was at only 9.4% then; two years later ROCE is 16.7% and ROE is 15.8%.

subsections.label: DSO
points: DSO at 66 days, up 3 days QoQ, but this is not surprising because Q4 is always the best in terms of DSO historically and Q1 typically dips.

key_figures.label: Blended India business EBITDA margin (Security + FM)
Maximum single contract contribution to revenue

subsections.label: India Security
points: Crossed a quarterly revenue milestone for the first time at INR2,004 crore, up 37.3% YoY.

subsections.label: Facility Management (FM)
points: FM EBITDA margin of 5.5% is now normalized to a new zone; management has constantly guided FM margins will be on an upward trajectory.
FM margin improvement journey started from 4% and is now as high as 5.5%; aspirationally should be operating near 6%, but timing uncertain.

subsections.label: International Security
points: Seen a very strong bounce back since last year, reporting highest ever quarterly revenue run rate.
Growth of 31% YoY nominal, 7% on constant currency basis; rupee movement also contributed to the reported growth.

EBITDA margin decline from Q4 to Q1 is on expected lines because Australia's Q4 has historically been the highest due to high-margin events, which fade out in Q1 — consistent with the previous pattern.

subsections.label: A P Securitas (APS) margin trajectory
points: APS is roughly 20% of SIS's size and carries lower margins given its lower scale post-acquisition.
There is a clear path to integration and raising APS margin profile through synergies and cost savings.
On a blended basis, margins are expected to return to SIS's original flagship Security margin levels (around 5.5%) over the next 4 to 8 quarters.
Currently only 51% stake has been acquired in APS; the remaining 49% is to be acquired subsequently, with the anniversary for that being 2028.

subsections.label: Contract diversification
points: SIS handles more than 16,000 different contracts in India, with no single contract contributing more than 1% of revenue, reflecting a highly diversified portfolio with no concentration risk.

subsections.label: Cash business (subsidiary)
points: DRHP has been filed for the Cash business IPO; company holds an active card and cannot disclose the subsidiary's financial performance details.
Waiting for a more opportune time window to list, given the current IPO rush and significant de-rating witnessed among peer comparables.

subsections.label: Updater Services share purchase
points: Management confirmed the purchase of Updater Services shares is a treasury operation.
It is currently the single stock purchased under this treasury activity; no broader intent beyond that was indicated.

subsections.label: APS stake acquisition structure
points: Only 51% stake acquired in APS so far; remaining 49% to be acquired subsequently over the next couple of years, with the anniversary being 2028.

subsections.label: Seasonal labor shortage
points: Every year, April through June before the monsoon sets in is a period of witnessed labor shortages; this subsides by around July when farm labor returns to blue-collar jobs.
Nothing exceptional to report this year compared to previous year trends; no exceptional labor shortage seen.

subsections.label: Australia wage hike pass-through timing
points: Contracts have built-in rise and fall clauses giving contractual right to pass through higher wage costs to customers immediately, but there is a timing lag: invoice raised, customer studies/processes it, sometimes pays at current rate until settled and then pays in arrears.
This timing mismatch is not dependent on contract expiry or renewal dates — it is a routine annual operation, not an exception tied to the recent Australia wage hike.

subsections.label: Cash IPO market conditions
points: IPO timing is being deferred due to the current IPO rush in the market and significant de-rating witnessed among peer comparables, with company awaiting a more opportune listing window.

key_figures.label: ELI scheme benefit paid to employee after 12 months continuous work

subsections.label: Labour Codes tailwind
points: Labour Codes model rules notified by the Government on May 8, 2026, triggering State Governments to notify implementation dates in their respective States.
Impact expected to be accretive at both EBITDA and PAT levels over the coming 3-4 quarters as efforts are underway on multiple fronts including contract negotiations.
Impact in Q1 is less evident since the process only started on May 8; impact should become more evident in Q2 and Q3.

Over the next 6 to 9 months, as labor code model rules get notified in different States, meaningful minimum wage hikes are expected across most major States, though perhaps not to the extent of the 45-47% hikes already seen in some states.

subsections.label: India margin outlook
points: Current blended India business margin of ~5.3-5.4% considered sustainable.
Objective is to move India margins from this range to a 5.5%-6% ballpark range.
FM margins have improved from 4% to 5.5% currently, with an aspiration to operate near 6%, though timing is uncertain ('it will happen when it will happen').

subsections.label: Minimum wage hike outlook
points: Difficult to predict exact minimum wage hike quantum or timing since labor/minimum wages is a concurrent subject decided by more than 30 State Governments.
Whether all States will follow a similar hike pattern to Karnataka (20%+), Haryana (40%+), and UP (23-24%) is uncertain.

subsections.label: APS margin convergence
points: Blended margins expected to converge back toward SIS's original flagship Security margins (around 5.5%) over the next 4 to 8 quarters as APS integration synergies and cost savings are realized.

subsections.label: Corporate long-term aspiration
points: Aspiration to be among the fewer than 100 companies in India (out of ~5,000 listed, ~500 with INR500 crore+ PAT) that consistently deliver 15% annualized profit growth with a 15%+ return profile.
FY26 was a year of rebound where the company delivered '15 and 15'; FY27 is hoped to be the second consecutive year (an inflection year) in that zone.

subsections.label: Cash business IPO
points: Company is waiting for a more opportune time window to list the Cash business, given the current IPO rush and de-rating among peer comparables.

guidance_ledger.statement: You will see the impact over the coming 3, 4 quarters that it will be accretive both at the EBITDA and PAT levels as efforts are underway at multiple fronts in terms of contract negotiations, etc.
Over the course of the next 6 to 9 months, as the labor codes model rules get notified at different States, they will also come through with some meaningful level of minimum wage hikes.
Our objective is to move from this range (5.3%-5.4%) to 5.5%, 6% ballpark range in India.
Aspirationally, we should be operating near 6%, but it will happen when it will happen; we are at 5.5% consistently.

guidance_ledger.metric: APS margin convergence with SIS flagship Security margins
guidance_ledger.statement: You will see on a blended basis, coming to the original margins that we used to operate over a period of the next 4 to 8 quarters.
We only have acquired 51% stake in the Company, and we still have to acquire 49% subsequently over the next couple of years. The anniversary for that '28.

guidance_ledger.metric: Corporate PAT / return profile aspiration (top-100 company)
guidance_ledger.statement: We want to drive SIS into that box of 100 companies in this country which deliver INR 500 crore plus in PAT and our material businesses with consistent year-after-year 15% growth in profits and 15% or greater return profile.

guidance_ledger.metric: FY27 as second consecutive '15 and 15' year
guidance_ledger.statement: FY '26 was a year of rebound. We delivered 15 and 15, and FY '27, I hope will be an inflection year or the second year where we'll be in that zone, hopefully.
We are waiting for a good time window... given the fact that the peer comparables have witnessed significant de-rating, we are waiting on a more opportune time to take this Company to market.
We've been continuously guiding that we will be consistently pursuing incrementally higher ROCE.
We want to grow at 15% and maintain 15% ROE... the two metrics that are super important are to be able to get growth above 15% and maintain returns over 15% on a multi-year basis.
Maintain over 15% return profile on a multi-year basis; ROCE currently at 16.5%, up from 14.3% a year ago, crossing the guided 15%+ mark.
Targeting around INR20,000 crores in FY27 — management called it a misquote but said 'it is also possible.'

guidance_ledger.metric: PAT (aspiration to be top-100 listed company)
guidance_ledger.statement: We are certain that in today's market environment... if we get to a INR500 crores PAT mark, that would clearly put us at top 100 listed companies, excluding the BFSI majors.
Your EBITDA margins will hover around 5%, 6%, maybe 6.5%. That won't change much... I see no difficulty in us getting to pre-COVID levels.
Can you reach the 6% mark in FY28? Or is that achievable in FY27? — 'I wouldn't be able to comment on that.'

guidance_ledger.metric: APS margin convergence with SIS India Security
guidance_ledger.statement: Over the next 18 months odd, as we consolidate branches, share back-office services, integrate procurement and cross-sell on technology... this should be close to converging. Budget at least 1 year, 1.5 years.
Currently, there is no new international market that we are looking at; SIS is very focused on India at the moment.
We don't do guidance by segment even on a consol basis.

risk_register.risk: Seasonal blue-collar labor shortage (April-June, pre-monsoon)
risk_register.note: Nothing exceptional this year; subsides by July when farm labor returns to blue-collar jobs, consistent with previous year trends.

risk_register.risk: Timing lag in wage cost pass-through to customers
risk_register.note: Rise and fall clauses allow immediate contractual right to pass through higher wages, but invoicing/processing/payment timing creates a routine mismatch, applicable in Australia (post 4.75% minimum wage hike) and elsewhere; not dependent on contract renewal dates.

risk_register.risk: Uncertainty in the quantum/timing of State-wise minimum wage hikes in India
risk_register.note: Minimum wages are a concurrent subject decided by 30+ State Governments; hard to predict with accuracy whether all States will follow the pattern of large hikes seen in Karnataka, Haryana and UP.

risk_register.risk: IPO market conditions for Cash business listing
risk_register.note: Current IPO rush and significant de-rating among peer comparables has led the company to wait for a more opportune listing window; SEBI card remains active, financial details cannot be disclosed.

risk_register.risk: Lower margin drag from APS acquisition
risk_register.note: APS (20% of company size) currently operates at lower margin due to lower scale; integration synergies and cost savings expected to close the gap over 4-8 quarters.

risk_register.risk: Labour Code gratuity/leave liability retrospective impact
risk_register.note: INR290 crore exceptional charge taken in Q3 FY26 due to revised wage definition under new Labour Codes; reassessed and INR38.8 crores reversed in Q4 FY26 via OCI; fully absorbed as an exceptional item with no further material downside currently envisaged.

risk_register.risk: Post-COVID minimum wage compression leading to worker unrest
risk_register.note: Annualized wage growth was artificially compressed to 3-5% per annum over the last 5 years, contributing to worker unrest in Haryana and Greater Noida; recent sharp wage hikes (Haryana +50%, UP +20-28%, Punjab/Uttarakhand +15%+) followed.

risk_register.risk: Industry fragmentation and compliance arbitrage by competitors
risk_register.note: Historically, unorganized/non-compliant competitors gained advantage via compliance arbitrage; expected to be neutralized as single LIN number, single labour license, and unified online filing under Labour Codes gets enforced.

risk_register.risk: No barriers to entry in security services sector
risk_register.note: Anybody can set up a security company; barriers exist only to scale, not entry, which limits pricing power to a modest brand premium rather than a monopoly-like advantage.

risk_register.risk: Geopolitical situation and unfavorable IPO market conditions
risk_register.note: Cited as the reason for deferring (not delaying) the cash business IPO; company awaiting more predictable geopolitical environment and welcoming stock market conditions.

risk_register.risk: Prudent receivables provisioning / expected credit loss increase
risk_register.note: ECL allowance increased from ~INR20 crores to ~INR50 crores YoY due to more prudent provisioning pressed by the Audit Committee, not due to any change in policy or larger expected receivable losses.

risk_register.risk: No labour cost arbitrage possible across states
risk_register.note: Wages are determined by the jurisdiction of work, not the worker's origin state, preventing SIS from sourcing cheap labour from low-wage states like Bihar and deploying at lower cost elsewhere.

themes.label: Labour Code implementation
themes.note: Model rules notified May 8-9, 2026; implementation underway, seen as a tailwind expected to be EBITDA and PAT accretive over the next 3-4 quarters.

themes.label: Wage inflation as revenue driver
themes.note: States like Haryana, UP, Karnataka, Telangana, Uttarakhand passed minimum wage hikes of 20-47%, versus sub-5% average since COVID; contracts pass these through directly to clients, boosting revenue and being broadly EBITDA-neutral to accretive.

themes.label: Market share consolidation opportunity
themes.note: New labor code definition of 'employer' shifts compliance onus to customers/principal employers, expected to drive a fundamental shift from unorganized to organized market share, similar to Australia's 90% compliant-provider usage versus 30-40% in India.

themes.label: Capital allocation / shareholder returns
themes.note: Fifth buyback approved (INR106 crore, first via open market route, max price INR478.50); cumulative shareholder returns since IPO to exceed INR700 crore across 9 capital return actions.

themes.label: APS acquisition integration
themes.note: APS currently drags blended margins due to lower scale, but integration synergies expected to converge margins to SIS flagship levels over 4-8 quarters; remaining 49% stake to be acquired by 2028.

themes.label: Cash business IPO timeline
themes.note: DRHP filed and active card in place, but company awaiting a more opportune listing window given the current IPO rush and peer de-ratings.

themes.label: Margin recovery to pre-COVID levels
themes.note: India blended margin at 5.3-5.4% with objective to reach 5.5-6%; FM margin improved from 4% to 5.5% with aspiration near 6%; ROCE and ROE up sharply from FY25 lows.

key_takeaways: Record FY26 performance: revenue of close to INR16,000 crore (+21% YoY) and EBITDA of over INR700 crore (+18.7% YoY), exiting with a record EBITDA run rate of INR207 crore per quarter.
Q1 FY27 revenue of INR4,604 crore, up 29.7% YoY and 2.5% QoQ; EBITDA at INR207 crore, up 36.2% YoY though flat QoQ.
Labour Codes rules notified May 8-9, 2026; implementation underway and expected to be EBITDA and PAT accretive over the coming 3-4 quarters.

Board approved the fifth buyback of INR106 crore via the open market route (a first for the company) at a maximum price of INR478.50, opening the following week; once concluded, cumulative shareholder returns since IPO would exceed INR700 crore.

India Security crossed a quarterly revenue milestone for the first time at INR2,004 crore (+37.3% YoY); International Security posted highest-ever quarterly revenue run rate of INR1,982 crore (+31% YoY, +7% constant currency); FM revenue grew 8% YoY to INR642 crore.
ROCE improved to 16.7% (from 14% a year ago) and return on equity to 15.8%, up sharply from the FY25 lows of 11.8% ROCE and 9.4% ROE.

Certain States (Haryana, UP, Karnataka, Telangana, Uttarakhand) have passed minimum wage hikes of 20% to 47%, well above the sub-5% average annual hikes seen since COVID; these are structured as pass-throughs to clients under open book costing, making them EBITDA-accretive and revenue-boosting for SIS.

Management highlighted the labor codes' redefinition of 'employer' (including the principal on whose premises work occurs) as a tectonic shift that will shift the compliance cost arbitrage conversation to customers, likely driving a fundamental shift in organized vs unorganized market share, similar to Australia where 90% of customers use compliant providers versus 30-40% in India.

quarters.summary: SIS Limited reported a milestone Q4 FY26 with record revenue, EBITDA and PAT, driven by strong execution across India Security, FM and International Security segments, aided by the APS acquisition and margin recovery towards pre-COVID levels. Management expects continued 15% revenue growth and 15%+ return profile on a multi-year basis, sees Labour Code implementation as a structural tailwind/inflection point for the industry, plans APS margin convergence over 12-18 months, and continues to evaluate the cash business IPO within FY27 subject to market conditions, while India remains the sole focus for geographic expansion.
