subsections.label: Exceptional item accounting treatment
points: The INR290 crore charge taken in Q3 FY26 relates to reassessment of gratuity and leave liabilities under the new Labour Code guidelines.

In Q4 FY26, after reassessment with auditors, the company reversed INR38.8 crores of this liability, which flows through Other Comprehensive Income (OCI) per accounting norms — this is a reassessment of liability, not a change in underlying facts.
Future additional expense from the wage-definition change is now factored into rate breakups with existing customers and will be passed through fully.

For the liability related to past periods, discussions are ongoing with customers; most have indicated they will reimburse when the amount is actually paid to employees at retirement — no accrued income is being created against this; it will hit P&L when cash flow impact accrues.

subsections.label: Depreciation walkthrough
points: QoQ depreciation increase of INR15 crores is largely due to a new MSS office lease signed in Australia (INR10 crores) and fixed asset additions in India (INR4 crores).
Full-year FY26 depreciation increase of ~INR50 crores over FY25 is attributable to leases (INR20 crores) and APS consolidation PPA accounting (INR10 crores).
Company highlighted that depreciation as % of revenue has averaged 1.2% since FY21, indicating nothing materially concerning in the depreciation trend.

subsections.label: Expected credit loss (ECL) provisioning
points: ECL allowance increased from ~INR20 crores to ~INR50 crores YoY; management attributed this to prudent provisioning pushed by the Audit Committee, not any change in policy or expectation of larger receivable losses, and should be seen in context of the INR16,000 crore revenue base.

subsections.label: Capital allocation
points: SIS returned a total of INR250 crores to shareholders in FY26 via buyback and dividend, taking total payout to 70%.
Since IPO (8 years), cumulative shareholder returns total INR600 crores: INR81 crores via dividend, INR270 crores via buyback (FY22-FY24), and INR250 crores this year.

subsections.label: Return profile & compounding story
points: Company frames itself as a compounding story targeting >15% growth and >15% return profile on a multi-year basis; ROCE has crossed the 15%+ guided threshold, now at 16.5%.
Aspiration to be among top 100 listed companies (excluding BFSI majors) by PAT, targeting ~INR500 crores PAT mark.

subsections.label: FM segment sustainability
points: FM segment margin has improved from 4.5% or lower to almost 5.5%, alongside reasonable revenue growth; both growth and margin improvement are considered sustainable by management.

FM headcount reduction (85,000 to 82,000) is due to closure of certain contracts and surge work ending towards Q4-end, not a sign of business contraction; FM remains steady state, growing, with improving margins.

subsections.label: International events-driven revenue pattern
points: Typical contracts in Australia/New Zealand run 3-5 years.

Q4 revenue benefits from events business (Australian Open, Australian Grand Prix) adding ~AUD20 million (~INR120 crores) without a corresponding increase in headcount, since these are existing long-term contracts tied to event timing.
This is a recurring year-on-year Q4 pattern (also seen in prior years), not a one-time item; revenue normalizes in Q1 and will pick up again in Q4 FY27.

Management stated there is no one-time or unsustainable revenue in the international business — a 10-year contract has been signed with Australian Grand Prix and a multi-year contract with Australian Open.

subsections.label: APS acquisition integration and margin convergence
points: AP Securitas (APS) is a strategic acquisition — SIS (No.1 in India security) acquiring the No.6/7 player, done at a reasonable valuation.
SIS Security ex-APS delivered 5.5% margin in Q4; APS delivered 4.2% margin (corrected from an initial 5% mention); blended margin ~5.2%.

Management sees the ~50-130bps margin gap as a synergy opportunity to be closed over the next 12-18 months via branch consolidation, shared back-office services, integrated procurement, and cross-selling of technology.

subsections.label: Market share and industry structure
points: SIS has barely 5% market share in security despite being the largest player; in mature markets like the US and UK, the largest security company holds >15% market share, suggesting long runway for consolidation.
There are only two Indian security companies with revenues above INR2,500 crores — Group 4 and SIS (SIS at ~INR6,000 crores, twice the size of Group 4).
Barriers are not to entry (anyone can start a security company) but to scale — this differentiates leaders like SIS.

subsections.label: FM diversification and resilience
points: Corporate offices/office spaces constitute less than 10% of the FM customer base, making the sector highly diversified across hospitals, schools, malls, airports, manufacturing establishments, etc.

Security and FM are described as essential, non-cyclical, recession-resistant services; during COVID, when the economy shrank by 7%, SIS grew by 7%, driven by demand shifting from offices to hospitals and manufacturing facilities.

subsections.label: APS acquisition rationale
points: AP Securitas is described as a classic strategic transaction — SIS (No.1 player) acquiring the No.6/7 player in Indian security, at a reasonable valuation.

Integration plan over ~18 months includes consolidating branches, sharing back-office services, integrating procurement, and cross-selling technology to converge APS margins with SIS India Security margins.

subsections.label: Cash business IPO
points: The cash business IPO is not delayed by the company but deferred due to external circumstances — largely the geopolitical situation and unfavorable IPO market conditions over recent months.
Objective is to unlock shareholder value; management is not under time pressure and will proceed when market conditions align, hopefully within FY27.
SEBI has extended DRHP validity to September 30, providing flexibility.
The cash business has delivered solid numbers for FY26 with a good outlook for FY27.

subsections.label: No new international market entry planned
points: Management stated SIS is currently focused on India, prioritizing consolidation of market share and accelerating solutioning; no new international market is being pursued at this time.

subsections.label: Labour Code implementation impact
points: The retrospective gratuity impact (INR290 crore charge) tied to the government's revised wage definition under the new Labour Codes was flagged as the one clear downside from Labour Code implementation, now fully absorbed as an exceptional item.
Implementation is not instantaneous — it will take time to percolate down to the last contract; this is described as the beginning of a fundamental industry shift rather than a completed change.

subsections.label: Wage growth compression post-COVID
points: Post-COVID, the government artificially compressed wage increases — annualized minimum wage growth in the country was only 3-5% per annum over the last 5 years, which caused worker dissatisfaction.
This contributed to worker unrest incidents in Haryana and Greater Noida in the recent past.
Subsequently, in the last 30 days, Haryana hiked minimum wages by 50%, Uttar Pradesh by ~28% (also cited as 20-odd percent), and Punjab and Uttarakhand by more than 15%.

subsections.label: Industry structure risk / no entry barriers
points: There are no barriers to entry in the security services sector — anyone, including retired policemen or ex-army personnel, can set up a security company; barriers exist only to scaling up, which is where established players like SIS differentiate.

subsections.label: No labour arbitrage / regulated wage structure
points: Wages paid to guards are strictly determined by the jurisdiction where they work (state minimum wage), not by where they are sourced from — hence no cost arbitrage is possible by sourcing low-cost labour from Bihar and deploying elsewhere.
There is no legal provision to send Indian security guards to work in international markets like Australia (immigration laws restrict this to high-skilled manpower not locally available).

subsections.label: Growth and return framework
points: Management does not provide segment-wise guidance even on a consolidated basis; historically SIS has hovered around 15% growth and 15% return profile since listing (from a ~INR6,000 crore company with ~INR100 crore PAT to a ~INR16,000 crore company with ~INR390 crore normalized PAT in FY26).
Aspiration is to continue compounding at approximately '15 is to 15' — >15% growth and >15% ROE/ROCE — on a multi-year basis.
Aspiration to become one of the top 100 listed companies by PAT (excluding BFSI majors), which management believes requires reaching ~INR500 crores PAT.

subsections.label: Margin outlook
points: EBITDA margin trajectory has improved from ~4.3% in Q1 FY26 to 4.6-4.7% by year-end (impacted by full-quarter APS consolidation); standalone India Security and FM segments are already at 5.5% margin, near pre-COVID levels of ~6%.

Management stated there is no difficulty envisaged in returning to pre-COVID EBITDA margin levels, but the industry is fundamentally a 5-6.5% EBITDA margin industry (not a 10% margin industry), comparable to global peers; management declined to commit on whether 6% margin is achievable in FY27 or FY28.

The industry is characterized as a 'growth and ROCE industry' rather than a high-margin industry — the key focus is sustaining 15% top-line growth and 15%+ returns on the INR16,000 crore revenue base.

subsections.label: FY27 revenue clarification
points: When asked about a media report quoting a ~INR20,000 crore FY27 revenue target, management called it a misquote but acknowledged such a figure is 'also possible.'

subsections.label: Cash business IPO timing
points: Management hopes to proceed with the cash business IPO within FY27, subject to improved geopolitical conditions and IPO market receptiveness; SEBI has extended DRHP validity to September 30.

guidance_ledger.statement: We want to grow at 15% and maintain 15% ROE... the two metrics that are super important are to be able to get growth above 15% and maintain returns over 15% on a multi-year basis.
Maintain over 15% return profile on a multi-year basis; ROCE currently at 16.5%, up from 14.3% a year ago, crossing the guided 15%+ mark.
Targeting around INR20,000 crores in FY27 — management called it a misquote but said 'it is also possible.'

guidance_ledger.metric: PAT (aspiration to be top-100 listed company)
guidance_ledger.statement: We are certain that in today's market environment... if we get to a INR500 crores PAT mark, that would clearly put us at top 100 listed companies, excluding the BFSI majors.
Your EBITDA margins will hover around 5%, 6%, maybe 6.5%. That won't change much... I see no difficulty in us getting to pre-COVID levels.
Can you reach the 6% mark in FY28? Or is that achievable in FY27? — 'I wouldn't be able to comment on that.'

guidance_ledger.metric: APS margin convergence with SIS India Security
guidance_ledger.statement: Over the next 18 months odd, as we consolidate branches, share back-office services, integrate procurement and cross-sell on technology... this should be close to converging. Budget at least 1 year, 1.5 years.
The cash IPO is deferred owing to circumstances... hopefully within FY27... SEBI has facilitated that by extending the DRHP validity to September 30.
Currently, there is no new international market that we are looking at; SIS is very focused on India at the moment.
We don't do guidance by segment even on a consol basis.

risk_register.risk: Industry fragmentation and compliance arbitrage by competitors
risk_register.note: Historically, unorganized/non-compliant competitors gained advantage via compliance arbitrage; expected to be neutralized as single LIN number, single labour license, and unified online filing under Labour Codes gets enforced.

risk_register.risk: No barriers to entry in security services sector
risk_register.note: Anybody can set up a security company; barriers exist only to scale, not entry, which limits pricing power to a modest brand premium rather than a monopoly-like advantage.

risk_register.risk: Geopolitical situation and unfavorable IPO market conditions

risk_register.risk: Prudent receivables provisioning / expected credit loss increase
risk_register.note: ECL allowance increased from ~INR20 crores to ~INR50 crores YoY due to more prudent provisioning pressed by the Audit Committee, not due to any change in policy or larger expected receivable losses.

risk_register.risk: No labour cost arbitrage possible across states
risk_register.note: Wages are determined by the jurisdiction of work, not the worker's origin state, preventing SIS from sourcing cheap labour from low-wage states like Bihar and deploying at lower cost elsewhere.

themes.label: Labour Code implementation
themes.note: Retrospective gratuity charge of INR290 crores was the key downside, now absorbed; management frames the broader Labour Code rollout (single LIN, single license) as a structural tailwind and potential inflection point for the industry.

themes.label: Margin recovery to pre-COVID levels
themes.note: Consolidated EBITDA margin improved from 4.3% in Q1 FY26 to 4.6-4.7% by year-end; India Security and FM standalone segments already at 5.5%, near pre-COVID ~6% levels.

themes.label: APS acquisition integration
themes.note: APS margin (4.2%) trails SIS India Security ex-APS (5.5%); management targets convergence over 12-18 months via branch consolidation, shared back-office, procurement integration and tech cross-sell.

themes.label: Capital allocation / shareholder returns

themes.label: Wage inflation as revenue driver
themes.note: Revenue is a function of price (driven by wages) multiplied by volume; recent sharp minimum wage hikes in Haryana, UP, Punjab and Uttarakhand are viewed as a positive for revenue, not a negative.

themes.label: Market share consolidation opportunity
themes.note: SIS holds only ~5% market share in Indian security versus >15% for market leaders in mature markets like the US/UK, indicating a long runway for scale-driven consolidation as Labour Codes get enforced.

key_takeaways: Q4 and FY26 marked a milestone quarter and one of the best growth years for SIS in the last 5-6 years post-COVID, marked by strong execution across all businesses with highest ever revenue, EBITDA margins and PAT.
Quarterly revenue of INR4,489 crores, a jump of 31% year-on-year and 7.3% quarter-on-quarter.
EBITDA for the quarter crossed the psychological INR200 crores mark for the first time at a record INR207 crores, 25.6% up year-on-year.
Last quarter's onetime exceptional charge of INR290 crores (Labour Code gratuity/leave liability) was reassessed, resulting in a reversal of INR38.8 crores in Q4, flowing through OCI.
India Security reported its highest ever revenue of INR1,925 crores (34.2% YoY growth), aided by consolidation of the APS acquisition.
International Security reported its highest ever quarterly revenue of INR1,950 crores, a growth of 36.9% YoY.
ROCE stands at 16.5%, up from 14.3% a year ago, crossing the guided 15%+ threshold.
DSO improved to 63 days, down by 4 days from the previous quarter, one of the best since 2023.
SIS returned a total of INR250 crores to shareholders this financial year (buyback + dividend), taking total payout to 70%; cumulative since IPO returns of INR600 crores.

Management views Labour Code implementation as a structural reset for the industry and a potential inflection point, despite the retrospective gratuity charge being the sole clear downside identified.
Company aspires to maintain a '15 is to 15' formula — 15%+ revenue growth and 15%+ return profile — on a multi-year basis, and to reach top-100 listed company status by PAT (~INR500 crores).

The expected credit loss that you guys report on the cash flow, which is as an allowance... has gone up dramatically... Anything to read in there?

TATAPOWER.about: Tata Power Company Ltd is primarily involved in the business of the generation, transmission and distribution of electricity. It aims to produce electricity completely through renewable sources. It also manufactures solar roofs and plans to build 1 lakh ev charging stations by 2025[1] The company is India's largest vertically-integrated power company.[2]

quarters.summary: Tata Power delivered its 27th consecutive quarter of PAT and EBITDA growth in Q1 FY27, with management guiding to continued strong capex execution (~INR25,000 crores for FY27), renewable capacity addition to ~9 GW by year-end, rooftop growth of 60-70% in FY27, Tata Projects turnaround expected within a quarter or two, and Mundra SPPA state approvals expected by August-September, while flagging curtailment (~5% industry-wide), transmission bottlenecks and ALMM policy flux as near-term risks.

subsections.label: Segment-wise 4-year CAGR performance
points: Transmission business: revenue CAGR 45%, EBITDA CAGR 19%, PAT CAGR 27% over last 4 years each quarter
Mumbai Transmission: revenue CAGR 7%, EBITDA CAGR 11%, PAT CAGR 21%
Renewable cluster overall: revenue up 22%, EBITDA up 23%, PAT up 37%
Generation business: revenue CAGR 11%, EBITDA CAGR 10%, PAT CAGR 2%, despite limited own-project capacity addition due to third-party project focus
Rooftop business: revenue growth of nearly 100% YoY; 4-year CAGR revenue ~58%, EBITDA growth 68% YoY, PAT growth >67% YoY, 4-year PAT CAGR 84%

subsections.label: Leverage and capital allocation
points: Net debt to underlying EBITDA of 3.41x and net debt to equity of 1.25x are within self-set guardrails for investment
Large investment program calibrated to maintain leverage discipline while pursuing growth opportunities including nuclear

subsections.label: Mundra Coal & Shipping cluster breakdown
points: EBITDA for the cluster declined while PAT grew, driven by a higher share of coal profits offsetting Mundra under-recovery
Mundra plant continues to have some under-recovery under the SPPA cost-reflective structure, but the effort is to ensure no loss on ROE perspective
Management declined to give a separate coal vs Mundra breakup on the call but offered to share details separately via IR

subsections.label: TBCB accounting nuance
points: TBCB projects currently under construction show revenue/PAT primarily from lease accounting rather than actual EBITDA sharing, hence the low implied 13% EBITDA margin
Actual regulated EBITDA comes from Mumbai (MO) transmission regulated business plus a share of profit from transmission assets in the Resurgent platform
Two TBCB projects to be commissioned in Q2, with subsequent ones in Q3 and Q4, after which actual line-item revenue/EBITDA/PAT will start flowing

subsections.label: Solar EPC discontinuation impact
points: Third-party solar EPC is no longer a focus area; company repurposed EPC workforce/resources to in-house development (5.5 GW pipeline plus PSP solutioning)
Previous year EPC business contributed ~INR100 crores of PAT; this year remaining legacy EPC work is being wrapped up, resulting in booked losses
No new EPC order book; only completing remaining legacy work (performance reviews, final billing, final collections), with no major further capex to be executed there

subsections.label: TP Solar margin/mix
points: This quarter saw higher third-party cell sales due to clientele mix change, boosting margin, but this was a small quantity, not a large sustained trend
Company expects some additional cell sale quantity for a few more quarters (linked to ALMM/open access/group captive requirements) but not a large sustained volume going forward

Module production increased (crossed 1,000 MW for first time in a quarter) while cell production reduced due to a line change; efficiency improvements are enabling premium pricing despite a yield sacrifice

subsections.label: Odisha DISCOM timing issues
points: Government payments delayed from Panchayati Raj departments (drinking water, street light) due to delayed state/central allocation; expected to be collected this quarter
Government directive to not disconnect supply up to 15th June during heat wave meant payments were not made during that period; that period is now over and collections are being pursued
Billing has a 1-month cycle, so high summer consumption billed in one month gets collected in the subsequent month, distorting quarterly numbers
Distribution business should be viewed on a 12-month rollover basis rather than quarter-to-quarter due to dependence on consumption/temperature/weather patterns
These are described as pure timing issues unrelated to the underlying business arrangement; operationally the Odisha DISCOM performed excellently

subsections.label: Delhi DISCOM
points: Same billing-cycle timing dynamic as Odisha applies to Delhi DISCOM — high summer billing collected with a lag (e.g., June billing collected in July)
On a 12-month basis the business is on track despite quarterly distortions; winter months typically show lower collections as a mirror effect

subsections.label: Rooftop realization mix
points: Difference between billed realization (~INR36-37/watt-peak) and order inflow realization (~INR28/watt-peak) is due to product/module mix differences, not a decline in realization

Under the government's ULA scheme, a large quantity of 1 kW systems uses different (lower-cost) modules versus higher-capacity installations using different module types (e.g., 450mm vs 580/630 series)
Averaging realization across these different mixes would be a wrong interpretation of true pricing trends

subsections.label: Rooftop growth potential and strategy
points: Rooftop penetration is only 40 lakh consumers versus a total addressable base of 25 crore consumers in India — market potential described as humongous
Product serves from the poorest consumers (1 kW) to larger commercial/industrial loads (2-20+ kW)
Addition of battery storage to rooftop offering makes customers self-sufficient in power and is expected to be a further growth driver
Company believes previously disclosed cumulative rooftop revenue target of INR30,000 crores by 2030 may be reached earlier, by 2029, given the pace of growth
Company is the largest player in rooftop, commands a pricing premium, and has built supply chain, channel partners, after-sales service and digital solutions that competitors cannot easily match

Management flagged that rooftop's phenomenal growth could have negative/cannibalizing implications for other businesses (distribution, IPP) over a 10-year horizon, though distribution network, devices and technology for managing multiple supplies will still be required

subsections.label: Manufacturing (cell/module) performance
points: Cell and module plants (started 2 years back) are now operating at full capacity
Module plant crossed 1,000 MW production in Q1 for the first time; production considered close to peak, while cell production is still catching up
Record PAT this year in manufacturing driven by steps to improve yield efficiency and manufacturing cost, alongside significant engineering effort
First quarter run-rate is typically not simply multiplied by 4 for the full year; historically the full year has been 4.5x to 5x the Q1 run-rate, and this trend is expected to continue

subsections.label: Solar EPC business status
points: Third-party EPC no longer a focus; company decided to repurpose EPC workforce to focus on in-house execution given 5.5 GW pipeline plus PSP-linked solutioning
This is the second consecutive quarter of an EBITDA-level loss in the EPC-linked line, driven by wrapping up remaining legacy EPC work

subsections.label: Pumped hydro / hydro project progress
points: Very good progress in pumped hydro construction; commissioning expected from beginning of calendar year 2029, with 3 units commissioned with a 2-month gap between each
Won SECI bid at attractive tariff for 1 unit (330 MW); balance 2 units under discussion with Tata Steel and other industrial procurers
New pumped hydro storage bids expected from NHPC and NTPC
Work on the 1,800 MW Shirwata PSP to start later this year, pending approvals; Board approval to follow once approvals are in place
Bhutan Khorlochhu (600 MW) PPA signed with UPPCL and has received regulatory approval; returns better than originally planned; plant expected operational in calendar year 2030
Dorjilung (1,125 MW) project financed by World Bank; financial closure being completed with PFC, IFC and other lenders
These pumped hydro/hydro projects carry 40-year PPAs and are located in areas well known to the company (echoing existing hydro assets over 110 years old)

Company plans to announce the next set of pumped hydro projects within the next 12 months, using available water reservoir sites, with DPRs underway; gaps planned between project commissioning (2029 and 2031) to maintain implementation focus

subsections.label: Mundra plant operations
points: Plant operating under Section 11 for scheduling purposes; SPPA concluded with Gujarat
Advanced stage of cabinet approval from 3 states expected in August, with the fourth state expected in September
All procurers taking full capacity, viewed as the most sustainable plant in the long run on tariff and merit order basis
Company expects to run the plant continuously through 2038

subsections.label: Distribution demand trends
points: National power demand growth was nearly 8.5% in Q1; May saw ~11% growth and June ~9.8%
July demand has consistently been in the range of 260-270 GW
Delayed and inadequate rains this year expected to lead to a longer summer and higher cooling-driven consumption
Industrial growth pickup is also contributing to increased power demand alongside cooling demand

subsections.label: Renewable auction market shift
points: Renewable energy auction volumes have been muted as large volumes of central-agency (SECI, NHPC, NTPC) PPAs were not fully tied up with state governments
Growing preference among state DISCOMs to conduct their own bidding rather than relying on central agencies
States increasingly seeking customized FDRE/RTC (round-the-clock) bids rather than standard solar/wind/hybrid bids
Company is directly bidding to states rather than through central agencies for solar/wind/hybrid, except for pumped hydro where central agency storage solutions are still relevant

subsections.label: Pumped hydro contracting strategy
points: Contracting approach for pumped hydro will be a mix: annuity-based bid contracts (e.g., 1 unit already tied up) and bilateral arrangements with large C&I customers (e.g., steel, cement industries such as Tata Steel)
No single uniform contracting model; combination of DISCOM/central agency deals and bilateral C&I deals expected

subsections.label: Nuclear exploration
points: Preliminary work underway on nuclear opportunities including land, geotechnical studies and water availability assessments
Firm plans to be developed once government rules on nuclear are notified

subsections.label: Tata Projects turnaround
points: Company is in final stages of closing legacy loss-making projects; only ~10% of legacy projects remain in last stage
One more quarter of impact expected on Tata Projects before financial performance improves
Strong pipeline of marquee global projects expected to drive a turnaround in Tata Projects' financial performance going forward

subsections.label: Transmission bottlenecks / curtailment
points: General curtailment of roughly 5% observed across the industry including company projects in Q1
Curtailment expected to settle in over the next few quarters as transmission and evacuation lines progress
Company has made progress on land and connectivity for RE projects; 500 MW project nearly ready for commissioning within 1-2 weeks, expected to drive a big ramp-up in Q2 commissioning

subsections.label: ALMM policy flip-flop
points: ALMM-II implementation saw a temporary rollback during the quarter, but management clarifies this is not a full rollback — ALMM-II continues for rooftop and utility-scale projects
The exemption applies only to projects with limited open access arrangements or behind-the-meter setups, representing only ~10% of total DCR requirement
Management does not see this as materially moving the needle; company's commitment to ingot and wafer capacity for ALMM-III remains on track

subsections.label: Coal price and export regulation risk
points: Coal prices have risen but only modestly (5-7% range); no major further changes expected, with up to 5% increase possible over the next 9 months
Indonesia's coal export regime requires domestic market obligation to be met before exporting; KPC was the first to comply with this requirement
No major changes expected in the Indonesian coal market due to the new regulations

subsections.label: Rithala Plant closure
points: Rithala Plant was closed long ago in 2016 due to tariff and depreciation issues; it is not listed in current capacity because it is not operating, and the matter has now been finalized with provisions made

key_figures.label: Next pumped hydro project pipeline announcement

subsections.label: Full-year performance seasonality
points: Management reiterated that Q1 typically understates the full year; historically Q1 x 4.5-5x approximates the full-year result, and a similar pattern is expected this year

Q2 capex plan of higher than INR6,000 crores, possibly closer to INR6,500 crores if all goes well, with almost half going to renewables to commission 800-900 MW

Odisha DISCOM performance next year should possibly peak, as it is expected to be the best year yet, driven by initiatives taken in recent years

Delhi regulatory commission has affidavit-committed to amortize the regulatory asset wind-down over 6 years up to 2032

key_takeaways: Tata Power has done exceedingly well, INR 1,401 crores of PAT in the quarter, which is an 11% increase, and EBITDA increase has been 8% to INR 4,249 crores.
This is the 27th consecutive quarter where we have seen increase in our PAT and EBITDA.
The transmission business has shown a revenue increase of 45% CAGR, 19% in EBITDA, and 27% in PAT over the last 4 years.
Renewable cluster revenue has gone up by 22%, the EBITDA by 23% and the PAT by 37%.
Rooftop business revenue has grown from last year to this year by nearly 100%; company plans to grow by about 60% to 70% this year.
For the first time, our module plant crossed 1,000 megawatt in the first quarter, and we expect that we have virtually peaked over there in terms of module production.

On the capital expenditure, for the first time, we spent INR 5,300 crores in the first quarter, and we expect that the INR 25,000 crores that we have lined up for this year, we'll be able to implement.
Net debt to underlying EBITDA is 3.41 and our net debt to equity is 1.25, within the guardrails that we have set for ourselves for the investment.
We are in very advanced stage of getting approval from 3 states [for Mundra SPPA], expecting that in the month of August; the fourth state will happen in September.
pressing_questions: What explains the muted growth in Odisha in this quarter? And can you please also touch upon the fact that the Tata Projects continues to make losses and the losses got only widened in this quarter?
Is it possible to quantify your losses due to curtailment in this quarter? And what do you make of the transmission bottlenecks for your projects?

In relation to the renewable energy auction volume, which after peaking in FY25 came off in FY26, what is your outlook in terms of how renewable energy auction volumes and their complexion is likely to pan out in FY27 and maybe the medium term?

In your cluster-wise results, when I look at TBCB projects line item, the EBITDA margin, which is implied is just 13% for Q1 FY27. Typically, TBCB projects should have much higher EBITDA margin given the asset profile and the depreciation that comes below the EBITDA line. What am I missing here?

On the solar EPC side, third-party EPC is no more a focus area, but it's the second quarter where we have posted a loss on an EBITDA level. Could you just explain why exactly at a loss at the EBITDA level itself?

Could you give me the details of how this tariff and how much of profits from the coal sales in Indonesia is getting knocked off when we are completing the tariff [for Mundra supplementary PPA]? Some color on the supplementary PPA tariff would be helpful?

If I look at the cluster-wise numbers that you have shared on the coal Mundra Coal and Shipping, so we see your EBITDA has declined, but your PAT has actually grown. Can you give us a breakup of that number of INR 2,732 crores of top line and INR 225 crores of PAT, how much came from the coal and how much the losses from Mundra?

quarters.summary: Tata Power reported record FY'26 financial performance (PAT nearly INR5,000 crores, EBITDA up ~11% to INR16,090 crores) despite Mundra being non-operational for 9 months; management guided FY'27 capex of ~INR25,000 crores, expects power demand to keep rising (peak demand to cross ~270 GW in 1-2 months), targets 2-2.5 GW of renewable commissioning per annum for the next 2 years (largely hybrid/FDRE, in-house cell/module sourced), expects Odisha DISCOM performance to peak next year, and expects Tata Projects to return to profit from FY'27, while coal monetization and nuclear SMR projects remain work-in-progress.

subsections.label: FY26 performance drivers
points: Strong financial and operational performance in FY '26 in spite of Mundra not operating for 9 months.
Full year PAT of nearly more than INR5,000 crores reported for the first time.
EBITDA growth of ~11% driven by strong performance of existing businesses of generation, transmission, distribution and renewables.
Quarterly EBITDA and PAT growth driven by all businesses collectively.

subsections.label: Solar cell/module and rooftop performance
points: Solar cell and module manufacturing plant operations stabilized with very good yields, delivering PAT of INR857 crores, more than double the previous year.
Rooftop solar installations doubled during the year, with PAT of nearly INR499 crores.

subsections.label: Odisha DISCOM performance
points: Odisha DISCOM PAT rose from INR439 crores in the previous year to INR809 crores this year.

subsections.label: Balance sheet and leverage discipline
points: Debt at approximately INR56,000 crores despite capex of nearly INR13,000 crores in the last financial year.
Leverage ratios stable: net debt to underlying EBITDA at 3.3x and net debt to equity at 1.2x, described as competitive for infrastructure/power industry.
Management committed to maintaining similar financial discipline for future investments; growth to be calibrated to maintain balance sheet discipline.

subsections.label: Delhi distribution regulatory orders
points: Regulatory upside pertains to matters from a few years back where approvals were previously denied or deferred; recurring phenomenon each year.
FY25 had INR333 crores of regulatory approvals; FY26 saw INR783 crores.
Pipeline of regulatory assets still being contested/discussed; some amount expected to materialize in FY27 but quantum difficult to predict; will provide better clarity quarter by quarter.

subsections.label: Deferred tax asset (Note 5)
points: Deferred tax asset is noncash, recognized given improved future profitability projections and carry-forward losses that management now expects to utilize within a defined time frame.
Adjustment made against standalone books; positively impacted consolidated profit for the quarter.

subsections.label: IEL and Mumbai Transmission profitability increases
points: IEL profitability increase linked to deferred tax created due to asset capitalization when a plant got commissioned; not a yearly recurring phenomenon, depends on asset capitalization timing and profitability of the specific plant.

Mumbai Transmission profitability increase is based on pure capex; described as recurring, since Mumbai transmission adds about INR1,000 crores of capex every year with a 70-30 structure yielding ~30% return on equity plus certain O&M.

subsections.label: Cash flow item — service concession arrangement
points: Movement in balance related to service concession agreement relates to capex spend on TBCB project (HBA/TBCB project); it is a onetime capex item shown in the capex figure in the investor presentation, appearing as a drag on cash flow for the year because related revenues have not yet been recognized.

subsections.label: Renewable business – growth outlook
points: Generation, transmission, distribution, renewable, renewable manufacturing, rooftop and utility scale businesses are all cited as key growth drivers for EBITDA over the next 2 years; Mundra drag now behind the company.
Last year saw a large amount of third-party project execution; this year everything will be in-house, utilizing captive cell/module manufacturing.

For every 2 GW of solar delivered, module/cell requirement multiplier is ~1.4x (i.e., ~2.8 GW of manufacturing capacity utilized for 2 GW solar), largely met from in-house capacity; intrasegment elimination in FY27 will reflect this (RPT-compliant margins).
2 GW FY27 commissioning ballpark includes solar and wind combined, with solar accounting for 1.5-1.8 GW; could be slightly higher if all goes well.

Large portion of FY27 commissioning capacity is expected to be hybrid/FDRE projects (combination of solar and wind) rather than pure solar or pure wind; wind turbines already tied up for these projects.

Slide 7 vs Slide 32/34 clarification: capacity figures on Slide 7 represent installed capacity, while contracted capacity (as per Slide 32) will be lower than installed; guidance was given on installed capacity basis.

subsections.label: Rooftop solar
points: Rooftop installations doubled in FY26; management expects continued strong growth in FY27 (50-60% growth even if not another 100%).
Target to increase rooftop market share to 20% within the next 3 years despite competition; market share of ~40% maintained in FY26.
Government subsidy for rooftop requires use of Indian-made cell and module, which will be catered from the company's existing manufacturing plant.
From 1st June 2026, only Indian-made cells can be used; many projects are not grandfathered, so some FY27 projects will require Indian-made cells and modules.

subsections.label: Odisha DISCOM outlook
points: Management expects next financial year to possibly be the best year yet for Odisha DISCOMs, as impact of initiatives taken in recent years (including last year) materializes.

Loss reduction trajectory agreed with Odisha regulator: all circles expected to reach 12-13% AT&C loss range within next 4-5 years, with roughly 2% annual reduction as a ballpark; North Odisha already at ~10% while other 3 circles are at ~18%.

subsections.label: Capacity pipeline breakdown
points: 26.3 GW figure (16.7 GW operational + pipeline) includes the 2,800 MW pumped hydro at Shirwata (work starting this financial year), and existing Bhutan hydro projects (600 MW + 1,125 MW, financing signed with World Bank).
Some projects will come online in 2030-31, the 1,125 MW Bhutan project in 2031-32; all solar and wind projects targeted for completion by 2030.

Of the 5 GW renewable pipeline, roughly 1 GW is a combination of plain wind and solar capacity, and 4 GW is a combination of ~2.5 GW FDRE and the rest hybrid wind-RTC projects; contracted capacity for FDRE/hybrid timeline (per FY32 slides) currently totals about 1,200 MW, lower than the installed capacity figures used for guidance.

subsections.label: Tata Projects performance
points: Tata Projects had legacy loss-making projects (dedicated freight corridor, Barmer refining project, and others) that have now largely been completed with minimal residual impact.
Subsequent/new projects secured by Tata Projects have good margins; management expects the business to return to profitability starting FY27, after losses in FY25 and FY26.

subsections.label: Wafer and ingot plant expansion
points: Company will start work on a new 10 GW wafer and ingot plant in 2 phases, to cater to existing cell and module plant operations.
Plant will require Indian-made wafers from 1st June 2028 onwards.

Existing solar cell and module manufacturing plant operations have stabilized with good yields and is well positioned to cater to both large utility scale and rooftop solar requirements, including Indian-made cell/module mandates.

subsections.label: Mundra SPPA (Supplementary PPA) resolution
points: SPPA concluded with Gujarat; finalization with other 4 procurer states expected within next 4-6 weeks, in advanced stage of government approval.

Plant already operating under Section 11 with the understanding that tariff will be as per the SPPA, which has been accounted for in quarterly results and will continue to be accounted for going forward.

Full plant (all 5 units) is operating; Section 11 facilitates operation and gives time for procurers to obtain necessary approvals; billing is per the SPPA and understanding reached with procurers and Ministry of Power.
Coal cost is a pass-through under the SPPA arrangement, including FOB cost components such as royalty or export duty changes.
Details of Gujarat SPPA already shared; further details on the arrangement with other 4 procurers will be shared once all parties sign.

subsections.label: Coal asset monetization
points: Thought process of monetizing coal assets post SPPA signing remains intact, contingent on market opportunity and valuation.
Considered premature to initiate sale process until SPPAs are signed with all procurers; timing of monetization decision will depend on market conditions at that time.

subsections.label: Hydro and pumped storage projects
points: Large exposure being taken in hydro (Bhutan hydro projects and Bhivpuri pumped hydro project); PPA agreed but pending regulatory approval process, which is in final stages with approval expected in the next few months.

subsections.label: Renewable bidding strategy — hybrid with storage
points: Company is pausing pure solar/pure wind bidding due to transmission delays; going forward will focus on hybrid renewable + storage (including pumped hydro) projects for better returns than projects bid in the last 2 years.
Such hybrid+storage arrangements being discussed not only with utilities but also with large C&I customers such as steel companies (in discussions with Tata Steel) and data centres.
Company examining opportunities to add new coal-based generation capacity where tariff is attractive and PPA is bankable, despite a general stance against new coal capacity.

subsections.label: Nuclear SMR initiative
points: Working with 3 state governments; land identified, water allocation approvals given and in pipeline, detailed geotechnical studies under progress.
Detailed DPR being prepared in collaboration with NPCIL for small modular reactor plants of 2 x 220 MW (440 MW) configuration.
DPR expected to be completed for some states within next 6 months; other aspects to be finalized with Nuclear Power Corporation will take more time.

subsections.label: Delhi DISCOM regulatory asset wind-down
points: Supreme Court and APTEL are monitoring the regulatory asset wind-down; regulatory commission has affidavit-committed to amortize it over 6 years up to 2032; company expects implementation per the affidavit.

key_figures.label: Expected Indonesian coal price movement range

subsections.label: Demand and heat wave/El Nino risk
points: Increase in power demand accelerating due to heat wave across the country and predicted severe impact from El Nino; power systems remain stable, with increased demand met mainly by coal-based and hydro plants, supported by renewables during solar/wind hours.

subsections.label: Coal price and Indonesian export policy risk
points: Imported coal-based plants have not seen material impact; adequate coal supply with only small, nominal increases in coal prices and shipping costs over the last 2 months.

Discussion ongoing for months regarding potential additional taxes on Indonesian coal exports; outcome yet to be decided; Indonesian coal prices expected to remain virtually flat, within plus/minus 5%.

subsections.label: Transmission and right-of-way delays affecting capex phasing
points: Capex guidance shortfall versus INR22,000-25,000 crore target attributed to delays in right-of-way and delays in transmission systems being built by others under TBCB (including ISTS projects), which were required for evacuation of company's renewable projects.

Projects deferred to current quarter/financial year rather than cancelled; ~600 MW of large utility-scale projects being completed this quarter; transmission projects being executed as ROW issues resolve.

Company now being extra cautious to avoid commissioning plants without permanent GNA (General Network Access); some capex planned last year was deferred specifically to avoid operating on temporary GNA; projects now only commissioned with certainty on transmission line and permanent GNA.

subsections.label: Curtailment risk on renewable generation
points: Curtailment occurring in a few locations, not on a continuous basis; evacuation allowances vary by location, ranging from as low as 20-25% to as high as 60-80%; considered a moving target.

Company continues to work with transmission companies and the Central Transmission Utility (CTU) to reduce curtailment; where GNA exists and curtailment occurs, company is reimbursed on a supply basis.

Lower solar PLF in FY26 attributed to lower resource availability, in addition to curtailment; company unable to quantify precise curtailment impact for FY26 or provide firm FY27 expectation given variability.

subsections.label: Regulatory approval uncertainty
points: Difficult to predict outcome or quantum of pipeline of regulatory assets under contestation/discussion for Delhi distribution business; some amount expected to materialize in FY27 but exact figure not quantifiable at this stage.

subsections.label: Capex guidance
points: FY26 capex guidance of ~INR22,000-25,000 crores (referenced as INR25,000 crores per Bhubaneswar presentation) fell short, actual capex was ~INR13,000 crores, due to project phasing delays (ROW, transmission system delays under TBCB); deferred projects to be completed this financial year rather than lost.
FY27 capex guided at approximately INR25,000 crores, covering large utility-scale solar/wind, distribution projects, transmission projects, hydro projects, pumped storage, and pure hydro capex.
Management expects a similar capital outlay of ~INR25,000 crores for FY28 as well.

subsections.label: Business outlook
points: All businesses — generation, transmission, distribution, renewable, renewable manufacturing, rooftop and utility scale — expected to give good profit and good returns over the next 2 years, with the Mundra drag now behind the company.
Management committed to calibrated growth balancing financial discipline and balance sheet strength while enhancing generation, transmission, distribution and hydro (including Bhutan) capacity.

key_takeaways: Tata Power has posted a very strong financial and operational performance in FY '26, in spite of the fact that Mundra did not operate for 9 months, reporting for the first time a full year PAT of nearly more than INR5,000 crores and EBITDA up nearly 11% to INR16,090 crores.
During the quarter, EBITDA jumped by nearly 10% to INR4,216 crores compared to INR3,829 crores last year, and PAT went up by 8% to INR1,416 crores compared to INR1,306 crores last year.

Solar cell and module manufacturing plant has stabilized operations with good yields, delivering a PAT of INR857 crores, more than double the previous year; rooftop solar doubled installations with a PAT of nearly INR499 crores.
Odisha DISCOM has done exceedingly well, with PAT of INR809 crores this year versus INR439 crores in the previous year.
Nearly 5 gigawatt of in-house renewable projects are under implementation, with 50% to be completed this financial year and the balance 50% in FY '28.
SPPA concluded with Gujarat for Mundra, with finalization expected with the other 4 states in the next 4-6 weeks; plant currently operating under Section 11 with tariff accounted for as per the SPPA.
Debt stands at approximately INR56,000 crores despite capex of nearly INR13,000 crores in FY26; net debt to underlying EBITDA is 3.3x and net debt to equity is 1.2x.
FY '27 capex guidance is approximately INR25,000 crores, covering utility-scale solar/wind, distribution, transmission and hydro projects; management expects a similar capital outlay in FY '28.

SANSERA.about: Sansera Engineering Ltd is an engineering-led manufacturer of complex and critical precision engineered components across automotive and non - automotive sectors. The company manufactures and supplies a wide range of precision forged and machined components for the automotive sector and for non - automotive sector it manufactures and supplies a wide range of precision components for aerospace, off-road, agriculture, and other segments.[1]

quarters.summary: Sansera delivered its highest-ever quarterly revenue in Q1 FY27 (INR10,213 million, +33% YoY) with resilient EBITDA/PAT margins (19.2%/8.6%). Management expects FY27 to end with high-teens (possibly touching 20%) top-line growth, driven by strong ADS order book momentum (peak revenue visibility of INR5,700 crore executable by FY31), continued auto ICE/xEV strength, and export traction, even as raw material and consumable cost inflation and supply-chain/capacity constraints persist; capex will continue to be phased per order visibility and return thresholds, funded largely through internal accruals/low leverage with no immediate fundraise planned, though inorganic opportunities in non-auto areas remain open.

subsections.label: Margin drivers
points: Margin expansion supported by operating leverage, disciplined cost absorption and a more favorable product mix, together helping offset inflationary pressures during the quarter.

Operating expenses increased in absolute terms as revenue scaled, and included the INR126 million provision for US import duty tariff incurred in the previous year; these amounts remain recoverable and efforts continue to pursue recovery, but a provision was made based on recovery risk assessment.

The INR169 million exceptional charge relates to settlement of a litigation matter in the U.S. District Court disclosed in the 2021 prospectus; settlement completed without any admission of liability; EBITDA figures exclude this exceptional item.
Other income increase primarily driven by higher forex gains during the period.
Gross margin expansion in Q1 vs Q4 attributed to mix plus forex, not to any material cost pass-through (pass-throughs not yet materialized).

Management believes Q1 margin (20.4% adjusted) is slightly elevated due to ~40% revenue coming from international revenue and strong mix/currency advantage; guidance given at start of year (targeting inching towards 19% full-year, vs 18.1% in FY26) is maintained, with possible overachievement.
CFO reiterated endeavor to sustain current margin levels while focusing on growth ('sustain margin while growing' philosophy).

subsections.label: Capital allocation and balance sheet
points: Capex program to continue to be phased in line with customer validations, order visibility and expected utilization; investments to meet internal return threshold and support profitable, sustainable growth.
Balance sheet focus remains on financial discipline, funding growth-led capex; working capital (receivables, inventory) monitored closely to ensure growth is supported by healthy cash conversion.
No updated overall capex number given for the year despite new order book and expansion; company continues to evaluate capex plans.

No immediate fundraise required at this time; company monitoring cash flows and comfortable funding investments through leveraging, which is currently at a very low level; will keep monitoring situation quarter-on-quarter and take appropriate decision if fundraise needed for any opportunity.

Current business updates/projections consider only organic growth, but management keeps eyes/ears open for inorganic opportunities in non-auto segments and will evaluate if something appropriate arises.

subsections.label: Order book dynamics
points: ADS customers - especially aerospace and semicon equipment manufacturers (SEM) - have very tall outsourcing targets from India's perspective, reflected in growing order book position.
Additional orders received in Q2 pushed ADS order backlog from INR44.4 billion to around INR57.5 billion currently, executable over the next five years.

ADS orders are structurally different from the standard order book: given as peak annual revenue for new business instead of total cumulative backlog; ADS value has been removed from standard order book numbers for other businesses to avoid duplication.

New large SEM order is from an existing customer, in the semicon space, won post the normal cutoff date (July 1) in the last couple of weeks; propels engagement with this single customer to almost $75 million worth of annual business.

Company is actively working on further RFQs on the table in semicon as well as aerospace division; INR5,700 crore is 'confirmed' order book executable by FY2031, not a target - actual achievement is expected to be higher as conversions are at an advanced stage, with many expected in Q2 and Q3.
New SEM order revenue expected to start becoming significant in calendar year 2027 and peak in calendar year 2029, driven by mother-machine arrival lead times.

Confirmed backlog of INR5,700 crore by FY31 includes aerospace, semicon and defense combined; any future wins will add to this bucket; this backlog is described as part of the broader INR8,000-9,000 crore company revenue vision for FY2031, not necessarily an upside to it.

subsections.label: Domestic and export demand trends
points: Domestic OEM customers across the board talking about hyper-growth, high vehicle volumes and continued consolidation of supply chain towards better capitalized, more capable suppliers.
PV exposure historically balanced between domestic and export markets; exports saw moderation last year but are now seeing traction back to normal growth trajectory.

Healthy growth seen in off-road segment and good growth from passenger vehicle segment in exports; domestic two-wheeler and PV industry demand continuing to surprise, extending strongly into Q2, with festive season (Q2/Q3) expected to sustain momentum through at least the next one and a half quarters.
Demand strong enough to stress supply chain on raw material/child parts; customer interventions are helping secure material in time.
Deliveries commenced into the energy segment for a key North American customer, expected to give sustained revenues from Q3.

Increased momentum from US customers to source more from Sansera India as a stop-gap arrangement while awaiting certainty on tariffs before starting planned US connecting rod manufacturing facility; contributing to increased exports of premium product.

subsections.label: Non-auto/ADS as growth driver
points: Non-auto segment delivered its highest-ever quarterly sales, with ADS remaining the primary growth driver within it.
Auto Tech-Agnostic and xEV segment achieved its highest-ever quarterly sales, reflecting accelerated EV adoption, especially in two-wheelers.
Auto ICE segment delivered healthy growth on a high base, with highest-ever quarterly performance across passenger vehicles, commercial vehicles, and scooters during the quarter.

subsections.label: Motorcycle/PV wallet share clarification
points: Management stated no wallet share has been lost with any customer; share has been increasing with TVS, Yamaha and Suzuki; motorcycle revenue growth (~12.5%) differs from industry volume growth (17-18%) as company reports on revenue basis, not volume, creating a possible gap; management to follow up offline on precise figures.

With Maruti, company has been gaining market share; Maruti remains a top customer with strong projected engagement over the next couple of years; ~75% of relevant component volumes supplied by Sansera to Maruti.

subsections.label: New order wins detail
points: New order wins of INR88 crore in PV-CV and INR75 crore in two-wheeler segment described as normal course of business given engagement with 87 customers; no further specific details provided beyond the large ADS/SEM order.

subsections.label: ADS capacity expansion
points: Recently inaugurated a surface treatment facility next to the ADS plant; in process of obtaining NADCAP validation for this; surface treatment allows completing production within a single facility, in line with Sansera's history of backward integration, giving better speed, quality control, and reduced external dependency as the company enters larger, more complex structural parts.

Relocating defense business to a dedicated facility separate from rest of ADS to provide focused infrastructure and enhanced operational execution, aimed at tapping opportunities in defense sector domestically and via exports; revenue capacity from dedicated defense facility estimated at ~INR500 crore over the next 5 years.

Building new 80,000 sq ft hangar for aero and SEM business; lines will be installed and validated by customers in this hangar in coming quarters; hangar expected to be commissioned in a month or two at the latest; existing facility plus extended hangar together expected to support revenue capacity of INR1,400-1,500 crore.
Special process facility approval/certification process underway, expected in maximum a month or two.

Working on a build-to-suit facility not far from existing location, discussions expected to conclude in August, facility ready in about 10 months, adding a further 100,000 sq ft (also referenced as 110,000 sq ft elsewhere); all facilities will be within a vicinity of 500 meters; this new facility expected to support revenue capacity of ~INR1,500 crore.
Total ADS facility revenue capacity across all sites targeted at ~INR3,500 crore by FY2031.

Capex is a continuous, parallel activity given machine lead times of 7-9 months; asset turns for ADS business comfortably between 2x and 2.25x when checking peak revenue potential versus assets invested.

Company has commissioned a large-size special process facility accommodating components up to 4 meters, complementing existing 5-axis machining facility (10 different types of 5-axis machining) to target more complex parts like door assemblies, fuselage, structural parts, seating elements in SEM and aerospace - moving up the value chain; hope to get NADCAP and customer approvals for this special process within the quarter, which will add capability, cut lead time for development/supplies, and be margin accretive.

subsections.label: Auto segment capacity expansion
points: At Pantnagar (Plant 6) and Manesar (Plant 4), setting up additional forging and machining capabilities mainly for crankshafts for two-wheeler and passenger vehicle OEMs, and connecting rods for PV OEMs.

At Bangalore Plant 2, augmenting machining capacity with focus on Auto Tech-Agnostic and xEV components, complemented by the Sansera-Nichidai JV which deepens presence in cold and warm forged precision components.
Projects on both ADS and auto sides will come on stream beginning Q3 FY27 onwards and will be completed within a year.

Pantnagar expansion is a fully automated crankshaft facility for two-wheelers, driven by substantial demand increase from south-based two-wheeler manufacturers and OEM outsourcing opportunities; crankshaft demand in north facilities also driving connecting rod demand manufactured in Bangalore.

Four-wheeler (Maruti and other OEM) volumes pushing demand for expansion; forging facility, secondary operations and heat treatment also being expanded in Pantnagar, not just machining; new multi-story building being constructed in Plant 2 as part of this expansion.
Any expansion in Auto, especially forging and heat treatment facilities, takes 18-24 months, requiring a roughly two-year forward view from customers to expand meaningfully.

subsections.label: Customer engagement and market share
points: Company engaged with most large OEMs, discussing capacity expansion given long lead times for facility expansion.
No wallet share lost with any customer in motorcycle segment; share increasing with TVS, Yamaha and Suzuki.
Maruti remains a top customer with strong projected engagement for the next couple of years; company gaining market share with Maruti.
Company engaged with 87 customers overall.

subsections.label: New segment opportunities beyond ADS
points: Growth prospects being explored in non-ADS/non-automotive areas including power sector (both transmission and storage) and humanoids, viewed as a potentially big opportunity as some peers have flagged; company will keep working on how to enter these segments.

Defense: current offering is precision machined components for small batch quantities to ISRO, HAL, with some exports to companies in Israel; now aiming to close large order wins for customers outside India, mainly in Europe, and to add sheet metal as an additional offering for both defense and aerospace, which is expected to significantly improve RFQ package competitiveness.

subsections.label: Organic vs inorganic growth stance
points: Current projections and business updates consider only organic growth.
Management keeps eyes and ears open for opportunities across segments, especially non-auto, and would evaluate an inorganic opportunity if something appropriate comes their way.
No capital raise deemed necessary at this time given strong cash flows and low leverage; balance sheet strong enough to fund investments through leveraging.

subsections.label: Capital allocation decision framework
points: Decisions on where to invest driven by return ratios and long-term strategy; a committee recommends and reviews quotations before quoting/deciding.

Nature of business and future prospects can take precedence over return ratio if there is a challenge in return ratio, particularly for aerospace, defense and semicon given the large opportunity size, while the automotive base business continues to grow in healthy double digits and generate customer interest, translating into a strong order book.

subsections.label: Cost inflation
points: Material cost increase not very substantial, primarily in aluminum (small portion of total material consumption) and in some consumables where exceptionally high inflation impacted the quarter.
Steel inflation limited; company engaging with customers for pass-through, currently in process but not yet translated into financials.

Higher labor costs have impacted especially Northern plants; company continues to engage with customers for compensation for tooling and higher labor costs; nothing of this has come into balance sheet/P&L yet in Q1.
Some cushion/short-term respite from forex movement (higher realization) while pass-through negotiations continue.

subsections.label: Supply chain and capacity stress
points: Strong demand from two-wheeler and PV segments is creating stress on the supply chain, both on raw material and child parts, and capacity constraints; customer interventions are helping secure material in time.

subsections.label: US tariff/litigation related
points: Provision of INR126 million made for US import duty tariff incurred in the previous year; amounts remain recoverable and efforts continue to pursue recovery, but provision made based on recovery risk assessment.
Exceptional charge of INR169 million for settlement of a US District Court litigation matter (disclosed in 2021 prospectus), settled without admission of liability.

subsections.label: ADS segment specific risks
points: Aerospace: significantly lower risk given ultimate customers Boeing and Airbus, increasing number of programs, and rising aircraft order backlogs; risk would only arise from a catastrophic event similar to what happened to Boeing about 6 years ago.

Semicon: current boom significantly driven by AI demand and data centers, with equipment suppliers (Sansera's primary market) very busy and expected to be unable to fully meet demand until FY29-FY30; this is described as the near-term risk/constraint characterization for the segment.
No components currently in production expected to hit significant end-of-life in the ADS business over the next few years.

subsections.label: US facility timeline uncertainty
points: Planned US facility for manufacturing connecting rods remains on hold, awaiting certainty on tariff situation before starting operations; in the interim, US customers are increasingly sourcing more from Sansera India as a stop-gap arrangement.

subsections.label: Growth outlook
points: Auto ICE segment expected to end FY27 with high-teens top-line growth with continuous focus on improving margin profile.
Management expects a good possibility of high-teens to 20% overall revenue growth in FY27 if current business trends continue.
Non-ADS business (all other businesses put together) expected to deliver mid-teens growth easily, with possibility of moving towards mid-teens to high-teens as the business evolves month-on-month.
ADS growth expectation of ~75-80% for FY27.

Too early to confirm whether 20%+ growth can be sustained for the next two-to-three years, but strong momentum is expected to continue; a roughly two-year customer view is needed before committing to meaningful capacity expansion given 18-24 month lead times for auto forging/heat treatment facilities.

subsections.label: Margin outlook
points: Q1 margin considered slightly elevated due to high international revenue mix (~40%) and favorable mix/currency; guidance given at the start of the year (inching towards 19% full-year, from 18.1% FY26) maintained, with possible overachievement.
Aspiration to achieve 20-20-20 targets; management does not want to commit to a specific number but reiterates achieving/slightly overachieving original guidance.
ADS and export businesses targeted to operate between 25% and 30% EBITDA margins; as capacity utilization improves, margins expected to move towards higher end (high-20s).

subsections.label: ADS ramp and revenue guidance timing
points: ADS revenue not expected to reach INR1,500 crore next year; there will be a progression depending on commissioning; INR5,700 crore is mandatorily executable by FY2031.
Exact ADS revenue guidance for next year to be given towards the end of this year, depending on status of plan, validation, and other factors.
Overall company revenue ambition of INR8,000-9,000 crore by end of decade / FY2031.

subsections.label: Capex outlook
points: No updated capex number given for the year despite new order book and expansion plans; capex plans continue to be evaluated and phased in line with customer validations, order visibility and expected utilization.

guidance_ledger.statement: We expect to end FY27 with high-teens top-line growth with continuous focus on improving margin profile.
It is a good possibility that we should be looking at between high-teens to 20% as overall revenue.
Non-ADS business itself, we should be able to look at a mid-teen kind of growth easily... more of mid-teens to high-teens kind of growth in our other businesses as well.
Our growth, which will be about 75%-80% in ADS.
Last year, our overall margin was 18.1%, and we would be more happier that if we are able to inch towards 19%... we would like to achieve it, slightly maybe overachieve it.
We are very aspirational, we are working towards achieving our 20-20-20 targets.

We are targeting or we are operating between 25% to 30% EBITDA margins in both these sectors [export and ADS]; as we improve our capacity utilization, the numbers would be more towards higher north of high-20s.

guidance_ledger.metric: Company revenue by end of decade

INR5,700 crores executable by FY2031... mandatorily executable or has to be executed by FY2031; execution timeline for order book to achieve peak revenue in next... years remains unchanged.
ADS is not going to go to INR1,500 crore revenue next year; there will be a progression... exact numbers we will be able to give you a guidance towards the end of this year.
By FY'31, our base plan as per the current visibility is to create a facility which will generate a revenue of about INR3,500 crores.
We would start seeing revenues in this new order, significant revenues, calendar year 2027, and it will peak calendar year 2029.
We have not [given an updated capex number]... we continue to evaluate our capex plans.

We don't think at this moment it is necessary for us to look at any additional fundraise... we will keep monitoring the situation... and take an appropriate decision if at all we need to look at a fundraise at some point of time.

key_takeaways: We started FY27 on a very strong note, delivering our highest-ever quarterly revenue while maintaining healthy profitability.

Our quarterly revenues crossed INR10,000 million milestone, reaching INR10,213 million, representing a year-on-year growth of 33%. EBITDA and PAT margins remained resilient at 19.2% and 8.6% respectively.
The non-auto segment delivered its highest-ever quarterly sales of INR1,998 million, registering an impressive 129.9% year-on-year growth... contribution increased to 20.8% of our overall sales.

Our cumulative unexecuted lifetime order book for five years, especially for ADS business, stood at INR44.4 billion as of quarter end... orders received in Q2 have pushed our ADS order backlog to around INR57.5 billion currently.
As of June 2026, our peak annual revenue of our new business ex of ADS stood at INR18.5 billion.

EBITDA for the quarter stood at INR1,961 million, reflecting strong year-on-year growth of 48%. Profitability also improved with EBITDA margin expanding by around 200 basis points to 19.2% compared with 17.2% in the same quarter previous year.
The quarter included an exceptional charge of INR169 million towards settlement of a litigation matter in the U.S. District Court.
Profit after-tax at INR874 million, up 39% year-on-year with PAT margins improving to 8.6%.
With this, we expect to end FY27 with high-teens top-line growth with continuous focus on improving margin profile.

quarters.summary: FY'26 was a record year for Sansera with highest-ever revenue and improving EBITDA/PAT margins, driven by ADS diversification, capacity expansion (Pantnagar) and the Nichidai JV. Management guided FY'27 to sustain similar growth with healthy profitability, citing H1 stronger than H2 in Auto due to base effect, continued caution on input cost inflation, and long-term visibility of ADS/company revenue scaling toward INR8,000-10,000 crores over the decade, though order inflows from international customers remained soft amid global uncertainty.

key_takeaways: FY '26 marked highest ever annual performance with a top line of INR34,979 million and improved EBITDA and PAT margins, reflecting strong operational resilience and successful delivery of growth objectives.
This also includes achievement of ADS segment guidance with ADS revenue from product sales reaching INR3,155 million, representing exceptional growth of 155% during the year.
Q4 FY '26 delivered highest ever quarterly revenue of INR9,987 million, with margins improving every quarter through the year, primarily led by revenue mix and operating leverage.
Core Auto ICE business delivered highest ever quarterly revenue of INR6,426 million, registering healthy Y-o-Y growth of 21.6%, driven by passenger vehicles and commercial vehicles.
Non-Auto business delivered record revenues of INR1,736 million, registering robust growth of 70.5% year-on-year, with ADS business more than doubling on a year-on-year basis.

New order booking for the quarter remained soft, largely from international customers due to global uncertainty; cumulative unexecuted lifetime order backlog for 5 years, especially for ADS business, stands at INR44.6 billion.
Company incurred capex of INR5,097 million in FY '26, expects similar level of investment in FY '27, directed towards expanding ICE capabilities and new ADS facilities.
Board approved acquisition of about 10 acres of land near the international airport for ADS expansion, anticipating running out of space given the strong momentum in aerospace and semicon.

SUPRIYA.about: Supriya Lifescience is engaged in the manufacturing of Active pharmaceutical ingredients (APIs). As of March 31, 2021, the company produces 38 APIs focused on diverse therapeutic segments such as antihistamine, analgesic, anaesthetic, vitamin, anti-asthmatic and anti-allergic.[1]

quarters.summary: Q1 FY27 revenue grew 31% YoY to Rs.190 crores despite ~Rs.35 crores of sales deferred due to water shortages; EBITDA declined 8.1% YoY to Rs.47 crores (margin 25%) due to temporary water and power cost headwinds, but management reiterated FY27 guidance of ~Rs.1,000 crores revenue and EBITDA margins of 32-35%, with a much stronger ramp-up expected in H2 FY27 as new launches (anesthetics, ADHD, contrast media) and Ambernath/CMO-CDMO opportunities scale up.
