subsections.label: Margin decline drivers
points: Delayed onset of monsoon led to water scarcity around the Lote MIDC plant, which depends on water supply from the Koyna River; the entire Lote MIDC industrial belt faced significant water shortage, causing sales deferment.
Maharashtra government changed the solar power policy, leading to increased fuel and power costs during the quarter, impacting EBITDA by Rs.8 crores.
Excluding one-off impacts, margins would have remained within guided range; challenges were largely external and transient in nature.

Retrospective solar subsidy cost (Rs.4.5-5 crores) relates to government asking payment from July 2025 backdated over a four-month period (March to July); matter is sub judice with a case filed by Solar Power Association members against MSEDCL.

Revenue mix (lower Europe sales) and production losses that prevented certain materials from going to regulated markets also contributed to EBITDA dip, in addition to backward integration mix decline.

subsections.label: Working capital and borrowings
points: For the full year, company has not utilized any working capital limits, except for letters of credit and bank guarantees.
Inventory was built up in anticipation of the planned Q2 maintenance shutdown; now that the shutdown plan has changed, inventory will need to be liquidated over the next three to four quarters.

subsections.label: CapEx and depreciation
points: Q1 FY27 CapEx driven by maintenance CapEx, smaller projects, formulation plant requirements and the Isambe (Patalganga) project.
Patalganga Phase-1 total CapEx earmarked at around Rs.200 crores, covering two API/advanced intermediate blocks and two formulation blocks; Phase-2 would have a similar or larger CapEx number.
Ambernath alone expected to contribute Rs.14-15 crores to depreciation, taking overall depreciation to near Rs.35-40 crores.

subsections.label: Therapy mix
points: Vitamins segment performed well in the quarter, linked to DSM ramp-up reaching a very stable state, close to peak volumes; dedicated DSM facility now up and running; pharma validation completed.
Cardiovascular product launched in Q3 FY26 has ramped up well; commercialized with good traction from domestic market and semi-regulated markets.
ADHD product continues to scale up, supported by healthy demand from LATAM and Europe.
Liquid anesthetic product remains on track with steady monthly supplies.

Cardiovascular advanced intermediate volumes have built up well in recent months, at almost commercialized manufacturing level, but full contribution still expected to take 9-12 months as customers remain under qualification/stability testing.

Anesthetic API launched is seeing good traction from semi-regulated markets like Korea and Taiwan; CEP filed, expected to be received between October-November, which will boost sales in regulated markets like Europe.
Revenue mix decline from backward integrated products attributed partly to lower Europe sales and production losses preventing materials from reaching regulated markets.

subsections.label: North America
points: Sequential improvement in North America driven by multiple US DMFs filed (at least 4-5), with customers picking up volumes for validation.
Once newer products launching scale up in North America, sales and exposure expected to rise further.
Company's exposure is currently larger in Europe, including for finished formulations; Europe and Latin America remain the highest revenue regions due to the inherent nature of the product portfolio.

Not much impact currently from US tariff scenario; a potential 100% tariff on pharma could emerge after a couple of years, but existing scenario has little tariff impact; too speculative to comment further.

subsections.label: New product launches
points: Launched two new anesthetic liquid inhalation products in Q2 FY27 from the Ambernath facility, expected to scale up over coming quarters.
Two ADHD product launches in the pipeline to strengthen the portfolio and support future growth.

Contrast media opportunity remains on track with development, expected to launch in H2 FY27; launch delayed by two quarters because R&D is still fine-tuning the technology given multiple variations in raw material cost, and the company is exploring alternate processes/technology to be cost-competitive since this is already a long-standing generic product.

Contrast media commercial approach: combination of API for non-regulated markets and, at Ambernath, tie-ups for finished formulation (Iohexol injection) targeting semi-regulated and regulated markets.

subsections.label: R&D investment and organizational build-out
points: R&D strength has grown from about 20-30 people to almost 70 people over the last two to three years, with new verticals like finished formulation added.
Two R&D segregations now exist: Lote (life cycle management historically) and Ambernath (API and finished formulation).
Company has invested in ESG-related certifications (EcoVadis Silver rating recently received, FSSAI, ISO) driven by CDMO/CMO collaborations with larger innovators/multinationals.
New dedicated pilot plant set up for scale-up of CMO/CDMO projects; dedicated project team spans R&D to pilot to commercial scale-up, led by technical lead Dr. Shirish Ambekar.

ATS-8 product: visibility of 250 metric tons target reiterated, to be achieved over the next two years once fully commercialized; not guided for the current year given gradual customer validation/stability/filing process.

key_figures.label: Adityapal implied quarterly revenue run-rate to achieve FY27 target

subsections.label: Maintenance shutdown plan revised
points: Company revisited earlier plan to undertake annual maintenance shutdown for Blocks A to D in August; instead will undertake maintenance in a phased manner, so Q2 FY27 production will not be significantly impacted.

Initially planned a large shutdown across multiple blocks in Q2, but due to production time already lost in Q1 from water/other issues, the shutdown has been pushed back; smaller debottlenecking activities will be taken up across blocks instead to avoid major production impact.

subsections.label: Patalganga (Isambe project)
points: Received all necessary clearances; developing facility in phases; will include two API/advanced intermediate blocks and two formulation blocks.
Boundary wall construction has already started (ground technically broken); work on constructing walls in full stream.
First focus at Patalganga will be on the API block along with utility blocks, covered under the Rs.200 crores Phase-1; formulation block will not start immediately.
As per MIDC requirement, ~40% completion expected within around 2.5 years from acquisition; company will manage legal requirements during construction.

Rationale for prioritizing API: company is closer to exhausting capacity at Lote; minor refurbishments at Lote will further enhance capacity, but Patalganga is being planned as a scale-up site for larger molecules/next launches.
Ambernath is not yet in full swing; finished formulation scale-up will happen there over next 2-3 years, so finished formulation at Patalganga will be considered in a phase-wise manner in Phase-2.

subsections.label: Block F
points: Work on Block F has not yet started; expected to begin in the next couple of quarters.

subsections.label: Water and power constraints
points: Facility located in Lote MIDC area depends on water supply from Koyna River; lower-than-normal water levels caused significant shortage across the industrial belt — first such incident faced, despite the area normally receiving some of the highest rainfall in Maharashtra.
Water issue has since been resolved; ample water now being received from Koyna River and MIDC; not expected to recur in Q2.
Company is working with consultants on water recycling for utility purposes (cooling towers etc.), though recycled water cannot be used in end product manufacturing given API nature of business.

A large part of the power cost increase in Q1 was retrospective in nature and will not recur in Q2; going-forward operational price increases (including raw material solvent price increases) will be passed on to customers since company operates on a purchase-order basis.

subsections.label: Export mix drivers
points: Exports continued to be a key growth driver contributing 81% of revenue in Q1 FY27, with Asia at 39%, Europe at 35%, and LATAM at 20% within exports.
Europe and Latin America remain the company's highest revenue regions given the current product portfolio's larger market share there.
Lower Europe sales during the quarter contributed to reduced EBITDA margin.

subsections.label: Systems and process strengthening
points: Company is under SAP implementation, expected to go live in another four to five months, further strengthening internal systems.
Introducing automation across sites; implemented softwares like TrackWise for quality management systems and documentation.
Site-level automation includes gravity flow systems and DCS systems to reduce manual intervention.

key_figures.label: Export revenue share from regulated markets (within >80% export contribution)

subsections.label: CMO/CDMO progress
points: Good progress on one large anesthetic CDMO contract; company is very close to signing a term sheet, with qualification work largely completed and quality approved at the back end; announcement expected next quarter.
Liquid anesthetic seen as one of the biggest areas of collaboration with an innovator, with potentially large opportunity size; project ongoing and moving well.
Four to five additional APIs/advanced intermediates under discussion with regulated-market customers, though at an initial stage.

Ambernath, a predominantly CMO/CDMO-driven site, has launched two anesthetic finished-formulation products and has five to six products in pipeline (tablets, injectables) with collaboration interest from customers in Europe and North America.
Management expects CMO/CDMO to become one of the company's strongest verticals over the next three to four years.

subsections.label: Competitive positioning
points: Company will not disclose individual product-level revenue or margin contribution details.

Contrast media market has limited formulators (four to five) who often keep specifications closed, requiring in-house R&D to fine-tune technology and processes to be cost-competitive against long-established generics.

subsections.label: Diversification strategy
points: Strategy focused on adding multiple verticals to de-risk the business: previously purely API-focused, now adding finished formulation vertical and CMO/CDMO vertical.
Bringing in professionals with expertise in these new verticals to build organizational readiness.
Capacity building underway to support scale-up of new product portfolio launches.

Growth beyond FY27 expected to continue at ~20% CAGR, supported by new API basket additions, newer therapies, Ambernath's finished formulation revenue post-audit, and CMO-CDMO collaborations across API, advanced intermediate, and finished formulation levels; management believes growth could exceed 20% given multiple ongoing initiatives, contingent on pace of regulatory approvals since over 80% of revenue comes from exports, largely from regulated markets.

Speculative future tariff on pharma products

subsections.label: Legal/regulatory matter (customs/export authorization)
points: Matter regarding a psychotropic drug export consignment remains sub judice; company has received a new export authorization from Central Bureau of Narcotics for the same consignment, which in the company's opinion should regularize the export, but the company is awaiting a High Court ruling.
Shipping bill for the consignment already filed and under investigation; company not free to cancel it; consignment value is very small/miniscule.
Each consignment of this product requires its own export permit; the issue is isolated to this one consignment and does not affect other customers, countries, or products.

Root cause was a two-day technical lapse/human oversight by the logistics department, where the export authorization had expired before the shipping bill was raised; all required documents were otherwise in place.
No provision has been made against these booked sales since the new re-export permit has been obtained and company believes the matter should be resolved amicably.
General manager involved in the matter remains in judicial custody; no other employees are involved in the matter.

subsections.label: Water scarcity risk
points: First-time water scarcity incident at Lote MIDC due to delayed monsoon onset and lower Koyna River water levels; impacted operations for about 15-20 days.
Company working with consultants on recycling water for utility use to mitigate future risk, though recycled water cannot be used in API end-product manufacturing.

subsections.label: Power/regulatory cost risk
points: Maharashtra government's change in solar power policy increased fuel and power costs; a portion of this was a retrospective charge (Rs.4.5-5 crores) which is under litigation via a case filed by Solar Power Association members against MSEDCL.
Ongoing power/raw material price increases will be passed on to customers given purchase-order based business model.

subsections.label: Tariff risk
points: Currently limited pharma tariff impact from the US, but a potential 100% tariff on pharma products could emerge after a couple of years; considered too speculative to quantify at this stage.
Company's exposure to North America is relatively small (~3% of revenue); Europe and Latin America remain larger markets, limiting current tariff risk.

subsections.label: Information/market conduct observation
points: An investor raised an observation of stock price reacting in correlation with earnings events across recent quarters (Q4 and Q1), suggesting possible information spillage; management stated this is not something they can speculate on or control.

key_figures.label: Margin guidance range for next 3-4 years

subsections.label: Revenue and margin trajectory
points: Trajectory towards Rs.1,000 crores revenue by FY27 remains firmly on track, supported by a robust product pipeline and sustained demand across key therapeutic segments including anesthetics, anti-diabetics, anti-anxiety, vitamins, and ADHD.
Company remains confident of EBITDA margin guidance range of 33% to 35% (later reconfirmed as 32% to 35%), despite Q1 miss, since one-off water and power cost impacts are viewed as transient.
Growth expected to be non-linear across quarters.

Management confident it can make up the lost Rs.25-30 crores of sales in the coming few quarters and still achieve the ~Rs.1,000 crores target for the full year while maintaining EBITDA margin between 32% and 35%.
Full-year confidence reiterated for the ~Rs.1,000 crores target even though recovery timing during Q2 specifically remains uncertain; recovery may spread across the next three quarters.

subsections.label: H2 FY27 ramp-up expectations
points: Ramp-up expected to be much stronger in the second half of FY27 versus current run rate, driven by liquid anesthetic scale-up from Ambernath, contrast media launch, and cardiovascular drug scale-up.

Potential exists to grow beyond the 20% CAGR trajectory given multiple initiatives (capacity addition, new products/verticals, CMO/CDMO opportunities at initial discussion stage), though this is contingent on pace of regulatory approvals given the export-heavy, regulated-market-driven revenue base.

subsections.label: Margin outlook with formulation mix shift
points: Margins expected to remain around the 33% to 35% guided range for at least the next three to four years, even as company moves towards finished formulation and CMO/CDMO business, because new products typically first scale up in semi-regulated markets before regulated markets, and this cycle will continue.

subsections.label: EU audit and regulatory approvals
points: EU audit for Ambernath facility scheduled for the second half of November.
CEP filing for anesthetic API expected to be received between October and November, which will further boost sales in regulated markets like Europe.
Growth beyond FY27/FY28 expected to continue at 20%+ CAGR, with potential acceleration once Ambernath is fully commercialized and Patalganga capacity comes online.

guidance_ledger.statement: Trajectory towards the Rs.1,000 crores revenue by FY27 remains firmly on track, supported by a robust product pipeline and sustained demand across key therapeutic segments including anesthetics, anti-diabetics, anti-anxiety, vitamins, and ADHD.
We have already said that we would be growing at a CAGR of about 20% year-on-year; the same trend would continue.
We remain confident of our guidance of EBITDA margins in the range of 33% to 35%; reconfirmed as closer to 32% to 35% while still confident of achieving the guidance of closer to Rs.1,000 crores.
Revenue for the quarter stood at Rs.190 crores, reflecting a 31% year-on-year growth.
EBITDA stood at Rs.47 crores, a decline of 8.1% year-on-year with EBITDA margins at 25%.
We are still confident that we will be able to make up for this lost Rs.25 crores - Rs.30 crores of sales in the coming few quarters.
Launched two new anesthetic liquid inhalation products in Q2 FY27 from Ambernath; two ADHD product launches in the pipeline.
On the contrast media opportunity, we remain on track with development and continue to progress as planned. We expect the products to be launched in H2 FY27.
We have already received the dates for audit from EU at Ambernath facility. The audit is scheduled for the second half of November.
We have received all necessary clearances and will be developing the facility in phases; boundary wall construction has already started; total CapEx earmarked for Phase-1 is around Rs.200 crores.
We haven't started it yet. We will be starting it in next couple of quarters.

We have revisited our earlier plan to undertake the annual maintenance shutdown for Blocks A to D in August, and we believe that we can undertake the maintenance in a phased manner instead of a complete shutdown; it will not impact Q2 FY27 production in any major way.
We had said that the 250 metric ton number will be achieved in the next two years' time once it is fully commercialized; not guided for this particular year.
Ambernath alone would contribute Rs.14-15 crores; overall should be nearing Rs.35-40 crores.
There is definitely potential in the business to grow beyond that 20%, keeping in mind the different areas in which management is working, though contingent on regulatory approval timing.
In the next three to four years, CMO, CDMO will come up as one of the company's strongest verticals.
The margins would remain at that 33% to 35% at least for the next three to four years.
We are actually under SAP implementation, so we will be live in another four to five months.
For it to be a larger contributor, it would still take at least 9 to 12 months because a lot of the customers are still under qualification.
We are very close to signing a term sheet. So, hopefully in the next quarter, we will be able to announce something good.
We achieved our FY '26 revenue target... Financial year '26 revenue grew to 18.9% year-on-year to INR828 crores, in line with our guided growth of ~20%.
EBITDA margins were at 35.5% for FY26, surpassing our guided range of 33% to 35%.
The 300 metric ton, I think will come very close to that number in FY27, looking at the current order book that we have.
The peak that we expect is about INR60 crores, which we'll be able to see in FY27.

In FY27, as far as the finished formulation liquid anesthetic ramp-up is there, we'll not see much revenue contribution. The liquid anesthetic contribution will only come from the API from the Lote side because it will take us 3 to 4 years to get the ramp-up in the finished formulation facility.
We have some indication from them that the audit would be scheduled in H2 of FY27... typically around October or November.
We still have not got the dates for USFDA audit. We are following up with them. However, due to unavailability of auditors, we are not able to get a date as of now.
In FY27, you can see some revenue contribution from Ambernath mainly coming in from the semi-regulated markets... the full effect of Ambernath revenue contribution will still take about 2 to 3 years.
I think the average will be somewhere between 24 to 25.17%, that would be the rate you will be landing to... for full year, you can expect somewhere around say 25.17%.
We are looking at around 170 to 180 days going forward... we believe that somewhere around 170 to 180 days, I think, should be a stable state number.
We will be able to maintain between 80 to 85 days even at the worst of times.

The larger guidance on FY28 and the next couple of years, we'll only be able to give in the coming few quarters because we still have not reached the full revenue potential of Ambernath, the regulatory approvals have not yet come in.
It completely depends on the product mix for us... up and until nothing is signed and the term sheets are not there, we'll not be able to guide on the full potential numbers.
Revenue will take at least 2 years because the development has also not started... I think it will still take 2 years minimum for some revenue to start coming in from this.
I'm not seeing any large revenue that can come in FY27.
We'll not be able to give any quarter-on-quarter guidance of the run rate... all quarters might not be linear growth.

key_takeaways: Revenue for the quarter stood at Rs. 190 crores, reflecting a 31% year-on-year growth. Demand remained strong during the quarter, but water shortages led to a deferment of sales of around Rs. 35 crores.

EBITDA stood at Rs. 47 crores, a decline of 8.1% year-on-year with EBITDA margins at 25%, impacted by water scarcity and a Maharashtra solar power policy change that had an impact of Rs. 8 crores at EBITDA levels.

Excluding these one-off impacts, margins would have remained within our guided range; we believe these are temporary disruptions and expect performance to improve in coming quarters while remaining firmly on track to achieve our FY '27 growth and margin objectives.
Exports contributed 81% of revenue in Q1 FY '27; within exports, Asia contributed 39%, Europe 35%, and LATAM 20%. Currently 72% of total revenues are fully backward integrated.

We launched two new anesthetic liquid inhalation products in Q2 FY '27 from Ambernath and expect them to scale up; two ADHD product launches are in the pipeline; contrast media products expected to launch in H2 FY '27.

Our trajectory towards the Rs. 1,000 crores revenue by FY '27 remains firmly on track, supported by a robust product pipeline and sustained demand across key therapeutic segments; we remain confident of our guidance of EBITDA margins in the range of 33% to 35%.

We have revisited our earlier plan to undertake the annual maintenance shutdown for Blocks A to D in August, and we believe that we can undertake the maintenance in a phased manner instead of a complete shutdown; it will not impact Q2 FY '27's production in any major way.
PAT stood at Rs. 24 crores as against Rs. 35 crores in Q1 FY '26; PAT margins stood at 12.7% for Q1 FY '27; CapEx for Q1 FY '27 stood at Rs. 16.58 crores.

quarters.summary: Supriya Lifescience delivered record Q4/FY26 revenue and EBITDA, achieving its FY26 revenue target (~19% YoY growth) and EBITDA margin at the upper end of its guided range despite geopolitical/supply-chain headwinds. Management reiterated ~20% annual revenue growth and 33-35% EBITDA margin guidance, and remains confident of reaching the INR1,000 crores revenue milestone by FY27, aided by Ambernath ramp-up, new product launches (anesthetics, ADHD, cardiovascular intermediate, contrast media) and the newly cleared Patalganga expansion, though growth will not be linear due to a scheduled Q2 FY27 maintenance shutdown.

key_figures.label: Current EBITDA margin range referenced in discussion

subsections.label: P&L Drivers
points: FY26 revenue growth of 18.9% YoY to INR828 crores was in line with guided growth of ~20%.
EBITDA margin of 35.5% for FY26 surpassed the guided range of 33% to 35%, driven by favorable product mix, expanding global demand and disciplined cost management.

Q4 EBITDA margin percentage looked slightly lower in relative terms versus FY26 because Ambernath expenses have started while Ambernath revenue has not yet started (per CFO/MD commentary on margin, not on gross margin specifically).

subsections.label: Capex & Capital Allocation
points: FY26 capex of INR152 crores was largely driven by spend on the Ambernath facility, along with maintenance capex and smaller projects including the Ribo Block and formulation plant requirements.
Patalganga Phase 1 total capex earmarked is around INR200 crores, to be spent over the next 2 years, covering two API/advanced intermediate blocks and two formulation blocks.
F block at Lote Parshuram expected to require INR40 crores to INR50 crores of capex.

subsections.label: Borrowings
points: For the full year, the company did not utilize any working capital limits, except for letters of credit and bank guarantees.

subsections.label: Working Capital & Cash Conversion
points: Working capital days increased as the business grew, driven by higher debtor days from revenue booked in the last two months of the year; company expects to stabilize at 170-180 days going forward as Ambernath comes into the picture.

Inventory days near 200 days attributed to higher inventory needs from backward integration on high-volume products (cardiovascular intermediate, liquid anesthetic) requiring larger intermediate holding, plus Ambernath inventory addition of INR10-15 crores.

Receivable days moved from 72 to 78 days mainly due to revenue booked in the last 2 months; management expects to maintain between 80-85 days even at worst times, partly aided by advance payments taken on control substances.

subsections.label: Cardiovascular Intermediate Demand
points: Company has locked in contracts with three to four very large users who will take up the 300 metric ton capacity; order book scaling is close to that number expected in FY27.
Full potential revenue from this product will not be realized in FY27 alone; it will be realized over the next 2 to 3 years, hence not fully reflected in the FY27 revenue guidance.
No degrowth is expected in any therapeutic category or product basket; growth timing differs by product due to regulated-market approval timelines.

subsections.label: Pricing
points: Company has not seen much pricing pressure on final API pricing in Europe or the U.S., as raw material/solvent price increases (linked to crude prices) have been passed on to customers via purchase-order-based working with customers, and customers have accepted these increases.

subsections.label: Therapeutic Mix
points: Growth in other/smaller therapeutic categories (beyond top therapies) driven by active introduction of anesthetic products (portfolio now has 6-7 products, fast-growing across regulated markets), cardiovascular and other advanced intermediates.
Antihistamines are fairly stable; vitamins have seen good growth as DSM volumes stabilized, with good traction in other vitamins like B12; anti-hypertensive also seeing good traction.

Smaller categories like anti-allergic exist but company is not aggressively pursuing non-regulated markets as it is margin-focused and prioritizes regulated markets, so contribution from these will remain limited.
Product additions are chosen based on China-sourcing gaps (China-plus-one strategy) with a view to future growth over the next 3 years.

subsections.label: New Product Contribution
points: Cardiovascular advanced intermediate and anesthetic API both scaled up and contributed to Q4 growth.
DSM contract has stabilized and contributed to revenue growth, alongside growth in the existing API basket across regulated markets like Europe and LATAM.
Q4 growth was a combination of new launches, stabilized DSM contract, and growth in the existing product basket — not solely CDMO/DSM driven.

subsections.label: Export & Regional Contribution
points: Export segment remained a key growth driver, contributing 82% of FY26 revenue.

Europe delivered healthy growth with a 40% revenue share during the year, driven mainly by CEP approvals secured for two to three products, enabling acquisition of new customers on existing CEP products.
Asia/domestic and semi-regulated markets saw growth as first-penetration markets for new product launches (3 products launched last year) due to lower regulatory barriers.

subsections.label: New Product Launches FY26
points: Key cardiovascular product introduced during Q3 FY26 and began contributing revenue in Q4 FY26; expected to gain higher momentum going forward.
ADHD product launched, seeing strong demand in LATAM and Europe, with further growth anticipated over coming quarters.
Liquid anesthetic product commercialized during the year, supported by steady monthly supplies.

Contrast media product development continued rather than launching immediately; company identified opportunities for further enhancement to improve product economics, pushing expected launch to H2 FY27.

Sevoflurane/liquid anesthetic finished formulation ramp-up will take 3-4 years to scale in the finished formulation facility; in FY27 revenue contribution will mainly come from the API side out of Lote, not the finished formulation.

subsections.label: R&D Evolution & Focus Areas
points: R&D approach evolved significantly over the last 5-6 years; previously focused only on life cycle management with low spend, but in the last 3 years two new R&D facilities were set up (Lote ~2 years back, Ambernath last year), and R&D spend has doubled.

R&D now focuses on three areas: (1) adding new APIs annually from newer therapies, focusing on niche molecules leveraging China-plus-one strategy; (2) CMO/CDMO/CRO tie-ups with larger multinationals/innovators; (3) formulations R&D at Ambernath focused on niche areas like liquid anesthetics and injectables.
R&D budget expected to continue growing over the next couple of years across these three areas.
Company successfully clearing USFDA surprise inspection (7 days, 7 manufacturing blocks, only 1 minor observation) attributed to better infrastructure and capacities built over the last 3-4 years.

subsections.label: GLP-1 / Semaglutide & Protein Opportunities
points: GLP-1 product development discussion with a large Indian generic company is at an advanced stage but not yet signed; revenue from this will take at least 2 years as development has not yet started (some development work has begun on their side).

Novel semaglutide tablet formulation: company holds a patent, differentiated from Novo's oral tablet via a different binding agent, with better absorption claimed; company has approached Novo regarding this; still doing further research.

Protein/weight-loss-drug-related opportunity remains an early-stage, first-of-its-kind technology for the Indian market; larger end users have bought small sample quantities and are developing finished formulations; no large revenue expected in FY27, still some time away.

subsections.label: Contrast Media Competitive Positioning
points: Company's contrast media technology/process is claimed to be more cost-efficient than the currently available route in the market.
Market for the contrast media molecule is large and growing YoY, with room for 2-3 large companies to gain a sizable share; company does not intend to be a market leader with more than 40-50% share.
Existing regulated-market customers with large requirements have been prompting the company to take up this product.
Company declined to disclose specific process details (e.g., iodine recovery) citing confidentiality after 2-3 years of R&D work.

subsections.label: Cardiovascular Backward Integration
points: Company has already achieved full backward integration for the cardiovascular product now that volumes have scaled up (previously running fewer synthesis steps, targeting more steps as volumes grew).

subsections.label: USFDA Inspection - Lote Facility
points: Lote facility received USFDA's Establishment Inspection Report (EIR) with a Voluntary Action Indicated (VAI) classification following a surprise inspection conducted in February 2026.
Inspection resulted in only one minor observation, which was proactively addressed, reinforcing credibility with global regulators for regulated-market growth.
Audit was a complete surprise, 7 days across 7 manufacturing blocks.

subsections.label: Patalganga Land Development
points: All clearances secured for Patalganga land; phased development to begin with Phase 1 groundbreaking in FY27.
Facility will include two API/advanced intermediate blocks and two formulation blocks.

A large portion of capex (~INR200 crores) will be allocated over the next 2 years toward Patalganga for further capacity building, anticipating scale-up of existing products, new launches, and growing CMO/CDMO demand from larger companies wanting to tie up on APIs/basket products.

subsections.label: Debottlenecking & Capacity Expansion
points: Company is undertaking debottlenecking activities across different blocks, one reason for the scheduled Q2 FY27 shutdown.
F block addition plus an extension to the D block, together with debottlenecking, will provide additional capacity of 150-200 KL, to be utilized over 2-3 years.
Company unable to quantify additional revenue potential from this new capacity at this stage; it is being built to support growth in existing APIs plus new launch products.

subsections.label: Ambernath Facility
points: Ambernath expenses have started while Ambernath revenue has not yet started at scale, impacting relative EBITDA margin optics for the year.
Some revenue generation from Ambernath has begun, but it is very small; full revenue effect of Ambernath expected to take about 2-3 years (some management commentary said 3-4 years).
In FY27, some revenue contribution from Ambernath is expected, mainly from semi-regulated markets.
Ambernath EU-GMP audit scheduled for H2 FY27 (typically around October/November); USFDA audit dates not yet obtained due to auditor unavailability, company continuing to follow up.

subsections.label: Annual Maintenance Shutdown
points: Annual maintenance shutdown scheduled in August (Q2 FY27) for older blocks A&D, meaning growth will not be linear across quarters.

subsections.label: Regional Growth Drivers
points: Europe and LATAM remain the largest markets for the current portfolio because most finished formulators are based in these geographies.

U.S. market contribution is around 1% currently in Q4 FY26 because the current portfolio inherently does not have a large market in the U.S.; new products being launched (anesthetic, ADHD, and future products) will have larger U.S. market potential, and exposure to the U.S. market is expected to grow over the next 3-4 years, though Europe and LATAM will remain the larger markets.
Asia and semi-regulated markets are typically the first-penetration markets for new product launches due to lower regulatory barriers, contributing to their growth this year.

subsections.label: Raw Material Cost Pass-Through
points: Increases in solvent prices linked to crude price increases have been passed on to customers via purchase-order-based commercial arrangements, with customers accepting the increases, limiting pricing pressure on final API.

subsections.label: Inventory Buildup
points: Higher inventory days (~200 days) driven by backward integration requiring higher volumes of raw material/intermediate holding for high-volume products like the cardiovascular intermediate and liquid anesthetic, plus added Ambernath inventory (INR10-15 crores).

subsections.label: Regulated Market Focus
points: Company strategy is to focus on regulated markets as a margin-focused company rather than aggressively pursuing non-regulated markets.

Customer traction: locked in contracts with three to four very large users for cardiovascular intermediate capacity, driven by customers wanting the company to be part of their dossier rather than participating in government PLI schemes.
Larger companies are seeking CMO/CDMO tie-ups with Supriya for APIs and basket-type products, informing capacity allocation decisions.

subsections.label: China-Plus-One Positioning
points: Company positions itself as a 'China plus one' alternative — targeting products where China currently supplies and India lacks manufacturers, viewing this as a long-term growth avenue rather than competing domestically (which management says would compress EBITDA to around 7%).
47+ years of manufacturing facility experience cited as basis for confidence in executing China-plus-one strategy.

subsections.label: Capital Allocation Priority
points: Management's current dominant priority is further capacity building, with a large portion of capex directed to Patalganga (~INR200 crores over next 2 years) and CMO/CDMO capacity, given growth visibility across existing products and new launches.

subsections.label: Q4 Headwinds
points: Industry-wide headwinds during Q4 arose from geopolitical challenges, including supply chain disruptions, elevated crude and solvent prices, and intermittent shortages, which impacted Q4 FY26 revenue by INR10 crores.
Despite these headwinds, resilient performance was delivered.

subsections.label: Regulatory/Approval Timing Risk
points: Ambernath USFDA audit dates not yet available due to auditor unavailability; EU-GMP audit for Ambernath scheduled H2 FY27 but has already seen delays due to auditor unavailability.
Contrast media launch delayed to H2 FY27 as further technology/process strengthening is pursued for better economics.

subsections.label: Non-Linear Growth Risk
points: Scheduled annual maintenance shutdown in August (Q2 FY27) for older blocks A&D means growth will not be linear across quarters.

key_figures.label: Liquid anesthetic finished formulation ramp-up timeline

subsections.label: Revenue & Margin Guidance
points: Company reiterated guidance of approximately 20% annual revenue growth and EBITDA margin of 33% to 35%.

Trajectory towards the INR1,000 crores revenue milestone by FY27 remains firmly on track, underpinned by a robust pipeline, planned launches of 3-4 products annually, and sustained demand across core therapeutic segments including anesthetics, antibiotics, anti-anxiety, vitamins and ADHD.
Growth won't be linear across quarters due to the scheduled Q2 FY27 (August) annual maintenance shutdown for older blocks A&D.

EBITDA margin guidance of 33-35% expected to continue over the next 5-6 years because new product launches (API or finished formulation) typically first scale in semi-regulated markets at lower prices before maturing into regulated markets over 2-3 years, and this cycle will recur as 3-4 new molecules are added annually.

Beyond FY27/into FY28-29, further guidance (including potential margin acceleration to 38-39% and peak revenue potential from Ambernath and Patalganga) will only be provided in coming quarters once Ambernath's regulatory approvals and CMO/CDMO opportunities are finalized; peak potential depends on product mix, which is not yet finalized for Patalganga.

subsections.label: Segment/Product-Specific Guidance
points: Cardiovascular advanced intermediate: 300 metric ton capacity utilization expected to be nearly reached in FY27 based on current order book, but full 300-ton revenue realization and beyond will occur over the next 2-3 years, not entirely within FY27.
DSM contract revenue seen reaching close to its INR60 crores peak in FY27, up from INR30-35 crores in FY26.
Liquid anesthetic finished formulation will not contribute much revenue in FY27; revenue in FY27 will mainly come from API sales out of Lote; finished formulation ramp-up will take 3-4 years.
Ambernath expected to start contributing revenue in FY27, mainly from semi-regulated markets, with full revenue effect taking 2-3 years (also stated as 3-4 years).
Effective tax rate guided at 24-25.17% for FY27.
Working capital days guided to stabilize at 170-180 days going forward; receivable days expected to be maintained between 80-85 days even in worst case.

guidance_ledger.statement: Trajectory towards the INR1,000 crores revenue milestone by financial year '27 remains firmly on track, underpinned by a robust pipeline, planned launches of 3 to 4 products annually and sustained demand across core therapeutic segments.
We iterate our guidance of approximately 20% annual growth revenue.
EBITDA margin, 33% to 35%.
We achieved our FY '26 revenue target... Financial year '26 revenue grew to 18.9% year-on-year to INR828 crores, in line with our guided growth of ~20%.
EBITDA margins were at 35.5% for FY26, surpassing our guided range of 33% to 35%.

For financial year '27, we plan to further strengthen our anesthetics and ADHD portfolios with ~2 new launch in each segment aimed at enhancing pipeline depth and supporting broader market penetration.
It is expected to be launching H2 financial year '27.
We have secured all clearances for the Patalganga land, with phased development to begin with Phase 1 groundbreaking in financial year '27.
The 300 metric ton, I think will come very close to that number in FY27, looking at the current order book that we have.
The peak that we expect is about INR60 crores, which we'll be able to see in FY27.

In FY27, as far as the finished formulation liquid anesthetic ramp-up is there, we'll not see much revenue contribution. The liquid anesthetic contribution will only come from the API from the Lote side because it will take us 3 to 4 years to get the ramp-up in the finished formulation facility.
We have some indication from them that the audit would be scheduled in H2 of FY27... typically around October or November.
We still have not got the dates for USFDA audit. We are following up with them. However, due to unavailability of auditors, we are not able to get a date as of now.
In FY27, you can see some revenue contribution from Ambernath mainly coming in from the semi-regulated markets... the full effect of Ambernath revenue contribution will still take about 2 to 3 years.
I think the average will be somewhere between 24 to 25.17%, that would be the rate you will be landing to... for full year, you can expect somewhere around say 25.17%.
We are looking at around 170 to 180 days going forward... we believe that somewhere around 170 to 180 days, I think, should be a stable state number.
We will be able to maintain between 80 to 85 days even at the worst of times.

As far as the growth in the next 3 to 4 years is concerned, we have already said that we'll grow 20% plus year-on-year. So, I think that kind of trend, we would continue. When Ambernath is fully commercialized and with Patalganga coming in, the growth can be accelerated, but that we'll be able to comment in the coming few quarters.

The larger guidance on FY28 and the next couple of years, we'll only be able to give in the coming few quarters because we still have not reached the full revenue potential of Ambernath, the regulatory approvals have not yet come in.
It completely depends on the product mix for us... up and until nothing is signed and the term sheets are not there, we'll not be able to guide on the full potential numbers.
Revenue will take at least 2 years because the development has also not started... I think it will still take 2 years minimum for some revenue to start coming in from this.
I'm not seeing any large revenue that can come in FY27.
We'll not be able to give any quarter-on-quarter guidance of the run rate... all quarters might not be linear growth.

key_takeaways: Delighted to report our highest ever revenue and EBITDA performance for the year with a record quarterly revenue achieved in Q4 FY26 of INR277 crores.
Financial year '26 revenue grew to 18.9% year-on-year to INR828 crores, in line with our guided growth of ~20%, while EBITDA stood at INR294 crores with a robust margin of 35.5%.

Lote facility had received the USFDA's Establishment Inspection Report, EIR, with a Voluntary Action Indicated classification following the surprise inspection conducted in February 2026, with only one minor observation.
Export segment, a key growth driver contributing 82% of the financial year revenues; Europe delivered healthy growth with a 40% share during the year.
Backward integration initiatives progressed in financial year '26 at 76%, strengthening cost efficiency and supporting sustainable growth.
We iterate our guidance of approximately 20% annual growth revenue and EBITDA margin, 33% to 35%.
Our trajectory towards the INR1,000 crores revenue milestone by financial year '27 remains firmly on track, underpinned by a robust pipeline.
We have secured all clearances for the Patalganga land, with phased development to begin with Phase 1 groundbreaking in financial year '27.

If everything comes online, Ambernath and Patalganga, what is the maximum potential for the company? I mean in terms of revenue and in terms of like overall margin structures because obviously, by then our expenses also would have been much more, there could be some operating leverage also which will kick in. Do you see like this 35%, 36% today, what we are doing can actually go to 38%, 39% because cost being like much more accretive to the overall business?

MTARTECH.about: MTAR develop and manufactures components and equipment for the defense, aerospace, nuclear and clean energy sectors. The co. was incorporated in 1970 by the promoters, Mr PR Reddy, Mr KSN Reddy and Mr PJ Reddy, to cater to the technical and engineering needs of the Indian govt in the post embargo regime. MTAR has manufacturing footprints in Hyderabad with seven units spread across a 4 km radius and a dedicated export facility as well. [1]In addition, the company also supplies specialised products such as Ball Screws, Water Lubricated Bearings, Roller Screws, Electro-Mechanical Actuation Systems, ASP assemblies etc. that find applications across diverse sectors.[2]

quarters.summary: MTAR delivered Q1 FY27 revenue of INR360.7 crores (up 130.4% YoY) and EBITDA margin of 23.6%, in line with annual guidance. Management reiterated confidence in achieving/exceeding FY27 guidance of 80% revenue growth (+/-5%) and EBITDA margin of 24% (+/-100bps), citing strong order inflows across nuclear, clean energy, aerospace & defense, and data center infrastructure, with closing order book already at INR5,143 crores plus an additional INR800 crores received on call day, taking total to over INR5,900 crores. Execution ramp-up across nuclear and aerospace expected in H2 FY27 and beyond, supported by capacity expansion in fuel cells (Phase 2 by Sep-Oct 2026, Phase 3 multifold expansion by March 2027) and new facilities for data center infrastructure and aerospace.

subsections.label: Revenue and margin drivers
points: Highest-ever quarterly revenue driven by strong execution of various products across verticals.
EBITDA margin improvement QoQ (20.11% to 23.54%) attributed to operating leverage from higher revenues and cost monitoring.
Gross margin decline YoY (47.65% to 45.61%) attributed to revenue mix change during the year.

PAT growth driven by revenues growing multifold as sectors where first articles were completed 2-3 years ago are now in production ramp-up stage, with customers increasing orders; in aerospace, first articles completed are yielding 10-15x volumes.

subsections.label: Working capital improvement initiatives
points: Improvement driven by better commercial terms negotiated with customers, better credit terms after reaching customer premises enabling faster delivery and collection, and daily/weekly monitoring of every working capital element.
Company targeting to sustain around 100 days working capital by year-end (revised from prior guidance of 150-175 days) considering long-cycle projects.
Combination of receivable and inventory day reductions (from ~340 days combined previously to ~220 days) expected to sustain, with working capital target at ~100 days.
Improvement achieved organically; inorganic reduction options exist but company will not pursue at cost of margins.

subsections.label: Capital allocation and funding
points: Company essentially debt-free except ~INR20-30 crores net debt after adjusting cash/investment balances.

Total capex requirement of ~INR500 crores for current and next year combined for ongoing expansion plans across verticals; not all will be spent this year, will spill into next 1-2 quarters of next fiscal year.
Targeting minimum 4-5x (up to 6x) asset turnover on capex spent.
Funding for capex and incremental working capital will be a combination of internal accruals and debt.
Within the 70:30 capex split, some Clean Energy capex is fungible and could be used for other sectors as well.

Company continues to prioritize projects and prudent capital allocation while pursuing long-term strategic opportunities, maintaining healthy working capital, strengthening operating cash flows, and maintaining a healthy balance sheet.

subsections.label: Nuclear order momentum
points: Highest-ever order inflows in nuclear segment during the quarter for Kaiga 5 & 6 reactors.
Looking forward to more orders from refurbishment of existing reactors during current quarter.
Refurbishment order execution timeline within 2 years; Kaiga 5 & 6 execution timeline ranges from 1 year to 3-3.5 years.
Nuclear division order book of close to INR800 crores never happened in company history before.
Civil nuclear vertical has transitioned to a more consistent, sustainable growth trajectory with substantially reduced cyclicality compared to the past (comparing to 5-10 years back).

Mahi Banswara NTPC-NPCIL partnership: four 700-megawatt reactor tenders already floated; MTAR participation expected to be much higher than Kaiga 5 & 6 (2 reactors) since these are 4 reactors; timeline uncertain, tender allocation process ~1 year, orders may come in next financial year.

subsections.label: Clean energy order momentum

Demand so high that order book execution focus is on ramping up capacity and operational efficiency rather than market share quantification.
Fuel cell backlog consists of short-cycle orders (within 1 year, 6 months, 2 months, or 1.5-2 years) rather than long multi-year execution; continuous order book replenishment expected.

subsections.label: Aerospace & defense order momentum
points: Anticipating volume orders for actuator assemblies for LCA Tejas Mark-1A and orders for wing kits and electromechanical actuators for various defense programs.
MNC aerospace business demonstrating phenomenal growth potential with significant demand from existing customers for already-qualified products.
Multiple new inquiries under discussion; immediate focus on completing first article qualification of existing products and ramping up volumes before onboarding new customers.
Content per platform for Tejas actuator program valued at INR140-150 crores, expected to grow further as MTAR works on other niche defense projects not discussed in detail.

subsections.label: Order book execution cycle characteristics
points: Overall order book is largely short-cycle (not spread over 5-10 years); majority executable within 1 year to 2 years, enabling continuous replenishment.

subsections.label: Civil nuclear power

points: Strong momentum continuing; Clean Energy will remain a major driver of revenues by end of fiscal year.
Data center infrastructure solutions: new segment entered; initial products in progress, qualification process underway; meaningful ramp-up expected over next year.
Hydropower and wind energy segments showing good traction; company continues to pursue select products in these areas.
New product revenue (~INR100 crores run-rate, ~50% of Clean Energy segment revenue run-rate) not a one-off; expected to continue growing, with second half stronger than first half.

New product growth is a combination of multiple products, not limited to fuel cell hot box assembly; includes strong growth in ball screws with export orders and a major contract with an MNC to supply ball screws for aerospace division.

subsections.label: Aerospace and Defense
points: Growth remains encouraging with multiple programs and customer engagements in progress.
MNC aerospace business demonstrating phenomenal growth potential driven by demand from existing customers for already-qualified products.

Key differentiator: pace of establishing customer-specific manufacturing capabilities including new dedicated aerospace facility and NADCAP-approved special processes facility, positively appreciated by customers.

Aerospace and defense expected to double revenues in current fiscal year with significant ramp-up spread over next 3-4 years, largely driven by existing programs/portfolio with further upside from new inquiries and additional products.
First articles established over last 1.5-2 years now moving into volume production for majority of programs; some still in process — an ongoing continuous process.

subsections.label: Products division
points: Products division growing rapidly due to work done across aerospace, clean energy, and other sectors over past couple of years.
Continuous process of developing new products for existing and new customers across segments; getting qualified for additional assemblies (e.g., enclosures, cable harness) for largest client.
Segment expected to continue growing quarter-on-quarter.

subsections.label: Innovation and qualification focus
points: Continuous investment in technologies and capabilities well ahead of broader market adoption across civil nuclear, aerospace and defense, and clean energy sectors.
Getting qualified for additional assemblies in products division and clean energy on an ongoing basis; results seen 6 months to 1 year after qualification in terms of volumes.
Ball screws qualification work done over past couple of years now yielding export orders and a major MNC aerospace contract.

Phase 2 to be commissioned by September-October 2026.

Facility designed to support multiple products under one roof for greater scale and operational efficiency.

Established new dedicated aerospace facility and NADCAP-approved special processes facility within a short time frame, positively appreciated by customers.

points: Setting up a dedicated facility for data center infrastructure solutions to support scale-up opportunity (8x current order potential, 8 sets per year target).

points: Oil & Gas facility to be operational by October 2026.
First articles already delivered to one customer; first article components for another customer currently under progress.

points: Data center infrastructure orders and products are entirely for export.
Ball screws segment has significant export orders including a major contract with an MNC to supply ball screws for aerospace division.
Sectors (civil nuclear, aerospace and defense, clean energy) witnessing strong growth across both domestic and international markets.

points: Negotiated better commercial and credit terms with customers, including credit terms activating after reaching customer premises, enabling faster delivery and collection.
Daily/weekly monitoring of every element of working capital.
Targeting to generate GST refund of almost INR70 crores per year to support cash flow from operations.

Mahi Banswara nuclear opportunity (4 reactors) expected to be much larger than Kaiga 5 & 6 (2 reactors).

Pursuing select products in hydropower and wind energy segments as additional diversification avenues.
5-year roadmap to pursue growth across all sectors; execution remains key near-term focus.
Prioritization of projects and prudent capital allocation emphasized alongside pursuit of long-term strategic opportunities.
Growth achieved organically; inorganic (M&A) growth options exist for reducing working capital days but company will not pursue if it comes at cost of margins.

key_takeaways: We received our highest-ever order inflows in this segment during the last quarter for Kaiga 5 & 6 reactors, and looking forward for more orders from refurbishment of existing reactors during the current quarter as well.

We expect to double our revenues in aerospace and defense segment during the current fiscal year, with a significant ramp-up from this base and spread over the next 3 to 4 years.

quarters.summary: Management raised FY27 revenue growth guidance from 50% to 80%+ (plus/minus 5%) with EBITDA margins around 24%, citing capacity expansion in clean energy (initial phase already commissioned), oil & gas plant commissioning by September end, strong nuclear order book execution, and ramp-up of aerospace volume production. Closing order book for FY26 stood at INR2,580 crores versus guidance of INR2,800 crores (shortfall due to deferred nuclear and defense orders), with estimated closing order book of ~INR5,000 crores by end of FY27.

subsections.label: Full Year FY26 vs FY25 Performance
points: Revenue from operations grew ~30% YoY to INR876 crores from INR676 crores.
EBITDA increased 41.7% YoY to INR171 crores from INR121 crores.
PBT increased 75.1% YoY to INR126 crores from INR72 crores.
PAT increased 76.2% YoY to INR94 crores from INR53.4 crores.
Growth driven by strong execution across key business segments on both YoY and QoQ basis.

subsections.label: Q4 FY26 vs Q4 FY25 Performance
points: Revenue more than doubled to INR306 crores from INR183 crores.
EBITDA increased 81% YoY to INR62 crores from INR34 crores.
PBT increased sharply to INR59.5 crores from INR18.6 crores.
PAT increased ~222% YoY to INR44 crores from INR14 crores.

subsections.label: Working Capital and Cash Flow
points: Working capital days improved to 172 days in FY26 from 267/278 days in Q3, supported by better payment terms negotiated with customers.
Company targets maintaining working capital at a similar level by end of current fiscal year.
Cash flow from operations rose to INR196.9 crores from INR101 crores in FY25, mainly due to additional margins and better payment terms.
Better payment terms (credit period and other factors) negotiated with multiple customers, not a one-time advance — described as a continuous process expected to sustain going forward.

subsections.label: Margins
points: Gross margin declined to 47.7% from 49.4% YoY, impacted by increased input prices of consumables and freight costs amid geopolitical uncertainties.

EBITDA margin came in at 19.5% versus prior guidance of 20-21% plus/minus 1%, shortfall attributed to gross margin impact from geopolitical uncertainties and increased headcount from ongoing expansion activities.
Sequential gross margin dip of 190 bps attributed to input cost increases from geopolitical situation, not any customer price renegotiation.
ROCE improved to 17.2% from 11.4%, and PAT margin improved to 10.7% from 7.8%; further improvement expected from increased turnover and operating leverage.

CFO stated fixed cost (salaries + other expenditure) is ~28% of revenue; with revenue increase, at least 5% operating leverage benefit is estimated, supporting confidence in meeting EBITDA targets even in a conservative scenario.

subsections.label: Debt and Capital Allocation
points: Total debt increased to ~INR370 crores to fund expansion plans; company considers debt an appropriate option currently given healthy debt-to-equity ratio.
Company repays debt while also raising fresh term loans, negotiating better INR loan terms.
Target debt-to-equity ratio of around 0.5 for the next 2 years (FY27-FY28).

subsections.label: Other Income / Forex
points: Other income of INR25 crores mainly from foreign exchange gain (mix of realized and unrealized).
Management expects continued forex gains given >70% of revenue from exports versus 30-35% imports, and banker guidance suggesting rupee depreciation trend to continue in the current financial year.

The outlook for next financial looks very positive. And having confidence in the execution of orders on hand, we are raising our guidance for FY '27 from 50% revenue growth to 80% plus - revenue growth, plus/minus 5%, with clear EBITDA margins of around 24% for the year.

The closing order book for FY '26 is at INR2,580 crores, and we had given a guidance of INR2,800 crores. The marginal difference is due to some nuclear orders and the defense orders being deferred to the current quarter, which does not have any impact on our business outlook for this year.

MTAR has been in civil nuclear program for more than 35 years. And now, we have the strongest order book of INR650 crores plus, and all these orders have to be executed over the next 3 to 3.5 years.
It has been a great year with a positive operating cash flow of INR196 crores. And we ended with net working capital days of 172 days compared to the previous quarter of 278 days.

Our EBITDA margin is at INR171 crores, which is 19.5%. We have guided around 20%, plus or minus 1%, we guided, and we achieved 19.5%, which is due to the gross margin impact due to prevailing geopolitical uncertainities and also increase in headcount due to ongoing expansions activities in the company.

SHAILY.about: The Company is engaged in the manufacture and sale of injection moulded precision plastic components, sub-assemblies for various requirements of Original Equipment Manufacturers (OEM). It also offers secondary operations in plastics like vacuum metalizing, hot stamping, and ultrasonic welding. Its manufacturing facilities are at Savli and Halol, Vadodara, Gujarat. [1]

quarters.summary: Management remains confident of exceeding its FY27 pen-device guidance of 36 million pens given strong Q1 execution (~9 million pens delivered) and improving line efficiencies, while gross margins are expected to normalize by Q3 FY27 after commodity/freight-driven pressure in Q1. Growth visibility continues in Healthcare (GLP-1/insulin scale-up, new geographies, emergency-use/on-body/reusable device pipeline), Consumer Electronics (new 5-component customer win, ramp from next year) and Semiconductor Trays (Q4 FY27 supply start), even as Consumer/home-furnishings demand stays soft in Europe/US and Abu Dhabi capacity targets commercial sales by end of FY28.

subsections.label: Gross margin decline
points: Gross margin declined sequentially post-March due to war-driven commodity (polymer) price increases and higher freight prices, including premium airlifted freight incidents.
Pass-through with some customers was delayed, happening between May and June, and with others as late as July, causing the gross margin decline in the quarter.
Gross margin expected to return to normalized levels by Q3 FY27.

subsections.label: Margin outlook
points: Management did not provide a specific margin number but expects margins to remain sustainable and improve on a year-on-year basis (carried from prior guidance context).

key_figures.label: Dr. Reddy's-linked order (referenced from prior press release)

subsections.label: Order intake
points: Received orders for injector pen supplies following regulatory approvals secured for the sale of Semaglutide in Canada and Brazil by pharmaceutical partners.
Signed 2 new platform projects during the quarter, strengthening long-term product pipeline.
Secured a global project from an FMCG customer and won new business in the LED lighting segment (Consumer segment).
Received business confirmations for new projects from Appliance and Automotive customers (Industrial segment).
Onboarded a new customer with orders covering 5 Consumer Electronic components.

subsections.label: Pen guidance vs execution
points: Despite line efficiency challenges, management expects to go beyond the 36 million pen guidance for FY27 given Q1 run-rate of ~9 million pens and improving line speeds, though this depends on customer partners' short-term supply chain issues and continued strong demand.

DRL-related issues: management did not name the customer publicly for the previously disclosed order but confirmed the partner has some challenges (impurities issue in Canada, technical issues in Brazil); management stated actual demand requires supplying more due to a supply gap, and confidence in guidance remains despite this.
Regulatory approvals remain largely in place across various global markets even amid a partner's specific issues.

subsections.label: Pricing
points: Contracts for GLP-1/insulin devices are volume and market-driven pricing contracts (not cost-plus), with an annual price review mechanism; pricing depends on the type of agreement, longevity of contract, and commitment, referencing a base index on inflation and polymers.

Chinese competitors are reportedly pricing generic devices around $1.50-$1.70, using older ('20-year-old') technology; some Chinese products allegedly infringe Shaily's patents and other suppliers' patents; Shaily's pricing is above $2, and management is not overly concerned about Chinese pricing pressure.

subsections.label: Geographic demand/market share
points: Once a market has shifted to a generic, switching a patient to another generic is difficult; management expects Shaily to be quite dominant in Canada and hold the Number 2 position (in terms of launches) with a significant share in Brazil.
In India, market share dynamics are described as unclear/fluid as generics compete and consolidate.
Newer geographies like Mexico, Turkey and Saudi Arabia (Middle East) are seen as future opportunities; management aims to be the largest player, not just top 3, in these newer markets.
Confident about scaling demand not only in the current year (36 million pens) but also into next year.

subsections.label: Healthcare
points: Segment revenue grew 85% YoY to INR142 crores, contributing ~51% of consolidated revenue and becoming the largest business segment for the quarter.
Growth continued to be led by the pen injector platform, including devices for GLP-1 and other chronic therapies.
Received orders for injector pen supplies following regulatory approvals for Semaglutide sale in Canada and Brazil by pharmaceutical partners.
Signed 2 new platform projects during the quarter, strengthening long-term product pipeline.
6 of 8 device platforms are now fully commercial and sold across global markets, developed within 7 to 8 years.
Delivered world's first generic Semaglutide launches in multiple markets and secured the first tentative U.S. FDA approval for generic Semaglutide.

Feedback from Brazil/Canada end customers on pen platforms has been above average/good with statistically strong device performance based on extensive batch-release testing trend data; no statistical decline observed.

subsections.label: Consumer
points: Revenue of INR116 crores, ~41% of consolidated revenue; reflects softer demand in home furnishings across Europe and United States, the largest export markets for this business.
Continued to expand customer relationships and add new programs strengthening future revenue pipeline despite the demand softness.
Secured a global project from an FMCG customer and won new business in LED lighting segment.
YoY, revenue declined 24% (INR116 crores vs INR151 crores), largely due to softer demand across Europe and U.S.; however, on a QoQ basis (Q4 to Q1), the Consumer business grew.
India's share of Consumer product supply is very negligible (~2%), so India market conditions make little difference to this business; the decline is driven by Europe/North America demand degrowth.

Management does not expect the Consumer segment to grow in the current year and expects it to be maintained at the level achieved in FY26; segment's performance is not expected to materially affect Shaily's overall bottom line even over a 3-year horizon.

subsections.label: Industrial
points: Revenue increased 25% YoY to INR23 crores, supported by new customer additions and increasing opportunities across engineering applications including Consumer Electronics.
Received business confirmations for new projects from Appliance and Automotive customers during the quarter.
Onboarded a new customer with orders covering 5 Consumer Electronic components.
Going forward, focus remains on building sustainable revenue streams, particularly through Consumer Electronics and Semiconductor Trays.

subsections.label: Healthcare strategy / pipeline diversification
points: Strategy: continue to scale GLP-1 and insulin, simultaneously expand into niche areas like emergency use devices, on-body injectors and more sustainable reusable devices, and forge partnerships with global pharma.

Appointed dedicated heads of business development for Europe and North America (priority growth markets); both are senior industry leaders. European head has a Masters from HEC Paris and business school from Burgundy School of Business with long medical devices/drug delivery experience; U.S. head previously worked at competitors including West, Phillips-Medisize, Stevanato, Haselmeier.

Company is in discussions and confident of securing a partnership with a major global pharmaceutical over the near term; expects to make an announcement in the next 4-6 quarters regarding innovator partnerships.

Emergency use auto-injector: working on molecules like epinephrine (others under confidentiality); based on the Toby auto-injector but with key design changes including automatic needle insertion, automatic injection, dose delivery and retraction; requires very high reliability (99.999% activation reliability) given patient-critical use; program ongoing for ~18 months, targeted for closure by end of '27; management believes no competitors currently offer a single emergency-use device.

Reusable auto-injector: developed to address landfill waste (~1 billion auto-injectors/year from Semaglutide/Tirzepatide therapy); testing performance this month/early next month; to be showcased for the first time at CPHI Milan; considered quite advanced in development.

On-body injector: for oncology treatments; developing partnership and progressing the 'Mira' device prototyped 2-3 years ago; delivery range target of 3ml-23ml, though 3ml-15ml deemed more likely achievable on current platform; currently under discussion/negotiation for a molecule (biologics/biosimilars).

Scale/economics: Emergency-use products projected in mid-single-digit to low-double-digit millions of dollars in value given device cost of $6-$10 per unit and high complexity/expense of the therapy; on-body injectors projected as low-millions, high-value/high-margin ($15-$35 per device); reusable auto-injector market size unknown as it depends on market showcase feedback.

Company confirmed no plans to enter pharmaceutical consumables beyond current scope and no plans for inhalers (no update on any prior Cipla inhaler engagement, and management clarified nothing was previously communicated regarding Cipla/inhalers).

subsections.label: New pen line ramp-up
points: Line speed increased by about 9% on the newly set-up line; further improvement plan requires additional equipment not yet received; once installed, line should see another 30% jump in speed, targeted before the end of the current quarter.

Strategy for next new line has been adjusted: instead of shipping the line and then ramping up, the company will complete ramp-up and reach 80%+ efficiency at the supplier before Factory Acceptance Test (FAT) and shipping; no R&D work is being done on this line.
Once the next line arrives (expected in a month or two), similar 80% efficiency should be achievable relatively quickly.

subsections.label: Pen injector capacity expansion
points: Additional 25 million pen capacity expected to become operational by end of September, taking total installed pen injector capacity to approximately 75 million pens per annum.
Machine utilization improved to 50.2% in Q1 FY27 compared with 48.7% in Q1 FY26, reflecting gradual improvement in capacity utilization.

subsections.label: Abu Dhabi facility
points: Roughly 50-55% of capacity has commitments/indications from customers currently; remainder is being worked on.

Plant is supposed to start selling by end of FY28, targeting commercial sales by then; capacity is positioned for markets opening up in Europe in FY28 plus insulin, and markets opening up globally in 2030-31.
Given FY28 production start, this facility will impact FY29 volumes.

subsections.label: Consumer Electronics plant (south India)
points: Started commercial supply; new customer awarded 5 new components, expected to go into supply just before the end of the financial year.
Location/land for the new south India plant has been secured, though not publicly announced.
Further update on plant setup expected in the next quarter's earnings call; plans are progressing as projected.

Ramp-up of the newly won 5-component business expected from next year onward, initially served from existing facility with additional tooling and automation investments; eventual dedicated south India plant investment of INR80-100 crores.

subsections.label: Semiconductor Trays capacity
points: Investment of about INR5 crores planned in existing facility to meet initial requirements; further investment decisions will depend on how the Indian semiconductor market develops and customer scale-up.

key_figures.label: India share of Consumer segment supply

subsections.label: Export/domestic mix shift
points: Exports accounted for approximately 58% of consolidated revenue in Q1 FY27 versus 76% in Q1 FY26; change primarily due to growing contribution of the Healthcare business, where products are supplied to global markets through Indian pharmaceutical customers (domestically routed export).
Healthcare sales growth has increased domestic-routed volumes (via Indian pharma companies exporting drugs), changing the export mix even though ultimate end-markets remain global.
Degrowth in Consumer business, which is mainly export-oriented, has also contributed to the lower export percentage.

Going forward, Healthcare business growth plus increasing focus on Semiconductor and Consumer Electronics businesses (more domestic-focused) is expected to increase the domestic revenue percentage over time.

subsections.label: UK subsidiary
points: A drop seen in UK subsidiary revenue is a timing issue: certain milestones were achieved at the very end of the month, but invoices are not raised until customer confirmation of milestone achievement is received; this revenue is expected to come back over the next 3 quarters.
Management declined to provide specific full-year UK subsidiary growth guidance when asked if ~15% growth was a safe assumption.

subsections.label: Global market positioning by geography
points: Canada: expected to be quite dominant given first-mover generic positioning.
Brazil: currently Number 2 in terms of launches, expected to retain significant share.
India: market share dynamics described as unclear and fluid.
Mexico, Turkey, Saudi Arabia/Middle East: seen as future opportunities where management aims to be the largest, not just top 3, player.

subsections.label: Supply chain disruption mitigation
points: Global operating environment remained challenging due to geopolitical situation in West Asia, impacting supply chains and commodity markets, leading to volatility in polymer prices, logistic disruptions, container availability constraints and elevated freight costs.

Company mitigated much of the impact through disciplined operational planning, supply chain management and calibrated pricing actions including pass-through mechanisms wherever applicable, ensuring business continuity.
Some premium freight incidents required airlifting material, contributing to cost pressure.
