subsections.label: Consumer Electronics strategy
points: Building up the portfolio with customers adding more products over time.
Management projects (not formal guidance) reaching $10 million revenue scale within 24-30 months.
Details on time taken to get qualified with the new customer remain confidential.
Products are internal components of small devices/appliances; described as very complex, in some cases more complex than components manufactured for pens and auto-injectors.
Company is looking to expand into the whole ecosystem of the customer's other devices, a process requiring further work with the customer.

subsections.label: Semiconductor Trays market
points: Trays are highly specialized with extremely critical dimensional tolerances, made of specialized conductive plastics; very few global players (less than a dozen) can produce them.
As India's semiconductor manufacturing ecosystem develops, tray requirement is expected to rise; company aims to be part of this ecosystem.
Trays are consumables required in large (millions) quantities depending on the scale of semiconductor capacity set up in India.

subsections.label: Competitive positioning - GLP-1 devices
points: Chinese competitors are pricing devices around $1.50-$1.70 using older, copycat technology (some infringing patents); Shaily's device pricing is above $2, and management is not overly concerned about this pricing gap given differentiation.

Currently less than half a dozen customers have launched in Canada/Brazil, apart from India, out of 5-7 total players; management expects about half a dozen additional customer launches in the next 2-3 quarters.

subsections.label: TAM commentary
points: Management declined to quantify the incremental TAM opened up by Semaglutide approvals in Canada and Brazil, stating it is not competent to comment on market size or market share for those markets, and pointed to third-party research reports instead.

subsections.label: Talent strategy
points: Appointed dedicated business development heads for Europe and North America to pursue innovator pharma partnerships.
Company retains talent through reputation, pay, and training rather than heavy reliance on ESOPs; ESOP schemes exist and other employees will become eligible in coming years.
New senior manufacturing, quality and automation talent ('Joe') has come on board and become fully active, bringing new ideas from significant industry experience.
Management does not see a current challenge in retaining or hiring new employees, citing a positive/fun work culture.

subsections.label: No plans for other pharma consumables/inhalers
points: Management confirmed the company will not get into pharmaceutical consumables beyond its existing focus areas.
No plans for inhalers; management clarified there has been no prior public statement regarding a Cipla inhaler collaboration.

subsections.label: Geopolitical and commodity risk
points: Continued uncertainty from the geopolitical situation in West Asia impacted supply chains and commodity markets, causing volatility in polymer prices, logistic disruptions, container availability constraints and elevated freight costs.
Premium freight incidents required airlifting material at additional cost.

subsections.label: Partner-specific supply issues
points: A pharmaceutical partner (unnamed) reportedly has impurity-related issues in Canada and technical issues in Brazil; despite this, actual demand requires Shaily to supply more due to a market gap, and most approvals remain in place across various markets.

subsections.label: Chinese competition / IP infringement
points: Two large Chinese companies are expected to enter the generic device supply curve with pricing around $1.50-$1.70; some Chinese products reportedly infringe not only Shaily's patents but also other key global suppliers' patents.

subsections.label: Consumer/home furnishings demand softness
points: Softer demand in home furnishings across Europe and United States (largest export markets) continues to pressure the Consumer segment; recovery depends on how the broader Europe/US demand environment evolves.

subsections.label: Execution risk on new lines
points: New production line ramp-up has faced ongoing speed/efficiency challenges requiring additional equipment; described as 'a constant struggle' by management, though a resolution timeline before quarter-end is targeted.

subsections.label: Pen volume guidance
points: Management reiterated confidence in exceeding the 36 million pen guidance for FY27, citing strong Q1 run-rate (~9 million pens), improving line efficiency, and continued strong demand, though execution depends partly on customer partners' supply chain situations.
Confidence in scaling extends beyond the current year into next year as well.

subsections.label: Margin outlook
points: Gross margin expected to normalize by Q3 FY27 after being pressured by commodity and freight cost increases and delayed pass-through in Q1.

subsections.label: Segment outlook
points: Consumer segment is not expected to grow in the current year and will likely be maintained at FY26 levels; full-year growth outlook remains difficult to project precisely.
Domestic revenue percentage is expected to grow going forward as Healthcare, Semiconductor and Consumer Electronics businesses (more domestic-focused) scale up.

FY27 focus areas: strengthen and ramp up newly commissioned capacities, deepen strategic customer relationships, accelerate innovation through IP-led platforms, and maintain operational excellence for sustainable and profitable growth.

subsections.label: Abu Dhabi and Consumer Electronics timelines
points: Abu Dhabi facility targeted to start commercial sales by end of FY28, impacting FY29 volumes.
Consumer Electronics business projected (not formal guidance) to reach $10 million revenue scale in 24-30 months.

subsections.label: Product development timelines
points: Emergency-use auto-injector program targeted for closure by end of calendar '27.
Reusable auto-injector to be showcased for the first time at CPHI Milan, with testing this month/early next month.
Innovator pharma partnership announcement expected within the next 4-6 quarters.

key_takeaways: Healthcare segment revenue grew 85% YoY to INR142 crores, contributing ~51% of consolidated revenue and becoming the largest business segment for the quarter.
Consolidated Q1 FY27 revenue was INR281 crores (up 14% YoY), EBITDA INR83 crores (up 18% YoY, margin 29.7%, +120bps), and PAT INR48 crores (up 17% YoY, margin 17.1%, +40bps).
Additional 25 million pen capacity expected operational by end of September, taking total installed pen injector capacity to approximately 75 million pens per annum.
Machine utilization improved to 50.2% in Q1 FY27 versus 48.7% in Q1 FY26.
Exports accounted for approximately 58% of consolidated revenue versus 76% in the corresponding quarter last year, mainly due to growing Healthcare business routed through domestic pharma customers.
Consumer segment revenue declined 24% YoY to INR116 crores due to softer home furnishings demand in Europe and US, while Industrial segment grew 25% YoY to INR23 crores.
Management appointed dedicated business development heads for Europe and North America and is confident of securing a partnership with a major global pharmaceutical over the near term.
Management believes the company will exceed its FY27 guidance of 36 million pens given Q1 run-rate of ~9 million pens and improving line efficiencies.
pressing_questions: So Amit, on that basis, you have done 9 million in 1Q despite all the challenges. 2Q, your efficiency is improving. In 3Q, 4Q, your line will be double and operating at a much higher efficiency. So but your full year guidance is 36 million. I mean, mathematically, you'll be beating your guidance even with adding the single line already at a much lower efficiency. So is it fair to believe that you will do much better than your guidance?

My second question we had put in a press release with respect to Dr. Reddy's INR423 crores order a few quarters back. We understand that they have issues with regard to impurities in Canada. Brazil also is stuck with for technical issues. In these circumstances, how comfortable are we with our guidance of 36 million? So if not for DRL, do we have likes of Apotex or somebody else, who will comfortably lift our shipments?
If the management could speak about the opportunity like quantify the incremental TAM, which has opened up for now with... the approvals received for Semaglutide in Canada and Brazil.
So from a full year perspective, how should we look at [Consumer segment growth]?
So safe to assume that for the full year, we can do at least 15% kind of growth in the U.K. subsidiary.

quarters.summary: FY26 saw healthcare revenue surge 139% to INR393 crores (40% of consolidated revenue, up from 21% in FY25) on commercial launch of Semaglutide pen injectors in India, Canada and other markets, while the consumer (home furnishings) segment de-grew 9% on weak Europe/US demand; management targets continued healthcare scale-up, ramp of new pen capacities (targeting ~36 million pens in FY27 and 40-60 million range over the next 2-2.5 years), consumer electronics and semiconductor tray ramp-up, Abu Dhabi facility build-out, and sustainable/improving margins into FY27, while flagging geopolitical/trade disruption, capacity ramp-up execution risk, and softer consumer demand as key watch items.

subsections.label: Capital allocation
points: Board approved an enabling resolution to raise up to INR500 crores; this is intended to be an annual affair, with the company seeking a fresh enabling resolution each year to maintain financial flexibility.
This is not a signal of any specific fundraise plan, but a disciplined approach to be prepared with capital for high-quality, high-growth opportunities.

Management clarified the fundraise resolution is not related to the Q4 supply commencement for semiconductor trays; it is an enablement option for future large, capital-intensive, time-sensitive projects (e.g., additional device capacities that cannot be serviced from India or Abu Dhabi).

subsections.label: Fixed asset turnover guidance for pen capacity
points: On the incremental revenue potential from the total 80 million pen capacity (30m existing + 25m added in March + 25m more by July/August), management said to look at 2 to 2.5x fixed asset turnover based on investment in fixed assets, rather than an incremental revenue number.

subsections.label: Healthcare segment
points: Healthcare was the standout performer in Q4 FY26 with revenue doubling in the quarter.
Full-year healthcare revenue growth reflects the compounding benefits of multiyear investments in R&D, pen injector platforms and drug delivery capabilities.
Actual FY26 pen device volumes were roughly 23.3-23.5 million, a little lower than the previously guided 25-26 million, primarily because capacities were not able to produce what had been projected.

UK subsidiary has seen the lowest margins and revenues in the past 2 years due to doing longer-term, milestone-based projects with multi-year engagement and delayed revenue recognition; management said to look at combined UK+UAE margins together for a better perspective, and margins/growth should be viewed on a year-on-year rather than quarter-on-quarter basis.
Two pharma customers who received Canada approval for Semaglutide are both supplied by Shaily; of the first 6 filers in Canada, ~70% use Shaily's device.

subsections.label: Consumer segment
points: Consumer segment de-grew in Q4FY26 primarily reflecting weaker market demand for home furnishings across Europe and the US, the two largest export markets for this vertical.
Consumer business saw degrowth in H2 of the year while H1 consumer business had grown; in Q4 there was also some cancellation of orders from the Middle East due to the war there.

Despite the softness, the consumer business continues to add new customer programs and management remains focused on building sustainability streams in this segment, particularly through consumer electronics and semiconductor trays.
Growth recovery in consumer will depend on how the global demand situation (US/Europe) pans out; management believes it will bounce back as it has in past cycles.

subsections.label: Industrial segment
points: Industrial segment growth reflects new customer additions and expanding engineering applications, including new business confirmations for power tool and LED light components.
These additions diversify the industrial business and expand the range of precision engineering applications Shaily offers, from automotive components to power tools and lighting infrastructure.

subsections.label: Recently announced pen injector order
points: A recently announced INR423 crores order book for pen injectors from a large domestic company is a supply agreement over 4 years; customer name withheld due to NDA.

subsections.label: New product launches
points: Commercial launch of Shaily Harmony and Shaily Neo pen injectors with multiple customers for Semaglutide in India and other global markets during the quarter.
Pen injectors manufactured by Shaily for Semaglutide successfully launched by customers in the Canadian market, marking entry into one of the most regulated pharmaceutical markets.
Shaily's Pen and its customer are the first to receive tentative approval in the US market for Semaglutide.
One customer received European market authorization for Teriparatide.

Eye-applicator machines recently commissioned for a single customer; market already exists for that customer as a substitute for an imported product, meant for regulated markets; commercialization factored into the current financial year.

subsections.label: Manufacturing quality/technical challenges
points: Rejection rate on the new pen injector line has come down to 8% from a previously flagged ~30%; speed has also increased, but breakdowns occur with increased speed/shifts that need permanent resolution.
Current line running at roughly 35-34 parts per minute on an 80 parts per minute rated line, translating to ~45% overall equipment efficiency; considered work in progress, not an impossible task.

Learnings from the first 25 million capacity phase are expected to lower (but not eliminate) initial rejections on the next 25 million capacity addition; investment cycle from triggering investment to going on stream is now expected to take 18-24 months versus a prior ~12 months given line complexity and limited global suppliers.
Semiconductor tray product looks simple but is technically complicated, made of conductive plastic; the technical competence required was the reason Shaily was selected as a supply partner.

subsections.label: Capacity ramp-up
points: The 25 million capacity installed in March is currently running at roughly 45% operational efficiency; company has been producing consistently at this level for the last 45 days and expects to enhance it in the coming months.
The additional 25 million capacity expected by July/August is purely for Semaglutide and will be used for global markets where the product is launched.
Of the original 30 million capacity (mixed across insulin, Teriparatide, auto-injectors etc.), only a small portion is used for Semaglutide.

Target by end of year is for both new lines to run at 65-67 parts per minute, giving combined capacity of ~40-42 million pens; this is expected optimum/peak utilization for this year, with further upgrades to be identified as more is learned about the lines.
By FY28, targeting 35-40 million pens of additional capacity to be more or less fully in supply.
Smaller capacities for products like Tristan and Toby are not yet in supply; once approved, those capacities will also be utilized.
By end of year, total Semaglutide capacity of ~50 million pens is targeted, intended to be fully utilized over the next 2 years; insulin capacity targeted to be utilized at least 60-70%.
Overall total pen capacity range of ~40-60 million pens is projected roughly 30 months from now (end of FY28).

subsections.label: Consumer electronics plant
points: Company is evaluating setting up a plant in South India for the consumer electronics business, with initial capex estimated at around INR100 crores.

subsections.label: Abu Dhabi facility
points: Building and scaling the Abu Dhabi facility is a stated priority for FY27.

Geopolitical tensions are not seen as having long-term impact on the project timeline; adequate additional time/buffer had been factored in for bringing up the Abu Dhabi facility, some of which is currently being consumed.

Abu Dhabi offers benefits on operational costs, ease of supply chain and availability of international talent, which is harder to attract in a city like Baroda; expat talent costs in India are much higher than in a country like Abu Dhabi.

subsections.label: Regulatory approvals and geographic rollout
points: Pen injectors launched by customers in Canada; entry into one of the most regulated and quality-demanding pharmaceutical markets validated manufacturing standards and regulatory compliance.
First to receive tentative approval in the US market for Semaglutide (Shaily's Pen and customer).
European market authorization received by a customer for Teriparatide.

Of the first 6 filers in Canada, ~70% use Shaily's device; in Brazil, filings are largely partnership-based making Shaily's exact share harder to track, but management is confident of being in the first wave of Brazil approvals.
Brazil approval expected 'very soon' (timing uncertain, could be end of this month or next); Turkey and Mexico approvals expected only after Brazil.

Adding another device to a drug filing in a market like Canada requires running a full development program, taking no less than 24-36 months, at a cost of roughly 70-80% of the original program cost (generic companies typically spend INR100-150 crores on a program).

subsections.label: Semiconductor tray supply geography
points: Supplies for the semiconductor tray agreement with the Korean company will currently be made in India, mainly to OSAT players; eventually, when fabs are set up in India, supply will extend to fab players; there is a possibility of exports for this business as well.
Supplies for the semiconductor tray customer expected to start in Q4 of the current financial year.

subsections.label: Consumer electronics supply geography
points: Supplies for the consumer electronics customer will happen both in India and via exports.

subsections.label: New customer wins and market entries
points: Successfully commenced commercial supplies to a consumer electronics customer during Q4 FY26, after several quarters of preparation and qualification; now an active participant in the consumer electronics precision component ecosystem, characterized by high complexity, tight tolerances and very few players.

Signed a supply agreement with a Korean company for manufacture and supply of semiconductor trays, marking entry into the semiconductor supply chain at a time when India is being positioned as an alternative manufacturing destination under the China Plus One framework.

Semiconductor trays are precision-critical, consumable components required by semiconductor plants daily; the market is more a volume game than a high value-share game relative to overall chip value, but represents a fairly decent value opportunity; other global players are in Korea, China and Philippines, some of which could set up shop in India and compete.

Company expects to be the sole manufacturing partner in India for its semiconductor tray customer at present; it is too early to assess pricing pressure risk if other global tray makers set up in India, though customer relationship quality and prior tie-ups could reduce switching.

subsections.label: 5-year opportunity ranking
points: Management views healthcare and consumer electronics as the two largest opportunities (ranked jointly #1), given consumer electronics' significantly larger overall market size versus the pen market, but the pen market has very limited players giving Shaily a significant scale-up opportunity as one of the few players present.

Semiconductor is seen as the second-largest scale-up opportunity, followed by industrial and consumer (roughly together); consumer is going through a rough patch currently but is expected to bounce back, consistent with past cycles.

subsections.label: Margin profile discussion for new verticals
points: Consumer electronics margins, ROCE and capex are difficult to specify at this stage; historically, when Shaily lacked scale in the home furnishings business, EBITDA margins were single digit and profit margins very low single digit.

Consumer electronics will go through a similar scale-dependent margin cycle (possibly faster ramp-up), with overheads remaining high until a certain scale (management suggested roughly 15-20 million units) is reached before good margins emerge.
Company declined to give specific margin numbers for the consumer electronics business, citing its B2B nature.

subsections.label: Customer feedback on Semaglutide launch
points: Two complaints received post-launch: one was a user error unrelated to the device; the other was device-related, involving a small printing issue (numbers printed).

Otherwise no complaints on device performance; management noted positive user trust signals observed on an online forum regarding the Dr. Reddy's generic Semaglutide product (also marketed by Torrent).

subsections.label: Innovator engagement
points: Conversations with innovator companies on new projects are advancing well, though no commercial agreements have yet been signed with innovator companies in the GLP-1 segment.

subsections.label: Organizational strengthening
points: Onboarded Mr. Joe Kam as Chief Operating Officer for Healthcare (announced earlier in February); he is taking real ownership and showcasing strong leadership, with a disciplined, quality-focused approach; responsible for India operations and any future global sites.

For consumer electronics and semiconductor hiring, focus will be on high technical expertise rather than organizational/administrative expertise; hiring expected to begin around Q1 of next FY through September/October next year; Middle East hiring remains purely healthcare-focused, not consumer electronics.

subsections.label: Capital readiness for large opportunities
points: The enabling fundraise resolution (up to INR500 crores annually) is meant to allow the company to act quickly on large, time-sensitive, capital-intensive projects such as setting up additional device capacities that cannot be serviced from India or Abu Dhabi.

subsections.label: Geopolitical and macro risk
points: Heightened geopolitical uncertainty during the quarter, particularly ongoing tensions across global trade corridors, impacted freight movement, supply chain and input cost dynamics.
For the plastics and polymer industry, this translated into raw material price inflation and selective logistical disruptions across certain export routes.
Geopolitics is viewed as having only a short-term impact, not materially affecting the Abu Dhabi project timeline, though some project time buffer is currently being consumed.

subsections.label: Consumer demand weakness
points: Weaker market demand for home furnishings across Europe and the US (Shaily's two largest export markets for this vertical) drove consumer segment degrowth.
Q4 also saw some order cancellations from the Middle East attributed to the war in that region.
Consumer segment growth recovery is dependent on how the global demand situation pans out.

subsections.label: Capacity ramp-up execution risk
points: New pen injector lines are very complex; ramp-up to full speed/efficiency is a process, with breakdowns needing permanent resolution as speed increases.
If capacity ramp-up does not go as planned, there is a risk to timely supply for Canada customers ('If we can't supply enough, then there is a risk').
A big unknown is the additional line expected in August, which is not yet installed; better clarity on FY27 volumes expected around the September/October earnings call.
Investment cycle for new lines now expected to take 18-24 months (vs prior ~12 months) given complexity and a limited number of global suppliers of these lines.

subsections.label: Competitive risk in semiconductor trays
points: Global players in semiconductor trays are based in Korea, China and Philippines; some could set up operations in India, creating competition; potential pressure on profitability from such entrants is difficult to assess at this early stage.

subsections.label: FY27 priorities
points: Continue scaling the healthcare vertical.
Build and scale the Abu Dhabi facility on plan.
Deeply ramp up consumer electronics and semiconductor programs.
Restore growth momentum in the consumer home furnishing segment.

subsections.label: Margin outlook
points: Management expects margins to be sustainable and improving when viewed on a year-on-year basis (not quarter-on-quarter), even as semiconductor and Abu Dhabi capacity ramp up; declined to give specific numeric margin targets.
Consumer/UK+UAE growth is expected to bounce back, per management, when viewed on a year-on-year basis.

subsections.label: Closing remarks
points: FY26 was marked by smooth execution and continued improvement in operational performance.
Focus remains on scaling new capacities and disciplined fund management.
Management remains confident of delivering profitable and sustainable growth in the years ahead.

themes.label: GLP-1/Semaglutide ramp-up
themes.note: Commercial launch of pen injectors for Semaglutide across India, Canada, and pending US/Brazil/Turkey/Mexico approvals, with customers asking for more product than current capacity allows.

themes.label: Capacity expansion
themes.note: New 25 million pen capacity added in March running at ~45% efficiency with rejection down to 8%, additional 25 million capacity targeted by July/August, but investment cycle now stretched to 18-24 months.

themes.label: Consumer/home furnishings demand softness
themes.note: Consumer segment de-grew 9% in FY26 on weak Europe/US demand and Middle East order cancellations, though new customer programs continue to be added.

themes.label: Diversification into consumer electronics and semiconductor
themes.note: Commenced commercial supplies to a consumer electronics customer and signed a Korean semiconductor tray supply agreement, seen as large new growth vectors alongside healthcare.

themes.label: Margin expansion
themes.note: FY26 EBITDA margin rose 630bps to 29.0% and PAT margin rose 540bps to 17.2%, with management guiding margins sustainable/improving on a year-on-year basis.

themes.label: Geopolitical/trade disruption
themes.note: Heightened geopolitical tensions caused raw material inflation and selective logistics disruption, with some buffer being consumed on the Abu Dhabi project timeline.

themes.label: Capital readiness for growth capex
themes.note: Annual enabling resolution to raise up to INR500 crores positions the company to act quickly on large, capital-intensive opportunities without signaling an imminent raise.

key_takeaways: Healthcare segment revenue doubled in Q4 FY'26 and surged 139% to INR393 crores for the full year, contributing 40% of consolidated revenue, up from 21% in FY'25.
Consumer segment de-grew in Q4 FY26, primarily reflecting weaker market demand for home furnishings across Europe and the US; full-year consumer revenues were INR511 crores, down 9%.
Industrial segment grew 60% YoY in Q4 FY26; full-year industrial revenues grew 41% to INR87 crores.

Commercial launch of Shaily Harmony and Shaily Neo pen injectors for Semaglutide in India and other global markets, including launches by customers in Canada, first tentative US approval, and European authorization for Teriparatide.

Commenced commercial supplies to a consumer electronics customer in Q4 FY26 and signed a supply agreement with a Korean company for semiconductor trays, marking entry into the semiconductor supply chain.
Board approved an enabling resolution to raise up to INR500 crores annually, intended as a standing capital-readiness measure rather than a signal of a specific fundraise.
Consolidated FY26 revenue grew 26% YoY to INR991 crores, EBITDA grew 61% to INR288 crores (margin 29.0%), and PAT grew 83% to INR170 crores (margin 17.2%); ROCE 35.8%, ROE 26.9%, debt-to-equity 0.3x.
FY27 priorities: continue scaling healthcare, build/scale the Abu Dhabi facility, ramp up consumer electronics and semiconductor programs, and restore growth momentum in consumer home furnishings.
pressing_questions: Given the INR423 crores pen injector order book from a large domestic company spread over 4 years, and given healthcare revenue grew 139% in FY26 while consumer declined 9%, what quarterly healthcare revenue run rate should be expected in FY27, what proportion of FY26's INR393 crores healthcare revenue was one-time ramp-up versus recurring supply, and at what point does consumer need to recover to sustain ~25% consolidated top-line growth? (Management declined to give quarterly numbers or breakup of one-time vs recurring revenue.)

On the semiconductor tray opportunity, what is the total addressable market and what percentage of the overall semiconductor value chain does this product represent? (Management described it as more of a volume/consumable game with a 'fairly decent value' but did not quantify the value share.)

If global semiconductor tray players from China, Korea or Philippines set up in India, will there be pressure on Shaily's profitability in this business, and how cost-competitive would a Chinese player be versus Shaily? (Management said it's too early to answer these questions.)
How should investors reconcile the 40-42 million combined new-line capacity figure with the separately mentioned 36 million pen target for FY27 — what is the right number for FY27 pen supplies?

SAMBHV.about: Incorporated in 2018, Sambhv Steel Tubes Ltd manufactures finished products, including ERW black pipes and tubes (hollow section) and Galvanized iron (GI) pipes, using intermediate products such as sponge iron, blooms/slabs, and hot rolled (HR) coil.[1]

quarters.summary: Sambhv delivered its highest ever quarterly revenue, EBITDA and PAT in Q1 FY27, with revenue growth of 31%, EBITDA growth of 31% and PAT growth of 70%, driven by value-added product mix and capacity utilization. Looking ahead, management guided Q2 FY27 EBITDA/ton of INR7,500-8,500, FY27 EBITDA/ton of INR7,500-8,500 with 10-15% revenue and volume growth over FY26 base, FY27 EBITDA margin of ~12% (+/-1-2%) and PAT margin of ~6% (+/-1%), while capacity expansion (Kesda greenfield SS, DFT ERW mill, captive power/solar) remains on track for commissioning by Q4 FY27, supported by an INR100 crore warrant issuance and peak term debt of INR800-850 crore plus INR200-300 crore working capital debt by end FY27.

subsections.label: Q1 FY27 performance drivers
points: Highest ever quarterly revenue, EBITDA and PAT performance.
Growth reflects strength of integrated operations, timely execution, and continued focus on value-added products.
19% YoY increase in EBITDA per ton (excluding sponge iron sales) to INR10,000, driven by higher value-added product mix.
PAT margin improvement to over 7% reflects benefit of high realization in value-added products.

subsections.label: Fund raise / warrant issuance rationale
points: Board approved preferential issue of fully convertible warrants raising up to INR100 crores; promoter family and management are participating.
Proceeds to fund capacity expansion, strengthen working capital, invest in wholly-owned subsidiary Sambhv Tubes Limited, and meet general corporate purposes.
Part of the money will be utilized in the parent company and part in the wholly-owned subsidiary.
Money will support working capital requirement and promoter contribution ahead of Q4 Kesda project completion, and fund solar/DFT/power plant capex.
Not an enabling provision — promoter family is serious about the infusion.
No other external fund raise currently planned in short/medium term, though board approval could be sought in future if required.

subsections.label: Debt and capex schedule
points: Peak debt guidance follows execution of Kesda Phase 1, power plant, DFT pipe mill and solar power plant.
Most of Kesda's INR930 crore capex to be deployed this year (FY27).
Power plant + DFT mill capex of INR200 crores split INR100 crores this year and INR100 crores next year.
Rooftop solar capex of INR25 crores split INR10-12 crores this year and balance INR13 crores next year.

subsections.label: Demand elasticity
points: Even amid lackluster demand commentary from peers, the quantity Sambhv produces and sells is relatively small (20,000-24,000 ton/month excl. GP), so demand elasticity does not impact the company much.

As a fully integrated player with margin captured from sponge iron making to ERW pipe making, the company has pricing power and is not dependent on coil manufacturer pricing, allowing it to place volumes on its own terms.

subsections.label: Pricing environment
points: MS pipe pricing is softening in line with other large players' commentary; expected to stabilize around another 3-5% downward move this financial year.
Company's pipe pricing is typically maintained at approximately INR1 below the market leader.

Stainless steel price realization currently looking good; import dependence in India supports domestic pricing, though QCO relaxation and resumption of shipments could introduce competition and soften SS pricing going forward.
Cost of Chinese stainless steel production versus Indian production is now more or less at par, reducing pricing competition concerns for now.

subsections.label: Stainless steel import substitution opportunity
points: Unorganized and import-driven thin-gauge flat product market is around 70,000-80,000 tons/month; new Kesda greenfield project targets replacing this segment.
India is import-dependent for stainless steel consumption due to inadequate domestic production, prompting QCO relaxation by government.

subsections.label: Co-branding stainless steel strategy
points: Sambhv sells CR coils only (not pipes) to co-branding MoU partners who manufacture and sell pipes under the Sambhv brand alongside their own brand.

Model follows approach of India's major stainless steel producers given ~800-900 small-scale pipe manufacturing plants across the country (each ~100-200 ton capacity) selling within local regions, making direct bypass of trade structure difficult.
Strategy helps build brand awareness and market presence in stainless steel segment.
Geographic focus for pipes/tubes: not currently expanding into the South (below Bangalore/Hyderabad); stronger presence in North; met sales targets in UP over the last six months.
Stainless steel is sold pan-India including Kerala, Chennai, Assam (East), Jammu, and West Coast, in preparation for upcoming capacity expansion.
MoU partners grew from 10 at end of last fiscal year to 28 currently, with 18 new partners added this quarter.
Current supply volume to co-branding MoU partners is 1,200 tons, targeting 2,500 tons by year end.

subsections.label: Product mix and margin trajectory
points: SS 200 series comprises ~90% of current SS production; nickel requirement is low and met through nickel scraps/alloys, providing some immunity to nickel price fluctuations.
Realization per ton is rising overall as SS share in the portfolio increases, but segment-wise (like-for-like) realization is not increasing much.
SS margin guidance maintained at INR15,000-16,000 per ton for the financial year.
EBITDA per ton by segment is not separately tracked because ERP does not support segment-wise EBITDA in an integrated facility.
SS EBITDA per ton bottomed at INR10,000 in Q3 FY26 but has run at a regular rate of INR15,000 over the last 3-4 quarters.
Monthly SS sales currently at 5,000 tons, with planned capacity expansion to 20,000-25,000 tons/month.
SS CR coil margin currently INR15,000-16,000/ton, with SS HR coil margin expected at INR12,000-13,000/ton post-Kesda.

subsections.label: Vajra Alloys investment rationale
points: Vajra Alloys formed by ex-MIDHANI professionals plus a Chennai-based listed company promoter, planning India's first private super alloy plant (currently only MIDHANI manufactures such alloys domestically).

Sambhv sees synergy in skillset/competence for super alloy manufacturing; proposed capacity by Vajra is small, so Sambhv is not entering the segment directly but will source raw material for value addition in its own manufacturing setup.

Super alloys (in rolled/flat/seamless pipe form) have use cases in aerospace, defence, marine, gasification plants, nuclear plants, semiconductors, data centers and critical power plants; ~90% currently imported into India.
Sambhv acquired a 15% stake in Vajra Alloys.

subsections.label: Competitive positioning vs Jindal Stainless (JSL)
points: JSL predominantly operates on >1mm thickness coil with wide coil (>1,200mm); Sambhv's coil is narrow width (currently 330mm, going up to 650mm in new plant).
Sambhv's future CR coil will focus on high-precision, lowest-grade thickness (0.1-0.4mm), a segment currently predominantly imported into India.
Company does not compete directly with JSL on product portfolio; business segment is same but product segments differ.
Company has qualified for PLI, expecting ~13% of revenue from central government incentive till 2030.

subsections.label: Pipe diameter market coverage
points: Currently manufacturing pipes up to seven inches diameter; up to five inches produced from internal coil, five to eight inches via coil procured from NMDC and other large players.
This up-to-seven-inch segment covers ~80% of industry SKU requirement in tonnage terms; remaining 20% is higher diameter pipes not currently manufactured.
Post-Kesda, company will have in-house capability up to seven-eight inch pipe from own coil; beyond that will continue to procure coil externally.

subsections.label: Realization by product (context)
points: MS pipe & tube net realization ~INR60,000/ton in Q1 FY27, guided to ~INR58,000/ton in Q2 FY27.
GP pipe net realization ~INR75,000/ton in Q1 FY27, guided to INR72,000-73,000/ton in Q2 FY27.
SS 200 series net realization ~INR1,40,000/ton in Q1 FY27, guided to INR1,30,000/ton in Q2 FY27.
SS 300 series net realization INR2,00,000-2,10,000/ton in Q1 FY27, guided to ~INR2,00,000/ton in Q2 FY27.

subsections.label: Capacity expansion roadmap progress
points: Company on track to increase total finished product capacity from 0.68 mtpa to over 2 mtpa by 2030.

Successful completion of brownfield expansion of stainless-steel CR coil facility at Kuthrel Unit 2, doubling capacity from 58,000 tpa to 1,16,000 tpa via debottlenecking; consent to operate now in place, expanded capacity to be utilized from this year.
Greenfield project at Kesda and Kuthrel Unit 2 continue to progress well and remain on track for commissioning in Q4 FY27.
Board approved 8MW captive behind-the-meter rooftop solar power plant at Kuthrel facility (INR25 crore investment) to reduce power cost and increase renewable energy usage.
Total SS coil capacity targeted to reach 4,76,000 tpa by Q4 FY27.
Current MS ERW production of 3,50,000 tons being expanded by 1,50,000 tons, plus additional 3,00,000-4,00,000 tons via Phase 2 of Kesda.

MS capacity has grown from 150,000 to 500,000 tons over the past 3 years; planned additional 1 million tons over next 3-4 years, targeting final ERW pipe/tube capacity of 5 lakh tons and total MS capacity of 10 lakh tons via DFT/Phase2/Phase3 by FY2030 (5 lakh tons via current+DFT by Q2 FY28).

Captive power plant capacity to grow from current 25MW to final 88-90MW, with a longer-term target of 150MW by 2030; power cost saving from captive power expected at INR180-200 crores post full build.

subsections.label: Kesda project execution status
points: Currently executing first phase of Kesda unit (3,60,000 tons out of entire 1.2 million tons envisaged across three phases).
Substructure (below-earth) work completed; superstructure work at advanced stage, allowing machinery installation during the current monsoon.
Management is optimistic about starting trial run and production by Q4 FY27.
Phase 2 currently under Board guidance; commentary on Phase 2/3 expansion plan to be announced once approved, likely post Q4 Phase 1 production start.
Kesda Phase 1 average capacity utilization guided at ~35% in FY28, rising to 60-65% in FY29.

subsections.label: Utilization dynamics
points: MS pipes and tubes utilization is above the 70% market norm at over 65% currently, essentially near peak efficiency achieved in Q1 FY27.
GP pipe and coil operating above 90%, well above market.
Stainless steel operating at 60% level, at the low end of the 60-65% market norm.
SS production has peaked, explaining the static quarter-on-quarter production/sales volume number in stainless steel.

subsections.label: Cost advantage from integration
points: Integrated manufacturer handling entire production process from iron ore and coal to finished pipe, sourced within 200-250 km radius in Chhattisgarh.
Access to India's highest-grade iron ore (one of world's largest mines) and lowest-cost domestic coal provides a cost advantage.
Gradual capacity approach mirrors earlier expansion in stainless steel (58,000 to 116,000 tons, now further major expansion).

subsections.label: Sponge iron self-sufficiency
points: Company does not source sponge iron externally; makes special grade sponge iron used only internally.
B-grade sponge iron not meeting internal quality requirement is sold as an allied/semi-intermediate product.
Mostly a scrap-based stainless-steel manufacturer with in-house capacity to cater to additional sponge iron requirement for Phase 1; no outside sourcing required currently.

subsections.label: Regional footprint
points: Pipes and tubes: not currently expanding into down South (below Bangalore and Hyderabad); presence stronger in North; sales targets met in UP over last six months.

Stainless steel: sold across whole of India, including Kerala, Chennai, Assam (East), Jammu, and the West Coast, targeting the entire Indian market ahead of capacity expansion to 20,000-25,000 tons/month.

subsections.label: Fuel supply shift
points: Shifted from LPG to PNG (piped gas from GAIL) in January 2026; no material cost or supply impact currently due to war situation; plant runs 24/7 with uninterrupted PNG supply.

subsections.label: Family governance / succession planning
points: No formal succession planning currently exists in the minds of promoters and Chairman Emeritus; four brothers oversee different parts of the family business, with Sambhv Steel Tubes run by Chairman Mr. Suresh Goyal and MD & CEO Mr. Vikas Goyal.
Professionals outside the promoter family have been hired into different functions, operating independently and reporting to MD & CEO / Chairman and Managing Director.
Third generation has been inducted but deployed at new project sites to gain first-hand execution experience, working from the bottom of the organization before climbing the ladder.
Shareholding is equally distributed among family members, reducing conflict risk per management.

subsections.label: Warrant issuance and future fund raising
points: INR100 crore fully convertible equity warrant issuance approved by Board, with promoter family and management participating, to fund capex, working capital, and subsidiary investment.
No other external fund raising currently on the table; may approach the market in future with Board approval if required, but not envisaged in short/medium term.

subsections.label: Vajra Alloys stake
points: Sambhv acquired a 15% stake in Vajra Alloys, gaining exposure to India's first planned private super alloy plant and PLI benefits expected at ~13% of revenue till 2030.

subsections.label: Pricing and demand risk
points: MS pipe pricing softening, expected to stabilize ~3-5% lower this financial year in line with peer commentary.
Stainless steel shipments delayed due to war situation affecting ship availability; QCO framework relaxation continuing to allow imports, which could increase competition once shipments normalize.
Possible pricing anomaly: domestic BIS-compliant producers face different compliance burden versus Chinese/other imports not under BIS compliance.

subsections.label: Nickel price exposure
points: 90% of current SS production is in 200 series with low nickel requirement, met via nickel scraps and other alloys, providing some immunity to nickel price fluctuations versus peers dependent on nickel-plated iron.

subsections.label: Anti-dumping/QCO regulatory risk
points: No anti-dumping duty currently on stainless steel; only a QCO relaxation is in effect.
A proposal for anti-dumping duty on stainless steel from South East Asian countries and China is under consideration by different ministries but not yet fructified.

subsections.label: Monsoon / seasonal impact
points: Q2 may see a dampener due to moisture in raw material, price softness in the market, and demand slowness during monsoon.

subsections.label: Safeguard duty expiry
points: Safeguard duty on steel (co-steel) ends in FY28; management does not foresee much price correction post expiry given equilibrium demand-supply, including ramp-down in Chinese production even as domestic primary-route capacity ramps up.

key_takeaways: Sambhv delivered its highest ever quarterly financial performance, with growth of revenue by 31%, EBITDA by 31%, and PAT by 70%.

Sambhv achieved its highest ever sales volume of value-added products, with strong contribution across all segments. Sales volume grew by 16% year-on-year, while value-added products volume increased by 27% year-on-year.
This resulted in 19% year-on-year increase in EBITDA to INR10,000 per ton, excluding sponge iron sales.
Achieved revenue of INR732 crores, total EBITDA of INR100 crores, and PAT of INR56 crores. EBITDA margin remained strong at 13%, while PAT margin improved to over 7%.
Successful completion of brownfield expansion of stainless-steel CR coil facility at Kuthrel Unit 2, doubling production capacity from 58,000 tons per annum to 1,16,000 tons per annum.
Greenfield project at Kesda and Kuthrel Unit 2 continue to progress well and remain on track for commissioning in Q4 FY27.

Board approved installation of 8-megawatt captive behind-the-meter rooftop solar power plant at Kuthrel facility, an INR25 crores investment, and a preferential issue of fully convertible warrants raising up to INR100 crores.
Secured product approvals from Engineers India Limited and Chennai Metro Rail Limited; signed 18 new MoUs under the Sambhv co-branding initiative, taking total base to 28 partners.

quarters.summary: FY26 was a landmark year for Sambhv with sales volume growth of 37%, revenue growth of 60%, EBITDA growth of 79% and PAT growth of 147%. Management guided EBITDA/ton of INR7,500-8,000 for Q1 FY27 and FY27 overall, volume growth of 10-15% YoY in FY27, and reiterated the Kesda greenfield (3,60,000 tpa SS) commissioning by Q4 FY27 with benefits visible from FY28, alongside a longer-term target of 2 million tons of finished capacity (with ~60% utilization) by 2030 and 10-12% market share aspirations in MS and SS.

subsections.label: Capex funding breakdown
points: Of the announced INR930 crores Kesda capex, INR200 crores was spent as of last quarter, now increased to INR300 crores; balance INR630 crores to be incurred.
Company plans to take around INR675 crores of term loan for Kesda capex; further capex from this project will be funded by debt.

Additional INR200 crores capex announced this quarter (power plant + DFT debottlenecking) is more or less debottlenecking and operational efficiency capex, to be funded through internal accrual and a maximum of INR150 crores debt.

Power plant expected to give power cost saving of INR60-70 crores; debottlenecking of rolling mill in Sarora gives additional capacity of 150,000 tpa; INR50 crores investment in DFT pipe mill route expected to unlock operating value of INR40-50 crores — combined operating boost of INR100-120 crores from the INR200 crore capex.

subsections.label: Debt prudence philosophy
points: Main purpose of IPO was to become financial prudent and reduce debt; management is very sceptical of debt-fuelled growth.
Internal metrics: long-term debt will not exceed 1.5x net worth and not exceed 1.5x forward EBITDA.
Expected peak long-term debt at max INR800 crores and INR200-300 crores of working capital debt for the currently announced capex.

subsections.label: EBITDA per ton drivers Q4 FY26
points: Q4 EBITDA/ton was above expectations; procurement of raw material (iron ore/coal) done in Q3 at bottom prices was used in Q4, creating a favorable cost-price gap.
HR coil prices suddenly rose in December as capacity excess converted into consumption, reducing the need for market discounts and improving finished product pricing.

Going forward, if HR coil prices remain maintained and raw material prices reduce a bit in the rainy season, margins could improve further; Q1 and Q4 are seasonally strong for the steel industry vs Q2/Q3.

subsections.label: Price pass-through to EBITDA
points: Realization increase of INR2,000-3,000/ton across MS, GP and SS; only 50-60% of price increase is passed through to EBITDA level, rest absorbed via credit notes/discounts to customers.
Raw material costs like zinc increased manifold and energy costs also rose during the war period, offsetting some of the realization gains.

subsections.label: Inventory increase rationale
points: Inventory increase of ~40% is in line with revenue growth of ~40% (from INR1,500 crores to INR2,400 crores).

Last year the company had just started stainless steel and coated products with lower capacity utilization and hence lower stock; this year full capacity utilization has led to proportionally higher stock.

subsections.label: Current investments clarification
points: Excess INR100 crores parked in liquid mutual funds at March year-end (insignificant risk, convertible to cash anytime); shown as current investment, not non-current.

subsections.label: Raw material cost stability
points: Iron ore and coal (basic raw materials) show limited price fluctuation; NMDC raised prices by ~INR250 after one month and ~INR200 before that; coal price increased only 5-10%.

60% of inventory is raw material (stabilized pricing), 40% is finished goods/stock-in-trade/stores-spares; company values WIP on cost basis, so no stock profit/loss distortion; parity between old and new stock pricing.

subsections.label: Aspirational margin/profitability profile (5-year)
points: Business typically operates on a median EBITDA margin of 12% plus-minus 2% in worst/best case scenarios.
PAT margin operating bandwidth is 5% plus-minus 1%: worst case 4%, best case (as shown in Q4) 6%.

subsections.label: Demand drivers across sectors
points: Solar sector: India has done 135 GW and target is 500 GW; about 4 million tons of steel to be consumed in this build-out.

Warehousing: currently at 25 crore sq ft with target of 100 crore sq ft by 2030; 5 million tons of steel will be used; warehousing pipe/tube requirement assumed at 60-70% (mentioned range 70-80%/60-70%).

Railways: ~1,300 terminals to be redeveloped, 400 new Vande Bharat trains to run; metro network to expand from 1,150 km to 3,000 km; 400 new airports to be built — all driving hollow section/stainless steel pipe and tube demand.
Stainless steel usage rising in train piping, railings at terminals, and metro interior/railings/track-side railings, all converting to pipe and tube form.
Government initiative to strengthen public transport cited as a demand tailwind (reference to PM's comments on public transport usage).

subsections.label: Stainless steel value chain explanation
points: SS is a three-step process: manufacture liquid metal, convert to slabs, convert slabs to HR coil, then cold-roll HR coil to CR coil.

Production number of 1,69,000 tons includes intermediate products (slabs ~60,000 tons, HR coils ~59,000 tons) which are captively consumed; only CR coil (~49,000 tons) is saleable, explaining the gap between production and sales figures.
From existing facility, only CR coil is sold as end product currently.

subsections.label: Carbon steel/coated value chain explanation
points: MS process has an added step versus SS: sponge iron manufacturing occurs before melting.
Coated steel process has an additional step: after HR, cold rolling is done, then the CR coil is galvanized, and the galvanized coil is converted into pipes.
90-95% of CR coil is converted into galvanized (GP); remainder converted directly into pipes (CRFH pipe).

subsections.label: 300 series stainless ramp-up plan
points: Last two quarters only ~10% of SS production was 300 series; plan remains 10-20% for now given management is focusing on strongly developing the P&T (pipes and tubes) co-branding section with ~10 MoU partners.
When Kesda starts, company will sell some SS HR coil and CR simultaneously, and enter utensil section and 400 series; at that time 300 series ratio could rise to 30-40% and 400 series to 10-20%.
Currently focus remains on 200 series where margins are good and market share needs to be captured strongly.

subsections.label: ERW/DFT production ratio
points: At current ~20,000 tpm pipe production, 15,000-16,000 tons/month comes from in-house coil and 4,000-5,000 tons/month from outside HR coil.

Going forward at 30,000-35,000 tpm, expect 20,000-25,000 tons/month in-house and 5,000-10,000 tons/month from outside coil, since large sizes (above 7 inches) can only be made from outside coil currently; DFT will make large/special sizes available immediately, improving delivery speed and margins.

subsections.label: Working capital cycle by segment
points: Cash conversion cycle of 17 days achieved in FY26 through significant planning efforts; expected to remain in this range in FY27.
Once stainless steel production ramps up (2028), cycle expected to rise to 25-30 days due to advanced raw material cycle and longer credit period in SS versus MS pipe/coated products.
Company will try to keep cycle below 17 days where possible; variation expected between 17-25 days currently.

subsections.label: Expansion projects progress
points: Greenfield project at Kesda and Kuthrel-2 progressing as scheduled; Phase 1 (3,60,000 tpa SS) remains on track for commissioning in Q4 FY27, with benefits visible in capacity utilization from FY28.
Debottlenecking projects for SS CR coils completed, increasing capacity from 58,000 tpa to 1,16,000 tpa; consent to operate expected within the week of the call.
ERW and tubes capacity being expanded by 1,50,000 tpa through Direct Forming Technology (DFT) at an estimated capex of INR50 crores; total ERW capacity to rise to 0.5 million tpa upon completion.
Public hearing completed for proposed 30 MW captive power plant at Sarora (capex ~INR150 crores), expected to make Sarora self-sufficient in power and improve operating efficiencies.

In Sarora, the 30MW plant will make it 100% self-sufficient in power; in Kesda, a 25MW plant will make Phase 1 of the rolling mill self-sufficient; Kuthrel currently still imports some grid electricity but plans exist to integrate with the power plant system going forward.

subsections.label: Direct Forming Technology (DFT) benefits
points: DFT allows immediate size changes versus the current 3-4 hours needed to change size on existing lines, improving right-time delivery.
Production capacity increases by about 10,000-12,000 tons per month from one machine.
Not very beneficial for small sizes; company plans to convert all large sizes (4 inches and above) to DFT.

subsections.label: 2030 capacity roadmap and milestones
points: Target of 2 million tons finished capacity by 2030, split as 10 lakh tons MS pipes & tubes, 3 lakh tons coated product, and 7 lakh tons stainless steel coil.

12 lakh tons shown in Slide 9 will be executed in three phases; Phase 1 (already announced, INR930 crores) covers 3,60,000 tons SS install capacity; Phase 2 and Phase 3 product composition not yet finalized.
Company aims for 10-12% market share in both MS pipe & coil and stainless steel flat products & coil by 2030.
Milestones will be announced progressively as each phase advances.

subsections.label: HR coil in-house capability
points: After transferring SS manufacturing facility to Kesda, in-house HR coil manufacturing capability improved from 6,000 tons of SS-linked capacity to 10,000 tons of HR coil, to be converted into ERW pipes plus supplemented by market-sourced HR coil.

subsections.label: Kesda ramp-up expectations
points: Phase 1 Kesda utilization expected to peak in Q3-Q4 of the ramp year; Q1 FY28 utilization won't be fully visible.
Average capacity utilization in first year of commissioning expected to be not more than 40%.

subsections.label: Distribution network expansion
points: Company has increased distributors by ~10% and dealers by ~40%, expanding market presence and penetration, cited alongside inventory growth in line with revenue growth.

subsections.label: Energy supply resilience during West Asia war
points: Company mostly depends on in-house power from captive power plants; also commissioned LNG-based pipeline (switched from LPG to PNG/LNG in January 2026), just before the war started.

Chhattisgarh PNG city gas distribution is limited; via MOU with GAIL and state of Chhattisgarh, PNG supply has been provided uninterruptedly to the company as a Chhattisgarh-based manufacturer, so plants ran 24x7 without shortage impact.

Large plants dependent on imported coking coal have seen rising costs; Sambhv's industry relies on domestically abundant coal at good, stable pricing, so the company was not adversely impacted by the war and even benefited from resulting price improvements.

subsections.label: Raw material stock valuation approach
points: Company defines all WIP inventory on a cost basis; no stock profit/loss recognized because raw material stock (iron ore, coal) is valued at real-time achieved/received cost, and pricing parity exists between old and new stock levels.

subsections.label: Competitive positioning vs Jindal Stainless
points: Chemical composition and physical properties of company's SS matches BIS/Indian standard, similar to Jindal Stainless.

Company currently produces SS 200/300 series via narrow width rolling mill and cold rolling mill; Jindal Stainless produces widths up to 2-2.5 meters, which is much larger, meaning company's use case is somewhat more restricted in the width sense.

subsections.label: Import/BIS standard dynamics
points: Government has set a specific deadline of October 10 after which no bill of lading for non-BIS standard imports will be allowed into India (previously extensions were given in 3-6 month increments).

Price increases in India have mirrored price increases in China due to the same energy/war crisis; nickel, chrome and copper prices have risen in both markets, so China's production cost is not meaningfully lower than India's, limiting dumping risk.

India lacks sufficient domestic capacity to fully meet consumption, so some import from China will continue; once BIS-standard licensing is granted, BIS-standard imported material will come in, but company sees no pricing pressure in the domestic market from this.

subsections.label: Value-added product plans (color coated sheets)
points: No current plan for color-coated/roofing sheets, but this remains on the table for the future if the company sees it can be a significant player leveraging its integrated facilities to penetrate the market.

subsections.label: PLI scheme (Ministry of Steel) participation
points: Signed MOU with Ministry of Steel under PLI scheme 1.2 for stainless steel CR coils, targeting manufacturing of thinner gauge coils for higher value applications.

PLI can be availed until 2030-31, capped at INR200 crores or install capacity tonnage production, whichever is lower; incentive percentage will be 13-15% depending on thickness/grade of steel manufactured.
Company expects to have three to four financial years to avail this PLI incentive post Q4 FY27 commissioning.

PLI is designed as a percentage incentive of revenue; if pricing wars occur, it acts as a safety net; if cost/price structure stays stable, PLI will directly improve margins, similar to benefits seen by other manufacturers (e.g., mobile electronics) under PLI schemes.

Seamless long product has been approved under PLI 1.2 scheme; full project planning/timeline will be announced only once complete government approvals are received (deemed imprudent to announce before that).

subsections.label: Co-branding stainless steel pipe MOUs
points: Six additional MOUs executed under co-branding for stainless steel pipe manufacturing this quarter, bringing total live MOUs to 10; discussions with several other partners in progress.
About 1,200 tons of quantity achieved via co-branding MoU holders; target for this year is ~2,500 tons/month via co-branding partnerships.

subsections.label: New product line philosophy
points: Company's philosophy is that new projects/products will be supplementary or complementary to the current integrated setup/skill set with low capex; no specific new product to be quoted as of this call.
Company plans to add two to three new product lines to its portfolio as part of the 2 million ton 2030 vision, though Phase 2/Phase 3 product composition for Kesda is not yet finalized.

subsections.label: West Asia war impact
points: War-related crisis affected the quarter, but company delivered highest ever revenue, EBITDA and PAT despite this.
Energy costs rose during the war period; zinc prices increased manifold as a raw material cost pressure.

Company mitigated import/energy risk via captive power and LNG/PNG conversion completed just before war escalation, and via reliance on domestic (not imported) coal versus large plants dependent on imported coking coal, whose pricing rose.

subsections.label: Monsoon/seasonal demand risk
points: Public reports/El Nino publications suggest a below-normal monsoon this time versus last year's phenomenally prolonged (4-5 month) monsoon that resided till November-December.
A below-normal monsoon could give a slight demand uptick for the steel industry; even in a normal monsoon scenario, cyclic Q2/Q3 demand softness is expected as usual.

subsections.label: Realization pass-through risk
points: Only 50-60% of realization increases are passed through to EBITDA; remainder absorbed via credit notes/discounts to customers, with raw material costs (zinc, energy) also rising.

subsections.label: Import/dumping risk (China)
points: Government has fixed October 10 deadline after which non-BIS standard import bills of lading will not be allowed; however, since China's production costs have risen similarly to India's, large-scale dumping is seen as unlikely and no pricing pressure is currently visible in the domestic market.

subsections.label: Near-term margin outlook
points: Q1 FY27 EBITDA/ton guided at INR7,500-8,000, contingent on HR coil and raw material price trends.
FY27 average EBITDA/ton expected at INR7,000-8,000 if current market conditions persist, with volume growth of 10-15% versus FY26.

If HR coil prices remain maintained and raw material prices ease slightly during monsoon while finished goods prices hold, performance could be even better; Q2/Q3 demand may soften slightly due to seasonal monsoon effects, as Q1/Q4 are typically strong for the steel industry.

subsections.label: Long-term margin/capacity outlook (2030)
points: At 2030 targeted product mix and ~60% capacity utilization, EBITDA/ton profile expected around INR8,000-9,000.
Business typically operates on a median EBITDA margin of 12% plus-minus 2% (worst/best case), and PAT margin bandwidth of 5% plus-minus 1% (worst case 4%, best case 6% as shown in Q4 FY26).

subsections.label: HR coil price/safeguard duty outlook
points: HR coil price moved ~20% from ~INR45,000/ton (Dec first week) to ~INR56,000/ton; company benefited from this pricing move even as raw material costs also rose.

Safeguard duty backup for 1-2 years is expected to protect against dumping; production and consumption of HR coil are now near parity, so HR coil prices are not expected to fall very low going forward.

Overall, if we say, in FY27, we can expect EBITDA in the range of 7,000 to 8,000 on an average side if the market situation continues to be like this.
A volume growth vis-a-vis '26 is around 10% to 15% is what we are expecting.
You can take a figure of 10 to 12%, 10 has become very bare minimum if there is any problem, and if we do better we can do around 12-12.5% as well.
The first phase of expansion having 3,60,000 ton per annum of stainless steel capacity remain on track for commissioning in quarter four, financial year 2027.
By Q4 FY '27 [ERW 150,000 ton capacity to come online].

We've set up a huge target that in the next four or five years, we want to reach 2 million tons of finished steel capacity... 10 lakh ton of MS pipes and tubes, 3 lakh ton of coated product and approximately 7 lakh ton of stainless steel coil.
We will have 10% to 12% of MS coil & pipe market share and 10% to 12% of stainless steel flat products & coil market share in 2030.
If we talk about 2030, sir, my capacity utilization will be around 60%.
If I do 60% capacity utilization, then my EBITDA profile should be around INR8,000 to INR9,000 per ton, the kind of product mix that we have announced.
Our business usually operates on a median margin of 12%, plus-minus 2% bracket in the worst-case scenario and the best-case scenario.
Our PAT's operating bandwidth is 5% plus-minus 1%. So 5% is a net profit margin, plus-minus 1%, worst-case scenario 4, best-case scenario which we have displayed in Q4 is 6%.
By another, like by FY28, we will have another INR300 crores to INR400 crores of additional capex that we may announce, depends on this particular announced capex execution and timeline.
In SS segment, we are going to achieve around 60% to 65% of the utilization... with that capacity expanded.
For MS pipe and coil, 65% to 70% MS pipes and tubes.
For GP, we can achieve around 80% to 90% easily.
For ERW, 70%-75% at max. That is the utilization that we can achieve after a DFT comes in line.
We are expecting a peak long-term debt of around INR800 crores at max and INR200 crores to INR300 crores of working capital.
FY27 will also remain in this range [17 days], our expectation is. But as soon as my stainless steel production goes live in 2028, at that time my cycle will be 25 to 30 days.

PLI scheme that for the thin gauge cold roll coil that we have received, we can avail it till 2030 or 2031 or so, but it will be capped at around INR200 crores or the install capacity tonnage production... In terms of percentage, it will be in the range of 13% to 15%.
What would be the utilization in '28? Would it be like greater than 60%-70%? It will be around that range only.
My capacity utilization will be around not more than 40% for the first year of commissioning.
This year's target is that about 2,500 tons per month, we should get pipe manufacturing done in co-branding with through our MoU holders.

key_takeaways: FY26 have been a landmark year for the Sambhv with a growth of total sales volume by 37%, revenue 60%, EBITDA 79% and PAT by 147%.
The first phase of expansion having 3,60,000 ton per annum of stainless steel capacity remain on track for commissioning in quarter four, financial year 2027.

We have completed the debottlenecking projects for stainless steel CR coils, which will increase capacity from 58,000 ton per annum to 1,16,000 ton per annum. We are expecting to receive the consent to operate in this week.

We are expanding our ERW and tubes capacity by 1,50,000 ton per annum through direct forming technology (DFT) with an estimate capex of INR50 crores. Upon completion, our total ERW pipes and tubes capacity will increase to 0.5 million ton per annum.

We have signed MOU with the Ministry of Steel under the PLI scheme 1.2 for stainless steel CR coils... we have executed six additional MOUs under the co-branding for stainless steel pipe manufacturing. With these additions, a total of 10 MOUs are now live under this initiative.

Revenue increased by 60% to INR2,413 crores. EBITDA increased by 79% to INR276 crores with EBITDA margin remain over 11%. PAT more than doubled to INR143 crores while PAT margin improved from 3.8% to 6%. We have delivered ROCE of 16% despite continuous capex.

The quarter marked our highest ever revenue, EBITDA and PAT performance despite the war-related crisis. Revenue increased by 38% to INR685 crores. EBITDA grew by 91% to INR92 crores... PAT more than doubled to INR56 crores. EBITDA margin improved significantly to 13% and PAT margin improved to 8%.

We have a target of 2 million ton of finished steel capacity in the next four or five years: 10 lakh ton of MS pipes and tubes, 3 lakh ton of coated product and approximately 7 lakh ton of stainless steel coil, aspiring to 10-12% market share in both MS and stainless steel by 2030.

KPEL.about: K.P. Energy(KPEL) is a part of the KP Group of Surat. It is involved in the development of utility scale wind power generation infrastructure. The major activities encompass siting of wind farms, acquisition of lands and permits, EPCC of wind projects, along with balance of plant (BoP) infrastructure. KPEL also owns and operates WTGs (Wind Turbine Generators) and solar power plant as an IPP( Independent Power Producers). The company undertakes projects principally in Gujarat. [1]

quarters.summary: KP Energy reported strong Q1 FY27 revenue growth (~126% YoY consolidated total income) driven by infrastructure development/EPC execution, but gross and EBITDA margins contracted sharply sequentially due to West Asia geopolitical disruption (Strait of Hormuz), fuel/logistics volatility, and rising right-of-way (ROW) costs for transmission. Management guided to 30-40% revenue growth for FY27 (down from prior 40-50% guidance), declined to give specific margin guidance, and reiterated confidence in order book visibility (2.16 GW / ~Rs.2,250 crore), IPP expansion (48.5 MW operational, plus 200 MW under PPA), and long-term sector tailwinds, while flagging grid/evacuation infrastructure pace and curtailment as watch items.

subsections.label: Margin pressure drivers
points: Q1 FY27 gross margin of ~20% vs 28% in Q4 FY26 reflects a sequential contraction of ~8 percentage points, explained by three major factors rather than execution ability.

Factor 1: West Asia geopolitical situation and Strait of Hormuz disruption impacted LPG availability, fuel, procurement, transportation, freight, logistics, and manpower availability; India's LPG import dependence on the Hormuz region made it particularly vulnerable, forcing costlier alternative spot purchases.

Labor availability disruption affected migrant labor mobility; demobilization/remobilization of manpower and equipment came at higher cost due to elevated accommodation and manpower costs and constrained availability of specialized resources.

Execution teams largely made up for productivity challenges to maintain project progress, but the associated cost impact could not be fully avoided; prolonged execution cycles would have meant continued absorption of fixed project and site overheads.

Factor 2: Volatility in fuel procurement and logistics affected equipment utilization; national fuel stock remained adequate but temporary government measures diverted bulk/commercial demand to retail channels, risking idle high-value specialized equipment (cranes, hydra cranes, excavators, trailers, DG sets) while hiring, manpower, and supervision overheads continued to accrue.

Factor 3: Increasing right-of-way (ROW) costs for transmission infrastructure — since late Q4 FY26, higher compensation expectations from landowners/farmers for transmission corridors and tower locations, which escalated following developments in Gujarat and culminated in a revised compensation framework; this escalation was already factored into Q1 cost assessment.

Management indicated Q1 should not be treated as an exact representative going forward but declined to assume immediate normalization of the environment; trying to rationalize planning and optimize execution to protect margins.
Margins also depend on project-stage mix (some projects beginning, some at peak, some ending), making a specific forward margin number inappropriate at this time.
Analyst noted margin trend comparable across renewable EPC sector peers, some of which saw margins fall by 12%, 7%, and 4%, indicating a sector-wide, not KP Energy-specific, issue.

subsections.label: Profitability despite margin compression
points: Despite percentage profitability pressure, absolute profit growth continued while scaling the business by more than 2x.
PBT and PAT both grew YoY in absolute terms even as margins contracted.

subsections.label: Order intake pace vs momentum
points: Despite strong on-ground wind sector activity, order inflow announcements have been slower because management is being selective in picking up orders based on cost components, execution capabilities, region (ROW cost variability, grid availability, connectivity), rather than execution constraints.
Company remains vigilant on all market opportunities and continues to make selective choices in order acquisition.

Order book value calculation: opening order book of Rs. 3,000 crore, less ~Rs. 500 crore executed in Q1, leaves Rs. 2,500 crore; stated current order book of Rs. 2,250 crore already factors in a conservative ~Rs. 250 crore adjustment for possible de-scoping of existing orders.
Order book in GW terms is distinct from order book in value terms; GW capacity reduces as projects get energized, while value-based order book is affected by milestone invoicing.

Company does not disclose order intake value at times due to client confidentiality requirements (clients wish to maintain business secrecy); management will pass on investor request to disclose order values to concerned management.

subsections.label: Pipeline for other states (Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh)
points: Grid/connectivity constraints and recent government resort to curtailment are holding back conversion of pipeline in newer states; generating capacity cannot always be encashed due to curtailment, creating setbacks for existing entities.
BESS (battery energy storage) services are being worked on as a solution to curtailment, to avoid being a victim of curtailment while expanding into other states.
Selectivity in orders is partly driven by desire not to block resources on projects facing these constraints.

subsections.label: Business mix / growth engine
points: Infrastructure development continues to be the primary growth engine of the business, growing ~142% YoY.
O&M business continued its growth trajectory, more than doubling YoY.
Sale of power revenue grew modestly YoY.
IPP currently a small share (2%) of total revenue as predominant focus remains on EPC business; expected to rise as new IPP capacity is commissioned.

subsections.label: CPP vs IPP comparison (analyst reference to KPI Green)
points: Analyst noted that at KPI Green, IPP contributes 18-20% of total revenue and helped sustain EBITDA margin despite pressure, since IPP carries higher margins than CPP/EPC.
KP Energy's IPP contribution remains low (2% vs 1% prior quarter) as EPC has been the predominant focus historically.

subsections.label: IPP expansion plan
points: Two new IPP projects with PPAs signed with sovereign entities (one signed in April, another in June/July), each 100 MW, both with ~24-month commissioning timelines from April 2026 onward.

Possibility of partial commissioning under these PPAs being explored, which could allow revenue generation starting roughly one year in, rather than waiting the full two-year period for the entire capacity.
Combined portfolio (48.5 MW existing + 200 MW new) would reach 248.5 MW at end of the ~2-year build-out.
Faster execution pace desired not only to reduce IDC (interest during construction) but also for quicker generation and revenue booking.

subsections.label: Geographic capacity expansion (Karnataka)
points: Karnataka identified as a new state for project development; company is in advanced-stage discussions and has already tied up connectivity, land, EHV, and PSS (pooling substation) arrangements.
Approximately 30% of the total work required for the Karnataka project has already been completed; a formal notification/press release is expected soon.
Management indicated it will slowly and steadily venture into different states beyond Gujarat and Karnataka.

subsections.label: Expansion beyond Gujarat
points: Management acknowledged that visible execution beyond Gujarat remains negligible to date, citing the need for thorough preparation before venturing into new geographies to avoid being caught off guard.

Rajasthan and Madhya Pradesh pipeline (flagged in prior quarter) has not yet progressed significantly to land/grid-connectivity-secured stage due to grid connectivity constraints and curtailment issues affecting new-state expansion timing.

subsections.label: Leadership changes
points: Prof. Sunil Maheshwari appointed as Vice Chairman, bringing four decades of experience across strategy, governance, business transformation, and organizational leadership across power, energy, infra, banking, and healthcare sectors.
Mr. Kapil Kriplani appointed as incoming Group CFO, bringing experience in finance, capital markets, and strategic growth initiatives.
Mr. Rajesh Shrivastava appointed as Executive Director.
BDO brought on board as Statutory Auditors.

Dr. Faruk G Patel described these four leadership/governance changes together as a signal of aggressive commitment by the promoter group; noted he remains involved in strategic and future development while a professional team handles day-to-day operations at KP Energy and other KP Group companies.

subsections.label: Group target revision
points: Group (KPI Green + KP Energy combined) has been targeting 10 GW by 2030 and is close to achieving that target; a revised group target is expected to be published soon.
Company-specific targets (in addition to group targets) are being worked on and will be published soon.

subsections.label: Related party transactions
points: Approximately 50% of the current order book (by value) is related-party business, with management stating all such transactions are conducted at arm's length.

Management views related-party IPP execution (e.g., for KPI Green) as a win-win — safe execution hands for the sister concern's capex and ease of operations for KP Energy — given KP Energy's leadership position in wind EPC with few direct peers.
Management stated third-party orders are evaluated on the same selection criteria as related-party orders, given abundant market supply and selective order-picking approach.
Promoter has invested in share warrants of KP Energy in the past year (per exchange notifications), reflecting confidence and intent to increase stake.
