subsections.label: Geopolitical / macro disruption
points: West Asia geopolitical situation and Strait of Hormuz disruption affected LPG availability, fuel, procurement, transportation, freight, logistics, and manpower availability, with broader knock-on effects for EPC execution economics.

Fuel procurement/logistics volatility from government measures managing abnormal demand diverted bulk/commercial fuel toward retail channels, risking idle specialized equipment and added remobilization costs.

subsections.label: Right-of-way (ROW) cost escalation
points: Rising ROW costs for transmission infrastructure, driven by higher landowner/farmer compensation expectations, escalated following farmer protests in Gujarat, culminating in a government-notified revised compensation framework.
If protests persist longer, execution and top-line delivery could be constrained despite company mobilization and willingness to execute.

subsections.label: Grid / transmission infrastructure pace
points: Management remains watchful of the pace of grid and transmission infrastructure development relative to renewable capacity growth, viewing it as a timing challenge rather than a structural concern given strong order book visibility to sequence projects.

Recent government resort to curtailment (over roughly the last quarter) has prevented some generating entities from encashing generation, a setback being addressed via BESS (battery storage) solutions.

subsections.label: Seasonal impact
points: Monsoon season creates a seasonally 'damp' quarter for execution/revenue, though this is not new and the company tries to offset it by capturing milestone-based revenue opportunities across projects.

subsections.label: Governance / market perception
points: An investor raised concerns about declining market cap and institutional ownership, questioning whether governance or related-party transaction concentration is contributing to a valuation discount; management stated it does not control share pricing/valuation and attributed this to other market factors.

An investor also raised concerns about the promoter's (Faruk Patel's) reduced visibility on recent calls versus prior periods; addressed directly by Dr. Faruk G Patel who joined the call to reassure investors.

subsections.label: KP Green Engineering margin read-through
points: Analyst asked whether CPP segment margin pressure seen at KPI Green and KP Energy would also reflect in KP Green Engineering; management declined to comment as it is a separately managed entity and suggested waiting for half-year results for clarity.

subsections.label: Revenue growth guidance revision
points: Management revised revenue growth guidance for FY27 down to 30-40% (from prior 40-50% guidance), citing on-ground uncertainties even though substantial order book is in hand.

In response to analyst pushback (given Q1 alone grew ~136% YoY), management reiterated internal planning targets to complete a substantial portion of the order book and separately stated commitment to 'at least 40 to 50%' growth versus last year if execution conditions (e.g., ROW-driven farmer protests) do not worsen, while keeping the external guidance conservative at 30-40%.

Management explicitly declined to give a specific margin guidance number for FY27, citing project-stage mix and factors beyond company control; stated Q1 should not be treated as a benchmark, but immediate normalization should also not be assumed.
No specific Q2 guidance given beyond noting it is seasonally a 'damp' quarter due to monsoons, with efforts to capture milestone-based revenue.

risk_register.risk: Sector-wide EPC margin compression

themes.label: Revenue/margin growth momentum
themes.note: Revenue grew ~126% YoY to Rs. 520.97 crore but gross margin contracted from 28% (Q4 FY26) to 20% (Q1 FY27) due to geopolitical, fuel/logistics, and ROW cost pressures.

themes.label: Order book strength & visibility
themes.note: Order book stands at 2.16 GW / Rs. 2,250 crore providing revenue visibility, though management is selective in fresh order intake and broader pipeline exceeds 2 GW.

themes.label: IPP & O&M annuity scale-up
themes.note: IPP portfolio at 48.5 MW operational, targeting 100 MW by FY27-end and 248.5 MW within ~2 years, expected to add ~Rs. 200 crore incremental revenue; O&M revenue also growing.

themes.label: India wind sector demand tailwind
themes.note: India added a record 6.05 GW of wind capacity in FY26, cumulative installed wind capacity crossing 56 GW, underpinning long-term sector opportunity.

themes.label: Geopolitical & input cost disruption
themes.note: West Asia/Strait of Hormuz disruption and rising right-of-way costs were the primary drivers of Q1 FY27 margin compression, described as an industry-wide, not company-specific, issue.

themes.label: Geographic expansion beyond Gujarat
themes.note: Karnataka project ~30% complete with connectivity/land tie-ups in place, but Rajasthan/Madhya Pradesh pipeline progress remains constrained by grid connectivity and curtailment.

themes.label: Governance & promoter visibility
themes.note: Investors raised concerns over declining market cap/institutional ownership and reduced visibility of Dr. Faruk Patel on calls; promoter joined the call directly to reassure stakeholders of continued commitment and leadership strengthening (Vice Chairman, Group CFO, Executive Director, new statutory auditor).

key_takeaways: We delivered a consolidated total income of approximately Rs. 520 crores, reflecting strong year-on-year growth.
We have seen some moderation in margins compared with certain earlier quarters.
Our current order book of 2.16 Gigawatt, valued at over Rs. 2,250 crores, provides us with strong revenue visibility.
There is one area where we remain watchful — the pace of grid and transmission infrastructure development.
We also see meaningful long-term potential in our upcoming IPP of 200-plus MW and O&M businesses, which can progressively add recurring and annuity-like revenue streams to the business.
A gross margin in Q1 FY27 was approximately 20% compared with that at 28% in Q4 FY26. This is a sequential contraction of approximately 8 percentage points.
Our profit before tax stood at Rs. 37.44 crores compared with Rs. 34.75 crores in FY26 Q1, while profit after tax stood at Rs. 26.08 crores compared with Rs. 25.42 crores last year similar quarter.
India added a record 6.05 GW of wind capacity in FY26, taking cumulative installed wind capacity beyond 56 GW.

quarters.summary: FY26 was a record year for KP Energy with revenue crossing INR 1,500 crore, EBITDA of ~INR 328 crore and PAT of INR 181 crore. Management guides to 40-50% revenue growth in FY27, backed by a ~2 GW / INR 3,000 crore order book, a growing O&M and IPP pipeline, new CERC power-trading license, and a long-term target of 10 GW by 2030, even as working capital and inventory build-up (due to turbine procurement and geopolitical supply-chain concerns) keep operating cash flow lower than revenue growth would suggest.

subsections.label: Operating cash flow / working capital
points: Cash flow from operations was lower vis-a-vis previous year due to increased inventory build-up for upcoming projects, driven by geopolitical situation making the company want to secure inventory and not lapse behind on procurement.
Company remains cash-operating positive on operational activity despite the increased inventory.
Debtor share is largely proportionate to revenue growth (from INR 958 crore to INR 1,506 crore); the change in operating cash flow trajectory was driven mainly by inventory, not debtors.
Other liabilities spiked due to advances made to and received from customers/suppliers to secure the supply chain amid geopolitical uncertainty.

Working capital cycle expected to remain proportionally higher with revenue growth (55% growth) and due to site implementation readiness needs for upcoming orders; described as part of normal operating business, not expected to revert to previous absolute levels but to scale proportionally.
Higher inventory currently held will eventually convert into debtors and be realized in cash going forward.

Cash from operations is being invested into inventory (WTG - wind turbine generator) and into working capital for mobilization of newly bagged 230+ MW orders, as well as initial investment/startup capital for two 100 MW IPP projects.

subsections.label: Margins
points: EBITDA margin improved from 20.46% in FY25 to 21.82% in FY26, indicating no cost concerns despite Q4 gross margin queries.
Q4 gross margin query on lower PLF in IPP projects addressed: power sales change from 6.18 to 5.62 was termed nominal and not a material driver of margin concerns.

EPC contracts with turbine procurement by KPEL carry different margins than those without turbine procurement — company pre-books/reserves turbines in advance to gain margin leverage, giving a fair share of margin versus a pure EPC contract without turbine, though a margin delta exists between the two contract types.

subsections.label: Capital allocation / financing
points: Interim dividend of INR 0.65 per share (FV INR 5) paid during FY26; Board recommended final dividend of INR 0.25 per equity share subject to shareholder approval at AGM.
Two 100 MW IPP projects together estimated at project cost of INR 1,700+ crore, of which ~INR 450+ crore would be funded via equity and the balance via debt.
New debt for upcoming IPP projects expected to carry interest cost in the range of 7.5%-8.5% depending on the funding cycle.
Promoter has previously invested ~INR 28 crore via share warrants and is expected to continue investing in company equity going forward.

subsections.label: Order book composition and timeline
points: Order book stands at nearly 2 GW across multi-year projects with a total value of approximately INR 3,000 crore, providing strong revenue visibility.
About 230 MW of new orders were added during the year, a testament to reputation for quality execution.

Previously the ~2 GW order book was expected to be completed by around September-October last year; three more orders (~230+ MW, ~INR 700-730+ crore ex-GST) were added in the last quarter, shifting completion expectations, with majority of projects now expected to be completed by FY27; further additions to the order book anticipated in coming months; company always plans a bit higher than the stated timeline.
On the INR 3,000 crore order book, approximately 50% is from Group entities and the balance 50% from outside the Group.
Order pipeline (distinct from order book) is entirely outside the Group; Group entity orders are only included in the order book once finalized, not in the pipeline.

subsections.label: O&M segment
points: O&M is a smaller-scale but high-quality annuity-style revenue stream being built by the company.
O&M portfolio is supported by a 24x7 network operation centre running IBM Maximo-based AI alerts and SCADA dashboards.
As installed base grows, O&M segment expected to increasingly contribute to quality and predictability of earnings.

subsections.label: IPP segment
points: IPP operational portfolio progressing steadily with a new pipeline of 200 MW additional capacity under development, which once fully operational will transform recurring revenue base and enhance quality/predictability of long-term earnings.

Two 100 MW IPP orders bagged; one already has a signed/being-signed Power Purchase Agreement (PPA), the other pending; both carry a 24-month delivery timeline from PPA date (first PPA timeline: 15 April 2026 to 15 April 2028).

Q4 unit generation for IPP portfolio declined quarter-on-quarter and IPP revenue declined YoY in Q4; management attributed this to a marginal seasonal decrease in wind performance between Q4 FY25 and Q4 FY26, expected to normalize with the season, with no concern on execution or operating assets.

KPI Green's wind IPP projects (its own capex) will continue to be executed by KP Energy on an arm's-length basis, given KP Energy's 1.5+ decade wind execution expertise and limited competition in the wind EPC segment; described as a win-win arrangement rather than KPI seeking an outside contractor.

subsections.label: India wind sector backdrop
points: India installed 6.05 GW of new wind capacity in FY26, the highest annual addition in the country's history, taking cumulative installed wind capacity above 56 GW and making India the fourth largest wind energy market in the world.
Wind energy accounts for approximately 9% of total installed power capacity, a share expected to grow.

India achieved total non-fossil fuel capacity addition of 55.3 GW in FY26, the highest in any single year in India's history; non-fossil fuel sources now represent over 50% of total installed power capacity, a milestone achieved five years ahead of the 2030 target.

Government target of 140 GW cumulative wind capacity by 2030 versus 56 GW currently implies 84 GW of new additions needed over roughly four years; India Wind Report 2025 gives a more conservative estimate of doubling to 107 GW by 2030.

India plans to deploy 30 GW of offshore wind by 2030, with initial bids of 4 GW being developed off the coasts of Gujarat and Tamil Nadu — a segment KP Energy is actively studying and positioning to enter.
Trajectory context: India added ~1.5 GW of wind annually in FY20 versus the record 6.05 GW added in FY26, showing the curve bending sharply upward, a trend expected to continue.

Offshore wind is at a nascent stage: Government of India identified Gujarat and Tamil Nadu for a planned 1 GW first phase, with a stakeholder consultation process underway on tariff, viability gap funding (VGF), and technology (most offshore turbine technology currently Chinese/European, with commercially viable single turbines around 12-16 MW versus 5 MW onshore turbines available in India). MNRE consultants and NIWE (National Institute of Wind Energy Assessment) are involved in wind data validation and policy consultation; KP Energy is already engaging with potential customers/consortium partners and will be positioned to bid once policy is finalized.

subsections.label: Power trading market context (CERC license)
points: India generated ~1,830 billion units of electricity in FY25, of which ~230 billion units (>13%) were traded through short-term markets.
Indian Energy Exchange total electricity volume traded in FY26 was 141 billion units, a 17% YoY growth.

Trading enables PAN-India utilization of energy regardless of generation state, positioning KP Energy to benefit by trading energy it generates or buys, PAN-India, via its new CERC interstate electricity trading license.

subsections.label: Integrated platform strategy
points: Management's stated strategy: the next decade of renewable energy will be led by companies that integrate generation, transmission, storage, and execution into one scalable ecosystem — the strategy KP Energy has been consistently building towards.

KP Energy has built an integrated renewable energy platform spanning energy modeling, land aggregation, wind resource assessment, evacuation infrastructure, EHV connectivity, project execution, and long-term O&M service.
Company continues strengthening forward and backward integration through strategic ISTS and STU connectivity acquisition.
Company evaluating future-focus opportunities including offshore wind and PSP (pumped storage plant) solutions to support grid stability and round-the-clock renewable energy requirements.
Company is actively scouting opportunities in other states of India.
Underpinning goal: KP Group's ambitious target of reaching 10 GW total by 2030.

subsections.label: CERC interstate electricity trading license
points: Received CERC (Central Electricity Regulatory Commission) interstate electricity trading license, enabling participation in power markets across the country on a pan-India basis, meaningfully broadening the addressable market into national renewable energy transactions.
Because trading is predominantly an activity where payments are made in advance, management does not see any stretch in working capital from this new business line.

subsections.label: Credit rating upgrade
points: CARE Ratings upgraded KP Energy's credit rating by two full notches from BBB (negative outlook) to A- (stable outlook) during FY26, reflecting a strengthened balance sheet and robust execution track record.

subsections.label: CSR / community initiatives
points: Company remains committed to creating impact beyond business through healthcare, education, skill development, and community welfare initiatives undertaken by the KP Human Development Foundation.

subsections.label: Related-party arrangement
points: KPI Green's wind IPP projects will continue to be executed by KP Energy on an arm's-length basis given KP Energy's execution expertise and limited wind-segment competition.

subsections.label: Geopolitical / supply chain risk
points: Geopolitical situation has made supply chain management more difficult, prompting the company to build up inventory to avoid falling behind on project execution and to secure supply.
Advances made to and received from customers/suppliers reflect efforts to secure supply chain amid the geopolitical situation, in case of missed procurement windows affecting delivery speed.

subsections.label: Working capital / cash flow risk
points: Increased inventory and working capital investment (for order mobilization and IPP project startup) have led to lower operating cash flow relative to revenue growth, though management does not consider this a fundamental concern and expects inventory to convert into debtors and cash over time.

subsections.label: Seasonal wind performance
points: Marginal decrease in wind performance in Q4 FY26 versus Q4 FY25 affected unit generation and IPP revenue; management characterizes this as a seasonal factor expected to normalize with the season.

subsections.label: Offshore wind policy uncertainty
points: Offshore wind opportunity remains nascent, pending government policy clarity on tariff structure and viability gap funding (VGF); most offshore turbine technology is not yet available domestically (mainly Chinese/European), which is a constraint until policy and technology availability mature.

subsections.label: FY27 priorities
points: Scale EPC execution to convert the near-2 GW order book into revenues with focus on timely project completion and quality delivery.
Accelerate IPP portfolio growth, aiming towards consistent annuity income for the coming 25 years.
Actively scouting opportunities in other states of India.
Underpinning goal of reaching 10 GW total by 2030.
Expected 40-50% revenue growth in FY27, supported by sufficient orders already in hand.
Majority of current order book projects expected to be completed by FY27, with further order additions anticipated in coming months.

themes.label: Revenue/margin growth momentum
themes.note: Consolidated revenue crossed INR 1,500 crore for the first time with 57% YoY growth, EBITDA up 68% and PAT up 57%, with Q4 EBITDA margin expanding 194 bps YoY.

themes.label: Order book strength & visibility
themes.note: Order book of ~2 GW / ~INR 3,000 crore, with 230+ MW added during the year, provides multi-year revenue visibility, though completion timelines have shifted to FY27.

themes.label: Working capital / inventory build-up
themes.note: Operating cash flow was lower than revenue growth due to elevated inventory (WTG stocking) and customer/supplier advances amid geopolitical supply chain concerns.

themes.label: IPP & O&M annuity scale-up
themes.note: IPP portfolio (48.5 MW operational, 200 MW new pipeline, two 100 MW projects with PPAs) and O&M (646 MW managed, +350% YoY Q4 revenue) are being built to add recurring, predictable earnings.

themes.label: India wind sector demand tailwind
themes.note: Record 6.05 GW wind capacity added in FY26 nationally, government targets of 140 GW wind and 500 GW non-fossil by 2030 create a multi-year structural demand tailwind for KP Energy.

themes.label: Power trading license (CERC) as new growth avenue
themes.note: New CERC interstate electricity trading license opens a pan-India power trading opportunity, expected to require minimal incremental working capital given advance payment norms.

themes.label: Offshore wind optionality pending policy clarity
themes.note: Offshore wind (30 GW target by 2030, 4 GW initial bids in Gujarat/Tamil Nadu) remains nascent, with KP Energy positioning for entry once government tariff/VGF policy and turbine technology availability mature.

key_takeaways: FY26 has been another landmark year for the company, marked by healthy financial performance, strong project executions, and strategic business expansion.
During the year, company has achieved significant growth on all the fronts including revenue, EBITDA, PAT.
During the year, company also achieved key strategic milestones including securing ISTS connected projects, expanding hybrid capability, receiving interstate electricity trading license from CERC.
Recently, we have become first in India to install 4.2 megawatt make in India windmill in South Gujarat.
We crossed INR 1,500 crores in revenue with EBITDA exceeding INR 328 crores and PAT reaching INR 181 crores.
Today, KP Energy has a renewable portfolio exceeding 3.7 gigawatt, project in hand exceeding 2.1 gigawatt, and a long-term vision of crossing 10 gigawatt by 2030.
Our current order book stands at nearly 2 gigawatt across multi-year projects with a total value of approximately INR 3,000 crores, providing strong revenue visibility in the coming years.
During the year FY26, CARE Ratings had upgraded KP Energy's credit rating by two full notches from BBB with a negative outlook to A- with a stable outlook.

So, in our IPP portfolio, so we have earlier I think we have this target of 100 megawatt and now I think we are targeting 250. So, how far can it go and what would be the plans to fund it, especially for capex this year?

In view of the current energy disruptions for the wind sector particularly why I think the government has these targets by 2030 and maybe some RPOs as well? But do we see or do we anticipate any stronger flagship policy pushes from the government for wind sector adoption?

We are not generating enough cash free cash flows in from our KP Energy company. What are the steps are we taking to generate cash and which will help us eventually to take low debt as against what we are seeing today?

On the INR 3,000 crores order book, how much is group entity orders and how much is non-group orders on the existing order book?

ABCAPITAL.about: Aditya Birla Capital Limited, the holding company for the financial services businesses of the Aditya Birla Group, is a universal financial solutions group catering to the diverse financial needs of its customers across their life stages.[1]

quarters.summary: ABCL delivered strong consolidated growth in Q1 FY27 (PAT +40% YoY, revenue +29% YoY) across NBFC, HFC, AMC and insurance businesses, backed by a Rs. 4,000 crore preferential capital raise. Management guided to continued NBFC/HFC scale-up (HFC targeting ₹1 lakh crore+ AUM and 15% RoE over 8-10 quarters), a new Gold Loan foray (200 branches by March 2027, ~1,000 over 3 years), life insurance FYP CAGR of 20%+ with VNB margin above 20% and doubling of Net VNB in 3 years, and health insurance targeting 100% combined ratio on IFRS basis this financial year, though management flagged higher input/energy costs creating uncertainty on future growth.

subsections.label: Overview
points: India's growth momentum continued to remain strong despite a challenging global backdrop, underpinned by healthy domestic demand, continued investment activity and broad-based credit growth.
Higher input and energy costs make the growth very uncertain in the future.
Performance supported by strong growth momentum, improved profitability along with healthy quality in lending and insurance businesses and continued expansion in AMC franchise.
Approach of pursuing growth opportunities while maintaining a strong focus on return of capital, along with disciplined execution, has enabled growth across businesses.

Capital has been provided for HFC's growth for the next several years and for NBFC growth for the next 3 years; company does not envisage any capital raise at ABCL, HFC or any other entity in the near future; growth capital for insurance also provided for the next 3 years.

subsections.label: Growth drivers
points: Strong start to FY27 with gross premium on sales basis growth of more than 50% YoY, continuing FY26 growth momentum in the industry.
Market share increase attributed to being the fastest-growing SAHI player during the quarter.

Grew strongly across both retail and group businesses; retail franchise diversified across retail distribution channels; proprietary channel and major bank/digital alliance partnerships all experienced impressive growth.

Launched Activ Yuva, a digital-first health insurance product designed specifically for young India, combining comprehensive health coverage with wellness-led engagement via HealthReturns™ incentivised wellness programme, built around the 'Eat, Move, Heal' philosophy.

Corporate business growth driven by focused and disciplined strategy to create a sustainable franchise; differentiated health-first insurance model now being taken to corporates with scale-up beginning.

subsections.label: IFRS transition
points: Company at forefront of transition to IFRS financial statements; Q1 FY27 financial statements prepared per IFRS principles.

Profit for Q1 FY27 versus loss in same period previous year on a comparative basis; claims ratio better than last year; company continues to endeavour to achieve 100% CoR on IFRS basis in this financial year.

subsections.label: Health First model / wellness engagement
points: Robust growth and superior unit economics driven by digitally enabled, differentiated Health First model scaled up over the last 10 years in business.
More than 50% of eligible retail consumers engage with the AI-driven consumer engagement engine for their health.
Customers earning Health Returns incentives show 6%+ lower loss ratios and 11%+ better persistency on an absolute basis (shown in slides 59 and 60).

Investments in managing customers with high health risks through interventions with more than 320K lives have led to improvement in their loss ratios by more than 13%, helping keep overall retail loss ratios well under control.

Management believes this business model gives a large competitive advantage as competitors also try to look at it seriously, but it requires large investment commitment and persistent efforts over many years to mature.

subsections.label: AI/claims technology
points: State-of-the-art AI/ML-driven claims auto-adjudication engine continues to enhance customer satisfaction and enable efficient claims management by reducing leakages and wastages.
AI including Gen-AI capabilities embedded across sales governance, claims management, underwriting and customer engagement, helping grow faster and reduce expense and claims.

key_takeaways: During the quarter, we delivered consolidated profit after tax increase of 40% year-on-year to 1,175 crore Rupees in Q1 of FY27. The total consolidated revenue grew by 29% year-on-year to 14,731 Crore Rupees in Q1 of FY27.

Our NBFC portfolio grew by 28% year-over-year, mainly driven by healthy growth across all segments. Q1 FY27 was a landmark quarter for our housing finance business. Our housing finance portfolio grew by 50% year-on-year and crossed the 50,000-crore milestone.

In insurance businesses, we remain among the fastest growing companies and continue to gain market share. The individual first year premium of the life insurance business grew by 20% year-on-year, and gross written premium of the health insurance business grew by 50% year-on-year.
In our AMC business, the quarterly average mutual fund AUM grew by 6% year-on-year.
In the NBFC business the profit after tax increased by 35% year-on-year and RoA expanded by 14 bps year-on-year to 2.39%.
In the HFC business, the profit after tax almost doubled year-on-year with a continued expansion in RoA.
In life insurance business, our VNB margin doubled year-on-year to 15.1% in Q1 FY27 driven by increased share of non-par, protection and annuity in the product mix.
We implemented IFRS in health insurance from this year reported a profit during Q1 FY27 compared to losses in Q4 and Q1 of last year. The combined ratio for the quarter was 106%.

We raised equity growth capital of 4,000 crore Rupees via preferential allotment, comprising 3,080 crore Rupees from our Promoter and Promoter Group and 920 crore Rupees from International Finance Corporation (IFC), a member of the World Bank Group.
As we move forward, I am pleased to announce our foray into Gold Loans business... We are going live in Q2 and we plan to scale to nearly 200 stand-alone gold loan branches by March 2027.

But the personal consumer share has increased from 12.5% to 14% over the last one year and the growth also has been 41%, wherein the yields in the same period, they have declined kind of 13 bps. How should we read into that?
Abhijit Tibrewal (Motilal Oswal): I'm just trying to understand what is the rate at which we used to do this [personal and consumer] business earlier versus what we are doing right now?

quarters.summary: Management remains confident on sustaining growth, gaining market share and improving profitability while maintaining portfolio quality across businesses. NBFC targets ~2.5% ROA by end of FY27 with credit cost guided at 1.1%-1.2% and margin expansion of 25-30 bps over 2-3 quarters; HFC targets RoA of 2.10%-2.15% (ROE 11.5%-12%, rising to 15%+ in 12-24 months) and AUM of Rs 1 lac crore in 24-30 months with NII range-bound at 5.10%-5.13%; Life insurance guides Individual FYP CAGR of 20%+ for next 3 years while maintaining VNB margins at 18-20% and doubling Net VNB in 3 years.

subsections.label: NBFC business (Rakesh Singh)
points: AUM reached Rs. 1,59,916 Crore in Q4 FY26, reflecting an 8% QoQ and 27% YoY growth; at this rate ABCL NBFC would be amongst the fastest growing diversified NBFCs at this scale.
AUM and profits nearly doubled in the last three years, demonstrating a track record of industry-leading, profitable growth.
AUM crossed Rs 1.5 lac Crore in February with Retail and MSME AUM surpassing Rs 1 Lac Crore.
Highest ever quarterly disbursement (~Rs 25,000 Crore), up 16% QoQ.
Udyog Plus, proprietary B2B platform, nearly doubled in scale with AUM crossing Rs 5,000 Crore.
Portfolio ranks amongst best-in-class in industry with credit costs at 1.04% in Q4, lowest ever.

Disbursements up 25% for the year, driven by Retail and MSME focus segments (68% of total disbursements, grew 33% YoY), reflecting sustained improvements in employee and branch productivity from re-engineering of customer journeys end to end.

Turnaround times across Retail and MSME journeys reduced by over 30% since start of year, powered by deeper integration with digital public infrastructure, efficient file processing, and underwriting platform upgrades with best-in-class rule engines and refreshed scorecards.
MSME proposition expanded with new product launches that saw encouraging response.
Personal and consumer business: disbursements growing 60% for full year to Rs. 18,738 Cr; AUM grew 8% QoQ and 38% YoY to Rs. 21,432 Crore; mix improved 106 bps to 13.4%.

Continued cohort corrections through the year; AI calling bots and behavioral analytics led to higher front-end efficiency and nearly half the flow rates vs last year, resulting in superior asset quality outcomes.
GS2/3 for personal and consumer reduced 50 bps sequentially and 260 bps YoY; GS3 stands at 1.3% as of March 2026.
MSME: Q4 disbursements Rs. 12,023 Crore (21% QoQ growth); book grew 31% YoY to Rs. 91,451 Cr, comprising 57% of overall AUM; 81% secured, 19% unsecured.

Category leader in secured MSME in growth and asset quality; secured MSME AUM growth (27% YoY) faster than industry; healthy asset quality on strong cashflows and collaterals; GS3 at 1%, down 20 bps QoQ, 50 bps YoY.

Unsecured business loans: disbursement growth 28% YoY in Q4, on back of consistent risk cohort calibrations; growth benefited from new product launches (nearly 20% of full year disbursements), with proposition for professionals doing well.
Udyog Plus supports full suite of trade credit solutions digitally and is recognized among top non-bank financers on TReDS exchanges.
Unsecured business loans GS2+GS3 down 90 bps sequentially; GS3 at 1.5%; 40% of GS3 book covered under government guarantee schemes, excluding which GS3 is 0.9%.
Corporate segment grew 3% QoQ, 15% YoY, comprising 29% of overall portfolio, in line with strategy to focus on Retail/MSME; wholesale asset quality improved with GS2+GS3 reduced by 60 bps YoY.
Entity-level GS2+GS3 at 2.4%, improving 38 bps QoQ and 136 bps YoY — lowest in last 5 years; ~72% of book is secured.
Stage 3 book well provided for with PCR of 47.8%, improved 358 bps QoQ.
Credit cost reduced 19 bps QoQ to 1.04%; full-year credit cost reduced 13 bps to 1.18%, better than guided range of 1.2%-1.3%; among the lowest of diversified NBFCs and lowest in last 5 years.
NII for full year increased 18% to Rs. 8,170 Crore; NIM incl. fee was 6.08% for the quarter; Opex to AUM ratio for quarter was 2%.
Q4 PAT Rs 825 Crore, up 7% QoQ, 27% YoY; full year profits grew 20% to Rs 3,001 Crore; ROA increased 6 bps QoQ to 2.31%.

AI progress: by end-FY26, ~65% of contact-centre calls and ~71% of service emails were straight-through processed; AI-driven fraud detection in loan origination via identity data, digital footprints and behavioral signals; AI/ML embedded in credit decisioning including AI co-pilots for credit assessment memos improving productivity, TAT, consistency and governance; GenAI bots in collections enhance contactability and self-cure with 100% call coverage and automated audits; GenAI use cases across operations span grievance handling, agent upskilling, digital contracting, automated letters, and real-time service NPS.

FY27 outlook: Retail and MSME segments to continue pivoting growth strategy; deepen customer relationships via relevant, timely solutions; scale new product variants and leverage ABCD App and Udyog Plus for direct sourcing; approach remains 'grow responsibly, stay close to customers, deliver steady long-term value'.

subsections.label: Housing Finance business (Pankaj Gadgil)
points: FY26 key highlights: highest ever disbursements of ₹25,332 crore (44% YoY growth); AUM reached ₹47,452 crore (53% YoY); ABG ecosystem contributed 17.4% of retail disbursements; Stage 2&3 reduced to 0.76% (63 bps YoY improvement); PBT ₹832 crore (98% YoY growth); ROA 1.88% and ROE 14.27% (note: RoA reported at 2.07% in Q4 elsewhere in transcript).
FY26 pivotal year for housing industry supported by structural tailwinds: rising urbanization, improving affordability, and increasing home ownership across income segments.
Initial guidance was RoA of 2.0%-2.2% over next 6-8 quarters; accelerated with RoA at 2.07% in Q4FY26, supported by strong operating leverage and disciplined execution.

Digital transformation since FY23 delivered: 4x processing capacity scale-up, 96% productivity improvement, TAT improvement from 21 days to 12 days, and Stage 2+3 improved from 4.99% (FY23) to 0.76% (FY26).

Distribution: comprehensive branch footprint assessment identified high-potential geographies; plan to open 100+ branches in FY27 with expansion in Tier 2/3 markets and deepened penetration in metro/Tier 1 cities, supporting target of ₹1 lac crore AUM in next 24-30 months.

AI use cases: FinWise (Sales Manager Productivity) - AI enabled Doc Assist for FTR logins, FinWise co-pilot for objection handling, FinWise+ for channel partner knowledge access; FinEngage for top-of-funnel engagement query handling; FinTellect for back-office automation and faster credit decisions (automated sufficiency/completeness checks, AI-generated CAMs); FinServe Assist for customer experience with ~40% reduction in repeat calls and NPS uplift.

Q4 margin compression: NII fell from 5.22% (Q3) to 5.03% (Q4), 19 bps decline; NIM fell from 4.13% to 4.07% (6 bps), attributed to seasonality and competitive pressures; other income fell from 1.09% to 0.97% due to lower Direct Assignment (DA) volumes (DA done for capital conservation and PBC mix criteria, both comfortable so DA was lower) plus mark-to-market losses on G-Sec-linked investments; insurance attachment income and BT-out repricing were consistent QoQ.

Opex to Average Loan Book improved to 2.4% for FY26 from 2.94% prior year (~50+ bps decrease); anticipate ~2.10%-2.13% this year despite 100+ new branches, driven by operating efficiencies net of branch expansion.
Stage 2+3 currently 76 bps (44 bps Stage3, 32 bps Stage2), among top 2 in industry, giving confidence credit cost will normalize.

subsections.label: Asset Management business (A. Balasubramanian)
points: Meaningful progress strengthening investment team and portfolio construction processes over the last year, resulting in sustained improvement in investment performance, stronger investor confidence, and consistent flows into flagship funds.
PMS/AIF business delivered 3x growth over the year; PMS/AIF AUM excluding ESIC mandate grew 14% YoY reflecting healthy underlying momentum.
EPFO mandate: all agreements signed, operationally ready to receive fund inflows, which will commence shortly.

Real Estate: fund raising underway for Aditya Birla Real Estate Credit Opportunities Fund - Series II, focused on senior secured lending to post-approval, brownfield real estate projects across Tier I cities.
Passive business witnessing significant momentum, outpacing industry growth, supported by a diversified 54 product suite.

Invested in technology/digital ecosystem: launch of new Investor App and enhanced Partner App to simplify customer interactions; built AI foundation across customer journeys via Voice AI, WhatsApp integration and intelligent chatbots.
Incorporated wholly owned subsidiary Aditya Birla Sun Life AMC International (IFSC) Limited at GIFT City and obtained a retail licence to strengthen presence.

subsections.label: Life Insurance business (Kamlesh Rao)
points: ABSLI premium growth of 15% in individual life insurance vs industry 10% and private industry 12%; proprietary business grew 3%, partnership business grew 23%.
Agency business focused on improving retail; direct business grew on productivity.
Proprietary business product mix favourable for growth; added 26 branches, total network now 450+ branches.
Partnership growth of 23% came across all 12 existing partner banks; healthy mix of private and public sector banks with dominant mindshare in many.
At Axis Bank, started with access to 25% of total business, expanded through good performance; will have access to more than 50% of business this year.
Traditional business incl. protection increased to 67%, ULIP came down to 33%, helping expand margins for the year.
Healthy growth in annuity segment (10% of retail new business).

Group life insurance: private industry grew 24%, overall industry grew 19%; calibrated approach to interest-rate-sensitive business caused degrowth in H1, full year grew 31%, enabling return to Rank 4 in group business, driven largely by profitable unit linked business; continue at rank 2 in ULIP AUM in industry.
Credit Life delivered 40% growth, supported by all partners, with 33% of business from captive NBFC/HFC channels.
Group term life continues at 18-20% ROE with healthy renewal book; Group AUM contributes 26% of overall AUM at Rs. 29,000 Cr.
13th month persistency reached 86.1% for full year; renewal premium grew 17% across Individual and Group; digital collections account for 83% of renewal premium.
Customer NPS improved to 66 from 59 last year; Opex to Premium ratio 21.2% including GST and Labour law impact.
22% of total AUM in equity, balance in debt; more than 82% of funds outperformed benchmarks YTD.
Digital adoption: 100% new business customers onboarded digitally, 83% of services available digitally, 67% STP, customer self-service ratio 94%.

AI initiatives under 'Saras.AI' program improving policy issuance, underwriting, and servicing, reducing manual effort, enabling faster underwriting, AI-led handling of conversations across email/calls/WhatsApp, equipping advisors with better insights/tools.

Margin expansion (VNB margin 20.6% vs LYSP 18.0%, +260 bps) driven by controlled ULIP mix, increase in Protection and annuity mix, healthy rider attachments; traditional business saw margin uptick from favourable interest rate and yield curve steepness in H2, partially offsetting GST impact.

Negative operating variance and assumption change variance explained: due to shift from IGAAP to IFRS regime (targeted FY26/FY27 with forbearance requested for FY27), conservatism in valuation interest rate does not unwind under IFRS; assumptions revisited including reduced paid-up benefits on some products; assumption changes largely relate to persistency/lapse experience being better than planned, requiring better reserving now but positive for embedded value growth long-term; reviewed annually, done in January.

subsections.label: Health Insurance business (Mayank Bathwal)
points: FY26 was an eventful year for insurance sector: GST reduced to nil rate, new Insurance Act, new Labour Code, upcoming transition to IFRS reporting from FY27 — all seen as supportive for long-term sector growth with some short-term issues to address.
Continued to be fastest-growing SAHI player during the year; market share increased from 12.6% to 13.7% (110 bps YoY).
Retail franchise grew 43% YoY, diversified across distribution channels; Proprietary channel with 1.86 Lakh+ agents grew 36%; bank and digital alliance partnerships also grew impressively.
Corporate business delivered 35% growth, driven by focused, disciplined strategy to build sustainable franchise; differentiated health-first model extended to corporates with positive response.

Profitability: net profit Rs.39 crores under new accounting (1/n) including new Labour code impact of Rs 5 crores and net GST impact of Rs 36 crores; under old accounting (without 1/n), net profit was Rs 85 crores.
Combined ratio 102% (old accounting) vs 103% (new/1/n framework), vs 105% on comparable basis — improvements reflect continued focus on unit economics ahead of industry.

Health First model resonating with consumers: 40-45% of retail consumers engaging via AI-driven consumer engagement engine; 11.25% of eligible customers earned Health Returns (up from 9% last year), reflecting deep engagement with wellness ecosystem; these customers show 8%+ lower loss ratios and 11%+ better persistency.
Investments in managing high health-risk customers through interventions with more than 270K lives led to loss ratio improvement of more than 9%, helping keep retail loss ratios under control.
Business model requires large investment commitment and persistent effort to mature, giving competitive advantage as scaling continues including corporate side.
AI/ML-driven claims auto-adjudication engine enhances customer satisfaction and reduces leakages/wastages; more than 25% of pre-auth requests processed straight through with no human involvement.
GenAI usage brought 35-40% productivity improvement in underwriting; agentic AI used extensively in renewals management for cost reduction and better consumer confidence/traction.
Consumer app Active Health created very high engagement, with MOU crossing 6 lakh consumers.
FY27 marks 10th year of operations; will continue investing in proprietary distribution franchise, work toward 100% combined ratio, scale Health First approach, and deepen AI/emerging tech embedding.

points: Guidance to grow Individual FYP at a CAGR of 20%+ for next 3 years while maintaining current VNB margins in 18-20% range and doubling absolute Net VNB value in 3 years.

key_takeaways: The consolidated profit after tax, excluding one-off items, increased by 30% year-on-year to 1,124 crore Rupees in Q4 of FY26. For the full year FY26, excluding one-off items, consolidated profit after tax grew by 21% year-on-year
The total consolidated revenue grew by 12% year-on-year in Q4 of FY26 and 14% year-on-year in FY26
Disbursements in the NBFC business grew by 28% year-on-year to about 24,950 crore Rupees and in the HFC business grew by 37% year-on-year to about 7,980 crore Rupees in Q4 FY26

Our NBFC portfolio grew by 27% year-over-year to about 1.6 lakh crore Rupees driven by growth in unsecured and secured business and personal and consumer loans. HFC portfolio grew by 53% year-on-year to about 47,450 crore Rupees

In insurance businesses, we remain among the fastest growing companies. In FY26, the individual first year premium of the life insurance business grew by 15% year-on-year and gross written premium of the health insurance business grew by 39% year-on-year
In our AMC business, the quarterly average mutual fund AUM grew by 14% year-on-year to about 4.35 trillion Rupees
In the NBFC business, the profit after tax increased by 27% year-on-year to 825 crore Rupees in Q4 FY26. The RoA increased by 6 bps year-on-year and sequentially to 2.31%
In the HFC business the profit after tax doubled year-on-year to 200 crore Rupees in Q4 FY26 and 647 Crore Rupees in FY26. The RoA increased by 63 bps year-on-year and 11 bps sequentially to 2.07%

Despite the changes in GST, there was an improvement in the profitability of our insurance businesses. In life insurance business our VNB margin expanded by 260 bps year-on-year to 20.6% in FY26 and in the health insurance business our combined ratio improved to 103% in FY26

We saw strong quality trends across our businesses despite volatile market conditions and uncertainties in operating environment. The GS2 and GS3 loans in the NBFC business declined by 38 bps sequentially to 2.42% and in the HFC business declined by 19 bps sequentially to 0.76%. We have seen no material impact from the geopolitical tensions in West Asia on our portfolio
AI is now becoming a core operating layer for us and we are scaling up its use across various areas such as underwriting, sales, voice calling, audit and compliance, customer service and operations
pressing_questions: So, first question on the margins in the NBFC business. The margins have compressed at almost 4 bps and this is despite a strong growth seen in the unsecured business. This unsecured growth has been continuing since the last 2 quarters now. When do we see the margins improving? Also, can you give the delta between secured and unsecured yields?

Sure. Correspondingly with the rise in margins, credit cost seems to be at almost historical low. So, there could be also some normalization expected here plus growing in the unsecured business would also entail a higher credit cost requirement. As you already mentioned 25-30 bps on the margin front and somewhat probably normalizing on the credit cost front, so, what could be the ROE which we could be looking at in FY27?

FY26 performance is very great and you're guiding again at 1.1-1.2% despite increasing unsecured business. What is your kind of a base case assumption behind this 1.1% to 1.2% guidance in terms of the current conflict because the current conflict is, of course, on certain scenario and that sort of is dragging on. So, based on your kind of assessment, what is your base case estimate where you are guiding for this 1.1% to 1.2%?

When I look at the numbers for this quarter, the opex growth has sharply outpaced the AUM growth and this is for the last three quarters as well. If you could give some light on why this opex growth has been increasing and specifically for this quarter?
In housing finance, we have seen margin compression on a q-o-q basis. What is the reason for that and what is the outlook for margins and ROA in the housing finance business for FY27?
Now in life insurance, there is negative operating variance and assumption change variance. So what are the reasons for that?
The last question is on NBFC. So have we seen spread compression on a line of business basis? Because there is a marginal decline in margin this quarter.

RVNL.about: Rail Vikas Nigam Ltd was Incorporated in 2003 by the Govt. of India, it is engaged in the business of implementing various types of Rail infrastructure projects assigned by MoR including doubling, gauge conversion, new lines, railway electrification, major bridges, workshops, Production Units and sharing of freight revenue with Railways as per the concession agreement entered into with Ministry of Railway. quarters.summary: Management guided for ~15% topline growth and ~15-20% bottom line growth for FY27, reiterating confidence after Q1 (19% YoY PAT growth), targeting INR 20,000-25,000 crore new work orders for the year (against ~INR 5,000-5,500 crore already secured in Q1), with order book mix expected to shift to 50-50 between railway management works and bidding/overseas works over the next two-three years, and management expecting ROE of ~12-13% and EBITDA margin of 5-7% over a three-year vision, while continuing to face geopolitical, labor availability and client payment challenges.

subsections.label: Order book composition and growth drivers
points: Order book continues to remain strong and diversified, providing healthy multi-year execution visibility.

Growth and movement in the order book was supported by new railway and multi-sector infrastructure works awarded to RVNL, steady execution leading to revenue recognition, and disciplined, margin-focused selective bidding strategy.
Strong and well-balanced order book positions the company confidently for sustained growth in coming years.
Order book is primarily driven by railways, followed by S&P, then ports/roads/highways, metros, power and transmission, and hydro and irrigation.

Bidding works, where margins are slightly lower, are also ongoing in parallel, but focus is on works with good margin.

points: Awarded by Bharat Sanchar Nigam Limited to provide high-speed broadband connectivity in rural and remote areas under the DB-1 model.

Initially faced challenges/problems in execution; situation has now improved; work going on in full swing in UP West and UP East.
Payment issues being deliberated with BSNL and are being resolved; some payments received, others in pipeline; hopeful of good revenue this year and remaining quarters.

Project in two parts: implementation of infrastructure at site (3-year timeline, extended by another 6-8 months due to ground line issues with duct and fiber), and maintenance for next 10 years starting automatically once handed over.

Will improve access to the Himalayan region, support the Char Dham pilgrimage corridor, strengthen border connectivity, boost tourism and local economies, and significantly reduce travel time in the region.

Submitted bids in Nepal for hydropower projects; in touch for submitting bids.

Focus basically in railways, metros, highways, and power transmission in these overseas areas.

subsections.label: Order book composition
points: Order book is primarily driven by railways, followed by signaling, then port/roads/highways, then metros, with smaller contributions from power & transmission and hydro & irrigation.

Growth and movement in the order book was supported by new railway and multi-sector infrastructure works awarded to RVNL, execution leading to revenue recognition, and a disciplined margin-focused selective bidding strategy.
This strong and well-balanced order book positions the company competently for sustained growth in the coming years.

subsections.label: Nomination vs bidding strategy
points: Breakup of order book between nomination and bidding is almost 50-50.
Business strategy is to focus on railway works already in pipeline (~30,000 crore works ongoing).
Company is talking to other PSUs and government for management works on a PMC basis, having received works from NMDC, Visakhapatnam Port Trust and others; focus is to get more PMC works.
Third vertical is bidding works, but the company is not bidding very aggressively; target is to secure at least 5-10% profit from each bidding work.

subsections.label: Order inflow vs execution reconciliation
points: Order book inflow (including JVs) was compared against execution of roughly INR 20,000 crore in revenue for the year, with order book still seeing an increase; part of the change comes from scope changes on many projects (especially in metro and other projects), including on gold projects, as per site requirements and client decisions.

Order book reviewed during last financial year was around INR 6,000 crore, and execution from bidding works stood around INR 6,300 crore, so order book inflow and execution broadly matched; in coming years execution from bidding works is expected to increase tremendously, as seen in the increase from INR 2,737 crore in FY24-25 to INR 6,283 crore in FY25-26 (~129% growth).

subsections.label: Contract pricing structure

LEMONTREE.about: Lemon Tree Hotels Ltd is largest mid-priced and the third largest overall hotel chain in India. It operate in the upscale segment and in the mid-priced sector, consisting of the upper-midscale, midscale and economy segments. It delivers differentiated yet superior service offerings, with a value-for-money proposition.[1]

quarters.summary: Management expects Q2 FY27 to show clear recovery from the Q1 aberration (West Asia conflict-led corporate travel slowdown), with July already strong and August solid. EBITDA margins are guided to recover toward 50% net EBITDA margin on a consolidated basis by FY28 (management stated FY27 will be better than 47% but FY28 should be ~50%), as renovation spend tapers off, GST input-credit loss is progressively mitigated via ARR repricing above Rs 7,500, and fee income compounds off an accelerating signings-to-openings pipeline. Fleur continues to deploy capital (targeting ~2,500 rooms via acquisitions/greenfield/brownfield backed by Warburg's Rs 960 crore infusion) while the Lemon Tree-Fleur demerger remains on track for completion in H1 CY2027 subject to SEBI, NCLT, shareholder and creditor approvals.

subsections.label: Margin decline drivers Q1 FY27
points: Net EBITDA margin drop of 99 bps YoY was due to Provision for Stock Appreciation Rights and the loss of input credit in GST levied, which increased expenses by 3.1% of total revenue in Q1 this year versus zero in the previous year same quarter.
Despite 250 bps combined impact from GST and SAR provision, margin decline was only ~100 bps because lower renovation OPEX in the P&L partly offset the impact.
Incremental renovation spend versus normal run-rate was about Rs 6 crore this year in Q1; this will disappear next year as renovation tapers.

subsections.label: Margin recovery trajectory
points: Four/five impacts have played out: a one-off property tax ex-gratia last year, ongoing GST impact, and the massive renovation impact of the last 3 years — all set to disappear except GST, which must be tackled via pricing.

Renovation spend is tapering off; EBITDA margins should recover, with next year's summer margin expected to be 2-2.5% higher than this year, and winter margins higher still due to seasonality/pricing/demand.
Management expects average net EBITDA margin of at least 50% next year, with elements of it visible even in H2 this year.

FY26 EBITDA margin was 49% with a 5.8% combined impact from GST, technology and renovation; GST impact will rise to 2%, technology will rise from 0.6% to 0.9%, but renovation will drop — net 1% reduction in expenses should take margin from 49% to 50%.
Management stated FY27 margin will not be 47% (better than that), and if FY28 does not reach 50%, they consider it an underperformance.

Below-the-line (corporate) expenses do not grow at the rate of revenue growth since investments in technology and people have largely been made; as revenue grows, below-the-line expenses as % of sales will keep reducing.

Hotel-level variable costs are about half of hotel expenses and grow with occupancy; fixed costs (the other half) grow at the rate of inflation — this operating leverage underpins the margin expansion thesis.

subsections.label: Debt and capital structure
points: Group debt (excluding Rs 200 crore cash in Lemon Tree and Fleur) is Rs 1,275 crore at group level, versus Rs 1,200-1,100 crore reported for Fleur.

Occasionally, while building 6 big hotels, debt may briefly cross 2x existing EBITDA; long-term plan is for Fleur debt-to-EBITDA to hover around 2x, seen as a sign of productive capital deployment — if it falls below 2:1, it raises the question of why the company is not growing.
Warburg Pincus is committed to putting in Rs 960 crore into Fleur before listing, to be deployed on new opportunities.

Debt for new hotel construction is matched against known/operating EBITDA rather than presumed EBITDA — a standard risk mitigation practice; acquisitions and builds are funded via a mix of upfront land payment (20-30% of project cost), phased construction spend, and roughly 1:1 debt-equity, with debt drawn mainly in the final year matched to free cash flow.
Gross debt reduced 11% YoY to Rs 1,475 crore as on 30 June 2026 versus Rs 1,657.9 crore a year earlier, with cost of debt down 53 bps to 7.48%.

subsections.label: Renovation case studies / ROI tracking
points: Keys Pimpri renovation cost roughly Rs 11 crore; Keys Whitefield cost about Rs 23 crore — both largely complete high-value renovations.
Second-level Keys renovation (Kochi, Trivandrum, Vizag) will be at about Rs 4-5 lakh per key; balance spend on 300 rooms to finish full Keys portfolio would be about Rs 13-14 crore.

Lemon Tree Premier Delhi renovation cost about Rs 50 crore, Lemon Tree Premier Hyderabad about Rs 35 crore, and Lemon Tree Hotel Delhi about Rs 30-35 crore — together about Rs 85 crore of total renovation spend on high-impact investments; management to share more case studies (EBITDA delta pre/post renovation) in the next investor presentation.
Target is 50% of renovation spend converting into EBITDA improvement, with cumulative renovation/CAPEX spend of about Rs 450 crore expected to break even within 2 years post-renovation.
Fleur reported FY26 net EBITDA (after fees) of Rs 550 crore on total capital deployed of Rs 4,300 crore, implying ROCE of 12.5-13%, with a post-renovation ROCE target of 15%.

points: Rooms opened (334) in Q1 were signed roughly 30 months prior on average.
Rooms signed in Q1 (1,020) are over 3x the inventory opened, indicating acceleration of the signing pipeline relative to openings.

As the company grows more aggressively, some managed contracts will be terminated due to lack of adherence to brand standards; net room addition should be tracked, though losses are expected to be immaterial relative to rooms opened.

points: Network and franchise revenue growth of 29% versus 6% for owned hotels is due to (a) same-store growth of 9-10% in the managed portfolio (some hotels opened last year stabilized this year on a low base) and (b) new hotels added to the managed portfolio contributing incremental revenue and fee income even while not yet at full stabilized capacity.

subsections.label: Rooms opened target confidence
points: Management remains confident of achieving ~2,000 Keys openings for FY27 despite Q1 openings of only 334 rooms, citing the existing pipeline and owner relationships, while acknowledging some slippage/wash is normal in this business.

subsections.label: Keys renovation and performance
points: Keys portfolio nearly 2/3rd renovated as of 30 June 2026, showing significantly improved performance with double-digit growth across all locations.

Hotels renovated earlier (Pimpri, Whitefield) show clear renovation impact in both occupancy and ARR — better pricing and more rooms filled post renovation, visible across a portfolio of 7 hotels, driving the 19% RevPAR increase.

Renovation types differ: high-value renovation (Rs 10-12 lakh/key) for locations like Keys Whitefield/Pimpri targeting both ARR and occupancy improvement (largely complete except Lemon Tree Delhi and Electronic City Bengaluru/Red Fox Hyderabad, completing October); smaller refurbishments (Rs 2.5-3 lakh/room, e.g. Keys Cochin, Vizag, Trivandrum) about 1/3 to 1/2 complete.
Full high-value renovation and refurbishment expected to complete within FY27; FY28 will revert to normal refurb-only spend (~1.2% of revenue).

Management targets Keys occupancy near Lemon Tree average and ARR reflecting full performance next year, working toward Rs 60 crore EBITDA from Keys, implying target revenue of Rs 115-120 crore at ~50% margin and Rs 13-14 lakhs EBITDA per room (Rs 6.5 lakhs per key).

subsections.label: ARR/pricing strategy
points: Only ~2-3% ARR growth in Q1 despite 19% Keys RevPAR growth because retail-channel filling (which carries lower net ARR due to commissions) was used to compensate for softer corporate demand triggered by the West Asia conflict.
Management describes this retail-heavy tactic as temporary, reacting to Q1 conditions; a more balanced approach returning in July/August aims to drive ARR higher while maintaining occupancy strength.

Red Fox by Lemon Tree ARR declined YoY in Q1 partly because Red Fox Delhi Airport was rebranded to Lemon Tree Delhi Airport; last 37 rooms of that 487-room portfolio are under renovation (running over 90% occupancy) and expected to complete by end of Q2; Lemon Tree Delhi and Hyderabad HITEC City are now fully renovated and showing good improvement despite mixed local market conditions.

subsections.label: GST mitigation via room-rate mix
points: GST input credit loss applies to the percentage of rooms sold below Rs 7,500 (currently 52% of company rooms below, 48% above); strategy is to increase the share of rooms priced above this threshold, not eliminate sub-Rs 7,500 rooms entirely (some hotels like Red Fox East Delhi/Jaipur will never cross this threshold).

Demand-dense market hotels with larger inventory and higher revenue per room are being repriced to progressively reduce GST impact toward near-zero: Aurika Mumbai from under 5% currently to 0% target next year; LTP Mumbai from 10-12% to 3-4% target; LTP Hyderabad from 7-8% to 0% target — following a Pareto/weighted-average approach.

subsections.label: Fee income mechanics
points: Fees from Fleur (Rs 22.6 crore, up 6% YoY) still account for 56% of network revenue; as Fleur growth accelerates to double digits, Lemon Tree's fee income from Fleur similarly accelerates in a virtuous cycle.

Third-party fee income of Rs 22.8 crore grew 42% YoY, driven by acceleration in signings (2,000 rooms 3 years ago, 3,500 rooms 2 years ago, ~5,000 rooms last year) which translate into openings ~3 years later and corresponding fee income; as long as the signing growth rate exceeds the opening growth rate, this remains a positive flywheel.
Fee quality varies by city tier — Tier 1/metro fees are higher than Tier 2, which are higher than Tier 3.
Total management fee from Lemon Tree of Rs 45.4 crore grew 21% YoY; pro forma figure of Rs 66 crore includes 2 retained leased hotels contributing an estimated Rs 20 crore EBITDA.

subsections.label: Direct/OTA channel mix
points: OTA contributes mid-30s to late-30s % of business depending on tactical deployment by month/quarter.

As retail plan was deployed more strongly in Q1, the proportion of business from direct channels also increased; management's plan is to keep growing direct share via loyalty program (2.5 million members) and website conversion improvements, with repeat demand at 45% of business.

subsections.label: Fleur asset development pipeline
points: Aurika, Shimla (90-room owned, Rs 108 crore deployed as on 30 June 2026): finishing work and operational licenses in final stage; expected to open shortly.
Aurika, Shillong (165-room leased, Rs 33 crore deployed): expected opening H2 FY28.
Aurika, Varanasi (47-room leased heritage): work begun, expected opening FY29.

Aurika, Nehru Place, Delhi: final approvals pending; expected capital deployment to be announced in due course; expected opening on or after FY2030. An extension of validity of the letter of award for another year was received from DDA, providing time for the project to attain all approvals.

subsections.label: Renovation timeline and cost structure
points: 300 rooms renovated this quarter at ~Rs 10 crore; a similar number (300 or a little more) anticipated next quarter, with 600-700 rooms renovated across H1 FY27 and 800 rooms slated for refurbishment in Q3/Q4.

High-value renovations (Rs 10-12 lakh/key) largely complete except old Red Fox/Lemon Tree Delhi, a small portion of Electronic City Bengaluru (rebranding to Lemon Tree Premier) and Red Fox Hyderabad (rebranding to Lemon Tree Hotel, complete by October).
Smaller refurbishments (Rs 2.5-3 lakh/room) at Keys Cochin, Vizag, Trivandrum are about 1/3 to 1/2 complete; refurb work can take a week to a month and costs much less than full renovation.
Full renovation of main hotels and refurbishment of most Keys/other hotels to complete within FY27; FY28 reverts to normal refurb-only spend, with typical spend around 1.2% of revenue.

Cumulative renovation+capex referenced at ~Rs 450 crore, including ~Rs 230 crore of pre-FY25/FY25 renovation capex; the incremental spend produced a revenue delta of roughly Rs 28-29 crore between Q1 FY26 and Q1 FY27.

subsections.label: Regional performance divergence
points: West Asia conflict led to lesser inbound traffic and uncertainty, which had second-order effects of lesser domestic travel; corporate demand declined most in high-density CBD locations like Mumbai, Hyderabad and Bengaluru.

In Delhi, Hyderabad and Bengaluru, retail strategy more than compensated for the decline in corporate traffic; in Mumbai and Gurgaon, retail could not fully compensate, leading to relative softness in these two markets.

Mumbai market near the airport saw about 2,000 new rooms open in the last 2 years (Novotel, Radisson and other brands), and this supply is still being absorbed, creating a temporary demand-supply mismatch expected to catch up rapidly.

Aurika Mumbai is now considered a stable, recognized brand; management is now focused on repricing/increasing ARR for Aurika Mumbai given its current occupancy levels rather than pursuing further occupancy gains.

subsections.label: International expansion strategy
points: Three international destinations operational: Nepal, Bhutan and Dubai, with fresh Nepal signings this quarter.

Preferred target markets are within ~3 hours' flight where many Indians travel (32 million traveled overseas last year, with over 12 million to UAE/Nepal/Thailand markets historically): UAE (largest, minimally affected by the war beyond a few days), Nepal (expanding significantly), Thailand (Bangkok, Phuket), and to a lesser extent Sri Lanka and Maldives.

Strategy rationale: monetize the loyalty program and repeat-customer base — 45% of demand is repeat, only half of which is in the loyalty program (2.5 million members); many loyalty members travel internationally to these short-haul markets, following the historical playbook of Marriott and Hilton going where their customers travel.

subsections.label: ERP and technology stack evolution
points: In its first 15 years, Lemon Tree's technology stack was archaic — reliance on Excel spreadsheets, a small revenue management system, and multiple vendors for property management and point-of-sale systems.
Post-COVID, an ERP implementation was undertaken, taking about 1.5 years and described as challenging.
Subsequent 2.5 years focused on efficiency improvements, revenue management, better sales integration (e.g., Salesforce), loyalty program and website upgrades.
Kartikeya (formerly Chief Digital and Technology Officer at Coca-Cola) has joined to run the technology vertical, reviewing existing implementations for further improvement.

Technology rollout currently focused in-house/owned portfolio (no owner approval needed); plan is to later extend to the managed portfolio, with new managed contracts stipulating that technology upgrades are at the owner's cost and linked to brand standards.

subsections.label: Sales structure and segment focus
points: Sales structure has been modified to bring focus by segment — airlines, MICE and weddings, and travel trade — at headquarters level, and geographically into 3 regional clusters: North & East, South & West.

Historically, the Lemon Tree model allocated limited space to banquets; management now recognizes weddings/banqueting as a meaningful revenue source and has restructured/added segment leaders (travel trade, MICE, weddings, airlines) to capture this in H2.

No plan to charge additional marketing/franchise fees for national brand campaigns; current fee structure (base fee + sales and marketing fee) already covers a marketing calendar addressing seasonality and quarterly themes (e.g., weddings/celebration theme in Q1/Q2).

subsections.label: Catering business (declined focus)
points: Management declined to pursue an airline catering business, citing focus on core strength of maximizing room revenue; F&B/catering considered a relatively smaller, non-core opportunity versus deepening penetration into India.

subsections.label: Direct channel growth ambition
points: Management intends to grow direct bookings via loyalty program and website conversion, reducing reliance on OTAs over time; this trend was already visible in Q1 as the retail plan pushed up the direct channel share.

subsections.label: Demerger scheme progress and timeline
points: Currently at approval stage with SEBI, after having received CCI approval and undergoing scrutiny by stock exchanges; NCLT process filing, meetings and hearings to follow.
Management indicated calendar year 2027 as the completion year, targeting the first half rather than later part of that year for completing the demerger and listing Fleur.

Process remains subject to SEBI, shareholder vote, creditors' approval and GST approval; after all approvals, listing takes about one more month; given limited control over approval timelines, management conservatively frames completion as late H2 of next year (~12 months from now, as noted by an analyst).
Patanjali Keswani to continue as Executive Director in Fleur for 5 years.

subsections.label: Fleur growth strategy and Warburg backing
points: Fleur was not a going concern for further growth once Aurika Mumbai opened and APG's originally agreed capital was fully deployed; Warburg bought out APG and is committing an additional Rs 960 crore (USD 100 million primary investment) at a USD 1 billion valuation, expected to trigger a significant growth spurt.

Active discussions are underway to add ~2,500 rooms (operating or under development), requiring an estimated Rs 2,500-3,000 crore of capital deployment, into the Fleur portfolio via a mix of brownfield, acquisitions of operating assets (at 6-8x multiples), deep-demand greenfield developments, and long-leased buildings; Fleur has Rs 200-300 crore of balance sheet cash available, and new acquired rooms typically take 3-3.5 years to open.

Investment focus is on three strategies: (1) markets with deep demand in the top 6-7 Indian cities, (2) international markets 3-5 hours' flight from India where many Indians travel overseas, and (3) emerging leisure/tourism destinations such as temple tourism.

Management stated they are not in an 'up cycle' — India occupancy is still in the mid-60s; an up cycle is defined as India occupancy crossing 70-72%, expected next year or the year after; capital allocation decisions in demand-dense (supply-constrained) markets are made independent of cycle timing, using conservative (down-cycle) assumptions for margin of safety.
Company expects to make a bunch of acquisition/development announcements for Fleur within the next few months.

Current Lemon Tree/Warburg stake in Fleur is 59%/41%, moving to 74%/26% post full transfer; post-distribution stake structure envisions Lemon Tree 41%, LT shareholders 33%, Warburg 26% pre-infusion, and post-infusion Lemon Tree 41% on 110, Warburg 36% on 110, LT shareholders 33% on 110.
Fleur is targeting rooms growth of over 50% by FY30, from under 6,000 currently operating plus 850-900 under construction, potentially reaching 3,300 rooms if acquisitions complete.

subsections.label: Lemon Tree standalone economics
points: Lemon Tree's asset-light model requires minimal capital going forward (aside from brand, marketing, generative search and tech investment, which is not meaningful), while fee income continues to accelerate — supply increased 15-16% this quarter, but fee income grew 42%.

Long-term plan targets an EBITDA margin around 75-80% for Lemon Tree over the next 3-4 years, on a much larger base of managed/franchised hotels, with below-the-line expenses targeted at 20-25% of revenue in that target state.

Management describes Lemon Tree as reinventing itself as an asset-light player at scale — a first-of-its-kind position in India's hotel space — and expects the market to increasingly appreciate the fee income growth trajectory over the next 6 quarters.

subsections.label: Geopolitical demand shock
points: West Asia conflict caused the biggest industry-wide impact in Q1: lesser inbound traffic and uncertainty, with second-order effects of reduced domestic corporate travel, hiring and relocation activity, particularly in high-density CBD markets like Mumbai, Hyderabad and Bengaluru.
Large corporate customers tightened belts on travel and T&E expenses, with some companies directly confirming a shift to Zoom calls instead of travel.

subsections.label: Mumbai supply overhang
points: Additional ~2,000 rooms (Novotel, Radisson and other brands) opened in the Mumbai airport micro-market over the last 2 years, creating a temporary supply-demand mismatch still being absorbed.

subsections.label: GST input credit loss
points: Loss of GST input credit on rooms sold below Rs 7,500 increased expenses by 3.1% of total revenue in Q1 FY27 versus zero in the prior-year quarter; this is an ongoing structural cost to be mitigated via repricing strategy, not eliminated entirely.

subsections.label: Stock Appreciation Rights provision
points: Provision for Stock Appreciation Rights (SAR) contributed to the margin decline in Q1 FY27.

subsections.label: Managed portfolio contract friction
points: As the company grows more aggressively into asset-light expansion, there will be cases of contract termination due to lack of adherence to brand standards, causing some room/fee losses — expected to be immaterial relative to overall growth.

subsections.label: Near-term demand outlook
points: Q2 is significantly better than Q1; July saw good recovery and August continues to be solid.

Q1 was described repeatedly as an 'aberration' across ARR, corporate demand and revenue mix; management expects resolution of these issues in Q2 with a return to a balanced mix of ARR and occupancy-driven growth.

subsections.label: Fee income and asset-light growth outlook
points: Rate of growth of signings significantly exceeds rate of growth of openings, creating a positive flywheel; this compounding effect is expected to become clearly visible over the next 2 years.
In FY29 (or FY29-30), the company expects to open ~5,000 rooms in the managed portfolio, representing 45% of current managed inventory of 12,000 rooms (excluding any Fleur contribution).
Management declined to give explicit CAPEX figures for FY27/FY28 on the call, deferring to follow-up (Nipun to share details).

subsections.label: Renovation timeline
points: Full renovation of main hotels and refurbishment programs to complete within FY27; FY28 reverts to normal refurb-only run rate (no major renovation), targeted at 1% of revenue.

subsections.label: Demerger timeline
points: Targeting completion and Fleur listing in H1 of calendar year 2027, subject to SEBI, NCLT, shareholder, creditor and GST approvals; conservative view places completion in late H2 of next year given limited control over approval processes.

points: FY27 EBITDA margin guided better than 47%, with FY28 target of 50%; Fleur targets 15% ROCE post-renovation and long-term debt-to-EBITDA around 2x; Keys portfolio targeted to reach Rs 60 crore EBITDA; Lemon Tree targets 2,000 rooms opened in FY27.

key_takeaways: Total revenue stood at Rs. 346.8 crore, up 9% year-on-year. Net EBITDA stood at Rs. 151.9 crore, up 7%.
Net EBITDA adjusted for GST impact and provision for stock appreciation rights stood at Rs. 162.5 crore in Q1 FY27, up 14% as compared to Rs. 142.1 crore in Q1 FY26.
PAT grew 19% to Rs. 57.3 crore and cash profit grew 17% to Rs. 96 crore.
Our gross ARR stood at Rs. 6,361, up 2% year-on-year and occupancy was 75.7%, up 314 basis points versus last year.

Our net EBITDA margin for Q1 FY27 stood at 43.8%, which was 99 basis points less than 44.8%, which we achieved last year in Q1 FY26. This drop was due to Provision for Stock Appreciation Rights and the loss of input credit in the GST levied, which increased our expenses by 3.1% of total revenue in Q1 this year versus zero in the previous year same quarter.
Our gross debt on 30th June 2026 stood at Rs. 1,475 crore, down 11% from Rs. 1,657.9 crore a year ago, and our cost of debt reduced to 7.48%, down 53 basis points versus a year ago.
Combined operational and pipeline inventory now stands at 23,381 rooms across 279 hotels in 170+ cities, of which 135 hotels, which is 11,946 rooms across 80-plus cities are already operational.
Network revenue for the quarter grew at 16% year-on-year to Rs. 576 crore with owned hotels contributing Rs. 320 crore and managed and franchised hotels contributing Rs. 256 crore.
Keys portfolio RevPAR in Q1 FY27 was up 19% year-on-year to Rs. 2,885 on the back of a 350-basis point improvement in occupancy to 67% and 13% growth in average room rate to Rs. 4,311.
For Lemon Tree on a pro forma basis in Q1 FY27, revenue stood at Rs. 65.7 crore versus Rs. 54 crore in Q1 last year, which is up 22%.
For Fleur on a pro forma basis, FY27 revenue stood at Rs. 311.4 crore versus Rs. 292 crore, up 7%.

quarters.summary: FY26 was Lemon Tree's best year on Occupancy, ARR, Revenue, EBITDA, PBT, PAT and Cash Profit, with margins pressured by renovation, tech and GST costs which management expects to reduce to ~3.7% of revenue by FY28. The Fleur demerger is progressing with CCI approval received and NCLT process ongoing (estimated 12-18 months); post-scheme Lemon Tree is expected to become a debt-free, asset-light, high-margin (steady-state ~70%+ fee flow-through, ~60% PAT margin) company, while Fleur will be a large ownership/development platform targeting 2,500 additional rooms with Warburg Pincus capital backing.
